items.text: Al-Shaykh al-Jalil Abu Ja‘far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Habbal al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Muhsin narrated to us from Yunus b. Thibyan from al-Sadiq Ja‘far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): Why do I see you alone? He said: I have abandoned the people, and they have abandoned me for Your sake. He said: Then why do I see you silent? He said: My awe of You has silenced me. He said: Then why do I see you exhausted? He said: Loving You has exhausted me. He said: Then why do I see you poor when I have enriched you? He said: Fulfilling my duty to You has impoverished me. He said: Then why do I see you humbled? He said: The greatness of Your majesty, which cannot be described, has humbled me; and that is rightfully Yours, O my Master. Allah, glorified is His majesty, said: So rejoice with the bounty from Me, for you shall have whatever you desire on the Day you meet Me. Associate with the people, and treat them with good manners, and distinguish yourself from them in their deeds, and you shall attain what you want from Me on the Day of Resurrection. And al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Allah, mighty and glorified, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): O Dawud! Rejoice by Me, seek pleasure by remembering Me, and seek enjoyment by speaking to Me. Soon, I will empty the abode of the transgressors, and I will place My curse upon the oppressors.

Yunus ibn Thibyan said: Al-Sadiq narrated to me from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: When Allah, blessed and exalted, willed to take the soul of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), He sent the Angel of Death down to him, who said: 'Peace be upon you, O Ibrahim.' He said: 'And upon you be peace, O Angel of Death. Have you come to summon me, or to announce my death?' He said: 'Rather, to summon you, O Ibrahim. So answer.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you ever seen a friend cause his friend to die?' He said: So the Angel of Death returned until he stood before Allah, great is His majesty, and said: 'My God, You have heard what Your friend Ibrahim said.' Then Allah, great is His majesty, said: 'O Angel of Death, go to him and say to him: Have you ever seen a lover who hates meeting his beloved? Indeed, the lover loves to meet his beloved.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad the just goldsmith narrated to us. He said: Isa ibn Muhammad al-Alawi narrated to us. He said: Abu Uwana narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Bazi al-Khazzaz narrated to us. He said: Ismail ibn Aban narrated to us, from Sallam ibn Abi Amra al-Khurasani, from Maruf ibn Kharbudh al-Makki, from Abu al-Tufayl Amir ibn Wathila, from Hudhayfa ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Hudhayfa! Indeed, the Proof of Allah upon you after me is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Disbelief in him is disbelief in Allah, associating partners with him is associating partners with Allah, doubt in him is doubt in Allah, heresy regarding him is heresy regarding Allah, denial of him is denial of Allah, and faith in him is faith in Allah -- for he is the brother of the Messenger of Allah, his deputy, the Imam of his nation and their master. He is the firm Rope of Allah and His firm Handle that has no crack in it. Two will be destroyed regarding him, to no fault of his: an excessive lover and one who falls short. O Hudhayfa! Do not ever split away from Ali, for you will have split from me; and do not ever oppose Ali, for you will have opposed me. Indeed, Ali is from me and I am from him. Whoever angers him has angered me, and whoever pleases him has pleased me.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us from 'Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Najran from al-Mufaddal b. Salih from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Musa b. 'Imran (peace be upon him) said: O Lord! I am pleased with what You have decreed, yet You cause adults to die and leave behind their young children. So Allah, exalted is His majesty, said: O Musa! Are you not pleased with Me as their Sustainer and Protector? He said: Of course, O Lord! You are the best Trustee, and the best Protector.

Ali ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Habbal al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khashshab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhsin ibn Isa narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Thibyan, who said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a prophet from among the prophets of the Children of Israel: If you would like to meet Me tomorrow in the Guarded Sanctuary, then be in this world alone, a stranger, worried, sorrowful, and shunning the people -- like a lone bird that flies in the wastelands, eats from the tops of trees, and drinks from the water of springs. When night comes, it shelters alone and does not shelter with the other birds; it finds comfort in its Lord and shuns the other birds.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa from al-Husayn b. Sayf from Sallam b. Ghanim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever says "there is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illallah) one hundred times when he goes to his bed, Allah builds a house for him in Paradise. And whoever seeks forgiveness (istighfar) one hundred times when he goes to his bed, his sins will fall away just as the leaves of a tree fall.

Al-Husayn b. Sayf said: My brother 'Ali b. Sayf narrated to me from his father Sayf b. 'Umayra from al-Hasan b. al-Sabbah. He said: Anas b. Malik narrated to me from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family). He said: Every obstinate tyrant is one who refuses to say "there is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illallah).

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Salama b. al-Khattab from Ibrahim b. Muhammad from Imran al-Za'farani from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: There is no man who supplicates and then seals his supplication by saying 'Whatever Allah wills — there is no power except by Allah' (ma sha'Allah, la quwwata illa billah) except that he is answered.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abu Jamila from Jabir from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: An angel from the angels passed by a man standing at the door of a house. The angel said to him: 'O servant of Allah, what makes you stand at the door of this house?' He said: 'A brother of mine is in it; I wanted to greet him.' The angel said: 'Is there close kinship between you and him, or did a need bring you to him?' He said: So he said: 'No, there is no kinship between us, nor did any need bring me to him — only the brotherhood of Islam and his sanctity. I pledge myself to him and greet him for the sake of Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.' The angel said: 'I am a messenger of Allah to you. He sends you His peace and says: It is only Me that you wanted, and it is to Me that you pledged. I have made Paradise obligatory for you, relieved you from My anger, and delivered you from the Fire.'

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, when Allah — Blessed and Exalted — sees the people of a village committing excess in sins, and there are three believers among them, He calls to them — Exalted is His majesty, and sanctified are His names: 'O people of disobedience to Me! Were it not for the believers among you who love one another for the sake of My majesty, who enliven My earth and My mosques with their prayers, and who seek forgiveness at dawn out of fear of Me, I would have sent down My punishment upon you and not cared.'
By this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is distraught by his sin and made happy by his good deed is a believer.

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhawayh al-Mu'addib (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' narrated to us from his father. He said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn the Master of Worshipers, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali the Master of Martyrs, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib the Master of Deputies (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever blesses me without blessing my family will not find the fragrance of Paradise, and indeed its fragrance can be found from the travel distance of five hundred years.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sahban, altogether, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he came out to him in a cloak dyed reddish. So the Bedouin said: O Muhammad! You have come out to me as though you are a young man! So he said: Yes, O Bedouin. I am a young man, son of a young man, brother of a young man. So the Bedouin said: O Muhammad! As for being a young man, then yes; but how are you the son of a young man and brother of a young man? So he said: Have you not heard Allah — Mighty and Majestic — saying: 'They said: We heard a young man mentioning them, called Ibrahim'? So I am the son of Ibrahim. And as for the brother of a young man: a caller called from the sky on the day of Uhud: 'There is no sword except Dhul-Fiqar, and there is no young man except Ali.' So Ali is my brother, and I am his brother.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Qasim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: A man wrote to al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him): "O my Master! Inform me of the best of this world and the Hereafter." So he wrote to him: "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. As for what follows: Whoever seeks the pleasure of God despite the discontent of the people, God will suffice him in the affairs of the people. And whoever seeks the pleasure of the people despite the discontent of God, God will entrust him to the people. And peace."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn al-Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn Ubaydullah ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us. He said: Yahya ibn al-Husayn ibn Ja'far narrated to me. He said: A shaykh from the people of Yemen named Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to me. He said: I heard Abd al-Razzaq say: A handmaid of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was pouring water upon him while he was making ablution for prayer. The pitcher fell from the hand of the handmaid upon his face, scraping him. Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) raised his head toward her. The handmaid said: "Surely God the Mighty and Majestic says: 'and those who restrain their anger.'" He said to her: "I have restrained my anger." She said: "'and those who pardon the people.'" He said: "God has forgiven you." She said: "'and God loves the doers of good.'" He said: "Go, for you are free."

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both). He said: I heard my grandfather the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) say to me: Perform the obligations of God, and you will be the most Godfearing of people. Be content with the portion of God, and you will be the richest of people. Abstain from the forbidden things of God, and you will be the most pious of people. Beautify your neighbourliness to your neighbours, and you will be a believer. Beautify your companionship with your companions, and you will be a Muslim.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn 'Amer from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Aban ibn Taghlub from 'Ikrama from Ibn 'Abbas. He said: When the first silver coin and gold coin hit the ground, Iblis looked to them. When he observed them, he took them and placed them on his eyes. Then, he embraced them to his chest. Then, he screamed. Then, he embraced them to his chest. Then, he said: You two are the joy of my eye and the fruit of my heart. I would not mind if the Children of Adam loved you instead of worshiping idols. For me, it is sufficient for the Children of Adam to love you.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from 'Abis ibn Hisham, from more than one person, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: The readers of the Quran are of three types: A man who read the Quran and took it as merchandise, used it to attract the rulers and to lord over the people. A man who read the Quran, memorized its letters but wasted its limits. And a man who read the Quran and applied the medicine of the Quran to the illness of his heart, kept vigil through the night by it, endured thirst during the day, stood in prayer in his mosques, and forsook his bed for its sake. Through such people Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repels calamities; through them Allah grants victory over the enemies; and through them Allah sends down rain from the sky. By God, such people in their recitation of the Quran are more precious than red sulfur.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) passed by a man planting a plant in a walled garden of his. So he stopped before him and said: Shall I not guide you to a plant with firmer roots, quicker ripening, sweeter fruits, and more lasting produce? He said: Of course — may my father and mother be your sacrifice, O Messenger of God. So he said: When you awake in the morning and when you reach the evening, say: Glory be to God, and all praise belongs to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the greatest. For indeed, if you say that, with each glorification you will have ten trees in Paradise of various kinds of fruit, and they are from the everlasting good deeds. He said: The man then said: I bear you witness, O Messenger of God, that this walled garden of mine is a charity given to the poor Muslims from the people of al-Suffah. So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: As for he who gives and fears God and testifies to goodness, We shall surely ease his way toward bliss. (92:5-7)

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Furat, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) is the vicegerent of God and my vicegerent, the proof of God and my proof, the gate of God and my gate, the elect of God and my elect, the beloved of God and my beloved, the friend of God and my friend, and the sword of God and my sword. He is my brother, my companion, my vizier, and my deputy. His lovers are my lovers, his haters are my haters, his supporters are my supporters, his enemies are my enemies, his war is my war, his peace is my peace, his word is my word, his command is my command, his wife is my daughter, his descendants are my descendants, and he is the Master of Deputies and the best of my entire nation.

The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Ubaydillah narrated to me, from his father, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them all) who said: The masters of the people in this world are the generous, and in the Hereafter are the pious.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Harun b. Muslim narrated to us from Mas'ada b. Sadaqa from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: A believer has seven obligatory rights over another believer from God, Mighty and Majestic: honouring him in his eyes, love for him in his heart, sharing with him from his wealth, prohibiting backbiting about him, visiting him during his illness, attending his funeral, and saying nothing about him after his death except good.

al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad b. Sinan. He said: Abu'l-Jarud Ziyad b. al-Mundhir narrated to us from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: The wilaya of Ali b. Abi Talib is the wilaya of God. Loving him is the worship of God. Obeying him is obligated by God. His friends are the friends of God, his enemies are the enemies of God, his war is God's war, and his peace is the peace of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali b. Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us from Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Rawyani from Abd al-Azim b. Abd al-Husni from Sulayman b. Ja'far al-Ja'fari. He said: I heard Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both) say: My father narrated to me from his father from the Master of Worshippers Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) passed by a man who was speaking superfluously. So, he stopped by him, and then said: Surely, you are dictating a letter to your Lord through your two guardian angels. So, speak about what concerns you, and leave that which does not concern you.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Nuh b. Shu'ayb al-Nishapuri from Ubaydullah b. Abdullah al-Dahqan from Urwa the nephew of Shu'ayb al-Aqraquqi from Shu'ayb from Abi Basir. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) narrating from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said one day to his companions: Which of you fast the whole year? So, Salman (may Allah's mercy be upon him) said: I, O Messenger of Allah. So, the Messenger of Allah said: So, which of you keep vigil at night? So, Salman said: I, O Messenger of Allah. He said: So, which of you completes the Quran every day? So, Salman said: I, O Messenger of Allah. So, one of his companions became angry and said: O Messenger of Allah! Salman is a man from Persia, and he wants to boast over us, the people of Quraysh. You said, 'Which of you fast the whole year?', and he said, 'I', when he eats on most days. You said, 'Which of you keep vigil at night?', and he said, 'I', when he sleeps most of the night. You said, 'Which of you completes the Quran everyday?', and he said, 'I', when he is silent for most of the day. So, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Cease, O person. How can you compare with Luqman the Wise? Ask him, and he will inform you. So, the man said to Salman: O Aba Abdillah! Did you not allege that you fast every day? He said: Yes. He said: I saw you eating on most days! He said: It is not as you think. I fast three days in a month, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten the like thereof.' [6:160] And I connect Sha'ban with the month of Ramadan, which is like fasting the whole year. He said: Did you not allege that you keep vigil at night? He said: Yes. He said: You sleep for most of the night! He said: It is not as you think, but I have heard my Beloved, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) say: 'Whoever goes to sleep in a state of purity, it is as though he has kept vigil all night', and I go to sleep in a state of purity. He said: Did you not allege that you complete the Quran every day? He said: Yes. He said: But you are silent on most days. He said: It is not as you think, as I have heard my Beloved, the Messe

Ja'far b. Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. Ali narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: When the scholars and wise men of the past wrote to one another, they wrote only about three things, without a fourth: Whoever is worried about the Hereafter, God will take care of his worries in this world. Whoever rectifies his inner self, God will rectify his outer self. Whoever rectifies that which is between him and God, Mighty and Majestic, God will rectify for him that which is between him and the people.

Muhammad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from Muhammad b. Isa from Mansur from Hisham b. Salim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: No reward follows a man after his death except in three things: a charity that he established during his life, which continues after his death; a tradition of guidance that he instituted, which is practiced after his death; and a righteous child who seeks forgiveness for him.

Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natanah (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Ja'far b. Salama al-Ahwazi from Ibrahim b. Muhammad. He said: Abu'l-Husayn Ali b. al-Mu'alla al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: I was informed from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) that he said: Surely, for Allah there are regions called Vengeance. When Allah gives a servant wealth and that servant does not pay what is due to Allah the Mighty and Majestic from it, Allah inflicts upon him a piece of land from those regions, so the wealth is squandered therein, then he dies and abandons it.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari and Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Imran b. Musa from al-Hasan b. Ali b. al-Nu'man from Muhammad b. Fudayl from Ghazwan al-Dabbi. He said: Abd al-Rahman b. Ishaq informed me from al-Nu'man b. Sa'd from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). He said: I am the Proof of Allah, the Caliph of Allah, the Path of Allah, the Gate of Allah, the Treasurer of Allah's Knowledge, the Keeper of Allah's Secret, and the Imam of creation after the best of creation, Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy (may Allah bless him and his family).

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah. He said: Sulayman ibn Muqbil al-Madini narrated to me. He said: Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father Muhammad ibn Ali from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali from his father Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: I visited the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) in the Quba Mosque, and with him was a group of his companions. When he caught sight of me, his face became radiant and he smiled, until I saw the shining whiteness of his teeth. Then he said: To me, O Ali! To me, O Ali! He kept drawing me closer until my thigh touched his thigh. Then he turned to his companions and said: O my companions! Mercy has come to you with the coming of Ali, my brother, to you. O my companions! Truly, Ali is from me and I am from Ali. His spirit is from my spirit and his clay is from my clay. He is my brother, my deputy, and my vicegerent over my Nation in my lifetime and after my death. Whoever obeys him has obeyed me, whoever supports him has supported me, and whoever opposes him has opposed me.

Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amer. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to us from Aban ibn Uthman. He said: Aban ibn Taghlub narrated to us from Ikrama, from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever wishes to live my life, die my death, enter the Garden of Eden — my abode — and grasp a branch planted by my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to which He said 'Be!' and it was, then let him accept the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib and follow the successors from among his descendants; for they are my progeny, created from my clay. I complain to Allah about their enemies from my nation — those who deny their virtue and sever my bond through them. By Allah, my son al-Husayn will surely be killed after me, and Allah will not grant them my intercession.

The elder jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa from 'Ali b. al-Hakam from Dawud b. al-Nu'man from Sayf al-Tammar from Abu Basir. He said: Al-Sadiq Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Indeed, the servant is in a period of respite in his affair between him and forty years of age. When he reaches forty years of age, God, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to His two angels: "Indeed, I have granted My servant a lifespan, so be harsh, be strict, and be vigilant; and record against him the small and the great of his deeds, and the minor and the major of them."

Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "Did We not give you lives long enough so that whoever wanted to be mindful could have done so?" [35:37] So he said: A rebuke to one who has reached eighteen years of age.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Salama b. al-Khattab from 'Ali b. al-Hasan from Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Mu'addab from 'Asim b. Humayd from Khalid al-Qalanisi. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: An elderly man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be given his book. On its apparent side — that which faces the people — nothing will be seen but sins. That will be prolonged upon him, so he will say: 'O my Lord! Will You command me to the Fire?' So the Almighty, exalted is His Majesty, will say: 'O elderly man! Indeed, I am ashamed to punish you while you used to pray in the abode of this world. Take My servant to Paradise.'

Muhammad b. 'Ali narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. Muhammad b. Abi'l Qasim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umar al-'Adani in Mecca from Abu'l 'Abbas b. Hamza from Ahmad b. Sawwar from 'Ubaydallah b. 'Asim from Salama b. Wardan from Anas b. Malik. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: If a believer dies leaving behind one sheet of knowledge, that sheet will be a curtain between him and the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. For every letter written on it, Allah, blessed and exalted, will grant him a city seven times wider than this world. And no believer sits a moment with a scholar except that his Lord, mighty and exalted, calls to him: 'You have sat to attend My beloved. By My glory and My majesty, I will surely make you dwell in Paradise with him, regardless.'

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani al-Mukattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: 'Ubaydallah b. Musa al-Habbal al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Muhsin narrated to us from Yunus b. Thibyan. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Surely, the people worship Allah, mighty and exalted, for three reasons. One group worships Him out of desire for His reward — that is the worship of the possessive, and it is of greed. Others worship Him out of fear of the Fire — that is the worship of the slaves, and it is of fright. But I worship Him out of love for Him, mighty and exalted — that is the worship of the nobles, and it is of safety. As He, mighty and exalted, says: "and they will be safe from the horror of that Day" [27:89], and as He, mighty and exalted, says: "Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive your sins" [3:31]. So whoever loves Allah, Allah will love him; and whoever Allah, mighty and exalted, loves, he will be among the safe ones.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Ziyad al-Nahdi, from 'Abdullah ibn Wahb, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: It is enough of a victory from God for the believer to see his enemy committing acts of disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim al-Mu'addab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashar from 'Ubaydallah ibn 'Abdullah al-Dahqan from Darast ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi'l 'Ala' from Thabit ibn Dinar from Sa'd ibn Turayf al-Khaffaf from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: I am the vicegerent of the Messenger of Allah, his vizier, and his inheritor. I am the brother of the Messenger of Allah, his deputy, and his beloved. I am the elite one of the Messenger of Allah and his companion. I am the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, the husband of his daughter, and the father of his descendants. I am the Master of the Deputies and the Deputy of the Master of Prophets. I am the decisive argument, the great sign, the highest ideal, and the gate of the Chosen Prophet. I am the Firm Handle, the pious word, and the faithful of Allah - exalted is His mention - over the people of this world.

Ahmad ibn Harun (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from his father Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami', from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: If a depraved person openly declares his depravity, then he has no sanctity and there is no backbiting [regarding him].

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Talha ibn Zayd, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Gabriel came to me from my Lord, exalted is His majesty, and said: O Muhammad! Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, conveys His greeting of peace to you and says: Give glad tidings to your brother Ali that I will not punish one who aligns with him, nor will I show mercy to one who opposes him.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Asadi al-Barda'i narrated to us. He said: Ruqayya bint Ishaq ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, from her father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: No servant's feet will move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four things: about his life and how he spent it, about his youth and how he used it, about his wealth — where he earned it and how he spent it, and about his love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to me. He said: Bakr b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Tamim b. Bahlul narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Salih b. Abi Salama al-Nasibini narrated to us. He said: Abu Awana narrated to us, from Abi Bishr, from Sa'id b. Jubayr, from A'isha. She said: I was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, when Ali b. Abi Talib came forward. So he [the Prophet] said: This is the Master of the Arabs. I said: O Messenger of Allah, are you not the Master of the Arabs? He said: I am the Master of the Children of Adam, and Ali is the Master of the Arabs. I said: And what is a Master? He said: One whose obedience was made obligatory, just as obedience to me was made obligatory.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qadi al-Alawi al-Abbasi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Nasir (may God sanctify his spirit) narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Rashid narrated to me, from his uncle Abu Ma'mar Sa'id ibn Khuthaym, from his brother Mu'ammar, who said: I was sitting with al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) when Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came and held onto the two doorposts. Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said to him: "O uncle, I seek refuge in God for you from being the one crucified at Kinasa." The mother of Zayd said to him: "By God, nothing drives you to say this except envy of my son." He (peace be upon him) said: "If only it were envy, if only it were envy" -- three times. Then he said: "My father narrated to me, from my grandfather (peace be upon them both), that from his progeny there will emerge a man named Zayd, who will be killed in Kufa and crucified at Kinasa. He will be exhumed from his grave. The gates of heaven will be opened for his spirit, and the inhabitants of the heavens will rejoice in him. His spirit will be placed in the crop of a green bird that roams wherever it wishes in Paradise."

Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: al-Ash'ath ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to us, he said: Shu'ayb ibn Umar narrated to me, from his father, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: I visited Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), and his brother Zayd (peace be upon him) was with him. Then Ma'ruf ibn Kharbudh al-Makki entered, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "O Ma'ruf, recite for me some of the gems of your poetry." So he recited: "By your life, Abu Malik is neither feeble nor weak in his strength, nor obstinate in his speech opposing the wise one when he forbids him. But he is an outstanding master, noble in nature, pleasant in his discourse. When you lead him, he leads obediently, and whatever you entrust to him, he suffices." He said: Then Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) placed his hand on Zayd's shoulders and said: "This is your description, O Abu al-Husayn."

The Sheikh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu al-Ward from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon to the people on the last Friday of Sha'ban. He praised and commended Allah, then said: O people! A month has shaded you containing a night better than a thousand months; it is the month of Ramadan. Allah has obligated its fasting and made voluntary prayer in one of its nights equivalent to seventy nights of voluntary prayer in other months. He has made a voluntary good deed therein like the reward of one who performed an obligation of Allah's obligations, and whoever performs an obligation therein, it is as if he performed seventy obligations in other months. It is the month of patience, and the reward of patience is Paradise. It is the month of sympathy. It is a month in which Allah increases the sustenance of the believer. Whoever feeds a fasting believer therein, it will be for him with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the freeing of a slave and forgiveness for his past sins. So it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah! Not all of us can feed a fasting person. He said: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, is generous. He gives this reward to those of you who cannot manage more than a sip of milk to feed a fasting person, or a drink of fresh water, or some small dates. And whoever lightens the burden on his servant therein, Allah will lighten his reckoning. It is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is the answering of prayers and freedom from the Fire. You cannot do without four traits therein: two with which you please Allah, and two you cannot do without. As for the two with which you please Allah: it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. As for the two you cannot do without: you ask Allah for your needs and Paradise, and you ask Allah for well-being therein and seek refuge in Him from the Fire.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us from Ishaq b. Muhammad, from Hamza b. Muhammad. He said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan b. Ali b. Muhammad b. Ali b. Musa b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them): 'Why did Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, obligate fasting?' The answer came in his response: 'So that the rich may feel the touch of hunger and thus give to the poor.'

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Salih ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi informed us. He said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us. He said: al-Walid ibn Hisham narrated to us. He said: Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm al-Dawsi. He said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) weeping. He greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: What makes you cry, O Mu'adh? He said: O Messenger of Allah, at the door there is a youth with a soft body, pure complexion, and good appearance, weeping over his youth as a bereaved mother weeps over her child, and he wants to enter upon you. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Let the youth enter, O Mu'adh. So he brought him in, and he greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: What makes you cry, O youth? He said: How can I not cry when I have committed sins such that if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were to take me for some of them, He would cast me into the Fire of Hell, and I see nothing but that He will take me for them, and will never forgive me. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Have you associated any partners with Allah? He said: I seek refuge in Allah from associating anything with my Lord. He said: Have you killed a soul that Allah has prohibited? He said: No. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they were like the great mountains. The youth said: Surely they are greater than the great mountains. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they were like the seven earths, their oceans, their sands, their trees, and all creatures therein. He said: Surely they are greater than the seven earths, their oceans, their sands, their trees, and all creatures therein. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they were like the seven heavens and their stars, and like the Throne and the Seat. He said: Surely they are greater than that. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) looked at him angrily, then said: Woe to you, O youth! Are your sins greater, or your Lord? So the youth fell o

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us. He said: Ahmad b. Salih narrated to us from Hakim b. Abd al-Rahman. He said: Muqatil b. Sulayman narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him): O Ali! You are to me as Habatullah was to Adam, and as Sam was to Nuh, and as Ishaq was to Ibrahim, and as Harun was to Musa, and as Sham'un was to Isa, except that there is no prophet after me. O Ali! You are my deputy and my vicegerent. So whoever denies your deputyship and your vicegerency, he is not from me and I am not from him, and I will be his adversary on the Day of Resurrection. O Ali! You are the best of my nation in virtue, the foremost of them in affability, the most knowledgeable of them, the most forbearing of them, the boldest of them in heart, and the most generous of them with their hands. O Ali! You are the Imam after me and the emir. You are the companion after me and the vizier. You have no equal in my nation. O Ali! You are the divider of Paradise and the Fire. By your love, the righteous will be known from the wicked, and the evil will be distinguished from the elect, and the believers from the disbelievers. May Allah's blessings be upon His Messenger Muhammad and his family.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from al-Husayn b. Ulwan from Amr b. Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) would, when he saw the crescent moon of Ramadan, face the qibla and say: O Allah! Let the crescent appear upon us with security, faith, peace, Islam, magnificent wellness, encompassing sustenance, warding of illnesses, recitation of the Quran, and assistance for prayer and fasting. O Allah! Deliver us to the month of Ramadan, deliver it to us, and accept it from us; until the month of Ramadan ends and You have forgiven us. Then he would face the people and say: O assembly of Muslims! When the crescent moon of Ramadan appears, the rebellious devils are chained, the gates of heaven, Paradise, and mercy are opened, and the gates of the Fire are closed. Prayers are answered, and at every breaking of fast, Allah frees captives from the Fire. Every night a caller calls: 'Is there anyone who asks? Is there anyone who seeks forgiveness? O Allah! Give every spender a replacement, and give every withholder a loss.' Until the crescent of Shawwal appears, and the believers are called to go forth to their rewards, for it is the Day of Reward. Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, by the One in whose Hand is my soul! It is not a reward of gold and silver coins.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Mu'adhi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Haywayh al-Jurjani al-Mudhakkir narrated to us. He said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Bilal narrated to us. He said: Abu Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Karram narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us. He said: Mu'awiya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. He said: I asked Ibn Abbas: What will be given to one who fasts the month of Ramadan and recognizes its right? He said: Prepare - O Ibn Jubayr - so that I may tell you something that your ears have never heard and that has never come to your heart. Empty yourself for what you have asked me about, for what you wanted is the knowledge of the ancients and the later ones. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: So I left him and prepared for the next day. I went early at dawn, prayed the dawn prayer, then mentioned the hadith. He turned his face toward me and said: Listen to what I say: I heard the Messenger of God (may blessings be upon him and his family) say: If you were to know what you have in Ramadan you would increase your thanksgiving to God. On the first night, God forgave all the sins of my Nation, raised you by two million ranks, and built fifty cities for you. On the second through tenth days, God records for every step the worship of a year and the reward of a prophet; gives domes of pearl in Paradise with houses of light; palaces in the Paradise of Eternity with heavenly maidens; cities in the Paradise of Refuge with tablespreads of food; cities in the Abode of Peace with beds of gold and spouses from the houris; the reward of martyrs and saints; the deeds of worshipers and ascetics; the gifts of scholars and retreaters; the fulfillment of seventy thousand needs with all creation seeking forgiveness for you. On the eleventh through twentieth days: the reward of four pilgrimages and Umras; sins changed to good deeds multiplied a million times; the worship of the people of Mecca and Medina; meeting the prophets Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Dawud, and Sulayman; fulfillment of needs and forty lights on the Day of Resurrection; garments and a she-camel from the grave; divine forgiveness for them and their fathers; angels ordered to seek forgiveness until the following year; all angels in heaven and earth visit your graves; seventy thousand protective angels, a t

On this day also, the Sheikh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Salama narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Absi narrated to us. He said: Muhalhil al-Abdi narrated to us. He said: Kudayra b. Salih al-Hijri narrated to us from Abu Dharr Jundub b. Junada (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) say three phrases to Ali (peace be upon him); each of which, if I had but one, would be more beloved to me than the world and all that is in it. I heard him say: O Allah! Assist him and assist others through him. O Allah! Support him and gain victory through him, for indeed he is Your servant and the brother of Your Messenger. Then Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: I bear witness to the allegiance, brotherhood, and deputyship of Ali. And Kudayra b. Salih said: Salman al-Farisi, al-Miqdad, Ammar, Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari, Abu al-Haytham b. al-Tayhan, Khuzayma b. Thabit the possessor of the two testimonies, Abu Ayyub the owner of the house of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family), and Hashim b. Utba al-Mirqal would also bear witness to the like of that for him. All of them were from the best of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family).

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Faqih al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. al-Husayn from Muhammad b. Jumhur, and from Muhammad b. Ziyad, from one who heard Muhammad b. Muslim al-Thaqafi say: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them) say: Indeed, Allah the Exalted has angels assigned to the fasting people. They seek forgiveness for them every day of the month of Ramadan until its end. They call to the fasting people every night at the time of their breaking of fast: 'Rejoice, O servants of Allah! You have hungered a little and you will be satiated much. You are blessed, and blessing be upon you.' Until, on the last night of the month of Ramadan, they call to them: 'Rejoice, O servants of Allah! Allah has forgiven your sins and accepted your repentance. So see how you will be when you start anew.'

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal narrated to us from his father from Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Rida from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Surely, the month of Ramadan is a great month. In it, Allah multiplies good deeds, erases sins, and uplifts ranks. Whoever gives charity in this month, Allah will forgive him. Whoever is good to his slave in it, Allah will forgive him. Whoever beautifies his character in it, Allah will forgive him. Whoever withholds his anger in it, Allah will forgive him. Whoever maintains family ties in it, Allah will forgive him. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Surely, this month of yours is not like the other months. When it comes to you, it comes with blessing and mercy; and when it leaves you, it leaves with the forgiveness of sins. This is the month of good deeds multiplied in it, and good actions in it are accepted. Whoever among you prays two voluntary units for Allah the Mighty and Majestic in this month, Allah will forgive him. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Surely, the truly wretched one is he who leaves this month without his sins being forgiven. Then he will lose, while the righteous win the rewards of the Generous Lord.

3 - Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-'Abbas b. Ma'ruf narrated to us from Muhammad b. Sinan from Talha b. Zayd from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Whoever says the takbir to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, one hundred times in the evening, it is as though he freed one hundred persons.

4 - My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: al-Haytham b. Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us from al-Husayn b. 'Ilwan from 'Amr b. Thabit. He said: Muhammad b. Humran narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them). He said: Whoever glorifies Allah thirty times per day, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will repel seventy forms of calamity from him, the smallest of which is poverty.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya b. Wahb from Amr b. Nuhayk from Sallam al-Makki from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) who was called Shayba al-Hudhali. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I am an old man whose age has advanced, and my strength has weakened from the worship I had accustomed myself to, of prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and jihad. So teach me, O Messenger of Allah, words by which Allah will benefit me, and make things easy for me, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Repeat it. So he repeated it three times. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: There is not a tree nor a clod of earth around you except that it has wept out of compassion for you. So when you pray Fajr, say ten times: 'Glory be to Allah the Great and by His praise; and there is no power nor strength except through Allah, the Exalted, the Great.' For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will protect you through that from blindness, insanity, leprosy, poverty, and senility. He said: O Messenger of Allah, this is for this world — what about the Hereafter? He said: You say after every prayer: 'O Allah, guide me from Your presence, shower me with Your grace, spread Your mercy upon me, and bestow Your blessings upon me.' He said: So he grasped them with his hand and departed. Then a man said to Ibn Abbas: How firmly your maternal uncle held on to those! Then the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Indeed, if he fulfills them on the Day of Resurrection — not having deliberately abandoned them — the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever of them he wishes.

6 - Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi 'Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Ziyad from Aban and others from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Whoever completes his fast with a good saying or a good action, Allah will accept his fast. So it was said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the good saying? He said: The testimony that there is no god but Allah; and the good action is giving out [zakat] al-Fitra.

Ali b. Ahmad b. Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Abu Ayyub Sulayman b. Muqbil al-Medini from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them). He said: Whoever sits with one who finds faults in us, or praises one who denies us, or connects with one who cuts us off, or cuts off from one who connects with us, or befriends one who is our enemy, or opposes one who is our friend, has indeed disbelieved in the One who revealed the Seven Oft-Coupled verses and the Great Quran.

8 - Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natana (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr from 'Abdullah b. al-Fadl al-Hashimi from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Blessed is he who lives a long life and beautifies his actions, for his ending will be good since his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is pleased with him. And woe to he who lives a long life and commits evil, for his ending will be evil since his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is discontented with him.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from Ayyub b. Nuh from Muhammad b. Ziyad from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever does good in what remains of his life will not be taken to account for what has passed of his sins. And whoever does evil in what remains of his life will be taken to account for both the first and the last.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, 'Ali is my deputy and my vicegerent, and his wife Fatima, the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, is my daughter, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn, the two Masters of the Youth of Paradise, are my two sons. Whoever aligns with them has aligned with me, and whoever opposes them has opposed me, and whoever defies them has defied me, and whoever is aloof with them is aloof with me, and whoever is good to them is good to me. May Allah connect with whoever connects with them, and cut off whoever cuts them off, and support whoever aids them, and cause failure to whoever fails them. O Allah, each of Your prophets and Your messengers had a heavyweight and a household; so 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn are my household and my heavyweight; so remove all uncleanliness from them, and purify them with a thorough purification.

The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil b. Salih from Muhammad b. Marwan. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) saying: Surely, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has in every night of the month of Ramadan freed ones and released ones from the Fire, except whoever breaks their fast on an intoxicant. And when it is the last night of it, He frees in it the like of what He freed in all of it.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to me from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Fadala from Sayf b. 'Umayra from 'Ubaydullah b. 'Abdullah from one who heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said when the month of Ramadan approached, three days before the end of Sha'ban, he said to Bilal: Call the people. So the people gathered, then he climbed the pulpit, praised Allah and commended Him, then said: O people! Indeed this month has approached you, and it is the Master of Months. In it there is a night that is better than a thousand months. In it the gates of Hell are locked and the gates of Paradise are opened. Whoever comes unto it yet is not forgiven, Allah cuts him off. Whoever has his parents yet is not forgiven, Allah cuts him off. Whoever has me mentioned in his midst yet does not send blessings on me and is not forgiven, Allah cuts him off.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Ali b. al-Aswad al-Ijli narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Hamid b. Yahya Abu Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us from al-Zuhri from Ubaydullah b. Abdullah from Ibn Abbas. He said: When the month of Ramadan would begin, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) would free every captive and give to every beggar.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Uthman b. Isa narrated to me from al-Ala' b. al-Musayyib from Abi Abdillah Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (upon them be peace). He said: Al-Hasan b. Ali (peace be upon them both) said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family): O father! What is the reward of one who visits you? So he said: Whoever visits me, or visits your father, or visits you, or visits your brother, it will be a right upon me to visit him on the Day of Resurrection so that I may redeem him from his sins.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from Muhammad b. Salim from Ahmad b. al-Nadr from Amr b. Shimr from Jabir from Abi Ja'far (upon him be peace). He said: For everything there is a spring, and the spring of the Quran is the month of Ramadan.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Jamil b. Salih from al-Fudayl b. Yasar from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: The memorizer of the Quran who acts by it is with the noble, righteous [angelic] scribes.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from al-Nadr b. Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Muhammad b. Marwan from Sa'd b. Turayf from Abi Ja'far al-Baqir from his father from his grandfather (upon them be peace). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever recites ten verses in a night will not be recorded among the heedless. Whoever recites fifty verses will be recorded among those who remember. Whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among the devoutly obedient. Whoever recites two hundred verses will be recorded among the humble. Whoever recites three hundred verses will be recorded among the winners. Whoever recites five hundred verses will be recorded among the strivers. Whoever recites one thousand verses will be assigned a qintar; and the qintar is fifty thousand gold weights, and each weight is twenty-four carats — the smallest of which is like Mount Uhud, and the largest of which is like what is between heaven and earth.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza al-Bata'ini, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever performs the witr prayer reciting the mu'awwadhatayn and 'Say: He is God, the One,' it is said to him: 'O servant of God, be glad, for God has accepted your witr.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes him travel a path to Paradise. Surely, the angels lay down their wings for the seeker of knowledge, being pleased with him. And indeed, those in the heavens and on the earth seek forgiveness for the seeker of knowledge — even the whale in the sea. The virtue of the scholar over the worshiper is like the virtue of the full moon over the rest of the stars on the night of the full moon. And surely, the scholars are the inheritors of the prophets. Indeed, the prophets did not bequeath a dinar or a dirham, but rather they bequeathed knowledge — so whoever takes from it has taken an abundant share.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Jamurani narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Sitting with the people of religion is the honour of this world and the Hereafter.

Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me in the year 307 AH. He said: My father narrated to me, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: O Ali! You are my brother, my vizier, and the bearer of my standard in this world and the Hereafter. You are the master of my Pond. Whoever loves you has loved me, and whoever hates you has hated me.

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to his companions: Shall I not tell you something, that if you do it, Satan would be as far from you as the East is from the West? They said: Of course. He said: Fasting blackens his face, charity breaks his back, loving for the sake of Allah and supporting one another in righteous deeds cut his tail, and seeking forgiveness cuts his artery. Everything has a purifier, and the purifier of the bodies is fasting.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Musa al-Kamandani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd, from Ubayd ibn Harun. He said: Abu Yazid narrated to us from Husayn, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: In the month of Ramadan, betake to much seeking of forgiveness and supplication. As for supplication, it will repel calamity from you; and as for seeking forgiveness, it will erase your sins.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Musa from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Surely, Allah, blessed and exalted, disliked six characteristics for me, and I disliked them for the deputies from my descendants and their followers after me: trifling in prayer, lewd talk while fasting, bragging after giving charity, coming to the mosques in a state of major impurity (janaba), peering into the houses [of others without permission], and laughing among the graves.

Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Amr al-Shami from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as). He said: "Surely, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah on the day that He created the heavens and the Earth" [9:36]. The best of the months is the month of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is the month of Ramadan. The heart of the month of Ramadan is the Night of Power. The Quran was revealed in the first night of the month of Ramadan, so welcome the month with the Quran.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from al-Qasim b. Muhammad al-Isfahani from Sulayman b. Dawud al-Minqari from Hafs b. Ghiyath. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as): Inform me about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, "The month of Ramadan, in which the Quran was revealed" [2:185] — how was the Quran revealed in the month of Ramadan when the Quran was only revealed over a period of twenty years from beginning to end? So he (as) said: The Quran was revealed altogether at once in the month of Ramadan to the Bayt al-Ma'mur. Then, it was revealed from the Bayt al-Ma'mur over a period of twenty years.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Aziz b. Yahya narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ammara narrated to us from his father from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said: A part of me will be buried in the land of Khurasan. No believer will visit it except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make Paradise mandatory for him and forbid his body from the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal informed us, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said: Indeed, in Khurasan there is a piece of land upon which a time will come when it becomes the frequented place of the angels. A group will continuously descend from heaven while another group ascends, until the Trumpet is blown. He was asked: O son of the Messenger of Allah, which piece of land is this? He said: It is in the land of Tus. By Allah, it is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. Whoever visits me in that piece of land, it will be as though he visited the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will record for him the reward of one thousand virtuous Hajj pilgrimages and one thousand accepted Umra pilgrimages, and I and my forefathers will be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Salt Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi. He said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: By Allah, there is not one among us except that he is killed — a martyr. So it was said to him: Then who will kill you, O son of the Messenger of God? He said: The evilest of God's creation in my era. He will kill me with poison, then he will bury me in an isolated abode and a strange country. Surely, whoever visits me in my isolation, God, Mighty and Majestic, will record for him the reward of one hundred thousand martyrs, one hundred thousand saints, one hundred thousand pilgrims of Hajj and Umra, and one hundred thousand holy warriors. He will be resurrected in our congregation, and he will be made our comrade in the exalted ranks of Paradise.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr al-Bazanti. He said: I read in a letter of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): Announce to my Shia that a visitation of me is considered by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to be equal to one thousand Hajj pilgrimages. He said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): One thousand Hajj? He said: Yes, by Allah, and one million Hajj for one who visits him recognizing his right.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), that a man from the people of Khurasan said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! I saw the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) in a dream, as though he was saying to me: 'How will you be when a part of me is buried in your land, and you are entrusted to guard my trust, and my star is hidden in your soil?' So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to him: I am the one buried in your land, and I am a part of your Prophet, and I am the trust and the star. Indeed, whoever visits me while knowing what God, blessed and exalted, has made obligatory regarding my right and obedience to me, then I and my forefathers will be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever has us as his intercessors will be saved, even if his sins are equal to the burden of the two weighty beings — the Jinn and mankind. And indeed, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from his father (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'Whoever sees me in his dream has truly seen me, because Satan cannot take my form, nor the form of any of my successors, nor the form of any of their followers. And indeed, a true vision is one part out of seventy parts of prophethood.'

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Thabit ibn Kinana narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas Abu Ja'far al-Khuza'i narrated to us. He said: Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Urni narrated to us. He said: Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Yahya, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) climbed the pulpit and gave a sermon, and the people gathered around him. He said: O assembly of the believers! Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed to me that I will die, and my cousin Ali will be killed. O people! I inform you of a matter: if you act by it, you will be safe, and if you abandon it, you will be destroyed. Indeed, my cousin Ali is my brother and my vizier. He is my vicegerent. He is the one who speaks on my behalf. He is the Imam of the pious, the Leader of the radiant and distinguished believers. If you seek his guidance, he will guide you. If you follow him, you will be delivered. If you oppose him, you will go astray. If you obey him, you will have obeyed Allah. If you disobey him, you will have disobeyed Allah. If you pledge allegiance to him, you will have pledged allegiance to Allah. And if you renege on your allegiance to him, then you will have reneged on your allegiance to Allah. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the Quran to me; and he [Ali] is the one who, whoever disobeys him, goes astray. Whoever seeks his knowledge from other than Ali will be destroyed. O people! Hear my words and recognize the truth of my advice. Do not do anything after me regarding my Ahl al-Bayt except that which you have been ordered to do regarding their protection, for they are my kin, my relatives, my brothers, and my children. You will be gathered and questioned about the Two Weighty Things, so look to how you treat them after me. They are my Ahl al-Bayt: whoever harms them has harmed me, whoever oppresses them has oppressed me, whoever belittles them has belittled me, whoever cherishes them has cherished me, whoever honours them has honoured me, whoever supports them has supported me, whoever lets them down has let me down. Whoever seeks guidance in other than them has belied me. O people! Fear Allah and look to what you will say when you meet Him, for I am the adversary of whoever harms them, and whoeve

Al-Shaykh al-Faqih Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Wahb al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Thawaba ibn Mas'ud narrated to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A son of Uthman ibn Maz'un (may Allah be pleased with him) passed away, and his grief intensified to the point where he took a place in his house as a place of worship to devote himself in prayer therein. This reached the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), and he said to him: O Uthman, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has not prescribed monasticism for us. The monasticism of my nation is striving in the way of Allah. O Uthman ibn Maz'un, Paradise has eight gates and the Hellfire has seven gates. Would it not gladden you that you will not approach any gate of them except that you find your son at your side, holding onto your waistband, interceding for you to your Lord? He said: Indeed, yes. So the Muslims said: And for us too, O Messenger of Allah, regarding our departed children, is there what Uthman has? He said: Yes, for whoever among you is patient and seeks reward from Allah. Then he said: O Uthman, whoever prays the Fajr prayer in congregation, then sits remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until the sun rises, shall have seventy ranks in the Highest Paradise, the distance between every two ranks being like the gallop of a swift, lean horse for seventy years. And whoever prays Dhuhr in congregation shall have fifty ranks in the Gardens of Eden, the distance between every two ranks being like the gallop of a swift horse for fifty years. And whoever prays Asr in congregation shall have the reward of freeing eight descendants of Isma'il, each of them being the head of a household. And whoever prays Maghrib in congregation shall have the reward of a virtuous Hajj and an accepted Umra. And whoever prays Isha in congregation shall have the reward of keeping vigil on the Night of Power.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi narrated to us, from his father, he said: Ahmad ibn Hisham narrated to us, he said: Mansur ibn Mujahid narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Badr, from Sawwar ibn Munib, from Wahb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, blessings of God upon him and his family, said: Indeed God, blessed and exalted, has an angel named Sakha'il who takes the writs for those who pray at every prayer from the Lord of the Worlds, exalted is His majesty. When the believers wake at dawn and rise, perform ablution, and pray the Fajr prayer, he brings from God, mighty and majestic, a writ for them, written therein: 'I am God, the Everlasting.
