My servants and handmaids, I have placed you in My protection and in My safeguarding, and under My care I have made you. By My glory, I will not forsake you, and your sins are forgiven until Dhuhr.' When the time of Dhuhr comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the second writ, written therein: 'I am God, the All-Powerful. My servants and handmaids, I have changed your evil deeds into good deeds, and I have forgiven your sins, and I have settled you through My pleasure with you in the abode of Majesty.' When the time of Asr comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the third writ, written therein: 'I am God, the Majestic. Majestic is My remembrance and great is My dominion. My servants and handmaids, I have forbidden your bodies from the Fire, and I have settled you in the dwellings of the righteous, and I have repelled from you by My mercy the evil of the wicked.' When the time of Maghrib comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the fourth writ, written therein: 'I am God, the Compeller, the Grand, the Most High. My servants and handmaids, My angels have ascended from you with satisfaction, and it is due upon Me to please you and give you on the Day of Resurrection your wishes.' When the time of Isha comes and they rise, perform ablution, and pray, he brings for them from God, mighty and majestic, the fifth writ, written therein: 'Indeed I am God. There is no deity other than Me, and

3 - Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi, who said: Al-Ma'mun said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of God, I have recognized your virtue, your knowledge, your asceticism, your piety, and your worship, and I see that you are more rightful to the caliphate than me. So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Through servitude to God, Mighty and Majestic, I take pride; and through asceticism in this world I hope for salvation from the evil of this world; and through piety from the forbidden I hope to win the spoils; and through humility in this world I hope for elevation in the sight of God, Mighty and Majestic. So al-Ma'mun said to him: I have decided to abdicate myself from the caliphate, give it to you, and pledge allegiance to you. So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to him: If the caliphate were yours and God made it for you, then it is not permissible for you to remove a garment that God dressed you with and give it to someone else. And if the caliphate were not yours, then it is not permissible for you to give me what is not yours. So al-Ma'mun said: O son of the Messenger of God, you must accept this affair. So he said: I will never do that willingly. He did not cease striving for days until he despaired. So he said: If you will not accept the caliphate and do not like my pledge to you, then be my crown prince so that the caliphate will be yours after me. So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: By God, my father narrated to me from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful, from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family): I will leave this world before you, killed by poison, oppressed. The angels of the heavens and the earth will weep for me, and I will be buried in a land of exile beside Harun al-Rashid. Al-Ma'mun wept, then asked who would kill him. Al-Rida said he could name his killer if he wished. Al-Ma'mun accused him of using these words to avoid the affair. Al-Rida swore he had never lied, and revealed al-Ma'mun's true motive: to make people say that Ali ibn Musa accepted the crown prince position out of worldly desire, not asceticism. So al-Ma'mun became angry, then said: You always treat me in a way that I hate, and you have felt safe from my authority. I swear by God, you must

The scholar and jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Malik ibn Anas, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The poor came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Messenger of God, the rich have the means to free slaves, and we do not. They have the means to perform the pilgrimage, and we do not. They have the means to give in charity, and we do not. They have the means to wage jihad, and we do not. So he (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever exalts God, Blessed and Exalted, one hundred times, it is better than freeing one hundred slaves. Whoever glorifies God one hundred times, it is better than sacrificing one hundred camels. Whoever praises God one hundred times, it is better than supplying one hundred horses in the way of God with their saddles, bridles, and riders. And whoever says "there is no god but God" one hundred times, he will be the best of people in deeds that day, except he who exceeds him. He said: The rich were told about that and they began practicing it. He said: So the poor returned to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Messenger of God, the rich have been told what you said and they began practicing it. So he (may God bless him and his family) said: That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whomever He wills.

2 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us... from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both). He said: The name of the Messenger of Allah in the Scrolls of Ibrahim is al-Mahi, in the Torah al-Hadd, in the Gospel Ahmad, in the Quran Muhammad. Al-Mahi effaces the images of idols. Al-Hadd opposes Allah's enemies. Ahmad is God's beautiful praise. Muhammad is praised by Allah, His angels, prophets and nations, and his name is on the Throne. He would wear Yemeni and white skullcaps, and padded ones with ear-flaps in wartime. He had a staff, a spear called al-Mamshūq, a tent called al-Kinn, bowls, cups, two horses, two mules (Duldul and al-Shahba'), two she-camels, swords (Dhulfiqar and others), a donkey Ya'fur, a turban al-Sahab, armor Dhat al-Fudul with silver rings, a flag al-'Uqab, a camel al-Dibaj, a banner al-Ma'lum, and a helmet al-As'ad. He handed all of these to Ali (peace be upon him) at his death, took off his ring and placed it on Ali's finger. Ali mentioned finding a parchment in one of his swords with three phrases: 'Maintain ties with those who cut you off, speak the truth even against yourself, and be good to those who wrong you.' He said: And the Messenger of Allah said: There are five things I will not abandon until death: eating on the ground with slaves, riding donkeys without saddles, milking goats by hand, wearing wool, and greeting children so that it may be a tradition after me.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I visited Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) and I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! The people say that you accepted the position of crown prince whilst showing asceticism toward this world! So he (peace be upon him) said: God knows my dislike for that. When I was given the choice between accepting that and being killed, I chose acceptance over being killed. Woe to them! Do they not know that Yusuf (peace be upon him) was a prophet and a messenger, yet when necessity compelled him to take over the treasuries of al-Aziz, he said to him: 'Appoint me over the treasuries of the land, for I am a knowledgeable guardian.' And necessity compelled me to accept that under coercion and compulsion, at the brink of destruction, knowing that I did not enter this affair except as one who intends to leave it. I complain to God, and He is the Helper.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us, from Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal, from his father. He said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Whoever recalls our tragedy and weeps for what was committed against us will be with us in our rank on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever is reminded of our tragedy, weeps, and makes others weep, his eye will not weep on the Day that the eyes will weep. And whoever sits in a gathering in which our affair is revived, his heart will not die on the Day that the hearts will die.

He said: And al-Rida (peace be upon him) said, regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, then for it' -- there is a Lord who forgives it.
He said: And al-Rida (peace be upon him) said, regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'So overlook with gracious forgiveness' [15:85]. He said: Forgiveness without reproach.

He said: And al-Rida (peace be upon him) said, regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is He who shows you the lightning in fear and in hope' [13:12]. He said: Fear for the traveller, and hope for the settler.

He said: And al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Whoever is unable to find a way to expiate his sins, then let him increase in sending blessings upon Muhammad and his family, for indeed it thoroughly destroys sins.

And he (peace be upon him) said: To God, Mighty and Majestic, sending blessings upon Muhammad and his family is equal to glorification (tasbih), pronouncing His oneness (tahlil), and exaltation (takbir).

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ziyad narrated to us. He said: al-Haytham b. Adi narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Yunus b. Abi Ishaq. He said: Abu al-Saqr narrated to us, from Adi b. Arta'a. He said: Mu'awiya said one day to 'Amr b. al-'As: O Aba Abdillah! Which of us is more cunning? 'Amr said: I am [more cunning] in impulsiveness, and you are [more cunning] in deliberation. Mu'awiya said: You have judged in my favor over yourself, for I am more cunning than you in impulsiveness. 'Amr said: Then where was your cunning on the day you raised the codices? He said: With that you have overcome me, O Aba Abdillah. Shall I not ask you about something in which you will be truthful with me? He said: By Allah, lying is repugnant, so ask about whatever you wish and I shall be truthful with you. He said: Did you cheat me after you counseled me? He said: No. He said: Rather, by Allah, you did cheat me. I am not saying in every instance, but in one particular instance. He said: And what instance is this? He said: The day Ali b. Abi Talib challenged me to a duel and I consulted you. I said: What do you think, O Aba Abdillah? You said: A worthy and noble opponent. So you advised me to duel him while you knew who he was, and I knew then that you had cheated me. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, a man challenged you to duel him who was of great honor and immense standing. In dueling him you would have achieved one of two good outcomes: either you would kill him, which would have been the slaying of equals, and you would increase in honor upon your honor and have your kingdom to yourself; or you would hasten to the company of the martyrs and the righteous — and what excellent company they are. Mu'awiya said: This is worse than the first. By Allah, I surely know that had I killed him I would have entered the Fire, and had he killed me I would have entered the Fire. 'Amr said to him: Then what drove you to fight him?! He said: Rulership has no blood bonds, and no one will hear this from me after you.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever takes on my religion, travels my path, and follows my tradition, then let him profess the superiority of the Imams from my Ahl al-Bayt over all of my nation, for indeed their likeness in this nation is like that of the Gate of Remission among the Children of Israel.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali b. al-Salt narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah b. al-Salt from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman from Amr b. Shimr from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Messenger (may God's blessings be upon him and his family): I have thanked Ja'far b. Abi Talib for four characteristics. So the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) called for him and informed him. He said: Had Allah not informed you, I would not have informed you. I have never drunk wine, because I knew that if I were to drink it, my intellect would depart. And I have never lied, because lying diminishes chivalry. And I have never committed adultery, because I feared that if I did it, it would be done to me. And I have never worshipped an idol, because I knew that it neither harms nor benefits. He said: Then the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) placed his hand on his shoulder and said: It is Allah's right, the Mighty and Majestic, to give you two wings with which you may fly with the angels in Paradise.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Fadl b. al-Abbas al-Baghdadi, a shaykh for the people of hadith, narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Ibrahim informed us. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ghalib b. Harb al-Dabbi al-Tamtami and Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Uthman b. Abi Shayba narrated to us. They said: Yahya b. Salim, the cousin of al-Hasan b. Salih — and the former was preferred over al-Hasan b. Salih — narrated to us. He said: Mis'ar narrated to us, from Atiyya, from Jabir. He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: On the gate of Paradise, it is written: 'There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, Ali is the brother of the Messenger of God,' two thousand years before God created the heavens and the earth.

Ali ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: I recited to Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Harith. I said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalaf al-Attar narrated to you. He said: Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us. He said: Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam narrated to us from his father from Said ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said: I asked the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) about the words that Adam received from his Lord by which He forgave him. He said: He asked Him by the right of Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, "forgive me," so He forgave him.

Yaqub ibn Yusuf ibn Yaqub, the jurist and shaykh of the people of al-Rayy, narrated to us. He said: Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn Utba al-Kindi narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sharik narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from al-A'mash from Ata. He said: I asked Aisha about Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and she said: That is the best of people; no one doubts regarding him except a disbeliever.

Yaqub ibn Yusuf ibn Yaqub narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahman al-Khayti informed us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Awdi narrated to us. He said: Hasan ibn Husayn al-Urni narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us from Sharik from Mansur from Rib'i from Hudhayfa. He was asked about Ali (peace be upon him), so he said: That is the best of people; no one doubts regarding him except a hypocrite.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sayrafi narrated to us, and he was from the people of hadith. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Bassam, the freed-slave of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Khayr narrated to us. He said: And Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Yunus and Abu al-Khayr narrated to us. They both said: Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us. He said: Abu Bukayr al-Nakha'i narrated to us from Sharik from Abu Ishaq from Abu Wa'il from Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib is the best of people; whoever disagrees has disbelieved.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Fudayl ibn Uthman from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki. He said: I saw Jabir leaning on his staff, going around the pathways and gatherings of the Ansar, saying: Ali is the best of people; whoever disagrees has disbelieved. O Ansar! Raise your children upon the love of Ali; if one refuses, then look into the affair of his mother.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Razi narrated to me. He said: My father Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Abbas ibn Harun al-Tamimi narrated to me. He said: My master Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (as) narrated to me. He said: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me. He said: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me. He said: My father Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me. He said: My father Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me. He said: My father al-Husayn ibn Ali narrated to me. He said: My brother al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me. He said: My father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) narrated to me. He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: You are the best of people, and no one will have doubt regarding you except a disbeliever.

Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Yahya b. al-Hasan b. Jafar b. Ubaydullah b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather Yahya b. al-Hasan b. Jafar b. Ubaydullah narrated to me. He said: Ibrahim b. Ali and al-Hasan b. Yahya narrated to me. They both said: Nasr b. Muzahim narrated to us from Abu Khalid from Zayd b. Ali from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: I was given ten characteristics by the Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah be upon him and his family). He did not give them to anyone before me, nor will anyone be given them after me. He said to me: O Ali! You are my brother in this world and in the Hereafter. You are the nearest of the people to me in position on the Day of Resurrection. My house and your house in Paradise face one another, like the house of two brothers. You are the deputy, you are the friend [of Allah], and you are the vizier. Your enemy is my enemy, and my enemy is the enemy of Allah. Your friend is my friend, and my friend is the friend of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Abdullah b. al-Nadr b. Sim'an al-Tamimi al-Kharqani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Jafar b. Muhammad al-Makki narrated to us. He said: Abu Muhammad Abdullah b. Ishaq al-Mada'ini informed us from Muhammad b. Ziyad from al-Mughira from Sufyan from Hisham b. Urwa from his father Urwa b. al-Zubayr. He said: We were sitting in a gathering in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (blessings be upon him and his family), discussing the deeds of the people of Badr and the Pledge of Ridwan. Abu al-Darda said: O people! Shall I not inform you of the one who has the least wealth, the most piety, and strives hardest in worship? They said: Who? He said: Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: By Allah, everyone in the gathering turned their faces away from him. Then a man from the Ansar stepped forward and said: O Uwaymir! You have said something that no one agreed with. Abu al-Darda said: O people! I am saying what I have seen, and let every people among you say what they saw. I witnessed Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) at the paths of Banu al-Najjar, when he had secluded himself from his followers, disappeared from those near him, and concealed himself among the palm trees. I lost track of him and he went far from me. I said: He went to his house. Then I heard a sorrowful voice and a plaintive tone, and he was saying: My God! How many perils have You alleviated from me and repelled by Your blessing? How many offenses have You been generous enough not to expose by Your kindness? My God! If I persist in disobeying You over the course of my life, and my sins become great in the records, then I have no hope except in Your forgiveness, nor do I hope for anything except Your pleasure. The voice preoccupied me, so I followed the trace, and it was Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) himself. I concealed myself and quieted my movement. He bowed in the dead of night, then broke into supplication, weeping, pouring out and lamenting. Among what he whispered to Allah, he said: My God! I think about Your forgiveness, and my errors become trivial. Then I remember the greatness of Your punishment, and my distress weighs upon me. Then he said: Alas, if I read in my record a sin that I have forgotten while You have tallied it, and it is said 'seize him!' -- then alas for such a seized one, whose kinsmen will not save him nor his tribe help him, yet the

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-'Abbas b. Ma'ruf, from Ali b. Mahziyar, from al-Husayn b. Sa'id, from Ali b. al-Nu'man, from Dawud b. Farqad. He said: I heard my father asking Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): When does the time of Maghrib begin? He said: When its seat disappears. He said: And what is its seat? He said: Its disk. He said: When does its disk disappear? He said: When you look and do not see it.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa and Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Baghdadi narrated to us, from Abu Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt al-Qummi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, who said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: When the sun sets, then the time of Maghrib has entered.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham or someone else. He said: I once climbed the mountain of Abu Qubays while the people were praying Maghrib, and I saw that the sun had not yet set but had merely hidden behind the mountain from the people. So I met Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and informed him of that. He said to me: And why did you do that? Woe to what you did! You should only pray it when you do not see it behind a mountain, whether it has fully set or gone down, so long as it is not covered by a cloud or a darkness that shades it. For indeed, your concern is only your own sunrise and sunset, and the people do not have to go searching.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. They said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Musa ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ja'far ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Maghrib prayer: Sometimes we pray while we fear that the sun may still be behind the mountain, or that the mountain has concealed it from us. So he said: You are not required to climb the mountain.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to pray the Maghrib prayer, and a clan of the Ansar called Banu Salama would pray with him. Their homes were at a distance of half a mile. They would pray with him, then return to their homes while they could still see where their arrows would land.

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: I heard him say: A man accompanied me who would delay Maghrib prayer and pray Fajr early in the darkness. I, however, would pray Maghrib when the sun set, and pray Fajr when dawn became clear to me. The man said to me: What prevents you from doing as I do? For indeed the sun rises upon a people before us, and it sets from us while it is still risen upon others beyond. He said: So I said: It is only incumbent upon us to pray when the sun has set from us and when dawn rises for us. There is nothing incumbent upon us except that, and it is incumbent upon those people to pray when it sets from them.

My father, Muhammad b. al-Hasan, and Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar — may God be pleased with them — narrated to us. They said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Musa b. Bashshar al-Attar, from al-Mas'udi, from Abdullah b. al-Zubayr, from Aban b. Taghlub, al-Rabi' b. Sulayman, Aban b. Arqam, and others. They said: We set out from Mecca until, when we were in the valley of al-Ajfar, we came upon a man who was praying while we could still see the rays of the sun. We felt displeasure within ourselves. He continued praying while we were supplicating against him, until he had prayed one unit of prayer while we were supplicating against him and saying: This one is from the youth of the people of Medina. But when we approached him, it turned out to be Abu Abdullah Ja'far b. Muhammad — peace be upon them both. So we dismounted and prayed with him. We had missed one unit. When we completed the prayer, we stood and went to him, saying: May we be made your sacrifice! You pray at this hour? He said: Once the sun sets, the time has entered.

The Shaykh, critical Imam, core of the religion, beauty of the Imams, rarity of the age, Abu al-Qasim Ahmad b. Hamza al-Nu'aymi (may Allah lengthen his life) informed us. The Shaykh, Imam, scholar, ascetic, supporter of the religion, pillar of Islam, Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Muhammad b. Abi al-Hasan b. Abd al-Samad al-Tamimi (may Allah be pleased with him) informed us. The Shaykh, jurist, scholar, ornament of the religion, my father, informed us. The Shaykh, jurist, scholar, father Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Abd al-Samad b. Muhammad al-Tamimi informed us. The majestic master, the scholar, Abu al-Barakat Ali b. al-Husayn al-Alawi al-Juri (may Allah illuminate his grave) and the Shaykh Abu Bakr Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us. They both said: The Shaykh, jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us on Friday, twelve nights remaining in Rajab, year 367. He said: The Shaykh Yahya b. Zayd b. al-Abbas b. al-Walid al-Bazzaz narrated to us in Kufa. He said: My uncle Ali b. al-Abbas narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Bishr b. Khalid al-Abdi narrated to us. He said: Amr b. Khalid narrated to us. He said: Abu Hamza al-Thumali narrated to us from Ali b. al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said: A good saying increases one's wealth, boosts one's sustenance, prolongs one's lifespan, makes one beloved to one's family, and enters one into Paradise.

Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Isma'il al-Sakuni narrated to us in his house in Kufa. He said: Ibrahim b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Nisapuri narrated to me. He said: Abu Ja'far b. al-Siri and Abu Nasr b. Musa b. Ayyub al-Khallal narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Sa'id narrated to us. He said: Damra b. Shawdhab narrated to us from Matar from Shahr b. Hawshab from Abu Hurayra. He said: Whoever fasts on the eighteenth of Dhul Hijja, Allah records for him the fasting of sixty months; and it is the day of Ghadir Khumm, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the hand of Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and said: "O people! Am I not more of a master over the believers?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "For whomever I am a master, Ali is his master." Then Umar said to him: "Bravo, bravo, O son of Abi Talib! You have become my master and the master of every Muslim." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "This day I have perfected your religion for you" [5:3].

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan b. Muhammad al-Sakuni narrated to us. He said: al-Hadrami narrated to us. He said: Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us. He said: Abu Awana narrated to us from Abu Balj from Amr b. Maymun from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'Ali is the master (wali) of every believer after me.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Durayd narrated to us, he said: Abu Hatim informed us from al-'Utbi - meaning Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydallah - from his father, he said: And 'Abdullah ibn Shabib al-Basri informed us, he said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Munqari narrated to us, he said: Al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: Qays ibn 'Asim said: I set out with a group from Bani Tamim to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So I entered, and al-Salsal ibn al-Dalhamas was with him. I said: 'O Prophet of God, admonish us with an admonition by which we may benefit, for we are a people who dwell in the wilderness.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Qays! Indeed with glory there is humiliation, and with life there is death, and with this world there is a Hereafter. For everything there is a reckoner, and over everything there is an observer. For every good deed there is a reward, and for every sin there is a punishment, and for every term there is a decree. And it is inevitable for you, O Qays, that you will have a companion who will be buried with you while it is alive, and you will be buried with it while you are dead. If it is noble, it will honor you; and if it is base, it will forsake you. Then it will not be gathered except with you, nor will you be resurrected except with it, nor will you be asked about anything except it. So make it nothing but righteous, for if it is righteous you will find comfort in it, and if it is corrupt you will find nothing but dread from it. And it is your deeds.' He said: 'O Prophet of God, I would love for these words to be in verses of poetry, so we may take pride in them before those Arabs around us, and preserve them.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ordered someone to bring Hassan. He said: I began reflecting on poetry that resembled this admonition, and the words came to me before Hassan arrived. I said: 'O Messenger of God, some verses have come to me which I think match what you want.' So I said to Qays: 'Choose a companion from your deeds, for indeed the companion of the youth in the grave is what he used to do. And after death you must surely prepare it for a day when the person is called and comes forward. If you are occupied with something, then do not

Ahmad b. Yahya al-Mukattib narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Sa'id al-Dimashqi narrated to us. He said: Al-Zubayr b. Bakkar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Dahhak narrated to us from Nawfal b. 'Amira. He said: Qusay b. Kilab advised his sons and then said: "O my sons! Beware of drinking wine, for even if it rectifies the bodies, it corrupts the minds."

Ali b. al-Husayn b. Shaqir b. Ya'qub b. al-Harith b. Ibrahim al-Hamadani narrated to us in his house in Kufa. He said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far b. Ahmad b. Yusuf al-Azdi narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Bazraj al-Hannat narrated to us. He said: Amr b. al-Yasa' narrated to us from Shu'ayb al-Haddad. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon him, saying: "Surely, our narrations are difficult and distressing. None can handle them except an angel brought near, a commissioned prophet, a believer whose heart has been tested by Allah for faith, or a fortified city." Amr said: So I said to Shu'ayb: "O Abu'l Hasan! What is the fortified city?" He said: I asked al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, about it, and he said to me: "The well-constituted heart."

Abu'l Husayn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani informed us, he said: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anbari narrated to us, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Asma' narrated to us, he said: Juwayriyya narrated to us from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: I found in some of the books of God, Mighty and Majestic: that Yusuf (peace be upon him) passed in his procession by the wife of al-'Aziz, and she was sitting on a garbage heap. She said: 'Praise be to God who made kings into slaves through their disobedience, and made slaves into kings through their obedience. Poverty has afflicted us, so give us charity.' Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: 'Neglecting blessings is the ailment that ends their continuance. So return to what purifies you from the filth of sin, for indeed the place of divine acceptance is the sanctity of hearts and the purity of deeds.' She said: 'I have not yet clothed myself in the garment of penitence, and I am ashamed that God should see me in a position of supplication while the eye has not yet shed its tears and the body has not fulfilled its regret.' Yusuf said to her: 'Then strive! For the path is the goal of possibility, before provisions run short and the allotted time expires.' She said: 'That is my belief, and you will hear of it if I outlive you.' So he ordered that a quintar of gold be given to her. She said: 'Sustenance alone suffices—I would not return to luxury while I am captive in divine wrath.' One of Yusuf's sons said to Yusuf: 'O my father, who is this woman for whom my liver is shattered and my heart has become tender?' He said: 'This is a creature of sorrow in the ropes of retribution.' Then Yusuf (peace be upon him) married her, and found her to be a virgin. He said: 'How is this when you had a husband?!' She said: 'He was afflicted by the loss of movement and the coldness of the passages.'

The Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us [...] from Abu Abdullah [Imam al-Sadiq] (as). He said: The neighbors of Umm Ayman came to the Messenger of God (s) and said: O Messenger of God, Umm Ayman did not sleep last night from weeping; she did not cease weeping until morning. He said: The Messenger of God (s) sent for Umm Ayman and she came. He said to her: O Umm Ayman, may God not cause your eyes to weep. Your neighbors came to me and informed me that you did not cease weeping all night. May God not cause your eyes to weep. What made you weep? She said: O Messenger of God, I saw a great and terrible dream, so I did not cease weeping all night. The Messenger of God (s) said to her: Describe it to the Messenger of God, for God and His Messenger know best. She said: It overwhelms me to speak of it. He said to her: The dream is not as you think, so describe it to the Messenger of God. She said: I saw this night as though some of your limbs were lying in my house. The Messenger of God (s) said to her: May your eyes sleep, O Umm Ayman. Fatima will give birth to al-Husayn, and you will raise him and care for him, and he will be part of my limbs in your house. When Fatima gave birth to al-Husayn (as), on the seventh day, the Messenger of God (s) ordered that his head be shaved, and charity be given equal to the weight of his hair in silver, and the aqiqa be performed for him. Then Umm Ayman prepared him and wrapped him in the cloak of the Messenger of God (s). Then she brought him to the Messenger of God (s), and he (s) said: Welcome to the carrier and the one being carried. O Umm Ayman, this is the interpretation of your dream.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Raja' al-Jahdari, from Ali ibn Jabir. He said: Uthman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Humran ibn A'yan, from Abu Muhammad, the shaykh of the people of Kufa. He said: When al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them) was killed, two young boys were captured from his camp. They were brought to Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, who called a warden and said: Take these two boys. Do not feed them good food, do not give them cold water, and make their prison cells narrow. The two boys would fast during the day, and when night came, they were given two barley loaves and a jug of pure water. When the boys' stay lengthened until a year had passed, one said to the other: O my brother, our stay has been long, and our lives may end and our bodies may waste away. When the elder comes, tell him of our situation and seek his closeness through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), so he may increase our food and drink. When night fell, the elder came with two barley loaves and a jug of pure water. The younger boy said to him: O elder, do you know Muhammad? He said: How would I not know Muhammad when he is my Prophet! He said: Do you know Ja'far ibn Abi Talib? He said: How would I not know Ja'far when Allah gave him two wings to fly with the angels wherever he wishes! He said: Do you know Ali ibn Abi Talib? He said: How would I not know Ali when he is the cousin and brother of my Prophet! He said to him: O elder, we are from the progeny of your Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and we are from the children of Muslim ibn Aqil ibn Abi Talib. We are captives in your hands. We ask you for good food but you do not feed us, for cold drink but you do not give it to us, and you have made our prison narrow. The elder fell upon their feet, kissing them and saying: May my soul be the ransom for your souls, and my face the shield for your faces! O progeny of the chosen Prophet of Allah! This prison gate before you is open, so take whichever path you wish. When night fell, he brought them two barley loaves and a jug of pure water, set them on the road, and said: Travel by night, my beloveds, and hide by day until Allah grants you relief and a way out. The two boys did that. When night fell, they came upon a

The Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (rh) narrated to us [...] from Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari. He said: I have heard the Messenger of God (s) describe the characteristics of Ali -- if only one were among all people, they would suffice as virtue: 'Whoever I am his master, Ali is his master.' 'Ali to me is as Harun was to Musa.' 'Ali is from me and I from him.' 'Ali is like myself; obedience to him is obedience to me.' 'The war of Ali is the war of God.' 'The friend of Ali is the friend of God.' 'Ali is the Proof of God and His vicegerent over His servants.'

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far Ahmad b. Ishaq b. Buhlul al-Qadi narrated to us in his house in the City of Peace (Baghdad). He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Yazid al-Sada'i narrated to us from Abu Shayba al-Jawhari from Anas b. Malik. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Promise me six things, and I will guarantee you Paradise: When you speak, do not lie. When you make a promise, do not break it. When you are entrusted, do not betray. Lower your gazes, guard your private parts, and withhold your hands and your tongues."

3 - Ahmad b. Ziyad (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: al-Qasim b. Muhammad al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Salt al-Harawi narrated to us. He said: When al-Ma'mun gathered the rhetoricians of Islam and other religions for Ali b. Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), including from among the Jews, Christians, Zoroastrians, Sabeans, and all the people of various doctrines, no one stood except that he had established his proof against him as though pelting a stone. Ali b. Muhammad b. al-Jahm went to him and said: O son of the Messenger of Allah! Do you claim the infallibility of the prophets? He said: Of course. He said: So what do you make of the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And Adam disobeyed his Lord and strayed' [20:121], and His saying: 'And the man of the whale, when he went off angrily, thinking that We could not restrict him' [21:87], and His saying regarding Yusuf: 'She desired him, and he [would have] desired her' [12:24], and His saying regarding Dawud: 'Then Dawud realized that We had tried him' [38:24], and His saying to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family): 'You hid in yourself that which Allah is to disclose. You fear the people when Allah has more of a right to be feared' [33:37]. So our master al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Woe to you, O Ali! Fear Allah, do not attribute immorality to the prophets of Allah, and do not interpret the Book of Allah by your own opinion, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'No one knows its interpretation except Allah and those deeply rooted in knowledge' [3:7]. As for His saying regarding Adam (peace be upon him): 'And Adam disobeyed his Lord and strayed' [20:121] -- Allah created Adam to be a Proof on His Earth and a vicegerent in His land. He did not create him for Paradise. Adam's disobedience was in Paradise, not on Earth, where he would fulfill the order of Allah. When he was sent down to the Earth and made a Proof and a vicegerent, he became immaculate, as He says: 'Surely, Allah chose Adam, Nuh, the Family of Ibrahim, and the Family of Imran over the worlds' [3:33]. As for His saying: 'And the man of the whale, when he went off angrily, thinking that We could not restrict him' [21:87] -- he thought that Allah would not restrict his sustenance. Did you not hear the saying of Allah: 'But when

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father al-Baqir Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Zayn al-Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father the Master of Deputies Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: Verily the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon to us one day and said: O people! The month of Allah has come to you with blessing, mercy, and forgiveness. It is a month that is considered by Allah to be the best of months. Its days are the best of days, its nights are the best of nights, and its hours are the best of hours. It is a month in which you were invited to be the guests of Allah, and you were made among the people of Allah's honour. In it, your breath is glorification, your sleep is worship, your deeds are accepted, and your supplications are answered. So ask Allah, your Lord, with sincere intentions and pure hearts, that He grant you success in fasting and reciting His Book. For indeed, the wretched is he who is deprived of Allah's forgiveness in this great month. Remember in your hunger and your thirst in it the hunger and thirst of the Day of Resurrection. Give charity to your poor and needy, respect your elders, be merciful to your young, maintain ties of kinship, guard your tongues, lower your gaze from that which is forbidden to look at, withhold your ears from that which is forbidden to hear, show mercy to the orphans of the people so that mercy may be shown to your orphans, and repent to Allah from your sins. Raise your hands to Him in supplication at the times of your prayers, for that is the best time — Allah Almighty looks upon His servants with mercy therein, He answers them when they whisper to Him, He fulfils them when they call out to Him, He grants to them when they ask Him, and He responds to them when they supplicate to Him. O people! Your souls are mortgaged by your deeds, so free them through your seeking forgiveness. Your backs are heavy from your burdens, so lighten them through the length of your prostrations

1 - Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Baghdadi al-Hafiz narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Thawab narrated to us. He said: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Kadih -- meaning Abu Ja'far al-Bajali --, from Abdullah ibn Lahi'a, from Abd al-Rahman -- meaning Ibn Ziyad --, from Salama ibn Yasar, from Jabir ibn Abdullah. He said: When Ali (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) with the conquest of Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to him: Were it not that sects of my nation would say about you what the Christians said about the Messiah Jesus son of Mary, I would have said about you today a statement such that you would not pass by any gathering except that they would take the dust from beneath your feet and seek healing from the remainder of your ablution water. But it suffices you that you are from me and I am from you; you inherit from me and I inherit from you. You are to me in the position of Harun to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me. You will fulfill my covenant and fight upon my sunnah. Tomorrow you will be my vicegerent at the Pond. You will be the first to come to me at the Pond, and the first to be clothed with me, and the first from my nation to enter Paradise. Your followers will be upon pulpits of light, with illuminated faces around me; I will intercede for them, and tomorrow they will be my neighbours in Paradise. Your war is my war, and your peace is my peace. Your secret is my secret, and your public affairs are my public affairs. The innermost thoughts of your heart are like mine. Your descendants are my descendants. You will fulfill my promises. The truth is with you, and the truth is upon your tongue, in your heart, and between your eyes. Faith is mixed into your flesh and blood just as it has mixed into my flesh and blood. No one who hates you will ever come to me at the Pond, and no one who loves you will be absent from it until they come to the Pond with you. He said: So Ali (peace be upon him) fell in prostration, then said: Praise be to Allah who blessed me with Islam, taught me the Quran, and made me beloved to the best of creation, the Seal of the Prophets and the Master o

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas b. al-Fadl al-Muqri' narrated to us. He said: Abu'l Hasan Ali b. al-Furat al-Isfahani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Jundal b. Waliq narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Hammad narrated to us from Sa'id from Ibn Abbas. He passed by a gathering of Quraysh that was insulting Ali b. Abi Talib (as), so he said to his guide: What are these people saying? He said: They are insulting Ali. He said: Bring me closer to them. When he reached them, he said: Which of you insulted Allah? They said: Glory be to Allah! Whoever insults Allah has associated partners with Him. He said: Then which of you insulted the Messenger of Allah (s)? They said: Whoever insults the Messenger of Allah has disbelieved. He said: Then which of you insulted Ali b. Abi Talib? They said: That indeed happened. He said: I testify by Allah and I testify for Allah that I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: Whoever insults Ali has insulted me, and whoever insults me has insulted Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then he went on. He said to his guide: Did they say anything when I said what I said to them? He said: They did not say anything. He said: How did you see their faces? He said: They looked at you with reddened eyes, as a goat looks to the knife of a butcher. He said: Tell me more, may your father be your ransom. He said: Squinting eyes and furrowed brows, lowered chins in humiliation — the look of a servile man to a glorious and dominant man. He said: Tell me more, may your father be your ransom. He said: I have nothing more. He said: But I have: Their living ones are a disgrace to their dead, and their dead are a shame for the ancients.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Basir, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: I heard him say: Whoever prays four units of prayer reciting Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad two hundred times -- fifty times in each unit -- he will not finish the prayer while there remains any sin between him and God, Mighty and Majestic, except that it will be forgiven for him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Shahham, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: No servant says seven times every day, 'I ask God for Paradise, and I seek refuge in God from the Fire,' except that the Fire says: 'O my Lord! Give him refuge from me.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Mu'adh ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: Be patient with the enemies of blessings, for you will never deal with the one who has disobeyed God regarding you with anything better than obeying God regarding him.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi'l Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far al-Azdi, from Amr ibn Abi'l Miqdam. He said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi once, God repels from him one thousand hateful things of this world and one thousand hateful things of the Hereafter. The least of the hateful things of this world is poverty, and the least of the hateful things of the Hereafter is the punishment of the grave.

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhuwayh al-Mu'addab (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mudrik ibn al-Hazhaz. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: O Mudrik! May Allah have mercy on a servant who draws the love of the people toward us, narrating to them what they would recognize, and leaving what they would deny.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: One day, Dawud (peace be upon him) went out to recite the Psalms. Whenever he recited the Psalms, there would not remain a mountain, a stone, a bird, nor a beast except that it would respond to him. He kept walking until he reached a mountain, and upon that mountain was a cloistered prophet called Hizqil. When he heard the echo of the mountains and the voices of the beasts and the birds, he knew that it was Dawud (peace be upon him). So Dawud said: O Hizqil! Do you permit me to climb up to you? He said: No. So Dawud (peace be upon him) wept. Then Allah, exalted is His majesty, revealed to him: O Hizqil! Do not humiliate Dawud, and ask Me for well-being. So Hizqil stood, took the hand of Dawud, and raised him up to him. Then Dawud said: O Hizqil! Have you ever been tempted to sin? He said: No. He said: Have you ever felt conceit from your state of worshiping Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? He said: No. He said: Have you inclined toward the world and desired to take from its lusts and pleasures? He said: Yes indeed, perhaps it has occurred in my heart. He said: What do you do when that happens? He said: I enter this ravine and reflect upon what is in it. He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) entered that ravine, and there was an iron bed with a decomposed skull and withered bones upon it. And there was an iron tablet with writing upon it. Dawud (peace be upon him) read it and it said: I am Arwa Shalam. I ruled for a thousand years, I built a thousand cities, and I deflowered a thousand virgins. Yet in the end, dust became my bed, stones became my pillow, worms and snakes became my neighbours. So whoever sees me, let him not be deceived by the world.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to us from Aban ibn Uthman and others from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Whoever completes his fasting with a good saying or a good action, God accepts his fasting from him. So it was said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! What is the good saying? He said: The testimony that there is no god but God; and the good action is giving out the fitra (alms).

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani informed me, saying: al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) gave a sermon to the people on the Day of Fitr, saying: O people! Indeed this day of yours is a day in which the righteous are rewarded and the wrongdoers suffer loss. It is the day most resembling the Day of your Resurrection. So remember, through your going out from your homes to your place of prayer, your coming out from your graves to your Lord. And remember, through your standing in your place of prayer, your standing before your Lord. And remember, through your return to your homes, your return to your abodes in Paradise or the Fire. And know, O servants of God, that the least reward for fasting men and women is that an angel calls to them on the last day of the month of Ramadan: 'Rejoice, O servants of God, for your past sins have been forgiven. So look to how you will conduct yourselves henceforth.'

Al-Sadiq Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said to some of his companions: When the eve of al-Fitr comes, pray the three units of Maghrib, then prostrate and say in your prostration: "O Possessor of everlasting bounty, O Possessor of power, O Selector of Muhammad and his supporter, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and forgive me every sin that I have committed and forgotten, while it is with You in a manifest book." Then say one hundred times: "I repent to God." And do takbir after Maghrib, the final Isha, the morning prayer, and the Eid prayer, just as you do takbir in the days of Tashriq, saying: "God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, and to God belongs all praise, God is the Greatest for what He has guided us to, and praise be to God for what He has made us face." But do not say in it: "and provide us from the cattle of livestock," for that is only for the days of Tashriq.

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba from Hamdan ibn Sulayman from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' from Salih ibn 'Uqba from 'Alqama ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: God, exalted is His majesty, said: God, exalted is His majesty, said: My servants! All of you are misguided except those I have guided. All of you are poor except those I have enriched. All of you are sinners except those I have protected.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba narrated to us, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqba, from 'Alqama, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) and claimed seventy dirhams from him as the price of a she-camel. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said to him: "O Bedouin, have you not already received that from me in full?" He said: "No." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said to him: "Then choose someone to judge between us." So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) went with him, and they sought judgment from a man of Quraysh. The man said to the Bedouin: "What do you claim against the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him." He said: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I have already paid him in full." The Qurayshi man said to the Bedouin: "What do you say to what the Messenger of Allah says?" He said: "I have not received it." So the Qurayshi man ruled in favor of the Bedouin against the Prophet. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) rose up in anger, dragging his cloak, and said: "By Allah, I shall go to one who judges between us by the judgment of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty." So he went with him to seek judgment from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said to the Bedouin: "What do you claim?" He said: "I claim seventy dirhams from him as the price of a she-camel I sold to him." He said: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I have already paid him in full." He said to the Bedouin: "What do you say to what the Messenger of Allah says?" He said: "I have not received it." Ali (peace be upon him) said: "O Bedouin, by Allah, I know that the Messenger of Allah has already paid you, but I shall ask you: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'I am the master of the children of Adam and I do not boast'?" He said: "Yes." Then Ali struck him with his sword and killed him. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: "O Ali, why did you kill the Bedouin?" He said: "Because he called you a liar, O Messenger of Allah, and whoeve

163/3 - My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba narrated to us from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih, from Alqama, who said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said — and I had said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me of whose testimony is to be accepted and whose testimony is not to be accepted. So he said: O Alqama, whoever is upon the natural disposition (fitra) of Islam, his testimony is accepted. He said: So I said to him: Is the testimony of one who commits sins accepted? So he said: O Alqama, if the testimony of those who commit sins were not accepted, then only the testimonies of the prophets and the successors (blessings of Allah be upon them) would be accepted, because they are the infallible ones, unlike the rest of creation. So whoever you do not see with your own eyes committing a sin, or two witnesses have not testified against him regarding that, then he is from the people of justice and concealment, and his testimony is accepted, even if he is sinful within himself. And whoever backbites him with what is actually in him, he has exited the guardianship of Allah the Mighty and Majestic and entered the guardianship of Satan. And indeed my father narrated to me, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever backbites a believer with what is actually in him, Allah will never unite them in Paradise; and whoever backbites a believer with what is not in him, then the bond between them has been severed, and the backbiter will dwell in the Fire forever therein — and wretched is the destination. Alqama said: So I said to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of Allah, indeed the people attribute to us the grandest of matters, and our chests have been constricted by that. So he (peace be upon him) said: O Alqama, indeed the contentment of the people cannot be possessed, and their tongues cannot be controlled. So how would you be safe from what even the prophets of Allah, His messengers, and His proofs (peace be upon them) were not safe from? Did they not accuse Yusuf (peace be upon him) of desiring adultery? Did they not accuse Ayyub (peace be upon him) of being afflicted due to his sins? Did they not accuse Dawud

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Mu'aqqal al-Qarmisini narrated to us. He said: Ja'far al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Ashaj narrated to us from Yahya b. Zayd b. 'Ali from his father from 'Ali b. al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said: One day, the Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) went out and prayed the Fajr prayer. Then, he said: O people! Which of you will rise against three persons who have sworn by al-Lat and al-'Uzza to kill me? For, by the Lord of the Ka'ba, they have lied. The people refrained, and no one spoke. So, he said: I do not see 'Ali b. Abi Talib among you. So, 'Amer b. Qutada stood up and said: Indeed, he had a fever this night and did not come out to pray with you. Do you permit me to inform him? So, the Prophet said: As you wish. So, he went to him and informed him. So, Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali came out as if released from a hobble, with a garment whose two ends he had tied around his neck. So, he said: O Messenger of God, what is this news? He said: This is a messenger of my Lord informing me about three persons who have risen against me to kill me, but they have lied, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. So, 'Ali said: O Messenger of God, I will be a military expedition for them alone. Let me just put on my clothes. So, the Messenger of Allah said: Rather, these are my clothes, and this is my shield, and this is my sword. So, he armored him, turbaned him, girded him, and mounted him on his horse. And Amir al-Mu'minin went out. Three days passed, and Gabriel did not come with news, nor was there any news from the earth. So, Fatima came forward with al-Hasan and al-Husayn upon her hips, saying: These two boys are about to be orphaned. So, the Prophet shed tears, weeping. Then, he said: O people! Whoever comes to me with news of 'Ali, I will give him the glad tidings of Paradise. The people dispersed in search, and the search parties went out. 'Amer b. Qutada came with glad tidings of 'Ali, and Gabriel descended upon the Prophet and informed him. Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali came forward with two captives, a severed head, three camels, and three horses. So, the Prophet said: Would you like me to inform you of what happened, O Aba al-Hasan? The hypocrites said: Just a moment ago, he was overtaken with distress, yet now he wishes to tell his story! So, the Prophet sai

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Mughira ibn Tuba, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: When the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) looked over the graveyards, he said: O people of the dust! O people of estrangement! As for your houses, they have been reinhabited. As for your wives, they have been remarried. As for your wealth, it has been distributed. This is the news from our side; so what is the news from your side? Then he turned to his companions and said: If they were permitted to speak, they would have informed you that the best provision is God-wariness.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from al-Husayn ibn Yazid from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: There is not a day that passes by a son of Adam except that the day says to him: O son of Adam! I am a new day, and I am a witness over you. So say what is good during me and do what is good during me, and I will testify for you on the Day of Resurrection; for indeed you will never see me again after it.

Muhammad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim narrated to me. He said: Harun b. Muslim narrated to us from Mas'ada b. Ziyad from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Surely, a Muslim person has three friends: A friend that says to him: 'I am with you, alive and dead' — that is his deeds. A friend that says to him: 'I am with you until you die' — that is his wealth, for when he dies, it goes to the heirs. And a friend that says to him: 'I am with you until the gateway of your grave, then I will leave you' — that is his child.

Ja'far b. Ali al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abdullah b. al-Mughira narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sakuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Death is not given its proper due by whoever considers tomorrow to be part of his lifespan.

Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon in Basra. After praising and commending Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and sending blessings upon the Prophet and his Family, he said: A duration -- even if it is prolonged -- is short. The past is a lesson for those who remain. The dead are an exhortation for the living. When yesterday passes, it does not return, and a person has no certainty of tomorrow. The first is a guide for the middle, and the middle is a leader for the last. Everyone will part from everyone, and everyone will follow everyone. Death will overcome all, and the colossal Day is approaching all. It is the Day in which neither wealth nor sons will benefit anyone -- only those who come to Allah with a sound heart. Then he (peace be upon him) said: O my Shi'a! Be patient upon the deeds whose rewards you cannot do without, and patiently refrain from the deeds whose punishment you will have no patience for. Indeed, we have found that patience upon the obedience of Allah is easier than patience before the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Know that you are within a finite term, an amplified hope, and numbered breaths. The term must inevitably end, the hope must inevitably be extinguished, and the breaths must inevitably be exhausted. Then his eyes filled with tears, and he recited: "And indeed, over you are watchers, honourable angels recording -- they know whatever you do." (82:10-12)

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from Isma'il b. Marar from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman from Abu Ayyub from Abu Hamza from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: All goodness is gathered in three traits: sight, silence, and speech. Every sight devoid of contemplation is negligence. Every silence devoid of thought is heedlessness. Every speech devoid of remembrance [of Allah] is prattle. Blessed is he whose sight is a lesson, whose silence is contemplation, whose speech is remembrance, who cries over his sins, and from whose evil people are safe.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Isma'il b. Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: Seize the opportunity to supplicate at five occasions: (1) during the recitation of the Quran, (2) during the adhan, (3) when rain falls, (4) when two rows meet for martyrdom, and (5) at the supplication of the oppressed, for it has no barrier beneath the Throne.

Muhammad b. al-Qasim al-Astarabadi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Ali from his father from Muhammad b. Ali from his father al-Rida from his father Musa b. Ja'far from his father Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father Muhammad b. Ali from his father Ali b. al-Husayn from his father al-Husayn b. Ali (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: How many a heedless person weaves a garment to wear, when it is actually his shroud; and builds a house to live in, when it is actually the place of his grave.

It was said to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): What is the preparation for death? He said: Performing the obligations, avoiding the forbidden, and encompassing oneself with noble virtues — then one does not care whether he approaches death or death approaches him. By Allah, Ibn Abi Talib does not care whether he approaches death or death approaches him.

And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in one of his sermons: O people! Indeed, this world is the abode of annihilation, and the Hereafter is the abode of permanence. So take from your passage for your permanent abode, and do not tear your veils before the One from whom your secrets are not hidden. Take your hearts out of this world before your bodies are taken out of it, for you were enlivened in this world, but you were created for the Hereafter. This world is but like poison - it is eaten by one who does not know it. Indeed, when a servant dies, the angels say: "What has he sent forth?" while the people say: "What has he left behind?" So send forth virtue that will be for you, and do not leave behind a burden that will be against you. For indeed, the deprived one is he who is deprived of the good of his wealth, and the envied one is he whose scales become heavy with charities and good deeds, through which his resting place in Paradise is beautified, and his passage on the Path is sweetened.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Thabit ibn Dinar, from the Master of the Worshippers Ali ibn al-Husayn, from the Master of the Martyrs al-Husayn ibn Ali, from the Master of the Successors, the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them all, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said: The Imams after me are twelve. The first of them is you, O Ali, and the last of them is the Qa'im, through whom God, exalted is His mention, will conquer the East and the West of the earth.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad al-Qubti. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: The people are heedless of what the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said regarding 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) on the day of the chamber of Umm Ibrahim, just as they were heedless of what he said regarding him on the Day of Ghadir Khumm. Indeed, the Messenger of God was in the chamber of Umm Ibrahim, and his companions were with him, when 'Ali came, but they did not make way for him. When he saw that they were not making way, he said: "O people! These are my Ahl al-Bayt. You trivialize them while I am alive among you. By God, if I am absent from you, God will not be absent from you. Serenity, solace, happiness, and glad tidings are for whoever follows 'Ali, aligns with him, and submits to him and to the deputies from his descendants. It is my responsibility to admit them into my intercession, for they are my followers, and whoever follows me is of me. This is a tradition that passed through me from Ibrahim (peace be upon him), because I am from Ibrahim and Ibrahim is from me, and my virtue is his virtue and his virtue is my virtue, and I am more virtuous than him. The confirmation of that is the saying of my Lord: "Offspring, one of the other, and God is Hearing, Knowing." And the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) had injured his leg in the chamber of Umm Ibrahim, so that the people came to visit him.

The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Yusuf b. al-Harith from Muhammad b. Mihran from Ali b. al-Hasan. He said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us from Ma'mar from Isma'il b. Mu'awiya from Nafi' from Ibn Umar. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, the Throne of the Lord of the Worlds will be adorned with every adornment. Then two pulpits of light — each a hundred miles in height — will be brought forth. One will be placed to the right of the Throne and the other to the left of the Throne. Then al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) will be brought forth. Al-Hasan will stand upon one of them and al-Husayn upon the other. The Lord, blessed and exalted, adorns His Throne with them just as a woman adorns herself with her earrings.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba narrated to us, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqba, from 'Alqama, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) and claimed seventy dirhams from him as the price of a she-camel. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said to him: "O Bedouin, have you not already received that from me in full?" He said: "No." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said to him: "Then choose someone to judge between us." So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) went with him, and they sought judgment from a man of Quraysh. The man said to the Bedouin: "What do you claim against the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him." He said: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I have already paid him in full." The Qurayshi man said to the Bedouin: "What do you say to what the Messenger of Allah says?" He said: "I have not received it." So the Qurayshi man ruled in favor of the Bedouin against the Prophet. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) rose up in anger, dragging his cloak, and said: "By Allah, I shall go to one who judges between us by the judgment of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty." So he went with him to seek judgment from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said to the Bedouin: "What do you claim?" He said: "I claim seventy dirhams from him as the price of a she-camel I sold to him." He said: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I have already paid him in full." He said to the Bedouin: "What do you say to what the Messenger of Allah says?" He said: "I have not received it." Ali (peace be upon him) said: "O Bedouin, by Allah, I know that the Messenger of Allah has already paid you, but I shall ask you: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'I am the master of the children of Adam and I do not boast'?" He said: "Yes." Then Ali struck him with his sword and killed him. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: "O Ali, why did you kill the Bedouin?" He said: "Because he called you a liar, O Messenger of Allah, and whoeve

Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abdillah b. Ja'far b. Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. Umar from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them): Al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) entered one day upon al-Hasan (peace be upon him). When he looked at him, he wept. Al-Hasan said to him: 'What makes you weep, O Abu Abdillah?' He said: 'I weep for what will be done to you.' Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What will be brought upon me is poison that will be secretly administered, and I will be killed by it. But no day will be like your day, O Abu Abdillah. Thirty thousand men will rush toward you, claiming they are from the community of our grandfather Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and professing the religion of Islam. They will gather to kill you, shed your blood, violate your sanctity, capture your children and women, and plunder your belongings. At that point, the curse will descend upon the Banu Umayya, the sky will rain ashes and blood, and everything will weep for you — even the wild beasts in the deserts and the fish in the seas.'

4 - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd b. Abdillah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to us, he said: al-Abbas b. Ma'ruf narrated to us [from Abdullah b. al-Mughira], he said: Abu Hafs al-Abdi narrated to us, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When you ask Allah, Mighty and Exalted, ask Him for the means to me.
