So I asked the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) about the means, and he said: It is my rank in Paradise. It consists of one thousand steps. Between each step is the travel distance of a galloping horse for a month. It ranges from a step of jewel to a step of chrysolite, a step of ruby to a step of gold, to a step of silver. It will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and set up with the ranks of the prophets, and it will be among the ranks of the prophets like the moon among the stars. No prophet, saint, or martyr will remain on that day without saying: 'Blessed is he whose rank this is.' Then, a call will come from Allah, Mighty and Exalted, heard by the prophets and all of creation: 'This is the rank of Muhammad.' I will then come forward, and on that day I will be wrapped in a gown of light, wearing the crown of sovereignty and the wreath of honor. Ali ibn Abi Talib will be before me, carrying my banner — the Banner of Praise — upon which is written: 'There is no god but Allah; the successful are those who prevail through Allah.' When we pass by the prophets, they will say: 'These are two Angels of Proximity; we do not know them and have not seen them before.' When we pass by the angels, they will say: 'These are two commissioned prophets.' This continues until I ascend the ranks with Ali following me. When I reach the highest rank, with Ali one rank below me, no prophet, saint, or martyr will remain without saying: 'Blessed are these two servants — how Allah has honored them!' Then a call will come from Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, heard by the prophets, the saints, the martyrs, and the believers: 'This is My Beloved Muhammad, and this is My Friend Ali. Blessed is he who loves him, and woe to he who hates him and lies against him.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: On that day, there will not remain a single person who loved you — O Ali — except that

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. 'Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father. He said: 'Abd al-Rahman b. Hammad narrated to us from 'Abdullah b. Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn b. Yazid. He said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) saying: A man will appear from the descendants of my son Musa. His name is the name of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). He will be buried in the land of Tus, which is in Khurasan. He will be killed with poison therein, and he will be buried therein as a stranger. Whoever visits him, recognizing his right, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will give him the reward of one who spent (in charity) before the conquest and fought.

Ahmad b. Ziyad al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from 'Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Muhammad b. 'Isa b. 'Ubayd, from Muhammad b. Sulayman al-Basri, from his father, from Ibrahim b. Abi Hajar al-Aslami, from Qubaysa, from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi, who said: I heard the Deputy of Deputies, the Inheritor of the Prophets' knowledge, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib saying: The Master of Worshippers 'Ali b. al-Husayn narrated to me, from the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib, from the Master of Deputies, the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: A part of me will be buried in Khurasan. No afflicted person will visit it except that Allah will ease his affliction, and no sinner except that Allah will forgive his sins.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa and Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: I read the letter of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): Convey to my Shi'a that my visitation equals in the sight of Allah a thousand Hajj pilgrimages. He (al-Bazanti) said: So I said to Abu Ja'far, his son (peace be upon him): A thousand Hajj? He said: Yes, by Allah, and a million Hajj pilgrimages for whoever visits him recognizing his right.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa and Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: No one from my devotees visits me recognizing my right except that I will intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection.

'Ali b. 'Abd Allah al-Warraq narrated to us, from Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah b. Abi Khalaf, from 'Imran b. Musa, from al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. al-Nu'man, from Muhammad b. Fudayl b. Ghazwan al-Dabbi, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman b. Ishaq informed me, from al-Nu'man b. Sa'd, who said: The Commander of the Faithful 'Ali b. Abi Talib (blessings of Allah upon him) said: A man from my offspring will be killed in the land of Khurasan by poison unjustly. His name is my name, and the name of his father is the name of the son of Imran, Musa (peace be upon him). Indeed, whoever visits him in his exile, Allah will forgive his sins — those past and future — even if they were like the number of stars, drops of rain, and leaves of trees.

Ja'far b. Muhammad narrated to us, from al-Husayn b. Muhammad, from his uncle 'Abd Allah b. 'Amir, from Sulayman b. Hafs al-Marwazi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both) saying: Whoever visits the grave of my son Ali (peace be upon him), he shall have seventy accepted Hajj with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. I said: Seventy accepted Hajj? He said: Yes, and seventy thousand Hajj. I said: Seventy thousand accepted Hajj? He said: Then he said: Many a Hajj is not accepted. Whoever visits him or stays overnight at his shrine, it shall be like one who visited Allah at His Throne. I said: Like one who visited Allah at His Throne? He said: Yes. When it is the Day of Resurrection, there shall be upon the Throne of Allah, Exalted is His Majesty, four from the ancients and four from the later ones. The ancients: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa. The four later ones: Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn. Then the carpet shall be extended, and the visitors of the Imams' graves shall sit with us — except that the highest in rank and closest in privilege shall be the visitors of the grave of my son Ali (peace be upon him). The Shaykh, the jurist Abu Ja'far (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The meaning of his saying (peace be upon him) 'shall be like one who visited Allah at His Throne' is not a likening, because the angels visit the Throne, seek refuge in it, circumambulate around it, and say: 'We visit Allah at His Throne,' just as people say: 'We make pilgrimage to the House of Allah, and we visit Allah' — not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is described with a place. Exalted is He far above that greatly.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-'Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah, from Ayyub b. Nuh, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Musa (peace be upon them) saying: Whoever visits the grave of my father (peace be upon him) in Tus, Allah will forgive his past and future sins. On the Day of Resurrection, a pulpit will be set up for him beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), until Allah the Exalted finishes the reckoning of His servants.

Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natana (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from 'Ali b. Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza b. Humran, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: My grandchild will be killed in the land of Khurasan in a city called Tus. Whoever visits him there, recognizing his right, I will take him by my hand on the Day of Resurrection and admit him to Paradise, even if he were among the people of major sins. I said: 'May I be your ransom, what is recognizing his right?' He said: 'To know that he is an Imam whose obedience is obligatory, a stranger, a martyr. Whoever visits him recognizing his right, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will give him the reward of seventy martyrs who were truly martyred before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salih al-Razi from Hamdan al-Diwani. He said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits me despite the distance of my abode, I will come to him on the Day of Resurrection at three stations so that I may deliver him from its terrors: when the books of deeds fly to the right and to the left, at the Path (Sirat), and at the Scale (Mizan).

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdullah al-Barqi from his father from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. Umar from Abu al-Jarud from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi from Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari. He said: Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon to us. He praised Allah and commended Him, then said: O people! In front of this pulpit of yours are four men from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) -- among them: Anas b. Malik, al-Bara' b. Azib al-Ansari, al-Ash'ath b. Qays al-Kindi, and Khalid b. Yazid al-Bajali. Then he turned his face toward Anas b. Malik and said: O Anas! If you had heard the Messenger of Allah say: 'Whoever I was his master, then this Ali is his master,' yet you did not bear witness to my wilaya today, then may Allah not cause you to die until He afflicts you with a leprosy that the turban cannot cover. As for you, O Ash'ath, if you had heard the Messenger of Allah say: 'Whoever I was his master, then this Ali is his master. O Allah! Befriend whoever befriends him and oppose whoever opposes him,' yet you did not bear witness to my wilaya today, then may Allah not cause you to die until both your eyes go blind. As for you, O Khalid b. Yazid, if you had heard the Messenger of Allah say the same, yet you did not bear witness today, then may Allah not cause you to die except the death of Jahiliyya. As for you, O Bara' b. Azib, if you had heard the Messenger of Allah say the same, yet you did not bear witness today, then may Allah not cause you to die except in the place from which you emigrated. Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari said: By Allah, I saw Anas b. Malik afflicted with leprosy, trying to cover it with a turban but unable to hide it. And I saw al-Ash'ath b. Qays with both his eyes gone blind, saying: 'Praise be to Allah who made Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib pray against me with blindness in this world, and did not pray against me with punishment in the Hereafter so that I be punished.' As for Khalid b. Yazid -- he died, and his family wanted to bury him. They dug a grave for him in his house and buried him. Wh

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalaf narrated to us. He said: Sahl ibn Amer narrated to us. He said: Zafir ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Sharik from Abi Ishaq. He said: I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): What is the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (may God bless him and his family): 'Whoever takes me as a master, then Ali is his master'? He said: He informed them that he is the Imam after him.

Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from Ja'far b. Salama al-Isfahani from Ibrahim b. Muhammad. He said: al-Qinad narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Hashim b. al-Burayd narrated to us from his father. He said: Zayd b. Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about the saying of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family): "Whoever takes me as a master, then Ali is his master." He said: He set him up as a sign so that the Party of Allah may be known through him at the time of the split.

Ali ibn Hatim (may God have mercy on him) informed me. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Muhammadi narrated to us. He said: Kathir ibn 'Ayash narrated to us, from Abu'l Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "Surely, your guardian is God, His Messenger, and those who believe" -- the verse. He said: A band of Jews had accepted Islam, among them Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad, Tha'laba, Ibn Yamin, and Ibn Suraya. They came to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said: "O Prophet of God! Indeed, Musa (peace be upon him) appointed Yusha' ibn Nun. So who is your successor, O Messenger of God, and who is our guardian after you?" Then this verse was revealed: "Surely, your guardian is God, His Messenger, and those who believe -- those who establish prayer and give zakat whilst they are bowing." Then the Messenger of God said: "Stand up." So they stood up and went to the mosque, when behold, a beggar was coming out. He said: "O beggar! Did anyone give you anything?" He said: "Yes, this ring." He said: "Who gave it to you?" He said: "That man who is praying gave it to me." He said: "In what position did he give it to you?" He said: "He was bowing." So the Prophet exclaimed takbir, and the people of the mosque exclaimed takbir. Then the Prophet said: "Ali ibn Abi Talib is your guardian after me." They said: "We are pleased with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muhammad as Prophet, and with Ali ibn Abi Talib as guardian." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And whoever aligns with God, His Messenger, and those who believe -- then surely, the Party of God will prevail." It is reported from Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: By God, I gave forty rings in charity whilst bowing, so that a verse may be revealed about me like what was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), but nothing was revealed.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad b. Ali al-Isfahani from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi narrated to us from Sulayman b. Abdullah al-Hashimi from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal from Jabir al-Ju'fi. He said: I heard Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) say to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him): O Ali! You are my brother, my deputy, and my inheritor. You are my vicegerent over my Nation in my lifetime and after my passing. Whoever loves you loves me, and whoever hates you hates me. Your enemies are my enemies, and your friends are my friends.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Indeed, God -- blessed and exalted be He -- established brotherhood between me and Ali ibn Abi Talib, and married him to my daughter from above His seven heavens, and made His angels of proximity bear witness to that, and made him my deputy and vicegerent. Ali is from me and I am from him; one who loves him loves me, and one who hates him hates me. And indeed the angels seek closeness to God through loving him.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Abbas b. Ma'ruf from Abu Ishaq from al-Hasan b. Ziyad al-Attar. He said: I said to Abu Abdillah [Imam al-Sadiq] (as): The saying of the Messenger of Allah that "Fatima is the Mistress of the Women of the People of Paradise" - was she [only] the Mistress of the Women of her world? He said: That is Maryam. Fatima is the Mistress of the Women of the People of Paradise from the former and the latter peoples. So, I said: So, the saying of the Messenger of Allah (s) that "al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the two Masters of the Youth of Paradise"? He said: They are, by Allah, the two Masters of the Youth of Paradise from the former and the latter peoples.

Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said: Furat b. Ibrahim b. Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zhahir narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. al-Fadl al-Hashimi narrated to us from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: The day of Ghadir Khumm is the greatest of the Eids of my Nation. It is the day in which God the Exalted commanded me to appoint my brother 'Ali b. Abi Talib as a sign for my Nation to be guided by after me. And it is the day in which God completed the religion, fulfilled the blessing upon my Nation, and chose Islam as their religion. Then he (may God bless him and his family) said: O people! 'Ali is from me and I am from 'Ali. He was created from my clay, and he is the Imam of creation after me. He will clarify for them what they differ regarding my Sunna. He is the Commander of the Faithful, the Leader of the shining marked believers, the ruler of the believers, the best of deputies, the husband of the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, and the father of the Guided Imams. O people! Whoever loves 'Ali, I love him; whoever hates 'Ali, I hate him; whoever connects with 'Ali, I connect with him; whoever cuts off 'Ali, I cut him off; whoever is aloof to 'Ali, I am aloof to him; whoever aligns with 'Ali, I align with him; and whoever opposes 'Ali, I oppose him. O people! I am the City of Wisdom and 'Ali b. Abi Talib is its gate - no one can come to the City except through the Gate. And whoever alleges that he loves me yet hates 'Ali has lied. O people! By He who raised me with prophethood and selected me over all creation: I did not establish 'Ali as a sign for my Nation in the Earth until God proclaimed his name in His heavens and made his wilaya obligatory for His angels.

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Nasr b. Muzahim, from 'Umar b. Sa'd, from Arta'ah b. Habib, from Fudayl al-Rassan, from Jabala al-Makkiyyah. She said: I heard Maytham al-Tammar (may Allah sanctify his soul) say: By Allah! This nation shall kill the son of its Prophet in Muharram, when ten days have passed from it. The enemies of Allah shall take that day as a day of blessing, and that shall come to pass, for it has preceded in the knowledge of Allah, exalted be His mention. I know that through a covenant entrusted to me by my master, the Commander of the Faithful (blessings of Allah be upon him). And he informed me that everything shall weep over him -- even the wild beasts in the deserts, the fish in the seas, the birds in the middle of the sky. The sun, the moon, the stars, the heaven, the earth, the believing humans and jinn, all the angels of the heavens, Ridwan and Malik and the bearers of the Throne shall weep over him, and the sky shall rain blood and ashes. Then he said: The curse of Allah is incumbent upon the killers of Husayn (peace be upon him), just as it is incumbent upon the polytheists who appoint another god alongside Allah, and just as it is incumbent upon the Jews, the Christians, and the Zoroastrians. Jabala said: I said to him: O Maytham, how will the people take the day on which Husayn b. 'Ali (peace be upon them) is killed as a day of blessing?! Maytham (may Allah be pleased with him) wept, then said: They will claim through a hadith they fabricate that it is the day on which Allah forgave Adam (peace be upon him), while Allah forgave Adam in Dhu al-Hijjah. They claim it is the day on which Allah accepted the repentance of Dawud (peace be upon him), while Allah accepted his repentance in Dhu al-Hijjah. They claim it is the day on which Allah brought forth Yunus (peace be upon him) from the belly of the whale, while Allah brought him forth in Dhu al-Qi'dah. They claim it is the day on which the ark of Nuh (peace be upon him) came to rest on Mount Judi, while it came to rest on the eighteenth of Dhu al-Hijjah. And they claim it is the day on which Allah split the sea

Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah b. 'Amir, from Ibrahim b. Abi Mahmud. He said: al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Muharram is a month in which the people of the Jahiliyya would prohibit fighting, but our blood was deemed lawful in it, our sanctity was violated in it, our offspring and our women were taken captive in it, fires were set ablaze in our tents, and what was in them of our belongings was plundered, and the sanctity of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was not observed in our affair. Indeed, the day of al-Husayn wounded our eyelids, made our tears flow, and humiliated our beloved, in the land of suffering and affliction. It bequeathed us suffering and affliction until the day of termination. So upon the like of al-Husayn let those who weep, weep, for indeed weeping diminishes the great sins. Then he (peace be upon him) said: My father (blessings of God upon him), when the month of Muharram would enter, would not be seen laughing, and intense grief would overcome him until ten days had passed from it. And when it was the tenth day, that day would be the day of his affliction and his mourning and his weeping, and he would say: It is the day in which al-Husayn (blessings of God upon him) was killed.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Malik. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Zayd narrated to me. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad b. Ziyad narrated to us. He said: Ziyad b. al-Mundhir narrated to us from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. He said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) said to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family): O Messenger of God, surely you love 'Aqil? He said: Yes, by God! I love him with two loves: a love for him, and a love for Abu Talib's love for him. And surely his son shall be killed in the love of your son. The eyes of the believers shall shed tears over him, and the angels made proximate shall pray over him. Then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) wept until his tears flowed onto his chest. Then he said: To God I complain of what my progeny shall encounter after me.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us from 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Faddal from his father from Abu'l Hasan 'Ali b. Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever shuns striving for his needs on the day of Ashura, God will fulfill his needs of this world and the Hereafter. And whoever makes the day of Ashura a day of his calamity, his grief, and his weeping, God, Mighty and Majestic, will make the Day of Resurrection a day of his joy and his delight, and his eye shall be cooled by us in the Gardens. And whoever calls the day of Ashura a day of blessing and stores anything in his household on it, what he has stored will not be blessed for him, and he will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with Yazid, 'Ubaydullah b. Ziyad, and 'Umar b. Sa'd (may God curse them) in the lowest pit of the Fire.

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from al-Rayyan b. Shabib, who said: I entered upon al-Rida (peace be upon him) on the first day of Muharram. He said to me: O son of Shabib! Are you fasting? I said: No. He said: Verily this day is the day on which Zakariyya (peace be upon him) called upon his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: "My Lord, grant me good offspring from Your presence; surely You are the Hearer of prayers" (1). So He answered him and ordered the angels, and they called out to Zakariyya while he was standing in prayer in the prayer-niche: "Surely God gives you glad tidings of Yahya" (2). So whoever fasts this day and then calls upon God, the Mighty and Majestic, God will answer him as He answered Zakariyya (peace be upon him). Then he said: O son of Shabib! Muharram is the month in which the people of the pre-Islamic era (Jahiliyya) would prohibit oppression and fighting due to its sanctity, yet this nation did not recognize the sanctity of its month nor the sanctity of its Prophet (may God bless him and his family). They killed his offspring in this month, captured his women, and plundered his provisions. May God never forgive them for that. O son of Shabib! If you were to cry over anything, then cry over Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him), for he was slaughtered like the ram is slaughtered. Eighteen men from the people of his house, the like of whom are not to be found on the earth, were killed with him. The seven heavens and the earths wept over his killing. Four thousand angels descended to the earth to help him, but they found that he had already been killed. So they remain at his grave, dishevelled and dusty, until the Qa'im rises; then they will be among his helpers. And their slogan is: "O vengeance for Husayn!" O son of Shabib! My father narrated to me from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon him): Surely, when my grandfather Husayn (blessings of God upon him) was killed, the sky rained blood and red dust. O son of Shabib! If you wept over Husayn (peace be upon him) to the extent that your tears came onto your cheeks, God will forgive all of your sins which you have committed, whether minor or major, whether little or excessive. O son of Shabib! If it pleases you to meet God, the Mighty and Majestic, while there is no sin upon you, then vi

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abu'l Khattab narrated to us from Nasr b. Muzahim al-Munqari from 'Umar b. Sa'd from Abu Shu'ayb al-Taghlabi from Yahya b. Yaman from a leader of Banu Sulaym from their elders. They said: We invaded the lands of Rome and entered a church from their churches. We found written therein: Does a congregation that killed Husayn hope for the intercession of his grandfather on the Day of Reckoning? They said: So we asked: Since when has this been in your church? They said: Three hundred years before your Prophet was sent.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakhai narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Salim from his father from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad from his father (peace be upon him). He said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) had two rings. The inscription on one of them was: 'There is no god but Allah, a preparation for the meeting with Allah.' And the inscription on the other was: 'Indeed, Allah brings about His command.' And the inscription on the ring of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was: 'Disgraced and wretched is the murderer of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both).'

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, from his father, from Abu Hamza, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of Allah upon them all), that a man came to him and said: O Abu al-Hasan! You are called the Commander of the Faithful; so who appointed you over them? He (AS) said: Allah, Exalted is His Majesty, appointed me over them. So the man came to the Messenger of Allah (SAWW) and said: O Messenger of Allah! Does 'Ali speak the truth? The Prophet became enraged and said: 'Ali is the Commander of the Faithful through guardianship from Allah. He awarded it above His Throne and made His angels witness that 'Ali is the vicegerent and Proof of Allah, and the Imam of the Muslims. His obedience is coupled with obedience of Allah and his disobedience with disobedience of Allah. So whoever was ignorant of him was ignorant of me, and whoever recognised him recognised me. Whoever denied his Imamate denied my prophethood, whoever denied his rulership denied my messengership. Whoever refuted his superiority lowered me, whoever fought him fought me, whoever insulted him insulted me, for he is from me, created from my clay. He is the husband of Fatima and the father of al-Hasan and al-Husayn. Then he (SAWW) said: I, 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and nine from the descendants of al-Husayn are the Proofs of Allah upon His creation. Our enemies are the enemies of Allah, and our friends are the friends of Allah.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Thabit ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Yazid ibn Qa'nab said: I was sitting with al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and a group from the tribe of Abd al-Uzza near the Sacred House of Allah, when Fatima bint Asad, the mother of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), approached. She was nine months pregnant and had been overtaken by labor pains. She said: My Lord! Indeed, I am a believer in You and in what has come from You of messengers and books. And I believe in the words of my grandfather Ibrahim the Friend (peace be upon him), and that he built the Ancient House. So by the right of the One who built this House, and by the right of the child in my womb, make my delivery easy for me. Yazid ibn Qa'nab said: We saw the House open from its back, and Fatima entered it and disappeared from our sight, and the wall sealed itself. We tried to open the lock of the door but it would not open. So we knew that this was a matter from the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then she came out after the fourth day, and in her hand was the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). Then she said: I have been given excellence over the women who came before me, because Asiya bint Muzahim worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in secret in a place where Allah does not like to be worshipped except out of necessity. And Maryam bint Imran shook the dried date palm with her hand until she ate fresh ripe dates from it. But I entered the Sacred House of Allah and ate from the fruits of Paradise and its sustenance. When I wanted to come out, a caller called out to me: O Fatima! Name him Ali, for he is Ali, and Allah, the Most High, the Supreme, says: I have derived his name from My name, and I have trained him with My discipline, and I have made him privy to the depths of My knowledge. He is the one who will break the idols in My House, and he is the one who will call the adhan from atop My House, and he will glorify Me and exalt Me. So glad tidings to the one who loves him and obeys him, and woe to the one who hates him and disobeys him.

The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abu Ja'far al-Kamandani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Najran, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ubaydullah al-Simeen, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: While the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was addressing the people, saying: "Ask me before you lose me, for by God, there is nothing from the past nor anything of the future that you ask me about except that I shall inform you of it." Then Sa'd ibn Abu Waqqas stood up before him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, tell me how many hairs are on my head and in my beard." He said to him: "Verily, by God, you have asked me about a matter regarding which my friend, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) had told me that you would ask. There is not a single hair on your head or in your beard except that at its root sits a devil. And indeed in your house there is an infant who shall kill al-Husayn, my son." And Umar ibn Sa'd was at that time a toddler, crawling on his hands.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar together narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ashari. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Razi narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Sayf ibn Amira from Muhammad ibn Utba from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman from his father from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: While I and Fatima and al-Hasan and al-Husayn were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), he suddenly turned his face towards us and started weeping. I said: Why do you weep, O Messenger of Allah? He said: I weep because of what shall be done to you after me. I said: And what is that, O Messenger of Allah? He said: I weep over the strike on you on the side of your head, and the slapping of Fatima on her cheek, and the stabbing of al-Hasan in the thigh, and the poison which he will be given to drink, and the killing of al-Husayn. He said: So the Ahl al-Bayt all wept together. Then I said: O Messenger of Allah! Our Lord did not create us save for trial. He said: Rejoice, O Ali, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has confided in me that none shall love you save a believer, and none shall hold malice for you save a hypocrite.

209/3 - Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas ibn Bakkar narrated to us. He said: Harb ibn Maymun narrated to us, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: When Fatima gave birth to al-Hasan (peace be upon them both), she said to Ali (peace be upon him): Name him. He said: I would not precede the Messenger of God in naming him. Then the Messenger of God came, and the child was brought to him in a yellow cloth. He said: Had I not forbidden you from wrapping him in yellow cloth? Then he cast it aside and took a white cloth and wrapped him in it. Then he said to Ali: Have you named him? He said: I did not wish to precede you. So he said: And I do not wish to precede my Lord, Mighty and Majestic. So God revealed to Jibra'il. Jibra'il descended and congratulated him from God. Then he said: God commands you to name him with the name of the son of Harun. He said: And what was his name? He said: Shabbar. He said: My tongue is Arabic. He said: Name him al-Hasan. So he named him al-Hasan. And when al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was born, God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Jibra'il that a son had been born to Muhammad, so descend to him and congratulate him. He said: So Jibra'il descended and congratulated him from God, Blessed and Exalted. Then he said: Indeed, Ali is to you in the position of Harun to Musa, so name him with the name of the son of Harun. He said: And what is his name? He said: Shubayr. He said: My tongue is Arabic. He said: Name him al-Husayn. So he named him al-Husayn.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Hammad b. Isa. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad narrated to us from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Jabir b. Abdullah said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) saying to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) three days before his death: The salutation of God be upon you, O father of the two sweet-smelling basils. I entrust my two basils of this world to you, for soon your two pillars shall collapse, and God is my successor over you. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, Ali (peace be upon him) said: This is one of my two pillars which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) told me about. And when Fatima (peace be upon them both) died, Ali (peace be upon him) said: This is the second pillar which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had mentioned.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan, known as Abu Ali b. Abduwayh, narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas ibn Bakkar narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. Yazid narrated to me from Umar b. Ali b. al-Husayn, from Fatima bint al-Husayn, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, from Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib. She said: When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was delivered from his mother's womb and I was attending to her, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: O aunt, bring my son to me. So I said: O Messenger of God, we have not cleansed him yet. He (peace be upon him and his family) said: O aunt, will you cleanse him?! Surely, God, blessed and exalted, has already cleansed and purified him.

He said: And Ahmad b. al-Hasan narrated to us by this chain from Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib. She said: When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was delivered from his mother's womb, I handed him over to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet placed his tongue in his mouth, and al-Husayn took to sucking the tongue of the Messenger of God. I reckoned that the Messenger of God was feeding him nothing but milk or honey. She said: Then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) passed urine, and the Prophet kissed him between his eyes. Then he handed him over to me while he was weeping and saying: May God curse the nation that will kill you, O my son! He stated this thrice. She said: So I said: May my father and my mother be ransomed for you! Who shall kill him? He said: A remnant of the party of aggressors from the Banu Umayya — may God curse them.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qittan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. `Ali al-Sikkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya narrated to us. He said: Qays b. Hafs al-Darimi narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to me. He said: Mansur b. Abu 'l-Aswad narrated to us from Abu Hassan al-Taymi from Nashit b. `Ubayd from a man from among them from Jarda' bint Simin from her husband Hirthima b. Abu Muslim. He said: We went fighting with `Ali b. Abu Talib (as) in Siffin. When we departed, he descended on Karbala' and offered his morning prayer on it. Then, he raised its dust towards himself and sniffed at it. Then, he said: Glad-tidings be to you, O dust, for there will be nations gathered from you who will enter Paradise without accounting. Hirthima returned to his wife, who was a Shi`a of `Ali (as). He said: Should I not narrate to you about your master, Abu'l-Hasan? He descended on Karbala' and prayed. Then, he raised its dust towards himself and said: Glad-tidings be to you, O dust, for there will be nations gathered from you who will enter Paradise without accounting. She said: O man! Surely, Amir al-Mu'minin says nothing but the truth. When al-Husayn (as) advanced, Hirthima said: I was in the expedition of those whom `Ubaydullah b. Ziyad had sent. When I saw the destination and the trees, I remembered the hadith and I sat on my camel. Then I came towards al-Husayn (as) and saluted him and informed him about that which I had heard from his father regarding that destination which al-Husayn (as) had descended on. He said: Are you with us or against us? I said: I am neither with you nor against you. I have left behind sons against whom I fear `Ubaydullah b. Ziyad. He said: Then go away where you will not be able to see our murder nor hear our voice, for, by the One in Whose hand is the soul of al-Husayn, none shall consciously hear us today and not come to our aid but that Allah will throw him headlong into Hell.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin al-Thaqafi, from Abu Basir, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) said: I am the martyr of the tear. No believer mentions me except that he sheds tears.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. `Imran al-Ash`ari. He said: Musa b. `Umar narrated to us from `Abdullah b. Sabbah al-Muzanni from Ibrahim b. Shu`aib al-Maythami. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Abu `Abdillah (as) say: When al-Husayn b. `Ali (as) was born, Allah ordered Jibra'il that he descend with a thousand angels and offer congratulations to the Messenger of Allah (s) from Allah and from Jibra'il. So Jibra'il descended and he passed by an island in the sea wherein was an angel, named Futrus, who was from the bearers (of the Throne). Allah had dispatched him for something and he had delayed it. So, He broke his wings and banished him to that island. He worshipped Allah therein for seven hundred years until al-Husayn b. `Ali (as) was born. The angel said to Jibra'il: O Jibra'il! Where do you intend (i.e. to go)? He said: Allah has bestowed a bounty on Muhammad. So, I have been sent to offer him congratulations from Allah and myself. He said: O Jibra'il! Carry me with you; perhaps Muhammad (s) will pray for me. So, he carried him. When Jibra'il entered the Prophet's presence, he conveyed to him the congratulations from Allah and himself and informed him about the state of Futrus. The Prophet (s) said: Say to him: Rub (yourself) against this newborn and revert to your abode. So Futrus rubbed (himself) against al-Husayn b. `Ali (as) and he ascended. He said: O Messenger of Allah! Your Nation will certainly kill him soon, and upon me is the remuneration for him. A visitor shall not visit him but that I will notify him and a Muslim shall not send his salutation upon him but that I will convey to him his salaam. A praying one shall not say a prayer upon him but that I will convey to him his prayer. Then he ascended.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Aziz b. Yahya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Umarah from his father from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father Muhammad b. Ali from his truthful forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Surely, God, Blessed and Exalted, assigned to my brother Ali b. Abi Talib virtues which cannot be enumerated by anyone other than Him. So whoever mentions a virtue from his virtues, acknowledging it, God will forgive him his past sins and the latter ones, even if he were to come on the Day of Resurrection with the sins of the two heavyweights (men and jinn). Whoever writes down a virtue from the virtues of Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him), the angels shall not cease seeking forgiveness for him as long as a trace of that writing remains. Whoever listens to a virtue from his virtues, God will forgive him the sins which he acquired through hearing. Whoever looks at a writing about his virtues, God will forgive him the sins which he acquired through sight. Then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Looking towards Ali b. Abi Talib is worship. His mention is worship. And the faith of a servant is not accepted except through his wilaya (authority/guardianship) and dissociation from his enemies.

Al-Shaykh al-Faqih Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq narrated to us. He said: Abdul Aziz b. Yahya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Al-Mughira b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Jabir b. Salama narrated to me. He said: Husayn b. Hasan narrated to us from Amir al-Siraj from Salam al-Khath'ami from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon him. He said: Whoever fasts one day in Rajab, from its beginning or its middle or its end, Allah will make Paradise obligatory for him. He will bring him to us, in our rank, on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever fasts two days in Rajab, it will be said to him: Resume your work, for everything that has passed has been forgiven. Whoever fasts three days in Rajab, it will be said to him: Everything that has passed and everything that will remain has been forgiven, so intercede for whichever sinner you wish from your brethren and acquaintances. Whoever fasts seven days in Rajab, the seven doors of Hell will be locked from him. Whoever fasts eight days in Rajab, the eight doors of Paradise will be opened for him, and he will enter whichever one he wishes.

Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. 'Amer narrated to us from his uncle 'Abdullah b. 'Amer, from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr. He said: A group of our shaykhs narrated to me, among them Aban b. 'Uthman, Hisham b. Salim, and Muhammad b. Humran, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: I am astonished at him who is alarmed by four things yet does not seek refuge in four [others]. I am astonished at him who fears the enemy, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Trustee.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'So they returned with bounty from God and grace -- no harm touched them.' And I am astonished at him who is anguished, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'There is no god except You; glory be to You, indeed I was from the wrongdoers.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'So We answered him and rescued him from anguish -- and likewise, We rescue the believers.' And I am astonished at him who is plotted against, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'And I delegate my affairs to God; indeed God watches over His servants.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'So God protected him from the evils of what they plotted.' And I am astonished at him who desires this world and its adornments, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'Whatever God wills; there is no power except by God.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'Although you see that I have less wealth and fewer children than you, then perhaps my Lord will grant me something better than your garden' -- and this 'perhaps' is an affirmation.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from al-Rayyan b. al-Salt from Ali b. Musa al-Rida from his father from his forefathers from Amir al-Mu'mineen, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of Allah said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Whoever interprets My words by his own opinion has not believed in Me. Whoever likens Me to My creation has not recognized Me. Whoever utilizes qiyas in My religion is not upon My religion."

My father narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated from Ali b. Ma'bad from al-Husayn b. Khalid from Ali b. Musa al-Rida from his father from his forefathers from Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever does not believe in my Pond, Allah will not direct him to my Pond. Whoever does not believe in my intercession, I will not intercede to Allah for him. Then he said: Surely, my intercession is for those of my Nation who have committed major sins. As for the pious, they will have no need for it. Al-Husayn b. Khalid said: So I said to al-Rida: O son of the Messenger of Allah! What is the meaning of Allah's saying 'They do not intercede except for whom He approves'? He said: They will not intercede except for those whose religion Allah approves of.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi al-Sahban narrated to us. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad b. Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to us. He said: Aban al-Ahmar narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon him. A man came to him and said: May my mother and father be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! Teach me a proverb. So he said: If Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has guaranteed sustenance, then why are you worried? If sustenance is allotted, then why be greedy? If the Judgment is true, then why go to gatherings? If the reward is from Allah, then why be lazy? If the future is truly from Allah, then why be miserly? If the punishment from Allah is the Fire, then why sin? If death is true, then why be gleeful? If the offer of Allah is true, then why plot? If Satan is the enemy, then why be heedless? If passing through the Path is true, then why be astonished? If all things are destined, then why be sorrowful? If this world is fleeting, then why be content with it?

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ma'mar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ramli narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Maruzi narrated to us. He said: 'Amr ibn Mansur narrated to us. He said: Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir from his father from Abu Harun al-'Abdi from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Ali ibn Abi Talib is the foremost of my nation in submission, the most knowledgeable of them, the most correct of them in religion, the best of them in certainty, the most forbearing of them, the most generous of them of hand, and the boldest of them in heart -- and he is the Imam and the Caliph after me.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. `Amrus al-Hamadani narrated to us in Hamadan. He said: Abu Ali al-Hasan b. Isma`il al-Qahtabi narrated to us. He said: Sa`id b. al-Hakam b. Abi Maryam narrated to us from his father from al-Awza`i from Yahya b. Abi Kathir from `Abdullah b. Murra from Salama b. Qays. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Ali is to the seventh heaven as the Sun is to the Earth during the day, and to the lowest heaven as the Moon is to the Earth during the night. Allah gave Ali so much virtue that if it were divided among the people of the Earth, it would have encompassed them. And He gave him so much understanding that if it were divided among the people of the Earth, it would have encompassed them. His gentleness was likened to the gentleness of Lut, and his character to the character of Yahya, and his asceticism to the asceticism of Ayyub, and his generosity to the generosity of Ibrahim, and his splendour to the splendour of Sulayman b. Dawud, and his strength to the strength of Dawud. His name is written upon every barrier in Paradise. My Lord gave me glad tidings of him, and it was good news to me. Ali is praiseworthy with the Truth, purified with the angels. He is my elite one, my sincere one, my manifest one, and my lantern, and my shield, and my companion. My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, made him amiable to me, so I asked my Lord not to take his soul before me, and I asked that He take his soul as a martyr. I was admitted into Paradise, and I saw that the houris of Ali were more than the leaves on the trees, and the palaces of Ali were as the number of humans. Ali is from me, and I am from Ali. Whoever befriends Ali has befriended me. The love of Ali is a blessing, and following him is a virtue. The angels are brought near through him, and the righteous jinn surround him. No one walks the Earth after me except that he is more noble than him in honour, pride, and creed. He was never hasty, nor inclined to corruption, nor obstinate. The Earth carried him and it honoured him. No one came out of a womb after me more honourably than him. And he did not descend upon a place except that it was auspicious. Allah bestowed wisdom upon him and clothed him with understanding. The angels sit with him but he does not see them. If revelation were to come to anyone after me, it

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her): That she woke up one day crying. So it was said to her: What is the matter with you? She said: My son al-Husayn (peace be upon him) has indeed been killed, and I had not seen the Messenger of God (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) since he died except this night. So I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! Why do I see you looking so pale and haggard? He said: I have not ceased since tonight digging the grave of al-Husayn and the graves of his companions.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab narrated to us, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Umar ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Habib ibn Abu Thabit, from Umm Salama, wife of the Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family): She said: I had not heard the wailing of the jinn since the Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) was taken until this night, and I do not see myself except that I have been afflicted with my son. She said: And a jinniyyah from among them came saying: Lo! O eye, shed tears strenuously, for who shall weep over the martyrs after me -- over a clan whom death is leading towards a despot in the kingdom of a slave.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Habib ibn al-Husayn al-Taghlubi narrated to us. He said: Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: The Prophet (S) was in Umm Salama's house. He told her not to let anyone enter. Then al-Husayn (AS) came as a small child. She could not hold him, and he entered upon the Prophet (S). Umm Salama followed him and found al-Husayn upon his chest while the Prophet was weeping, turning something in his hand. The Prophet said: O Umm Salama! Jibril informs me that this one shall be killed, and this is the soil upon which he will be killed. Keep it; when it turns to blood, my beloved has been killed. Umm Salama said: O Messenger of God, ask God to repel that from him. He said: I have done so. Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to me that for him is a rank none of the creatures shall attain, and that for him are Shi'a who will intercede and their intercession will be accepted, and that the Mahdi is from his offspring. Blessed is whoever is from the friends of al-Husayn. His Shi'a are, by God, the successful ones on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hafs, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Salim ibn Abu Ja'dah. He said: I heard Ka'b al-Ahbar saying: Indeed, it is in our book that a man from the offspring of Muhammad, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), will be killed, and the sweat of the riding animals of his companions shall not dry until they enter Paradise and embrace the wide-eyed houris. Then al-Hasan (peace be upon him) passed by us and we said: Is he this one? He said: No. Then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) passed by us and we said: Is he this one? He said: Yes.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us. He said: al-`Abbas b. Ma`ruf narrated to us from Muhammad b. Sahl al-Bahrani, who traced it to Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said: Those who have wept [excessively] are five – Adam, Ya`qub, Yusuf, Fatima bt. Muhammad (s) and `Ali b. al-Husayn (as). As to Adam, he wept over Paradise until his cheeks became like valleys. As to Ya`qub, he wept over Yusuf until his vision left and until he was told: "By Allah! You shall not cease to remember Yusuf until you become sick to the hilt or you are of those who perish" (12:85). As to Yusuf, he wept over Ya`qub until the inhabitants of the prison were hurt by it and they said: Either you weep by day and be silent at night or that you weep by night and be silent in the daytime. So, he agreed to one of those two with them. And as to Fatima bt. Muhammad (s), she wept over the Messenger of Allah (s) until the people of Medina were troubled due to it. And they said to her: "You give us trouble through the excess of your crying." So, she went out towards the graves of the martyrs and wept until her need was accomplished; then she would depart. And as to `Ali b. al-Husayn, he wept over al-Husayn (as) for twenty years or forty years. And food would not be placed in front of him, but he would weep until a retainer of his said to him: "May I be ransomed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! I fear for you lest you be of those who perish." He said: "I only complain of my sorrow and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you know not. Surely, I do not remember the perdition of the children of Fatima but that I am choked with tears because of that."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ashari narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abu Uthman, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Umarah al-Munshid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: He said to me: O Abu Umarah, recite for me about al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both). He said: So I recited and he wept. Then I recited again and he wept. He said: By Allah, I did not cease reciting to him and he continued weeping until I heard the lamentation from the house. He said: Then he said to me: O Abu Umarah, whoever recites about al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) and makes fifty people weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn and makes thirty weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and makes twenty weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and makes ten weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and makes even one person weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and weeps himself, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and feigns crying, for him is Paradise.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from his paternal uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Riqqi, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when he asked for water. When he drank it, I saw that he wept and his eyes brimmed with tears. Then he said: O Dawud, may God curse the killer of al-Husayn! How the remembrance of al-Husayn has embittered life! Indeed, I have never drunk cold water without remembering al-Husayn, and there is no servant who drinks water and then remembers al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and curses his killer, except that God writes for him a hundred thousand good deeds, erases from him a hundred thousand evil deeds, raises for him a hundred thousand ranks, and it is as though he has freed a hundred thousand souls, and God will gather him on the Day of Resurrection radiant of face.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Kharija, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has entrusted four thousand angels to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), dishevelled and covered in dust, who weep over him until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever visits him, cognizant of his right, they will escort him until they bring him to his place of safety. And if he falls ill, they will visit him morning and evening. And if he dies, they will attend his funeral and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Amr al-Zayyat, from Fa'id al-Hannat, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both). He said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), cognizant of his right, Allah will forgive him his past and future sins.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them), who said: Instruct our Shia to perform the visitation (ziyara) of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), for indeed his visitation repels destruction, drowning, burning, and being preyed upon by wild beasts. And his visitation is made incumbent upon whoever acknowledges the Imamate of al-Husayn as being from God, Mighty and Majestic.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan. He said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I observe Arafa at the grave of al-Husayn. He said: Well done, O Bashir! Any believer who comes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), cognizant of his right, on a day other than Eid, twenty Hajj and twenty 'Umra, approved and accepted, and twenty expeditions alongside a sent prophet or a just Imam are written for him. And whoever comes to it on the day of Eid, a hundred Hajj and a hundred 'Umra and a hundred expeditions alongside a sent prophet or a just Imam are written for him. And whoever comes to it on the Day of Arafa, cognizant of his right, a thousand Hajj and a thousand 'Umra, approved and accepted, and a thousand expeditions alongside a sent prophet or a just Imam are written for him. He said: Then I said to him: And how can I have the like of the standing place [at Arafat]? He said: He looked at me like one angered, then said: O Bashir! Indeed, when the believer comes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafa and washes in the Euphrates, then heads toward it, God, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him with every step a Hajj with its rituals — and I do not know it except that he said: and an expedition.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari. He said: Ibn Aisha and al-Hakam and al-Abbas narrated to us. They said: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abu Yaqub, from Ibn Abi Nu'm. He said: I was present with Ibn Umar when a man came to him and asked him about the blood of the mosquito. So he said: Where are you from? He said: From the people of Iraq. He said: Look at this man! He asks me about the blood of the mosquito while they have killed the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)! And I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: Indeed they are my two sweet basils from this world — meaning al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Abi Najran, from al-Muthanna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim. He said: I asked al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) about the ring of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) — to whom did it go? And I mentioned to him that I had heard that it was looted from his finger among what was looted. He (peace be upon him) said: It is not as they say. Indeed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) bequeathed to his son Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and placed his ring on his finger, and delegated his command to him, just as the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) had done with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the Commander of the Faithful had done with al-Hasan (peace be upon them both), and al-Hasan had done with al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). Then that ring came to my father (peace be upon him) after his father, and from him it came to me. So it is with me, and I wear it every Friday and pray with it. Muhammad ibn Muslim said: So I entered upon him on Friday and he was praying. When he finished the prayer, he extended his hand toward me, and I saw on his finger a ring whose inscription was: "There is no god but God, a preparation for the meeting with God." Then he said: "This is the ring of my grandfather Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them."

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Prophet (may God bless him and his family) would stand at the door of Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them both) at the break of every dawn and say: All praise is for God, the Doer of good, the Beautifier, the Bestower of favours, the Conferrer of benefits, through Whose grace righteous deeds are completed. Let a listener hear of the praise of God and His favour, and His trial is beautiful in our estimation. We seek refuge in God from the Fire, we seek refuge in God from the mornings of the Fire, we seek refuge in God from the evenings of the Fire. The prayer, O Ahl al-Bayt! "Indeed, God only desires to remove uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification" [33:33].

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Nawfali. He said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): The believer sees a dream and it comes to pass as he saw it, and sometimes he sees a dream but it amounts to nothing? So he said: Indeed, when the believer sleeps, an extended movement emerges from his spirit, ascending toward the heaven. So whatever the spirit of the believer sees in the kingdom of the heaven, in the place of Divine decree and regulation, that is the truth. And whatever he sees on the earth, those are confused dreams. I said to him: Does the spirit ascend to the heaven? He said: Yes. I said: Until nothing of it remains in his body? He said: No, were all of it to leave until nothing remained, he would certainly die. I said: Then how does it leave? He said: Do you not see the sun in the sky in its place, while its light and its rays are on the earth? Similarly, the spirit — its source is in the body, and its movement extends toward the heaven.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us, he said: One of our companions narrated to me, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when the servants sleep, their spirits exit toward the heaven. So what the spirit sees in the heaven is the truth, and what it sees in the atmosphere are confused dreams. Verily, the spirits are enlisted soldiers. So whichever of them recognizes the other unites with it, and whichever of them finds the other unfamiliar diverges from it. So when the spirit is in the heaven, they recognize each other and they loathe each other. And when they recognize each other in the heaven, they recognize each other on earth; and when they loathe each other in the heaven, they loathe each other on earth.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu'l Khattab narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abu Talib, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him). He said: I asked the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) about the man who sleeps and then sees a dream -- sometimes it is true and sometimes it is false. The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! There is no servant who sleeps except that his spirit is raised toward the Lord of the worlds. Whatever he sees in the presence of the Lord of the worlds is truth. Then, when God, the Mighty, the Omnipotent, commands the return of his spirit to his body, and the spirit is between heaven and earth, whatever it sees then are confused dreams.

And from him, by his chain, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, he said: And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Muhsin ibn Ahmad al-Maythami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: I heard him say: Indeed, Iblis has a devil called Haz', who fills what is between the East and the West every night, coming to people in their sleep.

19 - In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. (3) The shaykh, the jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us by recitation upon him. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Farawi (4), from his father. He said: I visited al-Fadl ibn al-Rabi' and he was sitting on a roof. He said to me: Come near to me. So I approached until I was alongside him. Then he said to me: Look toward the room in the house. So I looked, and he said: What do you see in the room? I said: A garment laid out. He said: Look carefully. So I pondered and looked and became certain. I said: A man in prostration. He said to me: Do you know him? I said: No. He said: This is your master. I said: And who is my master? He said: Are you feigning ignorance with me? I said: I am not feigning ignorance, but I do not know a master. Then he said: This is Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). Indeed I check on him day and night, and I have not found him at any time except in the state which I shall describe to you: He prays Fajr and then follows it with worship for an hour after his prayer until the sun rises. Then he prostrates and does not cease being in prostration until the sun passes midday. He had appointed someone to watch for the midday for him, and I do not know when the boy says: The sun has passed midday! — when he leaps up and begins the prayer without renewing his ablution, so I know that he did not sleep during his prostration nor did he drowse. He remains like that until he finishes the Asr prayer. When he prays Asr, he prostrates and does not cease being in prostration until the sun sets. When the sun sets, he leaps from his prostration and prays Maghrib without renewing anything. He remains in his prayer and worship until he prays the Isha prayer. When he prays Isha, he breaks his fast on something roasted (1) that is brought to him. Then he renews his ablution, then he prostrates, then he raises his head and sleeps a light nap. Then he rises and renews his ablution, then he rises and does not cease praying in the depths of the night until dawn rises. I do not know when the boy says: Indeed the dawn has risen! — when he has already leaped up f

The Shaykh Abu Ja'far narrated to me by reading to him. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: Al-Rashid summoned a man to invalidate the authority of Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) and to refute him and embarrass him in the assembly. So a sorcerer volunteered. When the banquet was brought, he cast a spell upon the bread; whenever the servant of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) tried to take a loaf, it flew from his hands. Joy and laughter overtook Harun. Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) raised his head toward a lion painted on a curtain and said: O lion of Allah, seize the enemy of Allah! He said: That image leaped forth like the mightiest beast of prey and devoured the sorcerer. Harun and his courtiers fell unconscious, and their minds were blown away in fear. When they recovered after a while, Harun said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): I ask you by my right over you, would you not ask the image to return the man? So he said: If the staff of Musa (peace be upon him) could return what it swallowed of the people's ropes and staffs, then this image would return what it swallowed of this man. And that was the most effective of things in the awakening of his soul.

He said: My father narrated to us from Sa'd b. 'Abdullah from Muhammad b. 'Isa b. 'Ubayd al-Yaqtini from al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Bashar, he said: An 'ammi shaykh from Qati'at al-Rabi' narrated to me — one whose word was accepted — he said: He said to me: I have indeed seen some of those who acknowledge the virtue of a man from the People of this House, and I have never seen anyone like him in his asceticism and virtue. He said: I said: Who? And how did you see him? He said: Al-Sindi b. Shahik gathered us — eighty men of renown attributed to goodness — in the days [of al-Sindi], and brought us in to Musa b. Ja'far (upon them both be peace). Al-Sindi said to us: O you people! Look at this man — has anything happened to him? For the people allege that he has been treated wrongly, and they make much ado about that. This is his residence and his furnishings — spacious for him and not restricted. The Commander of the Faithful has not intended any harm for him. He is only waiting for him to come so the Commander of the Faithful may converse with him. Here he is, healthy, with ample provision in all his affairs — so ask him. He said: And we had no concern except to look at the man and at his virtue and his character. Then he said: As for what he mentioned regarding the spaciousness and the like, it is as he mentioned. Except that I inform you, O people, that I was fed poison in nine dates, and that I will turn green tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow I will die. He said: So I looked at al-Sindi b. Shahik, and he was shuddering and shaking like a palm leaf. Al-Hasan said: This shaykh was from the best of the Sunnis — a truthful shaykh, whose word was accepted, and who was very much trusted by the people.

The Sheikh, the jurist Abu Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, from Thabit ibn Dinar, who said: I asked Zayn al-Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) about Allah, exalted is His majesty: Is He described with a place? He said: Allah is exalted above that. I said: Then why did He take His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) on a night journey to heaven? He said: To show him the dominion of the heavens and the wonders of His design and the marvels of His creation. I said: Then what about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then he drew near and hung suspended, and he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer' (53:8-9)? He said: That was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who drew near to the veils of light, and he saw the dominion of the heavens, then he (peace be upon him and his family) hung suspended and looked from beneath him toward the dominion of the earth, until he thought that he was in nearness to the earth like the distance of two bow-lengths or closer.

The esteemed Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, may God be pleased with him, said: My father, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from Abu al-Jarud, Ibn Bukayr, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-'Ijli, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, was killed, and there were found on him three hundred and twenty-something wounds from spears, sword slashes, or arrows. It is reported that they were all on his front side, because he, peace be upon him, would not turn his back.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Muthanna, from his mother Fatima bint al-Husayn (peace be upon him). She said: The crowd rushed into our pavilion while I was a young girl, and I had two gold anklets on my feet. A man began removing the two anklets from my feet while he was weeping. So I said: 'What makes you cry, O enemy of God?!' He said: 'How can I not weep when I am robbing the daughter of the Messenger of God!' So I said: 'Do not rob me.'
