He said: 'I fear someone else may come and take it.' She said: And they plundered everything in the structures, to the point that they were pulling the cloaks off our backs.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Basri, from Muhammad ibn Zakariyya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Abu Nu'aym, from the doorkeeper of Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad: When the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was brought, he ordered it placed before him in a gold basin and began striking his front teeth with a stick, saying: "Grey hair hastened to you, O Abu Abdillah." A man said: "Stop! I saw the Messenger of God kissing where you place your stick." He said: "A day for the day of Badr." Then Ali ibn al-Husayn was shackled and taken with the women and captives to prison, and I was with them. We passed no alleyway except that we found it full of men and women hitting their faces and weeping. They were imprisoned and it was made narrow for them. Then Ibn Ziyad (la) called for Ali ibn al-Husayn and the women, and the head of al-Husayn was present. Zaynab bint Ali (as) was among them. Ibn Ziyad said: "Praise be to Allah who has exposed you, killed you, and belied your narrations." Zaynab said: "Praise be to Allah who ennobled us with Muhammad and purified us with a thorough purification. Allah only exposes the transgressor and belies the wretched." He said: "How do you see what Allah has done with you, the Ahl al-Bayt?" She said: "Being killed had been ordained for them, so they have gone into their place of rest. Allah will gather you and them, and you will be judged by Him." Ibn Ziyad (la) became angry and concerned with her. Amr ibn Harith calmed him down. Zaynab said: "O Ibn Ziyad! What you have perpetrated against us is enough. You have killed our men, cut off our foundation, made our sanctity permissible, and taken our women and children into captivity. If that satisfies you, then you have been made satisfied." Ibn Ziyad ordered them back to jail, and sent the news of the killing of al-Husayn (as) to the frontiers. Then the captives and the head of al-Husayn were taken to the Levant. A group narrated to me: throughout the nights, they would hear the lament of the Jinn over al-Husayn until the break of dawn. When we entered Damascus, the women and captives were brought in by daylight with their faces uncovered. The cold people of the Levant said: "We have never seen captives more beautiful than these. Who are you?" Sakina bint al-Husayn (as) said: "We are the captives of the Family

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Lut ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn Ka'b, from Fatima bint Ali (blessings of God be upon them both): Then Yazid (may God curse him) ordered that the women of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) be imprisoned with Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) in a prison that had no protection from heat or cold, until their faces peeled. Not a stone was raised from the face of the earth in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) except that fresh blood was found beneath it. And the people saw the sun on the walls appearing red, as though it were sheets dyed with safflower. until Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was released with the women, and the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was returned to Karbala.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (rh) narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub b. Yazid narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal from al-Daylami -- and he is Sulayman -- from Abdullah b. Latif al-Taflisi. He said: Al-Sadiq Abu Abdillah Ja'far b. Muhammad (as) said: When al-Husayn b. Ali (as) was struck with the sword, and they prepared to sever his head, a caller called from the direction of the Lord of Glory, Blessed and Exalted, from the depth of the Throne, saying: 'O perplexed and misguided nation after its Prophet! Allah will not grant you success in Adha nor in Fitr.' Then Abu Abdillah (as) said: By Allah, they were never granted success, nor will they ever find success, until the Revolutionary of al-Husayn (as) rises.

The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amer narrated to us. He said: al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Amr ibn Ziyad from Mudrak ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, will gather the people on one plane. The scales will be brought out, and the blood of the martyrs will be weighed against the ink of the scholars. The ink of the scholars will outweigh the blood of the martyrs.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb al-Sayrafi from al-Haytham Abu Kahmas from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Six qualities will benefit a believer after his death: a righteous child who seeks forgiveness on his behalf, a mus'haf that is recited from, a well that he dug, a plant that he planted, running water that he gave in charity, and a beautiful tradition that is practiced after him.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad b. Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to us. He said: I heard Malik b. Anas the jurist of Medina say: I would visit al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as), and he would give me a pillow, show me esteem, and say: 'O Malik, indeed I love you.' I would be delighted by that and praise Allah for it. He was a man never free from three qualities: either fasting, standing in prayer, or remembering Allah. He was from the greatest worshippers and the greatest ascetics who were in awe of Allah. He would speak much hadith, his gatherings were pleasant, and he was of much benefit. Whenever he said 'the Messenger of Allah (s) said', his colour would turn green at one time and pale another, until one who knew him would not recognize him. I performed Hajj with him one year. When his ride was prepared at the Ihram, every time he intended to recite the talbiyya, his voice cut off in his throat, and he almost fell from his ride. So I said: 'Say it, O son of the Messenger of Allah, and you must say it.' So he said: 'O Ibn Abi Amir! How can I dare say "I am at Your service, O Allah, I am at Your service" while I fear that He may reply to me: "I am not here for you, nor for your pleasure!"'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi from Malik ibn Anas. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: I am astonished at one who is stingy in this world when it presents itself to him, or is stingy in it when it turns away from him. Spending when it presents itself will not harm him, and withholding when it turns away will not benefit him.

Malik ibn Anas said: And I heard al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: It was said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): Why do you not purchase a purebred horse? He said: I have no need for it, for I do not flee from one who attacks me, nor do I attack one who flees from me.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad the fair goldsmith narrated to us. He said: Isa ibn Muhammad al-Alawi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Sallam al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Wahid narrated to us. He said: Harb ibn al-Hasan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Isma'il ibn Sadaqa narrated to us from Abu al-Jarud from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: When this verse, 'And We have recorded everything in a Manifest Imam' [36:12], was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), two men stood from their sitting and said: O Messenger of Allah! Is it the Torah? He said: No. They said: Is it the Gospel? He said: No. They said: Is it the Quran? He said: No. Then, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali came forward; so, the Messenger of Allah said: It is he -- he is the Imam in whom Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has recorded the knowledge of everything.

Muhammad b. Harun al-Zanjani narrated to us. He said: Mu'adh b. al-Muthanna al-'Anbari narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Asma' narrated to us. He said: Juwayriyya narrated to us from Sufyan from Mansur from Abi Wa'il from Wahb. He said: I found in some of the books of Allah: When Dhul Qarnayn completed working on the wall, he went on his way. He journeyed with his soldiers when they came across an elder praying. He and his soldiers halted until he completed his prayer. Dhul Qarnayn said to him: Why did you not stop when my soldiers came into your presence? He said: I was speaking to One who has more soldiers than you, more glory in His power, and more intensity in His strength. Had I turned my face to you, I would not receive my need from Him. Dhul Qarnayn said: Can you come out with me? He said: Yes, if you guarantee me four qualities: blessings that do not falter, health without illness, youth without old age, and life without death. Dhul Qarnayn said: Which creature is able to have these! The elder said: I am with He who is capable of them and rules over them and you. Then he passed by a sage who said: Inform me of two things standing since Allah created them, two things moving, two things changing, and two things opposing. Dhul Qarnayn said: The standing are the heavens and earth; the moving are the sun and moon; the changing are night and day; the opposing are death and life. He said: Proceed, you are a sage. He journeyed until he passed by an elder turning over skulls, and asked him why. He said: To distinguish the noble from the lowly and the rich from the poor, but I could not for twenty years. Dhul Qarnayn left saying: No one has grieved over this other than me. He continued until he came upon a scholarly nation from the people of Musa, who guide to truth and judge by it. He said: I have gone around the world and never met anyone like you. Why are your graves at your doorsteps? They said: So we never forget death. Why no doors? No thieves among us. No governors? We do not oppress. No judges? We do not quarrel. No kings? We do not exalt. Why no differences? We are accommodating and compassionate. Why no disputes? Our hearts have affinity. Why no blame or killing? We overcame our natures with determination and tamed ourselves with forbearance. Why are you united? We do not lie, cheat, or slander. Why no poor? We redistribute evenly. Why no rudeness

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Abbas b. Ma'ruf from Ali b. Mahzayar from Fadala b. Ayyub from Aban b. Uthman from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Khalid b. al-Walid to a neighbourhood called Banu al-Mustalaq from Bani Judhayma, and there had been a rivalry between them and Bani Makhzum during the Age of Ignorance. When he came upon them, they had already obeyed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and had taken a letter from him. When Khalid came upon them, he ordered a caller to call to prayer, so he prayed and they prayed. When the Fajr prayer came, he ordered his caller to call, so he prayed and they prayed. Then he ordered the cavalry, and they launched a raid upon them, killing and wounding. They demanded their letter and found it, then they brought it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and told him what Khalid b. al-Walid had done. So he faced the qibla and said: O Allah, I dissociate myself before You from what Khalid b. al-Walid has done. He said: Then riches and goods were brought to the Messenger of Allah, and he said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Ali, go to Bani Judhayma from Banu al-Mustalaq and compensate them for what Khalid has done. Then he (peace be upon him and his family) raised his feet and said: O Ali, put the judgment of the people of Ignorance beneath your feet. So Ali (peace be upon him) went to them, and when he reached them, he judged among them by the judgment of Allah. When he returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said: O Ali, tell me what you have done. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I went and gave blood money for every life, a servant for every unborn child, and wealth for every property. I had surplus remaining, so I gave them enough for their dogs' water bowls and their shepherds' ropes. I still had surplus remaining, so I gave them for the fright of their women and the terror of their children. I still had surplus remaining, so I gave them for what they know and what they do not know. I still had surplus remaining, so I gave them so that they would be pleased with you, O Messenger of Allah. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Ali

The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Istarabadi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to us from their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from the Commander of the Faithful (God’s blessings upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: God, Blessed and Exalted, said: I have divided the Opening of the Book between Me and My servant. Half of it is for Me and half of it is for My servant, and for My servant is whatever he asks. When the servant says: “In the name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful,” God, exalted is His Majesty, says: “My servant has begun with My name, and it is My duty to fulfill his affairs and to bless him in his conditions.” When he says: “All praise belongs to God, the Lord of the Worlds,” God, exalted is His Majesty, says: “My servant has praised Me and he knows that the blessings he has are from Me, and that the calamities that were deflected from him were due to My grace. I testify to you that I will add to the blessings of this world for him the blessings of the Hereafter, and I will deflect from him the calamities of the Hereafter just as I deflected from him the calamities of this world.” When he says: “The Beneficent, the Merciful,” God says: “He has testified for Me that I am the Beneficent, the Merciful. I testify to you that I will surely increase his portion of My mercy and grant him generously his share of My bestowal.” When he says: “Master of the Day of Judgment,” God says: “I testify to you: just as he has acknowledged that I am the Master of the Day of Judgment, I will ease his reckoning, accept his good deeds, and overlook his sins.” When he says: “You alone we worship,” God says: “My servant has spoken the truth — he worships Me alone. I will reward him for his worship with a reward envied by all who opposed him.” When he says: “And from You alone we seek help,” God says: “He seeks help in Me and takes refuge in Me. I will help him in his affairs, assist him in his hardships, and take him by his hand in his calamities.”

It was said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): O Commander of the Faithful, inform us about "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" - is it from the Fatiha of the Book? He said: Yes, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would recite it and count it as a verse from it, and he would say: The Fatiha of the Book is the Seven Oft-Repeated Verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to me, from their two fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja’far, from his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his brother al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: Amir al-Mu’minin (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful” is a verse from the Opening of the Book, and it consists of seven verses, the completion of which is “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” I heard the Messenger of God (may God’s blessings be upon him and his family) saying: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, said to me: “O Muhammad! We have given you the Seven Oft-Repeated and the Great Quran.” So He singled out the favour upon me through the Opening of the Book and placed it equal to the Great Quran. Indeed, the Opening of the Book is the most noble of what is in the treasures of the Throne. And indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, chose Muhammad specifically and honoured him with it, and did not share it with any of His prophets, except Sulayman (peace be upon him), for He gave him from it “In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Do you not see that He relates about Bilqis when she said: “Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me. Indeed it is from Sulayman, and indeed it reads: In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful”? Indeed, whoever recites it whilst believing in the allegiance to Muhammad and his righteous family, submitting to their command, and believing in their apparent and hidden teachings, God, Mighty and Majestic, will give him for every letter of it a good deed, each one better for him than the world and all that is in it of its wealth and goodness. And whoever listens to a reciter reciting it will have the equivalent of one-third of the reciter’s reward. So let each of you increase from this good that is offered to you, for it is a treasure -- do not let its time pass away, lest regret remain in your hearts.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him). He said: When this verse was revealed—‘And Hell is brought near on that day’ (89:23)—the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) was asked about it. He said: The Faithful Spirit informed me that Allah, there is no god but He, when He gathers together the first and the last, Hell will be brought forward, led by a thousand bridles, each bridle held by a hundred thousand harsh and severe angels. It will have a crashing sound, fury, and roaring, and it will let out a roar such that, were it not that Allah the Mighty and Majestic had postponed them to the time of reckoning, it would have destroyed the entire assembly. Then a neck will extend from it, encircling all of creation—the righteous among them and the sinners. There is not a single servant whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic created—no angel and no prophet—except that he will cry out: My Lord, save me! Save me! But you, O Prophet of Allah, will call out: My community! My community! Then a bridge will be placed over it, finer than the edge of a sword, upon which there are three arches: on the first is trustworthiness and kinship, on the second is prayer, and on the third is the justice of the Lord of the Worlds—there is no god but He. People will be required to pass over it. Kinship and trustworthiness will hold them back; if they survive that, prayer will hold them back; if they survive that, the final destination will be with the Lord of the Worlds, the Mighty and Majestic. This is what His words, Blessed and Exalted, mean: ‘Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful’ (89:14). The people will be on the bridge—some clinging, some slipping with one foot while the other holds firm. The angels will surround them, calling out: O Forbearing One! Forgive and pardon! Return with Your bounty and grant safety! And the people will be falling into it like moths. When someone is saved by the mercy of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, he will look at it and say: Praise be to Allah who saved me from you after despair, through His grace and bounty. Indeed, our Lord is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative (35:34).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: People will pass through the Path (Sirat) in different ranks. The Path is thinner than a hair and sharper than the edge of a sword. Among them are those who pass like lightning, among them are those who pass like a galloping horse, among them are those who pass crawling, among them are those who pass walking, and among them are those who pass clinging to it, while the Fire seizes part of them and leaves part.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decides to resurrect the creation, He will cause the sky to rain upon the earth for forty mornings, and then the bones will reassemble and the flesh will grow.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saw a man from his Shi'a after a long time, and aging had left its mark on him. He was persevering in his walk. So he said: You have aged, O man. He said: In obedience to you, O Commander of the Faithful. So he said: You are still enduring. He said: Against your enemies, O Commander of the Faithful. So he said: I find remaining strength in you. He said: It is for you, O Commander of the Faithful.

Al-Rayyan b. al-Salt said: al-Rida (peace be upon him) recited a poem of Abd al-Mutalib to me: All the people blame time, but there is nothing as blameworthy in our time as us. We blame our time when the fault is in us; if time could speak, it would have attacked us. Surely, a wolf leaves the flesh of a wolf, but we knowingly eat one another.

Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah b. Amer from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Abdullah b. al-Qasim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: Be more hopeful in that which you have no hope than in that which you have hope. For surely, Musa b. Imran (peace be upon him) went to fetch fire for his family, yet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke to him and he returned as a prophet. The queen of Saba came out and accepted Islam with Sulayman (peace be upon him). The magicians of Pharaoh went out seeking glory for Pharaoh, yet they returned as believers.

Ali ibn Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He said: al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: My father narrated to me, from his father (peace be upon them both): That al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was the most devout of the people in his time, the most ascetic, and the most virtuous. When he performed Hajj, he would perform it on foot, and sometimes walked barefoot. When he remembered death, he wept; when he remembered the grave, he wept; when he remembered the Resurrection and the Gathering, he wept; when he remembered the passing on the Sirat, he wept; and when he remembered the presentation before Allah the Exalted, he gasped with a gasp that would cause him to faint. When he stood in his prayer, his limbs trembled before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. When he remembered Paradise and the Fire, he would be agitated like one stung by a snake, and he would ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge from the Fire. He would not recite 'O you who believe' from the Book of Allah except that he would say: 'I am at Your service, O Allah, I am at Your service.' He was never seen in any condition except remembering Allah, Glorified be He, and he was the most truthful of people in speech and the most eloquent in eloquence. And indeed, it was said to Mu'awiya one day: 'If you ordered al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib to climb the pulpit and deliver a sermon, his deficiency would become clear to the people.' So he called him and said: 'Climb the pulpit and speak words that will exhort us.' So he stood, climbed the pulpit, praised Allah and commended Him, then said: 'O people! Whoever knows me already knows me, and whoever does not know me — I am al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, the son of the Mistress of Women, Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of Allah. I am the son of the best of Allah's creation. I am the son of the Messenger of Allah. I am the son of the possessor of virtues. I am the son of the possessor of miracles and signs. I am the son of the Commander of the Faithful. I am the one ejected from my right. My brother al-Husayn and I are the two Masters of the Youth of Paradise. I am the son of the Rukn and the Maqam. I am the son of

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdullah. He said: Muhammad b. Tasnim narrated to me from al-Abbas b. Amer from Ibn Bukayr from Salam b. Ghanim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his forefathers (peace be upon them). The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever sweeps a mosque, Allah will record for him the freeing of a slave. And whoever removes from it something that irritates an eye, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will record for him a double portion of His mercy.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ali al-Qurashi from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. Umar from Yunus b. Thibyan from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: While Musa b. Imran (peace be upon him) was speaking to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, he saw a man beneath the shade of the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So he said: O my Lord, who is this whom Your Throne shades? So He said: This one was good to his parents and did not spread gossip.

Ja'far b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. 'Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. 'Ali narrated to me from his grandfather 'Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: I am astonished at the one who avoids food in fear of disease — how does he not avoid sins in fear of the Fire!

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. 'Imran al-Ash'ari from Muhammad b. 'Ali from 'Isa b. 'Abdullah al-'Alawi al-'Amri from his father from his forefathers from 'Ali (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: O Allah, have mercy on my vicegerents — three times. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, who are your vicegerents? He said: Those who convey my narrations and my Sunna, then teach them to my Nation.

'Ali b. Ahmad b. 'Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi 'Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi 'Abdullah from Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Qurashi from Muhammad b. Sinan from 'Abdullah b. Talha and Isma'il b. Jabir and 'Ammar b. Marwan from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'Isa b. Maryam (peace be upon him) went forth to fulfill a need of his, and he had three of his companions with him. He passed by three bars of gold on the road. So, 'Isa (peace be upon him) said to his companions: Surely, this kills people. Then, he continued walking. So, one of them said: I have a need. So, he left. Then, another one said: I have a need. So, he left. Then, the last one said: I have a need. So, he left. The three of them had gone to the gold. Two of them said to one: Buy us food. So, he went to buy food for them. He put poison in it so that he may kill them and not share the gold. The two said: When he comes, let us kill him so that we do not have to share. When he came, they went to him and killed him. Then, they ate, and they both died. So, 'Isa (peace be upon him) returned to them, and they were dead around it. So, he resurrected them by the permission of Allah the Exalted; then said: Did I not tell you that this kills people?!

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Safwan b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Abi al-Hazhaz from 'Ali b. al-Sirri. He said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying: Surely, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) placed the sustenance of the believers in places they do not expect. And that is because when a servant does not know the source of his sustenance, he increases in his supplications.

Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Hammad b. Isa, from al-Husayn b. al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: One silver coin earned in usury is more grievous in the sight of Allah than thirty acts of fornication, all of them with a mahram such as a maternal aunt or a paternal aunt.

Ali b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Qazwini, known as Ibn Muqbara, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us. He said: Jundal b. Waliq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Umar al-Mazini narrated to us from Abbad al-Kulaybi from Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from Ali b. al-Husayn from Fatima al-Sughra from al-Husayn b. Ali from his mother Fatima bt. Muhammad (blessings of Allah be upon them all). She said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out to us on the eve of Arafat and said: Indeed, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has dignified and forgiven you all in general, and Ali in particular. I am the Messenger of Allah to you and I am not one who favors his relatives. This Gabriel informs me that the truly happy one, the completely happy, the genuinely happy, is the one who loves Ali in his lifetime and after his death; and that the truly wretched one, the completely wretched, the genuinely wretched, is the one who hates Ali in his lifetime and after his passing.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya informed us. He said: al-Abbas b. Bakkar narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. al-Muthanna narrated to us from his uncle Thumama b. Abdullah from Anas b. Malik from his mother. She said: Fatima (peace be upon them both) did not see blood during menstruation nor during postpartum bleeding.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Mehran, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When death came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), he held me to his chest, then said: O my son, I advise you with what my father (peace be upon him) advised me when death came to him, and what he mentioned his father had advised him. He said: O my son, beware of oppressing one who has no supporter against you except God.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Whoever says "Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the greatest" forty times after every obligatory prayer before moving his legs, and then asks God, he will be given what he asked for.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Mukattab narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Damaghani narrated to us. He said: Yahya ibn al-Mughira narrated to us. He said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the night I was taken on my heavenly journey, Gabriel took my hand and admitted me into Paradise, and seated me upon a carpet from the carpets of Paradise. Then he handed me a quince, and it split into two halves, and there emerged from it a dark-eyed beauty whose eyelashes were like the front feathers of eagles. She said: 'Peace be upon you, O Ahmad. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. Peace be upon you, O Muhammad.' I said: 'Who are you, may God have mercy on you?' She said: 'I am the satisfied one whom Allah is satisfied with (al-Radiyya al-Mardiyya). The Powerful created me from three substances: my lower part is from musk, my upper part is from camphor, and my middle is from ambergris, and I was kneaded with the water of life. The Majestic said: Be! And I became. I was created for your cousin, your deputy, and your vizier, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).'

Al-Husayn b. Ali b. Shu'ayb al-Jawhari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: al-Fadl b. al-Saqr al-Abdi narrated to us. He said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us from al-A'mash from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went out wearing a khamisa, having wrapped himself in it. So it was said: O Messenger of Allah, who clothed you in this khamisa? He said: My beloved and my elect, my special one and my pure one, the one who fulfills on my behalf, my deputy, my inheritor, and my brother; the first of the believers to embrace Islam, the sincerest of them in faith, and the most generous of people in giving; the Master of the people after me, the Leader of the shining radiant believers, the Imam of the people of the Earth — Ali b. Abi Talib clothed me in it. Then he did not cease weeping until the pebbles became wet from his tears, out of longing for him.

14 - Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim. He said: Abu al-Salt Abd al-Salam ibn Salih narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to me, from Sufyan, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Habib ibn al-Jahm. He said: When Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) departed with us to the land of Siffin, he stopped in a village called Sanduda'. Then he ordered us and we turned away from it. Then he encamped with us at night in a barren land. So Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar rose and said: O Commander of the Faithful, do you make the people camp without water?! He said: O Malik, indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, will give us to drink in this place water sweeter than honey, softer than pure butter, colder than snow, and clearer than ruby. So we were amazed, though there is no amazement at the words of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). Then he came forward dragging his cloak, with his sword in his hand, until he stood on the barren land. He said: O Malik, dig - you and your companions. So Malik said: We dug and found a great black rock with a ring gleaming like silver. He said to us: Try to move it. So we tried with all of us - and we were a hundred men - but we could not move it from its place. Then the Commander of the Faithful drew near, raising his hand to the sky in supplication, saying: Tab tab Marya Alam tibu Thabutha Shamthiya Kuba Hahanu Thatu Dithabar Hutha - Amen, amen, O Lord of the Worlds, Lord of Musa and Harun. Then he seized it and hurled it forty cubits from the spring. Malik ibn al-Harith al-Ashtar said: Water appeared to us, sweeter than honey, colder than snow, and clearer than ruby. We drank and gave others to drink. Then he replaced the rock and ordered us to heap earth upon it. Then he departed. We had not gone far when he said: Which of you knows the location of the spring? We said: All of us, O Commander of the Faithful. So we returned and searched for the spring, but its location was hidden from us most extremely. We thought that the Commander of the Faithful was overcome by thirst, so we looked around and found the hermitage of a monk. We approached it and found a monk whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes from old age. We said: O monk, do you have water with which we might give our ma

Narrated to us Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani (may Allah have mercy on him), he said: Narrated to us Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan, he said: Narrated to us Bakr b. 'Abdullah b. Habib, he said: Narrated to us al-Fadl b. al-Saqr al-'Abdi, he said: Narrated to us Abu Mu'awiya, from Sulayman b. Mihran al-A'mash, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father Muhammad b. 'Ali, from his father 'Ali b. al-Husayn (upon them be peace), he said: We are the Imams of the Muslims, and the Proofs of Allah over the worlds, and the chiefs of the believers, and the leaders of the shining and distinguished ones, and the masters of the believers. We are a safeguard for the people of the earth, just as the stars are a safeguard for the people of the sky. We are those through whom Allah holds up the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission, and through us He holds the earth from shaking with its people, and through us He sends down the rain, and through us He spreads mercy, and He brings out the blessings of the earth. Had it not been for what is on the earth of us, it would have caved in with its people. He (upon him be peace) said: And the earth has not been empty since Allah created Adam of a Proof of Allah upon it, apparent and known, or hidden and concealed, and it will not be empty until the Hour rises of a Proof of Allah upon it. Had it not been for that, Allah would not be worshiped. Sulayman said: So I said to al-Sadiq (upon him be peace): Then how will the people benefit from the hidden and concealed Proof? He said: Just as they benefit from the sun when clouds conceal it (1).

The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far recited to us, attributed to one of them: "The wise scholar is the son of himself, His kind of knowledge has made him needless of his lineage. How vast is the difference between one whom you honor for the sake of others, And one whom you honor for his own sake."

A hadith narrated through a chain: The venerable Sheikh Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhawayh al-Mu'addib (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn Jafar ibn Jami al-Himyari narrated to us, from his father, saying: Yaqub ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umar, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When thirty years had passed for Isa (peace be upon him), Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him to the Children of Israel. Iblis (may Allah curse him) met him at the mountain pass of Bayt al-Maqdis — the pass of Afiq — and said: O Isa, are you not the one whose lordship is so great that you came into being without a father? Isa replied: Rather, the greatness belongs to Him who brought me into being; likewise He created Adam and Eve. Iblis said: O Isa, are you not the one who spoke in the cradle as a baby? Isa said: Rather, greatness belongs to Him who made me speak in my infancy. Iblis said: Are you not the one who fashions birds from clay? Isa said: Rather, greatness belongs to Him who created me. Iblis said: Are you not the one who heals the sick? Isa (peace be upon him) said: Rather, the greatness belongs to Him who heals them by His permission, and if He wills He causes me to be sick. Iblis said: Are you not the one who revives the dead? Isa said: Rather, the greatness belongs to Him who revives them by His permission, and inevitably He will cause to die what I have revived. Iblis said: Are you not the one who walks across the sea? Isa said: Rather, the greatness belongs to Him who tamed it for me. Iblis said: O Isa, there will come a day when heavens and earth and all therein will be below you, and you above all of it governing affairs and distributing provisions? Isa (peace be upon him) considered great this saying of the accursed disbeliever Iblis, and then he said: Glory be to Allah, filling His heavens and His earths, and the ink of His words, and the weight of His Throne, and the pleasure of His Self. Ibn Abbas said: When Iblis (may Allah curse him) heard that, he left in utter loss of self-control until he fell into the depths of the green sea. A woman from the jinn came walking along the seashore and found Iblis prostrate on a hard rock with his tears

Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abdullah b. Ja'far b. Jami' narrated to us from his father from Ibrahim b. Hashim from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Ibrahim b. Ziyad al-Karkhi. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah -- Blessed and Exalted -- will spread His mercy to the extent that even Iblis will hope for His mercy.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Muhammad b. Isma'il b. Bazi' from Abdullah b. Uthman from al-Husayn b. Mihran from Ishaq b. Ghalib from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever is ill-mannered has tormented himself.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Muhammad b. Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Layla from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever has been allotted foolishness, faith will be veiled from him.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: 'Abbad ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from his father Sulayman al-Daylami from 'Umayr ibn al-Harith from 'Imran ibn Maytham from Abu Sukhayla. He said: I went to Abu Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, and said: O Abu Dharr! I have seen discord, so what do you order me to do? He said: You must adhere to these two things: the Book of Allah and the Shaykh 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. For indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, saying: This is the first who believed in me, and the first who will shake hands with me on the Day of Resurrection. He is the Greatest Truthful One (al-Siddiq al-Akbar), and he is the Distinguisher (al-Faruq) who distinguishes between truth and falsehood.

`Ali b. Ahmad b. `Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from another person from al-Sadiq Ja`fa r b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: A man from the companions of Amir al-Mu’minin (as) had a doubt regarding his women. So, he (as) delivered a sermon and said: O people! Do not obey women under any condition, do not trust them with wealth, and do not leave them to run the affairs of families, for if they are left to do what they wish, they will want devastation and power, for we have seen that they have no piety with regards to their needs, and they have no patie nce with regards to their desires. Extravagance is a necessity for them, even if they have grown up. Astonishment follows them, even if they have grown old. They are not thankful for the many when they are prevented from the few. They forget good things, but they remember evil things. They are infatuated with the fleeting, they reach for defiance, and they defy on Satan’s behalf. So, turn away from them in every condition. Speak beautifully to them, and perhaps they will beautify their actions.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from `Abdullah b. `Abd al-Rahman al-Asm from `Abdullah al-B atal from `Amr b. Abi’l Miqdam from his father from Sa`id b. Jubayr from Ibn `Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) came out one day holding the hand of `Ali b. Abi Talib (as). He said: O people! O Bani Hashim! O Bani `Abd al-Mutalib! I am Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. Surely, I was created from a clay that four from my Ahl al-Bayt have been graced with: I, `Ali, Hamza, and Ja`far. So, a person said: O Messenger of Allah! Will these four be riding with you on the Day of Resurrection? So, he said: May your mother be bereaved with you! None will ride [on anything on] that day except for four: I, `Ali, Fatima, and Salih the prophet of Allah. As for me, I will mount the Buraq. As for my daughter Fatima, she will mount my she-camel, “the Muscular ”. As for Salih, he will mount the she-camel of Allah that was hamstrung. As for `Ali, he will mount a she-camel from the she-camels of Paradise – its reins will be of ruby, and it will wear two green garments. He will stop between Paradise and the Fire. The people will be sweating on that day, and a breeze will blow from the direction of the Throne, which will dry their sweat. The Angels of Proximity, the prophets, and the saints will say: “Who is this, other than an Angel of Proximity or a commissioned prophet?” So, a caller will call from the direction of the Throne: “O creation! This is not an Angel of Proximity or a commissioned prophet, but rather, he is `Ali b. Abi Talib, the brother of the Messenger of Allah in the world and in the Hereafter.”

My father `Ali b. Ahmad (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami from `Abd al-Athim b. `Abdullah al-Hasani from `Ali b. Muhammad b. `Ali b. Musa b. Ja`far b. Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as). He said: When Allah spoke to Musa b. `Imran (as), Musa said: My God! What is the reward of one who bears witness that I am Your messenger and Your prophet, and that You have spoken to me? He said: O Musa! My angels will come to him and give him glad tidings of My Paradise. Musa (as) said: My God! What is the reward of one who stands before You and prays? He said: O Musa! I boast about him to My angels when he is bowing, prostrating, standing, and sitting. I do not punish whoever I boast about to My angels. Musa (as) said: My God! What is the reward of one who feeds a poor person for Your sake? He said: O Musa! I will order My caller on the Day of Resurrection to call above the heads of the creatures: "So-and-so the son of so-and-son is from those freed by Allah from the Fire ." Musa (as) said: My God! What is the reward of one who connects with his blood-relative? He said: O Musa! I will give him harmony in his life, I will waive the pangs of death from him; and the treasury of Paradise will call to him: "Come to us and enter from whichever gate you wish." Musa (as) said: My God! What is the reward of one who abstains from harming the people and establishes noble virtues with them? He said: O Musa! On the Day of Resurrection, the Fire will call to him: "You have no way to get to me." He said: My God! What is the reward of one who remembers You with his tongue and his heart? He said: O Musa! I will shade him on the Day of Resurrection with the shade of My Throne, and I will put him under My auspices. He said: My God! What is the reward of one who relates Your wisdom privately and publicly? He said: O Musa! He will pass through the Path like lightning. He said: My God! What is the reward of one who is patient upon the harm and the insults of the people for Your sake? He said: I will assist them in the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. He said: My God! What is the reward of one whose eyes fill with tears out of humility before You? He said: O Musa! I will protect his face from the heat of the Fire, and I will protect him on the Great Day of Dismay. He said: My God! What is the reward

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab. He said: Al-Mughi ra b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. Khunays narrated to us from Abi `Abdillah al-Shami from Nawfal al-Bukali. He said: I went to Amir al-Mu’minin (s) while he was in the courtyard of the Mosque of Kufa. I said: Peace be with you, Amir al-Mu’minin, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. He said: And also with you, Nawfal, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. So, I said to him: O Amir al-Mu’minin! Exhort me. So, he said: O Nawfal! Do good, and good will come to you. So, I said: Give me more, Amir al-Mu’minin. So, he said: O Nawfal! Be merciful, and you will receive mercy. So, I said: Give me more, Amir al-Mu’minin. He said: O Nawfal! Say good things, and you will be remembered in goodness. So, I said: Give me more, Amir al-Mu’minin. He said: Avoid backbiting, for it is the treat of the dogs of the Fire. Then, he said: O Nawfal! One who alleges that he had a pure birth whilst eating the flesh of the people by backbiting has lied. One who alleges that he had a pure birth whilst hating me and hating the Imams from my descendants has lied. One who alleges that he had a pure birth whilst loving adultery has lied. One who alleges that he recognizes Allah whilst continually disobeying Allah every day and every night has lied. O Nawfal! Take my advice: do not be a captain, a corporal, a tax collector, or a postman. O Nawfal! Connect with your blood-relatives, and Allah will lengthen your life, beautify your form; and Allah will ease your Judgment. O Nawfal! Your joy would be to be with me on the Day of Resurrection, so do not be a helper of the oppressors. O Nawfal! Whoever loves us will be with us on the Day of Resurrection. Even if a man loved a stone, Allah would resurrect him with it. O Nawfal! Beware of adorning yourself for the people whilst battling Allah with your disobedience, for Allah would expose you on the Day you meet Him. O Nawfal! Maintain what I say to you, and you will achieve the best of this world and the Hereafter.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tajir narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mihran narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn Ilwan, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Badr ibn Abdullah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) saying: The best of deputies, the master of martyrs, and the nearest of people in station to the prophets will enter upon you from this door. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) entered. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: And why should I not say this, O Aba al-Hasan, when you are the keeper of my Pond, the fulfiller of my covenant, and the one who will discharge my debts on my behalf.

Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja`far al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrat ed to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Ahmad b. al-`Abbas and al-`Abbas b. `Amr al-Faqimi. They said: Hisham b. al-Hakam narrated to us from Thabit b. Harmaz from al-Hasan b. Abi'l Hasan from Ahmad b. `Abd al-Hamid from `Abdullah b. `Ali. He said: I carried belongings from Basra to Egypt and I placed it [there]. In one of the paths, I came across a tall elderly man who was very dark, bald, with white hair and a white beard, wearing two gowns – one white and the other black. So, I said: Who is this? So, they said:  This is Bilal, the mu'adhin of the Messenger of Allah (s). So, I took my tablets and gave them to him. I greeted him, then I said: Peace be unto you, O shaykh. So, Bila l said: And also with you. I said: May Allah bestow His mercy upon you. Narrate to me that which you have heard from the Messenger of Allah (s). So, Bilal said: Do you know who I am? He said: You are Bilal, the mu’adhin of the Messenger of Allah (s). So, Bilal and the man wept, until the people came to them and joined them in weeping. Then, he said: O boy! What country are you from? I said: I am from the people of Iraq. He said: Wow.  Then, he was silent for a moment. Then, he said: Write, O Iraqi brother. In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: “The mu’adhins are the trustees of the believers over their prayers, their fasting, their fle sh and their blood. They do not ask a thing of Allah except that He grants it to them, nor do they intercede in a thing except that their intercession is accepted.” I said: Tell me more, may Allah grant you mercy. He said: Write, in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: “Whomever sincerely gives adhan for forty years, Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection with the righteous and accepted deeds of forty saints.” I said: Tell me more, may Allah grant you mercy. He said: Write, in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I head the Messenger of Allah (s) say: “Whomever gives adhan for twenty years, Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection with a light like that of the sky.” I said: Tell me more, may Allah grant you mercy. He sai

My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Jamil b. Salih from al-Harith b. al-Mughira al-Nasri from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said: Whoever hears the mu’adhin say “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah” and says, in confirmation and expectation, “And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah”, it will be sufficient for him against all who reject and deny, and it will assist anyone who believes and testifies to it. He will receive a reward for every person who rejects, denies, believes, and testifies.

Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja`far al-Hamadani (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Salama al-Azhari narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: al-`Abbas b. Bakkar narrated to us. He said: `Abd al-Wahid b. Abi `Amr narrated to us from al-Kalbi from Abi Salih from Abi Hurayra from the Messenger of Allah (s). He said: On the Throne, it is written: “I am Allah. There is no god but Me. I am Alone without any partners. Muhammad is My Servant and My Messenger, and I have aided him with `Ali.” So, Allah revealed, “It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers.” [8:62] The “help” is `Ali (as), who [also] entered among the believers; so, he (as) is on both sides together.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Amir ibn Ma'qil, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: He said to me: O Abu Hamza, do not place Ali lower than where Allah has placed him, and do not raise Ali higher than where Allah has raised him. It is sufficient for Ali that he fights the people of the Return and that he weds the people of Paradise.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Ibrahim ibn Musa, the son of the sister of al-Waqidi, a shaykh of the Ansar, narrated to us. He said: Abu Qutada al-Harrani narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-'Ala' al-Hadrami, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu al-Hamra'. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the night of the Night Journey, I saw written on a pillar of the pillars of the Throne: 'I am Allah. There is no god but Me. I created the Paradise of Eden with My two hands. Muhammad is My elite one from My creation. I have aided him with Ali, and I have supported him with Ali.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, that he heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I have been given five things that were not given to anyone before me: the Earth has been made a pure place of prostration for me, spoils of war have been permitted to me, I have been supported by awe, I have been given comprehensive language, and I have been granted intercession.

My father and Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on them both) narrated to us. They said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa, from Musa b. al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Sama'a, from 'Abdullah b. Muskan, from al-Hakam b. al-Salt, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Take hold of the belt of this bald man - meaning 'Ali - for indeed he is the Greatest Truthful One (al-Siddiq al-Akbar), and he is the Distinguisher (al-Faruq) who distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Whoever loves him, Allah will guide him; whoever hates him, Allah will hate him; and whoever strays from him, Allah will destroy him. From him are the two descendants of my nation - al-Hasan and al-Husayn - and they are my two sons. From al-Husayn are the Imams of guidance: Allah gave them my knowledge and my understanding. So align yourselves with them, and do not take intimate allies from besides them, or else the anger of your Lord will descend upon you; and whoever has the anger of his Lord descend upon him, he will surely perish - and the life of this world is nothing but a deceptive enjoyment.

The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham b. Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us, from al-Hasan b. Mahbub, from Dawud b. Kathir al-Raqqi. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: Whoever attends the funeral of a believer until he is buried in his grave, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will assign seventy-thousand angels from among the attendants to attend his funeral and seek forgiveness for him when he comes out of his grave.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi'l Khattab, from al-Hasan b. Mahbub, from Ibrahim b. Muhzim, from Talha b. Zayd, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Pray over anyone who dies from the people of the qibla. His judgment is with Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us, from al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Faddal, from 'Ali b. 'Uqba, from Muyassir. He said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say: Whoever attends the funeral of a Muslim, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be given four intercessions. He will not say a thing except that the angel will say: 'And for you is something like that.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Hilal from al-Fadl ibn Dakin from Ma'mar ibn Rashid. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying: A Jew came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and stood before him, staring intently at him. So he said: 'O Jew! What is your need?' He said: 'Are you more virtuous, or Moses the son of Imran, the prophet whom God spoke to, who was given the Torah and the staff, for whom the sea was split, and who was shaded by the cloud?' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'It is disliked for a servant to praise himself, but I will say: When Adam (peace be upon him) committed the mistake, his repentance was that he said: O God! I ask You by the right of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad to forgive me. So God forgave it for him. When Noah (peace be upon him) boarded the Ark and feared drowning, he said: O God! I ask You by the right of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad to save me from drowning. So God saved him from it. When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire, he said: O God! I ask You by the right of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad to deliver me from it. So God made it cool and peaceful for him. When Moses (peace be upon him) cast his staff and felt fear in himself, he said: O God! I ask You by the right of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad to keep me safe from this. Then God, Majestic is His majesty, said: Fear not! Surely, it is you who is superior. [Quran 20:68] O Jew! If Moses were to meet me and then disbelieve in me and my prophethood, his faith would not avail him at all, nor would his prophethood avail him. O Jew! From my progeny is the Mahdi. When he appears, Jesus the son of Mary will descend to support him, and he will lead him forward and pray behind him.'

Abdullah ibn al-Nadr ibn Sam'an al-Taymi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Makki narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Atrush al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Salih ibn Ziyad Abu Shu'ayb al-Susi narrated to us. He said: Abu Thuman al-Sukkari - and his name is Abdullah ibn Maymun - narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Mu'izz al-Awdi narrated to us. He said: Imran ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Suwayd ibn Ghafla, from Tawus al-Yamani. He said: I passed by the Hijr and I found a person bowing and prostrating. I observed him, and he was Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). So I said to myself: A righteous man from the People of the House of Prophethood - by Allah, I shall seize his supplication! So I began watching him until he finished his prayer and raised the palms of his hands to the sky, and he began saying: My Master! My Master! These are my hands that I stretch out to You, filled with sins, and my eyes reach for You with hope. It is right for the one who supplicates to You with regret and humility that You answer him with bounteous generosity. My Master! Did You create me to be of the people of wretchedness, so that I may prolong my weeping? Or did You create me from the people of happiness, so that my hope may be delighted? My Master! Did You create my limbs to be stricken with rods? Or did You create my intestines to consume boiling water? My Master! If a slave were able to flee from his master, I would have been the first to flee from You; but I know that I cannot escape You. My Master! If my punishment were something that would expand Your sovereignty, I would have asked You for patience over that. However, I know that the obedience of the obedient does not expand Your sovereignty, and the disobedience of the disobedient does not diminish it. My Master! What am I, and what is my worth? Forgive my sins with Your grace, dignify me with Your covering, and pardon my reproach with the generosity of Your Face. My God and my Master! Have mercy on me when I lie in agony on my deathbed and my loved ones turn me over. Have mercy on me when I am laid out on the washing place and my righteous neighbours wash me. Have mercy on me when I am carried and my relatives take hold of the edges of my funeral bier. And have mercy on my loneliness, my estrangement, and m

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: In Medina, there was a foolish man who would make people laugh at him. He said: This man has exhausted me in trying to make him laugh -- meaning Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said: So Ali (peace be upon him) passed by, and behind him were two of his servants. The man came and snatched his cloak from his neck, then went away. Ali (peace be upon him) did not turn toward him. So they followed the man and took the cloak back from him. They brought it to him and placed it on him. He said to them: Who is this? They said: This is a foolish man whom the people of Medina laugh at. He said: Say to him: Indeed, God has a Day in which the invalidators will lose.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the people of religion have signs by which they are known: truthfulness of speech, fulfilling the trust, loyalty to the covenant, maintaining kinship ties, mercy towards the weak, little intimacy with women, giving of good, good character, breadth of disposition, and following knowledge and what brings one closer to God, the Mighty and Majestic. Blessed are they and good is their return! And Tuba is a tree in Paradise, its root is in the abode of the Prophet (may God bless him and his family), and there is no believer except that in his abode is a branch of it. No desire for anything occurs to his heart except that branch brings it to him. Even if a rider hastening traveled in its shade for a hundred years, he would not exit from it, and if a crow flew from its bottom, it would not reach its top until it fell from old age. Indeed, in this, desire! The believer is occupied with himself, while the people are at ease from him. And when the night covers him, he spreads his face and prostrates to God, the Mighty and Majestic, with the noble parts of his body, supplicating the One who created him for the liberation of his neck. Indeed, be like this!

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Indeed, God -- blessed and exalted -- distinguished His Messenger (may God bless him and his family) with noble character traits. So test yourselves: if they are in you, then praise God, the Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him to increase them in you. He mentioned them as ten: certainty, contentment, patience, gratitude, forbearance, good character, generosity, protectiveness, courage, and chivalry.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi informed us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: When death came to al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), he wept. It was said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, do you weep when you hold such a position with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), and you have performed Hajj twenty times on foot, and you have divided your wealth with your Lord three times -- even to the sandals? He (peace be upon him) said: I weep only for two reasons: the horror of the overlooking [of the Hereafter], and separation from loved ones.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Furat ibn Ibrahim ibn Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Thahir narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, the nephew of Yunus al-Baghdadi, narrated to us in Baghdad. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Nahshili narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida narrated to us from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), from Gabriel, from Michael, from Israfil, from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, that He said: I am Allah, there is no god but Me. I created the creation with My power. I selected from among them whomever I wished from My prophets, and I selected from all of them Muhammad as My Beloved, My Friend, and My Chosen One. I sent him as a messenger to My creation. I chose Ali for him, and I made him his brother, his successor, his vizier, and his representative to My creation after him. He is My vicegerent over My servants, so that he may clarify My Book to them and govern among them by My judgment. I made him the guiding sign from misguidance, My gate from which I am approached, My house — whoever enters it is safe from My Fire, My fortress — whoever seeks refuge in it is protected from the hateful things of this world and the Hereafter, My Face — whoever turns toward it, I shall not turn My Face away from him, and My proof in the heavens and the earths over all of My creatures therein. I shall not accept the deed of any doer among them unless they acknowledge his authority alongside the prophethood of Ahmad, My Messenger. He is My extended hand over My servants. He is the blessing with which I have blessed those whom I love among My servants. Whoever I love among My servants and take as a guardian, I make him recognize his authority and his knowledge. Whoever I hate among My servants, I hate him for his turning away from his knowledge and his authority. By My Might I have sworn, and by My Majesty I have vowed: No servant from among My servants shall align with Ali except that I shall displace him from the Fire and enter him into Paradise; and no servant from among My servants shall hate him and turn away from h

The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Hammad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Ghiyath al-Marisi. He said: Abu Yusuf Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from Abu Hanifa, from Abd al-Rahman al-Salmani, from Hanash ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) called me and directed me to Yemen to make peace between them. I said: O Messenger of God, they are a numerous people and they are of age, while I am a young man. He said: O Ali, when you reach the top of the pass of Afiq, call out with your loudest voice: O trees, O clods, O soil -- Muhammad the Messenger of God sends you greetings of peace. So I went, and when I reached the top of the pass, I overlooked the people of Yemen, and behold, all of them were advancing towards me with spears raised, spearheads leveled, bows slung, and weapons drawn. So I called out with my loudest voice: O trees, O clods, O soil -- Muhammad the Messenger of God sends you greetings of peace. And not a tree, a clod, nor any soil remained but it trembled with one voice: And upon Muhammad the Messenger of God and upon you, peace! Then the legs of the people shook, their knees trembled, the weapons fell from their hands, and they came to me hastening. So I made peace between them and returned.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from Ahmad ibn al-Nasr, he said: Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Turayf from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata from Ali (peace be upon him), he said: Indeed, the Jews came to a woman from among them named Abda and said: O Abda! As you know, Muhammad has destroyed the pillar of the Children of Israel and destroyed Judaism. The elites of the Children of Israel have paid dearly for this poison for him, and they will give you a reward if you poison him with this sheep. So Abda roasted the sheep and gathered the leaders in her house. She came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) and said: O Muhammad! You know what is obligatory for me [as your neighbor]. The leaders of the Jews are present with me, so honor me with your companions. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went with Ali (peace be upon him), Abu Dujana, Abu Ayyub, Sahl ibn Hunayf, and a group of Muhajirin. When they entered and the sheep was brought out, the Jews covered their noses with wool, stood on their feet and leaned on their staffs. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to them: Sit down. They said: When a prophet visits us, none of us sit down, and we would hate for our breath to reach him with anything harmful. The Jews lied - may the curse of God be upon them. They only did that out of fear of the fumes of the poison and its smoke. When the sheep was placed before him, its shoulder spoke and said: Stop, O Muhammad! Do not eat me, for I am poisoned. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) called for Abda and said to her: What caused you to do this? She said: I said to myself: If he is a prophet, it would not harm him; and if he is a liar or a sorcerer, I would have relieved my people from him. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said: The Peace sends you greetings and says: Say: In the name of Allah, by which every believer calls, and by which every believer reaches glory. By His light which illuminated the heavens and the earth. By His power before which every arrogant tyrant submitted and every rebellious devil was vanquished - from the evil of poison, sorcery, and evil touches. In the name of th

Salih ibn Isa ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ijli narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Abu Nasr al-Sha'rani narrated to us in the mosque of Humayd. He said: Salama ibn al-Waddah narrated to us from his father, from Abu Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Asim ibn Damra, from al-Harith al-A'war. He said: While I was walking with the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) in al-Hira, we came upon a monk striking the bell. Ali said: O Harith, do you know what this bell says? I said: God, His Messenger and the son of His Messenger's uncle know best. He said: It strikes the parable of the world and its ruin, saying: There is no god but God, truly, sincerely. The world deceived, occupied, lured, and misled us. O son of the world, slowly! Beat by beat! Gathering! The world perishes generation after generation. Each day weakens a pillar. We wasted the enduring abode and settled in the perishing. We do not know what we neglected until we die. Harith asked: Do Christians know? He said: If they knew they would not have deified Christ. I went to the monk, he struck the bell, I recited word by word. He accepted Islam and said: I found in the Torah that among the last prophets there would be one who interprets the bell.

Salih ibn Isa al-Ijli narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Manda al-Isfahani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us. He said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Anas, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and two men from among his companions on a dark, gloomy night, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to us: Go to the door of Ali. So we went to the door of Ali (peace be upon him), and one of us knocked on the door gently. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) came out to us, wrapped in a woolen garment with another like it draped over him, and in his hand was the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said to us: Has something happened? We said: Good news. The Messenger of Allah ordered us to come to your door, and he is following. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came and said: O Ali. He said: I am at your service. He said: Tell my companions about what happened to you last night. Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah, I am embarrassed. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah is not embarrassed by the truth. Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah, I was afflicted with ritual impurity (janaba) last night due to Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah. I sought water in the house but could not find any. I sent al-Hasan one way and al-Husayn another, but they took long. So I lay on my back, and then a voice called from the darkness of the house: Rise, O Ali, take the pail and bathe. Then I found a pail full of water with a silk cloth (sundus) over it.
