So I took the pail and bathed, wiped my body with the cloth, and placed the cloth back on top of the pail. Then the pail rose into the air, and a drop fell from it onto my head, and I felt its coolness upon my heart. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Bravo, bravo, O son of Abu Talib! You have arisen and your servant is Gabriel. As for the water, it is from the river of al-Kawthar. As for the pail and the cloth, they are from Paradise. Thus Gabriel informed me, thus Gabriel informed me, thus Gabriel informed me.

Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali b. Asad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub b. Yusuf b. Hazim narrated to us. He said: Umar b. Ismail b. Mujalid narrated to us. He said: Hafs b. Ghiyath narrated to us from Burd b. Sinan from Makhul from Wathila b. al-Asqa'. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Do not display gloating over the misfortune of your brother, or else Allah will have mercy on him and cause you tribulation.

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Muhammad b. al-Marzuban narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Ja'd narrated to us. He said: Shu'ba narrated to us from Abu Imran al-Juni from Abdullah b. al-Samit. He said: Abu Dharr (may God have mercy on him) said: I said: O Messenger of Allah! What about a man who works for himself and the people love him? He said: That is of the immediate glad tidings of the believers.

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Amiri narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Isa b. Ubayd al-Sadusi narrated to us. He said: Sulayman b. Amr narrated to us from Abdullah b. Hasan b. Hasan b. Ali from his mother Fatima bt. al-Husayn from her father, peace be upon him. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Indeed, the rectification of the beginning of this nation is through asceticism and certainty, and the destruction of its end is through stinginess and wishful thinking.

Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Fadl al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Jafar known as Ibn al-Tibban narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Khalid al-Muqri al-Kisai narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Dahir al-Razi narrated to us from his father from Sad b. Turayf from al-Asbagh b. Nubata. He said: One day, we were gathered around Amir al-Muminin, peace be upon him, in the Mosque of Kufa, when he said: O people of Kufa! Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has loved you in a way that He has not loved anyone else, so He uplifted your place of prayer. It is the house of Adam, the house of Nuh, the house of Idris, the place of prayer of Ibrahim the Friend, the place of prayer of my brother al-Khidr, peace be upon him, and my place of prayer. This mosque of yours is one of the four mosques that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has chosen for its people. It is as if I see it on the Day of Resurrection wearing two white garments, resembling one in ihram, interceding for its people and for whoever prayed in it, and its intercession will not be rejected. The days will not pass until the Black Stone is placed in it. There will surely come a time when it will be the place of prayer of the Mahdi from my progeny, and the place of prayer of every believer, and there will not remain a believer on Earth except that he has been in it or his heart has yearned for it. So do not forsake it, and come closer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by praying in it. Desire to come to it for the fulfillment of your needs. For if the people knew the blessing that is in it, they would come to it from every region of the Earth, even if they had to crawl on ice.

Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Salama ibn al-Bara al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Ubaydullah al-Thaqafi Abu al-Abbas narrated to us. He said: Isa ibn Muhammad al-Katib narrated to us. He said: al-Madaini narrated to me, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: The minds of women are in their beauty, and the beauty of men is in their minds.

Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qushayri narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Harish Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon them all). Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And do not forget your share of the world" [28:77]. He said: Do not forget your health, your strength, your free time, your youth, and your vitality -- to seek the Hereafter through them.

Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Said narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mansur ibn Abi al-Jahm and Abu Yazid al-Qurashi narrated to us. They said: Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Jafar ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: My brother Musa ibn Jafar narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) took the hands of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and said: Whoever loves these two, their father, and their mother will be with me in my rank on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani and al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us together. They said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya al-Juludi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. Ali ibn Hakim narrated to me, from al-Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: If a creature of Mine who recognizes Me disobeys Me, I will make one who does not recognize Me rule over him.

Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Mukattib narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn Sa'id ibn Qalbuwayh al-Mu'addal in al-Rafiqah narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Kathir al-Tamimi al-Yamani narrated to us, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Harb al-Hilali, the emir of Medina, say: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) say: Wellness is a hidden blessing -- when you have it, you forget about it; and when you lose it, you remember it.
He said: I heard al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Wellness is a blessing that gratitude cannot adequately requite.

Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Mukattib narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Tayyib Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Durayd al-Azdi al-Umani narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas ibn al-Faraj al-Riyashi narrated to us. He said: Abu Zayd al-Nahwi al-Ansari narrated to me. He said: I asked al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Arudi, and said: Why did the people abandon Ali (peace be upon him), when his closeness to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was such, and his position among the Muslims was such, and his striving for Islam was such? So he said: By God, his light dazzled their lights, and he surpassed them at the choicest part of every watering place, and people incline more toward those who resemble them. Have you not heard the first poet when he says: "Every sort inclines toward its own sort. Do you not see the elephant befriends elephants?" He said: And al-Riyashi recited to us, regarding this same meaning, from al-Abbas ibn al-Ahnaf: "A questioner says: How did you two part? So I gave a reply that was fair. He was not of my sort, so I left him. People are of various sorts and inclinations."

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Durustawayh al-Farisi narrated to us. He said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us. He said: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us. He said: Shu'ba narrated to us. He said: Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to me from Anas. He said: I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Whoever fasts one day from Rajab out of faith and anticipation, Allah -- blessed and exalted be He -- will place between him and the Fire seventy trenches, the width of each trench being the distance between heaven and earth.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from his father from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever fasts the first day of Rajab in desire for Allah's reward -- Mighty and Majestic is He -- Paradise is made mandatory for him. Whoever fasts a day in its middle will be able to intercede for the like of Rabi'a and Mudar. Whoever fasts a day at its end, Allah -- Mighty and Majestic is He -- will make him from the kings of Paradise and he will intercede for his father, his mother, his son, his daughter, his brother, his sister, his paternal uncle, his paternal aunt, his maternal uncle, his maternal aunt, his acquaintances, and his neighbours, even if among them was one deserving of the Fire.

Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Qushayri informed us. He said: Al-Mughira ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir al-Kilabi al-Kufi narrated to us from Amr ibn Thabit from Jabir from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: My love and the love of my Ahl al-Bayt is beneficial in seven places whose horrors are tremendous: at death, in the grave, at the Resurrection, at the Book, at the Judgment, at the Scale, and on the Path.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from Isma'il ibn Mihran from Sayf ibn Amira from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Nakha'i from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the best of worshipers, so he said: Those who, when they do good, are gladdened; when they do evil, seek forgiveness; when given, are thankful; when tested, are patient; and when angered, forgive.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from his father from Zur'a from Sama'a ibn Mihran from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Any traveler who prays the Friday prayer out of desire for it and love for it, Allah -- Mighty and Majestic is He -- will give him the reward of one hundred Friday prayers of a resident.

Muhammad ibn Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever opposes Ali ibn Abi Talib after me is a disbeliever, and whoever associates partners with him is a polytheist. Whoever loves him is a believer, and whoever hates him is a hypocrite. Whoever follows his traces is an adherent, whoever wages war against him is a traitor, and whoever rejects him is in falsehood. Ali is the light of Allah in His lands, and His proof upon His servants. Ali is the sword of Allah upon His enemies, and the inheritor of the knowledge of His prophets. Ali is the exalted word of Allah, and the word of his enemies is lowly. Ali is the master of the deputies and the deputy of the master of prophets. Ali is the Commander of the Faithful, the leader of the radiant believers, and the Imam of the Muslims. Allah does not accept faith except with his wilaya and his obedience.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Yasar narrated to us from their fathers, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to one of his companions one day: O Abdullah! Love for the sake of Allah and hate for the sake of Allah, befriend for the sake of Allah and oppose for the sake of Allah, for the guardianship of Allah cannot be attained except through that, and no man can find the taste of faith -- even if his prayers and fasting are abundant -- until he is like that. The brotherhoods of people in your time have become mostly based on worldly matters; on that basis they show affection, and on that basis they harbor hatred, and that will avail them nothing before Allah. So he said to him: How can I know that I have befriended and opposed for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? Who is the friend of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that I should befriend him, and who is His enemy that I should oppose him? The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) pointed to Ali (peace be upon him) and said: Do you see this one? He said: Yes. He said: The friend of this one is the friend of Allah, so befriend him. The enemy of this one is the enemy of Allah, so oppose him. Befriend the friend of this one even if he killed your father and your son, and oppose the enemy of this one even if he is your father and your son.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us from his father from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi from Aban and other than him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: Indeed, I pray for mercy for three -- and it is their right to be prayed for mercy: a person dear to his community who is afflicted with humiliation after glory, a rich person who is afflicted with need after needlessness, and a scholar who is undervalued by his people and the ignorant.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: You will never be able to please all people with your wealth, so please them with your good character.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Yahya informed us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Nafi narrated to us, he said: Umayya ibn Khalid narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: I heard my father narrating from his father, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), that he said: I heard the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) saying: O Ali, by He who split the grain and created the living being, indeed you are the best of creation after me. O Ali, you are my deputy and the Imam of my nation. Whoever obeys you has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys you has disobeyed me.

1 — The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Salih ibn Isa al-Ijli narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Bukayr narrated to us. He said: 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad al-Muhalabi narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Hilal ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura. He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) one day, and he said: 'I saw wondrous things last night.' He said: We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what did you see? Tell us about it — may our souls, our families, and our children be your ransom.' He said: 'I saw a man from my community — the Angel of Death had come to take his soul, and his filial piety toward his parents came and prevented it from him. I saw a man from my community upon whom the punishment of the grave had been extended — his wudu (ablution) came and prevented it from him. I saw a man from my community who had been surrounded by the devils — the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, came and delivered him from among them. I saw a man from my community panting, surrounded by the angels of punishment — his prayer (salat) came and prevented them from him. I saw a man from my community panting with thirst — every time he approached a water pond, he was turned away — then the fasting of the month of Ramadan came, gave him drink, and quenched him.' 'I saw a man from my community — the prophets were seated in circles, and every time he approached a circle he was expelled — his ritual bath from major impurity (ghusl) came, took him by the hand, and seated him beside me. I saw a man from my community — before him was darkness, behind him darkness, to his right darkness, to his left darkness, and beneath him darkness, immersed in darkness — his Hajj and Umra came, brought him out of the darkness, and led him into the light. I saw a man from my community speaking to the believers but they would not speak to him — his maintenance of family ties came and said: O assembly of believers, speak to him, for he used to maintain his family ties — so the believers spoke to him, shook his hand, and he was among them. I saw a man f

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us, from his father, who said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): Inform me of the death of Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): He said: When his appointed time came, his term was fulfilled, and his sustenance was cut off, the Angel of Death came to him and said to him: "Peace be upon you, O one whom Allah spoke to." Musa said: "And upon you be peace. Who are you?" He said: "I am the Angel of Death." He said: "What has brought you?" He said: "I have come to take your soul." Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "From where will you take my soul?" He said: "From your mouth." Musa (peace be upon him) said: "How, when I have spoken to my Lord, the Majestic, with it!" He said: "Then from your hands." He said: "How, when I have carried the Torah with them!" He said: "Then from your feet." He said: "How, when I have trodden upon Mount Sinai with them!" He said: "Then from your eyes?" He said: "How, when they have not ceased gazing toward my Lord with hope!" He said: "Then from your ears." He said: "How, when I have heard the speech of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, with them!" He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to the Angel of Death: Do not take his soul until he himself desires it. The Angel of Death departed, and Musa (peace be upon him) remained as long as Allah willed after that. And he buried him in the grave, and leveled the earth upon him. The one who was digging the grave was an angel in the form of a human. That was in the wilderness. Then a caller called out from the sky: 'Musa the one who spoke to Allah has died! So which soul will not die?' And my father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his father, peace be upon them, that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, was asked about the grave of Musa ibn Imran, peace be upon him, where it is. He said: 'It is near the great road, by the red sand dune.'

Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali b. Asad al-Asadi narrated to us in Ray in Rajab in the year 347 AH. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Ayyub narrated to me. He said: Ja’far b. Sunaid b. Dawud narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me. He said: Yusuf b. Muhammad b. al-Munkadir narrated to us from his father, from Jabir b. Abdullah. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The mother of Sulayman b. Dawud said to Sulayman (peace be upon him): "O my son! Beware of sleeping too much at night, for one who sleeps too much at night will be destitute [of good deeds] on the Day of Resurrection."

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Zaydan and Ali b. al-Abbas al-Bajliyan narrated to us. They said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us. He said: Mu‘awiya b. Hisham narrated to us. He said: Shayban narrated to us from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas. He said: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, greying has hastened to you. He said: [Surat] Hud, al-Waqi‘a, al-Mursalat, and ‘Amma yatasa’alun have greyed me.

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Jarir and al-Hasan b. Urwa and Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Wahbi narrated to us. They said: Muhammad b. Humayd narrated to us. He said: Zafir b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Uyayna narrated to us from Abu Hazim from Sahl b. Sa'd. He said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Muhammad! Live for as long as you wish, for indeed you will die. Love whomever you wish, for indeed you will be separated from him. Do whatever you wish, for indeed you will be recompensed for it. And know that the honour of a man is his standing in prayer at night, and his glory is his independence from the people.

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Barda'i narrated to us. He said: Umar b. Abi Aylan al-Thaqafi and Isa b. Sulayman b. Abd al-Malik al-Qurashi narrated to us. They said: Abu Ibrahim al-Tarjumani narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Sa'id al-Jarjani narrated to us. He said: Nahshal b. Sa'id narrated to me from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) said: The nobles of my nation are the carriers of the Quran and the companions of the night [prayer].

Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ja'far al-Alawi al-Hasani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ali b. Khalaf al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Hasan b. Salih b. Abi al-Aswad narrated to us. He said: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us from Muhammad b. Qays. He said: When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) would come back from a journey, he would begin with Fatima (peace be upon her). So, he would visit her, and he would prolong his stay. Once, he went out on a journey, and Fatima (peace be upon her) made two silver bracelets, a necklace, two earrings, and a curtain for the door of the house, in preparation for the arrival of her father and her husband (peace be upon them both). When the Messenger of Allah came, he visited her. His companions stood at the door, not knowing whether they should wait or leave due to his prolonged stay with her. So, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went out to them. Anger could be seen on his face, and he sat at the pulpit. Fatima (peace be upon her) thought that the Messenger of Allah had only done that because of what he had seen of the bracelets, necklace, earrings, and curtain. So she removed her necklace, earrings, and bracelets, and took down the curtain. She sent them to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), and said to the messenger: 'Say to him: Your daughter sends her greetings to you and says: Put this toward the cause of Allah.' When he came to him and informed him, he (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'She has done it - may her father be her ransom' - three times - 'This world is not of Muhammad nor of the Family of Muhammad. Had this world been worth the value of a wing of a mosquito before Allah in goodness, He would not have given a disbeliever a drink of water from it.' Then he stood and went to visit her.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Yusuf b. Aqil, from Ishaq b. Rahuwayh. He said: When Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) arrived in Nishapur and wanted to depart from it toward al-Ma'mun, the people of hadith gathered around him and said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, you depart from us without narrating a hadith that we may benefit from?' He had been sitting in the howdah, so he raised his head and said: 'I heard my father Musa b. Ja'far say: I heard my father Ja'far b. Muhammad say: I heard my father Muhammad b. Ali say: I heard my father Ali b. al-Husayn say: I heard my father al-Husayn b. Ali say: I heard my father, the Commander of the Believers, Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) say: I heard Gabriel (peace be upon him) say: I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say: 'There is no god but Allah' is My fortress; whoever enters My fortress is safe from My punishment. When the caravan continued on, he called out to us: 'With its conditions, and I am among its conditions.'

Muhammad b. Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan b. Abdullah b. Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Abbas al-Tamimi al-Razi narrated to me. He said: My father narrated to me. He said: My master Ali b. Musa al-Rida narrated to me. He said: My father Musa b. Ja'far narrated to me. He said: My father Ja'far b. Muhammad narrated to me. He said: My father Muhammad b. Ali narrated to me. He said: My father Ali b. al-Husayn narrated to me. He said: My father al-Husayn b. Ali narrated to me. He said: My father Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) narrated to me. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: I and Ali were created from one light.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Anbasa, the freedman of al-Rashid, narrated to us, saying: Darim ibn Qubaysa ibn Nahshal ibn Mujamma al-Sanaani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both) narrated to us, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both), from the Prophet (may God bless him and his family), who said: God, Mighty and Majestic, created one hundred thousand prophets and twenty-four thousand prophets — I am the noblest of them before God, and this is no boast. And God, Mighty and Majestic, created one hundred thousand deputies and twenty-four thousand deputies — Ali is the noblest of them before God and the most preferred of them. Al-Shaykh [al-Saduq] said: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Baghdadi al-Warraq also narrated this hadith to me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad, the freedman of al-Rashid, narrated to us, saying: Darim ibn Qubaysa narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), from the Prophet (may God bless him and his family).

The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. al-Husayn b. Sa'id narrated to us from Suhayl b. Ziyad al-Wasiti from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Rabi' from Muhammad b. Sinan from Abu al-Agharr al-Nakhkhas. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: Fulfilling the need of a believer is better than one thousand accepted Hajj pilgrimages with all their rites, freeing one thousand slaves for the sake of Allah, and equipping one thousand horses in the way of Allah with their saddles and bridles.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Idris narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. 'Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Nahawandi from Muhammad b. Sulayman al-Daylami from his father. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Winter is the springtime of the believer - its night is prolonged, which helps him stand in prayer; and its day is shortened, which helps him fast.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya informed us. He said: Ahmad b. Isa narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad b. Abdullah b. al-Hasan from Zayd b. Ali, peace be upon him. He said: Whoever comes to the grave of al-Husayn, peace be upon him, recognizing his right, Allah will forgive his past and future sins.

Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Haytham narrated to us. He said: Abbad b. Ya'qub al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Anbasa b. Bijad al-Abid narrated to me. He said: When Isma'il b. Ja'far b. Muhammad died and we finished his funeral, al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) sat down and we sat around him. He was silent and downcast. Then he raised his head and said: O people! This world is the abode of departure, and an abode of crookedness, not of straightness. However, the departure from the beloved brings a burning that cannot be repelled and a woe that cannot be deterred. People are only distinguished by beautiful mourning and soundness of thought. Whoever does not mourn for his brother, his brother will mourn for him. Whoever does not send forth a child, then he himself will be the one who proceeds without a child. Then he (peace be upon him) recited the words of Abu Khirash al-Hudhali mourning his brother: Do not think that I have forgotten his covenant, but rather my patience, O Umaym, is beautiful.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Aban al-Ahmar from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), and his garment was worn out. So twelve silver coins were brought to him. He said: O Ali! Take these silver coins and buy a garment for me to wear. Ali (peace be upon him) said: So I went to the market and bought a shirt for him with twelve silver coins. I brought it to the Messenger of Allah, and he looked at it and said: O Ali! A shirt less than this would suffice me. Do you think its owner will take it back? I said: I do not know. He said: Go see. So I went to its owner and said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) has disliked this. He wants a garment less than this. Please take it back. So he returned the silver coins to me. I came with them to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). He walked with me to the market to buy a shirt. He saw a slave girl sitting on the road crying. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to her: What is your matter? She said: O Messenger of Allah! The people of my house gave me four silver coins to purchase a thing for them, but I lost them, and I do not dare to return to them. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) gave her four silver coins and said: Return to your family. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went to the market and bought a shirt for four silver coins. He wore it and praised Allah. He went out and saw a naked man saying: Whoever clothes me, may Allah clothe him with the garments of Paradise. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) removed his shirt that he had bought and clothed the beggar. Then he returned to the market and bought another shirt with the four that remained. He wore it and praised Allah. He returned to his house and suddenly the slave girl was sitting on the road. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to her: Why haven't you gone to your family? She said: O Messenger of Allah! I have delayed in returning to them and I fear that they will beat me. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to her: Walk in f

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from his father from Abd al-Rahman b. Salim from al-Mufaddal from Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: When a servant stands before his Lord, exalted be His majesty, in the middle of the night, prays four units of prayer deep into a dark night, then prostrates a prostration of gratitude after completing his prayer, and says 'Whatever Allah wills, whatever Allah wills' one hundred times, Allah, exalted be His majesty, calls to him from above him: 'O My servant! How long will you say: Whatever Allah wills, whatever Allah wills! I am your Lord, and the will is Mine. I have willed the fulfillment of your need, so ask Me for whatever you wish.'

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami narrated to us. He said: Uthman b. Isa narrated to me from Khalid b. Najih from Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Misery was discussed in his presence, so he said: Misery is in three things: in a woman, in a creature, and in a house. As for the misery of a woman, it is in the exorbitance of her dowry and the disobedience of her husband. As for the creature, it is in its poor behaviour and its prevention of riding its back. As for the house, it is in the narrowness of its yard, the evil of its neighbours, and the plenitude of its faults.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Adami narrated to me. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali b. al-Nu'man narrated to me from Ali b. Asbat from al-Hasan b. al-Jahm. He said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him); I said to him: May I be your sacrifice! What is the limit of reliance on Allah (tawakkul)? So he said to me: That you not fear anyone besides Allah. He said: I said: Then what is the limit of humility? He said: That you give to the people of yourself that which you would like to be given. He said: I said: May I be your sacrifice! I desire to know — how am I in your view? So he said: Look to how I am in your view.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) would say: The basis of a person is his heart, his intellect, his religion, and his chivalry -- that is, whatever he makes of himself. The days change, and all people trace back to Adam equally.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, who said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): Who are the Family of Muhammad? He said: His descendants. I said: Who are his Ahl al-Bayt? He said: The Imams, the appointed successors. I said: Who is his Itra? He said: The People of the Cloak. I said: Who is his Umma? He said: The believers who affirmed what he brought from God, Mighty and Majestic, those who hold fast to the Two Weighty Things which they were commanded to hold fast to: the Book of God and his progeny, his Ahl al-Bayt, from whom God has removed uncleanliness and purified with a thorough purification. And these two are the vicegerents over the nation after the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).

11 - My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah and 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. They said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us from Muhammad b. Khalid al-Barqi from Ahmad b. Yazid al-Nishapuri. He said: 'Umar b. Ibrahim al-Hashimi narrated to me from 'Abd al-Malik b. 'Umayr from Usayd b. Safwan, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: When it was the day that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) passed away, the place was jolted with weeping, and the people were stunned just like the day the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away. A weeping man came hurrying, saying 'inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' [to Allah we belong and to Him we return], and he was saying: 'Today, the vicegerency of prophethood has been cut off.' Then he stood at the door of the house that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was in, and he said: May Allah have mercy on you, O Abu al-Hasan. You were the first of the people to enter Islam, the sincerest of them in faith, the most intense of them in certainty, the most God-fearing of them before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the greatest of them in effort, the most prudent of them over the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the most protective over his companions, the best of them in virtues, the most honoured of them in precedent, the highest of them in rank, the nearest of them to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the most similar to him in guidance, character, demeanor, and action, the most noble of them in status, and the most honoured to him. So may Allah reward you with goodness on behalf of Islam, His Messenger, and the Muslims. You were strengthened when his companions became weak, you emerged when they settled down, you rose when they languished, and you adhered to the path of His Messenger when they were his companions. You were truly his vicegerent—you did not quarrel nor plead despite the hypocrites, the anger of disbelievers, the hatred of enviers, and the malice of transgressors. You established the matter when they failed, you spoke when they stuttered, and you proceeded with the light of Allah when they halted—so they followed you and were guided. You were the quietest of them in voice, the highest in surpassing, the least of them in speech, the most corr

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Ishaq al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Abu Uruba al-Husayn b. Abi Ma'shar al-Harrani and Abu Talib b. Abi Awana informed me. They said: Abu Dawud Sulayman b. Sayf al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Waqid narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz al-Majashun, from Muhammad b. al-Munkadir, from Jabir b. Abdullah. He said: The angels were made happy on the Day of Badr and Hunayn when Ali (peace be upon him) cleared the brigades from before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). So whoever is not made happy by the sight of Ali (peace be upon him), then the curse of Allah is upon him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Dinuri narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Nishapuri informed me, he said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Maruzi narrated to us, he said: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, he said: Awf ibn Abi Jamila narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Hind al-Jamali, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Whenever I would ask the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), he would answer me; and whenever I was silent, he would begin speaking to me.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bishr narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn al-Haytham narrated to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, that whenever he would narrate to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), he would say: The best of the Ja'fars, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), narrated to me.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mu'addab narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bishr narrated to me. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Haytham narrated to us from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari. He said: Whenever Ali ibn Ghurab narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, he would say: The Truthful One about Allah, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), narrated to us.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ammar al-Jarudi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu al-Haytham, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted, will raise a group of people whose faces are of light, upon seats of light, wearing garments of light, in the shade of the Throne, at the rank of the prophets yet they are not prophets, and at the rank of the martyrs yet they are not martyrs. So a man said: Am I from them, O Messenger of God? He said: No. Another said: Am I from them, O Messenger of God? He said: No. It was said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? He placed his hand upon the head of Ali (peace be upon him) and said: This one and his Shi'a.

The esteemed elder Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Razi -- and his name is Abdullah b. Ahmad -- narrated to me from Sajjada -- and his name is al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Uthman, and the name of Abu Uthman is Habib -- from Muhammad b. Abi Hamza from Mu'awiya b. Wahb from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: A wise man sought another wise man for seven hundred parasangs for the sake of seven words. When he caught up with him, he said to him: O you! What is higher than the sky, wider than the earth, richer than the sea, harder than stone, hotter than fire, colder than the bitter cold, and heavier than the stabilizing mountains? So he said to him: O you! Truth is higher than the sky, justice is wider than the earth, a rich soul is richer than the sea, the heart of a disbeliever is harder than stone, the greedy and possessive is hotter than fire, despair in the mercy of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is colder than the bitter cold, and slander upon the innocent is heavier than the stabilizing mountains.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Musa al-Khashab from Ali b. al-Nu'man from Abdullah b. Muskan from Zayd al-Shahham. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: Whoever undertakes a matter from the matters of the people and acts justly, opens his door, raises his curtain, and looks into the matters of the people, it is a duty upon Allah the Mighty and Majestic to secure him from fear on the Day of Resurrection and to admit him into Paradise.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Salih ibn Abi Hammad narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wishes goodness for a people, He appoints for them a merciful ruler, and assigns to him a just vizier.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kamandani narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Mus'ab al-Hamadani. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: Fulfill trusts, even to the killer of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both).

My father, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: Fear God, and you must fulfill trusts to those who have entrusted you. For even if the killer of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) were to entrust me with something, I would certainly fulfill that trust to him.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Humran ibn A'yun, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He said: I heard the Master of Worshippers, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) saying to his Shia: You must fulfill trusts, for by He who truly sent Muhammad as a prophet, if the killer of my father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) were to entrust me with the sword that he used to kill him, I would fulfill that trust to him.

7 - Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi al-Hamadani al-Bazzaz informed us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us. He said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas. He said: When the family of Ya'qub was afflicted with what afflicted the people -- a shortage of food -- Ya'qub (peace be upon him) gathered his sons and said to them: O my sons, I have been informed that good food is being sold in Egypt by a righteous man who does not imprison people. So go to him and buy food from him, for he will be good to you, God willing. So they prepared and traveled until they arrived in Egypt. They entered upon Yusuf (peace be upon him), and he recognized them but they did not know him. He said to them: Who are you? They said: We are the children of Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful, and we are from Mount Canaan. Yusuf said: You are then the descendants of three prophets, yet you are not wise, and there is neither dignity nor humility in you. Perhaps you are spies for one of the kings who have come to my country. They said: O king, we are not spies nor men of war. Had you known our father, you would have honored us, for he is a prophet of Allah and the son of His prophets, and he is grieving. Yusuf (peace be upon him) said to them: What is the cause of his grief when he is a prophet of Allah and the son of His prophets, and Paradise is his abode, and he sees you in such numbers and strength? Perhaps his grief is only due to your foolishness, your ignorance, your lies, your scheming, and your treachery. They said: O king, we are not ignorant fools, and his grief did not come from us. Rather, he had a son who was the youngest among us named Yusuf. He went hunting with us and a wolf devoured him. Since then, he has been depressed, grieving, and weeping. Yusuf (peace be upon him) said to them: Are you all from one father? They said: Our father is one, but our mothers are different. He said: What compelled your father to send all of you? Could he not have kept one to keep him company? They said: He did -- he kept one, the youngest. He said: Why did he choose that one? They said: Because he is the most beloved to him after Yusuf. Yusuf said: I will keep one of

It is narrated in a report from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he said: Yusuf entered prison when he was twelve years old, and he remained in it for eighteen years, and he lived for eighty years after his release. That is one hundred and ten years.

On this same day, after the gathering, the virtuous scholar Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Muaddib narrated to us from Ahmad b. Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Abu Ghassan al-Nahdi narrated to us, saying: Yahya b. Salamah b. Kuhayl narrated to us from his father, from Abu Idris, from al-Musayyib b. Najabah, from Ali (peace be upon him) that it was said to him: Tell us about the companions of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family). Tell us about Abu Dharr al-Ghifari. He said: He learned knowledge and then sealed it, binding it with a tight seal. They said: What about Hudhayfah? He said: He learned the names of the hypocrites. They said: What about Ammar b. Yasir? He said: A believer filled to his very core with faith; he forgets, but when reminded, he remembers. It was said: What about Abdullah b. Mas'ud? He said: He recited the Quran, and it descended upon him. They said: Tell us about Salman al-Farisi. He said: He attained the knowledge of the first and the last, and he is an ocean that cannot be emptied, and he is from us, the Ahl al-Bayt. They said: Then tell us about yourself, O Commander of the Believers. He said: I was such that when I asked, I was given, and when I was silent, I was initiated.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi'l Khattab narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abi Ayyub from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: I heard him say: How beautiful are good deeds after sins! And how ugly are sins after good deeds!

My father narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi 'Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Harun b. al-Jahm from al-Mufaddal b. Salih from Sa'd b. Turayf from Abi Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: There are three types of injustice: an injustice that Allah will forgive, an injustice that He will not forgive, and an injustice that He will not neglect. As for the injustice that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will not forgive, it is associating partners with Allah (shirk). As for the injustice that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will forgive, it is when a man wrongs himself in what is between him and Allah the Mighty and Majestic. As for the injustice that Allah the Mighty and Majestic will not neglect, it is the ill-treatment among the servants.
And he (peace be upon him) said: What the oppressed takes from the religion of the oppressor is more than what the oppressor takes from the worldly goods of the oppressed.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn b. Sa'id, from Fadala b. Ayyub, from Yahya al-Halabi, from his father, from Abdullah b. Sulayman, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), that he said to a man: O so-and-so, do not sit with the wealthy, for indeed a servant sits with them while he sees that Allah has blessed him, but he does not stand up until he believes that Allah has not blessed him at all.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Mufaddal, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ‘And speak beautifully to the people’ [2:83]. He said: Say to the people better than what you would like to be said to you, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates the persistent curser, the habitual insulter, the frequent condemner of the believers, the obscene and the deliberately vulgar, the importunate beggar; and He loves the modest, the forbearing, the virtuous, and the self-restrained.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, who said: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: Acts of goodness (ma'ruf) protect against evil downfalls. Every act of goodness is a charity. The people of goodness in this world are the people of goodness in the Hereafter. The people of evil in this world are the people of evil in the Hereafter. The first of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise are the people of goodness, and the first of the people of the Fire to enter the Fire are the people of evil.

Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us in Rajab of the year 339 AH. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me in what he wrote to me in the year 307 AH. He said: My father narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, from Abu Jafar al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: In the Torah it is written, among what God, Mighty and Majestic, privately told Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): O Musa, fear Me in the secret of your affair, and I will protect you from behind your vulnerability. Remember Me in your solitude and in the pleasure of your delights, and I will remember you in your moments of heedlessness. Control your anger toward those I have given you authority over, and I will restrain My anger from you. Conceal the hidden part of My secret in your innermost self, and show courtesy in your public life on My behalf toward My enemy and your enemy among My creation. Do not cause Me to be insulted among them by revealing My concealed secret, lest you associate your enemy and My enemy in insulting Me.

Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Sad ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would say in his prostration: I whisper to You, O my Master, just as a servile slave whispers to his master. I request from You as one who knows that You give without diminishing what is with You. I seek Your forgiveness as one who knows that none forgives sins except You. I rely upon You as one who knows that You have power over all things.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sad ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Abu Hafs Amr ibn Khalid narrated to me from his brother Sufyan ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever seeks forgiveness from God, the Mighty and Majestic, seventy times after Asr, God forgives seven hundred sins for him that day. If he does not have any, then for his father. If his father does not have any, then for his mother. If his mother does not have any, then for his brother. If his brother does not have any, then for his sister. If his sister does not have any, then for the nearest relative, then the next nearest.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sahban, from Abu Imran al-Armani, from Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: There are people who, when something from the Quran is mentioned to them or they are told about it, one of them becomes so stunned that it seems as though if his hands and feet were cut off, he would not feel it. He said: Glory be to God! That is from Satan. They were not commanded to do this. Rather, it is only softness, tenderness, tears, and awe.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever prays the obligatory prayers at the beginning of their time and fulfills their rites, the angel raises them to heaven white and pure, and they chant to him: 'May God preserve you just as you preserved me, and may God entrust you just as you entrusted me to a noble angel.' And whoever prays them after their time without an excuse and does not fulfill their rites, the angel raises them black and dark, and they chant to him: 'You have wasted me! May God waste you just as you wasted me, and may God not take care of you just as you did not take care of me.' Then al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the first thing the servant will be asked about when he stands before God, exalted is His majesty, is the obligatory prayers, and about the obligatory zakat, and about the obligatory fasting, and about the obligatory Hajj, and about our wilaya, the Ahl al-Bayt. If he proclaims our wilaya and then dies upon it, his prayers, his fasts, his zakat, and his Hajj will be accepted from him. But if he does not proclaim our wilaya before God, exalted is His majesty, God the Mighty and Majestic will not accept anything from his deeds.

By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: When you pray an obligatory prayer, pray it on time like the prayer of one bidding farewell who fears he will never return to it again. Then direct your gaze toward the place of your prostration, for if you knew who was to your right and to your left, you would have perfected your prayer. And know that you are before Him who sees you while you cannot see Him.

13 - Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Ahmad Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Juludi al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya narrated to us. He said: Shu'ayb ibn Waqid narrated to us. He said: al-Qasim ibn Bahram narrated from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas. And Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us. He said: Abu Ahmad Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Juludi narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Mehran narrated to us. He said: Salama ibn Khalid narrated to us from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'They fulfill vows' [76:7]. He said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) became ill when they were young children. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) visited them along with two men. One of them said: O Abu al-Hasan, if you make a vow regarding your two sons, if Allah heals them. So he said: I will fast three days in gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Fatima (peace be upon her) said the same, and the two boys said: And we will also fast three days. Their maid Fidda said the same. So Allah healed them, and they began fasting, and they had no food. So Ali (as) went to a Jewish neighbour of his named Sham'un, who was a weaver of wool. He said: "Can you give me a bundle of wool for the daughter of Muhammad to spin? In return, I will give you three bushels of barley." He said: "Yes." So, he gave it to him, and he came back with wool and barley and informed Fatima (sa). She accepted them and spun one third of the wool. Then, she took a bushel of the barley, grounded and kneaded it, and baked five loaves from it - one for each person. Ali (as) prayed the sunset prayer with the Prophet (s), then he returned to his house and the five of them sat down. Ali (as) was the first to break bread when a beggar came to the door and said: "Peace be unto you, O Ahl al-Bayt of Muhammad. I am a beggar from the beggars of the Muslims. Feed me from what you are eating, and Allah will feed you from tables of Paradise." So, Ali (as) put the morsel down, and said: "O Fatima! You are glorious and certain in faith. O daughter of the best of all the people! Do you not see the desperate beggar, who came to the door hungry, complaining to Allah in poverty? He complained to us, starving and grieving. Every person

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ilyas, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Jahm. He said: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather. He said: I heard Abu Talib narrating from Abd al-Muttalib, who said: Once, while I was sleeping in the Hijr of Isma'il, I saw a dream that frightened me. So I went to the soothsayer of Quraysh, wearing a cloak of silk, and my hair flowing to my shoulders. When she looked at me, she recognized the change on my face, and she sat upright. At that time, I was the chief of my people. She said: What has happened to the chief of the Arabs that his colour has changed? Has something terrible from the vicissitudes of time troubled him? So I said to her: Indeed, this past night while I was sleeping in the Hijr, I saw as though a tree had sprung from my back. Its top had reached the heavens, and its branches had reached the East and the West. I saw a light shining from it seventy times greater than the light of the sun. I saw the Arabs and the non-Arabs prostrating before it, and every day it increased in greatness and in light. I saw a group from Quraysh wanting to cut it down, but whenever they approached it, a young man — the most beautiful of people in face and the cleanest in clothing — would seize them, break their backs, and gouge out their eyes. I raised my hand to reach for one of its branches, but the young man shouted at me: 'Stop! You have no share of it.' I said: 'For whom is the share when the tree is from me?' He said: 'The share is for those who have clung to it, and you shall return to it.' Then I noticed the colour of the soothsayer had changed. She said: 'If you have told the truth, a descendant of yours shall rule the East and the West and shall be raised as a prophet among the people.' Thereupon my worry lifted from me. Abu Talib used to narrate this hadith while the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had already appeared, saying: 'The tree was, by God, Abu al-Qasim the Trustworthy (al-Amin).'

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Muslim, the freed client of Banu Makhzum, from Sa'id ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard my father al-Abbas narrating, saying: When Abdullah was born to Abu Abd al-Muttalib, we saw a light in his face shining like the light of the sun. My father said: This boy will have an exalted matter. He said: I saw in my dream that a white bird emerged from his nostril, flew, and reached the East and the West. Then it returned until it perched on the roof of the Ka'ba, and all of Quraysh prostrated towards it. While the people were gazing at it in amazement, it became a light between heaven and earth, stretching until it reached the East and the West. When I woke up, I asked a soothsayer from Banu Makhzum, and she said: O Abbas, if your vision is truthful, there shall surely emerge from his loins a child whom the people of the East and the West will follow. Amina told me and said: When the labour pains seized me and the matter intensified, I heard noises and words that did not resemble human speech. I saw a brocade flag on a ruby pole that filled what was between heaven and Earth. I saw a light dazzling from his head that reached the sky. It was as though I saw the palaces of the Levant engulfed in light. I saw great birds spreading their wings around me. I saw Shu'ayra al-Asadiyya passing by and saying: O Amina! The soothsayers and idols will face much from your son! I saw a young man who was the tallest of the people, the fairest of them, and the most beautiful in clothing. I thought it was Abd al-Muttalib. He drew near to me and held the newborn, suckled him with his tongue. He had with him a tray of gold studded with emeralds and a comb of gold. He cut open his belly and took out his heart. Then, he split it open and extracted from it a dark black spot and threw it away. Then, he took out a green silk bag and opened it; in it was what looked like white powder and he filled the heart with it. Then, he returned it to its place and stroked his stomach. He bade him speak, and he spoke. I did not understand what he said except that he said: In the safety, protection, and care of Allah. I have fi

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sad ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him). He said: Seize the opportunity for supplication at five times: during the recitation of the Quran, during the call to prayer, when the rain falls, when two rows meet in battle for martyrdom, and during the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and the Throne.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talha al-Nahdi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Four are those whose supplication is never rejected, and for whose supplication the gates of heaven are opened and it reaches the Throne: the supplication of the parent for his child, the supplication of the oppressed against his oppressor, the supplication of the pilgrim until he returns, and the supplication of the fasting person until he breaks his fast.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: There is no one who is tested -- even if his test is severe -- who is more rightful to supplication than the one who is in well-being, who is not safe from being tested.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from his father from Wahb b. Wahb from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from Ali (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), when he saw a fresh fruit, would kiss it and place it on his eyes and his mouth, then say: "O Allah, just as You showed us its beginning in wellness, show us its ending in wellness."

Hamza b. Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim informed me from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Malik al-Juhni. He said: I gave Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) a fragrance. He took it, smelled it, and placed it on his eyes, then said: Whoever takes a fragrance, smells it, and places it on his eyes, then says: "O Allah, bless Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad," it will not fall to the earth before he is forgiven.

Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natana (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Ismail b. Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) taught me that whenever I put on a new garment, I should say: "Praise be to Allah who clothed me in fine clothing by which I beautify myself among the people. O Allah, make it a garment of blessing in which I strive for Your pleasure and build Your mosques." For whoever does that will not wear it except that he is forgiven.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad b. Isa from Abbas the servant of al-Rida from Abu'l Hasan al-Rida from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) would say: Whoever says, when he hears the call to the morning prayer: "O Allah, I ask You by the commencement of Your day, the passing of Your night, the attendance of those at Your prayer, and the voices of those who supplicate to You, to forgive me. Surely, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful" — and whoever says the like of that when he hears the call to the Maghrib prayer, then dies on that day or on that night, he will be a forgiven one.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to me, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever cuts out a new garment and recites 'Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree' (Surah al-Qadr) thirty-six times, and when he reaches 'the angels descend,' he takes out some water and sprinkles some of it lightly upon the garment, then prays two units of prayer wearing it and supplicates to his Lord, saying in his supplication: 'Praise be to God who has provided me with that which beautifies me among the people, covers my nakedness, and in which I pray to my Lord,' and praises God — he will continue to eat in abundance until that garment wears out.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Jafar narrated to me from Harun ibn Muslim from Masada ibn Sadaqa from Jafar ibn Muhammad from his forefathers (peace be upon them). The Prophet (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever sees a Jew, a Christian, a Zoroastrian, or anyone who is not upon the religion of Islam and says: 'Praise be to God who preferred me over you with Islam as a religion, the Quran as a Book, Muhammad as a prophet, Ali as an Imam, the believers as brethren, and the Ka’ba as a qibla' -- then God will never gather him with that person in the Fire.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever looks at one with a disability, or one who has been mutilated, or a person suffering from an affliction, then let him say secretly to himself without letting the person hear: "Praise be to God who granted me wellness from what He has afflicted you with, and had He willed, He would have done the same to me" three times, and then that affliction will never befall him.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) entered the mosque, and there was a group of people gathered around a man. He asked: "What is this?" They said: "An allama (a great scholar)." He said: "And what is an allama?" They said: "He is the most knowledgeable of the people in the lineages of the Arabs and their battles, the days of the Jahiliyya, the poems, and the Arabic language." So the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) said: "That is a knowledge whose ignorance does not harm and whose familiarity does not benefit."

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa‘d Abadi narrated to me, from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from al-Mufaddal b. Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja‘far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: Islam was built upon five pillars: prayer, zakat, fasting, hajj, and the wilaya of the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams from his descendants (blessings of God be upon them).

Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz informed me. He said: Abu Ahmad Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Farra' narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida narrated to me from his father Musa ibn Ja'far. He said: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq narrated to me. He said: My father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir narrated to me. He said: My father Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin narrated to me. He said: My father al-Husayn ibn Ali narrated to me. He said: My father Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon them) narrated to me. He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Faith is declaration with the tongue, recognition with the heart, and action with the limbs. Hamza ibn Muhammad said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim say: I heard my father say -- and he had narrated this hadith from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi, Abd al-Salam ibn Salih, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) with an identical chain of transmission -- Abu Hatim said: If this chain of transmission were recited upon an insane person, he would be cured.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Mubarak ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Islam is bare. Its garment is modesty, its ornament is faithfulness, its chivalry is righteous deeds, and its pillar is piety. Everything has a foundation, and the foundation of Islam is loving us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Nadr ibn Shuayb, from Khalid ibn Mad al-Qalanisi, from al-Qindi, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: A man came to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) and said: O Messenger of God, is everyone who says "there is no god but God" a believer? He said: Indeed, enmity towards us follows the Jews and the Christians. Surely, you will not enter Paradise until you love me, and he who claims that he loves me while hating this one — meaning Ali (peace be upon him) — has lied.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Thabit ibn Dinar, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): O Ali! I am the City of Wisdom and you are its Gate. The City can never be entered except through the Gate. One who claims that he loves me while hating you has lied, for you are from me and I am from you. Your flesh is from my flesh, your blood is from my blood, your spirit is from my spirit. Your secret is my secret, and your public is my public. You are the Imam of my nation and my vicegerent over it after me. Happy is the one who obeys you, and wretched is the one who disobeys you. The one who aligns with you has profited, and the one who opposes you has lost. The one who adheres to you has won, and the one who abandons you is destroyed. Your example and the example of the Imams from your descendants after me is like that of the Ark of Nuh: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever abandons it drowns. Your example is like that of the stars: whenever one star disappears, another star rises, until the Day of Resurrection.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Whoever sees his brother engaged in something he disapproves of and does not turn him away from it while he is able to do so, then he has betrayed him. And whoever does not avoid befriending a fool is close to adopting his character.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, established brotherhood between me and Ali ibn Abi Talib, and married him to my daughter above His seven heavens, and made His closest angels witness to that, and made him my deputy and vicegerent. So Ali is from me and I am from him; one who loves him loves me, and one who hates him hates me. And indeed, the angels seek closeness to Allah through love for him.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from Muhammad b. Isa b. Ubayd, from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman, from al-Hasan b. Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said: Surely, Allah -- Blessed and Exalted -- chose Islam as your religion, so beautify its company with generosity and beautiful character.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them).
