He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: An abundance of jesting takes away the dignity of one's face, an abundance of laughing erases faith, and an abundance of lying takes away one's radiance.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Ali ibn Ma'bad from al-Husayn ibn Khalid from Abi'l-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is a Muslim should not scheme or deceive others, for surely, I heard Gabriel (peace be upon him) say: 'Scheming and deception are in the Fire.'
Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever cheats a Muslim is not of us, and whoever betrays a Muslim is not of us.'

Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: Surely, Gabriel, the Trustworthy Spirit, descended upon me from the Lord of the Worlds and said: 'O Muhammad! Betake to good character, for surely poor character takes away the good of this world and the Hereafter.' Verily, the most resembling of you to me is the best of you in character.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Whoever prays a prescribed prayer, then glorifies [Allah] thirty times after it, no sin will remain on his body except that it will have shed.

Ja'far ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Ubayda al-Hadha' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: Captives were brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he ordered that they be killed, except for one man among them. The man said: 'May my father and mother be your sacrifice, O Muhammad! How did you release me from among them?' He said: 'Gabriel informed me from Allah, Mighty and Glorious, that you have five qualities that Allah and His Messenger love: intense jealousy over your women, generosity, good character, a truthful tongue, and courage.' When the man heard this, he embraced Islam and beautified his Islam, and he fought intensely alongside the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) until he was martyred.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Aziz b. Yahya al-Juludi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Atiyya narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Amr b. Sa'id al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Hisham b. Ja'far narrated to us, from Hammad, from Abdullah b. Sulayman -- and he was a reader of the scriptures -- he said: I read in the Gospel: O Isa! Be earnest in My command and do not languish. Listen and obey, O son of the pure, chaste virgin. You came into being without a male consort. I created you as a sign for the worlds, so worship Me alone and rely upon Me. Take the scripture with strength, go to the people of Syriac Syria, and convey to those before you that I am God the Eternal who shall never cease. Believe in the Prophet -- may God bless him and his family -- the unlettered one, the owner of the camel, the armour, the crown -- which is the turban -- the two sandals, and the rod -- which is the staff. He has wide eyes, a broad forehead, prominent cheeks, an aquiline nose, and well-spaced front teeth. His neck is like a silver jug, as though gold flows in his collarbones. He has hairs from his chest to his navel, but there is no hair on his stomach or his chest. He is tanned in colour, with a fine line of hair, and large hands and feet. When he turns, he turns with his whole body. When he walks, it is as though he steps firmly from a rock and descends a slope. When he comes among the people, he surpasses them. His sweat on his face is like pearls, and the fragrance of musk emanates from him. None like him was seen before him or after him. He is pleasant in scent, a marrier of women, with few offspring. His offspring is only from a blessed woman who has a house in Paradise, in which there is no clamour or weariness. He will care for her in the end times just as Zakariyya cared for your mother. She has two sons who will be martyred. His speech is the Quran, his religion is Islam, and I am Peace. Blessed is he who lives in his time, witnesses his days, and hears his words. Isa (peace be upon him) said: O Lord, what is Tuba? He said: A tree in Paradise that I planted, which shades the gardens. Its root is from Ridwan, its water is from Tasnim, its coolness is the coolness of camphor, and its taste is the taste of ginger. Whoever drinks from that spring one drink shall never thirst again. Isa (peace be upon hi

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Ahmad b. Dubays b. Abdullah al-Mufassir narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi al-Bahlul al-Marwazi narrated to us. He said: Al-Fadl b. Hurmuz Diyar al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Abu Ali al-Hasan b. Shuja al-Balkhi narrated to us. He said: Sulayman b. al-Rabi narrated to us. He said: I heard Kadih b. Ahmad saying: I heard Muqatil b. Sulayman saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: A man asked Ibn Abbas: What has Allah, blessed and exalted, concealed of Paradise, when He has already informed about its spouses, its servants, its good things, its drinks, and its fruits, and what Allah, blessed and exalted, mentioned of its affairs and revealed in His Book? So Ibn Abbas said: It is the Paradise of Eden. Allah created it on Friday, then He sealed it. No creature from the people of the heavens and the earth has seen it until its people enter it. He, the Mighty and Majestic, said to it three times: Speak. So it said: Tuba is for the believers. He, exalted is His Majesty, said: Tuba is for the believers, and Tuba is for you. Muqatil said: al-Dahhak said: Ibn Abbas said: So the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, said: [A believer is] only one who has six characteristics, then indeed he is among them: whoever speaks truthfully, fulfills his promise, fulfills his trust, is good to his parents, maintains his kinship ties, and seeks forgiveness from his sin - then he is a believer.

Abu al-Abbas Muhammad b. Ibrahim al-Talaqani, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad b. al-Qasim al-Anbari narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad b. Abi Ya'qub al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us. He said: It is narrated that A man came to Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have a need from you.' He said: 'Write it on the ground, for I can see hardship plainly upon you.' So the man wrote on the ground: 'I am poor and in need.' Ali, peace be upon him, said: 'O Qanbar, clothe him in two garments.' The man then stood up and recited poetry, saying: 'You have clothed me in a suit whose beauties will wear out, but I shall clothe you in garments of beautiful praise. If you have gained my good praise, you have gained a noble thing, and you will not find what you have gained wanting as a substitute. Indeed, praise keeps alive the memory of its bearer, like rain that brings life to the plains and the mountains. Never grow weary of a kindness you have begun, for every servant shall be recompensed according to what he did.' Ali, peace be upon him, said: 'Give him one hundred dinars.' It was said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, you have already made him wealthy!' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, say: Put people in their proper stations.' Then Ali, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed, I am astonished at peoples who buy slaves with their wealth but do not buy the loyalty of free people with their good deeds.'

Abu'l Abbas Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (rh) narrated to us. He said: Abu Ahmad `Abdillah b. Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Sa`id b. Bashir narrated to us. He said: Ibn Kasib narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Maymun al-Makki narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Muhammad narrated to us from his father from `Ali b. al-Husayn (as), that two men from Quraysh visited him, so he said: Shall I narrate about the Messenger of Allah (s) for you two? So, they said: Of course -- narrate to us about Abi'l Qasim. He said: I heard my father (as) say: Three days before the Messenger of Allah (s) passed away, Gabriel came down to him and said: "O Ahmad! Surely, Allah sent me to you to ennoble and honour you specifically. He asks you about that which He knows more than you regarding. He says: 'How do you find yourself, Muhammad?'" The Prophet (s) said: "O Gabriel! I find myself distressed. O Gabriel! I find myself in agony." On the third day, Gabriel came down with the Angel of Death. With them was an angel named Isma`il in the air, alongside seventy thousand angels. Gabriel (as) was before them, so he said: "O Ahmad! Surely, Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent me to you to ennoble and honour you specifically. He asks you about that which He knows more than you regarding. He says: 'How do you find yourself, Muhammad?'" He said: "O Gabriel! I find myself distressed. O Gabriel! I find myself in agony." So, the Angel of Death sought permission. Gabriel said: "O Ahmad! This is the Angel of Death, and he seeks your permission. He has never sought anyone's permission before you, nor will he seek anyone's permission after you." He said: "Grant him permission." So, Gabriel (as) granted him permission. He entered, came before him, and said: "O Ahmad! Allah has sent me to you, and He ordered me to obey you in what you command of me. If you order me to take your soul, I will take it, and if you would hate that, then I will leave it alone." So, the Prophet (s) said: "Would you do that, Angel of Death?" He said: "Yes. I was ordered to do that -- to obey you in what you command of me." So, Gabriel (as) said to him: "O Ahmad! Surely, Allah the Blessed and Exalted longs to meet you." So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: "O Angel of Death! Do what you have been ordered to do." So, Gabriel (as) said: "These are my last steps in this world. Surely, you were my only

14 - Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad b. Ishaq al-Madiri (1) narrated to us in Basra in Rajab in the year 318 AH. He said: Abu Qilaba Abd al-Malik b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Ghanim b. al-Hasan al-Sadi narrated to us. He said: Muslim b. Khalid al-Makki narrated to us. He said: Jafar b. Muhammad narrated to us from his father (peace be upon them both), from Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari, from Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: He said: Fatima (peace be upon her) said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family): O my father! Where can I find you on the Day of the Great Stand, the Day of Horrors, and the Day of Great Dismay? He said: O Fatima! At the Gate of Paradise, and with me is the Banner of Praise, and I am the intercessor for my nation to my Lord. She said: O my father! What if I do not find you there? He said: Find me at the Pond, where I give water to my nation. She said: O my father! What if I do not find you there? He said: Find me on the Path, where I am standing, saying: My Lord! Safeguard my Nation. She said: What if I do not find you there? He said: Find me at the Scale, where I am saying: My Lord! Safeguard my Nation. She said: What if I do not find you there? He said: Find me at the mouth of Hell, where I prevent its sparks and its flames from my Nation. So Fatima was gladdened by that — may the blessings of Allah be upon her, and upon her father, her husband, and her children (2).

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Basri narrated to us, he said: al-Mughira ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to me in the year 216 AH, he said: Qays ibn al-Rabi and Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abbad ibn Abdullah, he said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: No verse has been revealed from the Quran except that I knew where it was revealed, regarding whom it was revealed, regarding what it was revealed, and whether it was revealed on a plain or on a mountain. It was said: Then what was revealed regarding you? He said: Had you not asked me, I would not have informed you. This verse was revealed regarding me: "Surely, you are but a warner, and for every people there is a guide" [13:7]. The Messenger of God is the warner, and I am the guide to what he brought.

The venerable Sheikh, the jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Isam al-Kulayni narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni from Ali ibn Muhammad known as Allan from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rakhji. He said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) asking him about what Hisham ibn al-Hakam said regarding the body [of Allah] and what Hisham ibn Salim said regarding the form. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Leave the perplexity of the perplexed and seek refuge in Allah from Satan. The [correct] doctrine is not what the two Hishams said.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from al-Saqr ibn Dulf. He said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) about monotheism, and I said to him that I take the doctrine of Hisham ibn al-Hakam. So he (peace be upon him) became angry and said: 'What is with you and the doctrine of Hisham? Whoever claims that Allah is a body is not of us, and we dissociate from him in this world and the Hereafter. O Ibn Dulf! Surely, a body is generated, and Allah is its generator and its maker.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ali ibn Mahzayar. He said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them): May I be your sacrifice! Shall I pray behind one who claims the doctrine of the body and one who takes the doctrine of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Do not pray behind them, and do not give them from the zakat, and dissociate from them. Allah dissociates from them.

Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Wasil, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from his father. He said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both) when a man from the Khawarij came to him and said: O Abu Ja'far, what thing do you worship? He said: Allah. He said: Did you see Him? He said: The eyes have not seen Him through direct observation, but the hearts have seen Him through the realities of faith. He is not known by analogy, nor is He compared to people. He is described by His signs and known by His indicators. He does not oppress in His judgment. That is Allah, there is no deity except Him. He said: So the man left while saying: Allah is most knowing of where He places His message.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki. He said: al-Fadl ibn Sulayman al-Kufi narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Khalid. He said: I heard al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both) saying: Allah, blessed and exalted, never ceased to be Knowing, Powerful, Living, Everlasting, Hearing, and Seeing. I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, there are people who say that He, mighty and majestic, never ceased to be Knowing with a knowledge, Powerful with a power, Living with a life, Everlasting with a lastingness, Hearing with a hearing, and Seeing with a sight. He (peace be upon him) said: Whoever says that and believes in it has indeed taken other gods besides Allah, and has no part in our wilaya at all. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Allah, mighty and majestic, never ceased to be Knowing, Powerful, Living, Everlasting, Hearing, and Seeing by His Essence. He is far exalted above what the polytheists and the anthropomorphists say, greatly exalted.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammara, from his father. He said: I asked al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me about God — does He have pleasure and displeasure? He said: Yes, but not in the way that is found among creatures. Rather, the anger of God is His punishment, and His pleasure is His reward.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Asadi al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Indeed God, blessed and exalted, is not described with time, nor with place, nor with motion, nor with transition, nor with stillness. Rather, He is the Creator of time, place, motion, stillness, and transition. He is far exalted above what the oppressors say, greatly exalted.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Sabah ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, Hisham, Hafs, and others. They said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: We believe neither in fatalism nor in delegation.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Surely, Allah the Majestic revealed to this world: 'Tire those who serve you and serve those who reject you.' If a servant were to seek his Master alone in the darkness of the night and whisper to Him, Allah would secure the light in his heart. If he were to say: 'O Lord! O Lord!', the Majestic would call to him: 'I am at your service, My servant. Ask Me and I will grant you. Rely on Me and I will suffice for you.' Then He will say to His angels: 'O My angels! Look at My servant. He has sought Me alone in the darkness of the night while the idle ones are distracted and the heedless are asleep. Bear witness that I have forgiven him.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: Betake yourselves to piety, striving, and worship. Be ascetic in this world that is ascetic toward you, for surely it is deception — the abode of annihilation and evanescence. How many who were deceived by it were destroyed by it, how many who trusted it were betrayed by it, how many who relied on it were fooled and delivered to ruin. Know that before you is a dreadful path and a long journey. Your passage will be over the Bridge, and the traveler cannot do without provisions. Whoever journeys without preparing provisions will perish and be destroyed. The best provision is taqwa. Then remember your standing before Allah the Majestic, for He is the Just Judge. Prepare your answers to His questions, for He will surely ask you about how you treated the Two Weighty Things after me: the Book of Allah and my progeny. Beware of saying: 'As for the Book, we changed it and interpolated it; and as for the progeny, we abandoned them and killed them.' At that point, your recompense will be nothing but the Fire. Whoever of you desires to be delivered from the terror of that Day should align with my wali and follow my deputy and my vicegerent after me, Ali ibn Abi Talib — for he is the master of my Pond. He will repel my enemies from it and water my friends from it. Whoever is not watered from it will forever be thirsty and never be quenched. Who

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: A man came to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, inform me about noble character (makarim al-akhlaq). He said: Forgiving those who wrong you, maintaining ties with those who cut you off, giving to those who deprive you, and speaking the truth even if it be against yourself.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abdullah al-Sijistani, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both): He said: Whoever among the believers dies between the decline of the sun on Thursday and the decline of the sun on Friday, God will protect him from the pressure of the grave.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Anbasa ibn Bijad al-Abid, that a man said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both): Advise me. So he said: Prepare your belongings and ready your supplies for a long journey. Be an advisor to yourself, and do not depend on anyone else to send you that which will rectify you.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Bajali narrated to me. He said: Hammad ibn Waqid narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) that he said: Whoever says "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, glory be to Allah the Great" thirty times will receive riches, leave poverty behind, and knock on the gate of Paradise.

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), that he said: By Allah, Ali (peace be upon him) would eat the food of a slave and sit as a slave sits. He would buy two Sanbulani shirts and give his servant the better one, then wear the other. If the sleeve exceeded his fingers, he would cut it, and if it exceeded his ankle, he would shorten it. He ruled for five years without placing a brick upon a brick, nor a mud-brick upon a mud-brick, nor granting any land, nor bequeathing a silver or gold coin. He would feed the people wheat bread and meat, then return to his home and eat barley bread with oil and vinegar. Whenever two matters were presented to him, both pleasing to Allah, he would take the one that was harder on his body. He freed a thousand slaves from the toil of his own hands, by which his hands became dusty and his face sweated. No one among the people could bear his deeds, even as he would pray a thousand units of prayer day and night. The person who most resembled him was Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), yet no one among the people could bear his deeds after him.

A man from the Tabi'in heard Anas ibn Malik saying: This verse was revealed regarding Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): "Is the one who is devoutly obedient in the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord?" The man said: So I went to Ali (peace be upon him) to observe his worship. I swear by God, I came to him at Maghrib time and found him leading his companions in Maghrib prayer. When he finished it, he sat in supplication until he stood for the final Isha prayer. Then he entered his house, and I entered with him. I found him praying and reciting the Quran throughout the entire night until dawn. Then he renewed his ablution, went out to the mosque, and led the people in Fajr prayer. Then he sat in supplication until sunrise. Then the people came to him, and two men at a time would bring their disputes before him; whenever one pair finished, another two would come, until he stood for the Dhuhr prayer. He said: Then he renewed his ablution for Dhuhr and led his companions in Dhuhr prayer. Then he sat in supplication until he led them in Asr prayer. Then the people came to him, and two men would stand while two others sat; he judged between them and gave them edicts until sunset. Then I went out saying: I swear by God that this verse was revealed regarding him.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever feeds a hungry believer, God will feed him from the fruits of Paradise. Whoever clothes him from his nakedness, God will clothe him in brocade and silk. Whoever gives him a drink when he is thirsty, God will give him the sealed nectar to drink. And whoever assists him or alleviates his distress, God will shade him under the shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His shade.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Whenever the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was brought wealth, he would place it in the treasury of the Muslims. Then he would gather those entitled to it. Then he would thrust his hand into the wealth and scatter it to the right and left, saying: O gold! O silver! Do not deceive me -- deceive someone else. This is my harvest and the best of it is in it, since every harvester brings his hand to his own mouth. Then he would not leave until he had distributed everything in the treasury of the Muslims and given every person their due right. Then he would order it to be swept and sprinkled with water. Then he would pray two units of prayer in it. Then he would divorce the worldly life three times, saying after the taslim: O worldly life! Do not present yourself to me, do not make me long for you, and do not deceive me, for I have divorced you three times with no return.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu'l-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he was asked: What is the intellect? He said: Suppressing grief, speaking gently to enemies, and showing kindness to friends.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ashari, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Said al-Azdi, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Sabbah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will gather the former and the latter peoples on a single plain, and an intense darkness will cover them. They will cry out to their Lord saying: O Lord, remove this darkness from us! He said: Then a people will come forward with light walking before them, having illuminated the ground of the Resurrection. The people of the gathering will say: These are the prophets of God! Then the call will come from God: These are not prophets. The people of the gathering will say: Then these are angels! The call will come from God: These are not angels. The people of the gathering will say: These are martyrs! The call will come from God: These are not martyrs. They will say: Who are they? The call will come: O people of the gathering, ask them who they are! The people of the gathering will say: Who are you? They will say: We are the Alids. We are the progeny of Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family. We are the children of Ali, the friend of God. We are the ones singled out by the honor of God. We are the safe and assured ones. Then the call will come to them from God, the Mighty and Majestic: Intercede for your lovers, the people of your affection, and your Shia! So they will intercede, and their intercession will be accepted.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us. He said: Salama ibn al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Tasnim al-Warraq narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir from his father from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions one day: O my companions! Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — commands you to the wilaya of Ali ibn Abi Talib and to follow his example. He is your master and your Imam after me. Do not oppose him, lest you disbelieve; and do not separate from him, lest you go astray. Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — has made Ali a sign distinguishing between faith and hypocrisy: whoever loves him is a believer, and whoever hates him is a hypocrite. Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — has made Ali my designated successor, the beacon of guidance after me, the repository of my secret, the treasury of my knowledge, and my vicegerent among my family. I complain to God about those from my nation who will oppress him after me.

The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Iblis (may God curse him) used to penetrate the seven heavens. When Isa (peace be upon him) was born, he was blocked from three heavens, and he would instead penetrate four heavens. When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was born, he was blocked from all seven, and the devils were pelted with stars. Quraysh said: 'This is the Hour that we used to hear the people of the scriptures mention.' Amr ibn Umayya, who was among the most rebuked of the people of Jahiliyya, said: 'Look at these stars by which people are guided and by which the seasons of winter and summer are known. If they have been thrown, then that is the destruction of everything. But if they have remained and other things were thrown, then it is a new matter that has occurred.' On the morning of the Prophet's birth, all the idols had fallen on their faces. That night, the Iwan of Khosrow shook and fourteen battlements fell. Lake Sawa receded, the valley of Samawa flooded, the fires of Persia were extinguished after a thousand years. The Mobed dreamt of unruly camels leading Arabian horses across the Tigris. The arch of Khosrow cracked, the Tigris burst. A light spread from the Hijaz to the East. Every king's throne was overturned and kings were silenced. Soothsayers lost their knowledge, sorcerers' magic was nullified. Quraysh was glorified and called 'the Family of God.' Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: They were only called the Family of God because they were in the Sacred House of God. Amina said: My son, by God, was born and upheld himself on the ground with his hand. Then he raised his head to the sky and looked at it. Then a light came out from me that illuminated everything, and I heard a speaker saying: You have given birth to the master of mankind, so name him Muhammad. Abd al-Muttalib was brought to look at him. He took him and placed him in his lap and said: Praise be to God who gave me this pure boy who prevails over the

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (blessings of God upon them), from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), from Gabriel (peace be upon him). He said: God, Majestic is His Majesty, said: Whoever commits a sin, whether minor or major, and does not know that it is up to Me to punish him or forgive him, I will never forgive him that sin. And whoever commits a sin, whether minor or major, and knows that it is up to Me to punish him or forgive him, I will forgive him.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to me. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to me. He said: Ali b. al-Hakam narrated to me. He said: al-Husayn b. Abi al-Ala' narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Umm Ayman visited the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) and she had something in her coat. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said to her: What do you have with you, O Umm Ayman? She said: Indeed, so-and-so got married, and they sprinkled things upon her, and I took some of what was sprinkled. Then Umm Ayman wept and said: O Messenger of Allah, you married Fatima off but did not sprinkle anything on her. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: O Umm Ayman, why do you speak falsely? For indeed, when Allah, blessed and exalted, married Fatima to Ali, He ordered the trees of Paradise to sprinkle upon them from their jewels, garments, rubies, pearls, emeralds, and brocade, and they collected what they could not fathom. And surely Allah bestowed Tuba as the dowry of Fatima and placed it in the house of Ali.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from al-Ya'qubi, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever would be pleased to traverse the Path like a strong wind and enter Paradise without reckoning, then let him accept the guardianship of my friend, my deputy, my companion, and my vicegerent over my family and my nation -- Ali ibn Abi Talib. And whoever would be pleased to enter the Fire, then let him abandon his guardianship. For by my Lord's majesty and glory, he is indeed the gate of Allah that cannot be approached except through him, and he is the Straight Path, and he is the one about whose guardianship Allah will ask on the Day of Resurrection.

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhawayh al-Mu'addab (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: May God have mercy on a person who helps his father in his righteousness. May God have mercy on a father who helps his child in his righteousness. May God have mercy on a neighbour who helps his neighbour in his righteousness. May God have mercy on a companion who helps his companion in his righteousness. May God have mercy on an acquaintance who helps his acquaintance in his righteousness. May God have mercy on a man who helps his ruler in his righteousness.

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Be good to your parents, and your children will be good to you. Be chaste regarding the women of others, and your women will be chaste.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara ibn Ayan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Indeed, we, the Ahl al-Bayt, our chivalry is the forgiveness of those who wrong us.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi. He said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): Which qualities are most beautiful in a person? He said: Dignity without intimidation, generosity without seeking recompense, and preoccupation with something other than the enjoyments of this world.

Ja’far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma’il ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever sleeps exhausted from seeking lawful sustenance, sleeps forgiven.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari. He said: Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to me from his father, from Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah b. Sinan, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from al-Hasan b. Ali (peace be upon them both) that he said: Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was asked: What keeps faith steadfast? He said: Piety. Then it was said to him: What causes it to decline? He said: Greed.

Ali ibn Hatim al-Qazwini (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Nahwi narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu Ayyub Sulayman ibn Muqbil al-Madini, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), that he said: When a believer dies, seventy thousand angels attend his funeral until he reaches his grave. When he enters his grave, Munkar and Nakir come to him, seat him, and say to him: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?" He says: "My Lord is God, Muhammad is my prophet, and Islam is my religion." Then they expand his grave as far as his eye can see, bring him food from Paradise, and let comfort and relief enter upon him. That is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "And if he was of those brought near, then comfort and relief" -- meaning in his grave -- "and a Garden of Bliss" -- meaning in the Hereafter. Then he (peace be upon him) said: When a disbeliever dies, seventy thousand angels of punishment attend his funeral until he reaches his grave. He cries out to his carriers in a voice heard by everything except humans and jinn, saying: "If only I had another chance, I would be of the believers," and saying: "Return me, so that I may do righteous deeds in what I left behind." The angels of punishment reply to him: "No! It is merely a word you are saying." An angel calls out to them: "Were he returned, he would go back to what was forbidden to him." When he enters his grave and the people leave him, Munkar and Nakir come to him in the most horrifying form and stand him up. Then they say to him: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?" His tongue trembles and he cannot answer. They strike him with a blow from the chastisement of God, by which all things are terrified. Then they say to him: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?" He says: "I do not know." They say to him: "You did not seek knowledge, nor were you guided, nor did you triumph." Then they open a gate to the Fire for him and bring down to him boiling water from Hell. That is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "But if he was of the denying and astray, then a welcome of boiling water" -- meaning in the grave -- "and burning in Hell" -- meaning in the Hereafter.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to me. He said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has three hallowed things that cannot be compared to anything: His Book, which is His wisdom and His light; His House, which He made the qibla for mankind - He does not accept from anyone turning toward other than it; and the progeny of your Prophet (may God bless him and his family).

Ali ibn Isa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Ilwan al-Kalbi, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree from whose top come garments and from whose bottom come piebald horses, saddled and bridled, with wings. They do not defecate nor urinate. The friends of God ride them, and they fly with them in Paradise wherever they wish. Those who are below them say: "O our Lord, what has brought Your servants to this honor?" God, exalted is His majesty, says: "Indeed, they used to stand in prayer at night and not sleep, and they would fast during the day and not eat, and they would fight the enemy without cowardice, and they would give charity without stinginess."

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: There are five things without which one will not find much satisfaction. It was asked: What are they, O son of the Messenger of God? He said: Religion, intellect, modesty, beautiful character, and beautiful manners. And there are five things without which one will not find comfort in living: health, security, wealth, contentment, and an agreeable companion.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Salama ibn al-Khattab al-Barawastani, from Muhammad ibn al-Layth, from Jabir ibn Isma'il, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both): A man asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) about night prayer (qiyam al-layl) with the Quran. So he said to him: Glad tidings! Whoever prays one tenth of the night for Allah sincerely, seeking the pleasure of Allah — Allah the Mighty and Majestic says to His angels: 'Record for My servant, among good deeds, a number equal to what grows in the night of seeds, leaves, and trees, and the number of every reed, branch, and pasture.' Whoever prays one ninth of the night, Allah grants him ten answered supplications and gives him his book in his right hand on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever prays one eighth of the night, Allah gives him the reward of a patient martyr with a sincere intention, and he intercedes for his household. Whoever prays one seventh of the night, he will emerge from his grave on the day of resurrection with his face like the full moon, until he passes over the Bridge with the safe ones. Whoever prays one sixth of the night, he will be recorded among the repentant (awwabin) and his past sins will be forgiven. Whoever prays one fifth of the night, he will gather with Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful (Khalil al-Rahman), in his dome. Whoever prays one quarter of the night, he will be among the first of the triumphant, until he passes over the Bridge like a raging wind, and he will enter Paradise without reckoning. Whoever prays one third of the night, not an angel will remain except that it envies him his station with Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and it will be said to him: Enter through whichever of the eight gates of Paradise you wish. Whoever prays half the night — even if he were given the earth's fill of gold seventy thousand times, it would not equal his reward; and that would be greater for him than freeing seventy slaves from the descendants of Isma'il. Whoever prays two thirds of the night, he will have good deeds in the measure of the sands of 'Alij, the least of which is a deed ten times heavier than Mount Uhud. Whoever prays a full night, reciting the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, bowing, prostrating, and remembering — he is given such reward that

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazim ibn Hakim, from Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Surely, the Trustworthy Spirit Jibril informed me from my Lord, Blessed and Exalted: A soul does not die until its sustenance has been depleted. So fear Allah, and beautify your pursuit of livelihood. And know that sustenance is of two types: sustenance that you pursue, and sustenance that pursues you. So pursue your sustenance lawfully, for indeed you will consume it lawfully if you pursue it through its proper channels, but if you do not pursue it through its proper channels, you will consume it unlawfully. It is your sustenance, and you cannot but consume it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Ali ibn Ma'bad from al-Husayn ibn Khalid from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, peace be upon him. He said: Looking at our offspring is worship. So, it was said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! Is looking at the Imams from among you worship, or looking at all the offspring of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family? So, he said: Rather, looking at all the offspring of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, is worship.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us from Khalid al-Qalanisi from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said: When I rise to the Praiseworthy Station, I will intercede for those who have committed major sins from my Nation; so God will accept my intercession for them. By God, I will not intercede for those who harm my offspring.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sama'a ibn Mehran from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him. He said: When a worshiper's sins have increased and he does not find anything to atone for them, God, Mighty and Majestic, afflicts him with grief in this world to atone them. Then, if that suffices, otherwise He ails his body to atone them. Then, if that suffices, otherwise He intensifies his death to atone them. Then, if that suffices, otherwise He punishes him in his grave so that he may meet God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day he meets Him with nothing testifying against him for any of his sins.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us from his father. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: Whoever denies three things is not of our Shi'a: the Ascension (mi'raj), the questioning in the grave, and the intercession.

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father. He said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us from Hisham ibn Salim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him. He said: Poverty nearly becomes disbelief, and envy nearly overcomes destiny.

He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhuwayh al-Muʻaddab narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jaʻfar al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masʻada ibn Sadaqa, from al-Sadiq Jaʻfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: No thing has been added to something that is more virtuous than forbearance added to knowledge.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Adam, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala', from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: I heard him say: The most beloved of worshipers to God, Mighty and Majestic, is a man who is truthful in his speech, who maintains his prayers and what God has obligated upon him, along with fulfilling trusts. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever is entrusted with a trust and fulfills it has unfastened a thousand knots from his neck — knots of the Fire. So hasten to fulfill trusts, for when one is entrusted with a trust, Iblis assigns one hundred devils from his rebellious helpers to misguide him and whisper to him until they destroy him — except for one whom God, Mighty and Majestic, protects.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Hisham ibn Salim. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: It is unjust for a rider to say to one who is walking: 'The road!' (i.e., get out of my way).

Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me. He said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi narrated to me from Abdallah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from al-Husayn ibn Yahya ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn Talha, from Asbat ibn Nasr, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "By He who raised me as a bringer of glad tidings in truth, Allah will never punish a monotheist with the Fire forever, and the people of tawhid will intercede and their intercession will be accepted." Then he (peace be upon him) said: "Verily, when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will command a people whose deeds were evil in the abode of this world to the Fire. They will say: 'O our Lord! How could You bring us into the Fire when we would declare Your oneness in the world? How could You burn our tongues with the Fire when they spoke of Your oneness in the world? How could You burn our hearts when they pledged that there is no god but You? How could You burn our faces when we placed them in the dust for You? How could You burn our hands when we raised them in supplication to You?'" So Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, will say: 'My servants! Your deeds were evil in the abode of the world, so the Fire of Hell is your recompense.' So they will say: 'O our Lord! Is Your forgiveness greater, or our sins?' He will say: 'Rather, My forgiveness.' They will say: 'Is Your mercy vaster, or our sins?' He will say: 'Rather, My mercy.' They will say: 'Is our declaration of Your oneness greater, or our sins?' He will say: 'Rather, your declaration of My oneness is greater.' So they will say: 'O our Lord! Let Your forgiveness and Your mercy, which have encompassed all things, encompass us.' So Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, will say: 'My angels! By My glory and My majesty, I have not created any creation more beloved to Me than those who declare My oneness and that there is no god besides Me. It is My responsibility not to commit the people of My tawhid to the Fire. Enter Paradise, My servants!'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Imran narrated to me from his father Imran ibn Ismail. He said: Abu Ali al-Ansari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tamimi. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: While Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful (peace be upon him), was on the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis seeking a pasture for his sheep, he suddenly heard a voice and found a man standing in prayer who was twelve cubits tall. He said to him: 'O servant of God! Who do you pray to?' He said: 'To the God of heaven.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Is there anyone remaining from your people besides you?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'So from where do you eat?' He said: 'I collect from this tree in the summer and eat it in the winter.' He said to him: 'Where is your dwelling?' So he pointed with his hand toward a mountain. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Would you take me with you so that I may spend the night at your place?' He said: 'Before me is water that cannot be waded through.' He said: 'How do you manage?' He said: 'I walk on it.' He said: 'Then take me with you, for perhaps God will grant me what He has granted you.' So the worshipper took him by the hand and they went together until they reached the water, and he walked and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) walked with him until they reached his dwelling. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Which is the greatest of days?' The worshipper said to him: 'The Day of Religion — the day on which people demand recompense from one another.' He said: 'Would you raise your hand and I raise mine, and we supplicate to God Almighty to protect us from the evil of that day?' He said: 'And what will my supplication avail? By God, I have had a supplication for thirty years that has not been answered at all.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Shall I not tell you why your supplication has been withheld?' He said: 'Of course.' He said to him: 'When God Almighty loves a servant, He withholds his supplication so that he may continue to whisper to Him, ask Him, and seek from Him. And when He hates a servant, He hastens the granting of his supplication, or He casts despair of it into h

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi narrated to us, from his father, he said: Abdul Malik ibn Umair al-Shaybani narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: "I am the master of the prophets and the messengers, and superior to the close angels. My successors are the masters of the successors of the prophets and the messengers, and my progeny are the best of the progenies of the prophets and the messengers, and my companions who followed my path are the best companions of the prophets and the messengers, and my daughter Fatima is the lady of the women of the worlds, and the pure ones among my wives are the mothers of the believers. And my nation is the best nation brought forth for the people, and I am the prophet with the most followers on the Day of Resurrection. And I have a pool whose width is the distance between Busra and Sana'a, containing pitchers as numerous as the stars of the sky. And my successor at the pool on that day is my successor in this world." It was asked: "And who is that, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The leader of the Muslims, the commander of the faithful, and their guardian after me: Ali ibn Abi Talib. He will give drink from it to his friends and drive away his enemies from it, just as one of you drives away a strange camel from the water." Then he (may God bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: "Whoever loves Ali and obeys him in this world will come to my pool tomorrow and will be with me at my level in Paradise. And whoever hates Ali in this world and disobeys him, I will not see him nor will he see me on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be snatched away from me and taken to the left, toward the Fire."

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), he said: "Whoever mentions the name of God over food will never be asked about the blessing of that food."

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Whoever finds a crumb or a date and eats it, it will not leave his stomach until Allah forgives him.

Abdullah ibn al-Nadr ibn Sam'an al-Tamimi narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Makki narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Hasan Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Harrani narrated to us, he said: Salih ibn Ziyad narrated to us, he said: Abu Uthman Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Sukkari narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Mu'izz al-Awdi narrated to us, he said: Imran ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Tawus al-Yamani, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn, the Master of the Worshippers (peace be upon him), used to supplicate with this supplication: My God! By Your glory, Your majesty, and Your greatness! If I had worshipped You since the creation of my nature from the beginning of time, for the duration of the eternity of Your lordship, with every hair and every blink of an eye throughout perpetual eternity, with the praise and thanks of all creatures combined, I would still have fallen short of expressing gratitude for the most hidden of Your blessings upon me. And even if I ground the iron ores of the world with my teeth, plowed its earth with the lashes of my eyes, and wept out of fear of You as much blood and pus as the oceans of the heavens and the earths, that would be little compared to the much that is due from Your right upon me. And even if You, my God, were to punish me after that with the punishment of all creatures combined, and enlarged my form and body for the Fire, and filled Hell and its layers with me, until there was no one punished in the Fire except me, and there was no firewood for Hell other than me, that would still be little for You upon me compared to the much that I have deserved of Your punishment.

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Asadi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa b. Imran al-Nakhai narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid from Ali b. Salim from his father from Sa'd b. Turayf from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Ali! You are the Imam of the Muslims, the Commander of the Faithful, the Leader of the shining believers, the Proof of Allah after me over the whole creation, the Master of Deputies, and the Deputy of the Master of Prophets. O Ali! When I was taken up to the seventh heaven, and from there to the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary, and from there to the veils of light, my Lord, exalted be His majesty, honored me with His intimate whisper. He said to me: 'O Muhammad!' I said: 'I am at Your service, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You.' He said: 'Surely, Ali is the Imam of My friends, a light for whoever obeys Me, and the word that I have made binding upon the pious. Whoever obeys him has obeyed Me, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Me. So give him glad tidings of that.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah! Is my omen such that I would be mentioned there?! So he said: Yes, O Ali, so thank your Lord. So Ali (peace be upon him) fell in prostration, thanking Allah for what He had blessed him with. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: Raise your head, O Ali, for surely Allah has boasted about you to His angels.

The exalted and virtuous Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us from Harun b. Muslim b. Sa'dan from Mas'ada b. Sadaqa from al-Sadiq from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: When a Muslim sneezes and then remains silent due to some ailment, the angels say on his behalf: "Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds." And if he says: "Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds," the angels say: "May Allah forgive you."

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. 'Isa b. 'Ubayd narrated to us from Yunus b. 'Abd al-Rahman from Abu Jamila from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Allah, Exalted is His Majesty, said: O My saintly servants! Find felicity in your worship of Me in this world, for you will be delighted by it in Paradise.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from al-Husayn b. al-Hasan al-Qurashi from Sulayman b. Jafar al-Basri from Abdullah b. al-Husayn b. Zayd b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib from his father from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Surely, Allah, blessed and exalted, has disliked for you, O Nation, twenty-four characteristics and has prohibited them from you: He disliked fiddling in prayer; He disliked reminding others of goodwill in charity; He disliked laughing among graves; He disliked peeping in houses; He disliked gazing at the private parts of women - and he said: it causes blindness; He disliked speaking during intercourse - and he said: it causes muteness; He disliked sleeping before the final Isha; He disliked socializing after the final Isha; He disliked bathing beneath the sky without a cover; He disliked intercourse beneath the sky; He disliked entering rivers except with a cover - and he said: in the rivers are inhabitants and dwellers from the angels; He disliked entering bathhouses except with a cover; He disliked speaking between the adhan and iqama in the dawn prayer until the prayer is completed; He disliked sailing the sea in its frenzy; He disliked sleeping upon a roof that is not plastered - and he said: whoever sleeps on a roof not plastered, responsibility is absolved from him; He disliked that a man sleeps in a house alone; He disliked for a man to approach his wife while she is menstruating, for if he does so and the child comes out leprous or albinotic, then let him blame none but himself; He disliked that a man approaches a woman while having had a wet dream until he bathes from the dream that he saw, for if he does and the child comes out insane, then let him blame none but himself; He disliked that a man speaks to a leper except that there is between them the measure of an armlength - and he said: flee from the leper as you flee from the lion; He disliked urinating on the bank of a flowing river; He disliked that a man relieves himself under a tree that has blossomed or a date palm that has ripened - meaning borne fruit; He disliked that a man puts on sandals while standing

Muhammad b. Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Muhammad b. Sinan from Ammar b. Marwan from Samaa from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Surely, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed gifts upon a community, and they were not thankful, so it became a scourge for them; and He tried a community with afflictions, and they were patient, so it became a blessing for them.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya al-Ashari from Yaqub b. Yazid from Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Mazkharaf from Ali b. Uqba from Ibn Bukayr. He said: Al-Hajjaj took two clients of Ali (peace be upon him) and said to one of them: Dissociate from Ali. So he said: What will happen to me if I do not dissociate from him? He said: May Allah kill me if I do not kill you. So choose for yourself: the severing of your hands or your feet. The man said to him: It is retribution, so choose for yourself. He said: By Allah, surely I see in you a tongue, and I do not think you know who created you. Where is your Lord? He said: He is on the lookout for every oppressor. So he ordered the severing of his hands and feet and his crucifixion. Then his other companion came forward, and he said: What do you say? He said: I am of the opinion of my companion. So he ordered that his neck be struck and that he be crucified.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Ali al-Taflisi narrated to me from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Hamadani from Muhammad b. Ali al-Hadi from Ali b. Musa al-Rida from Imam Musa b. Jafar from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from al-Baqir Muhammad b. Ali from the Master of Worshipers Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of the Youth of Paradise al-Husayn from the Master of Deputies Ali (peace be upon him) from the Master of Prophets Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family). He said: Do not look to the plenitude of their prayers, their fasting, their pilgrimages, their good works, and their recitation at night. Look to the honesty of their words and the fulfillment of their trusts.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad b. Sinan from Isa al-Nahryari from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever recognizes Allah and glorifies Him will prevent his lips from speech and his stomach from food, and will occupy himself with fasting and standing in prayer. They said: May our fathers and our mothers be your sacrifice, O Messenger of Allah! Are these the friends of Allah? He said: Surely, the friends of Allah are silent and their silence becomes reflection; they talk and their talk becomes remembrance; they observe and their observation becomes a lesson; they speak and their speech becomes wisdom; they walk and their walking among the people becomes a blessing. Were it not for the terms that have been written upon them, their spirits would not have settled in their bodies out of fear of the punishment and out of desire for the reward.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad b. Sinan from Abu al-Jarud from Abu Jafar al-Baqir from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Whoever places himself in a position of suspicion should not blame those who think ill of him. Whoever keeps his secret will have the choice in his hands. Every conversation that exceeds two people will spread. Think the best of your brother until what you hear from him overcomes that. Do not assume the worst of a word that came from your brother while you find for it a good interpretation. You must seek out brothers of truthfulness, so increase your ties with them, for they are a resource in times of ease and a shield in times of adversity. Consult in your matters those who fear God. Love brothers according to the measure of their piety. Beware of wicked women, and be on guard even from the best among them. If they command you to do good, contradict them so they do not become bold with you regarding evil.

My father, may God be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Maliki narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Mu'ammal. He said: I met Musa ibn Ja'far, peace be upon them both, and he used to dye with red. So I said: May I be your sacrifice! This is not from the dyeing practice of your family. He said: Yes indeed, I used to dye with isatis (woad plant), but it loosened my teeth. Indeed, when a man would embrace Islam during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, he would do that. And indeed, the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, dyed with yellow, and the news reached the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and he said: "Islam." Then he dyed with red, and the news reached the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and he said: "Islam and faith." Then he dyed with black, and the news reached the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and he said: "Islam, faith, and light."

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Trimming the nails and taking from the mustache from Friday to Friday is a protection from leprosy.

Ali ibn Abdillah al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Mehzayar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal Sahib al-Taq, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever would love to be the noblest of people, let him fear Allah. Whoever would love to be the most God-fearing of people, let him rely upon Allah. Whoever would love to be the richest of people, let him have more trust in what is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than in what is in his own hand. Then he (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Shall I not tell you about the worst of people? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: He who hates the people and is hated by the people. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of someone worse than this? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: He who does not dismiss an offense, does not accept an excuse, and does not forgive a sin. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of someone worse than this? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: He from whose evil people are not safe, and whose good is not even hoped for. Indeed, Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) stood among the Children of Israel and said: O Children of Israel! Do not impart wisdom to fools, for you will have oppressed it; and do not withhold it from its people, for you will have oppressed them; and do not assist the oppressor in his oppression, for your virtue will become void. Matters are three: a matter whose rightness is apparent to you, so follow it; a matter whose misguidance is apparent to you, so avoid it; and a matter that is disagreed upon, so relegate it to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'O Dawud! Just as the sun does not diminish for one who sits in it, likewise My mercy does not diminish for one who enters into it. And just as evil omens do not harm one who does not believe in them, likewise the superstitious ones will not be saved from tribulation. And just as the closest of people to Me on the Day of Resurrection are the humble, likewise the furthest of people from Me on the Day of Resurrection are the arrogant.'

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Jumhur al-'Ammi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from 'Isam ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever from among our Shi'a preserves forty hadiths, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a learned scholar and a jurist, and He will not punish him.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim narrated to us. He said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to me. He said: Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to me. He said: Kamil ibn al-Ala narrated to us. He said: Habib ibn Abi Thabit narrated to us, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): O Ali! You are the master of my Pond, the bearer of my standard, the fulfiller of my promises, the beloved of my heart, and the inheritor of my knowledge. You are the custodian of the prophets' inheritance. You are the trustee of God in His earth. You are the Proof of God over His creatures. You are the pillar of faith, the lamp in the darkness, the lighthouse of guidance, and the raised banner for the people of this world. Whoever follows you is saved, and whoever turns away from you perishes. You are the clear road and the Straight Path. You are the leader of the luminous shining believers. You are the chief of the believers. You are the master of everyone of whom I am master, and I am the master of every believing man and woman. None shall love you except one who is pure of birth, and none shall hate you except one who is impure of birth. My Lord — Mighty and Majestic — never raised me up to heaven and spoke to me without saying to me: 'O Muhammad! Convey to Ali My greetings, and make him know that he is the Imam of My friends and the light of the people of My obedience.' Congratulations to you, O Ali, for this honour.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Asbat narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from Abu Basir, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said: O Abu Basir! We are the Tree of Knowledge. We are the People of the Household of the Prophet. In our house is the place where Gabriel descends. We are the treasurers of the knowledge of God. We are the repositories of the revelation of God. Whoever follows us is saved, and whoever turns away from us perishes -- this is a right upon God, the Mighty and Majestic.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub. He said: Ali ibn Ri'ab narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Do not belittle the poor among the Shi'a of Ali and his progeny after him, for surely a man from among them will intercede for the like of [the tribes of] Rabi'a and Mudar.

The esteemed jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Makhul ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad al-Yashkuri narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, from Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family): Who is your successor from your Nation, for no prophet was ever sent without having a successor from his nation? The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: It has not yet been revealed to me. So I waited as long as Allah willed. Then I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) called me and said: O Salman, you asked me about my successor from my Nation. Do you know who was the successor of Moses from his nation? I said: His successor was Joshua son of Nun, his attendant. He said: Do you know why he bequeathed to him?
