I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: He bequeathed to him because he was the most knowledgeable of his nation after him. And my successor, the most knowledgeable of my Nation after me, is Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Salama al-Ahwazi narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Uthman ibn Abi Shayba and Mahraz ibn Hisham narrated to us. They said: Mutalib ibn Ziyad narrated to us from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym. He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) was approached by Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and each of them was saying: 'I am the most beloved to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family).' So he (s) took Fatima to his stomach, Ali to his back, al-Hasan to his right, and al-Husayn to his left. Then he (s) said: You are from me, and I am from you.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Isa ibn Abdullah from his father from his grandfather from his forefathers. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever recites 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) when he goes to bed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will forgive fifty years of his sins.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ishaq ibn Harun from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: Allah the Blessed and Exalted designated four thousand angels at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) -- disheveled and dusty -- weeping for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever visits him, recognizing his right, they will be party to him until he reaches his home; if he becomes ill, they will visit him morning and evening; and if he dies, they will attend his funeral and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Hamza ibn Abdullah al-Ja'fari from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Hope in Allah with a hope that does not entice you to sin against Him, and fear Allah with a fear that does not deprive you of His mercy.

Muhammad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us from Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Amer b. Kathir al-Sarraj al-Nahdi from Abu al-Jarud from Thabit b. Abi Safiyya from Sayyid al-Abidin Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn b. Ali from the Master of Deputies, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) from the Master of Prophets Muhammad b. Abdullah, the Seal of the Prophets (may Allah bless him and his family), that he said: Surely, Allah, blessed and exalted, has obligated you to obey me, has prohibited you from disobeying me, and has made it mandatory for you to follow my command. He has obligated you to obey Ali after me in the same way that He obligated you to obey me, and has prohibited you from disobeying him in the same way that He prohibited you from disobeying me. He made him my brother, my vizier, my deputy, and my inheritor. He is from me and I am from him. Loving him is faith and hating him is disbelief. Whoever loves him loves me, and whoever hates him hates me. He is the master of whoever I am master of, and I am the master of every Muslim man and woman. He and I are the two fathers of this Nation.

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani al-Mukattib (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa b. Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid from Ali b. Salim from his father. He said: I visited al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them) in Rajab when it still had a few days left. When he looked at me, he said to me: O Salim! Have you fasted at all this month? I said: No, by Allah, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said to me: You have indeed missed out on a reward whose extent is known only to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Surely, this is a month that Allah gave virtue to, magnified its sanctity, and made His blessing incumbent upon those who fast in it. He said: So I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, if I fast something of what remains of it, will I attain some of the reward of those who have fasted in it? So he said: O Salim! Whoever fasts one day at the end of this month, that will be a source of safety for him from the severity of the pangs of death, and a source of safety for him from the horror of the resurrection and the punishment of the grave. Whoever fasts two days at the end of this month, he will thereby have safe passage upon the Path. Whoever fasts three days at the end of this month will be safe on the Day of the Greatest Dismay from its horrors and its severities, and will be given a release from the Fire.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahman b. Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Isa b. Abi Musa al-Ijli informed us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Abdullah b. Ziyad al-Arzami narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Hatim al-Minqari narrated to us. He said: Sharik narrated to us from Salim al-Aftas from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah said to Ali: O Ali! Your Shi'a will be the winners on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever insults one of them has insulted you, and whoever insults you has insulted me, and whoever insults me, Allah will enter him into the Fire of Hell forever in the misery of fate. O Ali! You are from me and I am from you. Your spirit is from my spirit, and your clay is from my clay, and your Shi'a were created from the surplus of our clay. So whoever loves them has loved us, and whoever hates them has hated us, and whoever opposes them has opposed us, and whoever adores them has adored us. O Ali! Surely, your Shi'a will be forgiven despite their sins and flaws. O Ali! I will be the intercessor for your Shi'a tomorrow when I attain the Praised Station, so give them glad tidings of that. O Ali! Your Shi'a are the Shi'a of Allah, and your supporters are the supporters of Allah, and your friends are the friends of Allah, and your party is the party of Allah. O Ali! Happy is whoever aligns with you, and wretched is whoever opposes you. O Ali! For you is a treasure in Paradise, and you are its Dhul Qarnayn.

The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him): that he was asked about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And it was said: Is there a healer?' [75:27]. He said: That is the saying of the son of Adam when death comes to him. He says: 'Is there a doctor? Is there a defender?' He said: 'And he realizes that it is the parting' [75:28] — meaning, the parting from family and loved ones at that moment. He said: 'And the legs are joined together' [75:29]. He said: This world and the Hereafter are joined together. He said: 'To your Lord that day is the driving' [75:30] — to the Lord of the Worlds on that day is the return.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: I heard him say: Indeed, no year has less rain than another; rather, God places it wherever He wills. When a people commit sins, God, exalted is His majesty, diverts from them what He had apportioned for them of rain in that year to others, and to the deserts, the seas, and the mountains. Indeed, God even punishes the scarab beetle in its burrow by withholding rain from the land where it dwells, because of the sins of those in its vicinity, though God has given it a passage to a path away from the locality of the sinful people. Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: So take heed, O people of insight. Then he said: We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), he said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: When fornication becomes prevalent, sudden deaths increase. When the measure is cheated, God seizes them with years of famine and shortage. When they withhold the almsgiving (zakat), the earth is prevented from its blessings of crops, fruits, and all its minerals. When they are unjust in their rulings, they cooperate in oppression and aggression. When they break their covenants, God empowers their enemy over them. When they sever family ties, wealth is placed in the hands of the wicked. And when they do not enjoin good, do not forbid evil, and do not follow the chosen ones from my Ahl al-Bayt, God empowers the worst among them over them, and then the best among them supplicate but are not answered.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Indeed, in the Torah it is written: O Moses, indeed I created you, formed you, and strengthened you, and I commanded you to obey Me, and I prohibited you from disobeying Me. So if you obey Me, I will help you in obeying Me. And if you disobey Me, I will not help you in disobeying Me. O Moses, to Me belongs the grace upon you in your obedience to Me, and to Me belongs the proof against you in your disobedience to Me.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Abu Yazid Muhammad b. Yahya b. Khalid b. Yazid al-Maruzi narrated to us in Ray in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 302 AH. He said: Ishaq b. Ibrahim al-Hanthali narrated to us in the year 238 AH -- and he is known as Ishaq b. Rahuwayh. He said: Yahya b. Yahya narrated to us. He said: Hisham narrated to us from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq who said: While we were with Abdullah b. Mas'ud showing our codices to him, a young man said to him: Did your Prophet tell you how many caliphs there would be after him? He said: You are young in age, and indeed no one before you has asked me about this. Yes, our Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told us that there would be twelve caliphs after him, like the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel.

Abu Ali Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abduwayh narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Rijal al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Hakam narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, from Mutrif, from al-Sha'bi, from his uncle Qays ibn Abd, who said: We were sitting in a circle in which was Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, when a Bedouin came and said: "Which one of you is Abdullah?" Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I am Abdullah." He said: "Has your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ever told you how many caliphs would come after him?" He said: "Yes, twelve, like the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel."

6 - 'Attab ibn Muhammad ibn 'Attab al-Waramini narrated to us. He said: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mufaddal and Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Sawwar narrated to us. They said: 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Hakam narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, from Mutrif, from al-Sha'bi. And 'Attab ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Anmati narrated to us, from Yusuf ibn Musa. He said: Jarir narrated to me, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from al-Sha'bi. And 'Attab ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Ayyub ibn Muhammad al-Wazzan narrated to us. He said: Sa'id ibn Maslama narrated to us. He said: Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated to us from al-Sha'bi. All of them reported from his uncle Qays ibn 'Abd. 'Attab said: This is the hadith of Mutrif. He said: We were sitting in the mosque, and 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud was with us. A Bedouin came and said: Is there an 'Abdullah among you? He said: Yes, I am 'Abdullah. What do you need? He said: O 'Abdullah! Has your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) informed you of how many caliphs there would be? He said: You have asked me about something that no one has asked me since I came to Iraq. Yes, twelve -- the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel. Abu 'Uruba said in his hadith: He said: Yes, the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel.
And Jarir narrated from Ash'ath, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family. He said: The caliphs after me are twelve, like the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Abu Bakr Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abda al-Nishapuri narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Qasim Harun b. Ishaq narrated to us. He said: My uncle Ibrahim b. Muhammad narrated to us from Ziyad b. Alaqa and Abd al-Malik b. Umayr, from Jabir b. Samura. He said: I was with my father in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, and I heard him say: There will be twelve emirs after me. Then, he lowered his voice. So I said to my father: What did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, say softly? He said: He said: All of them are from Quraysh.

Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Sa'igh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Ghadrani narrated to us. He said: Abu Ali al-Husayn b. al-Layth b. Bahlul al-Mosuli narrated to us. He said: Ghassan b. al-Rabi narrated to us. He said: Sulaym b. Abdullah, the freedman of Amer al-Sha'bi, narrated to us from Amer, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: The affair of my Umma will continue to prevail until twelve caliphs have passed, all of whom are from Quraysh.

10 - Salih ibn Isa ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ijli narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rowyani narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ijli narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to me, from his father, from Aban the client of Zayd ibn Ali, from Asim ibn Bahdala, he said: Shurayh the Judge said to me: I bought a house for eighty gold coins, I wrote a document and had just witnesses testify. This reached Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), so he sent his servant Qanbar to me and I came to him. When I entered upon him, he said: O Shurayh, you bought a house, you wrote a document, you had witnesses testify, and you weighed out money? I said: Yes. He said: O Shurayh, fear God, for indeed one will come to you who will not look at your document nor ask for your evidence, until he takes you out of your house departing and delivers you wholly to your grave. So make sure you did not buy this house from other than its rightful owner and that you did not pay with unlawful money, or else you will have lost both abodes together: this world and the Hereafter. Then he (peace be upon him) said: O Shurayh, if you had come to me when you bought this house, I would have written you a document on this template, and you would not have bought it even for two silver coins. I said: What would you have written, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: I would have written this document for you: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what was purchased by a lowly slave from a mortal urged to depart. He bought from him a house in the Abode of Vanity, from the side of the mortals to the garrison of the perished. This house has four boundaries: the first ends at the causes of destruction, the second at the causes of impairment, the third at the causes of calamity, and the fourth at ruinous desire and Satan the deceiver, and therein opens the door of this house. This deceived one, beguiled by wishful thinking, purchased from the one pursued by death the entirety of this house, by leaving the honour of contentment and entering the humiliation of worldly pursuit. Whatever befalls this buyer in what he bought, it is upon the One who wears out the bodies of kings and seizes the souls of tyrants like Khosrow, Caesar, Tubba, and Himyar, and all

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Asad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Wasiti narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Jarudi narrated to us. He said: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us from Sufyan al-Thawri and al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah has roaming angels on the earth who deliver the greetings of peace from my nation to me.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Hakam al-Za'farani narrated to me. He said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim al-'Abdi narrated to us. He said: Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami narrated to me, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He said: I entered the Mosque of Kufa, and there I found a man at the seventh pillar, standing in prayer, performing his bowing and prostration beautifully. So I came to look at him, but he preceded me to prostration. I heard him saying in his prostration: "O Allah! If I have disobeyed You, then indeed I have obeyed You in the most beloved of things to You, which is belief in You -- as a grace from You upon me, not as a favour from me upon You. And I have not disobeyed You in the most hateful of things to You: I did not attribute a son to You, nor did I take a partner for You -- as a grace from You upon me, not as a favour from me upon You. And I disobeyed You in certain things, not out of needlessness on my part, nor arrogance, nor pride against Your worship, nor denial of Your lordship, but rather I followed my caprice, and Satan made me slip after the proof and the clarity. So if You punish me, it is for my sin, and You would not be unjust to me; and if You have mercy on me, it is by Your magnanimity and Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones." Then he turned and left through the gate of Kindah. I followed him until he reached the resting place of camels of Banu Kalb. He passed by a black person and ordered him to do something I did not understand. So I said: Who is this? He said: This is Ali ibn al-Husayn. So I said: May God make me your sacrifice! What brought you to this place? He said: That which you saw.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Mu'adhi narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Faraj al-Sharuti narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn al-Muhallab narrated to us. He said: Abu Usama narrated to us. He said: Awf narrated to me, from Maymun. He said: al-Bara' ibn Azib informed me. He said: When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) ordered for the trench to be dug, a great and hard boulder appeared across the trench that the pickaxes could not break. So the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) came, and when he saw it, he took off his robe and picked up the pickaxe, and said: "In the name of God," and struck it once, breaking off a third of it. He said: "God is the Greatest! I have been given the keys to the Levant. By God, I can see its red palaces at this very moment." Then he struck it a second time and said: "In the name of God," and split off another third. He said: "God is the Greatest! I have been given the keys to Persia. By God, I can see the white palace of al-Mada'in." Then he struck it a third time and split the remainder of the boulder. He said: "God is the Greatest! I have been given the keys to Yemen. By God, I can see the gates of Sanaa from my place here."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to me from his father. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-'Abdi, from al-A'mash, from 'Abaya ibn Riba'i, from Abdillah ibn Abbas. He said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) one day, weeping and saying: To Allah we belong, and to Him we shall return. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: What is it, O Ali? So 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah! My mother Fatima bint Asad has died. He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wept, then said: May Allah have mercy on your mother, O Ali. Know that if she was a mother to you, she was indeed a mother to me. Take this turban of mine and take these two robes of mine, and shroud her in them. And instruct the women to perfect her funeral bath. Do not carry her out until I come, for I will personally attend to her affairs. He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came after a short while. Fatima, the mother of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), was brought out, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prayed over her a prayer the like of which he had never prayed over anyone before her. Then he recited forty takbirs over her. Then he entered her grave and lay down in it. No groan nor movement was heard from him. Then he said: O Ali! Enter. O Hasan! Enter. So they entered the grave. When they finished what was needed, he said to them: O Ali! Come out. O Hasan! Come out. So they came out. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) crawled until he was at her head. Then he said: O Fatima! I am Muhammad, the Master of the Children of Adam, and I do not say this boastfully. When Munkar and Nakir come to you and ask: Who is your Lord? Say: Allah is my Lord, Muhammad is my Prophet, Islam is my religion, the Quran is my Book, and my son is my Imam and my wali. Then he said: O Allah! Make Fatima steadfast in the firm word. Then he came out of her grave, sprinkled handfuls of dirt on her, then struck his right hand upon his left and shook them off. Then he said: By Him in Whose hand is Muhammad's soul! I have h

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Qutayba ibn Sa'id, from 'Amr ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Muslim. He said: He said: I went out with al-Hasan al-Basri and Anas ibn Malik until we came to the door of Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her). Anas sat at the door, and I entered with al-Hasan al-Basri. I heard al-Hasan saying: Peace be upon you, O mother, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. She said to him: And upon you be peace. Who are you, my son? He said: I am al-Hasan al-Basri. She said: What have you come for, O Hasan? He said to her: I have come so that you may narrate to me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So Umm Salama said: By Allah, I will surely narrate to you a hadith that my ears heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) — and if I did not, then may they become deaf; and my eyes saw it — and if they did not, then may they become blind; and my heart preserved it — and if it did not, then may Allah seal it; and may my tongue be muted if I did not hear the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): O Ali! There is no servant who meets Allah on the Day he meets Him while denying your wilaya, except that he meets Allah as a worshipper of idols or graven images. He (Abu Muslim) said: So I heard al-Hasan al-Basri saying: Allah is the Greatest! I bear witness that Ali is my master and the master of the believers. When he (al-Hasan) left, Anas ibn Malik said to him: Why do I see you reciting the takbir? He said: I asked our mother Umm Salama to narrate to me a hadith that she had heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali (peace be upon him). So she said to me such-and-such. So I said: Allah is the Greatest! I bear witness that Ali is my master and the master of every believer. He (Abu Muslim) said: So at that, I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: I bear witness upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said this statement three or four times.

The exalted Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani, servant of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Abdullah b. Ja'far b. Abdullah b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ali b. Abi Talib narrated to us. He said: Kathir b. Ayyash al-Qattan narrated to us from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad b. al-Mundhir from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (as). He said: When Isa b. Maryam (as) was born, he was one day old as if he were two months old. When he was seven months old, his mother took him by the hand and came with him to the scribes and sat him in front of the teacher. The teacher said to him: Say: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. So Isa (as) said: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. The teacher said to him: Say the alphabet. So Isa (as) raised his head and said: Do you know what the alphabet is? So he raised a stick to discipline him, and he said: O teacher, do not discipline me. If you know, then well; otherwise, ask me so that I may explain it to you. He said: Explain it to me. So Isa (as) said: Alif is the signs (alaa') of Allah, Ba is the delight (bahja) of Allah, Jim is the beauty (jamal) of Allah, and Dal is the religion (din) of Allah. Hawwaz: Ha is the horror (hawl) of Hell, Waw is the woe (wayl) of the people of the Fire, and Zay is the roar (zafir) of Hell. Hutti: the sins are dropped from those who seek forgiveness. Kalamun: the words (kalam) of Allah, for which there is no substitute. Sa'fas: a measure for a measure, and a reward for a reward. Qarashat: He gathers them and resurrects them. So the teacher said: O woman, take your son by the hand, for he is learned, and he has no need for a teacher.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab and Ahmad b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal narrated to us from Ali b. Asbat from al-Hasan b. Zayd. He said: Muhammad b. Salim narrated to me from al-Asbagh b. Nubata. He said: The Commander of the Believers (as) said: Uthman b. Affan asked the Messenger of Allah (s): O Messenger of Allah! What is the interpretation of the alphabet? So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Learn the interpretation of the alphabet, for therein is all wonders. Woe to a scholar who is ignorant of its interpretation. So, it was said: O Messenger of Allah! What is the interpretation of the alphabet? He said: As for Alif, it is the signs of Allah, a letter from His names. As for Ba, it is the delight of Allah. As for Jim, it is the Paradise of Allah, the majesty of Allah, and His beauty. As for Dal, it is the religion of Allah. As for Hawwaz, Ha is the Ha of the Abyss, so woe to whoever falls into the Fire. As for Waw, woe to the people of the Fire. As for Zay, it is a corner of Hell, and we seek refuge in Allah from what is in the corner, meaning the corners of Hellfire. As for Hutti, Ha is the dropping of sins from those who repent on the Night of Power, and what descends with Gabriel and the angels until the rise of dawn. As for Ta, Tuba is for them and a goodly reward, and it is a tree that Allah has planted, breathing into it of His spirit, and its branches can be seen from behind the fence of Paradise, sprouting jewels and garments, hanging over their mouths. As for Ya, it is the hand of Allah over His creation, glorified and exalted above what they associate. As for Kalamun, Kaf is the words of Allah, there is no change for the words of Allah, and you will never find besides Him a refuge. As for Lam, it is the familiarity of the people of Paradise among them in visits, greetings, and peace, and the mutual blame of the people of the Fire. As for Mim, it is the dominion of Allah that does not diminish and the permanence of Allah that does not perish. As for Nun, Nun and the Pen and what they inscribe, the Pen is a pen of light and a book of light in a Preserved Tablet, witnessed by those brought near, and Allah is sufficient as a Witness. As for Sa'fas, Sad is a measure for a measure and a piece for a piece, meaning the

My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to us. He said: al-Qasim b. Yahya narrated to us from his grandfather al-Hasan b. Rashid from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as). He said: If a man is wronged and he continues to pray against the one who wronged him, Allah, exalted is His majesty, says: 'Indeed, here is another who is praying against you, alleging that you wronged him. If you wish, I will answer your prayer and answer his prayer against you. And if you wish, I will delay both of you, and My forgiveness will encompass you both.'

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from Ahmad b. al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr b. Shimr, from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Habib b. Amr. He said: I visited Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) during the illness in which he passed away. He uncovered his wound, so I said: O Amir al-Mu'minin! Your wound is nothing serious, and there is no danger in you. So he said to me: O Habib! I, by Allah, am departing from you this very moment. He said: So I wept at that, and Umm Kulthum wept — and she was sitting beside him. So he said to her: What makes you weep, my daughter? She said: You mentioned, father, that you will depart from us this moment, so I wept. So he said to her: O my daughter, do not weep, for by Allah, if you saw what your father sees, you would not weep. Habib said: So I said to him: And what do you see, O Amir al-Mu'minin? So he said: O Habib, I see the angels of the heavens and the prophets, one after another, standing to receive me. And this is my brother Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), sitting with me, saying: Come forth, for what lies before you is better for you than what you are in. He said: So I did not leave his presence until he passed away (peace be upon him). When the next day came, al-Hasan (peace be upon him) arose as an orator on the pulpit. He praised Allah and commended Him, then said: O people! On this night, the Quran was revealed; on this night, Isa b. Maryam (peace be upon him) was raised up; on this night, Yusha' b. Nun was killed; and on this night, my father, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him), died. By Allah! None of the deputies before him will reach Paradise before him, nor any who will come after him. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) would send him on a military expedition, Gabriel would fight on his right side and Michael on his left. He left behind neither gold nor silver, except seven hundred silver coins remaining from his stipend, which he had been gathering to purchase a servant for his family.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Abbas b. Ma'ruf from Ali b. Mahzayar from al-Hasan b. Sa'id from Fadala b. Ayyub from Abdullah b. Muskan from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Shall I not inform you of who the Fire will be forbidden from anon? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The meek, the near, the tender, and the easygoing.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from his father from Safwan b. Yahya from al-Is b. al-Qasim. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as): A hadith is attributed to your father, and it says: 'The Messenger of Allah (s) was never satiated with wheat bread.' Is this correct? So, he said: No. The Messenger of Allah (s) never ate wheat bread at all, and he was never satiated with barley bread either.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to us, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qadi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: God, exalted is His majesty, said: O son of Adam, obey Me in what I have commanded you, and do not teach Me what is good for you.

By this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: God, exalted is His majesty, said: O son of Adam! Remember Me for a moment after the morning prayer and for a moment after the afternoon prayer, and I will suffice you from what worries you.

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Bakr b. Salih. He said: Abdullah b. Ibrahim al-Ghifari narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman from his uncle Abd al-Aziz b. Ali from Sa'id b. al-Musayyib from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Shall I not guide you to something by which God expiates sins and increases good deeds? It was said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: Performing ablution thoroughly despite hardships, taking frequent steps to these mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer. There is not one among you who leaves his house purified, prays in congregation with the Muslims, then sits waiting for the next prayer, except that the angels say: O God, forgive him. O God, have mercy on him. When you stand for prayer, straighten your rows and establish them, and close the gaps. When your imam says: God is the Greatest, then say: God is the Greatest. When he bows, then bow. When he says: God hears those who praise Him, then say: O God, our Lord, for You is all praise. Indeed, the best of rows is the first row of men, and the worst of them is the last.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Aban ibn Abd al-Malik, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) wanted to part from al-Khidr (peace be upon him), he said to him: Advise me. So among that which he advised him was that he said to him: Beware of bickering, and of walking without need, and of laughing without cause for astonishment. Remember your own mistakes, and beware of [mentioning] the mistakes of the people.

By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman called for his son at the time of his death, and he advised him, saying: O my son! Show indifference toward what is in the hands of people, for in that lies richness. Beware of seeking favors from people, for that is manifest poverty. Be better today than you were yesterday. When you pray, pray as one bidding farewell to this world, as though you will not return to it. And beware of that for which you must apologize.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), that he said: Love your Muslim brother, and love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. When you are in need, ask him, and when he asks you, give to him. Do not withhold goodness from him, for indeed he does not withhold it from you. Be a support for him, for indeed he is a support for you. If he is absent, protect him in his absence, and if he is present, visit him. Honour him and be generous to him, for he is from you and you are from him. If he reproaches you, do not part from him until you draw out his grudge and what is in his heart. When good befalls him, praise God for it, and if he is afflicted, support him and share in his burden.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-'Adawi narrated to us in the year 317 AH when he was 107 years old. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Tufawi narrated to us. He said: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us. He said: Sa'd al-Khaffaf narrated to us from 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, from Makhduj ibn Zayd al-Dhuhli, that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) established brotherhood bonds among the Muslims, then said: O 'Ali! You are my brother, and you are to me as Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me. Did you not know, O 'Ali, that the first to be called on the Day of Resurrection will be me? I will stand to the right of the Throne and be dressed in a green garment from the garments of Paradise. Then our father Ibrahim (peace be upon him) will be called, and he will stand to the right of the Throne in its shade, and he will be dressed in a green garment from the garments of Paradise. Then the prophets will be called one after another, and they will stand in two rows to the right of the Throne in its shade, and they will be dressed in green garments from the garments of Paradise. Surely, I inform you, O 'Ali, that my nation will be the first of nations to be reckoned with on the Day of Resurrection. Then I give you glad tidings, O 'Ali, that the first to be called on the Day of Resurrection will be you. This is because of your closeness to me and your rank with me. My banner will be handed to you — it is the Banner of Praise — and you will walk with it between the two rows. Truly, Adam and all whom God has created will be shaded by the shade of my banner on the Day of Resurrection. Its height is the travel distance of one thousand years. Its tip is a red ruby, its shaft is shining white silver, and its finial is a green pearl. It has three tassels of light: one tassel in the East, one tassel in the West, and one tassel in the middle of the world. Written on it are three lines: the first: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful; the second: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds; the third: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. The length of each line is the travel distance of one thousand years, and its width is the travel distance of one thousand years. You will walk with the banner, with al-Hasan to your right and al-Husa

The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Bukran al-Naqqash narrated to us in Kufa. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, from Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: Surely, the first thing that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created to teach His creation writing was the letters of the alphabet. If a man is struck on his head with a staff and it is claimed that he cannot articulate some words, then the ruling is that the letters of the alphabet be presented to him, and the blood money is paid in proportion to what he cannot articulate of them. And indeed my father narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), regarding the alphabet (Alif Ba Ta Tha). He said: The Alif stands for the bounties of Allah. The Ba for the delight of Allah. The Ta for the perfection of the Order through the Qa'im of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). The Tha for the reward of the believers for their righteous deeds. The Jim for the beauty and majesty of Allah. The Ha for the forbearance of Allah toward the sinners. The Kha for the obscurity of the people of sin before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The Dal for the religion of Allah. The Dhal for the One of Majesty and Nobility. The Ra for the Kind, the Merciful. The Zay for the earthquakes of the Resurrection. The Sin for the splendor of Allah. The Shin for: Allah willed what He willed and decreed what He decreed, and you do not will except that Allah wills. The Sad for the Truthful in promise in carrying the people over the Path and trapping the transgressors at the lookout. The Dad for: whoever opposes Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad has gone astray. The Ta for Tuba for the believers and a goodly reward. The Dha for the good impression the believers have of Allah and the poor impression the disbelievers have of Him. The Ayn stands for the Knower. The Ghayn for the Needless. The Fa for a crowd from the crowds of the Fire. The Qaf for: the collection and recitation of the Quran are upon Allah. The Kaf for the Sufficient. The Lam for the slander of the disbelievers in their fabrication of lies against Allah. T

Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Qushayri narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Kilabi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) narrated to us in the year 205 AH. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever recites after the Friday prayer the Opening of the Book once and "Say: He is Allah, the One" seven times, and the Opening of the Book once and "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak" seven times, and the Opening of the Book once and "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind" seven times, no calamity will befall him and no trial will afflict him until the next Friday. And if he says: "O Allah, make me from the people of Paradise, which is filled with blessings and built by angels, with our Prophet Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family) and our father Ibrahim (peace be upon him)," Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will gather him with Muhammad and Ibrahim in the Abode of Peace. May the blessings of Allah be upon Muhammad and Ibrahim and their pure families.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah and Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us together from Ya'qub b. Yazid. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Umayr narrated to us from Ali b. Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Zayn al-Abidin Ali b. al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said: Among the Children of Israel was a man who would exhume graves. A neighbour of his became ill and feared death. So he sent for the exhumer and said to him: 'How was my neighbourliness toward you?' He said: 'It was the most beautiful neighbourliness.' He said: 'Then I need something from you.' He said: 'Your need is fulfilled.' He said: So he brought out two shrouds for him and said: 'I want you to take the one that is more beloved to you, so that when I am buried, you do not exhume me.' So the exhumer refrained from that and refused to take it. So the man said to him: 'I would love for you to take it.' So he did not stop with him until he took the one that was more beloved to him. The man died, and when he was buried, the exhumer said: 'He has been buried, so how would he know whether I left his shroud or took it? I will take it.' So he went to his grave and exhumed it, when he heard a voice screaming at him: 'Do not do it.' The exhumer was startled by that, so he left him and abandoned what he was doing. He said to his children: 'What kind of father was I to you?' They said: 'You were the best of fathers to us.' He said: 'Then I need something from you.' They said: 'Say what you wish, for we will fulfill it, God-willingly.' He said: 'When I die, I want you to take me and burn me with fire. When I become ashes, grind me, then cast me in a stormy wind — half toward the earth, and half toward the sea.' They said: 'We will do so.' When he died, his children did what he had advised them. When they scattered him, Allah, exalted be His majesty, said to the earth: 'Gather what is in you', and said to the sea: 'Gather what is in you'. Then the man stood before Allah, exalted be His majesty. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'What caused you to advise your children to do this to you?' He said: 'By Your glory, fear of You caused me to do this.' Allah, exalted be His majesty, said: 'I will satisfy your victims, accept your fear, and forgive you.'

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said: When a man prepares his shroud, he is rewarded every time he looks at it.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Ali b. Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Indeed, in Paradise there are rooms whose outside can be seen from their inside, and whose inside can be seen from their outside. Those of my community who purified their speech, fed people food, spread peace, and prayed at night while people slept will inhabit them. So Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of God, and who from your community is able to do this? He said: O Ali, do you not know what purification of speech is? It is whoever says, when they awake and when they go to sleep, 'Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest' ten times. And feeding people food is the expenditure of a man on his family. As for praying at night while people are asleep: whoever prays Maghrib, the final Isha, and the morning prayer in the mosque in congregation, it is as though he kept vigil all night. And spreading peace is not being stingy in greeting every single Muslim with the salaam.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar. He said: Al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, said: The body does not weaken from that which the intention has strengthened it for.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Shu'ayb al-Aqraqufi, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both. He said: Whoever controls himself when he desires, when he is terrified, when he craves, when he is angry, and when he is pleased, Allah will forbid his body from the Fire.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Mubarak the servant of al-Rida, from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon them both. He said: A believer cannot be a true believer until he has three characteristics: a quality from his Lord, a quality from his Prophet, and a quality from his wali. As for the quality from his Lord, it is concealing his secret. Allah, exalted is His majesty, said: "He is the Knower of the Unseen, and He does not disclose His Unseen to anyone, except whom He is pleased with from among the messengers" [72:26-27]. As for the quality from his Prophet, it is being friendly with the people, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet, blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, to be friendly with the people, and said: "Take to clemency, enjoin in established virtues, and turn away from the ignorant" [7:199]. As for the quality from his wali, it is patience during distress and affliction. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And those who are patient during distress and affliction and at the time of tribulation -- these are the ones who have been sincere, and these are the Godfearing" [2:177].

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jafar al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Ilwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Dawud ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir from his forefathers, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of Allah, blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, said to al-Husayn, peace be upon him: O Husayn! A man called Zayd will come forth from your loins. He and his companions will surpass the necks of the people on the Day of Resurrection, shining with radiant marks, entering Paradise without judgment.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Razma al-Qazwini narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Isa al-Alawi al-Husayni narrated to us, he said: Abbad ibn Yaqub al-Asadi narrated to us, he said: Habib ibn Arta narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Dhakwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, who said: Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) narrated to me while grasping his hair, he said: My father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) narrated to me while grasping his hair, he said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) narrated to me while grasping his hair, he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) narrated to me while grasping his hair, from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) while grasping his hair, he said: Whoever harms a single hair of mine has indeed harmed me, and whoever harms me has indeed harmed God, and whoever harms God, God curses him to fill the heavens and fill the earth.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to me from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-A'mash, from Abaya ibn Rib'i. He said: A young man from the Ansar used to visit Abdullah ibn Abbas, and Abdullah would honour him and bring him close. It was said to him: You honour this young man and bring him close, yet he is a wicked young man who goes to the graves and exhumes them at night! So Abdullah ibn Abbas said: If that is the case, inform me. He said: The young man went out one night wandering through the graves, and Abdullah ibn Abbas was informed of that. He went out to see what would come of his affair, and stood at a distance watching him from where the young man could not see him. He said: He entered a grave that had been dug, then lay down in the burial niche, and called out at the top of his voice: 'Woe is me! When I enter my burial niche alone, and the earth beneath me speaks, saying: No welcome and no greeting to you! I hated you while you were on my back, so how about now that you are in my belly! Rather, woe is me when I look at the prophets standing, and the angels in rows — who tomorrow will save me from Your justice? Who among the wronged will deliver me? Who will protect me from the punishment of the Fire? I disobeyed one who is not to be disobeyed. I made promises to my Lord time after time, yet He found no sincerity nor loyalty in me.' He kept repeating these words and weeping. When he came out of the grave, Ibn Abbas embraced him and hugged him, then said to him: 'The best of grave-openers! The best of grave-openers! Your grave-opening is not for sins and transgressions.' Then they parted.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, the client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us. He said: Ja'far ibn Isma'il narrated to us from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father (peace be upon them all), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call: 'Where is Zayn al-Abidin?' It is as though I am looking at my descendant Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib swaying between the rows.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyya, from Sa'id ibn 'Alaqa, from Abu Sa'id 'Aqisa, from the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), from the Master of Deputies Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: O 'Ali! You are my brother, and I am your brother. I was chosen for prophethood, and you were selected for the Imamate. I am the patron of revelation, and you are the patron of interpretation. You and I are the two fathers of this Nation. O 'Ali! You are my executor, my vicegerent (khalifa), my vizier, my inheritor, and the father of my descendants. Your partisans (shi'a) are my partisans, your supporters are my supporters, your friends are my friends, and your enemies are my enemies. O 'Ali! You will be my companion at the Pond (Hawd) tomorrow, and you are my companion at the Praiseworthy Station (Maqam al-Mahmud). You are my standard-bearer in the Hereafter, just as you are my standard-bearer in this world. Truly, whoever befriends you will be made happy, and whoever is hostile to you will be made wretched. The angels draw near to Allah — glorified be His remembrance — through their love of you and their allegiance to you (wilaya). By Allah, those who love you in heaven are more numerous than those on earth. O 'Ali! You are the trustee of my Nation and the Proof of Allah (Hujjat Allah) over it after me. Your words are my words, your command is my command, obedience to you is obedience to me, your rebuke is my rebuke, your prohibition is my prohibition, and disobedience to you is disobedience to me. Your party is my party, and my party is the Party of Allah. "Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe as their patron — indeed, the Party of Allah will prevail." [5:56]

Narrated to us by the illustrious Shaykh Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him), who said: Narrated to us Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Jafar al-Hamdani (may God be pleased with him), who said: Narrated to us Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami, from Ali ibn Jafar, from his brother Musa ibn Jafar, from his father Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever perfects his ablution, beautifies his prayers, pays the zakat of his wealth, guards his tongue, withholds his anger, seeks forgiveness for his sin, and fulfills the duty of sincere counsel regarding the household of His Messenger, has indeed perfected the realities of faith, and the gates of Paradise are open for him.

Narrated to us Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him), who said: Narrated to us Saad ibn Abdullah, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Samad ibn Muhammad, who said: Narrated to us Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: Narrated to us Sudayf al-Makki, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrated to me -- and I never saw any Muhammadan who equaled him -- he said: Narrated to us Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) addressed us in a sermon and said: O people, whoever hates us, the Ahl al-Bayt, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a Jew. He [Jabir] said: I said, O Messenger of God, even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be a Muslim? He said: Even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be a Muslim.

By this chain of narration, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever separates from the Muslim community has indeed removed the yoke of Islam from his neck. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the Muslim community? He said: The community of the people of truth, even if they are few.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us. He said: Khalaf ibn Salim narrated to us. He said: Ghandar narrated to us. He said: Awf narrated to us, from Maymun Abu Abdullah, from Zayd ibn Arqam. He said: For a group from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), there were doors opening onto the mosque. So one day he said: Close these doors except the door of Ali. So the people spoke about that. He said: So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) stood, praised Allah and commended Him, then said: As for what comes after, indeed I was commanded to close these doors except the door of Ali, and some of you spoke about that. Indeed, by Allah, I did not close anything nor open it, but rather I was commanded with something, so I followed it.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tamimi narrated to me. He said: My father narrated to me. He said: My master Ali ibn Musa ibn Jafar narrated to me, from his father Musa ibn Jafar, from his father Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: It is not permissible for anyone to be in a state of janaba in this mosque except myself, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, and whoever is of my family, for they are from me.

And by this chain of narration, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Close the doors opening onto the mosque except for the door of Ali.

Ajmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Abu Abd al-Rahman Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Ali al-Nasa'i narrated to us in Egypt. He said: Muhammad ibn Wahb informed me. He said: Miskin ibn Bukayr narrated to us. He said: Shu'ba narrated to us from Abu Balaj, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that the doors of the mosque be closed, so they were closed, except for the door of Ali (peace be upon him).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Dinuri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Baghandi informed me. He said: Muhammad ibn Umar narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Amr narrated to us from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa from Abu Ishaq from al-Ala' from Ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Close the doors to the Mosque except for the door of Ali.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Tamim narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Hakam ibn Utayba from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla from his father. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: No servant will have believed until I am more beloved to him than himself, and my family is more beloved to him than his family, and my progeny is more beloved to him than his progeny, and my essence is more beloved to him than his essence. He said: Then a man from the community said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman! You never cease bringing hadiths by which God enlivens the hearts.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Razma al-Qazwini narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Isa al-Alawi al-Husayni narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Burayd narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah ibn Abi Rafi', from Awn ibn Ubaydullah. He said: I was with Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyya at the entrance of his house. Then Zayd ibn al-Hasan passed by him, and he raised his gaze toward him, then said: A man from the descendants of al-Husayn called Zayd ibn Ali will surely be killed and crucified in Iraq. Whoever looks at his exposed state and does not come to his aid — Allah will throw him face-first into the Fire.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir. He said: I was sitting with Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) when Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) came forward. When Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) looked at him as he was approaching, he said: 'This is a master from his Ahl al-Bayt, and the seeker of their vengeance. Truly noble is the mother who gave birth to you, O Zayd!'

Muhammad ibn Bukran al-Naqqash (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us in Kufa. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, client of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us. He said: Ahmad ibn Rashid narrated to me from his uncle Sa'id ibn Khuthaym, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He said: I performed Hajj and came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said to me: 'O Abu Hamza! Shall I not tell you about a dream I had? I saw as though I had entered Paradise, and I was brought a houri — I have never seen anyone more beautiful than her. While I was reclining on my couch, I suddenly heard a speaker saying: "O Ali ibn al-Husayn! Congratulations to you on Zayd. O Ali ibn al-Husayn! Congratulations to you on Zayd, congratulations to you on Zayd."' Abu Hamza said: Then I performed Hajj afterwards and came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). I knocked on the door; it was opened for me, and I entered. There he was, carrying Zayd in his arms — or he said: carrying a boy in his arms. He said to me: 'O Abu Hamza, this is the interpretation of my vision from before. My Lord has made it come true.' [12:100]

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyaba, who said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) gave me one thousand gold coins and ordered me to distribute them among the families of those who were killed alongside Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him). So I distributed them, and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, the brother of Fudayl al-Rassan, received four gold coins.

Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Hasani narrated to me. He said: Abu Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Wadi'i the judge narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Subayh narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him) said to me: regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic, 'Forgive with gracious forgiveness' [15:85]. He said: Forgiveness without blame.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Humran ibn A'yan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said: Salman al-Farisi (may God have mercy on him) said: One day, I was sitting with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) when 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) came forward. So he said to him: O 'Ali! Shall I not give you glad tidings? He said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: This is my beloved Gabriel, informing me from God — exalted is His majesty — that He has indeed given your lovers and your Shi'a seven characteristics: gentleness at death, harmony in the solitude [of the grave], light in the darkness [of the grave], security at the fright [of the Resurrection], justice at the Scale, passage over the Path, and entry into Paradise eighty years before the rest of the people of the nations.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ayyub ibn Nuh narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Humran narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Whoever speaks about his believing brother based on what his own eyes have seen and his own ears have heard — he is among those concerning whom God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Surely, those who love to see indecency spread among the believers will suffer a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyaba from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Backbiting (ghiba) includes saying about your brother that which Allah has concealed, and slander (buhtan) includes saying about your brother that which is not true of him.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shayba al-Zuhri, from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said: The worst of servants is a servant who has two faces and two tongues. He commends his brother in his presence and devours him in his absence. If he is given [a blessing], he envies him, and if he is afflicted, he abandons him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Musa ibn Umar al-Baghdadi narrated to us, from Ibn Sinan, from Awn ibn Ma'in the seller of hats, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) say: Whoever meets people with one face and disparages them with another face, will come on the Day of Resurrection with two tongues of fire.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bashar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Bakr narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us. He said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us from Thabit, from Anas. He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Obeying the authority is obligatory. Whoever abandons obedience to the authority has abandoned obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and has entered into His prohibition. Surely, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Do not let your own hands throw you into destruction.' (2:195)

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim. He said: Musa ibn Isma’il ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) narrated to me, from his father Isma’il, from his father Musa ibn Ja’far (peace be upon them both), that he said to his Shi’a: O community of the Shi’a! Do not humiliate your necks by abandoning obedience to your sultan. If he is just, then ask God to maintain him, and if he is unjust, then ask God to rectify him, for surely your rectification lies in the rectification of your sultan. Surely the just sultan is in the position of a merciful father, so love for him what you love for yourselves, and hate for him what you hate for yourselves.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Karkhi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: There are three signs of a child of adultery: poor treatment of people, a longing for adultery, and hatred of us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

And by this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Whoever prays the five prayers in congregation during the day and night, then think well of him and accept his testimony.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) and Ali ibn Abdillah al-Warraq both narrated to us. They said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Abu Turab Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Rawayani narrated to us from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani. He said: I visited my Master Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). When he saw me, he said to me: Welcome to you, O Abu'l-Qasim! You are truly our friend. He said: I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! I wish to present my religion to you; if it is acceptable, I shall remain steadfast upon it until I meet God, Mighty and Majestic. He said: Present it, O Abu'l-Qasim. Then I said: I say that God, the Most High, is One — nothing is like unto Him. He is free from two limits: the limit of negation and the limit of likening [to creation]. He does not have a body, nor a form, nor an accident, nor a substance — rather, He is the creator of bodies, the former of forms, the creator of accidents and substances, the Lord of all things, their Master, their Creator, their Maker, and their Originator. And [I say that] Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, the Seal of Prophets — there is no prophet after him until the Day of Resurrection. And his Law is the Seal of Laws — there is no law after it until the Day of Resurrection. And I say that the Imam, the Caliph, and the Master of Authority after him is ...the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), then al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then Ali ibn al-Husayn, then Muhammad ibn Ali, then Ja'far ibn Muhammad, then Musa ibn Ja'far, then Ali ibn Musa, then Muhammad ibn Ali, then you, my master. So Ali (peace be upon him) said: And after me is my son al-Hasan — so what will the people do with the successor after him? He said: I said: And how is that, my master? He said: Because his person will not be seen, nor will it be permissible to mention him by name, until he emerges and fills the earth with equity and justice just as it had been filled with oppression and tyranny. He said: I said: I affirm. And I say that their friend is the friend of God, their enemy is the enemy of God, obedience to them is obedience to God, and disobedience to them is disobedience to God. And I say that the Night Ascension (mi'raj) is true, the questioning in th

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Ali ibn 'Uqba, from his father, from Abu Basir, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). Anger was mentioned in his presence, so he said: Surely, a man becomes so angry that nothing ever pleases him, and he enters the Fire because of that. So when a man becomes angry while he is standing, let him sit, for the wrath of Satan will depart from him. And if he is sitting, let him stand. And if a man becomes angry at a blood-relative, let him go to him, draw near to him, and touch him; for when a blood-relative touches a blood-relative, he becomes calm.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Muthanna, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym. He said: I heard a man from the Ansar say: While the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was sheltering in the shade of a tree on an intensely hot day, a man came and removed his clothes, then began rolling on the scorching ground, burning his back once, his stomach once, and his forehead once, saying: "O self, taste this! For what is with God, Mighty and Majestic, is greater than what you have done to yourself." And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was watching what he was doing. Then the man put on his clothes and came forward. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) gestured to him with his hand and called him. He said to him: "O servant of God! I saw you do something that I have not seen anyone among the people do. What caused you to do what you did?" The man said: "Fear of God, Mighty and Majestic, caused me to do that. I said to my self: O self, taste this! For what is with God is greater than what you have done to yourself." The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: "You have feared your Lord as He is truly to be feared. Indeed, your Lord boasts about you to the people of heaven." Then he said to his companions: "O you who are present, come closer to your companion so that he may pray for you." So they came closer to him and he prayed for them, saying: "O God, gather our affairs upon guidance, make piety our provision, and Paradise our final abode."

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated to us. They said: Abu'l-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sirri narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Tarif al-Kinani, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: When Ali (peace be upon him) assumed the Caliphate and the people pledged their allegiance to him. He went out to the Mosque, turbaned with the turban of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), clothed in the cloak of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), wearing the sandals of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and girded with the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He ascended the pulpit and sat upon it firmly. Then he interlaced his fingers He placed [his hands] at the lower part of his abdomen, then said: 'O assembly of people, ask me before you lose me! This is the vessel of knowledge, this is the saliva of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), this is what the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) fed me morsel by morsel! Ask me, for I have the knowledge of the ancients and the latter ones. By Allah, if the cushion were folded for me and I sat upon it, I would surely give rulings to the people of the Torah according to their Torah until the Torah itself would speak and say: Ali has spoken the truth — he has not lied; he has issued rulings to you according to what Allah revealed in me! And I would give rulings to the people of the Gospel according to their Gospel until the Gospel itself would speak and say: Ali has spoken the truth — he has not lied; he has issued rulings to you according to what Allah revealed in me! And I would give rulings to the people of the Quran according to their Quran until the Quran itself would speak and say: Ali has spoken the truth — he has not lied; he has issued rulings to you according to what Allah revealed in me! While you recite the Quran night and day, is there anyone among you who knows what was

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat from Abu Basir. He said: Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said to me: Do you not become sad? Do you not worry? Do you not feel pain? I said: Of course, by God. He said: So when that happens to you, then remember death, your solitude in your grave, the streaming of your eyes onto your cheeks, the breaking of your joints, the worms eating your flesh, your afflictions, and your cutting off from this world; for indeed that prompts you to perform deeds and deters you from much of the greed over this world.

Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Abu Dharr (may God have mercy on him) passed by the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and with him was Jibra'il (peace be upon him) in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had sought his privacy. When he saw them both together, he withdrew from them without interrupting their conversation.
