Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: O Muhammad! This Abu Dharr has passed by us without greeting us. Had he greeted us, we would have returned his greeting. O Muhammad! He has a supplication that he uses, which is well-known among the people of the heavens. Ask him about it when you ascend to the heavens. When Jibra'il (peace be upon him) ascended, Abu Dharr came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: What prevented you, O Abu Dharr, from greeting us when you passed by us? He said: I thought, O Messenger of God, that the one with you was Dihya al-Kalbi, and that you had sought his privacy for some of your affairs. He said: That was Jibra'il (peace be upon him), O Abu Dharr. And he said: 'Had he greeted us, we would have returned his greeting.' When Abu Dharr learned that it was Jibra'il (peace be upon him), he was overcome with regret — as much as God willed — for not having greeted. So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: What is this supplication that you supplicate with? He informed me that you have a supplication well-known in the heavens. He said: Yes, O Messenger of God, I say: O Allah! I ask You for faith in You, and affirmation of Your Prophet, and wellness from all calamity, and thankfulness for wellness, and needlessness from the most evil of people.

Sulayman b. Ahmad al-Lakhmi narrated to us. He said: al-Hadrami narrated to us. He said: Abbad b. Yaqub narrated to us. He said: Thabit b. Hammad narrated to us from Musa b. Suhayb from Ubada b. Nasi from Abdullah b. Abi Awfa. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made brotherhood bonds between his companions and left Ali (peace be upon him) out. So he said to him: You have made brotherhood bonds between your companions but you left me out? So he said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, I have not left you behind except for myself. You are my brother, my deputy, and my inheritor. He said: What will I inherit from you, O Messenger of Allah? He said: What the prophets before me bequeathed. They bequeathed the Book of their Lord and the tradition of their prophet. And you and your two sons will be with me in my palace in Paradise.

Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Sa'igh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim Muhammad b. Isa b. Muhammad al-Wasqindi narrated to us, saying: My father informed us, saying: Ibrahim b. Dizil narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam b. Sulayman al-Jabali Abu Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ali b. Hashim narrated to us, from Mutayr b. Maymun, that he heard Anas b. Malik say: Salman al-Farisi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me that he heard the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: Surely, my brother, my vizier, and the best of those I leave behind after me is Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him.

Abu Abdillah al-Husayn b. Ahmad al-Alawi from the descendants of Muhammad b. Ali b. Abi Talib narrated to us. He said: Abu'l Hasan Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Ali narrated to us. He said: Abu Ali al-Hasan b. Ibrahim b. Ali al-Abbasi narrated to me. He said: Abu Sa'id Umayr b. Mardas al-Dawlaqi narrated to me. He said: Ja'far b. Bashir al-Makki narrated to me. He said: Waki' narrated to us from al-Mas'udi who raised it from Salman al-Farisi (may God have mercy on him). He said: Iblis passed by a delegation that was taunting the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), so he stood in front of them. The people said: Who is this that stands in front of us? He said: I am Abu Murra. They said: O Abu Murra, do you not hear our words? He said: Curse upon you! You insult your Master Ali b. Abi Talib! They said to him: From where did you learn that he is our Master? He said: From the saying of your Prophet: For whomever I am his Master, then Ali is his Master. O Allah, align with those who align with him, oppose those who oppose him, support those who support him, and abandon those who abandon him. They said to him: Are you one of those who align with him and his partisans? He said: I am neither of those who align with him nor of his partisans, but I love him, and none hates him except that I become their partner in their wealth and their children. They said to him: O Abu Murra, do you say anything regarding Ali? He said to them: Listen to me, O assembly of oath-breakers, deviators, and apostates. I worshipped Allah the Mighty and Majestic among the Jinn for twelve thousand years. When Allah destroyed the Jinn, I complained to Allah the Mighty and Majestic about my solitude, so He ascended me to the heaven of this world. I worshipped Allah the Mighty and Majestic in the heaven of this world for twelve more thousand years in the company of the angels. While we were thus glorifying and sanctifying Allah the Mighty and Majestic, a radiant beam of light passed by us. The angels fell in prostration due to that light and said: Glorious and Holy! The light of an Angel of Proximity or a commissioned prophet. Then a call came from the direction of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: This is not the light of an Angel of Proximity nor a commissioned prophet. This is the light of the clay of Ali b. Abi Talib.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakhai narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from Amr ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah sent Ali to Yemen. A horse escaped and kicked a man, killing him. The relatives brought him before Ali, who ruled the owner not liable. The relatives came to the Prophet complaining. The Prophet said: Ali is not an oppressor and was not created for oppression. The guardianship after me belongs to Ali; his judgment is his judgment and his word is his word. No one rejects them except a disbeliever, and no one accepts them except a believer. The Yemenis accepted. The Prophet said: This is your repentance.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Shamun from Abdullah b. Sinan from al-Fudayl b. Yasar. He said: I went to Zayd b. Ali (peace be upon him) on the morning that he set out in Kufa, and I heard him saying: Who among you will help me fight the Nabateans of the people of the Levant? For, by the One who sent Muhammad in truth as a bringer of good tidings, no one from you who helps me fight them except that I will take his hand on the Day of Resurrection and admit him into Paradise by the permission of God. He said: So when he was killed, I hired a mount and headed toward Medina. I entered upon al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both), and I said to myself: I will not inform him about the killing of Zayd b. Ali, for he will become distressed over it. So when I entered upon him, he said to me: O Fudayl, what did my uncle Zayd do? He said: The tears choked me, so he said to me: Did they kill him? I said: Yes, by God, they killed him. He said: Did they crucify him? I said: Yes, by God, they crucified him. He said: So he began to weep, and his tears flowed down both cheeks of his face as if they were pearls. Then he said: O Fudayl, did you join my uncle in fighting the people of the Levant? I said: Yes. He said: How many of them did you kill? I said: Six. He said: Perhaps you are in doubt about their blood? He said: And I said: If I were in doubt, I would not have killed them. He said: Then I heard him saying: May God make me a partner in that blood. By God, my uncle Zayd and his companions have passed away as martyrs, just like Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and his companions.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti from Hammad b. Uthman from Abdullah b. Abi Ya'fur from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of God (blessings be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon to the people in his Farewell Pilgrimage in Mina in the Mosque of Khayf. He praised God and commended Him, then said: May God grant joy to a servant who heard my sayings and understood them, then delivers them to those who did not hear them. For there may be a carrier of knowledge who is not a person of understanding, and there may be a carrier of knowledge who brings it to one who is more knowledgeable than him. Three things do not cause the heart of a Muslim to feel trouble: sincerity in deeds for God, wishing well for the Imams of the Muslims, and sticking to their community. For their supplications encompass those behind them. The Muslims are brethren: their blood is equivalent, and the lowest of them strives to protect them. They are one hand against those who oppose them.

4 - Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (upon them be peace). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (upon him be peace) said: I will surely describe Islam in a way that no one before me has described it, nor will anyone after me describe it: Islam is submission, and submission is sincerity, and sincerity is certainty, and certainty is performance, and performance is [good] action. Indeed, the believer takes his religion from his Lord and does not take it from his own opinion. O people, your religion, your religion! Hold fast to it, and let no one remove you from it, for a sin in it is better than a good deed in other than it, because a sin in it is forgiven, while a good deed in other than it is not accepted (3).

5 - Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr, from Hisham b. al-Hakam. He said: Abu Shakir al-Disani visited Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq (upon him be peace). He said to him: Indeed you are one of the shining stars, and your forefathers were brilliant full moons, your foremothers were great intellectuals (4), your origin is the most noble of origins, and when scholars are mentioned, then fingers are folded counting you first. So inform me, O riffling overflowing ocean, what is the proof of the creation of the world? Al-Sadiq (upon him be peace) said: It is proven by the nearest of things. He said: And what is it? He said: Al-Sadiq (upon him be peace) called for an egg and placed it on his palm. Then he said: This is a well-protected fortress. Inside it is a thin membrane (1), surrounded by liquid silver and liquid gold. Then it splits open in the form of a peacock. Did anything enter it? He said: No. He said: So this is the proof of the creation of the world. He said: You have informed succinctly, and you have spoken beautifully. And I have known that we do not accept except what we comprehend with our eyes, or hear with our ears, or feel with our hands, or smell with our noses, or taste with our mouths, or what is imagined in the hearts as perception, and what the intellect deduces with certainty. So al-Sadiq (upon him be peace) said: You mentioned the five senses, and they do not benefit anything without a proof, just as darkness is not cut off without a lamp (2).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) that a man visited him and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the proof for the origination of the world? He said: You were non-existent, then you came into existence. And you know that you did not bring yourself into existence, nor did one like you bring you into existence.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amer narrated to us, from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amer, he said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to me, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, he said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) one day, while he was in the mosque of Quba and the Ansar were gathered: O Ali, you are my brother and I am your brother. O Ali, you are my deputy, my vicegerent, and the Imam of my nation after me. God aligns with whoever befriends you, God is the enemy of whoever is your enemy, God hates whoever hates you, God supports whoever supports you, and God abandons whoever abandons you. O Ali, you are the husband of my daughter and the father of my descendants. O Ali, when I was taken up to the heavens, my Lord promised me three things regarding you. He said: O Muhammad! I said: I am at Your service, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You. Then He said: Ali is the Imam of the Godfearing, the Leader of the shining believers, and the Chief of the believers.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Sinan narrated to us, from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad b. al-Mundhir, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: I heard Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari saying that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was in the house of Umm Ibrahim one day, and a group of his companions was with him, when Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) came forward. When the Prophet (may God bless him and his family) saw him, he said: O assembly of people! The best of people after me has come forward to you, and he is your master. Obedience to him is obligatory like obedience to me, and disobeying him is prohibited like disobeying me. O people! I am the House of Wisdom and Ali is its key. The house cannot be reached except by the key. And whoever alleges that he loves me yet hates Ali has lied.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub b. Yazid narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Umayr narrated to us, from Aban b. Uthman, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Indeed the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said one day to Jabir b. Abdullah al-Ansari: O Jabir! You will remain until you meet my descendant Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib, known in the Torah as al-Baqir. When you meet him, deliver my salaam to him. So Jabir visited Ali b. al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and found Muhammad b. Ali (peace be upon them both) with him as a young boy. He said to him: O boy, come forward! So he came forward. Then he said: Turn around! So he turned around. Jabir said: The qualities of the Messenger of God, by the Lord of the Ka'ba! Then he turned to Ali b. al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and said: Who is this? He said: This is my son and the patron of the Order after me, Muhammad al-Baqir. So Jabir rose and fell upon his feet, kissing them, and said: May my soul be sacrificed for yours, O son of the Messenger of God! Accept the greeting of your father. Indeed the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) sends you his salaam. He said: Then the eyes of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) filled with tears. Then he said: O Jabir! Peace be upon my father, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), as long as the heavens and the earth endure. And upon you too, O Jabir, for delivering the greeting.

10 - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-A'mash, from Abaya ibn Rib'i, from Abdullah ibn Abbas who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey to the heavens, Gabriel brought him to a river called 'The Light' (al-Nur), and it is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'He created the darknesses and the light.' When he arrived with him at that river, Gabriel (peace be upon him) said to him: O Muhammad! Cross over with the blessing of Allah, for Allah has illuminated your sight and extended your view ahead. Indeed, this is a river that no one has ever crossed — not an Angel of Proximity nor a commissioned prophet — except that I immerse myself in it every day, then I come out and shake my wings. There is not a single drop that falls from my wings except that... He created the darknesses and the light (Quran 6:1) When he reached that river, Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: O Muhammad, cross over with the blessing of Allah, for Allah has illuminated your sight and extended the path before you. This is a river that no one has ever crossed -- neither a near-stationed angel nor a sent prophet -- except that I have one immersion in it each day; then I come out from it and shake my wings. There is not a drop that falls from my wings except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, creates from it a near-stationed angel having twenty thousand faces and forty thousand tongues, each tongue speaking in a language that the other tongue does not understand. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) crossed over until he reached the veils -- and the veils were five hundred veils, and from one veil to the next was a journey of five hundred years. Then Jibril said: Go forward, O Muhammad! The Prophet said to him: O Jibril, why will you not be with me? He said: It is not permitted for me to pass beyond this place. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went forward as Allah willed until he heard what the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, said: I am the Praised (al-Mahmud) and you are Muhammad -- I derived your name from My Name. Whoever maintains ties with you, I will maintain ties with him; and

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi'l-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar. He said: I heard my master al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Among what God, Mighty and Majestic, confided to Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him) was that He said to him: 'O son of 'Imran, one who claims to love Me has lied, for when the night befalls him, he sleeps away from Me. Does not every lover love seclusion with his beloved? Here I am, O son of 'Imran, watching over My lovers when the night befalls them — I divert their sights from their hearts and place My punishment before their eyes. They address Me as though witnessing Me directly and speak to Me as though in My very presence. O son of 'Imran, grant Me from your heart humility, from your body submission, and from your eyes tears in the darkness of the night, and call upon Me — for you will find Me near and responsive.'

By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication: My God! How can I call upon You when I have disobeyed You? And how can I not call upon You when You know of my love for You in my heart! Even if I have been disobedient, I stretch toward You a hand full of sins, and an eye extended with hope. My Master! You are the Greatest of the great, and I am the prisoner of the prisoners. I am a prisoner of my sin, ransomed by my crime. My God! If You seek me for my sin, then I shall seek You by Your benevolence. If You seek me for my crime, then I shall seek You by Your pardon. If You order me to the Fire, then I shall tell its inhabitants that I used to say: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. O Allah! Obedience gladdens You, and disobedience does not harm You, so grant me what gladdens You, and forgive me of what does not harm You, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih al-Jawaz, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever says "God knows" regarding something that God does not know, the Throne trembles out of exaltation of God, the Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nasir, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida, from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them). He said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the ascetic in this world. He said: The one who abandons its lawful things out of fear of being held to account for them, and abandons its unlawful things out of fear of punishment.

And by this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saw a man intensely mourning his son, so he said: O you! You have mourned over the minor calamity and been heedless of the major calamity. Had you prepared yourself for what happened to your son, your mourning would not have been so intense. Your calamity in abandoning preparedness for it is greater than your calamity over your son.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Three are the closest of creation to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection until He completes the Reckoning: a man whose power in the state of his anger does not lead him to oppress those under his authority; a man who walks between two and does not lean toward one of them over the other by even a barleycorn; and a man who speaks the truth whether it is against him or in his favor.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He said: I said to Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him: By what is the saved one known? He said: Whoever's actions are congruent with his words is saved, and whoever's actions are not congruent with his words is surely put down.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazim ibn Hakim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both. He said: Betake to going to mosques, for they are the houses of Allah on Earth. Whoever goes to them in a state of purity, Allah purifies him of his sins and records him among its visitors. So increase your prayer and supplication in them, and pray in different spots in the mosques, for every spot will bear witness for the one who prayed upon it on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us. He said: Mu'awiya ibn Wahb narrated to us. He said: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, saying: Seek knowledge and adorn it with forbearance and dignity. Humble yourselves to the one you are teaching knowledge to, and humble yourselves to the one from whom you sought knowledge. Do not be tyrannical scholars, lest your faults wash away your truth.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said: Betake to noble character (makarim al-akhlaq), for God Mighty and Majestic loves it. And beware of blameworthy actions, for God Mighty and Majestic hates them. Betake to reciting the Quran, for the degrees of Paradise are proportionate to the verses of the Quran; on the Day of Resurrection the reciter of the Quran will be told: 'Recite and ascend,' and each time he recites a verse, he ascends a degree. Betake to beautiful character, for it brings its possessor to the rank of one who fasts and stands (in night prayer). And betake to good neighbourliness, for God has commanded it. Betake to the tooth stick (siwak), for it is a purifier and a beautiful tradition. Betake to God's obligations and fulfill them. And beware of God's prohibitions and abstain from them.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: On the Day of Resurrection, two believing servants will be brought to stand for the reckoning. Both are from the people of Paradise, one was poor in this world and the other was rich in this world. So the poor one will say: "O Lord! For what reason was I made to stand? By Your glory, You surely know that You did not give me authority so that I could be just or unjust in it, nor did You grant me wealth so that I could fulfill what is due from it or withhold it, and my sustenance only came to me in bare sufficiency, according to what You knew and decreed for me." So God — Glorified be His Majesty — will say: "My servant has spoken the truth; release him, let him enter Paradise." The other will remain until the sweat flows from him so much that if forty camels were to drink from it, it would suffice them. Then he will enter Paradise. The poor one will say to him: "What kept you?" He will say: "The length of the reckoning. One matter kept coming to me after another, being forgiven of me, then I was asked about another matter, until God — Mighty and Majestic — encompassed me in His mercy and joined me with the repentant ones. So who are you?" He will say: "I am the poor one who was with you a little while ago." He (the rich one) will say: "Bliss has indeed changed you after my (leaving you)."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! You are my brother, and I am your brother. O Ali! You are from me, and I am from you. O Ali! You are my deputy (wasi), my vicegerent (khalifa), and the Proof of Allah (Hujjat Allah) over my nation after me. Whoever aligns with you will be made happy, and whoever opposes you will be made wretched.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: The Shi'a of Ali are the triumphant on the Day of Resurrection.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abu Raja' Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj, from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): "When the Day of Resurrection comes, you will be brought, O Ali, upon a noble steed of light, and upon your head will be a crown whose light has already illuminated [everything], and it will nearly blind the eyesight of the people of the gathering. Then a call will come from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is His glory — [asking]: 'Where is the vicegerent of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah?' So you will say: 'Here I am.' Then the caller will announce: 'O Ali! Admit those who love you to Paradise, and those who opposed you to the Fire. For you are the divider of Paradise, and you are the divider of the Fire.'"

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad ibn Harun narrated to us. He said: Ammar ibn Raja' narrated to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Amr informed us, from Abi Salama, from Abi Hurayra. That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, was approached by a man who said: O Messenger of Allah! Did you see how so-and-so travelled the sea with just a few goods and went to China, quickly returned, and came back with great gains, until his very friends envied him, and he was generous to his relatives and neighbours? So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Surely, whenever the wealth of this world increases in quantity and greatness, its owner increases in trial. So do not envy the people of wealth, except for one who is generous with his wealth in the way of Allah. But shall I not inform you of one who carries even fewer goods than your companion, who returns faster than him, who has greater spoils, and whose goodly things are preserved for him in the treasuries of the Throne of the Merciful? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Look to the one who is coming toward you. So we looked, and behold, a man from the Ansar with a shabby appearance. So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Today, this person has ascended to the heights of good deeds and acts of obedience, such that if they were divided among all the people of the heavens and the earth, the least of them would still have his sins forgiven and Paradise would be obligatory for him. They said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? So he said: Ask him to inform you of what he did today. So the companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, went to him and said to him: Congratulations to you over the glad tidings that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, has given regarding you. So what have you done today so that such can be written for you? So the man said: I do not know what I did special today, except that I left my house seeking a need that I had been delayed in pursuing. I feared that I

Muhammad ibn Bukran al-Naqqash, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi, the servant of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad narrated to me. He said: My father narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them, narrated to me. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Betake to the gardens of Paradise. They said: What are the gardens of Paradise? He said: Circles of remembrance (dhikr).

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Said al-Hasan b. Ali al-Adawi narrated to us. He said: Suhayb b. Abbad b. Suhayb narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad narrated to us from his forefathers from al-Husayn b. Ali (peace be upon them): The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) made adjudications with an oath alongside a single witness, and Ali (peace be upon him) made adjudications likewise in Iraq.

And by this chain of narration, from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father (peace be upon them both) from Jabir b. Abdullah. He said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) and ordered him to take oaths with a witness.

Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Hamza ibn al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Wazzan narrated to us from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Humran. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: When you enter the bathhouse, say at the moment you remove your clothes: "O Allah, remove from me the yoke of hypocrisy and make me steadfast upon faith." When you enter the first chamber, say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, and I seek refuge in You from its harm." When you enter the second chamber, say: "O Allah, remove from me the filthy impurity and purify my body and my heart." Then take hot water and place it on your head, and pour some on your legs. If you can swallow a sip of it, do so, for it purifies the bladder. Stay in the second chamber for a while. When you enter the third chamber, say: "We seek refuge in Allah from the Fire, and we ask Him for Paradise" -- repeat it until you leave the hot chamber. Beware of drinking cold water and fuqqa' in the bathhouse, for it upsets the stomach. Do not pour cold water on yourself, for it weakens the body. But pour cold water on your feet when you leave, for it draws disease out of your body. When you put on your clothes, say: "O Allah, dress me in God-consciousness and spare me from destruction." If you do this, you will be safe from every ailment.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Fazari. He said: Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi Nuwayra informed us, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from Qarn Abu Sulayman al-Dabbi. He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), sent some of his law enforcement to Lubayd al-Ataridi. They passed by him at the Mosque of Simak. So Na'im ibn Dajaja al-Asadi went to him and intervened between them and him. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) sent for Na'im, and he was brought to him. He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) raised something to strike him. So Na'im said: By God, indeed your companionship is humbling, and indeed opposing you is disbelief. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: And do you know that? He said: Yes. He said: Let him go.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. al-Saqr al-Sa'igh narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ayyub narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Musa informed us. He said: Hisham b. Yusuf informed us from Abdullah b. Sulayman al-Nawfali from Muhammad b. Ali b. Abdullah b. Abbas from his father from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Love Allah for what He nurtures you with of His blessings. Love me for the sake of Allah's love, the Mighty and Majestic. And love my Ahl al-Bayt for the sake of my love.

Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Mukatib (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Said al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Ma'mun narrated to us from his father al-Rashid, from al-Mahdi, from his father al-Mansur, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): You are my inheritor.

Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Furat b. Ibrahim b. Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Lu'lu'i narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. Nuh al-Jina'i narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from Muhammad b. Marwan from Abu Dawud from Mu'adh b. Salim from Bishr b. Ibrahim al-Ansari from Khalifa b. Sulayman al-Juhni from Abu Salama b. 'Abd al-Rahman from Abu Hurayra. He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went out to battle. When he returned to Medina — and Ali (peace be upon him) had been put in charge of its people — he divided the spoils and gave two shares to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So the people said: 'O Messenger of Allah! You have given Ali b. Abi Talib two shares, even though he stayed behind in Medina!' So he said: 'O people! I plead you by Allah and by His Messenger: did you not see the horseman who charged the polytheists from the right side of the army and defeated them? He then returned to me and said: O Muhammad! Indeed, I have one share with you, and I have dedicated it to Ali b. Abi Talib. And that was Gabriel (peace be upon him). O people! I plead you by Allah and by His Messenger: did you see the horseman who charged the polytheists from the left side of the army and defeated them? He then returned, spoke to me and said: O Muhammad! Indeed, I have one share with you, and I have dedicated it to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him). And that was Michael.' So by Allah, I have only given Ali the share of Gabriel and Michael (peace be upon them both). Then all the people exclaimed Allahu Akbar.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us from 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Abu Ahmad al-Azdi, from 'Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Abu 'Umar al-'Ajami, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: God — Mighty and Majestic is His glory — said: I am God; there is no god but Me. I created the kings, and their hearts are in My hand. Whenever a people obey Me, I make the hearts of the kings toward them [full of] mercy. And whenever a people disobey Me, I make the hearts of the kings toward them [full of] wrath. Behold! Do not busy yourselves with insulting the kings — repent to Me, and I will incline their hearts toward you.

Ja'far ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me from his grandfather 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sha'iri, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There are two classes of my Nation which, if they are rectified, my Nation is rectified, and if they are corrupted, my Nation is corrupted: the rulers and the reciters.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Bashar ibn Yasar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: If you intend something of good, then do not delay it. For a servant fasts on a hot day seeking what is with God, Mighty and Majestic, and God frees him from the Fire; and he gives charity seeking the face of God, and God frees him from the Fire.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said to some of his companions: Do not do unto others what you would not like to be done unto you; and if someone slaps your right cheek, then give him your left.

Al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ziyad al-Nahdi, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: It is sufficient as a victory from God for the believer that he sees his enemy acting in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic.
And by this isnad, he said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: There is not one foot that hastens to the Friday prayer except that Allah forbids its body from the Fire.
And he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever prays with them (the people) in the first row, it is as though he had prayed with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) in the first row.

Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Verily, upon every truth there is a reality, and upon every right action there is a light. So take whatever agrees with the Book of God, and leave whatever contradicts the Book of God.

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Sa'd al-Kinani, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Abdullah ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Ali! You are my vicegerent over my nation in my lifetime and after my death. You are to me as Sheeth was to Adam, as Sam was to Nuh, as Isma'il was to Ibrahim, as Yusha' was to Musa, and as Sham'un was to Isa. O Ali! You are my executor, my inheritor, and the one who will wash my body; you are the one who will bury me in my grave, fulfill my debts, and carry out my promises. O Ali! You are the Commander of the Faithful, the Imam of the Muslims, the leader of those with radiant marks, and the chief of the God-fearing. O Ali! You are the husband of the Mistress of Women, Fatima my daughter, and the father of my two grandsons al-Hasan and al-Husayn. O Ali! Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed the descendants of every prophet in his own loins, but He has placed my descendants in your loins. O Ali! Whoever loves you and aligns with you, I love him and align with him; whoever hates you and opposes you, I hate him and oppose him — for you are from me and I am from you. O Ali! Allah has purified us and chosen us; none of our forebears from the time of Adam have ever met in an illicit union. So none will love us except one whose birth was pure. O Ali! Rejoice at martyrdom, for you will be oppressed and killed after me. So Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah! Will that be while my religion is safe? He said: While your religion is safe. O Ali! You will never go astray and never slip. Were it not for you, the party of Allah would not be known after me.

The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Rayyan b. Shabib. He said: I heard al-Ma'mun say: I always loved the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), but I would show al-Rashid hatred toward them to become closer to him. When al-Rashid went for Hajj, I, Muhammad, and al-Qasim were with him. When he was in Medina, the people sought permission. The last permitted was Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both). He entered, and when al-Rashid looked at him, he stirred and stretched his sight and neck toward him until he entered the room. When he approached, al-Rashid fell to his knees and embraced him. Then he said: How are you, O Aba al-Hasan? How is your family? How is the family of your father? How are you all? What is your condition? He kept asking while Abu al-Hasan would say: Good, good. When he stood up, al-Rashid wanted to stand, but Abu al-Hasan swore upon him, so he sat. He embraced him, greeted him, and bid him farewell. Al-Ma'mun said: I was the boldest of my father's sons toward him. When Abu al-Hasan Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both) left, I said to my father: O Commander of the Faithful! I saw you behave toward this man in a way I never saw you behave with anyone from the sons of the Muhajirin, the Ansar, nor the Children of Hashim! So who is this man? He said: O my son, this is the inheritor of the knowledge of the Prophets. This is Musa b. Ja'far b. Muhammad. If you want correct knowledge, then it is with him. Al-Ma'mun said: At that point, love for them was planted in my heart.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from his father Ali b. Yaqtin. He said: The news was brought to Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both), while he was with a group of his household, about what Musa b. al-Mahdi had resolved regarding his affair. He said to his household: What do you advise? They said: We think that you should distance yourself from this man and hide yourself from him, for indeed his evil cannot be trusted. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) smiled and then said: Sakhina claimed she would overcome her Lord, but surely the one who contends with the All-Conquering will be overcome. Then he (peace be upon him) raised his hand to the sky and said: My God, how many an enemy has sharpened for me the blade of his knife, and honed for me the tip of his blade, and mixed for me deadly poisons, while the eye of his watch did not sleep concerning me. When You saw my weakness in bearing calamities and my inability against the onslaught of disasters, You diverted that from me by Your ability and Your power, not by my ability nor my power. You threw him into the pit he had dug for me, disappointed from what he hoped for in his worldly life, far removed from what he hoped for in his Hereafter. So to You is praise for that, as much as You deserve. My Master, O Allah, seize him by Your might, and blunt his blade against me by Your power. Make for him preoccupation in what concerns him and inability against whoever opposes him. O Allah, assist me against him with a present assault that may be a remedy for my rage and a fulfillment of my right against him. O Allah, connect my supplication with acceptance and rearrange my complaints with change. Acquaint him soon with what You have promised the oppressors, and acquaint me with what You have promised in answering the desperate. Surely You are possessor of great grace and noble beneficence. He said: Then the people dispersed, and they did not gather again except for reading the letter that arrived with the death of Musa b. al-Mahdi.

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: I heard a man from our companions say: When Harun al-Rashid imprisoned Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon him), night befell him. He feared that Harun would kill him. So Musa renewed his purification, faced the qibla, prayed four units for Allah the Mighty and Majestic, then supplicated: O my Master, save me from the prison of Harun and deliver me from his hands. O deliverer of the tree from between sand, clay, and water; O deliverer of milk from between excretion and blood; O deliverer of the child from between the placenta and the womb; O deliverer of fire from between iron and stone; O deliverer of the spirit from between the intestines and the bowels — deliver me from the hands of Harun. He said: When Musa (peace be upon him) supplicated with these supplications, Harun saw a black man in his dream, with a sword unsheathed in his hand, standing over Harun's head, saying: O Harun, release Musa b. Ja'far, or else I will strike your head with this sword. Harun feared his awe and called for his gatekeeper. He said: Go to the prison and release Musa b. Ja'far. The gatekeeper knocked on the prison door. The warden asked: Who is this? He said: The caliph calls for Musa b. Ja'far. The jailer shouted: O Musa, the caliph calls you. Musa stood terrified, saying: He calls me only for evil. He came to Harun trembling. He said: Peace upon Harun. Harun returned the greeting then said: I adjure you by Allah, did you supplicate tonight? He said: Yes. Harun said: What were they? He described his supplication. Harun said: Allah has answered your supplication. O gatekeeper, release this one. Then he called for robes and bestowed three upon him, mounted him on his horse, honoured him, and made him a companion for himself. Then he said: Give me the words so I may memorize them. Then he called for an inkwell and paper and wrote these words. He said: So he released him and handed him to his gatekeeper to deliver him to the house. So Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both) became honoured and noble with Harun, and he would visit him every Thursday.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad b. Isma'il from Mansur b. Yunus from Mansur b. Hazim, and Ali b. Isma'il al-Maythami from Mansur b. Hazim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: There is no breastfeeding after weaning. There is no continuous fasting. There is no orphanhood after puberty. There is no silence from day until night. There is no nomadism after the hijra. There is no emigration after the conquest [of Mecca]. There is no divorce before marriage. There is no emancipation before ownership. There is no oath of a child over his father. There is no oath of a slave over his master. There is no oath of a wife over her husband. There is no vow in disobedience [to Allah]. There is no oath in cutting [family] ties.

Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (ra) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah b. Amer from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Aban b. Uthman from Aban b. Taghlub from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever wants a way to me and wants my hand in his intercession on the Day of Resurrection should connect with my Ahl al-Bayt and bring joy to them.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to me from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Abdullah b. al-Hasan b. al-Hasan b. Ali from his father from his grandfather. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever says 'May Allah bless Muhammad and his family,' Allah, exalted be His majesty, says: 'May Allah bless you.' So let him increase in that. And whoever says 'May Allah bless Muhammad' and does not bless his family will not find the fragrance of Paradise, and its fragrance can be found from a journey of five hundred years away.

Ali b. Ahmad b. Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah. He said: My father narrated to us from Ali b. al-Nu'man from Fadl b. Yunus from Abdullah b. Sinan. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Whoever says twenty-five times every day: 'O Allah! Forgive the believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women,' Allah will record for him, for every believer who has passed and every believer who remains until the Day of Resurrection, a good deed, and will erase from him a sin, and will elevate him by a degree.

And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from Umar b. Yazid. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Whoever prays for forty of his brethren before he prays for himself, his prayer will be answered for them and for himself.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Sulayman ibn Rashid, from his father, from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said: I mentioned one of the prophets in the presence of Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and I blessed him, so he said: When one of the prophets is mentioned, then begin with the blessing upon Muhammad, then upon him. May God bless Muhammad and his family, and all the prophets.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abd Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, said: 'It reached Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that a freedman of hers was disparaging Ali (peace be upon him) and attacking him. So she sent for him, and when he came to her, she said: "O my dear son, it has reached me that you are disparaging Ali and attacking him." He said to her: "Yes, O my mother." She said: "Sit down — may your mother mourn you — until I tell you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then make your choice. Indeed we were nine women with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and it was my night' and my day with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet entered, beaming with joy, his fingers interlaced with Ali's, his hand placed on him. He said: 'O Umm Salama, leave the house and vacate it for us.' So I left and they turned toward each other, conversing privately. I could hear the sound of their speech but did not know what they were saying, until when midday came, I went to the door and said: 'May I enter, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No.' So I was overcome with a severe fall, from fear that he had sent me away in displeasure, or something had descended from the heavens. Then before long I came to the door The second time, I said: Shall I enter, O Messenger of God? He said: No. So I was saddened even more intensely than the first time. Then without delay I came to the door a third time, and I said: Shall I enter, O Messenger of God? He said: Enter, O Umm Salama. So I entered, and Ali (peace be upon him) was kneeling before him, saying: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God! If such-and-such were to happen, what do you command me? He said: I command you patience. Then he repeated the question a second time, and he commanded him patience. Then he repeated it a third time, so he said to him: O Ali, O my brother! If that happens from them, then unsheathe your sword and place it on your shoulder, And strike with it forward again and again until you meet me while your swor

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from a shaykh from Thumala. He said: I visited an old woman from the tribe of Tamim who was narrating to the people. I said to her: May God have mercy on you. Narrate to me some of the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him). She said: I will narrate to you while this elder — as you can see — is sleeping before me? I said to her: Who is this? She said: Abu al-Hamra', the servant of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). So I sat by him, and when he sensed me he straightened up sitting, and said: What? I said: May God have mercy on you. Narrate to me what you saw the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) do with Ali (peace be upon him), for God will ask you about it. He said: You have come to one well-informed. As for what I saw the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) do with Ali (peace be upon him), he said to me one day: O Abu al-Hamra'! Go and summon for me one hundred Arabs, fifty non-Arab men, thirty Coptic men, and twenty Abyssinian men. I brought them, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) stood and arranged the Arabs in a row, then arranged the non-Arabs in a row behind the Arabs, and arranged the Copts in a row behind the non-Arabs, and arranged the Abyssinians in a row behind the Copts. Then he stood and praised God and extolled Him, and glorified God with a glorification the like of which the creation had never heard. Then he said: O assembly of Arabs, non-Arabs, Copts, and Abyssinians! Have you affirmed the testimony that there is no god but God, alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger? They said: Yes. He said: O God, bear witness — he said it three times. Then on the third time he said: Have you affirmed the testimony that there is no god but God, and that I, Muhammad, am His servant and His messenger, and that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the Commander of the Faithful and the master of their affairs after me? They said: O God, yes. He said: O God, bear witness — he said it three times. Then he said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Abu al-Hasan! Go and bring me a parchme

The Shaykh, the Jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: Fasting in Sha'ban is a treasure stored for the servant on the Day of Resurrection. There is no servant who increases his fasting in Sha'ban except that Allah rectifies the affairs of his livelihood and protects him from the evil of his enemy. And indeed, the minimum reward for one who fasts a single day in Sha'ban is that Paradise becomes obligatory for him.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal informed us, from his father, who said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: Whoever seeks the forgiveness of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, seventy times in Sha'ban, Allah will forgive his sins, even if they were similar in number to the stars.

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf narrated to us from Amr ibn Jami' from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever finds pleasure in meeting God, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection with the testimony that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God in his record, and the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and it will be said to him: 'O friend of God, enter from whichever of them you wish,' then let him say when morning comes: 'Praise be to God who took away the night by His power and brought the day by His mercy as a new creation. Welcome to the guardians, and may God greet the two scribes.' Then he turns to his right, then to his left, and says: 'Write: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, I bear witness that there is no god but God, alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. And I bear witness that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, and that God will resurrect those in the graves. Upon that I live, and upon that I die, and upon that I will be raised, God willing. O God, convey my greetings of peace to Muhammad and his family.'

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Khazzaz narrated to us. He said: Isma'il ibn Ali al-Sindi narrated to me, from Muni' ibn al-Hajjaj, from 'Isa ibn Musa, from Ja'far al-Ahmar, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari say: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, my daughter Fatima will come forward on a she-camel from the camels of Paradise, its sides adorned, its muzzle of fresh pearl, its legs of green emerald, its tail of fragrant musk, and its eyes of red rubies. Upon it will be a dome of light whose exterior can be seen from within and whose interior can be seen from without. Inside it is the forgiveness of God, and outside it is the mercy of God. Upon her head is a crown of light. The crown has seventy pillars, each inlaid with pearls and rubies, glowing just as a brilliant star glows on the horizon of the sky. On her right are seventy thousand angels, and on her left are seventy thousand angels. Gabriel is grasping the muzzle of the she-camel, calling at the top of his voice: Lower your gazes until Fatima daughter of Muhammad passes! Then on that day, there will not remain a prophet, nor a messenger, nor a truthful one, nor a martyr, but that they lower their gazes until Fatima daughter of Muhammad passes through. She proceeds until she is alongside the Throne of her Lord, exalted be His majesty. She dismounts from her she-camel and says: My God and my Master! Judge between me and those who oppressed me. O God, judge between me and those who killed my son. Then there comes a call from the direction of God, exalted be His majesty: O My beloved and daughter of My beloved! Ask Me and you will be granted, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. For by My glory and My majesty, no injustice of an oppressor has escaped Me. Then she says: My God and my Master! My offspring, my Shi'a, the Shi'a of my offspring, those who love me, and those who love my offspring. Then there comes a call from the direction of God, exalted be His majesty: Where are the offspring of Fatima, her Shi'a, those who love her, and those who love her offspring? They come forward, surrounded by the angels of mercy. Fatima leads them until she

Hamza b. Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Zayd b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim informed us, from his father, from Ali b. Ma'bad, from al-Husayn b. Khalid, from Abu'l Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Whoever would like to board the Ark of Salvation, grapple onto the Firm Handle, and hold onto the firm Rope of Allah, should align with Ali after me, oppose his enemy, and accept the Imams of Guidance from his descendants; for surely, they are my vicegerents, my deputies, and the Proofs of Allah over His creation after me. They are the Masters of my Nation and the ones who will lead the pious to Paradise. Their party is my party, and my party is the Party of Allah, and their enemies' party is the Party of Satan.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Dharr Yahya b. Zayd b. al-'Abbas b. al-Walid al-Bazzaz (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us in Kufa. He said: My uncle 'Ali b. al-'Abbas narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. al-Mundhir narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. Salim narrated to us from Husayn b. Zayd from 'Ali b. 'Umar b. 'Ali from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from 'Ali b. al-Husayn from al-Husayn b. 'Ali from 'Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). He said: O Fatima! Surely, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, becomes angry with what angers you and becomes pleased with what pleases you. He said: Then Sandal came and said to Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both): O Aba 'Abdillah! These young men come to us from you with false narrations! So Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: And what is that, O Sandal? He said: It has come to us from you that you narrated to them that Allah becomes angry with what angers Fatima and becomes pleased with what pleases her. He said: So Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: O Sandal! Do you not narrate in what you relate that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, indeed becomes angry with what angers His believing servant and becomes pleased with what pleases him? He said: Of course. He said: Then why do you deny that Fatima (peace be upon her) is a believer for whom Allah becomes angry with what angers her and becomes pleased with what pleases her?! He said: So he said: Allah knows best where He places His message.

Abu'l-Hasan 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Shaqir al-Hamadani narrated to us in his house in Kufa... from 'Abdullah b. Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as). He said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (s): Sa'd b. Mu'adh has died. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) stood, and his companions stood with him. While standing at the door, he commanded that Sa'd be washed. When he was embalmed, shrouded, and carried on his coffin, the Messenger of Allah (s) followed him without sandals and without a cloak. He would take to the right of the coffin once and to the left once until he reached the grave. He entered the grave, placed him in the niche, leveled the bricks, and said: Give me stones, give me fresh soil to fill the gaps between the bricks. When he finished and leveled his grave, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Surely, I know that he will decay and that decay will reach him, but Allah loves a servant who, when he does a deed, perfects it. When he evened the earth upon him, the mother of Sa'd said: O Sa'd! Congratulations to you on Paradise. So the Messenger of Allah (s) said: O mother of Sa'd! Stop, do not make assumptions about your Lord, for Sa'd has been afflicted with constriction. So the Messenger of Allah (s) returned, and the people returned. They said: O Messenger of Allah! We saw you do for Sa'd what you have not done for anyone else. You followed his funeral without cloak and without sandals. He said: The angels were without cloaks and sandals, so I did the same. They said: You took to the right of the coffin once and to the left once. He said: My hand was in the hand of Gabriel (as), going where he took me. They said: You commanded his washing, prayed upon his funeral, and placed him in his grave, then you said: 'Sa'd has been afflicted with constriction.' He said: Yes. He had poor character when dealing with his family.

Muhammad b. Ahmad b. 'Ali b. Asad al-Asadi narrated to us in Ray in Rajab 347. He said: ... from Umm al-Darda' from Abu'l Darda'. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever awakes with a healthy body, safe in his path, having the provision of his day, then it is as if the whole world has been given to him. O Ibn Ja'sham! It suffices you from it that which stops your hunger and covers your nakedness. If you have a house that shelters you, then that is good. And if you have a beast to ride, then bravo! But if not, then bread and water from the jar. Whatever is beyond that is reckoning upon you or punishment.

Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Fadl al-Kufi (ra) narrated to us in the Mosque of Amir al-Mu'minin (as) in Kufa... Harun b. Kharija narrated to us. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as) said to me: How far is your house from the Mosque of Kufa? So I informed him. He said: There has not been an Angel of Proximity, nor a commissioned prophet, nor a righteous servant that entered Kufa except that he prayed in it. The Messenger of Allah (s) passed by it on his Night Journey, the angel sought permission, and he prayed two units there. An obligatory prayer in it is worth a thousand prayers, a voluntary prayer is worth five hundred, and sitting in it without even reciting the Quran is worship. So go to it, even if you must crawl.

Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ibrahim al-Laythi narrated to us... I heard Ibn Abi Layla say: I met Ka'b b. 'Ujra, and he said: Shall I not give you a gift? Surely, the Messenger of Allah came out to us, and we said: O Messenger of Allah! You taught us the salaam, but how do we send blessings? He said: Say: O Allah! Bless Muhammad as You blessed Ibrahim. Surely, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And send benedictions upon the Family of Muhammad as You sent them upon the Family of Ibrahim. Surely, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

Al-Hasan b. 'Abdullah b. Sa'id b. al-Hasan b. Isma'il b. Hakim al-'Askari narrated to us... from al-'Ala' b. 'Abd al-Rahman from his father from Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah (s) said: There may be a beggar who is disheveled, dusty, and wearing two tattered garments, who is refused at the doors, but if he were to ask something of Allah, He would fulfill it for him.

Al-Hasan b. 'Abdullah b. Sa'id narrated to us... Musa b. Isma'il b. Musa b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. 'Ali b. Abi Talib (as) narrated to us in 250 AH... from his grandfather Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from 'Ali b. Abi Talib (as), regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Can the reward for good be other than good?' [55:60] He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: Surely, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: What can the reward of one who has been blessed with monotheism be other than Paradise?

Ja'far b. al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja'far b. Batta narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from 'Abdullah b. Muskan, from Abi 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Indeed, the most deserving of people to wish wealth for others are the miserly, because when people become rich they would stop seeking their money. And the most deserving of people to wish righteousness for others are those with flaws, because when people become righteous they would stop pursuing their flaws. And the most deserving of people to wish forbearance for others are the foolish who need to be pardoned for their foolishness. Yet the miserly wish poverty upon the people, and those with flaws wish flaws upon the people, and the foolish wish foolishness upon the people. In poverty lies the need to turn to the miser, in corruption lies the exposure of the flawed, and in foolishness lies the recompense with sins.

Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja'far b. Batta narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Ishaq b. Sa'd narrated to us from Bakr b. Muhammad from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: People on Friday are of three states: A man who attends it attentively and silently before the Imam -- that is an expiation for his sins from one Friday to the next, plus three extra days, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever comes with a good deed shall have tenfold the like of it.' [6:160] And a man who attends it in commotion, flattery, and restlessness -- so that is his lot. And a man who attends it while the Imam delivers the sermon, then stands up to pray -- he has erred in the Sunna, and he is of those who, when he asks Allah Mighty and Majestic, if He wills He grants him, and if He wills He deprives him.

Muhammad ibn Bukran al-Naqqash (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, client of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Ubayd ibn Hamdun al-Ru'asi narrated to me. He said: Husayn ibn Nasr narrated to us, from his father, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: I complained to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) about a debt that I had, and he replied: O Ali! Say: "O God! Enrich me with Your lawful provisions away from Your forbidden things, and through Your grace make me independent of all others." For even if your debt were the size of Sabir, God would settle it on your behalf. Sabir is a mountain in Yemen, and there is no mountain in Yemen more majestic or magnificent than it.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Laythi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf ibn Ziyad narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Hammad narrated to us from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: I am the City of Wisdom — and that is Paradise — and you, O Ali, are its Gate. So how can the guided one be guided to Paradise, when one cannot be guided to it except through its Gate?

Al-Husayn ibn Yahya ibn Durays al-Bajali (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Maslama al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'a narrated to us from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: A man spoke disparagingly of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib in the presence of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, so 'Umar said to him: Do you know who owns this grave? Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. Do not mention 'Ali except in goodness, for if you disparage him you will hurt this one in his grave.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abu Dawud al-Mustaraqqq — whose name is Sulayman ibn Sufyan — who said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: People rise from their beds in three types: a type for whom it is to his benefit and not against him, a type against whom it is and not to his benefit, and a type for whom it is neither beneficial nor harmful. As for the type for whom it is to his benefit and not against him — he is the one who rises from his sleep, performs wudu, prays, and remembers God (Mighty and Majestic). As for the type against whom it counts and not to his benefit — he is the one who does not cease to disobey God until he falls asleep; so that is against him and not to his benefit. As for the type for whom it is neither beneficial nor harmful — he is the one who does not cease sleeping until morning; so that is neither for him nor against him.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Hamza. He said: Dawud b. Kathir al-Raqqi informed me. He said: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Whoever wishes that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, lighten for him the pangs of death, let him maintain his kinship ties and be dutiful to his parents; for when he does so, Allah will ease for him the pangs of death, and he will never be afflicted with poverty in his life.

And by this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Whoever desires that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, admit him into His mercy and settle him in His Paradise, let him beautify his character, extend fairness from himself, show mercy to the orphan, help the weak, and humble himself before Allah who created him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Sa'd al-Askaf, from Ziyad ibn 'Isa, from Abu'l-Jarud, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he used to say: Whoever frequents the mosques will gain one of eight things: a brother who will assist him for Allah's sake, or valuable knowledge, or a firm sign (a clear verse), or an awaited mercy, or a word that will guide him away from ruin, or he will hear a word that will lead him to guidance, or he will abandon a sin out of fear (of God), or out of modesty.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurara ibn A'yan. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed upon the people from one Friday to the next thirty-five prayers, among which is one prayer that God prescribed to be performed in congregation — and that is the Friday prayer — and He has exempted it from nine: the child, the elderly, the insane, the traveller, the slave, women, the ill, the blind, and whoever is at the distance of two parasangs.

And by this chain of narration. He said: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: The qunut in witr is like your qunut on Friday. You say in the supplication of the qunut: O Allah! Your light was perfected so You guided, so praise be to You, our Lord. You stretched out Your hand so You gave, so praise be to You, our Lord. Your forbearance became great so You pardoned, and praise be to You, our Lord. Your face is the most noble of faces, Your direction is the best of directions, Your gift is the most excellent of gifts and the most pleasant. You are obeyed, our Lord, so You give thanks; You are disobeyed, our Lord, yet You forgive whomever You wish. You answer the desperate, You remove harm, You heal the sick, and You deliver from the great distress. No one can repay Your favors, and no speech of any speaker can enumerate Your blessings.
