O Allah! To You gazes were raised, feet were moved, necks were stretched, hands were lifted, and supplications were made with tongues, and judgment was sought from You regarding deeds. Our Lord! Forgive us and have mercy on us, and judge between us and Your creation with truth — You are the best of those who judge. O Allah! To You we complain about the absence of our Prophet, the severity of the time upon us, the occurrence of trials, the gathering of enemies, the great number of our enemy, and our small number. So relieve all of that, O Lord, with a victory from You that You hasten, and a help from You that You strengthen, and a just Imam that You make appear — O God of Truth, Lord of the worlds. Then say in the qunut of witr after this: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him' seventy times, and seek refuge in Allah from the Fire many times. And say after completing the witr following the taslim: 'Glory be to my Lord, the King, the Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise' three times. 'Praise be to the Lord of the morning, praise be to the Splitter of the daybreak' three times.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Bundar ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Fadala, from Abu Abdillah or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon both of them). He said: I heard him say: When a boy reaches three years of age, it is to be said to him seven times: 'Say: There is no god but God.' Then he is left until he reaches three years, seven months, and twenty days, when it is to be said to him seven times: 'Say: Muhammad is the Messenger of God.' Then he is left until he reaches four years. Then it is to be said to him seven times: 'Say: God's blessings be upon Muhammad and his family.' Then he is left until he reaches five years. Then it is to be said to him: 'Which is your right and which is your left?' When he understands that, his face is turned toward the qibla and he is told: Prostrate. Then he is left until he reaches six years. When he reaches six years, he prays and is taught to bow and prostrate. Then he is left until he reaches seven years. When he reaches seven years, he is told: Wash your face and your hands. When he washes them, he is told: Pray. Then he is left until he reaches nine years. When he reaches nine years, he is taught the wudu and made to perform it, and commanded to pray and made to fulfill it. When he has learned the wudu and the prayer, God forgives his parents, God-willing.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar narrated to us. He said: Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami narrated to us from Harun ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il. He said: Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham informed me. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever delays Maghrib until the stars come out without a reason, then I dissociate from him before God.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Muhammad b. 'Isa b. 'Ubayd from 'Ubaydullah b. 'Abdullah al-Dahqan from Darast b. Abi Mansur from 'Abdullah b. Sinan. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Do not use basil twigs nor pomegranate twigs as toothpicks, for they both irritate the vein of leprosy.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said: I visited al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), and he said to me: O Hamza, where have you come from? I said to him: From Kufa. He said: Then he (peace be upon him) wept until his tears soaked his beard. So I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, why have you wept so much? He said: I remembered my uncle Zayd and what was done to him, so I wept. I said to him: And what did you remember of it? He said: I remembered his killing. An arrow had struck his forehead, so his son Yahya came to him and bent over him, and said to him: Be glad, O father, for you will meet the Messenger of Allah, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (blessings of Allah be upon them). He said: Yes, my son. Then he called for a blacksmith, who extracted the arrow from his forehead, and his soul departed with it. He was then taken to a waterway that flowed near the garden of Zaida, and a grave was dug for him there and he was buried, and water was made to flow over him. Among them was a servant from Sindh belonging to one of them, and he went to Yusuf ibn Umar the next morning and informed him of their burying of him. So Yusuf ibn Umar exhumed him and crucified him in Kunasa for four years. Then it was ordered that he be burned with fire, and his ashes were scattered in the winds. May Allah curse his killer and his betrayer. And to Allah, exalted is His name, I complain of what has befallen us, the Ahl al-Bayt of His Prophet, after his death. And through Him we seek help against our enemy, and He is the best helper.

Hadith 4: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn al-Qasim narrated to us by recitation: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Mu'alla narrated to us: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us: Abdallah ibn Bakr al-Muradi narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father [Imam al-Sadiq], from his grandfather [Imam al-Baqir], from Ali ibn al-Husayn [Zayn al-Abidin] (Peace be upon all of them.) He said: While the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was one day seated with his companions, mobilizing them for battle, there came to him an old man bearing the pallor of travel. He asked: Where is the Commander of the Believers? It was said: It is this one. He greeted him, then said: O Commander of the Believers, I have come to you from the direction of Syria. I am an old man of advanced age; I have heard of your virtues more than I can enumerate, and I believe you will soon be killed, so teach me from what Allah has taught you. He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, O elder. Whoever's two days are equal is in loss. Whoever's sole concern is this world, his regret at parting from it will be intense. Whoever's tomorrow is worse than his two days is deprived. Whoever does not care what he damages in his afterlife as long as his worldly life is safe is perishing. Whoever does not monitor the deficiencies in himself will be overwhelmed by passion (desire). Whoever is in deficit, death is better for him. O elder, this world is green and sweet and has its people. The Hereafter also has its people who restrained their souls from boasting before the people of this world; they do not compete for it, nor rejoice in its splendor, nor grieve at its miseries. O elder, whoever fears a night assault will have little sleep. How swift are the nights and days in the life of a servant! Keep your tongue in check and count your words; let your speech be reduced except for good. O elder, be content for the people with what you are content with for yourself, and do to the people what you love to be done to you. Then he [Imam Ali] turned to his companions and said: O people, do you not see the people of this world going about in various states — some writhing in their dying, some visiting the sick and being visited, some gasping out their last breath, some beyond hope, some laid out; and the seeke

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both): The Prophet (may God bless him and his family) prayed the funeral prayer over Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and said: Indeed, ninety thousand angels, including Gabriel, came to pray over him. So I said: O Gabriel, what did he do to deserve your prayer over him? He said: Because of his recitation of "Say: He is God, the One" (Surah al-Ikhlas) while standing, sitting, riding, walking, going, and coming.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Dawud ibn Sarhan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is not appropriate for a woman to leave herself without ornament, even if she just hangs a necklace on her neck. And it is not appropriate for her to leave her hand without dyeing, even if she just wipes it once with henna, even if she has aged.

By this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: When the time comes that Allah, Blessed and Exalted is His majesty, resurrects His servants, the days will be brought forth. The creatures will recognize them by their names and their adornments, and Friday will lead them, having a dazzling light, with the rest of the days following it as though it were a noble bride possessing dignity, being led to one of forbearance and affluence. Then Friday will be a witness and protector for those who hastened to the Friday prayer. Then the believers will enter Paradise in accordance with the extent of their precedence to the Friday prayer.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Ja'far b. Bashir al-Bajali narrated to us, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman b. A'yan, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said: Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgave a man from the people of the desert because of two phrases he supplicated with. He said: 'O Allah! If You punish me, then I am worthy of that, but if You forgive me, then You are worthy of that.' So Allah forgave him.

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdullah b. al-Mughira and Muhammad b. Sinan, from Talha b. Zayd, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: There is nothing more corrupting to the heart than sin. Indeed, the heart engages in sin, and it does not cease working upon it until it overcomes it, turning its bottom into its top and its top into its bottom.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said: There was a Jewish boy who would come frequently to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) until he (the Prophet) grew fond of him. Sometimes he would send him on an errand, and sometimes he would have him write a letter to a people. Then he (the Prophet) missed him for some days and asked about him. Someone said to him: You have left him on the last day of his life in this world. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went to him with some of his companions — and among his (peace be upon him) blessings was that he could hardly address anyone without receiving a response. So he said: O so-and-so! The boy opened his eyes and said: At your service, O Abu al-Qasim! He said: Bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. The boy looked at his father, but his father said nothing to him. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called to him a second time and said the same as he had said the first time. The boy looked to his father but his father said nothing to him. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called to him a third time. The boy looked to his father, and his father said: If you wish, say it; and if you wish, do not. So the boy said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you, Muhammad, are the Messenger of Allah. And he died in his place. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his father: Leave us. Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: Wash him and shroud him, and bring him to me so that I may pray over him. Then he left, saying: Praise be to Allah who saved a soul from the Fire through me today.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma'il al-Munqari, from his grandfather Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever eats clay, itching will occur in his body, he will suffer hemorrhoids, a bad malady will be stirred up in him, and strength will be taken from his legs and feet; and whatever is diminished from his deeds in the time between him and his health before eating it, he will be held accountable for it and punished for it.

Ja'far b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. 'Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. 'Ali narrated to me from his grandfather 'Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There are four things that will not enter a household — even one of them — except that it will be ruined and will not flourish with blessing: betrayal, theft, drinking wine, and adultery.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Amr b. Uthman, from Muhammad b. Adhafir, from Abu Hamza, from Ali b. al-Hazawwar, from al-Qasim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. He said: Fatima (peace be upon her) came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) and mentioned to him the weakness of her condition. So he said to her: Do you not know what Ali's station is with me? He sufficed me in my affairs when he was twelve years old. He fought with the sword before me when he was sixteen years old. He slew the champions when he was nineteen years old. He relieved my sorrows when he was twenty years old. And he lifted the gate of Khaybar when he was twenty-two years old, even though fifty men could not lift it. He said: Then the complexion of Fatima (peace be upon her) brightened, and her feet did not remain still until she came to Ali (peace be upon him) and informed him. So he said: How would it be if he had told you of all of Allah's grace upon me!

And by this isnad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from his father, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever gives one carat to someone from my Ahl al-Bayt in this worldly life, I will recompense him on the Day of Resurrection with a qintar.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: My intercession on the Day of Judgment will not be granted to one who delays the obligatory prayer beyond its appointed time.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Ibn Najiya, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyaba, from Najiya. He said: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: When you pray Asr on Friday, then say: 'O Allah! Bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, the deputies (awsiya) whom Allah is pleased with, with the best of Your blessings. Send benedictions to them with the best of Your benedictions. Peace be upon them, their spirits, their bodies, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' For whoever says this after Asr, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, records one hundred thousand good deeds for him, erases one hundred thousand sins from him, fulfills one hundred thousand needs for him, and raises him by one hundred thousand degrees.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu'l-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Uthman al-Ahwal narrated to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Mihran narrated to us. He said: I visited al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), and with him was a delegation of the Shia. So I heard him say: O community of the Shia! Be an adornment for us, and do not be a disgrace for us. Speak beautifully to the people. Guard your tongues and restrain them from superfluous and ugly speech.

My father (may God have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil and Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh and Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani and al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God be pleased with them) narrated to us. They said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu Hudba, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Tuba (eternal bliss) is for the one who has seen me. Tuba is for the one who has seen one who has seen me. Tuba is for the one who has seen one who has seen one who has seen me.

The illustrious Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to me. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Hammad b. 'Isa from Ibrahim b. 'Umar al-Yamani from Abu'l-Tufayl from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both) from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (blessings of God be upon him and his family) said to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him): "Write what I dictate to you." So he said: "O Prophet of God, do you fear that I may forget?" So he (blessings of God be upon him and his family) said: "I do not fear that you will forget, for I have prayed to God for you that He may protect you and not cause you to forget. But rather, write for your partners." He said: I said: "Who are my partners, O Prophet of God?" He said: "The Imams from your loins. By them my nation will receive rain, by them their supplications will be answered, by them God will ward off their calamities, and by them mercy will descend from the heavens. And this is the first of them." And he pointed with his hand to al-Hasan b. 'Ali (peace be upon him). Then he pointed with his hand to al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Then he said: "The Imams are from his progeny."

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Kinani from his grandfather from Abi 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Verily, God the Mighty and Majestic sent a book unto His Prophet (S) before death came to him and said: 'O Muhammad! This book is your will to the nobleman of your family.' So he said: 'Who is the nobleman of my family, O Gabriel?' He said: "'Ali b. Abi Talib." On the book were seals of gold. So the Prophet (S) gave it to 'Ali (AS) and ordered him to open one seal and act upon it. So he opened a seal and acted. Then he gave it to his son al-Hasan (AS), who opened a seal and acted. Then he gave it to al-Husayn (AS), who opened a seal and found: 'Go out with a people toward martyrdom, for they will not find martyrdom except with you. Ransom yourself for God the Mighty and Majestic.' So he did so. Then he gave it to 'Ali b. al-Husayn (AS), who opened a seal and found: 'Be silent, stick to your house, and worship your Lord until certainty comes.' Then he gave it to Muhammad b. 'Ali (AS), who found: 'Narrate and give edicts. Fear none but God.' Then he gave it to me, and I found: 'Narrate, give edicts, spread the knowledge of your Ahl al-Bayt, affirm your righteous forefathers. Fear none but God, and you are in protection and safety.' Then I will give it to Musa b. Ja'far, and likewise until the rise of the Mahdi (AS).

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Muqatil b. Sulayman from Abi 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: I am the master of the prophets, and my deputy is the master of the deputies, and his deputies are the masters of the deputies. Verily, Adam (peace be upon him) asked Allah the Mighty and Majestic to give him a righteous deputy. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'Verily I ennobled the prophets with prophethood, then I chose My creation, and I made the best of them the deputies.' Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'O Adam, depute Sheeth.' So Adam deputed Sheeth -- and he is Habatullah (the Gift of God) b. Adam. Sheeth deputed his son Shaban, who is the son of Nazla, the houri that Allah bestowed unto Adam from Paradise; so he married her to his son Sheeth. Shaban deputed Mujallath. Mujallath deputed Mahuq. Mahuq deputed Ghathmisha. Ghathmisha deputed Ekhnokh -- and he is Idris the Prophet (peace be upon him). Idris deputed Nahur. Nahur gave it to Nuh the Prophet (peace be upon him). Nuh deputed Sam. Sam deputed 'Athamir. 'Athamir deputed Bar'ithasha. Bar'ithasha deputed Yafith. Yafith deputed Barra. Barra deputed Jafsiyya. Jafsiyya deputed 'Imran. 'Imran gave it to Ibrahim the Friend of the Merciful (peace be upon him). Ibrahim deputed his son Isma'il. Isma'il deputed Ishaq. Ishaq deputed Ya'qub. Ya'qub deputed Yusuf. Yusuf deputed Buthriya'. Buthriya' deputed Shu'ayb (peace be upon him). Shu'ayb gave it to Musa b. 'Imran (peace be upon him). Musa b. 'Imran (peace be upon him) deputed Yusha' b. Nun. Yusha' b. Nun deputed Dawud (peace be upon him). Dawud (peace be upon him) deputed Sulayman (peace be upon him). Sulayman (peace be upon him) deputed Asif b. Barkhiyya. Asif b. Barkhiyya deputed Zakariyya (peace be upon him). Zakariyya (peace be upon him) gave it to 'Isa b. Maryam (peace be upon him). 'Isa deputed Sham'un b. Hammun al-Safa. Sham'un deputed Yahya b. Zakariyya. Yahya b. Zakariyya deputed Mundhir. Mundhir deputed Sulayma. Sulayma deputed Burda. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: Burda gave it to me, and I giv

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-'Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me. He said: Al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Abi Hamza narrated to me from his father from Abu Basir. He said: I said to Abi 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): What was the supplication of Yusuf (peace be upon him) in the pit, for we have disagreed regarding it? So he said: When Yusuf (peace be upon him) was in the pit and despaired of life, he said: 'O Allah! If the mistakes and sins have worn out my face before You, and You will not raise a voice from me to You, and You will not answer a supplication for me, then I ask You by the right of the elder Ya'qub. Have mercy on his weakness, and unite me with him, for You know his tenderness toward me and my longing for him.' He said: Then Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) wept. Then he said: And I say: 'O Allah! If the mistakes and sins have worn out my face before You, and You will not raise a voice from me to You, then I ask You by You, for there is nothing like You; and I turn to You through Muhammad, Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy. O Allah, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah.' He said: Then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Say this, and increase in it, for I often say it at great calamities.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ya'qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya b. Wahb from Abu Sa'id Hashim from Abi 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Four will not enter Paradise: the soothsayer, the hypocrite, the wine addict, and the backbiter (al-qattat) — and he is the gossiper (al-nammam).

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who raised it [to the Prophet]. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) visited his uncle Abu Talib while he was laid out [for burial]. So he said: O uncle! You adopted an orphan, you raised a child, and you supported an adult, so may God reward you with good on my behalf. Then he ordered Ali (peace be upon him) to wash him.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Mas'ud al-Mila'i, from Habba al-'Urni. He said: Abdullah ibn Umar saw two men disputing over the head of Ammar (may God be pleased with him). One said: 'I killed him!' and the other said: 'I killed him!' So Ibn Umar said: 'They are disputing over which of them will enter the Fire first!' Then he said: 'I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: His killer and his plunderer are in the Fire.' When this reached Mu'awiya, he said: 'We did not kill him; rather, the one who brought him killed him.' Shaykh Abu Ja'far ibn Babuwayh (may God be pleased with him) [responded]: By this logic, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would be the killer of Hamza (may God be pleased with him) and the killer of the martyrs with him, because he (peace be upon him and his family) is the one who brought them.

By this chain of transmission, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from Sa'd ibn Aws, from Bilal ibn Yahya al-Absi. He said: When Ammar (may God be pleased with him) was killed, they came to Hudhayfa, and they said: O Abu Abdullah! This man has been killed, and the people have differed, so what do you say? He said: Well then, since you insist, seat me up. He said: So they propped him against the chest of a man from among them, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) saying: Abu al-Yaqthan is upon the natural disposition (fitra) — three times — he will never leave it until he dies.

By this chain of transmission, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Siyah, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Aisha. She said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Ammar ibn Yasir was never given a choice between two matters except that he chose the more challenging of them.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith al-Baghdadi narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, who said: Shu'ayb ibn Rashid narrated to us from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) stood to address the people at Siffin on a Friday — five days before the battle of al-Harir — and said: Praise be to God for His surpassing blessings upon all His creation, the righteous and the wicked alike, and for His conclusive proofs over His creation — those who disobeyed Him and those who obeyed Him alike. If He pardons, it is out of His grace; if He punishes, it is for what their own hands have sent forth — and God is never unjust to His servants. I praise Him for His gracious trials and for the abundance of His blessings, and I seek His help in the religious matters that have befallen us. I believe in Him and I rely on Him — sufficient is God as a guardian. Then indeed I testify that there is no god but God, alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and His religion which He approved of. He was worthy of it and He chose him above all the servants to convey His message and His proofs over His creation — and He was, as He knew him to be, gentle and merciful. He was the most noble of God's creation in lineage, the most beautiful of them in appearance, the most valiant of them in spirit, the most dutiful of them to his parent, and the most trustworthy of them in covenant. Never did a Muslim or a disbeliever attach to him any complaint of injustice at all. Rather, he would be wronged, yet he would forgive; he would have power, yet he would pardon and overlook; until he passed away in obedience to God, patient over what afflicted him, striving for God as He ought to be striven for, worshiping God until certainty (death) came to him. His departure (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was the greatest calamity for all the people of the earth — the righteous and the wicked alike. Then he left among you the Book of God, which commands you to obey God and forbids you from disobeying Him. The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) entrusted me with a covenant that I will never depart from. Your enemy has come before you, and you have recognized who their leader is — he calls t

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said: Furat ibn Ibrahim ibn Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Thahir narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Abdi — known as Ibn al-Qari — narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Wasiti narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas. He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) on the pulpit saying, when word had reached him that some people from Quraysh were denying that he had called Ali the Commander of the Faithful, he said: O people! God, Mighty and Majestic, sent me to you as a messenger and ordered me to appoint Ali as your emir. Whoever I am their prophet, then Ali is their emir — an authority that God, Mighty and Majestic, has placed over you; and He commanded me to inform you of this, so that you may listen to him and obey him. When he commands you, comply; and when he forbids you from something, desist. Know that none of you should claim authority over me in my lifetime nor after my death, for God, Blessed and Exalted, has put him in command over you and called him the Commander of the Faithful — and no one before him was called by this name. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with regarding Ali. Whoever obeys me in it has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys me in it has disobeyed God, Mighty and Majestic — he will have no argument before God, Mighty and Majestic, and his end will be what God, Mighty and Majestic, described in His Book: 'Whoever disobeys God and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will put him into the Fire to abide eternally therein.' [4:14]

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated to me from Musa ibn Abi Ayyub al-Tamimi from Musa ibn al-Mughira from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim. He said: Ali (peace be upon him) was mentioned in the presence of Ibn Abbas after his death, so he said: 'How tragic is the loss of Abu al-Hasan! He passed away, by God — he never changed, never substituted, never fell short, never hoarded, never withheld, and never preferred anything except God. By God, this world was more trivial to him than the sole of his sandal. A lion in battle, an ocean in gatherings, a sage among sages. Alas, he has passed on to the exalted ranks.'

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya al-Dahqan narrated to me. He said: I was in Baghdad with the judge of Baghdad, whose name was Sama'a, when a man from the elders of Baghdad came to him and said: May Allah rectify the judge. I went on Hajj in past years and I passed through Kufa. During my return I entered its mosque. While I was standing in the mosque intending to pray, suddenly before me was a Bedouin woman with flowing locks of hair, wearing a woolen cloak, and she was calling out and saying: O renowned one in the heavens! O renowned one in the Earths! O renowned one in the Hereafter! O renowned one in this world! The tyrants and kings strove to extinguish your light and suppress your remembrance, but Allah refused and willed only exaltation for your remembrance and only brightness and completion for your light, even if the polytheists were averse. He said: So I said: O maidservant of Allah! Who is this that you describe with this description? She said: That is Amir al-Mu'minin. He said: So I said to her: Which commander of the faithful is he? She said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, through whom and through whose wilaya alone tawhid is valid. He said: So I turned toward her, and I did not see anyone.

The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Ruwayani narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud. He said: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) said regarding the saying of God the Mighty and Majestic, 'Faces on that Day will be bright, looking toward their Lord' (75:22-23). He said: Meaning [their faces will be] illuminated, awaiting the reward of their Lord.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu'l Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' narrated to me. He said: Abu'l Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) said, regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "Sight comprehends Him not, yet He comprehends all sight" [6:103]. He said: The imaginations of the hearts cannot comprehend Him, so how could the sight of eyes comprehend Him?!

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, the servant of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami narrated to us. He said: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl narrated to us. He said: I asked Aba Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about Allah, the Blessed and Exalted — will He be seen in the Resurrection? So he said: Glorified be Allah and exalted is He greatly above that! O Ibn al-Fadl! Surely, the sights only perceive that which has a colour and a modality, and Allah is the Creator of colours and modalities.

Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani al-Mukattab (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami narrated to us from Abd al-Azim b. Abdillah al-Hasani from Imam Ali b. Muhammad from Abu Muhammad b. Ali from his father al-Rida Ali b. Musa (peace be upon them). He said: Abu Hanifa departed one day from the presence of al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), and Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon him) encountered him. So he said to him: O young man, from whom does sin originate? He replied: It does not go beyond three possibilities: Either it is from God, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is not from Him, for it is not proper for the Generous One to punish His servant for what he did not commit; or it is from God, the Mighty and Majestic, and from the servant, and it is not proper for the strong partner to oppress the weak partner; or it is from the servant, and indeed it is from him, so if God punishes him, it is for his sin, and if He forgives him, it is by His generosity and munificence.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated, Ubaydullah ibn Musa Abu Turab al-Rawyani narrated from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud. He said: I said to al-Rida: O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say about the hadith that the people narrate that he said: 'Allah descends every night to the heaven of this world'? He said: May Allah curse those who distort the words from their places! By Allah, the Messenger of Allah did not say that. Rather, he said: 'Allah sends down an angel to the heaven of this world every night in the last third, and on Friday night at the beginning. He commands him and he calls: Is there any asker so I may grant him? Is there any repenter so I may accept? Is there any one asking forgiveness so I may forgive? O seeker of good, come forward! O seeker of evil, hold back!' He continues until dawn. At dawn, he returns to his place in the kingdom of heaven. My father narrated this from my grandfather, from his forefathers, from the Messenger of Allah.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hammad ibn Abdullah from Abu Basir from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: When a servant says while in prostration: 'O Allah, O my Lord, O my Master' three times, the Blessed and Exalted responds: 'Here I am, My servant, ask for your need.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, who said: Abu Khalid al-Ka'bi narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Any woman who moves something in the house of her husband from one place to another, wanting to improve it, Allah looks upon her - and whoever Allah looks upon, He does not punish. So Umm Salama said: Men have taken all the good, so what is there for poor women? He said: Rather, when a woman becomes pregnant, she has the status of one who fasts, prays, and strives. When she gives birth, she receives an incomprehensible reward. When she breastfeeds, each suckle equals freeing a descendant of Isma'il. When she finishes, an angel strikes her side: Continue working, Allah has forgiven you.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: There are three - whoever does not have them, his goodness can never be hoped for: he who does not fear Allah in private, he who does not become pious at old age, and he who is not ashamed of his faults.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn al-Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Isma'il ibn Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Surely, a servant will be imprisoned for a sin from his sins for a hundred years, while looking at his wives and brothers in Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qurashi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), that Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: None will be brought up from the earth on the Day of Resurrection except that two angels will be holding him by his arms, saying: Answer the Lord of Glory.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim narrated to me from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari. He said: I was afflicted with extreme poverty, so I visited Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) and he permitted me in. When I sat down, he said: O Abu Hashim! Which of the blessings of God the Mighty and Majestic upon you would you like to give thanks for? Abu Hashim said: I was struck dumb, not knowing what to say to him. So he (AS) preceded and said: He has given you faith, by which He has forbidden your body from the Fire. He has given you wellness, by which He has supported you in obedience. And He has granted you contentment, by which He has preserved you from self-abasement. O Abu Hashim! I only addressed you first with this because I thought that you wanted to complain to me about the One who has done this to you. And I have ordered one hundred gold coins for you — so take them.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ishaq ibn Ammar. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: There is no prayer for a haqin, nor for a haqib, nor for a haziq. The haqin is the one who has urine [and must go], the haqib is the one who has stool [and must go], and the haziq is the one whose foot has been constricted by a leather sock.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa. He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me one day: Do you know how to pray, O Hammad? He said: So I said: O my master, I have memorized the book of Hariz on prayer. He said: So he said: Never mind, stand and pray. He said: So I stood in front of him facing the qibla, and I commenced the prayer, bowed and prostrated. Then he said: O Hammad, you do not know how to pray! How repulsive it is for a man to have sixty years or seventy years pass over him and yet not establish a single prayer with its complete limits! Hammad said: So abasement befell me within myself and I said: May I be your sacrifice, teach me the prayer. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) stood facing the qibla, erect, and released both his hands upon his thighs with his fingers joined together, and drew his feet close until there was a gap of three fingers between them spread apart, and he turned the toes of both his feet toward the qibla, neither deflected from it, in submissiveness and tranquility, and said: God is Greatest. Then he recited al-Hamd with measured intonation and (Say: He is God, the One), then paused briefly for the measure of a breath while standing, then said: God is Greatest, while standing. Then he bowed and filled his palms over his knees spread apart, and pushed his knees back until his back was level — such that if a drop of water or oil were poured on him it would not slide off due to the evenness of his back — and he extended his neck and lowered his gaze. Then he glorified three times with measured intonation and said: Glorified is my Lord, the Magnificent, and His is the praise. Then he stood erect, and when he was firmly established in standing he said: God hears the one who praises Him. Then he recited the takbir while standing and raised his hands to the level of his face. Then he prostrated and placed his palms with fingers joined together between his knees in front of his face, and said: Glorified is my Lord, the Most High, and His is the praise, three times, and he did not rest any part of his body against another. And he prostrated on eight major limbs: And he prostrated on eight major limbs: the forehead, the two palms, the two centers of the knees, and the tips of the big toes of both feet — these

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Hafs narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Ismail narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Salama, from Abu al-Sadiq. He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: My religion is the religion of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and my lineage is the lineage of the Prophet. So whoever attacks my religion and my lineage has surely attacked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Shu'ayb al-Jawhari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Isa ibn Muhammad al-'Alawi narrated to us. He said: Abu 'Amr Ahmad ibn Abi Hazim al-Ghifari narrated to us. He said: 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Sharik, from Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', from al-Qasim ibn Hassan, from Zayd ibn Thabit who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Surely, I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and my progeny, my Ahl al-Bayt. Verily, they are the two vicegerents after me. They shall never separate until they return to me at the Pond.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Umar ibn Sa'd, from Yusuf ibn Yazid, from Abdullah ibn Awf ibn al-Ahmar. He said: When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) intended to set out to Nahrawan, an astrologer came to him and said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, do not travel at this hour — travel after three hours have passed from the day.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Why is that?' He said: 'Because if you travel at this hour, you and your companions will be afflicted with severe harm. But if you travel in the hour I have commanded you to go in, you will triumph, prevail, and obtain all that you seek.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you know what is in the belly of this beast — is it male or female?' He said: 'If I calculate, I will know.' Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Whoever ratifies you in this saying has belied the Quran.' 'Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in which land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.' [Quran 31:34] 'Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) would not claim what you are claiming. Do you allege that you can guide to the hour that steers one away from harm, and [identify] the hour that, if one travels in it, harm befalls him? Whoever ratifies you in this has become needless of seeking Allah's help for that matter, and made it more necessary to turn to you to repel harm from him, and it befits him to direct praise to you instead of to his Lord. So whoever believes in you in this has taken you as a rival and opponent to Allah.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, there is no omen except Your omen, and there is no harm except Your harm, and there is no good except Your good, and there is no god but You.' Then he turned to the astrologer and said: 'Rather, we belie you and oppose you. We will travel in the hour that you have prohibited.'

The esteemed Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh al-Qummi narrated to us, my father narrated, Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi. He said: Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq was asked about wine. He said: The Messenger of Allah said: The first things my Lord prohibited were idol worship, wine drinking, and quarrelling. God sent me as a mercy and to obliterate instruments and affairs of Jahiliyya. My Lord swore: No servant drinks wine except I give him boiling water on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Do not sit with the wine drinker, do not marry him, do not visit him in illness, do not attend his funeral. The wine drinker comes on the Day of Resurrection with darkened face, bleary eyes, slanted mouth, drooling, tongue dangling from the back of his head.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from his father from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: O Ziyad! Beware of argumentation, for it creates doubt, nullifies deeds, and degrades its doer. Perhaps a man may say something for which he is not forgiven. O Ziyad! There was once a community who left the knowledge they were entrusted with and sought knowledge they were spared from, until their discourse led them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they became perplexed; so much so that if a man were called from in front of him, he would reply from behind, or if called from behind, he would reply from in front.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to me, my father narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu al-Yasa' from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Beware of contemplating about Allah, for contemplation about Allah only increases in deviation. Surely, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be comprehended by sights, and He cannot be described by measurement.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Anbasa al-Abid, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Beware of arguing in religion, for indeed it distracts the heart from the remembrance of God, Mighty and Majestic, and it bequeaths hypocrisy, and it forms grudges, and it makes lying easy.

By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, created the intellect, He made it speak. Then He said to it: Come forth. So it came forth. Then He said to it: Go back. So it went back. Then He said to it: By My glory and My majesty! I have not created any creation more beloved to Me than you, and I do not perfect you except in those whom I love. Surely, by you I command, by you I prohibit, by you I punish, and by you I reward.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father. He said: I spoke to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), describing the worship, religion, and virtue of a certain person as being such-and-such. So he said: "How is his intellect?" So I said: "I do not know." So he said: "Indeed, reward is according to the measure of intellect. Indeed, a man from the Children of Israel used to worship God, Mighty and Majestic, on a green, verdant island abundant in trees and pure of water among the islands of the sea. An angel passed by him and said: 'O Lord, show me the reward of this servant of Yours.' God showed him that, and the angel considered it small. God revealed to him: 'Accompany him.' The angel came to him in human form and said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am a worshiper. We heard of your place and worship here, so I came to worship God with you.' He stayed with him that day. When morning came, the angel said: 'Your place is indeed a retreat.' He said: 'If only our Lord had a beast. If our Lord had a donkey, we would herd it here, for this grass goes to waste.' The angel said: 'Does your Lord not have a donkey?' He said: 'If He had a donkey, this grass would not go to waste.' God revealed to the angel: 'I only reward him according to the measure of his intellect.' And al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) never spoke to the worshipers at the full extent of his own intellect." He said: And the Messenger of God said: "We, the company of prophets, were commanded to speak to people at the level of their intellects."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abu Basir. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: The foundations of disbelief are three: greed, arrogance, and envy. As for greed, when Adam (peace be upon him) was forbidden from the tree, greed drove him to eat from it. As for arrogance, Iblis, when he was commanded to prostrate to Adam, was arrogant. As for envy, the two sons of Adam — when one of them killed his companion out of envy.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sukuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) who said: The pillars of disbelief are four: desire, fear, discontent, and anger.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from Abu Waki', from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-A'war, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: There is no good in lying, whether in seriousness or in jest, nor in one of you promising his child something then failing to fulfill it. Indeed, lying leads to immorality, and immorality leads to the Hellfire. One of you will keep on lying until it is said: "He lied and committed immorality." And one of you will keep on lying until there does not remain in his heart even the space of a needle's worth of truthfulness, and so he is called a liar before God.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from more than one person, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Do not backbite, or you will be backbitten; and do not dig a pit for your brother, or you will fall into it yourself; for indeed, as you judge, so shall you be judged.

By this isnad from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Yazid narrated to us from Isma'il ibn Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Sitting in the mosque waiting for the prayer is worship, as long as one does not commit an offense. It was said: O Messenger of Allah! What is the offense? He said: Backbiting.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a servant says 'Allah knows' but he is lying, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Did you not find anyone else to lie upon besides Me?!'

And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Wahb, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says 'Allah knows' regarding something that he does not know, the Throne shakes in veneration of Him.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir narrated to us from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri from Ali ibn Asbat from Ja'far ibn Sama'a from more than one person from Zurara ibn A'yan. He said: I asked Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him): What is the right that God has over His servants? He said: That they say only what they know, and that they stop at what they do not know.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ya'qub Ishaq ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reproached His servants with two verses from His Book: to not speak until they know, and to not reject what they do not know. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Was a covenant not taken from them in the Book that they would not say anything about Allah except the truth?' [7:169] And He says: 'In fact, they rejected the Book without comprehending it and before the fulfilment of its warnings.' [10:39]

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Ibn Shubruma. He said: I never mentioned a hadith that I heard from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) except that my heart would nearly break for him. I heard him say: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). Ibn Shubruma said: And I swear by God, he would not lie upon his father, and his father would not lie upon his grandfather, and his grandfather would not lie upon the Messenger of God. He said: Whoever acts by analogical reasoning (qiyas) is destroyed and has destroyed others. And whoever issues religious rulings to the people while he does not know the abrogating from the abrogated, nor the decisive from the allegorical, is destroyed and has destroyed others.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from more than one person, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) stood to deliver a sermon among the Children of Israel and said: O Children of Israel! Do not impart wisdom to the ignorant, for you will have wronged it; and do not withhold it from those worthy of it, for you will have wronged them.

My father narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: One who acts without insight is like one who travels without a path, and increasing his speed in travel only increases his distance from the path.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal. He said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: God, Mighty and Majestic, does not accept an action except with recognition (ma'rifa), nor does He accept recognition except with action. So whoever recognizes, his recognition will guide him to action. And whoever does not act, he has no recognition. Verily, part of faith is from its other part.

The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Rashid narrated to us. He said: Abu Ma'mar Sa'id ibn Khaytham narrated to us. He said: Sa'd narrated to me from al-Hasan al-Basri, that it reached him that someone was claiming to be diminishing Ali (peace be upon him). So he stood among his companions one day and said: I was determined to lock my door and not leave my house until death comes to me. I was informed that one of you claims that I diminish the best of people after our Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — his companion and intimate, the one who relieved distress in times of calamity, and the slayer of adversaries on the day of combat. A man has departed from you who recited the Quran and revered it, who acquired knowledge and preserved it, who possessed valor and employed it in obedience to his Lord — patient in the bitterness of war, grateful in hardship and distress. He acted by the Book of his Lord and gave sincere counsel to his Prophet, his cousin, and his brother. He was made his brother above all his companions, and he was entrusted with his secret. He strove for him in youth and fought alongside him in maturity. He slew adversaries and brought down knights in defense of God's religion, until war laid down its burdens. He held fast to the covenant of his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — no one could turn him aside, no opponent could sway him. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away while he was pleased with him. The most knowledgeable of Muslims in learning, the most understanding in comprehension, and the foremost in embracing Islam — none equals him in his virtues, none resembles him in his qualities. His soul was restrained from desires; he worked for God in moments of heedlessness; he perfected ritual purity in cold mornings; he was humble in prayers; he cut himself off from pleasures, exerting himself strenuously — of noble character and noble lineage. He followed the practices of his Prophet and traced the footsteps of his Master. So how could I say anything about him that would doom me?! No one I know finds fault with him. So spare us harm and av

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani, and Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Sa'igh (may God be pleased with them) narrated to us. They said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Abu Muhammad Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to me. He said: al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Quddus al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us from al-A'mash. [And through other parallel chains converging on al-A'mash.] And the wording of the hadith follows that of Mundil ibn Ali al-Anazi from al-A'mash, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Dawaniqi sent for me in the middle of the night to come. I remained thinking to myself: The commander of the faithful has not sent for me at this hour except to ask me about the virtues of Ali (peace be upon him). Perhaps if I inform him, he will kill me. Then I performed ablution, wrote my will, put on my shroud and perfumed myself, then went to him. When I arrived, I found Muhammad ibn Ibrahim the Imam sitting with him. When Abu Ja'far saw me, he said: Come closer, O Sulayman! So I came closer until my knees touched his knees. Then he said: What is with you? I have been told that you narrate hadith about Ali's virtues. Tell me the hadith of the bird. I narrated to him the hadith of the bird and the merits Ali displayed. Then he asked about Ali feeding the poor, the orphan and the captive. I recounted how Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them) gave their food to the needy for three days while fasting. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came to Fatima's house and found her weeping from hunger. He was grieved and Gabriel descended with Surah al-Insan (76) regarding their sacrifice. Then I narrated the virtues of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). When they fell ill, the Prophet visited them with some of his companions. He said: O Abu al-Hasan, make a vow for the recovery of your two sons. So Ali, Fatima, and their servant Fiddah all vowed to fast three days. When they recovered, they fasted. Each day at the time of breaking the fast, a needy person came to their door, and they gave away their food. The Prophet called out in Medina and gathered the people to witness their virtue. He declared their lineage and lofty status. The Prophet declared their uncle Ja'far i

The illustrious Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Sleep is the relaxation of the body, speech is the relaxation of the soul, and silence is the relaxation of the intellect.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to me from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Whoever does not have an exhorter from his heart, a chider from his soul, and does not have a guiding companion, his enemy has gained control of his neck.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fizari al-Kufi. He said: Ja'far ibn Sahl narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Muhammad from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa. He said: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said to me: Surely, the family of a man are like his prisoners. Whoever is blessed by Allah with a favor, let him be generous to his dependents. If he does not, that blessing is about to be removed from him.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Minhal al-Qassab together from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever gains wealth from four sources, it will not be accepted from him in four: whoever gains wealth from embezzlement, usury, betrayal, or theft, it will not be accepted from him in zakat, charity, Hajj, or Umra. And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not accept a Hajj or an Umra from forbidden wealth.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mada'ini narrated to me from Fadl ibn Kathir from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever meets a poor Muslim and greets him differently than the way he greets the rich, he will meet Allah the Mighty and Majestic on the Day of Resurrection while He is angry at him.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Rawyani narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to us from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Salman invited Abu Dharr (may God's mercy be upon them both) to his house and offered him two loaves. So Abu Dharr took the two loaves and turned them over. Salman said to him: O Abu Dharr! For what reason do you turn these two loaves over? He said: I feared that they were not well-baked. So Salman became intensely angry and said: How bold you are to turn these two loaves over! By God, the water that is beneath the Throne worked in this bread, and the angels worked in it until they tossed it to the wind, and the wind worked in it until it tossed it to the clouds, and the clouds worked in it until they rained it upon the earth, and the thunder and the angels worked in it until they placed it in its places, and the earth, wood, iron, animals, fire, firewood, salt, and more than I can count all worked in it. So how could you possibly fulfil this gratitude? So Abu Dharr said: I repent to God, and I seek God's forgiveness for what I did, and I apologize to you for what you disliked.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Bishr ibn Maslama from Misma' Abu Sayyar from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever gives charity when he awakes in the morning, Allah removes the bad omen of that day from him.

8 — Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father (peace be upon them all). He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) fell ill with the illness from which he recovered. Fatima the Mistress of Women (peace be upon her) visited him, and with her were al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). She had taken al-Hasan by her right hand and al-Husayn by her left hand, and they walked while Fatima was between them, until they entered the house of A'isha. Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sat on the right side of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the left side of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). They began pressing the part of the Messenger of God's body closest to them, but the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not awaken from his sleep. So Fatima said to al-Hasan and al-Husayn: 'My beloveds! Your grandfather has dozed off. So, depart for now and leave him until he awakes, then return to him.' They said: 'We are not leaving at this time.' So al-Hasan lay on the right arm of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and al-Husayn on his left arm, and they dozed off. They awoke before the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) awoke, and Fatima (peace be upon her), when they had slept, had returned to her house. So they said to A'isha: 'What did our mother do?' She said: 'When you two fell asleep, she returned to her house.' So they went out in a dark, pitch-black night of thunder and lightning, and the sky had let loose its rain. A light blazed for them, and they kept walking in that light, al-Hasan gripping with his right hand al-Husayn's left hand, both walking and talking, until they came to the garden of Banu al-Najjar. When they reached the garden they became confused and remained not knowing where to go. Al-Hasan said to al-Husayn: 'We have become confused and remain in this state, not knowing which way to go. So there is no harm in our sleeping at this hour until morning.' Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Go ahead, my

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Abu Turab Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Ruwyani narrated to us from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani. He said: I said to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of Allah! Narrate a hadith to me from your forefathers (peace be upon them). So he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The people will continue in goodness as long as there is variance among them; when they are equalized, they will perish. He said: I said to him: Tell me more, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Were the veil lifted from you, you would not wish to be buried. So I said to him: Tell me more, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: You cannot accommodate the people with your wealth, so accommodate them with a cheerful face and good reception. For I heard the Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah upon him and his family) say: You cannot accommodate the people with your wealth, so accommodate them with your character. So I said to him: Tell me more, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Whoever blames time will prolong his own regret. So I said to him: Tell me more, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Sitting with the wicked begets suspicion toward the righteous. So I said to him: Tell me more, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The worst provision for the Hereafter is aggression against God's servants. So I said to him: Tell me more, O son of the Messenger of Allah. So he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, fro

1 - The illustrious Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon them). He said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis, Gabriel mounted him upon the Buraq and they arrived at Bayt al-Maqdis. The prayer-niches of the prophets were displayed before him and he led prayer in them. Then he was returned. On his way back, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a camel caravan belonging to Quraysh. They had water in a vessel, and they had lost one of their camels and were searching for it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) drank from that water and poured out the remainder. When morning came, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Quraysh: Indeed, Allah — Exalted be His Majesty — has taken me on a Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis and showed me the traces of the prophets and their dwellings. And I passed by a caravan of Quraysh at such-and-such a place, and they had lost one of their camels. So I drank from their water and poured out the remainder. Abu Jahl said: He has given you the opportunity to expose him — so ask him how many pillars and lamps it has! So they said: O Muhammad! We have someone here who has entered Bayt al-Maqdis — describe for us how many pillars, lamps, and prayer-niches it has. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came and suspended the image of Bayt al-Maqdis before his face, and he began to inform them of what they asked him. When he had informed them, they said: Wait until the caravan arrives and we will ask them about what you have said. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: The proof of that is that the caravan will appear before you at sunrise, led by a grey camel. (1) The next morning they began looking toward the mountain pass, saying: The sun is about to rise. While they were in this state, the caravan appeared before them just as the sun rose, led by a grey camel. They asked them about what the Messenger of Allah (peace

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said: Furat ibn Ibrahim ibn Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Hamdani narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Shami narrated to us from his father. He said: Abu Jarir narrated to us. He said: 'Ata' al-Khurasani narrated to us, raising it (as a mursal narration) from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanam. He said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with a beast smaller than a mule and bigger than a donkey. Its back legs were longer than its front legs, and its stride covered as far as the eye could see. When the Prophet wanted to mount it, it refused. Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: This is Muhammad. So it humbled itself until it pressed against the earth. He said: He mounted it. Whenever it descended, its front legs would rise and its back legs would shorten; and whenever it ascended, its back legs would rise and its front legs would shorten. In the darkness of night, it passed by a loaded caravan. The caravan was scattered by the flapping of the Buraq. A man at the rear of the caravan called out to his servant at the front: O so-and-so! The camels have fled, and so-and-so dropped her load and broke her leg. The caravan belonged to Abu Sufyan. He said: Then he continued until he reached the valley of Balqa'. He said: O Gabriel! I am thirsty. So Gabriel took a bowl of water and gave it to him, and he drank. Then he continued and passed by a group of people hanging by their heels on hooks of fire. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are those whom Allah enriched with lawful things, but they sought the forbidden. He said: Then he passed by a group whose skin was being sewn with needles of fire. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are those who unlawfully take the virginity of women. Then he continued and passed by a man lifting a bundle of firewood; every time he was unable to lift it, more was added. He said: Who is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is the debtor who wants to repay, but every time he cannot, more is added to him. Then he continued until he was at the eastern mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis and felt a hot wind and heard a sound. He said: What is this wind I feel and this sound I hear, O Gabriel?
