He said: This is Hell. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: I

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Ahmad narrated to us. He said: Abu Yahya Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us. He said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us from al-Zuhri. He said: I was with 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and a man from his companions came to him. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: What news do you bring, O man? The man said: My news — O son of the Messenger of Allah — is that I have incurred a debt of four hundred gold coins, and I have no means to pay it off. I have weighty dependants and I have nothing to provide for them. He said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) wept intensely. I said to him: What makes you weep, O son of the Messenger of Allah? He said: Is weeping not reserved for afflictions and great hardships? They said: Indeed it is, O son of the Messenger of Allah. He said: What hardship and affliction is greater for the sanctity of a believer than to see his believing brother in a difficulty he cannot alleviate, and to witness him in poverty he cannot lift? He said: They then dispersed from that gathering. One of the opponents who used to slander 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: How astonishing are these people — on one occasion they claim that the heavens, the earth, and everything obey them and that Allah does not reject any of their requests, then on another occasion they admit to being unable to rectify the situations of the closest of their brothers! News of that reached the man of the story. He went to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, I was told that so-and-so said such-and-such, and that was harder on me than my difficult situation. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: Allah has permitted your relief. O so-and-so, bring my pre-dawn meal (suhur) and my breakfast (futur). She brought two morsels of bread. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said to the man: Take them, for we have nothing else. Allah will relieve you through them and grant you vast goodness through them. The man took them and went to the market not knowing what to do with them, pondering the weight of his debt and the condition of his dependants. Satan whispered to him: What good are these two in the face of your need? He passed by a fishmonger who had a fish that had gone bad and couldn't

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: A man's supplication for his brother in his absence generates sustenance and repels hateful things.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, he said: I saw Abdullah ibn Jundab at the station [of Arafat], and I had not seen a station more beautiful than his. He did not cease stretching his hands toward the sky while his tears flowed down his cheeks until they reached the ground. When the people departed, I said to him: O Aba Muhammad, I have never seen a station more beautiful than yours. He said: By Allah, I only supplicated for my brothers, and that is because Aba al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) informed me that whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, a call is made from the Throne: 'And for you is one hundred thousand fold.' So I disliked abandoning a guaranteed one hundred thousand fold for a single supplication that I do not know whether it will be accepted or not.

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ilwan, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: There is not a single believing man or believing woman — from those who have passed since the beginning of time or those who are yet to come until the Day of Resurrection — except that they will serve as intercessors for whoever says in their supplication: 'O God, forgive the believing men and women.' Indeed, a servant may be ordered to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and when he is brought to account, the believing men and women will say: 'O our Lord, this is the one who used to pray for us, so accept our intercession on his behalf.' Then God will accept their intercession for him, and he will be saved.

Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from my grandfather, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: Whoever supplicates for forty believers before supplicating for himself, his supplication will be answered.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Uqba al-Sayrafi, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi. He said: I said to Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man purifies himself after defecation while wearing a ring on his finger with 'there is no god but Allah' engraved on it. So he said: I consider that disliked for him. I said: May I be your ransom! Did not the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and every one of your forefathers (peace be upon them) do that while their ring was on their finger? He said: Indeed, but they would wear the ring on the right hand. So fear Allah and watch over yourselves. I said: What was the inscription on the ring of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)? He said: Why do you not ask me about those who came before him? I said: Then I ask you. He said: The inscription on the ring of Adam (peace be upon him) was: 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' He descended with it. And when Nuh (peace be upon him) boarded the Ark, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'O Nuh! If you fear drowning, then proclaim My oneness a thousand times, then ask Me for salvation — I will save you from drowning and those who believe with you.' He said: When Nuh (peace be upon him) and those with him were settled in the Ark and raised the sail, the wind stormed against them. Nuh feared drowning, and the wind rushed him, so he could not proclaim the tahlil a thousand times. So he said in Syriac: 'Haluliya a thousand, a thousand times, O Lord, settle [the waters].' He said: The sail settled and the Ark continued on. So Nuh (peace be upon him) said: 'Surely the words by which Allah saved me from drowning are worthy of never leaving me.' He said: So he engraved on his ring: 'There is no god but Allah, a thousand times; O Lord, rectify me.' He said: And when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was placed in the catapult, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) became angry. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'What makes you angry, O Jibra'il?' He said: 'O Lord! Your Friend — there is no one who worships You on the face of the earth besides him — yet You have empowered Your enemy and his enemy against him!' So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi from al-Husayn ibn 'Ilwan from 'Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). He said: I asked my father, the Master of Worshipers (peace be upon him), and I said to him: O father! Inform me about our grandfather, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): When he ascended to heaven and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him with fifty prayers, why did he not ask Him for a reduction for his community until Moses son of 'Imran (peace be upon him) said to him: Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for your community cannot bear that? So he said: O my son! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) does not make suggestions to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, nor does he return to Him regarding anything He commands him. So when Moses (peace be upon him) asked him that and became an intercessor for his community with Him, it was not permissible for him to reject the intercession of his brother Moses (peace be upon him). So he returned to his Lord asking Him for a reduction, until it was reduced to five prayers. He said: So I said to him: O father! Then why did he not return to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him for a reduction from five prayers, when Moses (peace be upon him) had asked him to return to his Lord and ask Him for a reduction? So he said: O my son! He (peace be upon him and his family) wished to secure for his community the reduction along with the reward of fifty prayers, due to the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like' [6:160]. Do you not see that when he (peace be upon him and his family) descended to earth, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came down to him and said: O Muhammad! Your Lord conveys greetings to you and says: 'They are five [counting as] fifty. My word is not changed, and I am not unjust to the servants.' He said: So I said to him: O father! Is it not the case that God, exalted be His remembrance, is not described with a place? So he said: Indeed, God is exalted above that. So I said: Then what is the meaning of the saying of Moses (peace be upon him) to the Messenger of

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi. He said: I said to 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say regarding the hadith that the scholars of hadith narrate: 'Verily, the believers will visit their Lord from their homes in Paradise?' He (peace be upon him) said: O Abu al-Salt! Verily, Allah — Blessed and Exalted — has favoured His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) over all of His creation, from the prophets to the angels. He made his obedience His own obedience, his following His own following, and visiting him in this world and the Hereafter as visiting Him. So He — Mighty and Majestic — said: 'He who obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah' [4:80], and He said: 'Verily, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to Allah — the hand of Allah is over their hands' [48:10]. And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever visits me in my life or after my death has visited Allah, the Majestic.' And the rank of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in Paradise is the highest of ranks, so whoever visits him at his rank in Paradise from his home has visited Allah — Blessed and Exalted. He said: So I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! Then what is the meaning of the report they narrate: 'The reward of saying There is no god but Allah is looking at the Face of Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: O Abu al-Salt! Whoever describes Allah with a face like faces has committed disbelief. Rather, the Face of Allah is His prophets, His messengers, and His Proofs (may Allah's blessings be upon them) — they are those through whom one turns towards Allah, His religion, and knowledge of Him. And Allah — Mighty and Majestic — said: 'All that is upon it shall perish, while the Face of your Lord shall remain' [55:26-27], and He — Mighty and Majestic — said: 'Everything is perishing except His Face' [28:88]. So looking at the prophets of Allah, His messengers, and His Proofs (peace be upon them) in their ranks is a great reward for the believers on the Day of Resurrection. And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever harbours hatred for my Ahl al-Bayt and my progeny will not see m

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of God, I am eager for jihad and energetic.' He said: 'Then fight in the way of God, for if you are killed, you will be alive with God receiving sustenance; if you die naturally, your reward is established with God; and if you return, you will emerge from sins as if you were just born.' The man said: 'O Messenger of God, I have two elderly parents who say they find companionship through me and dislike my departure.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Stay with your parents, for by the One in whose hand is my soul, comforting them for a day and a night is better than a year of fighting.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid. He said: Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi narrated to us from Hannan ibn Sadir from his father. He said: I said to Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him): 'Can a son repay his father?' He replied: 'There is no recompense for him except in two qualities: that the father be a slave, so he buys him and sets him free, or that there be a debt upon him, so he pays it off on his behalf.'

Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyya. He said: The Master of Worshippers, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), looked at Ubaydullah ibn al-Abbas ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and shed tears. Then he said: There is not a day more severe for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) than the day of Uhud, in which his uncle Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Lion of God and the Lion of His Messenger, was killed. After it, the day of Mu'ta, in which his cousin Ja'far ibn Abi Talib was killed. Then he (peace be upon him) said: But there is no day like the day of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Thirty thousand men advanced upon him, claiming to be from this community, each seeking nearness to God, Mighty and Majestic, through his blood. He was reminding them by God, yet they did not heed, until they killed him treacherously, oppressively, and antagonistically. Then he (peace be upon him) said: May God have mercy on al-Abbas, for indeed he sacrificed and endured hardship, and redeemed his brother with his own soul until his two hands were severed. So God, Mighty and Majestic, compensated him with two wings with which he flies with the angels in Paradise, just as He gave to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. And surely al-Abbas has a station with God, Blessed and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection that all the martyrs will envy.

The eminent jurist Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Nasr ibn Muzahim from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Mas'udi from al-'Ala' ibn Yazid al-Qurashi. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) said: My father narrated to me from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said: The Messenger of Allah said: Sha'ban is my month, and Ramadan is the month of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Whoever fasts a day in my month, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever fasts two days in my month, his past sins will be forgiven. Whoever fasts three days in my month, it will be said to him: 'Resume your deeds.' And whoever fasts the month of Ramadan, guards his private parts, holds his tongue, and stops harming people, Allah will forgive his past and future sins, free him from the Fire, place him in the Abode of Settlement, and accept his intercession for as many monotheist sinners as there are grains of sand in the desert of 'Alij.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his father (peace be upon them). He said: Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) visited Harun al-Rashid, and anger had overwhelmed him against a man. So he said to him: You only get angry for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so do not get angrier on His behalf than He gets for Himself.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz narrated to us from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (blessings be upon him and his family) passed by a group of people who were lifting a boulder competitively. He said: What is this? They said: Through this, we determine who is strongest among us. So he said: Shall I not inform you who is truly strongest among you? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The strongest among you is he who, when he is pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into sin or falsehood; when he is discontented, his discontentment does not lead him from speaking the truth; and when he has power, he does not take that which is not rightfully his.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Yunus ibn Zibyan, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) that he said: Gaining fame through worship is a cause for suspicion. Indeed, my father narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them): that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The most devout of people is one who establishes the obligations. The most generous of people is one who pays the zakat of his wealth. The most ascetic of people is one who avoids the forbidden. The most God-fearing of people is one who speaks the truth whether it is for him or against him. The most just of people is one who is pleased for people with what he is pleased with for himself, and dislikes for them what he dislikes for himself. The wisest of people is one who most frequently remembers death. The most enviable of people is one who, under the dust, is secure from punishment and hopes for reward. The most heedless of people is one who does not take heed from the changing of the world from one state to another. The greatest of people in danger in this world is one who does not consider this world a danger to himself. The most knowledgeable of people is one who combines the knowledge of all people with his own. The bravest of people is one who conquers his desires. The most valuable of people is the most knowledgeable among them, and the least valuable is the least knowledgeable. The person with the least pleasure is the envious one. The person with the least comfort is the miser. The stingiest of people is one who withholds what God, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated upon him. The most deserving of truth is the most knowledgeable of it. The least sanctified of people is the transgressor. The least loyal of people are kings. The person with the fewest friends is the king. The poorest of people is the greedy one. The wealthiest of people is one who is not a prisoner to avarice. The best of people in faith is the best of them in character. The noblest of people is the most God-fearing among them. The greatest of people in worth is one who leaves what does not concern him. The most pious of people is one who aband

Muhammad ibn Ali (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari. He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, God — blessed be He and exalted — chose me, selected me, and made me a messenger. He revealed the Master of Books to me. So I said: 'My God and my Master, indeed You sent Musa to Pharaoh, and he asked You to make his brother Harun a vizier to reinforce him and give credibility to his words. And indeed I ask You, O my Master and my God, to make for me a vizier from my family to reinforce me.' So God made Ali my vizier and my brother, and He placed courage in his heart, and He dressed him in awe over his enemy. He was the first to believe in me and affirm me, and the first to affirm the oneness of God with me. And indeed I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for that and He granted it to me. So he is the Master of the Successors. Adherence to him is happiness, and death in obedience to him is martyrdom. His name in the Torah is joined to my name. His wife is the greatest truthful one, my daughter. His two sons are the Masters of the Youth of Paradise, and they are my sons. He, his sons, and the Imams after them are the Proofs of God over His creation after the prophets. They are the gates of knowledge in my nation. Whoever follows them will be saved from the Fire, and whoever follows their example will be guided to the Straight Path. God, Mighty and Majestic, does not bestow love for them upon a servant except that He will bring him to Paradise.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn Muslim. He said: Abu Nu'aym al-Balkhi narrated to us from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may God's mercy be upon him). He said: I was holding the hand of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and we were walking together. We did not stop gazing at the Sun until it set. So I said: O Messenger of God, where does it go? He said: Into the sky. Then it is raised from one heaven to another until it is raised to the highest seventh heaven, until it is beneath the Throne. It then falls in prostration, and the angels appointed over it prostrate along with it. Then it says: O Lord, from where do You command me to rise — from my setting point, or from my rising point? That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Sun runs to a resting place appointed for it; that is the design of the Almighty, the All-Knowing' (36:38) — meaning thereby the fashioning of the Mighty Lord in His dominion over His creation. He said: Then Gabriel comes to it with a garment of radiance from the light of the Throne, proportioned to the hours of the day — long in summer, short in winter, or intermediate in autumn and spring. He said: Then it puts on that garment just as one of you puts on his clothes. Then it proceeds with it through the expanse of the sky until it rises from its rising point. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: It is as though I see it having been detained for about three nights, then stripped of its radiance, and commanded to rise from its setting point. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'When the Sun is rolled up, and when the stars fall' (81:1–2). And the Moon is likewise — in its rise, its course along the horizon of the sky, its setting, and its ascent to the seventh heaven. It prostrates beneath the Throne, and Gabriel comes to it with a garment from the light of the Footstool. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'He is the One who made the Sun a radiance and the Moon a light' (10:5). Abu Dharr (may God's mercy be upon him) said:

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Isa ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abdullah ibn Umar from Abdullah ibn Hammad from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Indeed, when Dhul Qarnayn reached the wall, he crossed it and entered into the darknesses. And behold, he found an angel standing upon a mountain whose height was five hundred cubits. The angel said to him: 'O Dhul Qarnayn! Was there not a path behind you?' Dhul Qarnayn said to him: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am an angel from the angels of the Most Merciful, assigned to this mountain. There is not a mountain that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created except that it has a vein reaching to this mountain. So when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wills to send an earthquake upon a city, He reveals it to me, and I shake it.'
By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Indeed, lightning does not strike one who is remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. 'Ammara narrated to us from his father, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Indeed, earthquakes, the two eclipses, and tremendous winds are among the signs of the Hour. So when you see something of that, then remember the coming of the Day of Resurrection and hurry to your mosques.

My father narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Musa b. Ja'far b. Wahb al-Baghdadi from Ali b. Ma'bad from Ali b. Sulayman al-Nawfali from Fitr b. Khalifa from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: When this verse was revealed — 'And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins' [3:135] Iblis climbed a mountain in Mecca called Thawr and screamed at the top of his voice to his demons, and they gathered to him. They said: 'O our master, why have you called us?' He said: 'This verse has been revealed, so who will address it?' A demon from the devils stood and said: 'I will address it through such-and-such.' He said: 'It is not for you.' Another stood and said the same, and he said: 'It is not for you.' Then the slinking whisperer said: 'I will address it.' He said: 'With what?' He said: 'I make promises and give them false hopes until they commit sin. When they commit sin, I make them forget to seek forgiveness.' He said: 'You are for it.' So he assigned him with this task until the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz informed me. He said: Musa b. Isma'il narrated to me from his father from Musa b. Ja'far from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). He said: A Jew had lent the Messenger of Allah gold coins, and he came to collect. He said to him: O Jew, I do not have anything to give you. He said: I will not leave you, Muhammad, until you repay me. He said: Then I shall sit with you. He sat with him until he prayed Thuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and the morning prayer in that spot. The companions were threatening the Jew. The Messenger of Allah looked at them and said: What are you doing to him? They said: O Messenger of Allah, a Jew has confined you! He said: My Lord did not send me to oppress a treaty-holder or anyone else. When daytime came, the Jew said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. Half my wealth is in the way of Allah. By Allah, I only did what I did to see your description in the Torah. I read your description in the Torah: Muhammad son of Abdullah, born in Mecca, emigrating to Tayba, neither rude nor harsh nor boisterous, not adorning himself with vulgarity or profane speech. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah. Here is my wealth -- judge in it as Allah has revealed. And the Jew had great wealth.

Also, Ali (peace be upon him) said: The bed of the Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) was a cloak. His cushion was leather, its filling was palm fibre. I folded it for him one night, and when morning came, he said: Indeed, the bed has prevented me from the night prayer tonight. So he ordered that it be made into a single layer.

By this chain of narration, He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah visited his daughter Fatima (peace be upon her), and on her neck was a necklace. He turned away from her. She cut it and threw it aside. The Messenger of Allah said to her: You are from me, O Fatima. Then a beggar came, and she gave him the necklace. The Messenger of Allah said: Allah's anger and my anger is intensified against whoever sheds my blood and harms me regarding my progeny.

By this chain of narration. He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah upon him and his family) sent an expedition. When they returned, he said: Greetings to a people who have completed the lesser struggle, yet the greater struggle remains upon them. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the greater struggle? He said: The struggle against the self. Then he said: The best struggle is when one struggles against the self that is between his two sides.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) visited Salman al-Farisi (may God's mercy be upon him) during his illness. And he said: O Salman! Verily, in your illness you have three characteristics: You are in a state of remembrance of God, the Mighty and Majestic; your supplication in it is accepted; and the illness does not leave upon you a sin except that it erases it. May God grant you wellness until the expiration of your appointed time.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Umar ibn Sahl ibn Isma'il al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Zayd ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh narrated to us. He said: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham narrated to us from Sufyan, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Khalid ibn Riba'i. He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) entered Mecca for one of his needs, and he found a Bedouin clinging to the curtains of the Ka'ba, saying: O Owner of the House! The House is Your house, and the guest is Your guest; and for every guest there is a gift from his host — so make my gift from You tonight forgiveness. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to his companions: Do you not hear the words of this Bedouin? They said: Yes. So he said: God is too generous to turn away His guest. He said: When the second night came, he found him clinging to that corner, saying: O Glorious One in Your glory! There is none more glorious than You in Your glory. Grant me glory through the glory of Your glory — a glory that no one knows how it is. I turn toward You, and I seek intercession with You by the right of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad over You. Give me that which none but You can give, and turn away from me that which none but You can turn away. He said: So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to his companions: This, by God, is the Greatest Name in Syriac. My beloved, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings upon him and his family), informed me of it. He asked Him for Paradise, so He gave it to him, and he asked Him to avert the Fire, so He averted it from him. He said: When the third night came, he found him clinging to that corner, saying: O One who cannot be encompassed by any place, and from whom no place is empty, who existed without a 'how' — — sustain this Bedouin with four thousand dirhams! He said: So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) proceeded to him and said: O Bedouin! You asked your Lord for hospitality and He gifted you; you asked Him for Paradise and He gave it to you; you asked Him to avert the Fire from you and He averted it. But on this night you ask Him for four thousand dirhams! The Bedouin said: Who are you? He said: I am 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. The Bedouin said: You, by God, are what I seek — with you I have laid down my need. He said: Ask, O Bedouin. He said: I

The exalted Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Ahmad Abd al-Aziz b. Yahya b. Ahmad b. Isa al-Juludi al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Sahl narrated to us. He said: Al-Khidr b. Abi Fatima al-Balkhi narrated to us. He said: Wahib b. Nafi' narrated to us. He said: Kadih narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them all). Regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin,' he said: Yasin is Muhammad (blessings of Allah upon him and his family), and we are the Family of Yasin.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Aziz b. Yahya narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Mu'adh narrated to me. He said: Sulayman b. Dawud narrated to us. He said: Al-Hakam b. Thahir narrated to us from al-Suddi from Abu Malik. Regarding the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: "Peace be upon the Family of Yasin" [37:130], he said: Yasin is Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad b. Ali al-Isfahani. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Umar al-Nahdi informed me. He said: My father narrated to me from Muhammad b. Marwan from Muhammad b. al-Sa'ib from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas. Regarding the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: "Peace be upon the Family of Yasin" [37:130], he said: Upon the family of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad b. Ali al-Isfahani from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Makhul b. Ibrahim informed us. He said: Abd al-Jabbar b. al-Abbas al-Hamadani narrated to us from Ammar b. Abi Mu'awiya al-Dihni from Amira bt. Af'a. She said: I heard Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) saying: This verse was revealed in my house: "Surely, Allah only wishes to remove uncleanliness from you, O Ahl al-Bayt, and purify you with a thorough purification" [33:33]. She said: There were seven in the house: the Messenger of Allah, Gabriel, Michael, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (blessings of Allah upon them). She said: And I was at the door, so I said: O Messenger of Allah! Am I not from Ahl al-Bayt? He said: You are from the wives of the Prophet. And he did not say: You are from Ahl al-Bayt.

By this chain of transmission, from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Isma'il b. Aban al-Azdi informed us. He said: Abdullah b. Khirash al-Shaybani narrated to us from al-Awwam b. Hawshab from al-Taymi. He said: I visited A'isha, and she narrated to us that she saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) He called Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). He said: O Allah, these are my Ahl al-Bayt, so remove uncleanliness from them and purify them with a thorough purification.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. Amer narrated to us from al-Mu'alla b. Muhammad al-Basri from Ja'far b. Sulayman from Abdullah b. al-Hakam from his father from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Surely, Ali is my deputy and my vicegerent. His wife, Fatima, the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, is my daughter. al-Hasan and al-Husayn, the two Masters of the Youth of Paradise, are my two sons. Whoever aligns with them has aligned with me, and whoever opposes them has opposed me, and whoever defies them has defied me, and whoever is neglectful of them has been neglectful of me, and whoever is good to them has been good to me. May Allah connect with whoever connects with them, and cut off whoever cuts them off, and support whoever aids them, and assist whoever assists them, and cause failure to whoever fails them. O Allah, each of Your prophets and Your messengers had a heavyweight and a household. So, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn are my household and my heavyweight; so remove uncleanliness from them and purify them with a thorough purification.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa b. Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Ali b. Salim from his father from Thabit b. Abi Safiyya from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever would be gladdened by Allah gathering all goodness for him should align with Ali after me, and align with his supporters, and oppose his enemies.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Al-Abbas b. al-Fadl narrated to us. He said: Abu Zur'a narrated to us. He said: Uthman b. Muhammad b. Abi Shayba al-Absi narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Numayr narrated to us, from al-Harith b. Hasira, from Abu Sulayman Zayd b. Wahb, from Abdullah ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: My wilaya and the wilaya of my Ahl al-Bayt is a safeguard from the Fire.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Fazari, from Abbad b. Ya'qub, from Mansur b. Abi Nuwayra, from Abu Bakr b. Ayyash, from Abu Qudama al-Faddani. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever is blessed by Allah with the recognition of my Ahl al-Bayt and their wilaya, then indeed Allah has gathered all goodness for him.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: Whoever establishes the obligations of God, abstains from what God has prohibited, perfects his wilaya to the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet of God, and dissociates himself from the enemies of God, Mighty and Majestic, then let him enter from whichever of the eight gates of Paradise he wishes.

Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Shu'ayb al-Jawhari (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Isa ibn Muhammad al-'Alawi narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri narrated to us in Kufa. He said: Al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-'Urni narrated to us from 'Amr ibn Jami', from 'Amr ibn Abi'l-Miqdam. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: These two verses were revealed concerning the people of our wilaya (guardianship) and the people of our enmity: 'As for one who is of those brought near — then relief and satisfaction' — meaning in his grave — 'and the Garden of Bliss' — meaning in the Hereafter. 'And as for one who is of those who belie the truth and are misguided — then his reception will be boiling water' — meaning in his grave — 'and burning in Hell' — meaning in the Hereafter.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them both) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who said: Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi and Abu Yusuf Ya'qub ibn Yazid al-Anbari the scribe narrated to us from Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever loves us, the Ahl al-Bayt, should praise God for the first of blessings. It was said: What is the first of blessings? He said: A pure birth. And none loves us except one whose birth is pure.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from more than one person, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever awakes and finds the coolness of our love upon his heart should praise God for the beginning of blessings. It was said: What is the beginning of blessings? He said: A pure birth.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ziyad al-Nahdi, from Ubaydullah ibn Salih, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! Whoever loves me, loves you, and loves the Imams from your descendants, let him praise God for the purity of his birth. For none will love us except one whose birth is pure, and none will hate us except one whose birth is impure.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Ishaq narrated to us. He said: Isma'il b. Ibrahim al-Hilwani informed me. He said: Ahmad b. Mansur Bazraj narrated to us. He said: Hadiyya b. Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abd al-Hamid b. Ja'far narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ziyad al-Yamami narrated to us from Ikrima b. Ammar, from Ishaq b. Abdullah b. Abi Talha, from Anas b. Malik. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: We, the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, are the masters of the people of Paradise: the Messenger of God, Hamza the Master of Martyrs, Ja'far the one of two wings, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and the Mahdi.

Ali ibn Abdallah al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdallah ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari narrated to us. He said: al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan from 'Amr ibn Khalid from Sa'd ibn Tarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: I am the master of the children of Adam, and you, O Ali, and the Imams from your descendants, are the masters of my nation. Whoever loves us has loved God, and whoever hates us has hated God, and whoever aligns with us has aligned with God, and whoever opposes us has opposed God, and whoever obeys us has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys us has disobeyed God.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Mansur al-Sayqal, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When I was taken on the Night Journey to heaven, my Lord enjoined upon me three phrases regarding Ali. He said: 'O Muhammad!' I said: 'I am at Your service, my Lord.' He said: 'Indeed, Ali is the Imam of the God-fearing, the leader of the bright-faced and radiant-limbed, and the chief of the believers.'

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Salama al-Ahwazi, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Ahmad ibn 'Imran ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Khalid ibn 'Isa al-Ansari, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who raises it [to the Prophet]. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: The saints (siddiqun) are three: Habib al-Najjar, the believer of Al Yasin, who says: 'Follow the messengers; follow those who do not ask you for any reward, and who are rightly guided' (Quran 36:20-21) and Hizqil, the believer of the Family of Pharaoh; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib — and he is the best of them.

And by this chain of narration, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali informed me, who said: Al-Abbas ibn Abd Allah narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mas'ud, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The most beloved of my Ahl al-Bayt to me and the best [person] I leave behind after me is Ali ibn Abi Talib.

And by this chain of narration, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Al-Hakam ibn Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Amr ibn Harith al-Ashja'i, from Bardha'a ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Khalil, from Salman (may God's mercy be upon him). He said: I visited the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) when he was dying, and he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib is the best of those I leave behind me.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim narrated to us. He said: Yahya ibn al-Husayn narrated to us from Sa'd ibn Tarif from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata from Salman al-Farisi (may God have mercy on him). He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) saying: O assembly of the Muhajirun and Ansar! Shall I not guide you to that by which, if you hold firmly to it, you will never go astray after me? They said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: This Ali is my brother, my legatee, my vizier, my inheritor, my vicegerent, and your Imam. So love him for the sake of love for me, and honour him for the sake of my honour, for indeed Gabriel commanded me to say this to you.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Alawiyya narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad. He said: Al-Mas'udi narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Qasim al-Kindi narrated to us from Sa'd ibn Talib from Uthman ibn al-Qasim al-Ansari from Zayd ibn Arqam. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Shall I not guide you to that by which, if you follow it, you will never be destroyed or go astray? They said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: Verily, your Imam and your wali is Ali ibn Abi Talib. So consult him, refer to him, and believe him, for Gabriel commanded me of this.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated to us in the City of Peace (Baghdad). He said: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya Abu Abdillah and al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sukuni narrated to us. They said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sukuni narrated to us. He said: Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us from Abu al-Mutahhar al-Madhari, from Sallam al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), from Abu Burza, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), He said: Surely, God — Mighty and Majestic — made a covenant with me regarding Ali. I said: 'O Lord, reveal it to me.' He said: 'Listen.' I said: 'I am listening.' He said: 'Surely, Ali is the Banner of Guidance, the Imam of My friends, the light of those who obey Me, and he is the word that I have bound upon the God-fearing. Whoever loves him loves Me, and whoever obeys him has obeyed Me.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) — in a long hadith — in which he says: Verily, when God, the Blessed and Exalted, made His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ascend [on the Night Journey], He said to him: O Muhammad! Your prophethood has been completed and your sustenance has been cut off, so who will be for your community after you? So I said: O Lord! I have examined Your creation, but I did not find anyone more obedient to me than Ali ibn Abi Talib. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Me too, O Muhammad, so who is for your community? I said: O Lord! I have examined Your creation, but I did not find anyone with a more intense love for me than Ali ibn Abi Talib. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Me too, O Muhammad, so inform him that he is the Banner of Guidance, the Imam of My devotees, and a light for whoever obeys Me.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith narrated to us in the City of Peace (Baghdad). He said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Rafi' al-Bahili narrated to us. He said: Abu Ghassan al-Masma'i narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us. He said: Imran ibn Jarir narrated to us from al-Hasan. He said: Umar said: Surely, I have never seen anyone among the people more fitting to lead them to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet than him — meaning, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Umar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Ghanam ibn Hakim narrated to us. He said: Shurayh ibn Maslama narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us from Abd al-Jabbar from al-A'sha al-Thaqafi from Abu al-Sadiq. He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said to me: This verse is for us or about us: 'And We wish to confer favour upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them Imams and make them the inheritors.' [28:5]

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Zayd narrated to us from Abdullah b. al-Fadl from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the night I was made to travel to heaven, my Lord — Mighty is His majesty — spoke to me and said: 'O Muhammad!' So I said: 'I am at Your service, my Lord.' So He said: Indeed, Ali is My Proof over My creation after you. He is the Imam of the people of My obedience. Whoever obeys him has obeyed Me, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Me. Therefore, establish him as a sign for your Nation so that they may be guided through him after you.

The eminent Shaykh Abu Jafar Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father and Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid and Jafar b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated to us. They said: al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah b. Amer from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Marazim b. Hakim from Abi Basir. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (upon him be peace) said to a man from his companions: Shall I not inform you of the reason why Salman and Abu Dharr embraced Islam? So, the man said — and he erred: As for the Islam of Salman, I know it, so inform me of the reason why Abu Dharr embraced Islam. So Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq said: Surely, Abu Dharr was in Batn Marr herding his sheep when a wolf came to the right of his sheep. So Abu Dharr drove it away with his staff. Then the wolf came to the left of his sheep. So Abu Dharr drove it away with his staff. Then he said to it: By Allah, I have not seen a wolf more wretched than you nor eviller. So the wolf said: Eviller — by Allah — than me are the people of Mecca. Allah sent them a prophet yet they belied him and insulted him. The words of the wolf reached the ears of Abu Dharr. He said to his sister: Bring me my feeding bowl and my vessel and my staff. Then he ran until he entered Mecca. He found a circle of people gathered, so he sat among them. They were insulting the Prophet and abusing him just as the wolf had said. So Abu Dharr said: This, by Allah, is what the wolf informed me of. They continued in this state until the day ended and Abu Talib came. Some of them said to others: Stop, for his uncle has come. When he came close, they honored and revered him. Abu Talib did not cease being their speaker and orator until they dispersed. When Abu Talib stood up, I followed him. He turned to me and said: What do you need? I said: This is the prophet raised among you. He said: What do you need from him? So Abu Dharr said to him: I believe in him and accept him, and he will not command me to do a thing except that I will obey him. So Abu Talib said: Do you bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah? He said: So I said: Yes, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. He said: Tomorrow at this hour, come to me. The

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: The feet of a false witness will not move from their place until the Fire becomes due for him.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa from 'Ali b. al-Hakam from Aban al-Ahmar from Salih b. Maytham from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: There is not a man who bears false witness over the wealth of a Muslim man to deprive him of it except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, decrees a deed to the Fire in its place for him.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Najran from Abi Jamila from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abi Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever conceals a testimony or gives a testimony to shed the blood of a Muslim person or to seize the wealth of a Muslim person will come on the Day of Resurrection with a darkness on his face extending as far as the eye can see, and blemishes on his face. The creatures will know him by his name and lineage. And whoever bears a true testimony to enliven the right of a Muslim person will come on the Day of Resurrection with a light on his face extending as far as the eye can see. The creatures will know him by his name and lineage. Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Do you not see that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "And bear true testimony for Allah."

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from a man from Abd al-Qays, from Salman (may the mercy of Allah be upon him), that he passed by the graves and said: Peace be upon you, O people of the graves from among the believers and the Muslims. O people of the abodes! Do you know that today is Friday? When he returned to his house and slept and sleep overcame his eyes, a visitor came to him and said: And upon you be peace, O Aba Abdillah. You spoke and we heard. You greeted and we returned it. You said: Do you know that today is Friday? And we know what the birds say on Friday. He said: And what do the birds say on Friday? He said: They say: Holy, holy, our Lord is the Merciful, the King. Whoever swears by His name falsely has not recognized the greatness of our Lord.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Hammad b. Isa from al-Husayn b. al-Mukhtar from Abi Abdillah Ja'far b. Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Surely, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates the one who sells his merchandise by swearing false oaths.

By this chain of narration, from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Uthman b. Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever swears by Allah must be truthful, and whoever is not truthful will have nothing with Allah. Whoever has someone swear to him by Allah must be pleased, and whoever is not pleased will have nothing with Allah.

Ali b. Ahmad b. Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah, from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal, from Abdullah b. Bukayr, from Zurara b. A'yan. He said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say: A man entered a mosque in which was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and hastened his prostration in a way that was unbefitting and less than what constitutes a prostration. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: He pecked like the pecking of a crow. If he dies upon this, he dies upon a religion other than the religion of Muhammad.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi al-Qurashi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Said ibn Ghazwan, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Satan does not cease to be fearful and panicked before the son of Adam as long as he prays the five prayers at their appointed times. But when he neglects them, Satan emboldens against him and leads him into great sins.

By this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Abu Basir, who said: I visited Umm Humayda to console her over [the death of] Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). She wept, and I wept due to her weeping. Then she said: O Abu Muhammad! If you had seen Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at the time of his death, you would have witnessed something astonishing, He opened his eyes and said: 'Gather for me all those who have kinship with me.' She said: We did not leave a single person out — all were gathered. She said: Then he looked at them and said: 'Surely, our intercession does not reach one who takes prayer lightly.'

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hijr ibn Za'ida, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever deliberately leaves off a single hair [unwashed] from the state of ritual impurity (janaba), then he is in the Fire.

Ali ibn Isa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Sulami, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) and said: O Muhammad! As-Salam (God) conveys the greeting to you and says: 'I created the seven heavens and all that is in them, and the seven earths and all that is upon them. I did not create a place more magnificent than the Rukn and the Maqam. Yet if a servant were to supplicate to Me there from the moment I created the heavens and the earths, and then were to meet Me as a rejector of the wilaya of Ali, I would cast him headlong into Saqar.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurara ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Friday prayer is an obligation, and gathering for it with the Imam is an obligation. If a man abandons three Fridays without a reason, he has abandoned three obligations, and none abandons three obligations without a reason except a hypocrite. And he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever abandons the congregational prayer out of aversion to it and to the Muslim congregation without a reason, then no prayer is [recorded] for him.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) stipulated upon the neighbours of the mosque that they must attend the congregational prayer. And he said: Groups of people who do not attend the prayers must certainly desist, or I shall command a mu'adhin to call the adhan and then make the iqama, then command a man from my household — and he is Ali — to burn their homes with bundles of firewood, because they do not come to the prayer.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Fajr. When he finished, he turned his face toward his companions and asked whether a group of people had attended. They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: Are they away (travelling)? They said: No. He said: Know that there is no prayer harder on the hypocrites than this prayer (Fajr) and Isha.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: There is no believer who lets his brother down when he is capable of supporting him, except that God lets him down in this world and the Hereafter.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever spreads a report against a believer intending thereby to disgrace him and destroy his reputation so that he falls in the eyes of the people — God, Mighty and Majestic, will remove him from His wilaya to the wilaya of Satan.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Salama al-Ahwazi narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Musa, the son of the sister of al-Waqidi. He said: Abu Qatada al-Harrani narrated to us from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-'Ala' al-Hadrami from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib from Ibn 'Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting one day, and with him were 'Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them all). So he said: O Allah! You know that these are my Ahl al-Bayt and the dearest of people to me. So love those who love them, hate those who hate them, align with those who align with them, oppose those who oppose them, and support those who support them. Make them purified from every uncleanliness and protected from every sin. Aid them with the Holy Spirit. Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: O 'Ali! You are the Imam of my nation and my vicegerent over it after me. You are the leader of the believers to Paradise. It is as though I see my daughter Fatima coming forth on the Day of Resurrection on a noble mount of light. To her right will be seventy thousand angels, to her left seventy thousand angels, before her seventy thousand angels, and behind her seventy thousand angels — leading the believing women of my nation to Paradise. Whichever woman prays five prayers in the day and night, fasts the month of Ramadan, makes pilgrimage to the Sacred House of Allah, gives zakat on her wealth, obeys her husband, and aligns with 'Ali after me — she will enter Paradise by the intercession of my daughter Fatima. She is truly the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds. It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah! Is she the Mistress of the Women of her own world? The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: That is for Maryam daughter of 'Imran. As for my daughter Fatima, she is the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds — from the first to the last. She will stand in her prayer niche, and seventy thousand angels from the nearest angels will greet her with salaam. They will call to her just as the angels called to Maryam, saying: 'O Fatima! Indeed Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds.' [3:42] Then he turned to 'Ali (peace b

The Shaykh, the Jurist Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Safwan b. Yahya, from Abu al-Sabah al-Kinani. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon him: Inform me about this saying -- whose saying is it? I ask Allah for faith and God-consciousness, and I seek refuge in Allah from the evil consequences of affairs. Surely the most honourable of speech is the remembrance of Allah, and the head of wisdom is obedience to Him. The most truthful of sayings, the most eloquent of exhortations, and the most beautiful of narratives is the Book of Allah. The most trustworthy of bonds is faith in Allah, and the best of creeds is the creed of Ibrahim, and the best of traditions is the tradition of the prophets of Allah, and the best of guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family. The best of provisions is God-consciousness, the best of knowledge is that which benefits, the best of guidance is that which is followed, the best of richness is richness of the soul, and the best of what is cast into the heart is certainty. The adornment of speech is truthfulness, and the adornment of knowledge is doing good. The most noble of deaths is martyrdom, and the best of affairs is that with the best consequence. What is little and sufficient is better than what is much and distracting. The wretched is one who is wretched in the womb of his mother, and the fortunate is one who learns from others. The shrewdest of shrewdness is piety, and the most foolish of foolishness is immorality. The worst of narration is falsehood, the worst of affairs is their innovations, the worst of blindness is blindness of the heart, and the worst of regret is regret on the Day of Resurrection. The greatest of sinners in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a lying tongue. The worst of earnings is the earning of usury, the worst of consumption is consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, and the most beautiful adornment for a man is tranquility with faith. Whoever seeks reputation, Allah will make him heard of. Whoever recognizes tribulation is patient with it, and whoever does not recognize it rejects it. Doubt is disbelief. Wh

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal, from Marwan b. Muslim. He said: Abu Abdillah Jafar b. Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: My father narrated to me from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). He said: Allah, exalted is His Majesty, said: Whichever servant obeys Me, I do not assign him to other than Me. And whichever servant disobeys Me, I assign him to himself, then I do not care in which valley he perishes.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr. He said: One who heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrated to me that he said: One who disobeys Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not truly love Him. Then he recited: You disobey God yet you manifest your love for Him -- this is impossible, a strange thing in conduct. Had your love been sincere, you would have obeyed Him, for surely the lover is obedient to the one he loves.
By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) would say: For every people is a government they watch for, and our government will manifest at the end of time.

By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) would frequently say: The knowledge of the clear path is evident for him who seeks it, but I see the hearts are blinded from the clear path. I am astonished at the one who perishes while his salvation is present, and I am astonished at the one who is saved.

By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) would say: Act with deliberation, for surely you will die. And choose for yourself, O human being, for it is as though what has already occurred never happened once it has passed, and as though what is yet to come has already been.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. al-Dahhak narrated to us. He said: Hisham b. Muhammad narrated to me from his father. Hisham said: And some of it was reported to me by Abu Mikhnaf Lut b. Yahya and more than one of the scholars, regarding words that occurred between al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and al-Walid b. Uqba. Al-Hasan, peace be upon him, said to him: I do not blame you for insulting Ali, peace be upon him, for indeed he lashed you eighty lashes for wine, and killed your father as a prisoner by the command of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, on the Day of Badr. And indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named him in more than one verse a believer, and named you a transgressor. And indeed the poet said regarding you and regarding Ali, peace be upon him: Allah revealed in the Book upon us, regarding Ali and regarding al-Walid, a recitation. So al-Walid assumed the position of disbelief, and Ali assumed the position of faith. He who was a believer worshipping Allah is not like one who was a transgressor, a traitor. Soon al-Walid will be summoned after a short while, and Ali to the recompense openly. So Ali will be rewarded there with gardens, and there al-Walid will be given humiliation.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Umar ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Asim narrated to us. He said: Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him). He said: Salman the Good (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, saying: O Aba al-Hasan! Rarely do you come while I am in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) except that he says: "O Salman! This one and his party are the triumphant on the Day of Resurrection."

By this chain of narration, from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib. He said: Atiyya ibn Ismail ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari narrated to me. He said: Abu Umara Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Khashshab narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas ibn Yazid al-Najrani and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Warraq narrated to us. They said: Dirar ibn Sard narrated to us. He said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hasan, from Anas ibn Malik. He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Ali will clarify for my nation that in which they will disagree after me.

By this chain of transmission, from Bakr ibn Abdullah, who said: Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah and Abdullah ibn al-Salt al-Juhdari narrated to us. They both said: Ibn A'isha narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hamadani, from his father, who said: When Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) buried Fatima, he stood at the edge of the grave — this was in the middle of the night, for he had buried her at night — then he began to recite: For every gathering of two intimate friends there is a parting, / And all that is done before death is brief. / Indeed my loss of one person after another / Is an indication that no intimate friend endures. / My memory will be turned away from, and my love forgotten, / And after me, the intimate friend will find another intimate friend.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Isa al-Farra', from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur. He said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: Whoever's outward appearance is weightier than his inner self, his Scale [of deeds] will be lightened.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Malik ibn Masma' ibn Malik, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: He said: O Sama'a! A believer will never be free from four trials: a neighbor who harms him, a devil who leads him astray, a hypocrite who follows his tracks, and a believer who envies him. I said: May I be your sacrifice! A believer who envies him? He said: O Sama'a! Know that he is the most severe of them against him. I said: And how is that? He said: Because he says something about him, and he is believed in that.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Salama al-Ahwazi narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdallah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Hammam narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Jamil al-Raqqi narrated to us. He said: Layth narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Abdallah ibn Abbas. He said: We were sitting in a gathering of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was among us. We saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pointing with his gaze toward the sky. So we looked, and we saw a cloud approaching. He said to it: 'Come forth.' So it came forth. Then he said to it: 'Come forth.' So it came forth. Then he said to it: 'Come forth.' So it came forth. Then we saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) standing upright on his feet, and he reached his hands into the cloud until the whiteness of the armpits of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became visible to us. Then he extracted from that cloud a white vessel filled with fresh dates. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ate from the vessel, and the vessel glorified [Allah] in the palm of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then he passed it to Ali ibn Abi Talib. So Ali (peace be upon him) ate from the vessel, and the vessel glorified [Allah] in the palm of Ali (peace be upon him). A man said: O Messenger of Allah! You ate from the vessel and then passed it to Ali ibn Abi Talib! Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, caused the vessel to speak, and it said: There is no god but Allah, Creator of darkness and light. Know, O people, that I am the gift of the Truthful to His Speaking Prophet. None eat from me except a prophet or a deputy of a prophet.

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadawayh al-Mu'addib (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad al-Mu'min, from al-Mushma'ill al-Asadi. He said: I went on Hajj one year, then I went to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Where have you come from, O Mushma'ill? I said: May I be your sacrifice! I was on Hajj. He said: Do you know what reward the pilgrim receives? I said: I do not know until you teach me. He said: When a servant circumambulates this House seven times, prays its two rak'ahs, and performs the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwa, God records six thousand good deeds for him, erases six thousand sins from him, raises him six thousand levels, fulfills six thousand of his worldly needs, and reserves the same for the Hereafter. I said to him: May I be your sacrifice! This is truly a great amount! He said: Shall I not inform you of something greater than that? I said: Of course. So he (peace be upon him) said: Fulfilling the need of a believing person is better than a Hajj, another Hajj, another Hajj — until he counted ten Hajj pilgrimages.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us.
