He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyya, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from the Master of Worshippers 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: The believer blends his knowledge with forbearance. He sits to learn, listens to be safe, and speaks to make understood. He does not disclose what he has been trusted with even to his friends, nor does he withhold his testimony from his enemies. He does not perform any righteous deed out of ostentation, nor does he leave it out of shyness. If he is praised, he fears what they say, and he seeks God's forgiveness for what they do not know. He is not deceived by the praise of those who do not know him, and he is mindful of the reckoning of those who do know him. The hypocrite forbids but does not restrain himself, and commands what he himself does not do. When he stands in prayer, he complains; when he bows, he slumps; when he prostrates, he pecks; and when he sits, he sprawls. He spends his evening preoccupied with food, even though he is not fasting; and he wakes up in the morning preoccupied with sleep, even though he did not stay up the night. If he speaks to you, he lies; if he makes a promise to you, he breaks it; if you entrust him with something, he betrays it; and if you disagree with him, he backbites you.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid. He said: Sahl ibn al-Marzuban al-Farisi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd ibn al-Mukhtar, from his father, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) went out one day while riding, and Ali (peace be upon him) went out walking alongside him. So he said to him: O Abu al-Hasan! Either ride or turn back, for God, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me that you should ride when I ride, walk when I walk, and sit when I sit — except when it is a limit from the limits of God that requires you to stand or be seated in it. God has not honoured me with an honour except that He has honoured you with its like. He distinguished me with prophethood and the mission and made you my wali in that — you uphold His commandments and manage His difficult affairs. By He who truly sent Muhammad as a prophet: he who denies you has not believed in me; he who repudiates you has not accepted me; and he who disbelieves in you has not believed in God. Your virtue is from my virtue, and my grace to you is the grace of God. And this is the saying of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic: "Say, in the grace of God and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate." [Quran 10:58] For the grace of God is the prophethood of your Prophet, and His mercy is the wilaya of Ali ibn Abi Talib. "In that" — meaning, in prophethood and wilaya — "let them rejoice" — meaning, the Shi'a — "it is better than what they accumulate" — meaning, their opponents with their families, their wealth, and their children in this world. By God, O Ali! You were not created except so that your Lord may be worshipped, so that through you the landmarks of religion may be known, and through you the path of study may be rectified. He who has strayed has strayed from you, and no one shall be guided to God, the Mighty and Majestic, who is not guided to you and to your wilaya. And this is the saying of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic: "And indeed I am most forgivin

The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) passed by a people who were weeping. So he said: What are these people weeping over? So it was said: They are weeping over their sins. He said: Then let them abandon them, and they will be forgiven.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz. He said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said to the apostles: O Children of Israel! Do not regret what you have missed from your world when your religion is safe, just as the people of this world do not regret what they have missed from their religion when their world is safe.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from his father, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: I heard my father narrating from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said: There is not a prayer whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before the people: Go to the fires that you have kindled on your backs and extinguish them with your prayer.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi from his father from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi from al-A'mash from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd. He said: Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari was asked about Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), so he said: He is the best of Allah's creation from the first to the last, with the exception of the prophets and the messengers. Surely, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not create any creation after the prophets and the messengers more honored by Him than Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and the Imams from his descendants after him. I said: What do you say about those who hate him and diminish him? So, he said: None hate him except a disbeliever, and none diminish him except a hypocrite. I said: What do you say about those who take him as their master and take the Imams from his descendants after him as their masters? So, he said: Surely, the Shi'a of Ali and the Imams from his descendants are the triumphant and secure ones on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said: What do you think, if a man were to go out calling people to misguidance, who would be the closest people to him? They said: His followers and his supporters. He said: And if a man were to go out calling people to guidance, who would be the closest people to him? He said: His followers and his supporters. He said: Likewise Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) — in his hand will be the Banner of Praise on the Day of Resurrection. The closest people to him will be his followers and his supporters.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Whoever goes to a blameworthy place and is accused [of something associated with it], he has none to blame but himself.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) would go out every morning and patrol the marketplaces of Kufa, one market at a time. With him was a whip on his shoulder, and it had two strips, and it was called al-Sabiba. He would stand at every market and call out: O merchants! Seek goodness [from Allah], conclude each transaction with ease, be close to the consumers, adorn yourselves with forbearance, abstain from lying and false oaths, desist from injustice, relieve the oppressed, do not come close to usury, maintain proper measurement and balance, do not undervalue the people's things, and do not spread corruption in the land. He would roam through all the markets of Kufa and say this. Then he would say: Pleasure will fade away from those who attained its sweetness from the forbidden, and what remains is sin and disgrace. Harsh consequences remain in its aftermath — there is no good in a pleasure after which comes the Fire.

By this chain of narration. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to call out to the people three times in Kufa after leading the final Isha prayer, so that the people of the mosque could hear: "O people! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy on you, for you have been called to departure. Why linger upon this world after you have been called to leave it! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy on you, and move forth with the best provision at your disposal, and that is God-consciousness. Know that your path leads to the Return, your passage is over the Sirat, the greatest horror is before you, and upon your road is an arduous steep pass and terrifying, fearful stations that you must pass through and halt at. Either by the mercy of Allah you are delivered from their horror, the greatness of their danger, the severity of their appearance, and the intensity of their trial; or by destruction after which there is no recovery."

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us. He said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad b. Umar from Musa b. Ibrahim from Abi'l Hasan Musa b. Ja'far from his father from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her) said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family): May my father and mother be your ransom! A woman who had two husbands, and they all die and enter Paradise - which of the two will she be with? He (s) said: O Umm Salama! She will choose the one with more beautiful character and who was better to his family. O Umm Salama! Surely, beautiful character achieves the good of this world and the Hereafter.

Ali b. Abdullah al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad b. Isma'il b. Bazi' from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Some of the companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said to the Prophet: O Messenger of Allah, why do we feel toward our children what they do not feel toward us? He said: Because they are from you, and you are not from them.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Abdi, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: O Abdullah! When you pray an obligatory prayer, pray it at its time like the prayer of one bidding farewell, who fears he will never return to it again. Then direct your gaze to the place of your prostration, for if you knew who was to your right and to your left, you would perfect your prayer. And know that you are in the presence of One who sees you while you cannot see Him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi, from Abu Ja'far al-Attar — a shaykh from the people of Medina. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of God! My sins have become numerous and my good deeds have weakened. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Increase your prostrations, for indeed it brings down sins just as the wind brings down the leaves of a tree.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Aban ibn Taghlub. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: Verily, when the believer has a nightmare, his sins are forgiven. And verily, when he is afflicted in his body, his sins are forgiven.

Ali ibn Isa (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Mujawir, from Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Tahhan, from Abu Basir. He said: I heard from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): that Isa, the Spirit of Allah, passed by a people who were making noise and commotion. So he said: What is wrong with these people? It was said: O Spirit of Allah! So-and-so the daughter of so-and-so is being given in marriage to so-and-so the son of so-and-so on this very night of hers. He said: They noise about today and will weep tomorrow. One of them said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Because their companion will die on this very night of hers. Those who agreed with his statement said: God has spoken the truth and His Messenger has spoken the truth. The people of hypocrisy said: How close is tomorrow! When they awoke in the morning, they came and found her in her [usual] state — nothing had happened to her. So they said: O Spirit of Allah! Surely, the one whom you informed us yesterday would die has not died! So Isa (peace be upon him) said: God does what He wills. Take us to her. So they went racing one another until they knocked on the door, and her husband came out. Isa (peace be upon him) said to him: Seek permission for me to see your wife. He said: So he went to her and informed her that the Spirit of Allah and His Word was at the door with a group. He said: She stayed veiled in her curtained area, so he entered upon her and said to her: What did you do last night? She said: I did not do anything except what I have been doing in the past. A beggar would come to us every Friday eve, and we would give him what would suffice him until the next [Friday]. He came to me this very night of mine, but I was occupied with my affairs and my family was busy. He called out but no one answered him. He called out again and no one answered, until he called out repeatedly. When I heard his calls, I got up, veiled myself, and gave him as we used to give him. So he said to her: Move away from your sitting place. Then, there was found beneath her clothes a serpent like a tree trunk, biting its own tail. So he (peace be upon him) said: Because of what you did, God has averted this from you.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir. He said: Awn ibn Abdullah ibn Masud became ill, so I went to visit him (in his illness). He said: Shall I not narrate a hadith from Abdullah ibn Masud to you? I said: Yes, of course. He said: Abdullah said: While we were with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), he suddenly smiled. So I said: What is the matter with you, O Messenger of God — why did you smile? He said: I am astonished at the believer and his fear of illness. If he only knew what reward he receives through illness, he would love to remain ill until he meets his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashar, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah al-Dahqan, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Musa ibn Ja'far (AS), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever sweeps a mosque on Thursday, the eve of Friday, and removes from it a speck of dust that could enter one's eye, he is forgiven.

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever makes the Quran his speech and the mosque his home, Allah will build a house for him in Paradise.

And by this isnad, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever hears the call in the mosque and then exits from it without a legitimate reason, then he is a hypocrite, unless he intends to return to it.

18 - Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Lakhmi informed me in what he wrote to me. He said: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Rumahis ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Habib ibn Qays ibn Amr ibn Ghaziyya ibn Jushm ibn Bakr ibn Hawazin narrated to us in Rimada al-Qaysiyin, the exalted Rimada. He mentioned that he was one hundred and twenty years old. He said: Ziyad ibn Tariq al-Jushami narrated to us, and he was ninety years old. He said: My grandfather Abu Jarwal Zuhayr narrated to us, and he was the chief of his people. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) took us captive on the day of the conquest of Khaybar. While he was separating the men from the women, I leapt forward until I sat before the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and recited to him a poem that I remembered from when he had grown up among us and been raised among the Hawazin tribe and when they had nursed him. So I began to say: 'Grant us favour, O Messenger of God, with generosity, for you are the man we hope and wait for. Grant favour to an egg that fate has hindered, scattering its nest in the changes of its time. War has left us only mourners in sorrow, their hearts burdened with grief and anguish. If you do not reach them with the blessings you spread — O most forbearing of people when tested — Grant mercy to women you used to suckle, when your mouth was filled with the pearls of their milk. When you were a small infant you used to nurse from them, and they watched over all you did and left undone. O best of those for whom chestnut steeds frolic when battle rages and sparks blaze! Do not abandon us like those whose ostriches have strayed; spare us, for we are a radiant community. We are grateful for favors even when others are ungrateful, and after this day we have reserves. Clothe with pardon the one you once nursed from among your mothers — indeed, pardon is celebrated. We hope for a pardon from you — O Guide of creation, do forgive and triumph. So forgive — may God pardon you from what you dread on the Day of Resurrection, when victory is guided to you.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'As for what belongs to me and the Children of Abd al-Muttalib, it is for God and for you.' The Ansar said: 'What is ours is for God and His Messenger.' So the Ansar returned what was in their hands of captives and wealth.

Narrated to us the illustrious Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, may Allah be pleased with him — he said: my father, may Allah be pleased with him, said: narrated to us Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari — he said: narrated to me Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub — he said: Abd Allah ibn Ghalib al-Asadi informed us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn, upon them both be peace, used to admonish the people and make them renounce this world and encourage them in the deeds of the Hereafter with this speech, every Friday, in the Mosque of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family. And it was preserved and written down. He would say: O people! Fear Allah, and know that you will return to Him; then every soul will find what it has done in this world, of good present, and what evil it has done, it will wish that there were a vast distance between itself and it. And Allah warns you of Himself. Woe to you, O son of Adam — the heedless one, though he is not neglected! O son of Adam, verily your appointed time is the fastest thing approaching you; it has already come towards you swiftly, seeking you, and is about to catch up with you. And it is as if you have already fulfilled your term, and the angel has seized your soul, and you have gone to your grave alone. Then your soul is returned to you, and your two angels, Munkar and Nakir, enter upon you forcefully for your questioning and rigorous testing. Know that the first thing they will ask you about is your Lord whom you used to worship, and about your Prophet who was sent to you, and about your religion which you used to practice, and about your Book which you used to recite, and about your Imam whom you used to follow. Then about your life — how you spent it — and your wealth, from where you acquired it and on what you spent it. So take your precautions, look after your soul, and prepare your answer before the examination, the questioning, and the trial. For if you are a believing, God-fearing person, knowledgeable of your religion, a follower of the truthful ones, and devoted to the guardians of Allah, Allah will inspire your proof and make your tongue speak with the right answer, and you will answer well and be given glad tidings of Paradise and the pleasure and most beautiful blessings of Allah, and the angels will

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sukuni. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: A riding animal has seven rights upon its owner: do not make it carry more than it can bear, do not make its back a sitting place for conversation, begin by feeding it when you dismount, do not brand its face, do not strike its face for it glorifies [Allah], offer it water when you pass by it, and do not strike it when it is startled, but strike it when it stumbles, for it sees what you do not see.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: I held the stirrup for the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), as he was about to mount. He raised his head and then smiled. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, I saw you raise your head and smile! He said: Yes, O Asbagh. I held al-Shahba' (the Prophet's mule) for the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), and he raised his head toward the sky and smiled. I said: O Messenger of God, you raised your head toward the sky and smiled! He said: O Ali, there is no one who mounts, then recites the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi), then says: "I seek forgiveness from God, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I repent to Him. O God, forgive me my sins, for none forgives sins except You" except that the Generous Master says: "O My angels, My servant knows that none forgives sins except Me, so bear witness that I have forgiven his sins."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Jurjani. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: The first congregational prayer came about when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, was praying with the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. Abu Talib passed by him with Ja'far and said: 'O my son, join the wing of your cousin.' When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, sensed him, he stepped forward to lead them both. Abu Talib departed joyfully, and he was saying: 'Indeed Ali and Ja'far are my two trustees / When the hardships of time and calamity strike. / By Allah, I will not abandon the Prophet, / Nor will any son of mine of noble lineage abandon him. / Do not abandon him, and support your cousin — / He is my brother through my mother among them, and my father.' He said: That was the first congregational prayer that gathered on that day.

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Ishaq al-Tajir from Ali b. Mahziyar from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from al-Husayn b. Ilwan from Amr b. Khalid from Zayd b. Ali from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Surely, the closest of you to me tomorrow and the most rightful to my intercession are the most truthful of you in speech, the most fulfilling of you in returning trusts, the best of you in character, and the closest of you to the people.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) was travelling with some of his companions in one of the streets of Medina, he dismounted from his riding animal, then fell in prostration and prolonged his prostration. Then he raised his head and returned, then mounted. His companions said to him: O Messenger of Allah! We saw you dismount from your riding animal, then you prostrated and prolonged the prostration. So he said: Indeed Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me and recited the greetings of my Lord to me, and gave me glad tidings that He will never disgrace me with regards to my Nation. I did not have wealth to give in charity nor a slave to free, so I liked to thank my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Abu Dharr (may God have mercy on him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) said: The longest of you in qunut in this world will be the most restful of you on the Day of Resurrection at the Stand.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Amr, from Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Ammar, who said: Harun al-Rashid wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him): Exhort me and be succinct. So he wrote to him: There is nothing that your eye sees except that it has an exhortation in it.

The exalted Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Asbat narrated to us. He said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrating from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) said: None of the proverbs of the prophets remain except the saying of the people: If you feel no shame, then do what you wish.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim. He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed a community went to a prophet of theirs and said: Ask your Lord to alleviate death from us. So he asked on their behalf, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, alleviated death from them. They multiplied until their homes became narrow for them, and the lineages proliferated. A man would wake up needing to feed his father, his mother, his grandfather, and his grandfather's grandfather, and to clean them and take care of them. They became too busy to seek a livelihood. So they came to him and said: Ask your Lord to return us to our lifespans as they were. So he asked his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and He returned them to their lifespans.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Salih, from Abdullah ibn Abbas. Regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'When he recovered, he said: Glory be to You! I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers.' He said: It means: Glory be to You, I repent to You for asking to see You, and I am the first of the believers that You cannot be seen.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amer narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amer, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muqatil ibn Sulayman. He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Musa (peace be upon him) ascended to Tur and spoke privately with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, he said: O my Lord! Show me Your treasures. He said: O Musa! My treasure is that when I will a thing, I say to it "Be!" and it is.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Musa ibn Imran said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of Me. So he said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of Me -- three times. He said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of your mother. He said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of your mother. He said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of your father. He said: So it was said, because of that, that the mother has two-thirds of righteousness, and the father has one-third.

Ali b. Ahmad b. Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi, from Abu Abdillah al-Khayyat, from Abdullah b. al-Qasim, from Abdullah b. Sinan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Among that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa b. Imran (peace be upon him): O Musa! Be like a worn-out robe, pure of heart, reclusive in your house, and a lantern in the night. You will be known among the people of heaven and hidden from the people of earth. O Musa! Beware of stubbornness, and do not be among those who walk without purpose, and do not laugh without astonishment, and weep over your sin, O son of Imran.

Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Ali b. al-Hakam, from Hisham b. Salim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Nuh (peace be upon him) lived for two thousand five hundred years. From them, he lived eight hundred and fifty years before he was commissioned, and he called his people for nine hundred and fifty years, and he spent two hundred years building the Ark, and five hundred years after he descended from the Ark and the water dried up -- establishing regions and settling his descendants across the countries. Then the Angel of Death came to him while he was in the sun, and said: Peace be upon you. Nuh replied and said to him: What has brought you here, O Angel of Death? He said: I have come to take your soul. He said to him: Will you allow me to move from the sun to the shade? He said: Yes. So Nuh (peace be upon him) moved from the sun to the shade. Then he said: O Angel of Death! My time in this world is like my movement from the sun to the shade; so proceed with what you were commanded to do. He said: So he took his soul (peace be upon him).

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-'Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi, from Sharif b. Sabiq al-Taflisi, from Ibrahim b. Muhammad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Isa b. Maryam (peace be upon him) passed by a grave whose occupant was being punished. Then, he passed by it the following year, and behold, he was not being punished. So he said: O my Lord! I passed by this grave last year and its occupant was being punished, then I passed by it this year and he is not being punished! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: O Spirit of Allah! A righteous son has grown up for him, who rectified a path and sheltered an orphan, so I forgave him due to what his son had done. He said: And Isa b. Maryam (peace be upon him) said to Yahya b. Zakariyya (peace be upon him): If something that is truly in you is said about you, then know that it is a sin you have been reminded of, so seek Allah's forgiveness for it. And if something that is not in you is said about you, then know that it is a good deed recorded for you without you having toiled for it.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from his father, from Khalaf b. Hammad, from Abu'l Hasan al-Abdi, from Sulayman b. Mehran, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr b. Habashi, from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: No banner was advanced to fight against the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, overturned it and overcame its companions, and they turned back humiliated. And the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) did not strike anyone with his sword Dhulfiqar except that they perished. And when he fought, Gabriel fought on his right side, Michael on his left side, and the Angel of Death before him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saqr al-Sa'igh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Bassam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Dimashqi narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Lahi'a, from Abu Qubayl, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: On the Day of Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave the banner to a man from his companions, and he returned defeated. Then he gave it to another, who returned showing cowardice to his companions and they showing cowardice to him — he brought the banner back in defeat. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him — he will not return until Allah conquers by his hands. When morning came, he said: Call Ali for me. It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, he has an eye ailment. He said: Call him. When he came, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spat in his eyes and said: O Allah, repel heat and cold from him. Then he gave him the banner and he advanced. He did not return to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) except with the conquest of Khaybar. Then he said: When he drew near to al-Qamus, the enemies of Allah from the Jews came at him shooting arrows and stones. Ali (peace be upon him) charged at them until he drew near the gate. He dismounted his leg, then descended in anger to the base of the gate's threshold and wrenched it out. Then he threw it forty cubits behind his back. Ibn Umar said: We were not amazed at Allah's conquest of Khaybar at the hands of Ali (peace be upon him), but we were amazed at his uprooting the gate and throwing it forty cubits behind him. Forty men tried to carry it but could not manage it. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was informed of that and said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, forty angels aided him in it.

It is reported that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote in his letter to Sahl ibn Hunayf (may God have mercy on him): By Allah, I did not wrench the gate of Khaybar and throw it forty arm-lengths behind my back by physical strength nor by a regimen of nourishment. Rather, I was aided by a celestial power and a soul radiant with the light of its Lord. I am of Ahmad just as light is of light. By Allah, had all the Arabs united against my fighting, I would not have fled; and had I been given the opportunity over their necks, none would have remained. He who does not care when his death descends upon him — his heart is steadfast in calamities. This was narrated to me — along with the entirety of the letter containing this passage — by Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him). He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us from Abu Bakr Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Hibbal al-Tabari. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhsin narrated to us from Yunus ibn Thibyan from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

The eminent and learned Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad b. Abi Ishaq b. Ahmad al-Laythi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Ali b. Muhammad b. Ali al-Mufti narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan b. Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us, from his father, from Yahya b. Ayyash, saying: Ali b. Asim narrated to us, saying: Abu Harun al-Abdi narrated to us, from Abu Said al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Rajab is the month of Allah, the Deaf, and it is a great month. It was called the Deaf because no month approaches it in sanctity and virtue before Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The people of the Age of Ignorance used to revere it in their ignorance, and when Islam came it only increased in reverence and virtue. Indeed, Rajab and Sha'ban are my two months, and the month of Ramadan is the month of my community. Whoever fasts a day of Rajab out of faith and seeking reward becomes entitled to the greatest pleasure of Allah, and his fasting on that day extinguishes the wrath of Allah, and a gate of the gates of the Fire is closed for him. Even if he were given the fill of the earth in gold, it would not be better than his fasting, and his reward cannot be completed with anything of this world short of good deeds, if he makes it sincere for Allah, Mighty and Glorious. He will have ten answered supplications at evening time. And whoever fasts two days of Rajab, no tongue can describe and no mind can comprehend his status before Allah. And whoever fasts three days, Allah places between him and the Fire a trench or a barrier whose distance is like the distance of seventy years of travel. Whoever fasts seven days, the seven gates of Hell are closed for him. Whoever fasts eight days, the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him. Whoever fasts ten days, Allah transforms his sins into good deeds. Whoever fasts fifteen days, a caller calls from heaven: Allah has forgiven what has passed. So begin a new account. And whoever increases, Allah increases for him. And whoever fasts twenty days of Rajab, it is as if he fasted twenty thousand years. And whoever fasts twenty-one days, on the Day of Resurrection he will see a palace of rubies. Whoever fasts twenty-two days, a

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us, from al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ismail b. Muslim al-Sukuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The pressure of the grave for the believer is an expiation for any wasted blessings of his.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Abdullah ibn Ghalib from Sa'd al-Iskaf from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: When any believer washes a [deceased] believer and says when he turns him over: "O Allah, this is the body of Your believing servant. You have removed his spirit from it and have separated between the two. So, Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness," Allah will forgive his sins of a year, except the major sins.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marrar from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever washes a dead believer and fulfills the trust in it, he is forgiven. It was said: And how does he fulfill the trust in it? He said: He does not inform others about what he sees.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab from Ghiyath ibn Kulub from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Instruct your dying to say 'there is no god but Allah' (la ilaha illallah), for whoever's last words are 'there is no god but Allah' will enter Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from 'Ali ibn Sayf from his brother al-Husayn from his father Sayf ibn 'Amira from 'Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever loses children and counts them for the sake of Allah, they will shield him from the Fire by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Yaqub b. Yazid, from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr, from Sayf b. Amira, from Ashath b. Suwar, from al-Ahnaf b. Qays, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may Allah have mercy on him). He said: One day, we were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) in the Quba Mosque, and we were a group of his companions, when he said: O my companions! A man who is the Commander of the Faithful and the Imam of the Muslims will enter upon you through this door. He said: So they looked, and I was among those who looked. Then, we saw Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) come through the door. So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) stood up, received him, embraced him, and kissed his forehead. He brought him and seated him at his side. Then he turned to us with his noble face and said: This is your Imam after me. Obedience to him is obedience to me, and disobedience to him is disobedience to me; and obedience to me is obedience to Allah, and disobedience to me is disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

1 - The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mu'adhi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us, from his father, from Yahya ibn Ayyash. He said: Ali ibn Asim al-Wasiti narrated to us. He said: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, while his companions were discussing the virtues of Sha'ban in his presence: and his companions were discussing the virtues of Sha'ban in his presence. He said: It is a noble month, and it is my month. The carriers of the Throne magnify it and recognize its right. It is a month in which the sustenance of the believers is increased, like the month of Ramadan. In it, Paradise is adorned. It was named Sha'ban because the sustenance of the believers branches out therein. It is a month in which deeds are multiplied: a good deed is rewarded seventyfold, evil deeds are erased, sins are forgiven, good deeds are accepted, and the Almighty -- glory be to His majesty -- boasts about His worshippers therein. He looks upon those who fast and those who stand in prayer, and He boasts about them to the carriers of the Throne. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) stood and said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Describe for us some of its virtues so that we may increase in our desire to fast and stand in prayer during it, and so that we may strive for the Majestic, the Mighty, the Glorious, therein. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever fasts the first day of Sha'ban, Allah will record seventy good deeds for him, each good deed being equivalent to one year of worship. Whoever fasts two days of Sha'ban, the ruinous sin will be erased from him. Whoever fasts three days of Sha'ban will be raised by seventy levels in Paradise of pearls and rubies. Whoever fasts four days of Sha'ban, his sustenance will be expanded for him. Whoever fasts five days of Sha'ban will be made beloved among the servants. Whoever fasts six days of Sha'ban will be spared from seventy types of calamity. Whoever fasts seven days of

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said one day on the pulpit of Kufa: I am the Master of the Successors and the Successor of the Master of the Prophets. I am the Imam of the Muslims, the Leader of the Pious, the Master of the Believers, and the husband of the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds. I am the one who wears a ring on the right hand, and whose forehead is dusty [from prostration]. I am the one who made the two migrations, and who gave the two pledges of allegiance. I am the patron of Badr and Hunayn. I am the one who strikes with two swords, and who charges on two horses. I am the inheritor of the knowledge of the former peoples, and the Proof of God over humanity after the prophets and Muhammad ibn Abdullah (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), the Seal of the Prophets. My allies will receive mercy, and my enemies are damned. And indeed, my beloved, the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), would frequently say to me: O Ali, loving you is God-consciousness and faith, and hating you is disbelief and hypocrisy. And I am the House of Wisdom, and you are its key. Whoever claims to love me while hating you is a liar.

On this day, after the assembly, the illustrious Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Samara. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, guide me to salvation. So he said: O Ibn Samara, when whims differ and opinions diverge, then hold fast to Ali ibn Abi Talib, for he is the Imam of my nation and my vicegerent over them after me. He is the Criterion (al-Faruq) who distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Whoever asks him, he will answer him. Whoever seeks direction from him, he will guide him. Whoever seeks truth from him will find it. Whoever seeks guidance from him will encounter it. Whoever seeks refuge in him will be safe. Whoever holds onto him will be saved. Whoever emulates him will be guided. O Ibn Samara, those who make peace with him and align with him will be at peace, and those who renege from him and oppose him will perish. O Ibn Samara, indeed Ali is from me, his spirit is from my spirit, and his clay is from my clay. He is my brother and I am his brother. He is the husband of my daughter Fatima, the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds from the former and the latter peoples. Indeed, from him are the two Imams of my nation and the two Masters of the Youth of Paradise, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and nine from the descendants of al-Husayn. Their ninth is the Qa'im of my nation, who will fill the earth with justice and equity as it was filled with injustice and oppression.

The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi. He said: Isma'il ibn Mehran narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Yazid from Sufyan al-Thawri. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father Muhammad ibn Ali from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali from his brother al-Hasan from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: Whoever fasts one day in Rajab, whether in its beginning, its middle, or its end, his past sins will be forgiven. Whoever fasts three days in the beginning of Rajab, three days in its middle, and three days in its end, his past and future sins will be forgiven. Whoever keeps vigil for one night of the nights of Rajab, Allah will free him from the Fire and will accept his intercession for seventy thousand sinners. Whoever gives in charity in Rajab, seeking the face of Allah, Allah will honor him on the Day of Resurrection in Paradise with a reward that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, he said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, he said: I heard Malik ibn Anas the jurist say: By God, my eye has not seen anyone more virtuous than Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) in asceticism, goodness, worship, and piety. I used to visit him and he would honor me and turn his attention to me. So one day I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the reward of one who fasts a day in Rajab out of faith and anticipation of reward? He said - and by God, whenever he spoke, he spoke the truth -: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever fasts a day in Rajab out of faith and anticipation of reward will be forgiven." So I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the reward of one who fasts a day in Sha'ban? He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever fasts a day in Sha'ban out of faith and anticipation of reward will be forgiven."

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Do not jest, or your light will dissipate. Do not lie, or your splendour will dissipate. Beware of two traits: restlessness and laziness. For if you are restless, you will not be able to bear a responsibility patiently; and if you are lazy, you will not fulfill a right. He said: And the Messiah (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever's worries multiply, his body becomes ill. Whoever's character worsens, his soul suffers. Whoever's speech multiplies, his errors multiply. Whoever's lying multiplies, his splendour dissipates. Whoever disputes men excessively, his chivalry dissipates.

By this chain of narration, from Darast ibn Abi Mansur, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awwad al-Ta'i, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Eating while full begets leprosy.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Indeed, Adam complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about what he was encountering of inner whispering and grief. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon him and said to him: O Adam, say: 'There is no power nor strength except by Allah.' So he said it, and the whispering and the grief departed from him.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani, the client of Bani Hashim, informed us. He said: al-Mundhir b. Muhammad informed us. He said: Ja'far b. Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from Amr b. Khalid. He said: Zayd b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: In every age there is a man from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, whom Allah uses as a Proof over His creation. The Proof of our age is my nephew Ja'far b. Muhammad — whoever follows him is not misguided, and whoever opposes him is not guided.

Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from Ali b. Ma'bad, from al-Husayn b. Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa b. Ja'far, from his father Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father Muhammad b. Ali, from his father Ali b. al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn b. Ali, from his father the Commander of the Faithful Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Gabriel informed me from Allah, exalted is His majesty, that He said: Ali b. Abi Talib is My Proof over My creation and the upholder of My religion. I shall bring forth from his loins Imams who will establish My command and call to My way. By them I repel the chastisement from My male and female servants, and by them I bring down My mercy.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to us, from al-Hasan b. Mahbub, from Abdullah b. Sinan. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying: There are three things that are the pride and adornment of the believer in this world and the Hereafter: prayer in the last part of the night, disregarding that which is in the hands of the people, and the wilaya of the Imam from the Family of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family).

Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Abbas b. Maruf from Hammad b. Isa from Hariz b. Abdullah, or another person. He said: A group from the Juhayna tribe visited Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), and he hosted them. When they wanted to depart, he supplied them, gifted them, and gave to them. Then he said to his servants: Step aside and do not assist them. When they finished, they came to bid him farewell. They said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! You have hosted us and beautified your hospitality, and you have given and been generous in your giving, yet you commanded your servants not to assist us for our journey. So he (peace be upon him) said: We are the People of a House that does not assist its guests in their journey from our place.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi, from Abu Zakariyya the believer, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) came to some youth from the Ansar and said: I want to recite to you, so whoever weeps will have Paradise. He recited the end of [Surat] al-Zumar, "Those who disbelieve will be driven to Hell in groups" [39:71] to the end of the chapter. The whole community wept except one youth. He said: O Messenger of Allah! I tried to weep, but my eyes shed no tears. He said: I will repeat it to you, and whoever tries to weep will have Paradise. So he repeated it to them, and the community wept and the youth tried to weep, and they all entered Paradise.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mu'addab (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Dahir narrated to us. He said: al-Fadl ibn Isma'il al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Salim narrated to us from his father. He said: I asked al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what do you say regarding the Quran? So he said: It is the word of God, the saying of God, the Book of God, the inspiration of God and His revelation. And it is the Glorious Book to which falsehood cannot come from before it or from behind it — a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy. [Quran 41:42]

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid. He said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of God, inform me about the Quran — is it the Creator, or is it created? So he said: It is not the Creator, nor is it created, but rather it is the Word of God.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt. He said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): What do you say regarding the Quran? He said: It is the word of God. Do not go beyond it, and do not seek guidance in other than it, or you will be misguided.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) wrote to one of his Shi'a followers in Baghdad: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. May God protect us and you from sedition — for if He does, then what a great blessing it would be! And if He does not, then that is perdition. We hold that argumentation regarding the Quran is an innovation (bid'a) in which the questioner and the answerer are equally partners: the questioner ventures into what is not his right, and the answerer takes upon himself what is not incumbent upon him. There is no creator but God, and everything other than Him is created. The Quran is the speech of God — do not assign it a name from yourself, lest you be among the misguided. May God make us and you of those who fear their Lord in the unseen, and who are in awe of the Hour.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) laughed one day until his molar teeth were visible. Then he said: Will you not ask me why I laughed? They said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: I am astonished at the affair of the Muslim person — there is nothing that God, Mighty and Majestic, decrees for him except that it is good for him in the end of his affair.

Ali ibn Isa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) saying: I asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) about the characteristics of the believer. So he (peace be upon him and his family) lowered his head, then raised it and said: In the believers there are twenty characteristics. Whoever does not have them in him, his faith has not been perfected. O Ali! Surely the believers are those who attend prayers, hasten to zakat, go on Hajj to the Sacred House of God, fast in the month of Ramadan, feed the needy, stroke the heads of orphans, cleanse their nails, cover their waists, when they speak do not lie, when they promise do not break it, when they are entrusted do not betray, when they speak are truthful, are like monks at night, are like lions in the day, fast during the day, stand in prayer during the night, do not harm a neighbor, no neighbor is harmed through them, walk gently on the earth, and their steps lead to the houses of widows and follow funeral processions. May God make us and you from the God-fearing.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi. He said: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl narrated to us from his father from Thabit ibn Dinar from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, God — Blessed and Exalted — revealed to me that He is going to appoint for me from my community a brother, an inheritor, a vicegerent (khalifa), and a deputy. So I said: 'O Lord! Who is it?' So He — Mighty and Majestic — revealed to me: 'O Muhammad! He is the Imam of your community and My Proof over it after you.' So I said: 'O Lord, who is it?' So He — Mighty and Majestic — revealed to me: 'O Muhammad! He is the one I love and who loves Me. He is the striver in My cause, the fighter of those who break My covenant, those who deviate in My judgment, and those who apostatize from My religion. He is truly My guardian — the husband of your daughter and the father of your descendants: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Salama al-Ahwazi from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Isma'il ibn Bashar informed us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Balaj al-Misri narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Madani from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir. He said: I heard Abu Umama say: Whenever 'Ali (peace be upon him) would say something, we would not doubt it. That is because we surely heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'The treasurer of my secret after me is 'Ali.'

And by this chain of transmission, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Al-Mas'udi narrated to me. He said: Yahya ibn Salim al-'Abdi narrated to us from Isra'il, from Maysara, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh. He said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) passed by on the mule of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) while Salman was in a gathering. Salman (may God's mercy be upon him) said: Will you not go and take him by his belt and ask him? For by Him who split the seed and gave life to the soul, none will inform you of the secret of your Prophet (may God bless him and his family) except him. He is the scholar of the earth and its master, and it is to him that it settles. If you were to lose him, you would lose knowledge and no longer recognize the people.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to me. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sarraf narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us from Ali ibn Hashim from Abu Rafi' from Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr from 'Abbad ibn Abdullah from Salman (may God's mercy be upon him) from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said: The best judge of my community and the most knowledgeable of my community after me is Ali.

By this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from his brother, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all), who said: Whenever a revelation came down to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) during the day, he would not sleep until he had informed Ali of it. And whenever it came down to him at night, he would not greet the morning until he had informed Ali of it.

Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Ahmad al-Sa'igh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) led his companions in the Fajr prayer one day. Then he sat with them conversing until the sun rose. One man after another began to rise and leave until only two men remained with him: an Ansari and a Thaqafi. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: "I know that you two have a need and wish to ask me about it. If you wish, I shall inform you of your need before you ask me; and if you wish, ask me." They said: "Rather, you inform us, O Messenger of God, for that would be clearer for the blind, further from doubt, and more steadfast for faith." So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "As for you, O brother of the Ansar, you are from a people who prefer others over themselves. You are a villager and this Thaqafi is a Bedouin — do you defer to him in asking?" He said: "Yes." So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "As for you, O brother of Thaqif, you came to ask me about your wudu and your salat and what reward you have in them. Know that when you plunge your hand in the water and say: 'In the name of God' (bismillah), the sins acquired by your hands will scatter. When you wash your face, the sins acquired by your eyes through their gaze and by your mouth through its speech will scatter. When you wash your arms, the sins to your right and your left will scatter. When you wipe your head and feet, the sins that your feet walked toward will scatter. This is for you in your wudu. When you stand for prayer, face the qibla, recite the Mother of the Book (al-Fatiha) and whatever is easy for you from the chapters, then bow and complete the bowing and prostration, testify the shahada, and recite the taslim — every sin between the previous prayer and the next prayer will be forgiven for you. This is for you in your prayer." "As for you, O brother of the Ansar, you came to ask me about your Hajj and your 'Umra and what reward you have in them. Know that when you set out on the path of Hajj and mount your

The venerable Shaykh Abu Jafar Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sad b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Ali b. al-Numan from Abdullah b. Talha from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: The fasting person is in the worship of Allah, even when he is sleeping on his bed, as long as he does not backbite a Muslim.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Yaqub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Sinan from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever fasts a day voluntarily seeking the reward of Allah, forgiveness becomes obligatory for him.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Abi Qutada al-Qummi. He said: Abdullah b. Yahya narrated to us from Aban al-Ahmar from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as). He said: The people discussed chivalry (futuwwa) around him, so he said: Do you think that chivalry is immorality and indecency? No! Rather, chivalry and manliness are serving food, giving generously, doing good, and withholding harm. As for that, it is wickedness and immorality. Then he (as) said: What is manliness? We said: We do not know. He said: Manliness, by Allah, is that a man places his dining table in his courtyard. And manliness is of two kinds: manliness at home and manliness while travelling. As for manliness at home, it is reciting the Quran, adhering to the mosques, walking with the brothers in their needs, and being good to the servant — for it brings joy to the friend and suppresses the enemy. As for manliness while travelling, it is having abundant and good provisions and sharing them with those who are with you, keeping the secrets of the people after you have parted from them, and being light-hearted in a way that does not anger Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then he (as) said: By Him who sent my grandfather (s) as a true prophet! Surely Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, provides for the servant in proportion to his manliness. Aid descends from the heaven in proportion to his expenditure. And patience descends in proportion to the severity of the affliction.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Hamza from Isma'il b. Abd al-Khaliq and Abi'l Sabah al-Kinani, together, from Abi Basir. He said: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) saying: Whoever withholds his harm from his neighbor, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will forgive his offense on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever purifies his stomach and his private parts will be a joyous king in paradise. And whoever frees a believing soul, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will build a house for him in paradise.

Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Ahmad b. Hisham al-Mu'addab (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Ahmad narrated to us. He said: Sulayman b. Ja'far al-Ja'fari narrated to me. He said: I said to Abi'l Hasan Musa b. Ja'far (as): O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say regarding the Quran, for some among us have disagreed regarding it? One group says it is created, and another group says it is not created. So, he (as) said: I do not say regarding that what they say, but rather I say that it is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi'l Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad b. Sinan from Isa al-Nahri Yari from Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: He who recognizes Allah and His greatness will have purified his speech, [purified] his stomach of food, and supported himself with fasting and standing in prayer. They said: May our fathers and our mothers be your sacrifice, O Messenger of Allah — are these the friends of Allah? He said: The friends of Allah are silent, and their silence is remembrance; they observe, and their observation is a lesson; they speak, and their speech is wisdom; and they walk, and their walking in the midst of the people is a blessing. Were it not for the term decreed for them, their spirits would not have remained settled in their bodies out of fear of punishment and out of desire for reward.

Ja'far b. Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. Ali narrated to me from his grandfather Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: The most beloved of my brothers to me is Ali b. Abi Talib (as), and the most beloved of my uncles to me is Hamza.

Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas b. al-Fadl b. Shadhan al-Muqri narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Harun narrated to us from Uzra al-Qattan. He said: Mas'ud Abu Abdillah al-Khiladi narrated to us. He said: Tulayd narrated to me from Abi'l Hijaf from Abi Idris from Mujahid from Ali (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said to me: O Ali! Whoever splits away from you has split away from me; and whoever splits away from me has split away from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us. He said: Abu Yusuf Ya'qub b. Muhammad al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Ibn Umara narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Abi'l Za'za' al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: Abu Thabit Abd al-Karim al-Jazari narrated to us from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Abdullah b. Abbas. He said: The Prophet (s) became immensely famished, so he went to the Ka'ba, held onto its cloak, and said: Lord of Muhammad! Do not starve Muhammad more than what You have already starved him. He said: So, Gabriel (as) came down with an almond. He said: O Muhammad! Allah, the Majestic, sends you peace. He said: O Gabriel! Allah is Peace, and peace is from Him, and peace will return to Him. He said: Surely, Allah commands you to break open this almond. So, he broke it open, and behold, a fresh green leaf appeared, upon which it was written: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I supported Muhammad with Ali, and aided him through him. He does not do justice to himself before Allah who distrusts Allah in His judgment, and impatiently awaits His sustenance.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qadi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Perform voluntary prayers in the time of heedlessness, even if they are only two quick rak'ahs, for they will bequeath the Abode of Nobility. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is the time of heedlessness? He said: Between Maghrib and Isha'.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, the mawla of Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: One day, the Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) was sitting with Ibn al-Hanafiyya when he said: O Muhammad, bring me a vessel of water so that I may perform ablution for prayer. So Muhammad brought him the water. He poured with his right hand over his left hand, then said: In the name of God. Praise be to God who made water pure and did not make it impure. Then he performed istinja and said: O God, fortify my private parts and keep them chaste, cover my private areas, and forbid me from the Fire. Then he rinsed his mouth and said: O God, make me utter my proof on the Day I meet You, and make my tongue free in Your remembrance. Then he rinsed his nose and said: O God, do not deprive me of the fragrance of Paradise, and make me of those who smell its fragrance, its coolness, and its sweetness. Then he washed his face and said: O God, whiten my face on the Day when faces are blackened, and do not blacken my face on the Day when faces are whitened. Then he washed his right hand and said: O God, give me my Book in my right hand and eternity in the Gardens in my left hand, and reckon me with an easy reckoning. Then he washed his left hand and said: O God, do not give me my Book in my left hand, and do not bind it to my neck; and I seek refuge in You from the fire-cuttings. Then he wiped his head and said: O God, envelop me in Your mercy, Your blessings, and Your pardon. Then he wiped his feet and said: O God, make my feet firm upon the Bridge on the Day when feet slip from it, and direct my striving toward what pleases You on my behalf. Then he raised his head, looked at Muhammad, and said: O Muhammad, whoever performs ablution like my ablution and says what I have said, God, Mighty and Majestic, will create from every drop an angel who glorifies Him, praises Him, and magnifies Him; and God, Mighty and Majestic, will record its reward for him until the Day of Resurrection.
