Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) used to say to his companions: O children of Adam! Flee from this world to God, and remove your hearts from it, for truly you cannot set it right, nor can it set you right; you will not remain in it, nor will it remain for you. It is the deceiver, the bringer of grief. Deceived is he who is deluded by it. Cheated is he who trusts in it. Destroyed is he who loves it and desires it. So repent to your Creator, be conscious of your Lord, and fear a Day in which no father will avail his child in the least, nor will any child avail his father in the least. Where are your fathers? Where are your mothers? Where are your brothers? Where are your sisters? Where are your children? They were called and they answered, they were entrusted to the earth, and they became neighbors to the dead, and they joined those who have perished. They departed from this world and parted from their loved ones. They became in need of what they had sent ahead, and became needless of what they left behind. So how much exhortation have you received, and how much rebuke, while you remain distracted and heedless! Your likeness in this world is like that of cattle — your concern is your stomachs and your private parts. Are you not ashamed before Him who created you?! He has promised the Fire to those who disobey Him, and you are not among those who can withstand the Fire. And He has promised Paradise and His proximity in the Highest Heaven to those who obey Him. So compete for it and be among its people. Be just with yourselves, be compassionate toward your weak and needy. Repent to God with sincere repentance. Be righteous servants and do not be arrogant kings or among the insolent pharaohs who rebel against Him who overpowers them with death — the Almighty of the almighty, Lord of the heavens and the earths, God of the first and the last, Master of the Day of Judgment, severe in punishment, painful in torment. No oppressor shall escape Him, nothing shall elude Him, nothing is hidden from Him, nothing can conceal itself from Him — His knowledge has encompassed all th

By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza. He said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is overwhelmed by blessings, let him say: 'Praise be to God, Lord of all the worlds.' And whoever is pressed by poverty, let him frequently say: 'There is no power or strength except through God, the High, the Great.' For it is indeed a treasure from the treasures of Paradise, and in it is a remedy for seventy-two ailments, the least of which is worry.

By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Isma'il ibn Dinar, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: The people of the Fire will howl therein just as dogs and wolves howl from the pain of the torment. What do you think, O Amr, of a people upon whom death is not decreed so that they might die, and whose punishment is not lightened — thirsty and hungry therein, their sight dimmed, deaf, mute, and blind, their faces blackened, disgraced and remorseful therein, under divine wrath so that no mercy reaches them, and the punishment is not lightened from them, They are burned in the Fire, they drink from boiling water, they eat from the Zaqqum tree, their noses are hooked with the iron hooks of the Fire, they are struck with iron maces, while the harsh and severe angels show no mercy. They are dragged on their faces in the Fire, shackled together with the devils, and bound in fetters and chains, If they call out, they are not answered, and if they ask for a need, it is not fulfilled for them. This is the state of those who enter the Fire.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu'l-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahim ibn Ali ibn Sa'id al-Jabali narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Nasr al-Khazzaz narrated to us. He said: Amr ibn Talha narrated to us from Asbat ibn Nasr, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. He said: I came to Abdullah ibn Abbas and said to him: O cousin of the Messenger of Allah! I have come to ask you about Ali ibn Abi Talib and the people's differing regarding him. So Ibn Abbas said: O Ibn Jubayr! You have come to ask me about the best of God's creation in the community after Muhammad, the Prophet of God. You have come to ask me about a man who had three thousand virtues in a single night — and that is the Night of al-Qurba. O Ibn Jubayr! You have come to ask me about the deputy of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and his minister, and his vicegerent, and the master of his Pond, his Banner, and his intercession. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn Abbas! If the oceans of the world were ink, and its trees were pens, and its people were scribes, and they wrote the virtues and excellences of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) from the day God — Mighty and Majestic — created the world until He brings it to an end, they would not reach even a tenth of what God — Blessed and Exalted — has granted him.

And by this chain of narration from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib. He said: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us from Isma'il ibn Aban, from Sallam ibn Abi 'Amra, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbudh, from Abu al-Tufayl, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: I heard the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) say: I am the master of the Prophets, and Ali ibn Abi Talib is the master of the Deputies, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the two masters of the youth of the people of Paradise, and the Imams after them both are the masters of the God-fearing. Our ally is the ally of God, and our enemy is the enemy of God. Obedience to us is obedience to God, and disobedience to us is disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us. He said: Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal informed us from his father from Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said: We are masters in this world and kings in the Hereafter.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Salama ibn al-Khattab al-Birawustani, from Ibrahim ibn Muqatil. He said: Hamid ibn Muhammad narrated to me from 'Amr ibn Harun, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: I had intended to marry Fatima, daughter of Muhammad (blessings of Allah upon them both), for a period, but I did not dare mention it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). That longing stirred in my chest night and day, until I visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: O Ali! I said: I am at your service, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Are you interested in marriage? I said: The Messenger of Allah knows best. I thought he intended to marry me to one of the women of Quraysh, and I was afraid of losing Fatima. I had not noticed anything, when the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to me and said: Answer the Prophet and hurry — we have never seen the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) more joyful than today. He said: So I hurried to him, and he was in the chamber of Umm Salama. When he looked at me, his face lit up with joy and he smiled, until I saw his white teeth gleaming. He said: Rejoice, O Ali! For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has relieved me of the concern I had about your marriage. I said: How is that, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Gabriel came to me with spikenard and cloves from Paradise and presented them to me. I took them and smelled them, then said: What is the reason for this spikenard and cloves? He said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded the angelic inhabitants of the Gardens and all that was therein to adorn all the Gardens with their plantations, trees, fruits, and palaces; and He commanded their winds to blow with all kinds of perfumes and fragrances; and He commanded their houris to recite therein Surah Ta-Ha, the Ta-Sins, Ya-Sin, and Ha-Mim-'Ayn-Sin-Qaf. Then a caller called from beneath the Throne: Verily! Today is the day of the wedding feast of Ali ibn Abi Talib! Verily! I take you as w

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us, from al-Qasim b. Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan b. Rashid, from Abu 'Abdullah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me on his pulpit: O Ali! Allah (mighty and majestic) has gifted you with the love of the needy and the oppressed on earth, so you were pleased with them as brethren and they were pleased with you as an Imam. Blessed is he who loves you and believes in you, and woe to he who hates you and belies you. O Ali! You are the banner of this nation; whoever loves you succeeds, and whoever hates you perishes. O Ali! I am the City of Knowledge and you are its gate - can a city be entered except through its gate?! O Ali! The people of your love are every penitent, mindful person, and every humble one who, if he swore upon Allah, would have his oath fulfilled. O Ali! Your brethren are every pure, devout striver who loves for your sake and hates for your sake - despised among creation but great in rank with Allah. O Ali! Those who love you are the neighbors of Allah in the Abode of Paradise; they do not grieve for what they left behind. O Ali! I am the guardian of whoever you befriend, and I am the enemy of whoever you oppose. O Ali! Whoever loves you has loved me, and whoever hates you has hated me. O Ali! Your brethren have withered lips; monasticism is recognized in their faces. O Ali! Your brethren rejoice in three stations: at the departure of their souls while I and you witness them, at the questioning in their graves, and at the Great Presentation and at the Bridge when creation is asked about their faith and they cannot answer. O Ali! Your war is my war, and your peace is my peace; and my war is the war of Allah. O Ali! Give glad tidings to your brethren, for Allah is pleased with them. O Ali! You are the Commander of the Faithful and the Leader of the Radiant Ones. O Ali! Your Shi'a are the chosen ones. Were it not for you and your Shi'a, no religion would be established for Allah, and were it not for your presence on earth, no rain would fall from the sky. O Ali! You have a treasure in Paradise. O Ali! You and your Shi'a are the establishers of justi

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Amr ibn Mughlis from Khalaf from Atiyya al-Awfi from Abu Said al-Khudri. He said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) about the saying of God, exalted is His praise: 'The one who had knowledge of the Book said' [27:40]. He said: That is the deputy of my brother Sulayman ibn Dawud. So I said to him: O Messenger of God, then what about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Say: God suffices as a witness between me and you, and the one who has knowledge of the Book' [13:43]? He said: That is my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Furat b. Ibrahim b. Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali al-Hamadani narrated to me. He said: Al-Husayn b. Ali narrated to me. He said: Abdullah b. Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to me. He said: Abd al-Wahid b. Ghiyath narrated to me. He said: Asim b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Juwaybir narrated to us from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. He said: We prayed the final Isha prayer one night with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family. When he recited the taslim, he turned his face toward us, then said: Verily, a meteor will fall from the sky at the rise of dawn and land in the house of one of you. Whoever has that meteor fall in his house, then he is my deputy, my vicegerent, and the Imam after me. When dawn drew near, every one of us sat in his house waiting for the meteor to fall in his house. The most desirous of the people for that was my father, al-Abbas b. Abd al-Muttalib. When dawn broke, the meteor fell from the air and landed in the house of Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said to Ali, peace be upon him: O Ali, by Him who raised me with prophethood, the deputyship, the vicegerency, and the Imamate have been obligated for you after me. Then the hypocrites, Abdullah b. Ubay and his companions, said: Muhammad has deviated in his love for his cousin and gone astray, and he only speaks about him out of desire. So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: 'By the star when it fades away' — God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: By the Creator of the star when it fades away — 'Your companion has not deviated' — meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and his family, in his love for Ali b. Abi Talib — 'nor has he gone astray. Nor does he speak out of desire' — meaning, with regards to him — 'It is not but a revealed revelation.'

A shaykh of the people of Ray called Ahmad b. Muhammad b. al-Saqr al-Sa'igh al-'Adl narrated this hadith to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Abbas b. Bassam narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Abi al-Haytham al-Sa'di narrated to me. He said: Ahmad b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to me. He said: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us from his father, from Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, from Abdullah b. Abbas, [a hadith] similar to that, except that he said in his hadith: A meteor falls from the sky at sunrise, and it lands in the house of one of you.

A shaykh from the people of hadith called Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan, known as Abu Ali b. Abd Rabbih al-'Adl, narrated this hadith to us. He said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ishaq al-Kufi al-Ju'fi narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Abdullah al-Sijzi Abu Ishaq narrated to us from Yahya b. al-Husayn al-Mashhadi from Abu Harun al-Abdi from Rabi'a al-Sa'di. He said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'By the star when it fades away.' He said: It is the star that fell at the break of dawn into the room of Ali b. Abi Talib. My father al-Abbas wanted that star to fall in his house so he could possess the deputyship, vicegerency, and Imamate. However, God refused that for anyone other than Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and that is the favour of God which He gives to whomever He wills.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan b. 'Ali al-'Adawi narrated to us. He said: Yusuf b. Yahya al-Isfahani Abu Ya'qub narrated to us. He said: Abu 'Ali Isma'il b. Hatim narrated to me. He said: Abu Ja'far Ahmad b. Salih b. Sa'id al-Makki narrated to us. He said: 'Amr b. Hafs narrated to us from Ishaq b. Najih from Khusayf from Mujahid from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave a wasiyya (will) to Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and said: O Ali! When the bride is brought to your house, remove her shoes when she sits and wash her feet, then pour the water at the farthest edge of your dwelling, for if you do so, Allah will remove seventy thousand types of poverty from your house and send down seventy thousand types of blessing and bestow seventy thousand mercies upon the bride. O Ali! Beware of intercourse on the first, the middle, and the last of the month, for verily insanity, leprosy, and mental decline come upon the child. O Ali! Do not speak during intercourse, for if a child is conceived, it may be mute. Let none of you look at the private parts of his wife, and lower your gazes. O Ali! Do not have intercourse with your wife while desiring another woman, for I fear that if a child is destined, it would be an effeminate man or a masculine woman. O Ali! Do not have intercourse with your wife in the state of menstruation, for if a child is destined, it will be leprous. O Ali! Do not have intercourse with your wife after the midday prayer, for if a child is destined, it will be cross-eyed. O Ali! Do not speak during intercourse and do not be hasty. O Ali! Do not have intercourse with your wife under a fruit tree, for the child may be an executioner. O Ali! Do not have intercourse on the rooftop, for if a child is destined, it will be a hypocrite. O Ali! If your wife is pregnant, do not have intercourse without ablution. O Ali! Do not have intercourse with your wife on the night of Eid al-Fitr, for the child may be evil. O Ali! Do not have intercourse on the night of Eid al-Adha. O Ali! Do not have intercourse under the open sky. O Ali! Do not have intercourse facing the qibla. O Ali! Do not have intercourse i

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me. He said: 'Ali b. Hassan al-Wasiti narrated to us from his uncle 'Abd al-Rahman b. Kathir al-Hashimi from Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father (as). He said: A man from the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (as) called Hammam, who was a worshiper, stood up and said: O Amir al-Mu'minin! Describe the Godfearing ones to me in such a way that it is as though I am looking at them. So, Amir al-Mu'minin (as) did not reply. Then, he said to him: Woe to you, Hammam, fear Allah and beautify, for Allah is with the Godfearing who beautify. So, Hammam said: O Amir al-Mu'minin! I ask you by Him who honoured you with that which He distinguished you with, and preferred you with what He gave you, and granted you with what you describe to me. So, Amir al-Mu'minin (as) stood on his feet, praised Allah and commended Him, blessed the Prophet and his Family, then said: As for that which comes after: Surely, Allah created the creation, and He was needless of their obedience and safe from their disobedience; for the disobedience of one who disobeys Him does not harm Him, and the obedience of one who obeys Him does not benefit Him. He apportioned their livelihood between them and placed them in their position in the world. Surely, Allah only caused Adam and Hawwa' (as) to fall from Paradise as a punishment for what they had done when He prohibited them and they defied Him; when He commanded them and they disobeyed Him. The pious therein are of the people of virtue -- their logic is sound, their apparel is prudence, and their sojourn is humility. They humble themselves before Allah through obedience, and they empty themselves. They lower their gaze from that which Allah forbade them from. Their ears are set upon knowledge. They remedy their souls in calamity just as they remedy their souls in tranquility. They are content with the predestination of Allah. Had it not been for the time that Allah has ordained for them, their souls would not remain in their bodies for the duration of a twinkling of the eye out of desire for reward and fear of punishment. The greatness of the Creator is in their souls, and everything else is insignificant in their eyes. It is as though they could see Paradise and are reclining in it. It is as though they could see the Fire and are suffering in it.

Muhammad b. Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Hafs narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. Harun Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi al-Mansuri narrated to me. He said: al-Qasim b. al-Husayn al-Zubaydi narrated to us. He said: Yahya b. Abd al-Hamid narrated to us. He said: Qays b. al-Rabi narrated to us from Abu Harun from Abu Sa'id. He said: On the Day of Ghadir Khumm, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, ordered a caller to call out for congregational prayer. Then he took the hand of Ali, peace be upon him, and said: O God! To whomever I am a master, Ali is his master. O God! Be a friend to whoever befriends him and an enemy to whoever opposes him. Then Hassan b. Thabit said: O Messenger of God, shall I recite a poem about Ali? The Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said to him: Do so. So he said: Their Prophet calls them on the Day of Ghadir / At Khumm, and how honoured is the Prophet as a caller / He says: Who is your master and your guardian? / They said, showing no hostility there: / Your God is our Master and you are our guardian / And you will never find among us a disobedient one today / Then he said to him: Stand, O Ali, for indeed I / Am pleased with you as an Imam and a guide after me / Then Ali stood, suffering from conjunctivitis / Seeking a cure for his eyes from his complaint / Then the best of people cured him with his saliva / So blessed is the one cured and blessed is the healer.

The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When the sun passes its zenith, the gates of heaven and the gates of Paradise are opened, and supplications are answered. So blessed is the one for whom a righteous deed is raised at that time.

By this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ayman ibn Muhriz, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no servant from our Shia who rises to pray except that angels surround him, equal in number to those who oppose him, praying behind him and supplicating to God on his behalf until he completes his prayer.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sa'd ibn Turayf. He said: 'Umayr ibn Ma'mun al-'Ataridi narrated to me. He said: I saw al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) he would sit in his place after praying Fajr until the sun rose. And I heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) say: Whoever prays Fajr then sits in his place remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until the sun rises, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will shield him from the Fire. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will shield him from the Fire. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will shield him from the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from one who heard Abu Sayyar say: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to Yusuf (peace be upon him) while he was in prison and said: Say after every obligatory prayer: 'O Allah, grant me relief and a way out, and provide for me from where I expect and from where I do not expect,' three times.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Maliki narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn al-Abbas narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever recites 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) sixty times in the first two units of the night prayer — thirty times in each unit — he will finish the prayer with no sin remaining between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ayyub ibn Sulaym al-Attar, from Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Kahili, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Whoever enters the market, buys a gift, and brings it to his family is like one who carries charity to a needy people. And let him begin with the daughters before the sons, for whoever gladdens a daughter, it is as if he freed a slave from the Children of Ismail. And whoever gladdens the eye of a son, it is as if he wept out of awe before God, the Mighty and Majestic. And whoever weeps out of awe before God, the Mighty and Majestic, God will enter him into the Gardens of Bliss.

Ali ibn Isa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qurashi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Indeed, Gabriel (peace be upon him) informed me of something that gladdened my eye and brought joy to my heart. He said: O Muhammad, whoever from your nation goes on an expedition in the cause of God, no raindrop from the sky or headache will afflict him except that it will count as martyrdom for him on the Day of Resurrection.

By this chain of narration. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: In Paradise there is a gate called the Gate of the Strivers. They will proceed toward it, and it will be open, while they are girded with their swords -- and the assembly gathered at the standing place -- and the angels welcome them. Whoever abandons jihad, Allah will clothe him in humiliation within himself, poverty in his livelihood, and effacement of his religion. Indeed, Allah, blessed and exalted, has given glory to my nation through the hooves of its horses and the posts of its spears.

By this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever conveys the message of a warrior is like one who has freed a slave, and he is his partner in the reward of his expedition.

Ja'far b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. 'Ali narrated to me from his grandfather 'Abd Allah b. al-Mughira, from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The horses of the warriors — their horses will be in Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Goodness, all of it, is in the sword and beneath the shade of the sword. The people cannot be set aright except by the sword. And the swords are the keys to Paradise and the Fire.

Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Ishaq al-Tajir narrated to us from Ali b. Mahziyar from Fadala b. Ayyub from Ismail b. Abi Ziyad from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever wishes for something whilst being pleased with Allah — Mighty and Majestic — will not leave this world until he is granted it.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyya, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Among the firmest bonds of faith is that you love for Allah, hate for Allah, give for Allah, and withhold for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever says, when entering the evening, three times: 'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, at nightfall and at midday' (Quran 30:17-18) no good occurring that night will miss him, and all its evil will be repelled from him. And whoever says the same when entering the morning, no good occurring that day will miss him, and all its evil will be repelled from him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Verily, an angel descends with a scroll at the beginning of the day and at the beginning of the night. It writes in it the deeds of the children of Adam. So fill its beginning with good and its end with good, for God Almighty will forgive you what lies between — God-willingly. And God Almighty says: 'Remember Me, and I will remember you' [2:152] and He whose Majesty is exalted says: 'And the remembrance of God is greater' [29:45]

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir narrated to us from his uncle Abdullah ibn Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: O Abu Harun! Indeed, we instruct our children to recite the Tasbih of Fatima (peace be upon her) just as we instruct them to perform salat. So cling to it, for no servant who clings to it becomes wretched.

By this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Atiyya al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said: Whoever says 'Bismillah (In the name of God)' when he leaves his house, the two angels say: 'You have been guided.' If he then says 'La hawla wala quwwata illa billah (There is no ability nor power except by God),' they say: 'You have been safeguarded.' If he then says 'Tawakkaltu alallah (I rely on God),' they say: 'You have been sufficed.' Then Satan says: 'How can I deal with a servant who has been guided, safeguarded, and sufficed?!'

And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said one day to Ali (peace be upon him): Shall I not give you glad tidings? He said: Of course, may my father and mother be your sacrifice, for you have never ceased to bring tidings of every good. He said: Gabriel informed me just now of something astonishing. Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: What did he inform you of, O Messenger of Allah? He said: He informed me that when a man from my nation sends blessings upon me and follows it with blessings upon my Ahl al-Bayt, the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the angels bless him seventy times, even if he is an erring sinner. Then his sins shed from him just as leaves shed from a tree. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: I am at your service, My servant, and may good fortune come to you. And Allah says to His angels: O My angels! You bless him seventy times, and I bless him seven hundred times. But when he blesses me without following it with blessings upon my Ahl al-Bayt, there are seventy veils between it and heaven, and Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) says: I am not at your service nor does good fortune come to you. O My angels! Do not bring up his supplication until he joins blessings on the Prophet with his progeny. So it will remain suspended until he follows me up with my Ahl al-Bayt.

And by this isnad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih al-Asadi, from Muhammad ibn Harun, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: If one of you prays without mentioning the Prophet (may God bless him and his family), his prayer is taken along a path other than the way to Paradise.

He said: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever does not bless me when I am mentioned in his presence will enter the Fire; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will have detached him from His mercy.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu'l-Husayn al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to me. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Yazid narrated to us. He said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to me from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Four people torment the inhabitants of the Fire beyond what they are already suffering. They drink from the boiling water and blazing fire, crying out in woe and destruction. The inhabitants of the Fire say to one another: 'What is wrong with these four who torment us beyond what we already suffer?' One is suspended in a coffin of embers; one drags his intestines; one has pus and blood flowing from his mouth; and one eats his own flesh. It is said to the companion of the coffin: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch died while he owed debts to people and did not find it in himself to repay or fulfill them.' Then it is said to the one dragging his intestines: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch did not care where urine touched his body.' Then it is said to the one with pus and blood flowing from his mouth: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch would mimic — he would look for every vile word, then spread it and imitate it.' Then it is said to the one eating his own flesh: 'What did this wretch do to torment us beyond what we already suffer?' He says: 'This wretch would consume the flesh of people through backbiting and walk about spreading gossip.'

And by this chain of transmission, he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever praises his believing brother to his face but backbites him behind his back — the bond of protection ('isma) between them has been severed.

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both): The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: In what is salvation tomorrow [on the Day of Judgment]? He said: Surely salvation is in not trying to deceive God, lest He deceive you. For indeed whoever deceives God, He will deceive him and strip faith from him — and he deceives himself, if he but knew. So it was said to him: And how does one deceive God? He said: He does what God has commanded, but intends by it something other than Him. So fear God and avoid riya' (showing off), for it is shirk (associating partners) with God. Surely the one who shows off will be called by four names on the Day of Resurrection: 'O disbeliever! O transgressor! O treacherous! O loser! Your deeds have fallen void, your reward has been nullified, and there is no share for you today. So seek your reward from the one you were working for.'

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhuwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mundal ibn Ali al-'Anazi, from Muhammad ibn Mutarrif, from Masma', from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When God, Blessed and Exalted, is angry with a nation but does not send down chastisement upon it, its prices rise, its lifespans are shortened, its merchants do not profit, its fruits do not ripen, its rivers are not bounteous, its rains are withheld from it, and its wicked people are set to rule over it.

By this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Zurara, from 'Isa ibn 'Abdullah al-Hashimi, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Umar ibn Abi Salama, from his mother Umm Salama (may God be pleased with her). She said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Imams from his descendants after me are the masters of the people of Earth and the Leaders of the bright-faced and shining believers on the Day of Resurrection.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us. He said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih ibn Abi Salama al-Nusaybi narrated to us. He said: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'A'isha. He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him and his family) say: I am the master of the former and the latter peoples, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib is the master of the deputies. He is my brother, my inheritor, and my vicegerent (khalifa) over my nation. His wilaya is obligatory, following him is a virtue, and loving him is a means of approach to God. His party is the Party of God, his Shi'a are the supporters of God, his friends are the friends of God, and his enemies are the enemies of God. He is the Imam of the Muslims, the master of the believers, and their commander after me.

Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Ali al-Tamimi. He said: My master Ali b. Musa al-Ridha (AS) narrated to me from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said: Whoever would be gladdened to look upon the red rod that Allah planted with His hand — and to be of those who hold fast to it — should take Ali and the Imams from his descendants as their guardian; for they are the choicest of Allah (Almighty and Majestic) and His elite; and they are the Immaculate (ma'sumun), free from every sin and error.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazwini, Abu'l-Hasan, known as Ibn Maqbara, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Amir narrated to us. He said: Isam ibn Yusuf narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Kilabi narrated to us. He said: Amr ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thabit. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever loves Ali in his life and after his death, God, Mighty and Majestic, shall write for him security and faith equivalent to all that the sun rises and sets upon. And whoever hates him in his life and after his death shall die the death of jahiliyya and be held accountable for what he did.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah narrated to me. He said: Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated to us from Hisham, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Ali! Your love will not settle in the heart of a believing person, then his foot slips on the Path (Sirat), except that a footing will be made firm for him until God the Mighty and Majestic enters him into Paradise through your love.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) became ill with the illness in which Allah took his soul, his Ahl al-Bayt and his companions gathered to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if something were to happen to you, who will be for us after you? Who will take charge of your authority over us?' But he did not give them any answer, and remained silent regarding them. On the second day, they repeated the question to him, but he did not respond to them about anything they had asked. On the third day, they said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, if something were to happen to you, who will be for us after you? Who will take charge of your authority over us?' He said to them: 'Tomorrow, a star will descend from the sky into the house of a man from my companions. Look for who he is, for he is my vicegerent over you after me, and the one who will take charge of my authority over you.' And there was not one among them except that he desired that the Prophet would say to him: 'You are the one who will take charge after me.' On the fourth day, each man among them sat in his room, looking for the descent of the star, when suddenly a star fell from the sky, its light overpowering the light of the world, until it landed in the room of Ali (peace be upon him). The people became agitated and said: 'By Allah! This man has gone astray and is misguided, and he does not speak regarding his cousin except by desire.' So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed regarding that: 'By the star when it descends! Your companion is neither misguided nor astray, nor does he speak from desire. It is but an inspired revelation.' (53:1-4) to the end of the surah.

Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi narrated to me from al-Mufaddal b. Salih al-Asadi from Muhammad b. Marwan from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever hates us, the Ahl al-Bayt, Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a Jew. It was said: O Messenger of Allah! Even if he bears witness to the two testimonies? He said: Yes, for indeed he only upheld these two sayings so that his blood may not be shed, or so that he may pay the jizya as a subordinate. Then he said: Whoever hates us, the Ahl al-Bayt, Allah will raise him as a Jew. It was said: How then, O Messenger of Allah? He said: If he were to reach the Dajjal, he would believe in him.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Abi al-Jawza' from al-Husayn b. Ilwan from Amr b. Khalid from Asim b. Abi al-Nujud al-Asadi from Ibn Umar from al-Hasan b. Ali (peace be upon them both). He said: I heard my father Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: If a Muslim person were to sit in his place of prayer in which he prays Fajr, remembering Allah the Mighty and Majestic until sunrise, he will have the reward of one who has made pilgrimage to the House of Allah, and he will be forgiven. If he sits in it until the moment in which prayer becomes permissible again after sunrise, then prays two or four units, all his past sins will be forgiven, and he will have the reward of one who has made pilgrimage to the House of Allah.

Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from al-Hakam b. Miskin al-Thaqafi from Abu al-Ala al-Khaffaf from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said: Whoever prays Maghrib and then follows it up without speaking until he prays two units, they are recorded for him in Illiyyin. And if he prays four units, an accepted Hajj is recorded for him.

Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us from Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami from Ya'qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Hamza from one who heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Whoever meets a pilgrim and shakes his hand is like one who touched the [Black] Stone.

Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abdullah b. Ja'far b. Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us from his father from Banan b. Muhammad b. Isa from his father from Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: There is no servant who wakes up fasting and is then insulted, who responds: 'Indeed, I am fasting. Peace be upon you,' except that the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'My servant sought refuge from My servant by fasting. Save him from My Fire and admit him into My Paradise.'

Abd al-Wahid b. Muhammad al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Muhammad b. Qutayba al-Nisapuri narrated to us. He said: Hamdan b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Nu'man narrated to us from Abdullah b. Talha from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Whoever fasts the twenty-seventh of Rajab, Allah records the reward of seventy years of fasting for him.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Wasiti, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mundhir ibn Yazid, from Yunus ibn Thibyan, who said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Whoever fasts on a hot day and is afflicted with thirst, Allah appoints one thousand angels to wipe his face and give him glad tidings. Once he breaks his fast, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "How sweet is your fragrance and your spirit! O My angels, bear witness that I have forgiven him."

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: There is no fasting person who is present with a people who are eating except that his limbs glorify [Allah], and the angels send blessings upon him, and their blessings are a seeking of forgiveness for him.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from his paternal uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi — that he asked Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about fasting while residing at home (not travelling). He said: Three days every month — the Thursday before the first Friday, the Wednesday before the second Friday, and the Thursday before the third Friday. Al-Halabi said to him: Is this one day out of every ten days? He said: Yes. And the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) has said: Fasting the month of Ramadan and three days every month removes anxieties from the chests. Fasting three days in every month equals fasting the whole year. Verily God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like.' [Quran 6:160]

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, client of the Children of Hashim, narrated to us. He said: al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Sulayman from 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi. He said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), when a man from the people of Tus entered upon him. He said to him: O son of the Messenger of God! What is [the reward] for one who visits the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)? So he said to him: O Tusi! Whoever visits the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), while knowing that he is an Imam from God whose obedience is obligatory upon the servants — God will forgive him his past and future sins, and will accept his intercession for seventy sinners, and he will not ask God, Mighty and Majestic, for any need at his grave except that He will fulfill it for him. He said: Then Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) entered, so [Imam Sadiq] seated him on his lap and began to kiss his forehead, then turned to him [the Tusi man] and said: O Tusi! Indeed he is the Imam, the Caliph, and the Proof after me. And from his loins will come forth a man who will be pleasing to God, Mighty and Majestic, in His heavens, and to His servants on His earth. He will be killed in your land by poison, in oppression and hostility, and will be buried there as a stranger. Verily, whoever visits him in his solitude — while knowing that he is an Imam after his father, whose obedience is obligatory from God, Mighty and Majestic — shall be as one who visited the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family and peace).

Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from al-Saqr ibn Dulaf. He said: I heard my master Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: Whoever has a need from God (Blessed and Exalted) should visit the grave of my grandfather al-Rida (peace be upon him) in Tus in a state of ghusl (ritual bath), pray two units at his head, and ask God for his need in his qunut — and it will be fulfilled for him as long as he does not ask for a sin or for severing family ties. Truly, the place of his grave is a plot from the plots of Paradise. No believer visits it except that God frees him from the Fire and brings him into the Abode of Eternal Settlement.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Mundhir al-'Ishrani narrated to us. He said: Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated to us from Abu Qanbal, from Abu'l-Jarud, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: "Verily, the ring knocker of the gate of Paradise is made from a red ruby upon sheets of gold. When the ring strikes the plate, it chimes and calls out: 'O Ali!'"

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim ibn Abbas narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Abu Qutada al-Harrani narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Zadhan, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah — Mighty and Majestic — opened Mecca, we set out, and we were eight thousand men. When evening came upon us, we had become ten thousand Muslims. So emigration was lifted, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no emigration after the conquest of Mecca.' Then we arrived at Hawazin, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Stand and behold your honour with Allah, Mighty and Majestic — speak to the Sun when it rises.' Ibn Abbas said: By Allah, I did not envy anyone except Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) on that day. I said to al-Fadl: 'Come, let us see how Ali ibn Abi Talib speaks to the Sun.' When the Sun rose, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) stood and said: 'Peace be upon you, O righteous, obedient servant — perpetually in the obedience of Allah, your Lord.' The Sun replied to him, saying: 'And upon you be peace, O brother of the Messenger of Allah, his vicegerent, and the Proof of Allah over His creation.' Then Ali (peace be upon him) fell prostrate in gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: By Allah, I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stand and take Ali (peace be upon him) by the head, helping him rise and wiping his face, saying: 'Rise, my beloved, for you have made the people of heaven weep by your weeping, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has boasted about you to the carriers of His Throne.'

15 — My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Marrar narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me from Yunus ibn Ya'qub. He said: Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was with a group of his companions, among whom were Humran ibn A'yan, Mu'min al-Taq, Hisham ibn Salim, and al-Tayyar; and another group of his companions, among whom was Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who was a youth. Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Hisham! He said: At your service, O son of the Messenger of Allah. He said: Will you not inform me of what you did with 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd and how you questioned him? Hisham said: May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah! I hold you in great reverence and am abashed before you, and my tongue does not function in your presence. Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When I command you something, then do it. He (Hisham) said: News had reached me about 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd and his sitting in the mosque of Basra, and that weighed heavily upon me. So I went out to him and entered Basra on a Friday. I came to the mosque of Basra, and there I found a large circle of people, with 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd wearing a black woollen cloak around his waist and another over his shoulders, while the people were posing questions to him. I asked the people to make way and they did. I then sat at the back of the gathering on my knees and said: O scholar, I am a stranger — will you grant me permission to ask you something? He said: Yes. I said to him: Do you have eyes? He said: O my son, what kind of question is this? I said: Such is my question. He said: O my son, ask, even if your question is foolish. I said: Answer me. He said: Ask. I said: Do you have eyes? He said: Yes. I said: What do you see with them? He said: Colours and persons. I said: Do you have a nose? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I smell scents with it. I said: Do you have a mouth? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I distinguish the flavours of things with it. I said: Do you have a tongue? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I speak with it. I said: Do you have ears? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with them? He said: I hear sounds with them. I said: Do you have hands? He said: Yes. I said: Wha

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Nasr, from Aban, from Zurara and Ismail ibn Abbad al-Qasri, from Sulayman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: When the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was carried on the Night Journey and arrived where God, Blessed and Exalted, willed, his Lord, Mighty is His Glory, whispered to him in confidence. Then when he descended to the fourth heaven, He called out to him: 'O Muhammad!' He said: 'I am at Your service, my Lord.' He said to him: 'Who from your community have you chosen to be your vicegerent after you?' He said: 'Choose that for me, so that You may be the one who decides for me.' So He said to him: 'I have chosen for you the best of you — Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us from Jamil ibn Salih from 'Abdullah ibn Ghalib from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: A believer ought to have eight characteristics: dignified in calamities, patient in tribulation, grateful in prosperity, content with what God has provided him, he does not wrong his enemies, nor does he burden his friends, his body toils but the people are at ease because of him. Surely, knowledge is the intimate friend of the believer, forbearance is his vizier, patience is the commander of his forces, kindness is his brother, and gentleness is his father.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi. He said: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to me. He said: al-Hasan ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Yunus ibn Zabyan. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Fatima (peace be upon her) has nine names with God, Mighty and Majestic: Fatima, al-Siddiqa, al-Mubaraka, al-Tahira, al-Zakiyya, al-Radiya, al-Mardiyya, al-Muhaddatha, and al-Zahra. Then he said: Do you know why she was named Fatima? I said: Inform me, my master. He said: She was severed from evil. Then he said: Had the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) not married her, there would have been no match for her on the face of the earth until the Day of Resurrection — from Adam to those after him.

Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. 'Amir narrated to us from Mu'alla b. Muhammad al-Basri from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti from 'Ali b. Ja'far. He said: I heard Aba'l-Hasan Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: While the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) was sitting, an angel with twenty-four faces entered upon him. The Messenger of Allah said to him: My beloved Jibra'il, I have never seen you in such a form. The angel said: I am not Jibra'il. I am Mahmud. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent me to marry the light to the light. He (peace be upon him) said: Who to whom? He said: Fatima to 'Ali. He said: When the angel turned away, behold, between his shoulders was written: 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, 'Ali is his deputy.' The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: How long has this been written between your shoulders? He said: Twenty-two thousand years before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Ahmad al-Sa'igh narrated to us, he said: Abu Abdillah Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Khalili narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Bakr al-Faqih, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali, from Ishaq ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): How was the birth of Fatima (peace be upon her)? So he said: Yes, Indeed, when Khadija (peace be upon her) married the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), the women of Mecca abandoned her. They would not visit her, nor greet her, nor allow any woman to visit her. Khadija (peace be upon her) became lonely because of that, and it was a source of distress, and her grief was a concern for him (may God bless him and his family). When she became pregnant with Fatima (peace be upon her), she would speak to her from her womb and console her. She kept this hidden from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family). One day, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) entered and heard Khadija speaking to Fatima (peace be upon her), so he said to her: O Khadija, who are you speaking to? She said: The fetus in my womb speaks to me and keeps me company. He said: O Khadija, this is Gabriel informing me that she is a female, and that she is the pure and blessed offspring, and that God, Blessed and Exalted, will make my progeny from her, and will make Imams from her progeny, and will make them His vicegerents in His earth after the cessation of His revelation. Khadija (peace be upon her) remained in that state until the time of her delivery came. She sent word to the women of Quraysh and Banu Hashim: Come and attend to me as women attend to women. They sent back to her: You disobeyed us and did not accept our words, and you married Muhammad, the orphan of Abu Talib, a poor man with no wealth. So we will not come, nor will we attend to any of your matter. Khadija (peace be upon her) grieved because of that. While she was thus, suddenly four tall dark-complexioned women entered upon her, as if they were women from Banu Hashim. She was startled when she saw them. One of them said: Do not grieve, O Khadija, for we are messengers from your Lord to you, and we a

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Uluwiyya al-Isbahani narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, he said: Abu Nuaym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, he said: Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, he said: Firas narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Aisha, who said: Fatima (peace be upon her) approached walking as if her walk were the walk of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet said: Welcome, my daughter! Then he seated her on his right or on his left. Then he whispered to her and she wept. Then he whispered to her again and she laughed. I said to her: The Messenger of Allah told you something and you wept, then told you something and you laughed. I have never seen joy closer to grief than your joy! I asked her about what he said, and she said: I would not reveal the secret of the Messenger of Allah. When he passed away, I asked her and she said: He confided in me and said: Indeed Gabriel used to review the Quran with me once every year, and this year he reviewed it with me twice. I do not think except that my appointed time has come. And you will be the first of my family to join me, and what an excellent predecessor I am for you. So I wept because of that. Then he said: Would you not be pleased to be the leader of the women of this nation, or the women of the believers? So I laughed because of that.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us, he said: Furat ibn Ibrahim ibn Furat al-Kufi narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to me, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sulayman al-Qattan informed me, he said: al-Hasan ibn Jibra'il al-Hamdani narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Jibra'il informed us, he said: Abu Abdillah al-Jurjani narrated to us, from Nuaym al-Nakha'i, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, he said: I was sitting before the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) one day, and before him were Ali ibn Abi Talib, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), when Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended to him with an apple in his hand. He greeted the Prophet with it, and the Prophet greeted Ali with it, so Ali greeted with it and returned it to the Prophet. The Prophet greeted with it and greeted al-Hasan with it, so he kissed it and returned it to the Prophet. The Prophet greeted with it and greeted al-Husayn, so al-Husayn greeted with it, kissed it, and returned it to the Prophet. The Prophet greeted with it and greeted Fatima, so she kissed it and returned it to the Prophet. The Prophet greeted with it a second time and greeted Ali with it, so Ali greeted with it a second time. When he was about to return it to the Prophet, the apple fell from the tips of his fingers and split into two halves. A light shone from it until it reached the sky of the world, and there were two lines written on it: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is a greeting from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to Muhammad al-Mustafa, Ali al-Murtada, Fatima al-Zahra, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn, the two grandsons of the Messenger of Allah, and a protection for their lovers on the Day of Resurrection from the Fire.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya narrated to us. He said: Umayr ibn Imran narrated to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Amr al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from Rib'i ibn Khirash, from Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman. He said: I saw the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) holding the hand of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), and he was saying: O people! This is al-Husayn ibn Ali, so recognize him. For by the One in whose hand is my soul, he will surely be in Paradise, and his lovers will be in Paradise, and the lovers of his lovers will be in Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I was with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) during his march to Siffin. When he halted at Naynawa, on the bank of the Euphrates, he called out at the top of his voice: 'O Ibn Abbas, do you recognize this place?' I said to him: 'I do not recognize it, O Commander of the Faithful.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'If you knew it as I know it, you would not pass through it without weeping as I weep.' He then wept at length until his beard was drenched and tears flowed down his chest, and we wept with him. He was saying: 'Alas, alas! What is it between me and the family of Abu Sufyan, what is it between me and the family of Harb, the party of Satan and allies of disbelief! Be patient, O Abu Abdullah — for your father has endured the like of what you shall endure from them.' Then he called for water, performed wudu as for prayer, and prayed as much as Allah willed him to pray. Then he recalled words similar to his first speech, except that he dozed off for a moment at the conclusion of his prayer and speech, then he awakened and said: 'O Ibn Abbas.' I replied: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Shall I not tell you what I saw in my sleep just now, during my brief rest?' I said: 'May your eyes sleep soundly and may you see good, O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'I saw as though men had descended from the sky, bearing white banners, girded with their swords — gleaming white swords — and they had drawn a circle around this land. Then I saw as though these palm trees had struck the earth with their branches, quivering in a pool of fresh blood. And as though al-Husayn — my little lamb, my fledgling, my morsel, and my very marrow — had sunk into it, crying for help but receiving none. And as though the white men had descended from the sky, calling out to him and saying: Be patient, O family of the Messenger, for you shall be slain by the hands of the worst of people, and Paradise — O Abu Abdullah — longs for you. Then they consoled me, saying: O Abu al-Hasan, rejoice, for Allah has gladdened your eyes by him on the Day of R

Our father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, when he was taken on the Night Journey to the heavens, did not pass by any creation of Allah except that he saw from it cheerfulness, kindness, and happiness toward him — until he passed by a creation of Allah who did not turn toward him, nor say anything to him. He found him frowning and scowling. So he said: 'O Jibril, I have not passed by any creation of Allah except that I have seen cheerfulness, kindness, and happiness from it — except this one. Who is this?' He said: 'This is Malik, the keeper of the Fire, and thus did his Lord create him.' He said: 'I would like you to request of him that he show me the Fire.' So Jibril said to him: 'This is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, and he has asked me to request of you that you show him the Fire.' So he revealed a portion of it for him, and he saw it. And he never smiled broadly again until Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, took him (in death).

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Layth ibn Sa'd. He said: I said to Ka'b while he was at Mu'awiya's court: 'How do you find the description of the Prophet's birth (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), and do you find any virtue for his progeny?' Ka'b turned to Mu'awiya to gauge his inclination, but God, Mighty and Exalted, caused speech to flow upon his tongue, and (Mu'awiya) said: 'Speak, O Abu Ishaq — may God have mercy on you — what do you have to say?' Ka'b said: 'I have read seventy-two books, all of which were revealed from heaven, and I have read all the scrolls of Daniel, and I found in all of them mention of his birth and the birth of his progeny, that his name is well known, and that no prophet was ever born upon whom the angels descended except Jesus and Ahmad (blessings of God upon them both). upon them both. And the veils of Paradise were never drawn for any human woman except Maryam and Aminah, the mother of Ahmad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). And the angels were never charged with guarding a woman who carried a child except Maryam, the mother of the Messiah, and Aminah, the mother of Ahmad. Among the signs of his conception was that on the night Aminah conceived him (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), a caller called out in the seven heavens: 'Rejoice, for tonight Ahmad has been conceived!' And likewise in the earths, and even in the seas. There was no creature that walked on the earth nor any bird that flew that day except that it knew of his birth. And seventy thousand palaces of red ruby and seventy thousand palaces of fresh pearl were built in Paradise on the night of his birth. It was said: 'These are the palaces of the birth.' The gardens of Paradise were adorned and it was said to them: 'Quiver and adorn yourself, for the Prophet of those devoted to you has been born.' So Paradise laughed that day, and it has been laughing until the Day of Resurrection. I have also heard that a fish from the fish of the sea, called Tamsoosus, the master of all fish, has seven hundred thousand tails, upon w

Ali ibn Isa al-Mujawar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Muqri, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Thuwayr ibn Said, from his father Said ibn Alaqa, from al-Hasan al-Basri. He said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), ascended the pulpit of Basra and said: O people, tell me my lineage! Whoever recognizes me, let him tell my lineage. If not, then I shall tell my own lineage. I am Zayd ibn Abd Manaf ibn Amir ibn Amr ibn al-Mughira ibn Zayd ibn Kilab. Then Ibn al-Kawwa stood up to him and said: O you! We do not know any lineage for you other than that you are Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim ibn Abd Manaf ibn Qusay ibn Kilab. So he said to him: O fool! Indeed, my father named me Zayd after his grandfather Qusay. And the name of my father is Abd Manaf, but the kunya overcame the name. And the name of Abd al-Muttalib is Amir, but the title overcame the name. And the name of Hashim is Amr, but the epithet overcame the name. And the name of Abd Manaf is al-Mughira, but the title overcame the name. And the name of Qusay is Zayd, but the Arabs called him Mujammi (the gatherer) because he gathered them from the furthest land to Mecca, so the title overcame the name.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, he said: al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): Indeed, a servant from among My servants may come to Me with a good deed, and I will grant him My Paradise. He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) said: O my Lord, and what is that good deed? He said: He brings happiness into My believing servant, even if by giving him a date. He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) said: It is right that one who recognizes You should never lose hope in You.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid. He said: I heard Yunus ibn Yaqub narrating from Sinan ibn Turayf, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: He said: We are the first household whose names God proclaimed. When God created the heavens and the earth, He ordered a caller, and he called out: "I bear witness that there is no god but God" three times, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God" three times, and "I bear witness that Ali is truly the Commander of the Faithful" three times.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza. He said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family): O Muhammad! Indeed I created you when you were nothing, and I breathed into you of My Spirit as an honour from Me that I bestowed upon you, so that I obliged all My creatures to obey you. Whoever obeys you has indeed obeyed Me, and whoever disobeys you has indeed disobeyed Me. And I have obliged the same regarding Ali and those of his progeny whom I have designated for Myself.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Abbad ibn Yaqub, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah’s blessings be upon him and his family) said: There is not a morning except that two angels call out, saying: “O seeker of good, come! O seeker of evil, stop! Is there a supplicant so that he may be answered? Is there one who seeks forgiveness so that he may be forgiven? Is there a penitent so that he may be pardoned? Is there an anguished one so that his anguish may be relieved? O Allah, hasten for the one who spends his wealth a replacement, and for the one who withholds, ruin.” This is their supplication until the sun sets.

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him): O Isa! I have not honoured any creature with the like of My religion, nor have I bestowed upon it a blessing like My mercy. Wash with water what is apparent of you, and heal with good deeds what is hidden, for indeed you are returning to Me. Prepare yourself, for all that is coming is near. And let Me hear from you a sorrowful voice.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever loves a disbeliever has indeed hated God, and whoever hates a disbeliever has indeed loved God. Then he (peace be upon him) said: The friend of the enemy of God is the enemy of God.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us, he said: al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from Sa'd ibn Turayf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in one of his sermons: O people! Listen to my words and reflect upon them from me, for indeed the separation is near. I am the Imam of humanity, the deputy of the best of creation, the husband of the Mistress of the Women of this Nation, and the father of the pure progeny and the guiding Imams. I am the brother of the Messenger of God, his deputy, his guardian, his vizier, his companion, his chosen one, his beloved, and his intimate friend. I am the Commander of the Faithful, the leader of the radiant and distinguished believers, and the master of the successors. My war is the war of God, and my peace is the peace of God.
