Obedience to me is obedience to God, my authority is the authority of God, my followers are the friends of God, and my supporters are the supporters of God. By Him who created me when I was nothing, the preservers among the companions of Muhammad (may God bless him and his family) know that the oath-breakers, the deviators, and the apostates are cursed upon the tongue of the unlettered Prophet; and indeed, those who fabricated lies have failed.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: One of my forefathers (peace be upon them) heard a man reciting Umm al-Quran (al-Fatiha), so he said: 'Thanksgiving and reward.' Then he heard him reciting 'Say: He is God, the One' (al-Ikhlas), so he said: 'He has believed and is secure.' Then he heard him reciting 'Indeed We sent it down' (al-Qadr), so he said: 'He spoke the truth, and was forgiven.' Then he heard him reciting Ayat al-Kursi, so he said: 'Bravo, bravo! The dissociation of this person from the Fire has descended.'

And by this chain of narration, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Surely, God — Mighty and Majestic — has one thousand whiffs of His mercy on Friday, and He gives every servant from it as much as He wills. So, whoever recites 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylati al-qadr' (Surah al-Qadr, 97:1) one hundred times after the Asr prayer on Friday, God gifts him those one thousand and their like.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying: Gabriel descended upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Muhammad! Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — conveys His greetings to you and says: 'I have prohibited the Fire upon the loins that bequeathed you, the womb that carried you, and the lap that adopted you.' So he said: O Gabriel! Clarify that for me. He said: As for the loins that bequeathed you, that is Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. As for the womb that carried you, that is Amina bint Wahb. As for the lap that adopted you, that is Abu Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Fatima bint Asad.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from his paternal uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Sharif ibn Sabiq al-Taflisi, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra al-Samandi. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: There was a famine among the Children of Israel, to the point that they exhumed the dead and ate them. Then they exhumed a grave and found in it a tablet upon which was written: "I am so-and-so the Prophet. An Abyssinian will exhume my grave. What we sent ahead — we found it; what we ate — we profited from it; and what we left behind — we lost it."

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever has the weight of a mustard seed of tribal chauvinism ('asabiyya) in his heart, God Almighty will raise him on the Day of Resurrection with the bedouins of the Age of Ignorance.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Ayyub Sulayman ibn Muqbil al-Madani, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf al-Zamm, from Abu Ubayda. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Whoever says in the marketplace: 'I bear witness that there is no god but God, alone, without partner; and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger,' God records one million good deeds for him.

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever says 'Glory be to God (subhan Allah)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it. Whoever says 'Praise be to God (alhamdulillah)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it. Whoever says 'There is no god but God (la ilaha illa Allah)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it. Whoever says 'God is the Greatest (Allahu akbar)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it. Then a man from Quraysh said: O Messenger of God, then we have many trees in Paradise! He said: Yes, but beware of sending fires upon them to burn them. For God, Mighty and Majestic, says: O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger, and do not invalidate your deeds.

Al-Shaykh al-Jalil Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, may God have mercy on him, said: My father, may God be pleased with him, narrated to me saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kamandani narrated to us saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari narrated to us saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran narrated to us, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said: God, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Adam, peace be upon him: O Adam, I shall gather all goodness for you in four sayings: one of them is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and the people. As for that which is for Me, you shall worship Me and not associate anything with Me. As for that which is for you, I shall reward you for your deeds when you are most in need of it. As for that which is between Me and you, upon you is the supplication and upon Me is the response. And as for that which is between you and the people, be pleased for the people with what you are pleased with for yourself.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari. He said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: My God! Your power is apparent, yet You have not appeared in any form. So they became ignorant of You and tried to measure You, while the true measure is other than how they describe You. And indeed I dissociate, O my God, from those who seek You through anthropomorphism. There is nothing like unto You. My God, they shall never comprehend You. The apparent blessings they have from You would be their indicator toward You, had they recognized You. And in Your creation, O my God, there is ample evidence that precludes them from grasping You through similitude, yet they equated You with Your creation, and thence they did not recognize You. They took some of Your signs as a lord, and by that they described You. You are exalted, my Lord, above what the anthropomorphists attribute to You.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) was asked - it was said to him: How was your morning, O son of the Messenger of God? He said: I awoke with a Lord above me, the Fire before me, death seeking me, and the Reckoning staring at me. I am held hostage by my deeds. I cannot find what I love, nor can I repel what I hate. The affairs are in the hand of one other than me - if He wills, He may punish me, and if He wills, He may pardon me. Which poor person is poorer than me?!

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to me from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: The affliction of the people is great: if we call them, they do not respond to us; and if we leave them, they will not be guided by anyone other than us.

Al-Mufaddal said: I heard al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say to his companions: Whoever finds the coolness of our love upon his heart, let him increase his supplications for his mother, for indeed she did not betray his father.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I said to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): A man saw his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in his dream, so what is that? He said: That is a man with no religion. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, cannot be seen when awake, nor in a dream, nor in this world, nor in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi al-Kufi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): Inform me about Allah, Blessed and Exalted -- Has He always been All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Knowing, and All-Powerful? He said: Yes. So I said to him: There is a man who claims allegiance to you, the Ahl al-Bayt, and he says: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has always been hearing through an instrument of hearing, seeing through sight, knowing through knowledge, and powerful through an instrument of power." He said: So he (peace be upon him) became angry, then said: Whoever says that and takes it as his religion is a polytheist (mushrik), and has nothing to do with our authority (wilaya). Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is an Essence that is All-Knowing, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and All-Powerful.

Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me in the year 307 AH. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated to us, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: A quarrel and dispute occurred between Salman al-Farisi (may God have mercy on him) and a man. The man said to him: Who are you, Salman? So Salman said: As for my beginning and your beginning, it was an impure drop of sperm. As for my end and your end, it will be a rotting corpse. On the Day of Resurrection, when the scales are placed, the one whose scale is heavy is the noble one, and the one whose scale is light is the vile one.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: Indeed, I will be killed, poisoned, and buried in a strange land. I know this through a covenant that my father entrusted to me, from his father, from his forefathers, from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family). Surely, whoever visits me in my place of exile, my forefathers and I shall be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever has our intercession shall be saved, even if his sins were equivalent to the burden of the two heavyweights (humanity and the Jinn).

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, saying: Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Nawanjiyy narrated to me, from Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Shu'ayri, from al-Rabi' — the companion of al-Mansur — who said: Al-Mansur sent for al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, summoning him regarding something that had been reported to him about him. When he arrived at his gate, the chamberlain came out to him and said: 'I seek God's protection for you against the tyranny of this oppressor, for I have seen his rage against you is severe.' Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: 'I have from God a protecting shield that will aid me against him, if God wills. Seek permission for me to enter.' So he sought permission and it was granted. When he entered, he gave the greeting of peace, and al-Mansur returned it. Then he said to him: 'O Ja'far, you well know that the Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him and his family, said to your father Ali ibn Abi Talib: "Were it not that factions of my community would say about you what the Christians said about Christ, I would say something about you such that you would pass no gathering without them taking the dust from beneath your feet to seek healing by it." And Ali, peace be upon him, said: "Two types of people will perish on my account, though I bear no guilt: the excessively devoted lover and the reckless defector." He said this as an apology from himself — that he does not approve of what the extremist or the defector says about him. By my life, if Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, had remained silent about what the Christians said of him, God would have tormented him. You know full well what false and slanderous things are said about you, and your silence about that and your contentment with it is the wrath of the Divine Judge.' The riffraff of Hijaz and the rabble of the people claim that you are the scholar of the age and its supreme authority, the proof of the Worshipped One and His interpreter, the vessel of His knowledge and the scale of His justice — His lamp by which the seeker cuts through the breadth of darkness to the light of illumination; and that God does not accept any deed from any doer who is ignorant of your station in this world, nor raises for him on the Day of

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-'Abdi, from al-A'mash, from 'Abaya ibn Rib'i, from 'Abdallah ibn 'Abbas, from his father. He said: Abu Talib said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): O nephew! Did God send you? He said: Yes. He said: Then show me a sign. He said: Call to that tree for me. So he called it, and it came forward until it prostrated before him. Then it went away. So Abu Talib said: I bear witness that you are truthful. O Ali, pray behind your cousin.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to me. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to me from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Thabit ibn Dinar al-Thumali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abdullah ibn Abbas: that a man asked him, saying: 'O cousin of the Messenger of God! Inform me about Abu Talib — was he a Muslim?' So he said: 'How could he not be a Muslim, while he is the one who said: "They knew that our son is not a liar with us, nor does he pay heed to false and baseless sayings." Indeed, the likeness of Abu Talib is like the companions of the Cave — who concealed the faith and feigned polytheism — so God gave them their reward twice.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said: Surely, the example of Abu Talib is like that of the Companions of the Cave, who kept their faith secret and displayed polytheism, so God gave them their reward twice.

The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Turayf narrated to us from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Learn knowledge, for surely learning it is a good deed, studying it is glorification, researching it is jihad, and teaching it to one who does not know it is charity. It is, before God, a means of nearness for its possessors, because it contains the markers of the permissible and the forbidden. It guides its seeker to the path of Paradise. It is a companion in loneliness, a friend in solitude, a weapon against enemies, and the adornment of friends. Through it, God raises peoples and makes them leaders in goodness who are followed. Their deeds are admired, their sayings are quoted, and the angels desire their friendship, wiping them with their wings during their prayers. For knowledge is the life of hearts, the light of sight from blindness, and the strength of bodies from weakness. God settles its bearer in the stations of the righteous and grants him the company of the elect in this world and the Hereafter. By knowledge, God is obeyed and worshipped; by knowledge, God is recognized and affirmed as One; by knowledge, family ties are maintained; and through it, the permissible and the forbidden are known. Knowledge is the leader of the intellect, and the intellect is its follower. God inspires it to the fortunate and deprives the wretched of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Makki, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Be truly modest before God. They said: What should we do, O Messenger of God? He said: If you do so, then none of you should sleep except that he sees death before his eyes. Let him guard his head and what it contains, and his stomach and what it consumes. Let him remember the grave and decay. And whoever desires the Hereafter, let him abandon the adornment of the life of this world.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Munqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i the judge. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): What is asceticism in this world? He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has defined that in His Book, and He said: So that you may not grieve at the things that pass you by, nor rejoice over that which has been given to you.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from al-Fadl ibn Yunus. He said: Ibn Abi al-'Awja' was one of the students of al-Hasan al-Basri, but he deviated from monotheism. It was said to him: You abandoned the school of your companion and entered into that which has no basis and no reality? He said: My companion was confused — he would argue for free will at one time, and for determinism at another. I do not know that he held any school consistently. He said: He came to Mecca out of rebellion and to denounce the pilgrims. The scholars disliked his questioning them and sitting with them due to the filth of his tongue and the corruption of his conscience. So he came to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and sat with him among a group of his peers. Then he said to him: O Abu 'Abdillah! Gatherings are trusts, and whoever has a cough must cough. Do you permit me to speak? Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Say what you wish. Ibn Abi al-'Awja' said: How long will you continue treading this threshing floor, taking refuge in this stone, worshipping this House built of bricks and clay, and running around it like a startled camel? Whoever thinks or reflects on this would know that this is an act founded by one who is neither wise nor far-sighted. So speak, for you are the head and the hump of this matter, and your father was its foundation and its order. Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: He whom God leads astray and blinds in heart finds the truth disagreeable and cannot relish it. Satan becomes his guardian and leads him to the watering holes of destruction without return. This House is one by which God has made His creation His servants, to test their obedience in coming to it. He urged them to venerate it and visit it, and He has made it the station of the Prophets and the qibla of those who pray to Him. It is a branch of His good pleasure and a path that leads to His forgiveness, erected upon the uprightness of perfection and the gathering of greatness. God created it two thousand years before He spread out the Earth. God — the Originator of spirits and forms — is most deserving of being obeyed in what He commands and being heeded in what He prohibits and forbids. Ibn Abi al-'Awja' s

Al-Husayn ibn 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us. He said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Ra'l al-'Abshami informed us. He said: Thubayt ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Ahwas al-Misri narrated to us. He said: A group from the people of knowledge narrated to us from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them. He said: While the Commander of the Faithful, blessings of God be upon them, was in the most difficult stand at Siffin, a man from the tribe of Dudan stood up before him and said: What is the matter with your people that they pushed you away from this affair, while you are the noblest in lineage, the closest in connection to the Messenger, and the most knowledgeable of the Book and the Sunna? He replied: You have asked, O brother of the Bani Dudan — and you have the right to ask and the bond of kinship — and indeed you are like one whose saddle-girth has loosened, releasing from a twisted rope. It is an authority over which the souls of some people were covetous, while the souls of others were generous in relinquishing it — and what an excellent Judge is God! So leave aside a plunder over which cries were raised in its enclosures, and come to the real matter regarding the son of Abu Sufyan, for time has made me laugh after making me weep. There is no wonder except in my neighbor and her question: 'Alas, do we have anyone?' I asked likewise. Wretched are the people who have lowered me! They have tried to practice deception in the religion of God. If the trials of affliction are lifted from us, I shall carry them upon the pure essence of the truth. And if it be the other outcome, then 'do not grieve over the transgressing people' [5:26]. Away from me, O brother of Bani Dudan.

Narrated to us Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa’id, who said: Narrated to us Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Hajjaj the just, who said: Narrated to us Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Nahwi, who said: Narrated to us Shu’ayb ibn Waqid, who said: Narrated to us Salih ibn Al-Salt, from Abdullah ibn Zuhayr, who said: Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Hadrami visited the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I have family members whom I treat kindly, but they mistreat me, and I maintain ties with them, but they cut me off.’ The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, ‘Repel [evil] by that which is better, and behold, the one between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one possessing great fortune.’ Al-Ala’ ibn Al-Hadrami said, ‘I have composed poetry that is better than this.’ He said, ‘What have you composed?’ So he recited to him: ‘Greet the holders of grudges, and their hearts will be moved by your noble greeting, for even the ignoble may be elevated. If they show goodness, then repay with the like of it, and if they withhold speech from you, then do not ask. For what harms you from it is hearing it, and what they said behind your back was never actually said.’ The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, ‘Indeed in poetry there is wisdom, and indeed in eloquent speech there is enchantment, and your poetry is beautiful, but the Book of Allah is more beautiful.’

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ta'i narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhsin narrated to us from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father (peace be upon them all). He said: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, your world means nothing to me except like the spit in the mouth of one who grasps a locust and then throws it out. What benefit is there in a blessing that passes away or a property that will be seized? O people, this world is a passing abode, not a permanent dwelling. Its people are of two types: the one who sold himself [for it] and destroyed himself, and the one who purchased himself and freed himself. What has perished of it is not hoped for in return, and what remains of it is not known as lasting. Its joy turns to sorrow, its sorrow is not repelled, its good is blotted out, and its evil cannot be turned away. (Quran 11:15-16) 'Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments — We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire. And lost is what they did therein, and worthless is what they used to do.' How can I endure the Fire when you could not bear the heated iron rod even for the sake of a game? How then can I be patient with a fire kindled by God's wrath? You flee from the pain of a needle, so how would you endure its scorpions, its irons, and its flames? By Allah, I have heard that a man from the inhabitants of al-Mada'in followed after the Hanifiyya (Islam) and donned its trappings and then abandoned it for the religion of the Zoroastrians, riding their horses and adopting their customs. May Allah fight him! He sold the part of the eternal, vast, abundant kingdom for the part of the perishable, meager, narrow world. O my Shia community, beware! The world has warned you with its fangs, snatching souls one after another like a wolf among a flock of scattered sheep. By Allah, I see how your Imam obeys Allah while you disobey. Your enemies transgress against Allah and you hold back. Those who love you are harmed for your sake while those who hate you are honoured on your account. By Allah, if

The illustrious Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh the jurist (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from his father. He said: I asked Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the middle night of Sha'ban. He said: It is a night in which Allah frees the necks from the Fire and forgives major sins in it. I said: Are there any extra prayers in it beyond the rest of the nights? So he said: There is nothing prescribed in it, but if you would like to perform voluntary worship in it with something, then upon you is the prayer of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and increase your remembrance of Allah — Mighty and Majestic — in it, and your seeking of forgiveness and supplication, for indeed my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Supplication in it is answered.' I said to him: Indeed the people say that it is the night of ordinance. So he (peace be upon him) said: That is the Night of Qadr in the month of Ramadan.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: All goodness is gathered in three qualities: sight, silence, and speech. Every sight devoid of consideration is negligence. Every silence devoid of thought is heedlessness. Every speech devoid of remembrance [of Allah] is prattle. Blessed is the one whose sight is a lesson, whose silence is contemplation, and whose speech is remembrance — who cries over his sin and from whose evil the people are safe.

3 - Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Said b. Abi Shahma narrated to us. He said: Abu Muhammad Abdullah b. Said b. Hashim al-Qinani al-Baghdadi narrated to us in the year 285 AH. He said: Ahmad b. Salih narrated to us. He said: Hasan b. Abdullah al-Wasiti narrated to us. He said: Abdullah b. Lahia narrated to us from Abu Qabil, from Abdullah b. Amr b. al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Yahya b. Zakariyya (peace be upon them) was overwhelmed by weeping, so he went to the children of the worshippers. He saw their worship garments and garments of asceticism, and he found within himself a love for worship. So he went to his mother and said: O mother, weave for me a garment of hair so that I may go to the children of the worshippers and worship with the rabbis and monks. So his mother said to him: Wait until the Prophet of Allah comes and I consult him about that. When Zakariyya (peace be upon him) entered, she told him about what Yahya said. Zakariyya said to him: O my son, what calls you to this while you are but a small boy! He said to him: O father, have you not seen one who is younger than me and has already tasted death? He said: Yes indeed. Then he said to his mother: Weave for him a garment of hair and a hood of wool. So she did. So he wore the garment upon his body, placed the hood on his head, then came to the Temple of Jerusalem and began worshipping Allah the Mighty and Majestic with the rabbis, until the hair garment consumed his flesh. He looked one day at what had wasted of his body and wept. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: O Yahya, do you weep because of what has wasted of your body! By My Might and Majesty, had you glimpsed the Fire a single glance, you would have worn a garment of iron, let alone the woven one. So he wept until the tears consumed the flesh of his cheeks, and his molars became visible to the onlookers. That news reached his mother. She entered upon him, and Zakariyya came, and the rabbis and monks gathered. They informed him of the loss of flesh from his cheeks. He said: I did not feel that. Zakariyya said: O my son, what calls you to this? I only asked my Lord to grant you to me so that my eye would be delighted with you. He said: You commanded me to do that, O father. He said: And when was that, my son? He said: Are you not the one wh

Muhammad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi'l Qasim narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. Umar from Thabit b. Abi Safiyya from Sa'id b. Jubayr from Abdullah b. Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O people! Who is better than Allah in speech, and more truthful than Allah in words? O people! Surely, your Lord, exalted is His majesty, has commanded me to establish Ali as a sign, an Imam, a caliph, and a deputy for you; and to take him as a brother and a vizier. O people! Ali is the gate of guidance after me and the caller to my Lord. He is the Righteous of the Believers, "And who is better in speech than he who calls to Allah, does righteous works, and says 'Surely, I am from those who submit'" [41:33]. O people! Surely, Ali is from me, his descendants are my descendants, and he is the husband of my beloved. His command is my command, and his prohibition is my prohibition. O people! Betake to obeying him and avoid disobeying him, for obeying him is obeying me, and disobeying him is disobeying me. O people! Surely, Ali is the saint of this nation, its distinguisher, and its inspired one. He is its Harun, its Yusha, its Asif, and its Shamun. He is its Gate of Remission and its Ark of Salvation. He is its Talut and its Dhul Qarnayn. O people! He is the affliction of the creation, the decisive argument, the great sign, the Imam of the people of this world, and the Firm Handle. O people! Surely, Ali is with the truth, and the truth is with him, and it is upon his tongue. O people! Surely, Ali is the divider of the Fire: a friend of his will not enter the Fire, and an enemy of his will not be saved from it. He is the divider of Paradise: an enemy of his will not enter it, and a friend of his will not slip away from it. O my companions! I have advised you and delivered the message of my Lord to you, but you do not love the advisors. I say this saying of mine, and I seek forgiveness of Allah for myself and for you.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa b. Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali b. Abi Hamza, from Yahya b. Abi Ishaq, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, peace be upon them. He said: The Prophet (s) was asked: Where were you when Adam was in Paradise? He said: I was in his loins. He descended to the Earth with me in his loins. I boarded the Ark in the loins of my father Nuh. I was thrown into the Fire in the loins of my father Ibrahim. None of my ancestors ever committed adultery. God, the Mighty and Majestic, did not cease transferring me from pure loins to purified wombs, guiding and guided, until God took my pledge in prophethood and my covenant in Islam. He clarified every one of my characteristics, and He established my mention in the Torah and the Gospel. He raised me to His heaven and derived for me a name from His most beautiful names — my nation are the praisers, the Possessor of the Throne is Mahmud (the Praised), and I am Muhammad.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Yunus ibn Thibyan, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: Darrar ibn Damra al-Nahshali visited Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan. He said to him: Describe 'Ali to me. He said: Rather, excuse me. So he said: No, rather describe him to me. So Darrar said to him: May Allah have mercy on 'Ali. By Allah, when he was among us, he was like one of us. He would draw us near when we came to him, he would answer us when we asked him, and he would bring us close when we visited him. No door was locked against us by him, and no barrier was placed between us and him. By Allah, despite his drawing us near and his closeness to us, we could not speak to him because of his awesome dignity, nor could we address him first because of his greatness. And when he smiled, it was like a strand of glistening pearls. So Mu'awiya said: Tell me more about him. So Darrar said: May Allah have mercy on 'Ali. By Allah, he prolonged his wakefulness and slept little. He would recite the Book of Allah throughout the watches of the night and at the edges of the day. He would give his life's blood freely for God and return to Him in tears. His curtains were never shut, and the full moons were never hidden from us. He would not seek the softness of reclining, nor would he make roughness coarser. If only you had seen him when he stood in his prayer niche, the night having drawn down its veils, the stars having set, while he clutched his beard and writhed with the writhing of the one bitten by a serpent, and wept with the weeping of the grieved, saying: 'O world! Is it me you present yourself to? Or is it me you yearn for? Go far, far away! I have no need of you. I have divorced you thrice — there is no return for you to me.' Then he would say: 'Ah, ah — how distant the journey, how few the provisions, and how rough the road!' He said: So Mu'awiya wept and said: That is enough, O Darrar! By Allah, that is how 'Ali was. May Allah have mercy on Aba al-Hasan.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: O Jabir! Is one who claims to uphold Shi'ism satisfied merely by declaring his love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt? By Allah, our Shi'a are only those who fear and obey Allah. They would not be recognized, O Jabir, except by their humility, their reverence, their frequent remembrance of Allah, fasting, prayer, their faithful care for neighbours who are poor, destitute, in debt, and orphaned, their truthfulness in speech, their recitation of the Quran, their restraining of their tongues from people except in goodness — and they were the trustees of their clans in all matters. Jabir said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, I do not know anyone today with these qualities. So he (peace be upon him) said: O Jabir, do not let the sects lead you astray. Does a man think it sufficient to say 'I love 'Ali and take him as my patron'? For even if he were to say 'I love the Messenger of Allah' — and the Messenger of Allah is better than 'Ali — then does not act by his example nor follow his Sunnah, his love for him would not benefit him at all. So fear Allah and act for what is with Allah. There is no relationship between Allah and anyone. The most beloved of servants to Allah and the most honoured in His sight are those who are the most God-fearing of them toward Him and the most obedient to Him. By Allah, none draws near to Allah — Majestic be His praise — except through obedience. We do not carry a guarantee of immunity from the Fire for anyone, nor does anyone have a binding argument against Allah. Whoever obeys Allah is our friend, and whoever disobeys Allah is our enemy. Our wilaya cannot be attained except through piety and righteous action.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: I went out with my father (peace be upon him) until we were between the grave [of the Prophet] and the pulpit, and he encountered people from the Shi'a. He gave them his salaam and they returned his salaam. Then he said: By Allah, I love your fragrance and your spirits, so support me in this through piety and striving. Know that our wilaya can only be reached through good deeds and striving. Whoever among you follows a servant [of God], let him act by his deeds. You are the Shi'a of Allah and you are the supporters of Allah. You are the forerunners of the former and the latter peoples — the forerunners in this world toward our wilaya, and the forerunners in the Hereafter toward Paradise. We have guaranteed you Paradise with the guarantee of Allah and His Messenger. None among the ranks of Paradise has more spouses than you, so compete with one another in attaining the higher ranks. You are the pure ones, and your women are the pure ones. Every believing woman is a bright-eyed houri, and every believing man is a truthful one (siddiq). And indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Qanbar: 'O Qanbar! Rejoice, give glad tidings, and be joyful, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) died while he was displeased with his community — except the Shi'a.' Beware! For everything there is a firm handle, and the firm handle of Islam is the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is a pillar, and the pillar of Islam is the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is a nobility, and the nobility of Islam is the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is a master, and the master of gatherings are the gatherings of the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is an Imam, and the Imam of the earth is the land inhabited by the Shi'a. By Allah, were it not for what of you is upon the earth, Allah would not have bestowed His blessings upon those who oppose you, nor would they have obtained good things. They have no share in this world or in the Hereafter. Every Nasib [opponent of the Ahlulbayt] — even if he worships and strives — is ascribed to this verse: 'Overburdened and exhausted, they wi

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us, from his father, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Sha'ban is my month, and Ramadan is the month of God, Mighty and Majestic. So whoever fasts a day in my month, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever fasts the month of Ramadan shall be freed from the Fire.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: Whoever says seventy times every day in Sha'ban, "I seek the forgiveness of God and I ask Him for repentance," God will record for him a dissociation from the Fire, a permit over the Path, and will grant him the Abode of Permanence.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said: Whoever gives charity in Sha'ban, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will nurture it for him just as one of you nurtures his young camel, until he arrives on the Day of Resurrection and it has become for him the like of Mount Uhud.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: O Ishaq! Soften your speech with the hypocrite, be sincere in your love for the believer, and if a Jew sits with you, then be gracious in his company.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. He said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, say: The seekers of this knowledge are of three types. Behold, recognize them by their qualities and their signs. One group among them learns for argumentation and disputation, one group among them learns for stonewalling and deception, and one group among them learns for understanding and action. As for the one of argumentation and disputation, you see him causing harm and quarreling with men in gatherings of discourse. He garbs himself in humility yet is void of piety. So may Allah crush his chest and sever his nose. As for the one of stonewalling and deception, he dominates over his peers among his kind, yet humbles himself before the rich who are below them. He is a consumer of their sweets and a destroyer of his religion. So may Allah blind his sight and sever his trace from the legacy of the scholars. And as for the one of understanding and action, you see him possessing melancholy and grief. He stands in prayer during the darkness of the night, and he bows in his cloak. He works and fears, fearful and trembling before everyone except every trusted one among his brethren. So may Allah strengthen his foundations and grant him safety on the Day of Resurrection.

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us from his father, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid al-Anbari. He said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from his father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, from his father Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them). He said: I said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him and his family): Inform me of the number of the Imams after you. So he said: O 'Ali! They are twelve. You are the first of them, and al-Qa'im is the last of them.

The illustrious Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us in the house of Sayyid Abu Muhammad. He said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu Ahmad Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn Isa al-Juludi al-Basri narrated to us in Basra in the year 317 AH. He said: al-Husayn ibn Humayd narrated to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us. He said: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Abaya ibn Rib'i, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic divided creation into two parts and placed me in the better part. That is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, regarding the companions of the right and the companions of the left. I am from the companions of the right, and I am the best of the companions of the right. Then He made the two parts into thirds, and placed me in the best third. That is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "The companions of the right hand - how blessed are the companions of the right hand! The companions of the left hand - how wretched are the companions of the left hand! And the foremost are the foremost" (56:8-10), I am from the foremost, and I am the best of the foremost. Then He made the thirds into tribes, and placed me in the best tribe. That is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "We made you into nations and tribes so that you may know one another. Surely, the noblest of you in the sight of Allah are the most God-fearing of you" (49:13), I am the most God-fearing of the descendants of Adam, and the noblest of them in the sight of Allah, Exalted is His praise - and I do not boast. Then He made the tribes into families, and placed me in the best family. That is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "Allah only desires to keep the uncleanness away from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification" (33:33).

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Ibn Harasa al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Ziyad al-Ahmar narrated to us from Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them), that he recited: "And their father had been a righteous man, so your Lord intended them to reach maturity and extract their treasure" [18:82]. Then Zayd said: Allah protected them because of the righteousness of their father. So who is more deserving of good protection than us?! The Messenger of Allah is our grandfather, his daughter is our mother, the Mistress of his Women is our grandmother, and the first to believe in him and pray with him is our father.

By this chain of narration, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn Hilal al-Ahmasi, he said: Sharik narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, who said: Al-Hajjaj sent for Yahya ibn Ya'mur and said to him: Are you the one who claims that the two sons of Ali are the sons of the Messenger of God? He said: Yes, and I can recite to you from the Quran regarding that. He said: Give it. He said: Grant me protection. He said: Protection is yours. He said: Does not God, Mighty and Majestic, say: "We bestowed upon him Ishaq and Ya'qub, each We guided; and Nuh We guided before, and from his descendants Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, and Harun - and thus We reward the doers of good"? Then he said: "And Zakariyya, Yahya, and 'Isa" - did 'Isa have a father? He said: No. He said: Yet God, Mighty and Majestic, attributed him in the scripture to Ibrahim. He said: What caused you to narrate such a hadith? He said: The covenant God took from the scholars regarding their knowledge - that they should not conceal knowledge they have learned.

4 - Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa b. Imran al-Nakha'i from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from Ali b. Salim from his father from Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Sa'd al-Khaffaf from al-Asbagh b. Nubata from Abdullah b. Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When I was taken up to the seventh heaven, and from it to the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary, and from the Lote Tree to the veils of light, my Lord, exalted be His majesty, called to me: "O Muhammad! You are My servant and I am your Lord. So submit to Me, and worship Me, and rely upon Me, and trust in Me, for indeed I am pleased with you as a servant, a beloved, a messenger, and a prophet, and with your brother Ali as a vicegerent and a gate. He is My Proof over My servants and the Imam of My creation. Through him, My friends are distinguished from My enemies, and through him the Party of Satan is distinguished from My Party. Through him My religion is established, My limits are preserved, and My judgments are carried out. Through you, him, and the Imams from his descendants, I have mercy on My male and female servants. Through the Qa'im from among you, I will fill My Earth with My glorification, My praise, My sanctification, My acclamation, and My exaltation. Through him I will purify the Earth from My enemies and bequeath it to My friends. Through him I will make the word of those who disbelieve in Me the lowest and My word the highest. Through him I will bring life to My servants and My countries with My knowledge. For him I will reveal the treasures and the resources by My will. To him I will reveal the secrets and the consciences by My wish. I will support him with My angels to aid him in carrying out My order and announcing My religion. Truly, he is My friend; verily, he is the guide of My servants."

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who said: I have not heard nor benefited from Hisham ibn al-Hakam during my long companionship with him anything better than this discourse regarding the description of the infallibility of the Imam. For I asked him one day about the Imam: is he infallible? He said: Yes. So I said: What is the description of infallibility in him, and by what is it recognized? He said: Indeed, all sins stem from four aspects, and there is no fifth: greed, jealousy, anger, and lust. These are all negated from him. It is not possible for him to be greedy toward this world while it is under his seal, because he is the treasurer of the Muslims, so for what would he be greedy? It is not possible for him to be jealous, because a person only envies one who is above him, and there is no one above him, so how could he envy one who is below him? It is not possible for him to get angry over any worldly affairs, unless his anger is for God, Mighty and Majestic, for indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory upon him the establishment of the legal limits, and that no blame of a blamer should overtake him regarding God, nor leniency in his religion, until he establishes the limits of God, Mighty and Majestic. And it is not possible for him to follow lusts and prefer this world over the Hereafter, because God, Mighty and Majestic, has made the Hereafter beloved to him just as He has made this world beloved to us. So he looks at the Hereafter as we look at this world. Have you ever seen anyone who abandoned a beautiful face for an ugly face, or delicious food for bitter food, or soft clothing for rough clothing, or an everlasting and enduring blessing for a transient and fleeting world?

1004 / 6 - Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Saydalani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Wasiti narrated to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us. He said: Khalid al-Hadha' informed us, from Abu Qilaba Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Jarmi, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became ill, and his companions were with him, Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with him) went to him and said to him: May my mother and my father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah -- which one of us will give you your funeral bath if this were to happen? He said: That is Ali ibn Abi Talib, for he will have no concern for any part of my body except that the angels will assist him in that. So, he said to him: May my mother and my father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah -- which one of us will pray over you if this were to happen? He said: Cease; may Allah have mercy on you. Then, he said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Ibn Abi Talib! Once you see that my spirit has departed from my body, then bathe me carefully, and shroud me with these two garments of mine, or in white Egyptian cloth and a Yemeni garment, and do not make my shroud extravagant. Then, carry me until you place me at the edge of my grave. The first one who will pray over me is the Almighty, glorified is His majesty, from above His Throne. Then, Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil among angelic soldiers -- none can enumerate them except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then, those that encircle the Throne, then, the inhabitants of heaven after heaven. Then, my Ahl al-Bayt and the women who are nearest -- they should gesture with a nod and give their salaam. Do not harm me with a mournful or despondent voice. Then he said: O Bilal! Gather the people for me. So the people gathered, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out wearing his turban and leaning on his bow, until he climbed the pulpit. He praised Allah and commended Him, then said: O my companions! What kind of a prophet was I to you! Did I not fight alongside you? Did I not have my tooth broken? Did my forehead not get dusty? Did blood not run down on my face until it covered my beard? Did I not suffer hardship and difficulty with the ignorant of my nation? Did I not tie a stone of hung

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Mutayl narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Aban ibn Taghlub. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, four thousand angels descended wanting to fight alongside al-Husayn ibn Ali (blessings of God be upon him), but they were not permitted to fight. So they went back to seek permission, and they descended [again], but al-Husayn (peace be upon him) had already been killed. So they are at his grave, disheveled and dusty, weeping for him until the Day of Resurrection, and their chief is an angel called Mansur (the Victorious).

The great Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani narrated to me, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: No one visits my father (peace be upon him) and is afflicted by hardship from rain, cold, or heat, except that God makes his body forbidden to the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Shami narrated to us. He said: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) - when he saw their ropes and their staffs, how did he sense fear in himself while Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not sense it when he was placed in the catapult and thrown into the fire? So he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when he was placed in the catapult, was relying on the lights of the Proofs of God, Mighty and Majestic, that were in his loins; and Musa (peace be upon him) was not like that. Therefore, he sensed fear in himself while Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abu Hudba. He said: I saw that Anas ibn Malik was bound with a headband, so I asked him about it, and he said: This is [the result of] the supplication of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So I said to him: How did that happen? He said: I was a servant of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He was given a gift of a roasted bird, and he said: O Allah! Bring me the most beloved of Your creation to You and to me to eat from this bird with me. So Ali (peace be upon him) came, and I said to him: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. And I wanted it to be a man from my own people. So the Messenger of Allah raised his hands a second time and said: O Allah! Bring me the most beloved of Your creation to You and to me to eat from this bird with me. So Ali (peace be upon him) came, and I said to him: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. And I wanted it to be a man from my own people. So the Messenger of Allah raised his hands a third time and said: O Allah! Bring me the most beloved of Your creation to You and to me to eat from this bird with me. So Ali (peace be upon him) came, and I said to him: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. And I wanted it to be a man from my own people. So Ali (peace be upon him) raised his voice and said: What keeps the Messenger of Allah away from me? So the Messenger of Allah heard him and said: O Anas! Who is this? I said: Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: Permit him [to enter]. When he entered, he said to him: O Ali! I have supplicated to God the Mighty and Majestic three times asking Him to bring me the most beloved of His creation to Him and to me to eat from this bird with me. Had you not come on the third time, I would have supplicated to God by your name asking Him to bring you to me. So Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah! I came three times. Each time Anas turned me away, saying: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. So the Messenger of Allah said to me: O Anas! What caused you to do this? I said: O Messenger of Allah! I heard the supplication and I wanted it to be a man from my own people. When it was the Day of the Dar, Ali (peace be upon him) asked me to bear witness [to his appointment], but I concealed it and said: I h

My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abu Raja' Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Whoever prefers any of my companions over Ali has disbelieved.

Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hamadani, the servant of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, saying: Al-Mundhir b. Muhammad informed us, saying: Ja'far b. Isma'il al-Bazzaz al-Kufi narrated to me, saying: Abdullah b. al-Fadl narrated to me, from Thabit b. Dinar, from Sa'id b. Jubayr, from Abdullah b. Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: He who denies the Imamate of Ali after me is like him who denied my prophethood during my lifetime; and he who denies my prophethood is like him who denies the lordship of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Isa al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to me from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: O Ali! You are my brother, my inheritor, my deputy, and my vicegerent among my family and my Nation, in my lifetime and after my death. One who loves you loves me, and one who hates you hates me. O Ali! You and I are the two fathers of this Nation. O Ali! I, you, and the Imams from your descendants are masters in this life and kings in the Hereafter. Whoever recognizes us has recognized Allah, and whoever denies us has denied Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakhai narrated to us, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: God, exalted is His majesty, said: "Had all the people gathered upon the wilaya of Ali, I would not have created the Fire."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Karkhi, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: If an enemy of Ali were to come to the Euphrates while it is flowing in abundance, its water overflowing over its two banks, and he took a drink from it and said 'In the name of God,' and when he drank it he said 'Praise be to God,' that would be nothing but carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine.

al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Hamza ibn al-Qasim al-Alawi al-Abbasi narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Zayyat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Turayf narrated to us from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), was asked about the reason for his burying Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), at night. So he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, she was angry with certain people and she disliked their presence at her funeral. And it is forbidden for whoever aligns with them to pray over any of her descendants.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-A'mash, from Abaya ibn Rib'i, from Abdullah ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Gabriel came to me and he was happy and joyful. So I said to him: My beloved Gabriel! Given your happiness, what is the status of my brother and cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib with his Lord? Gabriel said: O Muhammad! By Him who sent you with prophethood and chose you with messengership, I did not descend at this time except for this. O Muhammad, God the Most High, the Most Exalted, conveys His salaam to you and says: Muhammad is the prophet of My mercy, and Ali is the establisher of My proof. I shall not punish one who follows him even if he disobeys Me, nor shall I show mercy to one who opposes him even if he obeys Me. Ibn Abbas said: Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, Gabriel (peace be upon him) will come to me holding the Banner of Praise in his hand. It consists of seventy strips, each of which is wider than the Sun and the Moon. He will give it to me, and I will take it and give it to Ali ibn Abi Talib. A man then said: O Messenger of Allah! How will Ali be able to carry the Banner when you said that it consists of seventy strips, each of which is wider than the Sun and the Moon?! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became angry and said: O man! On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will give Ali strength like that of Gabriel (peace be upon him), beauty like that of Yusuf (peace be upon him), forbearance like that of Ridwan, and a voice resembling that of Dawud (peace be upon him). Had Dawud not been the reciter of Paradise, Ali would have been given a voice like his. Indeed, Ali will be the first to drink from the Salsabil and Zanjabil. And surely Ali and his Shi'a have a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that the former and latter peoples will envy.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Mutayyil al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Nahdi. He said: Thabit ibn Dinar al-Thumali narrated to us from the Master of Worshipers, Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: One day, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) looked toward Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who had come forward while a group of his companions were around him. So he said: Whoever wants to see Yusuf in his beauty, Ibrahim in his generosity, Sulayman in his splendor, and Dawud in his strength, then let him look at this one.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from Abu'l-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Ali is from me, and I am from 'Ali. May God fight whoever fights 'Ali. May God curse whoever opposes 'Ali. 'Ali is the Imam of all creation after me. Whoever approaches 'Ali has approached me, and whoever departs from him has departed from me. Whoever gives preference over him has given preference over me. I am at peace with whoever is at peace with him, and at war with whoever is at war with him. I am the ally of whoever aligns with him, and the enemy of whoever is his enemy.

Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us from Yasir, he said: When al-Rida (peace be upon him) became the crown prince, I heard him while he had raised his hands toward the sky and said: O Allah! Surely You know that I am compelled and under necessity, so do not hold me accountable, just as You did not hold Your servant and prophet Yusuf accountable when he was led into the governance of Egypt.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli informed us. He said: Abu Dhakwan narrated to us. He said: I heard Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas say: I have never seen al-Rida (peace be upon him) asked about anything except that he knew it. I have never seen anyone more knowledgeable than him about what had occurred in time up to his era and age. Al-Ma'mun would test him by asking about everything, and he would answer on it. All his speech, his answers, and his illustrations were with verses from the Quran. He would complete it every three days, and he would say: Had I wanted to complete it in fewer than three days, I would have done so. However, I never pass by a verse without contemplating it — what it was revealed about, and at what time — and for that reason I have come to complete it in three days.

Al-Suli said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Jahm narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Al-Ma'mun ascended the pulpit to inaugurate 'Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him), and he said: O people! The allegiance of 'Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon them) has come to you. By Allah, had these names been recited over the deaf and the mute, they would be cured by Allah's permission.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Suli informed us. He said: Harun ibn Abdullah al-Muhallibi narrated to me. He said: Di`bil ibn Ali al-Khuza`i narrated to us. He said: The news of the death of Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) came to me while I was staying in Qum. So I composed this ra-rhymed ode of mine: I see that [Bani] Umayya are excused if they kill, But I see no excuse for Bani al-Abbas. Sons of Harb, Marwan, and their kin, Bani Mu`ayt — masters of hatred and grudges. You are a people who killed their first for [protecting] Islam, Until when they came to power, they went all the way to disbelief. Head to Tus, to the grave of the pure one there, If you are one who seeks fulfillment through religion. There are two graves in Tus — the best of all people, And the grave of the worst of them — this is a lesson. The impure cannot benefit from nearness to the pure, Nor is the pure harmed by the nearness of the impure. Far be it! Every soul is pledged for what its own hands have earned — So take what you wish, or leave it.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi. He said: While I was standing before Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), he said to me: O Abu al-Salt! Enter this dome in which is the grave of Harun [al-Rashid] and bring me earth from its four sides. He said: I went and brought it. When I presented myself before him, he said: Give me the earth that is near the door. I gave it to him; he took it, smelled it, then threw it. Then he said: A grave will be dug for me here, and a rock will appear; even if every pickaxe in Khurasan were gathered against it, it would not be possible to uproot it. a rock [will appear — and] even if every pickaxe in Khurasan were gathered against it, it would not be possible to uproot it. Then he said: What is at the foot and what is at the head [of the grave site] is likewise. Then he said: Give me this dust, for it is from my burial ground. Then he said: A grave will be dug for me in this place, so order them to dig seven steps downward and to carve a tomb-niche for me. If they refuse and offer only a lateral grave, then order them to make the lateral niche two arm-lengths and a handspan, for God, Mighty and Majestic, will expand it for me as He wills. When they do that, you will see moisture near my head. Speak the words I will teach you, and the water will spring forth until the niche is filled. You will see small fish therein, so crumble [bread] the bread I will give you, and they will pick it up. When none of it remains, a large fish will emerge from it and devour the small fish until none of them remain. Then it will disappear. When it disappears, place your hand upon the water, and speak the words I will teach you, and it will recede until nothing remains. Do not do this except in the presence of al-Ma'mun. Then he (peace be upon him) said: O Abu al-Salt! Tomorrow I will enter upon this transgressor. If I come out with my head uncovered, then speak to me and I will speak to you. If I come out with my head covered, do not speak to me. Abu al-Salt said: When we woke the following morning, he put on his clothes and sat in his prayer niche waiting. While he was thus, the servant of al-Ma'mun entered and said to him: Answer the Commander of the Faithful. So he put on his sandals and his

The insigne Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn 'Adhafir, from his father. He said: I said to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him): Why did God prohibit carrion, blood, pork, and wine? He said: Indeed, God—Blessed and Exalted—did not prohibit these things for His servants, nor did He permit everything else for them, out of desire for what He permitted or asceticism toward what He prohibited. Rather, He—Mighty and Majestic—created creation and knew what would sustain their bodies and what would be beneficial for them, so He permitted that and made it lawful for them; and He knew what would harm them, so He forbade it from them. Then He permitted it for one in dire necessity, at the time when their body cannot be sustained except by it—so He permitted it only to the degree of subsistence and no more than that. Then he (peace be upon him) said: As for carrion, none who consume it do so without their body weakening, their strength diminishing, and their lineage being cut off; and the consumer of carrion does not die except suddenly. As for blood, its consumption causes yellow dropsy, rabies-like madness, hardening of the heart, and diminishing of compassion and mercy—so one's intimate companion will not be safe from them, nor will anyone who accompanies them. As for pork, God—Blessed and Exalted—transformed a people into various forms like the pig, the monkey, and the bear, then He prohibited consuming such transformed beings lest one benefit from them or take their punishment lightly. As for wine, He prohibited it due to its effect and its corruption. Then he (peace be upon him) said: The wine addict is like an idol-worshiper; it causes trembling, it destroys one's manly virtue, and it compels one to dare commit forbidden acts—from the shedding of blood to committing fornication—to the point where, when drunk, one is not to be trusted not to assault his own household while having no comprehension of what he is doing. And wine does not increase its drinker in anything but every

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated to us from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i al-Qadi. He said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: Iblis came to Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him) while he was communing with his Lord. An angel from the angels said to him: What do you hope to gain from him while he is in this state, communing with his Lord? He said: I hope to gain from him what I hoped to gain from his father Adam when he was in Paradise. Among what Allah the Exalted communicated to him was that He said to him: O Musa! I do not accept prayer except from one who humbles himself before My greatness, attaches his heart to the fear of Me, spends his day in My remembrance, does not sleep while persisting in sin, and recognizes the right of My friends and My beloved ones. Musa said: O Lord! By Your beloved ones and Your friends, do You mean Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub? He (Mighty and Majestic) said: They are that, O Musa, but I was referring to the one for whose sake I created Adam and Hawwa', and for whose sake I created Paradise and the Fire. Musa said: And who is he, O Lord? He said: Muhammad, Ahmad — I derived his name from My name, for I am the Praised (al-Mahmud). Musa said: O Lord! Make me of his nation. He said: You, O Musa, are of his nation if you recognize him and recognize his station and the station of his Ahl al-Bayt. Verily, his likeness and the likeness of his Ahl al-Bayt... Verily, his likeness and the likeness of his Ahl al-Bayt among those I have created is like the likeness of al-Firdaws in the gardens — its leaves do not dry up and its taste does not change. Whoever recognizes them and recognizes their right, I shall grant him forbearance in moments of ignorance and a light in moments of darkness. I will answer him before he calls out to Me, and I will give to him before he asks Me. O Musa, when you see poverty approaching, say: Welcome, O emblem of the righteous! And when you see wealth approaching, say: This is a sin whose punishment has been hastened. Indeed, this world is the abode of punishment — in it I punished Adam for his sin. I have made it cursed, and cursed is whatever is in it, except what is devoted to Me. O Musa, My righteous serva
