And it is possible that the manner of it is the relating of what some of the ʿAmmah narrate from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, as though he عليه السلام said: they narrate from ʿAlī عليه السلام that he did not perform salat over them, and that is contrary to the truth, as we have explained.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: When the funeral prayer becomes due at the time of an obligatory prayer, which of the two should I begin with? He said: Hasten the deceased to his grave, unless you fear that the time of the obligatory prayer will pass. And do not delay the prayer over the جنازة until sunrise or sunset.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one narrator, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام: “Does anything among these hours prevent you from performing salat over funerals?” He said: “No.”

Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: One may perform prayer over the جنازة at any hour, for it is not a prayer involving ruku' or sujud. Rather, only the prayer in which there is khushu', ruku', and sujud is considered disliked at sunrise and at sunset, because it sets between the two horns of Satan and rises between the two horns of a Satan.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in performing prayer over funerals when the sun sets and when it rises; it is only seeking forgiveness.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Salat over جنازة is disliked when the sun turns yellow and when it rises. So this report is explicit in indicating dislike rather than prohibition, and it is possible that its basis is taqiyyah, because that is the position of the generality.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: When you perform the funeral prayer over a woman, then stand at her head; and when you perform the funeral prayer over a man, then stand at his chest.

As for what ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Whoever performs the funeral prayer over a woman should not stand at her middle; rather, he should be at the area near her chest. And when he performs the prayer over a man, then he should stand at his middle. So this does not conflict with the first report, because the meaning of his saying, 'at the area near her chest,' is when he is close to the head. It may be expressed as being near the chest due to its closeness to it, and that is also further confirmed.

What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would stand in line with the navel of a man, and for women lower than that, toward the chest.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him how one performs the prayer over men and women, and he said: The man is placed nearest to where the men are, and the women are behind the men.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: When salat (prayer) was performed over the woman and the man, the woman was placed forward and the man was placed behind. And when salat (prayer) was performed over the slave and the free person, the slave was placed forward and the free person was placed behind. And when salat (prayer) was performed over the elder and the child, the child was placed forward and the elder was placed behind.

Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about the men and the women: how is the prayer to be performed over them? He said: The men are placed in front of the women, in the area nearest to the Imam, arranged in a row one after another.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from Zurārah and al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Concerning a man and a woman, how the salat is performed over them, he said: the woman is placed behind the man, and the man is to be in the position nearest to the Imam.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: The funerals of men and boys. So he said: The women are placed nearest to the qiblah, and the boys behind them, and the men behind that, and the Imam stands on the side nearest to the men.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ṣalt, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked him about a man and a woman over whom the salat is performed. He said: the man is placed in front of the woman, on the side toward the qiblah, so that the head of the woman is near the hip of the man on the side of his left; and her head also is on the side of the Imam’s left, while the head of the man is on the side of the Imam’s right.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one person, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the funerals of men and women when they are gathered together. He said: The men are placed first, according to the Book of 'Ali عليه السلام.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning: A man prays over two deceased persons or three dead persons—how should he pray over them? He said: If they are three, or two, or ten, or more than that, then let him perform one salat over them, saying five takbirs over them, just as he prays over one deceased person. Whoever prays over them all together should place one deceased person, then place the other next to the buttocks of the first, then place the head of the third next to the buttocks of the second, in a stair-like arrangement, until he has arranged all of them, whatever their number may be. When he has arranged them like that, he stands in the middle and pronounces five takbirs, doing as he does when he prays over one deceased person. He was asked: What if the dead are men and women? He said: He begins with the men, placing the head of the second next to the buttocks of the first, until he has finished arranging all the men. Then he places the head of the woman next to the buttocks of the last man, then places the head of the other woman next to the buttocks of the first woman, until he has arranged all of them. When they have been arranged in this way, he stands in the middle, in the midst of the men, and pronounces takbir over them as he prays over one deceased person. Thus, the proper way regarding these reports is to regard the matter as one of choice, because acting upon whichever of them it may be is permissible; this indicates that.

What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no objection to the man being placed forward and the woman placed behind, and to the man being placed behind and the woman placed forward—meaning in the salat (prayer) over the deceased.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning a man from whom vermin fall while he is in the salat (prayer). He said: He continues in his salat, and that does not invalidate his wudu (ablution).

From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ẓarīf — meaning Ibn Nāṣiḥ — from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no wudu (ablution) required because of pumpkin seeds and small worms; they are only like lice.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Akhī Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He said regarding a man from whom something like a pumpkin seed comes out: wudu (ablution) is upon him. So the proper way concerning it is that we interpret it to mean when it is smeared with feces and is not clean; and that which indicates this distinction is what follows.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who is in his salat (prayer), and a pumpkin seed comes out of him—what should he do? He said: If it came out clean from feces, then nothing is upon him, and it has not invalidated his wudu (ablution). But if it came out smeared with feces, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution); and if he is in his salat (prayer), he should break the salat (prayer), and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer).
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام: Is salat over the deceased performed in the masjid? He said: Yes.
Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام. The like of that.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from Abī Bakr ibn ʿĪsā ibn Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, who said: I was in the mosque when a جنازة (funeral bier) was brought, and I wanted to perform prayer over it. Then Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام came, placed his elbow on my chest, and kept pushing me until he brought me out of the mosque. Then he said: “O Abā Bakr, funeral prayers are not performed over the dead in the mosque.” So the correct understanding of this report is that it indicates a degree of reprehensibility, not prohibition.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The takbir over the deceased is five takbirs.
From him, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم pronounced five takbirs.
The takbir over the deceased is five takbirs. Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ṣalt, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Bukayr, from Qudāmah ibn Zāʾidah, who said: I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed the prayer over his son Ibrāhīm and pronounced five takbirs.
ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Wallad, who said: I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the takbir over the deceased, and he said: five.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Kulayb al-Asadi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the takbir over the deceased, and he indicated with his hand: five.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr al-Khazzāz, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the takbīr over funerals: is there in it anything fixed? He said: No. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم pronounced takbīr eleven, nine, seven, five, six, and four times. As for what this report contains of increasing the takbīr beyond five times, it is abandoned by consensus. It is possible that he عليه السلام was reporting the act of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in that regard, because he would pronounce takbīr over one funeral or two, then another funeral would be brought, and he would begin from where he had ended, making five takbīrs; so when that is added to what he had already pronounced, it exceeds five takbīrs. That is permissible, as we have explained in our major book. As for what it contains of four takbīrs, it is to be understood as a state of taqiyyah, because it is the doctrine of all those who opposed the Imāmiyyah; or it may be a report about the action of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم with the hypocrites or those suspected regarding Islam, for he عليه السلام used to act in that way. This indicates that.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would pronounce five takbirs over some people and four over others; and when he pronounced four takbirs over a man, he was regarded with suspicion.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī, from Ismāʿīl ibn Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed salat over a جنازة, and pronounced five takbirs over him; and he performed salat over another, and pronounced four takbirs over him. As for the one over whom he pronounced five takbirs, he praised Allah and glorified Him in the first takbir, and in the second he made du'a for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and in the third he made du'a for the believing men and believing women, and in the fourth he made du'a for the deceased, and he concluded at the fifth. And as for the one over whom he pronounced four takbirs, he praised Allah and glorified Him in the first takbir, and in the second he made du'a for himself and the people of his household, and in the third he made du'a for the believing men and believing women, and he concluded at the fourth, and he did not make du'a for him because he was a hypocrite.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, who said: I said to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, we relate in Iraq that ʿAlī عليه السلام performed salat over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, and said six takbirs over him; then he turned to those who were behind him and said: He had been one of those at Badr. He said: Then Jaʿfar said: It was not like that. Rather, he performed salat over him with five takbirs, then he lifted him and walked with him for a while, then placed him down and said five takbirs over him. He did that five times, until he had said twenty-five takbirs over him. And it is possible that by his saying four he meant to report what is said between the takbirs of du'a, because after the fifth takbir there is no du'a; rather, by it one departs from the جنازة. This indicates that.

What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Kūfī, whose لقب was Ḥamdān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I was sitting in the presence of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a man entered and asked him about the takbīr over funerals. He said: Five takbīrs. Then another entered and asked him about the salat over funerals, so he said to him: Four prayers. The first said: May I be made your ransom, I asked you and you said five, and this one asked you and you said four. So he said: You asked me about the takbīr, while this one asked me about the salat. Then he said: It is five takbīrs, between them are four prayers. Then he spread his palm and said: They are five takbīrs, between them are four prayers. And we have fully covered what pertains to this chapter in our major book.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, Zurarah, Ma'mar ibn Yahya, and Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: There is no recitation in the salat (prayer) over the deceased, nor any fixed supplication. You may supplicate with whatever occurs to you, and the most deserving of the dead to be supplicated for is the believer, and one should begin with salat upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from his paternal uncle Ḥamzah ibn Bazīʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Suwayd, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, concerning... Regarding what is known, he said about salat over funerals: He said: In the first, you recite Umm al-Kitāb; in the second, you invoke blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family; in the third, you supplicate for the believing men and the believing women; in the fourth, you supplicate for your deceased; and with the fifth, you depart.

And as for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qummī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn al-Qaddāḥ, from Jaʿfar, from his father: that ʿAlī عليه السلام, when salat was performed over a deceased person, would recite Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family—the rest of the hadith. So the interpretation regarding these two reports is taqiyyah, because they are in agreement with the doctrines of some of the ʿĀmmah.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: There is no taslim in the salat over the deceased.

From him, from ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī and Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليهما السلام, who said: There is no taslim in the prayer over the deceased.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the prayer over the deceased. He said: As for the believer, then it is five takbirs; and as for the hypocrite, then it is four; and there is no salam in it.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about the salat over the deceased. He said: Five takbirs; then when you have finished them, you give salām to your right. So the interpretation of this narration is taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrines of the generality.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Salt al-Ahwazi informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqdah informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Khalid, the mawla of Banu al-Sayda', narrated to us. That he prayed behind Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام over a جنازة, and he saw him raising his hands at every takbir.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAzramī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I prayed behind Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام over a جنازة, and he said the takbir five times, raising his hands with each takbir.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, who said: I asked al-Rida عليه السلام. I said: May I be your ransom, the people raise their hands in the takbir over the deceased in the first takbir, and they do not raise them after that. So should I limit myself to the first takbir as they do, or should I raise my hands in every takbir? He said: Raise your hand in every takbir.

Isma'il ibn Ishaq ibn Aban al-Warraq narrated to me, from Ja'far, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام would raise his hands in the first takbir over the funeral, then he would not do so again until he departed.

Sa'd, from Abū Ja'far, from his father, from 'Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū 'Abd Allāh, from his father, from 'Alī عليه السلام. That he would not raise his hands in the جنازة except once, meaning in the takbīr. So the proper understanding regarding these two narrations is a mode of permissibility and the lifting of obligation, even though what is more excellent is what the earlier narrations contained. And it is possible that they were issued in the context of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of many among the العامة.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi and Zurarah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he was asked about prayer for the child: when is prayer to be performed upon him? He said: When he understands salat (prayer). I said: And when does salat (prayer) become obligatory upon him? He said: When he is a son of six years, and sawm (fasting) is when he is capable of it.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Zurārah, who said: I saw a son of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام during the lifetime of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام; he was called ʿAbdullāh, a weaned child who had begun to walk. So I said to him, “O boy, who is this beside you?” referring to a mawlā of theirs. He said, “This is my mawlā.” The mawlā said to him jokingly, “I am not your mawlā.” He replied, “That is evil for you.” Then a stab was made during the boy’s funeral, and he died. So he was taken out in a basket to al-Baqīʿ. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام came out wearing a yellow khazz cloak, a yellow khazz turban, and a yellow khazz mantle. He went walking to al-Baqīʿ while leaning on me, and the people were offering him condolences for the son of his son. When he reached al-Baqīʿ, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام stepped forward and performed the salat over him, pronouncing four takbirs over him. Then he ordered that he be buried, and so he was buried. Then he took my hands and moved aside with me, then said: “He would not perform salat over children. Rather, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to order concerning them, and they would be buried one after another behind [the others], and salat would not be performed over them. I only performed salat over him for the sake of the people of al-Madīnah, lest they say: ‘They do not perform salat over their children.’”

As for what Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: One does not perform salat over the newborn, and he is the child who did not cry out, did not give a sound, and is not inherited from in the blood-money nor from anything else. But if he cried out, then perform salat over him and give him inheritance. So the proper way to understand this narration is that it indicates a kind of recommendation, according to what we mentioned earlier, or dissimulation (taqiyyah), in accordance with what the first report contained; and this confirms what we have said.

What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about the newborn, so long as the pen has not begun to run upon him, whether prayer is performed over him. He said: No; rather, the prayer is only upon the man and the woman when the pen has begun to run upon them.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated, from a man, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said: I said: At what age of years is salat (prayer) performed over the child? He عليه السلام said: Salat (prayer) is performed over him in every case, unless he is miscarried before completion.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: At what age in years and months is the funeral prayer performed for a child? He said: The prayer is performed over him in every case, unless he miscarries before completion. Thus, the way to understand these two reports is what we stated regarding the report of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān: that they are to be understood as taqiyyah, or as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation and requirement.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who catches one takbir of the prayer over the deceased. He said: He completes what remains.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Khalaf ibn Ziyad al-Qalanisi, from a man, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying regarding a man who catches with the Imam in the funeral prayer one takbirah or two takbirahs: he said, he completes the takbir while walking with it. فإذا لم يدرك التكبير he says the takbir at the grave. And if he reaches them after it has already been buried, he says the takbir over the grave.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the salat over the جنازة when a man has missed from it one takbir, or two, or three. He said: He pronounces the takbirs that he missed.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn ʿAmmar, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, from his father, that ʿAli عليه السلام used to say: What has preceded of the takbirs of the funeral prayer is not made up. So the correct understanding of this narration is that it is not made up in the manner it would originally be begun, with separation between them by supplication; rather, it is only made up consecutively. This indicates that.

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man catches one takbirah or two takbirahs in the salat (prayer) over the deceased, then let him make up what remains consecutively.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: There is no objection to a man offering salat over the deceased after he has been buried.

From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Mālik, the mawlā of al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If the salat over the deceased has passed you by until he is buried, then there is no harm in praying over him after he has been buried.

From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yūsuf, from Muʿādh ibn Thābit al-Jawharī, from ʿAmr ibn Jumayʿ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When salat over the deceased had passed him by, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform salat over the قبر.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ziyād ibn Marwān, from Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade that one should perform salat (prayer) upon a grave, or sit upon it, or lean upon it, or build upon it.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a deceased person over whom salat had been performed; then when the Imam gave salām, the deceased was found to be reversed, with his feet toward the place of his head. He said: He is to be straightened, and the salat is to be repeated over him, even if he has already been carried away, so long as he has not been buried. But if he has been buried, then the salat over him has passed, and no salat is performed over him while he is buried.

From him, from al-Sayyārī, from Muḥammad ibn Aslam, from a man from the people of al-Jazīrah, who said: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “Should one perform salat over the buried person after he has been buried?” He said: “No. If it were permissible for anyone, it would have been permissible for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Rather, salat is not performed over the buried person after he has been buried, nor over the naked person.” So the proper way regarding these reports is one of two possibilities. One of them is what our Shaykh used to hold, and that is that salat over the grave is only permissible for a day and a night, no more than that. Thus, whatever has been reported concerning the permissibility of salat over him after burial, he interpreted as referring to that day; and whatever has been reported that it is not permissible, he interpreted as referring to what is after that day. And the second possibility is that what is meant by the permissibility of salat over the buried person is supplication for him, apart from the prescribed salat; and that indicates this.

What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Saʿd, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿĪsā, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام arrived in Makkah and asked me about ʿAbdullāh ibn Aʿyan. I said, “He has died.” He said, “He has died? Do you know the location of his grave?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Then come with us to his grave so that we may pray over him.” I said, “Yes.” He said, “No, rather we shall pray over him here.” Then he raised his hands in supplication, strove earnestly in the supplication, and asked Allah to have mercy on him.

Al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim or Zurarah, who said: Salat (prayer) over the deceased after he is buried is only du'a (supplication). He said: Then al-Najashi—the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not perform salat (prayer) over him? He said: No, he only supplicated for him. And it is possible that the basis in the reports which include the permissibility of salat (prayer) over the grave is when it has not yet been covered with soil; then once it has been covered with soil, that is not permitted. This indicates that.

What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The deceased is prayed over so long as he has not been covered with earth, even if salat (prayer) has already been performed over him.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a جنازة that I did not catch until it had reached the grave: should I perform salat over it? He said: If you reach it before it is buried, then if you wish, perform salat over it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام pronounced five takbirs over Sahl ibn Hunayf, and he had been among the people of Badr. Then he walked for a while, then set him down and pronounced another five takbirs over him. He continued doing that until he had pronounced twenty-five takbirs over him.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: Tell me, if one takbīrah or more escapes me, what do you think? He said: You make up what you missed. I said: Should I face the qiblah? He said: Yes, while you are following the جنازة. For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came to the funeral of a woman from Banū al-Najjār and performed salat over her. Then he found that the grave-pit had not yet been prepared for them, so they placed the جنازة down, and no group came except that he said to them: Perform salat over her.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb ibn Fayhas al-Bajalī, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed salat over a جنازة, and when he had finished, a group came and said, “We missed the salat over it.” So he said: Indeed, the جنازة is not to have salat performed over it twice. Make du'a for him and speak خير. So the correct view regarding this narration is that it indicates a type of karāhah. And it is possible that his statement عليه السلام, “Indeed, the جنازة is not to have salat performed over it twice,” means in respect of obligation, even though it may be permissible to perform salat over it twice by way of recommendation and istihbāb. What is obligatory is only once, and whatever is added beyond that is mustaḥabb, recommended toward.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام: that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed salat over a جنازة, and when he had finished, some people came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, we did not catch the salat over it.” So he said: Salat is not performed over a جنازة twice; rather, supplicate for him. Thus, the appropriate understanding of this narration as well is the same as what we have already mentioned regarding the first report.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, and Sindī ibn Muḥammad, and Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, all from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Yazīd ibn Khalīfah, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام when a man from the people of Qum asked him and said: O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, do women perform salat over the جنازة? So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was, in the matter in which he declared the blood of al-Mughīrah ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ to be without protection—and he narrated a long hadith—and Zaynab, the daughter of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, passed away, and Fāṭimah عليها السلام came out among her womenfolk and performed salat over her sister.

From him, from al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Abū al-Mi‘zā, from Samā‘ah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: It is not appropriate for a young woman to go out to the funeral in order to perform salat over it, unless she is a woman who has entered into old age.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father عليه السلام, who said: There is no salat over a جنازة when a woman is with it. Thus, the sound interpretation of this narration is that it indicates a degree of dislike, not prohibition.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abū Usāmah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about vomiting: does it invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: No.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Kūfī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ghālib ibn ʿUthmān, from Rūḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about vomiting. He said: “There is no wudu (ablution) because of it, even if he vomits deliberately.”

And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no wudu (ablution) due to vomiting.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about what invalidates wudu (ablution). He said: An occurrence of passing wind whose sound you hear or whose smell you detect; and rumbling in the belly, unless it is something you can restrain; and laughter during salat (prayer); and vomiting.

And among what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Nosebleeding, vomiting, and using the toothpick such that it causes blood to flow—if you find something repugnant, it invalidates wudu (ablution); but if you do not find it repugnant, it does not invalidate wudu (ablution). So these two reports bear two possible meanings: one of them is that they were issued in the context of taqiyyah, because that is the view of some of the ʿāmmah; and the second is that they are to be understood as indicating a kind of recommendation, so that the reports do not contradict one another.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: If a woman dies, who among the people has the greatest right to perform the salat (prayer) over her? He عليه السلام said: Her husband. I said: Is the husband more entitled concerning her than the father, the child, and the brother? He said: Yes, and he washes her.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh, from Muḥassin ibn Aḥmad, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the prayer over a woman: is the husband more entitled to her, or the brother? He said: the brother.

Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: A woman dies while her brother and her husband are with her; which of the two is more entitled to perform the salat over her? He said: Her brother is more entitled to perform the salat over her. Thus, the interpretation of these two reports is that they are a kind of taqiyyah, because they conform to the doctrines of the ʿāmmah. The first part of the Book of al-Istibṣār fīmā ukhtulifa mina al-akhbār is completed, and in the second part it is followed by the Book of Zakat, by the praise of Allah, His favor, and His excellent granting of success; and blessings be upon the master of the messengers, Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and his good and pure ʿItrah.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about nosebleeding, cupping, and every flowing blood, and he said: There is no wudu (ablution) in this. Wudu (ablution) is only from your two ends with which Allah has blessed you.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: If I were to have a nosebleed enough to fill a vessel, I would do no more than wipe the blood from myself and perform salat (prayer).

And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Maḥmūd, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about vomiting, nosebleeding, and pus: do they invalidate wudu (ablution) or not? He said: They do not invalidate anything. As for what Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated in the report that we mentioned in the chapter before this, from his statement: If the blood is forced out, it invalidates, and if it is not forced out, it does not invalidate.

And among what Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr narrated from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man afflicted by flowing blood. He said: He performs wudu (ablution) and repeats. He said: And if it is not flowing, he performs wudu (ablution) and continues from where he left off. He said: And he does that between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Bint Ilyās, who said: I heard him saying: I saw my father, عليه السلام, when he had a nosebleed after he had performed wudu (ablution), with flowing blood, so he performed wudu (ablution). So it may bear several possibilities: one of them is that it be interpreted as a case of taqiyyah, according to what we have previously stated regarding it; the second is that we interpret it as recommendation rather than obligation; and the third is that we interpret it as washing the affected place, because that is also called wudu (ablution), as we have explained in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām. And what indicates this meaning is that which...

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Abū Ḥabīb al-Asadī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying about a man who gets a nosebleed while he is in a state of wudu (ablution): He washes away the traces of the blood and performs salat (prayer).

And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I heard him saying: If a man vomits while he is in a state of taharah, then let him rinse his mouth; and if he has a nosebleed while he is in a state of wudu (ablution), then let him wash his nose, for that suffices him, and he does not repeat his wudu (ablution).

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who passes by water in which there is a dead animal that has become putrid. He said: If the foul odor is predominant over the water, then he should not perform wudu (ablution) from it, nor drink from it.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Whenever the water overcomes the smell of the carcass, then perform wudu (ablution) from it and drink. But when the water changes and the taste changes, then do not perform wudu (ablution) from it and do not drink.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Regarding stale water: you may perform wudu (ablution) from it unless you find other water besides it. This does not contradict the first two reports, because the correct understanding in this report is when the water has changed by itself or by being adjacent to a pure object, for the prohibited use is only when it has changed due to impurity affecting it. According to this understanding, there is no contradiction between the reports.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Salim Abi al-Fadl, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Nothing invalidates wudu (ablution) except what comes out from your two lower outlets with which Allah has bestowed favor upon you.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said: I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about the fistula, and he said: Only three things invalidate wudu (ablution): urine, feces, and wind.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about what invalidates wudu (ablution). He said: minor ritual occurrence—when you hear its sound or find its smell—and rumbling in the stomach, unless it is something you can hold back, and laughing in salat (prayer), and vomiting. So the correct way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a type of recommendation, or upon the laughter in which one does not control himself and is not secure from having invalidated himself; and that which indicates this is:

What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from a group who heard him saying. Indeed, smiling during salat (prayer) does not invalidate the salat (prayer), nor does it invalidate the wudu (ablution). Rather, it is only laughter containing loud guffawing that cuts off the salat (prayer). His statement, peace be upon him (AS), 'Rather, it is only laughter containing loud guffawing that cuts off,' refers back to the salat (prayer) and not to the wudu (ablution). Do you not see that he said, 'laughter containing loud guffawing cuts off,' and 'cutting off' is only said regarding salat (prayer), because it is not customary for one to say, 'the wudu (ablution) was cut off'; rather, it is said, 'the salat (prayer) was cut off.' And it is possible that the two reports were issued in the context of taqiyyah, because they accord with the doctrines of some of the ʿāmmah.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about reciting poetry: does it invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: No.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about reciting poetry: does it invalidate wudu (ablution), or a man wronging his companion, or lying? He said: Yes, except if it is poetry in which he speaks truthfully, or it is a small amount of poetry, three or four verses. But as for one who does much false poetry, then it invalidates wudu (ablution). So the report may bear two possibilities: one of them is that a scribal corruption occurred to the narrator, such that it was narrated with the letter ṣād without a dot rather than ḍād with a dot, because that is among the things that diminish the reward of wudu (ablution). The second is that it is to be understood as recommended.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj and Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: There is no wudu (ablution) in kissing, nor in direct bodily contact, nor in touching the private part.

With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī Maryam, who said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who performs wudu (ablution), then calls his bondwoman and she takes him by the hand until he reaches the mosque? For indeed, some people among us claim that this is the touching referred to as al-mulāmasah. So he said: No, by Allah, there is no harm in that, and I have perhaps done that myself, and what is meant by this is not that. “Or you touched women.” It only means sexual intercourse in the private part.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about kissing: does it invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: There is no harm in it.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a man kisses a woman with desire, or touches her private part, he repeats the wudu (ablution). The proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as indicating a form of recommendation, or as meaning that he washes his hand, and that is called wudu, as has been stated earlier. That which indicates this interpretation is...

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who touched his wife's private part. He said: There is nothing upon him; and if he wishes, he may wash his hand. And because of a kiss, wudu (ablution) is not required.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who fiddles with his private part during the obligatory salat (prayer), and he said: There is no harm in it.

From him, from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about a man who touches his penis, or his private part, or lower than that, while he is standing performing salat (prayer): should he repeat his wudu (ablution)? He said: There is no harm in that; it is only a part of his body.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who performs wudu (ablution) and then touches the inner part of his anus. He said: his wudu (ablution) is invalidated. And if he touches the inside of his urethral opening, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution). And if he is in salat (prayer), he should break the salat (prayer), perform wudu (ablution), and repeat the salat (prayer). And if he opens his urethral opening, he repeats the wudu (ablution) and repeats the salat (prayer). So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it to mean that if he encounters some najasah (ritual impurity) there, then repeating the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him at that time. But whenever he does not encounter any such thing, then nothing is upon him, according to what we have stated previously.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Isa ibn 'Umar, the client of the Ansar, that he asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man: is it lawful for him to shake hands with a Magian? He said: No. Then he asked him: should he perform wudu (ablution) if he shakes hands with them? He said: Yes, indeed shaking hands with them invalidates wudu (ablution). Shaykh Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The correct approach regarding this report is that we interpret it as referring to washing the hand, because that is also called wudu (ablution), as we have explained. That is only required because they are impure. We only said that because of the consensus of the sect that this does not necessitate the invalidation of wudu (ablution). Also, we have already presented the reports which contain that nothing invalidates wudu (ablution) except what exits from the two passages or sleep; and they are to be carried upon their generality, and it is not permissible to specify them on account of this anomalous report.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever touches a dog, let him perform wudu (ablution). The discussion concerning this report is like the discussion concerning the first report: that it is to be understood as referring to washing the hand, due to the consensus that we mentioned and the reports that we presented before; and furthermore...

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a dog touching something from a man's body. He said: He should wash the place that it touched.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Indeed, Shaytan blows into the anus of the human being until it is made to seem to him that wind has come out from him; so his wudu (ablution) is not invalidated except by wind that he hears or whose smell he perceives.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about what invalidates wudu (ablution). He said: Hadath—when you hear its sound or find its smell—and rumbling in the belly, except for something you can restrain, or laughing during salat (prayer), and vomiting. We have already spoken about this report previously, and we said that the proper way concerning it is to interpret it as referring to a condition in which a person has no control over himself, so that he knows what occurs from him; and it is also possible to understand it as indicating recommendation.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from 'Umar ibn Hanzalah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about al-madhy, and he said: In my view, it is nothing but like phlegm.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān together, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about madhy, and he said: Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام was a man who experienced much madhy, so he felt shy to ask the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم because of the position of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. So he instructed al-Miqdād to ask him while he was sitting, and he asked him. Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him: It is not anything.

With this chain of transmission, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: Does madhy invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: No, and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it; rather, it is like saliva and mucus.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Aban, from 'Anbasah, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام say: 'Ali عليه السلام did not consider there to be any wudu (ablution) due to madhy, nor washing of what of it touched the garment, except in the case of the greater fluid.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, he said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about madhy, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution) because of it. Then I repeated the question to him in another year, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution), and he said: Indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام instructed al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad to ask the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he was shy to ask him, so he said: Regarding it, there is wudu (ablution). So this report does not conflict with what we have previously presented of the reports, because it is a solitary report. It also contains, in the account of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and his instructing al-Miqdād to ask the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the Prophet’s reply to him, something that conflicts with what is well known in this account, namely that which is contained in the narration of Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār: that when he asked him, he said to him, “It is nothing.” It is also possible that the narrator omitted part of the report, because Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, the narrator of this report, narrated this very account itself, for he said: “He instructed me to repeat the wudu (ablution).” I said to him, “Then if I do not perform wudu (ablution)?” He said, “There is no harm.”

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated that from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about madhy, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution) because of it. Then I repeated the question to him another year, and he instructed me to perform wudu (ablution) because of it. And he said: Indeed, 'Ali عليه السلام instructed al-Miqdad to ask the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, but he felt shy to ask him, so he said: concerning it, there is wudu (ablution). I said: And if I do not perform wudu (ablution)? He said: There is no harm. So this report came clarified and explained, indicating that the command to perform wudu (ablution) because of it was only for a kind of recommendation, not obligation. And it is possible that the recommendation in repeating wudu (ablution) due to madhy is directed only toward one from whom madhy exits with desire; that is indicated by this.

What Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abū Saʿīd al-Mukārī, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Madhy comes out from a man.” He said: “Shall I set for you a criterion regarding it?” He said: I said: “Yes, may I be made your ransom.” He said: “If it comes out from you with desire, then perform wudu (ablution); and if it comes out from you in other than that manner, then there is no wudu (ablution) upon you because of it.”

Al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about madhy: does it invalidate wudu (ablution)? He said: If it is from desire, it invalidates.

Al-Saffar narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Hukaym, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from al-Kahili, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about madhy, and he said: Whatever of it is accompanied by desire, then perform wudu (ablution). And that which indicates that these reports are to be understood as recommendation is that...

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no wudu (ablution) due to madhy from desire, nor from arousal, nor from kissing, nor from touching the private part, nor from lying together; and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it.

With this chain of transmission, from al-Ṣaffār, from al-Haytham ibn Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ṭāṭarī, from Ibn Ribāṭ, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There come out from the urethra al-manī, al-madhy, al-wady, and al-wadhy. As for al-manī, it is that for which the bones become relaxed and the body becomes languid from it, and in it there is ghusl. As for al-madhy, it comes out from desire and there is nothing due in it. As for al-wady, it is that which comes out after urination. And as for al-wadhy, it is that which comes out from illnesses, so there is nothing due in it.

As for what al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: Three things come out from the urethra: manī, and in it there is ghusl; and wady, from which there is wudu, because it comes from the dribbling of urine. He said: and madhy, there is no wudu in it; rather, it is like what comes out from the nose. His statement عليه السلام, 'and wady, from which there is wudu,' is to be understood as meaning that if he had not performed istibrāʾ from urine as we mentioned, and then something came out from him after that, repeating wudu becomes obligatory upon him, because it would be from the remainder of urine. He alerted to that by his statement, 'because it comes from the dribbling of urine,' indicating that this is either urine or mixed with urine. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned...

What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a man who urinates, then performs istinja', then afterward finds moisture, he said: If, after urinating, he draws his hand from between the anus and the testicles three times, and presses what is between them, then performs istinja', then if something flows out until it reaches the shanks, he should not be concerned. And that further clarifies it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Al-wadhy does not invalidate wudu (ablution); it is only like nasal mucus and spittle.

From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, who said: Zayd al-Shahham, Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to me from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said: If something of madhy or wadhy flows from your private part, then do not wash it, do not break the salat (prayer) for it, and do not invalidate the wudu (ablution) because of it. It is only in the position of phlegm. Everything that comes out of you after the wudu (ablution), then it is from the residual passages.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, he said: Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin narrated to me, saying: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who emits madhy while he is in salat, whether from desire or from other than desire. He عليه السلام said: From madhy there is wudu (ablution). His statement عليه السلام, 'From madhy there is wudu,' may be understood as an expression of astonishment regarding it, as though because of the well-known and evident ruling of not repeating wudu because of it, he said: 'Is this something from which wudu is performed?' It is also possible that it may be understood as a form of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of most of the 'ammah.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is in a state of taharah and trims his nails or his hair: must he repeat the wudu (ablution)? He said: No, but he should wipe his head and his nails with water. He said: I said: They claim that wudu (ablution) is required because of it. He said: If they dispute with you, then do not dispute with them, and say: This is the sunnah (prophetic tradition).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man trims his nails, cuts his moustache, and takes from the hair of his head and his beard—does that invalidate his wudu (ablution)? So he said: O Zurarah, all of this is sunnah (prophetic tradition), while wudu (ablution) is an obligation, and nothing from the sunnah invalidates the obligation; rather, that indeed increases him in purification.

Saʿd narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Aʿraj, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I trim my nails, my moustache, and shave my head; must I perform ghusl? He said: No, there is no ghusl upon you. I said: Then should I perform wudu (ablution)? He said: No, there is no wudu (ablution) upon you. I said: Then should I wipe water over my nails? He said: It is pure; there is no wiping required upon you.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: If a man cuts from his hair with his teeth, he should wipe it with water before he performs salat (prayer). He said: There is no harm; that only applies to iron. His statement, 'That only applies to iron,' is to be understood as carrying a kind of recommendation, not obligation.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: If a man trims his nails with iron, or cuts some of his hair, or shaves the back of his neck, then he must wipe it with water before he performs salat (prayer). He was asked: then if he has performed salat (prayer) and did not wipe any of that with water? He said: he repeats the salat (prayer), because iron is impure. And he said: because iron is the attire of the people of the Fire, while gold is the attire of the people of Paradise. So the proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a mode of recommendation rather than obligation, because it is an anomalous report that contradicts the many reports; and whatever proceeds in this manner is not acted upon, as we have explained.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام: Is wudu (ablution) to be performed because of food, or drinking milk—the milks of camels, cattle, and sheep—and their urine and their meat? He said: Wudu (ablution) is not performed because of it.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performed wudu (ablution), then ate meat or fat: may he perform salat (prayer) without washing his hand? He said: Yes. But if it was milk, he should not perform salat (prayer) until he washes his hand and rinses his mouth. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform salat (prayer) after having eaten meat without washing his hand; but if it was milk, he would not perform salat (prayer) until he washed his hand and rinsed his mouth. What this report contains of the command to wash the hands, rinse the mouth, and inhale water into the nose for one who has drunk milk is to be understood as recommendation, not obligation and requirement, as indicated by the first report.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from Abi Bakr, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام, “What should I do when I become junub?” He said: “Wash your hands and your private part, perform wudu (ablution) like the wudu of salat (prayer), then perform ghusl.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: The ghusl of janābah is obligatory, and the ghusl of the menstruating woman when she becomes pure is obligatory, and the ghusl of the woman in istiḥāḍah is obligatory: if she has used cotton padding and the blood passes through the cotton, then ghusl is upon her for every two salats, and for al-fajr there is a ghusl. But if the blood does not pass through the cotton, then ghusl is upon her once every day, and wudu (ablution) for every salat. And the ghusl of the woman in nifās is obligatory, and the ghusl of the deceased is obligatory, and the ghusl of one who touches a deceased person is obligatory.

With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from one of his men, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Ghusl is in seventeen situations, of which three are obligatory. So I said: May I be made your ransom, which of them are obligatory? He said: the ghusl of janabah, the ghusl of one who has washed a dead body, and the ghusl for ihram. His statement عليه السلام, “the ghusl for ihram,” even if it is not considered obligatory according to us, means that its reward is the reward of an obligation and its merit is its merit.

The ghusl of janabah and menstruation is one and the same. Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: And I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the menstruating woman: is there upon her a ghusl like the ghusl of the junub? He said: Yes.

With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim al-Aḥmar, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him: “Is there upon her a ghusl like the ghusl of the junub?” He said: “Yes,” meaning the menstruating woman. And we have already fully covered what relates to the obligation of these ghusls in the book Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām, and we discussed what opposes that in the fullest detail. However, we have mentioned here a number of reports on that matter in which there is sufficiency, if Allah wills.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-Luʾluʾī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Saʿd ibn Abī Khalaf, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Ghusl is in fourteen situations; one is obligatory, and the rest are sunnah. The meaning of this is that one of them is obligatory by the outward meaning of the Qur'an, even though there are other ghusls whose obligation is known through the sunnah.

As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated, from 'Ali ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: There is no ghusl upon the woman in nifas during travel. Its proper meaning is that ghusl is not upon her when she is unable to use water, whether because it is unavailable, or because she needs it for another use, or out of fear of the cold. What is not intended is that ghusl is not upon her in every circumstance.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever washes a dead person should perform ghusl. I said: If he touches him while he is still warm? He said: Then there is no ghusl upon him; but when he has become cold and then he touches him, he should perform ghusl. I said: What about the one who places him into the grave? He said: There is no ghusl upon him; he only touches the clothes.

With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The one who washes the dead body must perform ghusl. If a person kisses the dead after his death while he is still warm, then no ghusl is upon him; but if he touches him and kisses him after he has become cold, then ghusl is obligatory upon him. There is no harm in touching him after the ghusl and kissing him.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim al-Sayqal, who said: I wrote to him: May I be made your ransom, did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام perform ghusl when he washed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم at the time of his death? He replied: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is pure and purified, but Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام did perform it, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be established by it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, who said: I asked him about the dead person: if a human touches him, is there ghusl upon him? He said: He said, “If you touch his body when it has become cold, then perform ghusl.”

Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from some of our companions, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said: If a piece is cut from a man, then it is a dead part. So if a person touches it, then everything in which there is a bone, ghusl becomes obligatory upon the one who touches it. But if there is no bone in it, then no ghusl is upon him.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Touching the dead person at the time of his death and after his ghusl, and kissing him, there is no harm in it.

From him, from Faḍālah, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم kissed ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn after his death. Thus, the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them to mean that if the kissing takes place after death, before the body becomes cold, or after the ghusl, then ghusl does not become obligatory because of it, as we have explained in the report of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān. That report is detailed, while these two reports are general, and judging by the detailed report takes precedence over judging by the general one, and that does not conflict with this.

What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The one who has washed the dead body performs ghusl, and everyone who touches a dead body must perform ghusl, even if the dead body has already been washed. Because what this report contains in his statement, ‘even if the dead body has already been washed,’ is to be understood as a form of recommendation rather than obligation and requirement. We have already treated in full what relates to that in the book Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām, and there is sufficient discussion there, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

As for what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from a man who narrated to him, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about three persons who were on a journey: one of them was in janābah, the second was dead, and the third was without wudu (ablution). The time for salat (prayer) arrived, and they had with them only enough water for one of them. Who should take the water and perform ghusl with it, and what should they do? He said: The junub should perform ghusl, the dead person should be buried, and the one who needs wudu (ablution) should perform tayammum, because ghusl from janābah is an obligation, the ghusl of the dead is a sunnah, and tayammum is permitted for the other. As for what this report contains—that the ghusl of the dead is a sunnah—it does not contradict what we have said, for several reasons. One of them is that this report is mursal, because Ibn Abī Najrān said, "from a man," and did not mention who he was, and it is possible that he was not trustworthy. Even if it were accepted, what is meant by attributing this ghusl to the sunnah is that its obligation was known through the sunnah, because the Qur'an does not indicate that; rather, we only came to know it through the sunnah. We have already mentioned in the first chapter a narration that among the ghusls there are three obligations, including the ghusl of the dead.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan al-Taflīsī, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a dead person and a junub person who are together, while with them there is only enough water for one of them. Which of them should be washed? He said: When a sunnah (prophetic practice) and an obligation come together, the obligation is begun with first.

From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr al-Armanī, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a group who are on a journey, and one of them dies while there is among them a junub, and they have only a small amount of water, enough for only one of the two. Which of them should be attended to first? He said: The junub performs ghusl, and the deceased is left, because this is an obligation and that is a sunnah (prophetic tradition). So the proper way of reconciling these two reports is what we have already presented in the first report equally; moreover, it has been narrated that when the deceased and the junub are together, the deceased is given ghusl and the junub performs tayammum.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī narrated that from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A person in janabah and a deceased person come together in a place where there is only enough water for one of them. Which of the two has more right that the water be assigned to him? He said: The junub performs tayammum, and the deceased is washed with water. And the way of reconciling between them is that it be understood as a matter of choice, because both are obligatory. So whichever of them is washed with the water available, that is permissible.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about running water in which urine is passed. He said: There is no harm.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who urinates in flowing water. He said: There is no harm in it if the water is flowing.
From him, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in a man urinating in flowing water, and it is disliked that he urinate in still water.
From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in urinating in flowing water.

As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from al-Hasan, from some of his companions, from Misma', from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Verily, he صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade a man from urinating in flowing water except in a case of necessity, and he said: Indeed, water has inhabitants. So the correct understanding in this matter is that we carry it upon a type of karahah (disapproval), not upon prohibition and obligation.
