Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about ghusl on Friday, al-Adha, and al-Fitr. He said: It is a sunnah, not an obligation.

With this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Yaʿqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about ghusl (ritual bath) for Friday. He said: It is a sunnah (prophetic tradition) in travel and residence, unless the traveler fears the cold for himself.

And with this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the ghusl of the two Eids: is it obligatory? He said: It is a sunnah. I said: Then Friday? He said: It is a sunnah. As for what has been narrated that the ghusl of Friday is obligatory and the term obligation has been applied to it, the meaning in that is the emphasis of the sunnah and the intensity of its recommendation, and that is expressed by the term obligation; and among that is:

What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about ghusl on the day of Jumuʿah, and he said: It is obligatory upon every male and female, whether slave or free.

And with this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about the ghusl of Friday, and he said: It is obligatory upon every male and female, whether free or slave.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgets the ghusl on Friday until he has prayed. He said: If there is still time, then he must perform ghusl and repeat the salat; but if the time has passed, then his salat has been valid. So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as referring to a kind of recommendation, not obligation and requirement. Likewise, what has been narrated concerning making up the ghusl of Friday on the following day, and performing it earlier on Thursday if missing it is feared, is to be understood as recommendation.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated what we mentioned, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from his father, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who leaves the ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday, forgetfully or otherwise. He said: If he was forgetful, then his salat (prayer) is complete. But if he did so deliberately, then the ghusl is more beloved to me; so if he has done that, then let him seek forgiveness from Allah and not return to it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ja'far ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning: A man who does not perform ghusl on Friday in the early part of the day—he said: he should make it up in the latter part of the day; and if he is not able, then let him make it up on Saturday. And we have exhaustively covered what relates to this chapter in our book Tahdhib al-Ahkam.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one who practices mufakhkhaḏah: is ghusl obligatory upon him? He said: Yes, if he ejaculates.

As for what ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who plays with a woman and kisses her, then semen comes out from him—what is upon him? He said: If desire comes, and it spurts forth, and he experiences slackening due to its خروج, then ghusl is obligatory upon him. But if it is only something for which he does not find any slackening nor desire, then there is no harm. So this does not contradict what we have stated earlier, that the خروج of semen necessitates ghusl in every state. For his statement عليه السلام, “If it is only something for which he does not find any slackening nor desire, then there is no harm,” means when what came out was not semen, because what is considered far-fetched in customary experience and natural disposition is that semen should come out from a person while he finds for it neither desire nor pleasure. Rather, what is meant is when it becomes doubtful to a person and he thinks that it is semen, even though in reality it is not semen; he assesses it by the presence of desire in himself. So if he finds it, ghusl becomes obligatory upon him, and if he does not find it, he knows that what came out from him is not semen.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who sees that a man has intercourse with her in a dream in her private part until she emits fluid. He said: She performs ghusl (ritual bath).

And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Udaym ibn al-Ḥurr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees: is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: Yes. And do not tell them, lest they take it as a pretext.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Ṭāʾī, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated to me from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. He said: I said to him, “A woman or a slave-girl clings to me from behind while I am reclining on my side, and she moves upon my back, then desire comes to her and she emits fluid. Is ghusl (ritual bath) obligatory upon her or not?” He said: “Yes. If desire comes to her and she emits fluid, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her.”

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shadhan, from Yahya ibn Abi Talhah, that he asked a righteous servant about a man who touched the private part of his wife or his bondwoman, playing with her until she emitted fluid: is ghusl obligatory upon her or not? He said: Has she not emitted from desire? I said: Yes. He said: Ghusl is obligatory upon her.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Awdī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: When a woman or a female bondwoman emits from desire, whether a man had intercourse with her or had not had intercourse with her, whether it occurred in sleep or in wakefulness, then ghusl (ritual bath) is obligatory upon her.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man places his male organ upon the woman’s private part and ejaculates; is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: If any of the fluid reaches her, then she should wash it off, and there is nothing due upon her unless he penetrates. I said: Then if she reaches climax but he does not penetrate? He said: Ghusl is not obligatory upon her.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated this hadith in Kitāb al-Mashīkhah with another wording, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd. He said: I performed ghusl on Friday in al-Madinah, put on my clothes, and applied perfume. Then a servant-girl passed by me, and I pressed my thigh against her, so I emitted madhy and she also emitted madhy. I felt distress because of that, so I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about it, and he said: There is no wudu (ablution) upon you, and there is no ghusl upon her. The proper way to understand this report is that it is possible the listener erred in his hearing, and that he had only said, 'she emitted madhy,' but it occurred to him as 'she reached climax,' so he narrated it according to what he thought. It is also possible that he عليه السلام only answered him according to what appeared to him from his condition at that moment, and knew that he believed regarding his servant-girl that she had reached climax, while that was not so; thus he عليه السلام answered him according to what the ruling required, not according to his belief.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: How is it that ghusl becomes obligatory upon a woman if she sees in sleep that a man has intercourse with her in her private part, while ghusl is not made obligatory upon her if he has intercourse with her short of the private part while awake and she emits fluid? He said: Because she saw in her dream that the man had intercourse with her in her private part, so ghusl became obligatory upon her. But the other only had intercourse with her short of the private part, so ghusl did not become obligatory upon her because he did not insert it. If he had inserted it while awake, ghusl would have become obligatory upon her whether she emitted fluid or did not emit fluid. The basis in this report and what we mentioned in the first report is the same.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I said to Abī 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام: A woman experiences a wet dream in sleep and emits the greater fluid. He said: Ghusl (ritual bath) is not obligatory upon her. The correct understanding of this report is that if she sees the greater fluid during her sleep, but when she awakens she does not see anything, then ghusl is not obligatory upon her. This indicates that.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who sees in sleep what a man sees. He said: If she emits, then ghusl (ritual bath) is obligatory upon her; and if she does not emit, then ghusl is not obligatory upon her.

As for what al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from one who narrated it, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said: I said to him: Is ghusl required upon a woman from her janabah if a man has not come to her? He said: No. And which of you would be pleased to see, or endure that, to see his daughter, or his sister, or his mother, or his wife, or one of his female relatives standing to perform ghusl, and then he says: What is the matter with you? And she says: I had a wet dream, while she has no husband. Then he said: No, that is not upon them, and Allah has imposed that upon you. Allah, the Exalted, said: “And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves.” And He did not say that concerning them. So this is a mursal report which cannot be used to oppose what we have previously presented of the reports. And it is possible that the intended meaning in it is what we said regarding the first report equally, and that further clarifies it.

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd al-Ashʿarī, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who touches the private part of his slave-girl until she emits fluid, without intercourse, playing with her by his hand until she emits. He said: If she emits from desire, then ghusl is upon her.

And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a woman in a manner short of the private part, and the woman emits fluid. Is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: Yes.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a woman who sees in her sleep and then emits discharge: is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: Yes.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a woman who sees in a dream that a man has intercourse with her in her private part until she emits fluid. He said: She performs ghusl (ritual bath).

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him: When does ghusl (ritual bath) become obligatory upon the man and the woman? He said: When he inserts it, then ghusl, the mahr, and rajm become obligatory.

With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a woman near the private part, and neither of them emits semen: when does ghusl become obligatory? He said: When the two circumcised parts meet, then ghusl has become obligatory. I said: Is the meeting of the two circumcised parts the disappearance of the glans? He said: Yes.

And with this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from his father, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a virgin slave-girl without fully opening her. Is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: When the circumcised part meets the circumcised part, then ghusl has become obligatory, whether she is a virgin or non-virgin.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Ali عليه السلام did not deem ghusl obligatory for anything except upon the major fluid. The correct way to understand this report is that when the two circumcised parts do not meet, ghusl is not obligatory except with the major fluid, because a man may see in sleep that he had intercourse, then when he awakens he sees nothing; so ghusl is not obligatory upon him unless he awakens and sees the fluid. This indicates that it is specific to this situation.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sees in a dream until he experiences desire, and he thinks that he has had a wet dream; then when he wakes up, he does not see any fluid on his garment nor on his body. He said: Ghusl is not obligatory upon him. And he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: Ghusl is only due from the major fluid; so if he sees something in his dream and does not see the major fluid, then no ghusl is obligatory upon him.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who had a wet dream, then when he awoke he found a small amount of moisture. He said: It is nothing, unless he is ill, for then he becomes weakened, so ghusl is obligatory upon him. So this does not contradict the earlier report that ghusl becomes obligatory from the greater fluid, because it is not impossible that this fluid is itself the greater fluid, except that it comes out from the sick person little by little due to his weakness and lack of movement. For that reason, he عليه السلام differentiated in the report between the sick person and the healthy person, and that further clarifies it.

What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Miskān, from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man had a wet dream, then when morning came he looked at his garment and did not see anything on it. He said: He may perform salat (prayer) in it. I said: Then what about a man who saw in a dream that he had a wet dream, then when he rose he found a small amount of moisture on the tip of his private part? He said: Ghusl is not obligatory upon him. Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: Ghusl is only from the greater fluid. And it indicates also that the ruling of the sick person differs from the ruling of the healthy person.

What was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Hariz, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man sees something in sleep and feels desire, then he wakes up and looks but does not see anything; then after a short while it comes out. He said: If he is ill, then let him perform ghusl, and if he is not ill, then there is nothing upon him. He said: I said to him: So what is the difference between the two? He said: Because when a man is healthy, the fluid comes with a strong gush, but if he is ill, it does not come except afterward.

From him, from Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Wahb, from Dawud ibn Mahziyar, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man saw something in his sleep and experienced pleasure and desire, then he rose and did not see anything on his garment. He said: Then he said, If he is ill, then ghusl (ritual bath) is obligatory upon him; and if he is healthy, then there is nothing upon him.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who sees semen on his clothes after morning has come, while he had not seen in his sleep that he had experienced a wet dream. He said: Let him perform ghusl, wash his garment, and repeat his salat.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who sleeps and did not see in his sleep that he had a nocturnal emission, then he found water on his garment and on his thigh. Is ghusl (ritual bath) obligatory upon him? He said: Yes.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who finds semen on his garment and does not know that he had a nocturnal emission. He said: Let him wash what he found on his garment and perform wudu (ablution). This report does not contradict the first two reports, because the way to reconcile them is that the garment which no one else shares with him in using it—whenever he finds semen on it, ghusl (ritual bath) and repeating the salat (prayer) are obligatory upon him if he had already prayed, since it is possible that he had forgotten the nocturnal emission. But as for what someone else shares with him in using, it does not make ghusl obligatory upon him unless he becomes certain of the nocturnal emission.

Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام) was asked about a man who has contact with a woman in a manner short of the private part: is ghusl obligatory upon her if he ejaculates while she does not ejaculate? He said: There is no ghusl upon her. And if he does not ejaculate, then there is no ghusl upon him.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, raising it, said: If a man comes to a woman in her anus and does not ejaculate, then there is no ghusl (ritual bath) upon either of them. But if he ejaculates, then ghusl is upon him, and there is no ghusl upon her.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: How is it that ghusl becomes obligatory upon a woman if she sees in sleep that a man has intercourse with her in her farj, yet ghusl is not made obligatory upon her if he has intercourse with her short of the farj while awake and she emits fluid? He عليه السلام said: Because she saw in her dream that a man had intercourse with her in her farj, so ghusl became obligatory upon her. As for the other case, he only had intercourse with her short of the farj, so ghusl did not become obligatory upon her because he did not insert it. But if he had inserted it while awake, ghusl would have become obligatory upon her whether she emitted fluid or did not emit.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn Sūqah, from one who informed him, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who approaches his wife from behind. He said: It is one of the two approaches; ghusl is required in it. So it does not contradict the earlier reports, because this report is mursal and maqṭūʿ, in addition to being a solitary report. Something of this status cannot be used to oppose the musnad reports. Furthermore, it is possible that it was issued by way of taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrines of some of the ʿāmmah. Also, the liability is free of any obligation of ghusl, so the obligation of ghusl is not established upon it except by proof that yields knowledge. This report is from the solitary reports that do not yield knowledge nor warrant action, so acting upon it is not obligatory.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris together, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: A person in janabah should not touch a dirham or a dinar upon which the Name of Allah, Exalted is He, is written.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn and ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the junub and the menstruating woman touching silver coins with their hands. He said: There is no harm. So this does not contradict the first report, because it is possible that he only permitted that for him when the name of Allah, Exalted is He, was not on them, even if they were silver; and in the first report there is a prohibition from touching them when there is something of that upon them.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Isma'il ibn Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was with him, so he said: “O my son, read the mushaf.” He said: “Indeed, I am not in a state of wudu (ablution).” So he said: “Do not touch the writing, and touch the paper.”

From him, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about one who recites from the mushaf while he is without wudu (ablution). He said: There is no harm, but he should not touch the writing.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ together, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: Do not touch the muṣḥaf without taharah, nor in the state of janabah, and do not touch its script, and do not suspend it. Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, says: “None touch it except the purified.” So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as indicating a type of karahah rather than prohibition.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the junub: may he eat, drink, and recite the Qur'an? He said: Yes, he may eat, drink, recite the Qur'an, and remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as much as he wishes.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in a menstruating woman and a junub reciting the Qur'an.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him: May the woman in postnatal bleeding, the menstruating woman, the person in janabah, and the man while relieving himself recite the Qur'an? He said: They may recite whatever they wish.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from 'Abd al-Ghaffar al-Harithi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The menstruating woman may recite whatever she wishes from the Qur'an.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, he said: I asked him about the junub: may he recite the Qur'an? He said: up to seven verses. And in the narration of Zurʿah from Samāʿah, he said: seventy verses. This report does not contradict the earlier reports in two ways. One of them is that we specify the earlier reports by means of this report, and say that their statement, peace be upon them: There is no problem in the two of them reciting whatever they wish from any place they wish, means up to seven verses or seventy verses. And the second is that we interpret this report as indicating a kind of istihbab, not prohibition and obligation, while we interpret the earlier reports as indicating permissibility. As for the obligatory surahs containing sajdah, it is not permissible for the two of them to recite them in any حالت; what indicates that is what...

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed us of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The menstruating woman and the person in janabah may recite something. He said: Yes, whatever they wish, except the sajdah, and they may remember Allah in every state.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a menstruating woman who hears the verse of sajdah. He said: If it is from the obligatory prostration verses, she prostrates when she hears it. So this report does not contradict the first report, because it does not state that it is permissible for her to recite the verses of obligatory prostration. It only says: when she hears the verses of obligatory prostration, she prostrates. This also is to be understood as recommendation, because she is in a state in which prostration is not permissible for her.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abu Sa'id, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام: May a man apply dye while he is junub? He said: No. I said: Then may he enter janabah while he is dyed? He said: No. Then he remained silent a little, then said: O Abu Sa'id, shall I not direct you to something that you may do? I said: Yes. He said: When you have applied henna, and the henna has taken its place and fully settled, then at that time have intercourse.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Baḥr, from Kirdīn al-Mismaʿī, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام saying: A man should not dye himself while he is in a state of janabah, nor should he perform ghusl while he is dyed.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from ʿĀmir ibn Judhāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say: The menstruating woman does not apply dye, nor does the junub; and she should not enter janabah while dye is upon her; and he should not enter janabah while dye is upon him; and he should not apply dye while he is junub.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from Samāʿah, from ʿAlī, who said: I asked al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام about the junub and the menstruating woman: may they dye themselves? He said: There is no harm.

From him, from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from ʿAlī, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: May a man use dye while he is junub? He said: There is no harm in it. And about a woman using dye while she is menstruating? He said: There is no harm in it.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in a man applying dye and then becoming junub while he is dyed. And there is no harm in the junub using depilatory, undergoing cupping, and slaughtering. But he should not apply oil nor taste anything until he washes his hands and rinses his mouth, for it is feared that leucoderma may result from it. Thus, the proper way of reconciling these reports is that we carry the former upon a kind of dislike rather than prohibition, so that the reports do not contradict one another. And that which indicates this is:

What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAllān, from Jaʿfar ibn Yūnus, that his father wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. About the junub applying dye, or becoming junub while he is dyed; so he wrote: I do not like that for him. Thus this report came explicitly indicating karahah, not prohibition.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bahr, from Hariz, who said: I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: May a junub apply oil and then perform ghusl? He said: No. So the correct way to understand this report is that it indicates a type of karahah, in accordance with what we mentioned in the narration of al-Sakkuni.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, from Ḥarīz, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who has milk with him: may he perform wudu (ablution) from it for salat (prayer)? He said: No. It is only water and earth. Al-Shaykh Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This report indicates that whatever is not designated by the name of water is not permissible to use, and it conforms to the outward meaning of the Book and what is established in the principles.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, he said: I said to him: A man performs ghusl with rose-water and performs wudu (ablution) with it for salat (prayer)? He said: There is no harm in that. So this is an anomalous report, extremely anomalous. Even if it is repeated in the books, its source is only Yūnus from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and no one besides him narrated it. The group has agreed upon abandoning acting according to its apparent meaning, and whatever is of this status is not acted upon. And even if it were established, it could be that what is meant by wudu (ablution) in the report is beautification. We have already explained in our book Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām the discussion concerning that, and that this is called wudu in the language. And no one has the right to say that the report states that he asked him about rose-water with which he performs wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) and performs ghusl with it, because that does not contradict what we have said. For it is permissible that it be used for beautification, while along with that entry into salat (prayer) is intended by it, inasmuch as whenever a pleasant fragrance is used for entering into salat (prayer), that is better than intending by it only perfuming oneself and enjoyment, apart from the sake of Allah, Exalted is He. And his saying, 'he performs ghusl with it,' may mean the lifting of prohibition from using it in ghusl and the negation of extravagance concerning it, even though seeking permissibility for salat (prayer) by means of it is not valid. And it is also possible that what is meant by his saying 'rose-water' is water into which roses had fallen, because that is called rose-water even if it was not pressed from them. For everything that is adjacent to something else acquires from it a relational name, if adjacency is what is intended by it, as they say: the water of the jar, the water of the well, the water of the reservoir, and the water of the waterskins. All of that is an attribution of adjacency, and in that is the invalidation of reliance upon the report.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn Saʿdān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: The nose and the mouth do not become junub, because they are passages through which fluid passes.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no rinsing of the mouth upon you, nor sniffing water into the nose, because they are part of the interior.

From him, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from some of his companions, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Does the junub rinse his mouth and draw water into his nose? He said: No; it is only the exterior that becomes junub.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said: The jurist al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام said: There is no rinsing of the mouth, nor sniffing water into the nose, in ghusl or in wudu (ablution).

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about ghusl of janabah. He said: Pour water over your hands and wash your palms, then put your hand into the water and wash your private part, then rinse your mouth and inhale water into your nose, and pour water over your head three times, and wash your face, and let the water flow over your body. The implication here is that we understand this as recommended rather than obligatory, so that the reports do not conflict.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who became junub and then performed ghusl before urinating, then something came out of him. He said: He repeats the ghusl. I said: What about the woman, from whom something comes out after ghusl? He said: She does not repeat. I said: What is the difference between them? He said: Because what comes out of the woman is only the man's fluid.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who performs ghusl, then finds moisture, while he had urinated before performing ghusl. He said: If he had urinated before performing ghusl, then he does not repeat the ghusl.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who becomes junub, then performs ghusl before urinating, and then finds moisture after he has performed ghusl. He said: He repeats the ghusl. But if he had urinated before performing ghusl, then he does not repeat his ghusl; rather, he performs wudu (ablution) and cleans himself.

From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man from whose urethra something comes out after he has performed ghusl. He said: He must perform ghusl and repeat the salat, unless he had urinated before performing ghusl; then he does not repeat his ghusl. Muhammad said: And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Whoever performs ghusl while in janabah before urinating, then later finds moisture, his ghusl has been invalidated. But if he had urinated and then performed ghusl, then later found moisture, his ghusl is not invalidated; rather, wudu (ablution) is required of him.

From him, from Faḍālah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying concerning a man who saw something after ghusl: He said, if he had urinated after his intercourse before the ghusl, then let him perform wudu (ablution); but if he had not urinated until he performed ghusl, then afterward found moisture, then let him repeat the ghusl.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥajjāj, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Hilāl, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with his wife, then performs ghusl before urinating, and then something comes out of him after the ghusl. He said: There is nothing upon him; indeed that is among what Allah has lifted from him.

From him, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī Jamīlah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who became junub, then performed ghusl before urinating, then later saw something. He said: He does not repeat the ghusl; that is not something for which he saw [i.e. requiring repetition]. So the proper way of reconciling these two reports is one of two things: the first is that the one washing had exerted effort to urinate but it did not become possible for him, and in that case repeating the ghusl was not obligatory upon him. The second is that this applies specifically to one who did that forgetfully. And what indicates that is what...

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed us of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who is affected by janabah and forgets to urinate until he performs ghusl, then after the ghusl he sees something. Should he perform ghusl again? He said: No; it has been pressed out and descended from the passages.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, who said: I asked him about a man who performed ghusl before urinating, so he wrote: the ghusl is after urination, unless he had forgotten; then he does not repeat the ghusl because of it. So this report came clarifying all the hadiths in the manner that we mentioned: that this applies specifically to one who left it out forgetfully. As for what is contained in the report of Samāʿah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim mentioning the repetition of wudu (ablution), it is to be understood as recommended. And it is possible that what is meant by what came out after urination and ghusl is that which invalidates wudu (ablution); in that case wudu (ablution) becomes obligatory upon him. For that reason he, peace be upon him, said, 'He must perform wudu (ablution) and istinjāʾ,' in the hadith of Samāʿah, and that only applies to what invalidates wudu (ablution).

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Miskan, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform wudu (ablution) with one mudd and perform ghusl with one sa'.

With this chain of transmission, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform wudu (ablution) with one mudd and perform ghusl (ritual bath) with one sa'. A mudd is one and a half ratls, and a sa' is six ratls.

Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from ʿAli ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi. And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Musa ibn ʿUmar, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said: Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام said: Ghusl is with one saʿ of water, and wudu (ablution) is with one mudd of water. The saʿ of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is five mudds, and the mudd is two hundred and eighty dirhams, and the dirham is six daniqs, and the daniq is the weight of six grains, and one grain is the weight of two barley grains of average size, neither from the small ones nor from the large ones.

With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about the amount of water that suffices for ghusl, and he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed ghusl with one ṣāʿ, and performed wudu with one mudd. And the ṣāʿ in his time was five amdad, and the mudd was the measure of one riṭl and three uqiyyahs. His statement عليه السلام in this report, that the ṣāʿ is five amdad, and the explanation of the mudd as one riṭl and three uqiyyahs, accords with the report narrated by Zurārah, because he explained the mudd as one and a half riṭls; thus the ṣāʿ comes to six riṭls, and that corresponds to this amount. As for Sulaymān al-Marwazī’s explanation of the mudd as two hundred and eighty dirhams, it accords with the two reports, because its measure would be six riṭls by the Madinan standard. And his statement عليه السلام, five amdad, may be an error from the narrator, because what is well known from this narration is four amdad. It is also possible that this was a report about what the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to do when one of his wives shared with him in the ghusl, and that indicates this.

What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about the time of ghusl al-janabah: how much water suffices for it? He said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform ghusl with five mudd shared between him and his wife, and the two of them would perform ghusl together from one vessel.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام say: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform ghusl with a sa', and when one of his wives was with him, he would perform ghusl with a sa' and a mudd.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: For ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah and for wudu (ablution), that amount is sufficient of it which is sufficient of oil that moistens the body.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from Isḥāq, from Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: What suffices you for ghusl (ritual bath) and istinjāʾ is that by which you moisten your hand, and whatever other reports run along the same lines; for they are to be understood as indicating sufficiency, while the former reports indicate excellence. However, despite that, the water must necessarily flow over the limbs so that it may be considered washing, even if it is a small amount like oil; for whenever it does not flow, it is not called washing, and that would not be sufficient. And that which indicates this is:

What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: For the person in janabah, whatever amount of water runs over his body—whether little of it or much—then it has sufficed him.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, concerning wudu (ablution). He said: When the water touches your skin, that is sufficient for you.
From him, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskan, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Perform the wudu thoroughly if you find water; otherwise, a small amount suffices you.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام about ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and he said: Wash your right hand from the elbow to your fingers, and urinate if you are able to urinate. Then put your hand into the vessel, then wash whatever of it has touched you. Then pour water over your head and body, and there is no wudu (ablution) in it.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān and Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and he said: You begin with your hands, then wash your private part, then pour water over your head three times, then pour over the rest of your body two times. So whatever the water has flowed over has become tahir (ritually pure).

Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from ʿAli ibn Ismaʿil, from Hammad ibn ʿIsa, from Hariz, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever performed ghusl from janabah but did not wash his head, then afterward it occurred to him to wash his head, he has no choice but to repeat the ghusl.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was between Makkah and al-Madīnah, and Umm Ismāʿīl was with him. He had intercourse with a slave-girl of his, then instructed her, so she washed her body and left her head. He said to her: “When you want to ride, then wash your head.” She did that, and Umm Ismāʿīl came to know of it, so she shaved her head. Then when it was the following year, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام came to that place, and Umm Ismāʿīl said to him: “What place is this?” He said to her: “The place in which Allah rendered your hajj of the previous year void.” So this report is close to being one in which the narrator erred and did not preserve it accurately, and the matter became confused for him, because it is not impossible that he heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say to her: “Wash your head, and when you want to ride, then wash your body,” but he narrated it in reverse. What indicates that is that the narrator of this report, namely Hishām ibn Sālim, narrated this very report exactly in the manner we have stated.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated that from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I entered upon Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام in his tent while he was speaking to a woman, so I hesitated before approaching him. He said: Come near; this is Umm Isma'il. She came, and I maintain that this is the place in which Allah nullified her hajj last year. I had intended to enter ihram, so I said: Put water for me in the tent. The slave-girl took the water and placed it there, and I took advantage of her and had relations with her. Then I said: Wash your head and wipe it thoroughly in a way your mistress will not know. Then when you intend ihram, wash your body and do not wash your head, lest your mistress become suspicious. Then she entered the tent of her mistress and went to take something, and her mistress touched her head and found the stickiness of water. So she shaved her head and beat her. Then I said to her: This is the place in which Allah nullified your hajj.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: If the person in janabah immerses himself in water in a single immersion, that suffices him for his ghusl. So this does not conflict with what we have previously stated regarding the obligation of sequence, because the one who immerses is considered sequential in legal judgment, even if he is not sequential in actual performance. For when he comes out of the water, it is judged first that his head has become pure, then his right side, then his left side, so on this basis it is considered ordered. And it is possible that at the time of immersion, observing sequence is waived, just as in ghusl al-janabah the obligation of wudu is waived.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who becomes junub: is it sufficient for his ghusl of janabah that he stand in the rain until he washes his head and body, while he is able to do otherwise? He said: If he washes himself with it as he would perform his washing with water, that will suffice him. So this report also admits the possibility that he only permitted it for him when he himself washes the limbs at the time the rain falls upon him, according to the order in which they must be arranged. It also admits the possibility that the position regarding it is what we said concerning the first report: that it is sequential in legal ruling, not in actual performance; or that this is a ruling specific to him, excluding one who intends ghusl by placing water upon his body.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, from Ḥarīz, or from one who narrated it from him, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: The people of Kūfah narrate from ʿAlī عليه السلام that he used to command wudu (ablution) before ghusl from janabah. He said: They have lied against ʿAlī عليه السلام. They did not find that in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام. Allah, Exalted is He, said: “And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAwwāḍ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Ghusl suffices in place of wudu (ablution); and what wudu (ablution) is purer than ghusl?

From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Every ghusl is preceded by wudu (ablution), except ghusl al-janābah.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: I asked him, saying: How should I act when I become junub? He said: Wash your hand and your private part, perform wudu (ablution) as for salat (prayer), then perform ghusl (ritual bath). Thus, the correct way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation, and that does not conflict with that.

…of wudu (ablution) before the ghusl (ritual bath), and what indicates that is the statement of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in the narration of Ibn Abī ʿUmayr: “Every ghusl is preceded by wudu except ghusl al-janābah.”

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, that Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hamadani wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام, asking him about wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) in the ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday, so he wrote: There is no wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) with the ghusl of the Day of Friday, nor any other than it.

And from him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who performed ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah, or on the day of Jumuʿah, or on the day of ʿĪd: is wudu (ablution) required of him before that or after it? He said: No, neither before nor after; the ghusl suffices for him. And the woman is likewise in that: if she performs ghusl from hayd or other than that, then wudu (ablution) is not required of her, neither before nor after; the ghusl suffices for her.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Wahb, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Lu'lu'i, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from a man, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning: A man performs ghusl on Friday or otherwise; does it suffice for him in place of wudu (ablution)? So Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: And what wudu (ablution) is purer than ghusl? So the proper approach regarding these reports is that we carry them to mean that when these, or some of them, are combined with ghusl of janabah, then the obligation of wudu (ablution) falls away; but when these ghusls, or some of them, are separate from ghusl of janabah, then wudu (ablution) is obligatory before them, according to what has preceded, and what follows further clarifies that.

What al-Saffār narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Sulaymān ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said: When you wish to perform ghusl on Friday, then perform wudu (ablution), then perform ghusl.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr and ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If you come to the well while you are junub and do not find a bucket nor anything with which to draw water, then perform tayammum with the earth, for the Lord of the water and the Lord of the earth is One. And do not fall into the well, and do not spoil the people’s water for them.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Muskān, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated to me; he said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a junub man who comes upon a small amount of water on the road and wants to perform ghusl from it, but does not have with him a vessel with which to scoop from it, and his hands are dirty. He said: He puts in his hand, performs wudu (ablution), and performs ghusl. This is from what Allah, the Exalted, has said: “He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.” Thus, the correct way to understand this report is that he should take the water from the pool with his hand and not enter it himself, and perform ghusl by pouring the water over the body. His statement عليه السلام, “and his hands are dirty,” indicates the filth upon them in the sense of grime, not najasah, because najasah would spoil the water for use upon the body when it is a small amount, as we have already explained.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad and Aḥmad, the two sons of al-Ḥasan, from their father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: When a woman menstruates, her husband may approach her as he wishes, so long as he avoids the place of blood.

And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus Buzurj, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about what is permitted to the husband from a menstruating woman. He said: Everything except the front private part itself.

With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: A man approaching a woman in what is short of the private part while she is menstruating. He عليه السلام said: There is no harm, if he avoids that place.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is permissible for a man from a menstruating woman? He said: What is between the thighs.

And with this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is permitted to a man from a menstruating woman? He said: What is between her buttocks, but he must not penetrate.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding the menstruating woman: what is lawful for her husband from her. He said: She should wrap herself with a waist-wrapper down to the knees and leave her navel uncovered; then for him is what is above the waist-wrapper.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim al-Aḥmar, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about the menstruating woman: what is lawful for her husband from her? He said: She should wrap herself with a waist-wrapper down to the knees and uncover her legs, and for him is what is above the waist-wrapper.

From him, from al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Ḥajjāj al-Khashshāb, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about the menstruating woman and the woman in postnatal bleeding: what is permissible for her husband from her? He said: She should wear a shift, then lie down with him. So the proper way regarding these reports is one of two things: one of them is that we interpret them as indicating a kind of recommendation, while the earlier reports indicate permissibility and lifting of prohibition. The second is that we interpret them as a kind of taqiyyah, because they are in agreement with the doctrines of many of the ‘Āmmah.

As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about what is lawful for a man from a menstruating woman. He said: “Nothing, until she becomes pure.” So the intended meaning in his statement, “Nothing,” is that it is to be understood as meaning that nothing is lawful for him of intercourse in the private part, even though what is less than that is lawful for him. And the first two possible interpretations that we mentioned in the previous reports are also possible in this report.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the minimum of what menstruation may be, and he said: Its minimum is three days, and its maximum is ten.

With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام about the minimum of what menstruation may be, and he said: Its minimum is three days, and its furthest limit is ten.

And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: The minimum of menstruation is three, and its maximum is ten.

And Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The least duration of hayd is three days. If she sees blood before ten days, then it is part of the first menstruation; and if she sees it after ten days, then it is from another forthcoming menstruation.

And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Ziyād al-Khazzāz, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the woman with istiḥāḍah: what should she do when she sees blood, and when she sees yellow discharge, and how long should she leave the salat (prayer)? He said: The minimum of menstruation is three [days] and its maximum is ten, and she combines between the two salats (prayers).

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: the maximum that menstruation may be is eight, and the minimum that it may be is three. This report does not contradict the reports we have presented, due to the consensus of the sect being contrary to it, and because none of our companions held that the furthest limit of the days of menstruation is less than ten days. Even if it were accepted, it would be possible for us to interpret it as referring to a woman whose habit was eight days, then she became in a state of istiḥāḍah; for the most that is obligatory upon her is that she leave salat (prayer) during the days of her habit, and that is eight days, as we explained in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The qurʾ cannot be less than ten; whatever exceeds that, the least that it may be is ten, from the time she becomes pure until she sees blood.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, he said: I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: A woman sees blood for three days or four. He said: She leaves the salat. I said: Then she sees purity for three days or four days. He said: She performs salat. I said: Then she sees blood for three days or four days. He said: She leaves the salat. I said: Then she sees purity for three days or four days. He said: She performs salat. I said: Then she sees blood for three days or four days. He said: She leaves the salat; she does that for what is between that and a month. Then if it stops from her, otherwise she is in the position of the mustahadah.

And among what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from al-Sindī ibn Muḥammad al-Bazzāz, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who sees blood for five days and purity for five days, then sees blood for four days and purity for six days. He said: If she sees blood, she does not perform salat; and if she sees purity, she performs salat during the period between that and thirty days. Then when thirty days are completed, if she sees flowing blood, she performs ghusl, fastens her cloth, and uses cotton at the time of every salat; and if she sees yellowish discharge, she performs wudu (ablution). The proper way regarding these two reports is that we carry them upon a woman whose habit in menstruation has become confused and changed from its times, and likewise the days of her cycles, and the quality of the blood has become unclear to her, so that the blood of menstruation is not distinguishable for her from other than it. For if that is the case, then her obligation, when she sees blood, is to leave salat, and when she sees purity, she performs salat until she comes to know her habit. And it is also possible that this is the ruling of a woman in istihadah whose menstrual days have become confused for her, whose habit has changed, and whose bleeding has continued, while the quality of the blood is ambiguous; so she sees what resembles menstrual blood for three or four days, and she sees what resembles the blood of istihadah likewise, and she has not attained knowledge of which one of the two it is. Then her obligation is to leave salat whenever she sees what resembles menstrual blood, and to perform salat whenever she sees what resembles the blood of istihadah, for up to a month; then after that she does what a woman in istihadah does. And his statement, 'she saw purity for three or four days,' may mean what resembles the blood of istihadah, because istihadah is under the ruling of purity. For that reason he said in the report, 'then she does what a woman in istihadah does,' and that only occurs along with continuing blood. This is indicated by the report that we have cited in our larger book from more than one person who asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about menstruation and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) concerning it.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sinān, from Ḥafṣ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about one who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating. He said: He should give charity of one dīnār and seek forgiveness from Allah, Exalted is He.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿImrān al-Ḥalabī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever has intercourse with a menstruating woman, then half a dīnār is upon him, which he gives in charity.

And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, concerning a man who has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating: what is upon him? He said: He gives charity to a poor person in an amount sufficient for his fill.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Aban, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Amr, who said: 'Abd al-Karim said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who had intercourse with his slave-girl while she was menstruating. He said: 'He should seek Allah's forgiveness.' 'Abd al-Karim said: 'But the people say that half a dinar or a dinar is due from him.' So Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: 'Then let him give charity to ten needy persons.' Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The way to reconcile these reports is that we interpret intercourse, when it occurs at the beginning of menstruation, as requiring a dinar; if it is in the middle, half a dinar; and if it is at the end, a quarter of a dinar. Sometimes its value may equal the amount of charity to ten needy persons, and whenever one is unable to do that, charity to one needy person sufficient to satisfy his hunger will suffice, so that the reports may be harmonized. And that which indicates this detail is what follows.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from some of our companions, from al-Tayalisi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning: The kaffarah of menstruation is that he gives charity: if it was at its beginning, then one dinar; in its middle, half a dinar; and at its end, a quarter dinar. I said: What if he does not have what he may offer as kaffarah? He said: Then let him give charity to one needy person; otherwise, let him seek Allah’s forgiveness and not return to it, for seeking forgiveness is tawbah and a kaffarah for everyone who does not find a way to anything of the kaffarah.

As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Safwan, from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating, He said: He should not seek to do that, for Allah has forbidden that he approach her. I said: If he does it, is there any kaffarah upon him? He said: I do not know of anything regarding it; he should seek Allah's forgiveness.

And among what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Abī Jamīlah, from Layth al-Murādī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man having intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating, by mistake. He said: There is nothing upon him, though he has disobeyed his Lord.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a menstruating woman with whom her husband has intercourse. He said: Nothing is due upon him; he should seek Allah’s forgiveness and not return to it. Thus, the proper way regarding these reports is that they are to be understood as referring to when the man did not know from her condition that she was menstruating; then nothing is binding upon him. But as for when he knows that, then expiation is binding upon him according to what we have mentioned. And no one may say: This interpretation is not possible, because if these reports were to be understood as applying to the state of forgetfulness, he عليه السلام would not have said, “He seeks forgiveness from his Lord for what he did,” nor that “he disobeyed his Lord.” For it is not impossible to apply the statement to him that he disobeyed, nor to urge him to seek forgiveness, inasmuch as he was negligent in asking about her condition and whether she was menstruating or not, while knowing that had she been menstruating, intercourse with her would have been forbidden to him. So by this negligence he is disobedient, and seeking forgiveness becomes obligatory upon him. What clarifies this interpretation is the report of Layth al-Murādī mentioned earlier. He said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man having intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating by mistake. So he restricted the question by stating that his intercourse with her had been in error, and he عليه السلام answered him: Nothing is due upon him, though he has disobeyed his Lord.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from some of the truthful ones, who said: If a man is unable to obtain water but is able to obtain milk, then he should not perform wudu (ablution) with it; rather, it is only water or tayammum. But if he is unable to obtain water and there is nabidh, then I have heard Ḥarīz mention in a hadith that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed wudu (ablution) with nabidh when he could not obtain water. The first point concerning it is that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah said: ‘from some of the truthful ones,’ and it is possible that the one to whom he ascribed it was not an Imam; even if he believed him outwardly to be truthful, acting upon it is not obligatory. The second is that the group has agreed that wudu (ablution) with nabidh is not permissible, so using it as evidence also falls from consideration from this angle. And even if it were free of all of that, it would be possible to interpret it as referring to water into which a small amount of dates had been placed so that its taste might become pleasant and its salinity and bitterness be reduced, so long as it had not reached a point that stripped it absolutely of the name of water. For nabidh in the language is that in which something has been cast, and water into which a small amount of dates has been placed is called nabidh. And that which indicates this interpretation is what...

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, all together, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hamadhānī, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khayyāṭ, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from al-Kalbī al-Nassābah, that he asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about nabīdh, and he said: It is halal. He said: We prepare nabīdh and put into it the dregs and other than that. He said: Fie, fie! That is the foul-smelling khamr. He said: I said, may I be your ransom, then which nabīdh do you mean? He said: The people of al-Madīnah complained to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about the change in the water and the corruption of their constitutions, so he ordered them to prepare nabīdh. A man would instruct his servant to prepare it for him, so he would take a handful of dates and cast it into the waterskin; from it was his drink, and from it was his means of purification. So I said: How many dates were there in the handful? He said: Whatever the hand could carry. I said: One or two? He said: At times it was one, and at times it was two. I said: And how much did the waterskin hold? He said: Between forty and eighty, and more than that. I said: By which ratls? He said: The ratls of the measure of Iraq.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, who said: Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ narrated to me, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a woman whose menstrual blood ceases at the end of her days, he said: If her husband is overcome by desire, then she should wash her private part, and then her husband may touch her, if he wishes, before she performs ghusl (ritual bath).

And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad and Aḥmad, the two sons of al-Ḥasan, from their father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: When the blood stops and she has not performed ghusl, then her husband may come to her if he wishes.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his paternal uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a woman who had been menstruating and then saw purification: may her husband have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl? He said: No, not until she performs ghusl. He said: And I asked him about a woman who menstruated while traveling, then became pure, but did not find water for a day or two. Is it lawful for her husband to have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl? He said: It is not proper until she performs ghusl.

And from him, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ and Sindī ibn Muḥammad together, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A woman upon whom salat (prayer) becomes forbidden, then she becomes pure and performs wudu (ablution) without performing ghusl (ritual bath) — may her husband approach her before she performs ghusl? He said: No, not until she performs ghusl. So the proper way regarding these reports is that we carry them upon a degree of karāhah, not prohibition, and the earlier reports upon permissibility. What indicates that is what follows.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from one who heard it, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, concerning: If a woman becomes pure from menstruation but has not touched water, then her husband should not have intercourse with her until she performs ghusl. If he does so, then there is no harm in it. And he said: her touching water is more beloved to me.

And from him, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a menstruating woman who sees purity: may her husband have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl? He said: There is no harm, but after ghusl is more beloved to me.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: If a woman sees blood at the beginning of her first menstruation, and the blood continues with her after that, she leaves the salat (prayer) for ten days, then performs salat (prayer) for twenty days. If the blood continues with her after that, she leaves the salat (prayer) for three days and performs salat (prayer) for twenty-seven days. Hasan ibn 'Ali said, and Ibn Bukayr said: This is among the matters from which they find no alternative.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad and Aḥmad, the two sons of al-Ḥasan, from their father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, who said: Regarding the young girl when she menstruates for the first time: blood continues upon her, so she is deemed a mustaḥāḍah. She waits concerning salat (prayer), so she does not pray until the maximum period of menstruation has passed. When that has passed—and it is ten days—she does what the mustaḥāḍah does, then she performs salat (prayer), and she continues praying for the remainder of her month. Then, in the second occurrence, she leaves salat (prayer) for the minimum period that a woman leaves salat (prayer), and she sits out the minimum duration of menses, which is three days. If menstruation continues upon her, she performs salat (prayer) at the time of the salat (prayer) she had been performing, and she makes the time of her purity the maximum possible duration of purity, while making her leaving of salat (prayer) the minimum possible duration of menstruation. What is contained in the long report of Yūnus that we cited in our larger book does not contradict these two reports: namely, that one in this condition leaves salat (prayer) for seven days in the month and performs salat (prayer) for the rest of the month.
