That may be understood as referring to what affects each one of two months when two months are considered together, because if she leaves salat (prayer) in the first month for ten days and in the second for three days, half of that is approximately seven days. Thus it accords with what the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr contains, and it accords with all the principles.

As for what Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah, he said: I asked him about a young girl who menstruated for the first time, and her blood continued for three months, while she does not know the days of her menstrual cycles. He said: Her menstrual periods are like the menstrual periods of the women of her family. If the women of her family differ, then the maximum of her waiting period is ten days and its minimum is three days.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Bint Ilyās, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj and Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān together, from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: It is obligatory for the mustahadah to consider some of her womenfolk and follow their menstrual periods, then to add one day by way of precaution to that. This does not conflict with the earlier reports, because this is the ruling for one who has womenfolk; but as for one who has no womenfolk, or they differ, then the ruling is what we have mentioned. For that reason he said at the end of the report: if her womenfolk differ, then the maximum of her waiting is ten days and the minimum of it is three, so her ruling in that case is referred back to what the earlier reports contained.

My shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon them, concerning: A pregnant woman sees blood. He said: She leaves the salat (prayer), for sometimes blood remains in the womb and does not come out, and that is the bleeding.

With this chain of transmission, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, that he was asked about a pregnant woman who sees blood: should she leave the salat (prayer)? He said: Yes. Indeed, a pregnant woman may sometimes discharge blood.

From him, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the pregnant woman who sees blood. He said: Yes, indeed a woman may sometimes discharge blood while she is pregnant.

From him, from Safwan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام about a pregnant woman who sees blood while she is pregnant, just as she used to see before that in every month: should she leave the salat (prayer)? So he said: She leaves it if it continues.

From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a woman who sees blood during pregnancy. He said: She refrains for the days in which she used to menstruate; then if the blood exceeds the days in which she used to refrain, she should wait an additional three days, then after that she is in a state of istihadah.

From him, from Ṣafwān, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a pregnant woman who sees blood for three days or four days: should she perform salat (prayer)? He said: She should refrain from salat (prayer).

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said: I asked him about a pregnant woman who sees blood just as she used to see during the days of her menstruation, regularly in every month. He said: She refrains from salat just as she used to do during her menstruation, and when she becomes pure, she performs salat.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ḥumayd ibn al-Muthannā, he said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a pregnant woman who sees one gush or two gushes of blood during some days, and during a month or two months. He said: That is bleeding; this does not prevent her from salat (prayer).

And among what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sukuni, from Ja'far, from his father عليه السلام, that he said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Allah was not to place menstruation together with pregnancy. That means: if a woman sees blood while she is pregnant, she does not leave the salat (prayer), unless she sees it at the head of the child, when labor pains strike her; and if she sees blood then, she leaves the salat (prayer). So these two reports do not contradict the earlier reports, because the first report said: I asked him about a pregnant woman who sees one gush and two gushes during the days and during the month, and he said to him: that is a flowing discharge; this does not prevent her from salat (prayer). That is sound, because that is not the minimum of menstruation, for we have already explained that the minimum days of menstruation are three days. If she sees only one gush or two gushes, then it is not menstrual blood, and it is not permissible for her to leave salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting). As for the second report, which is his statement عليه السلام, 'Allah did not place pregnancy together with menstruation,' the way to understand it is that this is not the case with a pregnant woman whose pregnancy has become evident. Menstruation only occurs so long as the pregnancy has not become evident; once it becomes evident, menstruation has ceased. For that reason, we held that whenever it is delayed from her usual time by twenty days, then that is not menstrual blood. That is indicated by what...

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Ṣaḥḥāf, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The mother of my two children sees blood while she is pregnant; how should she act regarding salat (prayer)? He said: If the pregnant woman sees blood after twenty days have passed from the time in the month when she used to see blood and remain seated, then that is not from the womb nor from menstruation. So she should perform wudu (ablution), place cotton, and perform salat (prayer). But if the pregnant woman sees blood before the time in which she used to see a small amount of blood, or at that time in that month, then it is from menstruation. So she should refrain from salat (prayer) for the number of days she used to remain seated during her menses. If the blood stops before that, then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath) and perform salat (prayer). But if the blood does not stop except after the days in which she used to see blood have passed by one or two days, then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath), place cotton, bind herself, and perform the noon and afternoon salat (prayer). Then she should observe: if the blood, between that time and sunset, does not flow past the back of the cotton, then she should perform wudu (ablution) and perform salat (prayer) at each prayer so long as she has not removed the cotton. If she removes the cotton from herself and the blood flows, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her. But if she removes the cotton and the blood does not flow, then she should perform wudu (ablution) and perform salat (prayer), and there is no ghusl upon her. He said: If the blood, when the cotton holds it, flows from behind the cotton in a pouring manner and does not cease, then she must perform ghusl (ritual bath) three times in every day and night, then place cotton and perform salat (prayer): she performs ghusl for fajr, and performs ghusl for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr, and performs ghusl for maghrib and the later ʿishāʾ. He said: And likewise the mustaḥāḍah acts, for when she does that, Allah removes the blood from her.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a pregnant woman who sees blood for a day and two days. He said: If it is fresh blood, then she should not perform salat (prayer) during those two days; and if it is yellowish discharge, then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath) at the time of every two prayers. This report does not contradict what we presented earlier, that the minimum of menstruation is three days, because the correct way to understand it here is that she sees blood on one day and two days as consecutive blood, and then completes the three within the period of ten days. For whenever a menstruating woman sees blood for three days within the span of ten days, she is considered menstruating, even if that was not consecutive, according to what we narrated in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām in the report of Yūnus.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥajjāl, from Thaʿlabah, from Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a menstruating woman who becomes pure at the time of ʿaṣr: does she pray the first one? He said: No. She only prays the salat (prayer) at whose time she becomes pure.

With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Faḍl ibn Yūnus, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام. I said: If a woman sees purity before sunset, what should she do regarding the salat (prayer)? He عليه السلام said: If she sees purity after four qadam have passed from the sun’s decline, then she should not perform any salat except al-ʿAṣr, because the time of al-Ẓuhr entered upon her while she was in blood, and the time passed from her while she was in blood. So it was not obligatory upon her to perform al-Ẓuhr, and what Allah has lifted from her of the salat while she is in blood is more. He عليه السلام said: And if a woman sees blood after four qadam have passed from the sun’s decline, then she should refrain from the salat. Then when she becomes pure from the blood, she should make up al-Ẓuhr, because the time of al-Ẓuhr entered upon her while she was pure, and the time of al-Ẓuhr left her while she was pure, so she neglected the salat of al-Ẓuhr, and thus making it up became obligatory upon her.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said: I said: A woman sees that she has become pure at the time of al-ẓuhr, but she busies herself with her affairs until the time of al-ʿaṣr enters. He said: She should perform al-ʿaṣr alone; but if she neglected it, then two salats (prayers) are upon her.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn al-Rabīʿ, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If the menstruating woman becomes pure before al-ʿAṣr, she performs al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr. But if she becomes pure at the end of the time of al-ʿAṣr, she performs al-ʿAṣr. So this does not conflict with the first report, because his statement, 'if she becomes pure before the time of al-ʿAṣr,' may mean that this was during the time of al-Ẓuhr. For that reason, making up al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr became obligatory upon her. But if it were the time of al-ʿAṣr only and nothing else, then nothing would be obligatory upon her except the salat of al-ʿAṣr.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from Yaʿqūb, from Abī Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, concerning... Regarding the menstruating woman: if she performs ghusl during the time of ʿaṣr, she prays ʿaṣr and then prays ẓuhr. This also does not conflict with what we presented earlier, because he only informed about one who performs ghusl during the time of ʿaṣr, and it is possible that she had become pure during the time of ẓuhr but delayed the ghusl until she performed ghusl at a time in which ʿaṣr had become constrained. For that reason, he instructed her to perform ẓuhr after she prays ʿaṣr.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If the woman becomes pure before the rising of dawn, she prays Maghrib and the latter ʿIshaʾ. And if she becomes pure before the sun sets, she prays Zuhr and ʿAsr.

From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If the woman becomes pure before sunset, then she should perform the ẓuhr and the ʿaṣr salat (prayer); and if she becomes pure at the end of the night, then she should perform the maghrib and the ʿishāʾ salat (prayer).

From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Thaʿlabah, from Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā, from Dāwūd al-Zajjājī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If a woman is menstruating and becomes pure before sunset, she performs the ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers; and if she becomes pure at the end of the night, she performs the maghrib and the latter ʿishāʾ prayer.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū Jamīlah and Muḥammad his brother, from their father, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah, from the Shaykh عليه السلام, who said: If a woman becomes pure before the rising of dawn, she performs the maghrib and the latter ʿishaʾ prayers; and if she becomes pure before the sun sets, she performs the zuhr and ʿasr prayers. The proper way of reconciling these reports is that we say: if the woman becomes pure after the sun’s decline until four qadam have passed from it, then it is obligatory upon her to make up both zuhr and ʿasr together. If she becomes pure after the passing of four qadam, then only the makeup of ʿasr is obligatory upon her, and it is recommended for her to make up zuhr if her purity continues until sunset. Likewise, the makeup of maghrib and ʿishaʾ is obligatory upon her until midnight, and it is recommended for her to make them up until the time of dawn’s rising. In this way, there is no contradiction between the reports.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Concerning a woman for whom the time of salat entered while she was in a state of taharah, then she delayed the salat until she menstruated, he said: She makes it up when she becomes pure.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Shādhān ibn al-Khalīl al-Naysābūrī, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked him about a woman who begins menstruating after the sun has passed the meridian, and she has not performed the ẓuhr prayer: is she required to make up that prayer? He said: Yes.

As for what Ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi al-Ward, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a woman who is in the zuhr prayer and has prayed two rak'ahs, then she sees blood. He said: She rises from her place of prayer and does not make up the two rak'ahs. He said: And if she sees blood while she is in the maghrib prayer and has prayed two rak'ahs, then let her rise from her place of prayer, and when she becomes pure, let her make up the rak'ah that she missed from maghrib. So what this report contains regarding the dropping of making up the two rak'ahs from the zuhr prayer is directed to one who entered the prayer at the beginning of its time, because one whose ruling is such is not considered negligent; and if she was not negligent, making it up is not binding upon her. And what it contains of the command to repeat the rak'ah from maghrib is directed to one who entered the prayer when the time had become constricted and then menstruated; then what she missed is binding upon her at that point. And that which indicates that this is directed to one who was negligent is that...

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If a woman becomes pure during a prayer time and delays the salat (prayer) until the time of another salat (prayer) enters, then she sees blood, the qaḍāʾ of that salat (prayer) which she was negligent regarding is upon her.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning: A woman for whom dawn rises while she is menstruating in the month of Ramadan, then when morning comes she becomes pure, and she has already eaten, then she performs the Zuhr and ʿAsr salat (prayer)—what should she do regarding that day in which she became pure? He عليه السلام said: She should fast, but she should not count it.

And from him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman who menstruates in the month of Ramaḍān before the sun sets. He said: She breaks her fast when she menstruates.

From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Jamil ibn Darrāj and Muhammad ibn Humrān, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: At whatever hour the woman sees blood, then she breaks the fast of the fasting woman when she menstruates. And if she sees purity at any hour of the day, she makes up the prayer of the day and the night.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his paternal uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If menstruation comes upon a woman in the month of Ramadan before zawāl, then she has latitude to eat and drink. But if it comes upon her after the sun’s decline, then she should perform ghusl and count the fast of that day, so long as she has not eaten or drunk. So this report is an error from the narrator, because if seeing blood is what breaks the fast, then it is not permissible for her to count the fast of that day. Rather, it is only recommended for her to refrain for the rest of the day as a matter of discipline if she sees blood after zawāl. And that which indicates this is what...

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who sees blood in the morning, or after the day has risen, or at noon. He said: She breaks her fast. And if it is after al-ʿaṣr or after noon, then she should continue upon her fast and make up that day.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If a woman menstruates while she is in a state of janabah, one ghusl suffices for her.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who had relations with his wife, then she menstruated before performing ghusl. He said: She makes it one ghusl.

From him, from al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Ḥajjāj al-Khashshāb, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had intercourse with his wife, then she menstruated after he had finished. Should she make it one ghusl when she becomes pure, or should she perform ghusl twice? He said: She makes it one ghusl at the time of her purification.

As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh and Abī al-Ḥasan, peace be upon them, who said: Regarding a man who has intercourse with a woman and then she menstruates before performing ghusl from janābah, he said: the ghusl of janābah is obligatory upon her. So the proper way to understand this report is one of two possibilities: one of them is that we interpret it as indicating a kind of recommendation, and the second is that it is informing about the manner of the ghusl, because the ghusl of the menstruating woman is exactly like the ghusl of janābah. So it is as though he said: what is obligatory upon her is that she perform a ghusl like the ghusl of janābah. He did not say that the ghusl of janābah itself is obligatory and that, in addition to that, the ghusl of menstruation is also binding upon her. That which clarifies what we first mentioned concerning recommendation...

What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman with whom her husband has intercourse, then she menstruates before performing ghusl. He said: If she wishes to perform ghusl, she may do so; and if she does not do it, then there is nothing upon her. Then when she becomes pure, she performs one ghusl for menstruation and janabah.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna al-Khayyat, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The menstruating woman performs ghusl with nine ratls of water.

And with this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: For the menstruating woman, whatever amount of the wetness of water reaches her hair suffices for her.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the menstruating woman: how much water is sufficient for her? He said: “A faraq.” So this report and the first report are to be understood as referring to thorough completion and extra merit, while the second report refers to sufficiency without extra merit.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā Ja'far عليه السلام saying: The 'iddah and menstruation are entrusted to the women.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Concerning a woman who claimed that she menstruated three times in a single month, he said: Assign women from among her close associates to verify whether her menstruation in the past had been as she claimed. If they testify, then she has spoken truthfully; otherwise, she is lying. The correct way to reconcile the two reports is that if the woman is trusted, her word regarding menstruation and the waiting period is accepted; but if she is under suspicion, other women are assigned in accordance with what the report contains.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The woman in istihadah refrains for the days of her menstrual period, then she takes precaution by one or two days. If she sees purity, she performs ghusl; and if she does not see purity, she performs ghusl and inserts cotton. She continues to perform salat with that ghusl until blood appears upon the cotton; then, when the blood appears, she repeats the ghusl and replaces the cotton.

From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a woman who menstruates, then becomes pure, and then perhaps sees after that a slight amount of thin blood after her ghusl from her purity. He said: She should practice istizhar after her days by one day, or two days, or three, then she performs salat (prayer).

Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the menstruating woman: for how long does she practice precautionary waiting? He said: She practices precautionary waiting for one day, or two days, or three.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the menstruating woman: what is the limit of her waiting period? He said: She waits for the number of days she used to menstruate, then she adds a precautionary waiting of three days; then after that she is a woman with istihadah.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Zayyāt, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: A woman saw blood during her menstruation until it passed beyond its usual time; when should she begin to perform salat (prayer)? He said: She waits for the number of days she used to remain [in menstruation], then she exercises precaution up to ten days. If she sees the blood as flowing blood, then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath) at every time of salat (prayer). So the correct way regarding his statement عليه السلام, 'she exercises precaution by ten days,' is that we understand it to mean: up to ten days, because that is the maximum number of days of menstruation. Precaution is only required for one day or two days when the habitual period is less than that, and what indicates that is what follows.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Concerning a woman who sees blood, he said: If her period is less than ten days, she waits for ten days; and if her days are ten, she does not practice istiẓhār.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud, the mawla of Abi al-Mi'za, from one who informed him, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a woman who menstruates, then the time of her purity passes while she still sees blood. He said: She should exercise precaution by waiting one day, if her menstruation is less than ten days. If the blood continues after ten days, then she is a mustahadah. If the blood stops, she performs ghusl and offers salat (prayer).

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, concerning: A man performing wudu (ablution) with the leftover water of a menstruating woman. He عليه السلام said: If she is trustworthy, then there is no harm.

With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the leftover water of a menstruating woman, He said: Perform wudu (ablution) with it, and perform wudu (ablution) from the leftover water of the junub when she is trustworthy, and she washes her hand before putting it into the vessel. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform ghusl, he and ʿĀʾishah, in one vessel, and they would bathe together.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The leftover water of the menstruating woman may be drunk from, but wudu (ablution) is not performed with it.

And from him, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding the menstruating woman: one may drink from her leftover water, but wudu (ablution) is not performed from it.

From him, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him: “May wudu (ablution) be performed from the leftover water of the wudu (ablution) of a menstruating woman?” He said: “No.” So the proper way regarding these reports is what was detailed in the earlier reports, namely that if the woman is not trusted, then performing wudu (ablution) with her leftover water is not permissible. And it is possible that what is intended by them is a kind of recommendation, and what indicates that is what...

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Ḥajjāj al-Khashshāb, from Abī Hilāl, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: As for the menstruating woman, I drink from the remainder of her drink, but I do not like to perform wudu (ablution) from it.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār and Zurārah, from one of them عليه السلام, who said: The woman in nifās refrains from salat (prayer) for the days of her regular menstrual periods during which she used to remain [away from prayer]; then she performs ghusl and acts as the mustaḥāḍah acts.

With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: The woman in nifas sits out for the days of her menstruation that she used to menstruate, then she exercises precaution, performs ghusl, and offers salat (prayer).

With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The woman in nifas refrains for the number of days that she used to refrain during menstruation, and she takes an additional precaution of two days.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Yunus, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who gave birth and then saw blood more than she used to see. He said: Let her refrain for the days of her menstrual period during which she used to sit, then let her seek precaution up to ten days. If she sees flowing blood, then let her perform ghusl (ritual bath) at the time of every salat (prayer); and if she sees yellowish discharge, then let her perform wudu (ablution) and then pray. His statement عليه السلام, 'she seeks precaution by ten days,' means up to ten days, because particles with descriptive functions may stand in place of one another, as we have already explained in discussion of this.

With this chain of transmission, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام about a woman who experienced postnatal bleeding, then remained for thirty nights or more, became pure, and performed salat (prayer), then afterward saw blood or yellowish discharge. So he عليه السلام said: If it is yellowish discharge, then let her perform ghusl (ritual bath) and perform salat (prayer), and she should not refrain from salat (prayer). But if it is blood that is not yellowish discharge, then let her refrain from salat (prayer) for the days of her menstrual period, then let her perform ghusl (ritual bath) and perform salat (prayer).

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah and al-Fuḍayl, from one of the two of them, peace be upon him, who said: The woman in nifās refrains from salat (prayer) for the days of her menstrual periods during which she used to remain [in menstruation]; then she performs ghusl and prays, just as the mustaḥāḍah performs ghusl.

With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Mālik ibn Aʿyan, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman in postnatal bleeding: may her husband have intercourse with her while she is still in her nifās from the blood? He عليه السلام said: Yes, when there has passed for her, from the day she gave birth, a period equal to the number of days of her menstrual habit, then she adds one precautionary day; after that, there is no harm in her husband having intercourse with her. He instructs her to perform ghusl, so she performs ghusl, then he may have intercourse with her if he wishes.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: The woman in nifās sits out for forty days; then if she becomes pure, otherwise she performs ghusl and prays, and her husband may approach her, and she is in the position of a woman with istiḥāḍah: she fasts and she prays.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: It is as she had been, in accordance with what has passed regarding her previous children and what she has experienced. I said: Then if she had not given birth before? He said: Between forty and fifty.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: How long does the postpartum woman remain seated until she performs salat (prayer)? He said: Eighteen, seventeen; then she performs ghusl, uses a cloth, and performs salat (prayer).

'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The woman in nifas remains seated [i.e., refrains from acts requiring ritual purity], if the blood does not stop from her, for thirty or forty days, up to fifty.

Al-Hasan ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام saying: The woman in nifas remains seated for nineteen nights; then if she sees blood, she does as the mustahadah does. And we have also narrated from Ibn Sinan that which conflicts with this report: that the days of nifas are like the days of hayd. Thus, the two reports are in conflict.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about the woman in postnatal bleeding: how long does she refrain? He said: Indeed, Asma' bint 'Umays was instructed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to perform ghusl after eighteen days, and there is no harm in her taking an extra precaution by one day or two days. So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports that we have presented, because we have several approaches in discussing these reports. One of them is that these reports are solitary reports, differing in wording and contradictory in meaning; it is not possible to act upon all of them because of their contradiction, nor upon some of them, because some of them are no more deserving of being acted upon than others. The earlier reports are agreed upon regarding what they contain, because there is no disagreement that the days of menstruation are taken into consideration in postnatal bleeding; disagreement exists only concerning what exceeds that. When they conflict, it becomes necessary to leave acting upon them and to act upon what is agreed upon, as has been explained elsewhere. The second approach is that we carry these reports upon a kind of taqiyyah, because they agree with the position of the generality, and for that reason they differ just as the generality differ regarding the maximum days of postnatal bleeding, as though each of them gave a ruling according to the school he held. The third is that the reports were issued due to a particular circumstance, namely that they were asked about a woman upon whom these days had passed and in which she had not prayed, so they said at that point that she should perform ghusl and pray. And they did not say in any of them that this was a fixed limit such that considering less than it would not be permissible. That which indicates this meaning is what...

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, who raised it, saying: A woman asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: “I used to remain seated during my nifās for twenty days, until they gave me a ruling of eighteen days.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Why did they give you a ruling of eighteen days?” She said: “Because of the hadith that was narrated from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, that he said to Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays when she gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr.” Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Asmāʾ asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم when eighteen days had already passed for her; had she asked him before that, he would have instructed her to perform ghusl and do as the mustahādah does.” We have fully covered what relates to this chapter in our larger book; whoever wants it may find it there. As for what has been narrated regarding precautionary waiting for the woman in nifās by a day or two, its meaning is what we mentioned in the ruling of the mustahādah: that she takes it into consideration when her habit in menstruation is less than ten days, but when it reaches ten, then there is no precautionary waiting. And what has been narrated that she observes precautionary waiting by the like of two-thirds of her days is also of this kind, when her habit is five or six days; likewise what has been said that she observes precautionary waiting by the like of two-thirds of the days of her nifās. All of that we have cited in our larger book and clarified the correct aspect of it there.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn ʿUbdūs, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Layth al-Murādī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about the woman in postnatal bleeding: what is the limit of her nifās such that salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon her, and what should she do? He said: There is no fixed limit for her. Thus, the correct understanding of this report is that she does not have a specific fixed limit that cannot change, increase, or decrease, because that differs according to the differing conditions of women and their habits in menstruation, and there is no single matter here upon which all of them agree alike.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning a man who has milk with him: may he perform wudu (ablution) with it? He said: No. It is only water and earth. Thus he negated that anything other than water and earth may be used for purification, by the expression “only,” because that is what is understood from it, as we have explained in the large book.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about flour: may wudu be done with it? He said: There is no harm in using it for washing and benefiting from it. So the correct understanding of his statement, 'There is no harm in using it for washing,' is that he only meant by it the washing that is beautification and rubbing the body with it, not the wudu for salat (prayer). And that which clarifies this is what...

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who applies depilatory lime, then mixes flour with oil, kneads it with it, and rubs himself with it after the depilatory in order to remove its odor. He said: There is no harm in it.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: If you are in a situation where you cannot manage anything except clay, then perform tayammum with it, for Allah, Exalted is He, is more deserving of accepting the excuse, when you do not have with you a dry garment nor felt that you are able to shake off and perform tayammum with.

And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If you are in a situation in which you find nothing but clay, then there is no harm in performing tayammum with it.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Rifāʿah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: If the ground is wet, with neither dust in it nor water, then look for the driest place you can find and perform tayammum from it, for that is an easing from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: If he is in snow, then let him look at the felt of his saddle and perform tayammum from its dust, or from something dusty. And if he is in a condition where he finds nothing but clay, then there is no harm in performing tayammum from it.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn ʿUthman, from Zurarah, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said: I said: A man entered a thicket in which there is no water, but there is mud; what should he do? He said: He performs tayammum, for it is saʿid. I said: But he is riding and cannot dismount out of fear, and he is not in a state of wudu (ablution). He said: If he fears for himself from a beast or something else, and fears the passing of the time, then let him perform tayammum: he strikes with his hand upon the felt and the pack-saddle, performs tayammum, and performs salat (prayer). So it does not contradict the report of Abi Basir and the report of Rifaʿah, for in them he said: If you are not able to reach felt or a saddle that you can shake, then perform tayammum with mud. And in this report he said: He does not perform tayammum with mud. So if he is not able to dismount due to fear, he performs tayammum from the saddle, because the proper way of reconciling the reports is that when there is dust in the felt of the saddle or the garment, it is obligatory that he perform tayammum from it and not perform tayammum from mud. Then if there is no dust in the garment in the first place, he performs tayammum with mud. But if he fears dismounting, he performs tayammum from the garment even if there is no dust in it. And that which indicates that tayammum with felt and saddle is only permissible for him when there is dust in them...

What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Tell me, a rider stopping on the way, if he is not in a state of wudu (ablution), what should he do when he is unable to dismount? He said: He should perform tayammum from the felt cloth, or his saddle, or the mane of his riding animal, for there is dust in them, and he should pray.

Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub during travel and finds nothing during the journey except snow. He said: He performs ghusl with snow or with river water.

With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mu'awiyah ibn Shurayh, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah عليه السلام while I was with him, and said: Damp cold and snow affect us, and we want to perform wudu (ablution), but we find nothing except frozen water. So how should I perform wudu (ablution)? Should I rub my skin with it? He said: Yes.

As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿUbaydī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub while traveling and finds nothing but snow or frozen water. He said: He is in the position of necessity; he performs tayammum, and I do not regard it proper that he return to this land which endangers his religion.

From him, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If snow afflicts him, then let him look to the felt of his saddle, and let him perform tayammum from its dust or from something with him.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Rifa'ah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: If he is in snow, then let him look to the felt of his saddle and perform tayammum from its dust, or from something dusty. So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the way to reconcile them is that it is obligatory upon a person to rub himself with snow or ice, since it is water, when that is possible for him and he does not fear for himself from using it; and he should not turn away from that to tayammum with earth and dust. But if that is not possible for him, and he fears for himself from using it, then it is permissible for him to turn to tayammum, just as it is permissible for him to turn from water to earth in the presence of fear. And that which indicates this is what...

Al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Alawi, from al-'Umarki, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man in janabah, or not being in a state of wudu (ablution), who does not have water with him, while he comes upon snow and earth: which of the two is better? Should he perform tayammum, or wipe his face with snow? He said: Snow is better if he moistens his head and body with it; but if he is not able to perform ghusl with it, then let him perform tayammum.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from one of them عليه السلام, who said: If the traveler does not find water, then let him search as long as there remains time. Then if he fears that the time will pass him by, let him perform tayammum and pray at the end of the time. Then if he finds water, there is no qaḍāʾ upon him, and let him perform wudu (ablution) for what he is to face thereafter.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: If a man does not find a means of purification and he is in janabah, then let him wipe from the earth and pray. Then when he finds water, let him perform ghusl, and the prayer that he performed has sufficed him.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning A man performed tayammum and prayed, then he found water. So he said: As for me, I would have done so; indeed I would perform wudu and repeat [the prayer]. The correct way to understand this report is that repetition is obligatory if he finds water while time still remains. But if he prayed at the end of the time and the time has departed, repetition is not required of him. And that which indicates this is what...

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then found water after his prayer: should he perform wudu (ablution) and repeat the salat (prayer), or is his prayer valid? He said: If he finds water before the time has passed, he performs wudu (ablution) and repeats; but if the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him. And this report does not contradict that.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام: If he finds water after having prayed with tayammum while the time still remains? He said: His prayer has been completed, and there is no repetition upon him.

And what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: A man performed tayammum and prayed, then found water while still within the time. He said: His salat has passed, and he should purify himself.

And what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man on a journey who does not find water, so he performs tayammum, then prays, then comes upon water while some of the time still remains: should he proceed on the basis of his prayer, or should he perform wudu and repeat the salat (prayer)? He said: He should proceed on the basis of his prayer, for indeed the Lord of water is the Lord of earth.

And among what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Muskan, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performed tayammum and prayed, then reached water before the time had ended. He said: There is no repetition of the salat (prayer) upon him. The proper way regarding these reports is that we take his statement, “before the end of the time,” as referring to the state of the salat (prayer), not to the finding of water; because the time of tayammum is the end of the time, as we mentioned in our major book, and reports have also already preceded indicating that. So the intended sense in the first report would be: if he comes upon water after he has prayed with tayammum within its time; and in the second report: concerning a man who performed tayammum and prayed while he was within time, then afterward found water; and it is understood as involving advancement and delay in wording. And likewise the third report, his statement: he does not find water, then prays while some of the time still remains for him, then afterward comes to water. And likewise the fourth report, his statement: concerning a man who performed tayammum and prayed before the end of the time, then reached water. If this construction is permissible in these reports, then it does not conflict with what we have mentioned, and all the reports remain sound together.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from al-'Is, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who comes upon water while he is junub, after he had already prayed. He said: He performs ghusl and does not repeat the salat (prayer).

With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who became junub, then performed tayammum with earth and prayed, then later found water. So he عليه السلام said: He does not repeat it. Indeed, the Lord of water is the Lord of earth; thus he has performed one of the two purifications.

From him, from al-Naḍr, from Ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: If a man does not find means of purification and he is junub, then let him wipe from the earth and perform salat (prayer). Then when he finds water, let him perform ghusl (ritual bath), and his salat (prayer) which he performed has sufficed him.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from one who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who is afflicted with janabah on a cold night and fears for his life if he performs ghusl. He said: He performs tayammum, and when he is safe from the cold, he performs ghusl and repeats the salat.

Sa'd also narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan or someone else, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, similarly to that. The first point regarding it is that it is a mursal report with a broken sanad/isnad, because Ja'far ibn Bashir said in the first narration, ‘from the one who narrated it,’ and in the second narration he said, ‘from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan or someone else,’ so he reported it while being doubtful. That which proceeds in this manner is not obligatory to act upon. Even if the report were sound as it stands, it would be interpreted as applying to one who made himself junub deliberately, because whoever is like that, his obligation is ghusl in every state; if he is unable, he performs tayammum and offers salat, then repeats when he becomes able to use it. And that which indicates that one whose description is such, his obligation is ghusl in every state, is...

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, raising it, who said: If he became junub, then he must perform ghusl according to what occurred from him; and if he had a wet dream, he performs tayammum.

With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad, who raised it to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a person afflicted with smallpox who is struck by janabah. He said: If he became junub himself, then let him perform ghusl; but if he had a nocturnal emission, then let him perform tayammum.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid and Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr; and Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, all together from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man who was in... a cold land, and he fears that if he performs ghusl, some hardship from the ghusl will afflict him—what should he do? He عليه السلام said: He should perform ghusl, even if what may afflict him does afflict him. He said: And he mentioned that he had been suffering severe pain, then janabah befell him while he was in a cold place, and it was a very windy, cold night. So I called the servants and said to them: Carry me and wash me. They said: We fear for you. So I said: There is no alternative. Thus they carried me, placed me upon planks, then poured water over me and washed me.

With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is affected by janābah in a cold land and cannot find water, though it may be that the water is frozen. He said: He should perform ghusl according to what is available. He informed him that he had done that and became ill for a month from the cold. He said: He performed ghusl according to what was available, for ghusl is unavoidable. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام mentioned that he had been compelled to do it while he was ill, so they brought it to him warmed, and he performed ghusl, and he said: Ghusl is unavoidable.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: May a man perform, with one tayammum, the prayer of the night and the whole day? He said: Yes, so long as he does not invalidate it or find water.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who does not find water: should he perform tayammum for every salat (prayer)? He said: No, it is in the position of water.

Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from al-ʿAbbas, from Abi Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Saʿid ibn Ghazwan, from al-Sakkuni, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: There is no harm in his performing the prayer of the night and the day with one tayammum, so long as he does not invalidate it or find water.
As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from Abī Hammām, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said: He performs tayammum for every salat (prayer) until water is found.

One may not avail oneself of tayammum except for a single salat and its supererogatory prayer. The first thing about this report is that it is a solitary report, and despite that, its wordings differ while the narrator is one; for Abū Hammām, in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, narrated it from al-Riḍā عليه السلام without an intermediary, while in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, it is from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Yet the ruling is one, and this weakens using it as proof. Moreover, the narrator of this report with this very isnad narrated the like of what we mentioned, namely the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb from al-ʿAbbās, from Abū Hammām, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar عليه السلام; and we have already cited it. Thus it is known thereby that what this report contains is an error from the narrator. And even if this report is accepted, it is possible to interpret it as referring to one who later became able to use water but did not perform wudu (ablution). In that case, it is not permissible for him to make lawful for himself, by that prior tayammum, more than a single salat, and he must renew tayammum for the prayer he is yet to perform. That which indicates this is as follows. And it was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAbbās, from Abū Hammām, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said:

What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: May a man perform the prayers of the night and the day all of them with one tayammum? He said: Yes, so long as he does not enter a state of ritual invalidation or find water. I said: If he finds water and hopes that he will be able to obtain other water, and he thinks that he will be able to get it, but when he wants it that becomes difficult for him? He said: That nullifies his tayammum, and he must repeat the tayammum. On the basis that it is possible to interpret it as a type of recommendation, like renewing wudu (ablution) for every salat (prayer), and that it is a completion.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, that he said: Water is to be sought during travel: if the land is rough, then one ghulwah, and if the land is level, then two ghulwahs. More than that is not to be sought.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from ʿAli ibn Asbat, from ʿAli ibn Salim, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, he said: I said to him: “Should I perform tayammum and pray, then afterward find water while there is still time remaining for me?” He said: “Do not repeat the salat, for indeed the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth.” Then Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi said to him: “Should I search for water to the right and to the left?” He said: “Do not search, neither to the right nor to the left, nor in a well. If you find it on the road, then perform wudu (ablution) with it; and if you do not find it, then proceed.” Thus, the proper understanding of this report is the state of fear and necessity. But when excuses are absent, then seeking is unavoidable, in accordance with what the first report contained.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: If you do not find water and you intend tayammum, then delay tayammum until the end of the time; for if water escapes you, the earth will not escape you.

With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: If the traveler does not find water, then let him seek it so long as he remains within the time. Then if he fears that the time will escape him, let him perform tayammum and pray at the end of the time. Then if he finds water, there is no makeup upon him, and let him perform wudu (ablution) for what he is to face afterward. This report does not contradict the reports we cited in the chapter on repeating the prayer, which indicate that for one who prayed and then found water while time still remained, repetition is not obligatory upon him. For it may be said: if the obligation were connected to the end of the time, repetition would have been required of him; because we have already clarified the proper understanding of those reports, and we have said that the obligation is connected to the end of the time and no other understanding is permissible. We interpreted the statement, 'while time still remained,' to be connected to the state of the prayer, not to the existence of water; and on this basis there is no contradiction at all between these reports and those. As for what is contained in the report of 'Ali ibn Salim in the first chapter from the statement of the questioner, 'Should I perform tayammum and pray, then find water while some time still remains for me?' and he said, 'Do not repeat the prayer,' its intended sense is: 'Should I perform tayammum and pray while there remains for me enough time,' meaning the amount in which he may pray, so he prays and then the time exits.

Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He said: I said to him, “A man performed tayammum, then entered into salat (prayer), and he had sought water but was unable to obtain it; then water is brought when he enters into the salat (prayer)?” He said: “He continues in the salat (prayer). And know that it is not appropriate for anyone to perform tayammum except at the end of the time.”

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀṣim, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who does not find water, so he performs tayammum and stands in salat, then a servant comes and says, 'Here is the water.' He said: 'If he has not bowed in rukuʿ, then let him turn away and perform wudu (ablution); but if he has bowed, then let him continue in his salat.'
And al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated it from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀṣim, similarly.

And Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated it from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-Luʾluʾī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀṣim, similarly; thus the basis regarding... The source of these three narrations is one, and it is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀṣim. It is possible that the intended meaning in this report is a form of recommendation rather than obligation and necessity. It is also possible that the intended meaning is that it is obligatory for him to break off if he had entered into the salat (prayer) at the beginning of the time, because we have already explained that tayammum is not permissible except at the end of the time; therefore, for that reason, breaking off became obligatory for him.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who prayed one rakʿah with tayammum, then a man came carrying two waterskins of water. He said: He cuts off the prayer, performs wudu (ablution), then builds upon the one rakʿah. The proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon one who, after praying one rakʿah, had an occurrence that invalidates wudu (ablution) forgetfully; then it is obligatory upon him to perform wudu (ablution) and build on the prayer. But if he had not invalidated it, then turning away would not have been obligatory for him; rather, he would have had to continue in his prayer. And it is not possible to say regarding this report what we said regarding others, namely that wudu (ablution) is only obligatory upon him because he entered it before the end of the time; for if that were so, then it would not be permissible for him to build on the prayer, and restarting would have been obligatory upon him. What indicates the permissibility of what we have said is when he invalidates it forgetfully.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to him regarding a man who did not find water, and the salat (prayer) became due, so he performed tayammum and prayed two rak'ahs; then he found water: should he invalidate the two rak'ahs, or cut them off and perform wudu (ablution), then pray? He said: No, rather he should continue in his salat (prayer) and not invalidate them, because he entered it while he was in a state of taharah and had performed tayammum. Zurarah said: So I said to him: He entered it while being in tayammum, then prayed one rak'ah and broke his wudu, then found water. He said: He should leave, perform wudu (ablution), and build upon what has passed of his salat (prayer) which he prayed with tayammum.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn Saʿdān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from al-Muthannā, from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed tayammum, then stood and prayed, and a river passed by him after he had prayed one rakʿah. He said: Then let him perform ghusl and begin the salat anew. So I said to him: He had already completed all of his salat. He said: He does not repeat it. So this report may be understood as meaning that he had entered into the salat before the end of the time, and thus it became obligatory for him to recommence, according to what we have said. It is also possible that it is to be understood as referring to a kind of recommendation.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Sa'id al-A'raj. He said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the leftover water of the Jew and the Christian, and he said: No.

And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Washshāʾ, from one whom he mentioned. From Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he disliked the leftover drink of the child of zina, the Jew, the Christian, the polytheist, and everyone who opposed Islam; and the most severe of that, in his view, was the leftover drink of the nāṣib.

As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man: may he perform wudu (ablution) from the jug or vessel of another when he has drunk from it, on the assumption that he is a Jew? He said: Yes. I said: from that water from which he drinks? He said: Yes. The correct way regarding this report is that it be understood as referring to one who is presumed to be a kafir, but is not known with certainty to be so; for najasah is not ruled for him except along with knowledge of his condition, and predominance of conjecture is not acted upon in this matter. Or it is understood as referring to one who had been a Jew and then accepted Islam, for there is no harm in using his leftover water, and the ruling of najasah is removed from him.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who is in an open desert land, and he becomes junub while he has nothing upon him except a garment, and he has become junub in it, and he cannot find water. He said: He performs tayammum and prays naked, standing, gesturing by indication.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated to me from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning a man whom janābah has affected while he is in the open desert, and he has only one garment upon him, and his garment has been affected by semen. He said: He performs tayammum, puts aside his garment, sits with himself drawn together, then performs salat, indicating by gesture. Thus, the proper way to reconcile the two reports is that if he is in a place where no one can see his ʿawrah, he performs salat standing; and if that is not the case, he performs salat sitting. Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb also narrated the first report with his chain, and we have mentioned it in our major book, and it says: he performs salat sitting. According to this narration, there is no contradiction between the two reports in any circumstance.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub in a garment, or urine affects it, and he has no garment other than it. He said: He prays in it if he is compelled to use it.

And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who is naked and the time for salat (prayer) has arrived, then he finds a garment, half of which has blood on it, or all of it. Should he pray in it, or should he pray naked? He said: If he finds water, he should wash it; and if he does not find water, he should pray in it and not pray naked.

And Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, who said: I asked him about a man who becomes in a state of janabah in a garment, and he has no other than it with him, and he is unable to wash it. He said: He prays in it. So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because we interpret these reports as referring to a situation in which removing the garment is not possible due to necessity. Even so, when he becomes able to wash the garment, he washes it and repeats the salat (prayer). This is indicated by what follows.

What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about a man who has only one garment, and it is not permissible for him to perform salat (prayer) in it. and he does not find water with which to wash it. How should he act? He said: He performs tayammum and offers salat (prayer), then when he obtains water, he washes it and repeats the salat (prayer).

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. He was asked about tayammum, so he recited this verse: So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows. "The male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands," and he said: Wipe over your two palms from the place of the cut. And Allah, Exalted is He, said: And your Lord is never forgetful.

With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Kahili, who said: I asked him about tayammum. He said: He struck the carpet with his hand, then wiped his face with it, then wiped his two palms, one of them over the back of the other.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abā Ja'far عليه السلام about tayammum, so he struck the ground with his two hands, then raised them and shook them off, then wiped with them his forehead and his two palms one single time.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Dāwūd ibn al-Nuʿmān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about tayammum, So he said: ʿAmmār was affected by janabah, so he rolled about as an animal rolls. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him, while jesting with him: O ʿAmmār, you rolled about as an animal rolls. So we said to him: How is tayammum? Then he placed his hands upon the ground, then raised them, and wiped his face and his hands a little above the wrists.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him how tayammum is performed, so he placed his hand upon the earth and wiped with it his face and his forearms up to the elbows. So the correct approach regarding this report is that we carry it upon a form of taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrines of the generality. And it has been said in its interpretation that what is intended by it is the ruling, not the act, because when he wipes the outer side of the palm, it is as though he washed his forearms in wudu (ablution), and thus by wiping the two palms in tayammum he attains the legal effect of washing the two forearms in wudu (ablution).

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, all together from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about tayammum. He said: He struck the ground with his two hands, then raised them and shook them off, then wiped with them his forehead and his two palms once.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام. He described tayammum: he struck the ground with his two hands, then raised them and shook them off, then wiped his forehead and his two palms once.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning tayammum. He عليه السلام said: You strike the earth with your two palms, then shake them off, and wipe your face and your two hands with them.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Layth al-Muradi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning tayammum: He said: You strike the ground with your two palms twice, then shake them off, and wipe your face and your forearms with them.

And Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Isma'il ibn Hammam al-Kindi, from al-Rida عليه السلام, who said: Tayammum is one strike for the face and one strike for the palms.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about tayammum, and he said: Two times, two times for the face and the hands. So the way to reconcile these reports is that what they contain regarding one strike is to be specified for minor ritual purity, and what they contain regarding two strikes is for major ritual purity, so that the reports do not contradict one another. And that which indicates this distinction is:

What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, 'How is tayammum?' He said, 'It is one striking for wudu (ablution) and for ghusl from janabah. You strike with your two hands twice, then shake them off once: once for the face and once for the hands. And whenever you find water, then ghusl is upon you if you are junub, and wudu (ablution) if you are not junub.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about tayammum. So he struck the ground with his two palms, then wiped his face with them. Then he struck the ground with his left hand and wiped with it from his elbow to the fingertips, once over its back and once over its palm. Then he struck the ground with his right hand, then did with his left as he had done with his right. Then he said: This is tayammum in place of that in which ghusl is required, and in wudu (ablution): the face and the two hands up to the elbows; and he omitted that over which wiping of the head and the two feet had been required, so one does not perform tayammum with earth for that.
