As for what this hadith includes, namely that he wiped from the elbow to the fingertips, once over its palm and once over its back, it is to be understood according to what we have previously mentioned regarding taqiyyah or the ruling, in accordance with what has passed in the interpretation of the report of Sama'ah. And what it includes of separating the strike of the right and the left in wiping the two hands does not require that the strikes be three, because what is considered in each one of the two strikes is that it be with both hands together; so if, in one of the two strikes, the two hands are separated, that is not contrary to that. As for the report of Dawud ibn al-Nu'man from Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام, containing the story of 'Ammar, it does not require that, in ghusl from janabah, one strike be deemed sufficient, since what is stated in it is that he placed his two hands upon the ground, then raised them and wiped with them his face and his hands slightly above the wrists. For it only reports the manner of performing the act in tayammum, and it does not say that he did that with one strike or two strikes. Since that possibility exists, we interpret the report according to what has come in the detailed reports that we have cited.

Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that ʿAli عليه السلام said: The milk of a baby girl and her urine are such that the garment is washed from them before she begins to eat, because her milk comes out from her mother’s bladder. And the milk of a baby boy—the garment is not washed from it, nor from his urine, before he begins to eat, because the milk of the baby boy comes out from the upper arms and the shoulders.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the urine of the infant. He said: “Pour water over it; but if he has already eaten, then wash it thoroughly. And the boy and the girl are equal in rule.” So this does not conflict with the first report, because the first report only negated washing the garment from it in the manner that it is washed from the urine of an adult man, or from his urine after he has eaten food, and it did not negate that water be poured over it. The ruling of the girl’s urine is not like that, because her urine must necessarily be washed. And his statement, “the boy and the girl are equal in rule,” means after eating food, and this is also indicated by that.

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a young boy who urinates on a garment. He said: Pour a little water over it, then wring it out.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about the urine of a boy that gets onto a garment, and he said: “Wash it.” I said: “What if I do not find its place?” He said: “Wash the entire garment.” So this does not contradict what we have presented before, because it is possible that by his saying, “Wash it,” he meant: pour water over it; and it is also possible that he meant the urine of one who has eaten food.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no wudu (ablution) due because of madhy from desire, nor from erection, nor from kissing, nor from touching the private part, nor from lying together; and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about madhy that comes onto the garment. He said: If you know its place, then wash it; but if its place is hidden from you, then wash the whole garment.

From him, from ʿAlī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about madhy that reaches the garment and sticks to it. He said: He washes it, and he does not perform wudu (ablution). So the apparent meaning in his saying, ‘He washes it,’ is a form of recommendation. We have already fully covered what relates to this chapter in the larger book, and in what we have mentioned here and earlier in the book there is sufficiency, if Allah wills. And this very narrator has narrated what we mentioned.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about madhy that gets onto the garment. He said: There is no harm in it. Then when we repeated the question to him, he said: He should sprinkle water on it.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to him: Blood may be on the garment while I am in salat (prayer). He said: If you see it and you are wearing another garment besides it, then cast it off and perform salat (prayer). But if you have no other garment on you, then continue in your salat (prayer), and there is no repetition required of you so long as it does not exceed the measure of a dirham. If it is less than that, then it is nothing, whether you saw it or did not see it. But if you had seen it and it was more than the measure of a dirham, and you neglected washing it and performed many prayers in it, then repeat what you performed in it.

Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir, from Ismaʿil al-Juʿfi, from Abi Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Concerning blood that is on a garment: if it is less than the measure of a dirham, then he does not repeat the salat (prayer). If it is more than the measure of a dirham and he had seen it but did not wash it until he prayed, then he must repeat his salat (prayer). But if he had not seen it until he prayed, then he does not repeat the salat (prayer).

And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I said to Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام: What do you say regarding the blood of fleas? He said: There is no harm in it. He said: I said: It becomes abundant. He said: Even if it is abundant. He said: I said: Then if a man has spots of blood on his garment and does not know about it, then he comes to know of it but forgets to wash it and so he performs salat (prayer), then remembers after he has prayed, should he repeat his salat (prayer)? He said: He should wash it and not repeat his salat (prayer), unless it is gathered together to the amount of a dirham; then he should wash it and repeat the salat (prayer).

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon them, that they said: There is no harm in a man performing salat (prayer) in a garment that has blood on it scattered like sprinkles. If its owner had seen it before that, then there is no harm in it so long as it is not gathered together to the measure of a dirham.

As for what Mu‘āwiyah ibn Ḥakīm narrated from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muthannā ibn ‘Abd al-Salām, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: Indeed, I scratched my skin and blood came out from it. So he said: If it gathers to the measure of a chickpea, then wash it; otherwise, no. So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as a kind of recommendation rather than obligation, and that does not conflict with that.

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, who said: I saw Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام praying while blood was flowing from his shanks. Because this report is to be understood as referring to that from which it is difficult to guard oneself, such as persistent wounds and boils with which precaution is not possible; and that is indicated by this.

It is narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah and Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon him, who said: I asked him about a man afflicted with sores that continue to bleed without stopping: how should he perform salat (prayer)? He said: He should perform salat (prayer), even if the blood is flowing.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Muʿallā ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I entered upon Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام while he was performing salat (prayer), and my guide said to me, 'There is blood on his garment.' Then when he had finished, I said to him, 'My guide informed me that there is blood on your garment.' He said, 'I have boils, and I do not wash my garment until they heal.'

And among what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about a man who has an ulcer or a wound and is unable to bandage it or wash its blood. He said: He should perform salat (prayer), and he should not wash his garment every day except once, for he is not able to wash his garment every hour. So this report as well is to be understood as referring to recommendation, and we have fully covered what relates to this chapter in our larger book. Whoever wants it may examine it there, if Allah wills.

Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Jaʿfar, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, that he said: There is no harm in the droppings of chickens and pigeons affecting the garment.

As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Fāris, who said: A man wrote to him asking about the droppings of chickens: is salat (prayer) permissible in it? So he wrote: No. The correct way to understand this narration is that salat (prayer) is not permissible in it when the chicken is jallāl; it is also possible that it is to be understood as a kind of recommendation, or as having been stated in taqiyyah, because that is the view of many of the ʿāmmah.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the milks of camels, cattle, and sheep, and their urine and their meat. He said: Do not perform wudu (ablution) from it, and if anything from it reaches you or a garment of yours, then do not wash it, except that you do so for cleanliness. He said: And I asked him about the urine of riding animals, mules, and donkeys. He said: Wash it. If you do not know its place, then wash the entire garment. And if you doubt, then sprinkle water over it.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Aban, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in the dung of donkeys, but wash their urine.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the urine of horses and mules, and he said: Wash whatever of it has affected you.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla, from al-Washsha', from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Abi Maryam, who said: I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: What do you say regarding the urine of riding animals and their droppings? He said: As for their urine, then wash it if it touches you; and as for their droppings, they are of lesser concern than that.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man whom some of the urine of beasts touches: should he wash it or not? He said: He should wash the urine of the horse, the donkey, and the mule; but as for the sheep and everything whose meat is eaten, there is no harm in its urine.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the urine of donkeys and mules. He said: “Wash your garment.” He said: I said, “Then what about their droppings?” He said: “That is greater than that.” Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All of these reports are to be understood as indicating a kind of karahah (dislike). What indicates that is what we have presented in our major book, and also what has preceded in this book: that regarding that whose flesh may be eaten, there is no harm in its urine and dung. Since these things are not among those forbidden in flesh, their urine and droppings would not be forbidden. This is also indicated by that.

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, concerning: the urine of riding animals touching the garment, so he disliked it. I said: Are not their meats halal (permissible)? He said: Yes, but they are not among those which Allah has made for eating. So this report came as a clear explanation of all these reports, explicitly stating the karāhah of what they contain.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about the urine of the cat, the dog, the donkey, and the horse, and he said: It is like the urine of the human being. The correct way regarding this report is that we understand his saying, 'like the urine of the human being,' as referring back to the urine of the cat and the dog, because they are among those whose flesh is not eaten. It is also possible that the basis in these hadiths is a form of taqiyyah, because they accord with the doctrines of some of the ʿAmmah, and what also indicates this is that they were issued in the mode of disapproval due to taqiyyah.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: We were at a funeral, and in front of us was a donkey that urinated. Then the wind brought its urine until it struck our faces and our clothes. So we went in to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام and informed him, and he said: There is no harm upon you.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: It makes no difference to me whether urine affected me or water, if I do not know.

ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who prays while there is excrement on his garment from a human, a cat, or a dog: should he repeat his salat (prayer)? He said: If he did not know, then he does not repeat.

From him, from Safwan, from al-'Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who prayed for days in another man's garment, then the owner of the garment informed him that he does not pray in it. He said: He does not repeat anything of his prayer.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who urinates and then a small spot of his urine reaches part of his thigh, and he performs salat (prayer), then afterwards remembers that he had not washed it. He said: He should wash it and repeat his salat (prayer).

And what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, who said: I sent a question to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام with Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn. I said: Ask him about a man who urinates, and a spot the size of a speck from his urine reaches his thigh, then he performs salat (prayer), and afterward remembers that he had not washed it. He said: He should wash it and repeat his salat (prayer).

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Concerning a man who prayed two rakʿahs in a garment in which there was a spot of janābah, then came to know, he عليه السلام said: He must begin the salat (prayer) again. He said: And I asked him about a man who prays while on his garment there is janābah or blood, until he finishes his salat (prayer), then comes to know. He عليه السلام said: His salat (prayer) has passed as valid, and there is nothing upon him.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Wahb ibn 'Abd Rabbih, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning: Janabah affects the garment, and its owner does not know of it, so he performs salat in it, then comes to know after that. He عليه السلام said: He does not repeat if he had not known. So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the way to reconcile them is that when a person knows that najasah has occurred on the garment, but is negligent in washing it and then forgets until he performs salat, repetition becomes obligatory upon him due to his negligence. But if he did not know at all until after completing the salat, repetition is not required of him. Most of the narrations that we mentioned in the larger book indicate this, and we mentioned some of them in the chapter on the rulings of blood with this detail, including the narration of Muhammad ibn Muslim, Isma'il al-Ju'fi, Ibn Abi Ya'fur, and Jamil from some of our companions, and that further clarifies it.

What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man whose garment was affected by janabah or blood. He عليه السلام said: If he knew that janabah or blood had affected his garment before he performed salat, then he prayed in it and did not wash it, then he must repeat what he prayed. But if he thought that something had affected it, then he looked and did not see anything, it suffices for him to sprinkle it with water.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Sinan, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: If blood gets on a man's garment and he prays in it while he does not know, then there is no repetition required of him. But if he knew before he prayed, then forgot and prayed in it, then repetition is required of him.

From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who sees blood on his garment, then forgets to wash it until he performs salat (prayer). He said: He repeats his salat (prayer), so that he may be attentive regarding a thing when it is in his garment, as a punishment for his forgetting.

As for what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Wuhayb ibn Ḥafṣ, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who performed salat (prayer) while there was urine or janabah on his garment. He said: whether he knew of it or did not know, he must repeat it, meaning the repetition of the salat (prayer). If he came to know, then the correct way regarding his statement, 'whether he knew of it or did not know,' is that what is intended is his state at the time he began the salat (prayer), after knowledge had already previously come to him. For whenever prior knowledge of the occurrence of the impurity had been established and he then forgot, repetition is required of him, as we have explained; and what follows further clarifies that.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Sayf, from Manṣūr al-Ṣayqal, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man was affected by janābah during the night, so he performed ghusl. Then when morning came, he looked and found janābah on his garment. He said: Praise be to Allah, who has not left anything except that it has a limit. If, when he got up, he looked and did not see anything, then there is no repetition upon him. But if, when he got up, he did not look, then repetition is upon him.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I said: My garment was affected by blood from a nosebleed or some semen, and I marked its trace until I could get water for it. Then I got it, but the time of salat (prayer) came, and I forgot that there was something on my garment, so I prayed. Then afterward I remembered. He said: You repeat the salat (prayer) and wash it. I said: What if I had not seen its place, but I knew that it had affected it, so I searched for it but could not find it, then when I had prayed I found it? He said: You wash it and repeat the salat (prayer). I said: What if I thought that it had affected it, but I was not certain of that, so I looked and saw nothing, then I prayed, and afterward I saw something on it? He said: You wash it and do not repeat the salat (prayer). I said: Why is that? He said: Because you were upon certainty regarding your taharah (ritual purity), then you doubted, so it is not appropriate for you ever to overturn certainty with doubt. I said: Suppose I know that it has affected it, but I do not know where it is so that I may wash it? He said: You wash the area of your garment which you think it has affected until you are certain of its taharah (ritual purity). I said: Is it incumbent upon me, if I doubt whether something affected it, to inspect it? He said: No. Rather, you only want to remove the doubt that has occurred within yourself. I said: What if I see it on my garment while I am in salat (prayer)? He said: You break the salat (prayer) and repeat it if you had doubted a place on it and then saw it. But if you had not doubted, then you saw it fresh, you cut off the prayer, wash it, then continue upon the salat (prayer), because you do not know—perhaps it is something that fell upon you. So it is not appropriate to overturn certainty with doubt.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man whose garment is affected by something that renders it najis, then he forgets to wash it and performs salat in it, then later remembers that he had not washed it. Should he repeat the salat? He said: He does not repeat it; the salat has passed and it has been recorded for him. So it does not contradict the distinction that we mentioned, because the correct way regarding this report is that we interpret it as referring to when the time of the salat has already passed. For whenever one forgets to wash the najasah from the garment, repeating it is only required of him so long as he remains within the time; but when the time has passed, then there is no repetition upon him. And that has already been mentioned in the narration of Abī Baṣīr. And that which indicates the distinction we mentioned is what follows.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Sulayman ibn Rushayd wrote to him, informing him that he had urinated in the darkness of the night, and that his palm was touched by the coolness of a drop of urine. He had no doubt that it had touched him, but he did not see it. He wiped it with a cloth, then forgot to wash it, and applied oil, rubbing with it his two palms, his face, and his head; then he performed wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) and prayed. So he replied to him with an answer that I read in his own handwriting: As for what you merely supposed regarding what touched your hand, it is nothing unless it is established with certainty. If you were certain of that, then it would indeed be incumbent upon you to repeat the salat (prayers) that you had performed with that very wudu (ablution), namely those of them whose time still remained; but whatever had passed beyond its time, there is no repetition required of you for it. This is because when a man's garment is najis, he only repeats the salat that is still within its time; but if he is junub or he prayed without wudu (ablution), then he must repeat the obligatory salat (prayers) that he missed, because the garment is unlike the body. So act according to that, if Allah wills.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abū Usāmah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a junub who sweats in his garment, or who performs ghusl and then embraces his wife and lies with her while she is menstruating or junub, and some of her sweat touches his body. He said: All of this is nothing.

With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked, while I was present, about a man who had become junub in his garment and then perspired in it, He said: I do not see any problem with it. He said: He sweats so much that, if he wished to wring it out, he could wring it out. He said: So Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام frowned and said: If you insist, then sprinkle it with a little water.

With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Bukayr, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The garment does not render the man junub, and the man does not render the garment junub.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a shirt in which a man sweats while he is junub, until the shirt becomes wet. He said: There is no harm in it, and if he wishes to sprinkle it with water, then let him do so.

From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Munabbih ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān al-Kalabī, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about the junub and the menstruating woman who sweat in the garment until it clings to them. He said: Indeed, menstruation and janabah, where Allah Mighty and Majestic has placed them, are not from sweat; so they do not wash their garment.

With this chain of transmission, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn 'Isa and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a menstruating woman who sweats in her clothes: may she perform salat (prayer) in them before washing them? He said: Yes, there is no harm.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A menstruating woman sweats in her garment. He said: She should wash it. I said: Then if beneath the shift there is a waist-wrapper, and the sweat only reaches what is beneath the waist-wrapper? He said: She should not wash it. Thus, the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it to mean when there is some najasah there, because in the case of a menstruating woman, what is beneath the waist-wrapper generally does not remain free of najasah. For that reason, washing the garment becomes obligatory upon her. This indicates that.

What Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a menstruating woman who sweats in a garment that she wears. He said: There is nothing upon her, unless some of her fluid or some other filth touches it; then that specific spot which was affected is to be washed.

And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a menstruating woman: should she wash the clothes that she wore during her menses? He said: She washes whatever of the blood has affected her clothes, and she leaves aside whatever is other than that. I said to him: Even though she has perspired in them? He said: Indeed, perspiration is not from menstruation.

As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū Jamīlah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Asadī al-Naḥḥās, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: If a menstruating woman wears a garment and it remains on her until she becomes pure, then she should not perform salat in it until she washes it. If she has two garments upon her, she performs salat in the upper one of them. And if she has no garment other than one garment, then she should wash it when she menstruates, then wear it; then when she becomes pure she performs salat in it, even if she did not wash it. This report may bear the meaning that we mentioned regarding the first report, and it may also be understood as being carried upon recommendation. What it contains in his saying, ‘She washes herself when she menstruates, then wears it; then when she becomes pure she performs salat in it, even if she did not wash it,’ indicates that menstruation itself does not render sweat impure, because if it were so, the state would not differ by washing before that. And that which indicates that this is to be understood as recommendation is what...

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked about a menstruating woman who sweats in her garment. He said: If it is a garment that clings to her, then I do not like that she should perform salat (prayer) in it until she washes it.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn ʿUthman, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man became junub in his garment, and he did not have any garment other than it. He عليه السلام said: He prays in it, and when he finds water, he washes it. So this report bears two possibilities. One of them—and it is the more likely—is that some najasah from semen had reached the garment; in that case, he prays in it if he does not find another and cannot remove it, and repetition of the prayer would be upon him according to what we explained earlier. And it is also possible that what is meant is when janabah from what is haram affected him and he perspired in it; then he prays in it, and when he finds water, he washes it.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a garment in which a man becomes junub and sweats in it. He said: As for me, I do not like to sleep in it; and if it is winter, then there is no problem so long as he has not sweated in it. So the import of this report is a kind of dislike, and it is explicit in that; and it is possible that it is to be understood as referring to when the janābah is from what is haram.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I asked him about a man who becomes junub in his garment: may he dry himself with it after his ghusl? He said: Yes, there is no harm in it, unless the drop of semen in it is still wet; but if it has become dry, then there is no harm. The correct understanding of what this report contains regarding the permissibility of drying oneself with the garment when the semen is dry is that this applies if he does not dry himself with the place in which the semen is found, because if he were to dry himself with that place, the najasah would spread to him when it became wet.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a dog drinking from a vessel. He said: Wash the vessel. And about the cat, he said: There is no problem in performing wudu (ablution) from what remains of it; it is only one of the beasts.

With this chain of transmission, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fadl Abu al-'Abbas, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the leftover water of the cat, the sheep, the cow, the camel, the donkey, the horse, the mules, wild animals, and beasts of prey, and I did not leave anything except that I asked him about it. So he said: There is no problem with it. Until I came to the dog, he said: It is filth, impure; do not perform wudu (ablution) with its leftover water. Pour out that water, and wash it with earth the first time, then with water.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Mu'awiyah ibn Shurayh, who said: 'Udhafir asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, while I was with him, about the leftover water of the cat, the sheep, the cow, the camel, the donkey, the horse, the mules, and the beasts of prey: may one drink from it or perform wudu (ablution) from it? He said: Yes, drink from it and perform wudu (ablution). He said: I said to him: The dog? He said: No. I said: Is it not a beast of prey? He said: No, by Allah, it is najis (ritually impure); no, by Allah, it is najis (ritually impure).
Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah, from Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: the like of it.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about wudu (ablution) from water into which a dog had lapped, or a cat, or from which a camel or a beast or something else had drunk: may wudu (ablution) be performed from it, or ghusl? He said: Yes, unless you find other than it, then avoid it. So this report is not contrary to the earlier reports, because the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as referring to when the water is kurr or more than that; and what indicates that is what...

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in the leftover water of the cat: wudu (ablution) may be performed from it and it may be drunk from. And one must not drink from the leftover water of the dog, unless it is a large basin from which water is drawn.

With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about water in which beasts urinate, dogs lap, and the person in janabah bathes. He said: If it is the measure of a kurr, nothing makes it najis.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmar, from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the urine of bats that gets onto my garment, and I look for it but do not find it. He said: “Wash your garment.”

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in the blood of fleas and bedbugs, and in the urine of bats. The correct approach regarding this narration is that we interpret it as a form of taqiyyah, because it conflicts with the foundational principles of the madhhab. For we have already explained that everything whose flesh is not lawful to eat, salat is not valid in its urine; and the bat is among those whose flesh is not eaten, so salat is not valid in its urine. The first narration explicitly confirms these principles.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Do not perform salat (prayer) in a house in which there is wine or an intoxicant, because the angels do not enter it. And do not perform salat (prayer) in a garment that wine or an intoxicant has touched until you wash it.

And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from some of those who narrated it, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: If wine or an intoxicating nabidh touches your garment, then wash it if you know its place; and if you do not know its place, then wash all of it. If you prayed in it, then repeat your salat (prayer).

With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Khayrān al-Khādim, who said: I wrote to the man, asking him about a garment that wine and pork meat had come into contact with: may one perform salat (prayer) in it or not? For indeed our companions had differed concerning it. So he wrote: one must not perform salat (prayer) in it, for it is impure.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Nabīdh has touched my garment; may I perform salat in it? He said: Yes. I said to him: A drop of nabīdh fell into a jar from which I drink? He said: Yes. Indeed, the basis of nabīdh is halal, while the basis of khamr is haram.

From him, from Aḥmad al-Barqī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Sārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: If some wine touches my garment, may I perform salat (prayer) in it before washing it? He said: There is no harm; indeed, the garment does not intoxicate.

Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, who said: A man asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, while I was with him, about an intoxicant and intoxicating nabīdh getting onto the garment. He said: “There is no harm.”

And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Sayābah, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Sārah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: We mix with the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians, and we enter upon them while they are eating and drinking, and their cupbearer passes by and pours wine onto my clothes. He said: There is no problem with it, unless you wish to wash it.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Musa al-Hannat narrated to me; he said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who drinks wine, then spits it out from his mouth and it strikes my garment. He said: There is no harm. Thus, the sound approach regarding all these reports is that we carry them upon a mode of taqiyyah, because they accord with the doctrines of many of the 'ammah. We only said that because the earlier reports conform to the outward sense of the Qur'an. Allah, Exalted is He, said: “Indeed, wine, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are filth.” So He judged wine to be impurity.

And it has been narrated from them, peace be upon them, that they said: When two hadiths come to you from us, then present them to the Book of Allah. So whatever agrees with the Book of Allah, take it, and whatever contradicts it, discard it. And these reports contradict the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, so practice should be based on other than them. And that which indicates that these reports were issued by way of taqiyyah is that...

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar; and 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I read in a letter that 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad wrote to Abū al-Hasan عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, Zurarah has narrated from Abū Ja'far and Abū 'Abd Allah عليهما السلام regarding wine that affects the garment and the foot, that they both said: There is no problem in praying in it; only its drinking has been forbidden.” And someone other than Zurarah narrated from Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام that he said: “If wine or nabidh — meaning the intoxicating kind — reaches your garment, then wash it if you know its place; and if you do not know its place, then wash all of it. If you prayed in it, then repeat your salat (prayer). So inform me which of them I should follow.” So he wrote back in his own hand عليه السلام, and I read it: “Take the statement of Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام.” Thus he instructed him to adopt the statement of Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام which entails prohibition, and to leave his statement along with the statement of Abū Ja'far عليه السلام which entails permissibility. This indicates that that earlier report was issued by way of taqiyyah, because if it had not been so, then taking both of their statements together would have been more appropriate. Moreover, in none of the later reports that we have cited is there anything stating that there is no problem with praying in garments affected by wine; rather, he was only asked about a garment touched by wine, and he said: “There is no problem with it.” It is possible that this was a negation of prohibition concerning wearing it and benefiting from it, even if salat (prayer) in it is not permissible.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Abī al-Daylam, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who drinks wine, then spat onto my garment from his saliva. He said: “It is nothing.” So there is no ambiguity in this report, because he only asked him about the saliva of a wine-drinker, and he said to him: “There is no problem with it.” Saliva does not become impure; rather, the impure thing is only the wine.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man whose garment comes into contact with the body of the dead person. He said: He should wash whatever of the garment was touched.

As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim and Abī Qatādah, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man whose garment falls upon a dead donkey: is salat (prayer) valid in it before he washes it? He said: Washing it is not required of him; let him perform salat (prayer) in it, and there is no harm. So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it to mean that when a year has passed over that and it has become bone, then washing the garment because of it is not obligatory. This is indicated by that.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about touching the bone of the dead person, and he said: If a year has passed, then there is no harm in it.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام: I asked him about a man whose garment fell upon a dead dog. He said: He should sprinkle it with water and pray in it; there is no harm. So this report clarifies that the ruling regarding the dog, whether dead or alive, is the same concerning sprinkling water on the garment that touched it when it was dry. And the first report is to be taken as specific to the body of the human being, so there is no contradiction between them in any way.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about the sun: does it purify the ground? He said: If a place is filthy from urine or something else, and the sun reaches it, then the place dries, salat on that place is permissible. But if the sun reaches it and the filthy place does not dry and remains moist, then salat on it is not permissible until it dries. And if your foot is moist, or your forehead is moist, or some other part of you that touches that filthy place is moist, then do not perform salat on that. And if something other than the sun reaches it until it dries, then that is not permissible.

And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿUmarkī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about reed mats that urine falls upon: is salat (prayer) valid upon them when they have dried without being washed? He said: Yes, there is no problem.

And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abi Bakr, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: O Aba Bakr, everything upon which the sun has shone has indeed become tahir.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, he said: I asked him about the ground and the roof that urine or something similar reaches: does the sun purify it without water? He said: How can it become pure without water? The proper understanding of this report is that it does not become pure without water so long as it remains wet. Rather, purity is judged for it when the sun has dried it.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Hamzah al-'Alawi, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali, from Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the dead person who dies while in a state of janabah. He said: One ghusl is upon him.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام concerning a dead person who died while in janabah: How should he be washed, and how much water suffices for him? He said: He is to be given one ghusl, and that suffices for both janabah and the ghusl of the deceased, because they are two sanctities that have come together in one sanctity.

Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Muthanna, from Abi Basir, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them. Regarding the junub when he dies, he said: There is nothing upon him except a single washing.

As for what Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪṣ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who dies while he is junub. He said: He is to be washed one washing with water, then after that he is washed.

It was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū al-Qāsim Saʿīd ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿĪṣ, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man dies while he is in a state of janabah? He said: He is washed for janabah, then he is washed afterward with the ghusl of the dead.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: Some of our companions informed me from ʿĪṣ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, peace be upon him. He said: When the deceased dies, then proceed with his preparation and hasten it. And when the deceased dies while in janabah, he is given one ghusl, then after that he is washed. So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the first thing about these narrations is that their basis in all of them is ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, and he is one person, and it is not permissible for one individual to oppose a large group, as we have explained elsewhere. And even if it were sound, it could be understood as carrying a sense of recommendation rather than obligation and necessity. Moreover, it is possible that the point in these reports is that the command for ghusl after washing the deceased with the ghusl of janabah was in fact directed to the one washing him, as though it had been said to him: the deceased should be washed with the ghusl of janabah, then you yourself should perform ghusl. Thus, that may be an error from the narrator or the copyist, and this very narrator has himself narrated what we have mentioned.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: When the deceased dies while in janabah, he is given one ghusl, then washing is done after that.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, who said: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام: What is the limit of the water with which the deceased is washed, just as they have narrated that the junub performs ghusl with six arṭāl and the menstruating woman with nine arṭāl? So is there a set limit for the deceased regarding the water with which he is washed? So he عليه السلام wrote: The limit of washing the deceased is that he should be washed until he becomes pure, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: O ʿAlī, when I die, then wash me with seven water-skins from the well of Ghars.

And among what was narrated by Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Fuḍayl Sukkarah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, is there a fixed limit for water? He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: When I die, draw for me six water-skins from the well of Ghars, then wash me and shroud me. So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because they are to be understood as pertaining to a kind of recommendation. For the merit in washing the deceased is that abundant and ample water be used, and the water should not be restricted therein, although if one were to suffice with the amount that purifies him, whatever is encompassed by the name of ghusl (ritual washing) would be sufficient.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man who dies and there is no one present to wash him except women. He said: His wife, or a relative if he has one, washes him, and the women pour water over him by pouring. And regarding the woman, when she dies, her husband puts his hand beneath her shirt and washes her.

And with this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about a man washing his wife. He said: Yes, from behind the garment.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked him about a woman when she dies, so he said: Her husband puts his hand beneath her shirt and washes her up to the elbows.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a woman, when she dies and there is no woman with her to perform ghusl for her, he said: her husband should insert his hand beneath her shirt and wash her up to the elbows.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a man who dies while traveling in a land where none are with him except women, he said: he is buried and not given ghusl. And a woman who is with men in that same situation is buried and not given ghusl, unless her husband is with her; if her husband is with her, he gives her ghusl from above the garment, and pours water over her by pouring, and he must not look at her 'awrah. And his wife gives him ghusl if he dies. But the woman, if she dies, is not in the same position as the man; the woman is more unpleasant in appearance when she has died.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All of these reports indicate that it is appropriate for him to wash her from over the clothes. As for the woman, then what is preferable likewise is that she wash the man from over the clothes. And that which indicates this is...

What Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Kindī, from more than one person, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dies and has no one present to perform ghusl for him except women: may the women perform ghusl for him? He said: His wife or a woman who is a mahram may perform ghusl for him, and the women should pour water over him, pouring it from above the clothes.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abū Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn 'Alī al-Washshā', from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abā 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام saying: When a man dies among women, his wife washes him. If his wife is not with him, then the one among them who is most entitled to him washes him, and she wraps a cloth over her hands, and there is no objection in that.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning A man dies and there are no ones with him except women. He said: his wife washes him, because she is still connected to him during the waiting period ('iddah). But when she dies, he does not wash her, because he is not from her in a waiting period. Because the intended meaning of his statement عليه السلام, 'when she dies, he does not wash her,' is that he does not wash her while she is stripped of her clothes; for we only allow that he wash her from beneath the clothing, and most of the preceding narrations indicate this. And the difference between the man and the woman in this matter is that the woman may wash the man unclothed, although what is more virtuous and preferable is that she cover him and then wash him. It is not the same for the man, because it is not permissible for him to wash her except from behind the clothing.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man: is it proper for him to look at his wife when she dies, or to perform ghusl for her if there is no one with her to perform ghusl for her? And about the woman: may she look at the like of that from her husband when he dies? He عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that. Rather, the woman's family only does that out of dislike that her husband should look at something of her that they dislike.

Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who goes out on a journey and his wife is with him, then she dies: may he perform ghusl for her? He said: Yes. And likewise his mother, his sister, and the like of these; he places a cloth over her 'awrah.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about a man washing his wife. He said: Yes. It is only her family that prevents her out of partisanship.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from 'Ali, from Abi Basir, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: The husband may wash his wife in travel, and the woman may wash her husband in travel, when there is no man with them. So these reports, even if they are unrestricted regarding the permissibility of the man washing the woman and the woman washing the man, we restrict them by the reports that we have previously mentioned, because when one ruling is transmitted in both restricted and unrestricted form, there is no disagreement that the unrestricted should be carried upon the restricted. Moreover, this ruling is only permissible when women are absent if the woman has died, and men are absent if the man has died. What indicates that is what we have narrated among the previous reports, and that further clarifies it.

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abī Khālid, from Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: A man does not wash a woman, unless no woman is found; and that does not contradict that.

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, who washed Fāṭimah عليها السلام? He said: That was Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. He said: It was as though I considered that a grave matter from what he said, so he said: It is as though you felt constrained by what I informed you of? I said: Indeed that was so, may I be made your ransom. So he said: Do not be constrained, for she is a Ṣiddīqah; none but a Ṣiddīq would wash her. Do you not know that Maryam عليها السلام was washed by none but ʿĪsā عليه السلام?

And what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام: that ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام instructed that an umm walad of his should perform ghusl for him when he died, so she performed ghusl for him. Because the proper way regarding these two reports is that we restrict them specifically to those two عليهم السلام. And the basis for that is what the first report contains: that there was no one there who was permitted to directly handle Fāṭimah and Maryam عليهما السلام. And likewise is the statement regarding the second report; otherwise, the fundamental principle is what we have mentioned.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام: May I be your ransom, what do you say about a woman who is on a journey with men, among whom she has no relative by kinship, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her? He said: From her, only that which Allah has made subject to tayammum is to be washed, and she is not to be touched, nor is anything of her beauties that Allah has commanded to be covered to be uncovered. So I said: Then how is that to be done with her? He said: The inner sides of her palms are washed, then her face is washed.

From him, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man washing his wife. He said: Yes, from behind the garment; he must not look at her hair nor at anything of her. And the woman may wash her husband, because when he dies she remains in a waiting period from him; but when she dies, her waiting period has ended. And about a woman who dies on a journey while there is with her no mahram and no women, he said: She is buried as she is in her clothes. And about a man who dies while there is with him no mahram and no men, he said: He is buried as he is in his clothes.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man dies during travel among women, and there is no man with them; what should they do with him? He عليه السلام said: They should wrap him up in his clothes and bury him, and they should not perform ghusl on him.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Basri, who said: I asked him about a woman who died while with men. He said: She should be wrapped and buried, and she is not to be given ghusl (ritual washing).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Regarding a man who dies while traveling in a land where none are with him except women, he said: he is to be buried and not given ghusl (ritual washing). And a woman who is with men in that same situation is buried and not given ghusl (ritual washing).
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام. Its like.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū al-Jawzāʾ al-Munabbih ibn ʿAbd Allah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: If a man dies while traveling among women, and his wife is not among them, nor any woman related to him within maḥram kinship, he said: they should wrap him from the waist to the knees, and pour water over him by pouring, and they should not look at his ʿawrah, nor touch him with their hands, and they should purify him. And if women who are maḥram relatives are with him, they should wrap him, pour water over him by pouring, and touch his body, but they should not touch his private part.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning: Concerning a man who dies while women are with him and there is no man with them, he عليه السلام said: They should pour water over him from behind the garment, wrap him in his shrouds from beneath the covering, perform salat over him in a row, and place him in his grave. And a woman who dies among men while there is no woman with them, he عليه السلام said: They should pour water from behind the garment, wrap her in her shrouds, perform salat, and bury her. So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the reports we presented earlier, because we interpret them as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation. We only prohibited a woman from washing a man when she directly handles his body; but if she merely pours water over him, then there is no harm in it and there is merit in it. As for the woman, it has also been narrated that it is permissible for men to wash from her those parts they were permitted to look at among her visible features: the face and the hands; this indicates that.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: A companion of ours went to ask Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a woman who dies among men, among whom there is no mahram. Should they perform ghusl for her while her clothes are on her? He said: Then that would lead them into that matter; rather, they should wash her two hands.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who is on a journey with men among whom there is no mahram for her, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her? He عليه السلام said: Of her, that which Allah has made subject to tayammum is to be washed, and she is not to be touched, nor is anything of her beauties to be uncovered—those which Allah has commanded to be concealed. So I said to him: How is that to be done with her? He عليه السلام said: The inner sides of her hands are washed, then her face is washed, then the outer sides of her hands are washed.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim and 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who died during a journey while no women and no mahram were with her. He said: The places of wudu (ablution) are to be washed from her, salat (prayer) is to be performed over her, and she is to be buried.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a woman who dies while no mahram is with her. He said: Her hands are to be washed. So the proper way regarding these reports is that we carry them upon a mode of recommendation, while the foundational ruling is what we have stated earlier: that she is buried and is not given ghusl in any circumstance. What further clarifies that will follow.

What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Abī Jamīlah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who died while in a place where there was no other woman with them besides her. He said to him: If there is not among them her husband or a mahram relative of hers, they should bury her in her clothes and not perform ghusl for her. But if her husband or a mahram relative of hers is with them, then he should perform ghusl for her without looking at her ʿawrah. He said: And I asked him about a man who died while traveling with women, and there was no man with them. So he said: If he does not have a wife among them, then he should be buried in his clothes and not be given ghusl. But if he has a wife among them, then he should be given ghusl while wearing a shirt, without looking at his ʿawrah.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Abī al-Jawzā', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn 'Alī, from his forefathers, from 'Alī عليه السلام, who said: A group came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: A woman has died among us, and she has no relative with her. He said: What did you do with her? They said: We poured water over her. He said: Could you not find a woman from the People of the Book to wash her? They said: No. He said: Then why did you not perform tayammum for her?

As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Ibn Bint Ilyās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام say: If a woman dies while among men, and they do not find a woman to perform her ghusl, then some of the men should wash her from behind the clothes. And it is recommended that he wrap a cloth around his hands. So this report bears two possibilities: one of them is that the man in question is her husband, for it is permissible for him to wash her as we have stated, from behind the clothes; or that he is one of her blood relatives, and that is reinforced by this.

What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who died while only women were present with him. He said: A woman who is his mahram should perform his ghusl, and the women should pour water over him, and his garment should not be removed. And if it is a woman who died among men, while there is no woman with her and no mahram for her, then she should be buried as she is in her clothes. But if a mahram of hers is with her, he should wash her from over her clothes. The second view is that this may be understood to mean that they wash her by pouring water over her, just as we mentioned regarding their washing of the man, because that has indeed been narrated. And if all of that is understood as being recommended, then the basic principle is what we stated earlier: the obligation of burying her without ghusl.

And what we have mentioned was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Khurrazad, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Abi Sa'id, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: When a woman dies among a group of people among whom she has no mahram, they pour water over her. And if a man dies among women among whom he has no mahram... Abu Hanifah said: They should pour water over him. So Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: Rather, it is permissible for them to touch of him whatever it was permissible for them to look at of him while he was alive. Then when they reach the place at which it was not permissible for them to look while he was alive, nor to touch it, they should pour water over him. So what this report includes regarding the permissibility of a woman washing, of a man, those parts at which it was permissible for her to look while he was alive is to be understood as recommendation, and the basis is what we have stated previously.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz, from 'Uthman al-Nawwa', who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: I wash the dead. He said: Do you do it well? He said: I said: I wash [them]. He said: When you wash the deceased, then be gentle with him, do not squeeze him, and do not bring anything of camphor near his hearing passages.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: When you wash your deceased, be gentle with him, do not wring him, do not press any joint of his, and do not bring any of the camphor near his ears. Then take his turban and spread it folded over his head, cast its two ends behind him, and leave his forehead uncovered. I said: And the hanut, how should I apply it? He said: It is placed in his nostrils, on the places of his sajdah, and on his joints. I said: Then the shroud? He said: You take a piece of cloth and tie his lower part with it, drawing his thighs together with it so that what is there may be kept enclosed; and what is made from cotton is better. Then he is shrouded with a qamis, a wrapping cloth, and a burd in which the shroud is gathered.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ibn Miskān, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, and he said: Sit him up and press his stomach gently, then cleanse him of what comes out from pressing the stomach. Then lay him down, then wash him: begin with his right sides, and wash him with water and al-ḥuruḍ, then with water and camphor, then wash him with pure water, and place him in his shrouds. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: What this report contains in his statement, ‘Sit him up,’ agrees with the ʿĀmmah, and we do not act upon it. As for his statement, ‘Press him,’ it is possible that it is an indication of what is wiped over his stomach in the first two washings, not the third, as we have explained in our large book.

As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah and Dhubyān ibn Ḥakīm, from Mūsā ibn Ukayl al-Numayrī, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said: There is no harm in placing the deceased between your legs and standing over him to wash him. Then when you turn him to the right and to the left, you steady him with your legs so that he does not fall upon his face. So the import of his statement عليه السلام, 'There is no harm in placing him between your legs,' is to be understood as permissibility and the lifting of prohibition, because the sunnah (prophetic tradition) and what is more virtuous is that one stand at the side of the deceased and not mount over him, as we explained in our major book.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Musallī, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUbayd, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the ghusl (ritual washing) of the deceased. He said: A cloth is placed over him, then his private part is washed, and wudu (ablution) of salat is performed for him. Then his head is washed with lote leaves and ushnan, then with water and camphor, then with pure water, and seven sound leaves from the lote tree are placed in the water.

And from him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd, from Abū Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام informed me and said: The deceased is begun with at his private part, then wudu (ablution) is performed for him like the wudu of salat (prayer), and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Muʿadhi, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Layth, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abi Bashir, from Hafsah bint Sirin, from Umm Sulayman, from the mother of Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: When a woman dies and they intend to wash her, then let them begin with her abdomen, and let it be wiped with a gentle wiping if she is not pregnant. But if she is pregnant, then do not move her. Then when you intend to perform her ghusl, begin with her lower parts, and place over her ʿawrah a concealing cloth. Then take a piece of cotton and wash her, then insert your hand from beneath the cloth and wash her with cotton three times, and do well in wiping her before performing wudu (ablution) for her. Then perform wudu (ablution) for her with water in which lotus leaves have been placed, and he mentioned the hadith.

And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn al-Rizq al-Ghamushani, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام instructed me to press his abdomen, then perform wudu (ablution) for him with ushnan, then wash his head with lote leaves and his beard, then pour some of it over his body, then rub his body with it, then pour over him three times, then wash him with pure water, then pour over him water with camphor and with pure water, and place in it seven lote leaves.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī, from some of his companions, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abū Khaythamah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, my father instructed me to wash him when he passed away, and he said to me: “Write, O my son.” Then he said: “They will command you to do contrary to what you are doing, so say to them: ‘This is the written instruction of my father, and I do not go beyond his statement.’” Then he said: “You begin by washing his hands, then perform wudu (ablution) for him as the wudu of salat (prayer), then you take lote leaves,” and he mentioned the hadith.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yaqṭīn, he said: I asked al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام about the deceased: is there the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer) in it, or not? He said: Wash the deceased. Begin with his forearms, then wash them with al-ḥuruḍ, then his face and his head with lote leaves, then water is poured over him three times. And do not wash him except while in a shirt; a man inserts his hand and pours over him from above. And something of lote leaves and something of camphor are placed in the water. And he does not press his abdomen unless he fears something nearby, in which case he wipes it gently without pressing. Then the one who washed him washes his hand before shrouding him up to the shoulders three times; then when he has shrouded him, he performs ghusl (ritual bath). So it does not contradict the earlier reports, because what the report contains is an explanation of the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, and it did not require an explanation of the details of wudu (ablution), because that is known. And it did not refrain from explaining it because it is not obligatory; rather, because of what we have stated before. As for what has been narrated in reports that the ghusl of the deceased is like the ghusl of the junub alike, then if the ghusl of janabah does not contain wudu, then likewise the ghusl of the deceased; this is opposed by the reports which were narrated stating that every ghusl contains wudu except ghusl from janabah. And if the ghusl of the deceased is other than the ghusl of janabah, then wudu must be established in it. Moreover, the intent in their saying, 'the ghusl of the deceased is like the ghusl of janabah,' is the explanation of the manner of ghusl and observing the sequence in it, because the two are of one pattern, even if one of them contains wudu and the other does not, just as the ghusl of menstruation is like the ghusl of janabah, even though it contains wudu according to what we have explained, while the ghusl of janabah does not.
