What we mentioned was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Qāsim ibn Burayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The ghusl of the deceased is like the ghusl of janābah, and if he has abundant hair, then pour extra water over him three times. And that which opposes it...

What Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān or someone else, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: For every ghusl there is wudu, except janabah; and the manner of reconciling between them is what we have mentioned previously.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarak, who said: I said to Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon a needy man? He said: There is no fitrah upon him.
From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Yazīd ibn Farqad, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon the needy person? He said: No.

From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who receives from zakat: is the sadaqat al-fiṭrah due upon him? He said: No.

ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ismāʿīl ibn Sahl, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Yazīd ibn Farqad, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, that he heard him saying: Whoever receives from the zakat, then no fitrah is due upon him. And he said: Ibn ʿAmmār said that Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: There is no fitrah upon one who receives from the zakat.

From him, from Isma'il ibn Sahl, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, 'For whom is the fitrah permissible?' He said, 'For the one who does not find [means]. And whoever it is permissible for, it is not obligatory upon him; and whoever it is obligatory upon, it is not permissible for him.'

With this chain of transmission, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is zakat due upon one who has received zakat?” He said: “As for one who has received zakat al-mal, then zakat al-fiṭrah is due upon him; but there is no zakat due on what he received, and no fiṭrah is due upon one who receives fiṭrah.”

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: Is sadaqat al-fitrah due upon a needy man? He said: There is no fitrah due upon him.

From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Yazīd ibn Farqad al-Nahdī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who receives zakat: is the sadaqat al-fitrah due upon him? He said: No.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: I said to him: Is there zakat upon one who receives zakat? He said: As for one who receives zakat on wealth, then al-fiṭrah is upon him; and there is no fiṭrah upon one who receives al-fiṭrah.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said: I said: The poor person upon whom charity is given—does he have to give Ṣadaqat al-Fiṭrah? He said: Yes, he gives from that which is given in charity to him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man and Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: A man has nothing of the fitrah except what would suffice to discharge it on behalf of himself alone. Should he give it to a stranger, or should he and his dependants eat it? He said: He should give it to some of his dependants, then the other should give it on behalf of himself; they should pass it around among themselves, so that one fitrah counts on behalf of all of them.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Sadaqat al-fitrah is upon every head among your household: the young and the old, the free and the slave, the rich and the poor. For every person there is half a sa' of wheat or barley, or one sa' of dates or raisins, for the poor among the Muslims. And he said: Dates are more beloved to me. Thus, the proper approach regarding these hadiths and others of their kind is that we interpret them as indicating a kind of recommendation, not obligation and requirement, because the obligation pertains to one who is wealthy, the least state of which is that he possesses the amount upon which zakat becomes obligatory. Whoever is not like that is encouraged to give the zakat from what he receives and what is given in charity to him, but that is not obligatory, as we have explained, and what follows further clarifies that.

What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Zakat al-fiṭrah is one sāʿ of dates, or one sāʿ of raisins, or one sāʿ of barley, or one sāʿ of dried curds, on behalf of every person, free or slave, young or old. And there is no blame upon one who does not find what he can give in charity.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yūsuf, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Bashīr, from Ḥukaym, the mu'adhdhin of Banū ʿAbs, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, His saying, Exalted is He: “And know that whatever thing you gain, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger.” He said: By Allah, it is the gain that comes day by day, except that my father made our Shi'ah exempt from that, so that they may be purified.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Upon every person who gains or earns, the khums of what he acquires is due, for Fatimah عليها السلام and for those from her heirs after her who hold her authority, the proofs over the people. That belongs exclusively to them; they place it wherever they wish. And charity has been forbidden to them. Even a tailor who sews a shirt for five daniqs—one daniq of it belongs to us, except for whomever among our Shi'ah we have made lawful for them, so that birth may be wholesome for them through it. Indeed, there is nothing before Allah on the Day of qiyamah greater than zina. Indeed, the صاحب of the khums will stand and say: My Lord, ask these people by what they made lawful marriage relations.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said: One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام: “Inform me about khums: is it due on all that a man gains, whether little or much, from all kinds [of earnings], and also upon craftsmen? So how is that?” He wrote in his own hand: “Khums is after expenses.”

ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār said: Abū ʿAlī ibn Rāshid said to me: I said to him: You ordered me to undertake your affair and to take your due right, so I informed your followers of that. Then some of them said to me: What thing is his right? So I did not know what I should answer him with. He said: khums is obligatory upon them. I said: In what thing? He said: In their goods and their estates, and upon the merchant according to his trade, and the craftsman by his hand; and that is when it is possible for them after their expenses.

ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār said: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī wrote to him: ʿAlī read to me the letter of your father regarding what he had made obligatory upon the owners of landed properties: that he obligates upon them half of one-sixth after expenses, and that whoever whose estate does not cover its own expenses is not liable for half of one-sixth nor anything else. Those with us then differed concerning that, and they said: Khums is obligatory upon landed properties after expenses—meaning the expenses of the estate and its land tax, not the expenses of the man and his dependants. So he wrote—and ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār read it: Khums is due on it after his expenses, the expenses of his dependants, and after the land tax of the ruler.

As for what al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام say: Khums is only in spoils specifically. So this report may be understood in one of two ways. The first of them is that the intended meaning in it is that khums is only in spoils specifically by the outward wording of the Qur'an, because whatever is besides spoils, the obligation of khums in it was only known through the sunnah (prophetic tradition), and it was not intended that there is no khums in that at all. And the second way is that these earnings and benefits that accrue to a person are among the spoils that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the Qur'an; and he عليه السلام clarified that in the narration that we mentioned at the beginning of the chapter.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, who said: I said to Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: What do you say about a domesticated pigeon that was slaughtered outside the sanctuary and then brought into the Haram? He said: There is no problem in eating it if he was not in ihram; but if he was in ihram, then no. And he said: If it was brought into the Haram and then slaughtered there, then indeed it was slaughtered after it had entered its place of safety.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Miskan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning: Regarding a pigeon slaughtered in the hill area, he said: A muhrim must not eat it. If it is brought into Makkah, a person who is not in ihram may eat it in Makkah. But if it is brought into the Haram alive and then slaughtered in the Haram, he must not eat it, because it was slaughtered after it had reached its place of safety.

As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A slaughtered bird was given to us as a gift in Makkah, and our family ate it. He said: The people of Makkah do not consider there to be any harm in it. I said: Then what do you say? He said: Its price is upon them. So it is understood to mean that it had been slaughtered within the Haram. There is nothing in the report stating whether it was slaughtered in the hill or in the Haram. When that is not apparent from its wording, and there are reports that contain a detailed clarification of its meaning, then acting upon them is more appropriate. We have already presented some of them, and what follows increases that clarification.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Ubayd ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Shurayh, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: These people bring us these partridges. He said: Do not approach them in the Haram except what has been slaughtered. I said: We instruct them to slaughter them there. He said: Yes, eat it and feed me from it.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام was asked about game that was shot in the non-sacred area, then brought into the Haram while it was still alive, so he said: If he brings it into the Haram while it is alive, then its meat and keeping it become forbidden. And he said: Do not buy it in the Haram except that which had been slaughtered, and had been slaughtered in the non-sacred area, then brought into the Haram; then there is no harm.

From him, from Safwan, from Alāʾ ibn Razīn, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: Game is hunted in the area outside the Haram, slaughtered outside the Haram, then brought into the Haram and eaten? He said: Yes, there is no harm in it.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said: If the muhrim slaughters game, neither the halal person nor the muhrim may eat it, and it is like carrion. And if game is slaughtered in the Haram, then it is carrion, whether one in a halal state slaughtered it or one in a haram state.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: If the muhrim slaughters game outside the Haram, then it is carrion; neither one who is non-muhrim nor a muhrim may eat it. And if the non-muhrim slaughters game within the interior of the Haram, then it is carrion; neither one who is non-muhrim nor a muhrim may eat it.

As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: When the muhrim kills game, its compensation is due upon him, and he gives the game in charity to a poor person.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Isa and Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: If the muhrim strikes game within the Haram while he is in ihram, then he should bury it, and no one should eat it. But if he strikes it outside the Haram, then one who is halal may eat it, while the expiation is upon him.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a muhrim who struck game from which a non-muhrim eats. He said: There is nothing upon the non-muhrim; rather, the fidyah is only upon the muhrim.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan and Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who caught game while he was in ihram: may one who is not in ihram eat from it? He said: There is no problem; the expiation is only upon the muhrim. So the proper way regarding these reports is that we understand them to mean that when the muhrim catches the game while it is still alive, it is permissible for the non-muhrim to slaughter it and eat it; rather, what is forbidden to him is what the muhrim himself slaughters. It is also possible that what is meant by them is that he kills the game by shooting it, and it is only forbidden when he takes it while it is alive and then slaughters it. On this interpretation, there is no contradiction between the reports, and that which confirms the earlier reports...

What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Khallād al-Sindī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning: About a man who slaughtered a pigeon from the pigeons of the Haram, he said: upon him is the fidyah. I said: Then may he eat it? He said: No. I said: Then may he discard it? He said: If he discards it, then another fidyah is upon him. I said: Then what should he do with it? He said: He should bury it.

From him, from Abī Aḥmad, from one whom he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: The muḥrim strikes game and then offers compensation for it—may he eat it, or should he discard it? He said: Then there would be another compensation upon him. I said: So what should he do with it? He said: He should bury it. Were it not that it takes the ruling of carrion, according to what the earlier reports contain, he would not have ordered him to bury it; rather, he would have ordered him to feed it to those who are not in iḥrām.

Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Whenever a slave strikes game while he is in ihram, then it is upon the master, if he had given him permission to enter ihram.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a slave who caught game while he was in ihram: is there anything of the fidyah upon his master? He said: No, there is nothing upon his master. So it does not contradict the first report, because the proper way regarding it is that we understand it to mean that if he entered ihram without his master's permission, then whenever the matter is like that, there is nothing upon his master.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, said: I said to al-Rida عليه السلام: Should I perform istilam of the Yemeni, the Syrian, and the Western corners? He said: Yes.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would not touch except the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner; he would kiss them both and place his cheek upon them, and I saw my father doing that.

From him, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I was performing tawaf around the House when suddenly a man was saying: Why is it that these two corners are touched, while these two are not touched? So I said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم touched these two and did not approach these two, so do not approach them when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not approach them. Jamil said: And I saw Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام touching all of the corners. So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because both of them contain the account of the action of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. And it is possible that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not touch them because in touching them there is not the same merit and encouragement toward reward as there is in touching the Iraqi Corner and the Yemeni Corner. And he did not say that touching them is prohibited or disliked. For this reason, Jamil related that he saw Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام touching all of the corners; and had it not been permissible, he عليه السلام would not have done it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who performed eight circuits of the House in the obligatory tawaf. He said: He repeats until he completes it properly.

Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: The obligatory tawaf, if you add to it, is like the obligatory salat (prayer): if you add to it, then repetition is required of you; and likewise the sa'y.

As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf in eight circuits. He said: He should add six more to it.

From him, from 'Abbas, from Rifa'ah, who said: Ali عليه السلام used to say: If he performs eight circuits, then let him complete fourteen. I said: Should he perform four rak'ahs? He said: He performs two rak'ahs. Thus, the correct way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as applying to one who did that absentmindedly or forgetfully; for it is permissible for him to complete fourteen circuits. Repetition is only obligatory upon him when he did that deliberately. This is indicated by that.

I heard him say: Whoever performs tawaf around the House and mistakenly continues until he enters the eighth, then he should complete fourteen circuits, then perform two rak'ahs. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report contains, and the report before it, in his statement 'he performs two rak'ahs,' does not contradict what he narrated.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Ali عليه السلام performed eight circuits, then added six, then performed four rak'ahs, because if the matter is as we have described, then he prays two rak'ahs upon completing the two tawafs and proceeds to the sa'y. Then when he finishes his sa'y, he returns and prays two other rak'ahs. Thus he has acted upon both reports together, and that which indicates this is:

What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام performed the obligatory tawaf as eight circuits. So he left seven, and built upon one, and added six to it. Then he performed the two rakʿahs behind the Maqam. Then he went out to al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. When he finished the saʿy between them, he returned and performed the two rakʿahs that he had left at the first Maqam.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Abū Kahmas, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot and performed eight circuits of tawaf. He said: If he remembers before reaching the Corner, then let him stop, and it has sufficed for him. But if he does not remember until he reaches it, then let him complete fourteen circuits and perform four rakʿahs. So this does not contradict the earlier report that we presented from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from his statement: Whoever performs tawaf of the House and mistakenly continues until entering the eighth, then let him complete fourteen circuits. That report is general, while this report is detailed, and ruling by the detailed report takes precedence over the general one, as has already been explained.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from ʿAli al-Jarami, from them both, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: A man performed tawaf and did not know whether he had completed seven circuits or eight. He said: He should perform two rakʿahs.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who doubts during the obligatory tawaf. He said: He repeats it whenever he doubts. I said: May I be your ransom, what if he doubts in the supererogatory tawaf? He said: He builds upon the lesser number. So it does not contradict the first report, because this report is to be understood as referring to one who doubted before completing seven, since one in that state has no way to ascertain seven circuits with certainty. The first report refers to one who has completed seven circuits and is certain of them, and only doubted about what was in excess of them, so he does not pay attention to that doubt. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned is...

What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf around the House, then did not know whether he had completed seven circuits or eight. He said: As for the seven, he is certain of them; rather, his doubt fell upon the eighth, so let him perform two rakʿahs.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurarah, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: It is only disliked that a man combine between two weeks and two tawafs in the obligatory rite; as for the supererogatory rite, there is no problem.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Nahdī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: Joining [the rounds] is only disliked in the obligatory [tawaf]; but as for the supererogatory, then no, by Allah, there is no harm in it.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man performing tawaf who joins two sets of seven circuits together. He said: If you wish, I can narrate to you from the people of al-Madīnah. He said: So I said: No, by Allah, I have no need for that, may I be made your ransom. Rather, narrate to me that by which I practice religion before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: Do not join two sets of seven circuits together. Rather, each time you complete one set of seven circuits, perform two rakʿahs. As for the supererogatory tawaf, I have at times joined three and four. So I looked at him, and he said: Indeed, I am with these people.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: We asked him about combining in tawaf between two circuits of seven and three. He said: No; it is only one set of seven and two rakʿahs. And he said: My father used to perform tawaf with Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm and would combine, but that was only from him due to the circumstance of taqiyyah.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: A man asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who performs all the circuits of tawaf together and joins them. He said: No; each week is followed by two rakʿahs. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام only joined them because he was performing tawaf with Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm due to the circumstance of taqiyyah. So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the interpretation in them is one of two possibilities: one of them is that the earlier reports are to be understood as referring to merit and recommendation, while the later reports indicate mere permissibility without merit. The second possibility is that in these reports, joining was only considered disliked in the tawaf of obligation, not in the tawaf of supererogation. That was already clarified in the first two narrations at the beginning of the chapter in his statement: joining between two tawafs is only disliked in an obligatory tawaf, but as for supererogatory tawaf, there is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performs tawaf without wudu (ablution): is that tawaf counted? He said: No.

And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, that he was asked: “Are the rites performed without wudu (ablution)?” So he said: Yes, except for tawaf, for in it there is salat (prayer).

From him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked one of the two of them, peace be upon them, about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf while he was not in a state of ritual purity. He said: He should perform wudu (ablution) and repeat his tawaf; and if it was supererogatory, he should perform wudu (ablution) and pray two rak'ahs.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī al-ʿAmrakī ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performed tawaf and then remembered that he was without wudu (ablution). He said: He breaks off his tawaf and does not count it. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports, even if they are unrestricted, or most of them indicate that he repeats the tawaf, we carry them upon the tawaf of obligation, because of what we have previously presented from the hadith of Muḥammad ibn Muslim, and because it differentiated the ruling of the two tawafs: the tawaf of obligation and the tawaf of supererogation. Ruling by what is detailed is more appropriate than ruling by what is general, and what follows further clarifies that.

What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man performed tawaf without wudu (ablution). He said: If it was voluntary, then let him perform wudu (ablution) and pray.

From him, from al-Nakhaʿī, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: Indeed, I perform the supererogatory tawaf while I am without wudu (ablution). He said: Perform wudu (ablution) and pray, even if you did so deliberately.

Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who circumambulated the House for three circuits, then found the House empty and entered it. What should he do? He said: He must repeat his tawaf, and he has opposed the sunnah.

From him, from ʿAlī, from both of them, from Ibn Muskan, who said: He narrated to me from one who asked him about a man who performed three circuits of the obligatory tawaf around the House, then found an empty space in the House and entered it. He said: He has invalidated his tawaf and opposed the sunnah, so he must repeat it.

From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. Concerning a man who performed one circuit or two circuits, then went out with another man regarding his need, he said: If it was a supererogatory tawaf, he builds upon it; and if it was an obligatory tawaf, he does not build upon it.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Abī ʿAzzah, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام passed by me while I was in the fifth circuit of the tawaf, and he said to me: Go along so that we may return here to a man. I said: I am in five circuits; should I complete my seven-circuit tawaf? He said: Cut it short, and preserve it from where you cut it, until you return to the place from which you cut it, then continue upon it.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abbas, from Abdullah al-Kahili, from Abu al-Faraj, who said: I performed tawaf with Abu Abdillah عليه السلام for five circuits. Then I said: I wish to visit a sick person. So he said: Mark your place, then go and visit him, then return and complete your tawaf. So this does not contradict the earlier reports, because completion was only permitted for him since he had performed more than half. Repetition is required when what was done was less than half. No one may say: Why did you not also interpret the two reports as permitting completion in the tawaf of supererogatory worship, while requiring repetition in the tawaf of an obligatory act in every case? Because if that were so, there would be no difference between when it was more than half and when it was less than that, whereas they عليهم السلام did distinguish between the two tawafs when it was less than half and when it was more than that. This indicates that when it exceeds half, there is no difference between them regarding the permissibility of building upon it, except insofar as it is tawaf of an obligation, for the tawaf of supererogatory worship may be built upon in every case. Moreover, reports have also been transmitted mentioning the tawaf of obligation and that it is permissible to build upon it, so it is not possible to interpret them according to this view. He narrated that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Abi Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Sukayn ibn 'Ammar, from a man among our companions who was known by the kunyah Abu Ahmad, who said: I was with Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام in the tawaf, and his hand was in my hands, or my hands were in his hand, when a man with a need came to me. So I gestured to him with my hand and said to him: Stay as you are until I finish my tawaf. Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said during the tawaf: What is this? I said: May Allah set you aright, a man came to me with a need. He said to me: Is he a Muslim? I said: Yes. He said: Go with him concerning his need. I said to him: May Allah set you aright, and should I cut off the tawaf? He said: Yes. I said: Even if it is the obligatory one? He said: Yes, even if you are in the obligatory one. He said: And Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: Whoever walks with his Muslim brother regarding a need, Allah writes for him one million good deeds, erases from him one million evil deeds, and raises for him one million degrees.

As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from some of our companions, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, he said: Regarding a man who is performing tawaf and then a need arises for him, he said: there is no harm in his going to attend to his own need or the need of someone else and cutting off the tawaf. And if he wants to rest and sit, there is no harm in that. Then when he returns, he resumes his tawaf. If it is a supererogatory tawaf, he may resume after one circuit or two circuits; but if it is an obligatory tawaf, then if he went out for a need with another man, he does not resume from where he left off. And not even in his own need. So this is not contrary to what we have mentioned, because what he meant by saying, 'he does not resume,' is that he does not resume after one circuit or two circuits, distinguishing between obligatory tawaf and supererogatory tawaf as we have explained. Do you not see that he said at the beginning of the report, 'there is no harm in that; then when he returns, he resumes his tawaf'? Then he began a ruling specific to supererogatory tawaf, which is the permissibility of resuming when less than half has been completed. Then he followed that by his saying, 'and if it is in an obligatory tawaf, he does not resume,' meaning what was permitted for him in the supererogatory tawaf. And that is not contrary to what we have said.

Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام about the sick person: should tawaf of the Ka'bah be performed on his behalf? He said: No; rather, he should be taken around it.

From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The sick person who is overcome, and the one who has fainted, the stoning is done on his behalf and he is carried around for tawaf.

And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a sick man who arrives in Makkah and is unable to perform tawaf around the House, nor the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He said: He should be carried and taken around, trailing the ground with his feet, until his feet touch the ground during the tawaf. Then he should be made to stand at the base of al-Safa and al-Marwah if he is ill.
From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man for whom tawaf is performed and for whom the stoning is done. He said: Yes, if he is unable.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, he said: The overpowered sick person and the one who is unconscious may have the stoning done on his behalf and the tawaf performed on his behalf. So this does not contradict the reports we presented earlier, because the proper way regarding it is that we understand it to apply to one who cannot maintain his taharah and from whom ritual invalidation is not secure, such as one afflicted with abdominal illness and those similar to him. This indicates that.

What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he said: The one suffering from an abdominal illness and the one with a fracture are to have tawaf performed on their behalf, and ramy is done on their behalf.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered that tawaf be performed on behalf of one afflicted with an abdominal illness and one with a fracture; meaning that one in such a condition also has tawaf performed on his behalf only when he has been waited for some days, then does not recover, and missing it is feared; in that case, it is permissible that tawaf be performed on his behalf. This indicates that.

What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad al-Aḥmasī, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Bajalī, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, or wrote to him, about Saʿīd ibn Yasār: he had fallen from his camel and could not hold himself upright because of his abdomen. Should I perform the tawaf on his behalf and do the saʿy? He said: No; rather, leave him. If he recovers, he himself should make it up; otherwise, then you make it up on his behalf.

From him, from al-Lu'lu'i, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام about a man who performed part of his obligatory tawaf of the House, then fell ill with an illness in which he was unable to complete his tawaf, He said: If he has performed four circuits, he should instruct someone to perform three circuits on his behalf, and his tawaf is complete. But if he has performed three circuits and is unable to complete it, then this is among the things over which Allah has overcome him, so there is no harm in delaying it for a day or two. If recovery comes and he is able to perform tawaf, he should perform a full seven-circuit tawaf. But if his illness continues, he should instruct someone to perform a full tawaf on his behalf and to perform the salat on his behalf, and he has exited from his ihram. And the same applies in the stoning of the jamarat. And in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ya'qub: and he himself performs the salat.

Ahmad ibn 'Abdun informed me, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, who said: 'Ali ibn Ya'qub Abu al-Hasan al-Baghdadi narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Isma'il ibn Salih al-Saymari, who said: al-Hasan ibn Rashid narrated to me, who said: Hammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me, who said: Some of our companions narrated it; he mentioned it from al-'Abd al-Salih, Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal, peace be upon him. He said: Khums is in five things, and khums is divided into six shares. And he mentioned the detailed explanation of that in a lengthy report which we have cited in our large book, to its end; so whoever wants it may consult it there.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Jārūd, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: When booty came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, he would take its choicest part, and that belonged to him. Then he would divide what remained into five fifths, then take its khums, then divide the four fifths among the people. Then he would divide the khums that he had taken into five fifths: he would take the share of Allah for himself, then divide the four fifths among the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer; and he mentioned the hadith to its end. So this does not contradict the first report stating that the khums is divided into six shares, because it only contains an account of the action of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and that he عليه السلام only used to take from the khums the share of Allah and his own share, and these are two shares out of six. It is possible that he was content in that regard with the khums so that the remainder might be left in full for the other deserving recipients. There is nothing in the report stating that this is a binding rule in every circumstance such that مخالفة of it is impermissible; rather, it is only an account of his action عليه السلام, and that does not conflict with what the first report indicated regarding the obligation of dividing the khums into six shares. We have fully discussed what relates to this chapter in our larger book, so whoever wants it may find it there.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about speaking during tawaf, reciting poetry, and laughing during the obligatory prayer or other than the obligatory prayer: is that proper? He said: There is no harm in it, and poetry—whatever of it is of the kind in which there is no harm—likewise.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿImrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl, that he asked Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and he said: I had performed one circuit for him, then dawn rose. He said: Perform salat (prayer), then return and complete your saʿy. And in the obligatory tawaf, it is not appropriate that one speak in it except with du'a (supplication), dhikr (remembrance) of Allah, and recitation of the Qur'an. He said: And in the supererogatory one, a man may meet his brother, greet him with salam, and speak to him about something from the affairs of the Hereafter and the world. He said: There is no harm in it. So the proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation, not obligation and requirement.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from ‘Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: He was asked about a man who was unaware that he had to perform tawaf of the House until he returned to his family. He said: If it was due to ignorance, he must repeat the hajj, and a badanah is also due upon him.

Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who was unaware that he had to perform the obligatory tawaf of the House. He said: If that was due to ignorance in the hajj, he must repeat it, and a camel is due from him.

As for what ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said: I asked him about a man who forgot the obligatory tawaf until he returned to his land and had relations with women. What should he do? He said: He should send a sacrificial offering; if he omitted it during hajj, he should send it in hajj, and if he omitted it during ʿumrah, he should send it in ʿumrah, and he should appoint someone to perform on his behalf what he omitted of his tawaf. The correct way regarding this report is that we understand it to refer to Tawaf al-Nisa', because whoever omits Tawaf al-Nisa' forgetfully may appoint another in his place to perform his tawaf, and that is not permissible in the tawaf of hajj. This is indicated by what follows.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from a man, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man forgot the ṭawāf al-nisāʾ until he had gone in to his wife? He said: Women are not lawful for him until he visits the House. And he said: He should instruct that it be performed on his behalf if he does not perform hajj; and if he dies before ṭawāf is performed on his behalf, then his guardian or someone else should perform it on his behalf.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who arrives in Mecca while the heat has become intense upon him, so he performs tawaf around the Ka'bah and delays the sa'y until it becomes cooler. He said: There is no problem with it, and sometimes I have done it. He said: And sometimes I saw him delaying the sa'y until the night.

From him, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked one of the two of them, peace be upon them, about a man who performed tawaf around the House and became exhausted: may he delay the tawaf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah? He said: Yes.

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, who said: I asked him about a man who performed tawaf around the House and became fatigued: may he delay the tawaf between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah until tomorrow? He said: No. So this does not conflict with the first two reports, because the concession in the two reports only came regarding delaying the saʿy for an hour or two. But as for delaying it until the next day, it is not permissible, according to what the last report contains.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said: I said: A man was performing tamattu' and then entered into ihram for hajj. He said: He is not to perform tawaf of the House until he comes to 'Arafat. So if he performs tawaf before coming to Mina without an excuse, that tawaf is not counted.

As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man performing tamattuʿ who enters into iḥrām for hajj, then performs tawaf and saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah before his departure to Minā. He said: There is no harm in it. So it does not conflict with the first report, because it is to be understood as applying to the elderly man, the fearful person, and the woman who fears menstruation. But when that excuse is absent, there is consensus that it is not permissible in any circumstance; this indicates that.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Marrār, from Yūnus, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Khāliq, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: There is no objection to the elderly shaykh, the sick person, the woman, and the infirm bringing forward the tawaf of hajj before they depart to Minā.

From him, from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the mutamattiʿ: if he is an elderly shaykh, or a woman who fears menstruation, may he hasten the tawaf of hajj before coming to Minā? He said: Yes, whoever is like that may hasten it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: For the one performing ifrad hajj, when he has performed tawaf of the House and the safa and the marwah, should he bring forward Tawaf al-Nisa'? He said: No. Tawaf al-Nisa' is only after he comes to Mina.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from his father, who said: I heard Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام saying: There is no objection to advancing the tawaf of hajj and the tawaf of al-nisa' before the hajj, on the Day of al-Tarwiyah, before his departure to Mina. Likewise, there is no objection for one who fears some matter such that returning to Makkah will not be possible for him, to perform tawaf and bid farewell to the House, then proceed on as he is from Mina, if he is fearful. Thus, the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as referring to the compelled person who is not able to return to Makkah, according to what he mentioned in the report. That is not contradictory to the first report, because that one is to be understood as applying to the state of choice.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one whom he mentioned, said: I said to Abī al-Hasan عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, a mutamatti' visited the House and performed the tawaf of hajj, then performed Tawaf al-Nisa', then performed sa'y. So he said: The sa'y is not to be except before Tawaf al-Nisa'. So I said: Is anything due upon him? He said: There is no sa'y except before Tawaf al-Nisa'.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who performed the tawaf of hajj and the tawaf al-nisa' before performing sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He said: It does not harm him; he performs sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and he has completed his hajj. So this does not contradict the first report, because this report is to be understood as referring to one who did that deliberately.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Isma'il ibn Riyah, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about one performing the standalone 'umrah: is the tawaf al-nisa' obligatory upon him? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from 'Umar ibn Yazid or someone else, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The mu'tamir performs tawaf, does sa'y, and shaves. He said: and after shaving, he must necessarily perform another tawaf.

As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū Khālid, the mawlā of ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about one performing a separate ʿumrah: is ṭawāf al-nisāʾ required upon him? He said: ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is not required upon him. So this does not contradict what we presented earlier, because this report is to be understood as referring to one who entered for a separate ʿumrah during the months of hajj, then wanted to make it into tamattuʿ for hajj; that is permissible for him, and ṭawāf al-nisāʾ does not become binding upon him. This is because ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is only binding on the one performing the separate ʿumrah apart from hajj; when he converts it into tamattuʿ leading to hajj, its obligation falls from him. This indicates that.

What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, who said: Abū al-Qāsim Mukhalled ibn Mūsā al-Rāzī wrote to the man, asking him about the detached ʿumrah: is ṭawāf al-nisāʾ required upon the one performing it, and also regarding the ʿumrah by which one performs tamattuʿ up to the hajj? So he wrote: As for the detached ʿumrah, ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is required upon the one performing it. But as for the one by which tamattuʿ is performed up to the hajj, ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is not required upon the one performing it.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from al-ʿAbbās, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Abū Ḥārith asked him about a man who performed tamattuʿ with the ʿumrah up to the hajj, then performed tawaf, saʿy, and taqsir: is the tawaf al-nisāʾ required upon him? He said: No. Tawaf al-nisāʾ is only after returning from Minā.

As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Sayf, from Yūnus, from the one who narrated it, he said: Ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is only upon the pilgrim performing hajj. So this does not conflict with what we have mentioned, because this narration is mawqūf, not musnad to any of the Imams عليهم السلام. When it is not musnad, acting upon it is not obligatory, because it is possible that this was a view of Yūnus which he chose according to some of his opinions, just as he chose many views to which we are not bound to adhere, due to the establishment of proof for their invalidity.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan and Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' until he returned to his family. He said: Women do not become lawful for him until he visits the House. If he dies, then his guardian or someone else should perform it on his behalf. But as long as he is alive, it is not valid that it be performed on his behalf. And if he forgot the jamarat, the two are not equal: indeed, the throwing is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), while the tawaf is an obligation.

As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot ṭawāf al-nisāʾ until he returned to his family. He said: He should send someone, and ṭawāf should be performed on his behalf. If he dies before ṭawāf is performed on his behalf, then his guardian should perform ṭawāf on his behalf. The proper way to understand this report is that it is to be applied to one who is unable to return, for it is permissible for him to instruct someone to perform ṭawāf on his behalf. But as for one who is able to do that, returning is obligatory upon him, as indicated by what the first report contained.

What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning: About a man who forgot Tawaf al-Nisa' until he came to al-Kufah, he said: Women do not become lawful for him until he performs tawaf of the House. I said: Then if he is not able? He said: He should instruct someone to perform tawaf on his behalf.

Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said: He was asked about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf and did not perform the two rakʿahs until he had performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Then he performed tawaf al-nisāʾ and did not perform the prayer for that tawaf until he remembered while he was at al-Abṭaḥ. He said: He should return to the Maqām and perform two rakʿahs.

From him, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf and did not perform the two rakʿahs until he had gone between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then he performed the tawaf of النساء and did not perform the two rakʿahs until he remembered while he was at al-Abṭaḥ, so he prayed four. He said: He should return and pray four at the Maqām.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who forgot to perform the two rak'ahs of the obligatory tawaf, and did not remember until he arrived at Mina. He said: He should return to Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام and perform them there.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, who said: Someone narrated to me from the one who asked him about a man who forgets the two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer until he leaves, so he said: He appoints another. Ibn Muskan said: And in another hadith, if he has passed the miqat of the people of his land, then let him return and pray them. For Allah, the Exalted, says: “And take from the مقام of Ibrahim a place of prayer.”

As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from al-Nakhaʿī, Abū al-Ḥusayn, who said: Ḥanān ibn Sadīr narrated to us, saying: I made the visitation and then forgot the two rakʿahs of the tawaf. Then I came to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while he was at Qarn al-Thaʿālib, so I asked him, and he said: Pray in your place.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abi al-Sabbah, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who forgot to perform the two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام during the tawaf of hajj and 'umrah, so he said: If he is still in the town, he should perform two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And take from Maqam Ibrahim a place of prayer.” And if he has already departed, then I do not instruct him to return.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Durust, from Ibn Muskan, who said: 'Umar ibn Yazid narrated to me from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام.' That he asked him about a man who forgot to perform the two rak'ahs, the obligatory two rak'ahs, at Maqam Ibrahim عليه السلام until he reached Mina. He said: 'He should perform them in Mina.'

From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Muthannā, who said: I forgot to perform the two rakʿahs of the tawaf behind the Maqam until I reached Minā. So I returned to Mecca and performed them, then I went back to Minā. We mentioned that to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: Why did he not perform them wherever he remembered it? Thus, the proper way regarding these reports is that we interpret them as referring to one for whom returning to Mecca is difficult and who is not able to do so; and that which indicates this is as follows.

What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot to perform the two rakʿahs of the obligatory tawaf behind the Maqam. While Allah, the Exalted, has said: “And take from the Maqam of Ibrahim a place of prayer.” Until he has departed. So he عليه السلام said: If he has departed, then I do not wish to impose hardship upon him, and I do not order him to return; rather, he should pray wherever he remembers. And it is possible that the earlier reports are to be understood as referring to merit and recommendation, while the later reports indicate permissibility and the lifting of prohibition.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abu al-Fadl al-Thaqafi, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Pray the two rakʿahs of the obligatory tawaf, whether it be after dawn or after afternoon.

From him, from Muhammad, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the two rakʿahs of the obligatory tawaf. He said: Do not delay them for even an hour; when you have performed tawaf, then perform salat (prayer).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abi 'Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: I have not seen the people take from al-Hasan and al-Husayn عليهما السلام anything except the salat (prayer) after al-'asr and after al-ghadah in the tawaf of the obligatory rite.

As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the two rakʿahs of the obligatory tawaf. He said: Their time is when you finish your tawaf, and I consider it disliked at the yellowing of the sun and at its rising.

From him, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: One of the two عليهما السلام was asked about a man who enters Makkah after the morning prayer or after the ʿaṣr prayer, He عليه السلام said: He performs tawaf and prays the two rakʿahs so long as it is not at sunrise or at the time of its reddening. Thus, the correct approach regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as a form of taqiyyah, because that accords with the position of the generality. As for the last report, it is possible to interpret it as referring to the two rakʿahs of supererogatory tawaf, for that is disliked during these two times according to what most narrations indicate. And that which indicates this is:

What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbbās, from Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about tawaf after al-ʿAṣr, and he said: Perform tawaf and pray two rakʿahs before salat al-Maghrib at sunset. And if you perform another tawaf, then pray the two rakʿahs after al-Maghrib. And I asked him about tawaf after al-Fajr, and he said: Perform tawaf until, when the sun has risen, then perform the rakʿahs.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the prayer of the supererogatory tawaf after ʿAṣr, and he said: No. So I mentioned to him the statement of some of his forefathers: The people did not take anything from al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام except the prayer after ʿAṣr in Makkah. He said: Yes, but when you see the people turning toward something, then avoid it. I said: These people do it. He said: You are not like them.

As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about one who performs tawaf after al-ghadāh or after al-ʿaṣr while he is in the time of prayer: may he perform the two rakʿahs of tawaf, whether it was supererogatory or obligatory? He said: No. So the correct understanding of this report is what it contains: that it was the time of an obligatory prayer, and thus it was not permissible for him to perform the two rakʿahs of tawaf except after he had finished the present obligatory prayer.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṣabbāḥ al-Azraq, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said: Indeed, among the most intense matters the people will face on the Day of qiyamah is that the صاحبُ الخُمُسِ will stand and say: O my Lord, my khums. Yet we have made that lawful for our Shiʿah so that their births may be pure and their children may be purified.

From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUmar ibn Abān al-Kalbī, from al-Ḥalabī, from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Do you know from where zina entered upon the people?” I said, “I do not know.” He said: “It came from the side of our khums, the khums of Ahl al-Bayt, except for our good and pure Shiʿah; for it is made halal for them and for their births.”

From him, from Abi Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abi Salamah Salim ibn Mukram, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: A man said to him, while I was present, "Make the private parts lawful for me." So Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام was alarmed. Then a man said to him, "He is not asking you to waylay the road. Rather, he is only asking you about a servant-girl whom he buys, or a woman whom he marries, or an inheritance that comes to him, or trade, or something that was given to him." He said, "This is halal for our Shi'ah—the present among them and the absent, the dead among them and the living; whoever is born from among them until the Day of qiyamah, it is halal for them. By Allah, it is not halal except for the one for whom we have made it halal. And by Allah, we have not given anyone a guarantee of protection, nor is there between us and anyone any favoritism, nor does anyone have a covenant with us."

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from al-Hakam ibn 'Ilba' al-Asadi, who said: I was appointed over al-Bahrayn and acquired abundant wealth there. I spent from it, purchased many landed properties, bought slaves and slave-mothers who bore children for me. Then I set out for Makkah, carrying my dependents, the mothers of my children, and my wives, and I carried the khums of that wealth. I entered upon Abu Ja'far عليه السلام and said to him: “I was appointed over al-Bahrayn and acquired abundant wealth there, and I purchased properties, bought slaves, bought slave-mothers who bore children for me, and I spent from it. This is the khums of that wealth, and these are the mothers of my children and my wives, and I have brought it to you.” So he said to him: “Indeed, all of it belongs to us, and I have accepted what you have brought. I have made lawful for you the mothers of your children, your wives, and what you spent, and I guarantee for you, upon myself and upon my father, Paradise.”

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Basir, Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: The people were ruined through their bellies and their private parts, because they did not render to us our right. Lo, indeed our Shi'ah, with regard to that, and their fathers, are in absolution.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of our companions, from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: Whoever we have made lawful for him something that came to him from the acts of the oppressors, then it is lawful for him; and whatever of that we have forbidden, then it is forbidden for him.

Sa'd, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from al-Sanadi ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn Umar al-Zayyat, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: All people live off the surplus of the wrong done to us, except that we have made that lawful for our Shi'ah.

Saʿd, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a man from the cloth merchants entered upon him and said: “May I be your ransom, profits, wealth, and trade come into our hands, and we know that your right in them is established, yet we have been falling short regarding that.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “We would not be dealing fairly with you if we were to impose that upon you today.”

As for what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Ṭabarī narrated, he said: A man from the merchants of Fāris, from among the mawālī of Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, wrote to him asking his permission regarding the khums. So he wrote back to him: In the Name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful. Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, Generous. He has guaranteed reward for obedience and punishment for مخالفة. No wealth is lawful except by a means that Allah has made lawful. Indeed khums is our support for our religion, for our dependents, for our mawālī, and for what we ransom and purchase of our honor from those whose assault we fear. So do not withhold it from us, and do not deprive yourselves of our du'a as long as you are able to give it. For indeed paying it is the key to your sustenance, the purification of your sins, and what you send ahead for yourselves for the day of your need. And the Muslim is the one who fulfills to Allah what he has covenanted upon, and the Muslim is not the one who answers with the tongue while opposing with the heart. And peace.

Muhammad ibn Yazid said: A group from Khurasan came to Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام and asked him to absolve them from the khums. So he said: How far-fetched this is! You devote affection to us with your tongues, while you withhold from us a right that Allah has appointed for us and appointed us for, and that is the khums. We do not absolve any one of you from it.

And Ibrāhīm ibn Sahl ibn Hāshim narrated, saying: I was with Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام when Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad ibn Sahl entered upon him, and he used to administer the endowment for him in Qum. He said: “My master, absolve me concerning ten thousand dirhams, for I have spent them.” So he said to him: “You are absolved.” Then when Ṣāliḥ left, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “One of them pounces upon the wealth of the family of Muḥammad, and their orphans, their needy ones, their poor, and their stranded travelers, and takes it; then he comes and says: ‘Absolve me.’ Do you think he supposed that I would say: ‘I will not do so’? By Allah, Allah will surely question them about that on the Day of Resurrection with an intense questioning.” So the proper way of reconciling these narrations is what our Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, used to maintain: that whatever has been reported of concession regarding taking khums and disposing of it was reported only in the matter of marriages specifically, due to the reason previously mentioned in the reports from the Imams عليهم السلام, so that the births of their Shiʿah may be wholesome; and it was not reported concerning wealth. And whatever has been reported of strictness regarding khums and exclusive authority over it, then it pertains to wealth. And that which indicates this meaning...

What Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام wrote to him, and I myself read his letter to him on the road to Makkah. He said: What I have made obligatory in this year of mine—and this is the year two hundred and twenty only—is for a certain reason among the reasons; I dislike explaining the entire reason for fear of its spreading, and I shall explain the remainder of it to you, if Allah wills. Indeed my followers—may Allah set them aright—or some of them, have fallen short regarding what is obligatory upon them. I came to know that, and I wished to purify them and cleanse them by what I have enacted in this year of mine concerning the khums. Allah, Exalted is He, said: “Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them, and pray for them; indeed your prayer is a comfort for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. Do they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities, and that Allah is the Oft-Returning, the Merciful? And say: Act, for Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers; and you shall be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.” And I did not make that obligatory upon them in every year, nor do I make anything obligatory upon them except the zakat that Allah has made obligatory upon them. I have only made khums obligatory upon them in this year of mine regarding gold and silver upon which a year has passed. I did not make that obligatory upon them concerning goods, nor vessels, nor riding animals, nor servants, nor profit earned in trade, nor landed property—except for an estate whose matter I shall explain to you—as a lightening from me for my followers and as a favor from me upon them, because of what the ruler seizes from their wealth and because of what befalls them in their persons. As for spoils and gains, they are obligatory upon them in every year. Allah, Exalted is He, said: “And know that whatever you gain of anything, then indeed for Allah is its fifth, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, and the orphans, and the needy, and the traveler, if you believe in Allah and what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met. And Allah is Powerful

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two — meaning Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon them. He said: The month of Ramadan is affected by deficiency just as the other months are affected. So when you have fasted twenty-nine days and then the sky becomes cloudy, then complete the count as thirty. 2- ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Mufaḍḍal, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him. He was asked about the crescents. He said: They are the crescents of the months. So when you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. I said: What if the month was twenty-nine days — should I make up that day? He said: No, unless upright witnesses testify for you. If they testify that they had seen the crescent before that, then make up that day. 3- From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him. He said: Fasting is based on sighting, and breaking the fast is based on sighting; and sighting is not that one person sees it, nor two, nor fifty. 4- From him, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Rifāʿah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him. He said: The fasting of the month of Ramadan is by sighting, not by conjecture. The month of Ramadan may be twenty-nine days, and it may be thirty; it is subject to what affects the months in terms of completion and deficiency. 5- From him, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ayyūb and Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar, peace be upon him. He said: When you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. It is not by opinion nor by supposition, but rather by sighting. He said: And sighting is not that ten stand looking, then one says, 'There it is,' while nine look and do not see it. When one sees it, ten and a thousand see it. And when there is an impediment, then complete Shaʿbān as thirty. 6- al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ and Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, all together from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, peace be upon him. He was asked about the crescents, so he said: They are the crescents of the months. So when you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. I said: What if the month was twenty-nine

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani, who said: I wrote to him while I was in al-Madinah, asking him about the day concerning which there is doubt as to whether it is from the month of Ramadan: should it be fasted or not? So he wrote: Certainty is not entered by doubt. Fast upon sighting, and break the fast upon sighting. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Tusi said: The reports in this chapter are too many to be counted. We have cited a large portion of them in our major book, and have limited ourselves here to the amount that we have mentioned so that the book may not become too lengthy.

From the Book of Sawm (fasting), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, who said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: The people say that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days more often than he fasted thirty. He said: They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast less than thirty days until he was taken, and the month of Ramadan has not diminished, since Allah created the heavens, from thirty days and a night.

And it was narrated through another route, and it is: al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥudhayfah, from his father, from Muʿādh, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The people narrate that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days. He said: Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: No, by Allah, the month of Ramaḍān has not diminished, since Allah created the heavens and the earth, from thirty days and thirty nights.
And it was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The month of Ramaḍān is thirty days; it never decreases.

And he narrated it through another route, with wordings that add and omit compared to what preceded. He narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah, from his father, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: The people narrate among us that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted like this and this and this—and he gestured with his hand, placing one palm over the other—ten and ten and nine, more often than he fasted like this and this and this, meaning ten and ten and ten. He said: So Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast fewer than thirty days, and the month of Ramadan has not decreased from thirty days since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

And he narrated it through another route, from Abū ʿImrān al-Munshid, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “No, by Allah, the month of Ramadan has not diminished, nor does it ever diminish, from thirty days and thirty nights.” So I said to Ḥudhayfah: “Perhaps he said to you, ‘thirty nights and thirty days,’ as people say, the night comes before the day.” Ḥudhayfah said to me: “This is how I heard it.” This report is not sound for acting upon for several reasons. One of them is that the text of this report is not found in any of the compiled foundational books; rather, it is only found among anomalous reports. Another is that the book of Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr is free of this hadith, and it is a well-known, famous book; if this report had been authentic from him, he would have included it in his book. Another is that this report has differing wordings and disturbed meanings. Do you not see that Ḥudhayfah at one time narrates it from Muʿādh ibn Kathīr from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and at another time narrates it from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام without an intermediary, and at another time gives legal opinion by it from himself and does not ascribe it to anyone? This type of discrepancy is among what weakens objection by means of it and reliance upon its like. Another is that even if it were safe from all that we have mentioned, it would still be a solitary report that establishes neither knowledge nor practice, and solitary reports may not be used to object against the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the mass-transmitted reports that we have mentioned. And even if it were safe from all of that as well, there would still not be in its purport anything requiring acting upon numerical reckoning rather than the crescent sightings. I shall clarify the aspect of that, if Allah wills. As for the hadith narrated by al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥudhayfah from his father from Muʿādh ibn Kathīr, that he said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “People say that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine more often than he fasted thirty.” He said: “They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, from when Allah commissioned him until Allah took him, did not fast less than thirty days, and the month of Ramadan has not diminished, since Allah created the heavens and the earth, from thirty days.” This only indicates the denial

As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The people say that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days more often than he fasted thirty days. So he said: They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast except complete months. And that is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “and that you complete the number.” Thus, the month of Ramaḍān is thirty days, Shawwāl is twenty-nine days, and Dhū al-Qaʿdah is thirty days and never decreases; because Allah, the Exalted, says: “And We appointed for Mūsā thirty nights.” And Dhū al-Ḥijjah is twenty-nine days. Then the months are upon that pattern: one full month and one deficient month, and Shaʿbān is never completed.

And this hadith was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: The people narrate that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted the month of Ramadan twenty-nine days more often than he fasted thirty days. He said: They lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast except complete, and the obligations are not deficient. Indeed, Allah created the year as three hundred and sixty days, and He created the heavens and the earth in six days, so He withheld them from the three hundred and sixty days; thus the year is three hundred and fifty-four days, and the month of Ramadan is thirty days. And he continued the hadith to its end.
