And the dislike in the first report referred to pure silk.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad or another, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about what is permissible for a woman to wear while in the state of Ihram. He said: All garments, except the two gloves, the burqa' (head veil), and silk. I said: She may wear khazz (silk-like fabric). He said: Yes. I said: But its warp is ibrisam (raw silk), and it is silk. He said: As long as it is not pure silk, there is no objection.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The woman in ihram should not wear jewelry, and there is no objection to the pattern/design being in the garment itself.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Safwan ibn Yahya and Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no harm in a woman wearing the two khalkhals (ankle bracelets) and the mask (face veil), and this does not contradict the first report, because the dislike in the first report was only directed towards what was not the custom of women among the jewelry. As for what has become their custom, there is no harm in it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who has jewelry, anklets, musk, and earrings made of gold and silver on her; does she enter the state of ihram while wearing them, and she had been wearing them in her house before her pilgrimage? Should she remove them when she enters ihram, or leave them as they are? He said: She enters ihram while wearing them and keeps them on, without displaying them to the man in her carriage and during her journey.

Musa ibn al-Qasim said: Ibn Jabala narrated to us from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a woman who performs Hajj al-Tamattuʿ, then becomes menstruating before she performs the Tawaf al-Ifadah (of the House), so she departs for ʿArafāt. He said: Her Hajj becomes a Hajj al-Qirān (or rather, the text implies the status changes, but the ruling is discussed). I said: Is there something upon her? He said: Blood that she pours, and it is her sacrifice (Uḍḥiya). Muhammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His (the Imam's) statement 'upon her is blood that she pours' is to be understood as recommended (istibḥāb) rather than obligatory (wujūb), because when the Tamattuʿ is lost, her Hajj becomes Mufrad, and the Mufrad is not required to offer a sacrifice, as we have clarified. This indicates what we said regarding recommendation.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a woman who enters Mecca performing Tamattu' Hajj and menstruates before she becomes free (from Ihram); when does her Tamattu' status end? He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The fading of the sun on the Day of Tawreeyah. And Musa (peace be upon him) said: The morning prayer on the Day of Tawreeyah. I said: May I be your ransom, most of your followers enter on the Day of Tawreeyah, perform Tawaf and Sa'i, then enter Ihram for Hajj. He said: The fading of the sun. I mentioned to him the narration of Ajlan, Abu Salih, and he said: No. When the sun fades, the Tamattu' ends. I said: Then is she still in her Ihram, or does she renew her Ihram for Hajj? He said: No, and she remains in her Ihram. I said: Then is there a sacrifice (Hady) upon her? He said: No, unless she wishes to volunteer (for an extra sacrifice). Then he said: As for us, when we see the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah before we enter Ihram, the Tamattu' has passed us by.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from some of his companions, from Abi Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman comes performing Tamattu' Hajj, then she becomes menstruating before she performs Tawaf al-Ifadah (the circumambulation for release) with the Kaaba, so her purity falls on the night of Arafat.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she knows that she will become pure, perform Tawaf with the House, and be released from her Ihram, and join the people, then let her do so.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Durust al-Wasiti, from 'Ajlan Abu Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'A woman performing Tamattu' arrived in Mecca and saw blood (menses). He said: She performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, then sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf with the House (Kaaba). If she does not become pure, then when it is the Day of Tashriq (13th of Dhul-Hijjah), water is poured over her, and she pronounces the Talbiyah for Hajj from her house and goes out to Mina, and completes all the rituals. When she returns to Mecca, she performs two Tawafs and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. When she does that, everything becomes permissible for her except the marital bed of her husband.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Ajlan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman performing Tamattu' Hajj arrived in Mecca and saw blood (menses), what should she do? He said: She should perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah and sit in her house. When she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf with the House. If she does not become pure, then when it is the Day of Tawriyah, water is poured over her, she pronounces the Talbiyah for Hajj, and goes out to Mina. She completes all the rituals. When she does that, everything becomes permissible for her except the marital bed of her husband. And I said: Abdallah ibn Salih and I heard this Hadith in the Mosque. Abdallah went to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and came out to me, saying: I asked Abu al-Hasan about the narration of Ajlan, and he narrated to me something similar to what we heard from Ajlan. The explanation for these two narrations is one of two things: One is that they do not indicate that her Tamattu' has been completed, and it is permissible that one in her state should act according to what both narrations contain, and her Hajj becomes Qada' (individual/single) rather than being Tamattu'. Do you not see the first narration from his saying 'When she arrives in Mecca she performs two Tawafs'? If the meaning was the completion of Tamattu', there would be three Tawafs upon her. But she is only required two Tawafs and one Sa'i because her Hajj has become individual (Qada'). His saying in the two narrations 'She performs Sa'i between Safa and Marwah' is either to be understood as recommended (Istihbab) or applied to one who wishes to return to the status of those who are Muhrim (in Ihram). For we have explained in our Great Book that whoever performs Sa'i between Safa and Marwah has become Muhrim, unless he is driving a Hady (sacrificial animal), or his command to enter Ihram for Hajj afterwards is valid, because by Sa'i she has entered the state of being Muhrim, so she needs to restart Ihram for Hajj. The other explanation is to apply them to one who had performed more than half of the Tawaf, then saw blood. For if that is the case, she is in the position of one who has completed her Tamattu' and that is complete for her. This indicates that.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ishaq, from someone who asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who circumambulated the House four circuits while she was performing Umrah, then she had her menses, he said: She completes her circumambulation, and Umrah is not incumbent upon her, and her Tamattu' is complete, and she may circumambulate between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and that is because she added to half, and her Umrah has passed, and she will resume after Hajj, and the latter is confirmed by what the two reports contained of ordering her to perform Sa'i, for if the meaning was not what we mentioned of adding to half, that would not be permissible, because Sa'i is not except after circumambulation, as we clarified, and that which indicates that.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān said: It was narrated to me by Ishaq ibn 'Ammār from 'Umar ibn Yazīd who said: I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman He said: She completes all the rituals, except that she does not perform tawaf between Ṣafā and Marwah I said: For some of what she makes up from the rituals is greater than Ṣafā and Marwah, namely the standing at 'Arafāt; so why is it that she makes up the rituals but does not perform tawaf between Ṣafā and Marwah? He said: Because Ṣafā and Marwah, she can perform tawaf upon them whenever she wishes, whereas these standing places (like 'Arafāt and Muzdalifah), she cannot make them up if they pass her by

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who circumambulates between al-Safa and al-Marwah while she is menstruating; he said: No. Because Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.' The basis of inference from these two narrations is that they only prevented her from walking (sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah because she had not yet circumambulated (tawaf). And the nature of sa'y is that it occurs after tawaf. And they did not prevent her from sa'y because of her being a menstruating woman. Because we have clarified that purity (taharah) is not a condition for the validity of sa'y, although it is preferable.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Durust, from 'Ajlan, Abu Salih, that he heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a woman performs 'Umrah and then falls ill before she performs Tawaf, she advances the Sa'i and performs the rituals (Manasik); when she becomes pure and departs from Hajj, she makes up the Tawaf of 'Umrah, the Tawaf of Hajj, and the Tawaf of the Women, then she is released from all restrictions. The correct interpretation in this report is what we said in the two preceding reports, namely that we interpret it as referring to one who performed more than half of the Tawaf, for whom Sa'i is valid and she counts it; and his statement in the report 'she performs the Tawaf of 'Umrah' means the completion of the Tawaf of 'Umrah, not its beginning, and that which indicates this...

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman performing Tamattu' Hajj: if she enters the state of Ihram while pure, then menstruates before completing her Tamattu', she performs Sa'i but does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure, then she completes her Tawaf, and her Tamattu' is complete. And if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'i, nor does she perform Tawaf until she becomes pure. Thus, he (peace be upon him) clarified in this narration the correctness of what we mentioned, because he said: if she enters Ihram while pure, she performs Sa'i; and if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'i, nor does she perform Tawaf. Had the meaning been what we mentioned, there would be no difference between the two states. The difference exists because when she enters Ihram while pure, it is permissible that her menstruation occurs after completing the Tawaf or after passing through half of it; at that time, it is permissible for her to advance the Sa'i and make up what remains of the Tawaf upon her. But if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she has no way to perform any of the Tawaf, so consequently the Sa'i is also withheld. And this is clear, and praise be to Allah. And that which also indicates that it is permissible for her to perform Sa'i if she has completed the Tawaf or has performed more than half of it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who performed Tawaf with the House, then became menstruating before she performed Sa'i, he said: She performs Sa'i. I asked him about a woman who performed Tawaf between al-Safa and al-Marwa, then became menstruating between them, he said: She completes her Sa'i, and that does not invalidate it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah and Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a woman menstruates while she is performing Tawaf around the House or between Safa and Marwa, and she has passed half, she marks that place; when she becomes pure, she returns and completes the remainder of her Tawaf from the place she marked. And if she cut off her Tawaf in less than half, she must restart the Tawaf from the beginning. Because what this report encompasses specifically applies to Tawaf and not Sa'i, for we have clarified that it is permissible for a woman to perform Sa'i while menstruating or without Wudu. And this report, although Tawaf and Sa'i are mentioned in it, it is not impossible that the ruling that follows specifically applies to Tawaf according to what we have presented, and that which confirms what we mentioned regarding the permissibility of Sa'i for the menstruating woman.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who runs between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. He said: Yes, by my life, the Messenger of Allah commanded Asma' bint Umays to perform Ghusl, use Istithfar (place a cloth to stop the flow), and perform Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.

And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who performed three circuits or fewer of the tawaf, then saw blood. He said: She retains her place; when she becomes pure, she performs the tawaf and counts what has passed. The correct interpretation of this report is that we understand it as referring to the tawaf of the voluntary (nafl) prayer, because we have clarified that it is permissible to build upon it even if it is less than half. And similarly for the man when he becomes junub, his ruling is the same as the menstruating woman's, on equal footing.
Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The divorced woman does not perform Hajj during her waiting period.

From him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Safwan, from Abu Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: As for the woman whose husband dies, she goes out for Hajj and 'Umrah, but the divorced woman does not go out, because Allah, the Exalted, says: 'And they should not go out [of their houses] unless they have been divorced during a journey.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: The divorced woman performs Hajj during her waiting period. The appropriate interpretation of this report is to understand it as referring to the Hajj of Islam (obligatory), because in the Hajj of Islam there is no obedience to the husband required of her. Rather, she is not permitted to go out except with his permission, or if she is in a waiting period where he has granted permission, regarding the Hajj of voluntariness. This indicates that.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from he who mentioned him, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorced woman, does she perform Hajj during her waiting period? He said: If she is newly divorced (has not performed Hajj before), she performs Hajj during her waiting period. And if she has already performed Hajj, she does not perform Hajj until she completes her waiting period. And this indicates that there is no obedience due to the husband from her in the Hajj of Islam.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from 'Ulaya from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a woman who had not performed Hajj and had a husband, and he refused to give her permission for Hajj, so her husband was absent; is she permitted to perform Hajj? He said: No, his obedience is due from her in the Hajj of Islam.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Sa'id ibn Yasar from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever dies and has not performed the Hajj of Islam, and left nothing except enough for the cost of Hajj, then his heirs have more right to what he left; if they wish, they perform Hajj on his behalf, and if they wish, they consume it.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who instructed that Hajj al-Islam be performed on his behalf, but he left only fifty dirhams in total. He said: Hajj will be performed on his behalf from some of the stations that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) designated, from the nearby ones, so as not to contradict the first report. For the reasoning in this report is that we apply it to the one upon whom Hajj was obligatory, but he delayed it, then died without performing Hajj al-Islam. In that case, Hajj is performed on his behalf from some of the stations, because that runs the course of a debt upon him, and he left only the amount of what is due upon him, so his debt is paid with it. And the first report applies to the one upon whom Hajj was not obligatory; therefore, whatever of that specified amount he leaves, his heirs are more entitled to it, because nothing was obligatory upon him that needed to be paid on his behalf.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the first part of the night in the month of Ramadan, and delayed the ritual bath (ghusl) until the dawn (fajr) broke. He said: 'He completes his fast, and there is no make-up (qada) required of him.'

From him, from al-Baraqi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sulayman ibn Abi Zaynab, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), asking him about a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the month of Ramadan from the beginning of the night, and delayed the ghusl (ritual bath) until the dawn broke. He wrote back to me in his own handwriting, and I recognized it, while he was in the midst of performing ghusl from his janabah, completing his fast, and there was nothing upon him.

From him, from Sa'd ibn Isma'il, from his father Isma'il ibn Isa, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who became junub in the month of Ramadan and slept deliberately until morning; what is upon him? He said: This does not harm him, according to what his father (peace be upon him) said. He said: Aisha said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) became junub from intercourse, not from wet dream. He said: He does not break his fast and it does not matter. And a man who became junub and remained sleeping until morning; what is obligatory upon him? He said: Nothing upon him, he performs ghusl. And a man who became junub in the last part of the night and rose to perform ghusl but did not find water, so he went to seek it or sent someone to bring it to him, and it was difficult for him until morning; what should he do? He said: He performs ghusl when it comes, then he prays.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman ibn Isa, from al-Samma' ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him about a man who incurred janabah (major ritual impurity) during the night in Ramadan, so he slept knowing about it, and did not wake up until dawn overtook him. He said: He must complete his fast and make up one other day. I said: If that is the case for the man while he is making up the days of Ramadan? He said: Let him eat on that day and make it up, for it is not like Ramadan; none of the months are like Ramadan.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife during the month of Ramadan, or who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity), then slept until morning deliberately. He said: He completes that day, and upon him is its qada (making up the fast). The rationale in these two reports is that we interpret them as referring to one who awakens after his sleep, then delays the ghusl (ritual bath), and then sleep overtakes him until morning; for him is obligatory the qada of that day due to his negligence. And if he had not awakened at all, and sleep continued with him, then qada would not be obligatory upon him, according to what the earlier reports contained, and that which indicates this is what has been narrated.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Ibn Abi Ya'fur said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man becomes junub in the month of Ramadan, then he wakes up, then he sleeps until morning. He said: He completes his day and makes up one other day. If he does not wake up until morning, he completes his day and it is valid for him.

From him, from Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who experiences janabah (major ritual impurity) during Ramadan, then sleeps before performing ghusl (ritual bath). He said: 'He completes his fast and makes up that day, unless he awakens before the rise of Fajr (dawn). If he waits for water to be heated or drawn, and Fajr rises, then he does not make up that day.'

From him, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man becomes junub at the beginning of the night, then sleeps until morning in the month of Ramadan. He said: There is no penalty upon him. I said: But he woke up, then slept again until morning. He said: He must make up that day as a penalty.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the night of Ramadan, then deliberately omitted the ghusl (ritual bath) until dawn broke. He said: He must free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. He said: And he said: It is fitting that I do not think he will ever attain it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: He narrated to me Sulayman ibn Ja'far, from the Faqih (peace be upon him), who said: If a man becomes junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the night of Ramadan and does not perform ghusl until he reaches the morning, then upon him is the fasting of two consecutive months along with the fasting of that day, and he does not attain the reward (fadl) of that day.

From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah, from some of his freedmen, who said: I asked him about the nocturnal emission of the fasting person. He said: If he emits semen during the day in the month of Ramadan, he is not permitted to sleep until he performs the ritual bath. And if he emits semen at night in the month of Ramadan, he should not sleep until he performs the ritual bath, except for a short while. Whoever becomes junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) in the month of Ramadan and sleeps until morning, then upon him is freeing a slave or feeding sixty poor people, and he must make up that day and complete his fasting, and it will never catch up to him (i.e., the missed day is not counted as part of the six days of Shawwal or similar compensations if applicable, but here implies the specific expiation is for the delay). The meaning in these narrations is that we interpret them as referring to one who deliberately leaves the bath until morning, for upon him is one of these expiations. And the first narrations include one who sleeps intending to bathe before dawn, but sleep continues until morning. There is no contradiction between them in any case, nor does that contradict [this interpretation].

Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Ja'far, from Sa'd ibn Isma'il ibn Isa, from his father, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who became junub in the month of Ramadan and slept intentionally until morning, what is upon him? He said: This does not harm him, he does not break his fast, and he is not concerned, for my father (peace be upon him) said: Aisha said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became junub from intercourse, not from wet dream. Because it carries two meanings: one is that it was a way of exiting through taqiyya (dissimulation), for that is the narration of the general public from Aisha, and for that reason he (peace be upon him) also narrated it from her, and did not narrate it from his fathers (peace be upon them). And if it were sound, the correct view in it is: that whoever sleeps intentionally and his sleep continues until the rise of dawn, nothing is incumbent upon him. Rather, the qada (making up the fast) and kaffarah (expiation) are incumbent upon the one who intentionally leaves the ghusl, not the one who intentionally sleeps. And in the report it is not stated that he intentionally left the ghusl.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Habib al-Kha'thami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray the night prayer in the month of Ramadan, then become junub (in a state of major ritual impurity), then deliberately delay the bath until the dawn breaks.

And what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad from Habib al-Kha'thami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray the night prayer in the month of Ramadan, then become junub (in a state of major ritual impurity), then deliberately delay the bath until the dawn breaks. Therefore, the approach regarding these two narrations is to carry them upon a type of taqiyya (divine precaution/concealment) as we have clarified, because that is the narration of the general public from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And it is possible, while accepting its authenticity, that the reason for the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) deliberate delay of the bath was due to an excuse, either from cold or from lack of water and waiting for it, or for something else, and that is permissible in case of necessity as we have clarified.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi Khalid, said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf in a general manner, so he said: 'Hajj is performed on his behalf with whatever remains of his third.'

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn that he said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I have been compelled to ask you.' He said: 'Ask.' I said: 'Sa'd ibn Sa'd instructed that Hajj be performed on his behalf in a general manner, without specifying anything, and we do not know how that is to be understood.' He said: 'Hajj is performed on his behalf as long as he has wealth, so this does not contradict the first report, because that which is his wealth is one-third, and that is that by which the bequest is valid, and whatever exceeds it, the bequest is not valid by it, and that is what the first report encompassed.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the unmarried man performing Hajj on behalf of the deceased. He said: Yes, if the unmarried man does not have enough to perform Hajj for himself, then if he has enough to perform Hajj for himself, it is not valid for the deceased until he performs Hajj from his own wealth. And it is valid for the deceased if the unmarried man has wealth, and if he does not have wealth.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died without having performed the Hajj of Islam, and he had wealth, he said: A 'sarurah' (female slave or dependent woman) performs Hajj on his behalf, if she has no wealth of her own.

And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Rabi' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: There is no harm if a person who cannot afford Hajj (al-sarurah) performs Hajj on behalf of another person who cannot afford it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, who said: I wrote to him asking him about a man who was single (sarur) and had never performed Hajj, who performed Hajj on behalf of another single man who had never performed Hajj. Does that one Hajj suffice for each of them for the Hajj of Islam, or not? Make that clear to me, O my master, if God wills. He wrote back: That does not suffice. Therefore, the meaning in this report is that we should interpret it as: if the single man has wealth, then that one Hajj does not suffice for him. And we have narrated it in detail in the report of Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf. It is also possible that his saying 'That does not suffice' means for the one who performs Hajj when he becomes wealthy, because whoever performs Hajj on behalf of another and then becomes wealthy, Hajj becomes obligatory upon him. This indicates that.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Adam ibn Ali, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever performs Hajj on behalf of a person who does not have the wealth to perform Hajj with, it suffices for him until God grants him the means to perform Hajj and it becomes obligatory upon him.

And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Hajj of the poor (al-sarurah) is valid for him and for whoever performs Hajj on his behalf; it does not contradict the first report because the meaning of his statement 'it is valid for him' is as long as he is poor and has no wealth. When he becomes wealthy, Hajj becomes obligatory upon him, according to what the first report contained. And we said this because it is ambiguous and open to interpretation, while the first report is detailed, and ruling based on the detailed report regarding the ambiguous one is more appropriate.

And as for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Bakr ibn Salih, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'My son is with me, and I have ordered him to perform Hajj on behalf of my mother. Will one Hajj suffice for her?' He wrote back: 'No.' And his son was a 'sarrurah' (one who performs Hajj for others) and his mother was a 'sarrarah' (one for whom Hajj is performed). The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as the son having wealth, so it was not permissible for him to perform Hajj on behalf of his mother until he had performed Hajj for himself, or he gave [the cost of] a 'sarrurah' who had no wealth, according to what we have previously established, and this interpretation does not contradict [the other reports].

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Amr ibn Ilyas, who said: I performed Hajj with my father while I was a 'sarur' (one who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj), and I said: 'I would like to make my Hajj on behalf of my mother, for she has died.' He said: 'Let me ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for you.' Ilyas said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening: 'I am your ransom, this son of mine is a sarur, and his mother has died, and he wishes to make his Hajj on her behalf. Is that permissible for him?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is written for him and for her, and the reward of the act of piety is written for him, because in the report it is not established that the son was obligated to perform Hajj, but rather it implied that he was a sarur. And it is not impossible that what was obligatory upon him was the Hajj of Islam, and he merely volunteered to perform Hajj and intended by that Hajj on behalf of his mother, so it suffices for both of them. However, his state is not devoid of two matters: either he intended by it the Hajj on behalf of his mother regarding what was obligatory upon her, then it does not suffice for her and the Hajj remains obligatory upon him from his own wealth, as we have mentioned in the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him). Or if he intends the Hajj for himself and for her together, then it suffices for him and the mother is entitled to the reward, even if the obligation of the Hajj of Islam is not lifted from her. And that which indicates this is...'

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who shares in his Hajj with four or five of his mawali (clients/freemen). He said: If they are all 'surrah' (free persons capable of independent obligation), then they have their reward, and the Hajj of Islam (the obligatory one) does not suffice for them from the one who performed Hajj on their behalf; and the (single) Hajj obligation belongs to the one who performed it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The woman performs Hajj on behalf of her brother, and on behalf of her sister, and he said: The woman performs Hajj on behalf of her father.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man perform Hajj on behalf of a woman, and does a woman perform Hajj on behalf of a man?' He said: 'There is no harm in it.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'These two reports, even if they occurred in two years, indicate the permissibility of a woman performing Hajj on behalf of a man in all cases. However, it is preferable to specify them for a woman who has already performed her obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam), because if she were a newborn infant, it would not be valid for her to perform Hajj on behalf of a man, which indicates this ruling.'

Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan al-Lu'lu'i from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Musaddif who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does a woman perform Hajj on behalf of a man? He said: Yes, if she is a jurist (faqihah), a Muslim, and she has already performed Hajj. For indeed, there are women who are better than men. So he stipulated for the validity of her Hajj on his behalf the combination of the two conditions: knowledge of the rituals of Hajj, and that she has already performed Hajj. Thus, both must be considered together, and this is further confirmed.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Mufaddal, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A single man may perform Hajj on behalf of a single man, but a single woman may not perform Hajj on behalf of a single man.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Sulayman ibn Ja'far who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a virgin woman who performed Hajj on behalf of a virgin woman. He said: It is not proper.

Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) regarding A man who gave another man dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf as a single Hajj, so it is permissible for him to perform Umrah with Hajj (Tamattu'). He said: Yes, he only differed in order to gain more merit and goodness.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from al-Haytham ibn al-Nahdi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who gave another man dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf as a single Hajj, he said: 'He is not permitted to perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) with the Umrah to the Hajj, so as not to differ from the owner of the dirhams.' The explanation of this report is one of two matters: One is that he is given the choice, it is permissible for him to perform either of the two Hajjs, and neither is obligatory upon him over the other, just as Tamattu' is obligatory upon him if he performs Hajj for himself. The other is that the latter report is specific to one whose obligation is Ifrad (single Hajj); it is not permissible for him to be performed for as a Mutamatti', because that does not suffice for him. And the first applies to one whose obligation is Tamattu'; so if he gave for Ifrad and differed to the Tamattu' which is his obligation, it suffices for him. On the condition that the latter report is suspended (mawquf) and not fully connected (ghayr musnad), and a report like it is not objected to against the fully connected reports.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man performs Umrah as a Tamattu' (for Hajj), he has fulfilled the obligation of Umrah.

And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah' [2:196], concerning a man who performs Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj) instead of that individual Umrah (Umrat al-Mufradah), he said: Thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) command his companions.

And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan from Najjah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the Mu'tamir (one performing Umrah al-Mufradah) enters Mecca, if he is not a Mutamatti', then after he performs Tawaf around the House, and Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, and prays the two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), let him return to his family if he wishes. And he said: 'The Umrah al-Mufradah and the Umrah al-Mut'ah were revealed because the Umrah al-Mut'ah entered into the Hajj, but the Umrah al-Mufradah did not enter into the Hajj.' So it is not contradictory to what we have presented, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'and the Umrah al-Mufradah did not enter into the Hajj' means the Umrah that is performed in the months other than the months of Hajj. Because the Umrah al-Mufradah only enters into the Hajj if it occurs in the months of Hajj. And whenever the matter is as we mentioned, then it is not sufficient in place of the Umrah al-Mut'ah. And that which confirms what we have presented.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Umrah, is it obligatory? He said: Yes. I said: Then does it suffice for the one who performs Tamattu'? He said: Yes.
Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: For every month, an Umrah.
From him, from Yunus, from Ya'qub, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: For every month, an Umrah.'
Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And the Umrah is once every year.

And he also narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Jamil from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There are not two Umras in one year. The resolution between these two narrations is that there are not two Umras in the year with which one performs Tamattu' to Hajj. As for the Umra al-Mabtulah (the independent Umra) with which one does not perform Tamattu' to Hajj, it is permissible in every month, indeed in every ten days.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a man, from Ali, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Mecca once, twice, or four times in a year, what should he do? He said: When he enters, he should enter in the state of Talbiyah (Muhrim), and when he leaves, he should leave in the state of Ihlal (not having performed Umrah to end the Ihram). He said: And for every month, there is an Umrah. I asked: Will that be less? He said: It will be an Umrah for every ten days. Then he said: And by your right, indeed in this year of mine, there were six Umrahs. I asked: Why is that? He said: I was with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim in al-Ta'if, and whenever he entered, I entered with him.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from the multitude of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no objection to performing the independent Umrah during the months of Hajj, then he returns to his family.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who set out in the months of Hajj performing Umrah, then returned to his country. He said: There is no harm, and if he performs Hajj in his year and performs Hajj alone, there is no blood-offering (dam) upon him. Indeed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) set out before Tarwiyah to Iraq, and he had entered Mecca performing Umrah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from Isḥaq, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever enters Mecca with an 'Umrah and stays until the hilal (crescent) of Dhu al-Hijjah, then it is not permissible for him to leave until he performs Hajj with the people.

And what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated, he said: Some of our companions informed me that he asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) during the ten days of Shawwal. He said: I intend to perform an independent Umrah this month. He said to him: You are held hostage by the Hajj. The man said to him: Indeed, Medina is my home and Mecca is my home, and I have family between them and wealth between them. He said to him: You are held hostage by the Hajj. The man said to him: Indeed, I have orchards around Mecca and I need to go out to them. He said: You go out permissible and return permissible to the Hajj. The correct view regarding these two narrations is one of two things: either we interpret them as indicating a type of recommendation, or we interpret them as referring to one whose Umrah is Tamattu', for it is not permissible for him to go out because he is held hostage by the Hajj, according to what the two narrations contain. And in the two narrations it is not specified whether the Umrah was independent or the one performed for Tamattu' until Hajj; rather, it is general, and we interpret them with this distinction so that the narrations do not contradict each other, which indicates this meaning.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From what point does the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') differ from the Mu'tamir (one who performs Umrah)? He said: Indeed, the Mutamatti' is bound to the Hajj, but the Mu'tamir, once he has finished from it, goes wherever he wishes. And Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) performed Umrah in Dhi al-Hijjah, then departed on the Day of Tawriyah to Iraq, while the people were departing to Mina. Therefore, there is no harm in performing Umrah in Dhi al-Hijjah for one who does not intend Hajj.

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Basir asked him (the Imam), while I was present, about one who enters into ihram for Umrah during the months of Hajj, asking if he may return (home). He said: There is no Umrah in the months of Hajj where one returns to his family, but he is detained in Mecca until he completes his Hajj, because he only entered into ihram for that purpose. Thus, this report clarifies that it was not permissible for him to do so, because he entered into ihram for Hajj, and this applies only to one who intends Tamattu' (combining) Umrah with Hajj, as we have explained.

Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan from Isa ibn al-Qasim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the pilgrim from Kufa: is it better to begin with Medina or with Mecca? He said: with Medina.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Should I begin with Medina or Mecca? He said: Begin with Mecca and conclude with Medina, for it is superior. The meaning is that we should apply this to one who performs Hajj via the Iraq route, and it has been narrated that he may do whichever he wishes.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about passing through Medina during the outbound journey (al-badaya), is it better, or during the return journey (al-rija'a)? He said: There is no harm with that, whichever it is.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from one of them who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I am a man with a debt. Should I borrow money and perform Hajj? He said: It is better to pay off the debt.

And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Ukba, who said: Sadir al-Sayrafi came to me and said: Indeed, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sends you greetings and says to you: 'What is wrong with you that you do not perform Hajj? Borrow and perform Hajj.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in these two narrations is that we should interpret them as applying to the one who has wealth that will return to him, so he can pay off his debt. As for the one who does not have that, it is not permissible for him to borrow and perform Hajj, because the Hajj that has become obligatory upon him indicates this distinction.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Utba, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt, borrows money, and performs Hajj. He said: If he has means/assets in his wealth, there is no objection.

From him, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who borrows money and performs Hajj. He said: If he has wealth behind him (in reserve), and if an incident occurs to him, he can pay it off, then there is no objection.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulaym al-Farra' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the fasting person who applies kohl. He said: There is no harm in it; it is not food nor drink.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Gundar, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about kohl (eye makeup) for the fasting person. He said: There is no harm with it, for it is not food that is eaten.
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-La', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no harm with the kohl (eye cosmetic) for the fasting person.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the fasting person if his eye becomes painful, does he apply kohl with radish (or similar) and what is like that, or is it not permissible for him? He said: He does not apply kohl.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who applies kohl while fasting, so he said: No, for I fear that it may enter the head. Therefore, the ruling in these two reports and what follows their pattern is that we consider it to be kohl containing musk or something with a sharp scent, which may enter the throat; for that is disliked, as indicated by that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about kohl (eye makeup) for the fasting person, and he said: If it is kohl that does not contain musk and has no taste in the throat, there is no harm with it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from al-'Ala' ibn Muhammad from Muhammad from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the woman who applies kohl (eye makeup) while she is fasting, so he said: If it is not kohl that you find a taste of in her throat, then there is no objection (to it breaking the fast). And that which indicates that these two narrations came in the place of disapproval (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram).

Sa'd ibn Abdillah from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq and Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I use kohl that contains musk while I am fasting?' He said: 'There is no objection to it.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibrahim ibn Shayba, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about completing the prayer in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina). He wrote to me: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) loved increasing prayer in the two Sanctuaries, so increase [your prayer] in them and complete [it].'

From him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer and fasting in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), so he said: 'Complete them, even if it is a single prayer.'

Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Aban from Mis'ma from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: My father (peace be upon him) considered for these two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina) what he did not consider for others, and he said that completing the prayer in them is among the reserved (special) matters.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan, from Umar ibn Riyah, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'When I arrive in Mecca, do I complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said: 'Complete it.' I said: 'And when I pass through Medina, do I complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said: 'Complete it.'
From him, from Safwan, from Mismar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: When you enter Mecca, complete [the prayer] on the day you enter.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from al-Asfwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer in Mecca and Medina. He said: Complete it, even if you have not prayed in them except one prayer.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the prayer in Mecca and Medina, is it shortened (qasr) or complete (tamm)? He said: Shorten it as long as you do not intend to stay for ten days.

From him, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) and said: 'Our companions have differed regarding the two Harams (Mecca and Medina); some shorten the prayer and some complete it. I am among those who complete it, based on a narration our companions have transmitted regarding completion. I mentioned Abdullah ibn Jundab that he used to complete it. He said: May God have mercy on Ibn Jundab. Then he said to me: Completion is not valid unless you intend to stay for ten days, and pray the voluntary prayers as much as you wish.' Ibn Hadeed said: 'And it was my preference that he order me to complete [the prayer], so there is no contradiction between these two narrations and the preceding ones, because the command to shorten is only directed towards one who did not intend to stay for ten days, if he believes that completion is obligatory in them. And we did not say that completion in them is obligatory, but rather we said it is in the manner of excellence and recommendation.' Do you not see the narration of Ali ibn Hadeed from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) which implies that when Abdullah ibn Jundab was mentioned to him and that he used to complete [the prayer] in them, he had mercy on him? If his command to shorten was in the manner of obligation, he would not have had mercy on him, because he would be opposing him. Then Ali ibn Hadeed also clarified that at the end of the narration, because he said: 'And it was my preference that he order me to complete,' which clarified that he sought obligation, so he did not order him with that, because their commands (peace be upon them) imply obligation, and he did not say 'and he did not recommend it to me.' And these two narrations can bear another meaning, which is that whoever arrives in the two Harams should intend to stay for ten days and complete the prayer in them, even if he knows that he will not stay except for one day or two days. And this is what distinguishes these two places and sets them apart from other lands, because in other places, if a person does not intend to stay for ten days, it is not permissible for him to complete [the prayer]. And that which reveals this meaning.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Hasani who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about completing (the prayer) and shortening (it). He said: 'When you enter the two Sanctuaries, intend ten days and complete the prayer.' I said to him: 'I arrive in Mecca one or two or three days before Tawree (the 8th of Dhu al-Qi'dah).' He said: 'Intend a stay of ten days and complete the prayer.'

And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah about shortening (al-taqseer) and completing (al-timmam) the prayer in the two Holy Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina). He said: 'Do not complete (the prayer) until you intend to stay for ten days.' I said: 'Indeed, our companions narrated from you that you ordered them to complete (the prayer).' He said: 'Indeed, your companions would enter the mosque, pray, take their sandals, and leave, while the people were facing them (entering the mosque for prayer). So I ordered them to complete (the prayer). The explanation of this report is that completing the prayer is not obligatory except for one who intends to stay for ten days. And whoever does not intend that is free to choose between completing and shortening, even though completing is superior. And his saying (peace be upon him) to one who would leave the mosque at the time of prayer and not pray with the people was an order of obligation, and it was not permissible for him to leave it, for one whose way is this, because in doing so there is repelling taqiyyah (divine precaution), encouraging the self, and disparaging the school (of thought). And that is what reveals what we mentioned, that this (ruling) came out as taqiyyah.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Hisham narrated from you that you ordered him to perform the complete prayer (al-tamm) in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), and that was for the sake of the people.' He said, 'No, it was I and those who passed away from my fathers; when we entered Mecca, we completed the prayer and concealed ourselves from the people. And what we mentioned earlier regarding that it is appropriate to combine [the prayers] while staying for ten days is also based on recommendation (istihbab). And that which indicates this is what he narrated.'

Ali ibn Mahziyar said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (the second) [peace be upon him]: The narrations regarding the completion (full prayer) and shortening (reduced prayer) of the prayer in the two Sanctuaries have differed from your fathers (peace be upon him). Some command completing the prayer even if it is a single prayer, and some command shortening the prayer as long as one does not intend to stay for ten days. I remained upon the completion in both until we departed from our Hajj this year, and the jurists of our companions advised me to shorten [the prayer] if I do not intend to stay for ten days. I became constrained by this, so I sought your opinion. He wrote in his own hand: 'You know, may God have mercy on you, the virtue of prayer in the two Sanctuaries over others than them. So I love for you, when you enter them, not to shorten [the prayer] and to increase in them from the prayer.' I said to him after that, two years later, in person: 'I wrote to you such-and-such, and you answered with such-and-such.' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What do you mean by the two Sanctuaries?' He said: 'Mecca and Medina. And when you head from Mina, shorten the prayer. And when you return from Arafat to Mina, and visit the House, and return to Mina, complete the prayer for those three days.' And he indicated with his finger [saying] three.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Ali ibn Yaqtin who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about shortening the prayer in Mecca, so he said: 'Complete it (the full four rak'ahs), and it is not obligatory, except that I love for you what I love for myself.'

And with this chain of narration, from Yunus, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about shortening the prayer in Mecca, so he said: 'Complete it (the full four rak'ahs), and it is not obligatory, except that I love for you what I love for myself.'

And with this chain of narration, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer in the two Holy Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), so he said: 'I like for you what I like for myself: complete the prayer.'
And by this chain of narration, from Yunus, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that among the mentioned [matters] is completing [the prayer] in the two Sanctuaries.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'When we enter Mecca and Medina, do we complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said, 'If you shorten it, that is acceptable; and if you complete it, that is better, you will increase [in reward].'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the prayer in Mecca. He said: Whoever wishes, he completes (the prayer), and whoever wishes, he shortens (it).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Hammad ibn Udayis, from Imran ibn Humaran, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Should I shorten the prayer in the Sacred Mosque (Mecca) or complete it?' He said: 'If you shorten it, that is acceptable; and if you complete it, that is better, and the increase in goodness is goodness.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar and Abu Ali ibn Rashid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: From the storehouses of the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, is completeness in four places: the Sanctuary of Allah, the Sanctuary of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), the Sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the Sanctuary of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh said: Muhammad ibn Hammam ibn Sahil narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari who said: Muhammad ibn Humran al-Mad'ini narrated to us from Ziyad al-Qandi who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: O Ziyad, I love for you what I love for my self and I dislike for you what I dislike for my self. Complete the prayer in the two sanctuaries, in Kufa, and near the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).

From him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Matil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Abu Shibl, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Visit the grave of al-Tayyib (the Pure One) and complete the prayer near it.' I said: 'Complete the prayer?' He said: 'Complete it.' I said: 'Some of our companions consider it permissible to shorten it.' He said: 'Only the weaklings do that.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, who said: He who heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Complete the prayer (salat) in four places: in the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), the Mosque of Kufa, and the Sanctuary of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn Jarir, from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Complete the prayer in four places: in the Sacred Mosque (Mecca), the Prophet's Mosque, the Kufa Mosque, and the Sanctuary of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And no one should say, based on this report and the report narrated by Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, that completing the prayer is exclusive to the Sacred Mosque and the Kufa Mosque, so that if a person leaves them, there is no completion for him, because it is not impossible that in these two reports the two places were mentioned specifically out of respect for them. Then, in other reports, he mentioned groups [of places] in which these two mosques are included, while others are also included in them, and this is not far-fetched nor contradictory. And we have previously presented reports that encompass the generality of places, among which are these two mosques, including the first report from Hammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: In the Sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). After that, the hadith of Ziyad al-Qandi that he said: Complete the prayer in the two Sanctuaries and in Kufa, and he did not say: In the Kufa Mosque. As for what we presented from the reports regarding the mention of the two Sanctuaries in a general sense, they are too numerous to count. And if it is established that completing the prayer is in the Sanctuary of Allah and the Sanctuary of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and this is preferred over the mosque in a general sense, even if they were specified in these two reports, so too is it with the Kufa Mosque, because no one distinguishes between the two places.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, is the Fitrah (alms of fasting) obligatory on the people of the villages (rural areas)?' He said, 'The Fitrah is obligatory on everyone who consumes sustenance, and upon him to pay from that sustance.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Zakat al-Fitrah is incumbent upon every people according to what they feed their dependents, whether milk, raisins, or something else.

Sa'd narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from whomever narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man in the countryside who is unable to provide Fitrah, so he said: He should give charity of four Artals of milk.

Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmary from Abdullah ibn Hammad from Isma'il ibn Sahil from Hammad and Burayd and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: We asked them about the Zakat of Fitrah, and he said: A sa' of dates or raisins or barley, or half of that of wheat, or flour, or suweeq (crushed grain), or corn, or salt, from the small and the large, the male and the female, the adult, and whoever is supported by him are all equal. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between these narrations, because the basis for paying the Zakat is from the surplus of staple foods, and each group of people gives what they consume as their staple food, even if one type is superior to another. And if that is the case, then mentioning the different types in some narrations does not contradict the types not mentioned in others, because they are restricted to those for whom that is their staple food. And the people of each land have been distinguished by that, as we mentioned, and all of that is on the basis of preference and recommendation. And if a person gives from the types we mentioned that is not what they consume, that is also permissible. And it has been narrated that the people of the lands are distinguished regarding the Fitrah.

Ali ibn Hatim said: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hasani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani The narrations differed regarding al-Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), so I wrote to Abu al-Hasan, the Master of the Camp (peace be upon him), asking him about that. He wrote: Al-Fitrah is one Sa' of the staple food of your land. For the people of Mecca, Yemen, Ta'if, the outskirts of Syria, Yamamah, Bahrain, the two Iraqs, Persia, Ahwaz, and Kerman, it is dates. For the central regions of Syria, it is raisins. For the people of Jazira, Mosul, and all the mountains, it is wheat or barley. For the people of Tabaristan, it is rice. For the people of Khorasan, it is wheat, except for the people of Merv and Rayy, for whom it is raisins. For the people of Egypt, it is wheat. And for those other than these, it is whatever staple food predominates for them. For the Bedouins who dwell in the deserts, it is Qit (dried yogurt). Al-Fitrah is obligatory upon you and upon all people, and upon every male or female, young or old, free or slave, weaned or infant, whom you provide for. You pay it by weight: six Artals, where the Rital of Medina is one hundred and ninety-five dirhams. Thus, the total value of Al-Fitrah is one thousand and seventy dirhams.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about cupping for the fasting person, he said: Yes, if he does not fear weakness.

And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, who said: Three things do not break the fast of the fasting person: vomiting, seminal emission, and cupping. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was cupped while he was fasting, and he did not consider it blameworthy for the fasting person to use kohl.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no harm in the fasting person undergoing cupping, except in the month of Ramadan, for I dislike that he be deceived with his life, unless he does not fear weakness for himself. Indeed, when we desired cupping in Ramadan, we underwent it at night, so it does not contradict the earlier reports, because the reason for the dislike in it is directed only toward one who fears weakness. As for one who does not fear that, there is no harm with him in any case.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the fasting person, does he undergo cupping? He said: I fear for him. I said: Does he not fear for his own self? He said: Fainting or a fever rising in him. I said: What do you mean by fearing for him? He said: Fainting or a fever rising in him. I said: What if he is strong enough to bear it and fears nothing? He said: Yes, if God wills.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the fasting person use siwak with water or with a fresh twig, tasting its flavor? He said: There is no harm in it.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Ala' [al-Qalla'], from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The fasting person may use the siwak (tooth-stick) at any part of the day he wishes, and he should not use it with a fresh (green) twig, and he may rinse his mouth with water, and pour water over his head, and cool himself with his garment, and sprinkle the fan, and sprinkle the awning beneath him, and he should not immerse his head completely in water.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he disliked for the fasting person to use a moist siwak. And he said: It does not harm if he moistens his siwak with water, then shakes it off until nothing remains in it, and this indicates the permissibility of that as well.

Al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Musa ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Razi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Some of his companions asked him about using the siwak (tooth-stick) during the month of Ramadan. He said: 'It is permissible.' Some of them said: 'The moisture of the siwak enters the stomach.' He said: 'What do you say about the fresh (wet) siwak, whose moisture enters the throat?' He said: 'As for rinsing the mouth (madmadah), it is more moist than the fresh siwak. If a sayer says: 'Water is necessary for rinsing the mouth for the sake of the Sunnah,' then the siwak is necessary for the sake of the Sunnah which Jibril (peace be upon him) brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is it permissible for the fasting person to smell basil and perfume?' He said: 'There is no harm (in it).'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the fasting person, does he smell the basil or not? Do you see that permissible for him? He said: There is no objection.

Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from 'Abad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, who said: A man wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Does the fasting person smell the basil to enjoy its scent?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it.'
Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The fasting person should not smell the basil.

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Baqqah, from Al-Hasan Al-Siqqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the fasting person who wears a wet garment, he said: 'No' (it is disliked), and he should not smell the basil.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hasan ibn Rashid who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the menstruating woman make up the prayer?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'Does she make up the fast?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'From where does this come?' He said: 'Indeed, the first to make a comparison (qiyas) was Iblis.' I said: 'So the fasting person immerses himself in water?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Does urine soak the garment on his body?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'From where does this come?' He said: 'From that.' I said: 'Does the fasting person smell the rihan (basil/mint)?' He said: 'No,' because it is a delight, and it is disliked for him to delight in it. Therefore, the meaning in these narrations is a type of dislike rather than prohibition, and this was explicitly stated in the last narration. It is also possible that what is meant by the disliked 'rihan' is the narcissus, because it is more disliked than the basil.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Dawud ibn Isḥaq al-Ḥaddā' from Muhammad ibn al-'Isṣ who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbidding the use of narcissus (for scent). I said, 'May I be your ransom, for what reason is that?' He said, 'Because it is the scent of the foreigners (non-Arabs/Persians).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Abu Jamilyah, from Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a fasting person who rinses his mouth: He said: He should not swallow his saliva until he spits it out three times. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is specific to rinsing the mouth for the sake of prayer; as for rinsing for cooling down, it is permissible in all cases, as indicated by that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, who said: The fasting person in the month of Ramadan may use the miswak whenever he wishes. And if he rinses his mouth (madmadah) during the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, there is no penalty upon him and his fast is complete. But if he rinses his mouth during a time other than an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, he must repeat the fast. And it is preferable for the fasting person not to rinse his mouth.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: He narrated to me Sulayman ibn Haf al-Marwazi, who said: I heard him saying: When the fasting person rinses his mouth in the month of Ramadan, or inhales deliberately, or smells a strong scent, or sweeps a house and dust enters his nose and throat, then upon him is the fasting of two consecutive months, for that is considered breaking his fast for him, like eating, drinking, and intercourse. The correct interpretation of this report is that we construe it regarding one who rinsed for cooling, something entered his throat, he did not spit it out, and swallowed it deliberately; then the ruling upon him is the same as the ruling upon one who deliberately broke his fast for one day of Ramadan.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is permissible for the fasting man to taste from the pot.

From him (al-Shaykh), from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: Ibn Abi Ya'fur asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening: 'From the fasting person, is it permissible to pour medicine into his ear?' He said: 'Yes.' And he tastes the broth and sucks the young bird (to taste it).

From him (Al-Saffar) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi that he was asked: About the fasting woman who cooks the pot and tastes the broth while looking at it, he said: There is no objection (to it). And he was asked about the woman who has a young child and she is fasting, so she chews the bread for him and feeds him, he said: There is no objection to it. And the bird, if it belongs to her.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person, does he taste something and not swallow it? He said: No. And this does not contradict the earlier reports, because this narration is understood as referring to one who has a need for that, because the concession (rukhsah) was only revealed in that case when there is a compelling necessity leading to it, such as the spoilage of food, or the death of a child, or the death of a bird. As for when all of those are absent, then it is not permissible in any case.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from the multitude of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), in [the case of] A man who broke his fast deliberately for one day in the month of Ramadan without an excuse, he said: He frees a slave, or he fasts two consecutive months, or he feeds sixty poor people. If he cannot afford that, he gives charity according to his ability.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Masharqi, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who deliberately broke his fast for days in the month of Ramadan, what is upon him regarding the expiation? He wrote: Whoever breaks his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan, upon him is freeing a believing slave, and he must fast one day in place of that day.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had intercourse with his wife during the month of Ramadan and could not find what to give in charity to sixty poor people, he said: He gives in charity according to his ability. And it has been narrated that it is permissible for him to fast eighteen days in place of two months.
