And if she does not remember which day and which month, let her begin her waiting period from the day the news reaches her.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: If her husband dies while absent from her, she observes the waiting period (iddah) from the time the news reaches her, because she intends to mourn for him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: If he dies while absent from her, and evidence is established regarding his death, then her waiting period (iddah) is from the day the news reaches her, four months and ten days, because she must observe mourning for him in death for four months and ten days, during which she refrains from kohl, perfume, and dyes.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who is absent from his wife when he dies, he said: If the husband who is absent from her dies, she observes the waiting period (iddah) from the day the news reaches her, because she mourns him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman whose husband dies while he is absent, her waiting period (iddah) begins from the day the news reaches her, whether the testimony is established or not.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If a man divorces his wife while he is absent, and she does not know until a year or more or less later, then when she learns of it, she may marry without observing the waiting period (Iddah). And if her husband dies while he is absent, she observes the waiting period from the day the news reaches her, even if he had died a year or two before.

Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorced woman whose husband divorces her, and she does not know [of it] except after a year, and the woman whose husband dies, and she does not know of his death except after a year. He said: If two just witnesses come, then they do not observe the waiting period, and if not, they observe the waiting period.

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Safwan from 'Abdullah from al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said: A woman received news of her husband's death after a year or thereabouts. He said: If she is pregnant, her waiting period is until she gives birth to her child. And if she is not pregnant, her waiting period has passed if evidence is established for her that he died on such and such a day. And if she has no evidence, let her observe the waiting period from the day she heard. These two reports came as anomalous, contradicting all the hadiths. The detail contained in the latter report is also contradicted by the former report mentioned from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, because he said: She observes the waiting period from the day it reaches her, whether evidence is established for her or not. So it is permissible to depart from the numerous reports to these two reports, on the assumption that the narrator may have erred and heard the ruling of the divorced woman and thought it was the ruling of the one whose husband died, because the detail contained in the latter report and the consideration of the establishment of evidence and the completion of the waiting period upon childbirth and all that else is considered in it. And on this basis, the reports do not contradict each other. And it has been narrated that if the distance is close, it is permissible for her to marry from the day the man dies. That was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Saif ibn Umayra from Mansur who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Regarding the woman whose husband dies or divorces her while he is absent, he said: If he is at a distance of a few days' journey, she begins her waiting period from the day her husband dies. If he is far away, she begins from the day the news reaches her, because she must mourn for him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'What do you think if she becomes pregnant?' He said: 'He is her child.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and others, who said: The water (of semen) is the water of the man; he places it where he wills. However, if he brings forth a child, he does not deny it, and he is strict in denying the child.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, all of them, from al-Fath ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the conditions in Mut'ah (temporary marriage). He said: The conditions in it are such and such. If she says 'Yes', then that is permissible. And I do not say as was reported to me that the people of Iraq say: 'The water is yours and the land is yours, and I do not water your land with the water, and if something grows there, it belongs to the owner of the land,' because two conditions in one condition is invalid. And if you are granted a child, you accept it. And the matter is clear. So whoever wishes to confuse himself, let him confuse himself.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said: A man asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) while I was listening: A man marries a woman for a fixed term (mut'ah) and stipulates upon her that he will not acknowledge her child, but she subsequently brings forth a child. Should he deny the child? He emphasized in this matter and said: He denies (paternity). And how can he deny it, out of respect for it? The man said: But I suspect her (of not being the true mother or of other issues). He (al-Rida) said: It is not fitting for you to marry except a trustworthy (woman). Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'The fornicator marries not except a female idolator or a polytheess, and the female idolator none marries her except a fornicator or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Umar ibn Hanzalah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the conditions of Mut'ah (temporary marriage). He said: 'He stipulates upon her whatever he wishes of the gift (ata'ya), and he stipulates for the child if he wishes, and there is no inheritance between them. The meaning of his saying 'and he stipulates for the child if he wishes' is that we understand it to mean leaving withdrawal (al-'azl), and impregnating her in a manner that there will be a child according to the course of nature, because he has the option to stipulate withdrawal, and he has the option to stipulate impregnation, and he is free to choose in that matter. So the Imam (peace be upon him) expressed that which is a cause or like the cause of the child by the word 'child' using a form of metaphor. And the choice mentioned in the narration does not encompass accepting the child or rejecting him in every state.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The waiting period ('iddah) and menstruation are for the women; if they claim [them], they are believed.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father that Ali (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a woman who claimed she had menstruated three times in one month, he said: Appoint women from her close companions to testify that her menstruation occurred in the period she claimed. If they testify, she is believed; otherwise, she is lying. The meaning of this narration is that we apply it to a woman who is suspected in her claim. Do you not see that the narration includes the ruling for one who claims three menstruations in a month, which is rare in the custom of women and involves doubt? Therefore, it is appropriate to ask women from her close companions about her condition and act accordingly. Once the suspicion is removed, the woman's word is accepted exclusively.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Halab (Al-Halabi) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who bought a slave girl and she had not yet menstruated: He said, 'If she is young, and pregnancy is not expected, there is no waiting period (istibra') upon her, and he may have intercourse with her if he wishes.' And if she has reached puberty but has not menstruated, then there is a waiting period upon her.' He said, 'And I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl while she was menstruating: He said, 'When she becomes pure (from menstruation), let him touch her if he wishes.'

From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the young girl in whom pregnancy is not feared, and he said: 'There is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.'

Ali ibn Isma'il, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the young girl who has not yet had her first menstruation and has not reached puberty, if a man buys her, he said: There is no waiting period (istibra') upon her; he may consummate the marriage with her immediately.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Mansur ibn Hazim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the waiting period (istibra') of a female slave who has not yet reached menstruation, while he feared for her, and he said: 'Five and forty nights.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Rabi' ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the girl who has not yet reached menstruation, and pregnancy is feared for her. He said: Her womb is verified (cleared of pregnancy) by the one who sells her and the one who buys her, [through a period of] forty and four nights. Thus it is clarified in this report and the first report that this obligation applies only if pregnancy is feared for her, and this occurs only when she is of the age at which she menstruates.

Ali ibn Isma'il from Hammad from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Sinan said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a young girl who has not yet menstruated. He said: 'He should abstain from her for a month if she has been touched (consummated). I said: 'And what do you think if I buy her while she is pure, and her owner claims that he has not had intercourse with her since she became pure?' He said: 'If there is a trustworthy person with you, let him touch her.' He said: 'This matter is severe. If you must do it, be careful not to discharge semen upon her, so that it does not contradict the earlier reports which included her waiting period (istibra') of forty-five nights. For the basis of this report is that we interpret it as referring to one who menstruates once during this period, because the consideration in her istibra' is by one menstruation. And forty-five days are only considered for one who does not menstruate, if she is of an age to menstruate. The earlier report indicates this, which we presented at the beginning of the chapter from al-Halabi, that if he buys her while she is menstruating, then when she becomes pure, it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her, and this adds clarity to that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said: I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl while she was menstruating, should he ensure her womb is cleared by another menstruation, or is this one menstruation sufficient for him? He said: No, but this one menstruation is sufficient for him. If he ensures her womb is cleared by another, there is no harm; she is considered as surplus (extra).

And as for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Baraqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who sells a slave girl whom he has been abstaining from (sexual relations) with, is there upon him [the requirement of] istibra' (waiting period for pregnancy verification) from her? He said: Yes. And [I asked] about the minimum that suffices for istibra' for the buyer and the sold girl. He said: The people of Medina say: one menstruation. And Ja'far (peace be upon him) says: two menstruations. And I asked him about the minimum istibra' of a virgin. He said: The people of Medina say: one menstruation. And Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: two menstruations. So the way to handle this hadith is to carry it upon a type of recommendation (istihbab). And he clarified that in the preceding hadith by his saying: If he verifies her pregnancy with another menstruation, there is no harm; it is in the position of excess.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Muhammad ibn Hakim from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said: When you buy a female slave, and her master guarantees to you that she is in a state of ritual purity (free from menstruation or post-partum bleeding), there is no harm in having intercourse with her.

Ali ibn Isma'il from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who buys a slave-girl from another man, and he says, 'I have not had intercourse with her.' He said, 'If he trusts him, there is no harm in him having intercourse with her.' And he said regarding a man who sells a slave-girl to another man, 'It is upon him to verify her chastity before selling her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man buys a female slave while she is pure (not menstruating), and her owner claims that he has not touched her since she menstruated. He said: If you trust him, then touch her.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a female slave from a Muslim man who claims that he has already verified her virginity (istibra'). Is that sufficient, or is it necessary to verify her? He said: Verify her with two menstruations. I said: Is it permissible for the buyer to have sexual intercourse with her? He said: Yes, and he does not need to approach her genitals (for further verification). Therefore, the correct interpretation of this narration is that we should understand it as a recommended act (istihbab) rather than obligatory (farḍ) or mandatory (ijbar).

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifah said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a female slave who belongs to a woman, and she sells her. He said: There is no objection to her husband having sexual intercourse with her without requiring her to undergo istibra' (waiting period to confirm pregnancy).

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a female slave who belongs to a woman, so she sells her: He said, 'There is no harm in him having intercourse with her without her being tested (istibra').' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said, 'These two reports came absolutely (without condition), but the preferable course is to test her, which indicates that.'

Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah said: I bought a slave girl from Basra from a woman, and she informed me that no one had had intercourse with her. So I had intercourse with her, and I did not observe istibra' (waiting period to confirm virginity/pregnancy). I asked about that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he said: 'It is so; I have done that, and I do not intend to return [to observing it].'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who buys a slave girl, frees her, and then marries her: Does the marriage consummation take effect upon her before he observes her waiting period (istibra')? He said: She observes one menstrual period. I said: If he has intercourse with her [before the istibra' is complete], he said: There is no blame upon him.

And Abu al-Abbas al-Qabbagh narrated, he said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a female slave, freed her, then married her, and did not observe the waiting period (istibra') of her womb. He said: His choice was to do so, and if he did not do so, there is no blame. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All these narrations indicate that it is preferable for him to observe the waiting period, but when he leaves the istibra', he has left the more cautious and superior option, and there is no blame upon him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man buys a female slave who is pregnant; what is permissible for him from her?' He said: 'That which is below the private part.' I said: 'He buys a young girl who has not yet had her first menstruation and is not a virgin; should he purify her (istibra')?' He said: 'Her case is severe; if one like her is pregnant, he should purify her.'

Ali ibn Isma'il from Fadala from Aban from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the female slave whom a man buys while she is pregnant; does intercourse take place with her while she is pregnant? He said: No.

Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a female slave while she is pregnant, does he have intercourse with her? He said: No. I said: Below the vulva? He said: He does not approach her. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'He does not approach her below the vulva' is based on a type of dislike (karahah), not prohibition (haram), as indicated by the preceding narrations, and this indicates it.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-istibra' (verification of pregnancy/status) is obligatory upon the one who wishes to sell the slave-girl, if he intends to have sexual relations with her, and upon the one who buys her, al-istibra' is also obligatory. I asked him: 'Is it permissible for him to have relations with her in what is other than the vagina?' He said: 'Yes, before he verifies her status. And that which indicates that abstaining from that is better.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina, desiring to ask him about an issue. I began to feel shy of him. He said to me, 'O Abdillah, ask.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I bought a female slave.' Then I remained silent out of shyness for him. He said to me, 'I think you intended to have intercourse with her, but did not know how to do so.' I said, 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' He said, 'I think you intended to perform 'tafkheeth' for her, and you were shy to ask about it.' I said, 'Your shyness indeed prevented me from that.' He said, 'There is no harm in performing tafkheeth for her until she is verified as pregnant (istibra'), and if you wait, that is better for you.' I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I have heard more than one person say that tafkheeth is permissible.' Then he said. I said to him, 'And what is the benefit in me leaving it (waiting)?' He said, 'Like that. If there were harm in it, we would not have commanded it.' He turned to me and said, 'Indeed, a man comes to his female slave, and she becomes pregnant from him, and she sees blood, while she is pregnant. He thinks that is menstruation, so he sells her. Therefore, I do not like for a Muslim man to have intercourse with a pregnant female slave who has become pregnant from another man, until he comes to her and informs her. And it has been narrated that if four months of pregnancy have passed, it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her in the vagina.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifah ibn Musa said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'I buy a female slave, and she stays with me for months without menstruating, and this is not due to old age.' I said: 'And I showed her to the women, and they said she is not pregnant.' He said: 'Is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her in her private part?' He said: 'Indeed, wind can prevent menstruation without pregnancy, so there is no harm in touching her in the private part.' I said: 'If she is pregnant, what is mine from her if I wish?' He said: 'For you is what is below the private part until she completes four months and ten days of pregnancy.' He said: 'When her pregnancy exceeds four months and ten days, there is no harm in marrying her in the private part.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who has a concubine, and his son mounts her and has intercourse with her. He said: There was a man who had a concubine and a wife, and he ordered his son to mount his father's concubine, and the son had intercourse with her. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about that, and he said: It does not prohibit the father from having intercourse with her, but it is not fitting for him to approach her until she is cleared of the son's offspring. If offspring results from what is between them, the offspring belongs to the father, provided they both had intercourse with her in one day and one month.

From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said: A man from the Ansar came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'I have been tested with a great matter. I had intercourse with my female slave, then I went out for some need of mine. When I returned from the road, I found my boy between the legs of the female slave. She had become pregnant and gave birth to a boy nine months after that.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Retain the female slave and do not sell her, and spend on her until she dies or Allah provides for her a way out. If something happens to you, bequeath that she be spent on from your wealth until Allah provides for her a way out. Do not contradict these two reports and the first report, for what it entails is that he should not sell the female slave and keep her. There was no mention of the child in the two reports together, but that confirms the child's attachment to him, because he is not permitted to sell the mother only if the child is his. But if the child is from another man, then it is permissible to sell her in all cases.'

Al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from a man from our companions, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Isma'il, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave whom he had sexual relations with, and she would go out for his needs. She became pregnant, and he feared that the child might be his. What should he do? Should he sell the female slave and the child? He said: He sells the female slave and does not sell the child, nor does he bequeath to him anything from his inheritance.

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman, the freedman of Tribal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who had sexual relations with his slave-girl, and that he used to send her on his errands, and that she became pregnant, and that news reached him of her promiscuity/mixing with others, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and assigns him a share in his house. He said: Then it was said to him, 'A man who has sexual relations with his slave-girl, and he did not send her on his errands, and he suspected her (of infidelity), and she became pregnant.' He said: When she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and assigns him a share from his house and his wealth. This case is not like that other case. The principle in these two narrations is that it was permissible for him not to fully affiliate the child to himself, such that his having relations with her was not simultaneous with another man's relations with her in the same period; rather, she was one of those whom he had relations with occasionally. So when another man had relations with her and the matter became mixed up, it was permissible for him not to fully affiliate the child to himself; rather, that is obligatory. He does not deny the child either, due to the suspicion in that case, and he sets aside for him something from his wealth, and does not make him share with the rest of his children and heirs who are of sound lineage. And this does not contradict that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a slave-girl who belongs to a man, whom he circles (has intercourse with) while she is going out, and she becomes pregnant. He said: The man accuses her, or her family accuses her. I said: As for a clear/significant sign, no. He said: Then the child is attached to him.

From him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his slave-girl, who goes and comes (i.e., is not confined), and he had withdrawn (from her), and there had been no other act of his towards her. What do you say about the child? He said: I see that this should not be sold, O Sa'id. And I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said: Do you accuse her? I said: As for an apparent accusation, no. He said: Do your people accuse her? I said: As for something apparent, no. He said: Then how can you manage for the child not to be attached to you? Because the reasoning in these two reports is that if the slave-girl is trodden upon (i.e., has intercourse) by him at every time, it is not fitting that he should disown her child due to the suspicion which is not conclusive. And what we said in the first two reports was permissible if his treading upon her was not except at times, and at times when it predominates in his opinion that the child is not from him, so the ruling regarding it is what we said.

And as for what al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Ali ibn Sulayman from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Khattab, that he wrote to him asking about a cousin of his who had a slave girl serving him, and he would have intercourse with her. One day he entered her house and found a man serving her having intercourse with her, so he doubted about her [whether the child would be his or the servant's], so he threatened the slave girl, and she confessed that the man had committed fornication with her. Then she became pregnant and gave birth to a child. So he wrote: If the child is yours or there is resemblance from you in him, do not sell them [the child and the mother], for that is not permissible for you. And if the son is not from you and there is no resemblance from you in him, then sell him and sell his mother, so that does not contradict what we have previously mentioned from the narrations. Because the matter in that has been referred back to you, the owner of the slave girl, by considering [the signs of paternity]. If he knows that the child is from you by one of the means by which the attachment of children to fathers is established, he attaches him to you. And if the matter becomes ambiguous, he is prevented from selling him and does not attach him to you, according to what we have previously mentioned. And if he knows that he is not from you, it is permissible for him to sell him in all cases, according to what the news contained.

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a man in this era who had intercourse with his slave-girl, then doubted about her child. He wrote back: If there is resemblance in him [the child] from him [the master], then he is his child.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Hasan al-Siqill, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) being asked about a man who bought a slave-girl and then had intercourse with her before her womb was cleared (of pregnancy). He said: 'What a bad thing he did; he should seek Allah's forgiveness and not repeat it.' I said: 'And if he sold her to another, and she had not cleared her womb, then the second man sold her to another man, and he had intercourse with her and she had not cleared her womb, and then her pregnancy became evident with the third man?' He (Abu 'Abdillah, peace be upon him) said: 'The child belongs to the one whose bed it is (the last husband), and for the adulterer is the stone.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Hasan al-Siql, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked and mentioned a similar [ruling], except that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The child belongs to the one who has the girl, and he should be patient, for the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): The child belongs to the bed (of the owner), and for the adulterer is the stone.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about two men who had intercourse with a slave-girl during one period of purity (tahur). To whom does the child belong? He said: To the one who possesses the slave-girl, based on the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'The child belongs to the one whose bed (possession) it is, and for the fornicator is the stone.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If two or three men have intercourse with a slave girl in one period of purity, and she gives birth, and they all claim her, the master of the girl draws lots among them, and whoever draws the lot, the child is his, and he pays the value of the child to the owner of the girl. He said: If a man buys a slave girl, and another man comes and claims her, and she has already given birth to a child from the buyer, he returns the girl to him, and the child belongs to him for its value.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of three men who had intercourse with a woman during one period of purity, and this was in the pre-Islamic era before the emergence of Islam. He cast lots among them and assigned the child to the one whose lot was drawn, and placed two-thirds of the blood money on the other two. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) laughed until his incisors became visible, and said: 'I know nothing about it except what Ali ruled.' So these two reports do not contradict the earlier reports, because the explanation in them is that if the girl was shared between two or three men and they all had intercourse with her during one period of purity, the ruling was by casting lots. And the earlier reports only stipulated that the child belongs to the one who possesses the girl, when she was changing ownership.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Ali (peace be upon him) to Yemen, and when he arrived, he said to him: 'Tell me of the most surprising thing that has happened to you.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a group of men came to me who had purchased a female slave, and they all had intercourse with her in one period of purity, and she gave birth to a boy. They disputed over him, and each claimed him. So I cast lots among them, and gave him to the one whose lot was drawn, and I guaranteed him their share. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is not the case with a group of people who dispute and then entrust their matter to Allah, except that the lot of the rightful one will emerge.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Those who accuse their wives [of adultery] and have no witnesses except themselves.' He said: It is the accuser who accuses his wife. If he accuses her and then admits that he lied against her, he is flogged with the prescribed punishment and his wife is returned to him. And if he insists on proceeding, he must bear witness against her four times by Allah that he is of the truthful, and the fifth time let him invoke the curse of Allah upon himself if he is of the liars. And if she wishes to ward off the punishment from herself, and the punishment is stoning, she must bear witness four times by Allah that he is of the liars, and the fifth time that the wrath of Allah is upon her if he is of the truthful. If she does not do this, she is stoned; and if she does, the punishment is repelled from herself. Then they are not permissible for each other until the Day of Resurrection. I asked: What do you think if they were separated and she had a child, and the child died? He said: The mother inherits him. And if the mother dies, the maternal uncles inherit him. And whoever says that he is a child of fornication, he is flogged with the prescribed punishment. I asked: Is the child returned to him if he admits to him? He said: No, and no honor. The father does not inherit the son, and the son inherits the father.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: The one who performs li'an (conjugal imprecation) does so only by denying the child, and he said: When a man accuses his wife [of adultery], he performs li'an with her.

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The curse (l'an) does not take effect until the man enters with his wife, and the curse does not occur except by denying the child. Therefore, there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first two reports, because the first two reports are consistent with the apparent meaning of the Quran. Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves...' The verse did not stipulate the denial of the child in that matter, so it must be established in every place where the accusation occurred. And the first two reports also confirm this, with the fact that the first of the last two reports, if the intended meaning was the removal of the curse merely by the accusation in all cases, would be contradictory because he said 'The curse does not occur except by denying the child,' then he said 'And when the man accuses the woman, he curses her.' If the intended meaning was what some people went to, it would be contradictory as you see. The solution in these two reports is that the curse in the accusation does not occur merely by the accusation until he adds to that the claim of witnessing (consummation), and the ruling of denying the child is not like that, because whenever the child is denied, the curse becomes obligatory upon him even if he did not claim witnessing of the illicit act. Thus, the two rulings differ in denying the child and mere accusation from this aspect, and that which indicates that witnessing is a condition in the accusation...

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The *laman* (oath of excommunication) does not take effect until he claims that he has personally witnessed (the act).

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about a man who accuses his wife of adultery, he said: He is flogged, then they are separated, and he does not perform li'an with her until he says: 'I bear witness that I saw you doing such and such.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man accuses his wife of adultery, he does not perform li'an with her until he says: 'I saw between her legs a man committing adultery with her.' We have completed what relates to this chapter in our Great Book, and what we have mentioned is sufficient, God willing, and this adds clarification.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about a man who accuses his wife of adultery, he said: He is flogged, then they are separated, and he does not perform li'an with her until he says: I bear witness that I saw you doing such and such.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hanafiyya (al-Halabi), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a free woman whom her husband (who is a slave) accuses (of adultery), he said: They perform li'an (mutual imprecation).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a slave who accused his wife, and he said: They perform the *li'an* (mutual cursing) just as the free persons perform it.

From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the free man regarding marriage between him and the slave girl. He said: Yes. And between the slave and the free woman, and between the male slave and the female slave, and between the Muslim man and the Jewish woman and the Christian woman. And they do not inherit each other, and the free man and the slave girl do not inherit each other.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The free man does not perform *li'an* with the slave woman, nor the female dhimmi, nor the one he enjoys (temporary marriage). This implies two possibilities: First, the free man does not perform *li'an* with the slave woman if he has sexual relations with her by his right of ownership, and his statement 'nor the female dhimmi' is similar: if she is a slave woman who is a dhimmi. He distinguished between saying 'the slave woman' and 'the female dhimmi' because he likely meant by 'slave woman' a Muslim slave, then clarified by 'nor the female dhimmi' meaning if she is a slave woman who is a dhimmi. This is one view. The other view is that the intended meaning of 'the free man' is if he married a slave woman without his master's permission, because in that case there is no *li'an* between them, and the children will be slaves to her master, if there are children.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a free man performing li'an with a female slave, he said: Yes, if her master is the one who married her to him.

From him, from Ayyub, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the slave man who performs li'an with the free woman, he said: Yes, if his master had married her to him, he would perform li'an by the command of his master, and that would be the case. And he said: Between the free man and the slave woman, and between the Muslim man and the female dhimmi, there is li'an. And it is possible that this report came out as taqiyyah (prudent dissimulation), because among the opponents there are those who say there is no li'an between the free man and the slave woman.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from some of them, from Abu al-Maghra', from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'A slave man had a free woman under his ownership, and he accused her [of adultery].' He said: 'What do the people of Kufa say regarding her?' I said: 'They say she is flogged.' He said: 'No, but he performs li'an with her just as he performs li'an with a free woman, and he confirms what we have said regarding the establishment of li'an between them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Safwan from Hisham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a free woman whom her slave husband accuses (of adultery), and a free man for whom there is a slave woman under his authority who accuses him. He said: They perform al-li'an (mutual imprecation).

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-A'lawi, from al-'Umari, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a Muslim man who has a Jewish or Christian female slave under his ownership, and he fathers a child by her and accuses her (of adultery). Is there li'an (mutual imprecation) upon him? He said: No. The basis in his saying (peace be upon him): 'No, at the questioner's asking whether li'an is upon him,' is one of two things: One is that he returns to the denial of the child, so it is held that if he acknowledges the child and then denies it, his denial is not heeded, the child is established as his, and li'an does not occur between them. And if we say that he returns to the accusation (of adultery), then li'an does not occur between them merely by the accusation, according to what we have previously established, until he adds to it the claim of witnessing (the act).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sihran, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has a female slave for one of his children, and his children are young. He said: It is not permissible for him to have intercourse with her until he appraises her at a fair price, takes her, and the price becomes a debt owed by the child to him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has a female slave for one of his children, while his children are young, is it permissible for him to consummate the marriage with her? He said: He appraises her at a fair price, then takes her, and the value becomes a debt owed by the child to him.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Musa ibn Ja'far from 'Amr ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan ibn Sadqa who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said: 'Some of our companions have narrated that it is permissible for a man to marry the slave-girl of his son or the slave-girl of his daughter. I have a daughter, and for my daughter there is a slave-girl that I bought for her as part of her dowry. Is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her?' He said: 'No, except with her permission.' Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said: 'Is it not established that this is permissible?' He said: 'Yes, that is if he is the one who caused it (bought it).' Then he turned to me and pointed with his index finger and said: 'If you buy a slave-girl for your daughter or for your son, and the son is young and has not had intercourse with her, it is permissible for you to take possession of her and marry her. Otherwise, no, except with the permission of both (the son and the slave-girl). This does not contradict the earlier reports, because his saying 'It is permissible for you to take possession of her and marry her' is understood to mean that it is permissible for you if you have valued her and the price has become due in your debt for your child. As for before that, it is not permissible.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Ali from al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed li'an (oath of elimination) with his wife while she was pregnant, and her pregnancy had become evident, and he denied what was in her womb. When she gave birth, he claimed the child and acknowledged it, and asserted that it was from him. He said: The child is returned to him, and he inherits from her, and he is not lashed, because the li'an has concluded.

Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful would perform li'an in every state, except if she were pregnant. The meaning of 'except if she were pregnant' is that he would not establish the hadd punishment upon her if she declined from li'an. And the intended meaning is not that he did not proceed with li'an between them, as indicated by the first report, and it indicates what we have said.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the woman is pregnant, she is not stoned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who performed li'an with his wife and disowned her child, then he proved himself false (in his accusation). Is his child returned to him? He said: If he proved himself false, he is given the flogging (for li'an) and his child is returned to him, and his wife is not returned to him forever.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who performed li'an with his wife and disowned her child, then contradicted himself after li'an, claiming the child was indeed his. I asked: Will the child be returned to him (as a son)? He said: No, and not even with honor, and he will not be returned to him, nor will it be permissible for him until the Day of Resurrection. So he does not contradict the first report, because the meaning of His words 'he will not be returned to him' is that he is not attached to him with complete attachment, so inheritance is established between them. Rather, he is attached to him in that the son inherits from him, but the father does not inherit from the son. And the report that indicates this is the one we presented earlier in the first chapter on Li'an from Zurara, which adds further clarification to that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the mutual imprecation (mula'ana) in which the husband accuses [his wife], denies paternity of the child, performs the imprecation, separates from her, and then says afterwards: 'The child is mine,' while contradicting himself [by denying and claiming]. He said: As for the woman, she does not return to him ever. As for the child, I return him to him if he claims him, and I do not leave his child [without inheritance]. The father has no inheritance from the child, and the child inherits the father, but the father does not inherit the child; the child's inheritance goes to his maternal uncles. If the father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles inherit him, and they do not inherit from him. And if anyone claims him as the son of the fornicator, he is given the corporal punishment.

Yunus narrated from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in a man who said to his wife, 'I have not come to you as a virgin (or: you have not remained a virgin),' he said, 'It is of no consequence, because the virginity (or: the hymen) goes away without sexual intercourse.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man says to his wife, 'I did not find you a virgin,' and he has no proof, it is said: He is flogged with the hadd punishment and he is allowed to remain with his wife, so that it does not contradict the first report, because the appropriate interpretation is that he is flogged with ta'zir (discretionary punishment), not a complete hadd, so that he does not harm a Muslim woman by exposure (to divorce).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yunus from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who said to his wife, 'I did not find you a virgin (or chaste):' He is beaten. I said, 'If he repeated it,' he said, 'He is beaten, for he is likely to stop.' Yunus said, 'He is beaten with a disciplinary beating, not a fixed punishment (hadd), so as not to harm a believing woman by implication (ta'rid).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: If a man commits adultery with his father's wife or his father's slave girl, that does not prohibit her from her husband, nor does the slave girl become prohibited to her master. That prohibition from him occurs only when he has intercourse with the slave girl while she is permissible to him; thus, that slave girl becomes permanently prohibited to his father and to his son. And if a man marries a woman with a valid marriage, the woman becomes prohibited to his father and to his son.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I said to Abu Ishaq Musa (peace be upon him): A man married a woman, but he died before consummating the marriage with her; is she permissible for his son? He said: They dislike it, because he possessed the marriage contract.

As for what al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the least act a man performs with a woman that makes her unlawful for his son and his father. He said: The boundary in that is sexual intercourse, whether apparent or hidden, that resembles touching the two private parts. So it does not contradict the two earlier reports, because this report is contrary to the Book of Allah, while the two earlier reports are consistent with it. Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not marry those women whom your fathers married.' And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And the wives of your sons who are from your loins.' And He did not restrict it to penetration, so it is appropriate that the prohibition attaches to the contract itself. With the understanding that this report is disconnected (mursal) and its chain is Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Yunus, and he is weak. And Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) singled him out from among the men from whom the owner of Nawadir al-Hikmah narrated, and said: 'What is specific to his narration, I do not narrate it.' And this is his image in terms of weakness; he is not objected to with his hadith, and it is possible that, along with his safety from that, there are two meanings. One of them is that the intended meaning is that if it is from the father or the son, the intercourse is apparent or hidden, resembling touching the private part without a contract. For that is the least that makes the woman unlawful for the father and the son, as we will clarify later, that whoever commits fornication with a woman, it is not permissible for his father and his son to contract marriage with her. The second aspect is that the intended meaning by mentioning the woman in the report is the slave girl, because the slave girl does not become unlawful by ownership itself, just as the free woman becomes unlawful by the contract itself. Rather, what makes her unlawful is penetration or what follows its manner, such as kissing, stripping, and looking at what is not permissible for non-owners to look at. As we will clarify later, if Allah wills.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them) that Ali (peace be upon him) said: When a man marries a woman, her daughter becomes forbidden to him if he has had intercourse with the mother; and if he has not had intercourse with the mother, there is no harm in him marrying the daughter. But when he marries the daughter and has intercourse with her, or even if he has not had intercourse with her, the mother becomes forbidden to him. And he said: 'Your stepdaughters are forbidden to you, whether they are under your guardianship or not.'

Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman and then divorced her before consummating the marriage. He said: Her daughter is permissible for him to marry, but her mother is not permissible for him.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj and Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The mother and the daughter are the same (permissible to marry), if he has not consummated the marriage with her. He means: if a man marries a woman and then divorces her before consummating the marriage, then if he wishes he may marry her mother, and if he wishes he may marry her daughter.

And as for what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): A man married a woman and consummated the marriage with her, then she died. Is it permissible for him to marry her mother? He said: Glory be to Allah, how can her mother be permissible for him when he has consummated the marriage with her? I said to him: And if she died before he consummated the marriage with her, is her mother permissible for him? He said: And what is the thing that becomes forbidden to him from her when he has not consummated the marriage with her? Thus, the ruling in this narration is also what we said in the first two narrations. It is all the same, given that Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, the narrator of this hadith, said 'I asked him' and did not specify who he was. It is possible that the one who asked him was not the Imam, from whose opinion one must return. Therefore, if this possibility holds, the objection based on it is nullified.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Fadala ibn Ayyub from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave who was freed, then married, and gave birth. Is it permissible for his first master to marry her daughter? He said: No, she is forbidden to him, and she is his daughter. The free woman and the slave woman are equal in this matter.

Abu Abdillah al-Bazawfari from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far, from Ali ibn Uthman and Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has a female slave, and she has a daughter who is also a slave, and he buys her [the daughter]. Is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with her? He said: No.

From him, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has a female slave and has sexual relations with her; is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: No. She is as Allah the Exalted said: 'Your step-daughters who are in your households'

From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Jabalah, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him: A man had a female slave who was freed, then she married, and gave birth. Is it permissible for her former master to marry her daughter? He said: No, she is forbidden to him.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife, and she became separate from him, and she had a daughter who was a slave-girl, and he bought her; is it permissible for him to have intercourse with her? He said: No.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Aban ibn Uthman from Razin, the seller of fabrics, said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man had a female slave, he had intercourse with her, then he sold her or she died, then he found her daughter; does he have intercourse with her? He said: Yes. Allah only forbade this from the free women, but as for the female slaves, there is no harm.

As for what al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammam ibn Isa and Khalaf ibn Rabi', from al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave whom he had sexual relations with, and she died, and then he marries her daughter. He said: There is no harm; she is not in the same position as a free woman. This report does not mention the sexual relation (in the prohibition), but rather it implies that he may marry her, and it is permissible for him to marry her later by owning her and using her. And what is prohibited for him is the sexual relation with her, according to what was stated previously regarding others, and that which also indicates that the ruling of the slave woman and the free woman in this matter is the same.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave who was freed and married, and bore a daughter to her first master, whether he could marry his daughter. He said: She is forbidden to him, and she is his slave daughter; the free woman is the same in this regard. Then he recited: 'Your step-daughters who are in your households'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with a woman and kissed her, other than the fact that he had not ejaculated into her, then he married her daughter. He said: If he had not ejaculated into the mother, there is no harm (in marrying the daughter), and if he had ejaculated, he should not marry her.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from 'Ulay ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman and looked at her head and part of her body: may he marry her daughter? He said: No, if he saw from her what is forbidden for others to see, then it is not permissible for him to marry her daughter. 3- From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabi' who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who married a woman and stayed with her for days, unable to consummate the marriage, except that he had seen from her what is forbidden for others to see, then he divorced her: is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: Is it permissible for him, when he has seen from her mother what he saw? 4- Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) like it. Therefore, the ruling in these narrations is a type of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram), because the one that necessitates prohibition is the first narration, because it is consistent with the apparent meaning of the Book. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'And your stepdaughters who are in your households from your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage; but if you have not consummated the marriage, there is no blame upon you [to marry them].'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abdullah al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him about a man who has sexual intercourse with a woman, is she permissible for his son? Or if the son has sexual intercourse with her, is she permissible for his father? He said: If the father or the son touched her and took from her (consummated), then she is not permissible.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who committed fornication with a woman, is it permissible for his son to marry her? He said: No.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Indeed, the forbidden (act) does not invalidate the permissible.

From him, from Al-Hasan, from Safwan, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Indeed, the forbidden act does not corrupt the permissible. Therefore, the approach regarding these two reports is to specify them: if a man has a wife with whom he has consummated the marriage, and his father or son commits fornication with her, that does not make the wife forbidden to him. Similarly, it does not prevent him from having intercourse with the slave girl if her intercourse is after ownership, provided he had not yet contracted marriage with her and committed fornication with her, and owned her, then had intercourse with her, and then his son committed fornication with her, that prevents him from contracting marriage with her and making her permissible through ownership. This indicates this distinction.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has a female slave, and his son has sexual intercourse with her before the grandfather (father) has intercourse with her, or a man commits fornication with a woman, is it permissible for his son to marry her? He said: No. That is only if the father married her and had intercourse with her, then his son committed fornication with her, it would not harm him, because the forbidden act does not invalidate the permissible. And similarly with the female slave.

And as for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman from Murazm who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he was asked about a woman who ordered her son to have intercourse with a concubine belonging to her husband. He said: 'She is sinful and her son is sinful.' And some of these people asked me about this issue, so I said to them: 'Retain her, for the permissible does not invalidate the permissible, so it does not contradict the first report, because in this report it is not stated that she ordered her son to have intercourse with her before the father's penetration or after it. And if that is not explicit in its apparent meaning and it accommodates both meanings, we apply it to what we have previously established, because the detailed report is more worthy of being applied than the general one.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Kufi, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a boy who plays with a girl whom he does not own and has not reached puberty, is it permissible for his father to buy her and have intercourse with her? He said: The forbidden act does not make the permissible forbidden, so this report does not contradict the reports we have previously mentioned, because his saying 'plays with a girl' may be a metaphor for non-intercourse; as for with intercourse, then she becomes forbidden to him in all cases, according to what we have previously mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna said: I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man entered and asked him about a man who has sexual relations with a woman unlawfully (zina), whether he may marry her. He said: Yes, and [also] her mother and her daughter.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and a man asked him: 'A man committed fornication with a woman; is her daughter permissible (for him to marry)?' He said: 'Yes, for the forbidden act does not invalidate the permissible.'

From him, from Al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Sa'id asked him about a man who married a woman in a casual marriage (sifah), is her daughter permissible to him? He said: Yes, for the forbidden does not make the permissible forbidden. Muammad ibn Al-Hasan said: The explanation of these narrations with me, and what has come in its meaning, is that if a man has a wife and consummates the marriage with her, then he has sexual relations with her mother or daughter, she does not become forbidden to him. But if he has sexual relations with her while she is not his wife, then he intends to contract marriage with her, then that becomes forbidden to him. This indicates this distinction.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who has sexual relations with a woman, whether he may marry her daughter? He said: No (he cannot marry the daughter), but if he had a wife, then he had sexual relations with her mother or her sister, the one he has (the wife) is not forbidden to him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man commits fornication with a woman, her daughter does not become permissible to him forever, even if he had previously married the daughter and had not yet consummated the marriage, then his marriage is annulled. And if he married the daughter and consummated the marriage, then later committed fornication with her mother, his fornication with the mother does not annul the marriage to the daughter, provided he had already entered into her. And this is His saying: 'That which is forbidden does not annul that which is permissible, if it is thus.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman ibn 'Isa and 'Ali ibn Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had sexual intercourse with a woman (illicitly), whether he may marry her daughter? He said: Yes, O Sa'id, for the forbidden (relationship) does not invalidate the permissible.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from one who narrated it from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man committed fornication with a woman; is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: What a forbidden thing has ever made a permissible thing permissible. The ruling in these two narrations and what follows their pattern, which includes the wording of marriage in the future or present, is that if the fornication was with the woman without sexual intercourse and penetration, then as for with intercourse and penetration, it is not permissible, according to what we have previously mentioned, which indicates this distinction.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with a woman and kissed her, provided that he had not ejaculated into her, and then he married her daughter. He said: If he had not ejaculated into the mother, there is no harm (in marrying the daughter); but if he had ejaculated into her, he should not marry her daughter.

From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had illicit sexual relations with a woman, is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: If it was a kiss or something similar, let him marry her daughter. And if it was intercourse, then he should not marry her daughter, but she may marry him if she wishes. And that which indicates that sexual intercourse after entry does not prohibit anything additional to what we have previously mentioned.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hanafiyya (al-Halabi), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a young woman, then consummated the marriage with her, then was tested with her mother, and had intercourse with her mother: Is his wife forbidden to him? He said: No, for he does not make the permissible forbidden due to the forbidden.

From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who committed zina with the mother of his wife, or her daughter, or her sister, he said: That does not prohibit her from him. Then he said: Whatever was forbidden never made permissible what was lawful. And that which indicates what we said, that it prohibits at the beginning of marriage, is that it was prohibited due to breastfeeding; so if it is due to lineage, it is more worthy of prohibition. This was narrated.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who had sexual intercourse with a woman, whether he may marry her mother from breastfeeding or her daughter? He said: No.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu al-Maghra' from al-Halabi who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The woman who is publicly known for fornication is not married off, nor is the man who is publicly known for fornication married off, unless repentance is known from them.

And by the chain of narration, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him about a man who had illicit sexual intercourse with a woman, and then later wanted to marry her. He said: 'If she repents, it is lawful for him to marry her.' I asked him: 'How is her repentance known?' He said: 'He invites her to what they were upon of the forbidden act (illicit intercourse); if she refuses and seeks forgiveness from her Lord, then you will know her repentance.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who is permitted to marry a woman with whom he has been committing fornication. He said: If he perceives maturity (or good conduct) in her, then yes (it is permissible). Otherwise, he should court her for fornication. If she continues with him, she becomes forbidden to him. And if she refuses, he should marry her.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: He was asked about a man who was pleased with a woman and inquired about her; if the praise for her was something in fornication (or lewdness), he said: 'There is no harm in him marrying her and making her chaste.' The meaning in this report is one of two things: either that this is informing about the validity of the contract even if he had done a prohibited act, or that the intended meaning of his saying 'There is no harm in him marrying her and making her chaste' is 'if she repents,' and the report does not indicate that there is no harm in that while she persists in the lewd act.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorced his wife, or she redeemed herself (kharaj), or he separated from her (bara'a), is it permissible for him to marry her sister? He said: If he freed her bond of marriage and he did not have a right of return over her, then it is permissible for him to propose to her sister. From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him about a man whose wife redeemed herself from him, is it permissible for him to propose to her sister before her waiting period expires? He said: When her bond of marriage is freed and he does not have a right of return, then it is permissible for him to propose to her sister.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' from Aban from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant, [asking]: Does he marry her sister before she gives birth? He said: He does not marry her until the waiting period is complete. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as: If it is a revocable divorce in which he has the right of return, based on the reports we have previously presented, and they included that if he divorces her with a final divorce, it is permissible for him to contract marriage with her sister even if she has not exited the waiting period. Those reports are detailed, and acting upon them is more preferable than acting upon this general report.

And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife, does he marry her sister? He said: No, until her waiting period (iddah) expires. Therefore, the meaning in this report is also what we previously mentioned in the preceding report, namely interpreting it as referring to a revocable divorce (talaq raj'i) rather than an irrevocable one (talaq ba'in), because we only permitted that [marriage to the sister] in the case of an irrevocable divorce, and nothing else.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nuḍr ibn Suwayd from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: When a man has two sisters who are enslaved, and he marries one of them, then decides to marry the second, he should not marry the other until the first leaves his ownership, whether by him gifting her or selling her. And if he gifts her to his son, it suffices him.

Abu Abdillah al-Bazawfari from Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had two sister-slaves, and he had intercourse with one of them, then desired the other. He said: 'He should keep this one aside and have intercourse with the other.' I said: 'But his desire may be directed toward the first one.' He said: 'He should not approach her until he frees that one from his ownership.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about two sister-slaves and combining them, he said: It is valid, and I do not prefer it for you. And I asked him about a mother and daughter who are slave-women, he said: It is more intense for them, and I do not prefer it for you. So it does not contradict what has preceded from the narrations, because in its apparent meaning it is not that combining them in sexual intercourse is valid, and if that is not in its apparent meaning, we interpret it that combining them in ownership is valid, and his saying (peace be upon him) 'and I do not prefer it for you' is due to the dislike of combining them in ownership, because whoever owns them together, perhaps his soul will desire and his lust will call him to have intercourse with both, so he will do that and become blameworthy.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya ibn Sam, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what people narrate from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding certain matters of the private parts, which he did not command nor forbid for the general public, but only for himself and his offspring. I said, 'How can that be?' He said, 'A verse made them permissible, and another verse made them forbidden.' We said, 'Is it that one of them abrogated the other, or are both clear rulings that should be acted upon?' He said, 'He had already explained it to them when he forbade it for himself and his offspring.' We said, 'What prevented him from explaining that to the people?' He said, 'He feared that they would not obey.' And if the Commander of the Faithful had firmly established his position, he would have implemented the entire Book of Allah and all the truth.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife, then another man marries her after him, and she bears a child to the latter. Is the child of the latter permissible for marriage to the child of the first from a different woman? He said: Yes. And I asked him about a man who manumits his female slave, then another man marries her after him, and she bears a child to the latter. Is the child of the latter permissible for marriage to the child of the one who manumitted her? He said: Yes.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a female slave, has intercourse with her seeking offspring, but is not granted a child from her. He then gifts her to his brother or sells her, and she bears him children. Should he marry his son to the daughter of his brother from her? He said, 'Repeat it to me.' I repeated it to him. He said, 'There is no objection.'
