Al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Baraqi, from Ali ibn Idris, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a slave-girl who was in my ownership, and I had sexual intercourse with her, then she was freed from my ownership and gave birth to a daughter. Is it permissible for my son to marry her? He said: Yes, there is no objection, before and after intercourse, they are the same.

Al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sirafi said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about this matter, so he said: 'Repeat it to me.' I said to him: 'I had a slave-girl who did not bear me a child, so I sold her. She bore a child to someone else, and I have a child by another woman. Should I marry my child to her child?' He said: 'Marry the child she had before you [married her].' He means: before you had [a child with her].

And what Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali narrated, he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman and marries his son to her daughter, and he said: If the daughter is already married to him before he marries her, there is no harm. The way to understand these two reports is to interpret them as a type of dislike (karahah) rather than prohibition (haram), because the causes of prohibition are known, and nothing from among them is present here. And that which indicates that the intended meaning of both is a type of dislike is according to what we have previously established.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Abu Hammam Isma'il ibn Hammam, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who marries a woman and marries his daughter to her son, then divorces her, and another man marries her and she bears a daughter from him; he disliked that one of his sons marry her because she was his wife (mother of the son), so he divorced her, and she became like a mother to him, and before that she was a mother to him. This report came explicitly indicating the dislike (karahah) that we mentioned.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Does a man marry the woman who accepted him (as her husband)?' He said: 'Glory be to Allah, what did Allah forbid him from that?'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One should not marry the woman who received him (in childbirth) nor her daughter.

And Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Abu Muhammad Al-Ansari from Amr ibn Shimmer from Jabir who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the midwife, is it permissible for the newborn to marry her? He said: No, and not her daughter either, for she is from among his mothers. The resolution in these two narrations is to interpret them as indicating a type of dislike (karahah) if the midwife had accepted and raised the newborn. If she did not raise him, then that is not disliked either in any case, and that which reveals what we mentioned.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan about the midwife who attends to a man, is it permissible for him to marry her? He said: If she had attended to him once, twice, or three times, there is no harm. But if she had attended to him, raised him, and fostered him, then I prohibit myself from her, and my children, and in another narration, my close friend.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Do not marry (your daughter) to the son of the paternal uncle and the son of the maternal uncle without their permission.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not permissible for a man to marry two sisters (or close aunts) simultaneously, specifically between a woman and her paternal aunt, nor between a woman and her maternal aunt.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a woman who marries on top of her paternal aunt and maternal aunt. He said: There is no harm. And he said: Marry the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt upon the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister. And do not marry the daughter of the brother and the sister upon the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt, except with their consent. Then whoever does that, his marriage is invalid. With the understanding that the two reports can bear another meaning, which is that we interpret them as a form of taqiyya (prudent dissimulation), because all of the Sunnis differ with us in this matter and claim that this is a matter of consensus, and this is its ruling: taqiyya applies to it.

And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A woman is not married off to her paternal aunt, nor to her maternal aunt, nor to her milk-sister. The meaning in this report is like the meaning in what preceded regarding the paternal and maternal aunts of lineage, that it is not permissible without consent. As for with consent, there is no harm in it, similar to that of lineage. As for marrying her to her milk-sister, it is prohibited in all cases, unless the sister is separated by death or a definitive divorce.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad, what do you say about a man who marries a Christian woman in preference to a Muslim woman?' I said: 'I am your ransom, and what is my opinion before your opinion?' He said: 'You will say it, for you know my opinion by my statement.' I said: 'The marriage of a Christian woman to a Muslim man is not permissible, nor is the marriage of a non-Muslim woman [to a Muslim man].' He said: 'Why?' I said: 'Because of the statement of Allah, the Exalted: 'And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe.'' 'And [also] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you.' I said: 'His statement: 'And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe' abrogates this verse.' He smiled and then remained silent.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from Durusta al-Wasiti, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The marriage of the People of the Book is not proper (or: is not permissible). I said: 'I am your ransom, where is its prohibition?' He said: 'His saying, Exalted is He: Do not hold the ties of the disbelievers [in marriage].'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'The chaste women from those who were given the Book before you.' He said: It is abrogated by His saying: 'Do not hold to the ties of marriage of the disbelieving women.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the food of the People of the Book and their marriage, is it permissible? He said: Yes. A Jewish woman was under the authority of Talha.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the marriage of a Jewish woman and a Christian woman. He said: There is no objection to it. Do you not know that a Jewish woman was under the authority of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the believing man who marries a Christian and a Jew, he (the Imam) said: If he consummates the marriage with the Muslim woman, what does he do with the Jewess and the Christianess? I said to him: He will have desire for them. He said: If he does, he must prevent them from drinking wine and eating pork. And know that there is a slight displeasure (ghadadhah) upon him regarding their religion. And what has occurred in the manner of these narrations which included the permissibility of marrying Jewish and Christian women, they bear aspects of interpretation: one being that they may have been expressed as taqiyya (dissimulation), because all those who differ from us go to the permissibility of that, so it is permissible that these narrations came in agreement with them, just as their counterparts came for that reason. And another being that these narrations may have referred to the permissibility of marrying the weak-minded (or simple) women among them, who do not hold disbelief with firm adherence to it and tribal loyalty to it. And for one with this description, the marriage contract is permissible. This indicates it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the marriage of the Jewish and Christian women. He said: It is not suitable for a Muslim to marry a Jewish woman nor a Christian woman. Only the 'bluteh' (temporary marriage) is permissible from them, and this includes the state of necessity and the absence of a Muslim woman, and this runs in the manner of the permissibility of the meat of the dead animal when there is fear for the life.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is not fitting for a Muslim to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman while he finds a free Muslim woman or a slave Muslim woman.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud from Abu Ayyub from Hafs ibn Ghiyath said: Some of my brothers wrote to me to ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about some matters, so I asked him about the captive: does he marry in the land of war? He said: I dislike that. If he does in the land of the Romans, it is not forbidden and it is a marriage. As for the Turks, the Daylamites, and the Khazars, it is not permissible for him to do that. And among them is that he takes that as permission for the contract upon them, the contract of Mut'ah rather than permanent marriage, as we have clarified in what preceded, and this adds to the clarification.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara who said: I heard him say: There is no harm in marrying a Jewish or Christian woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah) even if he already has a permanent wife. As for what has been narrated in the reports that include rulings regarding what is established upon the validity of the contract, such as inheritance, divorce, and the waiting period (iddah), and similar matters, these reports encompass all that we have mentioned. It is also possible that these rulings are specific to a man who was Jewish or Christian and had a Jewish or Christian wife, and then he converted to Islam; for the contract does not cease upon his conversion, but remains valid, and these rulings apply to him according to what has come in the reports. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Regarding a man who migrated and left his wife among the polytheists, then she joined him afterwards: Should he retain her in marriage or does the bond of marriage between them cease? He said: No, rather he retains her and she is his wife.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr who said: Qasim ibn 'Urwah informed me from Abu al-Abbas al-Qabbagh who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while we were with him. About the 'ariyyah (temporary loan) of the private part, he said: It is haram. Then he paused for a little while and said: But there is no harm in a man making his female slave permissible (halal) for his brother.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Hasan al-Attar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the 'loan' of the private part (temporary marriage). He said: 'There is no harm in it.' I said: 'But if a child is born from it?' He said: 'It belongs to the owner of the girl, unless it is stipulated otherwise.' The correct interpretation of this narration is that we should understand the questioner's inquiry about the 'loan of the private part' as a form of concession, and that his intended meaning was the temporary marriage (mut'ah) which we have previously mentioned. He called it a 'loan' because it was not a permanent contract nor permanent ownership, thus resembling a loan (ariyyah) from which the owner can reclaim it; therefore, the name 'loan' was applied to it, even though strictly speaking, its permanent use is not permissible, as indicated by the first narration.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), that he said: For the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian, if his wife converts to Islam while he does not, he said: They remain upon their marriage, and they are not separated, and he is not left to take her out of the land of Islam into disbelief.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who has a Christian wife and she converts to Islam; is it permissible for her to remain with him? He said: If she converts, she is not permissible for him. I said: May I be your ransom, but if the husband converts after that, are they still on the marriage? He said: No, with a new marriage, so it does not contradict the first report, because the meaning is that we interpret it as applying to one who has breached the conditions of the dhimma (covenant). For if that is the case and his wife converts, he is awaited until her waiting period expires. If he converts, he is more entitled to her; and if he does not convert, she has been separated from him. And that which indicates this is that they say: Whenever they breach the conditions of the dhimma, their dhimma is invalidated, as narrated.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) accepted the Jizyah from the People of the Covenant on the condition that they do not consume usury, do not eat the meat of pigs, and do not marry sisters, nor the daughters of brothers, nor the daughters of sisters. Whoever among them does that, the covenant of God and His Messenger is released from them, and they have no covenant today. And it is possible that the report is specific to one who did not originally have a covenant, in that he is in the House of War. For if that is the case, the woman is awaited until her waiting period expires. If he converts before that, he has more right to her. And if her waiting period expires and he does not convert, then she has mastery over herself.

From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi, from Ali ibn Ri'ab and Aban together, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Zoroastrian man who had a wife upon his religion, then he converted to Islam or she converted. He said: Wait for the completion of her waiting period (iddah). If he converts, they remain upon their first marriage. If he does not convert until the waiting period is completed, then she is divorced from him. And that which indicates that as long as he is upon the conditions of the dhimma (non-Muslim subject), she does not divorce from him, even if her waiting period is completed.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the People of the Book and all those who have a covenant (dhimmah), if one of the spouses converts to Islam, they remain upon their marriage, and he is not permitted to take her out of the land of Islam to another land, nor sleep with her, but he visits her during the day. As for the polytheists, they are like the polytheists of the Arabs and others; they remain upon their marriage until the expiration of the waiting period (iddah). If the woman converts and then the man converts before the expiration of her waiting period, she is his wife. If he does not convert except after the expiration of her waiting period, then she is divorced from him and there is no claim for him upon her. And likewise all those who have no covenant. And it is not fitting for a Muslim to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman while he finds a free woman or a slave woman.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believer should not marry the Nāsibah (female opponent of the Imams) who is known for that (status).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abd Allah ibn Muskān said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Nāsibī (one known for enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) whose enmity is known. Can the believer marry him, while he is capable of repelling him, and he does not know of the repulsion? He said: The believer does not marry the Nāsibīyah, nor does the Nāsibī marry a believing woman, nor does the weak believer marry a believing woman.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from the multitude of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man entered upon Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said: 'Your mother, the Shaybaniyyah, is a Kharijite who curses Ali (peace be upon him). If it pleases you that I let you hear it from her, I will let you hear it.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'So when tomorrow comes, at the time you intend to go out as you usually do, return and hide in the side of the house.' He said: 'So when it was the next day, he hid in the side of the house, and the man came and spoke to her, and that was made clear from her, so he released her (from his desire/attention), and she pleased him.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilah and from Sindi, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the well-known woman (of the sect), should she be married to the Nāsib (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt)? He said: No, because the Nāsib is a disbeliever. I said: Should she be married to a man who is neither Nāsib nor well-known (of the sect)? He said: The one who is neither is more beloved to me than the well-known one.

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Nassaabi (one who hates the Ahl al-Bayt) was mentioned, so he said: Do not marry them, and do not eat their slaughtered meat, and do not reside with them.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nuḍr ibn Suwayd from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): By what is a man considered a Muslim, making his marriage and inheritance permissible, and by what is his blood protected? He said: His blood is protected by Islam when he manifests it, and his marriage and inheritance become permissible. He is not contradictory to what we have mentioned, because whoever manifests enmity and elevation (al-Naṣb) towards the Family of the Messenger (peace be upon him) has not truly manifested Islam, but is at the peak of manifesting disbelief. And the report only included those who manifested Islam, and these (the Naṣāʾib) are excluded from it.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Karim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Marry them to the Shakkak, and do not marry them off to others, because the woman takes from the religion of her husband and he compels her to his religion. This is not contradictory to what we have previously mentioned, because it is applicable to the weak-minded and the simple-minded among them, rather than those who openly declare enmity with those we mentioned, which clarifies what we have mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Should I marry a Murji'a or a Haruriyya? He said: There is no harm for you in the foolish ones of the women. Zurara said: I said, By Allah, they are nothing but believers or disbelievers. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And where are the people of piety? The saying of Allah, the Exalted, is truer than your saying. Except for the weak among men and women and children who cannot devise a means nor are they guided a way.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil, from Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Marry the dull/simple-minded women who do not exhibit enmity (towards the Ahl al-Bayt) and the weak/submissive ones.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May God perfect you. I fear that it is not permissible for me to marry, meaning, someone who is not upon the same [religious state] as he is. He said: What prevents you from the foolishness of women who are weak/ignorant, who do not raise [the standard of] enmity (Nasb) and do not know what you are upon?

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a woman whose husband dies, and she gives birth and marries before four months and ten days have passed for her. He said: If he had consummated the marriage with her, they were separated, and then she never becomes permissible to him again. She completes the waiting period remaining from the first [husband], and begins a new waiting period from the second [husband] of three menstrual periods. And if he had not consummated the marriage with her, they were separated, and she completes the waiting period remaining from the first [husband], and he is considered a suitor among suitors. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: His saying 'he is a suitor among suitors' is interpreted as referring to one who contracted the marriage with her while he did not know that she was in a waiting period. At that time, the contract is permissible for him after the completion of her waiting period. This indicates that.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him): 'It has reached us from your father that if a man marries a woman during her waiting period (ʿiddah), she is not permissible to him ever.' He said: 'This is if he was knowledgeable. But if he was ignorant, he divorces her, she completes her waiting period, and then he marries her with a new marriage contract.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Humran said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who married during her waiting period out of ignorance on her part. He said: 'I do not see any fault upon her, and they are separated from the one she married, and she does not become permissible to him forever.' The meaning in this report is that we assume he had intercourse with her; for if that is the case, she does not become permissible to him forever, whether he was ignorant or knowledgeable. And she becomes permissible with ignorance only if he had not had intercourse with her, which indicates that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man marries a woman during her waiting period and consummates the marriage with her, she becomes permanently forbidden to him, whether he was aware or ignorant. And if he did not consummate with her, she becomes permissible for the ignorant one, but not for the other (the aware one).

And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan from Jamil from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a woman who married before her waiting period ended, he said: They are separated, and she observes one waiting period for both.

Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in Regarding a woman who lost her husband or news of his death was brought to her, so she married, then her husband returned after that and divorced her, he said: She observes a single waiting period from both of them together, which is three months, and the latter [husband] cannot marry her ever.

Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan, from Jamil, from Ibn Bukayr, or from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the woman who marries during her waiting period. He said: They are separated, and she observes one waiting period from both of them together. These narrations are not contradictory to what preceded from the narrations, because in the apparent meaning of these narrations, the second husband had not yet consummated the marriage with her. And we only obligated the second waiting period if he had consummated the marriage with her. As for if he did not consummate, then one waiting period suffices for her, and there is no contradiction between the narrations.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman while she had a husband, and he did not know, then the first [husband] divorced her or died, then the second [husband] found out: Should he remarry her? He said: No, until her waiting period expires.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, then it became clear to him after he had consummated the marriage with her that she had an absent husband. He left her, then the husband arrived and either divorced her or died. Should the man who married her (and did not know she had a husband) marry her again after this? He said: 'I do not like for him to marry her until she marries another husband.' The reason in this report is a type of dislike (karahah). For that reason he said 'and I do not like for him to marry her,' and he did not say 'and it is not permissible.' The reason in the two reports, in my view, is that it was permissible for him to marry her if the woman did not intend (by choice) the marriage while knowing that her husband was still alive as he was; rather, he had been absent from her, so news of him was brought to her, or divorce from him reached her. Because if she had intended that while knowing the state of the husband, she would be a fornicator (zaniyah). And if she is a fornicator, it is not permissible for him to contract marriage with her ever, because whoever marries a woman with a husband (dhat ba'l) is not permissible for her ever, as we explained in our Great Book. And that which indicates that whenever she intends that while knowing the state of the husband, she is a fornicator.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: He was asked about a woman who had a husband absent from her, so she married another husband. He said: If it was brought to the Imam, and witnesses testified against her that she had an absent husband, and that his provisions and news came to her from him, and that she had married another husband, then it was upon the Imam to lash her and separate her from the one she married. It was said to him: What is done with the dowry she took from him? He said: If he had intercourse with her, he takes it; and if he did not have intercourse with her, then all that she took from him is forbidden to her, like the wage of the prostitute.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh and Sindiyy ibn Muhammad from Safwan ibn Yahya from Shu'ayb al-Aqarquti who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman who had a husband, and he did not know. He said: The woman is stoned, and there is no penalty upon the man if he did not know. I mentioned that to Abu Basir, who said to me: By God, Jafar (peace be upon him) said: The woman is stoned and the man is lashed with the legal punishment, and he said with his hands on his chest scratching it: I do not think that our Master's knowledge was complete. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between what Shu'ayb narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and what Abu Basir heard from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), because what Abu Basir heard was regarding the case where the man married her while he knew that she had a husband, and the penalty was incumbent upon him as well because he was an adulterer. There is no contradiction between the two reports and the two legal opinions; rather, the matter became confused for Abu Basir, so he did not distinguish one question from the other, and he assumed that there was a contradiction between them.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If a man sends news to his family or they are informed that he has divorced her, and she completes her waiting period, then she marries another man, and her first husband comes back, then the first is more entitled to her than this latter one; whether he had consummated the marriage or not. And the latter cannot marry her again, and she is entitled to the dowry for what he made lawful of her private part.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Asam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: If a man is announced to his family and they inform her that he has divorced her, so she observes her waiting period, then she marries another, and then the first husband comes later, then the first is more entitled to her than this latter one. Whether the first had consummated the marriage or not, the latter is never allowed to marry her again. She is entitled to the dowry from the latter because he made lawful her private part. There is no contradiction between these two reports and the earlier reports we presented, which state that he may marry her after the expiration of the waiting period, if her first husband divorced her. Because the explanation for these two reports is that we interpret them as referring to one who knew that she had a remaining husband and proceeded with the marriage. For she is not lawful to him forever. And this is what we said previously: that one who marries a woman who has a husband, if she is not divorced, is not lawful to her forever. And whoever has this ruling is a fornicator, and the ruling regarding him is what we said.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Nawfali, from al-'Ayashi, from 'Isa ibn 'Abdullah al-Hashimi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: There is no objection to marrying her during her postpartum bleeding period, but he should not have sexual intercourse with her until she is purified from the postpartum blood.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) lashed a man who married a woman during her postpartum bleeding period. So it does not contradict the first report, because it is possible that he only established the punishment upon him because he had intercourse with her before her postpartum blood had completely exited, rather than establishing the punishment because he married her. And that which indicates this is that the narrator of this hadith, who is Abdullah ibn Sinan, narrated the like of the first report.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated via his chain from Abdillah ibn Sinan, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the woman who gives birth: Is it permissible for her to marry before she becomes pure? He said: When she gives birth, she may marry, but it is not permissible for her husband to have intercourse with her until she becomes pure. It is also possible that the limit was established for her because she was still in the waiting period of her husband who died for her, because anyone in this situation needs to observe the longer of the two waiting periods. If she gives birth before the waiting period ends, she needs to complete four months and ten days. And if four months and ten days have passed for her, she waits for her childbirth after that. This indicates that.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from some of his teachers, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant; she gave birth before four months and ten days had passed, and she married before those four months and ten days were completed. He said: I see that he should divorce her, then not propose to her until the end of the two periods has passed. If the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her off; if they wish, they may keep her, and return his dowry to him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: It is not permissible for a terminally ill person to divorce, but he may marry. If he marries and consummates the marriage, it is valid; but if he does not consummate it until he dies in his illness, his marriage is void, she receives no dowry, and she inherits no share.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man whose death approaches, so he sends for his neighbor and marries him his daughter for one thousand dirhams. Is his marriage valid? He said: Yes. So it does not contradict the first narration, because the meaning in this report is that we assume he consummated the marriage with her, because if that were the case, the contract would be valid as detailed in the first report. And if he did not consummate the marriage with her and then died, the contract would be invalid.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Ziyad ibn Sūqah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Is there a limit for breastfeeding that is taken into account? He said: Breastfeeding does not prohibit (marriage) for less than breastfeeding for a day and a night, or fifteen consecutive sucklings from one mother, from the milk of one male (animal), without being interrupted by sucklings from another mother. And if a mother breastfed a boy or a girl ten sucklings from the milk of one male, and another mother breastfed her ten sucklings from the milk of another male, the marriage would not be prohibited.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman or another, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fifteen sucklings do not cause prohibition (permanent) prohibition (of marriage). This does not contradict the first report, because the way to reconcile them is to carry it upon the fact that they were separate, in that the suckling of another woman entered between them. For that does not cause prohibition, as clarified in the first report.'

And as for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-'Ala' ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Nursing does not make forbidden (in marriage) except that which causes the flesh to grow and the bone to strengthen.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition (of marriage) except that which nourishes the flesh and the blood.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We are a large household, and sometimes joy and sorrow gather men and women together. Sometimes a woman feels shy to uncover her head in front of the man with whom she shares breastfeeding kinship, and sometimes a man feels it is trivial to look at that. So, what is it that makes breastfeeding prohibitive?' He said: 'That which nourishes flesh and blood.' I said: 'And what is that which nourishes flesh and blood?' He said: 'It was said [that it is] ten sucklings.' I said: 'Does it make prohibitive with ten sucklings?' He said: 'Leave it [alone].' And he said: 'What makes kinship prohibitive, that is what makes breastfeeding prohibitive.' This does not contradict the first report either, because he did not say that ten sucklings make prohibitive by themselves, but rather he attributed it to others, saying: 'It was said.' So if that were authentic, he would have informed about it himself. And that which indicates this is that when the questioner asked him about the authenticity of that, he said to him: 'Leave it.' So if it were authentic, he would have said to him: 'Yes,' and he did not shift his answer to something else for the sake of some expediency.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition (in marriage) except that which strengthens the bone and grows the flesh. As for the first suckling, the second, and the third, up to ten, if they are separate (occasions), there is no objection.

And what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a boy who breastfeeds once and twice, and he said: 'It does not make marriage forbidden.' So I counted for him until I completed ten breastfeedings. He said: 'If they are separate, then no [it does not make it forbidden].' Therefore, these two narrations do not indicate that ten breastfeedings, if they are not separate, make it forbidden except through the implication of the context (dalil al-khitab), not by their explicit text (sarih), and the implication of the context may be set aside by those who consider it sound due to the establishment of a proof for the obligation of setting it aside, and the narration that necessitates turning away from the apparent meaning of the context and also indicates it has already passed.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him, 'What amount of breastfeeding makes kinship (mahram) prohibited?' He said, 'That which nourishes the flesh and strengthens the bone.' I said, 'Do ten sucklings make it prohibited?' He said, 'No, because they do not nourish the flesh nor strengthen the bone; ten sucklings.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Ten sucklings do not make anything (of kinship) forbidden.
From him, from his two brothers, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: Ten feedings do not prohibit anything.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, it was narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The breastfeeding that causes flesh and blood to grow is that which continues until the ribs are formed, the body is fully developed, and the soul (of the infant) is completed.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il who said: He narrated to me Abu al-Hasan Zarif from Tha'laba from Aban from Ibn Abi Ya'fur He said: I asked him about what is prohibited by breastfeeding. He said: When the infant breastfeeds until its belly is full, for that causes the growth of flesh and blood, and that is what causes prohibition. So there is no contradiction between these two narrations and the first narration which we relied upon, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'when he breastfeeds until his belly is full' is an explanation for every suckling, because it is what is considered in this chapter, rather than the meaning of the sucklings being the suckles, as many people assume, for that is what causes the growth of flesh and bone.

And regarding what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition (of marriage) except if it is performed by a woman who is compelled, or a servant, or a wet-nurse, and then she breastfeeds ten times, causing the boy to be satiated and to sleep. This report also does not contradict what we have previously presented, because its apparent meaning is set aside by consensus, since a woman who is neither compelled, nor a servant, nor a wet-nurse can still cause prohibition through breastfeeding, whether she is a woman volunteering to breastfeed a child, or she was asked to do so, or due to other causes leading to that. It is also possible that the intended meaning here is the negation of prohibition for one who breastfeeds him once or twice.

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'Some of your freed slaves married into a family, and the women claimed that there was breastfeeding (radha') between them.' He said, 'As for one breastfeeding and two breastfeedings, it is of no consequence unless the nurse is a hired woman who resides with them.' He (peace be upon him) explicitly clarified in this narration that what is meant by that is what we have stated regarding one and two breastfeedings, excluding what exceeds that until it reaches the limit that causes prohibition, as we have clarified.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfa ibn Mansur, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about breastfeeding, and he said: 'Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition except for what is sucked from a single breast over two complete years.' The approach in this report is to interpret his statement 'two complete years' as a time-condition for the breastfeeding itself, not as the duration to be observed for the prohibition to take effect. Thus, it is as if he said: 'Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition except for what is sucked from a single breast within two complete years.' And we said this because if breastfeeding occurs after the two years, it does not cause prohibition, which indicates this ruling.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ali ibn Asbat who said: Ibn Faddal asked Ibn Bukayr in the mosque, saying: 'What do you say about a woman who breastfed a boy for two years, then breastfed a girl for less than two years, until the two years were completed? Does that invalidate the relationship between them?' He said: 'That does not invalidate the relationship between them, because it is breastfeeding after weaning. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no breastfeeding after weaning.' Meaning, when two years are completed for the boy or the girl, they have exited the limit of milk, and it does not invalidate the relationship between him and anyone who drinks from his milk. He said: 'And our companions say that it does not invalidate unless the boy and the girl drink sip by sip.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no breastfeeding (that causes kinship) after the two years, before weaning.

From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no breastfeeding (creating kinship) after weaning.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, what is weaning?' He said: 'The two years which Allah the Exalted said.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Breastfeeding after two years, before weaning, causes prohibition (of marriage), because this report is consistent with the Sunni view, and it was issued in the manner of precautionary piety (taqiyyah).

Al-'Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla' narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about breastfeeding, and he said: Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition except what is sucked from a single breast for a year. This is a rare, unusual report, upon which action is withheld by consensus. And its ruling is that it is not objected against the numerous reports, for what we have clarified in other places.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the milk of the bull (sire), so he said: 'It is when your wife nurses from your milk and the milk of your son who is the son of another woman, then it is forbidden.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who had two wives, and each of them bore him a son. Then one of his wives went and breastfed a girl from among the people. Is it appropriate for his son to marry this girl? He said: No, because she was breastfed with the milk of the old man.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The concubine of a man breastfed a boy, and he has a daughter from another wife. Is it permissible for that boy to marry this daughter?' He said: 'I do not like to marry the daughter of a man from whose child's milk I have drunk.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Isa ibn Ja'far ibn Isa asked Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) about a woman who breastfed a boy for me, asking: Is it permissible for me to marry the daughter of her husband? He said to me: 'How good is what you asked from here! It is assumed that people will say: His wife is forbidden to him because of the milk of the stallion (sire). This is the milk of the stallion, nothing else.' I said to him: 'Indeed, the girl is not the daughter of the woman who breastfed for me; she is the daughter of another.' He said: 'Even if there were ten [daughters] scattered [from different sources], nothing would be permissible for you from them, and they would be in the position of your daughters.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Al-Hisham ibn Salim from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a boy who was nursed by a woman: is it permissible for him to marry her sister by the father through nursing? He said: No, for they have all been nursed from the milk of one single bull from one woman. I said: Does he marry her sister by the mother through nursing? He said: There is no harm in that, for her sister who did not nurse him, her bull was different from the bull of the one who nursed the boy, so the two bulls differed, so there is no harm.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Ibn Muskhan, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who breastfeeds from a woman while he is a boy, is it permissible for him to marry her sister through breastfeeding? He said: If the two women breastfed from one woman from the milk of one bull, then it is not permissible. And if the two women breastfed from one woman, and it was from the milk of two bulls, then there is no harm with that. And that which indicates this is that what is related to her by birth, marriage is prohibited between them, exceeding what we have mentioned previously.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who said: Ali ibn Shu'ayb wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A woman breastfed some of my children; is it permissible for me to marry some of her children?' He wrote back: 'It is not permissible for you to do so, because her children have become like your children.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man nurses from the milk of a woman, everything from her offspring becomes forbidden to him, even if the child is from a man other than the one who nursed him with his milk. And when he nurses from the milk of a man, everything from that man's offspring becomes forbidden to him, even if it is from a woman other than the one who nursed him.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah, from Ali ibn al-Malik, from Bakkar ibn al-Jarrah, from Bistam, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: From breastfeeding, only the womb (stomach) from which one nursed becomes prohibited. The correct interpretation of this report is that the prohibition does not extend to those related to the mother via breastfeeding, because such a person is only related to another womb, and what is specific to her womb by birth is what becomes prohibited. It is also possible that this was stated as precautionary piency (taqiyyah), because among the jurists is one who says that the prohibition does not extend beyond the two nursing individuals.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ali ibn Isma'il al-Daghshi from a man from the people of Syria from Abd Allah ibn Aban al-Zayyat from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who married his paternal uncle's daughter, and his paternal grandfather's concubine had breastfed him. Is she prohibited to the boy or not? He said: No. This is a continuous, disconnected report, and its ruling is that it is not raised against the continuous, authentic reports with sound chains. And if it were accepted, it would be interpreted as meaning that if the concubine had breastfed him with the milk of the grandfather (not the father), or if she had breastfed him with a type of breastfeeding that does not cause prohibition. And if it were complete breastfeeding, the uncle would have become a relative (prohibited) if the grandfather was from the father's side, and if the grandfather was from the mother's side, there is no basis for prohibition there.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about al-Mut'ah, and he said: It was revealed in the Quran: 'So for whatever you have taken of them [in temporary marriage], give them their dowries as an obligation.' And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Muskhan, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'If it were not for what Ibn al-Khattab anticipated me to, I would not have married except [in a way that led to] misfortune.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Marim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Mut'ah (temporary marriage) is that upon which the Quran was revealed and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) proceeded.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali al-Sa'i, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, I used to practice Mut'ah (temporary marriage), but I disliked it and took it as an ill omen, so I made a covenant with Allah between the Rukn and the Maqam, and I made upon myself a vow and fasting that I would not practice it. Then indeed that became difficult for me, and I repented of my oath, but I have the strength in my hand to practice it openly.' He said to me: 'You made a covenant with Allah that you would obey Him, and by Allah, if you do not obey Him, you will disobey Him.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, from 'Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) forbade the meat of domestic donkeys and the marriage of Mut'ah. The approach in this narration is to attribute it to taqiyya (dissimulation), because it agrees with the schools of the general public (Sunni). The earlier narrations agree with the apparent meaning of the Book and the consensus of the True Sect upon its requirement, so it is obligatory to act upon them rather than this unusual narration.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from 'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) said: The divorce of a male slave is [valid] if he maraws a free woman, or if he marries the slave-girl of another people, [the divorce] is up to the slave; and if he marries his master's slave-girl, the one who separates them is he [the master], if he wishes, and if he wishes he can take her away without divorce.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: If the slave and his wife belong to one master, then the master may take her whenever he wishes and return her whenever he wishes. And he said: The divorce of the slave is not valid if he and his wife belong to one master, unless the slave belongs to one man and the woman belongs to another man, and he married her with the permission of his master and the permission of her master. If he divorces her while in this status, his divorce is valid.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Ibn Udhaynah from Bukayr ibn A'yan and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ajli from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) that they said: In the slave man, he does not have the right of divorce except with the permission of his master. This does not contradict the first two narrations, because his saying 'he does not have divorce except with the permission of his master' allows for the meaning that it refers to when his wife is the slave of his master, rather than being a free woman or a slave belonging to someone other than his master. And the first two narrations included the specification of that, so giving precedence to them is more appropriate.

And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man maroffs his female slave to a free man or a slave. Is he entitled to take her back without divorce? He said: Yes, she is his slave; he takes her back whenever he wishes.

And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Muhammad ibn Ali from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: When a slave marries a free woman, the master has the right to separate them, and if the master marries the slave to a free woman, he has the right to separate them. These two rulings do not contradict what we have previously established, because in the first report it is stated that he has the right to take her back without divorce whenever he wishes, and in the second report it is stated that he has the right to separate them; neither explicitly states that this right exists while she is in his ownership or the slave is in his ownership. If this is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as him having this right by selling her or selling him, so that their sale constitutes separation between them, as we will explain in a separate chapter, and that which indicates this is here.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Halab from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man maroffs his male slave to his female slave, he separates them if he wishes. I asked him about a man who marries his female slave to a free man or to a slave belonging to another group. Is he entitled to take her back from him? He said: No, unless he sells her. If he sells her, and the buyer wishes to separate them, he separates them.

And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who had a female slave and he married her to another man. [I asked]: With whom is her divorce? He said: With her master. And that is because he married her while knowing that it was so. This report also carries what we previously mentioned, that by his saying 'with him is her divorce,' he meant 'her sale.' Thus, her sale is like the divorce. And it is permissible that the word 'divorce' be used metaphorically for that, because it is a cause of separation, just as divorce is so.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The divorce of a female slave is her sale.' It is also possible that the meaning of his saying 'from another man' is if that man is also her slave, and the report does not also indicate that he was not her slave. And if this possibility holds, it is permissible for him to separate them. We have previously presented this, and it is further clarified by this.

Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a man has a female slave and marries her to his male slave, he separates them if he wishes and unites them if he wishes.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his female slave to a man, should he separate them if he wishes? He said: If she is his slave, he may separate them if he wishes, for Allah, the Exalted, says: 'A slave who has no power over anything,' so the slave has no authority in the matter. And if her husband is free, then her divorce is her transaction (option). It is also possible that the meaning is if the master of the girl had stipulated for the husband at the time of the marriage contract that the divorce is in his hand, because that is permissible among the female slaves.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad who said: A man wanted to marry off his slave girl to a free man and stipulated that whenever he wished, he could separate them. Is that permissible for him? I was made your ransom, or not? So he wrote: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from al-Bukayr ibn A'yan and Burayd al-Ajli, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) who said: Whoever buys a female slave who has a husband, then her sale is her divorce; if the buyer wishes, he separates them, and if he wishes, he leaves them upon their marriage.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: The divorce of the female slave is her sale, or the sale of her husband. And he said regarding a man who marries his female slave to another man and then sells her: He said, 'It is a separation between them, unless the buyer wishes to keep them together.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his female slave to a free man or to the slave of another group. He said: He does not have the right to take her back. If he sold her, and the buyer wished to take her from the man, he may do so.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Salim Abu al-Fadl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man buys a female slave who has a free husband. He said: It is not permissible for anyone to have sexual relations with her until her free husband divorces her. Therefore, the meaning of this report is that we interpret it to mean that if the buyer agrees to that condition, it is not permissible for anyone [to have relations with her] until she is divorced by the free husband, as detailed in the preceding reports.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-'Ala' al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Any man who wishes to free his female slave and marry her, and make her manumission her dowry, may do so.

Muhammad ibn Adam from al-Rida (peace be upon him) in [the matter of] When a man says to his slave girl, 'I have freed you, and I have made your dowry your freedom,' he said: 'The manumission is valid and the choice is hers; if she wishes, she may marry herself [to him], and if she wishes, she may not. If she marries herself, then I would like for him to give her something, so that it does not contradict the earlier reports, because the choice is hers only if he begins the statement with manumission before marriage. For the manumission proceeds, and she is left with the choice regarding the marriage contract. And it is proper that he begin with marriage and make the dowry the manumission, so that the contract is valid and the marriage proceeds, and that which indicates this distinction is...'

Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who said to his female slave, 'I have freed you and made your manumission your dowry.' He said: 'She is freed and has the choice; if she wishes, she may marry him, and if she wishes, she may not. If she marries him, he must give her something [additional]. And if he said, 'I have married you and made your manumission your dowry,' then the marriage is valid and he does not give her anything.' And that which confirms what we said initially, that this is permissible.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who freed his slave-girl and made her manumission her dowry, then divorced her before consummating the marriage with her. He said: He should seek her consent for half of her value; if she refuses, then she has one day of service and he has one day of service. And he said: And if she has a child, he pays for her half of her value and she is freed.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), in [the matter of] If a man frees his slave-girl and says to her, 'Your manumission is your dowry,' and then divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, he said: 'Half of her returns to being a slave, and he has the option to keep her as a slave for the other half.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim from 'Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man freed his umm walad (concubine mother of his child) and made her manumission her dowry, then he divorced her before consummating the marriage with her. He said: He offers her that she be compensated for half of her value; if she refuses, then half of her is a slave and half is free.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a female slave and wishes to free her and marry her: should he make her manumission her dowry, or free her and then pay her dowry? And is there a waiting period for her from him, and how long is it? And if he frees her, is it permissible for him to marry her without a dowry, and how long does she wait from him? He said: He makes her manumission her dowry if he wishes, and if he wishes he frees her and then pays her dowry. If her manumission is her dowry, then she does not observe a waiting period. And it is not permissible to marry her if he frees her except with a dowry. And a man does not have sexual relations with the woman when he marries her until he gives her something, even if it is a dirham.

Al-Bazzaz, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Ibn Ribat, from Safwan, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The minimum act that makes the concubine unlawful for the man to have with his son is if he touches her or strips her.

From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn al-Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has a female slave, and she is uncovered, so he sees her or undresses her, without adding more than that, he said: She is not permissible for his son.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding Regarding a man who has a female servant, who undresses her and looks at her body with lust, and she looks at what is forbidden for others to see; is she permissible for his father? And if the father did that, is she permissible for his son? He (peace be upon him) said: If he looked at her with lust, and she looked at what is forbidden for others, she is not permissible for the son. And if the son did that, she is not permissible for the father. And this adds clarification.

Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the minimum act that, if a man performs with a woman who is not permissible to his father or his son, [makes her forbidden]. He said: The boundary in that is sexual intercourse, whether apparent or hidden, that resembles the touching of the two private parts.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the male slave: how many women are permissible for him? He said: Two are permissible for him, and he may take concubines as he wishes, if his master permits him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the male slave: how many women are permissible for him? He said: two women.

From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The male slave (mook (male slave) does not combine from among the women more than two wives.

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the male slave, how many women are permissible for him to marry? He said: Two women. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations are general regarding that it is not permissible for him to contract marriage with more than two women, and it is appropriate that we specify them by saying: It is not permissible for him to contract marriage with more than two free women. As for the slave women, then it is permissible for him to contract marriage with four of them, and that which indicates this.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a male slave marrying four free women. He said: No, but he may marry two free women, and if he wishes, he may marry four female slaves.

From him, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ziyād, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the freed slave (mamlūk), what is permissible for him from women? He said: Two free women or four slave women. He said: And there is no objection if his master permits him to buy from his own wealth, if he has wealth, a female slave or female slaves whom he may have intercourse with, and his slave women are permissible for him.

From him, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the male slave: how many women are permissible for him to marry? He said: two free women or four female slaves. And he said: There is no harm if he has wealth in his hand and is permitted in trade to buy whatever he wishes of the female slaves and have relations with them.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is no objection if a man permits his slave to purchase from his property, if he has a female slave or female slaves whom he may have intercourse with, and his slaves are permissible for him; and he said: It is permissible for the slave to marry two free women.

And Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And in another narration, the slave may marry two free women, or four female slaves, or two female slaves and one free woman.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The slave's divorce is not valid, nor his marriage, except with the permission of his master. I said: 'But the master married him with his own hand, so whose is the divorce?' He said: 'With the hand of the master.' Allah has made an example of a slave who has no power over anything; the divorce is not in his hand.

From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who marries his male slave to his female slave, then it occurs to him to take her away from him with his own consent. Is that considered a divorce by the slave? He said: Yes, because the master's divorce is her divorce, so the slave has no divorce except with the permission of his master.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked, while I was listening nearby, about the divorce of a slave. He said: He does not have the authority to divorce, nor to marry. Do you not hear God, the Exalted, saying: 'A slave owned, who has no power over anything'? He said: He has no power to divorce, nor to marry, except with the permission of his master. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report and the first report, although they are general in that he does not possess the right of divorce, we have specified them because when he is married to his master's female slave, since we have explained in the preceding chapter that if he is married to another master's female slave or to a free woman, then his divorce is valid, and the second report from this chapter indicates that. Therefore, for this reason, we specified them as we mentioned.

Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ali ibn Sulayman said: I wrote to him: May I be your ransom, a man had a slave boy and a slave girl. He married his slave boy to his slave girl, then the master had intercourse with her. Is anything required in that matter? He said: It is not appropriate for him to touch her until the boy divorces her. And this does not contradict the first report, which is that if both were his slaves, the separation is up to him, because he was prevented from having intercourse with her only as long as she was in the bonds of the slave before they were separated, because that is not permissible. And it is permissible for him only if he separates between them and she observes the waiting period of the divorced slave woman from him. Then at that time he may have intercourse with her. And his saying 'until the boy divorces her' means that she becomes clear from him and enters the ruling of the divorced woman for whom divorce is valid, and that is by the separation which we mentioned, and that which indicates that his divorce is effective if he is married to a slave woman other than his master's or to a free woman.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The freed slave (mamluk) if he has a slave-wife under him, and he divorces her, then his master frees her, she remains with him as one divorce. If not for the fact that his divorce is effective according to some of the cases we mentioned, she would be with him as two divorces, as she was initially. Because in that case, he does not possess a divorce that is valid for him to effectuate, and this also indicates that.

Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Layth al-Muradi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave woman, is her divorce valid? He said: If she is your slave, then no, for Allah the Exalted says: 'A slave who has no power over anything.' And if she is the slave of other people, or a free woman, then her divorce is valid.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sinan from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a woman who went to a group of men and informed them that she was a free woman, so one of them married her and gave her the dowry of a free woman. Then her master came and said: 'She is returned to him, and her offspring are slaves.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn al-Walid from al-Walid ibn Sabih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a free woman and found that she had concealed her status as a slave from him: He said, 'If the one who married her to him was not from her masters, then the marriage is invalid.' I asked, 'What should he do with the dowry that she took from him?' He said, 'If he finds something from what he gave her, let him take it; and if he finds nothing, he has nothing against her.' And if the one who married her to him was her guardian, he shall reclaim from her guardian what she took from him, and for her masters against him is one-tenth of the value of her price if she was a virgin, and if she was not a virgin, half of one-tenth of her value, for what he made lawful of her private part. He said, 'And she observes from him the waiting period of a slave.' I asked, 'If she brings forth a child?' He said, 'Her children from him are free, if the marriage was without the permission of the masters.' This report admits of several interpretations: the first is that this is a denial and astonishment, not a pure report regarding their being free, as if he said, 'How can they be free when the marriage was without the permission of the masters?' And the second is that the one who married her had two witnesses testify before him that she was free, and then her children would be free, which indicates that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about a female slave of a people who went to a tribe other than her own and informed them that she was free, 'I am free.' A man from them married her and she bore him children. He said: Her children are enslaved unless she establishes proof that two witnesses testified for her that she is free; then they are not enslaved and they become free.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya from Hariz from Zurarah who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): A slave woman who escaped from her masters went to a tribe other than her own tribe and claimed that she was free. A man seized her and married her. Later, her master caught her, and she had already borne children. He (peace be upon him) said: If the husband establishes proof that he married her on the basis that she was free, her children are manumitted, and the people take their slave woman. And if he does not establish proof, his back is lashed, and his children are enslaved. The third aspect is that the meaning is that they will be free if the price of the children is returned to the master of the girl; that indicates that.

Al-Bazzaz narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ayyub, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a slave girl who went to a group of people and claimed she was free, so a man from them married her and she bore him a child. Then her master came to them and established proof that she was a slave, and the girl confirmed this. He said: 'She and her child are returned to her master, and it is upon the master to pay her child to his father at his value on the day he returns to him.' I asked: 'If the father has no money to buy his son?' He said: 'The father must strive to raise the price until he pays it and takes his son.' I asked: 'If the father refuses to strive for his son's price?' He said: 'Then it is upon the Imam to ransom him, and he shall not be owned by a free person.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), concerning a man whose family presumed he had died or been killed, so his wife was married and his concubine was married; each of the two gave birth to a child from her husband. Then the first husband came, or the master of the concubine came, and the ruling in that matter was that the first takes his wife, for he is more entitled to her, and the master takes his concubine and her child, unless he takes willingly the price of the child.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the marriage of a female slave. He said: The marriage of a female slave is not valid except with the permission of her master.
