Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqqaq, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man marions a female slave without the knowledge of her owners. He said: It is fornication. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So marry them with the permission of their owners.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn Amirah from Ali ibn al-Mughira who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who enjoys the use of a woman's slave-girl without her permission. He said: There is no objection to it.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn Amayrah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who marries a female slave without the permission of her owners. He said: If she belongs to a woman, then it is permissible; and if she belongs to a man, then it is not permissible.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Umayrah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no harm in a man deriving benefit (in marriage) from a woman's slave-girl; as for a man's slave-girl, one may not derive benefit from her except with his permission. So there is no contradiction between these narrations and the earlier narrations, because the origin of these narrations is one, which is Saif ibn 'Umayrah; sometimes he narrates it from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and sometimes from Dawud ibn Farqad, and sometimes from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) without an intermediary. And with that, the earlier narrations are consistent with the saying of Allah, the Exalted: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Marry them with the permission of their masters.' And that is general for women and men; and these narrations are contrary to that, so it is more appropriate that action be taken according to these narrations. And it is possible, while accepting them, to specify the earlier narrations with these narrations, so we interpret these narrations as permitting that in the contract of temporary marriage (Mut'ah) but not in permanent marriage, and we specify the earlier narrations with that so that the narrations do not contradict each other.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū Sārah, who said: I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), so he said to me: 'It is permissible, and do not marry except a chaste woman, for indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: [Those who guard their private parts], so do not place your private part where you do not feel secure regarding your dirham (dowry/money).'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the beautiful, promiscuous woman: Is it preferable for a man to derive pleasure from her for a day or more? He said: If she is known for fornication, let him not derive pleasure from her, nor marry her.

From him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Haddad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), and he said: 'Yes, if she is 'Arifah (known/chaste).' I said: 'If she is not 'Arifah?' He said: 'Then offer yourself to her and say to her.' If she accepts, then marry her. If she refuses to be satisfied with your word, then leave her. And beware of the Kawashif, the Dawaa'i, the Baghayah, and those with husbands.' I said: 'What are the Kawashif?' He said: 'Those who expose themselves, and their homes are well-known, and they commit fornication.' I said: 'And the Dawaa'i?' He said: 'Those who invite to themselves, and they are known for corruption.' I said: 'And the Baghayah?' He said: 'Those known for fornication.' I said: 'And those with husbands?' He said: 'The divorced ones (in temporary marriage) who are not according to the Sunnah.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu al-Hasan Ali from some of our companions, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: Do not treat the believing woman with casual enjoyment (or take her for pleasure) so as to humble her. This report has a disconnected chain and is mursal (disconnected), and it is not objected to by the connected reports to which we have previously presented a portion. It is possible that, while accepting it, the intended meaning is that if the woman is from the family of nobility, it is not appropriate to treat her with casual enjoyment because of the disgrace that befalls her family in that regard, and the humiliation that befalls her, even if that is not forbidden.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurara who said: Ammar asked (while I was with him) about a man who marries the promiscuous woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah). He said: There is no harm, and if the other marriage (permanent) is (also there), let him guard his door.

From him, from Sa'dan, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the women of the city (Mecca/Medina). He said: 'They are capable (of marriage).' I asked: 'Should I marry from among them?' He said: 'Yes.' The way to reconcile these two reports, and what follows their pattern, is to consider them as permissible (general allowance), while the earlier reports are considered as indicating excellence and preference (recommendation), and likewise.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is permissible for a man to enjoy (marry) a Jewish woman and a Christian woman, even if he has a free (non-slave) woman.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, who said: I heard him saying: There is no harm in marrying a Jewish woman or a Christian woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah), while he already has a wife.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the marriage of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, so he said: There is no objection to it. I said: And the Magian woman? He said: There is no objection to it, meaning temporary marriage (mut'ah).
From him, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ibn Sinan, from Mansur al-Siqlabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is permissible for a man to enjoy (marry) a Magus woman.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah from al-Hasan al-Taflisī who said: I asked al-Ridha (peace be upon him): Is one permitted to enjoy (marry temporarily) the Jewish and Christian women? He said: Enjoying the free believing woman is more beloved to me, and she is greater in sanctity than them.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee, from Mansur ibn Buzurg, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awadd, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): If I marry a woman, is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her before I have paid her any part of her dowry? He said: Yes, it is merely a debt upon you.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man marries a woman for a known dowry, and he consummates the marriage with her before giving her the dowry. He said: He should advance to her whatever is little or much, unless he has wealth/assets from which, if an event occurs, he can pay it off, so there is no objection.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awass al-Ta'i, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman but does not have what he can give her (the dowry), and he consummates the marriage with her. He said: There is no objection; it is merely a debt upon him owed to her.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Abd al-Khaliq, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman and enters into her (consummates the marriage) before giving her anything. He said: It is a debt upon him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah and from al-Fudayl from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in [a narration] concerning A man married a woman, had intercourse with her, and she bore him a child, then he died. She claimed a portion of her dowry from his heirs and sought her inheritance. He said: As for the inheritance, she may claim it. As for the dowry, whatever she took from the husband before entering into intimacy with him is what entailed the permissibility of his intercourse with her, whether little or much. If she accepted it from him and entered into intimacy with him, she has nothing more after that.

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man and a woman who both perish, and the heirs of the woman come and claim the dowry (sadaq) from the heirs of the man. He said: 'And they have perished and the inheritance has been divided?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'They have nothing.' I said: 'And if the woman was alive and came after the death of her husband claiming her dowry?' He said: 'She has nothing, and she had remained with him acknowledging [the debt] until her husband perished.' I said: 'And if she died while he was alive, and her heirs came claiming her dowry from him?' He said: 'And she had remained [alive] until she died not claiming it?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'She has nothing.' I said: 'And if he divorced her and she came claiming her dowry?' He said: 'And she had remained not claiming it until he divorced her?' He said: 'She has nothing.' I said: 'When is the limit of that, i.e., if I claim it, it will not be for her?' He said: 'When she was presented to him and entered his house, and then claimed it after that, she has nothing. Indeed, it is much for her that an oath be sworn by Allah that she has no dowry from him. [Whether] little or much.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who enters into marriage with a woman, then she claims the dowry from him, he said: When he has entered with her, the immediate (dowry) has become due.

From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding the man who marries the woman and enters into her, then she claims the dowry against him, he said: When he enters into her, the immediate portion has been paid. There is nothing in these reports that contradicts what we mentioned, because all of them include that the woman claims the dowry, and likewise her heirs. And we did not say that she is given the dowry merely by her claim, but she needs evidence. And if she has nothing but her claim, she is not entitled to anything, according to what these reports include. Rather, we obligate her dowry after the establishment of evidence, and that which indicates that evidence is obligatory upon her.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man has intercourse with a woman and she then claims the dowry while he says, 'I have given it to you,' the burden of proof is upon her and the oath is upon him. And if the matter were according to what some of our companions believed—that if he had intercourse with her, it would invalidate the dowry—there would be no burden of proof upon her and no oath upon him, because intercourse has already removed the right, so there is no basis for establishing proof or an oath. It is also possible that the reason in those narrations is that if he did not specify a definite dowry but gave her something, that becomes her dowry and she has nothing else after that. And in none of them is it stated that he used to specify a definite dowry. What indicates this is what al-Fudayl ibn Yasar narrated in the preceding report from his saying: 'That which you took before he had intercourse with her is that which made her private part lawful to him, and she has nothing else after that.' This points to what we said, that he did not stipulate a definite dowry for her.

And as for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'Inform me about the dowry of the woman such that it is not permissible for the believer to exceed it.' He said, 'The Muhammadan Sunnah is five hundred dirhams. Whoever exceeds that, the excess is returned to the Sunnah, and there is no penalty upon him for more than five hundred dirhams. If he gave her from the five hundred dirhams one dirham or more of that, and then consummated the marriage with her, there is no penalty upon him.' I said, 'If he divorces her after he has consummated the marriage with her?' He said, 'There is no penalty upon him. Her condition was five hundred dirhams. When he consummated the marriage with her before she completed her dowry, he demolished the dowry, and she has nothing [of the excess]. She only has what she took before he consummated the marriage with her. If she claims [the excess] after that during his life or after his death, she has nothing.' The beginning of what is in this report is that it was not narrated by anyone other than Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, and Muhammad ibn Sinan is heavily criticized and very weak. And what is specific to his narration and no one else shares in it is not acted upon. On the basis that the report implies that the dowry is not increased beyond five hundred dirhams, and whenever it is increased, it is returned to five hundred. And this too we have explained in our Great Book as being contrary to this, and we said that the dowry is what they mutually agree upon, whether little or much. And that which reveals this is that it is not returned to five hundred if more than it is mentioned.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from al-Washsha', from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: If a man marries a woman and sets her dowry at twenty thousand, and gives ten thousand to her father, the dowry is valid and what he gave to the father is invalid. Regarding the statement in the hadith: 'If he gives her one dirham from the five hundred dirhams, then nothing is due from him afterwards, nor from her heirs,' this does not mean that nothing is due after he has fixed and specified her dowry. It is permissible that the meaning is: if he gives her one dirham from the five hundred (which is the Sunnah amount for dowry) and consummates the marriage with her, then she has nothing more due to her afterwards, nor to her heirs. This is what we have explained as valid, and on this basis all the narrations are consistent and do not contradict each other.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'ah, from more than one, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who married a woman but did not specify her dowry, then he consummated the marriage with her: 'She is entitled to the dowry of her equals.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man married a woman and did not specify a dowry for her. He said: She has nothing of the dowry. But if he had intercourse with her, then she has the dowir of her equals.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said: I asked him about a man who married a woman, entered into her (consummated the marriage), but did not specify a dowry for her. Then he divorced her. He said to her: 'She is entitled to the dowry of her equals, and he must provide her with mut'ah (consolation gift).'

Al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Abdillah al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman and erred in not specifying the dowry until he had intercourse with her. He said: The Sunnah, and the Sunnah is five hundred dirhams.

From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Usama ibn Hafs, and he was a custodian for Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man married a woman and did not specify a dowry, and in the conversation he said, 'I marry you upon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).' Then he died without her, or intended to consummate the marriage with her. What is her due from the dowry? He said: The dowry of the Sunnah. I said: People say, 'The dowry of her female relatives.' He said: It is the dowry of the Sunnah. And whenever I said something to him, he said: The dowry of the Sunnah. So there is no contradiction with the first narrations, because the meaning in the first narration is that we say the dowry of the like (of the wife) does not exceed the dowry of the Sunnah, which is five hundred dirhams, when there is consummation without specifying the dowry. And the narration is explanatory of the ambiguity of the first narrations. As for the second narration, it does not state that he consummated the marriage with her, and it is not impossible that he intended by that to inform about the maximum amount that is obligatory from the dowry of the Sunnah, for that is what is preferred, and that following the relatives in obligating the dowry of the like and specifying it is not obligatory. And upon this meaning, there is no contradiction between the narrations.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Consummation (sexual intercourse) in the vagina is what obligates the dowry (mahr) alone.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zur'arah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): When does the dowry become obligatory? He said: When he enters with her.

From him, from al-Riyān, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) regarding: A man who had intercourse with a woman, he said: When the circumcised parts meet, the dowry becomes obligatory and the waiting period [begins].

From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man and a woman, when does the ritual bath become obligatory upon them? He said: When he enters (with her), the ritual bath, the dowry, and the stoning become obligatory.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man marries a woman, then is secluded with her, closes the door upon her, and lowers the curtain, then divorces her, the dowry becomes obligatory, and her seclusion with him is considered consummation (dakhul).

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a young girl who had not yet reached puberty, whom he would not have intercourse with like an adult, or who married a virgin (ratqa') and she was brought to him, and he divorced her immediately after she was brought to him. He said: In these two cases, a trustworthy woman is sent to examine them. If they are as they entered (i.e., virgins), she is entitled to half of the dowry he specified for her, and there is no waiting period (iddah) for her from him. He said: And if the husband dies regarding them before divorcing them, then she is entitled to the inheritance and half of the dowry, and upon them is the waiting period of four months and ten days.

And as for what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the dowry (mahr), when does it become obligatory? He said: When the curtain is lowered and the door is closed firmly. He said: I married a woman during the lifetime of my father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and my soul longed for her, so my father forbade me, saying: Do not do it, O my son, do not go to her at this hour. But I insisted on doing so. When I entered upon her, I threw a cloak that was on me towards her, and I disliked her, and I went to leave. Then a female slave of hers stood up, lowered the curtain and closed the door firmly. I said: Stop, for what you want has become obligatory. So this narration does not negate the reports we have previously mentioned, because in the narration it is not stated that the dowry became obligatory. Nor is it impossible that he meant 'what you want has become obligatory' referring to settling with her over something she is pleased with. And even if it mentioned the dowry, it would not mean that the thing that made the dowry obligatory was lowering the curtain and secluding with her. Rather, it is not impossible that he (peace be upon him) made it obligatory upon himself as a voluntary gift, without it being obligatory in principle. And that which indicates this is that it has been narrated in this exact case that his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: She has only half the dowry. This indicates that if he gave her the entire dowry, he only gave it as a voluntary gift.

And Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) married a woman, and the door was closed. He said, 'Open it, and you shall have what you asked for.' When they opened it, he made a settlement with them. Ibn Abi Umayr (may God have mercy on him) used to say: 'The narrations have differed regarding this, and the way to reconcile them is that the judge should rule based on the apparent fact and obligate the man the full dowry if he lowered the curtain, except that the woman is not permitted, between herself and God, to take more than half the dowry. This is a good opinion and does not contradict what we have previously stated, because we only obligated half the dowry when there was knowledge of non-consummation and the ability to know that. But when the knowledge is removed or the ability to know is removed, the statement is what Ibn Abi Umayr said, and that which confirms what we mentioned as well.'

Al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Zarif, from Thalabah, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and she was brought to him, he closed the door, lowered the curtain, kissed her, and touched her, without having had intercourse with her afterwards, then he divorced her in that state. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no obligation upon him except half of the dowry.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Al-Hasan ibn Zur'ah from his father said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman according to her ruling (on the dowry). He said: Her ruling does not exceed the dowry of the women of the Family of Muhammad, twelve ounces and a nan, which is the weight of five hundred dirhams of silver. I said: What if you saw that he married her according to his ruling and she accepted? He said: Whatever he ruled regarding something, it is permissible for both of them, whether little or much. He said: I said: How come you did not validate her ruling upon him, but you validated his ruling upon her? He said: Because he made her the arbitrator, so it was not for her to exceed what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established and married his wives upon, so I returned it to the Sunnah. And because she made him the arbitrator and placed the matter of the dowry in his hands and accepted his ruling in that, so it is upon her to accept his ruling, whether little or much.

Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) concerning A man married a woman based on her stipulation or based on his stipulation, and he died or she died before he consummated the marriage with her, then he said to her: provision (mut'ah), inheritance, and no dowry for her. He said: If he divorces her and had married her based on her stipulation, the stipulation does not exceed five hundred silver dirhams, which is the dowry of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom his wife entrusts her dowry, and it is less than the dowry of his other wives. He said: 'It is added to the dowry of his wives, so it does not contradict the first report, because this narration is understood to be when she entrusts it to him on the condition that he makes it equal to the dowry of his wives; so whenever he falls short of that, it is added to it. But if it is absolute, the ruling is what the first report contained, that whatever he judges is valid.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf al-Azdi, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding: A man married a woman and stipulated for her that if he married another woman over her, or abandoned her, or took a concubine over her, then she is divorced. He ruled in that matter that the condition of God precedes your condition; if he wishes, he fulfills for her what he stipulated, and if he wishes, he keeps her and takes another over her and marries her.

Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Asam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Durays had under his authority the daughter of Humran, so he stipulated for her that he would never marry another woman during her lifetime and after her death, on the condition that she stipulated for him that she would not marry after him. So he made upon them both from the Hajj, the offering, the vows, and all wealth they possessed to be given to the poor, and every slave they owned to be freed, if each one of them did not fulfill his obligation to the other. Then he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned that to him. He said: Indeed, for her father Humran is a right, and that will not prevent us from saying the truth. Go, marry and be content, for that is nothing, and there is no burden on you and no burden on her, and that which you did is not binding. So he was content and had children after that.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Kahili said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and stipulated for her that he would not marry another woman besides her, and she agreed that this stipulation would be her dowry. He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: This is a valid stipulation; marriage is not valid except with a dirham or two dirhams.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur Buzurg, from Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man from your mawali married a woman, then divorced her, and she became independent of him. He wanted to remarry her, but she refused him except that he make a vow to God that he would not divorce her and would not marry another woman over her. He gave her that, then it occurred to him to marry another woman after that. So what should he do? He said: Bad is what he did, and he did not know what would occur in his heart by night and by day. Tell him to fulfill the condition for the woman, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The believers are upon their conditions.' So the way in this narration is one of two things: One is that it is to be understood as recommending (mustahabb), because whoever rules according to what the narration entails, it is recommended for him to fulfill the condition that his tongue offered, even if it is not obligatory. And the other way is that it is to be understood as based on taqiyya (dissimulation), because those who differ from us would obligate this condition and make him sinful if he violates it, and that which confirms the first narrations.

Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from Hammad from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who said to his wife: 'If I marry another woman upon you or take a concubine, you are divorced.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is of no effect.' Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever stipulates a condition other than the Book of Allah (Exalted and Mighty), that condition is not valid for him nor upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Zurarah ibn A'yan, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ajli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The woman who has possessed her own affairs, who is not foolish, and who is not under guardianship, her marriage without a guardian is permissible.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from 'Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Maysarah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If a woman is found in a barren place where there is no one, and I ask her, "Do you have a husband?" and she says, "No," then I marry her.' He said: 'Yes, she is the one verifying it upon herself.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the mature woman (thiyyib) who proposes marriage to herself, he said: She is more entitled to her own affair; she may manage her matter with whomever she wishes, provided he is a suitable match (kuf'), after she has previously married a man.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who is among the people of a house (i.e., under the guardianship of a male relative) and she dislikes for the people of her house to know about it. Is it permissible for her to appoint a man who wishes to marry her, saying to him, 'I have appointed you, so witness my marriage to you'? He said: No. I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, and if she is a virgin (ayyim)?' He said: And if she is a virgin. I said: And if she appoints someone else to marry her to him, will he marry her to him? He said: Yes. The reason in this report is that it was not permissible because she appointed him to marry her to himself, and that is not valid because the agent stands in the place of the principal, so he needs someone to contract on his behalf, and it is not valid for a person to contract on himself because the contract requires offer and acceptance, and that is not valid between a person and himself. And if she married herself to him without appointing him, that would be permissible according to what the earlier reports contained. And for the reason we mentioned, the questioner said to him: 'She appoints someone else to marry her to him?' He said: Yes, because that is valid to be estimated in him, and in the first case it is not valid, and it adds clarity to what we have presented.

Ali ibn Isma'il, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If a woman is the manager of her own affairs, she may sell, buy, emancipate, testify, and give from her wealth as she wishes; then her affairs are valid. She may marry if she wishes without the permission of her guardian, and if she is not like that, then her marriage is not valid except with the permission of her guardian.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Sa'd ibn Isma'il from his father who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who married a virgin or a divorcee, whose father and none of her relatives were known, but the woman appoints a proxy who marries her off without their knowledge. He said: 'It is not so.' His saying 'It is not so' is to be understood as referring specifically to the virgin, not excluding the divorcee. Nor is it prohibited that he be asked about two matters and answer one for the sake of some benefit, while relying in the answer to the other on the explanation previously given by him or his fathers (peace be upon them). It is also possible that he spoke in the manner of precautionary piety (taqiyyah), because it agrees with the belief of most of the common people, which confirms what we have presented.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from al-Baraqi, from ibn Faddal, from ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is permissible for the woman to marry herself off if she is a divorcee or widow, without the permission of her father, provided that what she did is acceptable.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The virgins (daughters) of the fathers are not married off except with the permission of their fathers.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The father is the only one who annuls the marriage.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The father is the only one who annuls the marriage.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them, he said: The young woman (bikr) is asked for her consent if she is between her parents, but she has no authority alongside the father. He said, and he said: Everyone else asks her for consent, except the father.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Sadan ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no harm in marrying a virgin if she consents, without the permission of her father. This report carries two meanings: one is that it is specific to the marriage of Mut'ah, according to what we have previously mentioned regarding the concession in that regard with the conditions we have mentioned; and the other is that it is to be understood as applying when she is mature and her father does not marry her to a suitable match and prevents her from doing so, in which case it is permissible for her to contract the marriage herself.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Salt said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the young girl whose father marries her off: does she have authority (to accept or reject) when she reaches maturity? He said: No. And I asked him about the virgin who reaches the maturity of women: does she have authority with her father? He said: She has no authority with her father as long as she is not married off (thayyibat).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a young girl whom her father marries off, then he dies while she is still a minor, and then she grows up before her husband consummates the marriage with her. Is the marriage valid upon her, or is the decision left to her? He said: Her father's marriage of her is valid.

From him, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Should I marry off a young girl who is three years old, or should I marry off a boy who is three years old, and what is the minimum age at which they can be married?' He said: 'When the girl reaches maturity and does not consent to the marriage, what is her status?' He said: 'There is no harm in that, provided her father or her guardian consented.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a young boy marrying a young girl. He said: If it was their two parents who married them, then it is valid, but they have the option (of annulment) when they reach maturity. If they consent afterwards, then the dowry is upon the father. I said to him: Is the father's divorce of his son permissible during his minority? He said: No. This does not contradict the earlier narrations, because his saying 'but they have the option when they reach maturity' means that they have the right to annul the contract either by divorce from the side of the spouse or by the wife demanding what necessitates divorce and requires its annulment. And he did not mean by 'the option' here the ratification or invalidation of the contract such that the contract is suspended pending their choice. And that which reveals this is his saying in the narration: 'If it was their two parents who married them, then it is valid.' For if the contract were suspended pending their consent, there would be no difference between the parents and others, and it would be valid for others too. And it is established that there is a difference between the two cases, so it is known that the meaning is what we mentioned.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn Sihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who wants to marry off his sister, he said: He should consult her, and if she remains silent, that is her consent; and if she refuses, he should not marry her off; and if she says, 'Marry me to so-and-so,' then he should marry her to whomever she approves of. And the orphan girl under the guardianship of a man should not be married off by him except with her consent.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said: Some of my paternal uncles wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a young girl whom her paternal uncle married off, but when she grew up, she refused the marriage?' He wrote in his own hand: 'She is not compelled to accept it, and the matter is hers (her choice).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a woman whom her brother married to a man, then after that her mother, her uncle, and a younger brother married her to another. She was entered by the second husband and became pregnant. They disputed over her. The first husband presented witnesses, so he attached her to himself (maintained the first marriage) and gave her both dowries. He prevented the husband who had the right to enter her (the second one) until she gave birth to her pregnancy, then he attached the child to its father. The ruling in this report is what we said in the first report: that the girl gave her affair to her two brothers, and the older brother preceded with the contract, so his contract is valid and the contract made by the younger brother is void. In any case, if the second one entered her, she is entitled to the dowry for what he made lawful of her private part, and the child is attached to him, because he contracted with her and did not know that his older brother had already contracted her to another before that, and it was a contract of doubt (shubha), so the child is attached to him.

Ali ibn Isma'il al-Mithamini from al-Hasan ibn Ali from some of his companions from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: The elder brother is in the position of the father. The implication in this report is that he is in the position of the father regarding the obligation of honoring him, submitting to his commands, and returning to his obedience. It is not meant that he is in the position of the father regarding the permissibility of contracting him to his younger sister without her consent, nor regarding seeking her opinion, based on what we have previously presented. And if it were explicit in that, we would interpret it as being due to taqiyya (dissimulation), because that is the view of some of the Sunnis.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has two wives and wishes to favor one of them with clothing and a gift; is that permissible? He said: There is no harm in that, but strive for justice between them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Mu'ammarr ibn Khallad said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Does a man prefer some of his wives over others? He said: No, and there is no harm in it regarding the female slaves. The meaning of this report is that we should interpret it as indicating a type of dislike (karahah), for the best is to equalize them on one level.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about enjoying (sexual relations) with the virgins who are between the parents (i.e., daughters), so he said: 'There is no harm,' and he did not say as those coarse/rough men say.

Abu Sa'id narrated from al-Halabi who said: I asked him about enjoying sexual relations with a virgin girl if she is under the guardianship of her parents without their permission. He said: There is no harm, provided she has not yet lost her virginity.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu al-Hasan Zarif, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The virgin who has a father may not contract mut'ah marriage except with her father's permission. The meaning in this report is one of several interpretations: one of them is that the virgin is a young girl who has not reached puberty, for it is not permissible to enjoy her except with her father's permission, which indicates this.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Muhraz al-Kha'thami, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about a girl from whom a man derives pleasure (temporary marriage), he said: Yes, unless she is a young girl who is deceived (due to immaturity). I said: May God perfect you, what is the limit at which, when she reaches it, she is not considered deceived? He said: A daughter of ten years. And among the reasons is that the report may have been issued in the manner of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah).

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Fudayl ibn Kathir al-Mada'ini, from al-Muhallab al-Dallal, that he wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) That a woman was with him in the house, then she married herself, making God and His angels witnesses to that, then her father married her to another man, so what do you say? He wrote: Permanent marriage is not valid except with guardianship and two witnesses, and temporary marriage (mut'ah) is not valid with a virgin. Conceal it from yourself, and keep it secret, may God have mercy on you. And from it: that the report came in a place of dislike rather than prohibition, which indicates that.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who marries a virgin for temporary marriage (Mut'ah), he said: It is disliked due to the defect (impurity) upon her family.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said: I asked him about a man who had a wife and then married another woman over her, is it permissible for him to favor one over the other? He said: He should favor the newlywed for the three days of her wedding celebration, if she is a virgin. Then he should equalize between them with the goodwill of one of them towards the other.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from al-Hudhrami from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man married a woman and he has another wife with him. He said: If she is a virgin, he should spend the night with her for seven days; and if she is a mature woman (thayyib), for three nights. This does not contradict the first report because the way to resolve it is to carry the first report on permissibility and the second report on preference, because the preference is that the virgin is not preferred with more than three nights due to the freshness of her wedding, and it is permissible to prefer her with seven nights. As for the non-virgin, she is not preferred with more than three nights, then he returns to equality and emphasizes that.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Husayn (Al-Halabi) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man who has two wives, one of whom is more beloved to him than the other: Is it permissible for him to prefer one over the other? He said: Yes, he may prefer some of them over others, as long as they are not four. And he said: If a man marries a virgin while he already has a divorcee (or mature woman), he may prefer the virgin by three days. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning contained in this report regarding his preference for some over others as long as they are not four is that if a man is permitted to marry four women and have intercourse with each one in turn (one night each), it is permissible when he has two wives to assign three nights to one and one night to the other, because she is not entitled to more than one night in every four nights.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd Allah ibn Muskhan from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: He marries the free woman over the slave woman, and does not marry the slave woman over the free woman, nor the Christian nor the Jewess over the Muslim woman. So whoever does that, his marriage is invalid. I asked him about a man who has two wives, and one is more beloved to him than the other. Is it permissible for him to favor her with something? He said: Yes, it is permissible for him to visit her for three nights and the other for one night, because he may marry four women, so he makes the two nights wherever he wishes. I said: So a woman is with him, and he marries a virgin girl? He said: He should favor her when he consummates the marriage with three nights. And it is permissible for the man to favor some of his wives over others as long as they are not four.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Humran from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to his wife from behind (in her rear), he said: There is no harm if she is pleased. I said: Then where is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'So come to them from where Allah has commanded you'? He said: This [command] is regarding seeking offspring. So seek offspring from where Allah has commanded you. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish'.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafsh ibn Suqah from whom he informed him, saying: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to his wife from behind her. He said: It is one of the two types of intercourse, and in it is the ritual bath (ghusl).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Musa ibn Abd al-Malik and al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Musa ibn Abd al-Malik from a man who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man coming to his wife from behind in her rear [anus], so he said: 'It was made permissible by a verse from the Book of Allah, the Exalted: The saying of Lut (peace be upon him), These are my daughters, they are purer for you, and He knew that they did not desire the vagina.'

From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or he informed me about the one who asked him, regarding a man who comes to his wife in that place (the anus) while a group of people are in the house. He said to me, and raised his voice, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever imposes on his slave what he cannot bear, let him free him.' Then he looked at the faces of the Ahl al-Bayt, then inclined towards me and said: 'There is no harm in it.'

From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to his wife in her rear (anus). He said: There is no objection to it.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, who said: I heard Safwan saying: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man from your mawalis ordered me to ask you about a matter, and he feared you and was shy from you to ask you. He said: What is it? I said to the man: To approach his wife in her posterior. He said: Yes, that is for him. I said: And do you do that? He said: No, we do not do that.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ishaq, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'I sometimes approach the female servant from behind, meaning her rear, and I ejaculate, so I have imposed upon myself that if I do this with a woman, I will give a dirham as charity, and this has become heavy upon me.' He said: 'There is no burden on you, and that is for you.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus or another, from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna, from Sadir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: 'The inner parts of the women are forbidden for my ummah.'

From him, with this chain, from Hashim and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Hashim said: 'Do not be solitary (vaginal) and do not be female (anal).' Ibn Bukayr said: 'Do not be female,' meaning the females (anal) other than this place (vagina). The meaning in these two narrations is a type of dislike (karahah), because it is preferable to avoid it, even if it is not forbidden, which indicates that.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi, raising it from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked him about having intercourse with women in their hindquarters (rectum). He said: 'There is no harm in it, but I dislike that you do it.' And the report which we previously mentioned from al-Rida (peace be upon him), and his saying 'We do not do that,' is evidence of the dislike of that, according to what we said. It also bears the possibility that the two reports came for the purpose of Taqiyya (dissimulation), because none of the general public (Sunni scholars) permits that except what is narrated from Malik, and his companions differ with him regarding it.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Rifa'ah ibn Musa who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mahrud (one with a defect) and the Mahrudah (female with a defect), is she returned from the marriage? He said: No. Rifa'ah said: And I asked him about the Brasa' (woman with leprosy/white patches), so he said: The Commander of the Faithful ruled regarding a woman whom her guardian married while she was Brasa', that she has the Mahr (dowry) because he made lawful her private part, and that the Mahr is upon the one who married her, and the Mahr became upon him because he concealed her defect. And if a man married a woman, or a man married her off, who did not know the inner nature of her affair (defect), there would be nothing upon him, and he would take the Mahr from her.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and then learned after marrying her that she had committed fornication. He said: If her husband wishes, he may take the dowry from the one who married her off to him, and she is entitled to the dowry for what he made lawful of her private part. And if he wishes, he may leave her. This report is not contradictory to what we mentioned earlier, because he only said: 'If he learns that she had committed fornication, he has the right to claim the dowry from her guardian.' He did not say that he has the right to return her (repudiate her). Nor is it impossible that he has the right to reclaim the dowry even if he does not have the right to annul the contract, because one of the two matters is separate from the other.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Marriage is only annulled due to leprosy, leprosy (or severe skin disease), madness, and blindness.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The leper, the insane woman, and the leperous woman are returned (in marriage). I asked: What about the one-eyed woman? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Rifa'ah ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman is returned (from the marriage contract) due to al-'afal, al-baras, al-judham, and al-junun; as for what is other than that, she is not returned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The leper (one with al-barsa'), the blind one, and the lame one are returned (i.e., the marriage contract is annulled).

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who marries a woman and she is brought to him blind, or leperous, or lame, he said: She is returned to her guardian, and the dowry remains upon her guardian. And if she has a defect that men do not see, the testimony of women regarding her is accepted.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ribab, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in [a narration]: In the case of a man who married a woman from her guardian, and then found a defect in her after he had consummated the marriage with her, he said: If the blind woman concealed her blindness, the leper concealed his leprosy, the insane woman concealed her insanity, the woman with exposed private parts concealed it, and anyone who had an obvious defect concealed it, then she is returned to her family without divorce, and the husband takes the dowry from the guardian who concealed it. If the guardian was not aware of anything of that, then he has nothing against him, and she is returned to her family. He said: If the husband suffered a loss from what she took from him, it is for him; and if he did not suffer a loss, then he has nothing. He said: She observes a waiting period from him as a divorced woman if he had consummated the marriage with her; and if he had not consummated the marriage with her, then there is no waiting period upon her and she has no dowry. The way to reconcile between these narrations is that what is added to insanity, leprosy, leprosy (white spots), blindness, and exposure of private parts, such as blindness, lameness, and obvious defects, which some narrations include, are held to be of a type of mild dislike (karahah), and it is recommended for one who is tested with that not to return her. As for the five things we mentioned, he has the right to return her in all cases, and that which confirms what we said is...

Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who marries into a family, and his wife is 'awra' (has a defect) and they did not specify it to him, he said: The marriage is not annulled; rather, the marriage is annulled due to leprosy, leprosy (specific type), madness, and blindness. I said: Do you see if he has consummated the marriage with her, what should he do regarding her dowry? He said: She has the dowry because he made her private part permissible to him, and her guardian who married her off must pay a penalty equal to what he brought to her.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who married a woman and found her to be leprous or hunchbacked: He said, if he had not yet entered into her (consummated the marriage) and had not yet specified (whether he would keep her or divorce her), then if he wishes he may divorce her, and if he wishes he may keep her, and she has no dowry. And if he enters into her, then she is his wife. This does not contradict the report we previously mentioned, that one of this type is returned without divorce, because his saying 'if he wishes he may divorce' is construed to mean 'if he wishes he may let her go,' because that is derived from the root of the language from the word 'divorce,' and it is not construed to mean the legal divorce due to the indication of the first report. As for his saying 'and if he enters into her, then she is his wife,' the way to understand this is to construe it to mean that if he enters into her with knowledge of her condition, then that is consent to her. And whenever he did not know that and entered into her, he has the right to return her, and she has the dowry for what he made permissible of her private part, according to what the earlier reports contained, and this is also confirmed.

From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The wife is returned (due to defects) for four things: leprosy, leprosy-like disease (al-Judham), madness, and blindness (al-Qaran), which is al-Afal (complete blindness). If these have not occurred upon her, she is returned; if they have occurred upon her, she is not returned. The reasoning in these two narrations is also what we said: that when he marries her with knowledge of her condition, he does not have the right to return her, because that is his consent, which indicates acceptance of the defect.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu al-Subbah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and found her to be qarna' (unable to conceive). He said: 'This one does not conceive, and her husband is unable to have intercourse with her, and he returns her to her family in a humiliated state without a dowry.' I said: 'But if he had consummated the marriage with her?' He said: 'If he knew of that before marrying her (meaning the inability to have intercourse), then he had intercourse with her, he has accepted her. And if he did not know except after he had intercourse with her, then if he wishes afterwards he may keep her, and if he wishes he may divorce her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The 'Innain (the deaf-mute) is given a waiting period of one year; then if his wife wishes, she may marry (another), and if she wishes, she may remain (married to him).

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband was afflicted such that he could never perform sexual intercourse; should she divorce him? He said: Yes, if she wishes.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man marries a woman while he is unable to have intercourse with women, he is given a year's respite until he treats his condition.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-Bukhtari from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: The 'Inn (impotent husband) is granted a delay of one year from the day his wife files a case against him; if he is cured (consummates), otherwise they are separated. If she agrees to stay with him and then seeks the option of separation after that, the option has fallen and she has no option. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations, although they are general regarding the 'Inn being delayed for a year, are predicated on the assumption that he had not entered with her at all. As for if he entered with her, even once, and then impotence occurred to him, she does not have an option against him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever has intercourse with a woman once, and then she is taken (by her guardian/father), she has no option (of khiyar al-ruju').'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Aban, from Ghiyath al-Tabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the 'Innain (a man with a specific sexual defect), if it is known that he is 'Innain and does not have intercourse with women, they are separated (divorced). And if he has intercourse with her in one thrust, they are not separated. And the man is not returned (divorced) due to a defect.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Hamzah said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: When a man marries a thayyib (previously married) woman who has been married to another husband, and she claims that he has not had intercourse with her since he entered into marriage with her, then the word in this matter is the man's, and it is upon him to swear by Allah that he has indeed had intercourse with her, because she is the claimant. He said: If he marries her while she is a virgin (bakr), and she claims that he has not reached her, then this case is known by women, so let a woman who is trustworthy among them look at her. If she says that she is a virgin, then it is upon the Imam to delay him for one year. If he has intercourse with her, then fine; otherwise, they are separated, and she is given half of the dowry, and there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdillah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from some of his teachers, who said: A woman said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or a man asked him about a man whose wife claims he has 'unna' (impotence/inability to consummate), and the man denies it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The midwife should insert the salve (khalooq) into her, and the man does not know. If it comes out and the salve is on his penis, she is truthful and he is lying; otherwise, she is lying and he is truthful.'

From him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Ishaq ibn Bunnan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A woman claimed against her husband during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he did not have intercourse with her, and he claimed that he did. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered her to apply saffron, then he would wash his penis. If the water came out yellow, he was believed; otherwise, he was ordered to divorce her. The way to reconcile these narrations is that the Imam has discretion in this matter, to rule as he wishes, based on what appears to him in the moment of certainty or taking precaution in acting upon one of these matters.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: There is a eunuch who enters upon the women of a man, and he hands them the water for ablution, so he sees their hair. He said: 'No' (it is disliked).

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the covering (qina') of free women by the eunuchs. He said: 'They used to enter upon the daughters of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and they would not cover themselves. Therefore, the meaning in this report is a form of taqiyyah (dissimulation/prudence), and acting upon the first report is more preferable and more cautious in religion.' And in another report, when he was asked about this issue, he said: 'Restrain yourself from this.' It was known from his restraining himself from answering that it was for a form of taqiyyah; he did not say what he had in mind regarding that, due to the usage of the sultans of the time of that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who separates from his wife without divorce or an oath, for a year, not approaching her bed. He said to me: Let him come to her family. He said: Whichever man makes an oath of abstention from his wife, and al-i'la' is that he says: 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period,' and says: 'By Allah, I will annoy you,' so he angers her, then he is given a respite of four months. Then after the four months he is taken and held in suspense. If he returns (fulfills), and al-ifa' is that he reconciles with his family, then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And if he does not return, compulsion for divorce is applied, and a divorce does not take place between them until he is held in suspense. And it is also after the four months that he is compelled to either return or be divorced.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man makes a vow from his wife, which is that he says 'By Allah, I will not have intercourse with you for such and such [period]', and he says 'By Allah, I will anger you', then he angers her, then he waits for her for four months. If he returns (to normalcy), and returning is that he reconciles with his family or divorces her at that time, and a divorce does not occur between them until it is suspended. If it is also after four months until he returns or is divorced.

From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about al-Ila' (oath of abstention from conjugal relations), what is it? He said: It is when a man says to his wife, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period,' or says, 'By Allah, I will keep you in suspense,' so he waits for her for four months. Then he is taken and brought to stand (before the judge/Imam) after the four months. If he returns (to conjugal life), which means he reconciles with his family, for indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And if he does not return, he is compelled to divorce her. So they do not divorce each other, and even if it were four months, as long as he does not refer the matter to the Imam.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man vowed not to approach his wife for three months. He said: So he said: Oath of abstention (Ila') does not become established until he swears for more than four months.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about al-Ila' (oath of abstention from conjugal relations), so he said: 'If four months pass and he is kept in suspense (between divorce and return), then either he divorces her or he returns (to conjugal life). I said: 'If he divorces her, does she observe the waiting period of the divorced woman?' He said: 'Yes.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who makes an oath of abstention from his wife until four months pass. He said: He is suspended. If he decides on divorce, his wife observes the waiting period just as the divorced woman does. If he returns (to conjugal life), he keeps her, and there is no harm.

From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Mansur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made an oath of abstention from his wife, and four months passed with her. He said: He is suspended. If he decides on divorce, she becomes divorced from him, and she has the waiting period of the divorced woman. If not, he expiates his oath, and he keeps her.

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who makes a vow of abstention (ila') from his wife. He said: 'Ila' is when the man says, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period.' Then he waits for four months. If he returns (to intimacy), that is fulfillment (ifa'). And fulfillment is when he reconciles with his family. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And if he does not return after four months, until he reconciles with his family or is divorced, he will be compelled to do so. And a divorce does not take effect between them until it is confirmed. And if it is after the four months, if he refuses, the Imam separates them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jarud that he heard Abu Ja'far (AS) saying: Regarding ila' (oath of abstention from conjugal relations), he is suspended after one year. I said, 'After one year?' He said, 'Yes, he is suspended after one year, so it does not contradict the earlier reports, because he said he is suspended after one year, and it is not in it that if it is less than that, he is not suspended. And this depends on the evidence of the context, and that may be set aside for another evidence, and we have previously presented what necessitates the return from it.'

And as for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Muhassan ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Maryam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from a man who made vow of abstention from his wife, he said: He is suspended before the four months and after them. The meaning of his saying (peace be upon him) 'suspended before the four months' is that we interpret it as being suspended for the purpose of obligating a ruling upon him during the specified period for that, which is the four months, without being obligated to divorce or consumption. And as for after the four months, then he is obligated either to divorce or consummation, as we have clarified. And it is possible that the meaning of 'ilā' (vow of abstention) in this report is 'ẓihār' (verbal divorce), for if it is so, then the period in it is three months, which indicates that.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed *dharam* (oath of abstention) from his wife. He said: If he had intercourse with her, then upon him is freeing a slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people. And if he did not, he is left for three months. If he returned (to intercourse), and if not, he is stopped until he is asked: Do you have a need for your wife, or will you divorce her? If he returned, there is nothing upon him and she is his wife. And if he divorces her (once), he has more right to take her back.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding Al-Ila' (oath of abstention from wife): When a man takes an oath not to approach his wife, nor touch her, nor join his head with her head, he is in ease (has time) as long as four months do not pass. When four months have passed and he is asked (to choose), either he returns (to intimacy) and touches her, or he resolves on divorce, so he frees her until she menstruates and purifies from her menses, then he divorces her with one pronouncement before he has intercourse with her, with the testimony of two just witnesses. Then he is more entitled to take her back as long as the three menstrual periods have not passed.

From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one granted time (mu'allah) is suspended after four months; if he wishes, he retains her with kindness, or releases her with grace. If he decides on divorce, it is a single revocable divorce, and he has the right to take her back.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Mu'allā (husband who delays consummation) when he is compelled (to choose) and does not return (to consummation), he is divorced with a final divorce.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: Indeed, the Mu'la is compelled to issue a final divorce. The rationale in these two reports, although the source in both is one (namely, Mansur ibn Hazim), is to interpret them as referring to the one whom the Imam sees fit to compel to issue a final divorce due to a certain consideration of interest, without that being obligatory in every Mu'la who is divorced.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Suwayd al-Qalla' from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who makes a vow of abstention from his wife. If he remains for four months and does not return, it is a pronouncement of divorce, then it is suspended. If he returns, it is two divorces in his hand; and if he resolves (to keep it final), it is a final separation from him. This narration, if taken at its apparent meaning, leads to contradiction with the narrations we presented in the first chapter, that the ruling of divorce and return is only required after the four months. The report implies that this period is a divorce, which is not correct. The correct interpretation is that if he divorces after the four months, it is a revocable divorce. If he returns (meaning he remarries her), it is two divorces in his hand. And if he resolves until the waiting period expires, it becomes a final separation, and he does not have the right to return her except with a new contract and a specified dowry.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the Mu'all (a husband who refuses to divorce his wife), if he refuses to be divorced, it was said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would make for him a pen of reeds, confine him in it, and prevent him from food and drink until he is divorced.

From him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Ishaq ibn Bunan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when the one to be kept apart (al-mu'allā) refused to divorce, would make for him a pen of reeds and give him a quarter of his sustenance until he divorced.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Khalaf ibn Hammam in a hadith of his, which he raises to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the Mawali (client), either he fulfills [the Imam's command] or he is divorced; if he does so, [it is accepted], but if not, his neck is struck [beheaded]. This report is Mursal (disconnected); it is not objected to with a similar [disconnected] report against the Musnad (connected) reports. And if it were sound, it would be interpreted as referring to one who refuses to accept the ruling of the Imam, whether [refusing] divorce or fulfillment, in opposition to him and to the Sharia of Islam. For whoever has this description is considered a disbeliever, and killing him is obligatory upon him. As for one who is not like that, it is not obligatory upon him to be killed; rather, imprisonment and constriction upon him until he is divorced or fulfills [the obligation] is sufficient, according to what the first two reports contained.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him): Is it permissible to have temporary marriage (mut'ah) with a slave girl with the permission of her owners? He said: Yes. Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So marry them with the permission of their owners.'
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: I asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who enjoys the concubinage of a man's slave girl with his permission; he said: 'Yes.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him): Is it permissible for a man to enjoy (have sexual relations with) a slave girl with the permission of her owners, while he has a free wife? He said: Yes, if it is with the permission of her owners, provided the free wife is pleased. I said: If the free wife gives him permission, he can enjoy from her? He said: Yes.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a female slave as a mut'ah (temporary marriage) in addition to a free woman. He said: No. The correct view is to consider that it is not permissible for him to marry her except with the permission of the free woman, as we have clarified in the narration of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', without that being forbidden in all cases.
