Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who performed *dhahir* (expiation of zihar) from his wife five times or more. He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: Upon him, for each time, is an expiation.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who performs zihar with his wife fifteen times, he said: For him are fifteen expiations.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who pronounced zihar against his wife five times or more. He said: Upon him, for each time, is an expiation.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir who said: Abu al-Ward asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while I was with him about a man who said to his wife, 'You are upon me like the back of my mother' one hundred times. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He is able to free one slave for each time.' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then is he able to feed sixty poor people one hundred times?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then is he able to fast for two consecutive months one hundred times?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'He should distribute [the expiations] among them.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in A man who performed *zihar* with his wife four times in one session, he said: 'Upon him is one expiation.' The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as meaning he bears one expiation in kind, which does not differ, just as the expiations differ in matters other than *zihar*; and the intended meaning is not that he bears one expiation for the many times.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding: A man who had ten female slaves, and he performed *dhahr* (expiation of consanguinity) from all of them together with a single statement, so he said: upon him are ten expiations.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) In the case of a man who pronounces Zihar from four women, he said: 'Upon him is one expiation.' The meaning in this report is what preceded the statement in similar cases, that we interpret it to mean that upon him is one expiation in kind, either freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people, according to the obligatory sequence in that matter. And it is not obligatory for some of them [the women] to have freeing [of a slave], and for some of them fasting, or feeding [the poor]. And the meaning of his saying 'one expiation' is not that one of the expiations suffices for the four women.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performs zihar from his slave-girl, so he said: The free woman and the slave-girl are equal in this.

Ali ibn Isma'il, from Fadala, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) About a man who performed *dhihar* from his slave girl, he said: It is like the *dhihar* of a free woman.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: He was asked about Dhihar (expiation by declaring oneself like the mother's back) upon a free woman and a slave woman; he said: Yes.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Ibn Bukayr from Hamzah ibn Humran who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made his slave-girl upon him like the back of his mother, so he said: He may approach her, and there is no penalty upon him. Therefore, the interpretation of this narration is that it applies if he omitted one of the conditions of the Dhihar, because Hamzah ibn Humran is reported to have said this in the book of Al-Bazzafi: He said this for a slave-girl, intending to please his wife. This indicates that he did not intend the true Dhihar, and if he did not intend that, his Dhihar is not valid, and the basis for the expiation does not attach to him.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about one who performed *dhahir* in the month of Sha'ban and could not find what to free [a slave], so he said: He waits until he fasts the month of Ramadan, then he fasts two consecutive months. If he performed *dhahir* while he was a traveler, he waits until he arrives [home]. And if he fasted and then acquired wealth, he must complete what he began.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from al-Ahwal, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), regarding: A man who fasted a month as the expiation for Dhahir, then found a slave to free, he said: 'He frees her and does not count the fasting.' The view in this narration is that we interpret it as a type of recommended act (istihbab) rather than obligatory (farḍ) and compulsory (ijbar).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, or others, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Sunnah divorce. He said: The Sunnah divorce is when a man intends to divorce his wife; if he has consummated the marriage with her, he leaves her until she menstruates and then becomes pure. When she becomes pure, he divorces her once in the presence of two witnesses. Then he leaves her until she completes three menstrual periods. When three periods have passed, she is definitively divorced from him by one divorce, and her husband is suitor among the suitors; if she wishes, she can marry him, and if she wishes, she does not. If she marries him with a new dowry, she is with him on two remaining divorces, and one has passed. If he divorces her once more while she is pure, in the presence of two witnesses, then leaves her until her periods pass, and when her periods pass before he revokes her, she is definitively divorced from him by two divorces, and she has control of her affairs and is permissible for other husbands, and her husband is a suitor among the suitors; if she wishes, she can marry him, and if she wishes, she does not. If he marries her with a new marriage and a new dowry, she is with him on one remaining divorce, and two have passed. If he wishes to divorce her with a divorce that does not make her permissible to him until she marries another husband, he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he witnesses upon her divorce one divorce. Then she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband. As for the divorce of the waiting period, he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he divorces her in the presence of two witnesses. Then he revokes her and consummates with her, then he waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has two witnesses witness upon another divorce. Then he revokes her and consummates with her, then he waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has the two witnesses witness upon the third divorce. Then she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband. And upon her is to observe three menstrual periods from the day he divorces her with the third divorce. If he divorces her once while pure with witnesses, then waits with he

From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: When a man intends divorce, he divorces her before the expiration of her waiting period without sexual intercourse. If he divorces her once and then leaves her until her waiting period expires, if he wishes to court her along with other suitors, he may do so. If he revokes her before the waiting period expires or after it, she is still considered his with one divorce. If he divorces her a second time and wishes to court her along with other suitors, provided he left her until the waiting period expired, and if he wishes, he may revoke her before the waiting period expires; if he does so, she is with him with two divorces. If he divorces her a third time, she does not become permissible to him until she marries another husband, and she inherits and is inherited from as she was in the blood-relationship of the first two divorces.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife until she was completely divorced from him and her waiting period ended, then she married another husband, and he divorced her again, then she married her first husband. Does that [subsequent] divorce annul the first divorce? He said: Yes. Ibn Sama'ah said: And Ibn Bukayr used to say: When a divorced woman is divorced by her husband, then he leaves her until she is completely divorced, then he marries her, she is considered with him as being on a new divorce. Ibn Sama'ah said: And al-Husayn ibn Hashim mentioned that he asked Ibn Bukayr about it, and he answered him with this answer. He said to him: Did you hear anything regarding this? He said: The narration of Rifa'ah. He said: Indeed Rifa'ah narrated that when a husband enters between them [the couple], he said: A husband and a non-husband are the same to me. I said: Did you hear anything regarding this? He said: No, this is from what Allah granted him of personal reasoning (ra'y). Ibn Sama'ah said: And we do not take the opinion of Ibn Bukayr, for the narration is that when there is a husband between them.

And Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Muawiya ibn Hakim from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira who said: I asked Abdullah ibn Bukayr about a man who divorced his wife once, then kept her in waiting period until the divorce became final (three divorces), then he married her again. He said: She is with him as she was in the first marriage. I said: But the narration of Rifah states that if there is a husband between them (a third party), [she becomes fully free]. He said to me: Abdullah, this [your view] is from what Allah has granted of intellect/reasoning.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn Umayrah from Abd Allah ibn Sinan who said: When a man divorces his wife, he should divorce her during a period of purity (from menstruation) before consummation, with witnesses. If he marries her again after that, she is considered with him as having been divorced once, and the first divorce is nullified. And if he divorces her twice, then refrains from her until the second menstruation passes, she is definitively divorced from him by two divorces, and he is suitor-like among the suitors. If he marries her again after that, she is with him as having had three divorces, and the two are nullified. If he divorces her three times during the waiting period, she does not become permissible to him until she marries another husband.

And this report was narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu al-Hasan from Saif ibn Umayrah from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) similarly. The correct approach in this narration is to interpret it in light of what we mentioned in the preceding narration, which is that if she marries after exiting her waiting period to a husband with a permanent contract and he consummates the marriage with her, then separates from her by death or divorce, it is permissible for her to return to the first husband with a new contract. And the husband's consummation in this case invalidates the divorce, whether it was one, two, or three [divorces]. And that which indicates that the husband demolishes the single divorce just as he demolishes the three [divorces].

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Rifah ibn Musa, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man divorced his wife with one divorce, so she became fully divorced from him. Then another man married her and divorced her according to the Sunnah, so she became fully divorced from him. Then the first man married her again. How many divorces does she have with him? He said: She has no [remaining] divorces. Then he said: O Rifah, what if he divorced her three times, then married her a second time, and the divorce count was completed? If he then divorces her once, she has three [remaining] divorces.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with a single divorce, then left her until her waiting period expired, and she married another man. Then the second husband died or divorced her, and the first husband remarried her. He said: She is upon him with two divorces remaining.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan from Mansur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a woman whom her husband divorced once or twice, then he left her until her waiting period expired, and another man married her; then if that man died or divorced her, and the first husband married her again, he said: Her status with him is according to what remains of the divorces.
From him, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), like it. Like it.

From him, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: Regarding a man who divorces his wife with a single divorce, then marries her after another husband, she is considered by him to still be in the state of the remaining divorce.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad from Abdullah ibn Muhammad who said: I said to him: It has been narrated from Abu Abdillah regarding a man who divorces his wife with the three divorces (of the Book and the Sunnah), so she becomes definitively divorced from him with one, and then marries another man, and he dies from her or divorces her, and she returns to her first husband, that she is considered to have two divorces, and one has already passed. He wrote: 'They are correct.' The meaning in these narrations is one of two things: either the second husband did not consummate the marriage with her, or he married her for a fixed term (mut'ah), or he was not of age. And if the marriage was permanent, this condition is observed for the second husband. And if any of these conditions is lacking, it is not permissible for her to return to the first if the divorce is the third. And if she returns to the first after the third and the first, this is not destructive of what preceded. And that which indicates the consideration of these conditions which we mentioned.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The woman who does not become permissible to her husband until she marries another man?' He said: 'She is the one who is divorced, then reconciled, then divorced, then reconciled, then divorced for the third time; so she is the one who does not become permissible to her husband until she marries another man who tastes her sweetness.'

Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in Regarding a man who divorces his wife with a single divorce, then revokes her after the expiration of her waiting period, and if he divorces her three times, she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband. If the other man marries her, does not consummate the marriage with her, and divorces her or dies, she is not permissible to the first husband until the second man has tasted her 'usaylah'. And that which indicates that it is observed that the husband must be mature and the marriage must be permanent.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said: I wrote to Al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man divorced his wife with the divorce by which she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband, and a boy who had not reached puberty married her. He (AS) said: No, until he reaches puberty. And I wrote to him: What is the limit of puberty? He (AS) said: That which imposes the obligations (of hudud/punishments) upon the believer.

And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with two divorces during the waiting period, then she contracted a temporary marriage (mut'ah). Is she permissible to her first husband after that? He said: No, until she marries another man.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a woman, then divorced her, and she became independent (from him), then another man married her for a fixed term (mut'ah); is she permissible for her first husband? He said: No, until she enters into what she exited from.

From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from al-Hasan al-Siqqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man divorced his wife with a divorce that does not make her permissible to him until she marries another husband, and then she married him for a temporary marriage (mut'ah). Is she permissible to the first husband? He said: No. Because Allah, the Exalted, says: 'So if he divorces her, she is not permissible to him afterwards until she marries another husband. So if he divorces her,' and the temporary marriage does not include a divorce.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Mudarib said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the eunuch, does he effect the release (of the wife)? He said: He does not effect the release.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in A man divorced his wife three times, so she became independent from him, and he wanted to remarry her. He said to her, 'I intend to remarry you, so marry another husband.' She said to him, 'I have married another husband and my self has become lawful to you.' Will his word be accepted and will he remarry her, and what should he do? He said, 'If the woman is trustworthy, her word is accepted.' The second view in the narrations we have presented is that they should be understood as being based on a form of taqiyyah (dissimulation), because it is the school of Umar, so it is permissible that the situation necessitated him giving a ruling in it that matches his school, which indicates that.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Amr ibn Thabit from Abdullah ibn Aqil ibn Abi Talib said: Two men differed regarding the case of Ali and Umar concerning a woman whom her husband had divorced with one or two divorces, then another man married her, and he either divorced her or died, so when her waiting period ended, the first husband married her. Umar said: 'She is upon what remains of the divorce.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah, does three [divorces] not annul [the bond], and one [divorce] not annul [it]?' (Implying that if three divorces are required to make her fully permissible again, one should suffice to return her to the first husband without a new marriage contract, or conversely, that the logic of 'annulment' applies equally).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'ah, from Ibn Ribat, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, all from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, that he asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who said: To his wife, 'You are forbidden to me,' or he divorced her with a clear divorce, or a final divorce, or a complete divorce, or an absolute divorce. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of this is of no effect. The divorce is that he says to her at the beginning of the waiting period, after she has purified herself from her menses, before he has intercourse with her: You are divorced, or 'I have taken back' (Istadda), meaning by that the divorce, and he calls two just men to witness against that.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Divorce occurs when he says to her, 'Observe the waiting period,' or when he says to her, 'You are divorced.'

From him, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, who said: The matter upon which there is consensus regarding divorce is that he says to her, 'You are divorced,' or 'Observe the waiting period.' It was narrated that he said to Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, 'How do you bear witness to his saying, 'Observe the waiting period'?' He said, 'He says, 'Bear witness that I have divorced you (or: Observe the waiting period).' ' Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said, 'This is an error. Divorce is not except as Bukayr ibn A'yan narrated: He says to her while she is pure from non-coitus, 'You are divorced,' and he calls two just witnesses. And everything other than that is void.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The hadiths that we have presented, from their saying 'Observe the waiting period,' can be interpreted in a way that does not contradict the sound ruling according to what Ibn Sama'ah said, because their saying 'Observe the waiting period' only serves as consideration (or: is effective) if preceded by the man's saying 'You are divorced,' then he says 'Observe the waiting period,' because his saying to her 'Observe the waiting period' does not have a meaning in itself, because she could say, 'From what [cause] do I observe the waiting period?' Therefore, he must say to her, 'Observe the waiting period, for I have divorced you.' Thus, the consideration is with the divorce, not with this saying, except that this saying serves as a clarifier for her that the ruling of divorce has become binding upon her and necessitates that for her. And if it were isolated without the word of divorce preceding it, it would not be considered according to what Ibn Sama'ah said.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who delegated the authority regarding his wife to a man, saying: 'Bear witness that I have delegated the authority of so-and-so to so-and-so.' Is that valid for that man? He said: 'Yes.'

Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who entrusts the matter of his wife to a man, and he said: 'Bear witness that I have entrusted the matter of so-and-so to so-and-so,' and he divorces her, is that permissible? He said: 'Yes.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Hilal al-Razi said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man appointed an agent to divorce his wife when she menstruates and becomes pure. The man went out, and it occurred to him (to change his mind), and he testified that he had annulled what he had ordered him to do, and that it had occurred to him regarding that. He (peace be upon him) said: Let him inform his family and let him inform the agent.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nuflī, from al-Sakkūnī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hands of two men; one of them divorced her, but the other refused. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) rejected validating that until they both agree together on the divorce.

From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman, from Mismar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hand of two men, so one of them divorced her and the other refused, so Imam Ali (peace be upon him) did not approve of that until they both agree on the divorce.

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Yaqṭīnī, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent to me a bundle of clothes, a group of servants, dinars, and funded a pilgrimage for me, a pilgrimage for my brother Musa ibn Ubayd, and a pilgrimage for Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, and ordered us to perform Hajj on his behalf. There was one hundred dinars among us, divided into thirds. When I intended to inspect the clothes, I saw clay in the folds of the garments. I asked the messenger, 'What is this?' He said, 'Whenever goods are sent, clay from the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is placed in them.' Then the messenger said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, 'It is a guarantee of safety by God's permission.' He ordered matters regarding the money for maintaining his family and needy people, and ordered the payment of three hundred dinars to Ruḥaym, a woman who was his, and ordered me to divorce her on his behalf, and to provide her with maintenance (mut'ah) with this money, and ordered me to witness her divorce before Safwan ibn Yahya and another whom Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā forgot his name.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ibn Ibraham from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who divorces his wife: He has the right to reconcile (with her). And he said: He does not divorce her with the third divorce until he has had sexual intercourse with her.

From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The remarriage (raj'ah) is in sexual intercourse; otherwise, it is only one revocation. We have fully detailed in the conditions of the revocable divorce (talaq al-'iddah) what relates to that in our Great Book, and something of it has preceded.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Jamil, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: Does the return (raj'ah) occur without sexual intercourse? He said: Yes.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the return (raj'ah) without sexual intercourse, does it constitute a return? He said: Yes. The explanation in these two narrations is that it is a return without sexual intercourse, meaning that he returns to the state he was in, namely that he has the right to consummate the marriage. If it were not for the return, that would not be permissible. And the narration does not indicate that it is permissible for him to divorce her with another divorce for the waiting period, even if he does not consummate. And we only consider the consummation for one who intends to do so. As for one who does not intend that, then intercourse is not a condition for him. And the return may be established by denying the divorce or by a kiss, although that is not sufficient for one who intends to divorce a second time, according to what we have completed in our Great Book, and that does not contradict this.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awwaz and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife and testified to the revocatory divorce (raj'ah) but did not have sexual intercourse, then he divorced her again in another period of purity in accordance with the Sunnah. Is the second divorce established without sexual intercourse? He said: Yes, if he testified to the revocatory divorce and did not have sexual intercourse, the divorce is considered the second one.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Al-Redha (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with two witnesses, then he reconciled with her, but did not have sexual intercourse with her after the reconciliation until she purified from her menstruation, then he divorced her again on a state of purity with two witnesses. Does the second divorce take effect upon her, having reconciled with her but not having had intercourse? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said: I asked him face-to-face about a man who divorced his wife with two witnesses during her purity (period), then he traveled and testified to her return (raj'a). When he returned, he divorced her without sexual intercourse. I asked: Is that permissible for him? He said: Her divorce has become valid, because in these narrations there is no indication that he must divorce her as a 'divorce of the waiting period' (talaq al-'iddah). We only prevent him from divorcing her as a 'divorce of the waiting period'. As for the 'divorce of the Sunnah', there is no harm in him divorcing her after that, according to what was included in the narration of Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad and others. And the more preferred view indicating the permissibility of this is that it is permissible for him to divorce her with another divorce for the Sunnah, even if he did not have intercourse with her.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Saif ibn Amirah from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: A man divorced his wife, then took her back with witnesses, then divorced her, then it occurred to him so he took her back with witnesses, then divorced her, then took her back with witnesses. Is she completely divorced from him? He said: Yes. I said: All of that was in one period of purity? He said: She is completely divorced from him. I said: If he did that with a pregnant woman, is she completely divorced from him? He said: This is not like that. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in this report is that if he divorces her three times in one period of purity, with two revocations in between according to the Sunnah, then she is completely divorced from him by the third, as we have mentioned, even if he had not consummated the marriage with her, because whenever he takes her back, it is permissible for him to divorce her another time according to the Sunnah, as we explained. And that is not found in the pregnant woman, because the pregnant woman, when he takes her back, it is not permissible for him to divorce her another time according to the Sunnah until she gives birth to what is in her womb. And it is only permissible for him to divorce her for the waiting period if he has intercourse with her after the revocation, according to what we will explain the statement about, God willing. And this does not contradict this report.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Kahmas (and his name is Haytham ibn Ubayd), from a man from the people of Wasit, from our companions, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'My uncle divorced his wife three times, one divorce in each purity period.' He said: 'Tell him to have her reviewed (by a new marriage contract), because the meaning in this report is that we assume he issued one additional divorce without a review, for we only permit the three divorions for the sake of the Sunnah in one purity period if he reviews between each two divorces, even if that is in one purity period, as we have clarified.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife with one divorce while she was pure, then kept her in his house until she had two menstruations and became pure, then divorced her with two divorces while she was pure. He said: This is if she had three menstruations from the day he divorced her with the first divorce, then she has become lawful for marriage. But how should I act or say this? And in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is narrated that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, give me a ruling regarding myself. He said: Regarding what shall I give you a ruling? She said: My husband divorced me while I was pure, then kept me so he did not have sexual intercourse with me, until I menstruated and became pure, then he divorced me with another divorce. Then he kept me so he did not have sexual intercourse with me, except that he uses me (for intimacy) and sees my hair, my neck, and my body, until I menstruated the third time and became pure, then he divorced me with the third divorce. He said, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: O woman, do not marry until you have had three fresh menstruations. For the three menstruations you had while you were in his house, you only had them while you were in his bonds (of marriage). What the main part of this narration contains is that if he divorces her with one divorce at each menstruation, then she observes the waiting period from the first divorce. The meaning of this is that if he divorces her a second time without revocation (regaining her), then his divorce does not take effect (as a final divorce), and the waiting period is upon her from the first divorce. And what he narrated at the end of the narration, which he found in the book of Ali (peace be upon him), admits two possibilities: One is that it was permissible because he revoked her (regained her) then divorced her, so the waiting period was upon her from the final divorce, if the divorces were according to the Sunnah as we have explained. And the other possibility is that it is based on precaution (Taqiyyah), because among the jurists there are those who permit the three divorces one after another at each menstruation

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: She who is divorced, then taken back, then divorced again, and there is no sexual intercourse between the first divorce and the second divorce, then she becomes permissible to him before marrying another husband. And she who is not permissible to him until she marries another husband, is she who has sexual intercourse between the first divorce and the second divorce. And no one should say, 'How is this distinction possible?' when all the narrations are general, and none of them contains the specific distinction you mentioned, such as...

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ash'ari from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-mut'ah, is it one of the four? He said: No.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Riab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I asked, 'What is permissible from temporary marriage (al-mut'ah)?' He said, 'As many as you wish.'

And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about al-Mut'ah (temporary marriage): Is it one of the four? He said: No, and not one of the seventy.

From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Temporary marriage (Al-Mut'ah) was mentioned to him. He was asked: Is it from the four [types of wives]? He said: Marry a thousand of them, for they are hired [women].

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has a wife, is it permissible for him to marry her sister in temporary marriage (mut'ah)? He said: No. I said: Zurarah narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that she is like the concubines; he may marry whomever he wishes. He said: No, she is one of the four [wives]. The resolution between these two reports is that we should interpret them as a form of precaution and excellence, while the earlier reports are interpreted as permitting it and removing the prohibition, which indicates that.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Make them from the four.' Safwan ibn Yahya asked him: 'Is it based on precaution (ihtiyat)?' He said: 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while she was in a state of purity (from menstruation) without sexual intercourse, and he witnessed with one man on that day, then waited five days, then witnessed with another man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They were only commanded to have both witnesses present together.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from the Imam (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about separating the two witnesses in divorce, and he said: Yes, and she counts the waiting period from the first of the two witnesses. And he said: It is not permissible until they both testify, so it does not contradict the first report because the way to resolve it is to interpret it as permitting the separation between them during the time of witnessing, not during the time of bearing the testimony, so that the two reports do not contradict each other.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one who divorces [his wife] during a state of purity in a single session after session, three times. He said: It counts as one.

From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Ali ibn Hadeed, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Kha'thami, from Amr ibn al-Bara', who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, our companions say that if a man divorces his wife once or a hundred times, it is only one divorce. And it had reached us from you and from your fathers that they used to say: if he divorces once or a hundred times, it is only one.' He said: 'It is as it reached you.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Humran from Zurara from one of them (peace be upon him) in the one who is divorced in a state of purity in one session three times, he said: She is one (divorce).

From him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurarah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If he divorces her for the waiting period more than once, the advantage (of revocability) over one divorce is not [applicable to] a single divorce [in the same way].

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabshi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) In the case of a man who appointed a man to divorce his wife and ordered him to divorce her according to the Sunnah, so he divorced her three times in one sitting. He said: It is returned to being one (revocable) divorce. When three months or three menstrual periods have passed, then it is finalized by one.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim, from a group of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Amawi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced [his wife] three times in one sitting. He said: As for me, I consider it to have taken effect (binding), and as for my father, he considered it to be one [divorce].

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I was with him when a man came and asked him. He said: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' He said: 'She becomes permanently divorced from him.' The man left, then another of our companions came and asked: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' He said: 'One divorce.' Another came and asked: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' He said: 'It is nothing (no effect).' Then he looked at me and said: 'It is as you see.' I said: 'How is this?' He said: 'This one believes that if a man divorces his wife three times, she becomes permanently divorced from him. And I believe that if a man divorces his wife three times in accordance with the Sunnah, she becomes permanently divorced from him. And if a man divorces his wife three times while she is in a state of purity, it is only one divorce. And if a man divorces his wife three times while she is not in a state of purity, it is nothing (no effect).'

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever divorces [his wife] three times in one session, it is not [considered] three; he who differs [from this], let him return to the Book of Allah. He mentioned the divorce of Ibn Umar, but this narration does not state that he divorced her three times with the obligatory conditions of divorce. It is possible that the intended meaning is if he divorced her while she was menstruating. The report which we have previously mentioned from Abu Basir, the narrator of this hadith, and the detailed hadith of Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz indicate that whoever divorces three times during menstruation, none of them take effect. And if he divorces her during purity, one takes effect, as we have previously mentioned. Taking the detailed hadith is more preferable than the general one. This is also indicated by his saying, 'Then he mentioned the hadith of Ibn Umar,' because Ibn Umar only divorced his wife while she was menstruating. If the intended meaning were what we mentioned, there would be no benefit in mentioning Ibn Umar in this place. And that which indicates that the divorce of Ibn Umar was during menstruation.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife three times in one sitting. He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) returned to 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar his wife, whom he had divorced three times while she was menstruating. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) annulled that divorce and said: 'Everything that contradicts the Book of Allah and the Sunnah is to be returned to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever divorces his wife three times in one sitting while she is in her menstruation period, it is not valid. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) rejected the divorce of Abdullah ibn Umar when he divorced his wife three times while she was menstruating, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) annulled that divorce and said: 'Everything that contradicts the Book of Allah is returned to the Book of Allah,' and he said: 'There is no divorce except during the waiting period.' It is also possible that his saying 'it is not valid' means that it does not constitute three divorces, because we have explained that it is returned to one, and that which clarifies what we mentioned.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar divorced his wife three times, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) counted it as one single divorce, and returned it to the Book and the Sunnah.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from al-Husayn ibn Ziyad al-Siql, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not testify for the one who divorces [his wife] three times in one sitting.' The meaning in this narration, likewise, is what we have previously stated: that if the divorce occurs during the state of menstruation, or the state of intoxication, or under compulsion, because each of these conditions invalidates the occurrence of the divorce.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Beware of the women who are divorced three times in one sitting, for they are considered to have one husband.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Beware of those who are triple-divorced, for they are wives (still in the waiting period). The correct approach regarding these narrations is also to interpret them as meaning that if the divorce occurs during menstruation, or according to one of the cases we have previously mentioned where the divorce does not take effect, it is permissible that the intended meaning is one who pronounces divorce with a condition, for that is also among what does not take effect, indicating this meaning.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Bashir ibn Ja'far from Abu Usamah al-Hannat said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A relative of mine or a man by marriage of mine swore that if his wife exits the door, she is divorced three times.' So she exited, and her husband had intercourse with her as God willed from the hardship. He ordered me to ask you, so he leaned towards me and said: 'Order him to keep her; it is not [considered] anything [i.e., the third divorce does not take effect].' Then he turned to the people and said: 'Glory be to God, they order her to marry [another man] while she still has a husband.'

Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: A man asked him (peace be upon him) while I was present, regarding a man who divorced his wife three times in one sitting. He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever divorces his wife three times according to the Sunnah, then she is fully divorced from him.' He then turned to me and said: 'So-and-so does not know how to say this properly, so it does not contradict the previously narrated reports, because he only said: Indeed, whoever divorces his wife three times according to the Sunnah, then she is fully divorced from him. And that does not happen except by consummating the marriage with her according to what the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) established in three times, upon the fixed conditions in that matter. And whoever divorces his wife three times in one instance, the three divorces are not enacted according to what is established in the Sunnah and confirmed in the Sharia. And he (peace be upon him) did not explicitly state that to the questioner due to a form of taqiyyah (dissimulation), and he said what serves as a reminder regarding it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, al-Baqir) (peace be upon him) along with some of our companions, and the reply came to me in his own handwriting. I said: 'You mentioned the matter of your daughter and her husband, may Allah rectify for you what you love to be rectified.' As for what you mentioned regarding his breaking his oath by divorcing her more than once, look (into the matter), may Allah have mercy on you. If he is among those who follow us and speak with our speech, there is no divorce upon him, because he did not do something he was ignorant of. And if he is among those who do not follow us nor speak with our speech, then effect an khula' (divorce by redemption) from him, for he only intended separation specifically.

From him, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from one of our companions, who said: Some of the Alawites, who used to belittle him, were mentioned in the presence of Al-Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: 'Indeed, he is remaining upon what is forbidden.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, how is that, while she is his mother (of the child)?' He said: 'How did he divorce her?' I said: 'How did he divorce her?' He said: 'He divorced her, and that is his religion (custom/practice), so she became forbidden to him.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife without observing the waiting period (iddah), then he withheld her (did not finalize the divorce) until the waiting period ended. Is it permissible for me to marry her? He said: Yes, a woman should not be left without a husband.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, who said: Several people from the companions of Ali ibn Abi Hamzah informed me that he asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the woman who is divorced in a manner contrary to the Sunnah. Should the man marry her? He said: Bind them to that which they bound themselves to, and marry them, and there is no objection to that.

Al-Hasan ibn Sam'a said, and I heard Ja'far ibn Sam'a, and he was asked about a woman who was divorced in a manner other than the Sunnah, 'Is it permissible for me to marry her?' So he said: He said, 'Yes.' I said to him, 'Do you not know that Ali ibn Hanzala narrated: 'Beware of the thrice-divorced women who are divorced other than according to the Sunnah, for they are women with husbands'?' He said, 'O my son, the narration of Ali ibn Abi Hamzah is more lenient for the people.' I said, 'So what did he narrate?' He said, 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Bind them to that which they bound themselves to, and marry them, for there is no harm.'

From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Abbas al-Qabbagh, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'Narrate from me that whoever divorces his wife three times in one sitting, she has become permanently divorced from him.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ash'ari narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Alawi, from his father, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the marriage of women given three divorces, and he said to me: 'Your divorce is not permissible for others [to marry them], and their divorce is permissible for you, because you do not consider the three [divorces] to be anything [i.e., one counts as one], while they obligate it [i.e., they consider three to be three].'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadl from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorced his wife three times, and a man wanted to marry her, what should he do? He said: He goes to him and says, 'You divorced so-and-so.' When he says 'Yes,' he leaves her for three months, then proposes to her directly.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent. He said: His divorce is valid in all cases, and his wife observes the waiting period (iddah) from the day he divorces her.

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Hashim ibn Hanan, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man divorces his wife while he is absent, and he knows that on the day he divorced her, she was menstruating. He said: It is valid. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations have come generally regarding the validity of the absent person's divorce in all cases, but it is appropriate to restrict them by stating that a month or more must have passed during his absence, which indicates this.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The absent husband, if he wishes to divorce his wife, should leave her for a month. And this report does not contradict [other reports].

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man leaves his home for travel, he is not permitted to divorce [his wife] until three months have passed.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him): 'For the absent husband whose wife is divorced, what is the duration of his absence?' He said: 'Five months or six months.' I said: 'What is the minimum limit below that?' He said: 'Three months.' Because the way to reconcile between these two reports and the first report is to say: 'The ruling varies according to the custom of women regarding menstruation. So whoever knows of his wife's condition that she menstruates once every month, it is permissible for him to divorce her after the month ends. And whoever knows that she does not menstruate except every three months or five months, it is not permissible for him to divorce her except after the passage of this period.' Thus, the consideration in the permissibility of that is the passage of one menstruation and its transition to a period of purity in which he did not have intercourse with her, and that varies according to what we have said.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Maskin, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man is absent from his wife for a year, or two years, or more, and then he returns and intends to divorce her, and she is in menstruation, he should leave her until she becomes pure, and then he divorces her.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Hajjaj al-Khashshab, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who was traveling, and when he entered the city, he brought with him two witnesses. When his wife met him at the door, he testified to her divorce. He said: Divorce does not take effect upon her. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it according to what the first report contained, that his divorce takes effect only insofar as she was in her menstruation, because if she had been pure, the divorce would have taken effect as it would have taken effect if he had not been absent at all. It is also possible that the report is specific to one who was absent from his wife during a period of purity, approached her with intercourse, and returned while she was still in that same period of purity; he may not divorce her except after her waiting period (istibra') by one menstruation.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from some of our companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: When the wife who has not been entered into (consummated) is divorced, she becomes free from the marriage bond by a single pronouncement.

From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her; she may marry immediately if she wishes, and this counts as one irrevocable divorce. And if he had fixed a dowry (mahr) for her, she is entitled to half of what he fixed.

From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Thabit ibn Shuraih, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man marries a woman and then divorces her before entering into her, there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her, and she may marry whenever she wishes from that moment, and it is considered one single divorce.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn Amirah from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman whom her husband divorced three times before consummating the marriage, he said: She is not permissible to him until she marries another husband, so it does not contradict the earlier reports which indicated that she becomes fully divorced (bayyinah) with one divorce, because the meaning in this report is that if he contracted marriage with her three times, divorcing her each time before consummation, then in this state she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Hammam ibn Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in A man divorced his wife, then left her until her waiting period expired, then he married her, then he divorced her without having intercourse with her, then he married her again, then he divorced her before having intercourse with her, until he did that to her three times. He said: She is not permissible to him until she marries a husband other than him.

From him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorced his wife, then left her until her waiting period expired, then married her again, then divorced her again without having intercourse with her, until he did that three times. He said: She is not permissible to him until she marries a husband other than him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Tirbal said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with a single divorce before consummating the marriage, and he testified to that and informed her. He said: She becomes permanently divorced from him at the moment he divorces her, while she is still considered among the suitors (not yet in a new waiting period). I said: If he marries her again and then divorces her with another single divorce before consummating the marriage? He said: She becomes permanently divorced from him at the moment he divorces her. I said: If he marries her again immediately and then divorces her with a single divorce? He said: She becomes permanently divorced from him, and she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said: A virgin (wife) who is divorced three times and marains in a non-consummated marriage, has become permanently divorced (ba'in), and is not permissible for her husband until she marries another man. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations indicate what we said, that whoever divorces his wife three times for the sake of the Sunnah, she is not permissible for him until she marries another man, because the 'divorce of the waiting period' does not occur in the case of a virgin or one not yet consummated, and we have clarified that among the conditions of the 'divorce of the waiting period' is cohabitation after the return, and both of these do not occur in the one who has not been entered into.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Kunanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of a pregnant woman is one (revocation), and her waiting period is the nearer of the two periods.
From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The pregnant woman is divorced with a single divorce.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Isma'il al-Ja'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (revocable) divorce; so when she gives birth to what is in her womb, she is definitively divorced from him.

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him about the divorce of the pregnant woman, so he said: One divorce, and her waiting period is until she gives birth to her pregnancy.

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the pregnant woman is one revocable divorce; if he wishes, he may take her back before she gives birth. If she gives birth before he takes her back, then she is definitively divorced from him, and he is one of the suitors.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'If a pregnant woman is divorced by her husband, then he revokes her, then divorces her again, then revokes her again, then divorces her for the third time,' so he said: 'She becomes definitively divorced from him and is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.' This does not contradict the earlier narrations which contained that the divorce of the pregnant woman is one, because we only mentioned that in the case of the divorce of the Sunnah (revocation during the waiting period). As for the divorce of the waiting period (final divorce), then it is permissible for him to divorce her during the duration of her pregnancy if he has revoked her and had intercourse with her. If it is said: 'How is this possible for you with what has been narrated that when he revokes her, it is not for him to divorce her a second time until she gives birth to what is in her belly?' He narrated that.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Siqall from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant, he said: He divorces her. I asked: And if he revokes the divorce? He said: Yes, he revokes the divorce. I asked: If it occurs to him after he has revoked it to divorce her again, he said: No, until she gives birth. It was said to him: The meaning in this report is that he does not have the right to divorce her with any type of divorce. And if that is not the case, we interpret it as meaning he does not have the right to divorce her with the divorce of the Sunnah if he has already revoked it until she gives birth. As for the divorce of the waiting period, it is permissible if he has had intercourse with her, and this indicates that.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a pregnant woman who is divorced with a divorce that does not become effective until she marries another husband. He said: Yes. I said: Did you not tell me: If he has intercourse with her, it is not permissible for him to divorce her? He said: Indeed, divorce is not valid except during a period of purity in which intercourse has not occurred, and a pregnancy that has become evident; and in this case, her pregnancy has become evident.

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Yazid al-Kunasī, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the pregnant woman, and he said: 'She is divorced once for the waiting period with witnesses.' I said: 'Does he have the right to take her back?' He said: 'Yes, and she is still his wife.' I said: 'If he took her back and had intercourse with her, then intended to divorce her with another divorce,' he said: 'He does not divorce her until a month passes after he had intercourse with her.' I said: 'If he divorced her a second time and testified, then took her back and testified to her return and had intercourse with her, then divorced her with the third divorce and testified to her divorce for each waiting period being a month, does she become fully divorced from him just as the woman divorced once becomes fully divorced, who does not become permissible to her husband until she marries another husband?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is her waiting period?' He said: 'Her waiting period is that she gives birth to what is in her belly, then she becomes permissible to the husbands.'

Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadlal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from al-Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari and Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from one of them, who said: Regarding a man who has a pregnant wife and wishes to divorce her: He divorces her when he intends the divorce, with the testimony of witnesses. If it occurs to him on that day or afterwards that he wishes to take her back (revocation), he shall take her back with the same [conditions], and he shall consummate. Then if it occurs to him, he divorces her again. Then if it occurs to him, he shall take her back as he took her back the first time. Then if it occurs to him, he divorces her; she is the one who does not become lawful to him until she marries a husband other than him, if he is the revoking one who intends consummation and retention, and he consummates.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man whose wife is with him, and he remains silent and does not speak. He said: 'Is he mute?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'It is known from him that he dislikes his wife and has aversion to her.' I said: 'Yes.' 'Is it permissible for his guardian to divorce her on his behalf?' He said: 'No, but he should write and bear witness to that.' I said: 'May God perfect you, he does not write and does not hear; how is she divorced?' He said: 'By that which is known from his actions, like what you mentioned of his aversion to her or his dislike for her.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nuflī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the mute woman is that he takes her head-covering and places it on her head, then he separates from her.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus in a mute man who wrote on the ground regarding the divorce of his wife, he said: If he does that at the onset of purity, with witnesses, and is understood from him as one would understand from a similar person, and he intends divorce, then his divorce is valid according to the Sunnah.

Abd al-Malik ibn Umar narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the divorce of the insane person who has lost their intellect; is it valid? He said: No. And about the woman if she is like that; is her sale and her dowry valid? He said: No.

Hammad narrated from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the insane person, does his divorce take effect? He said: I said: 'What is it?' He said: 'The foolish one who has lost his intellect.' He said: 'Yes.' The explanation in this report is one of two things: One is that it is to be understood as referring to the one who is deficient in intellect, not the one who completely lacks it, for such is his description, and he is among those who distinguish between matters significantly, so his divorce takes effect. And the divorce of the one who knows nothing at all does not take effect due to the complete loss of his intellect. The second explanation is that we understand it as meaning that it is permissible if his guardian manages his affairs on his behalf, rather than he managing them himself.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Khalid al-Qammam who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'For the foolish man who has lost his mind, is the divorce of his guardian valid over him?' He said: 'And why would he not be divorced by him?' I said: 'We cannot be sure that if he divorces her, he will not say tomorrow,

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of a young boy is valid when he reaches ten years of age.

From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all of them, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the divorce of a boy who has not yet reached puberty (had not experienced seminal emission) and his mahr (dowry). He said: If he divorces [her] in accordance with the Sunnah and places the mahr in its proper place, then there is no objection, and it is valid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the young boy (child) is not effective (null), so it does not contradict the two previous narrations, because the meaning in this narration is that we interpret it as referring to one who does not possess intellect and does not know how to divorce properly, because that (intellect/maturity) is considered for the validity of his divorce, which indicates that.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from several of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from several of our companions from Ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the boy is valid if he has reached the age of discernment, and so is his will and his gift, even if he has not undergone puberty.

Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the divorce of a boy who has not reached puberty and his dowry. He said: If he divorces for the sake of the Sunnah and places the dowry in its proper place and fulfills its right, there is no harm, and it is valid. This has been defined as ten years and above, according to what we have cited in our book, Al-Kabir.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married for mut'ah (temporary marriage) without witnesses. He said: There is no objection to the marriage absolutely without witnesses in what is between him and Allah, Exalted and Glorious. And the witnesses were made required in the marriage absolutely only for the sake of the child. And if it were not for that, there would be no objection to it.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is sufficient regarding witnesses for Mut'ah (temporary marriage)?' He said: 'One man and two women who witness it.' I said: 'What if they cannot find anyone?' He said: 'They will not be lacking [in validity].' I said: 'What if they fear that someone will learn of it? Is one man sufficient for them?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, were the Muslims during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) marrying without a clear proof/witness?' He said: 'No, and it does not contradict the first report, because the report does not prohibit the validity of Mut'ah marriage without a witness; rather, it implies that during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), they did not marry except with a witness, and that is the preferable option.' And just because that was not practiced in that era does not indicate that it is forbidden, just as we know that here there are many permissible things and others that were not used in that time, and that does not indicate their prohibition. And the report came in the place of precaution rather than obligation, so that the woman would not consider that to be indecency if she were not from those of knowledge. And that which reveals what we mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is permissible regarding witnesses in Mut'ah (temporary marriage)? He said: One man and two women. I said: If he dislikes [having] witnesses, he said: One man suffices for him, and that is due to the status of the woman, so that she does not say in herself, 'This is fornication.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Humaydi ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from al-'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The divorce of the terminally ill (patient of death) is not valid, but his marriage is valid.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The sick person may not divorce (his wife), but he may marry.

From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: For the sick person, it is permissible to divorce, and he may marry. If he marries and consummates the marriage, it is valid. But if he does not consummate it until he dies in his illness, his marriage is void, and she is not entitled to a dowry nor to inheritance.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi that he was asked about a man whose death approaches and he divorces his wife, is his divorce valid? He said: Yes, and if he dies she inherits him, and if she dies he does not inherit her. This does not contradict the earlier reports, because the way to reconcile them is to understand the earlier reports as meaning that he does not have the right to divorce her with a divorce that severs the inheritance between them. For divorce is of two types: revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in). In all cases, inheritance remains between them if it occurs during the illness, as long as she has not exited the waiting period ('iddah). Once she exits the waiting period, the wife inherits him for as long as there is between them and one year, provided she has not married. If she marries, her inheritance from him is cut off. And if she does not marry, she inherits him until one year. If the year passes completely, her inheritance from him is also nullified.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Rabi' al-Asamm, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' and Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu al-Ward, both of them from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man divorces his wife with a single divorce while in his illness, and then remains in that illness until her waiting period expires, she inherits him provided she has not married another. If she has married after the expiration of the waiting period, then she does not inherit him.

From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill, until a year passed for that reason. He said: She inherits him if he was in the illness in which he divorced her and did not recover from it.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sama'ani, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: A man divorced his wife while he was ill, with a single divorce, and he had previously divorced her twice. He said: She inherits him if he is in his illness. I asked: What is the definition of the illness? He said: He remains ill until he dies, even if that lasts for a year.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I heard him saying: Any woman who is divorced, then her husband dies before her waiting period (iddah) expires and she has not become fully divorced (haram) to him, then she inherits him and then observes the waiting period of the one who died for her (the deceased husband). And if she dies while in her waiting period and has not become fully divorced to him, then he inherits her. And if he is killed, she inherits from his blood money (diyah), and if she is killed, he inherits from her blood money, provided that one did not kill the other.

Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from Hammad from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorced his wife, then he died while she was in her waiting period: she inherits him and observes the waiting period of the deceased for her husband. And if she died while in her waiting period, he inherits her. And each of them inherits from the blood-money of the other, if one were killed, provided that one did not kill the other.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill. He said: She inherits him during his illness for the period between him and one year, if he dies in that illness. And she observes the waiting period of the divorced woman from the day he divorced her. Then she may marry if she wishes after her waiting period ends, and she inherits him between her and one year, if he dies in that illness. But if he dies after the year passes, she has no inheritance. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report contains from his saying 'then she may marry if she wishes after her waiting period ends, and she inherits him between her and one year' does not contradict what we have presented that when she marries, she does not inherit him, because most of what is in this report is the explicit permission for her to marry after the end of the waiting period. And his saying 'and she inherits him between her and one year' is a ruling specific to her if she does not marry, indicated by what we have presented from the reports that what I choose is that she only inherits him after the end of the waiting period if he divorced her for her detriment. And all the general reports that preceded are to be understood according to this distinction, indicating that.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill.
