He said: No. And that is because if a man accuses the boy, he is not flogged.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every mature person, whether male or female, who accuses a child or an adult, male or female, Muslim or non-Muslim, free or slave, upon him is the full penalty of accusation (hadd al-fariyah), and upon the non-mature person is the disciplinary penalty (hadd al-adab). As for what the beginning of this report included regarding the obligation of the full penalty upon one who accuses a child, it is to be understood as referring to one who accuses him of the lineage of adultery to one of his parents, by saying 'O son of the fornicator' or 'the fornicatress', or 'Your mother/father fornicated with you', because that obligates the full penalty upon him. As for if he accuses him with an accusation that does not extend to one of the two parents, then the full penalty is not obligatory upon him, but rather he is subject to disciplinary punishment (ta'zir). This is indicated by what we have previously mentioned from the earlier reports and what we have cited in the book Tahdhib al-Ahkam. As for what the report included regarding the obligation of the full penalty upon one who accuses a disbeliever, or a Jew, or a Christian, it is possible that the intended meaning is if his mother is Muslim, then the full penalty is obligatory upon one who accuses him due to the sanctity of the Muslim woman. If it is not so, then only disciplinary punishment is obligatory, according to what we have previously mentioned. It is also possible that the mention of 'hadd' (penalty) in the report refers to 'ta'zir' (disciplinary punishment) in both cases, even though the term 'hadd al-fariyah' is used for it, because that is also deserved by accusation, even if it is not a full hadd.

Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nu'fali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The wound (or blood money for a wound) is not inherited. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report should be understood to mean that it is not inherited in the same way property is inherited, such that each of them takes their share, even though each of the heirs has the right to claim the full amount in its entirety.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Ammar al-Sabati who said: I heard him say: The fixed punishment (al-hadd) is not inherited like the blood money (diyah) and wealth. However, whoever of the heirs stands by it and demands it, he is its guardian (wali). And whoever leaves it and does not demand it, he has no right to it. And that is like a man who slapped another man, and the slapped man has two brothers. If one of them pardons him, the other may demand his right, because it is their mother's right for both of them, and the pardon belongs to both of them.

Yunus from Hisham ibn Ibrahim al-Mashriqi, from one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would administer flogging for a small amount of nabidh (fermented drink) just as he would for a small amount of khamr (wine), and would execute for the third pouring of nabidh just as he would for the third pouring of khamr.

Yunus from Ibn Muskān from Sulaymān ibn Khālid said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would administer eighty (strikes) for intoxicating nabīdh, just as he would administer for wine, and he would execute in the third instance, just as he would execute the owner of wine.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when brought the drinker of wine, would strike him. If he was brought again, he would strike him. If he was brought a third time, he would strike his neck (kill him). I asked: What about Nabidh? He said: When the drinker of Nabidh is caught and has become slightly intoxicated (intashaa), he is struck eighty times. I asked: What if he is caught a second time? He said: Strike him. I asked: And if he is caught a third time? He said: He is killed just as the drinker of wine is killed. I asked: What if the drinker of Nabidh is caught and has not become fully intoxicated? Is he flogged? He said: No.

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'What do you think if the drinker of nabidh is caught and did not get drunk, will he be flogged with eighty [strikes]?' He said: 'No, and every intoxicant is forbidden.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about the one who drinks (wine), so he said: As for a man who had a slip (occasional drinking) from him, then I would excuse him; and as for another who makes it a habit, then I would severely punish him, because he considers all prohibitions permissible, and if people were left with that, they would become corrupt.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abi Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) would administer the beating (for drinking intoxicants) in the case of wine and nabidh: eighty for the free man, and the slave, and the Jew, and the Christian. I said: 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian?' He said: 'They do not have permission to make their drinking public; it happens in their houses.'

Yunus narrated from Sama'ah from Abu Basir who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would flog the free man and the slave, the Jew and the Christian, for wine and nabidh [fermented drink] eighty [strikes]. So I said, 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian and Jew?' He said, 'When they manifest that in a province among the provinces, because it is not for them to manifest its drinking.'

Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Muskān from Abū Baṣīr who said: The legal penalty (ḥadd) for the Jew, the Christian, and the slave regarding wine and drinking it is the same; and the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimmah) were settled upon the condition that they may drink it in their own houses.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the ta'zir (disciplinary punishment)?' He said, 'Less than the hadd (fixed punishment).' I said, 'Less than eighty?' He said, 'No, but it is less than forty, for that is the hadd of the slave.' I said, 'And how much is that?' He said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: According to what the ruler sees of the man's sin and the strength of his body. So the way to understand this report is to carry it on taqiyyah (dissimulation), for it is the view of some of the Sunnis.'

And as for what Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Saif ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave who slandered a free man. He said: 'He is flogged with eighty [lashes]. This is from the rights of the Muslims.' Then he said: 'As for what is from the rights of Allah (Exalted), then he is flogged with half the punishment.' I said: 'What is that which is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' He said: 'When he commits adultery and drinks wine, this is from the rights in which half the punishment is inflicted.' So the explanation for this report is also what we said in the first report, that it is to be understood as being based on Taqiyyah (dissimulation). And it is possible that the narrator heard that specifically regarding adultery, because it is from the rights of Allah (Exalted), and the punishment for the drinker was also from the rights of Allah, so he assumed it followed the same pattern, and that is not correct according to what we have indicated with the preceding reports.

And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala, from Aban, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father used to say: The punishment of the slave is half the punishment of the free person. This report is general, and it is permissible for us to specify it regarding the punishment of adultery, based on the indication of the earlier reports.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding in what amount the thief's hand is cut off, so he said: 'In a quarter of a dinar.' I said to him, 'In two dirhams?' He said, 'In a quarter of a dinar, regardless of what value the dinar reaches.' I said to him, 'Do you see one who steals less than a quarter of a dinar? Does the name 'thief' apply to him, and is he considered a thief with Allah in that state?' He said: 'Whoever steals anything from a Muslim that has been secured and protected, the name 'thief' applies to him and he is a thief with Allah, but the hand is not cut off except in a quarter of a dinar or more.' And if the hand of the thief were cut off for what is less than a quarter of a dinar, you would find most people with their hands cut off.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The hand of the thief is not cut off until his theft reaches one-quarter of a dinar, and Ali (peace be upon him) had cut [the hand] for an egg of iron. Ali (peace be upon him) said, and Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the minimum amount in which the thief's hand is cut, so he said: For an egg of iron. I said: And what is its price? He said: One-quarter of a dinar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave the penalty of cutting (the hand) for an egg. I said: 'What is the egg?' He said: 'An egg worth a quarter of a dinar.' I said: 'That is the minimum threshold for the thief,' and he remained silent.

Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The thief's hand is not cut off except for something whose value reaches a mijann, and that is one-quarter of a dinar.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Salamah from Abu Abdillah from his father that the Commander of the Faithful used to cut the hand of the thief for a quarter of a dinar.

From him, from al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the minimum amount in which the thief's hand is cut off. He said: 'In the egg of iron.' I said: 'And what is its price?' He said: 'One-quarter of a dinar.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The thief is not cut off until his theft reaches one-quarter of a dinar.' And indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) cut off [the hand] for the egg of iron.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Hamzah said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about in what amount the thief's hand is cut off. He gathered his two palms and then said: 'In the number of them [the dirhams].' This does not contradict the earlier narrations, which state that the minimum amount in which the thief's hand is cut off is one-quarter of a dinar, for two reasons: One is that it is not impossible that the value of the dirhams he indicated was one-quarter of a dinar, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) clarified this in the narration of Muhammad ibn Muslim, which we mentioned at the beginning of the chapter, when he was asked about one who stole two dirhams, and he said: 'In one-quarter of a dinar, whatever the value of the dinar has reached.' The other reason is that we may attribute it to taqiyya (dissimulation), because it is the view of some of the Sunnis.
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about at what amount the thief's hand is cut off. He said: The minimum is one-third of a dinar.

Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) cut off a man's hand for theft of a 'baydah'. I asked: 'Which baydah?' He said: 'A baydah of iron, valued at one-third of a dinar.' I said: 'This is the lowest threshold for the thief's hand-cutting.' He remained silent.

Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The thief's hand is not cut off except for something whose value reaches a *mijan*, and that is one-quarter of a dinar.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil from 'Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad ibn Humran, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The minimum amount in which the thief's hand is cut off is five dinars.
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Fadalah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), like it.

From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The thief's hand is cut off for anything that reaches the value of one-fifth of a dinar. And if he stole from crops or fruit or other than that, the way to resolve this is to carry these narrations on the basis of precaution (taqiyyah), because they agree with the views of many of them.

Yunus narrated from Muhammad ibn Humran from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The minimum amount in which the hand of the thief is cut off is five dinars, and the five dinars is the final limit beyond which cutting does not occur. Therefore, the approach in these narrations is to interpret them as a form of taqiyya (dissimulation), because among the general public (Ahl al-Sunnah) there are those who go to that opinion, and the Righteous Sect (al-Ta'ifa al-Muhiqqa) has agreed to act upon what the first narrations contained.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who took an egg from the war booty. They said, 'He has stolen, cut off his hand.' He said, 'I have not cut off anyone's hand for what he took, as long as he had a share in it.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam from Mis'ma ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he (peace be upon him) A man was brought who had stolen from the state treasury (bayt al-mal), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not amputated, for he has a share in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Four [categories of people] are not subject to the amputation penalty: the sneaky thief, the one who commits ghulul, whoever steals from the war booty, and the servant's theft, because it is treachery.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the egg that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) cut in it. He said: It was an egg of iron that a man stole from the war booty, so he cut it. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as he cut the one who stole from the booty and had no share in it. Indeed, one in this state is subject to the cutting of the hand. On the condition that the cutting is waived from him if he stole an amount equal to his share or slightly less than what requires cutting. As for what exceeded his share by the amount that requires cutting, cutting is obligatory upon him in all cases, as indicated by that.

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man who stole from the war booty items for which cutting (of the hand) is obligatory. He said: It is looked at to see how much he takes. If what he took is less than his share, he is flogged and his full property is returned to him. And if he took equal to what is his, there is nothing upon him. And if he took an excess equal to the value of a 'mijan' (a small leather bag or pouch), which is a quarter of a dinar, he is cut.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is left-handed or right-handed who stole, he said: His right hand is cut off in all cases.

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from one of his companions who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: If a man steals and his left hand is crippled (shala'), his right hand is not cut off, nor is his leg cut off, even if he is one-handed (ashal). Then, if he cuts the hand of another man, retribution (qisas) is taken from him, meaning his hand is not cut off for theft, but it is cut off for retribution. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it to mean that when the Imam sees from him, based on the evidence of the situation, the permissibility of pardoning him, if his left hand is crippled, it is permissible for him (to leave the right hand), so that he does not remain without a hand. And if it is not so, then cutting his right hand is obligatory upon him, according to what the first report contained and that which indicates this.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'If a man's left hand was cut off in retribution (qisas) and then he stole [the amount that requires cutting], what is done?' He said, 'He is not cut, nor is he left without a leg.' I said, 'And if a man's right hand was cut off in retribution and then he cut off a man's hand, is retribution taken from him or not?' He said, 'Only [the hand] is left in the right of Allah (Exalted and Majestic). But regarding the rights of people, retribution is taken from him in all four [limbs].'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Baraqi, from al-Nuflī, from al-Sakkūnī, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The hand is not cut off except for one who broke into a house or broke a lock.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who went to another man and said: 'So-and-so sent me to you to send such and such [amount/goods] to him.' The man gave it to him and believed him. Later, the sender met the recipient and said to him: 'Your messenger came to me, so I sent with him such and such.' The recipient said: 'I did not send him, and he did not bring me anything.' The messenger claimed that he had been sent and had delivered it to him. The recipient said: 'If evidence is found against him that he was not sent, his hand will be cut off. If no evidence is found, he will take an oath by Allah that he did not send him, and the other party will recover the money from the messenger.' I asked: 'What if he claims that need compelled him to do so?' He said: 'His hand will be cut off, because he stole a man's property.' The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as referring to one who is known for this, by scheming against the wealth of Muslims; it is permissible for the Imam to cut off his hand, because he is a corrupter in the land, not because he is a thief, because this is a stratagem (hi'lah) and not a theft that requires cutting off [the hand].

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a thief who had stolen dirhams from the sleeve of a man's garment. He said: 'If it was from his outer shirt, I would not cut his hand, but if it was from his inner shirt, I would cut his hand.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from a number of our companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no cutting (of the hand) for the one who steals a cloak, and there is no cutting for the one who steals dirhams from the man's garment.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Isa ibn Sabih said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the thief who steals from the top (of a garment), the thief who steals from the bottom, and the pickpocket. He said: 'They are not amputated.' The way to reconcile these two reports is to apply the distinction contained in the first two reports: that if the thief from the top takes from the upper part of the shirt, there is no amputation upon him; and if he takes from the lower part, amputation is obligatory upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The punishment for the grave-digger (who steals from a grave) is the same as the punishment for the thief.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Habib ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from 'Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The thief of the dead (grave robber) is amputated just as the thief of the living is amputated.

From him, from Habib ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Bashshar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A nabbash (grave digger/excavator) was captured in the time of Mu'awiya, so he said to his companions, 'What do you think?' They said, 'We will punish him and release him.' A man from the people said, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib did not do so.' He asked, 'What did he do?' He said, 'He would cut off the nabbash and said, 'He is a thief and one who uncovers the dead.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ja'fi, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and a letter came to him from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik regarding a man who dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and married her. The people had differed regarding us here: one group said, 'Kill him,' and another group said, 'Burn him.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'The sanctity of the dead is like the sanctity of the living. His punishment is that his hand be cut off for digging her up and stripping her of her clothes, and the punishment for fornication is established against him; if he were married, he would be stoned, and if he were not married, he would be flogged one hundred times.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Mahbub from 'Isa ibn Sabih said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the thief who digs, the thief who climbs, and the thief who steals secretly, so he said: The thief who digs and the thief who climb are cut (hand), but the thief who steals secretly is not cut.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Rahman al-Arzmī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Ali (peace be upon him) cut off the thief (of buried treasure).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn Saeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the nabbash (grave digger/excavator). He said: If grave-digging is not a customary practice for him, he is not amputated (of the hand) but is given ta'zir (discretionary punishment).

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The nabbash (grave digger/excavator), if he is known for that (digging up graves), his hand is cut off.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm from Ibn Bukayr from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the grave digger (nabbash): if he is taken the first time, he is flogged (ta'zir); if he returns, he is executed. These final narrations all indicate that the grave digger is only executed if that (repeated digging) is his habit/custom. As for if it is not his habit, he is examined: if he dug and took the shroud, execution is obligatory upon him; and if he did not take it, there is not upon him more than flogging. And upon this we base the narrations that we presented earlier and those that indicate that.

Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Fadala, from Musa, from Ali ibn Sa'id, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who was caught while digging (for treasure). He said: I do not see cutting (the hand) upon him, unless he is caught and has dug multiple times, then I cut him.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isa ibn Sabih, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the thief who steals from the top of a wall (al-tarrar), the thief who digs into a wall (al-nabbash), and the thief who steals secretly (al-mukhtalis). He said: 'They are not amputated (hand).' So we assume that something may have been omitted from the report, because we have narrated this exact report from Isa ibn Sabih in what preceded, in the narration of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Mahbub from him, who said: 'I asked him about these three, and he said: The tarrar and the nabbash are amputated, and the mukhtalis is not amputated.' And even if this detail had not come down, we would have based it on what we based the last two reports on.

Ali ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a man who was a thief (nabbash). The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) took him by his hair and struck his head against the ground. Then he ordered the people, and they trampled him until he died.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a thief (nabbash), so he delayed his punishment until Friday. When Friday came, he placed him under the feet of the people, and they continued to trample him with their feet until he died. The resolution in these two narrations is to interpret them as meaning: when the action is repeated by them three times and the limits (hudud) are established against them, then killing becomes obligatory upon them, just as it is obligatory for the thief. The Imam is free to choose the method of killing as he wishes, according to what he deems most effective in the situation.

Aban narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the young boy steals and has not reached puberty, the tips of his fingers are cut. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was the only one who did this, and I [also did it].

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: If the young boy steals and has not yet reached puberty, his fingers are cut. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a boy who had stolen but had not yet reached puberty, so he cut the flesh from the tips of his fingers, then he said: If you return (to stealing), I will cut your hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A young man was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) in whom there was doubt regarding whether he had reached puberty (via wet dream), so he cut off the tips of his fingers.

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from some of his companions, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the young boy who steals, and he said: If he is nine years old, his hand is cut off, and the penalty of God is not neglected.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hafsh al-Marwazi, from the man (peace be upon him) who said: When the boy completes eight years, his affairs are valid, and the fixed shares (of inheritance) and the fixed punishments have become obligatory upon him. And when the girl completes nine years, it is the same. The way to reconcile these two reports is to assume that if the action is repeated by them in multiple instances, the cutting (of the hand) is obligatory upon them, just as it is upon the man in the first instance. And the cutting is not obligatory upon them in the first instance, according to what the earlier reports contained, and that which indicates this distinction.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the child who steals. He said: If he is seven years old or less, he is excused (handed over/not punished). If he returns (steals again) after seven, his fingers are cut or scraped until they bleed. If he returns, the part below his fingers is cut. If he returns after that and has reached nine years old, his hand is cut. And the limit of Allah is not neglected. It is possible that the two reports are carried upon one who knows the obligation of cutting upon him from the children in theft, even if he has not yet reached puberty, for if it is so, it is permissible for the Imam to cut his hand.

Humayd ibn Ziyad narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Nahyakī, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Qasari, who said: I was in al-Madina when a boy who had stolen was brought to me. I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Ask him where he stole; did he know that there was a punishment for theft?' If he said 'Yes,' I said, 'What is that punishment?' If he did not know that the punishment for theft was cutting (the hand), then let him go free.' He said: 'So I took the boy and asked him, and I said to him, 'Did you know that there is a punishment for theft?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'What is it?' He said, 'I am struck (with the cane).' So I let him go free.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from some of our companions from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: The thief is not amputated until he confesses to the theft twice; if he returns [to confessing], he guarantees the theft, and he is not amputated if there are no witnesses. And he said: The fornicator is not stoned until he confesses four times; if there are no witnesses, and if he returns [to confessing], he is left alone and is not stoned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a free person confesses to theft once before the Imam, the hand is cut off. The approach in this narration is to interpret it as being based on taqiyyah (dissimulation), because it agrees with the view of some of the Sunnis. As for the narrations we cited in the book *Tahdib al-Ahkam* stating that when the thief confesses, the hand is cut off, they are general (mujmal) and do not specify whether he confessed in one instance or two. It is appropriate to interpret them according to the specification contained in the first report, which adds clarity to this.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I was with Isa ibn Musa when a thief was brought to him, and a man from the family of Umar was present. The man turned to me and asked, so I said: 'What do you say about the thief if he confesses to himself that he stole?' He said: 'His hand is cut off.' I said: 'And what do you say about the fornicator if he confesses to himself four times?' He said: 'We stone him.' I said: 'What prevents you from cutting off the hand of the thief if he confesses to himself twice, so that he is in the same status as the fornicator?'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever catches a thief and pardons him, that is for him; but if it is referred to the Imam, he will cut (his hand). If the one from whom it was stolen says, 'I forgive/pardon him,' the Imam will not leave him until he cuts (his hand) when it is referred to him. And the pardon/forgiveness is only before it is referred to the Imam. And those who guard the limits of Allah So when it reaches the Imam, no one has the right to leave it (unexecuted).

Ali (peace be upon him) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who takes the thief, whether he should present him to the Imam or leave him. He said: Indeed, Safwan ibn Umayya was lying in the Sacred Mosque, so he placed his cloak and went out to pour water. When he returned, he found his cloak had been stolen. He said: 'Whoever took my cloak?' and went looking for it, so he caught the thief and presented him to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Cut his hand.' Safwan said: 'You will cut his hand for the sake of my cloak, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then I forgive him for it.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Why did you not do this before you presented him to me?' I said: 'So the Imam is in the same position as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when presented to him?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And I asked him about forgiveness before it reaches the Imam?' He said: 'It is good.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man: if the thief's hand is taken, is it better to leave it or raise it (amputate it)? He said: Indeed, Safwan ibn Umayyah was reclining in the mosque on his cloak, then he stood up to urinate. He returned and his hand had been taken. He sought his companion and found him, and brought him to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: 'Cut his hand.' Safwan said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I forgive that to him.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Why was that not done before he was brought to me?' And I asked him about forgiveness regarding the fixed punishments before they are brought to the Imam, and he said: 'It is good.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from some of his companions, from some of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and confessed to theft. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) asked him: 'Do you recite anything from the Book of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, Surah Al-Baqarah.' He said: 'I have granted you pardon for your hand on account of Surah Al-Baqarah.' Al-Ash'ath said: 'Do you nullify a punishment (hadd) of Allah the Exalted?' He said: 'And what do you know about this? When the evidence is established, it is not for the Imam to pardon; but when the man confesses to himself, that is up to the Imam: if he wishes, he pardons, and if he wishes, he cuts.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, and he said: 'Whoever shows preference for Islam and disbelieves in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, there is no repentance for him, his execution becomes obligatory, his wife is separated from him, and his estate is divided among his children.'

From him and Ahmad together, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Every Muslim, among Muslims, who apostatizes from Islam and denies Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) prophethood and rejects it, then his blood is permissible for anyone who hears that from him, and his wife is separated from him on the day he apostatizes, so do not approach her, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him and not ask him for repentance.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That a man from the Muslims converted to Christianity, and he was brought before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). He invited him to repent (to return to Islam), but he refused. He grabbed his hair, then said: 'Tread on the slaves of Allah,' so he was trodden upon until he died.

Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from more than one of our companions from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding The apostate is asked to repent; if he repents, he is spared, otherwise he is killed. And the woman, if she apostatizes, is asked to repent; if she repents and returns, she is spared, otherwise she is confined to prison and hardship is imposed upon her in her detention.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj and others from one of the Imams (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who reverted from Islam, it was said: He is asked to repent; if he repents, well and good, otherwise he is killed. It was said to Jamil: What do you say if he repents and then reverted from Islam again? He said: He is asked to repent. It was said: What do you say if he repented, then reverted, then repented, then reverted? He said: I have not heard anything specific about this, but in my view, he is like the adulterer upon whom the hadd punishment is carried out twice, and then he is killed thereafter.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman from Mis'a ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The apostate's wife is separated from him, and his slaughtered meat is not eaten, and he is asked to repent for three days; if he repents, [he lives], otherwise he is killed on the fourth day.

Al-Husayn ibn Said said: I read a letter from a man to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'A man was born upon Islam, then he disbelieved, associated partners [with God], and exited from Islam. Is he repelled [to be repented] or is he killed and not repelled?' He wrote: 'He is killed.' As for the woman when she apostatizes, she is not killed in any case, but she is confined to prison indefinitely if she does not return to Islam. And this was included in the narration of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from more than one [narrator] from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and it adds clarification to that.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub (peace be upon him) from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far (peace be upon him) from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: When the woman apostatizes from Islam, she is not killed, but she is imprisoned forever.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three are kept imprisoned permanently: the one who is detained after death (to pay his debt), the woman who apostatizes from Islam, and the thief after the cutting of his hand and foot.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The apostate is asked to repent; if he repents, [he is spared], and if not, he is killed. He said: And the woman is asked to repent; if she repents, [she is spared], and if not, she is imprisoned in prison and confined.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a female slave who was a Christian, then she embraced Islam and bore a child for her master. Then her master died and bequeathed her freedom as a concubine during the time of 'Umar. She married a Christian named Dayrani and reverted to Christianity, then she bore two children and became pregnant with a third. He said: So he ruled that Islam should be presented to her. It was presented to her, but she refused. He said: Whatever child she bore while Christian, they are slaves to the brother whom she bore to her first master. And I will detain her until she gives birth to the child in her womb. When she gives birth, I will kill her. This does not contradict the earlier reports, because in this report, her execution was mandated because she apostatized from Islam and married a disbeliever. For this reason, the execution became obligatory upon her. And if she had not married, her ruling would be to be detained indefinitely, according to what the earlier reports contained.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from 'Ubayd Allah al-Mad'ani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: 'May I be your ransom, inform me about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:' Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [with] corruption is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the earth. He said: He tied with his hand [indicating four categories], then said: 'O Abu Abdillah, take them four by four.' Then he said: 'If he waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the earth with corruption, and killed [one person], he is killed.' And if he killed and took the wealth, he is killed and crucified. And if he took the wealth and did not kill, his hand and foot are cut off from opposite sides. If he waged war against Allah and His Messenger and strove in the earth with corruption and did not kill and did not take the wealth, he is exiled from the earth. I said: 'And what is the limit of his exile?' He said: 'One year. He is exiled from the land in which he acted to another land.' Then a letter is sent to that city stating that he is exiled, so do not eat with him, drink with him, or marry him until he departs to another. And a letter is sent to them also with the like of that, so this remains his state for one year. When that is done to him, he repents while he is humble.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'The penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [with] corruption is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be exchanged or that they be exiled from the land,' [to the end of the verse]. I said: Which of these penalties specified by Allah are upon them? He said: That is up to the Imam; if he wills, he will behead, if he wills, he will crucify, if he wills, he will exile, if he wills, he will kill. I said: Exile to where? He said: He is exiled from one province to another province. And he said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) exiled two men from Kufa to Basra. So the explanation in this report is one of two things: One is that we carry it on taqiyya (dissimulation), because among the general public (Sunni scholars) is one who says that the Imam is free to choose among these penalties, and does not restrict them to what the first narration and the reports we mentioned in our Great Book contained.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami from Ali ibn Asbat from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid from Abu Ubaydah ibn Bashir al-Kha'thami said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the road-cutter (qati' al-tariq), and I said, 'The people say that the Imam has discretion in his case; he may do whatever he wishes.' He said, 'Not whatever he wishes, but he acts according to their crimes.' He then specified: 'Whoever cuts the road, kills, and takes wealth, his hand and foot are cut off and he is crucified. Whoever cuts the road, kills, but does not take wealth, he is killed. Whoever cuts the road, does not take wealth, and does not kill, he is exiled from the land. The other view is that we say he has discretion if he fights, brandishes weapons, strikes, and takes wealth, even if he does not kill; in that case, his affair is referred to the Imam. This indicates this distinction.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Whoever draws his weapon in a garrison city (misr) and kills, he is executed (qisas) and exiled from that city. And whoever draws his weapon in non-garrison cities, strikes, kills, takes wealth, but does not kill, he is a muharib (warrior), and his penalty is the penalty of the muharib. And his affair is referred to the Imam; if he wishes, he kills him; if he wishes, he crucifies him; if he wishes, he cuts his hand and foot. He said: And if he strikes, kills, and takes wealth, it is upon the Imam to cut his right hand for theft, then hand him over to the heirs of the slain, who pursue him with the wealth, then kill him. Abu Ubaydah said to him: May God improve you, tell me, if the heirs of the slain forgive him? Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: If they forgive him, it is still upon the Imam to kill him, because he has fought God and His Messenger, killed, and stolen. Then Abu Ubaydah said to him: Tell me, if the heirs of the slain wish to take the blood money (diyah) from him and let him go, is that for them? He said: No, killing is upon him (i.e., he must be killed).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abi Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The blood money for accidental killing, if the man did not intend death, is one hundred camels, or ten thousand dirhams of silver, or one thousand sheep. And he said: The aggravated blood money, which resembles intentional killing but is not intentional, is superior to the accidental blood money by the teeth of the camels: thirty-three he-camels (hiqq), thirty-three young male camels (jadha'), and thirty-four two-year-old camels (thaniyya), all of which are of the breed of the male camel. And I asked him about the blood money, so he said: The blood money of a Muslim is ten thousand dirhams of silver, or one thousand mithqals of gold, or one thousand sheep. Regarding the teeth of the camels: three hundred camels. Regarding the teeth of the cattle: two hundred cattle. Ali from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: In accidental killing, it is one hundred camels, or one thousand sheep, or ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars. If it is camels, then twenty-five bint makhad (one-year-old female camels), twenty-five bint labun (two-year-old female camels), twenty-five hiqq (three-year-old female camels), and twenty-five jadha' (four-year-old male camels). And the aggravated blood money in accidental killing, which resembles intentional killing, is when one strikes with a stone or a staff with one or two strikes, not intending death, then it is thirty-three hiqq, thirty-three jadha', and thirty-four khalfa (young male camels), all of the breed of the male camel. And if it is sheep, then one thousand rams. And intentional killing is qawd (retribution) or rida' (blood money paid by the guardian of the slain). Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I heard Ibn Abi Layla saying: Abd al-Rahman said: I asked Abu Abdillah about what Ibn Abi Layla narrated, so he said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: The blood money is one thousand dinars, and the value of the dinars is ten thousand dirhams. And for the people of gold, it is one thousand dinars, and for the people of silver, it is ten thousand dirhams. For the people of cities (al-amisar) and the people of the desert (al-bawadi), the blood money is o

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Abdillah ibn Sinan ibn Sinan, and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Abdillahan ibn Al-Mughirah, and Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, all together from Ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding accidental killing that is similar to intentional killing, when one kills with a whip or a stick or a stone, the blood money for that is aggravated, and it is one hundred camels: forty of them are Khalifah (camels in their fifth year) between Thaniyyah (fourth year) and Bazl (sixth year) in their year, and thirty are Hiqqah (three-year-old female camel), and thirty are Bint Labun (two-year-old female camel). And for simple error, there are thirty Hiqqah, and thirty Bint Labun, and twenty Bint Makhad (one-year-old female camel), and twenty Ibn Labun (male one-year-old camel). And the value of each camel from silver is one hundred and twenty dirhams, or ten dinars. And from sheep, the value of each Nab (young camel) from camels is twenty sheep.

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the blood money for intentional killing, so he said: One hundred from the mature camels (masan), and if there are no camels, then in place of each camel, twenty from the mature sheep. As for what this narration includes regarding the difference in the ages of camels in cases of accidental and semi-intentional killing, and what the earlier narrations include, the way to understand it is that we interpret it as meaning the Imam has the discretion to act with whichever he chooses, according to what he sees in the situation as being more beneficial. And as for what it includes that if there are no camels, then in place of each camel there are twenty sheep, this bears two meanings: One is that the blood money of camels is only incumbent upon the people of the desert (Bawadi), so whoever from them refuses to give the camels, it is permissible to take from them in place of each camel twenty sheep at their valuation. And the other meaning is that we interpret it as applying to a slave who killed a free person, for that is incumbent upon him if his guardians wish to pay the blood money on his behalf.

Abu Jamilyah from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the slave who kills a free man intentionally. He said: One hundred of the mature camels (masann). If there are no camels, then for the place of each camel, twenty of the male sheep. As for the dirhams, ten thousand dirhams. And the earlier narrations point to that, and it is also confirmed by that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Whoever kills a believer intentionally is subject to retaliation (qisas), unless the heirs of the slain agree to accept the blood money (diyah) or agree to a sum greater or lesser than the standard blood money. If they do so among themselves, it is valid; if they do not agree, retaliation is executed. And he said: The blood money is ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars, or one hundred camels. As for what the preceding narrations contained regarding that one hundred and twenty dirhams are extracted from each camel.

And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, and 'Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, and Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, all from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever kills a believer intentionally is subject to retaliation (qisas), unless the heirs of the slain agree to accept the blood money (diyah). If they accept the blood money and the killer prefers that, then the blood money is twelve thousand (dirhams) or one thousand dinars.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad and al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The blood-money (diyah) is one thousand dinars, or twelve thousand dirhams, or one hundred camels. The basis in these two narrations is what he mentioned.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa together narrated that our companions reported: That [amount] is the weight of six [mithqals of gold], and if it is so, it returns to ten thousand dirhams. And it is possible that these reports came down due to taqiyyah (dissimulation), because that is the belief of the general public (Sunni scholars).

First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The 'Aqilah does not guarantee intentional killing, nor confession, nor settlement. Second: Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The 'Aqilah does not guarantee intentional killing, nor confession, nor settlement. Third: As for what Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Maythami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed another man intentionally, then the killer fled and could not be caught. He said: If he has wealth, the blood money is taken from his wealth; otherwise, it is taken from the nearest [male relative] then the nearest, for the blood of a Muslim man is not nullified. Fourth: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a man who killed another intentionally then fled and could not be caught until he died. He said: If he has wealth, it is taken from him; otherwise, it is taken from the nearest then the nearest. The meaning in these two narrations is that we interpret them as referring to the situation they encompass, which is the situation where the killer cannot be caught, either due to his flight or his death. Then the blood money is taken from his 'Aqilah. This obligation does not fall upon them while the killer is present/alive, and that which confirms what we said... Fifth: What Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Al-Jawza', from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Uwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The 'Aqilah does not guarantee except that upon which proof is established. He said: A man came to him and confessed in his presence, so he made it specific to his own wealth, and did not impose anything upon the 'Aqilah.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Women do not have the right of pardon (afw) nor the right of retribution (qawd). As for what Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Fudayl, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who pardoned a share-holder that his pardon is valid. And he ruled regarding four brothers, one of whom pardoned, saying: The remainder pays the blood money (diyah), and the one who pardoned is exempted by his share. And what Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding two men who killed a man intentionally, and he had two heirs, and one of the heirs pardoned: He said, When some of the heirs pardon him, the killing (retribution) is removed from him, and from the two (heirs) the blood money is reduced by the share of the one who pardoned, and they pay the remainder from their wealth to the one who did not pardon. And he said: The pardon of every share-holder is valid. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who killed two men intentionally, and they had heirs, and the heirs of one pardoned and the other refused. He said: He kills those who did not pardon, and if they wish to take the blood money, they take it. Abd al-Rahman said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): And two men killed a man intentionally, and he had two heirs, and one of the heirs pardoned. He said: When some of the heirs pardon him, the killing is removed from them, and from the two the blood money is reduced by the share of the one who pardoned, and they pay the remainder from their wealth to those who did not pardon. So there is no contradiction between these narrations and the first report from two aspects: One is that it is permissible for us to specify these narrations by saying: The pardon of whoever has a share in the blood money is valid, except if he is a woman, for she does not have valid pardon nor retribution. And the second is that these narrations only encompassed the

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who kills a woman intentionally: If the woman's family wishes to kill him, he tells them: Do so, provided they pay to his family half the blood money. And if they accept the blood money, then they receive half the blood money. Second: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a man kills a woman, and they want qisas (retaliation), they pay the difference in the man's blood money and retaliate with it. And if they do not do so, they accept the blood money as a complete payment, and the woman's blood money is half that of the man's. Third: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say regarding a man who intentionally kills his wife: If her family wishes to kill him, they pay to him half the blood money. And if they wish, they take half the blood money, which is five thousand dirhams. Fourth: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said: I asked: A man kills a woman? He said: If the woman's family wishes to kill him, they pay half his blood money and kill him. Otherwise, they accept the blood money. Fifth: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who intentionally kills a woman: He said: If her family wishes to kill him, they kill him and pay to him half the blood money. Sixth: As for what al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that a man killed a woman and Ali (peace be upon him) did not establish qisas between them but obligated the blood money: This does not contradict the earlier reports for two reasons: First, it is permissible that he did not establish qisas between them because the killing was not intentional, which requires qisas. Second, he did not establish qisas between them, so there is no need to return the difference in blood money, because the earlier reports included that there is qisas between them on the condition that they return the difference of her blood money to the man's guardians. S

First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The blood money (diyah) of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian is eight hundred dirhams. Second: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Ibrahim claims that the blood money of the Christian, the Jew, and the Magian is equal. He said: Yes, he speaks the truth. Third: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub and Ibn Bukayr, from Layth al-Muradi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the blood money of the Christian, the Jew, and the Magian. He said: Their blood money is all equal, eight hundred dirhams, eight hundred dirhams. Fourth: Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to Bahrain, and he found the blood money of a people from the Jews, Christians, and Magians there. He wrote to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: I found the blood money of a people from the Jews and Christians, and their compensation is eight hundred, eight hundred. And I found the blood money of the Magians, and you had not appointed for me regarding them. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to him saying: Their blood money is like the blood money of the Jews and Christians, and he said: Indeed, they are the People of the Book. Fifth: Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Durust, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the blood money of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian. He said: They are equal, eight hundred dirhams, eight hundred dirhams. Sixth: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is the blood money of the Dhimmi? He said: Eight hundred dirhams. Seventh: Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Layth al-Muradi and Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The blood money of the Christian and the Jew is eight hundred dirhams. As for what Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated from Ibn al-Mughira, from Mansur, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The blood money of the Christia

And Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The blood money (diyah) of the Jew and the Christian is four thousand dirhams, and the blood money of the Magian is eight hundred dirhams. And he also said: Indeed, the Magian has a book called 'Jamas'. So there is no contradiction between these narrations and the earlier ones, because the way to reconcile them is to apply them to one who is accustomed to killing the people of the covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma). If that is the case, then the Imam may obligate him the complete blood money of a Muslim on one occasion, and four thousand dirhams on another, according to what he deems most appropriate for the situation and most restraining. As for one for whom this is rare, there is no more than eight hundred dirhams upon him, according to what the earlier narrations contained, and that which indicates what we have said.

Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Samaan said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim who killed a dhimmi (non-Muslim subject). He said: 'This is a severe matter that people cannot bear. He should give their family the blood money of a Muslim, until he is deterred from killing the people of the land (non-Muslims generally) and from killing the dhimmi.' Then he said: 'If a Muslim became angry at a dhimmi and wanted to kill him and take his land, and paid their family eight hundred dirhams, then killing among the dhimmis would increase.' And whoever kills a dhimmi unjustly, it is forbidden for the Muslim to kill a dhimmi as a retribution (qisas), as long as they paid the jizya and did not deny it. As for the specific narration of Abu Basir, we have narrated from him that their blood money is eight hundred, like the other reports. And what his report contained regarding the distinction between the Jews, Christians, and Magians, he also narrated that there is no distinction between them and that they are equal in blood money. And we have presented that from him and from others, which adds to the clarification.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked him about the Magians, what is their boundary (status)? He said: They are from the People of the Book, and their legal ruling is like that of the Jews and Christians regarding the fixed punishments and blood money.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The free person is not killed for the slave; if the free person kills the slave, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating. Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The free person is not killed for the slave, even if he kills him intentionally; rather, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating if he kills him intentionally. And he said: the blood money of the slave is his price. Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The slave is killed for the free person, but the free person is not killed for the slave; rather, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating until he recovers. Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said: The saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'Retaliation is prescribed for you in the case of murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.' He said: The free person is not killed for the slave, but he receives a severe beating and is liable for his price, the blood money of the slave. Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The free person is not killed for the slave; and if the free person kills the slave, he is liable for his price and receives a severe beating. And whoever kills him by retaliation or by the fixed punishment, he has no blood money. Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no retaliation between the free person and the slave. Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he killed a free person for a slave who killed him intentionally, the meaning in this narration is that we interpret it as referring to one who is accustomed to killing slaves, because for such a person it is permissible for the Imam to kill him by it, so that others may be deterred from doing the like. As

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him, who said: If the mother of the child (umm al-walad) kills her master by mistake, she is freed and there is no blood money (diyah) upon her. And Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Ja'far, from his father, that he used to say: If the umm al-walad kills her master by mistake, she is freed and there is no penalty upon her; and if she kills him intentionally, she is executed for it. As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far, from his father, who said: If the umm al-walad kills her master by mistake, she pays the value (of her freedom) from herself; this does not contradict the first two narrations. Because the meaning in the first two narrations is that we interpret them as applying when her child is still alive; for if her master dies, she is freed from her child's share. The other narration is interpreted as applying to one who has no child; she is freed from his share, so the heirs should pay her off if they wish, and if they wish to sell her, they have that right.

1- Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who is found dead in a village or between two villages, so he said: The distance between them is measured, and whichever is closer, its people are liable (for the blood money). 2- Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it. 3- Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man killed in a village or near a village that the people of that village are liable (for blood money) if no evidence is produced against the people of that village that they killed him. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in these narrations is that the people of the village or tribe are only liable if the dead man is found among them, provided they are suspected of killing him and refuse to take the oath, as we have explained in our Great Book. As for if they are not suspected of killing him or if they respond to the oath, then there is no blood money upon them, and his blood money is paid from the treasury (Bayt al-Mal), and that which indicates this. 4- What Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad and al-Abbas and al-Haytham all from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man is found killed in the tribe of a people, they are all sworn an oath that they did not kill him and do not know his killer. If they refuse, they pay the blood money among themselves from their wealth, equally among all the tribe from the adult men. 5- From him (Muhammad ibn Qays) from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Ziyad from Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: My father (peace be upon him) was... If the people do not produce evidence for killing their dead man and do not swear that the suspects killed him, he swears the suspects fifty oaths by God that they did not kill him and did not know his killer. Then the blood money is paid to the heirs of the dead man, and that is if he was killed in one tribe. As for if he was killed in a camp or a market or a city, his blood money is paid to his heirs from the treasury.

First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whichever man is killed by the fixed punishment (hadd) or by retribution (qisas), he has no blood money (diyah) due to him. Second: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who was killed by retribution (qisas), does he have a blood money? He said: If that were the case, retribution would not be taken from anyone. And whoever is killed by the fixed punishment (hadd), he has no blood money. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These two reports came in the same year, and it is appropriate that we specify them by saying: If he is killed by a fixed punishment of God, he has no blood money from the treasury (bayt al-mal), and if he dies from something of the human fixed punishments, his blood money is upon the treasury. This indicates it. Third: What al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Hasan ibn Salih al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever we strike with a fixed punishment of God and he dies, there is no blood money for us [to pay], and whoever we strike with a fixed punishment in something of the rights of people and he dies, then his blood money is upon us.

First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Salih ibn Sa'id, from Yunus, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who was angry with his wife, or a woman who was angry with her husband, and one of them killed the other. He said: There is no qisas (retaliation) upon them if they are considered trustworthy (not intending death). If they are suspected, it is incumbent upon them to swear an oath to God that they did not intend killing. Second: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammam, from al-Halabi, and Hisham, and al-Nadr, and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Mukkan, all from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who was angry with a woman and claimed she died from his anger, he said: The diya (blood money) is complete and the man is not killed, so it does not contradict the first report, because we interpret the first report as meaning that only qisas was negated for them, but diya was not negated. The suspicion is removed by each of them swearing that he did not intend to kill his partner, then the diya becomes incumbent upon him.

1. Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fell upon a man and killed him, so he said: There is no liability upon him. 2. Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Wasshash from Aban ibn Uthman from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fell upon a man from above the house, and one of them died, he said: There is no liability upon the upper one, and no liability upon the lower one. 3. Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadala from Al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who falls upon a man and kills him, he said: There is no liability upon him. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The explanation in these narrations is that he is not liable if it was accidental due to slipping, but if someone pushed him, the liability is upon him, and he may seek compensation from the pusher. 4. What Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who pushed a man onto another man and killed him, he said: The blood money is upon the one who fell upon the man, for the heirs of the deceased. He said: And the one who was pushed may seek the blood money from the one who pushed him. He said: And if the one who was pushed suffered any injury, it is also upon the pusher.

First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mayamari, from Aban, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) "Ten men killed one man." He said: "If the heirs wish, they can kill them all, and they pay nine blood-wits (diyas). If they wish, they can choose one man and kill him, and the remaining nine pay the heir of the last killed man one-tenth of the blood-wit each, each man from them. Then the ruler disciplines them and imprisons them." Second: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding two men who killed one man, he said: "If the heirs of the killed man wish to kill them both, they pay a complete blood-wit and kill them both, and the blood-wit is shared between the heirs of the two killed men. If they wish to kill one of them, they kill him, and the remaining one pays half the blood-wit to the heirs of the killed man. If they do not pay the blood-wit of one of them and one of them is not killed, they accept the blood-wit of their companion from both of them. If the heirs accept the blood-wit, it is upon both of them." Third: Yunus, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: "If two or three men kill one man and wish to kill them, they return the surplus of the blood-wit. If the heirs accept the blood-wit, it is upon them. Otherwise, they take the blood-wit of their companion." Fourth: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding ten men who participated in killing one man, he said: "The heirs of the killed man choose, and whomever they wish they kill, and his heirs return upon the remaining nine for nine-tenths of the blood-wit." Fifth: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from al-Abbas and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: "When a group gathers to kill one man, the ruler rules that whomever they wish be killed, and they are not allowed to kill more than one. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'He who is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority, so let him not exceed limits in killing.' And if three men kill one, the ruler is given the choice of which of the three to kill, and the other two guarantee two-thirds of the blood-wit for the heirs of

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who ordered another man to kill a man, and he killed him, it was said: The one who killed him is executed for him, and the commander is imprisoned until he dies. As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Mahbub from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him, it was said: The master is executed for him. And Ali from his father from al-Nufali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Is the man's slave not like his sword? The master is executed and the slave is entrusted to prison. The resolution in these two narrations is to interpret them as referring to one who is accustomed to ordering his slaves to kill people, forcing them into it and compelling them to do so. Indeed, one whose image is this is obligated to be executed because he is a corrupter on earth. And we said that because the first narration is consistent with the apparent meaning of the Quran. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'For a life, a life.' And we know that he meant the killing soul, not others, without dispute. Therefore, that which contradicts that should not be acted upon.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about a man who manumitted a slave girl by agreement (mukatabah). The slave girl said, 'I have not paid from my manumission contract, so I am free by his account.' He said to her, 'Yes.' Then she paid part of her manumission, and her master had intercourse with her after that. He said: 'If he forced her into that, he is flogged with a quantity of the flogging corresponding to what she paid from her manumission, and the flogging is deferred from him corresponding to what remained of her manumission. And if she consented, she became a partner in the flogging; she is flogged like what is flogged for him.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a female slave who has entered into a contract of manumission (mukattabah) and her master has sexual intercourse with her, causing her to become pregnant: he must pay her the dowry of her equal (in status/value), and she is granted more time to pay off her remaining debt. If she cannot pay, she becomes an 'Umm al-Walad' (mother of a child who secures her manumission upon her master's death).
