Then, when He created things and there came to be an object of knowledge, the Knowledge from Him was applied to the known, and Hearing to the heard, and Sight to the seen, and Power to the empowered.' He (Abu Baseer) said: 'I said, "Has God always been moving?" He (the Imam) said: "God is Exalted above that. Movement is a quality originated through action." I said, "Has God always been speaking?" He said: "Speech is an originated quality, it is not eternal. God, Mighty and Majestic, was — and He did not speak."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, existed and there was nothing other than Him, and He has never ceased to be Knowing of what will occur — and His knowledge of it before its occurrence is like His knowledge of it after its occurrence.'

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the supplication 'Praise is for Allah, the end-point of His knowledge.' So he wrote back to me: Do not say 'end-point of His knowledge', for His knowledge has no end-point. Rather, say 'end-point of His pleasure.'

He (Ayyub ibn Nuh) wrote to Abu al-Hassan (peace be upon him) asking him about God — Mighty and Majestic — whether He knew the things before He created the things and brought them into being, or He did not know that until He created them and intended their creation and their coming into being, so He knew what He created at the time of creation, and what He brought into being at the time of bringing into being. So he (the Imam) endorsed in his own handwriting: 'God never ceased to be Knowing of the things before He created the things, just as His knowledge of the things after He created the things.'

I wrote to the man (peace be upon him) asking him that your followers had differed regarding the Knowledge. So some of them said, 'God did not cease to be a Knower before He did (created) the things'; and some of them said, 'We do not say that God did not cease to be a Knower, because the meaning of "He knows" is "He acts". So if we affirm the Knowledge (as eternal), then we have affirmed in the (pre-)eternity something along with Him'. So if you see fit — may God make me your ransom — that you teach me from that what I may stop at and not exceed. So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'God did not cease to be a Knower. Blessed and Exalted is His Mention.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Fudayl ibn Sukkarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام): “May I be sacrificed for you, if you see fit to teach me: did Allah, majestic is His Face, know before He created the creation that He is One? For your followers have differed. Some of them said: He had known before He created anything from His creation. And some of them said: the meaning of ‘He knows’ is ‘He does’; so today He knows that there is no other than Him before the bringing about of things.” So they said: “If we affirm that He never ceased being knowing that there is no other than Him, then we have affirmed along with Him something other than Him in His eternality.” So if you see fit, O my master, teach me that which I will not go beyond to anything else.” Then he (عليه السلام) wrote: “Allah has never ceased being Knowing. Blessed and Exalted is His mention.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said regarding the attribute of the Eternal: 'He is One, Self-Sufficient, singular in meaning — not with many different meanings.' He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: I said, 'May I be your ransom! A group from the people of Iraq allege that He hears with something other than that with which He sees, and He sees with something other than that with which He hears.' So he (the Imam) said: 'They have lied and deviated and anthropomorphized. Exalted is God above that! He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He hears with that with which He sees, and He sees with that with which He hears.' He (the narrator) said: I said, 'They allege that He is All-Seeing according to what they themselves comprehend.' So he (the Imam) said: 'Exalted is God! Rather, one comprehends (only) that which has the quality of a creature. And God is not like that.'

In the hadith of the atheist who asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said to him: 'Do you claim that He is Hearing, Seeing?' So Abu Abdillah said: 'He is Hearing, Seeing — Hearing without a bodily organ and Seeing without an instrument. Rather, He hears by Himself and sees by Himself. And my saying that He is Hearing by Himself does not mean that He is one thing and the Self is another thing; rather, I intended it as an expression from myself when I was the one questioned, and as a means of comprehension for you when you were the questioner. So I say: He hears with all of Himself — not that the whole of Him has parts, because for us the whole has parts; rather, I intended to make you understand and to express from myself. And my reference in all of that is nothing other than: He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware — without any difference in Essence, and without any difference in meaning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'Allah never ceased to be an Intender.' He said: 'The Intender cannot be except with an object of intention alongside it. Allah never ceased to be a Knower, Powerful — then He Willed.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Bukayr ibn A'yan who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Are the Knowledge of God and His Will different or the same? So he said: Knowledge is not the Will. Do you not see that you say 'I shall do such-and-such if God wills it' and you do not say 'I shall do such-and-such if God knows it'? So your saying 'if God wills it' is evidence that He has not yet willed it. So when He wills, that which He wills comes to pass, just as He wills it — and the Knowledge of God precedes the Will.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Inform me about the Will from God and from creation.' So he said: 'The Will from creation is the inner resolve, and what then manifests from them in action. But as for the Will from God the Exalted, His Will is His act of bringing into being — nothing other than that — because He does not deliberate, nor does He have whims, nor does He think; and these attributes are negated from Him, for they are the attributes of creation.' So the Will of God is the act itself, nothing other than that. He says to it: Be! — and it is — without a spoken word, without utterance by a tongue, without a whim, without thought, and without any modality for that, just as there is no modality for Him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayyna, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Allah created the Will by itself, then created the things through the Will.'

I was in the gathering of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when Amr ibn Ubayd entered upon him and said to him: 'May I be your ransom! Concerning the Word of God, Blessed and Exalted: "and whosoever My wrath befalls, he has indeed perished" [20:81] — what is that wrath?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the punishment, O Amr. Indeed, whoever claims that God has transitioned from one state to another has described Him with an attribute of a creature, and God the Exalted — nothing stirs Him so that He would change.'

From the hadith of the atheist who questioned Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Among his questions was that he said to him: 'Does He have pleasure and anger?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but that is not in the manner found among creatures.' That is because pleasure is a state that enters upon one, transferring one from one state to another, because the creature is hollow, active, and compound — things have an entry into it. But our Creator — there is no entry for things into Him, because He is One, uniquely one in Essence, uniquely one in Concept. So His pleasure is His reward, and His anger is His punishment — without any thing entering Him to provoke Him and transfer Him from one state to another, because that is among the attributes of the creatures who are incapable and needy.
The Will is originated.

Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created a Name with letters without sound, with words without speech, with a personality without a body, with resemblance without attributes, and with color without coloring. Dimensions are negated from Him, limits are remote from Him, the perception of every imaginer is veiled from Him — He is self-concealing without being covered. So He made it a complete word upon four parts together, none of which precedes another. He manifested three Names from it for the need of creation toward them, and He veiled one of them — and it is the Hidden, Treasured Name. These are the Names that manifested; the Manifest one is Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And He, Glorified be He, subjected four pillars to every Name of these Names, making twelve pillars in all. Then He created for every pillar from these thirty Names, a deed attributed to them. So He is: the All-Beneficent, the All-Merciful, the King, the Holy, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner, the Living, the Self-Subsisting — neither slumber nor sleep seizes Him — the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Wise, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supremely Great, the Most High, the Magnificent, the All-Powerful, the Able, the Source of Peace, the Bestower of Security, the Guardian, the Originator, the Builder, the Unprecedented Creator, the Lofty, the Majestic, the Generous, the Sustainer, the Life-Giver, the Death-Causer, the Resurrector, the Inheritor. These are the Names, and whatever was from the Most Beautiful Names until three hundred and sixty Names are complete — they are a relation to these three Names. These three Names are pillars, and He veiled the single Hidden, Treasured Name by these three Names. And that is His saying, the Exalted: 'Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the All-Beneficent; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names.'

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'Was God, Mighty and Majestic, aware of Himself before He created the creation?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Did He see it (His Self) and hear it?' He said: 'He was not in need of that, because He did not happen to ask it nor seek from it. He is His Self, and His Self is He. His Power is pervading. Thus, He is not in need of naming Himself.' But He chose names for others to call Him by, because when He is not called by His Name, He would not be recognized. Thus, the first of what He chose for Himself was al-Ali al-Azim (the Exalted, the Magnificent), because He is loftier than all things. So its meaning is Allah, and His Name is al-Ali al-Azim — it is the first of His Names. He is Exalted above every thing.
And by this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: I asked him about the Name — what is it? He said: 'An attribute of the described.'

A Name of God is other than Him, and everything upon which the name of a thing falls is a creature, apart from God. As for what tongues express or hands perform, it is a creation. And God is an end-point among His end-points, and the end-directed is other than the end-point, and the end-point is describable, and every describable thing is manufactured. The Maker of things is not described by a named limit; He did not come into being so that His coming-into-being would be known through the creation of another, and He did not terminate at an end-point except that it would be other than Him. Whoever understands this principle will never slip, and it is the pure Tawhid — so observe it, affirm it, and comprehend it by the permission of God. Whoever claims to recognise God through a veil, or through an image, or through a resemblance, is a polytheist, because His veil, His resemblance, and His image are other than Him. He is One, uniquely One — so how can one declare His Oneness who claims to have recognised Him through something other than Him? Indeed, only the one who recognises Him through God has recognised God. Whoever does not recognise Him through Him has not recognised Him; he has only recognised something other than Him. There is nothing between the Creator and the created, and God is the Creator of things — not from any thing that was. And God is named with His Names, yet He is other than His Names, and the Names are other than Him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of 'In the Name of God, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.' He said: 'The Ba is the Splendor (Baha') of God, and the Sin is the Sublimity (Sana') of God, and the Mim is the Glory (Majd) of God.' And some of them narrated: 'The Mim is the Kingdom (Mulk) of God. And God is the God of everything; the All-beneficent toward all His creation, and the All-merciful toward the believers in particular.'

He asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of God and their derivation — from what is 'Allah' derived? He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hisham! Allah is derived from ilah (God), and ilah necessitates a worshipper. The name is other than the named. Whoever worships the name without the meaning has committed disbelief and has not worshipped anything. Whoever worships the name and the meaning has committed shirk and worshipped two. Whoever worships the meaning without the name — that is tawhid. Do you understand, O Hisham?' He said: I said: Give me more. He said: 'God has ninety-nine names. If the name were the named, then each name would be a god. But God is a meaning to which these names point, and all of them are other than Him. O Hisham! Bread is a name for the edible, water is a name for the drinkable, cloth is a name for the wearable, and fire is a name for the burning. Do you understand, O Hisham — an understanding with which you can repel and contend against our enemies who take others alongside God, Mighty and Majestic?' I said: Yes. So he said: 'May God benefit you with it and establish you, O Hisham!' He (Hisham) said: By God, no one was able to subdue me in matters of tawhid until I attained this station of mine.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about the meaning of 'Allah'. So he said: [Allah is] the One Who dominates over whatever is subtle and whatever is great.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from al-Abbas ibn Hilal who said: I asked al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah — 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth' [24:35] — so he said: '(He is) a Guide for the inhabitants of the sky, and a Guide for the inhabitants of the earth.' And in the narration of al-Barqi: '(He is) Guidance for those in the sky and Guidance for those in the earth.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Fuzayl ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'He is the First and the Last' (57:3), and I said: 'As for the First, we have recognised it, but as for the Last, clarify its interpretation for us.' So he said: 'There is nothing that does not perish, or change, or into which change and decline enters, or that transfers from one colour to another, from one form to another, from one attribute to another, and from increase to decrease and from decrease to increase — except the Lord of the worlds. For He has never ceased nor will He cease to be in one state. He is the First before everything, and He is the Last in the same manner as He always has been.' Attributes and names do not vary upon Him as they vary upon others — like the human being who at one time is dust, at another time is flesh and blood, and at yet another time is decaying remains and bones; and like the date which at one time is raw, at another time half-ripe, at another ripe, and yet another a dried date — so the names and attributes change upon it. But God, Majestic and Mighty, is the opposite of that.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — and he had been asked about 'the First' and 'the Last' — and he said: 'The First' means not from a first before Him nor from a beginning preceding Him; and 'the Last' means not from an end-point in the way that is understood from the attributes of created beings. But He is eternal — First, Last — He has always been and will never cease, without a beginning and without an end. Temporal origination does not befall Him, nor does He change from one state to another. He is the Creator of all things.

Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), when a man asked him, saying: 'Inform me about the Lord, Blessed and Exalted — He has Names and Attributes in His Book, and are His Names and His Attributes the same as Him?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'This speech has two aspects. If you are saying they are Him, meaning He has number and multiplicity, then Exalted is Allah above that. And if you are saying that these Attributes and Names have eternally existed, then "eternally existed" carries two meanings. If you say they have existed eternally in His Presence, in His Knowledge, and He is deserving of them, then yes. But if you are saying that their images, their spellings, and their letters have eternally existed, then we seek refuge with Allah that there would be anything with Him other than Him.' 'Rather, Allah was and there was no creation, then He created them as a means between Him and His creation — they beseech Him through them and worship Him, and they are His Remembrance. And Allah was and there was no Remembrance, and the One Remembered through the Remembrance is Allah, the Eternal who never ceases to be. And the Names and the Attributes are created things, and the Meaning and the One Meant by them is Allah, upon Whom neither variance nor combination befits, for only what is fragmented varies and combines.' 'So Allah is not said to be combined, nor Allah little nor much, but He is the Eternal in His Essence, for whatever is besides the One is a fragment, and Allah is One, not fragmented, and not imaginable through fewness or manyness. And everything that is fragmented or imaginable through fewness or manyness is a creation evidencing its Creator. So your saying "Allah is All-Powerful" informs that nothing frustrates Him, and you negate powerlessness through that word, making powerlessness to be other than Him. Similarly, your saying "Knower" negates ignorance through the word. And when Allah annihilates things, He annihilates the image, the spelling, and the syllables, and He who never ceases to be remains ever a Knower.' Then the man said: 'How then did we name our Lord All-Hearing?' He said: 'Because nothing of what is perceived through ears is hidden from Him, and we do not describe Him with the hearing situated in the head. Likewise we named Him All-Seeing, because nothing of what is

A man in his presence said, 'God is the Greatest!' So he said: 'God is Greater than which thing?' So he said, 'Than everything'. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You have limited Him'. So the man said, 'How should I say it?' He said: 'Say, 'God is the Greatest, beyond description''.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Which thing is God Greater than?' I said, 'God is Greater than everything.' He said, 'Was there then something, so that He would be greater than it?' I said, 'And what is it (the correct meaning)?' He said, 'God is Greater than to be described.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about 'Subhan Allah.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Anafa (transcendent dignity) for God.'

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sulayman slave of Tirbal, from Hisham al-Jawaliqy, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Glory be to Allah' — what is meant by it? He said: 'His Transcendence.'

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, all from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): 'What is the meaning of al-Wahid (the One)?' So he said: 'The consensus of the tongues upon Him with Oneness — like His saying, the Exalted: "And if you were to ask them who created them, they would certainly say: Allah." [43:87]

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar al-Hamdani, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all together from al-Fatah ibn Yazid al-Jurjani, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: He is al-Latif (the Subtle), al-Khabir (the Aware), al-Sami' (the Hearing), al-Basir (the Seeing), al-Wahid (the One), al-Ahad (the Absolute One), al-Samad (the Self-Sufficient). He did not beget, nor was He begotten, and there is none equal to Him. Had He been as the anthropomorphists claim, the Creator would not be distinguished from the created, nor the Originator from the originated. But He is the Originator — there is a clear distinction between the One who shaped it, gave it form, and brought it into being, since nothing resembles Him, nor does He resemble anything. I said: Indeed, may God make me your ransom! But you said al-Ahad al-Samad, and you said nothing resembles Him; yet God is one (wahid) and the human being is one (wahid). Has not the oneness (wahidaniyya) become similar? He said: O Fatah! You have stated an impossibility — may God keep you firm! Indeed, resemblance is in meanings, not in names. As for names, they are one and the same, pointing to the named. This is because the human being, even if called 'one', is told he is a single body — not two. Yet the human being himself is not truly one, because his limbs are different and his colours are different; and one whose colours differ is not truly one. He is a collection of divided parts that are not equal: his blood is other than his flesh, his flesh other than his blood, his sinews other than his veins, his hair other than his skin, his darkness other than his whiteness. And so it is with all of creation. The human being is one in name, yet there is no other one like him in meaning. But God — Glorified is His Majesty — He is One, there is no other one like Him; no difference in Him, no variation, no increase, no decrease. As for the human being: he is the created, the fashioned, the composed from different parts and diverse substances — except that in their gathering together he is one thing. I said: May I be made your ransom — you have relieved me, may God relieve you! Now your saying 'al-Latif al-Khabir' — explain it to me as you explained al-Wahid (the One), for I know that His subtlety is contrary to the subtlety of His creation — yet

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, in a mursal report, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: He عليه السلام said: Know—may Allah teach you goodness—that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Eternal, and eternality is His attribute by which the rational person is led to know that there was nothing before Him and nothing with Him in His everlastingness. Thus it has become clear to us, by the acknowledgement of the people generally, through the conclusive force of this attribute, that there was nothing before Allah and nothing with Allah in His abiding, and the statement of one who claims that something was before Him or with Him is invalid. That is because if something had been with Him in His abiding, it would not be permissible for Him to be its Creator, since it would always have been with Him; so how could He be Creator of one that never ceased to be with Him? And if something had been before Him, that thing—not He—would have been first, and the first would have had more right to be the creator of the first. Then He, Blessed and Exalted, described Himself with names by which, when He created the creatures, obligated them in worship, and tested them, He called them to invoke Him. So He named Himself Hearing, Seeing, Powerful, Standing, Speaking, Manifest, Hidden, Subtle, All-Aware, Strong, Mighty, Wise, Knowing, and whatever resembles these names. So when the lying deniers saw those among His names, and had heard us relate concerning Allah that nothing is like Him and nothing among creation shares His state, they said: Tell us, if you claim that there is no likeness to Allah and no resemblance to Him, then how do you share with Him in His Most Beautiful Names and call yourselves by all of them? Indeed, in that there is proof that you are like Him in all His states, or in some of them rather than others, since you have gathered the goodly names. It is said to them: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has assigned to the servants names from His names while the meanings differ. This is like a single name gathering two different meanings. The proof of that is the accepted and widespread speech of people, and it is with that that Allah addressed creation: He spoke to them in what they understand so that it might be a proof against them regarding what they neglected. A man may be called a dog, a donkey, a bull, sweetness, bitterness, or a lion—all of that despite his being differen

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid whose nickname is Shabab al-Sayrafi, from Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari who said: I said to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): May I be sacrificed for you, what is Al-Samad? He said: The Master to whom one turns in matters great and small.

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about something concerning tawhid, and he said: Indeed Allah — blessed are His names by which He is called, and Exalted is He in the loftiness of His essence — is One. He singularized Himself with oneness in His uniqueness, then caused it to flow upon His creation. So He is One, Samad, Holy. Everything worships Him and everything turns toward Him, and He encompasses all things in knowledge.

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Barmaki, from Ali ibn Abbas al-Kharadhini, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Jafar al-Jafari, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said: It was mentioned in his presence that a group of people claim that God, Blessed and Exalted, descends to the nearest heaven. So he said: Indeed God does not descend, nor does He need to descend. Rather, His sight regarding the near and the far is the same — a close thing does not become far from Him, nor does a distant thing come near to Him. He has no need of anything; rather, all things are in need of Him. He is the Possessor of Bounty. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise. As for the statement of those who describe Him that He, Blessed and Exalted, descends — only one who attributes deficiency or increase to Him would say that; for every moving thing needs something to move it or something it moves with. So whoever entertains false conjectures about God is destroyed. Therefore, be cautious regarding His attributes lest you impose a limit upon Him, defining Him by deficiency or increase, or causing movement or motion, or decline, or descent, or rising, or sitting — for God is far more Majestic and Mighty than the descriptions of the describers, the characterizations of the characterizers, and the imaginations of the imaginers. Put your trust in the Mighty, the Merciful, Who sees you when you stand (for prayer) and your prostrations among those who prostrate.

And from him, he raised it (mursal), from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he said: I do not say that He is standing, so I would remove Him from His place; nor do I delimit Him to a place that He would be in; nor do I delimit Him to move in something from elements and body parts; nor do I delimit Him by the utterance of splitting a mouth. But rather, just as God (Blessed and Exalted) said: "Be!" and it becomes — by His will, without any hesitation within Himself. He is Samad, Singular, not needing an associate to remind Him of His kingdom nor to open for Him the doors of His knowledge.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Dawud ibn Abdillah, from Amr ibn Muhammad, from Isa ibn Yunus who said: Ibn Abi al-Awja' said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) during one of his dialogues with him: 'You have mentioned God, and thus referred to an absent [entity].' So Abu Abdillah said: 'Woe to you! How can He who is present with His creation as a witness be absent, and closer to them than the jugular vein — He hears their speech, sees their persons, and knows their secrets?' So Ibn Abi al-Awja' said: 'Is He in every place? Is it not that if He were in the sky, how could He be in the earth, and if He were in the earth, how could He be in the sky?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, you have described a created being who, when it moves from a place, a place becomes occupied by it and a place becomes empty of it, so it does not know, while it is in the place it came to be in, what is occurring in the place it was in. But as for God, the Magnificent of Glory, the King, the Judge — no place is ever empty of Him, no place is ever occupied by Him, and He is no closer to any place than to another place.'

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'May God make me your ransom, O my master! It has been reported to us that God is in a place besides another place, established upon the Throne, and that He descends every night during the latter half of the night to the nearest sky; and it has been reported that He descends on the evening of Arafat, then returns to His place.' So some of your followers said concerning this: 'If He were in one place other than another, then the atmosphere would encounter Him and surround Him, and the atmosphere is a subtle body that surrounds everything according to its measure — so how could it surround Him, Majestic is His laudation, according to this analogy?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote back: 'The knowledge of that is with Him, and He is the One who determines it with what is the best of measurements. Know that when He is in the nearest sky, He is just as He is upon the Throne — all things are equal to Him in knowledge, power, dominion, and encompassment.' And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa — similarly.

From him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yaqoub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynahh, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of the Exalted: 'Nowhere is there a secret counsel between three persons but He is the fourth of them, nor (between) five but He is the sixth of them' So he said: 'He is the One, uniquely singular in Essence, separate from His creation; and with that He described Himself. He encompasses everything through supervision, encompassment, and power. Nothing escapes from Him — not even the weight of an atom in the heavens nor in the earth, nor anything smaller than that nor larger — through encompassment and knowledge, not through His Essence, because places are limited, contained by four boundaries, and if it were through His Essence, it would necessitate His being contained (within those limits).'

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Beneficent is established upon the Throne' [20:5]. So he said: 'He is established upon everything, so there is not anything closer to Him than another thing.'

And by this chain, from Sahl, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Marid, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Most Merciful rose above the Throne' [Quran 20:5] So he said: 'He is equal in relation to every thing; there is nothing closer to Him than another thing.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God the Exalted: 'The Beneficent is even upon the Throne' [20:5]. So he said: 'He is even with regard to everything. There is nothing closer to Him than another thing. The remote is not far from Him, and the close is not nearer to Him. He is even with regard to everything.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Whoever claims that God is from a thing, or in a thing, or upon a thing, has committed blasphemy.' I said, 'Explain it to me.' He said, 'I mean by the containment of the thing around Him, or by an attachment supporting Him, or from a thing that preceded Him.' And in another report: 'Whoever claims that God is from a thing has made Him an originated being; whoever claims that He is in a thing has made Him contained; and whoever claims that He is upon a thing has made Him carried.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: Abu Shakir al-Daysani said, “Indeed, in the Qur'an there is a verse that is our statement.” I said, “What is it?” So he said: “And He is the One Who is God in the heaven and God in the earth.” So I did not know how to answer him. So I went for hajj and informed Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. He said, “This is the speech of a wicked heretic. When you return to him, say to him: ‘What is your name in al-Kufah?’ Then he will say, ‘So-and-so.’ Then say to him: ‘What is your name in al-Basrah?’ Then he will say, ‘So-and-so.’ Then say: ‘Likewise, Allah, our Lord—He is God in the heaven and God in the earth, and God in the seas, and God in the deserts, and in every place, God.’” He said: So I returned and went to Abu Shakir and informed him. He said, “This has been transmitted from al-Hijaz.”

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about tawhid. I said: 'Can I conceive of Him as a thing?' He said: 'Yes, without [being] comprehended by reason and without limit. So whatever your imagination falls upon from a thing — He is different from it. Nothing resembles Him, nor can the imaginations grasp Him. How can the imaginations grasp Him when He is different from what is conceived by reason and different from what is pictured in the imaginations? Rather, you can only imagine a thing [that is] beyond reason and without limits.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id who said: Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Is it permissible to say about God that He is a thing?' He said: 'Yes. It removes Him from the two limits — the limit of ta'til (denial of attributes) and the limit of tashbih (anthropomorphism).'

He (Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him) said: Indeed, God is distinct from His creation, and His creation is distinct from Him; and everything upon which the name 'thing' applies is a creation, apart from God.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara ibn A'yan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, God is distinct from His creation, and His creation is distinct from Him. Everything upon which the name "thing" falls, other than God, is a created being; and God is the Creator of all things. Blessed is the One like whom there is nothing, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' [Quran 42:11]

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Khaysama, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah is distinct from His creation, and His creation is distinct from Him; and everything upon which the name 'thing' applies, apart from Allah the Exalted, is a created thing, and Allah is the Creator of everything.

He said to the atheist when he asked him, 'What is He?' He said: 'He is a thing unlike all things. I reiterate through my words to establish a meaning: He is a thing in the true reality of thing-ness, except that He has no body, no form, cannot be sensed, cannot be touched, and cannot be perceived by the five senses. Imaginations cannot grasp Him, the passage of ages does not diminish Him, and time does not change Him.' So the questioner said to him: 'Do you say that He is All-Hearing and All-Seeing?' He said: 'He is All-Hearing and All-Seeing — Hearing without an organ, and Seeing without an instrument. Rather, He hears by Himself and sees by Himself. My saying that He is All-Hearing who hears by Himself and All-Seeing who sees by Himself does not mean that He is one thing and the Self is another thing. I merely wanted an expression for myself, since I was being asked, and to make you understand, since you were asking. So I say: He is Hearing in all His totality — not that His totality has parts — but I wanted to make you understand and to express myself. My only reference in that is to the fact that He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware — without any difference in the Essence and without any difference in meaning.' The questioner said to him: 'Then what is He?' Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said: 'He is the Lord, He is the Worshipped One, and He is Allah. My saying Allah does not mean affirming these letters — Alif, Lam, Ha — nor Ra, nor Ba. Rather, return to the meaning: a thing, the Creator of things and their Maker, and the attribute of these letters — and He is the meaning by which Allah, al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Aziz, and similar names of His are named. He is the Worshipped One, glorified and exalted.' The questioner said to him: 'But we find nothing imaginable except a created thing.' Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said: 'If it were as you say, then monotheism (tawhid) would be lifted away from us, since we were not charged with anything other than what is imaginable. But we say: every imaginable thing perceivable by the senses is thereby limited and represented, so it is created. For denial is invalidation and non-existence, and the second way is tashbih (anthropomorphism). The second is the resemblance (tashbih). Since resemblance is the quality of a creation that is manifestly composed and assembled — it was ine

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from whoever mentioned it: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Is it permissible to say that God is a thing?' He said: 'Yes — it takes Him out of the two limits: the limit of negation (ta'til) and the limit of comparison (tashbih).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, who transmitted it in mursal form, said: Al-Jathaliq (the Catholicos) asked the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), saying: 'Inform me about God Almighty and Majestic — does He carry the Throne, or does the Throne carry Him?' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'God Almighty and Majestic is the Carrier of the Throne and the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them and between them. And that is the word of God Almighty and Majestic: [Quran 35:41] Surely God upholds the heavens and the earth lest they fall apart; and if they were to fall apart, none could uphold them after Him — truly He is Forbearing, Forgiving. He said: 'Then inform me about His word: [69:17] And above them eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord on that Day. How can He say that, when you said that He carries the Throne and the heavens and the earth?' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The Throne — God the Exalted created it from four lights: a red light from which all redness became red, a green light from which all greenness became green, a yellow light from which all yellowness became yellow, and a white light from which all whiteness became white. And it is the Knowledge which God loaded upon the bearers, and that is a Light from His Magnificence. By His Magnificence and His Light do the hearts of the believers see; by His Magnificence and His Light do the ignorant ones oppose Him; and by His Magnificence and His Light do all those in the heavens and the earth from all His creatures seek the means to Him through diverse deeds and varied religions. Thus, every carried thing which God carries by His Light, Magnificence, and Power cannot of itself bring harm or benefit, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection. So everything is carried, and God Blessed and Exalted is the One Who upholds them both lest they fall apart, and Who encompasses them all, and He is the Life of everything and the Light of everything. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they say, with great exaltation. He said to him: 'Then inform me about God Almighty and Majestic — where is He?' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'He is here and here, above and below, surrounding us and with us, and it is His word: [Quran 58:7] There is no secret counsel of three but He is their four

Abu Qurra the narrator asked me to take him to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him). So I sought his permission, and he permitted me. He entered and asked him about the permissible and the forbidden, then said to him: 'Do you acknowledge that God is carried?' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Every carried thing is acted upon, attributed to something other than itself, and in need. The word "carried" is a term of deficiency in expression, while "carrier" is an agent and is praiseworthy in expression. Similarly are the words of one who says "above" and "below" and "higher" and "lower". God has said: "And to God belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them" [7:180] — and He did not say in His books that He is the carried one; rather He said that He is the Carrier on land and sea, and the Upholder of the heavens and the earth lest they decline. The "carried" is that which is other than God, and never has anyone who believes in God and His Majesty been heard to say in their supplication: "O Carried One!"' Abu Qurra said: 'But He said: "And above them eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord on that Day" [69:17], and He said: "Those who bear the Throne" [40:7].' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'The Throne is not God. The Throne is a name of knowledge and power — a throne in which everything exists. Then He attributed the carrying to others of His creation, because He subjugated His creation through the carrying of His Throne — and they carry His knowledge. And He created beings who glorify around His Throne, performing by His knowledge, and angels who record the deeds of His servants; and He subjugated the people of the earth through circumambulation around His House. And God settled upon the Throne as He said.' The Throne, and those who carry it, and those around the Throne — God is their Carrier, their Preserver, the Upholder, the Standing One over every soul, above everything, and upon everything. He cannot be called "the carried" nor "the lower" as a standalone word without connection to something else, for that would corrupt the word and the meaning. Abu Qurra said: 'Are you denying the report which states that when God is angry, His anger is known because the angels who carry the Throne feel its weight upon their shoulders and fall prostrate? And when the anger subsides, it becomes lighter and they return to their places.' Abu

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from al-Fuzayl ibn Yasar who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth' [2:255]. So he said: 'O Fuzayl! Everything is in the Kursi — the heavens and the earth, and everything is in the Kursi.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Majestic and Mighty: 'His Chair extends over the heavens and the earth' [2:255] — do the heavens and earth encompass the Chair, or does the Chair encompass the heavens and earth? He said: Rather, the Chair encompasses the heavens and the earth, and the Throne (al-Arsh) and everything — the Chair encompasses all.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'His Chair encompasses the heavens and the earth' — do the heavens and the earth encompass the Chair, or does the Chair encompass the heavens and the earth? So he said: 'Verily, everything is in the Chair.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The bearers of the Throne — and the Throne is Knowledge — are eight: four from us and four from whoever God wills.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Dawood al-Raqqi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and His Throne was upon the water.' He said: 'What are they saying?' I said: 'They say that the Throne was upon the water and the Lord was above it.' So he said: 'They have lied. Whoever claims this has made God a carried one, and described Him with the attribute of a creature, and it follows that the thing carrying Him would be stronger than Him.' I said: 'Explain it to me, may I be your sacrifice!' So he said: 'Indeed God loaded His religion and His knowledge upon the water before there was earth, sky, jinn, humans, sun, or moon.' Then when God intended to create the creatures, He scattered them before Him and said to them: 'Who is your Lord?' The first to speak was the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the Imams (God's blessings be upon them), and they said: 'You are our Lord.' So He loaded them with the knowledge and the religion. Then He said to the angels: 'These are the carriers of My religion, My knowledge, and My trustees among My creation, and they are the ones who will be held accountable.' Then He said to the Children of Adam: 'Acknowledge to God the Lordship, and to these persons the wilayah and obedience.' So they said: 'Yes, our Lord, we acknowledge.' Then God said to the angels: 'Bear witness!' So the angels said: 'We bear witness, lest they say tomorrow that we were unaware of this. Or lest you say: it was only our fathers who committed shirk before, and we were their offspring after them — so would You destroy us for what the wrongdoers did?' O Dawood! Our wilayah is confirmed upon them in the Covenant.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayyna, from al-Ahwal who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Spirit which was in Adam (peace be upon him) — His words: 'So when I have made him complete and blown into him from My Spirit' He said: 'This is a created spirit, and the Spirit which was in Isa was also created.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and a spirit from Him' (4:171). He said: It is the spirit of God — a created being. God created it in Adam and in Jesus.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic, 'And I breathed into him from My Spirit' — how was this blowing? So he said: 'The Spirit (Ruh) moves like the wind (Reeh), and it was named Ruh because it derived its name from Reeh (wind). He differentiated it from the term Reeh because the spirits are of the genus of the wind. And He attributed it to His Own Self because He chose it above the rest of the spirits — just as He said for a house among houses: "My house," and for a messenger among the messengers: "My Friend (Khalil)," and the likes of that. And all of that is created, made, newly-originated, nourished, and regulated.'

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what they report, that Allah created Adam in His image. So he said: It is a newly-originated, created image which Allah chose and preferred above all other different images, so He attributed it to Himself just as He attributed the Ka'ba to Himself and the Spirit to Himself. and He said: 'My House' and [15:29] 'I breathed into him from My Spirit.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya together raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) mobilised the people for the war against Mu'awiya for the second time. When the people assembled, he stood as a speaker and said: All praise is for God, the One, the Unique, the Samad (the eternally besought), the Singular, Who was not from a thing and created nothing from a thing that existed. A power through which He is distinct from all things, and through which all things are distinct from Him. So there is no attribute by which He can be attained, nor a limit in which examples can be set for Him. All elaboration of languages falls short before His attributes, and the variations of descriptions stray there, and the profundities of intellectual schools are bewildered in His dominion, and the comprehensive interpretations are cut short before the firmness in His knowledge, and veils from the unseen stand before His concealed mystery — so that even the aspiring intellects lose themselves in the lowest of its subtle matters. So blessed is God Whom the farthest reach of ambitions cannot attain, and Whom the deep diving of astute minds cannot grasp. Exalted is the One Who has no counted time, no extended term, no bounded description. Glory be to Him Who has no beginning that has started, nor a point of termination, nor a final end that perishes. Glory be to Him — He is just as He described Himself, and the describers do not reach His description. And He bounded all things at their creation — distinguishing them from any resemblance to Him and distinguishing Himself from any resemblance to them. He did not merge into them so that it would be said He subsists within them, nor did He withdraw from them so that it would be said He is separate from them, nor is He absent from them so that one would ask 'where?' — but, glory be to Him, His knowledge encompasses them, His making perfected them, and His preservation has enumerated them. The hidden secrets of the atmosphere do not escape Him, nor the mysteries of the concealed darkness, nor whatever is in the highest heavens to the lowest earths. For every thing there is a preserver and a watchman, and every thing is encompassed by a thing. And the Encompasser of all that it encompasses is the One, the Unique, the Samad, Whom the vicissitudes of times do not chang

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed Allah — Blessed is His Name, and Exalted is His Mention, and Majestic is His Laudation. Glorified is He, and Holy, and Individual, and One. He did not cease to be and will not cease to be. And He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden. So there is no first to His being First. Raised in His Highest Loftiness: Lofty of the Elements, Raiser of Structures, Magnificent of Authority, of High Eminence, Sublime Highness — He before Whom the describers are unable to describe His Essence, nor can they endure bearing recognition of His Divinity, nor can they reach His limits, because He, through qualitative states, cannot be reached.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all from al-Fatah ibn Yazid al-Jurjani, who said: The road brought me together with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) during my return from Mecca to Khurasan, while he was travelling to Iraq. I heard him saying: 'Whoever fears God will be feared, and whoever obeys God will be obeyed.' So I approached him subtly, arrived, greeted him, and he returned my greeting. Then he said: 'O Fatah! Whoever pleases the Creator will not care about the anger of the creatures, and whoever angers the Creator deserves that God unleash the anger of the creatures upon him.' And indeed the Creator cannot be described except by what He Himself has described Himself with — and how can One be described Whom the senses are unable to perceive, imaginations unable to grasp, passing thoughts unable to delimit, and visions unable to encompass? He is more Majestic than what the describers describe Him as, and more Exalted than what the characterisers characterise. He is distant in His closeness and near in His distance — so in His distance He is near, and in His closeness He is far. He established the 'how', so one cannot ask 'how'; and He established the 'where', so one cannot ask 'where' — for He transcends how-ness and where-ness.

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, raising it from Abi Abdillah (عليه السلام), said: While Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was delivering a sermon upon the pulpit of al-Kufah, a man known as Dhi'lib stood up before him, eloquent in speech and brave of heart. He said, "O Amir al-Mu'minin, have you seen your Lord?" He (عليه السلام) said, "Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! I would not worship a Lord whom I had not seen." He said, "O Amir al-Mu'minin, how did you see Him?" He (عليه السلام) said, "Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! Eyes do not see Him through the sight of vision, but hearts see Him through the realities of iman. Woe unto you, O Dhi'lib! Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in subtlety, yet not described by subtlety; عظِيم in greatness, yet not described by greatness; Great in majesty, yet not described by magnitude; Majestic in exaltedness, yet not described by coarseness." He is before everything, yet it is not said that anything is before Him; and after everything, yet it is not said that there is an after for Him. He willed things not through resolve; He is all-aware not through device; He is in all things without being mixed with them, and not separate from them. He is Manifest, not in the sense of direct contact; self-disclosing, not through the commencement of vision; far, not by distance; near, not by closeness; subtle, not by corporeality; existent, not after nonexistence. He is an Agent, not by compulsion; an Ordainer, not by movement; a Willer, not by inclination; Hearing, not by an instrument; Seeing, not by a tool. Places do not contain Him, times do not encompass Him, attributes do not limit Him, and slumbers do not overtake Him. His being precedes times, His existence precedes nonexistence, and His pre-eternity precedes beginning. By His endowing the faculties with perception, it is known that He has no faculty; by His bringing forth substances, it is known that He has no substance; by His placing opposites among things, it is known that He has no opposite; and by His pairing things together, it is known that He has no companion. He set light against darkness, dryness against moisture, roughness against softness, and cold against heat. He joins together its mutually hostile things and separates its closely related things; by their separation they indicate the One who separated them, and by their composition they indicate the One who composed them. And that is His, the Ex

Ismail ibn Qutayba said: I and Isa Shalaqan went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he initiated us by saying: How strange are those people who claim things against the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he never uttered at all! The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) addressed the people at Kufa and said: Praise be to God, the Inspirer of His servants to praise Him, and who created them upon the recognition of His Lordship — the One who points to His existence through His creation, and through the temporal origination of His creation to His pre-eternity, and through their mutual resemblance to each other to the fact that there is no resemblance to Him. He testifies through His signs to His power. His Essence is precluded from attributes, His being seen is precluded from eyes, and comprehending Him is precluded from imaginations. There is no time-limit to His being and no end-point to His permanence; the senses cannot encompass Him and veils cannot cover Him — the veil between Him and His creation is His very act of creating them, due to His transcendence from what is possible in their essences, and the possibility of what is impossible for Him, and the differentiation of the Maker from the made, the Limitless from the limited, and the Lord from the governed. The One — without the implication of a numeral; the Creator — not in the sense of movement; the All-Seeing — not by a tool; the All-Hearing — not by the separation of an organ; the Witness — not by contact; the Hidden — not by concealment; and the Manifest, the Distinct — not by the lapsing of a distance. His pre-eternity is an endpoint for the wanderings of thoughts, and His permanence is a restraint for the aspirations of intellects. His profound nature has dazzled the windows of sight, and His existence has suppressed the wanderings of imaginations. So whoever describes God has limited Him; whoever limits Him has numbered Him; whoever numbers Him has negated His pre-eternity; whoever says 'where' has assigned Him an endpoint; whoever says 'upon what' has isolated Him; and whoever says 'in what' has contained Him.

I wrote to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asking him about something concerning Tawheed. So he wrote back to me in his own handwriting: 'Praise belongs to God, Who inspires His servants to praise Him.' He mentioned similar to what Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated, up to his words: 'and His existence has suppressed the wanderings of imaginations.' Then he added: 'The first thing in religion regarding Him is recognising Him; and the perfection of recognising Him is affirming His Oneness; and the perfection of affirming His Oneness is the negation of attributes from Him — by the testimony of every attribute that it is other than the One described, and the testimony of the One described that He is other than the attribute, and their joint testimony together that duality is impossible for the Eternal.' So whoever describes God has limited Him, and whoever limits Him has numbered Him, and whoever numbers Him has negated His eternality. And whoever says 'How?' has sought to describe Him; and whoever says 'In what?' has contained Him; and whoever says 'Upon what?' has been ignorant of Him; and whoever says 'Where?' has isolated from Him; and whoever says 'What is He?' has attributed a nature to Him; and whoever says 'To what end?' has given Him a limit. He was a Knower when there was nothing to be known, a Creator when there was no creation, and a Lord when there was nothing being nourished. And thus our Lord is described, and He is beyond what the describers describe Him as.

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon after the afternoon prayer, and the people were amazed at the excellence of his description and what he mentioned of the glorification of God — may His majesty be exalted. Abu Ishaq said: I asked al-Harith: 'Did you not preserve it?' He said: 'I wrote it down.' So he dictated it to us from his book. Praise be to God who does not die and whose wonders never cease, for every day He is in a state of glory through the initiation of something new that had not been. He who does not beget, lest He have a partner in might; and who is not begotten, lest He be a perishable inheritor. Imaginations do not fall upon Him to liken Him to a standing apparition, nor do visions perceive Him so He would be altered after their passing. The One whose beginninglessness has no end, nor does His lastness have a limit or terminus. The One whom no time preceded and no era came before, who is not subject to increase or decrease, and cannot be described by 'where', 'what', or 'place'. The One who is hidden in the depths of concealed matters yet manifest in intellects through the signs of governance seen in His creation — whom the prophets were asked about, and they did not describe Him by limit or part, but described Him through His acts and pointed to Him through His signs. The intellects of thinkers cannot deny Him, for the One who originated the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them and between them, and He is their Maker — there is no withstanding His power. He who is remote from creation, so nothing is like unto Him. He who created His creation for His worship and enabled them upon His obedience through what He placed within them, and severed their excuses with the proofs — so with clear evidence was destroyed the one who perished, and by His favour was saved the one who was saved; and to God belongs all grace, as Originator and as Restorer. Furthermore, God — praise belongs to Him — opened praise with Himself, and sealed the matter of the world and the abode of the hereafter with praise for Himself, saying: 'He judged between them with truth, and it was said: and who is established upon the Throne without cessation, and who is exalted above creation without being distant from them nor physically contacting them. He has no limit that can be reached, and no likeness by which He can be known. Humbled is who

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sayf ibn Amira, from one who mentioned him, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Word of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'Everything will perish except His Face' [28:88]. So he said: 'What are they saying about it?' I said: 'They are saying: Everything will perish except the Face of God.' So he said: 'Glory be to God! They have spoken a grievous word! Rather, He meant by that the Face of God which is the way that leads to Him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Everything will perish except for His Face [28:88]' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever comes to Allah with what he has been commanded — namely, obedience to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) — that is the Face (of Allah) which will not perish.' And likewise He (Allah) said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah [4:80].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Sallam al-Nakhkhas, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We are al-Mathani which God gave to our Prophet Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). We are the Face of God, moving about on earth among you. We are the Eye of God among His creation, and His Hand extended with mercy upon His servants. Whoever recognized us, recognized us; and whoever was ignorant of us, was ignorant of us — and (we are) the Imams of the pious.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya together, from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them' He said: 'We, by God, are the most beautiful names (al-Asma' al-Husna), without whose recognition God does not accept any deed from His servants.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from al-Haytham ibn Abdillah, from Marwan ibn Sabbah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, God created us and made our creation excellent; and He formed us and made our forms excellent; and He made us to be His Eye among His servants, and His Speaking Tongue among His creation, and His Extended Hand over His servants with kindness and mercy, and His Face through which one comes to Him, and His Door which guides to Him, and His Treasurers in His heaven and His earth. Through us the trees bear fruit and the fruits ripen, and the rivers flow, and through us the rain of the heaven descends and the vegetation of the earth grows, and through our worship God is worshipped — and were it not for us, God would not be worshipped.

of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then when they displeased Us, We inflicted retribution on them' [43:55] — He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not grieve as we grieve. But He created friends (awliya') for Himself who grieve and are pleased, and they are created, nurtured beings. So He made their pleasure His own pleasure and their displeasure His own displeasure, because He made them the inviters to Him and the guides toward Him. For this reason they became as such, yet it is not that it (grief) reaches Allah as it reaches His creatures. Rather, this is the meaning of what He said regarding that. And He has said: 'Whoever insults a friend of Mine has declared war against Me and called Me to it.' And He said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah' [4:80]. And He said: 'Indeed, those who swear allegiance to you do but swear allegiance to Allah; the hand of Allah is above their hands' [48:10]. So all of this and the like of it is upon what I mentioned to you, and likewise is the pleasure and the anger and other things that are similar to that. Had it been that grief and weariness were to truly reach Allah — and He is the One who created them both — it would be permissible for one to say that one day the Creator would perish, because when anger and weariness enter Him, change would enter Him, and when change enters Him, annihilation cannot be ruled out. Then the Originator would not be distinguished from the originated, nor the Powerful from the one over whom power is exercised, nor the Creator from the created. Exalted is Allah above this speech, an immense exaltation. Rather, He is the Creator of things not out of need. So when He created not out of need, limitation and modality are impossible regarding Him. So understand, if Allah the Exalted wills.'

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he began to speak from himself without my having asked him: 'We are the Proof of God, and we are the Door of God, and we are the Tongue of God, and we are the Face of God, and we are the Eye of God among His creation, and we are the Masters of God's Command among His servants.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hassan al-Jammal, who said: Hashim ibn Abi Umara al-Janbi narrated to me, saying: I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say: 'I am the Eye of God, and I am the Hand of God, and I am the Side of God, and I am the Door of God.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazi', from Ali ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'O my regret, for what I wasted regarding the Side of Allah [39:56],' He said: 'The Side of Allah is the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and similarly those who came after him from the successors in the exalted station, until the matter reaches the last of them.'

I heard Abu Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) saying: Through us God is worshipped, and through us God is recognized, and through us God the Blessed and Exalted is declared One, and Muhammad is a veil of God the Blessed and Exalted.

One of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Bishr, from Mūsā ibn Qādim, from Sulaymān, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves. He said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, is greater, mightier, more majestic, and more exalted than to be wronged. But He joined us with Himself, so He made our being wronged His being wronged, and our wilayah His wilayah, where He says: Your wali is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe. Meaning the Imams from us. Then he said in another place: And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves. Then he mentioned something similar to that.

Allah has not been worshipped by anything like al-Bada'. And in a narration of Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Allah has not been glorified with the likes of al-Bada'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others besides them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: regarding this verse: 'Allah obliterates what He wills and establishes [what He wills]' then he said: 'And is anything obliterated except that which had been established? And is anything established except that which had not yet occurred?'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'God never sent a prophet until He took from him three characteristics: the acknowledgement of His Lordship, the renouncing of rivals (idols), and that God advances whatever He wills and delays whatever He wills.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'He decreed a term, and there is a term named with Him' He said: 'These are two terms — a determined term and a suspended term.'

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God the Exalted: 'Does the human being not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?' He said: So he said: 'Neither measured nor configured.' He said: And I asked him about His words: 'There surely came over the human being a period of time when he had not become a thing worthy of mention.' So he said: 'He was ordained without being mentioned.'

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Knowledge is of two types: a knowledge treasured with God which He has not disclosed to anyone from His creation; and a knowledge He taught to His angels and His messengers. As for what He taught His angels and His messengers, it will assuredly come to pass — He does not lie to Himself, nor to His angels, nor to His messengers. And there is a knowledge treasured with Him from which He brings forward what He wills, delays what He wills, and affirms what He wills.'

And by this chain, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from al-Fuzayl, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'From the matters are matters suspended in the presence of God. He brings forward from them whatever He wills, and He delays from them whatever He wills.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir and Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily for God there are two (types of) knowledge — a knowledge concealed and treasured, none knows it except Him, and from that comes al-Bada'; and a knowledge He taught to His angels, His Messengers, and His Prophets — and we know it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah did not make manifest (al-bada') regarding anything, except that it was in His knowledge before it became manifest to Him.

From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Juhani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah does not change His decision due to ignorance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Would something occur today that was not in the knowledge of God yesterday?' He said: 'No. Whoever says this, may God disgrace him.' I said: 'What is your view of what has occurred and what will continue to occur until the Day of Resurrection — is it not within the knowledge of God?' He said: 'Yes indeed, (even) before He created the creatures.'

Ali from Muhammad from Yunus from Malik al-Juhani, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If the people knew what reward lies in speaking about al-Bada', they would not languish from speaking about it.'

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'No prophet was ever granted prophethood until he acknowledged to God five characteristics: al-Bada' (the Manifestation of a New Divine Decree), and the [Divine] Will (al-Mashi'a), and prostration (al-Sujud), and servitude (al-'Ubodiyya), and obedience (al-Ta'a).'

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from Jahm ibn Abi Jahma, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu 'Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), peace be upon him — he said: 'Verily, Allah azwj Mighty and Majestic informed Muhammad saww of whatever had existed since the coming into being of the world, and of whatever would occur until the expiry of the world, and informed him of the Ordained (mahtum) matters from that, and He made an exception upon him regarding what was besides it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'God did not send any Prophet at all except with the prohibition of wine and that he acknowledge to God [the doctrine of] al-Bada'.'

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, who said: The Imam, the Knowledgeable One, عليه السلام, was asked, "How is the knowledge of Allah?" He said, "He knew, and willed, and intended, and measured, and decreed, and executed. So He executed what He decreed, and decreed what He measured, and measured what He intended. Thus by His knowledge was the will, and by His will was the intention, and by His intention was the measuring, and by His measuring was the decree, and by His decree was the execution." And knowledge is prior to will, and will is second, and intention is third, and measuring falls upon decree through execution. So for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there is al-badāʾ regarding what He knows, whenever He wills, and regarding what He intends for the measuring of things. But when the decree takes place through execution, then there is no badāʾ. Thus knowledge concerning the known is before its coming to be, and will concerning what is brought forth is before its concrete existence, and intention concerning the intended is before its establishment, and the measuring of these known things is before their detailing and their arrival into observable existence and time. And decree through execution is that which is made firm among the effected things possessing bodies, perceived by the senses, among those having color, smell, weight, and measure, and whatever creeps and moves among humans, jinn, birds, beasts, and other than that which is perceived by the senses. So for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in that there is badāʾ regarding what has no concrete entity. But when the concrete, understood, perceived thing takes place, then there is no badāʾ. And Allah does whatever He wills. So by knowledge He knew things before their being; by will He made known their attributes and their limits and brought them forth before manifesting them; by intention He distinguished their essences in their colors and attributes; by measuring He measured their sustenances and made known their beginning and their end; by decree He clarified their places to people and guided them to them; and by execution He explained their causes and made their affair clear. And that is the measuring of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

He said: 'Nothing comes into being in the earth nor in the sky except with these seven characteristics: by (His) will, and intention, and determination, and ordainment, and permission, and writing/decreeing, and a term. So whoever claims that he has the power to violate one of them has disbelieved.' And Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated it from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Muhammad ibn Umara, from Hariz ibn Abdullah and Ibn Muskan — similar to it.

And he also narrated it from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Zakariyya ibn Imran, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Nothing comes into being in the heavens nor in the earth except by seven — by (divine) ordainment, determination, intention, desire, writing, term, and permission. So whoever claims other than this has lied against God or rejected (the word of) God, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Nothing comes into being except what God has willed, intended, determined, and ordained.' I said: 'What is the meaning of willed?' He said: 'Initiating the act.' I said: 'What is the meaning of determined?' He said: 'Determining the thing in terms of its length and its breadth.' I said: 'What is the meaning of ordained?' He said: 'When He ordains it, He carries it out — and that is what there is no averting.'

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): '(He) desires, and intends, and determines, and ordains?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And He loves?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'And how does He desire, and intend, and determine, and ordain, while not loving?' He said: 'This is how it has come to us.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'God commands and does not will, and wills and does not command.' He commanded Iblis to prostrate to Adam, and willed that he not prostrate — and had He willed, he would have prostrated. And He forbade Adam from eating from the tree, and willed that he eat from it — and had He not willed, he would not have eaten.

Indeed, for Allah there are two Intentions and two Desires — an Absolute Intention and a Determined Intention. He forbids while He desires, and He commands while He does not desire.
