Or did you not see that He forbade Adam and his wife from eating from the tree, and yet He desired that — and had He not desired that they eat, their desire would not have prevailed over the Desire of Allah the Exalted. And He commanded Ibrahim to slaughter Ishaq, and He did not desire that he slaughter him — and had He so desired, the desire of Ibrahim would not have prevailed over the Desire of Allah the Exalted.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Dorost ibn Abi Mansour, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'He Desires and Intends, and He does not Love and is not Pleased. He Desires that nothing come into being except through His Knowledge, and He Intends similarly; He does not Love that it be said He is the third of three, and He is not Pleased with disbelief for His servants.'

Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said: God said: 'O son of Adam! By My will you came into being as one who desires for himself whatever he desires; and by My strength you fulfilled My obligations; and by My favour I gave you the strength to disobey Me. I made you hearing, seeing, and strong. Whatever good reaches you is from God, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself — and that is because I have greater right to your good deeds than you do, and you bear greater responsibility for your evil deeds than I do. And that is because I am not questioned about what I do, but they shall be questioned.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no constriction nor extension except that Allah has therein a will, an ordainment, and a trial.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, there is nothing wherein there is either a constriction or an extension from what God has commanded or forbidden, except that therein, for God Mighty and Majestic, is a trial and an ordainment.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, God created happiness and misery before He created His creation. So whoever God created as happy, He will not hate him ever — and even if he commits evil deeds, He hates his deed but does not hate him. And if he was (created as) miserable, God will not love him ever — and even if he performs righteous deeds, He loves his deed but hates him, because of what he will come to. So when God loves something, He will never hate it; and when He hates something, He will never love it.

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it (mursal), from Shu'ayb al-'Aqarqufi, from Abu Baseer, who said: I was seated before Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a questioner asked him, saying: 'May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of God! From where did misery befall the people of disobedience such that God decreed for them in His knowledge punishment for their deeds?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O questioner! The decree of God, Mighty and Majestic, is such that none of His creation can fulfill it as it deserves. So when He decreed that, He bestowed upon the people of His love the strength to recognize Him, and lifted from them the burden of deeds according to the reality of what they are deserving of.' And He bestowed upon the people of disobedience the strength for their disobedience — due to the precedence of His knowledge regarding them — and He prevented them from the capacity to accept from Him. So they conformed to what had preceded for them in His knowledge, and they were unable to attain a state that would save them from His punishment — because His knowledge is more deserving of the reality of ratification. And this is the meaning of: He willed what He willed — and it is His secret.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from Mu'alla ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The happy one is made to travel along the path of the miserable until the people say: How he resembles them! Nay, he is of them. Then happiness overtakes him. And the miserable one may be made to travel along the path of the happy ones until the people say: How he resembles them! Nay, he is of them. Then misery overtakes him. Verily, the one whom God has decreed as happy — even if nothing remains of the world except the duration of milking a she-camel — He will seal his end with happiness.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: From what God revealed to Moses (peace be upon him) and sent down to him in the Torah was: "I, I am God — there is no god except Me. I created the creatures and I created the good and caused it to flow upon the hands of those whom I love, so blessed is the one upon whose hands I caused it to flow." "And I am God — there is no god except Me. I created the creatures and I created evil and caused it to flow upon the hands of those whom I intend, so woe to the one upon whose hands I caused it to flow."

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Among some of what God revealed from His Books was: "I, I am God! There is no god except Me. I created the good and I created the evil. So beatitude is for the one upon whose hands I cause the good to flow, and woe be upon the one upon whose hands I cause the evil to flow, and woe is for the one who says, "How is this so" and "How is that so."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, from Mufazzal ibn Umar and Abd al-Mu'min al-Ansari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah (Mighty and Majestic) said: I am Allah. There is no god except Me. I am the Creator of good and evil. So beatitude is for the one upon whose hands I cause good to flow, and woe is for the one upon whose hands I cause evil to flow, and woe is for the one who says: How is that so, and how is this so? Yunus said: It means the one who denies this matter through his understanding of it.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from whomever mentioned it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from al-Fadl ibn al-Sakan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Recognize God through God, the Messenger through the Message, and the Masters of Authority through their enjoining of good, justice, and benevolence.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Uqba ibn Qays ibn Sim'an ibn Abi Rubayha — the freed slave of the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) — said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked: 'By what did you recognize your Lord?' He said: 'By that which He Himself made known to me.' It was said: 'And how did He make Himself known to you?' He said: 'No image resembles Him, nor can He be perceived by the senses, nor can He be compared with people.' He is Near in His remoteness and Remote in His nearness. He is above every thing, and it cannot be said that anything is above Him. He is before every thing, and it cannot be said that He has a before. He is within things, not like a thing that enters into another thing; and He is outside of things, not like a thing that exits from another thing. Glory be to the One Who is like this, and nothing else is like this. And for every thing there is an Initiator.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I debated a group and said to them: Indeed Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, is more Majestic, more Mighty, and more Benevolent than that He should be recognized through His creation; rather, it is the servants who are recognized through Allah. So he said: May Allah have mercy on you.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ishaq ibn Muhammad and others besides them, raising it [with an elevated chain], he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was seated in Kufa after his return from [the battle of] Siffeen, when an old man came forward and knelt before him, then said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful! Inform us about our march to the people of Syria — was it by an ordainment from God and pre-determination?' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, O Shaykh! You did not ascend any hill nor descend into any valley except by an ordainment from God and pre-determination.' So the Shaykh said to him: 'Will my exhaustion be counted [as reward] with God, O Commander of the Faithful?' So he said to him: 'Shh! O Shaykh! By God, God has magnified the reward for your travels while you were traveling, and for your staying while you were staying, and for your departure while you were departing, and you were not in any of your states being coerced nor compelled to it.' So the Shaykh said to him: 'And how were we not in any of our states being coerced nor compelled to it, when our march, our return, and our departure were by ordainment and pre-determination?' So he said to him: 'Do you think it was an unavoidable ordainment and a necessitated pre-determination? If it were so, reward and punishment would be invalidated, as would commanding [good] and forbidding [evil] and rebuke from God, and the meaning of promise and threat would crumble. Then no sinner would be blameworthy nor any good-doer praiseworthy, and the sinner would be more deserving of good treatment than the good-doer, and the good-doer would be more deserving of punishment than the sinner. That is the statement of the brothers of idol-worshippers, and the opponents of the All-Merciful, and the party of Satan, and the Qadariyya of this community and its Magians.' 'Indeed, God — Blessed and Exalted — imposed obligations through [man's] choice, and forbade [things] as a warning, and gives much for a little [deed], and is not disobeyed by being overpowered, and is not obeyed by compulsion, and did not give control as a delegation [of authority], and did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain, and did not send the Prophets as bearers of glad tidings and warners in futility. That is the conjecture of those who disbelie

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever claims that God commands with immorality has lied against God, and whoever claims that good and evil are His (responsibility) has lied against God.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) — he said: I asked him, and I said: 'Has God delegated the matter to the servants?' He said: 'God is mightier than that.' I said: 'So did He compel them to commit disobediences?' He said: 'God is more just and wiser than that.' He (the narrator) said, then he (the Imam) said: 'God said: O son of Adam! I have a closer claim to your good deeds than you, and you have a closer claim to your evil deeds than Me. You committed the disobediences through My strength which I placed in you.'

Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Yunus! Do not say according to the doctrine of the Qadariyya, for the Qadariyya did not speak according to the speech of the people of Paradise, nor according to the speech of the people of the Fire, nor according to the speech of Iblis. For the people of Paradise will say: All praise is due to God who guided us to this, and we would not have found guidance had God not guided us. [7:43] And the people of the Fire will say: Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us and we were a people gone astray. [23:106] And Iblis said: My Lord, by what You led me astray. [15:39] I said: By God! I do not say according to their speech. But I say: nothing can happen except with what God wills, intends, determines, and ordains. So he said: O Yunus! It is not like that. Nothing can happen except what God wills, intends, determines, and ordains. O Yunus! Do you know what the Desire (mashi'a) is? I said: No. He said: It is the primordial Remembrance (al-dhikr al-awwal). So do you know what the Intention (irada) is? I said: No. He said: It is the determination upon what He desires. So do you know what the Determination (qadar) is? I said: No. He said: It is the Engineering — the placement of limits between subsistence and perishing. He (the narrator) said: Then he said: And the Ordainment (qada') — it is the sealing and the realization of the concrete reality. He (the narrator) said: So I sought his permission to kiss his head, and I said: You have opened something for me that I was heedless of.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, Allah created the creation and He knew what they would come to. He commanded them and forbade them. So whatever He commanded them with from anything, He has placed for them the way to abandon it; and they will neither take it nor leave it except by the permission of Allah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn Qurt, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever claims that Allah commands evil and immorality has lied against Allah. Whoever claims that good and evil exist without the will of Allah has expelled Allah from His sovereignty. Whoever claims that sins are committed without the power of Allah has lied against Allah. And whoever lies against Allah, Allah will enter him into the Fire.'

There was a man in the mosque of al-Medina speaking about al-Qadar while people were gathering around him. So I said to him, 'O you, I want to question you.' He said, 'Ask.' I said, 'Can there be in the kingdom of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that which He does not will?' He lowered his head for a long time, then raised his head toward me and said to me: 'O you! If I say that there does happen to be in His kingdom what He does not will, then He is indeed subdued; and if I say that there cannot be in His kingdom except what He wills, I would be admitting to you (the right to commit) disobedience.' He (the narrator) said: So I told Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him): 'I asked this Qadari, and his answer was such and such.' So he (the Imam) said: 'He looked out for himself. But had he said other than what he said, he would have been destroyed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Za'lan, from Abu Talib al-Qummi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said, 'Did God compel the servants to commit acts of disobedience?' He said: 'No.' I said, 'Then did He delegate the matter to them?' He said: 'No.' He said: I said, 'Then what?' He said: 'A grace from your Lord between the two.'

Indeed, God is more merciful to His creation than to compel His creation to commit sins and then punish them for them; and God is mightier than to will a matter and have it not come into being. He (the narrator) said: So they (peace be upon them both) were asked: 'Is there a third position between compulsion and pre-determination?' They both said: 'Yes — more extensive than what is between the sky and the earth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Salih ibn Sahl, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about compulsion (jabr) and pre-determination (qadar). So he said: 'There is neither compulsion nor pre-determination; but there is a station between the two, in which lies the Truth that is between the two. None knows it except the Knowledgeable One (the Imam), or one whom the Knowledgeable One has taught it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad, from Yunus, from a number (of people), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Did God compel the servants to commit sins?' He said: 'God is too just to compel them to commit sins and then punish them for it.' So he said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! So did God delegate (the choice) to the servants?' (The narrator) said, so he said: 'If He had delegated to them, He would not have confined them with commands and prohibitions.' So he said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! So there is a (third) status between the two?' (The narrator) said, so he said: 'Yes, more extensive than what is between the sky and the earth.'

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “Indeed, some of our companions speak of compulsion, and some of them speak of capability.” He said: So he said to me, “Write: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:” “O son of Adam, by My will you became one who wills, and by My strength you fulfilled My obligations toward Me, and by My blessing you gained strength to disobey Me. I made you hearing and seeing. Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself. That is because I am worthier of your good deeds than you are, and you are worthier of your evil deeds than I am. And that is because I am not questioned concerning what I do, while they shall be questioned.” I have arranged for you everything you wanted.

Muhammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from one who narrated it to him, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is neither compulsion nor delegation, but rather a matter between two matters. He said: I said, 'And what is a matter between two matters?' He said: 'Its likeness is that of a man whom you see committing an act of disobedience, so you forbid him, but he does not desist. Then you leave him, and he commits that act of disobedience. It is not the case that, when he did not accept from you and you left him, you were the one who commanded him to commit the disobedience.'

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Allah is more generous than to burden the people with what they cannot bear, and Allah is mightier than that there should be in His dominion what He does not will.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Ali ibn Asbat who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about capability (istita'a). So he said: 'The servant is capable after four characteristics — that he be free in his path, healthy of body, sound of limbs, and there be a cause coming from God.' He said: I said, 'May I be your sacrifice — explain this to me.' He said: 'If the servant happens to be free in his path, healthy of body, sound of limbs, and he wants to commit adultery but does not find a woman, then he finds her — so either he restrains himself and refrains, just as Yusuf (peace be upon him) refrained, or he yields between himself and his desire and commits adultery, and so is called an adulterer; and he did not obey God by coercion, nor did he disobey Him by being overcome.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ali ibn Ibrahim, both from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Abdullah ibn Yazid, both from a man from the people of Basra, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the capability (istitaah). So he said: 'Are you capable of doing what has not yet come into being?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Are you capable of stopping what has already been decreed?' He said: 'No.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'So when are you capable?' He said: 'I do not know.' He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Indeed, God created creation and placed in them the instrument of capability, but then He did not delegate it to them. So they are capable of the deed at the time of the deed, along with the deed when they do that deed. But if they are not doing it in His dominion, they would not be capable of doing a deed they did not do — because God, Mighty and Majestic, is too Exalted for anyone to oppose Him in His dominion.' The man of Basra said: 'So the people are compelled?' He said: 'If they were compelled, they would be excused.' He said: 'Then has He delegated to them?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then what are they?' He said: 'He foreknew from them a deed, so He placed in them the instrument of the deed — so when they do it, they are with the deed, capable.' The man of Basra said: 'I testify that it is the Truth, and that you are the People of the House of Prophethood and the Message.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all of them from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Salih al-Nayli who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do the servants have any capability?' He said, then he said to me: 'When they perform the deed, they are capable — with the capability that God has placed within them.' He said, I said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'The instrument. For example, an adulterer — when he commits adultery, he was capable of the adultery at the time he committed it; and had he abstained from adultery and not committed it, he would have been capable of abstaining when he abstained.' He said, then he said: 'There is not for him any capability before the deed — neither little nor much — but at the time of the deed and the abstaining, he was capable.' I said: 'Then for what does He punish him?' He said: 'Due to the compelling proof and the instrument He has implanted within them. Indeed, God does not compel anyone to disobey Him, nor does He will with a determined will that anyone disbelieve. But when he does disbelieve, it was within God's will that he disbelieve; and they are within God's will and within His knowledge that they will not turn toward anything of goodness.' I said: 'Did He will that they disbelieve?' He said: 'I am not saying it like that. Rather, I say: He knew that they would disbelieve, so He willed disbelief due to His knowledge regarding them. But it is not a determined will — rather it is a will of choice.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of our companions, from Ubayd ibn Zurara who said: Hamza ibn Humran narrated to me, saying: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about capability (al-istita'a), but he did not answer me. So I went to him another time and said: 'May God keep you well! Something from it has settled in my heart that nothing will remove except something I hear from you.' He said: 'Whatever was in your heart will not harm you.' I said: 'May God keep you well! I say: God, Blessed and Exalted, does not burden His servants with what they are not capable of, and does not burden them except with what they can endure, and they do not do anything from that except by God's intention, His desire, His decree, and His pre-determination.' Then he said: 'This is the religion of God which I and my forefathers follow.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, God has argued against the people with what He gave them and made known to them. Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj — similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The recognition — from whose making is it?' He said: 'From the making of God. There is no making for the servants in it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'It was not for God to lead a people astray after He has guided them until He clarifies to them what they should guard against' [9:115] He (the Imam) said: 'Until He introduces to them what pleases Him and what angers Him.' And (the narrator) said: '(What about) Then He inspired it to understand its immorality and its piety [91:8]?' He (the Imam) said: 'He clarified to it what to come to and what to leave.' And (the narrator) said: '(What about) Surely We have shown him the way; he may be thankful or unthankful [76:3]?' He (the Imam) said: 'We made him recognize it — either he takes it or leaves it.' And concerning His words: 'And as for Thamud, We guided them but they preferred blindness over guidance' [41:17] He (the Imam) said: 'We made them recognize it, but they preferred blindness over guidance while they were knowing.' And in a narration: 'We clarified to them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Hamza ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We guided him to the two paths' [90:10]. He said: 'The path of good and the path of evil.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May God keep you well! Has there been placed in the people a faculty by which they can attain recognition?' He said: So he (the Imam) said: 'No.' I said: 'Then have they been charged with (attaining) recognition?' He said: 'No. Upon God is the clarification.' God does not impose upon any soul a duty but to the extent of its ability [2:286], and God does not lay on any soul a burden except to the extent to which He has granted it [65:7]. He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about His words: 'It was not for God to lead a people astray after He has guided them, until He clarifies to them what they should guard against [9:115].' He said: 'Until He makes known to them what pleases Him and what angers Him.'

Indeed, God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant except that He has made incumbent upon him, regarding it, the Proof from God. So whoever God has favoured by making him strong, his obligation upon him is to fulfill what He has charged him with and to bear [the burden of] those who are below him among those weaker than him. And whoever God has favoured by making him prosperous, his obligation upon him is his wealth, then his covenant of commitment toward the poor afterwards through his voluntary charitable acts. And whoever God has favoured by making him noble in his household and beautiful in his appearance, his obligation upon him is that he praise God the Exalted for that, and that he not be arrogant toward others so that he withholds the rights of the weak because of his noble state and beauty.

Muhammad b. Yahya, from Muhammad b. al-Husayn, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamily, from Durust b. Abi Mansur, from Burayid b. Mu'awiya, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not incumbent upon Allah's creatures that they recognise (Him on their own), but it is incumbent upon Allah that He introduce Himself to them, and it is incumbent upon the creatures — once He has introduced Himself to them — that they accept.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The one who does not recognize anything — is there anything upon him?' He said: 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu al-Hasan Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whatever God has concealed from the servants, it is removed from their accountability.

He said to me: 'Write!' So he dictated to me: 'From our doctrine it is that Allah argues against the servants with what He granted them and made known to them. Then He sent a Messenger to them and revealed the Book to them, and commanded in it and forbade. He commanded in it salat and fasting. So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) slept through the salat, and He said: "I cause you to sleep and I wake you up; so when you rise, perform the salat" — so that they may know, when that happens to them, how they should act. It is not as some say: "When one sleeps through it, he is destroyed." And likewise fasting: "I cause you to be sick and I cause you to recover; so when I heal you, make it up."' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And likewise when you look at all things, you will not find anyone in hardship, and you will not find anyone except that Allah has the proof (hujja) over him and Allah has the will (mashi'a) regarding him. And I do not say that they may do whatever they wish.' Then he said: 'Allah guides and leads astray, and He said: "And they were not commanded except with less than what they are capable of." And everything the people are commanded with, they have the capacity for it; and everything they do not have the capacity for, it is lifted from them. But the people — there is no good in them.' Then he (peace be upon him) recited: 'There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find what they should spend, so long as they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger — there is no way against the doers of good; and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. [9:91] Nor upon those who, when they came to you that you might carry them [9:92].' He said: 'So it was lifted from them because they do not find (the means).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Thabit ibn Sa'id who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Thabit! What have you to do with the people? Refrain from the people and do not invite anyone to your matter (al-Wilayah), for, by God, even if the people of the heavens and the people of the earths were to gather together to guide a servant whose straying God intends, they would not have the capability to guide him. And even if the people of the heavens and the people of the earths were to gather to lead astray a servant whose guidance God intends, they would not have the capability to lead him astray. Refrain from the people, and let no one say 'my uncle, my brother, the son of my uncle, and my neighbour', for when God intends good for a servant, He purifies his soul so that he does not hear good except that he recognises it, nor evil except that he rejects it. Then God casts a word into his heart by which He gathers his affair.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — whenever He intends good for a servant, imprints a spot of divine light in his heart, and opens the channels of hearing of his heart, and assigns an angel with him who guides him aright. And whenever He intends evil for a servant, He imprints a black spot in his heart, closes the channels of hearing of his heart, and assigns a devil with him who leads him astray.' Then he recited this verse: 'So whoever God wills to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He wills to lead astray, He makes his chest narrow and straitened, as though he were ascending into the sky.' [6:125]

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Devote your affairs to Allah and do not devote them to the people, for whatever is for Allah is indeed for Allah, and whatever is for the people will not ascend to Allah. And do not dispute with the people over your religion, for indeed disputation is a cause of sickness for the heart. Indeed Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family): [28:56] 'Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.' And He said: [10:99] 'Will you then compel the people until they become believers?' Leave the people, for the people take from the people, and you all take from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He decrees upon a servant that he should enter into this matter (of wilayah), he would be quicker to it than a bird is to its nest.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Should we invite the people to this matter? So he said: No, O Fuzayl! Verily, when God intends good for a servant, He commands an angel who seizes him by his neck and enters him into this matter, willingly or unwillingly.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar al-Hamdani — all of them from al-Fath ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the lowest of recognition. So he said: 'The acknowledgement that there is no god other than Him, and there is no resemblance for Him, and no counterpart, and that He is eternal, affirmed, existent without being absent, and that there is nothing like unto Him.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Tahir ibn Hatim during a state of orthodoxy, that he wrote to the man (the Imam): 'What is it without which the recognition of the Creator would be deficient?' So he wrote to him: '(God) has always been Knowing, Hearing, and Seeing, and He is the Doer of whatever He wills.' And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about that without which the recognition of the Creator would be deficient, so he said: 'Nothing is like Him, nor does anything resemble Him. He has always been Knowing, Hearing, Seeing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Baqqah, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Ibrahim ibn Umar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The matter of God, all of it, is wondrous — except that He has argued against you with what He has already made known to you of Himself.'

Whoever worships God through imagination (mere conjecture) has committed disbelief; and whoever worships the name without the meaning has committed disbelief; and whoever worships the name and the meaning has committed shirk (polytheism). And whoever worships the meaning by applying the names upon Him with His attributes with which He described Himself — so he pacts his heart upon it, and his tongue speaks with it in his private and public life — then those are the true companions of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). And in another narration: those are the true believers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of God and their derivation — from what is 'Allah' derived? He said: So he said to me: 'O Hisham! Allah is derived from ilah (deity), and ilah requires a worshipper (ma'luh). And the name is other than the named. So whoever worships the name without the meaning (reality) has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything; and whoever worships the name and the meaning has disbelieved and worshipped two; and whoever worships the meaning without the name — that is tawhid. Do you understand, O Hisham?' He said: So I said, 'Give me more.' He said: 'Indeed, God has ninety-nine names. If the name were the named, then every one of them would be a deity. But God is a meaning (reality) toward which these names point, and all of them are other than Him. O Hisham! Bread is a name for food, water is a name for the drink, cloth is a name for what is worn, fire is a name for what burns. Do you understand, O Hisham, an understanding with which you can repel and fight our enemies and those who take others alongside God — Majestic and Mighty?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: So he said: 'May God benefit you with it and affirm you, O Hisham.' Hisham said: By God, no one overcame me regarding tawhid until I reached my present station.

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), or said to him: 'May God make me your ransom! We worship the Beneficent, the Merciful, the One, the Singular, the Eternal.' He [the narrator] said: So he [the Imam] said: 'Indeed, whoever worships the Name apart from the One Named by the Names has committed shirk, blasphemed, and denied — and has not worshipped anything at all. Rather, worship God, the One, the Singular, the Eternal, the Named One by these Names — not the Names [themselves]. The Names are attributes by which He described Himself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza who said: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'Inform me about God — when did He exist?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When did He not exist, that I may inform you when He existed? Glory be to the One who never ceased to be and will never cease to be, Singular, the Eternal Refuge, who took neither a female companion nor a son.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said: A man came to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) from beyond the river of Balkh and said, 'I want to ask you a question; if you answer me in accordance with what I have, I shall affirm your Imamate.' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, 'Ask whatever you wish.' The man said, 'Inform me about your Lord — when was He, how was He, and upon what was His support?' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, established the «where» without a «where» for Himself, and established the «how» without a «how» for Himself, and His support was upon His own power.' So the man stood up, kissed his head, and said: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that Ali is the legatee of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), and the custodian after him with what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) stood for, and that you all are the truthful Imams, and that you are the successor after them.'

A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'Inform me about your Lord — when was He?' So he said: 'Woe unto you! The question "when was He" is only said of something that once was not. My Lord, Blessed and Exalted, ever was and never ceased to be living without a "how"; and there cannot be a "was" for Him, nor was there for His existence an occurrence of "how"; nor was there for Him a "where"; nor was He in anything; nor was He upon anything; nor did He create a place for His place; nor did He become powerful after bringing things into existence, nor was He weak before bringing anything into existence; nor was He lonely before He initiated anything; nor does anything mentionable resemble Him; nor was He ever empty of His Kingdom before He created it, nor will He ever be empty of it after its passing. He never ceased to be Living without a life, and a Capable King before He created anything, and a Compelling King after He created the universe. So there is no "how" for His existence, nor a "where" for Him, nor a (defined) limit for Him, nor can He be recognized by anything resembling Him, nor does He grow old due to the prolonged duration of existence, nor is He bewildered by anything — rather, out of fear of Him all things are bewildered. He was Living without a contingent life, without a describable existence, without a limited "how", without a "where" fixed upon Him, without a place neighboring anything. Rather, He is the Living, recognized, and a King — Power and Kingdom have never ceased to belong to Him. He created what He willed when He willed by His Will. He cannot be limited, nor divided, nor annihilated. He was the First without a "how" (qualitative state), and will be the Last without a "where". And everything perishes except His Face; to Him belongs creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds. Woe unto you, O questioner! My Lord — imaginations cannot encompass Him, doubts cannot descend upon Him, He is not confused, nothing transcends Him, nothing new befalls Him, He is not asked about anything, He does not regret anything, neither slumber nor sleep seizes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, who raised it (mursal) and said: The Jews gathered around their chief, al-Jalut, and said to him, 'This man is learned' — meaning Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) — 'so come with us to him that we may question him.' So they came to him, and it was said to them, 'He is in the palace.' So they waited for him until he came out. Then the chief of al-Jalut said to him, 'We came to question you.' So he (Imam Ali) said, 'Ask, O Jew, about whatever comes to you.' So he said, 'I ask you about your Lord — when was He?' He said: 'He was without there being any entities. He was without a how. He has always been without an extent and without a how. He was — there being no before for Him. He is before the before, without a before, and no end-point, and no termination. The end-point is cut off from Him, and He is the end-point of every end-point.' Then the chief of al-Jalut said, 'Let us go, for he is more knowledgeable than what is said about him.'

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mawsili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A rabbi from the rabbis came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, when was your Lord?' So he said to him: 'May your mother be bereft of you! And when was He not, that it could be said when He was? My Lord was before the before, without there being a before; and after the after, without there being an after. There is neither an end-point nor a termination to His end-point — the end-points are cut off before Him, thus He is the termination of every end-point.' Then he said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, are you then a prophet?' He said: 'Woe to you! I am but a servant among the servants of Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).' And it is reported that he (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Where was our Lord before He created the sky and earth?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where is a question about a place, yet God was and there was no place.'

The chief of al-Jalut said to the Jews: 'The Muslims claim that Ali (peace be upon him) is among the most skilled in argumentation and the most knowledgeable of the people. Let us go to him so that I may ask him a question and make him err in it.' So he came to him and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I want to ask you a question.' He said: 'Ask about whatever you wish.' He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, when was our Lord?' He said to him: 'O Jew, it is only said "when was he" about one who did not exist and then came to be. As for when He was — He was existing without there being any entity. He was existing without a "how" coming to be. Yes, O Jew! Then again, yes, O Jew! How can there be a "before" for Him? He is before the "before" without there being an end-point, and no termination of an end-point, nor is there an end-point that leads to it. The end-points cease at His presence. He is the end-point of every end-point.' So he said: 'I testify that your religion is the Truth and that whatever opposes it is false.'

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Was God (existing) and there was nothing?' He said: 'Yes, He was and there was nothing.' I said: 'So where would He be?' He was reclining, then sat upright and said: 'You have asked the impossible, O Zurara, and you inquired about place when there was no place.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mawsili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A rabbi from the rabbis came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, when was your Lord?' He said: Woe to you! "When was it?" is only asked about something that did not exist. But as for that which always was, you cannot say "when was it?" — He was before the "before" without there being a "before," and after the "after" without there being an "after," and there is no end-point of a limit for His limit to reach. Then [the rabbi] said to him: Are you a prophet? He said: For your mother be bereavement! I am but a servant from among the servants of the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Jews asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'Describe for us the lineage of your Lord.' So he waited three (days) without answering them. Then it was revealed: 'Say: He, Allah, is One' — to the end of it. And it was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about 'Say: He, Allah, is One.' So he said: The lineage of Allah to His creation is: One, Everlasting, Eternal, Perpetual — there is no support to hold Him, and He withholds all things by their supports. He recognizes the unknown and is known to every ignorant one. An absolute Singularity — neither are His creatures inside Him, nor is He inside His creatures. He cannot be felt nor discerned; the visions cannot perceive Him. He is High, so He is near; and He is close-by, so He is remote. He is disobeyed, so He forgives; and He is obeyed, so He is grateful. Neither does His earth contain Him, nor do His heavens bear Him. He carries all things by His Power — everlasting, eternal. He neither forgets, nor is distracted, nor makes mistakes, nor acts in vain. There is no delay in His will, and His judgment is recompense, and His command is inevitable. He did not beget, lest He leave an inheritance, and He was not begotten, lest He be shared with, and there was never for Him anyone as an equal.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, who said: He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked about Tawhid, and he said: 'Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — knew that in the end of times there would be peoples who investigate deeply. So God the Exalted revealed "Say: He, Allah, is One" and the verses from Surah al-Hadid up to His words: "and He is All-Knowing of what is in the chests" So whoever seeks beyond that has perished.

I asked al-Reza (peace be upon him) about tawhid (Divine Unity), so he said: 'Whoever recites "Say: He is God, the One" and believes in it, has indeed recognized tawhid.' I said: 'How should one recite it?' He said: 'Just as the people recite it, and add to it: "Thus is God, my Lord; thus is God, my Lord."'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Speak about the creation of God, but do not speak about God Himself; for speaking about God only increases its doer in bewilderment. And in another narration from Hariz: Speak about everything, but do not speak about the Essence of God.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And that to your Lord is the ending" (53:42) So when speech (discussion) reaches God (His Essence), hold back (and stop there).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! People will not cease to engage in discourse until they speak about God. So when you hear that, say: There is no god except God, the One, Who there is nothing like unto Him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha' who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ziyad! Beware of disputes, for they beget doubt, bring down one's deeds, and ruin the one who engages in them; and perhaps he may say something and not be forgiven for it. Indeed, in the past there were a people who abandoned the knowledge they were entrusted with and sought knowledge they were relieved of, until their discourse reached [the subject of] God and they became confused — to the extent that the man would be called from in front of him and he would answer from behind him, and he would be called from behind him and he would answer from in front of him. And in another report: 'until they wandered in the earth.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mayyah, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever speculates about Allah — how He is — is destroyed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'A king of great splendour was in a gathering of his, and he discussed the Lord, Blessed and Exalted. So he disappeared, and it is not even known where he is.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'Beware of speculating about God. But whenever you wish to look upon His Magnificence, then look upon the magnificence of His creation.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah reported with an elevated chain (mursal), saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O son of Adam! If a bird were to eat your heart, it would not be satiated by it, and if the eye of a needle were placed upon your eye, it would cover it. Do you intend with these two to recognise the kingdom of the heavens and the earth? If you are truthful, then here is the sun — a creation from the creations of God. So if you are able to fill your eyes from it, then it is as you say.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Ya'qubi, from some of his companions, from Abd al-A'la, the client of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man from the Jews named Sibakht came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have come to ask you about your Lord. Tell me, where is He? He (peace be upon him) said: He is in every place, yet He is not in any place. He said: Then how is He? He said: And how should I describe my Lord with kayfiyya, when kayfiyya itself is a creation, and Allah cannot be described through His creation? Then he said to him: What is the proof of Him? Then the stones upon which [the man] was sitting — nine of them — moved, and they spoke in a clear Arabic tongue: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Then they returned to their place. So Sibakht said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about something from the (divine) attributes. So he raised his hand toward the sky, then said: Exalted is the Compeller! Exalted is the Compeller! Whoever ventures into what is there (beyond) is destroyed.

I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) asking him: How does a servant worship his Lord when he cannot see Him? So he (peace be upon him) signed: O Abu Yusuf! My Chief, my Master, and the Bestower of blessings upon me and upon my forefathers is too Majestic to be seen. He said: And I asked him whether the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) had seen his Lord. So he (peace be upon him) signed: Indeed God, the Blessed and Exalted, caused His Messenger to see, through his heart, from the light of His Magnificence, what He willed.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: Abu Qurra the hadith narrator asked me to bring him to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him). So I sought permission for that, and he gave me permission. So he entered upon him and asked him about the permissible and the forbidden and the rulings, until his questioning reached tawhid. So Abu Qurra said: We have been narrated that God distributed the Vision and the Speech between two prophets: He distributed the Speech to Moses and the Vision to Muhammad. So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Who then is the one who conveyed from God to the two communities of jinn and humans that visions cannot comprehend Him [6:103], and they do not encompass Him in knowledge [20:110], and nothing is like Him [42:11]? Was it not Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: How can a man come to all creation and inform them that he came from God and that he is calling them to God by God's command, saying visions cannot comprehend Him, and they do not encompass Him in knowledge, and nothing is like Him, then say: I saw Him with my own eyes and encompassed Him in knowledge and He is in the form of a human? Are you not ashamed? The atheists could not have cast upon him this accusation that he came from God with something, then came with its opposite from another direction. Abu Qurra said: But He says: And certainly he saw it at another descent [53:13]. So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: After this verse is what indicates what he saw, where He says: The heart did not lie about what it saw [53:11] — He is saying the heart of Muhammad did not lie about what his two eyes saw. Then He informed of what he saw, saying: He saw of the greatest signs of his Lord [53:18]. The signs of God are other than God. And God has said: And they do not encompass Him in knowledge [20:110]. So if the visions were to see Him, they would have encompassed Him in knowledge, and recognition would have occurred. So Abu Qurra said: So you deny the narrations? So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: When narrations are in opposition to the Quran, I deny them, and the Muslims have formed consensus that He cannot be encompassed in knowledge, and visions cannot comprehend Him, and nothing is like Him.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about the sighting (of God) and what is reported by the general (Sunni) Muslims and the specific ones (Shias), and I asked him to explain that to me. So he wrote in his own handwriting: All have agreed, without dispute among them, that knowledge from the aspect of sighting is self-evident. So if it were permitted that God be seen with the eye, such knowledge would occur necessarily. Then that knowledge would not be free from either being iman (faith) or not being iman. If that knowledge from the aspect of sighting were iman, then the knowledge in this world acquired through attainment would not be iman, because it is its opposite — so there would be no believer in this world, since they have not seen God, Mighty is His mention. And if that knowledge from the aspect of sighting is not iman, then this knowledge acquired through attainment would not be free from diminishing in this world and not diminishing in the Hereafter. So this is evidence that God, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be seen with the eye, since the eye leads to what we have described.

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him), asking him about the vision (of God) and what the people differ about regarding it. So he wrote: The sighting is not possible unless there is air between the seer and the seen that the sight does not penetrate through. So when the air is cut off from between the seer and the seen, the sighting is not valid, and there would be confusion in that. Because whenever the seer equals the seen in the necessitating condition between them for vision, the confusion becomes obligatory, and that would be anthropomorphism (tashbih), because causes must inevitably be connected to their effects.

I was present with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when a man from the Kharijites entered upon him and said to him: 'O Abu Ja'far! What do you worship?' He said: 'Allah the Exalted.' He said: 'Have you seen Him?' He said: 'Rather, the eyes do not see Him through direct beholding of sight, but the hearts see Him through the realities of faith. He cannot be known by analogy, nor grasped by the senses, nor likened to people. He is described through the verses [of the Quran], recognized through the signs. He is not unjust in His judgment. That is Allah — there is no god except Him.' He (the narrator) said: The man left while saying: 'Allah knows best where He places His Message.' [6:124]

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mawsili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A rabbi came to the Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! Did you see your Lord when you worshipped Him?' He said, then he (the Imam) said: 'Woe to you! I have never worshipped a Lord I did not see.' He said: 'And how did you see Him?' He said: 'Woe to you! The eyes do not perceive Him through the witnessing of physical sight, but the hearts see Him through the realities of faith.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I brought up with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) the matter of what they narrate regarding the sighting [of God]. So he said: The sun is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Footstool (al-Kursi), and the Footstool is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Throne (al-Arsh), and the Throne is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Veil, and the Veil is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Curtain. So if they were truthful, then let them fill their eyes from the sun when there is no cloud beneath it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'When I was taken on the night journey to the heaven, Gabriel brought me to a place which Gabriel had never trodden upon before. So it was unveiled to him, and God showed him — from the light of His magnificence — what He willed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding His words 'Visions cannot comprehend Him' [6:103] He said: 'It means the grasping of the imagination. Do you not see His words: 'There has come to you Insight from your Lord' [6:104] It does not mean the sight of the eyes. 'Whoever therefore sees, it is for his own soul' — it does not mean seeing with his physical eye. 'And whoever is blind, it shall be against himself' — it does not mean the blindness of the eyes. Rather, He meant the grasping of the imagination, just as it is said: so and so has insight in poetry, and so and so has insight in jurisprudence, and so and so has insight in Dirhams, and so and so has insight in clothes. God is more magnificent than that He should be seen with the eye.'

I asked him about God — can He be described? So he said: 'Do you not read the Quran?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you not read His saying, the Exalted: "Visions cannot comprehend Him, and He comprehends (all) visions" [6:103]?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'So do you recognize the visions?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What are they?' I said: 'Visions of the eyes.' So he said: 'Indeed, the imaginations of the hearts are greater than the visions of the eyes. So He is such that the imaginations cannot comprehend Him, and He comprehends the imaginations.'

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Visions cannot comprehend Him, and He comprehends (all) visions' [6:103]. So he said: 'O Abu Hashim! The imaginations of hearts are more subtle than the visions of eyes. You can reach by your imagination al-Sind, al-Hind, and lands you have never entered and do not perceive with your sight — and yet the imaginations of hearts cannot comprehend Him. So how then could the visions of eyes?'

All things cannot be comprehended except through two means: through the senses and the heart. The senses comprehend through three modes: comprehension by penetration, comprehension by contact, and comprehension without penetration or contact. As for comprehension by penetration, these are sounds, smells, and tastes. As for comprehension by contact, these are the recognition of shapes such as the square and the triangle, and recognition of softness and roughness, heat and cold. As for comprehension without contact or penetration, this is vision — for it perceives things without contact or penetration in any space other than its own, nor in its own space. The comprehension of vision has a medium and a cause: its medium is the air and its cause is light. When the medium is continuous between it and the object seen, and the cause is present, one perceives what one faces of colours and figures. But when vision is directed at something for which there is no medium, it returns and reflects what is behind it — like a person looking in a mirror, whose vision does not pass through the mirror. When there is no medium for it, it returns and reflects what is behind it. Similarly, one who looks into clear water returns and reflects what is behind it, since there is no medium for the penetration of sight. As for the heart, its domain is over the atmosphere (al-hawa'); it comprehends all that is in the atmosphere and imagines it. When the heart is directed at what does not exist in the atmosphere, it returns and reflects what is in the atmosphere. Therefore, it is not fitting for an intelligent person to direct his heart toward what does not exist in the atmosphere regarding the matter of Divine Unity (tawhid) — Mighty and Majestic is God — for if he does so, he will only imagine what exists in the atmosphere, just as we have described regarding vision. Exalted is God above any resemblance to His creation.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, compiler of this book — may God have mercy on him — said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Abbas ibn Umar al-Fuqaymi, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said to the atheist who had asked him, 'From where do you prove the prophets and messengers?' He said: 'When we established that we have a Creator, a Maker, Exalted above us and above all that He created, and that this Maker was Wise and Transcendent — so that His creatures cannot behold Him nor touch Him, and He cannot deal with them directly nor they with Him, and He cannot argue with them directly nor they with Him — it is established that He has ambassadors among His creation who convey on His behalf to His creation and His servants, guiding them toward their interests and benefits and that by which they endure, while its neglect means their destruction. Thus it is established that there are those who command and forbid on behalf of the Wise, the All-knowing, among His creation, who convey from Him — Majestic and Mighty — and they are the prophets (peace be upon them) and His chosen elites from His creation: wise ones disciplined with wisdom, sent with it, yet without sharing in anything of the conditions of the people despite their commonality with them in creation and composition, supported by the Wise, the All-knowing with wisdom. Then this has been established in every era and time through what the messengers and prophets have brought of proofs and demonstrations, so that God's earth shall not be devoid of a divine authority who possesses knowledge indicating the truthfulness of his claim and the validity of his justice.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Verily God is more exalted and more noble than to be known through His creatures; rather, the creatures are known through God.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth.' I said: 'Whoever recognizes that he has a Lord, it is befitting for him to recognize that for that Lord there is pleasure and wrath, and that His pleasure and His wrath cannot be known except through revelation or a messenger. So whoever does not receive revelation, it is befitting for him to seek the messengers, and when he meets them he recognizes that they are the Divine Authority and that obedience to them is obligatory.' And I said to the people: 'Do you know that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was the Divine Authority from God over His creatures?' They said: 'Yes.' I said: 'So when the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) passed away, who was the Divine Authority over His creatures?' So they said: 'The Quran.' So I looked into the Quran and found that the Murji'ite, and the Qadariyya, and the atheist who does not believe in it all dispute using it, to the point of overpowering men through argumentation. So I recognized that the Quran cannot serve as a Divine Authority except with a custodian, and whatever he says concerning it would be true. So I said to them: 'Who is the custodian of the Quran?' They said: 'Ibn Mas'ud had some knowledge, and Umar had some knowledge, and Hudhayfa had some knowledge.' I said: 'All of it?' They said: 'No.' So I found no one who could be said to know all of it except Ali (peace be upon him). And when a matter arose among the people, this one said 'I don't know', and this one said 'I don't know', and this one said 'I don't know', but this one said 'I do know.' So I testify that Ali (peace be upon him) was the custodian of the Quran, and obedience to him was obligatory, and he was the Divine Authority over the people after the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), and that whatever he said regarding the Quran is the truth.' So he (the Imam) said: 'May God have mercy on you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim, from Yunus ibn Yaqub who said: There was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a group of his companions, among them Humran ibn Ayn, Muhammad ibn al-Numan, Hisham ibn Salim, and al-Tayyar, and (another) group among whom was Hisham ibn al-Hakam, and he was a young man. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hisham! Will you not inform me how you dealt with Amr ibn Ubayd and how you questioned him?' So Hisham said: 'O son of the Messenger of God! I hold you in too much reverence and am too embarrassed before you, and my tongue does not function in your presence.' So Abu Abdillah said: 'When I command you with something, then do it.' Hisham said: 'It had reached me what Amr ibn Ubayd was doing and his sitting in the mosque of Basra, and this weighed heavily upon me. So I went out to him and entered Basra on Friday. I then came to the mosque of Basra, and there I found a large circle in which was Amr ibn Ubayd, wearing a black woolen garment he had wrapped around as a lower garment and another he had wrapped around as an upper garment, and the people were questioning him. So I parted the people and they made way for me, then I sat at the back of the gathering upon my knees.' Then I said: O Scholar! I am a stranger; will you permit me to pose a question? He said to me: Yes. So I said to him: Do you have an eye? He said: O my son! What kind of question is this — it is something you can see; how do you ask about it? So I said: This is my question. He said: O my son, ask, even if your question is foolish. I said: Answer me about it. He said to me: Ask. I said: Do you have an eye? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I see colours and forms with it. I said: Do you have a nose? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I smell fragrances with it. I said: Do you have a mouth? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I taste food with it. I said: Do you have an ear? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I hear sounds with it. I said: Do you have a heart? He said: Yes. I said: What do you do with it? He said: I discern by it everything that comes to these bodily organs and senses. I said: Are these bodily organs not sufficient without the heart? He said: No. I said: How is that, when they are sound and healthy? He said: O my son!

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from the one he mentioned, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the people of Syria came to him and said: 'I am a man versed in theology (kalam), jurisprudence, and the laws of inheritance, and I have come to debate with your companions.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is your speech from the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), or from yourself?' He said: 'From the words of the Messenger of God and from myself.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Then you are a partner of the Messenger of God.' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you have heard the revelation from God, the Mighty and Majestic, informing you?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Is obedience to you then obligatory just as obedience to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is obligatory?' He said: 'No.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) turned toward me and said: 'O Yunus ibn Yaqub! This one has already defeated himself before he even spoke.' Then he said: 'O Yunus! If you were skilled in theological debate, you would have spoken to him.' Yunus said: 'Alas, what a cause for regret!' I said: 'May I be your ransom! I heard you forbidding theological disputation and saying: Woe upon the companions of kalam who say: this is logically consistent and this is not, and this follows and this does not, and this we understand and this we do not.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I only said: Woe upon them if they abandon what I say and go toward what they desire.' Then he said to me: 'Go out to the door and look at whoever you see from the theologians and bring him in.' He said: So I brought in Humran ibn Ayn, and he was skilled in theological speech, and I brought in al-Ahwal, and he was skilled in theological speech, and I brought in Hisham ibn Salim, and he was skilled in theological speech, and I brought in Qays ibn al-Masir — and in my estimation he was the best of them in theological speech — and he had learned the discipline of kalam from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him). When the gathering had settled and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — who before the Hajj season used to settle for some days in a mountain at the edge of the sacred precinct in a tent pitched for him — brought his head out of his tent, there was a camel trotting. He said:

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, who said: Al-Ahwal informed me that Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) sent for him while he was in concealment. He said: So I went to him and he said to me, 'O Abu Ja'far! What do you say — if a comer from among us comes to you, would you go out with him?' So I said to him, 'If it were your father or your uncle, I would go out with him.' He said, 'I intend to go out and fight these people, so come out with me.' I said, 'No, I would not do so, may I be your ransom.' He said, 'Are you placing your own self above mine?' I said to him, 'It is but one soul. If there is a Divine Authority (Hujja) for God on earth, then the one who stays behind from you is saved and the one who goes out with you is destroyed. And if there is no Divine Authority for God on earth, then the one who stays behind from you and the one who goes out with you are equal.' He said, 'O Abu Ja'far! I used to sit with my father at the dining table, and he would feed me the choicest morsels and cool the hot food for me until it cooled, out of compassion for me — yet he did not protect me from the heat of the Fire by informing you of the Religion and not informing me of it?' I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! It was out of his compassion for you from the heat of the Fire that he did not inform you — he feared for you lest you not accept it and thus enter the Fire. But he informed me: if I accept, I am saved; and if I do not accept, he would not care if I enter the Fire.' Then I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! Are you more virtuous, or the Prophets?' He said, 'Rather, the Prophets.' I said, 'Ya'qub said to Yusuf [12:5]: "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot a plot against you." Why did he not inform them so that they would not plot against him? Rather he concealed that from them. So likewise did your father conceal from you, for he feared for you.' He said, 'But by God! If you say that — your companion (the Imam) had already told me in Medina that I would be killed and crucified at al-Kunasa, and that in his possession is a scroll in which is written my killing and my crucifixion.' Then I performed Hajj and narrated to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) the words of Zayd and what I had said to him. So he said to me: 'You took him from in front of him and f
I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'and for every people is a guide' [13:7] So he said: 'Every Imam is a guide for the generation he is among.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Bureyd al-Ijali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'But rather, you are only a warner, and for every people is a guide' [Quran 13:7] So he said: 'The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) is the warner, and for every era there is a guide from us who guides them to what the Prophet of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) came with. Then the guides after him — Ali, then the successors, one after another.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, you are only a warner, and for every people is a guide' [13:7]. So he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the warner, and Ali is the guide.' O Abu Muhammad! Is there a guide today? I said: Yes, may I be your sacrifice! There has not ceased to be from among you a guide after a guide until it was handed over to you. So he said: May God have mercy on you, O Abu Muhammad! Had it been so that a verse was revealed to a man, then that man died, the verse would die, the Book would die. But it is living; it flows among those who remain just as it flowed among those who have passed.

...of God, Blessed and Exalted — Indeed, you are only a warner, and for every people is a guide [Quran 13:7]. So he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the warner and Ali is the guide. But, by God, it did not cease to be from us, and will not cease to be among us until the Hour.'

Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh Abū al-Ḥasan, Ṣāḥib al-Daylam, narrated to us; he said: I heard Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام saying, while there were some people from the people of al-Kūfah in his presence: How astonishing concerning the people: they took all of their knowledge from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, then acted by it and were guided, yet they think that the people of his Household did not take his knowledge—while we are the people of his Household and his progeny. In our homes the Revelation descended, and from us knowledge went out to them. Do they then think that they came to know and were guided, while we remained ignorant and went astray? Indeed, this is impossible.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Sabbah al-Muzani, from al-Harith ibn Husayrah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, who said: A man met al-Husayn ibn Ali عليه السلام at al-Tha'labiyyah while he was heading toward Karbala. He came to him and greeted him with salām. So al-Husayn عليه السلام said to him: “From which land are you?” He said: “From the people of al-Kufah.” He said: “Indeed, by Allah, O brother of the people of al-Kufah, had I met you in al-Madinah, I would have shown you the trace of Jibra'il عليه السلام in our house, and his descent with the revelation upon my grandfather. O brother of the people of al-Kufah, is it that the people drew knowledge from us and then they came to know while we remained ignorant? This is not something that can be.”

Ali Bin Ibrahim Bin Hashim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) saying: “There is no truth with anyone among the people, nor correctness, and no one among the people judges with a true judgment except that which came out from us, Ahl al-Bayt. And when matters become branched and confused for them, the error is from them and the correctness is from ‘Ali (عليه السلام).”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Muthannā, from Zurārah, who said: I was in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and a man from the people of al-Kūfah said to him, asking him about the saying of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام: “Ask me whatever you wish, for you will not ask me about anything except that I will inform you of it.” He عليه السلام said: “There is no one who possesses knowledge of anything except that it came forth from the presence of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. So let the people go wherever they wish, for by Allah, the matter is only from here,” and he gestured with his hand toward his house.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Abī Maryam, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to Salamah ibn Kuhayl and Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah: “Go east and west, and you will not find any sound knowledge except something that has come forth from us, Ahl al-Bayt.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from Muʿallā ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: He عليه السلام said to me: “Indeed, al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah is among those about whom Allah said:” “And among the people are those who say: We believe in Allah and in the Last Day, while they are not believers.” So let al-Ḥakam go east and go west. Indeed, by Allah, he will not attain the knowledge except from a Household upon whom Jibrāʾīl descended.
