ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about the testimony of the child of zina: “Is it valid?” He said: “No.” So I said: “Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah claims that it is valid.” He said: “O Allah, do not forgive his sin.” Allah did not say to al-Ḥakam: “Indeed, it is surely a reminder for you and your people.” So let al-Ḥakam go right and left; for by Allah, knowledge is not taken except from a Household upon whom Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) descended.

A number of our companions, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan ibn Yazid, from Badr, from his father, who said: Sallam Abu Ali Al-Khurasani narrated to me, from Sallam ibn Sa'id Al-Makhzumi, who said: While I was sitting in the presence of Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), there entered upon him 'Abbad ibn Kathir, the devotee of the people of Al-Basra, and Ibn Shurayh, the jurist of the people of Makkah; and with Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) was Maymun Al-Qaddah, the mawla of Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام). 'Abbad ibn Kathir asked him and said: 'O Abu 'Abdillah, in how many garments was Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) shrouded?' He said: 'In three garments: two Suhari garments and one Hibarah garment, and there was scarcity regarding al-burd.' It was as though 'Abbad ibn Kathir turned away in disapproval at that, so Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) said: 'Indeed, the palm tree of Maryam (عليها السلام) was only 'ajwah, and it descended from the heaven. So whatever grew from its root was 'ajwah, and whatever was from scattered pickings, then it is a mixed color.' So when they left his presence, 'Abbad ibn Kathir said to Ibn Shurayh: 'By Allah, I do not know what this parable was that Abu 'Abdillah gave me.' Ibn Shurayh said: 'This young man will inform you, for he is from them'—meaning Maymun. So he asked him, and Maymun said: 'Do you not know what he said to you?' He said: 'No, by Allah.' He said: 'He gave you a parable of himself, informing you that he is a descendant from the descendants of Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and the knowledge of Rasul Allah is with them. So whatever comes from them is correct, and whatever comes from other than them is mere gleanings.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Jabir, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, the hadith of the family of Muhammad is difficult and deemed very difficult. None believes in it except an angel brought near, or a prophet sent forth, or a servant whose heart Allah has tested for faith.” So whatever comes to you from the hadith of the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and your hearts soften toward it and you recognize it, then accept it. And whatever your hearts recoil from and you deny, then refer it back to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the knowledgeable one from the family of Muhammad. Rather, the ruined one is he to whom something from it is related which he cannot bear, so he says: ‘By Allah, this was not so; by Allah, this was not so.’ And denial is disbelief.

Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from ʿImrān ibn Mūsā, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Taqiyyah was mentioned one day in the presence of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), so he said: “By Allah, if Abū Dharr knew what was in the heart of Salmān, he would have killed him, while the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) had indeed established brotherhood between them.” So what do you think of the rest of creation? Indeed, the knowledge of the scholars is difficult, exceedingly difficult; none can bear it except a sent Prophet, or a brought-near angel, or a believing servant whose heart Allah has tested for faith.” Then he said: “Salmān only became one of the scholars because he is a man from us, Ahl al-Bayt; therefore, for that reason, I have attributed him to the scholars.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Sinān or someone else, who raised it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, our hadith is difficult, made difficult; none can bear it except enlightened breasts, or sound hearts, or good morals. Indeed, Allah took the covenant from our Shiʿah just as He took it from the children of Ādam: Am I not your Lord? So whoever is faithful to us, Allah will fulfill for him with Paradise; and whoever hates us and does not render our right to us, then he will be in the Fire, abiding forever.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and others, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from some of our companions, who said: I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan Ṣāḥib al-ʿAskar (عليه السلام): May I be made your ransom, what is the meaning of the saying of al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام), ‘Our hadith cannot be borne by a brought-near angel, nor by a sent prophet, nor by a believer whose heart Allah has tested for faith’? So the reply came: The meaning of the saying of al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام), that neither an angel nor a prophet nor a believer can bear it, is that the angel cannot bear it until he conveys it to another angel, and the prophet cannot bear it until he conveys it to another prophet, and the believer cannot bear it until he conveys it to another believer. So this is the meaning of the saying of my grandfather (عليه السلام).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Mansur ibn al-'Abbas, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq and Abu Basir, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “O Abu Muhammad, with us, by Allah, is a secret from the secret of Allah, and knowledge from the knowledge of Allah. By Allah, neither a near-stationed angel can bear it, nor a sent prophet, nor a believer whose heart Allah has tested for faith. By Allah, Allah has not charged anyone with that other than us, nor has He taken anyone into servitude by that other than us.” “Indeed, with us is a secret from the secret of Allah and knowledge from the knowledge of Allah. Allah commanded us to convey it, so we conveyed from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, what He commanded us to convey. But we found for it no place, no people, and no bearers who could bear it, until Allah created for that a people who were created from a clay from which Muhammad and his family and his offspring عليهم السلام were created, and from a light from which Allah created Muhammad and his offspring, and He fashioned them by the فضل of His mercy from which He fashioned Muhammad and his offspring.” “So we conveyed from Allah what He commanded us to convey, and they accepted it and bore that. Then that reached them from us, and they accepted it and bore it. And our mention reached them, so their hearts inclined toward our recognition and our hadith. Had they not been created from this, they would not have been like that. No, by Allah, they would not have borne it.” “Then he said: Indeed, Allah created a people for Jahannam and the Fire, so He commanded us to convey to them just as we conveyed to those others. But they recoiled from that, their hearts shrank away, they rejected it back upon us, they did not bear it, they denied it, and they said: ‘A lying sorcerer.’ So Allah sealed their hearts and made them forget that. Then Allah released their tongues with some of the truth, so they speak it while their hearts deny, so that this may serve as a defense for His awliya' and the people of His obedience.” “And were it not for that, Allah would not be worshipped in His earth. So He commanded us to refrain from them, and to veil and conceal. Therefore conceal from the one concerning whom Allah commanded refraining, and veil from the one concerning whom Allah commanded veiling and conceal

Masjid al-Khayf. So he said: “May Allah brighten a servant who hears my statement, then comprehends it, preserves it, and conveys it to one who did not hear it. For perhaps a bearer of fiqh is not himself a faqih, and perhaps a bearer of fiqh conveys it to one who is more understanding than him.” There are three things concerning which the heart of a Muslim man does not act treacherously: sincerity of action for Allah, sincere counsel toward the Imams of the Muslims, and adherence to their community, for their call encompasses those behind them. The Muslims are brothers; their blood is equal, and the least of them may uphold their covenant. And it was also narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abān, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, similarly; and it adds: “and they are one hand against those besides them.” And he mentioned in his hadith that he delivered the sermon during the Farewell Hajj at Minā in Masjid al-Khayf.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from some of our companions, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from a man of Quraysh from the people of Makkah, who said: Sufyān al-Thawrī said, "Take us to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad." He said: So I went with him to him, and we found him having mounted his animal. Sufyān said to him, "O Abū ʿAbdillāh, narrate to us the hadith of the sermon of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in Masjid al-Khayf." He said, "Leave me until I go for my need, for I have already mounted; when I return, I will narrate it to you." So he said, "I ask you by your kinship to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that you narrate it to me now." He said: So he dismounted, and Sufyān said to him, "Order for me an inkpot and paper so that I may record it." So he called for it. Then he said, "Write: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. The sermon of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in Masjid al-Khayf: May Allah brighten a servant who hears my statement, retains it, and conveys it to one whom it did not reach. O people, let the present convey to the absent. For perhaps a carrier of fiqh is not himself a faqīh, and perhaps a carrier of fiqh conveys it to one more understanding than he. Three things are such that the heart of a Muslim man does not act treacherously toward them: sincerity of action for Allah, giving sincere counsel to the Imams of the Muslims, and adherence to their جماعت, for their call encompasses those behind them. The believers are brothers; their blood is equal, and they are one hand against those besides them; the least of them may undertake their covenant." So Sufyān wrote it, then presented it to him, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام mounted. Sufyān and I departed, and when we were on part of the road, he said to me, "Stay where you are until I examine this hadith." So I said to him, "By Allah, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام has bound something upon your neck that will never leave your neck, ever." He said, "And what is that?" I said to him, "Three things toward which the heart of a Muslim man does not act treacherously: sincerity of action for Allah—we know that. But as for giving sincere counsel to the Imams of the Muslims, who are these Imams whose sincere counsel is obligatory upon us? Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, and everyone whose testimony is not admissibl

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not look upon a friend devoted to Him who strives himself in obedience to his Imam and in sincere counsel, except that he will be with us in the Highest Company.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever separates from the community of the Muslims by the measure of a handspan has indeed cast off the bond of Islam from his neck.

And by this chain, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever separates from the community of the Muslims and breaks the pledge to the Imam عليه السلام will come to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mutilated.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Ḥamzah, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, 'What is the right of the Imam upon the people?' He said: 'His right upon them is that they listen to him and obey him.' I said, 'Then what is their right upon him?' He said: 'That he distribute among them equally and act justly regarding the subjects. So when that is present among the people, he does not mind who takes here and there.'

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: similar to it. Except that he عليه السلام said: ‘Like this, and like this, and like this, and like this’—meaning from before him, and behind him, and from his right, and from his left.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār, from some of our companions, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Do not betray your leaders, and do not deceive your guides, and do not be ignorant of your Imams عليهم السلام, and do not split away from your bond, lest you fail and your strength depart. Upon this, let the foundation of your affairs be, and adhere to this path. For if you were to behold what those of you who have died have beheld—those who opposed that to which you are being called—you would hasten, come forth, and listen. But what they have seen is veiled from you, and soon the veil will be cast aside.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād and another, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr al-Ṣayrafī, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: The Prophet's (صلى الله عليه وآله) own soul was announced to him, while he was sound and had no pain. He said: The Trustworthy Spirit descended with it. He said: So he (صلى الله عليه وآله) called for the salat (prayer) to gather the people, and ordered the Muhājirīn and the Anṣār to come with weapons, and the people assembled. Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) ascended the pulpit and announced his own death to them. Then he said: I adjure by Allah the ruler over my community after me: that he be merciful to the body of the Muslims, honor their elder, show mercy to their weak, and respect their scholar; that he not harm them so as to humiliate them, nor impoverish them so as to lead them to disbelief, nor close his door to them so that their strong would consume their weak, and that he not keep them away in their military expeditions so that the progeny of my community would be cut off. Then he said: I have conveyed and sincerely advised, so bear witness. And Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: This was the last speech that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) spoke upon his pulpit.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī and another, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from a man, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, who said: Honey and figs from Hamdān and Ḥulwān came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. He ordered the officials to bring the orphans, and he enabled them at the tops of the vessels to lick from them, while he was distributing it to the people cup by cup. Then it was said to him, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why are they licking it?” He said, “Indeed, the Imam is the father of the orphans, and I only let them lick this out of the care of fathers.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, together from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Aṣbahānī, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: I am closer to every believer than his own self, and ʿAlī is closer to him after me. So it was said to him: What is the meaning of that? He said: It is the saying of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله): Whoever leaves behind a debt or dependents in loss, then it is upon me; and whoever leaves behind wealth, then it belongs to his heirs. So a man has no authority over himself when he has no wealth, and he has no command or prohibition over his dependents when he does not provide maintenance for them. And the Prophet, Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), and those after them bound themselves to this. From there, they became closer to them than their own selves. The reason for the Islam of the generality of the Jews was only after this statement from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and they felt secure for themselves and for their dependents.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ṣabbāḥ ibn Sayyābah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: Whichever muʾmin or Muslim dies and leaves a debt that was not incurred in corruption nor extravagance, then it is upon the Imam to discharge it. If he does not discharge it, then the sin of that is upon him. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: “The charities are only for the poor and the needy...” — the verse. So he is among the debtors, and he has a share with the Imam. If he withholds it, then its sin is upon him.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥannān, from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Rasūl Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said: “The Imamate is not suitable except for a man in whom there are three qualities: waraʿ restraining him from acts of disobedience to Allah, and forbearance by which he controls his anger, and good wilayah over those whom he governs, until he is to them like a merciful father.” And in another narration: “Until he is to the subjects like a merciful father.”

Muʿāwiyah said: “And after that I met al-Ṭabarī, Muḥammad, and he informed me, saying: ‘I heard ʿAlī ibn Mūsā (عليه السلام) saying...’” “The indebted person, when he incurs a debt or borrows concerning a rightful obligation”—the uncertainty is from Muʿāwiyah—“is to be granted a delay of one year. Then if his circumstances become ample, otherwise the Imam (عليه السلام) pays it on his behalf from Bayt al-Māl.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: We found in the Book of Ali عليه السلام: Surely the earth belongs to Allah; He causes whomever He wills from His servants to inherit it, and the end is for the God-conscious. I and the People of my Household are those whom Allah caused to inherit the earth, and we are the God-conscious, and the whole earth belongs to us. So whoever among the Muslims revives a land, let him cultivate it, and let him pay its land-tax to the Imam from the People of my Household, and he may keep what he consumes from it. Then if he abandons it or ruins it, and another man from the Muslims takes it after him and cultivates it and revives it, then he has more right to it than the one who abandoned it. He is to pay its land-tax to the Imam from the People of my Household, and he may keep what he consumes from it, until al-Qa'im from the People of my Household appears with the sword. Then he will take possession of it, withhold it, and expel them from it, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did take possession of it and withhold it, except for what is in the hands of our Shi'a; for he will make an arrangement with them regarding what is in their hands, and he will leave the land in their hands.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh informed me, from the one who narrated it, who said: The world and whatever is in it belong to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and to His Messenger, and to us. So whoever gains control over anything from it, let him have taqwa of Allah, and let him render the right of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and let him act righteously toward his brothers. If he does not do that, then Allah, His Messenger, and we are disassociated from him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I saw Mismāʿ in al-Madinah, and he had carried wealth to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that year, but Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام returned it. So I said to him, “Why did Abū ʿAbdillāh return to you the wealth that you carried to him?” He said: He said to me, “I said to him when I carried the wealth to him: I had been appointed over pearl-diving in al-Baḥrayn, and I obtained four hundred thousand dirhams. I have come to you with its khums, eighty thousand dirhams, and I disliked withholding it from you or exposing it [to loss], while it is your right which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed in our wealth.” So he said: “Is there for us, from the land and what Allah brings forth from it, only the khums? O Abū Sayyār, surely all the earth belongs to us, so whatever Allah brings forth from it of anything, it is ours.” I said to him, “Then I should carry all of the wealth to you?” He said: “O Abū Sayyār, we have made it wholesome for you and permitted you regarding it. So keep your wealth with you. And everything of the land that is in the hands of our Shiʿah is lawful for them until our Qāʾim rises.” Then he will collect from them the levy of what was in their hands, and he will leave the land in their hands. But as for what is in the hands of others, their earnings from the land are haram for them until our Qāʾim rises, whereupon he will take the land from their hands and expel them in humiliation. ʿUmar ibn Yazid said: Then Abū Sayyār said to me, “I do not regard anyone among the owners of estates, nor those who administer official functions, as consuming what is halal besides me, except one for whom they have made that lawful.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: “Is there zakat upon the Imam?” So he عليه السلام said: “You have spoken of an impossibility, O Abu Muhammad. Do you not know that the world and the Hereafter belong to the Imam? He places it wherever he wills and gives it to whomever he wills. That is permissible for him from Allah. Indeed, the Imam, O Abu Muhammad, never passes a night at all except that there is in his neck a right of Allah about which He will question him.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥamzah, from Abān ibn Muṣʿab, from Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān, or al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, “What do you have from this earth?” So he smiled, then said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام and commanded him to split open eight rivers in the earth with his big toe. Among them are Sayḥān and Jayḥān, and it is the river of Balkh, and al-Khushūʿ, and it is the river of al-Shāsh, and Mihrān, and it is the river of India, and the Nile of Egypt, and the Tigris, and the Euphrates. So whatever these water, or from which water is drawn, is for us; and whatever is for us is for our Shiʿah. And our enemy has no share in it except what he has usurped from it. And indeed our friend is surely in a far more expansive domain in what lies between this and this,” meaning between the heaven and the earth. Then he recited this verse: “Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world—usurped from them—while they shall be exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection, without usurpation.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Rayyān, who said: I wrote to al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom. It has been narrated to us that there is nothing of the world for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله except al-khums.” So the reply came: “Indeed, the world and whatever is upon it belongs to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah created Adam and granted him the world as an allotted domain. So whatever belonged to Adam (عليه السلام) belongs to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and whatever belonged to the Messenger of Allah belongs to the Imams from the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, all together from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام dug five rivers with his foot, and the tongue of the water followed him: the Euphrates, the Tigris, the Nile of Egypt, Mihrān, and the river of Balkh. So whatever they water, or whatever is watered from them, belongs to the Imam, and the sea surrounding the world belongs to the Imam.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad, from Humayd and Jabir al-'Abdi, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah made me an Imam for His creation, so He obligated upon me moderation regarding myself, my food, my drink, and my clothing, like the weak among the people, so that the poor may take my poverty as an example, and the rich may not be driven to transgression by his wealth.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام one day: “May I be sacrificed for you. I mentioned the family of so-and-so and the blessings in which they are, and I said: if this were for you, we would have lived with you.” So he عليه السلام said: “Far from it, O Muʿallā. Indeed, by Allah, if that had been so, it would have been nothing but managing through the night, traveling through the day, wearing coarse clothing, and eating rough food.” So that was kept away from us. Have you ever seen an injustice that Allah, the Exalted, turned into a blessing except this one?”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī Ḥammād, and a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and others, through different chains, concerning: The argumentation of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام against ʿĀṣim ibn Ziyād when he wore the cloak and abandoned the proper garment, and his brother al-Rabīʿ ibn Ziyād complained about him to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, saying that by this he had distressed his family and saddened his children. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Bring ʿĀṣim ibn Ziyād to me.” So he was brought to him, and when he saw him, he frowned at him and said to him: “Are you not ashamed before your family? Have you not shown mercy to your children? Do you think that Allah has made the good things lawful for you, yet He dislikes that you take from them? You are too insignificant before Allah for that.” And does Allah not say: “And the earth, He laid it out for the creatures; therein are fruits and date-palms with sheaths”? And does Allah not say: “He has let loose the two seas meeting together; between them is a barrier they do not transgress” up to His saying: “From them emerge pearl and coral”? So by Allah, making use of the blessings of Allah through action is more beloved to Him than speaking of them merely with words. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: “And as for the blessing of your Lord, then proclaim it.” Then ʿĀṣim said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, then why have you confined yourself in your food to roughness and in your clothing to coarseness?” He said: “Woe to you! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated the Imams of justice to measure themselves by the weaker people, so that the poor man may not be driven to anguish by his poverty.” So ʿĀṣim ibn Ziyād cast off the cloak and wore the proper garment.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said: I was present with Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and a man said to him, “May Allah keep you well. You mentioned that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام) used to wear coarse clothing, and used to wear a shirt for four dirhams and the like of that, while we see new clothing upon you.” So he said to him, “Indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام) used to wear that in a time when it was not objected to in his case. If he were to wear something like that today, he would become known by it. So the best clothing of every age is the clothing of its people, except that our Qāʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt (عليه السلام), when he rises, will wear the garments of ʿAlī (عليه السلام) and proceed according to the conduct of ʿAlī (عليه السلام).”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, who said: He (عليه السلام) sneezed one day while I was with him, so I said, "May I be made your ransom, what is said to the Imam when he sneezes?" He said, "They say: 'May Allah send blessings upon you.'"

Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Dīnawarī narrated to me, from ʿUmar ibn Zāhir, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He said: A man asked him about al-Qāʾim: "Should he be greeted as Amīr al-Muʾminīn?" He said: "No. That is a name by which Allah named Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. No one was named by it before him, and no one after him will name himself by it except a kāfir." I said: "May I be your ransom, then how should one greet him?" He said: "They should say: al-salāmu ʿalayka yā Baqiyyat Allāh." Then he recited: "Baqiyyat Allāh is better for you, if you are believers."

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, “Why was Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام named by this title?” He said, “Because he supplies them with knowledge.” Have you not heard in the Book of Allah: “and we bring provisions for our family”? And in another narration, he said, “Because the provision of the believers comes from him; he supplies them with knowledge.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Qazzāz, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, “Why was he named Amīr al-Muʾminīn?” He said, “Allah named him, and thus did He reveal in His Book:” “And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: Am I not your Lord? And that Muḥammad is My Messenger, and that ʿAlī is Amīr al-Muʾminīn.”

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام used to say: Indeed, Allah took the covenant of our Shi'ah concerning the wilayah while they were particles, on the day when He took the covenant from the particles, and the acknowledgment for Him of Lordship, and for Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله of prophethood.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Jaʿfarī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام; and from ʿUqbah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah created the creatures, so He created what He loved from among what He loved, and what He loved to create, He created from the clay of Paradise. And He created what He hated from among what He hated, and what He hated to create, He created from the clay of the Fire. Then He sent them forth in the shadows. So I said, 'And what are the shadows?' He said, 'Have you not seen your shadow in the sun? It is a thing, yet it is not a thing.' Then Allah sent the Prophets among them, calling them to acknowledge Allah, and this is His saying: And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say: Allah. Then He called them to acknowledge the Prophets, so some of them acknowledged and some denied. Then He called them to our wilayah, so by Allah, the one who acknowledged it was the one whom He loved, and the one who denied it was the one whom He hated. And this is His saying: So they were not going to believe in what they had denied before. Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: 'The denial was there.'

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAlī ibn Sayf, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Aḥmad ibn Rizq al-Ghumshānī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Our wilayah is the wilayah of Allah, without which He never sent any Prophet at all except with it.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “There was never any Prophet who came except with recognition of our right and our superiority over those besides us.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “By Allah,” there are indeed seventy rows of the angels in the heaven. If all the people of the earth were to gather to count the number of each row among them, they would not count them; and they indeed profess religion through our wilayah.

Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: The wilayah of ʿAlī عليه السلام is written in all the scrolls of the Prophets, and Allah did not send any messenger except with the prophethood of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله and his legatee, ʿAlī عليه السلام.

Yūnus narrated to us, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, appointed ʿAlī عليه السلام as a standard between Him and His creation. So whoever recognized him was a believer, whoever denied him was a disbeliever, whoever was ignorant of him was astray, whoever set up anything alongside him was a polytheist, and whoever came with his wilayah entered Paradise.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū Ḥamzah, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying: Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام is a door that Allah opened. So whoever enters it is a believer, and whoever exits from it is a disbeliever, and whoever neither enters it nor exits from it is among the class concerning whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: For Me, concerning them, is the decision.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, who said: Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) used to say: Indeed Allah took the covenant of our Shiʿah for our wilayah, while they were particles on the day when the covenant was taken upon the particles through acknowledging His Lordship and the prophethood of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله). And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, presented to Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) his community in the clay while they were shadows, and He created them from the clay from which Adam was created. And Allah created the spirits of our Shiʿah before their bodies by two thousand years, and presented them to him, and made them known to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and made them known to ʿAlī, and we recognize them in the tone of speech.

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'We are the guardians of the command of God, and the treasurers of the knowledge of God, and the repositories of the revelation of God.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'By Allah! We are indeed the treasurers of Allah in His sky and His earth — not over gold, and not over silver, but over His Knowledge.'

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What are you (plural)?' He said: 'We are the treasurers of Allah's knowledge, and we are the translators of Allah's revelation, and we are the conclusive proof upon those beneath the sky and above the earth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: God, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'The completion of My proof against the wretched ones of your community is due to their abandonment of the wilaya of Ali and the successors after you, for in them is your sunnah and the sunnah of the Prophets before you, and they are My treasurers over My knowledge after you.' Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Jibrail (peace be upon him) has informed me of their names and the names of their forefathers.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Fazalah ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ibn Abi Ya'fur! Indeed God is One, unified in His Oneness, unique in His Command. So He created creatures and destined them for that Command. So we are they, O Ibn Abi Ya'fur! We are the Divine Proofs of God among His servants, His treasurers over His Knowledge, and the custodians of that.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — created us and made our creation excellent; He formed us and made our forms excellent; He made us His treasurers in His heaven and in His earth; for us the tree spoke; by our worship, God — Mighty and Majestic — is worshipped; and were it not for us, God would not be worshipped.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Sahl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that a man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام while he was with his companions, greeted him, then said: To him: “By Allah, I love you and acknowledge your wilayah.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “You have lied.” He said: “Yes, by Allah, I do love you and acknowledge your wilayah,” and he repeated it three times. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “You have lied. You are not as you claim. Indeed, Allah created the spirits before the bodies by two thousand years, then He presented to us those who love us. So by Allah, I did not see your spirit among those who were presented. So where were you?” Then the man fell silent at that and did not reply to him. And in another narration, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “He was in the Fire.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, we recognize the man, when we see him, by the reality of faith and the reality of hypocrisy.

Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the Imam: has Allah delegated to him just as He delegated to Sulayman ibn Dawud? He said: Yes. And that is that a man asked him about an issue, so he answered him concerning it; then another asked him about that same issue, so he answered him differently from the answer given to the first; then another asked him, and he answered him differently from the answer given to the first two. Then he said: "This is Our gift, so withhold or give without reckoning." And this is how it is in the recitation of Ali عليه السلام. I said: May Allah keep you well, so when he answers them with this answer, does the Imam recognize them? He said: Glory be to Allah! Do you not hear Allah saying: "Surely in that are signs for those who discern." And they are the Imams. "And indeed it is on an abiding road." He never departs from it. Then he said to me: Yes, when the Imam looks at a man, he recognizes him and recognizes his color; and if he hears his speech from behind a wall, he recognizes him and recognizes what he is. Indeed Allah says: "And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your tongues and your colors. Surely in that are signs for the knowing ones." And they are the scholars. So he does not hear anything of a matter that is spoken except that he recognizes it, whether one saved or one doomed. Therefore, for that reason, he answers them with what he answers them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Akhi Hammad al-Katib, from al-Husayn ibn Abdullah, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: 'Was the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله the master of the children of Adam?' He said: 'By Allah, he was the master of all whom Allah created, and Allah did not create any creature better than Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله.'

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥajjāl, from Ḥammād, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام; and he mentioned the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, then he said: Amir al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: Allah has not created any living being better than Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله.

Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Murāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: O Muḥammad, I created you and ʿAlī as light—meaning a spirit without a body—before I created My heavens, My earth, My Throne, and My sea. Then you continued declaring My Oneness and glorifying Me. Then I gathered both of your spirits and made them one, and it was glorifying Me, declaring My holiness, and declaring My Oneness. Then I divided it into two, and divided the two into two, so they became four: Muḥammad one, ʿAlī one, and al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn two. Then Allah created Fāṭimah from a light, originating her as a spirit without a body. Then He wiped us with His right hand, so His light flowed into us.

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله): “Indeed, I created you when you were not a thing, and I breathed into you from My Spirit as an honor from Me by which I honored you when I made obedience to you obligatory upon all of My creation. So whoever obeys you has obeyed Me, and whoever disobeys you has disobeyed Me. And I made that obligatory regarding ʿAlī and regarding his offspring, from those among them whom I selected for Myself.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Abī al-Faḍl ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, who said: I was in the presence of Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام, and I brought up the differing of the Shīʿah. So he said: O Muḥammad, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, never ceased being singular in His Oneness. Then He created Muḥammad, and ʿAlī, and Fāṭimah. Then they remained for a thousand dahr. Then He created all things, and made them witness their creation, and caused their obedience to be binding upon them, and delegated their affairs to them. So they make halal whatever they will, and make haram whatever they will; and they do not will except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills. Then he said: O Muḥammad, this is the religion such that whoever goes ahead of it slips away, whoever falls behind it is effaced, and whoever adheres to it joins it. Take it to yourself, O Muḥammad.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Sahl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that some of Quraysh said: to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: “By what thing did you precede the Prophets, while you were sent as the last of them and their seal?” He said: “Indeed, I was the first of those who believed in my Lord, and the first of those who answered when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets and made them testify against themselves:” “Am I not your Lord?” They said: “Yes.” “So I was the first Prophet to say: ‘Yes’; thus I preceded them in acknowledging Allah.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥammād, from al-Mufaḍḍal, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “How were you when you were in the shadows?” So he عليه السلام said: “O Mufaḍḍal, we were with our Lord. There was no one with Him other than us, in a green canopy. We glorified Him, declared His holiness, proclaimed His oneness, and magnified Him. And there was neither any near angel nor any possessor of spirit other than us, until it became manifest to Him to create things. So He created whatever He willed, however He willed, from the angels and others besides them; then He conveyed the knowledge of that to us.”

I heard Yūnus ibn Ya‘qūb, from Sinān ibn Ṭarīf, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام). He says, he said: We are the first Ahl al-Bayt whose names Allah proclaimed. Indeed, when He created the heavens and the earth, He commanded a caller, and he called out: I testify that there is no god except Allah, three times; I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, three times; I testify that ‘Alī is truly the Commander of the Faithful, three times.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Husayn ibn Abdullah al-Saghir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah was when there was nothing that was. Then He created existence and place, and created the Light of lights by which the lights were illuminated, and caused to flow within it from His Light by which the lights were illuminated. And that is the light from which He created Muhammad and Ali. They remained two first lights when nothing had been brought into being before them. Then they continued to pass on, pure and purified, through the pure loins until they were separated in the purest of two pure ones: in Abdullah and Abu Talib عليه السلام.

Abu Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said to me, “O Jabir, indeed Allah, the first thing He created, created Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) and his progeny, the guiding ones, the guided ones. So they were phantoms of light before Allah.” I said, “What are the phantoms?” He said, “The shadow of light: luminous bodies without spirits, and he was supported by one spirit, and that is the Spirit of Holiness.” So by it he worshipped Allah, and his progeny, and for that reason He created them forbearing, learned, righteous, pure ones. They worship Allah through salat (prayer), sawm (fasting), sajdah (prostration), tasbih (glorification), and tahlil, and they perform the prayers, perform hajj, and fast.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd Shabāb al-Ṣayrafī, from Mālik ibn Ismāʿīl al-Nahdī, from ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥārith, from Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah al-ʿIjlī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There were three qualities in the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله that were not in anyone other than him: he had no shadow; and he would not pass through a road, then someone would pass through it after two or three days, except that it would be recognized that he had passed through it due to the pleasantness of his fragrance; and he did not pass by a stone or a tree except that it prostrated to him.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: When Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) was taken on the Ascension, Jabrāʾīl brought him to a place and then left him there. So he said to him, "O Jabrāʾīl, are you leaving me in this state?" He said, "Go on, for by Allah, you have indeed set foot in a place that no human being has ever set foot in, and no human being walked in before you."

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: Abū Baṣīr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) while I was present, and he said: “May I be your ransom, how many times was the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) taken on the Ascension?” He said: “Twice. Jibrāʾīl made him stop at a station and said to him: ‘Stay in your place, O Muḥammad, for you have stood at a station at which no angel has ever stood, nor any prophet. Surely your Lord performs salat.’ He said: ‘O Jibrāʾīl, and how does He perform salat?’ He said: ‘He says: Subbūḥun, Quddūs, I am the Lord of the angels and the Spirit; My mercy has preceded My wrath.’ So he said: ‘O Allah, Your pardon, Your pardon.’” He said: “And it was as Allah said: ‘two bow-lengths or nearer.’” Then Abū Baṣīr said to him: “May I be your ransom, what is ‘two bow-lengths or nearer’?” He said: “What is between its curve and its tip.” He said: “Between them was a veil, glittering and trembling, and I only know it as that he said: of zabarjad. Then he looked through something like the eye of a needle toward whatever Allah willed of the Light of Majesty.” Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “O Muḥammad.” He said: “At Your service, my Lord.” He said: “Who is for your community after you?” He said: “Allah knows best.” He said: “ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the master of the Muslims, and the leader of the radiant ones.” He said: Then Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said to Abū Baṣīr: “O Abā Muḥammad, by Allah, the wilayah of ʿAlī (عليه السلام) did not come from the earth; rather, it came from heaven directly.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Sayf, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): “Describe to me the Prophet of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).” He said: “The Prophet of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was fair, tinged with redness, intensely black-eyed, with eyebrows nearly joined, broad at the extremities, as though gold had been poured over his fingers, and with great shoulder joints.” When he turned, he would turn completely. The line of hair on his chest flowed from the hollow of his throat to his navel, as though it were a streak in purified silver. His neck up to his shoulders was like a silver ewer. His nose would nearly reach the water when he drank. When he walked, he leaned forward as though descending a slope. None like the Prophet of Allah was ever seen before him nor after him (صلى الله عليه وآله).

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, Allah represented my community to me in the clay and taught me their names just as He taught Ādam the names, all of them.” “Then the أصحابُ الرَّايَات passed by me, so I sought forgiveness for ʿAlī and his Shīʿah.” “Indeed, my Lord promised me, concerning the Shīʿah of ʿAlī, a special quality.” It was said, “O Rasūl Allāh, and what is it?” He said: “Forgiveness for those among them who believe, and that neither a minor sin nor a major sin of theirs will be left, and for them evil deeds will be changed into good deeds.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Sayf, from his father, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله addressed the people, then raised his right hand, clasping his palm, then said: “O people, do you know what is in my palm?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “In it are the names of the people of Paradise, and the names of their fathers and their tribes, until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he raised his left hand and said: “O people, do you know what is in my palm?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “The names of the people of the Fire, and the names of their fathers and their tribes, until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he said: “Allah has judged and been just, Allah has judged and been just: a party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام. In a sermon of his, specifically mentioning therein the state of the Prophet and the Imams عليهم السلام and their qualities. So our Lord, by reason of His forbearance, deliberateness, and compassion, was not prevented by the enormity of their crimes and the ugliness of their deeds from choosing for them the most beloved of His Prophets to Him, and the most honored of them before Him, Muhammad ibn Abdillah عليه السلام. His birth was in the very midst of honor, and his lineage-root in the depth of nobility; his ancestry was unblemished, his lineage unmixed, and his description was not unknown to the people of knowledge. The Prophets gave glad tidings of him in their books, the scholars spoke of him in their descriptions, and the wise pondered him through his attributes. Refined, unmatched; Hashimite, without equal; of al-Abtah, unsurpassed. His trait was modesty, and his nature generosity; formed upon the dignities and morals of prophethood, stamped upon the qualities and forbearances of messengership, until the causes of the decrees of Allah reached in him their appointed times, and by the command of Allah the decree proceeded concerning him to its final ends; the inevitable decree of Allah brought him to its utmost goals. Every community gave glad tidings of him to the one after it, and every father passed him on to a father, from loins to loins. No illicit union mixed his substance, and no unlawful relation defiled him in his birth, from Adam to his father Abdillah, within the best lineage-group, the noblest stock, the strongest clan, the most protected womb, and the safest lap. Allah chose him, approved him, and selected him, and gave him the keys of knowledge and the springs of wisdom. He sent him as a mercy to the servants and a springtime for the lands, and Allah sent down to him the Book, in which are clear expression and full clarification. “An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, so that they may attain taqwa.” He has made it clear for the people, laid out its path with knowledge, detailed it, clarified a religion, obligated duties, defined limits for the people and explained them, and disclosed matters to His creation and proclaimed them. In it are indications toward salvation and landmarks that call toward His guid

Dorost ibn Abī Manṣūr narrated to me that he asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام. Was Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله constrained by Abū Ṭālib? So he عليه السلام said: No. Rather, he was entrusted with the bequests, so he handed them over to him صلى الله عليه وآله. He said: I said, then did he hand over the bequests to him on the basis that he was constrained by him? So he عليه السلام said: If he had been constrained by him, he would not have handed the bequest over to him. He said: So I said, then what was the state of Abū Ṭālib? He عليه السلام said: He affirmed the Prophet and that which he brought, and he handed the bequests over to him, and he died that very day.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-'Abbas, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from Ya'qub ibn Salim, from a man, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: When Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was taken, the family of Muhammad عليهم السلام spent the longest night, until they thought that no sky shaded them and no earth bore them, because Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله had singled out the near and the far in Allah. While they were in that state, there came to them one whom they did not see, though they heard his speech. He said: Peace be upon you, O Ahl al-Bayt, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Indeed, in Allah there is consolation for every affliction, salvation from every destruction, and attainment of what has been lost. Every soul shall taste death, and you shall only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is kept away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed succeeded; and the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. Indeed, Allah chose you, preferred you, purified you, and made you the Ahl al-Bayt of His Prophet. He entrusted you with His knowledge, made you inherit His Book, made you the chest of His knowledge and the staff of His might, set forth for you a likeness from His light, protected you from error, and secured you from trials. So take consolation with the consolation of Allah. For Allah has not withdrawn His mercy from you, nor will He remove His blessing from you. You are the people of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through whom the blessing was completed, division was gathered, and the word came into harmony. You are His awliya'; whoever holds to your wilayah succeeds, and whoever wrongs your right perishes. Your love is an obligation from Allah in His Book upon His believing servants. Then Allah is powerful over aiding you whenever He wills, so be patient for the outcomes of affairs, for they return to Allah. Allah has accepted you from His Prophet as a trust, and entrusted to you His believing friends on the earth. So whoever fulfills his trust, Allah will grant him the reward of his truthfulness. So you are the entrusted trust; for you are the obligatory love and the prescribed obedience. Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has been taken, and he had completed the religion for you and made clear to you the path of deliverance, leaving no proof for the ign

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Isma‘il ibn ‘Ammar, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was seen in the dark night, a light was seen for him, as though it were a portion of the moon.

Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn al-Saghir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام. And Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Faddal, from some of his men, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Jibra'il عليه السلام descended upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said: 'O Muhammad, your Lord conveys peace to you and says: I have indeed forbidden the Fire for the loins that brought you forth, the womb that carried you, and the lap that cared for you. So the loins are the loins of your father Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the womb that carried you is Aminah bint Wahb, and as for the lap that cared for you, it is the lap of Abu Talib.' And in the narration of Ibn Faddal: 'And Fatimah bint Asad.'

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection as a community by himself; upon him will be the mark of the Prophets and the awe of kings.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣamm, from al-Haytham ibn Wāqid, from Muqarrin, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was the first one who affirmed al-Badāʾ. He will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment as a community by himself; upon him will be the splendor of kings and the mark of the Prophets.

Some of our companions, from Ibn Jamhūr, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, and from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, all together from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib will be resurrected as a community by himself. Upon him will be the splendor of kings and the mark of the Prophets, and that is because he was the first to speak of al-badāʾ. He said: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib had sent the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to his shepherds regarding camels of his that had strayed away. So he gathered them, but was delayed from returning to him. Then he took hold of the ring of the door of the Kaʿbah and began saying: “O Lord, will You destroy Your sign? If You do, then it is a matter that has appeared to You.” Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله came with the camels, while ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib had sent people in every road and every mountain pass searching for him, and he kept crying out: “O Lord, will You destroy Your sign? If You do, then it is a matter that has appeared to You.” When he saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, he took him and kissed him, and said: “O my son, after this I will not send you for anything, for I fear that you may be treacherously attacked and killed.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: When the master of al-Ḥabashah set out with the cavalry, and with them was the elephant, to demolish the House, they passed by camels belonging to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and drove them away. That reached ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, so he came to the master of al-Ḥabashah. The doorkeeper entered and said, "This is ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim." He said, "And what does he want?" The interpreter said, "He has come concerning camels of his that they drove away, asking you to return them." So the king of al-Ḥabashah said to his companions, "This is the chief of a people and their leader. I have come to his House, which he worships, to demolish it, while he asks me to release his camels! Had he asked me to refrain from demolishing it, I would have done so. Return his camels to him." Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said to his interpreter, "What did the king say to you?" So he informed him, and ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said, "I am the lord of the camels, and this House has a Lord who will protect it." So his camels were returned to him, and ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went back toward his home. On his way back he passed by the elephant and said to it, "O Maḥmūd." The elephant moved its head. He said to it, "Do you know why they brought you?" The elephant indicated with its head, "No." ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said, "They brought you to demolish the House of your Lord. Do you think you will do that?" It indicated with its head, "No." Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib returned to his home. When morning came, they took it to enter the Sanctuary, but it refused and would not comply with them. Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said to one of his retainers at that time, "Climb the mountain and look—do you see anything?" He said, "I see a darkness coming from the direction of the sea." He said to him, "Can your sight make it out completely?" He said, "No, but it is about to become clear." When it drew near, he said, "It is many birds, and I do not recognize them. Each bird carries in its beak a pebble like a small casting-stone, or smaller than a casting-stone." Then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said, "By the Lord of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, they want none but the people." Then when they came above their heads altogether, they cast the pebbles, and every pebble fell upon the top of a man’s head,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: A place would be spread for Abd al-Muttalib in the courtyard of the Ka'bah; it would not be spread for anyone other than him. He had sons who would stand at his head and keep away whoever came near him. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came, while he was a small child just beginning to walk, until he sat upon his thighs. One of them moved toward him to remove him from there, so Abd al-Muttalib said to him: 'Leave my son, for the angel has already come to him.'

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Muʿallā, from his brother Muḥammad, from Durust ibn Abī Manṣūr, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was born, he remained for some days without any milk for him. So Abū Ṭālib placed him upon his own breast, and Allah caused milk to come into it; thus he suckled from him for some days, until Abū Ṭālib came upon Ḥalīmah al-Saʿdiyyah, and he handed him over to her.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the likeness of Abū Ṭālib is the likeness of the Companions of the Cave: they concealed faith and outwardly showed shirk, so Allah gave them their reward twice.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Ishaq ibn Ja'far, from his father عليه السلام, who said: It was said to him, "They claim that Abu Talib was a disbeliever." So he said, "They have lied. How could he be a disbeliever while he was saying:" "Do you not know that we found Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم a Prophet, like Musa عليه السلام, written in the earliest books?" And in another hadith: "How could Abu Talib be a disbeliever while he was saying:" "They certainly know that our son is not deemed a liar by us, nor is heed paid to the speech of falsehood against him; and [he is] fair-faced, by whose face the clouds are asked for rain, a refuge for the orphans, a protection for the widows."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: While the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was in al-Masjid al-Haram and he was wearing new clothes, the polytheists threw the stomach contents of a she-camel upon him, filling his clothes with it. That affected him as Allah willed. Then he went to Abū Ṭālib and said to him, “O my uncle, how do you regard my standing among you?” He said to him, “What is that, O son of my brother?” So he informed him of the matter. Then Abū Ṭālib called Ḥamzah, took the sword, and said to Ḥamzah, “Take the stomach contents.” Then he headed toward the people, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was with him. He came to Quraysh while they were around the Kaʿbah, and when they saw him, they recognized anger in his face. Then he said to Ḥamzah, “Smear the stomach contents upon their moustaches.” So he did that until he had reached the last of them. Then Abū Ṭālib turned to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said, “O son of my brother, this is your standing among us.”

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abi 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said: When Abu Talib passed away, Jibra'il descended upon Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and said: “O Muhammad, leave Makkah, for you have no supporter in it.” Quraysh rose against the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), so he went out fleeing until he came to a mountain in Makkah called al-Hajun, and he made his way to it.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, raising it, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Abū Ṭālib professed Islam by the accounting of al-jummal. He said: In every language.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from their father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Abu Talib professed Islam by the reckoning of al-jummal, and he formed sixty-three with his hand.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān al-Kalbī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥazawwar al-Ghanawī, from Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah al-Ḥanẓalī, who said: I saw Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام on the day he opened al-Baṣrah, and he rode the mule of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. Then he said: “O people, shall I inform you of the best of creation on the Day when Allah gathers them?” Then Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī stood up before him and said: “Yes, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, narrate to us, for you were present while we were absent.” He said: “The best of creation on the Day when Allah gathers them are seven from the descendants of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. None denies their merit except a kāfir, and none rejects it except one who is obstinate.” Then ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, may Allah have mercy on him, stood and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, name them for us so that we may know them.” He said: “The best of creation on the Day when Allah gathers them are the messengers, and the best of the messengers is Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and the best of every community after its prophet is the waṣī of its prophet, until a prophet reaches him. Indeed, the best of the awṣiyāʾ is the waṣī of Muḥammad عليه وآله السلام. Indeed, the best of creation after the awṣiyāʾ are the martyrs. Indeed, the best of the martyrs are Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib. He has two dyed wings with which he flies in al-jannah; no one from this ummah besides him has been granted two wings. This is a thing by which Allah honored Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله and ennobled him. And the two grandsons are al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and al-Mahdī عليهم السلام; Allah makes him whomever He wills from among us, Ahl al-Bayt.” Then he recited this verse: “And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, then they are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, from among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous; and excellent are those as companions. That is the bounty from Allah, and Allah suffices as All-Knowing.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abū Maryam al-Anṣārī, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: I said to him, "How was the salat upon the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم)?" He said, "When Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) had washed him and shrouded him, he covered him. Then he admitted ten people to him, and they stood around him. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) stood in their midst and said:" Surely Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and submit with complete submission. So the people would say as he was saying, until the people of al-Madīnah and the people of al-ʿAwālī had performed salat over him.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAlī ibn Sayf, from Abī al-Maghrāʾ, from ʿUqbah ibn Bashīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said to ʿAlī (عليه السلام): “O ʿAlī, bury me in this place, raise my grave from the ground by four fingers, and sprinkle water upon it.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Al-ʿAbbas came to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام and said: “O Ali, the people have gathered intending to bury Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in the Baqiʿ of the prayer place, and that a man from among them should lead them.” So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام came out to the people and said: “O people, Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله is an Imam, living and dead, and he said: ‘I shall be buried in the place wherein I am taken.’” Then he said: “At the door, so perform salat upon him.” Then he instructed the people to pray upon him ten by ten, and then they would depart.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAlī ibn Sayf, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله passed away, the angels, the Muhājirūn, and the Anṣār performed salat upon him, group after group. He said: And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله saying during his good health and well-being: This verse was only sent down regarding salat upon me after Allah takes me. Surely Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and submit with a complete submission.

Some of our companions narrated it in mursal form from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Dāwūd ibn Kathīr al-Raqqī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “What is the meaning of the salām upon Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?” So he said: “Indeed, when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created His Prophet, his وصي, his daughter, his two sons, and all of the Imams, and created their Shiʿah, He took the covenant from them: that they should be patient, urge one another to patience, stand firm, and have taqwa of Allah.” And He promised them that He would deliver to them the blessed earth and the secure sanctuary, and that He would bring down for them al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, manifest to them the raised roof, grant them relief from their enemy, and the land which Allah will transform into peace, and deliver whatever is in it to them, with no blemish in it. He said: “There will be no contention there from their enemies, and they shall have therein whatever they love. Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم took the covenant regarding that from all of the Imams and their Shiʿah. The salām upon him is only a reminder of the very covenant itself and a renewal of it before Allah, so that perhaps He, Mighty and Majestic, may hasten it and hasten for you the peace with all that is in it.”

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: O Allah, send salawat upon Muhammad, Your chosen one, Your intimate friend, and Your confidant, the one who administers Your command.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Fārisī, from Abū Ḥanīfah Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Walīd ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from his father, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, Fāṭimah bint Asad came to Abū Ṭālib to give him glad tidings of the birth of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), so Abū Ṭālib said: “Be patient for a sabt, and I shall give you glad tidings of one like him, except for prophethood.” And he said: “The sabt is thirty years, and between the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) there were thirty years.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Sayyārī, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Fāṭimah bint Asad, the mother of Amīr al-Muʾminīn, was the first woman to emigrate to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله from Makkah to al-Madīnah on her own feet, and she was among the most dutiful of people toward Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. She heard Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله while he was saying: “The people will be raised on the Day of Resurrection naked, just as they were born.” So she said, “Oh, what shame!” Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to her, “Then I ask Allah to raise you clothed.” And she heard him mention the pressure of the grave, so she said, “Oh, what weakness!” Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to her, “Then I ask Allah to spare you that.” And one day she said to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, “I wish to free this servant-girl of mine.” He said to her, “If you do so, Allah will free with each limb of hers a limb of yours from the Fire.” When she fell ill, she made a bequest to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله and instructed that her servant be freed. Her tongue became unable to speak, so she began gesturing to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, and Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله accepted her bequest. Then one day while he was seated, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام came to him weeping. Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to him, “What makes you weep?” He said, “My mother Fāṭimah has died.” Rasūl Allāh said, “And by Allah, she was my mother as well,” and he rose quickly and went in. He looked at her and wept. Then he instructed the women to wash her and said, “When you have finished, do not do anything further until you inform me.” When they finished, they informed him of that, so he gave them one of his shirts, the one that touched his body, and instructed them to shroud her in it. And he said to the Muslims, “When you see me do something that I have not done before, then ask me why I did it.” When they had finished washing her and shrouding her, he صلى الله عليه وآله came in and carried her bier upon his shoulder. He remained beneath her bier until he brought her to her grave. Then he placed her down, entered the grave, and lay in it. Then he took her in his hands until he placed her in the grave. Then he bent over her for a long time, speaking confidentially to her, and saying to

Some of our companions, from the one who mentioned him, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿUmar ibn Abān al-Kalbī, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was born, the white lands of Persia and the palaces of al-Shām were opened up to Āminah. Then Fāṭimah bint Asad, the mother of Amīr al-Muʾminīn, came to Abū Ṭālib smiling and rejoicing, and informed him of what Āminah had said. So Abū Ṭālib said to her: Are you astonished at this? You will conceive and give birth to his successor and his minister.

ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm al-Hāshimī narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmar, from Usayd ibn Ṣafwān, a companion of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), who said: When it was the day on which Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) was taken, the place trembled with weeping, and the people were bewildered as on the day the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) was taken. A man came weeping, hurrying, uttering istirjāʿ, and saying, “Today the succession of prophethood has been cut off,” until he stopped at the door of the house in which Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) was. Then he said: “May Allah have mercy on you, O Abā al-Ḥasan. You were the first of the people in Islam, the sincerest of them in faith, the strongest of them in certainty, the most fearful of Allah among them, the greatest of them in hardship, the most protective of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the most trusted among them regarding his companions, the most excellent of them in virtues, the noblest of them in former precedence, the highest of them in rank, the nearest of them to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the most resembling him in guidance, character, bearing, and action, the most eminent of them in station, and the most honored of them before him.” “So may Allah reward you with goodness on behalf of Islam, His Messenger, and the Muslims. You were strong when his companions were weak; you came forth when they shrank back; you rose when they grew feeble; and you adhered to the path of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) when his companions lost resolve. You were truly his successor, neither contested nor made to plead, despite the spite of the hypocrites, the rage of the disbelievers, the hatred of the envious, and the insignificance of the sinful.” “You undertook the affair when they faltered; you spoke when they stammered; and you went forward with the light of Allah when they stood still. Then they followed you and were guided. You were the lowest of them in voice, the highest of them in devotion, the least of them in speech, the most correct of them in utterance, the greatest of them in judgment, the bravest of them in heart, the strongest of them in certainty, the best of them in deed, and the most knowledgeable of them in affairs.” “By Allah, you were the leader of the religion, at the beginning and at the end: the first when the people were divided, and the

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said: I, and ʿĀmir, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Judhāʿah al-Azdī were in the presence of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He said: Then ʿĀmir said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, the people claim that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was buried in al-Raḥbah.” He عليه السلام said, “No.” He said, “Then where was he buried?” He عليه السلام said, “When he passed away, al-Ḥasan عليه السلام carried him and brought him to the back of al-Kūfah, near al-Najaf, to the left of al-Gharī, to the right of al-Ḥīrah, and buried him between white mounds.” He said: Then later, I went to the location and supposed a particular place within it.
