Then I came to him and informed him, so he said to me, “You were correct. May Allah have mercy on you,” three times.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Qāsim ibn Muhammad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd came to me and said to me, “Ride.” So I rode with him, and we went until we came to the house of Ḥafṣ al-Kunāsī. I brought him out, and he rode with us. Then we went on until we came to al-Gharī, and we came to a grave. He said, “Get down; this is the grave of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام.” We said, “How did you know that?” He said, “I came to it with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while he was in al-Ḥīrah more than once, and he informed me that it is his grave.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿĪsā Shalqān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) had maternal kin among Banī Makhzūm, and a young man from them came to him and said, “O my maternal uncle, my brother has died, and I have grieved over him with intense grief.” He said to him, “Would you like to see him?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Then show me his grave.” He said: So he went out, and with him was the cloak of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), wrapped around him. When he came to the grave, his lips moved, then he struck it with his foot, and the man came out from his grave speaking in the Persian tongue. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said, “Did you not die while you were a man from the Arabs?” He said, “Yes, but we died upon the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of so-and-so and so-and-so, so our tongues were changed.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), who said: When Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was taken, al-Hasan ibn Ali (عليه السلام) stood in the Masjid of Kufa. He praised Allah, extolled Him, and sent salat upon the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), then said: O people, in this night a man has been taken away whom the former ones did not surpass, nor will the latter ones reach. He was indeed the bearer of the banner of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله); on his right was Jibra'il and on his left was Mika'il. He did not turn back until Allah granted victory to him. By Allah, he left behind neither white nor red, except seven hundred dirhams remaining from his stipend, with which he wanted to buy a servant for his family. By Allah, he was taken in the night in which the legatee of Musa, Yusha‘ ibn Nun, was taken, and the night in which Isa ibn Maryam was raised up, and the night in which the Qur'an was sent down.

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said: Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: When Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was washed, they were called from the side of the house: 'If you take the front of the bier, you will be sufficed regarding its rear; and if you take its rear, you will be sufficed regarding its front.'

Abdullah ibn Ja‘far and Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, both together, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, who said: I heard Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) saying: Fatimah, the daughter of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), was born five years after the mission of the Messenger of Allah, and she passed away when she was eighteen years and seventy-five days old.

Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Abdullah Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), that he heard him saying: When Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) passed away, al-Hasan and al-Husayn and two other men brought him out, until when they had gone out from al-Kufah, they left it on their right. Then they took the way through al-Jabbanah until they passed with him to al-Ghariyy, where they buried him, leveled his grave, and departed.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, Fāṭimah (عليها السلام) remained after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) for seventy-five days, and intense grief had entered her because of her father. Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) used to come to her, console her excellently regarding her father, soothe her soul, inform her about her father and his station, and inform her of what would occur after her among her descendants; and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) would write that down.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Al-ʿAmrakī ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Fāṭimah عليها السلام is truthful, a martyr, and indeed the daughters of the Prophets do not menstruate.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Razi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hurmuzani narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali عليه السلام, who said: When Fatimah عليها السلام passed away, Amir al-Mu'minin buried her secretly and effaced the place of her grave. Then he stood, turned his face toward the grave of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, from me, and peace be upon you from your daughter, your visitor, the one spending the night in the earth at your spot, for whom Allah chose swift joining with you. O Messenger of Allah, my patience has become little over your chosen one, and my endurance has faded over the chief of the women of the worlds, except that in taking consolation through your sunnah in your separation there is for me a place of solace. I indeed laid you in the niche of your grave, and your soul flowed forth between my throat and my chest. Yes; and in the Book of Allah there is for me the best acceptance: “Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we are returning.” The trust has been taken back, the pledge has been seized, and al-Zahra has been taken away. How ugly the green earth and the dusty land have become, O Messenger of Allah. As for my grief, it is everlasting; and as for my night, it is sleepless; and sorrow will not depart from my heart until Allah chooses for me your abode in which you reside. A festering anguish and a stirring sorrow—how quickly separation came between us. To Allah I complain, and your daughter will inform you of your community’s united oppression against her; so ask her insistently, and inquire from her about the condition. How much burning grief churned within her chest for which she found no way to disclose; and she will say: Allah judges, and He is the best of judges. This is the farewell of one departing, not one displeased nor wearied. If I leave, it is not from weariness; and if I remain, it is not from سوء ظنّ toward what Allah has promised the patient. Ah, ah—patience is more blessed and more beautiful. Were it not for the domination of those who seized control, I would have made remaining and staying here an inseparable commitment, and I would have wailed like a bereaved mother over the tremendous calamity. Thus, before the sight of Allah, your daughter is buried secretly, her right is usurped, her inheritance is withheld, though th

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), “Who washed Fāṭimah?” He said, “That was Amīr al-Muʾminīn.” And it was as though I considered that grave from his statement, so he said, “It is as though you have become constrained by what I informed you of.” He said: So I said, “That has indeed been so; may I be your ransom.” He said: So he said, “Do not be constrained, for she is a truthful one, and none but a truthful one would wash her. Do you not know that Maryam, none washed her except ʿĪsā?”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abdillah عليهما السلام, both said: Indeed, Fatimah عليها السلام, when there occurred from their affair what occurred, seized the collar of 'Umar and pulled him toward herself. Then she said: “Indeed, by Allah, O son of al-Khattab, were it not that I dislike affliction striking one who has no sin, you would know that I would surely swear upon Allah, then I would find Him swift in response.”

And by this chain of transmission, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: When Fāṭimah عليها السلام was born, Allah revealed to an angel, and caused the tongue of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله to speak by it, so he named her Fāṭimah. Then He said: “Indeed, I have set you apart through knowledge, and I have set you apart from menstruation.” Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “By Allah, Allah had indeed set her apart through knowledge and from menstruation in the Covenant.”

And by this chain, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) said to Fāṭimah (عليها السلام): “O Fāṭimah, arise and bring out that dish.” So she arose and brought out a dish in which there was tharīd and boiling meat broth. Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn ate from it for thirteen days. Then Umm Ayman saw al-Ḥusayn with something, so she said to him: “From where do you have this?” He said: “We have been eating it for days.” Then Umm Ayman came to Fāṭimah and said: “O Fāṭimah, when there is something with Umm Ayman, it is for Fāṭimah and her children; but when there is something with Fāṭimah, is there to be nothing from it for Umm Ayman?” So she brought some of it out for her, and Umm Ayman ate from it, and the dish was exhausted. Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) said to her: “Had you not fed her from it, you and your offspring would have continued to eat from it until the Hour is established.” Then Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “And the dish is with us; our Qāʾim (عليه السلام) will come forth with it in his time.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Alī, from ‘Alī ibn Ja‘far, who said: I heard Abā al-Hasan عليه السلام saying: While the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was seated, an angel entered upon him having twenty-four faces. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: My beloved Jibrā’īl, I have not seen you in a form like this. The angel said: I am not Jibrā’īl, O Muhammad. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent me to marry the light to the light. He said: Who to whom? He said: Fāṭimah to ‘Alī. He said: So when the angel turned away, there was written between his shoulders: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; ‘Alī is his legatee. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: Since when has this been written between your shoulders? He said: From before Allah created Adam by twenty-two thousand years.

Ali ibn Muhammad and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about the grave of Fatimah عليها السلام, so he said: She was buried in her house. Then when Banu Umayyah expanded the mosque, she came to be within the mosque.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Al-Khaybarī, from Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: Had Allah, Blessed and Exalted, not created Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام for Fāṭimah, there would not have been any equal match for her upon the face of the earth, from Ādam and those below him.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from one who heard Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: When death came to al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), he wept. So it was said to him, "O son of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), do you weep while you hold such a station with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and he said about you what he said, and you performed hajj twenty times on foot, and you divided your wealth three times, even sandal for sandal?" He said, "I only weep for two qualities: the terror of the point of arrival and the separation from loved ones."

Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah and ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother ʿAli ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Saʿid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Al-Hasan ibn ʿAli عليه السلام passed away when he was forty-seven years old, in the year fifty. He lived for forty years after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: Indeed, Jaʿdah daughter of Ashʿath ibn Qays al-Kindī poisoned al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام and poisoned a female slave belonging to him. As for his female slave, she vomited the poison; and as for al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, it remained in his stomach, then it caused swelling in him, and so he died.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Qasim al-Nahdi, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام) went out during part of his lifetime, and with him was a man from the descendants of al-Zubayr who believed in his Imamate. They halted at a watering place among those watering places, beneath a dry palm tree that had withered from thirst. A place was spread for al-Hasan (عليه السلام) beneath one palm tree, and a place was spread for al-Zubayri opposite him beneath another palm tree. He said: al-Zubayri then said, raising his head, 'If there were fresh dates on this palm tree, we would eat from it.' So al-Hasan said to him, 'Do you truly desire fresh dates?' Al-Zubayri said, 'Yes.' He said: so he raised his hand toward the sky and supplicated with words that I did not understand. The palm tree became green, then returned to its proper state, putting forth leaves and bearing fresh dates. The camel-driver from whom they had hired said, 'By Allah, this is sorcery.' Al-Hasan (عليه السلام) said, 'Woe to you, it is not sorcery; rather, it is the answered supplication of the son of a Prophet.' He said: then they climbed the palm tree and harvested what was on it, and it was sufficient for them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from his men, from Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, al-Hasan (عليه السلام) said: “Indeed, for Allah there are two cities, one of them in the east and the other in the west. Upon them is a wall of iron, and upon each one of them are a thousand thousand gates. In them are seventy thousand thousand languages; each language is spoken differently from the language of its companion. And I know all the languages, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them, and there is no hujjah over them other than me and al-Husayn, my brother.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sandal, from Abu Usamah, from Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام) went out to Makkah one year walking, and his feet became swollen. Some of his mawali said to him, "If you were to ride, this swelling would subside from you." He said, "No. When we come to this stopping place, a black man will meet you, and he will have some oil with him, so buy it from him and do not haggle with him." His mawla said to him, "May my father and mother be for you, we have not come to any stopping place in which there is anyone selling this medicine." He said to him, "Yes, indeed, he is ahead of you before the stopping place." So they travelled a mile, and there was the black man. Al-Hasan (عليه السلام) said to his mawla, "There is the man; take the oil from him and give him the price." The black man said, "O servant, for whom do you want this oil?" He said, "For Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali." He said, "Take me to him." So he went and brought him in to him. He said to him, "May my father and mother be for you, I did not know that you needed this. Do you think I would see that and still take a price for it? I am only your mawla. But supplicate to Allah that He grant me a sound male child who loves you, Ahl al-Bayt, for I left my wife in labor." He said, "Go to your home, for Allah has granted you a sound male child, and he is from our Shi'ah."

Sa'd and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, together, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali عليه السلام passed away on the day of Ashura, and he was fifty-seven years old.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿArzamī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There was between al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام one period of purity, and between them in birth there were six months and ten days.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Zayyāt, from a man from our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام descended to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله and said to him: “O Muḥammad, indeed Allah gives you glad tidings of a child who will be born from Fāṭimah, whom your community will kill after you.” So he said: “O Jibrāʾīl, and upon my Lord be peace; I have no need for a child who will be born from Fāṭimah and whom my community will kill after me.” Then he ascended, then descended عليه السلام, and said to him the like of that. So he said: “O Jibrāʾīl, and upon my Lord be peace; I have no need for a child whom my community will kill after me.” Then Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام ascended to the heaven, then descended and said: “O Muḥammad, indeed your Lord conveys peace to you and gives you glad tidings that He will place in his offspring the Imamate, the Wilayah, and the successorship.” So he said: “I am pleased.” Then he sent to Fāṭimah that Allah gives me glad tidings of a child to be born to you, whom my community will kill after me. So she sent back to him: “I have no need for a child from me whom your community will kill after you.” Then he sent to her that Allah has placed in his offspring the Imamate, the Wilayah, and the successorship. So she sent back to him: “I am pleased.” So his mother bore him with hardship, and brought him forth with hardship, and his bearing and his weaning were thirty months. Until, when he reached his full strength and reached forty years, he said: “My Lord, inspire me to give thanks for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and that I may do righteousness that pleases You, and set right for me in my offspring.” And had he not said, “Set right for me in my offspring,” all of his offspring would have been Imams. Al-Ḥusayn did not suckle from Fāṭimah عليها السلام, nor from any woman. He would be brought to the Prophet, and he would place his thumb in his mouth, and he would suck from it what sufficed him for two or three days. Thus the flesh of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام grew from the flesh of the Messenger of Allah and his blood. And none was born at six months except ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام. And in another narration from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: al-Ḥusayn would be brought to the Prophet صلى الله

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, raising it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then he cast a look at the stars, and said: Indeed, I am sick. He عليه السلام said: He calculated, and so he saw what would befall al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام; thus he said: Indeed, I am sick because of what would befall al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When there occurred in the matter of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) what occurred, the angels cried out to Allah with weeping and said: "Is this to be done to al-Husayn, Your chosen one and the son of Your Prophet?" He said: So Allah established for them the shadow-image of al-Qa'im (peace be upon him) and said: "By this one I shall take revenge for this one."

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: When help descended upon al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, until it was between the heaven and the earth, then he was given the choice of help or the meeting of Allah, so he chose the meeting of Allah.

Abu Kurayb and Abu Saʿīd al-Ashajj narrated to me; they said: ʿAbdullah ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from his father Idrīs ibn ʿAbdullah al-Awdī, who said: When al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was killed, the people wanted the horses to trample him. So Fiḍḍah said to Zaynab: “O my lady, Safīnah was once shipwrecked at sea and came out to an island, where he encountered a lion. He said: ‘O Abā al-Ḥārith, I am the mawlā of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).’ So it murmured before him until it stopped him on the road, while the lion remained crouching to one side. So let me go to it and inform it of what they intend to do tomorrow.” He said: She went to it and said, “O Abā al-Ḥārith.” So it raised its head. Then she said, “Do you know what they intend to do tomorrow with Abū ʿAbdillah (عليه السلام)? They intend to have horses trample his back.” He said: So it walked until it placed its paws upon the body of al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then the horses approached, but when they saw it, ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, may Allah curse him, said to them: “It is a disturbance; do not provoke it. Turn back.” So they turned back.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus, from Masqala al-Tahhan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying: When al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was killed, his wife from the clan of al-Kalb organized a mourning gathering for him, and she wept, and the women and the servants wept, until their tears dried up and ceased. Then while she was in that state, she saw a maidservant from among her maidservants weeping and her tears were flowing, so she called her and said to her: What is the matter with you, that among us your tears are still flowing? She said: When exhaustion afflicted me, I drank a drink of sawiq. He said: So she ordered food and sawiq, then she ate and drank, and fed others and gave them drink, and she said: We only want by that to strengthen ourselves for weeping over al-Husayn (عليه السلام). He said: And dark-colored garments were gifted to the Kalbi woman so that she might use them for the mourning of al-Husayn (عليه السلام). When she saw the garments, she said: What are these? They said: A gift that so-and-so sent so that you may seek help through them for the mourning of al-Husayn. So she said: We are not at a wedding, so what should we do with them? Then she ordered them removed, and they were taken out of the house. When they were taken out of the house, no trace or sign of them was perceived, as if they had flown between the heaven and the earth, and no أثر of them was seen after their departure from the house.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ḥasanī, may Allah have mercy on him, and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, both from Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq al-Aḥmar, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khuzāʿī, from Naṣr ibn Muzāḥim, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: When the daughter of Yazdajird was brought before ʿUmar, the young women of al-Madīnah looked on at her, and the mosque was illuminated by her radiance when she entered it. When ʿUmar looked at her, she covered her face and said: “Uff! Bīrūj bādā Hurmuz.” So ʿUmar said: “Is she insulting me?” and he moved against her. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “That is not for you. Let her choose a man from among the Muslims, and reckon her as part of his share from the fayʾ.” So he gave her the choice, and she came forward until she placed her hand on the head of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام. Amīr al-Muʾminīn said to her: “What is your name?” She said: “Jahān Shāh.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to her: “Rather, Shahrbānūyah.” Then he said to al-Ḥusayn: “O Abā ʿAbd Allāh, there shall be born to you from her the best of the people of the earth.” So she gave birth to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام used to be called: “The son of the two chosen ones,” for Allah’s chosen one from the Arabs was Hāshim, and from the non-Arabs was Fāris. And it is narrated that Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī said concerning him: “Indeed, a young man between Kisrā and Hāshim is surely the noblest of those upon whom amulets have been hung.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: There belonged to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) a she-camel upon which he performed hajj twenty-two times, and he never struck her with a single blow at all. He said: Then, after his death, she came, and we were not aware of her until one of our servants, or one of the mawālī, came to me and said: The she-camel has gone out and come to the grave of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, then knelt upon it, rubbing the grave with the front of her neck while she was moaning. So I said: Catch her, catch her, and bring her to me before they come to know of her or see her. He said: And she had never seen the grave at all.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from the one who mentioned it, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: When my father, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), passed away, a she-camel of his came from the pasture until she struck her neck upon the grave and rolled upon it. So I ordered concerning her, and she was returned to her pasture. My father (عليه السلام) used to perform hajj upon her and perform ʿumrah, and he had never struck her even a single strike at all.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Umarah, from a man, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: When it was the night in which 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام had been promised, he said to Muhammad عليه السلام: “O my son, get me water for wudu (ablution).” He said: “So I arose and brought him water for wudu (ablution).” He said: “I do not want this, for there is something dead in it.” He said: “So I went out and brought the lamp, and there was a dead mouse in it. So I brought him other water for wudu (ablution). Then he said: ‘O my son, this is the night that I was promised.’ He then gave instructions concerning his she-camel: that an enclosure be made for her and that fodder be set out for her. So she was placed in it.” He said: “It was not long before she came out until she reached the grave. She struck with her chest, moaned, and her eyes overflowed. Then Muhammad ibn 'Ali was informed, and it was said to him: ‘The she-camel has gone out.’ So he went to her and said: ‘Hush, now rise; may Allah bless you.’ But she did not do so. Then he said: ‘He used to go out upon her to Makkah, hanging the whip on the saddle, yet he would not strike her until he entered al-Madinah.’” He said: “And 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام would go out in the dark night carrying a sack containing purses of dinars and dirhams, going from door to door, knocking, then giving to whoever came out to him. So when 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام passed away, they missed that, and they came to know that it had been 'Ali عليه السلام who used to do it.”

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from his uncle ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Bint Ilyās, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: When death came to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, he lost consciousness; then he opened his eyes. And he recited: “When the Occurring Event occurs,” and, “Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory.” And he said: “All praise is due to Allah, Who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth; we may settle in Paradise wherever we wish. Excellent indeed is the reward of those who labor.” Then he passed away at that very hour and did not say anything further.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah and 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام passed away when he was fifty-seven years old, in the year ninety-five. He lived for thirty-five years after al-Husayn عليه السلام.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Mazyad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: My mother was sitting by a wall when the wall cracked, and we heard a severe crashing sound. So she gestured with her hand and said: ‘No, by the right of al-Muṣṭafā صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, Allah has not permitted you to fall.’ So it remained suspended in the air until she passed by it, then my father gave one hundred dīnārs in charity on her behalf. Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh (عليه السلام) once mentioned his grandmother, the mother of his father, and said: ‘She was a truthful woman; no woman like her was found among the family of al-Ḥasan.’ Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad, similarly.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī was the last of those who remained from the companions of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, and he was a man devoted to us, Ahl al-Bayt. He would sit in the Masjid of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, wrapped in a black turban, and he would call out: “O splitter of knowledge, O splitter of knowledge.” The people of al-Madīnah used to say, “Jābir is raving.” But he would say, “No, by Allah, I am not raving. Rather, I heard Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله say: ‘You will meet a man from me whose name is my name and whose qualities are my qualities; he will split open knowledge completely.’ That is what has led me to what I am saying.” He said: While Jābir was walking one day in one of the streets of al-Madīnah, he passed along a way where there was a school in which Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī was present. When he looked at him, he said, “O boy, come forward.” So he came forward. Then he said to him, “Turn back.” So he turned back. Then he said, “These are the qualities of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. By the One in whose hand is my soul, O boy, what is your name?” He said, “My name is Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.” Then he came to him, kissing his head and saying, “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you; your forefather Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله conveys salām to you and said that.” He said: Then Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn returned to his father while alarmed, and informed him of the matter. He said to him, “My son, has Jābir done this?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Stay in your house, my son.” Thereafter Jābir would come to him at the two ends of the day, and the people of al-Madīnah would say, “How astonishing about Jābir! He comes to this boy at the two ends of the day, while he is the last remaining of the companions of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله.” It was not long before ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام passed away. Then Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī would come to him out of honoring his companionship with Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. He said: Then he عليه السلام sat and narrated to them from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, so the people of al-Madīnah said, “We have not seen anyone more daring than this.” When he saw what they were saying, he narrated to them from Rasūl Allāh صلى الله

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Muthannā al-Ḥannāṭ, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), and I said to him, "Are you the heirs of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?" He said, "Yes." I said, "The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the heir of the Prophets, and he knew all that they knew?" He said to me, "Yes." I said, "Then you are able to give life to the dead and cure the blind and the leper?" He said, "Yes, by the permission of Allah." Then he said to me, "Come near to me, O Abū Muḥammad." So I came near him, and he wiped over my face and over my eyes, and I saw the sun, the sky, the earth, the houses, and everything in the town. Then he said to me, "Would you like to remain like this, with the same obligations and liabilities as the people upon the Day of Judgment, or return to how you were and have Paradise exclusively?" I said, "I return to how I was." So he wiped over my eyes, and I returned to how I was. He said: Then I narrated this to Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, and he said, "I bear witness that this is true, just as the day is true."

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I was with him one day when a pair of wood pigeons landed on the wall and cooed their cooing. So Abu Ja'far عليه السلام responded to them in their speech for a while. Then they rose, and when they flew onto the wall, the male cooed to the female for a while, then they flew off. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is this bird?' He said, 'O Ibn Muslim, everything Allah has created among birds, beasts, or anything possessing a spirit is more hearing toward us and more obedient than the son of Adam. This wood pigeon had become suspicious of his mate, so she swore to him, "I did not do it." Then she said, "Will you accept Muhammad ibn Ali as arbiter?" So they both accepted me, and I informed him that he was being unjust to her, so he believed her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥamzah, from his father, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: When Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) was brought to al-Shām, to Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, and arrived at his door, he said to his companions and those of Banī Umayyah who were in his presence, "When you see that I have rebuked Muhammad ibn ʿAlī, then you see that I have fallen silent, let each man among you turn against him and rebuke him." Then he ordered that permission be granted for him. So when Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) entered upon him, he said with his hand, "Peace be upon you," and thus included them all in the greeting. Then he sat down. Hishām became even more enraged at him because he had not greeted him with the caliphal salutation and had sat without permission. So he turned to rebuking him and among what he said to him was: "O Muhammad ibn ʿAlī, a man from among you continues to split the staff of the Muslims, call people to himself, and claim that he is the Imam, out of foolishness and little knowledge." And he rebuked him with whatever he wished to rebuke him with. When he fell silent, the people turned against him, one man after another rebuking him, until the last of them had finished. Then when the people fell silent, he (عليه السلام) rose standing and said, "O people, where are you going, and where are you being led? Through us Allah guided your first ones, and through us He will conclude with your last ones. If there is for you a kingdom brought forward, then indeed for us there is a kingdom deferred; and there is no kingdom after our kingdom, because we are the people of the ultimate end." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And the end is for the Godwary.” So he ordered that he be taken to prison. When he came to the prison, he spoke, and there did not remain a man in the prison except that he became drawn to him and inclined toward him. Then the keeper of the prison came to Hishām and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I fear for you from the people of al-Shām, lest they come between you and this authority of yours." Then he informed him of his affair. So he ordered regarding him, and he and his companions were carried on the postal mounts to be returned to al-Madinah. And he ordered that the markets not be opened to them, and he cut them off from food and drink. So they traveled for three days fi

Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah and al-Himyari, together, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother ʿAli ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Saʿid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said: Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Baqir passed away when he was fifty-seven years old, in the year one hundred and fourteen. He lived after ʿAli ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام for nineteen years and two months.

Wahb ibn Hafs narrated to me, from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, and Abū Khālid al-Kābulī were among the trustworthy associates of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام. He said: And my mother was among those who believed, were Godwary, and did good. And Allah loves the doers of good. He said: And my mother said: My father said: O Umm Farwah, I surely supplicate to Allah for the sinful ones among our Shiʿah a thousand times during the day and the night, because we, in what befalls us of afflictions, are patient upon what we know of the reward, while they are patient upon what they do not know.

Some of our companions, from Ibn Jamhūr, from his father, from Sulaymān ibn Samāʿah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr sent to al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd, who was his governor over the two sanctuaries, ordering: Burn down the house of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad. So he cast fire into the house of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and the fire caught at the door and the corridor. Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام came out, stepping over the fire and walking through it. And he was saying: I am the son of the roots of the earth; I am the son of Ibrāhīm, the Khalīl of Allah, عليه السلام.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Barqī, from his father, from the one whom he mentioned, from Rufayd, the mawla of Yazīd ibn ‘Amr ibn Hubayrah, who said: Ibn Hubayrah became angry with me and swore that he would surely kill me. So I fled from him and sought refuge with Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, and I informed him of my situation. He said to me: “Go back, and convey to him my greetings, and say to him: I have granted protection over your mawla Rufayd, so do not assail him with evil.” So I said to him: “May I be made your ransom, he is a Syrian of corrupt opinion.” He said: “Go to him just as I am telling you.” So I went. When I was in some of the open desert lands, a Bedouin met me and said: “Where are you going? I see the face of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Stretch out your hand.” So I did, and he said: “The hand of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Show your leg.” So I showed my leg, and he said: “The leg of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Show your body.” So I did, and he said: “The body of a slain man.” Then he said to me: “Bring out your tongue.” So I did, and he said to me: “Proceed, for there is no harm upon you, for in your tongue there is a message; if you were to bring it to the lofty mountains, they would submit to you.” He said: So I came until I stood at the door of Ibn Hubayrah and asked permission. When I entered upon him, he said: “His own legs have brought the traitor to you. Boy, bring the execution mat and the sword.” Then he gave orders concerning me, so I was bound and my head was fastened, and the executioner stood over me to strike my neck. So I said: “O Amīr, you did not seize me by force; rather, I came to you of my own accord, and here is a matter that I will mention to you, then after that you may do as you wish.” He said: “Speak.” I said: “Let me be alone with you.” So he ordered those present, and they left. Then I said to him: “Ja‘far ibn Muhammad conveys to you his greetings and says to you: I have granted protection over your mawla Rufayd, so do not assail him with evil.” He said: “By Allah, Ja‘far ibn Muhammad truly said these words to you and conveyed greetings to me?” So I swore to him, and he made me repeat it three times. Then he untied my shoulders and said: “I will not be satisfied with you until you do to me what I did to you.” I said: “My hand will not proceed to do that, nor is my

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from al-Khaybari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, and Mufaddal ibn Umar, and Abu Salamah al-Sarraj, and al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, and he said: “With us are the treasures of the earth and its keys, and if I wished to say with one of my legs, ‘Bring out what is within you of gold,’ it would surely bring it out.” He said: Then he gestured with one of his legs and traced a line with it upon the ground, and the earth split open. Then he gestured with his hand, and a gold ingot of about a handspan came out. Then he said, “Look carefully.” So we looked, and there were many ingots, some of them upon others, glittering. Then one of us said to him, “May I be your ransom, you have been given what you have been given, while your Shi'ah are in need.” He said: “Indeed, Allah will gather for us and for our Shi'ah the world and the Hereafter, and He will admit them into the Gardens of Bliss, and He will admit our enemy into the Blaze.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from some of his companions, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I had a neighbor who followed the ruling authority, and he acquired wealth. He prepared singing-girls, and used to gather people to himself, and drink intoxicants, and he used to harm me. So I complained to him personally more than once, but he did not desist. Then when I pressed him, he said to me, “O you, I am a man afflicted, and you are a man kept safe. If you would present me to your Master, I would hope that Allah might save me through you.” So that entered my heart concerning him. When I came to Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, I mentioned his condition to him. He said to me, “When you return to al-Kūfah, he will come to you, so say to him: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad says to you: Leave what you are upon, and I guarantee for you before Allah Paradise.” So when I returned to al-Kūfah, he came to me among those who came. I kept him with me until my house was empty, then I said to him, “O you, I mentioned you to Abū ‘Abdillāh Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, and he said to me: When you return to al-Kūfah, he will come to you, so say to him: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad says to you: Leave what you are upon, and I guarantee for you before Allah Paradise.” He said: So he wept, then said to me, “By Allah, Abū ‘Abdillāh really said this to you?” He said: So I swore to him that he had indeed said to me what I had related. So he said to me, “That is enough for you,” and went away. Then after some days, he sent for me and called me, and there he was behind his house naked. He said to me, “O Abū Baṣīr, no, by Allah, nothing remains in my house except that I have taken it out, and I am as you see.” He said: So I went to our brothers and gathered for him what I clothed him with. Then only a few days passed before he sent to me saying, “I am ill, so come to me.” I continued going back and forth to him and treating him until death came upon him. I was sitting with him while he was giving up his soul, and he fell unconscious for a spell, then recovered and said to me, “O Abū Baṣīr, your Master has fulfilled for us.” Then he was taken, may the mercy of Allah be upon him. Then when I performed hajj, I came to Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام and sought permission to enter upon him. When I entered, he said to me first from inside the house, while one of my feet was in the courtyard an

Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath, who said: He said to me: “Do you know what was the reason for our entering into this matter and our coming to know it, while we had no mention of it with us, nor any knowledge of anything of what the people had?” He said: I said to him, “What was that?” He said: “Abū Jaʿfar — meaning Abū al-Dawānīq — said to my father Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath: ‘O Muḥammad, find for me a man of intellect who can carry out something on my behalf.’ My father said to him: ‘I have found him for you; this is so-and-so ibn Muhājir, my maternal uncle.’ He said: ‘Bring him to me.’” He said: “So I brought my maternal uncle to him. Abū Jaʿfar said to him: ‘O Ibn Muhājir, take this wealth and go to al-Madīnah. Go to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥasan and a number of the people of his household, among them Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and say to them: “I am a stranger from the people of Khurāsān, and there are Shiʿah there from among your Shiʿah who have sent this wealth to you.” Give to each one of them on such-and-such a condition. Then when they take the wealth, say: “I am a messenger, and I would like to have with me your written acknowledgements that you have received what you have taken.”’” So he took the wealth and went to al-Madīnah, then returned to Abū al-Dawānīq while Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath was with him. Abū al-Dawānīq said to him: ‘What news do you bring?’ He said: ‘I went to the people, and these are their written acknowledgements of having received the wealth, except for Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad. I came to him while he was performing salat (prayer) in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, so I sat behind him and said: “When he finishes, I will mention to him what I mentioned to his companions.”’ Then he hastened and finished, then turned to me and said: ‘O you, be wary of Allah and do not deceive the Ahl al-Bayt of Muḥammad, for they are only recently removed from the rule of Banū Marwān and all of them are in need.’ So I said: ‘What is that? May Allah set you right!’ He said: ‘Then he brought his head close to me and informed me of everything that had taken place between me and you, as though he had been the third of us.’ He said: “Then Abū Jaʿfar said to him: ‘O Ibn Muhājir, know that there is no household of prophethood except that among it

Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah and 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far together, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu 'Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (عليه السلام) passed away when he was sixty-five years old, in the year one hundred and forty-eight, and he lived for thirty-four years after Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام).

Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: I enshrouded my father in two Shatwānī garments in which he used to enter ihram, and in a shirt from among his shirts, and in a turban that had belonged to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, and in a cloak which he had purchased for forty dinars.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Mas'ud, from al-Ja'fari who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Imams are the caliphs of God, Mighty and Majestic, in His earth.'

From him, from Mu'alla, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Sulayman ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The successors (Awsiya') are the gates of God, Mighty and Majestic, through which one approaches Him; and had it not been for them, God, Mighty and Majestic, would not have been recognized; and through them, God, Blessed and Exalted, has established His proof upon His creation.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Majestic is His Majesty: 'God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will make them successors in the earth, just as He made successors those who came before them' He said: 'They are the Imams.'

‘Isa ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from his father, who said: Ibn ‘Ukasha ibn Mihsan al-Asadi entered upon Abu Ja‘far, and Abu ‘Abd Allah (عليه السلام) was standing with him. He presented grapes to him, and he said: “One by one is how the very old man and the very young child eat; three and four at a time is how one who thinks he will not be satisfied eats; and eat it two by two, for that is recommended.” Then he said to Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام): “Why do you not marry Abu ‘Abd Allah, for he has reached the age of marriage?” He said: There was before him a sealed purse, and he said: “Indeed, a slave trader from the people of Barbar will soon come and lodge at the house of Maymun, and we shall buy for him a slave-girl with this purse.” He said: Then what was to occur occurred. One day we entered upon Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), and he said: “Shall I inform you about the slave trader whom I mentioned to you? He has arrived, so go and buy a slave-girl from him with this purse.” He said: So we went to the slave trader, and he said: “I have sold all that I had except for two sick slave-girls, one of whom is better than the other.” We said: “Bring them out so that we may look at them.” So he brought them out, and we said: “For how much will you sell us this one of sounder condition?” He said: “For seventy dinars.” We said: “Be fair.” He said: “I will not reduce it from seventy dinars.” We said to him: “We will buy her from you with this purse, whatever amount it reaches, and we do not know what is in it.” There was with him a man white of head and beard, who said: “Open it and weigh it.” The slave trader said: “Do not open it, for if it is deficient by even one grain from seventy dinars, I will not transact with you.” Then the old man said: “Come near.” So we came near, broke the seal, and weighed the dinars, and it was exactly seventy dinars, neither more nor less. So we took the slave-girl and brought her to Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), while Ja‘far was standing with him. We informed Abu Ja‘far of what had happened, so he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said to her: “What is your name?” She said: “Hamidah.” He said: “Hamidah in this world, praiseworthy in the Hereafter.” Then he said: “O Ja‘far, take her to yourself,” and she gave birth to the best of the people of the earth, Musa ibn Ja‘far (عليه السلام).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Sabiq ibn al-Walid, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, that Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Hamidah is purified from impurities like an ingot of gold. The angels never ceased guarding her until she was delivered to me as an honor from Allah for me and for the Divine Authority after me.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, altogether from Abū Qatādah al-Qummī, from Abū Khālid al-Zubālī, who said: When Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام was taken to al-Mahdī on the first occasion, he stopped at Zubālah. I was speaking with him, and he saw me grief-stricken, so he said to me: “O Abū Khālid, why do I see you grief-stricken?” I said, “How can I not be distressed when you are being taken to this tyrant, and I do not know what he will do concerning you?” He said: “There is no harm upon me. When such-and-such a month and such-and-such a day comes, then meet me at the first milestone.” I had no concern except counting the months and the days until that day came. I went to the milestone and remained there until the sun nearly set, and Shayṭān whispered in my breast, and I feared that I might doubt what he had said. While I was in that state, I suddenly saw a dark mass approaching from the direction of al-ʿIrāq, so I went out to meet them, and there was Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام at the front of the caravan upon a mule. He said: “Indeed, O Abū Khālid!” I said: “At your service, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.” He said: “Do not doubt; Shayṭān wished that you would doubt.” I said: “All praise belongs to Allah who delivered you from them.” He said: “Indeed, I shall return to them again; I will not be delivered from them.”

Ahmad ibn Mihran and Ali ibn Ibrahim, both together, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, who said: I was with Abu al-Hasan Musa (عليه السلام) when a Christian man came to him while we were with him at al-'Urayd. The Christian said: “I have come to you from a distant land and a difficult journey. For thirty years I asked my Lord to guide me to the best of religions, and to the best and most knowledgeable of servants. Someone came to me in sleep and described to me a man in upper Damascus, so I went to him and spoke with him. He said: ‘I am the most knowledgeable among the people of my religion, but another is more knowledgeable than I.’ So I said: ‘Guide me to the one more knowledgeable than you, for travel is not too great for me, nor is the distance too far. I have read the whole Gospel, the Psalms of Dawud, four books of the Torah, and the outward of the Qur'an until I comprehended it all.’ The scholar said to me: ‘If you seek knowledge of Christianity, I am the most knowledgeable of Arabs and non-Arabs in it. If you seek knowledge of the Jews, then Bati ibn Shurahbil al-Samiri is the most knowledgeable of people in it today. But if you seek knowledge of Islam, and of the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the Book of Hud, and everything sent down upon any Prophet in your age and before it, and what has descended from heaven of report whether someone knew it or not—wherein is clarification of everything, healing for the worlds, comfort for the one who seeks repose in it, and insight for the one for whom Allah intends good and who inclines to the truth—then I will guide you to him. Go to him, even if walking on your feet; if you cannot, then crawling on your knees; if you cannot, then dragging yourself on your backside; if you cannot, then on your face.’ I said: ‘Rather, I am able to travel in body and wealth.’ He said: ‘Set out at once until you come to Yathrib.’ I said: ‘I do not know Yathrib.’ He said: ‘Go until you come to the city of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), who was sent among the Arabs, the Arab Hashimi Prophet. When you enter it, ask about Banu Ghanm ibn Malik ibn al-Najjar by the door of its mosque, and display the attire and adornment of Christianity, for its governor is harsh toward them and the caliph harsher still. Then ask about Banu 'Amr ibn Mabdhul at Baqi' al-Zubayr. Then ask about Musa i

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm and Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, all together, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Yaʿqūb ibn Jaʿfar, who said: I was with Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) when a man from the people of Najrān in Yemen, one of the monks, came to him, and with him was a nun. Al-Faḍl ibn Sawwār sought permission for them, so he said to him: “When tomorrow comes, bring them both to the well of Umm Khayr.” He said: We came the next day and found that the people had come as arranged. He ordered a mat of palm-leaf strips, then sat, and they sat. The nun began with questions and asked many questions, all of which he answered. Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) also asked her about things regarding which she had nothing, then she accepted Islam. Then the monk turned to question him, and he answered him regarding everything he asked. The monk said: “I had been strong in my religion, and I left behind no one among the Christians on earth who reached my rank in knowledge. I had heard of a man in India who, whenever he wished, would make hajj to Bayt al-Maqdis in a day and a night, then return to his home in the land of India. So I asked about him, in which land he was, and it was said to me that he was in Subdhān. I asked the one who informed me, and he said: he knew the Name by which Āṣif, the companion of Sulaymān, prevailed when he brought the throne of Sabaʾ, and it is what Allah mentioned to you in your Book, and to us, the communities of religions, in our books.” Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said to him: “How many Names belonging to Allah are there by which the supplicant is not turned back?” The monk said: “The Names are many; but as for the decreed ones among them, by which the supplicant is not turned back, they are seven.” Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) said to him: “Inform me about what you preserve of them.” The monk said: “No, by Allah who sent down the Tawrah upon Mūsā, and made ʿĪsā a lesson for the worlds and a trial for the gratitude of those possessed of intellect, and made Muḥammad a blessing and mercy, and made ʿAlī (عليه السلام) a lesson and insight, and made the awṣiyāʾ from his progeny and the progeny of Muḥammad—I do not know; and if I had known, I would not have needed your speech in it, nor come to you, nor ask you.” Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said to him: “Return to the account of the Indian.” The monk said to him: “I had heard of these Names, but I did not

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: Al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ passed by a woman at Minā while she was weeping, and her children were around her weeping, and a cow of hers had died. He drew near to her and said to her, "What makes you weep, O maidservant of Allah?" She said, "O servant of Allah, we have orphaned children, and I had a cow from which came my livelihood and the livelihood of my children. It has died, and I have been left cut off, together with my children; we have no means." He said, "O maidservant of Allah, would you like me to revive it for you?" So she was inspired to say, "Yes, O servant of Allah." Then he withdrew, prayed two rakʿahs of salat (prayer), then raised his hand for a short while and moved his lips. Then he stood and called out at the cow, and prodded it with a prod or struck it with his foot, whereupon it rose upright standing upon the ground. So when the woman looked at the cow, she cried out and said, "ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah!" Then he mixed among the people, came to be between them, and went on, peace be upon him.

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, may Allah have mercy on him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I heard al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام informing a man of his own death. So I said to myself, “Indeed, he knows when a man from his Shiʿah will die.” Then he turned toward me somewhat angrily and said: “O Isḥāq, Rushayd al-Hajarī used to know the knowledge of deaths and afflictions, and the Imam is worthier of the knowledge of that.” Then he said: “O Isḥāq, do whatever you are doing, for your lifespan has come to an end, and you will die within two years. Your brothers and the people of your household will not remain after you except a little while, until their unity is broken apart and some of them betray others, until their enemy gloats over them. So this was what was within yourself?” So I said: “Then I seek the forgiveness of Allah for what occurred in my breast.” Isḥāq did not remain after this gathering except a short while until he died. Then only a little time passed over them before Banū ʿAmmār rose with the wealth of the people, and they became bankrupt.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il came to me while we had performed the Rajab 'umrah and were then in Makkah. He said, "O uncle, I intend to go to Baghdad, and I wished to bid farewell to my uncle Abu al-Hasan"—meaning Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام—"and I wished that you would go with me to him." So I went out with him toward my brother, and he was in his house in al-Hawbah, shortly after al-Maghrib. I knocked at the door, and my brother answered me, saying, "Who is this?" I said, "Ali." He said, "I am just coming out." He was slow in wudu (ablution), so I said, "Quickly!" He said, "I am hurrying." Then he came out, wearing a striped waist-wrapper tied at his neck, until he sat beneath the threshold of the door. Ali ibn Ja'far said: I bent toward him and kissed his head, and said, "I have come to you concerning a matter: if you see it as right, may Allah grant him success in it; and if it is otherwise than that, how often we err." He said, "What is it?" I said, "This son of your brother wishes to bid you farewell and depart for Baghdad." He said to me, "Call him." So I called him, and he had stood aside. He came near him, kissed his head, and said, "May I be your ransom, advise me." He said, "I advise you to be Godwary regarding my blood." He replied to him, "Whoever intends evil toward you, may Allah deal with him accordingly," and he began supplicating against whoever intended evil toward him. Then he returned, kissed his head, and said, "O uncle, advise me." He said, "I advise you to be Godwary regarding my blood." He said, "Whoever intends evil toward you, may Allah deal with him accordingly," and he did so. Then he returned, kissed his head, and again said, "O uncle, advise me." He said, "I advise you to be Godwary regarding my blood." So he supplicated against whoever intended evil toward him, then withdrew from him, and I left with him. Then my brother said to me, "O Ali, stay where you are." So I remained in my place. He entered his house, then called me, and I entered to him. He took a purse containing one hundred dinars, gave it to me, and said, "Tell your nephew to use it for assistance on his journey." Ali said: I took it and tucked it into the edge of my cloak. Then he handed me another hundred and said, "Give him this as well." Then he handed me another pu

Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Abdullah ibn Ja'far, both together, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said: Musa ibn Ja'far (عليه السلام) passed away when he was fifty-four years old, in the year one hundred and eighty-three, and he lived for thirty-five years after Ja'far (عليه السلام).

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Aḥmar, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام said to me, “Have you come to know of anyone from the people of al-Maghrib who has arrived?” I said, “No.” He said, “Rather, a man has arrived, so come with us.” Then he rode, and I rode with him until we came to the man. There was a man from the people of al-Madīnah with him, and he had slave girls. So I said to him, “Show them to us.” He showed us seven slave girls, and throughout all of that Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was saying, “I have no need of her.” Then he said, “Show them to us.” The man said, “I have nothing except a sick slave girl.” He said to him, “What harm is there for you in showing her?” But he refused him, so he left. Then on the next day he sent me and said, “Say to him: ‘What was your final price for her?’ Then when he says such-and-such, say: ‘I have taken her.’” So I went to him, and he said, “I did not want to reduce her from such-and-such and such-and-such.” So I said, “I have taken her.” He said, “She is yours, but tell me: who was the man that was with you yesterday?” I said, “A man from Banī Hāshim.” He said, “From which branch of Banī Hāshim?” I said, “I have nothing more than this.” He said, “I will tell you about this young maidservant. I bought her from the farthest part of al-Maghrib. Then a woman from the People of the Book met me and said, ‘What is this young maidservant with you?’ I said, ‘I bought her for myself.’ She said, ‘It is not fitting that this one should be with the likes of you. This slave girl ought to be with the best of the people of the earth. She will not remain with him except a little while, until she bears from him a غلام such that none like him will be born in the east of the earth nor in its west.’” He said: So I brought her to him, and she did not remain with him except a short while until she gave birth to al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from the one who mentioned him, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said: When Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) passed away and Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) spoke, we feared for him because of that. So it was said to him: “You have manifested a tremendous matter, and we fear this tyrant for you.” He said: “Let him exert his utmost effort, for he has no way against me.”

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, may Allah have mercy on him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Manṣūr, from his brother, who said: I entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام in an inner room in the middle of the house at night. Then he raised his hand, and it was as though there were ten lamps in the house. A man then sought permission to enter upon him, so he lowered his hand, and then gave him permission.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Jumhūr, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from al-Ghifārī, who said: A man from the family of Abū Rāfiʿ, the mawlā of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, called Ṭays, had a right due from me. He demanded payment from me, pressed me hard, and the people supported him. When I saw that, I performed the morning salat (prayer) in the Masjid of the Messenger عليه السلام, then I headed toward al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who at that time was in al-ʿUrayḍ. When I came near his door, he had come out riding a donkey, wearing a shirt and a cloak. When I looked at him, I felt shy before him. When he caught up with me, he stopped and looked toward me, so I greeted him. It was the month of Ramadan, and I said: “May Allah make me your ransom, your servant Ṭays has a claim upon me, and by Allah, he has publicly exposed me.” Within myself I thought that he would order him to desist from me, yet by Allah, I did not tell him how much was due from me, nor did I specify anything to him. He instructed me to remain seated until his return. I stayed there until I had performed the Maghrib salat (prayer), while I was fasting, and my chest became tight and I wanted to leave. Then he appeared before me with people around him; the beggars had gathered by him and he was giving charity to them. He went on and entered his house, then came out and called me. So I rose to him and entered with him, and he sat down and I sat. I said: “May I be made your ransom, the men of Ibn al-Musayyab are circulating, and I dislike that they should meet me while your servants are with me.” He said to me: “You are right. May Allah grant right guidance through you.” And he ordered them to leave whenever I sent them back. When I came near my house and felt safe, I sent them back. Then I went to my house, called for the lamp, and looked at the dinars. They were forty-eight dinars, while the man’s claim against me had been twenty-eight dinars. Among them was a dinar that shone, and I admired its beauty. I took it and brought it near the lamp, and on it there was a clear engraving: “The man’s due is twenty-eight dinars, and what remains is for you.” No, by Allah, I had not known what was due to him from me. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, Who honoured His wali.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, that he went out from al-Madinah in the year in which Harun performed hajj, intending the hajj. He came to a mountain on the left of the road as you are going to Makkah, called Fari'. Abu al-Hasan looked at it, then said: 'The builder of Fari' and its demolisher will be cut limb by limb.' So we did not know what that meant. Then, when he had departed, Harun arrived and camped at that place. Ja'far ibn Yahya climbed that mountain and ordered that a sitting place be built there for him. Then when he returned from Makkah, he climbed it and ordered it to be demolished. Then when he departed to al-'Iraq, he was cut limb by limb.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Hamza ibn al-Qasim, from Ibrahim ibn Musa, who said: I persistently pressed Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام regarding something that I was asking from him, and he would promise me. Then one day he went out to receive the governor of al-Madinah, and I was with him. He came near the palace of so-and-so and stopped beneath some trees, and I stopped with him, and there was no third person with us. So I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, this Eid has come upon us, and no, by Allah, I do not possess even a dirham, nor anything besides it.' So he scraped the ground intensely with his whip, then struck with his hand and took from it a gold ingot. Then he said: 'Benefit from it, and conceal what you saw.'

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Yāsir al-Khādim and al-Rayyān ibn al-Ṣalt, both of whom said: When the affair of the deposed one came to an end and authority was firmly established for al-Maʾmūn, he wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام requesting that he come to Khurāsān. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام excused himself with various reasons, but al-Maʾmūn continued corresponding with him about this until he knew that there was no escape for him and that he would not desist from him. So he عليه السلام departed, while Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was seven years old. Al-Maʾmūn wrote to him that he should not take the route of al-Jabal and Qumm, but rather go by the route of al-Baṣra, al-Ahwāz, and Fārs, until he arrived at Marw. Then al-Maʾmūn offered him the authority and the caliphate, but Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام refused. He said: then the succession to the heirship. He عليه السلام said: upon conditions that I shall stipulate to you. Al-Maʾmūn said to him: ask whatever you wish. Al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote: 'I am entering into the ولاية of the heirship on the condition that I neither command nor forbid, nor give legal verdicts, nor judge, nor appoint, nor dismiss, nor change anything of what is already established, and that you exempt me from all of that.' Al-Maʾmūn accepted all of those terms. He said: Yāsir narrated to me, saying: when the ʿĪd came, al-Maʾmūn sent to al-Riḍā عليه السلام asking him to ride out, attend the ʿĪd, lead the salat (prayer), and deliver the sermon. Al-Riḍā عليه السلام sent back to him: 'You know the conditions that were agreed between me and you upon entering into this matter.' Al-Maʾmūn sent again: 'I only intend by this that the hearts of the people may be reassured and that they may know your merit.' He عليه السلام continued to reply to him about that, but he insisted. So he عليه السلام said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, if you excuse me from that, it is more beloved to me; but if you do not excuse me, I will go out just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام went out.' Al-Maʾmūn said: 'Go out however you wish.' And al-Maʾmūn ordered the commanders and the people to come early to the door of Abū al-Ḥasan. He said: Yāsir the servant narrated to me that the people sat waiting for Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in the streets and on the rooftops—men, women, and children—and the commanders and soldiers gather

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yāsir, who said: When al-Maʾmūn departed from Khurāsān intending Baghdād, and al-Faḍl, the one with the two authorities, departed, and we departed with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, a letter from his brother al-Ḥasan ibn Sahl came to al-Faḍl ibn Sahl, the one with the two authorities, while we were at one of the stopping places: “I examined the turning of the year in the calculation of the stars, and I found in it that in such-and-such a month, on Wednesday, you will taste the heat of iron and the heat of fire. I think that you, Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and al-Riḍā should enter the bathhouse on this day, perform cupping there, and pour the blood over your hands so that its ill fortune may depart from you.” So the one with the two authorities wrote to al-Maʾmūn about that and asked him to ask Abū al-Ḥasan about it. Then al-Maʾmūn wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan asking him that, and Abū al-Ḥasan wrote back to him: “I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, and I do not think that you or al-Faḍl should enter the bathhouse tomorrow.” Then he sent the note back to him twice. Then Abū al-Ḥasan wrote to him: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, for I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in sleep this night, and he said to me: ‘O ʿAlī, do not enter the bathhouse tomorrow.’ And I do not think that you or al-Faḍl should enter the bathhouse tomorrow.” So al-Maʾmūn wrote to him: “You have spoken the truth, my master, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم has spoken the truth. I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, and al-Faḍl knows best.” He said: Yāsir said: “When evening came and the sun had set, al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to us: ‘Say: We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of what descends on this night.’ So we continued saying that. Then when al-Riḍā عليه السلام had performed the morning salat (prayer), he said to me: ‘Climb onto the roof and listen carefully; do you hear anything?’” So when I climbed up, I heard the uproar, and it intensified and increased. Then al-Maʾmūn entered through the door leading to his house from the house of Abū al-Ḥasan, saying: ‘O my master, O Abū al-Ḥasan, may Allah reward you concerning al-Faḍl. He refused, entered the bathhouse, and some people came upon him with swords and killed him. Three of those who entered upon him were seized, and one of them was his maternal cousin al-Faḍl i

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Musāfir, and from Al-Washshāʾ, from Musāfir, who said: When Hārūn ibn Al-Musayyab intended to confront Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Abū Al-Ḥasan Al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to me: “Go to him and say to him: Do not go out tomorrow, for if you go out tomorrow you will be defeated and your companions will be killed. If he asks you from where you came to know this, then say: I saw it in a dream.” He said: So I went to him and said to him: “May I be made your ransom, do not go out tomorrow, for if you go out you will be defeated and your companions will be killed.” So he said to me: “From where did you come to know this?” I said: “I saw it in a dream.” So he said: “The servant sleeps and has not washed his behind.” Then he went out, and he was defeated, and his companions were killed. He said: And Musāfir narrated to me, saying: I was with Abū Al-Ḥasan Al-Riḍā عليه السلام at Minā, and Yaḥyā ibn Khālid passed by and covered his head from the dust. So he said: “Poor ones, they do not know what will befall them in this year.” Then he said: “Even more astonishing than this is Hārūn and I being like these two,” and he joined his two fingers together. Musāfir said: So by Allah, I did not know the meaning of his statement until we buried him with him.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, who said: One of our companions informed me that he carried to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام a wealth of great value, but I did not see him pleased by it. He said: So I became distressed because of that, and I said to myself: I have brought this wealth, yet he has not been pleased by it. Then he said: O servant, the washbasin and the water. He said: Then he sat upon a chair, gestured with his hand, and said to the servant: Pour the water over me. He said: Then gold began to flow from between his fingers into the washbasin. Then he turned toward me and said to me: One who is like this does not care for that which you carried to him.

Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah and 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, both together, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: 'Ali ibn Musa عليه السلام passed away while he was forty-nine years and some months old, in the year two hundred and two. He lived after Musa ibn Ja'far for twenty years, except for two months or three.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Ali ibn Khalid, who said: Muhammad—and he was a Zaydi—said: I was at al-‘Askar, and news reached me that there was a man imprisoned there, brought from the region of al-Sham in chains, and they were saying that he had claimed prophethood. Ali ibn Khalid said: So I went to the door and maneuvered around the doorkeepers and the guards until I reached him, and there was a man of understanding. So I said: O man, what is your story and what is your matter? He said: I was a man in al-Sham worshipping Allah in the place that is called the place of the head of al-Husayn. While I was in my worship, a person came to me and said to me: Come with us. So I stood up with him, and suddenly I was with him in Masjid al-Kufa. He said to me: Do you know this masjid? I said: Yes, this is Masjid al-Kufa. He said: Then he performed salat and I performed salat with him. Then suddenly I was with him in the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله in al-Madinah. So he sent greetings upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and I sent greetings, and he performed salat and I performed salat with him, and he sent blessings upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. Then suddenly I was with him in Makkah. I remained with him until he completed his rites, and I completed my rites with him. Then suddenly I was in the place in al-Sham where I had been worshipping Allah, and the man departed. When the following year came, there he was again, and he did the like of his first act. When we had finished our rites and he returned me to al-Sham and intended to part from me, I said to him: I ask you by the right that enabled you to do what I have seen, that you tell me who you are. So he said: I am Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa. He said: Then the report spread until it reached Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Zayyat, so he sent for me, seized me, shackled me in iron, and carried me to Iraq. He said: So I said to him: Present the story to Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik. So he did, and he mentioned in his account what had occurred. Then there was written in response to his account: Say to the one who took you out from al-Sham in a single night to al-Kufa, and from al-Kufa to al-Madinah, and from al-Madinah to Makkah, and returned you from Makkah to al-Sham, that he should take you out of this imprisonment of yours. Ali ibn Khalid said: That distressed

A shaykh from our companions, called ʿAbdullāh ibn Razīn, narrated to me; he said: I was residing in al-Madīnah, the city of the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), and Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) used to come every day at midday to the mosque. He would dismount in the courtyard, go to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), offer salām to him, then return to the house of Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), remove his sandals, stand, and perform salat (prayer). Then Shayṭān whispered to me and said: “When he dismounts, go and take some of the dust that he treads upon.” So on that day I sat waiting for him in order to do this. When midday came, he (عليه السلام) approached riding his donkey, but he did not dismount in the place where he used to dismount; rather, he came and dismounted upon the rock that was at the door of the mosque. Then he entered and offered salām to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). He said: Then he returned to the place where he used to perform salat (prayer), and he did this for several days.
