So I said: “When he removes his sandals, I will come and take the pebbles that his feet tread upon.” But when the next day came, he arrived at midday, dismounted upon the rock, then entered and offered salām to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). Then he came to the place where he used to perform salat (prayer), but he prayed wearing his sandals and did not remove them, and he continued doing that for several days. So I said to myself: “This did not become possible for me here, but I will go to the door of the bathhouse, and when he enters the bathhouse, I will take some of the dust that he treads upon.” So I asked about the bathhouse that he entered, and it was said to me: “He enters a bathhouse in al-Baqīʿ belonging to a man from the descendants of Ṭalḥah.” I learned the day on which he entered the bathhouse, then went to its door and sat beside the Ṭalḥī, speaking with him while awaiting his coming (عليه السلام). The Ṭalḥī said: “If you want to enter the bathhouse, then get up and enter, for that will not be possible for you after an hour.” I said: “Why?” He said: “Because the son of al-Riḍā intends to enter the bathhouse.” He said: I said: “And who is the son of al-Riḍā?” He said: “A man from the family of Muḥammad who possesses righteousness and waraʿ.” I said to him: “And is it not permissible that anyone else enter the bathhouse with hi

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said: He (عليه السلام) came out to me, so I looked at his head and his feet so that I might describe his stature to our companions in Miṣr. While I was in that state, he sat and said: O ʿAlī, indeed Allah argued regarding the Imamate with the like of what He argued regarding Prophethood, and so He said: "And We gave him wisdom while yet a child." He said: "And when he reached his maturity," and "reaches forty years"; thus it is possible that wisdom be given while one is a child, and it is possible that it be given to him while he is a son of forty years.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn al-Rayyān, who said: Al-Maʾmūn employed every stratagem against Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), but he was unable to achieve anything concerning him. Then when he desired to give his daughter to him in marriage, he sent to two hundred maidservants from among the most beautiful there could be, with each one of them a goblet containing a jewel, to receive Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). When he sat in the place of the nobles, he did not turn toward them. And there was a man called Mukhāriq, a possessor of voice, lute, and rhythmic striking, with a long beard. Al-Maʾmūn summoned him, and he said, "O Commander of the Faithful, if it concerns anything from the affairs of the world, I shall suffice you regarding his matter." So he sat before Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). Then Mukhāriq gave a great cry, and the people of the house gathered around him, and he began striking his lute and singing. When he had done that for some time, and Abū Jaʿfar was not turning toward him, neither to the right nor to the left, then he raised his head toward him and said, "Fear Allah, O one with the little beard." He said: then the plectrum fell from his hand, and the lute as well, and he never had use of his hands until he died. He said: then Al-Maʾmūn asked him about his condition, and he said, "When Abū Jaʿfar shouted at me, I was struck by a terror from which I shall never recover."

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Dawood ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) while I had with me three letters without addresses, and they had become confused to me, so I became distressed. He took one of them and said: “This is the letter of Ziyad ibn Shabib.” Then he took the second and said: “This is the letter of so-and-so.” I was astonished, and he looked at me and smiled. He said: He gave me three hundred dinars and instructed me to carry them to one of the sons of his uncle, and he said: “Indeed, he will say to you: ‘Direct me to a trader who can buy goods for me with it,’ so direct him to one.” He said: So I went to him with the dinars, and he said to me: “O Abu Hashim, direct me to a trader who can buy goods for me with it.” So I said: “Yes.” He said: A camel-driver asked me to speak to him on his behalf so that he might include him in some of his affairs. So I entered upon him to speak to him for him, and I found him eating with a group, and I was unable to speak to him. So he said: “O Abu Hashim, eat.” And he placed food before me. Then he said, initiating it himself without being asked: “O boy, see to the camel-driver whom Abu Hashim brought to us, and attach him to yourself.” He said: One day I entered an orchard with him, and I said to him: “May I be made your ransom, I am strongly attached to eating clay, so supplicate to Allah for me.” He remained silent. Then after three days, initiating it himself, he said to me: “O Abu Hashim, Allah has removed from you the eating of clay.” Abu Hashim said: There is nothing more hateful to me than it today.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah al-Hāshimī, from ʿAlī ibn Muhammad or Muhammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hāshimī, who said: I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) on the morning of his wedding, when he had consummated with al-Maʾmūn’s daughter. I had taken some medicine during the night, so I was the first to enter upon him that morning. Thirst had afflicted me, and I disliked to ask for water. Then Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) looked at my face and said, “I think you are thirsty.” I said, “Yes.” So he said, “O boy, or girl, give us water to drink.” So I said to myself, “At this very moment they will bring him water in which they will poison him,” and I became distressed because of that. Then the servant came with the water, and he smiled at my face, then said, “O boy, hand me the water.” So he took the water and drank, then handed it to me, and I drank. Then I became thirsty again and disliked to ask for water, so he did as he had done the first time. When the servant came with the cup, I said to myself the like of what I had said the first time. So he took the cup, then drank, then handed it to me, and smiled. Muhammad ibn Hamzah said: This Hāshimī said to me, “And I think that he is as they say.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, said: A group from the people of the outlying regions among the Shiʿah sought permission to enter upon Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). So he permitted them, and they entered. Then they asked him, in a single session, about thirty thousand issues, and he (عليه السلام) answered, while he was ten years old.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Diʿbil ibn ʿAlī, that he entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and he ordered something for him. So he took it and did not praise Allah. He said: So he said to him, “Why did you not praise Allah?” He said, “Then afterwards I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and he ordered something for me, so I said, ‘All praise is for Allah.’ So he said to me, ‘You have become disciplined.’”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbdillah, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: I entered upon Abu Al-Hasan (عليه السلام), and he said: “O Muhammad, an event has occurred to the family of Faraj.” So I said, “ʿUmar has died.” He said: “All praise is for Allah,” until I counted for him twenty-four times. So I said: “My master, had I known that this would please you, I would have come to you barefoot, running.” He said: “O Muhammad, do you not know what he — may Allah curse him — said to Muhammad ibn ʿAli, my father?” He said: I said, “No.” He said: “He spoke to him regarding something, and then said, ‘I think you are intoxicated.’ So my father said: ‘O Allah, if You know that I have reached the evening fasting for You, then make him taste the bitterness of war and the humiliation of captivity.’” So by Allah, not many days passed before his wealth and all that he possessed were ruined; then he was taken captive, and now he has died — may Allah not have mercy on him. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took vengeance against him, and He continues to grant victory to His friends over His enemies.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I prayed with Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) in Masjid al-Musayyab, and he led us in salat in the place of the qiblah, evenly. And it was mentioned that the lote tree in the mosque had been dried up, with no leaves on it. So he called for water and prepared himself beneath the lote tree, and the lote tree came to life, put forth leaves, and bore fruit in that same year.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥajjāl and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from a man from the people of al-Madīnah, from al-Muṭarrifī, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام passed away, and he owed me four thousand dirhams. So I said to myself, “My wealth is gone.” Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام sent word to me: “When tomorrow comes, come to me, and let there be with you a scale and weights.” So I entered upon Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and he said to me: “Abū al-Ḥasan has passed away, and he owes you four thousand dirhams.” I said, “Yes.” Then he lifted the prayer mat that was beneath him, and there were dinars beneath it, so he handed them over to me.

Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah and al-Ḥimyarī, both together, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ʿAlī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī was taken, and he was twenty-five years, three months, and twelve days old. He passed away on Tuesday, with six days having passed from Dhū al-Ḥijjah, in the year two hundred and twenty. He lived after his father for nineteen years, less twenty-five days.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Khayrān al-Asbāṭī, who said: I came to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in al-Madīnah, and he said to me: “What is the news of al-Wāthiq with you?” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, I left him in good health. I am among the people who had most recently seen him; my last meeting with him was ten days ago.” He said: “The people of al-Madīnah are saying that he has died.” So when he said to me, “the people,” I knew that it was he. Then he said to me: “What happened to Jaʿfar?” I said: “I left him in the worst condition of the people, in prison.” He said: “Indeed, he is the صاحب الأمر. What happened to Ibn al-Zayyāt?” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, the people are with him, and the authority is his.” He said: “Indeed, it is an ill omen upon him.” He said: Then he was silent, and said to me: “It is inevitable that the decrees of Allah, the Exalted, and His judgments come to pass. O Khayrān, al-Wāthiq has died, al-Mutawakkil Jaʿfar has taken his seat, and Ibn al-Zayyāt has been killed.” So I said: “When, may I be sacrificed for you?” He said: “Six days after your departure.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, who said: I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), and I said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you. In all matters they sought to extinguish your light and to demean you, until they lodged you in this most repulsive inn, the inn of the vagabonds.” So he said: “Here, O Ibn Saʿīd.” Then he gestured with his hand and said: “Look.” So I looked, and there I was amidst elegant gardens and radiant gardens, in which were excellent fragrant ones, and youths as though they were hidden pearls, and birds, and gazelles, and rivers gushing forth. Then my sight was bewildered and my eye grew weary. So he said: “Wherever we may be, this is made ready for us; we are not in the inn of the vagabonds.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq al-Jallāb, who said: I bought many sheep for Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. He called me and brought me in from the stable of his house to a spacious place that I did not recognize. I began distributing those sheep to whomever he instructed me concerning. Then he sent to Abū Jaʿfar and to his mother and others among those whom he instructed me about. Then I sought his permission to depart for Baghdad to my father, and that was on the Day of al-Tarwiyah. So he wrote to me: “Stay with us tomorrow, then depart.” He said: So I stayed. When the Day of ʿArafah came, I remained with him, and I spent the night of al-Aḍḥā in a portico belonging to him. Then, at the pre-dawn time, he came to me and said: “O Isḥāq, rise.” He said: So I rose, and I opened my eyes, and there I was at my door in Baghdad. He said: Then I went in to my father while I was among my companions, and I said to them: “I was at al-ʿAskar on the Day of ʿArafah, and I came out to Baghdad by the Eid.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāhirī, who said: Al-Mutawakkil became ill from an abscess that appeared on him, and because of it he came near to destruction. No one dared to touch him with iron. So his mother vowed that if he were cured, she would carry to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام a great amount from her wealth. Al-Fatḥ ibn Khāqān said to him, “If only you would send to this man and ask him, for it may well be that he has a description of a remedy by which relief may come to you.” So he sent to him عليه السلام and described his illness to him. The messenger returned to him with the instruction that the pressed residue of sheep fat should be taken, mixed with rosewater, and applied to it. When the messenger returned and informed them, they began mocking his statement. Al-Fatḥ said to him, “By Allah, he is more knowledgeable concerning what he said.” So the residue was brought, and it was prepared as he had said and applied to it. Sleep overcame him and he became calm. Then it opened and what had been inside it came out, and his mother was given glad tidings of his recovery. So she carried to him عليه السلام ten thousand dinars under her seal. Then he recovered from his illness, and al-Baṭḥāʾī al-ʿAlawī informed against him that wealth and weapons were being carried to him عليه السلام. So he said to Saʿīd the chamberlain, “Attack him at night, take whatever wealth and weapons you find with him, and bring it to me.” Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad said: Saʿīd the chamberlain said to me, “I went to his house at night, and I had with me a ladder. I climbed to the roof, and when I descended partway down the steps in the darkness, I did not know how to reach the house. Then he called to me, ‘O Saʿīd, stay where you are until they bring you a candle.’ It was not long before they brought me a candle. So I descended and found that he was wearing a woolen cloak and a woolen cap, and there was a sajjādah upon a mat before him. I had no doubt that he was performing salat (prayer).” He said to me, ‘The rooms are before you.’ So I entered them and searched them, but I found nothing in them. I found the purse in his house sealed with the seal of the mother of al-Mutawakkil, and another sealed bag. He said to me, ‘The place of salat (prayer) is before you.’ So I lifted it and found a sword in an unsheathed cover. I took that and went to him. When he

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Nawfalī, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj said to me that Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wrote to him: “O Muḥammad, put your affairs together and take your precaution.” He said: “So I was putting my affairs together, and I did not know what he had written to me, until a messenger came to me, carried me away from Miṣr in fetters, seized everything I owned, and I remained in prison for eight years.” Then a letter came to me from him in the prison, in which was: “O Muḥammad, do not reside in the district of the western side.” So I read the letter and said: “He writes this to me while I am in prison? Indeed, this is astonishing.” Then it was not long before I was released, and all praise is due to Allah. He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to him asking him about his estates, so he wrote to him: “They will soon be returned to you, and what harm is there to you if they are not returned to you?” Then when Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj went to al-ʿAskar, an order was written for the return of his estates, but he died before that. He said: Aḥmad ibn al-Khaḍīb wrote to Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj asking him about going out to al-ʿAskar. So he wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام seeking his counsel, and he wrote to him: “Go out, for in it will be your relief, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.” So he went out, and he did not remain long except a little while until he died.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Ya'qub informed me, saying: I saw him — meaning Muhammad — before his death at al-'Askar in the evening, and he had received Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, so he looked toward him, and he fell ill the next day. Then I entered upon him to visit him during his illness after some days, while his condition had become severe. So he informed me that he عليه السلام had sent a cloth to him, and he took it, folded it, and placed it beneath his head. He said: Then he was shrouded in it. Ahmad said: Abu Ya'qub said: I saw Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام with Ibn al-Khadib, and Ibn al-Khadib said to him, 'Go on, may I be your ransom.' So he عليه السلام said to him, 'You are the one who will precede.' Then no more than four days passed until the shackle was placed on the leg of Ibn al-Khadib, then his death was announced. He said: It is narrated from him that when Ibn al-Khadib pressed him concerning the house that he was seeking from him, he sent word to him: 'I shall surely seat you, by Allah عز وجل, in a position from which no remnant of you will remain.' So Allah عز وجل took him during those days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, said: I took a copy of the letter of al-Mutawakkil to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام from Yahya ibn Harthamah in the year two hundred and forty-three, and this is its copy. In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. To proceed: the Commander of the Faithful recognizes your worth, observes your kinship, and deems your right obligatory. He considers, regarding you and the people of your household, such matters by which Allah may rectify your condition and theirs, confirm your honor and their honor, and bring blessing and security upon you and upon them, seeking thereby the pleasure of his Lord and the fulfillment of what has been made obligatory upon him concerning you and concerning them. And the Commander of the Faithful has seen fit to remove Abdullah ibn Muhammad from what he had been overseeing of war and salat (prayer) in the city of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, since he was as you mentioned regarding his ignorance of your right and his belittling of your worth, and because of what he imputed to you and ascribed to you of the matter from which the Commander of the Faithful knows your innocence, and the truthfulness of your intention in refraining from pursuing it, and that you did not put yourself forward for it. And the Commander of the Faithful has appointed over that Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, and ordered him to honor you, revere you, comply with your command and your view, and seek nearness to Allah and to the Commander of the Faithful through that. And the Commander of the Faithful longs for you and loves to renew acquaintance with you and to look upon you. So if you are inclined to visit him and remain in his presence for whatever duration you see fit, then you may set out, together with whomever you wish from your household, your mawali, and your attendants, in ease and tranquility, departing when you wish, halting when you wish, and traveling however you wish. And if you would like Yahya ibn Harthamah, the mawla of the Commander of the Faithful, and those with him from the troops, to accompany you, departing with your departure and traveling with your travel, then the decision in that is left to you until you arrive before the Commander of the Faithful. For there is no one among his brothers, his children, the people of his household, and his close associates who holds

Abu al-Tayyib al-Muthannā Yaʿqūb ibn Yāsir narrated to me, saying: Al-Mutawakkil used to say, “Woe to you! The matter of the son of al-Riḍā has wearied me. He refuses to drink with me, or to keep me company in drinking, or for me to find from him any opportunity in this.” So they said to him, “If you cannot get anything from him, then here is his brother Mūsā, a butcher, a musician; he eats, drinks, and pursues passions.” He said, “Send for him and bring him, so that we may use him to create a false impression among the people and say: the son of al-Riḍā.” So he wrote to him, and he was summoned honorably. All of Banū Hāshim, the commanders, and the people received him, on the understanding that when he arrived, he would allot him an estate, build for him in it, transfer to him the wine-drinkers and singing-girls, maintain ties with him, treat him generously, and appoint for him a splendid residence so that he himself could visit him there. When Mūsā arrived, Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام met him at Qanṭarat Waṣīf, a place where arrivals were received. He greeted him, gave him his due right, then said to him, “This man has brought you only to disgrace you and lower your standing, so do not admit to him that you have ever drunk nabīdh at all.” Mūsā said to him, “If he has invited me for this, then what way out do I have?” He said, “Do not diminish your worth and do not do it, for he only intends to dishonor you.” But he refused him, and he repeated it to him. When he saw that he would not respond, he said, “Indeed, this is a gathering upon which you and he shall never be brought together.” Then he remained for three years going early every day, and it would be said to him, “He is occupied today, so leave.” So he would leave. Then it would be said, “He has become intoxicated, so come early.” So he would come early, and it would be said, “He has taken medicine.” This continued for three years until al-Mutawakkil was killed, and he never met with him over it.

Some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, who said: Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd informed me, saying: I fell ill, and a physician came to me at night and prescribed for me a medicine that I should take at night for such-and-such a number of days. But I was not able to obtain it. The physician had not yet gone out the door when Naṣr came to me with a bottle containing that very medicine. He said to me: Abū al-Ḥasan conveys his greetings to you and says to you: Take this medicine for such-and-such a number of days. So I took it and drank it, and I recovered. Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī said: Zayd ibn ʿAlī said to me: The detractor refuses, saying: Where are the ghulāt from this hadith?

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others said: Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Khaqan was in charge of the estates and the land-tax in Qumm, and it occurred in... One day in his gathering, the mention of the 'Alawis and their doctrines came up, and he was intensely hostile toward them. So he said: “I have neither seen nor known in Surra Man Ra'a any man from the 'Alawis like al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Rida in his guidance, composure, chastity, nobility, and generosity, and in the esteem in which his household and Banu Hashim held him, giving him precedence over those among them of greater age and rank; and likewise among commanders, ministers, and the common people.” For one day I was standing near my father while it was his public audience day, when his doorkeepers entered and said, “Abu Muhammad ibn al-Rida is at the door.” He said loudly, “Give him permission.” I was astonished at what I heard from them, that they dared to address a man by his kunyah before my father in his presence, whereas no one was addressed by kunyah before him except a caliph, an heir apparent, or one whom the ruler had ordered to be so addressed. Then a dark-complexioned man entered, of fine stature, handsome face, sound body, and young age; he possessed majesty and awe. When my father saw him, he stood and walked a few steps toward him, and I do not know him to have done this for anyone among Banu Hashim or the commanders. When he came near him, he embraced him, kissed his face and chest, took his hand, seated him upon his own prayer-place, sat beside him facing him, and began speaking with him and offering himself in ransom for him. While I was amazed at what I was seeing from him, the chamberlain entered and said, “Al-Muwaffaq has arrived.” Whenever al-Muwaffaq came to my father, his doorkeepers and elite commanders would precede him and stand in two rows between my father’s sitting place and the door of the house until he entered and departed. Yet my father continued facing Abu Muhammad and speaking with him until he looked toward the private attendants and then said, “Whenever you wish—may Allah make me your ransom.” Then he said to his doorkeepers, “Take him behind the two rows so that this one—meaning al-Muwaffaq—does not see him.” So he rose, and my father rose, embraced him, and he departed. I said to my father’s doorkeepers and servants,

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja'far, who said: Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) wrote to Abu al-Qasim Ishaq ibn Ja'far al-Zubayri about twenty days before the death of al-Mu'tazz: "Remain in your house until the event occurs." Then, when Burayhah was killed, he wrote to him: "The event has occurred, so what do you order me to do?" He wrote back: "This is not the event; it is the other event." Then there occurred, regarding al-Mu'tazz, what occurred. And from him, he said: He wrote to another man: "The son of Muhammad ibn Dawud, 'Abd Allah, will be killed," ten days before his killing. Then, when the tenth day came, he was killed.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, known as Ibn al-Kurdiyy, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja'far, who said: Our circumstances had become constricted, so my father said to me, “Take us along until we go to this man,” meaning Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, “for generosity has been described of him.” So I said, “Do you know him?” He said, “I do not know him, nor have I ever seen him at all.” He said: So we set out toward him, and my father said to me while he was on his way, “How much we need that he order five hundred dirhams for us: two hundred dirhams for clothing, two hundred dirhams for debt, and one hundred for expenses.” And I said to myself, “If only he would order three hundred dirhams for me: one hundred with which I would buy a donkey, one hundred for expenses, and one hundred for clothing, and then I would depart to the mountain.” He said: When we reached the door, his servant came out to us and said, “Let ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm and Muḥammad his son enter.” So when we entered upon him and gave salām, he said to my father, “O ʿAlī, what kept you away from us until this time?” He said, “My master, I felt ashamed to meet you in this condition.” Then when we came out from his presence, his servant came to us and handed my father a purse, saying, “This is five hundred dirhams: two hundred for clothing, two hundred for debt, and one hundred for expenses.” And he gave me a purse and said, “This is three hundred dirhams. Put one hundred toward the price of a donkey, one hundred for clothing, and one hundred for expenses. And do not go out to the mountain; go instead to Sūrāʾ.” So he went to Sūrāʾ and married a woman, and today his income is one thousand dinars; yet despite this he still holds to al-Waqf. Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm said: So I said to him, “Woe to you! Do you want a matter clearer than this?” He said: He replied, “This is a matter upon which we have long proceeded.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū ʿAlī Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥārith al-Qazwīnī narrated to me, saying: I was with my father in Surrā man Raʾā, and my father used to practice veterinary work in the stable of Abū Muḥammad. He said: Al-Mustaʿīn had a mule the like of which had not been seen in beauty and size, and it would refuse its back, the bridle, and the saddle. Trainers had been gathered against it, but it gave them no means to ride it. He said: One of his close companions said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, why do you not send for al-Ḥasan ibn al-Riḍā so that he may come? Either he will ride it, or it will kill him, and you will be relieved of him." He said: So he sent for Abū Muḥammad, and my father went with him. My father said: When Abū Muḥammad entered the residence, I was with him. Abū Muḥammad looked at the mule standing in the courtyard of the house, then turned toward it and placed his hand on its croup. He said: I looked at the mule, and it had sweated until perspiration flowed from it. Then he went to al-Mustaʿīn and greeted him. He welcomed him and brought him near, then said, "O Abū Muḥammad, bridle this mule." So Abū Muḥammad said to my father, "Bridle it, O boy." Al-Mustaʿīn said, "You bridle it." So he put down his cloak, then stood and bridled it, then returned to his seat and sat down. Then he said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, saddle it." So he said to my father, "O boy, saddle it." He said, "You saddle it." So he stood a second time and saddled it, then returned. Then he said to him, "Do you think you can ride it?" He said, "Yes." So he rode it without it resisting him. Then he galloped it in the residence, then set it to a graceful gait, and it walked in the finest manner possible. Then he returned and dismounted. Then al-Mustaʿīn said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, how did you find it?" He said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I have not seen its like in beauty and vigor, and it is only fitting that the like of it should belong to the Commander of the Faithful." He said: Then he said, "O Abū Muḥammad, the Commander of the Faithful has bestowed it upon you." So Abū Muḥammad said to my father, "O boy, take it." So my father took it and led it away.

Ali, from Abi Ahmad ibn Rashid, from Abi Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I complained to Abi Muhammad عليه السلام of need, so he scratched the ground with his whip. He said: And I think he covered it with a cloth, and he brought out five hundred dinars. Then he said: O Aba Hashim, take, and excuse us.
Proceed, for there is no fear upon you, if Allah so wills. So they proceeded safely, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl al-Yamani, who said: A multitude descended upon al-Ja'fari from the family of Ja'far, and he had no ability to face them. So he wrote to Abu Muhammad عليه السلام complaining of that. He عليه السلام wrote to him: “You will be spared that, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.” Then he went out against them with a small band, while the people numbered more than twenty thousand, and he was with fewer than a thousand, and he overcame them.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-'Alawi, who said: Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) was imprisoned with 'Ali ibn Narmash, and he was the most hostile of the people and the harshest of them against the family of Abu Talib. And it was said to him, "Do this to him and do that," but he did not remain with him except for a day until he placed his cheeks before him in submission, and he would not raise his gaze toward him out of reverence and magnification. Then he came out from his presence while he had become the most perceptive of the people regarding him and the best of them in speech about him.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Nakhaʿī, who said: Sufyān ibn Muḥammad al-Ḍubaʿī narrated to me, saying: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام asking him about al-walījah, and it is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “And they did not take, apart from Allah, nor His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, nor the believers, any walījah.” I said to myself: “It is not in the Book—who do you think the believers are here?” Then the reply came back: “Al-walījah is the one who is set up apart from the Walī al-Amr. And your soul has spoken to you about who the believers are in this place; they are the Imams عليهم السلام who pledge security upon Allah, so He ratifies their guarantee.”

Ishaq said: Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari narrated to me, saying: I complained to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the constriction of imprisonment and the heaviness of the shackles. So he wrote to me: "Today you will pray the zuhr salat (prayer) in your home." Then I was brought out at the time of zuhr, and I performed it in my home just as he (peace be upon him) had said. And I was under hardship, so I wanted to ask him for dinars in the letter, but I felt shy. Then when I came to my home, he sent to me one hundred dinars and wrote to me: "If you have a need, then do not be shy and do not hold back; ask for it, for you shall see what you love, if Allah so wills."

Is'haq, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Aqraʿ, who said: Abū Ḥamzah Nuṣayr al-Khādim narrated to me, saying: I heard Abū Muḥammad more than once speaking to his servants in their own languages: Turkish, Roman, and Saqālibah. So I was amazed at that and said: This one was born in al-Madīnah, and he did not appear to anyone until Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed away, and no one had seen him, so how is this? I was speaking to myself about that, when he turned toward me and said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, distinguishes His proof from the rest of His creation by means of everything, and He gives him the languages, knowledge of lineages, lifespans, and events. Were it not for that, there would be no difference between the divine proof and the one over whom the proof is established.

Is'haq, from Al-Aqra‘, who said: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام asking him about the Imam, whether he experiences wet dreams. And I said to myself after the letter had been sent: “Wet dreams are from Satan, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has protected His Awliyā’ from that.” So the reply came: “The state of the Imams عليهم السلام in sleep is their state in wakefulness. Sleep does not change anything in them, and Allah has protected His Awliyā’ from the touch of Satan, just as your own self told you.”

Al-Ḥasan ibn Ẓarīf narrated to me. He said: Two questions stirred within my chest, and I wanted to write concerning them to Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام). So I wrote asking him about al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام): when he rises, by what will he judge, and where will be his assembly in which he judges among the people? And I had wanted to ask him about something for quartan fever, but I omitted mention of the fever. Then the reply came: You asked about al-Qāʾim; when he rises, he will judge among the people by his knowledge, like the judgment of Dāwūd (عليه السلام), and he will not ask for evidence. And you had wanted to ask about quartan fever, but you were made to forget; so write on a sheet and hang it upon the fever-stricken person, and he will recover by the permission of Allah, if Allah wills. O fire, be coolness and peace upon Ibrāhīm. So we hung upon him what Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) had mentioned, and he recovered.

Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib narrated to me, saying: I sat in wait for Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) on the roadside. When he passed by me, I complained to him of my need, and I swore to him that I did not have a single dirham or anything above it, nor any lunch nor dinner. He said: He (عليه السلام) said, "You are swearing by Allah falsely, while you have buried two hundred dinars. What I say is not to withhold the gift from you. O servant, give him what you have." So his servant gave me one hundred dinars. Then he turned to me and said, "You will be deprived of them at the time when you are most in need of them," meaning the dinars that I had buried. And he (عليه السلام) spoke the truth, and it happened just as he said. I had buried two hundred dinars and said, "It will be support and refuge for us." Then I was struck by intense necessity for something to spend, and the doors of livelihood were closed to me. So I dug for it, only to find that a son of mine had come to know its location, taken it, and fled, and I could not recover anything of it.

‘Alī ibn Zayd ibn ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī narrated to me, saying: I had a horse, and I was impressed with it, mentioning it often in gatherings. One day I entered upon Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, and he said to me, “What happened to your horse?” I said, “It is with me, and here it is at your door; I dismounted from it.” He said to me, “Exchange it before evening, if you can find a buyer, and do not delay that.” Then someone entered upon us, and the conversation was cut off. So I rose up thinking and went to my home, and informed my brother of the matter. He said, “I do not know what to say about this.” I was reluctant concerning it and withheld it from people by selling it, and we entered the evening. Then the groom came to us after we had performed the night salat (prayer), and he said, “O my master, your horse has died.” So I became grieved and knew that this was what he had meant by those words. He said: Then I entered upon Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام after some days, while saying to myself, “Would that he replace for me an animal, since I had been grieved by his words.” So when I sat, he said, “Yes, we shall replace an animal for you. O boy, give him my dark brown barḏawn. This is better than your horse, more easy to ride, and longer-lived.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shammun narrated to me; he said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated to me; he said: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) when al-Muhtadī had begun killing the mawālī: “O my master, praise belongs to Allah, who has preoccupied him away from us. It has reached me that he is threatening you and saying: ‘By Allah, I will surely expel them from the face of the earth.’” So Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) wrote in his own hand: “That is shorter for his lifespan. Count five days from this day of yours.” “And he will be killed on the sixth day, after humiliation and abasement that will befall him.” So it happened just as he (عليه السلام) had said.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shamūn narrated to me, saying: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), asking him to supplicate to Allah for me regarding the pain in my eye. One of my eyes had already gone, and the other was on the verge of going, so he wrote back to me: “May Allah preserve your eye for you.” Then the sound one recovered. And he wrote at the end of the letter: “May Allah reward you and make your recompense excellent.” I became distressed because of that, and I did not know anyone among my family who had died. Then after some days, news came to me of the death of my son Ṭayyib, and I then knew that the condolence was for him.

Is'haq said: 'Umar ibn Abī Muslim narrated to me, saying: A man from the people of Egypt, called Sayf ibn al-Layth, came to us in Surr Man Ra'a, complaining to al-Muhtadī about an estate of his which Shafīʿ al-Khādim had usurped from him and from which he had expelled him. So we advised him to write to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام and ask him to facilitate its affair. So Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام wrote to him: 'There is no harm upon you. Your estate will be returned to you, so do not go forward to the ruler. Meet the agent in whose hand the estate is, and frighten him with the Greatest Sovereign, Allah, Lord of the worlds.' So he met him, and the agent in whose hand the estate was said to him: 'It had been written to me at the time of your departure from Egypt that I should seek you out and return the estate to you.' So he returned it to him by the judgment of the judge Ibn Abī al-Shawārib and the testimony of the witnesses, and he had no need to proceed to al-Muhtadī. Thus the estate became his and remained in his possession, and there was no further issue concerning it after that. He said: And this Sayf ibn al-Layth narrated to me, saying: 'I left behind in Egypt, when I departed from it, a son of mine who was ill, and another son of mine older than him who was my trustee and caretaker over my dependants and my estates. So I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام asking him to supplicate for my sick son.' So he wrote to me: 'Your afflicted son has recovered, and the elder one—your trustee and caretaker—has died. So praise Allah and do not grieve in a way that would nullify your reward.' Then the news reached me that my son had indeed recovered from his illness, and that the elder one died on the day the reply of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام reached me.

Yaḥyā ibn al-Qushayrī from a village called Qīr narrated to me; he said: Abū Muḥammad had an agent who had taken for himself a room in the house, and with him there was a white servant. The agent desired the servant for himself, but he refused unless he brought him nabīdh. So he contrived to get nabīdh for him, then brought it in to him, while between him and Abū Muḥammad there were three locked doors. He said: The agent narrated to me, saying: I was alert when suddenly the doors were opening until he himself came and stood at the door of the room. Then he said: O you people, have taqwa of Allah; fear Allah. So when morning came, he ordered that the servant be sold and that I be removed from the house.

Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn al-Rabi' al-Sha'i informed me, saying: I debated a man from the Dualists in al-Ahwaz, then I came to Surra Man Ra'a, while something from his doctrine had remained attached to my heart. As I was sitting at the door of Ahmad ibn al-Khadib, Abu Muhammad عليه السلام approached from the residence of the authorities, heading toward the procession. He looked at me and gestured with his forefinger: 'One, One, Single.' So I fell down unconscious.

Is'haq, from Abū Hāshim al-Ja‘farī, who said: I entered upon Abū Muḥammad one day, while I intended to ask him what I should fashion a ring from so that I might seek blessing through it. So I sat down, and I was made to forget what I had come to him for. Then when I bade farewell and rose, he threw the ring toward me and said: 'You wanted silver, so We gave you a ring. You gained the stone and the crafting cost as well. May Allah bless you with joy, O Abū Hāshim.' So I said: 'O my master, I bear witness that you are the Walī of Allah and my Imam, through obedience to whom I practice my religion before Allah.' He said: 'May Allah forgive you, O Abū Hāshim.'

Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim Abū al-ʿAynāʾ al-Hāshimī, a freed slave of ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī by manumission, narrated to me, saying: I used to enter upon Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), and I would become thirsty while I was with him, but I regarded him with too much reverence to ask for water, so he would say: “O servant, give him water to drink.” And sometimes I would speak within myself about rising to leave and think about that, so he would say: “O servant, his mount.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn 'Abd al-Ghaffar, who said: The Abbasids came to Salih ibn Wasif, and Salih ibn Ali and others from those deviating from this direction also came to Salih ibn Wasif when he had imprisoned Abu Muhammad عليه السلام. So Salih said to them, “What can I do? I had assigned over him two men from the most evil persons I could find, but they have come to a tremendous state through worship, salat (prayer), and fasting.” So I said to the two of them, “What is his condition?” They said, “What can be said about a man who fasts by day and stands the whole night, not speaking and not occupying himself with anything else? Whenever we look at him, our limbs tremble, and there enters into us something we cannot control within ourselves.” So when they heard that, they departed disappointed.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Makfuf narrated to me; he said: Some of our companions narrated to me from some of the phlebotomists of al-ʿAskar who were Christians. That Abu Muhammad عليه السلام sent for me one day at the time of Salat al-Zuhr and said to me, "Perform phlebotomy on this vein." He then showed me a vein that I did not recognize among the veins that are usually opened. So I said to myself, "I have never seen a matter stranger than this: he is ordering me to perform phlebotomy at the time of Zuhr, though it is not a time for phlebotomy, and secondly it is a vein I do not know." Then he said to me, "Wait and remain in the house." When evening came, he called me and said, "Release the blood." So I released it. Then he said to me, "Stop," so I stopped. Then he said to me, "Remain in the house." When it was midnight, he sent for me and said to me, "Release the blood." He said: I was even more astonished than at my first astonishment, and I disliked to ask him. He said: So I released it, and white blood came out as though it were salt. He then said to me, "Restrain it," so I restrained it. Then he said, "Remain in the house." When morning came, he ordered his steward to give me three dinars. I took them and went out until I came to Ibn Bakhtishuʿ the Christian, and I recounted the story to him. He said to me, "By Allah, I do not understand what you are saying, nor do I recognize it in any branch of medicine, nor have I read it in any book. And I do not know in our time anyone more knowledgeable about the books of the Christians than so-and-so the Persian, so go to him." He said: So I hired a boat to al-Basrah, went to al-Ahwaz, then proceeded to فارس to my companion and informed him of the report. He said, "Give me some days." So I gave him time. Then I came to him asking for the answer. He said to me, "This that you are relating from this man was done once by al-Masih in his time."

Ali ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, said: Muhammad ibn Hujr wrote to Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام), complaining about Abd al-Aziz ibn Dulaf and Yazid ibn Abd Allah. So he wrote to him: As for Abd al-Aziz, you have been spared him; and as for Yazid, then for you and for him there is a standing before Allah. Then Abd al-Aziz died, and Yazid killed Muhammad ibn Hujr.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, said: Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) was handed over to Nahrir, and he used to constrain him and harm him. He said: Then his wife said to him, "Woe to you! Be wary of Allah. You do not know who is in your house." And she informed him of his righteousness, and said, "Indeed, I fear for you because of him." So he said, "I will surely throw him among the beasts of prey." Then he did that to him, and he (عليه السلام) was seen standing in salat (prayer) while they were around him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, who said: I entered upon Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام), and I asked him to write for me so that I might look at his handwriting and recognize it when it came. He said: 'Yes.' Then he said: 'O Ahmad, handwriting may differ for you between the thick pen and the fine pen, so do not doubt.' Then he called for the inkpot, and he wrote, and he kept drawing ink from the inkpot's channel. I said to myself while he was writing: 'I will ask him to gift me the pen with which he wrote.' When he finished writing, he turned to speak with me while wiping the pen with the cloth of the inkpot for a while. Then he said: 'Take it, O Ahmad,' and he handed it to me. I said: 'May I be your ransom, I am distressed by something affecting me within myself, and I had wanted to ask your father, but that was not decreed for me.' He said: 'And what is it, O Ahmad?' I said: 'O my master, it has been narrated to us from your forefathers that the sleep of the Prophets is upon their backs, the sleep of the believers is upon their right sides, the sleep of the hypocrites is upon their left sides, and the sleep of the devils is upon their faces.' He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is so.' I said: 'O my master, I strive to sleep on my right side, but I am unable, and sleep does not come to me upon it.' He remained silent for a while, then said: 'O Ahmad, come near me.' So I came near him. He said: 'Put your hand beneath your clothes.' So I put it in. Then he brought out his hand from beneath his clothes and inserted it beneath my clothes, and he wiped with his right hand over my left side and with his left hand over my right side three times. Ahmad said: 'Since he (عليه السلام) did that to me, I have not been able to sleep on my left side, and sleep does not come to me upon it at all.'

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, who said: There came out from Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, when al-Zubayrī was killed: “This is the recompense of one who forged a lie against Allah concerning His Awliya'. He claimed that he would kill me and that I would have no posterity. So how did he see the power of Allah?” And a son was born to him, whom he named M Ḥ M D, in the year two hundred and fifty-six.

Muḥammad and al-Ḥasan, the two sons of ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, narrated to me in the year two hundred and seventy-nine. They said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAbdī of ʿAbd Qays narrated to us, from Ḍawʾ ibn ʿAlī al-ʿIjlī, from a man from the people of فارس, whom he named, who said: I came to Surr Man Raʾā and remained at the door of Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام). He called me without my asking permission, and when I entered and gave salām, he said to me, “O Abā so-and-so, how are you?” Then he said to me, “Sit, O so-and-so,” and then he asked me about a group of men and women from my family. Then he said to me, “What has brought you?” I said, “A desire to be in your service.” He said, “Then remain in the house.” So I was in the house with the servants. Then I began buying necessities for them from the market, and I used to enter upon him without permission when he was in the men’s quarters. One day I entered upon him while he was in the men’s quarters, and I heard movement in the house. So he called out to me, “Stay where you are; do not move.” I did not dare either to go out or to enter. Then a maidservant came out to me carrying something covered. Then he called me, “Enter.” So I entered, and he called the maidservant back. He said to her, “Uncover what is with you.” So she uncovered a fair boy, handsome of face, and uncovered his stomach, and there was hair growing from his upper chest to his navel, greenish, not black. Then he said, “This is your master.” Then he ordered her, and she carried him away. I did not see him after that until Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) passed away. Then Ḍawʾ ibn ʿAlī said: I said to the Persian, “How many years would you estimate for him?” He said, “Two years.” Al-ʿAbdī said: I said to Ḍawʾ, “How many would you estimate?” He said, “Fourteen years.” Abū ʿAlī and Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: “And we estimate for him twenty-one years.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, and from more than one of our companions from Qumm, from Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-'Amiri, from Abu Sa'id Ghanim al-Hindi, who said: I was in the city of India known as interior Kashmir, and I had companions who would sit on chairs to the right of the king—forty men, all of whom read the four books: the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur, and the scrolls of Ibrahim. We used to judge between the people, teach them their religion, and give them legal answers regarding their halal and haram. The people would turn to us, from the king down to those beneath him. Then we discussed the mention of Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and we said: This Prophet mentioned in the books has remained unclear to us, and it is obligatory upon us to investigate him and seek his traces. Our view became united, and we agreed that I should go out and search on their behalf. So I departed with abundant wealth, and traveled for twelve months until I neared Kabul. A group of Turks attacked me, cut me off, took my wealth, wounded me severely, and I was taken to the city of Kabul. When its king learned of my case, he sent me to the city of Balkh, whose governor at that time was Dawud ibn al-'Abbas ibn Abi al-Aswad. News of me reached him—that I had set out from India in search, had learned Persian, and had debated jurists and theologians. So Dawud ibn al-'Abbas sent for me, brought me to his gathering, and assembled the jurists against me. They debated me, and I informed them that I had left my land seeking this Prophet whom I found mentioned in the books. He said to me: Who is he, and what is his name? I said: Muhammad. They said: He is our Prophet whom you seek. So I asked them about his laws, and they informed me. Then I said to them: I know that Muhammad is a Prophet, but I do not know whether he is this one whom you describe or not. So tell me where he is, that I may go to him and ask him about signs and proofs that I have. If he is the one I have sought, I will believe in him. They said: He has passed away صلى الله عليه وآله. I said: Then who is his legatee and successor? They said: Abu Bakr. I said: Name him for me, for that is his kunyah. They said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman, and they traced his lineage to Quraysh. I said: Then give me the lineage of Muhammad, your Prophet. So they gave it to me. Then I said: This is not the one I sought. The one I seek is his successor,

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr, Abū Ṣidām, and a group spoke after the passing of Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) about what was in the hands of the agents, and they wanted to investigate. So al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr came to Abū al-Ṣidām and said, “I intend hajj (pilgrimage).” Abū Ṣidām said to him, “Delay it this year.” Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr said to him, “I am alarmed in my sleep, and I must depart.” He made a bequest to Aḥmad ibn Yaʿlā ibn Ḥammād, and bequeathed wealth to the Nāḥiyah, and instructed him not to release anything except from his hand to his hand after his appearance. He said: al-Ḥasan said, “When I arrived in Baghdād, I rented a house and stayed in it. Then one of the agents came to me with garments and dīnārs and left them with me. I said to him, ‘What is this?’ He said, ‘It is what you see.’ Then another came to me with the like of it, and another, until they filled the house. Then Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq came to me with all that he had with him. I was amazed and remained thinking, then a note from the man (عليه السلام) came to me: ‘When such-and-such of the day has passed, carry what is with you.’” “So I departed and carried what was with me. On the road there was a vagabond highwayman with sixty men, but I passed by him and Allah kept me safe from him. Then I arrived at al-ʿAskar and lodged there. Then a note came to me: ‘Carry what is with you.’ So I packed it in the loads of the porters. When I reached the vestibule, there was a black man standing there. He said, ‘Are you al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Enter.’” “So I entered the house and entered a room and unloaded the porters’ packs. In a corner of the room there was much bread, and each of the porters was given two loaves, and they were sent out. Then there was a room with a curtain over it, and I was called from it: ‘O Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr, praise Allah for what He has bestowed upon you, and do not doubt, for Shayṭān would dearly love that you should doubt.’ Then two garments were brought out to me, and it was said, ‘Take them, for you will need them.’ So I took them and departed.” Saʿd said: “Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr returned, and he died in the month of Ramaḍān, and he was shrouded in the two garments.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Hammawayh al-Suwaydawi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said: I doubted at the time of the passing of Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام), and a great amount of wealth had accumulated with my father. So he carried it and boarded the ship, and I went out with him seeing him off. Then he was struck with a severe illness, and he said: “O my son, take me back, for this is death.” And he said to me: “Be wary of Allah regarding this wealth,” and he entrusted me with his testament; then he died. So I said to myself: “My father would not entrust anything that was not sound. I will carry this wealth to al-Iraq, rent a house on the riverbank, and not inform anyone of anything. If something becomes clear to me with the same clarity as it was in the days of Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام), I will carry it out; otherwise, I will cast it away.” Then I came to al-Iraq and rented a house on the riverbank, and remained for some days. Then suddenly there came to me a note with a messenger, in which was: “O Muhammad, with you is such-and-such inside such-and-such,” until he enumerated to me all that was with me, including what I had not fully known myself. So I handed it over to the messenger. Then I remained for some days during which no recognition was shown to me, and I became distressed. Then there came out to me: “We have established you in the place of your father, so praise Allah.”

Muhammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Nasāʾī, who said: I delivered certain things to al-Marzubānī al-Ḥārithī; among them was a gold bracelet. They were accepted, but the bracelet was returned to me. So I was instructed to break it, and I broke it, and there were inside it weights of iron and copper or brass. So I took them out and sent the gold on, and it was accepted.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl al-Khazzaz al-Mada'ini, the mawla of Khadijah daughter of Muhammad Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, said: A group from the people of al-Madinah, from the Talibiyyin, used to hold to the truth, and the stipends used to come to them at a known time. Then when Abu Muhammad عليه السلام passed away, a group among them turned back from the belief in the son. So the stipends came to those among them who remained firm upon the belief in the son, and they were cut off from the rest. So they are not mentioned among those who are remembered, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad said: A man from the people of al-Sawād delivered some wealth, but it was returned to him, and it was said to him: "Take out the right of the children of your uncle from it, and it is four hundred dirhams." The man had in his possession an estate belonging to the children of his uncle, in which there was a partnership, and he had withheld it from them. Then he examined it, and found that what belonged to the children of his uncle from that wealth was four hundred dirhams. So he took it out and sent the remainder, and it was accepted.

Al-Qāsim ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: A number of sons were born to me, and I used to write and ask for supplication, but nothing would be written back to me concerning them, so they all died. Then when al-Ḥasan, my son, was born to me, I wrote asking for supplication, and I received the reply: 'He will remain,' and all praise is due to Allah.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abi ʿAbdillah ibn Salih, who said: I had gone out in one year of the years in Baghdad. So I sought permission regarding departure, but permission was not granted to me. Thus I remained for twenty-two days, while the caravan had already departed to al-Nahrawan. Then permission was granted to me to depart on Wednesday, and it was said to me: 'Depart on that day.' So I departed while despairing of catching up to the caravan, but I reached al-Nahrawan while the caravan was still there. Then it was only that I fed my camels something before the caravan set out, so I set out as well. And he had supplicated for my safety, so I encountered no harm, and all praise is due to Allah.

ʿAlī, from al-Naḍr ibn Ṣabbāḥ al-Bajalī, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Shāshī, who said: A fistula appeared on my buttock, so I showed it to the physicians and spent wealth on it, but they said, “We do not know any cure for it.” So I wrote a note asking for du'a, and he (عليه السلام) wrote back to me: “May Allah clothe you in well-being and make you with us in this world and the Hereafter.” He said: Not even a Friday passed over me before I was cured, and it became like my palm. Then I called a physician from among our companions and showed it to him, and he said, “We had not known any cure for this.”

Ali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Yamani, who said: I was in Baghdad, and a caravan for the Yemenis had been prepared, and I wanted to go out with it. So I wrote seeking permission concerning that, and there came out: “Do not go out with them, for there is no good choice for you in going out with them, and remain in al-Kufah.” He said: I stayed, and the caravan departed. Then Hanzalah came out against them and overwhelmed them. And I wrote seeking permission to travel by water, but he did not permit me. So I asked about the ships that had gone out upon the sea in that year, and not a single ship among them was saved. A people from India, called al-Bawarij, came out against them and cut them off. He said: I visited al-'Askar, then I came to the passageway at sunset, and I did not speak to anyone nor make myself known to anyone. While I was performing salat (prayer) in the masjid after finishing the ziyarah, suddenly a servant had come to me and said to me, “Rise.” So I said to him, “Then where to?” He said to me, “To the house.” I said, “And who am I? Perhaps you were sent to someone other than me.” He said, “No, I was sent only to you. You are Ali ibn al-Husayn, the messenger of Ja'far ibn Ibrahim.” So he took me along until he lodged me in the house of al-Husayn ibn Ahmad. Then he spoke privately with him, and I did not know what he said to him, until he brought me everything that I needed. And I stayed with him for three days, and I sought his permission for the ziyarah from inside, so he permitted me, and I visited at night.

Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl ibn Zayd al-Yamānī said: My father wrote a letter in his own hand, and its reply came. Then I wrote in my own hand, and its reply came. Then a man from the jurists among our companions wrote in his own hand, but its reply did not come. So we looked into it, and the reason was that the man had become a Qarmaṭī. Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl said: I visited al-ʿIrāq and came to Ṭūs, and I resolved not to depart except upon clear proof regarding my affair and success in my needs, even if I had to remain there until I gave away charity. He said: During that time, my chest would become constricted by staying there, and I feared that the hajj might pass me by. He said: So one day I came to Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad seeking payment from him, and he said to me: Go to such-and-such a mosque, and a man will meet you there. He said: So I went to it, and a man came in to me. When he looked at me, he laughed and said: Do not grieve, for you will perform hajj in this year, and you will return to your family and your child safely. He said: So I was reassured, and my heart became calm, and I would say: This is the confirmation of that, and all praise is for Allah. He said: Then I came to al-ʿAskar, and a pouch came out to me containing dinars and a garment. I became upset and said to myself: Is this my recompense with these people? And I acted ignorantly, so I returned it and wrote a note. The one who took it from me gave me no indication about anything and did not speak of it with a single word. Then after that I regretted with intense remorse and said to myself: I have committed kufr by my rejection against my master. And I wrote a note apologizing for my act, confessing the sin, and seeking forgiveness for that. I sent it and remained wiping myself. While in that state I was thinking to myself and saying: If the dinars are returned to me, I will not untie their pouch, nor will I do anything with them until I carry them to my father, for he is more knowledgeable than I am, so that he may act concerning them as he wishes. Then there came out to the messenger who had brought the pouch to me: You did wrong by not informing the man that we at times do that for those devoted to us, and at times they ask us for that seeking blessing through it. And there came out to me: You erred in rejecting our kindness. But if you seek forgiveness from Allah, then Allah forgives you. As

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said: I doubted regarding the matter of Hajiz, so I gathered a few things, then I went to al-ʿAskar. Then there came out to me: “There is no doubt concerning us, nor concerning the one who stands in our place by our command. Return what is with you to Hajiz ibn Yazid.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Salih, who said: When my father died and the matter came to me, my father had upon the people promissory notes from the debtor’s wealth. So I wrote to him to inform him, and he wrote: “Demand it from them and exact repayment from them.” So the people paid me, except for one man upon whom there was a promissory note for four hundred dinars. I came to him demanding it, but he delayed me, and his son treated me lightly and behaved foolishly toward me. So I complained to his father, and he said, “And what was that?” Then I seized his beard, took hold of his leg, dragged him to the middle of the house, and kicked him many times. So his son went out crying for help to the people of Baghdad, saying: “A man from Qumm, a Rafidi, has killed my father!” Then a crowd of them gathered against me. So I mounted my animal and said: “Well done, O people of Baghdad! You side with the oppressor against the wronged stranger! I am a man from the people of Hamadan, from the people of the Sunnah, and this one attributes me to the people of Qumm and to rejection in order to take away my right and my wealth.” He said: Then they turned against him and wanted to enter his shop, until I calmed them down. Then the owner of the promissory note appealed to me and swore by divorce that he would indeed pay me my money, until I got them away from him.

ʿAlī, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Rizq Allāh, from Badr, the غلام of Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, who said: I came to al-Jabal while I did not hold to the Imamate; I loved them as a whole, until Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh died. During his illness he bequeathed that al-Shihrī al-Samand, his sword, and his belt be delivered to his Mawlā. So I feared that if I did not hand over al-Shihrī to Idhkūtakīn, I would suffer belittlement from him. So I appraised the animal, the sword, and the belt at seven hundred dinars within myself and informed no one of it. Then a letter came to me from al-ʿIrāq: 'Send the seven hundred dinars which are due to us from you, from the price of al-Shihrī, the sword, and the belt.'

Ali, from the one who narrated it to him, said: A son was born to me, so I wrote seeking permission regarding his purification on the seventh day. The reply came: “Do not do it.” Then he died on the seventh day or the eighth. Then I wrote informing of his death, and the reply came: “You will be granted another in his place and another besides him. You shall name him Ahmad, and after Ahmad, Ja‘far.” So it came to pass just as he had said. He said: I prepared for hajj and bade the people farewell, and I was about to depart, when the reply came: “We are averse to that, though the matter is up to you.” He said: My chest became constricted and I became grieved, so I wrote: “I remain committed to hearing and obedience, except that I am grieved by my staying back from hajj.” Then the signed reply came: “Let not your chest be constricted, for you will perform hajj next year, if Allah wills.” He said: And when the following year came, I wrote seeking permission, and permission was granted. Then I wrote: “I have taken Muḥammad ibn al-‘Abbās as my travel companion, and I am confident in his religiosity and trustworthiness.” The reply came: “Al-Asadī is an excellent travel companion, so if he comes, do not prefer anyone over him.” Then al-Asadī came, and I took him as my travel companion.

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAlawī said: Al-Majrūḥ deposited some wealth with Mirdās ibn ʿAlī for the Nāḥiyah, and Mirdās had in his possession some wealth belonging to Tamīm ibn Ḥanẓalah. Then an instruction came to Mirdās: “Dispatch the wealth of Tamīm together with what al-Shīrāzī deposited with you.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Isa al-Uraydi, Abu Muhammad, who said: When Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) passed away, a man from the people of Egypt came to Makkah with wealth for the Nāḥiyah. Disagreement arose over it, so some people said: “Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) passed away without a successor, and the successor is Jaʿfar,” while others said: “Abu Muhammad passed away leaving a successor.” So he sent a man whose kunyah was Abu Talib. He arrived at al-ʿAskar carrying a letter, then went to Jaʿfar and asked him for a proof, and he said: “That is not possible at this time.” Then he went to the door and delivered the letter to our companions, and there came out to him: “May Allah reward you concerning your companion, for he has died. He entrusted the wealth that was with him to a trustworthy person so that he may act regarding it as is required, and his letter has been answered.”

Ali ibn Muhammad said: A man from the people of Abah carried something to deliver to him, and he forgot a sword in Abah. So he sent on what was with him, and he wrote to him: "What is the news of the sword which you forgot?"

Al-Ḥasan ibn Khafīf, from his father, said: He sent servants to the city of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and with them were two servants, and he wrote to Khafīf that he should go out with them, so he went out with them. Then when they arrived at al-Kūfah, one of the two servants drank an intoxicant, and they had not left al-Kūfah until a letter arrived from al-ʿAskar ordering that the servant who drank the intoxicant be sent back and removed from service.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Ali ibn Ghiyath, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, who said: Yazid ibn Abdullah made a bequest of an animal, a sword, and wealth. The price of the animal and other than that was sent, but the sword was not sent. Then there came: 'There was, along with what you sent, a sword, but it did not arrive,' or as he said.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Shadhan al-Naysaburi, who said: Five hundred dirhams less twenty dirhams had been gathered with me, and I disliked sending five hundred dirhams less twenty dirhams. So I weighed out twenty dirhams from my own possession and sent them to al-Asadi, and I did not write what belonged to me in it. Then there came: 'Five hundred dirhams have arrived; twenty dirhams of them are yours.'

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī said: The letter of Abī Muḥammad (عليه السلام) used to arrive concerning the stipend for al-Junayd, the killer of Fāris, and Abī al-Ḥasan and another. So when Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) passed away, a resumption came from the Master regarding the stipend of Abī al-Ḥasan and his companion, and nothing came concerning the matter of al-Junayd. He said: I became grieved because of that, then the news of al-Junayd’s death arrived after that.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: I had a slave-girl with whom I was greatly taken, so I wrote seeking instruction regarding having a child from her. Then there came the reply: “Have a child from her, and Allah does whatever He wills.” So I had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant; then she miscarried, and died.

Ali ibn Muhammad said: Ibn al-‘Ajamī had assigned one-third of his estate to al-Nāḥiyah and wrote this down. Before setting aside the third, he had given some wealth to his son Abī al-Miqdām, and no one had become aware of it. Then he wrote to him: “Where is the wealth that you set aside for Abī al-Miqdām?”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Aqil 'Isa ibn Nasr, said: Ali ibn Ziyad al-Saymari wrote asking for a shroud, so he wrote back to him: “Indeed, you will need it in the year eighty.” Then he died in the year eighty, and he sent the shroud to him a few days before his death.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Imran al-Hamadhani, who said: There were five hundred dinars due from me to al-Nahiyah, and I became distressed because of it. Then I said to myself: I have shops which I bought for five hundred and thirty dinars; I have made them for al-Nahiyah for five hundred dinars, though I did not utter this. So he wrote to Muhammad ibn Ja'far: Take possession of the shops from Muhammad ibn Harun for the five hundred dinars that are owed to us by him.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad said: Jaʿfar sold, among those whom he sold, a Jaʿfarī female child who had been in the house and whom they had been raising. Then one of the ʿAlawīs was sent and informed the buyer of her situation, so the buyer said: “I am content to return her, provided that I not be deprived of anything from her price; so take her.” Then the ʿAlawī went and informed the people of the district of the matter, and they sent to the buyer forty-one dinars and instructed him to hand her over to her owner.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿAlawī said: There was a man among the close companions of Rūzḥusnā, and another was with him. He said to him, “There he is: he collects the funds, and he has agents,” and they named all the agents in the surrounding regions. This was conveyed to ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, the vizier, so the vizier intended to arrest them. Then the ruler said, “Find where this man is, for this is a grave matter.” So ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Sulaymān said, “Let us arrest the agents.” But the ruler said, “No. Rather, send to them some people unknown to them with funds, and whoever among them receives anything, he should be arrested.” He said: Then an order was issued to all the agents that they should not take anything from anyone, that they should refrain from doing so, and that they should feign ignorance of the matter. Then a man infiltrated to Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, whom he did not know, and met him privately. He said, “I have some money that I want to deliver.” Muḥammad said to him, “You are mistaken; I do not know anything about this.” He continued trying gently with him while Muḥammad kept feigning ignorance toward him. Spies were sent out, and all the agents refrained because of what had already been communicated to them.

Ali ibn Muhammad said: A prohibition was issued against visiting the graves of Quraysh and al-Ha'ir. Then, after some months, the vizier called al-Baqta'i and said to him: “Meet the Banu al-Furat and the Bursiyyin, and tell them not to visit the graves of Quraysh, for the caliph has ordered that everyone who visits be checked and seized.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from Abū Hāshim Dāwūd ibn al-Qāsim al-Jaʿfarī, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī (عليه السلام), who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) came, and with him was al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام), while he was leaning on the hand of Salmān. He entered al-Masjid al-Ḥarām and sat down, when a man of fine appearance and clothing approached, greeted Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and he returned the greeting. The man sat and then said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I ask you about three matters. If you inform me of them, I will know that the people have undertaken regarding your affair that which has been decreed against them, and that they are not secure in their worldly life and their Hereafter. But if it is otherwise, I will know that you and they are equal in the matter.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said to him: “Ask me whatever appears to you.” He said: “Inform me about a man: when he sleeps, where does his spirit go? And about a man: how does he remember and forget? And about a man: how does his child resemble the paternal uncles and the maternal uncles?” Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) turned to al-Ḥasan and said: “O Abā Muḥammad, answer him.” He said: al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) answered him. Then the man said: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I have never ceased bearing witness to it. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and I have never ceased bearing witness to that. And I bear witness that you are the وصي of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the one who upholds his proof”—and he pointed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn—“and I have never ceased bearing witness to it. And I bear witness that you are his وصي and the one who upholds his proof”—and he pointed to al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام)—“and I bear witness that al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī is the وصي of his brother and the one who upholds his proof after him.” And I bear witness concerning ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn that he is the one who upholds the affair of al-Ḥusayn after him. And I bear witness concerning Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī that he is the one who upholds the affair of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn. And I bear witness concerning Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad that he is the one who upholds the affair of Muḥammad. And I bear witness concerning Mūsā that he is the one who upholds the affair of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad. And I bear witness concerning ʿAlī ibn M

Likewise, Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: So I said to Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, “O Abū Jaʿfar, I wished that this report had come from a source other than Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh.” He said: “He had narrated to me ten years before the perplexity.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Ja‘far, from al-Hasan ibn Zarif and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: My father said to Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari: “I have a need from you, so when it is easy for you, let me be alone with you so I may ask you about it.” Jabir said to him: “Whichever time you prefer.” So he was alone with him on one of the days, and he said to him: “O Jabir, inform me about the Tablet that you saw in the hand of my mother Fatimah عليها السلام, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and what my mother told you was written in that Tablet.” Jabir said: “I bear witness by Allah that I entered upon your mother Fatimah عليها السلام during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and I congratulated her on the birth of al-Husayn. I saw in her hands a green Tablet, which I thought was of emerald, and I saw in it white writing resembling the color of the sun. So I said to her: ‘May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, what is this Tablet?’ She said: ‘This is a Tablet that Allah gifted to His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله. In it are the name of my father, the name of my husband, the names of my two sons, and the names of the awsiya’ from my descendants, and my father gave it to me to give me glad tidings by that.’” Jabir said: “Then your mother Fatimah عليها السلام gave it to me, so I read it and copied it.” So my father said to him: “Would you, O Jabir, show it to me?” He said: “Yes.” So my father went with him to the house of Jabir, and he brought out a parchment. He said: “O Jabir, look into your writing so that I may read to you.” Jabir looked into the copy and my father read it, and not a single letter differed from another letter. Then Jabir said: “So I bear witness by Allah that I saw it written in the Tablet exactly like this:” “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. This is a writing from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, to Muhammad, His Prophet, His Light, His envoy, His veil, and His guide. The Trustworthy Spirit descended with it from the Lord of the worlds. Magnify, O Muhammad, My names, be grateful for My blessings, and do not deny My favors. Indeed I am Allah; there is no g
