Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah; and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Ja‘far al-Tayyar saying: We were with Mu‘awiyah—I, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Umm Salamah, and Usamah ibn Zayd—and words passed between me and Mu‘awiyah. So I said to Mu‘awiyah: I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله say: I have greater authority over the believers than their own selves; then my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام has greater authority over the believers than their own selves. Then when Ali عليه السلام is martyred, al-Hasan ibn Ali عليهما السلام has greater authority over the believers than their own selves. Then after him, my son al-Husayn عليه السلام has greater authority over the believers than their own selves. Then when he is martyred, his son Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام has greater authority over the believers than their own selves, and you will meet him, O Ali. Then his son Muhammad ibn Ali عليهما السلام has greater authority over the believers than their own selves, and you will meet him, O Husayn. Then it is completed as twelve Imams, nine from the descendants of al-Husayn عليه السلام. Abdullah ibn Ja‘far said: And I called al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Umm Salamah, and Usamah ibn Zayd as witnesses, and they testified for me before Mu‘awiyah. Sulaym said: I had also heard that from Salman, Abu Dharr, and al-Miqdad, and they mentioned that they had heard it from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, from Ḥanān ibn al-Sarrāj, from Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān al-Kisāʾī, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, who said: I attended the funeral of Abū Bakr on the day he died, and I attended ʿUmar when allegiance was pledged to him, while ʿAlī عليه السلام was seated to one side. Then a Jewish youth came forward, handsome of face, radiant, wearing fine clothes, and he was from the descendants of Hārūn. He stood at the head of ʿUmar and said: “O Commander of the Faithful, are you the most knowledgeable of this community regarding their Book and the matter of their Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?” He said: ʿUmar lowered his head, so he said: “It is you whom I mean,” and he repeated the statement to him. Then ʿUmar said to him: “Why is that?” He said: “I have come to you seeking certainty for myself, while doubting in my religion.” So he said: “Take this young man.” He said: “And who is this young man?” He said: “This is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the cousin of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and this is the father of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, the two sons of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and this is the husband of Fāṭimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.” Then the Jew turned toward ʿAlī عليه السلام and said: “Are you as such?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “I wish to ask you about three, and three, and one.” He said: the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام smiled slightly and said: “O Hārūnī, what prevented you from saying seven?” He said: “I will ask you about three; if you answer me, I will ask about what comes after them, and if you do not know them, I will know that there is no knowledgeable one among you.” ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Then I ask you by the God whom you worship: if I answer you regarding all that you want, you must surely leave your religion and enter into my religion.” He said: “I came only for that.” He said: “Then ask.” He said: “Inform me about the first drop of blood that dripped upon the face of the earth—which drop was it? And the first spring that gushed forth upon the face of the earth—which spring was it? And the first thing that shook upon the face of the earth—which thing was it?” Then the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام answered him. Then he said to him: “Inform me about the other three. Inform me about Muḥammad صلى

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Sa'id al-'Usfuri, from 'Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed Allah created Muhammad and 'Ali and eleven from his descendants from the light of His magnificence. Then He established them as forms in the radiance of His light, worshipping Him before the creation of creation. They glorified Allah and declared His holiness, and they are the Imams from the descendants of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Khashshāb, from Ibn Samāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “The twelve Imams from the family of Muḥammad (عليهم السلام), all of them are muḥaddath, from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and from the offspring of ʿAlī; and the Messenger of Allah and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) are the two fathers.” Then ʿAlī ibn Rāshid said: “There was a brother of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn through his mother, and he denied that.” So Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) became stern and said: “Indeed, the son of your mother was one of them.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Mas‘adah ibn Ziyad, from Abu ‘Abdillah; and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibrahim, from Abu Yahya al-Mada’ini, from Abu Harun al-‘Abdi, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said: I was present when Abu Bakr died and appointed ‘Umar. A Jew from the leading men of the Jews of Yathrib came forward, and the Jews of al-Madinah claimed that he was the most knowledgeable of the people of his time, until he was brought to ‘Umar. He said to him: “O ‘Umar, I have come to you desiring Islam. If you inform me about what I ask you concerning, then you are the most knowledgeable of the companions of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the Book, the sunnah, and all that I wish to ask about.” He said: ‘Umar said to him: “I am not in that rank, but I shall direct you to the one who is the most knowledgeable of our ummah regarding the Book, the sunnah, and all that you may ask about, and he is that one.” He then pointed to ‘Ali عليه السلام. The Jew said to him: “O ‘Umar, if this is as you say, then what right have you to the people’s bay‘ah, when that one is the most knowledgeable among you?” So ‘Umar rebuked him. Then the Jew went to ‘Ali عليه السلام and said to him: “Are you as ‘Umar described?” He said: “And what did ‘Umar say?” So he informed him. He said: “If you are as he said, I will ask you about matters which I wish to know whether anyone among you knows them, so that I may know that in your claim you are the best of communities and the most truthful of them; and with that, I will enter into your religion, Islam.” Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام said: “Yes, I am as ‘Umar described to you. Ask whatever occurs to you, and I will inform you of it, if Allah wills.” He said: “Inform me about three, and three, and one.” ‘Ali عليه السلام said to him: “O Jew, why did you not say: inform me about seven?” The Jew said to him: “If you inform me of the three, I shall ask you about the rest; otherwise, I shall refrain. If you answer me regarding these seven, then you are the most knowledgeable of the people of the earth, the most excellent of them, and the worthiest of people over the people.” He said to him: “Ask whatever occurs to you, O Jew.” He said: “Inform me about the first stone placed upon the face of the earth, the first tree planted upon the face of the earth, and the first spring that gushed forth upon the face of the

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, who said: I entered upon Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), and before her was a tablet in which were the names of the successors from her offspring. So I counted twelve; the last of them was al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام). Three of them were named Muḥammad, and three of them were named ʿAlī.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, Allah sent Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) to the jinn and humankind, and after him He appointed twelve successors. Among them are those who passed before, and among them are those who remained; and with every successor a sunnah proceeded. The successors after Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) are upon the sunnah of the successors of Isa, and they were twelve, and Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was upon the sunnah of al-Masih.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together from al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Harish, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام, that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: To Ibn Abbas: Indeed, Laylat al-Qadr is in every year, and in that night the command of the year descends, and for that command there are authorities after Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. So Ibn Abbas said, 'Who are they?' He said, 'I and eleven from my loins, Imams who are muhaddathun.'

And by this chain, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said to his companions: Believe in Laylat al-Qadr, for it shall be for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, and for his eleven descendants after me.

And by this chain, Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) said: To Abū Bakr one day, Do not reckon those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive, receiving provision from their Lord. And I testify that Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), the Messenger of Allah, died as a martyr. By Allah, he will surely come to you, so be certain when he comes to you, for Shayṭān cannot take on his likeness. Then ʿAlī took Abū Bakr by the hand and showed him the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله). So he said to him: O Abū Bakr, believe in ʿAlī and in eleven of his descendants. They are like me except for prophethood. And repent to Allah from that which is in your hand, for you have no right in it. He said: Then he went away and was not seen.

Abu ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from ʿAlī ibn Samāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: The twelve Imams from the family of Muḥammad, all of them are muḥaddath, from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the offspring of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام). Thus, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) are the two parents.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Saʿīd ibn Ghazwān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There shall be nine Imams after al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, the ninth of them being their Qāʾim.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, from Abān, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū Ja‘far (عليه السلام) saying: “We are twelve Imams. Among them are Hasan and Husayn, then the Imams are from the offspring of Al-Husayn (عليه السلام).”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Abī Saʿīd al-ʿUṣfūrī, from ʿAmr ibn Thābit, from Abī al-Jārūd, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, I and twelve from my offspring, and you, O ʿAlī, are the anchor of the earth — meaning its pegs and its mountains. By us, Allah has fastened the earth lest it sink with its inhabitants. So when the twelve from my offspring go away, the earth will sink with its inhabitants, and they will not be granted respite.”

And by this chain, from Abī Saʿīd, raising it, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: From my offspring are twelve naqībs, noble ones, muhaddathūn, ones granted understanding. The last of them is al-Qāʾim bi-al-Ḥaqq, who will fill it with justice just as it had been filled with tyranny.

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Karram, who said: I swore within myself that I would never eat food during the day until the Qa'im of the family of Muhammad rises. Then I entered upon Abu Abdullah عليه السلام and said to him: A man from your Shi'a has made it binding upon himself for Allah that he will not eat food during the day ever until the Qa'im of the family of Muhammad rises. He said: Then fast, O Karram, but do not fast on the two Eids, nor the three days of al-Tashriq, nor when you are traveling, nor when ill. For when al-Husayn عليه السلام was killed, the heavens and the earth and those upon them and the angels cried out and said: Our Lord, grant us permission to destroy creation until we renew them from the face of the earth, because they violated Your sanctity and killed Your chosen one. So Allah revealed to them: O My angels, O My heavens, and O My earth, be still. Then He uncovered a veil from among the veils, and behind it were Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his twelve legatees عليهم السلام, and He took the hand of that one, the Qa'im, from among them, and said: O My angels, O My heavens, and O My earth, by this one I shall grant victory for this one. He said it three times.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Talib, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I, Abu Basir, and Muhammad ibn Imran, the mawla of Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, were in his house in Makkah. Muhammad ibn Imran said, "I heard Abu Abdillah عليه السلام saying: 'We are twelve muhaddathun.'" Abu Basir said to him, "Did you hear it from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام?" So he made him swear once or twice that he had heard it. Then Abu Basir said, "But I heard it from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, all together from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah, the Exalted, revealed to ʿImrān: “I am granting you a sound, blessed male child who will cure the blind and the leper, and bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah, and I will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel.” So ʿImrān informed his wife Ḥannah of that, and she was the mother of Maryam. Then when she conceived, in her own mind she thought that her pregnancy was a boy. Then when she gave birth to her, she said: “My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female.” “And the male is not like the female” — meaning: a daughter would not be a Messenger. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And Allah knew better what she had delivered.” So when Allah, the Exalted, granted ʿĪsā to Maryam, he was the one about whom ʿImrān had been given glad tidings and promised. Thus, when we say something about a man from among us, and it comes to be in his son or the son of his son, then do not deny that.

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar al-Yamānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: If we say something concerning a man, and it is not in him but is in his son or the son of his son, then do not deny that, for Allah, Exalted is He, does whatever He wills.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Abī Khadījah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: A man may rise with justice or with tyranny, and it is attributed to him, while he did not actually rise with it; then that may be his son or his grandson after him, so that is indeed what was meant.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Zayd Abī al-Ḥasan, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abī Nuʿaym, who said: I came to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) while he was in al-Madīnah, and I said to him: Upon me is a vow between al-Rukn and al-Maqām that, if I meet you, I will not leave al-Madīnah until I know whether you are the Qāʾim of the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم or not. But he did not answer me with anything. So I stayed for thirty days. Then he met me on a road and said: O Ḥakam, are you still here? I said: Yes, I informed you of what I had made binding upon myself for Allah, but you neither instructed me nor forbade me regarding anything, and you did not answer me with anything. He said: Come to me early tomorrow morning at the house. So I went to him in the morning, and he (عليه السلام) said: Ask about your need. So I said: I made binding upon myself for Allah a vow, fasting, and charity between al-Rukn and al-Maqām that, if I were to meet you, I would not leave al-Madīnah until I knew whether you are the Qāʾim of the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم or not. If it is you, I will remain attached to you; and if it is not you, I will travel through the land and seek livelihood. He said: O Ḥakam, all of us are Qāʾim by the command of Allah. I said: Then are you al-Mahdī? He said: All of us guide to Allah. I said: Then are you the صاحب السيف, the possessor of the sword? He said: All of us are possessors of the sword and inheritors of the sword. I said: Then are you the one who will kill the enemies of Allah, through whom the friends of Allah will be strengthened, and through whom the religion of Allah will become manifest? He said: O Ḥakam, how could I be that one when I have reached forty-five years of age, while the صاحب هذا الأمر, the master of this affair, is more recently acquainted with milk than I am and lighter upon the back of a riding animal?

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Abū Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about al-Qāʾim, so he said: All of us are قائم by the command of Allah, one after another, until the Owner of the Sword comes. Then when the Owner of the Sword comes, he will come with a matter other than that which had been.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Batal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: "The Day We shall call every people by their Imam." He عليه السلام said: "Their Imam is the one who is present among them, and he is the Qa'im of the people of his time."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir, by his chain, raising it, said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Whoever claims that the Imam needs what is in the hands of the people, then he is a disbeliever. Rather, it is the people who are in need that the Imam accept from them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “Take charity from their wealth, by which you cleanse them and purify them.”

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Isa ibn Suleyman al-Nahhas, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Khaybari and Yunus ibn Zabyan, both of whom said: We heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: There is nothing more beloved to Allah than bringing out dirhams to the Imam, and Allah shall indeed make for him, in Paradise, the dirham like Mount Uhud. Then he said: Allah, the Exalted, says in His Book: Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him many times over? He said: By Allah, it is specifically regarding maintaining support of the Imam.

And by this chain, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥammād ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Muʿādh, the صاحب of the cloaks, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: Indeed, Allah did not ask His creatures for a loan from what is in their hands out of any need on His part for that; and whatever right belongs to Allah, it is only for His Guardian.

I asked him about the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Who is there that will lend to Allah a good loan, so He will multiply it for him, and for him is a noble reward. He said: It was revealed regarding helping the Imam.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mayyāḥ, from his father, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “O Mayyāḥ, a dirham by which the Imam is supported is greater in weight than Uḥud.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from one of his men, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: A dirham by which the Imam is supported is superior to two thousand thousand dirhams spent in other aspects of righteousness.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, I take the dirham from one of you, while I am surely among the wealthiest of the people of al-Madīnah in possessions. I intend by that nothing except that you may be purified.”

Safwan ibn Yahya and Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Khalid Al-Kabuli, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'So believe in God and His Messenger and the Light which We sent down.' He said: 'O Abu Khalid! The Light, by God, are the Imams from the progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) until the Day of Resurrection. And they, by God, are the Light of God which He sent down; and they, by God, are the Light of God in the heavens and in the earth, by God!' O Abu Khalid! The light of the Imam in the hearts of the believers is more radiant than the brilliant sun by day. And they, by God, illuminate the hearts of the believers, and God, Mighty and Majestic, veils their light from whomever He wills, and their hearts are darkened. By God, O Abu Khalid! No servant loves us and takes us as his guardians until God purifies his heart; and God does not purify the heart of a servant until he submits to us and is at peace with us. So when he is at peace with us, God grants him safety from the severity of the Reckoning and secures him from the greatest terror of the Day of Resurrection.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, by his chain (of narration), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of God the Exalted: 'Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the Ummi, whom they find written down with them in the Torah and the Gospel — who enjoins upon them good and forbids them evil, and makes lawful to them the good things and makes unlawful to them the impure things' — up to His words: 'and they follow the Light which was sent down with him; those are the successful ones.' He said: 'The Light in this passage is Ali, the Commander of the Faithful, and the Imams (peace be upon them).'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'God has given the People of the Book a lot of good.' He said: 'And what is that?' I said: 'The word of God the Exalted: [28:52] Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they are believers in it — up to His words: [28:54] Those shall be given their reward twice because they were patient.' He (the narrator) said: Then he (the Imam) said: 'God has given you just as He gave them.' Then he recited: [57:28] O you who believe! Fear God and believe in His Messenger: He will give you two portions of His mercy, and make for you a light by which you will walk. meaning an Imam you follow.

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani, from Ali ibn Asbat and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God the Exalted: 'So believe in God and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down' He said: 'O Abu Khalid, the Light, by God, are the Imams (peace be upon them). O Abu Khalid, the light of the Imam in the hearts of the believers is more radiant than the bright sun by day. And they are those who illuminate the hearts of the believers. And God withholds their light from whomever He wills, so their hearts are darkened and they are covered by it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Amraki ibn Ali — all of them from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the word of Allah the Exalted: 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; the parable of His light is as a niche' — that is Fatima (peace be upon her); 'in which is a lamp' — that is al-Hasan; 'the lamp is in a glass' — that is al-Husayn; 'the glass is as if it were a brilliant star' — Fatima is a brilliant star among the women of the people of this world; 'kindled from a blessed tree' — that is Ibrahim (peace be upon him); 'an olive tree, neither eastern nor western' — neither Jewish nor Christian; 'whose oil would almost glow' — knowledge almost bursts forth from her; 'even if no fire had touched it — Light upon Light' — an Imam from her after an Imam; 'Allah guides to His Light whomever He wills' — Allah guides to the Imams whomever He wills; 'and Allah strikes examples for the people.' I said: (What about) 'Or like utter darknesses?' He said: The first one and his companion — 'waves cover him' — the third one; 'above him waves, darknesses' — the second one — 'one above another' — Muawiya and the strife of Banu Umayya. When the believer extends his hand in the darkness of their trial, he can barely see it. And whoever Allah does not give light — an Imam from the progeny of Fatima (peace be upon her) — he has no light of an Imam on the Day of Resurrection. And he said regarding His word: 'their light runs before them and on their right hands' — the Imams of the believers, on the Day of Resurrection, will run before the believers and on their right, until they lodge them in the dwellings of the people of Paradise.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Musa ibn Umar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). He said: I asked him about the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'They intend to extinguish the light of God with their mouths' [61:8]. He said: 'They intend to extinguish the wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) with their mouths.' I said: His words, the Exalted: 'but God will complete His light.' He said: 'He means: And God will complete the Imamate; and the Imamate — it is the Light.' And this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'Believe in God and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down' [64:8]. He said: 'The Light — it is the Imam.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays, who said: I heard Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام saying: “By Allah, we are those whom Allah meant by ‘the near of kin,’ those whom Allah paired with Himself and His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.” So He said: “Whatever Allah restores to His Messenger from the people of the towns, it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin, and the orphans, and the needy.” Specifically from us; and He did not assign for us a share in the charity. Allah honored His Prophet and honored us above feeding us the impurities of what is in the hands of the people.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted: And know that whatever you gain from anything, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin. He said: They are the relatives of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and the khums is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for us.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Al-Anfāl are what no cavalry horse nor riding-beast was urged against, or a people who made peace, or a people who gave with their own hands, and every ruined land, and the interiors of the valleys. So it belongs to Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله), and it is for the Imam after him; he places it wherever he wills.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from some of our companions, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ (عليه السلام), who said: The khums is from five things: from spoils, diving, treasures, mines, and salt-works. The khums is taken from each of these categories and assigned to those for whom Allah, the Exalted, has appointed it, while the remaining four-fifths are distributed among those who fought for it and administered it. The khums is divided into six shares: a share for Allah, a share for the Messenger of Allah, a share for the near relatives, a share for the orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the stranded traveler. The share of Allah and the share of the Messenger of Allah belong, by inheritance, to those vested with authority after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), so he has three shares: two shares by inheritance and one share apportioned to him from Allah; thus he has half of the complete khums, and the remaining half is for the people of his household. A share is for their orphans, a share for their poor, and a share for their stranded travelers; it is distributed among them according to the Book and the sunnah (prophetic tradition), in whatever suffices them for their year. If anything remains beyond them, it belongs to the wali, and if it falls short of their sufficiency, then it is upon the wali to spend from what is with him in the measure that suffices them. It only became obligatory upon him to maintain them because what remains beyond them belongs to him. Allah made this khums specifically for them, to the exclusion of the poor among the people and their stranded travelers, as compensation for them in place of the charities of the people, as a purification from Allah for them due to their kinship with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and as an honor from Allah for them above the impurities of the people. So He assigned specifically for them, from Himself, that by which He enriches them so as not to place them in a position of humiliation and need. There is no harm in the charities of some of them being given to others among them. Those for whom Allah has appointed the khums are the relatives of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) whom Allah mentioned when He said: And warn your nearest kindred. They are Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib themselves, their males and their females. No one from the households

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from one of our companions — whom I think was al-Sayyārī — from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said: When Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام) came to al-Mahdī, he saw him restoring wrongfully taken rights. So he said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why is our grievance not being redressed?” He said to him, “And what is that, O Abū al-Ḥasan?” He said: “When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, granted to His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) Fadak and what was around it, no cavalry or riding beasts had been sent against it.” So Allah sent down upon His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله): “And give the near relative his due.” But the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not know who they were, so he referred that matter to Jibrāʾīl, and Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) referred it to his Lord. Then Allah revealed to him: “Hand over Fadak to Fāṭimah (عليها السلام).” So the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) called her and said to her: “O Fāṭimah, Allah has commanded me to hand over Fadak to you.” She said: “I have accepted, O Messenger of Allah, from Allah and from you.” Her agents remained in it during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). Then when Abū Bakr assumed authority, he expelled her agents from it. So she came to him and asked him to return it to her. He said to her: “Bring me a black or a red one to testify for you concerning that.” So she brought Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) and Umm Ayman, and they testified for her. Thus he wrote for her an order that there be no interference. She left with the document in her possession, and ʿUmar met her and said: “What is this with you, O daughter of Muḥammad?” She said: “A document that Ibn Abī Quḥāfah wrote for me.” He said: “Show it to me.” But she refused, so he snatched it from her hand, looked at it, then spat in it, effaced it, and tore it up. Then he said to her: “Your father did not send cavalry or riding beasts against this, so put ropes around our necks.” Then al-Mahdī said to him: “O Abū al-Ḥasan, define its boundaries for me.” He said: “One boundary of it is Mount Uḥud, another boundary of it is al-ʿArīsh of Egypt, another boundary of it is the seacoast, and another boundary of it is Dūmat al-Jandal.” He said to him: “All of this?” He said: “Yes, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, all of this. All of this is among that over whose people the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not advance w

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying: Al-Anfāl is the nafal. And in Sūrat al-Anfāl there is cutting off the nose.

He was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And know that whatever you gain of anything, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives. So it was said to him: “Then what belonged to Allah, for whom is it?” He said: “For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and what belonged to the Messenger of Allah, then it is for the Imam.” Then it was said to him: “What do you see if one category among the categories is more and another category is less—what is done with it?” He said: “That is up to the Imam. Have you seen how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to act? Was it not that he only gave according to what he saw? Likewise is the Imam.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام). He was asked about the mines of gold, silver, iron, lead, and brass, so he said: “Upon them is khums (the one-fifth tax).”

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Zurārah, who said: The Imam عليه السلام grants stipends, gives extra allotments, and gives whatever he wishes before the shares are apportioned. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fought with a people and did not assign for them any share in the fayʾ, and if he had wished, he could have distributed that among them.

I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “And know that whatever you gain from anything, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin.” So Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ (عليه السلام), with his elbows upon his knees, then gestured with his hand and said: “By Allah, it is the profit day by day.” “Except that my father made his Shiʿah to be in allowance, so that they may be purified.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the khums, so he said: "It is upon everything that the people derive benefit from, whether little or much."

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn Yazīd, who said: I wrote: ‘May I be your ransom, teach me what the profit is and what its limit is. In your view—may Allah, Exalted is He, keep you—please favor me with clarifying that, so that I may not remain persisting upon something haram, with neither salat nor sawm for me.’ So he wrote: ‘The profit is from what comes to you in trade, from its gain, and from cultivated produce after expenses, or from a gift.’

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: I wrote to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): "Khums—should I pay it before the expenses, or after the expenses?" So he wrote: "After the expenses."

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Everything over which fighting took place upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is the Messenger of Allah, then its khums belongs to us, and it is not halal for anyone to buy anything from the khums until our right reaches us.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Nafi', who said: We sought permission to enter upon Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام), and sent word to him, so he sent word back to us: 'Enter two by two.' So I entered, along with a man who was with me, and I said to the man, 'I would like you to ask permission regarding the question.' He said, 'Yes.' So he said to him, 'May I be made your ransom, my father was among those whom Banu Umayyah took captive. I have known that Banu Umayyah had no right to forbid or permit, and that they possessed no right, whether little or much, in what was in their hands; rather, that belonged to you. So when I remember the condition in which I was, there enters into me from that something that nearly corrupts my mind in my present state.' So he said to him, 'You are absolved with respect to whatever there was of that, and everyone after me who is in a condition like yours is absolved from that.' He said: Then we stood up and went out, and Mu'attib preceded us to the group who were sitting and waiting for the permission of Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام). He said to them, ''Abd al-'Aziz ibn Nafi' has attained something the like of which no one has ever attained at all.' It was said to him, 'What is that?' So he explained it to them. Then two men stood and entered upon Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام), and one of them said, 'May I be made your ransom, my father was among the captives of Banu Umayyah, and I have known that Banu Umayyah had no right in any of that, whether little or much, and I would like you to make me absolved from that.' He said, 'And is that for us? That is not for us. We have no right to permit nor to forbid.' So the two men went out, and Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام) became angry. Then no one entered upon him that night except that Abu 'Abd Allah (عليه السلام) began by saying to him, 'Do you not wonder at so-and-so? He comes to me seeking from me legalization regarding what Banu Umayyah did, as though he thinks that belongs to us.' And no one benefited that night, whether by little or much, except the first two, for they had been sufficed regarding their need.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Zurays al-Kunasi, who said: Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: "From where did zina enter upon the people?" I said, "I do not know, may I be made your ransom." He (عليه السلام) said: "From the side of our khums, the khums of Ahl al-Bayt, except for our Shi'ah, the pure ones; for it is made halal for them for the sake of their birth."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Shuʿayb, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “We are a people whose obedience Allah has made obligatory. The anfal belong to us, and the choicest part of wealth belongs to us.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Rifāʿah, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding: The man who dies having no inheritor and no master—he عليه السلام said: “He is among the people meant by this verse.” “They ask you concerning al-anfāl.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. About buried treasure: how much is due on it? He عليه السلام said: "The khums." And about minerals: how much is due on them? He عليه السلام said: "The khums." Likewise, lead, brass, and iron, and everything that is from the minerals—there is taken from them what is taken from gold and silver.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṣabbāḥ al-Azraq, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said: Indeed, among the most severe circumstances for the people on the Day of qiyamah is that the صاحبُ الْخُمُسِ should stand and say: “O my Lord, my khums.” And we have made that lawful for our Shi'ah so that their births may be wholesome and their births may be purified.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about what is brought out from the sea, such as pearls, ruby, and chrysolite, and about the mines of gold and silver—what is due regarding them? He عليه السلام said: When its value reaches one dīnār, then khums is due on it.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said: I wrote to him: ‘O my Master! A man is given some wealth with which he is to perform hajj. Is khums due upon him regarding that wealth when it comes into his possession, or upon what remains in his hand after the hajj?’ So he عليه السلام wrote: ‘Khums is not upon him.’

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: Al-Rida عليه السلام sent a gift to my father, so my father wrote to him: ‘Is khums due upon me concerning what you sent to me?’ He wrote to him: ‘There is no khums upon you regarding what the owner of the khums sends.’

Sahl, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام): 'Ali ibn Mahziyar read to me the letter of your father (عليه السلام) concerning what he obligated upon the owners of estates: half of the sixth after the expenses, and that there is not upon one whose estate does not meet its expenses half of the sixth nor anything other than that. Then those with us differed regarding that, and they said: 'Khums is obligatory upon the estates after the expenses—meaning the expenses of the estate and its land-tax—not the expenses of the man and his dependants.' So he (عليه السلام) wrote: 'After his expenses and the expenses of his dependants, and after the land-tax of the ruling authority.'

Muḥammad ibn Zayd al-Ṭabarī narrated to me. He said: A man from the merchants of Fārs, from among some of the mawālī of Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, wrote to him asking permission concerning the khums. So he wrote to him: In the Name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the All-Compassionate. Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, Generous. He has guaranteed reward for deeds, and anxiety upon constriction. No wealth is halal except through a means that Allah has made halal. And indeed the khums is our support for our religion, for our dependants, for our mawālī, and for what we expend and purchase for the protection of our honor against those whose assault we fear. So do not withhold it from us, and do not deprive yourselves of our du'a for as much as you are able. For paying it is the key to your sustenance, the purification of your sins, and what you send ahead for yourselves for the day of your need. And the Muslim is the one who fulfills for Allah what he has pledged to Him, and the Muslim is not one who answers with the tongue while opposing with the heart. And peace.

And by this chain, from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, who said: A group from Khurāsān came to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام and asked him to release them from the khums. So he said: “How barren this is! You profess pure affection for us with your tongues, yet you withhold from us a right that Allah has appointed for us and has assigned us to it, and it is the khums.” “We do not make it lawful, we do not make it lawful, we do not make it lawful for any one of you.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, who said: I was in the presence of Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī (عليه السلام) when Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad ibn Sahl entered upon him, and he used to administer the waqf for him in Qumm. He said, “O my master, release me from liability for ten thousand, for I have spent it.” So he said to him, “You are released.” Then when Ṣāliḥ left, Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “One of them pounces upon the wealth that is the right of the family of Muḥammad, their orphans, their needy ones, their poor ones, and their stranded travelers, and takes it; then he comes to me saying, ‘Release me from liability.’ Do you think he supposed that I would say, ‘I will not do so’? By Allah, Allah will surely question them on the Day of Resurrection about that with an intense questioning.”

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Aba ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about ambergris and diving for pearls, so he عليه السلام said: “Khums is due upon it.”

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all together — from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whatever Ali (peace be upon him) came with, I take hold of it, and whatever he forbade from, I refrain from it. It flows for him from merit the like of what flowed for Muhammad (may God bless him and his family), and for Muhammad (may God bless him and his family) the merit is over all of what God, Mighty and Majestic, created. The one who disputes him in any of his rulings is like the one who disputes God and His Messenger, and the one who rejects him in a small or large matter stands at the limit of shirk with God. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was the Gate of God which cannot be approached except through him, and His Path such that whoever travels by other than it perishes. And likewise do the Imams of Guidance proceed one after another — God made them the pillars of the earth lest it shake with its inhabitants, and His far-reaching proof over those above the earth and those beneath the soil. And Amir al-Mu'minin (the blessings of God be upon him) used to say often: 'I am God's Distributor between Paradise and the Fire; I am the Greatest Differentiator; I am the owner of the Staff and the Branding Iron. All the angels, the Spirit, and the Messengers have acknowledged to me the like of what they acknowledged to Muhammad (may God bless him and his family), and I have been loaded with the like of his burden — and it is the burden of the Lord. And indeed the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) will be called and clothed, and I will be called and clothed; he will be questioned and I will be questioned, then I shall speak at the level of his speech. And I have been given qualities that no one before me has preceded me to: I was taught the deaths, the tribulations, the lineages, and the decisive speech. Nothing that came before me has escaped me, and nothing that is hidden from me has escaped me. I give glad tidings by the permission of God, and I fulfill on His behalf — all of that is from God who has empowered me with His knowledge.' Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur al-'Ammi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: Al-Mufaddal narrated to us saying, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon hi

Sa'eed al-A'raj narrated to us saying: I and Sulayman ibn Khalid went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he initiated [the conversation], saying: 'O Sulayman! Whatever has come from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), take with it, and whatever he forbade, refrain from it. The merit that flowed for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed for him, and for the Messenger of Allah is the merit over all of Allah's creation. One who finds fault with Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) regarding anything from his rulings is like one who finds fault with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and with His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And one who rejects him in something small or large is on the boundary of shirk with Allah. 'O Sulayman! Whatever has come from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), take with it, and whatever he forbade, refrain from it. The merit that flowed for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed for him, and for the Messenger of Allah is the merit over all of Allah's creation. One who finds fault with Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) regarding anything from his rulings is like one who finds fault with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and with His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And one who rejects him in something small or large is on the boundary of shirk with Allah. Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of Allah be upon him) was Allah's Door that cannot be accessed except through it, and His Way, such that whoever travels by other than it will perish. And by that, the Imams (peace be upon them) proceeded, one after another. Allah made them the pillars of the earth lest it shake with its inhabitants, and His conclusive proof upon those above the earth and those beneath the soil. Then he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: I am Allah's Distributor between Paradise and the Fire, I am the Great Differentiator, and I am the owner of the staff and the branding iron. All of the angels and the Spirit have acknowledged for me the likes of what they acknowledged for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). And I have been loaded with the likes of Muhammad's burden (peace be upon him and his family), and it is the Lord's burden. And Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) will be called, then clothed and made to speak; and I will be called, then clothed and

A merit of Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) is: whatever he came with, I take by it, and whatever he forbade from, I refrain from it. Obedience to him after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) flows as it flowed for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — the merit belongs to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). The one who goes ahead of him is like the one who goes ahead of God and His Messenger; and the one who claims superiority over him is like the one who claims superiority over the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family); and the one who rejects him in a small or large matter is at the limit of associating partners with God. For indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the Door of God through which one can only come to Him, and His Path — whoever traverses it reaches God, Mighty and Majestic. And likewise was Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) after him, and this flowed to the Imams (peace be upon them), one after another. God, Mighty and Majestic, made them the pillars of the earth lest it shake with its inhabitants, the support columns of Islam, and the bonds along the path of His guidance — no guide can guide except by their guidance, and no one strays from guidance except by falling short of their rights. They are the trustees of God over what He sent down of knowledge, excuses, and warnings — and the eloquent divine authority over those on earth. What flowed for the first of them from God flows for the last of them, and no one reaches that except by the assistance of God. And Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: I am the distributor of God between paradise and the fire — no one enters it except on the limit of my distribution. I am the Greatest Differentiator, and I am the Imam of those who come after me and the transmitter on behalf of those who were before me. No one precedes me except Ahmad (peace be upon him and his family), and he and I are upon one path except that he is the one called by his name. And I have indeed been given the six: knowledge of deaths, tribulations, bequests, and decisive speech — and I am the owner of the cycles and the state of states, and I am the owner of the staff and the branding iron; and the Beast that will speak to the people.

Abū Muḥammad al-Qāsim ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, raised it from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim, who said: We were with al-Riḍā عليه السلام in Marw. We gathered in the congregational mosque on Friday at the beginning of our arrival, and they discussed the matter of the Imamate and mentioned the extent of people’s disagreement concerning it. So I entered upon my master عليه السلام and informed him of the people’s disputation about it. He عليه السلام smiled and then said: O ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, the people have become ignorant and have been deceived by their opinions. Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not take the soul of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله until He completed the religion for him and sent down to him the Qur’an, in which is the clarification of everything. In it He clarified the halal, the haram, the limits, the rulings, and all that people need in full. We have not neglected anything in the Book. And He revealed during the Farewell Hajj, which was at the end of his life صلى الله عليه وآله: Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My blessing upon you, and approved Islam for you as a religion. And the matter of the Imamate is part of the completion of the religion. He صلى الله عليه وآله did not pass on until he clarified for his community the landmarks of their religion, made clear to them their path, left them upon the straight course of the path of truth, and established for them ʿAlī عليه السلام as a standard and an Imam. He left nothing needed by the community except that he clarified it. So whoever claims that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not complete His religion has rejected the Book of Allah, and whoever rejects the Book of Allah is a disbeliever in it. Do they know the worth of the Imamate and its place in the community such that their choosing in it should be valid? Surely the Imamate is too exalted in worth, too great in station, too high in place, too fortified in aspect, and too deep in depth for people to reach it by their intellects, attain it by their opinions, or appoint an Imam by their own choice. Surely the Imamate is that with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, singled out Ibrāhīm al-Khalīl عليه السلام after prophethood and intimate friendship, as a third rank and a virtue by which He honored him and magnified his mention, so He said: Indeed, I am making you an Imam for the people. So the Friend عليه الس

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Is'haq ibn Ghalib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in a sermon of his in which he mentions the state of the Imams (peace be upon them) and their qualities: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, has clarified His religion through the Imams of Guidance from the People of the Household of our Prophet, and illuminated through them the path of His manifest way, and opened through them the hidden springs of His knowledge. So whoever from the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) recognizes the obligatory right of his Imam will find the taste of the sweetness of his faith and will know the excellence of the beauty of his Islam — because God, Blessed and Exalted, has set the Imam as a beacon for His creation and made him a proof upon the people of His sustenance and His world, and God has clothed him with the crown of dignity and enveloped him with light from the All-Compeller, extending by a means toward the sky — his sustaining support is never cut off from him, and what is with God cannot be attained except by way of his causes, and God does not accept the deeds of the servants except through recognition of him. He is knowledgeable in whatever comes to him of the obscurities of darkness, the ambiguities of the established ways, and the confusions of trials. Thus God, Blessed and Exalted, never ceases to choose them for His creation from among the sons of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) from the posterity of each Imam — selecting them for that purpose, choosing them, being pleased with them for His creation, and approving them. Every time an Imam passes from among them, He appoints for His creation from his posterity an Imam — a clear standard, a luminous guide, a sustaining Imam, and a knowledgeable proof — Imams from God who guide by truth and by it deal justice; the proofs of God, His callers, and His shepherds over His creation. The servants are guided by their guidance, the lands are illuminated by their light, and prosperity grows by their blessing. God has made them the life of all beings, lamps for the darkness, keys to discourse, and pillars of Islam. God's decrees have run among them in their ordained course. So the Imam is the one chosen, the approved, the trusted guide, the upholder of hope. God chose him with that and fashioned him under His eye in t

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ narrated to me, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you,” so his answer was: “Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They believe in al-jibt and al-ṭāghūt, and they say to those who disbelieve: These are better guided in way than those who believe.” They say concerning the Imams of misguidance and the callers to the Fire: these are better guided in way than the family of Muḥammad. “Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whomever Allah curses, you shall never find for him any helper. Or do they have a share of the kingdom?” Meaning the Imamate and the khilāfah. “Then they would not give the people even a naqīr.” We are the people intended by Allah, and the naqīr is the small point in the middle of the date-stone. “Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them out of His grace?” We are the people who are envied for what Allah has given us of the Imamate, apart from all the creation of Allah. “So indeed We gave the family of Ibrāhīm the Book and the wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom.” He says: We made from among them the messengers, the prophets, and the Imams. So how do they affirm it in the family of Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) yet deny it in the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)? “So among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who turn away from it, and Hell is sufficient as a blaze. Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs, We shall soon make them enter a Fire; whenever their skins are thoroughly burned, We shall replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Mighty, Wise.”

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of God — Blessed and Exalted — 'Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His grace?' He said: 'We are the envied ones.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): [What is the meaning of] the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'But indeed We have given to the progeny of Ibrahim the Book' [4:54]? So he said: 'Prophethood.' I said: 'And the Wisdom?' He said: 'The understanding and the giving of judgment.' I said: 'And We have given them a grand kingdom?' So he said: 'The obedience (of the people).'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His Grace?' So he said: 'O Abu al-Sabbah! We, by God, are the envied people.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhayna, from Bureyd al-'Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: But indeed We have given to the Progeny of Ibrahim the Book and the Wisdom, and We have given them a Grand Kingdom. He said: 'He (God) made from them the Messengers, the Prophets, and the Imams. So how can they acknowledge it regarding the Progeny of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) yet deny it regarding the Progeny of Muhammad (may God bless him and his family)?' He (the narrator) said: 'I said: "and We have given them a Grand Kingdom"?' He (the Imam) said: 'The Grand Kingdom is that He (God) made the Imams among them. Whoever obeys them obeys God, and whoever disobeys them disobeys God. Thus it is the Grand Kingdom.'

Dawud al-Jassas narrated to us saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying 'And signs; and by the star they are guided' [16:16] He said: 'The star is the Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah upon him and his family), and the signs — they are the Imams (peace be upon them).'

Al-Haysam asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — and I was in his presence — about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And signs; and by the star they are being guided' [Quran 16:16] So he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) [said]: 'The star and the signs — they are the Imams (peace be upon them).'

I asked al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the word of God the Exalted: 'And signs; and by the star they are being guided' [16:16] He said: 'We are the signs, and the star is the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'And what do the Signs and the Warners avail a people who do not believe?' He said: 'The Signs — they are the Imams, and the Warners — they are the Prophets (peace be upon them).'

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani, from Musa ibn Muhammad al-Ijli, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, raising it (as a marfu' narration), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'They belied Our Signs, all of them' — meaning the Successors (Awsiya), all of them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr or someone else, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I said to him: 'May I be your sacrifice! The Shia are asking you about the interpretation of this verse: "About what are they asking one another? About the great news."' He said: 'That is up to me. If I desire, I shall inform them, and if I desire, I shall not inform them.' Then he said: 'But I will inform you of its interpretation.' I said: '"About what are they asking one another?"' He said: 'It is about Amir al-Mu'minin, blessings of God upon him. Amir al-Mu'minin, blessings of God upon him, used to say: There is no sign of God, Mighty and Majestic, that is greater than me, and no news of God greater than me.'

Bureyd ibn Mu'awiya al-'Ijli said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Fear Allah and be with the truthful ones' [9:119] He (peace be upon him) said: 'He meant us.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'O you who believe! Fear God and be with the truthful ones' [9:119]. He said: 'The truthful ones are the Imams, and the very truthful (are those who adhere) through obedience to them.'

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever loves to live a life resembling the lives of the Prophets, to die a death resembling the deaths of the martyrs, and to dwell in the Gardens which the All-beneficent has planted — then let him take Ali as his guardian, be loyal to his friends, and follow the Imams after him. For indeed they are my progeny, created from my essence. O God! Grant them my understanding and my knowledge. And woe to those of my community who oppose them! O God! Do not let them attain my intercession!

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed God, Blessed and Exalted, says: The completion of My argument against the wretched ones from your community is [concerning] those who abandon the wilayah of Ali, ally with his enemies, and deny his merit and the merit of the successors after him. For your merit is their merit, obedience to you is obedience to them, your right is their right, and disobedience to you is disobedience to them. And they are the guiding Imams after you. Your spirit flows in them, and your spirit is what has flowed from your Lord into you. They are your progeny from your essence, your flesh, and your blood. And God, Mighty and Majestic, has caused your Sunnah and the Sunnah of the Prophets before you to flow in them. They are the custodians of My knowledge after you. It is a right upon Me — I have chosen them, selected them, purified them, and am pleased with them. And salvation is for the one who loves them, allies with them, and submits to their merits. And Jibreel (peace be upon him) came to me with their names and the names of their forefathers, their beloved [followers], and those who submit to their merits.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazala ibn Ayyub, from Abu al-Maghra', from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever wants to live my life, and die my death, and enter the Garden of Eden which God, my Lord, planted with His own hand — let him take Ali ibn Abi Talib as his guardian, let him befriend his friend, and let him be inimical to his enemy, and let him submit to the successors after him. For indeed they are my progeny, from my flesh and blood; God gave them my understanding and my knowledge. I complain to God about the matter of my community — those who deny their merits, those who sever my connection to them. And I swear by God, they will surely kill my son. God shall not grant them my intercession!'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abd al-Qahhar, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever would be pleased to live my life, and to die my death, and to enter the Paradise which my Lord has promised me, and to hold fast to a branch that my Lord planted with His own hand — let him take Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and his successors after him as his guardians, for they will not lead you into a gate of straying, nor will they take you out from a gate of guidance. Therefore do not try to teach them, for they are more knowledgeable than you are. And I asked my Lord that there be no separation between them and the Book until they both arrive at the Pool together — like this,' and he joined his two fingers, 'and its breadth is what lies between Sana'a and Ayla, and therein are cups of silver and gold numbering the stars.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Verily the comfort, the rest, the success, the assistance, the achievement, the blessing, the benevolence, the forgiveness, the well-being, the ease, the glad tidings, the Divine pleasure, the nearness, the help, the empowerment, the hope, and the love from Allah — Mighty and Majestic — are for whoever befriends Ali and takes him as Imam, and disavows his enemies, and submits to his merits and to the successors after him. It is a right upon me that I include them in my intercession, and a right upon my Lord — Blessed and Exalted — that He answers me regarding them. For they are my followers, and whoever follows me is indeed from me.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim and Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from him who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Prophets and the Messengers are upon four categories. There is a Prophet who is informed within himself, without going beyond others; and there is a Prophet who sees in sleep and hears the voice, and does not see him (the angel) while awake, and was not sent to anyone, and upon him is an Imam — similar to how Ibrahim was above Lot (peace be upon him). And there is a Prophet who sees in his sleep and hears the voice and sees the Angel face to face, and has been sent to a group, be they few or many, like Yunus — God said to Yunus: 'And We sent him to a hundred thousand, or more' [37:147] He said: 'The "or more" refers to thirty thousand,' and upon him is an Imam. And the one who sees in his sleep and hears the voice and sees while awake — he is an Imam, like the Uli al-'Azm. And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was indeed a Prophet but not an Imam, until God said: 'I am making you an Imam for the people.' He (Ibrahim) said: 'And from my offspring?' God said: 'My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.' [2:124] Whoever worshipped an idol or a graven image cannot be an Imam.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Zayd al-Shahham who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, God (Blessed and Exalted) took Ibrahim as a servant before He took him as a Prophet, and indeed God took him as a Prophet before He took him as a Messenger, and indeed God took him as a Messenger before He took him as a close friend (Khalil), and indeed God took him as a close friend before He made him an Imam. So when He had gathered all these things for him, He said: [2:124] 'Indeed, I am making you an Imam for the people.' He (the Imam) said: And it was due to its greatness in the eyes of Ibrahim that he said: 'And from my offspring?' He said: [2:124] 'My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.' He (the Imam) said: 'The foolish one cannot be the Imam of the pious.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from Hisham, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The chiefs of the prophets and the messengers are five, and they are the Ulu al-Azm (Determined Ones) from the messengers, and upon them the millstone revolves — Noah, and Ibrahim, and Musa, and Isa, and Muhammad, may God's blessings be upon him and his family and upon all the prophets.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Is'haq ibn Abd al-Aziz Abu al-Saffatij, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Indeed God took Ibrahim as a servant before He took him as a Prophet, and took him as a Prophet before He took him as a Messenger, and took him as a Messenger before He took him as a friend (Khalil), and took him as a friend before He took him as an Imam. So when He gathered all these things for him and took his hand, He said to him: O Ibrahim, I am making you an Imam for the people. So great was it in the eyes of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he said: O my Lord, and from my offspring? He said: My covenant shall not be attained by the wrongdoers.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn 'Ajlan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know' [16:43] He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Reminder is I, and the Imams are the People of the Reminder. And regarding His words, Mighty and Majestic: 'And indeed it is a reminder/honor for you and for your people, and you will soon be questioned' [43:44] Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: We are his people, and we are the ones who will be questioned.

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): '[Quran 16:43]: So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know.' He said: 'Al-Dhikr (the Reminder) is Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and we are his people, the ones to be asked.' He (the narrator) said, I said: 'His word [Quran 43:44]: And it is indeed a Reminder for you and your people, and you shall soon be questioned?' He said: 'It means us, and we are the Ahl al-Dhikr (People of the Reminder), and we are the ones to be asked.'

I asked al-Reza (peace be upon him), and I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you! [Quran 16:43] 'Ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know.' So he said: 'We are the Ahl al-Dhikr (People of the Reminder), and we are the ones to be asked.' I said: 'So you are the ones to be asked and we are the questioners?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Is it truly a duty upon us that we ask you?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Is it truly a duty upon you that you answer us?' He said: 'No. That is up to us — if we wish, we do so, and if we wish, we do not.' Have you not heard the word of God, Blessed and Exalted: [38:39] 'This is Our gift — so bestow freely or withhold, without accountability'?

...of God, Mighty and Majestic 'And it is indeed a Reminder for you and your people, and you shall soon be questioned' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the Dhikr (Reminder), and the People of his Household (peace be upon them) are al-Mas'ulun (the ones to be questioned), and they are the Ahl al-Dhikr (People of the Reminder).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'And indeed it is a Reminder for you and for your people, and you shall soon be questioned' [43:44]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Reminder (Al-Zikr) is the Quran, and we are its people, and we are the ones who will be questioned.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when al-Ward, the brother of al-Kumayt, entered upon him and said, 'May God make me your ransom! I had selected seventy questions for you, but not one of them comes to my mind.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Not even one, O Ward?' He said: 'Yes, one has come to my mind.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'The Word of God, Blessed and Exalted: "So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know" — who are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'We [are they].' I said: 'Is it upon us to ask you?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Is it incumbent upon you to answer us?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to us.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'There are those among us who claim that the word of God, Mighty and Majestic, "So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know" [16:43], refers to the Jews and the Christians.' He said: 'In that case, they would be calling you to their religion.' He said, placing his hand upon his chest: 'We are the People of the Reminder, and we are the ones to be asked.'

I heard him saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: Upon the Imams are obligations that are not upon their followers, and upon our Shia are obligations that are not upon us. God Mighty and Majestic commanded them to ask us, saying: "So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know" [16:43]. Thus He commanded them to ask us, and it is not incumbent upon us to answer — if we wish, we answer, and if we wish, we refrain.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I wrote a letter to al-Ridha (peace be upon him), and among part of what I wrote was: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know.' [16:43] And God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And it was not for the believers to go forth all together; so why should not a company from every party among them go forth to gain understanding in religion, and to warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious?' [9:122] So the asking has been imposed upon them, while the answering has not been imposed upon you. He (the Imam) said: 'God, Blessed and Exalted, said: [28:50] But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires — and who is more astray than one who follows his own desires?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd al-Mu'min ibn al-Qasim al-Ansari, from Sa'd, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Are those who know and those who do not know equal? But rather, it is those with understanding who are mindful' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'But rather, we are those who know, and those who do not know are our enemies, and our Shia are those with understanding.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'Are those who know and those who do not know alike? Indeed, only those possessed of understanding take heed.' He said: 'We are those who know, and our enemies are those who do not know, and our Shias are the ones possessed of understanding.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr and Imran ibn Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We are those firmly rooted in knowledge, and we know its interpretation.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥammād, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, regarding the saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “and none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge.” So Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله is the most excellent of those firmly rooted in knowledge. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught him all that was sent down to him of the revelation and the interpretation, and it is not for Allah to send down to him something without teaching him its interpretation. And his successors after him know all of it. As for those who do not know its interpretation, when the knower among them speaks with knowledge, Allah answered them by His saying: “They say: We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.” And the Qur'an contains the specific and the general, the decisive and the allegorical, the abrogating and the abrogated; so those firmly rooted in knowledge know it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Those firmly rooted in knowledge' are the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams after him (peace be upon them).

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding this verse: 'Nay, it is clear signs in the chests of those who have been given knowledge' and he gestured with his hand toward his own chest.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz al-Abdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Nay, it is clear verses in the chests of those who have been granted Knowledge he said: 'They are the Imams (peace be upon them).'
