And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, regarding this verse: 'Nay, it is clear signs in the chests of those who have been given knowledge' Then he said: 'By Allah, O Abu Muhammad! It does not mean what is between the two covers of the Mushaf.' I said, 'Who are they, may I be sacrificed for you?' He said: 'Who could they possibly be other than us?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid Shaghir, from Haroun ibn Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Rather, it is clear verses in the chests of those who are granted Knowledge' He said: They are the Imams (peace be upon them) in particular.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said: I asked him about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Nay, it is clear verses in the chests of those who have been given knowledge' [29:49]. He said: 'They are the Imams (peace be upon them) in particular.'

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Muʾmin, from Sālim, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We chose from among Our servants; so among them is one who wrongs his own self, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by the permission of Allah. He عليه السلام said: "The one foremost in good deeds is the Imam, the moderate one is the one who recognizes the Imam, and the one who wrongs his own self is the one who does not recognize the Imam."

Al-Ḥusayn, from Muʿallā, from Al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him عليه السلام about His, the Exalted's, saying: Then We caused those whom We chose from among Our servants to inherit the Book. So he عليه السلام said: “What are you saying?” I said: “We say that it is regarding the Fāṭimīs.” He عليه السلام said: “It is not as you are taking it. The one who points with his sword and calls the people to opposition does not enter into this.” So I said: “Then which one is the wrongdoer to himself?” He عليه السلام said: “The one sitting in his house who does not recognize the right of the Imam. And the moderate one is the one who recognizes the right of the Imam. And the one foremost in good deeds is the Imam.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar, who said: I asked Abā Al-Ḥasan Al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those whom We chose from among Our servants. — the verse. He said: The children of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. And the one foremost in good deeds is the Imam, and the moderate one is the one who recognizes the Imam, and the one who wrongs himself is the one who does not recognize the Imam.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Wallād, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Those to whom We have given the Book recite it as it ought to be recited; they are the ones who believe in it. He عليه السلام said: They are the Imams عليهم السلام.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ghālib, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: When this verse was revealed, “The Day We shall call every people by their Imam.” The Muslims said, “O Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, are you not the Imam of all the people altogether?” He said: So Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said, “I am the Messenger of Allah to all the people altogether, but after me there will be Imams over the people from Allah, from my Ahl al-Bayt, who will stand among the people; then they will be denied, and the Imams of kufr and misguidance and their followers will oppress them.” So whoever befriends them, follows them, and affirms them, then he is from me and with me, and he will meet me. Indeed, whoever wrongs them and denies them is not from me, nor with me, and I am free of him.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Imams in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are two kinds of Imams. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “And We made them Imams who guide by Our command.” Not by the command of the people. They put the command of Allah before their own command, and the judgment of Allah before their own judgment. And He said: “And We made them Imams who call to the Fire.” They put their own command before the command of Allah, and their own judgment before the judgment of Allah, and they follow their desires in opposition to what is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام about His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: “And to every one We have appointed heirs from what the parents and the near relatives leave, and those with whom your right hands have ratified agreements” He عليه السلام said: “Rather, by that He meant the Imams عليهم السلام. By them Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ratified your agreements.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Musa ibn Ukayl al-Numayri, from al-Ala' ibn Sayabah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. Regarding His, the Exalted, saying: Surely this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright. He عليه السلام said: "It guides to the Imam."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Bistām ibn Murrah, from Isḥāq ibn Ḥassān, from Al-Haytham ibn Wāqid, from ‘Alī ibn Al-Ḥusayn Al-‘Abdī, from Sa‘d Al-Iskāf, from Al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “What is the matter with people who changed the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and turned away from his legatee? Do they not fear that the punishment may descend upon them?” Then he recited this verse: “Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the abode of ruin—Hell?” Then he said: “We are the favor with which Allah has blessed His servants, and through us whoever succeeds will succeed on the Day of Resurrection.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, raising it, concerning the saying: of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Which then of the favors of your Lord will you two deny?” “Is it with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم or with the Waṣī عليه السلام that you two deny?” It was revealed in Sūrat al-Raḥmān.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Al-Haytham ibn Wāqid, from Abī Yūsuf Al-Bazzāz, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام recited this verse: So remember the favors of Allah. He said: “Do you know what the favors of Allah are?” I said: “No.” He said: “It is the greatest of Allah’s blessings upon His creation, and it is our wilayah.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from ‘Alī ibn Hassān, from ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Kathīr, who said: I asked Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief” — the verse. He عليه السلام said: “What is meant by it is Quraysh altogether, those who opposed the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, set up war against him, and denied the bequest concerning his successor.”

Asbāṭ, the seller of al-Zuṭṭī, informed me, saying: I was in the presence of Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and a man asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Surely in that are signs for those who discern; and surely it is on an enduring road.” He said: “We are the ones who discern, and the path abides in us.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from Yaḥyā ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Asbāṭ ibn Sālim narrated to me. He said: I was in the presence of Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), then a man from the people of Hīt came in to him and said to him, “May Allah set you aright.” “What do you say concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ‘Surely in that are signs for the discerning’?” He (عليه السلام) said: “We are the discerning ones, and the path is established among us.”

Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern. He said: They are the Imams (عليهم السلام). The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: Beware of the discernment of the believer, for he looks by the light of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted: Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Kūfī, from ʿUbays ibn Hishām, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sulaymān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Surely in that there are signs for those who discern. So he said: They are the Imams عليهم السلام. And surely it is on an enduring way. He said: It will never depart from us.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn Ayyub, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) said regarding His, the Exalted's, saying: Indeed in that are signs for the discerning. He said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the discerner, and I am after him, and the Imams from my offspring are the discerners. And in another copy: from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn Ayyub, through his chain, similarly to it.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: The deeds are presented to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the deeds of the servants, every morning, both their righteous ones and their wicked ones. So beware of them. And this is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “Work, and Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger.” And he became silent.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Ṭāʾī, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers.” He عليه السلام said: “They are the Imams.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: I heard him saying: “What is the matter with you, that you offend the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?” Then a man said, “How do we offend him?” So he said, “Do you not know that your deeds are presented to him? Then when he sees in them an act of disobedience, that grieves him.” So do not offend the Messenger of Allah; rather, bring him joy.”

Ali, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Zayyat, from Abdullah ibn Aban Al-Zayyat—who held a distinguished position with Al-Rida عليه السلام—who said: I said to Al-Rida عليه السلام, "Pray to Allah for me and for my household." So he said, "Am I not already doing so? By Allah, your deeds are surely presented to me every day and night." He said: I regarded that as tremendous, so he said to me, "Do you not read the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?" And say: Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers. He said, "He is, by Allah, Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام."
He, by Allah, is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (peace be upon him).

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, who said: I heard al-Riḍā عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, the deeds are presented to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, their righteous ones and their wicked ones.”

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and he was a Messenger, a Prophet' — what is the Messenger and what is the Prophet? He said: The Prophet is the one who sees in his dream and hears the voice but does not directly behold the Angel; and the Messenger is the one who hears the voice, sees in the dream, and directly beholds the Angel. I said: The Imam — what is his rank? He said: He hears the voice but does not see (in dream) and does not directly behold the Angel. Then he recited this verse: 'And We did not send before you any Messenger, nor Prophet, nor Muhaddath.'

Al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas al-Ma'rufi wrote to al-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! Inform me: what is the difference between the Messenger, the Prophet, and the Imam?' He said — so he wrote, or said: 'The difference between the Messenger, the Prophet, and the Imam is that the Messenger is one unto whom Jibrail descends; he sees him and hears his speech, and the Revelation is sent down to him, and sometimes he sees in his dream something like the dream of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). The Prophet sometimes hears the speech and sometimes sees the figure but does not hear. And the Imam is one who hears the speech but does not see the figure.'

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Messenger, the Prophet, and the Muhaddath. He said: The Messenger is the one to whom Jibreel comes face to face, so he sees him and speaks with him — that is the Messenger. As for the Prophet, he is the one who sees in his dream, similar to the dream of Ibrahim and similar to what the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to see of the signs of prophethood before the revelation, until Jibreel (peace be upon him) came to him from God with the Message. And it was that Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), when prophethood and the Message were gathered for him from God, Jibreel would bring it to him and speak to him about it face to face. And among the Prophets is one for whom prophethood was gathered, and he sees in his dream, and the Spirit comes to him, speaks to him and narrates to him — without his happening to see it in the waking state. And as for the Muhaddath, he is the one who is spoken to, so he hears, but does not see (while awake) nor does he see in his dream.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Yaqub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Burayd — from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) — regarding His (God's) saying, Mighty and Majestic: And We did not send before you any Rasool, or Prophet, or Muhaddith.

I said: May I be your ransom! This is not our recitation. So what is the Messenger (Rasool), the Prophet (Nabi), and the Muhaddath? He said: The Rasool is one to whom the Angel appears and speaks to him. The Nabi is one who sees in his dream; and sometimes Prophethood and Messengership are combined in one person. The Muhaddath is one who hears the voice but does not see the form. He (the narrator) said: I said, May Allah keep you well! How does he know that what he saw in his dream is true and that it is from the Angel? He said: He is guided to it until he recognizes it. Verily Allah has sealed the Books with your Book and sealed the Prophets with your Prophet.

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Ḥasanī, from Mūsā ibn Muḥammad, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning His, the Exalted's, saying: And that if they had remained steadfast upon the path, We would surely have given them abundant water to drink. He عليه السلام said: It means, if they had remained steadfast upon the wilayah of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and the awṣiyāʾ from among his descendants عليهم السلام, and accepted obedience to them in their commands and their prohibitions, We would surely have given them abundant water to drink—meaning: We would have made their hearts drink faith. And the path is faith in the wilayah of ʿAlī and the awṣiyāʾ.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhūr, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthmān, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Those who say: Our Lord is Allah, then remain steadfast.” So Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام said: “They remained steadfast upon the Imams, one after another.” “The angels descend upon them: Do not fear, nor grieve, and receive glad tidings of the Paradise which you were promised.”

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from more than one person, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abī al-Jārūd, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said: “What do the people resent from us? For by Allah, we are the tree of the prophethood, the House of mercy, the معدن of knowledge, and the place where the angels come and go.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: We, the Ahl al-Bayt, are the tree of Prophethood, the place of the Message, the place frequented by the angels, the house of mercy, and the معدن of knowledge.

Some of our companions narrated from Khaythamah, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said to me: “O Khaythamah,” We are the tree of prophethood, the house of mercy, the keys of wisdom, the mine of knowledge, the locus of the message, the place where the angels come and go, the place of the secret of Allah, and we are Allah’s trust among His servants, and we are the greatest sanctuary of Allah, and we are the guarantee of Allah, and we are the covenant of Allah. So whoever fulfills our covenant has fulfilled the covenant of Allah, and whoever violates it has violated the guarantee of Allah and His covenant.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, ʿAlī (عليه السلام) was knowledgeable, and knowledge is inherited; and no knowledgeable one will perish except that there remains after him one who knows his knowledge, or whatever Allah wills.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, the knowledge that descended with Adam (عليه السلام) has not been raised, and knowledge is inherited. And Ali (عليه السلام) was the knowledgeable one of this community, and no knowledgeable one from among us has ever perished except that one from his family succeeded him who knew the like of his knowledge, or whatever Allah willed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: “Indeed, knowledge is inherited, and no knowledgeable one dies except that he leaves behind one who knows the like of his knowledge, or whatever Allah wills.”

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed, in 'Ali (عليه السلام) is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of a thousand Prophets from among the Prophets, and indeed the knowledge that descended with Adam (عليه السلام) was not raised, and no knowledgeable one dies such that his knowledge goes away; rather, knowledge is inherited.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from 'Umar ibn Aban, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed, the knowledge that descended with Adam (عليه السلام) was not raised away, and no learned one dies such that his knowledge goes away.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, raising it from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), said: They suck at the scant water and leave the mighty river. It was said to him: What is the mighty river? He said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the knowledge that Allah gave him. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathered for Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) the sunnahs of the Prophets, from Ādam onward in succession up to Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله). It was said to him: And what are those sunnahs? He said: The knowledge of the Prophets in its entirety. And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) placed all of that with Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام). Then a man said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, is Amīr al-Muʾminīn more knowledgeable, or some of the Prophets? So Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: Listen to what he is saying! Indeed, Allah opens the hearing of whomsoever He wills. I told him that Allah gathered for Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) the knowledge of the Prophets, and that he gathered all of that with Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), and yet he asks me: Is he more knowledgeable, or some of the Prophets?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Indeed, knowledge is inherited, so no knowledgeable one dies except that he leaves behind one who knows the like of his knowledge, or whatever Allah wills.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, the knowledge that descended with Ādam (عليه السلام) was not raised away. No knowledgeable one dies except that he has bequeathed his knowledge. Indeed, the earth does not remain without a knowledgeable one.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, that al-Ridha (peace be upon him) wrote to him: As for what follows: Indeed Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was the trustee of Allah among His creation. When he (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, we, the People of the House, were his inheritors. Thus we are the trustees of Allah in His earth. With us is the knowledge of calamities and deaths, the lineages of the Arabs, and the origin of Islam. And indeed we recognize the man when we see him, by the reality of his faith and the reality of his hypocrisy. And indeed our Shia are recorded with their names and the names of their fathers. Allah took the covenant upon us and upon them — they shall arrive where we arrive and enter where we enter. There is none upon the nation of Islam other than us and them. We are the noble ones, the saved ones; we are the vanguard of the prophets; we are the sons of the successors; we are those singled out in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; we are the most entitled of all people to the Book of Allah; and we are the most entitled of all people to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And we are those for whom Allah legislated His religion, and He said in His Book: 'He has legislated for you, O Family of Muhammad, from the religion what He enjoined upon Noah' — He has enjoined upon us what He enjoined upon Noah — 'and that which We revealed to you, O Muhammad, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa.' So He has taught us and conveyed to us the knowledge of what we know, and has entrusted to us their knowledge. We are the inheritors of the Determined Ones (Ulu al-Azm) from among the Messengers: 'Establish the religion, O Family of Muhammad, and do not be divided therein' — and be united as one community. Hard it is for the polytheists — those who associate others with the wilayah of Ali — what you call them to from the wilayah of Ali. Allah, O Muhammad, guides to Himself whoever turns in repentance, whoever answers your call toward the wilayah of Ali (peace be upon him).

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Indeed, the first successor upon the face of the earth was Hibat Allah ibn Adam, and there was no Prophet who passed except that he had a successor. The totality of the Prophets were one hundred and twenty thousand Prophets, and among them were five Possessors of Resolve: Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ʿĪsā, and Muḥammad عليهم السلام. And indeed, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was the Hibat Allah for Muḥammad, and he inherited the knowledge of the successors and the knowledge of those who were before him.” Indeed, Muḥammad inherited the knowledge of those before him from among the Prophets and the Messengers. Upon the pillar of the Throne it is written: ‘Ḥamza is the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger and the chief of the martyrs,’ and in the crest of the Throne: ‘ʿAlī is the Commander of the Faithful.’ So this is our proof against the one who denies our right and rejects our inheritance. And nothing has prevented us from speaking while certainty is before us; so what proof could be more eloquent than this?”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Zur‘ah ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: “Indeed, Sulayman inherited Dawud, and indeed Muhammad inherited Sulayman, and indeed we inherited Muhammad, and indeed with us is the knowledge of the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur, and the clarification of what is in the Tablets.” He said: I said, “Surely this is the knowledge.” He said: “This is not the knowledge. The knowledge is that which comes into occurrence day after day and hour after hour.”

Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Shuʿayb al-Haddad, from Zurays al-Kunasi, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, and Abu Basir was with him. So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Indeed, Dawud inherited the knowledge of the Prophets, and indeed Sulayman inherited Dawud, and indeed Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم inherited Sulayman, and indeed we inherited Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and indeed with us are the scriptures of Ibrahim and the tablets of Musa. So Abu Basir said, “Surely this is the knowledge.” He said, “O Abu Muhammad, this is not the knowledge. Rather, knowledge is that which occurs in the night and the day, day by day and hour by hour.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: He عليه السلام said to me: "O Abū Muḥammad, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not give the Prophets anything except that He had also given it to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله." He عليه السلام said: "And He gave Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله all that He gave to the Prophets." "And with us are the scriptures about which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘The scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.’" I said, "May I be sacrificed for you, are they the Tablets?" He عليه السلام said, "Yes."

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام. That he asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And We have certainly written in the Zabur after the Dhikr.” What is the Zabur, and what is the Dhikr? He عليه السلام said: “The Dhikr is with Allah, and the Zabur is that which was sent down upon Dawud. And every Book that was sent down, it is with the People of Knowledge, and we are they.”

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me about the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — did he inherit from all the Prophets?' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'From Adam until it reached himself?' He said: 'God did not send a Prophet except that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was more knowledgeable than him.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, "Indeed Isa ibn Maryam used to revive the dead by the permission of God." He said: "You speak the truth. And Sulayman ibn Dawud used to understand the speech of the bird, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was able to attain these stations."' He said, then he said: 'Indeed Sulayman ibn Dawud said to the hoopoe when he missed it and doubted its matter: [27:20] What is the matter that I do not see the hoopoe, or is it among those absent? — when he missed it, he grew angry at it and said: [27:21] I will punish it with a severe punishment, or slaughter it, or it must bring me a clear authority.' And indeed he was angry because it used to guide him to water. So this one — being a bird — had been given what Sulayman had not been given. And indeed the wind, the ants, humans, jinn, the satans, and the rebellious ones were all obedient to him, yet he did not know the water beneath the air, while the bird knew it. And God says in His Book [13:31]: And if there were a Quran by which mountains would be moved, or the earth would be cloven, or the dead be made to speak — and we have inherited this Quran which contains that by which mountains can be moved, cities can be traversed, and the dead can be revived, and we know the water beneath the air. And in the Book of God there are verses by which no matter is intended except that God permits it, along with what God has permitted from what He prescribed for those before us — God has made it for us in the Mother of the Book. Indeed God says [27:75]: And there is nothing concealed in the sky and the earth but it is in a clear Book. Then he said: [35:32] Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those We chose from among Our servants. So we are those whom God Mighty and Majestic has chosen, and made us inherit this wherein is the clarification of all things.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yūnus, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, concerning... The hadith of Bureyh: when he came with him to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), he met Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). Hishām related the account to him, and when he finished, Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) said to Bureyh: “O Bureyh, how is your knowledge of your Book?” He said, “I am knowledgeable of it.” Then he said, “How confident are you in its interpretation?” He said, “None is more confident than I am in my knowledge of it.” He said: Then Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) began reciting the Injīl. Bureyh said, “You are the one I have been seeking for fifty years, or one like you.” He said: So Bureyh believed, and his faith became excellent, and the woman who was with him also believed. Then Hishām, Bureyh, and the woman entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and Hishām related to him the conversation that had occurred between Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام) and Bureyh. So Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “Offspring, some of them from others, and Allah is Hearing, Knowing.” Then Bureyh said, “How do you have the Tawrāh, the Injīl, and the books of the Prophets?” He said, “They are with us as an inheritance from them. We recite them as they recited them, and we speak them as they spoke them. Indeed, Allah does not place a ḥujjah in His earth who is asked about something and says: ‘I do not know.’”

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: We came to the door of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام while we were seeking permission to enter upon him. We heard him speaking words that were not Arabic, so we supposed that they were in Syriac. Then he wept, and we wept because of his weeping. Then the servant came out to us and gave us permission, so we entered upon him. So I said: 'May Allah keep you well, we came to you seeking permission to enter upon you, and we heard you speaking words that were not Arabic, so we supposed that they were in Syriac. Then you wept, so we wept because of your weeping.' He عليه السلام said: 'Yes. I remembered Ilyas the Prophet, and he was among the devoted worshippers from the prophets of the Children of Israel.' So I said: 'Like what he used to say in his sajdah?' Then he spoke it in Syriac, and by Allah, we had not seen any priest or catholicos more eloquent in pronunciation than he was in it. Then he explained it to us in Arabic and said: 'He used to say in his sajdah: Will You punish me while I have made my hot middays thirsty for You? Will You punish me while I have rubbed my face in the dust for You? Will You punish me while I have avoided acts of disobedience for You? Will You punish me while I have kept my night awake for You?' He عليه السلام said: 'Then Allah revealed to him: Raise your head, for I shall not punish you. He said: Then he said: If You say, "I will not punish you," then were You to punish me, what would that be? Am I not Your servant and You my Lord? He عليه السلام said: Then Allah revealed to him: Raise your head, for I shall not punish you. Indeed, when I promise a promise, I fulfill it.'

I heard Abu Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “No one among the people claimed that he had compiled the Qur'an in its entirety as it was revealed except a liar; and none compiled it and preserved it as Allah, the Exalted, sent it down, except ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام) and the Imams after him (عليهم السلام).”

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from al-Munakhkhal, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he said: No one is able to claim that he possesses the entire Qur'an, all of it, its outward and its inward, except the successors.

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, among the knowledge that we have been given is the interpretation of the Qur’an, its rulings, and knowledge of the changing of time and its occurrences. When Allah intends good for a people, He causes them to hear; and if He were to make one hear who does not truly hear, he would turn away in aversion as though he had not heard.” Then he was silent for a short while, then he said: “If we were to find receptacles or a place of rest, we would speak; and Allah is the One whose help is sought.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Mu'min, from Abd al-A'la, mawla of the family of Sam, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, I indeed know the Book of Allah from its beginning to its end, as if it were in my palm. In it is the news of the heaven, the news of the earth, the news of what has been, and the news of what is to be.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'In it is the clarification of everything.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: The one who had knowledge from the Book said: “I shall bring it to you before your glance returns to you.” He said: Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) spread his fingers apart and placed them on his chest, then said: “And with us, by Allah, is the knowledge of the Book, all of it.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from one whom he mentioned; all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: “Say: Allah is sufficient as a Witness between me and you, and the one who has knowledge of the Book.” He said: “He meant us, and Ali is our first one, our most excellent, and our best after the Prophet عليه السلام.”

Shurays al-Wābishī informed me, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Greatest Name of Allah is made up of seventy-three letters. Asif had only one letter from it, and he spoke by it, so the earth between him and the throne of Bilqīs was swallowed up until he took hold of the throne with his hand. Then the earth returned as it had been, quicker than the blink of an eye. And with us are seventy-two letters of the Greatest Name, while one letter is with Allah, the Exalted; He has kept it exclusively with Himself in the knowledge of the unseen that is with Him. There is no might and no power except by Allah, the All-High, the All-Great.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Zakariyya ibn 'Imran al-Qummi, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from a man among the companions of Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, whose name I did not preserve, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: Indeed, 'Isa ibn Maryam عليه السلام was given two letters by which he used to act, and Musa was given four letters, and Ibrahim was given eight letters, and Nuh was given fifteen letters, and Adam was given twenty-five letters. And indeed Allah, the Exalted, gathered all of that for Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and indeed the Greatest Name of Allah consists of seventy-three letters. Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله was given seventy-two letters, and one letter was concealed from him.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali, from Abu al-Hasan, Sahib al-'Askar, عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: The Greatest Name of Allah is seventy-three letters. One letter was with Asif, so he spoke by it, and the earth was split open for him through what was between him and Saba; then he took the throne of Bilqis until he brought it to Sulayman. Then the earth spread back in less than the blink of an eye. And with us, of it, are seventy-two letters, while one letter is with Allah, exclusively reserved by Him in the knowledge of the unseen.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from Manīʿ ibn al-Ḥajjāj al-Baṣrī, from Mujāshiʿ, from Muʿallā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fayḍ, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: The staff of Mūsā belonged to Ādam (عليه السلام), then it came to Shuʿayb, then it came to Mūsā ibn ʿImrān. Indeed, it is with us, and I had seen it just recently. It is green, in its same form as when it was pulled from its tree, and it speaks when made to speak. It has been prepared for our Qāʾim (عليه السلام), who will do with it what Mūsā used to do with it. Indeed, it terrifies and swallows what they fabricate, and it does what it is commanded to do. Wherever it advances, it swallows what they fabricate; two branches are opened for it, one in the ground and the other in the ceiling, and between them are forty cubits, and it swallows what they fabricate with its tongue.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: I heard him saying: "The Tablets of Musa (عليه السلام) are with us, and the Staff of Musa is with us, and we are the inheritors of the Prophets."

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khurasani, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: Indeed, the Qa'im, when he rises in Makkah and intends to proceed to al-Kufah, his caller will call out: Lo, let none of you carry any food or drink. And he will carry the stone of Musa ibn 'Imran, and it is the load of a camel. He will not alight at any stopping-place except that a spring will gush forth from it. So whoever is hungry will be satisfied, and whoever is thirsty will be quenched. Thus it will be their provision until they come down at al-Najaf, behind al-Kufah.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn Saʿdān, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Asadī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) went out one night after dark, while he was saying in a murmur: “A murmur, a dark night; the Imam has come out to you. Upon him is the shirt of Ādam, and in his hand are the ring of Sulaymān and the staff of Mūsā (عليه السلام).”

Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Bishr ibn Ja'far, from Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: I heard him saying, 'Do you know what the shirt of Yusuf (عليه السلام) was?' He said: I said, 'No.' He said: 'When the fire was kindled for Ibrahim (عليه السلام), Jibra'il (عليه السلام) came to him with a garment from the garments of Paradise and clothed him with it, so neither heat nor cold harmed him while it was with him.' Then when death came before Ibrahim, he placed it in an amulet and hung it upon Ishaq, and Ishaq hung it upon Ya'qub. Then when Yusuf (عليه السلام) was born, he hung it upon him, and it remained on his upper arm until there occurred of his affair what occurred. Then when Yusuf brought it out from the amulet in Egypt, Ya'qub sensed its scent. And it is His saying: 'Indeed, I surely find the scent of Yusuf, were it not that you would deem me senile.' So that was the shirt which Allah sent down from Paradise. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, then to whom did that shirt pass?' He said, 'To its people.' Then he said, 'Every Prophet who left inherited knowledge or something else, it has indeed ended up with the family of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Sa'id al-Samman who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when two men from the Zaydiites came to him. They said: 'Is there among you an Imam whose obedience is obligatory?' He said: 'No.' The narrator then said they claimed: 'The trustworthy ones have informed us from you that you issue fatwas, acknowledge it and speak accordingly, and we can name them to you — so-and-so and so-and-so — they are people of piety and diligence, from among those who do not lie.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) became angry and said: 'I did not command them to this!' When they saw the anger in his face, they went out. He said to me: 'Do you know these two?' I said: 'Yes, they are both from the people of our market, from the Zaydiites, and they allege that the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is with Abdullah ibn al-Hasan.' He said: 'They lied — may Allah curse them! By Allah, Abdullah ibn al-Hasan has not seen it with his two eyes, not with one of his eyes, nor has his father seen it — O Allah! — unless he saw it with Ali ibn al-Husain (peace be upon him). If they were truthful, what is the mark on its hilt? And what is the trace at its striking-place? Indeed with me is the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with me is the banner of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), his armour, his equipment and his helmet. If they were truthful, what is the mark on the armour of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? And with me is the victorious banner of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with me are the Tablets of Moses and his Staff, and with me is the ring of Solomon son of David (peace be upon them both), and with me is the basin in which Moses (peace be upon him) used to offer the sacrifice. And with me is the Name which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he placed it between the Muslims and the polytheists, no arrow would reach from the polytheists to the Muslims. And with me is the like of what the angels brought, and the example of the weapons among us is like the example of the Ark among the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel were such that whichever household th

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Aʿyan, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “With me are the weapons of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, concerning which I am not disputed.” Then he عليه السلام said: “Surely the weapon is protected from him; if it were placed with the worst of Allah’s creation, he would become the best of them.” Then he عليه السلام said: “Surely this affair comes to the one for whom the jaw is turned; then when there is Allah’s will concerning him in it, he emerges, and the people say: ‘What is this that has happened?’ And Allah places for him a hand upon the heads of his subjects.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) left among his chattels a sword, a coat of mail, a spear, a saddle, and his grey mule; so ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام) inherited all of that.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: My father wore the armor of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, Dhāt al-Fuḍūl, and it trailed along the ground; and I wore it, and it was surplus on me.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about Dhu al-Fiqar, the sword of Rasul-Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, from where it was. He said: Jibra'il عليه السلام descended with it from the heaven, and its adornment was of silver, and it is with me.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said: The weapon is placed with us, and protected from it. If it were placed with the most evil of Allah’s creation, he would become the best of them. My father narrated to me that when he built at al-Thaqafiyyah, and there had been made for him a split in the wall, then the house was furnished. So when it was the morning of his wedding, he cast his gaze and saw opposite him fifteen nails. He was alarmed at that and said to her, “Move aside, for I wish to call my mawālī for a need.” Then he scraped it away, and there was not a single nail among them except that he found its tip turned away from the sword, and nothing from them had reached it.

I asked him about what the people relate: that a sealed parchment was entrusted to Umm Salamah. So he said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, ʿAlī (عليه السلام) inherited his knowledge, his weapons, and what was there. Then it passed to al-Hasan, then it passed to al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then, when we feared that we would be overcome, he entrusted it to Umm Salamah. Then, after that, ʿAlī ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) took possession of it. He said: So I said, Yes, then it passed to your father, then came to you, and after that it came to you? He said: Yes.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from 'Umar ibn Aban, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about what the people are saying, that a sealed scroll was handed over to Umm Salamah. So he said: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was taken, 'Ali عليه السلام inherited his knowledge, his weapons, and what was there. Then it passed to al-Hasan, then it passed to al-Husayn عليه السلام. He said: I said: Then it passed to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, then it passed to his son, then it came to you? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid Shabab al-Sayrafi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said: When death came upon Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), he called al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام). He said to al-Abbas, “O uncle of Muhammad, will you take the inheritance of Muhammad, settle his debt, and fulfill his promises?” He replied, “O Rasul Allah, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, I am an old man with many dependents and little wealth; who can bear your burden while you outdo the wind in generosity?” He said: then he (صلى الله عليه وآله) was silent for a little while, then said, “O Abbas, will you take the inheritance of Muhammad, fulfill his promises, and settle his debt?” He said, “May my father and mother be ransomed for you, I am an old man with many dependents and little wealth, and you outdo the wind.” He said, “Indeed, I shall give it to one who will take it with its due right.” Then he said, “O Ali, O brother of Muhammad, will you fulfill the promises of Muhammad, settle his debt, and take possession of his inheritance?” He said, “Yes, may my father and mother be ransomed for you; that is upon me and belongs to me.” He said: then I looked at him until he removed his ring from his finger and said, “Wear this during my lifetime.” He said: then I looked at the ring when I placed it upon my finger, and from all that he left behind I wished for the ring. Then he called out, “O Bilal, bring me the helmet, the armor, the banner, the shirt, Dhu al-Faqar, al-Sahab, the cloak, the al-abraqah, and the staff.” He said: by Allah, I had not seen it except at that very hour—meaning al-abraqah—then a piece was brought that nearly dazzled the eyes, and it was from the brocades of al-Jannah. Then he said, “O Ali, Jibra'il came to me with it and said: O Muhammad, place it in the ring of the armor and fasten yourself with it in the place of the belt.” Then he called for two Arabian sandals together, one of them patched and the other unpatched; and for two shirts: the shirt in which he was taken on the Night Journey, and the shirt in which he went out on the Day of Uhud; and for the three caps: the cap of travel, the cap of the two Eids and Fridays, and a cap that he used to wear while sitting with his companions. Then he said, “O Bilal, bring me

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, from Saʿīd al-Sammān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (ṣalawātullāh ʿalayh) saying: Indeed, the likeness of the weapon among us is like the Ark among the Children of Israel. Among the Children of Israel, whichever household the Ark was found at their door, they were given prophethood. So whoever among us the weapon comes to, he is given the Imamate.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn al-Sukayn, from Nūḥ ibn Darrāj, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “The likeness of the weapon among us is only like the Ark among Banī Isrāʾīl. Wherever the Ark turned, the kingdom turned; so wherever the weapon turns among us, knowledge turns.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say: “The likeness of the weapon among us is only like the Ark among the Children of Israel. Wherever the Ark turned, prophethood was given; and wherever the weapon turns among us, there is the authority.” I said, “So does the weapon become separate from knowledge?” He عليه السلام said, “No.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: The likeness of the weapon among us is only like the likeness of the Ark among the Children of Isrāʾīl: wherever the Ark turned, the kingdom turned; and wherever the weapon turns among us, knowledge turns.

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the Divine Proof cannot be established for Allah against His creatures except by an Imam, until He is recognised.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Divine Authority of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be established upon His creation except by an Imam until He is recognized.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Umarah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: 'The Divine proof of God cannot be established upon His creation except through an Imam, so that He may be recognized.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Aban ibn Taghlub who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Divine Authority (was) before the creation, and (is) with the creation, and (will be) after the creation.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Hajjal, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from Abu Basir who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: May I be sacrificed for you! I want to ask you a question — is there anyone here who would hear my words? He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) raised a curtain between him and another room, looked into it, then said: O Abu Muhammad! Ask about whatever comes to you. He said: I said: May I be sacrificed for you! Your Shia followers narrate that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a door (of knowledge) from which a thousand doors open for him. So he said: O Abu Muhammad! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a thousand doors — from each door a thousand doors open. I said: This, by God, is the knowledge! He then made marks in the ground for a while, then said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that. He then said: O Abu Muhammad! And with us is the Jami'a — and what do they know what the Jami'a is? I said: May I be sacrificed for you! And what is the Jami'a? He said: A parchment seventy cubits long by the cubit of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), dictated from his own mouth and written by Ali's right hand. In it is every permissible and forbidden thing, and everything the people need, to the extent of the blood-money for a scratch. He then extended his hand toward me and said: Do you permit me, O Abu Muhammad? I said: May I be sacrificed for you! I am but yours — do whatever you wish. So he pressed me with his hand and said: To the extent of this — as if he were angry. I said: This, by God, is the knowledge! He said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that. Then he was silent for a while, then said: And with us is the Jafr — and what do they know what the Jafr is? I said: And what is the Jafr? He said: A leather vessel containing the knowledge of the prophets, the successors, and the scholars who have passed from the Children of Israel. I said: This is the knowledge! He said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that. Then he was silent for a while, then said: And with us is the Parchment of Fatima (peace be upon her) — and what do they know what the Parchment of Fatima is? I said: And what is the Parchment of Fatima (peace be upon her)? He

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “The zanādiqah will appear in the year one hundred and twenty-eight, and that is because I looked into the Muṣḥaf of Fāṭimah (عليها السلام).” He said: I said, “And what is the Muṣḥaf of Fāṭimah?” He said: “When Allah, the Exalted, took His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), there entered upon Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), due to his passing, such grief as none knows except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah sent to her an angel to console her sorrow and speak to her. She mentioned that to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), and he said: ‘When you sense that and hear the voice, tell me.’” So she informed him of that, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) began writing everything that he heard until he compiled from that a Muṣḥaf. He said: Then he said: ‘Indeed, there is nothing in it of the halal and the haram, but in it is the knowledge of what will be.’”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, with me is al-Jafr al-Abyaḍ.” He said: I said, “So what is in it?” He said: “The Zabūr of Dāwūd, the Tawrah of Mūsā, the Injīl of ʿĪsā, and the Ṣuḥuf of Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام), and the halal and the haram, and the Muṣḥaf of Fāṭimah. I do not claim that there is a Qur’an in it, and in it is what the people need from us, while we do not need anyone, such that in it are the lashing, half a lashing, a quarter of a lashing, and the indemnity for a scratch.” And with me is al-Jafr al-Aḥmar.” He said: I said, “And what is in al-Jafr al-Aḥmar?” He said: “The weapons, and that is only opened for blood; the صاحب of the sword opens it for killing.” Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr said to him: “May Allah set you right! Do Banū al-Ḥasan know this?” He said: “Yes, by Allah, just as they know the night to be night and the day to be day. But envy and seeking the world lead them to rejection and denial; and if they had sought the truth through the truth, it would have been better for them.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) said: “Indeed, in the Jafr which they mention, there is that which displeases them, because they do not speak the truth, while the truth is in it.” So let them bring forth the judgments of Ali and his ordinances, if they are truthful; and ask them about the maternal aunts and the paternal aunts; and let them bring forth the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام), for indeed in it is the bequest of Fatimah (عليها السلام), and with it are the weapons of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Bring a book before this, or a trace of knowledge, if you are truthful.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said: One of our companions asked Aba 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) about al-Jafr, so he said: “It is an ox-hide filled with knowledge.” He said to him, “Then al-Jami'ah?” He said: “That is a scroll whose length is seventy cubits, in the width of the tanned hide, like the thigh of the camel, containing everything the people need; and there is no legal case except that it is in it, even the compensation for a scratch.” He said, “Then the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام)?” He said: So he remained silent for a long while, then said: “You indeed inquire into what you need and what you do not need.” Fatimah (عليها السلام) remained after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) for seventy-five days, and intense grief over her father entered upon her. Jibra'il (عليه السلام) used to come to her, console her excellently regarding her father, comfort her soul, inform her about her father and his place, and inform her of what would occur after her among her progeny; and 'Ali (عليه السلام) would write that down. So that is the Mushaf of Fatimah (عليها السلام).

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Bishr, from Bakr ibn Karib al-Ṣayrafī, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “With us is that by which we have no need of the people, while the people are in need of us. And with us is a book dictated by Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and written in the hand of ʿAlī عليه السلام, a scroll in which is every halal and haram. And indeed, you come to us with matters, and we know when you act upon it, and we know when you leave it.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar and Burayd ibn Muawiyah and Zurarah, that Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan said: To Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: The Zaydiyyah and the Mu'tazilah have gathered around Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, so does he have authority? So he عليه السلام said: By Allah, with me are two books in which is the naming of every Prophet and every king who will rule the earth. No, by Allah, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah is not in either one of them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Fudayl ibn Sakkarah, who said: I entered upon Abī 'Abdillāh (عليه السلام), and he said: "O Fudayl, do you know in what thing I was looking just a little before?" He said: I said, "No." He said: "I was looking in the Book of Fatimah (عليها السلام). There is no king who rules the earth except that he is written in it by his name and the name of his father, and I did not find anything in it for the offspring of al-Hasan."

Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, all together from al-Ḥasan ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Ḥarīsh, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī (عليه السلام), who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: While my father (عليه السلام) was performing tawaf around the Kaʿbah, suddenly a man wrapped in a turban, who had been assigned to him, interrupted his seven circuits until he brought him into a house beside al-Ṣafā. Then he sent for me, and we were three. He said: Welcome, O son of the Messenger of Allah. Then he placed his hand on my head and said: May Allah bless you, O trustee of Allah after his forefathers. O Abā Jaʿfar, if you wish, then inform me; and if you wish, I shall inform you; and if you wish, ask me; and if you wish, I shall ask you; and if you wish, affirm me truthful; and if you wish, I shall affirm you truthful. He said: I desire all of that. He said: Then beware that your tongue should speak during my questioning with a matter while you conceal for me other than it. He said: Only one in whose heart are two knowledges does that, with one of them opposing the other; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has refused that there be for Him any knowledge in which there is contradiction. He said: This is my question, and you have explained part of it. Inform me about this knowledge in which there is no contradiction: who knows it? He said: As for the totality of knowledge, it is with Allah, majestic is His mention; and as for that from it which the servants cannot do without, it is with the awṣiyāʾ. He said: So the man opened his head-wrap, sat upright, his face lit up, and he said: This is what I wanted, and for it I came. You claim that the knowledge in which there is no contradiction is with the awṣiyāʾ; so how do they know it? He said: Just as the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) used to know it, except that they do not see what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) used to see, because he was a Prophet and they are spoken to, and because he used to go in delegation to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and hear the revelation, while they do not hear. He said: You have spoken the truth, O son of the Messenger of Allah. I shall bring you a difficult question. Inform me about this knowledge: why is it that it does not appear as it used to appear with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله علي

From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: While my father was seated and in his presence were a number of people, he suddenly laughed until his eyes filled with tears. Then he said: 'Do you know what made me laugh?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'Ibn Abbas claims that he is among those who said: Our Lord is Allah, then stood firm [41:30]. So I said to him: Have you ever seen the Angels, O Ibn Abbas, informing you of their guardianship over you in this world and the next, along with security from fear and grief? He said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'The believers are but brothers' [49:10], and the entire community is included in this. So I smiled and said: You speak the truth, O Ibn Abbas! I adjure you by Allah — is there any contradiction in the rulings of Allah, Majestic is His Mention? He said: No. So I said: What is your view regarding a man who struck another man's fingers with a sword until they fell off, then he left, and another man came and severed his palm, and the case is brought to you while you are a judge — how would you rule? He said: I would tell this cutter to give him the blood money for his palm, and I would tell the one whose hand was cut to reach a settlement on whatever terms he wishes and to send him to people of justice. I said: Then contradiction has entered the rulings of Allah, Mighty is His Mention, and you have contradicted your first words. Allah, Mighty is His Mention, refuses to establish anything among His creation from the legal penalties without its interpretation existing on earth. Cut off the hand of the palm-cutter from its root, then give him the blood money for the fingers. Such is the ruling of Allah on the night in which His command descends. If you were to deny it after what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then Allah would admit you into the Fire just as He blinded your sight on the day you denied it against Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: Was it for that reason my sight was blinded? And what made you know that? By Allah, my sight was not blinded except by the stroke of an angel's wing. He said: So I smiled and left him that day due to the feebleness of his intellect. Then I met him and said: O Ibn Abbas! You did not speak with truthfulness as you did yesterday. Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) told you: The Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) is in every year, a

And by this chain, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said regarding Laylat al-Qadr: “In it every wise matter is made distinct.” He is saying: every wise matter descends in it, and the decisive matter is not two things; rather, it is one single thing. So whoever judges by that in which there is no disagreement, then his judgment is from the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and whoever judges by a matter in which there is disagreement, and considers himself correct, then he has judged with the judgment of al-Ṭāghūt. Indeed, in Laylat al-Qadr the explanation of affairs descends, year by year, to the Walī al-Amr. In it, he is commanded regarding the matter of himself with such and such, and regarding the affairs of the people with such and such. And besides that, there occurs for the Walī al-Amr every day the special, concealed, wondrous, stored knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, similar to what descends during that night of the command. Then he recited: “And if all the trees in the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas after it to replenish it, the Words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed Allah is Mighty, Wise.”

And by this chain, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah's blessings be upon him) used to say: 'Indeed We revealed it on the Night of Power' God Almighty and Majestic spoke the truth. God revealed the Quran on the Night of Power. 'And what will make you know what the Night of Power is?' — the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not know.' God Almighty and Majestic said: 'The Night of Power is better than a thousand months' in which there is no Night of Power. He asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'Do you know why it is better than a thousand months?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Because therein the angels and the Spirit descend by the permission of their Lord for every affair', and when God Almighty and Majestic permits something, He has approved it. 'Peace it is until the break of dawn' — He is saying: 'My angels and My Spirit submit their greetings upon you, O Muhammad, with My greeting, from the beginning of their descent until the break of dawn.' Then He said in another part of His Book: 'And guard yourselves against a trial which may not afflict particularly those of you who are unjust' (8:25) — regarding 'Indeed We revealed it on the Night of Power' (97:1). And He said in another part of His Book: 'And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; indeed messengers have passed away before him; if then he dies or is killed, will you turn back upon your heels? And whoever turns back upon his heels, he shall not do harm to God in the least, and God will reward the grateful' (3:144). He is saying in the first verse: when Muhammad passes away, the people of opposition to God's command Almighty and Majestic will say: 'The Night of Power expired with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).' So this is a trial that afflicted them specifically, and by it they turned back upon their heels — because if they were to say 'It did not pass away,' then there would inevitably have to be a command from God Almighty and Majestic during it, and if they acknowledged the command, there could be no escape from there being a Master for it.

And from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say frequently: Al-Taymī and Al-ʿAdawī would gather in the presence of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله while he was reciting “Indeed, We sent it down” with humility and weeping, and they would say: How intense is your tenderness for this surah. So Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله would say: Because of what my eye has seen, what my heart has comprehended, and what the heart of this one will see after me. So they would say: And what is it that you saw, and what is it that he will see? He said: Then he would write for them in the dust: “The angels and the Spirit descend therein, by the permission of their Lord, with every affair.” He said: Then he would say: Does anything remain after His, Mighty and Majestic, saying, “with every affair”? They would say: No. Then he would say: Do you know to whom that is sent down? They would say: To you, O Rasūl Allāh. He would say: Yes. Then he would say: Will Laylat al-Qadr exist after me? They would say: Yes. He said: Then he would say: Will that affair descend in it? They would say: Yes. He said: Then he would say: To whom? They would say: We do not know. Then he would take hold of my head and say: If you do not know, then know: it is this one after me. He said: So indeed they both came to recognize that night after Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله because of the intensity of the dread that entered into them.

O group of the Shia! Argue using Surah 'Verily We revealed it' (Al-Qadr) and you will prevail, for by Allah, it is the proof of Allah, Blessed and Most High, over creation after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and it is the chief of your religion, and it is the summit of our knowledge. O group of the Shia! Argue using: 'Ha Mim. By the Clarifying Book. Verily We revealed it on a Blessed Night. Verily We are warners' (Surah Al-Dukhan 44:1-3), for these verses pertain specifically to the Masters of Command after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). O group of the Shia! Allah, Blessed and Most High, says: 'And there is not a community but a warner has passed among them' (35:24). It was said: O Abu Ja'far! The warner is Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). He said: You speak the truth. Was there a warner from the sent ones in the regions of the earth while he was alive? The questioner said: No. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: What do you think — is not his emissary his warner, just as the Messenger of Allah in his mission from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was a warner? He said: Yes. He said: Similarly, Muhammad did not die except that he had an emissary warner. He said: If I were to say no, then the Messenger of Allah would have abandoned those in the loins of men from his community. He said: And does the Quran not suffice them? He said: Yes, if they find an interpreter for it. He said: And did the Messenger of Allah not interpret it? He said: Yes, he interpreted it to one man, and he explained to the community the status of that man — and he is Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). The questioner said: O Abu Ja'far! This was a special matter that the general public cannot bear. He said: Allah refused to be worshipped except in secret until there comes the appointed time in which His religion is manifested, just as the Messenger of Allah was concealed with Khadijah until he was commanded with the proclamation. The questioner said: It is fitting for the master of this religion to conceal. He said: Did not Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) conceal on the day he embraced Islam with the Messenger of Allah until his matter was revealed? He said: Yes. He said: Similarly is our matter, until the Book reaches its appointed term.

And from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Allah, majestic is His remembrance, indeed created Laylat al-Qadr at the very beginning of creating the world, and in it He created the first Prophet who would be and the first Waṣī who would be. And He decreed that in every year there would be a night in which the explanation of affairs would descend until its like in the coming year. Whoever denies that has rejected Allah’s knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, for the Prophets, the Messengers, and the Muḥaddathūn do not stand except that there is a proof upon them by what comes to them in that night together with the proof that Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) brings to them. I said: And do the Muḥaddathūn also receive Jibrāʾīl, or someone else from the angels (عليه السلام)? He said: As for the Prophets and the Messengers, blessings of Allah be upon them, there is no doubt; and it is necessary for those besides them, from the first day on which the earth was created until the end of the world’s annihilation, that there be a divine proof over the people of the earth, to whom that descends on that night from among whomever He loves of His servants. By Allah, the Spirit and the angels indeed descended with the command on Laylat al-Qadr upon Ādam; and by Allah, Ādam did not die except that he had a Waṣī. And everyone after Ādam from among the Prophets received the command in it and assigned it to his Waṣī after him. And by Allah, the Prophet was indeed commanded regarding what came to him of the affair on that night, from Ādam to Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), that he should appoint so-and-so as successor. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has indeed said in His Book specifically concerning the possessors of authority after Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله): “Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the earth just as He made those before them successors” up to His saying, “then those are the defiantly disobedient.” He says: I make you successors for My knowledge, My religion, and My worship after your Prophet, just as He made the successors of Ādam after him until He sends the Prophet who follows him: “They worship Me, not associating anything with Me.” He says: They worship Me with faith that there is no Prophet after Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله); so whoever says otherwise, then those are the defiantly disobedient.

He said: And he said. A man said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, do not be angry with me.” He said, “Why?” He said, “Because of what I wish to ask you about.” He said, “Speak.” He said, “And you will not be angry?” He said, “And I will not be angry.” He said, “What do you say about your statement concerning Laylat al-Qadr and the descent of the angels and the Spirit in it to the Awṣiyāʾ? Do they come to them with a matter that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله had not known, or do they come to them with a matter that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله knew? And I have known that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله died while none of his knowledge existed except that ʿAlī عليه السلام was preserving it.” Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said, “What is there between me and you, O man? And who brought you to me?” He said, “Al-Qaḍāʾ brought me to you in seeking the religion.” He said, “Then understand what I say to you: when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was taken on the night journey, he did not descend until Allah, Majestic is His mention, taught him the knowledge of what had been and what will be. Much of that knowledge was in summary form, and its explanation would come in Laylat al-Qadr. Likewise, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام had known the totalities of knowledge, and its explanation would come in the nights of al-Qadr just as it had been with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.” The questioner said, “Was there not explanation within those totalities?” He said, “Yes, but the command from Allah the Exalted only comes in the nights of al-Qadr to the Prophet and to the Awṣiyāʾ: ‘Do such and such,’ regarding a matter they had already known; they were commanded how to act concerning it.” I said, “Explain this to me.” He said, “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not die except while preserving the totality of the knowledge and its explanation.” I said, “So that which used to come to him in the nights of al-Qadr, what knowledge was it?” He said, “The command and the facilitation concerning what he had already known.” The questioner said, “Then does knowledge occur for them in the nights of al-Qadr besides what they knew?” He said, “This is among what they were commanded to conceal, and none knows the explanation of what you asked about except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” The

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Why do you see those whom God, Mighty and Majestic, has dispatched for wretchedness upon the people of misguidance from the armies of the Satans and their consorts to be more numerous than what you see of the Caliph of God whom He dispatched for justice and righteousness from among the Angels? It was said: O Abu Ja'far, how can anything be more numerous than the Angels? He said: As God, Mighty and Majestic, has willed. The questioner said: O Abu Ja'far, if I were to narrate this hadith to some of the Shi'a, they would deny it. He said: How would they deny it? He said: They would say that the Angels are more numerous than the Satans. He said: You are right. Understand from me what I am saying: there is not a single day or night except that all the Jinn and Satans visit the imams of misguidance, and an equal number of Angels visits the Imam of Guidance — until when the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) comes, Angels descend during it to the Master of the Command in a number that God, Mighty and Majestic, has created — or said: destined — from among the Satans as their equal number. Then they visit the master of misguidance and bring him fabrications and lies, until perhaps he wakes up in the morning saying: I saw such-and-such. But if one were to ask the Master of the Command about that, he would say: You saw a Satan who informed you of such-and-such, until he would interpret it for him and make known to him the misguidance upon which he stands. And by God, whoever believes in the Night of Power knows that it belongs to us exclusively, by virtue of the saying of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him) when death drew near him: This is your guardian after me — if you obey him you will be rightly guided. But whoever does not believe in what is in the Night of Power is a denier, and whoever believes in the Night of Power while holding a view other than ours — it is not permissible for him in truth except to say that it belongs to us; and whoever does not say so is a liar.
