Surely God, Mighty and Majestic, is too exalted to send down the Command with the Spirit and the Angels to a disbeliever, a transgressor. If they say that it descends to the Caliph who claims that authority, then their saying is worthless; and if they say that it does not descend to anyone, it cannot be that something

Ahmad ibn Idrees al-Qummi and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn Ayyub, from Abu Yahya al-San'ani, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: He said to me, "O Abu Yahya, indeed for us, on the nights of Friday, there is a matter of great significance." He said: I said, "May I be sacrificed for you, and what is that matter?" He said, "Permission is given to the souls of the deceased Prophets عليهم السلام, and the souls of the deceased successors, and the soul of the successor who is present among you, that it is ascended to the heaven until it reaches the Throne of its Lord. Then it circumambulates it seven times and performs salat (prayer) of two rak'ahs at each pillar from the pillars of the Throne. Then it is returned to the bodies in which it had been." So the Prophets and the successors come into the morning filled with joy, and the successor who is present among you comes into the morning having been increased in his knowledge by an immense abundance.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Yusuf al-Abzari, from al-Mufaddal, who said: Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام said to me one day—and before that he had not addressed me by my kunyah—: “O Abu ‘Abdillah.” He said: I said, “At your service.” He said: “For us, in every Friday night, there is joy.” I said: “May Allah increase you, and what is that?” He said: “When it is Friday night, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله reaches the Throne, and the Imams عليهم السلام reach it with him, and we reach it with them. So our spirits are not returned to our bodies except with acquired knowledge, and were it not for that, we would be exhausted.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Yunus or al-Mufaddal, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: There is no Friday night except that in it there is joy for the awliya' of Allah. I said: How is that, may I be your ransom? He عليه السلام said: When it is Friday night, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله comes to the Throne, and the Imams عليهم السلام come, and I come with them. Then I do not return except with acquired knowledge, and were it not for that, what is with me would be exhausted.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) saying: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad (عليه السلام) used to say: If we were not increased, we would be exhausted. Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Ṣafwān, from Abū al-Ḥasan, similarly.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Zurayh al-Muharibi, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said to me: “O Zurayh, were it not that we are increased, we would be exhausted.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Thaʿlabah, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “Were it not that we are increased, we would be exhausted.” He said: I said, “Are you increased with something that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not know?” He said: “Indeed, when that occurs, it is presented to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), then to the Imams, then the matter comes to us.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from one of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Nothing comes forth from the presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until it begins with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then with Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, then with each one after another, so that our last should not be more knowledgeable than our first.

Indeed, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there are two knowledges: a knowledge which He made manifest to His angels, His Prophets, and His Messengers. So whatever He made manifest to His angels, His Messengers, and His Prophets, we have known it. And there is a knowledge which He kept exclusively to Himself; then when something from it becomes manifest by Allah's will, He informs us of that, and it was presented to the Imams who were before us. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim; and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-'Amraki ibn Ali—altogether—from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام, similarly to it.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are two knowledges: a knowledge that is with Him, upon which He has not informed anyone from His creation; and a knowledge that He has conveyed to His angels and His messengers. So whatever He has conveyed to His angels and His messengers has indeed reached us.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḍurays, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are two knowledges: a knowledge disclosed and a knowledge withheld. As for the disclosed, there is nothing from what the angels and the messengers know except that we know it. And as for the withheld, it is that which is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the Mother of the Book; when it emerges, it takes effect.”

Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Suwayd al-Qallāʾ, from Abī Ayyūb, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are two knowledges: a knowledge that none knows except Him, and a knowledge that He taught to His angels and His Messengers. So whatever He taught to His angels and His Messengers (عليهم السلام), we know it.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, who said: A man from the people of Persia asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said to him: “Do you know the unseen?” So he said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Knowledge is spread out for us, so we know; and it is withheld from us, so we do not know.” And he said: “The secret of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, He confided it to Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, and Jibrāʾīl confided it to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and Muḥammad confided it to whomever Allah willed.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Sadīr al-Ṣayrafī, who said: I heard Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyan asking Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “The Originator of the heavens and the earth.” Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, originated all things by His knowledge, without any prior likeness existing before them. So He originated the heavens and the earths, and there were no heavens nor earths before them. Do you not hear His saying, Exalted is He:” “And His Throne was upon the water.” Then Ḥumrān said to him: “What is your view regarding His saying, majestic is His mention:” “The Knower of the unseen, so He does not disclose His unseen to anyone.” So Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “Except one whom He has approved from a Messenger.” “And by Allah, Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) was among those whom He approved. As for His saying, ‘The Knower of the unseen,’ then indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows what is hidden from His creation regarding whatever He determines of a thing and decrees in His knowledge before creating it, and before conveying it to the angels.” “So that, O Ḥumrān, is knowledge withheld with Him; to it belongs the will concerning it. He decrees it when He wills, and there occurs for Him regarding it such that He does not carry it through. But as for the knowledge that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, determines, then He decrees it and executes it; that is the knowledge which reached the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), then to us.”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Sadir Sadir said: When he (the Imam) arose from his gathering and went to his house, I and Abu Basir and Muyassar entered upon him and said to him, May we be sacrificed for you! We heard you saying such and such regarding the matter of your maidservant, and we know that you possess vast knowledge, but we are not attributing the knowledge of the unseen to you. He said: O Sadir! Have you not read the Quran? I said: Yes. He said: Did you find in what you read from the Book of God, the Mighty and Majestic: The one who had knowledge from the Book said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you (in the blink of an eye) He (the narrator) said: I said, May I be sacrificed for you! I have read it. He said: Do you know who the man was, and do you know what knowledge of the Book he had? I said: Inform me of it. He said: A measure like a drop of water in the green ocean -- that is what he had from the knowledge of the Book. I said, May I be sacrificed for you! How little this is! He said: O Sadir! How great this is that God, Mighty and Majestic, should attribute it to the Knowledge which I am about to inform you of! O Sadir! Did you also find in what you read from the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic: Say: God is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and the one who has the knowledge of the Book He (the narrator) said: I said, I have read it, may I be sacrificed for you! He said: Is the one with whom is all the knowledge of the Book more understanding, or the one with whom is part of the knowledge of the Book? I said: No, but the one with whom is all the knowledge of the Book. He said: So he gestured with his hand toward his chest and said: The knowledge of the Book, by God, all of it is with us! The knowledge of the Book, by God, all of it is with us!

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the Imam: does he know the unseen? So he said: “No; rather, when he intends to know a thing, Allah informs him of that.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Muskān, from Badr ibn al-Walīd, from Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Imam, when he desires to know, is taught.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Badr ibn al-Walid, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, when the Imam desires to know, he is informed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Mada'ini, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: When the Imam intends to know something, Allah lets him know that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Sulayman ibn Sama'ah and Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Batal, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) said: “Any Imam who does not know what will befall him and to what he will come, then that is not a Proof of Allah over His creation.”

A shaykh from the people of Qaṭīʿat al-Rabīʿ, from the general populace in Baghdad, from those from whom reports were transmitted, narrated to me, saying: He said: He said to me, “I have indeed seen one of those from the people of this Household whose excellence they speak of, and I have never seen anyone like him at all in his excellence and his devotion.” So I said to him, “Who was he, and how did you see him?” He said: “During the days of al-Sindī ibn Shāhak, eighty men of standing, ascribed to goodness, were gathered, and we were admitted to Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). Al-Sindī said to us, ‘O people, look at this man. Has any harm happened to him? The people claim that something has been done to him, and they speak much about that. Here is his lodging and his bedding, made spacious for him and not restricted. The Commander of the Faithful intended no evil for him; rather, he is only keeping him until he comes to debate with the Commander of the Faithful. Here he is, sound, and ease has been granted to him in all his affairs. So ask him.’” He said: “We had no concern except to look at the man, and at his excellence and his bearing. Then Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said, ‘As for what he mentioned of spaciousness and the like of it, it is as he said; except that I inform you, O group, that I have been given poison in seven dates. Tomorrow I shall turn green, and the day after tomorrow I shall die.’” He said: “Then I looked at al-Sindī ibn Shāhak, and he was shaking and trembling like a palm frond.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamilah, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, who said: My brother narrated to me, from Ja'far, from his father. He went to Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) with a drink on the night in which he passed away, and he said: O my father, drink this. He said: O my son, this is the night in which I shall be taken, and it is the night in which Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was taken.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm, who said: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام had known his killer, and the night in which he would be killed, and the place in which he would be killed, and his saying when he heard the cries of the geese in the house: “Screaming ones, to be followed by wailing ones.” And the saying of Umm Kulthūm: “If only you would pray tonight inside the house and order someone else to lead the people in salat (prayer),” but he refused her, and his going in and out frequently that night without a weapon, while he عليه السلام knew that Ibn Muljam—may Allah curse him—was his killer by the sword. Was this among that to which it was not permissible for him to expose himself? So he عليه السلام said: “That was so, but he was given the choice on that night so that the decrees of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, might come to pass.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from some of our companions, from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, became angry with the Shiʿah, so He gave me the choice of myself or them; so I protected them, by Allah, with myself.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Musāfir, that Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام said: To him: “O Musāfir, are there fish in this canal?” He said, “Yes, may I be your ransom.” So he said: “Indeed, I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله last night, and he was saying: ‘O ʿAlī, what is with us is better for you.’”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Abū Khadījah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I was with my father on the day in which he passed away, and he instructed me regarding matters of his ghusl, his shrouding, and his being entered into his grave. So I said: O my father, by Allah, since you fell ill I have not seen you in better condition than today; I do not see upon you the trace of death. So he said: O my son, did you not hear ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام calling from behind the wall: O Muḥammad, come quickly!

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Allah, the Exalted, sent down help upon al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام until it filled what was between the heaven and the earth. Then he was given the choice of help or meeting Allah, so he chose meeting Allah, the Exalted.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Sayf al-Tammar, who said: We were with Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), a group from the Shi'ah, in al-Hijr. So he said: "Is there an eye upon us?" Then we turned to the right and the left, but we did not see anyone, so we said: "There is no eye upon us." He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, and by the Lord of the structure"—three times—"if I had been between Musa and al-Khidr, I would have informed them that I am more knowledgeable than both of them, and I would have informed them of what was not in their possession. For Musa and al-Khidr (عليهما السلام) were given the knowledge of what had been, and they were not given the knowledge of what will be and what is to occur until the Hour is established. And we have inherited it from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) as an inheritance."

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah and a number of our companions, among whom were Abd al-A'la, Abu Ubaydah, and Abdullah ibn Bishr al-Khath'ami, heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: Indeed, I surely know what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and I know what is in Paradise, and I know what is in the Fire, and I know what has been and what will be. He said: Then he paused for a little while, and he saw that this had weighed heavily upon those who had heard it from him, so he said: I came to know that from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in it: "A clarification of everything."

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Jama'ah ibn Sa'd al-Khath'ami, that he said: Al-Mufaddal was with Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, so Al-Mufaddal said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, would Allah obligate the obedience of a servant upon the servants and withhold from him the news of the heaven?” He عليه السلام said: “No. Allah is more generous, more merciful, and more compassionate toward His servants than to obligate the obedience of a servant upon the servants and then withhold from him the news of the heaven, morning and evening.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying — while in his presence were people from his companions — 'I am astonished at a group of people who show loyalty to us and make us their Imams, and describe that obedience to us is obligatory upon them just as obedience to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), yet then they break their own argument and defeat themselves by the weakness of their hearts, so they diminish our right and blame that upon those whom God has given the proof of the right knowledge of us and submission to our command.' Do you think that God, Blessed and Exalted, would make obedience to His guardians obligatory upon His servants, and then hide from them the news of the heavens and the earth, and cut off from them the sources of knowledge regarding what comes to them of that by which their religion is upheld? So Humran said to him: 'May I be your ransom! What is your view of what occurred regarding the rising of Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) — their going forth and their rising with the religion of God, Mighty is His mention — and what befell them from the tyrants killing them and being victorious over them until they were killed and overcome?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Humran! Indeed God, Blessed and Exalted, had already decreed that upon them, and ordained it, and carried it through, and made it inevitable — on the path of their free choice — then He brought it about. It was by the preceding knowledge conveyed to them from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) that Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) rose, and it was by knowledge that those of us who remain silent, remained silent.' And had they, O Humran, when there descended upon them what descended from the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, and the victory of the tyrants over them — had they asked God, Mighty and Majestic, to repel that from them, and had they persisted in seeking the removal of the tyrants' kingdom and the end of their rule, He would have answered them and repelled that from them, and the expiry of the tyrants' period and the annihilation of their kingdom would have come faster than the dispersal of beads when their thread is cut and they scatter. And that w

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Maʿbad, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام at Minā about five hundred expressions from theological discourse, and I began saying: “They say such and such.” He said: “Then say: such and such.” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you! This is the halal and this is the haram; I know that you are its master and that you are the most knowledgeable of the people concerning it, but this is theological discourse.” So he said to me: “Woe to you, O Hishām! Allah, Blessed and Exalted, does not establish His proof over His creation by means of a proof who does not possess all that they need.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام saying: “No, by Allah! A knowledgeable one is never ignorant, such that he would know one thing and be ignorant of another thing.” Then he said: “Allah is more majestic, mightier, and more generous than to obligate obedience to a servant while veiling from him the knowledge of His heaven and His earth.” Then he said: “That is not veiled from him.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Humran ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Jibra'il عليه السلام came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with two pomegranates. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ate one of them, and he broke the other into two halves. He ate one half and fed Ali half. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O my brother, do you know what these two pomegranates are?” He said: “No.” He said: “As for the first, it is prophethood; you have no share in it. And as for the other, it is knowledge; you are my partner in it.” So I said: “May Allah keep you well, how was he his partner in it?” He said: “Allah did not teach Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله any knowledge except that He commanded him to teach it to Ali عليه السلام.”

ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) descended to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) with two pomegranates from Paradise. He gave them both to him, so he ate one of them and split the other into two halves. He gave ʿAlī (عليه السلام) half of it, and he ate it. Then he said: “O ʿAlī, as for the first pomegranate that I ate, it is prophethood, and you have no share in it; and as for the other, it is knowledge, so you are my partner in it.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: Jibraʾil descended upon Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) with two pomegranates from Paradise. Then ʿAli (عليه السلام) met him and said: What are these two pomegranates in your hand? He said: As for this one, it is prophethood; there is no share for you in it. And as for this one, it is knowledge. Then the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) split it into two halves, gave him one half, and the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) took its other half. Then he said: You are my partner in it, and I am your partner in it. He said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not know a single letter of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught him except that he had taught it to ʿAli. Then the knowledge came down to us. Then he placed his hand upon his chest.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Can the earth happen to be such that there is no Imam in it?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'Can there be two Imams (at the same time)?' He said: 'No, except that one of the two would be silent.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus and Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'The earth cannot be devoid [of an Imam] except that there would be an Imam in it, so that if the believers exceed in something, he would bring them back, and if they fall short in something, he would complete it for them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-'Amiri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The earth has never ceased to have for God in it a Divine Authority (Hujja) who makes known the permissible and the forbidden and who invites the people to the Way of God.
Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: 'Can the earth remain without an Imam?' He said: 'No.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), who said: Indeed God will not leave the earth without a knowledgeable one, and were it not for that, Truth would not be distinguished from falsehood.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah is more Majestic and more Magnificent than that He would leave the earth without a just Imam.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Usama; and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Usama and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Is'haq — from one whom he trusts among the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) — that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, indeed You do not leave Your earth empty of a Divine Authority of Yours over Your creatures.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: By Allah! Allah did not leave the earth since He took the soul of Adam (peace be upon him), except that in it there was an Imam through whom one is guided to Allah, and he is His proof upon His servants; and the earth cannot remain without an Imam who is a divine authority of Allah upon His servants.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the earth cannot be empty of a Divine Authority (Hujja), and I, by God, am that Divine Authority.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), "Can the earth remain without an Imam?" He said: "If the earth were to remain without an Imam, it would sink."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, “Can the earth remain without an Imam?” He said, “No.” I said, “For we narrate from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام that it does not remain without an Imam unless Allah, Exalted is He, becomes wrathful against the people of the earth, or against the servants.” So he said, “No, no; it would not remain. In that case, it would collapse.”

ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Muʾmin, from Abī Hirāsah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: If the Imam were to be raised from the earth for an hour, it would surge with its inhabitants just as the sea surges with its inhabitants.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, who said: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, "Can the earth remain without an Imam?" He said, "No." I said, "We narrate that it does not remain except when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, becomes wrathful with the servants." He said, "It does not remain; otherwise, it would sink."

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazi', from 'Ali al-Sa'i, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal Musa عليه السلام, who said: He عليه السلام said: "The extent of our knowledge is in three aspects: past, bygone, and newly occurring. As for the past, it is explained; as for the bygone, it is inscribed; and as for the newly occurring, it is a casting into the hearts and a tapping in the ears. And it is the most excellent of our knowledge, and there is no Prophet after our Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Zāhir, from ʿAlī ibn Mūsā, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said, "Inform me about the knowledge of your knowledgeable one." He said, "It is an inheritance from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and from ʿAlī عليه السلام." He said: I said, "We speak of it being cast into your hearts and tapped into your ears." He said, "Or that."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from the one who narrated it to him, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: I said to Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام): “It has been narrated to us from Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) that he said:” “Indeed, our knowledge is ghabir, and mazbūr, and a marking in the hearts, and a tapping in the ears.” So he said: “As for al-ghābir, it is what has preceded from our knowledge; as for al-mazbūr, it is what comes to us; as for the marking in the hearts, it is inspiration; and as for the tapping in the ears, it is the command of the angel.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn al-Mukhtār, who said: Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “If there were stoppers for your tongues, I would tell every person what is for him and what is against him.”

And by this chain, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Sinān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, who said: I heard Abā Baṣīr saying: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: From where did the companions of ʿAlī come to attain what came upon them, despite their knowledge of their deaths and their tribulations? He said: So he answered me, as if angered: From whom would that be except from themselves? So I said: What prevents you, may I be made your ransom? He said: That is a door that was closed, except that al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may the blessings of Allah be upon them both, opened a small part of it. Then he said: O Abā Muḥammad, those people had stoppers upon their mouths.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Zāhir, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abū Isḥāq al-Naḥwī, who said: I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and I heard him saying: “Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disciplined His Prophet upon His love,” so He said: “And indeed you are surely upon a magnificent character.” Then He delegated to him, so the Mighty and Majestic said: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.” And the Mighty and Majestic said: “Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah.” He said: Then he said: “And indeed the Prophet of Allah delegated to ʿAlī and entrusted him. So you submitted, while the people denied. By Allah, we love that you speak when we speak, and that you remain silent when we remain silent. We are in that which is between you and Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah has not placed any good for anyone in opposing our command.” A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: “I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying,” then he mentioned something similar to it.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān, from Yūnus, from Bakkār ibn Bakr, from Mūsā ibn Ashyam, who said: I was with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and a man asked him about a verse from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so he informed him about it. Then another person came in and asked him about that same verse, and he informed him contrary to what he had informed the first one. Because of that, there entered into me whatever Allah willed, until it was as though my heart were being cut open with knives. So I said to myself: I left Abū Qatādah in al-Shām, who does not err even regarding the wāw and the like of it, and I came to this one who makes all these mistakes. While I was in that state, another person entered and asked him about that same verse, and he informed him contrary to what he had informed me and what he had informed my two companions. Then my soul became calm, and I knew that this was from him as taqiyyah. He said: Then he turned toward me and said to me: O Ibn Ashyam, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, delegated authority to Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, so He said: “This is Our gift; so give or withhold without account.” And He delegated authority to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, so He said: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.” So whatever was delegated to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has indeed been delegated to us.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥajjāl, from Thaʿlabah, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon them, saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, delegated to His Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, the affair of His creation so that He may observe how their obedience would be. Then he recited this verse: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.”

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to one of the companions of Qays al-Masir: Indeed, God the Mighty and Majestic educated His Prophet, and excellent was His education of him. When He completed the education for him, He said: 'And indeed you are upon a magnificent character' [68:4]. Then He delegated to him the matter of the religion and the community so that he might govern His servants. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it' [59:7]. And indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was guided aright, made successful, and supported by the Holy Spirit. He neither slipped nor erred in anything of what he managed in governing the creation. Thus he conducted himself according to the manners of God. Then indeed God the Mighty and Majestic made obligatory the salat as two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs, being ten rak'ahs (per day). So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) added two rak'ahs to each two, and one rak'ah to al-Maghrib. So these became equal to the obligatory, and it is not permissible to omit them except during a journey; and he left the single rak'ah of al-Maghrib standing (unchanged) in both journey and residency. So God the Mighty and Majestic authorized all of that for him, and the obligatory prayers became seventeen rak'ahs. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) instituted the supererogatory prayers as thirty-four rak'ahs, double the obligatory. So God the Mighty and Majestic authorized that for him. And the obligatory and the supererogatory are fifty-one rak'ahs, among them two rak'ahs after the falling of darkness performed seated, counted as one rak'ah in the place of al-Witr. And God made obligatory in the year the fast of the month of Ramadan; and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) instituted fasting in Sha'ban and three days every month — equal to twice the obligatory. So God the Mighty and Majestic authorized that for him. And God the Mighty and Majestic prohibited wine specifically; and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited every intoxicant from all drinks. So God authorized all of that for him. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) found certain things repugnant and disliked them, but did not forbid them with the forbi

The two of them were saying: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, delegated to His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) the affair of His creation, so that He may observe how their obedience would be. Then he recited this verse: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.” Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun, from Zurarah — similarly to it.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Surely Allah, Blessed and Exalted, disciplined His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله). Then when He brought him to what He intended, He said to him: Indeed, you are surely upon a magnificent character. So He entrusted to him His religion, and He said: Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain. And surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordained the obligatory shares and did not assign anything to the grandfather, while the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) allotted to him one-sixth. So Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, approved that for him; and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) prescribed the blood-money for the eye and the blood-money for the life, and he prohibited nabīdh and every intoxicant. So a man said to him: "Did the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) prescribe that without anything having come regarding it?" He said: "Yes, so that He may know who obeys the Messenger from those who disobey him."

I found in the Nawādir of Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: No, by Allah! Allah did not delegate to anyone among His creation except to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and to the Imams. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: “Indeed We sent down to you the Book with the truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you.” And it continues to apply among the successors عليهم السلام.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Maythamī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: I heard him saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disciplined His Messenger until He made him upright upon what He willed, then He delegated to him. So He, Mighty is His remembrance, said: “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.” So whatever Allah delegated to His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), He has indeed delegated it to us.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from one of our companions, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ṣandal al-Khayyāṭ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning His, the Exalted's, saying: “This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without reckoning.” He عليه السلام said: “He gave Sulaymān a magnificent kingdom. Then this verse came to apply regarding the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so he had the authority to give whatever he wished to whomever he wished, and to withhold from whomever he wished. And Allah gave him better than what He gave Sulaymān, due to His saying:” “Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.”

Abu ʿAli al-Ashʿari, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Humran ibn Aʿyan, who said: I said to Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “What is the place of the scholars?” He said: “Like Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the companion of Sulayman, and the companion of Musa عليه السلام.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “Inquiry is only to us regarding the halal (permissible) and the haram (forbidden); but as for prophethood, then no.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Halabi, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, sealed the prophets with your Prophet, so there will never be any prophet after him; and He sealed the books with your Book, so there will never be any book after it. And He sent down in it the clarification of everything: your creation and the creation of the heavens and the earth, the account of those before you, the judgment of what is among you, the news of what will come after you, the matter of Paradise and the Fire, and what you are ultimately going to.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, ʿAlī (عليه السلام) was a muḥaddath. So I said: Are you then saying, a Prophet? He said: He motioned with his hand like this, then said: Or like the companion of Sulaymān, or like the companion of Mūsā, or like Dhū al-Qarnayn. Has it not reached you that he said: And among you is one like him?

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon them, who said: I said to him: “What is your rank, and whom do you resemble among those who passed before?” He said: “The companion of Mūsā and Dhū al-Qarnayn; both were knowledgeable, and they were not Prophets.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Abī Ṭālib, from Sadīr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام): “There is a people who claim that you are gods, and they recite to us Qur’an for that:” “And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God in the earth.” So he said: “O Sadīr, my hearing, my sight, my skin, my flesh, my blood, and my hair are disavowed from these people, and Allah is disassociated from them. These are not upon my religion nor upon the religion of my forefathers. By Allah, Allah will not gather me and them together on the Day of Resurrection except while He is wrathful against them.” He said: I said: “And among us there are people who claim that you are messengers, and they recite to us Qur’an for that:” “O messengers, eat from the good things and act righteously; indeed I am Knowing of what you do.” So he said: “O Sadīr, my hearing, my sight, my hair, my skin, my flesh, and my blood are disavowed from these people, and Allah and His Messenger are disassociated from them. These are not upon my religion nor upon the religion of my forefathers. By Allah, Allah will not gather me and them together on the Day of Resurrection except while He is wrathful against them.” He said: I said: “Then what are you?” He said: “We are the treasurers of the knowledge of Allah. We are the interpreters of the command of Allah. We are a people who are maʿṣūmūn. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has commanded obedience to us and forbidden disobedience to us. We are the conclusive proof over those beneath the heaven and above the earth.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Baḥr, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: The Imams are at the rank of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, except that they are not Prophets, and it is not permissible for them regarding women what was permissible for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. As for whatever is apart from that, then in it they are at the rank of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام sent to Zurarah that he should inform al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaybah that the successors of Muhammad, upon him and upon them be peace, are muhaddathun.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, who said: I entered upon 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام one day, and he said: “O Hakam, do you know the verse by which 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام used to know his killer, and by which he used to know the tremendous matters that he would relate to the people?” Al-Hakam said: So I said to myself, “I have come upon a knowledge from the knowledge of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn; by that I will know those tremendous matters.” He said: So I said, “No, by Allah, I do not know.” Then I said, “The verse—inform me of it, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.” He said: “It is, by Allah, the saying of Allah, Mighty is His remembrance:” “And We did not send before you any Messenger, nor Prophet, nor Muhaddath.” And 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام was a Muhaddath. Then a man called 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd—who was a maternal brother of 'Ali—said to him: “Glory be to Allah! A Muhaddath?” as though he was rejecting that. Then Abu Ja'far عليه السلام turned toward us and said: “Indeed, by Allah, the son of your mother had already known that.” He said: So when he said that, the man fell silent. Then he said: “It is that concerning which Abu al-Khattab was destroyed, for he did not understand the interpretation of the Muhaddath and the Prophet.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said: I heard Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام saying: “The Imams are scholars, truthful, granted understanding, and spoken to.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from a man, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: The Muḥaddath was mentioned in the presence of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, so he said: “He hears the voice, but does not see the person.” So I said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, how does he know that it is the speech of the angel?” He said: “He is given tranquility and dignity until he knows that it is the speech of an angel.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said: Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, 'Ali (عليه السلام) was a Muhaddath. So I went out to my companions and said, 'I have come to you with something astonishing.' They said, 'And what is it?' I said, 'I heard Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) saying: 'Ali (عليه السلام) was a Muhaddath.' They said, 'You have done nothing unless you ask him who it was that used to speak to him.' So I returned to him and said, 'I conveyed to my companions what you had conveyed to me, and they said: You have done nothing unless you ask him who it was that used to speak to him.' So he said to me, 'An angel used to speak to him.' I said, 'Are you saying that he was a Prophet?' He said, then he moved his hand like this: 'Or like the companion of Sulayman, or like the companion of Musa, or like Dhu al-Qarnayn.' Or has it not reached you that he said: 'And among you is one like him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibrahim ibn 'Umar al-Yamani, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) said: “O Jabir, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the creation in three categories, and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:” “And you shall be three kinds. Then the companions of the right hand—what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand—what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost—those are the ones brought near.” So the foremost are the Messengers of Allah (عليهم السلام) and the specially chosen ones of Allah from His creation. He placed within them five spirits: He supported them with the Holy Spirit, by which they knew things; He supported them with the spirit of iman, by which they feared Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He supported them with the spirit of strength, by which they were able to obey Allah; He supported them with the spirit of desire, by which they desired obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and disliked disobedience to Him; and He placed within them the spirit of movement, by which people go and come. And He placed in the believers and the companions of the right hand the spirit of iman, by which they feared Allah; and He placed in them the spirit of strength, by which they were able to obey Allah; and He placed in them the spirit of desire, by which they desired obedience to Allah; and He placed in them the spirit of movement, by which people go and come.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from al-Munakhkhal, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the knowledge of the knowledgeable one, so he said to me: “O Jābir, indeed in the Prophets and the Awṣiyāʾ there are five spirits: the Spirit of Holiness, the spirit of faith, the spirit of life, the spirit of strength, and the spirit of desire.” So by the Spirit of Holiness, O Jābir, they came to know what is beneath the Throne down to what is beneath the soil. Then he said: “O Jābir, these four are spirits that are affected by the two occurrences, except for the Spirit of Holiness, for it neither becomes diverted nor plays.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from ‘Abdullāh ibn Idrīs, from Muhammad ibn Sinān, from Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ‘Umar, from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the knowledge of the Imam concerning what is in the regions of the earth while he is in his house with his curtain let down over him. He said: O Mufaḍḍal, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, placed within the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله five spirits: the spirit of life, by which he moved and progressed; the spirit of strength, by which he rose and strove; the spirit of desire, by which he ate, drank, and approached women through what is halal; the spirit of faith, by which he believed and acted justly; and the Holy Spirit, by which he bore prophethood. Then when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is taken, the Holy Spirit passes on and comes to the Imam. The Holy Spirit neither sleeps, nor becomes heedless, nor engages in diversion, nor exults; while the four spirits sleep, become heedless, exult, and engage in diversion. And it was by the Holy Spirit that he would see.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: And thus We revealed to you a Spirit from Our Command. You did not know what the Book was, nor the faith. He عليه السلام said: It is a creature from the creatures of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, greater than Jibra'il and Mika'il. It was with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, informing him and directing him rightly, and it is with the Imams after him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Asbat ibn Salim, who said: A man from the people of Hit asked him, while I was present. About the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit from Our command.” So he said: “Since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down that Spirit upon Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, it has not ascended to the heaven, and it is surely within us.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: They ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is from the command of my Lord. He (عليه السلام) said: It is a creation greater than Jibra'il and Mika'il. It was with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and it is with the Imams, and it is from the Malakut.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام saying: They ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is from the command of my Lord. He عليه السلام said: It is a creation greater than Jibra'il and Mika'il. It was not with anyone who passed before except Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, and it is with the Imams, guiding them rightly. And not everything that is sought is found.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja‘far, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about knowledge: “Is it a knowledge that the knowledgeable one learns from the mouths of men, or is it in the Book with you, which you read and thereby come to know from it?” He said: “The matter is greater than that and more binding. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:” “And thus We revealed to you a Spirit from Our command; you did not know what the Book was, nor the faith.” Then he said: “What do your companions say regarding this verse? Do they affirm that he was in a state in which he did not know what the Book was, nor the faith?” So I said: “I do not know, may I be your ransom, what they say.” He said to me: “Yes, he indeed was in a state in which he did not know what the Book was, nor the faith, until Allah, the Exalted, sent the Spirit that is mentioned in the Book. Then when He revealed it to him, He taught by it the knowledge and the understanding. And it is the Spirit that Allah, the Exalted, gives to whomever He wills; so when He gives it to a servant, He teaches him understanding.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Asbat from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Sa'd al-Iskaf who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) asking him about the Spirit, 'Is it not Jibra'il?'. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Jibra'il (peace be upon him) is from the Angels, and the Spirit is other than Jibra'il'. He reiterated that upon the man, so he said to him: 'You have spoken a great thing from the speech. There is no one claiming that the Spirit is other than Jibra'il'. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You have strayed and are reporting from the strayed people'. Allah the Exalted is Saying to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Allah's Command will come, therefore do not hasten it; Glory be to Him, and Exalted is He above what they are describing. He Sends down the Angels with the Spirit, and the Spirit is other than the Angels'. May the Salawat of Allah be upon them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from one of our companions, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, "When does the later one come to know what is with the former?" He عليه السلام said, "In the last moment that remains of his soul."

Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah and a group with him, who said: We heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: The one who is after the Imam recognizes the knowledge of the one who was before him during the last moment remaining of his soul.

Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ali Bin Asbat, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him عليه السلام, “When does the Imam recognize his Imamate and when does the command come to its end with him?” He عليه السلام said, “In the last moment of the life of the first.”

Allah, the Exalted, said: “Those who believe, and whose offspring follow them in faith—We shall unite their offspring with them, and We shall not diminish anything from their deeds.” He said: “Those who believe” are the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and his offspring are the Imams and the awsiya', may the salawat of Allah be upon them. “We shall unite them with them,” and We did not diminish from their offspring the hujjah which Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله brought concerning 'Ali عليه السلام; their hujjah is one, and obedience to them is one.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Dāwūd al-Nahdī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: He said to me: “We are equal in knowledge and bravery, and in grants, according to the measure of what we are commanded.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Miskān, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: We, in the matter, and understanding, and the halal, and the haram, proceed in one single course. But as for the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and ʿAlī (عليه السلام), they have their own excellence.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, who said: I asked Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Surely Allah commands you to render trusts to their أهل, and when you judge between الناس, that you judge with justice. He said: 'It means us, that the first should hand over to the Imam after him the books, the knowledge, and the weapons; and when you judge between the people, that you judge with the justice that is in your hands.' Then He said to the people: 'O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you.' It means us specifically; He commanded all the believers, up to the Day of qiyamah, to obey us. Then if you fear a dispute regarding a matter, refer it to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to those vested with authority among you—thus it was revealed. And how could Allah, Mighty and Majestic, command them to obey the possessors of authority and yet permit disputing with them? Rather, that was said to those who were commanded, those to whom it was said: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you.'

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Surely Allah commands you to render the trusts to their rightful owners. He عليه السلام said: They are the Imams from the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, such that the Imam is to deliver the trust to the one after him, not single out anyone else with it, and not withhold it from him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Surely Allah commands you to render the trusts to their people. He عليه السلام said: They are the Imams. The Imam hands it over to the Imam after him, and he does not single out anyone other than him with it, nor does he withhold it from him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I asked Aba Abdillah (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Surely Allah commands you to render the trusts to their rightful owners. He (عليه السلام) said: Allah commanded the first Imam to hand over to the Imam after him everything that was with him.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Imam does not die until he knows who will be after him, so he bequeaths to him.

Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Abī ʿUthmān, from al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the Imam knows the Imam who will come after him, so he bequeaths to him.

Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: No scholar dies until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informs him to whom he should make his bequest.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn al-Tayyar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If there do not remain in the earth except for two, one of the two would be the Divine Authority (Hujja).'

Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, both together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If two remained, one of the two would be the Divine Authority upon his companion. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa — similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Karram, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If the people were only two men, one of the two would be the Imam.' And he said: 'The last one to die would be the Imam, lest anyone argue against God, Mighty and Majestic, that He left him without a divine authority of God upon him.'

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If there did not remain in the earth except two, one of the two would be the Divine Authority (Hujja)' — or (he said): 'the second would be the Divine Authority'. The doubt (in wording) is from Ahmad ibn Muhammad.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Nahdi, from his father, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'If there were not in the earth except two, the Imam would be one of the two.'

'Umar ibn Abān narrated to me, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I was in the presence of Abū 'Abdillāh (عليه السلام), and they mentioned the successors, and I mentioned Ismā'īl. So he said: 'No, by Allah, O Abū Muḥammad, that is not up to us, and it is only up to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He appoints one after another.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “Do you think that the bequeathing one from among us appoints whomever he wishes? No, by Allah. Rather, it is a covenant from Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله to one man after another, until the matter ends with its rightful possessor.” Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Minhal, from 'Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, similarly to it.

The Imamate is a covenant from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, covenanted to specifically named men. It is not for the Imam to withhold it from the one who comes after him. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'Take a successor from your family, for it has preceded in My knowledge that I will not send a prophet except that he shall have a successor from his family.' Dawud (peace be upon him) had several children, and among them was a boy whose mother was with Dawud, and he loved her. So Dawud (peace be upon him) went to her when the revelation came to him and said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed to me, commanding me to take a successor from my family.' His wife said to him: 'Let it be my son.' He said: 'That is what I intend.' And what had preceded in the inevitable knowledge of Allah was that it would be Sulayman. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Dawud: 'Do not be hasty before My command comes to you.' It was not long before two men who were disputing about sheep and a vineyard came to Dawud (peace be upon him). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud: 'Gather your sons; whoever judges this case correctly shall be your successor after you.' So Dawud (peace be upon him) gathered his children. When the two disputants presented their case, Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: 'O owner of the vineyard, when did this man's sheep enter your vineyard?' He said: 'They entered it at night.' He said: 'I rule against you, O owner of the sheep, with the offspring of your sheep and their wool for this year of yours.' Then Dawud said to him: 'Why did you not rule by taking the sheep themselves, when the scholars of the Children of Israel assessed it so, and the price of the vineyard was equal to the value of the sheep?' Sulayman said: 'The vineyard was not uprooted from its root — only its fruit was eaten, and it will return next year.' Then God Almighty revealed to Dawud: 'Verily the ruling in this case is what Sulayman ruled. O Dawud, you intended one thing and We intended another.' So Dawud went to his wife and said: 'We intended a thing, and God Almighty intended something else, and nothing prevailed but what God Almighty willed. So we are pleased with the command of God Almighty and submit to it.' And likewise the successors (peace be upon them) — it is not for them to overstep in this matter and pass it

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Bukayr and Jamīl, from ʿAmr ibn Muṣʿab, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Do you think that the bequeather from among us bequeaths to whomever he wishes? No, by Allah! Rather, it is a covenant from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) to one man, then another man, until it ended with himself.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Abu Jamila, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed the Testament descended from the heavens upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as an Ordinance — there did not descend upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) any sealed Ordinance except the Testament. So Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! This is your testament regarding your community, which is with the People of your Household.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Which of the People of my Household, O Jibra'il?' He said: 'The noble one of Allah among them and his offspring, so that they may inherit from you the knowledge of prophethood just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) made it to be inherited, and its inheritance is for Ali (peace be upon him) and your offspring from his lineage.' He said: And there were seals upon it. He said: So Ali (peace be upon him) opened the first seal and carried out what was therein. Then al-Hasan (peace be upon him) opened the second seal and carried out what he had been commanded therein. When al-Hasan passed away and departed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) opened the third seal and found therein: 'Fight! So kill and be killed, and go out with groups of people for martyrdom — there is no martyrdom for them except with you.' He said: So he (peace be upon him) did it. When he departed, he handed it over to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) before that. He opened the fourth seal and found therein: 'Be silent and withhold, for knowledge has been veiled.' So when he passed away and departed, he handed it over to Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). He opened the fifth seal and found therein: 'Interpret the Book of Allah the Exalted, and affirm your father, and make your son inherit, and cultivate the community, and uphold the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and speak the truth in fear and security, and do not fear except Allah.' So he did it. Then he handed it over to the one who follows him. He (Mu'adh) said: I said to him: 'May I be your sacrifice — are you him?' He said: 'My only concern, O Mu'adh, is that you will go and report against me.' He said: So I said: 'I ask Allah, Who granted you this rank from your forefathers, that He

Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Kinani, from Ja'far ibn Najih al-Kindi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ubaydullah al-Umari, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, God Mighty and Majestic sent down to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) a book before his passing. So he said: 'O Muhammad! This is your testament to the nobles from your family.' He said: 'And who are the nobles, O Jibril?' So he said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his sons (peace be upon them).' And upon the book there were seals of gold. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) handed it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and commanded him to break one seal from it and act according to what was in it. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) broke a seal and acted according to what was in it. Then he handed it to his son al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and acted according to what was in it. Then he handed it to al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Go forth with a group of people toward martyrdom — there is no martyrdom for them except with you — and offer yourself for God Mighty and Majestic.' And he did so. Then he handed it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Lower your head, be silent, stay in your home, and worship your Lord until certainty (death) comes to you.' And he did so. Then he handed it to his son Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Narrate to the people and issue verdicts for them, and do not fear anyone but God Mighty and Majestic, for there is no way for anyone against you.' And he did so. Then he handed it to his son Ja'far, and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Narrate to the people and issue verdicts for them, and spread the sciences of the People of your Household, and affirm your righteous forefathers, and do not fear anyone but God Mighty and Majestic — and you are in protection and security.' And he did so. Then he handed it to his son Musa (peace be upon him), and likewise Musa will hand it to the one after him, and thus until the rise of al-Mahdi — may God's blessings be upon him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Zurays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said: Humran said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, what is your view regarding what occurred in the matter of 'Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (عليهم السلام), and their rising and their standing for the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and what befell them from the tyrants killing them and prevailing over them, until they were killed and overcome?” So Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) said: “O Humran, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had indeed measured that for them, decreed it, carried it through, made it binding, then brought it to pass. So it was through prior knowledge of that, conveyed to them from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, that 'Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn stood forth; and it is with knowledge that whoever among us remained silent remained silent.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Harith ibn Ja'far, from Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Yaqtin, from Isa ibn al-Mustafad Abu Musa al-Darir, who said: Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to me, saying: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Was not Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) the scribe of the bequest, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) the one who dictated it, while Jibra'il and the proximate angels (peace be upon them) were the witnesses?' He said: So he (the Imam) remained silent for a long time, then said: 'O Abu al-Hasan! What you said did occur, but when the command came down upon the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), the bequest descended from the presence of God as a sealed document. Jibra'il descended with it along with the trustworthy ones of God — Blessed and Exalted — from among the angels. So Jibra'il said: O Muhammad! Command those in your presence to depart, except your successor, so that he may take it from us, and you may make us witness to your handing it over to him as his guarantor — meaning Ali (peace be upon him). So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) commanded those in the house to depart, except Ali (peace be upon him), while Fatimah was between the curtain and the door. Then Jibra'il said: O Muhammad! Your Lord conveys His greetings to you and says: 'This is the document of what I covenanted with you, and stipulated upon you, and witnessed upon you, and made My angels witness upon you — and it suffices with Me, O Muhammad, as Witness.' He said: The joints of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) trembled, and he said: O Jibra'il! My Lord — He is al-Salam, and from Him is peace, and to Him peace returns. The Mighty and Majestic has spoken truth and fulfilled His promise. Bring the document! So he gave it to him and commanded him to hand it over to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), and he said to him: Read it! So he read it letter by letter. Then he said: O Ali! This is the covenant of my Lord — Blessed and Exalted — to me, His stipulation upon me, and His trust. I have delivered, counselled, and fulfilled it. Ali (peace be upon him) said: And I bear witness for you — may my father and mother be your ransom — you have conveyed, counselled, and been truthful in all you said. And my hearing, my si

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm has narrated from his father, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣamm, from Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Bazzāz, from Ḥarīz, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), “May I be made your ransom, how short is your remaining, O Ahl al-Bayt, and how near your terms are to one another, despite the people’s need for you.” He said, “Indeed, for each one of us there is a scroll in which is what he needs to act upon during his appointed term. When what is in it from that which he was commanded has been completed, he knows that his appointed time has arrived. Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) comes to him, announcing his death to him, and informs him of what awaits him with Allah.” And al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) read his scroll that had been given to him, and what was to come of the announcement of his death was explained to him. Yet there remained in it matters not yet completed, so he went out for fighting. Among those matters that remained was that the angels had asked Allah concerning supporting him, and He gave them permission. They remained preparing themselves for fighting and making ready for that until he was killed. Then they descended, but his term had ended and he had been killed (عليه السلام). So the angels said, ‘Our Lord, You gave us permission to descend and You gave us permission to support him, and we descended, but You had already taken him.’ Then Allah revealed to them, ‘Remain by his grave until you see him when he has come out; then support him. And weep for him and for what you missed of supporting him. Indeed, you have been singled out for supporting him and for weeping over him.’ So the angels wept in consolation and grief over what they had missed of supporting him. Then, when he comes out, they will be his supporters.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: "When the Imam dies, by what is the one after him recognized?" He said: "The Imam has signs. Among them is that he is the eldest child of his father, and that merit and the bequest are in him, and that the riders come and say, 'To whom did so-and-so bequeath?' Then it is said, 'To so-and-so.' And the weapon among us is like the Ark among the Children of Israel; the Imamate is with the weapon wherever it may be."

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid Sha'ir, from Harun ibn Hamzah, from 'Abd al-A'la, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام): 'The one who leaps upon this matter, claiming it for himself—what is the proof against him?' He said: 'He is to be questioned about the halal (permissible) and the haram (forbidden).' He said: Then he turned toward me and said: 'Three proofs do not come together in anyone except that he is the صاحب of this matter: that he be the most entitled of the people in relation to the one before him, that the weapon be with him, and that he be the possessor of the manifest testament—such that, when you arrive in al-Madinah, you ask the common people and the children about it: To whom did so-and-so leave his bequest? They will say: To so-and-so son of so-and-so.'

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim and Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: It was said to him, “By what thing is the Imam recognised?” He said: “By the manifest bequest and by excellence. Indeed, no one is able to cast aspersion against the Imam regarding mouth, nor belly, nor private part, such that it would be said: ‘A liar,’ or ‘He consumes the wealth of the people,’ and whatever resembles this.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, “What is the sign of the Imam who is to come after the Imam?” So he عليه السلام said: “Purity of birth, good upbringing, and he does not engage in vain amusement nor play.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about the indication to the صاحب of this matter, so he said: The indication to him is seniority, merit, and the bequest. When the riders come to al-Madīnah and say, ‘To whom did so-and-so bequeath?’ it is said, ‘To so-and-so son of so-and-so’; and go around with the weapon wherever it goes. As for the questions, there is no proof in them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the command is in the eldest, so long as there is no disability in him.

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام), ‘May I be sacrificed for you, by what is the Imam recognized?’ He said: ‘By qualities. As for the first of them, it is that there has preceded from his father concerning him an indication toward him, so that it may be a proof against them. He is asked and he answers; and if one remains silent from asking him, he initiates; and he informs of what will be tomorrow; and he speaks to the people in every tongue.’ Then he said to me, ‘O Abu Muhammad, I shall give you a sign before you rise.’ It was not long before a man from the people of Khurasan entered upon us. The Khurasani spoke to him in Arabic, and Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام) answered him in Persian.
