So the Khurasani said to him, ‘By Allah, may I be sacrificed for you, nothing prevented me from speaking to you in Khurasani except that I thought you did not know it well.’ He said, ‘Glory be to Allah! If I were not able to answer you, then what excellence would I have over you?’ Then he said to me, ‘O Abu Muhammad, the Imam is not unaware of the speech of any among the people, nor of a bird, nor of a beast, nor of anything in which there is a spirit. So whoever does not possess these qualities is not an Imam.’

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: The Imamate does not return to be among two brothers after Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, ever. Rather, it proceeded from Ali ibn Al-Husayn, just as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.” So after Ali ibn Al-Husayn (عليه السلام), it is not to be except in the descendants and the descendants of the descendants.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he heard him saying: Allah refused to make it for two brothers after al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام. He was asked, "Can the Imamate be in a paternal uncle or a maternal uncle?" So he عليه السلام said, "No." I said, "Then in a brother?" He عليه السلام said, "No." I said, "Then in whom?" He عليه السلام said, "In my son." And at that time, he عليه السلام had no son.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said: The Imamate does not come together in two brothers after al-Hasan and al-Husayn. Rather, it is among the descendants and the descendants of the descendants.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him, "If some event occurs, and Allah does not show me that, then whom should I follow as Imam?" So he gestured toward his son Mūsā. He said: I said, "Then if an event happens to Mūsā, whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son." I said, "Then if an event happens to his son, and he leaves behind an elder brother and a young son, then whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son, then one after another." And in the copy of al-Ṣafwānī: "Then it is like this forever."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus; and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad Abu Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you. He said: It was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (عليهم السلام). I said to him: The people say, why is it that He did not name Ali and the People of his Household (عليهم السلام) in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: Say to them: the salat (prayer) was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), yet Allah did not specify for them three or four, until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the one who explained that to them. And zakat (alms-tax) was revealed to him, yet He did not specify for them that from every forty dirhams there is one dirham, until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the one who explained that to them. And hajj (pilgrimage) was revealed, yet He did not say to them: perform tawaf seven times, until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the one who explained that to them. And this was revealed: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you. And it was revealed concerning Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn. So the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said concerning Ali: Whoever I am his mawla, then Ali is his mawla. And he (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: I enjoin you concerning the Book of Allah and my Ahl al-Bayt, for I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not to separate between the two until they bring me to the Pond, and He granted me that. And he said: Do not teach them, for they are more knowledgeable than you. And he said: They will never bring you out from a gate of guidance, nor will they ever make you enter a gate of misguidance. Indeed Allah only desires to remove defilement from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification. Had the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) remained silent and not clarified who the People of his Household were, the family of so-and-so and the family of so-and-so would have claimed it. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed it in His Book as a confirmation of His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله). So they were Ali, al-Hasan, al-Hu

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Miskān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Rūḥ al-Qaṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. Concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers; and those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of Allah. I said, 'Regarding whom was it revealed?' So he said: 'It was revealed concerning authority. Indeed, this verse continued among the sons of al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام after him. Thus we are more entitled to the authority and to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله than the believers, the Muhājirūn, and the Anṣār.' I said, 'Then do the sons of Jaʿfar have a share in it?' He said: 'No.' I said, 'Then do the sons of al-ʿAbbās have a share in it?' He said: 'No.' Then I enumerated to him the clans of Banī ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and for all of that he kept saying: 'No.' He said: 'And I forgot the sons of al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, so I came to him after that and said to him, "Do the sons of al-Ḥasan عليه السلام have a share in it?" He said: "No, by Allah, O ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, no Muḥammadī has any share in it other than us."'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hāshimī, from his father, from Ahmad ibn ‘Īsā, from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Your wali is only Allah and His Rasool and those who believe.” He عليه السلام said: “It only means the one with greater authority over you, that is, the one more entitled regarding you, your affairs, your selves, and your wealth: Allah and His Rasool and those who believe,” meaning ‘Alī and his children, the Imams عليهم السلام, until the Day of Resurrection. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described them and said: “Those who establish the salat and give the zakat while they are bowing.” And Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام was in the Zuhr salat, and he had prayed two rak‘ahs and was in ruku‘, and upon him was a garment worth a thousand dinars. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had clothed him with it, and al-Najāshī had gifted it to him. Then a beggar came and said, “Peace be upon you, O wali of Allah, and the one with greater authority over the believers than their own selves. Give charity to a poor person.” So he cast the garment to him and gestured with his hand to him that he should take it. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down this verse concerning him, and made the bounty of his children by his bounty. Thus, everyone among his children who reaches the station of Imamate is of this same quality like him, and they give charity while they are bowing. And the beggar who asked Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام was from the angels, and those who ask the Imams from among his children are from the angels.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, Bukayr ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Burayd ibn Muawiya, and Abu al-Jaroud — all together — from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Messenger with the wilayah of Ali, and revealed to him: [5:55] Verily, only God is your guardian and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish salat and give zakat. And He made obligatory the wilayah of the Ulu al-Amr. But they did not know what it was, so God commanded Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to explain the wilayah to them just as he had explained to them the salat, the zakat, the fasting, and the hajj. So when that command came to him from God, the chest of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was constricted by it, and he feared that they would apostatize from their religion and that they would belie him. So his chest was constricted, and he referred to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: [5:67] O Messenger! Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, and God will protect you from the people. So he openly proclaimed the command of God, Exalted is His mention, and established the wilayah of Ali (peace be upon him) on the Day of Ghadir Khumm. He called for congregational prayer and commanded the people that those present should convey it to the absent. Umar ibn Udhayna said: 'All [the above narrators] said this together except for Abu al-Jaroud.' And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was that the obligatory duty was revealed after another obligatory duty, and the wilayah was the last of the obligations. So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: [5:3] This day have I perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, is saying: "I will not reveal upon you after this any obligation — I have already perfected the obligations for you."'

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: I was sitting in his presence when a man said to him: “Tell me about the wilayah of ʿAlī—was it from Allah or from His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?” He became angry, then said: “Woe to you! The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم feared Allah too greatly to say what Allah had not commanded him with. Rather, He made it obligatory, just as Allah made obligatory the salat (prayer), zakat (alms-tax), sawm (fasting), and hajj (pilgrimage).”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn together, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, obligated five things upon the servants. They took four and left one. I said: Can you name them for me? May I be sacrificed for you. He said: Salat, and the people did not know how they should pray, so Jibra'il عليه السلام descended and said: O Muhammad, inform them of the times of their salat. Then zakat was revealed, and he said: O Muhammad, inform them regarding their zakat as you informed them regarding their salat. Then sawm was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used, when it was the day of 'Ashura', to send to the surrounding villages, and they would fast that day. Then the month of Ramadan was revealed between Sha'ban and Shawwal. Then hajj was revealed, so Jibra'il عليه السلام descended and said: Inform them regarding their hajj as you informed them regarding their salat, zakat, and sawm. Then wilayah was revealed, and that came to him on the day of الجمعة at 'Arafah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you. The completion of the religion was through the wilayah of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام. At that, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: My community is newly removed from جاهلية, and whenever I inform them of this concerning my cousin, one speaker will say this and another speaker will say that. So I said within myself, without my tongue speaking it, then a decisive command came to me from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, absolutely, threatening me that if I did not convey it, He would punish me. Then it was revealed: O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed Allah does not guide the disbelieving people. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله took the hand of 'Ali عليه السلام and said: O people, there was not a Prophet among the Prophets before me except that Allah gave him life, then called him, and he answered Him. So soon I shall be called and I shall answer. I am to be questioned, and you are to be questioned, so what will you say? They sa

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṣabbāḥ al-Azraq, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), “A man from the Mukhtāriyya met me and claimed that Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya is an Imam.” So Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) became angry, then said, “Why did you not say something to him?” He said: I replied, “No, by Allah, I did not know what to say.” He said, “Why did you not say to him: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) gave the bequest to ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn. Then when ʿAlī (عليه السلام) passed away, he bequeathed to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn. If he had tried to turn it away from them both, they would have said to him, ‘We are two legatees just like you,’ and he would not have done that.” And al-Ḥasan bequeathed to al-Ḥusayn, and if he had tried to turn it away from him, he would have said, ‘I am a legatee like you, from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) and from my father,’ and he would not have done that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And those related by blood are nearer to one another.” It is about us and about our sons.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was revealed, it was among the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): "Greet Ali as Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Believers)." And it was among what God had affirmed upon them both on that day — O Zayd — the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to them both: "Arise and greet him as Amir al-Mu'minin." They said: "Is it from God or from His Messenger, O Messenger of God?" And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: "From God and from His Messenger." Then God Mighty and Majestic revealed [16:91]: "And do not break the oaths after confirming them, while you have made God a surety over you; surely God knows what you do" — meaning by this the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to them both and their words: "Is it from God or from His Messenger?" [16:92]: "And do not be like the one who unravels her yarn after spinning it strongly; you make your oaths a means of deceit between you so that the Imams would be more virtuous than your leaders." He (the narrator) said: I said: "May I be your ransom — Imams?" He said: "Yes, by God, Imams." I said: "But we recite 'arbaa' (أَرْبَى)." He said: "What is 'arbaa'?" And he gestured with his hand and discarded it. [16:92 cont.]: "Indeed, God tests you by it" — meaning by Ali (peace be upon him) — "and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that in which you differed. [16:93] And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation; but He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills; and you will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what you used to do." [16:94]: "And do not make your oaths a means of deceit between you, lest a foot slip after its firmness" — meaning after the words of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali (peace be upon him) — "and you would taste evil for having turned away from the way of God" — meaning by it Ali (peace be upon him) — "and for you will be a great punishment."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: When Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had completed his prophethood and fulfilled his days, Allāh, the Exalted, revealed to him: "O Muḥammad, you have completed your prophethood and fulfilled your days; so place the knowledge that is with you, and the faith, and the Greatest Name, and the inheritance of knowledge, and the traces of the knowledge of prophethood among your Ahl al-Bayt with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. For I shall never cut off the knowledge, the faith, the Greatest Name, the inheritance of knowledge, and the traces of the knowledge of prophethood from the descendants among your offspring, just as I did not cut them off from the offspring of the Prophets."

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and another, from Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn altogether, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir and Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said: Musa (عليه السلام) bequeathed to Yusha' ibn Nun, and Yusha' ibn Nun bequeathed to a descendant of Harun, and he did not bequeath to his own son nor to a descendant of Musa. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has the choice; He chooses whom He wills from among whom He wills. And Musa and Yusha' gave glad tidings of the Messiah (عليه السلام). So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent the Messiah (عليه السلام), the Messiah said to them: There shall soon come after me a Prophet whose name is Ahmad, from the descendants of Isma'il (عليه السلام), who will come confirming me and confirming you, and my proof and your proof. And after him it continued among the disciples, among the entrusted preservers. Allah, the Exalted, only named them the preservers because they were entrusted with preserving the Greatest Name, and it is the Book by which the knowledge of everything is known, which was with the Prophets (صلوات الله عليهم). Allah, the Exalted, says: “And We certainly sent messengers before you and sent down with them the Book and the Balance.” The Book is the Greatest Name, and it is only recognized through what is called the Book: the Tawrah, the Injil, and the Furqan. Within it is the Book of Nuh, and within it is the Book of Salih, Shu'ayb, and Ibrahim (عليه السلام). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed: “Indeed, this is surely in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa.” So where are the scriptures of Ibrahim? The scriptures of Ibrahim are only the Greatest Name, and the scriptures of Musa are the Greatest Name. The bequest continued in one scholar after another until they handed it over to Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله). So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), the descendants of the preservers submitted to him, while Banu Isra'il denied him. And he called to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and strove in His way. Then Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, revealed to him: Proclaim the merit of your wasi. So he said: My Lord, the Arabs are a harsh people; there has not been among them a book, nor has a prophet been sent to them, and they do no

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Yahya ibn Mu'ammar al-Attar, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said during his illness in which he passed away: “Call my close friend for me.” So the two of them sent to their fathers. When Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله looked at them, he turned away from them. Then he said: “Call my close friend for me.” So a message was sent to Ali عليه السلام. When he looked at him, he bent closely over him, speaking to him. When he came out, they met him and said to him, “What did your close friend tell you?” He said, “He narrated to me a thousand doors, each door opening a thousand doors.”

Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله taught ʿAlī, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, a thousand letters; each letter opens a thousand letters.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There was in the pendant strap of the sword of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله a small parchment. So I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, "What was in that parchment?" He said, "They are the letters, each letter opening a thousand letters." Abū Baṣīr said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said, "Then not even two letters from it will have come forth until the Hour."

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Fuḍayl ibn Sukkarah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “May I be sacrificed for you, is there a fixed limit for the water with which the deceased is washed?” He said: “Indeed, Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: ‘When I die, draw six waterskins of water from the well of Ghars, then wash me, shroud me, and embalm me.’” ‘Then when you have finished washing me and shrouding me, take hold of the whole of my shroud and sit me up; then ask me whatever you wish, for by Allah, you will not ask me about anything except that I will answer you regarding it.’”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ibn Abi Sa'id, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: When death came to Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), Ali (عليه السلام) came in to him, and he drew his head near. Then he said: "O Ali, when I die, then wash me and shroud me, then seat me upright, ask me, and write."

I and Kāmil al-Tammār entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام). Kāmil said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, there is a hadith narrated by so-and-so.” He said, “Mention it.” He said, “It was narrated to me that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) spoke to ʿAlī (عليه السلام) of a thousand gates on the day the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) passed away; each gate opens a thousand gates, so that is a thousand thousand gates.” He said, “That indeed was so.” I said, “May I be sacrificed for you, has that become manifest to your Shiʿah and your loyal followers?” He said, “O Kāmil, one gate or two gates.” So I said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, then from a thousand thousand gates of your merit, only one gate or two gates are narrated?” He said: Then he said, “And what could you possibly narrate of our merit? What you narrate of our merit is nothing but a thousand not joined together.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani and Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Aban, from Sulaym ibn Qays, who said: I witnessed the bequest of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام when he bequeathed to his son al-Hasan عليه السلام, and he made al-Husayn عليه السلام, and Muhammad, and all of his children, and the chiefs of his Shi'ah, and the people of his household witnesses over his bequest. Then he handed over to him the Book and the weapon, and said to his son al-Hasan عليه السلام: 'O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed me to bequeath to you, and to hand over to you my books and my weapon, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله bequeathed to me and handed over to me his books and his weapon; and he instructed me to command you that, when death comes to you, you should hand them over to your brother al-Husayn عليه السلام.' Then he turned to his son al-Husayn عليه السلام and said: 'And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed you to hand them over to this son of yours'—then he took the hand of Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام. Then he said to Ali ibn al-Husayn: 'And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed you to hand them over to your son Muhammad ibn Ali, and convey to him greetings from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and from me.'

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Bashīr, from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, when that which came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (صلوات الله عليه) came to him, he said to his son al-Ḥasan: “Come near me so that I may confide to you what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) confided to me, and entrust you with that which he entrusted to me.” So he did.

Al-Ajlah, and Salamah ibn Kuhayl, and Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, and Zayd Al-Yamami narrated to me; they said: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us. That ʿAli (عليه السلام), when he went to Al-Kufah, entrusted his books and the bequest to Umm Salamah. Then when Al-Hasan (عليه السلام) returned, she handed them over to him.

In the copy of al-Ṣafwānī: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf, from Abū Bakr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام). That ʿAlī, ṣalawātullāh ʿalayhi, when he went to al-Kūfah, entrusted his books and the bequest to Umm Salamah. Then when al-Ḥasan returned, she handed them over to him.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) bequeathed to al-Ḥasan, and he made al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), Muḥammad, all of his children, the chiefs of his Shiʿah, and the people of his household witnesses to his bequest. Then he handed over to him the Book and the weapon. Then he said to his son al-Ḥasan: “O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded me to bequeath to you, and to hand over to you my books and my weapon, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم bequeathed to me and handed over to me his books and his weapon. And he commanded me to command you that, when death comes to you, you should hand it over to your brother al-Ḥusayn.” Then he turned to his son al-Ḥusayn and said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded you to hand it over to this son of yours,” then he took the hand of his grandson ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn. Then he said to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn: “O my son, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded you to hand it over to your son Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, and convey to him greetings from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and from me.” Then he turned to his son al-Ḥasan and said: “O my son, you are the holder of the authority and the guardian of the blood. So if you pardon, that is for you; and if you kill, then one strike in place of one strike, and you do not sin.”

Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hasani raised it (the chain), and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmari, who raised it (the chain), said: When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was struck, the visitors gathered around him, and it was said to him: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, make your bequest!' So he said: 'Fold the pillow for me.' Then he said: 'Praise be to Allah as is His right, following His command, and I praise Him as He loves, and there is no god but Allah, the One, the Unique, the Eternal, as He has described Himself.' O people! Every person will encounter during his flight that which he flees from, and death is the driver of the soul toward it, and fleeing from it is to meet it. How many days I spent searching through them for the hidden secret of this matter, but Allah — Mighty is His mention — refused except to keep it hidden. How far away is hidden knowledge! As for my bequest: do not associate anything with Allah — Majestic is His praise — and as for Muhammad (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family), do not waste his Sunnah. Establish these two pillars and kindle these two lamps, and you will be free of blame as long as you do not stray. Every person carries the burden of his own effort, and the Merciful Lord has lightened it from the ignorant. A Merciful Lord, a Most-Knowing Imam, and a straight Religion. Yesterday I was your companion, today I am a lesson for you, and tomorrow I shall part from you. If the footing holds firm at this slippery place, that is the goal; and if the foot slips, then we were in the shades of branches, the shelter of winds, and under the shadow of a cloud whose mass dissolved in the atmosphere and whose traces faded on the earth. I was only a neighbor; my body was your neighbor for a few days, and soon you will be left with an empty body from me — still after movement, and silent after speech. Let my stillness, the dimming of my gaze, and the quietness of my limbs be your admonishment, for that is more admonishing for you than an eloquent speaker. I bid you farewell as one expecting reunion. Tomorrow you will witness my days, and Allah — Mighty and Majestic — will unveil my secrets, and you will come to know me after my place is empty and another stands in my place. If I survive, then I am the guardian of my own blood; and if I perish, then perishing is my appointed meeting; and if I forgive, then forg

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm al-ʿAqīlī, raising it, said: When Ibn Muljam struck Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), he said to al-Ḥasan: “O my son, when I die, then kill Ibn Muljam and dig for him in the rubbish dump.” Al-ʿAqīlī described the place as being at the gate of Ṭāq al-Maḥāmil, the place of the grillers and the sellers of heads. “Then cast him into it, for it is a valley from the valleys of Hell.”

Al-Kulayni and a number of our companions, from Ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: When death approached al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he said to al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'O my brother, I am bequeathing to you a bequest, so preserve it. When I die, prepare me, then direct me toward the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) so that I may renew my covenant with him. Then turn me toward my mother (peace be upon her), then return me and bury me in al-Baqi'. And know that there will befall me from Aisha what God and the people know of her deeds and her enmity toward God and His Messenger, and her enmity toward us, the People of the Household.' When al-Hasan (peace be upon him) passed away and was placed upon the bier, they carried him to the prayer-place of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) where he used to perform the funeral prayer. Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) performed the prayer over him, and he was carried and brought into the mosque. When he was brought to the grave of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), the one with the little eyes went to Aisha and said to her: 'They have brought al-Hasan to bury him alongside the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).' She came out hastily upon a saddled mule — and she was the first woman to ride a saddle in Islam — and said: 'Move your son away from my house! He shall not be buried in my house and violate the privacy of the Messenger of God.' Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Long ago, you and your father violated the privacy of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and brought into his house those whom he did not wish to be near him. And God will question you about that, O Aisha!'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from some of our companions, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the death came upon al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he said: 'O Qanbar! Look around — do you see from behind your door a believer from other than the progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him)?' He replied: 'God the Exalted, His Messenger, and the son of His Messenger know better than I.' He said: 'Call Muhammad ibn Ali for me.' So I (Qanbar) went to him, and when I entered upon him, he said: 'Has anything happened except good?' I said: 'Respond to Abu Muhammad.' So he hastened with his sandal strap without straightening it, and went out with me running. When he stood before him, he greeted. Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Sit down, for one such as you should not be absent from hearing a speech by which the dead are revived and the living can die. Be receptacles of knowledge and lanterns of guidance, for the light of the day — part of it is more luminous than other parts. Do you not know that God made the children of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) Imams and gave distinction to some of them over others, and gave the Psalms to Dawud (peace be upon him)? And you know what He chose to distinguish Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with. O Muhammad ibn Ali! I fear envy for you, for God has described the disbelievers with it, and God Almighty said: [2:109] unbelievers, out of envy from themselves, even after the truth became clear to them. And God Almighty will not give Satan authority over you. O Muhammad ibn Ali! Shall I tell you what I heard from your father regarding you?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I heard your father (peace be upon him) saying on the day of Basra: Whoever loves to honor me in this world and the next, let him honor Muhammad, my son. O Muhammad ibn Ali! If I wished, I could have informed you while you were still a drop of seed in your father's loins! O Muhammad ibn Ali! Do you not know that al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), after my passing and the departure of my soul from my body, will be the Imam after me? And before God — Majestic is His Name — it is in the Book as an inheritance from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), which God Almighty has assigned to him in the inheritance of his fat

And by this chain, from Sahl, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from Hārūn ibn al-Jahm, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: When al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام) was at the point of death, he said to al-Ḥusayn: O my brother, I entrust you with a وصية, so preserve it. When I die, prepare me, then direct me toward the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) so that I may renew my عهد with him, then take me to my mother Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), then return me and bury me in al-Baqīʿ. And know that there shall come upon me from al-Ḥumayrāʾ what the people know of her conduct, her enmity toward Allah and His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), and her enmity toward us, the Ahl al-Bayt. When al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) passed away and was placed upon his bier, they proceeded with him to the place of salat of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), where he used to perform salat over the dead. Then salat was performed over al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام). After the salat over him had been performed, he was carried and brought into the masjid. When he was brought to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the news reached ʿĀʾishah, and it was said to her: They have come with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī to bury him with the Messenger of Allah. So she came out hastily on a saddled mule, and she was the first woman in Islam to ride a saddle. She stopped and said: Move your son away from my house, for nothing shall be buried in it, nor shall the Messenger of Allah have his sanctity violated. Then al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may the salawāt of Allah be upon them both, said to her: Long ago, you and your father violated the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah, and you brought into his house one whose nearness the Messenger of Allah did not love; and Allah will question you about that, O ʿĀʾishah. My brother instructed me to bring him near to his father, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), so that he may renew his عهد with him. And know that my brother is the most knowledgeable of people concerning Allah and His Messenger, and the most knowledgeable concerning the taʾwīl of His Book, far above violating the Messenger of Allah in his privacy, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you. Yet you brought men into the house of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام), when that which came upon him came upon him, called his eldest daughter Fatimah bint al-Husayn (عليه السلام), and handed to her a wrapped book and an outward will. And 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was suffering from an abdominal illness among them, and they saw nothing except that he was overcome by what was with him. So Fatimah handed the book to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then, by Allah, that book came to us, O Ziyad. He said: I said, "What is in that book? May Allah make me your ransom." He said: "In it, by Allah, is whatever the children of Adam need from when Allah created Adam until the world passes away. By Allah, in it are the prescribed legal punishments, even the compensation for a scratch."

A number of our companions narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Sinān, from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: When that which came to al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) came to him, he entrusted his bequest to his daughter Fāṭimah outwardly, in a folded book. Then, when from the affair of al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) there occurred what occurred, she handed that over to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام). I said to him, 'So what is in it, may Allah have mercy on you?' He said, 'What the children of Adam need from when the world came to be until it passes away.'

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, when al-Ḥusayn, ṣalawāt Allāh be upon him, went to al-ʿIrāq, he entrusted Umm Salamah, raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā, with the books and the bequest. Then when ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام returned, she handed them over to him.

In the copy of al-Ṣafwānī: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Fulayḥ ibn Abī Bakr al-Shaybānī, who said: By Allah, I was indeed sitting with ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and his children were with him, when Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī came to him. He greeted him, then took the hand of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and withdrew with him, and said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله informed me that I would meet a man from the people of his Household called Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, whose kunyah would be Abū Jaʿfar. So when you meet him, convey to him my greetings. He said: Jābir departed, and Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام returned and sat with his father ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام and his brothers. When he had performed the Maghrib salat (prayer), ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What did Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī say to you? He said: He said that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: You will meet a man from the people of my Household whose name is Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, whose kunyah is Abū Jaʿfar, so convey to him my greetings. So his father said to him: Glad tidings to you, my son, for what Allah has singled you out for through His Messenger from among your household. Do not inform your brothers of this, lest they plot against you as the brothers of Yūsuf plotted against Yūsuf عليه السلام.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said: When death came upon Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام), before that he brought out a basket or a box that was with him and said: “O Muhammad, carry this box.” He said: So it was carried by four men. Then when he passed away, his brothers came claiming what was in the box, and they said: “Give us our share in the box.” So he said: “By Allah, you have no share in it; and if you had any share in it, he would not have handed it over to me.” And in the box were the weapons of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and his books.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) turned to his children while he was in the state of death, and they were gathered around him. Then he turned to Muhammad ibn ʿAlī and said: “O Muhammad, take this box to your house.” He said: “Indeed, there was neither any dinar in it nor any dirham, but it was filled with knowledge.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to Ibn Ḥazm that he should send to him the charity endowment of ʿAlī, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān. Ibn Ḥazm then sent to Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan, and he was the eldest of them, and asked him about the charity. So Zayd said: The guardian after ʿAlī was al-Ḥasan, and after al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and after al-Ḥusayn, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and after ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī; so send to him. So Ibn Ḥazm sent to my father, and my father sent me with the letter to him, until I delivered it to Ibn Ḥazm. Then some of us said to him: Do the sons of al-Ḥasan recognize this? He said: Yes, just as they recognize that this is night, but envy drives them. If they had sought the truth by the truth, it would have been better for them, but they seek the world.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to Ibn Ḥazm. Then he mentioned something similar to it, except that he said: Ibn Ḥazm sent for Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan, and he was older than my father (عليه السلام). A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ — similarly to it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: Only he who recognizes God truly worships God. As for one who does not recognize God, he is only worshipping Him like this — in error. I said: 'May I be made a ransom for you, so what is the recognition of God?' He said: 'Ratification of God, Mighty and Majestic, and ratification of His Messenger (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), and allegiance to Ali (peace be upon him), and following him and the Imams of Guidance (peace be upon them), and disavowal before God, Mighty and Majestic, of their enemies. Thus is God, Mighty and Majestic, recognized.'

More than one (narrator) narrated to us from one of the two of them (peace be upon them both) that he said: The servant cannot be a believer until he recognizes God, His Messenger, and all the Imams, and the Imam of his time, and refers (all matters) to him and submits to him. Then he said: How can he recognize the last one while he is ignorant of the first?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Inform me — is recognition of the Imam from you obligatory upon all creation?' He said: 'Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to all people as a Messenger and as a proof of God upon all His creatures in His earth. So whoever believes in God and in Muhammad as the Messenger of God, and follows him and ratifies him, then recognition of the Imam from us is obligatory upon him. And whoever did not believe in God and His Messenger, did not follow him, did not ratify him, and did not recognise both their rights, how can the recognition of the Imam be obligatory upon him, while he does not believe in God and His Messenger and recognise both their rights?' He said: I said, 'So what do you say regarding one who believes in God and His Messenger and ratifies His Messenger in all that God revealed — is the right of your recognition obligatory upon them?' He said: 'Yes. Are they not recognising so-and-so and so-and-so?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you think that God is the One Who placed the recognition of those ones into their hearts? By God! It was none other than Satan who placed that into their hearts. No, by God! None but God — Mighty and Majestic — inspires the believers with our right.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Only the one who recognizes God, Mighty and Majestic, and worships Him truly — that is, the one who recognizes God and recognizes his Imam from us, the People of the Household. And whoever does not recognize God, Mighty and Majestic, and does not recognize the Imam from us, the People of the Household, then he is only recognizing and worshipping other than God. Thus, by God, is the straying!'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Imams after the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). So he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was an Imam, then al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was an Imam, then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was an Imam, then Ali ibn al-Husayn was an Imam, then Muhammad ibn Ali was an Imam. Whoever denies that is like one who denies the recognition of God, Blessed and Exalted, and the recognition of His Messenger (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). Then the narrator said: I said, 'Then you — may I be sacrificed for you!' So I repeated it to him three times. So he said to me: Indeed I have only narrated to you so that you may be among the witnesses of God, Blessed and Exalted, in His earth.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one he mentioned, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You will not be righteous until you know, and you will not know until you ratify, and you will not ratify until you submit to four doors — the first of which is not correct except with its last. They strayed, the companions of the three, wandering in a far wandering. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, accepts nothing except righteous deeds, and Allah accepts nothing except fulfilment of the stipulations and covenants. So whoever fulfils Allah's, Mighty and Majestic's, stipulation and acts according to what is described in His covenant, shall attain what is with Him and complete what He promised. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, informed the servants of the paths of guidance and established for them therein the beacons, and informed them how they should travel. So He said: "And I am indeed Most Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds, then follows the right guidance." [20:82] And He said: "Allah only accepts from the God-fearing." [5:27] So whoever fears Allah with regard to what He commanded him, shall meet Allah as a believer in what Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) brought. Alas! Alas! A people passed away and died before being guided, and they thought they had believed, yet they had committed shirk from an aspect they did not perceive. Verily, whoever comes to the houses through their doors is guided, and whoever takes another path has walked the road of ruin. Allah has linked obedience to the guardian of His command with obedience to His Messenger, and obedience to His Messenger with obedience to Himself. So whoever abandons obedience to the masters of authority has obeyed neither Allah nor His Messenger — and this is the acknowledgement of what was revealed from the presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. "Take your adornment at every mosque," [7:31] and seek the houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted and His name to be mentioned in them. [24:36] For He informed you that they are "men whom neither commerce nor sale diverts from the remembrance of Allah and the keeping up of prayer and the giving of zakat — they fear a day in which the hearts and eyes shall be overturned." [24:37] Indeed Allah

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Saghir, from one who narrated to him, from Rib'i ibn 'Abdallah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: God refused to cause things to proceed except through causes. Thus He appointed a cause for every thing, and appointed an explanation for every cause, and appointed a knowledge for every explanation, and appointed a speaking gate for every knowledge. He who recognized it recognized him, and he who was ignorant of it was ignorant of him. That is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and us.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Everyone who professes religion to God Mighty and Majestic through worship in which he exerts his soul, and has no Imam for him from God — his striving is unaccepted, and he is straying and confused, and God abhors his deeds. His likeness is like the likeness of a sheep that strayed from its shepherd and its herd. It wandered going and coming all day. When the night enveloped it, it saw a herd of sheep with their shepherd; it yearned toward them and was deceived by them and spent the night with them in their pen. When the shepherd drove his herd, it did not recognize its shepherd or its herd, and it wandered confusedly seeking its shepherd and its herd. Then it saw another flock with their shepherd and yearned toward them and was deceived by them. The shepherd called out to it: Go back to your shepherd and your herd — for you are wandering and confused away from your shepherd and your herd! So it fled, frightened and bewildered, with no shepherd to guide it to its pasture or return it. While it was in this state, the wolf seized upon its being lost and devoured it. And likewise, by God, O Muhammad, anyone from this community who begins the morning without an Imam from God Mighty and Majestic — manifest and just — begins the morning straying and wandering. And if he dies in this state, he dies the death of disbelief and hypocrisy. Know, O Muhammad, that the tyrannous imams and their followers are truly cut off from the religion of God. They have gone astray and led others astray. Thus the deeds which they perform are like ashes blown fiercely by the wind on a stormy day — they cannot hold on to anything from what they have earned. That is the far straying.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Muqarrin who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ibn al-Kawwa' came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, [7:46] and upon the Heights there shall be men recognising all by their marks.' So he said: 'We are upon the Heights, we recognise our helpers by their marks. We are the Recognisers through whom alone God Mighty and Majestic can be known. We are the Recognisers whom God Mighty and Majestic shall introduce on the Day of Resurrection upon the Bridge — so none shall enter Paradise except one who recognises us and whom we recognise, and none shall enter the Fire except one who denies us and whom we deny.' Indeed, God Blessed and Exalted, had He willed, would have introduced Himself to His servants — but instead He made us His doors, His Bridge, His way and the Face through which one comes to Him. So whoever turns away from our wilayah, or prefers others over us, they shall fall off the Bridge. They are not equal — those to whom people cling, nor where people go, to turbid springs draining into each other — and those who go to us, to clear springs flowing by the command of their Lord, neither depleting nor terminating.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Bakr ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Rayyān ibn Shabīb, from Yūnus, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Abū Ḥamzah, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “O Abū Ḥamzah, one of you travels farsakhs and seeks a guide for himself, while regarding the paths of the heaven you are more ignorant than you are regarding the paths of the earth; so seek a guide for yourself.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And whoever is given wisdom, then indeed he has been given abundant good.” So he عليه السلام said: “Obedience to Allah and recognition of the Imam.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said to me, “Have you recognized your Imam?” He said: I said, “Yes, by Allah, before I departed from al-Kūfah.” So he said, “That is sufficient for you, then.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Burayd, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying regarding the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: Is he who was dead, then We gave him life, and made for him a light by which he walks among the people So he عليه السلام said: "Dead" means one who does not recognize anything, and "a light by which he walks among the people" means an Imam whom he follows. Like one whose likeness is in darkness, not coming out from it He عليه السلام said: "The one who does not recognize the Imam."

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Awrama and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Jadalī entered upon Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and he عليه السلام said: O Abū ʿAbdillāh, shall I not inform you of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have better than it, and they shall be secure from terror on that Day. And whoever brings an evil deed, their faces shall be cast into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do? He said: Yes, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, may I be your ransom. He said: The good deed is recognition of the wilayah and love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt; and the evil deed is denial of the wilayah and hatred for us, the Ahl al-Bayt. Then he recited this verse to him.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Al-Ṣabbāḥ Al-Kinānī, who said: Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) looked at Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ (عليه السلام) walking, and he said: Do you see this one? This one is from those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were deemed weak in the land, and to make them Imams, and to make them the heirs.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When death came to my father عليه السلام, he said: 'O Jaʿfar, I enjoin you to treat my companions well.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, by Allah, I will leave them such that a man among them may be in a city and not need to ask anyone.'

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Muthannā, from Sadīr al-Ṣayrafī, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, from the happiness of a man is that he should have a child in whom he recognizes a resemblance of his physical form, his character, and his traits. And indeed, I surely recognize in this son of mine a resemblance of my physical form, my character, and my traits,” meaning Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام).

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ṭāhir, who said: I was in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), then Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) came forward, so Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “This one is the best of creation, or better.”

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from one of our companions, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Ṭāhir, who said: I was in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, then Jaʿfar عليه السلام came forward, so Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “This is the best of created beings.”

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān, from Ṭāhir, who said: I was seated in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, when Jaʿfar عليه السلام came forward, so Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “This is the best of creation.”

Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Jabir Bin Yazeed Al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: He was asked about al-Qa'im عليه السلام, so he struck his hand upon Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام and said: “This one, by Allah, is a Qa'im from the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله.” Anbasah said: “When Abu Ja'far عليه السلام passed away, I went to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام and informed him of that, so he said: ‘Jabir spoke the truth.’” Then he said: “Perhaps you think that not every Imam is the Qa'im after the Imam who was before him.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: My father عليه السلام entrusted me with what was there. Then when death came to him, he said: “Call witnesses for me.” So I called four men from Quraysh for him, among whom was Nafi', the mawla of Abdullah ibn Umar. Then he said: “Write: This is what Ya'qub bequeathed to his sons:” “O my sons, surely Allah has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.” And Muhammad ibn Ali bequeathed to Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and instructed him to shroud him in his cloak in which he used to perform the Friday salat (prayer), to place his turban upon him, to square his grave, to raise it by four fingers, and to loosen his worn garments from him at his burial. Then he said to the witnesses: “You may depart; may Allah have mercy on you.” Then I said to him: “O my father, after they had left, this was not something that required witnesses to be called over it.” He said: “O my son, I disliked that you should be overcome and that it should be said, ‘He did not bequeath to him.’ So I wanted there to be a proof for you.”

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbdullāh al-Qallāʾ, from al-Fayḍ ibn al-Mukhtār, who said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), 'Take my hand out of the Fire; who is for us after you?' Then Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) entered before him, and at that time he was a boy. So he said: 'This is your master, so hold fast to him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Thubayt, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: I ask Allah, who granted your father this rank through you, to grant you from your offspring, before death, one like it. So he said: Allah has already done that. He said: I said: Who is he, may I be sacrificed for you? So he pointed to the righteous servant while he was lying down, and said: This one who is lying down, and he was a boy.

Abū ʿAlī al-Arrajānī al-Fārisī narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said: I asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān in the year in which Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī (عليه السلام) was seized, and I said to him: This man has come into the hands of this one, and we do not know what will become of him; so has anything reached you from him regarding any one of his sons? So he said to me: I had not thought that anyone would ask me about this matter. I entered upon Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad in his house, and there he was in a room in his residence, in a mosque belonging to him, and he was making duʿa, while on his right was Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), saying Āmīn to his supplication. So I said to him: May Allah make me your ransom; you know my devotion to you and my service to you, so who is the wali of the people after you? He said: Mūsā has put on the armor and it fit him evenly. So I said to him: After this, I have no need for anything else.

Ahmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Mūsā al-Ṣayqal, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, then Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام entered while he was a boy. So he said: “Commend him, and place his affair with those among your companions whom you trust.”

Is'haq ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: I was with my father one day, and 'Ali ibn 'Umar ibn 'Ali asked him, saying: “May I be sacrificed for you, to whom shall we turn, and to whom shall the people turn, after you?” So he said: “To the owner of the two yellow garments and the two locks of hair”—meaning the two braids—“and he is the one who will appear before you from this door, opening the two doors together with his hand.” Then we did not remain long before two hands appeared to us, taking hold of the two doors and opening them. Then Abū Ibrāhīm entered upon us.

Mansur ibn Hazim said to him: May my father and my mother be for you! Indeed, souls are approached in the morning and in the evening; so when that happens, then who will it be? So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: When that happens, then he is your master. And he struck with his hand upon the right shoulder of Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, as far as I know; and he was, on that day, five years old, while Abdullah ibn Ja'far was sitting with us.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Isa ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام), who said: I said to him, "If an event should occur—and may Allah not show me that—then whom should I follow as Imam?" He said: he gestured toward his son Musa (عليه السلام). I said, "If an event should occur to Musa, then whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son." I said, "If an event should occur to his son, and he leaves behind an older brother and a young son, then whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son." Then he said, "Thus it will always be." I said, "If I do not know him, nor know his location?" He said, "You should say: O Allah, I hold allegiance to whoever remains from Your proofs, from the offspring of the previous Imam. Indeed, that will suffice you, if Allah wills."

Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbdullāh al-Qallāʾ, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام mentioned Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while he was, at that time, a boy, and said: “This newborn is one such that no child born among us has been greater in blessing for our Shiʿah than him.” Then he said to me: “Do not be estranged from Ismāʿīl.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Fayd ibn al-Mukhtar. In a lengthy hadith regarding the matter of Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام), until Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) said to him: “He is your master whom you asked about, so stand before him and acknowledge his right.” So I stood and kissed his head and his hand, and I made du'a to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for him. Then Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) said: “Indeed, we had not been given permission regarding this before you.” He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, should I inform anyone of it?” He said: “Yes, your family and your children.” My family, my children, and my companions were with me, and Yunus ibn Zibyan was among my companions. So when I informed them, they praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Yunus said: “No, by Allah, not until I hear that from him.” He was hasty in this, so he went out and I followed him. So when I reached the door, I heard Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying to him—he had reached him before me: “O Yunus, the matter is as Fayd told you.” He said: So he said, “I have heard and obeyed.” Then Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) said to me: “Take him with you, O Fayd.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja‘far ibn Bashir, from Fudayl, from Tahir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام used to blame Abdullah, reproach him, admonish him, and say: “What has prevented you from being like your brother? For by Allah, I surely recognize the light in his face.” So Abdullah said: “Why? Is not my father and his father one, and my mother and his mother one?” So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said to him: “Indeed, he is from my very self, while you are my son.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, from Muhammad ibn Sinān, from Ya‘qūb Al-Sarrāj, who said: I entered upon Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام) while he was standing at the head of Abū Al-Hasan Mūsā, and he was in the cradle. He continued speaking privately to him for a long time, so I sat until he had finished. Then I rose toward him, and he said to me, “Come near to your master and greet him.” So I approached and greeted him, and he returned the greeting to me in an eloquent tongue. Then he said to me, “Go and change the name of your daughter whom you named yesterday, for it is a name that Allah hates.” A daughter had been born to me, and I had named her Al-Humayrā’. So Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام) said, “Comply with his command and you will be rightly guided.” So I changed her name.

Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu ʿAbdillah (عليه السلام) called Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام) one day while we were with him, and he said to us: “Hold fast to this one, for by Allah, he is your master after me.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl or someone else, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus, from Dawud ibn Zurbi, from Abu Ayyub al-Nahwi, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Mansur sent for me in the middle of the night, so I came to him and entered upon him while he was sitting on a chair, with a candle before him and a letter in his hand. He said: when I greeted him, he threw the letter to me while he was weeping, and said to me: This is the letter of Muhammad ibn Sulayman informing us that Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام has passed away. So surely we belong to Allah, and surely to Him we are returning. He said it three times, and: where is the like of Ja'far عليه السلام? Then he said to me: Write. He said: so I wrote the beginning of the letter. Then he said: Write: if he had appointed one specific man as his legatee, then bring him forward and strike his neck. He said: then the reply returned to him that he had appointed five as legatees: one of them was Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, and Muhammad ibn Sulayman, and 'Abdullah, and Musa عليه السلام, and Hamidah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, with something similar to this, except that he mentioned that he had bequeathed to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, and 'Abdullah, and Musa, and Muhammad ibn Ja'far, and a mawla of Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام. He said: So Abu Ja'far said, “There is no way to kill these.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, from ‘Alī ibn Al-Hasan, from Safwān Al-Jammāl, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about the Master of this affair, so he said: “Indeed, the Master of this affair does not amuse himself and does not play.” And Abū Al-Hasan Mūsā عليه السلام came forward while he was young, and with him was a Meccan she-goat kid, and he was saying to it: “Prostrate to your Lord.” So Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام took him and drew him close to himself, and said: “May my father and my mother be for the one who does not amuse himself and does not play.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from ʿUbays ibn Hishām, said: ʿUmar al-Rummānī narrated to me, from Fayḍ ibn al-Mukhtār, who said: I was in the presence of Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام when Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام came forward, and he was a boy. So I embraced him and kissed him, and Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “You are the ship, and this one is its captain.” He said: So I performed hajj the following year, and I had with me two thousand dinars. So I sent one thousand to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام and one thousand to him. Then when I entered upon Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said: “O Fayḍ, you made him equal to me.” I said: “I only did that because of your statement.” So he said: “Indeed, by Allah, it was not I who did that; rather Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did that for him.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Al-Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym Al-Ṣaḥḥāf, who said: I, and Hishām ibn Al-Ḥakam, and ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn were in Baghdad. Then ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn said: I was seated in the presence of Al-ʿAbd Al-Ṣāliḥ, when his son ʿAlī entered upon him. So he said to me: O ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, this is ʿAlī, the chief of my children. Indeed, I have bestowed upon him my teknonym. So Hishām ibn Al-Ḥakam struck his forehead with the palm of his hand, then said: Woe to you, how did you say it? Then ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn said: By Allah, I heard it from him exactly as I have said. So Hishām said: He informed you that the command is in him after him. Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Al-Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym Al-Ṣaḥḥāf, who said: I was in the presence of Al-ʿAbd Al-Ṣāliḥ. And in the copy of Al-Ṣafwānī, he said: I was, then he mentioned the like of it.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Nuʿaym al-Qābūsī, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, that he said: Indeed, my son ʿAlī is the eldest of my children, the most dutiful of them in my sight, and the most beloved of them to me; and he looks with me into al-Jafr, and none has looked into it except a Prophet or the successor of a Prophet.

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān and Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbbād al-Qaṣrī, both together from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said: I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام): “May I be sacrificed for you, I have indeed grown old in age, so take my hand away from the Fire.” He said: Then he gestured toward his son Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) and said: “This is your master after me.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah, from Al-Hasan, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said: I said to Abū al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: “Will you not guide me to the one from whom I should take my religion?” So he said: “This is my son, ‘Alī. Indeed, my father took me by the hand and brought me to the grave of Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then said: ‘O my son,’” “Indeed, I am placing upon the earth a خليفة.” And indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He says a word, He fulfills it.

Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Luʾluʾī, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAmr, from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, “Indeed, I have grown old and my bones have become frail, and I asked your father عليه السلام, and he informed me about you; so inform me who will be after you.” So he said, “This is Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.”

Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ziyād ibn Marwān al-Qandī—and he was from the Waqifites—who said: I entered upon Abū Ibrāhīm, and with him was his son Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. So he said to me: “O Ziyād, this is my son so-and-so. His document is my document, his speech is my speech, his messenger is my messenger, and whatever he says, then the word is his word.”

Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said: Al-Makhzūmī narrated to me—and his mother was from the descendants of Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام). He said: Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام) sent for us, so he gathered us and then said to us, “Do you know why I invited you?” We said, “No.” So he said: “Bear witness that this son of mine is my waṣī, the one who will undertake my affair, and my khalīfah after me. Whoever has a debt owed by me, let him take it from this son of mine. Whoever has been promised something by me, let him have it fulfilled through him. And whoever has no alternative but to meet me, then let him not meet me except with his letter.”

Ahmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam together, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who said: Written tablets came out to us from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while he was in prison: “My covenant is to the eldest of my sons, that he should do such-and-such and do such-and-such; and as for so-and-so, do not let him attain anything until I meet you, or Allah decrees death upon me.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who said: Tablets came out to us from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in al-Baṣrah, and written in them across was: “My covenant is to my eldest son: so-and-so is to be given such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such; and so-and-so is not to be given until I come, or Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decrees death upon me.” Surely Allah does whatever He wills.

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Muḥriz, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: He wrote to me from the prison: “So-and-so, my son, is the chief of my children, and I have bestowed my teknonym upon him.”

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū ʿAlī al-Khazzāz, from Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: I said to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: “Indeed, I fear that some event may occur and I may not meet you, so inform me who the Imam is after you.” So he said: “My son, so-and-so,” meaning Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Jahm, from al-Naṣr ibn Qābūs, who said: I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام), “I had asked your father (عليه السلام) who it is that will be after you, and he informed me that it is you. Then when Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) passed away, the people went right and left, while I and my companions held to you. So inform me who it is that will be after you from among your children.” He said, “My son, so-and-so.”

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn al-Ashʿath, from Dāwūd ibn Zurbī, who said: I came to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام with some wealth, and he took part of it and left part of it. So I said, "May Allah set you right, for what reason did you leave it with me?" He said, "Indeed, the holder of this command will ask it of you." Then, when news of his death came to us, Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, his son, sent to me and asked me for that wealth, so I handed it over to him.

‘Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Salit al-Zaydi, Abu al-Hakam said; and ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Umarah al-Jarmi informed me, from Yazid ibn Salit, who said: I met Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) while we were intending to perform ‘Umrah, at a place along the road. I said: “May I be made your ransom, do you recognize this place where we are?” He said: “Yes; do you recognize it too?” I said: “Yes. My father and I met you here while you were with Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام), and your brothers were with him. My father said to him: ‘May my father and mother be your ransom, all of you are purified Imams, and no one is free from death. So tell me something which I may relate to the one who will succeed me after me, so that he may not go astray.’” He said: “Yes, O Abū ‘Abdillāh, these are my children, and this one is their master,” and he pointed to you. “He has been taught judgment, understanding, generosity, and knowledge of what people need and of what they differ about in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. In him are good character and good response, and he is a gate from the gates of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in him is another quality better than all of that.” My father said to him: “What is it? May my father and mother be your ransom.” He (عليه السلام) said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, shall bring forth from him the relief of this Ummah, its succor, its banner, its light, its excellence, and its wisdom. He is the best newborn and the best youth. Through him Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will spare bloodshed, reconcile estrangement, gather what is scattered, mend what is split, clothe the naked, feed the hungry, give security to the fearful, send down rain, and show mercy to the servants. He is the best mature man and the best youth. His speech is judgment and his silence is knowledge. He clarifies for the people that wherein they differ, and he will lead his clan before the time of his maturity.” My father said to him: “May my father and mother be your ransom, has he been born?” He said: “Yes, and years have passed over him.” Yazīd said: Then someone came to us such that we could not speak in his presence. Yazīd said: So I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام): “Then you inform me with the like of what your father (عليه السلام) informed me.” He said to me: “Yes. My father (عليه

Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū al-Ḥakam, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Jaʿfarī and ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah narrated to me from Yazīd ibn Salīṭ, who said: When Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام made his bequest, he had as witnesses Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Jaʿfarī, Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Jaʿfarī, Isḥāq ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Jaʿfar ibn Ṣāliḥ, Muʿāwiyah al-Jaʿfarī, Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Saʿd ibn ʿImrān al-Anṣārī, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī, Yazīd ibn Salīṭ al-Anṣārī, and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Saʿd al-Aslamī, and he was the scribe of the bequest. First, he made them witnesses that he testified that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner for Him; that Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله is His servant and His Messenger; that the Hour is coming, in which there is no doubt; that Allah will raise those in the graves; that resurrection after death is true; that the promise is true; that the reckoning is true; that the decree is true; that standing before Allah is true; that what Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله brought is true; and that what the Trustworthy Spirit brought down is true. Upon that I live, upon it I die, and upon it I shall be raised, if Allah wills. And he made them witnesses that this is my bequest in my own handwriting. I have copied the bequest of my grandfather Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, and the bequest of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī; before that I copied it letter for letter; and the bequest of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad was likewise.
