I have bequeathed to ʿAlī, and then my sons are with him: if he wills, and perceives right guidance in them, and wishes to confirm them, then that belongs to him; and if he dislikes them and wishes to remove them, then that belongs to him, and they have no authority alongside him. And I have bequeathed to him my charities, my wealth, my mawālī, my young children whom I leave behind, and my children—Ibrāhīm, al-ʿAbbās, Qāsim, Ismāʿīl, Aḥmad, and Umm Aḥmad. The matter of my women, apart from them, belongs to ʿAlī. Also, a third of my father’s charity and my own third: he may place it wherever he sees fit and dispose within it as an owner disposes in his property. If he wishes to sell, gift, grant, or give it in charity to those whom I have named for him or to others besides those whom I named, that belongs to him. He is as myself in my bequest regarding my p

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali and Ubayd Allah ibn al-Marzuban, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام one year before he came to al-ʿIrāq, while ʿAlī, his son, was sitting before him. He looked at me and said, "O Muhammad, indeed there will be an upheaval in this year, so do not be distressed by that." He said: I said, "What will happen? May I be made your ransom, for what you mentioned has troubled me." So he said, "I shall go to the tyrant. Indeed, no evil will begin from him toward me, but from the one who will be after him." He said: I said, "And what will happen? May I be made your ransom." He said: "Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does whatever He wills." He said: I said, "And what is that? May I be made your ransom." He said, "Whoever wrongs this son of mine regarding his right, and denies his Imamate after me, is like one who wronged ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام in his right and denied his Imamate after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله." He said: I said, "By Allah, if Allah extends my life, I will surely submit to him his right and I will surely acknowledge his Imamate." He said, "You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. Allah will extend your life, and you will submit to him his right, acknowledge his Imamate, and the Imamate of the one who will come after him." He said: I said, "And who is that?" He said, "Muhammad, his son." He said: I said to him, "Acceptance and submission."

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb al-Zayyāt, who said: The one who had been seated in the presence of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام informed me that when they arose, he عليه السلام said to them: “Meet Abū Jaʿfar, then greet him عليه السلام and renew acquaintance with him.” Then when the people rose, he turned toward me and said: “May Allah have mercy upon al-Mufaḍḍal; he used to be content with less than this.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muʿammar ibn Khallad, who said: I heard al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and something was mentioned, so he said: “What is your need for that? This is Abū Jaʿfar; I have seated him in my seat and placed him in my position.” And he said: “We are a Household whose younger ones inherit from our elder ones, exactly and precisely, feather to feather.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: I entered upon Abu Jaʿfar al-Thani عليه السلام, and he discussed with me certain matters. Then he said to me: “O Abu Ali, doubt has been removed; there is no one for my father other than me.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Yaḥyā, from Mālik ibn Ashyam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Bashshār, who said: Ibn Qiyāmā wrote a letter to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, saying in it: “How can you be an Imam while you do not have a child?” So Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام answered him, as if angered: “And what has informed you that there will not be a child for me?” By Allah, the days and nights will not pass until Allah grants me a male child through whom He will distinguish between the truth and falsehood.

Some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: Ibn al-Najāshī said to me, 'Who is the Imam after your master? I desire that you ask him so that I may know.' So I entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام and informed him. He said: Then he said to me, 'The Imam is my son.' Then he said, 'Would anyone dare to say: My son, while he has no child?'

Ahmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, who said: We mentioned something in the presence of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام after Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام had been born to him, so he said: “What need do you have for that? This is Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. I have seated him in my seat and placed him in my position.”

Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Qiyama al-Wasiti, who said: I entered upon Ali ibn Musa (عليه السلام), and I said to him: “Can there be two Imams?” He said: “No, except that one of them is silent.” So I said to him: “Here you are; there is no silent one for you,” and Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) had not yet been born to him. So he said to me: “By Allah, Allah will surely bring forth from me that by which He will establish the truth and its people, and erase falsehood and its people.” Then after a year, Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) was born to him, and Ibn Qiyama was a Waqifi.

Ahmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Al-Ḥasan ibn Al-Jahm, who said: I was seated with Abū Al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, and he called for his son عليه السلام while he was small. He seated him in my lap and said to me: “Undress him and remove his shirt.” So I removed it, and he said to me: “Look between his shoulders.” So I looked, and there was on one of his shoulders something resembling a seal, embedded in the flesh. Then he said: “Do you see this? The like of it was in this place on my father عليه السلام.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Ṣanʿānī, who said: I was in the presence of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام when his son Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was brought, while he was still young. So he said: "This is the newborn such that no newborn has been born with greater blessing upon our Shiʿah than him."

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I said to al-Rida عليه السلام: We used to ask you before Allah had granted Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام to you, and you would say: Allah will grant me a boy. Now Allah has indeed granted him to you, and He has delighted our eyes. May Allah not show us your day. But if an event should occur, then to whom? So he pointed with his hand to Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, while he was standing before him. So I said: May I be your ransom, this is a son of three years. He said: And what harm is there in that? ‘Isa عليه السلام stood with the hujjah while he was a son of three years.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhūr, from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, who said: I heard Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm saying to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “Indeed, my son has heaviness in his tongue, so I will send him to you tomorrow, that you may wipe over his head and supplicate for him, for he is your mawla.” So he said: “He is the mawla of Abū Jaʿfar, so send him to him tomorrow.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdī, from Muhammad ibn Khallād al-Sayqal, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I was seated in the presence of ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad in al-Madīnah, and I had stayed with him for two years, writing from him what he heard from his brother, meaning Abā al-Hasan عليه السلام, when Abū Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام entered the mosque, the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله. Then ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar sprang up without shoes and without a cloak, kissed his hand, and honored him. So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him, “O uncle, sit down, may Allah have mercy on you.” He said, “O my master, how can I sit while you are standing?” Then when ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar returned to his gathering, his companions began reproaching him and saying, “You are the uncle of his father, and you do this to him?” He said, “Be silent. If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not deemed this white hair worthy, and has deemed this young man worthy, and placed him where He placed him, should I deny his merit? We seek refuge in Allah from what you are saying. Rather, I am his servant.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Khayrani, from his father, who said: I was standing before Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in Khurasan, when a man said to him: “O my master, if an occurrence were to happen, then to whom [would the matter go]?” He said: “To Abū Jaʿfar, my son.” Then it was as though the speaker considered the age of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام too small, so Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent ʿĪsā ibn Maryam as a Messenger, a Prophet, and the bearer of an initiated law, at an age younger than the age in which Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام is.”

I heard ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrating to al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and he said: “By Allah, Allah certainly granted victory to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.” So al-Ḥasan said to him: “Yes, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you, his brothers surely transgressed against him.” So ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar said: “Yes, by Allah, and we, his paternal uncles, transgressed against him.” So al-Ḥasan said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, what did you do? For I was not present with you.” He said: “His brothers said to him, and we as well: ‘There has never been among us an Imam of altered complexion.’ So al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to them: ‘He is my son.’ They said: ‘The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله judged by al-qāfah, so between us and you is al-qāfah.’ He said: ‘You send to them yourselves. As for me, no. And do not inform them why you invited them, and let yourselves remain in your houses.’” So when they came, they seated us in the orchard, and his paternal uncles, his brothers, and his sisters lined up. They took al-Riḍā عليه السلام, clothed him in a woolen robe and a cap of it, placed a spade on his neck, and said to him: ‘Enter the orchard as though you are working in it.’ Then they brought Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and said: ‘Attach this boy to his father.’ They said: ‘He has no father here, but this is his father’s uncle, and this is his father’s uncle, and this is his uncle, and this is his paternal aunt. But if he has a father here, then he is the owner of the orchard, for his feet and his feet are one.’ So when Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام returned, they said: ‘This is his father.’ ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar said: “So I stood up and sucked the saliva of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, then I said to him: ‘I bear witness that you are my Imam before Allah.’ Then al-Riḍā عليه السلام wept and said: ‘O uncle, did you not hear my father while he was saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “May my father be for the son of the best of the slave-women, the son of the Nubian woman, pure of mouth, select of womb. Woe to them! May Allah curse al-Uʿaybis and his offspring, the possessor of tribulation. He will kill them for years and months and days, impose abasement upon them, and give them to drink a goblet that causes endurance. And he is the outcast, the fugitive, the one bereaved through his father and his grandfather, the possessor of the ghaybah, about

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, who said: When Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام departed from al-Madīnah to Baghdād on the first of his two departures, I said to him at the time of his departure, “May I be your ransom, I fear for you on this journey, so to whom will the authority belong after you?” He turned his face toward me smiling and said, “The occultation is not where you supposed, in this year.” Then when he was taken out a second time to al-Muʿtaṣim, I went to him and said to him, “May I be your ransom, you are departing, so to whom will this authority belong after you?” Then he wept until his beard became soaked. Then he turned to me and said, “At this time it is feared for me; the authority after me belongs to my son ʿAlī.”

He said: He (my father) used to attend the door of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) for the service he had been assigned to. And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa would come at the time of dawn every night to learn news of the illness of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). There was a messenger who used to go between Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and my father; whenever he arrived, Ahmad would rise and my father would be alone with him. So one night I went out and Ahmad rose from the gathering and my father was alone with the messenger, and Ahmad circled around and stood where he could hear the speech. The messenger said to my father: 'Your Master conveys his greetings upon you and says to you: I am going to pass away, and the authority (Imamate) will pass to my son Ali, and his right upon you after me is what was my right upon you after my father.' Then the messenger departed and Ahmad returned to his place and said to my father: 'What did he say to you?' He said: 'Good.' He said: 'I heard what he said, so why do you conceal it?' and he repeated what he had heard. So my father said to him: 'God has forbidden upon you what you did, because God the Exalted says: "and do not spy" So preserve this testimony, for perhaps we will need it one day, and beware of revealing it before its proper time.' When morning came, my father wrote out the message in ten scrolls and sealed them, and handed them over to ten notables of the community, saying: 'If death should befall me before I request them back from you, then open them and act upon what is in them.' When Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed away, my father mentioned that he did not leave his house until about four hundred persons had pledged allegiance upon his hands, and the leaders of the community gathered at Muhammad ibn al-Faraj's home to discuss this matter. So Muhammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to my father informing him of their gathering with him and that if not for fear of publicity he would have come with them, and he asked him to come. So my father mounted and went to him and found the people assembled with him. They said to my father: 'What do you say regarding this matter?' My father said to those who had the scrolls: 'Produce the scrolls.' They produced them, and he said to them: 'This is what I was commanded with.' Some of them said: 'We would have liked there to be another witness with you in this matter.' He said

And in a copy of al-Safwani — Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Wasiti that he heard Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid, the freed slave of Abu Ja'far, narrating that he (the Imam) made him a witness upon this copied testament: Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid, the freed slave of Abu Ja'far, testifies that Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) made him a witness that he bequeathed to Ali his son, himself and his sisters, and he made the matter of Musa, when he reaches adulthood, to him. And he made Abdullah ibn al-Musawir a custodian over his estate — the properties, and wealth, and expenditures, and slaves, and other things — until Ali ibn Muhammad reaches adulthood. Abdullah ibn al-Musawir, from that day, came under him (Ali): standing with the matter of his own self and his sisters, and the matter of Musa came to him, standing for himself after the two of them, upon the stipulation of their father regarding his charities which he dispensed. And that was on a Sunday, the third night having passed of Dhu al-Hijja, in the year two hundred and twenty. Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid wrote his testimony in his own handwriting. And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) — who is al-Juwwani — testified to the same as the testimony of Ahmad ibn Abi Khalid at the beginning of this letter and wrote his testimony by his own hand. Nasr the servant testified and wrote his testimony by his own hand.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Nahdī, from Yaḥyā ibn Yasār al-Qanbarī, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام bequeathed to his son al-Ḥasan before his passing by four months, and he made me a witness to that, along with a group of the mawālī.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Bashshar ibn Ahmad al-Basri, from ‘Ali ibn ‘Umar al-Nawfali, who said: I was with Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام in the courtyard of his house, when Muhammad, his son, passed by us. So I said to him: ‘May I be sacrificed for you, is this one our master after you?’ He said: ‘No. Your master after me is al-Hasan.’

From him, from Bashshār ibn Aḥmad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Aṣfahānī, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Your master after me is the one who will perform salat (prayer) over me.” He said: “And we did not know Abū Muḥammad before that.” He said: “Then Abū Muḥammad came out and performed salat (prayer) over him.”

And from him, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Wahb, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, who said: I was present with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام when his son Muḥammad passed away. Then he said to al-Ḥasan: “O my son, renew gratitude to Allah, for He has brought about in you a matter.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Marwān al-Anbārī, who said: I was present at the passing of Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام). Then Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) came, and a chair was placed for him, so he sat upon it, and around him were the members of his household, while Abū Muḥammad was standing in a corner. Then when he had finished with the matter of Abū Jaʿfar, he turned toward Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) and said: “O my son, renew gratitude to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, for He has brought about in you a matter.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Qalānisī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “If an occurrence should take place—and I seek refuge in Allah—then to whom?” He said: “My covenant is to the eldest of my sons.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Muḥammad al-Isbāriqīnī, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAmr al-ʿAṭṭār, who said: I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام), while Abū Jaʿfar, his son, was still among the living, and I thought that he was the one. So I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, which of your sons should I designate? He said: Do not designate anyone until my command comes out to you. He said: I then wrote to him afterwards, asking in whom this matter would be. He wrote back to me: In the elder of my two sons. He said: And Abū Muḥammad was older than Abū Jaʿfar.

In the courtyard of his house, while the people were seated around him, they said: “We estimated that around him there were one hundred and fifty men from the family of Abī Ṭālib, Banī Hāshim, and Quraysh, besides his mawālī and the rest of the people.” Then he looked toward al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, who had come with his collar torn, until he stood at his right side, and we did not know him. Then Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام looked at him after a while and said: “O my son, renew gratitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for He has brought about in you a matter.” So the youth wept, praised Allah, and recited the istirjāʿ, and said: “All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and I ask Allah for the completion of His blessings for us through you, and indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we are returning.” So we asked about him, and it was said: “This is al-Ḥasan, his son.” We estimated him at that time to be twenty years old or somewhat older. On that day, we came to know him and understood that he had indicated him for the Imamate and established him in his place.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Daryāb, who said: I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام after the passing of Abū Jaʿfar, so I offered him condolences over him, while Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام was sitting. Then Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام wept, so Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام turned toward him and said to him: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed in you a successor from him, so praise Allah.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī, who said: I was with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام after his son Abū Jaʿfar had passed away, and I was thinking to myself, wanting to say: It is as though these two—I mean Abū Jaʿfar and Abū Muḥammad—at this time are like Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā and Ismāʿīl, the two sons of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and that their story is like their story, as Abū Muḥammad was the one anticipated after Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. So Abū al-Ḥasan turned toward me before I spoke and said: Yes, O Abū Hāshim, there occurred for Allah regarding Abū Muḥammad after Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that which had not been known for him, just as there occurred for Him regarding Mūsā after the passing of Ismāʿīl that by which his condition was disclosed. And it is just as your soul told you, even if the falsifiers dislike it. And Abū Muḥammad, my son, is the successor after me; with him is the knowledge of what is needed, and with him is the instrument of the Imamate.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Daryāb, from Abī Bakr al-Fahfakī, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wrote to me: Abū Muḥammad, my son, is the most sincere in disposition among the family of Muḥammad and the firmest of them in proof. He is the eldest of my sons, and he is the successor; to him the bonds of the Imamate and its rulings come to an end. So whatever you used to ask me, ask him about it, for with him is that which is needed.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Shāhawayh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Jallāb, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wrote to me in a letter: “You wanted to ask about the successor after Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and you were anxious about that, so do not grieve; for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not cause a people to go astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against.” “And your master after me is Abū Muḥammad, my son, and with him is what you need. Allah advances what He wills and delays what He wills.” “Whatever āyah We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or one like it.” “I have written that in which there is clarification and sufficiency for one who possesses an alert intellect.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from the one whom he mentioned, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, from Dāwūd ibn al-Qāsim, who said: I heard Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام saying: “The successor after me is al-Ḥasan. So how will it be for you regarding the successor after the successor?” So I said: “And why, may Allah make me your ransom?” He said: “You will not see his person, and it will not be permissible for you to mention him by his name.” So I said: “Then how should we mention him?” He said: “Say: al-Ḥujjah from the family of Muḥammad عليهم السلام.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bilal, who said: There came out to me from Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام, two years before his passing, informing me of the successor after him. Then, three days before his passing, there came out to me informing me of the successor after him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Abi Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I said to Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام): "Your majesty prevents me from asking you, so will you permit me to ask you?" He said: "Ask." I said: "O my master, do you have a son?" He said: "Yes." I said: "If an event occurs to you, then where shall I ask about him?" He said: "In al-Madinah."

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Makfūf, from ʿAmr al-Ahwāzī, who said: Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام showed me his son and said: “This is your Master after me.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥamdān al-Qalānisī, who said: I said to al-ʿAmrī, “Has Abū Muḥammad passed away?” So he said to me, “He has passed away, but he has left among you one whose neck is like this,” and he gestured with his hand.

There was issued from Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), when al-Zubayrī—may Allah curse him—was killed: “This is the recompense of one who dared against Allah concerning His awliyā'. He claimed that he would kill me and that I would have no offspring. So how did he see the power of Allah concerning him?” And a son was born to him, whom he named M Ḥ M D, in the year two hundred and fifty-six.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn and Muhammad, the two sons of Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Abdi of Abd Qays, from Daw' ibn Ali al-Ijli, from a man from the people of Persia, whom he named, who said: I came to Samarra and stayed at the door of Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام). He called me, so I entered upon him and offered greeting. He said, "What has brought you here?" He said: I said, "A desire to serve you." He said: Then he said to me, "Then remain at the door." He said: So I was in the house with the servants. Then I came to buy necessities for them from the market, and I used to enter upon them without permission when there were men in the house. He said: Then one day I entered upon him while he was in the men's quarters, and I heard movement in the house. So he called to me, "Stay where you are; do not move." So I did not dare either to enter or to leave. Then a maidservant came out toward me carrying something covered. Then he called to me, "Enter." So I entered, and he called the maidservant, and she returned to him. He said to her, "Uncover what is with you." So she uncovered a fair boy, handsome of face, and she uncovered his belly, and there was hair growing from his throat-pit to his navel, green, not black. Then he said, "This is your master." Then he ordered her, and she carried him away. So I did not see him after that until Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) passed away.

Muhammad ibn Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya, all together, from Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, who said: I and the Shaykh Abu 'Amr, may God have mercy on him, gathered in the presence of Ahmad ibn Ishaq. Ahmad ibn Ishaq nudged me to ask him about the Successor (the hidden Imam). So I said to him: 'O Abu 'Amr! I want to ask you about something, and I have no doubt regarding what I want to ask you. My belief and my religion is that the earth cannot be devoid of a Divine Proof (Hujja) — except when it is forty days before the Day of Resurrection. When that occurs, the Proof will be lifted and the door of repentance will be closed, such that no soul's faith shall benefit it if it had not believed before, nor if it had earned good through its faith.' 'Those would be the most wicked of God's creation, Mighty and Majestic, and they are those upon whom the Resurrection shall occur. However, I wished to increase in certainty, just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to show him how He revives the dead. He said: Do you not believe? He said: Yes, but so that my heart may be at peace.' 'And Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ishaq informed me from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: I asked him and said: With whom shall I deal, or from whom shall I take, and whose word shall I accept? So he said to him: Al-'Amri is my trusted one. Whatever he conveys to you from me, he conveys from me, and whatever he says to you from me, he says from me. Listen to him and obey, for he is the trustworthy, the reliable.' 'And Abu Ali informed me that he asked Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the same, and he said to him: Al-'Amri and his son are both trustworthy. Whatever they both convey to you from me, they convey from me, and whatever they both say to you, they say from me. Listen to them both and obey them, for they are both trustworthy and reliable. This is the word of two Imams, both of whom have passed, regarding you.' He said: Abu 'Amr then fell prostrate and wept. Then he said: 'Ask your need.' I said to him: 'You have seen the Successor from after Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'Yes, by God, and his neck was like this,' and he gestured with his hand. I said to him: 'There remains one (question).' He said to me: 'Go ahead.' I said: 'The name?' He said: 'It is forbidden for you to ask about that, and I do not say this from myself — it is

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar—and he was the eldest shaykh among the descendants of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله in al-ʿIrāq—so he said: I saw him between the two masjids, and he عليه السلام was a boy.

Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Ḥamzah ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar narrated to me; he said: Ḥakīmah, daughter of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, narrated to me, and she is the paternal aunt of his father. That she saw him on the night of his birth and after that.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalansi, who said: I said to al-'Amri: 'Has Abu Muhammad عليه السلام passed away?' So he said: 'He عليه السلام has passed away, but he عليه السلام has left behind among you one whose neck is like this,' and he indicated with his hand.
ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Fatḥ, the mawlā of al-Zurārī, who said: I heard Abū ʿAlī ibn Muṭahhar mention that he had indeed seen him عليه السلام, and he described his stature to him.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Shādhān ibn Nuʿaym, from a female servant of Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdah al-Naysābūrī, that she said: I was standing with Ibrāhīm at al-Ṣafā, then he, peace be upon him, came until he stood by Ibrāhīm, took hold of the book of his rites, and spoke to him about some matters.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ. That he saw him عليه السلام at the Black Stone, while the people were crowding and pulling toward it, and he عليه السلام was saying: “This is not what they were commanded to do.”

ʿAlī, from Abū ʿAlī Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Idrīs, from his father, that he said: I saw him, peace be upon him, after the passing of Abū Muḥammad, when he had reached adolescence, and I kissed his hands and his head.

Ali narrated from Abi Abd Allah ibn Salih and Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from al-Qanbari, a man from the descendants of Qanbar al-Kabir, a mawla of Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said: A discussion concerning Jaʿfar ibn ʿAli took place, and he was criticized. So I said to him, "Then there is no one other than him; have you seen him?" He said, "I have not seen him, but someone other than me has seen him." I said, "And who has seen him?" He said, "Jaʿfar has seen him twice, and he has an account concerning that."

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Muḥammad al-Wajnānī, that he informed me from one who saw him, that he came out of the house ten days before the event, while he was saying: O Allah, You know that it is among the most beloved of places, were it not for the expulsion—or words close to this.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Qays, from one of the henchmen of al-Sawād, who said: I saw Sīmāʾ only a short while ago in Surr Man Raʾā, and he had broken the door of the house. Then he عليه السلام came out to him, and in his hand was an axe, and he said to him: “What are you doing in my house?” So Sīmāʾ said: “Jaʿfar claimed that your father عليه السلام had passed away and that he had no son. So if it is your house, then I have withdrawn from you.” Then he left the house. ʿAlī ibn Qays said: A servant from among the servants of the house came out to us, so I asked him about this report. He said to me: “Who told you this?” I said to him: “Some of the henchmen of al-Sawād told me.” So he said to me: “Hardly anything remains hidden from the people.”
ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Makfūf, from ʿAmr al-Ahwāzī, who said: Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) showed him to me and said: “This is your Master.”
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Naysābūrī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from Abū Naṣr Ẓarīf al-Khādim, that he had seen him.

In the year two hundred and seventy-nine, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAbdī, from Ḍawʾ ibn ʿAlī al-ʿIjlī, from a man from the people of Fāris whom he named, that Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام showed him to him.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Aḥmad ibn Rāshid, from one of the people of al-Madāʾin, who said: I was a pilgrim of hajj with a companion of mine, and we came to the standing place. Then there was a young man sitting, wearing an izār and a ridāʾ, and on his feet were yellow sandals. I estimated the izār and the ridāʾ at one hundred and fifty dinars, and there was no trace of travel upon him. Then a beggar came near us, but we turned him away. So he went to the young man and asked him, and he picked up something from the ground and handed it to him. Then the beggar supplicated for him, exerted himself in the du'a, and prolonged it. Then the young man stood up and disappeared from us. So we went up to the beggar and said to him, 'Woe to you, what did he give you?' He showed us a marked piece of gold, which we estimated at twenty mithqāls. So I said to my companion, 'Our Mawlā is with us, and we do not know.' Then we went seeking him, and we went around the whole standing place, but we were unable to find him. Then we asked everyone who had been around him from the people of Makkah and al-Madīnah, and they said, 'He is a young ʿAlawī who performs hajj every year on foot.'

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from the one whom he mentioned, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, from Dāwūd ibn al-Qāsim al-Jaʿfarī, who said: I heard Abā al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام saying: “The successor after me is al-Ḥasan, so how will it be for you with the successor after the successor?” So I said: “And why, may Allah make me your ransom?” He said: “You will not see his person, and it is not permissible for you to mention him by his name.” So I said: “Then how should we mention him?” He said: “Say: the Ḥujjah from the family of Muḥammad, may Allah’s blessings and His peace be upon him.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah al-Salihy, who said: Our companions asked me, after the passing of Abu Muhammad عليه السلام, to ask about the name and the place. Then the answer came out: “If I direct them to the name, they will publicize it; and if they come to know the place, they will guide others to it.”

A number of our companions, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Rayyān ibn al-Ṣalt, who said: I heard Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام saying, and he was asked about al-Qāʾim. So he said: “His body will not be seen, nor will his name be mentioned.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The صاحب of this matter — none names him by his name except a disbeliever.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from the one who narrated it to him, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from his father, from some of his companions, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The nearest that the servants are to Allah, majestic is His remembrance, and the most pleasing state of theirs to Him, is when they have lost sight of the Proof of Allah, mighty and majestic, and he has not appeared to them, and they do not know his place, while in that state they know that the Proof of Allah, majestic is His remembrance, and His covenant have not been nullified. So at that time, expect relief morning and evening. For the most intense that the wrath of Allah is upon His enemies is when they have lost His Proof and he has not appeared to them, while He knows that His friends do not fall into doubt. Had He known that they would fall into doubt, He would not have concealed His Proof from them for the blink of an eye. And that only occurs over the heads of the worst of people.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mirdas, from Safwan ibn Yahya and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام): Which is superior: worship in secret with the concealed Imam from among you during the rule of falsehood, or worship in the manifestation of the truth and its rule with the manifest Imam from among you? He said: O Ammar, charity in secret, by Allah, is better than charity in public; and likewise, by Allah, your worship in secret with your concealed Imam during the rule of falsehood, and your fear of your enemy in the rule of falsehood and in a state of truce, is better than one who worships Allah, Mighty and Majestic is His remembrance, in the manifestation of the truth with the manifest Imam of truth in the rule of truth. Worship with fear in the rule of falsehood is not like worship with safety in the rule of truth. And know that whoever among you today performs an obligatory salat in congregation at its appointed time while concealing it from his enemy, then completes it, Allah will record for him fifty obligatory congregational prayers. And whoever among you performs an obligatory salat alone at its appointed time while concealing it from his enemy, then completes it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will record for him twenty-five obligatory prayers performed individually. And whoever among you performs a supererogatory salat at its proper time and completes it, Allah will record for him ten supererogatory prayers. And whoever among you performs a good deed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will record for him twenty good deeds. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, multiplies the good deeds of the believer among you many times over when he perfects his deeds, practices taqiyyah for the sake of his religion, his Imam, and himself, and restrains his tongue. Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Generous. I said: May I be made your ransom, by Allah, you have indeed made me desirous of action and urged me toward it, but I would like to know how it is that today our deeds have become better than the deeds of the companions of the manifest Imam from among you in the rule of truth, while we are upon one religion. He said: You preceded them in entering into the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in salat, sawm, hajj, every good deed and fiqh, and in wo

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Usāmah, from Hishām; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: The trustworthy ones from among the companions of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام narrated to me that they heard Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام saying in one of his sermons: “O Allah, I surely know that knowledge does not altogether withdraw, nor are its sources cut off, and that You do not leave Your earth without a proof from You over Your creation—either manifest, though not obeyed, or fearful and hidden—so that Your proofs may not be invalidated and Your awliyāʾ may not go astray after You have guided them. But where are they, and how many are they? They are the fewest in number, yet the greatest in worth before Allah, majestic is His mention.” They are the followers of the leaders of the religion, the guiding Imams, who discipline themselves by their manners and follow their path. At that point, knowledge rushes upon them with the reality of faith; their souls respond to the leaders of knowledge; they find ease in their hadith in matters that others find harsh; and they find intimacy with that from which the deniers feel estrangement and which the prodigal refuse. Those are the followers of the scholars. They keep company with the people of the world through obedience to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and His awliyāʾ, and they practice taqiyyah regarding their religion and out of fear of their enemy. Their souls are attached to the highest station. Their scholars and their followers are mute and silent in the rule of falsehood, awaiting the rule of truth. And Allah shall establish the truth by His words and efface falsehood. Ah, ah! Blessedness is for them for their patience upon their religion during the time of their truce; and how I long to see them in the time of the manifestation of their rule. And Allah will gather us and them in Gardens of Eden, along with those who were righteous from their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring.”

The height of the matter (of Religion), and its peak, and its key, and the door of all things, and the pleasure of the All-Merciful, Blessed and Exalted, is obedience to the Imam after recognising him. Then he said: 'Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says:' Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah, and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a keeper over them.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Sabbah who said: I bear witness that I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I testify that Ali is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that al-Hasan is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that al-Husayn is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that Ali ibn al-Husayn is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that Muhammad ibn Ali is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory.'

Hammad ibn Uthman narrated to us from Bashir al-Attar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: We are a people whom God has made obedience to obligatory, and you are following one whose ignorance people cannot be excused for.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and We gave them a grand kingdom' [4:54] he said: 'The imposed obedience.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Attar who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Participation has been established between the successors (Imams) and the Messengers with regards to obedience.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We are a people whom God, Mighty and Majestic, has made obedience to us obligatory. For us are the anfal (spoils of war), and for us is the choicest of wealth, and we are the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, and we are the envied ones about whom God said: "Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His grace?"

I mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) our statement regarding the successors — that obedience to them is obligatory. So he said: 'Yes.' They are the ones about whom God the Exalted said: 'Obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority from among you' [4:59] And they are the ones about whom God Mighty and Majestic said: 'But rather, only God is your guardian, and His Messenger, and those who have believed' [5:55]

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said: A Persian man asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'Is obeying you obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' He (the man) said: 'Like obedience to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Imams — do they all proceed in the matter (of religion) and obedience in one and the same manner? He said: Yes.

And by this chain, from Marwak ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Tabari, who said: I was standing by the head of al-Rida عليه السلام in Khurasan, and with him were a number of the Banu Hashim, among whom was Ishaq ibn Musa ibn 'Isa al-'Abbasi. So he said: O Ishaq, it has reached me that the people are saying that we claim that the people are our slaves. No, by my kinship to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, I have never said it at all, nor did I hear any of my forefathers say it, nor has it reached me from any of my forefathers that he said it. But I do say: the people are devoted to us in obedience, and loyal to us in the religion. So let the one who is present convey it to the one who is absent.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Abī Salamah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: We are those whose obedience Allah has made obligatory. The people have no choice except our recognition, and the people are not excused for ignorance of us. Whoever recognizes us is a believer, and whoever denies us is a disbeliever; and whoever neither recognizes us nor denies us is astray until he returns to the guidance that Allah has made obligatory upon him, namely our obligatory obedience. So if he dies upon his misguidance, Allah will do with him whatever He wills.

I asked him عليه السلام about the most excellent thing by which the servants draw near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: “The most excellent thing by which the servants draw near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is obedience to Allah, obedience to His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and obedience to those vested with authority.” Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Love for us is iman, and hatred for us is kufr.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام): "Shall I present to you my religion by which I worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" He said: "Bring it forth." He said: So I said, "I bear witness that there is no god except Allah alone, having no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, and affirming what he brought from the presence of Allah; and that Ali was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory; then after him al-Hasan was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory; then after him al-Husayn was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory; then after him Ali ibn al-Husayn was an Imam whose obedience Allah made obligatory, until the matter came to him." Then I said, "It is you, may Allah have mercy upon you." He said: "This is the religion of Allah and the religion of His angels."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ishaq, from one of the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Know that the companionship of the scholar and following him is a religion by which Allah is worshipped, and obedience to him is a means of acquiring good deeds, an effacer of evil deeds, a ذخيرة for the believers, an elevation among them in their lifetime, and a beauty after their death.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Surely God is too Majestic and Generous to be known through His creation; rather, creation is known through God.' He said: 'You speak the truth.' I said: 'Surely one who recognizes that he has a Lord, it is befitting for him to recognize that that Lord has pleasure and wrath, and that His pleasure and wrath cannot be known except through revelation or a messenger. So whoever does not receive revelation, it is befitting for him to seek the messengers. When he meets them, he should recognize that they are the Divine Authority (hujja) and that obedience to them is obligatory.' So I said to the people: 'Do you not know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was the Divine Authority from God over His creation?' They said: 'Yes.' I said: 'So when he passed away, who was the Divine Authority?' They said: 'The Quran.' So I looked into the Quran and found that the Murji'ites, the Qadariyya, and the atheist who does not believe in it, all use it in debate to the point of defeating men in their argumentation. So I recognized that the Quran cannot be a Divine Authority except with a custodian (qayyim), and whatever he says about it is the truth. So I said to them: 'Who is the custodian of the Quran?' They said: 'Ibn Mas'ud knew parts of it, and Umar knew, and Hudhayfa knew.' I said: 'All of it?' They said: 'No.' So I could not find anyone who could be said to know the Quran in its entirety except Ali (may God's blessings be upon him); and whenever there was a matter among the people, this one said: 'I do not know', that one said: 'I do not know', another said: 'I do not know', while he said: 'I do know.' Thus I testify that Ali (peace be upon him) was the custodian of the Quran, that obedience to him was obligatory, and that he was the Divine Authority over the people after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and that whatever he said about the Quran is the truth.' So he (the Imam) said: 'May God have mercy on you!' So I said: 'Surely Ali (peace be upon him) did not depart until he left a Divine Authority after him, just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had left; and the Divine Authority after Ali was al-Hasan ibn Ali.' And I testify about al-Hasan that he

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, "Is obedience to the awsiya' obligatory?" He said, "Yes." They are those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority from among you." And they are those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Your wali is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish salat and give zakat while they are bowing."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Abd al-A'la, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah عليه السلام saying: "Listening and obedience are the doors of goodness. The listener who obeys has no proof against him, and the listener who disobeys has no proof for him. And the Imam of the Muslims, his proof and his argument are completed on the Day when he meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Then he said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘The Day We shall call every people by their Imam.’"

Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, both together, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi, from Salih ibn Khalid, from Yaman al-Tammar, who said: We were seated in the presence of Abu ‘Abd Allah (عليه السلام), and he said to us: “Indeed, for the Master of this affair there shall be a ghaybah (occultation); the one who holds fast to his religion during it is like one stripping al-qatad thorn-bush.” Then he said, indicating like this with his hand: “Which of you can grasp the thorns of al-qatad with his hand?” Then he lowered his head for a long while, then said: “Indeed, for the Master of this affair there shall be a ghaybah (occultation), so let the servant have taqwa of Allah and hold fast to his religion.”

Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Isa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: When the fifth from the descendants of the seventh is missing, then Allah, Allah, regarding your religions; let no one remove you from them. O my son, there is inevitably an occultation for the Master of this matter, until one who used to profess this matter turns back from it. It is only a trial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by which He has tested His creation. If your fathers and your grandfathers had known a religion more correct than this, they would surely have followed it. He said: So I said, 'O my master, who is the fifth from the descendants of the seventh?' He said, 'O my son, your intellects are too limited for this, and your forbearance is too constricted to bear it; but if you live, you shall come to realize him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Musawir, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying: “Beware of publicizing it. By Allah, your Imam will surely go into ghaybah for years of your time, and you will surely be tested and purified until it is said: He died, he was killed, he perished, in which valley did he travel? And the eyes of the believers will surely shed tears over him, and you will surely be overturned as ships are overturned in the waves of the sea.” Then none will be saved except one whose covenant Allah has taken, and in whose heart He has written faith, and whom He has supported with a spirit from Him. And twelve confusing banners will surely be raised, such that it will not be known which is which. He said: So I wept, then I said: So what should we do? He said: Then he looked at sunlight entering the veranda and said: O Abu Abdillah, do you see this sun? I said: Yes. He said: By Allah, our matter is clearer than this sun.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Sudayr al-Sayrafi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, in the Master of this matter there is a resemblance to Yusuf (عليه السلام).” He said: I said to him, “It is as though you are referring to his life or his ghaybah (occultation).” He said: So he said to me, “And what is there to deny in that? This community is like swine. Indeed, the brothers of Yusuf (عليه السلام) were tribes, the sons of the Prophets. They traded with Yusuf, dealt with him, and spoke to him, while they were his brothers and he was their brother, yet they did not recognize him until he said:” “I am Yusuf, and this is my brother.” “So what does this accursed community deny in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, dealing with His hujjah at some time just as He dealt with Yusuf? Indeed, Yusuf (عليه السلام) had the kingdom of Egypt, and between him and his father was a journey of eighteen days. Had he wished to inform him, he would have been able to do so. Ya‘qub (عليه السلام) and his children, upon receiving the good news, traveled nine days from their desert dwelling to Egypt. So what does this community deny in Allah, Majestic and Mighty, dealing with His hujjah just as He dealt with Yusuf: that he may walk in their markets and tread upon their carpets until Allah permits that for him, just as He permitted for Yusuf? They said:” “Are you indeed Yusuf?” He said: “I am Yusuf.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, for the boy there will be a ghaybah (occultation) before he rises.” He said: I said, “And why?” He said: “He fears,” and he gestured with his hand toward his stomach. Then he said: “O Zurarah, and he is al-Muntazar, and he is the one regarding whose birth doubt will arise. Among them is one who says: ‘His father died without a successor’; and among them is one who says: ‘A pregnancy’; and among them is one who says: ‘Indeed, he was born two years before the death of his father.’ And he is al-Muntazar, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves to test the Shi'ah. So at that time, the falsifiers will fall into doubt, O Zurarah.” He said: I said, “May I be made your ransom, if I reach that time, what should I do?” He said: “O Zurarah, if you reach this time, then supplicate with this du'a: ‘O Allah, make me know Yourself, for if You do not make me know Yourself, I will not know Your Prophet. O Allah, make me know Your Messenger, for if You do not make me know Your Messenger, I will not know Your Hujjah. O Allah, make me know Your Hujjah, for if You do not make me know Your Hujjah, I will go astray from my religion.’” Then he said: “O Zurarah, there must inevitably be the killing of a boy in al-Madinah.” I said, “May I be made your ransom, is it not the army of al-Sufyani that will kill him?” He said: “No, rather the army of the family of so-and-so will kill him. It will come until it enters al-Madinah, then seize the boy and kill him. So when they kill him in rebellion, hostility, and ظلم, they will not be granted respite. Then at that moment, await the faraj, if Allah wills.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna, from ‘Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said: I heard Aba ‘Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying: “The people will lose sight of their Imam. He attends the season, so he sees them, while they do not see him.”

Munḏir ibn Muḥammad ibn Qābūs narrated to me, from Manṣūr ibn al-Sindī, from Abū Dāwūd al-Mustariq, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Mālik al-Juhanī, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: I came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and found him deep in thought, tracing in the ground. So I said: O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why do I see you pondering and tracing in the ground? Is it out of some desire for it? He said: No, by Allah. I have never desired it, nor the world, for even a single day at all. Rather, I was thinking about a child who will be from my loins, the eleventh of my descendants. He is the Mahdī who will fill the earth with justice and equity just as it had been filled with tyranny and oppression. There will be for him a ghaybah (occultation) and a state of bewilderment in which some people will go astray and others will be guided. So I said: O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, how long will the bewilderment and the occultation be? He said: Six days, or six months, or six years. I said: And will this indeed come to pass? He said: Yes, just as he is created. And how could you grasp this matter, O Aṣbagh? Those are the best of this Ummah together with the best of the righteous of this ʿItrah. I said: Then what will happen after that? He said: Then Allah does whatever He wills, for He has badaʾāt, wills, goals, and endpoints.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan ibn Sadir, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharrabudh, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, we are but like the stars of the sky: whenever one star disappears, another star rises, until when you point with your fingers and crane your necks, Allah will hide your star from you. Then the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib will become alike, and it will not be known which one is from which. So when your star rises, then praise your Lord.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muʿāwiyah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, for al-Qāʾim عليه السلام there shall be a ghaybah (Occultation) before he rises.” I said: “And why?” He عليه السلام said: “Because he fears,” and he gestured with his hand toward his belly, meaning killing.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “If word reaches you about an Occultation concerning the Master of this affair, then do not deny it.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mu‘awiyah, from ‘Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ibrahim ibn Khalaf ibn ‘Abbad al-Anmati, from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar, who said: I was in the presence of Abu ‘Abdillah (عليه السلام), and with him in the house were some people. So I thought that by this he only intended someone other than me. Then he said: “Indeed, by Allah, the Master of this أمر will surely be absent from you, and this matter will surely become obscure until it is said: ‘He died, he perished, in which valley did he go?’ And you will surely be overturned just as a ship is overturned in the waves of the sea. None will be saved except one whose covenant Allah has taken, and in whose heart He has written iman, and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him. And twelve ambiguous banners will surely be raised, such that it will not be known which is which.” He said: So I wept. He said: “What makes you weep, O Abu ‘Abdillah?” I said: “May I be made your ransom, how should I not weep while you are saying: twelve ambiguous banners will be raised, and it will not be known which is which?” He said: And in his gathering there was an opening through which the sun entered. So he said: “Is this clear?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Our matter is clearer than this sun.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Isma‘il Al-Anbari, from Yahya ibn Al-Muthanna, from ‘Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: For Al-Qa'im عليه السلام there are two occultations. During one of them, he attends the seasons, sees the people, and they do not see him.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and another, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, all together from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, from one of the companions of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, among those trusted, that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام spoke these words, and they were preserved from him, and he delivered them from the pulpit of al-Kūfah. O Allah, there must necessarily be for You proofs in Your earth, one proof after another over Your creation, guiding them to Your religion and teaching them Your knowledge, so that the followers of Your friends may not become divided. Whether manifest yet not obeyed, or concealed and awaited—if their persons are absent from the people during the time of their truce, their long-disseminated knowledge is not absent from them, and their teachings are established in the hearts of the believers, and they act by them. And he عليه السلام said in this sermon in another place: In whom would this be? Because of this, knowledge contracts when no bearers are found for it who preserve it and transmit it just as they heard it from the scholars, and who are truthful regarding them in it. O Allah, I surely know that knowledge does not altogether contract, nor are its sources cut off, and that You do not leave Your earth empty of a proof from You over Your creation—either manifest without being obeyed, or fearful and obscured—so that Your proof may not be nullified and Your friends may not go astray after You have guided them. But where are they, and how many are they? They are the fewest in number, the greatest in rank before Allah.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim ibn Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام. Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Say: Have you considered, if your water were to sink away, then who would bring you flowing water? He عليه السلام said: When your Imam is absent from you, then who will come to you with a new Imam?

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “If an occultation reaches you concerning your Master, then do not deny it.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: It is inevitable for the Master of this command to have an Occultation, and it is inevitable for him during his Occultation to have seclusion. Excellent is the dwelling of Ṭaybah, and with thirty there is no loneliness.

And by this chain, from Al-Washsha', from 'Alī ibn Al-Ḥasan, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said: Abū 'Abdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “How will you be when the violent seizure occurs between the two masjids, and knowledge withdraws just as the snake withdraws into its hole, and the Shī'ah differ, and some of them call others liars, and some of them spit in the faces of others?” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, there is no good in that.” So he said to me: “All good is at that time,” three times.

And by this chain, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdِ Allāh عليه السلام saying: ‘Indeed, for al-Qāʾim there shall be a ghaybah before he rises. Indeed, he fears,’ and he gestured with his hand toward his belly, meaning killing.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “For al-Qāʾim there are two occultations: one of them is short, and the other is long. In the first occultation, none knows his place in it except the select among his Shiʿah; and in the other, none knows his place in it except the select among his devotees.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Hassan, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Katheer, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “For the Master of this affair there will be two occultations; during one of them, he will return from it to his family,” “and during the other, it will be said: ‘He perished in whichever valley he travelled in.’” I said: “How should we act when it is like that?” He said: “When a claimant claims it, then ask him about matters; he will answer concerning them like him.”

Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ja‘far ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn al-Waleed al-Khazzaz, from al-Waleed ibn ‘Uqbah, from al-Harith ibn Ziyad, from Shu‘ayb, from Abu Hamza, who said: I entered upon Abu ‘Abdillah (عليه السلام), and I said to him, “Are you the master of this matter?” He said, “No.” I said, “Then your son?” He said, “No.” I said, “Then the son of your son—is it he?” He said, “No.” I said, “Then the son of the son of your son?” He said, “No.” I said, “Who is he?” He said, “The one who will fill it with justice just as it had been filled with ظلم and جور, after an interval among the Imams, just as the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was sent after an interval among the messengers.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar al-Baghdādī, from Wahb ibn Shādhān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Rabīʿ, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Umm Hāniʾ, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “But nay! I swear by the retreating ones, the runners, the hiders.” So he said: “An Imam will go into concealment in the year two hundred and sixty, then he will appear like a meteor, blazing in the dark night.” “So if you reach his time, your eyes will be gladdened.”

Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Usayd ibn Thaʿlabah, from Umm Hāniʾ. She said: I met Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام), and I asked him about this verse. “But nay! I swear by the retreating ones, the runners, the concealers.” He said: “The retreating one is an Imam who goes into concealment in his time, when his knowledge is cut off from the people, in the year two hundred and sixty. Then he will appear like a blazing meteor in the darkness of the night.” “So if you live to see that, your eye will be gladdened.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام, who said: When your knowledge is raised from among you, then expect the relief from beneath your feet.

A number of our companions, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “I hope that you are the Master of this affair, and that Allah will bring it to you without a sword, for allegiance has been pledged to you and the dirhams have been struck in your name.” So he said: “There is none among us to whom letters are directed, who is pointed out with fingers, who is asked about the issues, and to whom wealth is carried, except that he is assassinated or dies upon his bed, until Allah sends for this affair a boy from among us, hidden in birth and upbringing, yet not hidden in his lineage.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad and another, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Mūsā ibn Hilāl al-Kindī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: I said to him: Indeed, your Shiʿah in al-ʿIrāq are many. By Allah, there is none like you among your Ahl al-Bayt, so how is it that you do not rise? He said: O ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAṭāʾ, you have begun spreading your ears for the foolish. Yes, by Allah, I am not your Sahib. He said: I said to him, Then who is our Sahib? He said: Look for the one whose birth is hidden from the people; that one is your Sahib. Indeed, there is no one from us who is pointed at by fingers and chewed by tongues except that he dies in rage or is humiliated.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Al-Qāʾim will rise while there is no covenant upon his neck for anyone, nor any contract, nor any allegiance.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAṭṭār, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Manṣūr, from the one he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I said: When morning and evening come upon me and I do not see an Imam whom I may follow, what should I do? He said: Then love whom you used to love, and hate whom you used to hate, until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, manifests him.

ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Najīḥ, from Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The boy must inevitably have a ghaybah (occultation).” I said, “And why?” He عليه السلام said: “He will fear,” and he gestured with his hand toward his belly. “And he is al-Muntaẓar, and he is the one concerning whose birth people will doubt. So among them are those who will say: ‘A pregnancy’; and among them are those who will say: ‘His father died and left no successor’; and among them are those who will say: ‘He was born two years before his father’s death.’” Zurārah said: So I said, “What do you command me to do if I reach that time?” He عليه السلام said: “Supplicate to Allah with this duʿāʾ:” O Allah, make me know Yourself, for if You do not make me know Yourself, I will not know You. O Allah, make me know Your Prophet, for if You do not make me know Your Prophet, I will never know him. O Allah, make me know Your Ḥujjah, for if You do not make me know Your Ḥujjah, I will go astray from my religion. Aḥmad ibn al-Hilāl said: “I heard this hadith fifty-six years ago.”

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Then when the trumpet is sounded.” He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, from among us is an Imam, victorious and concealed. So when Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, intends to manifest His command, He impresses a mark into his heart; then he appears and rises by the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj, who said: Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) wrote to me: “When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, becomes wrathful with His creation, He removes us from their vicinity.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Salam ibn Abdullah; and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad; and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, all from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Salam ibn Abdullah al-Hashimi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali—and I had heard it from him. From Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: Talha and al-Zubayr sent a man from Abd al-Qays, called Khidash, to Amir al-Mu'minin (صلوات الله عليه), and they said to him: We are sending you to a man whom for long we have known, he and his أهل البيت, for sorcery and soothsaying. You are the most trusted among those with us, more than ourselves, that you will not refrain from that and that you will argue with him on our behalf until you bring him to a known matter. And know that he is the greatest of people in claim, so let that not overcome you regarding him. Among the ways by which he deceives people are food, drink, honey, oil, and being alone with a man. So do not eat his food, do not drink his drink, do not touch his honey or oil, and do not be alone with him. Beware of all of that from him, and set out with the blessing of Allah. When you see him, recite Ayat al-Sukhrah, and seek refuge in Allah from his plot and the plot of Satan. When you sit with him, do not allow him full gaze upon you, and do not feel at ease with him. Then say to him: Your two brothers in religion and your two cousins in kinship adjure you concerning estrangement, and they say to you: Do you not know that we left the people for you and opposed our clans regarding you since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) away? Then when you attained the slightest gain, you neglected our sanctity and cut off our hope. You have seen our actions regarding you, our ability to keep away from you, and the breadth of lands apart from you; and that the one who was turning you away from us and from our connection was less beneficial to you and weaker in defending you than we were. Morning has become clear to one who has two eyes. There has reached us from you violation against us and supplication against us. What is it that impels you to that? We used to see that you were the bravest horseman of the Arabs. Have you made cursing us a religion, and do you think that this will break us away from you? When Khidash came to Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād and Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān all together, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Naṣr ibn Muzāḥim, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Jarrāḥ ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Rāfiʿ ibn Salamah, who said: I was with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ṣalawātu Allāhi ʿalayhi, on the day of al-Nahrawān. While ʿAlī عليه السلام was sitting, a horseman came and said, “Peace be upon you, O ʿAlī.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him, “And upon you be peace. What is the matter with you—may your mother be bereft of you—that you did not greet me as Amīr al-Muʾminīn?” He said, “Yes, I shall inform you about that. I was with you when you were upon the truth at Ṣiffīn. But when you appointed the two arbiters, I dissociated myself from you and called you a mushrik. Then I came to not know where I should direct my wilayah. By Allah, for me to know your guidance from your misguidance is more beloved to me than the world and all that is in it.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him, “May your mother be bereft of you, stand near me and I will show you the signs of guidance from the signs of misguidance.” So the man stood near him. While he was like that, a horseman came galloping until he reached ʿAlī عليه السلام and said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, receive glad tidings of victory. May Allah gladden your eye. By Allah, the people have all been killed.” He said to him, “On this side of the river or beyond it?” He said, “Rather, on this side of it.” He said, “You have lied. By the One who split the grain and created the soul, they will never cross until they are killed.” The man said, “So my insight concerning him increased.” Then another came galloping on his horse and said the like of that to him, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام replied to him with the like of what he had replied to his companion. The doubting man said, “I even thought of charging at ʿAlī عليه السلام and splitting his head with the sword.” Then two horsemen came galloping, their horses drenched in sweat, and they said, “May Allah gladden your eye, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn. Receive glad tidings of victory. By Allah, the people have all been killed.” ʿAlī عليه السلام said, “Was it beyond the river or on this side of it?” They said, “No, rather beyond it. When they drove their horses into al-Nahrawān and the water struck the upper chests of their horses, they turned back and were struck down.” S

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Musa ibn Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-'Ijli, from Ahmad ibn Yahya known as Kurd, from Muhammad ibn Khudahiyy, from Abdullah ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Hashim, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Hababa al-Walibiyya who said: I saw the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) among the elite guard (shurtat al-khamis), and with him was a whip with two tips. He was striking with it the sellers of eel, moray, and catfish (forbidden fish), and saying to them: 'O sellers of the metamorphosed ones of the Children of Israel and the army of the clan of Marwan!' Then Furat ibn Akhnaf stood up toward him and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, and what is the army of the clan of Marwan?' He said: So he said to him: 'Peoples who shaved their beards and twisted their moustaches, so they were transformed.' I had never seen a speaker more eloquent than him. Then I followed him and continued to trail his footsteps until he sat in the open courtyard of the mosque. I said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, what is the sign of the Imamate — may God have mercy on you?' She said: He replied: 'Bring me that pebble,' and he gestured with his hand to a pebble. So I brought it to him, and he imprinted in it with his seal ring. Then he said to me: 'O Hababa! Whenever a claimant claims the Imamate and is able to imprint as you have seen, then know that he is an Imam whose obedience is obligatory; and the Imam — nothing that he wills escapes him.' She said: Then I departed, until the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed away. I came to al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was in the gathering of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the people were asking him. He said: 'O Hababa al-Walibiyya!' I said: 'Yes, my master.' He said: 'Give me what you have.' She said: So I gave it to him, and he imprinted in it just as the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had imprinted. She said: Then I came to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) while he was in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family). He drew me near and welcomed me, then said to me: 'Verily, within the sign there is a proof for what you desire — do you want the sign of the Imamate?' I said: 'Yes, my master.' He said: 'Give me what you have.' So I handed him the pebble, and he imprinted in

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Is'haq ibn Muhammad al-Nakha'i, from Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) when permission was sought for a man from the people of Yemen to see him. So there entered a man who was stout, tall, and large. He greeted him (peace be upon him) with the acknowledgment of wilayah, and he (peace be upon him) responded with acceptance and commanded him to sit. He sat down adjacent to me. I said to myself: 'If only I knew who this person is.' Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'This one is from the descendants of the Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble in which my forefathers (peace be upon them) had imprinted their signet rings and it was engraved. He has come with it, intending that I should imprint (my seal) in it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it here!' So he brought out a pebble, and on one side of it was a smooth surface. Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) took it, then brought out his signet ring and imprinted it therein, and it was engraved.
