It was as though I could see the engraving of his seal ring at that very moment: 'al-Hasan ibn Ali.' Then I said to the Yemeni: 'Had you ever seen him before this?' He said: 'No, by Allah; and I have for a long time been eager to see him, until just now a youth came to me whom I cannot see (anymore), and he said to me: Arise and enter. So I entered.' Then the Yemeni stood up and was saying: 'May Allah's mercy and His blessings be upon you, O People of the Household — a progeny, one from another. I testify by Allah that your right is obligatory, just as the obligation of the right of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the Imams after him — may Allah's salawat be upon them all.' Then he departed, and I did not see him after that. Is'haq said: Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari said: I asked him about his name, and he said: 'My name is Mihja' ibn al-Salt ibn Uqba ibn Sim'an ibn Ghanim, son of Umm Ghanim; and she was the Yemenite Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble in which the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and his descendants had imprinted, up to the time of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda and Zurara together, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya sent to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and secluded himself with him, and said to him: O my nephew! You know that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) handed over the testament and the Imamate after himself to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), then to al-Hasan (peace be upon him), then to al-Husayn (peace be upon him). And your father has been martyrized — may God be pleased with him and bless his soul — and he did not leave a testament. I am your uncle and the equal of your father, and my birth from Ali (peace be upon him), along with my age and my precedence, makes me more deserving of it than you in your youth. So do not dispute with me over the testament and the Imamate, and do not argue with me. So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: O uncle! Fear God and do not claim what is not your right. I admonish you lest you become of the ignorant. Indeed my father, O uncle — may the blessings of God be upon him — bequeathed to me before he set out toward Iraq, and covenanted with me concerning that an hour before he was martyred. These are the weapons of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), with me. So do not expose yourself to this matter, for I fear for you the shortening of your lifespan and the scattering of your affairs. Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, has placed the testament and the Imamate in the posterity of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). If you wish to know that, then let us go to the Black Stone until it arbitrates between us and we ask it about that. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The conversation between the two of them took place in Mecca. Both went until they arrived at the Black Stone. Ali ibn al-Husayn said to Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya: Begin yourself; beseech God, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him to make the Stone speak to you, then question it. So Muhammad beseeched earnestly in supplication and asked God, then called upon the Stone — but it did not answer him. Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: O uncle! Had you been a successor and an Imam, it would have answered you. Muhammad said to him: Then you supplicate to God

Sama‘ah ibn Mihran informed me; he said: Al-Kalbī the genealogist informed me; he said: I entered al-Madinah while knowing nothing of this matter. I came to the mosque, and there was a group from Quraysh there. I said: Tell me about the learned one of the people of this House. They said: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan. So I went to his house and sought permission. A man came out to me, and I thought he was his servant, so I said to him: Seek permission for me to enter upon your master. He went in, then came out and said to me: Enter. I entered, and there was an old man in retreat, intense in exertion. I greeted him, and he said to me: Who are you? I said: I am al-Kalbī the genealogist. He said: What is your need? I said: I have come to ask you. He said: Did you pass by my son Muhammad? I said: I began with you. He said: Ask. So I said: Tell me about a man who says to his wife: You are divorced by the number of the stars of the sky. He said: She becomes separated at the head of al-Jawza’, and the rest is a burden and punishment upon him. I said to myself: One. Then I said: What does the shaykh say regarding wiping over the khuffs? He said: Righteous people have wiped, but we, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not wipe. I said to myself: Two. Then I said: What do you say regarding eating al-jirrī — is it halal or haram? He said: It is halal, except that we, the Ahl al-Bayt, find it repugnant. I said to myself: Three. Then I said: What do you say regarding drinking nabīdh? He said: It is halal, except that we, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not drink it. So I stood and left his presence saying: This group lies against the people of this House. Then I entered the mosque and looked at a group of Quraysh and others from among the people. I greeted them, then said to them: Who is the most learned of the people of this House? They said: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan. I said: I have gone to him, but I found nothing with him. Then a man from the group raised his head and said: Go to Ja‘far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام, for he is the most learned of the people of this House. Some of those present reproached him. I said: Nothing prevented the people from guiding me to him the first time except envy. Then I said to him: Woe to you — he is the one I wanted. So I went until I came to his house and knocked at the door. A servant of his came out and said: Enter, O brother of Kalb. By Allah, that astonished me. I ent

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: We were in al-Madinah after the passing of Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), I and Sahib al-Taq, while the people had gathered around Abdullah ibn Ja'far, considering him the holder of the authority after his father. So we entered upon him, I and Sahib al-Taq, while the people were with him. That was because they had narrated from Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) that he said: the matter is with the eldest so long as there is no defect in him. We entered upon him asking him about what we used to ask his father. So we asked him about zakat, on how much it becomes obligatory. He said: on two hundred, five. We said: then on one hundred? He said: two dirhams and a half. We said: by Allah, the Murji'ah do not even say this. He raised his hand toward the sky and said: by Allah, I do not know what the Murji'ah say. He said: so we left his presence astray, not knowing where to turn, I and Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal. We sat in one of the alleys of al-Madinah, weeping and bewildered, not knowing where to turn or whom to seek. We were saying: to the Murji'ah? to the Qadariyyah? to the Zaydiyyah? to the Mu'tazilah? to the Khawarij? While we were in that state, I saw an old man whom I did not know, gesturing to me with his hand. I feared that he might be one of the spies of Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, for he had spies in al-Madinah watching to see whom the Shi'ah of Ja'far (عليه السلام) agreed upon, so that they might strike his neck. So I feared he was one of them. So I said to al-Ahwal: move away, for I fear for myself and for you. He only intends me and not you, so move away from me lest you perish and help against yourself. So he moved aside, not far away, and I followed the old man, for I thought that I would not be able to escape him. I continued following him, having resolved myself to death, until he brought me to the door of Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام). Then he left me and went away. There was a servant at the door who said to me: enter, may Allah have mercy on you. So I entered, and there was Abu al-Hasan Musa (عليه السلام). He said to me, initiating the speech: not to the Murji'ah, nor to the Qadariyyah, nor to the Zaydiyyah, nor to the Mu'tazilah, nor to the Khawarij; to me, to me. I said: may I be your ransom, your father has passed away? He said: yes. I said: has he passed

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Fulan al-Waqifi, who said: There was a cousin of mine called Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah; he was an ascetic and was among the most devout worshippers of his time. The ruler used to hold him in awe because of his seriousness in religion and his striving; sometimes he would confront the ruler with harsh words, admonishing him, commanding him to good, and forbidding him from evil. The ruler would endure him because of his righteousness. This remained his state until one day Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) came to him while he was in the mosque. He (the Imam) saw him and gestured to him; he came to him. He said to him: 'O Abu Ali! How beloved to me is what you are engaged in, and how it pleases me — except that you have no ma'rifa. So seek the ma'rifa.' He said: 'May I be your ransom! What is ma'rifa?' He said: 'Go and acquire jurisprudential knowledge and seek hadith.' He said: 'From whom?' He said: 'From the jurists of the people of Medina; then present the hadith to me.' He said: So he went and wrote (them) down, then came to him and recited them. He (the Imam) rejected all of it, then said to him: 'Go and attain the true ma'rifa.' The man was deeply concerned about his religion; he did not cease to watch for Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) until he (the Imam) went out to his estate; he met him on the road. He said to him: 'May I be your ransom! I will argue before God with you — guide me to ma'rifa.' He said: So he (the Imam) informed him about the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and what happened after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and informed him about the matter of the two men (Abu Bakr and Umar). He accepted this from him. Then he said to him: 'Who was after the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), then Al-Husayn (peace be upon him),' until he reached himself; then he fell silent. He said: He then said to him: 'May I be your ransom! Who is the Imam today?' He said: 'If I inform you, will you accept?' He said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom!' He said: 'I am he.' He said: 'Is there something I can use as evidence?' He (the Imam) said: 'Go to that tree,' — and he gestured with his hand toward the Umm Ghaylan (a type of acacia tree) — 'and say to it: Musa ibn Ja'far commands you to come forward.' He said

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṭayyib, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Manṣūr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I heard Yaḥyā ibn Aktham, the judge of Sāmarrāʾ, after I had exerted myself with him, debated him, conversed with him, kept company with him, and asked him about the knowledge of the family of Muḥammad. So he said: One day, as I entered circling the grave of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, I saw Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام circling it. So I debated with him regarding questions I had, and he brought them forth to me. Then I said to him: By Allah, I wish to ask you a question, and by Allah, I am ashamed of that. He said to me: I shall inform you before you ask me; you want to ask me about the Imam. I said: By Allah, that is indeed it. He said: I am he. I said: A sign? Then there was a staff in his hand, and it spoke and said: Indeed, my master is the Imam of this time, and he is the Proof.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I entered upon al-Rida عليه السلام while, at that time, I was a Waqifi. My father had asked his father about seven questions, and he answered him concerning six and withheld from the seventh. So I said: “By Allah, I will surely ask him about what my father asked his father; if he answers with the same answer as his father, that will be a proof.” So I asked him, and he answered with the same answer as his father had answered my father regarding the six questions. He did not add to the answer a waw nor a ya, and he withheld from the seventh. And my father had said to his father: “I will contend against you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection that you claimed that Abdullah was not an Imam.” So he placed his hand on his neck, then said to him: “Yes, contend against me with that before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Whatever sin there may be in it is upon my neck.” Then when I bade him farewell, he said: “There is no one among our Shi'a who is afflicted with an affliction or suffers a complaint and is patient upon that, except that Allah writes for him the reward of a thousand martyrs.” So I said to myself: “By Allah, there had been no mention of this.” Then when I went on and was on part of the road, the vein of al-Madini came out in me, and I suffered severe pain from it. Then the following year I performed hajj and entered upon him while some of my pain still remained. I complained to him and said: “May I be made your ransom, seek refuge for my leg,” and I stretched it out before him. He said to me: “There is no harm in this leg of yours, but show me your sound leg.” So I stretched it out before him, and he sought refuge for it. Then when I went out, it was only a short while before the vein came out in me, and its pain was slight.

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Qiyāmā al-Wāsiṭī — and he was from the Wāqifiyyah — who said: I entered upon ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him, "Can there be two Imams?" He said, "No, except that one of them is silent." So I said to him, "Here you are, and there is no silent one for you," and Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام had not yet been born to him. So he said to me, "By Allah, Allah will surely bring forth from me that by which He will establish the truth and its people, and obliterate falsehood and its people." Then after a year, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was born to him. It was then said to Ibn Qiyāmā, "Will this sign not satisfy you?" He said, "Indeed, by Allah, it is surely a tremendous sign, but how am I to deal with what Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said regarding his son?"

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, who said: I came to Khurāsān while I was a Wāqifī. I carried goods with me, and there was with me a patterned cloth in one of the bundles, but I was unaware of it and did not know its location. So when I arrived in Marw and lodged in one of its dwellings, suddenly there was a Madinan man from among its muwallads, and he said to me: Abu al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام says to you: Send to me the patterned cloth that is with you. He said: So I said, Who informed Abu al-Ḥasan of my arrival, when I have only just arrived, and I do not have any patterned cloth with me? So he returned to him and came back to me, and said: He says to you: Yes, it is in such-and-such a place, and its bundle is such-and-such. So I searched for it where he said, and I found it at the bottom of the bundle, and I sent it to him.

Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: I was Waqifī, and I performed hajj in that state. Then when I came to Makkah, something stirred in my chest, so I clung to al-Multazam. Then I said: O Allah, You have indeed known my seeking and my intention, so guide me to the best of religions. Then it occurred within me that I should go to al-Riḍā عليه السلام. So I came to al-Madīnah and stood at his door, and I said to the servant: Tell your master that a man from the people of Iraq is at the door. He said: Then I heard his call while he was saying: Enter, O ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, enter, O ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah. So I entered, and when he looked at me, he said to me: Allah has answered your supplication and guided you to His religion. So I said: I bear witness that you are the hujjah of Allah and His trustee over His creation.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Hulayl used to hold the view regarding ʿAbdullāh. Then he went to al-ʿAskar and retracted from that. So I asked him about the reason for his retraction, and he said: “I presented to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that I should ask him about that. Then he met me in a narrow road and inclined toward me. When he came alongside me, he directed toward me something from his mouth, and it fell upon my chest. I took it, and it was a parchment upon which was written: ‘It was not there, nor was it so.’”

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-'Abbas ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Zayd ibn Musa narrated to me, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: One day Umm Aslam came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, while he was in the house of Umm Salamah. She asked her about the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so she said: He has gone out for some needs, and he will return shortly. She waited for him at Umm Salamah's place until he صلى الله عليه وآله came. Umm Aslam said: May my father and mother be for you, O Messenger of Allah, I have read the books and learned of every Prophet and successor. Musa had a successor in his lifetime and a successor after his death, and likewise 'Isa. So who is your successor, O Messenger of Allah? He said to her: O Umm Aslam, my successor in my lifetime and after my death is one. Then he said to her: O Umm Aslam, whoever performs this act of mine, he is my successor. Then he struck his hand upon a pebble from the ground, rubbed it with his finger until he made it like flour, then kneaded it, then stamped it with his seal, then said: Whoever performs this act of mine, he is my successor in my lifetime and after my death. So I left his presence and went to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and I said: May my father and mother be for you, are you the successor of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله? He said: Yes, O Umm Aslam. Then he struck his hand upon a pebble, rubbed it until he made it like flour, then kneaded it and sealed it with his seal, then said: O Umm Aslam, whoever performs this act of mine, he is my successor. So I left his presence and went to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and I said: May my father and mother be for you, are you the successor of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله? He said: Yes, O Umm Aslam. Then he struck his hand upon a pebble, rubbed it until he made it like flour, then kneaded it and sealed it with his seal, then said: O Umm Aslam, whoever performs this act of mine, he is my successor. Then I went to al-Hasan عليه السلام while he was a boy, and I said to him: O my master, are you the successor of your father? He said: Yes, O Umm Aslam. And he struck with his hand, took a pebble, and did with it like their act. So I left his presence and went to al-Husayn عليه السلام, while I regarded

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Jārūd, from Mūsā ibn Bakr ibn Dāb, from one who narrated it to him, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام came to Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, carrying letters from the people of al-Kūfah, inviting him to themselves, informing him of their gathering, and commanding him to rise. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him: “Are these letters an initiative from them, or a response to what you wrote to them and invited them toward?” He said: “Rather, they are an initiative from the people, because of their recognition of our right, our kinship to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, what they find in the Book of Allah عز وجل regarding the obligation of loving us and the duty of obeying us, and because of the hardship, distress, and affliction in which we are.” Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him: “Obedience is an obligation from Allah عز وجل, and a sunnah (prophetic tradition) that He established among the former ones, and likewise He causes it to proceed among the latter ones. Obedience is to one of us, while love is for all of us. The command of Allah proceeds for His awliyāʾ by a connected judgment, a decisive decree, a determined inevitability, an apportioned measure, and an appointed term at a known time.” “So do not let those who have no certainty make light of you; surely they will never avail you against Allah in anything.” “So do not be hasty, for Allah does not hasten because of the hastening of the servants, and do not try to precede Allah, lest the affliction overpower you and strike you down.” He said: Zayd became angry at that, then said: “The Imam from among us is not one who sits in his house, lets down his curtain, and discourages from jihad, but rather the Imam from among us is one who protects his domain, strives in the way of Allah with the striving due to it, defends his subjects, and guards his sanctuary.” Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “O my brother, do you know within yourself anything of what you have ascribed to it, such that you may bring for it a witness from the Book of Allah, or a proof from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, or set forth an example by it? Allah عز وجل has made halal (permissible) what is halal, made haram (forbidden) what is haram, imposed obligations, set forth parables, and

ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mufaḍḍal, the mawlā of ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, narrated to us, saying: When al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, the one killed at Fakhkh, rose up and took control over al-Madīnah, he called Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar to pledge allegiance. So he came to him, and he said to him: “O son of my uncle, do not burden me with what the son of your uncle burdened your uncle Abā ʿAbdillāh with, lest there come forth from me what I do not want, just as there came forth from Abī ʿAbdillāh what he did not wish.” Al-Ḥusayn said to him: “I have only presented the matter to you; if you want it, you may enter into it, and if you dislike it, I will not compel you to it. And Allah is the One from Whom help is sought.” Then he bade him farewell. So Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar said to him when he bade him farewell: “O son of my uncle, you will indeed be killed, so strike with utmost resolve, for the people are immoral sinners: they display faith and conceal shirk.” And indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we are returning. I reckon your loss with Allah from among a band.” Then al-Ḥusayn went out, and what occurred in his affair occurred; all of them were killed, just as he (عليه السلام) had said.

And by this chain, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Jaʿfarī, who said: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan wrote to Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): As for what follows, I exhort myself to taqwā of Allah, and by it I exhort you, for it is Allah’s counsel to the former ones and His counsel to the later ones. Those who came to me from among Allah’s helpers upon His religion and the spread of His obedience informed me of your tenderness together with your abandonment. I had consulted concerning the call to al-Riḍā from the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), but you concealed it, and your father concealed it before you. Long ago you claimed what was not yours, and extended your hopes toward what Allah did not give you; so you followed desire and led astray. And I am warning you of what Allah warned you against from Himself. So Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) wrote to him: From Mūsā son of Abī ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar and ʿAlī, both sharing in humility before Allah and obedience to Him, to Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥasan. As for what follows, I warn you by Allah and myself, and inform you of the painfulness of His punishment, the severity of His retribution, and the full measure of His vengeance. And I exhort you and myself to taqwā of Allah, for it is the adornment of speech and the stabilization of blessings. Your letter reached me, in which you mention that I am a claimant, and my father before me, though you did not hear that from me. Their testimony will be written and they will be questioned. The greed of this world and its pursuits leaves for its people no pursuit for their Hereafter without corrupting for them the pursuit of their Hereafter within their worldly life. And you mentioned that I held people back from you out of desire for what is in your hands. Had I desired that into which you have entered, what kept me from it would not have been weakness regarding a sunnah nor lack of insight concerning a proof. Rather, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created people as mixed kinds, with differing peculiarities and instincts. So inform me about two expressions that I ask you about: what is al-ʿatraf in your body, and what is al-ṣahlaj in the human being? Then write to me with news of that. I am sending ahead to you a warning against disobeying the caliph, and urging you toward dutifulness and obedience to him, and that you seek safety for yourself before the cla

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all together, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) saying: 'O Thabit, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had appointed a time for this matter in the year seventy. Then, when al-Husayn, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, was killed, the wrath of Allah, Exalted is He, intensified against the people of the earth, so He delayed it until one hundred and forty.' Then we narrated it to you, but you spread the hadith, and so you uncovered the covering of concealment; and after that Allah did not set any time for it with us. And Allah effaces whatever He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Abu Hamza said: 'So I related that to Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), and he said: It had indeed been so.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام) when Mihzam entered upon him and said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, inform me about this matter that we are awaiting—when will it be?” He said: “O Mihzam, the time-setters have lied, the hasty ones are ruined, and the submitting ones are saved.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from his father, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about al-Qāʾim عليه السلام, so he said: “The time-setters have lied. We are a Household who do not set a time.”
Ahmad, by his chain, said: He said: Allah refused except to oppose the timing set by those who fix times.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Khazzāz, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr al-Khathʿamī, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: I said, “Is there a fixed time for this matter?” So he said, “The time-setters have lied, the time-setters have lied, the time-setters have lied.” Indeed, when Mūsā (عليه السلام) went as a delegate to his Lord, he promised them thirty days; then when Allah added ten to the thirty, his people said, “Mūsā has broken his promise to us,” so they did what they did. So when we narrate a hadith to you and it comes to pass in accordance with what we narrated to you, then say, “Allah has spoken the truth.” And when we narrate a hadith to you and it comes contrary to what we narrated to you, then say, “Allah has spoken the truth”; you will be rewarded twice.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from al-Sayyārī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said to me: “The Shiʿah have been nurtured by hopes for two hundred years.” He said: Yaqṭīn said to his son ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, “Why is it that what was said to us happened, while what was said to you did not happen?” He said: So ʿAlī said to him, “What was said to us and to you came from one source, except that your matter became present, so you were given its pure reality, and it occurred just as was said to you. But our matter has not yet arrived, so we were consoled with hopes. If it had been said to us that this matter would not happen until two hundred years or three hundred years, hearts would have hardened and most people would have turned back from Islam. But they said, ‘How swift it is, and how near it is,’ to draw together the hearts of the people and to bring the relief near.” Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim ibn Ismāʿīl al-Anbārī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mihzam, from his father, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: We mentioned in his presence the kings of the family of so-and-so, so he said: “People only perished because of their hastening regarding this matter. Indeed, Allah does not hasten because of the haste of the servants. Surely, for this matter there is an end-point to which it comes; when they reach it, they will neither advance it by an hour nor delay it.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim ibn Ismāʿīl al-Anbārī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mihzam, from his father, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: We mentioned before him the kings of the family of so-and-so, so he said: People have only perished because of their hastening for this matter. Indeed, Allah does not hasten on account of the haste of the servants. Indeed, for this matter there is an end-point to which it will arrive; so if they had reached it, they would neither advance it by an hour nor delay it.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb al-Sarrāj and ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that when Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was given allegiance after the killing of ʿUthmān, he ascended the pulpit and delivered a sermon which he mentioned, saying: In it: “Indeed, your trial has returned to the condition it was in on the day when Allah sent His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.” By the One who sent him with the truth, you will most certainly be thrown into confusion and most certainly be sifted thoroughly, until your lowest become your highest and your highest become your lowest, and those who had lagged behind will surely go ahead, while those who had gone ahead will surely fall behind. By Allah, I did not conceal a mark, nor did I speak a single lie, and I had indeed been informed of this station and this day.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Isma'il al-Anbari, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, from Abi al-Maghra', from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying: “Woe to the tyrants of the Arabs from a matter that has drawn near.” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, how many of the Arabs will be with al-Qa'im?” He said: “A small group.” I said: “By Allah, those among them who speak of this matter are surely many.” He said: “People must inevitably be tested, distinguished, and sifted, and through the sifting many people will be removed.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sayqal, from his father, from Mansur, who said: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said to me: O Mansur, this matter will not come to you except after despair; and no, by Allah, not until you are distinguished; and no, by Allah, not until you are thoroughly tested; and no, by Allah, not until the one who is wretched becomes wretched and the one who is felicitous becomes felicitous.

I heard Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام saying: Alif Lām Mīm. Do the people reckon that they will be left alone to say, “We believe,” while they will not be tested? Then he عليه السلام said to me, “What is the trial?” I said, “May I be sacrificed for you عليه السلام, according to us it is the trial in the religion.” So he عليه السلام said, “They will be tested just as gold is tested.” Then he عليه السلام said, “They will be purified just as gold is purified.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Sulaymān ibn Ṣāliḥ, raising it, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, this hadith of yours causes the hearts of men to shrink in aversion from it. So whoever acknowledges it, then increase him in it; and whoever denies it, then leave him. It is inevitable that there will be a tribulation in which every close insider and confidant will fall, until even the one who splits a hair with two hairs falls in it, until none remain except us and our Shiʿah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and ʿAli ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Sayqal, from his father, who said: I, al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah, and a group of our companions were sitting, while Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام was listening to our conversation, so he said to us: “What matter are you engaged in?” Far be it, far be it! No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until you are sifted. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until you are thoroughly tested. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until you are distinguished from one another. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass except after despair. No, by Allah, what you are stretching your eyes toward will not come to pass until the one who is to be wretched becomes wretched, and the one who is to be felicitous becomes felicitous.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Recognize your Imam, for when you have recognized him, it will not harm you whether this matter comes earlier or is delayed.”

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. “The Day We shall call every people by their Imam.” So he said: “O Fuḍayl, know your Imam, for when you know your Imam, it will not harm you whether this matter comes sooner or is delayed. And whoever knows his Imam, then dies before the Master of this matter rises, is at the rank of one who was sitting in his army—rather, at the rank of one who sat beneath his banner.” He said: “And some of his companions said: at the rank of one who was martyred with Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله.” Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), ‘May I be sacrificed for you; when will the relief be?’ So he said, ‘O Abu Basir, are you among those who desire the world? Whoever recognizes this matter has already been granted relief through awaiting it.’

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja‘far ibn Bashir, from Isma‘il ibn Muhammad al-Khuza‘i, who said: Abu Basir asked Aba ‘Abd Allah عليه السلام while I was listening, and he said: “Do you think I will reach al-Qa’im عليه السلام?” He said: “O Abu Basir, do you not know your Imam?” He said: “Yes, by Allah, and you are he,” and he took his hand. So he said: “By Allah, O Abu Basir, it will not matter to you if you are not sitting with your sword in the shade of the portico of al-Qa’im, may the blessings of Allah be upon him.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying: Whoever dies while not having an Imam, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah. And whoever dies while knowing his Imam, it will not harm him whether this matter comes sooner or is delayed. And whoever dies while knowing his Imam is like one who is with al-Qāʾim in his tent.

Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-'Alawi, from Sahl ibn Jumhur, from 'Abd al-'Azim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hasani, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-'Urani, from 'Ali ibn Hashim, from his father, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: It would not harm the one who dies awaiting our matter that he did not die in the midst of the tent of al-Mahdi and his army.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUmar ibn Abān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Recognize the sign; then when you recognize him, it will not harm you whether this matter comes earlier or is delayed.” Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “The Day We shall call every people by their Imam.” So whoever recognizes his Imam is like one who is in the camp of al-Muntaẓar (عليه السلام).

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abū Sallām, from Sowrat ibn Kuleyb, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And on the Day of Judgment you will see those who lied against Allah—their faces will be blackened. He عليه السلام said: One who says, "I am an Imam," while he is not an Imam. He said: I said, "Even if he were an ʿAlawī?" He عليه السلام said: "Even if he were an ʿAlawī." I said, "Even if he were from the descendants of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام?" He عليه السلام said: "Even if he were."

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Whoever claims the Imamate while he is not from its rightful people, then he is a disbeliever.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhūr, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtār, who said: I said to Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام): “May I be made your ransom.” “And on the Day of qiyamah you will see those who lied against Allah.” He (عليه السلام) said: “Everyone who claims that he is an Imam while he is not an Imam.” I said: “Even if he were a Fāṭimī and an ‘Alawī?” He (عليه السلام) said: “Even if he were a Fāṭimī and an ‘Alawī.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Dāwūd al-Ḥammār, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: ‘There are three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: one who claims an Imamate from Allah which does not belong to him, one who rejects an Imam from Allah, and one who alleges that those two have a share in Islam.’

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Yahya, the brother of Udaym, from al-Walid ibn Subayh, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: "Indeed, this matter is not claimed by anyone other than its rightful owner except that Allah cuts off his life."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever associates, alongside an Imam whose Imamate is from Allah, one whose Imamate is not from Allah, has committed shirk with Allah.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام): A man said to me: Recognize the last of the Imams, and it will not harm you that you do not recognize the first. He said: So he said: May Allah curse this one, for I hate him and do not recognize him. And can the last be recognized except by the first?

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, who said: I asked the Shaykh about the Imams, peace be upon them. He said: Whoever denies one of the living ones has indeed denied the departed ones.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Abī Wahb, from Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr, who said: I asked him عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And when they commit an immorality, they say: We found our fathers upon it, and Allah has commanded us to it. Say: Surely Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know? He said: So he عليه السلام said: Have you ever seen anyone who claimed that Allah commanded adultery, drinking wine, or anything from these prohibitions? So I said: No. He عليه السلام said: Then what is this immorality which they claim Allah commanded them with? I said: Allah and His Guardian know best. He عليه السلام said: This concerns the Imams of tyranny: they claimed that Allah commanded the people to follow a people whom Allah had not commanded them to follow. So Allah refuted that against them, informed that they had spoken a lie against Him, and named that from them an immorality.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Abī Wahb, from Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr, who said: I asked a righteous servant about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, those of them that are outward and those that are inward.” He said: So he said, “Indeed, the Qur’an has an outward and an inward. Thus, everything that Allah has forbidden in the Qur’an is the outward, and the inward of that is the Imams of tyranny. And everything that Allah, Exalted is He, has made lawful in the Book is the outward, and the inward of that is the Imams of truth.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAmr ibn Thābit, from Jābir, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And from the people are those who take peers besides Allah; they love them as the love of Allah.” He said: “By Allah, they are the associates of so-and-so and so-and-so; they took them as Imams besides the Imam whom Allah made an Imam for the people.” “So for that reason He said: ‘And if those who were unjust could but see, when they see the punishment, that all strength belongs to Allah altogether, and that Allah is severe in punishment. When those who were followed disown those who followed them, and they see the punishment, and the ties between them are cut off. And those who followed will say: If only we had another return, then we would disown them as they have disowned us. Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they shall not exit from the Fire.’” Then Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “By Allah, O Jābir, they are the Imams of oppression and their followers.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Dāwūd al-Mustariqq, from ʿAlī ibn Maymūn, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: Three people—Allah will not look toward them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: one who claims an Imamate from Allah that does not belong to him; one who denies an Imam from Allah; and one who alleges that both of them have a share in Islam.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, regarding the saying: of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah?” He عليه السلام said: “It means one who takes his opinion as his religion without an Imam from the Imams of guidance.”

Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A‘ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) saying: Every one who professes the religion of Allah through worship, exerting himself in it, while there is no Imam for him from Allah, then his striving is not accepted, and he is astray and confused, and Allah disdains his deeds. His likeness is the likeness of a sheep that has strayed from its shepherd and its flock. So it rushes about, going and coming throughout its day. Then when the night covers it, it sees a flock with a shepherd other than its own. It inclines toward it and is deceived by it, so it spends the night with it in its fold. Then when the shepherd drives his flock on, it does not recognize its shepherd and its flock, so it rushes about in confusion seeking its shepherd and its flock. Then it sees sheep with their shepherd, inclines toward them, and is deceived by them. So the shepherd cries out to it: Join your own shepherd and your flock, for you are wandering, confused, away from your shepherd and your flock. So it rushes off frightened, confused, and scattered, with no shepherd to guide it to its pasture or return it. While it is in that state, the wolf seizes the opportunity of its isolation and devours it. Likewise, by Allah, O Muhammad, whoever from this community begins the day without an Imam from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, manifest and just, begins the day astray and wandering; and if he dies in that state, he dies a death of disbelief and hypocrisy. And know, O Muhammad, that the imams of tyranny and their followers are surely removed from the religion of Allah. They have gone astray and led others astray. So their deeds which they do are like ashes upon which the wind blows fiercely on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they earned. That is the far error.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh (عليه السلام): “I mix with the people, and I often find myself amazed at some people who do not hold your wilayah and instead follow so-and-so and so-and-so, yet they possess trustworthiness, truthfulness, and loyalty; and there are other people who hold your wilayah, but they do not possess that trustworthiness, loyalty, or truthfulness.” He said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh (عليه السلام) sat upright and turned toward me as one angered, then said: “There is no religion for one who worships Allah through the wilayah of a tyrannical Imam who is not from Allah, and there is no blame upon one who follows the wilayah of a just Imam from Allah.” I said: “There is no religion for those, and there is no blame upon these?” He said: “Yes, there is no religion for those, and there is no blame upon these.” Then he said: “Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ‘Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light’?” It means: from the darknesses of sins to the light of tawbah and forgiveness, because of their wilayah toward every just Imam from Allah. And He said: ‘As for those who disbelieve, their guardians are the ṭāghūt; they bring them out of the light into the darknesses.’ What is meant by this is that they had been upon the light of Islam; then when they took the wilayah of every tyrannical Imam who was not from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, they departed by that allegiance to him from the light of Islam into the darknesses of disbelief. So Allah made the Fire incumbent upon them along with the disbelievers: ‘Those are the companions of the Fire; they shall remain therein forever.’

And from him, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Ḥabīb al-Sijistānī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “I shall surely punish every community in Islam that professes the wilayah of every unjust Imam who is not from Allah, even if the community is righteous and pious in its deeds. And I shall surely pardon every community in Islam that professes the wilayah of every just Imam from Allah, even if the community is unjust and sinful within itself.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Jumhūr, from his father, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to punish a community that has adopted as its religion allegiance to an Imam who is not from Allah, even if it is righteous and Godwary in its deeds. And indeed, Allah is surely ashamed to punish a community that has adopted as its religion allegiance to an Imam from Allah, even if it is unjust and evil-doing in its deeds.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said: One day Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام began with us and said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Whoever dies while there is no Imam over him, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah. So I said: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say that? He said: Yes, by Allah, he indeed said it. I said: So everyone who dies while there is no Imam for him, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah? He said: Yes.

ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about the statement of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله): “Whoever dies while he has no Imam, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah.” He said. I said, “A death of kufr?” He said, “A death of misguidance.” I said, “So whoever dies today while he has no Imam, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah?” So he said, “Yes.”

Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān, from al-Fuḍayl, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said, “Whoever dies not knowing his Imam, dies a death of Jāhiliyyah”? He said: “Yes.” I said: “A blind Jāhiliyyah of ignorance, or a Jāhiliyyah of not knowing his Imam?” He said: “A Jāhiliyyah of kufr, nifaq, and misguidance.”

Some of our companions, from ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī, from Mālik ibn ʿĀmir, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Zāʾidah, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: Whoever practices religion toward Allah without hearing from a truthful one, Allah will inevitably bind him to hardship; and whoever claims hearing from other than the door which Allah has opened, then he is a mushrik, and that is the trusted door over the hidden secret of Allah.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far, who said: I heard al-Rida عليه السلام saying: Indeed, Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, and his wife and his sons, are among the people of Paradise. Then he عليه السلام said: Whoever recognizes this matter from the children of Ali and Fatimah عليها السلام is not like the people.

Al-Washshā' narrated to me, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar al-Ḥallāl narrated to us, saying: I said to Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام): Inform me about the one from the children of Fāṭimah who opposes you and does not recognize your right—would he and the rest of the people be equal in punishment? He said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) used to say: Upon them is a double punishment.

ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Mīthamī narrated to us. He said: Ribʿī ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated to us. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh said to me: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Is the one who denies this matter, from Banī Hāshim and from others, the same?” So he said to me: “Do not say ‘the denier’; rather say ‘the rejecter,’ from Banī Hāshim and from others.” Abū al-Ḥasan said: “So I reflected upon it, and I remembered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding the brothers of Yūsuf:” “So he recognized them, while they were to him unrecognizing.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, who said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him: “Is the denier from among you and from among others the same?” So he said: “The denier from among us has two sins, and the one who does good has two good deeds.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “When an event occurs to the Imam عليه السلام, how should the people act?” He عليه السلام said: “Where is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?” “Why should not, then, a group from every party among them go forth, so that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious?” He عليه السلام said: “They are excused as long as they are engaged in seeking, and those who are waiting for them are also excused until their companions return to them.”

Ḥammād narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about the saying of the general Muslims: that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said, “Whoever dies while he has no Imam dies a death of Jāhiliyyah.” So he said: “It is true, by Allah.” I said: “If an Imam dies and a man in Khurāsān does not know who his successor is, does that excuse him?” He said: “It does not excuse him. When the Imam dies, the proof of his successor falls upon those who are with him in the town, and the duty of setting out belongs to those who are not in his presence when the news reaches them.” Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “So why should not a group from every party among them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware?” I said: “If a group sets out and some of them die before arriving and coming to know?” He said: “Allah, Majestic and Mighty, says:” “And whoever goes forth from his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah.” I said: “If some of them reach the town and find your door closed to you and your curtain let down, while you do not call them to yourself, and there is no one to direct them to you, then by what would they recognize that?” He said: “By the revealed Book of Allah.” I said: “How does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say it?” He said: “I see that you have spoken about this before today.” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Then recall what Allah revealed concerning ʿAlī (عليه السلام), what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said to him concerning al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn (عليهما السلام), what Allah singled ʿAlī (عليه السلام) out with, and what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said regarding him from his bequest to him and his appointment of him, what would happen to them, the acknowledgment of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn of that, his bequest to al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn’s submission to him by the word of Allah:” “The Prophet has a greater claim over the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers; and those of kinship, some of them have a greater claim over others in the Book of Allah.” I said: “The people have spoken regarding Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), and they say: how did it pass over, among the sons of his father, one who had kinship li

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “May Allah keep you well. News of your illness has reached us and we have become apprehensive, so if only you would inform us or teach us.” He said: “Ali عليه السلام was knowledgeable, and knowledge is inherited. Thus no knowledgeable one perishes except that there remains after him one who knows the like of his knowledge, or whatever Allah wills.” I said: “Is there then any leeway for the people, when the knowledgeable one dies, not to recognize the one after him?” He said: “As for the people of this city, no”—meaning al-Madinah—“but as for other towns, then according to the extent of their travel.” Indeed, Allah says: “And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a group from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware?” He said: I said, “What do you say about one who dies during that?” He said: “He is in the position of one who leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then death overtakes him; his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah.” He said: I said, “Then when they arrive, by what thing do they recognize their master?” He said: “He is granted tranquillity, dignity, and awe.”

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, regarding the Word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'How will it be when We bring from every community a witness, and bring you as a witness against them?' He said: 'It was revealed specifically regarding the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). In every generation of them there is an Imam from us as a witness over them, and Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is a witness over us.'

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: And thus We made you a middle nation so that you may be witnesses over the people [2:143] He said: 'We are the middle nation, and we are the witnesses of God over His creation and His proofs on His earth.' I said: 'the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: the religion of your father Ibrahim [22:78].' He said: 'He meant us specifically. He named you all Muslims from before in the books that have passed and in this Quran, so that the Messenger may be a witness over you.' Thus the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the witness over us with what he conveyed to us from God, Mighty and Majestic, and we are the witnesses over the people. So whoever ratifies the truth, we shall ratify him on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever denies the truth, we shall belie him on the Day of Resurrection.

And by this chain, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'So is he who was upon a clear proof from his Lord and a witness from Him follows it' [11:17] So he said: Amir al-Mu'minin, may God's blessings be upon him, is the witness over the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was upon a clear proof from his Lord.

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) [about] the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'And thus We made you a middle nation so that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you.' He said: 'We are the middle nation, and we are the witnesses of God, Blessed and Exalted, over His creation, and His proofs on His earth.' I said [about] His words, the Exalted: 'O you who believe! Bow down and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good that you may succeed, and strive hard in (the way of) God with a striving which is due to Him; He has chosen you.' He said: 'It means us, and we are the chosen ones, and God, Blessed and Exalted, has not placed in the religion any hardship — for hardship is more severe than constriction — the religion of your father Ibrahim: it means us in particular, and He named you all as Muslims.' God named us as Muslims from before, in the scriptures that have passed and in this Quran, 'so that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people.' Thus, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the witness over us with what he conveyed to us from God, Blessed and Exalted; and we are the witnesses over the people. So whoever ratifies on the Day of Resurrection, we shall ratify him; and whoever denies, we shall deny him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, from Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of God upon him) who said: Indeed, God — Blessed and Exalted — has purified us and protected us ('isma), and made us witnesses over His creatures, and His divine authority (hujja) in His earth, and made us [to be] with the Quran, and made the Quran [to be] with us — we do not separate from it, and it does not separate from us.

Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Jareer al-Qummi, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: “May I be sacrificed for you, you have known my devotion to your father, then to you. Then I swore to him, by the right of Rasool Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the right of so-and-so and so-and-so, until I ended with him, that whatever you inform me of will not go out from me to anyone among the people.” And I asked him about his father: “Is he alive or dead?” So he said: “By Allah, he has died.” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, your Shi'a narrate that in him is the sunnah of four Prophets.” He said: “By Allah, other than Whom there is no god, he has perished.” I said: “A perishing of occultation or a perishing of death?” He said: “A perishing of death.” So I said: “Perhaps you are practicing taqiyyah with me.” He said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “Did he appoint you by وصية?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Did he include anyone with you in it?” He said: “No.” I said: “Is there an Imam over you from among your brothers?” He said: “No.” I said: “So you are the Imam?” He said: “Yes.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “A man alluded to your brother Ibrāhīm and mentioned to him that your father is alive, and that you know of that what he knows.” So he عليه السلام said: “Glory be to Allah! Does the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله pass away, yet Mūsā عليه السلام does not pass away? By Allah, he has indeed passed away just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله passed away. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, ever since He took His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, has continually bestowed this religion upon the children of the non-Arabs and turned it away from the relatives of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, one after another; so He gives to these and withholds from those.” I certainly paid on his behalf, at the beginning of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, one thousand dīnars after he had nearly proceeded to divorce his wives and free his slaves. But you have indeed heard what Yūsuf faced from his brothers.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, who said: I said to Abī Al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام): “They have narrated from you concerning the death of Abī Al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) that a man said to you: ‘You came to know that through the statement of Sa‘īd.’ So he said: ‘Sa‘īd came after I had known of it, before his coming.’” He said: “And I heard him saying: ‘I divorced Umm Farwah bint Isḥāq in Rajab, one day after the death of Abī Al-Ḥasan.’ I said: ‘You divorced her while you had known of the death of Abī Al-Ḥasan?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ I said: ‘Before Sa‘īd came to you?’ He said: ‘Yes.’”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, who said: I said to al-Rida عليه السلام, "Inform me about the Imam: when does he know that he is an Imam—when news reaches him that his companion has passed away, or when he actually passes away? For example, Abu al-Hasan was taken in Baghdad while you are here?" He عليه السلام said, "He knows that when his companion passes away." I said, "By what means?" He عليه السلام said, "Allah inspires him."

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū al-Faḍl al-Shahbānī, from Hārūn ibn al-Faḍl, who said: I saw Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام on the day in which Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام passed away. So he said: “Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return.” Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام has passed away. So it was said to him: “And how did you know?” He said: “Because a humbleness before Allah entered into me that I had not known before.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musafir, who said: Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when he was taken away (to be imprisoned), commanded Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) to sleep at his door every night for as long as he was alive, until his news would come to him. He (Musafir) said: Every night we would spread a bed for Abu al-Hasan in the corridor, then he would come after the Isha prayer and sleep. When morning came, he would leave to his house. He said: He continued in this state for four years. Then when it was one of the nights, he was delayed from us, and the bed had been spread for him but he did not come as he used to. The household became apprehensive and frightened, and a great matter befell us due to his delay. When it was the next morning, he came to the house and entered to the family and went to Umm Ahmad and said to her: 'Bring what my father entrusted to you.' She shrieked and slapped her face and tore her collar and said: 'By Allah, my Master has died!' He stopped her and said to her: 'Do not speak of anything nor make it known until the news reaches the governor.' Then she brought out to him a chest and two thousand dinars, or four thousand dinars, and handed all of that over to him alone, not to others. And she said: 'He had said to me privately' — and she was beloved in his presence — 'Guard this trust with you and do not inform anyone of it until I die. Then when I pass away, whoever from my children comes to you and asks for it, hand it over to him, and know that I have died.' 'And by Allah, the sign of my Master has come to me.' So he took possession of that from her and commanded all of them to keep silent until the news arrived, and he left. He did not return to anything of the overnight sleeping as he used to do. And it was not long — only a few days — until there came the sealed letter with news of his passing. So we counted the days and examined the time, and it was so that he had died at the very moment when Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did what he did — staying away from the nightly sleeping and taking possession of what he took.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Yazīd al-Kunāsī, who said: I asked Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), “Was ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (عليه السلام), when he spoke in the cradle, the hujjah of Allah over the people of his time?” He said, “On that day he was a Prophet, the hujjah of Allah, though not sent as a messenger. Do you not hear his statement when he said:” “Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a Prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me salat and zakat as long as I remain alive.” I said, “So on that day, in that state while he was in the cradle, was he a hujjah of Allah over Zakariyyā?” He said, “In that state, ʿĪsā was a sign for the people and a mercy from Allah for Maryam when he spoke and spoke on her behalf. He was a Prophet, a hujjah over those who heard his speech in that condition. Then he became silent and did not speak until two years had passed for him, and Zakariyyā was the hujjah of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over the people after the silence of ʿĪsā for those two years.” Then Zakariyyā died, and his son Yaḥyā inherited from him the Book and the wisdom while he was a small child. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “O Yaḥyā, hold fast to the Book with strength,” and “We gave him judgment while still a child.” So when ʿĪsā (عليه السلام) reached seven years of age, he spoke with prophethood and messengership when Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him. Thus ʿĪsā became the hujjah over Yaḥyā and over all the people. And the earth, O Abū Khālid, does not remain even for a single day without a hujjah of Allah over the people, ever since the day Allah created Ādam (عليه السلام) and settled him on the earth.” So I said, “May I be made your ransom, was ʿAlī (عليه السلام) a hujjah from Allah and His Messenger over this Ummah during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?” He said, “Yes—on the day he established him for the people, set him up as a banner, called them to his wilayah, and commanded them to obey him.” I said, “And was obedience to ʿAlī (عليه السلام) obligatory upon the people during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and after his passing?” He said, “Yes, but he remained silent and did not speak alongside the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه و

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I said to al-Rida عليه السلام: We used to ask you, before Allah had granted Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام to you, and you would say: Allah will grant me a boy. Now Allah has indeed granted him to you, and our eyes have been delighted. May Allah not show us your day; but if an event should occur, then to whom? So he gestured with his hand toward Abi Ja‘far عليه السلام, while he was standing before him. So I said: May I be your ransom, this is a son of three years? He said: And what harm is there to him in that? Isa عليه السلام stood with the Divine Proof while he was a son of three years.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Sayf, from one of our companions, from Abu Ja‘far al-Thani عليه السلام, who said: I said to him عليه السلام: “They are speaking about the youth of your age.” So he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dawud that he should appoint Sulayman as the khalifah, while he was a young boy tending sheep. So the worshippers of the Children of Israel and their scholars objected to that. Then Allah revealed to Dawud عليه السلام: ‘Take the staffs of those speaking and the staff of Sulayman, and place them in a house, and seal them with the seals of the people. Then when the next day comes, whichever staff has put forth leaves and borne fruit, he is the khalifah.’” So Dawud informed them, and they said: “We are satisfied, and we submit.”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and another, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Muṣʿab, from Masʿadah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Abū Baṣīr said: I entered upon him, and with me was a boy guiding me, five years old, who had not reached puberty. So he said to me: How will you be when argument is made against you by one of the like of his age? Or he said: One of the like of his age will assume authority over you.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi' who said: I asked him, meaning Aba Ja'far عليه السلام, about something from the matter of the Imam, and I said: 'Can the Imam be a son less than seven years old?' So he said: 'Yes, and even less than five years old.' So Sahl said: 'Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated this to me in the year two hundred and twenty-one.'

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Khayrānī, from his father, who said: I was standing before Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in Khurāsān, when someone said to him, "O my master, if an event should occur, then to whom [shall we turn]?" He said, "To Abī Jaʿfar, my son." Then it was as though the questioner considered the age of Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام too small, so Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said, "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام as a Messenger, a Prophet, and the possessor of an initiated law, at an age younger than that in which Abū Jaʿfar is."

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said: I saw Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), and he had come out to me. So I began looking at him, and I continued to look at his head and his feet so that I might describe his stature to our companions in Miṣr. While I was like that, he sat down and said: O ʿAlī, indeed Allah has argued concerning the Imamate with the like of that by which He argued concerning prophethood, so He said: And We gave him judgment while yet a child. And when he reached his maturity and reached forty years. So it is permissible that wisdom be given to one while he is a child, and it is permissible that it be given to him while he is a son of forty years.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, said: ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): “O my master, the people object to you because of your young age.” So he said: “And what is it that they object to in that? The statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has indeed said to His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم):” “Say: This is my way; I call to Allah with insight, I and whoever follows me.” “So by Allah, none followed him except ʿAlī (عليه السلام), and he was nine years old, and I am a son of nine years.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar al-Ḥallāl, or someone else, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: I said to him: They argue against us, saying: None washes the Imam except the Imam. So he said: How would they know who washed him? Then what did you say to them? He said: So I said: May I be your ransom, I said to them: If my master says that he washed him beneath the Throne of my Lord, then he has spoken the truth; and if he says that he washed him in the far regions of the earth, then he has spoken the truth. He said: Not like this. He said: So I said: Then what should I say to them? He said: Say to them: I washed him. So I said: Shall I say to them that you washed him? He said: Yes.
Abu Maʿmar narrated to us; he said: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the Imam being washed by the Imam. He said: “It is the sunnah (tradition) of Mūsā ibn ʿImrān عليه السلام.”

And from him, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Yūnus, from Ṭalḥah, who said: I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام, “Indeed, the Imam is not washed except by the Imam.” So he said, “Do you not know who was present for his washing? Those who attended it were better than those who were absent from it.” Those who were present with Yūsuf in the well when his parents and his household were absent from him.”

We performed hajj with Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) in the year in which his son Mūsā (عليه السلام) was born. When we encamped at al-Abwāʾ, he set out lunch for us, and whenever he placed food for his companions, he would make it more abundant and better. He said: While we were eating, a messenger from Ḥamīdah came to him and said: Ḥamīdah says, “I feel the change in myself, and I have found what I used to find when my delivery approached, and you instructed me not to precede you regarding this son of yours.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) arose and went with the messenger. When he returned, his companions said to him: May Allah gladden you, and may we be your ransom; what happened with Ḥamīdah? He said: Allah kept her safe and has granted me a غلام, and he is the best of those whom Allah created among His creation. Ḥamīdah informed me about him with a matter she thought I did not know, while I knew it better than she did. I said: May I be your ransom, what was it that Ḥamīdah informed you about him? He said: She mentioned that when he came forth from her womb, he came forth placing his hands upon the earth and raising his head toward the sky. So I informed her that this is the sign of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the sign of the waṣī after him. I said: May I be your ransom, how is this among the signs of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the sign of the waṣī after him? He said to me: When it was the night on which my grandfather was conceived, a visitor came to my father’s grandfather with a cup containing a drink thinner than water, softer than butter, sweeter than honey, colder than ice, and whiter than milk. He gave it to him to drink and instructed him to have intercourse. So he rose, had intercourse, and my grandfather was conceived. Then when it was the night on which my father was conceived, a visitor came to my grandfather and gave him to drink just as he had given my father’s grandfather to drink, and instructed him with the like of what he had instructed him. So he rose, had intercourse, and my father was conceived. And when it was the night on which I was conceived, a visitor came to my father and gave him to drink what he had given them, and instructed him with what he had instructed them. So he rose, had intercourse, and I was conceived. And when it was the night on which my son was conceived, a visitor came to m

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying: "Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He loves to create the Imam, He commands an angel. So he takes a drink from water beneath the Throne and gives it to his father to drink. From that the Imam is created. Then he remains for forty days and nights in the womb of his mother, not hearing sound; then after that he hears speech." So when he is born, that angel is sent and writes between his eyes: "And the Word of your Lord has been completed in truth and justice; there is none who can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." Then when the Imam who was before him passes away, a beacon of light is raised for this one by which he looks upon the deeds of the creatures. By this Allah establishes the proof against His creation.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends to create the Imam from the Imam, He sends an angel. So he takes a draught from water beneath the Throne, then casts it, or delivers it, to the Imam, and he drinks it. Then he remains in the womb for forty days, not hearing speech; then after that he hears speech. Then when his mother gives birth to him, Allah sends to him that angel who took the draught, and he writes upon his right upper arm:” “And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; there is none to alter His words.” Then when he rises with this matter, Allah raises for him in every town a beacon by which he looks upon the deeds of the servants.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Muḥammad al-Muslī, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, the Imam hears in the belly of his mother.” So when he is born, it is inscribed between his shoulders: “And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; there is none who can alter His Words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.” Then when the command comes to him, Allah makes for him a pillar of light by which he sees what the people of every town are doing.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Ibn Mas‘ūd, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja‘farī, who said: I heard Isḥāq ibn Ja‘far saying: I heard my father saying: The awṣiyāʾ, when their mothers conceive them, she is overcome by a period resembling a fainting spell. She remains in that state for that day if it is daytime, or for that night if it is nighttime. Then she sees in her sleep a man giving her glad tidings of a knowledgeable, forbearing boy, and she rejoices because of that. She awakens from her sleep and hears from her right side, at the side of the house, a voice saying: You have conceived with خير, you will proceed to خير, and you have come with خير. Receive glad tidings of a forbearing, knowledgeable boy. She then feels lightness in her body, and after that she no longer finds heaviness in her sides and belly. When she reaches the ninth month, she hears an intense sound in the house. Then on the night in which she gives birth, a light appears to her in the house that she sees, and none sees it besides her except his father.
