Then when she gives birth to him, she gives birth to him seated, and she opens for him until he emerges cross-legged. After falling to the ground, he turns so that his face does not miss the qiblah wherever it may be. Then he sneezes three times, gesturing with his finger in praise, and he falls with the umbilical cord cut and circumcised, with his four incisors above and below, his canines, and his molars. Between his hands there is a light like a bar of gold, and throughout his day and night his hands flow with gold. Thus also are the Prophets when they are born, and the awṣiyāʾ are but offshoots from the Prophets.

More than one of our companions reported that he said: Do not speak regarding the Imam, for the Imam hears the speech while he is in the belly of his mother. Then when she gives birth to him, the angel writes between his eyes: And the Word of your Lord has been completed in truth and justice; there is none to alter His Words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing. Then when he rises with the Command, a beacon is raised for him in every town, from which he looks upon the deeds of the servants.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, who said: I and Ibn Faḍḍāl were sitting when Yūnus approached and said: “I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him, ‘May I be your ransom, the people have spoken much about the pillar.’” He said: “So he said to me, ‘O Yūnus, what do you think it is? Do you regard it as a pillar of iron raised for your companion?’” He said: “I said, ‘I do not know.’” He said: “‘Rather, it is an angel entrusted with every city; Allah raises the deeds of that city by means of him.’” He said: “Then Ibn Faḍḍāl stood, kissed his head, and said, ‘May Allah have mercy on you, O Abū Muḥammad. You never cease bringing the true hadith through which Allah relieves us.’”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: The Imam has ten signs: he is born purified and circumcised; when he falls upon the ground, he falls upon the palms of his hands, raising his voice with the two testimonies; he does not become junub; his eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep; he neither yawns nor stretches; he sees from behind him just as he sees from before him; his excretion has the fragrance of musk, and the earth is entrusted with concealing and swallowing it; when he wears the armor of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), it fits him exactly, and if someone else among the people, tall or short, wears it, it exceeds him by a handspan; and he is one who is spoken to until his days come to an end.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah created us from ʿIlliyyīn, and He created our souls from above that, and He created the souls of our Shi'a from ʿIlliyyīn, and He created their bodies from below that. So because of that, there is kinship between us and them, and their hearts yearn toward us.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb, from ʿImrān ibn Isḥāq al-Zaʿfarānī, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: “Indeed, Allah created us from the light of His magnificence, then He formed our creation from treasured, concealed clay from beneath the Throne. Then He settled that light within it, so we became a creation and luminous human beings. He did not grant anyone any share in the like of that from which He created us.” And He created the souls of our Shiʿah from our clay, and their bodies from treasured, concealed clay lower than that clay. And Allah did not grant anyone any share in the like of that from which He created them, except the Prophets. Therefore, we and they became the people, while the rest of the people became rabble for the Fire, and unto the Fire.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and another, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, who raised it to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, Allah has a river beneath His Throne, and beneath the river that is beneath His Throne is a light which He illuminated; and indeed, on the two banks of the river are two created spirits: Rūḥ al-Qudus and a spirit from His command. And indeed, Allah has ten clays: five from Paradise and five from the earth; then he explained the gardens and he explained the earth. Then he said: There is no Prophet nor Angel after that whom He formed except that He breathed into him from one of the two spirits, and He made the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) from one of the two clays. I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal (عليه السلام): What is al-jabl? He said: The creation other than us, the Ahl al-Bayt; for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created us from the ten clays and breathed into us from both spirits together, so how excellent its fragrance is. And another narrated from Abū al-Ṣāmit, who said: The clay of the gardens is Jannat ʿAdn, Jannat al-Maʾwā, Jannat al-Naʿīm, al-Firdaws, and al-Khuld; and the clay of the earth is Makkah, al-Madīnah, al-Kūfah, Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Ḥāʾir.

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to me, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed Allah created us from the highest ʿIlliyyīn, and He created the hearts of our Shiʿah from that from which He created us, and He created their bodies from below that. So their hearts incline toward us because they were created from that from which we were created. Then he recited this verse: “Nay! Indeed the record of the righteous is surely in ʿIlliyyīn. And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is? A written book, witnessed by those brought near.” And He created our enemy from Sijjīn, and He created the hearts of their adherents from that from which He created them, and their bodies from below that. So their hearts incline toward them because they were created from that from which they were created. Then he recited this verse: “Nay! Indeed the record of the wicked is surely in Sijjīn. And what will make you know what Sijjīn is? A written book.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Sadīr, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): “I left those devoted to your wilayah differing, some of them disavowing others.” He said: “And what have you to do with that? The people have only been charged with three things: recognizing the Imams, submitting to them in what comes to them, and referring back to them in that wherein they differ.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbdullāh al-Kāhilī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: If a people were to worship Allah alone, having no partner for Him, establish the salat, give the zakat, perform the hajj of the House, and fast the month of Ramadan, then say about something Allah did or the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did, ‘Why was it not done contrary to what was done?’ or find that within their hearts, they would thereby be mushriks. Then he recited this verse: “But no, by your Lord, they do not believe until they make you judge concerning what has arisen between them, then find within themselves no discomfort regarding what you have decided, and submit with full submission.” Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Hold fast to submission.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: I said to him عليه السلام: “Among us there is a man called Kulayb. Nothing comes from you except that he says: ‘I submit.’ So we named him Kulayb al-Taslīm.” He said: So he invoked mercy upon him, then said: “Do you know what submission is?” So we remained silent. Then he said: “By Allah, it is al-ikhbāt.” The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Those who believe, and do righteous deeds, and humble themselves to their Lord.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام regarding the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him therein goodness. He عليه السلام said: "The earning is submission to us, truthfulness concerning us, and that one should not lie against us."

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Kamil al-Tammar, who said: Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) said: Certainly, the believers have succeeded. Do you know who they are? I said: You know better. He said: Certainly, the believers who have succeeded are the submitters. Indeed, the submitters are the noble chosen ones. So the believer is a stranger; therefore, glad tidings for the strangers.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from al-Khashshāb, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir, from Rabīʿ al-Muslī, from Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: I heard him saying: “Whoever is pleased to complete the whole of faith, then let him say: My position in all matters is the position of the Āl of Muḥammad regarding what they kept hidden and what they made public, and regarding what reached me from them and what did not reach me.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah or Burayd, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Allah has indeed addressed Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) in His Book. He said: I said, “In which place?” He said: In His saying: And had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you and sought forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had sought forgiveness for them, they would surely have found Allah Ever-Relenting, Merciful. But no, by your Lord, they do not believe until they make you judge regarding that over which they disputed among themselves, concerning what they had covenanted upon themselves: that if Allah were to cause Muḥammad to die, they would not return this matter to Banī Hāshim. Then they should find in themselves no distress regarding what you have judged upon them, whether killing or pardon, and submit with full submission.

Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, may Allah have mercy on him, from ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm al-Ḥasanī, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from al-Ḥakam ibn Ayman, from Abī Baṣīr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Those who listen to the word, then follow the best of it.” Up to the end of the verse. He said: “They are those who submit to the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, those who, when they hear the hadith, neither add to it nor diminish from it; they bring it just as they heard it.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fuḍayl, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: He looked at the people circumambulating around the Kaʿbah and said: “This is how they used to circumambulate in the Jāhiliyyah.” They were only commanded to circumambulate it, then depart toward us, so that they may inform us of their wilayah and their affection, and present to us their support. Then he recited this verse: “So make hearts among the people incline toward them.”

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Dāwūd ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and he saw the people in Makkah and what they were doing. He said: “Deeds like the deeds of the Jāhiliyyah.” Indeed, by Allah, they were not commanded with this; and they were not commanded except that they should remove their untidiness and fulfill their vows. Then they should pass by us and inform us of their wilayah, and present to us their support.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal; all together from Abu Jamilah, from Khalid ibn Ammar, from Sadir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام while he was entering and I was leaving. He took my hand, then faced the House, and said: “O Sadir, the people have only been commanded to come to these stones and circumambulate them, then come to us and inform us of their wilayah toward us.” And this is the saying of Allah: “And indeed I am surely most forgiving to whoever repents and believes and acts righteously, then is guided.” Then he gestured with his hand to his chest: “To our wilayah.” Then he said: “O Sadir, shall I show you those who bar people from the religion of Allah?” Then he looked toward Abu Hanifah and Sufyan al-Thawri in that time, while they were circles in the mosque, and said: “These are the ones who bar from the religion of Allah without guidance from Allah and without a clear Book.” Indeed, these vile ones—if they were to sit in their houses, and the people went about and found no one to inform them about Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and about His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, then they would come to us, and we would inform them about Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and about His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Sinān, from Mismaʿ Kirdīn al-Baṣrī, who said: I used not to eat more than one meal in the night and the day. Sometimes I would seek permission to enter upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and find that the table had already been taken away, so that I would not see it before him. But when I entered, he would call for it, and I would partake of the food with him, and I would suffer no harm from that. Yet if I followed one meal with food eaten with someone else, I could not settle and I could not sleep because of bloating. So I complained of that to him and informed him that when I ate with him I was not harmed by it. He said: "O Abū Sayyār, you are eating the food of a righteous people; the angels shake hands with them upon their bedding." He said: I said, "And do they appear to you?" He then passed his hand over some of his children and said: "They are gentler with our children than we are with them."

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: O Husayn! And he struck with his hand toward cushions in the house: cushions upon which the Angels had long leaned, and sometimes we would pick up some of their fluff.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, who said: Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah al-Aḥmasī narrated to me, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī, who said: I entered upon ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), and I was kept waiting in the courtyard for a while. Then I entered the house, and he was picking up something, and he put his hand from behind the curtain, then handed it to whoever was in the house. So I said: May I be sacrificed for you, what is this thing that I see you picking up? He said: It is a remnant from the fluff of the angels. We gather it when we are alone and make it as a plaything for our children. So I said: May I be sacrificed for you, do they indeed come to you? He said: O Abū Ḥamzah, they indeed crowd upon our cushions.

Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, said: I heard him عليه السلام saying: There is no angel whom Allah sends down concerning any matter, except that he begins with the Imam and presents that matter to him; and indeed, the coming and going of the angels is from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to the Master of this Command.

Some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Yaḥyā ibn Musāwir, from Saʿd al-Iskāf, who said: I came to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) regarding some matter for which I used to come to him. He began saying, “Do not be hasty,” until the sun grew hot upon me and I began following the patches of shade. It was not long before a people came out toward me as though they were yellow locusts; they had woolen garments upon them, and worship had worn them down. He said: By Allah, the beauty of the people’s appearance made me forget what I had been occupied with. Then when I entered upon him, he said to me, “I see that I have caused hardship for you.” I said, “Yes, by Allah. A people passed by me and made me forget what I had been occupied with. I have never seen a people with a more beautiful appearance than them, in the dress of one man, as though their colors were like yellow locusts; worship had worn them down.” So he said, “O Saʿd, did you see them?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Those are your brothers from the jinn.” He said: So I said, “Do they come to you?” He said, “Yes, they come to us, asking us about the teachings of their religion, and their halal (permissible) and their haram (forbidden).”

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, from Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ibn Jabal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: We were at his door, then a people came out to us resembling the Zutt. Upon them were waist-wraps and coverings. So we asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about them, and he said: “These are your brothers from the jinn.”

Ahmad ibn Idrees and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Faddal, from one of our companions, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, who said: I came to Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) seeking permission to enter upon him, and there were camel saddles lined up at the door, and the voices had risen. Then a group came out wearing turbans, resembling the Zutt. He said: So I entered upon Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) and said: May I be made your ransom, your permission for me was delayed today, and I saw a people come out before me wearing turbans, and I did not recognize them. He said: Do you know who those are, O Sa'd? He said: I said: No. He said: They are your brothers from the jinn. They come to us and ask us about their halal (permissible) and their haram (forbidden), and the features of their religion.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, who said: Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) instructed me regarding some needs of his in al-Madinah, so I went out. While I was between the pass of al-Rawha’ upon my mount, suddenly there was a man waving his garment. He said: I turned toward him and thought that he was thirsty, so I handed him the water-skin, but he said to me, ‘I have no need of it,’ and he handed me a letter, the clay seal of which was still moist. He said: When I looked at the seal, it was the seal of Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام). So I said, ‘When was your meeting with the owner of the letter?’ He said, ‘Just now.’ And in the letter were matters commanding me to do them. Then I turned around, and there was no one with me. He said: Then Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) arrived, and I met him and said, ‘May I be made your ransom, a man came to me with your letter while its clay seal was still moist.’ So he said, ‘O Sadir, we have servants from among the jinn, and when we desire speed, we send them.’ And in another narration, he said: ‘We have followers from among the jinn just as we have followers from among humankind, so when we intend a matter, we send them.’

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from the one who mentioned him, from Muhammad ibn Jahrash, who said: Hakimah bint Musa narrated to me. She said: I saw al-Rida عليه السلام standing at the door of Bayt al-Hatab while he was conversing quietly, and I did not see anyone. So I said: O my master, to whom are you speaking secretly? He said: This is Amir al-Zahra'i; he came to me asking me and complaining to me. I said: O my master, I would love to hear his speech. He said to me: If you hear it, you will suffer fever for a year. I said: O my master, I would love to hear him. He said to me: Listen. So I listened, and I heard something like whistling, and fever overtook me, so I remained feverish for a year.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn Ayyub, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), who said: While Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was upon the pulpit, a snake approached from the direction of one of the doors of the masjid. The people intended to kill it, so Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) sent word that they should refrain, and they refrained. The snake came gliding until it reached the pulpit, then it raised itself and greeted Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام), so Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) indicated to it to stand until he finished his sermon. When he had finished his sermon, he turned to it and said, 'Who are you?' It said, 'Amr ibn Uthman, your khalifah over the jinn. My father died and instructed me to come to you and seek your view. I have come to you, O Amir al-Mu'minin, so what do you command me with, and what do you see?' Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) said to him, 'I advise you to have taqwa of Allah, and to return and assume the place of your father among the jinn, for you are my khalifah over them.' He said: So Amr bade farewell to Amir al-Mu'minin and departed, and he was his khalifah over the jinn. So I said to him, 'May I be made your ransom, does Amr come to you, and is that obligatory upon him?' He said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I was a travel companion of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi. When we were in al-Madinah, he went in to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, bid him farewell, and came out from him while he was cheerful, until we arrived at al-Ukhayrijah, the first stopping place on our route from Fayd to al-Madinah, on a Friday. We performed the midday salat, and when the camel rose to carry us on, I suddenly saw a tall dark-complexioned man carrying a letter. He handed it to Jabir, and Jabir took it, kissed it, placed it on his eyes, and it was from Muhammad ibn Ali to Jabir ibn Yazid, with wet black clay upon it. He said to him, 'When were you last with my master?' He said, 'Just now.' He said to him, 'Before the salat or after the salat?' He said, 'After the salat.' So he broke the seal and began to read it, and his face tightened until he reached its end. Then he held the letter, and I did not see him laughing or cheerful until he arrived in al-Kufah. When we reached al-Kufah at night, I passed that night, and when morning came I went to him out of reverence for him. I found that he had come out to me with ankle bones hung around his neck, riding upon a reed, and saying, 'I find Mansur ibn Jumhur an amir not commanded,' and verses similar to this. He looked into my face and I looked into his face, but he did not say anything to me, nor did I say anything to him. I began to weep because of what I saw of him, and children and people gathered around me and around him. He continued until he entered al-Rahbah and began moving about with the children, while the people were saying, 'Jabir ibn Yazid has gone mad, he has gone mad.' By Allah, not many days passed before a letter from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik came to his governor: 'Look for a man called Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, strike his neck, and send me his head.' So he turned to those sitting with him and said to them, 'Who is Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi?' They said, 'May Allah set you right, he was a man of knowledge, merit, and hadith, and he performed hajj; then he went mad, and there he is in al-Rahbah with the children, upon the reeds, playing with them.' He said: So he looked down upon him, and there he was with the children playing upon the reeds. So he said, 'All praise is due to Allah, who spared me from killing

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Manṣūr, from Faḍl al-Aʿwar, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said: We were, at the time of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), when he passed away, wavering like sheep that have no shepherd. Then we met Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, and he said to me, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, who is your Imam?” So I said, “My Imams are the family of Muḥammad.” He said, “You are ruined and have ruined others. Did not you and I hear Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: ‘Whoever dies while there is no Imam over him dies a death of Jāhiliyyah’?” So I said, “Yes, by my life.” And three days before that, or about that, I had gone in to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and Allah granted recognition. So I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), “Indeed Sālim said to me such and such.” He said: So he said, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, no one from among us dies until he leaves behind, after him, one who acts with the like of his deeds, follows his path, and calls to what he called to.” O Abū ʿUbaydah, what was given to Dāwūd was not withheld from being given to Sulaymān. Then he said, “O Abū ʿUbaydah, when the Qāʾim of the family of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) rises, he will judge with the judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān, not asking for evidence.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Aban, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام saying: “The world will not pass away until a man from me emerges, who will judge with the judgment of the family of Dawud عليه السلام, and he will not ask for proof; he will give every soul its due right.”

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام): “By what do you judge when you judge?” He said: “By the judgment of Allah and the judgment of Dawud. So when a matter comes to us that is not with us, Ruh al-Qudus conveys it to us.”

Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from ʿImrān ibn Aʿyan, from Juʿayd al-Hamdānī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, who said: I asked him, “By which judgment do you judge?” He said, “The judgment of the family of Dāwūd. So if something is difficult for us, Rūḥ al-Qudus conveys it to us thereby.”

Ahmad ibn Mihrān, may Allah have mercy on him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the status of the Imams? He عليه السلام said: Like the status of Dhū al-Qarnayn, and like the status of Yūshaʿ, and like the status of Āṣaf, the companion of Sulaymān. He said: Then by what do you judge? He عليه السلام said: By the judgment of Allah, and the judgment of the family of Dāwūd, and the judgment of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the Holy Spirit conveys it to us.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, from a man, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the Prophets from the clay of Illiyeen — their hearts and their bodies — and He created the hearts of the believers from that same clay, and He made the creation of the bodies of the believers from below that. And He created the disbelievers from the clay of Sijjeen — their hearts and their bodies. Then He blended between the two clays. Thus, from this, a believer begets a disbeliever and a disbeliever begets a believer, and from here a believer commits a sin and from here a disbeliever does a good deed. So the hearts of the believers yearn toward what they were created from, and the hearts of the disbelievers yearn toward what they were created from.

Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, created the believer from the clay of Paradise, and created the disbeliever from the clay of the Fire. And he (AS) said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, intends goodness for a servant, He purifies his soul and his body, so he does not hear anything of good except that he recognizes it, and he does not hear anything of evil except that he rejects it. He (the narrator) said: And I heard him (AS) saying: The clays are three (types) — the clay of the Prophets, and the believer is from that clay, except that the Prophets are from its purest part; they are the root and for them is their excellence, and the believers are the branches from a sticky clay. Likewise, God, Mighty and Majestic, will not separate between them and their Shia. And he (AS) said: The clay of the Nasibi is from black fashioned mud; and as for the weak ones (in understanding), they are from dust. No believer turns away from his faith, nor does a Nasibi turn away from his enmity, and God's Will prevails regarding them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Sahl who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your sacrifice! From which thing did God, Mighty and Majestic, create the clay of the believer?' So he said: 'From the clay of the Prophets, so it shall never become impure, ever.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and others, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Abu Nahshal who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to me, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Verily, God, Majestic and Mighty, created us from the highest 'Illiyyeen, and created the hearts of our Shia from what He created us from, and created their bodies from below that, and their hearts yearn towards us because they were created from what we were created from. Then he recited these verses: Nay! Verily the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyeen. And what will make you know what 'Illiyyoon is? A written record, witnessed by those brought near (to God). And He created our enemy from Sijjeen, and created their adherents' hearts from what He created them from, and their bodies from below that. So their hearts yearn towards them because they were created from what they were created from. Then he recited these verses: Nay! The record of the wicked is indeed in Sijjeen. And what will make you know what Sijjeen is? A written record. Woe on that day to the deniers.

Abdullah ibn Kaysan informed me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: I said to him, 'May I be made your ransom, I am your devotee Abdullah ibn Kaysan.' He said: 'As for the lineage, I recognise it; but as for you, I do not recognise you.' He said: I said to him, 'I was born in the mountains and grew up in the land of Persia. I mix with people in business and other matters. I come across a man and see in him good conduct, good morals, and abundant trustworthiness — then I investigate and find him to be an enemy of yours. And I come across a man and see from him evil morals, little trustworthiness, and malice — then I investigate and find him to be one of your followers. How can this be?' Then he said to me: 'Did you not know, O son of Kaysan, that God, Mighty and Majestic, took a clay from Paradise and a clay from the Fire, then mixed them both together, then separated this from that and that from this? So what you saw in those ones — the trustworthiness, good morals, and good conduct — is from what the clay of Paradise touched them with, and they will return to what they were created from. And what you saw in these ones — the little trustworthiness, evil morals, and malice — is from what the clay of the Fire touched them with, and they will return to what they were created from.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Salih ibn Sahl who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the believers from the clay of the Prophets?' He said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (AS), who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when He willed to create Adam (AS), sent Jibra'il (AS) in the first hour of Friday. He grabbed with his right hand a handful that extended from the seventh heaven down to the lowest heaven, and took some soil from each heaven. He grabbed another handful from the seventh earth, the highest, to the seventh earth, the farthest. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Word, and it held the first handful in the right hand and the second handful in the left hand, and split the clay into two portions, scattering from the earth and from the heavens. He said to those in his right hand: From you come the Messengers, Prophets, successors, truthful ones, believers, the blessed, and those whose honor I will — so it became binding for them what He said, as He said. And He said to those in his left hand: From you come the tyrants, polytheists, disbelievers, despots, and those whose humiliation and misery I will — so it became binding for them what He said, as He said. Then the two clays were mixed together. This is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Verily, Allah is the Splitter of the seed and the stone' — the seed (hab) is the clay of the believers upon which Allah cast His love, and the stone (nawa) is the clay of the disbelievers who were distant from every good; and it was called nawa because it was far (na'a) from every good and remote from it. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'He brings forth the living from the dead and the Extractor of the dead from the living' — so the living is the believer whose clay emerges from the clay of the disbeliever, and the dead who emerges from the living is the disbeliever who emerges from the clay of the believer; thus the living is the believer and the dead is the disbeliever. And this is His word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Is he who was dead and We gave him life?' — his death was the mixing of his clay with the clay of the disbeliever, and his life was when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, separated them by His Word. Likewise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings out the believer at birth from darkness after his entry into it, toward the light; and He brings out the disbeliever from light toward darkness aft

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: [48:4] He it is Who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the Momineen He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the iman (faith).' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic:' [58:22] and He has Supported them with a Spirit from Him He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the iman (faith).'

From him, from Ahmad, from Safwan, from Aban, from Fuzayl, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): [58:22] "Those — He has impressed the faith in their hearts" "Is it for them, regarding what He has impressed in their hearts, any agency over it?" He (peace be upon him) said: "No."

A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A'ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Abu Ja'far<sup>asws</sup>, having said: 'The tranquillity (mentioned in 48:4) is the faith.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Hisham ibn Salim, and others besides these two, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: [48:4] He it is Who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the faith.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Jamil, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) about the words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'He it is Who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers' [48:4] He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is the iman (faith).' He (the narrator) said: '(And what about) "and He has supported them with a Spirit from Him"' [58:22] He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is the iman (faith).' And (he asked) about His words: 'and He necessitated for them the word of taqwa (piety)' [48:26] He (عليه السلام) said: 'It is the iman (faith).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Qutaybah al-A'sha, who said: 'I heard Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying:' 'The mu'minah (female Believer) is more precious than the mu'min (male Believer), and the mu'min is more precious than red sulfur (al-kibrit al-ahmar). So who among you has (ever) seen red sulfur?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Kamil al-Tammar, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The people, all of them, are beasts' – [repeated] three times – 'except for a few from the Momineen; and the Momin is rare' – three times.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying to Abu Baseer: 'But, by Allah! If I were to find three Momineen from among you who are concealing my hadith, I would not have considered it permissible that I should be concealing a single hadith from them.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, who said: I went to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'By Allah, what affords you sitting back (from rising against the ruling authorities)?' He said: 'And why, O Sadir?' I said: 'Due to the abundance of your friends, your Shias, and your helpers. By Allah, had Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) possessed what you have of Shias, helpers, and friends, neither (the clan of) Taym nor (the clan of) 'Adiyy would have coveted it (the caliphate).' He said: 'O Sadir, and how many might they be?' I said: 'One hundred thousand.' He said: 'One hundred thousand?' I said: 'Yes, and two hundred thousand.' He said: 'Two hundred thousand?' I said: 'Yes, and half the world.' He (Sadir) said: So he (peace be upon him) fell silent from me, then said: 'Would it be easy upon you to travel with us to Yanbu'?' I said: 'Yes.' So he ordered a donkey and a mule to be saddled. I hastened forward and rode the donkey, so he said: 'O Sadir, do you see fit to yield the donkey to me?' I said: 'The mule is finer and more distinguished.' He said: 'The donkey is gentler with me.' So I dismounted, and he (peace be upon him) rode the donkey and I rode the mule. So we proceeded, and the time of salat arrived. He said: 'O Sadir, let us dismount to perform salat.' Then he said: 'This is marshy land; salat is not permissible in it.' So we traveled until we arrived at red ground, and he looked at a boy pasturing goats and said: 'By Allah, O Sadir! Had I Shias equal in number to these goats, sitting back (from rising against the ruling authorities) would not be permissible for me.' And we dismounted and performed salat. When we had finished the salat, I turned towards the goats and counted them, and they were seventeen.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'at ibn Mihran, who said: 'Abd Salih (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Sama'at! They believed upon their beds and they are scaring me. But, by Allah! It has been so that in the world and whatever was in it there was only one (person) who worshipped Allah, and had there been anyone else along with him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would have Added him in, where He is Saying:' [16:120] Surely Ibrahim was a community, obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not from the Polytheists. So it remained like that for as long as Allah so Desired. Then Allah Comforted him with Isma'il and Is'haq, and thus they became three. But, by Allah! The Momineen have always been few and the people of disbelief numerous. Do you know why that is so?' So I said, 'I do not know, may I be sacrificed for you!' So he said: 'They were made a comfort for the Momineen, to whom they pour out what is in their hearts, so they find rest in that and tranquility therein.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Al-Nadr, from Yahya ibn Abi Khalid Al-Qammat, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! How few we are — if we were to gather together upon a sheep, we would not (even be able to) finish it.' So he said: 'Shall I narrate to you something more strange than that? The Emigrants and the Helpers were gone,' — and he gestured with his hand — 'except three.' Humran said: 'So I said: "May I be sacrificed for you! What is the state of Ammar?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on Ammar — Abu al-Yaqzan — he pledged allegiance and was killed as a martyr." So I said within myself: "What thing is more superior than martyrdom?" So he looked at me and said: "Perhaps you think he is like the three. Far be it! Far be it!"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: 'I heard Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) saying:' 'Not everyone who speaks as being with our Wilayah is a Momin. But, it has been Made to be a comfort for the Momineen.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Fuzayl ibn Yasaar, from Abdul Wahid ibn Al-Mukhtar Al-Ansary, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abdul Wahid! It would not harm a man when he was upon that view (of al-Wilayah), whatever the people say for him, and even if they were to say he was insane; and it would not harm him, even if he was at the top of a mountain worshipping Allah until the death comes to him.'

'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu 'Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: Allah, Blessed and Most High, Said: 'If there does not happen to be in the earth except for one Momin, I would have Sufficed with him from the entirety of My creatures, and would have Made for him, from his iman, a comfort such that he would not be needy of anyone.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said: 'What would he care — the one whom Allah causes to recognise this matter (al-Wilayah) — if he were to be upon the summit of a mountain, eating from the vegetation of the earth, until death comes to him?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Kulayb ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: It is not befitting for the believer that he becomes estranged from his brother who is below him. The believer is highly valued in his religion.'

From him, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Khalid, from Fazalah bin Ayyub, from Umar bin Aban and Sayf bin Ameerah, from Fuzayl bin Yasaar, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) during an illness that had afflicted him such that nothing remained of him except his head (unaffected). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Fuzayl! I very frequently say: what burden is upon a man whom Allah has caused to recognise this matter (al-wilayah), even were he to be atop a mountain, until death comes to him?' 'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! The people have taken to the right and to the left, but we and our Shia have been guided to the Straight Path.' 'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! If the believer were to come to possess what lies between the east and the west, that would be better for him; and if he were to find his limbs cut off, that too would be better for him. O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! Allah does not do with the believer except that which is better for him.' 'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! Had the world equalled in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so much as the wing of a mosquito, He would not have given His enemy from it a single sip of water.' 'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! The one whose concern is a single concern — Allah suffices his concern; and the one whose concern scatters into every valley — Allah does not care in which valley he perishes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Mansur al-Sayqal and al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays — both said: We heard Abu Abdillah (AS) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (SAWW) said: "Allah Mighty and Majestic Said:' 'I do not Hesitate with regards to anything I Do like I Hesitate regarding the death of My Momin servant. I Love to Meet him and he dislikes death, so I Defer it from him; and he supplicates to Me, so I Answer him, and he asks Me, so I Give him; and if there did not happen to be in the world except for one Momin from My servants, I would Suffice with him from the entirety of My creatures, and I would Make his Iman a comfort for him, so that he would not feel estranged toward anyone.'

Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ali bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Zurara, from Muhammad bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'Allah fends off the destruction from the whole town due to the (existence of just) one Momin.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'A town would not be hit by a Punishment while there are seven from the Momineen therein.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one (narrator), from Abu Abdullah (AS), who said: It was said to him (AS) regarding the Punishment: when it befalls upon a people, does it strike the Momineen (believers)? He (AS) said: 'Yes, but they are saved after it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Nusayr Abu al-Hakam al-Khath'ami, from Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said: The believer is of two (types of) believers. So there is a believer who ratified the Covenant of Allah and was loyal to His Stipulation, and that is in the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: [33:23] From the Believers are men who ratified what Covenant Allah Made with them. So that is the one who would not be struck by the horrors of the world nor the horrors of the Hereafter, and that is from those who intercede and are not in need of being interceded for. And there is a believer like the stalk of the crop — sometimes it bends and sometimes it stands upright. So that is from those who would be struck by the horrors of the world and the horrors of the Hereafter, and that is from those who would be interceded for and who would not (themselves) intercede.

A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Khalid Al-'Ammi, from Khazir Bin 'Amro, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The believer is (of) two believers: a believer who is loyal to Allah with His Stipulations which He Stipulated upon him. so that one would be with the Prophets and the Truthful and the Martyrs and the Righteous, and a goodly company are they! [4:69] And that would be the one who intercedes and is not interceded for, and that one is from those who are afflicted neither by the horrors of the world nor the horrors of the Hereafter. And there is a believer whose foot has wavered with him, so that one is like the stalk of the crop — whichever way the wind tilts him he tilts — and that one is from those who are afflicted by the horrors of the world and the Hereafter, and he would be interceded for, and he is upon good.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (AS), who said: A man from al-Basra stood up before Amir al-Momineen (AS) and said: 'O Amir al-Momineen (AS)! Inform us about the brethren.' So he (AS) said: 'The brethren are of two types – the trustworthy brethren and the friendly brethren.' As for the trustworthy brethren, they are the palm, the wing, the family, and the wealth. So when you are with a brother of yours who is at the limit of trustworthiness, then spend your wealth and your body for him, be sincere to those who are sincere to him, and be an adversary to those who are his adversaries, and conceal his secrets and his faults, and manifest the good that is in him. And know, O questioner, that they are scarcer than red sulfur. And as for the friendly brethren, you attain your pleasure from them, so do not sever that from them, nor seek what lies beyond that from their consciences; and exert for them what they exert for you of a cheerful countenance and a sweet tongue.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah took a Covenant upon the Momin (to have patience) such that his words would not be accepted as true and he would not avenge himself against his enemy. No Momin will find any satisfaction for his soul except through its disgrace (before his own conscience), for every Momin is harnessed (bridled from his worldly desires).

A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: Rasool-Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said: Indeed, Allah took a covenant with the mu'min (believer) regarding four tribulations, the least (serious) of these being a mu'min who holds the same belief yet envies him; or a hypocrite who follows his tracks (to harm him); or a Satan who tempts him astray; or a disbeliever who witnesses his striving (against him). So what would remain of the mu'min after all of this?

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: No believer would escape from one of three, and perhaps all three would be gathered upon him – either the hatred of the one who happens to be with him in the house, closing the door upon him, bothering him; or a neighbour who would bother him; or the one in his way to his needs who would trouble him. And if a believer were to be at the top of a mountain, Allah Mighty and Majestic would Send a devil (shaytan) to him who would harm him, and Allah would Make his iman (faith) to be a comfort (uns) for him, such that he would not yearn for anyone with it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, from Dawood ibn Sirhan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying: Four (matters) the Believer would not be devoid of, or (at least) one of these: a Believer who envies him — and it is the most difficult of these upon him — and a hypocrite who removes his traces, or an enemy who fights against him, or a Satan who tempts him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'at ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Indeed, Allah Mighty and Majestic has made His friend a target for His enemy in this world.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, who said: I was in the presence of Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), and a man complained to him (عليه السلام) of his needs. So he (عليه السلام) said to him: 'Be patient, for Allah would soon Make a relief for you.' He (the narrator) said: 'Then he (عليه السلام) remained silent for a while, then turned towards the man and said: "Inform me about the prison of Al-Kufa — how is it?" So he said: "May Allah Keep you well (عليه السلام)! It is narrow, fetid, and its inhabitants are in the worst of conditions." He (عليه السلام) said: "So you are indeed in the prison, and you are wanting to be in spaciousness within it? Do you not know that the world is a prison for the believer (al-mu'min)?"'

From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ibrahim Al-Hazza', from Muhammad Bin Sagheer, from his grandfather Shuayb who said, 'I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The world is a prison for the Momin, so which prison is it that any good came from it?''

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Dawood ibn Abi Yazid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The believer is unappreciated. And in another report: That is because his good deed ascends to Allah, so it is not spread among the people, whereas the disbeliever is appreciated.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no muʾmin except that Allah has assigned to him four satans who tempt him, intending to lead him astray; and a disbeliever who seeks to attack him; and a muʾmin who envies him—and he is the hardest of them upon him; and a hypocrite who follows his slips.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: When the believer dies, satans numbering as many as Rabi‘ah and Mudar are let loose upon his neighbors, who had been preoccupied with him.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: There neither has been, nor will there be, nor is there any believer except that he has a neighbor who harms him; and if a believer were on an island from the islands of the sea, Allah would surely send to him someone who would harm him.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There has not been, in what has passed, nor in what remains, nor in that which you are in, any believer except that he has a neighbor who harms him.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: There has never been, nor will there be until the Hour is established, any believer except that he has a neighbor who harms him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the most severely afflicted of the people are the Prophets عليهم السلام, then those who come after them, then the most exemplary and then the next most exemplary.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Affliction, and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, singles out the believer for, was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, so he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was asked, “Who among the people is most severely afflicted in the world?” He said, “The Prophets, then those most like them, then those most like them.” Then the believer is afflicted according to the measure of his faith and the excellence of his deeds. So whoever has sound faith and good deeds, his affliction becomes more intense; and whoever has feeble faith and weak deeds, his affliction is less.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, great reward is with great affliction, and Allah does not love a people except that He afflicts them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: The most severely afflicted of the people are the Prophets عليه السلام, then the successors عليه السلام, then the most exemplary, and then the next most exemplary.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has servants upon the earth from among the sincere ones of His servants. No gift descends from the heaven to the earth except that He turns it away from them to others, and no affliction descends except that He turns it toward them.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: And with him was Sudayr, Indeed, Allah, when He loves a servant, immerses him in affliction thoroughly; and indeed we and you, O Sudayr, enter the morning with it and enter the evening with it.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAlāʾ, from Ḥammād, from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He loves a servant, He immerses him thoroughly in affliction and pours affliction upon him abundantly. Then when he calls upon Him, He says: “Here I am, My servant. If I hasten for you what you asked, indeed I am able to do that; and if I store it up for you, then what I have stored up for you is better for you.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Zayd al-Zarrād, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh (عليه السلام), who said: Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said: “Indeed, great affliction is met with great recompense. So when Allah loves a servant, He afflicts him with great affliction. Thus, whoever is pleased, for him with Allah is pleasure; and whoever is angered by the affliction, for him with Allah is wrath.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Zakariyyā ibn al-Ḥurr, from Jābir ibn Yazīd, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the muʾmin is only afflicted in the world according to the measure of his religion—or he said: according to the degree of his religion.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from one of his companions, from Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā al-Ḥaḍramī, from Muḥammad ibn Buhlūl ibn Muslim al-ʿAbdī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the believer is at the status of the scale’s pan: whenever there is an increase in his iman, there is an increase in his affliction.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “No forty nights pass over the believer except that a matter occurs to him which grieves him, by which he is reminded.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Nājiyah, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام): “Al-Mughīrah says that the believer is not afflicted with leprosy, nor with vitiligo, nor with such-and-such, nor with such-and-such.” So he said: “Then he is surely heedless of the Companion of Yā Sīn; he was crippled in the hand.” Then he drew back his fingers and said: “It is as though I am looking at his crippling. He came to them and warned them, then he returned to them on the following day, and they killed him.” Then he said: “Indeed, the believer may be afflicted with every affliction and may die by every kind of death, except that he does not kill himself.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed, the believer holds a most excellent station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic—three times. He surely tries him with affliction, then takes out his soul, limb by limb, from his body, while he praises Allah for that.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, in Paradise there is a station which no servant can attain except through affliction in his body.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Ḥannāṭ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said: I complained to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about what I was suffering from pains, and I was frequently ill. So he said to me: “O ʿAbd Allāh, if the believer knew what reward he has in afflictions, he would wish that he had been cut with scissors.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Yūnus ibn Ribāṭ, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, the people of the truth have never ceased, since they came to be, to remain in hardship. Verily, that is only for a short period, and [after it is] a long well-being.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Usamah, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, surely attends to the believer with affliction just as a man attends to his family with gifts during absence, and He protects him from the world just as a physician protects the sick person.

ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī, from Muḥammad ibn Buhlūl al-ʿAbdī, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Allah does not secure the believer from the turmoils of the world, but He secures him from blindness in it and from misery in the Hereafter.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Ṣaḥḥāf, from Dharīḥ al-Muḥāribī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام used to say: “Indeed, I dislike for a man to remain well in the world such that nothing from the afflictions befalls him.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Nūḥ ibn Shuʿayb, from Abū Dāwūd al-Mustariqq, raising it, said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was invited to a meal. When he entered the man’s house, he saw a chicken upon a wall that had laid an egg, and the egg fell upon a peg in the wall and remained fixed upon it; it did not fall and did not break. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was amazed by it. The man said to him, “Are you amazed by this egg? By the One who sent you with the truth, I have never suffered loss in anything at all.” He said: Then Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله rose and did not eat anything of his food, and said: “Whoever has not been afflicted with loss, Allah has no need of him.”

From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: Allah has no need of one who has no share for Him in his wealth and his body.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿUthmān al-Nawwāʾ, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicts the believer with every affliction, and causes him to die by every kind of death, but He does not afflict him with the loss of his intellect. Do you not see Ayyūb, how Iblīs was given power over his wealth, over his children, over his family, and over everything belonging to him, yet he was not given power over his intellect. It was left for him so that he might affirm the tawhid of Allah by means of it.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, there is a rank for the servant with Allah that he does not attain except by one of two traits: either by the loss of his wealth or by an affliction in his body.

From him, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muthannā al-Ḥannāṭ, from Abī Usāmah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “Were it not that My believing servant would find something in his heart, I would surely bind the head of the disbeliever with a band of iron such that his head would never ache, ever.”

Rasul-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The example of the believer is like the tender shoot of a crop: the winds bend it this way and that; likewise, the believer is bent by pains and illnesses. And the example of the hypocrite is like a straight iron bar which nothing affects until death comes to it and breaks it utterly.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: One day, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to his companions: “Accursed is every wealth that is not purified, and accursed is every body that is not purified, even if only once in every forty days.” So it was said: “O Messenger of Allah, as for the zakat of wealth, we have come to know it; then what is the zakat of bodies?” He صلى الله عليه وآله said to them: “That they be afflicted by an affliction.” He عليه السلام said: Then the faces of those who heard that from him changed. So when he صلى الله عليه وآله saw that their colors had changed, he said to them: “Do you know what I meant by my statement?” They said: “No, O Messenger of Allah.” He صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Rather, it is that a man is scratched by a scratch, struck by a mishap, stumbles a stumble, falls ill with an illness, is pricked by a thorn, and whatever resembles this,” until he mentioned in his hadith even the twitching of the eye.

Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “Is the believer afflicted with leprosy, vitiligo, and the like of this?” He said: “And has affliction been written for any except the believer?”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one who narrated it, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the mu'min is so noble before Allah that if he were to ask Him for Jannah and whatever is in it, He would give him that without anything diminishing from His dominion. And indeed, the kafir is so insignificant before Allah that if he were to ask Him for the world and whatever is in it, He would give him that without anything diminishing from His dominion. And indeed, Allah surely watches over His believing servant through affliction just as an absent one looks after his family with gifts, and He surely protects him from the world just as a physician protects the sick person.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Samāʿah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, in the Book of ʿAlī (عليه السلام) it is stated that the most severely afflicted of people are the Prophets, then the successors, then the most exemplary and then the next most exemplary. The believer is afflicted only in accordance with the measure of his good deeds. So whoever has sound religion and good deeds, his affliction becomes more intense. That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not make the world a reward for a believer nor a punishment for a disbeliever. And whoever has a feeble religion and weak deeds, his affliction is less. And affliction is swifter to the God-conscious believer than rain is to the low ground of the earth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Yunus ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), “This thing that has appeared on my face—people claim that Allah does not afflict a servant with it while He has a need of him.” He said to me, “Indeed, the believer from the family of Fir‘awn had contracted fingers, and he would gesture like this, stretching out his hands, and say:” “O my people, follow the messengers.” Then he said to me, “When the last third of the night begins, perform wudu (ablution) and stand for the salat (prayer) you pray. Then when you are in the final sajdah of the first two rak‘ahs, say while you are prostrating: ‘O Most High, O Most Great, O Most Beneficent, O Most Merciful, O Hearer of supplications, O Giver of good things, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and give me of the good of this world and the Hereafter that befits You, and turn away from me of the evil of this world and the Hereafter that befits You, and remove from me this pain’—and name it—‘for it has angered me and saddened me.’ And persist in the supplication.” He said: “I had not reached al-Kufah before Allah had removed it from me entirely.”

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-A'ala, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: Indeed, the poor among the Muslims will be moving about in the gardens of Paradise before their rich ones by forty autumns. Then he said: I shall set forth for you the likeness of that. The likeness of that is the likeness of two ships that passed by a tax collector. He looked into one of them and saw nothing in it, so he said: Let it go. And he looked into the other, and found it heavily laden, so he said: Detain it.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from his father, from Saʿdān, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "Afflictions are gifts from Allah, and poverty is a stored treasure with Allah."

And from him, raising it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: “O ʿAlī, indeed Allah has made poverty a trust among His creatures.” So whoever conceals it, Allah will give him the like of the reward of one who fasts and stands in worship; and whoever discloses it to one who is able to fulfill his need, but he does not do so, then he has killed him. Indeed, he did not kill him with a sword or a spear, but rather he killed him by the hurt he inflicted upon his heart.”

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Dāwūd al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣaghīr, from his grandfather Shuʿayb, from Mufaḍḍal, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “Whenever the servant increases in iman, he increases in constriction in his livelihood.”

And by his chain, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: Were it not for the insistence of the believers upon Allah in seeking sustenance, He would transfer them from the condition they are in to a condition more constricted than it.

From him, from some of his companions, raising it, he said: Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: Nothing is given to a servant from the world except as a lesson, and nothing is withheld from him except as a trial.

From him, from Nūḥ ibn Shuʿayb and Abū Isḥāq al-Khaffāf, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is nothing for the sincere ones among our Shi'a in the rule of falsehood except sustenance enough to live on. Go east if you wish, or go west; you will not be provided except with sustenance enough to live on.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, from one of his shaykhs, from Idris ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: O Ali, a need is Allah’s trust with His creatures. So whoever conceals it within himself, Allah gives him the reward of one who performs salat (prayer). But whoever discloses it to one who is able to relieve him and he does not do so, then he has killed him. Indeed, he did not kill him with a sword, nor a spearhead, nor an arrow, but he killed him by what he wounded from his heart.

And from him, from Aḥmad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Saʿdān, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will turn on the Day of Resurrection toward the poor among the believers, as one resembling an apologizer to them, and He will say: ‘By My might and My majesty, I did not make you poor in the world because of any humiliation of you before Me; and you shall surely see what I will do for you today. So whoever gave any one of you some kindness in the abode of the world, then take him by the hand and admit him into Paradise.’" He said: Then a man among them will say: ‘O my Lord, the people of the world competed regarding their worldly life: they married women, wore soft garments, ate food, lived in houses, and rode well-known mounts, so give me the like of what You gave them.’ Then He, Blessed and Exalted, will say: ‘For you, and for every servant among you, is the like of what I gave the people of the world from the time the world began until the world came to an end, multiplied seventy times.’

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqbah, from Isma'il ibn Sahl and Isma'il ibn 'Abbad, both of them raising it to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: There was none from the children of Adam who was a believer except that he was poor, and no disbeliever except that he was rich, until Ibrahim عليه السلام came and said: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve. So Allah placed among these wealth and need, and among those wealth and need.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from the one who mentioned it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: An affluent man came to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله wearing clean clothes, and he sat near Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. Then a poor man wearing dirty clothes came and sat beside the affluent man, so the affluent man gathered up his clothes from beneath his thighs. Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “Did you fear that something from his poverty might touch you?” He said, “No.” He said: “Then did you fear that something from your wealth might reach him?” He said, “No.” He said: “Then did you fear that he might soil your clothes?” He said, “No.” He said: “Then what made you do what you did?” He said: “O Rasūl Allāh, I have a companion who makes every ugly thing seem fair to me and makes every good thing seem ugly to me, and I have given him half of my wealth.” Then Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to the poor man: “Will you accept?” He said: “No.” The man said to him: “Why not?” He said: “I fear that what entered into you may enter into me.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī, from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: In the intimate discourse of Mūsā عليه السلام: O Mūsā, when you see poverty approaching, then say: ‘Welcome to the emblem of the righteous’; and when you see wealth approaching, then say: ‘A sin whose punishment has been hastened.’

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Ṭūbā is for the poor who are patient, and they are those who behold the dominion of the heavens and the earth.”

And by his chain, he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: “O group of the poor ones, be of good heart, and give Allah contentment from your hearts. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will reward you for your poverty. But if you do not do so, then there is no reward for you.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿĪsā al-Farrāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: When it is the Day of qiyamah, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will command a caller to call out before Him: “Where are the poor?” Then a great multitude from among the people will rise. He will say, “My servants,” and they will say, “Here we are, our Lord.” He will say, “I did not make you poor because of any humiliation of you before Me, but rather I chose you for the like of this day.” “So look through the faces of the people: whoever did a kindness to you, having done it only for My sake, then repay him on My behalf with jannah.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibrāhīm al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣaghīr, from his grandfather Shuʿayb, from Mufaḍḍal, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Were it not for the insistence of these Shiʿah upon Allah in seeking sustenance, He would have moved them from the condition in which they are to one more constricted than it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Kathir al-Khazzaz, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: He said to me: "Do you not enter the market? Do you not see the fruit being sold, and things among what you desire?" So I said, "Yes." He said: "Indeed, for you, for everything that you see and are unable to buy, there is a good deed."

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAffān, from Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed Allah, Majestic is His praise, apologizes to His believing servant who was made needy in the world, just as a brother apologizes to his brother. So He says: “By My might and My majesty, I did not make you needy in the world because of any abasement of you before Me. So lift this curtain and look at what I have compensated you with in place of the world.” He عليه السلام said: “So he lifts it and says: ‘What You withheld from me did not harm me, alongside what You compensated me with.’”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: When it is the Day of qiyamah, a group from among the people will rise until they come to the gate of Jannah and knock at its gate. It will be said to them, “Who are you?” They will say, “We are the poor.” It will be said to them, “Before the reckoning?” They will say, “You did not give us anything for which You would call us to account.” Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say, “They have spoken the truth; enter Jannah.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Mubārak, the غلام of Shuʿayb, who said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: I did not enrich the rich due to an honor of his before Me, and I did not impoverish the poor due to a humiliation of his before Me. Rather, it is among that by which I test the rich through the poor, and were it not for the poor, the rich would not deserve Paradise.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār and al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who both said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The affluent ones among our Shiʿah are our trustees over their needy ones, so safeguard us concerning them; may Allah safeguard you.”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said: Poverty is more adornment for the believer than the bridle-strap upon the cheek of a horse.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from his father, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I asked ʿAli ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And were it not that the people would become one community. He (عليه السلام) said: What is meant by that is the community of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), that if they were to be upon one religion as disbelievers, all of them, We would surely have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses. And if Allah had done that with the community of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), the believers would have grieved, and that would have saddened them; and they would not have married them, nor inherited from them.

Bakr al-Arqaṭ narrated to me from Abū ʿAbdillāh, or from Shuʿayb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. A man came in to him and said: “May Allah set you aright. I am a man devoted to you through my affection, and a severe need has afflicted me.
