I sought nearness through that with my household and my people, but it only increased me in distance from them.” He عليه السلام said: “What Allah has given you is better than what He has taken from you.” He said: “May I be your ransom, supplicate to Allah for me that He make me free of need from His creation.” He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah apportions the sustenance of whomsoever He wills at the hands of whomsoever He wills. But ask Allah to make you free of the need that compels you toward the ignoble of His creation.”

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who mentioned him, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: Poverty is the red death. So I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), "Is poverty from the dinar and the dirham?" He said, "No, but from the religion."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said: There is no heart except that it has two ears: upon one of them is a guiding angel, and upon the other is a tempting Satan. This one commands him and this one restrains him. Satan commands him to acts of disobedience, and the angel restrains him from them. And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Seated on the right and on the left; he does not utter any word except that with him is an observing one, ready.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq, from Saʿdān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the heart has two ears. So when the servant intends a sin, the spirit of faith says to him, “Do not do it,” and the Satan says to him, “Do it.” And when he is upon its belly, the spirit of faith is removed from him.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: There is no believer except that his heart has two ears within it: an ear into which the slinking whisperer blows, and an ear into which the angel blows. So Allah supports the believer by the angel; thus that is His saying: “And He supported them with a Spirit from Him.”
Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “upright, a Muslim.” He said: “Pure, sincere, with nothing in him of the worship of idols.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, raising it to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), said: Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: “O people,” It is only Allah and the Shayṭān, and the truth and falsehood, and guidance and misguidance, and right conduct and error, and the immediate world and the Hereafter, and the final outcome, and good deeds and evil deeds. So whatever is of good deeds belongs to Allah, and whatever is of evil deeds belongs to the Shayṭān—may Allah curse him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, that Amir al-Mu'minin, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, used to say: Blessedness is for the one who makes worship and du'a sincerely for Allah, and does not occupy his heart with what his eyes see, and does not forget the dhikr of Allah because of what his ears hear, and does not grieve his breast over what has been given to others.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from al-Minqarī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning the saying: of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed.” He عليه السلام said: “It does not mean the most deeds, but rather the most correct of you in deed. Correctness is only the fear of Allah, and truthful and good intention.” Then he عليه السلام said: “Preserving the deed until it becomes pure is harder than the deed itself. The sincere deed is that for which you do not want anyone to praise you except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And the intention is better than the deed. Indeed, intention is the deed.” Then he عليه السلام recited His saying, Mighty and Majestic: “Say: Each acts according to his manner” — meaning, according to his intention.

And by this chain, he said: I asked him عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.” He عليه السلام said: “The sound heart is that by which one meets his Lord while there is no one in it besides Him.” He عليه السلام said: “And every heart in which there is shirk or doubt is fallen. They only intended zuhd in the world so that their hearts might be emptied for the Hereafter.”

By this sanad/isnad, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Sindī, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said: No servant makes faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sincere for forty days — or he said: no servant beautifies the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for forty days — except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, makes him abstinent regarding the world, shows him its illness and its remedy, establishes wisdom in his heart, and causes his tongue to speak by it. Then he recited: “Indeed, those who took the calf shall be reached by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world; and thus do We recompense the fabricators.” So you do not see an adherent of bidʿah except humiliated, and a fabricator against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and against His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), and against the People of his House (صلوات الله عليهم), except humiliated.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: My father عليه السلام used to say: There is nothing more corrupting to the heart than a sin. Indeed, the heart commits the sin, and it continues with it until it overcomes it, and turns its upper part into its lower.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskan, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “So what has made them patient upon the Fire?” So he عليه السلام said: “How patient they are in doing that which they know will cause them to end up in the Fire.”

From him, from his father, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, there is no throbbing vein, nor a calamity, nor a headache, nor an illness except due to a sin; and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much. He said: Then he said: And what Allah pardons is more than that for which He calls to account.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said: No calamity befalls the servant except due to a sin, and what Allah forgives of is greater.

ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to say: Do not bare your teeth openly while you have committed disgraceful deeds, and the one who has committed evil deeds should not feel secure from a night assault.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī Usāmah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: Seek refuge in Allah from the assaults of Allah by night and day. He said: I said to him, “And what are the assaults of Allah?” He said, “The seizing for acts of disobedience.”

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Sulaymān al-Jaʿfarī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: All sins are grave, and the gravest of them is that upon which flesh and blood have grown, because it is either shown mercy or punished, and none enters Paradise except one who is pure.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Abān, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the servant commits a sin, then sustenance is withheld from him.

ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Nawfalī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mukhtār, from a man, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Accursed, accursed is the one who worships the dīnār and the dirham. Accursed, accursed is the one whose sleeve is blind. Accursed, accursed is the one who has intercourse with an animal.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: I heard him عليه السلام saying: “Beware of the belittled sins, for indeed they have one who seeks them out. One of you says: ‘I commit a sin and seek forgiveness.’” Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And We write what they have sent ahead and their آثار, and We have enumerated every thing in a manifest Imam.” And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: “Indeed, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, and it be in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.”

Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Thaʿlabah, from Sulaymān ibn Ṭarīf, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: Indeed, sin deprives the servant of sustenance.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Fuḍayl, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, a man commits a sin, and so sustenance is warded off from him. And he recited this verse: When they swore that they would surely cut its fruit in the morning, and they did not make any exception; so there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep.

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “When a man commits a sin, a black spot comes out in his heart. If he repents, it is erased; and if he increases, it increases until it overcomes his heart, and he will never succeed after that, ever.”

From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, the servant asks Allah for a need, and it may be that its fulfillment is to occur for him after a near term or after a delayed time. Then the servant commits a sin, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to the angel: "Do not fulfill his need, and deprive him of it, for he has exposed himself to My anger and has deserved deprivation from Me."

Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), who said: I heard him saying: “There is no year less in rain than another year, but Allah places it where He wills. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when a people act with acts of disobedience, diverts from them what had been decreed for them of rain in that year to others besides them, and to the deserts, the seas, and the mountains. And indeed Allah surely punishes the dung beetle in its hole by withholding rain from the land in whose place it is, because of the sins of those in its vicinity; and Allah has made for it a path in a route other than the quarter of the people of disobedience.” He said: Then Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) said: “So take a lesson, O people of insight.”

Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, a man commits a sin and is thereby deprived of salat al-layl, and indeed an evil deed moves more quickly upon its doer than a knife through flesh.

From him, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Whoever intends an evil deed, then let him not do it, for perhaps the servant commits the evil deed, and the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, sees him, then says: “By My honour and My majesty, I shall never forgive you after that.”

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Nahdī, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from a man, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said: It is a right upon Allah that He not be disobeyed in a house except that He exposes it to the sun until it purifies it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mismaʿ ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said: Rasul Allah (عليه السلام) said: Indeed, a servant may be detained on account of a sin from among his sins for a hundred years, while he looks at his wives in Paradise enjoying themselves.

Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from ʿĪsā ibn Ayyūb, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: There is no servant except that in his heart there is a white spot. So when he commits a sin, a black spot appears within that spot. If he repents, that blackness goes away; but if he persists in sins, that blackness increases until it covers the whiteness. Then when it has covered the whiteness, its possessor never returns to any good, ever. And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted upon their hearts.”

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Do not bare your teeth openly while you have committed disgraceful deeds, and do not feel secure from the night assault while you have committed evil deeds.

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū ʿAmr al-Madāʾinī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: My father عليه السلام used to say: Indeed, Allah has decreed a decisive decree that He does not bestow a blessing upon a servant and then take it away from him until the servant commits a sin by which he deserves that punishment.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Sadir, who said: A man asked Aba Abdillah (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “So they said: Our Lord, make farther apart the distances of our journeys; and they wronged themselves” — the verse. He (عليه السلام) said: “These were a people who had villages connected to one another, such that some of them could see others, and flowing rivers, and evident wealth. Then they disbelieved in the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and changed what was within themselves of Allah’s well-being, so Allah changed what they had of blessing. Indeed, Allah does not change what is with a people until they change what is within themselves. So Allah sent upon them the flood of al-‘Arim, and it drowned their villages, ruined their dwellings, took away their wealth, and replaced their gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and something of sparse lote trees.” Then he said: “That is how We recompensed them for what they disbelieved; and do We recompense any but the utterly ungrateful?”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Samāʿah, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Allah does not bestow a blessing upon a servant and then take it away from him unless he commits a sin by which he deserves that removal.”

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Haysam ibn Waqid al-Jazari, who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent a Prophet from among His Prophets to his people, and revealed to him: “Say to your people:” There are no inhabitants of a town nor any people who were upon My obedience and were granted ease therein, then changed from what I love to what I dislike, except that I change for them from what they love to what they dislike. And there are no inhabitants of a town nor any household who were upon My disobedience and were afflicted therein by hardship, then changed from what I dislike to what I love, except that I change for them from what they dislike to what they love. And say to them: ‘My mercy has preceded My wrath, so do not despair of My mercy, for no sin is too great before Me for Me to forgive it.’ And say to them: ‘They must not expose themselves, in stubbornness, to My anger, nor belittle My Awliya’, for indeed I have assaults at the time of My anger that nothing from My creation can withstand.’

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm al-Hāshimī, from his grandfather Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Sulaymān al-Jaʿfarī, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a Prophet from among the Prophets: “When I am obeyed, I am pleased; and when I am pleased, I bless, and there is no end to My blessing. And when I am disobeyed, I become wrathful; and when I become wrathful, I curse, and My curse reaches the seventh among the progeny.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said: Indeed, one of you may often be afflicted with fear of the ruler, and that is only because of sins. So guard yourselves against them as much as you are able, and do not persist in them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, raising it, said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: There is no pain more painful to the hearts than sins, and there is no fear more intense than death. What has passed is sufficient for reflection, and death is sufficient as an admonisher.

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Hilāl al-Shāmī, a mawla of Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام), who said: I heard al-Riḍā (عليه السلام) saying: Whenever the servants introduce sins that they had not been doing, Allah introduces for them afflictions that they had not been knowing.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbbād ibn Ṣuhayb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “When the one who knows Me disobeys Me, I set over him one who does not know Me.”

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ibn Arafah, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has in every day and night a caller who calls out: “Restraint, restraint, O servants of Allah, from acts of disobedience to Allah.” So were it not for grazing animals, nursing children, and elderly ones bowed in worship, the punishment would surely be poured down upon you in a pouring, crushing you with a crushing.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: If you shun the major sins which you are forbidden from, We shall expiate from you your evil deeds and admit you to a noble entrance. He عليه السلام said: "The major sins are those for which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the Fire obligatory."

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, who said: One of our companions wrote along with me to Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), asking him about the major sins, how many they are and what they are. So he (عليه السلام) wrote: The major sins are those for which Allah has promised the Fire; whoever avoids them, Allah expiates his evil deeds from him when he is a believer. And the seven destructive ones are: killing the unlawfully protected soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury, reverting to bedouin ways after migration, slandering chaste women, consuming the wealth of the orphan, and fleeing from the battle line.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him saying: The major sins are seven: killing the believer deliberately, slandering the chaste woman, fleeing from the battlefield, reverting to desert life after the hijrah, consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, consuming usury after the clarification, and everything for which Allah has made the Fire obligatory.

Yūnus, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed, among the major sins are disobedience to one's parents, despair of the mercy of Allah, and feeling secure from the plan of Allah. And it has been narrated that the greatest of the major sins is shirk with Allah.

Yūnus, from Ḥammād, from Nuʿmān al-Rāzī, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Whoever commits adultery exits from iman, and whoever drinks wine exits from iman, and whoever deliberately breaks the fast for one day of the month of Ramadan exits from iman.

From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdah, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام): "Does the adulterer not commit adultery while he is a believer?" He said: "No. When he is upon her belly, faith is stripped from him. Then when he rises, it is returned to him. Then if he repeats, it is stripped away." I said: "But he intends to return." So he said: "How many there are who intend to return, yet never return to it ever again."

Yūnus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except al-lamam. He said: “The immoralities are adultery and theft; and al-lamam is that a man falls into a sin, then seeks Allah’s forgiveness for it.” I said: “Is there a station between misguidance and kufr?” He said: “How many the bonds of īmān are!”

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about the major sins, and he said: They are seven in the Book of ʿAlī (عليه السلام): kufr in Allah, killing the soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury after the clarification, consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, fleeing from the battlefield, and reverting to desert-life after the Hijrah. He said: So I said, Are these the greatest sins? He said: Yes. I said: Is consuming one dirham from the wealth of an orphan unjustly graver, or abandoning the salat (prayer)? He said: Abandoning the salat (prayer). I said: Then you did not count abandoning the salat (prayer) among the major sins? So he said: What was the first thing I said to you? He said: I said: Kufr. He said: Indeed, the one who abandons the salat (prayer) is a kāfir, meaning without an excuse.

A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aṣamm, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, ṣalawātullāh ʿalayhi, said: There is no servant except that forty shields are upon him until he commits forty major sins. Then when he commits forty major sins, the shields are uncovered from him, and Allah reveals to them: “Cover My servant with your wings,” so the angels cover him with their wings. He said: Then he leaves nothing of ugliness except that he commits it, until he boasts before the people of his ugly deed. Then the angels say: “O Lord, this servant of Yours leaves nothing except that he has ridden into it, and we are ashamed of what he does.” So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to them: “Lift your wings away from him.” Then when that is done, he begins to hate us, the Ahl al-Bayt. At that point, his covering is torn away in the heaven and his covering in the earth, and the angels say: “O Lord, this servant of Yours has remained with his cover torn away.” So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to them: “If Allah had any need concerning him, He would not have commanded you to lift your wings away from him.” And Ibn Faḍḍāl also narrated it from Ibn Muskān.

ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “The major sins are despairing of the mercy of Allah, losing hope in the relief of Allah, feeling secure from the plan of Allah, killing the soul which Allah has made forbidden, undutifulness to parents, consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, consuming usury after the proof has been established, reverting to Bedouin ways after migration, slandering the chaste woman, and fleeing from the battle line.” Then it was said to him: “What do you say about one who commits a major sin and dies upon it? Does it remove him from faith? And if he is punished for it, will his punishment be like the punishment of the polytheists, or will there be an end for him?” He said: “He exits from Islam if he claims that it is permissible, and for that reason he is punished with the most severe punishment.” But if he acknowledges that it is a major sin, that it is forbidden for him, that he will be punished for it, and that it is not permissible, then he is punished for it, but his punishment is lighter than that of the first one. It removes him from faith, but it does not remove him from Islam.”

Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) regarding the saying of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله): “When a man commits adultery, the spirit of faith departs from him.” He said: “It is His saying:” “And He strengthened them with a spirit from Him.” That is what departs from him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The spirit of faith is taken from him as long as he is upon her belly; so when he descends, faith returns. I said to him, 'What is your view if he only considers it?' He said, 'No.' Do you see that if he considers stealing, would his hand be cut?

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Sabbah ibn Sayaba, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Muhammad ibn 'Abdah said to him, 'Does the adulterer commit adultery while he is a believer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No. When he is upon her belly, faith is stripped from him. So when he arises, it is returned to him.' I said, 'Supposing he intends to return?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'How often do they consider returning, then they do not return.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Aban from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The major sins are seven: among them is killing the soul deliberately, and associating partners with Allah the Magnificent, and slandering the chaste woman, and consuming usury after clear proof, and fleeing from the battle, and adopting pre-Islamic practices after emigration, and disobedience to the parents, and consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly.' He said: 'And adopting pre-Islamic practices and shirk are one (same).'
Aban, from Ziyad Al-Kunasi, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'And the one who, when his father calls him, curses his father, and the one who, when his son answers him, strikes him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Dawood, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'When the man commits adultery, the spirit of faith separates from him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is like the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: and when they spend, they do so not out of extravagance nor stinginess Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is more explicit than this. That is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: and He strengthened them with a Spirit from Him That is the one which separates from him.

Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah does not forgive that which is associated with Him, and He forgives what is below that for whom He wills. The major sins, and what is besides them. I said, 'Do the major sins fall within the exception?' He said, 'Yes.'
Yunus narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'Are the major sins excepted in that He forgives whom He wills?' He said: 'Yes.'

Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'And whoever is given wisdom, he has indeed been given a great deal of good.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The recognition of the Imam and avoiding the major sins upon which Allah has obligated the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Do the major sins (al-kaba'ir) take one out of faith (iman)?' He said: 'Yes.' And what is besides the major sins? The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, and the thief does not steal while he is a believer.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn al-Zayyat, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: Ibn Qays al-Masir and Amr ibn Zarr entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and I think Abu Hanifa was with them. Ibn Qays al-Masir spoke and said: 'We do not expel the people of our call and the people of our religion from faith due to sins and disobedience.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Ibn Qays! As for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he said: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, nor does the thief steal while he is a believer.' So go, you and your companions, wherever you wish.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who commits a major sin from the major sins and then dies. Does that exit him from Islam? And if he is punished, is his punishment like the punishment of the polytheists, or does he have a period and an end? He said: 'The one who commits a major sin from the major sins and alleges that it is permissible, that exits him from Islam and he is punished with the severest punishment. And if he was acknowledging that he sinned and died upon it, that exits him from faith (Iman) and does not exit him from Islam, and his punishment is lighter than the punishment of the first one.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Fear the belittled sins, for they are not forgiven.' I said: 'And what are the belittled sins?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man commits a sin, so he says, 'Good fortune is for me if there had not been for me other than that (sin).''

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ibn Fazzal and Al-Hajjal, all together from Tha'laba from Ziyad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) descended in a barren land, so he said to his companions: 'Bring firewood.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are in a barren land, there is no firewood in it.' He said: 'So let every person bring whatever he is able to bring.' So they brought it until they threw it in front of him, some on top of others. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This is how the sins accumulate.' Then he said: 'Beware of the belittled sins, for every thing has a seeker. Indeed, He who seeks it records what they have sent before and their effects, and We have enumerated everything in a Manifest Imam.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Nahiki, from Ammar ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no small (sin) with persistence (upon it), and there is no major (sin) with seeking forgiveness.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic And when they persist in what they have done, while they know He said: Persistence is when he commits a sin, then does not seek forgiveness from Allah, nor does he discuss repentance with himself. That is persistence.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'No, by Allah! Allah will not accept anything from his obedience, upon his persistence upon something from his disobedience'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The origins of disbelief are three: greed, arrogance, and envy. As for greed, when Adam (peace be upon him) was forbidden from the tree, greed carried him to eat from it; and as for arrogance, it was Iblees when he was commanded to prostrate to Adam, so he refused; and as for envy, it was the two sons of Adam when one of them killed his companion.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, Al Sakuni, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) narrated, saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The pillars of disbelief are four: desire (al-raghbah), awe/fear (al-rahibah), resentment (al-sakhat), and anger (al-ghadab).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Abdullah al-Dihqan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The first of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was disobeyed with were six: love of the world, and love of leadership, and love of food, and love of sleep, and love of comfort, and love of women.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That a man from Khas'am came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Which of the deeds is the most hated to Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' He said, 'The association (Shirk) with Allah.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Cutting off the relationship.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Enjoining the evil and forbidding the good.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Yazeed al-Sa'ig, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man who holds this position (of Wilayah/leadership), if he narrates he lies, and if he promises he breaks his word, and if he is entrusted he betrays. What is his status?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the lowest of the levels of disbelief, but he is not a disbeliever.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the signs of wretchedness are the stillness of the eye, the hardness of the heart, the intensity of greed in seeking the world, and persistence in sin.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people and said: 'Shall I inform you of the most evil of you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The one who withholds his gifts, strikes his slave, and provisions himself alone.' So they thought that Allah had not created a creature more evil than this. Then he said: 'Shall I inform you of the one who is more evil than that?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The one whose goodness is not hoped for, nor is there safety from his evil.' So they thought that Allah had not created a creature more evil than this. Then he said: 'Shall I inform you of the one who is more evil than that?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The foul-mouthed, cursing one, who when the believers are mentioned in his presence, he curses them, and when they mention him, they curse him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three (characteristics); whoever possesses them is a hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims that he is a Muslim.' He who, when entrusted, betrays; and when he narrates, lies; and when he promises, breaks his promise. Surely Allah does not love the treacherous. Then the Curse of Allah be on him if he was one of the liars. And mention Ismail in the Book; he was truthful in (his) promise, and he was a Messenger, a Prophet.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I inform you of those who are most remote from me in likeness?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah!' He said: 'The immoral, the scandalous, the foul-mouthed, the stingy, the arrogant, the malicious, the envious, the hard of heart, the one remote from every hope of goodness, the one not safe from every evil feared.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Asbat, raising it to Salman, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intends the destruction of a servant, He removes bashfulness from him. So when bashfulness is removed from him, you will not meet him except as deceitful and causing deception. So when he is deceitful and causing deception, trustworthiness is removed from him. So when trustworthiness is removed from him, you will not meet him except as rough and harsh. So when he is rough and harsh, the noose of faith is removed from him. So when the noose of faith is removed from him, you will not meet him except as a Satan, accursed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad Al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three (things) are cursed. Accursed is the one who does these – The defecation in the shade of encampments (public places), and the prevention of the allocated water, and the blocking of public roads'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three (things) are cursed. Accursed is the one who does this – The defecation in the shade of encampments (public places), and the prevention of the allocated water, and the blocking of the travelled road'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I inform you of the worst of your men?' We said, 'Yes, O Rasool-Allah!' So he said: 'Among the worst of your men are the slanderer, the audacious, the obscene, the one who eats alone, the one who withholds his provision, the one who beats his slave, and the one who causes his dependents to seek shelter with others.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muyassar, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I cursed five, and every answered Prophet [cursed them too]: The one who adds to the Book of Allah, and the one who abandons my Sunnah, and the one who denies the Divine Decree of Allah, and the one who legalizes for himself from my offspring what Allah has prohibited, and the one who appropriates the Fay' [booty/khums] for himself.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: To Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri in the mosque: 'Woe to you, O Abbad! Beware of al-riya' (showing-off), for whoever works for other than Allah, Allah will entrust him to the one he worked for.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Yazeed ibn Khalifa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'All showing-off is shirk. Indeed, whoever does a deed for the people, his reward is upon the people, and whoever does a deed for Allah, his reward is upon Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah Al-Madainy from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord He (peace be upon him) said: The man does something from the rewardable deeds, not seeking the Face of Allah by it, but rather seeking the approval (purification) of the people, desiring that the people hear of it (him). So this is the one who has associated (committed Shirk) with the worship of his Lord. Then he (peace be upon him) said: There is no servant who conceals good, so the days pass forever until Allah manifests goodness for him, and there is no servant who conceals evil, so the days pass forever until Allah manifests the evil for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Arafa, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Woe to you, O Ibn Arafa! Work for the sake of other than showing off and other than being heard of. Indeed, whoever works for other than Allah, Allah will dismiss him to what he worked for. Woe to you! No one performs a deed except that Allah returns it to him; if it is good, it is good, and if it is evil, it is evil.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I was having dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when he recited this Verse: But! The human being is evidence against himself * Although he puts forth his excuses O Abu Hafs! The human being cannot get closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by going against what Allah the Exalted Knows. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying: 'The one who does a secretive deed, Allah would Return it with a Returning - if it was good, so good, and if it was evil, so evil'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The angel joyfully ascends with the deed of the servant. So when he ascends with his good deed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Make it in Sijjin, for it is not I whom he intended with it."'

And by his chain, he said, Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: There are three signs for the show-off: He is active when he sees the people, and he is lazy when he is alone, and he loves to be praised in the entirety of his affairs.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Salim who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah (Mighty and Majestic) Says: 'I am the best Associate. The one who associates someone else with Me in a deed he does, I will not Accept it except what was (done) for Me purely'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who displays to the people what Allah loves and opposes Allah with what He dislikes, he will meet Allah while He is at war with him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Fadl Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: What is one of you doing by making a good deed apparent and concealing a bad one? Does he not reflect upon himself and realize that it is not so? And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'But indeed, the human being is a witness against himself.' Indeed, the inner self, when sound, strengthens the outward appearance. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jamhur, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiya, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who conceals goodness except that the days will not pass until Allah manifests goodness to him; and there is no servant who conceals evil except that the days will not pass until Allah manifests evil to him'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yahya ibn Bashir, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who intends Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with the little of his deeds, Allah will manifest for him more than what he intended; and the one who intends the people with the much of his deeds, through the exhaustion of his body and the wakefulness of his night, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will refuse except that He belittles it in the eyes of those who hear him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon the people wherein their inner secrets will become foul, and their outward appearances will become beautiful, out of greed for the world, not intending by it what is with their Lord. Their religion will be show-off (riya'), with no fear mingling in them. Allah will encompass them with punishment, so they will call out to Him with the supplication of the drowning one, but He will not answer them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I was having dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when he recited this Verse: But! The human being is evidence against himself * Although he puts forth his excuses O Abu Hafs! What is the human doing if he apologises to the people with against what Allah knows from him. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying: ‘The one does something secretly, Allah would Clothe it in return – if good, so good, and if evil, so evil’.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: The remaining upon the deed is more difficult than the deed itself. He said, 'And what is the remaining upon the deed?' He said, 'The man maintains relationships by helping (a relative) and he spends an expenditure for the Sake of Allah Alone, there being no associates for Him, so a secretive good deed is Recorded for him. Then he mentions it and it gets Deleted, and an open good deed is Recorded for him. Then he mentions it (again), and a showing-off is Recorded for him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who performs an act of goodness, and a person sees him, and he is pleased by that. He said: 'There is no harm. There is no one who does not love that goodness be apparent for him among the people, provided that he did not do that for that [reason alone].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), that he mentioned a man and said: He loves leadership. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Two fierce wolves among sheep whose shepherd has scattered are not more harmful in the religion of the Muslim than leadership.' He loves leadership. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Two fierce wolves among sheep whose shepherd has scattered are not more harmful in the religion of the Muslims than leadership.'
From him, from Ahmad, from Saeed ibn Janah, from his brother Abu Aamir, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: The one who seeks the leadership, is destroyed.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Muskan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Beware of these leaders who assume leadership, for by Allah, no slipper would tap behind a man except that he would be destroyed and cause destruction.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazie, and others, they raised it (to the Imam), saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Accursed is the one who is a leader! Accursed is the one who intends with it! Accursed is the one who discusses to himself with it!'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ayoub, from Abu Aqila Al-Sayrafi, who said, 'Karram narrated to me from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said,' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Beware of leadership (al-ri'asah), and beware of treading the heels of men.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! As for leadership, I have recognized it, and as for treading the heels of men, two-thirds of what is in my hand is not except from what I have treading the heels of men.' So he said to me: 'That is not where you are going with it. Beware of establishing a man besides the Proof (al-Hujjah), so you verify him in everything he says.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'Woe be unto you, O Abu Al-Rabie! Do not seek the leadership, nor become a wolf, nor devour the people by us, so Allah would impoverish you. And do not say regarding us what we do not say regarding ourselves, for you will be made to pause and inevitably be questioned. So if you are truthful, we will ratify you, and if you are a liar, we will belie you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ibn Mayyah, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who seeks leadership is destroyed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do you think that I do not know your best among you from your worst? Yes, by Allah, and indeed your worst is the one who loves to be followed (tread upon). Indeed, it is inevitable that he is either a liar or one deficient in opinion.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yusuf al-Bazzaz, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Indeed, among the people with the most intense regret on the Day of Judgment is the one who described [himself as] just, then acted contrary to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Qutaybah al-A'sha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Indeed, among the people with the most intense punishment on the Day of Judgment is the one who portrayed justice and acted without it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ibn Abi Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, among the people with the greatest regret on the Day of Judgment is the one who portrayed justice, then opposed it to something else.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So they shall be flung into it, they and the erring ones.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Baseer! They were a people who portrayed justice with their tongues, then were opposing to something else.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Khaythama, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Deliver to our Shias that whatever is with Allah cannot be attained except by deeds; and deliver to our Shias that the people with the utmost of regrets on the Day of Judgment would be the one who portrayed justice, then opposed it to something else'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, all of them, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) the laws of Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (peace be upon them): Tawhid (Oneness), Ikhlas (Sincerity), removing the idols, the upright Hanif nature, tolerance, neither priesthood nor wandering, in which He made the good things permissible and the bad things forbidden, and He lifted from them their burdens and the shackles that were upon them. Then He imposed upon him therein Salat, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj, enjoining good and forbidding evil, the Halal and the Haram, inheritance, hudud (legal punishments), faraid (obligations), and Jihad in the way of Allah. He added for him Wudu, and favored him with the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha) and the endings of the Surah Al-Baqarah and Al-Mufassal. He made permissible for him the war booty (Mughnam) and the spoils of land (Fay'), and supported him with awe, and made the earth for him a place of prostration (Masjid) and a purifier. He sent him to all, to the white and the black, to the Jinn and the humans. He gave him the Jizyah, the captives of the polytheists, and their ransom. Then he was burdened with what no one of the Prophets was burdened with, and a sword was sent down to him from the sky without a sheath, and it was said to him: 'Fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Therefore bear up patiently as did the Determined Ones from the Messengers bear up with'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Nuh, and Ibrahim, and Musa, and Isa, and Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)'. I said, 'How did they come to be the Determined Ones?' He said: 'Because Nuh was sent with a Book and a Law, and everyone who came after Nuh took by the Book of Nuh, and his Law and his manifesto, until Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came with the Parchments, and with determination he neglected the Book of Nuh, not having disbelieved in it.' So every Prophet who came after Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took by the Law of Ibrahim, and his manifesto, and by the Parchments, until Musa came with the Torah and his Law, and his manifesto, and with determination he neglected the Parchments. And every Prophet who came after Musa (peace be upon him) took by the Torah, and his Law, and his manifesto, until the Messiah (peace be upon him) came with the Evangel, and with determination he neglected the Law of Musa, as well as his manifesto. So every Prophet who came after the Messiah adhered to his Law and his manifesto, until Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) came. So he came with the Quran and with his Law and his manifesto. Thus, his Permissible is a Permissible up to the Day of Judgement, and his Prohibition is a Prohibition up to the Day of Judgement. So, these are the Determined Ones from the Messengers (peace be upon them).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of quarrelling and disputing, for these two cause illness in the hearts towards the brothers, and upon them hypocrisy grows.'
And by his chain He (peace be upon him) said: Whoever targets Allah as a goal (or mark) for quarrels, he will soon make much transition (from truth to falsehood).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not quarrel with a forbearing one, nor with a foolish one, for the forbearing one would detest you and the foolish one would harm you.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Umar Bin Yazeed, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Almost every time Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to me, he said: O Muhammad! Fear the hatred of the men and their animosity'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Kindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Beware of disputing with the men.'
From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abdul Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Beware of disputes/quarreling, for it inherits disgrace and manifests vulnerability.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Anbasa al-Abid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Beware of disputes, for they occupy the heart, cause hypocrisy, and earn grudges.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Angel Gabriel (peace be upon him) hardly came to me except that he would say: O Muhammad! Guard against the enmity of men and their hostility.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Mihran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) did not come to me at all except he advised me, and the last of his words to me were: 'Beware of consulting the people, for it uncovers the bareness and removes the honour'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) did not entrust me with anything [more] than what he entrusted me with regarding the animosity of the men.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdullah, from one of his companions, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who cultivates enmity will reap what he sowed.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Muyassar, who said: Anger was mentioned in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a man becomes angry and is not pleased until he enters the Fire. Therefore, whoever of men gets angry upon a people while he is standing, let him sit down immediately, for the filth of Satan will depart from him. And whoever of men gets angry upon a relative, let him draw near to him and let him touch him, for the relative, when touched, calms down.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Dawud, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Anger is the key to every evil.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: A Bedouin man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I dwell in the desert, so teach me the comprehensive words.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I order you not to get angry.' The Bedouin reiterated the question to him three times, until the man returned to himself and said, 'I shall not ask about anything after this. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not order me except with good.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And my father used to say: What is more difficult than anger? Indeed, when a man gets angry, he kills the soul which Allah has prohibited, and he slanders the married woman.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdul A'ala who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Teach me an advice which I can be advised with.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me an advice which I can be advised with.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Go, and do not be angry.' Then he reiterated to him, so he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Go, and do not be angry' – three times.'
From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn Amira, from the one who heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The one who restrains his anger, Allah will veil his bareness.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib Al-Sijistani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is written in the Torah, in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! Withhold your anger from the one whom I have given you authority over, I shall restrain My anger from you.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, and there is an increase in it: 'And when you are oppressed with an injustice, be pleased with My support for you, for My support for you is better than your support for yourself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is written in the Torah: O son of Adam! Remember Me when you are angered, I shall remember you during My anger, so I shall not eliminate you among those I eliminate.' And whenever you are oppressed with an injustice, be pleased with My support for you, for My support for you is better than your support for yourself.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, all from al-Wasshash, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abi Khadija, from Mu'la ibn Khunays, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me.' He said, 'Go and do not be angry.' The man said, 'I am content with that,' and went to his people. He found that a conflict had arisen among them; they had lined up in rows and put on their weapons. When he saw that, he put on his weapon, then stood with them. Then he remembered the words of the Messenger of Allah, 'Do not be angry,' so he threw down the weapon and came walking to the people who were the enemies of his people, saying, 'O you all! Whatever injury, or killing, or a blow without lasting effect was from you, upon me is (the compensation) from my wealth; I will fulfill it for you.' The people said, 'So whatever it was, it is for you; we are more entitled to it than you are.' He said, 'So the people reconciled and the anger departed.' He said, 'So the people reconciled and the anger departed.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, this anger is an ember from Satan that is kindled in the heart of the son of Adam. And when one of you becomes angry, his eyes turn red, his veins puff up, and Satan enters him. So when one of you fears that from himself, let him press himself to the earth, for the filth of Satan will depart from him at that time.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of his companions, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Anger is the destruction of the wise heart.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He who does not control his anger does not control his intellect.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja' Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who restrains his self from the vanities of people, Allah will discharge his self on the Day of Judgment; and the one who restrains his anger from people, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will restrain the punishment from him on the Day of Judgment.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who restrains his anger from the people, Allah would restrain the punishment from him on the Day of Judgment.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fear Allah and let not some of you envy others.' Indeed, from the laws of Isa ibn Maryam was traveling about in the lands, so he went out in one of his tours and with him was a man from his companions of short stature, and he used to frequently accompany Isa (peace be upon him). So when Isa reached the sea, he said: 'In the Name of Allah,' with correct certainty from him, and he walked upon the back of the water. So the short man said when he looked at Isa (peace be upon him) risking it, 'In the Name of Allah' with correct certainty from him. So he walked upon the water and caught up with Isa (peace be upon him). Then self-conceitedness entered into himself, so he said (to himself), 'This is Isa, the Spirit of Allah, walking upon the water and I am walking upon the water. So what is his merit over me?' So he sank into the water, and he cried for help to Isa. So he grabbed him from the water and extracted him. Then he said to him: 'What did you say, O Shortie!?' He said, 'I said, 'This is the Spirit of Allah, walking upon the water, and I am walking upon the water', and the self-conceitedness entered me due to that'. So Isa said to him: 'You had placed yourself in other than the place which Allah had Placed you in, therefore Allah Detested you upon what you said. So repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from what you said'. So the man repented and returned to his status which Allah had Placed him in. Therefore, fear Allah and you should not envy each other.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Poverty almost becomes disbelief, and envy almost overcomes destiny.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The disaster for the Religion is envy, self-conceit, and pride.

Yunus narrated from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'O son of Imran! Do not envy the people for what I have given them from My grace, and do not extend your eyes towards that, and do not let your soul follow it, for the envious one is displeased with My bounties, obstructing My apportionment which I have apportioned among My servants. And whoever is like that, then I am not from him and he is not from Me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Al-Fudayl ibn Ayaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The believer envies (in a good way) but does not envy (in a bad way), and the hypocrite envies (in a bad way) but does not envy (in a good way).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He who is prejudiced (or is made prejudiced for him) has removed the rein of faith from his neck.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Durost ibn Abi Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is prejudicial or is been prejudicial to, so the rein of Emān has been loosened from his neck'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He in whose heart is a mustard seed of prejudice (tribalism/partisanship), Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment along with the Bedouins of the Pre-Islamic period.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Khadir, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is prejudicial (shows bias/tribalism), Allah will join him with a gang from the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan ibn Mihran, from Aamir ibn al-Simt, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Prejudice (bias) would not admit anyone to Paradise except the prejudice of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and that is when he embraced Islam out of anger for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the story of the camel's stomach contents which were thrown upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

From him, from his father, from Fazalat, from Dawood ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Angels used to reckon that Iblees was from them, and it was in the Knowledge of Allah that he was not from them. So he brought out what was within himself with prejudice and anger, so he said: 'You created me from fire and You created him from clay'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked about al-‘asabiyyah (tribal prejudice/bias), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The al-‘asabiyyah upon which its doer sins is that a man sees the evil ones of his people as better than the good ones of other people. And it is not from al-‘asabiyyah if a man loves his people, but from al-‘asabiyyah is that he assists his people upon injustice.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Aban, from Hukeym who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the least of atheism (disbelief), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Arrogance is the least of it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Arrogance (al-kibr) may be found in the worst of people from every race, and arrogance is the Gown of Allah. So whoever disputes with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His Gown, Allah will not increase him except in lowliness.' Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by one of the streets of Medina, and Sawda was gathering manure. It was said to her, 'Move aside from the way of the Messenger of Allah!' So she said, 'The road is open (wide enough).' Then some of the people thought of grabbing her, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Leave her, for she is tyrannical (bully).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The Honour is the Gown of Allah, and the Pride is His Garment. So whoever holds onto any of these, Allah will cast him into Hell.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba, from Ma'mar ibn Umar ibn Ata', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Kibr (Pride/Arrogance) is the Gown of Allah, and the arrogant one disputes with Allah regarding His Gown.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Lays al-Muradi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Kibr (Pride/Arrogance) is the Gown of Allah. So whoever disputes with Allah regarding anything from that, Allah will cast him into the Fire.

From him, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He would not enter Paradise, the one in whose heart is the weight of a particle of arrogance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: He (the Imam) said: 'He will not enter Paradise whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance.' I said, 'So I said, 'We are from Allah and to Him we are returning' (Istirja'). He said: 'What is the matter with you saying Istirja'?' I said, 'Because of what I heard from you.' He said: 'It is not where you are going (understanding it). Rather, I mean the rejection (of Wilayah). Rather, it (arrogance) is the rejection (of Wilayah).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Arrogance is that you belittle the people and consider the Truth as foolish.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abdul Al-'ala ibn Ayn, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The greatest of arrogance is belittling the people and considering the Truth as foolish.' I said: 'And what is belittling the people and considering the Truth as foolish?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ignoring the Truth and maligning its people. So whoever does that, he has snatched from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His Gown (of Pride).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from his brother who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The arrogant ones will be made into the form of particles, and people will trample upon them until Allah is finished with the Reckoning.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from someone else, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abdul A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is arrogance?' He said, 'The greatest of arrogance is that you consider the Truth as foolish and you belittle the people.' I said, 'And what is considering the Truth as foolish?' He said, 'Ignorance of the Truth and criticizing its people.'

From him, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I eat good food, smell pleasant scents, ride luxurious animals, and a servant follows me. If you see any arrogance in this, I will not do it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) paused, then said, 'The accursed tyrant is the one who belittles people and ignores the truth.' Umar said, 'As for the truth, I do not ignore it, but I do not know what belittling is.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The one who considers people insignificant and is arrogant over them, that is the tyrant.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three (people), Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Judgment, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: an aged adulterer, a tyrannical king, and a stingy arrogant one.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when the elder Yaqub (peace be upon him) came to Yusuf (peace be upon him), the might of kingship entered him, so he did not descend to (welcome) him. So Jibra'il (peace be upon him) descended and said: 'O Yusuf! Extend your palm.' So a shining light came out from it and became in the atmosphere of the sky. So Yusuf said: 'O Jibra'il, what is this light which came out from my palm?' So he said: 'Prophet-hood has been removed from your descendants as a punishment for what caused you not to descend to the elder Yaqub, so there will not be a prophet from your descendants.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no servant but that there is wisdom in his head and an Angel withholds it. So when he is arrogant, (the Angel) says to him: 'Be humble, may Allah drop you!' So he does not cease to be the greatest of the people within himself and the smallest of the people in the eyes of the people. And when he is humble, Allah, Might and Majestic, raises him, then (the Angel) says to him: 'Be dignified, may Allah dignify you!' So he does not cease to be the smallest of the people within himself and the highest of the people in the eyes of the people.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of his companions, from al-Nahdi, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq Sha'ar, from Abdullah ibn al-Munzir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no one who becomes arrogant except due to a disgrace he finds within himself.' And in another hadith, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'There is no man who becomes arrogant or tyrannical except due to the disgrace he finds within himself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Asbat, from a man from our companions, from the people of Khurasan, from the descendants of Ibrahim ibn Sayyar, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah knew that sin is better for the believer than self-conceit, and if it were not for that, a believer would never be tested with sin.
From him, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from his brother Abu 'Amir, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one in whom self-conceit enters, is destroyed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, from Ali ibn Suweyd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the self-conceit that ruins the deed, so he said: 'Self-conceit has levels. One of them is that the evil of the servant's deed is adorned for him, so he sees it as good, so it astounds him and he reckons that he has done something good; and another is that the servant believes in his Lord, so he thinks he is doing a favour upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while for Allah, upon him with regards to it, is actually the Favour.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a man commits a sin, so he regrets it, and he performs a deed, so that pleases him, so he delays/slacks from that state of his. So for him to remain in that state of his (of regret) is better for him than what entered into him (of self-satisfaction/conceit).
