Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Nadr ibn Qirwash, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A scholar came to a worshipper and said to him, 'How is your prayer?' So he said, 'One like me is asked about his prayer, and I have been worshipping Allah since such and such (time).' He said, 'So how is your weeping?' He said, 'I weep until my tears flow.' So the scholar said to him, 'Indeed, your laughing while you are fearful (of Allah) is superior to your weeping while you are self-conceited. The self-conceited one, nothing from his deeds ascends.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from one of our companions, from one of the companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: Two men entered the Masjid; one was a worshipper and the other an immoral one. When they exited the Masjid, the immoral one became truthful (a siddiq) and the worshipper became immoral. This is because the worshipper entered the Masjid boasting about his worship, so his focus remained on that boasting, whereas the immoral one focused on remorse for his immorality and sought forgiveness from Allah, Exalted and Mighty, for the sins he had committed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man performs a deed while he is fearful and anxious, then he performs something from the righteousness, so something like self-importance enters him because of it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His state in the first state, while he was fearful, is a better state than his state of self-importance.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'While Musa (peace be upon him) was seated, Iblees came towards him, and upon him was a hood with various colors. So when he approached Musa (peace be upon him), he removed the hood and stood by Musa and greeted him. So Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Iblees." Musa said: "You, may Allah bring close your dwelling." He said: "Indeed, I only came to greet you due to your status with Allah."' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "So what is this hood?" He said: "By it I snatch the hearts of the children of Adam." Musa said: "So inform me of the sin which, when the son of Adam commits it, you gain mastery over him." He said: "When his self astounds him, and he considers his deeds numerous, and his sin seems small in his eyes."' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Dawood (peace be upon him): "O Dawood! Give glad tidings to the sinners and warn the truthful." He said: "How do I give glad tidings to the sinners and warn the truthful?" He said: "O Dawood! Give glad tidings to the sinners that I accept repentance and pardon the sin, and warn the truthful that they should not be self-conceited with their deeds, for there is no servant whom I set up for reckoning except that he would be destroyed."'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Hassan, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: How ugly it would be for the believer if there were a desire for him which disgraces him.

From him, from his father, from the one who mentioned it to whom it reached, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: 'The worst servant is a servant for whom there is greed driving him, and the worst servant is a servant for whom there is a desire disgracing him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Abdul-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Al-Zuhri, who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'I saw that all goodness has gathered in cutting off greed for what is in the hands of the people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from Musa ibn, from Musa ibn Sallam, from Sa'dan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is that which establishes faith in the servant?' He said, 'Piety (restraint).' And what is that which removes it from him?' He said, 'Greed.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever has a share of harshness (in his behaviour), the Emān is separated from him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If harshness (al-khuruq) were a visible creature, there would not be anything among what Allah created uglier than it.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, evil manners spoil the deed just as vinegar spoils honey.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuses the repentance of the one with bad manners.' It was said, 'And how is that so, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Because when he repents from a sin, he falls into a sin greater than it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from the one who mentioned it, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, evil character/manners spoils faith just as vinegar spoils honey.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Is'haq ibn Ghalib, from Al Husayn ibn Mihran, from Abdullah ibn Usman, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who worsens his manners, punishes his own self.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari narrated to me from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Ziyadi from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha who said, 'Aban ibn Uthman narrated to us from Fudayl from Abu Hamza from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:' Islam is built upon five: upon the Salat, and the Zakat, and the Sawm, and the Hajj, and the Wilayah, and we did not call out with anything as we called out with the Wilayah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Set me upon the limits of faith.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and the acknowledgement of what he brought from Allah, and the five prayers, and the payment of zakat, and fasting the month of Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to the House, and the Wilayah of our Wali and the enmity of our enemies, and entering with the truthful.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Islam is built upon five: upon the Salat, and the Zakat, and the Sawm, and the Hajj, and the Wilayah. And nothing was called out to like what was called out to regarding the Wilayah. So the people took the four and neglected this, meaning the Wilayah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Al-Arzamy, from his father, from Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: He said: The essence (athafiyy) of Islam is three: Salat, Zakat, and Wilayah. Not one of them is valid except with its two companions.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abdullah ibn al-Salt, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Islam is built upon five things: upon Salat, Zakat, Hajj, Sawm, and Wilayah. Zurara said, So I said, And which of those is superior? He said: Wilayah is superior because it is their key, and the Wali (Guardian) is the proof upon them. I said, Then which follows that in superiority? He said: Salat. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Salat is the pillar of your religion. He said, I said, Then which follows it in superiority? He said: Zakat, because He paired it with it and began with Salat before it; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Zakat removes sins. I said, And which follows it in superiority? He said: Hajj. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And to Allah is the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to undertake a way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Self-sufficient above the worlds. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: An accepted Hajj is better than twenty optional Salats. And whoever circumambulates this House with a circumambulation in which he counts its seven, and performs well his two Raka'ats, Allah will forgive him. And he said regarding the Day of Arafah and the Day of Muzdalifah what he said. I said, So what follows it? He said: Sawm (Fasting). I said, And what is the matter that Sawm became the last of all that? He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Fasting is a shield from the Fire. He said, Then he said: Indeed, the most superior of things is that which, if it is missed by you, there is no repentance from it except that you return to it and fulfill it exactly. Indeed, Salat, Zakat, Hajj, and Wilayah: nothing can occur in their place besides their fulfillment. And indeed, Sawm, if it is missed by you, or you are deficient, or you travel in it, you fulfill its place with other days, and you atone for that sin with charity, and there is no Qada (making up) upon you. And from those four, nothing else suffices you in its place. Then he said: The peak of the matter, and its hump, and its key, and the door of the things, and the Pleasure of the Beneficent is the obedience to the Imam after knowing him. Indeed, Allah,

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Islam is built upon five: Wilayah, Salat, Zakat, fasting of the month of Ramadan, and Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Isa ibn al-Sariy, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Narrate to me about that upon which the pillars of Islam are built, so that when I adhere to it, my deeds will be purified and the ignorance of what I do not know after it will not harm me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the affirmation of what he brought from Allah, and the right in wealth of Zakat, and the Wilayah which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded, which is the Wilayah of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever dies and does not know his Imam, dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority from among you.' So it was Ali (peace be upon him), then after him it became Hasan, then after him Husayn, then after him Ali ibn Husayn, then after him Muhammad ibn Ali. Then the matter remains thus. The earth does not become correct except with an Imam, and whoever dies without knowing his Imam dies a death of ignorance. And the neediest of what one of you will be to his recognition is when his soul reaches here. He said, and he pointed with his hand to his chest, saying at that time: 'I was upon a good matter.'

From him, from Abu Al-Jaroud who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! Do you recognize my affection for you, my severance from others towards you, and my allegiance to you?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' So I said, 'So I ask you a question to which you answer me, for I am blind of vision, have little ability to walk, and am not able to visit you at all times.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Ask for your need.' I said, 'Inform me of your Religion which you are making to be the Religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, you and your family, so that I may make it the Religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you have shortened the speech, you have indeed magnified the question. By Allah! I will surely give you my Religion and the Religion of my forefathers which we make to be the Religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: the testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the acknowledgement of what he brought from Allah, and the Wilayah for our Wali, and the disavowal from our enemies, and the submission to our command, and the awaiting of our Qaim, and the striving and the piety.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard him asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me about the Religion which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Necessitated upon the servants, which they have no leeway for being ignorant of, nor would anything else be Accepted from them. What is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat it to me.' So he repeated to him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony that there is no god except for Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and establishing the Salat, and giving the Zakat, and Hajj of the House by the one who has the capacity for a way to it, and Fasting the Month of Ramadan.' Then he was silent for a while, then said: 'And the Wilayah,' twice. Then he said: 'This is which Allah Necessitated upon the servants.' And the Lord will not Ask the servants on the Day of Judgement, saying: 'Why did you not increase upon what I Necessitate upon you?' But, the one who increases (the deeds), Allah would Increase (for) him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made a Sunnah, a beautiful Sunnah. It is befitting for the people to take by it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Abu Zayd al-Hallal, from Abdul Hameed ibn Abu al-A'la al-Azdi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed five (obligations) upon His creatures, so He granted concession in four, and did not grant concession in one.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan, from Amr ibn Hurayth, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was in the house of his brother Abdullah ibn Muhammad. I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what caused you to move to this house?' He said, 'Seeking solitude.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, shall I relate my religion to you?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'I make a religion of Allah with the testimony that there is no god except Allah Alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that the Hour is coming, no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves, and the establishment of Salat, and the giving of Zakat, and the fasting of the month of Ramadan, and the Hajj of the House, and the Wilayah of Ali, Commander of the Faithful, after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Wilayah of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and the Wilayah of Ali ibn al-Husayn, and the Wilayah of Muhammad ibn Ali, and for you after him, may the prayers of Allah be upon them all, and that you are my Imams, upon it I live and upon it I die, and I make a religion of Allah by it.' He said, 'O Amr, by Allah, this is the religion of Allah and the religion of my forefathers, which they made a religion of Allah with in private and in public. Therefore, fear Allah and restrain your tongue except from goodness, and do not say,

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'Shall I not inform you of Islam, its root, its branch, and the peak of its hump?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'As for its root, it is the Salat, and its branch is the Zakat, and the peak of its hump is the Jihad.' Then he said: 'If you wish, I will inform you of the doors of goodness.' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'The Sawm is a shield from the Fire, and the Sadaqah removes the mistakes, and the standing of the man in the depth of the night with the Dhikr of Allah.' Their sides forsake their beds

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Ghurrah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, foolishness is a lowly character trait; he extends himself (dominates) over those who are below him, and he submits to those who are above him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), regarding two men insulting each other, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The initiator among them is more unjust, and his burden (of sin) and the burden of his companion are upon him, as long as the oppressed one does not transgress.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The most hateful of the creatures of Allah is a servant whom the people fear his tongue.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you see a man who does not care what he says nor what is said to him, then he is either a straying one or an associate of Satan.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa,man ibn 'Isa, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Suleym ibn Qays, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah has prohibited Paradise upon every immoral one, obscene one, little of shame, nor caring what he says nor what is said for him, for if you scrutinize him, you will not find him except as a strayed one or an associate of Satan.' So it was said, 'O Rasool-Allah, and among the people are associates of Satan?' So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Have you not read the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: and shares with them in wealth and the children?' He (the narrator) said, 'And a man asked a Scholar, 'Is there among the people, the one who does not care what is said for him?' He said: 'The one who exposes the obscenities to the people and he knows that they would not be leaving him. So that is the one who does not care what he says and what is said regarding him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jameela, raising it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah hates the obscene, the self-practicing obscenity.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn Nadr, from Amr ibn Nu'man Al-Ju'fi, who said: There was a friend of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who rarely left his side. Whenever he went to a place, the friend would go with him. One time, while they were walking among the shoemakers, and with them was a Sindian slave boy walking behind them, the man turned around three times looking for his slave but did not see him. When he looked a fourth time, he said, 'O son of the adulteress! Where were you?' He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) raised his hand and struck his own forehead with it, then said, 'Glory be to Allah! You slander his mother. I used to think you had piety (war'), but it appears you do not.' The man said, 'May I be your ransom! His mother is a Sindian woman, a polytheist.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do you not know that for every community there is a form of marriage? Stay away from me.' He said: So I did not see him walking with him until death separated the two of them. And in another report, he said: 'For every community there is a form of marriage by which they are restrained from adultery.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If obscenity had a form/resemblance, its resemblance would be evil.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There was a man among the Children of Israel who supplicated to Allah that He grant him a son for three years. When he saw that Allah was not answering him, he said, 'O Lord! Am I far from You, so You do not hear me, or are You close to me, so You do not answer me?' He said: So a visitor came to him in his dream and said, 'You have been supplicating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for three years with an obscene tongue, an arrogant heart that is not pious, and an intention that is not sincere. So desist from your obscenities, let your heart fear Allah, and let your intention be improved.' He said: So the man did that, then supplicated to Allah, and a son was born to him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The obscenities is from the disloyalties, and the disloyal one would be in the Fire

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, immorality, obscenity, and insolence are from hypocrisy.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah hates the obscene, the vulgar, and the insistent beggar.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ayesha: 'O Ayesha! The obscenity, had it been represented by an image, would be an evil image'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his men, who said: The one who is obscene upon his Muslim brother, Allah would Remove the Blessings of his sustenance from him, and Allocate him to his own self, and Spoil his life upon him.

From him, from Moalla, from Ahmad ibn Gassan, from Sama'at who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said to me initiating: O Sama'at! What is this which is between you and your camelier? Beware of becoming immoral, or vociferous, or cursing! So I said, By Allah! That was so because he had been unjust to me. So he said: If he has been unjust to you, so you have profited upon him. This is not from my deeds nor do I order my Shias with it. Seek Forgiveness of your Lord and do not repeat. I said, I seek Forgiveness of Allah and I shall not repeat.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was one day with Ayesha when a man sought permission to enter. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of the clan.' So Ayesha stood up and entered the house, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave permission to the man. When he entered, he turned his face towards him with a cheerful expression, speaking with him until he finished and left his presence. Ayesha said: 'O Messenger of Allah! While you were mentioning this man with what you mentioned, then you turned your face to him with cheerfulness?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said at that: 'Among the worst of the servants of Allah is the one whose company is disliked due to his obscenity.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of people in the presence of Allah on the Day of Judgment are those who are honored out of fear of their evil.'
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whom the people fear his tongue, so he would be in the Fire'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most evil of the people on the Day of Judgment will be those who are honoured out of fear of their evil.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The quickest of the evil to receive punishment is transgression (al-baghyu).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Iblees says to his army, 'Cast envy and transgression between them, for both of these equate to Shirk in the presence of Allah.'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Misma'a Abu Sayyar, that Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) wrote to him in a letter: Be careful that you do not speak with a word of transgression ever, even if it pleases yourself and your clan.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib and Yaqoub Al Sarraj, altogether, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'O people! The transgressor will be guiding his companions to the Fire, and that the first one who transgressed against Allah was Anaaq, daughter of Adam. Thus, the first one whom Allah killed was Anaaq; and when sitting she would occupy one acre. And she had twenty fingers, in every finger there being two nails similar to a scythe. So Allah made a lion like the elephant, and a wolf like the camel, and an eagle like the mule to kill her. So they killed her, and Allah has killed the tyrants upon the best of their states, and (when they were) as safe as they could have been.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Wonder at the arrogant, the proud one, who was yesterday a drop of fluid, then tomorrow he will be a carcass.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The calamity of the lineage is the pride and the self-important'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan, from Uqba ibn Bashir Al-Asadi, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I am Uqba ibn Bashir Al-Asadi, and I am of noble lineage among my people.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not boast to us about your lineage. Indeed, Allah raises by faith (iman) those whom people consider lowly when they are believers, and lowers by disbelief (kufr) those whom people consider noble when they are disbelievers. So there is no superiority for anyone over anyone except by piety (taqwa).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Isa ibn al-Dahhak, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Wonder is shown to the boastful, the proud, and indeed he was created from a drop of fluid, then he will return to be a carcass, and he is, in what is between that, not knowing what will be done with him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so,' until he counted nine (ancestors). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Indeed, you are the tenth of them in the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A calamity of the lineage is pride.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Urwah ibn 'Uthman, from Ali ibn 'Isa, raising it, said: Among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa (peace be upon him), was: 'O Musa! Do not lengthen your hope in the world, lest your heart become hard, and the one of the hard heart is remote from Me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Ismail ibn Dubeys, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Allah creates the servant in the origin of creation as a disbeliever, he will not die until Allah causes him to love evil, so he approaches it. Thus, He tests him with arrogance and tyranny, so his heart becomes callous, his character becomes bad, his face becomes harsh, his vulgarity appears, his modesty decreases, and Allah uncovers his veil, and he indulges in the prohibitions and does not withdraw from them. Then he indulges in the sins of Allah and hates His obedience, and he leaps upon the people, not satiating from disputes. So ask Allah for well-being and seek it from Him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfaly, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There are two slaps (or inclinations): one from Satan and one from the Angel. The slap of the Angel is tenderness and understanding, and the slap of Satan is forgetfulness and hardness (ruthlessness).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Taref, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Injustice (al-zulm) is of three types: an injustice which Allah forgives, an injustice which Allah does not forgive, and an injustice which Allah does not leave (unpunished). As for the injustice which He does not forgive, it is Shirk (associating partners with Him). And as for the injustice which He does forgive, it is the injustice of a person to himself, in what is between him and Allah. And as for the injustice which He does not leave (unpunished), it is al-mudayanah (claims/due rights) between the servants.

From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Ghalib ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely your Lord is in the place of watching.' He said: 'An archway upon the Bridge (Sirat), not crossed by a servant who has been unjust (to others).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih and Ubayd Allah al-Tawil, from a Sheikh from al-Nakha', who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I have not ceased to be a governor since the time of al-Hajjaj until this day of mine. So is there repentance for me?' He remained silent. Then I repeated it to him, so he said: 'No, until you repay to every rightful one his right.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no injustice more severe than an injustice whose owner cannot find assistance upon it except for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When death approached Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), he pressed me to his chest, then said: 'O my son! I bequeath to you what my father (peace be upon him) bequeathed to me when death approached him, and what he mentioned that his father bequeathed to him.' He said: 'O my son! Beware of the injustice of one who cannot find a helper against you except for Allah.'

From him, from his father, from Haroun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who fears retaliation should refrain from oppressing the people.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wakes up not intending to be unjust to anyone, Allah will forgive him whatever he sins during that day, as long as he does not spill blood or consume the wealth of an orphan unlawfully.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever wakes up in the morning not thinking of being unjust to anyone, Allah will forgive whatever sins he commits.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever commits an injustice, he will be seized by it regarding his self, or his wealth, or his children.

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fear the injustice, for it would be a darkness on the Day of Judgement'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fear the injustice, for it is the darknesses of the Day of Judgment.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no one who is unjust with an injustice except that Allah seizes him with it regarding his self and his wealth. As for the injustice which is between him and Allah, so when he repents, Allah forgives him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ammar ibn Hakim, from Abdul A'ala, the slave of the family of Saam, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, initiating: The one who is unjust, Allah will set over him one who will oppress him (or upon his offspring), or upon the offspring of his offspring. I said, 'He commits injustice and Allah sets [an oppressor] upon his offspring or upon the offspring of his offspring?' So he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: 'And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring, would fear on their account, so let them fear Allah, and let them speak right words'.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a Prophet from among His Prophets, in the kingdom of a tyrant from the tyrants: 'Go to this tyrant and say to him: Indeed, I did not appoint you for shedding blood and seizing wealth, but I appointed you to restrain from Me the voices of the oppressed, for I will not leave their injustices (unpunished), even if they are disbelievers.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who consumes the wealth of his brother unjustly and does not return it to him, will eat an ember of Fire on the Day of Resurrection.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who acts with injustice, and the one who supports him, and the one who is pleased with him are partners; all three of them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The servant may be oppressed, so he does not cease to supplicate (against his oppressor) until he becomes unjust.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Whoever gives justification for an unjust one for his injustice, Allah will cause the one who would oppress him to overpower him; so if he supplicates, it will not be answered for him, and Allah will not recompense him for his being oppressed.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: Allah does not cause an oppressor to be conquered except by an oppressor, and this is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And thus do We make some of the unjust to befriend others.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marwazi, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who wakes up in the morning and he does not think of being unjust to anyone, Allah would forgive him what he had sinned'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: Two men came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding management and dealings between them. When he heard their speech, he said: 'Know that no one has achieved success with goodness from success achieved by injustice. Know that the oppressed one takes from the religion of the oppressor more than what the oppressor takes from the wealth of the oppressed one.' Then he said: 'Whoever does evil to people should not deny evil when it is done to him. Know that indeed, the son of Adam reaps only what he sows, and no one harvests sweetness from bitterness, nor bitterness from sweetness.' So the two men reconciled before they stood up.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who fears the retaliation should refrain from oppressing the people'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Be cautious of your personal desires just as you are being cautious of your enemies, for there is nothing more inimical to the men than their following of their own personal desires and the harvest of their tongues'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'By My Honour, and My Majesty, and My Magnificence, and My Greatness, and My Light, and My Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My Position! A servant would not prefer his own personal desires over My Desires except that I scatter his affairs over him, and confuse his world for him, and occupy his heart with it, and would not give him from it except what I have ordained for him. And by My Honour, and My Majesty, and My Magnificence, and My Light, and My Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My Position! No servant would prefer My Desires above his own personal desires except that I make My Angels guard him, and the skies and the earth would guarantee his sustenance, and I would back him from behind every trade with every trader, and the world would come to him and it (world) would be subdued.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Yahya ibn Uqayl, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I fear for you only two things: following personal desires and lengthening of hope. As for following personal desires, it turns one away from the truth; and as for lengthening of hope, it causes one to forget the Hereafter.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asammi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Fear the easy climb when its descent is steep/difficult.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Do not leave the soul and its desires unguarded; for its desires are its ruin. Leaving the soul to what it desires is its affliction, and restraining the soul from what it desires is its cure.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, raising it, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Had it not been that plotting and deception are in the Fire, I would have been the most skillful in plotting against people.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Naw ibn al-Hakam, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every treacherous one will come on the Day of Judgment with an imam (leader), with a lopsided mouth, until he enters the Fire; and every breaker of the allegiance to an Imam will come as a leper (mutilated), until he enters the Fire.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He is not one of us who plots against a Muslim.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about two towns from the people of war, for each of them having a king separately. They fought, then they reconciled. Then one of the two kings betrayed his companion, so he came to the Muslims and made peace with them on the condition that he would carry out a military expedition with them against that city. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for the Muslims to be treacherous, nor to instruct others with treachery, nor to fight alongside those who are treacherous. But they should fight the polytheists wherever they find them, and what the disbelievers pact upon them is not allowed upon them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every treacherous one will come with an imam on the Day of Judgment, with a lopsided mouth, until he enters the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said one day, while he was delivering a sermon on the pulpit in Kufa: 'O people! If it were not for my aversion to treachery, I would have been the most crafty of people. Indeed, for every act of treachery there is an act of immorality, and for every act of immorality there is an act of disbelief. Indeed, treachery, immorality, and betrayal are in the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Al-Qasim al-Sayrafi, the partner of Al-Mufaddal, said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Islam is that by which blood is saved (from being shed), and by which trusts are fulfilled, and by which private parts are made permissible (for intimacy), and the reward is based upon faith.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Faith (Iman) is acknowledgement and deed, and Islam is acknowledgement without deed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, The Bedouins say: We believe. Say: You do not believe but say, We are Muslims; and Emān (belief) has not yet entered into your hearts So he said to me: Do you not see that the Emān (faith) is other than Al-Islām?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Islam and Faith, 'What is the difference between the two?' But he did not answer him. Then he asked him (again). But, he did not answer him. Then they met in the street and the man had approached the ride to leave. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'It is as if you have approached the ride to leave?' So he said, 'Yes'. So he said: 'Meet me in the house'. So he met him and he asked him about Islam and Faith, what is the difference is between the two. So he said: 'Islam, it is the apparent which the people are upon – the testimony that there is no god except for Allah Alone, there being no associates for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, and establishment of the Salat, and giving the Zakat, and performing the Hajj of the House, and (observing) Sawm the Month of Ramazan. So this is Islam'. And he said: 'Faith is the recognition of this matter (Wilayah) along with this (all of the above). So if one acknowledges with it and does not recognise this matter, he would be a Muslim, but would be straying'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from al-Washa, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Bedouins said: We believe. Say: You do not believe, but say: We are Muslims. So whoever claims that they have believed, he has lied, and whoever claims that they have not become Muslims, he has lied'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Awn al-Qalanisi, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who meets the Muslims with two faces and two tongues will come on the Day of Judgment and for him will be two tongues of Fire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Shayba, from Al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The worst servant is a servant who has two faces and two tongues, flattering his brother when present and devouring him when absent. If he is given (a bounty), he envies him, and if he is afflicted, he abandons him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, raising it, said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to Isa, son of Maryam (peace be upon him): 'O Isa! Let your tongue in the secret and the public be one tongue, and similarly your heart. Indeed, I warn you of yourself, and suffice with Me as an All-Knowing.' Two tongues are not suitable in one mouth, nor two swords in one sheath, and similarly are the minds.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Rabi', and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, raising it, said: In the bequest of Al-Mufazzal, I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'No two men separate upon desertion except that one of them incurs disowning and cursing, and sometimes both of them deserve that.' So Mu'tabb said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is the unjust one, so what is the matter with the oppressed one?' He said: 'Because he does not invite his brother to reconciliation, nor does he overlook his speech.' I heard my father saying: 'When two dispute, and one overpowers the other, let the oppressed return to his companion until he says to his companion, "Yes, my brother, I am the unjust," until he cuts off the desertion between him and his companion. For indeed Allah, Blessed and High, is a Just Judge who takes for the oppressed from the oppressor.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no desertion (ceasing of relationship) for more than three (days).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wahb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who severs ties with his relatives who do not recognize the Truth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to sever ties with them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Saeed al-Qammat, from Dawud ibn Kathir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: My father (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any two Muslims who desert each other, and remain so for three days not reconciling, except that they both would have exited from Islam, and there would be no Wilayah between them. So whichever of the two preceded to speak to his brother, he would precede him to Paradise on the Day of Reckoning.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Satan tempts (causes discord) among the believers as long as one of them does not return from his religion. So when they do that, he lies down on his back and stretches, then says, 'I have succeeded.' May Allah have mercy on the man who unites two of our friends. O group of believers! Be united and sympathetic (to each other).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Mahfouz, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Iblis remains joyful as long as the two Muslims desert each other. So when they meet (reconcile), his knees tremble and his joints creak, and he calls out, 'O Woe to me, what I face from the doom!'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a hadith: 'Indeed, in mutual hatred is the 'shaver' (that which shaves away). I do not mean the shaver of hair, but the shaver of the Religion.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Fear the bareness (or severing), for it causes men to die.' I said, 'And what is the bareness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Severing the relationship (of kinship).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'My brothers and the sons of my uncle have constricted the house upon me and forced me out from it into another room, and if I were to speak to them, I could take what is in their hands.' He said to me, 'Be patient, for Allah will make a way of relief for you.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I left, and a plague occurred in the year one hundred and thirty-one, so they all died, by Allah, and not one of them remained.' He said, 'So I went out, and when I entered upon him, he said, 'What is the state of your family?' I said to him, 'They have died, by Allah, all of them, and not one of them remains.' So he said, 'They were cut off due to what they did to you, and their disobedience to you, and their severing of the womb-relationship. Would you love that they remained (alive) and they constricted (life) upon you?' I said, 'Yes, by Allah.'

From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'da, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): There are three characteristics whose owner will not die until he sees their evil consequences: tyranny, severing of the womb (kinship), and the false oath by which one confronts Allah. And indeed, the quickest obedience to receive reward is maintaining kinship. And indeed, people may be immoral yet maintain kinship ties, so their wealth increases and they become rich. And indeed, the false oath and severing of kinship leave the houses empty of their inhabitants, and they cause the displacement of relatives; and indeed, the displacement of relatives is the cutting off of the lineage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Anbasa al-'Abid, who said: A man came and complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about his relatives. So he (the Imam) said to him: 'Suppress your anger and do (maintain relationships).' So he said, 'They are doing and doing (bad things).' So (the Imam) said: 'Do you want to become like them, so that Allah will not look at you?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not cut off your kinship, even if they cut you off.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abū Ḥamza al-Thumālī, from his father, raising it to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (peace be upon him) said in his sermon: 'I seek refuge with Allah from the sins that hasten destruction.' So ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Kawwāʾ al-Yashkurī stood up to him and said: 'O Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Can there be sins that hasten destruction?' He said: 'Yes, woe to you, it is severing the womb (kinship). Indeed, the people of the household may gather and cooperate with one another while they are immoral, yet Allah grants them sustenance; and indeed, the people of the household may separate and cut off one another, yet Allah deprives them while they are pious.'

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Mumineen (peace be upon him) said: 'When they cut off the relationships, the wealth is made to be in the hands of the evil ones.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The least of ingratitude is the saying 'Uff' (a slight exhalation of impatience), and had Allah, Mighty and Majestic, known of anything lighter than it, He would have forbidden it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Be righteous (to your parents) and shorten (your way) to Paradise, and if you are disobedient and hard-headed, then shorten (your way) to the Fire.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Salih Al-Hazza', from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When it is the Day of Judgment, a cover from the covers of Paradise will be lifted, and its scent will be smelled by anyone who has a soul from a distance of five hundred years' journey, except for one type. I said, 'Who are they?' He said, 'The one ungrateful to his parents.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever looks at his parents with an abhorrent gaze while they are unjust to him, Allah will not accept any prayer from him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Furat, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in one of his speeches: 'Beware of ingratitude to the parents, for the aroma of Paradise is found from a travel distance of a thousand years, and it will not be found by the ungrateful one, nor by a severer of kinship ties, nor by an elderly adulterer, nor by one who drags his garment in pride. Indeed, greatness belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

From him, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad al-Sulami, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If Allah knew of anything lesser than 'Uf' (the exclamation of mild annoyance), He would have forbidden it, and it is among the lowest degrees of ingratitude (to parents); and among that ingratitude is that a man looks at his parents with a fixed, angry gaze.

Ali, from his father, from Haroun Bin Al Jahm, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: My father looked at a man and with him was his son, walking, and the son was leaning upon the arm of the father. So my father (peace be upon him) did not speak to him in aversion to him until he separated from the world.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The lowest degree of ingratitude (to parents) is the saying 'Uff' (a sigh of impatience), and if Allah had known of anything less than it, He would have forbidden it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He has disbelieved in Allah, the one who disavows from a lineage, and even if it was lowly.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He has disbelieved in Allah, the one who disavows from a lineage, and even if it was lowly.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Fazzal, from various men, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they both said: Disbelief in Allah the Magnificent is the disowning of a lineage, even if it was lowly.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Let there be a proclamation of war from Me upon the one who hurts My believing servant, and let him be safe from My anger, the one who honors My believing servant.' And if there were not from My creation in the earth, between the east and the west, except for one believer along with a just Imam, I would have sufficed by their worship from all that I created in My earth, and I would have established the seven skies and the earths due to them both, and would have made for them both a comfort from their faith, so they would not be in need of the comfort of anyone besides themselves.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Munzir ibn Yazeed, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is the Day of Judgment, a Caller will call out: “Where are the hinderers against My friends?” So a group will stand, there not being any flesh upon their faces, and it will be said: “These are the ones who hurt the believers, established hostility against them, were stubborn with them, and were violent with them regarding their religion.” Then they will be commanded to Hell.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Hammad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine, he has prepared himself for war against Me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever belittles a believer, whether poor or not poor, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not cease to belittle him and be hostile to him until he retracts from his belittling of him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine, he has prepared himself for war with Me, and I am the quickest of things to aiding My friends.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham bin Salim, from Moalla bin Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says: 'He has opposed Me, the one who humiliates My Momin servant'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Hammad ibn Bashir, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine, he has prepared himself for war against Me; and no servant draws near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him, and indeed, he continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him.' So when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees, and his tongue with which he speaks, and his hand with which he grasps. If he supplicates to Me, I answer him, and if he asks Me, I give him. And I do not hesitate about anything I intend to do as I hesitate about the death of the believer; he dislikes death, and I dislike disappointing him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammad, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey, he said: 'O Lord, what is the state of the believer in Your presence?' He said: 'O Muhammad, whoever dishonors a friend of Mine, he has declared war against Me, and I am the quickest to aiding My friends. And I do not hesitate in doing anything as I hesitate regarding the death of the believer, who dislikes death, and I dislike disappointing him.' And among My believing servants is one for whom wealth is not made correct except by richness, and if I were to turn him to other than that, he would be destroyed. And among My believing servants is one for whom poverty is not made correct except by poverty, and if I were to turn him to other than that, he would be destroyed. And a servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have obligated upon him. And indeed, he draws near to Me with the voluntary [acts] until I love him. So when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees, and his tongue with which he speaks, and his hand with which he grasps. If he calls upon Me, I answer him, and if he asks Me, I give him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He who humiliates a believer and belittles him due to the scarcity of his wealth and for his poverty, Allah will publicize him on the Day of Judgment upon the heads of the creatures.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'My Lord ascended me (in Mi'raj) and He revealed to me from behind the Veil what He revealed, and He spoke to me verbally until He said to me: O Muhammad! The one who disgraces a friend of Mine, so he has declared war against Me, and the one who battles Me, I battle him.' I said, 'O Lord! And who is this friend of Yours, for I have known that the one who battles You, You would battle him?' He said to me: 'That is the one from whom I have taken the Covenant for you, and for your successor, and for both your children with the Wilayah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: He who humiliates My believing servant, he has challenged Me to war. And I did not hesitate regarding anything that I do, as I hesitate regarding My believing servant. Indeed, I love to meet him, but he dislikes death, so I turn it away from him. And indeed, he supplicates to Me regarding a matter, so I answer him with that which is better for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim and Al-Fadl, two sons of Yazeed Al-Ashari, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The closest state a servant can reach to disbelief is that he establishes brotherhood with a man upon the Religion, yet he counts his slips and mistakes against him in order to rebuke him with them one day.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Is'hāq ibn 'Ammār, who said: I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of those who became Muslims with their tongues but did not purify faith to their hearts! Do not condemn the Muslims, nor pursue their exposures (slips/flaws), for whoever pursues their exposures, Allah will pursue his exposure; and whoever Allah the Exalted pursues, He will shame him, even if he is in his own house.' From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The closest state of the servant to disbelief is that a man establishes brotherhood with another man upon the Religion, so he counts against him his slips and his mistakes in order to rebuke him with them one day.

From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of those who became Muslims by their tongues but did not become Muslims by their hearts! Do not pursue the slips of the Muslims. For whoever pursues the slips of the Muslims, Allah will pursue his slip; and whoever Allah pursues his slip, He will expose him to shame.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim or al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not seek the slips/falls of the believers, for whoever pursues the slips of his brother, Allah will pursue his slips, and whoever Allah pursues his slips, He will expose him, even if he is inside his house.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The closest state of the servant to disbelief is that a man establishes brotherhood with another man upon the religion, so he counts his slips against him in order to rebuke him with them one day.

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The furthest a servant can be from Allah is that a man establishes brotherhood with another man while he memorizes his slips/mistakes in order to reproach him with them one day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever reproaches a believer, Allah will reproach him in the world and the Hereafter.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ismail ibn Ammar, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who broadcasts an immorality is like its initiator, and the one who rebukes a believer with something will not die until he commits it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who rebukes a believer with a sin will not die until he commits it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Backbiting is more rapid in consuming the religion of the Muslim man than food is in his belly.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Sitting in the mosque awaiting the prayer is worship as long as nothing occurs.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what occurs?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Backbiting.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who says regarding a believer what his eyes saw and his ears heard, so he is from those for whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Indeed, those who like that immorality should spread among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about backbiting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is that you say to your brother regarding his religion something he has not done, and affirm a matter upon him which Allah has veiled, for which no legal punishment (Hadd) has been established upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'What is the expiation for backbiting?' He said, 'You seek forgiveness of Allah for the one you backbit, every time you remember him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Malik ibn Atiyya from Ibn Abi Yafur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The one who slanders a believer or a female believer with what is not in him, Allah will resurrect him in the clay of Khabal until he exits from what he had said. I said, 'And what is the clay of Khabal?' He said, 'Pus that comes out from the private parts of the prostitutes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Backbiting is that you say about your brother what Allah has concealed from him, and as for the apparent matter in him, such as sharpness of temper and haste, then no [it is not backbiting], and slander is that you say about him what is not in him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The one who reports upon a believer with a report intending to defame him and demolish his dignity/personality, so that he falls from the eyes of the people, Allah will remove him from His guardianship to the guardianship of Satan, and Satan will not accept him.'

From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I said to him, 'The nakedness of the believer is prohibited upon the believer?' He said: 'Yes'. I said, 'You mean his lower part?' He said: 'It is not where you are going with it. But rather it is the broadcasting of his secrets'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding what came in the Hadith that the 'awrah (nakedness/vulnerability)' of the believer is prohibited upon the believer, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not that he uncovers him so you see something from him. Rather, it is that you report against him or fault him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Sama'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about Al-Islam and Al-Iman, are these two different?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Iman contains Al-Islam, but Al-Islam does not contain Al-Iman.' So I said, 'So describe these two to me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Islam is the testimony that there is no god except Allah and the ratification of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). By it, the bloods are saved, and upon it the marriages flow, and the inheritances, and upon its apparent are the communities of the people. And Al-Iman is the guidance and what is affirmed in the hearts from the characteristics of Al-Islam, and whatever the deeds make apparent with; and Al-Iman is higher than Al-Islam by a level. Al-Iman contains Al-Islam in the apparent, but Al-Islam does not contain Al-Iman in the hidden, although they are both together regarding the words and the description.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Iman contains Al-Islam, but Al-Islam does not contain Al-Iman.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Al-Iman includes Al-Islam, and Al-Islam does not include it. Al-Iman is what settles in the hearts, and Al-Islam is that upon which are the marriages, the inheritances, and the sparing of the bloods; and Al-Iman shares/includes Al-Islam, and Al-Islam does not share/include Al-Iman.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which of the two is superior, Al-Iman or Al-Islam, for those in front of us say that Al-Islam is superior to Al-Iman?' He said, 'Al-Iman is higher than Al-Islam.' I said, 'So renew that (explanation) for me.' He said, 'What do you say regarding the one who deliberately urinates or defecates in the Sacred Masjid?' I said, 'He would be lashed intensely.' He said, 'Correct.' He said, 'So what do you say regarding the one who urinates or defecates deliberately in the Kabah?' I said, 'He would be killed.' He said, 'Correct. Do you not see that the Kabah is superior to the Masjid, and that the Kabah is included in the Masjid and the Masjid is not included in the Kabah, and similar to that, Al-Iman includes Al-Islam, but Al-Islam does not include Al-Iman.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Al-Iman (faith) is that which settles in the heart and leads with it to Allah (Exalted and Majestic), and the deeds ratify it with obedience to Allah and submission to His Command; but Al-Islam (submission) is what is apparent from words or deeds, and it is what the communities of people are upon, from all of the sects. And by it, the bloods are saved, and upon it flow the inheritances, and the marriages are validated, and they gather upon the Salat (prayer), and the Zakat (alms-tax), and the Sawm (fasting), and the Hajj (pilgrimage).' Thus, by that, they are exiting from the Kufr (disbelief) and entering into the Iman; but the Islam does not include the Iman, but the Iman does include the Islam, and they are both together in the words and the deeds, just as the Ka'bah comes to be in the Masjid, and the Masjid is not in the Ka'bah, similarly the Iman includes the Islam, but the Islam does not include the Iman.' The Bedouins say: We believe. Say: You do not believe but say, We submit; and Iman (belief) has not yet entered into your hearts. And the Words of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) are the most truthful of the words. I said, 'So is there a preference for the Mu'min (Believer) upon the Muslim with regards to anything from the merits, and the Ordinances, and the legal punishments, and other than that?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No. They both flow with regards to that with one flow, but the Mu'min has superiority upon the Muslim regarding their deeds and (through) which they are getting closer to Allah (Exalted and Majestic).' I said, 'Isn't Allah (Exalted and Majestic) Saying: Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it, and you alleged they are together upon the Salat, and the Zakat, and the Sawm, and the Hajj along with the Mu'mineen (plural of Mu'min)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hasn't Allah (Exalted and Majestic) Said: Who is it that who will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He will Multiply it to him manifold? So, the Mu'mineen, they are those for whom Allah (Exalted and Majestic) would Multiply their good deeds, for every good deed, a multiple of seventy. Thus, this is the superiority

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The insulter of the believer is like one on the verge of destruction.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayub, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Insulting the believer is mischief (fusuq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr), and consuming his flesh is disobedience, and the sanctity of his wealth is like the sanctity of his blood'.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, a man from the Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Advise me.' So, among what he advised him with was that he said: 'Do not insult the people, lest you acquire enmity between them.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), regarding two men insulting each other, He said: The initiator of the two is more unjust, and his burden and the burden of his companion are upon him for as long as he does not apologize to the oppressed one.
