Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A man does not testify against another man with disbelief at all, except that one of the two will be returned with it: if he testified against a disbeliever, it was true; and if he testified against a believer, the disbelief returns upon him. Beware of reviling the believers.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The curse, when it goes out from the mouth of its owner, hesitates. So if it finds a way out (to the deserving), or else it returns upon its owner.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The curse, when it goes out from the mouth of its owner, bounces back and forth between the two (the curser and the cursed). So if it finds a way/path (to the one cursed), otherwise it returns to its owner.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu Hamza who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man says to his believing brother, 'Uff!', he exits from his Wilayah; and when he says, 'You are my enemy', one of the two has disbelieved; and Allah will not accept a deed from a believer while he is implicitly bearing ill-will against his believing brother.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Rabie, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no person who insults (verbally) in the eye of a believer except that he will die with the worst of deaths, and it is fitting that he does not return to goodness.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the believer slanders his brother, faith dissolves from his heart just as salt dissolves in water.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Al-Husayn ibn Hazim, from Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who slanders his brother regarding his Religion, so there is no sanctity between the two of them; and the one who deals with his brother with the like of what the people deal with him, so he is disavowed from what he is impersonating'.

From him, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Place the matter of your brother upon its best interpretation until there comes to you what would overwhelm you from him, and do not suppose evil with a speech that comes out from your brother while you can find an interpretation of it regarding goodness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Numan, from Abu Hafs Al-A'sha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who strives to fulfill a need of his brother but does not advise him, has betrayed Allah and His Messenger.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whichever believer walks regarding a need of his brother, but does not advise him, so he has betrayed Allah and His Messenger.'

From both of them together, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The one who walks regarding a need of his brother, then does not advise him with regards to it, he would be like the one who betrayed Allah and His Rasool, and Allah would be His Adversary.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Husayn ibn Hazim, from Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who consults his brother, but he is not sincere with him with a sincere opinion, Allah Mighty and Majestic would Confiscate his opinion.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any believer who walks with his believing brother regarding a need but does not advise him, has betrayed Allah and His Messenger.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Hassan, and a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, all from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any believer who has an obstruction between himself and another believer, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will place between him and Paradise seventy thousand walls; the distance from one wall to the next is a journey of one thousand years.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jamhur from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from his father from Ismail ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan who said: I was in the presence of al-Rida (peace be upon him), so he said to me: 'O Muhammad! Indeed, in the time of the Children of Israel, there were four believers. One of them came to the other three, who were gathered in the house of one of them, engaged in a discussion among themselves. He knocked on the door, and the slave came out to him. He said, 'Where is your master?' He said, 'He is not in the house.' The man returned, and the slave went to his master. He said to him, 'Who was the one who knocked on the door?' He said, 'So-and-so.' I told him, 'You are not in the house.' So he remained silent and did not care, and he did not blame his slave, nor was any of them saddened by his return from the door, and they continued in their conversation. When it was the next day, the man came early to them and found them, and they had gone out intending a property of one of them. He greeted them and said, 'I am with you.' They said to him, 'Yes,' and they did not apologize to him. The man was needy and of weak financial state. When they were on part of the way, a cloud shaded them, and they thought it was rain, so they hastened. When the cloud settled directly over their heads, a caller called out from within the cloud: 'O Fire! Seize them, and I am Jibra'il, the Messenger of Allah!' So a fire from within the cloud snatched the three men, and the man remained terrified, amazed at what had befallen the people, and he did not know the reason. So he returned to the city and met Yusha' ibn Nun (peace be upon him) and informed him of the news and what he had seen and heard. Yusha' ibn Nun (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that Allah was pleased with them, but then became angry with them, and that was due to their deed with you?' He said, 'And what was their deed with me?' So Yusha' narrated it to him. The man said, 'So I hereby make them free and excuse them.' He said: 'Had this been before, it would have benefited them, but as for now, no. And perhaps it might benefit them afterwards.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whichever believer has an obstruction between him and another believer, Allah will place between him and Paradise seventy thousand walls; the thickness of each wall is a journey of a thousand years, and the distance from one wall to the next is a journey of a thousand years.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding a Muslim who visits another Muslim or seeks a need while he is in his house, so he seeks permission from him, but he does not grant him permission and does not come out to him?' He said, 'O Abu Hamza! Whichever Muslim visits another Muslim or seeks a need while he is in his house, so he seeks permission from him and he does not come out to him, he will not cease to be in the Curse of Allah until they both meet.' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, (is he) in the Curse of Allah until they both meet?' He said, 'Yes, O Abu Hamza.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'dan, from Husayn ibn Ameen, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is stingy in helping his Muslim brother and in standing for him regarding his need, will be tried with helping one who sins on his behalf and will not be recompensed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Any man from our Shias who goes to a man from his brethren to seek his assistance regarding his need, but he does not assist him while he is able, Allah will test him by making him fulfill the needs of others from our enemies, and Allah will punish him for it on the Day of Judgment.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Al-Khattab ibn Mus'ab, from Sadeer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man does not leave assisting his Muslim brother until he strives in it and consoles him, except that he will be tried with assisting one who sins and he will not be recompensed.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: I heard him saying: 'The one to whom a man from his brethren intends to seek his help during one of his states, but he does not help him after being able upon it, so he has cut off the Wilayah of Allah, Mighty and Majestic'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, all from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Any believer who withholds from a believer something that he needs, while he is able to provide it from his own possession or from that of others, Allah will make him stand on the Day of Judgment with a blackened face, his eyes blue, his hands tied to his neck, and it will be said: 'This is the betrayer who betrayed Allah and His Messenger.' Then he will be commanded to be taken to the Fire.

Ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Yunus! Whoever withholds the right of a believer, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will make him stand on the Day of Judgment for five hundred years upon his feet until his sweat or blood flows, and a caller will call out from the presence of Allah: “This is the unjust one who withheld from Allah his right.” He (peace be upon him) said: “So he will be rebuked for forty days, then he will be commanded to be taken to the Fire.”'

Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufazzal ibn Umar said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who had a house, and a believer needed to dwell in it, but he prevented him from it,' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O My Angels! Is My servant being stingy upon My servant regarding dwelling in the house of the world? By My Honour and My Majesty! He shall not dwell in My Gardens, ever!'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'When his believing brother comes to him with a need, it is but a mercy from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that has been conveyed to him. If he accepts that need, he has connected it with our Wilayah, and he is connected with the Wilayah of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' And if he repels him from his need while he is able to fulfill it, Allah will cause a serpent of fire to gnaw him in his grave until the Day of Judgment. He will be either forgiven or punished; and if the seeker excuses him, his state will be worse. He said: 'And I heard him saying: Whoever a man from his brethren approaches seeking refuge/help from him in one of his states, and he does not grant him refuge after being able to do so, he has cut off the Wilayah of Allah, Blessed and High.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who looks at a believer with a look intended to frighten him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will frighten him on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Ishaq al-Khaffaf, from one of the Kufians, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever frightens a believer by a ruling authority in order to cause him distress, but it does not cause it, then he is in the Fire; and whoever frightens a believer by a ruling authority in order to cause him distress, and it does cause it, then he is with Pharaoh and the family of Pharaoh in the Fire.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever assists against a believer, even by half a word, will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Judgment, with 'Despaired of My Mercy' written between his eyes.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I inform you of the worst of you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah!' He said: 'Those who walk about spreading gossip, the separators between lovers, the seekers of faults of the righteous, the fault-finders.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Paradise is prohibited to the slanderers, the conveyers of gossip.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan al-Isbahani, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The worst of you are the carriers of gossip, the separators between the lovers, the seekers of faults in the righteous, and the fault-finders.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, who said: I wrote, along with Abd al-Malik ibn Ayn, to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), asking him about faith (Iman), what it is. So he wrote to me, along with Abd al-Malik ibn Ayn: 'You asked, may Allah have mercy on you, about faith; and faith is affirmation by the tongue, and a firm conviction in the heart, and action by the limbs. And faith is one part from another, and it is a house (domain), and similarly Islam is a house, and disbelief is a house.' So the servant may be a Muslim before he is a believer, and he does not become a believer until he becomes a Muslim. So Islam precedes faith, and it shares with faith. So when the servant commits a major sin from the major sins, or a minor sin from the minor sins which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade, he exits from faith; the name of faith drops from him, while the name of Islam remains established upon him. So if he repents and seeks forgiveness, he returns to the house of faith. And nothing drives him out to disbelief except denial (Juhud) and legalization (Istihlal) — that he says of the permissible, 'This is forbidden,' and of the forbidden, 'This is permissible,' and accepts that as religion. At that point, he exits from Islam and faith, entering into disbelief. And he is like the one who enters the Sanctuary (Haram), then enters the Ka'bah, and defecates in the Ka'bah; so he is expelled from the Ka'bah and from the Sanctuary, his neck is struck, and he goes to the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him about al-Iman and al-Islam. I said to him, 'Is there a difference between al-Islam and al-Iman?' He said, 'Shall I strike an example for you?' I said, 'Present it.' He said, 'The example of al-Iman and al-Islam is like the Ka'bah al-Haram (the Sacred House) from the Haram (the Sanctuary). One can be in the Haram and not be in the Ka'bah, but one cannot be in the Ka'bah until one is in the Haram. And one can be a Muslim and not be a Mu'min, and one cannot be a Mu'min until one is a Muslim.' He said, I said, 'So does something exit from al-Iman?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'So to what does it convert him?' He said, 'To al-Islam or to al-Kufr.' And he said, 'If a man were to enter the Ka'bah and his urine escaped from him, he would be exited from the Ka'bah and would not be exited from the Haram. So he would wash his garment and purify himself, then he would not be prevented from entering the Ka'bah. And if a man were to enter the Ka'bah and urinate therein intentionally (stubbornly), he would be exited from the Ka'bah and from the Haram, and his neck would be struck off.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reproached a people for publicizing (al-itha'ah) in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: And when there comes to them news of security or fear, they publicize it. Therefore, beware of publicizing.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who publicises our Hadith to us, he is in the status of the one who denied us our right. He said, and he said to Mu'alla ibn Khunays: 'The publiciser of our Hadith is like the denier of it'.
Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who publicises our hadith upon us, Allah will strip him of faith.'

Yunus ibn Yaqoub narrated from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who publicized our hadith did not kill us with an erroneous killing, but he killed us with a deliberate killing.

Yunus from Al-A'ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The servant will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment with blood moistening him, so something resembling a cupping cup or more than that would be handed over to him, and it would be said to him, 'This is your share from the blood of so-and-so.' So he would say, 'O Lord, You know that You caused me to die and I had not spilled any blood.' So He would say, 'Yes, you heard a report of such and such from so-and-so, and you reported it upon him, and it was transmitted until it came to so-and-so the tyrant, and he was killed because of it, and this is your share from his blood.'

Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) And he recited this Verse: 'This was because they disbelieved in the Signs of Allah and killed the Prophets unjustly; this was because they disobeyed and exceeded the limits.' He said: 'By Allah, they did not kill them by their hands, nor did they strike them with their swords, but they heard their narrations, publicized them, so they were seized upon it and killed. Thus, it became murder, transgression, and disobedience.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And they killed the prophets without right.' He said: 'By Allah, they did not kill them with their swords, but they publicized their secrets and exposed them, so they killed them.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) reproached a people for their publicising, so He said: 'And when there comes to them news of security or fear, they publicise it.' Therefore, beware of the publicising.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Utman, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abd Allah informed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who publicizes to us something from our affairs, he is like the one who killed us deliberately, and did not kill us erroneously.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Nasr ibn Sa'id, the freedman of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The publiciser of the secret is a doubter, and its speaker in the presence of those other than its deserving ones is a disbeliever; and whoever holds fast to the Firmest Handle, he will be saved.' I said, 'And what is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The submission (to God's will/peace).'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from a man from the Kufians, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the Religion two governments: the government of Adam, and it is the government of Allah, and the government of Iblis. So whenever Allah wants to be worshipped publicly, it is the government of Adam, and whenever Allah wants to be worshipped in private, it is the government of Iblis, and the one who publicizes what Allah wants to be a secret is one who departs from the Religion.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who opens his day by publicizing our secrets, Allah will cause him to be overcome by the heat of the iron and the constriction of the prisons.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There are five (things), if you were to come across these, so seek Refuge with Allah from these – Never has an immorality appeared among a people at all to the extent of it being performed openly except there appeared among them, the plague and the hunger which did not happen to be among their ancestors in the past.' And never have they (people) been deficient in the measuring and the weighing except that they were seized by the years (of famine), and difficult provision, and tyranny of the ruling authorities; and never have they (people) prevented the Zakāt except that the drops from the sky were prevented, and had it not been for the beasts, it would not have rained; and never have they (people) broken the Covenant of Allah and the Covenant of His Rasool except that Allah Caused them to be overcome by their enemies, and they seized part of what was in their hands; and never have they judged with other than what Allah Mighty and Majestic Sent down except that Allah Mighty and Majestic Made the fear (of battles) to be between them'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We found in the letter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): When adultery becomes prevalent after me, sudden death will increase. And when they are insufficient in the measuring and the weighing, Allah will seize them with the years (of famine) and the shortages. And when they withhold the Zakat, the earth will withhold its blessings from the crops, and the fruits, and the minerals, all of them. And when they are tyrannical in their judgements, they will assist each other upon the injustices and the animosities. And when they break the Covenant, Allah will cause their enemies to overcome upon them. And when they sever the relationships, the wealth will be made to be in the hands of the most evil of them. And when they do not enjoin with the good and do not forbid from the evil and do not follow the chosen ones from the People of my Household, Allah will cause the most evil of them to overcome upon them, so their best ones will be supplicating and it will not be Answered for them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ziyad al-Nahdy, from Abdullah ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the believer to sit in a gathering wherein Allah is being disobeyed, and he is not able to alter it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Why did I see you in the presence of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yaqoub?' He said, 'He is my maternal uncle.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is saying a great saying about Allah; He describes Allah, but He cannot be described. So either you sit with him and leave us, or you sit with us and leave him.' I said, 'He says whatever he wishes. What is upon me from him if I do not say what he says?' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not fear that an affliction might descend with him so it would hit all of you together? Do you not know of the one who was from the companions of Musa (peace be upon him), and his father was from the companions of Pharaoh? So when the cavalry of Pharaoh caught up with Musa (peace be upon him), he remained behind from him in order to advise his father, and he was coercing him until they reached a part of the sea, so they both drowned. The news came to Musa (peace be upon him) and he said: 'He is in the Mercy of Allah, but the affliction, when it descends, there is no defence to it from the one who is close to the sinner.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Do not accompany the people of innovation, and do not sit with them, lest you become in the eyes of the people like one of them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A person is upon the religion of his close friend and companion.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you see the people of doubt and innovation after me, then manifest disavowal from them, and frequently curse them, and speak about them, and strike them, and confound them, so that they do not covet corruption in Islam, and the people may beware of them and not learn from their innovations. Allah will write for you good deeds because of that, and raise your ranks in the Hereafter because of that.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the Muslim to establish brotherhood with the immoral, nor with the stupid, nor with the liar.

From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Salim al-Kinani, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when he ascended the pulpit, would say: 'It is befitting for the Muslim to avoid establishing brotherhood with three: the immoral (al-majin), the foolish (al-ahmaq), and the liar (al-kazzab).' As for the immoral: he adorns his deed for you, and loves that you be like him, and he does not assist you in the affairs of your religion and hereafter; and associating with him is aloofness and hardness of heart, and his entry and exit upon you is a disgrace. And as for the foolish: he does not indicate good to you, nor is he hoped for to ward off evil from you, even if he exerts himself; and perhaps he intends your benefit but harms you. Thus, his death is better than his life, his silence better than his speech, and his distance better than his nearness. And as for the liar: life is not pleasant with him. He transmits your narration and transmits the narration to you. Whenever he exhausts one story, he stretches it with another, to the extent that when he narrates with the truth, he is not believed; and he incites enmity among people, causing grudges to grow in the chests. Therefore, fear Allah and look out for yourselves.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafar, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim or Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O my son! Watch out for five, so do not accompany them, nor converse with them, nor travel with them on a road.' I said: 'O father! Who are they?' He said: 'Beware of accompanying the liar, for he is like a mirage; he brings the distant near to you and distances the near from you.' And beware of accompanying the immoral, for he would sell you for a meal or less than that. And beware of accompanying the stingy, for he would abandon you regarding his wealth when you are most in need of it. And beware of accompanying the stupid, for he intends to benefit you but actually harms you. And beware of accompanying the severer of his kinship ties, for I found him to be cursed in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in three places. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'So what is the matter with you that, if you took command, you would surely make mischief in the land and cut off your ties of kinship? Those it is whom Allah has cursed, so He has made them deaf and blinded their eyes.' And He said: 'Those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause mischief in the land; those are the ones who have the curse, and for them is the evil abode.' And He said in Surah Al-Baqarah: 'Those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause mischief in the land; those are the losers.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And indeed He has revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah's Signs disbelieved in and mocked at' – up to the end of the Verse. So he said: 'But rather it Meant by this: 'Whenever you hear the man who is denying the truth and is belying it, and is opposing regarding the Imams, so arise from his presence and do not sit with him wherever he may happen to be'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He who believes in Allah and the Last Day should not sit in a gathering wherein an Imam is derogated or wherein a believer is faulted.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Abd al-A'la, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit in a gathering wherein an Imam is faulted or a believer is disparaged.'

And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: 'Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Jumahi narrated to me, saying: 'Hisham ibn Salim narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)' He said: 'When you are afflicted with the people of al-Nasb (those of hostility, especially to the Imams) and their companionship, then be as if you are upon the rib of a camel (enduring patiently), until you arise. Indeed, Allah detests them and curses them. So when you see them conversing vainly in mentioning an Imam from the Imams, then arise, for the Wrath of Allah descends upon them there.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who sits in the presence of the insulters of the Guardians of Allah, so he has disobeyed Allah the Exalted.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever sits in a gathering wherein an Imam from the Imams is insulted, despite being able to stand up and leave, but he does not do so, Allah will clothe him in disgrace in the world, and punish him in the Hereafter, and strip him of the good of what He bestowed upon him from our recognition.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, who said: My father Ali ibn Al-Nu'man narrated to me, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Yaman ibn Ubaydullah, who said: I saw Yahya ibn Umm Al-Taweel standing by the sweepings, then he called out in a loud voice: 'O companions of the Friends of Allah! We are free from what you hear; whoever insults Ali (peace be upon him), upon him be the Curse of Allah, and we are free from the family of Marwan and what they worship besides Allah.' Then he lowered his voice and said: 'Whoever insults the Friends of Allah, do not sit with him; and whoever doubts in what we are upon, do not approach him; and whoever needs to ask you from your brethren, you have betrayed him.' We have prepared for the unjust a Fire, the enclosures of which shall encompass them; and if they cry for water, they shall be given water like molten brass which will scald their faces; evil is the drink and worse is the reclining couch.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Suleym the freedman of Tarbaal, who said: Hisham narrated to me from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The people are upon six categories.' He said: I said, 'Do you permit me to write it down?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'What shall I write?' He said, 'Write: The people of threat are from the people of Paradise and the people of Hell.' And write: And others have confessed their sins, they have mingled a good deed and an evil one. He said: I said, 'Who are these?' He said, 'Wahshi is among them.' And write: And others are those of whom delay is made, awaiting Allah's command; whether He will punish them or turn to them (mercifully). He said: And write: Except the weak from among the men and the women and the children, who have not the power to find a way. They cannot find a way to disbelief, nor can they find a way to faith; so these, it may be, Allah will pardon them. He said: And write: The people of Al-Araf. I said, 'And what are the people of Al-Araf?' He said: 'A people whose good deeds and evil deeds are equal. So if He enters them into the Fire, it is due to their sins, and if He enters them into Paradise, it is due to His Mercy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The people are upon six divisions, which all return to three divisions: Faith, Disbelief, and Straying. And they are the People of the Two Promises, whom Allah has promised Paradise and Hell: The Believers and the Disbelievers; The Weak and the Hopeful for Allah's Command, either He punishes them or He repents for them; And those who confess their sins, who mixed a righteous deed with an evil one; And the People of Al-A'raf.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the Sunnahs of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) like the Obligations of Allah (Exalted and Mighty) imposed obligatory obligations upon the servants. So whoever leaves an obligation from the obligatory ones, does not act upon it, and denies it, he is a disbeliever. And the Messenger of Allah commanded matters, all of them being good deeds. So whoever leaves some of what Allah (Exalted and Mighty) commanded His servants to do from the obedience, is not a disbeliever, but he is one who leaves the virtue, deficient in goodness.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Abi al-Hakam, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: By Allah, indeed disbelief (Kufr) is earlier than polytheism (Shirk), and more foul and greater. He said, then he mentioned the disbelief of Iblis when Allah said to him, 'Prostrate to Adam,' but he refused to prostrate. So disbelief is greater than polytheism. So whoever chooses against Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and refuses obedience and persists in major sins, then he is a disbeliever (Kafir). And whoever establishes a religion other than the religion of the believers, then he is a polytheist (Mushrik).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Salim ibn Abi Hafsah and his companions were mentioned in his presence, so he said: 'They deny that those who fought against Ali (peace be upon him) were polytheists (Mushrikun).' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Then they claim that they are disbelievers (Kuffar).' Then he said to me: 'Disbelief (Kufr) precedes polytheism (Shirk).' Then he mentioned the disbelief of Iblis when He said to him, 'Prostrate,' but he refused to prostrate. And he said: 'Disbelief precedes polytheism. So whoever is audacious against Allah, refuses obedience, and persists in major sins, he is a disbeliever (Kafir), meaning a disbeliever who is contemptuous (Mustakhiff).

From him, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'We have shown him the way, [so let him choose] either a grateful one or a thankful one.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Either he accepts [the Wilayah], so he is a grateful one, or he neglects [it], so he is an unbeliever.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever denies the faith, his work indeed would be Confiscated.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Neglecting the deed which he had acknowledged with it. From that is if he were to neglect the Salat from without an illness or a pre-occupation'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Musa ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about disbelief (Kufr) and association (Shirk), which of the two is earlier? He said to me: 'Have I not agreed with you to debate with the people?' I said: 'Hisham ibn Salim instructed me to ask you about that.' So he said to me: 'Disbelief is earlier, and it is denial.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Except for Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and he was one of the unbelievers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Does a believer enter the Fire?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by Allah.' I said: 'So none enters it except an unbeliever?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except the one whom Allah wills.' So when I reiterated it upon him time and again, he said to me: 'O Zurara! I say He (the narrator) said: 'Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hammad narrated to me from Zurara, who said: I said within myself,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he was asked about disbelief (kufr) and association (shirk), which of the two occurred earlier? So he said: Disbelief occurred earlier, and that is because Iblis was the first to disbelieve, and his disbelief was not association (shirk), because he did not call to the worship of other than Allah, and rather he called to that afterwards, so he associated (committed shirk).

Harun, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he was asked: 'What is the matter that the adulterer is not named as a disbeliever (Kafir), while the one who neglects the prayer has been named as a disbeliever, and what is the proof in that?' So he said: 'Because the adulterer and whoever resembles him only does that due to lust, because it overcomes him. And the one who neglects the prayer does not neglect it except by considering it insignificant, and that is because you will not find the adulterer going to the woman except while he is deriving pleasure from going to her, aiming at her. And everyone who neglects the prayer, aiming at it, his aim for neglecting it is not pleasure. So when pleasure is negated, insignificance occurs, and when insignificance occurs, disbelief occurs.' He said: 'And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked and it was said to him: 'What is the difference between the one who looks at a woman so he commits adultery with her, or looks at wine so he drinks it, and the one who neglects the prayer, to the extent that the adulterer and the drinker of wine are not considered insignificant like the one who neglects the prayer is considered insignificant? And what is the proof in that, and what is the reason that differentiates between them?' He said: 'The proof is that whenever you enter yourself into it, it is not inviting you with an inviter, and a dominant lust does not overcome you like adultery and drinking of wine. And you are inviting yourself to neglecting the prayer, and there is no lust there. So it is insignificance itself, and this is the difference between them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who doubts in Allah and in His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), then he is a disbeliever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What about the one who doubts in the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He is an Unbeliever (Kafir).' I said, 'So the one who doubts in the disbelief (Kufr) of the doubting one, so he is an Unbeliever (Kafir)?' So he withheld from me. So I reiterated upon him three times, and the anger became apparent in his face.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever denies the faith, his work has become worthless.' He said: 'The one who neglects the deed which he acknowledged.' I said: 'So what is the subject of the neglected deed to the extent that he is deemed to have left the entirety of it?' He said: 'From it is the one who leaves the Salat deliberately, neither from intoxication nor from an illness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakeym and Hammad, from Abu Masrouq, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked me about the people of Basra and said to me: 'What are they?' I said, 'Murjiites, Qadiriyya, and Harouriyya (sects)'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'May the Curse of Allah be upon those religions of the Unbelievers and the Polytheists, those who do not worship Allah upon anything'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and Ibn Sinan and Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Obedience to Ali (peace be upon him) is humiliation (in this world), and disobedience to him is disbelief in Allah.' It was said, 'O Rasool-Allah, and how can obedience to Ali (peace be upon him) be humiliation and disobedience to him be disbelief in Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) carries you upon the Truth, so if you obey him, you will be humbled, and if you disobey him, you will have disbelieved in Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', who said, 'Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, saying, I heard Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying' 'Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) is a door from the doors of Guidance. So whoever enters from the door of Ali is a believer, and whoever exits from it is a disbeliever, and whoever does not enter into it nor exits from it is in the class of those for whom Allah has the will (to decide their fate).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If the servants, when they were ignorant, paused and did not reject (the truth), they would not have been disbelievers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, appointed Ali (peace be upon him) as a flag between Him and His creatures. So whoever recognized him was a believer, and whoever denied him was a disbeliever, and whoever was ignorant of him was astray, and whoever appointed anything with him was a polytheist, and whoever came with his Wilayah entered Paradise, and whoever came with his animosity entered the Fire.

Yunus, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) is a door from the doors of Paradise; so whoever enters his door is a believer, and whoever exits from his door is a disbeliever, and whoever neither enters it nor exits from it is in the tier whose (fate) Allah desires regarding them.

He (peace be upon him) said: And hypocrisy is upon four pillars: upon the whims, the leisureliness, the grudges, and the greed. So the whims are upon four branches: upon rebellion, animosity, lustful desires, and tyranny. So the one who rebels, frequent changes of circumstances befall him, he is isolated from, and restrictions are placed upon him; and the one who transgresses, he is not secure from its harmful consequences, his heart is not tranquil, and he does not control himself from the lustful desires; and the one who does not rebuke his own self regarding the lustful desires, he dives into the evil deeds; and the one who is arrogant, he strays deliberately without a proof. And the leisureliness is upon four branches: upon inattention, expectations, awe, and procrastination. And that is because the awe repels from the truth, and the procrastination leads to carelessness in the deed until the deadline comes up upon him, and had it not been for the expectation, the human being would know the reckoning of what he is in, and if he were to know the reckoning of what he is in, he would die fearing from the horrors and the apprehension; and the inattentiveness cuts short the man from the deeds. And the grudges are upon four branches: upon arrogance, pride, egoism, and prejudice. So the one who is arrogant turns back from the truth, and the one who is proud is immoral, and the one who is egoistic persists upon the sins, and the one who is seized by the prejudice is tyrannous. So the most evil of the matters is a matter between turning back, immorality, persistence, and tyranny upon the path. And the greed is upon four branches: the jubilation, the hilarity, the obstinacy, and the abundance. So the jubilation is disliked in the Presence of Allah, and the hilarity is haughtiness, and the obstinacy is an affliction for the one who is desperate to carry upon the sins, and the abundance is sport, play, pre-occupation, and the changing for that which is lowly by that which is good. So that is the hypocrisy and its pillars and its branches. And Allah is Compelling upon His servants, Exalted is His Mention and Majestic is His Face, and good is everything which He Created, and His Hand is Extensive, and His Mercy Covers everything, and His Command is Manifest, and His Light is bright, and His Blessing is over-flowing, and His Wisdom is Illuminating, and His Book is Abso

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him a question, so he wrote to me: Surely the hypocrites strive to deceive Allah, and He shall Requite their deceit back to them, and when they stand up for the Prayer they stand up sluggishly; they do it only to be seen of men and do not remember Allah except for a little Wavering between that (and this), (belonging) neither to these nor to those; and whomsoever Allah Causes to err, you shall not find a way for him They are neither from the Unbelievers nor from the Believers, and they are not from the Muslims. They are displaying the Faith and they are becoming to the Disbelief and (with) the lies. May Allah Curse them

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jamhur from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam from al-Haytham ibn Waqid from Muhammad ibn Suleman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: He said: Indeed, the hypocrite forbids but does not keep away (from what he forbids), and he commands what he does not perform; and when he stands for prayer, he turns around. I said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, and what is the turning around? He said: The turning around. And when he bows, he crouches; in the evening his concern is dinner although he has not fasted, and in the morning his concern is sleep although he has not stayed awake (in worship). If he narrates to you, he lies; and if you entrust him, he betrays you; and if you are absent, he backbites you; and if he promises you, he breaks it.

From him, from Ibn Jamhur, from Suleyman ibn Sama' Sama'ah, from Abdul Malik ibn Bahr, raising it, similar to that, and there is an increase in it, When he bows, he crouches, and when he prostrates, he pecks, and when he sits, he rests on his heels.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The example of the hypocrite is like the example of the trunk of a palm tree. Its owner intended to benefit from it in one of his constructions, but it did not stand straight for him in the place he intended. So he moved it to another place, but it did not stand straight for him. So the end of that was that he burned it with fire.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whatever increase there is of the humility in the body over what is in the heart, so in our view it is hypocrisy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Bureyd al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the least of that which makes a servant a Mushrik. He said: The one who says for the kernel that it is a pebble, and for the pebble that it is a kernel, then makes a religion with it.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the least thing that makes a person a mushrik (polytheist). He said: 'The one who initiates an opinion, then loves it or hates over it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer and Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And most of them do not believe in Allah except they are associating others (with Him)' [12:106]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He obeys the Satan from where he does not even know, so he associates (commits shirk).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Durays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they are associating others (with Him) He said: It is the shirk of obedience, and it is not the shirk of worship. And regarding His Words, the Mighty and Majestic And among men is he who worships Allah on a corner (superficially) He said: The verse was revealed regarding a man, then it applies to his followers. Then I said: Every one who establishes anything besides you is from those who worship Allah superficially? He said: Yes, and it can be purely that.

Yunus, from Dawood ibn Farqad, from Hassan al-Jammal, from Amira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The people have been commanded with recognizing us, and referring to us, and submitting to us.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And if they were to fast, and pray, and testify that there is no god except Allah, and make it within themselves that they would not refer to us, they would become, due to that, polytheists.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a people worshipped Allah alone, with no partner for Him, and established the prayer, and gave the alms-tax, and performed the pilgrimage to the House, and fasted the month of Ramadan, then they said regarding something that Allah or the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did, Why was it not done differently than what was done, or they found that in their hearts, then they would be polytheists because of that.' Then he recited this verse: So no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge of that over which they dispute among themselves, then they will not find in their hearts any discomfort from what you judged and they will submit with [full] submission. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So upon you is submission.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'They have taken their Rabbis and their Monks for lords besides Allah.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, they did not invite them to worship themselves, and had they invited them to worship themselves, they would not have responded to them, but they permitted for them the prohibited and prohibited for them the permissible, so they worshipped them from where they did not feel [the shift].'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who obeys a man in a disobedience (to Allah), so he has worshipped him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Fuzayl, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It was said to Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), 'The one who testifies that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), is a believer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So where are the Obligations of Allah?' And I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'If faith (Iman) were merely speech, there would not have been revealed regarding it fasting, nor prayer, nor the permissible, nor the forbidden.' And I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Among us is a group of people who say, And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not created a creature more prestigious to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than the believer, because the angels are the attendants of the believers, and the vicinity of Allah is for the believers, and Paradise is for the believers, and the Houris are for the believers.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is the case of the one who denies the Obligations? He is a disbeliever.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Sallam al-Ju'fi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about faith, so he said: 'Faith is that Allah is obeyed and not disobeyed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hakam, who said: I wrote to the Pious Servant (peace be upon him), informing him that I am doubtful, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had said: 'My Lord, show me how You revive the dead,' and I would like you to show me something. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Indeed, Ibrahim was a believer and he loved that there be an increase in his faith, and you are doubtful, and the one who is doubtful has no good in him.' And he wrote: 'Doubt is only that which precedes conviction; so when conviction comes, doubt is not permissible.' And he wrote: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: And We did not find in most of them any (faithfulness to) the Covenant, and We found most of them to be transgressors.' He said: 'It was revealed regarding the one who is doubtful.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abu Ishaq al-Khurasani, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say in his sermon: 'Do not be suspicious, for you will be doubting, and do not be doubtful, for you will be disbelieving.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I was sitting at the left of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Zurara was at his right. Abu Baseer entered and said, 'O Abu Abdullah, what do you say about the one who doubts in Allah?' He said, 'A kafir (disbeliever), O Abu Muhammad.' He said, 'And (what about) the one who doubts in the Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'A kafir.' Then he turned to Zurara and said, 'He only disbelieves when he rejects (denies with conviction).'

From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halbi, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who believe and did not mix their faith with iniquity.' He said: 'With doubt.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the doubter and the disobedient one are in the Fire; they are neither from us nor to us.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The meaning of the hadith: The one who doubts in Allah after his birth, being upon the natural disposition (fitrah), would not incline to any good ever.
From him, from his father, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: No deed with doubt and denial will be of any benefit.

From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I said, 'We see a man who has worship, striving, and humility, but he does not speak with the Truth (Wilayah); will that benefit him in any way?' He said, 'O Abu Muhammad! The example of the People of the Household is like the example of a household among the Children of Israel. No one from them would strive for forty nights and supplicate except that he would be answered.' And indeed, a man from them strived for forty nights, then supplicated, but he was not answered. So he came to Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him), complaining to him of what he was in, and asked him for supplication. So Isa purified himself and prayed, then supplicated to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Isa! My servant came to me from other than the door through which I am approached.' 'He supplicated to me, and in his heart was doubt about you. So even if he were to supplicate to me until his neck breaks and his fingers scatter, I will not answer him.' He said, 'So Isa (peace be upon him) turned towards him and said, 'You supplicate to your Lord while you are in doubt about His Prophet?'' So he said, 'O Spirit of Allah and His Word! It has been, by Allah, what you said. So supplicate to Allah for me that He removes it from me.' So Isa (peace be upon him) supplicated for him, and Allah turned to him (with forgiveness) and accepted from him, and he came to be within the limit of the People of the Household.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the weak ones (of understanding), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is the one who is not guided by a means to disbelief so that he would disbelieve, nor is he guided by a way to faith; he is not able to believe, nor is he able to disbelieve. So they are the children, and whoever of the men and women is upon the intellect of the children, the Pen (of recording deeds) is raised from them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The weak ones (of understanding) are those who do not have the capacity to reason, nor are they guided to a way. He said: They are not able to reach faith, nor do they disbelieve; these are the children, and those of similar intellect to the children, from men and women.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ib, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the weak one (of understanding), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is the one who has no capacity of reason to repel disbelief by it, nor is he guided by it to the way of faith. He has not the capacity that he believes nor that he disbelieves.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the children, and those from the men and women who are upon a similar intellect to the children.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibnfan ibn al-Sim al-Bajali, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the weak ones?' He said to me, resembling a state of panic: 'Have you left anyone who can be considered weak? And where are the weak ones? By Allah, the adolescent girls have carried this matter of yours to the adolescent girls in their chambers, and the water-carriers are discussing it in the streets of Medina.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayoub, from 'Umar ibn Aban who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the 'weak ones' (al-mustad'afin), so he said: 'They are the people of Wilayah.' I said, 'Which Wilayah?' He said: 'Indeed, it is not the Wilayah in the Religion, but it is the Wilayah regarding marriage, inheritance, and social mingling. And they are not among the believers, nor among the disbelievers, and among them are those hoped for regarding the Command of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Muthanna, from Ismail al-Ja'far, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Religion which there is no leeway for the servants to be ignorant of it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Religion is vast but the Kharijites narrowed it upon themselves due to their ignorance.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you (peace be upon him)! Can I narrate to you (peace be upon him) with my Religion which I am upon?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. So I said, 'I testify that there is no god except for Allah (exalted is He), and I testify that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger, and I acknowledge with whatever he came with from the Presence of Allah (exalted is He), and I befriend you (peace be upon him) and disavow from your enemies and the ones who stay away from your rights and are ordering upon you and are oppressing you of your rights.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You are not ignorant of anything. It is, by Allah, that which we are upon.' I said, 'So would anyone be safe if he does not recognise this matter (Al-Wilayah)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except for the weak ones (of understanding).' I said, 'Who are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your womenfolk and your children.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is your view of Umm Ayman, for I testify that she is from the inhabitants of the Paradise, and she did not recognise what you are upon.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recognizes the differing of the people, so he is not a weak one (of understanding)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I remember these weak ones (of understanding), so I say that we and they are in the dwellings of Paradise.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah would not do that with you all, ever!'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yaqoub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, who said: A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while we were in his presence: 'May I be sacrificed for you, we fear that due to our sins we will be lodged in the dwellings of the weak ones (of understanding).' He said: 'No, by Allah, Allah will not do that with you ever.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who recognizes the differing of the people, so he is not a weak one (of understanding).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Khuza'i, from Ali ibn Suweyd, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the weak ones (of understanding). So he wrote to me: 'The weak one is the one to whom the proof has not been raised, and he does not recognize the differing. So when he recognizes the differing, he is not considered a weak one (of understanding).'

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Habib al-Khash'ami, from Abu Sara, the prayer leader of the mosque of the Banu Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Today there is no one weak (of understanding); the men have delivered to the men, and the women to the women.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And others are hopeful of Allah's Command' He said: A group who were polytheists killed the likes of Hamza and Ja'far and similar ones from the believers. Then they entered into Islam, acknowledged Allah and left polytheism, but did not recognize faith with their hearts. So they are considered among the believers and Paradise becomes obligatory for them. And they were not upon their denial to disbelieve so Hellfire becomes obligatory for them. So they are in that state: either He will punish them or He will accept their repentance.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, from a man who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The Murjuna are a people who were polytheists, so they killed the likes of Hamza and Ja'far and similar ones among the believers. Then, after that, they entered into Islam, so they affirmed the Oneness of Allah and left polytheism, but they did not believe [fully] to be among the believers. They did not believe, so Paradise is not obligatory for them; and they did not disbelieve [completely], so Hellfire is not obligatory for them. So they are in that state, hopeful for the Command of Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, all from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What do you say about the People of the A'raf?' I said: 'They are nothing but either believers or disbelievers. If they enter Paradise, they are believers, and if they enter the Fire, they are disbelievers.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, they are neither believers nor disbelievers. Had they been believers, they would have entered Paradise just as the believers entered it, and had they been disbelievers, they would have entered the Fire just as the disbelievers entered it. But they are a people whose good deeds and evil deeds are equal, so their deeds fell short, and indeed they are as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said.' I said: 'Are they from the people of Paradise or from the people of the Fire?' He said: 'Leave them where Allah has left them.' I said: 'So shall I postpone them?' He said: 'Yes, I postpone them just as Allah has postponed them. If He wills, He will admit them to Paradise by His mercy, and if He wills, He will drive them to the Fire because of their sins, and He will not wrong them.' I said: 'Will a disbeliever enter Paradise?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'Will anyone enter the Fire except a disbeliever?' He said: 'No, except if Allah wills. O Zurara! Indeed, I say 'What Allah wills', and you do not say 'What Allah wills'. Know that when you grow old, you will retract, and your knots will be loosened from you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from a man who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Those who mixed a good deed and another evil one — so those are a people of faith who are innovating in their faith from the sins that the believers censure and dislike. So those are the ones upon whom Allah may turn (mercifully).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: May Allah curse the Qadiriyya, may Allah curse the Kharijites, may Allah curse the Murjiites, may Allah curse the Murjiites. I said, 'You cursed these once, and these twice?' He said: 'These [the Kharijites] say that those who killed us are believers, so our blood is stained on their clothes until the Day of Judgment.' Indeed, Allah related about a people in His Book: 'We will not believe in a messenger until he brings us an offering which the Fire consumes.' Say: 'Messengers came to you before me with clear proofs and with that which you demanded; why then did you kill them if you are truthful?' He said: 'There was a period of five hundred years between the killers and the speakers, but Allah imposed the killing upon them due to their agreement with what they had done.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakeym and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Masrouq, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked me about the people of Basra: 'What are they?' So I said, 'Murjiites, Qadiriyya, and Harouriyya'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah curse that nation of the disbelievers, the polytheists who do not worship Allah upon anything.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The people of Syria are more evil than the people of Rome, and the people of Medina are more evil than the people of Mecca, and the people of Mecca disbelieve in Allah openly.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayoub, from Saif ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the people of Syria worse, or the people of Rome?' He said: 'The Romans disbelieved and were not inimical to us, but the people of Syria disbelieved and were inimical to us.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not sit with them, meaning the Murji'ah. May Allah curse them, and may Allah curse their sects, the Polytheists, who do not worship Allah upon anything of the things.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And those whose hearts are to be reconciled.' He said: They are a people who affirmed the Oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and gave up the worship of those worshipped besides Allah, and testified that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), yet they were doubtful regarding some of what Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) brought. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to reconcile them with wealth and gifts, so that their Islam might become good and they would remain firm upon the religion they had entered and acknowledged. And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) reconciled the chiefs of the Arabs from Quraysh and the rest of Mudar on the Day of Hunayn. Among them were Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Uyaynah ibn Husayn al-Fazari, and similar people among the masses. So the Ansar became angry and gathered to Sa'd ibn Ubadah. He led them to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at Al-Ji'rana and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you grant me permission to speak?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'If this matter of the wealth you distributed among your people is something Allah revealed, we are pleased; and if it is other than that, we are not pleased.' Zurara said: And I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of the Ansar, is all of you upon the word of your chief Sa'd?' They said: 'Our chief is Allah and His Messenger.' Then they said for the third time: 'We are upon the like of his word and his view.' Zurara said: So I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: So Allah diminished their light, and Allah prescribed a share for those whose hearts are to be reconciled in the Quran.
Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The ones with distorted hearts have never been more numerous than they are today.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Is'haq ibn Ghalib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Is'haq! How many do you see to be referred to in this Verse: 'And among them is one who blames you with respect to the charities; so if they are given from it they are pleased, and if they are not given from it, then they are full of rage?' Then he said: 'They are more than two-thirds of the people'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from a man who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The ones with hearts to be reconciled have never been more numerous than they are today; and they are a people who affirmed the Oneness of Allah and exited from polytheism, but the recognition of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and what he brought did not enter their hearts. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was kind to them, and the believers were kind to them after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so that they might recognize (the truth).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, who said: Abu Amr al-Zubayri narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'O Scholar, inform me: which deed is most virtuous before Allah?' He said, 'That which Allah does not accept any deed without.' I said, 'And what is that?' He said, 'Faith in Allah, the One besides whom there is no deity. It is the highest in degree, the most noble in station, and the most abundant in reward.' I said, 'Will you not inform me about faith? Is it speech and action, or speech without action?' He said, 'Faith is entirely action, and speech is part of that action, by obligation from Allah. He clarified it in His Book, its light is clear, its proof is established. The Book testifies to it for one and calls one to it.' I said, 'Describe it to me, may I be your ransom, so I may understand.' He said, 'Faith has states, degrees, layers, and stations. Among it is that which is perfect, its perfection being its end. Among it is that which is deficient, its deficiency being clear. Among it is that which is preponderant, its excess being greater.' I said, 'Indeed, faith becomes perfect, deficient, and increases.' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'How is that?' He said, 'Because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made faith obligatory upon the limbs of the son of Adam, divided it among them, and distributed it within them. Thus, there is no limb of his but that it has been assigned a specific aspect of faith, different from what its sister limb was assigned.' Among them is his heart, with which he understands, comprehends, and perceives. It is the commander of his body; the limbs do not return nor issue except by its opinion and command. Among them are his two eyes with which he sees, his two ears with which he hears, his two hands with which he grasps, his two legs with which he walks, his private part from which comes desire, his tongue with which he speaks, and his head upon which is his face. There is no limb among these but that it has been assigned a specific aspect of faith, different from what its sister limb was assigned, by obligation from Allah, Blessed is His Name. The Book speaks for it and testifies against it. So He made obligatory upon the heart what He did not make obligatory upon the hearing. He made obligatory upon the hearing what He did not make obligatory upon the t

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan or someone else, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about faith (Iman). He said: 'The testimony that there is no god except Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and the acknowledgement of what came from Allah, and what has settled in the hearts as ratification of that.' He said: I said, 'Is the testimony not a deed?' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'Is the deed from faith?' He said: 'Yes, faith does not exist except with a deed, and the deed is from it, and faith is not established except with a deed.'
