A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'What is Islam?' He said: 'It is the religion of Allah, its name is Islam, and it was the religion of Allah before you existed, where you are, and after you. So whoever acknowledges the religion of Allah is a Muslim, and whoever acts in accordance with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded, is a believer.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Ayoub ibn Al-Hurr, from Abu Baseer, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Sallam said to him: 'Khaysama ibn Abu Khaysama narrates from you that he asked you about Islam, and you said to him: Islam is he who faces our Qiblah, testifies our Shahadah, performs our Nusk, befriends our Auliya, and enmies our A'adwa, so he is a Muslim.' He said: 'Khaysama spoke the truth.' I said: 'And he asked you about Iman, and you said: Iman is belief in Allah, and affirmation with the Book of Allah, and that Allah is not disobeyed.' He said: 'Khaysama spoke the truth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about faith (Iman), so he said: 'The testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' I said, 'Is this not a deed?' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'So is the deed from faith?' He said: 'Faith is not established for him except with the deed, and the deed is from it.'

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Muyassar, from Hammad ibn Amr al-Nasibi, who said: A man asked the Knowledgeable One (peace be upon him), saying: 'O the Knowledgeable One, inform me, which of the deeds is most superior in the presence of Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That without which a deed is not accepted.' He asked: 'And what is that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith in Allah, which is the highest of deeds in rank, the most abundant in share, and the noblest in status.' I said: 'Inform me about faith, is it speech and deed, or speech without deed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith is all deed, and speech is part of that deed, by an imposition from Allah, which He clarified in His Book. Its light is clear, its argument is firm. The Book testifies with it and calls towards it.' I said: 'Describe that to me so that I may understand it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, faith has states, ranks, layers, and stations. From it is the complete, whose completion is ultimate, and from it is the deficient, whose deficiency is ultimate, and from it is the increasing, whose increase is predominant.' I said: 'Does faith indeed become complete, increase, and decrease?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, imposed faith upon the limbs of the children of Adam, divided it among them, and distributed it upon them. Thus, there is no limb of theirs except that it has been assigned a portion of faith, other than what its counterpart (sister limb) was assigned.' Among them is his heart, by which he understands, comprehends, and realizes, and it is the commander of his body, from whose view and command the limbs do not depart nor return. Among them are his two hands with which he grasps, and his two legs with which he walks, and his private part from which comes the act of copulation, and his tongue by which he recites the Book and testifies to it, and his two eyes with which he sees, and his two ears with which he hears. And He imposed upon the heart what He did not impose upon the tongue; and He imposed upon the tongue what He did not impose upon the two eyes; and He imposed upon the two eyes what He did not impose upon the hearing; and He imposed upon the hearing what He did not impose upon the two hands; and He imposed upon the two hands what He did not impose upon the two

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from one of our companions, from al-Ash'ath ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Hafsh ibn Kharjah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man asked him about the statement of the Murji'ah regarding disbelief and faith, and he said: Indeed, they argue against us and say, 'Just as the disbeliever among us is the disbeliever with Allah, so too we find that the believer, when he acknowledges his faith, is the believer with Allah.' So he (peace be upon him) said: Glory be to Allah! And how can these two be equal? Disbelief is an acknowledgment by the servant, so he is not required after his acknowledgment to provide proof. But faith is a claim that is not valid except with proof, and its proof is his deed and his intention. So when they agree, the servant is a believer with Allah. And disbelief is present in any one of these three aspects: from intention, or speech, or deed. And the rulings flow upon the speech and the deed. So how many are there whom the believers testify to having faith, and the rulings of the believers flow upon him, yet he is a disbeliever with Allah? And the one who applies the rulings of the believers upon him is correct, based on the apparent of his speech and his deed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a people for faith, from which there is no decline; and He created a people for disbelief, from which there is no decline; and He created a people in between, and deposited faith in some of them. So if He wills to complete it for them, He completes it; and if He wills to deprive them of it, He deprives them of it; and so-and-so from them was with temporary faith.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub and Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Kuleyb ibn Muawiya Al-Asady, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a servant may become a believer in the morning and an unbeliever in the evening, or an unbeliever in the morning and a believer in the evening; and a people are lent faith (Iman), then it is taken away from them, and they are named 'the lent ones' (Al-Mu'arun); then he (peace be upon him) said: 'So-and-so was from them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Isa Shalan, who said: I was sitting when Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) passed by, and with him was a goat. I said, 'O boy, what do you say about what your father does? He orders us with something then forbids us from it. He ordered us to befriend Abu al-Khattab, then he ordered us to curse him and disavow him.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, while he was still a boy: 'Indeed, Allah created a people for faith, from which it will not depart; and He created a people for disbelief, from which it will not depart; and He created a people in between those two, lending them faith. They are called the 'loaned ones' (al-mu'arun). When He wills, He strips it from them. And Abu al-Khattab was among those who were lent faith.' He said: So I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him of what I had said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and what he had said to me. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He is a spring of prophethood.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah created the Prophets upon prophethood, so they will not be except prophets; and He created the believers upon faith, so they will not be except believers; and He lent faith to a people. So if He wills, He completes it for them, and if He wills, He takes it away from them. He said: And among them, it flowed, so [there are] those who are stable and those who are temporary (deposited). And he said to me: So-and-so had temporary faith. So when he lied against us, that faith of his was taken away.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Habeeb, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah formed the Prophets upon their prophethood, so they will not revert (to disbelief) ever. And He formed the Successors upon their succession, so they will not revert ever. And He formed some of the believers upon faith, so they will not revert ever. And among them is one to whom faith is lent as a loan; so when he supplicates and persists in supplication, he dies upon faith.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer and others, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The heart happens to be, at a given moment of the day or night, in a state where there is neither disbelief nor faith, like a worn-out garment.' He said, 'Then he said to me: Do you not find that within yourself?' He said: 'The spot (or mark) appears from Allah in the heart, according to what He wills, of disbelief and faith.' A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, [narrated] similarly.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The heart becomes such that there is in it neither faith nor disbelief, resembling a lump of meat. Has not any one of you found that?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah created the hearts of the believers folded and obscure regarding faith. So when He intends to enlighten what is within them, He sprinkles them with wisdom and plants them with knowledge, and its Planter and the One in charge over it is the Lord of the worlds.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the heart trembles between the chest and the throat until it is tied to faith; so when it is tied to faith, it settles, and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the heart jingles in the chest, seeking the truth; so when it finds it, it becomes calm and settles. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited this verse: So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He intends to misguide, He makes his chest narrow and constricted, as though he were ascending to the sky. Up to His Words: 'as though he were ascending to the sky'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The heart is such that during a time from the night and the day, there is neither faith in it nor disbelief. Do you not find that to be so? Then after that, a spot from Allah appears in the heart of His servant with whatever He wills. If He wills, [He places] faith, and if He wills, [He places] disbelief.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Yunus ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah created the hearts of the believers wrapped up over faith. So when He intends to enlighten what is in them, He opens them with wisdom and plants them with knowledge, and its Planter and the One in charge of it is the Lord of the Worlds.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Fazzal from Ali ibn Uqba from Amr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to us one day: 'You will find a man who does not err in the letters Lam and Waw, an eloquent orator, yet his heart is darker than the dark night; and you will find a man who cannot express what is in his heart with his tongue, yet his heart shines like a lamp.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Mufaddal, from Sa'd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, hearts are four: a heart in which is hypocrisy and faith, an inverted heart, an imprinted heart, and a shining, pure heart. So I said, 'What is the shining one?' He said, 'It is like the form of a lamp.' As for the imprinted one, it is the heart of the hypocrite; and as for the shining one, it is the heart of the believer: if He gives, he is grateful, and if He tests him, he is patient; and as for the inverted one, it is the heart of the polytheist. Then he recited this verse: 'So is one who walks prone on his face better guided or one who walks upright on a straight path?' As for the heart in which is faith and hypocrisy, they were a people who were in Al-Ta'if. So if death overtook one of them upon his hypocrisy, he perished, and if it overtook him upon his faith, he attained salvation.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The hearts are three: an inverted heart that does not grasp any good, and it is the heart of the disbeliever; and a heart in which is a black spot, so good and evil wrestle in it, and whichever of the two prevails over it, it dominates; and an open heart in which are shining lamps, and its light will not be extinguished until the Day of Resurrection, and it is the heart of the believer.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the satanic insinuations (al-waswasah), even if they were frequent, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing in it; you should say, 'La ilaha illa Allah'.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A great matter occurs in my heart.' He said, 'Say, La ilaha illa Allah.' Jameel said, 'So whenever something occurred in my heart, I would say, La ilaha illa Allah, and it would go away from me.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I am destroyed!' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'The wicked one (Satan) came to you and said to you, 'Who created you?' So you said, 'Allah.' Then he said to you, 'Who created Him?' So he said, 'Yes, by the One who sent you with the truth, it was so.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'That, by Allah, is pure faith.' Ibn Abi Umeyr said, 'So I narrated that to Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and he said, 'My father narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) meant by his words, 'This, by Allah, is pure faith,' fearing that he might have been destroyed because that occurred to him in his heart.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: A man wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) complaining to him of insinuations (lammam) that flashed across his mind. So he (peace be upon him) answered in one of his speeches: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, if He wills, will establish you firmly, so He will not make for Iblees a way upon you.' A group of people had complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of insinuations that presented to them; it was more beloved to them if the wind were to sweep them away or a limb were cut off, than that they should speak about it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do you find that?' They said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul! That is explicit faith (Iman). So whenever you find it, say: We have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah.' 'We have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Janah, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad, from Abu Al-Yasa' Dawud Al-Abzari, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have become a hypocrite.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, you are not so; and had you been so, you would not have come to me to inform me of what caused you to doubt. I think the present enemy (Satan) came to you and said to you, 'Who created you?' So you said, 'Allah created me.' Then he said to you, 'Who created Allah?' He said, 'Yes, by the One who sent you with the truth, it was so.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Satan comes to you from the aspect of deeds, but is not strong enough upon you, so he comes from this direction perhaps he would make you waver. Therefore, whenever it is like that, let one of you mention Allah Alone.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali al-Ahmasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: By Allah, he will not be saved from the sin except the one who acknowledges it. He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Regret suffices as repentance.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: No, by Allah! Allah the Exalted did not intend from the people except two characteristics: that they acknowledge to Him the bounties, so He increases them, and (acknowledge) the sins, so He forgives them for them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'A man commits a sin, and Allah enters him into Paradise because of it.' I said: 'Does Allah enter him into Paradise because of the sin?' He said: 'Yes. He commits a sin, so he does not cease to be fearful of it, hating his own self, so Allah shows mercy on him and enters him into Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, a servant does not exit from a sin while persisting in it, and a servant does not exit from a sin except by acknowledgement.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Imran ibn al-Hajjaj al-Sabi'i, from Muhammad ibn Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever commits a sin, and knows that Allah is watching over it, if He wills He punishes him, and if He wills He forgives him; He forgives him even if he does not seek forgiveness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Hashim, from Anbasa al-Abid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah loves the servant that he seeks (forgiveness) to Him regarding the grievous crime, and He hates the servant if he takes lightly with the small crime.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Daqqaq, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from Zayd al-Qattat, from Aban ibn Taghlub, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no servant who commits a sin and regrets it, except that Allah forgives him before he seeks forgiveness; and there is no servant upon whom Allah bestows a favor, so he recognizes that it is from Allah, except that Allah forgives him before he praises Him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas, the freedman of Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who veils a good deed equals seventy good deeds, and the one who broadcasts an evil deed is forsaken, and the one who veils an evil deed is forgiven.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Sandal, from Yasser, from Al-Yasa' ibn Hamza, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who veils a good deed equals seventy good deeds, and the one who broadcasts an evil deed is rebuked, and the one who veils it is forgiven.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, decreed for Adam in his offspring: Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, one good deed is recorded for him; whoever intends a good deed and does it, ten good deeds are recorded for him; whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, no evil deed is recorded against him; and whoever intends it and does it, one evil deed is recorded against him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the believer intends a good deed but does not perform it, so one good deed is recorded for him; and if he performs it, ten good deeds are recorded for him. And indeed, the believer intends an evil deed that he would perform, but he does not perform it, so it is not recorded against him.

From him, from Ali ibn Hafs al-Awsī, from Ali ibn al-Sāḥib, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from his father, who said: I asked him about the two Angels: Do they know of the sin when the servant intends to do it, or the good deed? He said: 'Is the smell of the latrine and the smell of perfume the same?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'Indeed, when the servant intends a good deed, his breath exudes a pleasant smell, so the Companion of the Right says to the Companion of the Left: 'Arise, for he has intended a good deed.' When he does it, his tongue is his pen and his saliva is his ink, and it is recorded for him. And when he intends an evil deed, his breath exudes a foul smell, so the Companion of the Left says to the Companion of the Right: 'Pause, for he has intended an evil deed.' When he does it, his tongue is his pen and his saliva is his ink, and it is recorded for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fazl ibn Uthman al-Muradi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four [characteristics]; whoever possesses them, destruction will not be upon Allah's decree upon him after these, except for one who destroys himself.' The servant intends a good deed and performs it; if he does not perform it, Allah writes for him one good deed due to his good intention, and if he performs it, Allah writes for him ten [good deeds]. And he intends an evil deed to perform; if he does not perform it, nothing is written against him, and if he performs it, it is postponed for seven hours. And the Companion of Good Deeds says to the Companion of Evil Deeds, and he is the Companion of the Left: 'Do not be hasty; perhaps he will follow it with a good deed that will erase it.' Surely good deeds take away evil deeds. Or [through] seeking forgiveness. If he says: 'I seek forgiveness of Allah, who is no god except He, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Mighty, the Wise, the Forgiving, the Merciful, the Lord of Majesty and Generosity,' and repents to Him, nothing is written against him. And if seven hours pass and he does not follow it with a good deed and seeking forgiveness, The Companion of Good Deeds says to the Companion of Evil Deeds: 'Write [it] against the wretched, the deprived one.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a servant sins a sin, he is given respite from morning until night; so if he seeks forgiveness from Allah, it will not be recorded against him.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umair and Abu Ali Al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever performs an evil deed is respited regarding it for seven hours of the day. So if he says, 'I seek Forgiveness of Allah, Who, there is no god except for Him, the Living, the Eternal,' three times, it will not be written against him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, all from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a believing servant commits a sin, Allah grants him a respite of seven hours. If he seeks forgiveness from Allah, no record is kept against him; but if the hours pass and he does not seek forgiveness, one evil deed is recorded against him. Indeed, the believer is reminded of his sin even after twenty years, so he seeks forgiveness from his Lord and He forgives him; whereas the unbeliever forgets it from the moment he commits it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seventy times a day. So I said, 'Did he say: I seek forgiveness of Allah and I turn to Him?' He said, 'No, but he used to say: I turn to Allah.' I said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) repented and did not repeat, while we repent and repeat.' So he said, 'Allah is the One sought for help.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever performs an evil deed is respited regarding it for seven hours of the day. So if he says, 'I seek Forgiveness of Allah, the One there is no god except Him, the Living, the Eternal, and I repent to Him,' three times, it will not be written against him.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, the seller of garments, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the believer commits a sin, then he is reminded of it after twenty years, so he seeks forgiveness from Allah for it, and He forgives him; and He reminds him only so that He may forgive him. And indeed, the disbeliever commits a sin, so he forgets it from the moment he commits it.
From him, from a number of our companions, raising it, saying, they said: For everything there is a cure, and the cure for the sins is the seeking of Forgiveness.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya, altogether, from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no believer who commits a sin except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has appointed for him a respite of seven hours from the day. So if he repents, nothing is written against him, and if he does not (repent), Allah writes one evil deed against him.' So 'Abbad al-Basri came to him and said to him: 'It has reached us that you said: There is no servant who commits a sin except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has appointed for him a respite of seven hours from the day.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I did not say it like this, but I said: There is no believer,' and that was how my words were.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who says, “I seek forgiveness of Allah,” one hundred times every day, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will forgive him seven hundred sins, and there is no good in a servant who sins every day, seven hundred times.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah or from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, You empowered the Satan against me and made him flow from me like blood, so make something for me.' He said: 'O Adam, I have made for you that whoever from your offspring intends an evil deed, it is not recorded against him; if he does it, one evil deed is recorded against him. And whoever from them intends a good deed but does not do it, one good deed is recorded for him; if he does it, ten are recorded for him.' He said: 'O Lord, increase for me.' He said: 'I have made for you that whoever from them does an evil deed, then seeks forgiveness for it, I forgive him.' He said: 'O Lord, increase for me.' He said: 'I made repentance for them,' or said: 'I extended repentance for them until the soul reaches this (the throat).' He said: 'O Lord, that is sufficient for me.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repents one year before his death, Allah will accept his repentance.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a year is a long time.' Whoever repents one month before his death, Allah will accept his repentance.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a month is a long time.' Whoever repents one day before his death, Allah will accept his repentance.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a day is a long time.' Whoever repents before he sees (death), Allah will accept his repentance.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the soul reaches this [point of no return], and he dropped his hand to his throat, there would be no repentance for the knower, and for the ignorant there would still be repentance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, "What is your view of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who keep aloof from the great sins and the immoralities except for the 'Lamam'"? He said: "It is the sin that a man commits, and he remains (not committing it again) for as long as Allah so Desires, then he commits it (again) afterwards."

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I said to him: 'What about those who keep aloof from the great sins and the immoralities except for the 'Lamam'?' He said: 'The defiance after the defiance, i.e., the sin after the sin committed by the servant.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no believer but that he has a sin which he forsakes for a time, then he commits it again, and this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "except for the Lamam".' And I asked him about the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Those who keep aloof from the great sins and the immoralities, except for the Lamam". He said: 'The immoralities are adultery and theft, and the Lamam is when a man commits a sin, so he seeks forgiveness from Allah for it (and then commits it again).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Harith ibn Bahram, from Amr ibn Jumi', who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who comes to us seeking jurisprudence and the Quran and its interpretation, invite him; and the one who comes to us showing openly what Allah has veiled, turn him away.' A man from the group said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, I have been persisting upon a sin for a long time. I intend to turn away from it to something else, but I am not able to do so.' He said to him: 'If you are truthful, then Allah loves you, and nothing prevents Him from transferring you from it to something else except that you fear Him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no sin except that a believing servant has it imprinted upon him; he avoids it for a time, then commits it. Those who avoid the great sins and immoralities, except for minor slips. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Lammam is the servant who commits a sin after a sin, which is not from his nature, i.e., not from his inherent disposition.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believer's disposition is not lying, stinginess, and immorality; and sometimes he commits something from that which he does not persist in.' It was said, 'So he commits adultery?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but a child is not born for him from that seed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn Humran, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when it is His will to honor a servant who has a sin, He tests him with sickness. If He does not do that for him, He tests him with need (poverty). If He does not do that with him, He makes death difficult for him to compensate for that sin with it. He (peace be upon him) said: And when it is His will to humble a servant who has a good deed with Him, He grants health to his body. If He does not do that with him, He expands his sustenance for him. If he does not do that with him, He eases death for him to compensate for that good deed with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ismail ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the servant's sins are numerous and he does not have with him from his deeds that would expiate them, He tests him with grief to expiate them.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My Honour and My Majesty! I will not take a servant from the world while I intend to be merciful to him until I fully compensate him for every mistake (sin) he has committed, either through sickness in his body, or through constriction in his sustenance, or through fear in his worldly life. So if a remainder remains upon him, I will intensify (the punishment) for him at the time of death.' And by My Honour and My Majesty! I will not take a servant from the world while I intend to punish him until I fully fulfill for him every good deed he has done, either through expansion in his sustenance, or through health in his body, or through security in his worldly life. So if a remainder remains upon him, I will ease the death for him because of it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is terrified in his sleep, so his sins are forgiven for him, and he is tested in his body, so his sins are forgiven for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Sari ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wants good for a servant, He hastens his punishment in the world; and when He wants evil for a servant, He withholds his sins until he meets them on the Day of Judgment.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever affliction befalls you, it is on account of what your hands have wrought, and what He Pardons is more' 'There is none from the twisting of a vein, nor a stumbling over a stone, nor a slip of a foot, nor a scratch by wood, except it is due to a sin,' 'and what He Pardons is more.' So for the one for whom Allah Hastens the Punishment for his sin in the world, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more Majestic and more Benevolent and more Magnificent than for Him to Repeat Punishing him in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq, from Ali al-Ahmasi, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Worry and grief do not cease to be with the believer until they leave no sin for him.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Harith ibn Bahram, from Amr ibn Jumi' who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believing servant is indeed concerned/anxious in the world until he exits from it, and there is no sin upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'There is no servant whom I intend to admit to Paradise except that I afflict him in his body. If that is an expiation for his sins, or else I intensify [the affliction] upon him at his death until he comes to Me with no sin, then I admit him to Paradise.' And there is no servant whom I intend to admit to the Fire except that I make his body sound. If that is completion of his request for Me, or else I secure his fear from his ruler. If that is completion of his request for Me, or else I expand his sustenance for him. If that is completion of his request for Me, or else I ease his death for him until he comes to Me with no good deed for Me, then I admit him to the Fire.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Ibn Muskan, from one of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A Prophet from the Prophets of the Children of Israel passed by a man, part of him was under a wall and part of him was outside from it, the birds had dishevelled him and the dogs had ripped him apart. Then he continued and a city was raised for him, so he entered it, and there he was with a great one from its great ones, dead upon a bed decorated with brocade, with the incense burner around him. So he said: 'O Lord! I testify that You are a Just Judge, not a tyrant. This servant of Yours did not associate with You even for the blink of an eye, yet You caused him to die with that death; and this is Your servant who did not believe in You even for the blink of an eye, yet You caused him to die with this death.' So He said: 'My servant! I am as you said, a Just Judge not being tyrannous. That servant of Mine had an evil deed or a sin with Me, so I caused him to die with that death so that he would meet Me and nothing would remain upon him; and this servant of Mine had a good deed with Me, so I caused him to die with this death so that he would meet Me and there would not be a good deed for him with Me.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when an old man entered upon him and said, 'O Abu Abdullah! I complain to you about my children and their ingratitude, and my brothers and their disloyalty during my old age.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'O man! Indeed, for the Truth there is a dominion (era/condition), and for falsehood there is a dominion, and each one of these two is humiliated in the dominion of its counterpart.' And the least of what befalls the believer in the dominion of falsehood is ingratitude from his children and disloyalty from his brothers. And no believer attains anything of prosperity in the dominion of falsehood except that he is tried before his death, either in his body, or in his children, or in his wealth. Until Allah purifies him from what he earned in the dominion of falsehood and completes his share in the dominion of the Truth. So be patient and receive glad tidings.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-'Abbas ibn al-'Ala' from Mujahid from his father from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The sins that change the bounties are transgression; the sins that bring regret are murder; and that which brings down curses is injustice; and that which tears the veil is drinking wine; and that which withholds sustenance is adultery; and that which hastens annihilation is severing ties of kinship; and that which repels supplication and darkens the air is disobedience to the parents.

Ali ibn mahboub from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father (peace be upon him) was saying: We seek Refuge with Allah from the sins which hasten annihilation, bring death closer, and vacate the households, and they are cutting off of relationships, ingratitude, and neglect of righteousness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, or one of his companions, from Ayoub, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: 'One of our companions narrated to me, saying:' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When four (things) become prevalent, four (things) would appear. When adultery becomes prevalent, earthquakes appear; and when tyranny in judgment becomes prevalent, the raindrops are withheld; and when the covenant (of protection) is breached, polytheists are given preference over the people of Islam; and when Zakat is withheld, need (poverty/hardship) appears.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever affliction befalls you, it is on account of what your hands have wrought.' He said: 'It is [the first part], and [the second part] 'and He pardons most'.' I said, 'I did not mean this. What is your view of what afflicted Ali and those like him from the People of his Household (peace be upon them) from that [affliction]?' So he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to repent to Allah seventy times a day, even without having sinned.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever affliction befalls you, it is on account of what your hands have wrought.' 'What is your view of what hit Ali and the People of his Household (peace be upon them) after him? Is it due to what their hands had wrought, and they are the Pure People of the Household, the Infallible?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to turn to Allah and seek His Forgiveness during every day and night, one hundred times, without having sinned. Indeed, Allah Particularizes His Guardians with afflictions in order to recompense them for them without having sinned.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If people knew how the creation began, no two would disagree. Indeed God — Mighty and Majestic — before He created creation, said: 'Be sweet water! I shall create from you My Paradise and the people of My obedience. And be bitter water! I shall create from you My Fire and the people of My disobedience.' Then He commanded them both, so they were blended. Thus it came about that the believer begets the disbeliever and the disbeliever begets the believer. Then He took clay from the surface of the earth and kneaded it with an intense kneading, and they were like tiny particles crawling about. So He said to the companions of the right hand: 'To Paradise in peace!' And He said to the companions of the left hand: 'To the Fire, and I do not care!' Then He commanded a fire, so it blazed. He said to the companions of the left: 'Enter it!' But they were terrified of it. So He said to the companions of the right: 'Enter it!' And they entered it. So He said: 'Be cool and a safety!' And it became cool and a safety. The companions of the left said: 'O Lord, forgive us!' He said: 'I have forgiven you, so enter it.' They went but were terrified of it. Thus from that point, obedience and disobedience were established — these ones do not have the capacity to be from those, nor those from these.

A man asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Majestic and Mighty: "And when your Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants, and made them testify against their own souls: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes" — up to the end of the verse. So he (peace be upon him) replied, while his father was listening: My father narrated to me that God, Mighty and Majestic, seized a handful of the soil from which He created Adam (peace be upon him), and poured the sweet water of the Euphrates over it. Then He left it for forty mornings. Then He poured the salty, bitter water over it and left it for forty mornings. When the clay had fermented (like dough), He took it and kneaded it with an intense kneading. Then they came out like tiny particles — from its right side and its left. He commanded them all to enter the Fire. The companions of the right entered, and it became coolness and peace for them. But the companions of the left refused to enter it.

When God, Mighty and Majestic, intended to create Adam (peace be upon him), He sent water upon the clay. Then He grabbed a handful and kneaded it. Then He separated it into two groups with His Hand. Then He scattered them, and behold, they were crawling. Then He raised a fire for them and commanded the people of the left to enter it. So they went towards it but feared it and did not enter it. Then He commanded the people of the right to enter it. So they went and entered it. God, Majestic and Mighty, commanded the fire, so it became cool and safe for them. When the people of the left saw that, they said, 'Our Lord, forgive us.' So He forgave them, then said to them, 'Enter it!' So they went and stood at it but did not enter it. So He returned them all to clay and created Adam (peace be upon him) from it. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So these ones will never be able to become from those ones, nor those ones to become from these ones.' He said: 'They believe that the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was the first one to enter that fire.' And that is His word, Majestic and Mighty: 'Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed Faith upon seven portions: upon righteousness, truthfulness, conviction, contentment, loyalty, knowledge, and forbearance. Then He distributed that among the people, so whoever in whom He placed these seven portions, he is complete and capable. And He distributed for some of the people one portion, and for some two portions, and for some three, until they reached the seven. Then he said: Do not burden the owner of one portion with two portions, nor the owner of two portions with three, so that you break them. Then he said: It is like that until it reaches the seven.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Ibn Fazzal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abu al-Yaqthan, from Yaqub ibn al-Dahhak, from a man from our companions, Sirraj, who was a servant of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent me regarding a need, and he was at Al-Hira, I and a group of his slaves. So we went regarding it, then we returned gloomy. He said: And my bed was in the Ha'ir (enclosure) where we were lodging. So I came while I was in that state, and I threw myself (down). So while I was like that, behold, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had come over. He said: So he said, 'We have come to you,' or he said, 'I have come to you.' So I sat up straight, and he sat upon the middle of my bed. So he asked me about what he had sent me for, so I informed him. So he praised Allah. Then there flowed a mention of a group of people, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We disavow from them. They are not saying what we are saying.' He said: So he said, 'If they were befriending us and not saying what you are saying, would you be disassociating from them?' He said: I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'So since that which is with us is not what is with you, so it would be befitting for us to disassociate from you?' He said: I said, 'No, may I be sacrificed for you!' He said: 'And since that which is with Allah is what is not with us, so what is your view, should we drop it?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you! What should we do?' He said: 'So befriend them and do not disassociate from them. From the Muslims, there is the one for whom there is one portion, and from them is the one for whom there are two portions, and from them is the one for whom there are three portions, and from them is the one for whom there are four portions, and from them is the one for whom there are five portions, and from them is the one for whom there are six portions, and from them is the one for whom there are seven portions.' So it is not befitting that the owner of the one portion be burdened with what is upon the owner of the two portions, nor the owner of the two portions with what is upon the owner of the three, nor the owner of the three with what is upon the owner of the four, nor the owner of the four with what is upon the owner of the five, nor the owne

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever Allah intends good for a servant, and he commits a sin, He follows it with an affliction and reminds him of seeking forgiveness; and whenever He intends evil for a servant, and he commits a sin, He follows it with a bounty to make him forget seeking forgiveness, and he continues to indulge in it.' And this is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know.' With the bounties during the disobedience.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'We will gradually entice them from where they do not know.' He said: 'He is the servant who commits a sin, and the Bounty is renewed for him along with it. That Bounty distracts him from seeking forgiveness for that sin.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud Al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: How many are deceived by what Allah has bestowed upon him, and how many are gradually allured by Allah's veiling (of His punishment) upon him, and how many are captivated by the praise of people for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Time is but three days. The past day has gone with what was in it and will not return. If you did good in it, you will not grieve its departure but rejoice in what it brought; if you were negligent in it, your regret for its departure will be severe due to your negligence.' And you are in your day, which you have entered from tomorrow, in a state of surprise, not knowing if you will reach it. And if you do reach it, perhaps your share of negligence in it will be like your share of negligence in the past day. So one of the three days has passed, in which you were negligent; and a day you await, in which you are not certain of leaving negligence. And it is your day which you have entered. It is fitting for you to use your intellect and reflect on what you neglected in the past day: the good deeds you failed to acquire and the evil deeds you failed to avoid. And with this, while facing tomorrow, you are without confidence in reaching it and without certainty of acquiring a good deed or turning away from a frustrating evil. Thus, you are in your day which you face as in your day which you left behind. So act like a man who hopes from the days only for the day he wakes in and its night. So act or leave it, and Allah is the Helper in that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mazi (peace be upon him), who said: He is not from us, the one who does not account for himself every day. So if he does good, he asks Allah for increase, and if he does evil, he seeks forgiveness from Allah for it and repents to Him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Nu'man al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: O Abu al-Nu'man! Do not let the people deceive you regarding yourself, for the matter will reach you through them, and do not pass your day with such and such, for there is with you one who preserves your deeds for you. And do good, for I have not seen anything that is better in attainment nor faster in seeking than a new good deed for an old sin. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Nu'man — similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Be patient with the world, for it is but a moment. So whatever of it has passed, you will find neither pain nor joy for it; and whatever has not yet come, you do not know what it is. And it is only your moment which you are in now, so be patient in it upon the obedience of Allah, and be patient in it from the disobedience of Allah.'
From him, from one of our companions, raising it, said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Carry yourself for yourself, for if you do not do so, others will not carry you.'

From him, raising it, said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to a man: 'You have been made to be a physician yourself, and the illness has been clarified to you, and you have been made to recognize the sign of health, and you have been indicated upon the cure, therefore look how you are standing (burdened) upon yourself'.

From him, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to a man: 'Make your heart a righteous companion, or a child that maintains ties [with parents]; make your deed a parent that you follow; make your self an enemy that you strive against; and make your wealth a loan that you will return.'

And from him, raising it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man reaches the age of forty, it is said to him: 'Take caution, for you are without excuse.' And the forty-year-old is not more entitled to caution than the twenty-year-old, for what seeks them both is the same (death), and it is not sleeping. So work for what is in front of you from the horrors, and set aside useless speech.

From him from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hassan from Zayd al-Shahham who said: } } }, { Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Take for yourself from yourself; take from it during health before sickness, and during strength before weakness, and during life before death.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when the day comes, it says: 'O son of Adam, do good in this day of yours; I will testify for you with it in the Presence of your Lord on the Day of Judgment, for I did not come to you in what has passed, nor will I come to you in what remains.' And when the night comes, it says similar to that.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Shu'ayb ibn Abdillah from one of his companions, raising it, said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Advise me of an aspect of righteousness by which I may attain salvation.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'O questioner! Listen, then understand, then be convinced, then act; and know that people are of three types: an ascetic, a patient one, and a covetous one.' As for the ascetic, grief and happiness have exited his heart, so he does not rejoice in anything from the world, nor does he despair over anything from it that has left him; thus he is at peace. As for the patient one, he wishes for it in his heart; but when he attains from it, he restrains his self from it due to its evil consequence and its repulsiveness. If you were to look into his heart, you would be astonished by its chastity, humility, and resoluteness. As for the covetous one, he does not care from where the world comes to him, whether from its permissible means or its prohibited means, and he does not care what filth he has incurred in it, destroyed his soul, and lost his manliness; thus they are in a flood of confusion, tossing about.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not belittle what is beneficial on the Day of Judgment, nor belittle what is harmful on the Day of Judgment. So be among that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed you of, like those who witnessed it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, all from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If you are able to not be known (by people), then do so. And what is upon you if people do not praise you? And what is upon you if you are condemned by people while you are praised by Allah?' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), said: There is no goodness in life except for two men: a man who increases in goodness every day, and a man who makes up for his death/evil deeds with repentance. And how can he have repentance?' By Allah! Even if he prostrates until his neck is cut off, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not accept from him except through our Wilayah - the People of the Household. Indeed! And whoever recognizes our rights and hopes for the reward in us, and is pleased with his sustenance of half a Mudd every day, and what covers his bareness, and what covers his head, and they, by Allah, are fearful and anxious in that. They wish that it is their share from the world. And thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described them, saying: 'And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, that they will return to their Lord.' Then he said: 'What is that which they give? By Allah! They give with obedience, love, and Wilayah, and they are fearful in that. Their fear is not the fear of doubt, but they fear that they may be deficient in our love and our obedience.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Al-Hakam ibn Salim, who said: A group of people came in, so he advised them, then he said: 'There is not one of you except that he has visually perceived Paradise and what is in it, and visually perceived the Fire and what is in it, if you are affirming the Book.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'How beautiful are the good deeds after the evil deeds, and how ugly are the evil deeds after the good deeds.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: You are (living) in fixed terms and numbered days, and death comes unexpectedly. The one who cultivates goodness will harvest bliss, and the one who cultivates evil will harvest regret; and for every cultivator is what he cultivated. The slow-moving among you will not be preceded in his share, nor will the greedy one attain what was not decreed for him. Whoever is given good, Allah has given him; and whoever is protected from evil, Allah has protected him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Wasil, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to Abu Zarr and said, 'O Abu Zarr! Why do we dislike death?' He said, 'Because you have built up the world and ruined the Hereafter, so you dislike being transferred from habitation to ruin.' He said to him, 'So how do you see our arrival before Allah?' He said, 'As for the good-doer among you, he is like the absent one arriving at his family, and as for the bad-doer among you, he is like the runaway slave being returned to his master.' He said, 'So how do you see our state with Allah?' He said, 'Present your deeds to the Book. Indeed, Allah says: Surely the righteous are in bliss, and surely the wicked are in hellfire.' The man said, 'So where is the mercy of Allah?' He said, 'The mercy of Allah is near to the good-doers.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And a man wrote to Abu Zarr, may Allah be pleased with him, saying, The man said to him, 'And have you seen anyone who does wrong to the one he loves?' He said to him, 'Yes, your own soul is the most beloved of souls to you. So when you disobey Allah, you have done wrong to it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Be patient upon the obedience of Allah and observe patience from the disobedience of Allah, for indeed the world is but a moment. So what has passed, you will find neither joy for it nor grief, and what has not yet come, you do not know it. Therefore, be patient upon that moment in which you are, so it would be as if you have been glad tidings for you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Khizr (peace be upon him) said to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! The best of your days is the one that is in front of you, so see which day it is and prepare your answer for it, for you will be paused and questioned. Take your lesson from time, for time is long yet short. So work as if you can see the reward of your deed, so that it may make you more hopeful for the Hereafter, for whatever is coming from the world is like what has already passed from it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the quickest in reward for goodness is righteousness (al-birr), and indeed, the quickest in punishment for evil is transgression (al-baghy). And it suffices as a fault for a person that he sees in others what he is blind to in himself, or he reproaches people for what he himself cannot leave, or he harms his companion with what is not concerning him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It suffices as a fault for a person that he sees in people what he is blind to regarding his own self, and that he harms his companion with that which is meaningless.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj and Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the quickest reward for goodness is righteousness, and the quickest punishment for evil is transgression; and it suffices for a person as a fault that he looks into the faults of others while he is blind to the fault of his own self, or he hurts his companion with that which is meaningless to him, or he forbids people from that which he himself is not able to leave.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, some people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) after they had embraced Islam, and they said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Will a man from us be held accountable for what he did during the period of Ignorance after his Islam?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'The one whose Islam is good and the certainty of his faith is sound, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not hold him accountable for what he did during the period of Ignorance; and the one whose Islam is shallow and the certainty of his faith is not sound, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will hold him accountable for the former and the latter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Al-Minqari, from Fuzayl ibn Ayaz, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who is good during Islam, would he be seized for what he had done during the pre-Islamic period? So he (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who is good during Islam would not be seized for what he had done during the pre-Islamic period; but the one who is evil during Islam would be seized for the former and the latter.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub and others, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are 'Protected ones' whom He shields from affliction; so He gives them life in well-being, sustains them in well-being, causes them to die in well-being, resurrects them in well-being, and settles them in Paradise in well-being.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a people, protecting them from affliction. He created them in well-being, gave them life in well-being, caused them to die in well-being, and entered them to die in well-being, and admitted them into Paradise in well-being.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are 'Protected Ones' from His creation, whom He nourishes with His bounties, endows with His health, and admits to Paradise through His mercy. Afflictions and trials pass over them but do not harm them in the slightest.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Abu Dawud al-Mustariq who said, 'Amr ibn Marwan narrated to me saying, I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying' Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four characteristics have been raised (exempted) from my community: their mistakes, their forgetfulness, and what they were compelled to do, and what they could not endure.' And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Our Lord! Do not seize us if we forget or make a mistake; Our Lord! And do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us; Our Lord! And do not impose upon us that which we have no strength to bear.' And His Word: 'Except the one who is compelled while his heart is at rest with faith.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Nine characteristics have been dropped from my community: the mistake, and forgetfulness, and what they do not know, and what they cannot endure, and what they were compelled to, and what they were forced upon, and the evil omen, and the whispering in contemplation of the creation, and envy, provided it is not manifested by the tongue or the hand.'

From him, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (some) of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Musa (peace be upon him) said to Al-Khizr (peace be upon him): 'I have been sanctified by your company, so advise me.' He said to him: 'Adhere to that which, along with it, nothing will harm you, just as nothing will benefit you along with that which is other than it.'

From him, from Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Umayyah Yusuf ibn Thabit, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A deed does not harm along with faith, and a deed does not benefit along with disbelief.' Do you not see that He said: 'And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger, and they died while they were disbelievers.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah, from Abu Umayyah Yusuf ibn Thabit ibn Abu Sa'dah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Faith (Iman) is such that no deed harms it, and similarly, Disbelief (Kufr) is such that no deed benefits it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from the one who mentioned it, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Marid, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A hadith has been reported to us that you said: When you recognize (the Wilayah), then do what you will.' He said, 'I have said that.' I said, 'And even if they commit adultery, or steal, or drink wine?' He said to me, 'We are to Allah and to Him we shall return. By Allah, they have not done us justice by saying that we would be seized by the deed while it is dropped from them. I only said: When you recognize (the Wilayah), then do what you will, from little good and much, for it will be accepted from you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It was so that Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) was frequently saying in his sermons: 'O you people! Your Religion is your Religion, So the evil deed in it is better than the good deed in other (Religions), and the evil deed in it would be Forgiven, and the good deed in the other (Religions) would not be Accepted'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Musa from Ahmad ibn Umar from Yahya ibn Aban from Shihab said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If the people knew how Allah, Blessed and High, created this creation, no one would blame another.' So I said, 'May Allah keep you well! How is that?' He said?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, created parts reaching forty-nine parts. Then He made the parts into tenths, thus making the part ten tenths. Then He distributed it among the creation.' So He placed in one man a tenth of a part, and in another two-tenths of a part, until reaching a complete part; and in another a part and a tenth of a part, and another a part and two-tenths of a part, and another a part and three-tenths of a part, until reaching two complete parts. Then by that calculation, until reaching with the highest of them forty-nine parts. So the one in whom there is only a tenth of a part cannot be like the owner of the two-tenths; and similarly, the owner of the two-tenths cannot be like the owner of the three-tenths; and similarly, the one for whom a part is complete cannot be like the owner of the two parts. And if the people knew that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created this creation upon this, no one would blame another.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Muhammad, son of Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Al-Hasan, son of Ali, son of Abu Uthman, from Muhammad, son of Uthman, from Muhammad, son of Hammad Al-Khazzaz, from Abdul Aziz Al-Qarataysi, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abdul Aziz! Faith (Iman) consists of ten levels, like a ladder, from which one ascends step by step. So let not the one on the second step say to the one on the first, “You are not upon anything,” until he reaches the tenth. So do not dismiss the one who is below you, lest the one who is above you dismiss you. And when you see someone who is lower than you by a level, raise him to you with gentleness, and do not burden him with what he cannot endure, lest you break him. For whoever breaks a believer, upon him is its repair (or consequence).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sadeyr, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The believers are upon levels; some are upon one, some upon two, some upon three, some upon four, some upon five, some upon six, and some upon seven. So if you were to burden two upon the owner of the one, he would not be strong enough (for it); and three upon the owner of the two, he would not be strong enough; and four upon the owner of the three, he would not be strong enough; and five upon the owner of the four, he would not be strong enough; and six upon the owner of the five, he would not be strong enough; and seven upon the owner of the six, he would not be strong enough. And these are the levels.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Subah ibn Sayyaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: What are you and the disavowal? Some of you disavow others. Indeed, the believers, some of them are superior to some, and some of them are more frequent in prayer than some, and some of them have keener insight than some, and these are the ranks.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of our companions, raising it, said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I shall ascribe Islam with an ascription that none before me has ascribed, and none after me will ascribe except with the like of it. Indeed, Islam is submission, and submission is conviction, and conviction is ratification, and ratification is acknowledgement, and acknowledgement is deed, and deed is performance.' Indeed, the believer does not take his religion from his own opinion, but it comes to him from his Lord, so he takes it. Indeed, the believer's conviction is seen in his deed, and the disbeliever's denial is seen in his deed. So, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they did not recognize their matter. Therefore, take lesson from the denial of the disbelievers and the hypocrites in their evil deeds.

From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Mudrik ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Islam is bare, so clothe it with bashfulness (hayā'), and adorn it with dignity (waqār), and its manliness is righteous deed (al-'amal al-ṣāliḥ), and its pillar is piety (al-wara'), and for every thing is a foundation, and the foundation of Islam is our love, the People of the Household.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Mudrik ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather, may the prayers of Allah be upon them, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah created Islam, so He made for it a space/land, and He made for it a light, and He made for it a fortress, and He made for it a helper.' So as for its space/land, it is the Quran; and as for its light, it is Wisdom; and as for its fortress, it is the Good (al-Ma'ruf); and as for its helpers, it is I, and my People of the Household, and our Shia. So love my People of the Household and their Shia and their helpers. For when I was ascended to the lowest heaven, Jibril (peace be upon him) introduced me to the inhabitants of the heaven. Allah entrusted the love of me, and the love of my People of the Household and their Shia, into the hearts of the angels, so it is a deposit with them until the Day of Resurrection. Then he brought me down to the people of the earth and introduced me to the people of the earth. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, entrusted the love of me, and the love of my People of the Household and their Shia, into the hearts of the believers of my community. Thus, the believers of my community preserve my deposit regarding my People of the Household until the Day of Resurrection. So, if a man from my community were to worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for his lifetime, the days of the world, then he meets Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as hating my People of the Household and my Shia, Allah will not open his chest for anything except for Hypocrisy.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abdul Malik ibn Ghalib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is befitting for the believer to have eight characteristics: dignity during disturbances, patience during afflictions, gratitude during prosperity, contentment with what Allah has granted him, not being unjust to enemies, not being a burden to friends, his body should be tired from it (hard work) while people are at rest from him. Knowledge is the friend of the believer, forbearance is his vizier, intellect is the commander of his army, kindness is his brother, and righteousness is his father.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Faith has four pillars: reliance upon Allah, delegating the matter to Allah, contentment with the decree of Allah, and submission to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
