A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: You will not be righteous until you recognize, and you will not recognize until you ratify, and you will not ratify until you submit to the four doors; the first of them is not correct except by the last one. The companions of the three strayed and wandered with a far wandering. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, accepts only the righteous deed, and Allah accepts not except with fulfillment of the conditions and covenants. And whoever fulfills Allah's conditions and completes what is described in His covenant, attains what is with Him, and He completes His promise. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed the servants of the way of guidance and established for them the minarets therein, and informed them how to travel, so He said: 'And I am Forgiving to him who repents and believes and does righteous deeds, then follows the right Guidance.' And He said: 'Indeed, Allah accepts only from the pious.' So whoever fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in what He commanded, will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as a believer in what Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) brought. Far be it! Far be it! A people have perished and died before they were guided, and they thought that they were believing, and they associated (partners) from where they did not know. Indeed, whoever comes to the houses from their doors is guided, and whoever takes in other than them travels upon the road of perdition. Allah linked the obedience of the Guardian of His command with the obedience of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and the obedience of His Messenger with obedience to him. So whoever neglects the obedience of the Masters of Command, neither obeyed Allah nor His Messenger, and this is the acknowledgement of what was revealed from the presence of Allah. Take your adornment at every Masjid. And seek the houses which Allah has allowed to be exalted and that His Name may be mentioned in them. For He has informed you that they are men whom neither merchandise nor selling diverts from the Remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the keeping up of Salat and the giving of Zakat; they fear a Day in which the hearts and eyes shall be overt

From him, from his father, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, from his father (peace be upon them), who said: A group of people were presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during one of his military expeditions, so he said: 'Who are these people?' They said: 'Believers, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'And what has reached of your faith?' They said: 'Patience during affliction, and gratitude during prosperity, and contentment with the divine decree.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Forbearing, knowledgeable. They are so close to the Prophets through their jurisprudence that if you are as you describe yourselves, do not build what you will not dwell in, and do not amass what you will not consume, and fear Allah, to whom you will be returned.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O brother of Jau'f! Indeed, faith (Iman) is superior to submission (Islam), and indeed conviction (Yaqeen) is superior to faith, and there is nothing more precious than conviction.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'b, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah preferred Al-Iman over Al-Islam by a degree, just as He preferred the Ka'bah over Al-Masjid Al-Haram.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, or someone else, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abdul Hamid al-Wasiti, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad, Islam is a level.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'And faith is a level over Islam.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'And piety is a level over faith.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'And conviction is a level over piety.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'So people have not been given anything less than conviction, and you are merely holding onto the lowest level of Islam. Beware lest it slip from your hands.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the faith and the Islam. So he (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather it is the Islam, and the faith is above it by a level, and the piety is above the faith by a level, and the conviction is above the piety by a level; and there has not been distributed among the people anything scarcer than the conviction.' He said, I said, 'So which thing is the conviction?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The reliance upon Allah, and the submission to Allah, and the pleasure with the decree of Allah, and the delegation to Allah.' I said, 'So what is the interpretation of that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is how Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Iman is above Islam by a degree, and Taqwa is above Iman by a degree, and Al-Yaqeen is above Taqwa by a degree, and nothing has been distributed among the servants that is less [scarcely given] than Al-Yaqeen.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on one of his journeys, he met a group of riders. They said, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Who are you?' They said, 'We are believers, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'So what is the reality of your faith?' They said, 'Contentment with the decree of Allah, delegation to Allah, and submission to the command of Allah.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Scholars, wise ones, who almost could be from the wisdom of the Prophets. If you are truthful, do not build what you will not dwell in, and do not amass what you will not consume, and fear Allah, to Whom you will be returning.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi and Ibrahim ibn Mihran, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) led the people in the morning prayer, so he looked at a youth in the mosque; he was trembling and bowing his head, his complexion was yellowish, his body had become thin, and his eyes were sunken in his head. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'How is your morning, O so-and-so?' He said: 'I woke in the morning, O Messenger of Allah, with conviction (yaqeen).' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was astonished by his words and said: 'Indeed, for every conviction there is a reality; so what is the reality of your conviction?' He said: 'My conviction, O Messenger of Allah, is that which grieved me, kept me awake at night, and made my throat thirsty. My soul turned away from the world and what is in it, to the extent that it is as if I am looking at the Throne of my Lord, and the Reckoning has been established, and the creatures have been gathered for that, and I am among them.' And it is as if I am looking at the people of Paradise, enjoying themselves in Paradise, getting to know one another, and reclining on raised couches; and it is as if I am looking at the people of Hell, and they are being punished in it, shrieking. And it is as if I am now hearing the sighing of the Fire circulating in my ears. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: 'This is a servant whose heart Allah has illuminated with faith.' Then he said to him: 'Stick to what you are upon.' The youth said: 'Supplicate to Allah for me, O Messenger of Allah, that I may be granted martyrship with you.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated for him, and it was not long before he went out in one of the military expeditions of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he was martyred after nine men, and he was the tenth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon every truth (haqq) there is a reality (haqiqa), and upon every correct deed there is a light (nur).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrouq, from Yazeed ibn Ishaq Shairin, from Al-Husayn ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The noble character traits are ten. So if you have the capacity for them to be in you, let them be, for they may be in a man and not in his son, and in the son and not in his father, and in the slave and not in the free man. It was said, 'And what are they?' He said: 'Truthfulness in bravery, truthfulness of the tongue, fulfilling the trust, maintaining kinship, honoring the guest, feeding the beggar, repaying good deeds, being considerate to the neighbor, being considerate to the companion, and the head of them all is bashfulness (modesty).'

From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi, from Ismail ibn Abbad, who said, 'Bakr said, and I think I heard it from Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:' 'We love the one who is intellectual, understanding, scholarly, forbearing, kind, patient, truthful, and loyal. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has specialized the Prophets with the noble mannerisms. So whoever has them, let him praise Allah for that, and whoever does not have them, let him beseech Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him for them.' He said, 'I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what are these?' He said: 'These are piety, contentment, patience, gratitude, forbearance, bashfulness, generosity, bravery, self-esteem, goodwill, truthfulness of speech, and fulfillment of trust.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, chose Islam as a religion for you, so improve your companionship with it through generosity and good character.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man from the Banu Hashim, who said: Four (qualities): whoever possesses them, his Islam will be perfected; and even if he had sins from his head to his feet, truthfulness, bashfulness (modesty), good character, and gratitude would not diminish (his faith/status).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Riab, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I inform you of the best of your men?' We said, 'Yes, O Rasool-Allah!' He said: 'Indeed, among the best of your men is the pious, the pure, the generous in hand, pure in the two sides (mouth and backside), the righteous to his parents, and he does not burden his dependents on others.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud al-Ijli, from Zurara, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When God, Blessed and Exalted, created the creation, He created sweet water and salty bitter water. The two waters blended; then He took clay from the surface of the earth and kneaded it with an intense kneading. He then said to the companions of the right — who were like crawling particles — [proceed] to Paradise in peace; and said to the companions of the left: to the Fire, and I care not. Then He said [7:172]: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes, we testify' — lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: We were heedless of this. Then He took the covenant upon the Prophets, saying: Am I not your Lord? And that this is Muhammad, My messenger, and that this is Ali, the Commander of the Faithful? They said: Yes! So prophethood was confirmed for them. And He took the covenant upon the Determined Ones (Ulu al-'Azm): I am your Lord, and Muhammad is My messenger, and Ali is the Commander of the Faithful, and his successors after him are the guardians of My command and treasurers of My knowledge — peace be upon them — and that through al-Mahdi I shall grant victory to My religion, and through him I shall manifest My governance, and through him I shall exact revenge from My enemies, and through him I shall be worshipped willingly and unwillingly. They said: We acknowledge, O Lord, and we testify. And Adam neither denied nor acknowledged. Thus the determination was confirmed for these five regarding al-Mahdi, and Adam did not become one of the Determined Ones in acknowledging him — and this is His word, Mighty and Majestic [20:115]: And We had given a covenant to Adam before, but he forgot; and We found no firm resolve in him. He [the Imam] said: Rather, he [Adam] was left out. Then He commanded a fire and it was kindled. He said to the companions of the left: Enter into it; but they feared it. And He said to the companions of the right: Enter into it; so they entered it and it was cold and safe upon them. Then the companions of the left said: O Lord, forgive us! He said: I forgive you — go and enter. But they feared it. Thus, obedience, wilayah, and disobedience became established.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He extracted the offspring of Adam (peace be upon him) from his back in order to take the covenant upon them regarding His Lordship and prophethood for every prophet, the first one for whom He took the covenant upon them — regarding his prophethood — was Muhammad ibn Abdullah (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Adam: 'Look! What do you see?' He said: So Adam (peace be upon him) looked at his offspring, and they were tiny particles that had filled the sky. Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord! How abundant are my offspring! And for what purpose did You create them? So what do You want from them by taking the covenant upon them?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'That they worship Me, not associating anything with Me, and believe in My messengers and follow them.' Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord! Why do I see some of the particles greater than others, some of them have much light, some of them have little light, and some of them have no light?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Thus have I created them, in order to test them in all their states.' Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord! Will You permit me to speak?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Speak, for your spirit is from My Spirit, but your nature is contrary to My Being.' Adam said: 'O Lord! If only You had created them upon one likeness, one measure, one nature, one constitution, one colour, one lifespan, and equal sustenance — then some of them would not oppress others, and there would be no envy, hatred, or disagreement among them regarding anything.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O Adam! By My Spirit you spoke, but by the weakness of your nature you ventured into what you have no knowledge of. I am the Creator, the All-Knowing. By My knowledge I have differentiated in their creation, and by My will My command runs among them, and to My management and My ordainment they are coming. There is no alteration in My creation. Indeed, I created the jinn and mankind only that they worship Me. And I created Paradise for those among them who obey Me, worship Me, and follow My messengers

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi and Uqba, both together, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation. So He created those whom He loved from what He loved, and what He loved was that He created it from the clay of Paradise; and He created those whom He hated from what He hated, and what He hated was that He created it from the clay of the Fire. Then He sent them into the shadows. So I asked: 'And what are the shadows?' He said: 'Have you not seen your shadow in the sun — it is something, yet it is not a thing?' Then He sent Prophets from among them, and they invited them to the acknowledgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic — and that is His word, Mighty and Majestic: "And if you ask them who created them, they would certainly say: Allah." [43:87] Then they invited them to the acknowledgment of the Prophets; some acknowledged and some denied. Then they invited them to our Wilayah, and, by God, the one who loved acknowledged it, and the one who hated denied it. And that is His word: "But they were not going to believe in what they had belied before." [10:74] Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The denial was there (at that time).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from one of the elders of the Banu al-Najashiyy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The head (chief) of obedience to Allah is patience and satisfaction with Allah regarding what the servant loves or dislikes; and a servant will not be satisfied with Allah regarding what he loves or dislikes, except that it is better for him regarding what He loves or dislikes.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Lays al-Muradi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The most knowledgeable of the people with Allah is the one most satisfied with the Judgement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

From him, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Patience and satisfaction from Allah are the head of the obedience of Allah, and whoever is patient and satisfied from Allah regarding what He has decreed for him, whether he loves it or dislikes it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will decree for him regarding what he loves or dislikes, except what is better for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Among My believing servants are servants whose affairs of their religion cannot be rectified for them except through wealth, abundance, and health in the body. So I test them with wealth, abundance, and health of the body, so that I may rectify their religious affairs for them.' And among My believing servants are servants whose affairs of their religion cannot be rectified for them except through poverty, destitution, and sickness in their bodies. So I test them with poverty, destitution, and sickness, so that I may rectify their religious affairs for them. And I am the One Who knows best what rectifies the religious affairs of My believing servants. And among My believing servants is one who strives in My worship, rising from his sleep and the pleasure of his pillow, staying awake for Me through the nights, thus tiring himself in My worship. So I strike him with drowsiness for the night and the two nights, as a consideration from Me to him and a preservation for him, so he sleeps until morning. Then he rises, and he is disgusted with himself, fretting over it. And if I were to leave him alone to do what he intends from My worship, self-conceit would enter him because of that. So self-conceit would lead him to trial through his deeds, and there would come to him from that that which causes his destruction due to his conceit in his deeds and his satisfaction with himself, until he thinks that he has surpassed the worshippers and exceeded the limit of deficiency in his worship. Thus, he becomes distant from Me at that time, while he thinks he is drawing near to Me. So let the workers not rely upon their deeds which they perform for My reward. For if they strive and tire themselves and spend their lives in My worship, they would be deficient, not reaching the full measure of their worship in what they seek from Me of My generosity, the bliss in My Paradise, and the high ranks in My vicinity. But (they attain it) by My Mercy. So let them have trust in My grace, let them rejoice, and let them be assured in their good opinion of Me. For My Mercy will overtake them at that time, and from Me, My Pleasure will reac

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the one who minds about Allah that he does not consider Him as being slow regarding his sustenance, nor accuse Him regarding His Judgement.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Amr ibn Nuhayk, the seller of the Harawis, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O My believing servant, I do not turn away anything from you except that I make it better for you. So let him be pleased with My decree, and let him be patient with My trials, and let him be grateful for My bounties. I shall write him, O Muhammad, as one of the truthful (siddiqun) in My presence.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Malik ibn Atiyya from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that in... what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'O Musa ibn Imran! I have not created a creature more beloved to Me than My believing servant. Indeed, I test him for what is better for him, and I grant him health for what is better for him, and I turn away from him what is evil for him for what is better for him, and I am more Knowing of what suits My servant. So let him be patient with My afflictions, and let him be grateful for My bounties, and let him be pleased with My judgement. I shall record him among the truthful ones in My Presence when he acts by My pleasure and obeys My command.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The most rightful of Allah's creatures to submit to what Allah has decreed is the one who knows Allah, and the one who is satisfied with the Decree; the Decree comes upon him, and Allah magnifies his reward. And the one who is displeased with the Decree, the Decree passes over him, and Allah nullifies his reward.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid, from his father, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said to me: 'Asceticism (al-zuhd) has ten parts. The highest degree of asceticism is the lowest degree of piety (al-wara'), and the highest degree of piety is the lowest degree of conviction (al-yaqin), and the highest degree of conviction is the lowest degree of satisfaction (al-rida).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) met Abdullah ibn Ja'far, so he said: 'O Abdullah! How can the believer be a believer while he is angry at his portion (divine decree) and belittles his status, with Allah being the Ruler over him? And I am the guarantor that whoever does not have in his heart except satisfaction, that if he supplicates to Allah, He will answer him.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'By what sign is the believer known to be a believer?' He said, 'By submission to Allah and contentment with whatever befalls him, whether joy or anger.'

From him from his father from Ibn Sinan from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It did not happen that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying for something which had transpired: 'If only something else would have happened'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'No servant from My servants would hold on to Me besides anyone from My creatures, recognizing that from his intention, then the skies and the earth and those in them would plot against him, except that I would make an exit for him from between them; and no servant from My servants would hold on to any one from My creatures, recognizing that from his intention, except that I would cut off the causes of the skies and the earth from his hands, and I would harden the earth from beneath him, and I would not care in which valley he perishes.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hafs Al-A'sha, from Amr [Umar] ibn Khalid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: I went out until I reached this wall and leaned against it, and behold, there was a man wearing two white garments looking at my face. Then he said, 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn, why do I see you as gloomy and sad? Is it over the world? For the sustenance of Allah is present for the righteous and the immoral.' I said, 'I do not grieve over this, and it is as you say.' He said, 'So is it over the Hereafter? For the promise of Allah is true, and a Dominant King [or he said: All-Powerful] will judge in it.' I said, 'I do not grieve over this, and it is as you say.' He said, 'From what is your grief?' I said, 'From what we fear from the strife of Ibn al-Zubayr and what the people are enduring in it.' He laughed, then said, 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you seen anyone who supplicated to Allah but He did not answer him?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Have you seen anyone who relied upon Allah but He did not suffice him?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Have you seen anyone who asked Allah but He did not give him?' I said, 'No.' Then he disappeared from me.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, richness and splendour wander around. When they acquire a place of reliance (on God), they settle. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Hassan — similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from someone else, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, from Ali ibn Suweyd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him.' So he said: 'Reliance upon Allah has levels. Among them is that you rely upon Allah in all your matters. So whatever He does with you, you should be satisfied with Him. You should know that He does not withhold any goodness and grace from you, and you should know that the decision regarding that is for Him. Therefore, rely upon Allah by delegating that to Him, and trust in Him regarding it, and in other such matters.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He who is given three things is not denied three things: He who is given supplication (du'a) is given the answer (ijabah); and he who is given gratitude (shukr) is given increase (ziyadah); and he who is given reliance (tawakkul) is given sufficiency (kifayah). Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Did you recite the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. And He said: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor].' And He said: 'Call upon Me, I will answer you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from one of our companions, from Abbad ibn Yaqoub al-Rawajini, from Saeed ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I was with Musa ibn Abd Allah in Yanbu, and my travel expenses had run out during one of the journeys. So one of the sons of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Who do you hope for (to intercede) for what has befallen you?' I said, 'Musa ibn Abd Allah.' He said, 'Then your need will not be fulfilled, and your seeking will not be accomplished.' I said, 'And why is that?' He said, 'Because I have found in some of the books of my forefathers (peace be upon him) that Allah (Exalted and Majestic) says...' and he mentioned something similar. I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)! Dictate it to me.' So he dictated it to me. I said, 'No, by Allah! I will not ask him for a need after it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughirah or his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What was in the bequest of Luqman?' He said, 'It contained marvels, and the most impressive of what was in it was that he said to his son: Fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a fear that if you came to Him with the righteous deeds of the two masses (humans and jinn), He would punish you; and hope to Allah with a hope that if you came to Him with the sins of the two masses, He would have mercy on you.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'My father used to say: There is no believing servant but that in his heart are two lights: a light of fear and a light of hope. If this one were weighed, it would not exceed this one, and if this one were weighed, it would not exceed this one.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Is'haq! Fear Allah as if you can see Him, and even although you are not seeing Him, indeed He sees you. So if you think that He does not see you, then you have disbelieved; and if you know that He sees you and you present yourself to Him with disobedience, then you have made Him from the least significant of the observers upon you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, who said: 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:' The one who fears Allah, Allah makes everything fear him; and the one who does not fear Allah, Allah makes him fear from every thing.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Hamza ibn Abdillah al-Ja'fari, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recognizes Allah fears Allah, and the one who fears Allah, his soul becomes indifferent to the world.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A group of people act in disobedience and say, 'We hope,' and they remain in that state until death comes to them. He said: These are a people who sway in their expectations (of mercy); they are lying. They are not truly hoping. Indeed, whoever hopes for something seeks it, and whoever fears something flees from it.
And it is reported by Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, he raised it, saying: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A group of people from your mawali commit minor sins and say,

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Salih ibn Hamza, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'From the worship is the intense fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' It is only those of His servants who have knowledge who fear Allah Therefore fear not the people and fear Me And whoever is fearful of Allah, He will make for him an outlet He said, 'And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Love for fame and to be mentioned (popularity/dominance) will not exist in the heart of the one who is fearful (of Allah).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'From the preserved sermons of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is that he said: O people! For you there are markers/landmarks, so reach your markers, and for you there is an end/limit, so reach your end. Indeed, the Believer acts between two fears: between a term that has passed, not knowing what Allah will do with it, and between a term that remains, not knowing what Allah has decreed regarding it.' So let the believing servant take from his self for his self, and from his world for his Hereafter, and in his youth before old age, and in his life before death. And by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, there is no 'time for deeds' (musta'tab) after the world, and there is no abode after it except Paradise or Hellfire.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Mukan, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Sara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: A believer will not be a true believer until he is fearful and hopeful; and he will not be fearful and hopeful until he acts for what he fears and hopes for.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Fuzayl ibn Uthman, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The believer is between two fears: a sin that has passed, not knowing what Allah has done with it, and a lifespan that remains, not knowing what he will acquire from destruction during it. Thus, he does not wake up except as fearful, and nothing corrects him except fear.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) was saying: 'There is no believing servant except that in his heart are two lights: a light of fear and a light of hope. If this were weighed, it would not exceed this, and if this were weighed, it would not exceed this.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawud ibn Kathir, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Blessed and High, said: 'Let the workers not rely upon their deeds which they perform for My reward, for if they were to strive and exhaust themselves in their lifetimes in My worship, they would be deficient, not reaching the essence of My worship regarding what they seek from Me of My benevolence and the bounties in My Gardens and the high ranks in My vicinity, but (they should rely) on My Mercy. So let them trust in My Grace, let them hope, and let them be secure in their good opinion of Me, for My Mercy will encompass them, and My Pleasure will reach them from Me, and My Forgiveness will clothe them in My Pardon, for I am Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and with that I am Named.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Bureid ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, while he was upon his pulpit: By the One, there is no god except Him, a believer is never given the good of this world and the Hereafter except by the goodness of his hope/thoughts in Allah, and his hopefulness to Him, and the goodness of his character, and the restraint from backbiting the believers. By the One, there is no god except Him, Allah does not punish a believer after repentance and seeking forgiveness except by the evil of his hope/thoughts in Allah, and his deficiency in his hopefulness, and the evil of his character, and his backbiting of the believers. By the One, there is no god except Him, the hope/thought of a believing servant in Allah will not be good unless Allah is according to the hope/thought of His believing servant, because Allah is Generous. In His Hand are the good things. He is bashful that His believing servant should have good thoughts about Him, then He should disappoint his thought and his hope. So have good thoughts about Allah, and yearn towards Him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said: Have good thoughts about Allah, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am according to the thought of My believing servant regarding Me; if [it is] good, then [it is] good, and if [it is] evil, then [it is] evil.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of the Iraqis, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Hadrami, from his father, from Uthman ibn Zayd, from Jabir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Jabir! May Allah not remove you from the shortfall nor the deficiency.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man from the Children of Israel worshipped Allah for forty years. Then he offered an offering, but it was not accepted from him. So he said to himself, "It has not come to you except from yourself, and there is no sin except for you." He said: "So Allah, Blessed and High, revealed unto him: Your condemning yourself is superior to your worship for forty years."'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Isa ibn Ayoub from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: 'Frequently say: O Allah, do not make me among those who borrow (the religion temporarily), and do not remove me from deficiency.' I said, 'As for the temporary ones, I know that a man borrows the religion then exits from it. So what is the meaning of "do not remove me from deficiency"?' He said: 'For every deed you do for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, be deficient in your own estimation, for all people are deficient in their deeds between themselves and Allah, except for whom Allah preserves.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad the brother of Uram, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Do not let the doctrines go with you, for by Allah, our Shia is not except for the one who obeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) addressed the people during the Farewell Pilgrimage, so he said: 'O people! By Allah, there is nothing that brings you closer to Paradise and distances you from the Fire except that I have ordered you with it; and there is nothing that brings you closer to the Fire and distances you from Paradise except that I have forbidden you from it.' Indeed, the Trustworthy Spirit (Gabriel) breathed into my spirit that no soul shall die until it has completed its sustenance. Therefore, fear Allah and be diligent in seeking (livelihood), and let not the delay of anything from the sustenance cause one of you to seek it through what is not permissible, for what is with Allah is not attained except through obedience to Him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, and Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, altogether from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'O Jabir! Is it sufficient for the one who claims Shia-ism that he says he loves us, the People of the Household? By Allah, our Shia are only those who fear Allah and obey Him. And they, O Jabir, were not recognized except by humility, reverence, trustworthiness, frequent remembrance of Allah, fasting, prayer, righteousness towards parents, attending to the poor, the destitute, the indebted, and the orphans, truthfulness in speech, recitation of the Quran, restraining their tongues from people except for good, and being trusted by their clans in matters.' Jabir said: 'So I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We do not recognize anyone today with this description.' He said: 'O Jabir! Do not let the sects carry you away. It is enough for a man to say, 'I love Ali and follow his Wilayah,' yet not be a doer of that. If he were to say, 'I love the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family),' and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is better than Ali (peace be upon him), yet he does not follow his way and does not act by his Sunnah, his love for him would not benefit him at all.' So fear Allah and work for what is with Allah. There is no kinship between Allah and anyone. The most beloved of servants to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the most honored by Him, is the most pious of them and the most active in His obedience. O Jabir! By Allah, one does not draw near to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, except through obedience. And we do not have exemption from the Fire, nor is there a proof for anyone against Allah. Whoever is obedient to Allah is a friend to us, and whoever is disobedient to Allah is an enemy to us. And our Wilayah is not attained except through deeds and piety.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibnarrated from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When it is the Day of Resurrection, a neck (group) of the people will stand and come to the Door of Paradise and knock it. So it will be said to them, 'Who are you?' They will say, 'We are the people of patience.' It will be said to them, 'Upon what were you patient?' They will say, 'We were patient in obeying Allah and we were patient in refraining from disobeying Allah.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'They are speaking the truth. Admit them into Paradise.' Only those will be given their reward in full without reckoning, who are patient.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Fuzayl ibn Usman, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was saying: 'A deed is not belittled when accompanied by piety, and how can one belittle what is accepted?'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: O group of the Shia, the Shia of the Progeny of Muhammad! Be the 'Numruqah al-Wusta' (the central/intermediate group). The exaggerator (Al-Ghali) will return to you, and the follower (Al-Tali) will join you. A man from the Ansar, called Sa'd, said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what is the exaggerator?' He said, 'A people who say about us what we do not say about ourselves. So those are not from us, and we are not from them.' He said, 'So what is the follower?' He said, 'The scout who seeks goodness; goodness reaches him, and he is rewarded for it.' Then he turned to us and said, 'By Allah, there is no exemption (from accountability) with us from Allah, nor is there between us and Allah a kinship (that grants automatic favor), nor is there an argument for us against Allah, nor do we draw near to Allah except through obedience. So whoever among you is obedient to Allah, our Wilayah will benefit him; and whoever among you is disobedient to Allah, our Wilayah will not benefit him. Woe to you! Do not be deceived. Woe to you! Do not be deceived.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mufaddal ibn Umar,al ibn Umar, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and we mentioned the deeds. So I said, 'How weak are my deeds.' He said, 'Hush! Seek forgiveness of Allah.' Then he said to me, 'Indeed, a little deed with piety is better than a lot of deeds without piety.' I said, 'How can there be a lot without piety?' He said, 'Yes, like the man who feeds his food, is kind to his neighbors, and eases his burden (for others). So when the door of the prohibited is raised for him, he enters into it. So this is the deed without piety. And the other one may be such that he does not have much, but when the door of the prohibited is raised for him, he does not enter into it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Abu Dawud al-Mustariq from Muhassin al-Maysami from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not transfer a servant from the disgrace of disobedience to the honor of piety except that He enriches him without wealth, and honors him without a clan, and gives him companionship without a friend without another person.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu al-Maghra', from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Sa'id ibn Hilal al-Thaqafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I do not meet you except after years, so inform me of something I can adhere to.' He said, 'I advise you with the fear of God (taqwa), and devoutness (war'), and striving (ijtihad), and know that striving is not beneficial if there is no devoutness in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fear Allah and maintain your Religion with devoutness (al-wara').'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) advised us, commanded [good], and encouraged asceticism. Then he said: 'Upon you is devoutness (al-wara'), for whatever is with Allah cannot be attained except through devoutness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Striving (ijtihad) would not benefit if there is no devoutness (war') in it.

From him, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The most difficult of the worship is the devoutness (war').'

Hanan ibn Sadeer from Abu Sara al-Ghazzal from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Allah Mighty and Majestic Said: 'Son of Adam! Keep away from what I prohibited upon you, and you will be among the most devout of the people.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the devoutness (war') among the people, so he said: 'That which refrains from the prohibitions of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Asama, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Adhere to God-consciousness, piety, striving, truthful narration, fulfilling the trust, good character, and good neighborliness. Be callers to yourselves without your tongues, be an adornment and do not be a shame. And adhere to the prolongation of bowing and prostration, for indeed when one of you prolongs his bowing and prostration, Iblis cries out from behind him and says, 'Woe to me! He obeyed and I disobeyed; he prostrated and I refused.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Zayd, from his father who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Isa ibn Abdullah al-Qummi entered. He welcomed him and brought him near to his seat. Then he said: 'O Isa ibn Abdullah! He is not from us, and there is no prestige for the one who was in a city wherein were one hundred thousand or more, and in that city there was one who was more devout than him.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Amr ibn Saeed ibn Hilal who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Advise me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I advise you with the fear of Allah, and devoutness (war'), and striving (ijtihad), and know that striving would not benefit if there is no devoutness in it.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Assist us with devoutness (al-wara'), for whoever among you meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with devoutness, there will be for him a relief (faraj) with Allah. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Those who obey Allah and the Messenger are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets and the truthful and the martyrs and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.' Thus, from us (the Ahl al-Bayt) is the Prophet, and from us is the truthful, and the martyrs, and the righteous.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We do not count a man as a believer until he is obedient to and desirous of all our affairs. Indeed, among the obedience to our affairs and desiring it is piety (war'). So adorn yourselves with it, may Allah have mercy on you, and inflict hardship on our enemies with it, may Allah invigorate you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Al-'Ala', from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Be callers to the people without your tongues, so that they may see from you piety, striving, prayer, and goodness, for that is a call.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah al-Alawi, who said: 'Ubayyidullah ibn Ali informed me, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I frequently heard my father saying: 'He is not from our Shia, the one whose devoutness is not talked about by the women in their coverings; and he is not from our friends, the one who is in a town wherein are ten thousand men, among them is a creature of Allah who is more devout than him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah was not worshipped with anything more superior than chastity of the belly and the private part.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The most superior worship is the chastity of the belly and the private part'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The most superior of worship is chastity.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said: A man said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I am weak in deeds and few in fasting, but I hope that I do not eat except what is permissible.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Which striving is superior to chastity of the belly and the private part?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The two hollows by which most of my community will enter the Fire are the belly and the private part.'

And by his chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Three (things) I fear for my community after me: straying after recognition, and the deceptions of trials/strife, and the lustful desires of the belly and the private part.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from one of his companions, from Maymun al-Qaddah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no worship more superior than the chastity of the belly and the private part.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no worship more superior in the Presence of Allah than the chastity of the belly and the private part.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic And for the one who fears to stand before his Lord would have two Gardens He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who knows that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sees him and hears what he says and does, whether from goodness or evil, so that would deter him from the ugly of deeds. So that is the one who fears standing before his Lord, and forbids his self from personal desires.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Every eye will weep on the Day of Resurrection, except for three: An eye that stayed awake in the way of Allah, and an eye that overflowed from fear of Allah, and an eye that was restrained from the prohibitions of Allah.

From Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Among what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic and Exalted, whispered to Musa (peace be upon him) was: 'O Musa! Those who draw near to Me do not draw near with anything like piety (war') from My prohibitions. So I have granted them the Gardens of Eden, not sharing anyone else with them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From the most difficult of what Allah has imposed upon His creatures is the frequent remembrance of Allah. Then he said: 'I do not mean (saying) 'Glory be to Allah, and the Praise is to Allah, and there is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest', even though it is from it, but the remembrance of Allah in what He has permitted and prohibited. So if it was obedience, act upon it, and if it was disobedience, leave it.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We will proceed to what they have done of deeds, so We shall render them as scattered floating dust.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! Even if their deeds were more intensely whiter than the Coptic tapestry, but whenever the Prohibition was presented to them, they were not leaving it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that one of the Quraysh said to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'By what thing do you precede the Prophets, when you were sent as the last of them and their seal?' So he said: 'I was the first one to believe in my Lord, and the first one to respond when God took the covenant of the Prophets and made them testify against themselves:' 'Am I not your Lord?' — so I was the first Prophet who said: Yes. Thus I preceded them by acknowledging God, Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): May I be sacrificed for you! I see some of our companions afflicted with recklessness, irritability, and rashness, and I become intensely distressed by that. And I see those who oppose us, and I see them to be of good bearing. He said: Do not say good bearing (samt), for al-samt is the bearing of the road. Rather, say good countenance (sima'), for God, Mighty and Majestic, says: Their marks are on their faces from the traces of prostration [48:29]. He said: I said: So I see him of good countenance, and he has dignity, and I become distressed by that. He said: Do not be distressed by what you have seen of the recklessness of your companions, nor by what you have seen of the good countenance of those who oppose you. When God, Blessed and Exalted, intended to create Adam, He created those two clays and then separated them into two parts. He said to the companions of the right: Be a creation by My permission! So they became a creation at the level of particles that move about. And He said to the people of the left: Be a creation by My permission! So they became a creation at the level of particles that crawl along. Then He raised a fire for them and said: Enter it by My permission! The first to enter it was Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). Then the Determined Ones (Ulu al-Azm) among the Messengers followed him, along with their successors and their followers. Then He said to the companions of the left: Enter it by My permission! They said: Our Lord, You created us to burn us? So they disobeyed. He then said to the companions of the right: Come out of the fire by My permission! The fire did not wound any of them with a wound, nor did it leave any trace on them. When the companions of the left saw them, they said: Our Lord, we see that our companions have been saved. Forgive us and command us to enter. He said: I have forgiven you, so enter it. But when they drew near and the scorching heat struck them, they turned back and said: O our Lord! We have no patience for burning. And they disobeyed. He commanded them to enter three times; each time they disobeyed and turned back. And He commanded those others three times; each time they obeyed and came out. Then He said to them all: Be clay by

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: 'By what thing did you precede the children of Adam?' He said: 'I was the first one to acknowledge my Lord. Indeed, God took the Covenant of the Prophets and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. So I was the first one to answer.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: Ali bin al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who performs what Allah has imposed upon him, he is from the best of the people.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abdullah ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Be patient and excel in patience and remain steadfast.' He said: 'Being patient upon the Obligations.'

A number of our companions of ours, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abi al-Saffatij, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Be patient and excel in patience and remain steadfast.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Be patient upon the Obligations, and excel in patience upon the difficulties, and remain steadfast upon the Imams (peace be upon them).' And in the narration of Ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Saffatij, and there is an addition in it: 'Therefore fear Allah, your Lord, regarding what He has imposed upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Perform the obligations of Allah, and you will become the most pious of people.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man is upon a deed, let him persist upon it for a year. Then he should change from it, if Allah wills, to something else. And that is because the Night of Pre-determination (Laylat al-Qadr) will occur in it during that year of his, whatever Allah wills to be.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The most beloved of deeds to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is that which the servant persists upon, even if it be little.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Isa ibn Ayoub, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Najaba, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There is nothing more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a deed that is persisted upon, even if it be small.

From him, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I love to persist upon the deed, even if it is little.'

From him, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I love to present myself to my Lord with my deeds being even/regular.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Suleiman ibn Khalid who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of imposing upon yourself an obligation, and then abandoning it for twelve crescents (months).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is written in the Torah: 'O son of Adam! Free yourself for My worship, I shall fill your heart with riches and will not fatigue you to your seeking, and it would be upon Me to aim to excel you and fill your heart with fear from Me, and that if you don’t free yourself for My worship, I shall fill your heart with a pre-occupation with the world, then I will not excel you and will exhaust you to the seeking (of the livelihood)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Jameela who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Blessed and High, said: 'O My servants, the truthful ones! Enjoy with My worship in the world, for indeed you will be enjoying with it in the Hereafter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most superior of the people is the one who has passion for worship, so he embraces it, loves it with his heart, and engages with it with his body, and devotes himself to it; thus, he does not care whether he experiences ease or hardship in the world.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Shazan ibn al-Khalil who said, 'And I wrote from his book with a chain for him raising it to Isa ibn Abdullah,' he said, 'Isa ibn Abdullah said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):' 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is worship?' He said: 'The good intention in obedience, from the aspects from which Allah is obeyed. Indeed, O Isa, you will not be a believer until you know the abrogating from the abrogated.' He said, 'I said, may I be sacrificed for you, and what is the knowledge of the abrogating from the abrogated?' So he said: 'Is it not that you are with the Imam, settling your self upon the good intention in his obedience, so that Imam passes away and another Imam comes, so you settle your self upon the good intention in his obedience?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'This is the knowledge of the abrogating from the abrogated.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Harun ibn Kharjat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the worshippers are three types: A group worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, out of fear, so that is the worship of the slaves; and a group worshipped Allah, Blessed and High, seeking the reward, so that is the worship of the employees; and a group worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, out of love for Him, so that is the worship of the free ones, and it is the most superior of the worships.

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How ugly is poverty after wealth, and how ugly is sinning after destitution, and how ugly is sinning after wealth, and how ugly is sinning after destitution, and uglier than that is the one who worships Allah then leaves his worship.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The one who acts by what Allah has obligated upon him, he is the most worshipping of the people.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: There is no deed except with an intention.

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The intention of the Believer is better than his deed, and the intention of the disbeliever is more evil than his deed, and every deed is performed upon its intention'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn al-Husayn, from Amr, from Hasan ibn Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the limit of the worship which, when the performer does it, he would be a performer. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Good intention with the obedience'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Abu Hashim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The inhabitants of the Fire are eternally in the Fire because their intentions in the world were that if they were to remain in it, they would disobey Allah forever.' And the inhabitants of Paradise are eternally in Paradise because their intentions in the world were that if they were to remain in it, they would obey Allah forever. Thus, these and those are made eternal by their intentions. Then he recited the Words of the Exalted: 'Say, each acts according to his own disposition.' He said: 'According to his intention.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ahwal, from Sallam ibn Al-Mustanir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, every worship has a period of vigor, then it becomes a period of slackness. So whoever's vigor in worship adheres to my Sunnah, he has been guided; and whoever opposes my Sunnah, he has strayed, and his deed is in ruin. Indeed, I pray and I sleep, I fast and I break the fast, I laugh and I cry. So whoever turns away from my path and my Sunnah is not from me.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Death is sufficient as an exhortation, and certainty is sufficient as wealth, and worship is sufficient as a preoccupation.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'For everyone there is an enthusiasm (shirrah), and for every enthusiasm there is a decline (fitrah). So, 'Tuba' (a tree in Paradise) is for the one whose decline is towards goodness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This religion is robust, therefore delve into it with softness, and do not make the worship of Allah seem abhorrent to the servants of Allah, so you would become like the excessive rider who neither cuts (completes) a journey nor does a back (of an animal) remain (for him)'. Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muqarrin, from Muhammad ibn Sowqat, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not make the worship abhorrent to yourselves.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He loves a servant, and he performs a small deed, He recompenses him with much for the little; and it does not seem great to Him to recompense with much for a small deed.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Mansur, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father passed by me while I was performing Tawaf, and I was young and had strived in worship, so he saw me and I was perspiring profusely. He said to me: 'O Ja'far! O my son! When Allah loves a servant, He enters him into Paradise and is pleased with him for even a little [effort].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I strove in worship while I was a youth, so my father (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O my son, moderate what I see you doing, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He loves a servant, is pleased with him for the little (that he does).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Khashshab from Ibn Baqqah from Mu'adh ibn Thabit from 'Amr ibn Jumay' from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Ali! This Religion is robust, so delve into it with gentleness, and do not make the worship of your Lord hateful to yourself. For the excessive one (meaning the one who goes to extremes), there remains no back (to ride upon) nor land (to travel through). Therefore, act like the one who hopes to die in old age, and beware with the caution of the one who fears dying tomorrow.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Al-Hasan bin Mahboub, from Ali bin Ra'ab, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Patience is the head of Faith.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Patience is to Faith as the head is to the body; so when the head is gone, the body is gone. Similarly, when patience is gone, Faith is gone.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, all from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Asbahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hafs, indeed whoever is patient, is patient for a little while, and indeed whoever panics, panics for a little while.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon you is patience in all your affairs, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and commanded him with patience and gentleness, so He said: And bear patiently what they say, and leave them with a noble leaving, and dismiss Me and the deniers, the possessors of ease.' And the Blessed and High said: Repel evil with that which is best, so if there is enmity between you and him, it is as if he is an intimate friend. And none receive it except those who are patient, and none receive it except those of a great fortune. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was patient until they struck him with the bones of camels and threw them at him, so his chest constricted. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: And We certainly know that your chest constricts because of what they say. So glorify with the praise of your Lord and be of those who prostrate. Then they denied him and threw [dirt/bones] at him, so he was grieved by that. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: We know indeed that what they say certainly grieves you. For they do not deny you, but the unjust deny the signs of Allah. And certainly messengers before you were denied, but they were patient with what they were denied and harmed, until Our help came to them. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) imposed patience upon himself. Then they transgressed and mentioned Allah, Blessed and High, and denied Him. So he said: 'I have been patient regarding myself, my family, and my honor, but there is no patience for me regarding the mention of my God.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us. So be patient with what they say. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was patient in all his states. Then he was given glad tidings regarding his offspring with the Imams, and they were described with patience. So He, Majestic is His praise, said

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Muhammad Abdullah al-Sarraj, raised it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Patience is to Faith as the head is to the body, and there is no Faith for the one who has no patience.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Patience is to Faith as the head is to the body. So when the head goes, the body goes. Similarly, when patience goes, Faith goes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Marhoum, from Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the believer enters his grave, the prayer will be on his right, and the alms-tax on his left, and righteousness will hover over him, and patience will withdraw to a side. So when the two angels who oversee his questioning enter upon him, patience will say to the prayer, and the alms-tax, and the righteousness: 'Leave your companion to you. But if you are unable to help him, then I will be with him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What withheld you from the Hajj?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A great debt fell upon me, and my wealth is gone, and the debt that has become obligatory upon me is greater than the wealth that has gone. So if a man from our companions had not paid it for me, I would not have been able to go out.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If you are patient, you will be glad (of the reward), and if you are not patient, Allah will implement His decree, whether you are pleased with it or reluctant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Al Asbagh who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: Patience is of two types: patience during the calamity is good and beautiful; but better than that is patience when abstaining from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited upon you. And Remembrance is of two types: the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during the calamity; but superior to that is the remembrance of Allah when abstaining from what He has prohibited upon you, thus it serves as a barrier.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi from Al-Abbas ibn Amir from Al-Arzami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon the people in which dominion is not attained except by killing and tyranny, nor wealth except by usurpation and stinginess, nor love except by extracting the religion and following personal desires.' So whoever experiences that time, and is patient with poverty while having the ability to be wealthy, and is patient with hatred while having the ability to be loved, and is patient with humiliation while having the ability to be honored, Allah will grant him the reward of fifty truthful ones (siddiqun) from those who affirmed my prophethood.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When the death of my father, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), approached, he pressed me to his chest and said: 'O my son! I bequeath to you what my father bequeathed to me when death approached him, and what he mentioned that his father bequeathed to him: O my son! Be patient with the truth, even if it is bitter.'

From him, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, raising it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Patience is two types: patience upon affliction is good and beautiful; and the superior of the two types of patience is abstinence from the prohibitions.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: 'Yahya ibn Suleym al-Ta'i informed me,' who said: 'Amr ibn Shimr al-Yamani narrated, raising the hadith to Ali (peace be upon him):' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Patience is of three types: patience at the time of calamity, patience in performing obedience, and patience in avoiding disobedience. So whoever is patient during the calamity until he repels it with the goodness of his consolation, Allah will write for him three hundred ranks, with the distance between each rank being as the distance between the sky and the earth. And whoever is patient in performing obedience, Allah will write for him six hundred ranks, with the distance between each rank being as the distance from the edges of the earth to the Throne. And whoever is patient in avoiding disobedience, Allah will write for him nine hundred ranks, with the distance between each rank being as the distance from the edges of the earth to the utmost limit of the Throne.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me to go to Al-Mufazzal and console him regarding Ismail, and he (peace be upon him) said: Convey greetings to Al-Mufazzal and say to him, We have been bereaved of Ismail, so we were patient; therefore, be patient as we were patient. We intended a matter, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended a matter, so we submitted to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Amyera, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one from the believers who is afflicted with an affliction, so he is patient upon it, there would be for him the like of the Recompense of a thousand martyrs'.
