Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed favor upon a people but they were not grateful, so a calamity came upon them; and He tested a people with afflictions, so they were patient, and it became a blessing for them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Jameela, from his grandfather Abi Jameela, from one of his companions, who said: Had patience not been created before the affliction, the believer would have cracked apart, just as the egg cracks upon the rock.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have made the world between My servants a loan. So whoever lends Me a loan from it, I will give him ten for every one, up to seven hundred times, and whatever I desire from that; and whoever does not lend Me a loan from it, so I take something from him forcibly. If he is patient, I will give him three characteristics, such that if I were to give one of them to My angels, they would be pleased with Me from it.' He said, then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who, when a misfortune befalls them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return.' 'Those are they upon whom are blessings from their Lord.' So this (blessings) is one of the three characteristics. And mercy is the second, and guidance is the third. Then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for those from whom Allah takes something forcibly.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Shareek, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The magnanimity of patience in the state of need and destitution, and abstinence and riches, is greater than the magnanimity of giving.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May Allah have mercy on you! What is the beautiful patience?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is a patience wherein is no complaining to the people.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from one of his companions from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba from Abu al-Nu'man from Abu Abdillah or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The one who does not prepare patience for the calamities of time will be frustrated.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We are patient, and our Shia are more patient than us. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, how did your Shia become more patient than you?' He said, 'Because we are patient upon what we know, and our Shia are patient upon what they do not know.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who eats and is grateful, for him is a reward like the reward of the fasting one who counts his reward [with God]; and the one who is healthy and is grateful, for him is a reward like the reward of the afflicted one who is patient; and the one who is given [bounties] and is grateful, for him is a reward like the reward of the deprived one who is content.'

And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whatever Allah opens upon a servant the door of gratefulness, He does not keep hidden from him the door of increasing (bounties).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is written in the Torah: 'Thank the one who bestows favor upon you, and bestow favor upon the one who thanks you, for there is no decline of the bounties when they are thanked for, and there is no permanence for them when they are denied. Gratitude is an increase in the bounties and a safety from changes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yaqoub ibn Salim, from a man, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who is healthy and grateful, for him from the recompense is [what is] for the afflicted and patient; and the giver who is grateful, for him from the recompense is like the deprived and contented.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Fadl al-Baqbaq, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And as for the favour of your Lord, do announce (it)' He said: 'The One Who Favoured you with whatever He Graced you with, and Gave you, and was Good to you.' Then he said: 'So he announced with his Religion what Allah had Given him, and whatever He had Favoured with upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hasan ibn Jahm, from Abu Al-Yaqzan, from Ubaydullah ibn Al-Walid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There are three (things) with which nothing will harm [a person]: Supplication during distress, seeking forgiveness during sin, and gratitude during blessings.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He who is given gratitude is given increase. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor].'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from two men from our companions, who heard him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: 'Allah has not favored a servant with any blessing, so that he recognizes it in his heart and thanks Allah outwardly with his tongue, so that his speech is completed, until it is commanded for him to be given more.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Hisham, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The gratefulness of the bounties is keeping away from the prohibitions, and the completion of the gratefulness is the speech of the man (saying) 'The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Uyayna, from Umar ibn Yazeed who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The gratitude for every blessing, even if it is great, is that you praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who praises Allah upon a Bounty, so he has thanked Him, and the Praise is superior to that Bounty.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'Whatever blessing Allah favors a servant with, whether small or large, if he says, "The praise is for Allah," he has not yet fulfilled its gratitude.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Isa ibn Ayoub from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ismail ibn Abu Al-Hasan from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one upon whom Allah favours with a bounty, so he recognises it in his heart, so he has paid its gratitude.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a man from you drinks a single draught of water, and Allah obligates Paradise for him because of it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, he takes a vessel, places it to his mouth, recites the Name (of Allah), then drinks. Then he moves it away while still desirous of it, praises Allah, then returns to drink. Then he moves it away, praises Allah, then returns to drink. Then he moves it away, praises Allah. Thus, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, obligates Paradise for him because of it.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to grant me wealth, so He granted me, and I asked Allah to grant me a son, so He granted me a son, and I asked Him to grant me a house, so He granted me, and I fear that this might be a gradual [leading to ruin].' So he said: 'By Allah, with praise, no.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa' from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out from the Masjid and his riding animal had been lost. So he said: 'If Allah returns it to me, I will thank Allah with the true thanksgiving.' He said: 'So it was not long before it was brought to him, so he said: 'The praise is for Allah.' A man said to him: 'May I be your ransom, did you not say: I will thank Allah with the true thanksgiving?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Did you not hear me say: The praise is for Allah?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when a matter that pleased him reached him, would say: 'All praise is due to Allah for this favor.' And when a matter that grieved him reached him, he would say: 'All praise is due to Allah in every state.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: You should say three times, when you look at the afflicted one, without him hearing it: 'The Praise is for Allah Who gave me well-being from what He afflicted you with, and had He willed, He would have done so.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who says that will not be struck by that affliction ever.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hafs al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no servant who sees an afflicted person and says, 'Praise be to Allah who directed away from me what He afflicted you with, and favored me over you with health; O Allah, grant me health from what You afflicted him with,' except that he will not be afflicted with that trial.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: When you see a man who has been afflicted, and Allah has favored you, then say: 'O Allah, I am neither ridiculing nor priding myself, but I am praising You for the great bounty of Yours upon me.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on a journey, riding upon his she-camel. When he dismounted, he prostrated with five prostrations. So when he mounted, they said, 'O Messenger of Allah! We saw you doing something you had not done before.' He said, 'Yes. Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to me and gave me glad tidings from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So I prostrated to Allah in gratitude, one prostration for each glad tidings.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When one of you remembers a favor of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, let him place his cheek upon the dust in gratitude to Allah. So if he is riding, let him descend and let him place his cheek upon the dust; and if he is not able to descend due to publicity, let him place his cheek upon his saddle bow; and if he is not able, let him place his cheek upon his wrist, then let him praise Allah upon whatever He has favored him with.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Hisham ibn Ahmar, who said: I was travelling with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in one of the outskirts of Medina when he joined his legs from his mount and fell into prostration, prolonging it and prolonging it. Then he raised his head and rode his mount. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you have prolonged the prostration.' He said, 'Indeed, I remembered a bounty that Allah had favored me with, so I loved that I should thank my Lord.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Abdullah, Sahib Al Sayyari, regarding what I know, or someone else, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He said: Regarding what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! Thank Me as is the right of thanking Me.' So he said: 'O Lord! And how can I thank You as is the right of Your thanking, and there is no thanks with which I thank You except that You have favored with it upon me?' He said: 'O Musa! Now you have thanked Me, when you knew that that is from Me.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Raib, from Ismail ibn ibn al-Fazl, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you rise in the morning and when you settle in the evening, say ten times: 'O Allah, whatever blessing or health of religion or world has come to me, it is from You Alone, there is no partner for You. To You is the praise and to You is the gratitude for it upon me, O Lord, until You are pleased, and after the pleasure.' For indeed, when you say that, you have fulfilled the gratitude for whatever Allah has favored you with, during that day and during that night.

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Nuh (peace be upon him) used to say that whenever it was morning, so he was named due to that as a grateful servant. And he (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is truthful with Allah, he is rescued.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Ammar Al-Duhni, who said: I heard Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah loves every grieving heart, and He loves every grateful servant.' Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will say to one of His servants on the Day of Judgment: 'Did you thank so-and-so?' He will say, 'No, I thanked You, O Lord.' He will say, 'You did not thank Me because you did not thank him.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The most thankful to Allah are those who are most thankful to the people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The most perfect of the believers in faith is the best of them in character.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man from the people of Al-Madinah, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That which is placed upon the Scale of a person on the Day of Judgement, nothing is superior to good manners.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Four (qualities), whoever possesses them, his faith will be perfect, and even if he was (full of) sins from his head to his feet, that would not diminish his faith. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And they are truthfulness, and paying back the trusts, and bashfulness (modesty), and good character.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, the one of good character/manners has a reward like that of the fasting one who stands (in prayer).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most by which my community will enter Paradise is God-consciousness and good character.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn al-Ahmasi and Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, good character melts the sin just as the sun melts the ice.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Righteousness and good manners build the houses (households) and increase the life-spans.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man died during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so the grave diggers came to him, but when they were with him, they could not dig anything. They complained about that to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, our iron does not work in the earth; it is as if we are striking it against rock.' He said: 'Why? If your companion was of good character, bring me a cup of water.' So they brought it to him. He put his hand into it, then sprinkled it upon the earth with a sprinkle, then said: 'Dig!' He said: 'So the grave diggers dug, and it was as if it were sand falling upon them.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, good character (al-khuluq) is a gift that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grants to His creation. From it is natural disposition (sajjiyyah), and from it is intention (niyyah). So I said, 'Which of the two is superior?' He said: 'The one with the natural disposition is innate and cannot choose otherwise, while the one with intention is patient in obedience with patience; therefore, he is superior of the two.'

And from him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali Al-Lahabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gives the servant from the reward for good manners just as He gives to the fighter in the Way of Allah, morning and evening.

From him, from Abdullah Al-Hajjal, from Abu Uthman Al-Qabousy, from the one who mentioned him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, lent to His enemies manners from the manners of His friends, so that His friends may live among His enemies in their dominion. And in another report: 'And were it not for that, they would not have left a friend of Allah except that they would have killed him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-A'ala ibn Kamil, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you mingle with the people, if you have the capacity to not mingle with anyone from the people except that your hand would be higher upon him, then do so. For indeed, the servant may have some deficiency in worship, but he has good manners, so Allah will bring him, due to his good manners, to the rank of the fasting one who stands (in prayer).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Bahr al-Saqqa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Bahr! Good manners are an affluence.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I inform you of a hadith which is not in the hands of anyone from the people of Medina?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One day, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting in the Masjid, a slave girl of one of the Ansar came to him while he was sitting upright. So she grabbed a side of his clothes. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) stood up for her, but she did not say anything, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not say anything to her, to the extent that she did that three times.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) stood up for her during the fourth attempt, and she was behind him, so she took an edge of his cloth, then retracted. So the people said to her, 'May Allah deal with you and do (whatever He may)! You withheld the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) three times, neither did you say anything to him nor did he say anything to you. What was your need to him?' She said, 'For us there is a sick one. So my people sent me to take an edge from his cloth in order to heal him by it. So whenever I wanted to take it, he saw me, and stood up. So I was too embarrassed from him to take it while he sees me, and I disliked to ask him regarding taking it, therefore I took it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Habib al-Khash'ami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most preferable among you are those with the best manners, those who are easy to approach, who are familiar and make others familiar, and whose seats are frequently occupied (by guests/friends).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is amiable (gets acquainted with others), and there is no good in the one who neither gets acquainted nor is gotten acquainted with.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, good manners elevates its owner to the rank of the fasting one who stands (in prayer).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O sons of Abd al-Muttalib! You will never be equal to the people in their wealth, therefore meet them with the relaxed face and goodly cheerfulness.' And it is reported from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), except that he said: 'O Clan of Hashim.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three (things): whoever comes to Allah with one of them, Allah will obligate Paradise for him: spending from poverty, cheerfulness with all the world, and justice with oneself.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' So, among what he advised him was that he said: 'Meet your brother with a cheerful face.'

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the limit of good character?' He said, 'You soften your wing, and make your speech sweet, and meet your brother with a pleasant smile.'

From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Fuzayl who said: The good works and the goodly cheerfulness both amass the love and cause to enter the Paradise; and the stinginess and a frown face both cause remoteness from Allah and cause to enter the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Goodly cheerfulness removes grudges.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send a Prophet except with truthful narrations, and repayment of the entrustments to the righteous as well as the immoral.

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, and others, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not be deceived by their prayer and by their fasting, for sometimes the man becomes habitual with prayer and fasting to the extent that if he were to leave it, he feels terrified. But, test them when they are truthful in narration and in repaying the entrustments.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one whose tongue is truthful, his deed becomes pure.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When I first entered upon him, he said: Learn truthfulness before learning the Hadith.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Kahmas, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur conveys the greetings to you.' He said, 'And upon you and him be the greetings. When you go to Abdullah, convey the greetings to him and say to him that Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) says to you: 'Look at what Ali (peace be upon him) reached in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so adhere to it, for indeed Ali (peace be upon him) reached whatever he reached in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by truthful narration and the fulfillment of the trust.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ismail al-Basri, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Fuzayl! The truthful is the first one whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ratifies. He knows that he is truthful, and his soul ratifies him, knowing that he is truthful.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Ismail (peace be upon him) was named 'Truthful of the Promise' because he promised a man to meet him in a specific place, so he waited for him in that place for a year. Therefore, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named him 'Truthful of the Promise'. Then he said: The man came to him after that, so Ismail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'I did not cease waiting for you'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from his grandfather Al-Rabi' ibn Sa'd, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Rabi'! Indeed, a man may be truthful until Allah writes him as a truthful one (Siddiq).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The servant is truthful until he is recorded in the Presence of Allah among the truthful, and he lies until he is recorded in the Presence of Allah among the liars. So when he is truthful, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "He is truthful and righteous"; and when he lies, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "He is a liar and an immoral one".'

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Be callers to goodness for the people without your tongues, so that they may see from you striving, truthfulness, and piety.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, who said, Abu al-Walid Hassan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The one whose tongue is truthful, his deed becomes pure; and the one whose intention is good, his livelihood is increased; and the one who is righteous to his family, his lifespan is extended.

From him, from Abu Talib, raising it, said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not look at the length of the man's bowing and prostration, for that is something he has become accustomed to; were he to leave it, he would feel strange because of it. But look at the truthfulness of his narration and the repayment of his entrustment.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Bashfulness (al-hiya') is from faith (al-iman), and faith is in Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shyness (Al-Hiyā), chastity/modesty (Al-'Afāf), and tongue-tiedness (Al-'Iyy), meaning the modesty of the tongue, not the modesty of the heart, is from faith (Al-Īmān).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Mus'ab ibn Yazeed, from al-'Awwam ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who softens his face softens his knowledge.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Yahya, brother of Darim, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Bashfulness (al-hayā') and faith (al-īmān) are paired in one coupling; so when one of the two departs, its companion follows it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Al-Fadl ibn Kathir, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no faith for the one who has no bashfulness.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it, said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Bashfulness is of two types: bashfulness of intellect and bashfulness of foolishness. So the bashfulness of the intellect is knowledge, and the bashfulness of foolishness is ignorance.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali Al-Lahabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four (qualities), whoever possesses them, and even if he was (immersed) in sins from his head to his toe, Allah would change them to good deeds: Truthfulness, Bashfulness (Hiya), Good Manners, and Gratitude.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in his sermon: 'Shall I inform you of the best moral qualities of the world and the Hereafter? It is pardoning the one who oppressed you, and maintaining relations with the one who cut you off, and doing good to the one who did wrong to you, and giving to the one who deprived you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Ghurrat ibn Dinar al-Raqqi, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who said, he raised it (to the Prophet): The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not guide you to the best of the manners of the world and the Hereafter? (It is) maintaining relations with the one who cuts you off, and giving to the one who deprives you, and pardoning the one who oppresses you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah Nushayb al-Lafa'ifi, from Humran ibn Ayn, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three [traits] are from the nobilities of the world and the Hereafter: pardoning the one who oppresses you, maintaining relations with the one who cuts you off, and forbearance when foolishness is shown to you.'

Ali from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will gather the first and the last in one plain. Then a caller will call out: 'Where are the people of merit?' So a group of people will stand, and the angels will meet them and say: 'And what was your merit?' So they will say: 'We maintained relations with those who cut us off, and we gave to those who deprived us, and we pardoned those who oppressed us.' He said: 'So it will be said to them: You have spoken the truth. Enter Paradise.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Jahm ibn al-Hakam al-Madainy, from Ismail ibn Abu Ziyad al-Sakuny, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is upon you to practice pardoning, for pardoning does not increase the servant except in honour; therefore, pardon one another, Allah will honour you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The regret upon the pardoning is superior and easier than the regret upon the punishing.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Sa'dan, from Mu'tab who said: Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) was in his garden picking dates. I looked at one of his slaves who had taken a bunch of dates and threw it behind the wall. So I went to him, seized him, and brought him to the Imam. I said, 'May I be your ransom, I found this one and this bunch of dates.' He said to the slave, 'O So-and-so,' and he replied, 'At your service.' He asked, 'Are you hungry?' He said, 'No, my Master.' He asked, 'Are you naked (need clothes)?' He said, 'No, my Master.' He asked, 'Then for what reason did you take these?' He said, 'I desired that.' He said, 'Go, they are for you,' and he said, 'Leave him alone.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal who said: I heard Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) saying: 'No two parties ever met (in a confrontation) at all, except victory was for the one who was greater of the two in pardoning'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was brought the Jewess who had poisoned the sheep for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said to her: 'What carried you to do what you did?' She said: 'I said, if he is a Prophet, it would not harm him, and if he is a king, I relieved the people from him.' He said: 'So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Three (actions) with which Allah does not increase the Muslim except in honour: pardoning the one who oppressed him, giving to the one who deprived him, and maintaining kinship with the one who cut him off.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: ‘The best swallowing of the anger is for the one who is patient upon it, for the great Recompense is for the one (subjected to) great afflictions, and Allah does not Love a people except He Tests them’.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Be patient with the enemies of the favours, for you will not recompense the one who disobeys Allah regarding you with anything superior to obeying Allah regarding him.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Thabit, the mawla of the family of Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Suppressing the anger from the enemy during their power, as a form of dissimulation (taqiyyah), is prudence for the one who practices it, and a protection from exposure to affliction in the world. And opposing the enemies during their power and confronting them without dissimulation is neglecting the Command of Allah. Therefore, be polite to the people, for that will nourish (increase your standing) for you in their presence, and do not make enemies of them, lest they carry you on their necks (dominate you) and you become humiliated.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from one of his companions, from Malik ibn Husayn al-Sakuni, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who suppresses his anger except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, increases him with honor in this world and the Hereafter.' And those who restrain their anger and pardon the people; and Allah loves the doers of good. And Allah rewards him in place of that anger.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Usman, from Abdullah ibn Munzir, from al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever suppresses his anger while he is able to carry it out, Allah will fill his heart with security and faith on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: 'O Zayd! Be patient with the enemies of the favours, for you will not recompense the one who disobeys Allah regarding you with anything better than obeying Allah regarding him. O Zayd! Indeed Allah chose Islam and selected it, so be good companions of it with generosity and good character.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hafs al-Baya' al-Sabiri, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the most beloved ways to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are two sips: a sip of anger that is repelled by forbearance, and a sip of calamity that is repelled by patience.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: My father said to me: 'O my son! There is nothing that delights the eyes of your father more than swallowing a draught of anger, the consequence of which is patience, and there is nothing that brings me joy if I possess it, even if it costs the humility of my soul, like the red camels.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Mu'adh ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Be patient with the enemies of the favours (of God), for you will not recompense the one who disobeys Allah regarding you with anything better than obeying Allah regarding him.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Khallad, from Al-Sumaly, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'I do not love that I should humble myself for the sake of the red camels (great wealth), and there is no potion I have swallowed that is more beloved to me than the potion of anger, by which I do not requite its owner.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no potion that a servant swallows that is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than the potion of anger that he swallows when it churns in his heart, either through patience or through forbearance.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, who said: I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man does not become a worshipper until he becomes forbearing, and indeed, among the Children of Israel, a man was not counted as a worshipper until he remained silent for ten years prior to that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza, who said: The Believer mingles his deeds with forbearance; he sits to learn and speaks to understand. He does not narrate his entrusted secrets to his friends, nor does he conceal his testimony from his enemies. He does not do any act of truth for the sake of showing off, nor does he leave it out of shyness. If praised, he fears what they do not know; he seeks forgiveness from Allah for what they do not know. He is not deceived by the words of those who are ignorant of him, and he fears the recording of what he has done.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was saying: 'It would astound me, the man, if his forbearance comes across him during his anger'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the bashful one, the forbearing one.

From him, from Ali ibn Hafs al-Awsy al-Kufi, he raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah will not Honour (anyone) by ignorance at all, nor would He Humiliate (anyone) by forbearance at all'.

From him, from one of his companions, raising it, said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Suffice with forbearance as a helper.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are not forbearing, then become forbearing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Hafs ibn Abu Ayesha, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent one of his slaves on a need, and he was delayed. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out after him when he was delayed, and found him sleeping. So he sat by his head fanning him until he woke up. And when he woke up, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O so-and-so! By Allah, that is not for you; you sleep night and day. For you is the night, and for us, from you, is the day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah loves the bashful, the forbearing, the chaste, the abstemious.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboub, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Abbas ibn Aamir, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad Al-Musli, from Abu Muhammad, from Imran, from Saeed ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a dispute occurs between two men, two angels descend and say to the foolish one of the two: 'You spoke, and you spoke, and you are deserving of what you said; you will be recompensed for what you said.' And they say to the forbearing one of the two: 'You were patient and forbearing; Allah will forgive you if you complete that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But if the forbearing one replies to him, the two angels ascend.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said: 'From the signs of the understanding (fiqh) are forbearance, knowledge, and silence. Indeed, silence is a door from the doors of wisdom. Indeed, silence acquires love. Indeed, it is a pointer upon every goodness.'
From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Our Shia are the mute ones.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ali Al-Jawwani, who said: I witnessed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was saying to a slave of his called Saalim, and he placed his hand on his lips and said: 'O Saalim! Preserve your tongue and you will be safe, and do not load the people upon our necks.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa who said: I was present with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and a man said to him: 'Advise me'. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Preserve your tongue, you will be honoured, and do not enable the people to lead you, so your neck would be disgraced'.

From him, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Mas'ruq, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man who came to him: 'Shall I guide you to a matter by which Allah will admit you to Paradise?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Give from what Allah has given you.' He said: 'But what if I am more in need than the one to whom I give?' He said: 'Then help the oppressed.' He said: 'And what if I am weaker than the one I help?' He said: 'Then deal with the silly one (al-akhrak), meaning, indicate upon him (his affairs).' He said: 'What if I am sillier than the one I do this for?' He said: 'Then silence your tongue except from goodness.' Would it not please you that there should be a characteristic from these characteristics in you, pulling you to Paradise?

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Luqman said to his son: 'O my son! If you claim that speech is of silver, then silence is of gold.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Halabi, raising it (to the Prophet), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Withhold your tongue, for it is a charity by which you give charity upon yourself.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And a servant will not recognize the reality of faith until he guards his tongue.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Have you not seen those to whom it was said: Withhold your hands?' He said: 'It means: Restrain your tongues.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Halabi, raising it, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The salvation of the believer lies in the preservation of his tongue.

Yunus, from Musanna, from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Abu Zarr, may Allah have mercy on him, was saying: O seeker of knowledge! Indeed, this tongue is a key for goodness and a key for evil. Therefore, set a seal upon your tongue just as you set a seal upon your gold and your silver.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Khashshab from Ibn Baqqah from Mu'adh ibn Thabit from Amr ibn Jumay' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messiah (peace be upon him) was saying: 'Do not increase speech in that which is other than the Remembrance of Allah, for those who increase speech in that which is other than the Remembrance of Allah, their hearts become hard, but they do not know.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jameela, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'There is no day except that every limb from the limbs of the body pleads to the tongue, saying: I adjure you by Allah that we not be punished because of you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam al-Asadi, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the tongue of the son of Adam stands over all his limbs every morning, and it says, 'How have you fared?' So they say, 'With goodness, if you leave us,' and they say, 'Allah, Allah, regarding us,' and they adjure it, and they say, 'We are rewarded and punished only because of you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Qays Abi Ismail, and he mentioned that there is no problem with him from our companions, raising it (to the Prophet). He said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' So he said, 'Preserve your tongue.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said, 'Preserve your tongue.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said, 'Preserve your tongue. Woe to you! And what causes people to be thrown on their faces into the Fire except the harvest of their tongues?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who does not reckon his speech as part of his deeds, his sins will increase, and his punishment will approach.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah will punish the tongue with a punishment with which He does not punish any of the other body parts. So it will say, "O Lord! You have punished me with a punishment with which You did not punish anything else."' So it will be said to him: 'A word came out from you and it reached the east and west of the earth, so unlawful blood was shed because of it, and unlawful wealth was seized, and the private parts were violated; and by My Honour and My Majesty! I will surely punish you with a punishment with which I do not punish anything else from your body parts.'
And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: If there is anything with evil omen in it, so it is in the tongue.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, all together from Al-Washsha, who said: I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man from the Children of Israel, whenever he intended to worship, would remain silent before that for ten years.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Ghifari, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who sees the place (effect) of his speech on his deeds, would be scarce in his speech, except regarding what is meaningful'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Among the wisdoms of the progeny of Dawud (peace be upon him) is that the intellectual should be aware of his time, attentive to his affairs, and preserving his tongue.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believing servant does not cease to be written as a good-doer for as long as he is silent. So when he speaks, he is written either as a good-doer or an evil-doer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three (qualities), whoever does not have them, his deed is not complete: Piety that restrains him from the disobedience of Allah, and good character by which he manages people, and forbearance by which he repels the ignorance of the ignorant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, who said: I heard Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad! Your Lord conveys greetings to you, and says to you: Be polite with My creatures.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is written in the Torah among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! Conceal the hidden aspect of My secret in your inner self, and manifest politeness on My behalf in your public appearances to My enemy and your enemy from My creation, and do not become presumptuous for Me in their presence by manifesting the hidden aspect of My secret, lest your enemy and My enemy participate in insulting Me.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hamzah ibn Bazie, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'My Lord commanded me with being polite with the people just as He commanded with the fulfilment of the Obligations'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Politeness with the people is half the Emān, and kindness with them is half the life'. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Mingle with the righteous secretly and mingle with the immoral superficially (in public), but do not be attracted to them as they would oppress you. There will come a time, when, from the religious people, only those will be safe who are thought of as fools, and they would patience so much so that they will be called silly i.e. there is no intellect for him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from one of his companions, mentioning from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A group of people had little politeness towards the people, so they were expelled from Quraysh, and I swear by Allah, there was no problem with their lineage, and a group from other than Quraysh had good politeness, so they were joined with the elevated household.' He said, 'Then he said: The one who restrains his hand from the people, rather, he restrains one hand from them but they restrain many hands from him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: For everything there is a lock, and the lock of faith is kindness.
And by his chain, he said, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The one for whom kindness is apportioned, faith is apportioned to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Hammad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Kind (Rafiq) and He loves kindness. From His kindness to His servants is that He eases their grudges and their resistance against their desires and their hearts. And from His kindness to them is that He leaves them upon a command, intending to remove them from it as a kindness to them, so that He does not cast upon them the bonds of faith and its burden all at once, causing them to weaken. So when He wills that, He abrogates the command with another, and it becomes abrogated.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Muaz ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Kindness is a bounty and infringement is an evil omen.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is Kind (Rafiq), He loves kindness, and He grants upon kindness what He does not grant upon harshness.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Kindness is not placed upon anything except that it adorns it, and it is not removed from anything except that it dishonours it.'

Ali, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam, (It has been narrated) raising it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: 'In kindness there is increase and blessings; and whoever is deprived of kindness is deprived of goodness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Isma'il ibn Yasar, from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Arqam al-Kufi, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Whichever family is given their share of kindness, then Allah has expanded for them in sustenance. And kindness in managing one's livelihood is better than abundance in wealth. And kindness is such that nothing is lost from it, and extravagance is such that nothing remains with it. Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Kind, He loves kindness.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Hassan, from Musa bin Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Kindness (or gentleness) is half of life.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah loves kindness and assists upon it. So when you ride the lean animals, dismount them in their resting places. If the land is barren, hasten from it, and if it is fertile, dismount them in their places.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Had kindness (rifq) been a visible creature, there would not have been, among what Allah created, anything more beautiful than it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'aba ibn Maymun, from the one who narrated it, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Indeed, Allah is Kind (Rafiq), He loves kindness, and from His kindness to you is the easing of your grudges and the antagonism of your hearts. And indeed, He intends to turn the servant away from a matter, so He leaves it upon him until He turns it away by the Abrogating (Nasikh), disliking the heaviness of the truth upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No two people travel together or become companions except that the greater of the two in reward and the more beloved of the two to Allah, Exalted and Majestic, is the kinder of the two to his companion.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Fuzayl ibn Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who was kind during his lifetime would attain whatever he wanted from the people'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Najashi sent for Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions, so they entered upon him while he was in his house, sitting on the dust, and upon him were two threadbare garments. He said, so Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'We felt compassion for him when we saw him in that state.' So when he saw our reaction and the changing of our faces, he said: 'Praise be to Allah who granted victory to Muhammad and delighted his eyes. Shall I give you glad tidings?' So I said: 'Yes, O King.' He said: 'News has just come to me from your land, from one of my spies there, informing me that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted victory to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and destroyed his enemy, and captured so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so, when they met in a valley called Badr al-Arak. It is as if I am looking at it, where I used to graze for my master there, and he was a man from the Banu Dhamra.' Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O King, why do I see you sitting on the dust and wearing these threadbare garments?' He said to him: 'O Ja'far, we find in what Allah revealed to Isa (peace be upon him) that it is a right of Allah upon His servants to show humility to Him when He bestows a bounty upon them. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed a bounty upon me through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), I manifested this humility for Allah.' So when the news reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said to his companions: 'Charity increases its giver in abundance, so give charity, may Allah have mercy on you; and humility increases its possessor in elevation, so be humble, may Allah elevate you; and pardoning increases its possessor in honor, so pardon, may Allah honor you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, in the sky there are two angels assigned to the servants. So whoever is humble to Allah, they raise him (in status), and whoever is arrogant, they lower him.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) broke his fast on the evening of Thursday in the Mosque of Quba, so he said: 'Is there any drink?' So Aws ibn Khawlan al-Ansari brought him a vessel of buttermilk with honey. So when he placed it near his mouth, he set it aside, then said: 'Two drinks, one can suffice from the other. I neither drink it nor do I prohibit it, but I am being humble to Allah. For whoever is humble to Allah, Allah elevates him; and whoever is arrogant, Allah lowers him; and whoever is economical in his livelihood, Allah provides for him; and whoever is a spendthrift, Allah deprives him; and whoever frequently remembers death, Allah loves him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassash, from Dawud al-Hammarr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to it. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who frequently remembers Allah, Allah will shade him in His Paradise.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) mentioning that an Angel came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives you a choice: that you be a servant, a humble messenger, or a king, a messenger.' He said: So he looked at Jibreel and gestured with his hand [signaling] to be humble, so he said: 'A servant, a humble messenger.' The Messenger said, 'Along with that, nothing will be diminished from what is with your Lord.' He said: 'And with him were the keys of the treasures of the earth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From humility is that you are pleased with a seat below another's seat, and that you greet whoever you meet, and that you leave contention even if you are right, and that you do not love to be praised for piety.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa, do you know why I chose you with My Speech among My creation?' He said: 'O Lord, and why was that?' So Allah, Blessed and High, revealed to him: 'O Musa, I turned My servants over (examined them) and did not find among them anyone more humble to Me with his self than you, O Musa. Indeed, when you pray, you place your cheek upon the dust,' or he said: 'upon the ground.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) passed by the lepers while he was riding his donkey, and they were eating lunch. So they invited him to lunch. He said: 'Indeed, if I were not fasting, I would have done so.' When he returned to his house, he ordered food to be prepared, and he ordered that they should be refined/elegant in it. Then he invited them, so they had lunch with him, and he had lunch with them.

From him, from Ibn Fazzal and Muhassin bin Ahmad, from Yunus bin Yaqoub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at a man from the people of Medina who had bought something for his dependents and was carrying it. When the man saw him, he felt shy/embarrassed. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You bought it for your dependents and carried it to them. By Allah, had it not been for the people of Medina, I would have loved to buy something for my dependents and then carry it to them myself.'

From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him), was: 'O Dawud! Just as the closest of people to Allah are the humble ones, so too the most remote of people from Allah are the arrogant ones.'

From him, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, raising it to Abu Baseer who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) in the year in which Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) passed away, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What is the matter that you slaughtered a ram, and so and so slaughtered a camel?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Nuh (peace be upon him) was in the ship, and therein was what Allah willed, and the ship was under Command, so it performed the Tawaf of the House, and it is the Tawaf of the women, and Nuh (peace be upon him) had freed its way.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed unto the mountains: 'I shall be Placing the ship of Nuh, My servant, upon a mountain from you.' So they prolonged themselves and rose high, and the Judy humbled itself, and it is a mountain in your presence. So the ship struck the mountain with its keel. So Nuh (peace be upon him) said at that: 'O Mary Atqin', and it is in Assyrian: 'O Lord! Keep it well'. He (the narrator) said, 'So I thought Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was applying it to his own case'.

From him, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Humility is that you give people what you love to be given to you.

And in another Hadith, he said: 'I said, "What is the limit of humility such that when the servant practices it, he becomes humble?"' So he said: 'Humility has levels; among them is that a person recognizes his own worth and places it in its proper station with a sound heart, not loving to go to anyone except with the same as he loves to be brought to him.' If he sees a fault, he covers it with a good deed, the one who swallows his anger, who pardons people. And Allah loves the good-doers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said: '(What of) the nature of Allah upon which He has created mankind?' He said: 'Divine Unity (Tawheed).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'The nature made by God upon which He has fashioned people' (30:30) — what is that nature? He said: It is Islam. God fashioned them upon it when He took their covenant on divine unity (tawhid), saying: 'Am I not your Lord?' (7:172), and in it were the believer and the disbeliever.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'the nature made by God upon which He has created people' (30:30). He said: He created them all upon tawhid (Divine Unity/Oneness).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Being upright for God, not associating partners with Him' [22:31]. He said: 'The upright way (hanifiyya) is from the natural disposition (fitra) upon which God created the people; there is no alteration in God's creation' [30:30]. He said: 'He created them with the recognition (ma'rifa) of Him.' Zurara said: And I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their offspring, and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes!' — the verse [7:172]. He said: 'He extracted from the back of Adam his offspring until the Day of Resurrection. They came out like particles, and He introduced Himself to them and showed them Himself. Had it not been for that, not one of them would have recognized his Lord.' And he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every newborn is born upon the fitra — meaning the recognition that God, Mighty and Majestic, is his Creator. Likewise is His saying: "And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say: God"' [31:25].

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Abi Jamila, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'The fitrah of God upon which He has created the people' He said: 'He created them upon Tawhid.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who loves for the Sake of Allah and hates for the Sake of Allah and gives for the Sake of Allah, he is from those whose faith is perfect.

Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From the strongest bonds of faith is that you love for the sake of Allah and hate for the sake of Allah, and you give for the sake of Allah and you withhold for the sake of Allah.

Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal, Sahib al-Taqq, from Sallam ibn al-Mustanir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The affection of the believer for the believer for the sake of Allah is from the greatest of the branches of faith. Indeed! And whoever loves for the sake of Allah and hates for the sake of Allah and gives for the sake of Allah and withholds for the sake of Allah, then he is from the elites of Allah.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, those who love one another for the sake of Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon pulpits of light. The light of their faces, and the light of their bodies, and the light of their pulpits will have illuminated everything, to the extent that they will be recognized by it, so it will be said, "These are the ones who loved one another for the sake of Allah."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about love and hatred, are they from faith? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And is faith anything but love and hatred?' He made faith pleasing to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He made disbelief, transgression, and disobedience hateful to you; those are the rightly guided.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yahya, in what he knew, from Amr ibn Mudrik al-Ta'i, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: 'Which bond of faith is the strongest?' So they said, 'Allah and His Rasool know best,' and some of them said, 'The Salat,' and some of them said, 'The Zakat,' and some of them said, 'The Sawm,' and some of them said, 'The Hajj and the Umrah,' and some of them said, 'The Jihad.' So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For everything you said, there is merit, but that is not it. Rather, the strongest of the bonds of faith is love for Allah, and hatred for Allah, and the Wilayah of the Guardians of Allah, and the disavowal from the enemies of Allah.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Umar ibn Jabala al-Ahmasi, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The ones who love for the sake of Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon a land of green emerald, in the shade of His Throne, by His right hand, and both of His hands are right. Their faces will be whiter and more luminous than the rising sun. Every near angel and every sent prophet will envy them for their status. The people will say, 'Who are these?' So it will be said, 'These are the ones who loved for the sake of Allah.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gathers the former and the latter, a caller will stand and call out, making the people hear, and he will say: 'Where are those who love for the sake of Allah?' He said: 'So a neck (group) of the people will rise, and it will be said to them: Go to Paradise without reckoning.' He said: 'So the angels will meet them and say: To where?' They will say: 'To Paradise without reckoning.' He said: 'So they will say: So which group of people are you?' They will say: 'We are those who love for the sake of Allah.' He said: 'So they will say: And what were your deeds?' They will say: 'We used to love for Allah and hate for Allah.' He said: 'So they will say: Excellent is the recompense of the workers.'

From him, from Ali ibn Hassan, from the one who mentioned it, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three are the signs of the Believer: his knowledge of Allah, and whom he loves, and whom he hates.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a man may love you while not knowing what you are upon (in terms of Wilayah/authority), so Allah will enter him into Paradise due to his love for you; and indeed, a man may hate you while not knowing what you are upon, so Allah will enter him into the Fire due to his hatred for you.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn al-Arzymi, from his father, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you wish to know that there is goodness in you, look at your heart. If it loves the people of obedience to Allah and hates the people of His disobedience, then there is goodness in you and Allah loves you. And if it hates the people of obedience to Allah and loves the people of His disobedience, then there is no goodness in you and Allah hates you. And the person is with the one whom he loves.

From him, from Abu Ali al-Wasiti, from al-Husayn ibn Aban, from the one who mentioned, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If a man were to love a man for the Sake of Allah, Allah would Reward him upon his love for him, and even if it was so that the beloved was from the people of the Fire in the Knowledge of Allah; and if a man were to hate a man for the Sake of Allah, Allah would Reward him upon his hatred for him, and even if it was so that the hated one was from the people of the Paradise in the Knowledge of Allah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Bashir Al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There may be love for Allah and His Messenger, and love for the world. So whatever is for Allah and His Messenger, its reward is upon Allah; and whatever is for the world, it is nothing.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when two Muslims meet, the superior of the two is the one who has more intense love for his companion.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Ibn Fazzal, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: No two believers meet at all except that the superior of the two is the one who loves his brother more intensely.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Imran al-Sabi'i, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every person who does not love for the sake of the Religion and does not hate for the sake of the Religion, has no Religion.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'By My Honour, My Majesty, My Magnificence, My Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My Position! No servant would prefer My desire over his own desire except that I would suffice him against his losses, and I would make the heavens and the earth guarantee his sustenance, and I would be for him behind the trade of every merchant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My Honour, and My Majesty, and My Magnificence, and My Glory, and the loftiness of My Exaltedness! No believing servant would prefer My desires over his own desires in anything from the matters of the world, except that I shall make richness to be in his soul, and concern him regarding his Hereafter, and I shall guarantee the skies and the earth for his sustenance, and I shall be for him behind the trade of every trader.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of directing your gaze towards those who are above you in wealth, and suffice with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)': Let not their property and their children astound you And He said: 'And do not stretch your eyes after that with which We have provided wedded pairs of them, blossoms of the life of the world.' So if anything from that enters into you, then remember the life of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for indeed his provision was barley, his sweetener was dates, and his fuel was palm stalks when he found them.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abu Hammad, all together from Al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abu Khadeeja Salim ibn Mukram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who asked us, we gave it to him, and the one who managed without (asking), Allah enriched him.'
