Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is content with Allah with the little of livelihood, Allah will be pleased with him with the little of deeds.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: It is written in the Torah: 'O son of Adam! Be as you wish. Just as you pay back to you what you have paid out.' The one who is pleased with Allah with little sustenance, Allah accepts from him the small amount of deeds. And whoever is pleased with the little of the permissible, his expenditure becomes light, his earnings become pure, and he exits from the boundary of immorality.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Arafat, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is not content with sustenance except in abundance, will not be satisfied with deeds except in abundance; and the one who is content with little sustenance, indeed he will be satisfied with little deeds.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Asadi, from Salim ibn Mukram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The financial state of a man from the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) became difficult, so his wife said to him, 'If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and ask him.' So he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him). When the Prophet (peace be upon him) saw him, he said: 'The one who asks us, we give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah enriches him.' The man said, 'He did not mean anyone apart from me.' So he returned to his wife and informed her. She said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) is a human being, so inform him of it.' So he went to him. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saw him, he said: 'The one who asks us, we give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah enriches him,' to the extent that the man did that three times. Then the man went away, borrowed a pickaxe, went to the mountain, climbed it, and cut firewood. Then he brought it and sold it for half a Mudd of fine flour. He returned with it and ate it. Then he went the next day and brought more than that and sold it. He did not cease working and gathering until he bought a pickaxe. Then he gathered until he bought two young camels and a slave. Then he became wealthy to the extent that he became affluent. So he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and informed him of how he had come to ask him and how he had heard the Prophet (peace be upon him). The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I told you, the one who asks us, we give to him, and the one who manages without (asking), Allah enriches him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Furat, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever wishes to be the wealthiest of people, let him rely more on what is in the Hand of Allah than on what is in the hands of others.'

From him, from a number of our companions, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who is pleased from the world with whatever his apportionment is, the least of what is in it would suffice him; and the one who is not pleased from the world with what his apportionment is, there is nothing in it which would suffice him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from someone else, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Among the most blissful of My friends in My presence is a man of light state, possessing a share from prayer, who perfected the worship of his Lord in secrecy, and was hidden among the people. His livelihood was made sufficient (subsistence level), so he was patient with it. His death was hastened, so his inheritance was few and his mourners were few.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessed is the one who submits [to God] and whose livelihood is at the level of subsistence.'

Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah! Grant provision to Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and to whoever loves Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, chastity and sufficiency; and grant provision to whoever hates Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, wealth and children.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Nawfaly, raised it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a camel shepherd, so he sent to him to quench him, but he said, 'As for what is in their udders, it is for the morning, and as for what is in our containers, it is for the evening.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah! Increase his wealth and his children.' Then he passed by a sheep shepherd, so he sent for him to quench him. So he milked for him whatever was in its udders, and poured what was in his container into the container of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and sent a sheep to him, saying: 'This is what is with us, and if you love that we increase it for you, we will increase it for you.' He said, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah! Grant him sufficiency (al-kafaf).' One of his companions said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah! You supplicated for the one who repulsed you with a supplication which the majority of us love, and you supplicated for the one who relieved you of your need with a supplication which we all dislike.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, what is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and diverting. O Allah! Grant Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad sufficiency (al-kafaf).'

From him, from his father, from Abu Al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'My believing servant grieves if I restrict him, and that is closer to Me; and My believing servant rejoices if I expand for him, and that is more remote from Me.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Among the most blissful of My friends in My Presence is a believing servant who has a share of righteousness, who worships his Lord well, and worships Allah in secret. He was hidden among the people so that he was not pointed at by fingers, and his sustenance was sufficient (at subsistence level). So he was patient with it, and death hastened to him, so few were his inheritors and few were his mourners.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man who said, 'Hamza ibn Humran narrated to me saying, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whenever one of you intends goodness, let him not delay it, for the servant sometimes prays the prayer or fasts the day, and it is said to him: Do whatever you wish after it, for Allah has forgiven you.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jameela, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin your day with goodness, and dictate upon your preservers (the Two recording Angels) goodness at its beginning and goodness at its end; He will forgive you for what is between that, if Allah wills.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Murazim ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father used to say: 'When you intend a good deed, hasten to do it, for you do not know what will occur.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah loves from the good deeds that which is hastened.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Bashir ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you intend something of the good, do not delay it, for the servant fasts on a hot day intending what is with Allah, so Allah frees him from the Fire because of it, and do not consider small what you draw near to Allah with, even if it is half a date.

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever intends a good deed, let him hasten to do it and not delay it, for sometimes the servant performs the deed, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: 'I have forgiven you and will not write anything against you ever.' And whoever intends an evil deed, let him not do it, for sometimes the servant performs the evil, so Allah, Glorious is He, sees him and says: 'No, by My Honor and My Majesty, I will not forgive you after it ever.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When you intend for something of the good, do not delay it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may look upon the servant while he is upon something of the obedience, so He says: 'By My Honour and My Majesty! I will not punish you after it, ever!' And when you intend for an evil, do not do it, for indeed He may look upon the servant while he is upon something of the disobedience, so He says: 'By My Honour and My Majesty! I will not forgive you after it, ever!'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When any one of you intends a good deed or maintaining kinship ties, there are two devils with him, one on his right and one on his left; so let him hasten [to act] so that they do not prevent him from that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever intends for something of the goodness, let him hasten it, for in everything there is a delay, for the Satan therein has a glance (opportunity).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah has made the good heavy upon the people of the world, like its heaviness in their scales on the Day of Resurrection; and indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the evil light upon the people of the world, like its lightness in their scales on the Day of Resurrection.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn Hamza, from his grandfather, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say at the end of his sermon: 'Blessed is he who has good character, pure nature, sound inner self, and beautiful outward appearance; who spends his surplus wealth, restrains his surplus speech, and is fair to people with himself.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever guarantees four (matters) for me, I will guarantee for him four houses in Paradise: Spend (in charity) and do not fear poverty, and spread the greeting of peace throughout the world, and leave disputing even if you are right, and be fair to people with yourself.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Jaroud Abu Al-Munzir, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The chief of the deeds are three: Fairness with the people from yourself, until you are not pleased with anything except that you are pleased for them with the like of it; and equalizing with the brother in wealth; and remembering Allah upon every state.' (This remembrance) is not merely saying 'Glory be to Allah, and the Praise is for Allah, and there is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest' alone, but rather, when something comes to you which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has Commanded, you act upon it; or when something comes to you which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has Forbidden, you leave it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Yahya ibn Ahmad, from Abu Muhammad al-Maysami, from Rumayy ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Indeed! The one who is fair with the people from himself, Allah would not increase him in anything except for honour'.

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three are the closest of creation to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Judgment until the Reckoning is concluded: a man whose power does not invite him, in the state of his anger, to wrong those under his authority; and a man who mediates between two parties but does not incline with one against the other by even a barley seed; and a man who speaks the truth regarding what is for him and what is against him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The chief of deeds is fairness with people from yourself, and equalizing with the brother for the sake of Allah, and remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon every state.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Al-Hasan Al-Bazzaz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I inform you of the most difficult of what Allah has imposed upon His creation? Three things.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Fairness with the people from yourself, and equalizing your brother, and remembering Allah in every place.' He said: 'Indeed, I do not mean (merely saying) 'Glory be to Allah, and Praise be to Allah, and there is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest', and even though this is from that, but (rather) remembering Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in every place, when you advance upon obedience or upon disobedience.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Asama, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is not tested with anything more difficult for him than three characteristics from which he is deprived.' It was said, 'And what are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Equalizing in what is in his hand (generosity/spending), and fairness with himself (self-restraint), and remembering Allah frequently. Indeed, I do not mean (merely saying) 'Glory be to Allah' and 'Praise be to Allah' and 'There is no god but Allah', but rather remembering Allah when what is permissible comes to him, and remembering Allah when what is prohibited comes to him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from his grandfather Abi al-Bilad, raising it (to the Prophet), said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he was intending for one of his military expeditions, so he grabbed the reins of his riding animal and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed by which I may enter Paradise.' He said, 'Whatever you love that people should come to you with, go to them with it, and whatever you dislike that people should come to you with, do not go to them with it.' He freed the way of the riding animal.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Abdul-Karim, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Justice is sweeter than the water that quenches the thirsty. How extensive is justice when it is applied in a matter, even if it is little.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is fair with the people from himself, would be pleased with judging for others.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yusuf ibn Imran ibn Maysam, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Adam (peace be upon him): 'I shall summarize the speech for you in four sentences.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, and what are they?' He (Mighty and Majestic) said: 'One for Me, and one for you, and one regarding what is between Me and you, and one regarding what is between you and the people.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, explain them to me so that I may know them.' He (Mighty and Majestic) said: 'As for that which is for Me, worship Me and do not associate anything with Me; and as for that which is for you, I shall recompense you for your deeds with what you will be most in need of; and as for that which is between Me and you, upon you is supplication and upon Me is the response; and as for that which is between you and the people, be pleased for the people with what you are pleased with for yourself, and dislike for them what you dislike for yourself.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Rawh ibn Ukht al-Mu'alla, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Fear Allah and be just, for you find fault with a people who are not just.
From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Justice is sweeter than honey, softer than butter, and more fragrant than musk.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Uthman ibn Jabala, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three characteristics: whoever possesses them, or even one of them, will be in the shade of the Throne of Allah on the Day when there is no shade except His. [They are:] A man who gives people from himself what they ask of him; and a man who does not move forward a step nor backward a step until he knows that this is for the pleasure of Allah; and a man who does not find fault with his Muslim brother for a defect until he removes that defect from his own self, for indeed he does not remove one defect from it except that another defect becomes apparent to him, and sufficient for a man is occupation with his own self [rather than finding fault] with people.'

From him, from Abdul Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Giffari, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who consoles the poor from his wealth, and is fair with the people from himself, so he is a true Believer.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Khalid ibn Nafi', the seller of Al-Sabiri, from Yusuf Al-Bazzaz, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whenever two people dispute over a matter, and one of them gives half to his companion, he does not accept it from him unless he is given more than him (to be just to him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, for Allah is a Garden which none shall enter except for three; one of them being the one who judges regarding himself with the truth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Justice is sweeter than the water that quenches the thirsty. How extensive is justice when it is applied in a matter, even if it is little.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The nobility of the Believer is standing at night (for prayer), and his honour is his self-sufficiency from the people.

And by this chain, from Al-Minqari, from Abdul Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: I saw all goodness gathered in cutting off greed for what is in the hands of people; and whoever does not hope in people for anything and refers his matter to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in all his affairs, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will answer him in everything.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Ayn, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Seeking needs from people is dispossession of honor and departure of bashfulness; and despair of what is in the hands of people is dignity for the believer in his religion, and greed is present poverty.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Write for me to Ismail ibn Dawud the scribe, so that I may attain (some work) from him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I resent for you that you should seek from the likes of this one and his like, but you can count upon my wealth.'

From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Najm ibn Huteym Al-Ghanawy, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Despair of what is in the hands of the people is the honor of the Believer in his religion. Or have you not heard the words of Hatim: 'When you determine upon despair (from the people), you find richness when you recognize the self; and greed is poverty.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say to me: 'Let poverty/neediness towards people and self-sufficiency from them gather in your heart, so that your neediness towards them is in the softness of your speech and the goodness of your countenance, and your self-sufficiency from them is in the purity of your honor and the preservation of your dignity.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, who said: 'Ali ibn Umar narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say, then mentioned something similar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Exalted is His Mention, and fear Allah, by Whom you are asking by Him and the kinship; surely Allah was Ever-Watchful over you. So he said: These are the relationships of the people. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Commanded with their goodly maintenance, and magnified them. Do you not see that He Made it to be from Him?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: He said: It reached me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! My family members refuse except to leap upon me, cut me off, and insult me. So, should I reject them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then Allah will reject you all.' He said: 'So what should I do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintain ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who deprives you, and pardon the one who oppresses you, for when you do that, there will be for you from Allah a supporter.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said: 'A man maintains goodly relations with his relatives, and it so happens that there remains three years from his life, and Allah makes it to become thirty years, and Allah does whatever He so Desires to.'

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Khattab al-Awr, from Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Connecting with the relatives purifies the deeds, increases the wealth, repels the afflictions, eases the Reckoning, and delays the death.'

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from 'Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I bequeath to the present ones of my community and the absent ones from them, and those in the loins of men and the wombs of women until the Day of Resurrection, that they should maintain goodly relationships with the relatives, and even if one of them is at a travel distance of a year, for that is from the Religion.'

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hafs, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Maintaining ties of kinship improves character, makes the hand generous, purifies the soul, increases sustenance, and delays death.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The kinship (al-Rahim) is suspended from the Throne, saying: O Allah! Maintain the relationship with the one who maintains me, and cut off the relationship with the one who cuts me off.' And it is the kinship of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them). And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined.' And the kinship of every person of kin.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The first of the limbs to speak on the Day of Resurrection is the womb (kinship), saying: O Lord! The one who maintained me in the world, maintain what is between You and him; and the one who cut me off in the world, cut off what is between You and him today.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Connect with your relatives, even if it is by a sip of water; and the best of what you can connect with the relatives is keeping harm away from them; and connecting with the relatives delays the death [time] and brings love among the family.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The womb (kinship) is suspended by the Throne on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'O Allah! Maintain the one who maintains me, and cut off the one who cuts me off'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hannan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'The two edges of the Bridge (as-Sirat) on the Day of Resurrection are Kinship (Ar-Rahim) and Trust/Entrustment (Al-Amanah). So when the one who maintains kinship and fulfills the trust passes by, he will pass through to Paradise. And when the betrayer of the trust and the cutter of kinship passes by, no deed will benefit him alongside these two, and the Bridge will fling him into the Fire.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn Qurti, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Maintaining good relations with relatives improves character, makes the hand generous, purifies the soul, increases sustenance, and delays death.

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Khattab al-Awr, from Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintaining ties of kinship purifies deeds, repels afflictions, increases wealth, delays death for him in his lifetime, expands his sustenance, and fosters love among his family members. So let him fear Allah and let him maintain ties with his relatives.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Hakam al-Hannat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Connecting with the relatives and good neighborliness build up the dwellings and increase the lifespans.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The quickest of the rewards for a good deed is for maintaining good relationships with the relatives'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is pleased with the prolongation of his lifespan and the increase in his sustenance, let him maintain good relations with his kin.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) set out intending Basra, he encamped at Al-Rabada. A man from the Muharib tribe came to him and said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have borne the burdens of my people, and I asked among their groups for sympathy and assistance, but their tongues preceded me with criticism. So order them, O Amir al-Mu'minin, to assist me and urge them to sympathize with me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Where are they?' He said, 'Those are a group of them, where you see.' He said, so he spurred his riding animal and it galloped as if it were a male ostrich. Some of his companions galloped in pursuit of it, striving hard but could not catch up. So he arrived at the people, greeted them, and asked them what prevented them from sympathizing with their companion. They complained about him, and he complained about them. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'A man should maintain ties with his clan, for they are most deserving of his kindness and his hand's support. And the clan should maintain ties with its brother if time strikes him hard and the world turns away from him. Indeed, those who maintain ties and exchange favors are rewarded, and those who cut ties and turn away are burdened (with blame). He said, then he sent off his riding animal and said, 'Resolved.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'A man should not turn away from his clan, even if he possesses wealth and children, nor from their affection, their honor, and their defense with their hands and tongues. They are the people most vigilant for him from behind, most compassionate towards him, and most attentive to his needs if a calamity befalls him or some difficulties of affairs descend upon him.' And whoever withholds his hand from his clan, he only withholds one hand from them, but many hands will be withheld from him. And whoever softens his inner circle, his friend will recognize affection from him. And whoever extends his hand with goodness when he finds the opportunity, Allah will replace for him what he spent in his world, and multiply for him in his Hereafter. And a truthful tongue for a person, Allah makes it among the people better than the wealth he consumes and inherits. Let not one of you increase in arrogance and greatness in his own soul, and distance himself from his clan, if he is affluent in wealth. And let not one of you increase in asceticism towards his brother, nor distance himself from him, if he does not see magnanimity from him, and he is needy in wealth. And let not one of you be oblivious to kinship; with it is the need, if one were to cover it with what does not benefit him if he withholds it, nor harm him if he consumes it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hilal, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The family of so-and-so, some of them are righteous with the others and maintain ties (of kinship).' He said: 'Then their wealth will grow and they will grow, and they will not cease to be in that until they cut off (the kinship). So if they do that, it will vanish from them.'

From him, from someone else, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people will be immoral and not righteous, yet they maintain their kinships, so their wealth increases and their lifespans prolong. So how [will it be] if they were righteous and doing righteous deeds?'

And from him, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintain your kinship ties, even if it be with the greeting (as-salam).' Allah, Blessed and High is He, says: 'And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the kinship; surely Allah was Ever-Watchful over you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: There occurred speech between Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn al-Hasan until the clamor arose between them, and the people gathered. So they separated that evening because of that, and I went forth in the morning regarding a need, and behold, I found Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at the door of Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and he was saying: 'O maid! Tell Abu Muhammad to come out.' He said, 'So he came out,' and I said, 'O Abu Abdillah, what made you come so early?' He said, 'I recited a Verse from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, yesterday, so it worried me.' I said, 'And what is it?' He said, 'The Words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is His Mention: Those who join what Allah has Bidden to be joined, and have awe of their Lord, and they are fearing the evil Reckoning.' So he said, 'You speak the truth. It is as if I never read this Verse from the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, at all.' So they both hugged and wept.

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I have a cousin whom I maintain kinship with, but he cuts me off; and I maintain kinship with him, but he cuts me off. To the extent that I have contemplated cutting him off in response to his cutting me off. Do you permit me to cut him off?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you maintain it to him and he cuts you off, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, maintains it with both of you together. And if you cut him off and he cuts you off, Allah will cut off both of you.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I love that Allah should know that I have humbled my neck in maintaining kinship ties, and I hasten to visit my family before they become self-sufficient of me.'

From him, from Al-Washsha, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl al-Sayrafi, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the kinship of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them), the Imams (peace be upon them), is suspended from the Throne, saying: 'O Allah! Maintain relationship with the one who maintains relationship with me, and cut off the one who cuts me off.' Then it flows, after that, in the kinship of the believers. And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the kinship.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: 'Those who join what Allah has Bidden to be joined.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your relatives.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, and Hisham ibn al-Hakam, and Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was revealed regarding the kinship of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and it may also apply to your relatives.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Therefore, do not be among those who say for a thing that it is in one (and the same) thing.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Wassafi, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is pleased if Allah were to extend his lifespan and expand his sustenance, let him maintain goodly relations with his kin, for the kinship has a tongue on the Day of Resurrection, eloquent, saying: O Lord! Maintain relationship with the one who maintained it with me, and cut off the one who cut me off.' So the man would be seen to be on the goodly way, when the kinship that he had cut off comes to him, so it would plunge with him into the lowest depth into the Fire.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Safwan, from Al-Jahm ibn Humayd, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Relatives may be for me who are not upon my command (Wilayah). Do they have a right upon me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the right of kinship. Nothing cuts it off. And if they are upon your command, they have two rights: the right of kinship and the right of Islam.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Verily, maintaining ties of kinship and righteousness ease the Reckoning and protect from sins. So maintain ties with your relatives and be righteous with your brethren, even if it is through good greeting and responding to it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintaining kinship ties lightens the Reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and it is a delayer of the lifespan, and it protects from evil misfortunes; and charity given at night extinguishes the Anger of the Lord.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, maintaining kinship purifies the deeds, increases the wealth, eases the Reckoning, repels the afflictions, and increases the sustenance.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to the parents, good conduct.' What is this good conduct? He said: The good conduct is that you be good in their company, and that you do not burden them to ask you for anything from what they are in need of, even if they are self-sufficient. Is it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love'? He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And as for the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'If either of them or both reach old age with you, do not say to them 'Uff' (a sound of impatience) nor chide them.' He said: 'If they bore you, do not say to them 'Uff' nor chide them even if they hit you.' He said: 'And speak to them a gracious word.' He said: 'If they hit you, say to them both, 'May Allah forgive you both', so that is a gracious word from you.' He said: 'And lower for them the wing of humility from mercy.' He said: 'Do not fill your eyes with looking at them except with mercy and tenderness, and do not raise your voice above their voices, nor your hand above their hands, and do not walk in front of them.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Nafi' al-Bajali, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Do not associate anything with Allah, and even if you are burnt in the fire and punished, your heart should remain at rest with faith; and your parents, so obey them and be righteous to them, whether they are alive or dead; and if they order you to leave your family and your wealth, do so, for that is from faith."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: On the Day of Resurrection, something like a globe will come, so it will push the believer in the back and enter him into Paradise, and it will be said: 'This is righteousness.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked, 'Which deed is the most superior?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Prayer at its proper time, and righteousness with the parents, and striving in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'What is the right of the father upon his son?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Not calling him by his name, and not walking in front of him, and not sitting before him, and not letting him be insulted (by anyone).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: And I was in his presence when Abdul Wahid al-Ansari asked him about the righteousness to the parents, regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to the parents, good treatment,' so we thought that it was the Verse which is among the Children of Israel: 'And your Lord has decreed that you shall not worship except Him, and to the parents, good treatment.' So when it was later I asked him, so he said: 'It is that which is in Luqman: 'And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents, and if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them.' He said: 'Indeed, that is greater than Him commanding with maintaining ties with them and their rights upon every state, and if they strive with you that you should associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge.' So he said: 'No, but He commands with maintaining ties with them, and even if they strive with him for shirk, their right does not increase except in greatness.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents one of you from being righteous with his parents, whether alive or dead? He can pray on their behalf, give charity on their behalf, perform Hajj on their behalf, and fast on their behalf. Thus, that which he does for them will be done for him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will increase him, due to his righteousness and kinship, with much good.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khalid, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Should I supplicate for my parents if they do not recognize the truth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Supplicate for them and give charity on their behalf; and if they are alive and do not recognize the truth, then circle around them (be patient and gentle with them), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah sent me with mercy, not with ingratitude (or disobedience).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, whom should I be most righteous with?' He said, 'Your mother.' He said, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your mother.' He said, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your mother.' He said, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your father.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I am eager for jihad and am active.' He said to him, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'So perform jihad in the way of Allah, for if you are killed, you will be alive with Allah, being provided for; and if you die, your reward has been established by Allah; and if you return, you will return from sins as you were born.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have two elderly parents who claim they are comforted by me and they dislike my going out.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'So stay content with your parents, and by the One in Whose hand is my soul, their being comforted by you for a day and a night is better than a year of jihad.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, all from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ammar ibn Hayyan, who said: I informed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the righteousness of my son Ismail towards me, so he said: 'I used to love him, and now I have increased my love for him. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had a sister from breastfeeding come to him. When he looked at her, he was pleased with her, and he spread his cloak for her and seated her upon it. Then he turned to converse with her and smiled in her face. Then she arose and went away, and her brother came. But he did not do with him what he had done with her. So it was said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah! You did with his sister what you did not do with him, and he is a man.' So he said: 'Because she was more righteous with her parents than him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ibrahim ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My father has aged significantly and weakened, so we carry him when he has the need.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you have the capacity to attend to that from him, then do so, and feed him morsels with your hand, for it will be a shield for you tomorrow.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu al-Subbah, from Jabir, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have two parents who are non-Muslims (or adversaries).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Be righteous to both of them, just as you are righteous to the Muslims who are not among those who love us.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Three (matters) Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not grant an allowance (rukhsah) for anyone regarding them: paying back the trust to the righteous and the immoral, and fulfilling the covenant with the righteous and the immoral, and being righteous to the parents, whether they were righteous or immoral.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is from the Sunnah and the righteousness that a man should be known by his father's name (teknonymy).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, all from al-Wasshash from Ahmad ibn A'iz from Abi Khadija Salim ibn Mukarram from Mu'alla ibn Khunays from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came and asked the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) about righteousness with the parents, so he said: 'Be righteous with your mother, be righteous with your mother, be righteous with your mother, be righteous with your father, be righteous with your father, be righteous with your father,' and he began with the mother before the father.

Al-Washa' narrated from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abu Khadeeja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I had a daughter, and I raised her until she reached maturity. I dressed her in new clothes and adorned her with jewelry, then I brought her to a well and pushed her into its depths. The last thing I heard from her was her saying, 'O father!' So what is the expiation for that?' He (peace be upon him and his family) asked, 'Do you have a living mother?' He said, 'No.' He asked, 'Do you have a living maternal aunt?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So be righteous to her, for she is in the position of the mother. It will be an expiation for you for what you did.' Abu Khadeeja said, 'So I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When was this?'' He said, 'It was in the period of Ignorance (pre-Islamic era), and they used to kill their daughters out of fear that they would be captured as captives and give birth among other people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hannan ibn Sadeyr, from his father who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Can the son suffice [in repaying the debt of duty] to his father?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no sufficing for him except in two characteristics: if the father is an owned slave, so his son buys him and frees him, or if there are debts upon him, so he (the son) fulfils them on his behalf.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabr, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I am a young, active man and I love Jihad, and I have a mother who dislikes that.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Return and be with your mother, for by the One who sent me with the Truth as a Prophet, your comforting her for one night is better than your Jihad in the Way of Allah for a year.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the servant may be righteous to his parents during their lifetime, then they die, but he does not pay off their debts on their behalf, nor seeks forgiveness for them, so Allah writes him as unrighteous; and indeed, he may be unrighteous to them during their lifetime, not being righteous with them, but when they die, he pays off their debt and seeks forgiveness for them, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes him as righteous.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Ali ibn Maysara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, the seed of the believer may reside in the loins of the polytheist man, and no evil shall befall it; until when it transfers to the womb of the polytheist woman, no evil befalls her; until she gives birth to him. And when she gives birth to him, no evil befalls him until the Pen flows upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: 'I have felt compassionate concern about the curse of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) against Yaqteen and what he fathered.' So he said: 'O Abu al-Hasan! It is not as you suppose. The believer in the loins of a disbeliever is like a pebble in a mud brick. The rain comes and washes away the mud brick, but does not harm the pebble in the slightest.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He who awakens in the morning not being concerned with the affairs of the Muslims is not a Muslim.'

And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The most diligent of the people in rituals is the one most sincere in advising them, and the most submissive of them in hearts to the entirety of the Muslims.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Upon you is with the advising among His creatures, for you will never meet Him with a deed more superior than it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is not concerned with the affairs of the Muslims is not a Muslim.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The creation are the dependants of Allah, so the most beloved of the creation to Allah is the one who benefits the dependants of Allah and brings joy to a family.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat, from Fit'r ibn Khalifa, from Umar ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repels from a group of Muslims an adversity of water or fire, Paradise is obligated for him.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'aba ibn Maymun, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And speak to the people good words,' he said: 'Speak good to the people and do not say anything except good, until you know what it is.'

From him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jameela Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And speak to the people good words', he said: 'Speak to the people the best of what you love to be said about yourselves'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And He made me blessed wherever I was,' he said: 'Beneficial (to the people).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the respecting of Allah is the respecting the Muslim with old age.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not from us, the one who does not revere our elderly and show mercy to our young ones.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Aban, from Al-Wassafi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Revere your elders, and maintain ties with your relatives, and you do not maintain ties with them with anything better than refraining from causing them harm.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believers are truly brothers, sons of one father and one mother, and when a vein (of worry/sweat) is struck upon one of them, the others stay awake (in vigil/concern) for him.'

From him, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: I gathered myself in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be your ransom! Sometimes I feel grief without a calamity befalling me or a matter descending upon me, to the extent that my family and my close friend recognize that in my face.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, O Jabir! Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the believers from the clay of Paradise and caused a spirit from His Spirit to flow among them. Therefore, the believer is a brother to the believer, like his father and mother. So if a spirit from those spirits in a city from the cities is struck by grief, this one is grieved because it is from them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believer is the brother of the believer, his eye and his guide; he does not betray him, nor oppress him, nor deceive him, nor promise him a promise then break it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believer is the brother of the believer, like one single body. If one part of it complains, the pain of that is felt in the rest of its body; and their spirits are from one spirit, and indeed the spirit of the believer is more intensely connected to the Spirit of Allah than the connection of the rays of the sun to it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he is his eye, his mirror, and his guide. He does not betray him, nor deceive him, nor oppress him, nor lie to him, nor backbite him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and a man came to him. So he said to me: 'Do you love him?' I said, 'Yes.' He said to me: 'And why should you not love him, while he is your brother, and your partner in your religion, and your helper against your enemy, whereas his sustenance is upon someone else?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Urama from one of his companions from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Fudayl from Abu Hamza from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believer is a brother to the believer of his father and his mother, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the believers from the clay of the Gardens, and caused to flow into their forms from the wind of Paradise; therefore, they are brothers of a father and a mother.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The believer is the brother of the believer, his eye and his guide; he does not betray him, nor oppress him, nor deceive him, nor promise him a promise and then break it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a man, from Jameel, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believers are servants to one another.' I said: 'And how can they be servants to one another?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One benefits the other through the Hadith.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail al-Basri, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A number of Muslims went out on a journey, and they lost the way, so intense thirst struck them. They enshrouded themselves and stayed by the bases of the trees. Then an old man came to them, wearing white clothes, and said, Arise, for there is no harm upon you, for this is water. So they arose, drank, and were quenched. They said, 'Who are you? May Allah have mercy on you.' He said, 'I am from the Jinn who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: The believer is the brother of the believer, his eye, and his guide. Thus, you did not become wasted in my presence.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A Muslim is a brother of a Muslim; he does not oppress him, nor abandon him, nor backbite him, nor deceive him, nor deprive him.' Rabie said: 'A man from our companions asked me in Al-Madina, saying, "I heard Fuzayl saying that." I said to him, "Yes." He said, "For I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A Muslim is a brother of a Muslim; he does not oppress him, nor deceive him, nor abandon him, nor backbite him, nor betray him, nor deprive him."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: You have not yet established brotherhood upon this matter, but rather you are being recognised upon it.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan and Sama'ah, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: You are not yet establishing brotherhood upon this matter, but rather you are being recognised upon it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: From the rights of a believer upon his brother the believer is that he satiates his hunger, and covers his nakedness, and relieves him from his distress, and pays off his debt. So when he dies, he takes his place among his family and children.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr al-Hajari, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the right of the Muslim upon the Muslim?' He said to me, 'There are seven obligatory rights. From them, there is no right except that it is obligatory upon him. If he wastes any of them, he exits from the Wilayah of Allah and His obedience, and there is no share for Allah in him.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what are they?' He said, 'O Mu'alla! I am affectionate towards you. I fear that you will waste (them) and not preserve, and you will learn but not act.' I said to him, 'There is no strength except with Allah.' He said: 'The easiest of them is that you love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. And the second right is that you avoid his anger, follow his pleasure, and obey his command. And the third right is that you support him with your self, your wealth, your tongue, your hand, and your leg.' And the fourth right is that you become his eye, his guide, and his mirror. And the fifth right is that you are not satiated while he is hungry, nor you quenched while he is thirsty, nor you clothed while he is naked. And the sixth right is that if you have a servant and your brother does not have a servant, it is obligatory that you send your servant so he washes his clothes, prepares his food, and spreads his bed. And the seventh right is that you fulfill his oath, answer his call, visit his sick, and attend his funeral. And when you know that he has a need, you hasten to fulfill it, and do not force him to ask you for it, but you hasten with a hastening. So when you do that, your Wilayah is linked with his Wilayah, and his Wilayah with your Wilayah.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf, from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, who said: Some of our companions wrote, asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about certain matters, and instructed me to ask him about the right of the Muslim upon his brother. So I asked him, but he did not answer me. When I came to bid him farewell, I said, 'I asked you, but you did not answer me.' He said, 'I fear that you will be disbelieving. Indeed, among the most difficult of what Allah has imposed upon His creatures are three: The fairness of a man towards himself, until he is pleased for his brother from himself only with what he is pleased for his own self from him; and the sharing of wealth with the brother; and the remembrance of Allah in every state—not merely saying 'Glory be to Allah' and 'Praise be to Allah', but when Allah prohibits something for him, he leaves it.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Murazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah has not been worshipped with anything more superior than the fulfilling of the rights of the believer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The right of a Muslim upon a Muslim is that he should not be satiated while his brother is hungry, nor be quenched while his brother is thirsty, nor be clothed while his brother is naked. So how great is the right of a Muslim upon his Muslim brother. And he (peace be upon him) said: Love for your Muslim brother what you love for yourself. And when you are in need, ask him, and if he asks you, give to him. Do not grow weary of doing good to him, nor should he grow weary of doing good to you. Be a backer for him, for he is a backer for you. When he is absent, protect him in his absence, and when he is present, visit him, honor him, and respect him, for he is from you and you are from him. So if there is a grievance against you, do not part from him until you ask for his pardon. And if good befalls him, praise Allah, and if he is afflicted, support him, and if he is delayed (in paying debt), assist him. And when a man says to his brother 'Uff' (a sound of impatience), the Wilayah between them is cut off. And when he says 'You are my enemy', one of them has disbelieved. And when he slanders him, faith dissolves in his heart just as salt dissolves in water. And he (peace be upon him) said: It reached me that he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the believer's light shines for the people of the sky just as the stars of the sky shine for the people of the earth. And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the believer is the friend of Allah; Allah assists him and works for him, and he does not speak against him except with truth, nor does he fear anyone other than Him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: For a Muslim upon his Muslim brother, from the rights, is that he greets him when he meets him, and visits him when he is sick, and advises him when he is absent, and says 'Yarhamuk Allah' when he sneezes, and answers him when he invites him, and follows him (in funeral) when he dies. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Ma'mun al-Harithi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the right of the believer upon the believer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the rights of the believer upon the believer is affection for him in his chest, and sharing in his wealth, and taking care of his family in his absence, and helping him against whoever oppresses him, and if there were spoils distributed among the Muslims and he was absent, to take his share for him, and when he dies, to visit his grave.' And that he should not oppress him, and not deceive him, and not betray him, and not abandon him, and not belittle him, and not say 'Uff' to him. And if he says 'Uff' to him, then there is no Wilayah (bond of affinity) between them. And if he says to him, 'You are my enemy,' then one of the two has disbelieved. And if he suspects him, faith dissolves in his heart just as salt dissolves in water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ali Sahib al-Killal, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I was performing Tawaf with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and a man from our companions presented himself to me, asking me to go with him for a need. He gestured to me, and I disliked leaving Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) to go to him. While I was performing Tawaf, he gestured to me again. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saw him and said, 'O Aban, is this one wanting you?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Who is he?' I said, 'A man from our companions.' He said, 'He is upon the same status as you.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So go to him.' I said, 'Should I cut the Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And even if it is the Obligatory Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So I went with him, then I returned to him afterwards and asked him, saying, 'Inform me about the right of a believer upon a believer.' He said, 'O Aban, leave it, do not reiterate it.' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you,' but I did not cease reiterating upon him. He said, 'O Aban, would you share half of your wealth with him?' Then he looked at me and saw what had entered my mind, and said, 'O Aban, do you not know that Allah (Exalted and Majestic) has mentioned those who prefer others over themselves?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'But when you share half with him, you have not preferred him; rather, you and he are equal. You prefer him only when you give him from the other half.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah ibn Ayoub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), along with Ibn Abu Yafour and Abdullah ibn Talha. So he began by saying to him: 'O Ibn Abu Yafour!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Six characteristics, whoever possesses them will be in front of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and on the right of Allah.' Ibn Abu Yafour said: 'And what are they? May I be sacrificed for you.' A Muslim man should love for his brother what he loves for the dearest of his family, and a Muslim man should dislike for his brother what he dislikes for the dearest of his family, and advise him regarding Wilayah. So Ibn Abu Yafour wept and said: 'And how should he advise him regarding Wilayah?' He said: 'O Ibn Abu Yafour! When he is at that station, his concern is his primary focus. So he rejoices in his joy if he rejoices, and grieves in his grief if he grieves. And if he has something that can relieve him, he relieves him; otherwise, he supplicates to Allah for him.' He said: Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three are for you and three are for us: that you recognize our merit, and tread upon our heels (follow us closely), and await our outcome.' So whoever is like this will be in front of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and those who are below them will be illuminated by their light. And as for those on the right of Allah, if those below them were to see them, life would not be pleasant for them due to what they see of their merit. So Ibn Abu Yafour said: 'And what is the matter with them that they do not see them, while they are on the right of Allah?' He said: 'O Ibn Abu Yafour! They are veiled by the Light of Allah. Has not the hadith reached you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'Indeed, for Allah there are creatures on the right of the Throne, in front of Allah and on the right of Allah.' Their faces are whiter than snow and brighter than the shining sun. The questioner asks, 'Who are these?' So it is said, 'These are those who loved each other for the Majesty of Allah.'

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). A man entered, greeted, and he (peace be upon him) asked him: 'How are those from your brothers whom you left behind?' He said, 'They praised well, were praised, and extolled.' He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'How is the visiting/consolation of their rich ones towards their poor ones?' He said, 'Little.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And how is the observation/consideration of their rich ones towards their poor ones?' He said, 'Little.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So how is the connection/relating of their rich ones to their poor ones with regards to what is in their hands?' He said, 'You are mentioning manners; little is what it is among those in our presence.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So how do you claim about them that they are Shia?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Abu Ismail, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Shias in our presence are numerous.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'So do the rich show kindness to the poor, and do the righteous overlook the faults of the sinners, and do they help each other?' I said, 'No.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Those are not Shias. The Shia is the one who does this.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn Fuzayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Magnify your companions and revere them, and let not some of you scowl at others, nor harm one another, nor envy one another. And beware of stinginess; be the sincere worshippers of Allah.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Umar ibn Aban, from Sa'id ibn al-Hasan, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Does one of you come to his brother, insert his hand into his purse, take what he needs, and he does not repel him?' I said: 'I do not know that among us.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Then there is nothing [to worry about].' I said: 'Then [it is] destruction?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Surely the people have not yet been given their forbearance [or wisdom/insight].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Urama, raising it from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the right of the believer, so he said: 'Seventy rights. I will not inform you of all of them, but only seven, for I am sympathetic towards you, fearing that you will not be able to bear them.' So I said, 'Yes, if Allah wills.' He said: 'You should not be satiated while he is hungry, nor be clothed while he is bare; you should be his guide, his shirt which he wears, and his tongue which he speaks with; you should love for him what you love for yourself; and if you have a maid, you should send her to prepare his bed and attend to his needs by night and day. So when you do that, your Wilayah is linked with our Wilayah, and our Wilayah is linked with the Wilayah of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not oppress him, nor abandon him, nor betray him. And it is incumbent upon the Muslims to strive in maintaining connection, to cooperate in sympathy, and to provide relief to those in need, and for some to show sympathy to others, until they become as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded you: 'Merciful among yourselves, showing mutual mercy, grieving for what is hidden from you regarding their affairs,' in the manner that the group of the Ansar used to be during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is a right upon the Muslim that when he intends to travel, he should inform his brothers, and it is a right upon his brothers that when he returns, they should visit him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to his companions: 'Fear Allah and become righteous brothers, loving one another for the sake of Allah, maintaining ties, showing mercy, visiting each other, meeting, and remembering our matter (Wilayah), and reviving it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Kuleyb al-Saydawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Link (with each other), and do good and be compassionate, and become righteous brothers just as Allah Mighty and Majestic Commanded (you all to be).

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Link (You should) maintain ties (of kinship), and be affectionate, and show mercy, and be sympathetic.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is incumbent upon the Muslims to strive in connecting with one another, to cooperate in showing sympathy, and to assist those in need, and for some to show sympathy to others, until they become as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded you: merciful among yourselves, mutually compassionate, and grieving for what is hidden from you of their affairs, just as the group of the Ansar used to be in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who visits his brother for the Sake of Allah, not for anything else, seeking the Promise of Allah and accomplishing what is in the Presence of Allah, Allah would allocate seventy thousand Angels calling out to him: 'Indeed! You have done well, and the Paradise is (Made to be) better for you'.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Khaysama who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to bid him farewell, so he said: 'O Khaysama!' Deliver the greetings to those of our mawali (clients/followers) you see, and advise them with the fear of Allah the Magnificent, and that their rich ones should support their poor ones, and their strong ones their weak ones, and that their living ones should attend the funeral of their dead ones, and that they should meet up in their houses, for the meeting of some of them with others is a revival of our matter. May Allah have mercy on a servant who revives our matter. O Khaysama!
