Deliver to our mawali that we will not make them needless of anything from Allah except through deeds, and that they will not attain our Wilayah except through piety (war''), and that the people most full of regret on the Day of Resurrection will be the one who ascribed justice, then opposed it to something else.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) narrated that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down an angel to the earth. So that angel walked until he came to a door where a man was seeking permission from the owner of the house. The angel said to him: 'What is your need to the owner of this house?' He said: 'A Muslim brother of mine, whom I visited for the sake of Allah, Blessed and High'. The angel said to him: 'Did nothing bring you except that?' He said: 'Nothing brought me except that.' He said: 'I am a messenger of Allah to you, and He conveys greetings to you and says: Paradise is obligated for you'. And the angel said: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever visits a Muslim, it is not him that he is visiting, but he is visiting Me, and his reward upon Me is Paradise'.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Al Nahdy, from Al Husayn, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who visits his brother for the Sake of Allah, Allah Mighty and Majestic Says: “It is I you have visited, and your Reward is upon Me, and I shall not be Pleased for you as a Reward, (anything) less than the Paradise”.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who visits his brother in the outskirts of the city seeking the Face of Allah, so he is visiting Him, and it is a right upon Allah that He honours His visitor.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to him: You are My guest and you are visiting Me; upon Me is your reward, and I have obligated Paradise for you due to your love for him.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Ghurrah, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever visits his brother for the sake of Allah, during illness or health, not coming to him for deception nor for reciprocal exchange, Allah will assign to him seventy thousand angels who will call out behind him: You have done well, and Paradise is made better for you, for you are visitors of Allah, and you are a delegation of the Beneficent, until he arrives at his house.' So Yūsayr said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! And even if the place is distant?' He said: 'Yes, O Yūsayr, and even if the place is a year's journey, for Allah is Generous and the angels are numerous; they will escort him until he returns to his house.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn al-Nahdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits his brother for the sake of Allah and for Allah, will come on the Day of Resurrection striding between gowns of light, and not pass by anything except that it shines for him, until he stands before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to him: 'Welcome!' And when He says 'Welcome', Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will bestow upon him abundant gifts.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Bashir, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when the Muslim servant goes out from his house to visit his brother for the sake of Allah, not for anything else, seeking the Face of Allah with desire for what is with Him, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, assigns to him seventy thousand angels who call out to him from behind until he returns to his house: 'Indeed, you have done well, and Paradise is made better for you.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: No Muslim visits his Muslim brother for the sake of Allah and for Allah's sake, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls out to him: 'O visitor! You have done well, and Paradise is made sweet/better for you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a Garden which none enter except for three: a man who ruled against himself with the truth, and a man who visited his believing brother for the sake of Allah, and a man who preferred his believing brother for the sake of Allah.

Salih ibn Uqba from Uqba from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The visitation of the believer for the sake of Allah is better than freeing ten believing women, and whoever frees a believing woman, every limb protects a limb from the Fire, to the extent that the private part protects the private part.

Salih ibn 'Uqba, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whenever three believers gather in the presence of a brother of theirs, feeling secure of his actions, not fearing his ravages, and hoping for what is with Him, if they supplicate to Allah, He answers them; and if they ask, He gives them; and if they request increase, He increases for them; and if they remain silent, He initiates (with a gift).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, who said: I heard Abu Hamza saying, 'I heard Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever visits his believing brother for the sake of Allah, not for anything else, seeking by it the reward of Allah and the fulfillment of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seventy thousand angels from the time he leaves his house until he returns to it, calling out to him: "Indeed, you have done well, and Paradise is made better for you; you have taken a dwelling in Paradise."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Meeting the brethren is a great gain, even if they are few.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Ubaydah who said: I was a travel companion of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and I used to begin with mounting (the animal), then he (peace be upon him) would mount. So when we were both settled, he (peace be upon him) would greet and ask questions like a man who had no prior pact with his companion, and shake hands. He (the narrator) said, 'And it was so that whenever we descended, he (peace be upon him) descended before me. So when I and he were both established upon the ground, he (peace be upon him) would greet and ask questions like the one who had no pact with his companion.' So I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)! You are doing something which no one has done before us, and if you were to do it once, so it would be a lot.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know what is in the handshake? The two believers meet, so one of them shakes the hand of his companion, so the sins do not cease to fall from them both just as the leaves fall from the tree, and Allah (exalted is He) looks at it (the handshake) until they both separate.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when two believers meet and shake hands, Allah inserts His Hand between their hands, and shakes the hand of the one who loves his companion more intensely.

Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ayoub, from Al-Samyda, from Malik ibn Ayn al-Juhani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, inserts His Hand between their two hands and turns His Face towards the one who loves his companion more intensely. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turns His Face upon them both, the sins fall away from them just as leaves fall from the tree.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Ubeyda al-Hazza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when two believers meet and shake hands, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turns His Face towards them, and the sins fall from them just as leaves fall from the tree.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda', who said: I traveled with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a section of the carriage from Medina to Mecca. So he descended in one of the roads. When he had fulfilled his need and returned, he said: 'Give me your hand, O Abu Ubayda!' So I handed him my hand, and he pressed it until I felt the pressure/pain in my fingers. Then he said: 'O Abu Ubayda! There is no Muslim who meets his Muslim brother, shakes his hand, and twines his fingers with his fingers, except that their sins fall away from them just as the leaves fall from the tree on an autumn day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halbi, from Malik al-Juhni, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Malik! You are our Shia. Do you not see that you are exaggerating in our matter? Indeed, one cannot describe the attributes of Allah; so just as one cannot describe the attributes of Allah, similarly one cannot describe our attributes. And just as one cannot describe our attributes, similarly one cannot describe the attributes of the believer.' Indeed, when a believer meets a believer and shakes his hand, Allah does not cease to look at them, and sins fall from their faces just as leaves fall from the tree, until they part. So how can one describe the attributes of one who is like that?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I traveled with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). We unloaded our riding animals, then he walked a little. Then he came back, took my hand, and pressed it with a firm press. I said, 'May I be your ransom! Was I not with you in the carriage?' He said, 'Do you not know that when a believer walks a lap (or travels a distance) and then takes the hand of his brother, Allah looks at them both with His Face, and does not cease to face them with His Face, and says to their sins: 'Fall off from them!' So they fall off, O Abu Hamza, just as the leaves fall from the tree. Thus, they separate, and there is no sin upon either of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the limit of the handshake, so he said: 'A circle of a palm tree'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Amr ibn al-Afraq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is befitting for the two believers that when one of them is hidden from his companion by a tree, then they meet, they should shake hands.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from his father, from Uthman ibn Zayd, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you meets his brother, let him greet him and shake his hand, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, honored the angels with that, so do as the angels do.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Baqqah, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you meet each other, greet one another with salutations and handshakes; and when you separate, separate with seeking forgiveness.'

From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from his grandfather Muawiya ibn Wahb, or someone else, from Razin, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Muslims, when they went on military expedition with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and passed by a place with many trees, then went out to the open space, some of them would look at each other and shake hands.

From him, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Zayd ibn al-Jahm al-Hilali, from Malik ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man shakes the hand of his companion, the one who necessitates the handshake has greater reward than the one who waits (for it). Indeed, and the sins fall away between them until no sin remains.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he looked at me with a frowning face. So I said, 'What is that which caused you to change towards me?' He said: 'That which changed you towards your brethren. It reached me, O Is'haq, that you seated a doorman at your door who repels the poor Shias from you.' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I fear the publicity.' So he said: 'So are you not afraid of the calamity? And do you not know that when two believers meet and shake hands, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends down Mercy upon them both? And it is so that ninety-nine (parts) is for the one who more intensely loves his companion. So when they are concordant, the Mercy submerges them. So when they are seated discussing, the preserving Angels say to each other: 'Let us depart, for perhaps there is a private matter for them, and Allah has Veiled upon them'.' So I said, 'Isn't Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'He utters not a word but there is by him a watcher at hand'?' So he said: 'O Is'haq! If it was so that the preservers do not hear, so the Knower of the secrets Hears and Sees.'

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ayman ibn Muhriz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not shake the hand of a man at all and withdraw his hand until he was the one who withdrew his hand from him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described, and how can He be described? And He said in His Book: 'And they did not estimate Allah with the estimation that is due to Him,' so He would not be described with any estimation except that it would be less than that. And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) cannot be described, and how can one describe a servant whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has veiled with seven (veils), and made obedience to him on earth like obedience to Him in the sky? So He said: 'And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and from whatever he forbids you, keep back,' and 'Whoever obeys this one has obeyed Me, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Me,' and He delegated authority to him. And we cannot be described, and how can one describe a group of people whom Allah has removed the filth from, and it is doubt? And the believer cannot be described. And indeed, when a believer meets his brother and shakes his hand, Allah does not cease looking at them both, and sins fall from their faces just as leaves fall from the tree.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Fuzayl ibn Usman, from Abu Ubayda, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah turns His Face towards them both, and the sins fall away from their faces until they separate.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Shake hands, for it removes the grudges (or enmity).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) met Hudhayfa. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) extended his hand, but Hudhayfa withheld his hand. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Hudhayfa! I extended my hand to you, but you withheld your hand from me.' Hudhayfa said: 'O Messenger of Allah! In your hand is the desire (to greet me), but I was in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), so I did not like my hand to touch your hand while I was junub.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do you not know that when two Muslims meet and shake hands, their sins fall off just as the leaves of the tree fall off?'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, no one can estimate His worth; and likewise, no one can estimate the worth of His Prophet; and likewise, no one can estimate the worth of the believer. When he meets his brother and shakes his hand, Allah looks at both of them, and the sins fall from their faces until they part, just as the strong wind causes the leaves to fall from the tree.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Rifa'ah, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The handshake of the believer is superior to the handshake of the angels.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for you is a light by which you are recognized in the world, to the extent that when one of you meets his brother, he kisses him in the place of the light from his forehead.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The head of no one is to be kissed, nor his hand, except the hand of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), or whoever is intended to be the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by it.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Zayd Al Narsy, from Ali Bin Mazeyd a companion of Al Sabiri who said: I went over to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I took his hand and I kissed it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'But it is not correct except for a Prophet (peace be upon him) or a successor (peace be upon him) of a Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Extend your hand to me so I may kiss it.' So he extended it to me. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, your head as well.' So he did. I kissed it. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, your legs as well.' He said, 'I have sworn, I have sworn, I have sworn' three times; 'And there remains something, there remains something, there remains something.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever kisses for the sake of kinship, a relative, there is nothing upon him (no specific ruling or restriction), and the kiss of the brother is on the cheek, and the kiss of the Imam is between his eyes.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever pleases a believer, he has pleased me, and whoever pleases me, he has pleased Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from a man from the people of Kufa known as Abu Muhammad, from Amr ibn Shimmer, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The smile of a man in the face of his brother is a good deed, and removing the speck (of dust/annoyance) from him is a good deed, and nothing is more beloved to Allah than causing gladness to enter upon the believer.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ubaydullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to His servant Moses (peace be upon him) was that He said: 'For Me there are servants whom I will make permissible [to enter] My Paradise and make them rulers therein.' He said: 'O Lord, and who are these whom You make permissible to enter Your Paradise and make them rulers therein?' He said: 'The one who causes gladness to enter a believer.' Then he said: 'There was a believer who was in the kingdom of a tyrant, and he was terrified of him, so he fled from him to the domain of polytheism, and lodged with a man from the people of polytheism, so he shaded him, was kind to him, and entertained him.' So when death came to him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'By My Honor and My Majesty! If there were a dwelling for you in My Paradise, I would have settled you in it. But it is prohibited upon the one who dies having associated [partners] with Me. But, O Fire, settle down and do not harm him!' And his sustenance would be brought to him at the two ends of the day.' I said, 'From Paradise?' He said, 'From wherever Allah wills.'

From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most beloved of deeds to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is causing gladness to enter upon the believers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah Mighty and Majestic revealed to Dawood (peace be upon him): 'A servant from My servants comes to Me with a good deed, so I grant him My Paradise.' Dawood (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, and what is that good deed?' He said: 'Causing gladness to enter upon My believing servant, even if it be by giving a date.' Dawood (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, it is true for the one who knows You that he does not cut off his hope from You.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One of you should not think that when he causes gladness to enter upon a believer, he has done so for him alone. No, by Allah, it is for us as well. And by Allah, it is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) as well.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The most beloved of deeds to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is causing gladness to enter upon a believer: satisfying a Muslim's hunger or fulfilling his debt.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn ibn Mahboub, from Sadeer al-Sayrafi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in a lengthy Hadith: When Allah resurrects the believer from his grave, a resemblance (image) comes out with him, walking in front of him. Every time the believer sees a horror from the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, the resemblance says to him, 'Do not panic and do not grieve, and receive glad tidings of joy and honor from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' Until he stands before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so He reckons him with an easy reckoning, and commands that he be taken to Paradise, and the resemblance is in front of him. So the believer says to him, 'May Allah have mercy on you! What a good exit it was that you came out with me from my grave, and you have not ceased giving me glad tidings of joy and honor from Allah, until I saw that.' And he says, 'Who are you?' So it says, 'I am the joy which you caused to enter upon your believer brother in the world. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created me from it to give you glad tidings.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Jamhour, who said: Al-Najjashy was a man from the landowners, working as an administrator over Ahvaz and Fars. So one of the people of his workforce said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'In the register of Al-Najjashy, there is taxation due upon me, and he is a believer who follows your obedience. So if you see fit, write for me a letter to him.' He said: So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Cause gladness to your brother, Allah will cause you gladness.' He said: So when the letter reached him, he entered upon him while he was in his gathering. So when he was alone, he handed him the letter and said: 'This is the letter of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).' So he kissed it and placed it upon his eyes, and said to him: 'What is your need?' He said: 'Taxation upon me in your register.' So he said to him: 'And how much is it?' He said: 'Ten thousand Dirhams.' So he called his scribe and instructed him to pay it off for him. Then he released him from it and ordered that it be recorded for him for the next year. Then he said to him: 'Have I gladdened you?' So he said: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' Then he ordered for him a mount and a maid and a slave, and ordered for him a set of clothes. During all of that, he was saying to him: 'Have I gladdened you?' So he was saying: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' So, every time he said 'Yes', he increased for him until he was finished. Then he said to him: 'Carry away the furnishings of this room in which you were seated when you handed over to me the letter of my Master which you brought to me, and raise your needs to me.' He said: So he did and the man went out. So the man came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) after that and narrated to him the story in its entirety. So he (the Imam) became joyful with what was done. So the man said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! It is as if he has caused you to be glad, what he did with me.' So he (the Imam) said: 'Yes, by Allah! Allah and His Messenger have indeed been gladdened.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Mansur, from Ammar ibn Abi al-Yaqzan, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the right of the believer upon the believer.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The right of the believer upon the believer is greater than that. If I were to narrate it to you, you would disbelieve. Indeed, when the believer comes out from his grave, a likeness (mithal) comes out with him from his grave, saying to him, 'Receive glad tidings of prestige from Allah and joy.' So he says to it, 'May Allah give you glad tidings of goodness.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then it goes with him, giving him glad tidings of the like of what I said. And whenever he passes by a horror, it says, 'This is not for you'; and whenever he passes by a goodness, it says, 'This is for you'. So it does not cease to be with him, reassuring him from what he fears, and giving him glad tidings of what he likes, until it stands with him in front of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' So when He commands him to Paradise, the likeness says to him, 'Receive glad tidings, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you to Paradise.' He says, 'Who are you? May Allah have mercy on you. You have been giving me glad tidings from when I came out from my grave, and you comforted me on my way, and informed me about my Lord.' He says, 'I am the Joy which you used to cause to enter upon your brethren in the world. I was created from it to give you glad tidings, and to comfort your loneliness.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal — similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-H ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most beloved of deeds to Allah is the joy/pleasure that you cause to enter upon the believer, removing his hunger from him or relieving his distress from him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever brings gladness to a believer, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, creates from that gladness a creature. It meets him at his death and says to him, 'Receive glad tidings, O friend of Allah, with a favor from Allah and pleasure.' Then it does not cease to be with him until it enters his grave [meeting him], and it says to him the like of that. So when he is resurrected, it meets him and says to him the like of that. Then it does not cease to be with him at every horror, giving him glad tidings and saying to him the like of that. So he says to it, 'Who are you? May Allah have mercy on you.' So it says, 'I am the gladness which you brought upon so-and-so.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: A man was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he recited this Verse: 'And those who hurt the believing men and the believing women without them being deserving of it, they are guilty indeed of a false accusation and a manifest sin.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is the Reward for the one who causes the gladness to enter upon him?' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Ten good deeds.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, by Allah, and a thousand, thousand (million) good deeds.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Ali ibn Yahya, from Al-Walid ibn Al-'Ala', from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who causes gladness to enter upon a believer, he has caused it to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and the one who causes it to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he has linked that to Allah (Exalted is He); and similarly, the one who causes distress to enter upon him (the believer).

From him, from Ismail ibn Mansur, from Al-Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Any Muslim who meets a Muslim and gladdens him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will gladden him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is bringing joy to a believer: satiating his hunger, relieving his distress, or paying off his debt.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, from Al-Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'O Mufazzal! Listen to what I say to you, and know that it is the truth, and act upon it, and inform your brothers of the 'high standing' (Ilyat). I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what is the high standing of my brothers?' He said: 'Those who are eager to fulfill the needs of their brothers.' He said, then he said: 'And whoever fulfills a need for his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will fulfill for him on the Day of Resurrection a hundred thousand needs. From those, the first is Paradise, and from them is that He will admit his relatives, his acquaintances, and his brothers into Paradise, after they are not Nasibi (disbelievers in the Imams).' And it was so that whenever Al-Mufazzal asked a brother from his brothers for a need, he would say to him, 'Do you not desire that you be among the high-standing brothers?'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad who said, 'It was narrated to me from Khalid ibn Yazid from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a group from His creation, choosing them for fulfilling the needs of the poor of our Shia, so that He may reward them with Paradise for that. Therefore, if you are able to be among them, then be so. Then he said to us, 'By Allah, there is a Lord whom we worship, and we do not associate anything with Him.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Sadaqa al-Ahdab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Fulfilling the need of a believer is better than freeing a thousand slaves, and better than equipping a thousand horses in the way of Allah. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad — similar to the two hadiths.

Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Sandal, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The fulfilment of a need of a believer is more beloved to Allah than performing twenty Hajj, each time its performer spending one hundred thousand (dirhams).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Ismail ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, a believer is a mercy upon a believer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And how is that so?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Any believer who comes to his brother regarding a need, that is indeed a mercy from Allah sent to him and caused for him. So if he fulfills his need, he has accepted the mercy by accepting it; and if he turns him away from his need while he is able to fulfill it, he has turned away from himself a mercy from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent to him and caused for him.' And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hoards that mercy until the Day of Judgment, until the one who was turned away from his need becomes the judge over it. If he wills, he diverts it to himself, and if he wills, he diverts it to someone else. O Ismail! When it is the Day of Judgment and he is the judge over a mercy from Allah that has been initiated for him, to whom do you think he will divert it?' I said, 'I do not think he will divert it away from himself.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not guess, but be certain, for he will never turn it away from himself.' O Ismail! The one whose brother comes to him regarding a need, him being able to fulfill it, but he does not fulfill it for him, Allah will cause a hydra to gnaw his big toe in his grave until the Day of Judgment, whether he is forgiven or punished.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever performs Tawaf of the House (Kaaba) for seven circuits, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will write for him six thousand good deeds, erase from him six thousand sins, and elevate him by six thousand degrees.' He said: And Is'hak ibn 'Ammar added to it: 'And He will fulfill for him six thousand needs.' He said: Then he said: 'And fulfilling the need of a believer is superior to performing Tawaf and Tawaf,' until he counted ten.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A Muslim does not fulfill a need for another Muslim except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, calls out: 'Upon Me is your reward, and I will not be satisfied for you (as a reward) less than Paradise.'

From him, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Whoever performs one Tawaf of this House, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him six thousand good deeds, erase from him six thousand sins, and elevate for him six thousand levels, so that when he is at the Multazam, Allah will open for him seven doors from the doors of Paradise.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, is all this merit regarding the Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes, and I shall inform you of something superior to that: fulfilling the need of a Muslim is superior to performing Tawaf, and Tawaf, and Tawaf,' until he reached ten.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Kharqiyy, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever walks to fulfill the need of his believing brother, seeking thereby what is with Allah, until it is fulfilled for him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him the like of the reward of a Hajj and an Umrah, both accepted, and the fasting of two months from the Sacred months, and their I'tikaf in the Sacred Mosque.' And whoever walks for it with intention but it is not fulfilled, Allah will write for him the like of an accepted Hajj. Therefore, desire the good.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Compete with one another in doing good deeds for your brothers, and be among its people, for Paradise has a door called 'Al-Ma'ruf' (Good Deeds), none shall enter it except the one who performed good deeds during the life of the world.' For indeed, when a servant walks to fulfill the need of his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigns two angels to him, one on his right and one on his left, who seek forgiveness for him from his Lord and supplicate for the fulfillment of his need. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was more joyful with the fulfillment of a believer's need when it reached him than the needy person himself was.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: By Allah, performing one Hajj is more beloved to me than freeing one slave, and another, and another, and a similar one, and a similar one until it reaches ten, and a similar one, and a similar one until it reaches seventy; and looking after a family from the Muslims, satisfying their hunger, and clothing their nakedness, so that it would preserve their faces from the people, is more beloved to me than if I were to perform one Hajj, and another, and another, and a similar one, and a similar one until it reaches ten, and a similar one, and a similar one until it reaches seventy.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ali, the companion of Al-Shaeer, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'Among My servants is one who draws near to Me through a good deed, so I will judge him to be in Paradise.' Musa (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, and what is that good deed?' He (Allah) said: 'He walks with his believing brother in fulfilling his need, whether it is fulfilled or not fulfilled.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Ali ibn Ja'far who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'When his believing brother comes to him regarding a need, it is but a mercy from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that He sends to him. So if he accepts that, he has been linked with our Wilayah, and he is linked with the Wilayah of Allah. And if he repels him from his need while he is able to fulfill it, Allah will cause a beast of fire to gnaw him in his grave until the Day of Resurrection, whether he is forgiven or punished. And if the petitioner accepts his excuse, his state will be even worse.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when a need of his brother comes to a believer, and it does not happen to be in his presence, his heart becomes concerned with it; therefore, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will enter him into Paradise due to his concern for it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'The walking of a man to attend to the need of his believing brother is recorded for him as ten good deeds, and ten bad deeds are erased from him, and ten ranks are elevated for him.' He said: 'And I do not know him except that he said: And it is equivalent to freeing ten necks, and is superior to performing Itikaf for a month in the Sacred Mosque.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'For Allah there are servants in the earth who strive regarding the needs of the people; they are the secure ones on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever brings gladness to a believer, Allah will gladden his heart on the Day of Resurrection.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Sadaqa, from a man from the people of Hulwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'It is more beloved to me that I walk to fulfill the need of a Muslim brother of mine than to free a thousand persons and to carry in the way of Allah upon a thousand saddled and harnessed horses.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no believer who walks for his believer brother to fulfill a need, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him a good deed with every step, removes a bad deed because of it, raises his rank because of it, and after that adds ten good deeds, and he is granted intercession for ten needs.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever strives to fulfill the need of his Muslim brother, seeking the Face of Allah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him a thousand thousand (million) good deeds, and in them He will forgive his relatives, his neighbors, his brothers, his acquaintances, and whoever did him a favor in the world. So when it is the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to him: 'Enter the Fire.' So whoever you find in it who did you a favor in the world, remove him by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, unless he is a Nasibi (one of the hostile ones).

From him, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever strives to fulfill the need of his Muslim brother, and exerts himself in it, and Allah causes its fulfillment to flow through his hands, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him the reward of one Ḥajj, one ʿUmrah, and ʿItikāf (seclusion) for two months in the Sacred Mosque, along with the fasting of those two months. And if he exerts himself in it but Allah does not cause its fulfillment to flow through his hands, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him the reward of one Ḥajj and one ʿUmrah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The creatures are My dependants, and the most beloved of them to Me is the most kind to them and the most striving regarding their needs.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Umara who said: Hammad ibn Abi Hanifa, when he met me, would say, 'Reiterate your hadith upon me.' So I narrated it saying, 'We are reporting that a worshipper of the Children of Israel, when he reached the peak in worship, became a walker regarding the needs of the people, enduring with what was correct for them.'

A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from some of his companions from Abu Ummarah who said: Hammad ibn Abi Hanifah, when he met me, would say, 'Repeat your hadith to me so I may narrate it.' I said, 'It has been narrated to us that a worshipper from the Children of Israel, when he reached the utmost limit in worship, would become one who walked about attending to the needs of people, attending to what would benefit them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever assists his believing brother, the distressed, gasping for breath in his struggle, so he relieves his hardship and helps him succeed in his need, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him seventy-two mercies. He will hasten one of them to rectify his livelihood, and reserve seventy-one for him for the terrors and horrors of the Day of Resurrection.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever assists a believer, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will relieve him of seventy-three distresses: one in this world and seventy-two during the Great Distress.' He added: 'Where people are preoccupied with themselves.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever relieves a believer (of distress), Allah will relieve his heart on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Zareeh Al-Muharibi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whichever believer relieves a believer of a hardship, while he is insolvent, Allah will ease his needs in this world and the Hereafter.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And whoever covers a flaw of a believer that he fears, Allah will cover him with seventy flaws from the flaws of this world and the Hereafter.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Allah is aiding the believer as long as the believer is aiding his brother.' So benefit yourselves with the advice and desire the goodness.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever satiates a believer, Paradise becomes obligatory for him; and whoever satiates a disbeliever, it becomes a right upon Allah to fill his belly with As-Saqar (Hellfire), whether he was a believer or a disbeliever.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Feeding a man from the Muslims is more beloved to me than feeding an 'Afqa' from the people.' I said, 'And what is the 'Afqa'?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'A hundred thousand, or more.'

From him, from Ahmad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who feeds three persons from the Muslims, Allah would Feed him from three Gardens in the kingdom of the skies – Al-Firdows, and the Garden of Eden, and Tooba, and it is a tree coming out from the Garden of Eden. Our Lord Planted it with His own Hands'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no man who invites two believers into his house, feeds them, and satiates them, except that this is superior to freeing a slave.

From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever feeds a believer from hunger, Allah will feed him from the fruits of Paradise; and whoever quenches a believer from thirst, Allah will quench him from the Sealed Nectar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever gives a believer a drink of water from wherever he is able to provide water, Allah will give him, for each drink, seventy thousand good deeds; and if he gives him from where he is not able to provide water, it is as if he has freed ten necks from the children of Ismail.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Nu'aym al-Sahhaf, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you love your brethren, O Husayn?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you benefit their poor ones?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'But, it is an entitlement upon you that you love the one whom Allah loves. But, by Allah, you will not benefit anyone from them until you love him.' I said, 'Yes'. 'Are you inviting them to your house?' I said, 'Yes. I do not eat unless there are two of them with me, and three, and less, and more'. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'But their merit upon you is greater than your merit upon them'. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I feed them my food, and I give them my ride, and their merit upon me happens to be greater?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. When they come over to your house, they enter with the Forgiveness for you, and Forgiveness for your dependants, and when they go out from your house, they go out with your sins (having been Forgiven) and the sins of your dependants'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, who said: Our companions were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'I do not have lunch nor dinner except that two or three of them, or fewer or more, are with me.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Their merit upon you is greater than your merit upon them.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How is that, while I feed them my food, spend upon them from my wealth, and my dependents serve them?' He said, 'Indeed, when they come to you, they come with abundant sustenance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and when they leave, they leave with forgiveness for you.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Muqarrin, from Ubaydullah al-Wassaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'To feed a Muslim man is more beloved to me than to free an 'Ufqa from the people.' I said, 'And how much is an 'Ufqa?' He said, 'Ten thousand.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who feeds his brother for the sake of Allah, for him is a reward like that of the one who feeds a 'Fi'am' (a large crowd) from the people.' I said, 'And what is the 'Fi'am' from the people?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One hundred thousand from the people.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Sadeer al-Sayrafi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What prevents you from freeing a person every day?' I said, 'My wealth cannot bear that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Feeding a Muslim every day?' So I said, 'The rich or the poor?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the rich may also desire food.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A meal which my Muslim brother eats with me is more beloved to me than if I were to free a neck.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'To satiate a man from my brethren is more beloved to me than if I were to enter this market of yours, buy a head from it, and free him.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'It is more beloved to me that I take five dirhams and enter into this market of yours, and buy food with it, and gather a number of Muslims (to eat), than that I free a slave.'

From him, from Al-Washa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was asked, 'What equates to freeing a neck?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Feeding a Muslim man.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Shibl, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see anything equal to visiting the believer except feeding him, and it is a right upon Allah that He feeds the one who feeds a believer from the food of Paradise.'

Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'If I were to feed a needy believer, it would be more beloved to me than if I were to visit him; and if I were to visit him, it would be more beloved to me than if I were to free ten necks (slaves).'

Salih ibn Uqba from Abdullah ibn Muhammad and Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever feeds a wealthy believer, it is for him (as recompense) equal to freeing one neck from the children of Ismail, rescuing him from slaughter; and whoever feeds a needy believer, it is for him equal to freeing one hundred necks from the children of Ismail, rescuing them from slaughter.

Salih ibn 'Uqba from Nasr ibn Qabous from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The feeding of a believer is more beloved to me than freeing ten necks and ten Hajj pilgrimages. I said, 'Ten necks and ten Hajj?' He said, 'O Nasr! If you do not feed him, he will die, or you will direct him (elsewhere) so he comes to a Nasibi (Hostile one) and asks him; and death is better for him than asking a Nasibi. O Nasr! The one who revives a believer, it is as if he has revived all the people. So if you do not feed him, you have caused him to die, and if you feed him, you have revived him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever clothes his brother with a garment of winter or summer, it becomes a right upon Allah to clothe him from the garments of Paradise, and to ease upon him the pangs of death, and to expand for him in his grave, and that the Angels meet him when he exits from his grave with glad tidings. And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: 'And the Angels will meet them: This is your Day which you were promised.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever clothes one of the poor Muslims with a garment to cover his nakedness, or assists him with something from what sustains his livelihood, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seven thousand angels from among the angels who seek forgiveness for every sin he has committed, until the Trumpet is blown.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever clothes one of the poor Muslims with a garment to cover his nakedness, or assists him with something from what sustains his livelihood, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seventy thousand angels from among the angels who seek forgiveness for every sin he has committed until the Trumpet is blown.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever clothes a believer, Allah will clothe him from the green garments. And he said in another hadith: He will not cease to be in the guarantee of Allah as long as a fibre remains upon him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he used to say: The one who clothes a believer with a garment from his bareness, Allah will clothe him from the brocades of Paradise; and the one who clothes a believer with a garment from his adequacy, will not cease to be in a veil from Allah for as long as there remains a rag from the cloth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever removes a speck from the face of his believing brother, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him ten good deeds; and whoever smiles in the face of his brother, it will be a good deed for him.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says to his believing brother, 'Welcome!', Allah the Exalted writes for him a 'Welcome' until the Day of Resurrection.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nasr ibn Is'haq, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Nu'man, from Al-Haytham ibn Hammad, from Abu Dawud, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no servant in my community who is kind to his brother regarding Allah with anything from kindness, except that Allah would have him served by the servants of Paradise.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who honours his Muslim brother with a word being kind to him with it, and relieves his suffering, will not cease to be in the extended Shade of Allah. Upon him will be the Mercy for as long as he was in that.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'From what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has specially granted the believer is that He makes him recognize the righteousness of his brethren, even if it is little.' And righteousness is not defined by abundance. And that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: And they give preference over themselves, even though there is poverty for them. Then He said: 'And whoever is preserved from the niggardliness of his soul, those are the successful ones.' And whoever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes recognize with that, Allah will love him; and whoever Allah, Blessed and High, loves, He will fulfill his reward on the Day of Resurrection without reckoning. Then he said: 'O Jameel! Report this hadith to your brethren, for it arouses desire regarding righteousness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from al-Mufaddal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the believer presents his brother with a gift. I said, 'And what is the gift?' He said: 'A seat, a pillow, food, clothing, and a greeting. So Paradise prolongs the reward for him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to it: 'I have prohibited your food upon the people of the world except for a Prophet or a successor of a Prophet.' So when it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will reveal to it: 'Reward My friends for their gifts.' So male and female attendants will come out from it with them, platters covered with cloths of pearls. So when they look at Hell and its terror, and at Paradise and what is in it, their intellects will fly off and they will refuse to eat. So a caller will call out from beneath the Throne: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited Hell upon the one who eats from the food of His Paradise.' So the people will extend their hands and eat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is an obligation for the believer upon the believer that he veils upon him seventy major sins.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, altogether, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Adayy, who said: 'Muhammad ibn Sulayman dictated to me, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Be good, O Is'haq, to my friends to the best of your ability. And whenever a believer is good to a believer and assists him, it scratches the face of Iblis and ulcerates his heart.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan — from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'The dyeing of God, and who is better than God in dyeing?' He said: 'It is Islam.' And he said regarding His words, Mighty and Majestic: 'He has indeed grasped the firmest handle,' he said: 'It is faith in God alone, with no associate for Him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abdullah ibn Farqad, from Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of Allah (Mighty and Majestic): 'The dyeing of Allah, and who is better than Allah in dyeing?' He said: 'The dyeing is Islam.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one (narrator), from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both): regarding the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic: '[Take] the dyeing of God; and who is better than God in dyeing?' He said: 'The dyeing — it is Islam.' And he said regarding His Words, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever disbelieves in the taghut and believes in God, he has grasped the Firmest Handle.' He said: 'It is faith (iman).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is obligatory for the believer upon the believer that he advises him.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is obligatory for the believer upon the believer to offer sincere advice to him, in his presence and in his absence.
Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubeyda Al-Hazza', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: It is an obligation for the believer upon the believer, [to give] sincere advice.

Ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let the man from you advise his brother like his advising his own self.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The greatest of people in status with Allah on the Day of Resurrection is the one who walks most in His earth with sincere advice to His creatures.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Advising for the sake of Allah among His creatures is upon you, for you will not meet Him with a deed superior to it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Abi Talha, from Habib al-Ahwal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A charity which Allah loves is reconciling between the people when they are estranged, and bringing them close when they are distant.' From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: That I should reconcile between two people is more beloved to me than that I should give charity with two Dinars.
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you see a dispute between two from our Shia, so redeem it from my wealth'.

Ibn Sinan, from Abu Haneefa Sabiq Al-Hajj, who said: Al-Mufazzal passed by us while I and my brother-in-law were quarrelling over an inheritance. He paused with us for a while, then said to us, 'Come to the house.' So we went to him, and he reconciled between us with four hundred dirhams. He handed them over to us from himself until each one of us was confident with his companion. He said, 'Indeed, it is not from my wealth, but Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me that whenever two men from our companions dispute over anything, I should reconcile between them and redeem it from his wealth. So this is from the wealth of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The reconciler is not a liar.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb or Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'Deliver from me such and such regarding matters I have ordered.' I said: 'So I will deliver them from you, and I will say on my own behalf what you said to me, and other than what you said?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, indeed. The reconciler is not a liar; rather, reconciliation is not a lie.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the meaning of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Whoever kills a soul, it is as though he killed all the people; and whoever saves a soul, it is as though he saved all the people?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who extracts it from straying to Guidance, so it is as if he revived it; and the one who extracts it from Guidance to straying, so he has killed it.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What is the meaning of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: 'And whoever keeps it alive, it is as though he kept alive all the people'?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From burning or drowning.' I said, 'So (what about) the one who extracts it from straying to Guidance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is its greatest interpretation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halbi, from Abu Khalid al-Qammam, from Humran, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I ask you, may Allah improve you.' He said, 'Yes.' So I said, 'I was in a certain state, and today I am in another state. I used to enter the land (go out to people) and invite the man, the two, and the woman, and Allah would rescue whom He willed; and today I do not invite anyone.' He said, 'And there is no harm upon you if you leave between the people and their Lord. So whoever Allah intends to bring out from darkness to light, He brings him out.' Then he said, 'And there is no harm upon you if you perceive goodness in someone, to introduce something to him with an introduction.' I said, 'Inform me about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever keeps it alive, it is as though he kept alive all the people.' He said, 'From burning or drowning.' Then he was silent, then said, 'Its greatest interpretation is that you invite her, so she responds to you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Kuleyb ibn Muawiya al-Saydawi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Beware of the people! Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends good for a servant, He marks a spot in his heart, then leaves him, and he wanders around because of it and seeks it.' Then he said: 'If you were to speak to the people, say to them: We go where Allah goes, and we choose whom Allah chooses, and Allah chose Muhammad, and we chose the Progeny of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Thabit Abu Saeed, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Thabit! What is it with you and the people? Refrain from the people and do not invite anyone to your matter. By Allah, even if the inhabitants of the sky and the inhabitants of the earth were to gather together to misguide a servant whom Allah intends to guide, they would not have the capacity to do so.' Refrain from the people, and not one of you should be saying, 'My brother', 'my cousin', and 'my neighbour'. For indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends goodness for a servant, He purifies his spirit, so he does not hear of a good act except that he recognizes it, nor of an evil deed except that he denies it. Then Allah casts a word into his heart by which He gathers his affairs.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Al-Fudayl, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'We invite the people to this matter (Wilayah/Imamate).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Fudayl! Indeed, when Allah intends good for a servant, He commands an angel, who seizes him by his neck until He brings him into this matter, willingly or unwillingly.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Make this matter of yours for the sake of Allah, and do not make it for the people, for whatever is for Allah is for Allah, and whatever is for the people, it does not ascend to the sky.' And do not dispute with the people regarding your Religion, for disputing is a sickness of the heart. Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah Guides whom He Desires. Will you then force the people until they become Believers? Leave off the people, for the people are taking (their Religion) from the people, and you all are taking from Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him), and there is no equation. And indeed I heard my father saying: 'When Allah Ordains for a servant to enter into this matter (Al-Wilayah), he would be quicker to it than the bird to its nest'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a people for the truth; so when the door of the truth passes by them, their hearts accept it, even if they do not know it. And when the door of falsehood passes by them, their hearts reject it, even if they do not know it. And He created a people for the opposite; so when the door of the truth passes by them, their hearts reject it, even if they do not know it, and when the door of falsehood passes by them, their hearts accept it, even if they do not know it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdul Hameed ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends goodness for a servant, He marks in his heart a spot of light in his heart, so his hearing and his heart are illuminated by it, until he becomes more eager for what is in your hands (Al-Wilayah) than you are; and when He intends evil for a servant, He marks a black spot in his heart, so his hearing and his heart are darkened by it. Then he recited this Verse: So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He intends to make err, He makes his chest straitened and narrow as though he were ascending to the sky.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends goodness for a servant, marks a white spot in his heart, opens the ears of his heart, and assigns an angel to guide him; and when He intends evil for a servant, marks a black spot in his heart, closes the ears of his heart, and assigns a Satan to mislead him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Al-Sakhr! Indeed, Allah gives the world to whom He loves and whom He hates, but He does not give this matter (Wilayah) except to the elite of His creation. You, by Allah, are upon my religion and the religion of my forefathers, Ibrahim and Ismail. I do not mean Ali ibn Al-Husayn, nor Muhammad ibn Ali, even though these latter are upon the religion of those former ones.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Malik ibn A'yan al-Juhani, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'O Malik! Indeed, Allah gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He hates, and He does not give His religion except to whom He loves.'

From him, from Moalla, from Al-Washa, from Abdul-Kareem ibn Amr Al-Khasha'i, from Umar ibn Hanzala, and from Hamza ibn Humran, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, this world, Allah gives it to the righteous and the immoral, and He does not give faith except to His choicest ones from His creation.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Suleiman, from Muyassar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The world, Allah Mighty and Majestic gives it to the one He loves and the one He hates, and faith, He does not give it except to the one He loves.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So Allah saved him from the evil of what they planned.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But, they had extended (their hands) upon him, and killed him, but do you know what He saved him (from)? He saved him from their strife in his Religion.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Jameela, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It was in the bequest of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to his companions.' 'Know that the Quran is the guidance of the day and night, and the light of the dark night, in spite of any hardship and destitution.' 'So when an affliction presents itself, make your wealth subordinate to your own selves, and when a calamity descends, make your selves subordinate to your religion.' 'And know that the destroyed one is the one whose religion is destroyed, and the ruined one is the one whose religion is ruined.' 'Indeed, there is no poverty after Paradise, and indeed, there is no richness after Hellfire. Its captives are not freed, and its afflicted are not cured.'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie ibn Abdullah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Safety of the Religion and good health of the body is better than wealth, and wealth is an adornment from the adornments of the world, an excellence. Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Al-Fuzayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from one of his companions who said: A man from his companions used to visit Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), but he was absent for a time not performing Hajj. So one of his acquaintances came to him and said to him, 'So-and-so, what happened to him?' He began to lay down the speech, thinking that he meant wealth and the world. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'How is his religion?' He said, 'As you love.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, it is the richness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those shall be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured.' He said: 'For what they patiently endured was the dissimulation (Taqiyya).' And 'they repel evil with good.' He said: 'The good is the dissimulation (Taqiyya), and the evil is the broadcasting (of one's true faith).

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Umar al-A'ajamy, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Umar! Nine-tenths of the Religion is in dissimulation (Taqiyya), and there is no Religion for the one who does not practice dissimulation; and the dissimulation is regarding everything except regarding Al-Nabeez (an intoxicating drink) and the wiping upon the two socks (during ablution)'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Dissimulation (Taqiyya) is from the Religion of Allah.' I said, 'From the Religion of Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, by Allah! From the Religion of Allah. And indeed, Yusuf (peace be upon him) said, "O caravan! You are indeed thieves." By Allah! They had not stolen anything. And indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said, "I am sick." By Allah! He was not sick.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed altogether, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Habib ibn Bishr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: No, by Allah! There is nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than Taqiyya (dissimulation/prudence). O Habib! Indeed, whoever has Taqiyya, Allah will elevate him. O Habib! Whoever does not have Taqiyya, Allah will place him down. O Habib! The people are merely in a truce (of hostilities); so if that (hostilities) had been there, this (Taqiyya) would be there.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Jabir Al-Makouf, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Be cautious regarding your religion, so veil it with dissimulation (Taqiyya), for there is no faith for the one who has no dissimulation for himself. Indeed, you are among the people like bees are among birds. If the birds knew what is in the interiors of the bees, nothing would remain of them except that they would eat it. And if the people knew what is in your interiors, that you love us, the People of the Household, they would eat you with their tongues, and destroy you in private and in public.
