May Allah have mercy on a servant from you who was upon our Wilayah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the good deed is not like the evil.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The good deed is the dissimulation (Taqiyya), and the evil is the broadcasting (of one's true state).' And His Words, Mighty and Majestic: 'Repel the evil with that which is better.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That which is better is the dissimulation (Taqiyya), so if there is enmity between you and him, he becomes as if he were an intimate friend.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Amr Al-Kinani, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Amr! What is your view if I were to narrate to you a hadith or issue a verdict to you, then you come to me after that and ask me about it, so I inform you with a statement contrary to what I had informed you, or issue a verdict contrary to that, which of the two would you take?' I said, 'I take the newer of the two and leave the other one.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You are correct, O Abu Amr! Allah refused except that He be worshipped in secret. But, by Allah, if you were to do that, it would be better for me and for you; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refused for us and for you in His religion, except for dissimulation (taqiyya).'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Durust al-Wasiti, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The dissimulation (taqiyya) of any one of you has not reached the dissimulation of the Companions of the Cave. Indeed, they used to attend the festivals and tighten the sashes, so Allah gave them their reward twice.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Waqid Al-Lahham, who said: I faced Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on a road, so I turned my face away from him and passed by. Then I went to him after that and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I meet you but I turn my face away, disliking that it would be grievous upon you.' So he said to me, 'May Allah have mercy on you! A man met me yesterday in such and such a place and said, "Upon you be peace, O Abu Abdillah." How good (is your action), but (his pronouncing it in public was) not beautiful.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: It was said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The people are reporting that Ali (peace be upon him) said upon the pulpit of Kufa: O people! You will be called to insult me, so insult me. Then you will be called to disavow me, so do not disavow me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'How often do the people lie against Ali (peace be upon him).' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'He only said: You will be called to insult me, so insult me. Then you will be called to disavow me, and I am upon the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), but he did not say: Do not disavow me.' So the questioner said to him (peace be upon him), 'What do you think if he chose death rather than disavowal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! That would not be upon him, and he would have no excuse except what was for 'Ammar ibn Yasir, when the people of Mecca coerced him while his heart was at rest with faith.' Except the one who is compelled while his heart is at rest with faith. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him at that time: O 'Ammar! If they return (to coercing you), so return (to saying what you said), for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed your excuse and commanded you to return if they return.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham al-Kindi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Beware of doing a deed by which they would reproach us, for the child of the bad [character] shames his father with his deed. Be an adornment for the one to whom you have attached yourselves, and do not be a disgrace upon him. Pray among their clans, visit their sick, and attend their funerals. And do not let them precede you to any good, for you are more deserving of it than they. And by Allah, Allah was not worshipped with anything more beloved to Him than Al-Khab.' I said, 'And what is Al-Khab?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Al-Taqiyya (dissimulation).'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about standing up for the rulers, so he (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Dissimulation (Taqiyya) is from my religion and the religion of my forefathers, and there is no faith for the one who has no dissimulation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabi' ibn Abdillah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Dissimulation (Taqiyya) is applicable in every necessity, and its performer knows it best when it befalls him.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Muhammad bin Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'And what thing is more delighting to my eyes than the dissimulation (Taqiyya)? Indeed, the dissimulation is a shield of the believer.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What prevented Meysam, may Allah have Mercy on him, from the dissimulation (Taqiyya)?' By Allah, he had known that this Verse was Revealed regarding Ammar and his companions: 'except the one who is compelled while his heart is at rest on account of faith'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Dissimulation (Taqiyya) was instituted only to preserve blood (from being spilled). So when the blood is to be spilled anyway, then it is no longer dissimulation.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every time this matter comes closer, the (need for) dissimulation (Taqiyya) intensifies.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Ismail al-Ju'fi and Muammar ibn Yahya ibn Sam and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, who said: We heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Dissimulation (Taqiyya) applies to everything the son of Adam is compelled to, so Allah has permitted it for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'The dissimulation (Taqiyya) is a shield of Allah, between Him and His creatures.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Ahmad ibn Hamza from Al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Mix with them with outwardly (apparent) and oppose them inwardly (hidden) when the ruler is childish'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Abdullah ibn Asad, from Abdullah ibn Ata'a, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Two men from the people of Kufa were seized, and it was said to them,
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Salih, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of the consequences of the slips (of the tongues)'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Dissimulation (Taqiyya) is the shield of the believer, and dissimulation is the protection of the believer; and there is no faith for the one who has no dissimulation. Indeed, a servant to whom a hadith from our hadiths comes, and he makes Allah Mighty and Majestic a religion by it, in what is between him and Him, then honor befalls him in the world and light in the Hereafter. And indeed, a servant to whom a hadith from our hadiths comes, but he broadcasts it, then disgrace befalls him in the world, and Allah Mighty and Majestic removes that light from him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: I wish, by Allah, that I could redeem two characteristics in our Shia with part of the flesh of my arm: rashness and scarcity of concealment.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu Asama Zayd al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The people were commanded with two characteristics, but they wasted them, so they became from them upon nothing. (These two are) patience and concealment.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yunus ibn Ammar, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Suleyman! You are upon a Religion; whoever conceals it, Allah honors him, and whoever broadcasts it, Allah humiliates him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: We went to him as a group and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We intend to go to Iraq, so advise us.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Let your strong ones strengthen your weak ones, and let your rich ones assist your poor ones, and do not divulge our secret nor broadcast our matter. And whenever a hadith comes to you from us, and you find a witness or two witnesses for it from the Book of Allah, then take it; otherwise, pause with it, then refer it back to us until it becomes clear to you.' And know that the one awaiting this matter has a reward like that of the fasting one who stands (in night prayer). And whoever catches up with our Qa'im and goes out with him and kills our enemy, for him is a reward like that of twenty martyrs. And whoever is killed with our Qa'im, for him is a reward like that of twenty-five martyrs.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul A'ala who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The bearing of our matter is not merely affirming it and accepting it; from the bearing of our matter is veiling it and safeguarding it from those not deserving of it. So convey greetings to them and say to them: May Allah have mercy on a servant who attracts the affection of people to himself. Narrate to them what they know, and conceal from them what they deny.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, the one who establishes war with weapons against us is not more burdensome to us than the speaker who speaks against us with what we dislike. So when you recognize a broadcast from a servant, go to him and repel him from it. If he accepts from you, fine; otherwise, load upon him with one who is heavy upon him, and he will listen to him.' For indeed, a man from you seeks a need and is gentle/moderate in it until it is fulfilled for him. So be gentle/moderate regarding my need as you are regarding your own needs. If he accepts from you, fine; otherwise, bury his words under your feet and do not say, 'He says, and he says,' for that would be borne upon me and upon you. And by Allah, if you were saying what I say, I would acknowledge that you are my companions. This is Abu Hanifa, for whom there are companions, and this is Al-Hasan Al-Basri, for whom there are companions. And I am a man from Quraish, born to me by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I know the Book of Allah, and therein is the explanation of everything: the beginning of creation, the matters of the sky, the matters of the earth, the matters of the former ones, the matters of the latter ones, the matters of what was, and the matters of what will be. It is as if I am looking at that established before my eyes.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: 'Our secret has not ceased to be concealed until it came to be in the hands of the children of Kaysan, so they began to narrate it in the roads and the towns of the black land (Iraq).'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, the most beloved of my companions to me is the most pious, the most jurist, and the most retentive of our hadith; and the one of the worst state in my presence and the most detestable is the one who, when he hears a hadith attributed to us and narrated from us, does not accept it, is repulsed by it, denies it, and declares disbelievers those who follow it, while he does not know, perhaps the hadith originated from us and was attributed to us, and thus he becomes excluded from our Wilayah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Mu'alla! Conceal our matter and do not broadcast it, for whoever conceals our matter and does not broadcast it, Allah will honor him because of it in the world, and make it a light between his eyes in the Hereafter, guiding him to Paradise.' O Mu'alla! Whoever broadcasts our matter and does not conceal it, Allah will humble him because of it in the world, and remove the light from between his eyes in the Hereafter, and make it a darkness guiding him to the Fire. O Mu'alla! Indeed, dissimulation (Taqiyyah) is from my religion and the religion of my forefathers, and there is no religion for the one who has no dissimulation. O Mu'alla! Indeed, Allah loves to be worshipped in secret just as He loves to be worshipped openly. O Mu'alla! Indeed, the broadcaster of our matter is like the one who denies it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Did you inform anyone with what I informed you with?' I said, 'No, except for Suleyman ibn Khalid.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You have done well. Have you not heard the words of the poet: "Do not let my secret and your secret pass to a third! Indeed, every secret that exceeds two becomes common knowledge."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a matter, but he refused and withheld, then said: 'If We were to give you everything you want, it would be evil for you, and the one with this matter would be seized by the neck.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The Wilayah of Allah was kept secret by Him to Jibraeel (peace be upon him), and Jibraeel kept it secret to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and Muhammad kept it secret to Ali (peace be upon him), and Ali kept it secret to whoever Allah willed. Then you broadcast it. Who is the one who withheld even a single word he heard?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'In the wisdom of the progeny of Dawud (peace be upon him), it is befitting for the Muslim to be master of himself, focused on his affairs, and knowing the people of his time. So fear Allah and do not broadcast our hadith. If it were not for Allah defending His friends and exacting retribution for His friends from their enemies...' ...have you not seen what Allah did with the progeny of Barmak, and what Allah exacted for Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)? And the Banu Al-Ash'ath were upon great danger, so Allah defended them through their Wilayah for Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). And you are in Iraq, seeing the deeds of these Pharaohs, and what Allah has granted them respite. So upon you is Taqwa of Allah, and let not the worldly life deceive you, nor be deceived by the one who has been granted respite, for it is as if the Matter (of the Qaim) has arrived to you.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessed is the obscure servant whom Allah knows but whom people do not know. They are the lanterns of guidance and the fountains of knowledge. Every dark trial is cleared away for them. They are not the broadcasters of their knowledge, nor are they the quarrelsome show-offs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan al-Isbahani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Blessed is every obscure servant, who is not sought after by people; he knows people, but people do not know him. Allah recognizes him with pleasure. Those are the lanterns of guidance; every dark trial is lifted from them, and the door of every mercy is opened for them. They are not the boastful show-offs, nor the quarrelsome hypocrites.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Speak good, so you will be recognized by it, and do good, so you will be among its people, and do not be hasty show-offs. Indeed, the best of you are those who, when looked at, Allah is remembered; and the worst of you are the gossipers, the separators between loved ones, the seekers of faults of the righteous.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from the one who informed him, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Restrain your tongues and stay in your houses, for no matter will befall you that singles you out forever, and the Zaidites will ceaselessly be a shield for you forever.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: If this matter (Al-Wilayah) was in your hands and you have the capacity that you do not teach this, then do so. He said, 'And it was so that in his presence were some people, and they mentioned the broadcasting, so he said: Preserve your tongues, you would be honoured, and do not enable the people to sit upon your necks, for you would be disgraced'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, our matter is veiled, masked by the Covenant; so whoever tears the veil upon us, Allah will humble him.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, altogether, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A sigh of the one concerned for us, grieving over our injustice, is a glorification (tasbih); and his thinking of our matter is worship; and his concealment of our secret is jihad in the way of Allah.' Muhammad ibn Sa'id said to me: 'Write this in gold, for you will not write anything better than it.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Dahir, from Al-Hasan ibn Yahya, from Qutham Abu Qatada Al-Harrani, from Abdullah ibn Yunus, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man named Hammam, who was a worshipper, ascetic, and diligent, stood before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) while he was delivering a sermon. He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, describe to us the description of the believer, as if we are looking at him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hammam, the believer is the shrewd, the intelligent. His joy is on his face and his sorrow is in his heart. He is the most expansive in chest and the most humble in self. He restrains from everything perishable and is present for everything good. He is not spiteful, nor envious, nor quick to argue, nor abusive, nor fault-finding, nor backbiter. He dislikes elevation (status) and dislikes fame. He is long-suffering, far from worry, frequent in silence, dignified, remembering, patient, grateful. Gloomy in his thoughts, joyful in his poverty. Easy-going in nature, soft in manner, firm in loyalty, little in causing harm, neither pretentious nor excessive.' If he laughs, he does not burst out; if he is angry, he does not become reckless. His laughter is a smile, his questioning is for learning, and his reference is for understanding. His knowledge is abundant, his forbearance is great, and he is full of mercy. He is not stingy, nor hasty, nor weary, nor arrogant, nor unjust in his judgment, nor unfair in his knowledge. His self is harder than the slab, and his temperament is sweeter than honey. He is not greedy, nor panicky, nor violent, nor arrogant, nor pretentious, nor excessive. He is good in dispute, generous in reference, just when angry, and friendly when sought. He does not jeopardize, nor expose, nor be compulsive. He is pure in affection, firm in covenant, complete in contract. He is affectionate, maintaining ties, forbearing, calm, little in extravagance. He is pleased with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and opposes his desire. He is not harsh to those below him, nor does he engage in what does not concern him. He is a supporter of the Religion, a defender of the believers, a cave for the Muslims. Praise does not pierce his hearing, nor does greed pierce his heart, nor does play divert his judgment, nor does he reveal his knowledge to the ignorant.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the believer that he possess eight characteristics: dignified amidst the volatile, patient during affliction, grateful during prosperity, content with what Allah has granted him, not oppressing his enemies, nor being burdensome to his friends. His body is in exertion from it, and the people are at ease from him. Indeed, knowledge is the friend of the believer, forbearance is his vizier, patience is the commander of his army, kindness is his brother, and gentleness is his father.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ibn Fazzal from Mansur ibn Yunus from Abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: The believer is silent to be safe, and speaks to benefit. He neither discusses his entrustments with the friends nor does he conceal his testimony from the remote ones, nor does he do anything of the goodness for showing off, nor does he neglect it due to bashfulness. If he is praised, he fears what they might be saying, and he seeks Forgiveness of Allah for what they do not know. The words of the ignorant one do not deceive him, and he fears the counting of what he has done.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from someone who reported it, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believer has strength in religion, and firmness in gentleness, and faith in conviction, and eagerness in jurisprudence, and activity in guidance, and righteousness in uprightness, and knowledge in forbearance, and cleverness in gentleness, and generosity in truth, and moderation in wealth, and composure in poverty, and pardoning in power, and obedience to Allah in sincerity, and restraint in lust, and piety in desire, and eagerness in jihad, and prayer in busyness, and patience in hardship, and dignified in turmoil, and patient in difficulties, and grateful in prosperity. And he does not backbite, nor is he arrogant, nor does he cut off kinship, and he is not weak, nor harsh, nor rough, nor does his sight precede him, nor does his belly disgrace him, nor does his private part overcome him, nor does he envy people. He is reproached but does not reproach, and he is not extravagant. He helps the oppressed, and he is merciful to the poor. His soul is tired from him, but people are at rest from him. He does not desire the honor of the world, nor does he grieve over its disgrace. People have a concern upon which they have turned, and for him there is a concern that occupies him. No deficiency is seen in his judgment, nor weakness in his opinion, nor waste in his religion. He guides the one who consults him, and assists the one who assists him, and shields from vulgarity and ignorance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu Al-Abbas, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whose good deeds delight him and his evil deeds disgust him, he is a believer.'

Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Za'lan, from Abu Ishaq al-Khurasani, from Amr ibn Jumi' al-Abdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Our Shia are the pale, the withered, the slender, those who, when night covers them, welcome it with grief.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Our Shia are the people of guidance, and the people of piety, and the people of goodness, and the people of faith, and the people of victory and triumph.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur Buzurj, from Mufazzal who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Beware of the lowliness, for indeed, the Shia of Ali are those whose belly and private part are chaste, whose striving is intense, who act for their Creator, who hope for His reward, and who fear His punishment. So when you see those, then those are the Shia of Ja'far.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Shia of Ali (peace be upon him) were those with empty bellies and shrivelled lips, people of clemency, knowledge, and forbearance. They were recognized by their monasticism (zuhd). So assist one another in what you are upon, with piety and striving (ijtihad).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Safwan al-Jus, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is the one when he is angry, his anger does not lead him out of truth, and when he is pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into falsehood, and when he has power, he does not take more than what is for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Suleiman! Do you know who is the Muslim?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! You are more knowing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Muslim is the one from whom the Muslims are safe from his tongue and his hand.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And do you know who is the believer?' I said, 'You are more knowing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the believer is the one upon whom the Muslims trust with their wealth and their selves; and the Muslim is prohibited upon the Muslim that he is unjust to him, or abandons him, or drives him away with intransigence.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The believer is the one who, when pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into sin or falsehood; and when angered, his anger does not lead him away from the word of truth; and the one who, when able, his ability does not lead him to transgress into what is not his by right.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, raising it (to the Imam), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believers are calm and lenient, like the nosed camel; when it is tied, it submits, and if it is knelt down upon a rock, it kneels down.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three are from the signs of the believer: knowledge of Allah, and whom he loves and whom he dislikes.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Abu Ibrahim al-A'jamy, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believer is forbearing; he does not act foolishly, and if foolishness is shown to him, he forbears. He does not oppress, and if he is oppressed, he forgives. He is not stingy, and if stinginess is shown to him, he is patient.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Munzir ibn Ja'far, from Adam Abu al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The believer is the one whose earnings are good, his character is excellent, his inner self is sound, he spends the surplus of his wealth, he restrains the surplus of his speech, he spares people from his evil, and he does justice to people from himself.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Kahmas, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you about the believer? He is the one upon whom the believers trust with their lives and their wealth. Shall I not inform you about the Muslim? He is the one from whom the Muslims are safe from his tongue and his hand. And the emigrant is the one who emigrates from the evil deeds and leaves what Allah has prohibited. And the believer is sacred to the believer; he should not oppress him, abandon him, backbite him, or drive him away with a single push.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Maruf ibn Kharbouz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) led the people in the morning prayer in Iraq. When he finished, he preached to them, wept, and made them weep from the fear of Allah. Then he said: 'By Allah, I lived with a group of people in the era of my friend, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Indeed, they would become shaggy, dusty, and slim-bellied by morning and evening. Between their eyes was like the hoof of a goat [from prostration]. They would spend the night for their Lord prostrating and standing, rotating between their feet and their foreheads, whispering to their Lord, and asking Him to free their necks from the Fire. By Allah, I saw them with all this, and they were fearful and anxious.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you wish to know my companions, look at the one whose piety is most intense, who fears his Creator, and hopes for his Reward. And when you see these, then these are my companions.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Our Shia are those who exchange gifts in our Wilayah, love one another for our sake, visit one another to revive our affairs; those who, when angry, do not oppress, and when pleased, do not extravagance. They are a blessing upon their neighbors, and a safety for those who mix with them.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isa al-Nahrawari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who recognizes Allah and magnifies Him, prevents his mouth from speech, his belly from food, and excuses his self with fasting and standing (for prayer).' They said, 'By our fathers and our mothers, O Rasool-Allah! Are these the friends of Allah?' He said: 'Indeed, the friends of Allah were silent, so their silence was remembrance; they looked, so their looking was a lesson; they spoke, so their speaking was wisdom; they walked, so their walking among the people was a blessing. Had it not been for the terms ordained upon them, their spirits would not have remained in their bodies out of fear of punishment and longing for reward.'

From him, from one of his companions from the Iraqis, raising it, said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) addressed the people, so he said: 'O people! I am informing you about a brother of mine who was among the greatest of people in my eyes, and the foremost reason for his greatness in my eyes was his belittling of the world in his eyes.' He was outside the control of his belly, so he did not desire what he did not find, nor did he indulge excessively when he found it. He was outside the control of his private part, so it did not diminish his intellect and his opinion. He was outside the control of ignorance, so he did not extend his hand except towards a reliable benefit. He was neither lustful, nor angry, nor impatient. Most of his lifetime he was silent. So when he spoke, he surpassed the speakers. He did not enter into disputes, nor participate in allegations, nor present an argument until he saw a judge. He was not oblivious to his brethren, nor did he single himself out with anything besides them. He was weak and weakened, but when seriousness came, he was a fierce lion. He did not blame anyone for what an excuse would be valid for, until he heard the apology. He did what he said, and did what he did not say. When two matters presented to him, not knowing which was superior, he looked at the one closest to desire and opposed it. He did not complain of a pain except in the presence of one from whom he hoped for a cure, nor did he consult anyone except one from whom he hoped for good advice. He was not impatient, nor angry, nor complaining, nor lustful, nor revengeful, nor oblivious to the enemy. So upon you is with the likes of these noble character traits if you can endure them. If you cannot endure all of them, then taking the few is better than leaving the many. And there is no might and no strength except with Allah.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Whoever deals with people without oppressing them, speaks to them without lying to them, and makes promises to them without breaking them, is among those whose backbiting is prohibited, whose manliness (virtue) is complete, whose justice is evident, and brotherhood with him becomes obligatory.

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from his mother Fatima bint al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three characteristics: whoever possesses them has completed the characteristics of faith. When he is pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into falsehood; and when he is angry, anger does not lead him out of the truth; and when he is able, he does not exceed what is not for him.'

From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'For the people of religion there are signs by which they are recognized: truthfulness in narration, fulfilling trusts, keeping promises, maintaining kinship ties, showing mercy to the weak, and sparing attention to women (or: sparing obedience to women), giving goodness, having good character, having broad character, following knowledge, and that which brings one close to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' Tooba is for them, and an excellent return. Tooba is a tree in Paradise; its root is in the house of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). There is no believer but that in his house is a branch from it. No desire for anything strikes his heart except that it comes to him with that. And if a diligent rider were to travel under its shade for a hundred years, he would not exit from it. And if a crow were to fly from its bottom, it would not reach its top until it falls down old. So desire this! Indeed, the believer is preoccupied with himself, and people are at ease from him. When night covers him, he spreads his face and prostrates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with the nobility of his body, whispering to the One who created him, for the freeing of his neck. So be like this.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Suleyman ibn Amr al-Nakha'i who said, and Al-Husayn ibn Sayf narrated to me from his brother Ali, from Suleyman, from the one who mentioned it, From Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the best of the servants, so he said: 'Those who, when they do good, are joyful, and when they commit sins, seek forgiveness, and when they are given, they are thankful, and when they are afflicted, they are patient, and when they are angry, they forgive.'

And by his chain, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of you are the possessors of Nuha (intellect/reason).' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Who are the possessors of Nuha?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'They are the possessors of excellent morals, and strong reason, and those who maintain kinship ties, and those who are righteous to their mothers and fathers, and those who attend to the poor, the neighbors, and the orphans, and who feed people with food, and spread greetings throughout the world, and they pray while people are sleeping and heedless.'

From him, from Al-Haysam Al-Nahdi, from Abdul Aziz ibn Umar, from one of his companions, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which of the characteristics is the most beautiful for a man?' He said: 'Dignity without awe, generosity without seeking recompense, and preoccupation with that which is not the chattels of the world.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The recognition of the completion of the religion of a Muslim is his leaving speech in what does not concern him, and his scarcity of quibbling, and his forbearance, and his patience, and his excellence of manners.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Arafa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you of those who are most like me?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The best of you in character, the softest of you in bearing, the most righteous of you towards their kin, the strongest of you in love for their brethren in faith, the most patient of you with the truth, the most forbearing of you of anger, the best of you in pardon, and the strongest of you in fairness to themselves in both pleasure and anger.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: From the character of the believer is spending according to the level of need, and expanding (spending) according to the level of capacity, and being fair to people, and initiating them with the greeting of peace upon them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The believer is firmer/stronger than the mountain. The mountain loses its parts (is eroded), but no loss takes place in the religion of the believer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The believer is good in assistance, light in provisions, excellent in managing his livelihood; he is not bitten twice from the same hole.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Sahl ibn al-Harith, from al-Dilhat, the slave of al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'A believer does not become a true believer until there are three characteristics in him: a Sunnah from his Lord, and a Sunnah from His Prophet, and a Sunnah from His Guardian.' As for the Sunnah from his Lord, it is the concealment of his secret. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says: 'The Knower of the unseen! So He does not reveal His secrets to anyone, except to him whom He chooses from the Messenger.' And as for the Sunnah from His Prophet, it is being polite with the people, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with being polite with the people, so He said: 'Take to forgiveness and enjoin good.' And as for the Sunnah from His Guardian, it is patience during destitution and adversities.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, is saying: [40:60] "Surely those who are too proud to worship Me shall soon enter Hell abased."' He said: 'It (worship) is the supplication, and the most superior of the acts of worship is the supplication.' I said: '[9:114] "Most surely Ibrahim was very tender-hearted, forbearing."' He said: 'The tender-hearted one (awwah) — that is the one who supplicates much.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Ibn Mahbub, altogether from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Which act of worship is the most superior?' So he said: 'There is nothing more superior in the sight of God, Mighty and Majestic, than that He should be asked and sought from for what is with Him. And there is no one more hateful to God, Mighty and Majestic, than one who is too arrogant to worship Him and does not ask for what is with Him.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muyassir ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'O Muyassir! Supplicate and do not say that the matter has already been decided. Indeed, with God — Mighty and Majestic — there is a station that cannot be attained except by asking. And if a servant were to close his mouth and not ask, he would not be given anything. So ask, and you will be given. O Muyassir! There is no door that is knocked upon except that it is about to be opened for the one who knocks.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashshab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh, from Amr ibn Jumi', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever does not ask God, Mighty and Majestic, of His grace has indeed become poor.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Supplicate, and do not say that the matter has already been decided, for the supplication is worship.' Indeed, God Mighty and Majestic says: 'Surely those who are too proud to worship Me shall soon enter Hell, abased.' And He said: 'Call upon Me, I will answer you.'

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: It is incumbent upon you to supplicate, for you will not draw closer (to Allah) by anything similar to it. And do not abandon supplicating for a small (matter) due to its smallness. Indeed He who is the Owner of small things is also the Owner of great things.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from a man who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Supplication — it is the worship about which God (Mighty and Majestic) said: "Indeed those who are too proud to worship Me" — the verse [40:60]. Supplicate to God (Mighty and Majestic) and do not say that the matter has already been decided.' Zurara said: 'What he means is: your faith in the divine decree and pre-determination should not prevent you from being diligent in supplication and striving in it — or words to that effect.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The most beloved of deeds to God, Mighty and Majestic, on the earth is supplication, and the most superior of worship is chastity.' He said: 'And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was a man who frequently supplicated.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Husayn ibn Atiyya, from Abdul Aziz Al-Taweel, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A servant, when he supplicates, Allah, Blessed and High, does not cease to be in (the fulfilment) of his need for as long as he does not haste (in getting it answered)'. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Husayn ibn Atiyya, from Abdul Aziz Al-Taweel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, when the servant hastens and stands for his need, Allah, Blessed and High is He, says: 'Does My servant not know that I am Allah Who fulfills the needs?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Al-Walid ibn Uqba Al-Hajariy, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, a believing servant will not insist upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding his need, except that He fulfills it for him.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Hassan, from Abu al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked the insistence of people upon one another in asking (for favors), and He loved that for Himself; indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves to be asked and for what is with Him to be sought.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn al-Ahmasi, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: No, by Allah! No servant would insist upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah would answer him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah be Merciful upon a servant who seeks a need from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so he is insistent in the supplication, whether it is Answered for him or not Answered for him.' And he recited this Verse: 'And I will call upon my Lord, perhaps I shall not remain unblessed in calling upon my Lord.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek supplication during four timings: at the gusting of the winds, the decline of the shadows, the descent of the rain, and the first drop of blood of the murdered believer, for the doors of the sky are opened at these things.'

From him, from his father and someone else, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu Al-Abbas Fazl Al-Baqbaaq, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A supplication is answered in four places: during Al-Witr, and after Al-Fajr, and after Al-Zuhr, and after Al-Maghrib.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Seize the opportunity for supplication at four [times]: during the recitation of the Quran, and during the Adhan, and during the descent of rain, and during the meeting of the two rows [of armies] for martyrdom.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abdullah ibn Ata', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: My father, when he had a need from Allah, would seek it during this time, meaning the decline of the sun (at midday).

From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When one of you feels soft-hearted, let him supplicate, for the heart does not soften until it is sincere.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best time for you to supplicate to Allah, Exalted and Majestic, is the pre-dawn hours.' And he recited this verse regarding the words of Yaqoub (peace be upon him): 'Soon I will ask for your forgiveness from my Lord.' And he said: 'He delayed them until the pre-dawn.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father, when he sought a need, sought it at the decline of the sun (midday). So whenever he intended that, he would give something in charity, smell some perfume, go to the Masjid, and supplicate regarding his need with whatever he desired.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When your skin trembles (with emotion) and your eyes shed tears, then make supplication, make supplication, for your purpose has been aimed at (i.e., your prayer is likely to be answered). He said, and Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated it from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Muhammad ibn Abu Hamza, from Saeed, similarly.

From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Sandal, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves from among His believing servants every servant who supplicates. Therefore, it is upon you to supplicate during the pre-dawn period until the emergence of the sun, for it is a time in which the doors of the sky are opened, sustenance is distributed, and great needs are fulfilled.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is a certain hour in the night; if a Muslim servant coincides with it, then prays and supplicates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in it, He will answer him. I said: May Allah keep you well! And which hour of the night is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When half the night has passed, and it is the first sixth from the beginning of the half.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So they were not submissive to their Lord, nor were they humbling themselves.' He said: 'Submission (al-istikana) is yielding (humility), and humbling oneself (at-tadarru') is raising the hands and beseeching with them both.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halbi, from Abu Khalid, from Marwak the pearl seller, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He mentioned 'al-Raghbah' (desire/yearning) and displayed the inner side of his two palms towards the sky; and he said: 'Thus is 'al-Rahbah' (awe/reverence)', and he made the back of his palms towards the sky; and he said: 'Thus is 'at-Tadarru' (humble beseeching)', and he moved his fingers to the right and to the left; and he said: 'Thus is 'at-Tabattul' (devotion/earnestness)', and he raised his fingers once and lowered them once; and he said: 'Thus is 'al-Ibtihal' (supplication/calling out)', and he extended his hand facing his face towards the Qiblah; and he said: 'And there is no 'Ibtihal' until the tear flows'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah, from Al-ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man passed by me while I was supplicating in my prayer with my left hand, so he said, "O Abu Abdillah, with your right hand." So I said, "O servant of Allah, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is due a right upon this [the left hand] as His right upon this [the right hand]."' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Desire (al-rahbah) is that you extend your hands and display their inner parts; and Awe (al-rahabah) is that you extend your hands and display their back parts; and Beseeching (al-tadarru') is that you move the right index finger to the right and left; and Devotion (al-tabattul) is that you move the left index finger, raising it moderately in the sky and lowering it; and Invoking (al-ibtihal) is that you extend your hands and forearms to the sky; and Invoking is when you see the causes for weeping.'

From him, from his father or someone else, from Harun ibn Harija, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about supplication and raising the hands, so he said: 'It is upon four aspects. As for seeking refuge (al-ta'awwudh), face the Qiblah with the inner side of your palms. And as for supplication regarding sustenance, extend your palms and direct their inner sides towards the sky. And as for devotion (al-tabattul), it is a gesture with your index finger. And as for invocation (al-ibtihal), it is raising your hands so they exceed your head. And the supplication of humility (al-tadarru') is that you move your index finger from what faces your face, and it is the supplication of the fearful one.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but they were not submissive to their Lord, nor were they humbling themselves'. He said: 'Submission is yielding, and humbling is raising the hands and beseeching with them both'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, who said: We said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How is the asking to Allah, Blessed and Exalted?' He said, 'You extend your palms.' We said, 'How is the seeking of Refuge?' He said, 'You display with your palms; and the devotion is the gesturing with the finger; and the beseeching is moving the finger; and the invoking is that you extend your hands together.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no thing except that it has a measure and a weight, except for the tears, for the drop can extinguish an ocean of fire. So when the eye overflows with its water, neither will its face be burdened with darkness nor humiliation. So when they overflow, Allah prohibits them upon the Fire, and if a weeper were to weep in a community, they would be shown mercy.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela and Mansur ibn Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no eye that does not weep on the Day of Judgment, except for an eye that wept from the fear of Allah; and no eye that overflowed with its tears out of the dread of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would prohibit the rest of his body from the Fire; nor would it overflow upon his cheek, so that face would not be covered with darkness or humiliation. And there is nothing that does not have a measure and a weight, except for the tear, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would extinguish oceans of Fire with a little of it. So if a servant were to weep in a community, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would be Merciful to that community because of the weeping of that servant.

From him, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no drop more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a drop of tears shed in the darkness of the night out of fear of Allah, not intending anything else by it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Salih ibn Razin and Muhammad ibn Marwan and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every eye will be weeping on the Day of Judgment except for three: an eye that was closed from the prohibitions of Allah, an eye that stayed awake in obedience to Allah, and an eye that wept in the depth of the night from the fear of Allah.

Ibn Abi Umeyr from Jameel ibn Darraj and Dorost from Muhammad ibn Marwan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no thing except that it has a measure and a weight, except for the tears, for a drop of them extinguishes an ocean of Fire. So whenever the eye overflows with its water, its face will not be covered with soot nor humiliation. So when they overflow, Allah prohibits them upon the Fire, and if a weeper weeps in a community, they would be mercied.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man from his companions, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'My servants have not drawn closer to Me with anything more beloved to Me than three characteristics.' Musa said: 'O Lord, and what are they?' He said: 'O Musa, asceticism in the world, and piety from disobediences, and weeping from My fear.' Musa said: 'O Lord, so what is for the one who does that?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Musa! As for those ascetic in the world, they are in Paradise; and as for those weeping from My fear, they are in the Lofty Highest, no one shares with them; and as for those pious from My disobediences, I examine the people and do not examine them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I supplicate and desire to weep, but it does not come to me, and sometimes I remember some of my family who have died, so I lose sleep and weep. Is that permissible?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Remember them, and when your heart is softened, weep and supplicate to your Lord, Blessed and Exalted.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Anbasa Al-Aabid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you do not have weeping, then pretend to weep.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Saeed ibn Yasar, the seller of Sabir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I pretend to cry during supplication, but I do not have actual weeping.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, and even if it is like the head of a fly.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Abu Baseer: If you fear a matter taking place or a need which you require, so begin with Allah and glorify Him and extol upon Him just as He is rightful of it, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and ask your need, and try to cry and even if it (the teardrop) is like the head of the fly. Indeed, my father (peace be upon him) was saying: The closest of what the servant can be from the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is when performing prostration and while he is weeping.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ismail al-Bajali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If weeping does not come to you, then induce it; if a tear drops from you like the head of a fly, then give good tidings, give good tidings!

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Beware when one of you wants to ask his Lord for anything from the needs of the world and the Hereafter, that he does not do so until he begins with praising Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and eulogizing Him, and sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then he should ask Allah for his needs.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is merely the eulogizing, then the laudation, then the acknowledgement of the sin, then the asking. Indeed, by Allah, a servant does not exit from a sin except through acknowledgement.

And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'aba, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, except that he said: 'Then the laudation, then the acknowledgement of the sin'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you intend to supplicate, glorify Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and praise Him, and glorify Him, and extol Him, and laud upon Him, and send blessings upon Muhammad the Prophet and his Progeny, then ask, you will be given.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you seeks a need, let him praise his Lord and extol Him, for when a man seeks a need from a ruler, he prepares for him the best speech he is able to muster.' So when you seek a need, glorify Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, and praise Him and extol Him, saying: 'O the Most Generous of those who give, and O the Best of those who are asked, O the Most Merciful of those who are shown mercy, O the One, O the Eternal, O He who did not beget nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, O He who took no companion and no son, O He who does what He wills and decrees what He desires and ordains what He loves, O He who turns between a man and his heart, O He who is at the Exalted View, O He who is like nothing else, O the All-Hearing, O the All-Seeing!' And frequent the Names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the Names of Allah are many, and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny, and say: 'O Allah, expand upon me from Your permissible sustenance that which I can suffice with, and repay with regarding my trust, and connect with my kinship, and it be a help to me in Hajj and Umrah.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man entered the mosque, prayed two cycles, then asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The servant hastened his Lord. Then another came, prayed two cycles, then praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and sent blessings upon the Prophet and his Progeny. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Ask, you will be given.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Kahmas, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: A man entered the Masjid, so he began (asking) before the laudation upon Allah and the Blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The servant hastened with his Lord'. Then another one entered, so he prayed and lauded upon Allah Mighty and Majestic, and sent Blessings upon Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Ask, you would be Given'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is the laudation upon Allah and the Salat upon His Rasool before the asking, and if one of you goes over to the man seeking the need, so he would love it if you were to be saying to him good (words) before you ask him for the need'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'There are two Verses in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that I seek but do not find (understand).' He said, 'And what are they?' I said, 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Call upon Me, I will Answer you. So we supplicate to Him and do not see an Answer.' He said, 'Do you think Allah, Mighty and Majestic, broke His Promise?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So where is that (view of yours) from?' I said, 'I do not know.' He said, 'But I will inform you. The one who obeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in whatever He commanded him, then supplicates to Him from the aspect of the supplication, He answers him.' I said, 'And what is the aspect of the supplication?' He said, 'You begin by praising Allah and mentioning His bounties upon you, then thanking Him, then sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then mentioning your sins and acknowledging them, then seeking refuge from them. So this is the aspect of the supplication.' Then he said, 'And what is the other Verse?' I said, 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And whatever thing you spend, He replaces it, and He is the best of Sustainers. And I spend and I do not see a replacement.' He said, 'Do you think Allah, Mighty and Majestic, broke His Promise?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So where is that (view of yours) from?' I said, 'I do not know.' He said, 'If one of you earns wealth from its permissible source and spends it in permissible ways, he would not spend a Dirham except that He replaces it upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who wants his supplication to be answered, let him purify his earnings.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no group of forty men who gather and supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, regarding a matter, except that Allah answers them. If they are not forty, then four people supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ten times, except that Allah answers them. If they are not four, then one person supplicates to Allah forty times, and Allah, the Almighty, the Compeller, answers him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abdul A' from Abdul A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Any group of four men who gather upon a single matter and supplicate to Allah, they do not disperse except having received an answer.

From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'aba, from Ali ibn Uqba, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: My father (peace be upon him), whenever a matter grieved him, would gather the women and the children, then supplicate, and they would say 'Ameen'.

From him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur al-Sayqal, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes a man supplicates with a supplication, so it is answered for him, then that is delayed for a while.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'And why is that, so that he may increase in supplication?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Abi Hilal al-Madainy, from Hadeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when the servant supplicates, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the two angels: 'I have answered him, but withhold his need, for I love to hear his voice.' And when the servant supplicates, Allah, Blessed and High, says: 'Hasten his need for him, for I dislike hearing his voice.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sulayman, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The supplication is answered for a man, then it is delayed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, (for) twenty years.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was forty years between the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, 'Your supplication has been accepted,' and the Seizing of the Pharaoh.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from more than one of our companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant who is a friend of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) supplicates to Allah regarding the matter delegated to Him, so He says to the Angel allocated with him: 'Fulfil for My servant his need, but do not hasten it, for I desire to hear his call and his voice'; and the servant who is an enemy of Allah supplicates to Allah regarding the matter delegated to Him, so it is said to the Angel allocated with him: 'Fulfil for My servant his need and hasten it, for I dislike to hear his call and his voice'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So the people would say, 'This one has not been given except due to his prestige, and this one has not been prevented except due to his indignity'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believer does not cease to be in goodness and hope for the mercy of Allah, Exalted and Majestic, as long as he does not hasten, so he despairs and leaves supplication. I said to him, 'How does he hasten?' He said, 'He says, I have been supplicating since such and such (time) and I do not see the answer.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the believer supplicates to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding his need, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Delay its answer, out of desire for his voice and his supplication.' So when it is the Day of Judgment, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant, you supplicated to Me, so I delayed your answer, and your reward is such and such; and you supplicated to Me regarding such and such, so I delayed answering you, and your reward is such and such.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So the believer wishes that no supplication of his had been answered in the world, due to what he sees of the excellence of the reward.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'Supplication is the weapon of the believer, and the pillar of the religion, and the light of the heavens and the earth.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Supplications are the keys to success and the treasuries of prosperity. The best supplication is that which emanates from a pure chest and a pious heart. In intimate prayer lies the cause of salvation, and through sincerity comes liberation. When fear intensifies, then to God is the refuge.

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not guide you to a weapon that saves you from your enemies and generates your sustenance?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You should supplicate to your Lord by night and by day, for the weapon of the Believer is supplication (du'a).' .

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Supplication is the shield of the believer, and whenever you knock frequently on a door, it will be opened for you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he used to say to his companions: 'It is upon you to take up the weapon of the Prophets.' So it was said: 'And what is the weapon of the Prophets?' He said: 'Supplication.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Sa'id al-Bajali who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, supplication is more piercing than the spear-head.'
From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'The supplication is more piercing than the spear-heads of iron.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Supplication remains veiled/barred until blessings are sent upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.

From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever supplicates and does not mention the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), the supplication hovers over his head. So when he mentions the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), the supplication is raised.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not make me like the water container of the rider, for the rider fills his container and drinks it whenever he desires. Make me [part of] the beginning of the supplication, and at its end, and in its middle.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father and Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is mentioned, increase your sending of blessings upon him. For whoever sends one blessing upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), Allah sends a thousand blessings upon him in a thousand rows of angels, and nothing from what Allah created remains except that it sends blessings upon the servant for the blessing of Allah upon him and the blessing of His angels upon him. Therefore, whoever does not desire this is ignorant and deceived. Allah has disavowed him, and His Messenger, and his Household.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever sends blessings upon me, Allah and His angels send blessings upon him, and whoever wishes, let him be scarce (with it), and whoever wishes, let him be frequent (with it).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Prayer upon me and upon my Household removes hypocrisy.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Imran Al-Azdi, from Abdullah ibn Al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says, 'O Lord, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad' one hundred times, one hundred needs will be fulfilled for him: thirty for the world and the remainder for the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, all from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every supplication with which Allah (Exalted and Majestic) is supplicated is veiled from the sky until blessings are sent upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have dedicated a third of my supplications to you.' He said to him, 'Good.' The man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have dedicated half of my supplications to you.' He said to him, 'That is better.' The man said, 'I have dedicated all of my supplications to you.' He said, 'Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will suffice you from whatever concerns you regarding the affairs of your world and your Hereafter.' A man said to him, 'May Allah keep you well, how does he dedicate his supplication to him?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for anything except that he begins with the supplication (Salat) upon Muhammad and his Family (peace be upon them).'

Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Raise your voices with the blessings upon me, for it removes hypocrisy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: There is nothing in the Scale heavier than the Salat (blessings) upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. And indeed, when a man's deeds are placed in the Scale, it tilts due to them (his sins). So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) brings out the Salat upon him and places it in his Scale, so it outweighs them.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, from his men, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who has a need for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, let him begin with the Salawat upon Muhammad and his Progeny, then he should ask his need, then he should conclude with the Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more Benevolent than that He would accept the two ends and leave the middle, whenever there is Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, it is not blocked from Him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Abdul Salam ibn Nuaym, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I entered the House (the Kaaba) and nothing of supplication was present to me except the Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, no one has departed with anything superior to what you departed with.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Mufaddal ibn Salih al-Asadi, from Muhammad ibn Harun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When one of you prays and does not mention the Prophet and his Progeny (peace be upon them) in his prayer, his prayer is taken by a path other than the way to Paradise. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He in whose presence I am mentioned and does not send blessings upon me, will enter the Fire, so Allah will distance him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'And he in whose presence I am mentioned and forgets to send blessings upon me, he is made to err on the path to Paradise.'
