Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Thabit, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one in whose presence I am mentioned, and he forgets to send blessings upon me, Allah causes him to err on the path to Paradise.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father heard a man attaching himself to the House (Kaaba) and he was saying: 'O Allah! Send blessings upon Muhammad.' So my father said to him: 'O servant of Allah! Do not amputate it! Do not be unjust to us regarding our right! Say: O Allah! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the People of his Household.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah ibn Al-Jaroud Al-Hudhali, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yassar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no gathering in which the righteous and the immoral gather and they remain upon the remembrance of other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that it will be a regret upon them on the Day of Judgment.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wahb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: No group of people will gather in a gathering without mentioning Allah, Exalted and Majestic, and without mentioning us, except that gathering will be a regret upon them on the Day of Judgment. Then he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Our mention is from the mention of Allah, and the mention of our enemies is from the mention of Satan.'

And by his chain, he said, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The one who intends that he be measured with the fullest measure (maximum reward), so let him say whenever he intends to arise from his gathering, Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Honour, from what they are describing And peace be on the Messengers And the Praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is written in the Torah which has not been altered, that Musa (peace be upon him) asked his Lord, saying: 'O Lord! Are You close to me so I may whisper to You, or are You distant so I may call out to You?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Musa! I am the Companion of the one who Mentions Me.' So Musa said: 'Then who will be in Your Veil on the Day when there is no veil except Your Veil?' He said: 'Those who Mention Me, so I Mention them; and those who love one another for My sake, so I love them. Therefore, they are those whom, whenever I intend to strike the people of the earth with evil, I Remember them, and I repel it from them because of them.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Husayn ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no group of people who gather in a gathering and do not mention the Name of Allah, Exalted and Majestic, and do not send blessings upon their Prophet, except that that gathering becomes a regret and a burden upon them.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the Mention of Allah while you are urinating, for the Mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is good in every state; therefore, do not tire of the Mention of Allah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! Do not rejoice in the abundance of wealth, nor leave My remembrance in every state, for the abundance of wealth causes one to forget sins, and indeed, leaving My remembrance hardens the hearts.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is written in the Torah which has not been altered that Musa (peace be upon him) asked his Lord (may He be exalted) saying: 'My God! A situation comes upon me such that it would not be honourable and majestic for You that I should mention You therein'. So He said: 'O Musa! My Mention is good upon every state'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Musa: 'Increase your remembrance of Me by night and by day, and be humble during My remembrance, and be patient during My afflictions, and find peace during My remembrance, and worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. To Me is the final return. O Musa! Make Me your treasure and place your store of lasting righteous deeds with Me.'

And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Musa: 'Make your tongue behind your heart, you will be safe, and frequent My remembrance by night and day, and do not follow the sin in its quarry for you will regret, for the sin is a provision for the people of the Fire.'
And by his chain, He said: Among what Allah whispered to Musa (peace be upon him) He said: 'O Musa! Do not forget Me in every state, for forgetting Me causes the heart to die.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Usman, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O son of Adam! Mention Me in a gathering, I shall mention you in a gathering better than your gathering.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The one who mentions Me in a gathering of the people, I shall mention him in a gathering of the Angels.'
Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Wuhayb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Our Shias are those who, when they are alone, remember Allah frequently.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever frequently remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah will love him; and whoever frequently remembers Allah, two acquittals are written for him: an acquittal from the Fire and an acquittal from hypocrisy.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr, from Zurara ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Glorification of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) is from the Abundant Remembrance of which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke: 'Mention Allah with a frequent Mentioning.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Wassha from Dawud al-Hammarr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever frequently remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah will shade him in His Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believer dies by every type of death except the thunderbolt; it does not seize him while he is remembering Allah, Exalted and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The thunderbolts will not strike a dhakir (one who remembers Allah).' I said, 'And what is the dhakir?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recites one hundred verses.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wuheyb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the death of the believer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer dies with every death; he dies by drowning, and he dies by crushing, and is afflicted by beasts, and he dies by the thunderbolt, and the thunderbolt does not strike the one who remembers Allah, Exalted and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'The one who is preoccupied with My remembrance (dhikr) to the exclusion of asking Me (for his needs), I shall give him the best of what I give to the one who asks Me.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Harun ibn Kharjah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the servant may have a need for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so he begins with praising Allah and sending blessings upon Muhammad and the family of peace upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, until he forgets his need; then Allah fulfills it for him without his having asked Him for it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Suleyman ibn 'Amr, from Abu al-Maghra' al-Kassaf He raised it, saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever mentions Allah, Exalted and Mighty, in private, has indeed mentioned Allah frequently. Indeed, the hypocrites used to mention Allah publicly and did not mention Him in private.' They show off to people and do not mention Allah except for a little.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, raising it, said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Isa (peace be upon him): 'O Isa! Mention Me within yourself, I will mention you within Myself, and mention Me in your gathering, I shall mention you in a gathering better than the gathering of the human beings. O Isa! Soften your heart for Me and frequent My mention in the isolation, and know that My gladness is that you look to Me and become lively during that and do not become (like) dead.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The Angel does not write down except what he hears, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says: 'And remember your Lord within yourself humbly and fearing.' So no one knows the reward of that remembrance in the self of the man apart from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, due to His greatness.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who remembers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, among the oblivious ones is like the fighter among the battling ones.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, among the oblivious ones is like the fighter among the fleeing ones, and the fighter among the fleeing ones has Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Saeed al-Qammat, from al-Mufazzal, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, teach me a comprehensive supplication.' So he said to me, 'Praise Allah, for there would not remain anyone who prays except that he supplicates for you, saying, 'Allah hears the one who praises Him'.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which of the deeds is most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That you praise Him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Anbary, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to praise Allah three hundred and sixty times every day, corresponding to the number of the veins in the body, saying: 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin' frequently in every state.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, all from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithamī, from Ya'qūb ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: In the son of Ādam there are three hundred and sixty veins; from these, one hundred and eighty are moving, and from these, one hundred and eighty are still. If the moving ones were to stay still, he would not sleep, and if the still ones were to move, he would not sleep.' And it was so that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever it was morning, said: 'Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbil-'ālamīn' (The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds) frequently, upon every state, three hundred and sixty times, and whenever it was evening, said similar to that.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Sa'id ibn Janah, who said: Abu Mas'ud narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: Whoever says four times when it is morning, 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin' (Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds), has fulfilled the gratitude of his day; and whoever says it when it is evening, has fulfilled the gratitude of his night.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Every supplication that does not have praise before it is cut off. Rather, it is the praise, then the glorification. I said, 'I do not know what suffices from the praise and glorification.' He said: O Allah, You are the First, so there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, so there is nothing after You, and You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing below You, and You are the Mighty, the Wise.

And by this chain, he said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) What is the least of what would suffice me, from the Praise? He (peace be upon him) said: You should say, The Praise is for Allah Who is Exalted, so Subdues, and the Praise is for Allah Who is King, so is Able, and the Praise is for Allah Who is within, so is Knowing, and the Praise is for Allah Who Causes the living to die and Revives the dead, and He is Able upon everything.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of supplications is seeking forgiveness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Husayn ibn Saif, from Abu Jameela, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the servant frequents in seeking the Forgiveness, his parchment (record of deeds) is raised and it would be gleaming'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: The example of seeking forgiveness is like a leaf on a tree that is shaken, so it falls off; and the one who seeks forgiveness from a sin but continues to commit it is like the one mocking his Lord.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not rise from a gathering, even if it was small, until he sought forgiveness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, twenty-five times.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would seek forgiveness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seventy times every day, and repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seventy times. I said, 'Was he saying: I seek forgiveness of Allah and I repent to Him?' He said, 'He was saying: I seek forgiveness of Allah, I seek forgiveness of Allah, seventy times, and he was saying: And I repent to Allah, and I repent to Allah, seventy times.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Husayn ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The seeking of forgiveness and the saying "There is no god except Allah" is the best of worship.' Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, says: 'So know that there is no god but Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The poor came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the wealthy have what they use to free slaves, and we do not; they have what they use to perform Hajj, and we do not; they have what they use to give in charity, and we do not; they have what they use to strive in Jihad, and we do not.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever says Allahu Akbar (God is Greatest) one hundred times, it is better than freeing one hundred slaves; and whoever says Subhan Allah (Glory be to God) one hundred times, it is better than guiding one hundred camels; and whoever says Alhamdulillah (Praise be to God) one hundred times, it is better than carrying one hundred horses in the way of Allah, with their saddles, bridles, and riders; and whoever says La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but God) one hundred times, he is the most superior of people in deed that day, except for one who increases (in it).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So that reached the wealthy, and they did it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So the poor returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what you said reached the wealthy, so they did it.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That is Allah's grace; He grants it to whom He wills.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Fuzayl, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Frequent the Tahleel (declaring the Oneness of God) and the Takbeer (declaring the Greatness of God), for there is nothing more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than the Tahleel and the Takbeer.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The Tasbeeh (glorification) is half the scale, and 'Al-hamdu lillah' (praise be to Allah) fills the scale, and 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest) fills what is between the sky and the earth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a man planting a sapling in a wall of his. So he paused for him and said: 'Shall I indicate to you a plant whose roots are firm, whose growth is quick, whose fruit is sweet, and which remains (forever)?' He said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah!' So he said: 'When it is morning and evening, say: 'Glory be to Allah, and the Praise is for Allah, and there is no God except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest'. For you, if you say it, for every glorification, there will be ten trees in Paradise from various kinds of fruit, and these are from the righteous enduring good deeds.' He said: So the man said, 'So I testify, O Messenger of Allah, that this wall of mine is a charity, held in possession, for the poor Muslims, the people of charity.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed verses from the Quran: 'Then as for him who gives away and fears [God] and accepts the best, We will facilitate for him the easy end.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of worship is the saying: There is no god except Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Verily, supplication repels the decree and breaks it, just as the thread is broken, even though it has been twirled firmly.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Umar ibn Yazid who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Verily, supplication repels what has already been pre-determined and what has not been pre-determined.' I said: 'What has been pre-determined, I understand that — but what of what has not been pre-determined?' He said: 'So that it does not happen.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Bistam al-Zayyat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, supplication repels the divine decree, even though it has descended from the sky and has been firmly sealed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hammam Ismail ibn Hammam, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: Verily, supplication and affliction accompany each other until the Day of Judgment. Verily, supplication repels affliction even when it has been firmly decreed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Supplication repels the affliction that has descended and what has not yet descended.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I not point you to something in which the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) made no exception?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Supplication repels the decree, even though it has been firmly established.' And he clasped his fingers.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Supplication repels the decree even after it has been firmly decided. So increase your supplications, for it is the key to every mercy and the achievement of every need. What is with God — Mighty and Majestic — cannot be attained except through supplication. And indeed, there is no door that is frequently knocked upon except that it is imminent that it shall be opened for its seeker.

Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: 'Incumbent upon you is supplication, for supplication to Allah and seeking from Allah repels the affliction even after it has been pre-determined and decreed, with nothing remaining but its execution. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is supplicated and asked, He turns away the affliction with a complete turning away.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repels through supplication the matter which He knew would be supplicated for, and so He responds. And if the servant had not been granted success in making that supplication, he would have been struck by it — by something that would bend his face to the earth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al Maghra', from Al Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The most rapid (of supplications) and the quickest (to be answered) is the supplication of a man for his brother in his absence.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man's supplication for his brother in his absence will cause sustenance to flow and repel misfortunes.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding His saying, the Blessed and Exalted: And He answers those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them from His grace. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the believer who supplicates for his brother in his absence, so the angel says to him,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The supplication quickest to succeed for the Answering is the supplication of a brother for his brother in his absence. He begins by supplicating for his brother, so the Angel allocated to him says, "Ameen, and for you is the like of it."'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Ismail ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tameemi, from Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no believer who supplicates for the believers and the believing women, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will return upon him the like of what he supplicated for them with, from every believer and believing woman who passed away from the beginning of time or who is coming until the Day of Judgment.' Indeed, the servant is commanded to be dragged to the Fire on the Day of Judgment, so he is pulled, and the believers and the believing women say, 'O Lord! This is the one who was supplicating for us, so intercede for him on our behalf.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepts their intercession regarding him, so he attains salvation.

Ali, from his father, who narrated from his father, said: I saw Abdullah ibn Jundab in the standing place (of Arafat), and I did not see a standing place that was better than his standing. He continued extending his hands to the sky, and his tears were flowing upon his cheeks until they reached the ground. So when the people dispersed, I said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad, I have not seen any standing place that was better than your standing.' He said, 'By Allah, I did not supplicate except for my brethren. And that is because Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) informed me that whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, a call is made from the Throne: 'And for you is a hundred thousand times [the reward].' So I disliked that I should leave a guaranteed hundred thousand for one [supplication] which I do not know whether it will be answered or not.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Suwayr who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: 'The angels, when they hear a believer supplicating for his believing brother in his absence, or mentioning him with goodness, say: You are a good brother to your brother, for you supplicate for him with goodness while he is absent from you, and you mention him with goodness. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given you double what you asked for him, and lauded upon you double what you lauded upon him, and for you is the merit over him.' And when they hear him mentioning his brother with evil and supplicating against him, they say to him: You are an evil brother to your brother! Refrain, O you who is veiled over his sins and his private parts, and be still with yourself, and praise Allah who veiled over you, and know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more knowing of His servant than you are.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Abdullah al-Qummi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three (people), their supplications are answered: the Pilgrim, so consider how you could be his replacement (look after his affairs in his absence); and the fighter in the Way of Allah, so consider how you could be his replacement; and the sick one, so do not enrage him nor bore him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Five supplications are not blocked from the Lord, Blessed and Exalted: The supplication of the equitable Imam; and the supplication of the oppressed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic says: "I shall exact revenge for you, even if it be after a while"; and the supplication of the righteous child for his parents; and the supplication of the righteous father for his child; and the supplication of the believer for his brother in his absence, so He says: "And for you is the like of it".'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for it is raised above the clouds until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, looks at it, then He says: 'Raise it until I answer him.' And beware of the supplication of the father, for it is sharper than the sword.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who presents (or supplicates for) forty from the believers, then supplicates (for himself), it will be answered for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talha al-Nahdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four (people), a supplication would not be rejected for them until the Doors of the sky are Opened and it comes to the Throne – the parent for his child, and the oppressed against the one who oppressed him, and the one gone to perform Umrah until he returns, and the Fasting one until he breaks (the Fast)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is nothing quicker to an answer than the supplication of an absentee for an absentee.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Moses (peace be upon him) supplicated, and Aaron (peace be upon him) said 'Ameen', and the Angels (peace be upon them) said 'Ameen'. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Your supplication has been accepted, therefore be steadfast.' And whoever fights in the Way of Allah, he will be answered, just as He answered for both of you, on the Day of Judgment.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I accompanied him between Mecca and Medina. A beggar came, so he ordered that he be given. Then another came, so he ordered that he be given. Then another came, so he ordered that he be given. Then the fourth came, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah satisfy you.' Then he turned to us and said: 'Indeed, we have what we can give him, but I fear that we may become like one of the three whose supplication is not answered.' A man whom Allah gave wealth, so he spent it in that which was not its rightful place, then he says: 'O Allah, grant me,' so it is not answered for him. And a man who supplicates against his wife that he be freed from her, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made her matter to him. And a man who supplicates against his neighbor, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the way open for him to move away from his neighbor's vicinity and sell his house.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Four (types of people) for whom a supplication is not answered: A man who sits in his house saying, 'O Allah, grant me sustenance,' so it is said to him, 'Did I not command you to seek (it)?' And a man who has a wife, so he supplicates against her, so it is said to him, 'Did I not make her matter to you?' And a man who had wealth, so he squandered it, so he says, 'O Allah, grant me sustenance,' so it is said to him, 'Did I not command you with moderation? Did I not command you with rectitude?' Then He said, 'And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, and are between that, standing firm (in balance).' And a man who had wealth, so he lent it out without clear evidence, so it is said to him, 'Did I not command you with witnessing?' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Imran ibn Abu Aasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three people, their supplication is returned upon them: a man whom Allah granted wealth, so he spent it in other than its proper way, then he says, "O Lord, grant me sustenance," so it is said to him, "Did I not grant you?"' And a man who supplicates against his wife while he is unjust to her, so it is said to him, "Did I not make her matter in your hand?"' And a man who sits in his house and says, "O Lord, grant me sustenance," so it is said to him, "Did I not make for you the way to seek sustenance?"'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a neighbor of mine and what I endured from him. He said to me: 'Supplicate against him.' I said: 'So I did, but I did not see anything.' So I returned to him and complained to him. He said to me: 'Supplicate against him.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have done so, but I did not see anything.' He said: 'How did you supplicate against him?' I said: 'When I met him, I supplicated against him.' He said: 'Supplicate against him when he turns his back and when he faces you.' So I did it, and I did not delay long before Allah gave me rest from him.

And it is reported from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Whenever one of you supplicates against anyone, he should say: 'O Allah, strike him with an affliction for which there is no equal, and crack his sanctity'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have a neighbor from Quraysh, from the family of Muhriz, who has publicized my name and made me well-known; whenever I passed by him, he would say: This is the Rafidi, who carries the wealth to Ja'far ibn Muhammad.' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'So supplicate to Allah against him when you are in the night prayer, while you are prostrating in the final prostration of the first two cycles. So praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and glorify Him, and say:' O Allah, so-and-so son of so-and-so has publicized me and made me well-known, and angered me and exposed me to hardships. O Allah, strike him with an immediate arrow that occupies him with it from me. O Allah, bring closer his death and cut off his trace, and hasten that, O Lord, this moment, this moment. He said: 'So when we arrived in Kufa, we arrived at night, and I asked my family about him. I said: What happened to so-and-so? They said: He is sick. And the end of my speech had not passed until I heard a cry from his house, and they said that he had died.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Yaqub ibn Salim, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Al-A'ala ibn Kamil said to him, 'So-and-so does this to me and does that to me. If you see fit, supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is weakness with you. Say:' O Allah, indeed You suffice from every thing, and nothing suffices from You, so suffice me from the matter of so-and-so with whatever You will, and however You will, and from wherever You will, and whenever You will.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Misma'i, who said: When Dawud ibn Ali killed Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I will surely supplicate to Allah against the one who killed my master and took my wealth.' So Dawud ibn Ali said to him: 'You are threatening me with your supplication?' Hammad said: Al-Misma'i said: 'Mo'tab narrated to me that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) did not cease being in Ruku' and Sajdah throughout his night. So when it was in the pre-dawn hours, I heard him saying while he was in Sajdah: 'O Allah! I ask You by Your Strong Power and by Your Intense Majesty, which all Your creation is humble before, that You send Salat upon Muhammad and the People of his Household, and that You seize him at the moment, at the moment.' So he had not raised his head until we heard the shriek in the house of Dawud ibn Ali. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) raised his head and said: 'I supplicated to Allah with a supplication, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent an Angel upon him, so he struck his head with an iron sledgehammer, his bladder split from it, so he died.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu Masrouq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'We speak to the people, and we use as proof against them the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority from among you.' But they say, 'It was revealed regarding the commanders of the battalions.' So we use as proof against them the Word of Him, Mighty and Majestic: 'Only Allah is your Guardian and His Messenger,' up to the end of the verse. But they say, 'It was revealed regarding the believers.' And we use as proof against them the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it except love of kinship.' But they say, 'It was revealed regarding the relatives of the Muslims.' He said, 'So I did not leave anything that came to my mind from these arguments and similar ones, but I mentioned it. So he said to me: 'When it is like that, call them to the Mubahila (imprecation).'' I said, 'And how should I do it?' He said, 'Prepare yourself for three (days), and I think he said: 'And fast, and perform ghusl, and go out, you and he, to Al-Jabban (the place of meeting).'' So intertwine your fingers from your right hand with his fingers, then be fair with him, and begin with yourself. And say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths, Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Beneficent, the Merciful. If Abu Masrouq is denying the truth and claiming falsehood, then send down upon him a reckoning from the sky or a painful punishment.' Then return the supplication upon him, and say: 'And if so-and-so is denying the truth and claiming falsehood, then send down upon him a reckoning from the sky or a painful punishment.' Then he said to me: 'Indeed, you will not be long before you see that in him. And by Allah, I have not found any creature who will answer me to it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Mukhlad Abu al-Shukr, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The time during which the imprecation (Mubahila) is performed is what is between the emergence of the dawn and the emergence of the sun. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Makhlad Abu al-Shukr, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ahmad, from one of our companions, regarding the imprecation (Mubahala). He said: 'Intertwine your fingers with his fingers, then you should say: O Allah! If so-and-so has denied a truth and acknowledged a falsehood, then strike him with a reckoning/thunderbolt from the sky or with a punishment from Your Presence, and you should curse him seventy times.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the Imprecation (Mubahala), he (peace be upon him) said: 'Intertwine your fingers with his fingers, then you should say: O Allah! If so-and-so has denied a truth and acknowledged a falsehood, then strike him with a reckoning from the sky or with a punishment from Your Presence, and you should curse him seventy times.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, from one of his companions, who said: When the man denies the truth, and if you intend to perform mubahala (imprecation) with him, say: O Allah, Lord of the seven skies and Lord of the seven earths, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne! If so-and-so has denied the truth and disbelieved in it, then send down upon him a reckoning from the sky or a painful punishment.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from one of his companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are three hours in the night and three hours in the day in which He glorifies Himself. So the first of the hours of the day is when the sun is on this side, meaning from the east, its measure is from Al-'Asr, meaning from the west, up to the first Salat; and the first of the hours of the night is in the remaining third of the night, up to when the dawn breaks. He says: 'I am Allah, Lord of the worlds. I am Allah, the Almighty, the Wise. I am Allah, the Forgiving, the Merciful. I am Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I am Allah, the Master of the Day of Judgment. I am Allah, I have not ceased and will not cease. I am Allah, Creator of good and evil. I am Allah, Creator of Paradise and Fire. I am Allah, the Originator of all things, and to Me is the return. I am Allah, the One, the Eternal. I am Allah, the Knower of the unseen and the seen. I am Allah, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Believer, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Majestic. I am Allah, the Creator, the Evolver, the Fashioner. For Me are the Good Names. I am Allah, the Great, the Exalted.' He said, then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said from himself: 'And Greatness is His Robe, so whoever competes with Him for any part of that, Allah will cast him into the Fire.' Then he said: 'There is no believing servant who supplicates with these, with his heart facing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah fulfills his need, and if he was unfortunate, I hope he will be transformed into a fortunate one.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abdullah ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, glorifies Himself three times every day and night. So whoever glorifies Allah with what He glorified Himself with, then if he was in a state of misery, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will turn him to happiness. He should say: You are Allah, there is no god except You, Lord of the worlds. You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Beneficent, the Merciful. You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Mighty, the Exalted, the Great. You are Allah, there is no god except You, Master of the Day of Judgment. You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Forgiving, the Merciful. You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Mighty, the Wise. You are Allah, there is no god except You, from You the creation began and to You it returns. You are Allah, Who, there is no god except You, You have not ceased and will not cease. You are Allah, Who, there is no god except You, the Creator of good and evil. You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Creator of Paradise and the Fire. You are Allah, there is no god except You, One, Eternal, He neither begets nor is begotten, nor is there any equivalent to Him. You are Allah, there is no god except You, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Believer, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Exalted. Glory be to Allah from what they associate. He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Designer. For Him are the Good Names. There glorifies to Him whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Great, and the Greatness is Your Robe.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no thing greater in reward than the testimony that there is no god except Allah. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, nothing can equate to Him, and no one shares with Him in the affairs.'

From him, from Al-Fudayl ibn Abd al-Wahhab, from Is'haq ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, raising it (to the Prophet), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever says "La ilaha illa Allah" (There is no god but Allah), a tree is planted for him in Paradise made of red sapphire, its root in white musk, sweeter than honey, whiter than snow, and more fragrant than musk. In it are fruits like the breasts of virgins, rising above seventy coverings.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of worship is the saying "La ilaha illa Allah".' And he said: 'The best of worship is seeking forgiveness (Istighfar), and this is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: "So know that there is no god but Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin."'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer Layth al-Muradi, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Utba, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever says ten times, before the sun rises and before it sets: “There is no god but Allah, Alone, there is no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He causes death and gives life, and He is Ever-Living and will not die. In His Hand is the goodness, and He is Able over all things,” it will be an expiation for his sins for that day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Umar ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever prays the morning prayer and says, before shaking his knees, ten times,' There is no god except Allah, Alone, there is no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Ever-Living and will not die. In His Hand is the good, and He is Able over all things. And in the evening (he says) similar to it. A servant would not meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a deed superior to his deed, except for the one who comes with a similar deed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, brother of Udaym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says ten times, 'O Lord, O Lord', it will be said to him, 'At your service! What is your need?'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said: Ismail, son of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), fell sick, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Say, "O Lord, O Lord" ten times, for whoever says that will be called out: "At your service! What is your need?".'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who says, 'O Lord, O Allah, O Lord, O Allah,' until his breath is cut off, it will be said to him, 'At your service! What is your need?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man supplicates and says after his supplication, 'Whatever Allah willed, there is no might and no strength except with Allah,' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant has strived and submitted to My command. Fulfill his need.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who says, “Whatever Allah so Desires, there is neither might nor strength except with Allah,” seventy times, seventy types of afflictions will be averted from him, the least of which is suffocation.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is suffocation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He will not fall ill with insanity, so he would suffocate.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ghalib ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'and their shadows by the morning and the evening,' he said: 'It is the supplication before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and it is a time of acceptance.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Iblees, upon him be the Curse of Allah, sends out the armies of the night from when the sun sets and emerges. Therefore, increase the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during these two hours, and seek Refuge with Allah from the evil of Iblees and his armies, and shelter your young ones during those two hours, for they are the two hours of negligence.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Razin, the master of the Anmat, from one of the two (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says: 'O Allah, I call You to witness, and I call Your亲近 angels and the chosen bearers of Your Throne to witness that You are Allah, there is no god but You, the Beneficent, the Merciful; and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger; and that So-and-so and So-and-so are my Imam and my Guardian; and that their father is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali, and Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn, and So-and-so and So-and-so, until it reaches him (Al-Qaim), [these] are my Imams and my Guardians. Upon this I live, and upon this I die, and upon this I will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment; and I disavow So-and-so and So-and-so and So-and-so.' If he dies on that night, he will enter Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal and Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ishaq Al-Sha'iri, from Yazeed ibn Kalthama, from Abu Abdillah or from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: You say: 'I have become, by Allah, a believer upon the religion of Muhammad and his Sunnah, and the religion of Ali and his Sunnah, and the religion of the Successors and their Sunnah. I believe in their secrets and their public matters, and their seen and their unseen. And I seek Refuge with Allah from what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him) and the Successors sought Refuge from, and I desire for Allah what they desired for Him, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Shihab and Suleym al-Farra’, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says this when it is evening, will be wrapped by a wing from the wings of Jibraeel (peace be upon him) until morning, ‘I entrust to Allah, the Exalted, the Supreme, the Majestic, the Magnificent, myself and the one whose matter concerns me. I entrust to Allah my soul, which is feared, awed, and trembles before His greatness. Three times.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba and Ghalib ibn Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When it is evening, say: 'O Allah! I ask You at the approaching of Your night and the departure of Your day, and the presence of Your prayers and the sounds of Your supplications, that You send prayers upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and supplicate with whatever you like.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'There is no day that comes to the son of Adam except that that day says to him: O son of Adam! I am a new day, and I am a witness upon you, so speak good in me and do good in me, and I shall testify for you with it on the Day of Judgment, for you will not see me after it ever.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so that whenever Ali (peace be upon him) became evening, he would say: Welcome to the new night and the recording witness, write by the Name of Allah.' Then he would mention (do dhikr of) Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Al-Sindy, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the sun changes (at midday), remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; and if you are with a group of people who are pre-occupying you, then stand up and supplicate.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three (things) were transmitted successively by the Prophets, from Adam (peace be upon him) until they reached the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When he would morning, he would say: O Allah, I ask You for faith that accompanies my heart, and conviction until I know that nothing will befall me except what You have decreed for me, and make me pleased with what You have apportioned for me. And some of our companions have narrated it and added to it: 'Until I do not love the hastening of what You have delayed, nor the delaying of what You have hastened. O Living, O Eternal! By Your mercy I cry for help. Rectify for me all my affairs, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, ever. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his family.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, raising it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that he used to say: O Allah, I and this day are two creations from Your creations. O Allah, do not test me with it, nor test it with me. O Allah, do not let me be seen as audacious in disobeying You, nor as indulging in Your prohibitions. O Allah, turn away from me the doom, the adversities, the afflictions, the evil decrees, the gloating of the enemies, and the evil sight in myself and my wealth. He said: And there is no servant who says when evening comes and when morning comes, 'I am pleased with Allah as Lord, and with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as Prophet, and with the Quran as the announcer, and with Ali as Imam' three times, except that it becomes a right upon Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, to please him on the Day of Judgment. He said: And he used to say (peace be upon him) when evening comes: 'In the morning we are grateful to Allah, and in the evening we are praising Allah. So for You is the praise just as we came to You in the evening as submitters, safe.' He said: And when morning comes, he said: 'We have come to the evening as grateful to Allah, and we have come to the morning as praising Allah. And the praise is to Allah just as we came to You in the morning as submitters, safe.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no servant who says, when it is morning before the emergence of the sun, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest of all, and Glory be to Allah morning and evening, and the abundant Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no associate for Him, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny,' except that an Angel would initiate and make these to be in the middle of his wings, and ascend with these to the sky of the world. So the Angels would be saying: 'What is with you?' So he would be Saying: 'With me are words which were spoke by a man from the believers, and these are such and such'. So they would be saying: 'May Allah have Mercy on the one who said these words, and Forgive (his sins) for him'. He said: 'And every time he passes by a sky, he would say similar to that to its inhabitants, so they would be saying: 'May Allah have Mercy on the one who said these words, and Forgive (his sins) for him', until he would end up with these to the Bearers of the Throne. So he would be saying to them: 'With me are words which were spoke by a man from the believers, and these are such and such'. So they would be saying: 'May Allah have Mercy on this servant, and Forgive (his sins) for him. Go with these to the guardians of the treasures of the speeches of the believers, for these words are the treasure, until they write these down in the Register of the Treasures'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman ibn 'Isa, from 'Isa ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you wake up in the morning, say: 'O Allah! I seek refuge with You from the evil of what You created, spread, and released in Your lands and among Your servants. O Allah! I ask You by Your Majesty, Your Beauty, Your Forbearance, and Your Generosity, such and such.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-' from Al-'Ala' ibn Kamil, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and fearfully, and without being loud in speech during the evening.' 'There is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no Associate for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He causes to live and causes to die, and He causes to die and causes to live, and He is Able upon everything.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'In His Hand is the goodness'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'In His Hand is the goodness, but say just as I am saying it to you, ten times, and, 'I seek Refuge with Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing', when the sun emerges and when it sets, ten times'.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: After the morning prayer, say: 'The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the morning. The Praise is for Allah, the Splitter of the morning,' three times. O Allah! Open for me the door of the Command which wherein is the prosperity and the good health. O Allah! Prepare its way for me and show me its exit. O Allah! If You have Ordained for anyone from Your creatures capability upon me with the evil, so Seize him from his front, and his back, and from his right, and from his left, and from beneath his feet, and from above his head, and Enshroud him with whatever You so Desire to, from wherever You so Desire to, and however You so Desire to.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says when it is morning: 'O Allah, I have entered the morning under Your guarantee and Your protection. O Allah, I entrust to You my religion, my self, my worldly life, my Hereafter, my family, and my wealth; and I seek refuge in You, O Magnificent, from the evil of all Your creatures, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what Iblis and his soldiers confuse with.' When he says this speech, nothing will harm him on that day; and when it is evening and he says it, nothing will harm him that night, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you pray the Maghrib and the morning (Fajr) prayers, say: 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent,' seven times. For whoever says it, leprosy, vitiligo, insanity, and seventy types of afflictions will not befall him. He (peace be upon him) said: And when you morning and evening, say: 'The praise is for the Lord of the morning, the praise is for the Splitter of the dawn,' twice. 'The praise is for Allah, who removed the night by His power and brought the day by His mercy, and we are in health.' And recite the Verse of the Chair (Ayat al-Kursi), and the end of Surah Al-Hashr, and ten verses from Surah As-Saffat, and 'Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Honour, from what they describe. And peace be on the Messengers. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' So glorify Allah when you come to evening and when you come to morning. And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth. And at sunset and when you come to midday. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living and gives life to the earth after its death. And thus will you be brought forth. Holy, Holy, the Lord of the Angels and the Spirit. Your mercy precedes Your anger. There is no god except You. Glory be to You. I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me and turn to me. Indeed, You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) O Allah, to You is the praise. I praise You and seek Your assistance, and You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have entered the morning upon Your covenant and Your promise, and I believe in Your promise and fulfill Your covenant to the best of my ability. And there is no power and no strength except with Allah, Alone, without partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. I have entered the morning upon the fitrah of Islam, and the phrase of monotheism, and the religion of Ibrahim, and the religion of Muhammad. Upon that I live and die, if Allah wills. O Allah, keep me alive as long as You keep me alive with it, and cause me to die when You cause me to die upon it, and resurrect me when You resurrect me upon it, seeking Your pleasure and following Your path. To You I turn my back, and to You I delegate my affairs. The Progeny of Muhammad are my Imams, there is no Imam for me other than them. By them I follow, and them I befriend, and by them I am guided. O Allah, make them my guardians in this world and the Hereafter, and make me a friend of their friends and an enemy of their enemies in this world and the Hereafter, and join me with the righteous, and my fathers with them.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Teach me something I can say when it is morning and when it is evening.' So he said, 'Say: The Praise is for Allah Who does what He wills, and He alone does not do what others will. The Praise is for Allah just as Allah loves to be praised. The Praise is for Allah just as He is worthy of it.' O Allah, enter me into every goodness that You entered Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad into, and take me out from every evil that You took Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad out from, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi, from Amr ibn Mus'ab, from Furat ibn al-Ahnaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whatever you leave out of anything, do not leave out saying in every morning and evening: 'O Allah, I have reached morning seeking Your forgiveness in this morning and in this day for those deserving of Your mercy, and I disavow to You from those deserving of Your curse.' O Allah, I have reached morning disavowing to You in this day and in this morning from those among whom we are, from the polytheists and from what they used to worship. Indeed, they were an evil people, wicked. O Allah, make what You sent down from the sky to the earth in this morning and in this day a blessing upon Your friends and a punishment upon Your enemies. O Allah, befriend the one who befriends You, and be enemy to the one who is enemy to You. O Allah, end for me with safety and faith every time the sun rises or sets. O Allah, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small. O Allah, forgive the believing men and believing women, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. O Allah, indeed You know their movements and their dwellings. O Allah, protect the Imam of the Muslims with the protection of faith, and grant him a strong victory, and open for him an easy victory. And make for him and for us from You a persistent helper. O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so, and the differing sects upon Your Messenger and the Masters of Command after Your Messenger and the Imams after him and their Shias. And I ask You for increase from Your grace, and acknowledgment of what came from Your presence, and submission to Your command, and preservation of what You commanded with. I do not seek an exchange for it, nor sell it for a small price. O Allah, guide me among those You guided, and save me from the evil of what You decreed. Indeed You decree and it is not decreed upon You, and he whom You befriend is not humiliated. Blessed and Exalted are You. Glory be to You, Lord of the House. Accept from me my supplication and what I drew near to You with from goodness, and multiply it for me with a multiplied, great multiple. And give us from You mercy and a great reward. Lord, how excellent is what You tried me with, and how great is what You gav

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says at the end of the Fajr prayer and at the end of the Maghrib prayer, seven times: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is neither might nor strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent', Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will repel from him seventy types of afflictions, the easiest of which is the wind (hurricane), vitiligo, and insanity. And if he was wretched, his wretchedness will be erased, and he will be written among the fortunate.

And in a narration of Sa'dan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) similar to it, except that he said: 'The easiest of it is insanity, and leprosy, and vitiligo. And if he was wretched, I hope that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will transform him to be fortunate.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Similar to it, except that he said: 'Saying it three times in the morning and three times in the evening, one will not fear a Satan, nor a ruling authority, nor vitiligo, nor leprosy', and he did not say 'seven times'. Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'And I say it one hundred times'.

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you pray the morning and the Maghrib prayers, say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is neither might nor strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent,' seven times, for whoever says it will not be struck by insanity, nor leprosy, nor vitiligo, nor seventy types of afflictions.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Sa'd ibn Zayd, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: When you have prayed the Maghrib prayer, do not extend your leg and do not speak to anyone until you say one hundred times: 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'Ali al-'Azeem', and one hundred times in the morning. Whoever says it, Allah will repel from him one hundred types of afflictions; the least of which is vitiligo, leprosy, Satan, and the ruling authority.

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you evening comes, and you see the sun setting and turning away, then say:' 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Praise is to Allah Who did not take a son, and there was no partner for Him in the Kingdom.' Praise is to Allah Who is described and cannot be described, and He knows and cannot be fully known. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal. I seek Refuge with the Noble Face of Allah and by the Great Name of Allah from the evil of what He spread and created, and from the evil of what is beneath the earth, and from the evil of what is apparent and what is hidden. And from the evil of what was in the night and the day, and from the evil of Abu Murra (Satan) and what he begot, and from the evil of the Allurements, and from the evil of what I have described and what I have not described. So praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' He mentioned that it is a safety from the predatory beasts and from the Pelted Satan and from his offspring. He said: 'And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: When you morning comes,' 'Glory be to Allah, the King, the Holy,' three times. 'O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from the decline of Your Bounties, and from the changing of my health, and from the suddenness of Your Wrath, and from the attainment of wretchedness, and from the evil of what preceded in the Book.' 'O Allah! I ask You by the Might of Your Kingdom and the Intensity of Your Strength, and by the Magnificence of Your Authority, and by Your Power over Your creatures.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The supplication before the emergence of the sun and before its setting is a Sunnah, an Obligation with the emergence of the dawn and the Maghrib. You should be saying, ‘There is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no associates for Him. The Kingdom is for Him, and for Him is the Praise. He Causes to live and He Causes to die, and He Causes to die and He Causes to live, and He is Living and will not be dying. In His Hand is the goodness, and He is Able over everything’, ten times. And you should be saying, ‘I seek Refuge with Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing, from the suggestion of the Satan; and I seek Refuge with You, Lord, that they would be approaching me. Allah, He is the Hearing, the Knowing’, ten times before the emergence of the sun and before the setting. So if you were to forget, so make up for it just as you make up for the Salat when you forget it.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Say, 'I seek Refuge with Allah from the Pelted Satan, and I seek Refuge with Allah that he would approach me, and that Allah, He is the Hearing, the Knowing'. And say, 'There is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no associate for Him. He Causes to live and He Causes to die, and He is Able upon every thing'. He (the narrator) said, 'So a man said to him, 'Is it an Obligation?' He said: 'Yes, an Obligation, Limited. You should be saying before the emergence of the sun and before the setting, ten times. So if something is missed by you, so make up for it, from the night and the day'.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from a man, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-A'ala ibn Kamil Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the supplications is that which is befitting for its performer, when he forgets it, to make up for it.' He should say after the morning (prayer): 'There is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no associates for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He causes to live and He causes to die, and He is Living and will not die. In His Hand is the goodness, all of it, and He is Able upon everything,' ten times. And he should say: 'I seek Refuge with Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing,' ten times. So if he forgets anything from that, it would be upon him to make up for it.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the glorification (Tasbih), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not know of any specific/regularized glorification other than the Tasbih of Fatima (peace be upon her); and ten times after the dawn prayer, you should say.' 'There is no god except Allah, Alone, there is no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom, and for Him is the Praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Able over all things.' And you may glorify (Allah) as much as you wish, voluntarily.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever says when dawn rises: "There is no god but Allah, Alone, no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He gives life and causes death, and He is Ever-Living and will not die. In His Hand is the good, and He is Able over all things," ten times; and sends blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad ten times; and glorifies (SubhanAllah) thirty-five times; and proclaims Oneness (La Ilaha Illa Allah) thirty-five times; and praises Allah (Alhamdulillah) thirty-five times, will not be written among the heedless that morning. And when he says it in the evening, he will not be written among the heedless that night.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), asking him to teach me a supplication, so he wrote to me saying: 'When you are in the morning and in the evening,' 'Allah, Allah, Allah! My Lord, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I do not associate anything with Him.' And if you add to that, it is better. Then supplicate with whatever comes to you regarding your need. So it is for everything, by the Permission of Allah the Exalted. Allah does whatever He desires.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not leave supplicating with this supplication three times when you rise in the morning, and three times when you enter the evening: 'O Allah, make me within Your fortified shield, in which You place whomever You will,' for my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'This is from the treasured supplications.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the meaning of His words: 'And of Ibrahim who fulfilled it'?' He said: 'Words he used to express with.' I said, 'And what were they?' He said: 'When it was morning, he would say: I wake up and my Lord is praised. I wake up and I do not associate anything with Allah, and I do not supplicate to a god along with Him, and I do not take a guardian besides Him,' three times. And when it was evening, he would say it three times.' He said: 'Thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed in His Book: 'And of Ibrahim who fulfilled it'.' I said, 'And what is the meaning of His words regarding Nuh: 'Surely he was a grateful servant'?' He said: 'Words he used to express with.' I said, 'And what were they?' He said: 'When it was morning, he would say: I testify to You what has come to me from bounties or good health regarding religion or the world, is from You, Alone, there being no associates for You. So for You is the praise upon that, and for You is the abundant thanks.' He used to say it when it was morning three times, and when it was evening three times.' I said, 'So what is the meaning of His words regarding Yahya: 'And tenderness from Us and purity'?' He said: 'The tenderness of Allah.' I said, 'So what tenderness of Allah reached upon him?' He said: 'Whenever he said: O Lord! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Here I am, O Yahya.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, all from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says, when he takes to his bed, three times: Praise is for Allah Who is Exalted, so Subjugates; and the Praise is for Allah Who is Hidden, so is Informed; and the Praise is for Allah Who is a King, so is Powerful; and the Praise is for Allah who Revives the dead and Causes the living to die and He is Able upon everything would come out from the sins to be as he was the day his mother gave him birth

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When one of you retires to his bed, let him say: 'O Allah! I have retained my soul with You, so retain it in a place of Your Pleasure and Your Forgiveness, and if You return it to my body, return it as a believing soul, recognizing the rights of Your Guardians, until You cause it to die upon that.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' (peace be upon him) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he used to say: At his sleep time: I believe in Allah and disbelieve in al-Taghut. O Allah, protect me in my sleep and in my waking.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I not inform you about what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say when he retired to his bed?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'He used to recite the Verse of the Chair (Ayat al-Kursi) and say: In the name of Allah, I believe in Allah and disbelieve in the idols (al-Taghut). O Allah, protect me in my sleep and in my waking.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from wet dreams and from evil dreams, and that Satan would play with me in wakefulness and in sleep.'
