Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, altogether from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Tasbih of Fatima Al-Zahra (peace be upon her): When you take to your bed, glorify Allah (say Allahu Akbar) thirty-four times, praise Him (say Al-Hamd Lillah) thirty-three times, and glorify Him (say Subhan Allah) thirty-three times, and recite Ayat Al-Kursi, and the two Mu'awwidhatayn (Surahs Al-Falaq and An-Nas), and ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Saffat, and ten verses from its end.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hak-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a son of his came to him one night and said to him, 'O father, I wish to sleep.' So he said, 'O my son, say: I testify that there is no god except Allah, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger. I seek Refuge with the Magnificence of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Majesty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Authority of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Able over everything.' And I seek Refuge with the Pardon of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Forgiveness of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Mercy of Allah, from the evil of the venomous creature and the insect, and from the evil of every animal, small or big, by night or by day, and from the evil of the mischievous of the Jinn and the humans, and from the evil of the mischievous of the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and from the evil of the thunderbolts and the hail. O Allah, send Blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger. Muawiya said, 'So the good child would say, 'Good,' during the mention of the Blessed Prophet.' He said, 'Yes, O my son, the good, the blessed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Mufazzal ibn Umar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If you are able, do not sleep at night until you seek Refuge with eleven Letters (Phrases).' I said, 'Inform me with them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Say.' 'I seek Refuge with the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Majesty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Authority of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Beauty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Defence of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Prevention of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Grip of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Kingdom of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Face of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from the evil of what He Created, Spread, and Settled. And seek Refuge with it whenever you desire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: When one of you rises at night, let him say: 'Glorious is the Lord of the Prophets and the God of the Messengers, and the Lord of the weak, and the Praise is for Allah Who revives the dead, and He is Able over all things.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant has spoken the truth and has given thanks.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you rise from your sleep at night, say: 'All praise is for Allah Who returned my soul to me, so that I may praise Him and worship Him.' And when you hear the voice of the rooster, say: 'Glorious, Holy is the Lord of the Angels and the Spirit. Your mercy precedes Your anger. There is no god except You, Alone. I have done evil and been unjust to myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.' And when you stand, look towards the horizons of the sky and say: 'O Allah! Neither does a dark night hide from You, nor a sky with constellations, nor an earth with flatness, nor darkness upon darkness, nor a deep sea where one wave precedes another. From among Your creatures, You know the betrayal of the eyes and what the chests conceal. The stars have set and the eyes have slept, yet You are the Living, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes You. Glorious is my Lord, Lord of the worlds, and God of the Messengers. And all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when he rose at the end of the night, would raise his voice until the people of the house could hear, and he would say: O Allah, assist me upon the terror of the emergence (of the Day of Judgment), and expand for me the narrowness of the bed (grave), and grant me the goodness that is before death, and grant me the goodness that is after death.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), he said: You should say when you intend to sleep: 'O Allah, if You are to withhold my soul, then have mercy on it, and if You are to send it back, then protect it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) retired to his bed, he would say: 'O Allah, by Your Name I live and by Your Name I die.' And when he rose from his sleep, he would say: 'All praise is for Allah Who gave me life after having caused my death, and to Him is the Resurrection.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever recites at his bedtime the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi) three times, and the Verse in Surah Aal-Imran [Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge], and the Verse of Subservience, and the Verse of Prostration, two devils are assigned to him to protect him from the rebellious devils, whether they will or not, and with them are thirty angels from Allah who praise Allah, glorify Him, declare His oneness, magnify Him, and seek forgiveness for him until that servant awakens from his sleep, and the reward of that is for him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Aamir ibn Abdullah ibn Juza'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no one who recites the end of Surah Al-Kahf before sleeping except that he will wake up at the time he desires.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Supplication is the shelter of acceptance, just as clouds are the shelter of rain.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A servant never stretches out his hand toward Allah, the Almighty, the Compeller, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is too shy to return it empty until He places in it from the bounty of His mercy what He wills. So whenever one of you supplicates, let him not draw back his hands until he has wiped them over his face and his head.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Hamza, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) move his lips when he intended to go out, while he was standing at the door. So I said, 'I saw you moving your lips when you went out. Did you say anything?' He said, 'Yes.' Indeed, when a person exits from his house, he should say when he intends to go out: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest' three times. 'By Allah I exit, and by Allah I enter, and upon Allah I rely' three times. 'O Allah, open up goodness for me in this direction of mine, and end it for me with goodness, and protect me from the evil of every creature You seize by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on the Straight Path.' He would remain in the guarantee of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until Allah returns him to the place from which he came. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Hamza — similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I went to the door of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and coincidentally met him as he was exiting the door, so he said: 'In the Name of Allah, I believe in Allah, and I rely upon Allah.' Then he said: 'O Abu Hamza! When the servant exits his house, Satan presents himself to him. So when he says, "In the Name of Allah," the two angels say, "You are sufficed." When he says, "I believe in Allah," they say, "You are guided." When he says, "I rely upon Allah," they say, "You are protected." So Satan withdraws, and he says to his companion, "How can we deal with one who is guided, sufficed, and protected?"' He said: Then he said, 'O Allah, my honor is yours today.' Then he said: 'O Abu Hamza! If you leave the people alone, they will not leave you alone, and if you reject them, they will not reject you.' I said, 'So what should I do?' He said, 'Give them from your honor, for the day of your poverty and destitution.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Hamza, who said: I sought permission to enter upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he came out to me and his lips were moving. So I told him. He said: 'Did you realize that, O Thumali?' I said: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'By Allah, I spoke a speech that no one ever spoke, except that Allah would suffice him for what worries him from the affairs of his world and his Hereafter.' He said: I said to him, 'Inform me of it.' He said: 'Yes. The one who says when he exits from his house.' 'In the Name of Allah, Allah suffices me. I rely upon Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of all my affairs, and I seek refuge with You from the disgrace of the world and the punishment of the Hereafter.' Allah will suffice him for what worries him from the affairs of his world and his Hereafter.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says when he exits from the door of his house: 'I seek refuge with that with which the Angels of Allah seek refuge, from the evil of this new day which, when its sun sets, will not return, from the evil of myself, and from the evil of others, and from the evil of the Satans, and from the evil of the one who establishes hostility towards the Guardians of Allah, and from the evil of the Jinn and the humans, and from the evil of the predatory wild animals and the insects, and from the evil of indulging in the Prohibitions, all of them. I pledge myself with Allah from every evil. Allah will forgive him, turn to him, suffice him against worries, hold him back from evil, and protect him from harm.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you go out from your house, say: 'In the Name of Allah, I rely upon Allah. There is neither might nor strength except with Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of what I am going out for, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I am going out for. O Allah, expand upon me from Your grace, and complete Your favor upon me, and employ me in Your obedience, and make my desire to be in what is with You, and cause me to die upon Your religion and the religion of Your Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), whenever he went out, would say: 'O Allah, by You I go out, and to You I submit, and in You I believe, and upon You I rely. O Allah, bless for me this day of mine, and grant me its success, its victory, its help, its purification, its guidance, and its blessing, and turn away from me its evil and the evil of whatever is in it. In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, and the praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I have gone out, so bless me in my going out and benefit me with it.' He said, 'And whenever he entered his house, he said that (as well).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him), whenever he exited from his house, would say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I go out with the Might of Allah and His Strength, not by my might and my strength, but with Your Might and Your Strength. O Lord! I expose myself to Your sustenance, therefore bring it to me in well-being.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Sabbah al-Hadda’ who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: When you intend to travel, stand at the door of your house and recite the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in front of you, and on your right, and on your left, and say 'He is Allah, One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) in front of you, and on your right and on your left, and say 'I seek Refuge in the Lord of the people' (Surah al-Nas) and say 'I seek Refuge in the Lord of Al-Falaq' (Surah al-Falaq) in front of you, and on your right and on your left, then say: 'O Allah, protect me and protect what is with me, and keep me safe and keep safe whatever is with me, and deliver me and deliver what is with me with an excellent delivery'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you not seen the man who is protected but what is with him is not protected, and he is safe but what is with him is not safe, and he reaches (his destination) but what is with him does not reach?'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that whenever he used to go out from the house, he would say: "In the Name of Allah I go out, and upon Allah I rely, there is neither Might nor Strength except with Allah."

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: O Sabbah! If the man from you intends a journey, he should stand at the door of his house facing the direction he is heading towards, and recite Al-Hamd (Surah al-Fatiha) in front of him, on his right, and on his left; and the two Mu'awwidhat (Surah al-Ikhlas, Surah al-Falaq, and Surah an-Nas - note: text says Mu'awwidhatayn but lists three, or implies the two plus Ikhlas as per the list) in front of him, on his right, and on his left; and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in front of him, on his right, and on his left; and Ayat al-Kursi in front of him, on his right, and on his left. Then he should say: 'O Allah! Protect me and protect what is with me, and keep me safe and keep safe what is with me, and deliver me and deliver what is with me with Your excellent and beautiful delivery.' Allah will protect him and protect what is with him, and keep him safe and keep safe what is with him, and deliver him and deliver what is with him. Have you not seen the man who is protected but what is with him is not protected, and reaches (the destination) but what is with him does not reach, and is safe but what is with him is not safe?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: When you go out from your house for a journey or for staying at home, say: 'In the Name of Allah, I believe in Allah, I rely upon Allah, Whatever Allah so Desires, there is neither might nor strength except with Allah.' Then the devils will meet him and turn away, and the angels will strike their faces and say: 'What is your way to him? He has named Allah, believed in Him, relied upon Him, and said: Whatever Allah so Desires, there is neither might nor strength except with Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever says this statement will be with Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad when he stands before beginning the prayer.' O Allah! I turn towards You through Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and I present them before my prayer, and I draw near to You through them. So make me, through them, dignified in this world and the Hereafter, and from those who are brought near. You have bestowed upon me the favor of their recognition, so conclude for me with their obedience, and their recognition, and their Wilayah, for it is the happiness. And conclude for me with it, for You are Able over all things. Then you pray. So when you finish, you say: O Allah! Make me with Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in every well-being and affliction, and make me with Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad in every abode and return. O Allah! Make my life their life, and my death their death, and make me with them in all the stations, and do not separate me from them. Indeed, You are Able over all things.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of our companions, raising it, said: You should be saying before your entry into the Salat. O Allah! I give the lead to Muhammad Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to be in front of my need, and I divert by him to You regarding my seeking, therefore Make me to be dignified by them in the world and the Hereafter, and to be from the ones of Proximity. O Allah! Make my Salat to be Acceptable due to them, and my sins to be Forgiven due to them, and my supplication to be Answered due to them, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones!

From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I witnessed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) facing the Qiblah before the Takbir, and he said: 'O Allah, do not deprive me of Your Spirit, nor make me despair of Your Mercy, nor make me secure from Your Deceit, for none feel secure from the Deceit of Allah except the losing people.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have not heard this from anyone before you.' So he said: 'Indeed, among the greatest of the major sins in the presence of Allah is hopelessness from the Spirit of Allah, and despair from the Mercy of Allah, and security from the Deceit of Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Subah ibn Sayyaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever says, when he prays the Maghrib prayer, three times: 'All praise is for Allah, who does what He wills, and He alone does not do what others will' (or: 'and He does not do what He wills, unlike others'), will be given abundant goodness.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, raising it, said: He said: One should say after the two evening prayers: 'O Allah! In Your Hand are the ordainments of the night and the day, and the ordainments of the world and the Hereafter, and the ordainments of death and life, and the ordainments of the sun and the moon, and the ordainments of victory and defeat, and the ordainments of wealth and poverty. O Allah! Bless me in my religion, and in my world, and in my body, and in my family, and in my children. O Allah! Avert from me the evil of the mischief-makers among the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and the Jinn and the humans, and make my return to eternal goodness and bliss that does not cease.'

From him, from one of his companions, raising it (the hadith), said: The one who says after every prayer, while holding his beard with his right hand, 'O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, have mercy on me from the Fire,' three times, with his left hand raised, its palm facing the sky. Then he says, 'Rescue me from the painful punishment,' three times. Then he lowers his hand from his beard, then raises his hand and makes its palm facing the sky, then says, 'O Mighty, O Generous, O Beneficent, O Merciful,' and flips his hands, making both their palms facing the sky, then says, 'Rescue me from the painful punishment,' three times. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and the Angels, and the Spirit. Forgiveness is granted to him, and he is pleased, and forgiveness is linked to him until all creatures die, except for the two heavy ones, the Jinn and humans. And he said: When you have finished your Tashahhud, raise your hands and say: O Allah, forgive me with a decisive and firm forgiveness that leaves no sin, and I do not commit a prohibition after it ever. Grant me well-being with no affliction after it ever. Guide me with guidance after which I do not go astray ever. Benefit me, O Lord, with what You taught me, make it for me, and not against me. Provide me with sufficiency and make me content with it. O Lord! Turn to me. O Allah, O Allah, O Allah. O Beneficent, O Beneficent, O Beneficent. O Merciful, O Merciful, O Merciful. Have mercy on me from the Fire of blazing heat. Extend upon me from the abundance of Your provision. Guide me to what differed regarding the Truth by Your permission. Protect me from the Pelted Satan. Convey to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) from me many greetings and peace. Guide me by Your guidance. Enrich me with Your richness. Make me from Your sincere friends. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. Ameen. He said: The one who says this after every prayer, Allah will return his soul to him in his grave, and he will be alive, sustained, blissful, and joyful until the Day of Judgment.

From him, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), he said: You should say after Fajr prayer: 'O Allah, to You belongs all praise, an eternal praise with Your eternity, and to You belongs all praise, a praise with no end until Your pleasure, and to You belongs all praise, a praise with no limit until Your will, and to You belongs all praise, a praise for its speaker no reward except Your pleasure. O Allah, to You belongs all praise, and to You is the complaint, and You are the One asked for help. O Allah, to You belongs all praise as You are worthy of it. All praise is for Allah with all His praises, upon all His bounties, until the praise reaches where my Lord loves and is pleased.' And you should say after Fajr, before you speak: 'All praise is for Allah, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne. And Glory be to Allah, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne. And Allah is the Greatest, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne. And there is no god but Allah, filling the scale and the limit of pleasure and the weight of the Throne.' Repeat that four times. Then you should say: 'O Allah, I ask You the asking of the humble slave, that You send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You forgive our sins and fulfill our needs in this world and the Hereafter, with ease from You and well-being.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to Yusuf (peace be upon him) while he was in prison, and he said to him: O Yusuf! Say at the end of every prayer.' O Allah! Make for me a relief and an exit, and provide for me from where I expect and from where I do not expect.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says these words at every prescribed prayer, he will be protected in his self, his house, his wealth, and his children. I seek refuge for myself, my wealth, my children, my family, my house, and everything that is mine, with Allah the One, the Unique, the Eternal, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. And I seek refuge for myself, my wealth, my children, and everything that is mine, with the Lord of Daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, up to its end. And with the Lord of Mankind, up to its end. And with the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), up to its end.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Whoever says at the end of the obligatory prayer, 'O One who does what He wills and does not do what others will, there is none other than Him,' three times, then asks, he will be given what he asked for.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have prayed Al-Maghrib, pass your hand over your forehead and say.' 'In the Name of Allah, the Knower of the Unseen and the Seen, the Beneficent, the Merciful, Who there is no god except Him. O Allah, remove from me the worry, the gloom, and the grief,' three times.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I used to frequently complain about my eyes, so I complained of that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said, 'Shall I teach you a supplication for your world and your Hereafter, and a cure for the pain of your eyes?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'You should say at the end of Fajr prayer and the end of Maghrib prayer.' O Allah, I ask You by the right of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and make light in my vision, insight in my religion, conviction in my heart, sincerity in my deeds, safety in my self, expansion in my sustenance, and gratitude to You forever, as long as You keep me alive.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Shami narrated to me, saying: A man in Syria, called Hilqam ibn Abi Hilqam, narrated to me, saying: I went to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him). So I said to him: May I be your ransom, teach me a comprehensive supplication for the world and the Hereafter, and make it brief. He said: Say at the end of the Fajr prayer until the sun rises. "Glorious is Allah the Magnificent, and by His praise I seek forgiveness of Allah, and I ask Him from His grace." Hilqam said: I was in the worst state among my family members, and I did not know [why], until an inheritance came to me from a man whom I did not think had any kinship with me. And today I am among the wealthiest of my family, and that is not except due to what my master, the righteous servant (peace be upon him), taught me.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Abu Jameela, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to teach me a supplication for sustenance, so he taught me a supplication which I had not seen more abundant for sustenance than it. He said: Say: O Allah, grant me from Your extensive Grace a permissible, goodly sustenance, an extensive, permissible, goodly sustenance that suffices for the world and the Hereafter, poured out, welcome, wholesome, without toil and without favor from any of Your creatures, except as an extension from Your extensive Grace, for You said: 'And ask Allah of His Grace'. So from Your Grace I ask, and from Your Gift I ask, and from Your Full Hand I ask.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have delayed in receiving sustenance.' So he (peace be upon him) got upset, then said to me, 'Say.' O Allah, You have guaranteed my sustenance and the sustenance of every creature. O the best of those invoked, O the best of those who give, O the best of those who are asked, and O the most superior of those hoped from, do for me such and such.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said: A man from the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was delayed from him, then he came to him. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'What delayed you from us?' He said: 'Illness and poverty.' He said to him: 'Shall I not teach you a supplication by which Allah will remove from you the illness and poverty?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Say: There is no might and no power except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. I have placed my trust in the Living Who does not die, and all praise is for Allah Who did not take a companion nor a son, and there was no partner for Him in the dominion, and there was no guardian for Him from the disgrace, and exalt Him with great exaltation.' So it was not long before he returned to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah has indeed removed from me the illness and poverty.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Supplicate for the provision while you are in the prescribed prayer and you are in prostration: O Best of those asked from, and O Best of the Givers! Grant me provision and grant my dependents from Your extensive bounty, for You are the Possessor of the Great Bounty.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Baseer, who said: I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) of my need and asked him to teach me a supplication for seeking sustenance, so he taught me a supplication, and I did not remain in need since I supplicated with it. He said: Say it at the end of the night prayer. And you are in prostration: O best of those supplicated to, and O best of those asked from, and O most extensive of those who give, and O best of those hoped from! Grant me sustenance and expand upon me from Your sustenance, and provide for me a means of sustenance from Yourself. Indeed, You are Able over all things.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Dawud, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have dependents and a debt upon me, and my situation has become difficult, so teach me a supplication with which I will call upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to provide me with what I can pay off my debt with and assist me with my dependents.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'O servant of Allah! Perform ablution and perfect your ablution, then pray two cycles, completing the bowing and prostration, then say.' 'O Glorified, O One, O Benevolent, O Eternal! I turn to You by Muhammad, Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy (peace be upon him and his family). O Muhammad, O Messenger of Allah! I turn by You to Allah, your Lord and my Lord and the Lord of everything, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and his Household; and I ask You for a noble breath from Your breaths, and an easy breakthrough, and a wide sustenance, with which I gather my scattered affairs and pay off my debt and assist me with my dependents.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught this supplication: 'O Provider of the scarce, O Merciful to the needy, O Guardian of the believers, O Possessor of firm strength. Send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family, and provide for me, grant me well-being, and suffice me for what worries me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) looked at a man who was saying, 'O Allah, I ask You from Your permissible sustenance.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'You are asking for the subsistence of the Prophets. Say, O Allah, I ask You for a permissible, extensive, goodly sustenance from Your sustenance.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He should grant me the halal (permissible sustenance).' He said, 'Do you know what is the halal?' I said, 'That which is with us, the goodly earnings.' He said, 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: The halal is the sustenance of the Chosen ones.' Then he said, 'Say, I ask You from Your extensive sustenance.'

From him, from one of his companions, from Mufazzal bin Maziyd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Say: 'O Allah, expand for me in my sustenance, and extend for me in my lifespan, and make for me from among those by whom You help Your religion, and do not exchange me for someone else.'

From him, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) A supplication regarding sustenance: O Allah, O Allah, O Allah! I ask You by the right of those whose right upon You is great, that You send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You grant me the deed of what You taught me from the recognition of Your Right, and that You extend upon me what You have restricted from Your sustenance.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'We have delayed in receiving sustenance.' So he (peace be upon him) got angry, then said: 'Say.' O Allah, You have guaranteed my sustenance and the sustenance of every animal. So, O the Best of the supplicated to, and O the Best of the ones asked from, and O the best of the ones who give, and O the Most Superior of the ones hoped from, Do for me such and such.

Abu Baseer from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication: O Allah! I ask You for good means of living, a livelihood by which I gain strength for all my needs and connect through it in life to my Hereafter, without You making me luxurious in it so I rebel, or restricting it for me so I become miserable. Expand for me from the lawful sustenance of Your provision, and pour upon me from the flowing abundance of Your grace, a bounty from You that is complete and a gift that is not withheld. Then do not occupy me from thanking Your bounty due to its abundance, where its joy distracts me and the blossoms of its pride tempt me, nor due to its scarcity upon me, where its toil shortens my effort and fills my chest with its worry. Give me from that, O my God, self-sufficiency from the evil of Your creatures, and enough by which I attain Your pleasure. And I seek refuge in You, O my God, from the evil of the world and the evil of what is in it. Do not make the world a prison upon me, nor its separation a grief upon me. Bring me out of its trial, pleased with me, with my deeds accepted in it, to the house of eternal life and the dwellings of the righteous, and exchange for me with the perishable world the bliss of the abiding house. O Allah! I seek refuge in You from its decline and its turbulence, and the raids of its devils and its rulers, and its punishments, and from the aggression of those who aggress against me in it. O Allah! Whoever plots against me, plot against him, and whoever intends harm for me, intend harm for him. And remove from me the edge of him who set his edge against me, and extinguish for me the fire of him who lit the fuel for me. And suffice me against the cunning of the cunning, and blind for me the eyes of the disbelievers, and suffice me against the worry of him who brought his worry upon me, and repel from me the evil of the envious. And protect me from that with tranquility, and clothe me with Your fortified shield, and hide me in Your protective veil. And rectify my state for me, and verify my words with my deeds, and bless me in my family and my wealth.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Waleed ibn Sabih, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a debt of mine upon some people, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Say: O Allah! Grant an opportunity from Your opportunities to ease upon my debtors the repayment with it, and ease for me the collection of it through it. Indeed, You are Able over all things.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have encountered severe distress from the insinuations of the chest, and I am a man in debt, with dependents, and in need.' So he said to him, 'Repeat these words: I rely upon the Living Who does not die, and the praise is for Allah Who did not take a companion nor a son, and there was not for Him an associate in the dominion, and there was not for Him a guardian from the disgrace, and exalt Him with Takbeer.' 'I rely upon the Living Who does not die, and the praise is for Allah Who did not take a companion nor a son, and there was not for Him an associate in the dominion, and there was not for Him a guardian from the disgrace, and exalt Him with Takbeer.' And he did not long before he came to him and said, 'Allah removed the insinuations of my chest from me, and settled my debt for me, and expanded my sustenance for me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: He wrote to me on a piece of paper: O Allah! Return to all of Your creatures their grievances that are due from me, their small ones and their big ones, with ease from You and well-being. And what my strength cannot reach, and what the extent of my hand cannot encompass, and what my body and conviction and self are not strong enough to bear, therefore settle it for me from the abundance of what is with You from Your Grace. Then do not leave behind upon me anything from it; settle it from my good deeds, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones. I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no partner for Him. And I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. And that the Religion is as it was legislated, and that Islam is as it was described, and that the Book is as it was revealed, and that the Words are as they were narrated, and that Allah is the Clear Truth. May Allah mention Muhammad and his Household with goodness, and greet Muhammad and his Household with peace.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'e, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Hamza! What is the matter with you that whenever a fearful matter comes to you, you do not divert to one of the corners of your house, meaning (facing) the Qiblah, so you pray two Cycles of Salat, then you could be saying.' 'O Most Insightful of the lookers, and O Most hearing of the listeners, and O Quickest of the reckoners, and O Most Merciful of the merciful ones', seventy times. Every time you supplicate with these words, ask for a need'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Thabit, from Asma'a, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is afflicted with worry, or grief, or distress, or affliction, or adversity, let him say: Allah is my Lord, and I do not associate anything with Him. I rely upon the Living Who does not die.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When an affliction descends upon a man, or something severe, or a matter distresses him, let him uncover his knees and his forearms, and press them against the ground, and press his forehead against the ground, then let him supplicate for his need while he is in prostration.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Ammar Al-Dahhan, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the brothers of Yusuf threw Yusuf into the well, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to him and entered upon him and said: 'O boy, what are you doing here?' He said: 'My brothers threw me into the well.' He said: 'So would you like to be taken out from it?' He said: 'That is up to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He will extract me.' He said: So he said to him: 'Indeed Allah the Exalted is saying to you: Supplicate to Me with this supplication until I extract you from the well.' He said to him: 'And what is the supplication?' He said: 'Say:' O Allah, I ask You by the fact that to You belongs all praise, there is no god except You, the Bestower, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Possessor of Majesty and Generosity, that You send Salat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You make for me a relief and an exit from what I am in. He said: Then it was from his story what Allah mentioned in His Book.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That which Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) supplicated with against Dawud ibn Ali when he killed al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and seized the wealth of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was: 'O Allah! I ask You by Your Light which cannot be extinguished, and by Your Decrees which are not hidden, and by Your Might which does not expire, and by Your Favors which cannot be counted, and by Your Authority by which You restrained Pharaoh from Moses (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding the worry/distress. He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should perform ritual bath (ghusl) and pray two cycles of prayer, and say: O Reliever of the worry, and O Remover of the sadness, O Beneficent of the world and the Hereafter and Merciful to them both! Relieve my worry and remove my sadness. O Allah, the One, the Unique, the Eternal, who neither begot nor was begotten, and there was none equal to Him. Protect me and purify me and remove my affliction; and recite Ayat al-Kursi and the two Mu'awwidhat (Surahs 113 and 114).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you fear a matter, say: 'O Allah! You are such that no one suffices from You, and You suffice from every one of Your creatures; therefore, suffice me with such and such.' And in another hadith, he said: 'You should say: 'O Sufficer from every thing, and nothing suffices from You in the heavens and the earth! Suffice me for what worries me from the affairs of the world and the Hereafter, and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who enters upon a ruler whom he fears, let him say: 'By Allah I commence, and by Allah I shall succeed, and by Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) I divert to Him. O Allah! Ease for me his difficulty and make his harshness easy for me, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book.' And you should also say: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god except Him, upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Magnificent Throne. And I seek refuge by the might and strength of Allah from their might and their strength, and I seek refuge by the Lord of Al-Falaq from the evil of what He created, and there is no might nor strength except with Allah.'

From him, from a number of our companions, they raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: It was from the supplication of my father (peace be upon him) regarding the newly-occurring matters: 'O Allah! Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad.' And Forgive me, and Be Merciful to me, and Purify my deeds, and Ease my return, and Guide my heart, and Secure my fear, and Grant me good health in my life-time, all of it, and Affirm my proofs, and Forgive my mistakes, and Whiten my face, and Safeguard me in my Religion, and Ease my seeking (for livelihood), and Expand upon me regarding my sustenance for I am weak. And Overlook from my evil deeds what are with me by the Goodness with what is with You, and do not Grieve me for myself nor Grieve me for my intimate friends. And Grant me, O my God, an opportunity from Your Opportunities Removing with it from me the entirety of what I am afflicted with, and Return upon me what is better Ways with me. For my strength has weakened, and my reasons are scarce, and my hopes from Your creatures are cut off, and there does not remain except hoping in You, and reliance upon You and Your Power upon me. O Lord! If You are Merciful to me and Grant good health to me, is like Your Power upon me if You were to Punish me and Afflict me. My God! Mentioning Your Rewards comforts me, and the hoping for Your Bounties strengthens me, and I have not been isolated from Your Bounties since the day You Created me. And You are my Lord, and my Master, and my Defender, and my Shelter, and the Protector for me, and the Lenient to me, and the Merciful with me, and the Guarantor of my sustenance. And in Your Ordainment and Your Power is everything what I am in, therefore let it happen to be, O my Chief and my Master, regarding what You Judge, and You Ordain, and You Finalise, hasten my finishing from what I am in, the entirety of it, and the good health for me. For I cannot find anyone to repel that apart from You, nor do I rely with regards to it upon anyone except You. Therefore be, O the One with the Majesty and the Benevolence, during the goodness of my thoughts with You, my hope for you, and be Merciful on my desperation and my dependence, and the weakness of my (body) parts, and Favour with that upon me and upon every supplicant who supplicates You, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones, and Send Salawat upon Muhammad a

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Asbaat, from Ismail bin Yasar, from someone who reported it, said: He said: When a matter grieves you, so say at the end of your prostration (sujood), 'O Jibraeel! O Muhammad! O Jibraeel! O Muhammad!', repeating that, 'Suffice me for what I am in, for both of you are sufficing ones, and protect me by the Permission of Allah, for both of you are protectors'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Ayn, from Bishr ibn Maslama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I do not care if humans and jinn were to gather against me, as long as I say these words.' In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and from Allah, and to Allah, and in the Way of Allah, and upon the Religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, to You I submit my self, and to You I direct my face, and to You I seek refuge for my back, and to You I delegate my affair. O Allah, protect me with the protection of faith from in front of me, and from behind me, and from my right, and from my left, and from above me, and from beneath me, and from before me. And repel from me by Your Might and Your Strength, for there is no Might and no Strength except with You. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr — similar to it.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man said to me, 'What did you say when you entered upon Abu Ja'far at Al-Rabza?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I said: O Allah, You suffice from everything and nothing suffices from You, so suffice me with whatever You will, and however You will, and from wherever You will, and whenever You will.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Muyassar, who said: When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived at the presence of Abu Ja'far, Abu Ja'far stationed a slave of his above his head and said to him, 'When he comes to me, strike his neck.' So when Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered, he looked at Abu Ja'far and whispered something between himself and his own soul, not knowing what it was. Then he manifested (said aloud), 'O He Who Suffices all His creatures, and no one suffices Him! Suffice me from the evil of Abdullah ibn Ali.' He said: So Abu Ja'far became such that he could not see his slave, and the slave became such that he could not see him. So Abu Ja'far said, 'O Ja'far ibn Muhammad, I have exhausted you in this heat, so leave.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) exited from his presence. Abu Ja'far said to his slave, 'What prevented you from doing what I ordered you to do?' He said, 'No, by Allah, I did not see him, and indeed something came and stood between me and him.' So Abu Ja'far said to him, 'By Allah, if you narrate this hadith to anyone, I will surely kill you.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Ahmad ibn Abu Dawood, from Abdullah ibn Abdul Rahman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'Shall I teach you a supplication you can supplicate with, which we, the People of the Household, use whenever a matter worries us and we fear from the ruling authorities a matter we cannot face with, we supplicate with it?' I said, 'Yes, may my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah!' He said: 'Say, O the One who existed before everything, and O the One Who Brought everything into being, and O the One Who would be Remaining after everything! Send Salawāt upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Do for me such and such.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: Muhammad ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi wrote to me asking me to write to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a supplication he could teach by which relief is hoped for. So he wrote to me: 'As for what Muhammad ibn Hamza asked regarding teaching him a supplication by which relief is hoped for, say to him: He should persist with: O the One Who Suffices from everything and nothing suffices from Him! Suffice me what is worrying me from what I am in. For I hope that he will be sufficed from what he is in from the sadness, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.' So I informed him of that, and only a little time had passed until he came out from the custody (prison).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying to his son: 'O my son! Whoever from you is struck by a calamity or an affliction descends upon him, let him perform ablution and perfect the ablution, then let him pray two or four cycles of prayer, then let him say at the end of these:' 'O the Place of every complaint, and O the Listener of every whisper, and Witness of every gathering, and Knower of every secret, and O the Repeller of whatever He wills from affliction, and O the Friend of Ibrahim, and O the Whisperer to Musa, and O the Chosen One of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)! I supplicate to You with the supplication of one whose destitution is severe, whose plan is scarce, and whose strength has weakened. The supplication of the drowning, the stranger, the desperate one who finds no one to remove what he is in except You, O the Most Merciful of the merciful.' For indeed, whoever supplicates with it, Allah will remove [the affliction] from him, if Allah wills.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the son of Saeed's brother, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sadness enters me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Frequently say: Allah, Allah is my Lord; I do not associate anything with Him.' When you fear insinuation or self-talk, say: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, and the son of Your servant, and the son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand. Your judgment is just upon me, Your decree is executed upon me.' O Allah, I ask You by every Name that is Yours, which You revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept exclusively in the Knowledge of the Unseen with You, that You send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. And that You make the Quran the light of my vision, the spring of my heart, the relief of my sorrow, and the removal of my worry. Allah, Allah is my Lord; I do not associate anything with Him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: It was the supplication of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on the night of the Confederates (Al-Ahzaab): 'O the Crier/Helper of the distressed, and O the Answerer of the call of the desperate, and O the Remover of my sorrow! Remove from me my sorrow, and my worry, and my distress, for indeed You know my state and the state of my companions, and Suffice me against the terror of my enemies.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Israil, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said: Scrofula (an illness of the neck) came out with a slave girl of ours in her neck. So a man came to me and said: 'O Ali! Say to her that she should say, O Kind! O Merciful! O Lord! O my Master!', repeating it. He said: 'So she said it, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed it from her.' He said: 'And he said: This is the supplication which Ja'far Bin Suleyman supplicated with.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) for a supplication while I was behind him, so he said: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your Noble Face, and Your Great Name, and by Your Might which cannot be reached, and by Your Power from which nothing is prevented, that You do such and such with me.' He said, 'And he wrote to me a note in his own handwriting: Say, O He who is Exalted so He Dominates, and Hidden so He Knows, O He who is King so He is Powerful, and O He who Revives the Dead, and He is Able over all things. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, and do such and such with me. Then say, O There is no god but Allah, have mercy on me by the right of 'There is no god but Allah', have mercy on me.' And he wrote to me in another note, instructing me to say: 'O Allah, ward off from me by Your Might and Your Strength. O Allah, I ask You for Your blessings in this day of mine, and this month of mine, and this year of mine, and this month of mine, and whatever descends therein of punishment, or disliked events, or affliction, so turn it away from me and from my children by Your Might and Your Strength. Indeed, You are Able over all things.' O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the fading of Your blessings, and the changing of Your well-being, and from the suddenness of Your retribution, and from the evil of the writing (of deeds) that has preceded. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself, and from the evil of every creature, You are the Seizer of its forelock. Indeed, You are Able over all things, and indeed Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge, and counted all things with a count.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ibrahim ibn Hanan, from Ali ibn Sowrat, from Sama'ah who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whenever there is for you, O Sama'ah, a need to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say: O Allah! I ask You by the right of Muhammad and Ali, for indeed for both of them is a status/glory among You from the statuses, and a power/authority from the powers. So by the right of that status and by the right of that power, Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and do with me such and such. For indeed when it is the Day of Judgment, no Angel of Proximity, nor Messenger Prophet, nor tested Believer will remain except that he will be in need of them both on that Day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He used to say during an illness. O Allah! You have criticized certain people, saying: 'Say: Call upon those whom you claim (to be gods) besides Him, so they will not have the power to remove the distress from you nor to change it.' So, O the One besides Whom no one else has the power to remove my distress or change it, Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, Remove my distress and transfer it to those who call upon another god alongside You. There is no god other than You.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from Yunus ibn Abdul Rahman, from Dawud ibn Zurbi, who said: I fell sick in Medina with a severe illness, so that reached Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He wrote to me: 'Your illness has reached me, so buy a Sa' of wheat, then lie on your back and scatter it upon your chest however it scatters, and say:' O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which, when the desperate one asks You with it, You remove the harm from him, and grant him authority in the earth, and make him Your vicegerent over Your creatures, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You grant me health from my illness. Then sit up, gather the wheat from around you, and say the like of that, and distribute it, a Mudd to each poor person, and say the like of that. Dawud said: So I did that, and it was as if I had been released from a shackle, and not just one person did it, and he benefited from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Nuaym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One of his sons complained [of illness] to him, so he said: 'O my son! Say.' 'O Allah! Heal me with Your healing, and cure me with Your cure, and grant me well-being from Your affliction, for I am Your servant and the son of Your servant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! This (illness) which has appeared on my face, the people allege that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not afflict any servant with it for whom He has a need.' So he said to me: 'No! It was so that a believer of the people of Pharaoh was paralysed in his fingers, so he was saying like this' – and he extended his hand, and he was saying: 'O people! Follow the Messengers.' He said, 'Then he said: When it is the last third of the night, during its beginning, perform ablution and stand to your prayer which you tend to pray. So when you are in the last prostration of the first two cycles, so say:' While you are prostrating: 'O Ali! O Exalted! O Magnificent! O Beneficent! O Merciful! O Hearer of the supplications and O Giver of the goodness! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Give me from the goodness of the world and the Hereafter, what You are Rightful of it, and Exchange from me from the evil of the world and the Hereafter what You are Rightful of it, and Remove from me this pain' – and specify it – 'for it has infuriated me and grieved me', and be insistent in the supplication'. He said, 'So I had not even arrived at Al-Kufa until Allah removed it from me, all of it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, all from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you see a man who has been afflicted by a trial, say: 'Praise is for Allah Who granted me well-being from that which He afflicted you with, and preferred me over you and over many of those He created,' but do not make him hear what you said.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawud ibn Zurbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You place your hand upon the place where the pain is, and you say three times: 'Allah, Allah is my Lord truly. I do not associate anything with Him. O Allah, You are (the relief) for it and for all great troubles, so relieve it from me.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawood, from Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) For the pains, you should say: 'In the Name of Allah and by Allah! How many Bounties of Allah are in the calm veins and agitated veins, upon a grateful servant and an ungrateful servant.' And you should grab your beard with your right hand after the Obligatory Prayer, and say: 'O Allah, relieve my worries, hasten my good health, and remove my harm,' three times, and ensure that this is accompanied by tears and weeping.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from a man who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and complained to him of a pain in my body. So he said, 'Say, In the Name of Allah, then wipe your hand over it and say, I seek Refuge by the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Majesty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Magnificence of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Hold of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Messenger of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Names of Allah, from the evil of what I am cautious of, and from the evil of what I fear upon myself.' You should say it seven times. He said, 'So I did it, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed the pain from me by it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Washsha, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Awn, who said: Pass your hand over the place of the pain, then say: 'In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and there is no might and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. O Allah, wipe from me what I find (pain). Then pass your right hand and wipe the place of the pain three times.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Akhi Ghrām, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: You place your hand upon the place of the pain, then you say: 'In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and there is neither might nor strength except with Allah. O Allah, wipe away from me what I feel (the pain).' And you wipe the pain three times.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Isa, from his uncle, who said: I said to him, 'Teach me a supplication with which I may supplicate for a pain that has afflicted me.' He said, 'Say it while you are in prostration.' O Allah, O Beneficent, O Merciful, O Lord of the lords, and God of the gods, and O King of the kings, and O Master of the masters, heal me with Your healing from every ailment and sickness, for I am Your servant, turning about in Your grip.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: When you visit a sick person, say: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, from the evil of every swollen vein and from the evil of the heat of the Fire,' seven times.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a person has a complaint, let him say: 'In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I seek Refuge by the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah upon whatever He so desires, from the evil of what I find.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hisham al-Jawalyqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). O Sender-down of healing and Remover of illness, Send down upon what is with me from illness, a healing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ishaq, Sahib al-Sha'ir, from Husayn al-Khorasani, and he was a baker, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of pains in my body, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you pray, place your hand upon the place of your prostration, then say.' In the Name of Allah, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is the Messenger of Allah! Heal me, O Healer! There is no healing except Your Healing. A healing which does not leave out any sickness, a healing from every illness and disease.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to spread [recite] with this supplication: You place your hand upon the place of the pain and you say O pain, settle by the tranquility of Allah, and cool down by the dignity of Allah, and be barred by the barrier of Allah, and calm down by the calmness of Allah I seek refuge for you, O human being, by what Allah, Exalted and Glorious, would be sought by His Throne and His Angels on the Day of the tremor and the earthquakes You say that seven times, and not less than three

Muhammad ibn Yahya, Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ammar ibn al-Mubarak from Awn ibn Sa'd, the freedman of al-Ja'fari, from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: You place your hand upon the place of the pain and you say: O Allah, I ask You by the right of the Magnificent Quran, with which the Trustworthy Spirit descended, and it is with You in the Mother of the Book, 'Ali, the Wise, that You heal me with Your healing, and treat me with Your treatment, and grant me well-being from Your afflictions three times, and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Awfi, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurara, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: A pain appeared in my knee, so I complained about that to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: 'When you pray, say: O the Most Generous of those who give, and O the Best of those who are asked, and O the Most Merciful of those who have mercy, have mercy on my weakness and scarcity of resource, and grant me health from my pain.' He said: 'So I did it, and I was healed.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Ibn al-Mundhir who said: Loneliness was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: Shall I not inform you of something that if you say it, you will not feel lonely at night or during the day? In the name of Allah and by Allah, and I relied upon Allah, and indeed whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Allah accomplishes His command. Allah has decreed a measure for everything. O Allah, make me under Your wing and in Your shelter, and make me in Your security and in Your protection. So he said: It reached us that a man recited it for thirty years and left it for one night, so a scorpion stung him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) lifted Hasan and Husayn and said: I seek refuge for you two with the complete words of Allah and all His good names, generally, from the evil of the venomous reptile and the insect, and from the evil of every envious eye, and from the evil of an envious person when he envies. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) turned to us and said: This is how Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ismail and Ishaq (peace be upon them).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Bukayr, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: When you are in the evening and you look at the sun during its setting and departure, say: In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and all praise is for Allah, Who did not take a companion nor a son, and there was not for Him a partner in the dominion, and there was not for Him a guardian from the disgrace, and magnify Him with magnification. And all praise is for Allah, Who is described but cannot be described, and He knows but cannot be known. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal. And I seek refuge in the Face of Allah, the Generous, and by the Great Name of Allah, from the evil of what He created and scattered, and from the evil of what is beneath the earth, and from the evil of what is hidden and apparent, and from the evil of what I have described and what I have not described. And all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He mentioned that it is a security from every predatory beast, and from the accursed Satan and his offspring, and everything that bites or stings. And its reciter will not fear a thief nor a ghul (demon) when he speaks with it. He said: I said to him, 'I am a hunter of wild beasts, and I spend the night in the ruins and I am alone.' So he said to me, 'Say when you enter: In the name of Allah, I enter, and enter with your right leg; and when you exit, exit with your left leg, and mention Allah, for you will not see anything disliked.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Qutayba al-A'sha, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) taught me, saying: Say. In the Name of Allah the Majestic! I seek refuge for so-and-so with Allah the Magnificent, from the biting insects and the venomous reptiles, and the evil eye, and the general [plague of creatures], and from the Jinn and the humans, and from the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and from their spitting, their aggression, and their blowing [of spells], and by the Verse of the Throne, then recite it. Then you should say during the second time: In the Name of Allah! I seek refuge for so-and-so with Allah the Majestic, until you complete it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! I fear the scorpions.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look at the Daughters of Na'sh (Ursa Minor), the three stars; the middle one of them, by its side is a small star near it, which the Arabs call As-Suha, and we call it Aslam. Gaze at it with a solitary gaze every night, and say three times:' O Allah! Lord of Aslam! Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Hasten their relief and Keep us safe. Is'haq said: 'So I did not neglect it since my time (of having learnt that) except for once, so the scorpion stung me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in one of his military expeditions when they complained to him about the fleas that they were hurting them. So he said: 'When one of you takes his bed, let him say:' O the black leaper who does not care about a lock nor a door! I have sworn an oath upon you by the Mother of the Book that you shall not hurt me or my companions until the night departs and the morning comes with whatever it brings, and the morning that we know, until the morning returns, whenever it returns.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'When you encounter a wild beast, say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of Daniel and the Pit, from the evil of every ferocious lion.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Salih ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Harun, that he wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him for an amulet for the winds that afflict children. So he wrote to him in his own handwriting with these two amulets, and Salih claimed that Ibrahim sent them to me in his handwriting. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. I testify that there is no god except Allah. I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god except Allah and there is no Lord for me except Allah. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. There is no associate for Him. Glorious is Allah. Whatever Allah wills occurs, and whatever He does not will, does not occur. O Allah, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, Lord of Musa, Isa, and Ibrahim who fulfilled [Your promise], God of Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqoub, and the Tribes. There is no god except You. Glorious are You, along with what You numbered from Your Signs, and by Your Greatness, and by what the Prophets asked You with, and that You are the Lord of the people. You were before everything and You are after everything. I ask You by Your Name by which You hold the heavens from falling to the earth except by Your Permission, and by Your Perfect Words by which You revive the dead, that You should protect Your servant So-and-So from the evil of what descends from the sky and what ascends to it, and what emerges from the earth and what enters it. And peace be upon the Messengers, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. And he wrote to him also in his own handwriting: In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and to Allah, and as Allah wills, and I seek refuge in the Might of Allah, and the Compulsion of Allah, and the Power of Allah, and the Kingdom of Allah. This writing is a healing from Allah for So-and-So, son of So-and-So, son of Your servant and son of Your maid, both servants of Allah. May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you encounter a predatory beast, recite Ayat al-Kursi in its face, and say to it: I impose upon you by the Determination of Allah, and the Determination of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and the Determination of Suleiman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), and the Determination of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and the Pure Imams after him, for indeed it will turn away from you, if Allah wills.' He said: So I went out, and behold the beast had presented itself. I imposed upon it and said to it: 'Unless you step aside from our path and do not harm us.' He said: So I looked at it, and it had bowed its head, and put its tail between its legs, and turned away.

From him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Al-Jaroud, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says at the end of the obligatory prayer: 'I entrust to Allah the Magnificent, the Majestic, my self, my family, my children, and those whose affairs concern me; and I entrust to Allah the One hoped for, the One feared, the One humbled by His Greatness, everything, my self, my family, my wealth, my children, and those whose affairs concern me,' he will be shielded by a wing from the wings of Jibra'il (peace be upon him), and will be protected in his self, his family, and his wealth.

From him, raising it, he said: Whoever spends the night in a house and a room alone, let him recite Ayat Al-Kursi and let him say: 'O Allah, comfort my loneliness, secure my awe, and assist me upon my loneliness.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Yazeed ibn Murra, from Bukayr, who said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'O Ali! Shall I not teach you some words? When you fall into a predicament or an affliction, say:' In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will divert from you by it whatever He wills from types of affliction.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from the one who mentioned it, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: You should say: 'O Allah, I ask You, and the servants do not ask like I ask You. I ask You by the right of Muhammad, Your Prophet and Your Messenger, and Ibrahim, Your friend and Your elite, and Musa, Your speaker and Your whisperer, and Isa, Your Word and Your Spirit.' And I ask You by the Parchments of Ibrahim, and the Torah of Musa, and the Psalms of Dawud, and the Evangel of Isa, and the Quran of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and by every Revelation You Revealed, and every Judgment You Passed, and right You Fulfilled, and rich one You Enriched, and straying one You Guided, and begging one You Gave to. And I ask You by Your Name which You placed upon the night, so it turned dark, and by Your Name which You placed upon the day so it shone, and by Your Name which You placed upon the earth so it settled and the skies were underpinned by it so (became) upheld, and placed it upon the mountains, so were anchored. And by Your Name by which the sustenance are Sent with, and I ask You by Your Name by which the dead are revived with, and I ask You by the Bond of the Might from Your Throne and the limit of the Mercy from Your Book. I ask You that You should Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad and that You should Grace me the memorisation of the Quran, and the varieties of the knowledge, and that You affirm it in my heart and my hearing and my sight, and that You mingle it with my flesh and my blood and my bones and my brain, and that You Utilise by it my night and my day by Your Mercy and Your Power, for there is neither Might nor Strength except with You. O Living! O Eternal!' He said, 'And in another Hadith there is an addition:' 'And I ask You by Your Name by which Your servants supplicate with so it is Answered for them, and Your Prophets, so it is Forgiven for them and there is Mercy upon them.'
