'And I ask You by every Name You Revealed in Your Book, and by Your Name which Your Throne is stabilized, and by Your Name, the Single, the One, the Individual, the Solitary, the Exalted which Fills up the corners, all of them, the Immaculate, the Clean, the Blessed, the Holy, the Living, the Eternal, Light of the skies and the earth, the Beneficent

From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, he raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I shall teach you a supplication by which you will not forget the Quran.' O Allah! Have mercy on me by causing me to neglect Your disobedience forever as long as You keep me alive, and have mercy on me from burdening myself with what does not concern me, and grant me a good perspective in what pleases You regarding me, and make my heart steadfast in memorizing Your Book as You taught me, and grant me to recite it in the manner that pleases You regarding me. O Allah! Illuminate my sight with Your Book, expand my chest with it, gladden my heart with it, loosen my tongue with it, and employ my body with it, and strengthen me upon that and assist me on it, for there is no assistant upon it except You. There is no god except You. He said: And some of our companions have reported from Walid ibn Sabih, from Hafs al-Awar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you recognize the prolongation of affliction from its brevity?' We said: 'No.' He said: 'Whenever one of you is inspired to supplication during an affliction, then know that the affliction is short.'

Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: There is no affliction that descends upon a believing servant, but that God Mighty and Majestic inspires him to supplicate, except that the removal of that affliction would be imminent; and there is no affliction that descends upon a believing servant, but that he withholds himself from supplication, except that affliction would be prolonged. So whenever affliction descends, you must turn to supplication and humble pleading to God Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Isma'il ibn Sahl, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Say: O Allah, make me fear You as if I can see You, and make me happy with Your piety, and do not make me miserable by my eagerness to disobey You, and choose for me in Your decree, and bless me in Your ordainment, until I do not love the delay of what You hasten nor the hastening of what You delay; and make my self-sufficiency within myself, and grant me enjoyment with my hearing and my sight, and make them the inheritors from me, and help me against those who oppress me, and show me Your power in them, O Lord, and make my eyes delighted with that.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Suleiman al-Jassas, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'O Allah, assist me upon the terror of the Day of Judgment, and extract me from the world in peace, and marry me to the Houris, and suffice me for my livelihood and the livelihood of my dependents and the livelihood of the people, and enter me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Say: O Allah, I ask You from every goodness of which Your Knowledge is encompassing, and I seek Refuge with You from every evil of which Your Knowledge is encompassing. O Allah, I ask You for Your well-being in all my affairs, and I seek Refuge with You from the disgrace of the world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ali ibn Ziyad, who said: 'Ali ibn Baseer wrote to him, asking him to write for him at the bottom of his letter a supplication that he would teach him, so that by it he would be protected from sins, comprehensive for the world and the Hereafter. So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O He Who Manifested the beautiful and concealed the ugly, and did not tear the veil from me. O Generous of Pardon, O Excellent in Overlooking, O Vast in Forgiveness, O Extender of the Two Hands with Mercy, O Companion of every secret conversation, and O End-point of every complaint. O Generous of Pardoning, O Magnificent in Bestowing Favors, O Initiator of every blessing before it is deserved. O My Lord, O My Master, O My Lord, O My Helper. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad. And I ask You that You do not make me in the Fire, then ask whatever seems good to You.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi and Abu Talib, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: O Allah, You are my reliance in every worry, and You are my hope in every difficulty, and You are for me in every matter that befalls me, a Trustworthy and a Resource. How many worries are there such that the heart weakens from them, and plans become scarce regarding them, and the near and far ones abandon them, and the enemies gloat with them, and the affairs exhaust me in them. I revealed it to You and complained of it to You, turning away from those besides You. Therefore, relieve it, remove it, and suffice for me regarding it. For You are the Patron of every bounty and the Companion of every need, and the End-point of every desire. So, for You is abundant praise, and for You is the overflowing favor.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Say: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your Majesty and Your Beauty and Your Generosity that You do for me such and such.'

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'Increase in saying: O Allah, do not make me from the Mu'arreen, and do not remove me from Al-Taqsir.' I said: 'As for the Mu'arreen, I have understood them, but what is the meaning of He said to me: 'Increase in saying: O Allah, do not make me from the Mu'arreen, and do not remove me from Al-Taqsir.' He said: I said, 'As for the Mu'arreen, I have understood them, but what is the meaning of He said: 'Every deed you perform intending the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, be deficient in it in your own eyes, for all people, in their deeds, regarding what is between them and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are deficient.'

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman bin A'yun, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgave a man from the people of the desert due to two phrases with which he supplicated. He said: "O Allah, if You punish me, then I am deserving of that; and if You forgive me, then You are deserving of that." So Allah forgave him.'

From him, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his uncle, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: O the One Who pointed me to Himself and humbled my heart by my affirming Him, I ask You for security and faith in this world and the Hereafter.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, who said: I saw Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) in the courtyard of the Ka'bah at night, and he was praying. He prolonged the standing until he would lean on his right leg at one time, and on his left leg at another time. Then I heard him saying in a voice as if he were crying. O my Master! Will You punish me while Your love is in my heart? By Your might, if You do so, You will surely gather me and the people with whom I have long been an enemy for Your sake.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) taught us a supplication and instructed us to supplicate with it on the day of Friday: O Allah, I have directed myself to You with my need and revealed to You today my poverty and my destitution. Thus, today I am more hopeful for Your Forgiveness than for my deeds, and Your Forgiveness and Mercy are more capacious than my sins. So undertake the fulfillment of every need that is for me, by Your Power over it, and that is easy upon You, and by my poverty to You. For I have never attained goodness except from You, and no one has turned away evil from me except You. And I do not hope for my Hereafter and my world besides You, nor for my day of poverty and the day when people leave me alone in my pit. And I present myself to You, O Lord, with my poverty.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Atiyya, from Zayd al-Sa'igh, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Supplicate to Allah for us.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah! Grant them truthful narration, and fulfillment of the trust, and preservation upon the prayers. O Allah! They are the most deserving of Your creatures that You do this for them. O Allah, and do it for them.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Ali bin al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was saying: 'O Allah, bestow upon me reliance upon You, and delegation to You (of affairs), and pleasure with Your decree, and submission to Your command, until I do not love the hastening of what You have delayed, nor the delay of what You have hastened, O Lord of the worlds.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Suheym, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying while he was raising his hand towards the sky: 'O Lord! Do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, ever, neither less than that nor more.' He said, 'So it was with immediate flow of the tears from the sides of his beard. Then he turned towards me and said: O Ibn Abu Yafour! Yunus ibn Matta, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, left him to himself for less than the blink of an eye, so he committed that sin.' I said, 'So did he reach disbelief with it, may Allah keep you well?' He said: 'No, but death upon that state is destruction.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, raising it, said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him: Indeed your Lord says to you: When you wish to worship Me for a day and night as is the right of My worship, so raise your hands to Me and say: O Allah, for You is the praise, an eternal praise with Your eternity; and for You is the praise, a praise with no end to it besides Your Knowledge; and for You is the praise, a praise having no extension for it besides Your Desire; and for You is the praise, a praise having no Recompense for its speaker except Your Pleasure. O Allah, for You is the praise, all of it, and for You is the Favour, all of it, and for You is the Beauty, all of it, and for You is the Light, all of it, and for You is the Might, all of it, and for You is the Grandeur, all of it, and for You is the Magnificence, all of it, and for You is the world, all of it, and for You is the Hereafter, all of it, and for You is the night and the day, all of it, and for You is the creation, all of it, and in Your Hand is the goodness, all of It, and to You do the matters return, all of them, their public and their private. O Allah, for You is the praise, an everlasting Praise. You are the Good affliction, the One of Majestic Laudation, the concealed Bounty Giver, the Just Judge, the abundant Giver, the Good Rewarder, Lord of the one in the earth and Lord of the ones in the sky. O Allah, for You is the Praise in the seven mighty (skies), and for You is the Praise in the earth spread out, and for You is the Praise of the endurance of the servants, and for You is the Praise at the times of the afflictions, and for You is the Praise in the mountains (like) pegs, and for You is the Praise in the night when it covers, and for You is the Praise in the day when it brightens, and for You is the Praise in the Hereafter, and the former (life in the earth), and for You is the Praise in the doubles (Imams and the Magnificent Quran. And Glory be to Allah, and with His Praise, and the earth, all of it would be in His Grip on the Day of Judgment, and the skies would be (like) leaflets in His Right Hand. Glorious is He and Exalted from what they (people) are associating. Glory be to Him and with His Praise. Everything will perish except for His Face. Glory be to You, our Lord, and You are more E

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) dictated this supplication to me, and it is comprehensive for the world and the Hereafter. You should say after praising Allah and lauding Him: O Allah, You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Forbearing, the Benevolent; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Mighty, the Wise. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the One, the Subduer; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the King, the Compeller. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Merciful, the Forgiver. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Severe in Punishment; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Great, the Exalted. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Hearing, the Seeing; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Invincible, the All-Powerful. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Forgiving, the Appreciative; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Praiseworthy, the Glorious. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Forgiving, the Loving; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Affectionate, the Bestower. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Forbearing, the Recompenser; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Generous, the Noble. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the One, the Unique. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Unseen, the Witness; and You are Allah, there is no god except You, the Manifest, the Hidden. And You are Allah, there is no god except You, Knower of everything. Your Light is Perfect, so You Guide, and You Extended Your Hand, so You Gave. Our Lord, Your Face is the most Benevolent of faces, and Your Direction is the best of directions, and Your Gift is the most superior of gifts and the most delightful. You are obeyed, Our Lord, so You are thanked; and You are disobeyed, Our Lord, so You forgive whomever You will. You Answer the desperate ones, and Remove the evil, and Accept the repentance, and Pardon the sins. Your Favors cannot be repaid, nor can Your Bounties be counted, nor can the speech of a speaker reach Your Praise. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Hasten their relief, an

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Will you specialise me with a supplication?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Say: O One, O Glorified, O Unique, O Eternal, O He who did not beget and was not begotten, and there was none comparable to Him. O Mighty, O Generous, O Affectionate, O Bestower, O Hearer of supplications, O Most Generous of those asked, and O Best of those who give. O Allah, O Allah, O Allah.' I said, 'And Nuh (Noah) certainly called upon Us, so excellent are the Responders.' Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'Yes, excellent is the Responder, excellent is the One supplicated to, and excellent is the One asked from'. 'I ask You by the Light of Your Face, and I ask You by Your Might, and Your Power, and Your Compulsion, and I ask You by Your Kingdom, and Your Fortified Shield, and by Your Grip, and all Your Pillars, and by the right of Muhammad, and by the right of the Successors after Muhammad, that You should send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You should do such and such with me.'

From him, from one of his companions, from Husayn ibn 'Umara, from Husayn ibn Abu Saeed Al-Mukari and Jahm ibn Abu Jahma, from Abu Ja'far, a man from the people of Kufa who was known by his teknonym, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Teach me a supplication I can use to supplicate with.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, say: O the One I hope for every goodness, and O the One whose wrath I feel safe from at every stumble, and O the One Who gives much for a little, O the One Who gives to the one who asks Him out of His compassion and mercy, O the One Who gives to the one who does not ask Him and does not know Him! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and give me, due to my asking, from all the goodness of the world and all the goodness of the Hereafter, for it is not deficient what You have given me, and increase me from the expansiveness of Your grace, O Generous!'

And from him, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he taught his brother Abdullah ibn Ali this supplication. O Allah, raise my expectation upwards, and do not make me an object of covetousness for an enemy or an envier, and protect me while standing and sitting, awake and sleeping. O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and guide me to Your most straight path, and save me from the heat of Hell, and shake off from me the debt and the sin, and make me from the best of the choicest of the world.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa and Harun ibn Kharjah, who said: 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying.' Have mercy on me from what there is no strength for me with, nor any patience for me upon.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Hafs, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to him, 'Teach me a supplication.' He said, 'So where are you from the supplication of al-ilhah (insistence/urgency)?' I said, 'And what is the supplication of al-ilhah?' He said: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and what is between them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne, and Lord of Jibra'il, Mikail, and Isra'il, and Lord of the Magnificent Quran, and Lord of Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets. I ask You by that by which the sky is established, and by which the earth is established, and by which You separate the gathered ones, and by which You gather the scattered ones, and by which You provide for the living, and by which You counted the number of sands, and the weight of the mountains, and the measure of the seas.' Then you send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, then you ask Him for your need, and be insistent in the seeking.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Karram, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he used to say: O Allah, fill my heart with love for You, and fear of You, and affirmation and faith in You, and awe of You, and longing for You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. O Allah, make meeting You beloved to me, and make for me in Your meeting the best of mercy and blessing, and join me with the righteous, and do not delay me with the evil, and join me with the righteous of those who have passed, and make me with the righteous of those who remain, and take me by the way of the righteous, and assist me upon myself with what You assist the righteous upon themselves, and do not return me to evil after You have rescued me from it. O Lord of the worlds, I ask You for faith that has no end until meeting You, causing me to live and die upon it, and resurrect me upon it when You resurrect me, and free my heart from show-off and fame and doubt in Your religion. O Allah, give me victory in Your religion, and strength in Your worship, and understanding in Your creation, and two portions of Your mercy, and whiten my face with Your light, and make my desire to be what is with You, and cause me to die in Your way upon Your religion and the religion of Your Messenger. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness, old age, cowardice, stinginess, heedlessness, hardness of heart, weakness, and poverty. And I seek refuge in You, O Lord, from a self that is not satisfied, and from a heart that does not humble itself, and from a supplication that is not heard, and from a prayer that is not beneficial. And I seek refuge in You for myself, my family, and my offspring from the accursed Satan. O Allah, no one can protect me from You, and I find no shelter besides You, so do not abandon me, and do not return me to destruction, nor return me to punishment. I ask You for steadfastness upon Your religion, and affirmation of Your Book, and following of Your Messenger. O Allah, remember me with Your mercy and do not remember me with my sin, and accept from me, and increase me from Your grace, for I am longing for You. O Allah, make the reward of my speech and the reward of my sitting Your pleasure with me, and make my deeds and my supplication sincere for You, and make my reward Paradise by Your mercy, and gather for me all that I asked You for, and

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khas'ami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Zarr came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with him was Gabriel (peace be upon him) in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had secluded him (Gabriel). So when he (Abu Zarr) saw them, he turned away from them and did not cut off their conversation. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! This is Abu Zarr who has passed by us and did not greet us. Had he greeted, we would have returned the greeting to him. O Muhammad! Indeed, he has a supplication which he supplicates with that is well-known among the people of the sky, so ask him about it when I ascend to the sky.' So when Gabriel ascended, Abu Zarr came to the Prophet. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'What prevented you, O Abu Zarr, from greeting us when you passed by us?' He said: 'I thought, O Messenger of Allah, that the one who was with you, Dihya al-Kalbi, you had secluded for one of your matters.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That was Gabriel (peace be upon him), O Abu Zarr, and he said: Had he greeted us, we would have returned the greeting to him.' So when Abu Zarr knew that it was Gabriel (peace be upon him), regret entered him because he did not greet him, as Allah willed. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'What is this supplication that you supplicate with, for Gabriel (peace be upon him) has informed me that you have a supplication that you supplicate with which is well-known in the sky?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I say: O Allah! I ask You for safety and faith in You, and confirmation in Your Prophet, and well-being from all affliction, and gratitude for well-being, and neediness from the evil of people.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibnoub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, who said: 'I took this supplication from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and Abu Ja'far used to call it 'The Comprehensive'.' In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no associate for Him. And I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. I believe in Allah and in all of His Messengers, and in all of what He revealed with upon all of the Messengers, and that the Promise of Allah is True, and His Meeting is True, and Allah Spoke the Truth and the Mursil Prophets delivered (the Message). And the Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, and Glory be to Allah every time something Glorifies Allah, and just as Allah Loves that He be Glorified. And the Praise is for Allah every time something praises Him, and just as He Loves that He be Praised. And there is no god except Allah every time something Extols the Oneness of Allah, and just as Allah Loves that He be Extolled. And Allah is the Greatest, every time something exclaims the Greatness of Allah and just as Allah Loves that His Greatness be exclaimed. O Allah! I ask You for the opening of the goodness, and for its completion, and for its pleasures, and its benefits, and its Blessings, and what my knowledge reaches it, and what my memory falls short of its counting. O Allah! Draw closer to me the causes for its recognition, and Open its doors for me, and Overwhelm me with the Blessings of Your Mercy, and Bestow upon me the infallibility from the decline from Your Religion. And Purify my heart from the doubts, and do not Let my heart be pre-occupied with my world and my immediate life from the deferred Rewards of my Hereafter, and Pre-occupy my heart with the preservation of what is not Acceptable from me from being ignorant of it, and Humble my tongue for every goodness, and Purify my heart from the showing off, and do not Cause it (showing off) to flow in my joints, and Make my deeds to be sincerely for You. O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from the evil and the varieties of the immoralities, all of them, its apparent ones and its hidden ones, and its neglectful ones, and the entirety of what the Pelted Satan intends me with, and what the obstinate ruling authorities intend me with from what his knowledge encompa

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Say: 'O Allah, expand for me in my sustenance, and extend for me in my lifespan, and forgive me my sin, and make me from those whom You help Your religion with, and do not replace me with another.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he (peace be upon him) was saying: O the One Who is grateful for the little, and pardons the much, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Forgive me the sins whose pleasure has passed and whose consequence remains.

And by this chain, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was from his supplications that he would say: O Light! O Holy! O First of the foremost and O Last of the latter! O Beneficent! O Merciful! Forgive me the sins that change the bounties, and forgive me the sins that bring down calamities, and forgive me the sins that rupture the defences, and forgive me the sins that bring down afflictions, and forgive me the sins that assist the enemies, and forgive me the sins that hasten perishing, and forgive me the sins that cut off hope, and forgive me the sins that darken the atmosphere, and forgive me the sins that uncover the cover, and forgive me the sins that repel supplication, and forgive me the sins that repel the rain of the sky.

From him from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) } } }, { O my aid in my distress, and O my companion in my hardship, and O my guardian in my prosperity, and O my helper in my desire. He (peace be upon him) said: And it was from the supplication of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'O Allah, You wrote the traces, and You knew the news, and You inspected the secrets, so You settled between us and the hearts; therefore the secret with You is open, and the hearts are directed to You, and Your command for a thing when You intend it is that You say to it: Be, so it becomes.' So say with Your mercy to Your obedience that it should enter into every limb of my limbs, and do not leave me until I meet You; and say with Your mercy to Your disobedience that it should exit from every limb of my limbs, so it does not approach me until I meet You; and provide me from the world, and make me ascetic in it, and do not turn it away from me while I have desire for it, O the Beneficent.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala ibn Razin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, who said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) gave me this supplication.' All praise is for Allah, the Guardian of praise, its people, its end, and its place. He made sincere the one who affirmed His Oneness, and guided the one who worshipped Him, and granted success to the one who obeyed Him, and secured the one who held fast to Him. O Allah, O Possessor of Generosity, Glory, Beautiful Praise, and Laudation, I ask You with the asking of one who humbled his neck to You, whose nose was rubbed in the dust for You, whose face was covered in dust for You, whose self was subdued for You, whose tears flowed from Your fear, whose sobbing repeated, who confessed his sins to You, whose mistake exposed him before You, whose fault shamed him before You, whose strength weakened at that, whose stratagem diminished, whose sources of deception were cut off from him, and every falsehood wasted away from him, and his sins compelled him to the humility of his position before You, his submission to You, and his invocation to You. I ask You, O Allah, the asking of one who is at his status, I am more eager to You than his eagerness, and I am more supplicating to You than his supplication, and I invoke to You with the strongest invocation. O Allah, have mercy on the compliance of my speech, the humility of my position and my sitting, and my submission to You with my neck. I ask You, O Allah, for guidance from straying, insight from blindness, and right direction from misguidance. And I ask You, O Allah, for abundant praise during prosperity, the most beautiful patience during affliction, the best gratitude at the place of gratitude, and submission during doubts. And I ask You for strength in obeying You, weakness from disobeying You, fleeing to You from You, and nearness to You, O Lord, so that I may be pleased, and seeking everything that pleases You from me in pleasing Your creatures, seeking Your Pleasure. O Lord, whom do I hope for if You do not have mercy on me, or who will be kind to me if You exclude me, or whose pardon benefits me if You punish me, or whose gifts I hope for if You deprive me, or who controls my honor if You humble me, or whose humiliation harms me if You honor me? O Lord, how evil is my deed, and how ugly is my work, and how harsh is my heart, and how l

Ibn Mahboub said: Nuh Abu Al-Yaqzan narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Supplicate with this supplication: O Allah, I ask You by Your Mercy which cannot be attained from You except by Your Pleasure, and the exiting from all Your disobedience, and the entering into everything that pleases You, and salvation from every predicament, and the exit from every major sin that I committed deliberately, or slipped by me in error, or insinuated upon me by the whispers of Satan. I ask You for a fear that stops me at the limits of Your Pleasure, and by which every lustful desire insinuated by my whims is diverted from me, and my opinion is made to falter so that it does not exceed the boundary of Your permissibles. I ask You, O Allah, for taking hold of the best of what You know, and leaving the evil of all that You know, or my mistakes from where I do not know, or from where I do know. I ask You for expansion in sustenance, and asceticism in sufficiency, and the exit from every doubt through clarity, and correctness in every argument, and truthfulness in all situations, and fairness of people towards myself regarding what is against me or for me. and humility in giving the due right from all situations of anger and pleasure, and leaving both little and much of rebellion in my speech and action. and the completion of Your blessings in all things, and gratitude to You for them, so that You may be pleased, and after being pleased. And I ask You for the choice in everything where there is a choice, among the easy matters, all of them, not the difficult ones. O Generous, O Generous, O Generous. And open for me the door of the matter in which is health and relief, and open its door for me, and ease its exit for me. And whoever of Your creatures You have empowered over me, seize him from me by his hearing, his sight, his tongue, and his hand; seize him from his right, his left, behind him, and in front of him, and prevent him from reaching me with evil. Mighty is Your neighbor, and Majestic is the praise of Your Face, and there is no god but You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant. O Allah, You are my hope in every distress, and You are my reliance in every difficulty, and You are for me in every matter that befalls me a trust and a provision. So how many worries weaken the heart, in which strategy is scarce, the enemy gloats over, and matters ex

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Say, O Allah! I ask You for the words of the repentants and their deeds, and the light of the Prophets and their truthfulness, and the salvation of the Mujahideen and their reward, and the gratitude of the Chosen ones and their advice, and the deeds of the Rememberers and their conviction, and the faith of the scholars and their understanding, and the worship of the humble ones and their humility, and the wisdom of the jurists and their conduct, and the fear of the pious and their desire, and the affirmation of the believers and their reliance, and the hope of the good-doers and their righteousness. O Allah! I ask You for the reward of the grateful, and the station of the near ones, and the companionship of the Prophets. O Allah! I ask You for the fear of those who work for You, and the deeds of those who fear You, and the humility of those who worship You, worship You, and the conviction of those who rely upon You, and the reliance of the believers in You. O Allah! You are Knowing of my need without being taught, and You are Capacious for it without being strained. You are the One whom no beggar exhausts, and no attainer diminishes, and no speaker's words can reach Your praise. You are as You say, and above what we say. O Allah! Make for me a relief that is near, and a great reward, and a beautiful covering. O Allah! You know that I am upon injustice to myself and extravagance upon it, and I have not taken for You an opposite, nor a match, nor a companion, nor a son. O He whom questions do not confuse, O He whom nothing occupies from anything, nor hearing from hearing, nor sight from sight, and whom the insistence of the insistent does not tire. I ask You to relieve me in this hour of mine from where I expect and from where I do not expect. You revive the bones when they are dust, and You are Able over all things. O He to whom my little gratitude did not deprive me, and my great sin did not expose me, and He saw me upon disobedience but did not confront me, and He created me for what He created me for, but I did other than what He created me for. So what a good Master You are, O my Master, and what an evil servant I am. You found me, and what a good Seeker You are, O my Lord, and what an evil sought one I am. You fou

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Teach me a supplication and be brief.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Say: O One who pointed me to Himself and humbled my heart with believing in Him, I ask You for safety and faith.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever precedes in supplication — it will be answered for him when affliction befalls him, and the angels will say, 'A well-known voice, not veiled from the sky'; and whoever does not precede in supplication — it will not be answered for him when affliction befalls him, and the angels will say, 'This is a voice we do not recognize.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from Anbasa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever fears an affliction that may befall him, and then precedes it with supplication, God, Mighty and Majestic, will never show him that affliction.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Harun ibn Kharja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, supplication during prosperity brings forth needs during affliction.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever is pleased that his supplication be answered during hardship, let him increase his supplication during prosperity.

From him, from his father, from Ubaydullah ibn Yahya, from a man, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ghawwas al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: My grandfather used to say: 'Hasten in supplication, for when a servant is one who supplicates frequently and an affliction befalls him and he supplicates, it is said (by the Angels): A well-known voice. And when he is not one who supplicates frequently and an affliction befalls him and he supplicates, it is said: Where were you before today?'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from one who narrated to him, from Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Supplication after the affliction has descended does not benefit.'

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah Mighty and Majestic does not answer a supplication manifested by an inattentive heart. So whenever you supplicate, be attentive with your heart, then be convinced of the answer.

The Commander of the Faithful (may Allah's blessings be upon him) said: 'God Mighty and Majestic does not accept the supplication of a heedless heart.' And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whenever one of you supplicates for the deceased, he should not supplicate for him while his heart is heedless from him; rather, he should strive earnestly for him in the supplication.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from some of his companions, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Sulaym al-Farra', from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Whenever you supplicate, be attentive with your heart and believe that your need is at the door (imminent).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn Amira, from whoever mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — does not answer a supplication that comes from the surface of a hard heart.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated for rain and the people were given to drink until they said, 'It is drowning (flood)!' and the Messenger of Allah gestured with his hand and turned it back, saying: 'O Allah, around us and not upon us!' He said: So the clouds dispersed. And they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you supplicated for rain for us but we were not given to drink, then you supplicated for rain for us and we were given to drink.' He said: 'Indeed I supplicated and there was no intention for me in that; then I supplicated and I had an intention in that.'

O Sa'd! Learn the Quran, for the Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection in the most excellent form that any creature has ever seen. the creatures. The people will be in one hundred and twenty thousand rows — eighty thousand rows being the community of Muhammad, and forty thousand rows from the rest of the communities. Then it comes to the rows of the Muslims in the form of a man and gives the greeting. Then they look at him, They say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous! This man is from the Muslims; we recognise him by his description and attributes, except that he was more intensely devoted to the Quran than us — that is why he was granted splendour, beauty, and radiance that we were not granted.' Then it passes on until it comes to the rows of the martyrs. The martyrs look at him and say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Lord, the Merciful! This man is from the martyrs; we recognise him by his bearing and attributes, except that he is from the martyrs of the sea — that is why he was granted splendour and excellence that we were not granted.' He (the Imam) said: 'Then it passes on until it comes to the rows of the sea martyrs in the form of a martyr. The sea martyrs look at him and their astonishment intensifies; they say: This one is from the sea martyrs; we recognise him by his bearing and his attributes, except that the island where he was killed was of a far greater terror than the island where we were killed — that is why he was granted splendour, beauty, and radiance that we were not granted.' Then it passes on until it comes to the rows of the Prophets and Messengers in the form of a sent Prophet. The Prophets and Messengers look at him and their astonishment intensifies, and they say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous! This Prophet is a Messenger; we recognise him by his bearing and attributes, except that he was given abundant merit.' He (the Imam) said: 'Then they gather and go to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and ask him, saying: O Muhammad! Who is this? He says to them: Do you not recognise him? They say: We do not recognise him; this one is from among those upon whom Allah has not been angered, upon him. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says: 'This is the Proof of Allah upon His creation' — and he greets him. Then it passes on until it comes

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people! You are in a house of truce and you are upon the back of a journey, and the travel with you is swift. You have seen the night and the day, the sun and the moon, wearing out everything new and bringing near everything distant, and bringing every appointed thing. So prepare the provisions for the length of the passage.' He (the narrator) said: Then al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad stood up and said: 'O Messenger of God, and what is the house of truce?' He said: 'A house of communication and severance. When the tribulations confound you like patches of dark night, then cling to the Quran, for it is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted, and an accuser who is ratified. Whoever places it before him, it guides him to Paradise; whoever places it behind him, it drives him to the Fire. It is the guide that points to the best path.' It is a Book in which there is detail, explanation, and achievement. It is the decisive word, not jest. It has an outward and an inward: its outward is judgment and its inward is knowledge; its outward is elegant and its inward is profound. It has luminaries, and upon its luminaries are more luminaries. Its wonders cannot be counted nor do its rarities become exhausted. In it are the lanterns of guidance, the minarets of wisdom, and a guide to recognition for whoever knows its attribute. So let the seeker brighten his vision and extend his contemplation to its capacity — he will be rescued from ruin and freed from entanglement, for pondering is the life of the heart of the perceptive, just as the enlightened one walks in darkness with light. So upon you is excellence in sincerity and littleness of hesitation.

Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, the Mighty, the Compeller sent down His Book upon you all, and it is the truthful and righteous. Therein is your news, and the news of those before you, and the news of those after you, and the news of the heavens and the earth. And if someone were to come to you informing you all about that, you would have been astonished.'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'I will be the first delegate to the Mighty, the Compeller, on the Day of Resurrection — and (also) His Book and the People of my Household. Then (will come) my community. Then I will ask them: What did you do with the Book of God and with the People of my Household?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed this Quran, in it are beacons of guidance and lanterns for the darkness. So let a beholder brighten his sight and open his vision to the illumination, for indeed pondering is the revival of the heart of the insightful one, just as the enlightened one walks in the darkness with the light.

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: It was in the bequest of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) to his companions: 'Know that the Quran is a guidance for the day and a light for the dark night, upon whatever there may be of hardship and destitution.'

Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said: A man complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of pain in his chest, so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: Seek healing through the Quran, for indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'and a healing for what is in the chests' [Quran 10:57].

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: No, by God! Neither will the command nor the Caliphate ever return to the clan of Abu Bakr and Umar, nor ever to the Banu Umayya, nor ever among the children of Talha and al-Zubayr — and that is because they discarded the Quran, invalidated the Sunnah, and disrupted the rulings. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Quran is a guidance from straying, a clarity from blindness, a rescue from stumbling, a light from darkness, an illumination from newly-occurring events, a protection from destruction, a right guidance from temptation, an explanation from strife, and a conveyance from this world to the Hereafter; and in it is the perfection of your religion — and no one deviates from the Quran except toward the Fire.
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed the Quran is a prohibitor and a commander — it commands toward Paradise and prohibits from the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sa'd al-Askaf, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I was given the long Chapters in place of the Torah, and I was given the Hundred [Verses] in place of the Gospel, and I was given the Doubles in place of the Psalms, and I was preferred with the Detailed [Surahs], sixty-eight Chapters, and they are predominant over the other Books; and the Torah is for Moses, and the Gospel for Jesus, and the Psalms for David.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection in the best appearance/image, so it will pass by the Muslims and they will say, 'This man is from us.' It will pass them by to the Prophets, and they will say, 'He is from us.' It will pass them by to the Proximate Angels, and they will say, 'He is from us,' until it reaches the Lord of Might, Exalted and Majestic. It will say, 'O Lord! So-and-so, son of so-and-so, I made his throat thirsty and I kept awake his night in the house of the world; and so-and-so, son of so-and-so, I did not make his throat thirsty and I did not keep awake his night.' The Blessed and Exalted will say, 'Admit them into Paradise according to their stations.' So it will stand up and they will follow it. It will say to the Believer, 'Recite and ascend.' So he will recite and ascend until each man from them reaches his station which is for him, so it will make him descend into it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, altogether, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'If those between the East and the West were to die, I would not feel lonely as long as the Quran is with me.' And when he (peace be upon him) recited 'Master of the Day of Judgment', he would repeat it until he was on the verge of dying.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Is'haq ibn Ghalib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gathers the first and the last, behold, they are with a person who has turned towards them. No one had ever seen a form more beautiful than his. So when the believers look at him, and he is the Quran, they say: 'This is from us. This is the best thing we have seen.' So when he reaches them, he passes them. Then the martyrs look at him, until when he reaches the last of them, he passes them, and they say: 'This is the Quran.' So he passes all of them. Until when he reaches the Envoys (Prophets), they say: 'This is the Quran,' so he passes them, until he reaches the Angels, and they say: 'This is the Quran.' So he passes them, then he reaches until he stands on the right of the Throne. So the Compeller (Allah) says: 'By My Might and My Majesty, and the elevation of My position, I shall surely honor today whoever honored you, and I shall surely humble whoever humiliated you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can I recite the Quran in one night?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I do not like it if you were to recite it in less than a month.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'In how much time should I recite the Quran?' He said, 'Recite it in fifths, or recite it in sevenths. Indeed, with me there is a Mushaf divided into fourteen parts.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Indeed, my father asked your grandfather about completing the Quran every night.' So your grandfather said to him, 'Every night?' He said to him, 'In the month of Ramadan.' So your grandfather said to him, 'In the month of Ramadan?' My father said to him, 'Yes, as much as I am able.' So my father used to complete it, forty completions in the month of Ramadan. Then I completed it after my father; sometimes I would add and sometimes I would be deficient, according to my free time, my busyness, my energy, and my laziness. So when it was the Day of Fitr, I would designate one completion for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), another for Ali (peace be upon him), another for Fatima (peace be upon her), then for the Imams (peace be upon them) until I reached you, so I designated one for you since I entered this state. So what is for me because of that? He said, 'For you, because of that, is that you will be with them on the Day of Judgment.' I said, 'Allah is the Greatest! So for me is that?' He said, 'Yes,' three times.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: Abu Baseer asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I was present. So he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Should I recite the Quran in one night?' So he said: 'No'. So he said, 'In two nights?' So he said: 'No'. Until it reached six nights. So he gestured by his hand, and said: 'Ha!' Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! The ones who were before you from the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) used to recite the Quran in a month, and less. The Quran is such that it should not be recited by jabbering, but slowly and with clarity. Whenever you pass by a Verse wherein is a Mention of the Fire, pause at it and seek Refuge with Allah from the Fire'. So Abu Baseer said, 'Should I recite the Quran in one night of the Month of Ramazan?' So he said: 'No'. So he said, 'In two nights?' So he said: 'No'. So he said, 'In three?' So he said: 'Ha!', and gestured by his hand, 'Yes, the Month of Ramazan is such that nothing resembles it from the (other) months. For it is a right and a sanctity. Frequent from the Salat, whatever your capacity may be'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, a non-Arab man from my community recites the Quran in a non-Arab manner, so the angels raise it up as Arabic.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from one of his companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We hear the Verses in the Quran, but they are not with us exactly as we hear them, nor do we recite them perfectly as it reached us from you. So, are we sinning?' He said, 'No. Recite as you have learned, and there will come to you one who will teach you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Badr, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever recites 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' once, blessings are bestowed upon him; and whoever recites it twice, blessings are bestowed upon him and his family; and whoever recites it three times, blessings are bestowed upon him, his family, and his neighbors. And whoever recites it twelve times, Allah builds for him twelve castles in Paradise, so the Preservers (angels) say: 'Go with us to the castle of our brother so-and-so, so that we may look at it.' And whoever recites it one hundred times, his sins of twenty-five years are forgiven him, apart from blood (shedding) and wealth (misappropriation). And whoever recites it four hundred times, he has the reward of four hundred martyrs, each of whom had his horse hamstrung and his blood shed. And whoever recites it a thousand times in a day and night, he will not die until he sees his seat in Paradise, or it is shown to him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded these verses to descend to the earth, they clung to the Throne and said: 'O Lord, to where are You causing us to descend? To the people of errors and sins?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to them to descend: 'By My Might and My Majesty! No one from the Progeny of Muhammad and their Shias will recite you at the end of what I have imposed upon him from the prescribed [prayers] in every day, except that I will look at him with My Hidden Eye in every day with seventy glances, fulfilling for him in every glance seventy needs, and accepting him despite whatever he is in from disobediences.' And these are: the Mother of the Book, and the Verse of the Throne, and the Verse of Dominion.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever recites all the Musabbihaat before sleeping will not die until he sees Al-Qaim; and if he dies, he will be in the vicinity of Muhammad the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Khashshab from Ibn Baqqah from Mu'adh from 'Amr ibn Jumay' (it was raised) to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Rasul Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever recites four verses from the beginning of Al-Baqarah, and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), and two verses after it, and three verses from its end, will not see in himself or his wealth anything he dislikes, nor will Satan come near him, nor will he forget the Quran.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever recites 'We have indeed revealed it in the Night of Decree' and makes his voice loud with it, he is like the one who draws his sword in the way of Allah; and whoever recites it privately, he is like the one rolling in his blood in the way of Allah; and whoever recites it ten times, a thousand sins from his sins are forgiven for him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (may the prayers of Allah be upon him) used to say: 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' is a third of the Quran, and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' is a quarter of the Quran.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever recites one hundred verses, praying with them during a night, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him, due to it, the Qunoot (supplication) for a night; and whoever recites two hundred verses outside of prayer, the Quran will not argue against him on the Day of Judgment; and whoever recites five hundred verses during a day and a night, in the prayer of the day and the night, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him in the Guarded Tablet, a Qintar of good deeds; and the Qintar is one thousand two hundred Owqiya, and the Owqiya is greater than the mountain of Uhud.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hasan, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever a single day passes for him, and he prays in it five prayers, and does not recite in them 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Say, He is Allah, One), it will be said to him: 'O servant of Allah, you are not from the praying ones.'

And by this chain, from Al-Hasan ibn Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not fail to recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' after the obligatory prayer, for whoever recites it, Allah will gather for him the goodness of this world and the Hereafter, and forgive him and his parents and whatever they beget.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, raising it, he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Surah Al-An'am was revealed in its totality, escorted by seventy thousand angels until it was revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). Therefore, magnify it and revere it, for the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is in it in seventy places, and had the people known what is in its recitation, they would not have neglected it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashir, from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who recites Al-hakum at-takathur at sleep-time would be saved from the strife of the grave.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfaly, raising it, he said: Surah Al-Hamd is not recited upon a pain seventy times, except that it settles.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If Al-Hamd (Surah Al-Fatihah) were recited over a deceased person seventy times, then the soul were to return to him, that would not be a cause for astonishment.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Bakr, from Salih, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no one in the stage of childhood who commits to reciting every night: "Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of Al-Falaq" and "Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of the people", each one three times, and "Say: He is Allah, One" one hundred times; and if he is not able, then fifty times, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will divert from him every mental affliction or illness from the illnesses of children, and dangerous thirst, and spoilage of the stomach, and blood circulation disorders, forever, as long as he maintains this vow until he reaches old age.' So if he commits himself to that, or maintains it, he will be protected until the Day Allah, Mighty and Majestic, captures his soul.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari, who said: I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever suffices himself with one verse from the Quran, from the East to the West, will be sufficed, provided he has conviction.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the amulet. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Take a new jar and put water in it, then recite upon it "We have indeed revealed it in the Night of Predestination" thirty times, then hang it, and drink from it and perform ablution with it, and increase the water in it, God willing.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Idrees al-Harithi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Mufazzal! Protect yourself from all people by [In the Name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful] and by [Say: He Allah is One]' Recite them on your right, and on your left, and in front of you, and from behind you, and from above you, and from beneath you. So whenever you go over to a tyrannous ruling authority, then recite them when you look at him, three times. And close your left hand, nor releasing it until you come out from his presence.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Salama ibn Muhriz, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one whom Al-Hamd does not cure, nothing would cure him'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Whoever recites 'When he retires to his bed' (Idha awa), 'Say: O unbelievers' (Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun), and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Qul huwa Allahu ahad), Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him an immunity from shirk (polytheism).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Do not tire of reciting 'When the earth is shaken with its shaking', for whoever recites it in his optional prayers, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not strike him with an earthquake ever, nor will he die by it, nor by a thunderbolt, nor by a calamity from the calamities of the world until he dies. And when he dies, a noble Angel descends upon him from his Lord and sits by his head, and says: 'O Angel of Death, be kind to the friend of Allah, for he frequently remembered me and mentioned the recitation of this Chapter.' And the Chapter says to him similarly, and the Angel of Death says: 'My Lord has commanded me to listen to him and obey, and not to extract his soul until he instructs me with that. So when he instructs me, I will extract his soul.' And the Angel of Death does not cease to be with him until he instructs him with the extraction of his soul; and when the cover is lifted for him, so he sees his stations in Paradise, so he extracts his soul from the gentlest of what can be from the treatment. Then his soul is escorted to Paradise by seventy thousand Angels, hastening with it to Paradise.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The reciters of the Quran are three: A man who recites the Quran, so he takes it as a commodity and attracts the attention of the kings with it, and extends his control by it upon the people. And a man who recites the Quran, so he memorizes its letters and wastes its limits, and his standing is (like) the standing of the arrow. May Allah not cause a lot of these ones to be from the bearers of the Quran. And a man who recites the Quran, so he places the medicine of the Quran upon the illness of his heart. So he holds a vigil with it during his nights and remains thirsty due to it by his day, and he stands by it in his mosques, and ignores his bed due to it. So it is due to them that Allah the Mighty, the Compeller repels the affliction, and it is due to them Allah the Mighty and Majestic defends from the enemies, and it is due to them that Allah the Mighty and Majestic sends down the rain from the sky. Thus, by Allah, these ones among the reciters of the Quran are more rarer than the red ruby.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Yahya, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: I heard Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Quran was revealed in three parts: one-third is regarding us and our enemies, one-third is about Sunnah and examples, and one-third is about Impositions and regulations.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Quran was revealed in four quarters: a quarter is Permissible, and a quarter is Prohibitions, and a quarter is Sunnah and regulations, and a quarter is information of what was before you and news of what is to happen after you, and decisions of what (disputes there are) between you.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Quran was revealed in four quarters: a quarter is regarding us, and a quarter is regarding our enemies, and a quarter is Sunnah and examples, and a quarter is Obligations and regulations.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sariyy, from his uncle Ali ibn al-Sariyy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The first of what was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim, Iqra' bi-ismi Rabbik' and its last was 'Idha ja'a nasrullah'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Month of Ramadan is that in which the Quran was Revealed,' but rather it was Revealed during twenty years between its first and its last. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Quran was Revealed as a whole in one go during the Month of Ramadan to the Frequented House, and then it was Revealed in length over twenty years.' Then he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Parchments of Ibrahim were Revealed on the first night of the Month of Ramadan, and the Torah was Revealed when six days had passed from the Month of Ramadan, and the Gospel was Revealed when thirteen nights had passed from the Month of Ramadan, and the Psalms were Revealed when eighteen had passed from the Month of Ramadan, and the Quran was Revealed on the twenty-third of the Month of Ramadan.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not derive omens from the Quran.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn al-Warraq, who said: I presented to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a book in which was the Quran, sealed and adorned with gold, and a chapter was written at its end with gold. So he showed it to him, but he did not fault anything in it except the writing of the Quran with gold, and said: 'I do not like it if the Quran is written except with black (ink), just as it was written the first time.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Take the Mus'haf (Quran) during the second third of the month of Ramadan, so display it and place it in front of you and say: O Allah, I ask You by Your Revealed Book and what is in it, and in it is Your Greatest Name, the Magnificent, and Your Good Names, and what is feared and hoped for, that You make me from those emancipated by You from the Fire, and supplicate with whatever seems fit to you regarding your needs.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: For everything there is a spring, and the spring of the Quran is the month of Ramadan.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, or from someone else, from the one who mentioned it, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Quran and the Furqan, are they two things or one thing? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Quran is the entirety of the Book, and the Furqan is the Decisive, the Obligatory to be acted upon.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Quran is one, revealed from the Presence of One, but the differences come from the direction of the reporters.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The people are saying that the Quran was revealed upon seven letters (phrases).' He said: 'They are lying, enemies of Allah! But it was revealed upon one letter (phrase) from the Presence of the One.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Quran was revealed with the meaning of 'Iyyaka' (You) referring to the general community, while 'Yā Jārat' (O Neighbor) was heard by the specific neighbor. And in another report, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: Its meaning is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reproached His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with, so He means by it what has passed in the Quran, such as His saying: 'And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little,' meaning by that others than him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Revelation of the Quran. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Recite it just as you were taught.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) handed over to me a Mushaf (copy of the Quran) and said: 'Do not look into it.' So I opened it and read in it 'Lam yakulli allatheena kafaroo' [98:1], and I found therein the names of seventy men from Quraish, by their names and the names of their fathers. He said: 'So he sent a message to me: Send to me with the Mushaf.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) said: 'No man strikes one part of the Quran with another except that he disbelieves.'

From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Nadr, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Maryam Al-Ansari, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'A Mus'haf (parchment/copy of the Quran) fell into the sea, so they found it, and whatever was in it had been obliterated except for this Verse.' Indeed, to Allah do all affairs eventually come.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washsha from Aban from Maymun al-Qaddah said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Read.' I said, 'From which thing should I read?' He said, 'From the ninth Chapter.' So I began to seek it, so he said, 'Read from Surah Yunus.' For those who do good is the best [reward] and extra, and no darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am astonished at how I do not grow gray when I recite the Quran.''

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hajjal, from the one who mentioned it, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'In clear Arabic language'. He said: 'It (the Quran) explains the languages, and the languages do not explain it'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Aamir ibn Abdullah ibn Juza'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no servant who recites the end of Surah Al-Kahf except that he will wake up in the hour that he intends.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Salama, who said: A man recited to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening, certain phrases from the Quran that were not according to what the people were reciting. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Stop this recitation! Recite as the people recite, until the Qaim (peace be upon him) arises.' So when the Qaim (peace be upon him) arises, he will recite the Book of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) according to its precise limits, and he will bring out the Mus'haf (codex) which Ali (peace be upon him) had written. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) brought it out to the people when he had finished compiling and writing it, and said to them: 'This is the Book of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) just as Allah revealed it to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and I have gathered it from the two Tablets.' So they said: 'It is that which is with us, a comprehensive Mus'haf containing the Quran; we have no need for it.' So he said: 'By Allah, you will not see it after this day of yours ever! It was incumbent upon me to inform you when I had gathered it, so that you might recite it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Saeed ibn Abdullah al-A'raj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who recites the Quran, then forgets it, then recites it, then forgets it. Is there any blame upon him for it? He said: No.

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) said: 'No man strikes the Quran, part of it with the other, except that he disbelieves.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Sadeer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Surah Al-Mulk is the Defender; it protects from the punishment of the grave. It is written in the Torah as Surah Al-Mulk. And whoever recites it during his night, he has abundant reward and goodness, and he will not be recorded among the heedless due to it. And I bow (in prayer) with it after the last Isha prayer while I am seated, and indeed my father (peace be upon him) used to recite it during his day and his night. And whoever recites it, when the Nakir and Nakeer (questioning angels) come to him in his grave from the direction of his legs, his legs will say to them: 'There is no way for you two to what is before me. This servant used to stand upon me and recite Surah Al-Mulk every day and night.' And when they come to him from the direction of his chest/midsection, he will say to them: 'There is no way for you two to what is before me. This servant had sheltered Surah Al-Mulk inside me.' And when they come to him from the direction of his tongue, he will say to them: 'There is no way for you two to what is before me. This servant used to recite by me, every day and night, Surah Al-Mulk.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Farqad and al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who both said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and with us was Rabi'ah al-Ra'i. We mentioned the merit of the Quran. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If Ibn Mas'ud does not recite according to our recitation, then he is astray.' Rabi'ah said, 'Astray?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, astray.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for us, we recite according to the recitation of Ubayy.'

Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Quran which Jibraeel (peace be upon him) brought to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was seventeen thousand verses.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Husayn al-Farisi, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people of the Quran are at the highest rank among human beings, except for the Prophets and the Messengers. Therefore, do not belittle the people of the Quran in their rights, for they have from God, the Mighty, the Compeller, a lofty position.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The memoriser of the Quran, the one who acts by it, will be with the Ambassadors (angelic scribes), the honourable, the righteous.

And by his chain, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Learn the Quran, for indeed it will come on the Day of Resurrection to its companion in the form of a beautiful youth, pale of complexion. The Quran will say to him: I am the one who kept you awake during your night, and made you thirsty during your midday hours, and dried your saliva, and caused your tears to flow. I shall be with you wherever you go; and every merchant is behind his own trade, but I am for you today, surpassing the trade of every merchant.
