And there shall come to you a prestige from God, Mighty and Majestic — so receive glad tidings.' Then a crown shall be brought and placed upon his head. He shall be given the deed of security in his right hand, and the deed of eternal life in the Gardens of Paradise in his left hand, and he shall be clothed in two garments. Then it shall be said to him: 'Recite and ascend.' And every time he recites a verse, he ascends a level. And his two parents shall be clothed in two garments, if they were believers. Then it shall be said to both of them: 'This is because you taught him the Quran.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Minhal al-Qassab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever recites the Quran and he is a young believer, the Quran blends with his flesh and his blood, and God Mighty and Majestic places him with the honourable, righteous scribes [angels]. And the Quran will be a defender for him on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'O my Lord! Every worker has received the reward of his deeds except my [faithful] doer — so let him reach the most prestigious of Your gifts.' He said: 'Then God, the Mighty and Compeller, will clothe him with two garments from the garments of Paradise and place a crown of honour upon his head. Then it is said to him [the Quran]: Have We pleased you regarding him?' So the Quran says: 'O my Lord! I used to wish for him that which is superior to this.' So he is given security in his right hand and eternity in his left. Then he enters Paradise, and it is said to him: 'Recite and ascend a level.' Then it is said to him: 'Have We made him reach it and pleased you?' And he [the Quran] says: 'Yes.' He said: 'And whoever recites it frequently and regularly reviews it with difficulty — from the intensity of memorizing it — God Mighty and Majestic will give him the reward of this twice.'

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The most deserving of the people to show humbleness in private and in public is the bearer of the Quran; and the most deserving of the people in private and in public for salat and fasting is the bearer of the Quran. Then he called out in his loudest voice: 'O bearer of the Quran! Be humble with it and God will raise you, and do not seek glory through it or God will disgrace you. O bearer of the Quran! Adorn yourself with it for God's sake and God will adorn you with it; and do not adorn yourself with it for the people's sake or God will dishonor you with it.' Whoever completes the Quran, it is as if prophethood has been placed within his sides — yet no revelation comes to him. And whoever memorizes the Quran, it befits him not to act ignorantly alongside those who act ignorantly toward him, not to become angry toward those who are angry with him, and not to be irritable toward those who are irritable with him — rather, he should pardon, excuse, forgive, and forbear, out of reverence for the Quran. And whoever has been given the Quran, if he thinks that anyone from among the people has been given something superior to what he has been given, then he has magnified what God has belittled and belittled what God has magnified.

Salih al-Qammat narrated to us, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'The people are four (types).' So I said, 'May I be your ransom! And what are they?' So he said: 'A man given iman (faith) but not given the Quran; and a man given the Quran but not given iman; and a man given the Quran and given iman; and a man not given the Quran nor iman.' He said: I said, 'May I be your ransom! Explain their states to me.' So he said: 'As for the one given iman but not given the Quran, his example is like the example of the date — its taste is sweet, but there is no aroma for it. And as for the one given the Quran but not given iman, his example is like the example of the myrtle — its aroma is pleasant but its taste is bitter. And as for the one given the Quran and iman, his example is like the example of the citron (utruja) — its aroma is pleasant and its taste is good. And as for the one not given iman nor the Quran, his example is like the example of the colocynth — its taste is bitter and there is no aroma for it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, altogether from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from al-Zuhri who said: I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Which of the deeds is most superior?' He said: 'The one who alights and departs.' I said: 'And what is the one who alights and departs?' He said: 'Opening the Quran and completing it — every time one comes to its beginning, one travels to its end.' And he (also) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever God has given the Quran, and he sees that a man has been given something superior to what he was given, then he has indeed belittled something great and magnified something small.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from his father, from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The one who recites the Quran is rich, and there is no poverty after it; and if not, then there is no riches for him.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jamila, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of reciters of the Quran! Fear God, Mighty and Majestic, regarding what He has entrusted you with from His Book, for indeed I will be questioned and you will be questioned. I will be questioned about the delivery of the Message, and as for you, you will be questioned about what you were entrusted with from the Book of God and my Sunnah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs, who said: I heard Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying to a man: 'Do you love to remain in the world?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why?' He said, 'For the recitation of Say: He is Allah, One.' So he (peace be upon him) was silent from him. Then he said to him after a while: 'O Hafs! Whoever dies from our friends and our Shias and is not proficient in the Quran, will be taught in his grave, so that Allah may raise his status by it, for the levels of Paradise are according to the measure of the Verses of the Quran. It will be said to him: Recite and ascend. So he will recite, then he will ascend.' Hafs said, 'So I did not see anyone more intensely fearful upon himself than Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), nor anyone more hopeful of the people than him, and his recitation was grief. So whenever he recited, it was as if he was addressing a person.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad jointly, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Verily the one who struggles with the Quran and memorizes it with difficulty and with poor memory — for him are two rewards.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from al-Sabbah ibn Sayaba, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who has difficulty in (reciting) the Quran will have two rewards, and the one who has ease in it will be with the former ones.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sulaym al-Farra', from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'It is befitting for the believer that he not die until he learns the Quran, or is in the process of learning it.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be made your ransom! I used to recite the Quran but it has escaped from me, so supplicate to God, Mighty and Majestic, that He teach it to me.' He (the narrator) said: It was as if he (the Imam) was alarmed at that, and he said: 'May God teach it to you and to us all.' He said: 'And we were approximately ten.' Then he said: 'The surah is with the man who had recited it and then abandoned it. It will come to him on the Day of Resurrection in the most beautiful form, and will greet him. He will say: Who are you? It will say: I am such-and-such surah. Had you adhered to me and held fast to me, I would have brought you down to this rank. Therefore, it is upon you to (adhere to) the Quran.' Then he said: 'Among the people is one who recites the Quran so that it be said, so-and-so is a reciter; and among them is one who recites the Quran to seek worldly gains through it, and there is no goodness in that; and among them is one who recites the Quran to benefit from it in his salat, his night, and his day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever forgets a chapter of the Quran, it will be embodied for him in a beautiful form in a lofty station in Paradise. When he sees it, he will say: "What are you? How beautiful you are! If only you were mine!" So it will say: "Do you not recognize me? I am Surah such-and-such. Had you not forgotten me, I would have raised you to this (station)."'

Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Yaqub al-Ahmar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'There is a heavy debt upon me, and what has come upon me has caused the Quran to slip away from me.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Quran! The Quran! Verily the verse from the Quran and the chapter shall come on the Day of Resurrection until it ascends a thousand levels — meaning in Paradise — and it shall say: Had you memorized me, I would have brought you here.'

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man had learned a Surah (of the Holy Quran) and then forgot it or neglected it, and he enters Paradise, it will appear to him from above in the most beautiful form, saying: 'Do you recognise me?' He will say, 'No.' It will say: 'I am Surah such and such. You did not act by me and you abandoned me. But by God, had you acted by me, I would have made you reach this rank.' And it gestured with its hand to what was above it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Hajjaj al-Khashshab, from Abu Kahmas al-Haytham ibn Ubayd who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who recites the Quran and then forgets it. I reiterated the question to him three times: Is there any blame upon him for it? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, both together, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ya'qub al-Ahmar who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! Worries and other matters have afflicted me, until nothing of goodness remains without a portion of it having slipped away from me — even the Quran, a portion of it has slipped away from me.' He (the narrator) said: And he (the Imam) was alarmed when I mentioned the Quran. Then he said: 'Indeed a man forgets a chapter from the Quran, and it will come to him on the Day of Resurrection until it appears before him from a level among some of the levels, and says: Peace be upon you. He will say: And upon you peace — who are you? It will say: I am Chapter such-and-such. You wasted me and abandoned me. Had you but held fast to me, I would have brought you to this level.' Then he gestured with his finger. Then he said: 'You must adhere to the Quran — learn it! For among the people is one who learns the Quran so that it may be said, 'So-and-so is a reciter'; and among them is one who learns it seeking praise for his voice, so it is said 'So-and-so has a beautiful voice' — and there is no good in that. And among them is one who learns it and stands by it during his night and his day, not caring who knows of that and who does not.'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Quran is a covenant of God to His creatures; thus it is befitting for the Muslim person that he looks into his covenant, and that he recites from it fifty verses every day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, both from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from al-Zuhri who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: 'The verses of the Quran are treasures; so every time a vault is opened, it is befitting for you to look at what is in it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Fudayl ibn Uthman, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who raised the chain, he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Illuminate your houses by the recitation of the Quran, and do not make them (like) graves as the Jews and the Christians did — they prayed in their churches and synagogues and left their houses idle. For indeed, the house in which the recitation of the Quran is frequented, its goodness increases, its inhabitants are provided for abundantly, and it shines for the inhabitants of the heavens just as the stars of the sky shine for the inhabitants of the earth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, both together from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from Abd al-A'la, client of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Indeed, the house in which there is a Muslim person reciting the Quran, the inhabitants of the sky behold it just as the inhabitants of the world behold the radiant star in the sky.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The house in which the Quran is recited and wherein God, Mighty and Majestic, is remembered, its blessing will be abundant, the angels will attend it, and the devils will forsake it, and it will shine for the inhabitants of the sky just as the stars shine for the inhabitants of the earth. And indeed the house in which the Quran is not recited and God, Mighty and Majestic, is not remembered, its blessing will be scarce, the angels will forsake it, and the devils will attend it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Muadh ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'Whoever recites the Quran standing during his salat, God will write for him, for every letter, one hundred good deeds; and whoever recites it during his salat seated, God will write for him for every letter fifty good deeds; and whoever recites it outside his salat, God will write for him for every letter ten good deeds.' Ibn Mahbub said: 'And I heard it from Muadh in an approximation of what Ibn Sinan had narrated.'

Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'What prevents the trader among you, the one busy in his market, when he returns to his house, from not sleeping until he recites a chapter from the Quran, so that for every verse he recites, ten good deeds would be written for him, and ten evil deeds would be erased from him?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam or someone else, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from a man, from Jabir, from Musafir, from Bishr ibn Ghalib al-Asady, from al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever recites a verse from the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, during his salat while standing, one hundred good deeds are written for him for every letter. When he recites it outside of salat, God writes ten good deeds for him for every letter. If he listens to the Quran, God writes one good deed for him for every letter. If he completes the Quran at night, the angels pray over him until morning. If he completes it during the day, the guardian angels pray over him until evening, and he has an answered supplication, and it is better for him than all that is between the sky and the earth. I said, 'This is for the one who recites the Quran. What about the one who does not recite?' He said: 'O brother of the clan of Asad! God is Generous, Glorious, and Benevolent. When he reads whatever he has (of the Quran), God gives him that (reward).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Khalid ibn Madd al-Qalanisi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever completes the Quran at Makkah from one Friday to another Friday, or less than that, or more, and completes it on a Friday, Allah will record for him the reward and the good deeds from the first Friday that ever was in the world to the last Friday that will ever be; and if he completes it on any other day, likewise.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Saeed — both — from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever recites ten verses during a night will not be recorded among the heedless; whoever recites fifty verses will be recorded among those who remember God; whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among the devoutly obedient; whoever recites two hundred verses will be recorded among the humble and fearful; whoever recites three hundred verses will be recorded among the successful; whoever recites five hundred verses will be recorded among the diligent strivers; and whoever recites a thousand verses — a qintar of raw gold will be recorded for him. The qintar is fifteen thousand mithqal of gold, and the mithqal is twenty-four qirat — the smallest of which is like the mountain of Uhud, and the largest of which is what is between the sky and the earth.'

And this hadith has been narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever listens intently to a letter from the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, without himself reciting, God will write for him a good deed, erase an evil deed from him, and raise him a level. Whoever recites it looking (from the text) without a voice, God will write for him, for every letter, a good deed, erase an evil deed from him, and raise him a level. Whoever learns a letter from it openly (by heart), God will write for him ten good deeds, erase ten evil deeds from him, and raise him ten levels. He said: I do not say for every verse, but for every letter — 'Ba', or 'Ta', or the likes of these two. He said: And whoever recites a letter clearly while seated in his salat, God will write for him, because of it, fifty good deeds, erase fifty evil deeds from him, and raise him fifty levels. And whoever recites a letter while standing in his salat, God will write for him, for every letter, one hundred good deeds, erase one hundred evil deeds from him, and raise him one hundred levels. And whoever completes it (the Quran), there will be for him an answered supplication — either deferred or hastened. He (the narrator) said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you — completing all of it?' He said: 'Completing all of it.'

Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Completion of the Quran is up to where you know.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, raising it (as a mursal report) to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Whoever recites the Quran in the mushaf (written copy) will be given benefit in his eyesight, and the punishment will be lightened from his parents, even if they were disbelievers.'
I would love it if there were a Mushaf (Quran) in the house by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repels the devils.

Three (things) complain to God, Mighty and Majestic: a ruined mosque whose people do not pray in it, a scholar among ignorant ones, and a mushaf (Quran) hanging (somewhere), dust having settled upon it, not being recited from.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Mas'ada, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from his grandfather, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Recitation of the Quran from the Mushaf lightens the punishment from the parents, even if they were both disbelievers.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I have memorized the Quran by heart — is reciting it from memory superior, or looking into the Mushaf?' He said, so he said to me: 'Rather, recite it while looking into the Mushaf, for it is superior. Do you not know that looking into the Mushaf is an act of worship?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And recite the Quran in a measured recitation' [73:4]. He said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of Allah upon him) said: Pronounce it with clarity, and do not rush through it like the rushing of poetry, nor scatter it like the scattering of sand; but rather rouse your hardened hearts, and let not the concern of any of you be reaching the end of the surah.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from whoever mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Quran was revealed with grief, so recite it with grief.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Recite the Quran with the tones of the Arabs and their voices; and beware of the tunes of the people of immorality and the people of major sins, for there will come after me groups of people who will repeat the Quran in the manner of songs, lamentation, and monasticism — it will not pass their throats. Their hearts are inverted, as are the hearts of those who are amazed by their conduct.'

I mentioned the voice in his presence, so he said: 'Indeed, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to recite, and sometimes a passer-by would pass by him and would be struck unconscious from the beauty of his voice. And verily, the Imam — if he were to manifest anything of that, the people would not be able to bear its beauty.' I said: 'And did not the Messenger of God (blessings of God upon him and his family) lead the people in prayer while raising his voice with the Quran?' So he said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of God (blessings of God upon him and his family) used to impose upon the people behind him only what they could endure.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sulaym al-Farra', from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Arabise the Quran, for indeed it is Arabic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — revealed to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'Whenever you stand before Me, stand in the manner of the disgraced and poor; and whenever you recite the Torah, make Me hear it in a grief-laden voice.'

From him, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'My community has not been given anything more scarcely than three things: beauty, a beautiful voice, and memorisation (of the Quran).'

From him, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Among the most beautiful of beauties is beautiful hair and the melodious tone of a beautiful voice.

From him, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: For everything there is an ornament, and the ornament of the Quran is the beautiful voice.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Umar al-Sayqal, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Sakuni, from Ali ibn Ismail al-Maysami, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send a Prophet except with a beautiful voice.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was the most beautiful of people in voice with the Quran, and the water carriers would pass by and stop at his door, listening to his recitation, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was the most beautiful of people in voice.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Asadi from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is disliked to recite Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad in one breath.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'When I recite the Quran and raise my voice with it, Satan comes to me and says, You are showing off with this to your family and the people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Recite a recitation that is between the two [extremes], making your family hear, and modulate your voice with the Quran, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the beautiful voice in which modulation is performed.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Murazim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is upon you to pray in the mosques, to be good neighbors to the people, to bear testimony (when required), and to attend the funerals. Indeed, you cannot do without the people. Not a single one of you is self-sufficient from the people throughout his lifetime, and the people inevitably need one another.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How is it befitting for us to behave regarding what is between us and our people, and regarding what is between us and those who intermingle with us from the people?' He said: So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You should return their trusts to them, and you should establish testimony in their favour and against them, and you should visit their sick, and you should attend their funerals.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid altogether from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Habib al-Khath'ami who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Incumbent upon you is piety and diligence, and attend the funerals, and visit the sick, and be present in your mosques with your people, and love for the people what you love for yourselves. Is the man among you not ashamed that his neighbor knows his right while he does not know the right of his neighbor?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): 'How is it befitting for us that we conduct ourselves regarding what is between us and our people, and between those who intermingle with us from the people, from those who are not upon our matter (al-Wilayah)?' He said: 'Look to your Imams, those whom you follow and emulate, and do as they do. By Allah! Indeed they visit their sick ones, attend their funerals, give testimony for them and against them, and return the trusts to them.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Convey my greetings upon those of them whom you see obeying me and following my words. And I advise you all with the fear of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and devoutness in your religion, and striving for God, and truthfulness of speech, and fulfilling trusts, and prolonging prostration, and good neighbourliness. For it is by this that Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) came. Fulfil the trust to whoever entrusted you with it, whether he be righteous or wicked, for the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to command the return of even the thread and the needle. Maintain ties with your kin, attend their funerals, console their sick, and fulfil their rights. For when a man from you is devout in his religion, truthful in speech, fulfils trusts, and is of good character with people, it is said: This is a Ja'fari — and that gladdens me, and joy enters upon me from it, and it is said: This is the teaching of Ja'far. But when he is otherwise, its suffering and its disgrace come upon me, and it is said: This is the teaching of Ja'far. By God, my father (peace be upon him) told me that there used to be a man in a tribe from the Shias of Ali (peace be upon him), and he was its ornament — the most faithful of them in trusts, the most fulfilling of them in rights, and the most truthful of them in speech. Their wills and deposits were left with him. The tribe was asked about him, and they would say: Who is like so-and-so? He is the most faithful of us in trusts and the most truthful of us in speech.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not initiate the People of the Book with the greeting (As-Salam), and when they greet you, say: 'Wa Alaykum' (And upon you).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Jew, the Christian, and the Polytheist, when they greet a man while he is seated, how it is befitting that he replies to them? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should say, 'Alaykum' (Upon you).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Bureyd ibn Mu'awiya, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Jew, the Christian, and the Polytheist greet you, say 'Alayk' (Upon you).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham came, and with him were a group from Quraysh, and they entered upon Abu Talib and said, 'Your brother's son has annoyed us and annoyed our gods, so call him and command him to refrain from our gods, and we will refrain from his God.' He said, so Abu Talib sent for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and called him. When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) entered, he did not see in the room except polytheists, so he said, 'Peace be upon the one who follows the guidance.' Then he sat down, and Abu Talib informed him of what they had come to him with. He said, 'Is there not for them, in a single word, something better than this, by which they would dominate the Arabs and tread on their necks?' Abu Jahl said, 'Yes, and what is this word?' He said, 'You should say, 'There is no god but Allah.'' So they placed their fingers in their ears and went out fleeing, and they were saying, 'We did not hear of this in the former religion; this is nothing but a fabrication.' So Allah the Exalted revealed regarding their words: 'Saad. By the Quran containing remembrance... up to His saying: 'this is nothing but a fabrication.''

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You should say in reply to the Jew and the Christian, 'Peace'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'What is your view, if I needed a physician and he was a Christian, should I greet him and supplicate for him?' He said, 'Yes, but your supplication will not benefit him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'What is your view if I needed a physician and he was a Christian, should I greet him with peace and supplicate for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, indeed your supplication will not benefit him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Arafa, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I supplicate for the Jew and the Christian?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say to him, May Allah bless you in the world.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding the handshake of the Muslim with the Jew and the Christian. He said: 'From behind a cloth. So if he shakes your hand with his hand, then wash your hand.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Abbas ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Ma'mar, from Khalid Al-Qalanisi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The Dhimmi (non-Muslim subject) meets me and shakes my hand.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wipe it with dust and with the wall.' I said, 'And what about the Nasibi (Hostile one)?' He said: 'Wash it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who shook the hand of a Magian man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash his hand and he does not have to perform ablution.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who has a need for a Magian, or a Jew, or a Christian, or if he is an official or a landowner among the great people of his land, and the man writes to him regarding a great need: Should he begin with the greeting and send peace upon him in his letter, and he does that so that perhaps his need will be fulfilled? He (peace be upon him) said: As for beginning with it, no, but you send peace upon him in your letter, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to write to Kisra and Caesar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) About the man who writes to a man from the greats of the workers of the Magians, so he begins with his name before his own name, so he (peace be upon him) said:

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was a group in his presence whom he was narrating to, when a man from them mentioned a man, and he criticized him and complained of him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'And how can you find fault with your brother entirely? And which of the men is completely refined (free from faults)?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not scrutinize the people, lest you remain without a friend.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn al-Fudayl and Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Look at your heart, so when it rejects your companion, then one of you has done something wrong (innovated/changed).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Al-Hasan ibn Yusuf, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Al-Hakam, who said: I heard a man asking Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and the man said: 'Someone says that he likes me, so how do I know that he likes me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Test your heart; if you like him, then he likes you.'

Abu Bakr al-Habbal from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Qattan al-Madaini said, 'I heard my father saying, 'Mas'ada ibn al-Yasa' narrated to us,' 'I said to Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), 'By Allah, I love you!' So he bowed his head, then raised it and said, 'You have spoken the truth, O Abu Bishr! Ask your heart about what is for you in my heart regarding your love, for my heart has informed me about what is for me in your heart.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Do not forget me in your supplication.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And do you know that I might forget you?' He said, 'So I reflected within myself and said, 'He supplicates for his Shias, and I am from his Shias.' I said, 'No, you will not forget me.' He said, 'And how did you know that?' I said, 'I am from your Shias, and you supplicate for them.' So he said, 'Did you know with something other than this?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'If you wish to know what is for you with me, then look at what is for me in you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Look at your heart, for if it rejects your companion, then know that one of you has done something wrong.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'For the Muslim upon his brother, from the rights, is that he greets him when he meets him, and visits him when he is sick, and advises him when he is absent, and says the Name of Allah when he sneezes, saying: "The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, there is no associate for Him," and he says to him: "May Allah have mercy on you." So he answers him, saying to him: "May Allah guide you and rectify your affairs." And he answers him when he invites him, and follows him (his funeral) when he dies.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man sneezes, respond to his sneeze by saying

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I was in the presence of Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so he sneezed. So I said to him, 'May Allah send Salawat upon you.' Then he sneezed, so I said, 'May Allah send Salawat upon you.' Then he sneezed, so I said, 'May Allah send Salawat upon you,' and I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! When the likes of you sneezes, should we be saying just as we are saying for each other, 'May Allah have Mercy on you', or just as we are saying?' He said: 'Yes. Are you not saying, 'May Allah send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad'?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Mercy be upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad.' I said, 'Yes, and indeed Allah has sent Salawat upon him and been Merciful to him, and rather, our Salawat upon him is a Mercy for us, and a (means) of nearness.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'Yawning is from the Satan and the sneeze is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad said: I asked the Knowledgeable One (peace be upon him) about sneezing and what is the reason for saying 'Praise be to Allah' upon it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'For Allah has a favor upon His servant regarding the health of his body and the safety of his limbs, and the servant tends to forget the Mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon that; and when he forgets, Allah commands the wind, so it passes through his body, then He expels it from his nose, so he praises Allah upon that, and that praise of his at that time becomes a thankfulness for what he had forgotten.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ja'far ibn Yunus, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I counted in the room fourteen men. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) sneezed, and no one from the group spoke. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Are you not saying the Tasmit? Are you not saying the Tasmit? From the rights of the believer upon the believer is that when he is sick, you visit him, and when he dies, you attend his funeral, and when he sneezes, you say the Tasmit (or he said: You say the Tashmit), and when he invites you, you answer him.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The sneezing is a good thing; it benefits the body and reminds [one] of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' I said, 'Among us there is a group of people who say, He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are lying, may they not attain the intercession of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, who said: A man sneezed in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he said, 'The Praise is for Allah,' but Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) did not respond with 'Yarhamuk Allah' and said: 'You have been deficient of our rights.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever one of you sneezes, let him say, "The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send Salawat upon Muhammad and the People of his Household."' He said: So the man said it, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) responded by naming Allah (Yarhamuk Allah).

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ismail Al Basry, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said: I said to Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him), 'The people are disliking the sending of blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny in three places – during the sneezing, and during the slaughtering, and during the copulation'. So Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) said: 'What is the matter with them? Woe be unto them! They have become hypocrites, may Allah curse them!'.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) would say: 'May Allah forgive you and have mercy on you' when someone said to him 'May Allah have mercy on you' upon his sneezing. And when a person sneezed in his presence, he would say: 'May Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, have mercy on you'.

From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali or someone else, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: A boy who had not yet reached puberty sneezed in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he said, 'The Praise is for Allah.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'May Allah place blessings in you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man sneezes, let one say, 'All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, there is no associate for Him.' And when the man says the response, let him say, 'May Allah have mercy on you.' And when he responds, let him say, 'May Allah forgive you and us.' For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about a verse or something wherein was a mention of Allah, so he said: 'Whenever Allah is mentioned therein, it is excellent.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from Muhammad ibn Marwan, raising it (to the Imam), said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who says, when he sneezes, “The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds,” upon every state, will not find pain of the two ears and the teeth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the pain of the teeth and the pain of the ears: When you hear someone sneeze, begin with the Praise (Al-Hamd).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Uthman, from Abu Usama, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever hears a sneeze and praises Allah (Mighty and Majestic) and sends blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and his Household, he will not complain of his eyes nor his teeth.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you hear it, say it, even if there is an ocean between you and him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abi Najran, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A Christian man sneezed in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). So the people said to him, 'May Allah guide you.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'You should say, May Allah have mercy on you.' They said to him, 'He is a Christian.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah will not guide him until He has mercy on him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Huzayfa ibn Mansour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: A sneeze is beneficial for the entire body as long as it does not exceed three; so when it exceeds three, it is an illness and a disease.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely the most hateful of voices is the voice of the donkeys.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The ugly sneezing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever sneezes, then places his hand upon the bridge of his nose, then says: 'All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, abundant praise as He is worthy of it, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad the Prophet and his Progeny and grant him peace,' a bird smaller than a locust and larger than a fly will emerge from his left nostril, until it travels beneath the Throne, seeking forgiveness for him from Allah until the Day of Judgment.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, reporting it from a man from the general Muslims, who said: I used to sit in a gathering of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so by Allah, I had not seen a gathering nobler than his gathering. He said to me one day, 'From where does the sneeze come out?' So I said, 'From the nose'. So he said to me: 'You are wrong'. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! From where does it come out?' So he said: 'From the entire body, just as the sperm comes out from the entire body, and its exit is from the urethra'. Then he said: 'Have you not seen the person when he sneezes, his body parts shake? And the sneezer is safe from death for seven days'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The truthfulness of the statement is confirmed upon sneezing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man is narrating a hadith and a sneezer sneezes, he is a witness to the truth.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The sneezing is the ratification of truthfulness of a person’s words'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man sneezes three times, say 'Bismillah' for him, then leave him (if he sneezes again).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'From the respect of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is respecting the aged old man.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever recognizes the merit of an elder due to his age and dignifies him, Allah will secure him from the horror of the Day of Judgment.'

And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who dignifies the one with old age in Al-Islam, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) would Secure him from the horrors of the Day of Judgment.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu al-Khattab narrating from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Three [people]; none would ignore their rights except for a hypocrite well-known for his hypocrisy: the one with grey hair in Islam, the bearer of the Quran, and the just Imam.'

From him, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'From the respect of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the respect for the believer with gray hair (old age); and whoever honors a believer, he has begun by honoring Allah, and whoever treats lightly a believer with gray hair, Allah will send to him one who will treat him lightly before his death.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abu Baseer and others from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'From the respect of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the respect for the Muslim with grey hair (elderly).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Two men entered upon Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), so he placed a pillow for each one of them. One of them sat upon it, but the other refused. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Sit upon it, for no one refuses an honouring except for a donkey.' Then he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When an honourable one of a people comes to you, so honour him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When an honourable guest of a people comes to you, so honour him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When Udayy ibn Hatim arrived at the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) brought him into his house. There was in the house nothing except a sack and a pillow of leather. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spread it for Udayy ibn Hatim.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Awf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The gatherings are with the confidentiality.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The gatherings are with the confidentiality.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The gatherings are with confidentiality, and no one should narrate a saying that its owner wishes to keep secret, except with his permission, unless he is trustworthy or does so to mention him in a good light.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: With whomever you intermingle, if you are able to ensure that your hand is the upper one over them, then do so.

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and the house was packed with his people — among them were people from Khurasan, from Syria, and from the far regions. I could not find a place to sit. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had been reclining. Then he sat up and said: 'O Shias of the family of Muhammad! Know that he is not from us — the one who does not control himself during his anger, and who is not a good companion to those who accompany him, and of good character with those he deals with, and a good friend to those who befriend him, and a good neighbour to those who neighbour him, and courteous at the table with those who share his food. O Shias of the family of Muhammad! Fear Allah as much as you are able, and there is neither might nor strength except through Allah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Indeed we see you to be of the doers of good' [12:36] He said: He (Prophet Yusuf) used to make space for others in gatherings, lend to the needy, and assist the weak.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ala'a ibn al-Fuzayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Venerate your companions and dignify them, and let not some of you attack others, nor harm one another, nor envy one another; and beware of stinginess. Be the servants of God, the sincere, the righteous.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid and Tha'laba and Ali ibn Uqba, from some of those who narrated it, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), who said: Aloofness from people earns enmity.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When there are three people, two of them should not whisper privately to each other to the exclusion of their companion, for in that is something that saddens and hurts him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: When there are three people in a room, two of them should not whisper (to each other) to the exclusion of the third, for that is what saddens him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever interrupts his Muslim brother while he is speaking in his discourse, it is as if he has scratched his face.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nawfali, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, raising it (to the Prophet), said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to sit in three postures: Al-Qurfusa (squatting), which is that he raises his shins and faces them with his hands, and tightens his hand in his arm; and he used to kneel on his two knees, bending one leg and extending the other upon it; and he was not seen sitting cross-legged at all.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said: I saw Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) sitting with one of his legs placed on his thigh. I said: 'The people dislike this sitting posture and say: It is the sitting of the Lord.' He said: 'I only sat in this posture for tiredness, and the Lord does not get tired, nor does slumber seize Him, nor sleep.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Murazim, from Abu Suleyman Al Zahid, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is content with a seat without (seeking) prestige from the gathering, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) and His Angels would not cease to send Salawāt upon him until he arises.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was so that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to mostly sit facing the Qiblah.

Abu Abdillah al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sat in the posture of 'mutawarrika', his right leg upon his left thigh. So a man said to him, 'May I be your ransom, this is an abhorrent sitting posture.' He said, 'No, but rather it is something which the Jews say: when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was finished from creating the heavens and the earth and Established Himself upon the Throne, He sat in this posture to rest.' Allah is He besides Whom there is no god, the Everliving, the Eternal; slumber does not seize Him nor sleep And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) remained sitting in the 'mutawarrika' posture just as he was.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered a house, he would sit in the place nearest to the entrance at the time he entered.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The market of the Muslims is like their mosque. So whoever precedes to a place, he is more rightful to it until the night.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so that he did not used to take rent for the market rooms (stalls)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is befitting for those sitting in the summer that there be between every two people a distance equal to the length of an arm bone, so that one does not find it burdensome upon the other due to the heat.'
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) sitting in his house, at the door of his house, facing the Ka'bah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Reclining in the Masjid is the monasticism of the Arabs. Indeed, the believer's sitting place is his Masjid, and his monastery is his house.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Sitting cross-legged in the Masjid is the encirclement of the Arabs.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The cross-legged posture is the encirclement of the Arabs.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who wraps himself in a single garment. He said: 'If he covers his private part, there is no problem.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not allowed for the man that he sits cross-legged facing the Kabah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) and said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, a man is with a group, and speech flows between them, they joke and laugh.' He said: 'There is no harm as long as it is not [something specific].' So I thought he meant immorality/vulgarity. Then he said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would be visited by a Bedouin who would bring him a gift, then say: 'In place of it, give us the price of our gift.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would laugh; and when he was saddened, he would say: 'What happened to the Bedouin? I wish he had come to us.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'There is no believer except that he has humor (playfulness); I said, 'And what is the humor?' He said, 'Al-mizah (joyful banter/teasing).'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yahya ibn Sallam, from Yusuf ibn Yaqub, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yunus al-Shaybani, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'How is the humouring of some of you unto the others?' I said, 'Little'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not be doing so (being of little humour), for the humour is from the good morals, and you would be entering the cheerfulness by it upon your brother, and it was so that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would humour the man intending to cheer him up'.

Salih ibn Uqba from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the one who engages in playful banter within the group without obscenity.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Hasan ibn Kuleyb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The laughter of the believer is a smile.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansour, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abundant laughter deadens the heart. And he said: Abundant laughter dissolves the Religion, just as water dissolves salt.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, from ignorance is laughter without wonderment (or cause). And he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Do not show off your teeth in laughter when you have committed disgraceful deeds, and one who commits evil deeds is not secure from being caught overnight.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of joking, for it removes the water (dignity) of the face.'
From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When you love a man, do not joke with him and do not argue with him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithammi, from Anbasa Al-Abid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Frequent laughter removes the water (dignity/luster) of the face.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of joking, for it draws out foolishness, begets enmity, and it is the minor insult.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Khalid ibn Tahman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When you laugh loudly (guffaw), say when you finish: 'O Allah, do not detest me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn Farqad and Ali ibn Uqba and Tha'laba, raised it to Abu Abdillah and Abu Ja'far, or one of them (peace be upon him), who said: Frequent joking removes the water (dignity) of the face, and frequent laughter hurls out faith with a hurling.
Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithamī, from Anbasa Al-ʿĀbid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Joking is the smallest insult.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Beware of joking, for it removes the water (dignity) of the face and the sublimity of the men.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abu al-Abbas, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not dispute bitterly, for it will remove your glory, and do not joke excessively, for they will take liberties with you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), that he said: In a bequest of his to one of his sons, or he said: My father said to one of his sons: Beware of joking, for it removes the light of your faith and lightens your manliness.

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him) would cry and not laugh, and Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) would laugh and cry, and that which Isa (peace be upon him) did was superior to that which Yahya (peace be upon him) did.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ali ibn Fazzal, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Amr ibn Ikrama, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'There is a neighbor of mine who bothers me.' He said, 'Be merciful to him.' I said, 'May Allah not have mercy on him.' So he turned his face away from me. I disliked leaving him, so I said, 'He does such and such to me, and keeps doing it and bothers me.' He said, 'What do you think, if I were to bring him into the open, would you be more just than him?' I said, 'Yes, I would exceed (in fairness) upon him.' He said, 'That one is from those who envy people for what Allah has given them of His grace. When he sees a blessing upon someone, if that person has a family, he makes his affliction upon them; and if he has no family, he makes it upon his servant. If he has no servant, he stays awake at night and is wrathful by day.' A man from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I bought a house among the clan of so-and-so, and the closest neighbor to me is one from whom I do not hope for goodness nor do I feel safe from his evil.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded Ali (peace be upon him), Salman, Abu Dharr, and I forgot the other one, and I think it was Al-Miqdad, to call out in the Masjid with their highest voices that, 'There is no faith for the one whose neighbor is not safe from his deeds.' So they called it out three times. Then he gestured with his hand to every forty houses from in front of him, from behind him, from his right, and from his left.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: I read in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wrote between the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who joined them from the people of Yathrib: 'The neighbor is like the soul, neither to be harmed nor sinned against, and the sanctity of the neighbor upon the neighbor is like the sanctity of his mother.' The hadith is abbreviated.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Raja', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Good neighbourliness increases in the sustenance.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-Kahili, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Benjamin was taken from Yaqub (peace be upon him), he called out: O Lord! Will You not have mercy on me? You have taken my eyes and You have taken my son. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him: If they had both died, I would have revived them for you until I gathered you and them together. But remember the sheep that you slaughtered and roasted and ate, while so-and-so and so-and-so were fasting beside you, and you did not give them anything from it.'

And in another report he (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so after that, Yaqoub (peace be upon him) used to get his caller to call out during every morning, from his house, upon a Farsakh (about four miles), “Indeed! The one who wants the lunch, so let him come to Yaqoub (peace be upon him)!” And when it was evening, he called out, “Indeed! The one who wants the dinner, so let him come to Yaqoub (peace be upon him)!”'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Sa'dan, from Abu Mas'ud, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Good neighbourliness increases the lifespan, and building the households.'

From him, from Al-Nahiki, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Hakam al-Khayyat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Good neighbourliness builds the households and increases the life-spans.

From him, from one of his companions, from Salih ibn Hamza, from Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, from Abd Salih (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Good neighbourliness is not merely refraining from causing harm, but good neighbourliness is your patience upon the harm (done to you by the neighbour).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi from Ubeys ibn Hisham from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Good neighbourliness builds the households and prolongs the life-spans.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He said, and the room was full with his family members: 'Know that he is not from us, the one who does not have good neighbourliness with those who are in his neighbourhood.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believer is the one from whom his neighbour is safe of his deeds.' I said, 'And what are his deeds?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His injustice and his harshness.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him about the harm from his neighbour. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Be patient.' Then he came to him a second time, so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Be patient.' Then he returned to him and complained to him for the third time. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to the man who complained: 'When the people are commuting to the Friday prayer, take out your belongings to the road until those who are going to the Friday prayer see you. So when they ask you, inform them.' He said: 'He did so, and his harming neighbour came to him and said to him, 'Return your belongings, and by Allah, I will not repeat (harming you).'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Hasan al-Bajali, from Ubaydullah al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He has not believed in me, the one who spends the night satiated while his neighbour is hungry.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And there is none from the people of a town who spend the night (satiated) and among them is a hungry one, to whom Allah would Look (with Kindness) to them on the Day of Judgement.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: From the hardest of the misfortunes which break the back, is an evil neighbour; if he sees goodness (from you), he conceals it, and if he sees evil (in you), he spreads it.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I seek Refuge with Allah from the evil neighbour in a house of residence, whose eyes see you and whose heart watches over you; if he sees you in goodness, it pains him, and if he sees you in evil, it pleases him.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I seek protection with Allah from a bad neighbor in a residence of stay, whose eyes watch you and whose heart guards you; if he sees you in good, it displeases him, and if he sees you in evil, it pleases him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Aban, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, from Amr ibn Aqim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For every forty houses, they are neighbors, from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left.'

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The limit of the neighbourhood (jivār) is forty houses from every side: from in front of him, and from behind him, and from his right, and from his left.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) advised me, saying: 'I advise you with the fear of Allah, and the fulfillment of trusts, and truthful narration, and good companionship to whoever you accompany, and there is no strength except with Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you mix with people, if you are able to have your hand be the higher (more giving) over them, then do so.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No two people travel together except that the one with the greater reward and the one most beloved to Allah, Exalted and Majestic, is the one who is most kind/gentle to his companion.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The right of the traveller is that his companions stay with him (stand over him) when he is sick, for three (days).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Maintaining connection between the brethren while settled is visiting one another, and during travel is exchanging letters.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Returning an answer to a letter is obligatory, like the obligation of returning the greeting, and the one who initiates the greeting is closer to Allah and His Messenger.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to apportion his moments between his companions, so he would look at one and look at another with fairness. He said: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never extended his legs among his companions at all, and if a man were to shake his hand, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not remove his hand from his hand until it was he who was the one to leave. So when they discerned that, the man, whenever he shook his hand, would say with his hand, so he removed it from his hand.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: When the man is present, use his kunya (teknonym), and when he is absent, use his name.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you loves his Muslim brother, let him ask him about his name, the name of his father, the name of his tribe, and his clan. For it is from his obligatory right and the truthfulness of brotherhood that he asks him about that; otherwise, it is a recognition of foolishness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Abdul Malik ibn Qudama, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said one day to his companions: 'Do you know what is weakness (al-'ajz)?' They said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' So he said: 'Weakness is of three types: One of you hastens to prepare food for his companion, but he breaks his promise and does not come to him; and the second is that a man from you accompanies another man or sits with him, loving to know who he is and from where he is, but he separates from him before he gets to know that; and the third is a matter of women. One of you approaches his wife and fulfills his need, while she has not fulfilled her need.' Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As said, 'So how is that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'He should hold back and wait until that comes from both of them together.'
