He said, 'And in another hadith, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the most extreme of weaknesses is the weakness of a man who meets a man, is impressed by his manner, but does not ask him about his name, his lineage, and his place (residence).'

And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not let the decency go away between you and your brother, preserve it, for if it goes away, the bashfulness would go away.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Wasil, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not trust your brother with complete trust, for a sudden abandonment (or collapse) will never be repairable.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays and Uthman ibn Sulayman al-Nakhhas, from Mufaddal ibn Umar and Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Test your brothers by two characteristics. If they are in them, then if not, turn away, then turn away, then turn away – [for] preservation upon the prayers at their times, and righteousness with the brothers in hardship and ease.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not leave (saying) 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful', even if a poem follows it.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Do not write 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful' at the beginning of the letter to so-and-so, and there is no harm in writing it on the back of the letter to so-and-so.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not write 'To the father of so-and-so' inside the letter, but write 'To the father of so-and-so' upon the address.

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who begins with the man in the letter. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it. That is from the preference (generosity/honor) that the man begins with his brother to honour him.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn al-Ahmar, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with a man beginning with the name of his companion in the document before his own name.
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he would sprinkle dust upon the letter (to dry the ink), and said: 'There is no problem with it'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, that he saw letters of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sprinkled with dust

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon you to keep company with the person of intellect, even if you do not praise his generosity — but benefit from his intellect and guard yourself from his evil manners. And do not abandon the company of the generous person, even if you do not benefit from his intellect — but benefit from his generosity using your own intellect. And flee, with all manner of fleeing, from the lowly fool.'

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, from Aban, from Abu al-Udais who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Salih! Follow the one who makes you weep and he is a sincere adviser to you, and do not follow the one who makes you laugh and he is a deceiver to you. And you will all return before God and then you will know.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Consider whom you converse with, for there is no one upon whom death descends except that his companions are presented to him before God — if they were good, then good; and if they were evil, then evil. And there is no one who dies except that I present myself to him at his death.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of the people of Halab, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from an unnamed man from the people of the mountain, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Maintain your old associations, and beware of every newcomer who has no commitment, no trust, no obligation, and no covenant. And be wary even of the most reliable person in your presence.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The most beloved of my brethren to me is the one who presents my faults to me.'

Friendship cannot come to be except by its limits. So whoever has in him these limits, or something of them, then ascribe to him friendship; and whoever does not have in him anything of them, do not ascribe to him anything of friendship. The first of these is that his private and public behaviour toward you should be one and the same; the second is that he sees your honour as his honour and your fault as his fault; the third is that neither authority nor wealth should change him toward you; the fourth is that he does not deprive you of anything that his capacity can attain; and the fifth — which encompasses all of these qualities — is that he does not abandon you during calamities.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the papers that accumulate; can they be burned with fire while there is something from the Mention of Allah in them? He said: No, they must be washed with water first, before (burning).
From him, from Al-Washsha, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not burn the papers, but erase them and then burn them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a Name from the Names of Allah, when a man deletes it with his saliva. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Delete it with the cleanest of what you find.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Erase the Book of Allah, the Exalted, and His remembrance with the cleanest substance you can find,' and he forbade burning the Book of Allah, and forbade erasing it with pens.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Al Hassan Musa (peace be upon him) Regarding the surfaces in which there is Mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he said: ‘Wash it’.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Salim al-Kindi, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say whenever he ascended the pulpit: 'It is befitting for the Muslim to avoid establishing brotherhood with three types: the shameless immoral, the fool, and the liar.' As for the shameless immoral one, he beautifies his deed for you and desires that you be like him, and he does not assist you in the matters of your religion and your Hereafter; his closeness is aversion and harshness, and his coming and going is a disgrace upon you. And as for the fool, he gives you no good counsel, nor can he be relied upon to repel harm from you, even if he exerted himself; and sometimes when he intends your benefit, he ends up harming you. Thus his death is better than his life, his silence is better than his speech, and his distance is better than his nearness. And as for the liar, life with him brings you no ease: he spreads your words to others and brings others' words to you; every time he exhausts a tale, he pours out another like it, until even when he speaks truthfully, he is not believed, and he sows division among people through enmity, cultivating hatred in their hearts. So fear God, Mighty and Majestic, and look out for yourselves.

In a report of Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: It is not befitting for the Muslim man to establish brotherhood with the immoral person, for indeed he adorns his own deed to him, and he desires that he be like him, and he will not help him in the affairs of his worldly life, nor the affairs of his Hereafter; and his entry to him and his departure from his presence are a disgrace upon him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting for the Muslim man to establish brotherhood with the immoral, nor the fool, nor the liar.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his companions, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily the companion of evil infects, and an evil associate destroys — so look carefully at whom you associate with.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Ammar! If you love that the bounty be established for you, and magnanimity be completed for you, and life be set right for you, then do not associate with slaves and lowly people in your affairs, for if you entrust them they will betray you, and if they speak to you they will lie to you, and if you are afflicted they will abandon you, and if they promise you they will break their promise.

He said, and I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The love of the righteous for the righteous is a reward for the righteous; the love of the immoral for the righteous is a virtue for the righteous; the hatred of the immoral for the righteous is an adornment for the righteous; and the hatred of the righteous for the immoral is a disgrace upon the immoral.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Udhafir, from some of their companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (AS), from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: My father Ali ibn al-Husayn (blessings of God upon them both) said to me: 'O my dear son! Take note of five (types of people) and do not befriend them, nor converse with them, nor travel with them on any road.' I said: 'O my father, who are they? Introduce them to me.' He said: 'Beware of befriending the liar, for he is like a mirage — he draws the distant close to you, and distances what is close. Beware of befriending the immoral, for he will sell you out for a meal or less than that. Beware of befriending the miser, for he will abandon you in regard to his wealth at the time when you need him most. Beware of befriending the fool, for he intends to benefit you but harms you instead.' And beware of befriending the one who severs family ties, for I have found him cursed in the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, in three places: God, Mighty and Majestic, says [47:22-23]: 'But if you held command, you would surely spread corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship. Those are the ones God has cursed, so He made them deaf and blinded their eyes.' And the Mighty and Majestic says [13:25]: 'And those who break the covenant of God after its confirmation and sever what God has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the land — those will have the curse, and theirs will be an evil abode.' And He says in Al-Baqara [2:27]: 'Who break the covenant of God after its confirmation and sever what God has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the earth — those are the losers.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, who said: I heard al-Muharibi reporting from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: There are three (types of people) — sitting with them deadens the heart: sitting with the scoundrels, conversing with women, and sitting with the wealthy.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from the one who mentioned it, he said: Luqman (peace be upon him) said to his son: 'O my dear son! Do not draw too near, lest you become more distant; and do not be too remote, lest you be humiliated. Every creature loves its own kind, and indeed the son of Adam loves his fellow human. Do not display your goods except to one who seeks them. Just as there is no friendship between the wolf and the ram, similarly there is no friendship between the righteous and the immoral. Whoever draws near to tar, some of it will stick to him; similarly, whoever associates with an immoral person will learn from his ways. Whoever loves disputation will be insulted; whoever enters the haunts of evil will be accused; whoever keeps company with an evil companion will not remain safe; and whoever does not control his tongue will regret it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Do not befriend the people of innovation, nor sit with them, so that you become in the eyes of the people like one of them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A man is upon the religion of his close friend and his companion.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Yaqoub al-Hashimi, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of befriending the fool, for the closer you get to him (for his pleasure), the closer you are to your misfortune.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A Bedouin from the clan of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'Advise me.' Among what he advised him was: 'Endear yourself to the people, and they will love you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Being courteous to people is a third of the intellect.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Three things purify a man's love for his Muslim brother: he meets him with cheerfulness when he encounters him, and he makes space for him in the gathering when he comes to sit with him, and he calls him by the name most beloved to him.'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Being affectionate toward the people is half the intellect.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Being affectionate toward the people is half of the intellect.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever restrains his hand from the people, he restrains only one hand from them, and they will restrain from him many hands.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of his companions, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Sulayman ibn Ziyad al-Tamimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The close one is he whom affection has brought near, even if his lineage is distant; and the distant one is he whom affection has driven away, even if his lineage is near. There is nothing closer to something than a hand is to the body; and yet the hand, if it becomes treacherous, is cut off — and when cut off, the bleeding is stopped.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Whenever you love someone from your brothers, inform him of that; for indeed Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'My Lord, show me how You revive the dead.' He said: 'Do you not believe?' He said: 'Yes, but so that my heart may find reassurance.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all together from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Whenever you love a man, inform him of that, for it will be an affirmation of the cordiality between the two of you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Initiating the greeting (al-salam) is voluntary, and responding to it is an obligation.'
Whoever begins speech before the greeting (al-salam), do not answer him. And he said: Begin with the greeting before speech. So whoever begins with speech before the greeting, do not answer him.
And by this chain, he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most worthy of people with God and with His Messenger is the one who initiates the greeting of peace.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Salman (may God have mercy on him) used to say: Spread the greeting (salam) of God, for the greeting of God does not reach the unjust.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the spreading of the greeting (salaam).

From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The stingy one is the one who is stingy with the greeting (salam).'

Whenever one of you greets, let him be loud with his greeting. He should not say, 'I greeted but they did not respond to me', for perhaps he greeted but they did not hear it. So whenever one of you responds, let him be loud with his response, and the one greeting should not say, 'I greeted but they did not respond to me'. Then he said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Neither get angry nor anger others. Spread the greeting (salam) openly, make your speech pleasant, and pray at night while the people are sleeping — you will enter Paradise in safety'. Then he (peace be upon him) recited to them the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'the Giver of Peace (Al-Salam), the Granter of Security (Al-Mu'min), the Guardian (Al-Muhaymin)' [59:23].

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who initiates the greeting (salam) is more deserving of God and His Messenger.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever says "Peace be upon you" (al-Salamu alaykum), it is ten good deeds. And whoever says "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God" (al-Salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah), it is twenty good deeds. And whoever says "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings" (al-Salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh), it is thirty good deeds.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three [actions] are responded to with the plural response, even if the person is alone: when one sneezes, it is said, 'May Allah have mercy on you all,' even if there is no one else with him; and when a man greets another man, saying, 'Peace be upon you all,' and when a man supplicates for another man, saying, 'May Allah grant you well-being,' even if he is alone, for there are others [angels] with him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, raising it (to the Imam), said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three (people) do not receive the greeting (of peace): the one walking with the funeral, the one walking to the Friday prayer, and the one in the bathhouse.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Among the qualities of humility is that you greet the one you meet.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali (peace be upon him), passed by a group of people and greeted them. They said, 'Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings, and His forgiveness, and His pleasure.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to them, 'Do not exceed us with more than what the angels said to our father Ibrahim (peace be upon him). They only said, "The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O People of the Household."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, from the completion of the greeting for the one who is resident is the handshake, and the completion of the greeting for the traveler is the embrace.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'It is disliked for a man to say,

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The younger one should offer the greeting (al-Salam) upon the older, and the passer-by upon the seated one, and the few upon the more numerous.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindy, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The few initiate the many with the greeting (salam), and the rider initiates the walker, and the riders of mules initiate the riders of donkeys, and the riders of horses initiate the riders of mules.

I heard him saying: The rider should give salam upon the walker, and the walker upon the seated one; and when a group meets a group, the fewer should give salam upon the more; and when one person meets a group, the single individual should give salam upon the group.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The rider should give salam to the walker, and the standing one to the seated one.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When there is a group of people in a gathering, then (another) group proceeds and enters, it is upon the one entering last, when he enters, that he should greet them (with salam).

Whenever a group passes by a group of people, it would suffice for them if one of them gives the greeting. And when a greeting is given to a group of people and they are a group, it would suffice them if one of them responds.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: When a man from a group gives the greeting of peace, it suffices on their behalf.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When one from a group gives salam, it suffices for all of them; and when one responds, it suffices for all of them.
The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Water purifies and is not (itself) purified.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, by his chain, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'All water is pure until it is known to be impure.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Dawud al-Munshid, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'All water is pure until one knows that it is impure.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about sea water — is it purifying (tahur)? He said: Yes.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about sea water — is it purifying? He said: Yes.

One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Do not wash from the well in which the used water of the bathhouse gathers, for therein is the washing of the son of adultery, and he is not clean up to seven fathers; and therein is the washing of the Nasibi, and he is the worse of the two. Indeed, Allah did not create a creature more evil than the dog, and the Nasibi is lighter (more acceptable) to Allah than the dog. I said: Inform me about the water of the bathhouse; the one with major impurity, the child, the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian wash from it. He said: Indeed, the water of the bathhouse is like the water of the river; some of it purifies the other.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habeeb, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The water of the bathhouse is permissible (there is no problem with it) if it has a source (like a flowing spring or continuous supply).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I enter the bathhouse in the morning, and therein is the man with sexual impurity and others like that. So I stand and perform ghusl, and after I finish, their water splashes upon me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not flowing water?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about the gathering of water in the bathhouse from the bathing of people, which touches the garment. He said: There is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The water which the sun warms up, do not perform Wudu with it, nor perform Ghusl with it, nor knead with it, for it causes leprosy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is from the understanding (fiqh) of the man that he seeks out a place for his urination.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), 'Where should the strangers perform ablution?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should avoid the banks of the rivers, the thoroughfares, under the fruit-bearing trees, and the places of curse.' So it was said to him, 'And where are the places of the curse?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The doors of the houses.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, by his chain, raising it, said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked, 'What is the limit of defecation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not face the Qiblah, nor have your back to it, nor face the wind, nor have your back to it.' And it is reported in another Hadith: 'Do not face the sun nor the moon.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade a man to aim his urine from the roof or from something elevated in the air.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, said: Abu Hanifa exited from the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) was standing, and he (peace be upon him) was a young boy. So Abu Hanifa said to him (peace be upon him), 'O boy! Where can the strangers in your city place (their faeces and urine)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They should keep away from the courtyards of the Masjids, and banks of the rivers, and the places where the fruits fall from the trees, and the houses (places) of combat, and he should neither face the Qiblah by defecation nor urination, and should raise his clothes, and place it where he so desires to'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three characteristics are accursed for the one who does these – the defecation in the shade of the encampments, and the disrupter of (flow of) water, and obstruction of the travelled road'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When you enter the toilet, say: 'In the Name of Allah, O Allah, I seek refuge with You from the wicked, the expeller of filth, the impure, the unclean, the Satan, the pelted one.' So when you exit, say: 'In the Name of Allah, all praise is for Allah, Who saved me from the wicked, the expeller of filth, and removed the harm from me.' And when you perform ablution, say: 'I testify that there is no god except Allah, O Allah, make me among the repentant and make me among the purified, and all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you Name (Bismillah) during the Ablution (Wudu), your entire body becomes pure, and when you do not Name, nothing from your body becomes pure except what the water passes over.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'One should perform istinja (cleansing) and wash what is apparent from it upon the anus, and the finger should not be inserted into it.'

Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man when he intends to cleanse himself (istinja), with which of the two should he begin, the back part or the front part? So he said: With the back part, then with the front part.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the man to cleanse himself with his right hand.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Rabbih, who said: I said to him, 'What do you say regarding the ring (fass) that is made from emerald stone?' He said, 'There is no problem with it, but when one intends to perform istinja (cleansing after relieving oneself), he should remove it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Cleansing (of the private parts) with the right hand is from the repugnance (or roughness). And it is reported that if there is an illness in the left hand, it is a valid excuse.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the flow of urine stops, pour water (upon the discharging part).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Is there a limit for istinja' (cleansing the private parts)?' He said, 'It is not purified as long as there is (something) there.' I said, 'Supposing he cleans what is there, and the wind (of passing gas) remains?' He said, 'The wind is not looked at.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who urinates and it hits his thigh and his knee to the extent of a spot of urine, so he prays, then he remembers afterwards that he had not washed it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash it and repeat his prayer.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'How should a man sit when he intends to cleanse his private parts?' He said, 'Just as he sits for defecation.' And he said, 'He is only required to wash what is apparent from it, and he is not required to wash its inside.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I performed ablution one day and did not wash my manhood, then I prayed. So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Wash your manhood and repeat your prayer.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who urinates but forgets to wash his penis, then he performs the ablution for the prayer: He said: He should wash his penis; he repeats the prayer and does not repeat the ablution.

From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the man who urinates and forgets to wash his manhood until he performs ablution and prays, he said: He should wash his manhood and repeat the prayer, and he does not repeat the ablution.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you enter the toilet and fulfill your need, and you do not splash water (upon the excrement), then you perform Wudu and forget to cleanse yourself (Istinja), and you remember after you have prayed, then upon you is the repetition (of the prayer); and if you did splash water, and you forgot to wash your penis until you prayed, then upon you is the repetition of the Wudu and the Salat, and the washing of your penis, because urine is not like feces.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man urinates and there is no water with him.' He said: 'He should squeeze the base of his penis to its tip three times, and shake its tip. If something comes out after that, it is not urine, but it is from the sexual veins.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Ala', from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who urinated, then performed wudu and stood for the prayer, so he found wetness. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not need to perform wudu again; rather, that is from the veins (of urine).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Safwan, who said: A man asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) and I was present, so he said, 'I have an injury in my backside. So I perform Wudu and cleanse myself, then I find after that wetness and yellowness from the backside. Should I repeat the Wudu?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And you have purified it?' He said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. But, sprinkle water upon it and do not repeat the Wudu'. Ahmad, from Abu Nasr, who said: 'A man asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) with approximately the Hadith of Safwan.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I heard a man ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Sometimes I urinate and am unable to use water, and that is difficult for me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you urinate and wipe yourself, wipe your penis with your saliva. If you find something [impurity], say: This is from that [saliva].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man is overcome by urine and cannot hold it back.' He (peace be upon him) said to me, 'When he cannot hold it back, then Allah is more deserving of excuse; he may make it [fall] into a bag.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a eunuch who urinates and faces difficulty from that, and sees moisture after moisture. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform ablution, then sprinkle water once during the day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'A'la, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about urine that hits the body. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Pour water upon it twice.' And it is reported that it suffices to wash with an equal amount of water if it is on the tip of the foreskin and other parts. And it is reported that it is water, not filth, so it needs to be rubbed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Usman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) urinated, and I was standing by his head, and with me was a container, or he said, a pitcher. So when the flow of urine stopped, he gestured with his hand like this, 'To me.' So I gave it to him with the water, and he performed Wudu in his place.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far (peace be upon him) who said: One of you takes comfort from the oil, so he fills his body with it, and the water is more expansive than that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ablution is a limit from the limits of Allah, so that Allah may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him, and indeed the believer is not polluted by anything; rather, the like of oil suffices for him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazalah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father was saying that for the Ablution (Wudu) there is a Limit. The one who exceeds it would not be recompensed; and my father was saying: 'But rather, he would be bewildered'. So a man said to him, 'And what is its Limit?' He said: 'You should wash your face, and your hands, and wipe your head and your feet'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one in a state of major impurity (Janub), whatever water flows upon his body, be it little or a lot, has sufficed him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the major ritual bath (ghusl) for sexual impurity, how much water suffices? So he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to bathe with five handfuls between him and his companion (wife), and they would both bathe from one vessel.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq, from Harun ibn Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It suffices you from the ritual bath (Ghusl) and the cleansing (Istinja') what fills your right hand.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding the Ablution, he said: 'When the water touches your skin, so it is sufficient for you.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man who is in a state of major ritual impurity immerses himself in water with a single immersion, and then comes out; would that suffice him for his ritual bath?' He said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Muhammad and others from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: For Allah there is an Angel who records the extravagance in the Ablution just as he records his transgressions.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Two cycles of prayer with using the siwak are superior to seventy cycles of prayer without using the siwak. He (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If it were not that I would impose hardship upon my community, I would have ordered them to use the siwak with every prayer.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Asama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophets is the Siwak (brushing of the teeth with a twig).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) did not cease to advise me with the Siwak (brushing teeth) until I feared that I would lose my teeth or become toothless.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the Siwak, he said: Do not neglect it in every three [prayers], and even if you just pass it over [the teeth] once.
Ali, by his chain, He said, 'The lowest of the brushing of the teeth is that you rub with your finger'.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Bakr ibn Abu Sammak, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you stand (for prayer) at night, brush your teeth, for the angel comes to you and places his mouth upon your mouth, and there is no letter you recite and speak with except that it ascends with it to the sky, so let your mouth be of good aroma.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassha, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hakam ibn Hukeym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the rinsing (of the mouth) and the sniffing (of the water), is it (part) of the Ablution? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shazan ibn al-Khalil, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the rinsing (of the mouth) and the sniffing (of the water). He said: 'These two are not from the Ablution (Wudu); they are from the inside (of the body).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not upon you (to perform) rinsing (of the mouth) nor sniffing (of the water), because these two are (cleansing of the) inside.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aban and Jameel, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to us the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So he called for a cup, took a handful of water, and poured it over his face. Then he wiped his face from both sides together. Then he returned his left hand to the vessel, poured it over his right hand, and wiped its sides. Then he returned his right hand to the vessel, poured it over his left hand, and did just as he had done with the right hand. Then he wiped with what remained in his hand upon his head and his two feet, and he did not return these two to the vessel.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub, from Bukayr ibn A'yn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'Shall I not narrate to you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' So he took a handful of water with his right palm and washed his face with it. Then he took with his left hand a handful of water and washed his right hand with it. Then he took with his right hand a handful of water and washed his left hand with it. Then he wiped with the remainder of his two hands his head and his feet.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far (peace be upon him), who said: One of you takes comfort from the oil, and water is more expansive than that. Shall I narrate to you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? I said, ‘Yes’. He said, ‘So he entered his hand into the vessel and did not wash his hand, but he took a palmful of water and poured it upon his face. Then he wiped its two sides until he had wiped all of it. Then he took another palmful with his right hand and poured it upon his left side, then washed with it his right arm. Then he took another palmful and washed with it his left arm. Then he wiped his head and his feet with whatever remained in his hand.’

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I narrate to you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' So we said, 'Yes.' He called for a jug containing some water, then placed it in front of him, then bared his arms, then immersed his right palm in it, then said: 'This is how, when the palm is clean.' Then he scooped and filled it with water, so he placed it upon his forehead, then said: 'In the Name of Allah,' and poured it upon the sides of his beard. Then he passed his hand over his face and the apparent part of his forehead once. Then he immersed his left hand and scooped a full palmful with it, then placed it upon his right elbow, and passed his palm over his forearm until the water flowed upon the sides of his fingers. Then he scooped a full palmful with his right hand, placed it upon his left elbow, and passed his palm over his forearm until the water flowed upon the sides of his fingers. And he wiped the front of his head and the back of his feet with the remnant of his left [hand] and the remainder of the remnant of his right [hand]. He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah is Odd (One) and Loves the odd, so it would suffice you from the ablution three scoops: one for the face, and two for the two arms. And you wipe the front of your head with the remnant of your right hand, and whatever remains of the remnant of your right hand, [wipe] the back of your right foot. And you wipe the back of your left foot with the remnant of your left hand.' Zurara said, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'A man asked Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) about the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he narrated to him similar to that.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ribat, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the wudu for the salat, so he said: 'Once, once'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Maysara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The ablution is one (washing), one (washing), and he described the ankle as being on the back of the foot.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he called for water, filled his palm with it, and washed his face with it. Then he filled his palm and washed his right hand with it. Then he filled his palm and washed his left hand with it. Then he wiped upon his head and his two feet, and said: 'This is the Wudu of the one who did not have a new event, meaning by it the transgression/excess in the Wudu.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to him, 'Inform me about the extent of the face which is befitting for one to wash for the Ablution (Wudu) which Allah (Exalted and Majestic) speaks of?' So he said: 'The face which Allah (the Exalted) commanded with its washing is that which is not befitting for anyone to increase upon, nor be deficient from it; if he exceeds upon it, he would not be recompensed, and if he is deficient from it, he would sin. [It is] what the index finger, the middle finger, and the thumb would circumvent from the front of the head to the chin, and what the two fingers flow upon from the face, encircling, so it is from the face, and whatever is besides that, so it is not from the face.' I said, 'The temples (sides of the forehead) is not from the face?' He said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man who performs ablution, should he cover the interior of his beard? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not strike your faces with water with a striking motion when you perform your Ablution (Wudu), but gently splash the water with a gentle splashing.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, who said: I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him) asking him about the extent of the face, so he wrote: 'From the beginning of the hair to the end of the face, and likewise the two foreheads.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his brother Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: Allah necessitated upon the women, regarding the Wudu for the Salat, that they should begin with the inside of their arms, and regarding the men, with the back of the arm.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one who has his hand and leg cut off. He said: He should wash them.

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rafa'ah, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Rafa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the amputated one. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash what has been cut off from him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man whose hand was cut off from the elbow, 'How does he perform the ablution?' He said: 'He washes whatever remains of his upper arm.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'People say that the inner part of the two ears is from the face, and their backs are from the head.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is neither washing nor wiping upon them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shazan ibn al-Khalil al-Naysaburi, from Ma'mar ibn Umar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: It suffices for the wiping upon the head to be the area of three fingers, and similarly for the leg.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The two ears are not from the face, nor from the head. He said, And the wiping was mentioned, so he said: Wipe upon the front of your head, and wipe upon the two feet, and begin with the right side.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shazaan ibn al-Khalil, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Al-Husayn, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performed Wudu while wearing a turban, and removing the turban was heavy upon him due to the cold, so he said: Let him insert his finger (under the turban to wipe).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Will you not inform me from where you knew and said that the wiping is with part of the head and part of the two feet?' So he smiled and said: 'O Zurara! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said so and the Book was revealed with it from Allah, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Wash your faces', thus we recognized that the entire face ought to be washed. Then He said: 'and your hands as far as the elbows'. Then He detailed between the speech, so He said: 'and wipe your heads'. So we recognized when He said 'your heads' that the wiping is with part of the head due to the placement of the letter 'Ba'. Then He linked the two feet with the head just as He linked the two hands with the face, so He said: 'and your feet to the ankles'. Thus, we recognized when He linked it with the head that the wiping is upon part of it. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) interpreted that for the people, but they neglected it. Then He said: 'and if you do not find water, then betake yourselves to pure earth and wipe your faces and your hands from it'. So when the Wudu was established, if you do not find water, it affirmed part of the washing as wiping, because He said 'wipe your faces', then He linked with it 'and your hands'. Then He said 'from it', i.e., from that Tayammum, because He knew that that is more comprehensive. It did not proceed upon the face entirely, because he attaches from that earth with part of the palm, and does not attach with part of it. Then He said: 'Allah does not intend to put upon you any difficulty in the religion', and the difficulty is the narrowness.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'It suffices the woman for the wiping of the head that she wipes its front by the measure of three fingers, and she should not cast off her scarf from her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the wiping upon the two feet, how it is (to be done). So he placed his palm upon the toes and wiped them up to the two ankles, up to the back of the foot. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Supposing if a man were to do it with two fingers from his fingers, like this?' So he said: 'No, except with his palm'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you were to perform wudu and make the wiping of the two feet a washing, then you intended that that is what is obligatory, it would not be a valid wudu.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the wiping upon the two feet; and if it becomes apparent to you that you washed, so you washed, then wipe after it, so that the last of what is obligatory is the wiping.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There comes to be upon the man, sixty or seventy years, Allah not Accepting a Salat from him'. I said, 'And how can that be?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because he washes what Allah Commanded for the wiping'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, his uncle, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him). I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The footwear of the man happens to be torn, so he enters his hand and wipes the back of his foot, would that suffice him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) performed ablution (wudu), so he washed his face and his forearms, then he wiped upon his head and upon his slipper (open from the front), and did not enter his hand beneath the straps.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the one who dyes his head with henna, then it becomes inevitable for him with regards to the Ablution (Wudu). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not allowed until he pours water onto the skin of his head.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa — all of them from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When the water reaches the measure of a kurr, nothing can make it impure.

Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the water in which animals urinate, dogs lap, and the one in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) bathes. He said: When the water is of the measure of a kurr, nothing will make it impure.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — both from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara — who said: When the water is more than a rawiya, nothing will render it impure — whether something has decomposed in it or not — except if a smell comes from it that overpowers the smell of the water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'When the water in the well is a Kurr, nothing will pollute it.' I said: 'And how much is a Kurr?' He said: 'Three and a half spans in depth by three and a half spans in width.'

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Kurr of water: 'How much is its measure?' He said: 'When the water is three and a half hand spans in length, and likewise three and a half hand spans in breadth, and three and a half hand spans in its depth in the ground, then that is the Kurr of water.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Kurr of water is one thousand two hundred Ratls.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the water which nothing can pollute. He said: A kurr. I said: And what is the kurr? He said: Three spans by three spans.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The kurr of water is approximately like this jar of mine,' and he gestured with his hand toward a jar from those jars that are found in al-Medina.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the sick person, is there a concession for him regarding the wiping (over the socks)? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to him, 'Is there dissimulation (taqiyyah) in wiping the two shoes?' He said: 'There are three (acts) in which I do not exercise dissimulation with anyone: drinking the intoxicant, wiping the two shoes, and the mut'ah of Hajj.' Zurara said, 'And he did not say: It is obligatory upon you that you do not exercise dissimulation with anyone in them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the fracture, where splints are upon it, or there is a wound with it, how should he deal with the wudu, and during the ghusl of janabah, and the ghusl of Jumu'ah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash what the washing reaches from what is apparent, from what is not covered by the splints, and he should leave what is besides that from what he is not able to wash, and he should neither remove the splints nor tamper with the wound.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the wound, how should its owner deal with it? He said: He should wash what is around it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who has a sore in his arm, or something similar in a place of ablution, so he binds it with a cloth, and performs ablution, and wipes over it when he performs ablution. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the water hurts him, let him wipe over the cloth, and if the water does not hurt him, let him remove the cloth, then let him wash it.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the wound, how should I deal with it in washing it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash what is around it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, from Abdul A'ala, the slave of the family of Saam, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I stumbled and my nail broke, so I placed ointment on my finger. How should I proceed with the ablution?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This and its like are known from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' He has not laid upon you in the religion any hardship. Wipe over it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you are certain that you have had an occurrence (of breaking ablution), so perform ablution, and beware of renewing an ablution ever, until you are certain that you have had an occurrence.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you are seated in the state of ablution and do not know whether you washed your forearm or not, then repeat upon it, and upon all that you doubted that you did not wash or wipe, from what Allah has specified, as long as you are in the state of ablution. So when you rise from the ablution and are finished, you have entered another state, in prayer or other than prayer, and you doubt in part of what Allah has specified from what Allah the Exalted has obligated upon you regarding ablution, then there is nothing upon you. And if you doubt regarding wiping your head, and moisture hits your beard, then wipe with it upon it and upon the back of your feet; and if moisture does not hit, then the ablution is not broken by the doubt, and proceed in your prayer. And if you are certain that you did not complete your ablution, then repeat upon what you left with certainty until you complete the ablution. Hammad said, and Hariz said, and Zurara said: I said to him, 'A man left part of his forearm or part of his body in the major ablution (ghusl).' He said: 'If he doubts, then there is moisture with him and he is in his prayer, he wipes with it upon it; and if he is certain, he returns and repeats the water upon it as long as moisture does not hit. If doubt enters him and he has entered another state, let him proceed in his prayer and there is nothing upon him. And if it becomes apparent, he returns and repeats the water upon it. And if he sees it and there is moisture with him, he wipes upon it and repeats the prayer with certainty. And if he is doubting, there is nothing upon him regarding his doubt, so let him proceed in his prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If you remember while you are in your prayer that you have left out something obligatory from your ablution, then turn back (end your prayer), complete what you forgot from your ablution, and repeat your prayer. And it suffices you for wiping your head if you take the moisture from your beard when you forgot to wipe your head, and you wipe the front of your head with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man forgets to wash his right hand, so he washes his left hand and wipes his head and his two feet, and then remembers, he should wash his right hand and his left hand, and wipe his head and his two feet; and if he only forgot his left hand, let him wash the left hand and not repeat over what he had already performed of ablution. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Follow your ablution, part by part (sequentially).'

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Follow the sequence in the wudu (ablution) just as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Begin with the face, then with the hands, then wipe the head and the two feet, and do not bring forward anything before what you have been commanded to do; and if you washed the forearm before the face, then begin with the face and repeat upon the forearm; and if you wiped the foot before the head, then wipe upon the head before the foot, then repeat upon the foot. Begin with what Allah began with.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If you forget and wash your forearm before your face, then repeat washing your face, then wash your two forearms after the face. And if you begin with your left forearm before the right, then repeat washing the right one, then wash the left one. And if you forget wiping your head until you wash your feet, then wipe your head, then wash your feet.

And by this chain, he said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: When you perform part of your Ablution (Wudhu), so a need arises for you until your Ablution (Wudhu) dries up, so repeat your Ablution (Wudhu), for the Ablution (Wudhu) cannot be in parts.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I perform Wudu and the water runs out, so I call the maid, but she is slow in bringing me the water, and my Wudu dries out.' He said, 'Repeat.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Hammad ibn Uthman from Hakam ibn Hukeym said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot the forearms and the head from the Ablution (Wudu). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat the Ablution (Wudu). Indeed, the Ablution (Wudu), parts of it follow its parts (it is sequential).'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shaza'an, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Salim Abu al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The ablution (wudu) is not broken except by what comes out from your two lower ends, which Allah has favored you with.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the nosebleed: Does it break the wudu? He (peace be upon him) said: Only three things break the wudu: urine, faeces, and wind.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Satan blows into the anus of the human being until it seems to him that a wind has come out from him. So, the Ablution (Wudhu) does not break except by wind which you hear, or find its smell'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Zarif, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Abdullah ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no need for ablution (wudu) regarding the seeds of the pumpkin and the small insects; rather, they are at the status of lice.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Akhi Fudayl, from Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man from whom comes out something similar to a pumpkin seed, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no ablution upon him.' And it is reported that if it is stained with faeces, he must repeat the ablution.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What breaks the Ablution?' So they both said: 'Whatever comes out from your two lower ends, from the backside and the manhood, faeces or urine or semen or wind; and the sleep until the intellect goes (loose awareness). All sleep is disliked, except if you happens to hear the sounds' (in consciousness).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man: Is it permissible for him to insert medicine, then pray while it is with him? Does it break the ablution? He said: It does not break the ablution, and he should not pray until he removes it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who belches, so something comes out from him, should he repeat the wudu? He (peace be upon him) said: No.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Usamah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the vomit, does it break the ablution? He said: No.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man vomits while he is in a state of purity, let him rinse his mouth.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is in a state of purity and takes from his nails or his hair; should he repeat the ablution? He said: 'No, but he should wipe his head and his nails with the water.' I said: 'But they claim that it requires the ablution.' He said: 'If they dispute with you, do not dispute with them, and say: Thus is the Sunnah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no ablution (wudu) required for kissing, nor for touching the private parts, nor for sexual contact.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about nosebleed and cupping, and every flowing blood, so he said: There is no ablution (wudu) in this. Rather, the ablution is from your two lower ends which Allah, the Exalted, has favored with upon you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has an illness and cannot lie down, and ablution is difficult for him while he is sitting leaning on pillows; sometimes he dozes off while in that state. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He performs ablution.' I said to him: 'Indeed, ablution is difficult for him due to his condition.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sound becomes faint for him, then ablution becomes obligatory upon him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He delays Dhuhr and prays it with Asr, combining the two, and similarly Maghrib and Isha.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the light sleep (khafqah) and the two light sleeps (khafqatan), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not know what is the light sleep and the two light sleeps. Indeed, Allah says: 'But! The human being has an insight unto himself.' Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The one who finds the taste of sleep while standing, or sitting, so the Wudu is Obligated upon him.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from the one who mentioned it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There are two ears and two eyes; the two eyes sleep and the two ears do not sleep, and that does not break the wudu. So when the two eyes and the two ears sleep, the wudu breaks.

Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man cuts his hair with his teeth; should he wipe it with water before he prays? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem. Rather, that is regarding (cutting it with) the iron.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who treads upon a place that is not clean, then treads after it on a clean place, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if it is fifteen cubits or thereabouts.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when he passed over a dry excrement, so he trod upon it, and it hit his garment. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you have trodden upon an excrement and it hit your garment.' He said, 'Is it not dry?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no problem, for the earth cleanses part of it with part of it.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Safwan from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Muhammad al-Halabi who said: We lodged in a place, and between us and the Masjid was a dirty alleyway. So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he said: 'Where did you lodge?' I said: 'We lodged in the house of so-and-so.' He said: 'Between you and the Masjid is a dirty alleyway,' or we said to him: 'Between us and the Masjid is a dirty alleyway.' He said: 'There is no problem; the earth purifies one part of it with another.' I said: 'And the wet manure that I tread upon?' He said: 'The likes of that does not harm you.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who treads upon excrement or urine, should he repeat the ablution? He said: No, but he should wash what it hit. And in another report: If it is dry, he does not wash it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a pig coming out of the water, passing over the road, and water flowing from it. 'Can I pass over it barefoot?' He said: 'Is there not something dry behind it?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'So there is no problem. Indeed, the earth purifies one part with another.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If something flows from your manhood, either pre-seminal fluid (madhi) or semen (mani), and you are in the prayer, do not wash it, do not break the prayer, and do not invalidate the ablution for it. And if it reaches your behind, that is merely like phlegm. And everything that comes out from you after the ablution is from the sexual veins or from the haemorrhoids, and it is not significant, so do not wash it from your clothes unless it dirties you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the seminal fluid (madhi), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It and the phlegm (nukhama) are equal (in ruling).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about the seminal fluid (al-madhy), so he said: 'It does not break the wudu (ablution), and one does not have to wash the clothes or the body from it; rather, it is at the status of mucus and saliva.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the pre-seminal fluid (al-madhy) that flows until it reaches the thigh. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not break one's prayer, nor is it required to wash it from the thigh, because it has not exited from the exit of the semen. It is merely in the status of mucus.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The ritual bath (ghusl) is [required] from the sexual impurity (janabah), and on the day of Friday, and on the two Eids, and when you enter the state of Ihram, and when you enter Makkah and Al-Madinah, and on the day of 'Arafah, and on the day you perform Ziyarah of the House, and when you enter the Ka'bah, and during the night of the nineteenth, twenty-first, and twenty-third of the month of Ramadan, and [for] the one who washes a deceased person.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Friday washing, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is obligatory during the journey and during residing, except that it is exempted for the women during the journey due to the scarcity of the water'.
