And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The major washing (from sexual impurity) is an obligation, and the washing of the menstruating woman when she is clean is an obligation, and the washing of the woman with inter-period bleeding is an obligation when she inserts with the rag, and the blood exceeds the rag, so upon her is the washing for every two prayers, and for the dawn prayer, a washing. And if the rag suffices for the blood, so upon her is the washing once every day, and the ablution for every prayer'. And the washing for post-childbirth bleeding is an obligation, and washing for the child birth is an obligation. And washing of the deceased is an obligation, and washing for visitation is an obligation, and washing for entering the House is an obligation, and washing for the supplication for rain is an obligation. And washing in the first night of a month of Ramadan is recommended, and the washing of the night of the twenty-first, and the washing of the night of the twenty-third is a Sunnah, do not neglect these. For the Night of Pre-determination is hoped for in one of these. And washing for the day of Eid al-Fitr and washing for the day of the Sacrifice is a Sunnah, I do not like it to be neglected, and washing for the Istikhara. It is the recommended deed regarding the washing of the three nights from a month of Ramadan – the night of the nineteenth, and twenty-first, and the twenty-third.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: When you perform the ritual bath after the emergence of dawn, that bathing of yours suffices for the major impurity (janabah), Friday prayer, Arafat, sacrifice, shaving (the head), slaughtering, and pilgrimage; and whenever multiple obligations gather upon you, one bath suffices for them all. He said, then he said: And similarly for the woman, one bath suffices her for her major impurity, her ihram (state of consecration), Friday prayer, and her bath from menstruation and Eid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them), that he said: When the one with sexual impurity washes after the emergence of dawn, that washing suffices him from every washing necessitated upon him during that day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the ritual bath on the day of Friday, so he said: 'It is obligatory upon every male and female, slave or free.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the washing for the day of Friday, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is an obligation upon every male and female, whether a slave or free.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The ritual bath (Ghusl) on Friday is obligatory for men and women in the city (not traveling), and for men during travel, and it is not obligatory for women during travel. And in another report, it was permitted for women during travel due to the scarcity of water.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first, 'How did the washing for the day of Friday come to be an Obligation?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Blessed and High, Completed the Obligatory Salat with the optional Salat, and Completed the Obligatory Fasting with the optional Fasting, and Completed the Obligatory Wudu with the washing of the day of Friday, [covering] whatever was during that from the mistake, or shortening, or forgetfulness, or deficiency'.

A number of our companions, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Sabbah al-Muzani, from al-Harith ibn Haseerah, from al-Asbagh, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when he wanted to rebuke a man, would say: 'By Allah, you are even more deficient than the one who neglects the ghusl on Friday, and indeed he remains in purity until the next Friday.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, from his mother and the mother of Ahmad, daughter of Musa, said: We were with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in the wilderness, and we intended to go to Baghdad. So he said to us on the day of Thursday: 'Wash for the day of tomorrow, the day of Friday, for the water there will be scarce tomorrow.' So we both washed on the day of Thursday for the day of Friday.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the washing for major impurity (ghusl al-janabah), so he said: 'Begin with your two palms and wash them, then wash your private part, then pour water upon your head three times, then pour water upon the rest of your body twice. Whatever the water flows upon has been purified.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in a state of major impurity (janib) should pour water over his head three times; any less than that would not suffice him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said, 'How should the one with sexual impurity wash?' So he said: 'If nothing has hit his palm, he should immerse it in the water, then begin with his private part and cleanse it with three scoops. Then he should pour upon his head three handfuls, then pour upon his right shoulder twice and upon his left shoulder twice. So whatever the water flows upon, it suffices him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the one in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) immerses himself in the water with one immersion, that suffices him for his ritual bath (ghusl).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the woman who wears a bracelet and a hairpin on part of her arm, and she does not know if water flows beneath them or not. How should she act when she performs Wudu or Ghusl? He said: She should move them until water enters beneath them, or she should remove them. And regarding the tight ring, if one does not know if water flows beneath it when performing Wudu or not, how should he act? He said: If he knows that water does not enter it, let him remove it when he performs Wudu.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Abu Dawud, altogether from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who incurred major ritual impurity (janabah), so he stood in the rain until it flowed over his body: 'Would that suffice him from the ghusl?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar Al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) did not see any problem if the person in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) were to wash his head in the early morning and wash the rest of his body at the time of prayer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: ‘The one who performs the ritual bath for major impurity but does not wash his head, then it occurs to him that he should wash his head, must not find an alternative but to repeat the ritual bath.’

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Hammad, from Bakr ibn Karb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man washing from the major ritual impurity (janabah): does he wash his feet after the full bath? He said: If he is washing in a place where the water flows over his feet after the bath, then it is not upon him to wash them; and if he is washing in a place where his feet remain in stagnant water, then let him wash both of them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I wash in the bathroom (latrine) in which I urinate, and upon me are Sindian slippers.' So he said: 'If the water that flows from your body hits the bottom of your feet, then do not wash your feet.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shazan ibn al-Khalil, from Yunus, from Yahya ibn Talha, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The ablution (wudu) after the ritual bath (ghusl) is an innovation (bid'ah).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every washing, before it is an Ablution (Wudhu), except for the washing for the sexual impurity. And it is reported: 'There is nothing from the washing wherein is an Ablution (Wudhu) except for the washing for the day of Friday, for before it is an Ablution (Wudhu)'. And it is reported, 'Which Ablution (Wudhu) is more cleansing that the washing?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ring when I perform the ritual bath (Ghusl). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Turn it around from its place.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'With regard to the ablution (Wudu), turn it around, and if you forget [to remove it] until you stand in the prayer, then I do not order you to repeat the prayer.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father performed ghusl from janabah. It was said to him, 'You have left a spot on your back that the water did not reach.' He said to him, 'It was not upon you; if only you had remained silent.' Then he wiped that spot with his hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The woman may not let down her hair when she washes from the sexual impurity.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about what the women do regarding the hair and the plaits (curls). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It was not that they combed these, but rather they gathered it.' Then he described four possibilities, then said: 'They should be thorough in the washing.'
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whenever you come to water and there is little of it, sprinkle from your right and from your left and in front of you, and then perform wudu.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is in a state of janabah and reaches a small amount of water on the road, and he wants to perform ghusl from it, but he has no vessel to scoop with and both his hands are dirty. He said: He should place his hand (in it) and perform wudu, then perform ghusl. This is from what God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'He has not laid upon you any hardship in the religion'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Hammad, from Hareez, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: 'Every time the water overcomes the smell of the carcass, then perform wudu from the water and drink; and when the water changes and the taste changes, then neither perform wudu nor drink (from it).'

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — and I was seated (present) — about a pool of water that they came to, and therein was a carcass. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the water is overwhelming (in quantity) and the smell is not detected in it, then perform wudu (ablution).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about stagnant water and performing istinja from it while a carcass was in it. So he said: Perform wudu from the other side, and do not perform wudu from the side of the carcass.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the rotten water: you may perform wudu from it, unless you find other water, in which case you should avoid it.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cisterns which are between Mecca and Medina — wild animals come to them, dogs lap from them, and a sexually impure person bathes in them — can one perform wudu from them? He said: And how much is the measure of the water? I said: Up to half the shin and up to the knee, and less. He said: Perform wudu.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him, 'When does the ritual bath (ghusl) become obligatory upon the man and the woman?' He said, 'When he enters her, then the ritual bath, the dower (mahr), and the stoning (rajm) become obligatory.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the man who copulates with the woman near the private part but they do not discharge, 'When is the ritual bath (Ghusl) obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the two circumcised parts meet, the ritual bath becomes obligatory.' I said, 'The meeting of the two circumcised parts is the emergence of the glans?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who has intercourse with the virgin girl, neither ejaculating into her nor discharging upon her, is ritual bath obligatory upon her? And if she was not a virgin, then he had intercourse with her and did not ejaculate into her, is ritual bath obligatory upon her? He (peace be upon him) said: When the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, then the ritual bath becomes obligatory, whether she is a virgin or not.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man indulging in foreplay, is there a washing upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when he discharges.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the man who touches the private part of his young girl until she discharges water, without him having sexual intercourse, playing with her with his hand until she discharges. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When she discharges due to desire/excitement, then the ritual bath (ghusl) is upon her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'e, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the man who has intercourse with the woman in what is besides the private part, and the woman discharges [semen/fluid], upon her is the washing. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the woman who embraces her husband from behind, so she moves upon his back, and desire comes to her, and she discharges water; is the ritual bath obligatory upon her or not? He (peace be upon him) said: When desire comes to her and she discharges water, the ritual bath becomes obligatory upon her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, raised it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man has intercourse with a woman in her anus, if he does not discharge semen, there is no ritual bath (ghusl) upon either of them; and if he does discharge, then the ritual bath is upon him, and there is no ritual bath upon her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'A'la, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who sees (in a dream) until he feels desire, so he feels that he has ejaculated, but when he wakes up he does not see the water (semen) in his garment, nor on his body. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no ghusl upon him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The ghusl is only due to the great water (discharge). So when he sees in his dream, and does not see the great water, then there is no ghusl upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who had a wet dream. So, when he awoke, he found wetness. He said: 'It is not [requiring anything] except if he happens to be sick, then upon him is the ritual bath (ghusl).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: When you are sick and desire overtakes you, then perhaps it is the discharge, but it comes with a weak coming, not having strength due to your illness, hour after hour, little by little, so perform ritual bath (ghusl) from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Hariz, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man sees [a dream] in sleep and feels desire, then wakes up and looks but finds nothing. Then he waits afterwards and it comes out.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is sick, let him perform ghusl; and if he is not sick, there is nothing upon him [no ghusl required].' He (the narrator) said: 'So I said to him, 'What is the difference between the two?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because when the man is healthy, it comes with a spurt and strength, and when he is sick, it does not come except afterwards [without force/spurt].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman who sees in her sleep what the man sees. He said: If she discharges, then the ritual bath is upon her, and if she does not discharge, then the ritual bath is not upon her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who sees in sleep that a man is copulating with her in her private part, until she discharges. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should wash.' And in another report, he said: 'Upon her is a washing, but do not narrate this to them, lest they take it as an excuse.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who sleeps and does not perceive in his sleep that he has had a seminal emission, but finds water in his garment and on his thigh. Is there a ritual bath upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) and performed ghusl before urinating, and something came out from him. He said: 'He must repeat the ghusl.' I said: 'And for the woman, if something comes out from her after the ghusl?' He said: 'She does not repeat.' I said: 'So what is the difference between the two?' He said: 'Because what comes out from the woman is merely from the water of the man.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who performs ritual bath (ghusl), then finds wetness after that, and he had urinated before he bathed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had urinated before he bathed, then he does not repeat the bath.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who washes from the major impurity (janabah), then she sees a drop from the man after that; is there a washing upon her? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Abu Dawood, from Al Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zur'at, from Sama'at who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who becomes sexually impure, then he performs the ritual bath before he urinates, so he finds wetness after having bathed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He must repeat the ritual bath; and if he had urinated before he bathed, then he does not repeat his bath, but he performs ablution and cleans his private part.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one in major ritual impurity (junub), when he wants to eat and drink, should wash his hand, rinse his mouth, wash his face, and then eat and drink.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one with sexual impurity eating and drinking and reciting (the Quran). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, he can eat and drink and recite (the Quran), and mention Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whatever he so desires to.'

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: For the one in a state of major ritual impurity (al-junub), it is permissible to walk through all mosques, but he may not sit in them, except for the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) and the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Junub (one with major sexual impurity) sitting in the mosques. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he may pass through all of them, except for the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one who recites from the Mushaf while he is without wudu. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, but he should not touch the Book.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hariz who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The one in a state of major impurity state massages (with oil), then washes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) applies to his body and head khuluq (a type of hair oil/grease), perfume (tayyib), and a chewy substance like Roman gum (mastic) and mouth freshener, and what resembles them. He then performs ghusl (ritual bath). When he finishes, he finds something remaining on his body from the trace of the khuluq, perfume, and other things.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem (with his prayer/purity).'

Abu Dawud from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Fadalah ibn Ayoub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one with sexual impurity and the menstruating woman taking the chattel from the Masjid which happens to be in it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but they should not place anything in the Masjid'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who becomes sexually impure (junub), then wishes to sleep. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he wishes to perform ablution (wudu), let him do so, and the ritual bath (ghusl) is more beloved to me and superior to that. So if he sleeps and does not perform ablution and does not take a ritual bath, there is nothing upon him, God willing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with a man getting cupping done while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem if a man applies dye while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), and there is no problem if the one in a state of major ritual impurity applies kohl, gets cupping done, and slaughters (an animal). However, he should not taste anything until he washes his hands and rinses his mouth, for fear of vitiligo (or spreading of the dye/impurity) from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Usamah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) who sweats in his garment, or who bathes and then embraces his wife and lies with her while she is menstruating or in a state of major impurity, so that his body is affected by her sweat. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of this is not [a problem].'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Asama, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Rain falls on me while I am wearing a garment, so it becomes wet, and I am in a state of major ritual impurity (junub). If some of the semen that touched my body also touches the garment, can I pray in it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was present, about a man who became sexually impure (junub) in his garment and sweated in it. He said: 'I do not see a problem with it.' It was said to him: 'He sweats to such an extent that if he wished to wring it, he could wring it (and sweat would drip).' He said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) frowned in the face of the man and said: If you refuse (that it is pure), then (he should take) a little water to sprinkle it with.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Usamah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the garment in which there is major ritual impurity (janabah), and the rain falls upon me until it drenches me. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man urinates while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), then he cleans his private part (istinja), and his garment touches his body while he is still wet. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about semen that hits the garment. He said: If you know its place, wash it, and if its place is hidden from you, wash the whole garment.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Muyassar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I order a slave girl to wash my garment from semen, but she does not wash it thoroughly, so I pray in it when it is dry.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat your prayer. Indeed, if you had washed it yourself, there would be no blame upon you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about semen that hits the garment. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash the entire garment if its location is hidden from you, whether it was a little or a lot.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man experiences nocturnal emission and something touches his garment, he should wash the part that was touched; and if he thinks something touched it but is not certain and does not see its place, he should sprinkle it with water; and if he is certain that it touched it but does not see its place, he should wash his entire garment, for that is better.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the seminal fluid hitting the clothes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from 'Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'We do not consider an ablution (wudu) to be required for the seminal fluid (madhi), nor a ritual bath (ghusl) for whatever of it hits the garment, except for the great water (semen/madh').

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about urine that hits the body. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Pour water upon it twice, for it is merely water.' And I asked him (peace be upon him) about clothes hit by urine. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash it twice.' And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a child urinating on the clothes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Pour a little water upon it, then wring it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abu Mahmoud, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'When urine hits the mattress and the bedding, how should they be treated, given that it is thick and has a lot of padding?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash what is apparent from it on its surface.'

Ahmad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a garment that urine strikes and permeates to the other side, and about the fur and what is inside it of padding. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash what was struck by it, and touch the other side; and if the touch senses something from it has struck it, then wash it, otherwise sprinkle it with water.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Hakam ibn Hukeym Al-Sayrafi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I urinate but do not have water available, and something from the urine hits my hand, so I wipe it with the wall or the dust, then my hand sweats, so I wipe my face or part of my body, or it touches my clothes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said, 'In the book of Sama'ah, he raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):' If something from the urine of a cat touches the garment, then the prayer is not valid in it until you wash it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the urine of the infant. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Pour water over it, and if he has eaten [solid food], wash it with a washing. And the boy and the girl are equal in that according to the Sharia.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Fadl ibn Ghazwan, from al-Hakam ibn al-Hukaym, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I go to the market and need to urinate, and there is no water with me. Then I wipe it and dry it with my hand, then I wipe my hand on the wall and the ground, then I scratch my body after that.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, that the two (Imams) said: Do not wash your garment from the urine of an animal whose flesh is eaten.

Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the milk of camels, sheep, and cows, and their urines and their flesh. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not perform wudu from it if anything of it hits you, or your clothes, so do not wash it unless you wish to clean it.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the urines of beasts, mules, and donkeys. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash it. If you do not know its place, wash the entire garment. And if you doubt, sprinkle it (with water).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash your garment from the urine of that whose flesh is not eaten.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding the urines of animals hitting the clothes, he disliked it. So I said to him, 'Is not their flesh permissible?' He said: 'Yes, but it is not from what Allah made for eating.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Maryam, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the urines of the animals and their droppings?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for their urines, wash if it hits you, and as for their droppings, it is more than that.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Aban, from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with the dung of donkeys, and wash its urine.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Malik al-Juhani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what comes out from the nostrils of the animal and hits me. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If something from the urine of a cat hits the garment, then prayer is not valid in it until you wash it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Everything which flies, so there is no problem with its urine and its droppings.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-A'azz al-Nakhhas, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I treat the animals, so sometimes I go out at night and they have urinated or excreted, so one of them strikes it with its foot or its hand, so it splashes upon my clothes. So I wake up in the morning and I see its traces in it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muawiya ibn Hakim, from Al-Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while he was praying. My guide said to me, 'There is blood on his garment.' So when he finished, I said to him, 'My guide informed me that there is blood on your garment.' He said to me, 'I have pimples, and I do not wash my garment until it heals.'

Ahmad, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the man who has a sore or a wound, and he is not able to bandage it nor wash his blood. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray and not wash his garment every day except once, for he is not able to wash his garment every hour.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to him, 'Blood may be on the garment upon me while I am in prayer.' He said, 'If you see it and there is another garment upon you, cast it off and pray. And if there is no other garment upon you, continue in your prayer and there is no need to repeat upon you, as long as it does not exceed the measure of a dirham. And whatever is less than that is insignificant, whether you saw it beforehand or did not see it. And if you saw it and it is more than the measure of a dirham, and you neglected washing it and prayed many prayers in it, then repeat whatever you prayed in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) did not see any problem with blood that was not slaughtered, if it happens to be in the garment, so the man prays in it – meaning the blood of the fish.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said: A mother of a child of his son asked him, saying, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I wish to ask you about something, but I am shy to do so.' He said, 'Ask, and do not be shy.' She said, 'Menstrual blood struck my garment, so I washed it, but its trace did not disappear.' So he said, 'Dye it with red pigment (mishq) until it mixes and the trace disappears.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: Your blood is cleaner than the blood of someone else. When it is in your garment like a splatter of your own blood, there is no problem, and if it is the blood of someone else, whether little or much, then wash it.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan, who said: I wrote to the Man (peace be upon him): Does the blood of the cow follow the same ruling as the blood of the fleas, and is it permissible for anyone to analogize the blood of the cow to the fleas, so he prays in it, and to analogize in this manner and act upon it? So he (peace be upon him) signed: Prayer is permissible, and purification from it is superior.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the dog touches your garment, if it was dry then sprinkle it, and if it was wet then wash it.

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a dog touching a part of a man's body. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wash the place that it touched.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali Al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the wet mouse that had fallen into the water and was walking upon the clothes: 'Is one to pray in them?' He said: 'Wash what you see of its trace, and what you do not see, so sprinkle it with water.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: Is it permissible for the fox, the rabbit, or any of the wild beasts to touch (one), whether alive or dead? He said: It does not harm him, but he should wash his hand.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man whose clothes fall upon the body of the deceased. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it had been washed, then do not wash what hit your clothes from it; and if it had not been washed, then wash what hit your clothes from it — meaning when the dead body is cold.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man whose garment is touched by a pig, but he does not wash it, and he remembers that while he is in his prayer. How should he act? He said: If he had entered into his prayer, let him continue; and if he had not yet entered into his prayer, let him sprinkle what touched his garment, unless there is a trace in it, in which case he should wash it.

I wrote to a man asking him to ask Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about the well that is in the house for wudu — drops of urine fall into it, or blood, or something of filth like animal dung and such things fall into it: what purifies it until wudu from it for salat becomes permissible? So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting in my letter: 'Remove some buckets from it.'
And by this chain, he said: The water of the well is vast; nothing would pollute it except if it is changed by it (the filth).

...regarding the rats, and the cats, and the chickens, and the birds, and the dogs (falling into the well). He (peace be upon him) said: 'As long as they have not decomposed, or the taste of the water has not changed, then removing five buckets suffices you; and if the water has changed, then keep taking from it until the smell goes away.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Nothing pollutes the water except that which has flowing blood (i.e., a warm-blooded creature).

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the poisonous lizard (samma' abras) that falls into the well. He said: 'It is not anything (of concern). Stir the water with the bucket.'

Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what falls into wells. He said: 'As for the rat and its likes, draw out seven buckets from it, except if the water has changed, in which case draw it out until it becomes clean. If a dog falls into it and you are able to draw out its water, then do so. And everything that falls into the well that has no blood, like the scorpion, the beetles, and the likes of that — there is no problem.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When something small falls into the well and dies in it, draw out buckets from it; and if a sexually impure person (junub) falls into it, draw out seven buckets from it. But if a camel dies in it, or wine is poured into it, then let it be completely emptied.

I asked him about a man who slaughtered a sheep, and it convulsed and fell into a water well while its jugular veins were gushing blood. Can one perform wudu from that well? He said: Draw out from it between thirty and forty buckets, then one may perform wudu from it, and there is no problem with it. He said: And I asked him about a man who slaughtered a chicken or a dove and it fell into a well. Is it proper to perform wudu from it? He said: Draw out from it a few buckets, then one may perform wudu from it. And I asked him about a man who is drawing water from a well and his nose bleeds into it. Can one perform wudu from it? He said: Draw out from it a few buckets.

I said: A well from which pieces of skin come out in its water. He (peace be upon him) said: It is of no consequence. The salamander sometimes sheds its skin. And he said: It suffices you to draw out a bucket of water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ib, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the rope which is made of pig hair, by which water is drawn from the well. Can one perform wudu from that water? He said: There is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about faeces falling into the well. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Draw out ten buckets from it. But if it has melted/dissolved, then forty or fifty buckets.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abdul Kareem from Abu Baseer who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A well from which one draws water, performs wudu with it, washes clothes with it, and kneads dough with it, then it is known that a dead body was in it.' He said, 'There is no problem, and one does not wash the garment from it (again) nor repeat the prayer because of it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about Tayammum, so he struck the ground with his hand, then raised it and shook it, then wiped with it his two foreheads and his two palms once.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about Tayammum, so he recited this Verse: And (as for) the man who steals and the woman who steals, cut off their hands and He said: wash your faces and your hands as far as the elbows He said: Therefore wipe upon (the back of your) wrists from where is the place of the cut. And He said: and your Lord was not forgetful

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Kahili, who said: I asked him about Tayammum. He said, 'So he struck with his hand upon the rug, and wiped his face with it. Then he wiped his two hands, one of them upon the back of the other.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about Tayammum, so he said: 'Ammar ibn Yasir was afflicted with Janabah (major ritual impurity), so he rolled upon the ground as an animal rolls. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'O Ammar, you rolled as the animal rolls.' So I said to him, 'How is the Tayammum?' So he placed his hand upon the rough cloth (Misah), then raised it, so he wiped his face, then wiped above the wrist a little.' And it is reported from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Nawfali, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no wudu (ablution) from a mutawwa' (the place you walk on).' Al-Nawfali said, 'It means the place on which you step with your foot.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Alawi, from Sahl ibn Jamhur, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn al-Urni, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) forbade that a man performs tayammum with the dust of the road.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you do not find water and intend Tayammum, then delay the Tayammum until the end of the time (of prayer). So if the water is missed, the earth is not missed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: When the traveler cannot find water, let him seek it as long as he is within the time [for prayer]. But if he fears that the time will pass, let him perform Tayammum and pray at the end of the time. When he finds water, there is no repayment (Qada) upon him, and let him perform Wudu for what is next.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man does not find a purifier (water) and he is in a state of major impurity (junub), let him wipe from the earth (perform tayammum) and pray. So when he finds water, let him perform ghusl, and the prayer he has already prayed will suffice him.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Does a man pray the night and day prayers all of them with one ablution?' He said, 'Yes, as long as he does not incur a breakage.' I said, 'And does he pray with one tayammum the night and day prayers all of them?' He said, 'Yes, as long as he does not incur a breakage or find water.' I said, 'If he finds water and hopes that he will be able to find another water, and thinks that he will be able to find it whenever he wishes, but that is difficult for him?' He said, 'That breaks his tayammum, and upon him is to repeat the tayammum.' I said, 'If he finds water and has already entered into the prayer?' He said, 'So let him turn away and let him perform ablution as long as he has not bowed; if he has bowed, let him continue in his prayer, for the tayammum is one of the two purifiers.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Aasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who does not find water, so he performs Tayammum and stands in Salat. Then the boy came and said, 'Here is the water.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had not bowed, let him leave and perform Wudu; and if he had already bowed, let him continue in his Salat.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I am on a journey and the prayer time arrives, and there is no water with me, and it is said that water is nearby. Should I seek the water, searching right and left, while I am in the prayer time?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not seek the water, but perform tayammum, for I fear that you will be left behind from your companions, become lost, and the predators will devour you.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who passes by the water well and there is no bucket with him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon him that he descends into the water well. Indeed, the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth, so let him perform Tayammum.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Yaqoub ibn Salim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who does not have water with him, and the water is on the right of the road and the left, a couple of stone's throws away or approximately that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not order him to endanger himself, so that a thief or a predator might present himself to him.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Ibn Abi Yaf'ur and 'Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you come to the well and you are in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) and do not find a bucket or anything else to scoop the water with, then perform tayammum with the soil, for the Lord of the water and the Lord of the soil is One; and do not fall into the well, nor spoil the water for the people.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him about a man who was on a journey and had water with him, but he forgot it, performed Tayammum, and prayed. Then he remembered that he had water with him before the time for prayer expired. He said: 'Upon him is that he should perform Wudu and repeat the Salat.' He said, 'And I asked him about the Tayammum of the menstruating woman and the one with sexual impurity (Junub) — is it the same if they do not find water?' He said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who incurred major ritual impurity (janabah) during travel, and he had with him only a little water, and he feared that if he were to perform ghusl he would become thirsty. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he fears thirst, let him not spill a single drop from it, and let him perform tayammum with the soil, for the soil is more beloved to me.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ibn Abi Yafur who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) and with him is water sufficient only for his drinking. Should he perform Tayammum or Wudu? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Tayammum is superior. Do you not see that only half the purification has been made obligatory upon him?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jameel, who said: We said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A leader of a group of people experiences major ritual impurity during travel, and there is no water with him sufficient for the full bath. Should one of them perform ablution and he pray with them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but let him perform dry ablution and pray with them, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the dust a purifier.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: If the earth is wet and there is no dust nor water in it, look for the driest place you can find and perform Tayammum from its dust or something covered in dust; and if it is a situation where you can find nothing except clay, then there is no problem if you were to perform Tayammum with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who became junub during travel and found nothing except snow or frozen water. He said: 'He is in the position of necessity; he should perform tayammum, and I do not think he should return to that land which ruins his religion.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who incurred major ritual impurity (janabah) on a cold night, fearing for his life if he were to perform ghusl. He said: 'He should perform tayammum and pray. So when he is safe from the cold, he should perform ghusl and repeat the prayer.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who has sores and injuries and experiences sexual impurity. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with him not performing ghusl and performing tayammum.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one with pockmarks and the one with the broken limb perform tayammum with dust when sexual impurity hits them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one with pockmarks who was hit by sexual impurity. He said: If he was in a state of major impurity, let him perform Ghusl, and if he had a wet dream, let him perform Tayammum.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih and Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Ghifari, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was told that a man had sexual impurity upon a wound he had, so he was ordered to perform the ritual bath; he bathed, and the wound became infected, so he died. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'They killed him, may Allah kill them. Indeed, the cure for the wound was the question (i.e., asking if one could perform dry ablution instead of bathing).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to him, 'So-and-so was afflicted with major ritual impurity (janabah), and he was a person with pockmarks (majdur). So they washed him, and he died.' He said: 'They killed him. Why did they not ask? Why did they not perform tayammum? Indeed, the cure for the ailment is asking (for guidance).' He said, 'And that is reported regarding the one with a broken limb, and the one with internal illness: they perform tayammum and do not perform ghusl.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said: I entered upon al-Rida (peace be upon him), and in front of him was a jug; he intended to prepare from it for the prayer. So I approached him to pour water over his hand, but he refused that and said: 'Stop, O Hassan.' So I said to him: 'Why do you forbid me from pouring [water] on your hand? Do you dislike for me to be recompensed?' He said: 'You will be recompensed and I will be burdened.' So I said to him: 'And how is that?' So he recited: 'Have you not heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: Therefore whoever hopes to meet his Lord, so he should do righteous deeds, and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord?' And here I am performing ablution for the prayer, and it is the worship, so I dislike for anyone to participate with me therein.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from al-Qaddah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The beginning of the prayer is the ablution, its sanctification is the Takbeer, and its legalization is the Tasleem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sabbah al-Hazza', from Abu Asama, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and a man from the Mugheira clan asked him about something from the Sunnah. He said: 'There is nothing that anyone from the children of Adam needs except that a Sunnah has flowed regarding it from Allah and from His Messenger; he who recognizes it recognizes it, and he who denies it denies it.' The man said, 'So what is the Sunnah regarding entering the toilet?' He said: 'Remember Allah and seek refuge with Allah from the Satan, the Pelted one. And when you are finished, say: 'All praise is for Allah upon what He removed from me of harm, in ease and health.' The man said, 'So if a person is in that state and cannot be patient until he looks at what comes out of him?' He said: 'There is no human on earth except that two angels are assigned to him. So when he is in that state, they bend his neck, then they say: 'O son of Adam! Look at what you were toiling for in the world, to what it has become.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever performs wudu and wipes himself with a towel, for him is one good deed; and if he performs wudu and does not wipe himself, letting his wudu dry upon himself, for him are thirty good deeds.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Jarrah al-Hazza', from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs wudu for the Maghrib prayer, that wudu of his is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his day, except the major sins; and whoever performs wudu for the Fajr (morning) prayer, that wudu of his is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his night, except the major sins.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Qasim al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: While the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was seated, with him was his son Muhammad. He said: 'O Muhammad, bring me a vessel of water.' So he brought it to him, and he poured it with his right hand onto his left hand, then said: 'Praise is to Allah who made water purifying and did not make it impure.' Then he cleaned his private part and said: 'O Allah, fortify my private part and keep it chaste, and conceal my nakedness and prohibit it from the Fire.' Then he inhaled water and said: 'O Allah, do not prohibit the scent of Paradise from me, and make me among those who smell its scent, its fragrance, and its blossoms.' Then he rinsed his mouth and said: 'O Allah, cause my tongue to speak with Your remembrance, and make me among those with whom You are pleased.' Then he washed his face and said: 'O Allah, whiten my face on the Day when faces are blackened, and do not blacken my face on the Day when faces are whitened.' Then he washed his right hand and said: 'O Allah, give me my Book in my right hand and eternity in my left hand.' Then he washed his left hand and said: 'O Allah, do not give me my Book in my left hand, nor make it tied to my neck, and I seek refuge in You from the pieces of the Fires.' Then he wiped his head and said: 'O Allah, overwhelm me with Your mercy, Your blessings, and Your forgiveness.' Then he wiped upon his feet and said: 'O Allah, firm my feet upon the Bridge on the Day when feet waver, and make my striving in what pleases You about me.' Then he turned to Muhammad and said: 'O Muhammad, whoever performs ablution like my ablution and says what I said, Allah creates for him an angel from every drop, which glorifies Him, exalts Him, proclaims His greatness, and testifies to His oneness, and records for him the reward of that.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad ibn Qays who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying, and he was narrating to the people in Makkah: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed the Fajr prayer, then sat with his companions until the sun emerged. So the man after the man arose until there did not remain with him anyone except for two men, one from the Helpers and one from Saqeeff. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them both: 'I know that there is a need for the two of you that you would like to ask about it. So if you two want I can inform both of you before you even ask me, and if you want you can both ask me yourselves about it'. They both said, 'But, inform us before we ask you about it, for that is more clarifying for the blindness, and more remote from the doubts, and more affirming for the faith'. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'As for you, O brother of Saqeeff, so you came over to ask me about your Ablution and your Prayer, what there is for you regarding that from the goodness. As for your Ablution, so you, when you place your hand into your container, then you say, 'In the Name of Allah', there scatter from it what you accumulated from the sins. So when you wash your face, the sins which your eyes had accumulated with their looks, scatter away from you and are lost. So when you wash your arms, the sins which your right hand and your left hand had accumulated, scatter away from you. So when you wipe your head and your feet, the sins which you walked towards upon your feet scatter away from you. So this is for you from your Ablution'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Ablution is half of the Faith.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sabbah Al-Hazza', from Sama'ah, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). He prayed Dhuhr and Asr in front of me, and I sat with him until Maghrib time arrived. He called for ablution (wudu) and performed ablution for the prayer, then said to me, 'Perform ablution.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I am already upon my ablution.' He said, 'Even if you are upon an ablution. Indeed, whoever performs ablution for Maghrib, that ablution is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his day, except for the major sins. And whoever performs ablution for Fajr (the morning prayer), that ablution of his is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his night, except for the major sins.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The purification upon the purity has ten Rewards.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, via his chain, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When one of you finishes his ablution, let him take a handful of water and wipe his neck with it; that will be the freedom of his neck from the Fire.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man washes (takes a ritual bath) with rose water and performs ablution with it for prayer.' He said, 'There is no problem with that.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Wahhab, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one who touches a bone of a deceased person. He said: 'If it has been a year, there is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Hamza who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When a man is sleeping in the Sacred Masjid or the Masjid of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) and he experiences nocturnal emission and is affected by major impurity, let him perform tayammum and he should not pass through the Masjid except while in tayammum until he exits from it, then he should perform ghusl. And similarly, the menstruating woman, when menstruation affects her, she should do likewise; and there is no harm if they pass through the other Masjids, but they should not sit in them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a snake that entered a container of water and exited from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you can find water other than it, so spill it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed and cleared it by blowing, so some of that blood became small pieces and hit his water container. Is it valid for him to perform wudu from it? He said: If there is nothing apparent in the water, there is no problem; but if there is something apparent, he should not perform wudu from it. He said: And I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed while he was performing wudu, so a drop dripped into his water container. Is the wudu valid from it? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Safwan, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who needed wudu for salat but could not find water; he found enough water for his wudu for one hundred or one thousand dirhams, and he had the money. Should he buy it and perform wudu, or perform tayammum? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he should buy. The like of this happened to me, so I bought and performed wudu; and the amount of money spent on that is not large.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: I asked him about the cesspool that is above the well. He said: When it is above the well, then seven cubits [must separate them]; and when it is lower than the well, then five cubits from every direction — and that is sufficient.

So he said: 'If the well is in the upper part of the valley and the valley has urine flowing in it beneath the well, and the distance between the two is three cubits or four cubits, nothing of that would make it impure. However, if it were less than that, it would make it impure. And if the well is in the lower part of the valley and the water passes by over it, and the distance between the well and it is nine cubits, it would not make it impure; and whatever is less than that, then do not perform wudu from it.' Zurara said: 'So I said to him: What if the channel of urine is directly adjacent to it and it does not settle on the ground?' So he said: 'As long as there is no stagnation for it, there is no problem with it. And if a little of it settles but it does not penetrate the ground and has no depth to reach the well, there is no problem for the well from it, so wudu may be performed from it. That ruling only applies when all of it stagnates.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj Abdullah ibn Uthman, from Qudama ibn Abi Yazid al-Hammar, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him: 'What is the minimum distance that should be between the well — the water well — and the cesspool?' So he said: 'If the ground is flat (plain), then seven cubits; and if it is rocky (mountainous), then five cubits.' Then he said: 'The water flows toward the qibla direction, to the right; and flows from the right side of the qibla toward the left side of the qibla; and flows from the left side of the qibla toward the right side of the qibla; and cannot flow from the qibla direction toward the opposite direction (behind the qibla).'

the well that happens to be five cubits from the cesspool, or less or more — can wudu be performed from it? He said: 'Its abhorrence is not due to its proximity or distance; wudu and ghusl may be performed from it as long as the water has not changed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no harm in performing wudu from (water) from which an animal whose flesh is permissible to eat has drunk.
The residue (of the water drunk by) the doves, and the chicken, there is no problem with it, and the birds (as well).

I asked him (peace be upon him): 'Can one drink the leftover water of the animals, and can one perform ablution (wudu) from it?' He said: So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the camel, and the cow, and the sheep, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), the cat is a predator, but there is no objection to its leftovers. And I would be embarrassed before God to leave food because a cat has eaten from it.'

He was asked about what the dove had drunk from. So he said: 'Everything whose flesh may be eaten — perform wudu from its residue and drink from it.' And (he was asked) about what a falcon, or a hawk, or an eagle had drunk from. So he said: 'Everything from the birds — perform wudu from what it drinks, except if you see blood in its beak. So if you see blood in its beak, do not perform wudu from it and do not drink.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a jug in which a beetle was found, having died. He said: 'Throw it out and perform wudu from it; but if it was a scorpion, then discard the water and perform wudu from other water.' And about a man who has two vessels with water, and filth fell into one of the two but he does not know which one it is, and he is unable to obtain any other water. He said: 'He should spill both out entirely and perform tayammum.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from al-Washsha, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he used to consider disliked (makruh) the residue (leftover drinking water) of every creature whose flesh may not be eaten.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Anbasa, from Abu Abdillah (AS) who said: 'Drink from the residue (su'r) of the menstruating woman, but do not perform wudu from it.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ays ibn al-Qasim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Can the man and the woman perform ghusl from one vessel?' He said: 'Yes, they should pour [water] onto their hands before placing their hands in the vessel.' He said: And I asked him about the residue of the menstruating woman, so he said: 'Do not perform wudu from it; but you may perform wudu from the residue of the sexually impure woman when she is trustworthy, then she washes her hands before entering them into the vessel.' And it was so that the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to perform ghusl, he and Aisha, from one vessel, and they would both bathe together.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman — can one drink from her residue (of water)? He said: Yes, and he cannot perform wudu from it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Can a man perform wudu from the leftover water of a woman? He said: When she knows (how to perform) the wudu. And he must not perform wudu from the residue of the menstruating woman.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the residue (of water) of the Jew and Christian, and he said: No.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Washsha, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he considered disreputable the residue of the child of fornication, and the residue of the Jew, and the Christian, and the polytheist, and everyone who opposes Islam; and the most severe of these in his view was the residue of the Nasibi.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir — from them (peace be upon them) who said: When you insert your hand into the vessel before washing it, there is no problem — except if the filth of urine or sexual impurity (janabah) has touched it. So if you insert your hand into the vessel while there is something of that on it, then pour out that water.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abd al-Karim ibn Utba who said: I asked the Shaykh about a man who wakes up from his sleep and did not urinate — can he put his hand into the vessel before washing it? He said: No, because he does not know where his hand was, so let him wash it first.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbihi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the sexually impure man (junub) who forgets and immerses his hand into a vessel before washing it: that there is no problem, provided that nothing (of the impurity) had reached his hand.
I asked him about the man who urinates and nothing (from it) touched his hand — can he immerse it in the water? He (AS) said: 'Yes, even if he was in a state of janabah (sexual impurity).'

He was asked, 'How many times should the man pour upon his hand before he enters it into the vessel?' He said: 'Once for the ritual impurity of urine, twice for faeces, and three times for sexual impurity (janaba).'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The man places the mug which he uses to scoop from the container in a dirty place, then puts it back into the container.' He said: 'He should pour out three handfuls of water, then rub the mug.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding two gutters that were flowing, one of them with urine and the other with rainwater, so they mixed together and struck the garment of a man — that would not harm him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrouq, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If two gutters were flowing, one of them being a gutter of urine and the other a gutter of water, and they mixed together, then it touches you, there would be no problem in it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Kahili, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'I pass along the road and the water from the drain flows over me at times when I know that the people are performing wudu.' He said, 'There is no problem with it. Do not ask about it.' I said, 'And the rainwater flows over me, and I see change in it and I see in it traces of filth. The drops fall on me and it splashes on me, and the house has wudu performed on its roof which drips onto our clothes.' He said, 'There is no problem with that. Do not wash it. Everything that is touched by rainwater has become pure.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from some of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the clay of the rain: that there is no problem with it contacting the garment for three days, unless it is known that something has impurified it after the rain. So if it contacts the garment after three days (of rainfall), then wash it; and if the road was clean, do not wash it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayyna, from al-Ahwal who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I come out of the toilet, then I clean myself with water, and my garment falls into that water which I had cleaned myself with.' So he said: 'There is no harm in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said regarding the sexually impure person (junub) who washes (performs ghusl), so drops of water drip from his body into the vessel, and water splashes from the ground and ends up in the vessel: 'There is no problem with this, all of it.'

Regarding the man with sexual impurity (junub) who washes (performs ghusl), and some of the water splashes back into the vessel. So he said: 'There is no problem. (Allah) has not laid upon you a hardship in the Religion [22:78].'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I perform ghusl in a bathing place where urination takes place and ghusl from janabah (sexual impurity) is also performed, and so some water splashes into the vessel from the ground.
