So he said: There is no problem with it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Udaym ibn al-Hurr who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has set a limit for women, once every month.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'if you have doubt' [65:4]. So he said: 'Whatever exceeds the month, then it is doubt.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said: A woman came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him about a woman whose bleeding is continuous, so she does not know if it is menstruation or something else. He said to her: 'The blood of menstruation is warm, thick, black, with a spurt and heat; and the blood of istihada (inter-period bleeding) is yellow, cold. So when the blood has heat, spurt, and blackness, let her leave the prayer.' He said, 'So she went out and was saying, 'By Allah! If he had been a woman, she would not have added more to this (explanation).'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all together from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The blood of istihada (inter-period bleeding) and haydh (menstruation) do not come out from one place. The blood of istihada is cold, and the blood of haydh is hot.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Is'haq ibn Jareer who said: A woman from us asked me to introduce her to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So I sought permission for her, and he granted it. She entered, and with her was her slave girl. She said to him, 'O Abu Abdullah! Regarding the Words of the Exalted: "an olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west," what is meant by this?' He said to her, 'O woman! Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not strike the example for the tree; rather, He struck the example for the children of Adam. Ask about whatever you intend.' She said, 'Inform me about the lesbian with the lesbian; what is their legal punishment (hadd) in it?' He said, 'The legal punishment (hadd) is that of adultery. Indeed, on the Day of Judgment, they will be brought, and they will be clothed in cut-outs of fire, harnessed with fire-harnesses, and dressed in fire. Columns of fire will enter their bellies up to their heads, and they will be thrown into the Fire.' 'O woman! The first people to perform this deed were the people of Lot. The men satisfied their needs with men, so the women remained without men, and so they did as their men did, satisfying each other.' She said to him, 'May Allah keep you well! What do you say regarding the woman who menstruates, and the days of her menstruation exceed the limit?' He said, 'If her menstruation is less than ten days, she examines after one day, then she is considered one with inter-period bleeding (istihada).' She said, 'Supposing the blood continues with her for the month, and the two months, and three months, how does she deal with the prayer?' He said, 'She sits for the days of her menstruation, then she performs the ritual bath (ghusl) for every two prayers.' She said to him, 'Indeed, the days of her menstruation vary for her. The menstruation might precede by a day, or two days, or three, and delay similarly. How does she know it?' He said, 'The blood of menstruation is not obscure. It is hot blood; you find a burning sensation with it. And the blood of inter-period bleeding is putrid, cold.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, and Ahmad also reported it from Muhammad ibn Aslam from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Kufi, who said: One of our companions married a young girl who had not yet menstruated. When he deflowered her, blood flowed and continued flowing without stopping for about ten days. He showed her to the midwives and those women he thought had insight, but they differed; some said this is menstrual blood, others said it is virginity blood. He asked their jurists, such as Abu Hanifa and others, who said: 'This is a matter of confusion, and prayer is an obligatory duty, so let her perform ablution and pray, and let her husband abstain from her until she sees the whiteness (cessation of blood). If it is menstrual blood, prayer will not harm her, and if it is virginity blood, she has fulfilled the obligation.' The girl did as they said, and I performed Hajj that year. When we were in Mina, I sent a message to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), saying: 'May I be your ransom, we have a question that has become burdensome to us. If you permit me, I will come to you and ask you about it.' He sent back: 'When the crowd subsides and the road is clear, come, God willing.' Khalaf said: I stayed through the night until I saw the people's movement in Mina had decreased, then I headed to his tent. When I was near, I saw a black man sitting on the road. He asked, 'Who is the man?' I said, 'A man from the pilgrims.' He asked, 'What is your name?' I said, 'Khalaf ibn Hammad.' He said, 'Enter without needing permission, for he ordered me to sit here, and when you come, I will grant you entry.' I entered, greeted, and he returned the greeting while sitting alone on his carpet, with no one else in the tent. When I stood before him, he asked me and I asked him about his state. I said to him: 'A man from your mawali married a young girl who had not yet menstruated. When he deflowered her, blood flowed and continued without stopping for about ten days. The midwives differed regarding this; some said it is menstrual blood, others said it is virginity blood. What is befitting for her to do?' He said: 'Let her fear God. If it is menstrual blood, let her abstain from prayer until she sees purity, and let her husband abstain from her. A

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ziyad ibn Suqat, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who deflowers his wife or his maid, and she sees a lot of blood that does not stop from her for a day. How should she deal with the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inserts the kursuf (cotton wool). If the cotton comes out encircled with blood, then it is from the virginity (blood of defloration). She should perform ghusl and keep a piece of cotton with her, and she should pray. But if the krusuf comes out immersed in blood, then it is from the menstruation (haydh). She should abstain from the prayer for the days of menstruation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya raised it from Aban who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A young girl from us had an ulcer in her private part, and the blood was flowing. She did not know whether it was from the blood of menstruation or from the blood of the ulcer.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Instruct her to lie down on her back, then raise her two legs, then insert her middle finger. If the blood comes out from the right side, it is from menstruation, and if it comes out from the left side, it is from the ulcer.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Husayn ibn Nu'aym Al-Sahhaf, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, the mother of my children sees blood while she is pregnant; what should she do regarding the prayer?' He said to me: 'When the pregnant woman sees blood after twenty days have passed from the time in which she used to see blood during the month in which she used to sit (abstaining from prayer), then that is not from the womb, nor is it menstruation. So let her perform ablution, insert a cloth, and pray.' And when the pregnant woman sees blood before the time she used to see it, by a little, or during the time from that month, then it is menstruation. So let her abstain from prayer for the number of days she used to sit during her menstruation. If the blood stops before that, let her perform the ritual bath and pray. But if the blood does not stop except after the days she used to see blood have passed, by a day or two, let her perform the ritual bath, then insert a cloth, seek forgiveness (for the missed prayers), and pray the noon and afternoon prayers. Then let her look. If the blood is between them (noon and afternoon) and before Maghrib, and does not flow from behind the cloth, let her perform ablution and pray at the time of every prayer as long as the cloth is not removed. If she removes the cloth and the blood flows, the ritual bath becomes obligatory upon her. And if she removes the cloth and the blood does not flow, let her perform ablution and pray, and there is no ritual bath upon her. He said: 'And if the blood, when she holds the cloth, flows from behind the cloth continuously and does not stop, then upon her is that she should perform the ritual bath three times every day and night, insert the cloth, and pray. She should perform the bath for Fajr, perform the bath for Dhuhr and Asr, and perform the bath for Maghrib and Isha.' He said: 'And similarly, the one with inter-period bleeding (Istihaazah) does that. Indeed, when she does that, Allah removes the blood from her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his men, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the pregnant woman whose pregnancy is evident; she sees what the menstruating woman sees, from the blood. He said: That is the spilling of blood. If it is much red blood, she should not pray; and if it is little yellow blood, there is nothing upon her except ablution.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the pregnant woman who sees blood just as she used to see during the days of her menstruation, regularly every month. So he said: She should refrain from the Salat just as she used to do during her menstruation. So, when she is clean, she should pray.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, altogether from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the pregnant woman who sees blood, and she is pregnant, just as she used to see before that during every month. Should she neglect the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: She should leave it when there is blood.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Fazalah ibn Ayub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about the pregnant woman who sees blood, should she leave the prayer? So he said: Yes, for the pregnant woman sometimes throws out the blood.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, does the pregnant woman sometimes menstruate?' He said, 'Yes, and that is because the child in the belly of its mother, its sustenance is the blood. So, sometimes there is excess from it, it is repelled. So when it is repelled, the Salat is Prohibited upon her.' And in another report, '(He said): When it was like that, the birth would be delayed'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The post-childbirth woman (Nufasaa) refrains from prayer during the days of her regular period which she used to observe, then she performs ghusl and acts just as the one with irregular bleeding (Mustahaadha) does.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayn, who said: I said to him, 'The wife of Abd al-Malik gave birth, so he counted for her the days of her menstruation, then he ordered her to perform ghusl and insert a cloth (for istihada), and he ordered her to wear two clean garments, and he ordered her to perform salat. She said to him, 'I do not feel comfortable entering the mosque, so let me stand outside of it and prostrate within it.' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had ordered with it, and said: When the blood ceases from the woman and she sees purity.' And Ali (peace be upon him) had ordered with this before you: 'When the blood ceases from the woman and she sees purity.' So what did your companion do? I said, 'I do not know.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, said: A woman asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and she said: 'I was sitting (abstaining from prayer) due to my post-childbirth bleeding for twenty days, until they issued a verdict for me of eighteen days.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And why did they issue a verdict for you of eighteen days?' A man said: 'Due to the hadith which is reported from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying to Asma bint Umays when she experienced post-childbirth bleeding with Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Asma asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and eighteen days had already come to her, and had she asked him before that, he would have ordered her to perform the ritual bath and do what the one with inter-period bleeding does.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to him, 'When does the post-childbirth bleeding woman (Nufasa') pray?' He said: 'She sits for the duration of her menstruation, and examines herself for two days. If the blood stops, fine; otherwise, she performs ritual bath (Ghusl), inserts a cotton pad, secures it, and prays. And if the blood exceeds the size of a cloth (Kursuf), she binds it, performs ritual bath, then prays the morning prayer with one washing, and the noon and afternoon prayers with one washing, and the evening and night prayers with one washing. And if the blood does not exceed the size of a cloth, she prays with one washing.' I said, 'And the menstruating woman?' He said: 'Similar to that, in the same way. If the blood stops from her, fine; otherwise, she is one with inter-period bleeding (Istihaza). She does the like of the post-childbirth woman, in the same way. Then she prays and does not leave the prayer in any state, for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The prayer is the pillar of your religion.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The post-partum woman sits [abstaining from prayer] for the days of her menstruation which she used to menstruate, then she examines herself, and she performs the ritual bath and prays.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The post-childbirth woman (Nafsa'a) sits for her days which she used to sit during menstruation, and she examines in two days.

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Muawiya ibn Hakim from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who had post-childbirth bleeding (nifas), so she left the prayer for thirty days, then she became clean, then she saw blood after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should leave the prayer, because her days are the days of purity, and the days of post-childbirth bleeding have passed.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a woman who had post-childbirth bleeding, so she remained as such for thirty days or more, then she was clean, and she prayed. Then she saw blood, or yellowness. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was yellowness, let her perform ghusl, and let her pray, and she should not refrain from the salat.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who is struck by labor pains for days or two days and sees yellowness or blood, he said: 'She should pray as long as she does not give birth. So if the pain overcomes her and she misses a prayer, unable to perform it due to the pain, then upon her is the making up of that prayer after she becomes clean.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who becomes clean on Friday and mentions Allah. He (peace be upon him) said: As for the purity (ghusl), then no. But she should perform ablution (wudu) during the time of prayer, then she should face the Qiblah and mention Allah.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Hammad, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The menstruating woman performs ablution when she wishes to eat, and when the time for prayer arrives, she performs ablution, faces the Qiblah, extols (says La ilaha illallah), glorifies (says Allahu Akbar), recites the Quran, and remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is befitting for the menstruating woman that she performs ablution at the time of every prayer, then she should face the Qiblah and remember Allah for the duration of what she used to pray.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the woman is in menstruation, prayer is not permissible for her, and upon her is that she performs ablution, an ablution of the prayer, at the time of every prayer. Then she sits in a clean place and remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and glorifies Him, and praises Him, and extols His holiness, equal to the duration of her prayer. Then she is free for her needs.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), I said: 'When a woman sees purity before sunset, what should she do regarding the prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she sees purity after four steps of the shadow have passed from the decline of the sun, she should not pray except Asr, because the time for Dhuhr entered upon her while she was in blood, and the time exited from her while she was in blood, so it did not become obligatory upon her to pray Dhuhr, and what Allah has dropped from her regarding the prayer while she was in blood is more.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And when the woman sees blood after four steps of the shadow have passed from the decline of the sun, let her refrain from the prayer. So when she becomes clean from the blood, let her make up the Dhuhr prayer, because the time of Dhuhr entered upon her while she was pure, and the time of Dhuhr exited from her while she was pure, so she missed the Dhuhr prayer, therefore making it up became obligatory upon her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Muammar ibn Yahya, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who becomes clean at Asr; should she pray the first [prayer]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, she should pray the prayer for which she was clean.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda, who said: When the woman sees the purity (end of menstruation) and the time of the prayer has entered upon her, then she delays the ritual bath (ghusl) until the time for another prayer enters, upon her is the making up (qada) of that prayer which she neglected. So when she becomes clean during the time of the obligation of the prayer, and she delays the prayer until the time for another prayer comes, then she sees blood, upon her is the making up of that prayer which she neglected.

Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Whichever woman sees the purity (end of menstruation) while she is able to perform the ritual bath (ghusl) during the time of a prayer, but she delays it until the time for another prayer enters, then upon her is the making up (qada) of that prayer which she delayed; and if she sees the purity during the time of a prayer, so she rises to prepare for it, and the time of that prayer passes and the time for another prayer enters, then there is no making up for it upon her, and she should pray the prayer whose time has entered.

Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu al-Ward, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the woman who is in the Dhuhr prayer and has already prayed two cycles, then she sees the blood. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should rise from her place of prayer and not make up the two cycles. And if she saw the blood while she was in the Maghrib prayer and had already prayed two cycles, let her rise from her place of prayer. Then, when she is clean, let her make up the one cycle that was missed from Maghrib.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The menstruating woman makes up the fasts and does not make up the prayers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the menstruating woman make up the prayer?' He said: 'No'. I said, 'Does she make up the fasting?' He said: 'Yes'. I said, 'From where is this derived?' He said: 'Indeed, the first one who analogized was Iblees.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla from al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Ismail al-Ju'fi who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Al-Mughira ibn Sa'id reported from you that you said to him, 'The menstruating woman makes up the prayer.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'What is the matter with him? May Allah not reconcile him. The wife of Imran vowed what was in her belly as a dedicated one, and the dedicated one for the Masjid enters it, then does not come out of it ever.' So when she gave birth to it, she said, 'My Lord, surely I have brought it forth a female – (and Allah was more Knowing of what she gave birth to) - and the male is not like the female.' So when she had given birth to her, she entered her into the Masjid. So the Prophets drew lots over her, and the vote came out for Zakariyya, and Zakariyya took the responsibility for her. Thus, she did not come out from the Masjid until she was an adult. So when she became an adult to what the women tend to reach in adulthood, she went out. So was she able upon making up for those days which she went out, and it was upon her that she would happen to be in the Masjid for ever?

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Hammad, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The menstruating woman recites the Quran and praises Allah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The menstruating woman recites the Quran, and the post-childbirth bleeding woman, and the one in major ritual impurity as well.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'b, from Abu Ubaydah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who hears the prostration (verse). He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is from the obligatory ones, let her prostrate when she hears it.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the amulet that is hung upon the menstruating woman, so he said: 'Yes, if it is inside a skin, or silver, or an iron tube.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the amulet that is hung upon the menstruating woman. He said: 'Yes, there is no problem.' He said, and he said: 'She can recite it and write it, and her hand does not touch it.' And it is reported that she does not write the Quran.
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the minimum of what occurs from the menstruation (haydh). So he said: Three (days), and its maximum is ten (days).

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The minimum of the menstruation (haydh) is three days, and the maximum is ten days.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadhl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the minimum of what menstruation (haydh) can be. So he said: Its minimum is three (days) and its maximum is ten (days).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The pure period (tuhr) cannot be less than ten days; and whatever exceeds that — the minimum of it is ten, from the time she becomes pure until she sees the blood.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The minimum of the purity (tuhr) is ten days. That is because a woman, at the beginning of her menstruation (haydh), may have abundant blood, so her menstruation may last ten days. It continually decreases as she gets older until it returns to three days. When it returns to three days, her menstruation is lifted (she reaches menopause), and it will not be less than three days. When a woman sees blood during her days of menstruation, she must leave salat. If the blood continues for three days, she is menstruating. If the blood stops after she has seen it for a day or two days, she performs ghusl and prays salat, and waits from the day she saw the blood until ten days. If she sees blood during those ten days from the day she first saw blood, for a day or two days until three days are completed for her, then what she saw at the beginning together with what she sees after that during the ten days is from menstruation. If ten days pass from the day she first saw the blood and she does not see blood, then that day and the two days when she saw it were not from menstruation; rather it was from an illness — either from an ulcer in her abdomen or from internal causes. She must repeat the salat for those two days which she had abandoned, because she was not menstruating, and it is obligatory for her to make up what she missed of salat during the day and the two days. If three days are completed for her, it is menstruation, and it is the minimum of menstruation, and make-up is not obligatory upon her. The purity will not be less than ten days. When a woman menstruates and her menstruation is five days and then the blood stops, she performs ghusl and prays salat. If she sees blood after that before ten days from the day of her purification are completed, that is from menstruation — she leaves salat. If she sees the blood secondly from when she first saw the second occurrence, completing ten days, and it continues upon her, she counts from the first blood she saw and the second — ten days — and then she is a mustahazah (one with irregular bleeding) and does what the mustahazah does. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything a woman sees during her days of menstruation — whether yellow or red — is from menstruation, and everything

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-Is ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose menstruation had ceased for years, then something returned to her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should leave the prayer until she is clean.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of our companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman who has despaired of menstruation, her limit is fifty years. And it has been reported as sixty years as well.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Tariq, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the woman reaches fifty years, she does not see red (blood) unless she is a woman from Quraish.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The limit of the one who despairs from menstruation is fifty years.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa al-Nakhhas, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). I said: 'I buy a slave girl, and she stays with me for months without menstruating, and that is not due to old age. I show her to the women, and they tell me, 'She is not pregnant.' So is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her in her private part?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Menstruation can be withheld by the wind (or windiness) without pregnancy, so there is no problem if you touch her in the private part.' I said: 'But if she is pregnant, what is for me from her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you intend so, in what is besides the private part.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'at, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I buy the slave girl, and sometimes her menstruation is withheld due to spoilage of blood or wind in the womb, so she is given medicine for that, and she menstruates from that day. Is it permissible for me to do that, while I do not know if that is from pregnancy or from something else?' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not do that'. So I said to him: 'But rather, her menstruation had been withheld from her for a month, and if that were from pregnancy, it would have been a seed like the seed of the man who isolates (ejaculates outside).' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The seed, when it falls into the womb, becomes a clot, then a chewed lump, then to whatever Allah wills; and when the seed falls into other than the womb, nothing is created from it. Therefore, do not give her the medicine when her menstruation is withheld for a month, and her usual time for menstruation has passed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a mature slave girl, and she did not menstruate with him until six months had passed, and there was no pregnancy in her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the likes of her do menstruate, and it is not due to old age, then this is a defect, and you may return her (from the acquisition).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasa', from his father who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the woman who dyes (her hair) while she is menstruating. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Does the woman dye (her hair) while she is menstruating?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sawrat ibn Kuleyb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman, should she wash her clothes which she wore during her menstruation? He (peace be upon him) said: She should wash what has been hit by the blood from her clothes, and she can leave what is besides that. I said to him (peace be upon him), And she has sweated in them. He (peace be upon him) said: The sweat is not from the menstruation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Uqba ibn Muhraz, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The menstruating woman prays in her clothes as long as blood has not touched them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said: A mother of the child of his father asked him, so she said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I would like to ask you about something but I am too embarrassed from it'. So he said: 'Ask me and do not be embarrassed'. She said, 'The blood of menstruation hit my clothes, so I washed them, but its effects did not go away'. So he said: 'Dye it with Mishq (a dye) until it gets mixed up and goes away'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When a woman sees blood before ten days (have elapsed), it is from the first menstruation (haydh); and if it was after the ten (days), it is from the next menstruation (haydh).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the woman who sees blood before her regular time of menstruation. So he said: When she sees blood before her regular time of menstruation, let her abandon salat, for perhaps the time has come early for her. So if it is more than her days in which she used to menstruate, let her wait three days after her days have passed. Then if she has waited three days and the blood has not stopped from her, let her do as the woman with istihadha does.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from whoever informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the (regular) days of a woman (of menstruation) are ten days, she does not need to examine herself (beyond them); and when they are fewer, she should examine herself.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who sees yellowness during her (menstrual) days. So he said: 'She should not pray until her days have passed; and if she sees the yellowness outside of her (regular menstrual) days, she should perform wudu and pray.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the woman who sees the yellowness: so he said: 'If it was before the menstruation by two days, then it is from the menstruation; and if it was after the menstruation by two days, then it is not from the menstruation.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'When the woman sees the yellowness before the passing of her numbered days (of menstruation), she should not pray (salat); and if the yellowness was after the passing of her days of purity, she should pray (salat).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamza who said: Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) was asked — and I was present — about the woman who sees the yellowness (sufra). So he said: 'Whatever occurred before the menstruation (haydh) is part of the menstruation, and whatever occurred after the menstruation is not part of it.'

He said: The yellowness two days before the menstruation is from the menstruation; and after the days of menstruation it is not from the menstruation; and it during the days of menstruation is menstruation.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a ibn Mihran who said: I asked him about the virgin girl menstruating for the first time, when she sits (menstruating) during one month for two days, and during another month for three days, and it varies for her — her menstruation not occurring during the month with the same number of days. He said: For her is that she sits (in menstruation) and leaves the salat as long as she continues to see the blood, as long as she does not exceed ten (days). So when two months coincide with the same number of days, then those are her (regular) days.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman sees blood for three or four days.' He said: 'She should leave the salat.' I said: 'Suppose she sees purity for three or four days.' He said: 'She should pray.' I said: 'Suppose she sees blood for three or four days.' He said: 'She should leave the salat.' I said: 'Suppose she sees purity for three or four days.' He said: 'She should pray.' I said: 'Suppose she sees blood for three or four days.' He said: 'She should leave the salat. She should keep doing so for what is between her and a month. When the blood stops from her (all is well), otherwise she is at the status of the woman with istihadha.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad raising it (marfu'), from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about a girl who menstruated for the first time, and her bleeding continued for three months while she did not know the days of her menstrual cycles. So he said: Her menstrual cycles are like the menstrual cycles of her womenfolk. If her womenfolk have different (cycles), then the maximum she waits is ten days, and the minimum is three days.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar and others, from Yunus, from whoever narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a woman from whom the blood had stopped, and she did not know whether she had become pure or not. He said: She stands upright and presses her abdomen against a wall, inserts a white piece of cotton, and raises her right leg. So if there comes out upon the tip of the cotton something like the head of a fly of fresh blood, she has not yet become pure. But if nothing comes out, then she has indeed become pure — she should perform ghusl and pray.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'When the menstruating woman intends to perform ghusl, let her insert a piece of cotton. If something of blood comes out in it, she should not perform ghusl; but if she sees nothing, let her perform ghusl. And if she sees yellowness after that, let her perform wudu and pray.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibn Muskan, from Shurahbil al-Kindi, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), he said: I said: 'How would the menstruating woman know that she has become pure?' He said: 'She should lean her left leg against the wall, and insert the cotton with her right hand. If there was something the like of the head of a fly that came out upon the cotton, (she is still menstruating).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — it reached him that women, one of them would call for a lantern in the depths of the night to examine whether the menstrual blood had ceased; so he would censure this and say: 'When have women ever done this?'
he used to forbid women from examining themselves regarding menstruation (haydh) at night, and he would say: 'Indeed, it may turn out to be yellowness (sufra) or turbidity (kudra).'

I asked Abu al-Hasan the last (peace be upon him) and I said to him: The daughter of Shihab observes the days of her menstrual period, but when she performs the ritual bath (ghusl), she sees drop after drop (of blood). He (the narrator) said: So he (the Imam) said: 'Instruct her to stand at the base of the wall just as a dog stands, then have a woman press firmly between her hips with an intense pressing, for indeed it is only something that remains in the womb called al-Iraqah, and it will all come out.' Then he said: 'Do not inform women about this and similar things, and leave them with their impure ailment.' He (the narrator) said: So I did to the woman what he had said, and it ceased from her, and the blood did not return to her until she died.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The women today have innovated a style of combing — one of them deliberately takes the woolly hair braids which the hairdresser weaves together with the hair, then stuffs it with aromatic herbs, then places a thin cloth over it, then sews it with a needle, then places it on her head — then she is afflicted with sexual impurity. So he said: The women of former times would only comb the front part of their hair. So when the ritual bath (ghusl) befell them due to impurity, instruct her to soak her head thoroughly with water and squeeze it until it is saturated. When it is saturated, there is no problem for her. He said: I said, 'So what about the menstruating woman?' He said: She must fully undo the hairstyle.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Hasan al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The menstruating woman should perform ghusl with nine ratls of water.

Ali ibn Muhammad and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubayda who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who sees signs of purity while she is on a journey, and she does not have with her enough water for her ghusl, and the time for salat has come. He said: 'If she has with her enough water to wash her private part, then she should wash it, then perform tayammum and pray.' I said: 'Can her husband come to her (conjugally) in that state?' He said: 'Yes. If she has washed her private part and performed tayammum, there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The menstruating woman — whatever moisture of the water reaches from her hair, would suffice her.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the menstruating woman who washes herself (performs ghusl) while saffron remains on her body that the water has not removed. He said: There is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman who copulates with her husband and then she menstruates while she is in the bathroom — should she perform ghusl or not? He said: 'That which invalidates salat has come to her, so she does not need to perform ghusl.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman who menstruates while she is in a state of janabah — is a ghusl for janabah required of her? He said: The ghusl for janabah and the menstruation (haydh) is one.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The woman sees the blood while she is in a state of janabah. Should she perform ghusl from the janabah, or [is it] the ghusl of janabah and haydh [together]?' So he said: 'There has come to her what is greater than that.'

The one with istihaaza observes her [menstrual] days, so she neither prays during them, nor does her husband approach her. When her days pass and she sees the blood soaking through the cotton pad, she performs ghusl for Zuhr and Asr, delaying the Asr and hastening the Zuhr; and for Maghrib and Isha she performs a ghusl, delaying the Isha and hastening the Maghrib; and she performs ghusl for Fajr. She inserts a cloth and ties it like a loincloth, and she does not give the greeting of peace (salam). She presses her thighs together [with the lower part of her body] in the mosque while the rest of her body is outside; and her husband does not approach her during her days of purity (tuhr). But if the blood does not soak through the cotton pad, she performs wudu, enters the mosque, and prays each prayer with a [fresh] wudu; and this type of woman—her husband may approach her except during her days of haydh (menstruation).

I asked him about the woman who has istihadha, so he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was asked about the woman with istihadha, so he commanded her to wait during the days of her haydh, not praying during them, then to perform ghusl and insert cotton and use a cloth as a belt, then to pray until the blood comes through the cloth. He said: The bleeding woman performs ghusl between every two prayers, and the istidh-far is that she applies perfume and burns incense with dukhnah and other things, and the istithfar is that she fashions something like the breech strap of an animal.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a who said: The woman with istihadha — if the blood seeps through the cotton pad, she should perform ghusl for every two prayers, and a ghusl for al-Fajr; and if the blood does not exceed the cotton pad, then upon her is ghusl once every day and wudu for every prayer. And if her husband wishes to be intimate with her, then it should be at the time when she performs ghusl. This applies if her blood is fresh (dark red); but if it is yellowish, then upon her is only the wudu.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman with istihaaza (inter-period bleeding) performs ghusl at the time of the Dhuhr prayer, then she prays Dhuhr and Asr. Then she performs ghusl at Maghrib, and prays Maghrib and Isha. Then she performs ghusl at the morning prayer and prays Fajr. And there is no problem for her husband to come to her whenever he wishes, except during the days of her menstruation (haydh), when her husband must abstain from her. He said: And he (the Imam) said: No woman does this at all — seeking divine reward (ihtisab) — except that she would be cured of that condition.

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! When a woman waits for ten days and sees the blood, then she becomes clean and she waits for three days in a state of purity, then she sees the blood after that — should she withhold from the salat?' He said: 'No. This is a woman with istihadha (irregular bleeding). She should perform ghusl, insert cotton pad after cotton pad, combine the two prayers with one ghusl, and her husband may come to her if he so wishes.'

I asked him about the woman who menstruates and then the time of her purity passes while she still sees blood. So he said: She should wait cautiously for one day, if her menstruation is less than ten days. If the blood continues, then she is a mustahadha (woman with istihaaza). If the blood stops, she should perform ghusl and pray. He said: I said to him, 'What about the woman whose menstruation is seven or eight days, her cycle being constant and regular, then she menstruates for three days, then the blood stops and she sees whiteness — neither yellowness nor blood?' He said: 'She should perform ghusl and pray.' I said, 'She performs ghusl, prays, and fasts, then the blood returns?' He said: 'When she sees blood, she should withhold from salat and fasting.' I said, 'What if she sees blood one day and is pure the next day?' He said: 'When she sees blood, she should withhold; when she sees purity, she should pray. When the days of her menstruation have passed and purity continues with her, she should pray. Then if she sees blood, she is a mustahadha. I have laid out all of her matters for you completely.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from one who narrated to him, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The people used to die arbitrarily. So when the era of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came, he said: 'O my Lord! Appoint for death a cause by which the deceased shall be rewarded and by which the bereaved shall be consoled.' He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down serious illness (al-mum), which is pleurisy (al-birsam). Then He sent down the cure after it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The people used to die arbitrarily (without apparent cause), so Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'O my Lord, if only You would appoint a cause for death, by which it could be recognized, and the afflicted could be consoled.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the serious illness — and it is the pleurisy — then He sent down the cure after it.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Fever is the harbinger of death, and it is the prison of Allah in the earth, and it is the believer's share from the Fire.'

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Prophet Dawood (peace be upon him) passed away suddenly on Saturday, so the birds shaded him with their wings; and Musa, the Speaker with God (peace be upon him), passed away in the wilderness, so a shrieker cried out from the sky: 'Musa (peace be upon him) has died — and which soul will not die?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jamila, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'Verily, sudden death is a lightening for the believer and a regrettable seizing of the disbeliever.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad or someone else, from Ali ibn Hadid, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: 'Most of those who die from among our followers (die) from rapid abdominal illness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from a shaykh of our companions known by the teknonym Abu Abdillah, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Fever is the harbinger of death, the prison of God the Exalted in His earth, and its outburst is from Hell, and it is the share of every believer from the Fire.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is tried with every trial and dies with every (type of) death, except that he does not kill himself.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the death of the believer. So he said: 'The believer dies with every (type of) death — dying by drowning, and dying by being crushed (under a structure), and afflicted by predatory wild animals, and dying by thunderbolt — but it does not strike one who remembers Allah the Exalted.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Uthman al-Nawwa, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicts the believer with every affliction and causes him to die with every death, but He does not afflict him with the loss of his intellect. Do you not see how Ayoub (peace be upon him) was afflicted? How Iblees was given power over his wealth, his children, his family, and everything belonging to him, but was not given power over his intellect? He left for him that which he could use to affirm the Oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Zareeh, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Saeed Al-Khudry was from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he was straightforward/upright, but he was in agony/died for three days. So his family washed him, then he was carried to his prayer-mat, and he died in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When death becomes difficult for the dying one and his soul is being snatched away, he should be brought closer to his prayer-mat upon which he used to pray.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: When the snatching (of the soul) becomes difficult upon him, place him on his prayer-mat in which he used to pray, or on it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Aban, from Lays al-Muradi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah had granted Abu Sa'id al-Khudri this insight (or judgment), and his soul's extraction (death pangs) had become severe for him. So he said, 'Carry me to my prayer-mat.' So they carried him, and he did not long remain before he died.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim al-Sha'iri and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding directing the deceased, you face his face towards the Qiblah and place his feet towards what follows the Qiblah.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Face the Qiblah with the underside of his feet.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When one of you has a deceased person, shroud him facing the Qiblah; and similarly, when he is washed, a place for the washing is dug for him facing the Qiblah, so that he faces it with the soles of his feet and his face towards the Qiblah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Uqba! Allah will not accept from the servants on the Day of Resurrection except this matter which you are upon. And there is nothing between one of you and seeing what delights his eyes except that his soul reaches to this,' and he gestured with his hand to the jugular vein, then reclined. And Mualla was with me, so he nudged me to ask him. I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! When his soul reaches to this, what does he see?' I asked him 'What?' about ten times, and he said in all of them, 'He sees,' and did not add more to it. Then he sat up at the end and said, 'O Uqba!' I said, 'At your service and happiness!' He said, 'Did you refuse except that I teach you?' I said, 'Yes, O son of the Messenger of Allah! My religion is with your religion. So when my religion departs, how will it be for me with you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, every moment?' And I cried, so he was sympathetic to me and said, 'He sees them both, by Allah.' I said, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! Who are they?' He said, 'That is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him). O Uqba! A believing soul will never die until it sees them both.' I said, 'So when the believer looks at them both, does he return to the world?' He said, 'No, he goes ahead when he looks at them in front of him.' I said to him, 'Do they say anything?' He said, 'Yes. They both enter upon the believer together, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sits at his head, and Ali (peace be upon him) at his feet.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) leans over him and says, 'O friend of Allah! Receive glad tidings. I am the Messenger of Allah. I am better for you than what you left of the world.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rises, and Ali (peace be upon him) stands until he leans over him and says, 'O friend of Allah! Receive glad tidings. I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, whom you used to love. Indeed, I shall benefit you.' Then he said, 'Indeed, this is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' I said, 'Where did Allah place me, may I be your ransom, in the Book of Allah?' He said, 'In Surah Yunus.' The words of Allah, Mighty and

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Khalid ibn 'Umara, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the barrier is placed between him and speech, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) comes to him, and whomever Allah wills. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sits on his right, and the other one on his left. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says to him: 'As for what you hoped for, it is before you, and as for what you feared from it, you have been made safe from it.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and they say: 'This is your dwelling place in Paradise. If you wish, we can return you to the world, and for you there will be gold and silver therein.' He says: 'I have no need of the world.' At that, his color whitens, his forehead sweats, his lips contract, his nostrils spread, and his left eye sheds tears. Whichever of these signs you see, suffice with it. When the soul exits the body, it is presented to it just as it was presented to him while in the body, and it chooses the Hereafter. He is washed among those who wash him, and turned over among those who turn him over. When he is enshrouded in his kafans and placed on his bed, his soul comes out walking in front of the people. The souls of the believers meet him, greet him, and give him glad tidings of what Allah, Exalted is His Praise, has prepared for him from the bounties. When he is placed in his grave, the soul is returned to him up to his hips. Then he is asked about what he knows. When he provides what he knows, that door which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) showed him is opened for him, and its light, brightness, coolness, and fragrant breeze enter upon him. He said: I said, 'May I be your ransom, where is the squeezing of the grave?' He said: 'Far be it! There is no squeezing upon the believers from it. By Allah, this earth (of the believer) boasts over that earth (of the disbeliever), saying: 'A believer trod upon my back, and a believer did not tread upon you.' And the earth says to it: 'By Allah, I used to love you when you were walking upon my back. But when I am made to love you, you shall soon know what I will do with you.' So it expands for him to the extent of his vision.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Abd al-Rahim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Salih ibn Maysam narrated to me from Abayah Al-Asadi, that he heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, no servant will hate me forever and die upon that hatred, except that he will see me at his death in the place he dislikes; and no servant will love me forever and die upon that love, except that he will see me at his death in the place he loves.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) upon his right.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Yahya ibn Sabur, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the deceased: his eye sheds tears at the time of death. He said: That is when he sees the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he sees what pleases him. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Do you not see the man who sees what pleases him and what he loves, so his eye sheds tears because of that, and he laughs?

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aamir ibn Abdullah ibn Juz'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the soul reaches the throat, an angel comes to him and says to him: O you, or O so-and-so! As for what you were hoping for, then despair of it, and that is the return to the world; and as for what you were fearing, then you are secured from it.'

Aban ibn Uthman from Uqba that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, when the soul of a man reaches his chest, he sees. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what does he see?' He said, 'He sees the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of Allah says to him: I am the Messenger of Allah, receive glad tidings.' Then he sees Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and he says: I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, whom you used to love. Your love will benefit you today. He said, I said to him, 'Can it be that one of the people sees this and then returns to the world?' He said, 'No. When he sees this, he dies forever, and that is a great thing.' And that is in the Quran, the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who believed and were righteous. For them is good news in the life of the world and in the Hereafter; there is no changing the Words of Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said: Khattab al-Juhani used to mix with us and was extremely hostile to the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), and he was a companion of Najdat al-Haruriyya. I said: So I visited him to recover from the mixing and dissimulation, and behold, he was unconscious at the threshold of death. I heard him saying: 'What is the matter with me and you, O Ali?' So I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He saw him, by the Lord of the Ka'bah! He saw him, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwaz said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the soul of one of you reaches this (point), it is said to him: As for what you were cautious of from the worries of the world and its grief, so you are safe from it'; and it is said to him: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and 'Ali (peace be upon him) and Fatima (peace be upon her) are in front of you'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sign of the Believer when death approaches him is that his face whitens more intensely than the whiteness of his skin, his forehead sweats, and water flows from his eyes like the appearance of tears, so that is the exit of his soul; and for the Infidel, his soul exits like a pull from his jaw, like the foam of a camel, or just as the soul of a camel exits.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, altogether, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Samad ibn Basheer, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'May Allah keep you well. The one who loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and the one who hates meeting Allah, Allah hates to meet him.' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'By Allah, we indeed dislike death.' So he said: 'That is not where you are going with it. Rather, that is at the time of witnessing (death), when he sees what he loves, so there is nothing more beloved to him than proceeding (to meet Allah), and Allah the Exalted loves to meet him, and he loves to meet Allah at that time. And when he sees what he dislikes, so there is nothing more hateful to him than meeting Allah, and Allah hates to meet him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Mustahil, from Muhammad ibn Hanzala, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you, a hadith that I heard from some of your Shia and your Mawalis, reporting it from your father.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?' I said: 'They claimed that he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The most fortunate state for a man is what we are upon, when the soul is in this (world).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' When that is the case, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) comes to him, and Ali (peace be upon him) comes to him, and Jibraeel (peace be upon him) comes to him, and the Angel of Death (peace be upon him) comes to him. So that Angel says to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Indeed, so-and-so was a follower (Mawali) of you and of your Ahl al-Bayt.' He (peace be upon him) says: 'Yes, he used to have affinity with us and disavow our enemies.' So the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) says that to Jibraeel, and Jibraeel raises that report to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

And from him, from Safwan, from Jaroud ibn al-Munthir, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the soul of one of you reaches this (point)', and he gestured with his hand to his throat, his eyes would be delighted (i.e., he would die with a good ending).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Idrees al-Qummi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands the Angel of Death, so he returns the soul of the Believer to ease it upon him, and extracts it from the best of its states. The people say, 'Death was severe upon so-and-so,' but that is an easing from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon him. And He says: It is turned away from him (the severity) if he is one upon whom Allah is pleased, or one whom Allah loves his affair, that He does not pull the pull with the like of the skewer of wet wool. So the people say, 'Allah has eased death for so-and-so.'

From him, from Yunus, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) visited a man from his companions who was expiring, and he said: 'O Angel of Death, be kind to my companion, for he is a believer.' He said: 'Receive glad tidings, O Muhammad, for I am kind with every believer. And know, O Muhammad, that when I capture the soul of a son of Adam, his family panics. So I stand in a corner of their house and say: 'What is this panic? By Allah, we did not hasten it before its appointed term, nor is there any sin for us in its capture.' So if you are considerate and patient, you will be rewarded; and if you panic, you will sin and be burdened. And know that we have a return upon you, then another return. So beware, beware. There is no family in the east or west, of tents or of houses, except that I scan them five times a day. And I am more knowing of their young and their old than they are of themselves. And if I wanted to capture the soul of a gnat, I would not have the power over it until my Lord commands me to do so. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He only scans them during the times of prayer. So if he is among those who are regular in it at its times, he teaches him the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Angel of Death drives Iblis away from him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) attended a man from the Ansar, and he had a good status with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So he attended him at his death, and he looked at the Angel of Death at his head, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Be kind to my companion, for he is a believer.' So the Angel of Death said to him: 'O Muhammad, be pleased with yourself and delight the eyes, for I am kind and compassionate with every believer. And know, O Muhammad, that I am present with the son of Adam at the capture of his soul. So when I capture it, a crier from his family cries out at that time. So I stand aside by the side of the house, and with me is his soul, and I say to them: 'By Allah, we have not oppressed him, nor have we preceded his term, nor have we hastened his decree, and there was no sin for us in capturing his soul.' So if you are pleased with what Allah has done with him and you are patient, you will be rewarded and praised; and if you panic and are angry, you will sin and be burdened, and there is no criticism for you against us. And indeed, for us with you as well, is a remainder and a return. So beware, beware. And there is no family of those living in cities or in the desert, in land or in sea, except that I scan them five times every day at the times of prayer, until I am more knowing of them than they are of themselves. And if I, O Muhammad, wanted to capture the soul of a fly, I would not have the ability to capture it until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the One who commands its capture. And I prompt the believer at his death with the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn Al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people! I do not want to find a man who has a deceased person and waits with him until morning, nor a man who has a deceased person during the day and waits with him until night. Do not wait with your dead for the sunrise or the sunset. Hasten them to their resting places. May Allah have mercy on you.' So the people said, 'And you, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Yaqubi, from Musa ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Muyassar, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the deceased dies at the beginning of the day, he does not spend the afternoon (or night) except in his grave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you intend to wash the deceased, place a cloth between you and him to cover his private part from you, whether it is a shirt or something else. Then begin with his hands and his head, washing them three times with lotus leaves, then the rest of his body, and begin with his right side. When you intend to wash his private part, take a clean rag and wrap it around your left hand, then insert your hand from beneath the cloth that is on the deceased's private part, and wash it without seeing his nakedness. When you finish washing him with lotus leaves, wash him again with water and camphor, and something of his perfume. Then wash him with pure water with another washing, until when you have finished the three (washings), place him in a cloth, then dry him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about washing the deceased, so he said: 'Wash him with water and lotus (leaves). Then wash him upon the footsteps of that with another washing with water and camphor and fragrant powder if there was, and wash him for the third washing with clear water.' I said, 'Three washings for his body, all of it?' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'There would happen to be a cloth upon him when he is washed?' He said: 'If there is capacity that there happens to be a shirt upon him, so wash him from beneath it.' And he said: 'I would love it for the one who washes the deceased if he wraps a rag upon his hand when he washes him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The deceased is washed with three washings: once with lotus, once with water in which camphor is placed, and once more with clear water. Then he is enshrouded.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, my father wrote in his bequest that I should enshroud him in three garments: one of them being a cloak of his as a veil, and another cloth, and a shirt.' I said, 'And why did he write this?' He said: 'Out of fear of the words of the people.' And we bound him after that with a turban, and we cleaved the ground for him because he was hefty, and he ordered me to raise the grave from the ground by four spread fingers.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah al-Kahili, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about washing the deceased, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Face the undersoles of his feet towards the Qiblah until his face is facing the Qiblah. Then soften his joints, and if it is not possible for you, then leave it. Then begin with his private part with water of lotus and potash, so wash him with three washings, and use plenty of water, and wipe his belly with a gentle wiping.' Then turn to his head and begin with his right side from his beard and his head. Then do the same with his left side from his head, and his beard, and his face, and wash him with gentleness, and beware of roughness, and wash him with a gentle washing. Then lie him down upon his left side for the right side to be exposed to you. Then wash him from his head to his feet and wipe your hand upon his back and his belly with three washings. Then return him to his right side until the left side is exposed to you, so wash what is between his head and his feet, and wipe your hand upon his back and his belly with three washings. Then return him to his back and begin with his private part with water of camphor. Do as you did the first time, wash him with three washings with water of camphor and potash, and wipe your hand upon his belly with a gentle wiping. Then turn to his head and do as you did first, with his beard from both its sides, and his head, and his face, with water of camphor with three washings. Then return him to the left side until the right side is exposed to you, so wash him from his head to his feet with three washings. Then return him to the right side until the left side is exposed to you, so wash him from his head to his feet with three washings. And insert your hand under his shoulders and his forearms, and make the forearm and the palm, along with his side, clean. Every time you wash anything from it, insert your hand under his shoulder and in the inside of his forearms. Then return him to his back, then wash him with clear water just as you did at first, beginning with the private part. Then turn to the head and the beard and the face until you do just as you did first with clear water. Then put on a loin cloth on him with a cloth and place the cotton to be under it to pad him with a lot of cotton. Then tighten his thighs upon the cotton with the cloth with

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his men, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), who said: When you intend to wash the deceased, place him on the washing place facing the Qiblah. If he is wearing a shirt, remove his hand from the shirt, gather the shirt over his private part, and raise it from his feet to above the knees. If he is not wearing a shirt, cast a cloth over his private part. Proceed to the sidr (lotus) leaves, place them in a basin, pour water over them, and strike them with your hand until the foam rises. Isolate the foam into a container, and pour the remaining water into the jug containing the water. Then wash his hands three times, just as a person washes from major impurity, up to the half of the forearm. Then wash his private part and clean it. Then wash his head with the foam, being thorough in that, and strive that water does not enter his nostrils and ears. Then lay him on his left side and pour water from half his head to his feet three times, and rub his body gently, and similarly his back and belly. Then lay him on his right side and do the same with him. Then pour out that water from the jug and wash the jug with clear water, and wash your hands up to the elbows. Then pour water into the vessels and add camphor grains to it. Do with him as you did in the first time, starting with his hands, then his private part, and wipe his belly gently. If anything comes out, clean it. Then wash his head. Then lay him on his left side and wash his right side, back, and belly. Then lay him on his right side and wash his left side, just as you did the first time. Then wash your hands up to the elbows and the vessels, and pour clear water into them, and wash him with clear water as you washed him in the first two times. Then dry him with a clean cloth. Proceed to cotton, sprinkle some musk/perfume on it, and place it on his private part, front and back. Pack the cotton in his anus so that nothing comes out from him. Take a long cloth, one span wide, tie it from his loins, and bind his thighs tightly, wrapping it around his thighs. Then bring its end out from under his feet to the right side, and insert it into the place where you wrapped the cloth. The cloth should be long, wrapping his thighs from his loins to his knees with a tight wrap.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the deceased, 'Can he be washed in the open?' He said: 'There is no problem, and if he were to be veiled with a curtain, it is more beloved to me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his men, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), said: Regarding the embalming of the deceased and his enshrouding, he said: Spread the wrapping cloth, then spread the loincloth upon it, then spread the shirt upon it and fold the front of the shirt over it. Then take camphor powder and place it on his forehead, the place of his prostration, and wipe the camphor over all his joints, from his head to his feet, and in his head, neck, shoulders, elbows, and in every joint of his hands and legs, and in the middle of his palms. Then he is carried and placed upon his shirt, and the front of the shirt is folded over him, and the shirt should be without hemming or buttons.
