Two pieces of fresh palm stalks, each the length of an arm's span, are made for him: one is placed between his knees, half towards the shin and half towards the thigh, and the other is placed under his right armpit. Cotton or camphor is not placed in his nostrils, eyes, ears, or upon his face. Then he is turbaned: the middle of the turban is taken and wrapped around his head in circles. The excess of the right side is cast over the left, and the left over the right, then it is extended over his chest.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), by what he was enshrouded? He said: 'In three garments, two Suhari cloths and one Burd Hibernah garment.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enshroud the deceased, scatter upon every cloth something from the fragrant powder and camphor.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you wish to embalm the deceased, apply camphor to him, wiping with it the marks of prostration on his body, all his joints, his head, his beard, and upon his chest with the embalming mixture. And he (peace be upon him) said: The embalming of the man and the woman is the same. And he (peace be upon him) said: And I dislike that it be followed by the (smoke of) incense burning.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: We said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Is the turban part of the shroud for the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, the obligatory shroud is three garments and a complete garment, not less than that, which covers his entire body. So whatever increases beyond that is Sunnah, up to reaching five garments. So whatever increases beyond that is an innovation (bid'ah). And the turban is Sunnah.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ordered with the turban, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was turbaned.' And the Sheikh, Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), sent to us a dinar when Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hazza' died, while we were in Medina, and ordered us to buy him embalming material (hanut) and a turban, so we did it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The deceased is enshrouded in three (pieces of cloth), besides the turban and the cloth with which he ties his hips so that nothing of him is exposed; and the cloth and the turban are essential, but they are not part of the shroud.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father wrote in his bequest that I should enshroud him in three garments: one of them is a cloak of his which he used to pray in on Friday, and another garment, and a shirt. So I said to my father, 'Why do you write this?' He said, 'I fear that the people might overpower you, and if they say, 'Enshroud him in four or five,' do not do it. And wrap me with a turban, and do not count the turban as part of the enshrouding; rather, what is counted is what the body is wrapped with.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Usman Al Nawa’a who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I tend to wash the dead bodies'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And you are good (at it)?' I said, 'I wash'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you wash, so be gentle with it and neither press it nor touch its ears with camphor; and when you turban him, so do not turban him the turbanning of the Bedouins'. I said, 'How should I do (it)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Take the turban from its middle and display is upon his head, then turn it to its behind, and drop its two ends upon his chest'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How should I deal with the shroud?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Take a cloth and tighten it upon his seat and his legs.' I said, 'So (what about) the loincloth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not count as anything. Rather, you do so to secure what is there, lest something might come out from it, and what is made of cotton is superior to it. Then the shirt is torn when washed and removed from his legs.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then the shrouding shirt should be without buttons and hemming, and a turban is what his head is wrapped with, and its extra ends are returned upon his legs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the turban for the deceased. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Wrap it (around his head).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The deceased is enshrouded in five garments: a shirt with no buttons on it, a loincloth, a cloth with which his middle is bound, a cloak in which he is wrapped, and a turban with which he is turbaned, and its excess is cast upon his chest.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The camphor, it is the embalming material.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me regarding the shroud of Abu Ubayda al-Hazza': 'Indeed, the embalming material is camphor, but go and do as the people do.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' died while I was in Medina, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent me a dinar and said: 'Buy embalming material with this, and know that the embalming material is camphor, but do as the people do.' He said: 'So when I went, he followed me with a dinar and said: 'Buy camphor with this.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the embalming (hanut) for the deceased. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Place it in his prayer places (prostration spots).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade placing the embalming material (camphor) upon the coffin.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) raised his head towards the sky and smiled. So it was said to him: 'O Messenger of God! We saw you raise your head towards the sky and smile.' He said: 'Yes. I was astounded at two angels who had descended from the sky to the earth, seeking a righteous believing servant in a prayer place where he used to pray, in order to record his deeds for his day and his night. But they did not find him in his prayer place, so they ascended to the sky. And they said: 'Our Lord! Your believing servant, so-and-so — we sought him in his prayer place to record his deeds for his day and his night, but we did not find him, and we found him in Your ropes (held by illness).' So God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Record for My servant the likes of what he used to do in his well-being, from the goodness during his day and his night, for as long as he remains in My ropes; for it is upon Me to record for him the reward of what he used to do in his well-being, when I have held him back from it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the Muslim is overcome by the weakness of old age, God, Mighty and Majestic, commands the angel to record for him in that state of his the like of what he used to do when he was young, energetic, and healthy.' And similarly when he falls ill, God assigns an angel to him who writes for him during his illness what he used to do of the good in his good health, until God raises him and takes him (death). And similar to that is the disbeliever: when he is afflicted with sickness in his body, God writes for him what he used to do of evil in his good health.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: God Mighty and Majestic says to the angel assigned to the believer when he falls ill: 'Write for him what you used to write for him during his good health, for it is I who have placed him in My bonds (of illness).'
Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Sabbah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Staying awake one night due to illness is superior to a year of worship.'

When the two angels of the sick servant ascend to the sky every evening, the Lord — Blessed and Exalted — says: 'What have the two of you written for My servant during his illness?' So they say: 'Complaints.' So He says: 'It would not be just of Me toward My servant if I were to imprison him in one of My prisons and then forbid him from complaining.' Then He says: 'Write for My servant the like of what you two used to write for him in goodness during his health, and do not record against him any sin until I release him from My prison, for he is indeed in a prison from My prisons.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust, from Zurara, from one of the two of them (peace be upon them both) who said: Staying awake at night due to illness or pain is superior and greater in reward than a year of worship.

From him, from Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dorost, who said: I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saying: When the believer falls ill, God — Mighty and Majestic — reveals unto the companion (Angel) on the left hand side: 'Do not write any sin against My servant for as long as he is in My prison and My fetters'; and He reveals unto the companion (Angel) of the right hand side: 'Write for My servant what you would have written for him during his good health, from the good deeds.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Hajjaj, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The body becomes insolent when it does not fall ill, and there is no goodness in a body that does not experience illness to humble it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Fever for a night equates to worship for a year, and fever for two nights equates to worship for two years, and fever for three (nights) equates to worship for seventy years. He (the narrator) said: I said, 'What if he does not reach seventy years (of age)?' He said: 'Then it is for his mother and his father.' I said, 'What if they both do not reach (that)?' He said: 'Then it is for his relatives.' I said, 'What if his relatives do not reach (that)?' He said: 'Then it is for his neighbours.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Fever for a night is an expiation for what is before it and what is after it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding in how many garments the woman is shrouded. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is shrouded in five garments, one of them being the headscarf.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, raising it (to the Imam), said: I asked him about how the woman would be enshrouded. So he said: 'Just as the man would be enshrouded, apart from that a cloth would be tightened upon her breasts to press the breasts upon the chest and it would be tightened upon her back, and the cotton (padding) would be done for her more than what would be done for the man, and stuffing the front and the back with the cotton and the embalming (camphor), then the cloth would be tightened upon her with an intense tightening'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalat, from Qasim ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The man is enshrouded in three garments, and the woman, if she is large, in five: a shirt, a loincloth, a veil, and two wrappings.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The shroud is not perfumed with incense.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Water is not heated for the deceased, nor is fire hastened for him, nor is he embalmed with musk.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade following a funeral with an incense burner.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Get the best shrouds for your dead ones, for these are their adornments.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Jameela, from Jabir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is nothing better from your apparels than the white, therefore clothe your dead ones (in white)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from one of his companions, who said: It is recommended that there be in his shroud a garment in which he used to pray, clean, for that is recommended: that he be shrouded in what he used to pray in.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ibn Fazzal, from Marwan, from Abdul Malik, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought something from the covering of the Ka'bah. He fulfilled his need with part of it, and part remained in his hand. Is it permissible for him to sell it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He sells what he wishes, and gifts what he does not wish, and benefits from it, and seeks its blessings.' I said: 'Can the deceased be shrouded with it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Be choosy regarding the shrouds, for you will be resurrected in them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Flax (linen) was for the Children of Israel, they were enshrouded with it, and cotton is for the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Saeed, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'I shrouded my father in two Egyptian cloaks (shatwayn) which he used to wear as Ihram, and in a shirt from his shirts, and a turban that belonged to Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and in a cloak which I bought for forty dinars. If it were today, it would equal four hundred dinars.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from the one who reported it, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) enshrouded Usamah ibn Zayd in a red cloak of Hibrah, and that Ali (peace be upon him) enshrouded Sahl ibn Hunayf in a red cloak of Hibrah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The shroud should be Burda (fabric); if it is not Burda, then make it all cotton. If you do not find a cotton turban, then make the turban Sabiriyya (fabric).
Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from al-Washsha, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The deceased is not to be shrouded in black.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Rashid, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about clothes made in Basra according to the Yemenite style, from silk and cotton. Is it permissible for the deceased to be enshrouded in them? He (peace be upon him) said: If the cotton is more than the silk, then there is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! When I die, wash me with seven buckets from the well of Ghars.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya said, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the water with which the deceased is washed, asking: 'What is its limit?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'The limit of washing the deceased is that he is washed until he becomes clean, if Allah wills.' He said: And he wrote to him: 'Is it permissible that the deceased is washed and the water poured upon him enters into a cesspool well, or that a man performs the ablution for prayer and the water of his ablution is poured into a cesspool?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'That will end up in the cesspools.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it (to the Imam), said: The Sunnah regarding the embalming (camphor) is thirteen dirhams and a third, at most. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) descended unto the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with embalming, and its weight was forty dirhams. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) divided it into three parts: a part for himself, a part for Ali, and a part for Fatima (peace be upon her).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The least amount that suffices from the camphor for the deceased is one misqal. And in the narration of Al-Kahili and Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: The moderate amount from that is four misqals.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Two twigs are placed for the deceased, one on the right and the other on the left. He said: He said: The twig benefits the believer and the disbeliever.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Yahya ibn Ubada al-Makki, who said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri asking him about al-takhdir, so he said: 'A man from the Ansar died, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was notified of his death. He said to the one who was next in kinship from his relatives: 'Green your companion.' What is the least of the greened ones? He said: 'A green twig placed from the root of the hands to the collarbone.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from a man, from Yahya ibn Ubada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A wet twig of the length of a cubit is taken and placed, and he gestured with his hand from his collarbone to his hand, [saying it is] wrapped with his garment. He said, And the man said, I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) afterwards and asked him about it, so he said: Yes, I had narrated it to Yahya ibn Ubada.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is your view of the deceased when he dies, why is the twig placed with him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Punishment and Reckoning are staved off from him as long as the wood is wet.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And all the punishment is in one day, in one hour, the measure of what it takes to enter the grave and for the people to return. And the two fronds were made for that purpose, so no punishment or reckoning befalls him after they dry up, if Allah wills.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: The twigs are of the measure of a span; one is placed from the collarbone to where it reaches against the skin, and the other is on the left side from the collarbone to where it reaches above the shirt.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Two twigs are placed for the deceased, one on the right and the other on the left.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hariz and Fuzayl and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'For what reason is the twig placed with the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The punishment is averted from him as long as it is wet.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said: It was said to him (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Sometimes there is danger for me from the one whom I fear, so it is not possible to place the twig upon what you have narrated to us.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Enter it (in the grave) wherever it is possible.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the twig placed in the grave. He said: There is no problem.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from someone else from our companions, said: We said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! (Supposing) we are not able upon the (palm) twigs?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A lotus twig'. It was said, 'Supposing we are not able upon the lotus?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A different twig'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Muhammad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Bilal, that he wrote to him (peace be upon him) asking about the twig (of the palm tree). 'When we cannot find it, can we make something else its substitute in a place where the palm tree cannot be reached?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is permissible when the twig is scarce; and the twig is superior, and with it has the report come.'
And Ali ibn Ibrahim reported in another narration, He said: 'A pomegranate stick should be made in its place.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the twig (jaridah), whether it is placed beneath the garments or above them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Above the shirt and below the loins.' So I asked him (peace be upon him), 'From which side?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'On the right side.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to him, 'A person died while he was in a state of major ritual impurity (junub). How should he be washed, and what portion of the water suffices for him?' He said, 'He is washed with one washing; that suffices for him for his major impurity and for the washing of the deceased, because the two obligations have combined into one sanctity.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman who dies in her post-childbirth bleeding (nifas), how is she washed? He said: Similar to the washing of the clean (free from major impurity), and similarly the menstruating woman, and similarly the one in major ritual impurity (junub). Indeed, she is washed with one washing only.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahboub and Ahmad ibn Muhammad regarding the woman when she dies a puerpera (with post-childbirth bleeding) and her blood is abundant, she is placed up to the navel in a leather bag or a similar clean one, then she is enshrouded after that.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqteen who said: I asked the Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) about the woman who dies while her child is in her belly. He said: 'Her belly is split open and her child is extracted.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ismail ibn Mihran from Ali ibn Abu Hamza from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the woman who dies while the child is moving in her belly: should her belly be split open and her child extracted? He said: Yes. And in the narration of Ibn Abi Umayr, there is an addition: the child is extracted and her belly is stitched up.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'When the woman dies and in her belly is a moving child, split open her belly and extract the child'. And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the woman dying and the child is in her belly, so there is fear upon her, said: 'There is no problem if the man inserts his hand, so he cuts it and extracts it'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not touch the hair or the nails of the deceased, and if anything falls off from him, place it in his shroud.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Miham, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is disliked to shorten the nails of the deceased, or shorten his hair, or shave off his pubic hair, or close down a joint of his.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinji from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased who has hair on him, so can it be shaved off or clipped? He (peace be upon him) said: Do not touch anything from him. Wash him and bury him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When blood or something else comes out from the nostril of the deceased after the washing and hits the turban or the shroud, cut it off with the cutter.

From him, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Prophet or Imam), said: When the deceased is washed, then excretes after the washing, so the excretion should be washed off, and the (whole) washing would not be repeated.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When something comes out from the deceased after having been shrouded, and it hits the shroud, it should be cut off from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who dies and there is no one with him to wash him except women, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'His wife should wash him, or a female relative if there is one for him, and the women pour water over him by pouring, and regarding the woman, when she dies, her husband inserts his hand under her shirt, so he washes her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man: Is it permissible for him to look at his wife when she dies, or to wash her if there is no one else to wash her; and about the woman: Can she look at her husband in a similar manner when he dies? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that. The family of the woman does so because they dislike for her husband to look at something of her that they dislike.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man washing his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, from behind the cloth.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who dies and there is no one with him to wash him except women. Can the women wash him? He said: His wife or the one with his sanctity (mahram) should wash him, and the women pour water over him by pouring from above the clothes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I heard a companion of ours asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who dies with men, among whom there is no one with whom she can be married (non-mahram). Can they wash her while she is in her clothes? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then that burden will be placed upon them, but they should wash her palms.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the woman when she dies, so he said: 'Her husband inserts his hand under her shirt up to the elbows.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who dies during a journey, or in a land where there is no one with him except women, he said: 'He is buried and not washed.' And he said regarding the woman who is with the men in that same status, except if her husband is with her; so if her husband is with her, let him wash her from above the shirt, and pour water upon her with a pouring. And let his wife wash him when he dies, and the woman is not like the man; the woman is of worse appearance when she dies.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who goes out on a journey and his wife is with him, can he wash her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and (he can wash) his mother and his sister and similar to this, a cloth is cast upon her private part.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I heard a companion of ours asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who dies with men, and there is none with them who is her mahram (close male relative). Can they wash her while she is in her clothes? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then it will be incumbent upon them, but they wash her palms.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman when she dies and there is no woman with her to wash her, he said: Her husband inserts his hand under her shirt and washes her up to the elbows.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the Muslim man who dies during a journey and there is no Muslim man with him, and with him are Christian men, and with him are his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, both Muslim. How should his washing be dealt with? He (peace be upon him) said: 'His paternal aunt and his maternal aunt should wash him in his shirt, and the Christians should not go near him.' And about the woman who dies during the journey and there is no Muslim woman with her, and with her are Christian women, and her paternal uncle and her maternal uncle, both Muslims. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should wash her, and the Christian woman should not go near her, just as the Muslim woman would wash her, except that there is a shirt upon her, so the water is poured from above the shirt.' I said, 'If a Muslim man dies and there is no Muslim man with him nor a Muslim woman from his relatives, and with him are Christian men and Muslim women, with no kinship between him and them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Christian man washes himself, then he washes him, for there is desperation.' And about the Muslim woman who dies and there is no Muslim woman with her nor a Muslim man from her relatives, and with her is a Christian woman and Muslim men, with no kinship between her and them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Christian woman washes herself, then she washes her.' And about the Christian man who is on a journey and he is with the Muslims, and he dies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A Muslim should not wash him, nor is there prestige, nor should he bury him, nor stand upon his grave.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdul Rahman ibn Salim, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Who washed Fatima (peace be upon her)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That was Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' It was as if you were astonished by his words, so he said to me, 'It is as if you are constricted by what I informed you.' So I said, 'That was it, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said to me, 'Do not be constricted, for she was a truthful one (Siddiqah). None washed her except a truthful one. Do you not know that Maryam (peace be upon her) was not washed except by Isa (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so what do you say regarding the woman who is in travel with men, having no Mahram (close male relative) with them, nor a woman with them, and the woman dies? What should be done with her?' He said: 'Wash from her what necessitates Tayammum, and she is not touched, and nothing of her beauty (Mahasin) which Allah (Exalted and Mighty) commanded to be covered is uncovered.' I said, 'How is it done with her?' He said: 'The palm of her hands is washed, and her face, and the back of her hands is washed.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever falls ill for three (days) and does not complain to any of his visitors, I will replace his flesh with flesh better than his, and blood better than his. If I then restore him to health, I restore him without any sin upon him; and if I take his soul, I take it to My mercy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: God, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'There is no servant whom I afflict with an affliction and he does not complain to his visitors, except that I replace him with flesh better than his flesh and blood better than his blood. So if I take him (in death), I take him to My mercy; and if he lives, he lives and there is no sin for him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Fadl, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: God Mighty and Majestic said: "Whichever servant I afflict with an affliction, and he conceals it from his visitors for three (days), I will replace his flesh with flesh better than his, and blood better than his, and skin better than his. So if I keep him alive, I keep him without sin, and if he dies, he dies unto My mercy."

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Whoever falls ill for a night and accepts it with its (proper) acceptance, God Almighty and Majestic shall record for him the worship of sixty years.' I said: 'What is the meaning of its acceptance?' He said: 'He does not complain of what has afflicted him during it to anyone.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from al-'Azrami, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Whoever suffers illness for a night and accepts it with its (proper) acceptance, and renders his gratitude for it to Allah, it would be equivalent to sixty years of worship.' My father said: 'So I said to him: What is its (proper) acceptance?' He said: 'That he is patient over it and does not inform (anyone) about what befell him in it; then when it is morning, he praises Allah for what had been.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is sick for three days and conceals it, not informing anyone about it — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will replace for him his flesh with flesh better than his flesh, blood better than his blood, skin better than his skin, and hair better than his hair.' [The narrator] said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom — and how would He replace it?' He said: 'He would replace his flesh, blood, hair, and skin with [flesh, blood, hair, and skin] that has not committed a sin.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who washes a deceased person, let him perform ghusl. I said, 'And if he touches him as long as he is warm?' He said, 'There is no ghusl upon him. And when he cools down, then he touches him, let him perform ghusl.' I said, 'And the one who places him in the grave?' He said, 'There is no ghusl upon him; he only touches the clothes.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked: 'When a man closes the eyes of the deceased, is ritual bath (ghusl) upon him?' He said: 'If he touches him while he is still warm, then no; but if he touches him after he has cooled, then let him perform ritual bath.' I asked: 'So the one who washes him, does he perform ritual bath?' He said: 'Yes.' I asked: 'Does he wash the deceased, then enshroud him, before he performs ritual bath?' He said: 'He washes the deceased, then washes his hand from the dirt, then puts the shrouds upon him, then he performs ritual bath.' I asked: 'So the one who carries him, is ritual bath upon him?' He said: 'No.' I asked: 'So the one who places him in the grave, is ablution (wudu) upon him?' He said: 'No, except that he may perform ablution from the dust of the grave if he wishes.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who washes the deceased must perform ghusl (ritual bath). And if a person kisses the deceased while he is still warm, there is no ghusl upon him. But if he touches him and kisses him after he has cooled down, then ghusl is upon him. And there is no harm if he touches him after the ghusl and kisses him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who touches the deceased, is it befitting for him to perform ghusl because of it? He said: No. Rather, that is for the human being alone. He said: And I asked him about the man whose garment is touched by the body of the deceased, so he said: He washes what the garment was touched by.
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from al-Hajjal from Tha'laba from Ma'mar ibn Yahya said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbid the ghusl when one enters the grave.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) kissed Uthman ibn Maz'un after his death.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'Should the one who washed the deceased perform ghusl?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And the one who places him in the grave?' He said, 'No, for he only touches the clothes.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman al-Daylami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abdullah ibn Qays al-Masir came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'Inform me about the deceased, why is he washed with the washing of major ritual impurity (janabah)?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I will not inform you.' So he went out from his presence and met some of the Shias and said to them, 'I wonder at you, O group of Shias! You have accepted the Wilayah of this man and obeyed him, and if he invited you to worship him, you would respond to him; and I asked him about a matter, but there was nothing with him regarding it!' So when it was the following time, he came to him again and asked him about it, and he said, 'I will not inform you with it.' So Abdullah ibn Qays said to a man from his companions, 'Go to the Shias, be their companion, and display your Wilayah with them in their presence, and curse me and disavow from me. So when it is the time for Hajj, come to me until I hand over to you what you will use for it, and ask them to let you enter upon Muhammad ibn Ali. So when you arrive to him, ask him about the deceased, why is he washed with the washing of janabah.' So the man went to the Shias and was with them until the time of the season. So he looked at the religion of the people and accepted it with their acceptance, and concealed the matter from Ibn Qays, fearing that he would prevent the Hajj (by not paying for it). So when it was the time for Hajj, he came to him, and he gave him a Hajj (expense), and he went out. So when he arrived in Medina, his companions said to him, 'Stay behind in the house until we mention you to him and ask him for permission for you.' So when they arrived to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said to them, 'Where is your companion? You have not been just to him.' They said, 'We did not know what your acceptance would be from that.' So he ordered one of those present to bring him. So when he entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said to him, 'Welcome! How is your view of what you are in today, from what you were in beforehand?' So he said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! I wasn't in anything (before).' So he said, 'You speak the truth. As for your worship in those days, it was lighter upon you than your worship today,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked, 'What is the matter with the deceased that he discharges semen?' He said: 'The seed from which he was created, it is thrown out.'

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Harun ibn Hamza, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The creature does not die until the seed from which he was created comes out of him, either from his mouth or from his eyes.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Any believer who washes a believer and says, when turning him over: 'O Allah, this is the body of Your believing servant. You have taken his soul from him and separated it from the body. Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness (for him)', Allah will forgive him the sins of one year, except for the major sins.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Taref, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever washes a deceased person and fulfills the trust regarding him, Allah will forgive him. I said, 'And how does he fulfill the trust regarding him?' He said, 'He does not narrate what he sees.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no believer who washes a believer and says while washing him, 'Lord, Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness,' except that Allah forgives him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Among what Musa (peace be upon him) whispered to Allah was: 'O Lord, what is for the one who washes the dead?' So He said: 'I wash him from his sins just as his mother gave birth to him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad and Abdullah ibn Sinan, altogether, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is befitting for the guardians of the deceased among you that they should announce to the brethren of the deceased his death, so that they may witness his funeral, pray over him, and seek forgiveness for him; thus, reward is recorded for them, and forgiveness is recorded for the deceased; and he (the announcer) earns reward for them and for what they earned for their deceased through seeking forgiveness.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the funeral (of the deceased), should the people be notified (proclaimed) about it? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The funeral (of the deceased) is announced to the people.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Aban, not knowing except that it was mentioned from Abu Hamza, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), whenever he saw a funeral approaching, would say: 'The praise is to Allah, Who did not make me from the perished masses.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Nahdi, raising it (to the Imam), said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), whenever he saw a funeral, said: 'The Praise is for Allah Who did not make me to be from the perished masses'.

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ta'i, from Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever faces a funeral or sees it and says: Allah is the Greatest. This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. O Allah, increase us in faith and submission.' Praise is for Allah Who was strengthened by power and subdued the servants with death. No angel remains in the sky except that he weeps out of mercy for his voice.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from someone else, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Sunnah regarding carrying the funeral coffin is that you face the side of the bier with your right side, so the left side adheres to your right shoulder. Then you pass over it to the other side, and turn from behind it to the third side of the bier. Then you pass over it to the fourth side, which is on your left.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Sunnah is that the bier (coffin) is carried from its four sides, and whatever carrying is done after that is voluntary.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about lifting the coffin by its four corners. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are in a place of dissimulation (taqiyyah), begin with the right hand, then the right leg, then return from your place to the right side of the deceased, not passing behind his leg at all until you face the coffin. So take his left hand, then his left leg, then return from your place and do not pass behind the coffin at all until you face it, doing as you did first.' So if you are not practicing dissimulation in it, then the lifting of the coffin according to the Sunnah is to begin with the right hand, then the right leg, then the left leg, then the left hand, until you circle around it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukeyl, from Al-A'ala ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You begin carrying the coffin from its right side, then you pass over it from behind to the other side, then you continue until you return to the front; thus is the circling of the millstone over it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn 'Uzafir, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Walking behind the coffin is superior to walking in front of it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Yunus ibn Abi Yaqzan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Walk in front of the coffin of the knowledgeable Muslim, and do not walk in front of the coffin of the denier (of faith), for indeed, in front of the coffin of the Muslim are angels hastening him to Paradise, and indeed, in front of the coffin of the disbeliever are angels hastening him to the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) walked behind a coffin, so it was said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, why do you walk behind it?' He said, 'The angels, I see them walking in front of it, and we are following them.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about walking with the funeral procession, so he said: 'In front of it, and on its right, and on its left, and behind it.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Walk in front of the funeral procession and behind it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from al-Hajjal from Ali ibn Shajara from Abu al-Wafa' al-Muradi from Sadir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The one who loves to walk the walk of the Honourable Recorders (Angels), so let him walk by the side of the coffin.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked, 'What should I do when I go out with the funeral procession, walking in front of it, or behind it, or to its right, or to its left?' So he said: 'If he (the deceased) was an opponent (of the Ahl al-Bayt), do not walk in front of him, for the Angels of Punishment will be facing him with the varieties of Punishment.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at a funeral for one of his relatives. When he had prayed over the deceased, his guardian said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Return, O Abu Ja'far, having been recompensed, and do not tire yourself because you are too weak to walk.' So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Permission has been given to you regarding the return, so return, and for me is a need which I want to ask you about.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Rather, it is a merit and a recompense; therefore, he who follows it is recompensed in accordance with the distance he walks with the funeral. As for his permission, we did not come by his permission, nor will we return by his permission.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, raised it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two commanders, yet they are not two commanders in status: It is not for the one who follows a coffin to return until he is permitted, and a man who performs Hajj with a woman, so it is not for him to depart (abandon her) until she has fulfilled her rituals.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) attended the funeral of a man from Quraish, and I was with him, and Ata'a was among them. A woman shrieked, and Ata'a said to her, 'Will you be quiet or shall we return?' He said, so she did not be quiet, so Ata'a returned. I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Ata'a has returned.' He said, 'And why?' I said, 'This woman shrieked, so he said to her, 'Will you be quiet or shall we return?' But she did not be quiet, so he returned.' He (Abu Ja'far) said, 'Proceed with us. For if we, when we see something of falsehood along with the Truth, were to leave the Truth for it, we would not fulfill the right of a Muslim.' He (the narrator) said, 'So when he had prayed over the funeral, its guardian said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Return, having been recompensed, may Allah have mercy on you, for you are not strong enough for walking.' But he refused to return. I said to him, 'He has permitted you to return, and I have a need which I want to ask you about.' He said, 'Proceed. For it is not by his permission that we came, nor is it by his permission that we return. Rather, it is a merit and a reward that we sought. For according to what the man follows the funeral, the man is recompensed for that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the believer is placed in his grave, it is called out: 'Indeed, the first of your gifts is Paradise, and the gift of the one who followed you (your coffin) is Forgiveness.'

Ali, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from a man from his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever escorts the coffin of a believer until he is buried in his grave, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seventy angels from the escorts, who will escort him and seek forgiveness for him when he exits from his grave until the Pausing station.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The first of what the believer is bestowed with is that forgiveness is granted for the one who followed his coffin.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever escorts a deceased person until the funeral prayer is performed over him, he will have one 'Qirat' of reward; and whoever accompanies him to his grave until he is buried, he will have two 'Qirats' of reward; and one Qirat is like the mountain of Uhud.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who walks with a funeral procession until the prayer is performed over the deceased, then returns, there is for him one Qirat of reward. And if he walks with it until it is buried, there is for him two Qirats; and the Qirat is like the mountain of Uhud.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever follows a funeral, Allah will write for him four Qirats: one Qirat for following it, one Qirat for the prayer over it, one Qirat for waiting until the burial is completed, and one Qirat for the consolation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Among what Musa (peace be upon him) whispered to his Lord was that he said: 'O Lord, what is for the one who escorts a coffin?' He said: 'I assign to him an angel from My angels, with them are banners, escorting them from their graves to their place of gathering.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The one who carries a coffin from its four sides, Allah would forgive him forty major sins.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever takes hold of one corner of the coffin, Allah will forgive him twenty-five major sins, and when he takes hold of four (corners), he will be released from sins.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Isa ibn Rashid, from a man from his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who holds the four sides of the coffin, Allah will forgive him forty major sins.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about how to pray (Salat al-Janazah) upon the men and the women. He said: 'The man is placed in front, facing the men, and the women are placed behind the men.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who prays over two dead bodies or three dead bodies, how should he pray over them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there were three, or two, or ten, or more than that, let him pray over them one prayer, exclaiming five Takbeers over them just as he prays over one deceased, and he has prayed over them all.' He places one deceased, then places the other parallel to the first, then places the head of the third parallel to the rear of the second, like a staircase, until he finishes with all of them, whatever their number. So when he has arranged them thus, he stands in the middle and exclaims five Takbeers, doing as he does when he prays over one deceased. He was asked: 'What if the deceased were men and women?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should begin with the men, placing the head of the second parallel to the rear of the first, until he finishes with all the men. Then he places the head of the woman parallel to the rear of the last man, then places the head of the other woman parallel to the rear of the first woman, until he finishes with all of them.' So when he has arranged them thus, he stands in the middle, in the middle of the men, and exclaims Takbeers and prays over them just as he prays over one deceased. And he was asked about a deceased who had been prayed over, and when the Imam concluded, the deceased was found upside down, his feet in the place of his head. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should be straightened and the prayer is repeated over him, even if he had been carried, as long as he had not been buried. If he had been buried, the prayer has passed; he is not prayed over while he is buried.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When he would pray the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) upon a woman and a man, he would place the woman first and delay the man; and when he would pray upon a slave and a free person, he would place the slave first and delay the free person; and when he would pray upon an elder and a younger person, he would place the younger first and delay the elder.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about men and women, how is the prayer offered for them? He said: The men are in front of the women, facing the Imam; they are lined up one behind the other.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the funerals of men, children, and women, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The women are placed closest to the Qiblah, the children are placed below them, and the men are placed beyond that, and the Imam stands opposite the men.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the funerals of men and women when they are gathered together, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The men are preceded [in burial], as it is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from his father Zakariyya ibn Musa, from Al-Yasa' ibn Abdullah Al-Qummi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who prays upon a deceased person alone. He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And two men?' He said: 'Yes, but the other one should stand behind the other, and not stand by his side.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One cannot pray (upon the deceased) with shoes on, and there is no objection to (praying) with socks.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of the rows in prayer is the first one, and the best of the rows in funerals is the last one.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and why?' He said: 'Because it becomes a veil for the women.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He prays upon the funeral, the person closest to it, or he instructs the one he likes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'When a woman dies, who is most rightful in offering the funeral prayer (Salat) upon her?' He said, 'Her husband.' I said, 'Is the husband more rightful than the father, the son, and the brother?' He said, 'Yes, and he washes her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman who dies, 'Who is most rightful to pray upon her?' He said: 'The husband.' I said, 'The husband is more rightful than the father, the brother, and the son?' He said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Imam is present at the funeral, he is the most rightful of the people to perform the prayer upon it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one closest to the deceased among the people should pray over the funeral, or he should instruct the one he wishes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased: Is Salat (prayer) performed upon it without ablution? He said: Yes. It is merely Takbeer (exalting God), Tahmid (praising God), Tasbih (glorifying God), and Tahlil (declaring oneness), just as you say Takbeer and Tasbih in your house without ablution.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who catches the funeral procession while he is not in a state of ablution. If he goes to perform ablution, the prayer upon it will be missed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform tayammum and pray.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'id, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'The deceased is brought out and I am not in a state of ablution. If I go to perform ablution, the prayer will be missed by me. Is it permissible for me to pray upon it while I am without ablution?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is more beloved to me that you be in a state of purity.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about the man who is suddenly confronted by the funeral procession while he is in a state of not having performed ablution. He said: 'Let him exclaim Takbir along with them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'at, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who passes by a funeral while he is without ablution, what should he do? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should strike with his hands upon a brick wall and perform Tayammum with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is befitting for the sick person among you to inform his brothers of his illness, so they visit him, and he is rewarded through them, and they are rewarded through him.' He said: So it was said to him: 'Yes, they are rewarded for their walking to him, so how is he rewarded through them?' He (the narrator) said: So he (the Imam) said: 'By earning good deeds for them, he is rewarded through them. Ten good deeds are written for him for that, ten ranks are raised for him, and ten evil deeds are erased from him.'
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you falls ill, let him give permission to the people to come to him, for there is no one except that he has an answered supplication.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Sayf ibn Amira who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you visits his brother (who is ill), let him (the patient) ask him (the visitor) to supplicate for him, for his supplication is like the supplication of the Angels.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from the wife of Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked, 'How should the women pray upon the funeral procession when there is no man with them?' He said: 'They should form rows together, and a woman should not be in front of them (leading them).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When the man is not present, a woman should step forward to be in their midst, and the women stand on her right and left, with her in the middle; she proclaims the Takbeer until she is finished with the Salat.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani from al-Mitham from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I said, 'Does the menstruating woman pray upon the funeral?' He said: 'Yes, and she does not form a row with them; she stands separately.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman praying upon the deceased. He said: 'Yes, and she should not form a row with them.'

Hammad, from Hareyz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The menstruating woman prays upon the deceased body because there is no bowing nor prostration in it; and the one with major ritual impurity performs tayammum and prays upon the deceased body.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does anything from these timings prevent you from praying the Salat upon the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Prayer is performed upon the deceased at any hour, for it is not a prayer of bowing and prostration; rather, prayer is disliked at the rising of the sun and at its setting, which are the times of humbless, bowing, and prostration, because the sun sets between the two horns of Satan and rises between the two horns of Satan.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it (to the Imam), said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Why has the Takbeer upon the deceased been made five (times)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It was brought in from each Salat, one Takbeer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to proclaim Takbeer five times over a group of people, and over another group four times. So when he proclaimed Takbeer four times over a man, they would accuse him, meaning of hypocrisy.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Suleiman ibn ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made the prayer obligatory five times and appointed for the deceased, from each prayer, one Takbeer.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Bakr, do you know how many Takbiirs are in the Salat upon the deceased?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Five Takbiirs.' Then he said: 'Do you know from where the five have been taken?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The five Takbiirs have been taken from the five (daily) Salats; from each Salat is one Takbeer.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the prayer upon the deceased, so he said: 'You exclaim five Takbeers. You say at the beginning of the first Takbeer: I testify that there is no God except Allah, Alone, there being no associates to Him, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad and upon the Imams of Guidance, and forgive us and our brethren who preceded us with faith, and do not make rancor in our hearts for those who believe. Our Lord, You are Gracious, Merciful. O Allah, forgive our living and our dead from the believing men and the believing women, and unite our hearts with the hearts of our good ones, and guide us to what we differ in, from the Truth, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to the Straight Path.' So if the second Takbeer cuts off upon you, it will not harm you. You should say: O Allah, Your servant, son of Your servant, and son of Your maid. You are more knowing of him than I am. He is needy to Your Mercy and You are needless from him. O Allah, so overlook his sins and increase in his good deeds and forgive him and have mercy on him, and illuminate for him in his grave, and cause him to meet his Proof and his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and do not deprive us of his reward and do not try us after him. You should say this until you finish the five Takbeers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the prayer upon the deceased, he said: You say Takbir, then send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then you say: 'O Allah, Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maid, I do not know of him except good, and You are more knowing of him than I am. O Allah, if he was a good-doer, increase in his goodness and accept from him; and if he was a bad-doer, forgive his sin and have mercy on him, and make his grave spacious, and make him among the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)'. Then you say the second Takbir and say: 'O Allah, if he was pure, purify him; and if he was erroneous, forgive him'. Then you say the third Takbir and say: 'O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not test us after him'. Then you say the fourth Takbir and say: 'O Allah, record him with You among the 'Illiyun, and succeed him among his offspring in the later generations, and make him among the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)'. Then you say the fifth Takbir and turn away (conclude the prayer).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Takbeer upon the deceased, so he said: 'Five. You should say in the first of them: I testify that there is no god but Allah, Alone, without partner. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Then you should say: O Allah, this one enshrouded before us is Your servant and the son of Your servant, and You have taken his soul to Yourself, and he is in need of Your Mercy, and You are Self-Sufficient regarding his punishment. O Allah, we do not know from his exterior except goodness, and You are more Knowing of his inner self. O Allah, if he was a good-doer, increase in his goodness, and if he was a bad-doer, overlook his sins. Then you say Takbeer for the second time, and do that in every Takbeer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You say Takbir, then you testify, then you say: 'We are for Allah and to Him we return. Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, Lord of death and life. Send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family. May Allah recompense Muhammad with the best recompense for what he did for his community and for what he conveyed of the messages of his Lord.' Then you say: 'O Allah, Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant, his forelock is in Your hand, he has departed from the world and is in need of Your mercy, and You are free from punishing him. O Allah, we do not know from him except good, and You are more knowing of him. O Allah, if he was a doer of good, increase in his goodness and accept from him; and if he was a doer of evil, forgive his sin and have mercy on him and overlook him by Your mercy.' O Allah, join him with Your Prophet and establish him with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. O Allah, lead us and him along the path of guidance, and guide us and him to Your straight path. O Allah, Your forgiveness, Your forgiveness. Then you say Takbir a second time and say the like of what you said, until you finish five Takbirs.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him), saying, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people raise their hands during the Takbeer upon the deceased during the first Takbeer only, and do not raise them afterwards. So shall I restrict myself to the first Takbeer as they do, or shall I raise my hands during every Takbeer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Raise your hand during every Takbeer.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim Abu al-Sakhar, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the prayer upon the deceased, you should say: 'O Allah, You created this soul and You caused it to die. You know its secret and its public matters. We have come to You interceding on its behalf, so accept our intercession. O Allah, appoint over it those it accepted as rulers, and gather it with those it loved.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara and Ma'mar ibn Yahya and Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: In the prayer upon the deceased, there is no specific recitation, nor a prescribed supplication; you may supplicate with whatever comes to your mind. The deceased have the most right that the believer supplicates for them, and that he begins with sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no greeting (taslim) in the prayer upon the deceased.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no greeting (salam) in the prayer upon the deceased.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna ibn al-Walid, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed seventy prayers upon Hamza.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pronounced seventy Takbeers upon Hamza, and Ali (peace be upon him) pronounced twenty-five Takbeers upon Sahl ibn Hunayf in your presence.
