He said: He pronounced five, five (at a time). Whenever the people caught up with him, they would say, 'O Commander of the Faithful, we did not catch up with the prayer upon Sahl.' So he would lay him down and pronounce five (Takbeers) upon him until he reached his grave, having done so five times.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you pray (Salaat) upon the believer, supplicate for him and strive for him in supplication; and if he was standing (in prayer) but of weak understanding, then exclaim Takbeer and say: 'O Allah, forgive those who repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blaze.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If he was of weak understanding, then say: 'O Allah, grant forgiveness to those who repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire.' And when you do not know his state, then say: 'O Allah, if he loved goodness and its people, then forgive him, have mercy on him, and overlook him.' And if the one of weak understanding is weaker than you in the Way (of Allah), then seek forgiveness for him based on the aspect of intercession, not based on the aspect of Wilayah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The (Divine) Mercy is upon two aspects – the aspect of Wilayah and the aspect of intercession.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from a man, from Suleman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You should say: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and accept his intercession, and whiten his face, and increase his followers.' O Allah, forgive me, and have mercy on me, and turn towards me. O Allah, forgive those who repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire. So if he was a believer, he would be included in it, and if he was not a believer, he would be excluded from it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Thabit Abu Al-Miqdam, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and behold, there was a funeral for someone from his neighbors. So he attended it, and I was near him, and I heard him saying: O Allah, indeed You are the One who created these souls, and You cause them to die, and You revive them, and You are more Knowing of their secrets and their apparent states than we are, and of their permanence and their temporary nature. O Allah, and this is Your servant, and I do not know of any evil from him, and You are more Knowing of him, and we have come to You interceding for him after his death. So if he is deserving (of mercy), then accept our intercession regarding him, and resurrect him with those whom he used to befriend.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Abdullah ibn Ubay ibn Salul died, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was present at his funeral. Umar said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'O Messenger of Allah! Has not Allah forbidden you from standing at his grave?' So he was silent. Umar said again, 'O Messenger of Allah! Has not Allah forbidden you from standing at his grave?' So he said to him, 'Woe be unto you! And what do you know what I said? I said: O Allah! Fill his belly with fire, and fill his grave with fire, and his origin with fire.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Thus he exposed from the Messenger of Allah what he disliked (to expose).'

Sahl, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man from the hypocrites died, so Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) went out walking and encountered a slave of his. He said to him, 'Where are you going?' He said, 'I am fleeing from the funeral of this hypocrite so that I do not pray over him.' Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Stand by my side, and whatever you hear me say, say the like of it.' He said: So he raised his hands and said, 'O Allah! Humble Your servant among Your servants and Your people. O Allah! Cause the heat of Your Fire to reach him. O Allah! Make him taste the intensity of Your punishment, for he used to befriend Your enemies, be inimical to Your friends, and hate the People of the Household of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you pray (Salat) upon the enemy of Allah, say: 'O Allah, we do not know of So-and-so except that he is an enemy of Yours and of Your Messenger. O Allah, fill his grave with fire, and fill his interior with fire, and hasten him to the Fire, for he used to befriend Your enemies and be inimical to Your friends, and hate the People of the House of Your Prophet. O Allah, straiten his grave upon him.' So when he is raised (from the grave), say: 'O Allah, do not raise his status, and do not purify him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: If he was a denier of the Truth, then say: 'O Allah, fill his belly with fire and his grave with fire, and send down upon him snakes and scorpions.' And that is what Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said for an evil woman from the Banu Umayya; my father prayed over her and said this phrase: 'And make the devil her companion.' Muhammad ibn Muslim said: So I said to him, 'For what reason do you place the snakes and scorpions in her grave?' He said: 'The snakes will bite her and the scorpions will sting her, and the devils will accompany her in her grave.' I said, 'Will she feel the pain of that?' He said: 'Yes, intense.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, who said: You should say: 'O Allah, humiliate Your servant among Your servants and Your city. O Allah, make Your fire reach him and make him taste the severity of Your punishment, for he used to be inimical to Your friends and befriend Your enemies, and used to hate the People of the Household of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A woman from the Banu Umayya died, so I attended her (funeral). So when they had prayed over her, and raised her, and she came to be in the hands of the men, he said: 'O Allah! Place her down and do not raise her, and do not purify her.' He said, 'And she was an enemy of Allah.' He said, 'And (an enemy) of ours.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no visiting the sick for eye ailments, and a sick-visit does not take place within less than three days. When it becomes necessary, then one day yes and one day no. When the illness is prolonged, the sick person and his family are left (to manage on their own).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The visitation (of the sick) is (to last) the measure of a suckling interval of a she-camel or the milking of a she-camel.

A retainer of Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) told me, saying: One of his followers fell ill, so we went out to visit him — we were a group from among the followers of Ja'far. Then Ja'far (peace be upon him) met us on the road and said to us: 'Where are you headed?' We said: 'We are going to visit so-and-so.' He said to us: 'Stop.' So we stopped. He said: 'Does one of you have an apple, or a quince, or a citron, or a spoonful of perfume, or a piece of incense?' We said: 'We have none of these with us.' He said: 'Do you not know that a sick person is comforted by every single thing that is brought in to him?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Musa ibn Qadim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The completion of the visit to the sick person is that you place your hand upon his forearm and hasten your departure from his presence, for the visit of the foolish is more burdensome upon the sick person than his own pain.
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The completion of the visitation is that you place your hand upon the patient when you go to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: that Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of God upon him) said: 'Verily, among the visitors of the sick with the greatest recompense in the presence of God, Mighty and Majestic, is the one who, when he visits his brother, shortens the sitting — unless the patient happens to love that and wants it and requests it from him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Part of the completion of visiting the sick is that the visitor places one of his hands upon the other or upon his forehead.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not bury your dead one in the grave, but place him away from it by two cubits or three, and leave him to prepare himself.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Khurasani, from his father, from Yunus, who said: A hadith I heard from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): I do not remember it except that when I am in the house, it straitens upon me. He (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When you bring the deceased to the edge of his grave, delay him for a moment, for he is preparing himself for the questioning.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halbi, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurara, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and with him was a man from the Ansar. A coffin passed by, so the Ansari stood up, but Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) did not stand up. So I remained seated with him (peace be upon him), and the Ansari did not remain standing until they had passed with it, then he sat down. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What made you stand up?' He said: 'I saw Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) do that.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) did not do that, nor did anyone from us, the People of the Household, ever stand up for it.' The Ansari said: 'You have cast doubt on me, may Allah rectify you. I thought I had seen him do so.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was seated, and a funeral passed by him. So the people stood up when the funeral emerged. So Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'A funeral of a Jew passed by, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on its path, seated. So he disliked that the head of the deceased Jew be higher than his, therefore he stood up for that.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting for anyone to enter the grave wearing two shoes, nor two socks, nor a turban, nor a cloak, nor a cap.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Descend into the grave with the turban and the cap on your head, and without the shoes and the pallium; and loosen your buttons, and by that the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed.' And let him seek Refuge with Allah from the Pelted Satan, and let him recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and the Two Protecting Chapters (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn), and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Al-Ikhlas), and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat Al-Kursi). And if he is able to bare his cheek and place it on the ground, let him do so; and let him testify (the Shahadah) and let him mention (Allah) whatever he knows until he ends up to his companion (the deceased).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Misma'i, from Ismail ibn Yasar al-Wasiti, from Saif ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Descend into the grave with a turban on your head, and not a cap, and not a cloak, and not shoes, and loosen your buttons. I said, 'And the socks?' He said, 'There is no problem with the socks during a time of necessity and dissimulation.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who enters the grave, so he should not exit except from the side of the two legs.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it (to the Imam), said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The man enters the grave from wherever he wishes, and he does not exit except from the side of his legs.' And in another report, he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: For every house there is a door, and the door of the grave is from the side of the two legs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abdullah ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man descends into the grave of his father, and the father does not descend into the grave of his son.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is disliked for the man that he should descend into the grave of his son.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When Ismail son of Abu Abdullah died, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) came to the grave, loosened himself, and sat. Then he said: 'May Allah have mercy on you and send blessings upon you,' and he did not descend into his grave, and said: 'This is how the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did with Ibrahim (peace be upon him).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Zurara, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the grave, how many can enter it? He said: That is up to the guardian; if he wills, he will allow an odd number, and if he wills, he will allow an even number.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Ali ibn Maysara, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The husband is more rightful with his wife until he places her in her grave.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Aban, from Abdullah ibn Rashid, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when his son Ismail (peace be upon him) died, and he was lowered into his grave. Then he threw himself onto the ground facing the Qiblah, and said: 'This is what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did with Ibrahim.' Then he said: 'Indeed, a man is lowered into the grave of his father, and he is not lowered into the grave of his son.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yahya ibn Amr, from Abdullah ibn Rashid, from Abdullah al-Anbary, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can the man bury his son?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He cannot bury him in the soil.' I said, 'So can the son bury his father?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you bring the deceased to the grave, pull him in by his feet; so when you place him in the grave, recite Ayat al-Kursi. And say: 'In the name of Allah, and in the way of Allah, and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)'. O Allah, expand for him in his grave and join him with his prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And say, as you said during the prayer upon him, once: From Allah, if he was a good doer, then increase in his goodness, and if he was an evil doer, then forgive him, have mercy on him, and overlook him. And seek forgiveness for him as much as you are able. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so that whenever Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered the deceased into the grave, he said: O Allah, turn the earth away from his sides, and ascend his deeds, and grant him pleasure from You'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid, all from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Harun ibn Kharja, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you bring forth the deceased, say: 'In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, to Your mercy, not to Your punishment.' So when you place him in the grave niche, place your hand on his ear and say: 'Allah is your Lord, and Islam is your religion, and Muhammad is your Prophet, and the Quran is your Book, and Ali is your Imam.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about the deceased, so he said: 'Place him in the grave starting from the direction of the feet, and press the earth against the sides of the grave to a height of four spread fingers, and square his grave.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Place him with a gentle placing. So when you place him in his grave (lahd), let the closest of the people to his head mention the Name of Allah upon him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and seek refuge from Satan, and let him recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and the Two Protecting Chapters (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn), and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Al-Ikhlas), and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi). And if he is able to bare his cheek and press it against the ground, he should do so, and he should testify and mention whatever he knows until he reaches his companion.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mahfuz al-Iskaaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you want to bury the deceased, let the wisest one who enters his grave be at his head, and let him uncover his right cheek until it is exposed to the ground, and bring his mouth close to his ear and say: 'Listen, understand!' three times: 'Allah is your Lord, and Muhammad is your Prophet, and Islam is your Religion, and so-and-so is your Imam. Listen and understand'; and repeat it to him three times, this is the Talqeen (indoctrination).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: When the deceased is placed in his grave, say: 'In the name of Allah and in the way of Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Your servant, son of Your servant, has lodged with You, and You are the best of hosts. O Allah, make spacious for him in his grave and join him with his Prophet. O Allah, we do not know from him except good, and You are more knowing of him.' So when you place the brick/slab upon him, say: 'O Allah, connect his loneliness and comfort his solitude, and settle upon him from Your mercy a mercy that suffices him from the mercy of anyone other than You.' So when you leave his grave, say: 'We are from Allah and to Him we shall return, and the praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, raise his rank in the highest Illyin and succeed him among the remaining generations, O Lord of the worlds.'

From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: When you place the deceased in his Lahd (grave niche), recite Ayat al-Kursi and strike your hand upon his right shoulder, then say, 'O so-and-so, say: I am pleased with Allah as Lord, and with Islam as Religion, and with Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as Prophet, and with Ali (peace be upon him) as Imam,' and name the Imam of his time.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said, I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What should I say when I place one of our deceased in his grave?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Say: O Allah, this is Your servant so-and-so, and the son of Your servant, who has lodged with You, and You are the best of those with whom one lodges. He has indeed become in need of Your Mercy. O Allah, and we do not know from him except goodness, and You are more Knowing of his inner self, while we are witnesses to his outward self.' O Allah, cause the earth to be firm away from his sides, and teach him his Proof (al-Hujjah), and make this day the best day that comes upon him, and make this grave the best house he has lodged in, and turn him into goodness from what he was in, and widen for him in his entrance, and comfort his loneliness, and forgive his sin, and do not deprive us of his reward, and do not mislead us after him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The shroud is slit from the head of the deceased when he is placed in his grave.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from one of his companions from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Place the deceased in the grave with a gentle placing.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you place the deceased in the grave, you say: 'O Allah, this is Your servant and the son of Your servant and the son of Your maid. He has descended to You, and You are the best of those to whom he descends.' So when you lower him from the direction of the feet and dangle him, you say: 'In the name of Allah and by Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, to Your mercy, not to Your punishment. O Allah, make spacious for him in his grave, and teach him his proof, and confirm him with the firm word, and protect us and him from the punishment of the grave.' And when you level the soil over him, you say: 'O Allah, turn the earth away from his sides, and ascend his soul to the souls of the believers in 'Illiyyin, and join him with the righteous.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, who said: Ali ibn Bilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Sometimes a person dies with us and the ground is damp, so we spread the grave with saaj (wood) or we cover it. Is that permissible?' So he wrote: 'That is permissible.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Shuqran, the slave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), cast the cotton spread upon him in his grave.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Husayn ibn Usman from Ibn Muskan from Aban ibn Taghlib said, I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) placed a brick upon the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So I said, 'What is your view if a man were to place a brick upon him, would it harm the deceased?' He said: 'No'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, who said: I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'What Allah wills, not what the people will.' So when he arrived at the grave, he stepped aside and sat down. And when the deceased was placed in his grave niche (lahd), he stood up and threw soil upon him three times with his hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you cast the soil upon the deceased, say: 'In faith in You and affirmation of Your Resurrection, this is what Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) promised us.' He (peace be upon him) said: And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever casts soil upon a deceased and says this statement, Allah will grant him a good deed for every particle (of soil).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at the funeral of a man from our companions. So when they buried him, he (peace be upon him) stood at his grave and threw soil upon it from the side facing his head three times with his handful. Then he spread his palm upon the grave and said: 'O Allah! Widen the earth for him on his two sides, and ascend his soul to You, and grant him pleasure from You, and settle in his grave from Your mercy that which makes him independent of the mercy of anyone other than You.' Then he went away.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) spread the soil upon the deceased, so he held it for a while in his hand, then spread it, and he did not exceed three handfuls. He said, so I asked him about that, and he said: O Umar! I was saying: 'Belief in You and confirmation of Your Resurrection. This is what Allah and His Messenger promised,' up to His words, 'submission'. Thus was what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do, and by it the Sunnah has flowed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: A son of one of the companions of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) died, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) attended. When he was placed in the grave niche, his father stepped forward and threw soil upon him. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) took his hands and said: 'Do not throw soil upon him, and whoever is a close relative of his should not throw soil upon him, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the parent or one with womb relationships from throwing soil upon their deceased.' So we said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, are you forbidding us from this alone?' He said: 'I am forbidding you from throwing soil upon your close relatives, for that causes hardness in the heart, and whoever is hard of heart is distant from his Lord.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Qudama ibn Zaida, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) placed his son Ibrahim with a gentle placing, and squared his grave.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is recommended that a wet twig be inserted with him in his grave, and his grave be raised from the ground by the measure of four clenched fingers, and water be sprinkled upon it, and he be left alone.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked him about a man placing his hand on the grave, what is it and why did he do it? So he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did it upon his son after sprinkling (water). I asked him how I should place my hand on the graves of the Muslims, so he gestured with his hand to the ground and placed it upon it, then raised it, and he was facing the Qiblah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do a special thing for those who died from the Banu Hashim that he did not do for anyone else among the Muslims. When he prayed over the Hashimi and sprinkled his grave with water, he would place his palm on the grave until his fingers were seen in the clay. So the stranger would arrive or the traveler from the people of Medina, and he would see upon the new grave the mark of the palm of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he would say, 'One from the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) has died.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, my father said to me one day during his illness: 'O my son! Bring some people from the Quraysh, from the inhabitants of Medina, so that I may have them bear witness.' He said: 'So I brought some of them to him, and he said: 'O Ja'far! When I die, wash me, shroud me, and raise my grave four fingers' height, and sprinkle it with water.' So when they went out, I said: 'O father! If you had instructed me with this, I would have done it, and why did you want to bring a group of people to you to bear witness?' So he said: 'O my son! I wanted that there should be no dispute.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding sprinkling the water upon the grave. He said: 'The punishment would be staved off from him for as long as the moisture is in the soil'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Sprinkling the grave was [practiced] during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished (with the burial at) the grave, sprinkle it with water, then place your hand by his head and press your palm upon it after the sprinkling.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) stood upon the grave of a man from the Shia and said: 'O Allah! Grant companionship to his loneliness, and comfort his solitude, and settle upon him from Your mercy that which makes him independent of the mercy of anyone besides You.'

Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Supplication is made for the deceased when he is placed in his grave, and the grave is raised above the ground by four fingers.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not apply clay on the grave from other than its own clay.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was paved with red gravel.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: When Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) returned from Baghdad and proceeded to Al-Madina, his daughter died in Faid. So he buried her and ordered one of his slaves to apply plaster to her grave, write her name on a tablet, and place it in the grave.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade adding to the grave soil that had not been taken out from it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The one who is created from soil is buried in it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from al-Hajjal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Minhal, from al-Harith bin al-Mughira, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the seed falls into the womb, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends an angel who takes from the soil in which he is to be buried, dissolves it in the seed, so his heart does not cease to yearn towards it until he is buried in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Nahdi who raised the chain of narration, said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever dies before (the age of) forty, then (his life) has been cut short; and whoever dies within less than fourteen days (of illness), then his death is a sudden death.'

From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Buhlul ibn Muslim, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever dies within less than fourteen days (of illness), his death would have been a sudden death.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Condolences are not offered except at the grave. Then they should disperse, in case an event were to occur regarding the deceased, so they would hear the sound.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The offering of condolences is [performed] to the bereaved after the burial.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Consolation (ta'ziyah) is not offered except at the grave. Then they disperse, so that an event does not occur regarding the deceased, and they hear the sound.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The offering of condolences is the Obligation after the burial.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, who said: When Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) died, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out and walked in front of the coffin without shoes or a cloak.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the owner of the calamity (bereaved) that he should place down his cloak until the people know that he is the owner of the calamity.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rifa'ah al-Nakhhas, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) comforted a man for his son, so he said: 'Allah is better for your son than you are, and the reward of Allah is better for you than your son.' So when his sobbing reached him afterwards, he returned to him and said to him: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) has passed away, so what is for you with it is similar.' So he said, 'My son was a drunkard.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'In front of him are three qualities: the testimony that there is no god except Allah, and the mercy of Allah, and the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So one of them will not be missed for him, if Allah wills.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the owner of the calamity (bereaved) that he should not wear a cloak (outer garment) and that he should be in a shirt (inner garment) until he is recognized (as a bereaved).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: I saw Musa (peace be upon him) offering condolences before the burial and after it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mihran, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second wrote to a man: 'You mentioned your bereavement with your son Ali, and mentioned that he was the most beloved of your children to you, and likewise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, only takes from the parent and others the purest of what is with his family to magnify through it the reward of the bereaved by the bereavement. So may Allah magnify your reward, and make your consolation good, and strengthen your heart, indeed He is Powerful, and may Allah hasten the successor to you, and I hope that Allah has done so, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comforts one who is grieving, will be clothed in a garment of honor in the Standing (Place of Reckoning) with which he will be beautified.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever consoles a bereaved person, he will have the like of his reward, without anything being reduced from the reward of the bereaved.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who dies while the child is moving in her belly: Should her belly be split and the child taken out? He said: Yes, and her belly would be stitched.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When a woman dies and there is a child in her womb that is moving, and it is feared for him, then split open her belly and extract the child.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a woman whose child dies in her womb, and it is feared for her: 'There is no harm if the man inserts his hand, cuts it off, and extracts it, when the women are not gentle with it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The miscarried child, when four months are completed for it, is washed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about the Salat (prayer) upon the child, when should Salat be prayed upon him? He said: When he has reasoning (acquires intellect). I said: When does the Salat become obligatory upon him? So he said: When he is a son of six years of age; and the Fasting is when he can endure it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, who said: A son of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) died, and he was informed of his death. So he ordered that he be washed and shrouded, and he walked with him and prayed upon him. A prayer mat was placed, so he stood upon it, then he stood at his grave until he finished, then he departed, and I departed with him until I was walking alongside him. So he said: 'Indeed, Salat was not performed upon one like this, and he was a boy of three years old. Ali (peace be upon him) used to order that he be buried and Salat not be performed upon him, but the people did something, so we do similar to it.' He said: I said, 'So when is Salat obligatory upon him?' So he said: 'When he has intellect for Salat, and is a boy of six years old.' I said, 'So what do you say regarding the children?' So he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about them, so he said: Allah is more Knowing of what they were doing.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about the miscarried child (siqt), how to deal with it. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'The miscarried child is buried with its blood, in its place.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), passed away, three Sunnahs were enacted regarding him.' As for the first: when he died, the sun was eclipsed, and the people said, 'The sun is eclipsed due to the loss of the Messenger of Allah's son.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and lauded Him, then said: 'O people! The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah; they move by His command, obedient to Him. They do not eclipse for the death of anyone nor for his life. So if they eclipse, or one of them, pray.' Then he descended from the pulpit and prayed Salat al-Kusuf (Prayer of the Eclipse) with the people. When he gave the greeting of peace, he said: 'O Ali! Arise and prepare my son.' So Ali (peace be upon him) arose, washed Ibrahim, embalmed him, and shrouded him. Then he went out with him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) proceeded until he brought him to his grave. The people said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forgot to pray Salat upon Ibrahim due to the grief that entered him.' So he stood upright and said: 'O people! Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me with what you said. You claimed that I forgot to pray Salat upon my son due to the grief that entered me. Indeed, it is not as you thought, it is not as you imagined, but the Subtle, the Aware has prescribed five Salats for you, and made for your deceased one Takbir from each Salat, and He commanded me that I should not pray Salat except upon one who prays Salat.' Then he said: 'O Ali! Descend and dig the Lahd (side niche) for my son.' So he descended and dug the Lahd for Ibrahim in his grave. The people said, 'It is not befitting for anyone to descend into the grave of his son, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not do so.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'O people! It is not forbidden upon you to descend into the graves of your children, but I do not fear that if one of you loosens the shroud from his son, the Shaytan will play with him, causing grief to enter him that will nullify his reward.' Then he turned away (peace b

Ali, from Ali ibn Shiyrah, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Husayn al-Harshoush, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The people are speaking against us and refuting our statement that Salat (funeral prayer) is not prayed over a child because he has not prayed (Salat). They say: Salat is not prayed except over one who has prayed. So we say: Yes. They say: What is your view if a Christian or a Jew were to become Muslim, then died immediately, what is the answer regarding him?' He said: 'Say to them: What is your view if this one who became Muslim immediately then forged a lie against a person, what would be obligated upon him regarding his forgery?' If they say: 'The Hadd (legal punishment) is obligated upon him,' then it is said to them: 'So if this child who has not prayed were to forge a lie against a person, would the Hadd be obligated upon him?' If they say: 'No,' then it is said to them: 'You are correct. Salat is only prayed over one upon whom Salat and the Hadds are obligated, and Salat is not prayed over one upon whom neither Salat nor the Hadds are obligated.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Hasan the first (peace be upon him) Regarding the one struck by lightning and the drowned: He (peace be upon him) said: They are awaited for three days, unless their state changes before that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the drowned person: is he washed? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he is absolved (of minor impurities).' I said: 'And how is he absolved?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is left for three days before he is buried; and similarly, the one struck by lightning, for perhaps they think he has died and he has not died.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: The drowned one is washed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa from Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The drowned one is withheld until his state changes and it is known that he has died, then he is washed and enshrouded. He said: And he was asked about the one struck by lightning, so he said: If he is struck, he is withheld for two days, then he is washed and enshrouded.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, the brother of Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Five are awaited with them unless they alter: the drowned, the one struck by lightning, the one with intestinal ailments, the one crushed, and the one subjected to fumes.'

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: The people in Mecca were struck by many lightning bolts during one of the years, and a great number of people died from that. So I entered upon Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and he began speaking without me asking him: 'It is befitting for the drowned one and the one struck by lightning that they be awaited for three days; they are not buried unless a breeze comes from him indicating his death.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, it seems as if you are informing me that many people have been buried alive.' He said, 'Yes, O Ali! Many people have been buried alive; they did not die except inside their graves.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who is killed in the Way of Allah, should he be washed, enshrouded, and embalmed? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is buried as he is in his clothes, except if there is still breath in him and then he dies, for then he is washed, enshrouded, embalmed, and prayer is performed upon him. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed prayer upon Hamza and enshrouded him because he had been stripped.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ismail ibn Jabir and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I said to him, 'How do you view the martyr, should he be buried with his blood?' He said, 'Yes, in his clothes with his blood, and he is neither embalmed nor washed, and he is buried as he is.' Then he said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) buried his uncle Hamza in his clothes with the blood in which he was struck, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) cloaked him with his own cloak, but it was short from his legs. So he called for lemongrass for him and placed it upon him, and prayed seventy prayers upon him, and exclaimed seventy takbeers upon him.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Abu Maryam who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The martyr, if he has breath (ramaq), is washed, shrouded, embalmed, and prayer is performed over him; and if he does not have breath, he is buried in his clothes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu al-Jawza, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Remove from the martyr the fur coat, the shoes, the beret, the turban, the belt, and the trousers, unless blood has touched them. If blood has touched them, they are left; and nothing tight is left upon him except that it is loosened.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who is killed in the way of Allah is buried in his clothes, and he is not washed unless the Muslims find him while he still has some breath left, and then he dies afterwards; in that case, he is washed, enshrouded, and embalmed. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) enshrouded Hamza in his clothes and did not wash him, but he prayed over him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man who is eaten by predatory wild animals and birds, so his bones remain without flesh; how should he be dealt with? He said: He is washed, enshrouded, Salat is prayed over him, and he is buried. And if the deceased is in two halves, Salat is prayed over the half in which is the heart.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a killed person is found and only flesh is found without bones for him, he is not prayed upon; and if bones are found without flesh, he is prayed upon.
He said, 'And it is reported that one should not pray Salat upon the head, when it is isolated from the body'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man is found to have been killed, if a complete limb is found for him, he is prayed upon and buried; and if a complete limb is not found for him, he is not prayed upon and is buried.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, raising it (narrating) from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When a piece is cut off from a man, it is considered dead (for ritual purity purposes), and when a man touches it, then for every part that contains a bone, the ritual bath (ghusl) becomes obligatory upon the one who touched it; and if there is no bone in it, then there is no ritual bath upon him.

Sahl, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the man is cut in the middle into two halves, Salat (prayer) would be prayed upon that in which is the heart.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abu Khalid, who said: Wash everything from the deceased who drowned, and the one eaten by the predatory wild animals, and everything except the one who was killed between the two swords. So if he had a remnant of life (breath), he would be washed, otherwise, no.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who died in a ship in the sea, how should he be dealt with? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is placed in a barrel, its head is sealed, and it is thrown into the water.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding the man who dies with the people in the sea, he said: He is washed, and enshrouded, and Salat is prayed over him, and weighted, and thrown into the sea.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man dies in the ship and it is not possible to reach the coast, he is enshrouded, embalmed, wrapped in a cloth, and cast into the water.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a group who were on a journey, walking along the coast of the sea, and they found a dead man, nude, whom the sea had cast ashore? They themselves were semi-naked, having nothing upon them except an izar (loincloth). How should they pray Salat upon him while he is nude, and they have no surplus clothing with which to enshroud him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A pit is dug for him, and he is placed in his Lahd (grave niche), and a brick/stone is placed upon his private part so that his private part is covered by the brick/stone. Then they pray Salat upon him, then he is buried.' He (the narrator) said: 'I said: So they do not pray Salat upon him when he is buried?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One does not pray Salat upon the deceased after he is buried, nor does one pray Salat upon him while he is nude until his private part is covered.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' Kirdeyn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The stoned man and the stoned woman are washed, embalmed, and enshrouded before that, then they are stoned, and Salat is prayed upon them; and the one killed in (legal) retaliation is at that status. He is washed, embalmed, enshrouded, and Salat is prayed upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the crucified one, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that my grandfather (peace be upon him) prayed Salat upon his uncle?' I said, 'I know that, but I do not understand it clearly.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I shall clarify it for you. If the face of the crucified one was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his right shoulder; and if his back was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. For indeed, between the East and the West is the Qiblah. And if his left shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his right shoulder, and if his right shoulder was towards the Qiblah, so stand by his left shoulder. And however he was inclined, do not cease to be by his shoulder, and let your face be towards what is between the East and the West, and do not face towards him nor face away from his back completely.' Abu Hashim said, 'And I have understood it, Allah willing! I understood it, by Allah!'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Yaqoubi, from Musa ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Muyassar, from Harun ibn Al-Jahm, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not leave the crucified one after three (days), until he is brought down and buried.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was killed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded Fatimah (peace be upon her) to prepare food for Asma bint Umays for three days, and to go to her with her womenfolk, and stay with her for three days. Thus, the Sunnah became established that food be prepared for the bereaved for three days.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A mourning gathering (ma'tam) is prepared for the family of the deceased for three days, from the day he died.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the neighbours of the bereaved that they should feed him food for three days.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz or someone else, said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) bequeathed three hundred dirhams for his mourning ceremony, and he considered this to be from the Sunnah, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Prepare food for the family of Ja'far, for they have been preoccupied (with their grief).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah al-Kahili, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'My wife and the wife of Ibn Marid go out to the mourning gatherings, so I forbid them. My wife says to me: If it is forbidden, forbid us from it until we leave it; and if it is not forbidden, for what reason do you forbid us? So when a death occurs in our family, no one comes to us.' He said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'You are asking me about the rights. My father (peace be upon him) used to send my mother and Umm Farwa to fulfill the rights of the people of Medina.'

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever visits a Muslim person during his illness, on that day seventy thousand angels send blessings upon him — if it was in the morning, until the evening, and if it was in the evening, until the morning — along with that, for him is a corner in Paradise.
Whoever visits a patient, seventy thousand angels accompany him seeking forgiveness for him until he returns to his house.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whichever believer visits a sick believer, he plunges into divine mercy with a deep plunging. So when he sits, the mercy overwhelms him. So when he departs, God assigns seventy thousand angels to be with him, seeking forgiveness for him and seeking mercy for him, and they say: 'You have done good, and Paradise has been made good for you' up to that very hour the next day. And there would be for him, O Abu Hamza, a kharif in Paradise. I said: And what is the kharif, may I be your ransom? He said: A vast expanse in Paradise that a rider would travel in it for forty years.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from a man from his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whichever believer visits a believer for the sake of God, Mighty and Majestic, during his illness, God will appoint for him an angel from the visitors who will visit him in his grave and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits a sick person from among the Muslims, Allah appoints with him forever seventy thousand angels who envelop his dwelling, glorifying therein, sanctifying, proclaiming the unity of God, and proclaiming God's greatness until the Day of Resurrection — half of their prayers being for the visitor of the sick.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whichever believer visits a sick believer during his illness in the morning, seventy thousand angels would escort him. So when he sits, mercy would overwhelm him, and they would seek forgiveness from God, Mighty and Majestic, for him until the evening; and if he visits him in the evening, there would be for him the like of that until the morning.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits a sick person, Allah — Mighty and Majestic — assigns an angel with him, visiting him in his grave.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whichever believer visits a sick believer in the morning, seventy thousand angels escort him; and when he sits, mercy overwhelms him and they seek forgiveness for him until evening. And if he visits him in the evening, he shall have the like of that until the morning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It was among what Musa (Moses) confided to his Lord, that he said: O Lord! What reward is reached by visiting the sick? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: I will appoint an angel with him, visiting him in his grave until his resurrection.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits a patient, a caller from the sky will call out to him by name: O so-and-so, you have done good, and your walking (visiting) has been made good for you by the rewards from Paradise.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'e, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A son whom a man precedes (in death) is superior to seventy sons whom he leaves behind after him, all of them having ridden the cavalry horses and fought in the Way of Allah.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) visited Khadijah when her son Qasim passed away, and she was crying. So he said to her: 'What makes you cry?' She said: 'The milk flows, so I weep.' He said: 'O Khadijah! Would you not be pleased when it is the Day of Resurrection that you come to the Gate of Paradise and he is standing there, so he takes your hand and enters you into Paradise and settles you in its best part? And that is for every believer. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more Wise and Generous than to deprive the believer of the fruit of his heart and then punish him after it forever.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mihran, who said: A man wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the Second, complaining to him of his bereavement with his son and the intensity of the grief that had entered him. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Do you not know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chooses from the wealth of the Believer and from his children, his soul, in order to recompense him for that?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When a child of a believer dies, and Allah is most Knowing of what the servant said, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to His angels: 'Did you take the child of so-and-so?' So they say: 'Yes, our Lord.' So He says: 'So what did My servant say?' They say: 'He praised You and said Istirja (returned to Allah).' So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'You took the fruit of his heart and the delight of his eyes,' 'and he praised Me and said Istirja.' 'Build for him a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, who said: He narrated to us Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: He narrated to us Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He loves a servant, takes (deaths) the child most beloved to him.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever from the Muslims has two children who precede him (to the next life), they will be reckoned in the Presence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as a veil for him from the Fire, by the Permission of Allah, the Exalted.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When Tahir, the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), passed away, the Messenger of Allah forbade Khadijah from weeping. She said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, but the milk was flowing over him, so I cried.' He said: 'Would you not be pleased that you find him standing at the gate of Paradise? When he sees you, he will take your hand and enter you into Paradise, in its purest place and most fragrant.' She said: 'And is that so?' He said: 'Allah, the Most Honourable and the Most Benevolent, is not one to deprive a servant of the fruit of his heart, so that he remains patient, exercises self-restraint, and praises Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and then punishes him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The reward of the believer from his child when he dies is Paradise, whether he is patient or is not patient.

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman bin Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdullah or Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is astounded by the man whose child dies while he is praising Allah, so He says: 'O My angels! My servant, I took his beloved (child), and he is praising Me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever has children who precede him (to the afterlife), they will be reckoned in the Presence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as a veil for him from the Fire, by the Permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Suleiman ibn 'Amr al-Nakha'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is struck with a bereavement, let him recall his bereavement with that of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), for it is among the greatest of the calamities.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Thaqafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: If you are struck by a calamity in your own self, or in your wealth, or in your children, then remember your calamity with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for the creatures have never been struck by a calamity like his, at all.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Ju'fi, from a man, from his father, who said: When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was martyred, al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent news to al-Husayn (peace be upon him), while he was in al-Mada'in. So when he read the letter, he said: 'O what a calamity! How great it is.' This was in addition to what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said: 'Whoever among you is struck by a calamity, let him recall his calamity with me, for no calamity greater than it will befall him.' And he (peace be upon him and his family) spoke the truth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, they heard a voice but did not see a person, saying: 'Every soul shall taste death, but you shall only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection; then whoever is removed from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise, he indeed has succeeded.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'In Allah is a replacement for every dying one, and a consolation for every bereavement, and a compensation for what is lost. So rely on Allah and hope in Him, and the deprived one is only he who is deprived of the reward.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Suleiman ibn Sama'ah from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to them, and the Prophet was enshrouded, and in the house were Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). He said: Peace be upon you, O People of the House of Mercy! Every soul shall taste death. And only will you be given in full your reward on the Day of Resurrection; so whoever is removed away from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise he indeed has succeeded. And what is the life of the world except the enjoyment of deception. Indeed, in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a consolation from every calamity, and a successor to every dying one, and a attainment for what is lost. So in Allah rely, and to Him hope, for indeed the one who is afflicted is the one who is deprived of the reward. This is my last stepping of the world. They said: We heard the voice but did not see the person.

From him, from Salama, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shammam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, condolences came to them; a messenger arrived whom they heard but did not see in person, so he said: 'Peace be upon you, O People of the Household, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' Every soul shall taste death, but you shall only be paid your full reward on the Day of Resurrection; then whoever is removed far from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise, he indeed has succeeded. And what is the life of the world except the enjoyment of delusion. In Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is consolation for every calamity and a replacement for every deceased one, and a attainment for what is lost. So rely on Allah and hope in Him, for the deprived one is he who is deprived of the reward. And peace be upon you.

From him, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Similar to it, and there is an increase in it: 'I said, Who were the ones in the house? He said: 'Ali, Fatima, Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them).

From him, from Salma, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Armani, from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, a visitor came to them and stood at the door of the house, so he greeted them, then said: Peace be upon you, O Progeny of Muhammad! Every soul shall taste death, but only you will be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is removed from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise, he indeed has succeeded. And the life of this world is but the enjoyment of delusion. In Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a successor to every perishing one and a consolation for every calamity and a compensation for what is lost. So trust in Allah and rely upon Him, and in His Help for you during the calamity, so be pleased. Indeed, the one who is truly afflicted is the one who is deprived of the reward. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. And they did not see anyone [else]. So some of those in the house said: 'This is an angel from the sky whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent to you to console you.' And some of them said: 'This is al-Khadir (peace be upon him) who has come to you to console you with your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Al-Hasan ibn Ali, altogether, from Abi Jameela, from Jabir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is al-jaza' (panic/intense grief)?' He said: 'The most intense al-jaza' is shouting with woe, wailing, slapping the face and chest, and pulling out the hair from the forelocks.' And whoever establishes lamentation, he has abandoned patience and taken to a path other than its way. And whoever is patient, says 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' (I have returned to my Lord), and praises Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then he is pleased with what Allah has done, and his reward falls upon Allah. And whoever does not do that, divine decree flows upon him, and he is condemned, and Allah the Exalted nullifies his reward.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Similar to it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Aamir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ali ibn Ismail al-Mithammi from Rabi' ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, patience and affliction race to the Believer, so the affliction comes to him while he is patient; and indeed, panic and affliction race to the Infidel, so the affliction comes to him while he is panicking.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Striking the Muslim's hand upon his thigh during bereavement is a nullification of his reward.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Marouf ibn Harrabouz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no servant who is struck by a calamity, so he says the Istirja (Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un) upon remembering the calamity, and he is patient when it strikes him suddenly, except that Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sins; and every time he remembers his calamity and says Istirja upon the remembrance of the calamity, Allah will forgive him every sin he acquired in between.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Dawood Bin Razeyn, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who remembers his difficulty (bereavement), and even though it may be after a while, Surely we are for Allah and to Him we are returning and the praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds O Allah! Recompense me upon my difficulty and Replace upon me that which is superior than it, would have for him from the Recompense, similar to what he had during the first shock.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: O Is'haq! Do not count as a calamity one upon which you are granted patience and have thereby obligated for yourself from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the reward; rather, the calamity is that from which its owner is deprived of its reward and recompense when he does not exercise patience at its occurrence.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from the wife of Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The shouting/crying out upon the deceased is not befitting, nor is tearing of the clothes.

Sahl, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The striking of a man's hand upon his thigh during bereavement leads to the nullification of his reward.

Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Fuzayl ibn Muyassar, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man came and complained to him of a calamity that had befallen him. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Know that if you are patient, you will be rewarded; and if you are not patient, the decree of Allah which He has decreed upon you will still pass over you, and you will be excused (or burdened with sin depending on interpretation).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Mahziyar, from Quteiba Al-A'sha, who said: I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to visit a son of his, and I found him at the door; he was worried and sad. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, how is the child?' He said, 'By Allah, he is still with it.' Then he entered and stayed for a while, then came out to us, and his face had turned pale, and the change and sadness had gone. He said, 'I hoped that the child had recovered, so I said, 'How is the child, may I be sacrificed for you?' He said, 'And he has gone to his Way.' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you were worried and sad while he was alive, and I saw your state at this time, and he has died in a state other than that. So how is this?' So he said, 'We, the People of the Household, only panic before the calamity. So when the Command of Allah occurs, we are pleased with its decree and submit to its command.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Shouting (aloud) over the deceased is not correct, nor is it befitting, but the people do not understand it, and patience is better.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Alaa' ibn Kamil, who said: I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a crier from the house cried out. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) stood up, then sat down, recited the Istirja', and returned to his conversation until he finished it. Then he said: 'We love that we are in good health regarding ourselves, our children, and our wealth. So when the Decree occurs, it is not for us to love what Allah does not love for us.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from one of our companions, who said: A group of people came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and found a son of his who was sick. They saw concern and grief in him, and he would not remain at rest. He said, 'By Allah, if anything happens to him, we fear that we will see from him what we dislike.' He said, 'They did not wait long before they heard the outcry upon him. Behold, he had come out to them with a cheerful face, in a state different from what he had been in before. They said to him, 'May Allah sacrifice us for you! We were afraid that, from what we saw of you, if it were to happen, we would see from you what would sadden us.' So he said to them, 'We love to be healthy regarding those we love. But when the Command of Allah comes, we submit regarding what we love.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Among what Musa (peace be upon him) whispered to his Lord was that he said: 'O Lord! What is for the one who comforts the bereaved?' He said: 'I shall shade him in My Shade on the Day there is no shade except My Shade.'
