Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abdullah, from Ali ibn Mansur, from Ismail Al-Jawzi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comforts one who is grieving, will be clothed on the Day of Standing (Resurrection) with a garment of honor that will be loved for it.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Umari, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who comforts the bereaved, Allah will shade him in the Shade of His Throne on the Day when there is no shade except His.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comforts a person in bereavement, he will have a reward similar to that of the bereaved, without any reduction from the reward of the bereaved.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the deceased dies, Allah sends an angel to the most pained one of his family, and he wipes upon his heart, causing him to forget the anguish of grief; and had it not for that, the world would not be inhabited (by people living through the grief).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, prolonged His favor upon His servants by three things: He cast the smell upon them after the soul (departure), and had it not been for that, a friend would not bury a friend; and He cast the comfort upon them, and had it not been for that, the lineages would be cut off; and He cast the insect upon this grain, and had it not been for that, their kings would have hoarded it just as they hoard gold and silver.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When the deceased dies, Allah sends an angel to the most pained one of his family, and he wipes upon his heart, causing him to forget the anguish of grief; and had it not for that, the world would not be inhabited.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the visitation of the graves, He said: 'They (the deceased) derive comfort from you, so when you are absent from them, they become scared/lonely.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the visitation of the graves and the construction of the mosques therein, so he said: As for the visitation to the graves, there is no problem with it, and do not build the mosques by them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Fatima (peace be upon her) lived after her father for seventy-five days; she was not seen smiling nor laughing. She would visit the graves of the martyrs twice every Friday, on Monday and Thursday, and she would say: 'Over there was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); over there were the polytheists.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Does the believer know the one who visits his grave?' He said, 'Yes, and he does not cease to derive comfort with him for as long as he is by his grave. So when he arises and leaves from his grave, loneliness enters into him from his leaving from his grave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How is the greeting to the inhabitants of the graves?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, you should say: Peace be upon the people of the dwellings, from the Muslims and the Believers. You have preceded us, and we, God willing, will be joining you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Amr bin Abu al-Miqdam, who said: I passed by Al-Baqi' cemetery with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so we passed by the grave of a man from the people of Kufa from the Shias. He (peace be upon him) paused at it and said: 'O Allah, have mercy on his estrangement, and connect his loneliness, and comfort his solitude, and settle upon him from Your mercy that which makes him independent of the mercy of others besides You, and join him with those who used to be his friends/protectors.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: You should say: 'Peace be upon you, from the abodes of a believing people, and we, if Allah wills, will be joining you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How is the greeting to be upon the inhabitants of the graves?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say.' Peace be upon the inhabitants of the houses, from the Muslims and the Believers. May Allah have mercy on the preceding ones from us and the delayed ones, and we, if Allah wills, are joining with you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: I was in Fayd, so I walked with Ali ibn Bilal to the grave of Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'. So Ali ibn Bilal said to me, 'The inhabitant of this grave narrated from Al-Rida (peace be upon him):' 'He said: Whoever comes to the grave of his brother, then places his hand upon the grave and recites 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylati al-qadr' seven times, will be secure from the Great Panic, or the Day of Panic.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Visit your dead, for they rejoice at your visitation, and let each of you seek his need at the grave of his father and at the grave of his mother, with whatever he supplicates for them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Believer visits his family, so he sees what he loves, and it is veiled from him what he dislikes; and the Infidel visits his family, so he sees what he dislikes, and it is veiled from him what he loves. He (peace be upon him) said: And among them is one who visits every Friday, and among them is one who visits according to the measure of his deeds.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no believer, nor any infidel, except that he comes to his family at the decline of the sun. So when he sees his family doing righteous deeds, he praises Allah for that; and when the infidel sees his family doing righteous deeds, regret befalls him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the deceased visiting his family. He said: 'Yes'. So I said, 'In how many visitations?' He said: '(Once) during the Friday, and (once) during the month, and (once) during the year, in accordance with his status'. So I said, 'In which image does he come over to them?' He said: 'In the image of a nice bird, falling upon their walls, and looking upon them. So if he sees them with goodness, he is happy; and if he sees them with evil and needy, he is with grief and gloom'.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Dorust al-Wasiti, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abdul Rahman al-Qasir, who said: I said to him, 'Does the believer visit his family?' He said, 'Yes. He seeks permission from his Lord, so He grants it. He sends two angels with him, and they come to them in one of the forms of birds, alighting in his house, looking at them, and hearing their speech.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), 'Does the believer visit his family?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'How often?' He said, 'According to their merits. Among them is one who visits every day, and among them is one who visits every two days, and among them is one who visits every three days.' He said, 'Then I perceived in the flow of his speech that he was saying: The one with the lowest status among them visits every Friday.' I said, 'At what time?' He said, 'At the decline of the sun, and the like of that.' I said, 'In what form?' He said, 'In the form of a sparrow, or smaller than that. So Allah, the Exalted, sends an angel with him, who shows him what pleases him and conceals from him what he dislikes, so he sees what pleases him and returns with delight of the eye.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Bashir al-Dahhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Abu Jameela from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the enemy of Allah is carried to his grave, he calls out to his pallbearers, "Do you not hear me, O my brethren? I am complaining to you what your wretched brother has fallen into. The enemy of Allah deceived me, so he imprisoned me and did not release me, and swore to me that he was an advisor to me, so he overwhelmed me."' "And I complain to you of the world which deceived me until when I was greedy to it, it knocked me down. And I complain to you of the selfish friends who gave me hope, then disavowed from me and abandoned me. And I complain to you of the children whom I protected and preferred them over myself, so they consumed my wealth, and betrayed me. And I complain to you of wealth which I prevented from it the Right of Allah, so its consequences were upon me and its benefits were for others. And I complain to you of a house which I spent upon it my earnings and it became a dwelling for others." "And I complain to you of the prolonged boarding in my grave calling out to me: 'I am a house of insects! I am a house of darkness, and the loneliness, and the straitness! O brothers! Withhold me whatever you are able to and be cautioned of the likes of what I face, for I have received news of the Fire, and the disgrace, and the belittling, and the Wrath of the Almighty, the Compeller.' O my regret upon what I neglected regarding the Side of Allah! And O prolonged wailing! So there is not for me a sympathetic intercessor to be merciful to me. So, if there was a possibility of return for me I would be from the Believers'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) (He narrated) similar to it, and added to it: 'So he does not stop calling out until he is placed in his grave. So when he enters his pit, the soul returns to his body and the two Angels of the Grave come to him, so they test him.' He (the narrator) said, 'And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) would weep when he mentioned this Hadith.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not know what to do with the people. If we narrate to them what we heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), they laugh, and if we remain silent, it is not bearable for us.' He said, so Zamrah ibn Ma'bad said, 'Narrate to us.' So he said: 'Do you know what the enemy of Allah says when he is carried on his bier?' So we said, 'No.' He said: 'For he says to his bearers: Do you not hear that I am complaining to you? The enemy of Allah deceived me and imprisoned me, then did not release me. And I complain to you of brothers with whom I established brotherhood, so they abandoned me. And I complain to you of children whom I protected, so they abandoned me. And I complain to you of a house in which I spent my earnings, so its inhabitants became others than me. So be kind to me and do not hasten.' He said, so Zamrah said, 'O Abu al-Hasan! If he speaks with this speech, he is likely to pounce upon the necks of those who carry him.' He said, so Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, if Zamrah has ridiculed the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then seize him with a seizure of grief/sorrow.' He said, so he remained for forty days, then died, and a slave of his was present with him. He said, so when he was buried, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came to him and sat by him, and said to him, 'From where have you come, O so-and-so?' He said, 'From the funeral of Zamrah. I placed my face upon him when the soil was leveled over him, and I heard his voice. By Allah, I recognized it just as I recognized it when he was alive.' 'He was saying: Woe to you, O Zamrah ibn Ma'bad! Today every friend has abandoned you, and your destination has become the Hellfire, wherein is your dwelling, your overnight stay, and your daytime stay.' He said, so Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'I ask Allah for well-being. This is the recompense of the one who ridicules the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the grave has speech every day. It says: 'I am a house of estrangement, I am a house of loneliness, I am a house of the worm, I am the grave. I am a garden from the gardens of Paradise, or a pit from the pits of the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I heard you saying: All of our Shias are in Paradise, in the state they were in.' He said, 'I have told you the truth. All of them, by Allah, are in Paradise.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, but sins are many and major.' He said, 'As for the Day of Resurrection, all of you will be in Paradise by the intercession of the Obeyed Prophet or the Successor of the Prophet. But, by Allah, I fear for you in the Barzakh.' I said, 'And what is the Barzakh?' He said, 'The grave, from the time of his death until the Day of Resurrection.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'When you attend to the dying person before he dies, prompt him with the testimony that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no partner for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'You prompt your dying ones at the time of death with "There is no god but Allah," while we prompt our dying ones with "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family."'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When you find a man during the agony of death, instruct him with the words of relief: There is no god except Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god except Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and whatever is in them and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne; and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. He (the narrator) said: Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Had I found Ikrima at the time of death, I would have benefited him.' It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'With what would he have benefited him?' He said: 'He would have instructed him with what you are upon (i.e., al-Wilayah).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Kufi, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said: A man from my household fell ill, so I went to visit him as a sick-visitor. I said to him, 'O son of my brother! I have a piece of advice for you — will you accept it?' He said, 'Yes.' So I said, 'Say: I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no associate for Him.' So he testified to that. I said, 'This will not benefit you unless it comes from you with firm conviction.' So he affirmed that it was from him with conviction. Then I said, 'Say: I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.' So he testified to that. I said, 'This will not benefit you until it comes from you with firm conviction.' So he affirmed that it was from him with conviction. Then I said, 'Say: I testify that Ali is his successor, and he is the Caliph after him, and the Imam of obligatory obedience after him.' So he testified to that. I said to him, 'You will never benefit from that until it comes from you with firm conviction.' So he affirmed that it was from him with conviction. Then I named the Imams one by one, and he acknowledged each and affirmed that he was upon conviction. It was not long before the man died, and his family grieved over him with intense grief. He (the narrator) said: I was absent from them, then came back to them after that and found them in good condition. I said, 'How do you find yourselves? How is your composure, O woman?' She said, 'By Allah! We were struck by a great calamity with the death of so-and-so — may Allah have mercy on him — but what consoled my heart was a dream I saw last night.' I said, 'And what was that dream?' She said, 'I saw so-and-so — meaning the deceased — alive and well.' I said, '(Are you) So-and-so?' He said, 'Yes.' I said to him, 'Had you not died?' He said, 'Yes, but I was saved by the words that Abu Bakr had instilled in me, and had it not been for that, I would nearly have been destroyed.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We were in his presence, and in his presence was Humran, when a slave of his entered and said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is Ikrama in the throes of death' — and he used to hold the views of the Kharijites, but he was also devoted to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to us: 'Wait for me until I return to you.' And we said: 'Yes.' He was not long before he returned, and said: 'Know that had I reached Ikrama before the soul had settled at its place, I would have taught him certain words he would have benefitted by. But I found him and the soul had already settled at its place.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is that speech?' He said: 'It is, by God, what you all hold. Therefore, instruct your dying ones at the time of death with the testimony that there is no god except God, and the Wilayah.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no one to whom death presents itself except that Iblees assigns one of his devils to command him to commit disbelief and to make him doubt his religion until his soul departs. So the one who was a believer, he will not have power over him. Thus when you attend your dying ones, instruct them in the testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His Messenger, until he dies. And in another narration, he said: Instruct him with the words of relief (kalimat al-faraj) and the two testimonies, and enumerate for him the acknowledgement of the Imams (peace be upon them) one after one, until the speech is cut off from him.

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say, whenever death came to any member of his household: 'Say: There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and whatever is between them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne; and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all the worlds. When the sick person said it, he would say: 'Go, for there is no harm upon you.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! Even if an idol worshipper were to recite what you (believers) recite at the exit of his soul, the Fire would not consume anything from his body, ever!'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered upon a man from the Clan of Hashim who was in the throes of death. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Say: There is no god except Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. There is no god except Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and all that is between them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. So he said it, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Praise be to Allah Who rescued him from the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Abi Salama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Death came to a man, so it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has been presented with death.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood up, and with him were some of his companions, until they came to him while he was unconscious. He said, 'O Angel of Death, restrain from the man until I question him.' So the man regained consciousness. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What did you see?' He said, 'I saw a lot of whiteness and a lot of darkness.' He said, 'So which of the two was nearer to you?' He said, 'The darkness.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Say, O Allah, forgive me the abundance of my disobedience to You, and accept from me the little of my obedience to You.' So he said it. Then unconsciousness came upon him, so he said, 'O Angel of Death, lighten from him until I question him.' So the man awoke. He said, 'What did you see?' He said, 'I saw a lot of whiteness and a lot of darkness.' He said, 'So which of the two was nearer to you?' He said, 'The whiteness.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'May Allah forgive your companion.' He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'When you are present with a dying person, say to him this speech, for him to say it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Rashid, from al-Murtajil ibn Ma'mar, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Ubadah al-Asadi, from Habbat al-Urini, who said: I went out with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to the back (of Kufa), so he paused at the Valley of Peace as if addressing a group of people. So I stood due to his standing until I was exhausted. Then I sat until I was tired. Then I stood until there came to me the likes of what came to me the first time. Then I sat down until I was tired. Then I stood and gathered my robe and I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! I sympathize with you from the long standing, so rest for a while.' Then I spread the robe in order for him to sit upon it. So he said to me, 'O Habbat! It was only a discussion with a Believer, or comforting him.' I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! And they are like that?' He said, 'Yes, and if the covering is uncovered for you, you would see them in groups and groups discussing.' So I said, 'Bodily or in spirit form?' So he said, 'The souls. There is none from a Believer who dies in a spot from the spots of the earth, except that it is said to his soul: 'Join at the valley of peace, and it is a spot from the Garden of Eden'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Umar, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'My brother is in Baghdad and I fear he will die there.' He said, 'What does it matter where he dies? Indeed, no believer remains in the east or west of the earth except that Allah will gather his soul to the Valley of Peace.' I said to him, 'And where is the Valley of Peace?' He said, 'At the back of Al-Kufa. Indeed, I see them as groups and groups, sitting and conversing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, they report that the souls of the believers are in the craws of green birds around the Throne.' He said, 'No, the believer is more prestigious to Allah than for Him to place his soul in the craw of a bird, but they are in bodies like their own bodies.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ismail ibn Mihran from Dorust ibn Abu Mansur from Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the souls are in the form of bodies in a tree in Paradise, recognizing each other and asking about one another. So when the soul arrives among the souls, they say, 'Leave it alone, for it has escaped from a great terror.' Then they ask it, 'What happened to so-and-so? And what happened to so-and-so?' If it says to them, 'I left him alive,' they hope for him; and if it says to them, 'He has perished,' they say, 'He has perished! Perished!'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the souls of the Believers, so he (peace be upon him) said: '(They are) in chambers in Paradise, eating from its food and drinking from its drinks, and they are saying: Our Lord! Establish the Hour for us and Accomplish for us what You have promised us, and Join our later ones with our former ones.'

Ali, from his father, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from Yunus ibn Hammad, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the deceased dies, they gather at his presence asking him about those who have passed away and those who remain. So if one had died and did not come to them, they say, 'He has perished, he has perished.' And some of them say to others, 'Leave him until he settles from what has passed upon him from death.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn 'Abdi from Yunus ibn Zabyan who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'What are the people saying regarding the souls of the Believers?' I said: 'They say they are in the craws of green birds in lamps beneath the Throne.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! The Believer is more prestigious to Allah than for Him to make his soul be in the craw of a bird. O Yunus! If that were the case, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali, and Fatima, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and the Proximate Angels (peace be upon them) would come to him. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, captures him, He makes that soul into a form like its form in the world, so they eat and drink. And when the visitor comes to them, they recognize him by that very image which he had in the world.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zur’at, from Abu Baseer who said, I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We are narrating about the souls of the Believer that they are in the craws of green birds grazing in the Paradise, and sheltering to the lamps beneath the Throne'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Then, what is in the craws of birds?' I said, 'So where are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'In a Garden like in the (shape of) bodies in the Paradise'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the souls of the Polytheists, so he said: 'They are in the Fire, being punished.' They are saying, 'Our Lord! Do not establish for us the Hour, and do not bring to completion for us what You have promised us, and do not join our later ones with our former ones.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the souls of the disbelievers are in the Fire of Hell, being presented to it. They say: 'Our Lord, do not establish the Hour for us, and do not bring to completion what You promised us, and do not join our later ones with our former ones.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, by a chain of his, said:

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The worst water on the face of the earth is the water of Barhout, and it is that which is in Hadhramaut, upon which the spirits of the disbelievers drink.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of the Jews are the Jews of Baysaan, and the worst of the Christians are the Christians of Najran, and the best of the water upon the face of the earth is the water of Zamzam, and the worst of the water upon the face of the earth is the water of Barhout, and it is a valley in Hazramaut, upon which the spirits of the disbelievers and their evil ones descend.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Zurays al-Kunasi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The people mention that our Euphrates comes out from Paradise. So how is that, when it flows from the West, and springs and valleys pour into it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I hear that for Allah is a Garden which Allah created in the West, and the water of your Euphrates comes out from it. And to it go out the souls of the believers from their graves at every evening.' So they fall upon its fruits, eat from it, and enjoy themselves therein. They meet and recognize each other. So when dawn rises, they break out from the Garden, and they are in the air between the sky and the earth, flying, going and coming, and they visit their graves when the sun rises. They meet in the air and recognize each other.' He said: 'And for Allah is a Fire in the East, which He created to settle therein the souls of the disbelievers. They eat from its Zaqqum and drink from its boiling water during their night. So when dawn rises, they break out to a valley in Yemen called Barhout, which is more intense in heat than the fires of the world. Therein they meet and recognize each other. So when it is evening, they return to the Fire. Thus, they are like that until the Day of Judgment.' He said: I said, 'May Allah keep you well! So what is the state of the Monotheists, the acknowledgers of the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), from the sinning Muslims, who die and have no Imam for them, nor do they recognize your Wilayah?' So he said: 'As for these, then they are in their graves, not coming out from them. So whoever among them has righteous deeds, and enmity does not appear from him, then a furrow is grooved for him to the Garden which Allah created in the West. So the breeze comes to him from it into his grave until the Day of Judgment. So he meets Allah, and He reckons him by his good deeds and his evil deeds.' Either to the Garden or to the Fire. So these are paused for the Command of Allah. He said: 'And so Allah deals with the weak-minded, the foolish, the children, and the children of the Muslims who have not reached puberty.' So as for the Hostiles (Nasibis) from the people of the Qiblah, then a furrow is grooved for

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Maysar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Garden of Adam (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It was a garden from the gardens of the world, in which the sun and the moon rise, and if it had been from the Gardens of the Hereafter, he would not have come out of it ever.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked about the children?' So he said, 'He was asked, and he said: Allah is more Knowing of what they were doing.' Then he said, 'O Zurara! Do you know his words: 'Allah is more Knowing of what they were doing'?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'For Allah has the Volition regarding them.' Indeed, when it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will Gather the children, and those from the people who died in the period (of inter-prophetic gap), and the old man who met the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he did not have intellect, and the deaf, and the mute who did not have intellect, and the insane, and the foolish who did not have intellect, and every one of them will have an argument against Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So Allah will send to them an Angel from the Angels, who will inflame a fire for them. Then Allah will send to them an Angel who will say to them, 'Indeed, your Lord commands you to leap into it.' So whoever enters it, it will be for him a coolness and safety, and he will be admitted to Paradise; and whoever stays behind from it, he will enter the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from someone else, raising it, that he was asked about the children, so he said: When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah will Gather them and Inflame a fire for them, and Command them to throw themselves into it. So whoever was in the Knowledge of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, as being a fortunate one, would throw himself into it, and it would be a coolness and safety upon him; and whoever was in His Knowledge as a wretched one, would refuse. So Allah would Command with them to go to the Fire, and they would be saying, 'O our Lord! You are Commanding us to go to the Fire, and the Pen never flowed against us!' So the Compeller would be Saying: 'I had Commanded you verbally, but you did not obey Me, so how would it have been if I had Sent My messengers with the hidden matters to you?' And in another Hadith: 'As for the children of the Believers, they will be joined with their fathers, and the children of the Polytheists will be joined with their fathers, and this is the Word of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Those who believe and their offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the boys. So he said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the boys and the children, so he said: Allah is more Knowing with what they were doing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the children who died before reaching adulthood?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about them, so he said: Allah is more Knowing of what they were doing.' Then he turned towards me and said, 'O Zurara! Do you know what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) meant by that?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'He meant: Cease from judging them, and do not say anything regarding them, and refer their knowledge to Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who believe and their offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring.' He said: 'The sons would be deficient from the deeds of the fathers, so We will join the sons with the fathers in order for their eyes to be delighted with that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the one who died during the period (of the prophets), and about the one who did not incur sin, and the insane. So he (peace be upon him) said: Allah will present His argument against them. He will raise a fire for them and say to them: Enter it. So whoever enters it, it will be for him a coolness and peace, and whoever refuses, He will say: Behold, you are here. I commanded you, but you disobeyed Me.

And by this chain, it was said: Three are those against whom argument is made – the mute, the child, and whoever died during the period (of prophethood). So a fire is raised for them and it is said to them: 'Enter it!' So whoever enters it, it becomes for him coolness and peace; and whoever refuses, the Blessed and Exalted says: 'This I commanded you, but you disobeyed Me.'

And by this chain, it was said: Three [groups] against whom argument is made the mute, the child, and the one who died during the period [of prophethood], so a fire is raised for them and it is said to them: Enter it. So whoever enters it, it becomes for him a coolness and peace and whoever refuses, the Blessed and High says: 'This I commanded you, but you disobeyed Me.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, the compiler of this book, may God have mercy on him, says: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the most superior means by which servants draw near to their Lord, and what the most beloved of that is to God, Mighty and Majestic. So he said: 'I do not know of anything, after the recognition (of the Wilaya), that is more superior than this salat.' Do you not see that the righteous servant Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said: 'And He has enjoined upon me the salat and the zakat for as long as I live'? [Quran 19:31]

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The most beloved of deeds to God, Mighty and Majestic, is salat, and it is the last of the bequests of the Prophets (peace be upon them). So how excellent is the man who performs ghusl or wudu, and completes the wudu properly, then steps aside to where no one can see him, and God watches over him while he is in ruku' or sajdah! Indeed when the servant prostrates and prolongs his prostration, Iblees cries out: O woe is me! He obeyed and I disobeyed, and he prostrated and I refused.

I heard al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'The servant cannot happen to be (any) closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than when he is performing sajdah, and that is the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'And make obeisance and get closer (to Allah)' [96:19].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifa who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When the praying one stands for the salat, Mercy descends upon him from the horizons of the sky to the horizons of the earth, and the angels surround him, and an angel calls out: If this praying one only knew what is in the salat, he would not turn away.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the believing servant stands in his salat, Allah looks at him' — or he said: 'Allah turns towards him' — 'until he leaves, and the Mercy shades him from above his head to the horizons of the sky, and the angels surround him from around him to the horizons of the sky, and Allah assigns an angel standing over his head, saying to him: O you praying one! If you knew who was looking at you and whom you are whispering to, you would not turn away, nor would you ever cease to be in your place.'
Abu Dawud, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl, from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: The salat is an offering of every pious one.

From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Isma'il ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'An obligatory salat is better than twenty Hajj; and a Hajj is better than a house filled with gold given in charity until it is depleted.'

A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: A man passed by the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he was repairing one of his chambers. The man said: 'O Messenger of God, shall I not help you?' He said: 'As you wish.' When he had finished, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'What is your need?' He said: 'Paradise.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) fell silent, then said: 'Yes.' When he turned to leave, he called to him: 'O servant of God, assist us by prolonging the prostration.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The example of salat is like the example of the central pole of a tent: when the pole stands firm, the ropes and the pegs and the covering are of benefit; and when the pole breaks, neither a rope nor a peg nor a covering is of any benefit.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani from the one who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely good deeds take away evil deeds.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The prayer of the believer at night erases what he committed of sin during the day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever Allah accepts from him one prayer, He will not punish him, and whoever from whom He accepts a good deed, He will not punish him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Abdullah, son of Muhammad, son of Isa, from his father, from Abdullah, son of Al-Mughira, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Prayer is a scale; whoever fulfills it, will be fulfilled (with reward).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hashim Abu Saeed Al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Five prayers that you may pray at any time: the prayer of the eclipse, the prayer upon the deceased, the prayer of Ihram, the missed prayer, and the prayer of Tawaf; from dawn until the sun rises, and after Asr until night.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Five prayers are not to be neglected in any state: when you perform Tawaf of the House, and when you intend to enter Ihram, and the Salat of the Eclipse, and when you forget [a prayer] so pray it when you remember, and the Salat of the Funeral.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Four prayers that a man should pray at any time: A missed prayer, so whenever you remember it, fulfill it; and the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf; and the prayer of the eclipse; and the funeral prayer. These four you may pray at all times.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Suleiman al-Amiri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was ascended, the prayer was revealed as ten rak'at, two by two. So when Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn were born, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) increased seven rak'at as gratitude to Allah. So Allah permitted that for him, and he left Al-Fajr (prayer) as it was, not increasing in it due to the narrowness of its time, because it is attended by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. So when Allah commanded him to shorten (the prayer) during travel, he removed six rak'at for his community, and left Al-Maghrib as it was, not reducing anything from it; and rather, the omission applies to whatever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had increased. Thus, whoever doubts the original obligation in the first two rak'at, should face (continue) his prayer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from A'iz al-Ahmasi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I wanted to ask him about the night prayer. So I said, 'Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'And upon you be peace. Yes, by Allah, we are indeed his sons, and we are not merely his relatives' — he said this three times. Then he said, without me asking him: 'When you meet Allah having performed the five obligatory prayers, He will not ask you about anything besides that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Harun, from Harun ibn Kharrajah, who said: I mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a man from our companions, and I praised him well. So he said to me: 'What is the status of his Salat (prayer)?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sayyari, and al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the fifty-one rak'at, so he said: 'The hours of the day are twelve hours, and the hours of the night are twelve hours; and from the emergence of dawn to the emergence of the sun is one hour, and from the setting of the sun to the setting of the twilight is darkness (ghasaq), and for every hour two rak'at, and for the darkness one rak'at.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said: It was said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Why does the man incline to the left during the prayer?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because the Ka'bah has six boundaries, four of them are on your left and two of them are on your right. Therefore, for this reason, the inclination occurs to the left.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the servant stands up and fulfills the optional prayer, so the Lord is astonished by His angels regarding him, so He says: 'O My angels! My servant is fulfilling what I did not obligate upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The nobility of the Believer is his prayer at night, and the honor of the Believer is his restraint from the vanities of the people.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Harun ibn Kharjah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Salat is assigned to an angel who has no other work besides it. So when one finishes from it, he captures it, then ascends with it. So if it was from what is accepted, it is accepted, and if it was from what is not accepted, it is said to him: 'Return it to My servant.' So he descends with it until he strikes it upon his face, then he says: 'Uff to you! You do not cease to produce deeds that tire Me.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Qaddah, from Abu Abd al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Do not leave the prayer deliberately, for whoever leaves it deliberately, the religion of Islam has disavowed him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Monasticism which they innovated' [57:27]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The night prayer (Salat al-Layl)'.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from one of the students known as Ra's al-Madary, who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'The best place for the two feet for the prayer is the two slippers.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Jibraeel (peace be upon him): 'O Jibraeel! Which spots are the most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' He said: 'The mosques, and the most beloved of their people to Allah are the first of them to enter and the last of them to exit from them.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), peace be upon him, who said: There is no cloudy day during which the time of midday (Zawal) is concealed from the people, except that there is a rebuke (Zajrah) from the Imam to the sun until it appears, so that it becomes a proof upon the people of every town, for those who attend to its prayer and for those who neglect it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Abu Hamza, or from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, in Al-Kufa there are accursed mosques and blessed mosques. As for the blessed one, it is the Mosque of Ghaniyyin. By Allah, its Qiblah is balanced and just, and its clay is good. A believing man established it, and the world will not pass away until two springs gush out from it and two gardens are in its presence. However, its people are accursed and it is taken away from them. And the Mosque of Bani Zafar, which is the Mosque of Al-Sahla, and a mosque in Al-Khmar'a, and the Mosque of Ju'fi, and it is not their mosque today. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is extinct'. As for the accursed mosques, they are the Mosque of Thaqif, the Mosque of Al-Ash'ath, the Mosque of Jarir, the Mosque of Simak, and a mosque in Al-Khmar'a built upon the grave of a Pharaoh from the Pharaohs.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah from Ubeys ibn Hisham from Salim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Four mosques were renewed in Al-Kufa in happiness for the killing of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him): the Mosque of Al-Ash'ath, and the Mosque of Jarir, and the Mosque of Simak, and the Mosque of Shabas ibn Rabi'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Abdullah who said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he asked us: Is there among you anyone who has the knowledge of my uncle Zayd ibn Ali? So a man from the group said: I have knowledge from the knowledge of your uncle. We were with him one night in the house of Muawiya ibn Ishaq al-Ansari when he said: Come, let us go pray in Masjid al-Sahla. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And did he? He said: No, a matter came up that preoccupied him from going. So he (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, if he sought refuge with Allah through it for a year, He would have sheltered him. Do you not know that it is the place of the house of the Prophet Idris (peace be upon him), and in which he used to sew? And from it Ibrahim (peace be upon him) marched to Yemen with the Amaliqa, and from it Dawud (peace be upon him) marched against Jalut. And indeed in it is a green stone, in which is the likeness of every Prophet, and from beneath that very stone the clay of every Prophet was taken, and it is the resting place of the Rider. It was said: And who is the Rider? He (peace be upon him) said: Al-Khizr (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Uthman, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, and Masjid al-Sahla was mentioned, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, it is the residence of our Master (al-Qaim) when he arises with his people.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurara, who said: He said to me: 'Do you know why the cubit and the two cubits have been established?' I said: 'Why?' He said: 'For the place of the obligatory [prayer], it is for you that you may pray optional [prayers] from the decline of the sun until the shadow reaches one cubit. So when it reaches one cubit, begin with the obligatory [prayer] and leave the optional [prayers].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to the mosque and its inhabitants have already prayed; should he begin with the prescribed prayer or offer optional prayers? So he (peace be upon him) said: If he is within a good time, there is no harm in offering optional prayers before the obligatory one; and if he fears missing out due to the passage of time, let him begin with the obligatory prayer, for it is the Right of Allah (Exalted and Majestic). Then let him offer optional prayers with whatever he desires. Indeed, a person has leeway to pray the optional prayers at the beginning of the time of the obligatory prayer, unless he fears missing the obligatory one; and the superior manner, when a person prays alone, is to begin with the obligatory prayer when its time enters, so that the merit of the beginning of the time belongs to the obligatory prayer. And it is not forbidden upon him to pray the optional prayers from the beginning of the time until near the end of the time.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said, 'Can I pray an optional prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, at the beginning of the time, when you are with an Imam whom you follow. So when you are alone, begin with the prescribed prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'When the time for the obligatory prayer enters, should I pray the optional prayer or begin with the obligatory one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The preference is that you begin with the obligatory prayer, and the Dhuhr prayer is delayed by a cubit from midday for the sake of the prayer of the Returners (Al-Awwabin).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When the time for the obligatory prayer enters, should I pray the optional prayer or begin with the obligatory prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The preference is that you begin with the obligatory prayer.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Al-Husayn ibn Rashid from Al-Husayn ibn Aslam who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan the second (peace be upon him): 'I am in the market, I recognize the time, and it is difficult for me to enter and pray.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Satan accompanies the sun in three states: when it rises, when it is high, and when it sets. So pray after the midday decline, for Satan intends to make you fall upon a limit from which you are cut off from him.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Husayn ibn Rashid from al-Husayn ibn Aslama who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him), 'I am in the market and recognize the time, but it becomes difficult for me to enter [the market] so that I may pray.' He said, 'Satan aligns with the sun in three conditions: when it rises, when it is high (at noon), and when it sets. So pray after Zawal (decline), for Satan wants to place you on a boundary that is cut off for you without it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: If you forget a prayer or pray it without ablution, and there are missed prayers upon you, then begin with the first of them, call the Adhan for it and perform the Iqamah, then pray it, then pray what comes after it with an Iqamah, an Iqamah for each prayer. And he (peace be upon him) said: And if you have prayed Dhuhr and the morning prayer has been missed by you, and you remember it, then pray the morning prayer whenever you remember it, even if it is after Asr; and whenever you remember a prayer that has been missed by you, pray it. And he (peace be upon him) said: If you forget Dhuhr until you have prayed Asr, and you remember it while you are in the prayer or after its completion, intend it as the first, then pray Asr, for it is four [rak'at] in place of four [rak'at]. If you remember that you did not pray the first [Dhuhr] and you are in the prayer of Asr, and you have prayed two rak'at from it, intend it as the first, then pray the two remaining rak'at, and stand and pray Asr. And if you remember that you did not pray Asr until the time for Maghrib enters, and you do not fear missing it, then pray Asr, then pray Maghrib. And if you have already prayed Maghrib, stand and pray Asr. And if you have prayed two rak'at from Maghrib, then you remember Asr, intend it as Asr, then stand and complete it with two rak'at, then give the Salam, then pray Maghrib. So if you have prayed the last Isha and forgotten Maghrib, stand and pray Maghrib. And if you remembered it and you have prayed two rak'at from the last Isha, or you are standing in the third [rak'at], intend it as Maghrib, then give the Salam, then stand and pray the last Isha. And if you have forgotten the last Isha until you have prayed Fajr, then pray the last Isha. And if you remember it while you are in the first rak'at or in the second of the morning [prayer], intend it as Isha, then stand and pray the morning [prayer], and call the Adhan and perform the Iqamah. And if Maghrib and the last Isha have been missed by you together, begin with them before you pray the morning [prayer]. Begin with Maghrib, then the last Isha. If you fear that the morning prayer will be missed if you begin with them, then begin with Maghrib, the

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him about a man who forgot the Dhuhr prayer until the time for Asr entered. He said: 'He should begin with Dhuhr; and similarly, the prayers should begin with that which you forgot, unless you fear that the time for the prayer will expire, so you should begin with that which is currently within its time, then pray that which you forgot.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who prayed without purity, or forgot prayers that he did not pray, or slept through them, so he said: He should make up for it when he remembers it, at whatever hour he remembers it, from night or day. So when the time for the prayer enters and he has not completed what has passed, let him make up for what he does not fear the time of this present prayer will depart, and this is more deserving of its time, so let him pray it. So when he has made it up, let him pray what has passed from what is missed, and he should not offer an optional prayer by even one rak'ah until he has made up the obligatory prayer, all of it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a prayer is missed by you and you remember it during the time of another [prayer], if you know that if you were to pray the missed one, you would still be within the time [of the current one], then begin with the one that was missed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Establish the prayer for My remembrance.' And if you know that if you were to pray the one that was missed, the one after it would be missed, then begin with the one whose time you are currently in, so pray it, then establish the other one.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd alman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot a prayer until the time for another prayer entered. He said: When he forgets the prayer or sleeps through it, he prays when he remembers it. So when he remembers it while he is in a prayer, he begins with that which he forgot. And if he remembers it with an Imam during the Maghrib prayer, he completes it with one Rak'ah, then prays Maghrib, then prays Al-'Atamah (Isha) after it. And if he had prayed Al-'Atamah alone, so he prayed two Rak'at from it, then remembers that he forgot Maghrib, he completes it with one Rak'ah, so the Maghrib prayer becomes three Rak'at. Then he prays Al-'Atamah after that.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who forgot the Dhuhr prayer until the sun set, and he had already prayed Asr. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), or my father (peace be upon him), used to say: If he is able to pray it before the Maghrib time passes, he should begin with it; otherwise, he should pray Maghrib and then pray it (Dhuhr).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who led a group in the Asr prayer, and he remembered while he was praying that he had not prayed the first [prayer]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him consider the missed one as the first, and let him resume after it the Asr prayer, and the people have already completed their prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed is His Name: 'Surely prayer is a timed ordinance upon the Believers.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It means obligatory, and does not mean a time of missing it. If that time passes and then he prays it, his prayer is not considered rendered. And had it been so, Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) would have been destroyed when he prayed it outside its time. But rather, whenever he remembered it, he prayed it.' He (the narrator) said, 'Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And whenever you are convinced or doubt regarding its time that you did not pray it, or within the time of its missing that you did not pray it, you pray it. So if you doubt after the time of missing has passed, an obstacle has entered, so there is no repetition upon you from doubt until you are convinced. So if you are convinced, then upon you is that you pray it in whatever state you were.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who slept through the 'Isha prayer and did not rise until after midnight, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray it and fast until morning.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding the words of Allah, Blessed is His Name, Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. He said: It means obligatory. And it does not mean a time of loss, such that if that time passes and he prays it, his prayer is not considered fulfilled. And if that were the case, Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them both) would have been destroyed when he prayed it outside its time. But whenever he remembered it, he prayed it. Then he said: And whenever you are certain or doubt regarding its time that you did not pray it, or regarding its time of loss that you did not pray it, you must pray it. If you doubt after the time of loss has passed, then an obstacle has entered, so there is no requirement for you to repeat it due to doubt until you become certain. If you become certain, then it is upon you to pray it in whatever state you are.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who slept through the ‘Atmah (late night prayer) and did not wake up until after midnight. He said: He performs it and remains fasting until morning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to place the walking stick in front of him when he prayed.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The length of the saddle-bag of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was one cubit, and when he prayed, he would place it in front of him to veil himself from those who would pass in front of him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man: Does anything that passes in front of him cut off his prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: Nothing cuts off the prayer of the believer, but ward off (the passerby) as much as you can. And in a narration of Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Nothing cuts off the prayer, neither a dog, nor a donkey, nor a woman, but cover yourself with something. So if there is in front of you a measurement of a cubit raised from the ground, then you have covered yourself. Al-Kulayni and Al-Fazl said regarding this: You should cover yourself with something and place in front of you what you use to protect yourself from the passerby. If you do not do so, there is no harm in it, because the one for whom the pray-er is praying is closer to him than the one who passes in front of him, but that is the etiquette of the prayer and its reverence.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Hanifa came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I saw your son Musa (peace be upon him) praying while people were passing in front of him, and he did not stop them, and what is in it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Call Musa for me.' So he was called, and he said to him, 'O my son! Abu Hanifa mentions that you were praying while people were passing in front of you, and you did not forbid them.' He said, 'Yes, O father! The One Whom I was praying to was closer to me than them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) embraced him to himself, then said, 'O my son! By my father and my mother, O the mine of the secrets!' And this is an education from him (peace be upon him), not that he neglected the merit.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who prays to the side of the man, near to him, he said: 'When there is a place between them of one saddle-bag (cubit), there is no problem.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is praying and a woman is by his side, to his right or to his left. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it if she is not praying.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man and a woman praying at one time, the woman on the right of the man by his side. He said: 'No, unless there is between them a shibr (span) or a dhirab (cubit).'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about a man who prays in a corner of the room, and his wife or his daughter prays beside him in the other corner. He said: It is not befitting for him to do that. But if there is a span's width between them, it suffices him. He said: And I asked him about a man and a woman accompanying each other in a carriage, praying together. He said: No, but the man should pray first. So when he has prayed, the woman prays.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Idris ibn 'Abdullah al-Qummi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is praying and parallel to him is a woman standing upon her bed by his side. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If she was seated, it would not harm him, and if she was praying, then no (it does not harm him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Rabaat, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was praying, and Aisha was sleeping, lying sideways in front of him, and she was not praying.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is praying and a woman who is praying parallel to him or to his side, he said: If her prostration is simultaneous with his bowing, there is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When you stand for the prayer, you must be devoted to your prayer, for only what you are devoted to is counted for you from it. And do not play with your hand, nor your head, nor your beard, nor speak to yourself, nor yawn, nor stretch, nor fold your hands, for that is what the Magians do. And do not cover your head, nor keep your feet wide apart, nor spread them like a camel spreads them, nor sit on your heels, nor stretch out your arms, nor crack your fingers, for all of that is a deficiency in the prayer. And do not stand for the prayer sluggishly, nor drowsy, nor heavy, for these are from the traits of hypocrisy. For Allah, Glorious is He, forbade the believers from standing for the prayer while they are intoxicated—meaning the intoxication of sleep—and He said to the hypocrites: 'And when they stand up for the prayer, they stand up sluggishly; they do it only to be seen of men and (they) do not remember Allah except for a little.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan Al-Farsi, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah dislikes for you, O community, twenty-four characteristics and forbids you from them. He dislikes for you frivolity/playfulness during the prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter into your prayer, you must have humility and focus upon your prayer, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is, says: 'Those who are humble in their prayers.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Abi Jahmat, from Jahm ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) stood for prayer, he was like the trunk of a tree; nothing moved from him except what the wind moved from him.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when he stood for prayer, his color would change. And when he prostrated, he would not raise his head until he perspired profusely.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said: Regarding the man who yawns and stretches during the prayer, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from Satan, and he has no control over it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi al-Walid, who said: I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Najiya Abi Habeeb asked him, saying: 'May Allah make me a ransom for you. I have a mill in which I grind (flour). Sometimes I stand during a part of the night, and I know from the mill that the servant has slept, so I strike the wall to wake him up.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, you are in obedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seeking His provision.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you stand in prayer, do not play with your beard, nor with your head, nor with the pebbles while you are praying, unless you level them where you will prostrate, for there is no harm.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is befitting for the one who recites the Quran that when he passes by a verse from the Quran wherein is a question or a caution, he should ask Allah during that for the goodness he hopes for, and ask Him for well-being from the Fire and from the Punishment.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Saeed al-Sabiri (the seller of Sabir), who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can the man weep during the prayer?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Congratulations! Congratulations, and even though it (tears) may be the like of the head of a fly'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who is behind the Imam and the Imam passes by a question (verse) or by a Verse wherein is the mention of Paradise or Fire. He said: There is no problem with him asking during that, and seeking Refuge from the Fire during the Salat, and asking Allah for the Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about mentioning a Chapter from the Book to supplicate with during the prayer, such as 'Say: He is Allah, One', so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are supplicating with it, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Everything with which you speak to Allah during the obligatory prayer, there is no problem (with it).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Al-Fadl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was Ascended to the sky, he reached the Frequented House (Bayt Al-Mamour), and the time for prayer arrived, so Jibril called the Adhan and the Iqamah. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) moved forward, and the Angels and the Prophets formed rows behind Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended with the Adhan upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), his head was in the lap of Ali (peace be upon him). So Jibraeel (peace be upon him) called the Adhan and the Iqamah. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) awoke, he said: 'O Ali, did you hear?' He said: 'Yes'. He said: 'Did you memorize?' He said: 'Yes'. He said: 'Call Bilal and teach him.' So Ali (peace be upon him) called Bilal and taught him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Adhan and the Iqamah are thirty-five letters,' and he counted them with his hand, one by one: the Adhan is eighteen letters, and the Iqamah is seventeen letters.

Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al-Jammal, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Azan is recited twice by twice, and the Iqamah is recited twice by twice'.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'O Zurara! Open the Adhan with four Takbirs, and conclude it with two Takbirs and two Tahliils.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about yawning during the Adhan and the Iqamah, so he said: 'We do not recognize it.'
