Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja' Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you recite the Adhan, be eloquent with the Alif and the Ha, and send blessings upon the Prophet every time you mention him, or when a reciter mentions him during the Adhan or otherwise.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you recite the Adhan and the Iqamah, two rows of angels pray behind you, and when you recite the Iqamah, one row of the angels pray behind you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Does one Adhan suffice?' He said: 'If you pray in congregation, it does not suffice you except with an Adhan and an Iqamah; and if you are alone and hastening to a matter fearing it will be missed by you, an Iqamah suffices you, except for Fajr and Maghrib, for it is befitting that you give Adhan for them and give Iqamah, due to the reason that there is no shortening in them as there is in the other prayers.'

Abu Dawood, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible for a man to speak during the Adhan?' He said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'During the Iqamah?' He said, 'No.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: There is no problem if a man were to recite the Azan without being in ablution, but he cannot recite the Iqamah unless he is upon ablution.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who arrives to the Imam when he is concluding (the prayer). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon him to repeat the Adhan, so let him enter with them in their Adhan. And if he finds them to have dispersed, he should repeat the Adhan.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the Azan: Is it permissible for it to be from someone who is not knowledgeable? He said: The Azan is not correct, and it is not permissible for it to be recited except by a knowledgeable Muslim man. So if he knows the Azan, he recites it with it; and if he is not knowledgeable, his Azan is not valid, nor is his Iqamah, nor should he be followed (as an Imam). And he was asked about a man who recites the Azan and Iqamah in order to pray alone, and then another man comes and says to him, 'We should pray in congregation.' Is it permissible for them to pray with that Azan and Iqamah? He said: No, but he should recite an Azan and an Iqamah.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the man who forgets the Adhan and the Iqamah until he enters into the Salat, he (peace be upon him) said: If he remembered before he recited, let him send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and let him recite the Iqamah; and if he had already recited, let him complete his Salat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever makes a mistake in the Adhan by bringing forward or delaying (a phrase), he should return to the first one which he delayed until he completes it at its end.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The man may recite the Azan while he is seated, but he may not recite the Iqamah except while he is standing; and you may recite the Azan while you are riding, but you may not recite the Iqamah except while you are upon the ground.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Does the man recite the Adhan while he is not facing the Qiblah?' He said, 'If the Tashahhud is facing the Qiblah, there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman, is there upon her an Adhan and an Iqamah? He said: No.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Maryam Al-Ansari, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Iqamah of the woman is that she says Takbir and testifies that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Harun! The Iqamah is part of the Salat. So when you establish it, do not speak, nor gesture with your hand.'

And by this chain, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleiman ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: None of you should recite the Iqamah for the Salat while he is walking, nor while riding, nor lying down, unless he is sick; and let him be stable/established in the Iqamah just as he is stable in the Salat, for indeed when he begins the Iqamah, he is in the Salat.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man enters the mosque and he is not following his companion (the Imam), and there remains upon the Imam one verse or two verses, so he fears that if he were to recite the Adhan and Iqamah, the Imam would go into Ruku', then let him say: 'The Salat has been established! The Salat has been established! Allah is the Greatest! Allah is the Greatest! There is no god except Allah!', and let him enter into the Salat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suweyd, from Yahya ibn Imran ibn Ali Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Azan before Fajr, so he said: 'If it is in a congregation, then no (it is not done), and if he is alone, then there is no problem (it is permissible).'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Sitting between the Adhan and the Iqamah is recommended in all prayers, provided that no other prayer is performed before the Iqamah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from one of our companions, from Ismail ibn Jabir that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would recite the Azan, and someone else would recite the Iqamah, and he said, 'He would recite the Iqamah, while someone else had already recited the Azan'.

A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sariy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Adhan is recited slowly (melodiously), and the Iqamah is recited quickly (flowingly).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, raising it, said: He said: On the Day of Resurrection, three will be upon dunes of musk — one of them a Muezzin who called the Adhan with anticipation (of reward).

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) is forgiven for the extent of his voice, and everything that hears it testifies on his behalf.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi'i ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he heard the Mu'adhdhin giving the Adhan, would say similar to what he was saying in every phrase.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahboub from Jameel ibn Salih from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nadri from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever hears the Mu'adhdhin saying, 'I testify that there is no god except Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' and he says, affirming and anticipating (reward), 'And I testify that there is no god except Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family),' and he suffices with these two (testimonies) from those who refused and denied, and he is aided by these two (testimonies) [for] whoever acknowledges and testifies, there is for him from the reward the number of those who denied and rejected, and the like of the number of those who acknowledged and recognized.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahboub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The height of the wall of the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was one qamah (stature). So he (peace be upon him and his family) would say to Bilal: 'When the time enters, O Bilal, climb above the wall and raise your voice with the Adhan, for Allah has assigned a wind with the Adhan that raises it to the sky. And indeed, the angels, when they hear the Adhan from the people of the earth, say: 'These are the voices of the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) affirming the Oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,' and they seek forgiveness for the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) until they finish from that Salat.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Husayn ibn Asad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yaqthan, (it was) raised to them (peace be upon him), who said: The man should say when he has finished with the Adhan and is seated: 'O Allah, make my heart righteous, my livelihood constant, my sustenance continuous, and make for me a dwelling and a resting place near the grave of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a muezzin were to repeat in the testimonies, and in 'Hasten to the prayer' or 'Hasten to success', twice or thrice, and more than that, when it is so that he intends by it the gathering of the people in order to gather them, there would be no problem with it.

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Suleyman Al-Ja'fari who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Recite the Adhan in your house, for it repels the Satan, and it is recommended for the sake of the children.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed al-Rashidi, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The superior act (fadhil) when entering the mosque is that you begin with your right foot when you enter, and with the left when you exit.

Ali, from his father, from Abdullah bin al-Mughira, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter the mosque, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family); and when you exit, do that (as well).

And from him, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Aban and Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you stand for the prayer, say: O Allah! I present Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) before my need, and I turn to You through him, so make me esteemed through Him in Your presence in this world and the Hereafter, and of those who are brought near. Make my prayer acceptable through him, and my sin forgiven through him, and my supplication answered through him. Indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hashimy, from Abu Hafs al-Attar, a Sheikh from the people of Medina, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever one of you prays the Prescribed Salat and exits from the Masjid, so let him pause by the door, then let him say, O Allah! You Called me, so I answered Your Call, and I prayed the Prescribed Salat, and I spread out in Your earth just as You Commanded me. So I ask You from Your Grace, the working in Your obedience, and keeping aside from Your Anger, and sufficiency of the sustenance by Your Mercy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Aban ibn Taghlub who said: I was praying behind Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Muzdalifa. When he finished, he turned toward me and said: 'O Aban! The five obligatory prayers — whoever upholds their limits and preserves their prescribed times will meet God on the Day of Resurrection, and for him will be a covenant with Him by which He will admit him into Paradise. And whoever does not uphold their limits and does not preserve their prescribed times will meet God with no covenant for him — if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.'

I prayed Maghrib with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Muzdalifa. When he finished, he recited the iqamah and prayed the last Isha without praying any rak'at between the two. Then, a year later, I prayed with him: he prayed Maghrib, then stood and performed four voluntary rak'ats, then recited the iqamah and prayed the last Isha. Then he turned to me and said: 'O Aban! These are the five obligatory prayers. Whoever establishes them and preserves their prescribed times will meet God on the Day of Resurrection, and for him with God will be a covenant by which He will admit him into Paradise. But whoever does not pray them in their prescribed times and does not preserve them — that matter is up to Him: if He wills, He will forgive him, and if He wills, He will punish him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Yunus ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It was said to him, while I was present: 'The man happens to be in his salat, devoid (of distractions), then self-conceit (ujb) enters him.' So he said: 'When the beginning of his salat was with an intention seeking his Lord, then whatever enters him after that will not harm him. So let him continue in his salat and let him debase Satan.'

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Every lapse in the salat is dropped from it, except that God the Exalted completes it with the voluntary prayers. The first thing the servant will be reckoned for is the salat; if it is accepted, what is besides it will be accepted. The salat, when it is raised during the beginning of its prescribed time, returns to its owner and it is white, shining, saying: 'You preserved me, may God protect you.' And when it is raised outside its prescribed time, without its proper limits, it returns to its owner and it is black, dark, saying: 'You wasted me, may God waste you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said: I asked Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who are unmindful of their prayers' He said: It is the wasting (of prayer).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Uthina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: While the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was seated in the mosque, a man entered. He stood up and began to pray, but did not complete his ruku' nor his sujud. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He pecked like the pecking of a crow. If this man were to die while his prayer is like this, he would surely die upon a religion other than mine.'

From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Do not be careless with your salat, for the Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said at the time of his passing: 'He is not of me, the one who belittles his salat; he is not of me, the one who drinks an intoxicant. He will not come to me at the Fountain — no, by Allah.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Satan does not cease to be alarmed by the believer as long as he preserves upon the five prayers. But when he wastes them, he becomes audacious against him and leads him into grave sins.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Iys ibn al-Qasim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By God! Fifty years may pass over a man and God has not accepted a single prayer from him. So what thing is more difficult than this? By God! You know among your neighbors and your companions those who, if they were to pray for one of you, you would not accept it from them due to their belittling of it. Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, does not accept except what is good. So how would He accept what is treated with contempt?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the servant stands in prayer and lightens his prayer, Allah, Blessed and High, says to His angels: 'Do you not look at My servant? It is as if he sees that the fulfillment of his needs is in the hand of someone other than Me. Does he not know that the fulfillment of his needs is in My Hand?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man performs one prayer completely, all of his prayers are accepted, even if they are not complete; and if he spoils all of them, nothing is accepted from him, nor is an optional prayer or an obligatory one reckoned for him; and indeed, the optional prayer is only accepted after the acceptance of the obligatory prayer; and when the man does not perform the obligatory prayer, the optional prayer is not accepted from him, and the optional prayer is made only to complete what was spoiled of the obligatory prayer.

And by this chain, from Hariz, from Al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who preserve their Prayers.' He said: 'It is the Obligatory [prayer].' I said: 'Those who are constant at their Prayer?' He said: 'It is the optional [prayer].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The Words of the Exalted: 'Surely the Salat was a timed ordinance for the Believers.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A fixed/affirmed prescription, and it is not [forbidden if] you hasten a little or delay a little, in a way that harms you, as long as you do not waste that wasting [i.e., fail to pray entirely].' For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to a people who wasted the Salat and followed the lustful desires: 'So they will meet Ghayya.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Any believer who preserves the obligatory prayers and prays them at their proper time, he is not among the oblivious (unaware) ones.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first said: 'When death presented itself to my father, he said to me: O my son, indeed the one who takes prayer lightly will not attain our intercession.'

Muhammad narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For everything there is a face, and the face of your religion is the Salat; so let not one of you disgrace the face of his religion. And for everything there is a nose (or pride), and the nose of the Salat is the Takbir.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: You raise your hands at the opening of the prayer opposite your face, and do not raise them all the way.

And from him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you stand for the prayer and say Takbir, raise your hands, and do not let your palms exceed your ears, i.e., parallel to your cheeks.

From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: The minimum that suffices from the Takbir during the turning (to prayer) is one Takbir; and three Takbirs are better, and seven are superior.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you are an Imam (prayer leader), one Takbir suffices for you, because with you are those with needs, the weak, and the elderly.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Takbir in the five Obligatory Salats is ninety-five Takbirs, from which the Takbirs of the Qunut are five.

And it was reported as well, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, and he explained them: in the Dhuhr prayer there are twenty-one takbirations, and in the Asr prayer there are twenty-one takbirations, and in the Maghrib prayer there are sixteen takbirations, and in the last Isha prayer there are twenty-one takbirations, and in the Fajr prayer there are eleven takbirations, and there are five takbirations of the Qunut in the five prayers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you commence the prayer, raise your two palms, then extend them fully, then say Takbir three times, then say: 'O Allah, You are the True King, there is no god but You, Glory be to You, I have wronged myself, so forgive my sin, for no one forgives sins except You.' Then say Takbir twice, then say: 'Here I am and at Your service, and goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not to You, and the Guided one is the one You guide, there is no refuge from You except to You, Glory be to You, and Your tenderness, Blessed and Exalted, Glory be to You, Lord of the House.' Then say Takbir twice, then say: 'I turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, upright and Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my rituals, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, no partner for Him, and by that I was commanded, and I am of the Muslims.' Then seek refuge from the accursed Satan, then recite the Opening of the Book.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When I stand for the prayer, I recite 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful' in the Opening of the Quran.' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'So when I have recited the Opening of the Quran, do I recite 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful' with the Chapter?' He said: 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran al-Hamdani, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! What do you say regarding a man who begins with 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful' in his prayer, alone in the Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha). So when he comes to other than the Mother of the Book from the Surah, he leaves it.' So the Abbasid said, 'There is no problem with that.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote by his own handwriting: 'Repeat it twice, notwithstanding his nose,' meaning the Abbasid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abbad ibn Yaqoub, from Amr ibn Mus'ab, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The beginning of every Book revealed from the sky is "In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful". So when you recite "In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful", it does not matter if you do not seek Refuge (from the Satan); and when you recite "In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful", it will veil you regarding what is between the sky and the earth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there something fixed regarding the recitation in the prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, except for the Friday prayer. You recite in it Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah Al-Munafiqun.'

Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you are behind an Imam and he recites Al-Hamd and finishes its recitation, you say, 'You are the Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds', and you do not say 'Ameen'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: That which is recorded/accepted from recitation and supplication is only that which one hears with oneself.

Abu Dawood, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Does it suffice for me if I recite in the obligatory prayer only the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha) when I am in a hurry or something hastens me?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) prayed Al-Maghrib with us, so he recited the two Mu'awwidhat (Chapters 113 & 114) in the two Rak'at.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is permissible for the sick person to recite in the obligatory prayer only the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and it is permissible for the healthy person regarding the make-up of the voluntary prayer at night and during the day.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is disliked to combine the two Surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the optional prayer, there is no problem.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, by a chain of his, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is disliked to recite 'Say, He is Allah, [the] One' in one breath.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not recite in the obligatory prayer with less than one Chapter, nor with more.'

Abu Dawood, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, by his chain, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The prayers of the repentant, the fifty [rak'ahs], all of them [are performed] with "Say: He is Allah, [the] One".'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Should a man recite during his prayer while his garment is over his mouth?' He said, 'There is no problem with that, if his ears can hear his own humming.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from the one who mentioned it, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It suffices you from the recitation with them the like of talking to yourself'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Talbiyah of the mute, his testimony, and his recitation of the Quran during the Salat is the movement of his tongue, and the gesturing by his fingers.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Amr ibn Saeed al-Madaini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the man who forgets a letter from the Quran and remembers it while he is bowing (ruku'), is it permissible for him to recite during the bowing? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but when he prostrates (sajdah), let him recite.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus from Muhammad ibn Zawiya from Abu 'Ali ibn Rashid who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you, you wrote to Muhammad ibn Al-Faraj teaching him that the most superior of what one recites in the obligatory [prayers] is 'Inna anzalnahu' (We revealed it) and 'Qul huwa Allahu ahad' (Say, He is Allah, One), and my chest is constricted by reciting these two during Al-Fajr [prayer].' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not let your chest be constricted by these two, for the merit, by Allah, is in these two.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I prayed behind Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) for days, and it was so that whenever it was a prayer wherein is no loud recitation, he (peace be upon him) recited loudly with 'In the Name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful'; and he (peace be upon him) used to recite loudly during both the two Chapters.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not utter your Salat loudly nor be silent with it'. He said: 'The silent (khafitah) is what is less than what you can hear (yourself), and the loud (jahar) is that you raise your voice intensely'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: Muath ibn Muslim narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Do not leave reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' in seven places: in the two rak'at before Fajr, the two rak'at of midday (Dhuhr), two rak'at after Maghrib, two rak'at from the beginning of the night prayer, the two rak'at of Ihram, and Fajr when you begin the morning with it, and the two rak'at of Tawaf. And in another report: that one should begin in all of these with 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and in the second rak'at with 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun', except in the two rak'at before Fajr, for one should begin with 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun', then recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in the second rak'at.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the man who leads the people in prayer and makes a mistake. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one behind him corrects him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the man who is praying in a place, then intends to move forward: He should cease recitation while walking until he reaches the place he intends, then he should recite.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man stands in prayer and intends to recite a chapter, so he recites 'Say: He is Allah, One' and 'Say: O you disbelievers'.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He may return (break his recitation) from every chapter, except from 'Say: He is Allah, One' and 'Say: O you disbelieurs'.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Sabir, the mawla of Bassam, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) led us in the Maghrib prayer, and he recited the two Mu'awwidhat (Chapters 113 and 114), then said: 'These two are from the Quran.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it upon the Imam that he should make those behind him hear, even if they are numerous?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him recite a moderate recitation.' And do not raise your voice in your prayer, nor conceal it, but seek a way between that.

Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book in his prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no prayer for him unless he begins with it, whether in loud or silent recitation.' I said, 'Which of the two is more beloved to you when he is fearful or in a hurry: should he recite with a Chapter or the Opening of the Book?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Opening of the Book.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: When something from the four determined Verses is recited and you hear it, then prostrate (Sajdah), and even if you are without ablution, and even if you are in a state of major impurity (Junub), and even if the woman is not praying (due to menstruation); and for the rest of the Quran, you have the choice therein: if you wish, you prostrate, and if you wish, you do not prostrate.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who heard the Sajdah (verse) being recited. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not prostrate unless he is attentive to its reciter, listening to it intently, or he is praying his prayer with the reciter. As for if he is praying in one corner and you are praying in another corner, then do not prostrate for what you have heard.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If you pray with a group of people and the Imam recites 'Read in the name of your Lord Who created' or something from the determined Verses, and finishes his recitation and does not prostrate, then indicate with a gesture; and the menstruating woman should prostrate when she hears the prostration (verse).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the man who recites the Sajdah verse at the end of the Surah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should prostrate (Sajdah), then stand up and recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah), then bow (Ruku') and prostrate (Sajdah).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Do not recite in the Prescribed Prayer anything from the determined Verses, for the prostration is an addition to the Prescribed Prayer.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muawiya ibn Aamir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the recitation behind the Imam in the last two Rak'at, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Imam recites the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and those behind him glorify (Tasbeeh). So when you are alone, then recite in them, and if you wish, then glorify.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What suffices from the recitation in the last two rak'at?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That you say,

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'What should the man say behind the Imam when he says, "Allah hears the one who praises Him"?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should say, "The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds," and he should lower his voice.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who does not straighten his back during the prayer, so there is no prayer for him'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'e, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) performing rukūʿ with a bow lower than the bowing of every one I ever saw performing rukūʿ, and it was so that whenever he performed rukūʿ, he formed wings with his hands (spreading them).

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you raise your head from the bowing (ruku'), straighten your back, for there is no prayer for the one who does not straighten his back.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sindi ibn Al-Rabi', from Saeed ibn Janah, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in his house in Medina, so he said initiating: 'The one who completes his Rukū, loneliness would not enter into him in the grave'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad, from Hisham who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Would it suffice me if I were to say in place of the Glorification during the Rukū and the Sajdah, There is no god except for Allah and Allah is the Greatest He said: 'Yes'.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Uqba who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saw me in Al-Medina and I was praying, and I bent my head and I extended in my bowing, so he (peace be upon him) sent a message to me: ‘Do not do it’.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you prostrate, say the Takbir and say: 'O Allah, to You I have prostrated, and by You I have believed, and to You I have submitted, and upon You I have relied, and You are my Lord. My face has prostrated to the One who created it and cleaved its hearing and sight. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.' Then say: 'Glorious is my Lord, the Most High, and by His praise,' three times. So when you raise your head, say between the two prostrations: 'O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, deliver me, and ward off [evil] from me. Indeed, I am poor in need of whatever good You send down to me. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs Al-Awr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was so that whenever Ali (peace be upon him) performed Sajdah, he postured (went down) like the posture of the slender camel, meaning his going down.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when he performed Sajdah, moved three fingers from his fingers, one after the other, with a slight movement as if he was counting the Glorifications, then raised his head.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying while he was in prostration: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You exchange my bad deeds for good ones, and reckon me with an easy reckoning.' Then he said during the second (prostration): 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You suffice me with the provisions of the world and every terror before Paradise.' And he said during the third: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), since You have forgiven me the many sins and the few, and accepted from me my slight deeds.' Then he said during the fourth: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), since You have brought me into Paradise and made me from its dwellers, and since You have saved me from the blasts of the Fire by Your mercy. And may Allah bless Muhammad and his family.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who remembers the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he is in the prescribed prayer, either bowing or prostrating, so he sends blessings upon him while he is in that state. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. The sending of blessings upon the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is like the form of the Takbir and the Tasbih, and it is ten good deeds, which eighteen angels compete to deliver to him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Sayabat, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can I supplicate while I am in prostration (sajdah)?' He said, 'Yes, supplicate for the world and the Hereafter, for He is the Lord of the world and the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he supplicates to his Lord while he is in prostration. So, what do you say when you prostrate? I said, 'Teach me, may I be sacrificed for you!' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Say:' 'O Lord of the lords, and O King of the kings, and O Master of the masters, and O Compeller of the compellers, and O God of the gods! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and do such and such with me.' Then say, 'I am Your servant, my forelock being in Your grip.' Then supplicate with whatever you wish and ask Him, for He is Generous, and nothing is too great for Him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Baseer prayed Salat with us in a street of Makkah, and he said while he was prostrating, and a she-camel of their cameleer had strayed, 'O Allah! Return to so and so, his camel'. Muhammad (the narrator) said, 'So I went over to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: 'And he did so?' I said, 'Yes'. So he remained silent. I said, 'So, should he repeat the Salat?' He said: 'No'.

Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I used to spread out the bed for my father, waiting for him until he would come. So when he would lie down upon his bed and sleep, I would arise to go to my own bed. One night he was delayed, so I went to the Masjid seeking him, and that was after the people had dispersed.' So there he was in the Masjid, prostrating, and there was no one in the Masjid apart from him, and I heard his yearning and he was saying: 'O Allah! You are my Lord, truly, truly. I am prostrating to You, O Lord, as a servant and a slave. O Allah! My deeds are weak, so Increase these for me. O Allah! Save me from Your Punishment on the Day You will be Resurrecting Your servants, and Turn towards me for You are the Oft-Turning, Merciful'.

Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Jareer Al-Rawwasy, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hassan Musa (peace be upon him), and he was saying: 'O Allah! I ask You for rest at the time of death, and pardon at the time of reckoning,' repeating it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Abdullah ibn Hilal who said: I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the separation of our wealth and what had entered upon us (as a result of it). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon you with the supplication while you are prostrating, for the closest of what the servant can happen to be to Allah is when he is prostrating'. He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So shall I supplicate during the Obligatory (Salat) and specify my need?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had done that, and he (peace be upon him) supplicated against a people with their names and the names of their fathers; and Ali (peace be upon him) did so after him (peace be upon him and his family)'.

A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was with Aisha one night, so he arose to pray the optional prayer. Aisha woke up and struck with her hand but did not find him, so she thought that he had gone to her slave girl. She stood up and circled around him, and she trampled upon his neck (peace be upon him and his family) while he was prostrating, weeping. He was saying: 'My dark garments and my views prostrate to You, and my heart believes in You. I acknowledge to You the blessings, and I confess to You the great sin; I did evil and wronged myself, so forgive me. Indeed, none forgives the great sin except You.' I seek refuge with Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge with Your pleasure from Your anger, and I seek refuge with Your mercy from Your wrath, and I seek refuge with You from You. I cannot fully reach Your praise and eulogy upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.' So when he finished, he said: 'O Aisha! You have caused pain to my neck. What did you fear, that I would stand up to go to your slave girl?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from his father who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who says in his bowing and his prostration and his standing: "May Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad", Allah would write for him the like of the bowing, and the prostration, and the standing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ja'far ibn Ali, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) prostrating after the prayer, so he spread his arms upon the ground and pressed his forehead to the ground in his supplication.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khaqan, who said: I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third [Imam] prostrating the prostration of gratitude, and he spread out his arms and pressed his chest and belly to the ground. So I asked him about that, and he said: 'Such is how we love to do it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz who said, 'One of our companions narrated to me.' Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), when he raised his head from the last rak'ah of Witr, would say: 'This is the station of one whose good deeds are a bounty from You, and his gratitude is weak, and his sin is great, and he has nothing except Your repelling [punishment] and Your mercy.' For You said in Your Book Revealed upon Your Dispatched Prophet (peace be upon him): 'They used to sleep but little in the night, and in the morning they sought Forgiveness.' My sleep has been long and my standing [in prayer] has been little, and this is the morning, and I am seeking Forgiveness from You for my sin, with the seeking of forgiveness of one who can find for himself neither harm nor benefit, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection.' Then he would fall down in prostration (peace be upon him).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mazi (peace be upon him be peace (about) what I should say in the prostration of gratitude, for our companions differed regarding it, so he (peace be upon him) said: Say while you are prostrating. O Allah, I bear witness to You, and I bear witness to Your angels, and Your prophets, and Your messengers, and all of Your creation, that You are Allah my Lord, and Islam is my religion, and Muhammad is my prophet, and Ali, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, up to the last of them, are my Imams. With them I befriend and from their enemies I disavow. O Allah, I adjure You by the blood of the oppressed (three times). O Allah, I adjure You by Your promise upon Yourself regarding Your guardians, that You make them victorious over Your enemy and their enemy, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the protected ones from the family of Muhammad. O Allah, I ask You for ease after difficulty (three times). Then place your right cheek on the ground and say: O my refuge, when the paths weary me and the earth is straitened for me despite its vastness, and O Creator of my creation, have mercy on me, although You were needless of my creation. Send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the protected ones from the family of Muhammad. Then place your left cheek (on the ground) and say: O Humiliator of every tyrant, and O Honorer of every humbled one. And I swear by Your Might that my striving has reached its end (three times). Then say: O Affectionate, O Bestower, O Remover of great distress (three times). Then return to prostration and say one hundred times: Thank You, Thank You. Then ask for your need, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Suleiman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the prostration of gratitude, so he wrote to me: 'A hundred times: 'Thank you, thank you,' and if you wish, 'Forgiveness, forgiveness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! This, which has appeared on my face, the people allege that Allah has not afflicted a servant with it in whom He has a need.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. The Believer of the Pharaoh's household was of crippled fingers, so he would say like this,' and he extended his hand and said: 'O people! Follow the Messengers.' He said: 'Then he said to me: When it is the last third of the night during its beginning, perform ablution, then stand for your prayer which you tend to pray. So when you are in the last prostration from the first two rak'at, say while you are prostrating:' 'O Ali, O Magnificent, O Beneficent, O Merciful, O Hearer of the supplications, O Giver of goodness! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the People of the Household of Muhammad.' And give me from the goodness of the world and the Hereafter whatever You deem to be rightful, and turn away from me from the evil of the world and the Hereafter what I am deserving of. And remove from me this pain' – and you specify it – 'for it has anguished me and grieved me' – and insist in the supplication.' He said: 'So I did it, and I had not even arrived in Kufa until Allah had removed all of it from me.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'dan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) used to say in his prostration: 'My worn-out face prostrates to Your Remaining, Everlasting, Magnificent Face. My humble face prostrates to Your Honorable Face. My poor face prostrates to the Face of my Lord, the Self-Sufficient, the Generous, the Exalted, the Magnificent.' O Lord, I seek Your forgiveness from what has been and I seek Your forgiveness from what will be. O Lord, do not exhaust my afflictions. O Lord, do not let my enemies gloat over me. O Lord, do not make my decree bad. O Lord, indeed there is no Defender nor Preventer except You. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with the best of Your blessings, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with the best of Your blessings. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from Your seizures, and I seek refuge in You from all Your anger and wrath. Glory be to You, there is no god except You, Lord of the worlds. And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say while prostrating: 'Have mercy on my humility before You, and my supplication to You, and my loneliness from the people, and make me comfortable with You, O Generous One.' And he used to say also: 'You advised me but I did not heed, and You deterred me from Your prohibitions but I did not desist, and You enriched me with Your favors but I did not thank You for Your pardon. Your pardon, O Generous One! I ask You for ease at death, and I ask You for pardon at the reckoning.' And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say while prostrating: 'There is no god except You, truly, truly! I prostrated to You, O Lord, in submission and servitude. O Magnificent, indeed my deed is weak, so multiply it for me. O Generous, O Gracious, forgive my sins and my crime, and accept my deed. O Generous, O Compeller, I seek refuge in You from failing or bearing injustice.' O Allah, from You is the bounty, and You provide its gratitude, and upon You is the reward of what You bestowed from its reward, by the grace of Your prolongation and the nobility of its return.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ziad ibn Marwan, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to say in his prostration: 'I seek Refuge with You from a Fire, its heat not being extinguished; and I seek Refuge with You from a Fire, its renewal not wearing out; and I seek Refuge with You from a Fire, its thirst not being quenched; and I seek Refuge with You from a Fire, its bareness not being coated.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When one of you recites the Sajdah verse from the decisive (obligatory) ones, let him say in his prostration: 'I have prostrated to You as an act of worship and servitude, not being too arrogant to worship You, nor too proud, nor too exalted, but I am a humble servant, fearful, seeking refuge.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ziyad al-Qandy, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), 'Teach me a supplication, for I have been afflicted with something' – and he had been imprisoned in Baghdad where he was accused of their wealth. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Whenever you pray, prolong your prostration (sujood), then say: O One for whom there is no one, until your breath runs out. Then say: O One whom the frequency of supplication does not increase except in generosity and nobility, until your breath runs out. Then say: O Lord of the lords, You are, You are, You are the One from whom hope is cut off except for You. O Exalted, O Magnificent.' Ziyad said, 'So I supplicated with it, and Allah relieved me and freed my way.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halbi, from his father, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was praying, so I counted for him in the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood) sixty glorifications (tasbihat).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamza ibn Humran and Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who both said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and there were some people with him. So he led them in the Asr prayer, and we had already prayed. We counted for him during his bowing, 'Glorious is my Lord the Magnificent', thirty-four or thirty-three times. And one of them said in his hadith: 'And his praise during the bowing and prostration was the same.' This is because he (peace be upon him) knew the capacity of the people for the length of his bowing and prostration, and that is because it is reported that the virtue for the Imam is to lighten [the prayer] and pray with the weakest of the people.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the least of what would suffice the sick, from the Glorification during the Rukūʿ and the Sajdah?' He said, 'One Glorification'.

Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no word lighter upon the tongue than it, nor more eloquent than 'Subhanallah' (Glory be to Allah).' I said: 'Will it suffice me during the Ruku' and Sujood if I say in place of the Tasbih: 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah), 'Alhamdulillah' (Praise be to Allah), and 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest)?' He said: 'Yes, all of that is the Dhikr of Allah.' He said: I said: 'We know Alhamdulillah and La ilaha illallah, so what is the interpretation of Subhanallah?' He said: 'It is a sense of respect (Anafah) for Allah. Do you not see that when a man is astounded by something, he says 'Subhanallah'?'.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I am the prayer leader of a district mosque, so I bow with them, and I hear the thumping of their slippers while I am bowing.' He said, 'Remain in your bowing for a duration similar to your bowing. If (the sound) ceases, or else, stand upright.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abu Al-Abbas Al-Fadl ibn Abdul-Malik, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not perform prostration (Sajdah) except upon the earth or what the earth produces, except for cotton and flax (linen).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Do I prostrate upon the asphalt, meaning the bitumen/pitch?' He said, 'No, and not upon the cloth, nor the cotton pads, nor upon the wool, nor upon anything from the animals, nor upon food, nor upon anything from the fruits of the earth, nor upon anything from the feathers.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the lime (plaster) upon which faeces and the bones of the dead were burned, then the mosque is plastered with it. Can one perform prostration upon it? So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me in his own handwriting: 'The water and the fire have already purified it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father called for the Khumrah (a small piece of flax), but it was delayed for him, so he took a handful of pebbles and placed them on the carpet, then performed Sajdah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with standing upon the prayer mat made of hair and wool, when one prostrates on the ground. And if it is made from the growth of the earth, then there is no problem with standing upon it and prostrating upon it.

Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Saeed, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: Do not perform Sajdah upon the Qir (bitumen/asphalt), nor upon the Sarouj (cement/construction material).
Muhammad ibn Yahya, by his chain, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Prostration upon the earth is obligatory, and upon the khumrah is a sunnah.
Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not perform Sajdah upon gold, nor upon silver.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The man does not perform sajdah upon anything upon which the rest of his body is not. Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Humran, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: My father (peace be upon him) used to pray upon the khumrah (a small piece of flax), placing it upon the carpet and performing sajdah upon it. So when there was no khumrah, pebbles were placed upon the carpet where he would perform sajdah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he disliked to perform Sajdah upon a paper upon which there is writing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amriki Al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man who prays upon the wet growing grass. He said: 'When he presses his forehead to the ground, there is no problem.' And (I asked him) about the thick growing lawn grass, which touches new ground. He said: 'No problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, that one of our companions wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Mazi (peace be upon him) asking him about the prayer upon glass, and he said: So when my letter reached him, I thought and said to myself, 'It is from what the earth produces, and it is not for me to ask him about it.' He said, so he wrote to me: 'Do not pray upon glass, and even if your soul tells you that it is from what the earth produces, it is from salt and sand, and both have been metamorphosed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn that some of our companions wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him) asking him about prayer on glass. He said: When my letter reached him, I pondered and said to myself, 'It is something that the earth produces, so I do not need to ask him about it.' He said: He wrote to me, 'Do not pray on glass, even if your soul tells you that it is from what the earth produces. However, it is from salt and sand, and they are metamorphosed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The entire forehead, from the middle of the hair of the head to the two eyebrows, is the place of prostration. So, whichever part from that falls to the ground, it suffices you, the measurement of a dirham and the measurement of the tip of the finger.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you place your forehead upon a mound, do not raise it, but drag it upon the ground.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the place of the forehead of the one prostrating, can it be higher than the place of standing? He said: No, but it should be even. And in another hadith regarding prostration on raised ground, he said: If the place of your forehead is higher than your legs by the measure of a brick, there is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from one of his companions, from Musadif who said: A boil (dummal) broke out on me, so I was prostrating (sajdah) on a side. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw its mark, so he said: 'What is this?' I said: 'I am unable to prostrate due to the boil, so I am prostrating sideways.' He said to me: 'Do not do so, but dig a small hole, place the boil in the hole, until your forehead falls upon the ground.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, by a chain of his, said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about the one who has an illness in his forehead, not being able to perform Sajdah upon it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should place his chin upon the ground.' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: 'They are falling down upon their chins in Sajdah.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) level the pebbles when he intended to prostrate.

Muhammad, from Al-Fadl, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Does the man blow in the place of his forehead during the prayer?' So he said, 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prostrates while wearing a turban, and his face does not touch the ground. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That does not suffice him until his forehead touches the ground.'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)far (peace be upon him) who said: When you stand in the prayer, do not join your foot with the other; leave a gap between them of a finger's width, the least of that being up to a span, and more is allowed. Drop your shoulders, extend your hands, do not interlace your fingers, and let them rest on your thighs in front of your knees, and let your gaze be towards the place of your prostration. When you bow, align your feet in your bowing, placing between them a span's distance. Place your palms upon your knees, placing your right hand on your right knee before the left. Reach the tips of your fingers to the center of the knee, and spread your fingers when you place them on your knees. When the tips of your fingers reach your knees during bowing, that suffices you. And what I love is that you place your palms firmly on your knees, so your fingers are in the center of the knee and you spread between them. Straighten your back, extend your neck, and let your gaze be towards what is between your feet. When you intend to prostrate, raise your hands with the Takbir and fall down prostrating. Begin with your hands, placing them on the ground before your knees, placing them together. Do not spread your forearms flat like a beast spreads its forearms, nor place your forearms on your knees and thighs. Rather, wing with your elbows. Do not join your palms to your knees, nor bring them close to your face; they should be parallel to your shoulders. Do not place them directly in front of your knees, but divert them slightly from that. Extend them on the ground with an extension, and pull them towards you with a pull. And if there is a garment beneath them, it does not harm you. And if you lead them to the ground, that is better. And do not spread between your fingers during your prostration, but gather them all together. He said: And when you sit for your Tashahhud, join your knees to the ground and separate between them slightly. Let the back of your left foot be on the ground, and the back of your right foot be on the inside of your left foot. Let your buttocks be on the ground, and the tip of your right big toe be on the ground. Be

And by these chains, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: When the woman stands in the prayer, she gathers her two feet and does not separate them, and she brings her hands to her chest due to the location of her breasts. When she bows, she places her hands above her knees upon her thighs so that she does not bend down excessively, causing her backside to rise. When she sits, she sits on her backside, not as the man sits. And when she lowers herself for prostration, she begins by sitting on her two knees before her hands, then she prostrates, pasting her body to the ground. When she is in her sitting, she brings her thighs together and raises her knees from the ground. And when she rises, she slips away smoothly, not raising her backside first.

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not sit between the two prostrations with a full, deep sitting (i.e., do not sit fully upright and settled).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the woman performs prostration (sujūd), she should extend her forearms.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) inclined [to prostrate], he bowed down while exclaiming Takbir.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: When a man prostrates, then intends to stand up, he should not knead his hands in the ground, but he should extend his palms without placing his buttocks on the ground.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-His father, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked him about the sitting of the woman during the prayer. He said: 'She should clasp her thighs (together).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, who said: The woman, when she prostrates, should be clasped (compact), and the man, when he prostrates, should be open (spread out).

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'What is the meaning of "Therefore pray to your Lord and make a sacrifice"?' He said: 'The sacrifice (anhar) refers to moderation in standing, that he should straighten his back and his neck/face.' And he said: 'Do not place one hand over the other, for that is what the Magians do, and do not cover your face, do not hold your limbs tightly, do not sit on your heels, and do not spread out your arms.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — all of them from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara who said: Zurara said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had obligated of the salat. He said: Five prayers during the night and the day. I said: Has He named them and clarified them in His Book? He said: Yes. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Establish prayer from the declining of the sun to the darkness of the night' [17:78]. The declining of the sun is its zenith-passing; so between the declining of the sun and the darkness of the night are four prayers — Allah named them, clarified them, and fixed their times. The darkness of the night is its midpoint. Then He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: [17:78] '...and the recitation of dawn; indeed the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.' That is the fifth. Allah the Exalted also said regarding this: [11:114] 'Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night' — and its two ends are the Maghrib and the morning, and the early hours of the night is the last 'Isha prayer. And the Exalted said: [2:238] 'Guard your prayers and the middle prayer' — and it is the Zuhr prayer, and it is the first prayer that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed, and it is the middle of the day and the middle of the two daytime prayers, which are the morning prayer and the 'Asr prayer. And in some recitations: [2:238] 'Guard your prayers and the middle prayer — the 'Asr prayer — and stand before Allah in devout obedience.' He said: This verse was revealed on a Friday while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on a journey. The Messenger of Allah performed it (the Jumu'a prayer) and left it upon its condition during both travel and residence, and added two rak'at for the resident. The two rak'at which the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) added on Friday for the resident were in place of the two sermons with the Imam. Therefore, whoever prays on Friday without a congregation should pray it as four rak'at, like the Zuhr prayer on other days.

And by his chain, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: What God had obligated upon the servants from salat was ten rak'at, and in them is recitation, and there is no doubt (i.e., inadvertent mistake) in them. Then the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) added seven, and in them is doubt (allowed), and there is no recitation in them.

And by his chain, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: God prescribed the salat, and the Messenger of God (blessings of God be upon him and his family) established the Sunnah upon ten aspects: the salat of the resident and the traveler, and the salat of fear in three aspects, and the salat for the eclipse of the sun and the moon, and the salat of the two Eids, and the salat for rain, and the salat over the deceased.

Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Indeed the salat was always a timed ordinance upon the believers' — meaning it is obligatory.

Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the obligatory elements in the salat, and he said: 'The time, and the purity, and the qibla, and the facing, and the ruku', and the sujud, and the supplication.' I said, 'What about what is besides that?' He said: 'A sunnah within an obligation.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: For salat, there are four thousand limits. And in another narration: For salat, there are four thousand doors (chapters).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ten rak'at are — two rak'at from Zuhr, and two rak'at from Asr, and two rak'at of Subh, and two rak'at of Maghrib, and two rak'at of the later Isha. Doubt is not permissible in these, and whoever doubts in any of these must restart the prayer from the beginning. These are the prayers which God — Mighty and Majestic — prescribed upon the believers in the Quran and delegated to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) added seven rak'at to the prayer, and these are the Sunnah in which there is no Quranic recitation — but rather glorification (tasbih), proclamation of God's oneness (tahlil), magnification (takbir), and supplication. Doubt can only occur in these. So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) added to the prayer of the resident — not the traveler — two rak'at each in Zuhr, Asr, and the later Isha, and one rak'a in Maghrib for both the resident and the traveler.
The salat is of three thirds — a third being purity, a third being ruku, and a third being sujud.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habeeb, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Tashahhud, so he said: 'Had it been as they say, obligatory upon the people, they would have been destroyed. Rather, the people were saying the easiest of what they knew. If you praise Allah, it suffices for you.'

And in another report from Safwan, from Mansur, from Bakr ibn Habeeb, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What should I say in the Tashahhud and the Qunut?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Say with the best of what you know, for if it were fixed, the people would be destroyed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Yahya ibn Talha, from Sawrah ibn Kuleyb, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the least of what would suffice from the Tashahhud, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The two testimonies'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Should I recite in the Tashahhud: Whatever is good, so it is for Allah, and whatever is bad, so it is for others?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is what Ali (peace be upon him) was saying.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the Imam that he makes those behind him hear the Tashahhud, and they should not make him hear anything.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halbi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whatever you mention Allah with, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), is part of the Salat (prayer). And if you say,

And by this chain, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are in a row, greet with a greeting to your right and a greeting to your left, because on your left is the one who greets you; and when you are the Imam, greet with one greeting while you are facing the Qiblah.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you have finished the prayer, turn away to your right.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who stands in the row behind the Imam, and there is no one on his left.
