How should he greet? He (peace be upon him) said: He should greet once on his right.

And by this chain, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you stand from the Rak'ah, rely upon your palms and say, "By the Might of Allah and His Strength, I stand and sit," for Ali (peace be upon him) used to do that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you sit in the first two rak'at, so you perform the Tashahhud, then stand, so say, 'By the Might of Allah and His Strength I am standing and sitting'.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Qunut in the five (obligatory) prayers, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform Qunut in all of them.' He said, 'And I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) after that about the Qunut, so he said to me: 'As for what you recite loudly, do not doubt (its validity).'

Ahmad narrated from Al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal who said: I prayed behind Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) for days, and he used to perform Qunut in every prayer, both in those wherein recitation is loud and in those wherein it is not loud.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Qunut, so he said: 'In what is recited aloud.' I said to him, 'I asked your father about that, and he said: 'In all five [prayers].' He said: 'May Allah have mercy on my father. The companions of my father came to him and asked him, so he informed them with the truth. Then they came to me as doubtful, so I issued a fatwa to them with taqiyyah (dissimulation).'

Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform Qunut in every two Rak'at, obligatory or optional, before the Ruku'.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Qunut, so he said: (It is recited) in every obligatory and optional prayer.
And by this chain, from Yunus, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who neglects the Qunut, turning away from it, so there is no Salat for him.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Qunut is in every Salat, in the second Rak'at, before the Ruku'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Ismail ibn Al-Fazl, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Qunut and what is to be said during it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever Allah ordains upon your tongue, and I do not know of anything fixed for it.'

By this chain, from Fazalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Qunut in the obligatory prayer is supplication, and in the Witr is the seeking of forgiveness.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man forgot the Qunut, so he remembered it while he was in one of the parts of the prayer path (sequence). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should face the Qiblah, then let him say it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'I dislike for the man that he should turn away from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) or leave it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the least (recitation in) the Qunut, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Five Glorifications'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It would suffice you in the Qunut (to say): 'O Allah! Forgive us, and have mercy on us, and grant us health, and pardon us in the world and the Hereafter. You are Able over everything.'
Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I do not recognize Qunut except before the Ruku'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, who said: 'Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen narrated to me, saying: I asked a virtuous one (peace be upon him) about the Qunut in the Witr and Fajr prayers, and what is recited aloud in it, before the Ruku' or after it. So he (peace be upon him) said: Before the Ruku', when you finish your recitation.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ziyad al-Qandy, from Dorost, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: He said: The Qunut is [performed] in every prayer, in the obligatory and the optional.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the Imam that he should move/turn when he has offered the greeting (Salām) until those behind him have completed the prayer (Salāt). He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about the man who leads the prayer, is it befitting for him to follow up with his companions after the greeting? So he said: He glorifies (God) and goes wherever he wishes for his need, and a man should not follow up specifically to follow up the Imam.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any man who leads a people in prayer, upon him is that he sits after the Taslim (greeting), and he does not leave that place until those behind him, who were preceded (in prayer), complete their prayer. That is obligatory upon every Imam when he knows that among them is one who was preceded, and if he knows that there is no one among them who was preceded in prayer, then let him go wherever he wishes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Mansour ibn Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who prays an Obligatory Salat and follows up to another, so he is a guest of Allah, and has a right upon Allah that He be Benevolent with His guest.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Hasan ibn al-Mughira that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The superiority of the supplication after the Obligatory (prayer) over the supplication after the optional (prayer) is like the superiority of the Obligatory (prayer) over the optional (prayer). He said, then he said: 'Supplicate to Him and do not say that the matter is finished, for the supplication is the worship.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Surely those who are too proud to worship Me shall soon enter Hell abased.' And He said: 'Call upon Me, I will Answer you.' And he said: 'Whenever you intend to supplicate to Allah, so glorify Him, praise Him, declare His holiness, laud Him, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then ask, you will be given.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The supplication after the obligatory prayer is superior to the voluntary prayer.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recites the Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) before bending his legs from the obligatory Salat, Allah will forgive him, and let him begin with the Takbir.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Abi Najran, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever glorifies Allah at the end of the obligatory prayer with the glorification of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her), one hundred times, and follows it with 'La ilaha illa Allah', Allah will forgive him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from al-Khaybari, from al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr and Abu Salma al-Sarraj, who said: We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he was sending la'an (asking for Allah's wrath) at the end of every prescribed prayer on four from the men and four from the women: So-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and Muawiya (and he named them), and so-and-so woman, and so-and-so woman, and Hind, and Umm al-Hakam, the sister of Muawiya.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you have a doubt in the Glorification (Tasbih) of Fatima Al-Zahra (peace be upon her), so repeat it.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). That he used to glorify with the glorification of Fatima (peace be upon her), so he would connect it and not break it.

And by this chain, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Uqba, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah was not worshipped with anything from the praises superior to the Glorification of Fatima (peace be upon her), and if there had been anything superior to it, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would have bestowed it upon Fatima (peace be upon her).

And from him, from Abu Khalid Al-Qammat, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The glorification of Fatima (peace be upon her) every day at the end of every prayer is more beloved to me than a prayer of a thousand units (rak'at) every day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The least of what suffices you from supplication after the obligatory prayer is that you should say: 'O Allah, I ask You of every good of which Your Knowledge has encompassed, and I seek refuge with You from every evil of which Your Knowledge has encompassed. O Allah, I ask You for Your well-being in all my affairs, and I seek refuge with You from the disgrace of the world and the punishment of the Hereafter.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu Al-Abbas Al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The supplication is answered in four places: in Al-Witr, and after Al-Fajr, and after Al-Zuhr, and after Al-Maghrib.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not forget the two duties', or he said: 'It is upon you to adhere to the two duties at the end of every prayer.' I said, 'And what are the two duties?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Asking Allah for Paradise and seeking Refuge with Allah from the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Suleyman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said: A man (peace be upon him) wrote to me: In the prostration of gratitude, say one hundred times: 'Thanks, thanks', and if you wish, 'Pardon, pardon'.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, by his chain, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one whose fingers move faster than his tongue, so (he will be) counted in his favour.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawood al-Ajaly, a slave of Abu al-Maghra'a, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three have been given the power to hear the creatures: Paradise, the Fire, and the Maiden Houries. So when the servant prays and says: "O Allah, liberate me from the Fire, and admit me into Paradise, and marry me to the Maiden Houries," the Fire says: "O Lord, Your servant has asked You to emancipate him from me, so emancipate him." And Paradise says: "O Lord, Your servant has asked You for me, so settle him in me." And the Maiden Houries say: "O Lord, Your servant has proposed to You for us, so marry him to us." So if he finishes from his prayer and did not ask Allah for anything from this, the Maiden Houries say: "This servant is an ascetic regarding us." And Paradise says: "This servant is an ascetic regarding me." And the Fire says: "This servant is ignorant regarding me."'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) A supplication to be recited at the end of every prayer you pray. If there is an illness in you from disease and pain, so when you complete your prayer, wipe your hand upon the place of your prostration from the ground, and supplicate with this supplication, and pass your hand over the place of your pain seven times, saying. O the One Who Compressed the earth upon the water, and Filled the atmosphere with the sky, and Chose for Himself the best of the Names! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and do such and such with me, and Grace me with such and such, and Grant me good health from such and such (pain).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: You wipe with your right hand upon your forehead and your face at the end of Al-Maghrib prayer and the other prayers, and you say: 'In the Name of Allah, the Knower of the Hidden and the Apparent, the Beneficent, the Merciful, Who there is no god except Him. O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from worry, grief, sickness, deficiency, lowliness, disgrace, and immoralities, whatever is apparent of them and whatever is hidden.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul Malik al-Qummi, from Idrees his brother, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When you have finished your prayer, say: O Allah, I follow Your religion by Your obedience, and Your Wilayah, and the Wilayah of Your Messenger, and the Wilayah of the Imams (peace be upon them), from their first to their last, and I name them. Then say: O Allah, I follow Your religion by Your obedience and their Wilayah, and pleasure with what You have preferred them with, without arrogance nor being arrogant against the meaning of what You revealed in Your Book, upon the limits of what reached us regarding it and what did not reach us, believing, accepting, submitting to that, pleased with what You are pleased with. O Lord, I intend Your Face and the Hereafter by it, fearing and desiring to You with regards to it. So keep me alive upon that for whatever duration You cause me to live, and cause me to die upon that whenever You cause me to die, and resurrect me upon that whenever You resurrect me. And if there was a deficiency from me in what is past, then I repent to You from it and wish to You regarding what is in Your Presence. And I ask You to safeguard me from Your disobedience, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, ever, for whatever duration You keep me alive, neither less than that nor more. The self is prone to evil except what You are merciful with, O most Merciful of the merciful ones. And I ask You to safeguard me by Your obedience until You cause me to die upon it and You are pleased with me, and to end for me with happiness, and do not turn me away from it ever. And there is no strength except with You.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Muhammad al-Wasiti, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not leave (saying) at the end of every prayer.' 'I seek Refuge for myself and for whatever my Lord has graced me with, with Allah, the One, the Last,' until you end it (Surah 112); 'and I seek Refuge for myself and whatever my Lord has graced me with, with the Lord of Al-Falaq,' until you end it (Surah 113); 'and I seek Refuge for myself and whatever my Lord has graced me with, with the Lord of the people,' until you end it (Surah 114).

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). 'If you see fit, O my Master, to teach me a supplication with which I may supplicate at the end of my prayers, by which Allah will gather for me the goodness of the world and the Hereafter.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'You should say.' 'I seek Refuge with Your Benevolent Face, and Your Might which cannot be assailed, and Your Power, from which nothing can be prevented, from the evil of the world and the Hereafter, and from the evil of all pains.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who performed the obligatory prayer, and when he finished and raised his head from the second prostration of the fourth rak'ah, he broke his ablution. He said: As for his prayer, it has passed, and the Tashahhud remains; and indeed, the Tashahhud is a Sunnah in the prayer, so let him perform ablution and return to his seat or a clean place, and then perform the Tashahhud.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man whose ablution breaks after he raises his head from the last prostration, before he performs the Tashahhud, he said: He should leave and perform ablution. So if he wishes, he returns to the mosque, and if he wishes, [he does so] in his house, and if he wishes, wherever he wishes. He sits and performs the Tashahhud, then gives the greeting. And if the breaking of ablution occurred after the Tashahhud, then his prayer has passed (is completed).

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who forgets the opening Takbir. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah, from Aban, from Al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik or Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who prays but did not open with the Takbir, will the Takbir of the Ruku' suffice him? He said: No, but he should repeat his prayer if he remembers that he did not say Takbir.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), said: The Imam bears the imaginations (of the followers) of those behind him, except for the opening Takbir.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: Indeed, Allah has made the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood) obligatory, and the recitation is a Sunnah. So whoever deliberately leaves the recitation, he must repeat the prayer, and whoever forgets the recitation, his prayer is complete and there is nothing upon him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot the Mother of the Quran (Al-Fatiha). He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has not yet bowed (in ruku'), let him repeat the Mother of the Quran.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I prayed the prescribed prayer but forgot to recite in my prayer, all of it.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Is it not so that you had completed the bowing and the prostration?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Your prayer is complete, when it was out of forgetfulness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who doubts while he is standing, not knowing whether he had performed Rukū' or not. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform Rukū' and perform Sajdah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who forgot that he had not bowed (ruku') until he prostrated (sajdah) and stood up. He said: 'He should begin again.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When he is convinced that an extra rak'ah has been added to the prescribed prayer, he should not count it, and he should restart the prayer from the beginning, provided he was certain with conviction.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who erred, so he did not know whether he had performed one prostration or two. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform another prostration another, and it is not upon him, after the completion of the prayer, to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who doubted, so he did not know whether he had performed one prostration or two. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should prostrate until he is convinced that they are two prostrations.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man upon whom doubt fell, and he did not know whether he prostrated once or twice, he (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him prostrate one more.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you doubt in the first two Rak'at, so repeat'.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I said to him, 'A man does not know whether he has prayed one rak'ah or two.' He said, 'He should repeat (the prayer).' I said to him, 'A man did not know whether he had prayed two or three.' So he said, 'If the doubt enters him after he has entered the third rak'ah, he should proceed in the third, then pray the other (one), and there is nothing upon him, and he should offer Salam.' I said, 'So if he does not know whether he was in the second or the fourth?' He said, 'He should offer Salam, and stand, so he should pray two rak'ahs, then offer Salam, and there is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The repeating is regarding the first two Rak'at, and the omission is (allowed) during the last two Rak'at.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you doubt in the Maghrib (prayer), so repeat it, and when you doubt in the Fajr (prayer), so repeat it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays and does not know whether he has prayed one or two [rak'at]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should face [the qibla] until he is convinced that he has completed [the prayer], and this applies to Friday [prayer], and to Maghrib, and to the prayer during the journey.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hazrami, who said: I prayed the Maghrib prayer with my companions. So when I had prayed two rak'at, I gave the salam. So one of them said, 'You only prayed two rak'at, so repeat.' So I informed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Perhaps you repeated?' I said, 'Yes.' He smiled, then said: 'It would have sufficed you if you had stood and prayed one rak'at.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no omission (of obligatory acts) in the Maghrib and Fajr prayers.

I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), I and Humran ibn A'yan. So Humran said to him: 'What do you say regarding what Zurara says, and I have differed with him in it?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What is it?' He said: 'He claims that the timings of the salat were delegated to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and he was the one who established them.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So what do you say?' I said: 'Jibreel (peace be upon him) came to him on the first day with the first timing, and on the last day with the last timing. Then Jibreel (peace be upon him) said: what is between them is a time.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Humran! Zurara says that Jibreel (peace be upon him) came only as an indicator to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and Zurara speaks the truth. Rather, God made that [the determination of prayer times] to be for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and he established it, and Jibreel (peace be upon him) indicated it to him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Allan, from Hammad ibn Isa and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Rib'i ibn Abd Allah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'Indeed among things are things with leeway and things with constraint. Salat is among those with leeway — it may be prayed early at one time and delayed to another. But the Friday (prayer) is among those with constraint: its time on a Friday is the moment the sun passes its zenith, and the time for Asr on that day corresponds to the time of Zuhr on other days.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'For every salat are two timings, and the beginning of the time is the best of it; and it is not for anyone to make the last of the two times as his time, except in the case of an excuse without an illness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazala ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar or Ibn Wahb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: For every salat there are two times — the beginning of the time is the better of the two.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May God keep you well! For each salat, is the beginning of the time superior, or its middle, or its end?' So he said: 'Its beginning. Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, loves from the goodness what is hastened.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf ibn Amira, from his father, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The merit of the beginning time over the end time is like the merit of the Hereafter over the world.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the virtue of the beginning of the prayer time over the last is better for a man than his children and his wealth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Know that the beginning of the time is always superior, so hasten with goodness as much as you are able; and the most beloved of deeds to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is what the servant persists in doing, even if it be little.'

Ahmad ibn Idris and another, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Mansur ibn Hazim or someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (blessings of God upon him) said: 'The one who is attentive to the timings of salat will never fully indulge in the pleasures of the world.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalat, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed but did not know whether he was in the third or the fourth (rak'ah). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever his guess (wahm) leads him to, if he thinks he is in the third and has some notion in his heart of the fourth, he should give the greeting of peace (salam) to himself and his own self, then he should pray two rak'ahs, reciting in them with the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah).'

And from him, from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If his doubt is established regarding the third and the fourth, he should conclude (the prayer), and pray two rak'at, and four prostrations with the Opening of the Book while he is seated, intending in the Tashahhud.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I said to him, 'For the one who does not know whether he is in the fourth or in the two, and he has secured the two,' he said: 'He should bow in two rak'at and perform four prostrations while standing, with the Opening of the Book, and perform Tashahhud, and there is nothing upon him; and if he does not know whether he is in the three or in the four, and he has secured the three, he stands and adds another to them, and there is nothing upon him.' And he does not invalidate certainty with doubt, nor does he insert doubt into certainty, nor does he mix one with the other, but rather he invalidates doubt with certainty and completes upon certainty, so he builds upon it, and he does not count the doubt in any of the states.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who does not know whether he prayed two rak'at or four. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He performs the Tashahhud and gives the Salam, then stands up and prays two rak'at with four prostrations, reciting in them the Opening of the Book. Then he performs the Tashahhud and gives the Salam. And if he had prayed four, these two are a supererogatory prayer (Nafl); and if he had prayed two, these two complete the four. And if he speaks, let him perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdatay al-Sahw).'

Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: The omission (doubt) is only what is between the third and the fourth, and in the two and in the four is of that same status. And whoever forgets and does not know whether he prayed three or four, and his doubt is equal, he should stand and complete (the prayer), then sit, so he performs the Tashahhud and offers Salam, and prays two Rak'at and four Sajdahs while he is seated. So if his imagination was more towards the four, he should perform Tashahhud and Salam, then recite the Opening of the Book, and bow and prostrate, then recite and prostrate two Sajdahs, and perform Tashahhud and Salam. And if his imagination was more towards the two, he should arise and pray two Rak'at, and perform Tashahhud and Salam.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who prayed but did not know whether he prayed two, three, or four [rak'at], he (peace be upon him) said: 'He stands and prays two [rak'at] while standing, then offers the salām, then he prays two [rak'at] while sitting, and offers the salām. So if it was four [rak'at], the two [rak'at] are optional (nafl), otherwise the four are complete.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayabat and Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you do not know whether you prayed three or four, and your opinion leans toward three, then build upon three; and if your opinion leans toward four, then offer the salām and depart; and if your doubt is equal, then depart and pray two rak'at while you are seated.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you do not know whether you have prayed two or four, and your doubt does not lean towards anything specific, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām, then pray two Rak'at and four Sajdahs, reciting Umm al-Qur'an in both of them, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām. So if you had only prayed two, these two would complete the four, and if you had prayed four, these two would be optional (Nafl). And if you do not know whether you have prayed three or four, and your doubt does not lean towards anything specific, then offer the Salām, then pray two Rak'at while you are seated, reciting in them Umm al-Kitab. And if your doubt leans towards the three, then stand and pray the fourth Rak'ah and do not perform the two Sajdahs of forgetfulness. So if your doubt leans towards the four, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām, then perform the two Sajdahs of forgetfulness.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the one who does not know whether he prayed three or four, and his imagination regarding that is equal, he said: 'When the imagination is equal between three and four, he has the choice: if he wishes, he prays one rak'ah while standing, and if he wishes, he prays two rak'ah and four prostrations while sitting.' And he said regarding a man who does not know whether he prayed two or four, and his imagination goes towards four or towards two rak'ah, that he prays two rak'ah and four prostrations. And he said: 'If your imagination goes towards two and four, it is the same, and the imagination in this case is not like it in the case of three and four.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you doubts in his prayer, so he does not know whether he has increased or is deficient, let him prostrate two prostrations while he is seated, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) named them Al-Murghimatayn (The Compelled Two).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Bukayr, the two sons of Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When one is convinced that he has increased in his prescribed prayer, he should not rely upon it, and he should re-commence his prayer with a fresh commencement, provided that he was convinced with certainty.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: The one who preserves his omission and completes it, so there are no two prostrations of omission upon him. Rather, the omission is upon the one who does not know whether he increased or decreased from it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Aamir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fazalat ibn Ayoub from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who increases in his prayer, so upon him is the repeating'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you do not know whether you have prayed five or four, then prostrate the two prostrations of forgetfulness after your salutation, while you are seated, then offer salutation after them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umayyah (Isa), from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever preserves his omission and completes it, then there is no Sajdat al-Sahw (two prostrations of forgetfulness) upon him. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Dhuhr with the people for two Rak'at, then he was forgetful and gave Salam. So Dhul-Shimalayn said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, has anything been revealed regarding the Salat?' He said, 'And what is that?' He said, 'You only prayed two Rak'at.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Are you saying the like of his words?' They said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him and his family) stood up and completed the Salat with them and prostrated with them the two prostrations of forgetfulness.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'What is your view of the one who prays two Rak'at and thinks that they are four, so he gives Salam and departs, then remembers after he has gone that he only prayed two Rak'at?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should restart the Salat from its beginning.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So what was the matter that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not restart the Salat, but rather he completed with them what remained of his Salat?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not leave his seat. So if he had not left his seat, then let him complete what was deficient from his Salat, when he had preserved the first two Rak'at.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the man who prays two rak'at from the prescribed prayer, then forgets and stands before sitting between the two, he said: 'Let him sit as long as he has not bowed, and his prayer is complete. If he does not remember until he bows, let him proceed in his prayer. So when he offers the salutation, he performs two prostrations while he is sitting.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Amr ibn Saeed, from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqa, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) offer the salām in the first two rak'at?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And his state was what it was?' He said, 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended for them to understand.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who speaks forgetfully during the prayer, saying, 'Straighten your rows!' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should complete his prayer, then he should perform two prostrations.' So I said: 'Are the two prostrations for forgetfulness before or after the salutation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'After.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Hal-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You should say in the two prostrations of forgetfulness: 'In the name of Allah and by Allah. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Al-Halby said, 'And I heard him another time saying: In the name of Allah and by Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed, then gave the salām in two rak'at. So one behind him asked him, 'O Messenger of Allah! Did something new occur in the prayer?' He said: 'And what is that?' They said, 'You only prayed two rak'at.' So he said: 'Was it like that, O Zal al-Yadayn?' And he used to be called Zal al-Shimalayn. So he said: 'Yes'. So he built upon his prayer and completed the prayer with four (rak'at). And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah is the One who caused him to forget as a mercy for the community. Do you not see that if a man were to do this, he would be faulted and it would be said, 'Your prayer is not accepted'? So whoever enters upon him today, that one says, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established a Sunnah and it became an example, and he performed two prostrations for the sake of the speech.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you stand in the first two rak'ahs and do not perform the Tashahhud, and you remember before you bow, then sit and perform the Tashahhud; and if you do not remember until you have bowed, then continue in your prayer as you are. So when you have finished, perform two prostrations (Sajdatan) without bowing in them, then perform the Tashahhud that you missed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you stand in the two rak'at of the Dhuhr prayer or other than these, and you do not perform the Tashahhud in them, and you remember that in the third rak'ah before you bow (perform Ruku'), so sit down and perform the Tashahhud, and stand to complete your prayer. So if you do not remember until you have bowed, so continue in your prayer until you are finished. So when you are finished, then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdatay al-Sahw) after the greeting (Taslim), before you speak.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who errs so he stands during a state of sitting or sits during a state of standing. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform two prostrations after the salutation, and these two are the constrainers, they constrain the Satan.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Safwan, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: If you do not know how many (rak'at) you have prayed and your doubt does not settle on a specific number, then repeat the prayer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Abu Baseer, who said: We said to him: 'A man doubts frequently in his prayer to the extent that he does not know how many he has prayed nor what remains upon him.' He said: 'He should repeat.' We said to him: 'But that is frequent upon him. Every time he repeats, he doubts.' He said: 'He should continue in his doubt.' Then he said: 'Do not accustom the wicked one (Satan) from yourselves by breaking the prayer, so you would embolden him, for Satan is wicked and gets used to what he is accustomized to. Therefore, let one of you continue in the doubt and should not frequently break the prayer, for if he does that time and again, the doubt will not return to him.' Zurara said: 'Then he said: 'The wicked one only wants to be obeyed. So when he is disobeyed, he will not return to one of you.'

Hammad, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: When you doubt, so you do not know whether you are in the third or in the second, or in the first, or in the fourth, so repeat and do not continue upon the doubt.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I complain to you about what I experience of whispers (waswasa) in my prayer, to the extent that I do not know whether I have prayed with increase or decrease.' So he said: 'When you enter into your prayer, strike your left thigh with your right forefinger (which is reciting/tasbih), then say: 'In the name of Allah, and by Allah I rely upon Allah. I seek refuge with Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the Pelted Satan.' For indeed you slaughter him and repel him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Imam praying with four or five people, and two of them say that they prayed three (rak'at), and three say that they prayed four, and these say 'Stand' and those say 'Sit', and the Imam is inclined with one of the two or is equal in doubt; so what is obligatory upon him? He said: There is no omission (sahw) upon the Imam if those behind him safeguard his omission with certainty, and there is no omission upon those behind the Imam if the Imam does not omit, and there is no double omission in an omission, and there is no omission in Maghrib and Fajr, nor in the first two rak'at of every prayer, nor in a voluntary prayer. So when those behind him differ from the Imam, then upon him and upon them, in precaution, is the repetition and taking by certainty.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no omission (sahw) upon the Imam (prayer leader), nor is there an omission upon the one who prays behind the Imam, nor is there an omission upon the omission, nor a repetition upon the repetition.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When omissions become numerous upon you, continue in your prayer, for it is on the verge of leaving you; it is only from Satan.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Ammar Al-Sabati narrated a report from you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?' I said, 'He reported that the Sunnah is obligatory.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where is he going? Where is he going? It is not like this. I narrated to him, rather I said to him: The one who prays and is devoted to his prayer, not distracting himself in it, or not omitting anything in it, Allah turns to him as he turned to it. So perhaps half of it is raised, or a quarter, or a third, or a fifth. And we have only commanded the Sunnah so that by it what is deficient from the obligatory prayer is completed.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: A man said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I was listening, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I frequently make mistakes in the prayer.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And has anyone ever been safe from it?' So he said, 'I do not think anyone makes more mistakes than me.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Abu Muhammad! The servant, a third of his prayer is raised for him, and half of it, and three-quarters of it, and less and more, according to the measure of his omission therein, but it is completed for him from the optional prayers.' He said, so Abu Baseer said to him, 'I do not see that the optional prayers should be left in any state.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, it should not.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they said: You have from your prayer only that portion for which you were attentive; so if you were negligent of all of it, or heedless of its performance, it is folded up and struck upon the face of its performer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ib al-Mughira, who said: In the book of Hariz, he said: I forgot that I was in an obligatory prayer until I bowed, while I intended it as voluntary. He said: It is that which you stood in. If you stood intending an obligatory prayer, then doubt entered you, so you are in the obligatory prayer. And if you entered into a voluntary prayer and intended it as obligatory, so you are in the voluntary prayer. And if you entered into an obligatory prayer, then remembered a voluntary prayer that was upon you, so continue in the obligatory prayer.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who is greeted while he is in prayer. He said: 'He replies with 'Salamun 'Alaykum' (Peace be upon you) and does not say 'Wa 'Alaykum as-Salam' (And upon you be peace), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was standing in prayer when 'Ammar ibn Yasir passed by him and 'Ammar greeted him. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) replied like this.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man sneezes during his prayer, let him praise Allah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I hear a sneeze while I am in prayer, so should I praise Allah and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'Yes. And when your brother sneezes and you are in prayer, say, 'The praise is for Allah,' and send blessings upon the Prophet. And if there is estrangement between you and your companion, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who is in prayer and sees a snake or a scorpion, and kills them if they harm him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who kills the bug, the flea, the louse, and the fly during the prayer: Does it break his prayer and his ablution? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who is standing in the obligatory prayer and forgets his bag or belongings, fearing their loss or destruction. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He cuts his prayer and secures his belongings, then he resumes the prayer.' I said: 'If he is in the obligatory prayer and an animal escapes from him, or his animal escapes, so he fears it will go away or he will suffer hardship from it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with him cutting his prayer.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Muhammad, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), whenever he found a louse in the Masjid, he buried it among the pebbles.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you are in the obligatory prayer and you see a slave of yours who has absconded, or a debtor of yours upon whom is wealth (due to you), or a snake you fear for yourself, then cut off the prayer and pursue the slave, or your debtor, and kill the snake.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If you find a louse while you are praying, bury it among the pebbles.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ubeyda al-Hazza', who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever builds a mosque, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.' Abu Ubeyda said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me on the road to Mecca, and I had leveled out a mosque with stones. So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We hope that this will be from that.' So he said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a mosque that is inside a house, so the people of the house intend to widen a section of it or relocate it to another place. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about a place that is filthy, then is cleaned and made into a mosque. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Soil is poured upon it until it covers it, so it becomes purer.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from al-Ays said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the synagogues and the churches, 'Is it correct to break these two in order to build the Masjids?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the shaded mosques, is it disliked to pray therein? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but it would not harm you today, and if justice (the Qaim) had been established, you would see what would be done regarding that.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him, can a man hang weapons in the mosque? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and as for the Great Mosque, then no, for my grandfather (peace be upon him) forbade a man trimming an arrow in the mosque.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Alawi, from Sahl ibn Jamhur, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn al-Uranni, from Amr ibn Jumi' who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the mosques with pictures, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that, but it will not harm you today, and if the justice had been established, you would see what would be done regarding that.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the rattling/clattering of the Persians (non-Arabs) in the mosques.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade unsheathing the sword in the mosque, and sharpening the arrows in the mosque. He said: 'It was built for other than that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the ablution performed in the Masjid, and he disliked it due to the faeces and the urine.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about sleeping in the Sacred Masjid and the Masjid of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, so where would the people sleep?'

From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding sleeping in the mosques?' He said, 'There is no harm in it, except in the two mosques: the Mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Sacred Mosque.' He said, 'And he used to take my hand in some part of the night, so he would sit in a corner, then sit down and converse in the Sacred Mosque. So sometimes he slept, and I slept. So I spoke to him regarding that, so he said, 'It is only disliked to sleep in the Sacred Mosque which was in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). But as for sleeping in this place, there is no harm in it.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Mihran Al-Karkhi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'If a man is in the Masjid during Salat and wants to spit,' so he said, 'On his left. And if he is not in Salat, he should not spit facing the Qiblah, and he may spit on his right and his left.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, raising it from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I dislike praying in their mosques.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not dislike it. There is no mosque built except that it is built upon the grave of a Prophet or a successor of a Prophet who was killed, and a sprinkle of his blood hit that spot. Therefore, Allah loved that He be remembered in it. So perform in it the obligatory [prayer] and the optional [prayers], and pay back in it what has passed you by [of missed prayers].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Asama Zayd Al-Shahham, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Do not approach the Prayer while you are intoxicated.' He said: 'The sleep (intoxication).'

A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Sleep does not break the ablution in any part of the prayer.

A group of our people narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from ibn Sinan, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Sleep is not excused in any part of the prayer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What the people are reporting is that the prayer in congregation is superior to the prayer of a man alone by twenty-five prayers.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'They are speaking the truth.' I said, 'Do two men constitute a congregation?' He said, 'Yes, and the man stands on the right of the Imam.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from his father who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Juhani came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, "O Messenger of Allah! I am in the countryside, and with me are my family, my children, and my slaves. So I recite the Adhan and Iqamah and pray Salat with them. Are we a Jam'at (congregation)?" He (peace be upon him) said, "Yes."' He said, "O Messenger of Allah! The slaves follow the drops of the rain/clouds, and there remain myself, my family, and my children. So I recite the Adhan and Iqamah and pray Salat with them. Are we a Jam'at?" He (peace be upon him) said, "Yes."' He said, "O Messenger of Allah! My children scatter among the livestock, and there remain myself and my family. So I recite the Adhan and Iqamah and pray Salat with them. Am I a Jam'at?" He (peace be upon him) said, "Yes."' He said, "O Messenger of Allah! The wife goes for her needs, so there remains me alone. So I recite the Adhan and Iqamah, so I pray Salat. Am I a Jam'at?" He (peace be upon him) said, "Yes. The Believer alone is a Jam'at."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah, from his father (peace be upon him), said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who prays the five [prayers] in congregation, so think good about him.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Would not the man from you be embarrassed if there happens to be a slave girl for him, and he sells her, so she could be saying, “He did not happen to be present for the Salat”?'

Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and Al-Fudayl, said: We said to him, 'Are the prayers in congregation an obligation?' So he said, 'The prayers are an obligation, and the gathering is not an obligation in all of the prayers, but it is a Sunnah, and whoever leaves it out of preference for it and for the congregation of the believers without an excuse, then there is no prayer for him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'Let those who are behind the Imam be the men of understanding and intelligence among you. So if the Imam forgets or becomes tired, they should correct him. And the best of the rows is the first one, and the best of the first row is that which is nearest to the Imam. And the superiority of the congregational prayer over the prayer of a lone man is twenty-five degrees in Paradise.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad by his chain who said: He (peace be upon him) said: The superiority of the right flanks of the rows over its left flanks is like the superiority of the congregation over the individual prayer.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is reckoned for you when you join them (in congregational prayer), even if you do not follow their recitation, similar to what is reckoned for you when you are with those whose recitation you do follow.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifa who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, Umar ibn Hanzala came to us from you with a timing.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Then he would not have lied against us.' I said: 'He mentioned that you said: Verily, the first salat Allah obligated upon His Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) is Al-Dhuhr, and it is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: [17:78] Establish the prayer from the declining of the sun. So when the sun declines, nothing prevents you except your optional prayer. Then you do not cease to be within the time until the shadow becomes one upright stature, and that is the end of the time. So when the shadow becomes one upright stature, the time of Al-Asr enters. And you do not cease to be in the time of Al-Asr until the shadow becomes two upright statures, and that is the evening. So he said: 'He spoke the truth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf ibn Amira, from his father, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the sun declines, the time of Dhuhr enters, except that there is an optional prayer (subha) preceding it — and that is up to you: if you wish, prolong it, and if you wish, shorten it.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When shall I pray Dhuhr?' He said: 'Pray eight (rak'at) at zawaal, then pray Dhuhr, then pray your optional prayer (subha), whether long or short, then pray Asr.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadhala ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira and 'Umar ibn Hanzala and Mansur ibn Hazim — they said: We used to estimate the sun at al-Madina by the cubit (shadow). So he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I not inform you of something clearer than this? When the sun declines, the time of Zuhr has entered, except that before it there is an optional prayer (subha), and that is up to you — if you wish, you prolong it, and if you wish, you shorten it.' And Sa'd narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nadhri and 'Umar ibn Hanzala, from Mansur — similar to it, and in it: 'It is up to you. If you have lightened your optional prayer (subha), then (begin Zuhr) when you finish your optional prayer; and if you have prolonged it, then (begin Zuhr) when you finish your optional prayer.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the sun declines, the time of the two salats has entered, except that this one (Zuhr) is before this one (Asr). And Sa'd reported, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, and al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, altogether from al-Qasim and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, from al-Qasim — similar to it, and in it: 'The time of al-Zuhr and al-Asr enters together.' And he added: 'Then you are in the time belonging to both of them together, until the sun sets.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim al-Bajali, from Salim Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A person asked him while I was present, so he said: 'Sometimes I enter the mosque and some of our companions are praying the Asr and some of them are praying the Zuhr.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I ordered them with this. If they had prayed at one (same) time, they would have been recognised, and they would have been seized by their necks.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Sa'id, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him about what has come in the hadith that you should pray al-Zuhr when the sun (i.e. its shadow) was one stature and two statures, and one cubit and two cubits, and one foot and two feet — from this and from that. So when is this, and how is this, and the shadow can sometimes be half a foot? He said: The hadith says 'the shadow of the stature' and does not say 'the stature of the shadow', and that is because the shadow of the stature varies — sometimes it increases and sometimes it decreases — while the upright object is always one stature, it does not change. Then he said: One cubit and two cubits, and one foot and two feet. So one cubit and two cubits became the explanation of one stature and two statures during the time in which the shadow of the stature is one cubit and the shadow of two statures is two cubits. Thus the shadow of the stature and two statures, and one cubit and two cubits, coincide in every season, both recognized, one being interpreted by the other and supported by it. So when it was a time in which the shadow of the stature was one cubit, the prayer time would be one cubit from the shadow of the stature, and the stature would be one cubit from the shadow. So when the shadow of the stature is less or more, the prayer time would be determined by the cubit and the two cubits. So this is the interpretation of the stature and two statures, and the cubit and two cubits.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, who said: When you have prayed Zuhr, the time of Asr has entered, except that there is an optional prayer (subha) before it — that is up to you. If you wish, you may prolong it, and if you wish, you may shorten it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I am with the Imam, and I finish the recitation before he finishes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Retain one verse, glorify Allah, and praise Him. So when he finishes, recite the verse and bow.'

From him, from Ahmad, from Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'aba, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the prayer behind the adversaries, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are not in my presence except at the status of the walls.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from the one who asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I pray behind the one whom I do not follow with (i.e., a Non-Shia), so when I finish my recitation and he has not finished, he (peace be upon him) said: 'So glorify (with Tasbih) until he finishes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you pray behind an Imam whom you do not follow, recite behind him, whether you hear his recitation or do not hear it.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Your mawali have differed, so can I pray behind them all?' He said, 'Do not pray except behind the one whom you trust in his religion.' Then he said, 'And I have mawali.' I said, 'Companions?' He said, interrupting before I finished mentioning them, 'Did Ali ibn Hadeed instruct you with this, or is this from what you have been instructed by Ali ibn Hadeed?' I said, 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Humran ibn Ayn, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! We pray with these people on Friday, and they pray at the time (different to ours). So what should we do?' He said: 'Pray with them.' So Humran went out to Zurara and said to him: 'We have been ordered to pray with them in their prayer.' Zurara said: 'This cannot be except with explanation (ta'wil).' Humran said to him: 'Rise until you hear from him.' He said: 'So we entered upon him, and Zurara said to him: May I be sacrificed for you! Humran claims that you ordered us to pray with them, but I denied that.' He said to us: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to pray two rak'at with them. So when they finished, he would stand and add two rak'at to them.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Five cannot lead the people (in prayer) in any state: the leper, the one with vitiligo, the insane, the son of adultery, and the Bedouin.

And by this chain With regards to two men differing, so one of them says, 'I was your Imam', and the other one says, 'I was your Imam', so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Both of their Salāt are complete'. So I said, 'Supposing each one of them says, 'I was following you'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Both their Salāt are spoilt, and let them both resume'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the ruling on prayer behind a slave?' He said, 'There is no problem with it if he is a jurist (faqih), and there is not anyone more learned than him there.' I said, 'Can I pray behind the blind man?' He said, 'Yes, if there is someone to guide him (to face the Qiblah), and he is the best of them.' He said, 'And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: None of you should pray behind the leper, the one with vitiligo, the insane, the physically restricted, the son of adultery, and the Bedouin should not lead the Muhajirun (immigrants).

Ali ibn Muhammad, and others, from Sahl ibnarrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group from our companions who gather and prayer time arrives, so some of them say to others, 'Proceed, O so-and-so.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The people should be led in prayer by the one who is most proficient in reciting the Quran. If they are equal in recitation, then the one who migrated earlier. If they are equal in migration, then the eldest in age. If they are equal in age, then let the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah and most understanding of the Religion lead them. And none of you should proceed to lead the man in his house, nor the one in authority in his domain.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ghayath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the boy who has not yet reached puberty leading the people (in prayer) and giving the Adhan.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man leading the woman in prayer in his house, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, she should stand behind him.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Ibn Sinan, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman leading the women, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are all together, she leads them in the optional prayer. As for the obligatory prayer, no; and she should not precede them, but she should stand in the middle of them.'

Ahmad, from Al-Husayn, from Fazalat, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who leads the women (in prayer) when there is no man with them, in the obligatory prayer, he said: Yes, and if there is a boy with him, let him stand beside him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer behind the Imam: Do I recite behind him? He said: As for the prayer in which the recitation is not pronounced aloud, then that has been made for him, so do not recite behind him; and as for the prayer in which the recitation is pronounced aloud, then the command to pronounce it aloud is for those behind him to listen attentively. So if you hear, then listen attentively, and if you do not hear, then recite.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you pray behind an Imam whom you follow, do not recite behind him, whether you hear his recitation or do not hear it, unless it is a prayer in which the recitation is loud and you do not hear it, so recite.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: When you are behind an Imam whom you follow, then be silent and glorify (God) within yourself.

And from him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Qutayba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you are behind an Imam whom you are pleased with, in a prayer wherein the recitation is made loud, and you do not hear his recitation, then you recite for yourself; and if you hear the humming (of the Imam), then do not recite.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara who said: I asked one of the two (peace be upon them) about the Imam being responsible for the prayer of the people. He said: No.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said that Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) would say: 'The one who recites behind an Imam whom he follows, and he dies, he will be resurrected on a religion other than the Fitrah.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who prays the prayer alone, then he finds a congregation, he said: He should pray with them and make it the obligatory prayer.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I pray (individually), then I enter the mosque, and the prayer is established, and I have already prayed.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Pray with them. Allah will choose the one of the two that is more beloved to Him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered the mosque and the prayer had commenced. So while he was standing praying, the Mu'adhdhin gave the call to prayer and announced the establishment of the prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him pray two Rak'at, then let him resume the prayer with the Imam, and let the two Rak'at be voluntary.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Dhuhr prayer arrives, but we are not able to descend (from the upper floor) during the time until they descend, and we descend with them, so we pray. Then they stand and hasten, so we stand and pray Asr, and we show them as if we are bowing (in ruku'). Then they descend for Asr, so they place us in front, and we pray with them.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray with them, may Allah not send blessings upon them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'I attend the mosques with my neighbor and others, so they instruct me to lead the prayer with them. I have already prayed before I went to them, and sometimes the weak and the ignorant pray behind me, following my prayer. I dislike advancing [to lead] when I have prayed in the state of those I have specified to you who follow my prayer. So order me regarding this with your command, to which I will adhere and act upon, God willing.' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Pray with them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever prays with them in the first row is with them in the first row is like the one who prays behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
