Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who was praying, so the Imam came out, and the man had already prayed one rak'ah from an obligatory prayer. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was a just Imam, let him pray another (rak'ah) and finish, and he should make these two voluntary (prayers), and let him enter with the Imam in his prayer, just as he is.' And if he is not a just Imam, let him build upon his prayer, just as it is, and he should pray another rak'ah with him, sitting, for the duration of saying: 'I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). Then let him complete his prayer with him, according to what he is able to, for dissimulation (taqiyyah) is vast, and there is nothing from dissimulation except that its performer is recompensed upon it, God willing.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah Al-Arjani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who prays in his house, then goes to a mosque from their mosques, and prays with them, will emerge with their rewards.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who catches the second rak'ah of the prayer with the Imam, and it is the first for himself. How should he act when the Imam sits? He (peace be upon him) said: He should sit upright and not sit fixedly. So when the third is for the Imam and it is the second for him, let him wait a little when the Imam stands, for the time it takes to perform the Tashahhud, then he should catch up with the Imam. He said: And I asked him about the one who catches the last two rak'ahs of the prayer, how should he deal with the recitation? So he (peace be upon him) said: Recite in them, for they are the first two for you, and do not make the beginning of your prayer its end.

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Mithammi, from Is'haq ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Imam is ahead of me by one rak'ah, so it happens to be one for me and two for him. So, should I perform the Tashahhud every time I sit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, for rather, the Tashahhud is a Blessing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Imam is ahead of you by one rak'ah and you attain the final recitation, you recite in the third of his prayer, and it is the second for you; and if you do not attain with him except one rak'ah, you recite in it and in the one that follows it. And if he is ahead of you by one rak'ah, you sit in the second for you and the third for him, until the rows are equal in standing. He said, and he said: When you find the Imam prostrating, remain in your place until he raises his head; and if he is sitting, you sit; and if he is standing, you stand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you catch the Imam having already bowed, and you say the Takbir and bow before he raises his head, then you have caught the Ruk'ah. But if the Imam raises his head before you bow, then the Ruk'ah has been missed by you.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to the mosque while they are in prayer, and the Imam has already led him by one rak'ah or more. The Imam falls ill, so he takes his hand, and he happens to be the closest of the people to him, so he appoints him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He completes the prayer of the people, then sits until they finish the Tashahhud, and he gestures to them with his hand to the right and left. Thus, his gesture to them with his hand is the Taslim (greeting), and the completion of their prayer, and he completes whatever was missed by him or remains upon him.'

From him, from Al-Fadl and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man entered with a group in their prayer, while he did not intend it to be a prayer. Then their Imam broke his ablution, so he took the hand of that man and brought him forward, so he led them in prayer. Would their prayer be sufficient by his prayer, while he did not intend it to be a prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: It is not befitting for the man that he enters with a group in their prayer while he does not intend it to be a prayer, but it is befitting for him that he intends it to be a prayer. If he had already prayed, then he has another prayer, otherwise he should not enter with them. Their prayer would suffice for the group, even if he did not intend it. Their prayer would suffice for the group, even if he did not intend it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who led a group in prayer, so he prayed one rak'ah with them, then died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should bring forward another man, and they should count the rak'ah, and they should place the deceased behind them, and whoever touches him must perform ghusl.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Maruk ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'What do these people say regarding the man who misses two rak'at with the Imam?' I said: 'They say he should recite Al-Hamd and a Surah in them.' He said: 'This is one who overturns his prayer, making its beginning its end.' I said: 'How should he deal with it?' He said: 'He should recite the Opening of the Book in every rak'ah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'I came to the Imam, and he had preceded me by one rak'ah during the Fajr prayer. So when he offered the Taslim, it occurred to me in my heart that I had completed [the prayer]. So I did not cease to remember Allah until the sun rose. So when it rose, I stood up and remembered that the Imam had preceded me by one rak'ah.' He said, 'If you were in your place, then complete with one rak'ah, and if you had already departed, then upon you is the repetition [of the prayer].'

A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudalat ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed with a group, and he considered it to be the first (Dhuhr), while it was actually Asr. He (peace be upon him) said: 'alayhi) said: 'So let him consider it to be the first (Dhuhr), and he should pray Asr.' And in another Hadith: 'So if he knows that they were in the Asr prayer, and he had not prayed the first (Dhuhr), then he should not enter with them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about an Imam who led a group in prayer, and he remembered that he was not in a state of ablution. So he left, took a man by the hand, brought him forward, and placed him ahead, while the one who was placed ahead did not know what the group had already prayed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray with them. So if he errs, the group should glorify with him and build upon the prayer of the one who was before him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the one who raises his head before the Imam. Should he return and bow if the Imam is delayed in raising his head? He (peace be upon him) said: No.

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) enter the Sacred Masjid during the Asr prayer. When the congregation was bowing (in Ruku'), he bowed alone, then prostrated two prostrations, then stood up and continued until he joined the rows.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib'i from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I said to him, 'Can a man move backwards while he is in the prayer?' He said, 'No'. I said, 'So can he move forward?' He said, 'Yes, whatever he desires to, towards the Qiblah'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes for the prayer but does not find a place in the row. Should he stand alone until he finishes his prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, there is no problem if he stands parallel to the Imam.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If a group prays and between them and the Imam is what cannot be stepped over, then that Imam is not an Imam for them. And any row whose people pray with the Imam's prayer, and between them and the row that precedes them is a measure of what cannot be stepped over, then that is not [valid] for them. So if there is between them a curtain or a wall, then that is not a prayer for them, except for the one who is near the door. He said, and he said: 'These chapels were not in the time of anyone from the people, but rather the tyrants innovated them.' For the one who prays behind it, following in the prayer of the one who is inside it, is not a prayer. He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'It is fitting that the rows be complete and connected, one to the other, with nothing between two rows that cannot be stepped over; the measure of that should be the falling of the body of a person [in prostration].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter the mosque and the Imam is bowing (ruku'), and you think that if you walk to him he will raise his head before you catch up with him, then say Takbir and bow (ruku'), and when he raises his head, prostrate (sajdah) in your place. So if he stands, join the row, and if he sits, sit in your place. So when he stands, then join the row.

Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who catches up with the Imam while he is seated performing Tashahhud, and there is no one behind him except for one man on his right. He said: 'He should not precede the Imam, nor should he be behind the man, but the one who enters with him should sit behind the Imam. So when the Imam offers Salam, the man should stand and complete the Salat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, raising it, said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) praying with a group, and he was by a corner in his house, near the wall, and all of them were on his right, and there was no one on his left.

Ahmad ibn Idris and others from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who leads a group in prayer while they are in a place lower than his place where he is praying. He said: If the Imam is on something resembling a platform, or on a place higher than their place, their prayer is not valid; and if he is higher than them by the measure of a finger, or more, or less, when the elevation is by the belly of a wadi (ravine). So if the land is flat, or if there is an elevation in a part of it, so the Imam stands in the elevated place and those behind him stand lower than him, and the ground is flat, except that they are in a sloping place, he said: There is no problem. He said, and he was asked: If the Imam stands lower than the place of those who pray behind him? He said: There is no problem. And he said: If a man is above a house or other than that, whether it is a shop or something else, and the Imam is praying on the ground lower than him, it is permissible for the man to pray behind him and follow his prayer, even if he is higher than him by a great amount.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad said: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) mentioned that he ordered the one who asked him about a man who prayed beside a man, so he stood on his left, and he did not know. Then he realized while he was in his prayer how he should act. He said: 'He should move him to his right.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the man who prays in a single shirt, or in a long gown (qaba'), or in a quilted gown, and there is no loin-cloth (izar) upon him. He said: If he has a woven shirt, or a gown that is not wide/open at the bottom, then there is no problem with it; and the single cloth worn as a waist-wrap, and trousers, all of that there is no problem with it. And he said: When he wears trousers, let him place something on his shoulder, and even if it be a rope.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) praying in a single loincloth that was not wide, which he had tied around his neck. So I said to him, 'What is your view regarding a man who prays in a single shirt?' He said, 'If it is thick, there is no problem with it.' And the woman prays in the outer garment (dir' ) and the head-covering (miqna'ah) if the outer garment is thick, meaning if it is covering. I said, 'May Allah have mercy on you, does the slave girl cover her head when she prays?' He said, 'There is no head-covering required for the slave girl.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who leads a group in prayer wearing only a shirt, without a cloak upon him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting unless there is upon him a cloak or a turban, with which he covers himself.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Beware of Al-Tihaf Al-Samma'. I said, 'And what is Al-Tihaf Al-Samma?' He said: 'To insert the garment from beneath your arm and place it on one shoulder.'
Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who prays in trousers, having nothing else with him, he said: He should place the waistband upon his shoulder.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel who said: Murazim asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) — and I was present with him — about the man who is present (i.e., not traveling) praying in an izar (loincloth/garment) while wearing it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should place a handkerchief or a turban on his neck, wearing it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting that you wear a loin cloth loosely above the shirt while you are praying, nor wear the trouser on top of the shirt when you are praying, for it is from the adornments of the pre-Islamic period.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if one of you were to pray in the one cloth and his loin cloth is loose. The Religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is faultless.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who prays and inserts his hands beneath his garment. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is another garment upon him, either a loin cloth or trousers, then there is no problem; and if there is not, then it is not permissible for him; and if he inserts one hand and does not insert the other, then there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who wraps himself in one garment during prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not wrap himself in one garment. But as for him girding himself, if he covers his shoulders, then there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not correct for the Muslim woman to wear from the scarves and the gowns what does not cover anything.

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'at, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who is in a wilderness of the earth, having only one garment on, and he becomes junub (sexually impure) in it, and there is no water with him. How should he deal with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform tayammum and pray naked, seated, indicating with gestures.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man came out of a ship naked, or his clothes were stripped from him, and he found nothing to pray in.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray by gestures. If it was a woman, she places her hand over her private part, and if it was a man, he places his hand over his private part. Then they sit and gesture with their heads, neither prostrating nor bowing, lest what is behind them be exposed. Their prayer is gesturing with their heads.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if they were in water or a deep sea, they do not prostrate upon it, and the direction (facing the Qiblah) is lifted from them. They gesture in that with gestures; their raising (of heads) is considered facing the Qiblah, and their lowering (is considered prostration).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'The time for al-Maghrib is when the redness disappears from the east.' 'And do you know how that is?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Because the east overlooks upon the west like this,' and he raised his right hand above his left, 'So when it disappears from over here, the redness goes away from over there.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Buraid ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the redness disappears from this side — meaning from the east — then the sun has set from the east of the earth and its west.

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Verily God created a veil of darkness from what adjoins the east, and He appointed an angel over it. So when the sun sets, that angel scoops a handful with his hand, then faces the west with it following the twilight and releases it little by little from his hands, and continues until he reaches the west at the disappearance of the twilight, whereupon he releases the darkness. Then he returns to the east. When the dawn rises, he spreads his two wings and drives the darkness from the east to the west until the west is completed with it at the rising of the sun.

The time of the setting of the disc (sun) and the obligation of breaking the fast (iftar) is that you stand parallel to the Qibla and look for the redness which rises from the east. So when it has passed the top of the head toward the western direction, then the iftar has become obligatory and the disc (sun) has set.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The time for Maghrib is when the disc (of the sun) disappears. So if you see it after that, and you have already prayed, then repeat the salat, and your fast continues, and refrain from the food if you had taken something from it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifa who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Umar ibn Hanzala came to us from you with the (prayer) timings. He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Then he would not have lied against us.' I said: He said the time for Maghrib is when the disc (of the sun) disappears, except that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to, when the journey was pressing upon him, delay the Maghrib and combine it with the Isha. So he (the Imam) said: 'He spoke the truth.' And he said: 'The time for Isha is when the twilight disappears until a third of the night, and the time for Fajr is when it (the dawn) appears until it brightens.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'The time for Al-Maghrib is when the sun sets and its disc disappears.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zayd al-Shahham who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time of al-Maghrib. So he said: 'Jibrail (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) with two times for every salat, except for al-Maghrib salat — for its time is one, and its time is when it becomes obligatory.'

And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, for every salat there are two times, except for Maghrib — for its time is one, and its time is its obligation, and the time of its expiry is the falling of the twilight redness. And it is also narrated that for it there are two times, the last of its time being the falling of the twilight redness. And this does not contradict the first hadith [stating] that it has one time, because the twilight redness (shafaq) is the redness (humra), and between the setting of the sun and the disappearance of the twilight redness there is only a small thing — and that is that the sign of the sun's setting is when the redness reaches the direction of qibla, and between the redness reaching the qibla and its disappearance there is only the measure of time in which a person can pray Maghrib and its nawafil when he prays them with deliberateness and tranquillity. And I have observed this more than once, and that is why the time of Maghrib is narrow.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, who said: 'Ali ibn Asbaat asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while we were listening: 'Is the twilight the redness or the whiteness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The redness. If it were the whiteness, it would be until the third of the night.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Imran ibn Ali al-Halbi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When does the 'Atamah (Isha prayer) become obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When the twilight disappears.' And the twilight is the redness. So Ubaydullah said, 'May Allah keep you well! After the disappearance of the redness, a strong light remains, crossing [the sky].' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, the twilight is only the redness, and the light is not from the twilight.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the sun sets, the time for the two prayers enters, except that this one is before this one.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa from Aban from Abu Baseer from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Had it not been that I would impose hardship upon my community, I would have delayed the Isha prayer until a third of the night.' And it is also reported (that he said): 'Until half the night.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The time for the Maghrib prayer during travel is until a quarter of the night.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, who said: I wrote to him: 'A man is in a house, and its walls prevent him from looking at the redness of the sunset (Al-Maghrib) and recognizing the disappearance of the twilight, and the time for the last prayer of Al-Isha. When should he pray it, and how should he deal with it?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'He should pray it when it is upon this description, at the abundance of the stars; and Al-Maghrib is at their clashing, and the whiteness of the disappearance of the sun [is] the abundance of the stars until their clarity.'

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, who said: I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Our companions mention that when the sun declines, the time for Dhuhr and Asr has entered, and when it sets, the time for Maghrib and the last Isha has entered, with this being earlier than that during travel and residence, and that the time for Maghrib is until a quarter of the night.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The timing is like that, except that the time for Maghrib is narrow, and its end is the departure of the redness and its turning to whiteness in the western horizon.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: Zurara asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the fur of foxes, weasels, squirrels, and others of the hairy animals. So he brought out a book, claiming it was a dictation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), that the prayer in the fur of anything whose eating is prohibited is invalid; so the prayer in its fur, hair, skin, urine, dung, and milk, and everything from it is invalid, that prayer is not accepted until you pray in something else from what Allah has permitted its consumption. Then he said: O Zurara, this is from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so memorize that, O Zurara. If it is from what its flesh is eaten, then the prayer in its fur, urine, hair, dung, milk, and everything from it is permissible, when you know that it is pure, having been purified by slaughter. If it is other than that, from what you have been forbidden to eat and its eating is prohibited upon you, then the prayer in everything from it is invalid, whether it was purified by slaughter or not purified.

And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah and Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about wearing the fur and praying in it, so he said: 'Do not pray in it unless it is from what was purified (slaughtered).' He said, I asked: 'Is the purified not that which is purified by the iron?' So he said: 'Yes, if it is from that whose flesh is edible.' I said: 'And what is edible besides sheep?' He said: 'There is no problem with the squirrel, for it is an animal that does not eat flesh, and it is not of that which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited; for he prohibited everything with a fang and a claw.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Salat is disliked in the furs (leather garments) except for what is made in the land of Al-Hijaz, or from that which is known to have been purified (slaughtered).

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I enter the market of the Muslims, meaning this people who claim Islam, and I buy the furs from them for trade. So I say to its owner: 'Is it not purified (slaughtered)?' He says: 'Yes.' So is it correct for me to sell it upon the condition that it is purified?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. But there is no problem if you sell it and say: 'The one from whom I bought it stipulated to me that it is purified.'' I said: 'And what spoils that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The permitting by the people of Iraq of the dead (animal), and they claim that tanning the skin of the dead is its slaughter. Then they are not pleased to lie about that except against the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is benefit derived from anything of the dead animal (maytah)?' He said: 'No.' I said, 'It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a dead sheep and said: 'What was upon the owners of this sheep? If they did not benefit from its flesh, they could have benefited from its skin?' He said: 'That sheep belonged to Sawda bint Zama'a, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and it was a skinny sheep from which no benefit was derived from its flesh, so they left it until it died. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What was upon its owners? If they did not benefit from its flesh, they could have benefited from its skin' — if it had been slaughtered (thakka).

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Ash'ari, who said: One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding the fur that is bought from the market?' He said: 'If it is guaranteed (i.e., from a slaughtered animal), there is no problem.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from a man who asked Al-Maazy (peace be upon him) about the prayer in foxes. He forbade from the prayer in it and in the garment that is underneath it. So I did not know which of the two garments was the one that sticks to the fur or the one that sticks to the skin. So he (peace be upon him) signed by his handwriting: 'The one that sticks to the skin'. He said, 'And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) mentioned that he was asked about this matter, so he said: 'Do not pray in the garment that is above it, nor in the one that is underneath it'.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) asking him, 'Is one permitted to pray in a hat of pure silk, or a hat of brocade?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Prayer is not permissible in pure silk.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman al-Daylami, from Fureyt, from Ibn Abi Yafour, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the otter hunters came to him and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding the Salat in the otter (fur)?' So he said, 'There is no problem with the Salat in it.' The man said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, it is dead, and it is my profession, and I understand it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'I know it better than you.' The man said, 'It is my profession, and there is none who knows it better than I.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) smiled, then said to him, 'Do you say that it is an animal that comes out of the water, or is caught from the water, and when the water is lost [or it is removed from water], it dies?' The man said, 'You speak the truth, may I be sacrificed for you, this is how it is.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'So you say that it is an animal that walks on four, and it is not like the fish, so its slaughter is its exit from the water?' The man said, 'Yes, by Allah, this is what I say.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, has permitted it and made its slaughter its death, just as He has permitted the fish and made their slaughter their death.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ahwas He said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about praying in the skins of predatory animals, so he said: Do not pray in them. He said: And I asked him, Can a man pray in a silk garment? So he said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Numayri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who is traveling and has a knife in his sock, which he cannot do without, or tied in his trousers, and a key he fears losing, or a belt in his waist containing iron. He said: There is no problem with the knife and the belt for the traveler during a time of necessity, and similarly the key he fears losing or is in forgetfulness; and there is no problem with the sword, and similarly the weapon in war; but in other cases, prayer is not permissible in anything of iron, for it is unclean and transformed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdill, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man wears a single garment up to his chest, he may pray in it. He said: And I read in a letter of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), asking him about the fennec fox [skin], whether one may pray in it, so he wrote: There is no problem with it. And I wrote asking him about the skins of rabbits, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: It is disliked. And I wrote asking him about a garment lined with silk, whether one may pray in it, so he wrote: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from the one who mentioned it, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the beaver and the squirrel, and the fox. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no goodness in all of that except for the squirrel, for it is an animal that does not eat meat'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he disliked that one should pray while wearing a garment in which are images.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can one pray in the tailyasan (shawl) made by the Magians?' He said, 'Is it not washed with water?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'The new cloth made by the weaver, can I pray in it?' He said, 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays in the woman's garment and in her lower garment (izar), and makes a turban with her headscarf (khumar). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if she is trustworthy (ma'munah).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the black dirhams in which there are images (embossed figures), can a man pray while they are with him? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if they are hidden (out of sight).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The prayer is disliked in the dyed garment that is deeply saturated and dark.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not pray in what is gauzy or sieves, meaning the sparkling [garment]. And it is reported: 'Do not pray in a black cloth.' But as for the socks, or a cloak, or the turban, so there is no problem.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Abu Yazeed Al-Qasmi (and Qasam is a tribe from Yemen in Al-Basra), from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the skins of Al-Darish from which shoes are made, so he (peace be upon him) said: Do not pray in them, for they are tanned with the excretion of dogs.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding pure sable (fur), that there is no problem with it. But as for that in which the fur of rabbits is mixed, or other than that which resembles this, then do not pray in it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That he disliked wearing a shirt hemmed with brocade, and he disliked wearing silk, and wearing embroidered clothes, and he disliked the red saddlecloth, for it is the saddlecloth of Iblis.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Halabi who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The soft leather shoes are with us in the marketplace, we buy them. So what do you think regarding the prayer in them?' He said, 'Pray in them until it is said to you that they are exactly from the dead (animal) [i.e., their leather is confirmed to be from a dead animal, making them impure].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Prayer is disliked except in three [items of clothing]: the socks, the turban, and the cloak.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can I pray in the black cap?' He said, 'Do not pray in it, for it is the apparel of the people of the Fire.'

Ali, from Sahl, from one of his companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I walk through the market and buy a khuff (leather sock), not knowing whether it is pure or not.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Pray in it.' I said, 'And what about the na'l (leather shoe)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Similar to that.' I said, 'I am constrained from this.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do you prefer to turn away from what Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to do?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about praying in a Jurmuq (gaiter/large slipper), and I brought a Jurmuq to him and sent it to him, so he said: 'One may pray in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who prays and a bird is in his sleeve. He said: If he fears it flying away, there is no problem. He said: And I asked him about the anklets, is it permissible for women and children to wear them? He said: If they are silent, there is no problem, and if they have a sound, then no.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Safwan, from Al-Ays ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed in the garment of another man for days, then the owner of the garment informed him that he does not pray in it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not repeat anything from his prayer.'

And by this chain, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays and in his garment is excrement from a human, or a cat, or a dog. Should he repeat his prayer? So he (peace be upon him) said: If he did not know, then he does not repeat.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them) said: The prayer is not repeated due to blood that is not visible, except for the blood of menstruation, for its little or much in the garment, whether you see it or do not see it, is the same.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from some who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If your garment is touched by wine or an intoxicating Nabeez, then wash it if you know its place. But if you do not know its place, then wash it entirely; and if you prayed in it, then repeat your prayer.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Khayran al-Khadim who said: I wrote to the Man (peace be upon him) asking him about the garment that is hit by wine and the flesh of the pig, 'Can one pray in it or not?' For our companions have differed regarding it, so some of them said, 'Pray in it, for Allah has only prohibited its drinking,' and some of them said, 'Do not pray in it.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Do not pray in it, for it is filth.' He said, 'And I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who lends his garment to the one whom he knows eats the catfish or drinks wine, and he returns it. Can he pray in it before washing it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He cannot pray in it until he washes it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who prayed two rak'at in a garment in which there was major ritual impurity, then he came to know of it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is that he re-commences the prayer.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man who prayed and in his garment was major ritual impurity or blood, until he finished his prayer, then he came to know.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His prayer has passed, and there is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who sees blood in the clothes of his brother while he is praying. He said: He should not notify him until he finishes (the prayer).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man whose garment was affected by major ritual impurity (janabah) or blood. He (peace be upon him) said: If he knew that his garment had been affected by major ritual impurity before he prayed, then he prayed in it without washing it, he must repeat what he prayed. And if he did not know of it, there is no need for him to repeat. And if he thought something had affected it, so he looked but saw nothing, it suffices him if he sprinkles it with water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, who said: I sent a question to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, saying: 'Ask him about a man who urinates and a drop of his urine hits his thigh, so he prays and then remembers afterwards that he had not washed it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash it and repeat his prayer.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays and in his garment is excrement from a human, or a cat, or a dog. Should he repeat his prayer? He said: If he did not know, then he does not repeat.
Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Wash your garment from the urine of everything whose flesh is not eaten.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who vomits in his clothes. Is it permissible for him to pray in it without washing it? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Abu Jameel al-Basri, who said: I was with Yunus in Baghdad, and I was walking with him in the market. So the owner of the Fuqa'a (a fermented drink) opened his drink, and it spattered and hit the clothes of Yunus. So I saw him as gloomy due to that until the sun started its decline. So I said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad! Will you not pray?' So he said, 'I do not intend to pray until I return to the house and wash this wine from my clothes'. So I said to him, 'Is this your opinion or it is something you are reporting?' So he said, 'Hisham Bin Al-Hakam informed me that he asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fermented drink, so he said: 'Do not drink it, for it is a kind of wine. So when it hits your clothes, so wash it'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti from Qasim al-Sayqal who said: I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'I manufacture the sheaths for the swords from the skins of dead donkeys, and my clothes get hit. So can I pray in these?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'Take (other) clothes for your prayer'. So I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the 2nd, 'I had written to your father (peace be upon him) with such and such. So that was difficult upon me, so I started making these from the skins of wild donkeys properly slaughtered'. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'Every righteous work is with patience. May Allah have Mercy on you. So it was such that what you are making is of wild (donkeys), slaughtered, so there is no problem'.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can a man pray while he is veiled (covering his head and body with a single garment)?' He said, 'As for praying on the ground, no; and as for praying on the animal (mount), there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Bakr Al-Hazramy, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays and upon him is his dye. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not pray while it is upon him, but he should remove it when he intends to pray.' I said, 'If his henna and his cloth are clean?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He cannot pray while it is upon him; and the woman as well, she cannot pray and upon her is her dye.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abd al-Malik al-Qummi entered upon him and said, 'May Allah improve your state; do I prostrate while my hand is inside my garment?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you wish.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, I do not fear for you because of this and things similar to it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who prays while gesturing upon his animal, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should uncover the place of prostration.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Musadif, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who prayed an obligatory prayer while his hair was curled, he said: He should repeat his prayer.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), who said: We order our children to perform Salat when they are five years old, so you should order your children to perform Salat when they are seven years old. And we order our children to fast when they are seven years old, with whatever they can bear from fasting the day, whether it is up to half the day, or more than that, or less. So when thirst and hunger overcome them, they break their fast, until they become accustomed to fasting and are able to endure it. So order your children to fast when they are nine years old, for whatever they can bear of fasting the day. So when thirst overcomes them, they break their fast.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rabi'i ibn Abdullah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to order the children to combine between Maghrib and 'Isha, and he would say: 'It is better than them sleeping through it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the children when they form rows in the obligatory prayer. He said: 'Do not delay them from the obligatory prayer, and separate them (from one another).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan ibn Sadeer, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Do you pray the optional prayers while you are seated?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'I do not pray them except while seated, since I gained this much weight and reached this age.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'We narrate and say: The one who prays while he is seated without an illness, his two rak'at of prayer would be (counted as) one rak'at, and two prostrations would be (counted as) one prostration.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not like this. It is complete for you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man and the woman whose eyesight fails, so the doctors come to them and say, 'We will treat you for a month or forty nights, lying down; in that state, you should pray.' So he permitted them in that regard and said, 'But whoever is driven to necessity, not desiring excess nor transgressing the limit, no sin shall be upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the sick person when he is unable to stand and prostrate. He said: 'He can gesture with his head, and for him to place his forehead on the ground is more beloved to me.'
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, raising it, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar (peace be upon him), who said: The sick person indicates with gestures.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one with incontinence, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He continues upon his prayer.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked, 'A man prays while he is seated, and recites the Chapter. When he intends to conclude it, he stands and performs Ruku' at the end of it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'His prayer is the prayer of the standing one.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Muawiya ibn Maysara, that Sinan asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who extends one of his legs in front of him in the prayer while he is seated. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' And I do not see except that he (peace be upon him) said (this) regarding the disabled and the sick. And in another Hadith, 'He prays in a squared position and with both legs extended. All of that is permissible (wide/leeway).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah, who said: He was asked about the prisoner whom the polytheists capture, so the prayer time arrives, but the one who imprisoned him prevents him from it. He said: 'He indicates with gestures.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who remember Allah standing and sitting and lying on their sides,' he said: 'The healthy pray standing, 'and sitting' refers to the sick praying seated, and 'lying on their sides' refers to those who are weaker than the sick who pray seated.'

Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The sick person prays sitting. If he is unable, he prays lying down. He says Takbir, then recites. When he intends to bow (Ruku'), he closes his eyes, then glorifies (says SubhanAllah), then opens his eyes, so that opening his eyes is raising his head from Ruku'. When he intends to prostrate (Sujood), he closes his eyes, then glorifies. When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, so that opening his eyes is raising his head from prostration. Then he performs Tashahhud and finishes.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the sick person: Is it permissible for him to stand upon his bed and prostrate upon the ground? He said: If the bed is thick, to the measure of a brick or less, it is correct for him to stand upon it and prostrate upon the ground; and if it is more than that, then no.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazim who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the sick person who is unable to perform the prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever Allah has overcome [with weakness or incapacity], Allah is more worthy of excusing [for it].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Ma'mar ibn Umar, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the sick person: does he make up the prayer if he was unconscious? He (peace be upon him) said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibrahim al-Kazzaz, Abu Ayub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who was unconscious for days and did not pray, then he regained consciousness. Does he pray what he missed? He said: There is nothing upon him.

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the sick person who becomes unconscious and then regains consciousness. How does he make up his prayer? He said: He makes up the prayer for the time at which he regained consciousness.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to him, 'A man became ill and left the optional prayers.' He said, 'O Muhammad, it is not an obligation. If he fulfills it, it is better for him to do so; and if he does not do it, there is nothing upon him.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Al-Ays ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man upon whom the prayers of the year had accumulated due to illness. He (peace be upon him) said: He does not need to make them up.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying regarding the one who is unconscious (maghmā 'alayhi): 'That which Allah has caused to overcome him, then Allah is more worthy of excusing him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sun has not risen upon a day superior to the day of Friday.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs ibn Al-Bakhtari, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When it is the day of Friday, the Proximate Angels descend with them, having papers of silver and pens of gold. So they sit at the doors of the Masjid upon chairs of light, and they record the people according to their ranks, the first and the second, until the Imam comes out. So when the Imam comes out, they fold their parchments. And they do not descend regarding anything from the days except on the day of Friday, meaning the Proximate Angels.

Ahmad narrated from Al-Husayn, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) preferred that when he returned (from a journey) and when he set out (on a journey) in winter, it should be during the night of Friday. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah chose a thing from every thing, so He chose from the days the day of Friday.'

And from him, from Al-Nadhr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The hour during which supplication is answered on Friday is the time between the Imam's completion of the sermon until the people are evenly arranged in the rows, and another hour is from the end of the day until the setting of the sun.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Friday is the master of the days. Allah multiplies the good deeds in it, erases the bad deeds in it, raises the ranks in it, answers the supplications in it, removes the hardships in it, and fulfills the great needs in it. And it is the day of increase; in it are the emancipated and the freed from the Fire.' If anyone from the people supplicates in it, having recognized its right and its sanctity, it becomes a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to make him from His emancipated and freed ones from the Fire. So if he dies on its day and its night, he dies a martyr and is resurrected secure. And if anyone takes lightly its sanctity and wastes its right, it becomes a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to cause him to enter the Fire of Hell, unless he repents.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Friday has a right and a sanctity, so beware of wasting or being deficient in anything from the worship of Allah and drawing near to Him through righteous deeds and abandoning all prohibitions, for Allah multiplies the good deeds therein, erases the bad deeds therein, and raises the ranks therein. He said, and he mentioned that its day is like its night. So if you are able to spend it in prayer and supplication, then do so, for your Lord descends on the first part of the night of Friday to the lowest heaven, and He multiplies the good deeds therein and erases the bad deeds therein, and indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, Generous.

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Yaf'ur, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him, 'How was Friday named?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathered His creation in it for the Wilayah of Muhammad and his successor regarding the Covenant. Thus, He named it the day of Friday (Jumu'ah) due to the gathering (Jama'ah) of His creation in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the day of Friday and its night, so he said: 'Its night is luminous and its day is a day of brilliance, and there is no day upon the earth on which the sun sets that is more pardoned from the Fire than it. The one who dies on the day of Friday, recognizing the right of the People of this Household, Allah has written for him freedom from the Fire and freedom from the Punishment; and the one who dies on the night of Friday is liberated from the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah preferred Friday over other days, and indeed the Gardens are adorned and decorated on Friday for those who attend it, and you will race towards Paradise according to your racing towards Friday, and indeed the gates of the sky are opened for the ascension of the deeds of the servants.'

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the meaning of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then hasten to the Remembrance of Allah'?' He said: 'Work (do good deeds) and hasten, for it is a busy day for the Muslims, and the reward of the deeds of the Muslims during it is proportional to the busyness imposed upon them, and the good deeds and the sins are multiplied during it.' He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, it has reached me that the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to prepare for Friday on the day of Thursday, because it is a busy day for the Muslims.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The sun does not rise on a day superior to the day of Friday, and the speech of the birds in it, when some meet others, is: 'Peace, peace! A good day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The hour during the day of Friday in which a believer supplicates, his supplication is answered.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when the Imam comes out.' I said: 'Indeed, the Imam hastens and delays.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sun declines.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Uzafir from Umar ibn Yazeed who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Umar! When it is the night of Friday, angels descend from the sky in the number of particles, in their hands are pens of gold and sheets of silver. They do not write up to the night of Saturday except for the Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), so increase in it.' And he said: 'O Umar! Indeed, it is from the Sunnah that you send Blessings upon Muhammad and upon the People of his Household on every Friday a thousand times, and on the other days one hundred times.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his brother Isḥāq ibn Ibrahim, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'It has reached me that the day of Friday is the shortest of the days.' He said, 'It is so.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, how is that?' He said, 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gathers the souls of the polytheists beneath the eye of the sun. So when the sun stagnates, Allah punishes the souls of the polytheists by the stagnation of the sun for an hour. So when it is the day of Friday, the sun does not stagnate; Allah raises the punishment from them due to the merit of the day of Friday, so the stagnation does not occur for the sun.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Let one of you adorn himself on the day of Friday by washing, applying perfume, combing his beard, and wearing the cleanest of his clothes. Let him prepare for Friday, and let tranquility and dignity be upon him during that day. Let him perform good worship of his Lord, and let him do good as much as he is able, for Allah looks upon the people of the earth to multiply the good deeds.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Umar Al-Jurjany, from Muhammad ibn Al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever trims his moustache and clips his nails on the day of Friday, then says: "In the Name of Allah, upon the Sunnah of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad," Allah will write for him, for every hair and every clipping, the freeing of a neck, and he will not become sick with a sickness that afflicts him except the sickness of death.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The ritual bath (ghusl) on Friday is obligatory for men and women when at home (in residence), and for men when travelling.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not neglect the ghusl on the day of Friday, for it is a Sunnah, and smell the perfume, and wear the best of your clothes, and let your completion of the ghusl be before the midday sun passes (Zawal). So when it passes, stand up, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The ghusl is obligatory on the day of Friday.'

Ali, from his brother, from Ismail ibn Abdul Khaliq, from Muhammad ibn Talha, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Trimming the moustache and the nails, and washing the head with the hibiscus on the day of Friday negates poverty and increases livelihood.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who trims his moustache, clips his nails, and washes his head with the hibiscus on the day of Friday is like the one who frees a slave.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Trimming the moustache and the nails from Friday to Friday is a safety from leprosy.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Al-Fudayl, who said: We said to him (peace be upon him), 'Is it sufficient if I perform the ritual bath after dawn for Friday?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Washing the head with the hibiscus (khittim) every Friday is a safety from leprosy and insanity.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made obligatory during every seven days thirty-five prayers, from which is a prayer obligatory upon every Muslim to attend it, except for five: the sick, the slave, the traveler, the woman, and the child.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Friday prayer is obligatory upon the one who is within two Farsakhs of it.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Friday [prayer], so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is obligatory upon the one who is within two farsakhs of it. So when one exceeds that distance, there is nothing upon him [obligatory].'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was saying: The sermon, the Friday prayer, and the two-rak'ah prayer do not take place upon fewer than five people: the Imam and four.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Aamir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fazalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The least of what suffices for the Friday prayer is seven, or five being the least.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah obligated upon the people, from Friday to Friday, thirty-five prayers; from these is one prayer that Allah obligated to be performed in congregation, and it is the Friday prayer, and He exempted it from nine: the young child, the old man, the insane, the traveler, the slave, the woman, the sick, the blind, and the one who is more than two farsakhs away.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Jamil, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There should be three miles between the two congregations, meaning there is no Friday prayer except in what is between them; and the Friday prayer is not valid except with a sermon. He said: So when there are three miles between the two congregations in the Friday prayer, there is no harm if these [one group] hold a Friday prayer and those [the other group] hold a Friday prayer.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rabi' and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The time for the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Friday is when the sun declines.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sun declines on the day of Friday, so begin with the Obligatory (prayers).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Sufyan ibn Al-Simt, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the time for the Asr prayer on the day of Friday, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is in a time similar to the Dhuhr prayer on other than the day of Friday.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Salat on the day of Friday, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came down with it, with a short time-span. When the sun declines, pray it.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'When the sun declines, I should pray two Rak'at, then pray it?'' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for myself, when the sun declines, I do not begin with anything before the Obligatory (Salat).' Al-Qasim (the narrator) said, 'And Ibn Bukayr used to pray two Rak'at and he was doubting regarding the midday (point). So when he was convinced of the midday, he began with the Obligatory (Salat) during the day of Friday.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: Abu al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn wrote to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) via me: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Your followers are differing regarding the Fajr prayer. Among them is one who prays when the first dawn rises elongated vertically in the sky, and among them is one who prays when it spreads horizontally at the bottom of the horizon and becomes clear. I do not know the better of the two times to pray in it. So if you see fit to teach me the better of the two times and define it for me, and how I should act when the moon is present and the dawn cannot be distinguished until it turns red and morning comes, and how I should act with clouds, and what the limit of that is during journey and at home — I will do so, God willing.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting, and I read it: 'The dawn — may God have mercy on you — is the white horizontal line. It is not the vertical whiteness. So do not pray, whether on a journey or at home, until you distinguish it clearly.' For God, Blessed and Exalted, has not left His creation in doubt about this. He said: "Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread of the dawn." [2:187] The white thread is the horizontal one, by which eating and drinking become forbidden during the fast, and similarly it is that by which prayer becomes obligatory.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Inform me of the most excellent of the timings for the Fajr salat. So he said: At the emergence of dawn. Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'and the morning recitation; surely the recitation at dawn was always witnessed' — meaning the Fajr salat. The angels of the night witness it and the angels of the day. So when the servant prays the morning prayer at the emergence of dawn, it is affirmed for him twice — recorded by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The morning (Fajr) is that which, when you see it spreading horizontally, it is as if it is the white light of Sura.
Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The time for al-Fajr is from when it begins until it brightens.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The time of al-Fajr (dawn prayer) is when the dawn breaks until the morning brightens the sky, and it is not befitting to delay that deliberately; but it is a time (of leeway) for the one who is occupied, or forgets, or sleeps.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) who said: When the night reaches its midpoint, a whiteness appears in the middle of the sky resembling a pillar of iron, the world being illuminated by it. It lasts for a while, then disappears and darkness returns. Then when a third of the night remains, a whiteness appears from the eastern direction, illuminating the world. It lasts for a while, then disappears — and that is the time for the night salat. Then it darkens before dawn, then the true dawn rises from the east. He said: 'And whoever wishes to pray the night salat at midnight, that is permissible for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is befitting for the Imam who addresses the people on Friday that he wears a turban in winter and summer, and wears a Yemeni or Adeni cloak, and delivers the sermon while standing, praising Allah and lauding Him, then advising with the fear of Allah, and reciting a short chapter from the Quran, then he sits. Then he stands, praises Allah and lauds Him, sends blessings upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and upon the Imams of the Muslims, and seeks forgiveness for the believing men and women. When he finishes this, the Mu'adhdhin calls the prayer, and he prays two Rak'at with the people, reciting in the first Surah al-Jumu'ah and in the second Surah al-Munafiqun.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday, it is not befitting for anyone to speak until the Imam finishes his sermon; and when the Imam finishes the two sermons, one may speak in the interval between that and the establishment of the prayer. Whether one hears the recitation or does not hear, it suffices.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the sermon of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), was it before the prayer or after it? So he said: Before the prayer. He delivers the sermon, then he prays.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer on the day of Friday, so he said: 'As for [praying] with the Imam, it is two rak'at, and as for the one who prays alone, it is four rak'at, in the status of Dhuhr — meaning when there is an Imam delivering the sermon. As for when there is no Imam delivering the sermon, it is four rak'at, even if they pray in congregation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The third Adhan on the day of Friday is an innovation.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Take your adornment at every Masjid.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'During the two Eids and Friday.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every preacher is a Qiblah, meaning when the Imam addresses the people on the day of Friday, it is befitting for the people that they face towards him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is nothing fixed regarding the recitation except for Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Recite in the night of Friday with Al-Jummah and Sabbih Ismaka al-A'la; and in the dawn prayer with Surah Al-Jummah and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad; and in the Friday prayer with Al-Jummah and Al-Munafiqun.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'With what should I recite in the Fajr prayer on the day of Friday?'
