He said: 'Recite in the first [rak'ah] Surah Al-Jumu'ah, and in the second Surah Al-Ikhlas (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad), then perform Qunut until they both become equal [in length/duration].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Jameel, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah honoured the believers with Friday, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established it as glad tidings for them and as a rebuke to the hypocrites. It is not fitting to neglect it, so whoever neglects it deliberately, there is no prayer for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the recitation in the Friday prayer when I pray alone four [rak'at], do I recite aloud? He said: 'Yes.' And he said: 'Recite with Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun on the day of Friday.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from one of our companions, from Sama'at, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Qunut on the day of Friday is in the first Rak'ah after the recitation. You should say in the Qunut: 'There is no god except Allah, the Forbearing, the Benevolent. There is no god except Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. There is no god except Allah, Lord of the seven skies and Lord of the seven earths and whatever is in them and whatever is between them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne. And the Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.' O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad just as You Guided us by him. O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad just as You Honoured us with him. O Allah! Make us from those You Chose for Your Religion and Created him for Your Paradise. O Allah! Do not Let our hearts to deviate after having Guided us, and Bestow Mercy upon us from Yourself. You are the most Benevolent.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the Qunut of the Friday prayer: 'When the Imam prays, he performs Qunut in the first Rak'ah; and if he prays four (Rak'ahs), then (perform Qunut) in the second Rak'ah before the Ruku'.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Aban, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the ruling on the Qunut on the day of Friday?' He said: 'You are my messenger to them regarding this: when you pray Salat in a congregation, it is in the first Rak'at, and when you pray Salat alone, it is in the second Rak'at before the Rukū'.'

Ali ibn Muhammad and others from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: The optional prayer on the day of Friday is six rak'at in the early morning, and six rak'at in the middle of the day, and two rak'at when the sun declines. Then pray the Obligatory prayer and pray six rak'at after it.

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Ali ibn Abdul-Aziz, from Murad ibn Kharajat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, so whenever it is the day of Friday, and the sun is from the east to the west by its measure, during the time of the 'Asr prayer, I pray six rak'at. So when the day swells, I pray six. So when the sun dips or declines, I pray two rak'at, then I pray the Dhuhr prayer, then I pray six after it.'

A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, or from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If you are in doubt regarding the midday (for Dhuhr prayer), so pray two Rak'at. But when you are convinced, so begin with the Obligatory (Salat).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You should say during the last prostration of the optional prayers after Maghrib on the night of Friday: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your Noble Face and Your Great Name that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You forgive my great sin,' seven times.

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Frequent the sending of blessings upon me during the dark night and the brilliant day, the night of Friday and the day of Friday.' He was asked, 'Up to how much is the 'frequent'?' He said: 'Up to one hundred, and whatever exceeds, so it is superior.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn from Ali ibn Abdullah from Yazeed ibn Is'haq from Harun ibn Kharajah from Al-Mufaddal from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: There is nothing with which Allah is worshipped on the day of Friday that is more beloved to me than sending blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said: He (peace be upon him) said: When you pray on the day of Friday, say: O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, the Successors, the Pleased with, with the most superior of Your Blessings, and Bless upon them with the most superior of Your Blessings, and the greetings be upon him and upon them, and the Mercy of Allah and His Blessings. For whoever says it at the end of Al-Asr prayer, Allah will write for him one hundred thousand good deeds, erase from him one hundred thousand sins, fulfill for him one hundred thousand needs through it, and raise for him one hundred thousand levels.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is recommended that you recite at the end of the forenoon on Friday, Surah Al-Rahman in its entirety.' Then you should say, every time you recite 'Which then of the Favours of your Lord will you two deny?', 'There is nothing from Your Favours, Lord, that I deny.'

And by this chain, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recites Al-Kahf during every night of Friday, it would be an expiation for what is between the Friday to the (next) Friday'. He said, 'And it is reported by others as well regarding the one who recites it on the day of Friday after Al-Zohr and Al-Asr – similar (Rewards) to that'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to go to the Masjid early on Friday when the sun was at the height of a spear's shadow. And when it was the month of Ramadan, he would go before that. And he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The Fridays of the month of Ramadan have a merit over the Fridays of the other months just as the month of Ramadan has a merit over the other months.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who caught the Friday prayer and the people were crowded, so he said Takbir with the Imam and bowed (Ruku'), and he was unable to prostrate (Sujood). The Imam stood up while the people were in the second Raka'ah, and this man stood with them. The Imam bowed, and this man was unable to bow in the second Raka'ah due to the crowding, but he was able to prostrate. What should he do? Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: As for the first Raka'ah, it is complete up to the Ruku'. Since he did not prostrate for it until he entered into the second, that was not sufficient for him. When he prostrated in the second Raka'ah, if he intended this prostration to be the first Raka'ah, then the first Raka'ah is complete for him. And when the Imam offers Salam, he should stand and pray one Raka'ah, then prostrate in it, then recite Tashahhud and offer Salam. And if he did not intend that that prostration was for the first Raka'ah, then neither the first nor the second is valid for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, raising it, said: It was said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Some people claim that the waxing (of the head/body) on Friday is disliked.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not where they are going. Which cleanliness is more cleansing than the waxing on Friday?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I prayed behind Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) at midday, and I said, 'By my father and my mother, what is the time for Asr?' He said, 'The time when you kneel your camels.' I said, 'When it is not during a journey?' He said, 'When the shadow is less than one foot, less than two-thirds of a foot, it is the time for Asr.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Misma'a Abu Sayyar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the time for the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Friday during travel. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'At the decline of the sun, and that is its time on the day of Friday, when not traveling.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was so that whenever Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in a journey, or due to a reason of a need, would gather together Al-Zohr and Al Asr (Salāt), and between Al-Maghrib and Al-Isha (Salāt). He (the narrator) said, 'And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with hastening the last Isha (Salāt) during the journey before the disappearing of the twilight (redness)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I and a group of our companions were traveling together, with Muyassar among them, between Mecca and Medina. We set out while we were uncertain about the time of midday (zawal). Some of us said to others, 'Walk with us a little until we are certain of the midday, then we will pray.' So we did, and we had not walked except a little until the caravan of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) appeared to us. I said, 'The caravan has arrived.' I saw Muhammad ibn Ismail and said to him, 'Have you prayed?' He said to me, 'My grandfather instructed us, so we prayed Dhuhr and Asr together, then we set out.' I went to my companions and informed them of that.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The time for Al-Maghrib during the journey is up to a third of the night, and it is also reported as up to half the night.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The shortening [of prayer] is in a Bareyd, and the Bareyd is four Farsakhs.

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the least distance at which the traveler shortens (his prayer)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A Bareyd.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: While we were seated and my father was in the presence of a governor of the Banu Umayya over Medina, my father came and sat down, so he said: 'I was in the presence of this man earlier, and he asked them about the shortening (of prayer). A speaker from them said, 'In three (days)', and a speaker from them said, 'One day and night', and a speaker from them said, 'An early journey (or a short distance).' So he asked me, and I said to him: 'When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) received the revelation of the shortening from Jibraeel (peace be upon him), the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked him, 'In what distance is that?' He said, 'In a Bareyd (post-stage). He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'And what is the Bareyd?' He said, 'What is between the shadow of 'Ayr to the shade of Wueyr.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Then time passed, and the Banu Umayya were seen constructing signs along the road, and they remembered what Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had spoken of, so they measured what is between the shadow of 'Ayr to the shade of Wueyr, then divided it into twelve miles, so it became three thousand and five hundred cubits for each mile. So they placed the signs. Then when the Banu Hashim became victorious, they changed the matter of the Banu Umayya out of zeal, because the hadith is Hashimite, so they placed beside each sign another sign.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the limit of the miles at which shortening (of prayer) becomes obligatory. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) set the limit of the miles from the shade of 'Ayr to the shade of Wueyr, and these two are mountains in Medina. So when the sun rises, the shadow of 'Ayr falls to the shadow of Wueyr, and that is the mile upon which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) placed the ruling of shortening.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a group who went out on a journey. When they reached the place where shortening (salat) became obligatory for them, they shortened. When they had traveled two farsakhs, or three farsakhs, or four, a man lagged behind them, and their journey was not complete/straightforward except with him. So they stayed waiting for his arrival to them, and their journey was not complete except with his arrival. So they stayed upon that for days, not knowing whether they should continue in their journey or return. Is it befitting for them to complete the prayer or to persist in shortening it? He (peace be upon him) said: If they had reached the distance of four farsakhs, let them persist in shortening, whether they stay or return; and if they had traveled less than four farsakhs, let them complete the prayer, whether they stay or return. So when they continue, let them shorten.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When should a man shorten [his prayer] when he intends to travel?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When he loses sight of the houses.' I said, 'The man intends to travel, so he goes out when the sun declines.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When you go out, pray two rak'at.' And al-Husayn ibn Sa'id reported from Safwan and Fadalah, from al-Ala', similar to it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the sun declines and you are in the city, and you intend to travel, then pray complete (Salat). But when you go out after the decline (of the sun), then shorten Al-Asr (Salat).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said: I went out with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) until we reached Al-Shajara. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Nabbal!' I said, 'At your service.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not obligatory upon anyone from the people of this camp to pray four [rak'at] except me and you, and that is because the time for prayer entered before we went out.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who returns from his journey and the time for prayer has entered. He said: 'He should pray two rak'at. And when he goes out on a journey and the time for prayer has entered, let him pray four (rak'at).'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who is traveling, then returns and enters the houses of Kufa. Should he complete the prayer or should he shorten it until he comes to his family? He said: No, he should shorten it until he comes to his family.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed while he was a traveler, so he completed the prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was within the [prescribed] time, let him repeat [the prayer]; and if the time has passed, then no [need to repeat].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to him, 'A man who missed a prayer from the prayers of the journey, and remembered it while in residence.' He said, 'He should make up what he missed as it was missed. If it was a prayer of the journey, he should perform it in residence like it. And if it was a prayer of residence, let him make up the prayer of residence during the journey as it was missed.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who went out on a journey, then staying (became apparent) for him while he was in his prayer. He said: He completes (the prayer) when staying becomes apparent for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who is in Basra and is from the people of Kufa, having a house and residence there, so he passes through Kufa, and he is merely passing through, not intending to stay except for the time it takes to prepare for a day or two days. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He stays in the outskirts of the city and shortens (his prayer).' I said, 'And if he goes to his family?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the complete (prayer).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I was listening: 'Regarding the traveler who considers staying for ten days,' he said: 'Let him complete the prayer. And if he does not know whether he will stay a day or more, let him count thirty days, then let him complete [the prayer]. And if he stayed a day or one prayer [time],' Muhammad ibn Muslim said to him: 'It has reached me that you said five [days].' He said: 'I had said that.' Abu Ayoub said: 'So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, can it be less than five?' He said: 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a who said: I asked him about salat at night and during the day when neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the stars can be seen. He said: 'Exert your judgment and deliberately aim for the Qibla to the best of your ability.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Abdillah al-Farra', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man from our companions said to him: 'Sometimes the prayer time is confused for us on a cloudy day.' So he said: 'Do you know those birds which are with you in Iraq that are called roosters?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'When their calls rise and respond to each other, then the sun has declined,' — or he said: 'Then pray it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah ibn Ayyub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'When you pray salat and you are facing other than the Qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed facing other than the Qiblah, and you are still within the prayer time, then repeat it. But if the prayer time has passed, do not repeat it.'

And by this chain, from Fadala, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a man who prayed the morning prayer at night, the moon having deceived him, and he slept until the sun rose; then he was informed that he had prayed at night. He said: He must repeat his prayer.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I am a man who is a muezzin. So whenever it was a cloudy day, I could not recognize the time.' So he said: 'When the rooster crows three consecutive times, the sun has declined and the time for salat has entered.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever prays salat outside of its prescribed time, there is no salat for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Investigation (tahkharri) always suffices when the direction of the Qibla is not known.'

Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding a man who prays salat facing other than the qibla and realizes this while in the salat, before he has completed it — he said: If he was facing somewhere between the east and the west, let him turn his face toward the qibla the moment he realizes it; and if he was facing the back of the qibla (directly opposite), let him cut short the salat, then turn his face toward the qibla, then begin the salat anew.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man happens to be in a wilderness of the earth on a cloudy day and he prays toward other than the Qibla. Then (the sky) clears and he comes to know that he had prayed toward other than the Qibla. How should he deal with it? He said: If he is still within the prayer time, then let him repeat his prayer; but if the prayer time has passed, then his striving (ijtihad to determine the direction) suffices him.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Qiblah of the one confused, so he (peace be upon him) said: He prays wherever he desires.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Alah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, Alah, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, Alah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, Alah, from Ismail ibn Rabaah, Alah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you pray and you see that you are within the time, and the time has not yet entered, then the time enters while you are in the prayer, so it has sufficed you.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pray facing Bayt Al-Maqdis?' He said, 'Yes.' So I said, 'Did he make the Ka'bah behind his back?' He said, 'As for when he was in Makkah, no; and as for when he emigrated to Al-Madinah, yes, until he was turned towards the Ka'bah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Four categories of people upon whom the complete prayer is obligatory, whether they are in travel or in residence: the hirer (of animals), the worker (of it), the shepherd, and the mailman, because it is their occupation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: There is no shortening (of prayer) upon the sailors in their ships, nor upon the hirers (of animals) and the cameleers. And in another report: The hirer, when the journey extends for him, let him shorten (his prayer). He said: And the meaning of 'the journey extends for him' is that he makes two stages (of travel) into one stage.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the man who goes out to his estate and stays for one day, two days, or three days: does he shorten (the prayer) or pray complete? He (peace be upon him) said: He prays the complete prayer, every time he arrives at an estate from his estates.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Bedouins do not shorten [their prayers], and that is because their houses are with them.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man has estates, some of them near each other. He goes out and stays in them. Should he pray complete or shorten?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Complete'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Wassa from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but whoever is driven to necessity, not desiring, nor exceeding the limit.' He said: 'The desiring is the hunter, and the exceeding is the thief. It is not for these two that they should eat the dead when they are desperate to it. It is Prohibited upon them both. It is not upon them just as it is upon the Muslims, and it is not for them that they should be shortening in the Salat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who goes out for hunting, should he shorten [the prayer] or complete [it]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should complete [the prayer], because it is not a rightful travel.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about him) about the sailors and the Bedouins, 'Is it upon them to shorten [the prayer]?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, their houses are with them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Imran ibn Muhammad, from Imran al-Qummi, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'When a man goes out for hunting, traveling for a day or two days, should he shorten (the prayer) or complete it?' He said, 'If he goes out for his livelihood and the provision of his dependents, let him break (fast) and let him shorten (the prayer); but if he goes out to seek the superfluous (leisure/hunting for sport), then no, and there is no prestige (for him to shorten).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the traveller who prays behind the resident, he said: He prays two rak'at and proceeds wherever he wishes.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the traveller who prays with the Imam and attains two Rak'at from the Salat. Would that suffice him? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the prayer during the journey. He said: 'Two rak'at, with nothing before them or after them, except that it is befitting for the traveller to pray four rak'at after Maghrib, and let him pray voluntarily at night whatever he wishes if he is encamped; and if he is riding, let him pray upon his animal while he is riding, and let his prayer be with gestures, and let his head be where he intends the prostration, lower than his bowing.'

Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not leave the four rak'at after the Maghrib prayer, neither in residency nor on a journey.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The prayer during travel is two rak'at, with nothing before them or after them, except for Maghrib, for after it are four rak'at. Do not leave them in residence or in travel, and there is no making up of the daytime prayer upon you, and pray the night prayer and make it up.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Zareeh who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The night prayer was missed by me during the journey, so can I fulfil it during the day?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if you can bear it'.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Aban ibn Taghlib who said: I went out with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in what is between Mecca and Medina, so he would say: 'As for you, you are youths, you delay; and as for me, I am an old man, I hasten.' So he would pray the night prayer at the beginning of the night.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays upon his riding animal. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He indicates by gestures, making the prostration lower than the bowing.' I said, 'Can he pray while he is walking?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, indicating by gestures, and let him make the prostration lower than the bowing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who prays the voluntary prayers in the cities, while he is upon his riding animal, facing wherever it turns him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, from Abu al-Harith, who said: I asked him, meaning Al-Reza (peace be upon him), about the four rak'at after Maghrib during travel: 'The cameleer hurries me and does not allow me to pray on the ground. Should I pray them in the carriage?' He said: 'Yes, pray them in the carriage.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Pray the two Rak'at of Al-Fajr in the carriage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) being asked about the prayer in the ship, so he said: 'If you are able to go out to the hard ground, then go out. But if you are not able, so pray standing. But if you are not able, so pray seated, and investigate (the direction of) the Qiblah'.

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the prayer in the ship. So he said: 'He should face the Qiblah. So when it turns, and he is able to face towards the Qiblah, let him do so; or else, let him pray wherever it faces him.' He said: 'So if he is able to stand, let him pray standing; or else, let him sit, then let him pray.'

Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who is in the ship and does not know where the Qiblah is, he said: He should strive to determine it, but if he does not know, he prays facing its head (front).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the prayer in the ship, so he said: 'If it is heavily laden such that when you stand in it it does not move, then pray standing; and if it is light and rolls, then pray seated.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I was with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in the ship on the Tigris. The time for prayer arrived, so I said, 'May I be your ransom, should we pray in congregation?' He said, 'Do not pray a congregation prayer in the belly of a valley.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while I was a youth, so he described voluntary acts and fasting to me. He saw the heaviness of that on my face, so he said to me: 'This is not like the obligatory duty; whoever neglects it is destroyed. Rather, it is voluntary. If you are occupied with it or neglect it, you make it up.' Indeed, they disliked that their deeds be raised one day complete and one day deficient. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Those who are constant at their Prayer.' And they disliked that they pray until the day declines, for the gates of the sky are opened when the day declines.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The obligatory and optional prayers are fifty-one rak'ahs in total. Among them are two rak'ahs after 'Atamah (night prayer) prayed while seated, which are counted as one rak'ah while standing. The obligatory among these are seventeen rak'ahs, and the optional are thirty-four rak'ahs.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, and Al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik and Bukayr, said: We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray voluntary prayers equal to twice the obligatory ones, and he would fast voluntary fasts equal to twice the obligatory ones.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the most superior of what the Sunnah has established regarding the prayer, so he said: 'The completion of fifty.' And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, similar to it.

Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Hanan, who said: 'Amr ibn Hurayth asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was seated, and he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to pray eight rak'at at midday, and four of the first (Zohr), and eight after it, and four of Asr, and three of Maghrib, and four after Maghrib, and the last Isha being four, and eight of the night prayer, and three of Witr, and two of Fajr, and the morning prayer as two rak'at.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And if I were strong enough to do more than this, would Allah punish me for the abundance of prayer?' So he said, 'No, but He would punish for neglecting the Sunnah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is there anything [prayer] before the last 'Isha and after it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, other than that I pray two rak'at after it, and I do not count them as part of the night prayer.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hajjaj al-Khashshab, from Abu al-Fawaris, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbade me from speaking between the four Rak'at which are after Maghrib.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Our companions differ regarding the voluntary prayer; some of them pray four and forty, and some of them pray fifty. So inform me with which you act, how it is, so that I may act upon the like of it.' He said, 'I pray one and fifty.' Then he said, 'Hold on!' And he counted with his hand: 'The midday is eight, and four after the Dhuhr, and four before the Asr, and two after the Maghrib, and two before the last Isha, and two after the Isha while seated, accounted as one while standing, and eight for the night prayer, and the Witr is three, and two of the Fajr, and the Obligatory ones are seventeen. So that is one and fifty.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the voluntary prayers during the day, so he mentioned that he prays eight rak'at before Dhuhr and eight after it.

From him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The prayer of Al-Zawal is the prayer of the repentant.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'During the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the Mercy of his Lord.' He said: 'It means the night prayer.' I said to him, 'And the parts of the day, so that you may be well pleased.' He said: 'It means performing voluntary prayer during the day.' I said to him, 'And the retreat of the stars.' He said: 'Two Rak'at before the morning prayer.' I said, 'And after the prostrations.' He said: 'Two Rak'at after the Maghrib prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would, when he prayed the final Isha prayer, order that his water for ablution and his toothbrush be placed by his head, covered. He would then lie down for as long as Allah willed. Then he would rise, brush his teeth, perform ablution, and pray four rak'at. Then he would lie down again, then rise, brush his teeth, perform ablution, and pray four rak'at. Then he would lie down until, when morning was approaching, he would rise and pray the Witr, then pray the two rak'at. Then he said: 'Certainly you have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent exemplar.' I said: 'When did he stand (for night prayer)?' He said: 'After a third of the night.' And he said in another hadith: 'After half the night.' And in another report: 'His standing, bowing, and prostration were equal, and he would brush his teeth every time he rose from his sleep, and he would recite the verses from Surah Aal-Imran: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth..." up to His words: "Indeed, You do not fail to fulfill the promise."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pray from the night thirteen rak'at, including the Witr, and the two rak'at of Fajr, during travel and residence.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said: Ismail ibn Sa'd al-Ahwas narrated to me, saying: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): How many rak'at are in the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: Fifty-one rak'at. Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa — similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely the rising by night is the firmest way to tread and the best speech.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The meaning of His Words, and the best speech is the standing of the man from his bed, intending Allah by it, not intending anything else by it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The servant is awakened three times during the night, so if he does not stand (for prayer), Satan comes to him and urinates in his ear.' He said: 'And I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: They used to sleep but little in the night He said: 'They missed very few nights, not standing (for prayer) in them.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Umar ibn Yazeed, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, in the night there is a time which a Muslim servant matches by praying and supplicating to Allah during it, except that he is answered during every night.' I said, 'May Allah keep you well! So which time from the night is it?' He said: 'When half the night passes, during the first sixth of the remaining half.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man from your mawali, from their righteous ones, complained to me about what he faces from sleep, and said, 'I intend to stand for prayer at night, but sleep overcomes me until morning, and sometimes I make up my prayers for the month consecutively, and for two months I bear the heaviness of it.' So he said, 'A delight of the eye for him, by Allah.' He said, 'And he did not permit him to pray in the first part of the night, and said, 'Making up the prayers during the day is superior.' I said, 'But among our women are young girls who love goodness and its people, and are eager for prayer, but sleep overcomes them so that sometimes they make it up, and sometimes they are too weak to make it up, and they are strong upon it in the first part of the night.' So he permitted them to pray in the first part of the night when they were too weak and missed making up the prayers.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A man is not praised if he rises from the end of the night, prays his prayer in one go, and then one single unit/stroke, and then goes to sleep.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man prays the two rak'at of the Witr, then stands up and forgets the Tashahhud until he bows, and remembers while he is bowing.' He said, 'He should sit from his bowing, perform the Tashahhud, then stand up and complete (the prayer).' I said, 'Did you not say regarding the obligatory prayer, that if he remembers it after having bowed, he should continue, then perform two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdatay al-Sahw) after he finishes, and perform the Tashahhud in them?' He said, 'The optional prayer is not like the obligatory prayer.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub and Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the most superior of the timings for Al-Witr. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dawn is the beginning of that'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail ibn Abi Sara, who said: Aban ibn Taghlib informed me, saying: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): At what time did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pray Al-Witr? He said: At the time like the setting of the sun, up to the time of the Maghrib prayer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Where is the place of the two Rak'at that are before the morning prayer?' He said: 'Before the emergence of the dawn. So when the dawn emerges, the time for the morning prayer has entered.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Asbaat, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said: I prayed behind Al-Rida (peace be upon him) in the Sacred Masjid, the night prayer. So when he was free, he made the place of rest a prostration.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Kindi, from Ismail ibn Jabir or Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I stand [for prayer] at the end of the night, and I fear the morning [will come before I finish].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Recite Al-Hamd [Surah Al-Fatiha], and hasten, and hasten.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who stands (for prayer) at the end of the night and he fears that the morning will catch him suddenly; should he begin with Al-Witr, or pray the Salat in its complete form so that Al-Witr becomes the last of that? He said: 'Rather, he should begin with Al-Witr.' And he said: 'I used to do that.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Hafs ibn Salim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Taslim (salutation) in the two Rak'at of Al-Witr, so he said: 'Yes, and if you have a need, go out and fulfill it, then return and bow in one Rak'ah.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the Qunut in the Witr prayer. Is there anything fixed to be followed and said? So he (peace be upon him) said: No. Laud upon Allah (Mighty and Majestic) and send Blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and seek Forgiveness for your grievous sin. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Every sin is grievous.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Qunut in the Witr prayer is seeking forgiveness, and in the obligatory prayer, it is supplication.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Seek forgiveness of Allah in the Witr prayer seventy times.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Numan, from his father, from one of his men, who said: A man came to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have been deprived of night prayer.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'You are a man whose sins have restricted you.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I read in the letter of a man to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The two Rak'at which are before the Fajr prayer, are they from the night prayer or from the daytime prayer, and at what time should I pray them?' So he wrote in his own handwriting: 'Include them in the night prayer completely.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Bureyd ibn Zamra Al-Laysi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who is occupied/busy from the midday prayer time: 'Should he hasten [the prayer] from the beginning of the day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when he knows that he will be occupied, so he should hasten it during the forenoon, all of it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: When it was the day of the conquest of Mecca, a tent of black hair was pitched for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at Al-Abtah. Then water was poured upon it from a bowl in which the traces of dough were seen. Then he determined the Qiblah in the forenoon, so he bowed in eight Raka'at. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had not bowed in these before that, nor (did he) afterwards.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pay back what has been missed from the daytime prayers during the daytime, and what has been missed from the night prayers during the night.' I said: 'Can I pay back two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'Yes, pay back Witr always.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Murazim who said: Ismail ibn Jabir asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May Allah keep you well! Upon me are many optional prayers, so what should I do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Pay them back.' He said to him, 'They are more numerous than that.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Pay them back.' I said, 'I cannot count them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Be at it.' Murazim said, 'And I was sick for four months, not praying optional prayers therein. I said, 'May Allah keep you well, and may I be your ransom, I was sick for four months, not praying an optional prayer.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Payback is not upon you. The sick one is not like the healthy one. Everything that Allah overcomes upon you, Allah is more deserving of excusing you regarding it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The best way to make up the optional prayers is to make up the night prayers at night, and the day prayers during the day.' I said, 'So there will be two Witr prayers in one night?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said, 'And why do you order me to pray Witr and two Witr prayers in one night?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'One of them is a make-up (qada)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man for whom the daytime prayers were missed, when should he make them up? He (peace be upon him) said: Whenever he wishes. If he wishes, after Maghrib, and if he wishes, after Isha.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man for whom the daytime prayers are missed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray them, if he so desires, after Maghrib, and if he so desires, after 'Isha'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Qummi from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Amira, raising it, said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed by a man who was praying the forenoon prayer in the Mosque of Kufa, so he pressed his side with the whip and said: 'You slaughtered the prayer of the repentant, may Allah slaughter you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So shall I leave it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is your view of the one who forbids a servant when he is praying?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'And the denial of Ali (peace be upon him) is sufficient for its forbiddance.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassha, from Aban, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fulfillment of the Witr prayer after the Dhuhr prayer, so he said: 'Fulfill it as Witr always, just as it was missed by you.' I said: 'And two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'Yes. Is it not so that one of the two is a fulfillment (of the missed one)?'
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Al-Mugheira, from Abu Jareer Al-Qummy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to fulfill twenty Witr prayers in one night.

From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When two Witr prayers gather upon you, or three, or more than that, then fulfill them as they have been missed, distinguishing between every two Witr prayers with one Salat, because the Witr is the last one; do not precede anything before its first one, the first is the first. So begin with the first when you fulfill the Salat of your night, then the Witr. He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Two Witr prayers cannot be in one night except that one of the two is a Qada (make-up) prayer.' And he said: 'If you pray Witr at the beginning of the night and stand (to pray) at the end of the night, then your first Witr is a Qada, and whatever you prayed from the Salat during your entire night, let it be Qada until the end of your Salat, for these are for your night, and let the last of your Salats be the Witr, the Witr of your night.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Ali ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man has from the optional prayers so many that he does not know what they are due to their abundance; what should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Let him pray until he does not know how many he has prayed due to their abundance, so he will have fulfilled by the measure of his knowledge.' I said, 'Suppose he is not able to fulfill them due to many occupations?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'If his occupation is in seeking a livelihood that is necessary, or a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him; and if his occupation is for the world, being preoccupied with it from the prayer, then upon him is the fulfillment, or else he will meet Allah as slighting, negligent, wasting the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' I said, 'Suppose he is not able to fulfill them, so would it be suitable for him to give charity?' So he was silent for a while, then said, 'Yes, let him give charity.' I said, 'And what should he give charity with?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'According to his capacity, and the least of that is a Mudd for each poor person in place of each prayer.' I said, 'And how many prayers obligate upon him a Mudd for each poor person?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'For every two Rak'at from the night prayer, and every two Rak'at from the daytime prayer.' So I said, 'He is not able.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'A Mudd for every four Rak'at.' I said, 'He is not able.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'A Mudd for every night prayer, and a Mudd for the daytime prayer, and the prayer is superior, and the prayer is superior.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Know that the optional prayer is in the status of a gift; whenever it is brought, it is accepted.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a number of our companions, that Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) whenever he was distressed, he left the optional (prayer).

And from him, from Ali ibn Ma'bad or someone else, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For the hearts there is a welcoming (inclination) and a turning back (aversion). So whenever it inclines, perform optional prayers, and whenever it turns back, stick to the obligatory prayers.'

And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Abdullah ibn Ali al-Sarrad, who said: Abu Kahmas asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'Should a man pray his optional prayers in one place or distribute them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he should distribute them here and there, for they will testify for him on the Day of Judgment.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man fulfills something from his fifty [outstanding] prayers in the Sacred Mosque, or in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), or in the Mosque of Kufa. Would the one rak'ah be reckoned for him with the multiplication of what has come from your forefathers (peace be upon them) regarding these mosques, to the extent that it would suffice him, when there are ten thousand rak'ahs upon him, if he were to pray one hundred rak'ahs, or less, or more? And what would be his state?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'It would be reckoned for him with the double [reward]. But, if there happen to be shortened ones from the prayer, (these would be) at their state. So he would not do it except for the increase, being closer to it than the deficiency.'

Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fazl al-Nowfaly, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man in haste, what is that which would suffice him in the optional (prayer)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Three glorifications in the recitation, and a glorification in the bowing, and a glorification in the prostration.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Prayer of Fear. He said: The Imam stands, and a group of his companions comes and stands behind him, while another group faces the enemy. The Imam prays one Rak'ah with them. Then he stands, and they stand with him, so he represents them standing, and they pray the second Rak'ah. Then some of them greet each other with Salaam, and then they disperse. They stand in the place of their companions, and the others come and stand behind the Imam. The Imam prays the second Rak'ah with them. Then the Imam sits, and they stand and pray another Rak'ah. Then he greets them, and they disperse by his greeting. He said: And in the Maghrib prayer, it is similar to that. The Imam stands, and a group comes and stands behind him. Then he prays one Rak'ah with them. Then he stands, and they stand, so the Imam represents them standing, and they pray the two Rak'ahs. They perform Tashahhud, and some of them greet each other. Then they disperse, stand in the place of their companions, and the others come and stand behind the Imam. He prays one Rak'ah with them, reciting therein. Then he sits and performs Tashahhud. Then he stands, and they stand with him, and he prays another Rak'ah with them. Then he sits, and they stand and complete another Rak'ah. Then he greets them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prayed with his companions during the Expedition of Dhat al-Riqa', the Prayer of Fear. So he separated his companions into two groups: he stationed one group facing the enemy and one group behind him. He said Takbir, and they said Takbir. He recited, and they listened silently. He bowed (Ruku'), so they bowed. He prostrated (Sajdah), so they prostrated. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) completed (the prayer) standing, and they prayed one Rak'ah by themselves. Then some of them offered Salam to the others. Then they went out to their companions, so they stood facing the enemy, and their companions came over, so they stood behind the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). So he prayed one Rak'ah with them. Then he performed Tashahhud and offered Salam upon them. So they stood and prayed one Rak'ah by themselves, then some of them offered Salam to the others.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If you are in a land of fear, and you fear a thief or a predatory beast, then pray (Salat) upon your animal.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the captive whom the polytheists imprison, so the prayer time presents itself, but the one who imprisoned him prevents him from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He indicates by gestures.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: I asked him (peace be upon him), saying: 'If I am on the road to Mecca and we descend for prayer in places where there are Bedouins, should we pray the obligatory prayer on the ground, reciting the Mother of the Book alone, or should we pray upon the ride, reciting the Opening of the Book and the Chapter?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you fear, pray the obligatory and non-obligatory prayers upon the ride; and when you recite Al-Hamd and a Chapter, it is more beloved to me, and I do not see any problem with what you do.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'But if you are in danger, then (perform your prayer) on foot or on horseback' [2:239], 'How should he pray?' and 'What should he say when he fears from a predatory beast or a thief, how should he pray?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should say Takbir and indicate with a gesture of his head.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him), who said: When the horses gallop and the swords are restless, two exclamations of Takbir would suffice him. So this is another reduction.

From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira who said: I heard one of our companions mention that the minimum that suffices in the combat prayer, from the Takbir, is two Takbirs for each Salat, except for Maghrib, for it there are three.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve will cause you distress.' He said: In the two Rak'at, one is reduced from them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the prayer of combat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When they meet and fight, then the prayer at that time is the Takbir; and if they are standing, unable to perform the prayer with the congregation, then the prayer is by gestures.'

Muhammad narrated from Ahmad from Ahmad from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'What is your view if the one standing in prayer does not have wudu, what should he do and he is not able to dismount?' He said: 'He should perform tayammum from his pad, or his saddle, or the mane of his animal, for there is dust in it; and he prays and makes the sajdah lower than the ruku', and he does not turn towards the qiblah, but in whichever direction his animal turns, except that he faces the qiblah with the first takbirah when he turns.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who encounters a wild beast, and the time for prayer has arrived, and he is unable to walk due to fear of the beast. If he stands to pray, he fears the beast during his bowing and prostration, and the beast is in front of him facing away from the Qiblah. If he turns towards the Qiblah, he fears the lion will leap upon him. How should he act? He said: He should face the lion, pray, and gesture with his head while standing, even if the lion is facing away from the Qiblah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'There is neither an Azan nor an Iqamah on the day of Al-Fitr and Al-Adha; their Azan is the rising of the sun. When it rises, they go out. And there is no Salat before them nor after them. And whoever does not pray Salat with an Imam in a Jam'ah, then there is no Salat for him, nor is there Qada' upon him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There is no prayer on the day of Al-Fitr and Al-Adha except with an Imam.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya, who said: I asked him about the prayer of the two Eids, so he said: 'Two rak'at. There is nothing before them and nothing after them, and there is neither an Adhan nor an Iqamah in them. He exalts Allah with twelve Takbirs in them. He begins by exalting Allah and commencing the prayer.' Then he recites the Opening of the Book, then he recites 'By the Sun and its brightness', then he exalts Allah with five Takbirs. Then he exalts Allah and bows, so his bowing is with the seventh (Takbir). Then he prostrates two prostrations. Then he stands and recites the Opening of the Book and 'Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?' Then he exalts Allah with four Takbirs, prostrates two prostrations, recites the Tashahhud, and gives the Salam. He said: 'And thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) do. And the sermon is after the prayer. It was only Uthman who innovated the sermon to be before the prayer.' And when the Imam delivers the sermon, let him sit for a little while between the two sermons. And it is befitting for the Imam to wear a Burda (cloak) on the day of the two Eids, and to wear a turban, whether it is Shati (a type of turban) or Qaiz (a simple head covering). And he should go out to the open ground where he can look at the horizons of the sky, and he should not pray upon a woven mat, nor prostrate upon it. And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to go out to Al-Baqi', so he would lead the people in prayer.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the day of Fitr or the day of Adha: 'If only you would pray in your mosque?' So he said: 'I love to come out to the horizons of the sky.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the prayer of the two Eids, he said: He should exclaim Takbir, then recite, then exclaim five [Takbirs], and perform Qunut between every two Takbirs. Then he should exclaim the seventh Takbir and bow with it. Then he should prostrate, then stand for the second [rak'ah], so he should recite, then exclaim four [Takbirs], and perform Qunut between every two Takbirs. Then he should exclaim Takbir and bow with it.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) forbade taking out the weapons during the two Eids, except if there happens to be an enemy present.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father was brought the 'Khumra' on the day of al-Fitr, so he ordered it to be returned, then he said: 'This is a day on which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to love to look at the horizons of the sky and to place his face upon the ground.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Salma, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Two Eids coincided during the era of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he addressed the people, then said: 'This is a day in which two Eids are gathered. So whoever wishes to join us [in prayer], let him do so, and whoever does not do so, then there is an allowance for him, meaning the one who was laid back [or preferred to stay away].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who missed one rak'ah with the Imam during the days of Tashreeq. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He completes the prayer and says Takbir.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Sunnah upon the people of the cities is that they should go out from their cities during the two Eids, except for the people of Makkah, for they pray in the Sacred Masjid.

Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fazl Al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Two rak'at from the Sunnah are not prayed in any place except in Medina. He would pray in the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during Eid, before he goes out to the musalla (praying place). That is nowhere except in Medina, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did so.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Ahmad ibn Suleyman, all from Murra, the slave of Muhammad ibn Khalid, who said: The people of Al-Medina cried out to Muhammad ibn Khalid regarding the request for rain (Istisqa'), so he said to me, 'Go to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and ask him, for they have cried out to me.' So I went to him and told him, and he said to me, 'Tell him to go out.' I said to him, 'When should he go out, may I be sacrificed for you?' He said, 'On the day of Monday.' I said, 'How should he deal with it?' He said, 'He should take out the pulpit, then go out walking just as he would walk on the day of the two Eids, and in front of him would be the Muezzins, in their hands being their walking sticks, until when he ends up to the praying place, where he would pray two Rak'at with the people, without an Azan or an Iqamah. Then he would ascend the pulpit, and overturn his cloak, so that he would make that which is upon his right to be upon his left, and that which is upon his left to be upon his right.' Then he should face the Qiblah, and he would exclaim one hundred Takbirs, raising his voice with it. Then he would turn towards the people on his right, so he would Glorify Allah with one hundred Glorifications raising his voice with it. Then he would turn towards the people on his left, so he would extoll the Oneness of Allah raising his voice with it. Then he would face the people, so he would Praise Allah with one hundred Praises. Then he would raise his hands, and he would supplicate. Then they would be supplicating, so I hope that they would not be unsuccessful.' He (the narrator) said, 'He did so. So when we returned, the rain came, and they said, 'This is from the teaching of Ja'far (peace be upon him)'. And in a report of Yunus, 'So we had not returned until we were drenched'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Prayer for Rain, so he said: 'It is like the Prayer of the two Eids; one recites in it and proclaims Takbir in it just as one recites and proclaims Takbir in those. The Imam goes out and emerges to a clean place in tranquility, dignity, humility, and submissiveness, and the people emerge with him.' So he praises Allah, glorifies Him, and lauds Him, and strives in supplication, and frequently recites Tasbih, Tahleel, and Takbir, and prays two Rak'at like the Prayer of the two Eids, in supplication, asking, and striving. So when the Imam gives the Taslim, he turns over his garment and makes the side that was on the right shoulder be on the left, and that which was on the left be on the right, for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did it like that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) overturning his cloak when he prayed for rain, so he said: 'A sign between him and his companions, that aridity is turned into fertility.'

And in a report of Ibn Al-Mugheira, He (peace be upon him) said: 'One exclaims Takbir in the Prayer for Rain just as one exclaims Takbir in the two Eids — seven in the first (Rak'ah) and five in the second, and he prays before the sermon, and he is loud with the recitation, and he supplicates for rain while he is seated.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) led the people in Dhuhr and Asr prayers when the sun began to decline, in congregation, without any reason; and he led them in Maghrib and the last Isha prayer before the disappearance of the twilight, without any reason, in congregation. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did this only so that the time might be expanded for his community.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I attended the Maghrib prayer on a rainy night in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). When it was close to the twilight, they called the adhan and established the iqama, and they prayed Maghrib. Then they gave the people time until they had prayed two rak'at. Then the muadhdhin stood up in his place in the mosque, and he established the prayer, and they prayed Isha. Then the people dispersed to their homes. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said: Yes, indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to do this.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'When you combine between the two salats, do not perform optional (prayers) between the two.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Hammad ibn Uthman who said: Muhammad ibn Hakim narrated to me saying, 'I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying:' The combining of the two salats is when there are no optional prayers between the two; but if there are optional prayers between the two, then there is no combining.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) led us in the Zuhr and Asr prayers at the time of the sun's decline, with one adhan and two iqamas, and said: 'I am occupied with a matter, so perform optional prayers.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abbas al-Naqid who said: What was in my possession dispersed, and my business associates left me. So I complained of that to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), and he said to me: Combine the two prayers, the Dhuhr and the Asr — you will see what you love.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), was taken [from this world], three Sunnahs were established regarding it. As for one of them: when he died, the sun was eclipsed, and the people said, "The sun was eclipsed due to the loss of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)." So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and lauded Him, then said: "O people! The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah, moving by His command, obedient to Him. They do not eclipse for the death of anyone, nor for his life. So when they eclipse, or one of them, pray." Then he descended and prayed with the people the prayer of the eclipse.'

Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: We said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'These winds and darknesses that occur, should one pray for them?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Every fear of the sky, from darkness, or wind, or terror, so pray for it the prayer of the eclipse, until it settles.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: The time for the Salat of the eclipse is during the hour in which it eclipses, at the rising of the sun and at its setting. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is Obligatory.

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about the prayer of the eclipse during the time of the obligatory prayer, so he said: 'Begin with the obligatory prayer.' It was said to him: '(What if it was) at the time of the night prayer?' So he said: 'Pray the eclipse prayer before the night prayer.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the sun is totally eclipsed and obscured, and you did not know, then you came to know after that, so upon you is the making up (of the missed prayer); and if it did not become totally obscured, so there is no making up upon you. And in another report, when one knows of the eclipse and forgets to pray, so upon him is the making up; and if he did not know of it, so there is no making up upon him. This is when the whole of it is not totally obscured.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ali ibn al-Fad al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said: I wrote to him: 'When the sun or the moon is eclipsed and I am riding and am not able to dismount,' he wrote to me: 'Pray upon your mount upon which you are.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ja'far: 'O Ja'far! Shall I confer upon you? Shall I give you? Shall I gift you?' So Ja'far said to him: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'So the people thought that he would give him gold or silver, and the people anticipated for that.'
