So he said to him: 'I am giving you something, if you were to act upon it every day, it would be better for you than the world and whatever is in it, and if you were to do it in between two days, Allah would forgive you whatever is between them, or every Friday, or every month, or every year, He would forgive you whatever is between them.' You should pray four Rak'at. You begin by reciting and saying, when you are finished: 'Glory be to Allah, and the Praise is for Allah, and there is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.' You say that fifteen times after the recitation. So when you bow, say it ten times. So when you raise your head from the bowing, say it ten times. So when you prostrate, say it ten times. So when you raise your head from the prostration, say it ten times between the two prostrations. So when you perform the second prostration, say it ten times. So when you raise your head from the second prostration, say it ten times, while you are seated, before you stand. So that is seventy-five glorifications in every Rak'at, three hundred glorifications in four Rak'at. In four (Rak'at) there are one thousand two hundred glorifications, and extollations of Oneness, and exclamations of Takbir, and praises. If you so desire, pray it during the day, and if you so desire, pray it at night. And in a report of Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'You should recite in the first (Rak'at) When the Earth is Shaken, and in the second And the Runners, and in the third When there comes the Help of Allah, and in the fourth Say: He is Allah, One.' I said, 'So what is its reward?' He said: 'If there were upon him sins like the grains of sand, Allah would forgive them for him.' Then he looked at me and said: 'But rather, that is for you and for your companions.'

And it has been narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You pray it at night, and you pray it during the journey at night and the day, and if you wish, make it from your optional prayers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who is in a hurry, prays the Salat of Ja'far in isolation, then fulfills the glorifications while he is going regarding his needs.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Sulayman, who said: I wrote to the Man (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the Prayer of Glorification in the carriage?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'When you are traveling, so pray.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ibn Mahboub, raising it (to the Imam), said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say in the last Rak'ah of the Salat of Ja'far (peace be upon him): O One Who is Clothed in Honour and Dignity! O One Who Girds Himself with Glory and is Generous with it! O One to whom Glorification is befitting alone! O One whose Knowledge encompasses all things! O Possessor of Bounty and Grace! O Possessor of Favours and Grace! O Possessor of Power and Generosity! I ask You by the knots of Honour on Your Throne, and by the peak of Mercy in Your Book, and by Your Greatest, Most Exalted Name, and Your Perfect Words, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You do for me such and such.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Abi al-Qasim, mentioning it from the one who narrated it, from Abu Saeed al-Madainy, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I teach you something you should say in the Salat of Ja'far?' So I said, 'Yes'. So he said: 'When you are in the last prostration of the four rak'at, say when you have finished your glorification.' 'Glorious is the One Who is Clothed in Honour and Dignity! Glorious is the One Who Girds Himself with Glory and is Honoured with it! Glorious is the One, to whom glorification is not befitting except Him! Glorious is the One Whose Knowledge encompasses all things! Glorious is the One of Grace and Bounties! Glorious is the One of Power and Benevolence!' O Allah, I ask You by the knots of Honour from Your Throne, and the peak of Mercy from Your Book, and Your Greatest Name, and Your complete Words which have attained Truth and Justice. Send Blessings upon Muhammad and his Family, and Do such and such with me.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The one who prays the Salat of Ja'far, Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, will write for him from the reward the like of what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ja'far.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, by Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who prays four Rak'at, reciting in every Rak'at 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' fifty times, will not finish (complete his prayer), and there will be a sin (remaining) between him and Allah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, by his chain, raised it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The one who prays two Rak'at with 'Say He is Allah, One' in every Rak'at sixty times, finishes, and there is not a sin between him and Allah.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever prays the Maghrib prayer, and after it prays four Rak'at, and does not speak until he has prayed ten Rak'at, reciting in each Rak'at Al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad, it would be equivalent to (freeing) ten necks (of slaves).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Kurdous, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever purifies himself, then lies down upon his bed, his bed becomes like his mosque. So if he rises during the night and remembers Allah, his sins scatter away from him. And if he rises at the end of the night, purifies himself, prays two Rak'at, praises Allah, lauds Him, and sends blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then whatever he asks Allah for, He grants it: either He gives him exactly what he asked for, or He reserves for him what is better for him.

Ali ibn Muhammad, by his chain, from one of them (peace be upon him), regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely the rising by night is the firmest way to tread and the best speech.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'These are two Rak'at after Al-Maghrib. You should recite in the first Rak'at with the Opening of the Book, and ten verses from the beginning of Al-Baqarah, and the Verse of Al-Sakhra, and from His Words: "And your God is one God! There is no god but He; He is the Beneficent, the Merciful. Surely in the Creation of the skies and the earth..." up to His Words: "...there are signs for a people who understand." And fifteen times: Say, He is Allah, One.'" And in the second Rak'at, the Opening of the Book, and the Verse of the Throne, and the end of Al-Baqarah, from His Words: "To Allah belongs whatever is in the skies and whatever is in the earth," up to the end of the Chapter. And fifteen times: Say, He is Allah, One. Then, after this, supplicate with whatever you desire.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who persevered upon it, there would be written for him, with each Salat, six hundred thousand performances of Hajj.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When it is the middle of Sha'ban, pray four Rak'at, reciting in each Rak'at Al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad one hundred times. When you finish, say: 'O Allah, I am needy to You, and I seek Refuge with You, and fearful from You, and Sanctuary with You. Lord, do not change my name. Lord, do not change my body. Lord, do not overload my afflictions. I seek Refuge with Your Pardon from Your Punishment, and I seek Refuge with Your Pleasure from Your Wrath, and I seek Refuge with Your Mercy from Your Punishment, and I seek Refuge with You from You. Majestic is Your Praise. You are as You Praised Yourself, and above what the speakers are saying.' He said, and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: On the day of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, news was given to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding it: 'Whoever prays in it at any time he desires, twelve Rak'at, reciting in each Rak'at with the Mother of the Quran and a Chapter whatever is easy.' When he finishes and gives Salam, he sits in his place, then recites the Mother of the Quran four times, and the three Mu'awwidhat (Chapters 112, 113, 114), each one four times. When he finishes and he is in his place, he says: 'La ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar, wa al-hamdu lillah, wa subhan Allah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' four times. Then he says: 'Allah, Allah Rabbi, la ushriku bihi shay'an' four times, then he supplicates, so he does not supplicate with anything except that it is answered for him regarding every need, except if he were to supplicate regarding a catastrophe (to befall upon a) people, or cutting-off of a relationship.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halbi, from Amr ibn Hurayth, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray two Rak'at, and seek Allah's choice (Istikhara), so by Allah, no Muslim seeks Allah's choice except that He chooses for him definitively.'

Multiple narrators from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Basri from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi from Harun ibn Kharja from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you intend a matter, take six pieces of paper and write in three of them: 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Goodness is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, for so-and-so son of so-and-so: Do it'; and in the other three: 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Goodness is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, for so-and-so son of so-and-so: Do not do it'. Then place them beneath your prayer mat, then pray two Rak'at. When you are finished, prostrate and say one hundred times: 'I seek Allah's choice by His mercy, a choice in well-being.' Then sit upright and say: 'O Allah, choose for me and select for me in all my affairs, in ease from You and well-being.' Then strike with your hand to the papers, mix them, and draw one. If three 'Do it' come out consecutively, do the matter you intended; and if three 'Do not do' come out consecutively, do not do it; and if one 'Do it' comes out and the other two are 'Do not do', then draw from the papers up to five, and look at the majority of them and act upon it, and leave the sixth, as you are not in need of it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, who said: Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding Ibn Asbaat, saying: 'What is your view for him?' Ibn Asbaat was present with all of us. 'If he were to travel by land or sea to Egypt, inform him of the best route by land.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The land. And go to the Masjid at a time other than that of the obligatory prayer. So pray two Rak'at, and seek Allah's choice (Istikhara) one hundred times. Then see what occurs in your heart, and act upon it.' And he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'The land is more beloved to me for him.' He said: 'And to me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazam who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When one of you intends something, let him pray two Rak'at, then let him praise Allah and laud Him, and let him send blessings upon Muhammad and the People of his Household, and he should say: O Allah! If this matter is good for me in my religion and my world, then make it easy for me and decree it for me; and if it is other than that, then turn it away from me.' So I asked him: 'What should I recite in these two?' So he said: 'Recite in these two whatever you wish, and if you wish, recite in these two: Say, He is Allah, One, and Say, O you unbelievers!'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Sometimes I intend a matter, and two inclinations separate me: one commands me and the other forbids me.' He said, 'So when you are like that, pray two Rakʿat, and seek the choice of Allah one hundred times and one, then look at which of the two matters is more decisive for you, so do it, for the goodness is in it, if Allah wills. And let your seeking of choice be in safety, for sometimes the choice for a man is in the cutting of his hand, the death of his child, and the loss of his wealth.'

Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) raised it from them (peace be upon him) that he said to one of his companions, and he had asked him about the matter to continue in it, and he could not find anyone to consult, so how should he be dealing with it? He said: 'Consult your Lord.' So he said to him, 'How?' He said to him: 'Intend the need within yourself, then write out two pieces of paper, in one, 'No', and in one, 'Yes', and make these two to be inside two balls of clay.' Then pray two Rak'at of Salat, and make these two to be behind you. and say, 'O Allah! I hereby consult You in this matter of mine, and You are the best of the consultants and advisers, therefore advise me with what is correct for me in it and the best safety.' Then insert your hand, so if it was 'Yes', so do it, and if it was 'No', do not do it. This is how you consult your Lord.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have dependents, and upon me is a debt, and my condition has become difficult, so teach me a supplication; when I supplicate with it, Allah will grant me sustenance by which I can pay off my debt and assist my dependents with it.' So he said, 'O servant of Allah! Perform ablution and perfect your ablution, then pray two rak'ahs, completing the bowing and prostration in them, then say: 'O Glorious! O One! O Generous! I turn to You through Muhammad, Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy. O Muhammad! O Messenger of Allah! I turn through You to Allah, Your Lord and the Lord of all things, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his Ahl al-Bayt. And I ask You for a breath from Your breaths, and an easy opening, and abundant sustenance, by which I may gather my scattered affairs, pay off my debt, and assist my dependents.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn al-Walid ibn Sabih, from his father who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Walid! Where is your shop in relation to the Masjid?' So I said, 'By its door'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever you intend to go to your shop, so begin with the Masjid, and pray two Rak'at therein, or four.' Then say, 'I came with the Might of Allah and His Strength, and I came without any might from me nor strength, but, by Your Might and Your Strength, O Lord.' O Allah, I am Your servant seeking from Your Grace just as You Commanded me, therefore Make that to be easy for me, and I am free from anxiety in Your well-being'.

A number of our companions, from Al-Barqi, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Attar, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: 'O so-and-so, do you not go forth for your needs? Do you not pass by the greatest Mosque with you in Al-Kufa?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'So pray four Rak'at in it.' Say in them: 'I go forth with the might and power of Allah. I go forth without any might from me nor any power, but with Your might, O Lord, and Your power.' I ask You for the blessing of this day and the blessing of its people; and I ask You to provide me from Your grace with something permissible and goodly, which You bring to me with Your might and Your power. And I am humble/submissive in Your well-being.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn ibn Urwah, the son of the sister of Shuayb Al-Aqarqufi, from his maternal uncle Shuayb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is hungry, let him perform wudu and pray two rak'at, then say: O Lord, I am hungry, so feed me, for he will be fed from that moment.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: When you go out for your needs after the obligatory prayer, pray two Rak'at. When you finish the Tashahhud, say: 'O Allah, I have gone out seeking from Your Grace as You commanded me, so provide me with a permissible, goodly sustenance and grant me well-being in what You have provided me.' Repeat this three times. Then pray two more Rak'at. When you finish the Tashahhud, say: 'By the might and power of Allah, I go out without any might or power from myself, but by Your might, O Lord, and Your power. I disassociate from might and power [in myself] and turn to You. O Allah, I ask You for the blessings of this day and its people, and I ask You to provide me from Your Grace with a broad, goodly, permissible sustenance, which You bring to me by Your might and power, while I am humble in Your well-being.' Say this three times.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have invented a supplication.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Leave me from your invention. When a matter befalls you, turn urgently to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and pray two Rak'at, gifting them to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' I said, 'How should I do it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'You perform Ghusl and pray two Rak'at, opening them with the opening of the obligatory prayer, and performing the Tashahhud of the obligatory prayer.' So when you finish the Tashahhud and offer Salam, say: 'O Allah, You are As-Salam (the Peace), and from You is As-Salam, and to You returns As-Salam. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and convey to the soul of Muhammad from me the Salam, and to the souls of the truthful Imams my Salam, and return to me the Salam from them, and the Salam be upon them and the Mercy of Allah and His Blessings.' O Allah, indeed these two Rak'at are a gift from me to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so reward me for them what I hoped for and awaited in You and in Your Messenger, O Guardian of the Believers! Then prostrate and say: 'O Living, O Eternal, O Living Who does not die, O Living, there is no god except You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O Most Merciful of the merciful,' forty times. Then place your right cheek and say it forty times. Then place your left cheek and say it forty times. Then raise your head and extend your hand and say it forty times. Then return your hand to your neck and rest on your index finger and say that forty times. Then take your beard with your left hand and weep or wail and say: 'O Muhammad, O Messenger of Allah, I complain to Allah and to you of my need, and to the People of your Household, the rightly guided, of my need, and through you I turn to Allah regarding my need.' Then prostrate and say: 'O Allah, O Allah,' until your breath is cut off, 'Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and do such and such for me.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So I am the guarantor upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that he will not depart until his need is fulfilled.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the man whose matter has grieved him or who desires a need, he said: 'He should pray two Rak'at, reciting in one of them "Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad" a thousand times, and in the other once. Then he should ask for his need.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Duweyl, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, teach me a supplication for fulfilling the needs.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have an important need for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then perform Ghusl, wear your cleanest clothes, and smell some perfume. Then go out beneath the sky and pray two Rak'at. Commence the prayer by reciting Fatihat al-Kitab (the Opening of the Book) and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Say, He is Allah, One) fifteen times each.' Then you bow (Ruku') and recite it fifteen times, then complete the prayer like the Prayer of Tasbih, except that the recitation is fifteen times. So when you give the Salam, recite it fifteen times. Then you prostrate (Sajdah) and say in your prostration: 'O Allah, every worshipped entity from Your Throne to the settlement of Your earth is false except You, for You are Allah, the Evident Truth. Fulfill for me such and such a need. At this moment, at this moment,' and persist in what you desire.

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever performs ablution and perfects the ablution, and prays two Rak'at, completing their bowing and their prostrations, then sits and lauds Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and sends blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then asks Allah for his need, has indeed sought goodness in its habitats; and whoever seeks goodness in its habitats will not be unsuccessful.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Uthman Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Abdullah ibn Wazzah and Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ismail ibn al-Arqat and his mother Umm Salma, sister of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I fell ill in the month of Ramadan with a severe illness to the extent that I became heavy (bedridden), and the Banu Hashim gathered at night for the funeral, and they considered that I was dead, so my mother panicked over me. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to her: 'My aunt! Ascend to the top of the house, go out to the open sky, and pray two Rak'at. So when you have said the Taslim, say:' 'O Allah! You gave him to me when he was nothing. O Allah, and indeed I ask You to gift him to me anew, so lend him to me.' He said: So she did it, and I regained consciousness and sat up, and they called for Suhoor (pre-dawn meal) for them, which was Harisa (a dish of meat and grain). So they partook of the Suhoor with it, and I partook with them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the matter that a seeker seeks from his Lord, he said: 'Give charity during your day to sixty poor people; upon each poor person is one Sa' (measure), by the Sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So when he and his family). So when it is night, you bathe in the remaining third (of the night) and wear the least that one who has dependents wears from clothes, except that upon you, from those clothes, should be an izar (loincloth). Then you pray two Rak'at. So when you place your forehead in the final Rak'at for prostration, you extol Allah, magnify Him, glorify Him, and sanctify Him, and mention your sins, and acknowledge with what you recognize from them specifically, then you raise your head. Then when you place your head for the second prostration, you seek the choice of Allah one hundred times: 'O Allah, I seek Your choice.' Then you supplicate to Allah with whatever you wish, and ask Him of it; and every time you prostrate, expose your knees to the ground, then raise the loincloth so that you expose them, and place the loincloth behind you between your buttocks and the inner part of your shins.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you desire a need, pray two Rak'at, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and ask, and you will be given it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a woman entered upon him and mentioned that she had left her son, having placed a quilt over his face, saying he was dead. He said to her: 'Perhaps he did not die. So arise and go to your house, perform ghusl, pray two Rak'at, supplicate, and say: O the One Who endowed him to me when there was nothing, renew His endowment to me.' Then move him, and do not inform anyone of that.' She said: 'So I did it, and moved him, and behold, he was crying.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb al-Aqarquqi from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Ali (peace be upon him) was dismayed by something, he hastened to prayer. Then he recited this verse: And seek assistance through patience and prayer.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Take a prayer place in your house. So whenever you fear something, wear two thick garments from the thickest of your clothes, and pray in them. Then kneel on your knees, cry out to Allah, ask Him for Paradise, and seek refuge with Allah from the evil of that which you fear. And beware that Allah does not hear from you a word of rebellion, even if you are pleased with yourself and your clan.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! I am a man who has aged, and I have married a young virgin, and I have not yet entered upon her. I fear that when I enter upon her on my bed, she will dislike me due to my dye (hair color) and my old age.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you go in, instruct them before she comes to you that she should be in a state of wudu. Then you should not approach her until you have performed wudu and prayed two rak'at.' Then glorify Allah, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Then supplicate to Allah, and instruct those with her to say 'Ameen' to your supplication. And say: 'O Allah! Grant me her affection, her love, and her pleasure, and make me pleased with her. Then unite us with the best of unions and the most intimate of alliances, for You love the permissible and dislike the forbidden.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And know that affection (al-ilf) is from Allah, and separation (al-firk) is from Satan, so that he may make disliked that which Allah has permitted.'

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When one of you intends to marry, what does he do?' I said, 'I do not know.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he intends that, let him pray two Rak'at, and praise Allah, then let him say:' O Allah! I intend to marry, so ordain for me from the women the one who is most chaste in her private part, and most protective of me regarding herself and my wealth, and one of extensive sustenance, and the greatest of blessings; and ordain for me a good child, making him a righteous successor during my life and after my death.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who desires that he should have a pregnancy (offspring), let him pray two Rak'at after the Friday prayer, prolonging in them the bowing and prostration. Then he should say: O Allah! I ask You by what Zakariyya asked You when he said: My Lord! Do not leave me alone (without offspring), and You are the Best of inheritors. O Allah! Grant me a goodly offspring, surely You are the Hearer of the supplication. O Allah! By Your Name I have made her permissible (for intercourse), and in Your Trust I have taken her. So if You decree a child in her womb, then make it a boy, and do not make for the Satan any share or partnership in him.

They both said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is your view of the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Indeed the charities are only for the poor and the needy and those appointed over them and those whose hearts are to be reconciled and for (freeing) the slaves and the debtors and in the way of God and the wayfarer — an obligation from God.' Should all of these be given (the charity) even if one does not recognize (the Imam's authority)? He said: 'The Imam gives to all of them altogether, because they acknowledge obedience to him.' He (the narrator) said: I said: 'But if they do not recognize?' He said: 'O Zurara, if he were to give only to those who recognize, excluding those who do not recognize, there would be no place for it (the obligation). Rather, he gives to those who do not recognize so that they may incline toward the Religion and become steadfast upon it. But as for today, you and your companions must not give it except to the one who recognizes. So whoever among these Muslims you find who recognizes, give to him ahead of others.' Then he said: 'The share of those whose hearts incline and the share of the slaves is general, and the rest is specific.' He said: I said: 'What if they (the deserving recipients) cannot be found?' He said: 'It cannot be that an obligation which God Mighty and Majestic has obligated has no deserving recipient for it.' He said: I said: 'What if the charities are insufficient for them?' He said: 'Indeed God has prescribed for the poor, in the wealth of the rich, what suffices them; and had He known that it would not suffice them, He would have increased it for them. It (poverty) did not reach them from the direction of the obligation of God, but they were afflicted because of those who withheld their rights — not from what God had prescribed for them. And had people paid their rights, they (the poor) would all be living a good life.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the verse of zakat was revealed — 'Take charity out of their wealth to cleanse them and purify them thereby' [9:103] and it was revealed in the month of Ramadan. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered his herald, who called out among the people: 'God has imposed zakat upon you just as He has imposed salat upon you.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, imposed it upon them from gold and silver, and He imposed the charity from camels, cattle, sheep, wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. He called out among them with that during the month of Ramadan, and excused them from what was besides that. He said: Then He did not impose anything on their wealth until a year had passed over them from the next year. They fasted and broke their fast. So he ordered his herald, who called out among the Muslims: 'O Muslims! Purify your wealth — your prayers will be accepted!' He said: Then he dispatched the agents of the charity and the agents of the tax.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Rifa'a ibn Musa that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: God has not imposed upon this community anything more difficult upon them than zakat, and because of it the common folk among them perish.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan and more than one other, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — has ordained for the poor, within the wealth of the rich, what is sufficient for them; and had it not been for that, He would have increased it further for them. Rather, they are impoverished due to the withholding of those who withheld it from them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Buraid and Fuzayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) both having said: Indeed, Allah imposed zakat along with salat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Mubarak al-Aqarqufi, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, established zakat as a sustenance for the poor and as an increase for your wealth.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed zakat just as He imposed salat; and if a man were to carry the zakat and give it openly, there would be no fault upon him for that. And that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed in the wealth of the rich, for the poor, what would suffice the poor; and had He known that what He imposed for them would not suffice them, He would have increased it for them. And rather, the poor come into what they experience due to the withholding of those who withhold their rights from them — not due to the prescribed rate.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has imposed an obligation for the poor in the wealth of the rich — they will not be praised except by fulfilling it — and it is the zakat. By it their blood is protected, and by it they are named Muslims. But Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has imposed in the wealth of the rich rights other than zakat, for He (Mighty and Majestic) said: 'And those in whose wealth there is a known right' [70:24]. So the 'known right' is from other than the zakat, and it is something which the man imposes upon himself in his wealth. It is obligated upon him that he impose it upon himself according to his capacity and the extent of his wealth, and he pays what he imposed upon himself, if he wishes, every day, or if he wishes, every Friday, or if he wishes, every month. And Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has also said: 'and lend to Allah a goodly loan' [57:18], and this is other than the zakat. And Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has also said: 'and spend out of what We have given them secretly and openly' [14:31]. And al-ma'un (acts of kindness) as well: it is a loan one gives, a possession one lends, and an act of goodness one performs. And among what Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has also imposed in wealth other than zakat is His (Mighty and Majestic) saying: And whoever fulfills what Allah has imposed upon him has discharged what was due from him, and has rendered gratitude for what Allah has blessed him with in his wealth, when he praises Him for what Allah has blessed him with therein — for the capacity He has favored him with over others — and for having granted him success in fulfilling what Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has imposed upon him, and aided him in it.

We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and with us was an owner of wealth, and they mentioned the zakat, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The zakat is not something by which its payer is praised, and it is merely an outward thing — he has only preserved his blood by it and is called a Muslim by it, and had he not paid it, his salat would not have been accepted. And verily upon you, regarding your wealth, is other than the zakat.' So I said, 'May Allah set things right for you! And what is upon us regarding our wealth, other than the zakat?' So he said: 'Glory be to Allah! Do you not hear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying in His Book: And those in whose wealth there is a known right — for the one who asks and for the deprived?' I said, 'What is this known right that is upon us?' He said: 'It is something which a man does with his wealth — he gives it during the day, or during the week, or during the month, little or much — except that he is persistent in it.' And the words of the Mighty and Majestic: And they withhold the necessities of life. It is the loan which he extends, and the good deed which he performs, and the household chattels which he lends, and among these is the zakat. So I said to him: 'We have neighbors who, when we lend them household chattels, they break them and damage them. Is there blame upon us if we withhold from them?' So he said: 'No, there is no blame upon you if you withhold from them when they are like that.' He said: I said to him: '(What about the verse) And they give food out of love for Him to the poor, the orphan, and the captive?' He said: 'That is not from the zakat.' I said: 'The words of the Mighty and Majestic: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly?' He said: 'Not from the zakat.' He said: So I said: 'The words of the Mighty and Majestic: If you give alms openly, it is good, and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you?' He said: 'Not from the zakat, and your helping your relatives is not from the zakat.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Might and Majestic: 'And those in whose wealth is a known right, For the asker and the deprived.' 'Is it besides the Zakat?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the man whom Allah grants wealth from his possessions, so he gives from it a thousand, and two thousand, and three thousand, and the less and the more, so he connects with it his kin, and carries by it the burdens from his people.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Al-Qasim ibn Abdul Rahman Al-Ansari, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man came to my father Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'Inform me about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And those in whose wealth there is a known right. For the beggar and the deprived. The man said, 'So if it is not from the Zakat nor from the charity, what is it?' He said, 'It is something which the man takes out from his wealth; if he wishes, he gives more, and if he wishes, he gives less, according to what he possesses.' The man said to him, 'And what should he do with it?' He said, 'He uses it to maintain kinship, to feed a guest, to carry a burden, or to help a brother for the sake of Allah, or to repel a calamity that befalls him.' The man said, 'Allah knows best where He places His messages.'

And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Safwan Al-Jammal, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'For him who asks and for him who is denied.' He said: 'The denied one is the constrained one who is denied the toil of his hands regarding buying and selling.' And in another report, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that they said: 'The deprived is the man, there is nothing wrong with his intellect, but the livelihood is not extensive for him, and he is constrained.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and a man asked him regarding how much Zakat is obligated from the wealth. He said to him: 'Do you intend the apparent Zakat or the hidden Zakat?' He said, 'I intend both of them together.' He said: 'As for the apparent, it is twenty-five in every thousand, and as for the hidden, do not monopolize for yourself what your brother is more in need of than you are.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Aamir ibn Juza'ah, who said: A man came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O Abu Abdullah, give me a loan to be repaid when I am financially ease.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Until you realize a harvest?' The man said, 'No, by Allah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Then until your profit in a trade?' He said, 'No, by Allah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Then until a contract is fulfilled?' He said, 'No, by Allah.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'Thus, you are from those for whom Allah has made a right in our wealth.' Then he called for a bag containing dirhams, inserted his hand into it, and handed him a handful. Then he said to him, 'Fear Allah and do not be extravagant nor stingy, but be upright in between. Indeed, squandering is from extravagance.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And do not squander wastefully.' Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) — similar to that.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah and someone else, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from a man from the people of Sabata, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Ammar al-Sabati: 'O Ammar, you are a lord of much wealth?' He said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So do you pay what Allah has imposed upon you from the Zakat?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So you take out the known right from your wealth?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So you connect with your relatives?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And you connect with your brothers?' He said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ammar, indeed wealth perishes and the body wears out, and the deed remains, and the Judge is Living and will not die. O Ammar, whatever you send forward, it will not precede you, and whatever you delay, it will not join you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Charities are only for the poor and the needy".' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The poor is the one who does not ask the people, and the needy is more straitened than him, and the wretched is the most straitened of them.' Thus, everything that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has imposed upon you, its public (giving) is superior to its secretive (giving), and everything that is voluntary, its secretive (giving) is superior to its public (giving). And even if a man were to carry the zakat of his wealth upon his shoulder and distribute it publicly, that would be good and beautiful.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if you disclose your charitable expenditures, it is good; and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is besides the Zakat. Indeed, the giving of Zakat is public, not secret.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he was asked about the poor and the needy, so he said: The poor is the one who does not ask, and the needy is the one who is more straitened than him, the one who asks.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I mentioned something to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Be patient, for I hope that Allah will do something for you, if Allah wills.' Then he said: 'By Allah, Allah does not delay from the believer in this world any good that He hastens for him in it.' Then he belittled the world and said: 'What is it?' Then he said: 'The possessor of bounty is in danger, for it is obligatory upon him the rights of Allah in it. By Allah, if bounty comes upon me from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, I do not cease to be apprehensive about it, and he moved his hand until I take out the rights that are obligatory for Allah upon me regarding it.' So I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, you are in your capacity and you fear this?' He said: 'Yes, so I praise my Lord for what He has favored me with.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the ornaments; is there Zakat upon them? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the ornaments, 'Is there Zakat regarding it?' He said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ornaments, 'Should I purify (pay Zakat)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Then there would not remain anything from it'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and one of them asked him about the ornaments, whether there is Zakat upon it. He said: No, even if it reached one hundred thousand.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the wealth which is not worked with (in business) nor is it changed over. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The zakat is imposed upon it every year, except if it is cast (into a single mass/coin).'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The zakat of the ornaments is its lending it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Harun ibn Kharja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'My brother Yusuf was appointed as a custodian for these people, and in that capacity he acquired much wealth. He made that wealth into ornaments, intending to flee from the zakat. Is there zakat upon it?' He said, 'There is no zakat upon the ornaments, and whatever loss he incurred upon himself by wearing them and preventing himself from their merit is greater than what he fears from the zakat.'

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I said to him, 'Something has accumulated in my possession and remains for about a year; should I purify it (pay Zakat)?' He said, 'No. Everything upon which a year has not passed in your possession has no Zakat due on it; and everything that is not a mineral (rikaz), there is nothing upon you regarding it.' He (the narrator) said, 'And what is the mineral?' He said, 'The silent carved [ornaments].' Then he said, 'When you intend that, melt it, for there is no Zakat in the melting of gold and the carving of silver.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from one of our companions, that he said: There is no Zakat upon the gold dust (tibrs), but rather it is upon the Dinars and the Dirhams.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Bukayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Zakat in the jewels and their like, even if they are numerous.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Sadeer Al-Sayrafi, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who had wealth, so he took it and buried it in a place. When a year passed over it, he went to take it out from its place, so he dug the place in which he thought the wealth was buried, but did not find it. So he remained like that for three years. Then he dug the place from all its sides, and he came across the wealth with his own eyes. How should he purify it (pay Zakat)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should purify it for one year, because it was absent from him, even if he had withheld it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man whose wealth was hidden from him for five years, then it came to him, so he did not reject the capital wealth. How much should he purify (pay Zakat on)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'One year'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Durust, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Zakat on the debt, except if it is the owner of the debt who is delaying it; so if he is not able to take it, there is no Zakat upon it until he takes possession of it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt upon people, and the zakat is withheld in it. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no zakat upon him regarding it until he takes possession of it. So when he takes possession of it, then upon him is the zakat. And if its withholding is prolonged by the people until complete years pass, so there is no zakat upon him until it comes out (to him). So when it comes out, he pays the zakat for that year of his. And if he was taking from it little by little, let him purify (pay zakat) what comes out from it first, then first. And if his chattels, and his debts, and his wealth are in his business in which he moves day by day, taking and giving, selling and buying, so it is like the principal in his hand, so upon him is the zakat. And it is not befitting for him to change that when the state of his chattels and his wealth is upon what I have described to you, so he delays the zakat.

Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who borrowed wealth, and a year passed over it while it was in his possession, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who lent it to him pays its zakat, then there is no zakat upon him; and if he does not pay, the borrower pays.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man gave wealth to another man as a loan, with a stipulation that the zakat is upon the lender or the borrower. He (peace be upon him) said: No, but its zakat is upon the borrower, provided it remains with him for a full year. I said: So there is no zakat upon the lender? He (peace be upon him) said: The wealth is not purified (zakkat) from two aspects in one year. And there is nothing upon the one handing it over, because there is nothing in his hand; rather, the wealth is in the hand of the one who took it. So whoever has the wealth in his hand, he purifies it. I said: So does he purify the wealth of another from his own wealth? He (peace be upon him) said: It is his wealth as long as it is in his hand, and that wealth is not for anyone other than him. Then he (peace be upon him) said: O Zurara! What do you see regarding the loss of that wealth and its profit? For whom is it and upon whom? I said: For the borrower. He (peace be upon him) said: So for him is the excess, and upon him is the deficiency, and for him is that he marries, wears from it, and eats from it. And it is not befitting for him that he purifies it (as a gift), but he must purify it, for it is upon him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who has a debt upon him and in his hand is wealth belonging to others. Is Zakat upon him? He said: If it is a loan, and a year passes over it, then he should purify it (pay Zakat).

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdul Hamid ibn Sa'd, said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who sold goods on credit for three years from a wealthy man, whose right and wealth are trusted. Would he purify that wealth every year that passes by, or would he purify it when he takes it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he purifies it when he takes it.' I said to him: 'For how long does he purify it?' He said: 'For three years.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who informed him, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt upon him, and in his hand is wealth to pay off his debt, and the wealth belongs to someone else. Is there Zakat upon it? He (peace be upon him) said: When he borrows and a year passes over it, so the Zakat is upon him, if there is an excess in it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If there is a deposit with you and you move (use) it, so upon you is the Zakat. But if you do not move (use) it, so there is nothing upon you.

Not one of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I wrote to him asking him about a man upon whom is the dower of his wife, which she does not seek from him, either out of kindness to her husband or out of shyness. He wrote: Zakat is not obligatory upon him except in his wealth.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who forgets or assists (the borrower) and his wealth does not cease to remain as outstanding debts. How should he deal with his Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should purify it (pay Zakat), and he would not pay for what is upon him from the debts. But rather, the Zakat is upon the owner of the wealth'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Zurra from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they both said: Any man who has wealth placed (saved) until a year passes over it, then he must purify it (pay Zakat); and even if there is debt upon him equal to it or more than it, let him purify (pay Zakat) on what is in his hand.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Is there a known time for the Zakat to be given during it?' So he said: 'That differs based on when the man attains the wealth; and as for Al-Fitra, its time is known.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'My zakat becomes due upon me in a specific month. Is it permissible for me to withhold a portion of it, fearing that someone may come to me asking for it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the year passes, then extract it from your wealth, do not mix it with anything, then give it however you wish.' He (the narrator) said: I said, 'And if I write it down and establish it as correct for me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It will not harm you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked about the man upon whom zakat becomes due during the year at three times: does he delay it until he pays it at one time? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it becomes due, he should extract it.' And regarding zakat on wheat, barley, dates, and raisins: when does it become obligatory upon its owner? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he harvests it, and when he evaluates it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man whose half of his wealth is in cash (ayn) and half is in debts (dayn), so Zakat becomes due upon him. He said: 'He should pay Zakat on the cash and leave the debt.' I said: 'What if he collects it after six months?' He said: 'He should pay Zakat on it when he collects it.' I said: 'What if a year passes for him and the month in which he usually pays Zakat arrives, and for half his wealth a year has passed, and for the other half six months have passed?' He said: 'He should pay Zakat on that upon which a year has passed, and leave the other until a year passes for it.' I said: 'What if he desires to pay Zakat on that (the other half) as well?' He said: 'How good that is!'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who pays his Zakat, so he distributes some of it and keeps some of it, seeking the place for it, and it remains from its beginning to its end for three months, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'If a man has wealth in his possession, can he purify it (pay Zakat) when half the year has passed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but [one must wait] until the year passes over it and it becomes due upon him. Indeed, it is not for anyone to pray Salat except at its appointed time, and similarly is Zakat; and no one can Fast for the month of Ramadan except during its month, except for making up missed fasts; and every obligation is only rendered when it becomes due.'

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Can a man purify his wealth when a third of the year has passed?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No. Can one pray the first (noon) prayer before midday?' And it has been reported as well that he allowed it when the recipient is suitable for the zakat, that he can hasten it for him before the due time for zakat, except that he would be responsible for it when the due time for zakat comes and the recipient has become affluent or turned apostate; he would have to repeat the zakat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father sold a piece of land to Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik for money, and he stipulated in the sale that he would pay the zakat on this money from himself for six years.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father sold a piece of land belonging to Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik for such and such thousand dinars, and he stipulated upon him the zakat of that wealth for ten years, and he did that only because Hisham was the governor.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who has children, and one of his children is absent, and he does not know where he is, and the man dies. So how is the inheritance of the absent one from his father handled? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is set aside (isolated) until he comes.' I said: 'So, upon his wealth is Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until he comes.' I said: 'So when he comes, does he pay Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until a year passes over it while it is in his hand.'

And by this chain, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who benefits from wealth, he said: 'He does not purify it (pay Zakat) until a year passes over it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had wealth deposited, and when it was near the head of the year, he spent it before the year passed over it. Is Zakat upon him? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who inherited wealth while the man was absent; is Zakat upon him? He said: No, until he arrives. I said: Does he purify it when he arrives? He said: No, until a year has passed over it and it is in his possession.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from Shu'ayb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Every thing from which wealth flows upon you, so purify it (pay Zakat), and every thing you inherit or is gifted to you, so face the next year with it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, from Yunus, from Abdul Hameed ibn Awwaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who has wealth with him, and a year passes over it, then he acquires other wealth before a year passes over the first wealth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When a year passes over the first wealth, he should pay zakat on both of them together.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bought goods, so the goods became unsalable upon him, and he had already paid the zakat of his wealth before purchasing them with it. Is there zakat upon him, or (does he wait) until he sells it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he withheld it in order to seek the profit (price rise) upon the capital, then upon him is the zakat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought goods and they became un-saleable upon him, and he had already paid Zakat on his wealth before buying the goods. When should he pay Zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: If he withheld his goods seeking to recover his capital wealth, then there is no Zakat upon it; and if he withheld it after he had recovered the capital of his wealth, then upon him is the Zakat after he had withheld it after (the recovery) of the capital wealth. He (the narrator) said, And I asked him about the man who has deposits of wealth with him to work with these. So he (peace be upon him) said: When the year passes by, let him pay Zakat on it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has goods with him as deposits, which remain with him for a year, two years, or more than that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Zakat upon him until he sells it, unless he was given it as his capital wealth, so he withholds it seeking profit (price increase). So when he does that, Zakat becomes obligatory upon it; but if he was not given it as his capital wealth, there is no Zakat upon him until he sells it; and if he withholds it for whatever reason he withholds it, then when he sells it, upon him is only the Zakat of one year.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, that he said: Every wealth with which you trade, upon you is the Zakat regarding it when the year passes by over it. Yunus said, The interpretation of that is that everything which is worked for trade from animals and other than them, upon him is the Zakat regarding it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad bin Isa, from Is'haq bin Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'A man buys a maid-servant, keeps her with him so that her value increases, and he intends to sell her. Is there Zakat upon her price?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until he sells her.' I said, 'So when he sells her, should he purify (pay Zakat) on her price?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until the year passes over it, and it (the price) is still in his hands.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj al-Karkhi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Zakat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever trading asset is in your hand where there is a profit, and nothing prevents you from selling it except that you seek to increase your profit (by holding it), then purify it (pay Zakat). And whatever trading asset is in your hand where there is a loss, that is another matter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not take wealth for trade (mudarabah) except wealth upon which you pay zakat or its owner pays zakat. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If there are goods with you in the house, stored away, and you are given capital for them, but you turn away from selling them, then upon you is their zakat.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abdul Khaliq, who said: Saeed al-A'raj asked him (peace be upon him) and I was listening, and he said: 'We press the oil and the butter, seeking trade with it. So sometimes it remains with us for the year and the two years. Is there Zakat upon it?' He said: 'If you profit something in it, or if you find the capital of your wealth (intact), then upon you is its Zakat. And if you are merely waiting with it because you find nothing but a loss, then there is no Zakat upon you until it becomes gold or silver. So when it becomes gold or silver, then purify it (pay Zakat) for the year in which you traded in it.'

Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is there anything (zakat) upon the mules?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. So I said, 'So how did it come to be upon the horses and not upon the mules?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because the mules do not reproduce, and the female horses give birth, and there is nothing upon the male horses'. He said, 'So I said, 'So what is regarding the donkeys?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing with regards to them'. I said, 'Is there anything upon the horse, or the camel which the man happens to be riding upon?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, there is nothing upon what is fed (not grazing). Rather, the charity (zakat) is upon the grazing animal sent out in its pasture during its year which the man acquired. But, as for what is besides that, so there is nothing with regards to it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Zakat upon the slave except the slave acquired for trade, for he is from the wealth upon which Zakat is paid.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that both were asked about what is regarding the slaves. So they both said: 'There is nothing upon the head [of the slave] anything more than a Sa'a of dates, when the year passes by upon him; and there is nothing upon his price until the year passes by over it'.

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man did not purify (pay zakat on) his camels or his sheep for two years, then he sold them on condition that the buyer would purify them for what has passed. He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, its zakat is taken from him, and the seller pursues it with him, or the seller pays its zakat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) did not take anything from young camels until a year passed over them, and he did not take charity from working camels, and it was as if it was not obligatory to take anything from the males because they are beasts of burden.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd al-Ijaly, and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both), who said: Regarding the charity (Zakat) of camels: in every five, one sheep, until it reaches twenty-five. So when it reaches that, then regarding it is a Bint Makhad (a one-year-old female camel). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches thirty-five. So when it reaches thirty-five, then regarding it is a Bint Labun (a two-year-old female camel). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches forty-five. So when it reaches forty-five, then regarding it is a Hiqqah Taruqat al-Fahl (a three-year-old female camel left with the stallion). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches sixty. So when it reaches sixty, then regarding it is a Jadh'ah (a four-year-old female camel). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches seventy-five. So when it reaches seventy-five, then regarding it are two Bintay Labun (two two-year-old female camels). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches ninety. So when it reaches ninety, then regarding it are two Hiqqatay Taruqata al-Fahl (two three-year-old female camels left with the stallion). Then there is nothing regarding it until it reaches one hundred and twenty. So when it reaches one hundred and twenty, then regarding it are two Hiqqatay Taruqata al-Fahl (two three-year-old female camels left with the stallion). So when one increases upon one hundred and twenty, then regarding every fifty is a Hiqqah (three-year-old female camel), and regarding every forty is a Bint Labun (two-year-old female camel). Then the camels return to their ages (the cycle repeats). And there is nothing upon the 'Nayyif' (the extra ten in a round number like 130, 140, etc.), and there is nothing upon the fractions (remainders less than the threshold), and there is nothing upon the working camels. Rather, that is upon the Saimah al-Ra'iyah (the grazing herd). He said: I said, 'Is there anything regarding the Bukt al-Saimah (the mixed-breed grazing camels)?' He said: 'Similar to what is regarding the Arabian camels.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding five young camels (qala'is) is one sheep, and there is nothing regarding less than five; and regarding ten are two sheep, and regarding fifteen are three sheep, and regarding twenty are four (sheep), and regarding twenty-five are five (sheep), and regarding twenty-six is a Bint Makhad (a young female camel in its fourth year) up to thirty-five. And Abd al-Rahman said, 'This is a difference between us and the people. So when it is increased by one, so regarding these would be a Bint Labun (a young female camel in its fifth year) up to forty-five. So when it is increased by one, so regarding these would be a Hiqqah (a mature female camel in its sixth year) up to sixty. So when it increases by one, so regarding these would be a Jadh'ah (a young female camel in its seventh year) up to seventy-five. So when it increases by one, so regarding these would be two Bint Labun up to ninety. So when there are more camels, so regarding every fifty would be a Hiqqah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no khums (or zakat) in young camels until a full year passes over them from the day they are born.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'They shall have what they were miserly with collared around their necks on the Day of Resurrection.' So he said: 'O Muhammad! There is no one who withholds anything from the Zakat of his wealth except that God, Mighty and Majestic, will make that, on the Day of Resurrection, a serpent of fire encircling his neck, gnawing at his flesh until he is freed from the Reckoning.' Then he said: 'It is the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: They shall have what they were miserly with collared around their necks on the Day of Resurrection — meaning what they were miserly with of the Zakat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, raising it from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: While the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was in the mosque, he suddenly said: Stand up, O so-and-so! Stand up, O so-and-so! Stand up, O so-and-so! — until he had expelled five persons. Then he said: Get out from our mosque — do not pray in it while you are not giving zakat.

Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever withholds a carat of zakat is neither a believer nor a Muslim. And this is [the meaning of] His saying — Mighty and Majestic: [23:99] 'My Lord, send me back [23:100] perhaps I may do righteous deeds which I had neglected.' And in another narration: 'His salat will not be accepted.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is none who owns wealth subject to zakat — palm trees, or farmland, or a vineyard — who withholds the zakat of his wealth, except that Allah will collar him with the soil of his land, to be encircled by it from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.'

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Two bloods in Islam are permissible by Allah — none shall execute judgment regarding them until Allah sends our Qa'im of the Ahlulbayt. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends our Qa'im of the Ahlulbayt, he will judge regarding them both with Allah's judgment, requiring no proof against them: the married adulterer — he will stone him; and the withholder of zakat — he will strike his neck.' A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashshab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh ibn Thabit, from 'Amr ibn Jami', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no man who pays the zakat such that it decreases from his wealth, nor does anyone withhold it such that it increases in his wealth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no servant who withholds a dirham from its rightful (spending) except that he will spend two in other than its rightful place; and there is no man who withholds a right from his wealth except that God Mighty and Majestic will collar him with a snake of fire on the Day of Resurrection.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Accursed! Accursed is the wealth from which zakat has not been paid.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — meaning the First — who said: I heard him saying: 'Whoever pays the zakat on his wealth completely and places it in its (appropriate) place will not be asked on the Day of Judgment from where he earned his wealth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mihran, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, They shall have what they were niggardly of to cleave to their necks on the Day of Judgement He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is none from a servant who prevents anything from the Zakat of his wealth except that Allah, on the Day of Judgement, would Make that to be a serpent of Fire in his neck, eroding his flesh, until he is free from the Reckoning; and these are the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: They shall have what they were niggardly of to cleave to their necks on the Day of Judgement.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What they were niggardly with, from the Zakat.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who withholds the zakat will ask for return at the time of death,' and this is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: A prescribed prayer is better than twenty Hajjs, and a Hajj is better than a house filled with gold spent in righteousness until it is depleted. He said, then he said: 'And there is no success for the one who wastes twenty houses of gold for twenty-five dirhams.' So I said, 'What is the meaning of twenty-five dirhams?' He said: 'The one who withholds the Zakat, his prayer is paused until he purifies it (pays the Zakat).'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Accursed! Accursed is the wealth from which Zakat is not paid.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from the one who mentioned it, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever withholds a Qirat of the Zakat, let him die if he wills a Jew or a Christian.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ayoub ibn Rashid, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The one who withholds the Zakat will be collared with a bald snake, and it will eat from his brain. And that is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'They shall have what they were niggardly of to cleave to their necks on the Day of Judgement.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the Zakat is prevented, the earth is prevented from its blessings.'

Abu Abdillah al-Asimiy, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his father Asbaat ibn Salim, from Salim, the mawla of Aban, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no bird that is hunted except by its neglecting the glorification (tasbih), and there is no wealth that is lost/wasted except by its neglecting the zakat.'
