Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Hariz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no one possessing wealth of gold or silver who withholds its zakat, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will detain him on the Day of Resurrection in a stony valley, and will send against him a hornless serpent that seeks him, while he flees from it. So when it sees that he has no escape from it, it will overpower him, seize him with its hand, and bite him as one bites a radish. They shall have what they were niggardly of to cleave to their necks on the Day of Judgement And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And there is no one possessing wealth of camels or sheep or cattle who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will detain him on the Day of Resurrection in a stony valley, wherein he will be trampled by every hoofed animal with its hooves, and torn by every toothed animal with its teeth. And there is no one possessing wealth of dates or vines or crops who withholds its zakat, except that Allah will collar him with the produce of his land, stretching from the earth up to the seventh earth, until the Day of Resurrection.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah, from his father (peace be upon him), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A servant does not withhold Zakat, so it increases in his wealth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who prevents a Right of Allah (Mighty and Majestic) would spend double the like of it in falsehood (the wrong way).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will resurrect a group of people from their graves on the Day of Resurrection with their hands tied to their necks, unable to reach even the width of a fingernail with them. With them will be angels taunting them with severe taunt, saying: 'These are the ones who withheld a little good from a lot of good! These are the ones whom Allah gave, but they withheld the right of Allah in their wealth.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Uthman ibn Rushayd, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbouz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, paired the Zakat with the Salat, so He said: 'Establish the Salat and give the Zakat.' Thus, the one who establishes the Salat and does not give the Zakat has not established the Salat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd al-Ijli, and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the cows: in every thirty cows, one Tabi' (one-year-old cow) is due, and there is nothing due for less than that; and in forty cows, one Musinnah (two-year-old cow) is due, and there is nothing due for what is between thirty and forty until it reaches forty. So when it reaches forty, then in it is one Musinnah, and there is nothing due for what is between forty and sixty. So when it reaches sixty, then in it are two Tabi' up to seventy. So when it reaches seventy, then in it is one Tabi' and one Musinnah up to eighty. So when it reaches eighty, then in every forty is one Musinnah up to ninety. So when it reaches ninety, then in it are three Tabi' (one-year-olds). So when it reaches one hundred and twenty, then in every forty is one Musinnah. Then the cows are accounted for according to their ages. And there is nothing due on the 'Nayyif' (extra ten), nor on the fractions, nor on the 'Awilah' (working cows). Indeed, the Zakat is on the grazing herd. And whatever has not completed a year in the possession of its owner, there is nothing due upon it until the year passes over it. So when the year passes over it, it becomes obligatory upon it.
Zurara narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'Is there anything [regarding] the buffaloes?' He said: 'Similar to what is [regarding] the cows.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd, and Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the sheep: for every forty sheep, one sheep is due, and there is nothing due for what is below forty. Then there is nothing due until it reaches one hundred and twenty; when it reaches one hundred and twenty, one sheep is due in the same manner. When it exceeds one hundred and twenty, two sheep are due. There is nothing more than two sheep until it reaches two hundred; when it reaches two hundred, it is due in the same manner. When it exceeds two hundred by one sheep, three sheep are due. Then there is nothing more than that until it reaches three hundred; when it reaches three hundred, three sheep are due. When it increases by one, four sheep are due until it reaches four hundred. When four hundred is complete, one sheep is due for every hundred, and the previous rule is dropped. There is nothing due for what is below one hundred after that, and there is nothing due for the 'nayyif' (the surplus between the hundreds). And they both said: For everything upon which the year has not passed while it is with its owner, there is nothing due. When the year passes over it, it becomes obligatory.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The charity (Zakat) is not due upon the fed ones, nor upon the nourisher, and the nourisher is that which feeds two, nor upon a milking sheep, nor upon the stallion of the sheep.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: An 'Akulah' is not taken, and the 'Akulah' is the large/old one from the ewes among the sheep, nor its mother, nor the stallion ram.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When does the charity (Zakat) become obligatory upon the lamb?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is a year old (has its teeth cut/grown).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the wealth of the orphan, is there Zakat upon it? He said: When it is a deposit, there is no Zakat upon it, and when you work with it, you are responsible (guarantor) for it, and the profit is for the orphan.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan and Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Is'haq ibn Ammar from Abu al-Atarid al-Khayyat who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The wealth of the orphan is in my possession, so can I trade with it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When you move it, zakat is upon you.' He said, 'I said, 'What if I move it for eight months and leave it for four months?'' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Zakat is upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is there Zakat upon the wealth of the orphan?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless it is traded with or worked with.'

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, both having said: There is nothing upon the wealth of the orphan regarding the debt and the silent wealth (immovable assets); but as for the produce (crops/gains), upon it is the obligatory charity (Zakat).

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I sent a message to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). That I have young brothers, so when does Zakat become obligatory upon their wealth? He (peace be upon him) said: When Salat becomes obligatory upon them, Zakat becomes obligatory. I said: So what about those upon whom Salat is not obligatory? He (peace be upon him) said: When they are traded with (i.e., their wealth is used in commerce), then purify it (pay Zakat).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about the trustee: 'Would he pay the Zakat al-Fitr on behalf of the orphans if they have wealth?' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'There is no Zakat upon an orphan.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is nothing (due) in the wealth of the owned slave, and even if he had a thousand thousand, and even if he was in need, he would not be given anything from the Zakat.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman from our family is mixed up (insane/confused); is there Zakat upon her?' He said: 'If it was worked with (i.e., her wealth was utilized/managed), then Zakat is upon her, and if it was not worked with, then no.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Musa ibn, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who is possessed (by insanity or minority), and she has wealth in the hand of her brother. Is Zakat upon him? He said: If her brother trades with it, then Zakat is upon him.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abd Salih (peace be upon him) similar to it

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Zakat regarding the wealth of the contracted slave.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'An owned slave has wealth in his hands; is Zakat upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said, 'And not upon his master?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. It is what he did not give to his master, and it is not for the owned slave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Suleman ibn Khalid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The companions of my father came to him and asked him about what the Sultan takes, to differentiate for them. And he knew that Zakat is not permissible except for its deserving ones, so he ordered them to reckon with it (as being Zakat). So my thought wandered about them, and by Allah, I said to him: O my father! If they were to hear it, then none of them would pay Zakat.' So he said: O my son! Allah loves a right to be manifested.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the tenth (ushr) which is taken from the man, 'Can one reckon with it to be from his zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he so desires.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who inherits land or buys it, and he pays its kharaj (land tax) to the Sultan; is there a 'ushr (tithe) upon it? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn Al-Qasim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding Zakat, he said: 'Whatever the Banu Umayya take from you, count it as Zakat, and do not give them anything more than what you can manage, for wealth would not remain in this state if you were to pay Zakat twice.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Malik, from Abu Qatada, from Sahl ibn al-Yasa' that when Sahl established Sahlabad, he asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about what was to be taken from it, what was obligated upon him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the Sultan takes its tax (kharaj), then there is nothing upon you; and if the Sultan does not take anything from it, then upon you is the payment of the tenth (ushr) of whatever is in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: Whatever the tenth-part collector takes from you and throws into a jug, it is from your zakat; and whatever he does not throw into the jug, do not reckon it as your zakat.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man left behind with him: A man left behind with his family an expense of two thousand, for two years, upon which is Zakat. He said: If he was present, then upon him is Zakat, and if he was absent, then there is no Zakat upon it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who placed a thousand dirhams for his dependents as expense money, and a year passed upon it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was staying, it is subject to Zakat, and if he was absent, it is not subject to Zakat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man leaves behind for his family three thousand dirhams as expenses for two years. Is Zakat due upon it?' He said, 'If he was present, then Zakat is due upon it, and if he was absent, then there is nothing in it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who gives the zakat of his wealth to a man and he considers him to be financially straitened, but he finds him to be affluent, he said: It is not sufficient for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ibrahim, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who hastened to give the zakat of his wealth, then the recipient became affluent before the end of the year, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The giver must repeat the zakat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu al-Maghra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made the rich and the poor partners in the wealth; therefore, it is not for them to direct it to other than their partners.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Bukayr and Al-Fudayl and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Buraed al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the two said: Regarding the man who is among one of these sects/followers of personal desires – the Haruriyya, and the Murji'ah, and the Uthmaniyya, and the Qadariyya – then he repents and recognizes this matter (Wilayah) and improves his view: Does he have to repeat every Salat he prayed, or Sawm, or Zakat, or Hajj, or is there no repeating upon him of anything from that? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no repeating upon him of anything from that, other than the Zakat. It is inevitable that he pays it, because he placed the Zakat in a place other than its proper place, and rather, its proper place is the people of Wilayah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no man who withholds a dirham of a right except that he spends two [dirhams] in what is not its right; and there is no man who withholds a right in his wealth except that Allah collars him with it, a snake of fire, on the Day of Resurrection.' He said: I said to him, 'A man who is knowledgeable paid his Zakat to other than its rightful recipients for a period. Is it upon him to pay it a second time to its rightful recipients when he knows them?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: I said, 'And if he did not know its rightful recipients so he did not pay it, or he did not know that it was upon him, and then he learned of that?' He said: 'He should pay it to its rightful recipients for what has passed.' He said: I said to him, 'Suppose he did not know its rightful recipients, so he gave it to one who was not deserving of it, and he had sought and exerted himself, then he learned afterwards the evil of what he had done.' He said: 'It is not upon him to pay it another time.' And from Zurara, similar to it, except that he said: 'If he exerted himself, then he is blameless; and if he was deficient in the exertion regarding the seeking, then no.'

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, charity and alms-tax are not given preferentially to the near (kin), nor are they prevented from the remote (non-kin).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the zakat, 'Can it be placed among those who do not recognize (wilayah)?' He said: 'No, nor the zakat of al-fitra.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Abbad ibn Suheib from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who was negligent in paying his zakat during his lifetime. So when death approached him, he calculated all that he had been negligent about from the zakat that was obligatory upon him, then he bequeathed that it be paid out and given to the one it is due to. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible; that is paid out from all the wealth. It is merely in the status of a debt, if it were upon him. The inheritors have nothing until they pay what he bequeathed from the zakat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man did not purify his wealth (pay Zakat), so his Zakat was taken at the time of his death and paid. Would that suffice for him?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And if he bequeathed a bequest from his third, and Zakat had not been paid on it, would it suffice for him from his Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes. Zakat is reckoned for him, and no optional (Zakat) is upon him, and upon him is the obligatory (Zakat).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Shu'ayb, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'There is a lot of Zakat upon my brother, so can I pay it off or fulfill it on his behalf?' He said to me, 'And how is it for you with that?' I said, 'Precaution (Ihtitat).' He said, 'Yes, then you relieve it from him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): A man dies and upon him is five hundred dirhams of Zakat, and upon him is the Hajj of Islam, and he leaves three hundred dirhams. So he bequeaths with the Hajj of Islam, and that the debt of Zakat be fulfilled from him. He (peace be upon him) said: Hajj is performed on his behalf from the nearest [portion], and the remainder is given for the Zakat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first: 'A man died, and upon him is Zakat, and he bequeathed that the Zakat be fulfilled from him, and his children are needy. If they pay it, that would be extremely harmful to them.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They should pay it, and then return it to themselves, and take something out from it and give it to others.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'For what reason did God make the zakat twenty-five in every thousand, and why did He not make it thirty?' So he said: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, made it twenty-five — taken from the wealth of the rich in the measure of what suffices the poor. And if people were to pay out the zakat from their wealth, no one would be needy.'

Abu Ja'far al-Mansur wrote to Muhammad ibn Khalid — who was his governor over Medina — that he should ask the people of Medina about the five from two hundred in zakat, how it came to be the weight of seven, and this was not the case in the era of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). He instructed him that among those he asks should be Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: He asked the people of Medina, and they said: 'We found those who were before us upon this.' So he sent for Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He asked Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and he said the same as the jurists of the people of Medina. Then he said: 'What do you say, O Abu Abdillah?' He said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) assigned one uqiyya in every forty uqiyyas. When you calculate that, it comes out to the weight of seven — and it had been the weight of six, and the dirham was five dawaniqs.' Habib said: We calculated it and found it to be exactly as he had said. So Abdullah ibn al-Hasan turned to him and said: 'From where did you take this?' He said: 'I read it in the Book of your mother Fatima.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent back: 'I only informed you that I had read it; I did not inform you that it is with me.' Habib said: Muhammad ibn Khalid kept saying to me, 'I have never seen the likes of this!'

Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Sabbah al-Hazza', from Qutham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me about zakat — how did it come to be twenty-five from every thousand, not less or more? What is its rationale?' So he said: 'Verily, God, Mighty and Majestic, created all of creation and knew their young and their old, their rich and their poor. So He made twenty-five poor people out of every thousand human beings. And had He known that would be insufficient for them, He would have increased it for them, because He is their Creator and He is most knowing of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal who said: A man from the atheists asked me, saying, 'How did the zakat come to be twenty-five dirhams from every thousand?' So I said to him, 'Indeed that is like the salat — three [units], and two, and four.' He accepted it from me. Then I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) after that. So I asked him about that, and he said: 'Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, calculated the wealth and the poor, and He found what would suffice them to be twenty-five from every thousand, and if that had not sufficed them, He would have increased it for them.' He said: So I returned to him and informed him, and he said, 'This question came on a camel from the Hijaz.' Then he said, 'If I were to give obedience to anyone, I would give it to the master of this speech.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: No one shall be given less than five dirhams from the zakat, and it is the least amount that Allah, Exalted and Majestic, prescribed for the zakat in the wealth of the Muslims. Therefore, do not give anyone from the zakat less than five dirhams, and upwards.

And from him, from Ahmad, from Abdul Malik bin Utba, from Is'haq bin Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can one give a man eighty dirhams from the zakat?' He said, 'Yes, and increase it.' I said, 'Can I give him a hundred?' He said, 'Yes, and enrich him, if you are able to enrich him.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked, 'How much is given to the man from the Zakat?' He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you give, enrich him.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Saeed ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You give him from the zakat until you enrich him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man dies and leaves dependents. Are they given from the Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, until they grow up and reach adulthood, and can ask, from where would they be living when that is cut off from them.' So I said, 'They do not know (the Wilayah/Religion).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Their deceased [father] should be preserved among them, and the Religion of their father should be made beloved to them, so they will not long before they pay attention to their father's Religion. So when they reach adulthood and turn to others, then do not give to them.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man, knowledgeable and meritorious, who died and left upon him a debt that he had been afflicted with, which was not due to corruption, nor extravagance, nor was he known for begging. Would the thousand and the two thousand be paid off on his behalf from the Zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassha from Ahmad ibn A'iz from Abu Khadija from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The offspring of a Muslim man, when he dies, are given from the zakat and the fitra, just as their father was given, until they reach adulthood. So when they reach adulthood and recognize what their father recognized, they are given; and if they become Nasibi (Hostile Ones), they are not given.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ubayda ibn Abdullah ibn Ajlan al-Sakuni, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I distribute something among my companions to maintain good relations with them by it, so how should I give to them?' He said, 'Give to them based on their emigration in the Religion, and their intellect, and their jurisprudence.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all together, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the zakat: 'Is it preferable to give to some of those who do not ask, over others?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the one who does not ask is preferable to the one who asks.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man gives a thousand dirhams from the zakat, so he distributes it, and he discusses with himself that he should give it to a man from it, then he changes his mind about him and isolates him and gives it to someone else. He said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who takes a thing to the man, then he changes his mind for him, so he makes it to be for someone else. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘There is no problem’.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from those whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) About a man who takes something for a man, then it becomes clear to him (or he changes his mind), so he gives it to someone else, he said: There is no harm.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I have near relatives upon whom I spend, and I prefer some of them over others. When the time for Zakat comes, should I give them from it?' He said, 'Are they deserving of it?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'They are superior to the others, so give them.' I said, 'So who is it that is obligatory upon me from my near relatives, such that I do not count Zakat upon them?' He said, 'Your father and your mother.' I said, 'My father and my mother?' He said, 'The two parents and the children.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musanna, from Abu Baseer, who said: A man asked him (peace be upon him) and I was listening. He said: 'Can I give the zakat of my wealth to my relatives while they do not recognize (the Wilayah)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not give the zakat except to a Muslim (who recognizes the Wilayah), and give them from your wealth other than the zakat.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you think that only the zakat is in the wealth? What Allah has imposed in the wealth other than the zakat is more. You give from it to the relatives and the objectors among those who ask you, so you give to them as long as you do not recognize them as Nasibi (hostile). So when you recognize them as Nasibi, do not give to them except if you fear their tongue, so you buy your religion and your honor from them.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who has relatives, clients, and followers who love the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), but they do not know the Master of this Command (the Imam). Should they be given from the Zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man has zakat due from him, and he has needy relatives who are not familiar (with Wilayah). Can he give them from the zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and there is no prestige. He should not make the zakat a preservation for his wealth. He can give them from other than the zakat if he wishes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Five people are not given anything from the Zakat: the father, and the mother, and the child, and the slave, and the wife; and that is because they are his dependents who are obligatory upon him.

Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the Zakat, one may give from it to the brother, the sister, the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the maternal uncle, and the maternal aunt, and one may not give to the grandfather nor the grandmother.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man from your mawla has relatives, all of whom believe in you, and he has zakat. Is it permissible for him to give them all of his zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Imran ibn Ismail ibn Imran al-Qummi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third [Imam], 'I have male and female children; is it permissible for me to give them something from the Zakat?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'That is permissible for you.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Jazzaki who said: I asked Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'Should I pay the tenth of my wealth to the children of my daughter?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Muhammad Al-Wabishi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One of our companions asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who bought his father from the zakat, the zakat of his wealth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has bought the best of slaves; there is no problem with that.'

Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man upon whose father there is a debt, and for his father there is a provision. Can he give his father from his zakat to pay off his debt? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and who is more deserving of it than his own father?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man upon whom Zakat became due, and his father died, and there was a debt upon him. Can he pay his Zakat for his father's debt, and for the son there is much wealth? He (peace be upon him) said: If his father had bequeathed him wealth, then a debt manifested upon him which he did not know about at that time, so he can settle it on his behalf, he settles it from all the inheritance and does not settle it from his Zakat. And if he had not bequeathed him wealth, there is no one more deserving of his Zakat than the debt of his father. So when he pays it for his father's debt in this state, it suffices for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man sent the zakat of his wealth to be distributed, but it was lost. Is there liability upon him for it until it is distributed? He (peace be upon him) said: If he found a place for it but did not hand it over, then he is liable for it until he hands it over. And if he did not find someone to whom he could hand it over, so he sent it to its deserving people, then there is no liability upon him, because it has gone out from his hand. And similarly is the trustee to whom it is entrusted; he is liable for what was handed over to him when he finds the owner to whom he was ordered to hand it over. But if he does not find him, then there is no liability upon him.

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When a man gives out the zakat from his wealth, then designates it for a group of people, and it gets lost, or he sends it to them and it gets lost, then there is nothing upon him.

Hariz from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: When he extracts it from his wealth, so it gets wasted, and he had not specified it for anyone, so he is not accountable for it.

Hariz from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man whose brother sent his zakat to him to distribute it, but it got wasted. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon the messenger, nor upon the payer, any responsibility.' I said, 'So if he does not find a deserving one for it, and it gets spoilt, and altered, would he be responsible?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but if he recognised a deserving one for it, so it got damaged, or spoilt, so he would be responsible for it until he extracts it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad from Al-Hasan from Jameel from Bukayr said, I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who sends his zakat, but it gets stolen or wasted. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who informed him, from Dorost, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the zakat, if a man sends it to a city other than his own city, he said: There is no problem if he were to send the third, or a quarter. The doubt is from Abu Ahmad.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who is given the zakat to distribute: Is it permissible for him to take something from it from the city he is in to another? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abdul Kareem ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to distribute the charity of the people of the countryside among the people of the countryside, and the charity of the people of the city among the people of the city, and he did not distribute it between them equally. Rather, he distributed it according to the number of those present from them, and he did not see anything fixed in that.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, who said: We were with Abu Baseer, and Amr ibn Ilyas came to him and said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad! My brother in Halab sent me wealth from the zakat to distribute it in Al-Kufa, but the road was cut off for it. Is there a narration with you regarding it?' He said, 'Yes. I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about this matter, and I did not think anyone would ask me about it ever. So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! A man sends his zakat from one land to another, and the road is cut off for it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It has sufficed him, and if it were me, I would pay it again.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The charity (zakat) of the Emigrants (Muhajirun) is not permissible for the Bedouins, nor is the charity of the Bedouins permissible for the Emigrants.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Umayyah (Aban ibn Uthman), from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man is given the zakat, and he distributes it among his companions; can he take something from it (for himself)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is given wealth to distribute among those whom it is permissible for him to give to: Is it permissible for him to take something from it for himself, even if it has not been specified for him? He (peace be upon him) said: He may take for himself an amount equal to what he gives to others.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who gives dirhams to another man to distribute them and place them in their designated places, while the distributor is among those permitted to receive charity. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if he takes for himself what he gives to others.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it is not permissible for him to take if he is instructed to place it in specified places, except with the owner's permission.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man takes the zakat, it is like his own wealth; he does with it whatever he wishes. He said, and he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed a duty upon the wealth of the rich for the poor, a duty for which they are not praised except by fulfilling it, and it is the zakat. So when it reaches the poor, it is at the status of his own wealth; he does with it whatever he wishes. I said, 'Does he marry with it and perform Hajj from it?' He said, 'Yes, it is his wealth.' I said, 'So is the poor person rewarded if he performs Hajj from the zakat just as the rich person, the owner of the wealth, is rewarded?' He said, 'Yes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'An old man from our companions, called Umar, asked Isa ibn A'yan while he was needy. Isa ibn A'yan said to him: 'Indeed, I have some zakat with me, but I will not give you from it.' He said to him: 'And why?' He said: 'Because I saw you buying meat and dates.' He said: 'I only profited by a dirham, so I bought meat with two dinars (or coins), and dates with two dinars (or coins), then I returned with two dinars (or coins) for a need.' He said: So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) placed his hand on his forehead for a while, then raised his head, then said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, looked at the wealth of the rich, then looked at the poor, and made in the wealth of the rich that which suffices them. And if it did not suffice them, He would have increased it for them. Rather, he should give him what he eats, drinks, wears, marries with, gives in charity, and performs Hajj with.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was seated, saying: 'I have been given from the zakat, so may I gather it until I perform Hajj with it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. May Allah reward the one who gives you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Ismail al-Shaeery, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man gives to another man from the zakat of his wealth to perform Hajj with it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth of zakat can be used for Hajj.' So I said to him (peace be upon him), 'He is a Muslim man giving to a Muslim man.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is needy, let him give to him for his need and his poverty, and he should not say to him, 'Perform Hajj with it.' He can do with it afterwards whatever he wishes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Amr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man in whose possession have gathered from the zakat five hundred or six hundred [coins]. Can he buy a person (slave) with it and free him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then he is unjust to another group regarding their rights.' Then he (peace be upon him) remained silent for a while, then said: 'Unless he happens to be a Muslim slave in desperation, so he buys him and frees him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave the zakat of his wealth, one thousand dirhams, but could not find a place to give that to. So he looked at a slave being sold, whoever wanted him, and bought him with those one thousand dirhams which he had given from his zakat, and freed him. Is that permissible for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with that.' I said: 'Suppose when he is freed and becomes free, he trades and becomes a craftsman, and acquires wealth, then he dies and has no heir. So who will inherit him if he has no heir?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The poor believers will inherit him, those who are entitled to the zakat, because he was bought with their money.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal and Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ibrahim ibn al-Sindi, from Yunus ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The loan of the believer is a booty, and it hastens the recompense. If he is affluent, he will pay you back, and if he dies before that, you will count it as Zakat for yourself.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Lending wealth supports the Zakat.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever lends a man a loan until he becomes affluent (pays it back), his wealth is in zakat, and he is in prayer with the angels until he pays it back.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer and Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ijaly and Fuzayl ibn Yasaar, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah imposed zakat alongside salat on wealth, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established it as a sunnah for nine things, and the Messenger of Allah exempted whatever was besides these — in gold, silver, camels, cattle, sheep, wheat, barley, dates, and raisins — and exempted whatever was besides that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Bakr al-Hazrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prescribed zakat upon nine things: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, camels, cattle, and sheep — and pardoned [everything] besides that.' Yunus said: 'The meaning of his statement that zakat is on nine things and pardons what is besides that — this was only during the beginning of prophethood, just as the salat used to be two cycles (rak'at), then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) added seven cycles to it. Likewise, zakat: he established it and made it a sunnah at the beginning of his prophethood upon nine things, then he extended it to all grains.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second: Is it permissible to take out from what is obligatory in the crops, from the wheat and the barley, and what is obligatory upon the gold, dirhams, being the value of what equates to it, or is it not permissible except to take out from each thing that which is in it? So he (peace be upon him) answered: Whichever is easier, take out.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man who gives from his zakat of dirhams [in the form of] dinars, and from his zakat of dinars [in the form of] dirhams, by the value. Is that permissible? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The owner of seven hundred [dirhams] takes the zakat if no one else is found.' I said, 'But the zakat is obligatory upon the owner of seven hundred.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His zakat is charity upon his dependents, and he does not take it unless he relies entirely on the seven hundred such that it is exhausted in less than a year; this one takes it. And the zakat is not permissible for one who has a profession and possesses wealth upon which zakat is obligatory.'

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying that the charity (Zakat) is not permissible for the professional, nor for the one with capability, normal, strong, so let them keep themselves away from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ismail ibn Abdul Aziz, from his father, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man from our companions who had eight hundred dirhams, and he was a glass polisher, and he had many dependants. Is it permissible for him to take from the Zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad, does he profit from his dirhams what would provide for his dependants and there is an excess?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'How much is the excess?' I said, 'I do not know'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the excess upon the provision is the amount of half the provision, then he should not take the Zakat; and if it is less than half the provision, he takes the Zakat.' I said, 'So, is Zakat imposed upon his wealth that he must pay?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'What should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should expand upon his dependants with it in their food, drink, and clothing; and if something remains from it, he can give it to others; and whatever he takes from the Zakat, he dedicates it to his dependants until he brings them up to the level of the people.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Zakat, is it permissible for the owner of the house and the servant? He said: Yes, unless his house is a house of yield (rent), so that dirhams are extracted for him from its yield which suffice for himself and his dependents. If the yield does not suffice for himself and his dependents regarding their food, clothing, and needs without extravagance, then the Zakat becomes permissible for him. But if its yield suffices them, then no.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man whose father, or uncle, or brother provides for his provision (maintenance); can he take from the Zakat and expand (his means) with it, if they do not expand (provide sufficiently) for him in everything he needs? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn Wahb said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has three hundred dirhams or four hundred dirhams, and he has dependants, and he is a craftsman, so he does not earn enough for his expenses from it. Should he suppress it (keep the capital intact) and eat the profit, and not take the zakat, or should he take the zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but he should look at its excess (profit), so he should provide for himself with it, and whoever of his dependants can be provided for from that, and he should take the remainder from the zakat, and he should conduct business with this (capital) and not spend it.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has eight hundred dirhams, and for his son there are two hundred dirhams, and he has ten dependents, and he provides for them with it with difficulty, and he has no profession in his hand, but rather he trades with it, and it remains absent from him for months, then he consumes from its excess. Do you see that for him, when Zakat becomes due, that he should take it out from his wealth and return it to his dependents, bestowing upon them with it the provision? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, but he should take from it the thing, the dirham.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Zakat becomes permissible for the owner of seven hundred [dirhams] and prohibited for the owner of fifty [dirhams]. I said to him, 'How can this be?' He said: 'If the owner of seven hundred has many dependents, and if he were to distribute it among them, it would not suffice him, so he should spare himself [from giving it away] and take it for his dependents. As for the owner of fifty, it is prohibited upon him if he is alone and is a craftsman/tradesman, working with it, and he attains from it what suffices him, God willing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Abdul Aziz, from his father, who said: I and Abu Baseer entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Abu Baseer said to him: 'We have a friend, and he is a truthful man, who follows our religion.' He said: 'Who is this, O Abu Muhammad, whom you are praising?' He said: 'Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Sabih.' He said: 'May Allah have mercy on Walid ibn Sabih. What is the matter with him, O Abu Muhammad?' He said: 'May I be your ransom, he has a house worth four thousand dirhams, and he has a slave girl, and he has a slave who draws water on a camel every day, costing between two and four dirhams, besides the camel's feed, and he has dependents. Is it permissible for him to take from the Zakat?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And he has these assets?' He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, do you order me to tell him to sell his house, which is his honor and his birthplace, or to sell his slave girl who protects him from heat and cold and preserves his face and the faces of his dependents, or to tell him to sell his slave and his camel, which is his livelihood and sustenance? Rather, he takes the Zakat, and it is permissible for him, and he does not sell his house, nor his slave, nor his camel.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who has dirhams which he uses for trade, and upon which zakat has become obligatory, and the surplus he earns from his wealth is sufficient for his dependents' food and clothing, but it does not suffice for their sauces (condiments), and it is merely what provides for them in food and clothing. He (peace be upon him) said: So let him look at the zakat of that wealth of his, and let him extract from it something, little or much, and give it to one of those to whom zakat is permissible, and let him count what remains of the zakat upon his dependents, and let him buy with that their sauces and what improves their food, without extravagance, and he himself should not eat from it, for indeed sometimes the poor are more extravagant than the rich. So I said, 'How can the poor be more extravagant than the rich?' He said, 'The rich spend from what is given (earned) to them, and the poor spend from what is not given (earned) to them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'They report from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that charity is not permissible for the rich, nor for the one with strong resources.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct for the rich.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is given to the Zakat collector?' He said, 'Whatever the Imam sees (appropriate), and nothing is fixed/measured out for him.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man is a slave, and his master is a Muslim man, and he has wealth from which he pays zakat, and the slave has a young child who is free. Is it sufficient for his master to give to the son of his slave from the zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawud al-Sarri, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the drinker of wine, 'Would he be given anything from the Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masrouq, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Hilal ibn Khaqan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who neglects Zakat, while it has been obligated for him, is like the one who withholds it, while it has been obligated upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah Al-Alawi, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who neglects the Zakat while it has become obligatory for him is like the one who withholds it while it has become obligatory upon him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man from our companions is too shy to take from the zakat. So can I give him from the zakat and not specify to him that it is from the zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give him and do not specify to him, and do not humiliate the believer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man is in need, so charity is sent to him, but he does not accept it as charity; he is held back by modesty, embarrassment, and withdrawal. Should we give it to him in a manner other than that, even though it is charity from us?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. If it is zakat, he has the right to accept it. But if he does not accept it as zakat, do not give it to him. And it is not befitting for him to be embarrassed by what Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has imposed; it is merely an obligation of Allah for him, so he should not be embarrassed by it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic And give its due on the day of its harvest They all said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from the charity; he gives the poor man a handful after a handful, and from the harvest a handful after a handful until he finishes, and he gives the guard a known wage, and he leaves from the palm trees Mi'a Farat or Umm Jarour, and what is in the enclosure for the guard, the bunch, the two bunches, and the three, for guarding it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not pick (fruits) at night, nor harvest at night, nor slaughter (the sacrificial animal) at night, nor sow at night, for if you do so, the contented one and the beggar will not come to you. So I said, 'What is the contented one and the beggar?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The contented one is the one who is content with what you give him, and the beggar is the one who passes by you and asks you.' And if you harvest at night, the beggar will not come asking. And give its due on the day of its harvest. At the time of harvest, meaning the grasping (taking) after the grasping when you harvest it; and when it comes out, the handful after the handful; and similarly at the time of picking (fruits), and similarly at the time of sowing. And do not sow at night, because you give from the seed just as you give from the harvest.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Abu Maryam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic And give its due on the day of its harvest He said: You give the poor person the bale on the day of your harvest. Then when it falls into the threshing floor, then when it falls into the sa' (measure), the tenth and half the tenth (is given as zakat).

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And give its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be extravagant.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: Among the extravagance in harvesting and reaping is that a man gives in charity with both his palms together.' And my father, whenever something of this was presented to him, and he saw one of his servants giving charity with both his hands, would shout at him, 'Give with one hand, the handful after the handful, the bale after the bale, from the ears of corn.'

Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Ahl al-Zimma (people of the covenant), 'What is upon them from that which preserves their blood and their wealth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Kharaaj (land tax). So if the Jizyah (poll tax) is taken from their heads, then there is no claim upon their land, and if it is taken from their land, then there is no claim upon their heads.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Magians: 'Was there a Prophet for them?' So he said: 'Yes.' Has it not reached you the letter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to the people of Mecca: 'Become Muslims, or else I will initiate war against you'? So they wrote to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'Take the jizya (tax) from us and leave us upon the worship of the idols'. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to them: 'I do not take the jizya except from the People of the Book'. So they wrote to him, intending by that to belie him: 'You allege that you do not take the jizya except from the People of the Book, then you take the jizya from the Magians of Hawar'. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to them: 'It was so that the Magians had a Prophet for them, but they killed him, and (they had) a Book which they burnt'. Their Prophet came to them with their Book in twelve thousand skins of bulls.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the charity (zakat) of the people of the jizya, and what is taken from them from the price of their wine, the flesh of their swine, and their carcasses. He (peace be upon him) said: The jizya is upon them in their wealth; it is taken from them from the price of the flesh of the swine or wine, and everything taken from them of that, its burden is upon them, and its price is permissible for the Muslims, which they take as part of their jizya.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the tax (jizyah) is not lifted from the land of jizyah, and rather, the tax is the provision for the emigrants, and the charity (zakat) is for its people whom Allah has specified in His Book, and they have nothing from the tax. Then he said: 'How vast is Allah's justice!' Then he said: 'The people become enriched when justice is established between them, and the sky sends down its sustenance and the earth brings forth its blessings by the permission of Allah, the Exalted.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the people of the jizyah (taxpayers), is anything taken from their wealth and their livestock besides the jizyah? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with a man passing by fruit and eating from it, provided he does not spoil it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade building walls in Medina in the places of passers-by. He said: 'And when a palm tree reached maturity, he ordered that openings be made in the walls in the places of passers-by.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jareer, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, except that he said: 'And he should not spoil it, nor carry it away.'

Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from his father, from Yunus or others, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, it reached me that you used to do something regarding the produce of Ayn Ziyad, and I love to hear it from you.' So he said to me, 'Yes. I used to order that when the fruit ripened, grooves be made in its walls so that people could enter and eat. And I used to order that every day ten structures be set up, with ten people sitting on each be placed. Whenever ten had eaten, ten others would come, and for each person of them, a Mudd of fresh dates was given.' And I used to order for all the neighbors of the estate—the old man, the old woman, the child, the sick, the woman, and whoever was unable to come and eat from it—that for each person of them, a Mudd was given. So when it was the picking time, I paid the workers, the supervisors, and the men their wages, and I carried the remainder to Medina. Then I distributed among the people of the houses and the deserving ones, the two camel loads, and the three, the less and the more, according to their deservingness. And after that, four hundred Dinars remained for me, while its gross produce had been four thousand Dinars.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from the one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from his father, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when the fruits reached maturity, ordered that the walls be grooved.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about grains — which of them are subject to zakat? He said: Wheat, barley, corn, millet, rice, hulless barley (sult), lentils, and sesame — all of these are subject to zakat, and those resembling them.

And he said: 'Everything which is measured by the sa' that reaches the awsaq, upon it is the zakat.' And he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) made the sadaqa upon everything that the earth grows, except what is in the greens and the vegetables, and everything that spoils the same day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I read in a letter of 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! It has been reported from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) placed zakat upon nine things: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, sheep, cattle, and camels; and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) excused [from zakat] whatever was besides that.' So a questioner said to him: 'With us there are many things that are multiples of that.' He said: 'And what is it?' He said to him: 'Rice.' So Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I am telling you that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) placed zakat upon nine things and excused whatever was besides that, and you say: With us there is rice, and with us there is corn — but corn existed in the era of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family)!' So he (peace be upon him) signed [in response]: 'It is as such; and zakat is upon everything that is measured by the sa'a.' And 'Abdullah wrote: And it is reported by other than this man from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about grains, so he said: 'And what are they?' He said: 'Sesame, and rice, and millet — and all of this is produce like wheat and barley.' So Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'On all grains, there is zakat.'

And it is also narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Whatever enters the qafeez, it follows the same ruling as wheat, barley, dates, and raisins.' He said: 'So inform me, may I be sacrificed for you — is there zakat on rice and what resembles it from the grains, chickpeas, and lentils?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote in response: 'They were right — zakat is on every thing that is measured (by volume).'

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We have unripened dates (raTba) and rice — what is obligatory upon us regarding them?' He said (peace be upon him): 'As for the unripened dates (raTba), there is nothing upon you regarding it.' And as for the rice — whatever was irrigated by the sky (rain), then with the one-tenth (tithe, 10%); and whatever was irrigated by the bucket, then half of the one-tenth (5%), from everything that you measure by the sa'a', or he said: 'weighed by the measure.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Sama'a, from one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the crops — what is subject to zakat from them? He said: Wheat, barley, corn, rice, rye, and lentils — all of these are among what zakat must be paid on. And he said: Everything measured by the sa'a that reaches the awsaq threshold — zakat is due upon it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no zakat upon vegetables nor upon melons and their like, except what accumulates with you from their produce and remains with you for a year.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he was asked about vegetables/greenery: is there zakat on them even if they are sold for great wealth? So he said: No, until a year passes over it.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What (zakat) is (due) regarding vegetables?' He said: 'And what are they?' I said, 'Herbs and melons and the like from vegetables.' He said: 'Nothing (is due) upon it, except that if the likes of it are sold for wealth and a year passes over it, then the zakat is (due) upon it.' And regarding fresh fruit from plums and what resembles it — is there zakat upon it? He said: 'No.' I said, 'Then what about its price?' He said: 'Whatever amount from its price over which a year has passed, purify it (pay zakat on it).'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar and someone else, from Yunus who said: I asked Abu al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about potash — is there zakat on it? So he said: No.
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about cotton and saffron: 'Is there zakat upon them?' He said: 'No.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) regarding the orchard wherein happen to be fruits such that if they were sold they would constitute wealth — is there zakat obligated upon it? He said: No.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, who said: I asked him about the zakat on raisins and dates. He said: For every five awsaq, one wasq (is the zakat), and the wasq is sixty sa'as, and the zakat on both of them is equal. But as for grain crops, the tithe (one-tenth) applies to what is irrigated by the sky (rain), and as for what is irrigated by the bucket and water-lifting devices, then only half the tithe (one-twentieth) is due.

We mentioned to him al-Kufa and what land tax had been imposed upon it, and what the members of his household had done there. So he said: 'Whoever accepted Islam voluntarily, his land was left in his possession, and one-tenth (ushr) was taken from him from what the sky and rivers watered, and half the tenth (5%) from what was irrigated by rope/bucket — this applies to what they cultivated from it. As for what they did not cultivate, the Imam takes it and leases it to those who cultivate it; and it belonged to the Muslims, and upon the lessees in their shares was the tenth and half the tenth. And there is no zakat on less than five awsuq. As for what was taken by the sword, that is up to the Imam — he leases it as he sees fit, just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did at Khaybar: he contracted its black (cultivated land) and its white (palm trees), meaning its land and its palms. The people say it is not valid to contract out land and palm trees, yet the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) contracted Khaybar; and upon the contractors, besides the land contract, was the tenth and half the tenth in their shares. He also said: The people of al-Taif accepted Islam, and the tenth and half the tenth were imposed upon them. The people of Mecca — the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entered it by force; they were captives in his hand, and he freed them and said: Go, for you are all free (tulaqa).

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the zakat: For what the sky and the rivers irrigate, when it is flowing water or it is unwatered land, the one-tenth is due. And whatever is irrigated by the water-lifting devices and the buckets, or watered by the large water-skin, then half of the one-tenth is due.

They both said to him 'This land which its people farm — what do you see regarding it?' So he said: 'Every land which the Sultan hands over to you — whatever you cultivate in it — upon you is (the obligation) regarding what Allah brings forth from it, that which has been apportioned to you.' 'And it is not upon the entirety of what Allah brings forth from it that the one-tenth (ushr) is due; rather, upon you is the one-tenth only on what arrives in your hand after its distribution to you.'

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the minimum upon which zakat becomes obligatory from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. So he said: Five awsaq, by the wasq of the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). So I said: How much is the wasq? He said: Sixty sa'as. I said: Is there then zakat on grapes, or does it only become obligatory when one turns them into raisins? He said: Yes, when it is estimated (by valuation), its zakat is to be taken out.

Regarding what the sky (rain) and the rivers irrigate, or if it was rain-fed (without human effort), is the one-tenth (10%); and as for what the water-wheels and the buckets irrigate, then it is half of the one-tenth (5%). So I said to him: 'But the land which happens to be with us — we irrigate it by the buckets, then the water increases and so the rivers irrigate it.' So he said: 'And does this indeed happen with you like that?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'The half and the half — half with half of the one-tenth, and half with the one-tenth.' So I said: 'The land is irrigated by the buckets, then the water increases and it gets irrigated by one irrigation and two irrigations by canal.' He said: 'And in how much is the one irrigation and the two irrigations by canal?' I said: 'In thirty or forty nights, while before that six or seven months had passed in the land (under bucket irrigation).' He said: 'Half of the one-tenth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about dates and raisins — what is the minimum that makes zakat obligatory on them? He said: Five awsaq. And the Mi'a Fa'ira and Umm Ju'rur (two inferior date varieties) are left out — zakat is not paid on them even if they are numerous. And one or two clusters are left for the guard who is among the palm trees watching over them, and that is left for his dependents.

He said: For every two hundred dirhams, five dirhams [are due] from silver; and if it falls short, there is no zakat upon you. And from gold, for every twenty dinars, half a dinar; and if it falls short, there is nothing upon you.

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) so he said: 'I am a goldsmith working with my hands, and there gathers in my possession five and ten (items). Is there zakat on it?' He said: 'When two hundred dirhams have accumulated and a year has passed over them, then indeed the zakat is due upon them.'

There is nothing (payable as Zakat) in less than twenty mithqal of gold. So when twenty mithqal are complete, then half a mithqal (is payable) up to twenty-four. So when twenty-four are complete, then three-fifths of a dinar (is payable) up to twenty-eight. Thus it continues on this accounting: every time it increases by four.
When the zakat exceeds twenty dinars, then for every four dinars there is one-tenth of a dinar.
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about gold: 'How much zakat is in it?' He said: 'When its value reaches two hundred dirhams, then zakat is due upon it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn Bashar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'In how much did the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) set the zakat?' He said: 'In every two hundred dirhams, five dirhams. But if it falls short, there is no zakat on it. And regarding gold, in every twenty dinars, half a dinar. But if it falls short, there is no zakat on it.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about gold and silver: 'What is the minimum on which zakat is due?' He said: 'Two hundred dirhams, and its equivalent from gold.' He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about the small change — the five and the ten. He said: 'There is nothing due on it until it reaches forty, then one dirham is given for every forty dirhams.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), he said: I said to him: One hundred and ninety Dirhams, and nineteen Dinars — is there any zakat upon it? So he said: When gold and silver combine and that reaches two hundred Dirhams, then zakat is due on it, because the essence of wealth is the Dirhams, and everything apart from the Dirhams — whether gold or chattels — is a commodity referred back to the Dirhams in matters of zakat and blood money (diyat).
