Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Zayd al-Sa'igh, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I was in a town of the towns of Khurasan called Bukhara, and I saw dirhams being minted there — one third silver, one third copper, and one third lead — and they were accepted among the people there, and I used to work with them and spend them.' He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that, provided they are accepted among them.' I said: 'What is your view — if a lunar year passes while they are in my possession, and they contain that which makes zakat obligatory upon me, shall I pay zakat on them?' He said: 'Yes, for it is simply your wealth.' I said: 'Then if I take them to a city where such coins are not spent, and they remain with me until a year passes over them — shall I pay zakat on them?' He said: 'If you know that they contain pure silver such that zakat is obligatory upon you regarding it, then pay zakat on whatever pure silver is yours in them, and leave aside the rest from the impurities.' I said: 'And if I do not know what pure silver is in them, except that I know that they contain that which makes zakat obligatory?' He said: 'Then smelt them until the silver is purified and the impurities burn away, then pay zakat on whatever silver was extracted for one year.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charity (sadaqa) repels the evil death.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar — all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ghalib, from one who narrated it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Righteous deeds and charity both negate poverty, they both increase the lifespan, and they both repel ninety evil types of death. And in another narration: And they both repel the evil (type of) death from my Shia.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ismail al-Jawhari, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: If I were to perform a Hajj, it would be more beloved to me than if I were to free a neck (slave), and a neck — until it reached ten, and similar to it, and similar to it, until it reached seventy. And if I were to support a household from the Muslims, satisfying their hunger, clothing their nakedness, and restraining their faces from (begging of) the people, it would be more beloved to me than if I were to perform a Hajj, and a Hajj, and a Hajj — until it reached ten, and ten, and ten, and similar to it, and similar to it, until it reached seventy.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in the Replacement (recompense from God) will be generous in giving.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Treat your sick ones with charity, repel afflictions with supplication, and draw down sustenance with charity. For indeed it passes through the jaws of seven hundred devils, and there is nothing heavier upon Satan than charity given to a believer, and it falls into the Hand of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, before it falls into the hand of the servant.'
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The land of the Day of Resurrection is fire, except for the shade of the believer — for his charity will shade him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Charity given with the hand protects from an evil death, repels seventy types of afflictions, and finds its way through the beards of seventy devils — all of them commanding him not to do it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: It was in the bequest of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to the Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God and His peace be upon him): 'And as for charity, give to your utmost, give to your utmost, until it is said, "He has been extravagant," though you will not have been extravagant.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: It is recommended for the sick person that he give to the beggar with his own hand, and that he instruct the beggar to supplicate for him.

Several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from several, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Give charity, even if it is with a Sa' of dates, or even with part of a Sa', or even with a handful, or even with part of a handful, or even with one date, or even with half a date. So whoever cannot find (even that), let him give with soft words.' For indeed, one of you will meet Allah, and it will be said to him: 'Did I not do (such and such) with you? Did I not make you hearing and seeing? Did I not make for you wealth and children?' So he will say, 'Yes.' Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say: 'So look what you have sent ahead for yourself.' He said: 'So he will look in front of him, and behind him, and to his right, and to his left, and he will not find anything with which he can shield his face from the Fire.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, or someone else, from Muhammad ibn Uzafar, from Umar ibn Yazeed who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the charity upon the people of the valleys and the wilderness, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give charity upon the children, and the women, and the sick, and the weak, and the old'; and he (peace be upon him) had forbidden [giving to] those who are able, meaning the ones with the (earning) capacity.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Zur'ah, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Give to the old man and the old woman, and the young boy and the young girl, and to whoever mercy falls upon in your heart; and beware of (giving to) everyone,' and he said with his hand and shook it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The people of the valleys (or plains) are encroaching upon us, and among them are the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians, so do we give charity to them?' He said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed Al-Nowfaly, from Ismail ibn Abu Ziyad Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not cut off the question of the beggar; if it were not for the fact that the poor lie, the one who repels them would not prosper.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Give to the beggar, even if he is upon the back of a horse.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: It was among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa (peace be upon him): He said, 'O Musa! Honour the beggar with a small gift or with a beautiful reply.' Because there will come to you one who is neither human nor Jinn, an Angel from the Angels of the Beneficent, who will test you regarding what I have bestowed upon you and ask you about what I have given you. So see how you are dealing, O son of Imran.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib Al-Ghalib Al-Asadi, from his father, from Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, who said: I was present with Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) one day when he prayed the morning prayer, and behold, a beggar was at the door. So Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Give to the beggar and do not repel a beggar.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ayman ibn Muhraz, from Abu Asama Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not withhold anything from a beggar at all; if he had something, he would give it, or else he would say: 'Allah will bring it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not repel the beggar, even if it is with a burnt hoof.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed and others, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from the one who mentioned it, he said: When you give them, teach them the supplication, for the supplication is answered for them through you, and it is not answered for them regarding their own selves.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Do not belittle the supplication of anyone, for it is accepted for the Jew and the Christian regarding you, but it is not accepted for them regarding their own selves.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Salih ibn Razin, who said: Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih handed over to me some dirhams from the zakat to distribute. So I came to him one day and he asked me, 'Did you distribute them?' So I said, 'No'. So he made me listen to words wherein was some harshness. So I dropped what remained with me from the dirhams and I arose in anger. So he said to me, 'Return, until I narrate to you something which I heard from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him)'. So I returned. So he said, 'I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When I find my zakat, I take it out and hand it over to one whom I trust to distribute it'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with that. Indeed, he is one of the givers'. Salih said, 'So I took the dirhams when I heard the hadith, and I distributed them'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: If goodness (charity/kindness) were to flow upon eighty palms (i.e., be distributed through eighty people), all of them would be recompensed for it, without the original donor having anything of his reward diminished.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has with him only the provision for his day: Should he give preference to the one who has the provision for his day over the one who has nothing, and should he give preference to the one who has the provision for a month over the one who has less than it, and the year in a similar manner, or is all of that the sufficiency (kafaf) for which he is not blamed? So he (peace be upon him) said: It is a matter wherein the best of you is the one most eager for preferring (others) over himself, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And they give preference over themselves, even though poverty may afflict them.' And the other matter is that he is not blamed for sufficiency (kafaf), and the higher hand is better than the lower hand, and begin with those whom you support.

He said, and Bakr ibn Salih narrated to us from Bundar ibn Muhammad al-Tabari from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Sa'i from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'Advise me.' He said, 'I order you with the fear of Allah.' Then he was silent, so I complained to him about the scarcity of what was in my hand, and I said, 'By Allah, I have become naked, and my nakedness reached such an extent that Abu so-and-so removed two garments that were upon him and clothed me with them.' He said, 'Fast and give charity.' I said, 'Can I give charity from what has reached me from my brethren, even if it is little?' He said, 'Give charity from what Allah has provided you with, even if you have to prefer (others) over yourself.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I said to him, 'Which charity is the most superior?' He said, 'The effort (struggle) of the poor person.' Have you not heard the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And they prefer (others) before themselves, even though poverty may afflict them'? Here is the superiority.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'I guaranteed upon my Lord that no one would ask (for something) without a need, except that the asking would compel him for a day until he would ask for a need.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Follow the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for he said: 'Whoever opens for himself a door of begging, Allah opens for him a door of poverty.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Malik ibn Husayn al-Sakuni, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who asks [for something] without having a need, and then dies, until Allah makes him needy to it, and Allah affirms for him the Fire because of it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from one who heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Beware of asking people (for what they have), for it is a humiliation in the world, and a poverty that you hasten, and a lengthy reckoning on the Day of Resurrection.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Had the beggar known what is in the begging, no one would beg from anyone; and had the giver known what is in the giving, no one would have repelled anyone'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, raising it (to the Prophet), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The hands are three: The Hand of Allah is the upper one, and the hand of the giver is what follows it, and the hand of the recipient is the lowest of the hands. Therefore, refrain from begging to the extent of your ability. Indeed, sustenance is behind veils; so whoever desires may veil his shame and take his sustenance, and whoever desires may tear down the veil and take his sustenance. And by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of you were to take a rope, then enter the width of this valley, and gather firewood until its two ends do not meet, then he enters the market with it, sells it for a mud of dates, takes a third of it, and gives in charity two thirds of it, it would be better for him than if he were to ask the people, whether they give him or withhold from him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibrahim ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves for Himself a thing and hates it for His creation. He hates for His creation the act of begging (asking from others), and loves for Himself that one should ask Him. And there is nothing more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than that one should ask Him. So let not one of you be shy to ask Allah from His Grace, even if it is just a strap of a slipper.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A branch of the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and they greeted him, so he returned the greeting to them. They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have a need for you.' He said, 'Present your need.' They said, 'It is a great need.' He said, 'Present it, what is it?' They said, 'Guarantee for us Paradise upon your Lord.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) lowered his head, then struck the ground with his finger, then raised his head and said, 'I will do that for you on the condition that you do not ask anyone for anything.' So it was that a man from them would be traveling, and his whip would fall, so he would dislike saying to a person, 'Hand it to me,' fleeing from asking, so he would dismount and take it himself. And he would be at the table, and one of the seated would be closer to the water than him, so he would not say, 'Hand it to me,' until he would stand up and drink.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-A'ala, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on a servant who is chaste and self-restraining, and who refrains from begging, for it hastens the disgrace in the world, and the people do not make him self-sufficient in anything.' He said, 'Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) cited a verse of Hatim: "When I recognized despair, I found it to be riches; when the soul recognized it, greed was poverty."'

Ali ibn Muhammad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sayrafi, from Mufazzal ibn Qays ibn Rummana, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned to him some of my state. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O maid! Bring that bag! These are four hundred dinars which Abu Ja'far sent to me, so take them and ease (your financial problems) with them.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I said, 'No, by Allah! May I be sacrificed for you! This is not my purpose, but I would love it if you could supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I shall be doing it, but beware of informing the people with all of your state, for you would be belittled by them.'

And it is reported from Luqman (peace be upon him) that he said: To his son: 'O my son! I tasted patience and ate the bark of trees, but I did not find anything more bitter than poverty. So if you are tried by it for a day, do not manifest it to the people, lest they belittle you and not benefit you with anything. Return to the One who tested you with it, for He is more able to provide your relief, and ask Him. [Consider] the one who asked Him and was not given [what he wanted], or relied upon Him but was not rescued.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyas, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, disliked for me six characteristics, and I disliked them for the Successors from my children, and their followers after me; among them is Al-Mann (reproach/embarrassing the recipient) after charity.'
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, raising it, said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The reproach demolishes the favour'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) sent to a man five wasqs of Al-Bughayba dates, and the man was among those who hoped for his voluntary gifts and anticipated his support, and he did not ask Ali (peace be upon him) or anyone else for anything. A man said, A man to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'By Allah, So-and-so has not asked you, and one wasq from the five wasqs would have sufficed him.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to him: 'May Allah increase the number of believers! You are stingy while I am giving. For the sake of Allah, if I do not give to the one who hopes for me except after he asks, and then I give him after he asks, I have not given him the cost of what I have taken from him. And that is because I have exposed him to risking his face, which he places on the ground for my Lord and his Lord, during his worship of me and his seeking of his needs from me.' So whoever does this to his Muslim brother, knowing that he is a recipient of his charity and kindness, and does not confirm Allah in his supplication for him, where he wishes for him Paradise with his tongue but is stingy with him over the chaff of his wealth, then that is because the servant may say in his supplication: 'O Allah, forgive the believing men and the believing women.' If he supplicates for them with forgiveness, he has asked for Paradise for them. So how just is he who does this with his tongue and does not confirm it with his action?

Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Nuh ibn Abdullah, from Al-Dahli, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The good deed (charity/gift) should be initiated (before asking); as for the one you give after he asks, you have merely satisfied him by what he sacrificed his dignity for you. He spends his night awake, restless, standing between hope and despair, not knowing where to turn for his need. Then he resolves to go for it, so he comes to you with his heart quivering and his limbs trembling. You would see his face flushed with blood, not knowing whether he will return with sorrow or with joy.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Sandal, from Yasser, from Al-Yasa' ibn Hamza, who said: I was in the gathering of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), narrating to him, and a large crowd had gathered to him, asking him about the Halal and the Haram. Then a tall, fair-skinned man entered and said: 'Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! I am a man from your lovers and the lovers of your fathers and forefathers (peace be upon them). I have returned from Hajj, and my expenses are lost, and I have nothing with me to reach a stage (of travel). So if you see fit, advance me to my city. By Allah, it would be a favor upon me. So when I reach my city, I will give in charity that which you command me to give on your behalf, for I am not a recipient of charity.' He said to him: 'Sit, may Allah have mercy on you!' And he turned to the people, narrating to them until they dispersed. He remained with Suleiman Al-Ja'fari, Khaysama, and myself. He said: 'Do you allow me to enter?' Suleiman said to him: 'May Allah advance your affair.' So he arose and entered the chamber and remained for a while. Then he came out, closed the door, and put his hand out from the top of the door and said: 'Where is the Khurasani man?' He said: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Take these two hundred Dinars and be assisted by them in your provisions and expenses, and be blessed by them, and do not give charity with them on my behalf. Go, so that I do not see you and you do not see me.' Then he came out. Suleiman said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! You have been generous and merciful, so why did you veil your face from him?' He said: 'Out of fear that I might see the humiliation of asking in his face, for fulfilling his need. Have you not heard the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'The one who conceals a good deed equals seventy Hajj, and the one who publicizes a bad deed is forsaken, and the one who conceals it is forgiven for it'? Have you not heard the words of the ancients: 'Whenever I go to Him to seek a need, I return to my family with my face undamaged'.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, by a chain mentioning from Al-Harith Al-Hamadani who said: I conversed with Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), so I said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! A need has presented itself to me.' He said: 'So you view me as a rightful one for it?' I said, 'Yes, O Amir al-Mu'minin!' He said: 'May Allah recompense you goodly from me.' Then he arose to the lantern, so he extinguished it and sat down, then said: 'But rather, I extinguished the lantern perhaps I would see the humiliation of your need in your face, so speak, for I heard Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: The needs are an entrustment from Allah in the chests of the servants, so the one who conceals it, a worship would be Written for him, and the one who exposes it, it would be a right upon the one who hears it that he assists him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Asbagh, from Bundar ibn Aasim, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'The best means and recourse of approaching me for help is the appeal of a man who has received help from me once, then asks for help again. My hands have done a good deed for him before the Lord. I have found denying a later appeal for help cuts off the appreciation for the favour already received. I dislike for my soul to deny help for the second time, which may cause to discontinue the appreciation for the earlier help and favour. It is just like a poet has said: If you face to risk the dignity of your face, you should face such risk before a king and generous person. If a generous person promises to do a favour to you and he does it in time without any delays; and if he favour come as soon as an appeal is made, the appeal become more preferable than the favour. And when asking is with the attaining, paired up, the asking overweighs and everything attained becomes lighter.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Arise early with charity and be eager for it. For there is no believer who gives in charity intending by it what is with God, so that God may ward off from him the evil of what descends from the sky to the earth on that day, except that God protects him from the evil of what descends from the sky to the earth on that day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah send blessings upon him and his family) said: 'Verily Allah — there is no god except Him — surely repels through charity: disease, abscesses, burning, drowning, collapse, and madness.' And he (may Allah send blessings upon him and his family) counted seventy categories of evil.

A Jew passed by the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Al-Sam be upon you.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Upon you.' His companions said, 'But he greeted you with death!' He (the Prophet) said, 'Death be upon you' — then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'And that is how I replied.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This Jew will be bitten by a black snake in the nape of his neck, and it will kill him.' So the Jew went and gathered a lot of firewood and carried it. Then, before long, he came back. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Put it down.' He placed the firewood down, and behold — a black snake was in the middle of the firewood, biting on a stick. So he said: 'O Jew! What did you do today?' He said, 'I did not do anything except carry this firewood of mine. I came back with it, and I had two cakes with me; I ate one and gave the other in charity to a poor person.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'By it God repelled it from him.' And he said: 'Indeed, charity repels an evil death from the human being.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'They used to consider that charity wards off [harm] from the greatly wronged/oppressive man.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Amr al-Nakha'i, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Hasten with charity, for the affliction does not bypass it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Hanan ibn Sudeyr, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, charity repels seventy afflictions from the afflictions of the world, including the evil death. Its performer will never die an evil death, along with whatever is stored up for its performer in the Hereafter.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Bishr ibn Salama, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever gives charity when he enters the morning, Allah will remove from him the inauspiciousness of that day.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from more than one (narrator), from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to Ismail ibn Muhammad, having mentioned to him that his son had given charity on his behalf: 'He is (still) a man.' He (the Imam) said: 'So command him to give charity, even if it be with a piece of bread.' Then he (the narrator) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from the Children of Israel had a son who was beloved to him. Someone came to him in his sleep and said: Your son — on the night he consummates (his marriage) with his wife — will die.' He said: When that night came and his father had prepared for it, his father feared that prediction. But in the morning, his son was safe. So his father went to him and said: O my dear son! Did you do anything good last night? He said: No, except that a beggar came to the door, and they had stored food for me, so I gave it to the beggar. He (the father) said: By this, God has averted (death) from you.

And by this chain, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There was a piece of land to be divided between me and a man, and that man was an astrologer. He would seek the fortunate hour to go out in it, while I would go out in the inauspicious hour. So we divided, and the better of the two shares came to me. The man slapped his right hand on his left and said, "I have never seen a day like today!" I said, "Woe to another! What is that?" He said, "I am an astrologer. I made you go out in the inauspicious time and I went out in the fortunate time, then we divided and the better share came to you!" So I said, "Shall I not narrate to you a hadith my father narrated to me?" He said, "The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever would be pleased that God repel from him the ill omen of his day, let him begin his day with charity — God will remove from him by it the ill omen of his day. And whoever loves that God remove from him the ill omen of his night, let him begin his night with charity — God will repel from him the ill omen of his night." And I said: "And I had begun my going out with charity. So this is better for you than the knowledge of astrology."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: There was a man from the Children of Israel who had no child, so a boy was born to him, and it was said to him, 'He will die on the night of his wedding.' The boy remained, and when it was the night of his wedding, he looked at an old, weak man. The boy felt pity for him, called him, and fed him. The beggar said to him, 'You have revived me, may Allah revive you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then a visitor came to him in his sleep and said to him, 'Ask your son what he did.' So he asked him, and he informed him of what he had done. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The visitor came to him again in his sleep and said to him, 'Indeed, Allah has revived your son for you due to what he did for the old man.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah ibn Ayyub, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), so an overhang from the overhangs of the mosque fell and struck a man, but it did not harm him, and injured his leg. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask him what he did today.' So they asked him, and he said: 'I went out, and in my sleeve was a date. So I passed by a beggar and gave him a date in charity.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'By it, Allah repelled [the harm] from you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Ismail ibn Abdul-Khaliq al-Ju'fi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the survival of the Muslims and the survival of Islam is that wealth should come to be in the hands of one who recognizes the right/truth in it and does good/acts of kindness in it; for among the annihilation of Islam and the annihilation of the Muslims is that wealth should come to be in the hands of one who does not recognize the right/truth in it, nor does he do any act of kindness in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made for acts of kindness (al-ma'ruf) a people from His creation, making them love its performance; and He directed the seekers of acts of kindness to seek them out, and made their fulfillment easy for them, just as He made the rain easy for the barren land, so that it may revive it and revive its people through it. And indeed, Allah made for acts of kindness enemies from His creation, making the acts of kindness hateful to them and making their performance hateful to them; and He prohibited the seekers of acts of kindness from seeking them, and prohibited their fulfillment upon them, just as He withholds the rain from the barren land to destroy it and destroy its people. And what Allah pardons/forgives is more abundant.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, among the most beloved of Allah's servants to Allah is the one to whom acts of kindness are made beloved, and to whom performing them is made beloved.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every act of kindness is charity, and the best of charity is that given from the back of affluence (ease), and begin with those you support, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and Allah does not blame the one who is in subsistence.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every act of kindness is a charity, and the one who points to the goodness is similar to its doer, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Loves the rescuers of the grief-stricken.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Ma'ruf (acts of kindness/goodness) is something besides the Zakat, so draw closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through righteousness and maintaining ties of kinship.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do the act of kindness to the one who is deserving of it, and to the one who is not deserving of it; for if he is not deserving of it, then you become the one who is deserving of it.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from a man from the people of Saabat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Ammar: 'O Ammar, you are a lord of much wealth?' He said: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So do you pay what Allah has obligated upon you from the zakat?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So do you take out the known (amount) from your wealth?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So you give it to your relatives?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So you give it to your brethren?' He said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ammar! The wealth perishes, and the body decays, but the deeds remain, and the Judge is Alive and does not die. O Ammar! Whatever you send forward, does not leave you behind; whatever you delay does not catch up with you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Hadeed ibn Hakeem or Murazam, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any believer who conveys a kindness to his believing brother, has thereby conveyed it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform acts of kindness to everyone; if he is deserving of it, [then good for him], and if not, then you are deserving of it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'ir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A Bedouin from the Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Advise me.' Among what he advised him with was that he said, 'O so-and-so! Do not be stingy regarding the act of kindness with its deserving ones.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn al-Walid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The first to enter Paradise will be Al-Ma'ruf and its people, and the first to arrive at my Basin (al-Hawd) will be [them].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Overlook the slips of the performers of acts of kindness and forgive them, for the hand of Allah, the Exalted, is over them like this,

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: Acts of kindness protect against evil encounters.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessing hastens more to the house from which kindness is sought/obtained, than the blade in the hump of the camel, or the flood to its destination.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The doing of acts of kindness repels the evil encounters.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Dawud ibn Farqad or Qutaybah al-A'sha, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, may our fathers and mothers be sacrificed for you. Indeed, the people of kindness (al-ma'ruf) in the world were known by their kindness, so by what will they be known in the Hereafter?' He said: 'Indeed, when Allah, Blessed and High, brings the people of Paradise into Paradise, He commands a sweet, fragrant wind, which clings to the people of kindness. So no one among them passes by a group of the people of Paradise except that they find their scent, so they say, 'This one is from the people of kindness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from one of our companions, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The people of kindness in the world are the people of kindness in the Hereafter. It will be said to them: 'Indeed, your sins have been forgiven for you, so gift your good deeds to whomever you wish.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people of kindness in the world are the people of kindness in the Hereafter, and the people of evil deeds in the world are the people of evil deeds in the Hereafter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for Paradise there is a gate called Al-Maʿrūf (Kindness/Goodness). None shall enter it except the people of Al-Maʿrūf. And the people of Al-Maʿrūf in the world are the people of Al-Maʿrūf in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'dan, from Hatim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I viewed that the act of kindness (al-ma'ruf) is not correct except with three characteristics: making it insignificant, concealing it, and hastening to it. For indeed, when you make it insignificant, you magnify it in the presence of the one to whom you are doing it; and when you conceal it, you complete it; and when you hasten to it, you make it welcoming; and if it were otherwise, you would trivialize it and cause annoyance.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'For everything is an outcome (fruit), and the outcome of the act of kindness is a quick relief (from distress).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Amira, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Mufaddal ibn Umar: 'O Mufaddal! If you wish to know whether a man is wretched or fortunate, look at his generosity and his kindness, to whom he directs them. If he directs them to those who are their rightful recipients, then know that he is destined for goodness; but if he directs them to those who are not their rightful recipients, then know that there is no goodness for him with Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Mufazzal! If you want to know whether a man is going towards goodness or towards evil, look at where he places his act of kindness. If he places his act of kindness with its rightful people, then know that he is going towards goodness. And if he places his act of kindness with other than its rightful people, then know that there is no share for him in the Hereafter from the Creator.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sulayman al-Bajali, from Ismail ibn al-Hasan ibn Ismail ibn Shu'ayb ibn Maysam al-Tammarr, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Madaini, from a man, from Abu Mikhnaf al-Azdi, who said: A group of the Shia came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! If you were to take out this wealth and distribute it among these chiefs and elites, preferring them over us, so that when affairs become established, you would return to what Allah has accustomed you to of equal distribution and justice among the subjects.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Are you instructing me, woe to you, that I should seek victory through injustice and tyranny against those whom I have been appointed over from the people of Islam? No, by Allah! That will not happen as long as the night-talker converses and a star is seen in the sky. By Allah, if their wealth were my wealth, I would equalize between them, so how [can I do so] when it is truly their wealth?' He said: Then he fell silent for a long time, then raised his head and said: 'Whoever among you has wealth, let him beware of corruption. For giving it in that which is not its right is wastefulness and extravagance. He raises the mention of his owner among the people but lowers him in the sight of Allah. And whoever places his wealth in that which is not its right and with those who are not its rightful recipients, Allah will deprive him of their gratitude, and their affection will be for others.' If there remains with him from them a remnant of those who manifest gratitude to him and show him sincerity, that is merely flattery and a lie. If a slipper slips from their owner, then he needs their assistance and reciprocity, he will be a close friend but a bad companion. And whoever places his wealth in that which is not its right and with those who are not its rightful recipients, he will not have from the share of what is given to him except the praise of the petty and the commendation of the evil, as long as he is bestowing favor upon them. The speech of the ignorant is 'How generous he is!', while he is stingy in the sight of Allah. So which share is more wicked and more loss-making than this share, and which benefit of goodness is less than this goodness? So whoever amon

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: If the people were to take (earn) what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had Commanded them with, and they spend it in what Allah has Forbidden them from, it would not be Accepted from them; and if they were to take (earn) what Allah has Forbidden them from, and they spend it in what Allah has Commanded them with, it would not be Accepted from them until they take it from its rightful way and spend it in a rightful manner.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Jameela, from Durays who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah has given you this surplus from the wealth so that you may direct it where Allah directs it, and He did not give it to you so that you may hoard it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not involve yourself in a matter for your brother whose harm upon you is greater than its benefit for him. Ibn Sinan said: It is like if there is a large debt upon a man and you have wealth, so you pay it off on his behalf; your wealth is spent, yet his debt is not cleared.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from the one who heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: Do not expend from yourself for your brethren what is more harmful to you than it is beneficial for them.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Jurjani, from the one who narrated it, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said: Do not obligate upon yourself the rights (of others), and be patient with calamities, and do not enter into something whose harm upon you is greater than its benefit for your brother.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah curse those who block the paths of kindness.' It was said, 'And what are those who block the paths of kindness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man receives a favor, but he fails to appreciate it, so the provider of the favor refrains from doing that same favor to others.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'How few are the ones who are grateful for the act of kindness'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is shown kindness, let him reciprocate it. If he is unable to do so, let him praise the one who did it. If he does not do so, he has been ungrateful for the favor.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: It is inscribed upon the door of Paradise: 'Charity is [rewarded] with ten, and the loan is with eighteen.' And in another report, 'fifteen'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no believer who lends to a believer, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, except that Allah will record for him his reward by accounting it as charity until his wealth returns to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of the Exalted: 'There is no good in most of their secret counsels except (in him) who enjoins charity or goodness.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He means by 'goodness', the loan.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Uqba ibn Khalid, who said: I, Al-Mu'alla, and Uthman ibn Imran entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). When he saw us, he said: 'Welcome, welcome to you! Faces that love us and we love them. May Allah make you with us in this world and the Hereafter.' Uthman said to him: 'May I be your ransom.' He said: 'Yes, what is it?' He said: 'I am an affluent man.' He said to him: 'May Allah bless you in your affluence.' A man comes to me and asks me for something, and it is not the time for my Zakat.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'The loan with us has eighteen [rewards], and charity has ten. And what is the harm upon you if you are as you say, affluent? Give it to him. So when it becomes the time of your Zakat, count it from the Zakat. O Uthman! Do not repel him, for repelling him is great with Allah.' O Uthman! If you knew the status of the Believer with his Lord, you would not slacken in fulfilling his need. And whoever brings joy to a Believer, he has brought it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And fulfilling the need of a Believer repels insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Ibrahim ibn al-Sindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A loan to the Believer is a booty, and haste is better. If he is affluent, he would pay it back, but if he were to die, you can count it as being from the Zakat.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Secretive charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Ammar! By Allah, charity given in secret is superior to charity given openly, and similarly, by Allah, worship performed in secret is superior to worship performed openly.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Secretive charity extinguishes the wrath of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'The one who wants that Allah should shade him on the Day when there is no shade except His shade' — saying it three times, and the people feared to ask him, so he said: 'Let him grant respite to the insolvent, or waive for him from his right.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said on a hot day, and he bent his palm: 'Who would like to be shaded from the outburst of Hell?' He said it three times, and the people said each time, 'Us, O Messenger of Allah!' So he said: 'The one who respites a debtor or leaves the insolvent.' Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik said to me, 'My father informed me that he necessitated a debtor of his in the Masjid. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came back and entered his house, and we were seated. Then he came out in the midday heat. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) uncovered his veil and said: 'O Ka'b! You two have not ceased to be seated?' He said, 'Yes, may my father and my mother be sacrificed for you.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gestured by his palm: 'Take the half.' He said, 'So I said, 'May my father and my mother be sacrificed for you.' Then he said: 'Pursue him for the remainder of your right.' He said, 'So I took the half and dropped for him the (other) half'.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Asbaat, from Yaqoub bin Salim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Free the way of the insolvent just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, frees it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Al-Hasan ibn Al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended the pulpit one day, praised Allah and extolled Him, and sent blessings upon His Prophets (peace be upon them), then said: 'O people! Let the present among you convey to the absent. Indeed, whoever grants respite to an insolvent person, for him with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is a charity equal to his wealth every day until he pays it back in full.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he is in hardship, then respite until he becomes able (to pay). And giving it as charity is better for you if you know that he is insolvent, so give charity on his behalf with your wealth, for that is better for you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Hasan ibn Khunays, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'There is a debt due for Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyaba upon a man who has died, and we had spoken to him that he should release him (from the debt), but he refused.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to him! Does he not know that for him there would be ten [times the value] for each dirham when he releases him? So when he does not release him, rather there would be one dirham for him in exchange for one dirham.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Walid ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Mu'tab, who said: Muhammad ibn Bishr al-Washa' came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him to speak to Shihab so that he would lighten the burden on him until the season (of Hajj) expired. There was a debt of one thousand dinars owed to him by Muhammad. So he (the Imam) sent for him, and he came to him. The Imam said to him: 'You know the state of Muhammad and his cutting off from people to be with us, and he has mentioned that you have a thousand dinars owed to you by him, which have not gone into a belly or a private part (marriage), but have gone as a debt on men and expenses he incurred. And I would love for you to make him free from it.' Shihab said: 'Perhaps you are from those who claim that good deeds are taken from him and given to me.' He said: 'That is so in our hands (the narrations).' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah is more Generous and more Just than that His servant comes close to Him, stands in the clear night (in prayer), or fasts in the hot day, or circumambulates this House, and then He strips him of that and gives it to you. But Allah has abundant bounty that suffices the believer.' So Shihab said: 'Then he is free (from my debt).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Suleyman al-Farra', the freedman of Tirbal, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever upon whom the bounties of Allah are magnified, the provision/cost of the people upon him intensifies. Therefore, preserve the bounties by bearing the provision/cost, and do not expose them to decline, for rarely does the bounty leave a person and nearly return to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Abu Ayyub al-Madani, the freedman of the Banu Hashim, from Dawud ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ja'fari, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant upon whom the bounties of Allah have become manifest, except that the provision/cost of the people upon him intensifies. So whoever does not attend to the needs of the people, he has exposed the bounty to perishing.' He said: 'I said: May I be your ransom, and who has the ability to attend to the needs of this creation?' He said: 'Rather, the people in this regard, by Allah, are the believers.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Husayn al-Sahhaf: 'O Husayn! Allah does not manifest the bounties upon a servant until he manifests the provision/cost of the people upon him. So whoever is patient for them and stands by their affairs, Allah will increase His bounties upon him in their eyes; and whoever is not patient for them and does not stand by their affairs, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will remove that bounty from him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever upon whom the bounties are magnified, the provision of the people becomes heavy upon him; so if he stands with their provision, he attracts an increase of the bounties upon him from Allah, and if he does not do so, he has exposed the bounty to its removal.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Arafat, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ibn Arafat! The bounties are like the camels tethered in their enclosure. It is upon the people how good they are in their vicinity. So if they are bad in their treatment and receiving them, they flee from them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Be good in the vicinity of the Bounty.' I said, 'And what is being good in the vicinity of the Bounty?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The gratefulness to the one who has favoured (you) with it, and fulfilments of its rights.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Improve your dwelling with the bounties of Allah, and beware lest they be transferred from you to others. Indeed, they have never been transferred from anyone except that they almost returned to him.' He said: 'And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: It is rare for something to turn away and then face you again.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ahmad ibn Suleyman, who said: A man asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was circumambulating (the Kaaba), and said to him: 'Inform me about 'al-Jawad' (the Benevolent/Generous).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your speech has two aspects. If you are asking about the created, then the 'Jawad' is the one who fulfills what Allah has obligated upon him. And if you are asking about the Creator, then He is the 'Jawad' if He gives, and He is the 'Jawad' if He withholds, because if He gives to you, He gives you what is not yours, and if He withholds from you, He withholds what is not for you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the limit of generosity?' He said, 'You give out from your wealth the right that Allah has obligated upon you, and place it in its appropriate place.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ja'far, from his fathers (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The generous one is beloved in the heavens, beloved in the earth; he was created from sweet clay, and the water of his eyes was created from the water of Al-Kawthar. And the stingy one is hated in the heavens, hated in the earth; he was created from salty/marshy clay, and the water of his eyes was created from the water of Al-Awsaj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Mahdi, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: The generous one of good character is under the shelter of Allah; Allah does not leave him alone until He enters him into Paradise. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet or Successor except as a generous one. And there was never anyone from the righteous except as a generous one. And my father never ceased to advise me with generosity until he passed away. And he said: 'The one who takes out the complete Zakat from his wealth, and places it in its proper place, will not be questioned: From where did you earn your wealth?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Saeed al-Mukari, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A delegation from Yemen came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and among them was a man who was their greatest speaker and the most intense in questioning during his argument with the Prophet (peace be upon him). So the Prophet (peace be upon him) became angry until the vein of anger swelled between his eyes, his face darkened, and he looked down to the ground. Then Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: 'Your Lord conveys His greeting to you and says to you: This is a generous man who feeds food.' So the anger subsided from the Prophet (peace be upon him), and he raised his head and said to him: 'Had Jibraeel not informed me from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that you are generous and feed food, I would have expelled you and made you a topic of discussion for those who come after you.' The man said to him: 'And indeed, your Lord loves generosity?' He said: 'Yes.' The man said: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah; and by the One who sent you with the truth, I shall not turn away anyone from my wealth.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was the father of guests. So when they were not with him, he would go out seeking them, close his door, take the keys, and go out seeking the guests. And when he returned to his house, he found a man, or someone resembling a man, in the house. So he said: 'O servant of Allah, by whose permission did you enter this house?' He said: 'I entered it by the permission of its Lord.' He repeated that three times. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) recognized that it was Jibraeel (peace be upon him). So he (Jibraeel) praised Allah, then said: 'Your Lord has sent me to a servant from His servants to take him as a close friend.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'So inform me who he is, so I may serve him until I die.' He said: 'You are he.' He said: 'And why is that so?' He said: 'Because you never asked anyone for anything, and you were never asked for anything, so you said, "No."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, which of the people are the most superior in faith?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The most generous of them (those who spread their hand the most).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yahya, from Ayub ibn Ayn, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'On the Day of Resurrection, a man will be brought forth and it will be said to him: 'Present your argument.' He will say: 'O Lord, You created me and guided me, and You expanded sustenance upon me. I did not cease to expand upon Your creatures and make things easy for them, so that You would spread Your mercy upon me on this Day and make it easy for me.' So the Lord, Exalted is His Praise and High is His Mention, will say: 'My servant speaks the truth. Admit him into Paradise.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The generous one is close to Allah, close to Paradise, and close to the people.' And I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Generosity is a tree in Paradise; whoever holds onto one of its branches will enter Paradise.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Yasar al-Khadim, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The generous one eats the food of the people so that they would be eating from his food; and the stingy one does not eat from the food of the people so that perhaps they might eat from his food.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said to his son Al-Hassan (peace be upon him): 'O my son! What is generosity?' He said: 'Giving during ease and hardship.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Shall I inform you of something that brings one closer to Allah, closer to Paradise, and farther from the Fire? He said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Adopt generosity, for Allah created His creation with His mercy for His mercy, so He made them worthy of kindness and a place for goodness, and a face for people to strive towards, in order to revive them just as rain revives the arid land. Those are the believers, the secure ones on the Day of Judgment.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'Do not kill the Samiry, for he is generous.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Ja'far al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A generous youth, burdened with sins, is more beloved to Allah than a worshipping stingy old man.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from a man, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the sun rises and with it are four Angels. One Angel calls out: 'O performer of the goodness, complete (it) and receive glad tidings!' And an Angel calls out: 'O performer of the evil, remove (it) and shorten (it)!' And an Angel calls out: 'Giving the expenses remains behind and withholding is damaging!' And an Angel sprinkles it (the earth) with the water, and had it not been for that, the ground would burst.

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Usman ibn Isa, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic Thus will Allah show them their deeds to be intense regret to them He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the man who leaves his wealth and does not spend it in obedience to Allah out of stinginess, then he dies leaving it for the one who works with it in obedience to Allah or in disobedience to Allah. So if he works with it in obedience to Allah, he sees it in the Scale of someone else, so he experiences regret, and the wealth was once his; but if he works with it in disobedience to Allah, that wealth enables him (the spender) to disobey Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Rashid, from Sama'ah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is certain of the Replacement (by Allah), his soul will be generous with expenditure.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Whoever extends his hand with kindness when he finds the means, Allah will replace for him what he spent in his world, and multiply it for him in his Hereafter.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'dan, from Al-Husayn ibn Ayman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'O Husayn! Spend and have certainty in the Replacement from Allah, for neither will a slave nor a maid be stingy with expenditure regarding what Pleases Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that they would end up spending in what Angers Allah, Mighty and Majestic'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Allah sends down aid (provision) from the sky to the servant in proportion to the expenditure. So whoever is certain of the Replacement (Allah's return), his soul will be generous with spending.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: A slave of his came to him, so he said to him: 'Have you spent anything today?' He said, 'No, by Allah.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'From where will Allah replace upon us? Spend, and even if it is one dirham.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He who guarantees four [qualities] with four [verses/verses of guidance] will be in Paradise: Spend [in the way of God] and do not fear poverty, and do justice to the people from yourself [even if it is against you], and spread the greeting of peace throughout the world, and leave argumentation even if you are right.

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who guarantees four [things] with four [verses/concepts] will be in Paradise: Spend and do not fear poverty, and be just to people regarding yourself, and spread peace throughout the world, and avoid argument even if you are right.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) heard a man saying: "A greedy person is more treacherous than an unjust person." He (the Imam) said to him, "You are mistaken. An unjust person may repent, seek forgiveness, and return the usurped property to its owners." But a greedy person, when he exercises greed, withholds Zakat, charity, maintaining kinship ties, hosting guests, spending in the way of Allah, and the gates of virtue." And it is forbidden for Paradise to admit a greedy person.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When Allah has no need for a servant, He tests him with stinginess.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to the Clan of Salima: 'O Clan of Salima, who is your master and leader?' They replied, 'O Messenger of Allah, our chief is a man who is stingy.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) then said, 'And what illness is more severe than stinginess?' Then he said, 'Rather, your chief is the one with the white body, Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abu al-Jahm, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: The miser is the one who is miserly with what Allah has Obligated upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is nothing which obliterates Islam as much as greed obliterates it.' Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For this greed has a creeping nature like the creeping of an ant, and branches like the branches of polytheism.' And in another copy, 'thorns'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He is not considered stingy who pays the obligatory Zakat on his wealth and gives the dowry among his people.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know what the greedy one (al-shahih) is?' I said, 'He is the miser (al-bakhil).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Greed (al-shuh) is more severe than miserliness. Indeed, the miser is stingy with what is in his hand, but the greedy one is greedy for what is in the hands of people and for what is in his own hands, until he sees nothing in the hands of people but wishes it were his, whether by permissible or prohibited means, and he is not content with what Allah has granted him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He is not the miser who pays the obligatory zakat from his wealth and gives the distinct gifts among his people. Rather, the true miser is the one who does not pay the obligatory zakat from his wealth, and does not give the distinct gifts among his people, and he squanders in what is besides that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Sufyan from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A time will come upon the people when the one who asks the people will live and the one who remains silent will die. I said, 'So what should I do if I attain that time?' He said, 'Assist them with what is with you, and if you do not find (material means), then strive (for it).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abdul A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most virtuous charity is that which is given from a position of wealth (without need for return).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most superior of charities is a charity that comes from the surplus of the hand.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And feed the desperate one, the poor.' He said: 'He is the chronically ill person who is unable to go out due to his chronic illness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd ibn Tareyf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then as for him who gives and is pious and believes in that which is best [reward], Allah the Exalted will give for one [good deed] tenfold or up to a hundred thousand; so what is more We will facilitate for him the easy [end].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not desire any good except that Allah makes it easy for him.' And as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient, [the Imam] said: 'He is stingy with what Allah gave him and rejects the best [reward], believing that Allah gives tenfold or up to a hundred thousand for one [good deed]; so what is more We will facilitate for him the difficult [end].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not desire any evil except that Allah makes it easy for him.' And his wealth will not avail him when he falls.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, he does not fall into a well, nor from a mountain, nor from a wall, but he falls into the Fire of Hell.'

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: 'There is no thing except that I have assigned to it one who takes possession of it other than Me, except for charity (sadaqah), for I receive it with My Hand with a reception, to the extent that a man gives charity with a single date or half a date, so I nurture it for him just as a man nurtures his foal and his young camel, so it comes on the Day of Resurrection and it is like Mount Uhud and greater than Mount Uhud.'
