A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman al-Azramy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and they were both seated upon the Safa (mat). So he begged from them, so they said: 'Charity is not permissible except for a painful debt, or a repulsive loss, or abject poverty. So, is there anything from this in you?' He said, 'Yes'. So they gave him. And the man had begged from Abdullah ibn Umar and Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, and they had given him and had not asked him about anything. So he returned to them and said to them, 'What is the matter with you? You did not ask me about what Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) asked me?' And he informed them with what they had said. So they said, 'Those two have been fed with the food of knowledge'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from the one who narrated to him, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not ask my community in their gatherings, so you would make them miserly.'

And in another report, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Spend from the good things that you earn,' so he said: 'The people had earned evil earnings during the Pre-Islamic period. So when they became Muslims, they wanted to take these out from their wealth in order to give charity with it. So, Allah, Blessed and High, Refused except that they should take out from the good of what they had been earning.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'I am an old man with many dependents, weak in strength, and possessing little wealth. Is there any assistance for my time?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) looked at his companions, and his companions looked at him. He said: 'He has made us hear the speech, and made you all hear it.' Then a man stood up to him and said: 'I was like you yesterday.' So he took him to his house and gave him an ingot of gold. They used to trade with the ingot, which was gold and silver. The old man said: 'Is this all of it?' He said: 'Yes.' The old man said: 'I accept your ingot, for I am neither a jinn nor a human, but I am a Messenger from Allah to test you. I found you to be grateful, so may Allah recompense you with good.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When one of you is constrained (in wealth), let him inform his brother, and he should not support himself (by hiding his need).
Muhammad ibn Ali from Ma'mar, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said in one of his sermons: 'The most superior deed is maintaining the dignity with the wealth'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There are three things; if the Believer knows them, they will result in an increase in his lifespan and the continuation of blessings upon him.' So I said, 'And what are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His prolonging his bowing and prostration in his prayer, and his prolonging his sitting with his food when he is feeding others at his table, and his doing kindness to his family.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'A group of people have excess wealth with them, and their brethren have an intense need, and the Zakat is not sufficient for them. Is it permissible for them to be satiated while their brethren are hungry, for indeed the times are difficult?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not wrong him, nor abandon him, nor deprive him. So it is incumbent upon the Muslims to strive regarding him, to maintain good relations, to assist him, and to show sympathy to the needy. And the kindness from you should be upon what Allah has commanded regarding them: compassionate among themselves being merciful to each other

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and others, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: From the obligatory causes of Allah's forgiveness, Blessed and Exalted is, feeding of food.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'From the faith is good character and feeding the food.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from the one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of you is the one who feeds food, spreads greetings, and prats while the people are sleeping.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Umar ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'We, the People of the Household, have been commanded to feed food, and to give gifts among the people, and to pray when the people sleep.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Fayz ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The redeemers are: feeding food, spreading greetings, and prayer at night while people are sleeping.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves the spilling of blood and the feeding of food.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Among the most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is satisfying the hunger of the believer, or relieving his distress, or paying off his debt.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the feeding of food and the spilling of blood.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Captives were brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and a man from them was presented to have his neck struck. So Jibra'il said to him: 'Delay this one for today, O Muhammad.' So he returned him and brought out another, until he was the last of them. So he called for him to have his neck struck, but Jibra'il said to him: 'O Muhammad, your Lord conveys greetings to you and says to you: This captive of yours feeds food, entertains guests, is patient in adversity, and carries burdens.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Jibra'il has informed me about you from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with such and such.' And I have hereby emancipated you.' He said to him: 'Does your Lord love this?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah, and you are the Messenger of Allah, and by the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, I shall not repel anyone from my wealth, ever!'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: The sustenance is quicker to the one who feeds the food than the knife in the hump (of a camel).

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: 'Among the causes that necessitate the forgiveness of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is feeding food.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muammar ibn Khallad, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), whenever he ate, would be brought a platter which was placed near his table. He would select the best of the foods that were brought, take a bit of each, and place them in that platter. Then he would order for it to be given to the poor. But he will not attempt the uphill road Then he would say: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that not every human being is able to emancipate a neck, so He made for them the way to Paradise.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Let the man spend with moderation and sufficiency, and he should forward the surplus from it for his Hereafter, for that is more lasting for the bounties, and closer to the increase from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and more beneficial regarding good health.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, moderation is a matter which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves, and indeed, extravagance is a matter which Allah hates, to the extent of your throwing the date-stone, for it is suitable for something, and to your pouring out the remainder of your drink.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And they ask you about what they should spend. Say: The spare (al-'afw).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The spare is the middle (moderate amount).'
Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said, Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: The moderation (leads to) prosperity, and the extravagance (leads to) ruination.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three are redeemers.' So he mentioned the third as being moderation in wealth and in poverty.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Mudrik ibn Abi Al-Hazhaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'I guarantee for the one who is moderate that he will not be impoverished.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Hammad ibn Waqid al-Lahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man were to spend whatever was in his hands in the way of Allah, it would not be better, nor would he be successful. Is it not that Allah the Exalted says: 'And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, and do good; surely Allah loves the doers of good'? Meaning the moderate ones (in spending).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from his father Ubayd, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ubayd! Extravagance begets poverty, and moderation begets wealth.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'A person will not be in poverty (while observing) moderation'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Abd al-Aziz, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: We are on the road to Mecca and wish to enter the state of Ihram, so we apply oil, but there is no lime with us with which we scrub off the oil, so we scrub with flour. And a thought entered me regarding that, which Allah knows best. He said: 'Is it fear of extravagance?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'There is no extravagance in what improves the body. Indeed, I sometimes order the pure [oil] to be rubbed in with oil, so I massage with it. But rather, extravagance is in what spoils wealth and harms the body.' I said: 'So what is austerity?' He said: 'Eating bread and salt while you are able to have something else.' I said: 'So what is moderation?' He said: 'Bread, meat, milk, vinegar, and butter; once this and once that.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is generous with you, then be generous, and when He withholds from you, then withhold, and do not try to out-generous Allah, for He is the Most Generous.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is moderate in his living, Allah would Grace him, and the one who squanders (wastes), Allah would Deprive him'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Hassan, from Musa bin Bakr who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ease and gentleness is half of one's sustenance, and a person would not be impoverished in his moderation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to wait until darkness fell and half the night had passed, then take a sack containing bread, meat, and dirhams, carry it upon his neck, and go with it to the needy people of al-Medina, distributing it among them while they did not recognize him. When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed away, they noticed the absence of that and came to know that it had been Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a male beggar comes to you at night, do not turn him away.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out during a night in which it had drizzled, and he was intending to go to the canopy of the Banu Sa'ida. So I followed him, and there was something that had fallen from him, and he said: 'In the name of God; O God, return it to us.' Then I came to him and greeted him. Then he said: 'Mu'alla?' I said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' So he said to me: 'Search with your hand, and whatever you find, hand it over to me.' So I found a great deal of scattered bread, and I kept handing him whatever I found. Then I was faced with a sack of bread that I was unable to carry. So I said: 'May I be your ransom! Let me carry it on my head.' He said: 'No, I have more right to it than you. But come along with me.' He said: So we came to the canopy of Banu Sa'ida, and we found a group of people sleeping there. He went on tucking the bread — one loaf and two loaves — until he reached the last of them. Then we left. So I said: 'May I be your ransom! Do these people know the truth?' He said: 'If they had known it, we would have shared with them the fine seasoning — and the fine seasoning is salt.' Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted, has not created anything except that it has a treasurer who stores it — except for charity, for the Lord attends to it Himself. And my father, when he gave something in charity, would place it in the hand of the beggar, then take it back from him, kiss it and smell it, then return it to the hand of the beggar. A charity given at night extinguishes the anger of the Lord, erases great sin, and eases the reckoning. And a charity given by day yields wealth and increases one's lifespan. When Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon them both) passed by the shore of the sea, he threw a morsel from his provisions into the water. Some of the disciples said to him: 'O Spirit of God and His Word! Why did you do that, when it was from your own provisions?' He said: 'I did that for an animal from among the animals of the water to eat, and its reward with God is great.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr Al-Ahwal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited this verse: 'And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are moderate between those [extremes]'. He said: So he took a handful of pebbles and closed his hand tightly around them, then said: 'This is the stinginess (al-iqtar) which Allah mentioned in His book'. Then he took another handful, so he opened his palm completely, then said: 'This is the extravagance (al-israf)'. Then he took another handful, so he opened part of it and withheld part of it, and said: 'This is the moderation (al-qawam)'.

And from him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from 'Abdullah ibn Aban, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the spending upon the dependants, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is between the two (limits of) abhorrence – the extravagance and the miserliness'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Ibn Abi Yaf'ur and Yusuf ibn 'Umara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, with extravagance is scarcity of blessing.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Often a poor person is more extravagant than the rich one. Indeed, the rich one spends from what he has been given, and the poor one spends from that which does not belong to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And give its due on the day of its reaping, and do not be extravagant; surely He does not love the extravagant.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So-and-so, the Ansari (he mentioned his name), had a farm. When he harvested it, he would give it all in charity, leaving himself and his dependents with nothing. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made that extravagance.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not make your hand shackled to your neck, nor extend it completely, lest you sit blameworthy and regretful.' He said: 'Al-ih'sar is poverty/destitution.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ajlan, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). A beggar came, so he stood up to a basket containing dates, filled his hand, and offered it to him. Then another came and asked him, so he stood, took a handful with his hand, and offered it to him. Then another came and asked him, so he stood, took a handful with his hand, and offered it to him. Then another came and asked him, so he stood, took a handful with his hand, and offered it to him. Then another came, so he said: 'May Allah be our and your Provider.' Then he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was such that no one asked him for anything from the world except that he gave it to him. So a woman sent her son to him, saying: 'Go to him and ask him. If he says to you, And in another copy, 'So he gave it to him, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, taught him moderation, so He said:

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, Regarding the Words of the Exalted: 'And those who, when they spend, do not squander nor are stingy, but maintain a middle ground.' So he (peace be upon him) extended his palm, separated his fingers, and tilted them slightly. And regarding the Words of the Exalted: 'Nor extend it completely.' So he (peace be upon him) extended his palm and said: 'Like this.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The moderation (qawam) is what slips out from between the fingers, while something of it remains in the palm.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleyman ibn Salih who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the lowest degree of what comes from the limit of extravagance?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Your devaluing your kept garment, and pouring out the excess from your vessel, and you eating the dates and throwing the pits here and there.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ammar Abu Aasim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There are four for whom (supplications) would not be Answered – One of them is the one for whom is wealth, so he spoils it, then he is saying, ‘O Lord, Grace me!’ So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “Did I not Command you with the moderation?’

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The first thing that is begun with in the Hereafter is the charity of water, meaning regarding the recompense.'

Muhammad, from Abdullah bin Muhammad, from Ali bin Al-Hakam, from Aban bin Uthman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The most superior of the charities is cooling a parched liver (quenching one's thirst).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever provides water in a place where water is found is like the one who emancipates a slave; and whoever provides water in a place where water is not found is like the one who revives a soul; and whoever revives a soul is as if he has revived all people.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazim, from Musadif who said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) between Mecca and Medina, so we passed by a man at the base of a tree who had thrown himself down (fainted). He said: 'Let us go to this man, for I fear that he has been struck by thirst.' So we went, and there was a man from the Faraseen (Romans/Byzantines) with long hair. He asked him: 'Are you thirsty?' He said: 'Yes.' He said to me: 'Descend, O Musadif, and give him water.' So I descended and gave him water, then I rode, and we went. So I said: 'This is a Christian man. Do you give charity to a Christian?' He said: 'Yes, when they are in a state like this.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abu al-Bilad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Teach me a deed by which I may enter Paradise.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Feed people and spread the greeting of peace.' The Bedouin said, 'I cannot endure that.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Do you have camels?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'So look after a camel and provide water for it for a family who do not drink water except intermittently, so that perhaps your camel will not be exhausted and your water-skin will not be damaged until Paradise becomes obligatory for you.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves cooling the hot liver (of the thirsty), and whoever gives a drink to a hot liver from an animal or from another source, Allah will shade him on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a group of the Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him to appoint them over the charities of the livestock, saying, 'Let this portion which Allah has made for the workers upon it be for us, for we are more deserving of it.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'O sons of Abdul Muttalib! Indeed, charity is not permissible for me nor for you, but I have been promised intercession.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, he (peace be upon him and his family) has indeed been promised it. So what is your opinion, O sons of Abdul Muttalib, when I take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise? Do you see me giving preference to others over you?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charity is the dirt of the hands of the people, and Allah has prohibited for me from it, and from other than it, that which He has prohibited, and indeed, charity is not permissible for the children of Abdul Muttalib.' Then he said: 'By Allah, if I were to stand at the door of Paradise and grab its ring, you would know that I would not prefer anyone over you. So be pleased with yourselves for what Allah and His Messenger are pleased with for you.' They said: 'We are pleased.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Is the charity permissible for the Banu Hashim?' He said: 'That is the obligatory charity upon the people, it is not permissible for us. As for that which is other than that, there is no problem with it. And if it were like that, they would not be able to go out to Makkah. The majority of these waters are charity.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Abdullah Al-A'raj, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the charity permissible for the mawalis (clients/freedmen) of Banu Hashim?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the charity which is prohibited upon the Banu Hashim, what is it? He said: It is the Zakat. I said: So is the charity of some of them permissible upon others? He said: Yes.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Give the Zakat to those of the Banu Hashim who desire it, for it is permissible for them, and it is prohibited only upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the Imam who comes after him, and the Imams, may the prayers of Allah be upon them all.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Yazeed, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is not able to maintain good relations with us, let him maintain good relations with the poor of our Shias; and the one who is not able to visit our graves, let him visit the graves of the righteous of our brethren.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Nawfali, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who extends a hand of favor to one of my family members, I shall suffice him on the Day of Resurrection.'

And from him, from his father, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I will be an intercessor on the Day of Judgement for four types of people, and even though they may have come with the sins of the people of the world – a man who helped my children; and a man who spent his wealth for my descendants during constraints; and a man who loved my children by the tongue and by the heart; and a man who strived regarding the needs of my children when they were either expelled or displaced.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to ask Shihab to give from his Zakat for his mawali (clients/slaves), and indeed, the Zakat was prohibited upon them (the Imams), but not upon their mawali.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'If you disclose your charitable expenditures, it is good,' he said: 'He means the obligatory Zakat.' I said: 'And if you conceal it and give it to the poor?' He said: 'He means the voluntary charity.' Indeed, they used to prefer the manifestation of the obligatory duties and the concealment of the voluntary ones.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from the one who narrated it, from Moalla ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the zakat that is obligatory upon me in a place where I cannot pay it. He said: 'Set it aside. If you trade with it, you are responsible for it, and the profit belongs to it. And if you die while it is set aside, without having employed it in trade, there is nothing upon you. And if you do not set it aside and trade with it in the entirety of your wealth, then for it is its share of the profit, and there is no expense upon it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mu'adh ibn Kathir said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Leeway is given to our Shias to spend from what is in their hands in a good manner. So when our Qaim rises, it will be prohibited for every owner of a treasure to hoard his treasure until he brings it to him, so that he may use it to assist against his enemy.' And this is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah, give them tidings of a painful punishment.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Fortify your wealth with the Zakat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, charity pays off debt and replaces it with blessing.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: al-Jahm ibn al-Hakam al-Mada'ini narrated to me, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Give charity, for indeed charity increases wealth abundantly, and give charity — may God have mercy upon you.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Muhammad, his son: 'O my son! How much remains with you from those expenses?' He said, 'Forty dinars.' He said: 'Bring it out and give charity with it.' He said, 'Nothing else remains with me other than it.' He said: 'Give charity with it, for God Mighty and Majestic will replace it. Do you not know that for everything there is a key, and the key to provision is charity? So give charity with it.' So he did it, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had not waited ten days before four thousand dinars came to him from a source. Then he said: 'O my son! We gave forty dinars to God, and God gave us four thousand dinars.'
He said, and Ali ibn Hassan narrated to me, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Cause the sustenance to descend by charity.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'No servant gives good charity in this world except that God betters the succession over his children after him.' And he said: 'Good charity pays off debts and leaves behind blessing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamila, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'Whoever maintains ties with a relative through a hajj or an umrah, God will record for him two hajjs and two umrahs. And similarly, whoever bears a burden on behalf of a close friend, God will multiply his reward twofold.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: 'Which charity is most superior?' He said: 'That given to a relative who is hostile.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charity carries ten (rewards), and a loan carries eighteen, and maintaining ties with (religious) brethren carries twenty, and maintaining family ties carries twenty-four.'

Several of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The most pleasing of you to God is the one who is most generous toward his dependants.

A man said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I have an estate in the mountain from which I profit three thousand dirhams every year. I spend two thousand dirhams of it on my dependants, and I give one thousand dirhams of it in charity every year.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If the two thousand suffices them for all that they need for their year, then you have been considerate for yourself, and been guided to your right conduct, and you have placed yourself during your lifetime at the status of what the living one bequeaths at his death.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: 'It is befitting for the man that he extends provision to his dependants, lest they wish for his death.' [And he recited this verse:] 'And they give food out of love for Him to the poor and the orphan and the captive' [76:8]. He said: 'The captive is the man's dependants. It is befitting for the man, when there is an increase in bounty, that he increases upon his captives in the extent of their provision.' Then he said: 'So-and-so — God bestowed bounty upon him, but he withheld it from his captives and gave it to so-and-so, so God took it away.' Mu'ammar said: And that so-and-so was present.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Rabi' ibn Yazid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The upper hand is better than the lower hand, and begin with those whom you support.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: The owner of bounty is obligated to extend generously to his dependants.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The believer eats by the desire of his family, and the hypocrite — his family eats by his desire.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his father, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Did the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to provide his dependants with a goodly provision?' He said: 'Yes. The soul, when it recognizes its provision, is content with it and the flesh grows upon it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It suffices as a sin for a person that he wastes/neglects those whom he provides for.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Ansari, from Ali ibn Ghurab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Accursed, accursed is the one who throws his burden upon the people! Accursed, accursed is the one who wastes those whom he provides for.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Hamzah, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'To enter the market with me having dirhams to buy meat with it for my dependents, and they have desired it, is more beloved to me than if I were to emancipate a person.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when it was morning, would go out early in search of livelihood. So it was said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, where are you going?' He said, 'To give charity to my dependents.' It was said to him, 'Do you give charity?' He said, 'The one who seeks the permissible (halal), it is a charity from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon him.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The believer adheres to the discipline of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When He expands [his provision], he expands, and when He withholds [from him], he withholds.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Murazim, from Muaz ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is from the good fortune of the man that he happens to be the overseer upon his dependants.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser al-Khadim, who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is befitting for the Believer that he reduces from the provision of his dependants during the winter and increases in their fuel.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Who are those towards whom I incline and whose maintenance is obligatory upon me?' He said: 'The two parents, and the child, and the wife.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: An orphan was brought to Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of Allah upon him), and he said: 'Let the closest person to him from his clan bear his expenses, just as they would consume his inheritance.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: 'Who among a man's relatives is obligated upon him to spend on?' He said: 'The two parents, and the child/children, and the wife.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Sadir al-Sayrafi who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Shall I feed a beggar whom I do not know to be a Muslim?' He said: 'Yes, give to one whom you do not know to have wilayah or enmity toward the Truth.' Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And speak good words to the people' (2:83). And do not feed one who has declared hostility against something of the Truth, or calls toward something of falsehood.

He was asked about the beggar who asks and it is not known what he is. He said: Give to the one for whom mercy occurs in your heart. And he said: Give less than one Dirham. I said: What is the most one can give? He said: Four Dawaneeqs.

Islam is built upon five things: upon salat (prayer), and zakat (alms-tax), and hajj (pilgrimage), and sawm (fasting), and al-wilayah (guardianship). And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The fast is a shield from the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: 'Shall I not inform you of something that, if you were to do it, Satan would distance himself from you just as the East is distanced from the West?' They said, 'Yes (please).' He said: 'The Fast blackens his face, charity breaks his back, love for the sake of Allah and cooperation in righteous deeds cuts off his followers, and seeking forgiveness cuts off his vital vein; and for everything is a purification (zakat), and the zakat of the bodies is fasting.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba, from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I inform you of the root of Islam, its branch, its peak, and its high point?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Its root is salat, its branch is zakat, and its peak and high point is jihad in the way of God. Shall I inform you of the doors of goodness? Fasting is a shield.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr who said: For every thing there is a zakat, and the zakat of bodies is the fast.

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: My father said: 'Verily, a man fasts one day voluntarily, seeking what is in the presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah enters him into Paradise through it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Salama Sahib al-Sabiri, from Abu al-Sabbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah — Blessed and Exalted — says: The fast is for Me, and I shall recompense upon it.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sulayman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And seek assistance with patience' he said: 'Patience is fasting.' And he said: 'When an affliction and difficulty befalls a man, let him fast, for God, Mighty and Majestic, is saying: "And seek assistance with patience," meaning fasting.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mundhir ibn Yazid, from Yunus ibn Zabyan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever fasts for the sake of God, Mighty and Majestic, for a day during intense heat and thirst strikes him, God assigns a thousand angels with him, wiping his face and giving him glad tidings. Until when he breaks the fast, God, Mighty and Majestic, says to him: How sweet is your fragrance and your spirit! My angels, bear witness that I have indeed forgiven him.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The fasting person is in a state of worship, even if he is on his bed, as long as he does not backbite a Muslim.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever conceals his fast, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His angels: 'My servant seeks refuge from My punishment, so grant him refuge.' And Allah, the Exalted, has assigned His angels to supplicate for the fasting ones, and He did not command them to supplicate for anyone except that He answers them regarding it.

Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, assigned His angels to supplicate for the fasting ones. And he (peace be upon him) said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) informed me from his Lord that He said: 'I did not command My angels to supplicate for anyone of My creation except that I answered them regarding it.'
And by this chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The sleep of the fasting one is worship, and his breathing is glorification.

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Might and Majestic, Revealed unto Musa (peace be upon him): 'What prevents you from whispering to Me?' So he said: 'O Lord! I delay from the whispering due to the smell of the mouth of a fasting one.' So Allah, Might and Majestic, Revealed unto him: 'O Musa! The smell of the mouth of a fasting one is more aromatic in My Presence than the smell of musk.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqa, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Have a midday nap, for Allah feeds the fasting one and quenches him in his sleep.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Salma (the companion of Al-Sabiri), from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: For the fasting one there are two joys: a joy at the time of his breaking the fast, and a joy at the time of meeting his Lord.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Samman al-Armani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the fasting one sees a group of people eating, or a man eating, every hair of his supplicates for him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Munzir ibn Yazeed, from Yunus ibn Zibyan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who fasts for the sake of Allah for a day in intense heat, so thirst hits him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigns a thousand angels to him, wiping his face and giving him glad tidings. Until when he breaks his fast, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "How aromatic is your fragrance and your spirit. My angels! Bear witness that I have forgiven him."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you fast, let your hearing, your vision, your hair, and your skin fast, and he enumerated other things besides this, and he said: 'The day of your fasting should not be like the day of your breaking (fasting)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Kazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Jabir ibn Abdullah: 'O Jabir! This is the month of Ramadan. Whoever fasts its day, stands in prayer from its night, keeps his belly and private parts chaste, and restrains his tongue, will emerge from his sins as he emerged from the month.' So Jabir said: 'O Messenger of Allah! How beautiful is this hadith!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Jabir! And how severe/difficult are these conditions.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, fasting is not merely abstaining from food and drink. Then he said: Maryam said, 'I have vowed a fast to the Beneficent,' i.e., a fast of silence. And in another copy: 'i.e., silence.' So when you fast, preserve your tongues, lower your gaze, do not dispute, and do not envy. He said: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) heard a woman insulting her maid while she was fasting. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called for food and said to her, 'Eat.' She said, 'I am fasting.' He said, 'How can you be fasting when you have insulted your slave girl? Indeed, fasting is not merely from food and drink.' He said: And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast from the prohibited and the ugly, leave off quarreling and hurting the servant, and let the dignity of fasting be upon you, and do not make the day of your fasting like the day of your breaking fast.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyub, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When one of you fasts the three days of the month, he should not dispute with anyone, nor act ignorantly, nor be hasty to swear and make oaths by Allah. If anyone acts ignorantly towards him, let him bear it (patiently).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no righteous servant who is insulted, so he says, “I am fasting. Peace be upon you. I shall not insult you just as you have insulted me,” except that the Lord, Blessed and High, says: “My servant sought protection with fasting from the evil of My servant, so I have protected him from the Fire.”'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Poetry (or recitation) should not be sought/recited at night, nor should it be sought/recited during the month of Ramadan at night or by day. So Ismail said to him, 'O my father! Indeed, it is among us.' He said, 'And even if it is among us.'

And by this chain, he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when it was the month of Ramadan, would not speak except with supplication, glorification, seeking forgiveness, and glorification (Takbeer). So when he broke his fast, he said: 'O Allah, if You will, You do it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Washa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, fasting is not merely from food and drink alone.' Indeed, Maryam (peace be upon her) said: 'Surely I have vowed a fast to the Beneficent,' i.e., silence. Therefore, preserve your tongues, and lower your gaze, and do not envy one another, and do not dispute. For indeed, envy consumes faith just as fire consumes firewood.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The lie breaks the ablution and breaks the fast of the one who is fasting.' I said, 'We are destroyed.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not where you are going with it. Rather, that is the lie upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and upon His Messenger, and upon the Imams (peace be upon them).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyas, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah disliked for me six characteristics, then I disliked them for the successors from my offspring and their followers after me: obscenity during fasting.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassa' from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted until it was said, 'He will not break his fast.' Then he broke his fast until it was said, 'He will not fast.' Then he fasted the fast of Dawud (peace be upon him), one day and one day not. Then he passed away while fasting three days in the month. He said: 'Indeed, these equate to the fasting of the whole month, and they remove the 'wahr' of the chest, and the 'wahr' is the anxiety.' Hammad said: 'So I said, 'And which days are these?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first Thursday of the month, and the first Wednesday after the tenth of it, and the last Thursday in it.' So I said, 'How did these days become the ones in which is to be fasted?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, those before us from the nations, whenever punishment descended upon any one of them, it descended during these days. Thus, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted these fearful days.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), at the beginning of his mission, would fast continuously until it was said, 'He will not break his fast,' and he would break his fast continuously until it was said, 'He will not fast.' Then he abandoned that and fasted one day and broke fast one day, which is the fast of David (peace be upon him). Then he abandoned that and fasted the three white days (13th, 14th, 15th). Then he abandoned that and distributed it, fasting two days in every ten days, with a Wednesday in between two Thursdays. So he was taken (died), and peace be upon him and his family, while he was still acting upon that.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast until it was said, "He does not break his fast." Then he fasted one day and broke one day. Then he fasted on Mondays and Thursdays. Then he transitioned from that to fasting three days in the month: Thursday at the beginning of the month, Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month. And he used to say: "That is the fasting of the whole time (the entire month)."' And my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'There is no one more hateful to me than a man to whom it is said, "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do such and such," so he says, "Allah will not punish me if I strive hard in prayer." It is as if he sees that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) left something of the excellence due to inability (or weakness) on His part.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Did any of your forefathers fast in the month of Shaban?' He said, 'The best of my forefathers is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he fasted it.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halbi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Did any of your forefathers ever fast in Sha'ban?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of my forefathers, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), fasted it.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it. As for what has come regarding the fasting of Sha'ban, he (peace be upon him) was asked about it, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast it, nor did any of my forefathers (peace be upon them).' He said that because a group said: 'Fasting it is obligatory, like the fasting of the month of Ramadan, and its obligation is like the obligation of the month of Ramadan, and whoever breaks a day from it, upon him is expiation like what is upon the one who breaks a day from the month of Ramadan.' And the words of the Scholar (peace be upon him): 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast it, nor did any of my forefathers (peace be upon them)' means: 'They did not fast it as an obligatory obligation,' contradicting the words of the one who claimed it is obligatory. And rather, they used to fast it as a Sunnah with virtue, and there is nothing upon the one who does not fast it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Sabih, from Anbasa al-Abid, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away while fasting Sha'ban and Ramadan, and three days of every month: the first Thursday, the middle Wednesday, and the last Thursday; and Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon them) used to fast those days.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Salma, the companion of Al-Sabiri, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinany, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fasting Shaban and the month of Ramadan consecutively is a repentance from Allah, by Allah!'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Aban, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fasting Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan consecutively is a repentance from Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, and from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to connect what is between Sha'ban and Ramadan, and he would say: 'Fasting two consecutive months is a repentance from Allah.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast in Sha'ban and Ramadan, linking them, and he forbade the people from linking them, and he used to say: 'These two are the months of Allah, and they are an expiation for what is before them and for what is after them from sins.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about fasting while in the city (not traveling). He said: Three days in every month: Thursday from one week, and Wednesday from a week, and Thursday from another week. And he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Fasting the month of patience (Ramadan) and three days from every month remove the 'balabel' (hardness/roughness) of the chests, and fasting three days from every month is fasting for the whole time. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about fasting in the month, how is it? He said: Three days in the month, one day in every ten days. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it.' Three days in the month is fasting for the whole time.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara He said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the most meritorious of what the Sunnah prescribed regarding voluntary fasting, so he said: Three days in every month: Thursday in the beginning of the month, and Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday in the end of the month. I said to him: Is this all that the Sunnah has prescribed regarding fasting? He said: Yes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, who said: It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What has come regarding fasting on Wednesday?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the Fire on Wednesday, so He made fasting on it obligatory to seek refuge by it from the Fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Indeed, the day of Wednesday is fasted because no past community was punished except on the day of Wednesday, the middle of the month. Therefore, it is recommended to fast that day.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Imran, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If there are two Thursdays in the beginning of the month, then fast the first of them, for it is superior; and if there are two Thursdays in the end of the month, then fast the last of them, for it is superior.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the pre-dawn meal (suhur) for the one who intends to fast, is it obligatory upon him? So he said: There is no harm in not taking the pre-dawn meal if he wishes. And as for during the month of Ramadan, then it is preferable that he takes the pre-dawn meal; we love that it is not neglected during the month of Ramadan.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the pre-dawn meal (suhur) for the one who intends to fast, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for during the month of Ramadan, then there is merit in the pre-dawn meal, even if it is by drinking a sip of water; and as for voluntary fasting, whoever wishes to take the pre-dawn meal, let him do so, and whoever does not do so, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon him), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The pre-dawn meal (Suhoor) is a blessing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'My community should not leave the pre-dawn meal, even if it were upon stems (remaining after harvest).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Hassan ibn Mukhtar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is al-wisal in fasting?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no continuous fasting, nor silence from day until night, nor emancipation before ownership.'
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The continuation (of fasting) is that he makes his dinner his pre-dawn meal.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who performs continuous fasting fasts for a day and a night, and breaks his fast in the pre-dawn hours.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Aban from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about fasting the whole time, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'We have always disliked it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about fasting the whole time, so he disliked it and said: There is no problem if one were to fast for one day and break (not fast) for one day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who partook of the pre-dawn meal, then went out from his house, and the dawn had emerged and was clear. He (peace be upon him) said: He should complete that fast of his, then let him make it up. So, if he partook of the pre-dawn meal during other than the month of Ramadan after the dawn, he should break (his fast). Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father was praying one night, and I was eating. So he finished and said: As for Ja'far, he has eaten and drunk after the dawn.' So he instructed me, so I broke the fast of that day, which was other than the month of Ramadan.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him about a man who ate and drank after the dawn had emerged during the month of Ramadan. He said: If he stood up and looked, but did not see the dawn, so he ate, then returned and saw the dawn, let him complete his fast and there is no making it up again for him. And if he stood up and ate and drank, then looked to the dawn and saw that the dawn had emerged, let him complete his fast and he should compensate for it with another day, because he began with eating before looking, so upon him is the making up again.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I instruct the maid to look whether the dawn has emerged or not, so she says, "It has not emerged," so I eat, then I look, and I find that it has emerged when she had looked.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Complete your day, then compensate for it. Indeed, if it were you who had looked, there would have been no compensation upon you.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who went out during the month of Ramadan while his companions were eating their pre-dawn meal (suhoor) in a house. He looked at the dawn and called out to them. Some of them refrained, but some of them thought he was joking, so he ate. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He completes his fast and makes up for it (qada).'.

Safwan ibn Yahya from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'I have to make up for the day and the two days from the month of Ramadan, so I take the pre-dawn meal in the morning. Should I break (not fast) that day and make up for it in place of that day with another day, or should I complete upon the fast of that day and make up for it with another day?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but you break that day, because you ate in the morning, and you should make up for it another day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ibn Umm Maktum called the Adhan for the morning prayer, and a man passed by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while he was eating the pre-dawn meal (suhoor). He invited him to eat with him, but he said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the Mu'adhdhin has called the Adhan for Fajr.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said, said, 'This is Ibn Umm Maktum, and he calls the Adhan at night. When Bilal calls the Adhan, then at that time, refrain (from eating).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The dawn is that which, when you see it extending horizontally, resembles the whiteness of the Milky Way.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the white thread from the black thread, so he said: 'The whiteness of the day from the blackness of the night.' He said: 'Bilal used to call the Adhan for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and Ibn Umm Maktoum (who was blind) used to call the Adhan at night, and Bilal would call the Adhan when dawn emerged. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you hear the voice of Bilal, then stop eating and drinking, for it has become morning.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him). Regarding the Words of Allah the Exalted: 'It is made lawful to you to go to your wives on the night of the Fast' — the Verse. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was revealed regarding Khawwat ibn Jubayr al-Ansari, and he was with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) during the Khandaq (Battle of the Ditch), and he was fasting. So evening came and he was upon that state, and it was such that before the revelation of this Verse, whenever one of them fell asleep, the food and drink was prohibited upon him. So Khawwat went to his family when it was evening, so he said, 'Is there any food with you?' So they said, 'No, do not sleep until we prepare food for you.' So he reclined and fell asleep. So they said to him, 'You have done it (fallen asleep)?' He said, 'Yes.' So he spent the night upon that state. So in the morning, he went to the ditch, and fainting overcame him. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him. So when he saw that which was with him, he informed him of how his matter was. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Verse regarding him: 'And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread at Dawn'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'When does the food and drink become prohibited for the fasting one, and when does the Dawn Prayer become permissible?' He said, 'When the dawn appears and is like the white Coptic fabric, then the food becomes prohibited, the fast begins, and the Dawn Prayer becomes permissible.' I said, 'So we are not in the time [for eating] until the rays of the sun rise?' He said, 'Far be it! Where are you going? That is the Prayer of the children.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the number of months in the presence of God is twelve months in the Book of God, from the day He created the heavens and the earth. So the foremost of the months is the Month of God — Mighty is His mention — and it is the Month of Ramadan. And the heart of the Month of Ramadan is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr). And the Quran was revealed in the first night of the Month of Ramadan. Therefore, welcome the month with the Quran.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from al-Misma'i, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) advising his children: 'When the month of Ramadan enters, strive yourselves, for therein are the livelihoods distributed, and the life spans are written, and therein is written the delegation of God — those who journey to Him — and in it is a night wherein the deed is better than the deed in a thousand months.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever is not forgiven in the month of Ramadan will not be forgiven until the next (Ramadan), unless he attends Arafat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) preached to the people in the last Friday of Sha'ban. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! A month has come over you in which there is a night better than a thousand months — it is the Month of Ramadan. Allah has obligated its fasting and made the standing of a night in it with voluntary prayer like the voluntary prayer of seventy nights in other months. And He made, for whoever performs in it a voluntary act from among the good deeds and piety, [a reward] like the reward of one who fulfilled an obligation from the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and whoever fulfills in it an obligation from the obligations of Allah is like one who fulfilled seventy obligations from the obligations of Allah in other months. It is the month of patience, and verily the reward of patience is Paradise; and the month of mutual sympathy. It is a month in which Allah increases the provision of the believer. Whoever provides the iftar meal for a fasting believer in it shall have, due to that, before Allah: the emancipation of a slave and forgiveness for his past sins. It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, not all of us are able to provide the iftar for a fasting person.' He said: 'Allah is generous — He gives this reward to one who can only manage a sip of milk with which to break a faster's fast, or a drink of sweet water, or a few dates, if he cannot do more than that. And whoever lightens [the burden of] his owned slave in it, Allah will lighten His reckoning from him. It is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is the answering [of supplication] and liberation from the Fire. You cannot do without four characteristics: two with which you please Allah, and two which you cannot do without. As for the two with which you please Allah, Mighty and Majestic: it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And as for the two which you cannot do without: you ask Allah for your needs and Paradise, and you ask for well-being, and you seek refuge in Him from the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, when the month of Ramadan arrived — and that was with three days remaining from Sha'ban — he said to Bilal: 'Call out among the people'. So he gathered the people. Then he ascended the pulpit, praised God and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! Indeed this month — God has singled you out with it and it has come to you, and it is the master of the months. There is a night in it better than a thousand months; in it the gates of the Fire are locked and the gates of the Gardens are opened. So whoever reaches it and is not forgiven, may God remove him far. And whoever finds his parents alive and is not forgiven, may God remove him far. And whoever has me mentioned in his presence and does not send blessings upon me — God will not forgive him, and may God remove him far.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to turn his face toward the people and say: 'O group of people! When the crescent of the month of Ramadan rises, the rebellious devils are shackled, the doors of the sky are opened, the doors of the Gardens are opened, the doors of Mercy are opened, and the doors of the Fire are closed, and supplication is answered. And in it, God has, at every breaking of the fast, those whom He emancipates from the Fire; and a caller calls out every night: Is there one who petitions? Is there one who seeks forgiveness? O Allah, give every spender a replacement, and give every hoarder ruin!' — until when the crescent of Shawwal rises, the believers are proclaimed: 'Come to your rewards, for it is the Day of the Prize!' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Know that, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, it is not a prize of dinars or dirhams.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — has, in every night of the Month of Ramadan, those who are freed and released from the Fire, except for the one who breaks his fast with an intoxicant. And when it is the last night of it, He liberates in it the like of what He liberated during the whole of it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the redness disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, then the sun has set in the east of the earth and its west.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about breaking the fast before the prayer or after it. He said: If there are with him a group of people, fearing that he will detain them from their dinner, so let him break the fast with them; and if it is other than that, let him pray and then break the fast.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who fasted in the month of Ramadan, so he ate and drank out of forgetfulness. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him complete his fast, and there is no making up for it upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who forgets and eats during the month of Ramadan, he said: He should complete his fast, for it is something which Allah fed him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who deliberately broke his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan without an excuse. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should emancipate a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. If he is not able, he should give in charity with whatever he can afford.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who broke his fast for one day from the month of Ramadan deliberately, so he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I am destroyed, O Messenger of Allah.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'The Fire, O Messenger of Allah.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'And what is the matter with you?' He said, 'I had intercourse with my wife.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Give in charity and seek forgiveness.' The man said, 'By the One who magnified your right, I have not left in the house anything, neither little nor much.' He (the narrator) said: 'Then a man from the people entered with a sack of dates containing twenty sa', which is ten sa' by our sa'. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Take these dates and give in charity with them.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, upon whom shall I give in charity with them, and I have informed you that there is neither little nor much in my house?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'So take it and feed it to your dependents and seek forgiveness of Allah.'
