He (the narrator) said: 'So when we came out, our companions said, 'He began with emancipation.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Emancipate, or fast, or give in charity.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who plays with his wife during the month of Ramadan until he discharges semen. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the expiation similar to what is upon the one who copulates.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Bureyd al-Ijli, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he had broken his fast during the month of Ramadan for three days. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is asked, He is asked, "Is there a sin upon you regarding your breaking the fast during the month of Ramadan?" So if he says, "No", then it is upon the Imam to kill him; and if he says, "Yes", then it is upon the Imam to flog him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, and Sama'ah narrated, saying: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who was found breaking his fast three times during the month of Ramadan, and the case was referred to the Imam (peace be upon him) three times. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is killed on the third (time).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn Suqat, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who plays with his wife or his slave girl, and he is making up a fast of the month of Ramadan, so his water descends and he ejaculates, he said: Upon him is the expiation similar to what is upon the one who copulates during the month of Ramadan.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked him about a man who broke his fast for one day from the month of Ramadan deliberately. He said: He should give in charity twenty Sa's and he should make up for it.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who went to his wife while he was fasting and she was fasting, so he said: If he coerced her, then upon him are two expiations; and if she consented, then upon him is an expiation and upon her is an expiation; and if he coerced her, then upon him is the striking of fifty lashes, being half the Hadd; and if she consented, he is struck with twenty-five lashes and she is struck with twenty-five lashes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked: about a man who touches something from the woman, would that spoil his fast or break it? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is disliked for the young man for fear that the semen may precede (discharge).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The kiss does not break the fast.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the fasting person who kisses the slave girl and the wife?' He said: 'As for the old man like me and like you, there is no problem. And as for the young, lustful man, no, because he is not safe from desire, and kissing is one of the two lustful desires.' I said, 'So what do you think regarding someone like me who has a slave girl, and he plays with her?' He said to me, 'You are lustful, O Abu Hazim. How is your food intake?' I said, 'If I am satiated, it harms me, and if I am hungry, it weakens me.' He said: 'I am like that. So, how are you with women?' I said, 'And there is nothing [to it].' He said: 'But I, O Abu Hazim, whatever I desire to do, that happens from me, until I do it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who had a wet dream at the beginning of the night, or had intercourse with his wife, then he slept deliberately during the month of Ramadan until morning. He said: He completes his fast for that day, then he makes it up after he breaks his fast from the month of Ramadan, and he seeks forgiveness of his Lord.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the man who has intercourse with the slave girl during the month of Ramadan, then he sleeps before he performs the ritual bath. He said: 'He completes his fast and makes up for that day, unless he wakes up before the dawn rises. So if he waits for the water to be warmed or drawn, and the dawn rises, then he does not make up for his day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who becomes sexually impure (junub), then sleeps until morning. Can he fast that day voluntarily? He said: Is he not free to choose between himself and midday? He said, And I asked him about the man who has a wet dream during the day in the month of Ramadan. He completes his fast as he is. He said: There is no problem.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Ibn Sinan, who said: My father wrote to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he was making up the fast of the month of Ramadan, and said: 'I woke up in the morning with the washing (of major impurity), and sexual impurity struck me, so I did not perform the ritual bath until the dawn emerged.' So he (peace be upon him) answered him: 'Do not fast this day, and fast the next day.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who becomes junub at night during the month of Ramadan, so he forgot to perform ghusl until a week had passed, or the month of Ramadan ended. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the making up of the prayer and the fast.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The fasting one may submerge his body in the water, but he should not immerse his head.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The fasting one and the one in Ihraam do not immerse their head in the water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The fasting person can submerge his body in water, pour water over his head, cool himself with his garment, cool himself with a hand-fan, and cool himself with a blower placed beneath him, but he must not immerse his head in the water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Haytham, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not attach your garment to your body while it is wet and you are fasting, until you wring it out.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Hamadani, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who stays still in the water. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, but he should not immerse himself in it; and the woman should not stay still in the water because she carries the water with her private part.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Musanna al-Hannat and al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who immerses himself in water. He said: 'No,' and (also) the one in Ihram. He said, 'And I asked him about the fasting person who wears the wet garment. He said: 'No'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the fasting one who performs ablution for the prayer, so water enters his throat. He said: If his ablution was for an obligatory prayer, there is nothing upon him; and if his ablution was for an optional prayer, he must make it up.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the fasting one who rinses his mouth: He said: 'He should not swallow his saliva until he spits it out three times.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the fasting one who rinses his mouth and inhales (water into the nose), he said: 'Yes, but he should not be excessive (in swallowing the water).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, who said: The fasting person in the month of Ramadan may brush his teeth whenever he wishes. And if he rinses his mouth during the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, there is nothing upon him, and his fast is complete. And if he rinses his mouth during a time other than that of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, he must repeat his fast. And it is preferable for the fasting person that he does not rinse his mouth.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskam, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the fasting one vomits, then upon him is the making up of that day, and if nausea comes to him without him vomiting, then let him complete his fast.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the fasting one vomits, he has broken his fast, and if nausea comes over him without him vomiting, let him complete his fast.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muawiya from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one who is overcome by nausea (but does not vomit) while fasting, he said: Let him complete his fast and he does not have to make it up.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who regurgitates from his stomach until it reaches his throat, then he returns it back into his stomach, while he is fasting. He said: 'It is not with anything' (i.e., it does not break the fast).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about regurgitation, does it break the fast of the fasting person? He (peace be upon him) said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the regurgitation (qals), and it is the belching (jush'a) by which food rises from the man's stomach without it being a full vomit, while he is standing in the Prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That does not break his ablution, nor does it cut off his Prayer, nor does it break his Fast.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the fasting person, can he get cupping done? So he said: 'I fear upon him.' I said: 'Does he not fear upon himself?' He said: 'The fainting, or by it the bile would be stirred.' I said: 'What is your view if he is strong upon that and he does not fear anything?' He said: 'Yes, if he so desires to.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'A'ala, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about cupping for the fasting person. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he does not fear weakness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked: About the man who enters the bathhouse while he is fasting, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, as long as he does not fear weakness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who enters the bathhouse while he is fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who enters the bathhouse while he is fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the fasting person who complains of his ear and pours medicine into it. He said: There is no problem with it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, that he asked him about the man who is injected, being ill, in the month of Ramadan. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The fasting one, it is not allowed for him to be injected.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Lays al-Murady, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who gets cupping done and pours oil into his ear. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, except for the snuff, for it is disliked.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man and the woman, is it permissible for them to insert medication while they insert medication while they are fasting? He said: There is no problem.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from his father who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the enema which a person inserts while he is fasting?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'There is no problem with the solids.'
Whoever provides for the breaking of the fast (iftar) of a fasting person, for him shall be the like of his reward.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Your providing for the breaking of the fast of your fasting brother is superior to your own fast.

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), on the days he fasted, would order a sheep to be slaughtered and cut into pieces and cooked. Then when evening came, he would lean over the cooking pots until he could smell the aroma of the broth — while he was fasting. Then he would say: 'Bring the bowls; fill them for the family of so-and-so, and fill them for the family of so-and-so.' Then he would be brought bread and dates, and that would be his dinner. May God bless him and his forefathers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Haroun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him) who said: Sudeyr came to my father (peace be upon him) during the month of Ramadan, and he said: 'O Sudeyr! Do you know which nights these are?' He said: 'Yes, may my father be sacrificed for you — these are the nights of the month of Ramadan. But what is that?' So he said to him: 'Are you able, during each night of these nights, to free ten slaves from the descendants of Ismail?' Sudeyr said to him: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you — my wealth does not amount to that.' So he did not cease to reduce [the number] until he reached one slave. In each case he said: 'I am not able to do that.' Then he said to him: 'So are you able to provide the breaking of the fast for a Muslim man each night?' He said: 'Yes, and [even] ten.' So my father (peace be upon him) said to him: 'That is what I intended, O Sudeyr! Your providing the breaking of the fast for your Muslim brother is equivalent to [freeing] one slave from the descendants of Ismail (peace be upon him).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Suleyman al-Farra', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the fasting one who applies kohl, he said: There is no problem with it; it is neither food nor drink. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleyman al-Farra', from someone else, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one who is afflicted with conjunctivitis during the month of Ramadan: can he sprinkle his eyes during the day while he is fasting? He said: He sprinkles it when he breaks the fast, and he does not sprinkle it while he is fasting.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the kohl for the fasting person, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the kohl is such that there is no musk in it, and it has no taste in the throat, then there is no problem with it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the tooth-brushing for the fasting person, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, he may brush his teeth at any time of the day he desires.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the fasting person who brushes his teeth with water. He said: 'There is no problem with it.' And he said: 'He should not brush with a wet toothstick.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the fasting one who extracts his tooth, he said: No, nor should he bleed his mouth, nor should he brush with a wet stick.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him) That Ali (peace be upon him) disliked that the fasting person should perfume himself with musk.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadda', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbid the use of narcissus (daffodil). So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Why is that?' He said: 'Because it is the aroma of the non-Arabs.' And one of our companions informed me that the non-Arabs used to smell it when they were fasting, and said, 'It restrains hunger.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfaly, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), whenever he fasted, would apply perfume, and he would say: 'The perfume is a gift of the fasting one'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Does the fasting person smell the rose (aroma) and the perfume?' He said: 'There is no problem with it.' And it is reported that he did not smell the rose because it is disliked for him to derive pleasure from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the menstruating woman make up the Prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'Does she make up the Fast?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'From where does that come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the first one who analogized was Iblis'. I said, 'And the fasting one can submerge in the water?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So can he wear wet clothes upon his body?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'From where does that come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From that'. I said, 'Does the fasting one smell the rosemary?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because it is a pleasure, and it is disliked for him to derive pleasure.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'Can the fasting one chew the gum?' He said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Beware of chewing gum, for I chewed gum today while I was fasting, and I found something from it in myself.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the fasting woman who cooks in a pot and tastes the broth while looking at it, so he said: 'There is no problem.' He said, 'And he was asked about the woman who has a child and she is fasting, so she chews the bread and feeds it to him, so he said: 'There is no problem,' and the bird, if it were hers.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Husayn ibn Ziyad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem for the male cook and the female cook if they taste the broth, and he is fasting.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibnada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Fatimah (peace be upon her) would chew for Al-Hasan, then for Al-Husayn (the prayers of Allah be upon them both), while she was fasting in the month of Ramadan.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hus-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting one who tastes something and does not swallow it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who gets thirsty in the month of Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem if he were to suck the ring.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhassan ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The ring in the mouth of the fasting one is not a problem (does not break the fast), but as for the date-stone, then no (it breaks the fast).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba Al Hashimy who said, I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the old man and the old woman who are weakened from the Fasting during the Month of Ramazan. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should give in charity every day with a handful of wheat'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about an old man who was weakened from fasting the month of Ramadan. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give in charity every day with what suffices as a meal of a poor one'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The elderly man and the one suffering from thirst, there is no blame upon them if they break their fast during the month of Ramadan, and each one of them should give charity every day with a mudd of food, and there is no making up (qada) for them. If they are unable (to give charity), then there is nothing upon them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And upon those who are able [to fast, but do so] is a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [for each day],' he said: 'Those who were able to tolerate the fasting, but old age has hit them, or thirst, or something resembling that, so upon them, for each day, is a handful (of food to be fed to the poor).'

Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who is struck by thirst to the extent that he fears for his life. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He drinks by the measure of what sustains his breath, and he does not drink until he is fully quenched.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We have young women and young men who are unable to fast due to the intensity of the thirst that strikes them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let them drink by the measure that quenches their souls and what they are cautious of (from harm/exhaustion).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I had fever in Medina one day during the month of Ramadan, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent to me a dish containing vinegar and oil, and said: 'Break your fast, and pray while you are seated.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I wrote to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) asking him what the limit of the illness is in which its owner breaks the fast, and the illness in which its owner leaves the prayer while standing. He said: 'Rather, the human being is a seer upon himself.' And he said: 'That is up to him; he is more knowing of himself.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him), 'What is the limit of the illness that obligates its bearer to break the fast, just as it obligates him during travel, as mentioned in the verse: whoever among you is sick or on a journey He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is entrusted with it and delegated to himself. So if he finds weakness, let him break the fast, and if he finds strength, let him fast it, whatever the illness may be.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The fasting one, when he fears for his eyes from the conjunctivitis (eye infection), breaks [his fast].

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who finds in his head pain from a severe headache, is it permissible for him to break [the fast]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he suffers a severe headache, and when he has a severe fever, and when his eyes are sore with severe soreness, then it has become permissible for him to break [the fast].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: He asked him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was listening: 'What is the limit of the illness due to which the fasting is left?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he is not able to have the pre-dawn meal (suhoor).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Umm Salama (may Allah have mercy on her) complained about her eyes during the month of Ramadan, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) instructed her to break the fast, and said: 'The evening meal (delayed until night) would destroy your eyes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the limit of the patient when he is convalescing during the Fasting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to him. He is more knowing of himself. When he is strong, so let him Fast'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khathʿami, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Do not say “Ramadan”, but say “the Month of Ramadan”, for you do not know what Ramadan is.’

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sa'd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We were eight men in his presence, and we mentioned Ramadan, so he said: Do not say 'This is Ramadan', nor 'Ramadan is gone', nor 'Ramadan has come', for Ramadan is a Name from the Names of God, Mighty and Majestic — it neither comes nor goes. It is only the transient thing that comes and goes. But rather say 'Month of Ramadan', for the month is annexed to the Name, and the Name is the Name of God, Mighty is His Mention, and it is the month in which the Quran was revealed — He made it a parable and a festival.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both), said: I asked both of them about a man who became ill and did not fast until another Ramadan overtook him. They said: If he was cured, then delayed (paying the fidya) before the next Ramadan overtook him, he should fast the days he missed, and give in charity for each day a mudd of food to a poor person, and he must make up the fasts. And if he did not cease to be ill until another Ramadan overtook him, he should fast the days he missed, and give in charity for the first (Ramadan) for each day a mudd to a poor person, and there is no making up of the fasts upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding a man who falls ill, and the month of Ramadan arrives for him, and it passes while he is still sick, and he does not recover until another month of Ramadan arrives. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give charity for the first [one], and fast the second. So if he recovered in between, and did not fast until another month of Ramadan arrived, he should fast both of them together, and give charity for the first one.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Fuzayl, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had missed a portion of the month of Ramadan, and then the next month of Ramadan caught up with him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is that he should fast, and that he should feed a poor person for each day. So if he was sick in the interval between that until the next month of Ramadan caught up with him, then there is nothing upon him except fasting, if he recovers. And if the illness continued upon him and he did not recover, then upon him is that he should feed a poor person for each day.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who has a few days of the month of Ramadan upon him, can he make them up separately? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with making up the month of Ramadan at different times. Rather, the fasting that is not done separately is the expiation for Zihaar, and the expiation for blood, and the expiation for the oath.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one who makes up for the month of Ramadan in a discontinuous manner. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has memorized his (number of missed) days, then there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever breaks a part of the fast of Ramadan due to an excuse, then making it up consecutively is superior, and if he makes it up separately, it is good, there is no objection.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If there is something upon a man from the fasting of the month of Ramadan, let him make it up in whichever month he wishes, consecutive days. So if he is unable, let him make it up however he wishes, and let him count the days. So if he separates them, it is good, and if he continues them, it is good.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about making up for the month of Ramadan during Dhu al-Hijjah, or can I cut it piece-meal? He (peace be upon him) said: Make it up in Dhu al-Hijjah, and cut it if you wish.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who was sick during the month of Ramadan, and when he recovered he intended to perform Hajj, how should he deal with making up the fasts? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he returns, let him fast them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who wakes up in the morning intending to fast, then it occurs to him to break it, so he breaks it. He said: 'He has the choice between himself and midday.' I said: 'Does he make it up if he breaks it?' He said: 'Yes, because it is a good deed which he intended to perform, so let him complete it.' I said: 'If a man intends to fast from the rising of the day, does he fast?' He said: 'Yes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the voluntary fasting one whose need presents itself to him. He (peace be upon him) said: He has the choice between himself and Asr; and if he remains until Asr, then it becomes clear to him that he should fast, if he had not intended that, then he may fast that day if he wishes.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His words: 'The fasting one is with the choice until the decline of the sun', he said: 'That is regarding the Obligatory [fasting]. But as for the Optional [fasting], then for him is that he breaks [his fast] at any hour he desires until the setting of the sun.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Regarding the man who changes his mind after he wakes up and the day has risen, in a Fast of that day, in order to make up for it from a Month of Ramazan, and he did not happen to have that intention from the night (before). He said: 'Yes, let him Fast it, and let him rely with it when nothing new happens'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad, from Bureyd Al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had relations with his wife on a day he was making up from the month of Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: If he had relations with her before the decline of the sun, there is nothing upon him except one day in place of one day; and if he had relations with her after the decline of the sun, then upon him is that he gives charity to ten poor people; if he is not able, he should fast one day in place of one day, and fast three days as an expiation for what he has done.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who makes up for the month of Ramadan, and her husband coerces her to break the fast, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to coerce her after the decline of the sun (midday).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Salih ibn Abdullah al-Khash'ami, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who intends fasting, and his brother who is upon his matter (Wilayah) meets him; should he break his fast? He (peace be upon him) said: If it is voluntary fasting, it suffices him and is counted for him; and if it is making up for an obligatory fast, he must, he should make it up.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who has days [of fasting] from the month of Ramadan [to make up], can he fast optional [fasts]? He said: No, until he makes up what is upon him from the month of Ramadan.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a number of [missed] fasts upon him from the month of Ramadan, does he fast optional [fasts]? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until he makes up for what is upon him from the month of Ramadan.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who dies and upon him are prayers or fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one closest to the people in inheritance should make it up for him.' I said: 'And if the one closest to him is a woman?' So he is a woman?' He said: 'No, except for the men.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about a man who was reached by the month of Ramadan while he was sick, so he died before he recovered. He said: There is nothing upon him, but the one who recovers should make up for him, then if that one dies before making it up, he makes it up for the one who died.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Maryam al-Ansari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man fasts something from the month of Ramadan, then he does not cease to be sick until he dies, so there is nothing upon him. And if he recovers, then gets sick, then dies, and there was wealth for him, charity should be given on his behalf in place of each day by a mudd; and if there was not wealth for him, his guardian should fast on his behalf.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who dies and upon him is a debt [of fasting] from the month of Ramadan. Who should pay it off on his behalf? He said: The closest of the people to him. I said: And if the closest of the people to him was a woman? He said: No, except the men.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad who said: I wrote to Al-Akheir (peace be upon him): A man died and upon him was a debt of making up fasts from the month of Ramadan for ten days, and he has two guardians. Is it permissible for both of them to make it up for him together, five days by one of the two guardians and five days by the other? So he (peace be upon him) signed: The elder of his guardians should make it up for him, ten days, by guardianship, if Allah wills.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man dies and upon him is the fasting of two consecutive months due to an illness, then upon him is that he should give in charity for the first month, and make up the second month.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We command our young children to fast when they are seven years old, with whatever they can endure of fasting the day. If it is until midday and more than that, or less, then when thirst and hunger overcome them, they break their fast, until they get accustomed to fasting and can endure it. So command your young children, when they are nine years old, with whatever they can endure of fasting. If thirst overcomes them, they break their fast.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at what age the child is taken for fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: Between fourteen and fifteen years of age. So if he fasts before that, let him be. And indeed, my son So-and-so fasted before that, so I let him do it.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the child, when can he fast? He said: When he is strong upon fasting.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the boy is able to endure fasting for three consecutive days, then fasting the month of Ramadan becomes obligatory upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who embraced Islam during the middle of the month of Ramadan, what is upon him regarding his fasting? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him except for what he embraced Islam in.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: Regarding a man who became Muslim during the middle of the month of Ramadan, that there is nothing upon him except for what he faces coming.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group who embraced Islam during the month of Ramadan, and some days had already passed from it. Is it upon them to fast the days that passed, or the day on which they embraced Islam? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no making up (qada) upon them, nor for the day on which they embraced Islam, except if they embraced Islam before the emergence of dawn (fajr).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about going out when the month of Ramadan enters. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except regarding what I am informing you of: going out to Makkah, or a military expedition in the Way of Allah, or wealth you fear its destruction, or a brother you intend to bid farewell to, and even if he is not a brother from the father and the mother.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who enters the month of Ramadan while he is resident and does not intend to travel, then it occurs to him after entering Ramadan that he should travel. So he remained silent, and I asked him again. So he said: 'Residing is superior, unless he has a need that makes it inevitable for him to go out in it, or he fears for his wealth.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Therefore whoever of you is present in the Month, he shall Fast therein.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What can be clearer than it! The one who is present, so let him Fast it, and the one who travels, so he should not Fast it'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave charity to the sick of my community and its travelers with the shortening (of prayer) and the breaking (of the fast). Would it not please one of you that when Allah gives him a charity, he should return it (by not accepting the concession)?

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Yahya ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one fasting during the journey in the month of Ramadan is like the one breaking the fast in it during residence. Then he said: Indeed, a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, should I fast the month of Ramadan while traveling?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, it is easy upon me.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave charity to the sick of His community and its travelers with breaking the fast in the month of Ramadan. Would it not please one of you if He gave him a charity that he would like to return it?'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of my community are those who, when they travel, break their fast and shorten (the prayer); and when they are shown kindness, they rejoice; and when they sin, they seek forgiveness. And the worst of my community are those who are born into blessings, fed with them, eat the best of food, wear soft clothes, and when they speak, they are not truthful.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man travels during the month of Ramadan, he breaks his fast. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) left Medina for Mecca during the month of Ramadan, and the people were with him, including those walking. When he reached Kura' al-Ghameem, he called for a cup of water between Dhuhr and Asr, drank, and broke his fast. Then the people broke their fast with him, while some people remained fasting; he called them the 'disobedient ones' (al-'usawah), and indeed, the ruling is taken from the final action of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God named a group of people who fasted when he broke the fast, and shortened [the prayer], as 'the disobedient ones', and said: 'They are the disobedient ones until the Day of Resurrection, and we indeed know their sons and the sons of their sons until our day today.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Suleiman ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a man were to die whilst fasting during the journey, I would not pray over him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man fasted during the journey.' So he said: 'If it had reached him that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that, then upon him is the making up (for it); and if it did not reach him, then there is nothing upon him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who fasts during the journey out of ignorance, does not make it up.

Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Lays al-Muradi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man travels during the month of Ramadan, he should break his fast; and if he were to fast it out of ignorance, he would not make it up.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to face the Qibla and raise his two hands whenever the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, then say: O God! Cause it to rise upon us with security, and faith, and wellbeing, and Islam, and encompassing good health, and abundant sustenance, and warding off of illnesses. O God! Grant us its fasting and its night prayer and recitation of the Quran in it. O God! Give it to us safely, and receive it back from us safely, and keep us safe in it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When it is the first night of the month of Ramadan, then say: O Allah, Lord of the month of Ramadan and Revealer of the Quran! This is the month of Ramadan in which You revealed the Quran, and in which You sent down clear signs from guidance and the Criterion. O Allah, grant us its fasting and help us in its night prayer. O Allah, preserve it for us, keep us safe therein, and receive it back from us in ease from You and forgiveness. And place in what You decree and ordain from the inevitable matter, in what is distinguished from the Wise command during the Night of Power, from the decree that cannot be returned or changed — that You write me among the pilgrims of Your Sacred House whose hajj is accepted, whose sa'i is appreciated, whose sins are forgiven, and from whom evil deeds are expiated. And place in what You decree and ordain that You extend my life-span for me and expand for me from the permissible provision.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said: 'Supplicate with this supplication during the month of Ramadan, welcoming the entry of the (new) year.' And he mentioned that whoever supplicates with it in expectation of reward, sincerely, will not be afflicted during that year with strife nor an affliction by which his religion and his body would be harmed, and God — Mighty is His mention — would protect him from the evil of what that year would bring. O God! Indeed I beseech You by Your Name to which every thing submits, and by Your Mercy which encompasses every thing, and by Your Might by which You have subjugated every thing, and by Your Magnificence before which every thing is humbled, and by Your Power to which every thing is subdued, and by Your Omnipotence which overwhelms every thing, and by Your Knowledge which encompasses every thing. O Light! O Holy! O First before every thing, and O Everlasting after every thing! O God! O Beneficent! O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and forgive me the sins which alter blessings, and forgive me the sins which bring down punishments, and forgive me the sins which cut off hope, and forgive me the sins which give dominance to enemies, and forgive me the sins which repel supplication, and forgive me the sins by which the descent of affliction is deserved, and forgive me the sins which withhold the rain of the sky, and forgive me the sins which uncover the veil, and forgive me the sins which hasten annihilation, and forgive me the sins which bequeath remorse, and forgive me the sins which rupture inviolabilities. And clothe me with Your fortified armor which cannot be shot at, and grant me well-being from the evil of what I fear by night and day in this coming year of mine. O God! Lord of the seven heavens and the seven earths, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them; and Lord of the Magnificent Throne, and Lord of the Seven Doublings (al-Fatiha) and the Magnificent Quran, and Lord of Israfil, and Mika'il, and Jibra'il, and Lord of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and his household, the Chief of the Messengers and the Seal of the Prophets. I beseech You by You and by what You have named, O Magnificent! You are the One who bestows with magnificence, repels every danger, gives every abundance

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen who said: Amr ibn Shimr narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him), whenever the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, would face toward the Qibla and then say: 'O Allah! Cause it to begin for us with security, faith, safety, Islam, and all-encompassing wellbeing. O Allah! Grant us its fasting, its night prayers, and recitation of the Quran in it. O Allah! Preserve it for us, and receive it back from us, and keep us safe throughout it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he used to say whenever the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared: 'O God! Enter it upon us with safety, and Islam, and certainty, and faith, and righteousness, and divine enablement for what You love and are pleased with.'

Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whenever the Month of Ramadan arrives, say: O Allah! The Month of Ramadan has arrived, and You have made its fasting obligatory upon us, and You revealed the Quran in it as a guidance for the people and clear signs of guidance and the Criterion. O Allah! Help us in fasting it. O Allah! Accept it from us, keep us safe in it, and receive it back from us in ease from You and good health. for You are All-Powerful over everything, O Most Merciful of the merciful!

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication during the Month of Ramadan: O Allah! It is to You I beseech, and from You I seek my needs. (There are) ones who seek needs from people, but I do not seek my needs except from You alone, there being no associates for You; and I ask You by Your grace and Your pleasure that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the People of his Household. And that You make for me in this year a way to Your Sacred House — a hajj pilgrimage that is righteous, accepted, pure, and devoted solely to You, by which my eyes are delighted and my rank is raised, and grant me that I lower my gaze and guard my chastity and refrain by it from all of Your prohibitions until there is nothing more preferable to me than obedience to You, fearing You, acting according to what You love, and abandoning what You abhor and forbid. And make all of that easy, prosperous, and with well-being, and inspire me with gratitude for what You have bestowed upon me. And I ask You to make my death a martyr's death in Your way, under the banner of Your Prophet, alongside Your friends. And I ask You to vanquish Your enemies and the enemies of Your Messenger through me. And I ask You to honor me by humiliating whoever You wish from Your creatures, and do not humiliate me through honoring any of Your friends. O Allah! Make for me a way with the Messenger. Sufficient for me is Allah — whatever Allah wills.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir, from some of his men, that Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication during every day of the month of Ramadan: O Allah! This is the month of Ramadan, and this is the month of fasting, and this is the month of turning back (to You), and this is the month of repentance, and this is the month of forgiveness and mercy, and this is the month of emancipation from the Fire and success with Paradise. O Allah! So preserve it for me and receive it from me, and aid me in it with the best of Your aid, and grant me success in it for obedience to You, and free me therein for Your worship, Your supplication, and recitation of Your Book; and magnify for me therein the blessing, and better for me therein the outcome, and make sound for me therein my body, and expand for me therein my sustenance, and suffice me therein in what concerns me, and answer for me therein my supplication, and cause my hopes to reach fruition therein. O Allah! Remove from me therein drowsiness, laziness, weariness, slackening, hardness of heart, heedlessness, and delusion. O Allah! Keep from me therein ailments, illnesses, worries, griefs, symptoms, diseases, errors, and sins; and repel from me therein evil, obscenity, hardship, affliction, exhaustion, and toil — for You are the Hearer of supplication. O Allah! Shelter me therein from the accursed Satan — his whispering, his mocking, his blowing (of evil breath), his puffing (of arrogance), his insinuations, his snares, his deceit, his tricks, his false hopes, his deceptions, his vanity, his strife, his infantry, his traps, his helpers, his followers, his companions, his adherents, his allies, his partners, and all of their schemes. O Allah! Provide me therein with the completion of its fast and the fulfilment of ambition in its night-prayer, and the perfection of what pleases You therein with patience, faith, certainty, and seeking Your reward; then accept that from us with abundant increase and magnificent recompense. O Allah! Provide me therein with earnestness, striving, strength, vigor, returning to You, repentance, desire, awe, anxiety, tender-heartedness, truthfulness of tongue, fear of You, hope in You, reliance upon You, trust in You, and abstinence from Your prohibitions — through rig

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Whenever you see the crescent moon, do not depart, and say: 'O Allah, I ask You for goodness of this month, its commencement, its light, its help, its blessings, its purity, and its sustenance. And I ask You for the goodness of whatever is in it and the goodness of whatever is after it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of whatever is in it and the evil of whatever is after it. O Allah, let it come upon us with security, faith, peace, Islam, blessings, and divine guidance toward what You love and are pleased with.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The camel hirer and the cameleer who travels and has no fixed residence should complete the prayer (four rak'ahs) and fast the month of Ramadan (fully, without shortening).
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions who said: The man would not break (the Fast) during a Month of Ramazan except in a way of Truth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding the man who escorts his brother for a journey of a day, or two days, or three. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is during the month of Ramadan, let him break his fast.' I said, 'Which is superior: fasting or escorting him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Escorting him. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has exempted it from him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'News of one of my companions has reached me from Al-Awas, and that was during the month of Ramadan. Should I go to meet him and break (my fast)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Should I go to meet him and break (my fast), or should I stay and fast?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go to meet him and break (your fast).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from a number from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I said, 'A man escorts his brother during the month of Ramadan for the day and the two days.' He said, 'He breaks his fast and makes up for it.' It was said to him, 'Is that superior, or does he stay and not escort him?' He said, 'He escorts him and breaks his fast, for that is a right upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Wasi', from Ismail ibn Sahl, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) left Medina during the remaining days of Sha'ban, so he was fasting. Then the month of Ramadan entered upon him while he was traveling, so he broke his fast. It was said to him, 'You fast Sha'ban and break your fast in the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'Yes. Sha'ban is up to me; if I will, I fast, and if I will, I do not; and the month of Ramadan is a fixed determination from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon me to break the fast.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Uzafir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I fast these three days of the month. Sometimes I travel, and sometimes an illness befalls me, so is it obligatory upon me to make them up?' He said to me: 'Only the obligatory [fasts] necessitate making up. As for the non-obligatory [fasts], you have the choice in them.' I said: 'The choice during travel and illness?' He said: 'Illness, Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, has exempted you from it, and travel: if you wish, make it up, and if you do not make it up, there is no blame upon you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about fasting three days in the month, is there a making up for it upon the traveler? He said: No.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Marzuban ibn Imran said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'I intend to travel, so should I fast for the month in which I travel?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'So when I return, do I make it up?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, just as you did not fast, similarly you do not make it up.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Bilal, from Al-Hasan ibn Bassam Al-Jammal, from a man who said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in what is between Makkah and Al-Medina in the month of Sha'ban, and he was fasting. Then we saw the crescent of the month of Ramadan, so he broke his fast. So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Yesterday was from Sha'ban and you were fasting, and today is from the month of Ramadan and you are not fasting?' So he said: 'That was voluntary (fasting), and for us is that we do what we so desire to, and this is an Obligation, so it is not for us that we do except for what we have been Commanded for'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the man who leaves his house intending to travel while he is fasting, so he (peace be upon him) said: He said: If he leaves before the middle of the day, let him break his fast and make up for that day; and if he leaves after the decline (of the sun), let him complete his day.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man sets out during the month of Ramadan after midday, he should complete his fast; and when he sets out before midday, he should break his fast.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who travels during the month of Ramadan, whether he should fast or break his fast: He said, 'If he departs before midday, let him break his fast; and if he departs after midday, let him fast.' And he said, 'This is recognized by the words of Ali (peace be upon him): I fast and I break until when the sun declines, determination is made upon me,' meaning the fasting.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man travels during the month of Ramadan and departs after midday, he is obligated to fast that day and count it as part of Ramadan. If he enters a land before the emergence of dawn with the intention of staying there, he is obligated to fast that day. If he enters after the emergence of dawn, there is no fasting obligation upon him, and if he wishes, he may fast.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who returns from a journey during the month of Ramadan, such that he sees he will enter upon his family in the forenoon or at the rising of the day. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the dawn breaks and he is outside and has not yet entered upon his family, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who returns from a journey during the month of Ramadan, and enters to his family when it is morning, or when the day has risen. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the dawn emerges and he is outside and has not yet entered to his family, he is with the choice: if he wills, he fasts, and if he wills, he breaks [the fast].'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who came back from a journey during the month of Ramadan and had not eaten anything before midday. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a traveler who arrived at his family before the decline of the sun, and he had already eaten. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to eat anything that day, nor should he have sexual intercourse during the month of Ramadan, if he has a wife.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, who said: He (peace be upon him) said regarding the traveler who enters his family during the month of Ramadan and had eaten before his entry: He should refrain from eating for the remainder of his day, and upon him is the making up (of the fast). And He (peace be upon him) said regarding the traveler who enters his family while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) before midday, and had not eaten: Upon him is that he completes his fast, and there is no making up for it upon him, meaning when his impurity was from a wet dream.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: When you arrive at a land and you intend to stay in it for ten days, so fast and complete (the prayers); and if you intend to stay for less than ten days, so break (do not fast) what is between you and the month. So when it reaches a month, so complete the prayers and the fasts, even if you say, 'I shall be leaving tomorrow'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who is overtaken by the month of Ramadan while traveling, and he stays for some days in a place; is fasting upon him? He said: No, until he intends to stay for ten days. And if he intends to stay for ten days, he fasts and completes the prayer. I asked him about a man who has outstanding days from the month of Ramadan while he is traveling, and he repays them when he stays in a place; he said: No, until he intends to stay for ten days.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who travels during the month of Ramadan, is it for him that he attains from the women? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who had relations with his wife during the month of Ramadan while he was a traveler. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba al-Hashimi, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan, meaning Musa (peace be upon him), about the man who copulates with his wife during the journey while it is the month of Ramadan. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who travels and with him is a slave girl during the month of Ramadan, can he have intercourse with her? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who travels during the month of Ramadan and with him is a slave girl, and whether it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her during the day. He said: 'Glory be to Allah! Does he not recognize the sanctity of the month of Ramadan? For him, during the night, is a long duration.' I said, 'Is it not for him that he can eat, drink, and shorten (the prayer)?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has granted concession to the traveler regarding breaking the fast and shortening (the prayer) as a mercy and alleviation for the place of fatigue, exertion, and difficulty of travel. But He did not grant him concession regarding intercourse with women during the day while traveling in the month of Ramadan. He obligated upon him making up the fasts, and did not obligate upon him making up the complete prayers when he returns from his journey.' Then he said: 'And the Sunnah cannot be measured by analogy, and I, whenever I travel during the month of Ramadan, do not eat except for the bare necessities, and do not drink until I quench my thirst completely.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who goes to his slave girl during the day in the month of Ramadan while traveling. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This one does not know the right of the month of Ramadan. For him, during the night, is a long duration (for rest/recovery).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Does the menstruating woman make up the fast?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'Does she make up the prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said, 'From where does this come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first one to analogise was Iblees.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a woman who woke up fasting, and when the day rose or it was evening, she menstruated. Should she break the fast? He said: Yes, and even if it was the time of Maghrib, let her break. He said: And I asked him about a woman who saw purity at the beginning of the day from the month of Ramadan, so she bathed and did not eat. So what should she do during that day? He said: She breaks the fast for that day, for her breaking is due to the blood.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who begins her menstruation during the month of Ramadan before the sun sets. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She breaks her fast when she begins menstruating.'

Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the woman who gives birth after Asr, would she complete that day or break (the fast)? He (peace be upon him) said: She would break, and she would make up for that day.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman with post-menstrual bleeding (mustahadha). He said: 'She fasts the month of Ramadan, except for the days in which she used to menstruate, then she makes them up after it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I wrote to him (peace be upon him): A woman became clean from her menstruation or from the blood of her postpartum bleeding at the beginning of a day in the month of Ramadan, then she experienced istihadah (continuous non-menstrual bleeding). She prayed and fasted the entire month of Ramadan without doing what the woman with istihadah does, which is performing ghusl for every two prayers. Is her fasting and her prayer valid or not? He (peace be upon him) wrote: She must make up her fasting, but she does not make up her prayer.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who woke up in the morning fasting, and when the day rose, or it was the evening, she menstruated. Would she break her fast? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, and even if it was just before Maghrib, let her break her fast. And regarding a woman who saw signs of purity at the beginning of the day during the month of Ramadan, but did not bathe and did not eat. How should she deal with that day? He (peace be upon him) said: Her breaking of the fast is due to the blood (menstruation).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who fell ill during the month of Ramadan and died in Shawwal, so she bequeathed to me that I make up the fasts on her behalf. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Was she cured from her illness?' I said: 'No, she died in it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not make up the fasts on her behalf, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not make it obligatory upon her.' I said: 'But I desire to make up the fasts on her behalf, and she had bequeathed that to me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'How can you make up for something which Allah did not make obligatory upon her? So, if you desire to fast for yourself, then fast.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a woman who fell ill during the month of Ramadan, or menstruated, or travelled, and then died before the end of the month of Ramadan. Does her fasting have to be made up on her behalf? He said: As for menstruation and illness, no; and as for travel, yes.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who makes a vow upon herself to fast two consecutive months. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She fasts, and resumes her days which she stayed (from fasting), until she completes two months.' I said, 'What is your view if she has despaired of menstruation (i.e., reached menopause), does she make it up?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She does not make it up; the first (period) suffices for her.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'My wife made it upon herself the fasting of two months. She gave birth to her child, and pregnancy overtook her, so she was not strong enough for the fasting.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Let her give in charity, in place of each day, a Mudd for a poor person.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the free man upon whom fasting of two consecutive months is obligatory due to Dhikr (Zihar), so he fasts one month then falls sick. He said: He starts again, and if he increased upon the other month by a day or two days, he builds upon what remains.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The fasting for the expiation of the oath in Dhihar is two consecutive months, and consecutiveness is that he fasts one month and fasts from the other month some days or a part of it. So if something occurs to him that causes him to break his fast, he breaks it, then he makes up for what remains upon him. And if he fasts one month, then something occurs to him, so he breaks before he fasts anything from the other month, so he has not maintained consecutiveness, he must repeat the entire fasting.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who has the fasting of two consecutive months upon him, can he break the continuity between the days? He (peace be upon him) said: If he fasts more than a month and connects it, then a matter presents itself to him and he breaks the fast, then there is no problem. But if it is less than a month, or exactly a month, then upon him is that he repeats the fasting.
