A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had the fast of two consecutive months upon him due to Dhikr (Zihar), so he fasted Dhu al-Qadah. Then Dhu al-Hijjah entered upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast Dhu al-Hijjah entirely, except for the days of Tashreeq. He makes them up on the first day of Muharram until he completes three days, so he will have fasted two consecutive months.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it is not befitting for him to approach his wife until he makes up the three days of Tashreeq which he did not fast. And there is no harm if he fasts a month, then fasts some days from the following month. Then if a reason presents itself to him, he can break it, then make them up after the completion of the two months.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who fasted during the two months of Sha'ban, then the month of Ramadan caught up with him, he said: He should fast Ramadan and resume the fasting. So if he fasted during the two months and added one day to the half, he has fulfilled the remainder.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man upon whom fasting for a month was made obligatory, so he fasted fifteen days of it, then a matter presented itself preventing him, he said: If he had fasted fifteen days, then for him it is permissible to make up what remains, and if he had fasted less than fifteen days, it would not suffice for him until he fasts a complete month.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about breaking the fast of the expiation for an oath, and the expiation for Dhihar, and the expiation for killing. He said: If fasting two consecutive months is upon a man, and he breaks his fast or falls ill during the first month, then upon him is that he repeats the fasting. And if he fasted the first month, and fasted part of the second month, then an excuse presents itself to him for which there is a valid reason, then upon him is that he makes up for it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who killed a man by error during the Sacred Month. He said: 'The wergild is intensified upon him, and upon him is the emancipation of a neck, or fasting two consecutive months from the Sacred months.' I said, 'Supposing something enters into this?' So he said: 'What is it?' I said, 'The day of Eid and the days of Tashreeq?' He said: 'He should fast them, for it is a right that is obligatory upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man killed a man in the Sanctuary.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a wergild and a third, and he must fast two consecutive months from the Sacred Months, and emancipate a neck, and feed sixty poor people.' I said: 'Does something enter into this?' He said: 'And what would it be?' I said: 'The two Eids, and the days of Tashreeq?' He said: 'He must fast them, for it is a right necessitated upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every fast can be separated (broken into parts) except for the three days [of expiation] regarding an oath.

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The fasting of three days as an expiation for an oath is consecutive, there cannot be a gap between them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Aban, from Al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The seven days and the three days in Hajj are not separated; rather, they are at the status of the three days regarding the oath.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Karram, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have made it upon myself to fast until the Rising of the Qaim (peace be upon him).' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Fast, and do not fast during the journey, nor the two Eids, nor the days of Tashreeq, nor the day wherein there is doubt from the month of Ramadan.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, who said: Al-Husayn wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man vowed to fast a known number of days, so he fasted some of them, then he fell ill and broke his fast. Should he begin his fasting anew, or should he count what has passed?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'He should count what has passed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn Abdullah, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Upon me is the fasting of a month if my uncle comes out of prison.' So he came out. I woke up in the morning intending to fast, and one of our companions came to me. So I called for the midday meal and ate with him. He said, 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who made it upon himself the fasting of a month in Al-Kufa, and a month in Al-Madina, and a month in Al-Makkah, due to an affliction he was tested with. So it was fulfilled that he fasted a month in Al-Kufa, and he entered Al-Madina and fasted eighteen days in it, and the camelier (or the one riding the camel) did not remain upon it (i.e., did not complete the fast while traveling). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He fasts what remains of it when he arrives at his city.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that Ali (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a man who vowed to fast for a 'time' (zaman), he said: The 'time' is five months, and the 'season' (hin) is six months. Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Yielding its fruit in every season (hin) by the permission of its Lord.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who fasts a fast that he has stipulated upon himself, or who fasts from the Sacred Months, and the month and the two months pass by him without him fulfilling it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not fast during the journey, nor should he make up anything from the voluntary fasts except the three days which he used to fast from each month, and he should not make them equal in status to the obligatory [fasts], except that I love for you that you remain constant upon the righteous deed.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And as for the one who fasts the Sacred Months, it suffices him that he fasts three days in place of each month from the Sacred Months.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man who makes it upon himself for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the fasting of a specified day. He said: 'He should fast it always, during travel and residence.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: Indeed, my mother had made a vow upon herself for Allah: if Allah were to return one of her children from something she feared for him, she would fast on the day he returns, as long as she lived. So she traveled with us to Mecca, and it became doubtful upon us; we did not know whether she should fast or break her fast. So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that, and informed him of what she had vowed upon herself. He said: 'She should not fast during the journey, for Allah has exempted her from His right regarding the fast, but she should fast what she has made upon herself [as the vow].' He said: I asked, 'What do you think if she returns and neglects that?' He said: 'I fear that she might see in that which she vowed what she dislikes [i.e., a consequence or sign of displeasure].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Idrees ibn Zayd and Ali ibn Idrees, who said: We asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed a vow that if he was freed from prison, he would fast the day in which he was freed. Then he became unable to fast due to an illness that afflicted him or for some other reason, so it prolonged for the man during his lifetime, and a lot of fasts had gathered upon him. What is the expiation of that fast? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He expiates for each day with a Mudd of wheat or barley.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed a vow regarding fasting, so he was unable to fulfill it. He said: 'My father used to say: Upon him, in place of each day, is a Mudd.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who vowed upon himself that if he was safe from an illness, or freed from prison, that he would fast every Wednesday, and it was the day in which he was released. So he was unable to fast due to an illness that afflicted him, or other than that. So it was prolonged for the man during his lifetime, and a lot of fasts accumulated upon him. What is the expiation for that? He (peace be upon him) said: He should give in charity, for each day, with a Mudd of wheat, or the price of a Mudd.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one who does not fast the three days from every month, and fasting is difficult upon him. Is there a redemption (expiation) for it? He (peace be upon him) said: A Mudd of food for each day.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Fasting is difficult upon me.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'A dirham you give in charity is superior to fasting a day.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'And I do not like for you to neglect it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yazeed ibn Khalifa, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying, 'I get a headache when I fast these three days, and it is difficult for me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do as I do when I travel. For when I travel, I give in charity for each day a Mudd of the food of my family with which I provide them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Uqba, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! I have aged and weakened from fasting, so what should I do with these three days in every month?' He said, 'O Uqba, give in charity a dirham for each day.' I said, 'One dirham?' He said, 'Perhaps it is heavy for you, and you are belittling the dirham.' I said, 'The favors of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon me are abundant.' So he said, 'O Uqba, feeding a Muslim is better than fasting for a month.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about the crescents, so he said: 'They are the crescents of the months. So whenever you see the new moon, fast; and when you see it (again), break your fast.'
Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I do not permit regarding the crescent moon except the testimony of two just men.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: The testimony of women is not valid regarding the new moon.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of God upon him) said: The testimony of women is not valid regarding the crescent moon, and it is not valid except the testimony of two just men.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from al-Fadl ibn Uthman, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon the people of the Qibla except the sighting; it is not upon the Muslims except the sighting.'

Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whenever you see the crescent moon, fast; and when you see it (again), break the fast. And it is not by opinion, nor by guessing. And the sighting is not that ten persons stand, one of them says 'It is there', while nine look but cannot see it. Rather, if one sees it, a thousand (can) see it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, from al-Salt al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the crescent moon sets before the twilight (afterglow), then it is for its [first] night; and when it sets after the twilight, then it is for two nights [the second night].

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hamza Abu Ya'la, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid, who elevated it (as a mursal), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When the new moon of the month of Rajab is confirmed, count fifty-nine days and fast on the sixtieth day.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr and Muhammad ibn Abi Suhban, from Hafs, from Amr ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharija, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Count Sha'ban as twenty-nine days. If it is cloudy, then start the morning fasting. If it is clear and you looked for it but did not see anything, then start the morning not fasting.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When they see the crescent before the decline (of the sun), it is for the past night, and when they see it after the decline, it is for the coming night.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Murazim, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the crescent moon forms a complete encirclement, it is for two nights, and when you see the shadow of your head in it, it is for three nights.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), or to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'A man deliberately postpones the month in the short days, so he fasts it for a year.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Husayn ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Hamza who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I delay the fasting of three days from each month to the winter, then I fast them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with that.'

Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who has upon him (to make up) three days of the month. Is it permissible for him to delay them, or to fast them at the end of the month? He said: There is no problem. I said: Should he fast them consecutively or separate between them? He said: Whatever he likes; if he wishes, he fasts them consecutively, and if he wishes, he separates between them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the fasting of the Day of Arafat, so he said: Do I fast it today, and it is a day of supplication and asking (of needs).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast the Day of Arafah since the fasting of the month of Ramadan was revealed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb al-Naysaburi, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not fast on the day of Ashura, nor on the day of Arafat, in Mecca, nor in Medina, nor in your hometown, nor in any of the cities.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: 'Muhammad ibn Abi Umair narrated to us from Zayd al-Narsy, who said: I heard Ubayd ibn Zurara asking Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)' about the fasting of the day of Ashura, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever fasts it, his share from the fasting of that day is the share of Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad.' I said, 'And what is their share from that day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Fire. May Allah protect us from the Fire and from the deed which brings one closer to the Fire.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Aban, from Abdul Malik who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Fast of Tasua and Ashura from the month of Muharram, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Tasua is a day in which Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were surrounded in Karbala, and the cavalry of the people of Syria gathered against him and encamped upon him, and Ibn Marjana and Umar ibn Sa'd rejoiced at the abundance and multitude of the cavalry, and they considered Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, to be weak, and they were convinced that no helper would come to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) nor would the people of Iraq support him, by my father, the oppressed, the alienated.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And as for the day of Ashura, it is a day in which Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed as a corpse among his companions, and his companions were corpses around him, stripped. So, can a Fast be on that day? No! By the Lord of the Sacred House, it is not a day of Fasting, and it is not except a day of grief and calamity that entered upon the inhabitants of the sky and the inhabitants of the earth and all the believers.' And it is a day of joy and happiness for Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad and the people of Syria. May Allah be Wrathful upon them and upon their offspring. And that is a day in which all the spots of the earth wept for him, except for the spot of Syria. So whoever fasts it or considers it fortunate, Allah will resurrect him with the progeny of Ziyad, morphed of the heart, Angered upon; and whoever hoards provisions in his house, Allah the Exalted will cause hypocrisy to be the end result in his heart until the day he meets Him, and He will snatch away the Blessing from him and from the people of his household and his children, and the Satan will be his partner in all of that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the fasting of the day of Al-Fitr, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting to fast it, nor the fasting of the days of Al-Tashreeq.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the two days after the breaking of the fast (Eid al-Fitr): are they fasted or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike for you that you fast them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, is there for the Muslims an Eid other than the two Eids?' He said, 'Yes, O Hassan, the greatest of them and the most noble.' I said, 'And which day is it?' He said, 'It is the day in which the Commander of the Faithful, peace and prayers of Allah be upon him, was appointed as a sign for the people.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is befitting for us to do on it?' He said, 'Fast it, O Hassan, and increase your prayers upon Muhammad and his family, and disavow to Allah those who oppressed them, for the Prophets, peace and prayers of Allah be upon them, used to order the Successors that on the day in which the Successor was appointed, it should be taken as an Eid.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, so what is for the one who fasts it?' He said, 'The fasting of sixty months; and do not leave the fasting of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, for it is the day in which Prophethood descended upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its reward is like sixty months for you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a mercy to the worlds on the 27th of Rajab. So whoever fasts that day, Allah writes for him the fasting of sixty months. And on the 25th of Dhi al-Qadah, the House (Kaaba) was placed, and it is the first mercy placed upon the face of the earth. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it a resort for the people and a security. So whoever fasts that day, Allah writes for him the fasting of sixty months. And on the first day of Dhi al-Hijjah, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the Friend of the Beneficent, was born. So whoever fasts that day, Allah writes for him the fasting of sixty months.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from his father, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there an Eid for the Muslims other than the day of Friday, and Al-Adha, and Al-Fitr?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the greatest of them in sanctity.' I said, 'And which Eid is it? May I be your sacrifice.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The day in which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) appointed the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: Whoever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla. I said, 'And which day is it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What do you do with the day? Indeed, the year circulates. But it is the eighteenth of Dhi al-Hijjah.' So I said, 'And what is befitting for us to do on that day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You remember Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, therein with fasting, and worship, and remembrance of Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad. For indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he should take that day as an Eid. And thus the Prophets (peace be upon them) used to do; they would bequeath to their successors with that, so they would take it as an Eid.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht, from Hamdan ibn al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Sayqal, who said: Abu al-Hasan, meaning al-Rida (peace be upon him), came out to us on the twenty-fifth day of Dhi al-Qadah, and he said: 'Fast, for I have become a fasting person.' We said: 'May we be sacrificed for you, which day is it?' He said: 'It is a day in which Mercy was spread, the land was spread out, the Ka'bah was established, and Adam (peace be upon him) descended.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Is'hāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Your breaking the fast for your believing brother is superior to your voluntary fasting.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Ays, from Najm ibn Huteym, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever intends fasting, then visits his brother and asks him to break his fast in his presence, let him break it, and let him bring him joy, for it is recorded for him on that day as ten days' [reward]. This is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who visits his brother while he is fasting, and breaks his fast in his presence, and does not inform him of his fasting so as to do him a favour, Allah will write for him the fasting of a year.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Dinawari, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Salih ibn Uqba, who said: I entered upon Jamil ibn Darraj, and in front of him was a tray with a Gassanite dish from which he was eating. He said, 'Come near and eat.' I said, 'I am fasting.' So he left me until he had finished it, and only a little remained. Then he insisted upon me, 'Will you not break your fast?' I said to him, 'Why did you not do this earlier?' He said, 'I wanted to discipline you with that.' Then he said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever a believing man visits while he is fasting, and asks him to eat, and he does not inform him of his fasting so as to favor him with his breaking of the fast, Allah, Majestic is His Praise, will write for him for that day the fasting of a year.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from one of his companions, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mazi (peace be upon him): 'I enter upon a group of people while they are eating, and I have already prayed Asr, and I am fasting. So they say to me, 'Break your fast.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Break, for it is superior.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, Muhammad ibn Isa, Al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim ibn Sufyan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Your breaking of the fast in the house of your Muslim brother is superior to your fasting seventy times over, or ninety times over.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: It is not correct for the wife that she fasts the optional fast except by the permission of her husband.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Nasheeth ibn Salih, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is from the understanding (fiqh) of the guest that he should not fast voluntarily except with the permission of his host; and from the obedience of the wife to her husband is that she should not fast voluntarily except with his permission and command; and from the correctness of the slave, his obedience, and his sincerity to his master is that he should not fast voluntarily except with the permission of his master and his command; and from the righteousness of the child is that he should not fast voluntarily except with the permission of his parents and their command; otherwise, the guest would be ignorant, the wife disobedient, the slave wicked and disobedient, and the child disloyal.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar and others, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, by a chain he mentioned, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man enters a city, he is a guest upon those in it from the people of his religion, until he departs from them. And it is not befitting for the guest that he should fast except with their permission, lest they prepare something which would spoil for them. And it is not befitting for them that they should fast except with the permission of the guest, lest he be shy of them, so he would desire the food but leave it for them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is not for the wife to fast voluntarily except with the permission of her husband.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Amr ibn Jubayr al-Azrami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A woman came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband upon the wife?' He said, 'It is more than that.' She said, 'Inform me of something from that.' He said, 'She does not fast (voluntarily) except with his permission.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he fasted, if he could not find sweet food, would break his fast with water.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man breaks his fast with lukewarm water, it cleanses his liver, washes the sins from the heart, and strengthens the vision and the glare.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Sindy, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Breaking the fast upon water washes the sins from the heart.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from the one who mentioned it, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he broke his fast, would begin with a sweet, breaking his fast upon it. If he could not find it, then a lump of sugar or dates. If all of that was unavailable, then lukewarm water. And he would say: 'It cleanses the stomach and the liver, and improves the breath and the mouth, and strengthens the teeth, and strengthens the eyeballs, and clears the vision, and washes away sins with a washing, and settles the rising veins and the dominant bitterness, and cuts the phlegm, and extinguishes the heat from the stomach, and removes the headache.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to break his fast on dates during the season of dates, and on fresh dates during the season of fresh dates.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would first break his fast with fresh dates during the season of fresh dates, and with dried dates during the season of dried dates.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Fuzayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The ritual bath (ghusl) in the month of Ramadan is at the time of the sun's setting, shortly before it. Then one prays, then breaks the fast.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How many nights should one bathe during the month of Ramadan?' He said: 'The night of the nineteenth, and the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third.' I said, 'And if it is difficult for me?' He said: 'The twenty-first and the twenty-third.' I said, 'And if it is difficult for me?' He said: 'That is enough for you now.'

Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn al-Qasim (al-Qasim) who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the night in which what is sought is sought, when is the bath (ghusl)? So he (peace be upon him) said: From the beginning of the night; and if you wish, when you stand (for prayer) at its end. And I asked him about the standing (for prayer), so he said: You stand in its beginning and its end.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Abu Baseer said to him, 'What do you say regarding the Prayer in the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'For the month of Ramadan is a sanctity and a right, unlike any of the other months. Pray what you are able to during the month of Ramadan, voluntarily by night and by day. So if you are able to pray a thousand cycles (rak'ah) every day and night, then do so. Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) at the end of his life used to pray a thousand cycles every day and night. So pray, O Abu Muhammad, an increase during Ramadan.' So I said, 'How much? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'For the twenty nights, you should pray during every night twenty cycles - eight cycles being before the dusk (Isha), and twelve cycles after it, besides what you were praying before. So when the last ten days enter, pray thirty cycles during every night - eight cycles being before the dusk, and twenty-two cycles after it, besides what you were doing before that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaq and Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to increase in his prayer during the month of Ramadan. When he prayed the 'Isha prayer, he would pray after it, so the people would stand behind him. He would enter (his chamber) and leave them, then he would come out again, so they would come and stand behind him. He would leave them and enter (again) repeatedly. He said, and he said: 'Do not pray after the 'Isha prayer in other than the month of Ramadan.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the last ten [days] entered, would tighten his gown, keep away from the women, revive the night [in prayer], and devote himself to worship.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Hasan, from Suleyman Al-Ja'fari, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray one hundred cycles on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third, reciting in each cycle, "Say: He, Allah, is One" ten times.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Shuayb Al-Mahamili, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), when it was the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third, would engage in supplication until the night declined. So when the night declined, he prayed.
The Month of Ramadan is thirty days, not being deficient, ever! And from him, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfa — similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, God — Blessed and Exalted — created the world in six days, then He subtracted those from the days of the year; and the year is three hundred and fifty-four (354) days. Sha'ban will never be complete, ever; Ramadan will never be deficient — by God — ever! And an obligation (fard) can never be deficient. Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — says: 'and that you complete the number' (Quran 2:185) And Shawwal is twenty-nine days. And Dhu al-Qa'dah is thirty days, due to the Words of God — Mighty and Majestic: 'And We appointed with Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was complete: forty nights' (Quran 7:142) And Dhu al-Hijjah is twenty-nine days. And al-Muharram is thirty days. Then the months after that alternate: a complete month and a deficient month.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfa ibn Mansur, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The month of Ramadan is thirty days, not deficient, by Allah, ever!

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You should say during the last ten days of the month of Ramadan, every night: 'I seek refuge in the Majesty of Your Noble Face lest the month of Ramadan pass me by, or dawn rise from this night of mine, while You have a sin or a debt against me for which You will punish me.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ayoub ibn Yaqteen, or someone else from them (peace be upon him). The supplication for the last ten (nights): You should say on the first night, O He who causes the entry of the night into the day, and the entry of the day into the night, and the Extractor of the living from the dead, and the Extractor of the dead from the living! O Sustainer of whom He wills without measure! O Allah, O Beneficent, O Allah, O Merciful, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah! For You are the Beautiful Names, and the Exalted Examples, and the Greatness, and the Loftiness! I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his Family, and to make my name in this night among the fortunate, and my soul with the martyrs, and my good deeds in 'Illiyin, and my bad deeds forgiven. And to grant me conviction with which my heart is gladdened, and faith which removes doubt from me, and to please me with what You have apportioned for me, and give us good in the world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the punishment of the fire, and grant us therein Your remembrance, and Your gratitude, and hopefulness to You, and return, and success for what You succeeded Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) in. And you should say on the second night: O He who brings forth the day from the night, so we are in darkness, and the Mover of the sun to its resting place by Your decree! O Mighty, O Knowing, and the Ordainer of the moon's phases until it returns like the old palm branch! O Light of every light, and the destination of every hope, and the Guardian of every blessing! O Allah, O Beneficent, O Allah, O Holy, O One, O Alone, O Solitary, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah! For You are the Beautiful Names and the Exalted Examples. Then you return to the first supplication up to his words: 'I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family,' up to the end of the supplication. And you should say on the third night: O Lord of the Night of Decree, and the Maker of it better than a thousand months, and Lord of the night and the day, and the mountains and the seas, and the darknesses and the lights, and the earth and the sky! O Creator, O Fashioner, O Affectionate, O Benefactor, O Allah, O Beneficent, O Allah, O Eternal, O Allah, O Initiator, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah! For You are the Beautiful Names and the Exalted Examples, a

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad bin Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the supplication in the month of Ramadan, during every night you should say: 'O Allah, I ask You regarding what You judge and measure from the ordained matter, from the wise decree, from the judgment that is neither returned nor changed, that You write me among the pilgrims of Your Sacred House, whose Hajj is accepted, their evil deeds expiated from them, their sins forgiven, their striving appreciated.' And that You make, regarding what You judge and measure from the ordained matter, from the wise decree, during the Night of Predestination, from the judgment that is neither returned nor changed, that You prolong my life, and expand my sustenance, and make me among those by whom You help Your religion, and do not replace me with others.

Muhammad ibn Isa, by his chain, from the Righteous Ones (peace be upon them) who said: You should repeat this supplication on the night of the 23rd of Ramadan, prostrating, standing, and sitting, in every state, and throughout the whole month, whenever it is possible for you and whenever the time presents itself, saying after praising Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): O Allah, be for your guardian, so-and-so ibn so-and-so, during this hour and every hour, a guardian, a protector, a helper, a proof, a guide, an aid, and a witness, until You settle him in Your earth willingly and grant him enjoyment therein for a long time. And you should say on the fourth night: O Splitter of the dawn, and Maker of the night as tranquility, and the sun and moon for calculation, O Mighty, O Knowledgeable, O Possessor of Favor and Grace, Strength and Power, Bounty and Bestowal, Kingdom and Honor, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O Allah, O Merciful, O Allah, O Solitary, O One, O Allah, O Manifest, O Hidden, O Living, O, there is no god but You, to You belong the Beautiful Names, the Lofty Examples, and the Greatness. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family, and to make my name among the fortunate in this night, and my soul with the martyrs, and my good deeds in the Illiyyun, and my bad deeds forgiven, and to grant me certainty that touches my heart, and faith that removes doubt from me, and contentment with what You have apportioned for me, and give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the burning punishment, and grant me remembrance of You, gratitude to You, hope in You, return to You, repentance, and success in what You succeeded Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) in. And you should say on the fifth night: O Maker of the night as clothing, and the day as livelihood, and the earth as an expanse, and the mountains as pegs, O Allah, O Conqueror, O Allah, O Compeller, O Allah, O Listener, O Allah, O Near, O Allah, O Answerer, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah, to You belong the Beautiful Names, the Lofty Examples, the Greatness, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family, and to make my name among the fortunate in this night, and my soul with the martyrs, and my good deeds in the Illiyyun, and my bad deeds forgiven, and

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When it is the last night of the month of Ramadan, say: 'O Allah, this is the month of Ramadan in which You revealed the Quran, and it is coming to an end, and I seek refuge with Your noble Face, O Lord, lest the dawn rise from this night of mine, or the month of Ramadan pass away, while there is a debt or sin against me for which You intend to punish me on the Day I meet You.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding bidding farewell to the month of Ramadan. O Allah, You said in Your Revealed Book: 'The month of Ramadan is that in which the Quran was revealed.' And this is the month of Ramadan, and it has passed. So I ask You by Your Noble Face and Your Complete Words. If there remains upon me a sin that You have not forgiven me, or You intend to punish me for it, or measure it out to me, let the dawn of this night rise, or this month end, only after You have forgiven it for me. O Most Merciful of the merciful ones. O Allah, to You is the praise with all its praises, its beginning and its end, whatever You said of Yourself from it, and what the praising creatures said, the diligent, the counted, the reverent, who mention You and give thanks to You. Those whom You supported in fulfilling Your right, from the varieties of Your creation, from the Proximate Angels, the Prophets, and the Messengers, and the varieties of speakers and glorifiers of You from all the worlds. Because You brought us to the month of Ramadan, and upon us from Your bounties, and with us from Your portion and favor, and the manifesting of Your grace. Therefore, to You belongs the ultimate praise, the eternal, the perpetual, the constant, the continuous, which does not cease throughout eternity. Majestic is Your praise. You supported us in it until we fulfilled its fasting and its standing in prayer, and whatever was from us in it of righteousness, or gratitude, or remembrance. O Allah, so accept it from us with the best of Your acceptance, and Your overlooking, and Your excusing, and Your pardoning, and Your forgiveness, and the reality of Your pleasure. Until You make us successful in it with every sought good and generous bestowed gift, and protect us in it from every feared thing, or brought affliction, or earned sin. O Allah, I ask You by the greatness of what anyone from Your creation asked You of, from the noble of Your Names, and the beautiful of Your praise, and the specific of Your supplication. That You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You make this month of ours the greatest month of Ramadan that has passed us since You sent us down to the world. A blessing in the protection of my religion, and the salvation of my soul, and the fu

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Feed (eat) on the day of Al-Fitr before you go out to the prayer place.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suweyd, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He should eat on the day of Al-Fitr before he prays, and he should not eat on the day of Al-Azha until the Imam finishes (the prayer).

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When it is the first day of Shawwal, a caller proclaims: O Believers! Go forth to your awards.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Jabir! The awards of Allah are not like the awards of these kings.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the Day of Awards.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: When it is the morning of the Day of Fitr, a caller proclaims: 'Go forth to your awards!'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Ismail Al-Razi, from Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding fasting, for it has been narrated that they will not be granted success in fasting?' He said, 'Indeed, the supplication of the Angel has been answered regarding them.' I said, 'And how is that? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'When the people killed Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded an Angel to call out: O you unjust community, the killers of the family of their Prophet! May Allah not grant you success in fasting nor in breaking the fast.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'O Abdullah! There is no Eid for the Muslims, neither Al-Adha nor Al-Fitr, except that it renews grief for the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them) within it.' I said, 'And why is that?' He said, 'Because they see their rights in the hands of others.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Abdullah ibn Latif al-Taflisi, from Razin, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was struck with the sword, his head fell, then they began to cut off his head. A caller called out from the middle of the Throne: 'Indeed! O you confused community, the strayed ones after their Prophet! May Allah not grant you success for Eid al-Adha nor for Eid al-Fitr.' He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So, by Allah, there is no doubt that they were not granted success, nor will they be granted success until the avenger of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) takes revenge.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Harrani, from Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Nawfaly, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I broke my fast on the Day of Al-Fitr with figs and a date.' So he said to me, 'You have gathered together a blessing and a Sunnah.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Yaqub ibn Yazeed from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar or someone else from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when perfume was brought to him on the day of Eid al-Fitr, would begin with his wives.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every person you include among your dependents, whether free or slave, upon you is to pay the Fitra on their behalf. He (peace be upon him) said: And giving the Fitra before the Prayer is superior, and after the Prayer is (counted as) charity.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Fitra, so he (obligatory) Fitra, so he said: 'Upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, from every human being, a Sa' of wheat, or a Sa' of dates, or a Sa' of raisins.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Dates are superior in the Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr) compared to other foods, because they provide benefit more quickly; and that is because when it falls into the hand of its owner, he eats from it. He said, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Zakat was revealed while the people did not yet have wealth, so it was the Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr).'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Fitra is that you give it before you go out to the Eid, so it is Fitra; and if it was after you go out to the Eid, so it is charity.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Fitra (alms-tax on the head), how much should be paid on behalf of every head from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins? He said: A Sa'a, by the Sa'a of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about hastening the Fitra by one day, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'So what do you think if we gather it and make its price silver and give it to one Muslim man?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Jameel ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with a man giving on behalf of his dependents while they are absent from him, and with his instructing them so that they give on his behalf while he is absent from them.

A number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said: I wrote to the Imam (peace be upon him) asking him about the Fitra and how much should be paid. He wrote back: 'Six Ratls of dates by the Medinite measure, and that is nine Ratls by the Baghdadi measure.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, and he was a pilgrim with us, said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) via the hand of my father; may I be sacrificed for you. Indeed, our companions differed regarding the Sa'a; some of them say the Fitra is by the Medinite Sa'a, and some of them say by the Iraqi Sa'a. So he wrote to me: The Sa'a is six Ratls by the Medinite measure, and nine Ratls by the Iraqi measure. He said, and he informed me that by weight it is one thousand one hundred and seventy weights.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man and Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man does not have with him anything from the Fitra except what he can pay for himself alone. Should he give it to a stranger, or should he eat it himself and his dependents?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give it to one of his dependents. Then the other one should give it from himself in turn. Thus they repeat it, and it becomes on behalf of all of them together, one Fitra.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I said, 'Regarding the poor person upon whom charity is given, is Zakat al-Fitr obligatory upon him?' He said, 'Yes, he should give from what is given as charity to him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl al-Basri, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I wrote to him: 'Does the executor purify [pay zakat] on behalf of the orphans with the Zakat of al-Fitra if they have wealth?' So he wrote: 'There is no zakat upon an orphan.' And [he asked] about a slave whose master dies while he is absent from him in another city, and in his hand is wealth belonging to his master, and the time for Fitra arrives: 'Can he purify [pay zakat] on behalf of himself from the wealth of his master, and it has already gone to the orphans?' He said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is there Fitra upon the people of the valleys?' So he said: 'The Fitra is upon everyone who consumes food. So upon him is that he pays from that subsistence.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about a man in the desert who was unable to give the Fitra. He said: 'He should give in charity four Artals of milk.'

A number of our companions, from Saahl ibn Ziyaad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a guest from his brothers with him, and the Day of Fitrah arrives; does he pay the Fitrah on his behalf? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. The Fitrah is obligatory upon everyone who has dependents, from male or female, young or old, free or slave.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if a man gives to another man on behalf of two heads, and three, and four, meaning the Fitra.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureyd, from Malik Al-Juhni, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Zakat of Fitra. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it to the Muslims. So if you do not find a Muslim, then give it to a weak one (poor Muslim), and give to your relative from it if you wish.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the charity of Fitra, 'Can I give it to other than the people of Wilayah, from the poor ones of my neighbours?' He said: 'Yes. The neighbour is more rightful with it, due to the place (status) well known'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man pays the Zakat of al-Fitra on behalf of his Mukatab (contracted slave), the slave of his wife, his Christian and Magian slave, and whoever he closes his door upon (i.e., dependents under his roof).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Mu'ttab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Go and give the Fitra on behalf of our dependents, and give on behalf of the slaves, and gather them together and do not leave any of them, for if you leave a person from them, I would fear the loss for him.' I said: 'And what is the loss?' He said: 'Death.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his brother Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said: I sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) some dirhams, for me and for others, and I wrote to him informing him that they are from the Fitra of the dependents. So he wrote in his own handwriting: 'I have taken possession of it, and accepted'.

Abu Al-Abbas Al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said: I asked him about the Fitra, for whom is it? He said: For the Imam. I said to him, 'So can I inform my companions?' He said: 'Yes, the ones whom you intend to purify from them.' And he said: 'There is no problem if you were to give, and convert the price of that as silver (cash).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third that a group of people asked me about the Fitra, and they ask me to carry its price to you; and this man had been sent to you last year, and he asked me to ask you, but I forgot that, and I have sent to you this year on behalf of each head from my dependents, a dirham, based on the value of nine Rats per dirham. So what is your view, may Allah be my ransom for you, regarding that? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The Fitra, questions about it have become numerous, and I dislike everything that leads to publicity. Therefore, cease mentioning it, and collect from those who pay it, and withhold from those who do not pay it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when it was the last ten [days], would seclude himself in the mosque, and a dome made of hair was set up for him, and he would roll up his apron and fold his bed. And some of them said, 'And he would isolate himself from the women.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for isolating himself from the women, no [he did not do so].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Battle of Badr took place in the month of Ramadan, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not perform I'tikaf. When it was the following year, he performed I'tikaf for twenty nights: ten for his current year and ten as compensation for what was missed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) secluded himself (in the mosque) during the month of Ramadan in the first ten days. Then he secluded himself in the second year during the middle ten days. Then he secluded himself in the third year during the last ten days. Then he did not cease to seclude himself during the last ten days.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Itikaaf (seclusion in the mosque) except with fasting.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Musa ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Itikaaf except with Fasting'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Itikaf (seclusion) except with fasting in the general Masjid.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding Itikaf in Baghdad in some of its mosques?' So he said: 'There is no Itikaf except in a congregational mosque in which a just Imam has prayed the congregational prayer, and there is no harm if one performs Itikaf in the mosque of Al-Kufa, and Al-Basra, and the mosque of Al-Madina, and the mosque of Makkah.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no Itikaf (spiritual retreat) except during the last ten days of the month of Ramadan. And he said: Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I do not consider Itikaf to be valid except in the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), or the Mosque of the Messenger (Al-Masjid Al-Nabawi), or a congregational Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Jami'). And it is not befitting for the person performing Itikaf to leave the mosque except for a necessity that is required, and then he should not sit [outside] until he returns. And the woman is similar to that [in ruling].

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about Itikaf (seclusion in a mosque). He said: Itikaf is not valid except in the Sacred Mosque, or the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), or the Mosque of Kufa, or a general congregation mosque, and you should fast as long as you are in Itikaf.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalat ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: The one performing Itikaaf in Makkah prays in whichever of its houses he desires; it is the same to him whether he prays in the Masjid or in its houses.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one performing Itikaaf in Makkah may pray in whichever of its houses he desires, and the one performing Itikaaf elsewhere may not pray except in the Masjid which he has specified.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband was absent, so he returned while she was in Itikaaf (seclusion) by her husband's permission. She exited from the mosque to her house when news of his arrival reached her, and she prepared herself for her husband until he had intercourse with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had exited the mosque before three days had passed, and she had not stipulated a specific duration in her Itikaaf, then upon her is the penalty of the one who performs Zihaar.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Itikaaf (seclusion) is not valid in less than three days, and whoever performs Itikaaf should Fast; and it is befitting for the one performing Itikaaf that when he does perform Itikaaf, he should stipulate just as the one who wears an Ihraam stipulates.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When one performs Itikaaf for a day and there is no stipulation, it is for him to go out and terminate the Itikaaf. And if he stays for two days and there is no stipulation, it is not for him to terminate his Itikaaf until three days have passed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) initiated me without my asking him, so he said: 'The Itikaf is for three days, meaning the Sunnah, if Allah wills.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The sky remains overcast over us in Iraq for a day, two days, and three days. So which day should we fast?' He said: 'Look at the day on which you fasted in the past year, and fast on the fifth day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Khudri, from some of his elders, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Fast in the coming year on the fifth day from the day you fasted in during the former year.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Sayyari who said: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to al-Askari (peace be upon him) asking him about what has been narrated regarding the calculation for fasting from your forefathers — specifically counting five days between the first of the past year and the second year that is coming. So he (the Imam) wrote back: 'Correct. But count five (days) for every four years, and in the fifth year count six, between the former and the new (year). As for the rest, it is (always) five and five.' Al-Sayyari said: 'This is due to the matter of the leap year.' He said: 'Our companions have calculated it and found it to be correct.' He said: 'And Muhammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to him in the year 238 (AH): This calculation is not feasible for every person to act upon. Rather, this is only for the one who understands the yearly cycles and knows when the leap year falls, and then the crescent of the month of Ramadan is confirmed for him on the first night. So when the crescent is confirmed for its night and he knows the years, it will be correct for him, if God wills.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed we remain in winter for a day or two days without seeing any sun or star. So which day should we fast?' He said: 'Look at the day in which you fasted from the previous year, count five days, and fast on the fifth day.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not upon the one performing Itikaaf that he goes out from the Masjid except to the Friday (Prayer), or a funeral, or defecation.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: I was in Al-Madina during the month of Ramadan, so I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I intend to perform Itikaaf, so what should I say and what should I impose upon myself?' He said, 'Do not go out of the mosque except for a need that is indispensable, and do not sit under the shades until you return to your seat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the one performing Itikaaf to exit the mosque except for a need that is indispensable. Then, he should not sit [outside] until he returns. Nor does he exit for anything except for a funeral or to visit a sick person, and he should not sit [outside] until he returns. And the Itikaaf of the woman is similar to that.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the male performing Itikaaf becomes sick and the female performing Itikaaf menstruates, so he should go to his house, then return when he is cured and he should Fast. And in another report from him: 'That is not upon the sick one'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the female performing Itikaaf, when she menstruates, he said: She should return to her house, and when she is clean, she returns, and she makes up for what is upon her.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one performing Itikaaf who sleeps with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he does, so upon him would be what is upon the one who does Zihaar'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one performing Itikaaf who had relations with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is in the status of the one who breaks a fast of a day from the month of Ramadan.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one performing Itikaaf going to his wife, so he said: He should not go to his wife at night nor during the day while he is performing Itikaaf.

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man was captured by the Romans and did not fast the month of Ramadan, and he did not know which month it was.' He said: 'He should fast a month, and he should envisage and calculate. So if the month he fasted was before the month of Ramadan, it would not suffice him; and if it was after Ramadan, it would suffice him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yahya ibn Amr ibn Khalifa al-Zayyat, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of youths! It is upon you to use the marital relationship (al-bah). So if you are not in a position to do so, upon you is with the Fasting, for it is its subduer.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Al-Sakhar Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim, raised it to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) looked at the people on the Day of Fitr playing and laughing, so he said to his companions and turned towards them: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the month of Ramadan as a race track for His creation so that they might compete in His obedience to achieve His Pleasure. So a group preceded in it and succeeded, and others were left behind and failed. So the wonder, the utmost wonder, is from the laughing and playing ones on the day in which the do-gooders are rewarded and the deficient ones lose out. And I swear by Allah! If the covering were removed, the good-doer would be occupied with his goodness and the evil-doer with his evil.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥarz ibn Muḥammad, who said: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him), 'Why did Allāh obligate fasting?' So the answer came: 'So that the rich may experience the pangs of hunger, and thus feel compassion for the poor.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Imran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A group of people were brought to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), while he was sitting in the Masjid in Kufa. He found them eating during the day in the month of Ramadan. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to them: 'Did you eat while breaking the fast?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Are you Jews?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'Christians?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'So on what basis are you different from Islam?' They said, 'But we are Muslims.' He said: 'So are you travelers?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'Is there among you an illness that obligates breaking the fast, which we are not aware of, for you are more perceptive of yourselves? Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "But! The human being is evidence against himself."' They said, 'But we have become such that there is no excuse in us.' He said, so the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) smiled, then said: 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' They said, 'We testify that there is no god except Allah, and we do not know Muhammad.' He said: 'But he is the Messenger of Allah.' They said, 'We do not know him with that. Rather, he is a Bedouin who called to himself.' He said: 'If you accept, or else I will surely kill you.' They said, 'Even if you do so.' So he assigned the Thursday police to them and went out with them to the rear of Kufa. He ordered that two pits be dug, and one was dug beside the other. Then a large hole, like a pomegranate, was pierced between them. He said to them: 'I will place you in one of these two pits and ignite fire in the other, so I will kill you with the smoke.' They said, 'And even if you do so, for rather, this worldly life will end.' So he placed them gently into one of the two pits, then ordered the fire, so it was ignited in the other pit. Then he began calling out to them, time after time: 'What are you saying?' So they answered him: 'Decide what you decide,' until they died. He said, then he turned away, and the caravans traveled with his deed, and the people discussed it. So one day, while he was in the Masjid, a Jew from the people of Yathrib came to him. The Jews in Yathrib had acknowledged that he was their m

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the day in which there is doubt whether it is from Sha'ban. He said: 'That I fast a day from Sha'ban is more beloved to me than that I break the fast of a day from the month of Ramadan.'

I asked him about the day in which there is a doubt about whether it is from the month of Ramadan — one does not know whether it is from Sha'ban or from Ramadan — and one fasted it, and it turned out to be from the month of Ramadan. He said: It is a day of success granted to him, and there is no make-up obligation upon him.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man fasts the day about which there is doubt whether it is from the month of Ramadan, and it turns out to be so.' He said: 'It is something for which he was divinely granted success.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ribat, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I fasted the day concerning which there is doubt, and it turned out to be from the month of Ramadan — shall I make it up?' He said: 'No, it is a day for which you were granted divine success (tawfiq).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Janah, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Bashir al-Nabbal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about fasting on the day of doubt. So he said: Fast it. For if it be from Sha'ban, it would be a voluntary fast, and if it be from the Month of Ramadan, then it is a day for which you were granted success.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man fasted for a day, not knowing whether it was from the month of Ramadan or from another month. Then a group of people came and testified that it was from the month of Ramadan. Some people said, "According to us, it is not accepted."' He said, 'Yes, it is accepted.' I said, 'They say: You fasted while you did not know if this was from the month of Ramadan or from another.' He said, 'Yes, count it.' For indeed, it is something God has guided you to. Indeed, the day of doubt should be fasted as being from Sha'ban and not as being from the month of Ramadan, because it is forbidden that a person act alone in fasting on the day of doubt. Rather, he should make the intention from the night before that he is fasting from Sha'ban. So if it turns out to be from the month of Ramadan, it suffices for him through the grace of God the Exalted and by what He has eased upon His servants — and had it not been for that, the people would have been destroyed.

I entered upon Abu al-Abbas at al-Hira, so he said, 'O Abu Abdillah, what do you say regarding the fast today?' So I said, 'That is up to the Imam — if you fast, we fast, and if you break the fast, we break the fast.' So he said, 'O boy, bring me the food!' So I ate with him. and I know, by God, that it was a day from the month of Ramadan. So my breaking the fast for a day and making it up is easier upon me than that my neck be struck off, and God not be worshipped.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from al-Khadir ibn Abd al-Malik, from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the day in which there is doubt — for the people are alleging that whoever fasts it is at the status of one who breaks a fast during the month of Ramadan. So he said: They lied! If it was from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day for which he was given divine success, and if it was from other than it, then it is at the level of what has passed of the days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said — and he was at al-Hira during the era of Abu al-Abbas —: 'I went in to him while the people had doubts about the fast, and by Allah it was indeed from the month of Ramadan. I greeted him and he said: O Abu Abdillah, did you fast today? I said: No, and the meal was in front of him. He said: Come near and eat. He said: So I drew near and ate. He said: And I said: Fasting is with you and breaking fast is with you.' Then the man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): You broke fast in a day from the month of Ramadan? He said: Yes, by Allah! Breaking a fast of a day from the month of Ramadan is more beloved to me than having my neck struck.

Verily, when Allah, Blessed and High, took the covenants of the servants, He commanded the (Black) Stone, so it swallowed them. And for that reason, (the pilgrim) says: 'My entrustment, I have fulfilled it, and my covenant I have renewed, so that you (the Stone) may testify for me with loyalty.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Bukeyr, from al-Halabi who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Why was kissing the Stone prescribed?' He said: 'When God, Mighty and Majestic, took the covenant of the Children of Adam, He summoned the Stone from Paradise and commanded it, so it swallowed the covenant. Thus, it testifies for those who fulfill their covenant with it.'
