Muhammad ibn Yahya and someone else, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammat, from Bukayr ibn A'yan who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): For what reason did Allah place the Stone in the corner in which it is found, and not in any other corner? And for what reason is it kissed? And for what reason was it brought out from Paradise? And for what reason was the covenant of the servants and the pledge placed in it and not in any other? And what is the explanation for that? Inform me — may Allah make me your ransom — for my contemplation of this matter is truly astonishing. He said: So he (the Imam) said: You have asked and complicated yourself with the question, and investigated thoroughly. So understand the answer, free your heart, and direct your hearing. I shall inform you, if Allah wills. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, placed the Black Stone — which is a jewel that was brought out from Paradise to Adam (peace be upon him) — in that corner due to the reason of the covenant. And that is because when He took from the offspring of Adam, from their backs, their progeny, at the time when Allah took the covenant upon them in that place, and in that place He manifested Himself to them. And from that place the bird shall descend upon al-Qa'im (peace be upon him). The first to pledge allegiance to him shall be that bird, which is, by Allah, Jibra'il (peace be upon him). And al-Qa'im shall lean his back against that station. It is the proof and the evidence upon al-Qa'im, and it is a witness for whoever was loyal to it in that place, and the witness against whoever fulfilled the covenant and pledge to it which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took upon the servants. As for the kissing and the istilam (touching), it is due to the reason of the covenant — a renewal of that covenant and primordial pledge, and a renewal of the pledge of allegiance — so that they fulfill to it the covenant which Allah took from them in the primordial pledge, and so that they come to it every year and fulfill to it that covenant and trust which were taken from them. Do you not see that you say: 'My trust I have fulfilled, and my pledge I have renewed' — so that it may witness for you regarding fulfillment? By Allah, none fulfills that except our Shi'a, and none has preserved that covenant and primordial pledge except our Shi'a. And indeed t

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding the one in Ihram who dies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is washed, and enshrouded, and his face is covered, and he is not embalmed, and no perfume touches him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram who dies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is washed and shrouded in all his garments; he is treated just as the one not in Ihram is treated, except that perfume is not applied to him.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali died at Al-Abwa while he was in Ihram, and with him were Al-Hasan, Al-Husayn, and Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, and Abd Allah and Ubayd Allah, the two sons of al-Abbas. So they shrouded him, covered his face and head, and did not embalm him. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is how it is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the woman in Ihram who dies while she is in her menstruation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Perfume should not touch her, even if there were women with her who were not in Ihram.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abdullah ibn Farqad, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he was prevented at Al-Hudaybiyya, shortened (his hair/nails) and freed from Ihram, and offered a sacrifice. Then he departed from it, and shaving (of the head) was not obligatory upon him until he fulfilled the ritual. So, as for the confined one, only shortening is upon him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram who breaks his leg: 'What would be his state, and what is upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is free from Ihram, from everything.' I said: '(In terms of) women, clothes, and perfume?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, from the entirety of whatever is prohibited upon the one in Ihram.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Has it not reached you the words of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): "Free me where you restricted me, by Your decree which You ordained upon me"?' I said: 'May Allah keep you well! What are you saying regarding Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He must perform Hajj the next year.' I said: 'Inform me about the confined one (al-mahsur) and the prevented one (al-masdud). Are they equal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'So inform me about the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when the Polytheists prevented him. Did he fulfill his Umra?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he performed Umra after that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The confined one is not the prevented one. The confined one is the sick person, and the prevented one is the one whom the polytheists prevent, just as they returned the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his companions, not due to illness. And for the prevented one, women are permissible, but for the confined one, women are not permissible. He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who was confined (by illness) and sent the sacrificial animal (hady). He (peace be upon him) said: He sets a time with his companions. If it is for Hajj, the time for the offering is the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr). So when it is the Day of Sacrifice, let him shorten (hair) from his head, and shaving is not obligatory upon him until he fulfills the rituals. And if it is for Umrah, let him observe the time when his companions enter Mecca, and the hour he appointed for them. So when that hour arrives, he shortens (hair) and frees from Ihram. And if he fell sick on the way after entering Ihram, and intended to return, he returns to his family and sacrifices a camel (or animal), or he stays in his place until he is cured. If it was during Umrah, and when he is cured, Umrah becomes obligatory upon him. And if Hajj was outstanding upon him, he returns or stays; if Hajj is missed, then Hajj is upon him from the next year. Indeed, al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) went out for Umrah, and fell sick on the way. The news reached Ali (peace be upon him), while he was in Medina, so he went out seeking him, and caught up with him at al-Suqya, where he was sick. He said: 'O my son, what is your complaint?' He said: 'I complain of my head.' So Ali (peace be upon him) called for a camel, sacrificed it, shaved his head, and returned him to Medina. So when he was cured from his ailment, he performed Umrah. I said: 'Do you see that when he was cured from his ailment, before he went out for Umrah, were women permissible for him?' He said: 'Women are not permissible for him until he circumambulates the House (Kaaba), and (performs Sa'i between) al-Safa and al-Marwa.' I said: 'So what was the matter with the Mes

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man is confined (by illness), he should send forward his sacrificial animal. So when he recovers and finds lightness in himself, let him proceed if he thinks he can catch up with the people. So if he arrives in Makkah before slaughtering the sacrificial animal, let him remain in his Ihram until he completes all the rituals, and let him slaughter his animal, and there is nothing upon him. And if he arrives in Makkah and his animal has already been slaughtered, then upon him is the Hajj next year or the Umrah. I said, 'And if he dies while in Ihram before he reaches Makkah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj should be performed on his behalf if it was the Hajj of Islam, and Umrah should be performed on his behalf; it is merely a debt upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the one confined (by illness) who did not bring the sacrificial animal, he said: 'He should perform the rituals and return. So if he cannot find the price of a sacrificial animal, he should fast.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man is confined (by illness) and he sends his sacrificial animal (hady), and his head hurts before he sacrifices his animal, then he should slaughter a sheep in the place in which he is confined, or he should fast, or give charity. And the fasting is for three days, and the charity is for six poor people, half a Sa' for each poor person.

Sahl, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Rafa'at, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man who stipulates (for Umrah) while intending the Tamattu' (pilgrimage type), but he is confined (by illness or obstacle); would it suffice him if he does not perform Hajj the next year? He said: He should perform Hajj the next year; and the pilgrim is like that when he is confined. I said: A man who brings the sacrificial animal, then he is confined. He said: He should send his sacrificial animal. I said: Should he perform Tamattu' the next year? So he said: No, but he should enter into what he had exited from.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man whom a ruler seized unjustly on the Day of 'Arafah before he could perform Tawaf al-Wada' (or complete his rites), so he sent him to Mecca and detained him. When it was the Day of Sacrifice, he freed his way. I said: 'What should he do?' He said: 'He should join the pilgrims and stand at Jum'ah, then depart to Mina, where he should throw the pebbles, slaughter the sacrifice, and shave his head, and there is nothing upon him.' I said: 'And if he is freed on the Day of al-Nahr (Day of Sacrifice), what should he do?' He said: 'This one is prevented from Hajj. If he had entered Mecca as Mutamatti' (performing Umrah with Hajj), let him circumambulate the House seven times, then perform Sa'i seven times, shave his head, and slaughter a sheep. If he was performing Qiran or Ifrad exclusively for Hajj, there is no slaughter upon him, and there is nothing upon him.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The prevented one slaughters where he was prevented, and his owner returns and goes to the women, and the confined one sends his sacrificial animal and appoints them a day, so when the sacrificial animal arrives, this one frees himself from Ihram in his place. I said to him, 'What do you think if they return his dirhams and do not slaughter on his behalf, and he has already freed himself and gone to the women?' He said, 'Let him repeat, and there is nothing upon him, and let him refrain from the women now when he sends (the animal).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram neither marries (himself) nor is married off, nor proposes marriage, nor witnesses a marriage; and if he marries, his marriage is invalid.

Ahmad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a man from the Ansar married while he was in Ihram, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) invalidated his marriage.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Isma'il ibn Al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the one in Ihram, when he marries while being in Ihram, separation is effected between the two of them, then they do not remarry each other ever.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: The one in Ihram cannot get married. So if he were to do so, then his marriage would be invalid.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the man who is not in Ihram to marry the one in Ihram, while he knows that it is not permissible for him. I said to him, 'What if he does so and the one in Ihram has intercourse with her?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If they were both knowing, then upon each one of them is a sacrificial animal (Badanah). And upon the woman, if she was in Ihram, is a sacrificial animal, and if she was not in Ihram, there is nothing upon her, except if she had known that the one who married her was in Ihram. So if she knew, then married him, then upon her is a sacrificial animal.'
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram, can he divorce? He said: Yes.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the one in Ihram, can he buy the slave girl and sell? He said: Yes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man in Ihram who had intercourse with his wife while she was also in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Were they both ignorant or both knowing?' I said, 'Answer me regarding both cases together.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they were both ignorant, they seek forgiveness of their Lord and proceed with their Hajj, and there is nothing extra upon them. But if they were both knowing, separation is effected between them from the place where they committed the act, and upon them both is a sacrificial animal (each), and upon them is the performance of Hajj the following year. So when they reach the place where they committed the act, separation is effected between them until they complete their rituals, and they return to the place where they attained what they attained.' I said, 'So which of the two Hajjs is for them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first, in which they committed what they committed, and the other is upon them as a punishment.'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, raised it to one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: The meaning of 'separation between the two' is that they are not alone, and that there is a third person with them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the one in Ihram who has intercourse with his wife: He (peace be upon him) said: If he has fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel, and Hajj the following year; and if he has not fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel, and there is not upon him Hajj the following year. He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife while he was in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him; and if he was not ignorant, then upon him is the driving of a camel, and upon him is Hajj the following year. So when he reaches the place where he had intercourse with her, their two caravans are separated, so they do not gather in one tent unless there is someone else with them, until the sacrificial animal reaches its place.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about one in Ihram who had intercourse with his wife, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He has come to a grievous matter.' I said, 'Issue a verdict to me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Did he coerce her or did he not coerce her?' I said, 'Issue a verdict regarding both together.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had coerced her, so upon him would be two sacrificial animals (badanatan); and if he did not happen to have coerced her, so upon him would be a sacrificial animal, and upon her would be a sacrificial animal, and they would both be separate from the place in which they did what they did, until they both end up to Makkah, and upon them both would be the Hajj of the next year, it being inevitable from it.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So when they both end up to Makkah, so she would still be his wife just as she used to be?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. She would be his wife just as she used to be. So when they both end up to the place which from the two of them was what was, separated would be effected between them until they were free from their Ihram. So it would have been ended from them. My (peace be upon him) father (peace be upon him) was saying that'. And in another report, '(He (peace be upon him) said): 'So if he was not able upon a sacrificial animal, so he should feed sixty poor ones, for each poor one being one Mudd. So if he was not able, then he should Fast for eighteen days, and upon her as well would be similar to it if he did not happen to have coerced her'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about a man in a state of Ihram who had intercourse with his slave girl who was in a state of Ihram.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Is he financially solvent or insolvent?' I said, 'Answer me regarding both of them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Did he instruct her to enter Ihram, or did he not instruct her, or did she enter Ihram on her own accord?' I said, 'Answer me regarding both of these [scenarios].' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'If he was financially solvent and knew that it was not befitting for him, and he was the one who instructed her to enter Ihram, then upon him is a camel; and if he wishes, a cow, or if he wishes, a sheep. And if he did not instruct her to enter Ihram, then there is nothing upon him, whether he was financially solvent or insolvent. And if he instructed her and he was financially insolvent, then upon him is the blood of a sheep or fasting.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife while they were both in Ihram. He said: 'If the woman aided with desire along with the desire of the man, then upon them both is the sacrifice (hady), and they are separated from each other until they complete the rituals and until they return to the place where they had intercourse. And if the woman did not aid with desire and her companion compelled her, then there is nothing upon her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a person in Ihram who looked at his wife and discharged semen or seminal fluid while he was in Ihram. He said: There is nothing upon him, but let him perform Ghusl and seek forgiveness from his Lord. And if he carried her without desire, so he discharged semen or seminal fluid, then there is nothing upon him. And if he carried her or touched her with desire, so he discharged semen or seminal fluid, then upon him is Dam (blood of a sacrificial animal). And he said regarding the one in Ihram who looks at his wife and descends upon her with desire until he discharges, said: Upon him is a Badana (a young female camel).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram who places his hand upon his wife without desire. He said: 'Yes, he corrects her veil upon her, and corrects her garment upon her, and her carriage.' I said: 'Does he touch her while she is in Ihram?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'The one in Ihram places his hand with desire?' He said: 'He spills the blood of a sheep.' I said: 'And if he kisses?' He said: 'This is more intense. He slaughters a camel.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who kissed his wife while he was in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a camel (or sacrificial animal), and even if he did not discharge semen, it is not for him to eat from it.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Riab, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar! The state of the one in Ihram is constricted. So whoever kisses his wife without desire while he is in Ihram, upon him is the blood of a sheep. And whoever kisses his wife with desire and discharges semen, upon him is a camel, and he seeks forgiveness of his Lord. And whoever touches his wife with his hand while in Ihram with desire, upon him is the blood of a sheep. And whoever looks at his wife with a lustful look and discharges semen, upon him is a camel. And whoever touches his wife or holds her close without desire, there is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram who plays with his wife until he discharges semen without sexual intercourse, or he does that during the month of Ramadan. What is upon them both? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon them both, the expiation is like what is upon the one who copulates.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz, from Sabbah al-Hadhdha', from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What do you say regarding a person in Ihram who masturbates and discharges semen?' He said, 'I consider upon him the same ruling as upon the one who has intercourse with his wife while he is in Ihram: a camel (as fidya), and performing Hajj the following year.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who looked at the leg of a woman and discharged semen. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was wealthy, then upon him is a camel; and if he was in between (wealth levels), then a cow; and if he was poor, then a sheep. Indeed, I did not make that upon him because of the water (semen), but because he looked at what was not permissible for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, regarding the one in Ihram who looked at other than his wife, and discharge descended: he said: Upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal), because he looked at that which is not permissible for him. And if he did not discharge, then let him fear Allah and not repeat, and there is nothing upon him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram kissing his mother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with this; this is a kiss of mercy. What is disliked is the kiss of lust.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who heard the speech of a woman from behind a wall, and he was in Ihraam, so he desired her until he discharged. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one in Ihram who listened to a man copulating with his wife, so he discharged (semen), he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one in Ihram, to whom a beautiful woman of good constitution is described, and he discharges (semen), he said: There is nothing upon him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his wife on the Day of Sacrifice before performing Tawaf (Ziyaarah). He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had intercourse with her with desire, then upon him is a camel; and if it was without that, then a cow.' I said, 'Or a sheep?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Or a sheep.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' who had intercourse with his wife and had not yet performed the Ziyarah (of the Imam's shrine). He said: 'He should sacrifice a camel, and I fear that his Hajj has been broken if he was knowing, and if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him.' And I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife before he performed the Tawaf al-Nisa' (Circumambulation of the Women). He said: 'Upon him is a fat camel, and if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him.' He said: 'And I asked him about a man who kissed his wife and he had performed the Tawaf al-Nisa' but she had not performed it. He said: 'Upon him is blood (dam) which he would spill from himself.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his wife when he had sacrificed, before he visited the House. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should spill blood.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the one in Ihram has intercourse with his wife before he comes to Al-Muzdalifa, then upon him is (performing) the Hajj next year.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had upon him the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa'), alone. So he circumambulated five circuits from it, then his belly was struck (with pain). So he feared that he might be caught by surprise (by the pain or death), so he went out to his house, so he relieved himself (from urine/stool), then he had intercourse with his slave girl. He (peace be upon him) said: He should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate the House (Kaaba) with two circuits, completing what had remained upon him from his circumambulation, and he should seek forgiveness of Allah, and he should not repeat (the full seven circuits). And if it was the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa'), so he had circumambulated three circuits from it, then went out and had intercourse, so he has spoiled his Hajj, and upon him is a Badatah (a camel), and he should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate a full week (seven circuits).

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who circumambulated the House seven times as the obligatory circumambulation, then performed Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa for four circuits, then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need, then he had intercourse with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: He should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate three circuits, and seek forgiveness of his Lord, and there is nothing upon him. I said: But if he had performed the obligatory circumambulation of the House, then circumambulated four circuits, then his belly ached, so he went out and fulfilled his need, then had intercourse with his wife? He said: His Hajj is spoiled, and upon him is a camel (as expiation), and he should perform Ghusl, then return and circumambulate seven circuits, then perform Sa'ee, and seek forgiveness of his Lord. I said: Why did you not make it upon him, when he had intercourse with his wife before he finished his Sa'ee, just as you made upon him a sacrificial offering when he had intercourse with his wife before he finished his circumambulation? He said: Indeed, the circumambulation is obligatory, and therein is prayer, and the Sa'ee is a Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I said: Is it not that Allah says, 'Surely As-Safa and Al-Marwa are among the rituals of Allah'? He said: Yes, but He has said regarding them, 'And whoever does good voluntarily, then surely Allah is Grateful, Knowing'. So, if the Sa'ee were obligatory, He would not have said, 'And whoever does good voluntarily'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who said to his wife or to his slave girl, after he had shaved (his head), but had not performed Tawaf and had not performed Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa: 'Cast off your garment,' and he looked at her private parts. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him, if there was nothing other than looking.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not make permissible for yourself any game while you are in the state of Ihram, nor (make it permissible) while you are not in Ihram within the Sanctuary (Haram). Do not point it out to one who is permitted to hunt, nor to one who is prohibited, so that they may hunt it. And do not indicate it to it, so that it may be made permissible due to you, for therein is a ransom (fidyah) for the one who deliberately targets it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram does not point out to the prey; so if he points it out and it is killed, then upon him is the ransom.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the one in Ihram who hunts prey out of ignorance. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is an expiation.' I said, 'What if it was an error?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is the error in your view?' I said, 'He throws at this palm tree and hits another palm tree.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, this is the error, and upon him is the expiation.' I said, 'What if he deliberately caught a bird, slaughtered it while he was in Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the expiation.' I said, 'Did you not say that error, ignorance, and deliberation are not equal? So for what reason does the deliberate one surpass the ignorant and the erring one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He sinned and played with his religion.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma' ibn Abdul-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the one in Ihram hunts a prey and hits two, then upon him are two expiations, their penalty.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the one in Ihram catches the prey inside the Haram (sanctuary) and he is in Ihram, then it is befitting for him that he buries it and no one eats it; and when he catches it in the Hal (unrestricted area), then the one not in Ihram eats it, and upon him is the ransom.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man ate from prey that was caught by one in Ihram, while he (the man) was not in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: So let the one who is not in Ihram eat from it, and there is nothing upon him. Indeed, the ransom (fidyah) is upon the one in Ihram.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the flesh of wild animals that is gifted to a man, and he is given as a gift, and he does not know if it was hunted and he did not instruct with it, can he eat it? He said: No. He said, And I asked him, Can the one in Ihram eat the cured meat of wild animals? He said: No.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Jamil, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The hunted prey from wild animals is in the possession of a man among his family, or from birds. Is it prohibited while he is in his house?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; it does not harm him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abū al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Mu‘āwiya ibn ‘Ammār, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: Whatever you trample, or your camel tramples upon, while you are in iḥrām, then upon you is its ransom. And he (peace be upon him) said: Know that there is no ransom upon you for anything you come to, while you are ignorant of it and you are in iḥrām during your Ḥajj, nor during your ‘Umra, except for the hunted prey; for upon you regarding it is the ransom, whether it was out of ignorance or deliberate.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the one in Ihram who catches the prey, makes it bleed, then releases it: 'Upon him is its penalty.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram who is in need, so he finds the dead animal (carcass) and the hunted prey, which of these two should he eat? He said: He should eat from the hunted prey what he loves to eat from his own wealth. I said: Yes (why is that?). He said: Rather, upon him is the ransom, so let him eat and let him pay the ransom.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Ibn Bukayr and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who was compelled by necessity to eat a carcass or hunted prey, while he is in the state of Ihram, he said: He should eat the hunted prey and pay its ransom.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, said: The one in Ihram pays the ransom of the prey from wherever he attains it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever upon whom a sacrifice (hady) is obligated while in his state of Ihram, for him is that he may slaughter it wherever he wishes, except for the ransoming of the hunted prey, for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'an offering to be brought to the Kabah'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one upon whom is obligated the ransom of a hunted prey that he caught while in Ihram, if he was a pilgrim of Hajj, he should sacrifice his offering which is obligated upon him at Mina; and if he was a pilgrim of Umrah, he should sacrifice at Mecca, facing the Kaaba.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding the one in Ihram when he attains a prey, so the ransom is obligated upon him, therefore it is upon him that he should sacrifice; if it was during Hajj, at Mina where the people sacrifice; so if it was during an Umrah, he should sacrifice at Makkah. And, if he so desires, he can leave it until he proceeds (to Makkah), so he buys it, for it would suffice from him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a person in Ihram who caught an ostrich or a wild donkey. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a Bant camel.' I said, 'If he cannot afford a Bant camel?' He said: 'So let him feed sixty poor people.' I said, 'If he cannot afford to give charity?' He said: 'So let him fast eighteen days, and the charity is one Mudd for each poor person.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about a person in Ihram who caught a cow. He said: 'Upon him is a cow.' I said, 'If he cannot afford a cow?' He said: 'So let him feed thirty poor people.' I said, 'If he cannot afford to give charity?' He said: 'So let him fast nine days.' I said, 'If he catches a gazelle?' He said: 'Upon him is a sheep.' I said, 'If he cannot afford it?' He said: 'So the feeding of ten poor people. If he cannot afford what he should give in charity, then upon him is the fasting of three days.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has upon him a camel as an obligation for ransom, he said: 'If he cannot find a camel, then seven sheep. And if he is not able, he should fast for eighteen days.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Or the equivalent of it in fasting.' He said: 'He should evaluate the price of the sacrifice as food, then he would fast for each Mudd one day. So when the equivalents exceed two months, there is nothing more upon him than that.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'If the one in Ihram kills an ostrich,' he said, 'Upon him is a badanah (a mature female camel) from the camels.' I said, 'He kills a wild donkey?' He said, 'Upon him is a badanah.' I said, 'So (what about) a cow?' He said, 'A cow.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding one in Ihram who killed an ostrich. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a Badaanah (a camel or cow). So if he cannot find it, then feeding sixty poor people.' And he said: 'If the value of the Badaanah is more than the feeding of sixty poor people, he does not exceed feeding sixty poor people; and if the value of the Badaanah is less than the feeding of sixty poor people, there is not upon him except the value of the Badaanah.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding one in Ihram who shot an antelope and hit it in its hand, causing it to limp from it. He (peace be upon him) said: If the antelope walked upon it and grazed, then upon him is a quarter of its value. And if it went upon its face, so he does not know what it did, then upon him is the redemption (fidyah), because he does not know, perhaps it has perished.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a fox. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is blood (diem). I said, 'And a rabbit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Similar to what is upon the fox.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a person in Ihram who caught a rabbit or a fox. He said: Regarding the rabbit is (a penalty of) a sheep.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Ahmad ibn Ali from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The jerboa, the hedgehog, and the lizard, when the one in Ihram kills them, upon him is a kid (young goat); and the young goat is better than it, but rather I have made this upon him so that he may be deterred from hunting something else.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the one in Ihram attains the hunted prey, and cannot find what he can use to expiate from the place where he attained the prey, the value of its penalty should be assessed in dirhams from the livestock; then the dirhams should be assessed as food for each poor person, being half a sa'; so if he is not able to provide the food, he should fast one day for each half sa'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who attained an ostrich egg while he was in Ihram. He said: 'He should send a male camel for each egg.' I said: 'What if the eggs spoil entirely, or remain good entirely?' He said: 'Whatever is produced from the sacrificial animal is the sacrifice reaching the Kaaba; and if it is not produced, there is nothing upon him.' So whoever cannot find a camel, upon him is a sheep for each egg. If he cannot find one, then charity upon ten poor people, for each poor person a Mudd. If he is not able, then fasting for three days.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who bought ostrich eggs for a man in Ihram, so the man in Ihram ate them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is a ransom upon the one who bought it for the one in Ihram, and upon the one in Ihram is (also) a ransom.' I said, 'And what is upon both of them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon the one not in Ihram is a penalty of the price of the eggs, for each egg being a Dirham; and upon the one in Ihram is the penalty, for each egg being a sheep.' A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubeyda – similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who passed by while he was in Ihram, so he seized an antelope, milked it, and drank its milk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal), and a penalty in the Haram.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a person in Ihram who broke the horn of an antelope. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The ransom is obligatory upon him.' I said, 'And if he broke its hand?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he broke its hand and it did not graze, then upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

Muhammad ibn Aqeel from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Yazeed Al-Rifa'i, raising it (to the Imam). That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about the standing at the Mountain (Jabal al-Rahmah), why it was not in the Sanctuary (Haram)? So he said: 'Because the Ka'bah is His House and the Haram is its door. So when they came to it as delegates, He stopped them at the door, supplicating.' It was said to him: 'So why has Al-Mashar Al-Haram become inside the Haram?' He said: 'Because when He permitted them to enter, He stopped them at the second Veil. So when their supplication at it was prolonged, He permitted them to offer their sacrifice. So when they fulfilled their minor rituals, they were purified by it from the sins which were a veil between them and Him. He permitted them the visitation upon purity.' It was said to him: 'So why was fasting prohibited during the Days of Tashreeq?' He said: 'Because the people are visitors of Allah, and they are in His hospitality, and it is not fitting for a Host that He should make His guests fast.' It was said to him: 'So what is the meaning of hanging onto the curtains of the Ka'bah?' He said: 'It is like a man who has a felony and a sin with another, so he hangs onto his garment, supplicating to him and humbling himself to him that he would overlook his sin.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Safwan, or a man, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Al-Muzdalifa is the place in the lands of Allah with the most insects. So when it is the night of Al-Tarwiyya, a Caller calls out from the Presence of Allah: 'O group of insects, depart from the delegation of Allah!' He said: 'So they go out into the mountains and fill them, where they are not seen. So when the pilgrims depart, they return.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram, when he catches a dove, then for it is a sheep; and if he kills its chicks, then for it is a lamb; and if he tramples the egg, then upon him is a Dirham.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the dove and what resembles it: when the one in Ihram kills it, (he must offer) a sheep; and if it was chicks, he must equate them from the lambs. And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who trod on an ostrich egg and broke it while he was in Ihram: Ali (peace be upon him) judged that he should send a male camel to match the number of the eggs among the camels; whatever gets pregnant and remains safe until it gives birth, the offspring is an offering that reaches the Ka'bah.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad altogether, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the one in Ihram kills a sand grouse, then upon him is a lamb that has been weaned from milk and has grazed on trees.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a person in Ihram who trod on an egg of a sand grouse and broke it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should send a stallion for the number of eggs from the sheep, just as he sends the stallion for the number of ostrich eggs from the camels.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), regarding the egg of the sandgrouse, is a young sheep; when the one in Ihram attains it, similar to what is regarding the egg of the ostrich, a young she-camel.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a chick while he was in Ihram, outside the Haram (Sanctuary). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a lamb, and there is no evaluation upon him because he is not inside the Haram.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from the one who narrated to him, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the price of what is in the turtle dove, the laughing dove, the quail, the sparrow, and the nightingale. So he (peace be upon him) said: Its price is [one price]. But if he catches it while he is in Ihram in the Haram, then [the penalty is] two prices, and there is no blood [sacrifice] upon him regarding it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the lark, the sparrow, and the wren, the one in Ihram kills them. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is a Mudd of food for each one of them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about two men who caught a prey while they were in Ihram. Is the penalty shared between them, or is there a penalty upon each one of them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but upon them both is that each one of them must compensate for the prey.' I said: 'Indeed, some of our companions asked me about that, and I did not know what is upon him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you encounter something like this and do not know, then you must exercise precaution (ihtiyat) until you ask about it and learn.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj — similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a group of people gather upon a hunt, and they are in Ihram during its hunting, or they eat from it, so upon each one of them is its price.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Yusuf al-Tatari, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A hunted prey eaten by a group of people in Ihram.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon them is a sheep, and there is not upon the one who slaughtered it, except for a sheep.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who bought a hunted prey. A female companion of theirs said to them, 'Make a share for me in it for one Dirham.' So they made it for her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon each person from them is a ransom.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al-Hannat, who said: We went out, six of us from our companions, to Makkah. So we ignited a great fire in one of the encampments, intending to place upon it pure meat, and we were in Ihram. So a bird passed by us flapping; it was either a dove or like it. So its wings got burnt, and it fell into the fire, so it died. So we were gloomy due to that. So I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Makkah, informed him, and asked him. So he said: 'Upon you is one ransom, the blood of a sheep. You all share in it, because that was from you not by deliberation. And if that had been deliberate from you, in order to catch the prey, so it fell, I would have obligated upon each one of you the blood of a sheep.' Abu Wallad said, 'And that was from us before we had entered the Haram.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding two people in Ihram who caught prey, he said: Upon each one of them is the ransom.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with the one in Ihram hunting fish, and eating its salted and fresh varieties, and provisioning himself with it. Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, a provision for you. He said: Its salted [fish] is that which you eat. And the distinction between the two is: every bird that is in the bushes, lays its eggs on land, and hatches on land, it is from the prey of the land; and whatever is from the prey of the land that is on land, lays its eggs in the sea, and hatches in the sea, it is from the prey of the sea.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: ‘Everything whose origin is in the sea and is found in both the land and the sea, it is not befitting for the one in Ihram to kill it. So if he kills it, then upon him is the penalty, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said.’

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram who killed a locust. He said: 'A handful of food; and if there were many, so upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding one in Ihram who killed a locust, he said: He should feed a date, and the date is better than a locust.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Know that whatever insects you trample, or which your camel tramples, upon you is its ransom.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) passed by a group of people eating locusts, so he said: 'Glory be to Allah, and you are in Ihram?' They said: 'It is from the game of the sea.' So he said to them: 'Throw it into the water then.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The one in Ihram steps aside from the locusts when they are on the road, so if he has no alternative, he kills them, and there is no penalty upon him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about locusts entering the provisions of people, so they tread on them without deliberately intending to kill them, or they pass by them on the road and step on them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you find a way to avoid them, avoid them; but if you kill them without deliberation, there is no problem.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from al-Tayyar from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: The one in Ihram cannot eat the birds of the water.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the one in Ihram who hunts birds. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the expiation for everything he attains.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a person in Ihram who catches prey, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the expiation.' I said, 'And if he catches another?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he catches another, there is no expiation upon him, and he is among those for whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: And whoever returns (to it), Allah will inflict retribution on him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If the one in Ihram kills a dove inside the Haram, then upon him is a sheep, and the price of the dove, a Dirham or like it, which he gives in charity or feeds the doves of Mecca with. If he killed it inside the Haram and he was not in Ihram, then upon him is its price.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who ate an egg of a dove of the Haram, while he was in Ihram. He said: Upon him, for each egg, is blood (of a sacrificial animal), and upon him is its price, a sixth or a quarter of a Dirham. (The word 'al-wahm' is from Salih). Then he said: The blood (of a sacrificial animal) is necessitated upon him for eating it while he was in Ihram; and the penalty (of its price) is necessitated upon him for taking an egg of a dove of the Haram.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yazeed ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) From a man in Ihram who passed by while he was inside the Haram; he seized the neck of a gazelle, milked it, and drank from its milk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is blood (damm), and its penalty for being inside the Haram is the price of the milk.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If you catch the game while you are in Ihram inside the Haram, the ransom is doubled upon you; and if you catch it while you are Halal (not in Ihram) inside the Haram, its price is single; and if you catch it while you are in Ihram in the Hil (unrestricted area), then upon you is only one ransom.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him), who said: The penalty is indeed doubled for what is less than the Bidadah (a specific type of camel), until it reaches the Bidadah. So when it reaches the Bidadah, it is not doubled, because it is the greatest that can be. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And whoever magnifies the rituals of Allah, then indeed it is from the piety of the hearts.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al-Hannat, from Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A person in Ihram deliberately kills a bird between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the ransom, and the penalty, and he will be reprimanded.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'But if he did it deliberately in the Ka'ba?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the ransom, and the penalty, and he will be lashed less than the Legal Penalty (Hadd), and he will be stood before the people so that others may be deterred.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah will certainly try you with some game which your hands and your lances can reach.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wild animals were gathered for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during the Umrah of Al-Hudaybiyya to the extent that their hands and their spears could reach them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Two just persons among you' [5:95]. He said: 'The just ones are the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him.' Then he said: 'This is from what the scribes erred with (during the compilation) of the Quran'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it Regarding the Words of Allah the Exalted: 'What your hands and your lances can reach.' He said: 'What the hands can reach are the eggs and the chicks, and what the spears can reach, so it is what the hands cannot get to it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Judges by it two just persons among you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The just ones are the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from what the scribes erred with.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who ate from the flesh of a hunted prey not knowing what it was, and he was in Ihraam. He said: 'Upon him is blood of a sheep'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who completed his Hajj, then turned back, and when he had exited the Haram, a prey faced him near the Haram, and the prey was heading towards the Haram. So he shot at it and killed it. What is upon him regarding that? He said: He ransoms it in the same manner.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I asked the man (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram drinking water from a bottle or a water container made from the skin of hunted prey. Is that allowed or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He can drink from its skin.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I was accompanying Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in the journey between Mecca and Medina. When he arrived at the Sanctuary (Haram), he dismounted, performed ritual bath (ghusl), and took his sandals in his hands, then entered the Sanctuary barefoot. So I did what he did. He said: 'O Aban! Whoever does what you saw me do, out of humility for Allah, Allah will erase one hundred thousand bad deeds from him, record for him one hundred thousand good deeds, build for him one hundred thousand levels (of reward), and fulfill for him one hundred thousand needs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ubayda, who said: I accompanied Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the journey between Mecca and Medina. So when he arrived at the Haram, he performed ghusl, took his sandals in his hands, and then walked in the Haram for a while. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you enter the Haram, take the Izkhir (fragrant grass) and chew it.' And he (peace be upon him) used to instruct Umm Farwa with that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter the Haram, take from the Izkhir (fragrant grass) and chew it. Al-Kulayni said, 'I asked one of our companions about this, so he said, 'It is recommended to do so to freshen the mouth with it for kissing the Stone'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dharih, who said: I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) in the Sanctuary (Haram) before entering it or after entering it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not harm you whichever of those you do; and if you bathe in Mecca, there is no problem, and if you bathe in your house when you settle in Mecca, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you enter Mecca while you are performing Tamattu', and you look at the houses of Mecca, then cut off the Talbiyya. And the boundary of the houses of Mecca which existed before today is 'Aqabat Al-Madaniyyin, and indeed the people have built anew in Mecca what did not exist before. Therefore, cut off the Talbiyya, and upon you is the Takbeer, the Tahleel, the Tahmeed, and the praise of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with whatever you are able.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer, from his father who said: Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: When you see the houses of Makkah, cut off the Talbiyya.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The performer of Tamattu', when he looks at the houses of Makkah, cuts off the Talbiyya.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the Mutamatti', when does he cut off the Talbiyya? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he looks at the chairs (tents/structures) of Makkah at the end of Thi Tuwwa.' I said, 'Houses of Makkah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'From where should I enter Makkah, as I have come from Al-Madina?' He said: 'Enter from the upper part of Makkah. And when you exit intending Al-Madina, then exit from the lower part of Makkah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) that whenever he arrived in Makkah, he would begin with his house before he circumambulated.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic is, says in His Book: 'And purify My House for those who circumambulate it and stand to Pray and bow down and prostrate themselves.' Thus, it is befitting for the servant that he does not enter Makkah except when he is clean, having washed his sweat and impurities, and purified himself.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you arrive at the Haram, if God wills, perform the ritual bath (ghusl) upon entering it. And if you perform it beforehand, then perform the bath from the Well of Maymoun, or from Fakh, or from your house in Mecca.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you arrive at the Well of Maymoun or the Well of Abdul Samad, perform ghusl, take off your sandals, walk barefoot, and maintain tranquility and dignity.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'If you perform ghusl in Makkah, then sleep before you perform Tawaf, so repeat your ghusl.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who performs a ritual bath for entering Makkah, then sleeps, and then performs ablution before entering. Would that suffice him, or should he repeat? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It would not suffice him, because he entered with only ablution.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man does not enter Makkah with tranquility except that he is forgiven. I said, 'What is the tranquility?' He said, 'Humbleness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter the Sacred Masjid, enter it barefoot, with tranquility, dignity, and reverence. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever enters it with reverence, Allah will forgive him, if Allah wills.' I said, 'What is the reverence?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Tranquility; do not enter it with arrogance.' So when you reach the door of the Masjid, stand and say: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and from Allah, and whatever Allah willed. And peace be upon the prophets of Allah and His messengers. And peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, and peace be upon Ibrahim. And praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' So when you enter the Masjid, raise your hands and face the House (Kaaba) and say: 'O Allah, I ask You in this standing of mine, at the beginning of my rituals, that You accept my repentance, overlook my errors, and remove my burden. Praise is to Allah who brought me to His Sacred House. O Allah, I testify that this is Your Sacred House, which You made a refuge for people, a secure abode, blessed, and a guidance for the worlds.' O Allah, I am Your servant, the city is Your city, and the House is Your House. I have come seeking Your mercy and intending to obey You, obedient to Your command, pleased with Your decree. I ask You with the asking of the desperate to You, the one fearful of Your punishment. O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy, and employ me in Your obedience and pleasure.

And Abu Baseer reported from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: You should say while you are at the door of the Masjid: 'In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and from Allah, and whatever Allah so Desires, and upon the Religion of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the best of the Names are for Allah, and the Praise is for Allah. And, the greetings be upon Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The greetings be upon Muhammad son of Abdullah. The greetings be upon you O Prophet, and the Mercy of Allah, and His Blessings.' The greetings be upon the Prophets of Allah, and His Rasools. The greetings be upon Ibrahim, Friend of the Beneficent. The greetings be upon the Mursil Prophets. The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. The greetings be upon us and upon the righteous servants. O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Your Blessings be upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and be Merciful to Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, just as You Send Favours, and Blessings, and were Merciful upon Ibrahim and the progeny of Ibrahim, You being the Praiseworthy, the Glorious. O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, Your servant, and Your Rasool, and upon Ibrahim, Your Friend, and upon Your Prophets and Your Rasools, and Greetings be upon them, and Peace be upon the Mursils. And the Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah! Open for me the doors of Your Mercy, and Enable me in Your obedience, and Your Pleasure, and Protect me with protection of the belief forever for as long as You keep me remaining (alive), Majestic being the Praise of Your Face. The Praise is for Allah Who Made me to be from His delegates, and His visitor, and Made me to be from the ones who build His Masjids, and Made me to be from the ones who whisper to Him. O Allah! I am Your servant, and Your visitor in Your House, and upon every Host there is a right for the one whom comes to him, and visits him, and You are the best of the Hosts, and the most Honourable visited One. So I ask You, O Allah, O Beneficent, by You being Allah Who, there is no god for Him. You are Alone, there being no associates for You, and by You being One, Alone, Last, not begetting and not being begotten, and there being no one as a match for Him. And that Muhammad is Your servant, and Your Rasool. Blessings be upon him

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Quraish demolished the Ka'bah, they found a stone in its foundations containing a writing which they could not read properly, until they called a man who read it, and it said: 'I am Allah, the Lord of Bakka. I sanctified it on the day I created the heavens and the earth, and I placed it between these two mountains, and I surrounded it with seven angels, encircling it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah sanctified His Haram (sanctuary), that its emptiness should not be trodden upon, or its trees should not be cut down, except for Al-Idhkhir, or its birds should not be hunted.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Mecca on the day he conquered it, he opened the door of the Ka'bah and ordered that the images in the Ka'bah be obliterated. Then he took hold of the two hinges of the door and said: 'There is no god but Allah, Alone, with no partner. He fulfilled His promise and helped His servant and defeated the confederates alone. What are you saying and what do you think?' They said: 'We think good and we say good, O noble brother and noble cousin's son, and you have gained power.' He said: 'So I say as my brother Yusuf said: No reproach upon you today; may Allah forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful. Indeed, Allah has made Mecca sacred from the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. its game is not driven away, its trees are not cut, its dry grass is not gathered, and its lost items are not picked up except by one who announces it.' Al-Abbas said: 'O Messenger of Allah, except for al-idhkhir, for it is for the grave and the houses.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Except for al-idhkhir.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: 'Indeed, Allah sanctified Mecca on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and it is sacred until the Hour arises. It was not permissible for anyone before me, nor will it be permissible for anyone after me, and it was not permissible for me except for a moment of a day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We used to say that it is necessary to begin with the Stone and end with it. But as for today, the people have become numerous.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I was circumambulating (the Kaaba) and Sufyan al-Thawri was near me, so he said, 'O Abu Abdillah! What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) do with the Stone when he reached it?' I said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would touch it (istalam) during every obligatory and optional circumambulation.' He said, 'So he stayed behind me a little. When I reached the Stone, I passed by it and walked, but I did not touch it. So he caught up with me and said, 'O Abu Abdillah! Did you not inform me that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to touch the Stone during every obligatory and optional circumambulation?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'But you passed by it and did not touch it.' I said, 'The people showed respect for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that they do not show for me, and whenever he reached the Stone, they would make a way for him until he touched it, and I dislike the congestion (of pushing people).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sayf al-Tammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I went to the Black Stone and found congestion at it, so I did not find anyone except one of our companions. I asked him, and he said, 'It is necessary to touch it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'If you find it empty, [touch it]; otherwise, greet it from afar.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj and did not touch the Stone, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from the Sunnah. So if he is not able, then Allah is closer to excusing (him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I cannot reach the Black Stone.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'When you perform the obligatory Tawaf, it will not harm you.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Stone when one is not able to touch it and there is much congestion, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the old man, the weak, and the sick, they are excused; and I do not like that you leave touching it unless you have no choice.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked about the Black Stone, and whether people fight over it when they are many. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is like that, then gesture towards it with your hand.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not upon the women to be loud with the Talbiyya, nor to touch the Stone, nor to enter the House, nor to perform Sa'y between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, meaning the Harwala (trotting).
