A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Musa, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Touch the Corner (of the Black Stone), for it is the Right Hand of Allah among His creatures. He shakes hands with His creatures by it, like the shaking of hands of a servant or a man. The one who touches it testifies to loyalty.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about touching the Stone from the side of the Door. He said: 'Is it not that you intend to touch the Corner?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'It will suffice for you whatever your hand can reach.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Perform Tawaf around the House (Kaaba) seven circuits, and say during the Tawaf: 'O Allah! I ask You by Your Name by which one walks upon the surface of the water just as one walks upon the hard ground. And I ask You by Your Name by which Your Throne shakes, and I ask You by Your Name by which the feet of Your Angels shake.' And I ask You by Your Name by which Musa (peace be upon him) called upon You from the side of Mount Tur, so You answered him and cast love upon him from Yourself. And I ask You by Your Name by which You forgave Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) whatever of his sin had preceded and whatever had followed, and You completed Your favor upon him, that You do with me such and such, whatever You please of the supplication. And every time you reach the Door of the Kaaba, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And say in what is between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone: 'Our Lord! Grant us good in the world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.' And say during the Tawaf: 'O Allah! I am needy to You, and I am fearful seeking refuge, so do not change my body nor replace my name.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan who said, 'Ayoub, brother of Adeym, narrated to me from the Sheikh, who said to me, my father (peace be upon him) said:' 'Whenever you face the water spout, say: O Allah! Emancipate my neck from the Fire, and expand upon me from Your permissible sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the wicked ones of the Jinn and the humans, and enter me into Paradise by Your mercy.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Abdul Salam ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Nuaym, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I entered the Obligatory Tawaaf but could not begin with anything from the supplications except for the sending of Blessings upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) (Salawat), and I performed the Sa'ee, so that was that (as well)'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No one from the beseechers would be Given anything superior that what you would be Given'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What should I say when I face the Stone?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Exclaim the Greatness (of Allah) and send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I heard him (peace be upon him) when he went to the Stone, saying: Allah is the Greatest, peace be upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Aasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) reached the Stone before reaching the water spout, he would raise his head, then say: 'O Allah, enter me into Paradise by Your Mercy,' and while looking at the water spout, he would say: 'And save me by Your Mercy from the Fire, and grant me well-being from illness, and expand for me from the permissible sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the wicked of the Jinn and humans, and the evil of the wicked of the Arabs and non-Arabs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When he reached the back of the Kaaba, when passing by the Stone, [he would say]: 'O Possessor of Favors and Grace and Benevolence and Generosity! Indeed my deed is weak, so multiply it for me and accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is recommended that you say between the Corner and the Stone: 'O Allah, grant us good in the world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'An appointed angel says: Ameen.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not touch (with his hand) except the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner. Then he would kiss them both and place his cheek upon them both. And I saw my father doing it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I was circumambulating the House, and there was a man saying, 'What is the matter that these two corners are touched and those two are not touched?' So I said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touched these two and did not bother with those two. Therefore, do not bother with those two when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not bother with them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi, raising it from Zayd al-Shahham, Abu Usamah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I was circumambulating with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Whenever he reached the Stone, he wiped it with his hand and kissed it; and whenever he reached the Yamani Corner, he embraced it. I said, 'May I be your ransom, you wipe the Stone with your hand and embrace the Yamani Corner?' He said, 'Rasool Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I do not come to the Yamani Corner except that I find Jibraeel (peace be upon him) having preceded me to it, embracing it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-A'ala ibn Al-Muqadd, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'An angel is assigned to the Yamani corner since Allah created the heavens and the earth; he has no constant task (hijjir) except saying Ameen to your supplications. So let a servant consider what he is supplicating for.' I said to him, 'What is the hijjir?' He said, 'It is a word from the speech of the Arabs, meaning there is no work for him [other than that].' And in another report, 'There is no work for him apart from that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Yamani Corner is a door from the doors of Paradise; Allah did not close it since He opened it. And in another report: 'It is our door to Paradise from which we enter.'

A number from our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Ibrahim ibn Sinan, from Abu Maryam who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) circumambulating, and it was such that he did not pass by the Yamani corner during his circumambulation except that he touched it, then he was saying: 'O Allah! Turn towards me (with Mercy) until I repent, and Protect me until I do not repeat'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Abu al-Faraj al-Sandy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I was circumambulating with him around the House (Kaaba), so he said: 'Which of these is greatest in sanctity?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you are more knowing of this than I.' He repeated it to me, so I said to him, 'Entering the House.' He said: 'The Yamani corner is upon a door from the doors of Paradise, opened for the Shiah of the Progeny of Muhammad, closed off for others. And there is no believer who supplicates with a supplication at it, except that his supplication ascends until it adheres to the Throne, with no veil between it and Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Surely, in this place, meaning when one passes the Yamani Corner, there is an Angel who has been granted the hearing of the people of the earth. So whoever sends blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when he reaches it, the Angel delivers it to him.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, or someone else, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: There was a man in Makkah, a client of the Banu Umayya, called Ibn Abi 'Awanah, who had obstinacy (towards the Ahl al-Bayt). And whenever Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or one of the elders of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) entered Makkah, he would abuse him. And indeed, he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was in the Tawaf, and he said, 'O Abu Abdillah! What do you say regarding touching the Stone?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touched it.' He said to him, 'I do not see you touching it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I dislike that I should hurt the weak ones or be hurt (due to congestion).' He said, 'So you have claimed that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touched it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' 'But it was so that whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was seen, they recognized his right for him, and as for me, they do not recognize my right for me.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): 'From where should I touch the Kaaba when I have finished my Tawaf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From its back.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) He was asked about touching the Kaaba, so he said: 'From its back.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are in the seventh circuit, go to Al-Muta'awwaz, which is where you stand at the back of the Kaaba, parallel to the Door, and say: O Allah! The House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and this is the place of the one seeking refuge with You from the Fire. O Allah! From You is the comfort and the relief.' Then touch the Yamani corner, then go to the Stone and finish with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that whenever he reached the Multazam, he said: to his mawali, 'Remove me from the crowd so that I may acknowledge my sins to my Lord in this place, for this is a place where a servant does not acknowledge his sins to his Lord and then seek forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished your Tawaf and reached the rear of the Kaaba, which is opposite Al-Mustajar, slightly before the Yamani Corner, then spread your hands towards the House, press your belly and cheek against the House, and say: 'O Allah, the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and this is the place of the one seeking refuge with You from the Fire.' Then acknowledge to your Lord for what you have done, for there is no believing servant who acknowledges to his Lord his sins in this place except that Allah will forgive him, if Allah wills. And you should say: 'O Allah, from You is the comfort, the relief, and the health. O Allah, my deeds are weak, so multiply them for me, and forgive me what You have taken notice of from me, which was concealed from Your creatures.' Then seek refuge with Allah from the Fire, and choose for yourself from the supplications, then touch the Yamani Corner, then go to the Black Stone.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever stays in Makkah for a year, then the Tawaaf (circumambulation) is superior for him than the Salat (prayer); and whoever stays for two years, a mixture of that and that applies; and whoever stays for three years, the Salat is superior for him than the Tawaaf.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba), for those other than the inhabitants of Makkah, is superior to the Salat (Prayer); and the Salat (Prayer) for the inhabitants of Makkah is superior.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Tawaf before the Hajj is superior to seventy Tawafs after the Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed one circuit or two circuits of Tawaaf, then went out with a man for a need, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was an optional Tawaaf, he builds upon it (completes the circuits), and if it was an obligatory Tawaaf, he does not build upon it (i.e., repeats it).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them). Regarding the man who excretes wind during the Obligatory Tawaaf, and he had circumambulated part of it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should go out and perform ablution. So if he had completed the half, he would build upon his Tawaaf; and if it was less than half, he would repeat the Tawaaf'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Imran al-Halbi, who said: 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)' about a man who performed Tawaf around the House (Kaaba) for three circuits of the obligatory (Tawaf). Then he found empty space from the House, so he entered it. How should he deal with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should complete his Tawaf, and he has opposed the Sunnah, therefore he must repeat his Tawaf.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man performs circuits around the House, then complains (of a need or illness), he should repeat the Tawaf, meaning the obligatory one.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf), then became ill with an ailment that prevented him from completing the Tawaf. He (peace be upon him) said: If he had performed four circuits, he should instruct someone to perform three circuits on his behalf; thus his Tawaf is complete. And if he had performed three circuits and was unable to perform the Tawaf, then this is from what Allah has overcome him with, so there is no harm if he delays the Tawaf for one day and two days. So if the illness leaves him, he returns and performs seven (circuits). And if his illness prolongs, he should instruct someone to perform seven (circuits) on his behalf, and he himself prays two cycles, and someone performs Sa'i on his behalf, and he has exited his Ihram. And similarly he does regarding the Sa'i and regarding the pelting of the Jamarat.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Azza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was in the fifth circuit of the Tawaf. He said to me, 'Go, until we bid farewell to a man over there.' I said to him, 'But I am in the fifth circuit, so I should complete my seven circuits.' He said, 'Cut it, and remember it from where you cut it, until you return to the place from which you cut it, and build upon it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Sukayn ibn Ammar, from a man from our companions who was teknonymed Abu Ahmad, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) during the Tawaf, his hand in my hand, when a man presented himself to me having a need for me. So I gestured to him with my hand and said to him, 'Stay as you are until I finish my Tawaf.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me, 'What is this?' I said, 'May Allah keep you well, a man came to me regarding a need.' He said to me, 'Is he a Muslim?' I said, 'Yes.' So he said to me, 'Go with him regarding his need.' I said to him, 'May Allah keep you well, should I cut the Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And even if I was in the Obligatory one?' He said, 'Yes, and even if you were in the Obligatory one.' He said, 'And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever walks with his Muslim brother regarding his need, Allah will write for him a thousand thousand good deeds, erase from him a thousand thousand sins, and raise for him a thousand thousand levels.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure.' He said: When the servant commits a felony in other than the Haram, then he flees into the Haram, there is no leeway for anyone to seize him inside the Haram. But he is prevented from the market, and he is neither sold to nor fed, nor given drink, nor spoken to. For when that is done with him, he would desire to come out, and he would be seized. And when he commits a crime inside the Haram with a felony, the Legal Punishment (Hadd) is established upon him inside the Haram, because he did not leave for the Haram its Sanctity.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure.' He said: If a thief steals in other than Makkah, or commits a felony upon himself, and flees to Makkah, he is not seized for as long as he remains in the Sanctuary (Al-Haram), until he exits from it. But he is prevented from the market, and he is neither bought from nor sat with, until he exits from it, at which point he is seized. And if he commits that same crime inside the Sanctuary, he is seized inside it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who was in the course of an Obligatory Tawaaf (circumambulation), so the time for an Obligatory Salat (Prayer) caught him, he said: He should cut his Tawaaf and offer the Obligatory Prayer, then he should return and complete what remains of his Tawaaf.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was in the Obligatory Tawaaf, so the Prayer was established. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray the Obligatory [Prayer] with them. So when he is free, he can build [complete his prayer] from where he had cut it [stopped].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'If a man tires during the Tawaf, is it permissible for him to rest?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, he may rest, then stand and continue building upon his Tawaf, whether in an obligatory one or another; and he may do that in his Sa'i and in all of his rituals.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the man who rests during his Tawaf. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. I used to have an enclosure placed for me, so I would sit upon it.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf) but did not know whether he had performed six or seven circuits. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him repeat his Tawaf.' I said: 'So he lost it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see anything to be upon him, and the repetition is more beloved to me and superior.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who did not know whether he had circumambulated six or seven, he said: He should do it again.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one who performed Tawaf of the House as an obligatory Tawaf, but did not know whether he had performed six circuits or seven. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should face [the Kaaba] again.' I said: 'So he lost that one.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who doubted during the Obligatory Tawaaf. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat [the Tawaaf] every time he doubts.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What about a doubt during the optional Tawaaf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should build upon the lesser [number of circuits].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharjah, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who circumambulated the House with eight circuits, the obligatory one. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat it until he is certain (that it is correct).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said, 'A man performed the Obligatory Tawaf of the House, but he did not know whether he performed six, or seven, or eight circuits.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat his Tawaf until he is certain.' I said, 'Suppose he performed eight times as an optional Tawaf, and he forgot.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him complete two Tawafs (to make it fourteen), then pray four cycles. But as for the Obligatory, let him repeat it until he completes seven circuits.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who performed Tawaf but became confused, saying: 'Did I do four circuits or did I do three circuits?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Which of the two Tawafs was it, an optional Tawaf or an obligatory Tawaf?' He said: 'If it was an obligatory Tawaf, let him throw what is in his hand and start anew; and if it was an optional Tawaf, and he is certain of three and in doubt regarding the fourth that he had circled, let him build upon the three, for it is permissible for him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performed Tawaf around the House (Kaaba), then he went out to Al-Safa, so he performed Tawaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa. While he was performing Tawaf, he remembered that he had left part of his Tawaf around the House. He (peace be upon him) said: He should return to the House and complete his Tawaf, then he should return to Al-Safa and Al-Marwa and complete what remains.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, who said: Sulayman ibn Khalid asked him (peace be upon him) and I was with him, about a man who circumambulated the House six circuits. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And how does he circumambulate six circuits?' He said: 'He faced the Stone and said, "Allah is the Greatest," and he committed to one (circuit). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He should circumambulate one circuit.' He said: 'Supposing he loses it until he goes back to his family?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should instruct someone to circumambulate on his behalf.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot, so he circumambulated eight circuits. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he remembers before he reaches the corner, let him cut it'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is disliked for a man to combine between the two sevens and the two circumambulations in the obligatory [prayer], but as for the optional [prayer], there is no problem.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Muhammad ibn Walid from Umar ibn Yazid who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say, 'The joining (of circuits) is disliked only in the obligatory [prayer]; as for the optional [prayer], by Allah, there is no harm in it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performed Tawaf by the Kaaba, then went out and performed Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. While he was performing Tawaf, he remembered that he had left out one circuit of his Tawaf by the House. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return to the House and complete his Tawaf, then return to As-Safa and Al-Marwah and complete what remains.' I said: 'What if he started with As-Safa and Al-Marwah before starting with the House?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should go to the House, perform Tawaf by it, then resume his Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.' I said: 'So what is the difference between these two?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because this one had entered into something of the Tawaf, and this one had not entered into anything of it.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Tawaf between al-Safa and al-Marwa before he performed Tawaf by the House, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform Tawaf by the House, then return to al-Safa and al-Marwa and perform Tawaf between them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who arrives as a pilgrim and the heat becomes intense upon him, so he performs Tawaf by the Kaaba and delays the Sa'i until it cools. He said: 'There is no problem with it, and sometimes I do it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Rafa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tawaf by the House, so the time for Asr prayer enters. Should he perform Sa'i before he prays, or should he pray before he performs Sa'i? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but he should pray, then perform Sa'i.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: I witnessed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was being carried around the Kaaba in a litter, and he was severely ill. So whenever he reached the Yemeni Corner, he would order them, and they would place him on the ground. Then he would extend his hand from the opening of the litter until he dragged it on the ground, then he would say: 'Raise me.' So when he did that repeatedly in each circuit, I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! Indeed, this is difficult for you.' So he said: 'I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'That they may witness benefits for them'.' So I said: 'Benefits of the world or benefits of the Hereafter?' So he said: 'All.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one with stomach trouble, and the broken (of body parts), Tawaaf would be performed on their behalf, and the rocks would be pelted on their behalf.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the patient who is overcome [by illness], can Tawaf be performed for him on behalf of the Kaaba? He said: No, but he should be carried [to perform] Tawaf.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The children are carried around (for Tawaf) and stones are thrown on their behalf. He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the woman is sick and does not have full use of her intellect, she is carried around (for Tawaf) or Tawaf is performed on her behalf.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Ismail ibn Abdul Khaliq, who said: I was beside Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and with him were his son Abdullah and the son who followed him. A man said to him, 'May Allah keep you well! Does a man perform Tawaf on behalf of another man who is residing in Mecca, with no illness preventing him?' He said, 'No. Had that been permissible, I would have ordered my so-and-so son to perform Tawaf on my behalf,' mentioning the younger one, and they were both listening.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abū al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Ibn Abī Umayr, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, and Ibn Abī Umayr, from Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished your circumambulation (ṭawāf), go to the Standing Place of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) and pray two cycles (rakʿatayn), and make it in front of you, and recite in the first of them the Surah of al-Tawḥīd: 'Qul huwa Allāhu ʾAḥad', and in the second: 'Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn'. Then testify (tashahhud) and praise Allah, and extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask Him that He should accept from you. And these two cycles are the obligatory ones. It is not disliked for you to pray them at any time you wish, at the rising of the sun and at its setting. And do not delay them for a while after you have circumambulated and finished, so pray them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Umays, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) praying the two cycles of the obligatory Tawaf near the Maqam, close to the shade of the Masjid.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf) and finished it when the sun set. He (peace be upon him) said: The two cycles (Rak'atayn) became obligatory upon him at that time, so let him pray them before the Maghrib prayer.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Should I pray the two cycles of the obligatory Tawaaf behind the Standing Place (Maqam Ibrahim) where it is at the present time, or where it was in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Where it is at the present time.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I did not see the people taking from al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon him) except for the prayer after 'Asr and after the morning (Fajr) during the obligatory Tashriq) in the Tawaf of the Fard (obligatory pilgrimage).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, who said: One of the two Imams (peace be upon them) said: 'The man should pray the two cycles of the Tawaf, the obligatory Tawaf and the optional one, with [Surah] Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad and [Surah] Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs the Obligatory Tawaf after Asr prayer, should he pray the two cycles when he finishes from his Tawaf? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' Have not the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) reached you: 'O children of Abd al-Muttalib! Do not prevent the people from the Prayer after Asr, lest you prevent them from the Tawaf.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: It is not befitting that you pray the two cycles of the obligatory Tawaf except near the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). As for the optional (prayers), then (pray) wherever you wish from the Masjid.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I circumambulated four circuits and became tired, so can I pray its two cycles while seated?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'So how does a man pray the night prayer when he is ill and finds slackness, while seated, and this one cannot pray?' He said, 'Is it correct for you to perform Tawaf while you are seated?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So pray while standing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to pray the two cycles at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) during the circumambulation of Hajj and Umrah. He said: If he was in the city, he should pray two cycles at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), he should pray two cycles. For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And take for yourselves a place of Prayer by the standing-place of Ibrahim.' And if he had already travelled, then I would not order him to return.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man forgot the two cycles behind the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and did not remember until he traveled from Mecca. He (peace be upon him) said: So let him pray them where he remembered, and when he remembered them while he is in the city, he should not leave until he fulfills them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed the Obligatory Tawaaf and did not pray the two cycles until he performed Tawaaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. Then he performed the Tawaaf of the Women (Tawaaf al-Nisa) and did not pray the two cycles until he remembered it at Al-Abtah, so he prayed four cycles. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return and pray four cycles at the Standing Place (of Ibrahim).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, who said: I forgot the two cycles of the prayer of Tawaf behind the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) until I reached Mina, so I returned to Mecca and prayed them. We mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Why did you not pray them where you remembered?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who performed the obligatory Tawaf and forgot the two Rak'ahs until he had performed Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, he said: 'He should mark that place, then he should return and pray the two Rak'ahs, then he should return to his place.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: He was asked about a man who performed the obligatory Tawaf, but did not pray the two Rak'ahs; then he performed the Tawaf between al-Safa and al-Marwa; and after that he performed the Tawaf of the Women (Tawaf al-Nisa'), and did not pray for that Tawaf either, until he remembered at al-Abtah. He said: 'He should return to the Maqam Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and pray.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who entered Mecca after the Asr prayer, so he performed Tawaf by the House, and we had taught him how to pray, but he forgot, so he sat until the sun set. Then he saw the people performing Tawaf, so he stood up and performed another Tawaf before praying the two cycles for the obligatory Tawaf. He said: 'Ignorant?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn Za'lan, from al-Husayn ibn Bashaar, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna and Hanaan, said: We performed Tawaf by the House, the Tawaf of the women, and we forgot the two Raka'at. So when we arrived at Mina, we remembered them, so we went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him, and he said: 'Pray them at Mina.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hilal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The first thing the Qaim manifests from justice is that his caller will announce: 'The performer of the optional circumambulation should yield to the performer of the obligatory circumambulation, [allowing access to] the Black Stone and the circumambulation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Tawaaf (circumambulation), 'Does the man suffice by the counting of his companion?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Ayoub, brother of Adeym, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is recitation while I am performing Tawaaf superior, or mentioning Allah, Blessed and High?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Recitation'. I said, 'Supposing he passes by a (Verse of the) Prostration and he is performing Tawaaf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should extend his head towards the Kaaba'.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musanna, from Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hanzali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not perform Tawaf around the House (Kaaba) while you are wearing a burthulah (a type of cloak or outer garment).

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu al-Faraj who said: Aban asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Was there a Tawaf of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by which he was recognized?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to perform Tawaf by night and by day, ten circuits: three at the beginning of the night, and three at the end of the night, and two when it was morning, and two after midday; and whatever was in between that was his rest.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abdul-A'la, who said: I saw Umm Farwa performing Tawaf around the Kaaba, wearing a cloak and disguised. She touched the Stone with her left hand. A man among those performing Tawaf said to her, 'O maid of Allah, you have deviated from the Sunnah.' She said, 'We are in no need of your knowledge.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know why Al-Ta'if has been named so?' I said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) supplicated to his Lord that He should grant his family from the fruits, He cut off for them a piece from the earth, so it came forward until it performed Tawaf by the House (Kaaba) seven (circuits). Then Allah settled it in its place. And indeed, Al-Ta'if was named so due to the Tawaf by the House.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ziyad al-Qandi, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! I am in the Sacred Mosque, watching the people perform Tawaf around the House while I am seated, and I become sorrowful because of that.' He said: 'O Ziyad, there is no harm on you, for the believer, when he leaves his house intending Hajj, does not cease to be in Tawaf and Sa’ee until he returns.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Leave the Tawaf while you are still desirous of it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Musa ibn Isa Al-Yaqoubi, from Muhammad ibn Maysar, from Abu Al-Jahm, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a woman who vowed to perform Tawaf on four (crawling), he said: 'She performs one circuit (Asbūʿ) for her hands and one circuit for her legs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan who said: I asked him (asws) about three who entered into the Tawaaf. So one of them said to his companion, 'Memorise the Tawaaf (count)'. So when they thought that they had finished, one said, 'With me there are six circuits'. He (asws) said: 'If all of them doubt, let them resume (start over); and if they do not doubt, and each one of them knows what is in his hand (count), let them build (upon their count)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the woman who performs Tawaf with the child and performs Sa'i with him, is that sufficient for her and for the child? He said: Yes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is recommended that you perform three hundred and sixty circuits (usbu'at), which is the number of the days of the year. So if you are not able, then three hundred and sixty shawt (half-circuits). So if you are not able, then whatever you are able to perform of the Tawaf.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Can we drink while we are in the Tawaaf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed Tawaf upon his she-camel, Al-Adhba', and he would touch the corners with his staff and kiss the staff.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Tawaf during the Ten (Days of Dhu al-Hijjah) is superior to seventy Tawafs during the Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a woman who vowed to perform Tawaf on four (crawling): She should perform one circuit (Usbu') for her hands and one circuit for her legs.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was visited in the mosque, and it was said to him, 'A predator among the birds is upon the Kaaba; nothing from the doves of the Sanctuary passes by it except that it strikes it.' So he said, 'Set up a trap for it and kill it, for it has become a heretic.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr from Muawiya said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever inclines therein to wrong unjustly.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Every injustice is heresy, and striking the servant without a fault is from that heresy.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever inclines therein to wrong unjustly, We will make him taste of a painful punishment.' He said: 'Every injustice that a man commits against himself in Mecca, from theft, or being unjust to anyone, or any of the injustices, then I consider it to be heresy (ilhad), and due to that, one should fear from residing in the Sanctuary (al-Haram).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a man in the unrestricted area (al-hill), then entered the Sanctuary (al-haram). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not killed, nor fed, nor given drink, nor sold to, nor sheltered, until he exits the Sanctuary, and then the Legal Punishment (hadd) is established upon him.' I said, 'So what do you say about a man who kills inside the Sanctuary, or steals?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Legal Punishment (hadd) is established upon him inside the Sanctuary, quietly, because he did not consider the Sanctuary to have sanctity.' And Allah the Exalted has said: 'So whoever acts aggressively against you, inflict injury on him according to the injury he has inflicted on you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for the one who is inside the Sanctuary.' Then he said: 'So there is no aggression except upon the oppressors.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you have finished the two cycles (of prayer), go to the Black Stone, kiss it, and touch it, or gesture towards it, for it is necessary to do so. And he (peace be upon him) said: If you are able to drink from the water of Zamzam before you go out to Al-Safa, then do so, and say when you drink: 'O Allah, make it beneficial knowledge, abundant sustenance, and healing from every illness and disease.' He (peace be upon him) said: And it has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said when he looked at Zamzam: 'Had it not been that I would burden my community, I would have taken from it a bucket or two buckets.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the man has finished his Tawaf and prayed two cycles, let him go to Zamzam and draw from it a bucket or two buckets, and let him drink from it and pour it upon his head, back, and belly, and say: 'O Allah, make it beneficial knowledge, extensive sustenance, and healing from every illness and disease.' Then he should return to the Black Stone.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I saw Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) on the night of the visitation performing the Tawaf of the women, and he prayed behind the Maqam. Then he entered Zamzam, drew water from it with his hand using the bucket that is next to the Stone, drank from it, and poured some upon his body. Then he looked into Zamzam twice. And one of our companions informed me that he saw him, a year after that, doing the same.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said, 'Jameel narrated to me saying, I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):' 'Is there a prescribed supplication that I should say upon As-Safa and Al-Marwa?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say when you stand upon As-Safa:' There is no god except Allah Alone, no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Able over all things. Three times.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayoub, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'How should the man recite upon As-Safa and Al-Marwa?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should say: There is no god except Allah, Alone, no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He revives and causes to die, and He is Able over every thing.' Three times.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdul-Hamid ibn Saeed, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the door of Al-Safa. I said, 'Our companions have differed regarding it; some say it is the one next to the watering place (Zamzam), and some say it is the one next to the Stone.' He said: 'It is the one next to the watering place. It was newly made by Dawood, and Dawood opened it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Ali ibn Al-Numan, raising it (to the Imam), said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when he ascended Al-Safa, would face the Kaaba, then raise his hands, then say: 'O Allah, forgive me every sin that I have committed at any time. So if I return (to sinning), then return to me with forgiveness, for You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.' O Allah, deal with me what You are worthy of, for if You deal with me what You are worthy of, You will show mercy to me; and if You punish me, then You are Self-Sufficient from my punishment, and I am in need of Your mercy. So, O He to Whose mercy I am in need, have mercy on me. O Allah, do not deal with me what I am worthy of, for if You deal with me what I am worthy of, You will punish me, and You will not be oppressing me. I have come to fear Your justice, and I do not fear Your injustice, so O He Who is Just and does not act unjustly, have mercy on me.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Walid, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who intends to increase his wealth, let him prolong the standing upon As-Safa and Al-Marwa.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abi al-Jaroud, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There is nothing (specifically) prescribed to be performed upon Al-Safa.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Asbaat, from a mawla (freedman/companion) of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from the people of Medina, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ascend Al-Marwa, so he attached himself upon the rock which was at the top part of the pathway, and faced the Kabah.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Jahm al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from one of his companions, who said: I was behind Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) upon al-Safa or upon al-Marwa, and he did not increase upon two words: 'O Allah! I ask You for good expectation of You in every state, and truthfulness of intention in reliance upon You.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the Sa'ee (brisk walking) between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa. He said: When you reach the house that is on your right at the beginning of the valley, so briskly walk (sa') until you reach the first alleyway on your right after you have crossed the valley towards Al-Marwa. So when you reach it, stop the brisk walking and walk normally. And when you come from Al-Marwa, begin from the alleyway which I described to you. So when you reach the door that is facing Al-Safa after you have crossed the valley, stop the brisk walking and walk normally. For indeed, the brisk walking (Sa') is upon the men, and the brisk walking is not upon the women.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: My father used to perform Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, covering the distance from the door of Ibn Abbad until he raised his feet from the ravine, not reaching the alleyway of the progeny of Abu Husayn.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no area more beloved to Allah than the Sa'ee, because therein every tyrant is humbled.' And it is reported that he was asked, 'Why was the Sa'ee made?' So he said: 'To humble the tyrants.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said: There is no ritual more beloved to Allah than the Sa'ee, and that is because therein every tyrant is humbled.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Taymuli, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Halabi, from his father, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa has been made to humble the tyrants.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Descend from Al-Safa walking to Al-Marwa, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity until you reach the marker, which is at the edge of the Sa'ee area. So walk briskly (filling your chest with breath) and say: 'In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, and may Allah send Blessings upon Muhammad and upon His Household. O Allah, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know, and You are the Mighty, the Benevolent' until you reach the other marker. So when you pass it, say: 'O Possessor of Favor and Grace and Generosity and Blessings and Bounty, forgive my sins, for there is no Forgiver of sins except You.' Then walk, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity until you reach Al-Marwa. So climb upon it until the House (Kabah) appears to you, and do upon it as you did upon Al-Safa, and circumambulate between them seven circuits, beginning with Al-Safa and ending with Al-Marwa.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a mawla (freedman/companion) of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from the people of Medina, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) begin the Sa'ee from the house of Al-Qazi Al-Makhzoumi. He said, 'And he continued as he was, up to the alleyway of the perfume sellers.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muawiya ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Sayrafi, from one of our companions who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa: is it an Obligation or a Sunnah? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is an Obligation.' I said: 'Is it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "there is no blame on him if he goes round them both"?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That was regarding the Umra of the adjudication (Umrat al-Qada).' Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stipulated upon them that they would raise (remove) the idols from Al-Safa and Al-Marwa. So a man pretended to be busy and neglected the Sa'ee until the days had passed, and the idols returned. So they (people) came to him (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! So-and-so did not perform Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, and the idols have returned.' Therefore, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed: "there is no blame on him if he goes round them both" i.e., and upon them were the idols.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who neglected the Sa'y deliberately. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the Hajj from the future year.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who began with Al-Marwa before Al-Safa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat. Do you not see that had he begun with his left before his right during the ablution, he would intend to repeat the ablution?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa for eight circuits, what is upon him? He said: 'If it was a mistake, one is dropped, and he counts with seven.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: We performed Hajj and we were first-timers, so we performed Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa for fourteen circuits. So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; seven are for you and seven are dropped.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali al-Sa'igh, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was present, about a man who began with Al-Marwa before Al-Safa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat. Do you not see that if he had begun with his left before his right, he would be required to begin with his right, then return to his left?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Whoever performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa for fifteen circuits, eight are dropped and he is counted with seven; and if he began with Al-Marwa, let him drop (it all) and let him begin with As-Safa.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Hal-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Sa'ee (walking) between As-Safa and Al-Marwa upon the animal. He said: 'Yes, and upon the carriage.'

Muawiya ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the man who performs Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa while riding. He said: 'There is no problem, and walking is superior.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tawaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, can he rest? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, if he so desires, he may sit upon Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, and between the two, so he can sit.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One does not sit between As-Safa and Al-Marwa except due to tiredness.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the women who perform Tawaf upon camels and beasts of burden; is it sufficient for them to stand beneath As-Safa and Al-Marwa? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, as long as they can see the House.'
And from him, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no Sa'ee required of the rider, but he should hasten a little.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When a man enters into the Sa'ee (circumambulation) between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and the time for prayer enters, should he slow down, or should he cut it off, pray, and return, or remain as he is in his state until he finishes?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there not a place of prostration (Masjid) upon both of these? No, but he should pray, then return.' I said: 'Should he sit upon both of these?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Or is he not like one who performs Sa'ee upon the animal?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'If a man performs Sa'ee between al-Safa and al-Marwa for three circuits or four, then he urinates, can he complete his Sa'ee without wudu?' He said, 'There is no problem, and if he completed his ritual with wudu, it would be more beloved to me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayyub and Hammad ibn Isa, all from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you have completed your Sa'y and you are in the state of Tamattu', then shorten your hair from its sides and your beard, and take (clip) from your moustache, and trim your nails, and leave some of them for your Hajj. And when you do that, you have become permitted from everything from which the one in Ihram is freed, and you have become prohibited from it. So perform Tawaf around the House voluntarily as much as you wish.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) shaving [the hair] from his Umrah [state], and taking [cutting] from the sides of all his hair upon the comb. Then he gestured to his moustache, so the barber took from it. Then he gestured towards the sides of his beard, so he took from it, then he arose.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Rafa'ah ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tawaf around the House and Sa'i, can he voluntarily perform Tawaf before he shortens (his hair/nails)? He (peace be upon him) said: I do not like it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one in Ihram who shortens (hair/nails) from some parts and does not shorten from others, he said: It suffices him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Aslam, who said: When Abu Ja'far, meaning the son of Al-Reza (peace be upon him), wanted to shorten his hair for the Umrah, the barber wanted to take from the sides of the head, so he said to him: 'Begin with the forelocks', so he began with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a performer of Tamattu' who clipped his nails and cut the hair of his head with scissors. He said: 'There is no problem, as not everyone can find scissors.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man performing Tamattu' who forgot to shorten (his hair and nails) until he entered the state of Ihram for Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should seek forgiveness from Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who entered into Umrah and forgot to shorten (his hair, nails, etc.) until he entered into Hajj. He said: He should seek forgiveness of Allah, and there is nothing upon him, and his Umrah is complete.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan al-Ruqi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Umrah with Hajj (Tamattu'), entered Mecca, performed Tawaf and Sa'i, wore his clothes, and exited Ihram, but forgot to shorten (his hair/nails) until he went out to Arafat. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. He builds upon the Umrah and its Tawaf, and the Tawaf of the Hajj follows it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who circumambulated the House, then [performed sa'i] between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and he had performed Tamattu', then he hastened and kissed his wife before he shortened [his hair] from his head. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is blood to spill; and if he copulated, then upon him is a camel or a cow.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' who had intercourse with his wife and had not shortened (his hair, nails, etc.), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should sacrifice a camel, and I fear that his Hajj has been broken if he was knowledgeable (of the ruling), but if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom. When I fulfilled my rituals for the Umrah, I went to my wife and I had not shortened (my hair/nails).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon you is a camel.' I said: 'When I intended that from her, and she had not shortened, she prevented me. But when I overcame her, she cut some of her hair with her teeth.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on her. She is more understanding than you. Upon you is a camel, and there is nothing upon her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj) who shaved his head in Makkah. He said: If he was ignorant, there is nothing upon him; and if he deliberately did that in the beginning of the months of Hajj, within thirty days from it, there is nothing upon him; and if he deliberately did it after the thirty days during which the hair is allowed to grow for the Hajj, then upon him is a dam (blood/sacrifice) that he must spill. And in another report, he said: So when it is the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), he passes the razor over his head.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is befitting for the performer of Tamattu' with the Umra to the Hajj, when he is free from Ihram, that he should not wear a shirt, and let him resemble the ones in Ihram.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one performing Tamattu' who comes, fulfills his Tamattu', then a need arises for him, so he goes out to Al-Madinah, or to Dhat 'Irq, or to one of the places. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return to Makkah with an Umrah if it is in a month other than the month in which he performed Tamattu', because for every month there is an Umrah, and he is pledged with the Hajj.' I said: 'And if he enters during the month in which he went out?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) was residing here, so he went out to meet some of them. So when he returned, he reached Dhat 'Irq, he entered into Ihram from Dhat 'Irq for the Hajj, and entered (Makkah) while he was in Ihram for the Hajj.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj, intending to go out to Al-Ta'if. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should begin with Hajj from Makkah, and I do not love for him that he should go out from it unless he is in Ihram, and he should not exceed Al-Ta'if, for it is near to Makkah.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who fulfilled his Tamattu', then a need presented itself to him, so he intended to go out to it. He (attend to) it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him perform Ghusl for Ihram, and let him begin with the Hajj, and let him go regarding his need; and if he is not able to return to Makkah, he should go to Arafat.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The performer of Tamattu' is detained; he does not leave Mecca until he goes out for Hajj, unless his slave absconds or his mount goes astray, so he goes out in Ihram, and he does not travel except to the extent that he does not miss Arafat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Murazim, and Shuayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from the man performing Tamattu': when the night of Arafah enters, he circumambulates and performs Sa'ee, then he frees himself (from Ihram), then he enters Ihram again and goes to Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Maymoun, who said: Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) arrived performing Tamattu' on the night of Arafah, so he circumambulated, and freed from Ihram, and went to one of his slave girls. Then he began with the Hajj and went out.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Tamattu', 'When does it occur?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He performs Tamattu' as long as he thinks he can catch up with the people at Mina.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb Al-Mithammi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no problem for the performer of Tamattu' if he does not enter into Ihram from the night of Tarwiyah, whenever it is easy for him, as long as he does not fear missing the two stations.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding the performer of Tamattu' who entered on the Day of Arafah, he said: 'His Tamattu' is complete until the Talbiyyah is cut off.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who intends to enter the state of Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: She should perform ghusl, and place cotton in her private area, and wear a garment other than her Ihram clothes, and face the Qiblah, and not enter the mosque, and recite the Talbiyah for Hajj without prayer.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, who said: I mentioned to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) the case of the istihada (inter-period bleeding) woman, so he mentioned Asma' bint Umays, and said: Indeed, Asma' gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr at al-Bayda', and in her giving birth was a blessing for the women, for those from them who give birth, or menstruate. So, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her, and she stuffed herself (with cotton) and girded herself with a belt, and entered into ihram.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The menstruating woman wears Ihram while she does not pray.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. When the time comes (for her purity), let her wear Ihram.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a woman who menstruates while she intends to enter the state of Ihram, so she becomes pure (from menstruation). He said: She should perform ghusl, place cotton (kursuf) in her private area, wear the Ihram clothes, and enter Ihram. When night falls, she removes them and wears her other clothes, until she is fully pure.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from al-Ala' ibn Sabih and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Ali ibn Ri'ab and Abd Allah ibn Salih, all of them reporting it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman performing Tamattu', when she arrives in Mecca and then menstruates, stays in the period between her arrival and the Day of Tarwiyah. If she becomes pure, she circumambulates the House and performs Sa'ee between al-Safa and al-Marwa; and if she does not become pure until the Day of Tarwiyah, she performs Ghusl and stuffs herself (with cotton), then performs Sa'ee between al-Safa and al-Marwa. Then she goes out to Mina. So when she fulfills the rituals and visits the House, she performs the Tawaf of her Umrah, then performs the Tawaf of the Hajj. Then she goes out and performs Sa'ee. So when she does that, she has been released from everything from which the Muhrim is released, except for the bed of her husband. So when she performs another seven circuits (Tawaf), the bed of her husband becomes permissible for her.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Durust al-Wasiti, from Ijlan Abu Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman performing Tamattu' who arrived in Mecca and saw blood. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, then she sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf by the House; and if she does not become pure, when it is the Day of Tarwiyah, she pours water upon herself and begins with the Hajj from her house, and goes out to Mina and fulfills all the rituals.' So when she arrives in Mecca, she performs two Tawafs by the House, then she performs Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. So when she does that, then everything is permissible for her except the bed of her husband.

Muhammad narrated from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibn Ribat, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Ajlan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman performing Tamattu' arrives [at Mecca], and she sees blood. What should she do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She performs Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf by the House. And if she does not become pure, when it is the Day of Tarwiyah, she pours water upon herself, enters into Ihram for Hajj, and goes out to Mina, and fulfills all the rituals. When she does that, then everything is permissible for her except the bed of her husband.' He (the narrator) said: 'I and Ubaydullah ibn Salih heard this Hadith in the Mosque. So Ubaydullah went to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he came out to me and said: I have asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the narration of Ajlan, so he narrated to me with approximately what we heard from Ajlan.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ubayd Allah ibn Salih, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A woman performing Tamattu' performs Tawaf, then menstruates?' He said: 'She performs Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and she fulfills her Tamattu'.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman performing Tamattu': if she enters the state of Ihram while pure, then menstruates before she completes her Tamattu', she performs Sa'ee but does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure. Then she completes her Tawaf, and she has completed her Umrah. And if she entered Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'ee and does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Durust, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When the woman performs Umrah, then she becomes ill before she performs Tawaf, she brings forward the Sa'i and performs the rituals. So when she is pure and has returned from Hajj, she fulfills the Tawaf of Umrah, and the Tawaf of Hajj, and the Tawaf of Women, then she is permissible from everything.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one of his companions, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman comes performing Tamattu', but she menstruates before she performs Tawaf by the House, and her purity comes to be on the Day of Arafaat.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If she knows that she is pure to perform Tawaf by the House, and she could be free from her Ihram, and she could catch up with the people, then let her do so'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman who performed Tawaf by the House, then she menstruated before she performed Sa'ee. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should perform Sa'ee'. He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who performed Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, so she menstruated between the two.
