He (peace be upon him) said: 'She would complete her Sa'ee'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman performing Tamattu': When she enters the state of Ihram while pure, then menstruates before she completes her Tamattu', she performs Sa'i and does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure. Then she completes her Tawaf, and her Tamattu' is complete. And if she entered Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'i and does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That Asma' bint Umays gave birth to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her, when she intended to enter the state of Ihram from Dhu al-Hulayfa, to stuff herself with cotton and rags and to begin with Hajj. So when they arrived in Mecca and had performed the rituals, and eighteen days had passed for her, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her to perform Tawaf by the House and to pray, and the blood had not ceased from her, so she did that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman experiencing post-childbirth bleeding would perform Tawaaf by the House (Kabah), and she would Pray, and she would not enter the Kabah.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a girl who had not yet menstruated, who went out with her husband and her family. She menstruated, but she was shy to inform her family and her husband until she completed the rituals, while remaining in that state. Then her husband had intercourse with her. Then she returned to Kufa and said to her family, 'Such and such happened.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon her is the driving of a camel (for sacrifice), and upon her is the Hajj next year, and there is nothing upon her husband.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad from a man who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When the menstruating woman performs Tawaf, then she intends to bid farewell to the House, so let her stand at the nearest door from the doors of the Masjid, and let her bid farewell to the House.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I sent a message to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Some of the women among us who are menstruating have fallen ill, so what should she do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should wait for the time between her and the Tarwiah (8th of Dhul-Hijjah). If she becomes pure, let her begin (the Hajj rites); otherwise, the Tarwiah should not enter upon her except while she is in Ihram.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Fuzayl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When the woman performs the Tawaf of the women, and has completed more than half, then she menstruates, she may depart if she wishes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). A man came to him at night and said, 'May Allah improve you. A woman with us has menstruated and has not performed the Tawaf of the women.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I have been asked about this matter today.' The man said, 'May Allah improve you, I am her husband, and I would like to hear that from you.' He (peace be upon him) fell silent as if he were conversing with himself, and he said, 'Her beauty will not remain upon her, and she is not able to stay behind from her companions. She can go, and her Hajj is complete.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When it is the Day of Tarwiyya, if God wills, then perform ghusl, wear your two garments (of ihram), and enter the Masjid barefoot, with tranquility and dignity upon you. Then pray two cycles of prayer near the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) or in the Hijr. Then sit until the sun declines, so pray the prescribed prayer, then say at the end of your prayer as you said when you wore ihram from Al-Shajara, and wear ihram for the Hajj. Then proceed, with tranquility and dignity upon you. So when you reach Al-Rafda, before Al-Radm, say 'Labbay'. So when you reach Al-Radm, and overlook Al-Abtah, raise your voice with the Talbiyah until you arrive at Mina.

And in a narration of Abu Baseer from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When you intend to enter the state of Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah, do as you did when you intended to enter Ihram: trim your moustache, clip your nails, shave your pubic hair if you have any, pluck your armpits, perform Ghusl, and wear your Ihram garments. Then go to the Sacred Masjid and pray six Raka'at before entering Ihram, supplicate to Allah and ask Him for assistance, and say: 'O Allah, I intend the Hajj, so make it easy for me and release me from where You have detained me by Your decree which You have ordained upon me.' And you should say: 'My hair, skin, flesh, and blood are prohibited for You, from women, perfume, and garments; I intend thereby Your Face and the Abode of the Hereafter. Release me from where You have detained me by Your decree which You have ordained upon me.' Then recite the Talbiyah from the Sacred Masjid just as you recited it when you entered Ihram, and say: 'Here I am, O Allah, for a Hajj that is complete and delivered to You.' And if you are able for your journey to Mina to coincide with the decline of the sun, do so; otherwise, whenever it is easy for you from the Day of Tarwiyah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked him about a man who came to the Sacred Mosque, and he had intended the Hajj, can he circumambulate the House? He said: Yes, as long as he has not entered into Ihram.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Ahmad Amr ibn Hurayth al-Sayrafi said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'From where should I begin with the Hajj?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you so desire, from your ride, and if you so desire, from the Ka'bah, and if you so desire, from the road'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'From which mosque shall I enter into Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyya?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'From whichever mosque you desire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Suleyman ibn Muhammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'When shall I exclaim the Talbiyya for the Hajj?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you go out to Mina.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the Shi'b Dubb is upon your right and Al-Uqba is upon your left, so exclaim the Talbiyya for the Hajj.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sayf al-Tammarr, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We used to perform Hajj on foot, but something from you reached us, so what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The people perform Hajj on foot and they ride.' I said, 'I am not asking you about that.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Then about what did you ask?' I said, 'Which of the two is more beloved to you that we should do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Riding is more beloved to me, for that is stronger for you in supplication and worship.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about whether walking is superior or riding. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man is affluent, and he walks in order to lessen his expenditure, then riding is superior for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rafa'ah and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about Hajj, whether walking is superior or riding? He said: Rather, riding, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed Hajj riding.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Rafa'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the walking of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — was it from Makkah or from Al-Madina? He said: 'From Makkah'. And I asked him, 'When I visit the House, should I ride or walk?' So he said: 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to visit riding'. And I asked him about riding, whether it is superior or the walking? So he said: 'The riding'. I said, 'The riding is superior than walking?' He said: 'Yes, because Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rode'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about when the walking of the walker should cease. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he pelts the Jamarat al-Aqaba and shaves his head, then his walking has ceased, so let him visit (the Kaaba) riding.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad from Ismail from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the one upon whom is the walking during the Hajj, when he pelts the Jamarat, he visits the House riding, and there is nothing upon him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' when he is an old aged man, or a woman who fears menstruation, who hastens the circumambulation of Hajj before going to Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. The one who is like this, he hastens.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about the man who enters into Ihram for Hajj from Mecca, then sees the House (Kaaba) as being vacant, so he performs circumambulation by it before he goes out upon anything (to Mina). He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said, 'The one performing Qiran or Tamattu' (literally: the one who is free/independent), when he has circumambulated the House and (performed sa'i between) Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, hastens the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa'). He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, the circumambulation of the women is (to be done) after going to Mina.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Mecca with women whom he had instructed, so they performed Tamattu' before the Day of Tarwiyah by one day, or two days, or three. So he feared menstruation for some of them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When they have completed their Tamattu' and have exited Ihram, let him look to the one whom he fears menstruation for, so he should instruct her to perform Ghusl and begin with the Hajj from her place. Then she should perform Tawaf around the House, and around As-Safa and Al-Marwa. So if something occurs with her, she completes the remainder of the rituals while being a Haidh (menstruating).' So I said, 'Is it not so that the Tawaf of the women remains?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'So she is held in pledge until she finishes it?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'So why leave her until she completes her rituals?' He said, 'One ritual remaining upon her is easier for her than if all the rituals remained upon her, out of fear of menstruation.' I said, 'Supposing the cameleer refuses to stay with her, and the fellow travelers?' He said, 'That is not for them. She should seek their support until they stay with her, until she is pure and completes her rituals.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Muawiya ibn Ammar, and Hammad, from al-Halby, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with hastening the circumambulation (Tawaf) for the elderly man and the woman who fears menstruation, before going out to Mina.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked, 'A man who was performing Tamattu' and declared the intention for Hajj.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not perform Tawaf by the House until he goes to Arafat. So if he performs Tawaf before he goes to Mina without a valid reason, then he will not be counted with that Tawaf.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ismail ibn Abdul Khaliq, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no problem if the old aged man, and the sick, and the woman, and the disabled were to hasten the Tawaaf of the Hajj before the going out to Mina'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Mufrid (one performing exclusive Hajj) who enters Makkah: should he bring forward his Tawaf or delay it? So he (peace be upon him) said: '(It is) the same'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the performer of exclusive Hajj (Mufrid) who brings forward his Tawaf, or delays it? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, it is the same, whether he hastens it or delays it.'

3. Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Mufrid al-Hajj (one performing exclusive Hajj): does he bring forward his Tawaf or delay it? He said, 'He brings it forward.' A man next to him said, 'But my Sheikh did not do that; when he arrived, he stayed in Fakh until the people returned to Mina, then he went with them.' I said to him, 'Who is your Sheikh?' He said, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).' I asked about the man, and he was the half-brother of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) from the mother's side.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who is an old, elderly man or sick, fearing the crowding and pressing of the people, who enters into Ihram for Hajj and departs to Mina before the Day of Tarwiyah. He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Does a healthy man depart seeking a place and rest in that place?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'Does he hasten by one day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By two days?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By three?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'More than that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is upon the Imam to pray the Dhuhr prayer in Mina, then he stays overnight there and remains until the sun rises, then he departs to Arafat.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Rafa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Do the people go out to Mina in the morning?' He said, 'Yes, until the setting of the sun.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you direct yourself to Mina, say: 'O Allah, to You I hope and to You I supplicate, so grant me the fulfillment of my desire and rectify my deed for me.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is from the Sunnah that the Imam does not depart from Mina to 'Arafah until the sun rises.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halbi, from Abdul Hameed al-Ta'i who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We are walkers, so what should we do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the owners of the rides, they used to pray the morning prayer in Mina, and as for you, go until you pray in the road.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you depart for Arafat, say while you are heading towards it: 'O Allah, to You I have turned, and upon You I have relied, and Your Face is what I intend. Therefore, I ask You to bless my journey, fulfill my needs, and make me among those whom You boast about to those who are superior to me.' Then proclaim the Talbiyya while you are going to Arafat. When you arrive at Arafat, strike your tent at Namira; and Namira is the bottom of Uraynah, before the standing place and before Arafat. When the sun declines on the Day of Arafat, perform ghusl and pray Dhuhr and Asr with one Adhan and two Iqamas. You hasten Asr and combine the two prayers to free yourself for supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the boundary of Arafat is from the bottom of Uraynah and Thawiyya and Namira to Dhi al-Majaz; and behind the mountain is the standing place.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The ritual bath on the Day of Arafah is when the sun declines, and you should combine the Dhuhr and Asr prayers with one Adhan and two Iqamas.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The boundary of Arafat is from the two Mazamin up to the furthest point of the Standing Station.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: The pilgrim cuts off the Talbiyya on the Day of Arafah at the decline of the sun.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ceased the Talbiyya when the sun declined on the Day of Arafah, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to cease the Talbiyya when the sun declined on the Day of Arafah. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: So when you cease the Talbiyya, then upon you is the Tahleel, the Tahmid, the Tamjeed, and the Thana' upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Misma'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Arafaat, all of it is a Pausing Station, and the most superior of the Pausing Station is at the base of the mountain.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you stand at Arafat, draw near to the plateaus, and the plateaus are the mountains, for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The companions of the Arak trees have no Hajj,' meaning those who stand at the Arak trees.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said regarding the Pausing Station: 'Arise from the middle of Urna'. And he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The companions of Arak, there is no Hajj for them'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Stand in the left side of the mountain, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood at Arafat in the left side of the mountain. So when he stood, the people rushed to the heels of his camel and stood beside him. So he moved it nearby, so they did the same. Then he said: 'O people! The place of the heels of my camel is not the Station (Mawqif), but all of this is the Station,' and he gestured with his hand to the Station. And he did the same in Al-Muzdalifa. So whenever you see a gap, fill it with yourself and your mount, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves that those gaps be filled. And move from the plateaus and avoid the Arak bushes. So when you stand at Arafat, praise Allah, extol His holiness, glorify Him, laud Him, and proclaim His Greatness with one hundred Takbirs. And recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' one hundred times, and choose for yourself from supplications whatever you like, and strive, for it is a day of supplication and asking. And seek refuge with Allah from Satan, for Satan will not astound you in a place more beloved to him than to astound you in that place. And beware of being occupied with looking at the people, and turn your attention towards yourself. Let what you say be: 'O Allah, Lord of all the Stations, free my neck from the Fire, expand for me from the Halal sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the mischievous among Jinn and humans.' O Allah, do not plot against me, nor deceive me, nor drag me down. O Most Hearing of the hearers, and O Most Seeing of the seers, and O Quickest of the Reckoners, and O Most Merciful of the merciful! I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to do for me such and such. Let what you say, while you are raising your hands to the sky, be: 'O Allah, my need which, if You grant it, what You withhold from me will not harm me; and if You withhold it, what You give me will not benefit me. I ask You for the liberation of my neck from the Fire.' O Allah, I am Your servant, and a possession of Your Hand, and my forelock is in Your Hand, and my term is in Your Knowledge. I ask You to enable me to do that which pleases You about me, and to accept from me my

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) paused at Arafat, so when the sun was about to set, before it rushed [to set], he said: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, and from the scattering of affairs, and from the evil of what occurs by night and day.' My weakness has become a supplicant seeking refuge in Your forgiveness, and my fear has become a supplicant seeking refuge in Your security, and my humiliation has become a supplicant seeking refuge in Your honor, and my perishable face has become a supplicant seeking refuge in Your Everlasting Face. O the best of those asked, and O the most generous of those who give, clothe me with Your mercy, and dress me with Your health, and turn away from me the evil of all Your creation. Abdullah ibn Maymun said, 'And I heard my father saying: O the best of those asked to, and O the most extensive of those who give, and O the most merciful of those who are made merciful, then ask your need.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is nothing prescribed (in particular) from the supplications of the evening of Arafah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, who said: I saw Abdullah ibn Jundub at the Mawqif (Station), and I did not see a station that was better than his station. He continued extending his hands to the sky, and his tears were flowing upon his cheeks until they reached the ground. So when the people left, I said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad! I have not seen a station at all that was better than your station.' He said, 'By Allah, I did not supplicate except for my brethren. And that is because Abu Al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) informed me that whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, a call is made from the Throne, and for you is a hundred thousand times the like of it. Therefore, I disliked that I should leave a guaranteed hundred thousand times for one person, whom I do not know if he will be answered for or not.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubayd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, who said: Isa bin Ayn, when he performed Hajj, would turn to supplication for his brethren when he arrived at the Station (Mawqif), until the people departed. I said to him, 'You spend your wealth and exhaust your body, and when you come to the place where needs are presented to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, you turn to supplicating for your brethren and neglect yourself?' He said, 'I am relying upon the supplication of the Angels for me, and am in doubt regarding the supplication for myself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafaat at the Mawqif, and he was calling out in a loud voice: 'O people! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was the Imam, then Ali ibn Abi Talib, then al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then Ali ibn al-Husayn, then Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), then Hah!' So he called out three times to those in front of him, and on his right, and on his left, and behind him, making twelve calls in total. And Amr said: 'So when I went to Mina, I asked the masters of Arabic about the interpretation of Hah So they said: 'Hah' in the language of the clan of so-and-so means 'I', so ask me.' He said: 'Then I asked others as well from the masters of Arabic, and they said the same.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When Arafaat is constricted, what do they do?' He said, 'They ascend to the mountain.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When is the departure from Arafat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the redness disappears, meaning from the eastern side.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The polytheists used to depart (from Arafat) before the sun set, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) opposed them, and he departed after the setting of the sun.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sun sets, depart with the people, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity, and depart with seeking forgiveness, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Then hasten on from where the people hasten on and seek the forgiveness of Allah; surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.' So when you reach the red dune on the right of the road, say: 'O Allah, have mercy on my standing, increase my knowledge, safeguard my religion for me, and accept my rituals.' Beware of the excitement which the people do, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people, Hajj is not the excitement of cavalry, nor the racing of camels, but fear Allah and walk with a beautiful walk, do not trample the weak, nor trample a Muslim, be considerate and moderate in walking, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would restrain his she-camel until its head would touch the front of the saddle, and he would say: O people, upon you is calmness, thus the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is to be followed.' Muawiya said, 'And I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: O Allah, emancipate me from the Fire,' and he repeated it until he departed. So I said to him, 'Are you not departing, for the people have already departed?' So he said, 'I fear the congestion, and I fear that I might participate in impeding a person.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharjah, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying at the end of his speech when he departed: 'O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from being unjust, or being treated unjustly, or cutting off a relationship, or harming a neighbour.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who departed from Arafat before the setting of the sun. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a camel (badanah) which he should sacrifice on the Day of Sacrifice. So if he is not able, he should fast for eighteen days in Makkah, or on the road, or among his family.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, appoints two angels at the two narrow points of Arafat, so they say: 'Safety! Safety!'
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Two angels make way for the people on the night of Muzdalifa at the two narrow points.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya and Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Do not pray the Maghrib prayer until you arrive at Jam', so pray Maghrib and the last Isha prayer there with one Adhan and two Iqamas. Descend into the valley floor on the right side of the road, near the Mash'ar. It is recommended for the first-timer to stand at the Sacred Mash'ar, tread upon it with his foot, and not pass the basins on the night of Muzdalifa. And he should say: 'O Allah, this is Jam'. O Allah, I ask You to gather for me therein all encompassing goodness. O Allah, do not make me despair of the goodness which I ask You to gather for me in my heart. And I seek from You to make known to me what You made known to Your Guardians in this my station, and to protect me from all encompassing evil.' And if you can stay awake during that night, then do so, for it has reached us that the doors of the sky are not closed that night for the voices of the believers, who have a humming sound like the humming of bees. Allah, Exalted is His Praise, says: 'I am your Lord, and you are My servants. You have fulfilled My Right, and it is a Right upon Me to answer you.' Thus, Allah removes from whom He wills their sins that night, and forgives whom He wills.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cycles of prayer after Maghrib on the night of Muzdalifa, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray them after Isha, four cycles.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is recommended for the first-timer that he walks to the Sacred Monument and enters the House.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Remain in a state of purity after you have prayed Fajr, then stand; if you wish, stand near the mountain, and if you wish, stand wherever you wish. So when you stand, praise Allah, laud Him, and mention from His blessings and trials as much as you are able, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And let your words be: 'O Allah, Lord of the Sacred Monument, free my neck from the Fire, and expand for me from Your permissible sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the deviant Jinns and humans.' O Allah, You are the best of those sought, the best of those supplicated to, and the best of those pleaded to. And for every visitor there is a recompense, so make my recompense in this place of mine that You excuse my stumbles, accept my excuses, and overlook my mistakes, then make piety from the world my provision. Then depart when it brightens for you sufficiently to see the places of the hooves of the camels.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Which time is most beloved to you for departing from Jam'?' He said: 'A little before the sun rises, that is the most beloved of the times to me.' I said: 'And if we remain until the sun rises?' He said: 'There is no problem with it.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not cross the valley of Muhassar until the sun rises.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: To one of his sons: 'Did you walk briskly in the valley of Muhassar?' He said, 'No.' So he ordered him to return until he walked briskly. His son said to him, 'I do not know it.' So he said to him, 'Ask the people.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from one of our companions who said: A man passed by the valley of Muhassar, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) ordered him, after his leaving to go to Makkah, that he should return, and he should walk briskly.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you pass by the valley of Muhassar, and it is a great valley between Jam' and Mina, and it is nearer to Mina, so walk briskly in it until you cross it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stirred his she-camel and said: 'O Allah, secure my Covenant for me, and accept my repentance, and answer my supplication, and be in my place among those I left behind.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The brisk movement (walking) in the valley of Muhassar is one hundred steps.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the boundary of Jam' (the two narrow points). He said: 'What is between the two narrow points up to the valley of Muhassar.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn Al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The boundary of Al-Muzdalifa is from Muhassar up to the two narrow points.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When the people are numerous at Jam' and there is narrowness upon them, what should they be doing?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should be arising to go to the two narrow points (Ma'azim).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Azdi, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: The brisk walking (ramal) in the valley of Muhassar is a measurement of one hundred cubits.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Hakeem, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A non-Arab man and a weak woman are with the Bedouin cameleer. When he departs with them from 'Arafat, he passes with them just as he passed with them to Mina and does not encamp with them at Jam'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that they prayed there, so it has sufficed them?' I said: 'And if they did not pray there?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They mention Allah in it. So if they had mentioned Allah in it, it has sufficed them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! These two companions of mine were ignorant that they should pause at Muzdalifa.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They should return to their places and pause at the Mash'ar for a while.' I said, 'But no one informed them until today, and the people have left.' So he (peace be upon him) lowered his head for a while, then said: 'Is it not so that both of them had prayed the morning prayer at Muzdalifa?' I said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not so that they had both performed Qunoot in their prayer?' I said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Their Hajj is complete.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Mash'ar is from Muzdalifa, and Muzdalifa is from the Mash'ar. And indeed, a little supplication suffices them.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a man who departs from 'Arafat and goes to Mina?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him return and go to Jam', and let him stand there, even if the people have already departed from Jam'.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man departed from Arafat, passed by Al-Mash'ar, but did not stand (pause) until he reached Mina, and threw the Jamarah, and he was unaware until the day rose. He (peace be upon him) said: He should return to Al-Mash'ar and stand there, then return and throw the Jamarah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Khas'amy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who did not pause at Al-Muzdalifa and did not spend the night there until he went to Mina, he said: 'Did he not see the people and did he not acknowledge Mina when he entered it?' I said, 'If he was ignorant of that?' He said: 'He should return.' I said, 'If that opportunity has been lost?' He said: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever departs from Arafat with the people and does not remain with them at Jam', and proceeds to Mina deliberately or by taking it lightly, then upon him is a camel (as a sacrifice).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub al-Kub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not befitting for anyone to take from the soil of what is around the Ka'bah. And if he takes anything from that, he should return it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I took a perfume from the perfumes of the Standing Place (Maqam Ibrahim), and soil from the soil of the House (Kaaba), and seven pebbles.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what you have done. As for the soil and the pebbles, return them.'

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from the one who narrates it, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'My uncle swept the Ka'bah and took from its soil, so we heal with it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Return it to it.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zayd al-Shahham who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I go out from the Masjid and in my garment is a pebble.' He said: 'So return it, or throw it back into the Masjid.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who paused with the people at Jam', then departed before the people departed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him, and if he departed before the emergence of the dawn, then upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Saeed al-Samman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) hastened the women at night from Al-Muzdalifa to Mina, and ordered those of them upon whom was a sacrificial animal (hady) that she should pelt (the Jamarah), and she should not depart until she has slaughtered (the animal); and those of them who did not have a sacrificial animal upon her, that she should go to Makkah until she has performed visitation (Ziyarah).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: There is no problem with a man departing at night if he is afraid (for his safety).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Whichever woman or man, being fearful, departs from the Sacred Monument (Muzdalifah) at night, there is no problem; let him pelt the Jamarah, then let him proceed and instruct someone to sacrifice on his behalf; and the woman shortens (her hair), and the man shaves (his head). Then let him perform Tawaf by the House (Kaaba) and by As-Safa and Al-Marwa, then let him return to Mina. So if he goes to Mina and no sacrifice has been made on his behalf, there is no problem if he sacrifices himself, and let him carry the hair when he shaves in Mecca to Mina; and if he wishes, he may shorten (his hair) if he had performed Hajj before that.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the women and children to depart at night, to pelt the Jamarat at night, and to pray the morning prayer in their homes. So if they feared menstruation, they would go to Mecca, and they would appoint someone to offer the sacrifice on their behalf.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no problem with the women proceeding (from Muzdalifah) when the night declines, so they pause at the Sacred Monument for an hour, then they are taken to Mina so they pelt the Jamarah, then they wait for an hour, then they shorten (their hair/nails) and go to Mecca so they perform Tawaf, except if they intend that an animal be slaughtered on their behalf, for they appoint someone to slaughter on their behalf.

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, there are women with us, so should I depart with them at night?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, you intend to do as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did.' I said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Depart with them at night, and do not depart with them until you pause with them at Jam', then depart with them until you bring them to the Great Jamarah, so they should pelt the Jamarah. If there is no slaughter upon them, let them take from their hair and shorten their nails, and proceed to Mecca facing it, and perform Tawaf by the House, and perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. Then let them return to the House and perform a week's Tawaf, then let them return to Mina, and they will have completed their Hajj.' And he said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Usamah with them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the women and the weak to depart from Jam' at night and to throw the Jamarah at night. So if they wish to visit the House, they should appoint someone to slaughter on their behalf.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawood Al-Raqqi, who said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) at Mina when a man came and said, 'A group of people arrived on the day of the sacrifice, and they have missed the Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'We ask Allah for health, and I see that each one of them should spill the blood of a sheep, and they should be freed from the Ihram, and upon them is the Hajj in the future if they return to their lands; and if they stay until the days of Al-Tashreeq in Makkah, then they should go out to a juncture of the people of Makkah and enter into Ihram from it, and perform Umrah, so there would not be upon them the Hajj in the future.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever reaches Jam', he has accomplished the Hajj. And he said: Whichever Muhrim is a Qarin (one who combines Tamattu' and Ifrad), or an Ifradi (one performing exclusive Hajj), or a Mutamatti' (one performing Tamattu'), arrives and has missed the Hajj, so let him free himself from Ihram with Umrah, and upon him is the Hajj in the following year. He said, and he said regarding a man who catches up with the Imam and he is in Jam', so he said: If he thinks that he will reach 'Arafat, so he will stand in it for a little while, then he will reach Jam' before the emergence of the sun, so let him go to it; and if he thinks that he will not reach it until they depart, so he should not go to it, and let him stay in Jam', so he has completed his Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who arrives at the Sacred Monument on the Day of Sacrifice before the decline of the sun, has accomplished the Hajj.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever arrives at the Sacred Monument (Mash'ar al-Haram) and upon it are five from the people, before the sun declines, then he has accomplished the Hajj.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who arrives at the Sacred Monument (Mash'ar al-Haram), and upon it are five from the people, so he has accomplished the Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Do you know why three (Sacred Monuments) have been placed there?' I said, 'No'. He said: 'So whoever attains any one of them, has attained the Hajj.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Take the pebbles for the Jamarah from Jam', and if you take them from your place of departure in Mina, it will suffice you.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the pebbles with which the Jamarat are pelleted. So he said: 'They are taken from Jam', and they are taken after that from Mina.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Take the pebbles for pelting the Jamarah from Jam', and if you take them from your place of departure in Mina, it will suffice you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Pick up the pebbles and do not break any of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The pebbles of the Jamarah, if you take it from the Haram, it suffices you, and if you take it from other than the Haram, it does not suffice you. He said, and he said: Do not pelt the Jamarah except with pebbles.

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the pebbles of the Jamarah. He said: The solid (single-structured) ones from it are disliked. And he said: Take the multi-colored ones.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The pebbles for pelting the Jamarah should be like the fingernail, and do not take them black, nor white, nor red. Take them kuhl-colored, dotted. You should hurl them with a hurl, place them on the thumb, and push them with the nail of the forefinger. Throw them from the middle of the valley, and make them all from your right. Do not throw at the Jamarah (singular), and stand at the first two Jamarat, and do not stand at the Jamarat al-Aqabah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is allowed to take the pebbles for pelting the Jamarat from all parts of the Haram, except from the Sacred Masjid and Masjid al-Khief.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: From where is it befitting to take the pebbles of the Jamarah? He said: Do not take them from two places: from outside the Haram, and from the pebbles of the Jamarah; and there is no problem with taking them from the rest of the Haram.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Take the pebbles of the Jamarat, then go to the furthest Jamarah which is at Aqaba, and throw it from its front, and do not throw it from its top, and say while the pebble is in your hand: 'O Allah, these are my pebbles, so count them for me and raise them in my deeds.' Then you throw and say with each pebble: 'Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, drive away Satan from me. O Allah, [as] confirmation of Your Book and upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, make it an accepted Hajj, an accepted deed, an appreciated effort, and a forgiven sin.' And let there be between you and the Jamarah a distance of ten cubits or fifteen cubits. So when you go to your mount and return from the throwing, say: 'O Allah, in You I have trusted and upon You I have relied, so good is the Lord, good is the Guardian, and good is the Helper.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it is recommended that the Jamarat be thrown while in a state of ritual purity.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about pelting the Jamarah on the Day of Nahr (Sacrifice), 'What is the matter with it that it is pelted alone, and the other Jamarat are not pelted on the Day of Nahr?' So he said: 'All of them used to be pelted, but they left that.' So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so can I pelt them all?' He said: 'Do not pelt them all. Are you not pleased that you do similar to what we do?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Humran, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about pelting the Jamarat, so he said: 'They used to all be pelted on the Day of Nahr (sacrifice). So I used to pelt them all after that.' Then I narrated it to him, so he said to me: 'Are you not pleased that you should do as Ali (peace be upon him) used to do?' So I left it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), and from Ibn Udhaynah, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: The Jamarat used to be pelted altogether. I said, 'So can I pelt them (all)?' So he said, 'No. Are you not pleased that you should be doing just as I do?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Saeed al-Roumy, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) pelted the Great Jamarah, so he saw the people standing still. So he stood up in their midst, then called out in a loud voice: 'O people! This is not a standing stop!' three times. So I did it (as well).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man from the Ansar: 'When you have pelted the Jamarat, there would be for you with each pebble (pelted), ten good deeds being written for you for whatever is from your life in the future'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the pelting of the Jamarat, he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'With each pebble he pelts with, a major destructive sin is erased from him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Pelt during every day at the decline of the sun, and say as you said when you pelted the Jamarat al-Aqabah. So begin with the first Jamarah and pelt it from its left in the middle of the ravine, and say as you said on the day of the sacrifice. Stand on the left of the road and face the Qiblah, then praise Allah and extol Him and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then proceed a little, so supplicate to Him and ask Him that He accepts from you. Then move forward a little, then do that at the second one, and do as you did with the first one; and pause and supplicate to Allah as you supplicated. Then go to the third, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity, so pelt, and do not pause at it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Jamarat (pillars of stone), so he said: 'Stand at the two Jamarat and do not stand at the Jamarat al-Aqabah.' I said: 'Is this from the Sunnah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What should I say when I pelt?' So he said: 'Exclaim Takbeer with each pebble.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Take the pebbles of the Jamarah with your left hand, and throw with your right.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, and Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: 'Peleing the Jamarah is from the emergence of the sun until its setting.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said to Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba: ‘What is the time limit for pelting the Jamarah?’ So Al-Hakam said, ‘At the decline of the sun’. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: ‘What is your view if there were two men, so one of them says to his companion, ‘Guard our provisions for us until I return’, would he miss the pelting? By Allah, it is what is between the emergence of the sun and its setting’.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the camel herders, when they came at night, to throw (the pebbles).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ismail ibn Hammam said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not pelt the Jamarah on the day of the sacrifice until the sun rises.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'You should pelt the Jamarat from the middle of the valley, and place each Jamarah to your right. Then turn to the other side when you pelt the Jamarat Al-Aqabah.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Muhammad Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the ritual bath (ghusl) when one intends to pelt (the Jamarah). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Sometimes I bathe. But, as for it being from the Sunnah, then no (it is not so).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) when pelting the Jamarah. So he said: 'Sometimes I do so, and as for it being from the Sunnah, then no (it is not), but it is due to the heat and the sweat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Jamarat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not pelt the Jamarat except while you are in a state of purity.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who forgot to pelt the Jamarat on the second day, so he began with the Jamarat al-Aqabah, then the middle one, then the first one; he should delay what he pelts with, and he should pelt the middle Jamarah, then the Jamarat al-Aqabah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, and Hammad, from Al-Halby, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who pelts the Jamarah in reverse order. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat upon Al-Wusta (the middle), and Jamarat Al-Aqabah.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Karim ibn Amr, from Abdul A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man pelts the Jamarah with six pebbles, and one falls among the (other) pebbles. He said: He should repeat it, if he so desires, from that moment, and if he so desires, from the next day when he intends the pelting; and he should not take from the pebbles of the Jamarah. He said: And I asked him about a man who pelts Jamarat al-Aqabah with six pebbles, and one falls in the carriage. He said: He should repeat it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I went to pelt (the Jamarah), and I found six pebbles in my hand.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Take one from beneath your foot.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who took twenty-one pebbles and threw them, but one remained, and he did not know which of them was deficient from, he said: 'So let him return and let him throw each one with a pebble.' If a pebble falls from a man and he does not know which of them it was, he said: 'He should take a pebble from under his feet and throw with it.' He said: 'And if you throw with a pebble and it falls in a carriage, so repeat in its place. And if it hits a person or a camel, then it falls upon the Jamarat, it will suffice you.' And he said regarding a man who threw the Jamarat, so he threw the first one with four, and the last two with seven, seven: 'He should return and throw the first one with three, and he would have been freed.' And if he had thrown the first one with three, and threw the last two with seven, seven, so let him return and let him throw all of them with seven, seven. And if he had thrown the middle one with three, then threw the other one, so let him throw the middle one with seven. And if he had thrown the middle one with four, he should return and throw with three. He said, 'I said, The man reverses in throwing the Jamarat, so he begins with Jamarat al-Aqabah, then the middle, then the great one.' He said: 'He should return and throw the middle, then he would throw Jamarat al-Aqabah, and even if it is the next morning.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man forgot to throw the Jamarat until he arrived in Mecca.' He said, 'He should return and throw them, separating each two throws by an hour.' I said, 'What if he missed that and left?' He said, 'There is nothing upon him.' He said, 'I said, 'And what about a man who forgot the Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa?'' He said, 'He should repeat the Sa'ee.' I said, 'What if he missed that until he left?' He said, 'He should return and repeat the Sa'ee. Indeed, this is not like throwing the Jamarat. Indeed, throwing is a Sunnah, and the Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa is an obligation.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, and someone else, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who departed from Jam' until he arrived at Mina, and an incident occurred to him so he did not pelt the Jamarah until the sun set. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pelt twice when it is morning; one of them in the morning, and it is for the previous day, and the other at the decline of the sun, and it is for his day.'

And from him, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a woman who was ignorant that she should pelt the Jamarah, until she departed to Mecca?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let her return and let her pelt the Jamarah, just as she was pelting; and for the man, it is like that (as well).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the one who is fearful (of missing the prescribed times), there is no problem if he were to pelt the Jamarat at night, and sacrifice (the animal) at night, and depart (from Mina) at night.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he disliked pelting the Jamarah at night, and he permitted it for the slave and the herdsman with regards to pelting the Jamarah at night.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one with a broken bone and the one with stomach illness, the Jamarah is pelted on their behalf. He (peace be upon him) said: And the children, the Jamarah is pelted on their behalf.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the sick person for whom the Jamarat are pelted. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, he is carried to the Jamarah, and it is pelted on his behalf.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina, walking and riding. So I said to myself that I would ask him when I go over to him, but he initiated me with the hadith and said: 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to go out from his house walking when he pelted the Jamarah; and my house today is further than his house. So I ride until I get to his house. So when I arrive at his house, I walk until I pelt the Jamarah.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Musanna, from a man, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pelt the Jamarah while walking.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) walking after the Day of Sacrifice until he pelted the Jamarah, then he returned riding; and I saw him walking after he passed by the Masjid in Mina. He said, and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Nawfaly narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Salih from one of his companions who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) dismounted from his animal slightly above the Masjid in Mina, until he turned to pelt the Jamarah at the spot of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, why did you dismount here?' He said, 'For here is the spot of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the spot of the Banu Hashim, and I love to walk in the encampments of the Banu Hashim.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Kuleyb Al-Asady, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the sacrifice (al-nahr), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for Mina, then it is three days, and as for in the cities (al-buldan), then it is one day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The days of Al-Adha are two days after the day of sacrifice, and one day in the provinces (cities).

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever performs Hajj and Umrah together, then whatever offering is easy to obtain,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'A sheep.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A sheep suffices for the Qiran (Tamattu') Hajj.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting for a man to stay in Makkah for a year. I said, 'What should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He should move away from it. And it is not befitting for anyone to raise a structure above the Ka'bah.' And it is reported that staying in Makkah hardens the hearts.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Zareeh, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you have completed your rituals, return, for it is more desirable for you to return.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who performs Tamattu' during the months of Hajj, then stays in Makkah until the Hajj of the following year arrives, upon him is a sheep.' And the one who performs Tamattu' in other than the months of Hajj, then resides (as a neighbor/sojourner) until the Hajj arrives, there is no blood (sacrifice) upon him. Rather, it is an individual Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad). And the sacrifice (Udhiyah/Qurbani) is upon the people of the cities (who reside there).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the sacrifice (al-adha): Is it obligatory upon the one who finds the means for himself and his dependents? So he said: As for himself, he should not leave it; and as for his dependents, if he wishes, he can leave it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who arrived in Makkah with his sacrifice during the ten (days of Dhu al-Hijjah), he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his offering was obligatory, he should not slaughter it except in Mina; and if it was not obligatory, let him slaughter it in Makkah if he wishes; and if he had decorated it and yoked it, he should not slaughter it except on the Day of Sacrifice.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'When a man exits from his Hajj with an animal upon which a sacrificial blood (dam) is obligatory, is it sufficient for him to slaughter it when he returns to his family?' He said, 'Yes.' And he said, 'As far as I know, he should give it in charity.' Is'haq said, 'And I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'When a man exits from his Hajj with what obligates upon him the blood (dam), and he does not spill it until he returns to his family,' he said, 'He should spill it among his family, and he should eat something from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I drove a camel for the Umrah, where should I slaughter it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'In Makkah.' I said, 'What should I give from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat a third, gift a third, and give in charity with a third.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The people of Makkah are denying you, saying that you slaughtered your offering in your house in Makkah.' So he said, 'Verily, all of Makkah is a place of sacrifice.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from the one who narrated to him, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the lowest [age] that suffices from the years of the sheep regarding the sacrificial offering (Hady), so he said: 'The Jadh'ah of the sheep.' I said, 'And what about the goat?' He said: 'The Jadh'ah of the goat does not suffice.' I said, 'And why?' He said: 'Because the Jadh'ah of the sheep can impregnate, but the Jadh'ah of the goat cannot impregnate.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the camel and the cow, which of the two is superior to be sacrificed with? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Those with the womb (i.e., females capable of bearing young).' So I asked him (peace be upon him) about their ages. He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the cow, it does not matter to you with which of its ages you sacrifice. And as for the camel, it is not valid unless it is a thani (two-year-old) or what is above it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The years (ages) of the cow you sell are the same, and its aged one, with regards to the sacrifice, is equal.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the ewe, is it more beloved to you or the goat? He (peace be upon him) said: If the goat is male, then it is more beloved to me; and if the goat is female, then the ewe is more beloved to me. He (the narrator) said, I said, So can the castrated one be sacrificed with? He (peace be upon him) said: No, unless there is no other. And he (peace be upon him) said: The young sheep (jadh') is suitable, but as for the goat, it is not suitable. I said, Is the castrated one more beloved to you or the ewe? He (peace be upon him) said: The suckling is more beloved to me than the ewe, and if it is castrated, then the ewe (is more beloved).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man buys a sacrificial camel that is thin, and finds it to be fat, it suffices for him; and if he buys it as thin and finds it as thin, it does not suffice for him.
Aban, from Abdul Rahman, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: The ram in your land is superior to the camel.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who buys a sacrificial animal (hady) and it had a defect, blindness or something else, he (peace be upon him) said: If he had paid its price in cash, it suffices for him; and if he had not paid its price, he should return it and buy another in its place, a sheep, or a cow. He (the narrator) said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Buy a fat male for the Tamattu' (sacrifice); if you do not find one, then a 'majwūn' (a specific type of young animal); if you do not find one, then from the male goats; if you do not find one, then an ewe; if you do not find one, then whatever is easily available of the sacrificial animals. He (peace be upon him) said: And for the Tamattu' sacrifice, the jadha' (two-year-old) from the sheep suffices, but the jadha' from the goat does not suffice. He (the narrator) said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who bought a sheep, then intended to buy a fatter one than it: He should buy it, and when he buys it, he should sell the first one. He (the narrator) said, and I do not know (whether he meant selling the sheep or the goat).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The charity of a loaf of bread is better than a ritual (offering of) a thin (animal).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrificial animal whose ear is torn, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If its tear is a mark (from branding), then there is no problem, and if it is a tear, then it is not suitable.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not offer a sacrifice with the one who limps, its limp being evident, nor with the lean one, nor with the scabby one, nor with the one with torn ears, nor with the one with the tail cut off, nor with the one that has no eye.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the sacrificial animal (udhiyah) whose horn is broken, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the interior horn is sound, it suffices.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the aged animal whose teeth have fallen out, that there is no problem with it regarding the sacrificial animals; and if you bought it as thin and found it as fat, it would suffice you; and if you bought it as thin and found it as thin, then it would not suffice. And in another report, 'The limit of thinness is when there is not anything of fat upon its kidneys.'

Muhammad ibn Isa reported it, from Yaseen al-Darir, from Hariz, from Al-Fudayl, who said: I performed Hajj with my family one year, and the sacrificial animals were expensive. So I went and bought two sheep for a high price. So, when I examined their cuticles, I regretted it with an intense regret due to what I saw with them from the thinness. So I went over to him and informed him of that. So he said: ‘If there was something from the fat upon their kidneys, they would both suffice’.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Sulami, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: Some of the Khawarij asked me about this verse: 'Of sheep, two; and of goats, two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females? Or what is in the wombs of the two females? Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful. And of camels, two; and of cows, two.' What is that which Allah has permitted from that, and what is that which He has prohibited? But I did not have anything (to answer with). So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was a pilgrim, and I informed him of what had happened. He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted in the sacrificial offering in Mina the domestic sheep and the domestic goat, and prohibited that one sacrifice the mountain (wild) ones.' And as for His words 'And of camels, two; and of cows, two', indeed Allah, Blessed and High, permitted in the sacrificial offering the Iraab camel, and prohibited the Bukhaty in it; and permitted the domestic cow that one sacrifice with it, and prohibited the mountain (wild) one. So I returned to the man and informed him with this answer. He said: 'This is something which the camels carried from Al-Hijaaz.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'You have benefits in them till a specified time.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If one needs its back, ride it without being harsh upon it; and if it has milk, milk it with a milking that does not exhaust it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If your camel gives birth, milk it for a time that does not harm its offspring, then sacrifice both (the mother and the offspring). I asked: 'Do I drink from its milk and give others to drink?' He said: 'Yes.' And he said: 'Indeed, Ali, Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), when he saw people walking who were exhausted by walking, would carry them upon his sacrificial camels.' And he said: 'If a man's mount strays or perishes, and with him is a sacrificial animal (hady), let him ride upon his sacrificial animal.'
