Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the she-camel that gives birth; can I milk her? He said: Milk her with a milking that is not harmful to the offspring. Then sacrifice them both together. I said: Can one drink from its milk? He said: Yes, and give drink (to others), if he so desires.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Everyone who brings a sacrificial animal voluntarily, and his sacrificial animal gets exhausted, so there is nothing upon him. He should slaughter it, and he should take the rein of the yoke, so he should immerse it in the blood, and he should strike its hump with it, and there would not be a replacement upon him. And whatever was from the penalty of the hunting, or a vow, and it gets exhausted, so it would be upon the like of that, and upon him would be a replacement. And every thing which enters the Haram and it gets exhausted, so there would be no replacement upon its owner, be it a voluntary one or something else.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a sacrificial animal, so it died or was stolen before he slaughtered it. He said: 'There is no problem, and if he replaces it, that is better, and if he does not buy (another one), there is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from a man who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the camel which a man offers as a sacrifice, so it either breaks (a body part), or it perishes. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his sacrificial animal was ensured (liable for loss), so upon him would be (another one) in its place; and if it did not happen to be ensured, so there is nothing upon him'. I said, 'And can he eat from it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the obligatory sacrificial animal (Hady) when it suffers a break or damage. Can its owner sell it and use its price to acquire another sacrificial animal? He said: He should sell it, give its price in charity, and offer another sacrificial animal.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said: When a man finds a stray sacrificial animal, he should announce it on the day of sacrifice, the second day, and the third day; then he should slaughter it on behalf of its owner on the evening of the third day. And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who sends the obligatory sacrificial animal, but the animal perishes in the road before it reaches its destination, and he has no capacity to send another: Allah (Glorious is He) is the Foremost with the excuse, unless he knows that when he asks (for a replacement) he will be given it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a sacrificial animal for his 'Umrat al-Tamattu'. He brought it to his family, tied it, then released it, and it perished. Would it suffice him, or should he repeat (offer another)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It would not suffice him unless he has no financial strength to offer another.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who bought a ram but it perished. He said: 'He should buy another one in its place.' I said, 'Supposing he buys another one in its place, then finds the first one?' He said: 'If both of them were standing (available), so let him slaughter the first one, and let him sell the other one, and if he so desires to, he can slaughter it; and if it was so that he had already slaughtered the other one, so let him slaughter the first one along with it'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man whose sacrificial animal (hady) strays, so another man finds it and slaughters it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had slaughtered it at Mina, it has sufficed for its owner from whom it had strayed; and if he had slaughtered it in other than Mina, it has not sufficed for its owner.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bought a sacrificial animal and slaughtered it. A man passed by and recognized it, and said: 'This is my she-camel that strayed from me yesterday.' And two men testified to that. He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Its meat is for him, and it does not suffice for either of the two (as a sacrifice).' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And due to that, the Sunnah is established with marking it and yoking it when it is recognized.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would slaughter two rams on the Day of Sacrifice, one on behalf of himself and the other on behalf of someone from his community who could not find (afford) it; and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would slaughter two rams, one on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the other on behalf of himself.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a group of people for whom the sacrificial animals were too expensive, and they were performing Tamattu', and they were traveling companions, and they were not of one family, and they had gathered in their journey and their tent was one. Is it for them that they should slaughter one cow? He said: I do not like that unless it is from necessity.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from a man called Sawada, who said: We were a group in Mina, and the sacrificial animals were too expensive. So we looked around and there was Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) standing upon a flock, bargaining with the sheep, and he was intensively bargaining with them. So we stopped and waited. When he finished, he turned towards us and said: 'I think you have been astounded by my bargaining.' So we said, 'Yes'. He said: 'The one who is cheated (in excessive spending) is neither praiseworthy nor rewarded. Is there a need for you?' So we said, 'Yes. May Allah keep you well! The sacrificial animals have become too expensive for us.' He said: 'So gather together and buy a camel among yourselves.' We said, 'And our expenditure would not reach (that).' He said: 'So gather together and buy a cow among yourselves and slaughter it.' We said, 'And our expenditure would not reach (that).' He said: 'So gather together and buy a sheep among yourselves and slaughter it among yourselves.' We said, 'Does it suffice for seven?' He said, 'Yes, and it suffices for seventy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Humran, who said: The sacrificial camels became expensive in Mina one year, to the extent that the single camel reached one hundred dinars. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about that, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Participate in it [share in it].' I said, 'How many?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is lighter, so it is superior.' I said, 'On behalf of how many would it suffice?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'On behalf of seventy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn Qar'ah, from Zayd ibn Jaham, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The performer of Tamattu' could not find a sacrificial animal.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Did he not have one Dirham to go to his people with, so he could be saying to them, 'Participate me with this Dirham?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So mention the Name of Allah upon them, standing in a row.' He said: 'That is when they are lined up for slaughter. You tie their forelegs from the hooves to the knees, and the falling of their sides is when they fall upon the ground.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How is the camel slaughtered?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is slaughtered while it is standing, from the right side.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'An-Nahr' (sacrificing by cutting the throat from the front) is in the 'Labbah' (upper chest), and 'Adh-Dhabh' (slaughtering by cutting the windpipe and veins) is in the 'Halq' (throat).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: The Jew or the Christian should not slaughter your sacrificial animal for you. So if it is a female animal, let her slaughter it herself, and she should face the Qiblah, and say: 'I have turned my face toward Him Who originated the heavens and the earth, upright. O Allah, from You and for You.'

And from him, from Muawiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to place the knife in the hand of a child, then the man would grasp the hand of the child, and he would slaughter.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you buy your sacrificial animal, face the Qiblah with it, and slaughter it or sacrifice it. And say: 'I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth, upright, and I am not of the polytheists.' Surely my Prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are (all) for Allah, the Lord of the worlds. There is no associate for Him; and with that I am Commanded, and I am from the Muslims. O Allah, from You and for You. In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, accept from me. Then move the knife and do not break its bones until it dies.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You begin at Mina with the slaughter before the shaving, and in the 'Aqiqah with the shaving before the slaughter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim al-Bajali, from Abu Khadeeja, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sacrificing his camel with its left leg tied. Then he stood by the side of its right leg and said: 'In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, this is from You and for You. O Allah, accept it from me.' Then he made an incision in its throat (larynx), then removed the knife with his hand. So when it fell down, he cut the place of slaughter with his hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn A'mar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered, when he sacrificed, that a piece of meat be taken from each beast, then thrown into a cooking pot, then cooked. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him) ate from it, and sipped from its broth.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah the Exalted: 'Then when they fall down by the side' He said: 'When it falls upon the ground, so eat from it, and feed the contented one and the passer-by.' He said: 'The contented one is the one who is pleased with what is given to him and does not get angry, nor frowns, nor twists his jaw in anger; and the passer-by is the one who passes by you so that you feed him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meats of the sacrificed animals, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to give in charity a third to their neighbours, and a third to the beggars, and a third they would keep for the Ahl al-Bayt.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from one or more, all from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrificial animal (hady), 'What can the one who offers it eat from it during his Tamattu' and other than that?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Just as he eats from his sacrificial animal (for Hajj).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the expiation for game, when its owner eats from its meat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He eats from his sacrifice (udhiyah) and gives the expiation (fid'ah) in charity.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then when they fall down, eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The contented is the one who is content with whatever you give him; and the mu'tarr is the one who passes by you; and the beggar is the one who asks you with his hand; and the ba'is is the poor one.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about taking out the meat of the sacrificial animals from Mina, so he said: 'We used to say: Do not take anything out of it due to the people's need for it. But as for today, since the people have become numerous, there is no problem with taking it out.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a slave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan Al-Awwal (peace be upon him) call for a camel and sacrifice it. So when the slaughterers struck its jugular veins, it fell to the ground, and they exposed a part of its hump. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Cut it, eat from it, and feed (others).' So when they fall down, eat from them and feed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade us from the meat of the sacrificial animals after three days, then He permitted it and said: 'Eat from the meat of the sacrificial animals after three days, and store it up.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade giving the butcher anything from the hides of the sacrificial animal and its collars/coverings.

And in the narration of Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One may benefit from the hide of the sacrificed animal, and buy provisions with it, and if one gives it in charity, that is superior. And he (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sacrificed a camel and did not give the butchers its hide, nor its collar, nor its reins, but he gave it in charity; and do not give the butcher anything from it, but give him from other than that.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim, from Abu Shibl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The believer, when he shaves his head in Mina, then buries it, will come on the Day of Resurrection, and every hair will have a tongue, eloquently reciting the Talbiyah in the name of its owner.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is it for the man that he should wash his head with the hibiscus (flower) before he shaves off his head?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should shorten it and wash it'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Sacrifice would shave his head, clip his nails, trim his moustache, and trim the sides of his beard.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: When you buy your sacrificial animal, and weigh its price, and it becomes in your saddle (or among your riding animals), then the offering has reached its place. So if you wish to shave (your head), then shave.

And by his chain, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who was ignorant of shortening his hair or shaving it, until he departed from Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him return to Mina until he shaves his hair there or shortens it, and upon the Sarurah (one performing Hajj for the first time) is that he should shave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the first-timer that he should shave; and if he had (already) performed Hajj (before), then if he so desires he can shorten, and if he so desires he can shave. He (peace be upon him) said: And when he adheres his hair or curls (braids) it, so upon him is the shaving, and the shortening is not for him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Upon the first-timer (Al-Saroura) is that he shaves his head completely and does not merely shorten (the hair), and indeed, shortening is for the one who has performed Hajj (before).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to shorten his hair while he was a pilgrim, until he departed from Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that he cast off his hair except in Mina.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then let them fulfill their needful acts (tafathahum).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the shaving and what is in the skin of the human being.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who shaves his head in Makkah, he said: He should return the hair to Mina.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Sunnah regarding the shaving (of the head) is that it should reach the bones.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A woman shortens her hair for her Umrah by the measure of a fingernail.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who visits the House before shaving, he said: It is not befitting unless he is forgetful. } }, { Then he said: Indeed, people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the day of sacrifice, and some of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I slaughtered; and some said: I shaved before I threw (the pebbles). So they did not leave anything that it was befitting for them to delay except that they brought it forward, so he said: There is no harm.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man from our companions pelted the Jamarah on the Day of Sacrifice and shaved before he slaughtered.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was visited on the Day of Sacrifice by groups of Muslims who said, O Messenger of Allah! We slaughtered before we pelted, and we shaved before we slaughtered, and there did not remain anything from what was befitting for them that they should bring forward except that they delayed it, and there was nothing from what was befitting for them that they should delay except that they brought it forward. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'No blame, no blame.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad altogether, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding a man who visited the House before shaving [his head]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he visited the House before shaving, and he knew that this was not befitting for him, then upon him is the blood of a sheep [as expiation].'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who forgot to sacrifice at Mina until he had visited the House (the Kaaba), so he bought (an animal) in Mecca and then slaughtered it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; it suffices for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man enters Makkah and cuts from its trees.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Cut what has entered upon you, and do not cut what has not entered your house upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A tree whose root is in the unrestricted area (al-hill) and its branches are in the sanctuary (al-haram).' He said: 'Its root is prohibited due to the location of its branches.' I said: 'Suppose its root is in the sanctuary and its branches are in the unrestricted area?' He said: 'Its branches are prohibited due to the location of its root.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The camel is released in the Sanctuary to eat whatever it desires.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the tree which a man uproots from his house in the Haram: He said, 'If the house was built and the tree was in it, then it is not for him to uproot it; and if it grew in his house and it is for him, then he should uproot it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mu'tamir (one performing Tamattu' Hajj) when he shaves his head before visiting the House (Kaaba), whether he applies henna to it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the henna, and the clothes, and the perfume, and everything except for the women.' He repeated it to me twice or three times. I said: 'And I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the henna, and the clothes, and the perfume, and everything except for the women.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'The performer of Tamattu' covers his head when he shaves [it].' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son! Shaving his head is greater [in significance/act] than covering it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Yunus, the mawla of Ali, from Abu Ayoub Al-Khazzaz, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) after he had slaughtered [the sacrificial animal], he shaved [his head], then applied musk to his head, and visited the House [the Kaaba], and upon him was a shirt, and he was performing Tamattu'. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub, [narrating] similarly.

Safwan from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said: I asked Abā Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about the Muṭamattiʿ when he shaves his head, what is permissible for him? So he (peace be upon him) said: Everything except for the women.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' who does not find (afford) the sacrificial animal. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast the day before Al-Tarwiyah, and the day of Al-Tarwiyah, and the day of Arafah.' I said: 'What if he arrived on the day of Al-Tarwiyah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast three days after Al-Tashreeq.' I said: 'What if his camel-herder did not wait for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast the day of Al-Hasbah, and two days after it.' I said: 'And what is Al-Hasbah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The day he departs.' I said: 'Should he fast while he is a traveler?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Is he not a traveler on the day of Arafah? We, the People of the House, say that due to the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "Fasting three days during the Hajj" — He means during Dhi al-Hijjah.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said: The one who cannot find (afford) a sacrificial animal (hady) and wishes to bring forward the three days (of fasting) during the first ten (days of Dhu al-Hijjah), so there is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the performer of Tamattu' who could not find a sacrificial animal. He said: 'He should fast three days during the Hajj: one day before Tarwiyya, the day of Tarwiyya, and the day of Arafat.' I said, 'What if he misses that?' He said: 'He should take a pre-dawn meal on the night of al-Hasba (departure) and fast that day and the two days after it.' I said, 'What if his camel-herder does not wait for him? Can he fast them on the way?' He said: 'If he wishes, he can fast them on the way, and if he wishes, (he can fast them) when he returns to his family.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' who enters on the Day of Tarwiyah and has no sacrificial animal with him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So he should not fast that day, nor the Day of Arafah, and he should take a pre-dawn meal on the night of al-Hasbah, so he would be fasting in the morning, and it would be the Day of Nafar, and he would fast the two days after it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I said to him, 'A man performing Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj, in his bag are his clothes. Does he sell from his clothes and buy his sacrificial animal (Hady) from them?' He said, 'No. This is what the Believer adorns himself with. He should fast and not take anything from his clothes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Mutamatti' who finds the price but does not find the sheep, he said: He should leave the price with one of the people of Mecca, and instruct someone to buy for him and slaughter on his behalf, and that would suffice for him. So if Dhu al-Hijjah passes, he delays that to the Dhu al-Hijjah of the next year.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yahya Al-Azraq, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a person performing Tamattu' who had with him the price of a sacrificial animal (Hadayy), and he could have found a sacrificial animal equivalent to what he had with him. But he did not cease to hesitate and delay that until, when it was the end of the day, the price of sheep increased, so he was not able to buy a sacrificial animal with what he had. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast three days after the Days of Tashreeq.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Tamattu', but cannot find a sacrificial animal, so he fasts the three days. So when he fulfills his ritual, it becomes evident to him that he should stay in Mecca. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wait for the arrival of the people of his land. So when he thinks that they have entered, let him fast the seven days.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about a man who performed Tamattu' but could not find what to offer as a sacrifice until, on the day of departure, he found the price of a sheep. Should he slaughter it, or should he fast? He said: 'Rather, he should fast, for the days of slaughter have passed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who does not fast during Dhu al-Hijjah until the crescent of Muharram is seen, upon him is the blood of a sheep, and it is not for him to fast, and he should slaughter it at Mina.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' who fasted three days during the Hajj, then he found/afforded a sacrificial animal (had) on the day he exited from Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His fasting suffices him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Whoever dies and does not have a sacrificial animal for his Umrah (Mut'ah), then his guardian should fast on his behalf.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about a man who performs Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj) and does not have a sacrificial animal (hady), so he fasts three days during Hajj, then dies after returning to his family before fasting the seven days. Is it upon his guardian to fulfill it on his behalf? He said: 'I do not see that he is obligated to fulfill it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Tamattu' and there is not with him what he could buy a sacrificial animal (hady) with. So when he fasts three days during the Hajj, he becomes financially able (easier). Should he buy a sacrificial animal and sacrifice it, or should he leave that and fast seven days when he returns to his family? He (peace be upon him) said: He should buy a sacrificial animal and sacrifice it, and the fasting which he had fasted becomes optional (nafl) for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raised it (to the Imam). Regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever does not find (an animal) should fast for three days during the Hajj and seven when he returns; these ten are complete.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Its completion is the completion of the sacrificial animal.'

One of our companions, from Ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Karkhi, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'The one performing Tamattu' arrives and has no sacrificial animal with him. Should he fast for as long as it is not obligatory upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should be patient until the Day of Sacrifice. If he does not find (one), then he is from those who could not find (one).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ritual bath (ghusl) when one visits the House (Kaaba) from Mina, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I bathe from Mina, then I visit the House.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the ghusl for Ziyarah: If a man washes at night and visits during the night with one ghusl, does that suffice him? He (peace be upon him) said: It suffices him as long as he does not incur what obligates wudu. If he incurs it, then he should repeat his ghusl at night.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is befitting for the performer of Tamattu' that he should visit the House (the Kaaba) on the Day of Sacrifice, or from its night, and he should not delay that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! A performer of Tamattu' visits the House (the Kaaba), so he performs the Tawaf of Hajj, then he performs the Tawaf of the Women (Nisa), then he performs Sa'ee.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Sa'ee does not occur except before the Tawaf of the Women.' So I said: 'Is there anything upon him (a penalty)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Sa'ee does not occur except before the Tawaf of the Women.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And let them go round the Ancient House.' He said: 'The obligatory circumambulation is the circumambulation of the women.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And let them fulfill their vows and let them go round the Ancient House.' He said: 'The Tawaaf of the women.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Had it not been for what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed upon the people of the 'Tawaaf of the Women', the man would have returned to his wife, and his wife would not have been permissible to him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the eunuchs and the aged women, is the Tawaaf of the women upon them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the Tawaaf is upon all of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' (the final circumambulation) until he had intercourse with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: Women are not permissible for him until he visits the House (performs Tawaf al-Nisa'). And he (peace be upon him) said: He should be ordered to have it performed on his behalf, if he does not perform Hajj again. But if he dies before Tawaf is performed on his behalf, then his guardian or someone else should perform it on his behalf.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman performing Tamattu' who performs Tawaf by the House and by As-Safa and Al-Marwa for the Hajj, then returns to Mina before she performs Tawaf of the House. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Does she not visit the House?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let her perform Tawaf.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Sama'ah, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who performed the Tawaf of Hajj and the Tawaf al-Nisa before performing Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. So he said: 'It does not harm him; he performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and he is free from his Hajj.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not spend the nights of Al-Tashreeq except in Mina. So if you spend the nights in other than it, then upon you is blood (of a sacrificial animal). And if you leave on the first night, the middle of the night should not pass for you unless you are in Mina, unless your occupation is with your rituals, or you have left from Makkah. And if you leave after the middle of the night, it does not harm you if you see the morning in other than it. He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about a man who visited (the Kaaba) in the evening. So he did not cease to perform his Tawaf, supplicate, and perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, until the dawn emerged. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him. He was in the obedience of Allah.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Ziyarah (visiting the Kaaba) from Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he visits during the day or in the evening, he must not see the dawn break except while he is in Mina. And if he visits after midnight and approaches dawn, there is no harm if the dawn breaks while he is in Mecca.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of our companions, Regarding a man who visits the House (Kabah), so he sleeps in the road, he said: ‘If he spent the night in Makkah, then upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal); but if it was such that he had exited from it, then there is nothing upon him, and even if in the morning he is in besides Mina’. And in another report from Abul Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who visits (the Kabah) but he sleeps in besides Mina, he said: ‘When he exceeds Aqaba Al-Medinayn, then there is no problem if he sleeps’.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the pilgrim departs from Mina, so he exits from Mecca, and passes the houses of Mecca, then he sleeps, then it becomes morning before he comes to Mina, then there is nothing upon him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Do not enter your houses in Makkah when you are performing Ziyarah (visiting the Kaaba) — meaning the inhabitants of Makkah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to Makkah during the days of Mina, after finishing the visitation of the House, then he performs Tawaf of the House voluntarily. He said: 'Staying in Mina is superior and more beloved to me (peace be upon him).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the visitation after the visitation of Hajj during the days of Tashreeq, so he said: 'No'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And mention Allah during the numbered days.' He said: 'The Takbeer (exclaiming Allahu Akbar) is during the Days of Tashreeq, from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer on the third day. And in the cities (AmSar), [it is for] ten prayers. So when the people leave after the first [day], the people of the cities cease [the Takbeer], and whoever stays in Mina and prays Dhuhr and Asr there, let him exclaim Takbeer.'

Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The Takbeer during the days of Tashreeq is at the end of the prayers.' He said: 'The Takbeer in Mina is at the end of fifteen prayers; and in the other cities, it is at the end of ten prayers.' And the first Takbeer is at the end of the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), saying in it: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illa Allahu wa Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahi al-hamd. Allahu Akbar 'ala ma hadana, Allahu Akbar 'ala ma razaqana min bahimat al-an'am.' And it was made to be in the other cities at the end of ten prayers because when the people leave in the first departure, the people of the cities withhold from the Takbeer, and the people of Mina continue to Takbeer as long as they are in Mina until the final departure.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And mention Allah during the numbered days.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'These are the days of Al-Tashreeq. When they stayed in Mina after the sacrifice, they would boast, and one of them would say, 'My father used to do such and such.' So Allah, Majestic is His Praise, said: 'Then when you depart from Arafat, mention Allah as you mentioned your fathers, or with a greater mention.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the Takbeer is: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. Allah is the Greatest. And for Allah is the Praise. Allah is the Greatest upon what He has guided us. Allah is the Greatest upon what He has graced us with from the beasts of the livestock.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Takbeer during the days of Tashreeq is from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Asr prayer of the last day of Tashreeq, if you stay in Mina; and if you leave, there is no Takbeer upon you. And the Takbeer is that you say: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. And to Allah belongs the praise. Allah is the Greatest for what He guided us [to]. Allah is the Greatest for what He provided us from the beasts of grazing livestock. And the praise is to Allah for what He tried us with.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who missed one cycle (rak'ah) with the Imam from the prayer during the days of al-Tashreeq. He said: He completes his prayer, then he says Takbeer. And I asked him about the Takbeer after each prayer, so he said: As many as you wish, for it is not a fixed number, meaning regarding the speech.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The inhabitants of Mecca, when they visit the House and enter their houses, complete (the prayer), and when they do not enter their houses, shorten (the prayer).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the people of Makkah, when they depart as pilgrims, they shorten (their prayers), and when they visit (the Kaaba) and return to their homes, they complete (their prayers).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Pray in the Masjid al-Khief, and it is the Masjid of Mina, and it was the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in his era, by the minaret that is in the middle of the Masjid, and above it towards the Qiblah approximately thirty cubits, and to its right, and to its left, and behind it, approximately to that extent. So investigate that location, and if you are able to make your place of prayer within it, then do so, for indeed a thousand Prophets have prayed in it; and it is named 'al-Khief' because it is elevated from the valley, and whatever is elevated from it is called 'Khief'.

Muawiya ibn 'Ammar said, I said to Abu Abdullah (to him), 'The people of Makkah complete the prayer at 'Arafat.' He said, 'Woe to them' or 'Woe be upon them! And which journey is more difficult than it? No, they do not complete (the prayer).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Pray six cycles of prayer in the Masjid of Mina at the base of the minaret.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We want to hasten the travel, and it was the night of departure when I asked him, so at which hour should we depart?' So he said to me: 'As for the second day, do not depart until the sun declines, and it was the night of departure.' And as for the third day, when the sun whitens (rises fully), then depart upon the Blessings of Allah. So whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him. Had He remained silent [about the latter part], no one would have remained except that he would have hastened, but He said: 'and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Faraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I asked him, 'Can a man send forward his tent and his luggage before the departure?' So he said: 'No, does he not fear that the one who sends forward his luggage that Allah the Exalted may withhold him?' He said: 'But he can leave behind whatever he desires, [provided he] does not enter it into Makkah.' I said, 'So if I hasten due to forgetfulness, fulfilling my rituals, and I quicken with it, beginning and the freeing [from Ihram]?' So he said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you intend to depart during the two days, it is not permissible for you to depart until the sun declines; and if you delay until the last of the days of Tashreeq, which is the final day of departure, there is no blame upon you regarding which hour you depart and cast the stones, whether before or after midday. So when you depart and reach Al-Hasbah, which is Al-Bat'ha, if you wish to stay a little, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father would stay there, then mount and enter Makkah without having slept in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, and from Hammad, from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who hastens during the two days, so he should not depart until the sun declines. So if evening overtakes him, he should spend the night and not depart.
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Imam prays the Dhuhr prayer on the day of departure in Mecca.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem if the man departs during the first departure, then he stays in Makkah.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you depart during the first departure, then if you wish to stay in Makkah and spend the night in it, there is no problem with that. He said, and he said: When the night comes after the first departure, so spend the night in Mina, and it is not for you to leave it until you reach the morning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, who said: I wrote to him that our companions have differed regarding us, so some of them said that the departure on the last day after midday is superior, and some of them said before midday. So he wrote: Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Dhuhr and Asr in Mecca, and that could not happen unless he had departed before midday?

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Suleiman ibn Abu Zaynab, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father was saying: 'If there was a road for me to my house from Mina, I would not enter Makkah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, altogether from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked my father, after he had departed from the Station (Mina), 'Do you think Allah will disappoint all of them?' My father said, 'No one stands at this Station except that Allah forgives him, whether he be a believer or an infidel, except that their forgiveness is upon three stations.' As for the believer: Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin and what will follow, and frees him from the Fire. And that is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' Those will have a portion of what they have earned, and Allah is Swift in Reckoning. And among them is one whom Allah forgives what preceded of his sin, and it is said to him: 'Improve in what remains of your life.' And that is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then whoever hastens [departure] in two days - there is no sin upon him; and whoever remains behind - there is no sin upon him.' Meaning: the one who dies before he departs, so there is no sin upon him; and the one who delays, so there is no sin upon him, for the one who fears the major sins. As for the general Muslims, they say: 'The one who hastens in the two days, so there is no sin upon him,' meaning in the first departure; and 'the one who delays, so there is no sin upon him,' meaning for the one who fears hunting. Do you not see that Allah prohibits hunting after He permitted it in His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And when you have completed the rites, then hunt'? And in the interpretation of the general Muslims, its meaning is: 'And when you have completed the rites, then fear hunting.' And as for the infidel who stands at this Station [for] the adornment of the worldly life: Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin if he repents from polytheism in what remains of his life; and if he does not repent, He pays him in full his reward and does not deprive him of the reward of this Station. And that is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment - We will pay them in full [the price of] their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived [there

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Al-Mustaneer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He who has intercourse with women while in his state of Ihram, it is not for him to depart in the first departure. And in another report, (he said): 'Hunting as well.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Ismā'īl ibn Najīḥ al-Rammāḥ who said: We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina on one of the nights, so he said: 'What are these people saying regarding [the verse] So whoever hastens [his departure] in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, indeed there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, indeed there is no sin upon him for the one who fears [God]. It is for you all, and the people are the multitude, and you are the pilgrims.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Abbad Imran ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whilst my father (peace be upon him) and I were in the tawaf, a very tall man (sharjab) from among the men approached. I asked: 'What is a sharjab, may God set you right?' He said: 'A tall one.' He then said: 'Peace be upon you,' and he inserted his head between me and my father. He said: So my father and I turned toward him and we returned his greeting. Then he said: 'I wish to ask you, may God have mercy on you.' My father said to him: 'We shall complete our tawaf, then you may ask me.' When my father completed the tawaf, we entered al-Hijr and prayed two rak'as. Then he turned and said: 'Where is the man, O my son?' And there he was, behind him, having already prayed. He said: 'From where is the man?' He said: 'From the people of Syria.' He said: 'And from which of the people of Syria?' He said: 'From those who dwell in Jerusalem.' He said: 'Have you read the two Books?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Ask about whatever comes to you.' So he said: 'I ask you about the origin of this House, and about His words: Nun, and the Pen and what they write [68:1], and about His words: And those in whose wealth there is a known right for the one who asks and for the deprived [70:24-25].' He said: 'O brother of the people of Syria, hear our hadith and do not lie against us. For whoever lies against us in anything has lied against the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and whoever lies against the Messenger of God has lied against God, and whoever lies against God, God the Mighty and Majestic will punish him. As for the origin of this House: God, Blessed and Exalted, said to the Angels: I am going to place a vicegerent on earth [2:30]. The Angels responded to God the Mighty and Majestic, saying: Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood? So He turned away from them. They saw that as a sign of His anger, so they sought refuge at His Throne. So God commanded an Angel from the Angels to build for Him a house in the sixth heaven, called al-Durrah, opposite His Throne. He designated it for the inhabitants of the heavens; seventy thousand Angels circumambulate it every day, never returning (again), and seeking forgiveness. So when Adam descended to the lowest heaven, He commande

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: I was with my father in al-Hijr. While he was standing in prayer, a man came to him and sat beside him. When he finished, he greeted him, then said: I ask you about three things that none knows except you and one other man. He said: What are they? He said: Inform me, what was the cause of the circumambulation (tawaf) of this House? So he said: When God Mighty and Majestic commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam (peace be upon him), they objected to Him. They said: [2:30] Will You place therein one who makes mischief and sheds blood, while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You? God Blessed and Exalted said: I know what you do not know. So He became angered at them. Then they beseeched Him for repentance, so He commanded them to circumambulate al-Durah — and it is the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Oft-Frequented House) — and they remained circumambulating it for seven years and seeking forgiveness from God Mighty and Majestic for what they had said. Then He turned to them with mercy after that and was pleased with them. This was the origin of the circumambulation. Then God made the Sacred House (Ka'ba) facing al-Durah as repentance for those among the Children of Adam who sin, and as purification for them. And he said: You have spoken the truth.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Nothing is slaughtered in Makkah except the camel, the cow, the sheep, and the chicken.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whatever of the birds arrays (its wings in flight), so it is not for you to take it out (from the Haram), and whatever does not array (its wings in flight), so it is for you to take it out. He said, 'And I asked him about the Ethiopian chicken (Turkey).' He said, 'It is not from the game (hunted birds). Rather, the game is what flies between the sky and the earth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was present, about the Ethiopian chicken (Turkey), that it is brought out from the Haram. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not fly on its own.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibrahim ibn Shayba, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about completing the prayer in the two Sanctuaries. So he wrote to me: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to love increasing prayer in the two Sanctuaries, so increase in them and complete (do not shorten).'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer and fasting in the two Sanctuaries, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Complete them, even if it is one prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about shortening (the prayer) in Makkah, so he said: 'Complete it, and it is not obligatory, except that I love for you what I love for myself.'
Yunus from Ziyad ibn Marwan said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer in the two Sanctuaries, so he said: I love for you what I love for myself – complete the prayer.
Yunus narrated from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), that among the treasures preserved is the completion of prayer in the two Sanctuaries.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'When we enter Makkah and Al-Medina, do we complete (the prayer) or shorten (it)?' He said, 'If you shorten, that is it; and if you complete, it is better and increases (in reward).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'a from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Misma'a from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: My father used to view for these two Harams what he did not view for other than these two, and he was saying: 'The completion (of prayer) in them is from the matters of the preserved treasures'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali bin Mahziyar, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that the reports have differed from your forefathers (peace be upon him) regarding the complete [prayer] and the shortening in the two Harams. So, from these is that one should complete the prayer, even if it is just one [rak'ah], and from these is that one should shorten for as long as one does not intend to stay for ten days. And I did not cease to be upon the complete [prayer] therein until we commenced with our Hajj in this year of ours. So, the jurists of our companions advised me with the shortening when I did not intend staying for ten days. So I came to be shortening, and have been distressed by that, until I recognize your view. So he wrote to me in his own handwriting: 'I have taught you, may Allah have Mercy on you, the merits of the prayer in the two Harams over the other places, therefore I love for you that when you enter these two, that you should not shorten, and frequently pray the prayer in these two Harams'. So I said to him orally, after two years, 'I wrote to you with such and such, and you answered me with such and such'. So he said: 'Yes'. I said, 'Which thing did you mean by the two Harams?' So he said: 'Makkah and Al-Medina'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the most superior place in the Masjid to be prayed in. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Hateem, what is between the Stone and the Door of the House.' I said, 'And that which follows that in superiority?' So he mentioned that it was by the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). I said, 'Then which (spot) follows it in superiority?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By the Stone.' I said, 'Then which (spot) follows that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Every (spot) that is closest to the House.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Ubayda, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is prayer in the entire Haram (Sacred Precinct) the same?' He said, 'O Abu Ubayda! Is prayer in the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) all the same? So how can it be the same in the entire Haram?' I said, 'So which part of it is most superior?' He said, 'That which is between the Door and the Black Stone.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Multazam: 'For which thing is it adhered to, and which thing is mentioned therein?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By it is a river from the rivers of Paradise, in which are cast the deeds of the servants, every Thursday.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Kahili, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Frequent the prayer and supplication in this mosque. Indeed, for every servant there is sustenance to which he is allowed access within a specific measure.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Salama, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The prayer in the Sacred Masjid is equivalent to one hundred thousand prayers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The prayer in the Sacred Masjid equals one hundred thousand prayers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I stand and pray in Mecca, and a woman is seated in front of me, or passes by.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem. Rather, it was named Bakkah because therein men and women wail (or weep/cry out).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: Al-Tayyar said to him, and I was present, 'This, which is increased, is it from the Masjid?' So he said: 'Yes, they have not yet reached the remoteness of the Masjid of Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from Zurara, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who prays in Mecca, placing the Maqam (Station of Ibrahim) behind his back while he is facing the Qiblah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm. He may pray wherever he wishes in the Masjid, either in front of the Maqam or behind it. The most superior of these spots is Al-Hateem, and Al-Hijr, and by the Maqam. And Al-Hateem is parallel to the Door (of the Ka'bah).'

Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The right (boundary) of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in Makkah was between Al-Hazwarah and Al-Mas'a. That is which was the line of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), meaning the Masjid.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who prays in congregation in his house in Makkah, is it superior or (him praying) alone in the Sacred Masjid? So he said: 'Alone'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah, from Muawiya, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-Hateem, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is what is between the Black Stone and the Door.' And I asked him (peace be upon him), 'Why has Al-Hateem been named as such?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because the people squash (hatam) each other over there.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Khalid, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: My father used to say: 'The one entering the Ka'bah enters, and Allah is Pleased with him, and he exits having been neutralized from the sins.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about entering the Ka'bah. He said: 'Entering it is entering into the Mercy of Allah, and exiting from it is exiting from the sins. He is preserved (sinless) regarding what remains of his lifetime, and forgiven for him whatever preceded of his sins.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the Ka'bah. He said: 'Between the two pillars, stand upon the red marble slab, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed upon it. Then he turned towards the corners of the House and pronounced Takbeer towards each corner from it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, Ammar, who said: I saw the Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) enter the Kaaba, so he prayed two cycles upon the red marble slab. Then he stood and faced the wall between the Yemeni corner and the Western corner, so his hand fell upon it and adhered to it, and he supplicated. Then he moved to the Yemeni corner, so he adhered to it and supplicated. Then he went to the Western corner, then he went out.

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is necessary for the first-timer (al-sarura) to enter the House before he returns. So when you enter it, enter it with tranquility and dignity. Then go to every one of its corners. Then say: 'O Allah, indeed You said, "And whoever enters it shall be secure," so secure me from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.' And pray between the two pillars that are adjacent to the red marble slab. And if the people are numerous, face each corner from your place where you prayed. And supplicate to Allah and ask Him.

And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was exiting from the Ka'bah, and he was saying: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,' until he had said it three times. Then he said: 'O Allah, do not overwhelm our afflictions, O our Lord, and do not let our enemies gloat over us, for indeed You are the One who causes harm and confers benefit.' Then he descended and prayed beside the stairs, placing the stairs on his left, facing the Ka'bah, with no one between him and it. Then he went out to his house.

And from him, from Ismail ibn Hammam who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) entered the Kaaba, so he prayed in its four corners; he prayed two cycles in each corner.'

And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) enter the Ka'bah, then intended to be between the two pillars, but was not able to do so, so he prayed beside it. Then he exited and went until he had left the Masjid.

And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When I enter the Ka'bah, what should I do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hold the two rings of the door when you enter, then proceed until you reach the two pillars, so offer prayer upon the red marble. Then, when you exit from the House, and descend from the stairs, offer two cycles of prayer on your right.'

And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, regarding the supplication for the child. He said: Pour upon yourself a bucket from the water of Zamzam, then enter the House. So when you stand at the door of the House, take the ring of the door, then say: 'O Allah, the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and You have said: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure', therefore secure me from Your punishment, and rescue me from Your wrath.' Then enter the House, so perform two rak'at of prayer upon the red marble slab. Then stand before the pillar which is opposite the Stone, and press your chest against it, then say: 'O One, O the Alone, O the Glorious, O the Near, O the Remote, O the Mighty, O the Wise, Do not leave me alone, and You are the Best of inheritors, Endow to me from Yourself a goodly offspring. You are the Hearer of the supplication.' Then circle by the pillar, and press your back and belly against it, and supplicate with this supplication. So if Allah wills something, it will happen.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you intend to leave Mecca and go to your family, bid farewell to the House, and perform Tawaf around the House for seven circuits. If you are able to touch the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner in each circuit, do so; otherwise, begin with it and end with it. If you cannot do that, then it is permissible for you to do what you can. Then go to the Mustajar (the spot where the door opens into the House) and do there as you did on the day you arrived in Mecca, and choose for yourself from the supplications. Then touch the Black Stone, then press your belly against the House, placing one hand on the Stone and the other on what is near the door. Praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then say: 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, Your Messenger, Your Prophet, Your Trustworthy, Your Beloved, Your Confidant, and Your Chosen one from Your creation. O Allah, as he delivered Your messages, and strove in Your way, and proclaimed Your command, and was harmed for Your sake, and worshipped You until certainty came to him.' O Allah, turn me back successful, victorious, answered for me with the best of what any of Your delegates returns with, from forgiveness, blessing, mercy, pleasure, and well-being. O Allah, if You cause me to die, forgive me; and if You keep me alive, grant me it next year. O Allah, do not make this the last visit to Your House. O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, and son of Your maid. You carried me on Your beasts and journeyed me through Your lands until You brought me to Your Sanctuary and Your security. And it was in my good opinion of You that You would forgive my sins. So if You have already forgiven my sins, increase Your pleasure with me and bring me close to You in position, and do not distance me. And if You have not forgiven me, then from now on, forgive me before my home departs from Your House. For this is the time of my departure, if You have permitted me, not turning away from You nor from Your House, nor being replaced by You nor by it. O Allah, protect me from before me, behind me, to my right, and to my left, until You bring me to my family. So whe

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) bid farewell to the House. So when he wanted to exit from the door of the Masjid, he fell prostrate. Then he stood up, faced the Ka'bah, and said: 'O Allah, I return upon that there is no god except You.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the year two hundred and twenty-five, bidding farewell to the House after the sun had risen, and performing Tawaf of the House, touching the Yamani Corner during each circuit. So when it was the seventh circuit, he touched it and touched the Stone, and wiped with his hand, then wiped his face with his hand. Then he went to the Maqam (Standing Place of Ibrahim), so he performed two cycles of Salat behind it. Then he went out to the back of the Ka'bah, to the Multazam, so he adhered to the House, and uncovered the cloth from his belly, then paused upon it for a long time, supplicating. Then he went out from the door of al-Hannatayn and faced it. He said, So I also saw him in the year two hundred and seventeen bidding farewell to the House at night, touching the Yamani Corner and the Black Stone during each circuit. So when he was in the seventh circuit, he adhered to the House at the back of the Ka'bah, near to the Yamani Corner, and above the elongated Stone, and uncovered the cloth from his belly. Then he went to the Stone, so he kissed it, and wiped it, and went to the Maqam, so he performed Salat behind it. Then he went and did not return to the House. And his pausing at the Multazam was of a measurement of what some of our companions take to perform Tawaf of seven circuits, and some of them eight.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Abu Ismail, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Behold, I am about to exit. May I be your ransom! From where should I bid farewell to the House?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go to Al-Mustajar between the Stone and the Door, and bid farewell from there. Then go out, and drink from Zamzam. Then depart.' So I said, 'Should I pour [water] upon my head?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not go near the pouring.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Ya'qub ibn Yazeed, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Qutham ibn Ka'b, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You are accustomed to performing Hajj.' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let your final promise/covenant with the House be that you place your hand upon the Door and say: 'The beggar is at Your Door, so give in charity upon him with Paradise.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Muawiya ibn Ammar and Hafs ibn Al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: It is befitting for the pilgrim, when he has completed his rituals and intends to depart, to buy dates with a dirham to give in charity, so that it serves as an expiation for whatever may have entered upon him during his Hajj, such as scratching or lice falling off, or similar to that.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you intend to leave Mecca, buy dates with a dirham and give them in charity, handful by handful, so that it serves as expiation for whatever was from you during your ihram and whatever was from you in Mecca.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man performs Istimta' with the Umrah, he has fulfilled what was upon him from the obligatory Umrah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Umrah, 'Is it obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So the one who performs Tamattu', would it suffice him from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'In every month is an Umra'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'In every month is an Umra'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Makkah during the year, once, or twice, or four times, what should he do? He (peace be upon him) said: When he enters, let him enter while reciting the Talbiyyah; and when he exits, let him exit while being free from Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: And for every month there is an Umrah. So I said, Can it be less? He (peace be upon him) said: For every ten days there is an Umrah. Then he (peace be upon him) said: By your right, I have performed six Umras in this year of mine. I said, Why is that so? He (peace be upon him) said: I was with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim in Al-Ta'if, so every time he entered, I entered with him.
