A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the exclusive Umrah during the months of Hajj. Then he can return to his family.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the exclusive Umrah during the months of Hajj. Then he returns to his family, if he wills.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar Al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who went out during the months of Hajj to perform Umra, then he returned to his country. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; and even if he performed Hajj in that year, and performed exclusive Hajj, so there is no blood (of a sacrificial animal) upon him, for Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) went out to Iraq one day before Al-Tarwiyya, and he had entered to perform Umra.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'From where does the distinction lie between the Mutamatti' and the Mu'tamir?' He said: 'The Mutamatti' is bound to the Hajj, and the Mu'tamir, when he is free from it, goes wherever he wishes. And Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) performed Umra in Dhi al-Hijjah, then he departed on the Day of Tarwiyah to Iraq, while the people were departing to Mina. And there is no harm in performing Umra in Dhi al-Hijjah for one who does not intend Hajj.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'It has reached us that an Umrah in the month of Ramadan equals a Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That was only regarding a woman to whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had promised [a reward]. So he (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Perform Umrah in the month of Ramadan, so it is for you a Hajj.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who said: I was staying in Al-Madina during the month of Ramadan in the year two hundred and thirteen. So when Eid al-Fitr approached, I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about whether going out for an Umrah during the month of Ramadan is superior, or staying until the month ends and I complete my fasting. He wrote to me a letter which I read in his own handwriting: 'You asked, may Allah have mercy on you, which Umrah is superior? An Umrah during the month of Ramadan is superior. May Allah have mercy on you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Isa al-Farra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When one commences the Umrah with Ihram in Rajab and exits Ihram in another month, his Umrah is for Rajab; and when he commences in a month other than Rajab and performs Tawaf in Rajab, his Umrah is for Rajab.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when he intended to perform the 'Umrah, would wait until the morning of the twenty-third of the month of Ramadan, then he would go out commencing (the 'Umrah) during that day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who entered into Ihram in one month and freed from it in another, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is recorded for him according to what he intended, or it is recorded for him according to the superior of the two.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one performing 'Umra may perform 'Umra in whichever month of the year he desires, and the most superior 'Umra is the 'Umra of Rajab.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassha from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'The Umrah performed after the Hajj.' He said, 'When the razor enables [shaving] the head.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Murazam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The performer of the exclusive Umra cuts off the Talbiyya when the camel places its hooves in the Haram.
Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Talbiyah of the Mu'tamir is cut off when he enters the Haram.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever performs Umrah from Al-Tan'eem, let him not cut off the Talbiyya until he looks at the Masjid.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the performer of Umra arrives in Makkah and performs Tawaf and Sa'ee, if he wishes, let him proceed upon his mount and let him join his family.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskaan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Umrah of the one who is tested (or: the Umrah performed with a specific condition/ruling) — he performs Tawaf by the House (Kaaba), and by Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, then he frees himself from Ihram. So if he desires to depart from that moment, he departs.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who comes performing Umrah, the exclusive Umrah. He (peace be upon him) said: It suffices him if he performs Tawaf around the House, and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and shaves (his head), that he performs one Tawaf around the House; and whoever wishes to shorten (his hair), he shortens.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Umar or someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The performer of the Umra performs Tawaf, then Sa'ee, then shaves (his head). He (peace be upon him) said: And it is necessary for him, after the shaving, to perform another Tawaf.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Ismail ibn Riyah, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the performer of the exclusive Umrah, is there Tawaf Al-Nisa upon him? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa who said: Abu al-Qasim Mukhallad ibn Musa al-Razi wrote to the man (Imam), asking him about the Umrah al-Mabtulah: Is the Tawaf al-Nisa upon its performer? And the Umrah which one performs with Tamattu' to the Hajj? So he wrote: As for the Umrah al-Mabtulah, then upon its performer is the Tawaf al-Nisa; and as for the one which is performed with Tamattu' to the Hajj, then there is not upon its performer the Tawaf al-Nisa.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you are in the state of freedom (not in Ihram), and you kill game in the open land between Al-Bareed and the Sanctuary, then upon you is its compensation. So if you blind its eye, or break its horn, or wound it, you give charity.

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who was gifted a domesticated dove while he was in the Haram (sanctuary). He said: If he kills something from it, let him give in charity the price of it, approximately equal to what it was worth in value.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hakam, who said: I said to a slave of ours, 'Prepare lunch for us.' So he took birds from the Haram, slaughtered them, and cooked them. So I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Bury them, and pay the expiation for each of these birds.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the game hunted in the unrestricted area (Al-Hill), then it is brought to the Sanctuary (Al-Haram) while it is alive. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he brings it into the Sanctuary, it becomes prohibited for him to eat it and to keep it. Therefore, do not buy in the Sanctuary except what has been slaughtered in the unrestricted area, then brought to the Sanctuary already slaughtered; there is no problem with the permissible (animals).'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, that Al-Hakam asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who was gifted a dove inside the Al-Haram, clipped (of feathers). So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Take it and be good to it, and feed it until when its feathers are complete (grown back), so free its way'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Muthanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Karib al-Sayrafi, who said: We were a group who bought a bird, so we clipped its wings and entered Mecca with it. The people of Mecca faulted that upon us. So Karib sent to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him, so he said: 'Entrust it to a Muslim man from the people of Mecca, or a Muslim woman. So when its wings grow straight (are restored), free its way.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever hits a bird inside the Sanctuary while he is free (not in Ihram), upon him is the price, and the price is one Dirham, which he uses to buy feed for the doves of the Sanctuary.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Khallad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who slaughtered a dove from the doves of the Sanctuary (Al-Haram): He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the expiation.' I said: 'So can he eat it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'Can he throw it away?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then there would be another expiation upon him.' I said: 'So what should he do with it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should bury it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who went out with a bird from Makkah to Al-Kufa. He said: 'He should return it to Makkah'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the dove, one dirham, and regarding the fledgling, half a dirham, and regarding the egg, a quarter of a dirham.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about a man who caught a bird in the unrestricted area (al-Hill), bought it, and brought it into the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and it died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If, when he brought it into the Sanctuary, he released its way (let it go free) and it died, then there is nothing upon him; and if he kept it until it died with him inside the Sanctuary, then upon him is the expiation (fidyah).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who hunted game in the open land (al-hill), and it went due to his hunting until it entered the Sanctuary (al-haram), and it died. Is the compensation upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: No, there is no compensation upon him, because he hunted where he hunted, and it was permissible for him. Rather, the example of that is the example of a man who set a snare in the open land next to the Sanctuary, and game fell into it, and the game struggled until it entered the Sanctuary. Thus, there is no compensation upon him, because it was something that happened afterwards. So I said: This is the analogy (qiyas) in the presence of the people. So he (peace be upon him) said: Rather, I compared for you a thing with a thing.

Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ziyad, Abu al-Hasan al-Wasiti, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a group who locked the door upon a bird from the doves of the Haram, so it died. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon them is the price of each bird, half a dirham, by which the doves of the Haram are fed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Misma' ibn Abdul Malik, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who was in Ihram inside the Haram, he shot a prey outside the Haram and killed it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the compensation, because the injury came to it from the Haram.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who shot a prey outside the Haram in the unrestricted area (Hill). So the prey survived until it entered the Haram. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Its flesh is prohibited, like the dead meat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying regarding the domesticated birds of Makkah, which are not the doves of the Sanctuary: 'Whoever slaughters a bird from them while he is not in Ihram, then upon him is that he gives in charity an amount superior to its price. And if he was in Ihram, then a sheep for each bird.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I sent a message to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that a brother of mine had bought doves from Al-Medina, so we went with them to Makkah. So we performed Umrah and we stayed until the Hajj. Then we brought out the doves along with us, from Makkah to Al-Kufa. So is there anything upon us with regards to that? He (peace be upon him) said to the messenger: 'I think they were delightful (for food). He should slaughter a sheep in place of each bird.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man plucked a dove from the doves of the Sanctuary.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give charity to a poor person, and he should give with the very hand with which he plucked it, for it has caused it pain.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A slaughtered bird was gifted to us in Makkah, so our family ate it.' He said, 'The people of Makkah do not see any problem with it.' I said, 'So what do you say?' He said, 'Upon them is its price (penalty).'

One of our companions, from Abu Jareer Al-Qummi, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We buy hawks and enter them into the Haram, so is that permissible for us?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything from the birds that enters the Haram, from those that array their wings, has entered into its safety, so free its way.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazeed ibn Khaleefa, who said: There was by the side of my house a basket containing two eggs from the doves of the Haram. The boy went to overturn the basket, not knowing that there were two eggs in it, so he broke them. I went out and met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and mentioned that to him, so he said: 'Give in charity two handfuls of fine flour.' He said: Then I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) afterwards and informed him, so he said: 'The price of two birds, to feed the doves of the Haram with it.' I met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and informed him, so he said: 'He spoke the truth. Narrate with it, for rather, he took it from his forefathers.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two chickens that were fattened, which I slaughtered while I was in Makkah. So he said to me: 'Why did you slaughter them?' I said: 'A slave girl from the people of Makkah came to me with them and asked me to slaughter them, so I thought I was in al-Kufa and did not remember the Sanctuary (al-Haram).' So he said: 'Upon you is their price.' I said: 'How much is their price?' He said: 'One dirham, and it is better than them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazalah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Makkah, and Dawud ibn Ali was with us. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Dawud ibn Ali said to me, What do you say, O Abu Abdillah, regarding the dove we hunted and clipped (its wings)? I said: 'It is plucked and fed. When it is straight (wings grown back), it is freed.'

Ahmad, from Al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about an ostrich egg which I ate in the Al-Haram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give in charity with its price'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Muthanna, who said: We went out to Makkah, so the women caught a dove from the doves of Amaj when we reached Al-Bareed. So the women plucked out its wings. Then they entered Makkah with it. So Abu Baseer went over to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look around for a woman not having a problem with her, so give the bird to her to look after it and keep it. When its wings are straight (grown back), she should free it'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Imran al-Halby, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is disliked from the birds?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which arrays its wings hovering upon your head'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed al-Attar, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man kills a lion inside the Haram (sanctuary).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a ram to be slaughtered.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding a man who caught an antelope in the unrestricted area (al-Hill), so he bought it and brought it into the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and the antelope died in the Sanctuary. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If when he brought it into the Sanctuary he freed its way (so it could leave) and it died, then there is nothing upon him; and if he kept it until it died with him in the Sanctuary, then upon him is the expiation (fidyah).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether, from Ibn Abi Nasr, who said: Hamza bin al-Yasa informed me, saying: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the leopard that was bought in Mina and taken out of the Haram. He said: 'Everything from the predatory wild animals that enters the Haram in captivity, you must take it out.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a tree, the root of which is in the Haram (sanctuary) and its branches are in the Hil (unrestricted area). A bird was on one of its branches; a man threw [a stone] at it and felled it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is its compensation, when its root is in the Haram.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik bin Atiyya, from Abdul A'ala bin Ayn, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who caught prey in the unrestricted area (al-Hill), so he tied it to the side of the Sanctuary (al-Haram). The prey went with its tie until it entered the Sanctuary, with the tie around its neck. The man pulled it with his rope until he brought it out of the Sanctuary, while the man himself was in the unrestricted area. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Its price and its flesh are prohibited, like the dead animal.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ahmad ibn Abi Ali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding a man who performed an exclusive Umrah, so he slept with his wife while he was in Ihram, before he finished his Tawaf and Saee. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is a camel for the spoiling of his Umrah, and upon him is that he stays in Makkah until another month enters, so he goes out to one of the Miqat points, enters Ihram from it, then performs Umrah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who performs an Umrat al-Mufradah, and he performs the Tawaf of the House as the obligatory Tawaf, then he has intercourse with his wife before he performs Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has spoiled his Umrah, and upon him is a camel (as expiation), and he stays in Makkah free from Ihram until the month in which he performed Umrah passes, then he goes out to the time which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated for the people of his country, so he enters Ihram from it and performs Umrah.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zurara who said: The one who brings a sacrificial animal for an Umrah without performing Hajj, let him sacrifice it before he shaves his head.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The performer of the 'Umra, when he ushers the sacrificial animal, shaves (his head) before he slaughters (it).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever brings a sacrificial animal for an Umrah, let him slaughter it before he shaves (his head); and whoever brings a sacrificial animal while he is performing Umrah, he slaughters his sacrifice at the slaughter place, which is between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and this is called Al-Hazwara.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the expiation for the Umrah, where should it be?' So he said: 'In Makkah, unless he delays it to Hajj, in which case it will be in Mina, and hastening it is superior and more beloved to me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent a sacrificial animal (hady) with a group of people, and appointed a day with them when they would yoke their sacrificial animal and enter into Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is prohibited upon him what is prohibited upon the one in Ihram on the day he appointed with them, until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination.' So I said, 'What is your view if they delay in their appointed time and are slow in traveling with it? Is there blame upon him regarding the day which he appointed with them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and he is released (from Ihram) on the day which he appointed with them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who sends a sacrificial animal voluntarily, not as an obligation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He appoints a day with his companions, and they yoke it. When that time comes, he refrains from what the one in Ihram refrains from, until the Day of Sacrifice. When the Day of Sacrifice arrives, it suffices for him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Harun ibn Kharaja, who said: Indeed, Murad sent a she-camel and ordered that it be yoked and marked on such and such a day. So I said to him, 'It is befitting that he does not wear clothes.' So he sent me to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Al-Hira, and I said to him, 'Indeed, Murad did such and such, and he is unable to leave the clothes due to the status of Ziyad.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Instruct him to wear the clothes and let him slaughter a cow on the Day of Eid al-Adha on behalf of himself.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Asram ibn Hawshab, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: The valleys of the Haram (sanctuary) flow into the Hil (unrestricted area), and the valleys of the Hil do not flow into the Haram.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a corner of the Sacred Mosque, and a group of people were reciting the Talbiyyah around the Ka'bah. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you see these who are reciting the Talbiyyah? By Allah, their voices are more hateful to Allah than the voices of donkeys.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who recites the Talbiyyah for Hajj or Umrah, but does not intend the Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid, and it is not befitting for him to do so.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding these people who perform exclusive Hajj, when they arrive in Makkah and perform Tawaf of the House, they are free (from Ihram restrictions); and when they say the Talbiyyah, they enter Ihram. Thus, they remain alternating between being free and being bound until they depart to Mina without having performed Hajj nor Umrah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Hafs al-Mu'adhdhin, who said: Ismail ibn Ali led the people in Hajj in the year 140 [AH], so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) fell off his mule. Ismail paused over him, but Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Keep going, for the Imam does not pause.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Sarin, who said: I said to him, 'What do you say regarding staying in Mina after the people have departed?' He said: 'When he has fulfilled his ritual, let him stay as long as he wishes, and let him go wherever he wishes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked him in the Sacred Mosque, 'Who is the greatest of people in burden (of sin)?' He said: 'The one who stands at these two stations, Arafat and Muzdalifah, and performs Sa'ee between these two mountains, then performs Tawaf by this House, and prays behind the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), then says to himself or thinks that Allah has not forgiven him, so he is from the people with the greatest burden.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We were in his presence, and they mentioned the water on the road to Mecca and its heaviness. So he said: 'The water is not heavy unless the camel is unique with it, so there does not happen to be upon it except for the water.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who rides a mount, let him bequeath.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A Makkan person should not lead the pilgrimage season.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Kaloub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them) That Ali (peace be upon him) disliked the Hajj and Umrah to be performed upon the camels feeding on dung.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Shireh, from Ali ibn Suleyman, who said: I wrote to him asking him about the deceased who dies at Arafat, whether he should be buried at Arafat or transferred to the Haram, so which of the two is superior? So he wrote: 'Carry him to the Haram and bury him, for it is superior.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Exalted is His Praise: 'Then let them fulfill their needful acts.' He said: 'It is what happens from the man who is in his Ihram. So when he enters Makkah, so he would speak with good speech. That would be an expiation for that which was from him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who narrated to him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when Al-Qa'im (peace be upon him) arises, he will return the Sacred House to its foundation, and the Mosque of the Messenger to its foundation, and the Mosque of Kufa to its foundation. And Abu Baseer said: 'To the place of the date-sellers from the Mosque.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who exits from the two Harrams after the rising of the day, before he has offered the Zuhr and Asr prayers, is called from behind him: "May Allah not accompany you!"'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who designated his slave girl as a hady (sacrificial offering) for the Ka'bah. What should he do? He said: A man came to my father who had designated his slave girl as a hady for the Ka'bah. So he said to him: 'Evaluate the slave girl or sell her. Then instruct a caller to stand upon the Hajar al-Aswad (the Rock) and call out: 'Indeed! Whoever has insufficient funds, or has been cut off (by bandits), or whose food has run out, let him come to so-and-so, son of so-and-so!' And instruct him to give to the first one first until the price of the slave girl is depleted.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who gives birth on the Day of Arafaat, what should she do with her child? Should Tawaaf be performed on its behalf, or what should be done with it? He (peace be upon him) said: There is nothing upon it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you. I had a fat ram to slaughter as a sacrifice. So when I took it and laid it down, it looked at me, so I pitied it and was moved with compassion for it. Then I slaughtered it.' He said to me, 'I would not like you to do so. Do not raise something (for slaughter) and then slaughter it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sallam, from Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn Isam, from Dawood al-Raqqi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I had some wealth upon a man, and I feared it would be lost. So I complained to him about that. He said to me: 'When you go to Makkah, perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abdul Muttalib and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abu Talib and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abdullah and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Amina and pray two Rak'ahs on her behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Fatima bint Asad and pray two Rak'ahs on her behalf. Then supplicate that your wealth be returned to you.' He said: 'So I did that. Then I went out from the Door of Al-Safa, and there was my debtor standing there saying, 'O Dawood! You withheld me for long. Come, take possession of your wealth'.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: We were in Makkah, and high prices struck us regarding the sacrificial animals, so we bought it for one Dinar, then for two Dinars, then we could not find it for a small amount nor a large amount. So Hisham al-Mukari wrote a note to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and informed him of what we had bought, then we could not find it for a small amount nor a large amount. So he signed: 'Look at the first price, and the second, and the third, then give in charity the equivalent of a third of it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman and Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who performs Hajj on behalf of another, and he commits something during his Hajj which necessitates that he performs Hajj again in the following year, or an expiation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It (the Hajj) is complete for the first one, and upon this one is what he committed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban, from Abu al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'I gifted a slave girl to the Ka'bah and was given five hundred dinars, so what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Sell her, then take her price, then stand upon this wall, the wall of the Hijr, then call out and give to everyone who has been cut off (by bandits) and every needy one from the pilgrims.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal and Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah, from Abu Khalid Al-Qammam, from Abdul-Khaliq Al-Sayqal, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You have asked me about something which no one would ask me except for the one whom Allah so Desires to.' He said: 'The one who travels to this House (the Kaaba) and he knows that it is the House which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has Commanded with, and recognises us, the People of the Household, as it is our right to be recognised, would be safe in the world and the Hereafter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail al-Khash'i, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When we arrive in Mecca, our companions go to perform Tawaf and leave me to guard their belongings.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'You are greater than them in reward.'

By his chain, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murazam ibn Hakim, who said: I accompanied Muhammad ibn Musadif. So when we entered Medina, I fell ill. So he used to go to the Masjid and leave me alone. So I complained of that to Musadif, and he informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with it. So he (peace be upon him) sent a message to him: 'Your sitting with him is superior to your Salat in the Masjid.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sufyan ibn Ibrahim al-Jariri, from al-Harith ibn al-Haseera al-Asadi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I entered with my father to the Ka'bah, and he prayed upon the red marble slab between the two pillars. He said: 'In this place, the people made a pact: if the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) dies or is killed, they will not return this command (leadership) to anyone from his Household ever.' I said, 'And who were they?' He said: 'The first one, and the second one, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and Salim ibn al-Habibah.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Abu Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and Abu Haneefah had said to him, 'The people were astonished at you yesterday while you were at Arafat, haggling over your sacrificial camels with the most intense bargaining.' He said, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And what is the Pleasure of Allah if I am cheated in my wealth?' He said, so Abu Haneefah said, 'No, by Allah! There is little or much Pleasure of Allah in this, and we do not come to you with anything except that you come to us with what there is no way out for us from.'
Sahl, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for anyone to sit with bent knees and arms around it, facing the Ka'bah.

Sahl narrated from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ibn Abi Najran or someone else, from Hanaan, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Ka'bah complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about what it endures from the breaths of the polytheists. So Allah revealed to it: 'Be calm, O Ka'bah, for I will replace them with a people who clean themselves with the twigs of the tree.' So when Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), He revealed to him with Jibra'il (peace be upon him) the Siwak and the Khilal.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'We are in Makkah, or in Al-Madina, or Al-Heera, or the places where merit is hoped for. So, sometimes a man goes out to perform ablution, and another comes and takes his place.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who is first to a place is more rightful to it for his day and his night.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever removes a harmful obstruction from the path of Makkah, Allah writes for him a good deed; and whoever is written for him a good deed, He does not punish him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The servant does not cease to be within the limits of the circumambulation (Tawaf) by the Ka'bah for as long as the shaving of the head is upon him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Taymuli, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When it is the days of the season (Hajj), Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends angels in the forms of humans who buy the provisions of the pilgrims and the merchants. I said, 'So what do they do with it?' He said, 'They throw it into the sea.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Husayn ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Adha) is among the days in which it is fasted, and the Day of Ashura is the day in which it is not fasted.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is for the one who visits the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) purposely?' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'For him is Paradise.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hariz, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, said: Indeed, the Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Ziyarah of the graves of the martyrs, and the Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equate to having performed a Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Al-Sadusi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comes to me as a visitor, I shall be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Al-Mu'alla Abu Shihaab, who said: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O my father! What is [the reward] for the one who performs Ziyarah to you?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O my son! Whoever performs Ziyarah to me while I am alive or after I have died, or performs Ziyarah to your father, or performs Ziyarah to your brother, or performs Ziyarah to you, it is a right upon me that I visit him on the Day of Resurrection and I clear him of his sins.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman al-Daylami, from Abu Hajar al-Aslami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who comes to Makkah as a pilgrim and does not visit me in Al-Medina, I shall turn away from him on the Day of Judgement; and the one who comes to me as a visitor, my intercession is obligated for him; and the one for whom my intercession is obligated, Paradise is obligated for him.' And the one who dies in one of the two Sanctuaries, Makkah and Al-Medina, will not be exposed (to scrutiny) and will not be reckoned with; and the one who dies as an emigrant to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be resurrected on the Day of Judgement along with the companions of Badr.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The people have been commanded to come to these stones, so they perform Tawaf by them; then they should come to us, informing us of their Wilayah, and presenting to us their support.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The completion of Hajj is meeting the Imam.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yahya ibn Yasar, who said: We performed Hajj and passed by Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Hajj of the House of Allah, and Ziyarah of the grave of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the Shia of the Family of Muhammad, welcome to you!'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, from Sadeyr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Begin with Makkah and end with us.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Shall I begin with Al-Medina or with Makkah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with Makkah and end with Al-Medina, for it is superior'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter the city, perform ritual bath before entering it or when you enter it. Then go to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then stand and send greetings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then stand by the front pillar from the right side of the grave, near the head of the grave, at the corner of the grave. You are facing the Qiblah, with your left shoulder towards the grave and your right shoulder towards what faces the pulpit, for it is the place of the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And you should say: I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, without partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. And I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and I testify that you are Muhammad ibn Abdullah. And I testify that you have delivered the messages of your Lord, and advised your community, and strove in the way of Allah, and worshipped Allah sincerely until certainty (death) came to you with wisdom and goodly admonition, and you fulfilled that which was upon you from the truth. And you were kind to the believers and harsh upon the disbelievers, so Allah brought you to the highest honor of the station of the honored. Praise is to Allah who saved us through you from polytheism and misguidance. O Allah, so make Your blessings and the blessings of Your near angels, and Your righteous servants, and Your sent prophets, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and whoever glorified You, O Lord of the worlds, from the first and the last, upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger and Your Prophet and Your Trustworthy and Your Confidant and Your Beloved and Your Chosen and Your Special and Your Elite and Your Choice from Your creation. O Allah, give him the Degree and the Means in Paradise, and raise him to a Praised Station, which the first and the last will envy. O Allah, indeed You said: 'And if they, when they wronged themselves, had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful.' And I have come to Your

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Uthman ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan Musa, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon him), who said: My father, Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), would stand at the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), send greetings upon him, testify to his delivery (of the Message), and supplicate with whatever came to his mind. Then he would lean his back against the Marwah, the small, narrow green stone that faces the grave, press himself against the grave, lean his back against the grave, and face the Qiblah, saying: 'O Allah, to You I have turned my back for support, and to the grave of Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, I have leaned my back. And I have faced the Qiblah which You were pleased with for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' O Allah, I have become such that I do not possess for myself any of the good I hope for, nor do I repel from it any of the evil I fear for it. And the affairs have come to be in Your Hand, so there is no poor one poorer than I. Indeed, I am poor for whatever good You send down to me. O Allah, return me to You with goodness, for there is none who can repel Your Grace. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from my name being changed, or my body being altered, or Your Bounties being removed from me. O Allah, honor me with Taqwa (piety), adorn me with Bounties, immerse me in Al-Afiyah (health/wholeness), and grant me Shukr (gratitude) for Al-Afiyah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), 'How is the greeting to be upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at his grave?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Say, 'The greeting be upon the Messenger of Allah.' The greeting be upon you, O Beloved of Allah! The greeting be upon you, O elite of Allah! The greeting be upon you, O trustworthy one of Allah!' I testify that you preached to your community, and struggled in the Way of Allah, and worshipped Him until conviction came to you. So, may Allah recompense you with the most superior of what He would recompense a Prophet for his community. O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, superior than what You blessed upon Ibrahim and the progeny of Ibrahim, You being the Praised One, the Glorious.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) arrive at the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he placed his hand upon it and said: 'I ask Allah, Who selected you and chose you and guided you and guided (us) through you, that He should send blessings upon you.' Then he said: 'Surely Allah and His Angels send blessings upon the Prophet; O you who believe! Send blessings upon him and submit to him with a (complete) submission.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, that Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is for them to pass by Al-Medina, so they would greet upon Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from nearby, even though the Blessings do reach him (peace be upon him and his family) from afar.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about passing by at the rear of the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and not offering greetings to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) did not do that.' I said: 'So he (peace be upon him) would enter the Masjid and offer greetings from afar, not approaching the grave?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Offer greetings to him when you enter and when you exit, and from afar.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray by the side of the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and even though the prayer of the believers reaches him, from wherever they may be.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of our companions who said: I was present with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and Harun the Caliph, and Isa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Yahya, in Medina. They had come to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So Harun said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Proceed!' But he refused. So Harun proceeded, greeted, and stood to the side. And Isa ibn Ja'far said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Proceed!' But he refused. So Isa proceeded, greeted, and stood with Harun. Then Ja'far said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Proceed!' But he refused. So Ja'far proceeded, greeted, and stood with Harun. And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) proceeded, so he said: 'Peace be upon you, O my father! I ask Allah, Who chose you and selected you and guided you and guided through you, that He send blessings upon you.' So Harun said to Isa, 'Did you hear what he said?' He said, 'Yes'. So Harun said, 'I testify that he is truly his father.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished with the supplication by the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then go to the Pulpit, wipe it with your hand, and hold its two pomegranates (which are the Soflawan), and wipe your eyes and your face with them, for it is said that it is a healing for the eyes. And stand by it, so praise Allah and extol Him, and ask your need, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What is between my Pulpit and my house is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my Pulpit is upon a channel from the channels of Paradise, and the channel is the small door.' Then you go to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and pray therein whatever comes to you. So when you enter the Masjid, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And when you exit, do the same, and frequent praying in the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When it was the year forty-one, Muawiya intended to perform Hajj, so he sent a carpenter and sent the tools, and wrote to the governor of Medina that he should remove the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and make it according to the measure of his own pulpit in Syria. So when they rose to remove it, the sun was eclipsed and the earth was shaken, so they refrained and wrote about that to Muawiya. So he wrote back to them, stressing upon them to do what they were doing. So they did that, and the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is the entrance which you see.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Jameel, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That which is between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon a channel from the channels of Paradise, and the legs of my pulpit were grown in Paradise.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'Is it a garden today?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, indeed, if the cover were removed, you would see it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the boundary of the Masjid of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'From the pillar which is at the head of the grave, to the two pillars from behind the pulpit, on the right of the Qiblah; and it was so that from behind the pulpit there was a path through which the sheep could pass and the man could pass sideways, and the courtyard of the Masjid was from the tiles (al-balaat) to the courtyard (al-sahn).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The boundary of the Garden in the Masjid of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) is up to the side of the shaded area, and the boundary of the Masjid is up to the two pillars from the right of the Pulpit up to the street from what follows the night market.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Saeed, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abdul A'ala, the slave of the progeny of Saam, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How much was the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was three thousand and six hundred cubits, broken (squared).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'What is between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The house of Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them) is between the house in which is the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) up to the door which faces the alleyway, up to Al-Baqi'. He said: 'So if you were to enter from that door, and the wall is in its place, it would hit your left shoulder.' Then he named the rest of the houses. And he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Prayer in my mosque equals a thousand prayers elsewhere, except for the Sacred Mosque, for it is superior.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Hammad ibn Uthman from Al-Qasim ibn Salim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you enter from the door of Al-Baqie, the house of Ali (peace be upon him) is on your left, at the distance of a goat's passage from the door, and it is beside the house of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and their two doors are joined together.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Jameel ibn Darraj said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That which is between my pulpit and my houses is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon a channel from the channels of Paradise, and a prayer in my mosque equals a thousand prayers in what is besides it from the mosques, except for the Sacred Mosque.' Jameel said: I said to him, 'Are the houses of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the house of Ali from it?' He said: 'Yes, and superior.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu al-Samit, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A prayer in the Prophet's mosque (peace be upon him and his family) equals ten thousand prayers.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is the prayer in the house of Fatima (peace be upon her) superior, or in the Garden?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'In the house of Fatima (peace be upon her)'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umeyr, and someone else, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the prayer in the house of Fatima (peace be upon her) like the prayer in the garden?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And superior (to it).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Jahm, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), 'Which of the two is superior: staying in Makkah or staying in Al-Medina?' He said, 'What do you say?' I said, 'And what is my word compared to your word?' He said, 'Your word returns you to my word.' So I said to him, 'As for me, I claim that staying in Al-Medina is superior to staying in Makkah.' He said, 'Indeed, if you say that, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said that on the day of Fitr. He went to Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and greeted him in the Masjid, then said: 'We have been preferred over the people today by our greeting Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazam who said: I, along with Ammar and a group, entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Medina. He asked, 'What is your stay?' Ammar replied, 'We have released our backs (set out on journey) and we have been given leave for fifteen days.' He said, 'You have attained the stay in the city of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the prayer in his mosque. Work for your Hereafter and be abundant for yourselves. Indeed, a man may be clever in the world, and it will be said, 'How clever is so-and-so!', but the truly clever one is the one who is clever regarding the Hereafter.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Amr al-Zayyat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever dies in Al-Medina, Allah will resurrect him among the Secured ones on the Day of Judgement – among them are Yahya ibn Habeeb, and Abu Ubeyda al-Haza’a, and Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter the Masjid, if you are able to stay for three days—Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday—then pray between the grave and the pulpit on Wednesday at the pillar that is next to the grave, and supplicate to Allah there and ask Him for every need you desire in the Hereafter or in the world; and on the second day at the pillar of repentance; and on Friday at the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), opposite the pillar of abundant fragrance. So supplicate to Allah at these places for every need, and fast those three days.

Ibn Abi Umeyr from Muawiya ibn Ammar said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Fast Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, and pray on the night of Wednesday and the day of Wednesday by the pillar that follows the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family); and on the night of Thursday and the day of Thursday by the pillar of Abu Lubabah; and on the night of Friday and the day of Friday by the pillar that follows the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And supplicate with this supplication for your need, and it is: O Allah, I ask You by Your Honour, and Your Strength, and Your Power, and all that Your Knowledge encompasses, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You do for me such and such.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The lost property (luqata) is of two types: the lost property of the Sanctuary (Al-Haram) is publicized for a year; if you find its owner, [return it], otherwise give it in charity; and the lost property of elsewhere is publicized for a year; if its owner comes, [return it], otherwise it becomes like part of your wealth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who finds lost property in the Sanctuary. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not touch it. And as for you, there is no problem, because you publicize it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Fuzayl ibn Ghazwan, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Al-Tayyar said to him, 'I found a dinar during the circumambulation whose writing had been obscured.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Raja'a al-Arjani, who said: I wrote to Al-Tayyib (peace be upon him), 'I was in the Sacred Mosque, so I saw one Dinar. So I bent down to take it, and there was another one. So I searched in the gravel, and there was a third one. So I took them and publicized them, but no one recognized them. So what is your view regarding that?' So he wrote, 'I understood what you mentioned from the matter of the Dinars. So if you were in need, then give in charity with a third of it, and if you are wealthy, then give in charity with all of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all together from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not neglect visiting the shrines, all of them: Masjid Quba, for it is the mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day, and the drinking place of Umm Ibrahim, and Masjid Al-Fazeekh, and the graves of the martyrs, and Masjid Al-Ahzaab, and it is Masjid Al-Fath.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it has reached us that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he visited the graves of the martyrs, would say: 'Peace be upon you for what you endured patiently; so good is the final outcome of the Home (Hereafter).' And let what you say at Masjid Al-Fath be: 'O Helper of the distressed, and O Responder to the supplication of the desperate! Remove my worry, my grief, and my distress, just as You removed from Your Prophet his worry, his grief, and his distress, and sufficed him against the terror of his enemy in this place.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We visit the mosques around Medina, so which of them should I begin with?' He said: 'Begin with Quba, so pray in it and frequent it, for it is the first mosque in this earth wherein the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed.' Then go to the drinking place of Umm Ibrahim, so pray in it, and it is the dwelling of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his place of prayer. Then you go to the mosque of Al-Fadikh, so pray in it, for your Prophet had prayed in it. When you have fulfilled this side, you go to the side of Uhud, so begin with the mosque which is near the Harrah, so pray in it. Then you pass by the grave of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and greet upon him. Then you pass by the graves of the martyrs, so stand by them and say: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the houses! You have preceded us and we are following you.' Then you go to the mosque which was in the open space beside the mountain, on your right when you enter Uhud, so pray in it. For there the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) went out to Uhud when he met the Polytheists. They did not move away until the time for prayer arrived, so he prayed in it. Then pass by again until you return, so pray by the graves of the martyrs as Allah has decreed for you. Then proceed on your way until you come to the Mosque of the Confederates (Al-Ahzaab), so pray in it and supplicate to Allah in it. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated in it on the Day of the Confederates and said: 'O Helper of the distressed, and O Responder to the call of the desperate! O Helper of the worried, remove my anxiety, my distress, and my grief, for You see my state and the state of my companions.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fatima (peace be upon her) lived after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for seventy-five days. She was not seen smiling nor laughing. She would visit the graves of the martyrs twice every week, on Mondays and Thursdays, saying: 'Here was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and here were the polytheists.' And in another report, Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that she used to pray there and supplicate until she died (peace be upon her).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Masjid Al-Fadikh, why was it named Masjid Al-Fadikh? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because of a palm tree named Al-Fadikh, therefore it was named Masjid Al-Fadikh.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halbi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you visited the Mosque of Quba, or the Mosque of Al-Fadikh, or the drinking place of Umm Ibrahim?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, no trace of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) remains, except that it has been changed, apart from this.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you intend to exit from the city, perform ghusl, then go to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) after you have finished with your needs, and do as you did upon your entry. And say: 'O Allah, do not make it the last visitation of the grave of Your Prophet. If You cause me to die before that, then I testify in my death upon what I testified upon in my life that there is no god except You, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about bidding farewell to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say: May Allah bless you. Peace be upon you. May Allah not make it the last of my greetings upon you.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abu al-Abbas who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sanctify Medina?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. He sanctified Bareed by planting therein.' I said, '(What about) its hunting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The people would not be belied.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I was in the presence of Ziyad ibn Abdillah, and with him was Rabi'ah al-Ra'i. So Ziyad said, 'What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sanctify from Medina?' He said to him, 'A Bareed, in a Bareed.' So he said to Rabi'ah, 'And it was many miles in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' So he was silent and did not answer him. So Ziyad turned towards me and said, 'O Abu Abdillah, what are you saying?' So I said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sanctified from Medina what is between its two Labeets.' He said, 'And what is between the two Labeets?' I said, 'What is encompassed by the heat (hills/area).' He said, 'And what did he sanctify from the trees?' I said, 'From 'Ayyr to Wu'ayr.' Safwan said, Ibn Muskan said, Al-Hasan said, 'A person asked him while I was seated, so he said to him, 'And what is between the two Labeets?' He said, 'What is between the two Saurayn to the Saniyya.'

And in a report of Ibn Muskann, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The boundary of what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sanctified from Al-Medina is from Dhubab to Waqim, and Al-Ureyz and An-Naqb from the front of Makkah.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Makkah is the Sanctuary of Allah, which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) sanctified; and Al-Madinah is my Sanctuary, what is between its two hills is a Sanctuary where its trees are not to be cut down. It is what is between the shade of 'A'ir to the shade of Wueyr. And its hunting is not like the hunting of Makkah; this is eaten and that is not eaten, and it is a Bairid (a specific area).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever causes an incident in Medina or shelters an incident-maker, upon him is the Curse of Allah.' I said, 'And what is the incident?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The killing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you depart from Makkah to Al-Madina and reach Dhu al-Hulayfah, while you are returning to Al-Madina from Makkah, then go to the Mu'arras (resting place) of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). If you are within the time for a prescribed prayer or an optional one, pray therein; and if it is outside the time for a prescribed prayer, then stay there for a while, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to rest there and pray.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal and Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from one of our companions, that he did not rest, so Al-Rida (peace be upon him) ordered him to leave so that he might rest.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! Our camel-herd passed by with us and did not let us disembark at Al-Mu'arras.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is necessary that you return to it.' So I returned to it.

And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, who said: Ali ibn Asbaat said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while we were listening: 'We had not rested (in the Muarras), so Ibn Al-Qasim ibn Al-Fudayl informed us that he had not rested, and that he asked you, so you ordered him to return to the Muarras so that he might rest therein.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' He said to him: 'If we leave and rest therein, what should we do?' He said: 'You should pray therein and lie down.' And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to pray therein after the night prayer (Al-Atamah). Muhammad said to him: 'If one passes by it at a time other than that of a prescribed prayer?' He said: 'After Al-Asr.' It was said: 'Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked about this, so he said: 'Permission for this is granted only in the two cycles of the Tawaf (circumambulation), for Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) did so.' And he said: 'One should stay until the time for the prayer enters.' He said: 'I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! So the one who passes by it at night or by day, does he rest therein, or is the resting only at night?' He said: 'If one passes by it at night or by day, let him rest therein.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the Masjid of Ghadir Khumm during the day, while I was a traveler, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray in it, for there is merit in it, and my father used to order with that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Hassan al-Jammal, who said: I carried Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from Medina to Mecca. So when we arrived at Masjid al-Ghadir, he looked to the left side of the mosque and said: 'That is the place where the foot of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) set, where he said: 'For whomever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.' Then he looked to the other side and said: 'That is the place of the tents of So-and-so, and So-and-so, and Salim, the Mawla of Abu Hudhayfa, and Abu Ubaydah al-Jarrah.' So when they saw him raising his hands, some of them said to others: 'Look at his eyes; they are rolling as if they were the eyes of a madman.' So Jibreel (peace be upon him) descended with this Verse: 'And those who disbelieve would almost smite you with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: He is mad. And it is naught but a Reminder to the Worlds.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The performance of the prayer is recommended in the Mosque of Al-Ghadeer, because the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) established there the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and it is a place in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, manifested the Truth.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no Prophet nor a successor of a Prophet who remains in the earth for more than three days, until his soul, and his bones, and his flesh are raised to the sky; and rather, they are sent to the places of their traces, and they deliver greetings to them from afar, and they hear them in the places of their traces from nearby.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'For every Imam there is a pact in the neck of his friends and his Shia; and among the completion of loyalty to the pact and good performance is the Ziyarah of their graves. So whoever visits them with desire for their Ziyarah and affirmation of what they desired therein, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent for me and Muhammad ibn Hamza during his illness. So Muhammad ibn Hamza preceded me to go to him, and Muhammad informed me, 'He did not cease saying, 'Go to al-Hayr, go to al-Hayr!' So I said to Muhammad, 'Did you not say to him that I am going to al-Hayr?' Then I went over to him and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I am going to al-Hayr'. So he said: 'Look into that'. Then he said to me: 'Muhammad, there is a secret for him from Zayd ibn Ali, and I dislike it that he should hear that'. So I mentioned that to Ali ibn Bilal, and he said, 'What does he have to do with al-Hayr and he (himself) is (from) al-Hayr?' So I proceeded to al-Askar and I went over to him. So he said to me: 'Be seated!', when I wanted to arise (to leave). So when I saw him glancing at me, I mentioned to him the words of Ali ibn Bilal. So he said to me: 'Did I not say to you that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would perform Tawaaf by the House, and he would kiss the (Black) Stone, and the sanctity of the Prophet and the Believer is greater than sanctity of the House (Kaaba)? However, Allah Mighty and Majestic Commanded him that he should pause at Arafaat, and rather it is a place wherein Allah Loves that He be mentioned therein. Thus I loved it that you supplicate to Allah for me where Allah Loves that He be supplicated to'. And he mentioned from him that he said, and did not memorise it from him, he said: 'But rather, these are places wherein Allah Loved that He be worshipped, thus I loved it that he should supplicate for me where Allah Loves that He be worshipped. Did you not say to him such and such?' He (the narrator) said, 'I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! If I was good similar to this, I would not have referred the matter upon you'. These are the words of Hashim, not my words'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I was sitting beside Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he was sitting with his arms around his knees, facing the Ka'bah. He said: 'Indeed, looking at it is an act of worship.'
