Then a man from Bajilah came to him, called Asim ibn Umar, and said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Ka'b al-Ahbar used to say that the Ka'bah prostrates to Bayt al-Maqdis every morning.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'So what do you say about what Ka'b said?' He said: 'He spoke the truth; the statement is what Ka'b said.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'You lied, and Ka'b al-Ahbar lied with you,' and he was angered. Zurara said: 'I did not see him face anyone else by saying 'You lied' except him.' Then he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not create a spot on the earth more beloved to Him than it.' Then he gestured with his hand towards the Ka'bah, and said: 'Nor is anything more prestigious to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than it. For it, Allah sanctified the sacred months in His Book the day He created the heavens and the earth: three consecutive ones for the Hajj — Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah — and a separate month for the Umrah, which is Rajab.'

And by this chain, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there are one hundred and twenty mercies around the Kaaba. From these, sixty are for the circumambulators, forty for the praying ones, and twenty for the beholders.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Abdillah al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for the Ka'bah there is a moment in every day in which forgiveness is granted to whoever circumambulates it, or whose heart inclines towards it, or whom an excuse prevents from reaching it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Rabat, from Sayf al-Tammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever looks at the Ka'bah, a good deed is written for him and a bad deed is erased from him, until he turns his gaze away from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Looking towards the Ka'bah is worship, and looking towards the parents is worship, and looking at the Imam is worship. And he said: 'The one who looks towards the Ka'bah, one good deed is written for him and ten sins are deleted from him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abdul Aziz, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever looks at the Ka'bah with understanding, and recognizes from our rights and our sanctity as much as he recognizes from its rights and its sanctity, Allah will forgive his sins and suffice him for the concerns of the world and the Hereafter.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Nu'aym ibn al-Walid, from Yunus al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you come to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), go to the Euphrates and perform ghusl near his grave, and face him, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity until you enter the grave from the eastern side. And say when you enter it: 'Peace be upon the Angels of Allah who have descended, peace be upon the Angels of Allah who follow, peace be upon the Angels of Allah who brand, peace be upon the Angels of Allah who are stationed in this sanctuary.' So when you face the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), say: 'Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon the Trustworthy of Allah upon His Messengers and the decisive ones in His command, the Seal of what preceded and the Opener of what followed, and the Guardian over all of that, and peace be upon him and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' Then you say: 'O Allah, send blessings upon the Commander of the Faithful, Your servant and the brother of Your Messenger, whom You chose with Your knowledge and made a guide for whom You willed from Your creation, and the guide for whom You sent with Your messages, and the Judge of the Religion by Your justice and the separator of Your judgment among Your creation, and the Guardian over all of that, and peace be upon him and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' O Allah, send blessings upon al-Hasan ibn Ali, Your servant and the son of the one You chose with Your knowledge and made a guide for whom You willed from Your creation, and the guide for whom You sent with Your messages, and the Judge of the Religion by Your justice and the separator of Your judgment among Your creation, and the Guardian over all of that, and peace be upon him and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' Then you send blessings upon al-Husayn and the rest of the Imams (peace be upon them) as You sent blessings and peace upon al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Then you come to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and say: 'Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you, O son of the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah bless you, O Abu Abdillah.' I testify that you delivered from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, what you were commanded, and feared no

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan, the Master of the Army (peace be upon him), who said: You should say by the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Peace be upon you, O Abu Abdullah! Peace be upon you, O Proof of Allah in His earth and His witness upon His creation. Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! Peace be upon you, O son of Ali al-Murtada! Peace be upon you, O son of Fatima al-Zahra!' I testify that you established the prayer, gave the alms-tax, enjoined the good, forbade the evil, and strove in the way of Allah until the certainty (death) came to you. So may Allah send blessings upon you, living and dead.' Then place your right cheek upon the grave and say: 'I testify that you are upon clear evidence from your Lord. I come acknowledging the sins, so intercede for me with your Lord, O son of the Messenger of Allah!' Then mention the Imams by their names, one by one, and say: 'I testify that you are the Proof of Allah.' Then say: 'Record for me with you a covenant and a promise that I have come to you to renew the covenant, so bear witness for me with your Lord that you are the witness.' Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Zayd ibn Ishaq, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you have finished greeting the martyrs, go to the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), place it in front of you, then pray whatever prayer comes to you.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: You should say in Baghdad: 'Peace be upon you, O Guardian of Allah! Peace be upon you, O Proof of Allah! Peace be upon you, O Light of Allah in the darknesses of the earth! Peace be upon you, O who appeared for Allah in His affair! I have come to you recognizing your right, being an enemy of your enemies, so intercede for me with your Lord, and supplicate to Allah, and ask your need.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And you should greet with this to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Harun ibn Muslim from Ali ibn Hassan from Al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: My father was asked about visiting the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: Pray in the mosques around it, and it will suffice in all places that you say: Peace be upon the Guardians of Allah and His elites. Peace be upon the trustworthy ones of Allah and His beloved ones. Peace be upon the helpers of Allah and His caliphs. Peace be upon the places of recognition of Allah. Peace be upon the dwellings of the remembrance of Allah. Peace be upon those who manifest the command and prohibition of Allah. Peace be upon the callers to Allah. Peace be upon those settled in the pleasure of Allah. Peace be upon those refined in the obedience of Allah. Peace be upon the pointers to Allah. Peace be upon those who, whoever befriends them has befriended Allah, and whoever is inimical to them has been inimical to Allah, and whoever recognizes them has recognized Allah, and whoever is ignorant of them has been ignorant of Allah, and whoever holds fast to them has held fast to Allah, and whoever loosens from them has loosened from Allah. I testify to Allah that I am at peace with those who are at peace with you, and at war with those who are at war with you, a believer in your secrets and your public declarations, entrusting all of that to you. May Allah curse the enemies of the Progeny of Muhammad from the Jinn and humans, and I disavow to Allah from them, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny. This will suffice for all visits, and you should frequent sending blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny, and name them one by one by their names, and disavow to Allah from their enemies, and choose for yourself from supplication whatever you like, and for the believing men and women.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is [the reward] for the one who performs Ziyarah of one of you?' He (peace be upon him) said: '[It is] as if he has performed Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, raising it (to the Prophet), said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Ali! Whoever visits me during my lifetime or after my death, or visits you during your lifetime or after your death, or visits or after your death, or visits your two sons during their lifetime or after their death, I guarantee for him on the Day of Resurrection that I will deliver him from its terrors and hardships until I place him with me in my rank.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn Abi Wahb al-Qasri, who said: I entered Medina, so I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I came to you and I have not performed the Ziyarah of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Bad is what you have done. Had you not been from our Shiah, I would not have looked at you. Do you not visit the one whom Allah visits along with the Angels, and the Prophets visit him, and the believers visit him?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I had no knowledge of that.' He said: 'Know that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) is superior in the Presence of Allah than all the Imams, and for him is the reward of their deeds, and they are distinguished according to the measure of their deeds.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Bashir al-Dahhan who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I go to recognize [the grave] at the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Well done, O Bashir! Whoever of the believers comes to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, on a day other than the day of Eid, Allah will write for him twenty Hajjs and twenty Umrahs, properly performed and accepted; and twenty Hajjs and Umrahs with a sent Prophet or a just Imam. And whoever comes to him on the day of Eid, Allah will write for him one hundred Hajjs and one hundred Umrahs and one hundred military expeditions with a sent Prophet or a just Imam.' I said to him, 'How is it for me with the likes of the Standing (at Arafat)?' He looked at me as if slightly angry, then said to me, 'O Bashir! Indeed, when the believer comes to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafah, and performs Ghusl from the Euphrates, then turns his face towards him, Allah will write for him, with every step, a Hajj with its rituals — and I do not know except that he said: 'And a military expedition.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Zayd Al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), peace be upon him, who said: The Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals twenty Hajjs and superior, and [is equal] to twenty Umrahs and a Hajj.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik, who said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when a group of people passed by a group of people riding donkeys. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where are these intending to go?' I said: 'The graves of the martyrs.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is preventing them from the Ziyarah of the martyr, the alienated?' So a man from the people of Iraq said: 'Is his Ziyarah obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His Ziyarah is better than a Hajj and an Umrah, and an Umrah and a Hajj' until he had counted twenty Hajjs and Umrahs. Then he said: 'Accepted, properly performed (ones).' He (the narrator) said: 'By Allah, I had not arisen until a man came to him and said to him: 'I have performed nineteen Hajjs, so supplicate to Allah to grant me completing the twentieth Hajj.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you performed the Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His Ziyarah is better than twenty Hajjs.'

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Saeed al-Madainy, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, can I go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'Yes, O Abu Saeed! Go to the grave of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the most fragrant of the fragrant, the purest of the pure, and the most righteous of the righteous. So when you visit him, Allah will write for you, because of it, twenty-five Hajjs.'

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Sadaqa, from Salih al-Nayli, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, Allah will write for him the reward of freeing a thousand slaves, and [reward him] like the one who rides out with a thousand saddled and bridled horses in the way of Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Kharjah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah has assigned four thousand angels, dishevelled and dusty, to weep over him until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever visits him, recognizing his right, they will escort him until they bring him to his safe place; and if he is sick, they will visit him in the morning and evening; and if he dies, they will witness his funeral and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There are four thousand angels by the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), dishevelled and dusty, weeping for him until the Day of Resurrection. Their chief is an angel called Mansour. So no visitor visits him but they welcome him, and no one bids him farewell but they accompany him; and no sick person becomes ill but they visit him, and no deceased person dies but they pray over his funeral and seek forgiveness for him after his death.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq, from one of our companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever visits Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) recognizing his right, Allah (Exalted is He) will forgive him whatever preceded from his sins and whatever is delayed.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Miskan, from Gassan Al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sins and what followed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Musa ibn Umra, from Gassan al-Basri, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Muawiya ibn Wahb who said: I sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so it was said to me, 'Enter'. So I entered and found him in his prayer mat in his house. So I sat until he finished his prayer, and I heard him as he was conversing with his Lord, saying: 'O He who distinguished us with honor, and distinguished us with the successorship, and promised us intercession, and gave us knowledge of what has passed and what remains, and made the hearts of people incline towards us.' Forgive me and my brothers, and the visitors of the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who spent their wealth and sent their bodies, desiring our goodness and hoping for what is with You regarding maintaining ties with us, and bringing joy to Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and answering our command, and bringing rage to our enemy, intending thereby Your pleasure. So suffice them from us with contentment, and protect them by night and day, and compensate for their families and children who were left behind with the best compensation, and accompany them, and suffice them from the evil of every stubborn tyrant, and every weak or strong of Your creation, and the evil of the devils of humans and jinn, and give them the best of what they hoped for from You in their exile from their homelands, and what they preferred us with over their sons, families, and relatives. O Allah, our enemies criticized them for their departure, but that did not prevent them from traveling to us, and opposing those who opposed us. So have mercy on those faces which the sun has changed, and have mercy on those cheeks which rolled upon the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and have mercy on those eyes from which tears flowed out of mercy for us, and have mercy on those hearts which were anxious and burned for us, and have mercy on the cry which was for us. O Allah, I entrust to You those souls and those bodies until we meet them at the Pond on the Day of Thirst. So he remained as he was in prostration, supplicating with this supplication. So when he finished, I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, if this

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Himyari, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qummi, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who performs Ziyarah of the grave of my father in Baghdad is like the one who performed Ziyarah of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), except that for the Messenger of Allah and for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them both) is their distinct merit.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the Ziyarah of the grave of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) being like the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)? He said: Yes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is the Ziyarah of Al-Reza (peace be upon him) superior or the Ziyarah of Abu Abdullah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'The Ziyarah of my father is superior, and that is because all people visit Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and my father is visited only by the special ones from the Shiah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari from Hamdan ibn Ishaq who said, 'I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or it was narrated to me from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — the doubt is from Ali ibn Ibrahim — who said, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:' Whoever visits the grave of my father in Toos, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what was delayed. He said, 'So I performed Hajj after the visitation, then I met Ayub ibn Nuh, and he said to me, 'Abu Ja'far the second (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of my father in Toos, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what was delayed, and Allah will build for him a pulpit adjacent to the pulpit of Muhammad and Ali (peace be upon him), until Allah finishes the reckoning of the creatures.' So I saw him, and he had performed the visitation, and he said, 'I came seeking the pulpit.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, from Ibrahim ibn Ahmad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Saeed al-Makki, from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Mazini, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of my son Ali, there is for him with Allah the reward of seventy accepted Hajjs. I said, 'Seventy Hajjs?' He said, 'Yes, and seventy thousand Hajjs.' I said, 'Seventy thousand Hajjs?' He said, 'Perhaps a Hajj is not accepted. But whoever visits him and spends the night at his side is like the one who visited Allah at His Throne.' He said, 'Yes. When it is the Day of Judgment, there will be upon the Throne of the Beneficent four from the former [prophets] and four from the later ones. As for the four who are from the former, they are Noah, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (peace be upon them). And as for the four from the later ones, they are Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). Then the area will be extended, and those who visited the graves of the Imams (peace be upon them) will sit with us, except that the one with the highest rank and the closest in receiving gifts will be the visitors of the grave of my son Ali (peace be upon him).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for the one who performs Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is like the one who visits Allah, Mighty and Majestic, above His Throne.' I said, 'So what is for the one who performs Ziyarah of one of you (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is as if he performed Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who reported it, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the dwelling of one of you is far away, and the house is distant, let him go to the highest place of his house, and let him pray two cycles (of prayer), and let him gesture with the greetings towards our graves, for that arrives to us.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali al-Hakam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you intend to perform the Ziyarah of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), perform it while you are in grief, distressed, dishevelled, dusty, hungry, and thirsty, and ask him for your needs, and leave from him, and do not take it as a homeland.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Karram, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A person takes from the clay of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and benefits from it, while others take and do not benefit from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by the One (God) besides Whom there is no god, no one takes it unless he believes that Allah will benefit him by it, and if he believes, Allah will indeed benefit him by it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, by the head of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), there is red clay in which there is healing from every disease except for Al-Sam (death). He (the narrator) said, 'So we went to the grave after having heard this Hadith, so we dug by the head of the grave. So when we had dug the measurement of a cubit, there appeared to us, from the head of the grave, like red coastal sand the size of a Dirham (coin). So we carried it to Al-Kufa, and we blended it, and went around giving it to the people for them to use it as medication.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Rizaqallah ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Suleyman ibn Umar al-Sarraj, from one of our companions, who said: The clay of the grave of Al-Hus-Husayn (peace be upon him) is taken from near the grave up to a distance of seventy cubits.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'For the place of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), there is a known sanctity; whoever recognizes it and seeks refuge by it is granted refuge.' I said, 'Describe its place to me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Measure out from the place of his grave today, twenty-five cubits from its front, and twenty-five cubits by his head, and twenty-five cubits from around his legs, and twenty-five cubits from behind him.' And the place of his grave from the day he was buried is a Garden from the Gardens of Paradise, and from it is an ascending stairway from which the deeds of his visitors ascend to the sky, and there is none from an Angel, nor a Prophet in the skies, except that they are asking Allah to permit them regarding the performance of Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So a multitude descends and a multitude ascends.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Abdullah ibn al-Khattab from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sinan from Misma' from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Hanan from his father who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadeer, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) every day?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, no.' He said: 'So how discourteous you are.' He said: 'Do you visit it every Friday?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit it every month?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit it every year?' I said, 'It may happen (in some years).' He said: 'O Sadeer, how discourteous you are towards al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Do you not know that for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are two million angels, dishevelled and dusty, who weep and visit (the grave), not ceasing. And it is not difficult upon you, O Sadeer, to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) five times every week, and once every day.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, there are many farsakhs (travel distances) between us and him.' So he said to me: 'Ascend to your roof, then turn right and left, then raise your head to the sky, then face towards the grave and say: 'As-salamu alayka ya Aba Abdillah, as-salamu alayka wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu' (Peace be upon you, O Abu Abdillah, peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah). A visitation (ziyarah) is written for you, and the visitation is equivalent to a Hajj and an Umrah.' Sadeer said: 'So I used to do it in the month more than twenty times.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Harun ibn Kharjat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When it is the middle of Sha'ban, a caller calls out from the highest horizon: 'O visitors of the grave of Al-Husayn! Return, forgiven for you, and your reward is with your Lord, and Muhammad is your Prophet.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who designated his slave girl as a hady (sacrificial offering) for the Ka'bah. How should he deal with it? He said: A man came to my father who had designated his slave girl as a hady for the Ka'bah. So he said to him: 'Evaluate the slave girl or sell her. Then instruct a caller to stand at the Hajar al-Aswad (Black Stone) and call out: 'Indeed, whoever has insufficient funds, or whose path has been cut off, or whose food supply has run out, let him come to so-and-so.' And instruct him to give [the money] to the first one, then the next, until the price of the slave girl is depleted.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban, from Abu al-Hurr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'I gifted a slave girl to the Ka'bah, and I was given five hundred dinars for her. So what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Sell her, then take her price, then stand upon the wall of the Hawd (Basin of the Ka'bah), then call out and give to everyone who has been cut off (by bandits or circumstances) and every needy one among the pilgrims.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from his two brothers, Muhammad and Ahmad, from Ali ibn Yaqoub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Saeed ibn Amr al-Ju'fi, from a man from the people of Egypt, who said: My brother bequeathed to me a slave girl who was a singer for him, a luxury, and made her a gift (hadya) to the Sacred House of Allah. So I arrived in Mecca and asked, and it was said to me, 'Hand her over to the Banu Shayba,' and other words were said to me, so there was conflict regarding it. A man from the people of the Masjid said to me, 'Shall I guide you to one who will guide you to the truth in this?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So he pointed to an old man sitting in the Masjid and said, 'This is Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), so ask him.' I said, 'So I went to him (peace be upon him) and asked him, and related the story to him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, the Ka'bah neither eats nor drinks, and whatever is gifted to it is for its visitors. Sell the slave girl, and stand on the Hajar al-Aswad and call out: Is there one who has been cut off (by bandits), and is there one who is needy among its visitors? When they come to you, ask about them, give to them, and distribute her price among them.' He said, 'So I said to him, 'Some of those I asked instructed me to hand her over to the Banu Shayba.' He said, 'But, our Qaim (the Imam), if he had risen, would have seized them, cut off their hands, circled with them, and said: These are the thieves of Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from one of our companions, who said: A woman handed over to me some yarn and said, 'Hand it over at Makkah so that the covering of the Ka'bah may be sewn with it.' But I disliked handing it over to the guards, and I knew them. So when I arrived in Medina, I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A woman gave me some yarn and instructed me to hand it over at Makkah so that the covering of the Ka'be may be sewn with it. But I disliked handing it over to the guards.' He said, 'Buy honey and saffron with it, and take clay from the grave of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and knead it with rainwater, and put some of the honey and saffron in it, and distribute it among the Shias so that they may use it to heal their sick.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Muawiya was the first to hang two shutters on his door in Makkah.' So he prevented the pilgrims of the House of Allah from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Equal is the one who dwells in it and the one who visits it.' And the people, when they arrived in Makkah, the visitor would lodge with the dweller until he fulfilled his Hajj. And Muawiya was the owner of the chain of which Allah the Exalted spoke: 'A chain whose length is seventy cubits, thrust him into it.' 'Surely he did not believe in Allah, the Magnificent,' and he was the Pharaoh of this community.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Aban ibn Uthman from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Abdillah from his father (peace be upon them) said: The houses of Makkah did not have doors, and the people of the cities would come with their pitch (bitumen), so they would enter and strike (the walls) with it. And the first one to install doors for it was Muawiya.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not perform Hajj after his arrival in Medina except for one, and he had performed Hajj in Mecca with his people, (multiple) Hajjs.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Isa al-Farra', from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed ten Hajjs in concealment.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed twenty Hajjs.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Hammam, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he departed from Mina, took the road of Dabb, and returned by what is between Al-Mazimayn, and it was his practice that whenever he traveled by a road, he did not return by it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he performed the Hajj of Al-Islam, set out when four days remained from Dhu al-Qadah until he arrived at Al-Shajara, so he prayed there. Then he led his mount until he arrived at Al-Bayda', so he entered into Ihram from there and proclaimed the Hajj, and drove along one hundred camels. And the people all entered into Ihram with the Hajj, not intending an Umrah, nor knowing what Al-Mut'ah was. Until when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) arrived in Mecca, he circumambulated the House, and the people circumambulated with him. Then he prayed two cycles near the Maqam (Station of Ibrahim), and kissed the Stone, then said: 'I begin with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began with.' So he went to Al-Safa and began with it. Then he circumambulated between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa seven times. So when he had completed his circumambulation at Al-Marwa, he stood as a preacher. So he ordered them to release themselves (from Ihram) and make it an Umrah, and it is something which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had commanded. So the people released themselves, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Had I faced from my matter what I managed, I would have done as I commanded you.' And he did not have the ability to release himself due to the sacrificial animal which was with him. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its destination.' So Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'sham said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Teach us as if we were created today. What is your view of this which you ordered us with? Is it for this year of ours, or for every year?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No, but it is for ever and ever.' And indeed a man stood up and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! We go out as pilgrims and our heads are dripping.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'You will never believe in this, ever!' He said: And Ali (peace be upon him) came from Yemen until he arrived for the Hajj. So he found Fatima (peace be upon her) had released herself, and he found the scent of perf

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sacrificed thirty-six with his own hand, and Ali (peace be upon him) sacrificed what remained.' I said, 'Thirty-seven?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who was in charge of the camels of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was Najiya ibn Jundub Al-Khuzai Al-Aslamy, and the one who shaved the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him) during his Hajj was Ma'mar ibn Abdullah ibn Haratha ibn Nasr ibn Awf ibn Aweij ibn Adi ibn Ka'b. He (peace be upon him) said: And when it was the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and he was shaving him, the Quraysh said, 'O Ma'mar! The ear of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) is in your hand, and in your hand is the razor.' So Ma'mar said, 'By Allah! I count it as a great favor from Allah upon me.' He (peace be upon him) said: And Ma'mar was the one who used to prepare the ride for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). So the Messenger of Allah said, 'O Ma'mar! The ride tonight is loose.' So Ma'mar said, 'By my father and my mother! I had tightened it just as I used to tighten it, but some of those who envy me for my place from you, O Messenger of Allah, intended that you would replace me.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'I would not have done it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed three distinct Umras: an Umra in Dhi al-Qadah, entering into ihram from Usfan, and this is the Umra of Al-Hudaybiyya; and an Umra entering into ihram from Al-Juhfa, and this is the Umra of Qaza (compensation); and an Umra entering into ihram from Al-Ji'rana after returning from Al-Ta'if from the expedition of Hunayn.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) perform Hajj other than the Farewell Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, twenty Hajjs.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam, all from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed the Umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah, and made up the Umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah from the following year, and from al-Ji'rana when he returned from al-Ta'if; three Umrahs in total, all of them in the month of Dhi al-Qadah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed Umrah in Dhi al-Qadah three times; all of that coincided with his Umrah of Dhi al-Qadah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with some questions, some of them with Ibn Bukayr and some with Abu al-Abbas. So the answer came with his dictation: You asked about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for Allah upon the people is a pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to undertake to it a way.' He means by it the Hajj and the Umrah together, because both of them are obligatory. And I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah.' He said: He means by their completion, their fulfillment, and abstaining from what the one in Ihram abstains from during them. And I asked him about the Words of the Exalted: 'the greater Hajj'. What is meant by 'the greater Hajj'? So he said: The greater Hajj is the standing at Arafat and the pelting of the Jamarat, and the lesser Hajj is the Umrah.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Fadl Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Both are obligatory.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is Hajj obligatory on the rich and the poor?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj is obligatory upon all people, their elders and their young ones. So whoever has an excuse, Allah will excuse him.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Umrah is obligatory upon the creation, in the status of Hajj upon the one who has the ability for it, because Allah the Exalted says: 'And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah', and indeed the Umrah was revealed at Al-Medina. I said to him, 'So the one who enjoys (Tamattu) with the Umrah to the Hajj, would that suffice from him?' He said: 'Yes'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, all together, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Hajj obligatory upon those with the capacity (al-jiddah) every year, and this is His word, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage of the House for whoever is able to undertake a journey to it.' And whoever disbeliees, then indeed Allah is Self-sufficient of the worlds.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'So the one from us who did not perform Hajj, so he has disbelieved?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the one who says, 'It is not like this', so he has disbelieved'.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the Hajj obligatory upon the people of Al-Jeddah every year.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: There is no obligation of Hajj nor Umra upon the slave until he is freed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Jarir al-Qummi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Hajj is obligatory upon the people of wealth (Al-Jiddah) every year.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the Hajj obligatory upon the inhabitants of Al-Jeddah every year.

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), Which thing was the place of the House (Ka'ba) when the water was [there], in the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And His Throne was upon the water' [11:7]? He said: 'It was a white Mahaat, meaning a gem (pearl).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Khadija, who said: Verily, Allah Mighty and Majestic sent down the Stone for Adam (peace be upon him) from Paradise, and the House (Ka'ba) was a white gem. Then Allah Mighty and Majestic raised it to the heavens, and its foundation remained. And it (the heavenly House) is directly above this House; every day seventy thousand angels enter it, never returning to it again. Then Allah Mighty and Majestic commanded Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them both) to construct the House upon its foundations.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Salih al-Lafa'ifi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — spread the earth from beneath the Kaaba to Mina, then spread it from Mina to Arafat, then spread it from Arafat to Mina. So the earth originates from Arafat, and Arafat from Mina, and Mina from the Kaaba.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashimi, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The place of the Ka'ba was a mound of white earth, shining like the light of the sun and the moon, until the two sons of Adam — one of the two — killed his companion, and it turned black. When Adam descended, Allah raised the earth, all of it, for him until he saw it, then said: 'This is for you, all of it.' He said: 'O Lord! What is this white, radiant land?' He said: 'It is in My land, and I have made it incumbent upon you to circumambulate it seven hundred times every day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Marwan, from a number of our companions, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the Sacred Masjid: For what reason did God name it al-Ateeq (the free)? So he said: There is no house that God placed upon the face of the earth except that it has a lord (owner) and dwellers who dwell in it — apart from this House (Kaaba), for there is no lord for it except God, Mighty and Majestic, and it is the Free (al-Hurr). Then he said: Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, created it before the earth, then He created the earth after it and spread it out from beneath it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from whoever informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'Why was the House (Kaaba) named al-Atiq (the Free)?' He said: 'It is a free house, freed from the people. No one has ever owned it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abu Zurara al-Tamimi, from Abu Hassan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, willed to create the earth, He commanded the winds, and they struck the surface of the water until it became waves. Then it foamed, and it became a single unified foam. He gathered it in the place of the House (Kaaba). Then He made it a mountain of foam. Then He spread out the earth from beneath it. And this is the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Verily, the first house established for the people is the one at Bakka, blessed.' And it was also narrated from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), similar to it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever dies and has not performed the Hajj of Islam, provided he was not prevented from doing so by a need that overwhelms him, or an illness that makes him unable to perform Hajj, or a ruler who prevents him, then let him die as a Jew or a Christian.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, And whoever was blind with regards to this, he shall (also) be blind in the Hereafter; and more straying from the way So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is the one who delays himself for the Hajj, meaning Hajj of Al-Islam, until the death comes to him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The merchant delays himself regarding Hajj.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no excuse for him, and if he were to die, he would have left a law from the laws of Islam.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'What is your view of a merchant who has wealth when he delays the Hajj every year, and he is not occupied from it except by trade or debt?' So he said, 'There is no excuse for him delaying the Hajj. If he dies having left the Hajj, he has left a law from the laws of Islam.' Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zarih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever dies and has not performed the Hajj of Islam, and was not prevented from that he was not prevented by a need that crushes him, or an illness in which he cannot endure the Hajj, or a ruler who prevents him, so let him die as a Jew or a Christian.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who dies while he is healthy and affluent, and has not performed Hajj, then he is from those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And We will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment blind.' I said, 'Glory be to Allah, blind?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would blind him from the path of Truth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who departs from Makkah while not intending to return to it, his term has drawn near and his punishment has approached.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Husayn ibn Usman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who goes out from Makkah and he does not intend to return to it, so his term (death) has drawn near and his punishment has approached.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say to his sons: 'O my sons! Look upon the House of your Lord, so that it should not be empty of you, so that you should not be argued with (or lose out/miss out).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb from Yunus ibn Imran ibn Maysam from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: He said to me, 'What is wrong with you that you do not perform Hajj this year?' I said, 'There were business dealings between me and some people, and I had affairs, and perhaps that would be better (for me later).' He said, 'No, by Allah, Allah will not do good for you in that.' Then he said, 'A servant is not withheld from this House except because of a sin, and He pardons most of it.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no goodness in neglecting the Hajj'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If the people were to neglect the Hajj, they would not be respited of the punishment, or he said: The punishment would descend upon them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father who said: I mentioned the House (Kabah) to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he said: 'If they were to suspend it for one year, they would not be (given the) Respite (from the Punishment)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say to his sons: 'O my sons! Look to the House of your Lord, so that it should not be empty of you, and so that you should not be questioned (or have conflict/second thoughts).'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Religion will not cease to be standing as long as the Ka'bah stands.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Hisham ibn Salim, and Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, and others, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If the people were to neglect Hajj, it would be upon the governor to compel them to do so and to stay there; and if they were to neglect the visitation of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), it would be upon the governor to compel them to do so and to stay there. So if they do not have wealth, he should spend from the treasury of the Muslims on them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If the people were to neglect the Hajj, it would be obligatory upon the Imam to compel them to perform the Hajj, whether they wish to or refuse, for this House has indeed been established for the Hajj.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man who is insolvent (poor/debt-ridden) has another man perform Hajj on his behalf, that counts as one Hajj for him. So if he becomes affluent afterwards, the Hajj (obligation) remains upon him. And similarly, the Nasibi (Hostile One) when he recognizes (the Wilayah), the Hajj is upon him, even if he had already performed Hajj.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from a number of our companions from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who did not have wealth, so some people from his companions performed Hajj on his behalf. I asked: Has he fulfilled the Hajj of Islam? He said: Yes. But when he becomes affluent after that, upon him is that he performs Hajj. I said: And will that Hajj of his be complete or deficient if he did not perform Hajj from his own wealth? He said: Yes. The Hajj of Islam is fulfilled for him, and it will be complete and not deficient. And if he becomes affluent, let him perform Hajj. He said: And he was asked about a man who has camels, he hires them out and earns from them, so he performs Hajj while he is a renter (of the camels/means). Would that suffice him from his Hajj? Or he carries trade to Mecca, so he performs Hajj and earns wealth in his trade or loses it? Would his Hajj be complete or deficient, or would it not be [complete] until he goes with it to Hajj and does not intend anything else, or he intends both together? Would that fulfill his Hajj? He said: Yes, his Hajj is complete.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Hajj on behalf of another, does that suffice him from the Hajj of Islam? He said: Yes. I said: Is the Hajj of the camelier (one who leads the caravan) complete or deficient? He said: Complete. I said: Is the Hajj of the hired one complete or deficient? He said: Complete.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina who said: I wrote to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who performed Hajj and neither knew nor recognised this matter (Al-Wilayah). Then Allah favoured upon him with his understanding and the Religion with it, is the Hajj of Al-Islam upon him (to perform again), or has it been fulfilled? He said: He has fulfilled an Obligation of Allah, and the (repeating of the) Hajj is more beloved to me. And about a man who is among one of these types from the people of the Qiblah, a devout Nasibi. Then Allah favours upon him, so he recognises this matter (Al-Wilayah). Has the Hajj of Al-Islam been fulfilled from him, or it is (still) upon him that he should perform Hajj the coming year? He said: The (performance of the) Hajj is more beloved to me.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Hamdani wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I performed Hajj, and I am an adversary (of the Hajj rites), and I was a novice (first-timer), so I entered performing Tamattu' (Umrah followed by Hajj).' He (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Repeat your Hajj.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man passes through intending to go to Yemen or other cities, and his route is through Mecca, so he catches up with the people as they are setting out for Hajj, and he sets out with them to the shrines. Would that suffice him as the Hajj of Islam? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man goes out for trade to Makkah, or he has camels which he hires out; is his Hajj deficient or complete?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but his Hajj is complete.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who freed a slave of his on the eve of Arafat: Would a Hajj suffice for the slave, a Hajj of Al-Islam? He said: Yes. I said: So if a mother of a child is taken to Hajj by her master, would it suffice from her? He said: No. I said: Is there any recompense for him regarding her Hajj? He said: Yes. He said: And I asked him about a boy of ten years performing Hajj. He said: Upon him is the Hajj of Al-Islam when he attains puberty, and similar to that is the girl, upon her would be the Hajj when she menstruates.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second [Imam al-Baqir] about the child, when is he considered to be in the state of Ihram? He (peace be upon him) said: When he can safeguard [himself, i.e., reach the age of discernment/maturity].

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zureys, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding a man who set out as a pilgrim for the Hajj of Islam, and he died on the way, he said: If he died in the Sanctuary (Haram), the Hajj of Islam suffices for him; and if he died outside the Sanctuary, then his guardian should perform the Hajj of Islam on his behalf.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bureyd al-Ijaly, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who set out as a pilgrim, and with him was a camel of his, and expense money, and provisions. So he died on the way. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was Sarurah (one who had not yet performed the obligatory Hajj), then died in Ihram, then the Hajj of Al-Islam suffices for him. And if he died while he was Sarurah before he entered into Ihram, his camel and his provisions and his expenses and whatever was with him are made to be for the Hajj of Al-Islam. So if there is something excess from that, then it is for the inheritors, if there are no debts upon him.' I said, 'What is your view if the Hajj was optional (Nafl), then he died on the way before he entered into Ihram, for whom would be his camel, and his expense money, and whatever was with him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'All that was with him and whatever he left would be for the inheritors, except if there are debts upon him, so they are paid off on his behalf; or if he had bequeathed a bequest, so that bequest is executed for the one to whom he bequeathed it, and that is taken from his one-third.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rafa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed to walk to the Sacred House of Allah, would that suffice for him as the Hajj of Islam? He said: 'Yes'. I said: 'And if he performs Hajj on behalf of others and he has no wealth, and he had vowed to perform Hajj walking, would that suffice for him?' He said: 'Yes'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Aamir ibn Ameyra, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'It has reached me from you that you said: If a man died and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and some of his family performed Hajj on his behalf, would that suffice for him?' He said, 'Yes. I bear witness to this from my father, that he narrated to me that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, my father died and did not perform Hajj.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Perform Hajj on his behalf, for that will suffice for him.'

From him, from Safwan, from Hakam ibn Hukeym who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A person died and had not performed Hajj and did not bequeath that Hajj be performed, so one of his family members, a man or a woman, performed Hajj on his behalf. Would that suffice, and serve as a discharge (Qaza) for him, and would the Hajj be for the one who performed it, and would the one who performed it on his behalf be rewarded? He (peace be upon him) said: If the pilgrim was not Sarurah (one who has already performed Hajj), it would suffice for both of them together, and the reward would be for the one who performed his Hajj.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Rifa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and did not perform the Hajj of Islam, and did not bequeath it, is it fulfilled on his behalf? He said: Yes.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Rifa'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man and the woman who die and have not performed Hajj, is the Hajj of Islam fulfilled on their behalf? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about a man who died and left a son who did not know whether his father had performed Hajj or not. He said: 'The son should perform Hajj on his behalf. If his father had already performed Hajj, an optional (Hajj) is recorded for the father, and an obligatory (Hajj) for the son. And if his father had not performed Hajj, an obligatory (Hajj) is recorded for the father, and an optional (Hajj) for the son.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a servant performs Hajj ten times, there would still be upon him the Hajj of Islam as well, when he has the capacity to do so. And if a young boy performs Hajj ten times, then attains puberty, upon him would be the Obligation of Islam. And if an owned slave performs Hajj ten times, then is freed, upon him would be the Obligation of Islam, when he has the capacity for it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever five years pass for him and he does not perform Hajj to his Lord, while he is affluent, indeed he is deprived.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, for Allah there is a Caller who calls out: 'Whichever servant upon whom Allah has bestowed favor and expanded his sustenance, yet does not make a pilgrimage to Him once every five years to seek His additional rewards, that one is indeed deprived.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, caused Adam and his wife to eat of the wheat, He expelled them both from Paradise and caused them to descend to the earth. Adam descended upon al-Safa and Hawwa descended upon al-Marwa. Al-Safa was named thus because it was derived from the name of Adam al-Mustafa (the Chosen), corresponding to the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely Allah chose Adam and Noah.' And al-Marwa was named Marwa because it was derived from the name al-Mar'a (the woman). Adam said: 'Nothing separated me from her except that she is not permissible for me. Had she been permissible for me, she would have descended with me upon al-Safa, but she was forbidden to me because of that, and separation was effected between me and her.' Adam remained isolated from Hawwa. He would visit her during the day, conversing with her upon al-Marwa. But when night came and he feared being overcome by his desires, he would return to al-Safa and sleep there. Adam had no comfort except her, and for that reason women were called 'nisa'', because Hawwa was the 'uns' (companionship/comfort) for Adam. Allah neither spoke to him nor sent him a messenger. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed upon him repentance and conveyed to him certain words. When he spoke these words, Allah turned towards him in mercy and sent Jibraeel (peace be upon him) to him. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O Adam, you who repent from your error and are patient through your tribulation. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent me to you to teach you the rites through which you can be purified.' He took him by his hand and led him to the place of the House (Ka'ba). Allah sent down upon him a cloud that shaded the place of the House, and the cloud was aligned with the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House above). He said: 'O Adam, mark with your foot the area where this cloud has shaded you, for a house of white gem will be brought forth for you, becoming your qibla and the qibla of your offspring after you.' Adam (peace be upon him) did so, and Allah brought forth beneath the cloud a house of white gem. And Allah sent down the Black Stone, which was whiter than milk and more radiant than the sun; it turned black only because the poly

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Qalanisi, from Ali ibn Hassan, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when Adam (peace be upon him) was sent down to the earth, he was sent down upon al-Safa. It is for that reason that al-Safa was named as such, because al-Mustafa (the Chosen One) descended upon it, and the hill was given a name derived from the name of Adam. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah and the family of Ibrahim and the family of Imran above the worlds' [3:33]. And Hawwa (Eve) was sent down upon al-Marwa. Al-Marwa was named 'Marwa' because the woman (al-mar'a) descended upon it, and the hill was given a name derived from the name of the woman. They are two hillocks to the right and left of the Ka'ba. So Adam said, when he was separated from Hawwa: 'Nothing would have separated me from my wife except that she has become forbidden to me.' So he kept away from her, but he would visit her during the day and converse with her. When night came, he feared his soul would overcome him regarding her, so he returned and spent the night upon al-Safa. It is for that reason that women (al-nisa') were named as such, because Adam had no companionship (uns) apart from her. So Adam remained in that state for as long as God willed him to remain. God neither spoke to him nor sent him a messenger, while the Lord, Glorified be He, boasted of his patience to the angels. When the time arrived that God, Mighty and Majestic, intended to accept Adam's repentance, He sent Jibrail (peace be upon him) to him. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O Adam, you who are patient in your tribulation, repentant from your sin! God, Mighty and Majestic, has sent me to you to teach you the rites by which God intends to accept your repentance.' So Jibrail (peace be upon him) took Adam (peace be upon him) by the hand until he brought him to the site of the House (Ka'ba). A cloud descended from the sky and shaded the site of the House. Jibrail (peace be upon him) said: 'O Adam! Mark with your foot where the cloud shades, for it is a qibla for you and for the last of your posterity among your children.' So Adam marked with his foot where the cloud shaded. Then he took him to Mina and showed him the mosque of Mina. He marked with his foot and extended the boundary of the Sac

When Adam circumambulated the House (Kaaba) and arrived at Al-Multazam, Jibrail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Adam, acknowledge your sins to your Lord in this place.' He (the narrator) said: So Adam (peace be upon him) stopped and said: 'O my Lord, for every doer of deeds there is a recompense, and I have done deeds, so what is my recompense?' So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Adam, I have forgiven your sin.' He said: 'O my Lord, and for my children, or for my offspring?' So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Adam, whoever from your offspring comes to this place, acknowledges his sins, and repents just as you repented, then seeks forgiveness, I will forgive him.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Adam departed from Mina, the angels met him and said: 'O Adam! Righteous is your Hajj. But indeed we have performed Hajj of this House before you performed yours by two thousand years.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said: Abu Bilal al-Makki narrated to me saying: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) circumambulate the House (Kaaba), then pray two cycles between the door and the Black Stone. So I said to him: I have not seen any of you pray in this place. He replied: This is the place where Adam's repentance was accepted.

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about Adam (peace be upon him) — when he performed Hajj, with what did he shave his head? So he said: 'Jibreel (peace be upon him) descended unto him with a precious gem (yaquta) from Paradise, and he passed it over his head, and his hair scattered off.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abu Talib, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Hajj by incurring debt, and he had performed the Hajj of Islam. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, Allah will pay off the debt for him, if Allah wills.'

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can a man borrow money and perform Hajj, when there is something behind him that can pay it off on his behalf, in the event that death occurs to him?' He said, 'Yes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man upon whom is a debt; can he borrow and perform Hajj? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is for him a means/asset in wealth, so there is no problem.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hammam, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man has a debt upon him, and wealth presents itself to him; should he pay off his debt or perform Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pay off part of it and perform Hajj with part of it.' I said: 'Supposing it is not enough except for the expenditure of Hajj?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pay off [the debt in] one year and perform Hajj in [another] year.' I said: '(Supposing if) the wealth is given from the Sultan (ruling authority)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from someone else, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'There is a debt upon me, and dirhams come into my hand. If I distribute them among the creditors, nothing will remain. Should I perform Hajj with it, or distribute it among the creditors?' He said: 'Perform Hajj with it, and supplicate to Allah that He should pay off your debt for you.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who borrows money and performs Hajj, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has wealth left behind, and if death were to befall him, it would be paid off from him, so there is no problem.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If one of you makes a profit, he should take something from it, set it aside, and say,

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from a sheikh, who raised the hadith to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), He said to him: 'O so-and-so! Reduce the expenditure in the Hajj so that you will be eager for the Hajj, and do not increase the expenditure in the Hajj so that you will become weary of it.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The sacrificial animal (hady) is from the expenditure of the Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The sacrificial animal (hady) of the Hajj is from the Hajj (expenditure).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Za'lan, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hammad ibn Talha, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Isa! I love that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sees you, in the period between one Hajj and the next, while you are preparing for the Hajj.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Hamza ibn Ya'la, from one of the Kufis, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who returns from Makkah, while intending the Hajj for the coming year, will have his lifespan increased.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who becomes Muslim and intends to perform Hajj, and the season for Hajj has presented itself: should he perform Hajj or be circumcised? He (peace be upon him) said: He should not perform Hajj until he is circumcised.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem if the woman circumambulates without having been circumcised, but as for the man, so he should not circumambulate unless he is circumcised.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who had a husband who refused to give her permission to perform Hajj, and she had not yet performed the Hajj of Islam. So her husband was absent from her, and he had forbidden her to perform Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no obedience to him upon her regarding the Hajj of Islam, so let her perform Hajj if she wishes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman who goes out with someone other than a guardian. He said: There is no problem. If she has a husband or a brother's son who are capable of going out with her, and she has no financial capacity (to pay for their travel), then it is not befitting for her to sit (stay behind), nor is it befitting for them to prevent her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who intends to perform Hajj and has no close male relative (mahram) with her, is it permissible for her to perform Hajj? He said: Yes, if she is trustworthy (safe from fitnah).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the free woman who performs Hajj to Mecca without a guardian, so he said: 'There is no problem with her going out with a reliable group.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A man does not leave behind upon his family with something superior than two Cycles (of Prayer) which he Prays when intending the going out to travel.' He should be saying, 'O Allah! I entrust to You, myself, and my family, and my wealth, and my offspring, and my world, and my Hereafter, and my entrustments, and the completion of my (pending) works' except that Allah would Give him what he asks for'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad Al-Ahowl, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya Al-Ijaly, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), when he intended to travel, would gather his dependents in a room, then say: 'O Allah! I entrust to You this morning my self, my wealth, my family, and my children, the present among us and the absent. O Allah! Protect us and protect upon us. O Allah! Make us in Your vicinity. O Allah! Do not deprive us of Your bounty, and do not change what is with us of Your grace and favor.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is travel disliked on any of the disliked days, such as Wednesday and others?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Begin your travel with charity, and recite the Verse of the Throne when it becomes apparent to you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Give charity and go out on whichever day you desire.'
