A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father used to say: 'He is not regarded (as worthy), the one who leads (prayer) in this House (the Kaaba), if there are not in him three characteristics: good character by which he behaves with his companion, or forbearance by which he controls his anger, or piety which restrains him from the prohibitions of Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He is not regarded (as ready), the one who travels upon this road (to Makkah), if there are not in him three characteristics: piety that restrains him from disobeying Allah, and forbearance by which he controls his anger, and good companionship with those who accompany him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and the House (the Kaaba) was crammed with its people. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not from us, the one who does not have good companionship with the one who accompanies him, and friendly association with the one who associates with him, and eating together with the one who eats with him, and sharing living space with the one who shares living space with him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Select the comrade, then embark on the journey'. And Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not accompany in your journey the one who does not see for you the merit upon him, just as you are seeing the merit for him upon you'.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hariz, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you accompany, so accompany someone like you, and do not accompany the one who suffices (needless) from you, for in that, is humiliation for the Believer.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'You know my situation, the extent of my generosity, and my willingness to provide for my brothers. So, if I accompany a group of them on the road to Mecca, I can extend my generosity upon them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not do it, O Shihab! If you extend (your generosity) and they extend (their expectations), you will burden them; and if they withhold (their share), you will humble them. Therefore, accompany your equals.'

Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man goes out with an affluent group, and he is the least of them in wealth. The group provides the expenditure, and he is not able to provide the like of what they provide.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that he should humiliate himself to go out with those who are like him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said: I accompanied Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and he was heading towards Makkah. So when he prayed, he said: 'O Allah, free our way, and improve our travel, and improve our health.' And every time he ascended a hillock, he said: 'O Allah, for You is the Nobility over every nobility.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), during his journeys, when he descended [from a height], he would glorify [Allah], and when he ascended, he would proclaim the Greatness [of Allah].

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Qasim al-Sayrafi, from Hafs ibn al-Qasim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon the height of every bridge is a devil. So whenever you reach it, say, "In the Name of Allah," he will move away from you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Say: O Allah, I ask You for conviction for myself, and forgiveness, and well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, You are my trust, and You are my hope, and You are my support, and You are my helper. With You I disembark and with You I travel. He (peace be upon him) said: And whoever goes out on a journey alone, let him say: 'Whatever Allah wills, there is no strength except by Allah. O Allah, comfort my loneliness, and help me in my solitude, and complete my absence (from home).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Hajj is in the well-known months: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijja. It is not for anyone to perform Hajj in what is besides these.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Hajj is (performed in) the well-known months' so whoever determines the performance of the Hajj therein And the Obligation is the Talbiyya, and the Ish'ar, and the Taqlid So whoever does that, so he has done the Hajj and the Hajj is not determined except during these months which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says are 'the well-known months' and these are Shawwal, and Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah

Ali ibn Ibrahim, by his chain, said: The months for the Hajj are Shawwal, and Dhu al-Qadah, and ten (days) from Dhu al-Hijja; and the months for visitations are twenty (days) from Dhu al-Hijja, and Al-Muharram, and Safar, and the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten (days) from the month of Rabi' al-Akhar.

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the Sanctuary and its boundary markers — how some came to be closer than others and some farther apart He said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, caused Adam to descend from Paradise, he descended upon Mount Abu Qubays. He complained to his Lord of loneliness and that he could no longer hear what he used to hear in Paradise. So God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down upon him a red ruby, and he placed it at the site of the House (Kaaba). Adam used to circumambulate it, and its light reached the locations of the boundary markers — thus the boundary markers were set according to its light, and God made it a Sanctuary. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hammam Ismail ibn Hammam al-Kindi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): similar to this.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Jibraeel (peace be upon him): 'I am Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I have had mercy on Adam and Hawwa when they complained to Me of what they complained. So descend upon them with a tent from the tents of Paradise, and console them from Me due to the separation from Paradise, and gather both of them in the tent, for I have had mercy on them due to their weeping and their fear in their loneliness.' And the tent was pitched upon al-Tur'a which is between the mountains of Makkah. He said: Al-Tur'a is the place of the House (Kaaba) and its foundations which the Angels had raised before Adam. So Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended upon Adam with the tent, to the measurement of the corners of the House and its foundations, and he pitched it. He said: And Jibraeel brought down Adam from al-Safa and brought down Hawwa from al-Marwa, and gathered both of them in the tent. He said: And the pole of the tent was a rod of red ruby, so its light and radiance illuminated the mountains of Makkah and what surrounded them. He said: And the light of the pole extended — so it marks the places of the Sanctuary today, from every direction, from wherever the light of the pole reached. He said: Thus Allah made it a Sanctuary due to the sanctity of the tent and the pole, because both of them were from Paradise. He said: And because of that, Allah Mighty and Majestic made the good deeds in the Sanctuary to be multiplied and the evil deeds multiplied. He said: And the ropes of the tent were extended around it, so the ends of its pegs reached what is around the Sacred Mosque today. He said: And its pegs were of pure gold from Paradise and its ropes were of purple braids. He said: And Allah Mighty and Majestic revealed to Jibraeel (peace be upon him): 'Descend upon the tent with seventy thousand angels to guard it from the rebellious devils, and to comfort Adam, and to circumambulate around the tent in reverence of the House and the tent.' So he descended with the angels, and they were present at the tent, guarding it from the insolent rebellious devils, and circumambulating around the corners of the House and the tent every day and night, just as they circumambulated in the heavens around the Frequented House (Bayt al-Ma'mur). He said: The corners of the Sacred House on earth are directly beneath the Frequented House which is in the heav

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Hajj is of three types: Hajj al-Mufrad, Hajj al-Qiran, and Hajj al-Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj. And with these, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered, and the merit is in them, and we do not command the people except with them.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Mansur Al-Sayqal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj with us is upon three types: a Mutamatti' pilgrim, and a Mufrid pilgrim who brings the sacrifice, and a Mufrid pilgrim for Hajj.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Which type of Hajj is superior?' He said: 'Al-Tamattu'. And how can anything be superior to it, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If I had faced from my affairs what I faced, I would have done what the people did.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not know of a Hajj for Allah other than Al-Mut'ah. When we meet our Lord, we will say: 'Our Lord, we acted by Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet,' while the people will say: 'We acted by our own opinions.' So Allah will place us and them wherever He wills.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever performs Hajj, let him perform Tamattu'; indeed, we do not compromise with the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Some people say: Perform the Hajj exclusively (Qiran), and some people say: Pair it and bring the sacrificial animal, and some people say: Perform Tamattu' with the Umra until the Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If I were to perform Hajj for a thousand years, I would not pair it except as a Mutamatti'.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who said: 'Ali ibn Muyassar wrote to him, asking him about a man who performed 'Umra during the month of Ramadan, then the season (for Hajj) presented itself to him. Should he perform Hajj exclusively (Ifrad) for Hajj, or should he perform Tamattu'? Which of the two is superior? So he wrote to him: 'Performing Tamattu' is superior.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Hajj, so he said: 'Perform Tamattu'. Then he said: 'When we stand before Allah, Exalted and Majestic, we say: O Lord, we held fast to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, while the people say: We acted according to our own opinions.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Mut'ah, by Allah, is superior, and with it the Quran was revealed, and the Sunnah proceeded.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the year in which he performed Hajj, and that was in the year two hundred and twelve. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! By which method did you enter Mecca: exclusively (Mufrid) or for Tamattu'?' He said, 'For Tamattu'. I said to him, 'Which of the two is superior: the one who performs Tamattu with Umrah until Hajj, or the one who performs exclusively and brings the sacrificial animal?' He said, 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: The one who performs Tamattu with Umrah until Hajj is superior to the one who performs exclusively and brings the sacrificial animal. And he used to say: The pilgrim does not enter with anything more superior than Tamattu'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abdul Malik ibn Amr, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): About performing Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform Tamattu'.' He said, 'So it happened that he (peace be upon him) performed the exclusive Hajj in that year or after it, so I said, 'May Allah keep you well! I asked you and you instructed me with Tamattu', and I see you to have performed the exclusive Hajj this year?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'But, by Allah, the merit is in that which I had instructed you with, but I am (physically) weak, so it was difficult upon me, the two circumambulations between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, therefore, due to that, I performed the exclusive Hajj'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from his uncle Ubaydullah, that he said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I was present, so he said, 'I performed Umrah in the Sacred Months, and now I have arrived as a Mutamatti' (one who combines Umrah and Hajj). So I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, 'Good is what you have done. We do not compromise with the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So when our Lord resurrects us, or we return to our Lord, we shall say: 'O Lord! We held fast to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family),' and the people would say, 'We followed our own opinions.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will deal with us and with them as He wills.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fadl Al-Hashimi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) along with my brothers, so we said, 'We intend the Hajj, and some of us are Sarurah (those who have not performed Hajj before).' He said: 'Upon you is the Tamattu', for we do not fear a Sultan (ruling authority) regarding the Tamattu with the Umrah to the Hajj, and keeping away from the intoxicants, and the wiping upon the two socks.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who does not have a sacrificial animal with him and performs exclusive (Hajj) turning away from the Tamattu', so he has turned away from the Religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Umayr, from Muawiya, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'They say regarding the Hajj of the Mutamatti' that his Hajj is Makki and his Umrah is Iraqi.' He said, 'They are lying. Is it not so that it is linked? He does not exit from it until he fulfills his Hajj.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abdul Malik ibn Ayn, who said: A group of our companions performed Hajj. So when they arrived in Medina, they visited Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'Zurara instructed us to begin with the Hajj (by saying 'Labbayk Hajj') when we enter the state of Ihram.' So he (peace be upon him) said to them, 'Perform Tamattu'.' So when they left his presence, I entered upon him and said, 'May I be your ransom! If you do not inform them with what you informed Zurara, we will go to Kufa and they will consider him a liar.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Bring them back.' So they entered upon him, and he (peace be upon him) said, 'Zurara spoke the truth.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, no one will hear this from me after this day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan who said: A group of our companions performed Hajj, and when they arrived in Madinah, they visited Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). They said, 'Zurarah commanded us to commence our Hajj with Talbiyah when we entered the state of Ihram.' He (the Imam) said to them, 'Perform Hajj al-Tamattu'.' When they left from his presence, I entered upon him and said, 'May I be your ransom, if you do not inform them of what you informed Zurarah, we will surely go to Kufah and make him a liar.' He said, 'Call them back.' So they entered upon him, and he said, 'Zurarah has spoken the truth.' Then he said, 'By Allah, no one will hear this from me after this day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Safwan, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Upon the one performing Tamattu' (Umrah to Hajj) are three circumambulations of the House and two Sa'ees between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. And upon him, when he arrives in Mecca, is one circumambulation of the House, two Rak'ahs at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and one Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. Then he shortens (his hair/nails), and this is permissible for the Umrah. And upon him, for the Hajj, are two circumambulations and one Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. And he prays two Rak'ahs at each circumambulation of the House, at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The performer of Tamattu' upon him are three circumambulations of the House, and two circumambulations (Sa'ee) between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, and the cutting off of the Talbiyah from his Tamattu' when he looks at the houses of Makkah, and he enters into Ihram with the Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyyah, and he cuts off the Talbiyah on the Day of Arafah when the sun declines.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Upon the one performing Tamattu' with Umrah to Hajj are three circumambulations of the House, and he prays two cycles for each circumambulation, and two Sa'ees between As-Safa and Al-Marwa.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Qarin (one who performs Hajj al-Qiran) is not [valid] except with the ushering of the sacrificial animal, and upon him are two circumambulations of the House and one Sa'ee between al-Safa and al-Marwa, just as the Mufrid does; he is not superior to the Mufrid except by the ushering of the sacrificial animal.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Muqarin (one who performs Hajj al-Qiran) does not have [his status] except with the accompanying sacrificial animal, and upon him is circumambulation of the House, and two cycles of prayer at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and circumambulation after Hajj, and it is the circumambulation of the women.

Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I drove the sacrificial animal, and I performed the pairing (Qiran).' He said, 'And why did you do that? The Tamattu' is superior.' Then he said, 'It will suffice you therein with one circumambulation of the House and one Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa.' And he said, 'Circumambulate the Ka'bah on the Day of Sacrifice.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have purchased a camel, so what should I do with it?' He said: 'Go until you reach Masjid Al-Shajara, pour water over yourself, and wear your two garments. Then kneel it facing the Qiblah. Then enter the mosque, pray, then complete your prayer. Then go out to it and mark it from the right side of its hump. Then say: 'In the Name of Allah, O Allah, from You and to You. O Allah, accept from me.' Then go until you reach Al-Bayda', and recite the Talbiyyah.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about decorating the sacrificial animal and yoking it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not matter which of those you do.' And I asked him about marking the sacrificial animal, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, from the right side.' So I said, 'When should we mark it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you intend to enter the state of Ihram.'

Aban, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, and Zurara, said: We asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the sacrificial camel: how is it marked, and when does its owner enter the state of Ihram, and from which side is it marked, and is it sacrificed while tied down (ma'qulah) or kneeling (barikah)? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is sacrificed while tied down, and it is marked from the right side.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the sacrificial camel (budn), how is it marked? He said: It is marked while it is tied down, and it is slaughtered while it is standing. It is marked from its right side, and its owner enters into Ihram when it is yoked and marked.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the sacrificial camels are many, he stands between two of them, then marks the right one, then the left one. And he does not mark until he is ready for the Ihram, because when he marks, and yokes, and decorates, the Ihram becomes obligatory upon him, and it is in the status of the Talbiyyah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The sacrificial camel is marked from the right side, and the man stands on its left side. Then he yokes it with an old slipper in which he has prayed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj al-Ifrad. He arrived in Mecca, circumambulated the House, prayed two cycles near the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and performed Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him exit Ihram and make it a Tamattu' Hajj, unless he had brought the sacrificial animal (Hady).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who circumambulates the House and [performs the walk] between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa is released [from Ihram], whether he likes it or not.'

Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from the one who informed him, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: ‘Whoever performs Tawaf (circumambulation) between these two stones, Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, is released from Ihram, except for the one who is ushering the sacrificial animal (Qarin/Mufrid with Hady).’

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Tamattu' (Hajj al-Tamattu') for the people of Sarif, nor for the people of Marr, nor for the people of Mecca. That is for him whose family is not present in the Sacred Mosque.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked, 'Is there Tamattu' for the people of Makkah?' He said: 'No, and neither for the people of Bustan, nor for the people of Zat Irqin, nor for the people of Usfan, and those similar to them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'That is for him whose family is not present in the Sacred Masjid,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whose dwelling is eighteen miles in front of it, and eighteen miles behind it, and eighteen miles to its right, and eighteen miles to its left, so there is no Tamattu' for him, like Marr and what resembles it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Dawood, from Hammad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the people of Makkah: do they perform Tamattu'? He said: 'There is no Tamattu' for them.' I said: 'And the one who resides in it?' He said: 'When he stays in it for a year or two years, he does as the people of Makkah do.' I said: 'And if he stays for a month?' He said: 'He performs Tamattu'.' I said: 'From where?' He said: 'He exits from the Haram.' I said: 'Where does he begin with the Hajj?' He said: 'From Makkah, in the manner that the people say.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who resides in Mecca for a year should perform the deed of the people of Mecca, meaning he should perform the exclusive Hajj (Hajj al-Fard) with the people of Mecca, and whoever stays for less than a year, then for him is that he should perform Tamattu' (the Hajj of Tamattu').

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the Muqim (resident of Makkah), is it for him to perform Tamattu' with the Umrah until the Hajj? He said: Yes. He goes out to the boundary of his land, so he pronounces the Talbiyah if he wishes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever enters Mecca for Hajj on behalf of another, then stays for a year, he is considered a resident of Mecca (Makki). So when he intends to perform Hajj for himself, or intends to perform Umrah after having left from Arafat, it is not for him to enter the state of Ihram in Mecca, but he must go out to the Miqat (juncture), and every time he turns back, he must return to the Miqat.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Abu Al-Fazl, who said: I was residing in Makkah, so I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'From where should I enter the state of Ihram for Hajj?' He said: 'From where the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Ihram, from Al-Ji'ranah. Victories came to him in that place: the conquest of Al-Ta'if, and the conquest of Khaybar, and the Conquest [of Makkah].' So I said, 'When shall I depart?' He said: 'If you are a first-time pilgrim (Sarr), then when one day of Dhu al-Hijjah has passed, and if you have performed Hajj before that, then when five days have passed from the month.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The resident of Makkah, when he enters it for Umrah during the months other than the Hajj months — in Rajab or Sha'ban or the month of Ramadan or any other of the months except the Hajj months, for indeed the Hajj months are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah — whoever enters it for Umrah during the months other than the Hajj months, then intends to enter the state of Ihram, let him go out to Al-Ji'ranah and enter Ihram from there. Then he should come to Makkah and not break the Talbiyah until he looks at the House. Then he should circumambulate the House and pray two Rak'at at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Then he should go out to As-Safa and Al-Marwa and circumambulate between them. Then he should shorten (his hair/nails) and free himself (from Ihram). Then he should renew the Talbiyah on the Day of Tarwiyah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: When a man performs Hajj with his son and he is young, he should instruct him to recite the Talbiyyah and to perform the Hajj as obligatory. If he is not proficient in reciting the Talbiyyah, it should be recited on his behalf, circumambulation should be performed for him, and prayer should be offered on his behalf. I asked, 'Is there not for them [the children] what they should slaughter?' He said: 'Slaughter should be offered on behalf of the young ones, and the adults should fast, and the prohibitions that apply to the one in Ihram regarding clothing and perfume should be observed for them. If they kill game, the expiation is upon their father.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Ayoub, brother of Adeym, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, 'From where should the children undress (and wear Ihram)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father used to get them to undress (and wear Ihram) from Fakkhan'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from his father who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have young children with me and I fear the cold for them. From where should they enter the state of Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Take them to Al-Araj so they may enter Ihram from it, for when you reach Al-Araj, you enter Tihama.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'And if you fear for them, take them to Al-Juhfa.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Look at the children who are with you, and send them to Al-Juhfa or to Batin Marra, and do with them what is done with the Muhrim (one in Ihram), circumambulate with them, and throw stones on their behalf. And whoever among them cannot find a sacrifice, let his guardian fast on his behalf. And Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) would place the knife in the hand of the child, then a man would hold his hands, so he would slaughter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: There is neither Hajj nor Umrah upon the owned slave until he is freed.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about boys of ours who entered Makkah with us for Umrah, and they went out with us to 'Arafat without being in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Tell them to perform Ghusl, then enter into Ihram, and slaughter a sacrifice on their behalf just as you slaughter for yourselves.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Everything that befalls the slave while he is in the state of Ihram, the expiation is upon the master, if he permitted him to enter into Ihram.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a slave of ours whom I took with me, and I ordered him, so he performed Tamattu' and entered into Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, and I did not slaughter on his behalf. Is it for him to fast after the departure, and the days mentioned by Allah, Exalted and Mighty, have passed? He said: Why did you not order him to perform the exclusive Hajj? I said: I sought the goodness. He said: Just as you sought the goodness, so slaughter a fat sheep, and that would be on the last day of departure.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah, that he was asked about a man who ordered his young slaves to perform Tamattu' Hajj, He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon him to sacrifice on their behalf.' I said, 'Suppose he gave them dirhams, and some of them sacrificed, and some of them kept the dirhams and fasted?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It suffices him from them, and he is at choice; if he wishes, he can leave it (the money with them).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he ordered them and they fasted, it would have sufficed him from them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man who has not yet performed Hajj (Sarurat), performing Hajj on behalf of the deceased. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if the Sarurat does not have what he can perform Hajj with for himself. But if he has what he can perform Hajj with for himself, then it is not sufficient for him until he performs Hajj from his own wealth. And it is sufficient on behalf of the deceased, whether the Sarurat has wealth or if he does not have wealth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died as a Saroura (one who has not yet performed Hajj) and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and he had wealth, he (peace be upon him) said: A Saroura (one who has not yet performed Hajj) would perform Hajj on his behalf, the one who does not have any wealth.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and bequeaths a Hajj, so a man is given dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf, but he dies before performing Hajj, then the dirhams are given to another. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he died in the way or in Makkah before fulfilling its rituals, then it suffices for the first one.' I said: 'If he was afflicted with something that invalidates his Hajj until the Hajj of the next year becomes obligatory upon him, does it suffice for the first one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Because the hired one is responsible for the Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who gave a man what he could perform Hajj with, so an event occurred with the man, he said: If he had set out and was hit (died) on part of the road, then it suffices for the first (deceased), and otherwise, no.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Ayoub, from Bureyd al-Ijli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who entrusted wealth to me, so he died, and there was nothing for his children, and he had not performed the Hajj of Islam. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform Hajj on his behalf, and whatever remains, give it to them.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah — from Muhammad ibn Abi Yusr — from Dawud ibn Abdillah — from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Muhammad — from Isa ibn Yunus, who said: Ibn Abi al-Awja was among the students of al-Hasan al-Basri, but he deviated from monotheism. It was said to him: 'You have abandoned the school of your teacher and entered into something that has no foundation.' He said: 'My teacher was confused; sometimes he would speak of predestination (qadar), and sometimes he would say: the matter is not up to me. I do not know the truth of his affair.' When he arrived at the House — meaning during the season of pilgrimage — he saw the people in their circumambulation, their running, and their supplications, and he said: 'O Abu Abdillah, who are these people who circle around this stone, rub themselves against it, and rush toward it like the rushing of the wind? Are these not people of reason?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'These are the ones whom Allah intended from among His servants, and He made this House into watering places for the drawing of their religious obligations. Then they frequented it as the station of His prophets, and He beckoned them toward competing in closeness to Him, and He thickened its structure so that it would be a symbol for the continuance of worship in honor of it. It is the place of response for those who answered Him from the ancients and the latter ones. There is no believer except that his heart yearns toward it and longs for it.' 'Do you not know that Allah loves to be obeyed from where He has commanded and to be feared where He has forbidden, and it is not for anyone to go beyond His command to something other than His command? Have you not heard Allah say: "And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers"?' He (the narrator) said: Ibn Abi al-Awja gave him no response.

And it is reported that the Commander of the Faithful (may God's blessings be upon him) said in one of his sermons: Had God, Majestic is His praise, intended for His prophets, when He sent them, to open for them the treasures of gold and the mines of pure ore and the plantations of gardens, and to gather the birds of the sky and the beasts of the land along with them — He would have done so. But had He done so, trials would have ceased, recompense would have been nullified, tidings (divine commandments) would have dissolved, those who merely profess belief would not have merited the rewards of those truly tested, believers would not have attained the reward of the righteous, and names (titles of honor) would not have been binding upon those who deserve them with a clear meaning. For that reason, had God sent down a sign from the sky that caused their necks to bow in submission, had He done that, the trials would have been lifted from all people altogether. But God, Majestic is His praise, made His messengers possessors of strength in the resolve of their intentions yet appearing weak in what the eyes could observe of their outward condition — a contentment whose self-sufficiency fills the hearts and the eyes, and a poverty whose hardship fills the ears and the sight. Had the prophets been people of invincible strength and unassailable might, and had they possessed a dominion toward which men's necks would crane and to which the belts of their mounts would be drawn tight, it would have been easier upon creation in the matter of trial and would have kept them further from arrogance, and they would have believed out of an overpowering dread upon them or an inclining desire — and so intentions would have been mixed and good deeds divided. But God willed that the following of His messengers, the affirmation of His books, the humility before His countenance, the submission to His command, and the surrender to His obedience be matters belonging exclusively to Him, untainted by any other admixture. And the greater the trial and the test, the more abundant the reward and the recompense. Do you not see that God, Majestic is His praise, tested the earliest of mankind from the time of Adam to the last of them in this world, with stones that neither harm nor benefit, neither see nor hear? He made them into His Sacred House which He established for people as a place of st

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Riab, from Musadif, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who performs Hajj on behalf of the man who has not performed it (Saroura), he said: 'If she had already performed Hajj, and she was a Muslim, an understanding one (faqeehah); for there are women who are more understanding than men.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The man performs Hajj on behalf of the woman, and the woman performs Hajj on behalf of the man.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman from our family, her brother died and he bequeathed [the cost of] a Hajj, and the woman had already performed Hajj. She said: 'If I am well, I will perform Hajj on behalf of my brother, and I am more rightful to it than others.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if she performs Hajj on behalf of her brother; and if she has wealth, let her perform Hajj from her own wealth, for it is greater for her reward.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The woman performs Hajj on behalf of her brother and on behalf of her sister. And he said: The woman performs Hajj on behalf of her son.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)... ...regarding a man who gave a man dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf, an exclusive Hajj. Would it be permissible for him to perform Tamattu' with Umrah to Hajj? He said: Yes, he merely differed from him in performing the more meritorious one.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Hariz, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave a man money for Hajj to perform Hajj on his behalf from Al-Kufa, but he performed Hajj on his behalf from Al-Basra. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, if he fulfills all its rituals, then his Hajj is complete.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who died and bequeathed a Hajj. Is it permissible that Hajj be performed on his behalf from other than the city in which he died? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is below the Miqat, so there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim from Salih ibn Al-Sindi from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Aban ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who was bequeathed a Hajj, but did not have sufficiency (of funds) to perform it from Al-Kufa, that it would suffice for him to perform Hajj from besides the juncture.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf, the Hajj of Islam, but the entirety of what he left did not reach (the required amount), except for fifty Dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform Hajj on his behalf from one of the junctures which Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used as a juncture (to wear Ihram), from nearby'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, or from a man, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Saeed, from the one who asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed twenty dirhams for Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man should perform Hajj with it from a place where its required expenditure would suffice it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Ahmad, son of Muhammad, from Muhammad, son of Ismail, who said: I instructed a man to ask Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who takes the responsibility for performing a Hajj from one man, but it is not sufficient for him. Is it permissible for him to take from another man and increase the capacity with it, and it would suffice for both of them together, or to share both of them if one of them does not suffice him? So he mentioned that he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is more beloved to me that it be exclusive to one. And if it does not suffice him, then he should not take it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ja'far al-Ahowl, from Usman ibn Isa, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the man who is given the responsibility of performing Hajj, but he hands it over to someone else?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhassin ibn Ahmad from Aban from Umar ibn Yazeed who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man is bequeathed a Hajj, but it does not suffice for it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So he should proceed with it until he performs Hajj before the time [is due/ends].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Does a man perform Hajj on behalf of the Nasibi?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'No.' I said, 'And if it was my father?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So if it was your father, then yes.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I wrote to him, 'A man performs Hajj on behalf of the Nasibi (Hostile one), would there be a sin upon him when he performs Hajj on behalf of the Nasibi, and would that be beneficial to the Nasibi or not?' So he wrote: 'Do not perform Hajj on behalf of the Nasibi, nor perform Hajj with him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'Your Mawla, Ali ibn Mahziyar, bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf from an estate, a quarter of which is designated for you, for one Hajj each year, up to twenty Dinars. And that the road to Al-Basra was cut off, causing the expenses to double upon the people, so twenty Dinars are no longer sufficient. And several of your Mawali have bequeathed similarly regarding their Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Make three Hajjs count as two, God willing.'

Ibrahim said, And Ali ibn Muhammad al-Husayni wrote to him that, 'A cousin of mine bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf with fifteen dinars in every year, but it does not suffice, so what are your orders regarding that?' So he wrote: 'He should make two Hajjs to be regarded as one Hajj, Allah is Knowing of that.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'When a man performs Hajj on behalf of his brother, or his father, or a man from the people, is it befitting for him to say something?' He said, 'Yes. He should say after entering into Ihram: O Allah, whatever befalls me during this journey of mine from fatigue, or hardship, or affliction, or untidiness, then recompense so-and-so for it, and recompense me for fulfilling it on his behalf.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi – similar to it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is obligatory upon the one who performs Hajj on behalf of a man?' He said, 'He should name him in the places and the stations.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to him, 'Do you see the one who performs Hajj on behalf of his father, or his mother, or his brother, or others, should he say something?' He said, 'Yes. He should say when he enters the state of Ihram: O Allah, whatever hardship, or untidiness, or difficulty befalls me, reward so-and-so for it, and reward me for my performance on his behalf.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yahya Al-Azraq, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'If a man performs Hajj on behalf of another man, is it permissible for him to perform Tawaf on behalf of his relatives?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he has completed the rituals of Hajj, let him do whatever he wishes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya raised it (narrated it) and said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who gave wealth to a man to perform Hajj on his behalf, but he performed Hajj for himself. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It would be (reckoned as being) on behalf of the owner of the wealth'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Mansur bin al-Abbas, from Ali bin Asbaat, from a man from our companions called Abdul Rahman bin Sinan, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), when a man came to him and gave him thirty dinars to perform Hajj on behalf of Ismail. He did not leave out anything from the Umrah to the Hajj except that he stipulated it upon him, to the extent that he stipulated upon him that he should perform Sa'i from the valley of Muhassar. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O this man! When you do this, it will be a Hajj for Ismail with whatever he spent from his wealth, and for you will be nine (times as much) with what you exhaust yourself from your body.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yusuf, from Abu Abdullah al-Mumin, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'For the man who performs Hajj on behalf of another, what is his recompense and reward?' He said, 'For the one who performs Hajj on behalf of a man is the recompense and reward of ten Hajjs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abduwayh ibn Amir and others, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all of them from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Ismail was born, Ibrahim carried him and his mother upon a donkey, and Jibrail came with him until he placed him at the location of the Hijr, and with him was some provisions and a waterskin containing some water. The House in those days was a red hillock of mud. Ibrahim said to Jibrail (peace be upon him): 'Is it here that you were commanded?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: And in those days, Mecca was covered in Salam and Samur trees, and around Mecca in those days were people from the Amalekites. And in another narration from him as well, he said: When Ibrahim turned to leave, Hajar said: O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us? He said: I am leaving you both to the Lord of this House. He said: So when the water ran out and the boy became thirsty, she went out until she ascended al-Safa and called out: Is there anyone kind in the valley? Then she descended until she came to al-Marwa and called out similarly. Then she turned back to her son, and behold, his heel was kicking in water. So she gathered it, and it accumulated — and had she left it, it would have flowed away.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) left Ismail at Makkah, the child became thirsty. There was a tree between al-Safa and al-Marwa. So his mother went out and stood upon al-Safa, saying: 'Is there anyone in the valleys who is kind?' But no one answered her. So she proceeded until she reached al-Marwa, and said: 'Is there anyone in the valleys who is kind?' But she received no answer. Then she returned to al-Safa and said the same thing, doing this seven times. God then established this as a sunnah. Jibrail (peace be upon him) came to her and said: 'Who are you?' She replied: 'I am the mother of a son of Ibrahim.' He said to her: 'To whom did he leave you?' She said: 'Since you ask, I did say to him when he intended to leave, O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us? He said: To God, the Mighty and Majestic.' So Jibrail (peace be upon him) said: 'He has indeed entrusted you to One Who Suffices.' He (the Imam) said: The people used to avoid the path to Makkah due to the lack of water. The child kicked with his foot and Zamzam gushed forth. He said: She returned from al-Marwa to the child, and the water had already flowed. So she began gathering soil around it, fearing the water would drain away — had she left it, it would have become a free-flowing stream. He said: When the birds saw the water, they circled above it. A caravan from Yemen, intending to travel, passed by. When they saw the birds, they said: 'Birds only circle like that over water.' So they came to them. Hagar's group gave them water to drink, and the caravan fed them from their food. God, the Mighty and Majestic, established for them through this a means of livelihood. And the people would pass through Makkah, and they would feed them from food and give them water to drink.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to perform the Hajj and to bring Ismail with him to perform it, and to settle him in the Sacred Precincts. So they performed the Hajj on a red camel, with none accompanying them except Jibra'il (peace be upon him). When they reached the Sacred Precincts, Jibra'il said to him: 'O Ibrahim, dismount and perform the ritual bath before They both entered the Sacred Sanctuary and dismounted, then performed the ritual bath. Jibra'il showed them how to prepare for the ihram, and they did so. Then he commanded them to enter into ihram for the Hajj and instructed them in the four talbiyahs with which the Messengers had made the proclamation. Then he led them to al-Safa where they stopped. Jibra'il stood between them, faced the House, and proclaimed Allahu Akbar — and they both did likewise. He said 'La ilaha illa Allah' — they followed. He praised Allah and they praised. He glorified and they glorified. He exalted Allah, and they did the same. Jibra'il advanced and they advanced with him, praising and glorifying Allah the Mighty and Majestic, until he brought them to the Black Stone. Jibra'il reverently touched the Stone and commanded them both to do likewise. He then led them in seven circuits of circumambulation, then stood with them at the station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and prayed two rak'ahs — and they both prayed. He then showed them all the rites and what they should do. When they had completed their rites, Allah commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to depart. Isma'il remained alone, with no one but his mother. In the following year, Allah gave Ibrahim (peace be upon him) permission for the Hajj and the building of the Ka'ba. The Arabs had been performing pilgrimage to it, though it was only a heap of rubble — its foundations were still recognizable. When the people departed, Isma'il gathered the stones and placed them inside the Ka'ba. When Allah granted them permission for the construction, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) arrived and said: 'O my son, Allah has commanded us to build the Ka'ba.' They cleared it and found a single red stone. Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'Place its foundation upon it.' Allah sent down four angels to gather the stones for him. Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both) laid the stones while the angels handed them stones, until it reached

Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ibrahim to build the Kaaba and to raise its foundations and show the people their rituals. So Ibrahim and Ismail built the House every day, course by course, until they reached the place of the Black Stone. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Then Mount Abu Qubays called out to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'There is a trust with me for you!' So it gave him the Stone, and he placed it in its place. Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) called out among the people for the Hajj and said: 'O people! I am Ibrahim, the Friend of God! God commands you to perform the Hajj of this House, so perform its Hajj!' So those who would perform Hajj until the Day of Resurrection answered him, and the first to answer him were from the people of Yemen. He said: And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) performed the Hajj — he himself, his family, and his children. So whoever claims that the one to be slaughtered was Ishaq — it would have been from this very place he was slaughtered. And it is mentioned from Abu Basir that he heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) both claiming that it was Ishaq, while Zurara claimed that it was Ismail.

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — meaning al-Ridha — said to al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm: 'Which thing is al-Sakina in your view?' He said: 'I do not know, may I be your ransom, and what is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A fragrant wind that comes out from Paradise, possessing a form like the face of a human being. It accompanies the Prophets, and it is that which descended upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he built the Kaaba — it began guiding thus and thus, and so he built the foundation upon it.' [Second chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat] He said: 'I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-Sakina, and he mentioned similar to it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them both) were commanded to build the House and its building was completed, Ibrahim sat upon a corner, then called out: 'Come for the Hajj! Come for the Hajj!' Had he called out 'Come all of you to the Hajj!', none would have performed Hajj except those who were in those days human beings in physical form. But he called out: 'Come for the Hajj!' Thus the people responded from within the backs of men: 'Here I am, O Inviter to God! Here I am, O Inviter to God, Mighty and Majestic!' So whoever responded ten times will perform Hajj ten times, and whoever responded five times will perform Hajj five times, and whoever responded more than that will perform Hajj by that count, and whoever responded once will perform Hajj once, and whoever did not respond will not perform Hajj.

From him, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Kaaba, in the era of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), was nine cubits, and it had two doors. Then Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr rebuilt it and raised it to eighteen cubits. Then al-Hajjaj demolished it and rebuilt it to twenty-seven cubits.

It is reported from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The height of the Kaaba in those days was nine cubits, and there was no roof for it. So the Quraysh placed a roof on it of eighteen cubits. Then it did not cease to be so, until al-Hajjaj demolished it in his campaign against Ibn al-Zubayr, and rebuilt it and made it twenty-seven cubits.

(Abu Baseer) heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) mentioning: When it was the Day of al-Tarwiya, Jibrail said to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Quench yourself with water' — so it was named al-Tarwiya. Then he went to Mina and lodged overnight there. Then in the morning he took him to Arafat and pitched his tent at Namira, before Arafat. He built a mosque with white stones, and the traces of Ibrahim's mosque were recognizable until it was incorporated into this mosque at Namira where the Imam prays on the Day of Arafat. He prayed Zuhr and Asr there. Then he proceeded to Arafat and said: 'This is Arafat — acknowledge your rites here and confess your sins' — so it was named Arafat. Then he departed to al-Muzdalifa — so it was named al-Muzdalifa because he approached (izdalaf) it. Then he stood at al-Mash'ar al-Haram; God commanded him to slaughter his son, while he had seen in him his noble traits and character and had grown fond of him. When morning came, he departed from al-Mash'ar to Mina and said to his mother: 'Visit the House (Kaaba) — you go — and keep the boy here.' Then he said: 'O my son! Bring the donkey and the knife so I may offer the sacrifice.' Aban said: So I asked Abu Baseer: 'What did he mean by the donkey and the knife?' He said: 'He intended to slaughter him, then carry him on it, prepare him, and bury him.' Ismail replied: 'You will find me, if God wills, among the patient ones.' He said: When Ibrahim resolved to carry out the slaughter, [Ismail] said: 'O my father, cover my face and bind my restraints.' [Ibrahim] said: 'O my dear son, binding and slaughter together — by God, I will not combine them both upon you today!' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: He spread the donkey's saddle-pad for him, laid him upon it, took the knife, and placed it against his throat. Then an old man came forward and said: 'What do you intend with this young man?' [Ibrahim] said: 'I intend to slaughter him.' The man said: 'Glory be to God! A youth who has not disobeyed God in the twinkling of an eye — and you would slaughter him?' [Ibrahim] said: 'Yes, God has commanded me to slaughter him.' The man said: 'Rather, your Lord has forbidden you from slaughtering him. It is only Satan who commanded you this in your dream.' [Ibrahim] said: 'Woe to you! The words I heard are what brought me to the state you see. No, by God, I will not speak t

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Where did Ibrahim (peace be upon him) intend to slaughter his son?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon the middle Jamarah.' And I asked him about the ram of Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'What was its color, and where did it descend?' He said: 'It was white, and it was horned, and it descended from the sky upon the right mountain of the Masjid of Mina. It walked in darkness, ate in darkness, looked in darkness, excreted in darkness, and urinated in darkness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ismail (peace be upon him) buried his mother in Al-Hijr, and built a chamber upon it, lest the grave of the mother of Ismail (peace be upon him) be trampled upon in Al-Hijr.

One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Hijr is the house of Ismail, and therein is the grave of Hajar, and the grave of Ismail.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Hijr: is it part of the House (Kaaba), or is there something (else) from the House in it? He said: No, not even (the size of) a nail clipping. But Ismail (peace be upon him) buried his mother in it, and he disliked that it should be trampled upon, so he built a chamber upon it. And therein are the graves of the Prophets (peace be upon them).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid Shabab al-Sayrafi, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The virgin daughters of Ismail (peace be upon him) are buried in Al-Hijr, in the section adjacent to the third corner (of the Kaaba).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The children of Ismail (peace be upon him) did not cease to be the governors of the House, and they established for the people their Hajj and the matters of their religion, inheriting it from an elder to an elder, until the time of Adnan ibn Uddad. So the term prolonged upon them, their hearts hardened, they became corrupt, and innovated in their religion, and expelled one another. Thus, from them were some who went out seeking livelihood, and from them were some who went out disliking fighting. And in their hands were many things from the Hanifiyyah (uprightness), from the prohibition of mothers and daughters and whatever Allah prohibited in marriage, except that they permitted the wife of the father, and the daughter of the sister, and joining between two sisters. And in their hands was the Hajj, and the Talbiyyah, and the Ghusl from the Janabah, except what they innovated in their Talbiyyah and in their Hajj from the Shirk (polytheism). And between Ismail (peace be upon him) and Adnan ibn Uddad was Musa (peace be upon him).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar said: He informed me, Muhammad ibn Ismail from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Saeed al-A'raj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: The Arabs did not cease to be upon something of the Hanifiyyah (uprightness/religion of Ibrahim), maintaining kinship, honoring the guest, and performing Hajj to the House. They would say, 'Fear the wealth of the orphan, for the wealth of the orphan is a shackle.' They refrained from certain prohibitions out of fear of punishment, and respite was not granted to them if they violated the prohibitions. They would take from the bark of the trees of the Sanctuary and hang it on the necks of the camels, so no one would dare to take from those camels wherever they went, nor would anyone dare to hang something other than the bark of the trees of the Sanctuary. Whoever did that was punished. And as for today, respite is granted to them. The people of Syria came and set up the catapult on Abu Qubays. So Allah sent upon them a cloud like the wing of a bird, which rained thunderbolts upon them, incinerating seventy men around the catapult.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the man who is given the money for Hajj; he performs Hajj with it and spends liberally upon himself, and there remains an excess from it. Should he return it to him? He (peace be upon him) said: No, it is for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who takes dirhams to perform Hajj on behalf of another man. Is it permissible for him to spend from them on other than Hajj? He said: If he guarantees the Hajj, then the dirhams are for him; he does with them what he likes, and upon him is the performance of the Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: Umar ibn Yazeed sent me to Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal with dirhams and said, 'Say to him: if he intends to perform Hajj with it, let him perform Hajj; and if he intends to spend it, let him spend it.' I said, 'So I spent it and did not perform Hajj.' Hammad said, 'So our companions mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: You have found the Sheikh, a jurist.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'O my Master! I hope to fast in Medina during the month of Ramadan.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'You will fast in it, if Allah wills.' I said, 'And I hope that our departure will be in the first ten days of Shawwal, and Allah has accustomed me to visiting the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his Household, and visiting you. So perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of your father, and perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of my father, and perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of a man from my brothers, and perhaps I will perform Hajj for myself. So what should I do?' He said, 'Perform Tamattu'.' I said, 'I have been residing in Mecca for ten years.' So he said, 'Perform Tamattu'.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Musa ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): 'I intended to circumambulate on your behalf and on behalf of your father.' So it was said to me: 'The successors are such that circumambulations are not to be performed on their behalf.' So he said to me: 'But, circumambulate whatever you are able to, for it is allowed.' Then I said to him after that by three years: 'I had sought your permission regarding the circumambulation on your behalf, and on behalf of your father, so you permitted me with regards to that. So I circumambulated on behalf of you both what Allah so Desired. Then something occurred in my heart, so I acted by it.' He said: 'And what was it?' I said, 'I circumambulated one day, on behalf of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' So he said three times: 'May Allah send Blessings upon Rasool-Allah.' Then on the second day, on behalf of Amir Al-Momineen. Then on the third day I circumambulated on behalf of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him); and on the fourth day on behalf of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); and on the fifth day on behalf of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); and on the sixth day on behalf of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him); and on the seventh day on behalf of Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him); and on the eighth day on behalf of your father Musa (peace be upon him); and on the ninth day on behalf of your father Ali (peace be upon him), and on the tenth day on your behalf, my Master. And they are those whom I make to be a Religion of Allah, by their Wilayah. So he said: 'Then, by Allah, you have made a Religion of Allah with the Religion which He will not be Accepting from the servants, apart from it.' I said, 'And sometimes I circumambulate on behalf of your mother Fatima (peace be upon her), and sometimes I do not circumambulate.' So he said: 'Frequent from this, for it would be the most superior of what you act upon, Allah Willing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can I share my parents in my Hajj?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Can I share my brothers in my Hajj?' He said, 'Yes. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made a Hajj for you and a Hajj for them, and for you is a reward for connecting with them.' I said, 'So can I circumambulate on behalf of a man and a woman while they are in Al-Kufa?' He said, 'Yes. You should say when you begin the circumambulation: 'O Allah, accept from so-and-so, on whose behalf I am circumambulating.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Amr ibn Ilyas, who said: I performed Hajj with my father while I was a Sarurah (one who has not yet performed Hajj). So I said, 'I would like to make my Hajj on behalf of my mother, for she has died.' He said to me, 'Wait until I ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for you.' So Ilyas said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was listening, 'May I be your sacrifice! This son of mine is a Sarurah, and his mother has died, so he would like to make his mother has died, so he would like to make his Hajj for her. Is that permissible for him?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is written for him and for her, and it is written for him the reward of righteousness.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira entered upon him and said to him, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, I have a daughter who is capable/standing for me in all matters, and she is a first-born. Can I make my Hajj for her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, its reward will be for her, and there will be for you the like of that, and nothing will be diminished from her reward.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who performs Hajj and dedicates his Hajj and Umrah, or part of his circumambulation, for one of his family members, while he is absent from him in another city. I said, 'Will that reduce his reward?' He said, 'No. It is for him and for his companion, and for him is a reward besides that with what he has linked.' I said, 'And if he is deceased, does that enter upon him?' He said, 'Yes, to the extent that if he is under Wrath, it is forgiven for him, or if there is constriction upon him, it is expanded upon him.' I said, 'So he, in his place, knows that that deed has reached him?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And even if he was a Nasibi (hostile one), does that benefit him?' He said, 'Yes. It is lightened from him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while I was in Medina after returning from Mecca, 'I intend to perform Hajj on behalf of my daughter.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So make that for her, now.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who partners his father, and his brother, and his relatives in his Hajj, he said: 'Then, a Hajj will be written for you similar to their Hajj, and your reward will be increased due to what you linked (with them).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ath, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hazrami, from his father who said: I returned from Makkah, so I met Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) in the Masjid, and he was seated in what is between the grave and the pulpit. So I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! When I go out to Makkah, sometimes a man says to me, 'Circumambulate on my behalf, seven circuits, and pray two cycles.' But I am too preoccupied from that, so when I return, I do not know what I should say to him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you go to Makkah, so fulfill your rituals, circumambulate seven circuits and pray two cycles, then say, "O Allah! This circumambulation and these two cycles are on behalf of my father and my mother, and on behalf of my wife, and on behalf of my children, and on behalf of my protectors, and on behalf of the entirety of the people of my city, their free ones, and their slaves, and their white ones, and their black ones."' So you would not be saying to the man, 'I have performed a circumambulation on your behalf, and prayed two cycles on your behalf,' except that you would be truthful (in saying that). So you would not be saying to the man, 'I conveyed the greetings to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family),' except that you would be truthful (in saying that).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), 'How many can I participate in my Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As many as you like to'.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Imran al-Armani, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you were to share a thousand people in your Hajj, there would be a Hajj for each one, without your Hajj being reduced by anything.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Hajj is in known months: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijja. So whoever intends to perform Hajj should let his hair grow when he sees the crescent of Dhu al-Qadah, and whoever intends to perform Umrah should let his hair grow for a month.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who intends the Hajj: can he remove (his hair) from his head during all of Shawwal, as long as he has not seen the crescent? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem, as long as he has not seen the crescent.

Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Do not take (cut) from your hair while you intend the Hajj in Dhu al-Qadah, nor in the month in which you intend to go out for the Umrah.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of our companions, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The man, when he sees the crescent of Dhi al-Qadah, and he intends the going, should neither take (hair) from his head not from his beard.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Retain your hair for the Hajj when you see the crescent of Dhu al-Qadah, and for the Umrah for a month.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'From the perfection of the Hajj and the Umrah is that you enter into Ihram from the Mawaqit (stations) which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated, and you do not pass them except while you are in Ihram. For he designated for the people of Iraq, and at that time there was no Iraq, Batn Al-Aqiq from the direction of the people of Iraq; and he designated for the people of Yemen, Yalamlam; and he designated for the people of Al-Taif, Qarn Al-Manazil; and he designated for the people of Al-Maghrib (the West), Al-Juhfa, and it is Mahya; and he designated for the people of Al-Madinah, Dhu Al-Hulayfah. And whoever's dwelling is behind these Mawaqit, from what faces Mecca, then his Mawqit is his dwelling.'
