Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Ihram is from five Mawaqit (stations of entering the state of Ihram) which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. It is not befitting for a pilgrim (Hajj) nor for a pilgrim (Umra) to enter Ihram before them, nor after them. He designated Dhul Huleifa for the people of Medina, and it is Masjid al-Shajara, where prayer is performed and Hajj is obligated therein. He designated Al-Juhfa for the people of Syria. He designated Al-Aqiq for the people of Najd. He designated Qaran al-Manazil for the people of Taif. He designated Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. And it is not befitting for anyone to turn away from the Mawaqit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The end of the Aqeeq is Bareyd Awtaas. And he said: The Bareyd of Al-Ba's is before Ghamra by two Bareyds.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The boundary of Al-Aqeeq is what is between Al-Maslakh up to Aqaba Ghamra.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Owtaas is not from Al-Aqeeq.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, and Yunus ibn Yaqoub narrated, saying: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Ihram, 'From which part of the Aqeeq is it superior that I should enter the state of Ihram?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'From its beginning is superior.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'We wear Ihram from the road of Al-Basra, and we do not know the boundary of the width of Al-Aqeeq.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Wear Ihram from Wajra.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The beginning of the Aqeeq is Bareed al-Ba'as, and it is six miles from the Maslakh on the side facing Iraq, and between it and Ghamra are twenty-four miles, which is two Bareyds. One of our companions said, 'When you exit from the Maslakh, enter into Ihram at the first Bareed that faces you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into Ihram for Hajj during months other than the months of Hajj, before the specific time designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He (peace be upon him) said: 'His Ihram is not [invalidated] by anything. If he wishes to return to his house, let him return, and I do not see any blame upon him. And if he wishes to continue, let him continue. So when he reaches the proper time, let him enter into Ihram from there and make it an Umrah, for that is superior to his returning, because he has publicly announced the Ihram for Hajj.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Hajj is during known months: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. It is not for anyone to enter the state of Ihram for Hajj in months other than these, and it is not for anyone to enter Ihram before the time designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Indeed, the example of that is like the one who prays four (rak'ahs) during travel and leaves the two (rak'ahs).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who enters into Ihram for Hajj during other than the months of Hajj, so there is no Hajj for him; and the one who enters into Ihram before reaching the Miqat, so there is no Ihram for him'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Mihran ibn Abi Nasr, from his brother Rabah, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We are reported in Kufa that Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the completion of Hajj and Umrah is that the man should enter into Ihram from the houses of his family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Has Ali (peace be upon him) said this?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said that for the one whose house is behind the Miqat. And, had it been as they say, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have prevented [people] from going out with their clothes to Al-Shajara.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Maysara, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while my complexion had changed. He said to me: 'From where did you enter into Ihram?' I said: 'From such and such a place.' He said: 'Often the seeker of goodness stumbles.' Then he said: 'Would it please you if you were to pray Dhuhr during travel as four (rak'cycles')?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So it is, by Allah, like that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who enters into Ihram before the appointed time, and attains from the women and the game, so there is nothing upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not befitting for anyone to enter into Ihram before the designated Mawaqit (stations) which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had fixed, except if he fears missing the month regarding the Umrah.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who arrives performing 'Umrah of Rajab, and the crescent of Sha'ban appears for him before the time (of entering 'Umrah state). Should he enter the state of Ihram before the time and designate it for Rajab, or should he delay the Ihram until the actual time (of the crescent) and designate it for Sha'ban? He (peace be upon him) said: He enters Ihram before the time, so it remains for Rajab, because Rajab has its merit, and it is the one he intended.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to enter the state of Ihram until he entered the Haram. He (peace be upon him) said: My father said: He should go out to the Miqat of the people of his land. So if he fears that the Hajj will be missed, he should enter Ihram from his place. So if he is able to go out from the Haram, let him go out, then let him enter Ihram.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I wrote to him, saying: Some of your mawali in Basra perform Ihram at Batan Al-Aqeeq, and there is no water in that place, nor any lodging, and the cost for them in that regard is severe. Their companions and their cameldrivers hasten them. And behind Batan Al-Aqeeq, by fifteen miles, there is a station wherein is water, and it is the station they are encamping in. So do you think they should perform Ihram from the place of water, for the ease it brings them and the lightness upon them? He wrote back: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated the Miqat stations for their people and for those who come to them from other than their people. And in it is a concession (rukhsah) for the one who has an excuse (illah). Therefore, none should exceed the Miqat except for the one who has an excuse to do so.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I set out with my family on foot, and I did not commence the Ihram (pilgrial consecration) until I reached Al-Juhfa. I had been suffering from illness, so the people of Medina would ask about me, saying, "We met him, and he was wearing his normal clothes." They did not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family be peace had permitted the one who was sick or weak to commence Ihram from Al-Juhfa.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Rafaa'ah bin Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man to whom severe illness strikes before he enters Makkah. He said: 'He should not enter it except in Ihram.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who passed the time when people enter the state of Ihram, but he forgot or was unaware, so he did not enter Ihram until he arrived in Mecca. He feared that if he returned to the time/place, he would miss the Hajj. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should exit the Haram (sanctuary), enter Ihram, and that will suffice him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who did not know to enter the state of Ihram until he had entered the Haram (sanctuary of Mecca). What should he do? He (peace be upon him) said: He should exit the Haram, then he should commence with the Talbiyah for Hajj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them)... ...regarding a man who forgot to enter the state of Ihram or was unaware, and he had performed all the rituals, circumambulated, and performed Sa'ee. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His intention suffices him if he had intended that, so his Hajj is complete, even if he did not recite the Talbiyya.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a patient who fainted until the time came: 'He enters Ihram from it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Ihram from Ghamra. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it if one enters into Ihram from it, and Bareed al-Aqee al-Aqeeq was more beloved to me (peace be upon him).'

Safwan from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman who was with a group of people, so she experienced menstruation. So she sent a message to them and asked them. So they said, 'We do not know if Ihram is upon you or not, while you are menstruating.' So they left her until she entered the Haram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there was sufficient time for her, let her return to the time (of Dhu al-Qadah) and enter Ihram from it; and if there was not sufficient time for her, let her return to whatever she is able to do after exiting the Haram, by a measure that does not cause her to miss it (the Hajj).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Wardan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is from Mecca at a travel distance of ten miles cannot enter it except in Ihram.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Sowrat ibn Kuleyb, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A woman from our family went out with us, but she was unaware of the Ihram, so she did not enter the state of Ihram until we entered Makkah, and we forgot to instruct her regarding that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So instruct her, and let her enter the state of Ihram from her place in Makkah or from the Masjid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you reach al-Aqiq from the direction of Iraq, or reach one of these miqat stations, and you intend to enter the state of Ihram, Allah willing, then pluck your armpits, clip your nails, remove your pubic hair, and trim your moustache, and it does not harm you whichever of these you begin with. Then brush your teeth, perform ghusl, and wear your two garments, and let your completion of these acts be, Allah willing, at the decline of the sun (midday); and if it is not at the decline of the sun, it does not harm you, except that I love for it to be with choice at the decline of the sun.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: The Sunnah regarding the Ihram is the clipping of the nails, and taking off the moustache, and shaving the pubic area.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: Abu Baseer asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and I was present, so he said: 'When I shave for the first Ihram, what should I do regarding the final shaving, and how much time is between them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When there are two Fridays between them, fifteen days, then shave.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad, from Safwan, from Abu Saeed Al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with shaving (unwanted hair) before entering the state of Ihram, by fifteen days.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Mahziyar, who said: Al-Hasan bin Saeed wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A man entered into Ihram without Ghusl or without Salat, knowingly or out of ignorance; what is upon him regarding that, and what is befitting that he should do?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should repeat.'

One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, who said: We were in Medina, and Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. So I said, 'Shaving it is better,' and Zurara said, 'Plucking it is better.' So we sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he permitted us while he was in the bathhouse waxing, and he had waxed his armpits. So I said to Zurara, 'Does it suffice you?' He said, 'No, perhaps this deed is for him, and it may not be allowed for me that I should do it.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'In what (discussion) are you two?' So I said, 'Zurara is disputing with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. I said shaving is better, and Zurara said plucking is better.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'You have hit the Sunnah and Zurara has erred. Shaving it is better than plucking it, and waxing it is better than shaving it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said to us, 'Get the waxing done.' So we said, 'We did that three days ago.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Repeat it, for the waxing is cleanliness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Your washing in the daytime is for your day, and your washing at night time is for your night.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who performs the ritual bath (ghusl) in Medina for his Ihram. Does that suffice him from the Ghusl of Dhu al-Hulayfa? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' Then a man came to him while I was in his presence, and he said: 'One of our companions performed a ritual bath, and a need presented itself to him until evening.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat the ritual bath. His bathing during the day is for that day of his, and at night is for his night.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then wore a shirt before entering the state of Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His bath has been broken.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed the ritual bath for his Ihram, then clipped his nails, he said: He should wipe them with the water, and he does not repeat the bath.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: We sent a message to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and we were a group, and we were in Al-Medina, saying, 'We intend to bid you farewell.' So he sent a message to us: 'Wash yourselves in Al-Medina, for I am afraid that finding water would be difficult for you in Dhi al-Hulayfa. Therefore, wash in Al-Medina, and wear the clothes in which you will enter the state of Ihram, then come individually or in twos.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ala'a ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When a man washes and he intends to enter the state of Ihram, so he wears a shirt before he recites the Talbiyya, then upon him is (repeating of) the washing.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Darraj, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding the man who performs ritual bath (ghusl) for Ihram, then wipes his head with a handkerchief; he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who anoints himself with oil containing perfume while intending to enter the state of Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: Do not anoint with oil containing musk or amber, whose scent remains in your head after you enter Ihram. And anoint with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter Ihram, before the bath and after it. So when you enter Ihram, the oil becomes prohibited for you until you are released (from Ihram).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not anoint yourself with oil containing musk or amber when you intend to enter the state of Ihram, for the sake of the scent that remains in your head after you have entered Ihram; and anoint yourself with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter Ihram. So when you enter Ihram, the oil becomes prohibited for you until you are released (from Ihram).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with a man anointing himself with oil before he washes for Ihram, or after it, and he used to dislike the thick oil that remains.'

Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'ala, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man in Ihram who anoints himself with oil after the bath. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' So we anointed ourselves in his presence with cassia bark, and he mentioned that his father used to anoint himself with oil after washing for Ihram, and that he anoints with oil as long as it is not expensive, or an oil containing musk or amber.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then entered the Masjid al-Shajara and prayed, then went out to the boys and said: 'Bring what you have of the flesh of the game so that we may eat it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding a man who prayed Dhuhr in the Masjid al-Shajarah and entered into Ihram, then touched perfume, or hunted game, or had intercourse with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: There is nothing upon him as long as he has not said the Talbiyyah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from one of his companions, who said: I wrote to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): A man entered the Masjid al-Shajarah, prayed, and entered into Ihram, then exited the mosque. It became inevitable for him, before he recited the Talbiyyah, to break that state by having intercourse with women. Is that permissible for him? He (peace be upon him) wrote: Yes, or there is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): What do you say regarding a man who prepares for Ihram and is free from everything except that he has not said the Talbiyah? Is it permissible for him to break that state and have intercourse with women? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from some of his companions, from al-Washa', from Ali ibn Abi Hamza who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Verily, the ark of Noah was commanded; it circumambulated the House (Kaaba) when the land was drowned. Then it came to Mina during its [appointed] days, then the ark returned. It was commanded, and it circumambulated the House with the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa').'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrating to Ata'a, saying: The length of the ark of Noah was one thousand and two hundred cubits, and its width was eight hundred cubits, and its height in the sky was two hundred cubits. It circumambulated the House (Ka'ba) and performed sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa seven circuits, then it rested upon Mount Judi.

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Musa ibn Imran passed by among seventy prophets upon the glens of al-Rawha, upon them were the Qatwaniyya cloaks, saying: "Here I am, Your servant, son of Your servant."'

Musa, the Prophet (peace be upon him), passed by the glens of Al-Rawha upon a red camel whose halter was made of palm fibres. Upon him were two Qatwani cloaks, and he was saying: 'Here I am, O Benevolent One! Here I am!' He said: And Yunus ibn Matta passed by the glens of Al-Rawha, and he was saying: 'Here I am, O Remover of grievous anguish! Here I am!' He said: And Isa ibn Maryam passed by the glens of Al-Rawha, and he was saying: 'Here I am, Your servant, son of Your maidservant! Here I am!' And Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) passed by the glens of Al-Rawha, and he was saying: 'Here I am, O Possessor of the Lofty Ascents! Here I am!'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Musa (peace be upon him) entered ihram from Ramla in Egypt. He said: And he passed through the glens of al-Rawha in a state of ihram, leading his she-camel with a halter made of palm fiber, wearing upon him two Qatwani cloaks, reciting the talbiyya while the mountains responded to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that Suleyman ibn Dawood (peace be upon him) performed Hajj of the House (Kaaba) accompanied by the Jinn and the humans, and the birds, and the winds, and he clothed the House with Egyptian linen (qabati cloth).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from al-Mufaddal, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Seven hundred prophets have prayed in Masjid al-Khayf, and what is between the corner (of the Ka'ba) and the Maqam (Station of Ibrahim) is indeed fraught with the graves of the prophets, and Adam is truly in the sanctuary of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zayd al-Shahham, from an unnamed narrator, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) performed Hajj and with him were seventy prophets from the Children of Israel. The nose-ropes of their camels were made of palm-fibre. They were reciting the Talbiyya, and the mountains were responding to them. Upon Musa were two Qatwani cloaks. He was saying: "Here I am! Your servant, son of Your servant!"'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Abu Bilal al-Makki, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) enter al-Hijr from the side of the door. Then he stood performing salat at a distance of two cubits from the House. So I said to him: I have not seen anyone from your family pray in front of the Mizab. He said: This is the prayer place of Shabbar and Shabbir, the two sons of Harun (Aaron).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid Shabab al-Sayrafi, from Muawiya ibn Ammar al-Duhni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Seventy Prophets are buried in what is between the Yamani Corner and the Black Stone. Allah caused them to die of hunger and adversity.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when Dawud (peace be upon him) took his stand at Arafat, he looked at the people and their multitude, so he ascended the mountain and turned to supplicate. When he had completed his rituals, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to him and said to him: 'O Dawud! Your Lord says to you: Why did you ascend the mountain? Did you think that the voice of one who speaks would be hidden from Me?' Then he took him to the sea, to Jeddah, and caused him to descend into the water, traveling for forty mornings on land. Then there was a rock, which he split open, and there was a worm in it. He said to him: 'O Dawud! Your Lord says to you: I hear the voice of this one in the belly of this rock at the bottom of this sea. So did you think that the voice of one who speaks would be hidden from Me?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muawiya ibn Ammar, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: It does not harm you whether you enter into Ihram at night or by day, except that the superior of that is at the decline of the sun.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Ihram is not valid except after a prescribed prayer. If you enter Ihram after it, after the greeting (of prayer), and if it is a voluntary prayer, you pray two cycles and enter Ihram after them. So when you turn from your prayer, praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And say: 'O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who answered You, believed in Your promise, and followed Your command, for I am Your servant and in Your hold. I am protected only by what You protect, and I take only what You give.' And You have mentioned Hajj, so I ask You to establish it for me upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, strengthen me in what I am weak in, and accept my rituals from me with ease and well-being from You, and make me among Your delegates whom You pleased and chose and named and ordained. O Allah, perfect for me my Hajj and Umrah. O Allah, I intend Tamattu' with Umrah to Hajj upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). If something occurs that prevents me, then release me where you prevented me, according to the decree You decreed upon me. O Allah, if it is not a Hajj, then an Umrah. I enter Ihram for You with my hair, skin, flesh, blood, bones, marrow, and nerves, abstaining from women, clothes, and perfume, seeking Your Face and the Hereafter by that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it suffices you to say this once when you enter Ihram. Then stand and walk comfortably. When the ground is level with you, whether walking or riding, then say the Talbiyah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I intend to perform Tamattu' with the Umrah until the Hajj, so what should I say?' He said, 'You should say, O Allah, I intend to perform Tamattu' with the Umrah until the Hajj, upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and if you wish, you can keep in mind that which you intend (instead of saying it).

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) enter into Ihram at night or during the day?' So he said, 'During the day.' I said, 'At what time?' He said, 'At the Dhuhr prayer.' So I asked him, 'When do you think we should enter into Ihram?' He said, 'It is the same upon you. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered into Ihram at the Dhuhr prayer because the water was scarce, as if it were at the tops of the mountains, so a man would leave to acquire that from the morning, and they could hardly manage to find the water. And these waters are newly occurring.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one who says, 'Free me, for You withheld me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is freed where he was withheld.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Or should he not say it?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He is free (to perform the prayer) if he is detained, whether he makes a stipulation or not.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami and Zayd al-Shahham, and Mansur ibn Hazim, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered us that we should exclaim the Talbiyya and not specify anything, and he said: 'The people of the concealment in the mind are more beloved to me.'

Ahmad, from Ali, from Sayf, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, that he asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: The keeping (of the intention) in the mind is more beloved to me, therefore exclaim Talbiyya and do not specify.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Do you consider that if a man were to enter the state of Ihram at the end of a prescribed prayer, would that suffice him?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you have prayed in the Masjid al-Shajara, say while you are seated at the end of the prayer, before you arise, what the one in Ihram would say. Then arise and walk until you reach the mile, and al-Bayda is level with you; so when it is level with you, then proclaim the Talbiyah.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: When a man enters into the state of Ihram after the prescribed prayer, should he recite the Talbiyah when he rises with his camel, or while seated after the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: He may do whichever of those he desires. Al-Kulayni said: And this, in my view, is from the matters of ease (permissibility), except that the merit in it is that he should manifest the Talbiyah where the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) manifested it, at the edge of Al-Bayda', and it is not permissible for anyone to exceed a mile of Al-Bayda' unless he has already manifested the Talbiyah; and the first of Al-Bayda' is the first mile that meets you on the left of the road.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Pray the prescribed prayers, then enter into Ihram for Hajj or for Umrat al-Tamattu', and go out without Talbiyah until you ascend to the beginning of Al-Bayda', to the first mile on your left. So when the ground becomes level for you, whether you are riding or walking, then say Talbiah. It will not harm you whether you enter Ihram at night or during the day. And the Masjid of Dhu al-Hulayfa is that which was outside the pavilions, from the courtyard of the Masjid. Then today, there is nothing of the pavilions remaining from it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one performing Umra exclusively stipulates to his Lord that He releases him as He had withheld him, and the one performing the exclusive Hajj stipulates to his Lord: if it is not a Hajj, then (let it be) an Umra.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It used to be that whenever the Children of Israel offered a sacrifice, a fire would emerge consuming the sacrifice of the one from whom it was accepted, and indeed Allah made the Ihram in place of the sacrifice.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked him, 'Why was the Talbiyya instituted?' So he said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): "Proclaim to the people the Hajj"' "They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every deep pass." So he called out, and was answered from every direction, [with the people] saying 'Labbayya' (Talbiyya).

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Talbiyya is: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayk la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika lak, labbayk. Dha al-maaraj, labbayk. Labbayk, da'iyan ila dar al-salam, labbayk. Labbayk, ghaffara al-dhunub, labbayk. Labbayk, ahla al-talbiyya, labbayk. Labbayk, dha al-jalali wa al-ikram, labbayk. Labbayk, marhuban wa marghuban ilayk, labbayk. Labbayk, tubdi'u wa al-ma'adu ilayk, labbayk. Labbayk, kasshafa al-kurabi al-'itham, labbayk. Labbayk, 'abduka wa ibnu 'abdayk, labbayk. Labbayk, ya karim, labbayk.' You should say this at the end of every prescribed or optional prayer, and when your camel rises for you, and when you ascend a height or descend a valley, or meet a rider, or when you wake from your sleep, and at dawn. Increase in it as much as you can, and be loud with it. And if you leave some of the Talbiyya, it will not harm you, except that its completion is superior. And know that it is necessary to have the four Talbiyyat at the beginning of the speech, and they are the obligation, and they are the Oneness (Tawhid), and by it the Messengers exclaimed. And increase in 'Dha al-Maaraj', for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to increase in it. And the first to exclaim Talbiyya was Ibrahim (peace be upon him), saying: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls you to perform Hajj to His House.' So they answered Him with the Talbiyya. So no one remained whose covenant was taken with loyalty in the back of a man or the belly of a woman, except that he answered with the Talbiyya.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Asad ibn Abu Al-A'ala, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl, from the one who saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he was in Ihram, having exposed his back until he showed it to the sun, he was saying: 'Here I am among the sinners, here I am!'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, raising it (to the Prophet), said: Indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered into Ihram, Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said to him: 'Order your companions with the 'Ajji and the 'Sajji'; and the 'Ajji is raising the voice with the Talbiyya, and the 'Sajji is the slaughtering of the camels.' And he said: Jabir ibn Abdullah said, 'We did not reach Al-Rowha until our voices were hoarse (from loud recitation).'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with you reciting the Talbiyya while you are not in a state of purity, and in every state.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al-Khazzaz, from Abu Saeed Al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not upon the women to be loud with the Talbiyya.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from various men, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who exclaims the Talbiyya seventy times while in his Ihram, with faith and considering it as a good deed, Allah will cause a thousand thousand angels to testify for him with freedom from the Fire, and freedom from hypocrisy.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah.' He said: 'Its completion is that there be no sexual intercourse, nor immorality, nor disputing during the Hajj.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, all from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you enter the state of Ihram, you must have God-consciousness, remember God frequently, and speak little except in goodness. Indeed, part of the perfection of Hajj and Umrah is that a person protects his tongue except from goodness, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said. So whoever determines the performance of the Hajj therein, there shall be no obscenity nor immorality nor quarrelling during the Hajj. And the obscenity is copulation, and the immorality is lying and insulting, and the quarrelling is the words of the man, 'No, by Allah!' and 'Yes, by Allah!' And know that the man, when he swears with three oaths consecutively in one place while he is in Ihram, has quarrelled. Therefore, upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal) to be spilled, and he should give in charity with it. And when he swears one false oath, he has quarrelled, and upon him is blood to be spilled, and he should give in charity with it. And he said: Guard against boasting, and upon you is piety that restrains you from disobeying Allah, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Then let them fulfil their needful acts, and let them be loyal to their vows and let them go round the Ancient House.' Abu Abdillah said: From al-Tafath is that you speak while in your Ihram with ugly speech. So when you enter Mecca and circumambulate the House, and you speak with good speech, that becomes an expiation. He said: And I asked him about the man who says, 'No, by my life!' and 'Yes, by my life!'. He said: This is not from the quarrelling. Rather, the quarrelling is 'No, by Allah!' and 'Yes, by Allah!'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Baseer from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: When one swears three consecutive oaths truthfully, he has quarrelled and upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal); and when one swears with one false oath, he has quarrelled and upon him is blood.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram who intends to perform a deed, so his companion says to him, 'By Allah, do not do it.' So he says, 'By Allah, I will do it.' So he opposes him a few times. Does it necessitate upon him what necessitates upon the one who quarrels? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, what is meant by this is honoring his brother. Rather, that (penalty) is what was for the sake of Allah wherein is a disobedience.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Regarding quarrelling is a sheep, and regarding insults and immorality is a cow, and copulation spoils the Hajj.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of our companions, from one of them (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wore Ihram in two cotton cloths.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The two garments of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in which he entered into Ihram were both Yemeni: Ibri and Zafar, and in them he was shrouded.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about the qamis (shirt) whose warp is silk and its weft is from yarn. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if one enters into Ihram wearing it; rather, what is disliked is the pure (silk) from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Shu'ayb Abu Salih, from Khalid Abu Al-A'la Al-Khaffaf, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and upon him was a green gown (burd), and he was in Ihram.

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I was seated in his presence, and he was asked about a man who enters into iḥrām wearing a garment containing silk. So he called for a qurqubī loincloth and said: 'I enter into iḥrām in this, and it contains silk.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram wearing the buttoned Taylasan, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes,' and in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'A Taylasan is not worn until its buttons are removed.' So my father narrated to me: 'That is disliked out of fear that the ignorant one would place buttons upon it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to that, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is disliked out of fear that the ignorant one would button it. But as for the jurist, there is no problem if he wears it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not wear a garment that has buttons while you are in Ihram, except if you turn it inside out, nor a garment that you drape over your shoulders, nor trousers, except if you do not have an izar (loincloth), nor two socks, except if you do not have two shoes. And I asked him about the one in Ihram who pairs between the clothes in which he entered Ihram and others. He said: There is no problem with that if they are clean.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram who covers himself with two garments. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and with three, if he wishes, to protect himself from the cold and the heat by them.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with the one in Ihram changing his clothes. But, when he enters Makkah, he should wear the two garments of his Ihram in which he entered the state of Ihram, and it is disliked that he sells them.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram wearing Khazz (animal fur). He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn A'izh, from Al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does a man enter into Ihram in black cloth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He enters into Ihram in black cloth, and the deceased is shrouded in it.'

Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the man who enters into Ihram in a dirty garment. He said: 'No,' and I do not say it is forbidden, but I prefer that he purify it, and its purification is washing it. And the man should not wash the garment in which he is in Ihram until he is free from Ihram, even if it becomes dirty, except if sexual impurity touches it or something [else requiring washing], then he should wash it.

Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the printed garment, can a man enter into Ihram while wearing it? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, but what is disliked is the silk-blended (garment).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a garment that is dyed with saffron, then washed; can I wear it while I am in Ihram? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. Saffron is not from the perfumes, but I dislike that you wear what makes you prominent among the people.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a garment that is touched by saffron, then it is washed but the color does not disappear. He was asked: 'Is one prohibited from wearing it in Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it when its aroma disappears, and even if all of it was dyed, as long as it turns to whiteness and is washed, there is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with a man entering the state of Ihram in a garment dyed with Mishq, and there is no problem with the one in Ihram changing his clothes. I said, 'If something touches it, he washes it?' He said, 'Yes, and even if he discharges semen in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who wears a bed-cover, the back of which is red and its lining is yellow, which has been worn for a year and two years. He (peace be upon him) said: 'As long as it does not have a smell, there is no problem; and every garment that is dyed and washed, it is permissible to wear Ihram in it. But if it is not washed, then no.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Najih, from Abul Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem for the one in Ihram to wear the ring. And in another report, (He said): He should not wear it for adornment.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'My family is with me, and I intend to tighten my expenditure around my waist.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, for my father (peace be upon him) was saying: From the strength of the traveller is the protection of his expenditure.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram tightening the turban around his belly. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) was saying: He can tighten the money-belt in which is his expenditure (money), to be confident from it, for it is from the completion of his Hajj'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihraam packing the Dirhams inside his clothes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he can wear the money-belt and the purse'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ays ibn Al-Qasim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman in Ihram may wear whatever she desires of clothes, except silk and the two gloves, and the veil (Naqaab) is disliked.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'She may let the cloth drape over her face.' I said, 'What is the limit of that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Up to the tip of the nose, to the extent that she can see.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman in Ihram, 'What of the clothes can she wear?' He said: 'She can wear all clothes, except those dyed with saffron and the dye plant (wars); and she cannot wear the two gloves, nor an ornament with which she adorns herself for her husband; and she cannot apply kohl except due to a reason; and she cannot touch perfume; and she cannot wear an ornament, nor Firanda (a decorative flower); and there is no problem with a pattern in the clothes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed by a veiled woman who was in Ihram, so he said: 'Enter into Ihram, uncover your face, and let down your garment from the top of your head, for if you were to veil (your face), your complexion would not change.' A man asked: 'To where should she let it down?' He said: 'To cover her eyes.' I said: 'Does it reach her mouth?' He said: 'Yes.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The female in Ihram should not wear jewelry, nor dyed clothes, except if it is dyed with a dye that does not fade (or return to its original state).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the woman who has upon her the necklaces, and the anklets, and the bangles, and the earrings, from gold and silver; she enters into Ihram while they are upon her, and she used to wear them in her house before her Hajj. Should she remove them when she enters Ihram, or leave them in their state? He (peace be upon him) said: She enters Ihram while wearing them, without displaying them to the men during her riding and her walking.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Sabiriyya turban in which there is a silk print, whether a woman is prohibited from wearing it while in Ihram. He said: 'Yes, but that is disliked only if its warp and its weft are entirely silk.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Saeed asked me about the Khameesa (a type of shirt/upper garment) whose warp is silk, whether I should let her wear it, and he had felt the cold, so I ordered him to let her wear it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Uyayna, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for the woman to wear while she is in Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'All clothes, except the two gloves, the burqa (veil), and silk.' I said, 'She can wear khazz (silk-like fabric)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'Supposing its warp is ibrisam (raw silk) and it is (also) silk?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As long as it is not purely silk, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The female in Ihram must not wear the niqab, because the Ihram of the woman is in her face, and the Ihram of the man is in his head.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman: Is it permissible for her to wear a silk garment while she is in Ihram? He (peace be upon him) said: No, and it is permissible for her to wear it when she is not in Ihram.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed by a woman in Ihram who had veiled herself with a hand fan, so he himself removed the hand fan from her face.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Hariz, from Aamir ibn Juza'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can the female in Ihram wear dyed clothes?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it, except the conspicuous dyed garment and the conspicuous necklace.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Muhammad al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman when she enters the state of Ihram, can she wear the trousers? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Rather, what is intended by that is the covering (sutrah).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man whose slippers were destroyed and he was not able to find two slippers, he (peace be upon him) said: Let him wear the two socks (khuffayn) if he is compelled to do so, and let him tear them from the top of the foot; and if he wears the tilasan (a sleeveless garment), let him not button it on; so if he is compelled to wear a qaba (a long coat) due to cold, and he cannot find a garment other than it, let him wear it inside out, and let him not put his hands into the sleeves of the qaba.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Rafa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram wearing the two khuff (leather socks) and the two jawaban (socks). He said: 'When he is in need of them.'

Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musanna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with a man wearing Ihram while his weapon is upon him, if he fears the enemy.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is in desperate need of a garment while he is in Ihram, and he has nothing with him except a qaba' (a sleeveless coat), then let him invert it, and let him make its upper part its lower part, and wear it. And in another report, he turns its back to be its front, when he cannot find anything else.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hijjam, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram may wear trousers if he does not have a loincloth with him, and he may wear the two leather socks if he does not have shoes with him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever wears a garment that is not befitting for him to wear while he is in Ihram, if he does that out of forgetfulness, or mistake, or ignorance, then there is nothing upon him; and whoever does it deliberately, then upon him is blood (of a slaughtered animal).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about various types of different clothes which the person in Ihram wears when he needs them. What is upon him? He said: For every type from it, there is an expiation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who enters into Ihram while wearing a shirt: He said, 'He should remove it without tearing it; and if he wore it after entering Ihram, he should tear it and remove it from what is below his legs.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Khalid ibn Muhammad Al-Asamm, who said: A man entered the Sacred Mosque while in Ihram, so he entered into Tawaf wearing a shirt and a robe. The people came upon him, tearing his shirt, and he was firm (did not remove it). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw them handling his shirt and tearing it, so he said to him, 'What did you do?' He said, 'I entered Ihram like this, with the shirt and robe on.' He said, 'Remove it from your head; it is not removed from your feet. Rather, it was ignorance.' Then someone else came to him and asked him, saying, 'What do you say about a man who enters Ihram with a shirt on?' He said, 'He should remove it from his head.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: If you wear a garment in your Ihram that is not permissible for you to wear, then recite the Talbiyah and repeat your Ghusl. And if you wear a shirt, then tear it and remove it from beneath your feet.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'The one in Ihram is pestered by flies when he intends to sleep; can he cover his face?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but he should not cover his head; and the woman, when sleeping, there is no harm if she covers her entire face when sleeping.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Abdul Malik al-Qummi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The one in Ihram performs ablution, then covers his face with a handkerchief, concealing it entirely.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the person in Ihram who sleeps on his face on his wrapping garment. He said: There is no problem with it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram who feels cold in his ears and covers them; he said: 'No'.

I was between Mecca and Medina, I and a companion of mine. We discussed the Ansar; one of us said they were drawn from various tribes, and one of us said they were from the people of Yemen. Then we arrived at Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was sitting in the shade of a tree. He began the hadith without our asking. He said: When Tubba' came from the direction of Iraq, with scholars and sons of the prophets in his company, When he reached the valley of Hudhayl, some people from certain tribes came to him and said: You are coming to the people of a town who have been playing games with people for a long time, until they made their land a haram and their building a lord or goddess. He said: If things are as you say, I will kill their fighters, enslave their descendants, and demolish their building. His two eyes then flowed down until they fell onto his cheeks. Then he summoned the scholars and sons of the prophets. He said: Examine my case and inform me why this has befallen me. They refused to tell him until he firmly pressed them. They said: Tell us what you said to yourself. He said: I said to myself that I would kill their fighters, enslave their descendants, and demolish their building. They said: We see nothing that has befallen you except because of that. He asked: And why is that? They said: Because the city — — is the haram of Allah, the House is the House of Allah, and its inhabitants are the descendants of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful. He said: You have spoken truly. What is my way out of what I have fallen into? They said: Turn your thoughts to something else; perhaps Allah will restore it to you. He turned his thoughts to good, and they returned. His irises returned until they settled back in their place. He summoned the people who had advised him to demolish it and executed them. Then he came to the House, covered it, and provided food for thirty days — one hundred camels each day — until the bowls were carried to the wild beasts on the mountaintops and fodder was scattered in the valleys for the wildlife. Then he departed from Mecca to Medina and settled there a people from the people of Yemen, from Ghassan — and they are the Ansar. [In another narration: he covered it with niṭa' cloth and perfumed it.]

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the master of Abyssinia came with the elephant, intending to demolish the Ka'ba, they passed by the camels of Abd al-Muttalib and drove them away. So Abd al-Muttalib directed himself to their leader to ask for the return of his camels. He sought permission to see him, and he granted it. It was said to him: 'This is the noble of Quraysh, or the great one of Quraysh — a man of intellect and noble character.' So he honoured him and drew him near. Then he said to his interpreter: 'Ask him what his need is.' He said: 'Your companions passed by my camels and drove them away; I would like you to return them to me.' The narrator said: He was astonished at his request to him for the return of the camels, and said: 'This is the one you claim is the great one of Quraysh and whose intellect you praise — and he refrains from asking me to withdraw from the House he worships! But had he asked me to withdraw from demolishing it, I would have done so for him.' The interpreter informed him of the king's words, and Abd al-Muttalib said to him: 'That House has a Lord who will defend it; I only asked you for my camels because of my need for them.' So he ordered their return to him. Abd al-Muttalib departed until he met the elephant at the edge of the Sanctuary. He called to it: 'Mahmud!' It moved its head. He said to it: 'Do you know why they have brought you?' It shook its head: No. He said: 'They have brought you to demolish the House of your Lord — will you do it?' It shook its head: No. He (the Imam) said: Abd al-Muttalib departed from it, and they brought the elephant to enter the Sanctuary. When it reached the edge of the Sanctuary, it refused to enter. They struck it but it still refused. They led it around all sides of the Sanctuary — each time it resisted against them and would not enter. And God sent upon them birds like swallows, each carrying in its beak a stone the size of a lentil or so. Each bird would hover over a man, then release the stone upon his head, and it would come out from his behind — until none remained from them except one man who fled. He went about narrating to people what he had seen, when a bird from among them suddenly appeared. He raised his head and said: 'This is one of th

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Abdillah al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the Quraysh in the pre-Islamic period demolished the House. When they intended to build it, there was an impediment placed between them and it, and awe was instilled in their hearts, until a speaker from among them said: Let each man bring the best of his wealth, and do not bring any wealth that you have earned through cutting off family ties or forbidden means. So they did so, and the way was cleared between them and building it. So they built it until they reached the place of the Black Stone. They quarrelled about which of them would place the Black Stone in its position, to the extent that evil nearly broke out among them. They agreed that the first one to enter through the gate of the Masjid would decide. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entered. When he came to them, he ordered a cloth to be spread out, then placed the Stone in the middle of it. Then the tribes grasped the sides of the cloth and raised it. Then he (peace be upon him and his family) took it and placed it in its position. Thus God distinguished him for it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim and others, via different chains, transmitted it in raised form, saying: The Quraysh demolished the Ka'ba because floodwaters would come from the upper areas of Makkah and enter it, causing it to crack; and a golden gazelle with legs of jewels was stolen from the Ka'ba, and its walls were short — and that was thirty years before the Sending of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So the Quraysh intended to demolish the Ka'ba, rebuild it, and expand its floor area. Then they became fearful and worried that if they put the pickaxes to it, a punishment might descend upon them. So Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said: 'Leave me to begin — if it pleases God, nothing will befall me; and if it is otherwise, we shall stop.' So he climbed upon the Ka'ba and moved a stone from it, and a snake appeared before him, and the sun was eclipsed. When they saw that, they wept and supplicated, saying: 'O God! We intend nothing but repair!' So the snake disappeared from them, and they demolished it and moved its stones around it until they reached the foundations that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had laid. When they wanted to expand its floor area and moved the foundations that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had laid, an intense earthquake struck them along with darkness. So they refrained from it. The building of Ibrahim was: length thirty cubits, width twenty-two cubits, and height nine cubits. So the Quraysh said: 'We should increase its height.' So they built it. When the construction reached the place of the Black Stone, the Quraysh quarrelled over placing it, and every tribe said: 'We have the greatest right to it — we shall place it.' When the dispute intensified among them, they agreed to accept the judgment of whoever entered through the gate of Banu Shayba. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) appeared, and they said: 'This is Al-Amin (the trustworthy one) who has come!' So they made him the judge, and he spread his cloak — some say it was a Tarauni garment that he had — and placed the Stone in it. Then he said: 'Let a man come from each quarter of Quraysh.' They were: 'Utba ibn Rabi'a from Banu 'Abd Shams, Al-Aswad ibn Al-Muttalib from Banu Asad ibn 'Abd Al-'Uzza, Abu Hudhayfa ibn Al-Mughira from Banu Makhzum, and Qays ibn 'Adiyy from Banu Sahm. They lifted it, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) placed it in its

Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) shared with the Quraysh in building the House (Kaaba), and there came to be for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), from the door of the Kaaba to the midpoint between the Yamani corner and the Black Stone. And in another report: it was for the Banu Hashim, from the Black Stone to the Syrian corner.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, and someone else, narrated it with an elevated chain (marfu'). He said: In the Kaaba there used to be two gazelles of gold and five swords. So when Khuza'a overcame Jurhum at the Sanctuary, Jurhum threw the swords and the two gazelles into the well of Zamzam, and threw rocks into it, and filled it up and concealed its traces. So when Qusayy overcame Khuza'a, they did not know the location of Zamzam, and its location was hidden from them. So when Abdul Muttalib prevailed, and a mat would be spread for him in the courtyard of the Kaaba — something that was not done for anyone else there — while he was sleeping in the shade of the Kaaba, he saw in his dream that a visitor came to him and said: 'Dig Barra.' He said: 'And what is Barra?' Then he came to him on the second day and said: 'Dig Tayba.' Then he came to him on the third day and said: 'Dig al-Masouna.' He said: 'And what is al-Masouna?' Then he came to him on the fourth day and said: 'Dig Zamzam — it will neither run dry nor be disparaged; it quenches the great pilgrims in the presence of the white-footed crow, by the colony of ants.' And there was a rock near Zamzam from which ants would emerge, and the white-footed crow would alight upon it every day to catch the ants. So when Abdul Muttalib saw this, he recognized the location of Zamzam. So he said to Quraysh: 'I have been commanded during four nights to dig Zamzam, and it is our heritage and our glory, so come, let us dig it.' But they did not respond to him. So he began digging it by himself, and he had only one son, al-Harith, who used to assist him in the digging. So when that became difficult for him, he went to the door of the Kaaba, then raised his hands and supplicated to God, Mighty and Majestic, and made a vow to Him that if He were to grant him ten sons, he would sacrifice the most beloved of them to Him as an act of drawing near to God, Mighty and Majestic. So when he dug and reached the well — the well of Ismail — and knew that he had reached the water, he proclaimed Takbir, and Quraysh proclaimed Takbir. And they said: 'O Abu al-Harith! This is our heritage and we have a share in it.' He said to them: 'You did not assist me in digging it. It belongs to me and my children until the end of eternity.'

Al-Hasan ibn Rashid said: I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saying: When Abd al-Muttalib dug Zamzam and reached its bottom, there came out to him from one of the sides of the well a foul stench that alarmed him, but he refused to turn back. His son al-Harith came out from him. Then he dug until he went deep, and found at its bottom a spring flowing to him with the fragrance of musk. Then he dug, and had not dug more than a cubit when sleep overcame him. He saw a man of great stature, beautiful hair, handsome face, fine clothing, and pleasant fragrance, and he was saying: 'Dig and you will gain! Strive and you will be safe! Do not hoard it for the distribution. The swords are for others, and the well is for you!' The well is for you. You are the greatest of the Arabs in honor, and from you will emerge its Prophet and its Guardian, and the noble descendants — the wise, the scholars, the perspicacious. And the swords are for them. But they are not today from you nor for you; rather in the second generation from you. By them God will illuminate the earth, bring out the devils from its corners, humiliate them in their might, destroy them after their strength, humiliate the idols, and kill their worshippers wherever they may be. Then after him there will remain a descendant from your descendants — he will be his brother and his vizier, lesser than him in age, able against the idols, not disobeying him in a single letter, concealing nothing from him, and consulting him in every matter that befalls him.' Abd al-Muttalib was exhausted from this. He found thirteen swords leaning to his side. He took them and intended to spread the news, but said: 'How can I, when I have not yet reached the water?' Then he dug, and had not dug a palm's width when the horn of the gazelle appeared to him along with its head. He extracted it, and inscribed on it was: 'There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God; Ali is the Guardian of God; Ali is the Guardian of God; so-and-so is the Caliph of God.' I asked him and said: 'So-and-so — when will he be, before him or after him?' He said: 'He has not yet come, nor has any of his signs appeared.' Abd al-Muttalib came out, having extracted the water. As he was ascending, there was a black creature with a long tail rushing ahead of him to the top. He struck it and cut off most of its tail, then sought it but it escaped. And s

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ali, master of the mats, from Aban ibn Taglib who said: When al-Hajjaj demolished the Kaaba, the people scattered its soil. When they came to rebuild it and intended to build it, a snake came out toward them and prevented the people from construction until they fled. They came to al-Hajjaj and informed him. He feared that he himself had been the cause of preventing its construction. So he ascended the pulpit, then adjured the people and said: 'I adjure by Allah any servant who has knowledge of what we are afflicted with, to inform us of it.' He (Aban) said: An old man stood up toward him and said: 'If there is knowledge with anyone, it is with a man whom I saw come to the Kaaba, take its measurements, and then depart.' Al-Hajjaj said: 'Who is he?' He said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him.' He said: 'That is the mine of such knowledge.' So he sent for Ali ibn al-Husayn, may Allah's blessings be upon them both. He came and informed him of what had occurred — that Allah had prevented his construction. Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, said to him: 'O Hajjaj! You deliberately destroyed the construction of Ibrahim and Ismail, threw it in the road, and allowed it to be plundered, as if you regarded it as your own inheritance. Ascend the pulpit and adjure the people that not one of them who took anything from it should remain without returning it.' He (Aban) said: So he did that and adjured the people that not one of them should remain with something without returning it. He said: They returned it. When he (the Imam) saw the soil gathered, Ali ibn al-Husayn, may Allah's blessings be upon them both, came and laid the foundation and commanded them to dig. He said: The snake disappeared from them, and they dug until they reached the site of the (original) foundations. Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, said to them: 'Move aside.' So they moved aside. He approached it, covered it with his cloak, then wept. Then he covered it with soil with his own hand. Then he called the builders and said: 'Place your building.' So they placed the building. When its walls rose, he ordered the soil to be turned over and cast into its interior. It is for this reason that the House (Kaaba) is elevated, requiring steps to ascend to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn al-Muthanna al-Khatib, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl and Bishr ibn Ismail, who said: Muhammad ibn Ismail said to me: 'Shall I cheer you up, O son of Muthanna?' I said: 'Yes,' and I arose to him. He said: 'This indecent man entered just now, so he sat opposite Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Then he turned to him and said to him: 'O Abu al-Hasan, what do you say regarding the one in Ihram, can he shade himself on the carriage?' He said to him: 'No.' He said: 'So can he shade himself in the tent?' He said to him: 'Yes.' So he repeated the words to him, like a scoffer, laughing, saying: 'O Abu al-Hasan, so what is the difference between this and this?' He said: 'O Abu Yusuf, indeed the Religion is not by analogy, like your analogies. You are playing with the Religion. We did as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did, and we said as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to ride his mount, so he did not shade himself upon it, and the sun bothered him, so he would cover part of his body with the other part, and sometimes he would cover his face with his hand. And when he dismounted, he would shade himself in the tent, and in the house, and by the wall.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the shade for the one in Ihram, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Brightness is for the One for whom you are wearing Ihram.' I said, 'I am feverish and the heat is intense upon me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that the sun sets along with the sins of the ones in Ihram?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Qasim al-Sayqal, who said: I did not see anyone who was more strict regarding the shade than Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He used to order the dome and the two curtains to be removed when he entered the state of Ihram.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the woman for whom a shade is established and she is in Ihraam. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So the man upon whom a shade is struck and he is in Ihraam?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when he has a headache, and he would give in charity with one Mudd for each day'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said: I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Is it allowed for the one in Ihram to walk under the shade of the carriage?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. He (the narrator) said, 'And a man asked him (peace be upon him) about the shade for the one in Ihram, from the harm of rain or sun, and I was listening. So he (peace be upon him) ordered him that he should expiate with a sheep, and slaughter it at Mina'.

Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Musa ibn Umar, from Muhammad ibn Mansour, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the shade for the one in Ihraam. He said: 'He should not shade except from a reason of illness.'

Ahmad narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa al-Kilabi who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first: 'Ali ibn Shihaab complains of his head, and the cold is severe, and he intends to enter the state of Ihram.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is as you claim, let him shade himself. And as for you, brightness (or clarity) is for the One for whom you are wearing Ihram.'
