Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can the one in Ihram veil himself from the sun?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he is an old man.' Or he said: '(If he is) with an illness.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'The one in Ihram shades upon his carriage, and he expiates when the sun and rain harm him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'How much is the expiation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A sheep.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with the tent upon the women and the children, and they are in Ihraam.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram may not cover himself from the sun with a garment, and there is no objection if he covers part of himself with another part (of his body).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that my paternal aunt is with me and she is my colleague, and the heat is intense upon her when she wears Ihraam. So, what is your view for me if I were to shade upon myself and upon her? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Shade upon her alone'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurara, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram, can he cover himself? He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for [covering] from the heat and the cold, then no.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said: I asked him about a person in Ihram who shaded himself during his Umrah. He said: Blood (slaughter of an animal) is obligatory upon him. He said: And if he went out to Mecca and shaded himself, it is also obligatory upon him blood for his Umrah, and blood for his Hajj.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said: We were in the hallway of Yahya ibn Khalid in Mecca, and there was Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) and Abu Yusuf. So Abu Yusuf stood up to him and squatted in front of him and said, 'O Abu al-Hasan, may I be sacrificed for you, does the one in Ihram shade himself?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'So does he shade by the wall and the carriage, and enter the house and the tent?' He said, 'Yes.' So he said, 'Yes.' So Abu Yusuf laughed as if mocking. So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O Abu Yusuf, indeed the Religion is not by analogy like your analogy and the analogy of your companions. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded in His Book regarding divorce and emphasized it with two witnesses, and He was not pleased with them except if they were two just men. And He commanded in His Book regarding marriage and left it without witnesses. So you have brought two witnesses in what Allah has voided, and you have voided two witnesses in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has emphasized, and you have accepted the divorce of the insane and the intoxicated.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed Hajj, so he entered Ihram and did not shade himself, and entered the house and the tent, and shaded with the carriage and the wall. We did as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did. So he was silent.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one in Ihram cannot immerse himself into the water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one in Ihram does not immerse himself in water, nor does the fasting person.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not touch anything of the perfume, nor of the oils, while in your state of Ihram; and beware of the perfume in your food; and restrain your nose from the pleasant scent, and do not hold it back from the foul smell, for it is not fitting for the one in Ihram to take pleasure in a pleasant scent.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one in Ihram must not touch anything of the perfume, nor the basil (or aromatic herb), nor derive pleasure from it, nor from a pleasant wind. So whoever is tested by something of that, let him give in charity according to the measure of what he did, according to his capacity.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Whoever eats saffron deliberately, or food in which there is perfume, so upon him is blood (slaughter of an animal). So if it was due to forgetfulness, so there is nothing upon him, and he should seek Forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram should withhold his nose from the pleasant scent, and he should not withhold his nose from the foul smell.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, similar to it. And he said: There is no problem with the good scent between As-Safa and Al-Marwa from the scent of the perfumers, and he does not have to hold his nose.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when perfume was uncovered in front of him so that he might look at it, and he was in Ihraam, so he covered his nose with his garment from its aroma.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'The potash (alkali) in it contains perfume; do I wash my hands with it while I am in Ihram?' He said, 'When you intend to enter the state of Ihram, look at your provisions and separate that which you do not need.' And he said, 'Give something in charity as expiation for the potash with which you washed your hand.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one in Ihraam whose clothes are hit by the perfume, he said: There is no problem with him washing it with his own hand.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Hasan ibn Harun, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I ate khabees (a porridge) until I was satiated, and I am in ihram.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have finished your rituals and intend to exit from Makkah, buy dates with one dirham and give them in charity, so it will be an expiation for that, and for what entered into your ihram from what you do not know.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer, from his father who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the salt wherein is saffron, for the one in Ihraam?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for the one in Ihraam that he should eat anything wherein is saffron, nor anything from the perfumes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Al-Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is disliked that the one in Ihram should sleep upon a yellow bed or upon a yellow bed-spread.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not smell perfume while you are in the state of Ihram, nor anything in which there is saffron, and do not taste food in which there is saffron.

Saffan narrated from Abu al-Maghra' who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram washing his hand with ash (potash). He (peace be upon him) said: 'My father used to wash his hand with white ash (potash).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: There is no problem with smelling the idhkhir, the qaysum, the khuzama, the shi'ah, and their like, while you are in the state of ihram.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram who touches perfume while he is asleep and does not know. He said: 'He should wash it, and there is nothing upon him.' And about the one in Ihram who is anointed by the one not in Ihram with aromatic oil, and the one in Ihram does not know what is upon him. He said: 'He should wash it as well, and let him be cautious.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram eating the citron. He said: 'Yes'. I said to him, 'Its smell is aromatic.' He said: 'The citron is food. It is not from the perfumes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about henna, so he said: 'The one in Ihram may touch it and heal his camel with it, and it is not considered perfume, and there is no problem with it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I placed my two Ihram garments along with clothes that had been incensed (perfumed), so I found their aroma in them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Spread them out in the wind until their aroma disappears.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not look into the mirror while you are in the state of Ihram, because it is from the adornments; and the woman in Ihram should not apply kohl with blackness, for indeed blackness is an adornment.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The one in Ihram must not look into the mirror for adornment; so if he looks, he should recite the Talbiyya.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the kohl (eye powder) for the one in Ihram. He said: As for the blackness (kohl), then no. But (yes) with the Sabr and Al-Hudhud.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the one in Ihram complains of his eyes, let him apply kohl that contains neither musk nor perfume.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one in Ihram should not apply kohl except for pain. And he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with applying kohl while you are in Ihram, provided it does not contain perfume whose scent is found. But as for adornment, then no.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the one in Ihram complains (of illness), let him be treated with that which he eats, while he is in Ihram.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by Ka'b ibn 'Ujra, and lice were scattering from his head while he was in Ihram. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do the insects of your head harm you?' He said: 'Yes.' So whoever among you is sick or has an ailment of the head, he (should effect) a compensation by Fasting or alms or sacrificing. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered him to shave his head, and made the fasting to be for three days, and the charity to be upon six poor ones, for each poor one being two Mudds, and the sacrifice a sheep. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And everything in the Quran where it says

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man of impaired vision asked him (peace be upon him), and I was present, so he said, 'Can I apply Kohl when I enter the state of Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' And why would you apply Kohl? He said, 'I am of impaired vision. So when I apply Kohl, it benefits me, and when I do not apply Kohl, it harms me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So apply Kohl.' He said, 'Suppose I place something else along with the Kohl?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What is it?' He said, 'I take two rags, fold them into squares, place one rag over each eye, and bind them with a strip to the back of my head. So when I do that, it benefits me, and when I neglect it, it harms me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So do it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man whose hands and feet crack while he is in the state of Ihram; may he be treated? He said: Yes, with butter and oil. And he said: When the one in Ihram complains, let him be treated with whatever is permissible for him to eat while he is in Ihram.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the person in Ihram who squeezes a pimple and binds a bandage over an ulcer. He said: There is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man from you is afflicted with a wound (khuraj) or a boil (dummal), let him bandage it and let him treat it with oil or butter.

Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Saeed al-A'raj who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram who has a fracture; does he treat it or bind it with a cloth? He said: Yes. And similarly, the ulcer that is on the body.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Imran al-Halbi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the person in Ihram who has a wound, so he treats it with a medication containing saffron. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the saffron is dominant in the medication, then (it is not permissible); and if the other medicines are dominant over it, then there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Najiya, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram whose ears are hit by the wind, so he fears that he would fall sick. Is it correct for him that he closes his ears with the cotton? He said: Yes, there is no problem with that when he fears that, or else, so no.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: There is no problem with the Muhrim tying a strip around his head due to headache.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram getting cupping done. He (peace be upon him) said: No, unless it is inevitable, so let him get cupping done, and the place of the cupping should not be shaved.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muthanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one in Ihram may not get cupping done unless he fears for himself that he will be unable to pray.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram whose nails grow long or one of them breaks and causes him harm. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not cut any of it if he can bear it. But if it causes him harm, let him cut it, and let him feed, in place of each nail, a handful of food.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the one in Ihram who clips a nail: He said, 'He should give in charity with a palmful of food.' He said, 'Two nails?' He said, 'Two palmfuls.' I said, 'Three?' He said, 'Three palmfuls.' I said, 'Four?' He said, 'Four palmfuls.' I said, 'Five?' He said, 'Upon him is blood (of a slaughtered animal) to be spilled. So if he were to cut ten or more than that, there would not be upon him except for blood (of a slaughtered animal) to be spilled.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the one in Ihram clips the nails of his hands and his feet in one place, so upon him is one blood (of a slaughtered animal); and if they were in two different places, so upon him would be two bloods (of two slaughtered animals).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to clip his nails while in ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let them be.' I said: 'But a man from our companions issued a fatwa that if he cuts his nails, he should repeat his ihram, so he did.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is blood (of a slaughtered animal) to be spilled.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram cannot take (cut) from the hairs of one not in Ihram.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever shaves his head or plucks his armpit hair out of forgetfulness, or in error, or out of ignorance, there is nothing upon him; and whoever does it deliberately, upon him is blood (of a slaughtered animal).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If the one in Ihram plucks from the hair of his beard, or anything from other than it, then upon him is that he feeds a poor person in his hand.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who grabs his beard while he is in Ihram, so he tampers with it, so some hairs get plucked off from it and they remain in his hand, out of error, or deliberately. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not harm him'.

Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you places his hand upon his head or his beard while he is in Ihram, and some hair falls off, let him give in charity two handfuls of rusk or Suweeq (a type of bread/broth).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazala ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Abu Al-Jaroud, who said: A man asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a louse while he was in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done.' He said, 'So what is its expiation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no expiation for it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the one in Ihram who killed a louse?' He said: 'There is nothing upon him regarding the lice, and it is not befitting that he deliberately kills it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one in Ihram must not deliberately flick lice from his garment or from his body. If he does one of those things, let him feed food in its place.' I said, 'How much?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'One handful.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is your view if I were to find a louse or a bug upon me, can I throw them off?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and their young ones. They tend to ascend in other than their place of ascending'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whatever the one in Ihram fears upon himself from the beasts of prey, and the snakes, and other than them, let him kill it. And if it does not intend (to attack) you, so you should not attack it.

Ali from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter the state of Ihram, avoid killing all animals, except the viper, the scorpion, and the rat, for they damage the water skins and burn down the houses of the people. And as for the scorpion, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) extended his hand to the stone, and a scorpion stung him, so he said: 'May Allah curse you! You do not spare the righteous nor the sinner.' And the snake, if it intends (to attack) you, kill it; if it does not intend (to attack) you, do not intend (to attack) it. And the vicious dog and the wild beast, if they intend (to attack) you, kill them; if they do not intend (to attack) you, do not intend (to attack) them. And the treacherous black snake, kill it in all cases, and throw the crow and the buzzard upon the back of your camel.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The snake, the treacherous black one, and every evil snake, and the scorpion, and the mouse (which is the small rat), can be killed in the Haram (sanctuary) and in Ihram (state of pilgrimage consecration). The crow and the buzzard are to be pelted (with stones). So if thieves present themselves to you, defend yourself from them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one in Ihram may kill the wasp, the eagle, the treacherous black snake, and the wolf, and whatever he fears might attack him. And he (peace be upon him) said: The vicious dog is the wolf.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a person in Ihram who killed a wasp. He said: 'If it was by mistake, there is nothing upon him.' I said: 'No, but it was deliberate.' He said: 'He should feed something from food.' I said: 'If it intended (to attack) me?' He said: 'Everything which intends (to attack) you, so kill it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about the person in Ihram killing the bug and the flea when they intend (to attack) him. He said: Yes.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The jerboa, the hedgehog, and the lizard: when the one in Ihram causes them to die, the expiation is a kid (young goat); and the kid is better than it, but I said this in order to deter (people) from hunting other than these.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the tick is not from the camel, and the tick-bite (or swelling) on the camel is like the lice on your body; therefore, do not cast it off, and cast off the ticks.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram removing ticks from the camel. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he cannot remove the halamah (the lump of flesh at the base of the horn).'.

Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Armany from Abu Abdillah from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The one in Ihram may kill whatever he fears upon himself.

Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with killing the flea, and the louse, and the bug inside the Haram.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Ahmad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I scratched my head while I was in Ihram, so a louse fell down.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'What do you make upon me as expiation for it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And what do I make upon you for a louse? There is nothing upon you for it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one in Ihram slaughters the cow, the camel, and the sheep, and whatever does not array its wings from the birds, and whatever is permissible for the one not in Ihram to slaughter inside the Haram, so it is also permissible for the one in Ihram (to slaughter) in the unrestricted area as well as in the Haram.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the one in Ihram slaughter his camel or slaughter his sheep?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said to him, 'Does he cut grass for his riding animal and his camel?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he cuts whatever he wishes from the trees until he enters the Haram. So when he enters the Haram, then no.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you scratch your head, scratch gently, and do not scratch with the nails, but with the tips of the fingers.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the one in Ihram washes from major ritual impurity (Janabah), he pours (water) over his head and separates the hair with his fingers, part from part.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with the one in Ihraam entering the bathhouse, but he should not massage (his body).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not (correct) for the one in Ihraam that he answers by (saying), ‘Labbeyk’ (Here I am!), until his Ihraam is off. I said, ‘How should he be saying?’ He (peace be upon him) said: ‘He should be saying, ‘(Yes) O Sa’d!’’.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one in Ihram picking (cleaning) his teeth; he said: There is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the one in Ihram brush his teeth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'And if he bleeds, does he brush his teeth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, it is from the Sunnah.' And it is also reported that he should not bleed.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about whether the one in Ihram can scratch his head and wash with water. He (peace be upon him) said: He can scratch his head as long as he does not intend killing an insect, and there is no problem with him washing with water and pouring it over his head as long as he is not 'mulabbid' (covered with lice powder). If he is mulabbid, he should not pour water over his head except due to wet-dream.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The squatting (ihtiba') is disliked for the one in Ihram, and it is disliked in the Sacred Masjid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Hallal al-Razi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about two men who fought while they were both in Ihram. He said: 'Glory be to Allah, evil is what they have done.' I said: 'They have done it, so what is required of them?' He said: 'Upon each one of them is blood (damm).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the one in Ihram grappling (with someone). Is it correct for him to do so? He said: It is not correct for him out of fear that an injury might hit him, or some of his hair might fall off.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abdullah ibn Sa'id, who said: Abu Abd al-Rahman asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram treating the back of the camel. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He casts off the insects from it and does not bleed it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the person in Ihram who has scabies that harms him. He said: 'He may scratch it. And if blood flows from it, there is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'All goodness is in the sword and beneath the shadow of the sword; and nothing can straighten the people except the sword, and the swords are the keys of Paradise and the Fire.'

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For Paradise there is a gate called the Gate of the Mujahideen. They will proceed toward it and it shall be open, and they will be girded with their swords, while the multitude stand at the place of gathering and the angels welcome them.' Then he said: 'So whoever abandons jihad, God, Mighty and Majestic, will clothe him with humiliation and poverty in his livelihood and obliterate his religion. Verily, God, Mighty and Majestic, has made my community self-sufficient by the hooves of its cavalry and the points of its spears.'

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The cavalry horses of the warriors in this world will be their horses in Paradise, and the robes of the warriors are their swords.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibrail (peace be upon him) informed me of a matter by which my eyes were delighted and my heart rejoiced. He said: O Muhammad, whoever from your community fights in the way of God, and a drop of rain from the sky falls upon him, or a headache afflicts him, God, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him martyrdom.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from one of his companions who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote in a letter to one of the caliphs of the Banu Umayya: And among what he has squandered is the jihad, which God — Mighty and Majestic — has preferred over all deeds, and has preferred its performer over all other workers with a preference in ranks, forgiveness, and mercy — because through it religion became manifest, through it religion is defended, and through it God purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth for paradise, a successful and triumphant transaction, stipulating upon them in it the preservation of the [divine] limits. The first of these [limits] is the call from obedience to servants toward obedience to God — Mighty and Majestic —, and from worship of servants toward worship of God, and from the wilayah of servants toward the wilayah of God. So whoever is called to the jizya and refuses shall be killed and his family taken captive; but the [true] call is not from obedience to a servant toward obedience to another servant like him. And whoever acknowledges the jizya shall not be exceeded against, nor shall his covenant be violated, and he shall be burdened with less than his capacity. The fay' (war spoils) shall belong to the Muslims in general, not to any particular group. And if there is fighting and captives, conduct in that shall be according to his [the Prophet's] sira, and action in that shall be according to his sunnah from the religion. Then he burdened the blind and the lame — those whom God, Mighty and Majestic, had already exempted, who cannot find what to spend on jihad — and he burdens those who are able with what they cannot bear. Rather, [the correct system was that] the people of each garrison city would fight those adjacent to them, with justice maintained among them in military expeditions. But all of that has vanished, to the point that people have become two types: a hired man acting as mercenary after God's transaction, and an employer who fines his companion after God had excused him. The hajj was taken away and wasted, and the people were impoverished. So who is more crooked than the one who made this crooked? And who is more upright than the one who set this upright? He imposed jihad upon the servants while cutting off [the support of] jihad from the servant

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Haydara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Jihad is the most superior of things after the obligatory duties.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ja'far ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Alawi, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas, from Isma'il ibn Ishaq, all together from Abu Rawh Faraj ibn Qurra, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa who said: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to me, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami who said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) said: 'As for what follows: Verily, jihad is a gate from the gates of Paradise that God has opened for His special friends, and has permitted for them as an honor from Him and a blessing He has stored up. And jihad is the garment of taqwa, and the fortified armor of God, and His firm shield. So whoever abandons it out of aversion to it, God will clothe him with the garment of humiliation, and affliction will engulf him, and he will depart from God's pleasure, and he will be abased by pettiness and degradation, and his heart will be sealed with barriers, and truth will be displaced from him through the wasting of jihad, and he will be subjected to humiliation and denied justice. Beware! I have called you to fight these people night and day, secretly and openly, and I said to you: "Attack them before they attack you!" For by God, no people have ever been attacked in the interior of their homes without being humiliated. But you were complacent and abandoned one another until raids were launched upon you and your homelands were seized from you. This brother of Ghamid — his cavalry has entered al-Anbar and killed Hassan ibn Hassan al-Bakri and driven your cavalry from its positions. And it has reached me that a man from them would enter upon a Muslim woman and another woman under protection, and would snatch her anklets, her bracelets, her necklaces, and her earrings, and she could not prevent him except by saying 'innā lillāhi wa-innā ilayhi rāji'ūn' and begging for mercy. Then they departed unharmed — no man of them was wounded nor was any blood shed. So if a Muslim man were to die of grief after this, he would not be blamed for it; rather, in my view he would be worthy of it. How astonishing, how astonishing! By God, it melts the heart and brings sorrow — this gathering of these people upon their falsehood, and your scattering from your truth. So shame on you and woe to you, for you have become a target to be shot at! They raid you and you do not counter-raid; they fight against you and you do not fight b

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hafs al-Kalbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Indeed, God (Mighty and Majestic) sent His Messenger with Islam to the people for ten years, but they refused to accept until He commanded him to fight. Thus, the good is in the sword and beneath the sword, and the matter will return just as it began.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Jibreel informed me of a matter by which my eyes were delighted and my heart was gladdened. He said: O Muhammad! Whoever from your community fights a military campaign in the way of God — no drop of rain from the sky or headache afflicts him except that it will be for him a (status of) martyrdom on the Day of Resurrection.'

And by this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever delivers the message of a warrior (ghazi) is like one who has freed a slave, and he will be his partner in the reward of his military expedition.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever backbites a believing combatant, or harms him, or stays behind him in his family with evil, a scale will be set up for him on the Day of Resurrection, so his good deeds will be exhausted, then he will be cast into the Fire, if the combatant was in the obedience of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, obligated the Jihad and magnified it, and made it His victory and His helper. By Allah! Neither the world nor the Religion can be correct except by it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fight battles, so that your children may inherit glory.'

And by this chain, that Abu Dajjana Al-Ansary wore a turban on the Day of Uhud with his own turban and let the tail of the turban hang between his shoulders until he began to swagger, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, this is a walk that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates, except when fighting in the way of Allah.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Strive (in Jihad), you will acquire (gain spoils/victory).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) He said: 'All goodness is in the sword, and beneath the sword, and in the shade of the sword.' He said, 'And I heard him saying: 'Indeed, all goodness is tied to the forelocks of the cavalry horses until the Day of Resurrection.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father (peace be upon him) said: There are two rulings for war. When the war is active, its weapons have not been put down, and its people have not been defeated, then every prisoner taken during that state, the Imam has a choice regarding him. If he wishes, he strikes his neck, and if he wishes, he cuts off his hand and his leg from opposite sides without stopping (the bleeding) and leaves him wallowing in his blood until he dies.' Indeed, the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to make corruption in the land is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land; that is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. Do you not see that the choice which Allah has granted the Imam is over one thing, and it is the Infidelity, and it is not over different things. So I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: or they be exiled from the land?' He said: 'That is the seeking, that you pursue him with the cavalry until he escapes. So if the cavalry seizes him, a ruling is passed upon him with some of the rulings which I described to you.' And the other ruling is when the war puts down its weapons and its people are defeated, so every prisoner taken during that state, so he is in their hands, then the Imam has a choice regarding him. If he wishes, he favors them and sends them free, and if he wishes, he ransoms their selves, and if he wishes, he enslaves them, so they become slaves.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman Al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about two groups of the believers, one of them being the rebellious (bāghiya) and the other just ('ādila), and the just one defeated the rebellious. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the just group to pursue the fleeing, nor to kill the prisoner, nor to finish off the battlefield, nor to execute the wounded. And this ruling applies if no one from the rebellious group remains, and they do not have a faction (fi'a) to which they can return. But if they have a faction to which they can return, then their prisoners are killed, their fleeing are pursued, and their wounded are executed.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said: I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) dealt with the people of the Qiblah (Muslims) in a manner contrary to the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the people of polytheism.' He said, 'He became angry, then sat down, then said: By Allah, he dealt with them with the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Conquest.' Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) wrote to Malik, while he was at the forefront of his vanguard on the Day of Basra, instructing: 'Do not thrust (the spear) into one who is not facing you, do not kill a fleeing one, do not continue striking an injured one, and whoever closes his door, he is safe.' So he took the letter and placed it in front of him upon the saddle before reading it, then said, 'Fight.' So they fought them until they made them enter the markets of Basra. Then he opened the letter, read it, then ordered a caller who called out with what was in the letter.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Uthafar, from Uqba ibn Bashir, from Abdullah ibn Sharik, from his father, who said: When the people were defeated on the Day of the Camel, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not pursue the fleeing, and do not attack the injured; and whoever closes his door, he is secure.' So when it was the Day of Siffin, he killed the advancing and the retreating, and attacked the injured. So Aban ibn Taghlib said to Abdullah ibn Sharik: 'These are two different practices.' He said: 'The people of the Camel killed Talha and Al-Zubayr, and Muawiya was standing personally, and he was their leader.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The one who flees from two men during the fighting in the advance (al-zahf) has fled (retreated), and the one who flees from three men during the fighting in the advance has not fled (has not retreated).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Misma ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Surah al-Bara'ah (Disavowal) with Ali (peace be upon him), he sent some people with him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who lets himself be made a captive without having sustained any heavy injuries, so he is not from us (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Whoever allows himself to be taken captive without sustaining a heavy injury, he is not ransomed from the Public Treasury, but he is ransomed from his own wealth if his family wishes.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Khashshab from Ibn Baqqah from Mu'adh ibn Thabit from 'Amr ibn Jumay' from Abu ' from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: He was asked about the duel between the two lines after the permission of the Imam (peace be upon him). He said: 'There is no problem, but it is not sought except by the permission of the Imam (peace be upon him).'

A number of our companions narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Ibn al-Qaddah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man challenged a certain person from Banu Hashim to a duel (al-baraz), but he refused to duel him. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) asked him, 'What prevented you from dueling him?' He replied, 'He was the horseman (strongman) of the Arabs, and I feared that he would overpower me.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Indeed, he has transgressed against you. If you had duelled him, you would have overcome him. And if a mountain transgresses against a mountain, the transgressor is crushed.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) challenged a man to a duel. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) learned of this and said, 'If you do something like this again, I will reprimand you. And if someone challenges you to something like this and you do not respond, I will also reprimand you. Have you not noticed that it is transgression (bagh)?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Isa ibn Yunus, from Al-Awzari, from Al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: When you take a prisoner who is unable to walk and you have no carrier with you, then send him back and do not kill him, for you do not know what the ruling of the Imam is regarding him. He said, and the prisoner said: When he becomes a Muslim, his blood is saved and he becomes booty (property of the Muslims).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Feeding the prisoner is a right upon the one who imprisoned him, and even if he intended killing him the next day. So it is befitting that he feeds him, and quenches him, and shades him, and is kind with him, whether he was an Infidel or someone else.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The prisoner's food is upon the one who captured him as a right upon him, and even if he is an infidel who will be killed the next day, it is befitting for him to be kind to him, feed him, and give him drink.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the food of the prisoner, and he said: 'Feeding him is a right upon the one who captures him, and even if he intends to kill him the next day, for it is befitting that he is fed, and given drink, and shaded, and treated with kindness, whether he is an infidel or not.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from one of the companions of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the captive whom the enemy takes from the Muslims during fighting, from the children of the Muslims or from their owned slaves, so they hold them. Then the Muslims afterwards fight them and gain victory over them, capture them, and take from them what they had taken from the owned slaves of the Muslims and their children whom they had taken from the Muslims. How should they be dealt with, from the children of the Muslims and their owned slaves? He said, so he said: 'As for the children of the Muslims, they are not evaluated in the share of the Muslims, but they are returned to their father, or their brother, or to their guardian with witnesses. And as for the owned slaves, they are evaluated in the share of the Muslims, so they are sold and their masters are given the value of their price from the Public Treasury of the Muslims.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man whose enemy met him and acquired wealth or chattels from him, then the Muslims acquired that. How should one deal with the chattels of the man? He said: If they acquired it before they had possessed the man's chattels, it is returned to him; and if they acquired it after having possessed it, then it is war booty (fa'i) for the Muslims, and he has the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him, 'The battalion which the Imam sends, so they acquire war booty, how is it distributed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they fought over it with a commander whom the Imam appointed over them, one-fifth is taken out from it for Allah and for the Messenger, and four-fifths are distributed between them. And if they did not fight the Polytheists over it, everything which they acquired is for the Imam; he makes it wherever he likes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad, altogether from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said: One of my brothers wrote to me to ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about certain matters from the Sunnah. So I asked him, or wrote to him with them. Among what I asked him was: 'Inform me about the army when it battles in the land of war, acquires booty, and then another army joins them before they exit to the House of Peace (Dar al-Salam), and they did not encounter an enemy until they all exited to the House of Peace. Would they share in the booty?' He said: 'Yes'. And about a raiding party that was in a ship, and the owner of the horse did not ride his horse. How is the booty distributed among them?' He said: 'For the horseman two shares, and for the foot soldier one share.' I said: 'And if they did not ride and did not fight upon their horses?' He said: 'What do you think if they were in an army, and the foot soldiers were sent forward, fought, and acquired booty, how would it be distributed among them? Would I not have made two shares for the horseman and one share for the foot soldier, even though they acquired the booty without the horsemen?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Husayn ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man has multiple horses during a military expedition, a share is allocated to him for only two of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from one of his companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: The khums is taken from the war booty and is made for the one whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it for, and four-fifths are distributed among those who fought for it and had authority over it. He (peace be upon him) said: And for the Imam is the choicest part of the wealth; he may take the fine slave girl, the fine animal, the garment, and the chattels from whatever he loves and desires, so that is for him before the distribution of the wealth and before the extraction of the khums. He (peace be upon him) said: And there is nothing for the fighters from the lands, nor what they overcome over it, except what the soldiers possess, and there is not anything from the war booty for the Bedouins, even if they fought with the Imam, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made a treaty with the Bedouins that he would leave them in their homes and they would not emigrate, on the condition that if a raid came upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from his enemies, he would summon them and fight with them, and they would have no share in the war booty, and it is a flowing Sunnah regarding them and others. And the land that is taken forcibly by cavalry or riders, it is dedicated and left in the hands of the one who cultivates it and revives it and manages it, according to what the governor deems correct for them in accordance with their capacity, from the right, half, third, and two-thirds, according to what is correct for them and does not harm them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Bedouins: Is jihad upon them? He said: No, except if there is a fear for Islam, so they are sought for assistance. I said: So do they have anything from the jizyah? He said: No.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Ali (peace be upon him), regarding the man who comes to the people (combatants), and they had acquired war booty, and he had not been present for the fighting. So Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'They are the deprived ones', and (but still) he ordered that it should be distributed to them.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the war booty, so he said: One-fifth is taken out from it for Allah, and one-fifth for the Messenger, and whatever remains is distributed among it remains is distributed between those who fought for it, and those who were in charge of it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the women with him in the war so that they would treat the wounded, and he did not distribute to them anything from the war booty, but he gifted it to them voluntarily.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The best of companions (friends) are four, and the best of battalions are four hundred, and the best of armies are four thousand, and ten thousand would not be overcome due to scarcity (of numbers).

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fuzayl ibn Khaysam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'An army of ten thousand would not be defeated due to scarcity (of numbers)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleyman ibn Dawood Al-Minqari, who said: An-Nadr ibn Ismail Al-Balkhi informed me, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Shahr ibn Howshab. He said: Al-Hajjaj said to me and asked me about the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) going out to his battlefields, so I said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) participated in Badr with three hundred and thirteen, and participated in Uhud with six hundred, and participated in Al-Khandaq (The Trench) with nine hundred. He said: From whom are you saying this? I said: From Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: Strayed is the one, by Allah, who walks upon other than his way.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The cavalry horses used to be wild in the Arab lands, so Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) ascended Mount Jiyad, then they shouted: 'Do not be loose, do not be loose!' He said: 'So there did not remain a horse excepted no horse but that it gave its hand (foreleg) to them and enabled its forelock (to be touched by them).'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Goodness is tied to the forelocks of the horses until the Day of Resurrection.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'All goodness is tied in the forelocks of the cavalry horses until the Day of Resurrection.'

From him, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim Al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who ties up an old horse, three sins are erased from him every day and eleven good deeds are written for him; and the one who ties up a hybrid horse, two sins are erased from him every day and seven good deeds are written for him; and the one who ties up a workhorse intending by it beauty, or fulfilling needs, or repelling an enemy from him, one sin is erased from him every day and six good deeds are written for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) raced the cavalry horses that were prepared, from Al-Hafya to the mosque of the Banu Zureiq, and awarded them from three palm trees (clusters of dates). So he gave the first one a cluster, and gave the second one a cluster, and gave the third one a cluster. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), (it is) exactly the same.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no racing (sabaq) except in a camel's hoof, or a horse's hoof, or an arrowhead, meaning archery.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) raced the cavalry horses and set the prize for their victory as an Awqiya of silver.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If an animal balks for one of you, meaning it stands in the land of the enemy or in the Way of Allah, then let him slaughter it and not hamstring it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is nothing which the Angels attend except for the pledge (of a contest) and the playing of the man with his wife.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: Archery (throwing of arrows) is one of the arrows of Islam.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Imran ibn Musa from Al-Hasan ibn Tariq from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, raising it, said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And prepare against them whatever force you can and horses tied at the frontier': 'Archery'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no pre-payment (sabaq) except in a camel's hoof, or a horse's hoof, or an arrowhead, meaning archery.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he used to attend the archery and the horse-racing contest

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Polytheists raided the free-pasture land of Medina, so a caller called out in it, 'O evil morning!' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) heard it while among the cavalry, so he rode his horse in pursuit of the enemy. The first of his companions to catch up with him was Abu Qatada on his horse. And beneath the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was a saddle whose two pads were of fine linen, containing neither roughness nor pride. So he sought the enemy but they did not encounter anyone, and the cavalry followed him in succession. So Abu Qatada said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the enemy has dispersed. If you see fit, let us race.' He said, 'Yes.' So they raced, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out first among them. Then he turned towards them and said, 'I am the son of the 'Awateek from Quraysh. It is the steed of the ocean,' meaning his horse.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The polytheists raided the pasture area of Medina, and an announcer cried out in it: 'How bad is this morning!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) heard it while among the cavalry, so he mounted his horse in pursuit of the enemy. The first of his companions to reach him was Abu Qatadah on his horse. The saddle of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had two pads made of palm fiber, containing no extravagance or pride. They pursued the enemy but found no one, and the cavalry followed one after another. Abu Qatadah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the enemy has departed; if you see fit, let us race.' He said: 'Yes.' They raced, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) emerged as the winner among them. Then he turned to them and said: 'I am the son of the three 'Awatik women of Quraysh; indeed, it is al-Jawad al-Bahr,' meaning his horse.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Fazara, from Anas or Haysam ibn al-Bara', who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The thief enters my house wanting my life and my wealth.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Kill him, and I bear witness to Allah and whoever hears it that his blood is on my neck (responsibility).'

And by his chain, that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was visited by a man who said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! A thief entered upon my wife and stole her ornaments.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, if he had entered upon a son of Safiyyah, he would not have been pleased with that until he had covered him with the sword.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'When the robbing thief comes upon you, kill him. So whatever [blood/gold] he takes from you, his blood is upon my neck [as guarantee].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is killed defending his right (from oppression), he is a martyr.'

And by this chain, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is killed facing his oppression, he is a martyr.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Maryam! Do you know what is 'facing his oppression'?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The man who is killed instead of his family, and instead of his wealth, and similar to that.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Maryam! Indeed, from jurisprudence is the recognition of the truth.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who fights for his wealth. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who is killed for his wealth, he is at the status of the martyr.' I said, 'Is his fighting better, or not fighting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, if it were me, I would not fight and leave him.'

From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Washa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Arta'ah ibn Habib Al-Asadi, from a man, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is exceeded against with regards to a charity of his wealth, so he fights and is killed, so he is a martyr.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) About the man who is on a journey and with him is a slave girl, and a group comes intending to take his slave girl. Should he prevent his slave girl from being taken even if he fears being killed upon himself? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said: 'And similarly, if it was his wife with him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said: 'And similarly, the mother, and the daughter, and the daughter of the paternal uncle, and the relatives, should he prevent them even if he fears being killed upon himself?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said: 'And similarly, the wealth, they intend to take it during a journey, so he prevents it even if he fears being killed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the words of Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'By Allah! A thousand strikes with the sword are easier than death upon a bed.' He said: 'In the Way of Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Above every person of righteousness is a [more meritorious] righteous deed, until he is killed in the Way of Allah. So when he is killed in the Way of Allah, there is no righteous deed above it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Anbasa, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no drop more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a drop of blood in the way of Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, raising it, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) addressed [the people] on the Day of the Camel. So he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! I came to these people, invited them, and argued with them, so they invited me to wait for the executioner and to step forward for spear-throwing. So for their mother is the bereavement. I have been, and am not, threatened by war, nor am I scared by the striking. I am the one who blunted their sharp edges and dispersed their groups. With that heart, I face my enemy, and I am upon what my Lord promised me of victory, support, and triumph. And I am upon conviction from my Lord and without doubt in my affair.' O people! Death does not miss the one who stays, nor does it frustrate the one who flees. There is no escape from death, and whoever does not die is killed. And indeed, the best of deaths is being killed. And by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a thousand strikes with the sword are easier upon me than death upon a bed. And wonder at Talha, who rallied the people against the son of Affan, until when he was killed, he gave me his clasp with his right hand willingly, then he broke his allegiance to me. O Allah! Seize him and do not delay him. And indeed Al-Zubayr broke his allegiance to me, cut off my kinship, and backed my enemy against me, so suffice him today with whatever You desire.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'What is the matter that the martyr is not tested in his grave?' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The lightning above his head suffices as a test.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who is killed in the Way of Allah, Allah will not introduce him to anything from his sins.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalanisi, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which Jihad is the most superior?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whose horse is hamstrung and his blood is shed in the Way of Allah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, smiles at a man in a battalion when a predator or a thief comes upon them, so he defends them, allowing them to pass.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Your helping the weak is from the most superior of the charity.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musanna, from Fitr ibn Khaleefa, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, may the prayers of Allah be upon them, said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Rasool Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repels from a group of Muslims an adversity of water or fire, Paradise is obligated for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a group of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A community is not sanctified unless the right of its weak is taken from its strong without hesitation.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Arafa, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'You must enjoin the good and forbid the evil, or else your wicked ones will be appointed over you; then your good ones will supplicate, but their supplication will not be answered for them.'
And by his chain, he said, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The most evil of the people are the people who fault the enjoining of the good and the forbidding of the evil.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Yahya ibn Uqayl, from Hasan, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon, so he praised Allah and extolled Him. And he said: As for what follows, indeed those who were before you were destroyed because of whatever acts of disobedience they committed, and the Rabbis and the Scholars did not forbid them from that. And when they persisted in the acts of disobedience and the Rabbis and the Scholars did not forbid them from that, the punishments descended upon them. So enjoin the good and forbid the evil, and know that enjoining the good and forbidding the evil does not bring the term (of life) nearer nor cut off the livelihood. Indeed, the Command descends from the sky to the earth like drops of rain to every soul, with whatever Allah has measured for it, of increase or decrease. So if a misfortune befalls one of you in family, or wealth, or self, and he sees in his brother an abundance of family, or wealth, or self, let it not be a trial/distress for him. For indeed the Muslim man is free from treachery as long as he does not conceal a lowliness that becomes apparent. So he fears it when it is mentioned, and the base people are tempted by it. He is like the left-paralyzed one who awaits the first success from his dice, so that the booty is obligated for him and the debt is repelled from him. And similarly, the Muslim man who is free from treachery awaits from Allah the Exalted one of the two good things: either the caller of Allah (death), for what is with Allah is better for him, or the sustenance of Allah. So when he is with family and wealth, and with him is his religion and his lineage, indeed wealth and sons are the crop of the world, and righteous deeds are the crop of the Hereafter, and Allah may gather both of these for some people. So fear Allah as He has warned you from Himself, and fear Him with a fear that is not an excuse, and work without showing off nor being heard (fame), for whoever acts for other than Allah, Allah leaves him to the one he has acted for. We ask Allah for the stations of the martyrs, and the companionship of the happy ones, and the association of the prophets.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent two angels to the people of a city to overturn it upon its inhabitants. So when they arrived at the city, they found a man supplicating to Allah and pleading humbly. One of the angels said to his companion: 'Do you not see this supplicator?' He said: 'I have seen him, but I must proceed with what my Lord has commanded me.' He said: 'No, but I will not do anything until I refer it back to my Lord.' So he returned to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and said: 'O Lord, I arrived at the city and found Your servant so-and-so supplicating to You and pleading to You.' He said: 'Proceed with what I commanded you, for that man has never had his face clouded with anger towards Me at all.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That a man from Khas'am came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me, what is the most superior of Islam?' He said, 'Belief in Allah.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Maintaining relationships.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Enjoining the good and forbidding the evil.' He said, 'So the man said, 'So which of the deeds is most hateful to Allah?' He said, 'Association with Allah.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Cutting off relationships.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Enjoining the evil and forbidding the good.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered us to meet the people of disobedience with unfriendly faces.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, raising it, said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The enjoining of the good, and the forbidding from the evil are two creatures from the creatures of Allah. So the one who helps these two, Allah would Honour him, and the one who abandons these two, Allah would Abandon him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), whenever he passed by a group quarrelling, would not pass them until he said three times: 'Fear Allah', raising his voice with it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Arafa, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying: When my community leave it upon each other for the enjoining of the good and the forbidding of the evil, so they would be authorising afflictions from Allah the Exalted'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How will it be with you when your women become corrupt and your youth become immoral, and you do not enjoin the good nor forbid the evil?' It was said to him, 'And will that happen, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'Yes, and something worse than that.' 'How will it be with you when you enjoin the evil and forbid the good?' It was said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, and will that happen?' He said, 'Yes, and something worse than that.' 'How will it be with you when you see the good as evil and the evil as good?'

And by this chain, it was said that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates the weak believer who has no religion for him.' So it was said to him: 'And what is the believer who has no religion for him?' He said: 'The one who does not forbid from the evil.'
