And by this chain, I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: He was asked about enjoining the good and forbidding the evil: 'Is it obligatory upon the entire community?' He said: 'No.' It was said to him: 'And why?' He said: 'Rather, it is upon the strong, the obeyed, who is knowledgeable of the good and the evil, not upon the weak who is not guided of the way, to which from which, he should be speaking from the truth to the falsehood.' And from among you there should be a community inviting to the better and enjoin what is good and forbid the evil. Thus, these are particular ones and not the general public, just as Allah Mighty and Majestic Said: 'And of Musa's people was a party who guided (people) with the truth, and thereby did they do justice.' And He did not Say: 'And it is upon the people of Musa', nor 'Upon every one of his people', and in those days they were different communities, and the community can be one (man), just as Allah Mighty and Majestic Said that: 'Surely Ibrahim was a community, obedient to Allah'. He is Saying: 'Obedient to Allah Mighty and Majestic'. And it is not upon the one who knows that in these times of truce from danger, when there was not strength for him, nor an excuse, and do obedience. Mas'ada said, 'And I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and he was asked about the Hadeeth which came from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that: 'The most superior of the Jihad is the just word in the presence of an unjust leader', what is its meaning?' He said: 'This is upon a stipulation that he would enjoin him (with the good) after having recognised it (himself), and along with that, he (the leader) would accept it from him, or else, so no!'.

And with this chain, I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: He was asked about commanding the good and forbidding the evil, whether it is obligatory upon the entire nation, so he said: No. He was asked: Why? He said: It is only upon the strong, obeyed, and knowledgeable person who knows the good from the evil. It is not upon the weak person who cannot find a way to distinguish which is which, saying from the truth to falsehood. And the proof of that is the Book of Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, His saying: 'Let there be from among you a nation that invites to good, enforces what is right, and forbids what is wrong.' This is specific, not general, just as Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, said: 'And from the people of Moses is a nation that guides by the truth and thereby administers justice.' And He did not say 'upon the nation of Moses' nor 'upon all his people,' for they at that time were different nations. And 'nation' can mean one person and upwards, just as Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, said: 'Indeed, Abraham was a nation, obedient to Allah.' Meaning obedient to Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious. And it is not obligatory upon anyone who knows this during this period of respite if he has no strength, no excuse, and no obedience (to enforce). Mas'adah said: And I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: He was asked about the hadith that came from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that 'The best jihad is a word of justice before an unjust Imam.' What is its meaning? He said: This is when he commands it after knowing it, and he is accepted for it in that matter; otherwise, no.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yahya al-Taweel, Sahib al-Minqari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is sufficient for the believer's honor that when he sees an evil, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows of his denial of it in his heart.

And by this chain, he said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Only a believer is commanded to enjoin good and forbid evil, so he gives advice, or if ignorant, so he learns; and as for the owner of the whip or sword, no.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mufaddal ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'O Mufaddal! The one who exposes himself to an unjust ruler, and an affliction befalls him, he will not be rewarded for it, nor will he be granted patience for it.'

Ali, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ghayath ibn Ibrahim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), whenever he passed by a group who were quarrelling, would not pass them until he said three times: 'Fear Allah, Fear Allah', raising his voice with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mahfuz al-Iskaaf, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) throw pebbles at the Jamarat al-Aqaba and then depart. So I walked in front of him like a path-clearer for him. And behold, a pale man, an Amraki, had inserted a peg into the ground, resembling a settler, and tied it to his tent. The people were standing, unable to pass. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O this man, fear Allah, for that which you are doing is not for you.' He (the narrator) said, So the Amraki said to him: 'Can't you just go about your work? The one who is burdened (with the duty of forbidding evil), whose identity is unknown, keeps coming to me saying: O this man, fear Allah.' He (the narrator) said, So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) raised the halter of a camel of his that was tied, lowered his head, and passed by. And the Amraki, the slave, left him.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about jihad: Is it a sunnah or an obligation? So he said: Jihad is of four kinds — two are obligatory, and one is a sunnah that cannot be established except alongside the obligatory. As for one of the two obligations, it is a man's striving against his own soul from the disobedience of God, Mighty and Majestic, and that is among the greatest jihads; and fighting those of the disbelievers who are nearest to you is an obligation. As for the jihad that is a sunnah that cannot be established except alongside an obligation, fighting the enemy is obligatory upon the entire community, and if they were to abandon jihad, the punishment would certainly come upon them — this is among the punishments of the community; and it is a sunnah upon the Imam alone to go to the enemy with the community and fight them. As for the jihad that is sunnah, it is every sunnah that a man establishes and strives in its establishment, fulfillment, and revival; the working and striving for it is among the most excellent of deeds, because it revives a sunnah. And indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever establishes a good sunnah shall have its reward and the reward of those who act upon it until the Day of Judgment, without anything being diminished from their rewards.

And by his chain, from Al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked my father (may the prayers of Allah be upon him) about the wars of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the questioner was from our lovers, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with five swords; three of them are brandished, so they will not be sheathed until war puts down its burdens, and war will not put down its burdens until the sun rises from its west. When the sun rises from its west, all people will be safe on that day, so on that day no soul's faith will benefit it if it had not believed before or acquired good through its faith. And one of them is restrained, and one of them is sheathed, which was unsheathed to other than us, and its ruling is for us. As for the three brandished swords: one is against the Arab polytheists. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'So kill the polytheists wherever you find them...' If they repent (meaning they believe) and establish prayer and pay zakat, then they are your brothers in religion. So for these, nothing will be accepted except killing or entering Islam, and their wealth and offspring will be captives, according to what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established, for he took captives, forgave, and accepted ransom. The second sword is against the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma). Allah the Exalted said: 'And speak to people good words.' This verse was revealed regarding the People of the Covenant, then it was abrogated by His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day... from those who were given the Book, until they pay the jizyah with their own hands and they are humbled.' So whoever of them is in the House of Islam, nothing will be accepted from them except the jizyah or killing, and their wealth is war booty and their offspring are captives. When they accept the jizyah upon themselves, taking them as captives is prohibited for us, their wealth is prohibited, and marrying them is permissible for us. And whoever of them is in the House of War, it is permissible for us to take them as captives and their wealth, and marrying them is not permissible for us, and nothing will be accepted from them except entering the House of Islam

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) sent a brigade. So when they returned, he said: 'Welcome to the people who have accomplished the smaller jihad, and there remains the greater jihad.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family), what is the greater jihad?' He said: 'The jihad of the self.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer Regarding the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'Save yourselves and your families from a Fire.' I said, 'How can one save them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Enjoin with what Allah has Commanded with, and forbid them from what Allah has Forbidden them. So if they obey you, you would have saved them, and if they disobey you, you would have fulfilled what is upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire,' [he was asked] 'How can we save our families?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should enjoin them [to do good] and forbid them [from evil].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever seeks the pleasure of the people with what angers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, his praisers from the people will be condemners; and whoever prefers the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, even if it annoys the people, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will suffice him with the enmity of every enemy, the envy of every envious one, and the aggression of every aggressor, and Allah will be for him a Helper and a Supporter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever pleases a ruler by incurring the anger of Allah, has exited from the religion of Islam.'

And by this chain, said, 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who seeks the pleasure of the people with what Angers Allah (Mighty and Majestic), his praisers from the people would become his condemners'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Amra al-Sulami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man asked him, and said: 'I used to go frequently on military expeditions, travel far in seeking reward, and prolong my absences. Then that was prohibited for me, and they said: There is no military expedition except with a just Imam. So what is your view — may God keep you well?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you wish, I can give you a general answer, and if you wish, I can give you a specific one.' He said: 'Rather, give me a general answer.' He said: 'Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — will resurrect people according to their intentions on the Day of Resurrection.' He (the narrator) said: It was as if he desired the specific answer. He said: 'Then give me a specific one — may God keep you well.' So he said: 'Give me a case.' The man said: 'I went on a military expedition and encountered the polytheists — is it befitting to fight them before inviting them (to Islam)?' He said: 'If they had attacked and been fought and fought back, then you may proceed on that basis. But if they were a people who had not attacked and had not fought, then it is not permissible for you to fight them until you invite them.' The man said: 'So I invited them, and one responded to me, affirming Islam in his heart, and he was within Islam. But injustice was then done against him in judgment, his sanctity was violated, his wealth was taken, and transgression was committed against him — so how does this matter turn out, since I was the one who invited him?' He said: 'Both of you will be rewarded for what occurred. And him being with you — protecting your sanctity from behind, defending your qibla, safeguarding your Book, and preserving your blood — is better than him being against you, demolishing your qibla, violating your sanctity, shedding your blood, and burning your Book.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), he said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man from your followers — news reached him that a man is giving away a sword and a horse in the way of God. So he went to him and took them both, while being ignorant of the proper manner of the Way (of Jihad). Then his companions met him and informed him that the Way with these (rulers) is not permissible, and ordered him to return them both.' So he (the Imam) said: 'Then let him do so.' He said: 'He sought the man but did not find him, and he was told that the man had already departed.' He (the Imam) said: 'Then let him be stationed and not fight.' He said: 'In places like Qazween, al-Daylam, and Asqalan, and what resembles these border regions?' He (the Imam) said: 'Yes.' Then he said to him: 'Can he wage jihad?' He (the Imam) said: 'No, except if he fears for the offspring of the Muslims.' He said: 'What do you think — if the Romans were to invade the Muslims, would it not be fitting for him to prevent them?' He (the Imam) said: 'He should be stationed and not fight. But if he fears for the very core of Islam and the Muslims, he may fight — and his fighting will be for himself, not for the (unjust) ruler.' He said: 'I said: And if the enemy comes to the very place where he is stationed, how should he act?' He (the Imam) said: 'He should fight in defense of the core of Islam — not for these (rulers) — because in the extinction of Islam is the extinction of the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'
Ali, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran, from Yunus, from al-Reza (peace be upon him): similar to it.

'Abbad al-Basri met Ali ibn al-Husayn (blessings of God be upon him) on the road to Mecca and said to him: 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn! You have abandoned jihad and its hardship and turned toward the Hajj and its ease. Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, says:' "Indeed God has purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth in exchange for Paradise; they fight in the way of God, so they kill and are killed — a promise binding upon Him in truth, in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran. And who is more fulfilling of his covenant than God? So rejoice in the transaction you have made with Him, and that is the great triumph." [9:111] So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Complete the verse.' And he said: "The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the fasters, those who bow, those who prostrate, those who enjoin good and forbid evil, and those who preserve the limits of God — and give glad tidings to the believers." [9:112] Then Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'When we find those who possess these characteristics, then jihad alongside them is superior to the Hajj.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira who said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah said to al-Ridha (peace be upon him) while I was listening: 'My father narrated to me from his household, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that he said to one of them: In our lands there is a garrison post called Qazween, and an enemy called al-Daylam. So is there any jihad or ribat?' So he (the Imam) said: 'It is upon you with this House (Kaaba), so perform its hajj.' Then he repeated the statement to him, and he (the Imam) said: 'It is upon you with this House (Kaaba), so perform its hajj.' Is one of you not pleased that he may be in his home, spending upon his family from his earnings, awaiting our matter (the Rising)? If he attains it, he will be like one who was present at Badr with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). And if he dies while awaiting our matter, he will be like one who was with our Qa'im (peace be upon him) — like this — in his tent,' and he joined his two index fingers together. 'And I am not saying like this,' and he joined his index finger and middle finger, 'for this one is longer than this one.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'He spoke the truth.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from whoever mentioned it, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalanisi, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: Indeed I saw in a dream that I said to you: Fighting alongside other than the Imam whose obedience is obligatory is forbidden, like carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine. And you said to me: It is like that. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is like that, it is like that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said — he thinks from Abu Hamza al-Thumali — from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whenever the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) wanted to send out a military expedition (sariyya), he would call them and have them sit before him, then he would say: 'March in the name of God, and with God, and in the way of God, and upon the religion of the Messenger of God. Do not commit excesses with the war gains, do not mutilate the dead, do not be treacherous, do not kill the decrepit elderly, nor a child, nor a woman, and do not cut down a tree unless you are compelled to do so. And whichever man — from the lowest of the Muslims to the most virtuous among them — extends his protection toward a man from the polytheists, then that man is under protection until he hears the word of God. If he follows you, he is your brother in the faith; and if he refuses, then escort him to his place of safety, and seek assistance from God against him.'
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) forbade the throwing of poison into the cities of the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suhayb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) never planned a night attack against an enemy at all.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) sent me to Yemen and said to me: 'O Ali, do not fight anyone until you call him (to Islam). And I swear by God, that God should guide one man through your hands is better for you than all that the sun rises upon and sets, and his wilayah belongs to you, O Ali.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) would never fight until the sun declined (past midday), and he would say: 'The gates of the heavens are opened, mercy draws near, and victory descends.' And he would say: 'It is nearer to the night, and more fitting that the killing be few, the pursuer returns, and the vanquished escapes.'

Ali, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a city from the cities of the people of war: is it permissible to direct water against them and to burn it with fire, or to bombard it with catapults until they are killed, when among them are women, children, the aged elderly, Muslim captives, and merchants? He (AS) said: 'One may do that to them, and one should not hold back from them because of these (people). And there is no blood money (diya) upon them for the Muslims, nor any expiation (kaffara).' And I asked him about women — how the jizyah has fallen from them and been lifted from them. He (AS) said: 'Because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade fighting against women and children in the abode of war, except if they fight. If she (a woman) fights as well, then hold back from her as much as you can while not fearing a breach (in the battle line).' Since he forbade killing them in the abode of war, then in the abode of Islam it is all the more so. And if she refused to pay the jizyah, killing her would not be possible. Since killing her is not possible, the jizyah is therefore lifted from her. And if men refused to pay the jizyah, they would be violators of the covenant, and their blood would be licit and their killing (permissible) — because killing men is permissible in the land of polytheism. Similarly, the crippled among the people of dhimmah, the blind, the dying elderly, the woman, and children in the land of war — for this reason the jizyah is lifted from them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), whenever he sent out a battalion, would supplicate for it.

Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to, when he sent a commander of his upon a battalion, order him to fear Allah Mighty and Majestic in his own private conduct first, then regarding his companions generally. Then he would say: 'Attack in the Name of Allah and in the Way of Allah. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah, and do not be treacherous, do not commit excesses, do not mutilate, do not kill any child nor any monk in a mountain retreat, do not burn palm trees nor flood them with water, do not cut down a fruit-bearing tree, and do not burn down crops — for you do not know, perhaps you will be in need of them. And do not hamstring from among the livestock whose flesh may be eaten, except what is absolutely necessary for you to eat. And when you encounter an enemy of the Muslims, call them to one of three things: if they respond to any one of them, then accept from them and restrain yourselves from them — call them to Islam; if they enter into it, accept it from them and restrain yourselves from them. And call them to emigration (hijra) after Islam; if they do that, then accept it from them and restrain yourselves from them. If they refuse to emigrate and choose to remain in their homelands and refuse to enter the abode of hijra, then they will be at the status of the Bedouin believers — upon them will apply what applies to the Bedouin Muslims, and they will have no share in the war booty (fay') nor in any distribution, unless they migrate in the Way of Allah. If they refuse these two, then call them to pay the jizya (tribute) in submission and humiliation. If they pay the jizya, accept it from them and restrain yourself from them. If they refuse, then seek the help of Allah Mighty and Majestic against them and wage jihad against them for the sake of Allah as is His right. And when you besiege the people of a fortress and they request that they descend upon the judgment of Allah Mighty and Majestic, do not grant them that — instead, let them descend upon your judgment, then judge among them afterwards as you wish. For if you leave them upon the judgment of Allah, you will not know whether you are reaching the judgment of Allah regarding them or not. And when you besiege the people of a fortress and they request permission to descend under the responsibility (dhimma) of Allah and the responsibility of His Messenger, do not let them de

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj, both of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whenever the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) sent out a military expedition, he would call its commander, seat him by his side, and seat his companions before him; then say: 'March in the name of God, and with God, and in the way of God, and upon the religion of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). Do not be treacherous, do not steal from the spoils, do not mutilate, and do not cut down a tree unless you are compelled to. Do not kill a decrepit old man, nor a child, nor a woman.' And whichever man, from the lowest to the most excellent of the Muslims, grants protection to any of the polytheists, he is under protection until he hears the word of God. When he hears the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: if he follows you, he is your brother in your religion; and if he refuses, seek God's assistance against him and deliver him to his place of safety. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly, except that he said: And whichever man from the Muslims grants protection to a man from the polytheists — whether in the farthest part of the army or its nearest — he is under protection.

I said to him: 'What is the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): "The lowest of them acts by their covenant of protection"?' He said: 'If an army of Muslims besieges a people of the polytheists, and a man approaches and says: "Give me security until I meet your companion and debate him," and the lowest of them grants him the security, then it becomes obligatory upon the most superior of them to honor it.'

Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) allowed the granting of security (aman) by an owned slave to the people of a fort from the forts, and said: 'He is from the believers.'

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: There is no man who grants security to a man upon a covenant of protection, then kills him, except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection bearing a banner of treachery.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — or from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — who said: If a people besiege a city and those inside ask them for security (aman), and they say 'no', but the besieged think they said 'yes', and they descend to them, they would be under protection.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: I read in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) wrote a document between the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who joined them from the people of Yathrib: that every raiding party which fights must do so in a manner where they take turns according to proper conduct and equity among the Muslims — for no war is permissible except with the permission of those responsible for it; and that the neighbor is like oneself, without causing harm or committing sin; and the sanctity of the neighbor upon the neighbor is like the sanctity of his own mother and his own father. No believer should make peace apart from another believer during fighting in the way of God, except on the basis of justice and equality.
A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The enemy of action is laziness.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: My father (peace be upon him) said to one of his children: 'Beware of laziness and boredom, for these two prevent you from your share of the world and the Hereafter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is lazy regarding his purification and his prayer, there is no goodness in him for the matter of his Hereafter, and whoever is lazy regarding that which rectifies the matter of his livelihood, there is no goodness in him for the matter of his world.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I am hateful towards the man, or hateful for the man who becomes lazy from the matters of his world; and the one who is too lazy about the matters of his world, so he would be lazy about the matters of his Hereafter.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Salih ibn Umar, from Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not seek assistance from the lazy one, nor should you consult an incapable one.

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'When things get paired, the pairing of the laziness and the frustration, so the result which is manifested by these two, is the poverty'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) wrote to one of his companions: 'As for what follows, do not argue with the scholars, nor debate with the fools, lest the scholars hate you and the fools abuse you; and do not be lazy regarding your livelihood, lest you become a burden upon others,' or he said: 'upon your family.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Hubab al-Jallab, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who buys one hundred sheep on the condition that he exchanges them for such and such. He said: It is not permissible.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy the sheep, or a group buys the sheep, then they are brought into a house, then a man stands at the door and counts one, two, three, four, and five, then he draws the lot.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not valid. The lots are only valid if the distribution is just.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys the shares of the butchers before the share is drawn out. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not buy anything until he knows from where the share comes out. So if he buys something, he has the choice (to accept or reject it) when it comes out.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has sheep, he gives them out (for pasture) with a tribute of butter, a known amount, or known dirhams, from every sheep such and such. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with the dirhams, and I do not like it if it is with the butter.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Al Maghra, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun, who asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): He said: 'The shepherd is given the sheep in the mountain to pasture them, and for him is their wool and their milk, and he gives us dirhams for every sheep.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.' So I said: 'The people of the Masjid say it is not allowed because among them are those who have neither wool nor milk.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'And is it not that he purifies it by that? Some of it goes and some of it remains.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who handed over to a man his sheep along with butter and known dirhams, for each sheep such and such [amount] in every month. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with the dirhams, but as for the butter, I do not like that except if it is milk, so there is no problem.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Musanna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The foundling (child) is neither bought nor sold.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Musanna, from Hatim ibn Ismail al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The abandoned child is free; so if he wishes to choose a guardian other than the one who nourished him, he may do so. If the one who nourished him seeks the maintenance expenses from him, and he is affluent, he returns it to him; and if he is insolvent, whatever was spent upon him is considered charity.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: The abandoned (child) is free. So when he grows older, if he so desires, he may choose as a guardian the one who picked him up, or else let him return the expenditure to him, and let him go and choose as a guardian the one whom he so desires.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the foundling (abandoned child). He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is neither to be sold nor bought, but employ her for whatever was spent upon her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the foundling, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is free; he is neither sold nor gifted nor sold.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the child of adultery (bastard): do I buy him, or sell him, or make him serve? He said: Buy him, and enslave him, and make him serve, and sell him. But as for the foundling, do not buy him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Fazzal, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'If there is a slave girl belonging to me who was born of adultery, can I perform Hajj with her price and marry her?' He said, 'Do not perform Hajj with it, nor marry her from it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'd, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the bones of the elephant, is it permissible to sell them or buy them, from which the combs are made? He said: There is no problem. There used to be for my father a comb, or combs, from them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who had wood, so he sold it to those who make flutes from it. He said: 'There is no problem.' And (I asked him) about a man who had wood, so he sold it to the one who takes it to make crosses from it. He said: 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Muhammad ibn Mudarib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with selling the animal dung.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the leopards and the predatory birds, can one seek trade in them? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Isa al-Qummi, from Amr ibn Jarir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mulberry tree: Do we sell it if it is made into a cross and an idol? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who hires out his ship and his animal to those who carry wine and pigs in or upon them. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the monkey from being bought or sold.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abdul Momin, from Jabir, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who rents out his house, in which wine is sold. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Its rent is prohibited.'

One of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarraj, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when Muattib came to him and said, 'Two men are at the door.' He said, 'Let them in.' So they entered. One of them said, 'I am a saddler who sells tiger skins.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Are they tanned?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Qasim al-Sayqal, who said: I wrote to him: 'The scabbards of swords, which are called As-Safan, are made from fish skins; is it permissible to use them for work, given that we do not eat their flesh?' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about buying the (goods of) betrayal and the stolen (goods). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if there happens to have mixed up something else along with it. So as for the stolen (goods) exactly, so no, except if there happens to be goods of the Sultan (ruling authority), so there is no problem with it'.

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man from us who buys from the Sultan from the camels of charity and the sheep of charity, while he knows that they take from the people more than the right which is obligatory upon them. He said, so he said: 'The camels and sheep are no different than the wheat and the barley and other than that; there is no problem with it until you recognize the prohibited [part] with your own eye.' It was said to him: 'So what do you think regarding a charity collector who comes to us and takes the charities of our sheep, so we say to him, 'Sell them to us,' and he sells them to us. So what do you think regarding buying them from him?' He said: 'If he has taken them and segregated them, then there is no problem.' It was said to him: 'So what do you think regarding the wheat and the barley? The apportioner comes to us, so he apportions our share and takes his share and segregates it with a measure. So what do you think regarding buying that foodstuff from him?' He said: 'If he had taken possession of it with a measure, and you were present during that measurement, then there is no problem with buying it from him without measuring it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who buys from the office bearer, and he is an unjust one. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can buy from him for as long as he does not know that he has been unjust to anyone in it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The purchase of stolen goods and goods of betrayal is not valid when it is recognized as such.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, who said: They wanted to sell the dates of the orchard of Abu Ziyad, so I wanted to buy them. Then I said, 'I will wait until I seek the counsel of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' So I sent Mu'adh to ask him, and he said, 'Tell him to buy them, for if he does not buy them, someone else will buy them.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Nahdi, from Ibn Abi Anjarah, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever buys stolen goods while he knows, he has participated in its shame and its sin.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Abu Umar al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man in whose presence stolen goods were found, he said: He is liable (for the value) unless he produces witnesses against his seller.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about selling the juice, so it becomes wine before the price is taken possession of. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he sold its fruit to the one he knows will make it something Prohibited, there would not be a problem with that. But as for when it is juice, it should not be sold except with cash.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the price of the juice before it boils, for the one who buys it to cook with it or to make it into wine. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you sell it before it becomes wine, and it is permissible, then there is no problem.'
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazeed ibn Khalifa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) disliked selling the juice with a delay.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Sa'd, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a Christian who became a Muslim, and with him was wine and pigs, and upon him was a debt. Can he sell his wine and his pigs so he can fulfill his debt? So he said: No.

Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the juice of the grapes to the one who makes it into a Prohibited (substance). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. You can sell it as a Permissible (substance), so he makes that into a Prohibited (substance). May Allah distance him and break him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Abu Ayyub said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man ordered his slave to sell his vineyard's produce as juice, but he sold it as wine, then came to him with its price.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'The most beloved of things to me is that he should give its price in charity.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I wrote to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who has a vineyard, can he sell the grapes and the dates to one whom he knows that he will make it into wine or an intoxicant? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He sells it as permissible in the time when its drinking or eating is permissible, so there is no problem with selling it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had dirhams as a debt upon another man, so he sold wine or pigs while he (the creditor) was watching, and he paid him off. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. As for the creditor, it is permissible, and as for the seller, it is prohibited.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Mansour, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I have dirhams owed to me by a Dhim by a Dhimmi man. He sells wine and pork, and I am present. Is it permissible for me to take them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You have dirhams owed to you by him, so he pays you your dirhams.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has dirhams (a debt) owed to me, and he sells wine and pigs with them, then pays off the debt from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem,' or said: 'Take it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hanaan, from Abu Kahma, who said: A man asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the juice (of grapes), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I have a vineyard and I press it every year, and I put it in jugs, and I sell it before it boils.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. But if it boils, then its sale is not permissible.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is so; we sell our dates to those we know make wine from them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, regarding A Magian sold wine or pigs for a specified term, then he became a Muslim before the wealth became due. He (AS) said: 'For him are his dirhams.' And he (AS) said: 'If a man becomes a Muslim and he has wine and pigs, then he dies while they are in his ownership and he has a debt, his creditor or his guardian (who is not a Muslim) sells his wine and his pigs and pays off his debt.' And it is not for him to sell it while he is alive, nor to keep it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abū al-Ḥasan, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from one of our companions, from al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a Christian who became a Muslim, and with him was wine and pigs, and upon him was a debt. Can he sell his wine and his pigs and pay off his debt? He said: No.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the mortgage (collateral) and the guarantor in a credit sale, so he said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who gives an advance payment regarding the animals or the foodstuff, and he holds the security deposit as the mortgage. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; you secure your wealth from your owner.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who has a pledge (collateral) with him but does not know whose it is among the people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that he sells it until its owner comes.' I said: 'He does not know whose it it is among the people.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there excess or deficiency in it?' I said: 'If there is excess or deficiency in it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is deficiency in it, it is easier for him; he sells it and is rewarded for what is deducted from his own wealth. And if there is excess in it, it is more difficult for him; he sells it and retains the excess until its owner comes.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who pledged a security deposit for an unspecified time, then he was absent. Is there a time for him that he sells his security? He said: No, until its owner comes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the mortgage (rahn), so he (peace be upon him) said: If the mortgage is greater than the wealth of the debtor, and it is destroyed, he must pay the excess to the owner of the mortgage; and if it is less than his wealth, and the mortgage is destroyed, the owner returns to him the excess of his wealth; and if the mortgage is equal, there is nothing upon him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the mortgage security deposit, whether both parties would return the excess. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying that'. I said, 'How would they both be returning (the excess)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the mortgage was more than what was deposited with, then it was damaged, the mortgagee would return the excess to his companion; but if it was not equal, the mortgagor would return whatever was deficient from the right of the mortgagee.' He said, 'And like that was the word of Ali (peace be upon him) regarding animals and other than that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the mortgage (rahn), if it perishes in the possession of the mortgagee (murtahin) without his having destroyed it, the right returns to the mortgagor (rahin), so he takes it. But if he (the mortgagee) had destroyed it, the excess value is returned between the two of them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who takes a security deposit for a mortgage of one hundred Dirhams and it is equated to three hundred Dirhams, so it is destroyed. Is it upon the man that he returns to his companion two hundred Dirhams? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, because he took a deposit wherein was excess, and wasted it.' I said, 'Supposing half the deposit was destroyed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It would be upon the reckoning of that.' I said, 'So they would both be returning the excess?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

And by this chain, he this chain, he said, I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'If a man mortgages a slave and a house, and the affliction (loss of value) hits it, upon whom would that be?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon his master.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is your view if he kills a person (diyya is paid), upon whom would that be?' I said, 'It is in the neck of the slave.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not see that his wealth has not gone away?' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is your view if his price was one hundred Dinars, so it increased and reached two hundred Dinars, for whom would that be?' I said, 'For his master.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Like that is what would be against him, what would be for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, regarding the man who mortgages with the man a mortgage, so something hits it or it is lost. He said: He returns his wealth to him (complete).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who mortgages a slave, or a garment, or jewelry, or household goods. So the owner of the goods says to the mortgagee, 'You are free (permitted) to wear this garment, so wear the garment, benefit from the goods, and use the servant.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for him when he permits it for him, and I do not like that he does it.' I said, 'If he mortgages a house that has a yield, for whom is the yield?' He said: 'For the owner of the house.' I said, 'If he mortgages barren land, so the owner of the land says, 'Cultivate it for yourself,' ' He said: 'This is not like that. He cultivates it for himself, and it is permissible for him just as he permitted it for him, except that he cultivates it with his own wealth and improves it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding the barren land which a man holds as a mortgage, wherein there is no fruit, so he cultivates it and spends his wealth upon it, it is reckoned for him his expenditure and his work exclusively. Then he considers the share of the land, so he reckons it from the wealth with which the land was mortgaged until his wealth is fulfilled. So when his wealth is fulfilled, let him hand over the land to its owner.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who mortgaged his slave girl with a group of people. Is it permissible for him to copulate with her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Those who hold her as security would hinder between him and that.' I said, 'What is your view if he is able upon her alone?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, I do not see that as a prohibition upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who takes the beast and the camel as a pledge for his wealth. Is it permissible for him to ride it? He said: If he feeds it, then it is permissible for him to ride it, and if the one who pledged it feeds it, then it is not permissible for him to ride it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ismail ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who borrowed one hundred dinars from a man and mortgaged his jewellery for one hundred dinars. Then the man came to him and said to him, 'Lend me the gold which I have mortgaged with you as a loan (for use).' So he lent it to him, and the security got destroyed with him. Is there anything upon him for the owner of the loan regarding that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It (loss) is upon the owner of the security deposit which he had mortgaged, and he is the one who destroyed it, and there is nothing upon the wealth of this one (lender).'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you hold a mortgaged slave or an animal and he dies, so there is nothing upon you, but if the animal is damaged or the slave absconds, so you are responsible.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Riyah Al-Qalla', who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man whose brother died and left a box containing some mortgage deposits (rhuun); upon some was the name of their owner and the amount they were mortgaged for, and upon some it was not known who they were for nor the amount they were mortgaged for. So what do you see regarding this one whose owner is not recognized? He said: 'It is like its entirety.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Al-A'ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who mortgaged his slave girl to a group of people: Is it permissible for him to copulate with her? He said: 'Those who hold her as security would hinder between him and her.' I said: 'What is your view if he was able to be alone with her?' He said: 'Yes, I do not see a problem with it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man owes me some dirhams, and his house was a mortgage (pledge), so I intended to sell it.' He said, 'I seek Refuge for you with Allah that you would remove the shade from his head.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who has a debt upon another man, and with him is the mortgaged property. property; can he buy the mortgaged property from him? He said: Yes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to gather firewood, draw water, and sweep, and Fatima (peace be upon her) used to grind, knead, and bake.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdal ibn Malik, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Kahili, from Mu'adh, the seller of garments, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to milk the goat of his family.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Ibn Abi Yafur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When they differ regarding the mortgage, one of the two says, 'I mortgaged it for a thousand dirhams,' and the other says, 'For one hundred dirhams,' then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The owner of the thousand is asked for proof. If he does not have proof, the owner of the hundred swears an oath.' And if the mortgage item is less than what was mortgaged or more, and they differ, one says, 'It is a mortgage,' and the other says, 'It is a trust with you,' then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The owner of the trust is asked for proof. If he does not have proof, the owner of the mortgage swears an oath.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who mortgages something with his companion, and there is no proof between them regarding it. The one holding the mortgage claimed it was for a thousand, and the owner of the mortgage said, 'It is only for one hundred.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The burden of proof is upon the one holding the mortgage that it is for a thousand; and if he does not have proof, then the oath is upon the mortgagor.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who said to another man, 'A thousand dirhams are owed by you to me.' The man said, 'No, but it is an entrustment (deposit).' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The word is the word of the owner of the wealth, along with his oath.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheyb who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about some goods in the hands of two men. One of the two is saying, 'I had entrusted it to you', and the other is saying, 'It is a mortgaged item'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The (final) word is the word of those who is saying, 'It is a mortgaged item with me', unless if the one who claims that he had entrusted it were to come with witnesses'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The owner of the deposit and the owner of the merchandise are both entrusted (liable only for negligence). And he (peace be upon him) said: When the borrowed item perishes with the borrower, he is not liable (for compensation) unless a condition was stipulated upon him. And he (peace be upon him) said in another Hadith: When he is a just Muslim, there is no liability upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no liability (guarantee) for the borrowed item (ariyyah) except if one has stipulated a guarantee for it, except for the dinars, for they are guaranteed even if no guarantee was stipulated for them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the borrowed item (for use) under guarantee?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'For all that you borrow, if it is damaged, you are not liable for its damage except for gold and silver, for these two are liable (for damage) unless it is stipulated that whenever they are damaged, their damage is not liable upon you; and similarly, for all that you borrow, if it is stipulated upon you, it is liable upon you; and gold and silver are liable upon you even if it is not stipulated upon you.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al- from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, [from Muhammad], from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the borrowed item (ariyyah) which a person borrows, so it perishes or is stolen, so he said: 'If he was trustworthy (amin), then there is no liability (ghurm) upon him.' He said, 'And I asked him about the one who manages the capital (istabdi'u) so it perishes or is stolen, is there a guarantee upon its owner?' So he said: 'There is no liability upon him after it turns out that the man was trustworthy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the borrowed item, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no liability upon the borrower for the borrowed item when it perishes, if he was trustworthy'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who borrowed a garment, then he took it and mortgaged it. Then the owners of the goods came to their goods. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They take their goods.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the entrustment of gold and silver. He said: 'Everything that is from the entrustments and is not under guarantee, (its liability) does not become obligatory.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who entrusted a man with a thousand dirhams, so it was lost. So the man said, 'It was an entrustment (wadi'ah) with me,' and the other one said, 'It was merely a loan (qard) upon you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth remains obligated for him (the borrower) unless he establishes the proof that it was an entrustment.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man handed over an entrustment to another man, so he placed it in the house of his neighbour, and it got lost. So is it obligated upon him if he opposed his instruction and took it out from his own property? So he (peace be upon him) signed: He is responsible for it, Allah willing.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Najran from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent to Safwan ibn Umayyah and borrowed from him seventy coats of mail with their neckpieces. He asked, 'Is it forcibly, O Muhammad?' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) replied, 'No, it is a loan with guarantee.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the bleacher who spoils. He said: 'Every hired person who is given a wage on the condition that he repairs [the work], and he spoils it, then he is liable [for the loss].'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the washerman and the dyer, if something is stolen from them, and it does not become clear with definite evidence that they stole it, whether it is a small or large amount, if they present evidence, there is no liability on them; but if they do not present evidence and claim that the item which was claimed against them has been lost/stolen, they are liable (guaranteed) if they do not have evidence to support their claim.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a bleacher to whom I had handed over a garment, and he claimed that it had been stolen from among his goods. He said: 'So upon him is that he establishes proof that it was stolen from among his goods, and there is nothing upon him. And if all his goods were stolen, there is nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the bleacher (or tailor) to whom a garment is submitted, with a stipulation upon him that he returns it at a specified time. He (peace be upon him) said: If he delays beyond the time and the garment is lost after the specified time, then he is liable (guarantor).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abi al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the garment that one hands over to the fuller (bleacher), and he burns it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is liable (for the loss), for you only handed it over to him to repair it, and did not hand it over to him to spoil it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought to him a man who had hired a man to repair his door, and he struck the door of his house, and he struck the nail and the door cracked, so Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) held him liable.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the bleacher and the jeweller, are they liable? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The people would not be straightened unless they are made to be liable.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Yunus used to work by it and seize (by it – holding people liable)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a case of a man who had hired another man to mend his door; the hired man drove a nail and the door cracked, so Amir al-Mu'minin held him liable.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Isma'il ibn Marrar from Yunus who said: I asked al-Rida' (peace be upon him) about the tailor and the jeweler, are they liable (for defects)? He said, 'People do not behave well unless they are held liable.' He said, 'And Yunus would act according to this and accept (liability).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who hired a cameleer's camels and sent oil with him to a land, so he claimed that some of the oil skins broke and he spilled what was inside them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he wishes, he takes the oil,' and he said: 'He claims it broke, but he is not believed except with a just proof.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sailor: I carry food with him, then I take possession of it from him, and it is deficient. So he (peace be upon him) said: If he is trustworthy, then do not hold him liable.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who carried foodstuff with another man in a ship, and it was deficient, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is liable.' I said, 'Perhaps it increased.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know that it increased by anything?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who hired a ship from a sailor, so he loaded it with foodstuff, and he stipulated upon him that if the foodstuff was deficient, it would be upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is allowed.' I said to him (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes the foodstuff is excessive.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Does the sailor claim that something had increased in it?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The excess is for the owner of the foodstuff, and the deficiency is upon him when there was a stipulation upon him for that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, who said: My father carried goods to Syria with a cameleer, and mentioned that one load from it was lost. So I mentioned that to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Did you accuse him?' I said: 'No'. He said: 'So do not hold him liable (guarantee the loss).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the cameleer who breaks what he carries or spills it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is trustworthy, there is nothing upon him, but if he is not trustworthy, he is liable.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The hired associate is liable (for loss/damage) except from a predator, or from drowning, or burning, or an arrogant thief.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt of one hundred dirhams by number upon him, so he paid me one hundred dirhams by weight. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, provided there was no stipulation.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Usury arises from the stipulations; it is the stipulations that spoil it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man has some clear dirhams with me. He meets me and says to me, He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you have checked the price for him on that day, then there is no problem with that.' I said: 'I did not weigh it and did not cash it, but rather it was a speech between me and him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that the dirhams were with you and the dinars were with you?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So there is no problem with that.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba al-Hashimi, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who has dinars for one of his associates, so he takes silver dirhams in their place for his needs. On the day he took possession, the rate was seven and seven and a half dirhams per dinar. The owner of the wealth might seek some of the silver, but it is not present, so he buys it for him from the money-changer at this price or similar. Then the price changes before they account for it, until the silver becomes twelve dirhams per dinar. Is that permissible for him, given that when he took possession, the rate was seven and seven and a half per dinar? He (peace be upon him) said: When the silver is handed over to him in accordance with the dinars, the fluctuation in exchange rates does not harm him, and there is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who has Dinars upon him. He said: There is no problem if he takes their value in Dirhams.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had Dinars owed to him by another man, so he assigned another man in place of the debtor for the Dinars. Can he take them as Dirhams at the current exchange rate? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he desires.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who sells me silver (dirhams) for gold (dinars), and I weigh from it and weigh for him until I finish, and there is no transaction between me and him except that in his silver there are weak (coins), counterfeit ones, and what is not permissible, so he says, 'Check them and return the weak ones.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it, but do not delay that for more than one day or two days, for it is essentially exchange (sarf). I said, 'And if I find in his silver an excess equal to the amount of the weak (coins) in it?' He said: 'This is precaution (ihtiyat); this is more beloved to me (peace be upon him).'
Safwan from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'The dirhams for the dirhams and the lead?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The lead is invalid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked him about currency exchange (as-sarf). I said to him: 'The caravan/group sometimes hurries and departs, so we are unable to obtain the Damascus dirhams and the Basran dirhams, and instead it is permissible with a Sabur [a specific weight/measure] of the Damascus and Basran [coins].' He said: 'And what is the Rifqa (caravan/group)?' I said: 'The people associate with one another and gather for departure. So when they hurry, and sometimes we are unable to obtain the Damascus and Basran [dirhams], we send with the proceeds [proceeds of sale], and they exchange one thousand and fifty dirhams from it with one thousand from the Damascus and Basran [dirhams].' He said: 'There is no goodness in this. Why do you not place gold in it due to its increase [in value/weight]?' I said to him: 'Can I buy one thousand dirhams and one dinar with two thousand dirhams?' He said: 'There is no problem with that. Indeed, my father (peace be upon him) used to be more accommodating with the people of Medina than I was, and he used to say this. So they would say: 'This is merely fleeing [from the strict rule]. If a man came with one dinar, he would not be given one thousand dirhams, and if he came with one thousand dirhams, he would not be given one thousand dinars.' And he used to say to them: 'Excellent is the fleeing from the forbidden to the permissible.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir used to say to my father, 'O Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on you! By Allah, we know that if you took a dinar and the exchange rate was eighteen, and you went around Medina seeking someone who would give you twenty, you would not find him. And what is this except fleeing?' And my father used to say, 'You speak the truth, by Allah, but it is fleeing from falsehood to truth.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who exchanges the Kufiyya coin for the Shamiyya coin, weight for weight. The money-changer says, 'I will not exchange for you until you exchange for me a Yusufiyya for a Ghillah, weight for weight.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' We said, 'Indeed, the money-changer only sought the surplus of the Yusufiyya over the Ghillah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who has some dirhams for me, so I go to him and say, 'Exchange them for dinars without me taking possession of anything.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' I said, 'There are dinars for me, so I go to him and say, 'Exchange them for me into dirhams and keep them established with you,' and I do not take anything from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who purchased from a man with a dinar, so he took half as goods and half as silver (dirhams). He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' And I asked him: 'Is it permissible that he takes half as silver or goods, and leaves the other half until he comes later and takes it as silver or goods?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that he leaves anything from it until he takes it all, so he should not do it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who brings me silver (dirhams), so I buy it from him with dinars (gold coins). I occupy myself with checking its weight, evaluating it, and the excess between me and him in it, so I give him the dinars and say to him: 'It is not a sale between me and you, for I have cancelled the sale between us. Your silver with me is a loan, and my dinars with you are a loan, until you come to me tomorrow and I will sell it to you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'
