Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the lead (dirhams) bought with the silver (dirhams), he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the lead was predominant upon it, so there is no problem with it'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt owed to me, and he pays part in dinars and part in dirhams. When he comes to settle the account with me to fulfill the obligation, but the price/rate of the dinars has changed, should I calculate for him the rate that existed on the day he gave me the dinars, or the rate of the day on which I settle with him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The rate of the day he gave you the dinars, because you withheld their benefit/profit from him.'

Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me with silver (dirhams) to sell to me, wanting by it the silver that I have. It is certain that he does not want the dinars, he wants only the silver, and he does not rise until he takes my silver. So I buy the dirhams for him with the dinars, and his dinars are not with me complete, so I borrow from him from my neighbor, and I give it to him to complete his dinars, and perhaps I do not secure its weight. He said: Does he not take the full amount of what is for him? I said: Yes. He said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father bought a piece of land and stipulated upon its owner that he would give him silver (dirhams), every dinar for ten dirhams.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Abu Al-Magra, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I go to the money-changer with dirhams and buy dinars from him, and he weighs for me more than my due right. Then I buy from him, in exchange for those dinars, dirhams.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it, but do not weigh less than your due right.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who says to the jeweller, 'Make this ring for me, and I will exchange for you a fresh dirham for a worn dirham.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about buying gold that contains silver, mercury, and dirt, with dinars and dirhams. He said: 'Do not exchange it except with dirhams.' He said: 'And I asked him about buying silver that contains lead and dirhams; when it is pure, it is deficient by two or three dirhams from every ten. He said: 'It is not valid except with gold.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdullah, the slave of Abd Rabbih, wholed of Abd Rabbih, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the gemstone which is extracted from the mine, and in it are gold, silver, and brass all together, how do we buy it? So he (peace be upon him) said: You buy it with the gold and the silver entirely.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarquqi, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the ornamented sword for cash, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about selling it on credit, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the cash is equal to what is in its silver, then there is no problem with it, or let him give the foodstuff (as barter).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Ali ibn Maymoun al-Sa'ig, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about what is swept from the dirt, which I sell, so what shall I do with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it in charity, for either it is yours or it is for its rightful one.' I said, 'Supposing therein is gold and silver and iron, so for which thing shall I sell it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Sell it with foodstuff.' I said, 'Supposing there are relatives for him who are needy, can I give it to them from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad, who said: He was asked about the ornamented sword and the iron sword that is gilded, can it be sold for dirhams? He said: Yes, and with gold. And he said: It is disliked to sell it on credit (with delay). And he said: If the price is more than the silver (value of the decoration), there is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Hamza, from Ibrahim ibn Hilal, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A goblet containing gold and silver, can I buy it with gold or silver?' He said: 'If you are able to purify it, then no (do not buy), and if you are not able to purify it, then there is no problem (you may buy).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I said to him (peace be upon him), 'Dirhams come to me with some surplus (remainder), so we buy it with the money (coins).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible, but look at the surplus between the two, weigh the brass (or base metal) and weigh the surplus, so place it with the good dirhams, and take weight by weight.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya or someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the substance of al-usrub (a type of silver coin), and when it was pure it contained silver. Is it permissible for a man to pay an advance sum of named dirhams for it? He said: If the dominant name upon it is al-usrub, then there is no problem with that, meaning it is not recognized except by the name al-usrub.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the ornamented swords in which there is silver, can they be sold for gold to a specified term? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The people did not differ regarding the credit (sale on deferred payment) that it is usury (riba). They only differed regarding 'hand to hand' (cash) transactions.' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'So can it be sold for dirhams in cash?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: It is more beloved to me if there is something else (a commodity) along with it.' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'When the dirhams given are more than the silver contained in the sword?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And how is the precaution for them with that?' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'Because they claim that they recognize that (the value difference).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they recognize that, then there is no problem; otherwise, it is more beloved to me if they include something else (a commodity) along with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man has dirhams (silver coins) as a debt upon him for me, so he gives me kohl (eye cosmetic).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Silver is exchanged for silver, and whatever is from kohl is a debt upon him until he returns it to you on the Day of Resurrection.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'A man should not buy silver with gold except hand-to-hand, nor buy gold with silver except hand-to-hand.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who buys dirhams from another man with dinars, so he weighs them, pays them off, and calculates their price to see how many dinars they are. Then he says, 'Send your slave with me so that I may give him the dinars.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that he separates from him until he takes the dinars.' I said, 'But he is in a house alone, and their places are close to one another, and this is burdensome for them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he finishes weighing them and paying them off, let him instruct the slave whom he sends to be the one who conducts the transaction with him, and he should hand over the silver to him and take possession of the dinars from him at the place where he hands over the silver to him.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about selling gold for dirhams, so he said: Send a messenger so he would fulfill its price for you, and he should be saying, 'Give and take', and your messenger would happen to be with him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the disbursement of the Dirhams coated over. So he said: 'When it was such that the silver overwhelmed upon it, so there is no problem'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Jameel, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a group of people from the inhabitants of Sijistan entered upon him and asked him about the dirhams that were coated over. He said: 'There is no problem with it, provided it was a license (or permitted) in the city.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Fadl Abu al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dirhams that are carried (as currency). He said: 'If you spend what is permissible among the people of the city, there is no problem; and if you spend what is not permissible among the people of the city, then there is [a problem].'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who lent a man dirhams, so he returned to him better ones from them with his own goodwill, and the borrower and the lender knew that he had only lent them so that better ones would be given back from them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem when the borrower agreed himself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who lends another man impure dirhams, and takes from him fresh dirhams, which please him. He said: 'There is no problem,' and mentioned that this is from Ali (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would have a two-year-old camel as a debt, so he would give back the four-year-old one.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who borrows dirhams from a man and returns the misqal (a unit of weight/value), or he borrows the misqal and returns the dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is no stipulation, there is no problem, and that is the excess (fadl). Indeed, my father, may Allah have mercy on him, used to borrow inferior dirhams and would return to him superior dirhams. He said to me: O my son, return them to the one from whom I borrowed them. So I would say: O father, his dirhams were inferior, and these are better than them. So he would say: O my son, this is the excess, so give it to him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a basket of unripened dates as a debt upon him, so he takes from him a basket of fresh dates, and these are fewer than those. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' I said: 'Suppose there is for me a basket of unripened dates as a debt upon him, so I take from him a basket of ripe dates, and these are more than those?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, if it is well-known between you two.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others, said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who borrows a loan from another man and gives him a pledge, whether a servant, or a utensil, or clothes. So he (the lender) needs something from its benefit, so he seeks permission from the borrower to use it, and the borrower permits him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is pleased with it, there is no problem.' I said: 'Those among us narrate that every loan that brings a benefit is invalid.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not the case that the best of loans is that which brings a benefit?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the loan which attracts benefit, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of loans is that which attracts benefit.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Bishr ibn Maslama, and others, from the one who informed them, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The best loan is that which attracts benefit.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to me, so I buy goods for him from the people and guarantee payment on his behalf. Then he comes to me with the dirhams, so I take them and withhold them from their owner, and I take the good-quality dirhams and give the inferior ones in their place. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he guarantees payment, perhaps the burden becomes heavy upon him, so he hurries to pay before I ask for it, and he withholds [payment] after receiving [the goods]; there is no objection to this.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, in the wisdom of the progeny of Dawud (peace be upon him): It is befitting for the intellectual Muslim that he is not seen traveling/moving except for three [purposes]: restoration of his livelihood, or provision for his Hereafter, or pleasure in that which is not forbidden. And it is befitting for the intellectual Muslim that he has an hour in which he devotes himself to his affairs between himself and Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and an hour in which he meets his brethren, with whom he exchanges advice and they exchange advice with him regarding the matters of their Hereafter; and an hour in which he leaves his soul and its pleasures in that which is not forbidden, for indeed these are an aid upon those two hours.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rabi', from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The perfection, every perfection is in three (matters), and he mentioned regarding the third, being the management of the livelihood.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah and others, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The correction/management of wealth is from faith.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) measuring dates with his hand. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! If you could have ordered one of your sons, or one of your slaves, so they would have sufficed for you.' So he said: 'O Dawud! It is not correct for the Muslim person except three: understanding in the Religion, and patience upon the calamity, and good management regarding the livelihood.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Zarih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, intends goodness for a family, He sustains them with leniency in their livelihood.

From him, from Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Salih ibn Hamza, from one of our companions who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon you to correct/manage the wealth, for therein is a stimulant for the benevolent and a self-sufficiency from the wicked ones'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man gives another man silver (dirhams) as a loan, on the condition that he repays it to him in another land, and makes this a condition upon him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with a man taking dirhams in Mecca and writing for them bills of exchange (safatij) to be paid in Kufa.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who sends money to a land, the one whom he wants to send it with says, 'Lend it to me, and I will pay you back when you arrive in the land.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That they both disliked sailing the sea for trade.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'What is more excellent in seeking (livelihood) is the one who sails the sea for business.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, who said: I had carried merchandise to Mecca, but losses occurred upon it, so I entered the city with it to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I carried merchandise that incurred losses upon me, and I have resolved to travel to Egypt, so shall I travel by land or by sea?' He said, 'Egypt is the place of death; shortest-lived people are destined for it.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'How beautiful is the seeking for one who sails the sea.' Then he said to me, 'It is not against you if you go to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), pray two cycles there, and ask Allah for guidance (Istikhara) a hundred times. Whatever is resolved for you, act upon it.' So if you ride by land, say: 'All praise is for Allah Who made this subservient to us, and we were not able to do it, and surely to our Lord we must return.' And if you sail the sea, when you are in the ship, say: 'In the Name of Allah, its course and its anchorage. Surely my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.' So if the waves heave upon you, lean on your left side and gesture towards the wave with your right hand, and say: 'Settle me with the settling of Allah, and be tranquil with the tranquility of Allah, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent.' Ali ibn Asbaat said, 'So I sailed the sea, and whenever the wave rose, I would say what he had said, and it would subside as if it had not been.' Ali ibn Asbaat said, 'And I asked him, saying, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the tranquility (Sakinah)?' He said, 'A wind from Paradise, having a face like the face of a human, more fragrant than musk. And it is that which Allah sent down upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at Hunayn, so the polytheists were defeated.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding sailing the sea for trade, the man is deceived in his religion.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from one of his companions, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'From the good fortune of a person is that his business is in his own city, and his companions are righteous, and he has children by whom he can seek assistance.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Taymi, from Ja'far ibn Bakr, from Abdullah ibn Abi Sahl, from Abdullah ibn Abdul Kareem, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three [things] are from the good fortune: the obedient wife, and the righteous children, and the man who is granted his livelihood in his own city, going out to his family in the morning and returning in the evening.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: From the good fortune of a person is that his business is in his own city, and his companions are righteous, and he has children whom he can seek assistance from; and from the misery of a person is that he has a wife with whom he is fascinated, yet she betrays him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding two men who shared in wealth, profited from it, and where there was a debt against the wealth and a debt upon both of them; one said to his partner, 'Give me the capital, and for you is the profit, and upon you is the charge.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it if they stipulate it. If the stipulation opposes the Book of Allah, then it is returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said: Regarding two men, for each of them there was food with his companion, and each of them did not know how much was for him with his companion. So each one of them said to his companion, 'For you is what is with you, and for me is what is with me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that if they are both pleased and their souls are content.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who has a debt upon another man, so he says to him before the term becomes due: 'Expedite for me half of my right, on condition that I remit the other half from you.' Is that permissible for one of them? He said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who has a debt due at a specified term, so his creditor comes to him and says, 'Pay me such and such an amount, and I shall write off the remainder for you,' or 'Pay me part of it, and I shall extend the term for what remains upon you.' He said: 'I do not see any problem with it, for it does not increase upon the principal of his wealth.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says: 'Then you shall have your principal; neither shall you deal unjustly nor will you be dealt with unjustly.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Reconciliation is permissible between the people.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A Jew or a Christian had four thousand dirhams in my possession, and he died. Is it permissible for me to reconcile with his heirs without informing them of the exact amount?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until you inform them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazeed who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who guaranteed for another man with a guarantee, then reconciled upon it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not entitled to anything except that which he had reconciled upon.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn 'Uzafir, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a man has a debt upon another man, and the creditor delays (the debtor) until he (the creditor) dies, then the debtor reconciles with his inheritors upon something (a reduced amount), so that which the inheritors take is for them, and whatever remains is for the deceased until he is fulfilled from it in the Hereafter; and if he does not reconcile with them upon anything until he dies, and does not pay it off, then all of it is for the deceased to seize him (the debtor) with (in the Hereafter).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Atiyya, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chose for His prophets farming and agriculture, so that they might not dislike anything from the drops of the sky.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah made the sustenance of His Prophets in the crops and the udders, lest they dislike anything from the drops of the sky.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Umara, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Adam was descended to the earth, he needed food and drink, so he complained of that to Jibraeel (peace be upon him). Jibraeel said to him: 'O Adam, become a farmer.' He said: 'So teach me a supplication.' He said: 'Say: O Allah, suffice me with the provisions of the world and every horror before Paradise, and clothe me with health until livelihood becomes welcoming to me.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of our companions who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: The best of deeds is farming, which you cultivate, so the righteous and the immoral eat from it. As for the righteous, whatever he eats from it, it seeks forgiveness for you; and as for the immoral, whatever he eats from it, it curses him; and the beasts and birds eat from it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim, from Yazeed ibn Harun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The farmers are the treasures of the creatures; they cultivate goodness which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will be the best of people in standing position and the closest in status, and they will be called 'the Blessed ones'.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Salih ibn Ali ibn Atiyya, from a man he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by a group of the Ansar while they were plowing, so he said to them: 'Plow, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah causes growth by the wind as He causes growth by the rain.' He said: 'So they plowed, and their crops grew abundantly.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sadeyr, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Children of Israel came to Musa (peace be upon him) and asked him to ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to send rain from the sky upon them whenever they wished, and to withhold it whenever they wished. So he asked Allah for that for them, and Allah said: "That is for them, O Musa." So Musa informed them, and they plowed and did not leave anything except that they sowed it.' Then they caused the rain to descend according to their will and withheld it according to their will, so their crops became like mountains and thickets. Then they harvested, trod, and winnowed, but they found nothing. So they raised a clamor to Musa (peace be upon him) and said: 'We only asked you to ask Allah to send rain upon us whenever we wished, so He answered us, but then He made it harmful to us.' So he said: 'O Lord, the Children of Israel are raising a clamor over what You have done with them.' He said: 'And why is that, O Musa?' He said: 'They asked me to ask You to send rain whenever they wished and withhold it whenever they wished, so You answered them, but then You made it harmful to them.' He said: 'O Musa, I was the One who decreed for the Children of Israel, but they were not pleased with My decree, so I left it to their will, and it turned out to be what you saw.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you intend to plant crops, take a handful of seeds, face the Qiblah, and say: 'Have you considered what you cultivate? Is it you who cause it to grow, or are We the Causers of its growth?' three times. Then say: 'But Allah is the Grower' three times. Then say: 'O Allah, make it blessed grain and grant us safety in it.' Then scatter the handful in your hand onto the clear ground.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Jallab, from al-Hudhayni, from Ibn Arafat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wants to pollinate the palm tree, when it was such that it would not bear (fruit) nor irrigate, so let him take two small dried fish, and let him grind these between the two grinding plates. Then he should sow a little of it in every sprout from it, and he should keep the remainder in a clean bundle, then make it to be in the heart (centre) of the palm tree. He would benefit, Allah (Exalted is He) Willing'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I saw your garden, so have you planted anything in it afterwards?' I said, 'I intended to take stems from your garden (and plant these)'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I inform you with what is better for you than it and quicker?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When dates ripen and you are about to pick them as fresh dates, plant them, it (the crop) will produce just like what you planted. So I did that and it grew as the same like it'.

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said, He (peace be upon him) said: Whenever you plant a tree or vegetation, so recite upon every twig or seed, 'Glorious is the Resurrector, the Inheritor', so it would almost never be wrong, Allah Willing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from one of the two (peace be upon them) who said: You should say, whenever you plant or sow, The parable of a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky. It yields its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about cutting the lote tree, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from your companions asked me about it, so I wrote to him: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had cut a lote tree and planted grapes in its place.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: It is disliked to cut the palm tree. And he was asked about cutting the tree, so he said: 'There is no problem.' I said, 'So what about the lote tree (sidr)?' He said: 'There is no problem with it. Rather, it is disliked to cut the lote tree in the wilderness because it is scarce there, and as for here, then it is not disliked.'

From Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Basheer, from Ibn Muzarib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not cut down the fruit-bearing trees, for Allah would Send upon you a difficult Punishment.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Do not rent out the land with wheat, nor with barley, nor with dates, nor with the canal, nor with the sprouts (of water), but with gold and silver, because gold and silver are guaranteed, and these are not with a guarantee.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Do not rent out the land with dates, nor with wheat, nor with barley, nor with the canal (water channel), nor with the sprouts (water remnants). I said, 'And what are the canals?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The drinking spots (water channels), and the sprouts are the remnants of the water, but accept it with gold, and silver, and the half (share), and the third, and the quarter.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not rent out the land for wheat, then cultivate it with wheat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Bureyd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who accepts (rent for) the land with dinars or with dirhams, he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has land upon which is a known tax (kharaj), which sometimes increases and sometimes decreases, so he hands it over to a man on the condition that he pays its tax and gives him two hundred dirhams in the year. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about renting out land in exchange for food, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is from the food of that very land, then there is no goodness in it.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who rented land from another man, so he said, 'Its rent is such and such, on the condition that I cultivate it. If I do not cultivate it, I will give you that.' So he did not cultivate it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He may take it if he wishes to leave it (uncultivated), and if he wishes not to leave it (uncultivated), he may not take it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Al-Washa', who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who buys from a man a dry, known land for one hundred kurrs, on the condition that he gives him the produce from the land. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is prohibited.' I said to him: 'What do you say, may Allah make me your ransom, if he buys from him the land with a known measure and wheat from other than it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Ahmad, son of Muhammad, from Muhammad, son of Sahl, from his father, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man for whom the farmer cultivates saffron, and guarantees to give him, for every jarib of land that is tilled, a weight of such and such dirhams. So sometimes it is deficient and he incurs a loss, and sometimes it is excessive and increases. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it if they are both pleased (with the arrangement).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Al-Sabbah, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) conquered Khaybar, he left it in their hands upon a stipulation of half. So when the fruit reached maturity, he sent Abdullah ibn Rawahah to them, who evaluated it for them. So they came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, He has increased (the estimation) upon us. So he sent a message to Abdullah, and he said: 'What are they saying?' He said, 'I had evaluated upon them with something, so if they so desire to they can take with what we have evaluated, and if they so desire to, we take it'. So a man from the Jews said, 'By this (justice) stand the skies and the earth'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not guarantee the land with a specified quantity of wheat, but (guarantee it) with half, a third, a quarter, and a fifth; there is no problem with it. And he said: There is no problem with sharing the crops (muzara'ah) with a third, a quarter, and a fifth.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, that he said: Regarding the man who cultivates on a sharing basis, so he farms someone else’s land, saying, 'A third is for the oxen, and a third for the sowing, and a third for the land.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not mention anything from the seeds, and the cows, but he should be saying, 'Cultivate such and such therein, if you so desire to, for a half, and if you so desire to, for a third'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who cultivates another's land, so he stipulates upon him a third for the sowing seeds, and a third for the oxen (ploughing). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting that he mentions sowing, nor oxen, for the speech makes it Prohibited.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who cultivates the land, so he stipulated a third for the sowing and a third for the oxen. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting that he mentions anything, for the speech makes it prohibited.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I partner with the non-Muslim (Al-Ilj) such that the land, the seed, and the oxen are from me, and the oversight, irrigation, and labor in the crop until it becomes wheat and barley are upon the non-Muslim. Then the distribution occurs, so the Sultan takes his right, and what remains remains on the stipulation that for the non-Muslim is one-third of it, and for me is the remainder.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with that.' I said, 'So would it be for me if he were to return to me from what the land produced the seed, and the remainder be divided?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Rather, you partnered with him on the stipulation that the seed is from you, and upon him is the irrigation and the oversight.'

Muhammad ibn ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has land from the tax-land, and he hands it over to another man on the condition that he cultivates it, improves it, and pays its tax, and whatever surplus there is, it is shared between them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who gives his land to another man, and therein are pomegranates, or palm trees, or fruit, so he says: 'Irrigate this with the water and cultivate it, and for you is half of what is produced.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who gives the land to another man, so he says: 'Cultivate it and it is for you for three years, or five years, or whatever Allah wills.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about al-muzāraʿah (sharecropping), so he said: 'The expenditure is for you, and the land is for its owner. So whatever Allah brings out from it of anything, it is divided upon the half. And thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) give the people of Khaybar when they came to him, so he gave it to them on the condition that they cultivate it, and for them is half of what it produces.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Al-Qabalah (leasing) is that you come to the barren land, so you accept it from its owners for twenty years, or less than that or more, so you cultivate it and pay what is due upon it, so there is no problem with it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the crop-sharing (muzara'ah) of the Muslim with the Polytheist, where the seeds and oxen are from the Muslim, and the land, water, tax, and labor are upon the Polytheist. He said: There is no problem with it. He said: And I asked him about the crop-sharing. I said: A man sows in the land a hundred Jarib or less or more, of food or something else. Then a man comes to him and says: Take from me half the price of this seed which you have sown in the land, and half of your expenditure upon me, and partner me in it. He said: There is no problem. I said: And if the one who sows in it had not bought it with a price, and rather it is something that was with him? He said: So let him evaluate it at a price as it is sold on that day, so let him take half the price and half the expenditure and partner him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The toiler upon his family is like the combatant in the Way of Allah.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The one who seeks from the Grace of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what suffices his dependents, is greater in reward than the combatant in the Way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If the man is insolvent (in debt), so he works with whatever he has provided for himself and his family but does not seek the Prohibited, so he is like the combatant in the Way of Allah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a great town, and in it were Dhimmi dependents. The Sultan would take the Jizyah from them, and he would give them [the collected amount]. From one of them, fifty would be taken, and from some of them, thirty, and less and more. So the owner of the town would make a settlement with the Sultan on their behalf, then he would take from them more than what he gave to the Sultan. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is prohibited.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī said: Abu Najīh al-Mismāʿī narrated to me from al-Fayḍ ibn al-Mukhtār. I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! What do you say regarding a land I lease from the Sultan, then I rent it out to my lessees upon a stipulation that whatever Allah brings out from it of anything, the half and the third of that is for me, after the right of the Sultan?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. That is how I deal with my lessees.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with leasing the land from its owner for twenty years, and less than that and more. So he cultivates it and pays whatever taxes are upon it, and he does not include the non-Muslims (Ahl al-Zimma) in anything from the lease, because it is not permissible.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the man who takes possession of the land with the goodwill/agreement of its owners, upon a condition he stipulated by him with them, and if he repairs in it a repair or renews in it a building, then for him is the rent/profit of its houses, except that which was in the hands of its farmers beforehand. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he has entered into the lease of the land upon a known matter, then he should not deal with what is in the hands of its farmers, unless he had stipulated with the owners of the land regarding what is in the hands of the farmers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a town belonging to some people of the Ahl al-Zimma (people of the covenant). I do not know if its origin (ownership) was theirs or not, other than that it was in their hands and upon them was the land tax (kharaj). So the Sultan (ruling authority) exceeded upon them, and they sought me out, so they gave me their land and their town on the condition that I would suffice them against the Sultan with whatever amount (of tax), whether little or much. So the excess would be for me after that, a remainder after what the Sultan takes whatever he takes. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that; for you is whatever was from the excess.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, from Yunus, who said: I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who leased land or other property from a man for a specified number of years. Then the lessor wanted to sell his land which he had leased out before the expiration of the specified term. Is it for the lessee to prevent him from the sale before the expiration of the term for which he leased it from him to him, and what is obligated for the lessee for it? He (peace be upon him) wrote to him: He may sell if he stipulates upon the buyer that for the lessee would be from the years what was (contracted) for him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani and Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim al-Hamadani, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and asked him about a woman who rented out her property for ten years, on the condition that she would be given the rent at the end of each year, and nothing of the rent would be advanced to her unless the time had passed. She died three years before or after that time. Is it obligatory upon her heirs to enforce the lease until the time, or does the lease become terminated by the death of the woman? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'If there was a specified time for her which had not yet reached and she died, then that lease is for her heirs. If that time had not yet reached, and a third of it had, or half of it, or something from it, then her heirs would be given in accordance with whatever had reached from that time, God willing.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Razi who said: A man wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third: A man leased a property from a man, so the lessor sold that property which he had leased out in the presence of the lessee, and the lessee did not deny the sale, and he was present for it, a witness upon it. So the buyer died, and for him were inheritors, can they retract that in the inheritance or would it remain in the hand of the lessee up to the expiration of his term? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Up to the expiration of his term.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid bin Jareer, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man who leases the land from the farmers, so he sub-leases it out with more than what he had leased it with, and he undertakes therein the share of the Sultan (ruling authority). He said: There is no problem with it. The land is not like the employee, nor like the house. The excess of the employee’s wages and the house is prohibited.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who leased from the Sultan (ruling authority) from the government land (ard al-kharaj) for a specified amount of Dirhams, or for a specified amount of foodstuff. Then he sub-leased it and stipulated upon the one who cultivated it that he would distribute half, or less than that or more, and for him in the land after that would be the excess. Is that correct for him? He said: Yes, when he digs out a river for them or does some work for them to assist them with that, so that would be for him. He said: And I asked him about the man who leases a land from the government land for a specified amount of Dirhams, or with a known amount of foodstuff, so he sub-leases it piece by piece, or a Jareyba by a Jareyba, with a specified thing. So there happened to be some excess for him regarding what he had leased from the Sultan, and he had not spent anything upon it. Or he leases out that land in pieces upon a stipulation that he would give them the seeds and the expenditure. So there happens to be some excess for him regarding that, upon his lessees, and would there be for him the fertility of the land or would it not be for him? He said: Whenever you lease a land, so you spend something therein, or do some repair work in it, so there is no problem with what you have mentioned.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al Maghra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who leases a land, then sub-leases it for more than what he leased it for, he said: There is no problem. This is not like the shop (hanut) nor the employee (ajir). Indeed, the excess of the employee and the shop is prohibited.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man rents a house for ten dirhams, dwells in two-thirds of it, and rents out the remaining third for ten dirhams, there is no problem with it. He should not rent it out for more than what he rented it for, unless he makes an improvement in it.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdul Kareem from Al-Halby who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I lease the land for a third or a quarter, so I sub-lease it for half.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'Suppose I lease it for a thousand dirhams and sub-lease it for two thousand?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is not allowed.' I said, 'How did the first become allowed and the second not allowed?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Because this is guaranteed, and that is not guaranteed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: When you lease land for gold or silver, do not sub-lease it for more than what you leased it for; and if you leased it for half or a third of the produce, you may sub-lease it for more than what you leased it for, because gold and silver are guaranteed (liable for loss).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who leases a house, then sub-leases it for more than what he leased it for. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not correct unless he makes an improvement in it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that I rent a single millstone, then I hire it out for more than what I had hired it for, unless something new is introduced in it, or a loss is incurred in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zurara ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a pasture to graze in for fifty dirhams, or less or more, so he intended to include with him anyone who would graze in it and take the price from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him include with him whoever he wishes for part of what he gave, and even if he includes with him forty-nine [sheep], and his own sheep is one dirham, there is no problem.' And if he grazed in it before he lets them in, for a month or two months or more than that, after making it clear to them, there is no problem. And it is not for him to sell it for fifty dirhams and graze with them, nor for more than fifty and not graze with them, unless he has done work in the pasture, such as digging a well or cutting a canal, or he exerted himself in it with the consent of the owners of the pasture. So there is no problem with him selling it for more than what he bought it for, because he has done work in it, and because of that it is valid for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), that he was asked: About the man who contracts for the work, then does not work in it himself, and hands it over to another, so he profits from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless it so happened that he had done some work in it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al-Hakam Al-Khayyat, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I contract to tailor a garment for one dirham, and I hand it over to the client for more than that, increasing only for the cutting/sewing.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem in what you contract as work, then you increase the price in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Maymun the goldsmith, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I undertake work in which there is goldsmithing and engraving, so I stipulate with the engraver on a condition. When the accounting comes between me and him, I make him reduce from the stipulated amount.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is that with his agreement?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with buying green crops, then leaving them until you harvest them if you wish, or feeding them [to animals] before they form ears, while they are still grass. And he (peace be upon him) said: There is also no problem with buying crops that have already formed ears and ripened with wheat.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to buy the green crop?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, there is no problem with it.'

From him, from Zurara, similar to it. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with you buying the green crops or the straw while green, then you leave it if you wish until it grows ears, then you harvest it. And if you wish to feed your animal straw, there is no problem with it before it grows ears. But as for when it has grown ears, do not feed it the whole stalk, for that is spoilage.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a crop that was sold while it was grass, then it became grain. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem when he says, 'I am buying from you what comes out from this crop'. So when he buys it and it is grass, if he wishes he can use it up (as grass), and if he wishes he can wait for it (to become grain).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Al-Muhaqala and Al-Muzabana. I said, 'And what is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buying the fruit of the palm tree with the dates, and the crop with the wheat.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about buying the green plants (al-qasheel). The man buys it and does not cut it, and it begins to sprout during his leaving it until its ear emerges as barley or wheat. And he had bought it from its origin upon a stipulation that whatever there is of the tax (kharaj) is upon the non-Muslim (al-'ilj). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he stipulated when he bought it that if he so desires he would cut it, and if he so desires he would leave it as it is until it becomes an ear, otherwise it is not befitting for him that he leaves it until it becomes an ear.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, and there is an increase in it: 'So if he were to do it, upon him would be its maintenance and its expenditure, and for him would be whatever comes out from it'.

Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who cultivated a crop, whether he was a Muslim or a confederate (dhimmi), and spent expenditure on it. Then it became necessary for him to sell it due to his relocation from his place or for a need. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should buy it with silver (dirhams), for its origin is foodstuff.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted regarding Al-Araya that it can be bought by estimating its dates, and said: 'Al-Araya is the plural of Ariyah, and it is the palm tree that belongs to a man in the house of another man, so it is permissible for him to sell it by its estimation of dates, and that is not permissible regarding anything else.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a Muslim man who has a pasture (land) containing a mountain (rocky area) that is sold. His Muslim brother comes to him, and he has sheep and is in need of a mountain. Is it permissible for him to sell the mountain to him as he sells it to others, or should he prevent him from the mountain if he asks for it without a price? And what is his status regarding it, and what can he take? He said: It is not permissible for him to sell his mountain to his brother, because the mountain is not his mountain. Rather, it is permissible for him to sell it to a non-Muslim.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Idrees ibn Zayd, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We have uncultivated lands (diya'), and they have boundaries, and therein are pastures. And for a man from us there are sheep and camels, and he needs those pastures for his camels and his sheep. Is it permissible for him to reserve (hima) the pasture for his need of it?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the land is his land, then it is permissible for him to reserve it and dedicate it to what he needs it for.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I said to him, 'The man sells the pasture?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the land is his land, then there is no problem.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Abdullah who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who has a pasture (land/estate), and it has boundaries that reach twenty miles, and less or more. A man comes to him and says to him, 'Give me from the pasture of your estate, and I will give you such and such a dirham.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the estate is his, there is no problem.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about selling the pasture when it is dry, so the man directs his water to it, irrigates the land, and waters the grass, and he is the one who dug the river, and the water belongs to him, so he plants in it whatever he wishes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the water belongs to him, let him plant in it whatever he wishes, and sell it for whatever he likes.' He said: 'And I asked him about selling the harvest of wheat and barley and the rest of the harvests. He said: It is permissible, so let him sell it if he wishes.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Musa ibn Ibrahim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the sale of pasture (kal'a) and meadows, so he said: There is no problem with it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had reserved Al-Naqi' for the cavalry horses of the Muslims.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a share of water (shirb) with a group of people in a canal, wherein there are partners. If some of them become self-sufficient from their share, can he sell his share? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he wishes, he can sell it for silver (dirhams), and if he wishes, he can sell it for a measure of wheat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, all together, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Al-Nitaaf and Al-Arba'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Arba' is that a dam is built, so water is held back and the land is irrigated with it, then one becomes independent of it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not sell it, but lend it to your neighbor.' And Al-Nitaaf is that one has the right to drink (from a source), so he becomes independent of it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not sell it, but lend it to your brother or your neighbor.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the flood of the valley of Mahzour that the upper part should withhold the water upon the lower part for the palm trees up to the two ankles, and for the crops up to the two shoe straps. Then the water should be sent to the lower part from that for the crops to the shoe strap, and for the palm trees to the ankle. Then the water should be sent to the lower part from that. Ibn Abi Umeyr said: And Mahzour is a place of the valley.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding a waterflow of the valley of Mahzour that the upper part should withhold upon the lower part, for the palm tree up to the (level of) the two ankles, and for the cultivation up to the two shoe-straps.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the waterway of the valley of Mahzour: for the palm trees, the water can reach up to the two ankles, and for the farmers (of grain), up to the two shoe-straps.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled regarding the irrigation of palm trees by the flow (of water) that the upper parts are irrigated before the lower, and the water is left up to the two ankles. Then the water is channelled to the lower parts which follow it. It should be like that until the gardens are irrigated and the water is depleted.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whichever people revive something from the land and develop it, they are more rightful with it, and it is for them.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any man who goes to a ruined well, extracts it, digs out its rivers (water channels), and develops it, then charity (khums/zakat) is upon him regarding it. And if it was land belonging to a man before him who was absent from it, neglected it, and let it become ruined, then he comes afterwards seeking it, then the earth is Allah's and for the one who develops it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever revives dead land, it is for him.'

Hammad narrated from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Baseer, and Fuzayl, and Bukayr, and Humran, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever revives dead land, it is for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'Surely the earth is Allah's; He causes such of His servants to inherit it as He so desires, and the end is for those who are pious.' I and the people of my Household are those who inherited the earth, and we are the pious, and the earth, all of it, is for us. So whoever from the Muslims revives a land, let him develop it, and let him pay its taxes (kharaj) to the Imam from my Household, and for him is whatever he consumes from it. So if he neglects it or ruins it, and another man from the Muslims takes it from after him, so he develops it and revives it, so he would be more rightful with it than the one who neglected it. So let him pay its taxes to the Imam from my Household, and for him is whatever he consumes. Until the Appearance of Al-Qa'im (peace be upon him) from my family with the sword, so he would allow it and prevent it, and he would throw them out from it just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) allowed it and prevented it. Except whatever was in the hands of our Shiah, for he would cut it out for them upon what is in their hands and he would leave the land in their hands.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever plants a tree, or digs a valley from the beginning, with no one else having preceded him, and revives dead land, then it is for him, as a decree from Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Mansour ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a house containing other houses, and their pathway was one shared in the courtyard of the house. So one of them sold his house to a man. Is it for his partners in the pathway that they can take the right of pre-emption? He said: If he sold the house and turned its door to a road other than that, then there is no pre-emption for them, and if he sold the pathway along with the house, then for them is the right of pre-emption.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the shares are drawn (lots), the (right of) pre-emption is lifted.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled regarding pre-emption (shuf'ah) between partners in lands and dwellings, and said: 'No harm and no causing harm.' And he said: 'When the markings are marked and the boundaries are defined, then there is no pre-emption.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Ishaq Shaeer, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about pre-emption (shuf'ah) in houses: Is it an obligatory right for the partner, and is it presented to the neighbor so that he is more entitled to it than others? He said: Pre-emption in sales applies when there is a partner, so he is more entitled to it with the price.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Pre-emption is not for the Jew and the Christian. And he said: There is no pre-emption except for a partner who has not been distributed (his share). And he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The trustee of the orphan is at the status of his father. He takes the pre-emption for him if it was an advantage for him in it. And he said: For the absentee is pre-emption.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Pre-emption (shuf'ah) does not occur except for two partners as long as they have not divided (the property). So when they become three, there is no pre-emption for one of them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Kahili, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A house shared by a group, they divided it; each one took a portion, built upon it, and left a courtyard between them for their passage. Then a man came and bought the share of one of them. Is that for him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, but he must close his door and open a door to the road, or descend from the top of the house and close his door. If the owner of the pathway wishes to sell it, then they are more entitled to it; otherwise, it is his pathway, and he comes until he sits at that door.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithamī, from Aban, from Abu Al-Abbas and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said: We heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Pre-emption (al-shuf'ah) does not occur except for a partner who has not been distributed (his share).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no pre-emption in a ship, nor in a river, nor in a road.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who leased land from the lands of the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma) which is subject to land tax (kharaj), and its inhabitants were unwilling, and he acquired it from the Sultan due to the inability of its inhabitants to pay/manage it, or without such inability. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When its owners are unable regarding it, then it is for you to take it, unless they cause you harm. And if you give them something and the selves of its inhabitants are agreeable to you for it, then take it.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man who bought from them land from the lands of the kharaj, and he built in it or did not build, except that some people from the People of the Covenant settled in it. Is it for him to take from them the rent of the houses when they pay the jizyah of their heads?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should stipulate with them. So whatever he takes after the stipulation, it is permissible (halal).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurara, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with buying the land of the Ahl al-Dhimma (people of the covenant) when they cultivate it and revive it, so it is for them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and from Al-Sabati, and from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they asked both of them: about buying the land of the Dehqans (landed gentry/farmers) from the land of the Jizya (taxation lands). So he said: 'If that is the case, it will be snatched away from you, or you will pay from it whatever is upon it in terms of land tax.' Ammar said, 'Then he faced me and said: Buy it, for you have from the right (entitlement/value) that is more than that.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about buying the land of the Dhimmis, so he said: There is no problem with it. So it will be, when that occurs, at their status; you will pay from it just as they pay. He said: And a man from the people of the Nile asked him about a land he bought at the mouth of the Nile, so the people of the land say it is their land, and the people of the Astana say it is from our land. He said: Do not buy it except with the consent of its inhabitants.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have a land of tax (kharaj), and I have become straitened by it.' He was silent for a while, then said, 'If our Qaim rises, your share in the land would be greater than it, and if our Qaim (peace be upon him) were to rise, Al-Astan would be more ideal than their pieces (of land).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! I supplicate Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He grant me the halal (permissible sustenance).' He said: 'Do you know what is the halal?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! As for that which is with us, it is the goodly earnings.' He said: 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: The halal is the food of the Chosen Ones, but say: I ask You from Your extensive sustenance.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) looked at a man who was saying, 'O Allah, I ask You from Your permissible sustenance.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'You ask for the food of the Prophets. Say, O Allah, I ask You for extensive, goodly sustenance from Your sustenance.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Ismail al-Fadl al-Hashimi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the forced labor in the villages and what is taken from the porters and the hired workers in the villages, so he said: 'Stipulate upon them. So whatever you stipulate upon them from the dirhams and the forced labor, and whatever is besides that, then it is for you, and it is not for you to take anything from it until you have stipulated to them beforehand, even though you are certain that every one who lodges in that village takes that from him.' He said: 'And I asked him about a man who built houses or a house in his right of easement next to his neighbor, so the people of the house became his neighbors. Is it for him to repulse them while they are unwilling?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are free; they lodge wherever they wish and move wherever they wish.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Ali al-Asraq, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed to Ali (peace be upon him) at the time of his passing, saying: O Ali! Do not let the peasants be oppressed in your presence, and do not let the taxes increase upon the land you have placed upon it, and do not let forced labor be upon a Muslim' — meaning the employee.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to write to his officials: 'Do not conscript the Muslims [for forced labor]; and whoever asks you for something other than the obligatory tax, he has exceeded [his right], so do not give it to him.' And he used to write advising kindness to the peasants, and they are the hired laborers.
