A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The lodging upon the people of the taxation is for three days.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Lodging is due upon the people of the tax (non-Muslims) for three days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashshar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who indicates (shows) the houses and the estates, and takes the fee for it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a remuneration (fee), there is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, or someone else, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was listening, so he said to him: 'We instruct a man to buy for us the land, and the slave, and the house, and the servant, and we make a fee for him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from the companions of Al-Raqiq, who said: I bought a slave girl for Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he gave me four dinars, but I refused (to accept them). So he said to me: 'Take them!' So I took them, and he said: 'Do not take from the seller.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard my father asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and I was listening, so he said to him: 'Sometimes we instruct the man so he buys for us the land, and the house, and the slave, and the slave girl, and we make a fee to be for him'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

And from the two of them, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al-Wallad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and others, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), they said: He said. There is no problem with the fee of the broker; he buys for the people day after day for a known amount, and he is like the employee.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I bought a slave girl for Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So when I went to pay them the dirhams, I said, 'Can I ask for a reduction?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade reduction after the deal.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with a slave girl, presenting her for sale. He began bargaining with me and I bargained with him. Then I sold her to him. He joined his hand upon mine (to conclude the deal). I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I only bargained with you to see whether bargaining is appropriate or not.' And I said, 'I have deducted ten dinars from the price for you.' He said: 'Far be it! Indeed, this reduction should have been before the clasping of the hands. Have the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) not reached you: "The reduction after the clasping of the hands is prohibited."'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'hhaq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who employs another man for a known wage, and sends him to a property. Then another man gives him dirhams and says, 'Buy such and such with this, and whatever profit you make is between me and you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who employed him permits it, there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus, from Suleiman ibn Salim, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who employed another man with specified expenses and dirhams, on the condition that he send him to a land. When he arrived, a man from his companions invited him to his house for a month or two months, and he attained with him what made him needless from the expenditure of the employer. So the employee looked at what would have been spent upon him during the month if he had not invited him, so the one who invited him had sufficed him. So from whose wealth is that sufficient expenditure? Is it from the wealth of the employee or from the wealth of the employer? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was in the interest of the employer, then it is from his wealth, and otherwise it is upon the employee.' And (I asked) about a man who employed a man with specified expenses and did not explain anything, on the condition that he send him to another land. So whatever was from the provisions of the employee, from washing the clothes and the bath, upon whom is it? He said: 'Upon the employer.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ismail ibn Ammar, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to another man and says, 'Write for me a promissory note for dirhams.' So he says to him, 'I will take from you and write for you [in front of him].' He (the narrator) said, So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who hired a slave, so the slave said, 'Ask my master for whatever you wish, and for me, upon you is such and such specified dirhams.' So, does it obligate the employer, and is it permissible for the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not obligate the employer, and it is not permissible for the slave.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said: I was with Al-Reza (peace be upon him) regarding one of the needs, and I intended to leave to go to my house. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Come with me and spend the night in my presence.' So I went with him and entered into his house along with Al-Mu'tab. So he (peace be upon him) looked at his servants who were working with the clay in the animal enclosure, and other such work, and there was a black man with them who was not from them. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Who is this man with you?' So they said, 'He is helping us and we would give him something.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you agreed his wages with him?' So they said, 'No. He would be pleased from us with whatever we give him.' So he (peace be upon him) faced towards them to strike them with the whip, and was angered due to that with an intense anger. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Why are you taking it upon yourself?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I have forbidden them from the likes of this many a time, to make anyone work with them until they agree his wages beforehand. And know that there is no one who would work for you anything without an agreed wages, and then you increase something for him three times over upon his wages, he would still think that you have been deficient in his wages; and when you agree his wages beforehand, then give his wages to him, he would praise you upon the loyalty. So if you were to increase it even by a grain, he would recognise that for you and view that you have given him more.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the carrier and the employee, he said: 'His sweat should not dry up until you give him his wages.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan, from Shu'ayb who said: We hired for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a group of people working in his orchard, and their term was until the afternoon. So when they finished, he said to Mu'ttab: 'Give them their wages before their sweat dries up'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day should not employ a worker until he informs him of his wages, and the one who employs a worker then withholds him from Friday (prayer) bears his sin, and if he does not withhold him, they share in the reward.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a man who hires an animal to a known place, so he exceeds it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The rent would be accounted for him in accordance with whatever he has exceeded with, and if the donkey is injured, so he would be responsible'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who hires an animal, saying, 'I have hired it from you up to such and such a place. If I exceed it, then for you is such and such an increase,' and he specifies that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with all of it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad [from a man] from Abu al-Maghra' from al-Halbi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who hired an animal to a known place, so the animal died. He (peace be upon him) said: If he exceeded the condition, he is liable; and if he entered a valley without securing it (for safety), he is liable; and if it fell into a well, he is liable, because he did not secure it from it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'I was sitting with a judge from the judges of Medina when two men came to him. One of them said, "I hired this one to take me to the market on such and such a day, and he did not do it." The judge said, "There is no fee for him." I said: "So I called him and said, "O servant of Allah, it is not for you to go away with his right." And I said to the other, "It is not for you to take everything that is upon him. Reconcile, so that you return (some fees) between you two."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Muhammad al-Halby, who said: I was sitting in the presence of a judge among the judges, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was sitting with him. Two men came to him, and one of them said: 'I hired the camel of this man to carry my goods to one of the mines. I stipulated upon him that he bring me into the mine on such and such a day, because it is a market day, and I fear I might miss it. So if he were to detain me from that, I would deduct from the hire charge for each day he detains me, such and such an amount. And indeed, he detained me from that time for such and such days.' The judge said: 'This is an invalid stipulation; pay him his full hire charge.' When the man arose, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: 'This stipulation of his is valid, as long as he does not deduct the entirety of his hire charge.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I hired a mule to Qasr Ibn Hubeyra, going and coming, for such and such (amount), and I went out in seeking the debt for me. So when I got near to the arch of Al Kufa, I was informed that my companion had gone to the Nile. So I diverted towards the Nile. So when I got to the Nile, I was informed that my companion had gone to Baghdad. So I pursued him, and I was successful with it, and I was free from what was between me and him, and we returned to Al Kufa, and the going and coming was of (a duration of) fifteen days. So I informed my companion with my excuse, and I wanted to release myself from him from what I had done and to please him, so I offered him fifteen Dirhams. But he refused to accept. So we both agreed with (going to) Abu Hanifa. So I informed him with the story and the man informed him of it. So he said to me, 'And what did you do with the mule?' So I said, 'I have handed it over to him, safely.' He said, 'Yes, after fifteen days!' So he (Abu Hanifa) said, 'And what do you want with the man?' He said, 'I want the hire charges for my mule withheld from me for fifteen days.' So he said, 'I do not see for you a right, because he had hired it to Qasr Ibn Hubeyra, so he differed and rode it to the Nile, and to Baghdad. So he is responsible for the price of the mule and the hire charges are dropped. So when he returned the mule safely and you took possession of it, the hire charges are not obligated upon him.' He said, 'So we came out from his presence and the owner of the mule went on to say 'We are from Allah and to Him we are returning', due to what Fatwa Abu Hanifa had issued with. So I gave him something, and freed myself from him. Then I went on Hajj during that year. So I informed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) with what Fatwa Abu Hanifa had issued with. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is due to these (types of) judgements and what resembles these that the sky withholds its water and the earth prevents its Blessings'. He said, 'So I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'So what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I view for him, upon you, similar hire charges of a mule going from Al Kufa to the Nile, and similar hire charges of a mule riding from the Nile to Baghdad, and a similar hire charges of a mule from Baghdad to

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who hired an animal, so he gave it to someone else, and it died. He said: If he had stipulated that no one else would ride it, he is responsible for it, and if he did not specify, there is nothing upon him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who hires a ship for a year, or less, or more. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The hire charge is binding until the time for which it was hired, and the choice in taking the hire charge belongs to its owner; if he wishes, he takes it, and if he wishes, he leaves it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man who rents the house and the ship from the man for a year, or more or less. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Its rent is necessitated up to the time which he had hired it to, and the choice regarding taking the rent is up to its owner, if he so desires to he takes, and if he so desires to he leaves'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The neighbour is like the self, without causing harm nor being a sinner.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Samura ibn Jundab had a tree in the garden of a man from the Ansar, and the house of the Ansari was at the gate of the garden, and he used to pass by it to his palm tree and did not seek permission. So the Ansari spoke to him that he should seek permission when he came, but Samura refused. When he refused, the Ansari went to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him and informed him of the news. So the Messenger of Allah sent a messenger to him and informed him of what the Ansari said and what he complained about, and said: 'If you intend to enter, seek permission.' But he refused. When he refused, he bargained with him until he reached the price that Allah willed, but he refused to sell it. He said: 'For you is a tree extended to you in Paradise,' but he refused to accept. So the Messenger of Allah said to the Ansari: 'Go and uproot it and throw it at him, for there is no harm and no causing harm.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a group of people who had springs in a land, close to one another. A man intended to make his spring lower than its original position. If he did so, some of the remaining springs would be harmed, while others would not be harmed due to the solidity of the land. He said: He said, 'Whatever is in a solid place will not be harmed, and whatever is in soft, flat land will be harmed. And if he offers his neighbor to place his spring at the same level and measurement, he said, 'If they both agree, there is no harm.' And he said, 'There should be a distance of one thousand cubits between the two springs.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Ishaq Shair, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who saw a sick camel while it was being sold, so a man bought it for ten dirhams. Then he came and partnered a man in it for two dirhams for the head and the skin. It was judged that the camel was cured, so its price reached dinars. He said, so he said to the owner of the two dirhams, 'Take a fifth of what it reached.' But he refused, saying, 'I want the head and the skin.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not for him. This is the harm, and his right has been given to him when he is given the fifth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man had a canal in a town, and a man intended to dig another canal to his own town. What should be the distance between them so that one does not harm the other in the land, whether it is solid or soft? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'According to the reckoning that one of the two does not harm the other, if Allah wills.' He said: And I wrote to him (peace be upon him): A man had a mill on the river of a town, and the town belonged to another man. So the owner of the town intended to divert the water to his town through a different river, thereby disabling this mill. Is that for him or not? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should fear Allah and act with goodness in that, and not harm his believing brother.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged between the people of the city regarding the water sources of the palm trees, that the benefit of one should not be prevented, and he judged between the people of the desert that the surplus water should not be prevented in order to prevent the surplus of fodder, and he said: 'No harm and no causing harm.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who came to a mountain and dug a canal in it, so the water of the first canal caused the other canal to dry up. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should share the barriers of the well, night by night (alternatively), so they look at which of the two is harming its companion. If the latter is seen to be harming the former, then let it be closed.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed Samurat ibn Jundab had a date palm, and its pathway to it was in the middle of the house of a man from the Ansar. So he used to come and enter to his palm without permission from the Ansari. So the Ansari said to him, 'O Samurat! You do not cease to surprise us upon a state which we do not like to be surprised upon. So whenever you enter, seek permission.' So he said, 'I will not seek permission regarding a pathway, and it is my pathway to my palm.' So the Ansari complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent for him, so he came to him. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'So-and-so has complained about you and alleged that you pass by him and his family without his permission. So seek permission from him whenever you intend to enter.' So he said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Do I seek permission regarding my pathway to my palm?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Leave it alone, and for you will be its place, a palm in such and such a place.' So he said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'For you will be two.' He said, 'I do not want it.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) did not cease to increase for him until it reached ten palms. So he said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'For you will be ten in such and such a place.' But he refused. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Leave it alone, and for you will be its place, a palm in Paradise.' He said, 'I do not want it.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Indeed you are a harmful man, and there should neither be a harm nor a harm caused upon a Believer.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered with it, so it was uprooted, then it was thrown at him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Go, and plant it wherever you desire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said: I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'The human being, when he saves the foodstuff for his year, his back is lightened and he rests, and Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) did not buy a tie (of marriage) until they had secured the foodstuff for their year.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Abu Muhammad Al-Zuhli, from Abu Ayoub Al-Madaini, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The soul, when it secures its sustenance, settles (in peace).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'The soul tends to disturb its owner when there does not happen to be the livelihood for it what can be relied upon. So when its livelihood is kept aside, it feels secure'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding a man who sold palm trees and excluded one palm tree for himself, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged for him the entrance to it and the exit from it, and the span of its branches.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The distance between a drinking well and a drinking well is forty cubits, and the distance between an irrigating well and an irrigating well is sixty cubits, and the distance between a spring and a spring is five hundred cubits. And the road, when its people dispute over it, its boundary is seven cubits.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a yard between two houses, so he claimed that Ali (peace be upon him) judged for the owner of the house from whose side the fence was.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the palm trees that the single palm and the two palms for the man in the other's garden, so they differed regarding the rights of that, so he judged regarding it that for every palm from those, from the land is the reach of a frond from its fronds when it is distant.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sanctuary (haram) of the regular well is forty cubits around it. And in another report, fifty cubits, except if it is near a stagnant/decayed spot or by the road, so it becomes less than that, down to twenty-five cubits.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There should be between the two wells five hundred cubits if the ground is solid, and if the ground is soft, then a thousand cubits.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, said: The sanctuary of the river is its banks and what is adjacent to them.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a fence between two houses, so he claimed that Ali (peace be upon him) judged with it for the owner of the house whose side the fence was facing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who came to the land of a man and cultivated it without his permission. When the crop matured, the owner of the land came and said, 'You cultivated without my permission, so your crop is for me, and for you upon me is whatever you have spent.' Is that for him or not?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the farmer is his crop, and for the owner of the land is the rent for his land.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Nuymari, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding a man who rented a house and therein was a garden, so he cultivated in the garden and planted palm trees, and trees, and fruits, and other than that, and did not consult the owner of the garden regarding that. So he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the rent, and the owner of the house would evaluate the planting and the cultivation for a fair price, so he would give it to the planter; and if he had consulted, so upon him is the rent, and for him is the planting and the cultivation. He could have uprooted it and gone with it wherever he so desired.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq, from Harun ibn Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys palm trees to cut them for their trunks, so the man is absent and leaves the palm trees as they are, not having been cut. Then the man returns and the palm trees have borne fruit. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fruit is for him; he can do with it whatever he wishes, except if the owner of the palm trees used to irrigate it and look after it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Rayyan ibn Al-Salt, or a man from Rayyan, from Yunus, from Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the earth is Allah's; He dedicated it to His servants. So whoever leaves a land fallow for three consecutive years without a valid excuse, it is taken from his hand and given to another. And whoever neglects claiming his right for ten years, then he has no right.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever from whom land is taken, then he remains for three years not seeking it, it would not be permissible for him after three years that he seeks it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Imran ibn Abi Aasim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There are four whose supplication is not answered for them. One of them is a man who had wealth, so he lent it out without proof. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Did I not command you with witnesses?"'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ibn Baqqah, from Abu Abdillah al-Mumin, from Ammar ibn Abu Aasim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There are four whose supplication is not answered.' So he mentioned the fourth: a man who had wealth, so he lent it out without a proof. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would say: 'Did I not command you with witnesses?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one whose right goes away without having any proof, would not be recompensed.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Jallab who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: When injustice becomes more overwhelming than the truth, it is not permissible for anyone to think good of anyone else until he recognizes that good from him.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Zakariyya ibn Ibrahim, raising it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in a hadith of his, that he said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The one who trusts an untrustworthy one, so there is no argument for him upon Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The trustworthy one does not betray you, but you trusted the untrustworthy one.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever knows of a servant of Allah that he is a liar when he speaks, and breaks his word when he promises, and is treacherous when entrusted, and then entrusts him with a trust, it becomes a right upon Allah the Exalted to test him in it, and then He will neither compensate him nor reward him (for his loss).

Ali ibn Ibrahim [from his father] from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, all from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Muskan, from Abu Al-Jaroud, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever I narrate to you something, ask me about it from the Book of Allah.' Then he said in his hadith: 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden the saying of "it was said" and "he said", the spoiling of wealth, and the abundance of questioning.' So they said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, and where is this from the Book of Allah?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: There is no good in most of their secret counsels — the Verse.' And He said: And do not give away your property to the foolish which Allah has Made for you a (means of) support And He said: Do not put questions about things which if declared to you may trouble you

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who entrusts a drinker of wine with an amanah (trust/pledge) after knowing it in him, then there is no guarantee for him from Allah, nor is there any reward for him, nor a compensation.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from some of our companions, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It makes no difference to me whether you entrust [the wealth] to a treacherous person or to one who wastes it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates al-qil wa al-qal (idle talk/gossip), wastage of wealth, and abundant questioning.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: Indeed Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, hates 'al-qil wa al-qal' (rumor-mongering/gossip), wasting of wealth, and excessive questioning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq Shair, from Harun ibn Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cow, the sheep, and the camel that are in the pasture and spoil something; is there responsibility (damages) upon them? He said: If it spoils during the day, there is no responsibility upon it, because its owner protects it; and if it spoils at night, then there is responsibility upon it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from one of our companions, from Al-Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And Dawud and Sulaiman when they both gave judgement concerning the field when the people's sheep pastured therein.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The pasturing (nafash) does not occur except at night. Indeed, it is upon the owner of the field to protect the field during the day, and it is not upon the owner of the cattle to protect it during the day.' Rather, their grazing and sustenance are during the day. So whatever they spoil [during the day], there is no blame upon them. And it is upon the owners of the cattle to protect the cattle from the fields of the people at night. So whatever they spoil at night, they are responsible for it, and that is the 'nafash'. And indeed Dawud (peace be upon him) judged that the owner of the crop should receive the necks of the sheep, and Sulayman (peace be upon him) judged that he should receive the 'risl' and 'thallath', which is the milk and the wool, for that year.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara and Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who had a slave, so a jeweller or someone else hired him from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he were to waste something or abscond from him, then his masters are responsible.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who borrows a slave owned by a group of people, and he is faulted, then he is liable (responsible), and the one who borrows a free young person, and he is faulted, then he is liable.'

One of our companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Zarif al-Akfani, said: He authorized a slave of his regarding buying and selling, so he became bankrupt, and a debt was necessitated upon him. So he was seized due to that debt which was upon him, and the price of the slave was not equal to the debt upon him. So he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you sell him, the debt will be necessitated upon you, and if you liberate him, the debt will not be necessitated upon you.' So he liberated him, and nothing was necessitated upon him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left a debt upon him, and left a slave; the slave had wealth in trade, and a son, and in the hand of the slave was wealth and merchandise, and upon the slave was a debt which the slave had borrowed during the lifetime of his master in his trade. And the inheritors and the creditors of the deceased disputed regarding what was in the hand of the slave from the wealth and the merchandise, and regarding the neck (ownership) of the slave. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that there is no way for the inheritors upon the neck of the slave, nor upon what is in his hand from the merchandise and the wealth, except if they assume responsibility for the debt of all the creditors, then the slave and whatever is in his hand from the wealth would be for the inheritors. But if they refuse, the slave and whatever is in his hand would be for the creditors. The slave and whatever is in his hand from the wealth would be evaluated, then that would be distributed among them by shares.' So if the price of the slave and whatever is in his hand is insufficient for the wealth of the creditors, they return upon the inheritors for what remains for them, if the deceased had left anything. He said: 'And if there is excess from the price of the slave and whatever was in his hand from the debt of the creditors, it is returned to the inheritors.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man permits his slave to engage in trade, and debt comes to be upon him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If he permitted him to incur debt, then the debt is upon his master. And if he did not permit him to incur debt, then there is nothing upon the master, and the slave is sought out (to pay) the debt.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', from Mansoor ibn Yunus, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who hires out himself, so he has banned the sustenance upon himself'. And in another report, (He said): 'And how can he not have banned it, and whatever he acquires in it, so it is for his Lord who hired him'.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about hiring out (ijarah), so he said: 'It is good, there is no problem with it if he fulfills his capacity. Musa (peace be upon him) hired out himself and stipulated, saying: 'If you wish, eight (years), and if you wish, ten (years)'. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed regarding it: "You should serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be of your own free will."'

Ahmad, from his father, from Muhammad ibnarrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man engages in trade; if he hires out himself, is he given whatever he acquires in his trade?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not hire out himself, but let him seek sustenance from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and engage in trade, for when he hires out himself, he restricts sustenance upon himself.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Manage the major affairs of yours yourself, and delegate what is easy to others. I said, 'What kind of thing?' He said, 'The purchase of real estate and what resembles it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Arqat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not be a wanderer in the markets, nor manage the minute details of goods yourself, for it is not befitting for a Muslim man of noble lineage and religion to manage the purchase of minute goods himself, except for three things; for it is befitting for the one of religion and lineage to manage them himself: real estate, slaves, and camels.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is nothing which a man leaves behind which is more difficult upon him than the silent wealth; how should he deal with it?' He said: 'He should place it in the wall, meaning in the garden or the house.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Ziyad, from Aban ibn Uthman who said: Ja'far (peace be upon him) called me and said: 'Did so-and-so sell his land?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is written in the Torah that whoever sells land or water and does not place it in land or water, its price goes away with annihilation.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Wahb al-Hariri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The buyer of the real estate receives sustenance, and the seller of it is annihilated.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Murazim, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Musadif, his slave: 'Acquire a piece of land or a property, for when a calamity or misfortune befalls a man, and he remembers that behind his back there is something to support his family, he becomes more generous with himself.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Salam, from Hisham ibn Ahmar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: The price of real estate is annihilated (invalid) unless it is made to be in real estate similar to it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) entered Medina, he drew a line around it with his foot, then said: 'O Allah, do not bless the one who sells its four corners.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al- Asamm, from Misma'a who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'There is a land of mine which is sought from me and they (buyers) are coveting it'. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar! Do you not know that the one who sells the water and the clay, his wealth goes away as dust?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I can sell it for a lot of money and buy what is of a more expansive area from what I sell'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So there is no problem'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Seek refuge with Allah from the overwhelming burden of debt, the overwhelming pressure of men, and the ruin of widows.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The one who seeks this sustenance from its permissible means in order to provide for himself and his family is like the combatant in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' So if he is overwhelmed (by poverty), let him borrow upon Allah and upon His Messenger what he can provide for his family with. So if he dies and has not paid it back, it is upon the Imam to pay it. So if he does not pay it, its burden is upon him. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: 'The charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials over them... up to His words: and those in debts.' So he is the poor, needy, in debt.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan ibn Ibrahim al-Hamdani, raised it to one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). He said: 'I love for the man that there be a debt upon him, intending its repayment.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, [from Ibn Abi Umeyr], from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Every sin is expiated by being killed in the Way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except for the debt. There is no expiation for it except its payment, or the creditor fulfils it, or the one who has the right excuses it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Abbas, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Imam settles the debts of the believers, except for the dowries of the women.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) claiming a debt from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays. He said, 'He has taken my right.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'It is the one who killed him that has taken your right.' Then he said to Al-Walid, 'Stand up to the man and pay him from his right, for I wish to cool his skin which was already cold.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Abdul Kareem, from the people of Hamdan, from Abu Thumamah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), 'I intend to reside in Makkah or Al-Madina, and there is a debt upon me, so what do you say?' He said, 'Return and pay it to the one who is owed your debt, and ensure that you meet Allah, the Exalted, with no debt upon you. Indeed, the Believer does not betray.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Nakhāʿī, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Faḍālah, from Mūsā ibn Bakr, who said: I cannot count how many times I heard Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (peace be upon him) reciting: 'If there is a debt upon me, O Umaym, then Imrān ibn Mūsā is the one who lent [the money].'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: Beware of debt, for it is a humiliation during the day and a burden/stress during the night, and it requires payment in this world and payment in the Hereafter.

A number of our companions narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from ibn al-Qaddah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: Beware of debt, for it is humiliation during the day, a burden during the night, and a settlement in this world and a settlement in the Hereafter.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: 'What is the ascetism (zuhd) in the world?' He said: 'Woe to you! It is its forbidden things (haram), so avoid them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Jahm ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Muslim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Asceticism (zuhd) in the world is not by squandering wealth nor by forbidding what is permissible (halal); rather, asceticism in the world is that you not place greater trust in what is in your hand than in what is with God, the Mighty and Majestic.

I heard Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) saying: 'Zuhd (asceticism) in the world is [comprised of] shortening of hope, gratitude for every blessing, and restraint (wara') from everything that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribaat, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one upon whom is a debt, so he intends to fulfil it, he would have two Protectors from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assisting him upon the payment of his entrustment. So if his intention is deficient regarding the payment, they are deficient in assisting him by the measure of what he reduces from his intention.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man from us has something with him to meet his expenses with, and upon him is a debt. Should he feed his family until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, grants him ease so he could fulfill his debt, or should he borrow upon his back in bad times and difficult earning, or accept charity?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fulfill his debt with whatever is with him, and he should not consume the wealth of the people except that with him is what he can pay their rights to them.' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is saying: 'And do not swallow up your property among yourselves by false means, except if there happens to be a compromising trade among you.' And he should not borrow upon his back except that there is fulfillment with him. And if he was to go around the doors of the people, they would return him with the morsel and the two morsels, and a date and two dates, unless if there happens to be a guardian for him who would fulfill his debts from after him. There is none from us who dies except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Makes a guardian for him who would stand with regards to his promises and his debts, so he would fulfill his promises and his debts.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The house and the slave girl are not sold to settle debts, and that is because the man must have a shelter to dwell in and a servant to serve him.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Bureyd al-Ijli, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'There is a debt upon me,' and I think he said, 'For the orphans,' and I fear that if I sell my estate, I will remain with nothing. So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not sell your estate, but give some of it and withhold some.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to ask for payment/help, and I was present. He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'We do not have anything with us today, but a shipment (khitr) and a brand of camels (wasima) will come to us, so we will sell them and give you, God willing.' The man said to him, 'Promise me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I promise you what I am hoping for, when I am more hopeful of what I am expecting than you are of what you are expecting from me?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from al-Fadl ibn Sulayman, from al-Abbas ibn Isa, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was straitened by financial difficulty, so he went to one of his freedmen and said to him, 'Lend me ten thousand dirhams until I have ease.' He said, 'No, because I do not have it, but I want a bond.' He said, 'So he tore a tassel from his robe and said to him, 'This is the bond.' He said, 'So his freedman disliked that, so he was angered and said, 'Am I more worthy of fulfillment than Hajib ibn Zurara?' He said, 'You are more worthy of that than he is.' He said, 'So how did Hajib mortgage a bow, and it is merely a stick, for a hundred carriers, and he is an Infidel, yet he fulfills his pledge, while I would not fulfill my pledge for a tassel of my robe?' He said, 'So the man took it from him and gave him the dirhams, and placed the tassel in a container. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, eased the wealth for him, so he carried it to the man, then said to him, 'I have brought your wealth, so give me my bond.' He said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I lost it.' He said, 'Then do not take your wealth from me. One like me is not one who treats his pledge lightly.' He said, 'So the man brought out the container, and there was the tassel in it. So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) gave him the dirhams and took the tassel, threw it away, and departed.'

From him, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Isa ibn Abdullah, who said: Abdullah was presented with death, so his creditors gathered around him and demanded the debt owed to them. He said, 'I have no wealth with which to give to you, but be pleased with whichever you choose from the two sons of my uncle: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn Ja'far.' The creditors said, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far is wealthy and delays (payment), but Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is a man with no wealth, truthful, and he is more beloved to us.' [A man] with no wealth, truthful, and he is more beloved to us. So he sent for him and informed him of the news. He said, 'I guarantee the wealth for you until harvest time,' as a show of kindness, and there was no harvest for him. The people said, 'We are pleased,' and they held him as a guarantor. When the time of harvest came, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the wealth available to him, so he paid it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Uthman ibn Ziyad, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have a debt upon a man, and he intends to sell his house so that he may pay me.' He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I seek refuge for you with Allah that you should take him out from the shade of his head.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muhraz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Debts are of three types: A man who has a debt owed to him, so he grants respite; and when he has a debt owed to him, he gives it and does not delay, so that is for him and not against him. And a man who, when he has a debt owed to him, demands full payment; and when he has a debt owed to him, he pays it in full, so that is neither for him nor against him. And a man who, when he has a debt owed to him, demands full payment; and when he has a debt owed to him, he delays payment, so that is against him and not for him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man with whom wealth of mine was held, so he contended with me over it and swore an oath. Then wealth of his came to be with me; should I take it in place of my wealth that he took, and dispute it and swear upon it, just as he did? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he betrayed you, do not betray him, and do not enter into what you blamed him for.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man has a right against me, and he denies it to me. Then he entrusts me with wealth. Is it for me to take my wealth from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. This is betrayal.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man had wealth owed to him by another man, so the debtor denied it and took it away. Then afterwards, wealth came to be with the man whose wealth had been taken, from that same debtor. Can he take it from him in place of the wealth that man had taken from him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, but for this there is a statement (du'a) to be made: 'O Allah, I take this wealth in place of my wealth which He took from me, and I do not take what I take from it as treachery, nor as injustice.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Abdul Ghaffar al-Jazzi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who died while he had a debt upon him. He said: If wealth came into his hands without corruption, Allah will not hold him accountable when He knows of his intention [to pay], except for the one who did not intend to pay from his trust, so he is like the thief; and similarly is the Zakat, and similarly is the one who permits himself to take away the dowries of the women.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who takes on a debt and does not have the intention of paying it, he would be at the status of the thief.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Talha ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not sell the debt by the debt'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt upon another man. Then a man came to him and bought it from him [with an item/goods]. Then he went to the one upon whom the debt was due and said to him, 'Give me what is due from So-and-so for me, for I have bought it from him.' How should the repayment be in that case?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The man upon whom the debt is due returns his wealth (the value) to the one who bought it, from the man who had the debt.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): A man bought a debt owed by a man. Then he went to the debtor and said to him, 'Pay me what so-and-so owes you, for I have bought it from him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pay him the price that he had paid to the original creditor, and the one upon whom the wealth was due would be free from all that remained upon him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn Uthman said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and complained to him about a man from his companions. It was not long before the one complained against came. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is the matter so-and-so is complaining against you?' So he said to him: 'He complains about me that I collected my right from him'. He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sat up in anger, then said: 'It is as if when you collected your right, you did not offend'. They are fearing the evil Reckoning Do you see that they feared Allah that He would be inequitable to them? No, by Allah! They did not fear except for the collection (of debts), so Allah Mighty and Majestic named it the evil Reckoning. So the one who collects by it, he has offended.

Muhammad ibn Yahya raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him, 'I have some wealth due from one of the al-Hasaniyyun, and its collection has tired me, and there has been some speech between me and him, and I do not fear that something which would cause me distress may occur between me and him regarding that.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'This is not the way for debt collection, but when you go to him, prolong your sitting and maintain silence.' The man said, 'So I did that only for a little while, until I took my wealth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Khadir ibn Amr al-Nakha'i, who said: One of the two Imams (peace be upon them) said regarding a man who has a debt due from another man who denies it: If he (the creditor) asks him to swear an oath, it is not for him to take anything from him after the swearing; and if he leaves it and does not ask him to swear, then he (the creditor) is upon his right.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no pain except the pain of the eyes, and there is no stress except the stress of debt.'

And by this chain, it was said, Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The debt is a yoke of Allah in His earth. So whenever Allah wants to humiliate a servant, He places it in his neck.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Abi Talha (or Abu) Talha, the seller of Sabir, and Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, and Hakim al-Hannat, all together from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever withholds the wealth of a Muslim man, while he is able to give it to him, fearing that if that right were to go out from his hand he would be impoverished, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more able to impoverish him than he is to annihilate himself by withholding that right.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he disliked that a man should lodge with another man while he has a debt upon him, even if he had clarified it for him, except for three days.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who lodges with the man and has a debt upon him, can he eat from his food? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, he eats from his food for three days, then he should not eat anything after that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to Ali (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'There is a debt of mine upon a man, so he gave me a gift.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Count it from your debt upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Huzayl ibn Hayyan, the brother of Ja'far ibn Hayyan Al-Sayrafi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I handed over some wealth to my brother Ja'far, so he gives me what I spend, and I perform Hajj from it, and I give in charity. I had asked those around us, and they mentioned that this is invalid and not permissible, and I would love to reach your verdict.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Did it reach you before you handed over your wealth to him?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So take from it what he gives to you, eat from it, drink, perform Hajj, and give in charity. So when you arrive in Iraq, say, Ja'far ibn Muhammad gave this verdict to me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has wealth with another man as a loan, so he gives him something from his profit, fearing that he might cut that off from him, so he takes his wealth without it having been stipulated upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that, as long as it is not a stipulation.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said: I was delayed from the Hajj, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What has delayed you from the Hajj?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, I guaranteed a man, but he shamed me (failed to pay).' He said: 'What is it to you and the guarantees? Do you not know that they destroyed the former generations?' Then he said: 'A people committed many sins, so they feared them and feared a severe fear, and others came and said, Your sins are upon us So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the punishment upon them. Then the Blessed and High said: 'You feared Me and were audacious against Me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding the man who transfers the debt of another man to a third party. So the one who transferred it says to him, 'You are free from what I owe you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he frees him (from the debt), then it is not for him to return to him (the debtor), and if he does not free him, then it is for him to return to the one who transferred it (the creditor).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), similar to it. Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithamī, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Al-Abbas, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man guaranteed for a man the person of another man, saying, 'If you bring him to me, or else five hundred dirhams are upon you.' The Imam (peace be upon him) said: 'He is obligated to bring the person, and no dirhams are upon him.' Then he said, 'If he had said, 'Five hundred dirhams are upon me if I do not hand him over to you,' the Imam (peace be upon him) said: 'The dirhams would be obligated upon him if he did not hand him over to him.'

Humayd, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who assigns upon another man with dirhams, can he retract against him? He (peace be upon him) said: He cannot retract against him ever, except if he had become bankrupt before that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people are saying the guarantor is liable for the debt.' He said: 'There is no loss upon the guarantor; the loss is upon the one who consumed the wealth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had guaranteed the person of another man, so he imprisoned him, and said: 'Seek out your companion (the one for whom he guaranteed).'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Excellent is the aid toward taqwa of God — wealth.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Our Lord! Grant us good in the world and good in the Hereafter' The pleasure of God and Paradise in the Hereafter, and livelihood and good character in this world.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad — he elevated it (mursal) to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'It was said to him: "What is the matter that the companions of Isa (peace be upon him) used to walk upon the water, and that is not found among the companions of Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family)?" He said: "The companions of Isa (peace be upon him) were spared the concerns of livelihood, while these ones were tried with livelihood."'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ask God for sufficiency in the world and well-being, and in the Hereafter, for forgiveness and Paradise.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no goodness in one who does not love to amass wealth from halal (permissible) means — with which he protects his dignity, fulfils his debt, and maintains his family ties.

In his bequest to al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Seek assistance with some of this [world] for this [hereafter], and do not become a burden upon the people.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Ansari, from Ali ibn Ghurab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Accursed is the one who throws his burden upon the people.'

From him, from Ahmad, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Zareeh ibn Yazeed al-Muharabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Excellent is the world as an aid towards the Hereafter.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Zarih al-Muharbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The best of aids toward the Hereafter is the world.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said: A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'By Allah, we indeed seek the world and love to attain it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'What do you love to do with it?' He said: 'I benefit myself and my family with it, maintain kinship with it, give in charity with it, perform Hajj, and perform Umrah.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not seeking the world; this is seeking the Hereafter.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Wealth that withholds you from injustice is better than poverty that carries you to sin.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The believer's spending of the morning or the evening upon bereavement (thukl) is better for him than his spending a morning or an evening upon war (harab). So we seek Refuge with Allah from the war.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali al-Ahmasy, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The world is the best assistance for seeking the Hereafter.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Zareeh al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The world is the best of assistance for the Hereafter.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from his father who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Uzafir! You are dealing (co-operating) with Abu Ayoub and Al-Rabie, so what would your situation be when you are Called with among the supporters of the unjust ones?' He (the narrator) said, 'My father was dumbfounded. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him when he saw what had hit him: 'Yes, Uzafir! But rather, I have scared you with what Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has Scared me with'. Muhammad (the narrator) said, 'My father went forth and he did not cease to be gloomy, distressed, until he died'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Zurara met me coming out from his presence. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Walid! Do you not wonder at Zurara? He asked me about the 'amal (office/position) of these people. What did he want? Did he want me to say 'No' to him so he could report that from me?' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Walid! When did the Shia ask about their 'amal? Rather, the Shia used to say: 'One can eat from their food, and drink from their drink, and find shade under their shadow.' When did the Shia ask about this?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hadeed who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Fear Allah, and maintain your religion with piety (al-wara'), and strengthen it with dissimulation (al-taqiyyah) and self-sufficiency with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, whoever humbles himself to the ruler and to those who oppose him in his religion, seeking what is in their hands for his worldly life, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will suppress him and detest him, and leave him to himself. If he succeeds in securing something from his worldly life, and something from it comes to him, Allah, Majestic and Mighty is His Name, will remove the blessings from it, and will not recompense him for anything he spends on Hajj, nor freeing a neck, nor righteousness.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I had a friend who was one of the scribes of the Banu Umayya, so he said to me, 'Seek permission for me from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) to see him.' So I sought permission for him, and he granted it. When he entered, he greeted and sat down, then said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I was in the office of these people, so I acquired much wealth from their worldly affairs, and I closed my eyes regarding their demands.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Had it not been for the Banu Umayya finding someone to write for them, collect the booty/taxes for them, fight on their behalf, and bear witness for their groups, they would not have deprived us of our rights. And if the people had left them and what is in their hands, they would not have found anything except what fell into their own hands.' He said, 'So the youth said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is there a way out for me from it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If I tell you to do it, will you do it?' He said, 'I will do it.' He said to him, 'So exit from all that you acquired in their office. For whoever you recognize among them, return his wealth to him, and for whoever you do not recognize, give it in charity. And I guarantee for you, upon Allah (Exalted and Majestic), Paradise.' The youth kept his head lowered for a long time, then said, 'I have done it, may I be sacrificed for you.' Ibn Abu Hamza said, 'So the youth returned with us to Kufa, and he did not leave anything upon the face of the earth except that he extracted from it, even his clothes that were on his body.' He said, 'So I apportioned a share for him, and we bought him clothes and sent him expenses.' He said, 'And not many months passed until he fell ill, and we used to visit him.' He said, 'So I entered upon him one day and he was in the transit (of death). He opened his eyes, then said to me, 'O Ali! By Allah, your Master kept his promise to me.' Then he died. So we took care of his affairs, and I went out until I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). When he looked at me, he said, 'O Ali! By Allah, we kept our promise to your companion.' I said, 'You have spoken the truth, may I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, this is how he said to me at the time of his death.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said: Baseer said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about their office-bearers (or: their actions/positions), so he (peace be upon him) said to me: O Abu Muhammad! No, and not (even) for a mark of a pen. Indeed, one of you would not attain anything from their world except that they would take from his religion an equivalent amount, or he said: Until he loses from his religion an equivalent amount.

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I was sitting in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at the door of his house in Medina, so he looked at the people passing by in droves. He said to one of those present: 'Has an event occurred in Medina?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! A governor has been appointed over Medina, so the people are going in the morning to congratulate him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The man is fed with the matter to be congratulated for, and indeed it is a door from the doors of the Fire.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Basheer, from Ibn Abi Yafour, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when a man from our companions entered upon him and said to him, 'May Allah keep you well. Indeed, sometimes the man from among us is afflicted by financial straitness or difficulty, and he is summoned to construction; he builds it, or to a canal; he rents/digs it, or to a dam; he repairs it. So what do you say regarding that?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that I should tie a knot for them, or tie up a bag for them, and that for me is what is between its two ends. No, and not (even) for a circumflex with a pen. Indeed, the assistants of the unjust, on the Day of Resurrection, will be in pavilions of Fire until Allah judges between the servants.'

Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'So-and-so conveys the greetings to you, and so-and-so, and so-and-so.' He said, 'And the greetings be upon them.' I said, 'They are asking you for supplication.' He said, 'And what is the matter with them?' I said, 'Abu Ja'far has imprisoned them.' He said, 'And what is the matter with them and with him?' I said, 'He employed them, and he imprisoned them.' He said, 'And what is the matter with them and with him? Did I not forbid them? Did I not forbid them? Did I not forbid them? They are of the Fire, they are of the Fire, they are of the Fire.' He said, 'Then he said: O Allah, deceive their Sultan from them.' I said, 'So I departed from Makkah and asked about them, and behold, they had been released after this speech by three days.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Jahm ibn Humeyd, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do you not take protection of their Sultan (ruling authorities)?' I said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why (not)?' I said, 'My Religion would flee from me'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So are you determined upon that?' I said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Now, your Religion is safe for you'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman al-Minqari, from Fuzayl ibn Iyaz, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about certain things from the earnings (trade/commerce), so he forbade me from them, and said: 'O Fuzayl! By Allah! The harm of these (ruling authorities) upon this community is more severe than the harm of the Turks and the Daylam.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about abstention (war') from the people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who abstains from the prohibitions of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and keeps away from these (ruling authorities).' And when he does not guard against the doubtful matters, he falls into the forbidden (haram), and he does not recognize it. And when he sees the evil so he does not deny it, whereas he is able to do so, then he loves to disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And the one who loves to disobey Allah, so he has duelled against Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with enmity. And the one who loves the survival of the unjust ones, so he has loved to disobey Allah. Indeed, Allah the Exalted praised Himself upon the destruction of the unjust ones, so He said: So the roots of the people who were unjust were cut off; and all Praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.
