A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raised it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not incline towards those who are unjust, so the Fire would touch you', he said: 'He is the man who goes to the Sultan, so he loves his remaining until such time as he enters his hand into his bag and gives him something.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Hisham from the one who informed him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A group from those who believed in Musa (peace be upon him) said, 'If we go to the army of Pharaoh and are in it, and gain from his worldly life, then when what we hope for from the victory of Musa (peace be upon him) occurs, we will turn to him.' So they did it. When Musa (peace be upon him) and those with him turned towards the sea, fleeing from Pharaoh, they rode their animals and hastened in their journey to catch up with Musa (peace be upon him) and his army so that they would be with them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent an Angel who struck the faces of their animals and returned them to the army of Pharaoh, so they became among those who drowned with Pharaoh. And it is reported from Ibn Fazzal from Ali ibn Uqba from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'It is a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that you end up with those you lived with in his worldly life.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Abi Rashid, from Ibrahim ibn al-Sindi, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said: I described to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) the ones who speak with this matter (Wilayah) from those who perform the work of the Sultan (ruling authority), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When they rule over you, they will bring leniency upon you and benefit you in your needs.' I said: 'Among them are those who do that and among them are those who do not.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one among them who does not do that, disavow him, as Allah (exalted be He) disavows him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Humayd, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have been appointed toiled with a job/work, so is there an exit for me from that?' He said, 'How many are those who seek an exit from that but it becomes difficult for them.' I said, 'So what do you see?' He said, 'I see that you should fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and not repeat it.'

Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hashimi, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ziyad ibn Abi Salama, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'O Ziyad, you are working the work of the Sultan.' I said, 'Yes.' He said to me, 'And why?' I said, 'I am a man with magnanimity, and upon me are dependents, and there is nothing behind my back (no wealth).' He said to me, 'O Ziyad! That I should fall from a high place and be cut into piece after piece is more beloved to me than that I should govern for any one of them as an office-bearer, or roll out a carpet for one of them, except for that which I will mention.' I said, 'I do not know, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'Except for relieving the suffering of a Believer, or freeing his chains, or paying off his debt.' O Ziyad! The easiest of what Allah does to the one who governs for them is that a pavilion of fire is set up over him until Allah finishes the reckoning of the creatures. O Ziyad! So if you are given charge of any of their affairs, do good to your brethren, one for one, and Allah is behind that. O Ziyad! Whichever man from you governs for any one of them, then treats equally between you and them, say to him: 'You are an impersonating liar.' O Ziyad! When you remember your power over the people, remember the power of Allah over you tomorrow, and the depletion of what you gave to them from them, and the remaining of what you gave to them upon you.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ibn Sinan, from Habib, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man from this group was mentioned in his presence, who had been appointed to a position of authority. He said: 'How does he treat his brethren?' I said: 'There is no goodness in his conduct.' He said: 'Uff! They are entering into what is not befitting for them, and they are not doing good for their brethren.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no tyrant except that with him is a believer, by whom Allah defends the believers, and he is the one with the smallest portion in the Hereafter — meaning the believer with the smallest portion due to his companionship with the tyrant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Zakariyya Al-Saydalani, from a man from the Banu Hanifa, from the people of Bust and Sajistan, who said: I accompanied Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the year in which he performed Hajj during the beginning of the caliphate of Al-Mu'tasim. So I said to him while I was with him at the meal, and there was a group from the governors of the Sultan: 'Our governor is a man who befriends you, O People of the Household, and loves you. And a tax is levied on me in his office. So if you see fit, may I be sacrificed for you, write to him a letter of favor for me.' He said to me: 'I do not know him.' So I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, he is upon what I said regarding his love for you, O People of the Household, and your letter will benefit me with him.' So he took the paper and wrote: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. As for what follows, the bearer of this letter of mine has mentioned about you a beautiful doctrine, and that what is for you from your work is what you have done well in it. So be good to your brethren, and know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will question you about the weight of particles and mustard seeds.' He (the narrator) said: So when I arrived in Sajistan, the news preceded to Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah Al-Naysaburi, and he was the governor. So he welcomed me two farsakhs from the city. So I handed over the letter to him. He kissed it and placed it on his eyes, then said to me: 'What is your need?' So I said: 'A tax is levied on me in your office.' He said: So he ordered for the tax to be removed from me and said to me: 'You will not pay any tax as long as I have authority.' Then he asked me about my dependents, so I informed him of their number. So he ordered for me and for them with what would provide for us and extra. So I did not pay any tax during his term in office as long as he was alive, and he did not cut off my connection (favor) until he died.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are allies alongside the Sultan (ruling authority) by whom He defends His allies.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: We went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Hakam al-Sarraj said to him, 'What do you see regarding the one who carries the saddles and their equipment to Syria?' He said, 'There is no problem. You today are at the status of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). You are in a truce (hudna), so if the mutual exchange of tribute/gifts (mubayana) occurs, it will be prohibited upon you to carry the saddles and weapons to them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahboub from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abu Sarah from Hind al-Sarraj who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May Allah improve you. I used to carry weapons to the people of Syria and sell them to them. When Allah made this matter known to me, I felt constrained by that and said: I will not carry to the enemies of Allah.' He said: 'Carry to them, for Allah repels by them our enemy and your enemy, meaning the Romans; and sell to them. So when war is between us, do not carry. For whoever carries to our enemy weapons with which they assist themselves against us, then he is a polytheist.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the two parties from the people of falsehood who meet in battle, can I sell them the weapons? He (peace be upon him) said: Sell them what is defensive for them, like the armor and the shoes, and items such as these.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from al-Sarrad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I sell weapons.' He said, 'Do not sell them during the tribulation.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the skilled/tradesman who is trustworthy. And in another narration: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, loves the believing skilled/tradesman.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, who said: I heard a man ask Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so he said, 'I treat/work with flour and sell it, and the people say it is not befitting.' So Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And what is wrong with it? Everything that is sold is permissible if the servant fears Allah in it, so there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Yahya al-Khaza'i, from his father Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him that a boy had been born to me. He said: 'Did you not name him Muhammad?' I said: 'I have done so.' He said: 'So do not beat Muhammad, nor insult him. May Allah make him a delight of your eye during your lifetime and a true successor after you.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, in which profession should I place him?' He said: 'If you keep him away from five things, then place him wherever you wish.' Do not make him a money-changer, for the money-changer is not safe from usury. And do not make him a seller of coffins, for the owner of coffins rejoices in the plague when it occurs. And do not make him a food trader, for he is not safe from hoarding. And do not make him a butcher, for mercy is stripped from the butcher. And do not make him a slave trader, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of people is the one who sells people.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I gave a boy to my maternal aunt and forbade her from making him a butcher, or a cupper, or a goldsmith.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Qasim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Musa ibn Zanjawiya al-Tafleysi, from Abu Umar al-Hannat, from Ismail al-Sayqal al-Razi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and with me were two garments. He said to me: 'O Abu Ismail! Many garments come to me from your side, but these two garments that you are carrying do not come to me like them.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, the mother of Ismail spun them, and I wove them.' He said to me: 'A weaver?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do not be a weaver.' I said: 'Then what should I be?' He said: 'Be a polisher.' And there were two hundred dirhams with me, so I bought swords and old mirrors with them, and I arrived in Rayy with them, and I sold them for a great profit.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, who said: A sheikh from our Kufan companions narrated to me, saying: 'Isa ibn Shafaqiyya entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he was a magician. People would come to him, and he would take payment for that. So he said to him: 'May I be your ransom! I am a man whose profession was magic, and I used to take payment for that, and it was my livelihood. I have performed Hajj from it, and Allah favored me with meeting you, and I have repented to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So is there for me any way out regarding anything from that?' He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Loosen it, and do not tie it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the earning of the cupper, so he said: There is no problem with it when he does not stipulate (specify wages).

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Hanan ibn Sadeer who said: We entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and with us was Farqad the cupper. He said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I perform a work and I have asked about it more than one and not just two, and they claimed that it is a disliked work, and I love to ask you about it. If it is disliked, I will refrain from it and perform other works, for I will end up in that according to your word.' He said, 'What is it?' He said, 'Cupping.' He said, 'Eat from your earnings, O cousin, and give in charity, and perform Hajj from it, and marry, for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had cupping done and gave the wage, and if it were forbidden, he would not have given it.' He said, 'May Allah make me your ransom, I have a male goat which I hire out, so what do you say regarding its earnings?' So he said, 'Eat its earnings, for it is permissible for you, and the people dislike it.' Hanan said, 'I said, For what reason do they dislike it and it is permissible?' He said, 'For the people reproaching one another (for that work).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from 'Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had cupping done, and a slave of the Banu Bayadah did cupping on him, and he gave him (payment). And if it were forbidden, he would not have given him. So when he was finished, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Where is the blood?' He said, 'I drank it, O Messenger of Allah.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It was not befitting for you to do that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made it a barrier for you from the Fire, so do not repeat it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the earning of the cupper, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is disliked for him that he should stipulate (a fixed price), and there is no problem upon you if you stipulate it and bargain with him. Rather, it is disliked for him and there is no problem upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the earnings of the cupper, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'The wage of the male goat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Although the Arabs used to hire out (pay) with it, there is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father said to me: 'O Ja'far! Dedicate to me such and such of my wealth for the lamenters to lament me for ten years at Mina, during the days of Mina.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira died, so Umm Salama said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'The family of al-Mughira have established a lamentation, so I will go to them.' He permitted her, so she wore her clothes and prepared herself, and from her beauty she was like a fairy. Whenever she stood up and let down her hair, it covered her body, and she tied her ornaments at its ends. She eulogized her cousin in front of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), saying: 'I announce the death of Al-Walid ibn Al-Walid, Abu Al-Walid, the youth of the clan, the protector of the reality, the glorious one who ascends in seeking the frequent one. He was a rain in the years, a spring of abundant water, and a provision.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not object to that from her, nor did he say anything.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ismail, all together, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer, who said: A woman was with us in Al-Hayy, and she had a slave girl who was a lamenter. She came to my father and said, 'O uncle, you know that my livelihood is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and then from this slave girl, the lamenter. I would like you to ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that. If it is permissible, (fine); otherwise, I will sell her and eat from her price until Allah brings relief.' My father said to her, 'By Allah, I consider it a significant matter that I should ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about this question.' He said, 'So when we proceeded to him, I informed him with that. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Does she stipulate (a price beforehand)?' I said, 'By Allah, I do not know whether she stipulates or not.' He said: 'Tell her not to stipulate, and she can accept whatever is given.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Uzafir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he was asked about the earnings of the female lamenter, and he said: 'It is permissible for her [to earn it] by striking one of her hands upon the other.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the women emigrated to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a woman called Umm Habeeb emigrated among them, and she was a circumciser who circumcised the girls. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw her, he said to her: 'O Umm Habeeb, is the work that was in your hand still in your hand today?' She said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, unless it is forbidden, so forbid me from it.' He said, 'No, but it is permissible, so come closer to me until I teach you.' She said, 'So I approached him, and he said: 'O Umm Habeeb, when you do it, do not overdo it, i.e., do not uproot it entirely, but scrape it, for it is brighter for the face and more pleasing to the husband.'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Umm Habeeb had a sister called Umm Atiyya, and she was a hairdresser (meaning a ladies' maid). When Umm Habeeb returned to her sister, she informed her of what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said to her. So Umm Atiyya came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him of what her sister had said to her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Come closer to me, O Umm Atiyya! When you attend to the girl, do not wash her face with a rag, for the rag absorbs the water of the face.'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A female hairdresser came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said to her: 'Have you left your work or are you still established upon it?' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I do it unless you forbid me from it, so I shall refrain from it.' He said to her: 'Do it. But when you comb hair, do not polish the face with the rag, for it removes the water of the face, and do not attach the hair with the hair.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Mukram, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about the ribbons that women place on their heads, attaching them to their hair, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem for the woman with whatever she adorns herself with for her husband.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I said to him, 'It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed the connector (hairdresser) and the connected (client).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not over there (what you are thinking it to be). But rather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed the connector who committed adultery during her youth, so when she grew older, she led the women to the men, so that is the connector and the connected.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was a woman called Umm Tayba who used to circumcise the girls. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) called her and said to her: 'O Umm Tayba! When you circumcise the girls, scrape lightly and do not overdo it, for it is cleaner for the complexion of the face and more pleasurable for the husband.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the earnings of the female singers, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which men enter upon her for is prohibited, and that which she is invited to the weddings, there is no problem with it.' And it is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from the way of Allah.'
From him, from Hakam Al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The female singer who attends the weddings, there is no problem with her earnings.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Ayoub ibn Al-Hurr, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The wage of the female singer who attends the weddings is not problematic, provided she is not the one whom men enter upon (for private entertainment).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) was asked about procuring the female singer, so he said: 'The slave girl may be a distraction for the man, and her price is no more than the price of a dog, and the price of a dog is ill-gotten wealth (suh't), and the ill-gotten wealth is in the Fire.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Fazzal, from Saeed bin Muhammad al-Tahiri, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked him about the selling of the singing slave-girls, so he said: 'Buying them and selling them is prohibited, and teaching them is disbelief, and listening to them is hypocrisy.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, from Nasr ibn Qabous, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The female singer is accursed, and accursed is the one who consumes her earnings.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said: Is'haq ibn Umar bequeathed at the time of his death regarding his slave-girl singers that we should sell them and carry their price to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Ibrahim said: So I sold the slave-girls for three hundred thousand dirhams and carried the price to him. I said to him: Indeed, a mawla of yours, called Is'haq ibn Umar, has bequeathed at the time of his death the selling of his slave-girl singers and carrying the price to you. I have sold them, and this price is three hundred thousand dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: I have no need for it. Indeed, this is ill-gotten gain (suh't). Teaching them is disbelief (kufr), and listening to them is hypocrisy (nifaq), and their price is ill-gotten gain (suh't).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Al-Fadl ibn Kathir, from Hassan al-Mu'allam, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about teaching, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not take a wage for teaching.' I said: 'Poetry, and letters, and what resembles that, stipulating (a price) upon it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, after the children are equal in your presence in teaching, not preferring some of them over others.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abu Qurra, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'These people say that the earnings of the teacher are ill-gotten gain (suh't).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying, enemies of Allah! They merely intend that the Quran should not be taught. And if a man were to give the teacher the wergild (diyah) of his child, it would be permissible for the teacher.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Suleyman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Mushaf (copies of the Quran) shall not be bought (for a price). So when you buy, say: I am only buying from you the paper, and whatever is in it from the leather/cover, and its decoration, and whatever is in it from the work of your hands, for such and such (amount).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the selling of the parchments (copies of the Holy Quran) and buying them, so he said: 'Do not buy the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but buy the iron (ink pigment), and the paper, and the two covers, and say, "I am buying this from you for such and such (an amount)."'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Usman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about buying the parchments (copies of the Quran) and selling them, so he said: 'The paper was only placed by the pulpit, and the space between the pulpit and the wall was the measure of what a sheep could pass through, or a man walking sideways.' He said: 'The man would come and write from that, then indeed they would sell it after that.' I said, 'So what do you think regarding that?' He said to me, 'Buying is more beloved to me than if I were to sell it.' I said, 'So what do you think if I were to give a recompense for its writing?' He said, 'There is no problem, but this is how they were doing (in those days).'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Hashim, from Sabiq al-Sindi, from Anbasah al-Warraq, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'I am a man who sells the Mushaf (copies of the Quran). If you forbid me, I will not sell them.' He said, 'Do you not buy paper and write in it?' I said, 'Yes, and I prepare/bind them.' He said, 'There is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — both from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir used to say: I did not think that Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) would leave behind a successor more virtuous than himself — until I saw his son, Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). I intended to admonish him, but he admonished me instead.' His companions said to him: 'With what did he admonish you?' He said: I went out to one of the outskirts of Medina during an intensely hot time. Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali met me — he was a heavyset, large man — leaning upon two black servants, or two freed men. I said to myself: Glory be to God! An elder from the elders of Quraysh, at this hour, in this state, in pursuit of worldly livelihood. I shall surely admonish him! So I approached him and greeted him. He returned my greeting with a rebuke, while he was dripping with sweat. I said: May God keep you well — an elder from the elders of Quraysh, at this hour, in this state, in pursuit of worldly livelihood. Tell me, if your appointed hour arrived while you were in this state, what would you do? He said: If death came to me in this state, it would come to me while I was engaged in an act of obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic — by which I protect myself and my family from depending on you and on the people. Rather, what I truly feared was if death came to me while I was engaged in an act of disobedience to God. So I said: You speak the truth — may God have mercy on you. I intended to admonish you, but you have admonished me instead.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Momineen (blessings of God upon him) used to strike with the hoe and cultivate the lands. And the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) used to suck the date pits with his mouth and then plant them, and they would sprout within the hour. And indeed Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) freed one thousand owned slaves from his own wealth and the toil of his own hands.

I came across Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in one of the streets of Medina on a scorching summer day of intense heat. I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Given your station with God the Mighty and Majestic, and your kinship to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), you are exerting yourself on such a day?' He said: 'O Abd al-A'la! I have gone out in search of livelihood so that I may be self-sufficient from the likes of you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Amira and Salama Sahib al-Sabiri, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) freed a thousand owned slaves from the toil of his own hands.

Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): "You would be the finest of servants were it not that you consume from the public treasury and do not work with your own hands."' He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) wept for forty mornings. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to iron: 'Soften yourself for My servant Dawud!' And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, softened iron for him, and he used to make a coat of armour every day and sell it for a thousand dirhams. He made three hundred and sixty coats of armour and sold them for three hundred and sixty thousand, and became needless of the public treasury.

A man came across Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), and under him was a pile of date stones. He said to him, 'What is this beneath you, O Abu al-Hasan?' He replied, 'One hundred thousand date clusters, if God wills.' He [the narrator] said: He planted them, and not a single stone from them failed to sprout.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra, from Ammar al-Sajistani, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) placed a rock upon the path to divert the water from his land, so by God, neither a camel nor a human being has moved it until this very hour.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asbat ibn Salim who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he asked us about Umar ibn Muslim, what he was doing. So I said: 'He is a righteous man, but he has abandoned trade.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The work of Satan!' — (saying it) three times. 'Does he not know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) bought a caravan of camels that came from Syria, and he gained profit from it — with which he paid off his debts and distributed among his relatives? God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Men whom neither trade nor selling diverts from the remembrance of God' — up to the end of the verse [24:37]. The story-tellers say: These men were not merchants. They lie! Rather, they did not abandon the prayer in its prescribed time. And he (who does both) is superior to one who attends the prayer but does not trade.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) used to go out with loads of date stones. It would be said to him: 'O Abu al-Hasan! What is this with you?' He would say: 'Palm trees, God willing.' He would plant them, and not a single one of them failed to sprout.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) working in his land, his feet having become soaked in sweat. I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, where are the men (workers)?' He said, 'O Ali! Those who worked by their hands in their land and in my father's land, who are better than me.' I said to him, 'Who are they?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful, and my forefathers (peace be upon them), all of them had worked by their hands. And this is from the work of the Prophets, the Messengers, the Successors, and the Righteous.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, who said: I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and behold, he was in his garden, holding a spade in his hand, and he was using it to open the water (flow), and he was wearing a shirt resembling cotton cloth, as if it were stitched to him due to its tightness.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from his father who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) gave my father one thousand and seven hundred dinars, so he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Trade with these'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Know that there is no real interest for me in its profits, although the profits are desirable in it, but I loved that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, would see me exposing myself to its benefits'. He (the narrator) said, 'So I made a gain of one hundred dinars for him in it. Then I met him, so I said to him, 'I have made a gain for you in it, of one hundred dinars'. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was happy with that with an intense happiness, and he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Corroborate it in the capital of my wealth'. He (the narrator) said, 'So my father died and the wealth was with him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent a message to me, writing: 'May Allah grant us and you good health. There is for me with your father Muhammad, one thousand and eight hundred dinars, I had given him to trade with. So hand it over to Umar ibn Yazeed'. He (the narrator) said, 'So I looked in the book of my father, so there was in it for Abu Musa, with me, a thousand and seven hundred dinars, and I had profited for him in it by one hundred dinars which Abdullah ibn Sinan and Umar ibn Yazeed both knew of it'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'I do not know how to perform manual labor with my hands, nor do I know how to trade, and I am a laborer and needy.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Work, so carry [loads] upon your head, and become independent of the people. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had carried a stone upon his shoulder and placed it in a wall from his walls. And indeed, the stone is in its place, and it is not known how deep it is, except that it is there.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I work in some of my estates until I sweat, although there are those who can suffice for me, so that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, may know that I seek the permissible livelihood.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from his father who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) handed over to me seven hundred dinars and said, 'O Uzafir! Spend it in something. It is not that I have greed for that, but I love that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would see me striving for its benefits.' Uzafir said, 'So I made a profit in it of one hundred dinars, so I said to him during the circumambulation, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted me one hundred dinars in it.' So he said: 'Record it in the capital of my wealth.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Ziyad ibn Isa, and he is Abu 'Ubayda al-Haddad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not consume one another's wealth by false means,' so he said: 'The Quraysh used to gamble a man with his family and his wealth, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade them from that.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) [the verse]: 'Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it' — it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is Al-Maysir?' He said: 'Whatever you gamble with, even if it is dice and walnuts.' It was said, 'So what are Al-Ansab?' He said: 'Whatever is sacrificed for their gods.' It was said, 'So what are Al-Azlam?' He said: 'Their divining sticks with which they seek omens.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jaroud who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, and the thief does not steal while he is a believer, and the plunderer does not plunder a plunder of honor while he is a believer.' Ibn Sinan said: I said to Abu al-Jaroud, 'And what is a plunder of honor?' He said, 'Similar to what Hatim did when he said, 'Whoever takes something, it is for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The gambling (qimar) and the plundering (nuhba) are not valid.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He used to forbid the walnuts from being eaten when the children used to bring them from the gambling, and he said: 'It is an ill-gotten gain (suh't).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the scattering (of sweets/nuts) from sugar and almonds and their like, is it permissible to eat it? He said: It is disliked to eat what is seized (or scattered as plunder).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The children are playing with walnuts and eggs and are gambling (with these)'. So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not eat from it, for it is prohibited.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): 'Children play with walnuts and eggs and gamble [with them].' He said: 'Do not eat from them, for they are unlawful.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Isa al-Farra, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Four [things] are not permissible in four [acts of worship]: Betrayal (al-khiyanah), Booty/Plunder (al-ghulul), Theft (al-sariqah), and Usury/Interest (al-riba). These four are not permissible in Hajj, nor Umrah, nor Jihad, nor Charity (Sadaqah).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man acquires wealth from non-permissible means, then performs Hajj, and recites the Talbiyya, he is called out: 'Neither service nor support for you'; and if it was from permissible means, and he recites the Talbiyya, he is called out: 'Service and support for you'.
Ahmad narrated from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The prohibited earnings manifest in the offspring.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'I have earned wealth; I closed my eyes in seeking it, [mixing] the permissible and the prohibited. I intend repentance, but I do not know which part is permissible and which is prohibited, and they have become mixed up for me.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, 'Give in charity a fifth of your wealth, for Allah, Exalted is His Name, is pleased with the fifth from the things, and the rest of the wealth is permissible for you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from a man who named him, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The world yearned for a people with purely permissible earnings, but they did not desire it, so they passed by. Then it yearned for a people with permissible and doubtful earnings, so they said, 'We have no need for the doubtful,' and they expanded within the permissible. Then it yearned for another people with prohibited and doubtful earnings, so they said, 'We have no need for the prohibited,' and they expanded within the doubtful. Then it yearned for a people with purely prohibited earnings, so they sought it, but they could not find it. And the believer in the world eats at the status of the desperate (one who eats only out of necessity).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from the one who mentioned it, from Dawud al-Sarri, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'O Dawud! The prohibited [earnings] do not flourish, and if they do flourish, there is no blessing for him in it, and whatever he spends of it he is not rewarded for it, and whatever he leaves behind, it becomes his provision to the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya said, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man bought a farm or a servant from a man with wealth that he had taken from banditry (cutting off the road) or from theft. Is it permissible for him to benefit from the fruits of this farm, or is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with this female servant whom he bought from the thief or from the bandit? So he (peace be upon him) signed: There is no good in anything whose origin is prohibited, and it is not permissible to utilize it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who attained wealth from the work of the Banu Umayya, and he gives charity from it, maintains kinship ties from it, and performs Hajj so that what he had earned may be forgiven for him, and he says, 'Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'An error does not expiate an error, but a good deed removes an error.' Then he said: 'If he mixed the permissible with the prohibited, so they all became mixed, and the permissible is no longer distinguished from the prohibited, then there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Ibn Abi Umeyr from one of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We will proceed to what they have done of deeds, so We shall render them as scattered floating dust.' He said: 'Even if their deeds were intensely whiter than the tapestries, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would say to them: Be scattered floating dust!' And that is because whenever the prohibited [means] was displayed unto them, they grabbed it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ammar bin Marwan, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the fraud (al-ghulul). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is defrauded from the Imam (peace be upon him) is ill-gotten gain (suh't), and consuming the wealth of the orphan and its like is ill-gotten gain. And ill-gotten gains are of many types; among them are the payments for the immoralities, and the price of wine and the intoxicating nabidh, and usury after the proof. So as for the bribe in judgment, then that is disbelief in Allah the Magnificent and in His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The ill-gotten gain (al-suh't) is the price of the deceased (animal), and the price of the dog, and the price of wine, and the dowry of the prostitute, and the bribe in judgment, and the payment of the soothsayer.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Ill-gotten gains (al-suh't) are of numerous varieties; among them are the earnings of the cupper when he stipulates (a fixed price), and the payment of the adulteress, and the price of wine. As for the bribe in judgment, it is disbelief in Allah the Magnificent.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazeed ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about ill-gotten gain (al-suh't), so he said: 'The bribe in judgement.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Amari, from Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah al-Amiri, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the price of the dog that does not hunt, so he said: 'It is ill-gotten gain (suh't). As for the hunting dog, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from someone else from Al-Sha'iri from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever spends the night awake regarding his earnings and does not give his eyes their share of sleep, then that earning is prohibited.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The manufacturers, when they stay awake the whole night, so it is ill-gotten gain (suh't).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the earnings of slave girls, for if they do not find (sustenance from work), they commit adultery, except for a slave girl who is known for her handiwork; and he forbade the earnings of the slave boy who is not skilled in handiwork, for if he does not find (sustenance), he steals.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised two punishments regarding the wealth of the orphan; one of them is the punishment of the Hereafter, which is the Fire. And as for the punishment in the world, it is His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring,' the Verse; Meaning, let him fear that if he leaves behind his offspring they would be treated by them like these orphans.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ajlan Abi Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about devouring the wealth of the orphans, so he (peace be upon him) said: It is as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: 'Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only devouring into their bellies fire, and they will be burned in a Blaze.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, without me asking him: 'Whoever shelters an orphan until his orphanhood ceases or he becomes self-sufficient, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated Paradise for him, just as He has obligated the Fire for the one who devours the wealth of the orphan.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the man who has the wealth of orphans in his possession, and he is in need of it, so he extends his hand and takes it, intending to return it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to consume except in moderation, not being extravagant.' So if it was from his intention that he would not return it to them, then he is in the same status as those to whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Zubyan ibn Hakim al-Awdi, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have a daughter of my brother who is an orphan, so sometimes something is gifted to her, so I eat from it. Then I feed her something after that from my wealth, so I say: O Lord, this for this!' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever is poor, let him eat reasonably.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who manages something for the orphans and he is needy, having nothing to sustain him, so he collects their wealth and stands in their place, so let him eat in a measured manner and not be extravagant; and if it was that standing in their place does not pre-occupy him from what he works for himself, so he should not take anything from their wealth.'

Uthman from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if you intermingle with them, so they are your brethren' He said: It means the orphans. When a man has custody of orphans in his care, let him spend from his own wealth in proportion to what he spends for each of them, so he mixes with them and they all eat together. And he should not take anything (extra) from their wealth. Rather, it is the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'so let him eat reasonably.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The reasonableness is the daily bread, and it refers to the executor or the custodian regarding their wealth, and what is correct for them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeyr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Isa ibn Musa asked me about the custodian of orphans regarding the camels, and what is permissible for him from them. I said: When he cleans its water-trough, and seeks out its stray ones, and cures its diseases, then for him is that he can take from its milk without exhausting its udder nor spoiling its young.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever is poor, let him eat reasonably.' He said: 'That is a man who withholds himself from livelihood (to manage orphans' affairs), so there is no harm if he eats reasonably if he is managing their wealth for them. If the wealth is small, he should not eat anything from it.' He said: I said, 'What is your view of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And if you intermingle with them, then they are your brethren He said: 'You take from their wealth an amount that suffices for them, and you take from your wealth an amount that suffices for you, then you spend it.' I said, 'What is your view if they are orphans, young and old, and some of them have better clothing than others, and some eat more than others, and their wealth is together?' He said: 'As for the clothing, the cost of each person's clothing is upon him individually. As for the eating of food, make it all-inclusive, for the young are likely to eat as much as the old.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from one of our companions, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the orphan whose yield in a month is twenty dirhams, how should it be spent on him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'His sustenance from the food and the dates.' And I asked him about spending a third of it on him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and half of it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asbaat ibn Salim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A brother of mine died, so he bequeathed to an elder brother of mine and included me with him in the bequest, and he left a young son of his, and he had wealth. So my brother worked with it, and whatever was excess, he submitted it to the orphan, and guaranteed his wealth for him.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If your brother has wealth that covers the orphan's wealth, if it is lost, there is no problem with it. And if he does not have wealth, he should not expose the orphan's wealth (to loss).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the wealth of the orphan, he said: The worker with it is liable (guarantor), and for the orphan is the profit when there is no wealth for the worker with it. And he said: If it incurs loss, he pays it.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding a man who has the wealth of an orphan with him, he said: If he is needy and has no wealth of his own, then he should not touch the orphan's wealth; and if he trades with it, then the profit is for the orphan and he is responsible (liable for any loss).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Asbat ibn Salim who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said, 'My brother instructed me to ask you about the wealth of an orphan in his custody, which he trades with.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If your brother has wealth that is sufficient to cover the orphan's wealth if it is lost or if something befalls it, he should compensate him for it; otherwise, he should not expose the orphan's wealth (to risk).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is appointed guardian over an orphan's wealth, can he borrow from it? He said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to borrow from the wealth of orphans who were in his guardianship, so there is no problem with that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'If a man is appointed guardian over an orphan's wealth, can he borrow from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to borrow from the wealth of an orphan who was in his care.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding A man has some wealth of orphans with one of his family members, so he hands it over to him. He takes from it dirhams which he needs, and the one who had the wealth of the orphans does not know that he has taken anything from their wealth. Then he becomes affluent after that. Which is better for him: to give it to the one in whose hand it was, or to hand it over to the orphan who has reached maturity? And would it suffice if he hands it over to his companion as a gift and does not inform him that he had taken some wealth of his? He (peace be upon him) said: Whichever of those he does will suffice for him, when he delivers it to its owner. For this is from the secrets (of the guardian's intention). If it is from his intention to return it to the orphan, if he has reached maturity, in whichever manner he wishes, even if he does not inform him that he had taken something for him; and if he wishes, he can return it to the one in whose hand it was. And he (peace be upon him) said: If the owner of the wealth is absent, let him hand it over to the one in whose hand it was.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabie, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who was appointed guardian over an orphan's wealth, so he borrowed something from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) had borrowed wealth from the orphans who were in his guardianship.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Mus'ab Al-Hamdani, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There are three matters in which no one has an excuse: paying back the trust to the righteous and to the immoral; fulfilling the covenant with the righteous and with the immoral; and being dutiful to the parents, whether they are both righteous or both immoral.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Bukayr, from al-Husayn al-Shaybani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man from your mawali permits the wealth of the Banu Umayya and their blood, and indeed, some deposits have come to him from them.' So he said, 'Return the trusts to their owners, even if they are Magians, for that would not be the case until our Qaim from the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon him) rises, so he would permit and prohibit.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Repay the entrustments, even if it be to a murderer of the children of the Prophets.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Abi Hafs, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fear Allah, and upon you is the performance of the trust to the one who entrusted you, and even if the murderer of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) had entrusted me with a trust, I would have returned it to him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in a bequest of his: 'Know that if the one who struck Ali (peace be upon him) with the sword and his killer were to entrust me and seek my good counsel and consult me, then if I had accepted that from him, I would have repaid the trust to him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Hafs ibn Qurt, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman in Medina, the people were placing the slave girls with her to train them, and we said: We have not seen the likes of what is poured upon her from the livelihood.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'She was truthful in the discussions, and repaid the entrustments, and that brings the livelihood.' Safwan said: 'And I heard it from Hafs after that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He is not one of us who breaks the trust.' And he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Trustworthiness brings livelihood, and treachery brings poverty.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan, meaning Musa (peace be upon him), about a man who entrusted a man with some valuable wealth, and the man upon whom is the wealth is a man from the Arabs, powerful enough that he does not give him back anything, and he (the entruster) is not able upon him with anything, and the man who entrusted him is a wicked foreigner. So he did not give him anything. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Say to him, Return it to him, for he had entrusted him with an entrustment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Kathir ibn Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyaba, who said: When my father Sayyaba died, a man from his brethren came to me and knocked on the door. I went out to him, and he offered me condolences, saying, 'Did your father leave anything?' I said to him, 'No.' So he handed me a bag containing one thousand dirhams and said, 'Keep it well and eat from its surplus.' I entered to my mother, happy, and informed her. In the evening, I went to a friend of my father and bought Sabiriyya goods, sitting in a shop. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, granted me much goodness in it. When Hajj approached, it occurred in my heart. I went to my mother and said, 'It has occurred in my heart that I should go out to Mecca.' She said to me, 'Return the dirhams of so-and-so to him; bring them.' I brought them to him and handed them over, as if I had gifted them to him. He said, 'Perhaps you considered it small, so I will increase it for you.' I said, 'No, but Hajj has occurred in my heart, so I preferred that your money remain with you.' Then I went out and fulfilled my Hajj rituals, then returned to Medina. I entered with the people to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who gave general permission. I sat among the back rows of the people, and I was young. People began asking him, and he answered them. When the crowd thinned, he gestured to me, so I approached him. He said to me, 'Do you have a need?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I am Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyaba.' He said to me, 'What happened to your father?' I said, 'He died.' He expressed condolences and mercy. He said, 'Then he said to me, 'Did he leave anything?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'From where did you perform Hajj?' I began and narrated to him the story of the man. He did not leave me until he said, 'What did you do with the one thousand?' I said, 'I returned it to its owner.' He said to me, 'You have done well.' He said to me, 'Shall I advise you?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'Upon you is truthfulness in speech and repayment of the trust; you will share the people in their wealth like this,' and he joined his fingers together. He said, 'So I memorized that from him, and I attained three hundred thousand dirhams.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who had wealth for his son, and the father had a need for it. He said: 'The father may eat from it. As for the mother, she may not eat from it except as a loan upon herself.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the man who eats from the wealth of his son. He said: 'No, except if he is compelled to it, so he may eat from it with reasonableness, and it is not suitable for the son to take anything from the wealth of his father except if his father permits him.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man: 'You and your wealth are for your father.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And I do not like for him to take from the wealth of his son except what he is in need of, from what is necessary. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not love corruption/mischief.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Abdul Kareem, from Ibn Abu Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has wealth for his son, and he wishes to take from it, he said: 'Let him take. If his mother is alive, I do not like that she takes anything from it except as a loan upon herself.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who is in need of his son's wealth. He said: 'He may eat from it whatever he wishes, without extravagance.' And he said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): The son does not take anything from his father's wealth except by his permission, and the father takes from his son's wealth whatever he wishes, and it is permissible for him to have relations with his son's slave girl if the son has not already had relations with her.' And he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man: 'You and your wealth are for your father.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'ala, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for a man from the wealth of his son?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His subsistence without extravagance, when he is in need of it.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I said to him, 'What about the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to the man who came to him and presented his father, so he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You and your wealth are for your father'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, he came with his father to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he said, 'O Messenger of Allah! This is my father, and he has been unjust to me regarding my inheritance from my mother.' So the father informed him that he had spent it upon him and upon himself. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You and your wealth are for your father', and there was not anything with the man; would the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) have withheld the father for the sake of the son?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom,' a woman handed over some wealth from her own wealth to her husband for him to work with, and said to him when she handed it over to him: 'Spend from it. If an event occurs with you [i.e., you die], whatever you have spent from it is permissible and good. If an event occurs with me [i.e., I die], whatever you have spent from it, then it is permissible and good.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat the question to me, O Sa'id.' So when I went to repeat the question to him, the owner of the matter intervened, and he was present with me, so he repeated to him (peace be upon him) similar to that. When he finished, he (peace be upon him) pointed with his finger to the owner of the question and said: 'O you! If you know that she delegated that to you, between you and her and between Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then it is permissible and good,' three times. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Majestic is His Name, says in His Book: "But if they of themselves be pleased to give up to you a portion of it, then eat it with enjoyment and with wholesome result."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about what is permissible for the woman to give in charity from her husband's household wealth without his permission. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The food (or provisions served to guests).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, all from al-Washa', from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The people in the early times, whenever they found something and took it, it would be withheld (from them); they would not be able to take a step until they threw it back, so its seeker would come after them and take it. And indeed, the people have become audacious in what is more than that, and it beyond that, and it will return to being as it was.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: With regards to the found property, he should raise it (look for its owner) for a year, then it would be like the rest of his own wealth.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man found one Dinar in his house.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Does anyone else enter his house?' I said, 'Yes, many.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is found property (Luqatah).' I said, 'And a man who finds one Dinar in his own box?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Does anyone else put his hand in his box, or does anyone else place something in it?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So it is for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the found property (luqatah). He said: 'It should be announced for a year, whether it is little or much.' He said: 'And whatever is less than a dirham, it should not be announced.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboob, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a house in which silver (coinage) is found, so he said: If it is inhabited and its people are in it, then it is for them; and if it is ruined and its people have evacuated from it, then the one who found the wealth is more rightful for it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Sa'id ibn Amr al-Ju'fi, who said: I went out to Mecca while I was among the people in the most difficult financial condition, so I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). When I left his presence, I found a bag at his door containing seven hundred dinars. I returned to him immediately and informed him. He said: 'O Sa'id, fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and present it among the gatherings,' and I hoped that he would allow me to keep it. So I went out gloomy, and I came to Mina and secluded myself from the people, searching until I reached the standing place (Mawqif). I lodged in a room away from the people. Then I said, 'Who recognizes the bag?' The first voice I heard was from a man above me saying, 'I am the owner of the bag.' I said to myself, 'You, so be it.' I asked, 'What is the mark of the bag?' He informed me of its mark, so I handed it over to him. He said: So he went aside and counted them, and the dinars were in their original state. Then he counted seventy dinars from them and said, 'Take these; they are permissible, better than seven hundred prohibited ones.' So I took them. Then I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him of how I secluded myself and what I did. He said: 'Indeed, when you complained to me, we ordered thirty dinars for you. O Maid, bring them!' So I took them, and I was among my people in the best financial condition.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Al-Hajj, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said, 'I have acquired some wealth, and I feared for my soul regarding it. If I were to find its owner, I would hand it over to him and be rid of it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'By Allah, if you were to find him, would you hand it over to him?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Then it is I, by Allah, there is no other owner for it but me.' He said, 'So he made him swear an oath that he would hand it over to whomever he commanded him to.' So he swore an oath. He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go and distribute it among your brethren, and for you is security from what you feared from it.' He said, 'So I distributed it among my brethren.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, from Abu al-A'ala, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man found some wealth, so he announced it (as found property). When a year passed, he bought a servant with it. The seeker of the wealth came and found that the maid who had been bought with the dirhams was his daughter. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not entitled to take except his dirhams, and the daughter is not for him. Rather, he has only the principal of his wealth, and indeed his daughter was a slave owned by people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Ja'far who said: I wrote to the man (Imam asws), asking him asws about a man who bought a camel or a cow for the sacrifice. So when he slaughtered it, he found in its inside a packet in which were dirhams or dinars or a jewel. For whom would that be? So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'Introduce it to the seller, so if he does not recognize it, then the thing is for you. May Allah grant you sustenance with it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever finds something, it is for him; so let him enjoy it until its seeker comes to him. So when its seeker comes, he should return it to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the found property, so he said: Do not pick it up. But if you are tested by it (i.e., you pick it up), then announce it for a year. If its seeker comes, then return it; otherwise, place it in the display of your wealth, flowing upon it whatever you flow upon your own wealth, until a seeker comes for it. If no seeker comes for it, then bequeath it in your will.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, I found a sheep.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I found a camel.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'With it are its shoes and its watering pouch. Its shoes are its hooves and its watering pouch is its hump, so do not bother it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever finds wealth or a camel in a wilderness from the earth which was exhausted and its owner had abandoned from what he did not pursue it, so someone else finds it and stands to look after it and spends expenditure until he revives it from the exhaustion and from the death, so it is for him, and there is no way for him (the previous owner) upon it. But rather it is like the ownerless thing.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the found staff, and the splinters, and the pegs, and the ropes, and the harnesses, and the likes of it. He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'There are no seekers for these'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asam, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say regarding the animal: when its owners release it, or if they are unable to provide its fodder or expenses, then it belongs to the one who revives it. He (peace be upon him) said: And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who left his animal in a pasture, saying: If he left it in a place with fodder, water, and security, then it is for him; he may take it whenever he wishes. But if he left it in a place without fodder and without water, then it belongs to the one who revives it.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahboub from Safwan al-Jammal, that he heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever finds a stray animal and does not announce its finding, then it is found in his possession, then it belongs to its owner, and a similar share is from the wealth of the one who concealed it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazid who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man said: I shall surely sit in my house, and I shall pray, and I shall fast, and I shall worship my Lord; as for my livelihood, it shall come to me.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is one of the three whose supplications are not answered for them.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do you think that if a man were to enter his house and lock his door, anything would fall upon him from the sky?

We were seated in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when al-A'la ibn Kamil came and sat in front of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: Supplicate to Allah that He may provide me [sustenance] in ease. So he (peace be upon him) said: I will not supplicate for you. Seek, just as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) inquired about a man while I was in his presence, so it was said to him: 'Poverty has afflicted him.' He said: 'So what is he doing today?'
