It was said: 'He is at home worshipping his Lord.' He said: 'So from where is his livelihood?' It was said: 'From one of his brothers (in faith).' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By God! The one who provides his livelihood is a more devoted worshiper than he.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever seeks livelihood in this world in order to be self-sufficient from people, to expand (sustenance) upon his family, and to show kindness to his neighbor, will meet God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, and his face will be like the moon on the night of the full moon.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Khalid al-Kufi, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Worship has seventy parts, the most superior of which is seeking the lawful.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Minqari, from Hisham al-Saydalani who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hisham! Even if you see the two battle lines having met, do not abandon seeking your livelihood on that day.'

Ahmad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Safwan, from Khalid ibn Najih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Convey the greeting of peace to those of your companions whom you meet, and say to them that so-and-so, son of so-and-so, sends you greetings of peace. And say to them: Adhere to taqwa (God-consciousness) of God — Mighty and Majestic — and what can be attained through it of what is with God. I swear by God, I do not command you except with what we command our own selves. So adhere to diligence and striving. And when you have performed the morning prayer and dispersed, rise early in seeking your livelihood, and seek the permissible, for God — Mighty and Majestic — will sustain you and assist you in it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbihi who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Even if you think, or it reaches you, that this matter will occur tomorrow, do not abandon seeking livelihood; and if you are able to not be a burden [on others], then do so.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Al-'Ala', who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Is one of you unable to be like the ant? For the ant drags (sustenance) to its hole.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masrouq, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Bazi'e, from Ahmad ibn A'aiz, from Kuleyb Al-Saydawi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for me regarding livelihood, for my affairs have worsened upon me.' So he answered quickly, 'Go out and seek.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Gifts are of three types: a gift of reward, a gift of conciliation, and a gift for the sake of Allah, Exalted and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a large estate, and when it is the day of al-Mihrjan or al-Nayrouz, they gift him something; they are not doing so to draw near to him with that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Are they not among the praying ones?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Then let him accept their gift and reciprocate, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If a shoulder (cut of meat) were gifted to me, I would accept it, and that was from the religion; and if a disbeliever or a hypocrite were to gift me a wasq, I would not accept it, and that was from the religion. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refused to me the scum of the polytheists and the hypocrites, and their food.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Abu Jareer al-Qummi, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who gives a gift to his near relative, intending the reward, and he is a ruler (Sultan). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and for maintaining kinship ties, then it is permissible, and for him is that he takes it when it is for the reward.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Qummi said to him, 'We have an estate wherein are houses of fire, the Magians gift to it cows, sheep, and dirhams. So is it permissible for the lords of the town to take that? And for the houses of their fire, there are attendants who stand over it.' He said, 'Let the master of the town take it. There is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): A poor man gifts me a gift, exposing himself to what is in my presence, so I take it and do not give him anything. Is it permissible for me? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, it is permissible for you, but do not leave out giving him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to accept the gift but did not accept the charity, and he would say: 'Exchange gifts, for the gift removes resentment and clears out the grudges of enmity and malice.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the honor of a man for his Muslim brother is that he accepts his gift and reciprocates with what he has, and he does not burden him with anything.'
And by his chain, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: If an animal limb is gifted to me, I would accept it.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: The ones sitting around the man are participants in the gift.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, raising it, he said: When a gift of food is given to a man, and there are people with him, they are his partners in it, the fruit and other such items.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'To gift my Muslim brother a gift that benefits him is more beloved to me than to give in charity an equivalent amount.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi, from Al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Give gifts with nabiq, so that cordiality and loyalty may live.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Exchange gifts, you will love one another; exchange gifts, for they remove enmity.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Exchange gifts, you will find affection. Exchange gifts, for indeed it removes malice.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One dirham of interest (usury) is more grievous than seventy adulteries, all of which are with those of close kin (incestuous).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The eater of usury (interest), the one who feeds it, its scribe, and its witness are equal.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who consumes usury (riba), while he believes it is prohibited for him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not harm him until he consumes it deliberately. So when he consumes it deliberately, he is in the status which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has spoken of.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abu al-Maghra, from al-Halbi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Every interest (riba) that people consumed due to ignorance, then repented, it is accepted from them if their repentance is recognized from them.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man inherited wealth from his father and knew that there was interest in that wealth, but it had been mixed in trade with other permissible wealth, then the permissible part is permissible and good, so let him consume it; and if he recognizes something from it that is interest, let him take the capital of his wealth and return the interest.' And whoever man acquired much wealth in which he had increased with interest, and was ignorant of that, then recognized it afterwards, and intended to remove it from what has passed, it is for him, and he should leave it regarding what he resumes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to my father and said: 'I have inherited wealth, and I know that its owner, from whom I inherited it, used to deal in riba (usury/interest). I recognize that there is riba within it and I am certain of this. Its permissibility is not pleasing to me due to my state of knowledge regarding it. I have asked the jurists of the people of Iraq and the people of Hijaz, and they said: 'It is not permissible to consume it.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If you know that within it is wealth known to be riba, and you know its owners, then take the principal of your wealth and return what is besides that. And if it is mixed up, then consume it with pleasure and wholesomeness, for the wealth is yours. Avoid what the owner used to do, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had abolished what had passed of the riba and prohibited for them what remained.' Therefore, whoever is ignorant of it, his ignorance grants him leeway until he recognizes it. So when he recognizes its prohibition, it becomes prohibited for him, and the punishment becomes obligatory upon him regarding it if he indulges in it, just as it is obligatory upon the one who consumes riba.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Usury (riba) is two types: a usury that is eaten and a usury that is not eaten. As for that which is eaten, it is your gift to a man, seeking from him a reward greater than it; that is the usury which is eaten. And it is His Word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever you give as usury, so that it may increase in the property of the people, it will not increase in the Presence of Allah.' And as for that which is not eaten, it is the usury which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade and promised the Fire for.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have seen that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned Riba (usury/interest) in more than one verse and repeated it.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Do you know why that is?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So that people do not refrain from doing good deeds.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited usury (riba) so that people would not refrain from doing good deeds.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Usury (Riba) does not occur except in what is measured by volume or weighed.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr [from Ubayd ibn Zurara], who said: It reached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) concerning a man that he was consuming usury (riba) and he called it 'al-liba' (milk), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enables me [over him], I will strike his neck.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Khashshab from Ibn Baqqah from Mu'adh ibn Thabit from 'Amr ibn Jumay' from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no riba (usury/interest) between a man and his son, and there is no riba between a master and his slave.'

And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no interest (usury) between us and the people who war against us. We can take a thousand Dirhams from them with one Dirham, and we can take from them and we cannot give them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no riba (usury/interest) between a man and his son, and between him and his slave, nor between him and his family. Rather, the riba is in what is between you and what you do not own. I said, 'So regarding the polytheists, is there riba between me and them?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'For they are owned slaves.' So he said, 'You do not own them [exclusively]. Rather, you own them along with others; you and others are equal regarding them. Thus, that which is between you and them is not from that [exclusive ownership category], because your slave is not like your slave [who is exclusively yours] and the slave of another [who is jointly owned].'
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Trade increases in the intellect.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad al-Za'farani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever seeks trade becomes independent of people. I said, 'And even if he is the breadwinner?' He said, 'And even if he is the breadwinner. Indeed, nine-tenths of livelihood are in trade.'

Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Jahm, from Fuzayl al-Awr, who said: I witnessed Mu'adh ibn Kathir, and he said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have become affluent, so I will leave trade.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you do, your intellect will diminish,' or something similar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ismail, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What work do you engage in?' I said, 'I do not engage in any work these days.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Like that, your wealth will go away,' and it became difficult upon him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Faraj al-Qummi, from Mu'adh, the seller of silks, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Mu'adh! Have you become weak in trade, or have you become indifferent to it?' I said, 'I have not become weak in it, nor have I become indifferent to it.' He said: 'So what is the matter with you?' I said, 'We were awaiting a matter, and that was when Al-Walid was killed, and I had much wealth, and it was in my hand, and there was nothing for anyone upon me, and I did not see myself consuming it all until I die.' So he said: 'You are leaving it, and leaving it is a depletion of the intellect. Strive for your dependents, and beware that they should not be the ones striving for you.'

Muhammad and others, from Ahmad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Hisham ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was saying to Musadif: 'Go early to your honour,' meaning the marketplace.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fudayl ibn Abu Qurra, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man, and I was present, so he said: 'What has withheld him from the Hajj?' It was said, 'He left trade and his wealth became scarce.' He said, 'And he was leaning, so he sat upright, then said to them: Do not leave trade, lest you be belittled. Trade, may Allah bless you.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Expose yourselves to trade, for therein is wealth for you from what is in the hands of the people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, the seller of garments, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have considered leaving the marketplace, and in my hand is something (wealth/capital).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then your opinion (or status/standing) will be diminished, and people will not seek your counsel or assistance in anything.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have refrained from trade and withheld from it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And why is that? Is it weakness on your part? That is how your wealth goes away. Do not refrain from trade, and seek from the Grace of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, and he was the in-law of Bureyd al-Ijaly, who said: Bureyd said to Muhammad, 'Ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) for me about something I intend to do. Indeed, people have deposits and wealth in my hand, and I am moving about in them, and I have intended to withdraw from the world and to give to each one with a right his right.' He said, so Muhammad asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that and informed him of the story and said, 'What do you see for him?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Does he begin with himself by paying the debt? No! But he should take and give, upon Allah, Majestic is His Name.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Uqba, who said: Abu al-Khattab, before he was spoiled, used to carry the questions to our companions and return with their answers. He reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Buy, even if it is expensive, for sustenance descends with the purchase.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu al-Jaroud, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: I heard Amir al-Mu-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) saying upon the pulpit: 'O group of businessmen! Jurisprudence, then the business! Jurisprudence, then the business! Jurisprudence, then the business! By Allah, usury in this community is more hidden than the creeping of an ant on a dark rock. Mix your oaths with truthfulness. The merchant who is immoral is in the Fire, except for the one who takes the right and gives the right.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever sells and buys, let him preserve five characteristics, or else he should neither buy nor sell: usury, swearing oaths, concealing defects, praising [the goods] when he sells, and condemning [the goods] when he buys.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was in Kufa among you; every morning he would leave the palace early and circulate through the markets of Kufa, market by market. With him was a whip on his shoulder, which had two ends and was called 'Al-Sabayba'. He would stop at the people of each market and call out: 'O group of merchants! Fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic!' When they heard his voice (peace be upon him), they would throw down what was in their hands, direct their hearts to him, and listen with their ears. He would say (peace be upon him): 'Prioritize seeking Allah's choice (Istikhara), find blessings in ease, draw near to the buyers, adorn yourselves with forbearance, keep away from oaths, avoid lying, turn away from injustice, give justice to the oppressed, do not approach usury, fulfill the measure and the scale, do not deprive people of their goods, and do not wander in the land causing corruption.' He would circulate through all the markets of Kufa, then return and sit for the people.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from some of his family members, who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not grant Hakim ibn Hizam permission to engage in trade until he guaranteed to him the acceptance of returns by the regretful buyer, the respite for the insolvent, and taking the due right in full or in part.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man says to you, 'Buy for me', do not give him from what is with you, even if that which is with you is better than it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Generosity (or discounting) is from the gains (profit). He said this to a man whom he was advising, and with him was a commodity he wanted to sell.'

And by his chain, it was said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed by a slave girl who had bought meat from a butcher, and she was saying, 'Increase it for me', so the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Increase it for her, for it is greater for the blessings.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man says to another man, “Come, I will sell to you with a good deal,” the profit is prohibited for him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from some of our companions from Aban from Aamir ibn Juza'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who has a sale (item) and sets a known fixed price: whoever remains silent from him among those who buy from him, he sells it to him at that price; and whoever bargains with him and refuses to buy from him at that price, he increases the price for him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he increases it for two men or three, there is no problem with that. But as for him doing it with every one who refuses to him and bargains with him, and prevents it from those who did not do that, then I do not like it except that he sells it with one price (for everyone).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The owner of the commodity is more rightful to bargaining.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Asbaat, raising it (to the Prophet), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade bargaining during the time between the emergence of the dawn and the emergence of the sun.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Rahman ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: I was informed from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he disliked two types of sales: 'Itrah wa Khudh' (drop and take) without turning over (checking), and buying what has not been seen.
Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Deliberate cheating (of the gullible) is ill-gotten gain (suh't).
From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Cheating the Believer is Prohibited.

Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq, from Haroun ibn Hamza, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whichever servant settles (accepts returned goods) regarding his sale, Allah the Exalted would settle his mistakes on the Day of Judgement.

Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, from Is'haq ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Daghshi, who said: I was at the door of Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, so the slave of Shihab came out and said, 'I want to ask Hashim al-Saydani about the hadith of the merchandise and the goods.' He said, 'So I went to Hashim and asked him about the hadith. He said, 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the merchandise and the goods, so he said: Yes, there is none who has merchandise or goods with him except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordains one who will profit him. So if he accepts (the buyer), or else He directs it to another, and that is because he rejected upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, raised the hadith, saying: Abu Umamah, a companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), was saying: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Four [qualities] in which if one is found, his earnings are good: when he buys, he does not fault [the goods]; and when he sells, he does not praise [them excessively]; and he does not conceal defects; and in between that, he does not swear oaths.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, who said: He said: I was informed that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) disliked two types of sales: 'Atkh khudh' (drop and take) without turning over (the goods to check them), and buying what has not been seen.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashshar, from a man, who raised it (to the Imam). Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Men whom neither merchandise nor selling diverts from the Remembrance of Allah,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are the merchants whom neither business nor selling diverts them from the Remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When the timings of the Prayer enter, they deliver to Allah His Right with regards to it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleyman ibn Salih and Abu Shibl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The profit a believer makes on a believer (in a small transaction) is considered like interest (riba), except if he buys for more than one hundred dirhams, so profit upon it for your daily sustenance, or if he buys it for trade, so make a profit upon them and be kind to them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The one who trades without knowledge plunges into usury, then plunges into it (again/repeatedly)'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: Let not sit in the marketplace except the one who comprehends buying and selling'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The market of the Muslims is like their mosque, so whoever precedes to a place is more rightful to it until the night,' and he (peace be upon him) did not charge rent upon the rooms of the marketplace.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The market of the Muslims is like their Masjid, meaning when one precedes to the market, it is for him like the Masjid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan, from his father, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Al-Fazl! Is there any place for you whereby you can sit in and do business with the people?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is none from a Believing man who goes or comes to his gathering or his marketplace, so he is saying when he places his foot in the marketplace, "O Allah! I ask You from its goodness and the goodness of its people", except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would allocate with him one (Angel) who would protect him, and guard him until he returns to his house.' So he (the Angel) would be saying to him: 'I have rescued you from its evil and the evil of its people on this day of yours by the Permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and I have graced its goodness and the goodness of its people to you in this day of yours'. So when he sits in his seat, he says when he sits, "I testify that there is no god except for Allah, One, not having any associates for Him, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Rasool. O Allah! I ask You from Your Grace, Permissible, good, and I seek Refuge with You from being unjust and suffering injustice; and I seek Refuge with You from loss-making deals and false oaths'. So when he says that, the Angel who is Allocated with him, says to him: 'Receive glad tidings! There is no one in your market which is more ampler than you in a share. The good has been hastened and the evil has been obliterated from you, and you will be receiving what Allah has Apportioned for you with ampleness, Permissible, good, with Blessings therein'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter your marketplace, say: 'O Allah, I ask You for its goodness and the goodness of its people, and I seek Refuge with You from its evil and the evil of its people. O Allah, I seek Refuge with You from being unjust or suffering injustice, or rebelling or being rebelled against, or exceeding or being exceeded against. O Allah, I seek Refuge with You from the evil of Iblis and his army, and the evil of the wicked ones of the Arabs and the non-Arabs. Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no god except Him, upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Magnificent Throne.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you buy something from goods or otherwise, exclaim Takbeer, then say: 'O Allah, I have bought it seeking from Your Grace, so send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, make for me therein a grace. O Allah, I have bought it seeking from Your sustenance, so make for me therein sustenance.' Then repeat each one three times.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Huzayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you buy a slave girl, say: 'O Allah, I consult You and seek Your choice of goodness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you intend to buy something, say: 'O Living, O Guardian, O Eternal, O Kind, O Merciful! I ask You by Your Honour and Your Power and what Your Knowledge encompasses, that You apportion for me from the trade today that which has the greatest sustenance, the widest grace, and the best outcome, for there is no goodness in that which has no good outcome.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you buy an animal or a head (slave), say: 'O Allah, enable for me that it has the longest life, the most benefit, and the best outcome.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you buy an animal, say: 'O Allah, if it is great in blessings, abundant in benefit, and of auspicious forelock, then facilitate its purchase for me; and if it is otherwise, then turn me away from it to that which is better for me. Indeed, You know and I do not know, and You are able and I am not able, and You are the Knower of the unseen.' Say this three times.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from his father who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not buy from a corrupter (one who mixes/adulterates goods), for there is no blessing in his transaction.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'There are people among us from the Kurds, and they do not cease coming with trade, so we intermingle with them and buy from them.' He said, 'O Abu al-Rabi', do not intermingle with them, for the Kurds are a tribe from the tribes of the Jinn. Allah has uncovered the veil from them, so do not intermingle with them.'

Ahmad ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah from one of his companions from Ali ibn Asbaat from Husayn ibn Kharajat from Maysar ibn Abdul Aziz who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not deal with people who have defects, for they are the most unjust of things.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not intermingle and do not have dealings except with those who have grown up in goodness.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Be cautious of having dealings with the people with deformities, for they are the most unjust ones'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Al-Husayn ibn Mayyah, from Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Beware of inter-mingling with the lowly people (rif-raff), for the lowly do not lead to the goodness.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Fazl al-Nawfali, from Ibn Abu Yahya al-Razi, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not mix with, nor have dealings with, anyone except the one who grew up in goodness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Husayn ibn Kharjah, from Maysar ibn Abdul Aziz, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not have dealings with those who have deformities, for they are the most unjust of things.'

A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Husayn ibn Kharijah, from Muyassir ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not form contracts/deal with people who have a chronic ailment/disability, for they are the most unjust of things.'

Sadyr said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is incumbent upon the man in seeking livelihood? He said: When you open your door and spread out your merchandise, you have fulfilled what is upon you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from the one who mentioned him, from al-Tayyar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Which thing do you deal in? Which thing do you make?' So I said, 'I am not involved in anything.' He said: 'Then take a place, sweep its yard, sprinkle water on it, and spread out your merchandise therein. When you do that, you will have fulfilled what is obligated upon you.' He (the narrator) said: 'I went and did it, and I was granted provision.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hammad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The fulfilment [of the transaction] does not occur until the scale inclines [tilts in favour of the buyer].

From him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Murazim, from a man, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: The one who takes the scale in his hand, so he intends that he take a full measure for himself, does not take except for an overweighing (measure); and the one who gives, so he intends that he would give equal, does not give except for a deficient (measure).

From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Ubayd ibn Ishaq who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I am an owner of palm trees, so inform me of a limit to which I should adhere regarding it in terms of full measurement.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Intend full measurement. So if deficiency comes to you by hand, while you have intended full measurement, you are from the people of full measurement; and if you intend deficiency, then you give full measurement, you are from the people of deficiency.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musanna al-Hannat, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man intends to give the full measure, but when he measures, he is not good at measuring.' He said, 'So what do those around him say?' I said, 'They say, He does not give the full measure. He said, 'This one, it is not befitting for him that he measures.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: So that the full measurement is not achieved until it tilts (in favor of the buyer).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He is not from us the one who cheats us.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from a man from his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to him selling flour, so he said: 'Beware of cheating (ghish), for whoever cheats will be cheated in his wealth. And if he has no wealth, he will be cheated in his family.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade mixing milk with water for the purpose of selling.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: I was selling the sabiriyya (fabric) in the shade, so Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) passed by me and said to me: 'O Hisham! Indeed, selling in the shade is cheating (ghishsh), and indeed, cheating is not permissible.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Jameela, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by food in the market of Medina, so he said to its owner: 'I do not see your food except as good,' and he asked him about its price. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him that he should insert his hands into the food, so he did, and he brought out food that had perished. So he said to its owner: 'I do not see you except as having gathered betrayal and cheating for the Muslims.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Abu Ja'far al-Fazari, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) called a slave of his named Musadif and gave him one thousand dinars, and said to him: 'Equip yourself until you go out to Egypt, for my dependents have multiplied.' He said: So he equipped himself with goods and went out with the merchants to Egypt. When they approached Egypt, a caravan coming out of Egypt met them. They asked them about the goods they had, what its condition was in the city, and the goods were general commodities. They informed them that there was nothing of it available in Egypt. So they swore oaths and made a contract that they would not sell their goods for less than a profit of one dinar per dinar. When they had collected their wealth and returned to the city, Musadif came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with him were two bags, in each of which was one thousand dinars. He said: 'May I be your ransom, this is the capital, and this other is profit.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This profit is large, but what did you do with the goods?' So he narrated to him how they had acted and how they had sworn oaths. He said: 'Glory be to Allah! You swear oaths against a group of Muslims that you will not sell to them except for a profit of a dinar per dinar.' Then he took one of the bags and said: 'This is my capital, and we have no need for this profit.' Then he said: 'O Musadif! A dispute of swords is easier than seeking the permissible (halal).'

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Hamza, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) stood at the door of Ibn Abu Mueet, and the camels used to stand therein, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'O group of middlemen! Lessen the oaths, for (although) these are more profitable for the price, (but) are (eventually) destructive for the profits'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Three (types of people) Allah the Exalted will not look at them on the Day of Judgement; one of them is a man who takes Allah as a commodity. He neither buys except with an oath, and he does not sell except with an oath.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Za'lani, from Abu Ismail, raising it from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), that he (peace be upon him) was saying: 'Beware of swearing the oath, for it frees up the price and it obliterates the Blessings'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Al-Ghufari, from Al-Qasim ibn Ishaq, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A sign of the Pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, among His creatures is the justice of their rulers, and the cheapness of their prices; and a sign of the Anger of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, upon His creatures is the inequity of their rulers, and the expensiveness of their prices.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed Allah, the Majestic and Mighty, has assigned an Angel to regulate the price, so it will not become high due to scarcity, nor become low due to abundance.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hajjal, from one of his companions, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, appointed an Angel over the price (of goods), managing it by His Command.
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned an Angel to manage the prices.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Sa'd, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the goods came into possession of Yusuf ibn Yaqub (peace be upon them), he stored the food in houses and ordered one of his agents, so he would say, 'Sell for such and such,' and the price was fixed. So when he knew that it had increased during that day, he disliked that the high price (inflation) pass over his tongue, so he said to him, 'Go and sell,' but did not name a specific price for him. So the agent went not far, then returned to him. So he said to him, 'Go and sell,' and he disliked that the high price pass over his tongue. So the agent went, and the first of those who measured came. So when it reached less than what was there yesterday by a measure, the buyer said, 'Enough for you! I only wanted such and such.' So the agent knew that he had inflated (by giving less) by a measure. Then another came to him and said to him, 'Measure out for me.' So he measured. So when it reached less than that which he had measured for the first one by a measure, the buyer said to him, 'Enough for you! I only wanted such and such.' So the agent knew that he had inflated by a measure, until it became one for one.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Hafs ibn Umar, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: High prices worsen the manners, remove the trustworthiness, and wear out the magnanimity of the Muslim.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-hukrah (monopolization/hoarding for price control) is not [restricted/defined] except in wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and butter.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Food supplies ran out in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Muslims came to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! The food has run out and there remains nothing of it except with so-and-so, so order him to sell it to the people.' He (peace be upon him) praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, 'O so-and-so! The Muslims have mentioned that the food has run out except for a small amount with you, so bring it out and sell it as you wish, and do not withhold it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Monopolizing (al-hukrah) is when one buys food that is not available in the city except from him, so he hoards it. So if there is food in the city, or if others are selling it, there is no problem with seeking a premium price for his goods. He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about oil, so he said: If it is with others besides you, there is no problem with withholding it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu al-Fadl Salim al-Hannat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is your trade?' I said, 'I am a wheat merchant (Hannat). Sometimes I arrive when there is a market surplus (nafaq), and sometimes I arrive when there is a market slump (kasad), so I withhold it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what do those in front of you say about it?' I said, 'They say,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who hoards food and waits for it [to raise prices]. Is that permissible? He said: If the food is abundant, sufficient for the people, then there is no problem with it; and if the food is scarce, not sufficient for the people, then it is disliked that he hoards the food and leaves the people with no food.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The bringer (of the food) is Graced with sustenance, and the monopoliser is an accursed'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Monopolizing (hoarding) during abundance is for forty days, and during hardship and affliction is for three days. So whatever exceeds forty days during abundance, its owner is accursed, and whatever exceeds three days during scarcity, its owner is accursed.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: High prices and drought struck the people of Medina, to the extent that the affluent man would mix wheat with barley and eat it, and buy only part of the food (required). There was good quality food with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) which he had bought at the beginning of the year. So he said to one of his adherents: 'Buy some barley for us so I can mix it with this food, or sell it, for we dislike that we should eat good quality food while the people eat the perished (food).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Jahm ibn Abi Jahma, from Mu'tab, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me, while prices had increased in Medina: 'How much food do we have?' I said, 'We have enough for many months.' He said, 'Take it out and sell it.' He said, 'I said to him, 'But there is no food in Medina.' He said, 'Sell it.' So when I had sold it, he said, 'Buy (food) along with the people day after day.' And he said, 'O Mu'tab! Make the daily provision for my dependents half barley and half wheat, for Allah knows that I am able to feed them wheat of its own kind, but I love that Allah should see me that I have managed the livelihood in a good way.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Mu'ttab, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to order us, whenever the fruit became ripe/harvested, to take it out and sell it, and buy [new fruit] with the Muslims, on a day-to-day basis.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nasr ibn Is'haq al-Kufi, from Abbad ibn Habeeb, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Buying wheat negates poverty, and buying flour initiates poverty, and buying bread is annihilation (of wealth).' He said: I said to him, 'May Allah keep you alive, so what about the one who is unable to buy wheat?' He said: 'That is for the one who is able but does not do it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Mundhir al-Zabbal, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you have a dirham, buy wheat with it, for the loss (of value) is in the flour.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Al-Sabbah! Buying the flour is a disgrace, and buying the wheat is an honour, and buying the bread is poverty. We seek Refuge with Allah from the poverty.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A group of people complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) about the rapid depletion of their food, so he said: 'Do you measure or heap?' They said: 'We heap, O Messenger of Allah' — meaning the rough estimate. He said: 'Measure and do not heap, for it is greater for the blessings.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Measure your food, for indeed the blessing is in the measured food.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma'a, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar! When the maid intends to prepare the food, instruct her to measure it, for indeed the blessing is in what is measured.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: A man complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about the profession (of trading), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look at the saleable items, buy them, then sell them. So whatever you profit from, hold to it (continue with it).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man looks into a business and sees nothing in it (no profit), let him turn to another.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Bashir al-Nabbal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you are granted success in something, persist in it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from 'Urwa ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let not one of you meet the caravan of goods coming from outside the city [to buy from them before the others], and let not one who is present in the city sell to one who is in the countryside [by sending goods ahead], and the Muslims are partners in providing sustenance for one another.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Minhal al-Qassab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Do not receive (goods) before others (are able to), and do not buy what is received (before others), and do not eat from it.
Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah bin Yahya al-Kahili, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said: I said to him, 'What is the limit of al-talaaqee?' He said, 'Rawha.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibnman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not receive [goods] outside the city, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the receiving [of goods outside the city].' I said: 'And what is the limit of the receiving?' He said: 'What is less than a Gadwa or a Rawha.' I said: 'And how much is the Gadwa and the Rawha?' He said: 'Four Farsakhs.' Ibn Abi Umeyr said: 'And what is above that, so it is not (classified as) receiving [outside the city].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said during the Farewell Hajj: 'Indeed! The Trustworthy Spirit (Jibrail) has inspired into my heart that no soul will die until it has completed its ordained provision. Therefore, fear God Almighty and Majestic, and be upright in seeking; and do not let the delay of any provision lead you to seek it through any means of disobedience to God. For God, Blessed and Exalted, has distributed provisions among His creation as lawful, and He has not distributed them as unlawful. So whoever fears God Almighty and Majestic and is patient, God will bring him his provision through its lawful means; and whoever tears down the veil of concealment and acts hastily and takes it through other than its lawful means, an equivalent amount will be deducted from his lawful provision, and he will be held to account for it on the Day of Resurrection.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no soul except that God, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed for it its sustenance as permissible, coming to it in good health; and He has also presented to it the forbidden from another direction. So if it takes anything from the forbidden, He deducts it from the permissible that He had decreed for it; and with God, beyond these two, there is abundant grace. And that is His word, Mighty and Majestic: 'And ask God from His grace.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O you people! The Holy Spirit has breathed into my heart that no soul shall die until it has fully received its sustenance, even if it is delayed. Therefore, fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and be proper in your seeking. And do not let the delay of anything in the Presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, drive you to seek it through disobedience of Allah, for indeed what is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be attained except through obedience.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadija, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Even if the servant were inside a rock, God would bring him his sustenance — so be moderate in your seeking.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn Abi Ziyad, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — created the creatures and created their sustenance along with them, permissible and wholesome. So whoever takes anything from it through forbidden means, a corresponding amount is deducted from that permissible sustenance.'
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: How many a person exhausts himself yet livelihood is scarce for him, and how many a moderate seeker is assisted by the divine decrees.

The high price of goods was mentioned in the presence of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: 'What concern of mine is its expensiveness? If it is expensive, it is upon Him (God); and if it is cheap, it is upon Him (God).'

From him, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Let your seeking of livelihood be above the earning of the squanderer and below the seeking of the greedy one who is pleased with his world and reliant upon it; but rather, descend yourself from that to the station of the equitable and self-restrained one. Raise yourself above the station of the neglectful and the weak, and earn what is inevitable from it. Indeed, those who are given wealth and then are not grateful — there is no wealth for them.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, who raised it (as marfu'), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) frequently used to say: 'Know with certain knowledge that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not made it possible for the servant — even if his striving is intense, his resourcefulness great, and his endurance abundant — to surpass what has been decreed for him in the Wise Remembrance; nor has He prevented the servant, in his weakness and scarcity of means, from reaching what has been named for him in the Wise Remembrance. O people! No one gains even a fraction by his cleverness, and no one loses even a fraction by his foolishness. So the one who knows this and acts accordingly is the most at ease among people in his benefit, and the one who knows this yet abandons it is the most burdened among people in his loss. How often one who is blessed is being gradually lured astray through those blessings, and how often one who appears deceived among the people is actually being cared for. So come to your senses, O you who strive, from your striving; restrain your haste; awaken from the slumber of your heedlessness; and reflect upon what has come from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon the tongue of His Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family). And preserve these seven letters, for they are from the words of the People of Wisdom and from the firm decrees of Allah in the Wise Remembrance. That no one should meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with any of these traits — associating partners with Allah in what He has made obligatory upon him; venting rage at the cost of his own destruction; approving of a matter that another commits; seeking to gain favor with a creature by manifesting an innovation in his religion; being pleased that people praise him for what he has not done; the arrogant and conceited; or the one possessing pomp and pride. O people! The predators, their ambition is transgression; the animals, their ambition is their bellies; the women, their ambition is men; and the believers — they are compassionate, fearful, and trembling. May Allah make us and you among them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musalli, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah the Exalted has expanded in the sustenances of the foolish ones, so that the intellectuals may take lesson, and they may know that the world and whatever is in it is not attained by action nor by means.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O people! I have not left out anything that brings you closer to Paradise and distances you from the Fire, except that I have informed you about it. Indeed, the Holy Spirit has breathed into my heart and informed me that no soul shall die until it has completed its sustenance.' Therefore, fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and be diligent in seeking (sustenance), and do not let the delay of something from the sustenance cause you to seek it through disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, what is with Allah, Majestic is His Name, cannot be attained except through obedience to Him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who stipulates a condition opposite to the Book of Allah, it is not valid for him, nor is it valid for the one upon whom it is stipulated, and the Muslims are upon their conditions in what conforms to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The stipulation (of return) regarding animals is three days for the buyer, whether it was stipulated or not. So if the buyer does something new regarding what he bought before the three days, that is acceptance from him, so there is no stipulation. It was said to him, 'And what is the new occurrence?' He said: 'If he touches, or kisses, or looks at it in a way that was prohibited to him before the purchase.'

Ibn Mahboub from Ibn Sinan said, I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who buys an animal or a slave and stipulates [a period] for a day or two days, so the slave or the animal dies, or an event occurs with him, upon whom is the guarantee of that? He said: Upon the seller until the stipulation expires for three days, and the sold item becomes for the buyer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The two parties in a transaction have the option (to cancel) until they separate, and the owner of the animal has three days.' I said: 'A man buys goods from another man, then leaves them with him and says, 'Bring us the price.'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he comes within the time between then and three days, otherwise there is no sale for him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The two parties in a sale have the option [to cancel] until they separate, and the owner of the animal has the option for three days.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel, from Fazeyl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the stipulation (option of return) in animals?' He said, 'Up to three days for the buyer.' I said, 'So what is the stipulation regarding other than animals?' He said, 'The two parties are with the choice as long as they have not separated. So when they separate, there is no choice after their agreement from both of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Any man who buys from a man a sale, they both have the option (of rescinding) until they separate. So when they separate, the sale becomes binding.' He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father bought a land called Al-Urayz, so he purchased it from its owner for dinars. He said to him: I will give you silver (dirhams) with every dinar ten dirhams. So he sold it to him with it. So my father arose, and I followed him, so I said: O father! Why did you arise quickly? He said: I wanted that the sale would become binding.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said: ‘I heard Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) saying: ‘I was sold (something) by a man. So when he had sold it, I arose, walked some steps, then I returned to my seat, in order for the sale to become binding when we separated’.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a maid-servant with a stipulation (of return/choice) from a man for a day or two days, so she died while with him, and the price had been paid. Upon whom would the responsibility (for the price) be? He said: There is no responsibility upon the one who bought until he completes his stipulated period.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said, 'A man buys goods from another man, then leaves them with him, saying, "(Keep it) until I come to you with its price.'" He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he brings its price within the period between it and three days, (the sale stands); otherwise, there is no sale for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who bought goods from a man and made the sale binding, except that he left the goods with the seller and did not take possession of it, saying, 'I will come to you tomorrow, God willing.' Then the goods were stolen. Whose wealth would that be? He said: 'From the wealth of the owner of the goods, which are in his house, until the goods are taken possession of and removed from his house. So when they are removed from his house, the buyer is liable for their value until he returns their money to him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The warranty period for the sale of slaves is three days if there is a defect or leprosy or something similar, and its warranty is one year for insanity; so whatever is after the year is not valid.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id ibn Yasar who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We mix with people from As-Sawad and others, so we sell to them and profit upon them with ten percent, twelve percent, and ten percent to thirteen percent, and we delay that between us and them for a year and similar to it. And the man writes for us upon his house or his land with that wealth which contains the surplus that we took from him as a purchase (security), and he has sold and taken the price from him. So we await him: if he comes with the wealth to a set time between us and him, we will return the purchase (security) to him. But if the time comes and he does not bring us the dirhams, then it is for us. So what do you see regarding that purchase (security)? He said: I see that it is for you if he does not do it, and if he comes with the wealth at the time, then return it to him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, or someone else, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah or Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the man who buys the thing which spoils during its day, and he leaves it until he comes with the price. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he comes with the price between it and the night, then [the sale stands], otherwise, there is no sale for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said: I bought a loader, so I gave part of its price and left it with its owner. Then I was detained for a few days, then I came to the seller of the loader to take it, so he said, 'I have sold it.' So I laughed, then I said, 'No, by Allah, I will not let you go, or I will seek judgment against you.' So he said to me, 'Would you be pleased with Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash?' I said, 'Yes.' So we went to him and related our story to him. So Abu Bakr said, 'By whose words do you like that I judge between the two of you, by the words of your companion or someone else?' He said, 'I said, by the words of my companion.' He said, 'I heard him saying: Whoever buys something and brings the price within what is between it and three days, otherwise there is no sale for him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bought a sheep, kept it for three days, then returned it: He (peace be upon him) said: 'If during those three days he drank its milk, he should return it along with three amdad (handfuls of grain); and if there was no milk for it, there is nothing upon him.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who sells an item, so the buyer says, 'It is for such and such,' being less than what the seller said. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The word is the word of the seller along with his oath, when the item remains standing in its essence.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the two merchants are truthful, blessings are bestowed upon them. And when they lie and betray, no blessings are bestowed upon them. And they both have the option (to cancel the deal) as long as they have not separated. So if they differ, the word is the word of the owner of the goods, or they both leave it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about buying palm trees, vineyards, and fruits for three years or four years. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' They say: 'If it does not produce in this year, it will produce in the next. And if you buy it in one year, do not buy it until it ripens. So if you buy it for three years before it ripens, there is no problem.' And he (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who buys a named fruit crop from a land, but all the fruit of that land perishes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They disputed regarding that to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). They would mention that dispute. When he saw that they did not cease the dispute, he forbade them from that sale until the fruit ripens, and he did not prohibit it absolutely, but he did that because of their dispute.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to sell the palm tree when it has borne fruit?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Its sale is permissible until it is in splendour.' I said, 'And what is the splendour? May I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When it turns red and yellow, and similar to that.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rib'i who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have a palm grove in Basra, so I sell it, and I name the price, and I exclude the kurra (a unit of measurement) of dates, or more, or a cluster of dates.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the sale for two years?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, that is a great matter among us.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'As for you, if you are saying that, then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had permitted that, but they were unjust to each other, so he (peace be upon him) said, 'The fruit is not sold until its goodness appears.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a wall contains different fruits, and some of them have ripened, there is no problem with selling them all together.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Ismail ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about selling the fruit before it is ripe, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is such that in that land, selling it is [like selling] a crop which has ripened, then selling all of that is permissible.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I give the man twenty dinars for his fruit, on the condition that I say to him: When your fruit is established for any amount, it is mine for that price. If you are pleased, I will take it, and if you dislike, I will leave it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'You have no leeway to give him [the money] and not stipulate anything.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, he does not name a specific amount, and Allah knows that is from his intention.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is not correct if that is from his intention.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who said to another, 'Sell to me the fruit of your palm tree, this one in which there is, for two qafizs of dates, or less, or more,' naming whatever he wished, so he sold it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Dates and half-ripened dates from one palm tree, there is no problem with it.' But if one mixes the old dates or the half-ripened dates, it is not valid; and raisins and grapes are similar to that.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muawiya ibn Maysara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the palm tree (yield) for two years. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'So the fresh dates (rutab) can be sold for this picking, and such and such a picking after it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) had sold the henna for such and such a harvest.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Yahya ibn Abi al-A'ala who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever sells a palm tree that has been pollinated, the fruit belongs to the seller, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged with that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the buying of fruit, he said: When it is unspoilt, so there is no problem with buying it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying to him: 'I sold a man such and such a palm tree for such and such dirhams, and the palm tree had fruit in it. So the one who bought it from me went and sold it to another man with a profit, and he had not paid me nor had he taken possession from me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that. Did he not guarantee the price to you?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So the profit is for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged that the fruits of the palm tree belong to the one who pollinated it, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the vineyard, when is its sale permissible? He said: When it sets fruit and becomes vines.

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from 'Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from 'Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the vineyard (vines), when is it permissible to sell them? He said: When they form knots and become woody stems.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about buying food that is measured or weighed, is it permissible to buy it without measuring or weighing? He said: If you go to a man regarding food that has already been measured or weighed, and you buy it from him with a profit margin, there is no problem if you buy it and do not measure or weigh it, provided that the first buyer had taken it by measurement or weight. If you say at the time of sale, 'I give you such and such profit in it,' and you are satisfied with your measurement or weighing, then there is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the man who buys foodstuff, then sells it before it is measured, he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not correct for him'.
