Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who buys foodstuff, then sells it before he takes possession of it. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem. And if the man appoints the buyer from him to take possession of it and measure it, he said: There is no problem (with that).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bought from another man a measure of food by a known volume, then the seller said to the buyer, 'Buy this other measure from me without measuring, for it is like the one you bought.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid except if he measures it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever of the foodstuffs you specify a volume for, it is not valid as an estimation (gharar). This is what is disliked from the selling of foodstuffs.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt of one Kurra of foodstuff. So he bought one Kurra from another man, and said to the man, 'Go and take full payment of your Kurra (from that man).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-ʿAṭārid, who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'I buy foodstuff, so I incur a loss in the beginning and profit in the end, so I ask my companion to deduct from me for each kurra such and such (amount).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This has no goodness in it, but he should deduct from you as a lump sum.' I said: 'If he deducts from me more than what I lost?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said: 'So if I take out one kurra and two kurras, so the man says,

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari, from Abdul Malik ibn Amr, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I buy food, then I measure it, and with me is one who has witnessed the measuring, and I measured it for myself. So he says to me, 'Sell it to me', so I sell it to him with that measurement which I measured out.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man bought the hay of a stack, each kurra for a known amount. He takes possession of the hay and sells it before the grain is measured. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskann, from Is'haq al-Madainy, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who board a ship, buy food, and haggle over it. Then one of them buys it, and they ask him for whatever they want of the food. He becomes the owner of the food, the one who hands it over to them and takes the price. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; I do not see them except that they have shared with him.' So I said: 'Indeed, the owner of the food invites a measurer, so he measures it for us, and for us are laborers who measure it for him, so there are increases and decreases.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem as long as there is not much error.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bought foodstuff from a man with dirhams, so he took half of it and left half of it. Then he came after that and the foodstuff had increased in price or decreased. He (peace be upon him) said: If on the day he bought it, he priced it for such and such, then his price is for him. And if he had only taken some and left some, and did not specify a price, then his price is the price of the day in which he takes it, whatever it was.

Muhammad ibn Yahya said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man hired a worker to build for him or do other work, and began giving him food, cotton, and other things. Then the price of the food and cotton changed from the price at which he gave it, either decreasing or increasing. Should he account for him at the price of the day he gave it, or at the price of the day of accounting? So he (peace be upon him) signed: He should account for him at the price of the day he stipulated to him, if God wills. And he (peace be upon him) answered regarding the money that becomes due to the man, so he is given food with it at its due time, and he is not cut off (from service). Then the price changes. So he (peace be upon him) signed: For him is the price of the day he was given the food.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), saying: 'We buy food from the ships, then we measure it, and it increases.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'And sometimes it is less upon you.' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So when it is less, do they return the deficiency to you?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem (with the increase as well).'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the surplus/excess in measuring and weighing, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is not an infringement (exceeding limits), then there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan, who said: I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). Mu'ammarr the oil merchant said to him, 'We buy the oil in its skins (zigaq), and a deficiency is calculated for us in it due to the place of the skin.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If it increases and decreases, there is no problem; but if it increases and does not decrease, do not go near it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he was asked: about food in which some of it is mixed with some other, and some of it is better than some other. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If both are seen together, there is no problem, as long as the good does not cover the bad.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who has two varieties of one type of food, and their price is one thing, and one of the two is better than the other. So he mixes them both together, then he sells them both for one price. He said: 'It is not correct for him to do that; he is cheating the Muslims by it, until he clarifies it.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys food, and it becomes better for him and more saleable for him if he moistens it, without seeking an increase in it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is a sale that is not valid except by that, and it cannot be sold except by that, without him seeking an increase in it, then there is no problem. And if he is merely deceiving the Muslims with it, then it is not valid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not correct for the man that he sell by a Sa'a (a unit of measurement of four handfuls) of other than a Sa'a of the city.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not permissible for a man to sell using a Sa' other than the Sa' of the people of the city, for indeed a man hires a camel driver and measures for him with the Mudd of his house; perhaps it will be smaller than the Mudd of the marketplace. And if he were to say, 'This is smaller than the Mudd of the marketplace,' he would not be bound by it, but he would bear that and place it in his trustworthiness. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct except for one Mudd, and the trustees are at this status.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a people who make their qufzan smaller, selling by them. He said: 'Those are the ones who undervalue (shortchange) the things of the people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with as-Salam (advance payment for goods) being by a known measure up to a known term. It is not given until the threshing, and not until the harvest.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-salam (advance payment for goods) in foodstuff, with a known measure, until a known term. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man: is it permissible for him to give an advance payment (salim) for food with a man who has no crops, nor food, nor livestock, except that when the term arrives, he buys it and fulfills the delivery? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he guarantees it to a specified term, there is no problem with it.' I said: 'What is your view if he fulfills part of it to me and is unable to fulfill the rest? Is it permissible for me to take back the capital of my wealth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, that is good.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who gives an advance payment regarding a crop, so he takes some of his foodstuff and some remains which is not yet due/settled. So his partner presents the capital of his wealth to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should take it, for it is permissible.' I said, 'Suppose he sells what he has taken possession of from the foodstuff, so he doubles it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he does, then it is permissible.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him about a man who gives an advance payment regarding other than a crop or a palm tree. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should name a specific amount to a specified term.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether, from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Hammad from Al-Halby who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom I had advanced dirhams for foodstuff. So when my foodstuff was released to him, he sent the dirhams back to me and said: 'Buy food for yourself and fulfill your right.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that someone other than you should be put in charge of that, and you should stand with him until you take hold of that which is yours, and you should not rely upon yourself (alone) for its buying.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who gives Dirhams as advance payment for foodstuff for a term. The foodstuff is released (delivered), but he (the seller) says: 'I do not have foodstuff with me, but look at its value, so take its price from me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from al-Ays ibn al-Qasim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who advanced another man dirhams in exchange for wheat. When the due date arrived, the debtor did not have food, but he found with him animals, belongings, and slaves. Is it permissible for him to take from those goods in exchange for his food? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, he specifies such and such for such and such, a sa'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb and Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sold foodstuff for dirhams for a specified term. When that term arrived, he (the buyer) demanded payment, so he (the seller) said, 'I do not have dirhams with me; take foodstuff from me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it. Rather, he has dirhams; he may take whatever he wishes with them.'

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who advanced dirhams for food, so what was due to him was released, and he sent the dirhams back to him, saying: 'Buy food and fulfill your right.' Do you see any problem with it? He said: 'If someone else were with him, that would be fulfilled.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who advanced his dirhams for five sealed containers of wheat or barley for a specified term, and the one who owed the wheat and barley was unable to repay all of what was due to him when it became due. So he asked the owner of the right (the buyer) to take half of the foodstuff, or a third, or less than that, or more, and take back the capital of what remained of the foodstuff in dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' And regarding saffron, a man advances his dirhams for twenty mithqals, or less than that or more. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if the one who owes the saffron is unable to give him all of his goods, that he take half of his right, or a third, or two-thirds, and take back the capital of what remains from his right.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who buys the foodstuff of a specific town: and if he does not specify for him the foodstuff of that specific town, he may give it from wherever he wishes.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muawiya ibn Hakim from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'A man gives me an advance for food, but when the time comes, I do not have food. Can I give him dirhams equal to its value?' He said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has willed nothing but to make the livelihoods of the believers come from where they do not expect.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Be more hopeful in that for which you have no hope than in that for which you have hope. For indeed Musa (peace be upon him) went to obtain fire for his family, but he returned to them while he was a commissioned Prophet.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from one who mentioned it, from Abdallah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them both), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Be more hopeful regarding that which you do not expect than you are regarding that which you do expect — for Moses son of Imran (peace be upon him) went out to fetch fire for his family, and God Mighty and Majestic spoke to him, and he returned as a sent Prophet; and the queen of Sheba went out and she submitted [to God] with Solomon (peace be upon him); and the magicians of Pharaoh went out seeking honour for Pharaoh, and they returned as believers.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the sustenance of the believers from where they do not reckon, and that is because when a servant does not know the direction of his sustenance, his supplication increases.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is Umar ibn Muslim doing?' I said: 'May I be your sacrifice! He has devoted himself to worship and abandoned trade.' He said: 'Woe to him! Does he not know that one who abandons the seeking (of livelihood) will not have his supplications answered?' Indeed, a group from among the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when the verse was revealed: 'And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out, and He will provide for him from where he does not reckon,' they locked their doors and devoted themselves to worship, saying: 'We have been provided for.' This reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and he sent for them and said: 'What drove you to what you have done?' They said: 'O Messenger of God! Our provisions were guaranteed for us, so we devoted ourselves to worship.' He said: 'Indeed whoever does that, his supplications will not be answered. You must seek (your livelihood).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who sells another man foodstuff in bulk (akrar), but there is not with him what he can complete for him of what he had sold. So he says to him, 'Take from me in place of each qafiz of wheat, two qafiz of barley, until you have fulfilled whatever was deficient from the measure.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct, because the origin of the barley is from the wheat, but he should return the dirhams to him by an accounting of whatever was deficient from the measure.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Baseer and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The wheat and the barley are head to head; one of them does not increase upon the other.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Two sealed measures of barley are not to be sold for one sealed measure of wheat, and they are not to be sold except like for like, and the same applies to dates. He said: And he was asked about a man who buys wheat and finds with its owner only barley, is it permissible for him to take two for one? He said: No, for the origin of both is one, and Ali (peace be upon him) used to count barley as equal to wheat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the wheat and the barley, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are equal, there is no problem.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the wheat and the flour, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are equal, there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to exchange one qafiz of wheat for two qafiz of barley?' He said, 'It is not permissible except like for like.' Then he said, 'Barley is from wheat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man said to another, 'Sell me the fruit of your palm tree, this one that is in it, for two Qafeez of dates, or less than that, or more, naming whatever he wishes.' So he sold it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dates and the unripened dates from a single palm tree are one; there is no problem with it. But if one mixes the old dates and the unripened dates, it is not valid; and the raisins and the grapes are like that.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Sayf al-Tammār, who said: I said to Abu Baseer, 'I would like you to ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who exchanged two baskets containing cooked unripened dates for one basket containing split dates.' He said, 'So Abu Baseer asked him about that, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is disliked.' Abu Baseer said, 'And why is it disliked?' He said, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) disliked that one wasq of the dates of Medina be exchanged for two wasqs of the dates of Khyber, because the dates of Medina were the inferior of the two, and it never happened that Ali (peace be upon him) disliked the permissible.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What do you say regarding bartering wheat with sawiq (mash of wheat and barley)?' He said, 'Similar with similar, there is no problem with it.' I said, 'Suppose he has a yield (extra quality/quantity) or has an excess?' He said, 'Does he not have maintenance (cost/effort) for it?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'This by this.' And he said, 'When the two things are different, there is no problem with two with one, hand to hand.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Jameel, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Wheat with flour is like-for-like, and Sawiq with Sawiq is like-for-like, and barley with wheat is like-for-like, there is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who hands over foodstuff to the miller, so he stipulates that he could give its owner twelve ratls for every ten (given to him). He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'So (what about) the man who hands over the sesame seeds to the oiler who guarantees for him one ratl of oil for every Sa'a of sesame seeds?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not valid to barter dry dates with fresh (wet) dates, because the dates are dry and the fresh ones are wet; when the fresh ones dry out, they reduce in volume/weight. And it is not valid to barter barley with wheat except in a one-to-one ratio, and he said: The measurement (kayl) follows one rule. It is disliked to barter one Qafeez of almonds for two Qafeez, and one Qafeez of dates for two Qafeez. But it is valid to barter one Sa'a of wheat for two Sa'as of dates, and one Sa'a of dates for two Sa'as of raisins. And if this [the one-to-one rule] differs from dried fruits, then it is good. And it follows in food and fruits with one rule. Or he said: There is no problem with exchanging goods as long as they are not measured by volume (kayl) or weighed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) disliked bartering one Qafeez of almonds for two Qafeez of almonds, and one Qafeez of dates for two Qafeez of dates.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who advanced oil to a man upon the condition that he would take butter from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not befitting for the man to leave behind (for someone) the butter for oil, nor the oil for the butter'.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'at who said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about the grapes (bartered) with the raisins. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct except similar with the similar'. I said, 'And the dates and the raisins?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Similar with similar'.
And in another Hadith, by this chain He (peace be upon him) said: 'The different (items), two similar (portions bartered) with one, hand to hand, there is no problem'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid, from Abu Al-Rabie who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is your view regarding bartering dates and unripened red dates, a similar portion with a similar portion?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'So (what about) the cooked juice and the juice, similar with similar?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A camel for two camels, and an animal for two animals, hand to hand (immediate exchange), there is no problem with it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, raising it from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about selling the spinning yarn with the expanded fabric, and the spinning yarn is more in weight than the clothes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave (bartered) with two slaves, and the slave with the slave and the dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with all of the animals, hand to hand.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the camel (being exchanged) for two camels, hand to hand, and on credit. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem if you specify by age, two Jadh' or two Sani.' Then he (peace be upon him) ordered me, so I struck off the word 'credit'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whatever is from different foodstuffs, or goods, or something of the things that differ in quality, there is no problem with selling it, two similar (portions) for one, hand to hand. As for respite (on credit), then it is not valid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Commander of the Faithful disliked bartering meat with an animal.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Dawood ibn Al-Husayn, from Mansour, who said: I asked him about (bartering) one sheep for two sheep, and one egg for two eggs. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, as long as it is not by measure or by weight.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who said to a man, 'Hand over to me your sheep and your camels to be with me. So if they give birth, I shall exchange for you, if you so desire, its females for its males or its males for its females.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is an abhorrent act, except if he were to exchange after what has been born and he identifies it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whatever of the foodstuffs you have specified by measuring (kayl), it is not valid to sell by estimation (mujazafah). This is from what is disliked regarding the sale of food.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt of one hundred Kurra of dates owed to him by another man, and he has palm trees. So he goes to him and says, 'Give me this palm tree of yours in exchange for what is upon you (the debt).' It was as if he (peace be upon him) disliked it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about two men who share palm trees between them, so one of them says to his companion, 'Either you take this palm tree for such and such a specified measurement, or you give me half of this measurement, whether it increases or decreases, or else I take it for that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about walnuts which one is unable to count, so they are measured with a measure, and what is in it is counted, then what remains is measured according to that count, so he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a sale in which there is a measure or weight, he estimates it, then takes it upon an approximation of whatever is in it. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has cattle, can he sell their milk without measuring? He said: Yes, until it stops or something from it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'at, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about milk that is bought while it is still in the udder. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he milks it for you into a bowl (sukurrjah), so he says, 'Buy from me this milk which is in the bowl, and whatever is in its udders, for a specified price.' If there happens to be nothing in the udders, then whatever is in the bowl is what is sold.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abu Sa'id, from Abdul Malik ibn Amr, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy one hundred rawiyas of oil, so I display one rawiya and two, then I weigh both of them, then I take the rest of it based on that measurement.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who buys from another man the wool of one hundred ewes and what is in their bellies of pregnancy for such and such dirhams?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that; if there is not pregnancy in their bellies, the capital of his wealth is in the wool.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'at al-Nakhas, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), saying to him, 'Is it permissible for me to buy the absconded slave girl from the people, give them the price, and seek her myself?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buying her is not permissible unless you buy from them something along with her, a garment or goods, so you should say to them,

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade the purchase of the fisherman's net, [where one says], 'Strike with your net, so whatever comes out, it is from my property for such and such (price).'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If there is a grove (of fish) wherein there are no reeds, something from the fish is taken out, so whatever is in the grove can be sold.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, all of them, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who accepts the jizyah (tax) of the heads of men, and the kharaj (land tax) of the palm trees, the bushes, and the birds, while he does not know whether anything from this will ever exist or not. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he knows of one of those things that it has come into existence, then buy it and accept it with that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man from our companions, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys plaster, so he measures some of it and takes the remainder without measuring. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Either he takes all of it based on his verification (estimation), or he measures all of it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who bought a garment and did not stipulate any condition with its seller. Then he disliked it and returned it to the seller, but the seller refused to accept it back except for a small deduction (price reduction). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to take it back with a deduction. If he was ignorant (of the ruling) and took it back and sold it for more than its price, he must return to the original seller whatever was the increase.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who said to another man, 'Sell my garment for ten dirhams, and whatever remains [of the price] is for you,' he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who carries the goods for the people of the market and they have established a price upon it, so they are saying, ‘Sell, and whatever is the increase, so it is for you’. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘There is no problem with that, but he cannot sell them for profit (sharing basis)’.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and others from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the fee of the middleman (simstar); he buys for the people day after day for a specified amount; he is essentially in the status of the wage-earners.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the middleman who buys for a fee, so the silver coins are handed over to him and it is stipulated upon him that, 'If you bring what you have bought, then whatever I choose I will leave [with you].' So he goes and buys, then comes with the goods, so he says, 'Take what you are pleased with and leave what you dislike.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who buys the Herawi and Quhi bags, so the man buys ten garments from it, and it is stipulated upon him that he takes his choice of each garment with a profit of five or less, or more. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like this sale. Do you consider if he does not find a choice other than five garments, and finds the remainder to be equal?' His son Ismail said to him, 'They had stipulated upon him that he would take ten from them,' and he repeated it to him repeatedly. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, it was stipulated upon him that he would take the best of them. Do you consider if there are not except five garments, and he finds the remainder to be equal?' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'And I do not like this, and he disliked it due to the place of deception (ghabn).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is disliked to buy the garment with a dinar that is not [specified as] a dirham, because it is not known how much of the dirham the dinar is.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who buys all the goods for a price, then he evaluates each garment at what it is worth, until the total capital of his wealth is covered. Can he sell it for a profit? He said: No, until he clarifies to him that he has fixed the price.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Goods were brought to my father (peace be upon him) from Egypt, so he prepared food and invited the merchants to it. They said, 'We take it from you for 'dah' and 'dowazdah' (ten and twelve).' My father asked them, 'And how much is that?' They said, 'For every ten thousand, two thousand.' My father said to them, 'I sell you this goods for twelve thousand.' So he sold it to them through bargaining.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike selling ten for eleven, and ten for twelve, and similar to that from sales, but I sell to you for such and such a fixed price.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And goods came to me from Egypt, so I disliked selling them like that, and it was grievous upon me, so I sold them for a fixed price.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We send dirhams with an exchange rate to Ahwaz, so goods are bought for us with them. Then we wait. When they are sold, the exchange rate is placed against them. So when we sell them, is it upon us to mention to him the exchange rate of the dirhams in the murabahah (resale for profit), to suffice us from that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but when it is murabahah, inform him of that, and if it is musawamah (fixed price bargaining), there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who said to me, 'Buy this cloth and this animal for me, specifying it, and I will profit you in it with such and such.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him buy it, and you should not obligate the sale before he obligates it or you buy it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Asbaat ibn Salim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We buy the 'Adl' (a bundle containing one hundred garments, a mix of good and bad), and a man comes to us and takes ninety garments from the bundle, with a profit of one dirham per dirham [of cost]. Is it befitting for us to sell the remainder based on what we sold [for the ninety]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless he buys the garment alone [separately].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the Salam (advance payment for goods) regarding the merchandise when you describe the length and the width.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about as-salam (advance payment for goods), and it is as-salf (advance payment) regarding silk and the goods which are made in the city in which you are. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if it is for a known term.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: There is no problem with As-Salam (advance payment for goods) in the merchandise when you specify the length and the width.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me seeking goods for ten thousand dirhams, or less or more, and I have only goods worth one thousand dirhams. So I borrow from my neighbor and take from this one and that one, then I sell them to him. Then I buy them from him (or instruct someone to buy them) so I return them to their owners. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about a man who sold an item which was not with him, for a specified term, and guaranteed the sale to him. He said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man comes to me seeking goods, so I negotiate with him on the profit, then I buy it and sell it to him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if he desires, he takes it, and if he desires, he leaves it?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said: 'But one among us considers it invalid.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why?' I said: 'Because he sells what is not with him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what do you say regarding the sale of Salam (advance payment for goods), where its owner has sold what is not with him?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is valid only because they name it Salam. Indeed, my father used to say: There is no problem with selling every type of goods which you can find at the time in which you sell it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man comes to me seeking silk goods, and I do not have any of them with me. He negotiates with me and I negotiate with him regarding the profit and the term, until we agree on something. Then I go and buy the silk for him and invite him to it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you see, if he finds a sale that is more beloved to him than what is with you, would he be able to turn to it and leave you, or if you find that, would you be able to turn from it and leave him?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn Najih, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man comes to me and says, 'Buy this garment for me, and I will profit you such and such.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if he desires, he takes, and if he desires, he leaves?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. Rather, the speech makes it permissible and the speech makes it prohibited.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem if you sell to the man the goods that are not with you, haggling over them, then you buy for him approximately that which he sought, then make it binding upon yourself, then you sell it to him afterwards.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who sold a sale which was not with him to a specified term, and guaranteed the sale. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

One of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarraj, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Mu'tab came to him and said, 'There are two men at the door.' He said, 'Let them enter.' So they entered, and one of them said, 'I am a butcher, and I sell the milk before I slaughter the sheep.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it, but link it [the milk] to the sheep of such and such a land.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from one of our companions, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the good (quality), there are two supplications, and regarding the inferior (quality), there are two supplications. It is said to the owner of the good quality: 'May Allah bless you and the one who sold it to you,' and it is said to the owner of the inferior quality: 'May Allah not bless you nor the one who sold it to you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Al-Washa, from Aasim ibn Humayd, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What trade do you engage in?' I said, 'I sell foodstuff.' So he said to me: 'Buy the good (quality) and sell the good (quality), for when you sell the good (quality), it is said to you: 'May Allah bless you and the one who sold it to you.''

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn Suqah, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mundhir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man comes to me seeking the 'inah [buy-back], so I buy the goods for him with a profit margin, then I sell them to him, then I buy them back from him in my place.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he has the option, if he wishes he sells, and if he wishes he does not sell, and you also have the option: if you wish you buy, and if you wish you do not buy, so there is no problem.' He (the narrator) said: 'I said: 'But the people of the Masjid allege that this is invalid, and they say that if he brings it back after some months, it would be correct.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is preceding and delaying, so there is no problem with it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-'Inah, and I said, 'Indeed, most of our merchants today give al-'Inah, so let me relate to you how it is done.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go ahead.' I said: 'A haggling man comes to us wanting money, so he haggles with us, and we have no goods. He says, "I will profit you ten, eleven," and I say, "And I, ten, eleven." So we do not cease bargaining until we agree upon a matter.' When we finish, I say to him, 'Which goods do you prefer that I buy for you?' He says, 'Silk, because we do not find anything less wasteful than it.' So I go, having made a verbal agreement without a formal sale. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if you wish, you do not give it, and if he wishes, he does not take from you?' I said, 'Yes.' He (the narrator) said: 'So I go and buy that silk for him, and I bargain to the best of my ability. Then I bring it to my house and sell it to him. Sometimes I add a little to him over the verbal agreement, sometimes I give it to him as agreed, and sometimes we struggle and nothing happens. When he buys from me, he does not find anyone more expensive with it than the one from whom I bought it, so he sells it to him. Then he comes, takes the dirhams, and hands them to him; and sometimes he comes to assign it to me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You do not hand them over except to the owner of the silk.' I said: 'And sometimes the sale does not agree between me and him, and I seek from him, and he accepts it from me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if he wishes, he does not do it, and if you wish, you do not return it?' I said, 'Yes. If he were to die, it would be from my wealth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with this. When you do not exceed this, there is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umeyra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who sought a garment from another man using a 'bi'ina' (buy-back) arrangement. The seller said, 'I do not have it with me, but here are dirhams; take them and buy with them.' So he took them and bought a garment as he desired, then came back to sell it to him. The Imam (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if the garment deteriorates, it is from the wealth of the one who gave him the dirhams?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'If he wishes, he buys it, and if he wishes, he does not buy it.' I said, 'So there is no problem with it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man contracted a buy-back deal (ta'yin), then his debt became due, but he could not find what to pay it with. Can he contract another buy-back from his companion whom he had contracted the first buy-back with, and pay it? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Ja'far ibn Hannan said to him, 'What do you say regarding al-'inah (buy-back) in a man who sells to a man, saying to him, 'I sell to you for ten, twelve (Persian) and for ten, eleven (Persian)'?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is invalid, but he should say, 'I profit upon you regarding all the dirhams, such and such,' and he should bargain with him on this, so there is no problem with it.' And he (the narrator) said: 'I bargain with him and there are no goods with me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man upon whom there is some wealth for me, and he is insolvent. So I buy a sale (item) from a man to a specified term, upon a stipulation that I guarantee that from him for the man, and he fulfils me that which is upon him? He said: There is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hadeed, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Salsabeel asked me for one hundred thousand dirhams on the condition that she would profit me ten thousand. So I lent her ninety thousand, and I sold her a garment and wool, which were valued at one thousand dirhams, for ten thousand dirhams.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' And in another report: 'There is no problem with it. Give her one hundred thousand and sell her the garment for ten thousand, and write two agreements for her.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man has wealth that is due to his companion. Can he sell him a pearl worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, and delay the payment from him to a specified time?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem. My father instructed me to do so, and I did that.' And he claimed that he asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about it, so he said to him the same.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'There are dirhams due to me from a man, and he says to me,

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man for whom I want to establish a buy-back deal with wealth, and there is already some wealth of mine upon him before that. So he asks me for wealth, increasing the wealth that is already mine upon him. Would it be correct if I were to increase the wealth and sell him a pearl worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, saying: 'I sell you this pearl for one thousand dirhams on the condition that I defer your payment of its price and my wealth upon you, such and such months.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Excess of sleep is a cause of ruin for religion and the world.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from the one who mentioned him, from Bashir al-Dahhan who said: I heard Abu al-Hassan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: Verily, God — Majestic and Mighty — detests the servant who sleeps much and is idle.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan and Salih al-Nayli, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hates an abundance of sleep and an abundance of idleness.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I and Umar were in Al-Medina, so Umar sold Harawiyya saddlebags, each bag from it for such and such. So I took it and distributed it, but they found a defect, so they returned it. So Umar said to them, 'I shall give you its price which I sold it with'. They said, 'No, but we shall take from you a price of the cloth'. So Umar mentioned that to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is binding for him (the buyer)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from one of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), regarding the man who buys a garment or goods and finds a defect in it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the item is still intact in its essence, he may return it to him and take back the price; but if the garment has been cut, or stitched, or dyed, he returns it with a deduction for the defect.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Any man who buys something that has a defect or a flaw, which was not made clear to him, and he alters it after taking possession, then learns of that flaw or defect, the sale is confirmed upon him, and he is refunded an amount corresponding to the deficiency caused by that defect and flaw in the price, had it not had that defect.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I intend to go out to some of the mountains.' He said, 'The people will inevitably face turbulence in their year.' I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! When we sell to them with credit (nasi'ah), it yields more profit.' He said, 'So sell them with a delay of one year.' I said, 'With a delay of two years?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'With a delay of three?' He said, 'No.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man whom a group of people had instructed to buy a camel for them with cash, and they would give him extra for deferment (credit). So he bought a camel for them, and one of them was with him. He (peace be upon him) forbade him to take from them extra above his cash price for the deferment.

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who buys goods for a deferred period, he said: He is not permitted to sell it with markup (murabahah) except for the same period for which he bought it; and if he sells it with markup without informing the buyer, then the buyer has the right to a similar period of deferment.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Bashar ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sells goods on credit, then buys them back from the owner from whom he had sold them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with it.' So I said to him, 'Can I buy my own goods?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not your goods, nor your cow, nor your sheep.' Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Bashar ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who was a close relative to me, who died and left young children, and left owned slave boys and girls, and he had not bequeathed. So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, taking her as a mother of a child (of his), and what is your view regarding selling them? He said: 'If there is a guardian for them who manages their affairs, sells on their behalf, and looks out for their interests, he is rewarded in doing so.' I said: 'So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, taking her as a mother of a child?' He said: 'There is no problem with that. When the custodian sells on their behalf, being considerate of their interests regarding what is beneficial for them, it is not for them to retract regarding what the custodian has done for them, being considerate of their interests regarding what is beneficial for them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said: A man from our companions died and did not bequeath, so his matter was raised to the judge of Al-Kufa, and he appointed Abdul Hameed as the custodian of his wealth. The man had left behind young heirs, goods, and slave girls. Abdul Hameed sold the goods, but when he intended to sell the slave girls, his heart weakened regarding their sale, because the deceased had not appointed him as executor by will, and his custodianship was by the order of the judge, and because they are 'furuj' (chastity/sexual organs). He said: So I mentioned that to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him: A man from our companions dies and does not bequeath to anyone, and leaves behind slave girls, so the judge appoints a man from us to sell them, or said: A man from us is appointed to do that, but his heart weakens because they are 'furuj'. So what is your view regarding that? He said: If the custodian is like you and like Abdul Hameed, then there is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who buys a slave while he is an absconder from his family. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid except if he buys another thing along with it, so he would say, 'I buy from you this thing and your slave for such and such.' So if he is not able to take the slave, the price he paid is considered for the thing.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad altogether, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'ah al-Nakhhas, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I said, 'I bargained with a man for a slave girl of his, and he sold her to me with my option (hukm). So I took possession of her from him upon that. Then I sent to him a thousand dirhams and said to him, 'This thousand is my option upon you.' But he refused to accept it from me, and I had already touched her before I sent to him the thousand dirhams.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that you should evaluate the slave girl with a fair price. So if her price was more than what you sent to him, it is upon you to return to him what was deficient from the price; and if her price was less than what you sent to him, then it is for him.' He said: 'I said, 'What is your view if I find a defect in her after having touched her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for you to return her, and for you is to take the value of what is between the health and the defect.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a slave who is owned by partners, if one of them sells his share, his companion says, 'I am more rightful to it.' Would that be for him? He said: 'Yes, if there is one (partner).' It was said, 'Is there shuf'ah (preemption) regarding animals?' So he said: 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the buying of the Roman women, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy them and sell them.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about buying the slaves of the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma) when they acknowledge/endorse that for them. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When they acknowledge that for them, then buy and marry.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a people from the enemies who reconciled (signed a peace treaty), then they breached it, and perhaps they breached it because justice had not been done upon them. Is it correct to buy from their captives? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was from the enemies who had manifested their enmity, so buy from them (their captives), and if it was a number who were alienated and had been unjust, so do not buy from their captives'. He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a captive of Al-Daylam who had stolen from each other and the Muslims had attacked them without an Imam (peace be upon him), is buying them Permissible? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When they had been endorsed with the slavery so there is no problem with buying them'. He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a people from the ones under the responsibility (Ahl Al-Zimma) who have been hit by hunger (famine), so a man comes over with his son, so he says, 'This is for you, so feed him, and he would be a slave for you'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You cannot sell the free, for it is not correct for you, nor from the people under the responsibility (Ahl Al-Zimma)'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'ah al-Nakhhas, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'The Romans raid the Saqaliba and steal their children, both slave-girls and slave-boys. They take the boys, castrate them, and then send them to Baghdad to the merchants. What do you think regarding buying them, knowing that they have been stolen, and they were raided not in a war that was between them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in buying them; they are taken out of polytheism and brought into the house of Islam.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slaves of the people of the covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma), can I buy some of them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy, when they have been endorsed with slavery.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I entered the market intending to buy a slave girl, and she said to me,

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Muhammad ibn Mysar, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who looks at his price while he is being weighed, will not succeed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'ah who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who participated with another man regarding a slave girl of his, and said: 'If we profit from her, then half of the profit is for you, and if she is of little value (or incurs loss), then there is nothing upon you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see any problem with this, if the master of the slave girl is pleased with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the stipulation in slave girls that they should not be sold, nor inherited, nor gifted. So he said: That is allowed, except for inheritance, for she can be inherited, and every stipulation that opposes the Book of Allah is rejected.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said to me: 'O youth, what is your profession?' I said, 'The slaves (or servants).' He said: 'I advise you with an advice, so memorize it: Do not buy anything with a defect, nor a defect, and ensure the contract.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man buys a slave who has wealth. For whom is his wealth?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If the seller knew that he had wealth, then it is for the buyer, and if he did not know, then it is for the seller.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man buys the owned slave and his wealth.' He said, 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'Supposing the wealth of the owned slave is more than what he was bought with?' He said, 'There is no problem with it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a mature slave girl, and she did not menstruate with him until six months had passed for her, and there was no pregnancy with her. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the likes of her tend to menstruate, and that is not due to old age, then this is a defect for which she can be returned.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a slave girl who was pregnant, and he did not know of her pregnancy, so he copulated with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return her to the one from whom he bought her, and half of a tenth of her value should be returned to him due to his copulation with her.' And Ali (peace be upon him) had said: 'The one who is not pregnant is not returned if her master copulated with her, and a discount is made for him from her price corresponding to a defect, if there was one in her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abdul Malik ibn Umeyr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: She who is not pregnant is not returned if her master has copulated with her, and for him is the compensation for the defect; and the pregnant one is returned, and with her is returned half of a tenth of her price. And in another report, if she was a virgin, then a tenth of her price, and if she was not a virgin, then half of a tenth of her price.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who bought a slave girl, so he copulated with her, then he found a defect in her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is valued while she is healthy, and she is valued with the defect, then the seller returns to the buyer the difference between the healthy value and the defective value.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bought a slave girl and had intercourse with her, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he finds a defect in her, it is not for him to return her, but he is returned the value of what the defect diminished [her price].' I said, 'Is this the saying of Ali (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), that he was asked: about the man who buys a slave girl, so he has intercourse with her, then finds a defect in her after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not return her to her owner, but she is evaluated for the difference between the defect and her health, so it is returned to the buyer. Allah forbid that He make a wage for her.'

Humayd, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who buys the slave girl, so he copulates with her, and he finds her pregnant, he said: He should return her, and return something along with her.

Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who buys the pregnant slave girl, so he copulates with her while he does not know (of her pregnancy). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return her and clothe her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who bought a slave girl and she bore him a child, then it was found that she had been stolen. He (peace be upon him) said: The master takes the slave girl, and the man takes his child by paying her price.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who narrated it, from Zurara ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who sold a slave girl on the condition that she was a virgin, but he did not find her to be so. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She cannot be returned to him, and nothing is obligated upon it, for it may go away during a state of illness or an event that befalls her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Al-Sayyari who said: It has been reported from Ibn Abi Layla that a man came to him with a disputant of his, so he said, 'This one sold me this slave girl, but I did not find upon her pubic area when I uncovered it any hair, and she claimed that it had never been for her at all.' So Ibn Abi Layla said to him, 'The people tend to play tricks with this until they remove it, so what is it which you dislike?' He said, 'O judge! If it was a defect, so judge for me with it.' He said, '(Wait) until I come out to you, for I find some pain in my belly.' Then he entered and came out from another door, so he went to Muhammad ibn Muslim Al-Thaqafi, so he said to him, 'What do you report from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the woman who does not have hair upon her pubic area? Does that happen to be a defect?' So Muhammad ibn Muslim said to him, 'As for this explicitly, I do not know it, but Abu Ja'far narrated to me from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'Everything that was in the original creation, so any increase or deficiency, it is a defect.' So Ibn Abi Layla said to him, 'You have sufficed me.' Then he returned to the people, so he judged for them with the defect.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Farra, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man buys a slave girl from the market, and she gives birth, then a man comes and establishes proof that she is his slave girl, having neither been sold nor gifted.' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'He returns his slave girl to him, and compensates him from what he benefited.' He said: 'It is as if its meaning is the value of the child.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from a man bought a slave girl on the condition that she was a virgin, but he did not find her to be a virgin. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The excess of the value is returned to him when it is known that he is truthful.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said: The slave girl may be returned due to four characteristics: insanity, leprosy, vitiligo, and hunchback (a pair of humps), except if the hunchback is such that it curves the back inward and pushes the chest outward.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Asbaat from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The option (to return) regarding animals is three days for the buyer, and regarding non-animals is that the two separate, and the 'new occurrences of the year' are returned after the year.' I said, 'And what are the new occurrences of the year?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Insanity, leprosy, vitiligo, and the pair (of humps). So whoever buys and these new occurrences befall it, the ruling is that it is returned to its owner until the completion of the year from the day he bought it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Hammam said: I heard al-Rida’ (peace be upon him) saying: 'The slave is returned due to the happenings of the year, such as madness, leprosy, and vitiligo.' We asked, 'How is the return due to the happenings of the year?' He said, 'This is the beginning of the year. If you buy a slave with any of these traits, between you and Dhu al-Hijjah, you can return him to his owner.' Muhammad ibn Ali then asked, 'Is runaway status included in this?' He said, 'Runaway status is not included, unless proof is presented that he was a runaway while with the owner.' It is also narrated from Yunus that the warranty period for madness, leprosy, and vitiligo is one year. And al-Washsha’ narrated that the warranty period for madness alone is one year.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Habeeb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who bought a slave from another man, and with the seller were two slaves. So he said to the buyer, 'Go with both of them and choose whichever you wish, and return the other,' and he had taken the money. So the buyer went with both of them, and one of them absconded from his presence. He said: Let him return the one who is still with him and take back half the price from what he gave to the seller, and go in search of the slave. If he finds him, he can choose whichever of the two he wishes and return the half money which he had taken; and if he does not find him, the slave is shared between them, half for the seller and half for the buyer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about men who shared in a slave girl, so they entrusted one of them with the stipulation that the slave girl would be with him, so he copulated with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Part of the legal punishment (Hadd) is staved off from him by the measure of what is for him in her from the cash, and he is whipped by the measure of what is not for him in her; and the slave girl is evaluated upon him with a price and it is binding upon him. And if the evaluation is less than the price with which the girl was bought, her former price is obligated. And if her evaluation on that day in which she was evaluated is more than her price, that price is obligated, and he is belittled because he bedded her.' I said, 'And if one of the partners wishes to buy her apart from the man?' He said: 'That is for him, and it is not for him that he buys her until he exonerates her, and it is not upon someone else that he buys her except with the price.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn A'iz from Abu Salama from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding two slave men, to whom it was delegated that they buy and sell with their own wealth, so there was a dispute between them. So this one went running to the master of that one, and that one ran to the master of this one, and they were equal in strength. So this one bought that slave from his master, and that one went and bought the other slave from his master, and they returned to their place, and each one of them clung to his companion and said to him, 'You are my slave, as I have bought you from your master.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Judgement is made between them from where they separated; the path is measured. So whichever of the two was closer, he is the one who preceded the one who was further. And if they were equal, then it is a return to their masters; they came equally and separated equally, except if one of the two preceded his companion, then the predecessor is entitled to him; if he wishes, he sells him, and if he wishes, he keeps him, and it is not for him to harm him by it.' And in another report, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the distance is equal, a lot is drawn between them, so whichever of the two the lot falls on, he becomes his slave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Captives from Yemen were brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When they reached Al-Juhfa, their expenses ran out, so they sold a girl from the captives, whose mother was with them. When they arrived at the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he heard her crying and said: "What is this crying?" They said: "O Messenger Allah, we needed expenses, so we sold her daughter." He sent for her price, and she was brought back, and he said: "Sell them both together or keep both of them together."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two brothers who are owned slaves, whether they are separated from each other, and about the woman and her child? He (peace be upon him) said: No, it is prohibited, except if they want that.
