Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a slave girl was bought for him from Kufa. He said: So she went to attend to one of the needs, and she said, 'O mother!' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Do you have a mother?' She said, 'Yes'. So he ordered that she be returned, and said: 'I do not feel safe if I were to keep her, from seeing in my children what I dislike.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The young slave girl, the man buys her.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If she has become needless from her parents, then there is no problem.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the man who buys a boy or a girl, and for him is a brother or a sister or a father or a mother in a city from the cities. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not send him to another city if he is young, and do not buy him. So if he has a mother, and she is pleased and he is pleased, then buy him if you wish.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl, who said: A slave said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I said to my master, 'Sell me for seven hundred dirhams, and I will give you three hundred dirhams'.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'If you had something on the day you stipulated to give him, then it is upon you to give it; and if you did not have anything on that day, then there is nothing upon you'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Fuzayl who said: A slave on loan said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I said to my master, 'Sell me for seven hundred Dirhams and I shall give you three hundred Dirhams'. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'If it was that there was wealth for you on the day you stipulated, so it would be upon you that you give it, and if there did not happen to be any wealth for you on that day, so there is nothing upon you'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the *salam* (advance payment for goods) in animals. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' I said, 'What is your view if I were to make *salam* for known years, or something known from the slaves, so I give him less than his stipulation, and above it by the agreement of their own selves?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who gave a man a promissory note (wariq) in exchange for a servant (wasif) for a specified term, so the owner said to him, 'We could not find a servant for you, so take the value of your servant today as a promissory note.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not take except his servant or the promissory note that he gave him the first time; no extra is added to it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the Salam (advance payment for goods) in animals when their teeth (age) are described.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with the Salam (advance payment) in animals when you name a known thing.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that his father did not view anything wrong with the Salam (advance payment) in animals, with a known amount for a known period.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who gives an advance payment for sheep, specifying their ages to a known term. He gave the four-year-old in place of the five-year-old. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that he gave the advance payment for known ages to a known term?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who gave an advance payment for a servant of known age and known color, then he is given below his stipulation or above it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is from the goodwill of yourself and from him, then there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who gives an advance payment (salam) for sheep, specifically two-year-olds and one-year-olds, and other than that, up to a specified term. He said: There is no problem if the one upon whom is the sheep is not able to provide all of what is upon him, that the owner of the sheep takes half of it, or a third of it, or two-thirds of it, and they take the capital value of what remains from the sheep in dirhams, and they take below their stipulation, and they do not take above their stipulation. And garments are also like wheat, and barley, and saffron, and sheep.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who gave an advance payment for servants of known and unknown ages, then was given less than his stipulation. He said: 'If it is with the goodwill/agreement of yourself and him, then there is no problem.' He said: 'And I asked him about a man who gives an advance payment for sheep, specifying the two-year-old and the one-year-old, and other than that, for a named term. He said: There is no problem with it.' If the one upon whom the debt lies is unable to provide all that is due, and it is asked if the owner of the right (buyer) should take half the sheep or a third of it, and take back the capital value of what remains of the sheep in dirhams? He said: 'There is no problem, and he should not take less than his stipulation except with the goodwill/agreement of his partner.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Hadeed ibn Hakim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man buys skins from the butcher, giving him a known amount every day.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about *al-salam* (advance payment for goods) regarding animals, so he said: 'Known ages and counted numbers until a known term, there is no problem with it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the advance payment (salaf) regarding meat. He said: 'Do not be near it, for sometimes he gives you the fatty, and sometimes the almost spoilt, and sometimes the boney. Buy it after viewing, hand to hand.' He said: 'And I asked him about the advance payment regarding containers of water. He said: 'Do not go near it, for sometimes he gives you deficient, and sometimes complete, but buy it after viewing, and it is safer for you and for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who has sheep, from which he milks a large quantity of milk every day. What do you say about the one who buys five hundred ratls (a unit of weight) from him, or more than that, one hundred ratls for a specific amount of dirhams, and then takes from him a certain number of ratls every day until he fulfills what he bought from him? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with this and similar cases.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Qutaybah al-A'sha said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was in his presence, and a man said to him, 'My brother goes to the mountain to bring sheep, so he gives an advance payment (salam) for the sheep, specifying known ages, for a known term, so he is given a four-year-old in place of a two-year-old.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Is it by the goodwill/agreement of his companion (the seller)?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'From the mannerisms of the Prophets (may God's blessings be upon them) is love for women.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I do not think a man can increase in goodness of faith unless he also increases in his love for women.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad who said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three (things) are from the practices (sunnah) of the Messengers: perfume, the removal of (unwanted) hair, and frequency of marital relations.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sukayn al-Nakha'i — and he used to engage in devotional worship and had abandoned women (marriage), perfume, and (good) food. So he wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him about that, and he (the Imam) wrote back to him: 'As for your words regarding women, you have indeed known what the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) had of women; and as for your words regarding food, the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to eat meat and honey.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I do not think a man increases in goodness in this matter (Wilayah) except that he also increases in his love for women.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not love anything from your world except women and perfume.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Bakkar ibn Kardam and more than one (other narrator), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The delight of my eyes was placed in salat (prayer), and my pleasure in women.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Hassan, from some of our companions, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) asked us, 'Which of things is the most pleasurable?' He said: We mentioned other things, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The most pleasurable of things is copulation with women.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The delight of my eyes has been placed in salat (prayer), my pleasure in this world is women, and my two sweet-scented ones are Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Qatada, from a man, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The people do not enjoy in the world and the Hereafter a pleasure greater for them than the pleasure of women.' 'It has been adorned for people, the love of desires, from women and sons' – up to the end of the verse. Then he said: 'And the people of Paradise do not enjoy anything in Paradise more desirable to them than marriage, neither food nor drink.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who neglects marriage out of fear of poverty has distrusted Allah with conjecture.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him of destitution (lack of resources). He said to him: 'Marry.' So he married, and sustenance was expanded upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim [from his father] from Salih ibn al-Sindi from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A youth from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him of neediness. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Marry.' The youth said, 'I am too shy to return to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Then a man from the Ansar caught up with him and said, 'I have a beautiful daughter, so marry her to him.' He said: 'So Allah expanded (sustenance) upon him.' He said: 'So the youth came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and informed him. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of youths! Upon you is marriage.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah Al-Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Al-Mu'min, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is the hadith that people narrate true, that a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him of need/poverty, so he ordered him to marry, and he did? Then he came to him and complained to him of need, so he ordered him to marry, until he ordered him three times?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: '[Yes]' it is true. Then he said: 'Sustenance is with the women and the dependents.'

And from him, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who neglects marriage out of fear of poverty, has had a poor opinion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And let those who do not find the means to marry keep chaste until Allah makes them self-sufficient out of His Grace.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should keep marrying until Allah enriches them from His Grace.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How much is the dower, meaning in the Mut'a?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever they both agree upon, up to whatever they so desire from the term'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Barqi, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Abu Saeed, from Al-Ahwal, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What is the lowest amount with which one can contract a Mut'ah marriage?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A handful of wheat.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Mut'a of the women. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible, and it suffices in it the Dirham and what is above it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the lowest dower for Mut'a, what is it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'A handful of fine flour, or Suweeq (crushed grain), or dates.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The lowest amount by which Mut'ah (temporary marriage) is permissible is a handful of food, and some of them have reported, a miswak (toothbrush twig).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: If she was menstruating, then [the waiting period is] one menstruation, and if she was not menstruating, then [the waiting period is] a month and a half.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The waiting period of Mut'a is forty-five days, and the precaution is forty-five nights.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: The waiting period of Mut'a is forty-five days. It is as if I am looking at Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) counting with his hand forty-five. So when the term passes, there is separation without a divorce.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Baseer, who said: There is no problem with you increasing [the period] and her increasing [it] when the term is cut off between the two of you. She should say, 'I hereby permit you with another term with agreement from her,' and that is not permissible for other than you, until her waiting period expires.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, and from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom. A man marries a woman for Mut'ah (temporary marriage), and marries her for a month. Then it occurs in his heart, and he wishes that his stipulation be more than a month. So, is it permissible for him to increase her in her recompense (dowry) and increase in the days before the days he stipulated for her expire?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Two stipulations are not allowed in one stipulation.' I said: 'What should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give charity to her with whatever remains of the days, then he resumes with a new stipulation.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who reported it, he said: Indeed, when a man marries a woman by Mut'ah, there is upon her a waiting period for others. So when he intends to marry her, there is not upon her from him a waiting period; he can marry her whenever he desires.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He can stipulate upon her whatever he so desires from the days (term).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man marries by Mut'ah for a year, or less or more.' He said, 'When it is a known thing to a known term.' I said, 'And she is irrevocably divorced without a (formal) divorce?' He said, 'Yes.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, who said: I sent a message to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'What is the lowest term for Mut'ah? Is it allowed for a man to perform Mut'ah with a stipulation of (copulating) once?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from a man whom he named, said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries the woman for a single 'ard (visit/going to bed). He said: There is no problem, but when he is finished, let him turn his face away and not look.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When there remains upon him something from the dower, and he knows that she has a husband, then whatever she has taken is for her due to what she has permitted of her private parts, and he shall withhold from her whatever remains with him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn Aban, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can I marry the woman for a month, so I withhold something from her?' He said, 'Yes, take from her by the measure of whatever she has differed. If it was half a month, then the half (dower), and if it was a third, then the third.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Isṣ, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him): 'A man marries a woman in Muṭʿah (temporary marriage). She stipulates to him that she will come to him every day until she fulfills his condition, or she stipulates certain known days during which she will come to him. Then she deceives him and does not come to him as stipulated. Is it permissible for him to hold her accountable for the days she did not come, so that he withholds from her dower based on that calculation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. He looks at what was cut off from the stipulation, so he withholds from her dower by the amount of what she did not fulfill for him, except for the days of menstruation, for they are for her. Thus, there is not for him except what was permissible for him of her private parts.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym who said, Al-Rayyan ibn Shabeeb wrote to him, meaning Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man marries a woman by Mut'ah (temporary marriage) for a known term with a specified dower, and gives her part of her dower, and she delays him with the remainder. Then he consummates the marriage with her, and after consummation, before he pays her the remainder of her dower, he learns that she had married herself (to another) and has a husband residing with her. Is it permissible for him to withhold the remainder of her dower or is it not permissible? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should not give her anything because she has disobeyed Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I happen to be in one of the roads, so I see a beautiful woman, and I am not secure if she happens to be with a husband, or from the prostitutes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not upon you; rather, upon you is that you ratify her regarding herself.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Muyassar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If I meet a woman in the wilderness where there is no one else, and I ask her,

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no problem with him marrying by Mut'a with the virgin only if fear of disgrace to her family will not affect her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the virgin whom the man marries by Mut'a. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem as long as he does not destroy her virginity.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries by Mut’a with a virgin girl. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that for as long as he does not belittle her.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdullah ibn 'Umayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I said, 'At what age is a girl no longer considered a child (pre-pubescent)? Is it a girl of six or seven?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, it is a girl of nine who is no longer considered a child, and all of them have formed a consensus upon that a girl of nine is no longer considered a child, except if there happens to be a weakness in her intellect, or else, so when she reaches nine (years), she has reached puberty.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: One does not marry by Mut'a with the slave girl except with the permission of her owner.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if one were to marry the slave girl by Mut'a with the permission of her master.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with a man enjoying (in temporary marriage) the slave-girl of a woman; but as for the slave-girl of a man, he does not enjoy her except with her master's permission.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is your view if she gets pregnant?' He said, 'It is his child.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and others, said: The water (seed) of the man, he can place it wherever he desires, except that when a child comes, he cannot deny it, and he was strict in the denial of the child.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, all together from al-Fatah ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the stipulations in Mut'ah (temporary marriage), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The stipulation therein is with such and such (amount), and to such and such (term). So if she says, "Yes", that is allowed for him.' And do not say, as it has reached me, that the people of Iraq say: 'The water (seed) is mine, and the land is yours, and I will not irrigate your land with the water, and if something grows there, it belongs to the owner of the land.' For the two stipulations in one stipulation are void. And if she is granted a child, he accepts it, and the matter is clear. So whoever desires to confuse himself, let him confuse himself.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The most superior of intercessions is that you intercede between two people regarding a marriage until Allah brings them together.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who marries off a bachelor is among those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will look upon (with mercy) on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Bashir ibn Hamza, from a man from Quraish who said: A cousin of mine sent a message to me; she had much wealth. You know the abundance of men proposing to me, but I did not marry them myself. I did not send for you out of desire for men, but rather because it reached me that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted it in His Book, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) explained it in his Sunnah, but Zafar prohibited it. So I desired to obey Allah, Mighty and Majestic, above His Throne, and to obey the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and to disobey Zafar. So marry me by way of Mut'ah. So I said to her, 'Not until I go to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and consult him.' So I went to him and informed him. He said, 'Do it. May Allah send blessings upon both of you as spouses.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who marries the woman by Mut'ah for a known number of days. So she comes to him during one of her days and says, 'I have committed adultery before my coming to you, by an hour or by a day.' Would it be permissible for him to sleep with her, and she has acknowledged to him her adultery? He said: 'It is not befitting for him to sleep with her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who entered a slave girl to enjoy her, then forgot to stipulate (the term and dowry) until he had intercourse with her. Would the punishment of the adulterer be obligatory upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he enjoys her after the marriage, and he seeks forgiveness from Allah for what he did.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Isa ibn Suleiman, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man meets a woman and says to her, 'Marry yourself to me for a month,' and he does not specify the particular month. Then he goes away and meets her after years. He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'For him is his month if he had specified it, and if he did not specify it, there is no way for him upon her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with the man who marries by Mut'a with the woman upon his decision, but there is no alternative for him from giving her something, because if there was to occur an event with him (of death), there would not happen to be any inheritance for her.

Ali, from his father, from one of his companions, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'A man marries a woman by Mut'a, then her family members leap upon her, so they get her married without her permission, publicly, and the woman is a truthful woman. How would it be resolved?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should not enable her husband upon herself until her stipulations (of Mut'a) have expired, along with waiting period'. I said, 'If her stipulation is for a year and her husband is not patient for her, nor her family members, for a year?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let her first husband fear Allah, and let him give in charity upon her with the (unexpired) days, so she has been tried, and the house (environment) is a house of truce, and the Believers are in dissimulation'. I said, 'Supposing he were to donate upon her with her (unexpired) days, and she observes her waiting period, how would she deal?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When she is alone with the man (second husband), so let her said, 'O you! My family leapt over me, so they got me married to you without my consent, and did not seek instruction from me, and I now agree. Therefore, you should now solemnise my marriage with a correct marriage, with regards to what is between me and you'.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), said: I said to him, 'A man came to a woman and asked her to marry herself to him. She said, 'I marry myself to you on the condition that you seek from me whatever you wish of looking or touching, and attain from me what a man attains from his wife, except that you do not enter your private part into my private part, and you enjoy whatever you wish, for I fear the loss of virginity (or exposure).' He said, 'He has only what was stipulated.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all together, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me and to Suleiman ibn Khalid: 'I have prohibited the Mut'ah for the two of you from myself as long as you both are in Medina, because you two frequently come to me, so I fear that you would be seized, and it would be said, 'These are the companions of Ja'far.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman who permitted the private part of her slave girl to her son. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for him.' I said, 'So would her price be permissible for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but rather, it is permissible for him what she had permitted for him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man permits the private part of his slave girl to his brother.' He said, 'Yes, for him is what he permits for him from her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Bakr Al-Hazrami, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My wife permitted her slave girl to me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Marry her if you wish.' I said, 'Can I sell her?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, rather it is permitted to you from her whatever she has permitted.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Suleym al-Farra', from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who permits the private part of his slave girl for his brother, he said: 'There is no problem with that.' I said, 'Supposing he makes her give birth?' He said: 'His child would be entrusted to him and the slave girl would be returned to her owner.' I said, 'Supposing he had not permitted for him with regards to that?' He said: 'He had permitted that for him, so it was not safe for that to happen.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man permits his slave girl to his brother.' He said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'Supposing she were to come with a child?' He said, 'He would keep his child and return the slave girl to her owner.' I said, 'Supposing he had not permitted to him regarding that?' He said, 'He had permitted for him, and it was not safe for that to happen.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, and Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who says to his wife, 'Permit your slave girl to me, for I dislike that she should see me uncovered.' So she permitted her to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him from her except for that, and it is not for him to touch her, nor to sleep with her.' And Hisham added in it, 'Is it for him to sleep with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him except for that which she said.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a woman who permitted her slave girl to me, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is for you.' I said: 'But what if she were joking?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And how could it be for you what is in her heart? So, if you know that she was joking, then no.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Shibl, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A Muslim man was tried, so he committed fornication with the slave girl of his brother. So what is his repentance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He goes to him and informs him, and asks him to make that a permissibility for him, and he does not repeat.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'Supposing he does not make a permissibility for him from that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and he is an adulterer, a betrayer.' I said, 'So the Fire is his destination?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The intercession of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and our intercession is nullified by your sins, O group of the Shias! Therefore, do not keep repeating (your sins) and rely upon our intercession.' For by Allah, he will not attain our intercession when he indulges in this until he is hit by the pain of the Punishment and sees the horrors of Hell.

And by his chain, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleiman ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the man who marries the slave girl of his wife, then asks her to make him permissible (with her), but she refuses. So he says, 'Then I will divorce you,' and he avoids her bed, so she makes him permissible. He said: 'This is a usurper; so where is he from kindness?'

And from him, from Suleyman ibn Salih who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man deceives his wife, so he says, 'Make me free from your slave girl, that she may wipe my belly and massage my leg, and from my touching her,' meaning by his touching her is marriage (sleeping with her). He (peace be upon him) said: 'The trickery is in the Fire.' I said, 'If he does not intend trickery by that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Suleyman! I do not see you except that you are deceiving her regarding the mating of her slave girl.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Jameel ibn Darraj and Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the wife of a man who has a servant for her who had been immoral, so he became needy to her milk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Instruct her such, so she would permit her in order to make her milk to be good'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man has a slave girl for one of his sons, and his son is young.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to sleep with her until he appraises her at a just price, then takes her, and the price remains due upon him for his son.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man for whom one of his sons has a slave girl, while his sons are young, is it permissible for him to sleep with her? He (peace be upon him) said: He should evaluate her at a just price, then take her, and the price of her shall be upon him for his son.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'If a man has a slave girl for his son, is it permissible for him to sleep with her?' He said, 'He appraises her for himself with a price, and bears witness upon himself for her price; this is more beloved to me.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a slave girl of a young son of mine, 'Is it allowed for me to sleep with her?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'No, until you free her'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'I had gifted a slave girl to my daughter when I married her off. She remained with her in her husband's house until her husband died, and then she returned to me, along with the slave girl. Is it permissible for me to have sexual relations with the slave girl?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Assess her at a just price, and bear witness to that, then if you wish, have relations with her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, said: I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl and did not have a husband for her. Does he clear her womb? He said: Yes. I said: If she has not menstruated? So he said: Her matter is difficult. So if he goes to her, he should not discharge the seed until it becomes clear whether she is pregnant or not. I said: And in how much time would it become clear for him? He said: In forty-five days.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who bought a slave girl whose owner had not yet had intercourse with her: Does he clear her womb? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. I said: A slave girl who has not yet menstruated, what is done with her? He (peace be upon him) said: Her case is difficult, except that if he has intercourse with her, he should not ejaculate into her until it becomes clear to him if she is pregnant. I said: And in how much time does it become clear to him? He (peace be upon him) said: In forty-five nights.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hisham ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah or to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'When a man buys a slave girl who has not yet reached puberty, or who has despaired of menstruation,' he said: 'There is no harm in not clearing her womb.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who buys a slave girl from another man, and the seller says, 'I have not slept with her,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he trusts him, there is no harm in him going to her.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who sells a slave girl to another man: 'It is upon him to clear her womb before he sells her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Rabie ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who had not reached menstruation, and pregnancy was feared for her. He said: 'The one who sells her must clear her womb by five and forty nights, and the one who buys her must clear her womb by five and forty nights.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who buys the slave girl and she has not menstruated. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should isolate her for a month if she had been touched.' He said, 'So what is your view if he buys her and she is pure, and her owner claims that he has not slept with her since she became pure?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is trustworthy with you, then let him touch her.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is the difficult matter. So, if you must do it, be careful not to let the water descend into her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl and she was menstruating (ṭāmith). Should he clear her womb with another menstruation, or would this menstruation suffice for him? He said: No, but this menstruation suffices this menstruation suffices for him. If he clears her with another, there is no problem; it is in the nature of preference (fadl).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Humran, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a slave girl: Can he have sexual intercourse with her before the period of gestation (istibra') is completed and she has not been cleared? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, when the obligation is established for her and she becomes part of his wealth. So if she dies, she is from his wealth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who bought a slave girl from a man for a specified price, then they separated. He (peace be upon him) said: The sale is obligated, and it is not for him to sleep with her while she is with her owner until he takes possession of her and informs her owner; and the price, if they did not stipulate it, is cash.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Adhere to the mothers of the children, for in their wombs is the blessing.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from one of his companions from Abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Seek the children from the mothers, for in their wombs is the blessing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Rifa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), so I said, 'I buy a slave girl, and she stays with me for months and does not menstruate, and that is not due to old age. So I show her to the women, and they say, 'She is not pregnant.' So, is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her in her private part?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Menstruation can be withheld by the wind without pregnancy. So there is no problem if you touch her in the private part.' I said, 'But if she is pregnant, what is for me from her, if I intend?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is besides the private part.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the slave girl whom a man buys while she is pregnant, he said: He should not go near her until she gives birth to her child.

Sahl, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man buys a slave girl while she is pregnant; what is permissible for him from her?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Whatever is besides the private part.' I said, 'So he buys a young slave girl who has not yet menstruated and is not a virgin; does he have to observe her waiting period (istibra')?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Her matter is difficult. When it is the likes of her, suspend her and let her free her womb (i.e., observe a waiting period).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the pregnant slave girl whom a man buys, so he attains from her besides the private part. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' I said, 'Supposing he attains from her in that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you intend deception?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who emancipates the slave girl and says, 'Your dower is your emancipation,' so he said: 'It is good.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a slave girl and intends to emancipate her and then marry her: does he make her emancipation her dowry, or does he emancipate her then give her a dowry? And is there a waiting period for her from him, and how long is her waiting period if he emancipates her? And is it permissible for him to marry her without a dowry, and how long is her waiting period from someone else? He said: He makes her emancipation her dowry if he wishes, and if he wishes he can emancipate her then give her a dowry. And if her emancipation is her dowry, then she observes a waiting period, and it is not permissible to marry her when he emancipates her except with a dowry. And the man cannot have intercourse with the woman when he marries her until he gives her something, even if it is a dirham.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man says to his slave girl, 'I emancipate you and marry you, and I make your dower your emancipation,' then it is valid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a wife and a concubine, and it becomes inevitable for him to emancipate his concubine and marry her. He (peace be upon him) said: If he wishes, he stipulates upon her that her emancipation is her dower, for that is permissible; or he stipulates upon her, if he wishes, he divides (his time) for her, and if he wishes he does not divide; and if he wishes he prefers the free woman over her. So if she is pleased with that, there is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, and Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about a slave man marrying four free women. He said: No, but he can marry two free women, and if he wishes, he can marry four slave girls.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the owned slave, what is permissible for him from women? He said: Two free women, or four slave girls. He said: And there is no problem if his master permits him to buy from his wealth, if he has a slave girl or slave girls whom he may have relations with, and his slave girls are permissible for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid together, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about the owned slave (male or female), how many women are permissible for him to marry? He said: Two free women, or four slave girls. And he said: There is no problem if he has wealth in his possession and is permitted in trade, that he may keep as many concubines as he wishes from the slave girls and have relations with them.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the owned slave whose master permits him to buy from his wealth a slave girl, two, or three, and his enslaved women are permissible for him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He sets a limit for him which he does not exceed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-H ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man permits his slave to acquire concubines from his wealth, then he may buy as many as he desires, after he has been permitted to do so.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not permissible for the slave to free himself, nor to marry, nor to give from his wealth, except with the permission of his master.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man whose slave married without his permission, so he consummated the marriage with her. Then the master learned of that. He said: 'That is up to his master; if he wishes, he separates them, and if he wishes, he validates their marriage. If he separates them, the woman keeps what she was given as dower, unless he was excessive, in which case she is given an excessive dower. And if he validates the marriage, they remain upon their first marriage.' I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'For the basis of the marriage was disobedience.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He came to something permissible, and he did not disobey Allah. He disobeyed his master, and did not disobey Allah. That is not like coming to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited for him, such as marriage during a waiting period and similar cases.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a slave who married without the permission of his master, so he said: 'That is up to his master; if he wishes, he validates it, and if he wishes, he separates them.' I said, 'May Allah keep you well! Al-Hakam ibn Uteybah, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and their companions say that the origin of the marriage is invalid, and the master's validation is not permissible for him.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He did not disobey Allah; he only disobeyed his master. So when he validates it, it is valid for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'I was a slave owned by a group of people, and I married a free woman without the permission of my masters. Then they emancipated me after that. Should I renew my marriage with her when I was emancipated?' He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Did they know that you had married a woman while you were their slave?' He said: 'Yes, and they were silent regarding me and did not reproach me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their silence from you after their knowledge is an acknowledgment from them. Remain upon your first marriage.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding an owned slave who married without the permission of his master, has he disobeyed Allah?' He said: 'He disobeyed his master.' I said, 'Is it prohibited?' He said: 'I do not claim that it is prohibited, and say to him that he should not do it except with the permission of his master.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any free woman who marries herself to a slave without the permission of his master has legalized her private parts, and there is no dower for her.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who marries without the permission of her owner. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is prohibited for her, and it is adultery.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who marries without the permission of her masters. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is prohibited for her, and it is adultery.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a male slave, so there happens to be for his master or for his mistress, a slave girl. So he intends to unite the two of them. Would he marry her to him with a valid marriage, or would it suffice him if he says, 'I have married you to so-and-so,' and he gives something from himself, or on behalf of the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and even if it is a mud (small measure), and I have seen him give a dirham.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Ishaq al-Kaffaf, from Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Would it please you if you had a guide, O Abu Harun?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' So he gave me thirty dinars and said: 'Buy a Kasoumiyya servant.' So I bought him. When I went to Hajj, I visited him. He said to him: 'How do you find your guide, O Abu Harun?' He said, 'Good.' So he gave him twenty-five dinars and said to him: 'Buy a Shamiyya slave girl, for their children are a delight.' So I bought a Shamiyya slave girl and married her to him. She bore me three daughters. I gifted one of them to one of the children of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I hope that He will make my reward from it Paradise. And two daughters remained, which brought me thousands of pleasures.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a slave girl whom he would have sexual relations with, and news reached him that she had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can have sexual relations with her, for her sale is her divorce, and that is because they are both unable to do anything regarding their matter when they are sold.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Abi Hamid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who is sold and for her is a husband, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Her sale is her divorce'.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, from Abu Ja’far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), both said: The one who buys a slave girl who has a husband for her, so her sale is her divorce. So, if the buyer so desires to, he effects separation between them, and if he so desires to he leaves them both upon their marriage.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) He said: The divorce of the slave girl is her sale, or the sale of her husband. And he said regarding the man who marries his slave girl to a free man, then sells her: It is a separation of what is between them, unless the buyer desires to leave them (to remain married).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Zur'a, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who had a slave girl between them, so they married her to a man. Then a man bought part of the two shares. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes prohibited to him by his purchase of her, and that is that her sale is her divorce, unless he buys her from all of them entirely.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a slave girl in common with another partner, so one of them emancipates his share. The slave girl says to the one who did not emancipate: 'I do not desire you; appraise me and leave me as I am, serving you.' What is your view if the one who did not emancipate the other half intends to have sexual relations with her? Is that for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to do that, because there do not be two private parts for the woman. And it is not befitting for him to make her serve [exclusively], but he should make her serve [alternately]. So if she refuses, there is a day for herself and a day for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who share a slave girl, so one of them emancipates his share. The slave girl says to the one who did not emancipate his share, 'I do not want you to evaluate me; leave me as I am, and I will serve you.' And he wanted to marry the other half. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to do so, because there are not two private parts for the woman, and it is not befitting that he makes her serve, but he should evaluate her so he can make her work for it (to be paid off).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad ibn [Qays], from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a slave girl shared between two men who both emancipated her together. Then one of the two permitted her private part to his partner. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for him. And whichever of the two dies before his companion, half of her becomes free from the side of the one who died, and half remains managed (as a slave).' I said: 'What is your view if the remaining one of the two wants to touch her, is that for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless he decides her emancipation and marries her with her pleasure, similar to what he intends.' I said to him: 'Hasn't half of her become free? She has controlled half her neck, and the other half is for the remaining one of the two?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'If she makes her master permissible regarding her private part and permits it to him, is that allowed for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not allowed for him.' I said: 'Why is it not allowed for her, just as you permitted the one who had half of her, when he permitted her private part to his partner from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the free woman does not gift her private part, nor lend it, nor permit it. But for her from herself is a day, and for the one who managed her is a day. If he wishes to marry her by Mut'ah with something during the day in which she controls herself, let him enjoy her with something, little or much.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who shared a slave girl, so they married her to a man. Then the man bought one of the two shares. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes prohibited to him.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shaza'an, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a slave girl whom he would sleep with, and news reached him that she had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can sleep with her, for her sale is her divorce, and that is because they are both unable to do anything regarding their matter when she is sold.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie ibn Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who is sold and for her is a husband, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Her sale is her divorce'.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, from Abu Ja’far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who buys a slave girl who has a husband for her, so her sale is her divorce. So, if the buyer so desires to, he effects separation between them, and if he so desires to he leaves them both upon their marriage.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The divorce of the slave girl is her sale, or the sale of her husband. And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the man who marries his slave girl to a free man, then sells her: He (the free husband) is separated from her, unless the buyer wishes to leave them (to remain married).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Zur'a, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who had a slave girl between them, so they married her to a man. Then a man bought part of their shares. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes prohibited to him by his purchase of her, and that is that her sale is her divorce, unless he buys her from all of them entirely.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a concubine of a man who gave birth to a son for her master. Then he separated from her, so he married her to his slave. Then her master died and emancipated her. So her son inherited her husband from his father. Then her son died, so she inherited her husband from her son. So they came disputing, the man saying, 'She is my wife, and I have not divorced her,' and the woman saying, 'He is my slave, and he should not copulate with me.' So the woman said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! My master kept me as a concubine, so he made me give birth to a son. Then he separated from me, and married me to this slave of his. So when death presented itself to my master, he emancipated me at his death, and I am the wife of this one, and he has become a slave owned by my son whom I bore from my master. And my son died, so I inherited him. Is it correct for him to copulate with me?' He said to her, 'Has he copulated with you since he became your slave and you were willing?' She said, 'No, O Amir al-Mu'minin.' He said, 'If you had done it, I would have stoned you. Go, for he is your slave. There is no authority for him upon you. If you wish, you can sell him; if you wish, you can manumit him; if you wish, you can emancipate him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who married a mother of a child of a slave of his. Then the man died, so his son inherited her. So there came to be a share for him in the husband of his mother. Then the son died. Would his mother inherit him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. I said, So, when she inherits him, how would she deal, and he is her husband? He (peace be upon him) said: She would separate from him, and there would be no way for him over her, and he would be her slave.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra and Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a woman who has a slave husband, so his master died and she inherited him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no marriage between the two of them'.

Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a free woman who is under the ownership of a slave (as his wife), so she buys him. Would his marriage be invalidated? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, because he is an owned slave who is not able to possess anything.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who had a slave husband, so she inherited him and emancipated him: Would they remain upon their first marriage? He said: No, but they must renew with another marriage.

Humayr ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and others, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman who inherited her husband, so she emancipated him. Would they remain upon their first marriage? He said: No, but they must renew their marriage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave girl who was under a slave [husband], so the slave girl was emancipated. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her command is in her hands; if she wishes, she keeps herself with her husband, and if she wishes, she removes herself from him.' And he mentioned that Barirah was with a husband of hers, and she was an owned slave. So Ayesha bought her and emancipated her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave her a choice and said: 'If she wishes, she stays with her husband, and if she wishes, she separates from him.' And it was so that her masters, who had sold her, had stipulated upon Ayesha that their mastership would be for her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The mastership is for the one who emancipates.' And meat was given in charity to Barirah, so she gifted it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So Ayesha kept it aside and said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) does not eat the meat of charity.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came, and the meat was kept aside, so he said: 'What is the matter with this meat not having been cooked?' So she said, 'O Messenger of Allah! It was given in charity to Barirah, and you do not eat the charity.' So he said: 'It is charity for her, and for us it is a gift.' Then he ordered with cooking it. Thus, there flowed three Sunnahs in it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Barirah had a husband, so when she was emancipated, she was given the choice.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you emancipate your two slaves, a man and his wife, there is no marriage between them.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you wish for him to be her husband, that is with a dower.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who marries his slave to his slave girl, then he emancipes her. Would she have a choice regarding him or not?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, she would have a choice in it when she is emancipated.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from the one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding Barirah: there are three Sunnahs when she was emancipated: regarding the choice, and regarding the charity, and regarding the mastership.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: (He) mentioned that Bureyra was a slave of Ayesha and had a husband for her who was a slave. So when she was emancipated, Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: ‘Choose! If you so desire to you can stay with your husband, and if your so desire to, so no’.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a pregnant slave girl, and her pregnancy had become evident, so he slept with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done.' I said: 'So what do you say regarding it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Did he isolate (withdraw) from her or not?' I said: 'Answer me regarding the two aspects.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had isolated from her, let him fear Allah and not repeat (the act), and if he had not isolated from her, he should not sell that child, nor inherit him, but he should emancipate him and allocate for him something from his wealth by which he can live, for he has nourished him with his seed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever has intercourse with a slave girl who is pregnant by another man, then upon him is that he should emancipate her child, and he should not enslave, because the water participated in him to complete the child.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) seeking his counsel regarding marriage, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Marry, and let it be with one who is of Religion, may your hands be enriched.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Al-Nadr, from one of his companions, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who marries a woman intending her wealth, Allah will make that wealth his reliance.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man marries a woman for her beauty or her wealth, he is left to those (i.e., he may get only that), and when he marries her for her religion, Allah will grant him both beauty and wealth.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who belongs to a man, whom he has sexual relations with, and she gives birth, and she attaches the child to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Does the man accuse her, or does his family accuse her?' I said: 'As for apparent [evidence], no.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then the child is necessitated upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleym, the mawla of Tarbal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who slept with a slave girl of his, and that he used to send her regarding his needs, and that she became pregnant, and that news of immorality about her reached him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When she gives birth, he keeps the child, so he should not sell him, and he makes for him a share in his house.' He said, 'It was said to him: A man slept with a slave girl of his, and that he did not used to send her regarding his needs, and that he accused her, and she became pregnant.' So he said: 'When she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and he makes for him a share from his house and his wealth, and this is not the like of that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from a man from our companions, from Abdul Hameed ibn Ismail, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a slave girl whom he slept with, and she used to go out regarding his needs. So she became pregnant, and he feared that the child may not be from him. How should he deal with it? Should he sell the slave girl and the child? He (peace be upon him) said: He sells the slave girl but does not sell the child, and he does not inherit him anything from his inheritance.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his slave girl who used to go and come, and he had isolated himself from her and there did not happen to be anything from him to her. What do you say regarding the child? He (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that this should not be sold, O Saeed!' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Does he accuse her?' So I said, 'As for an apparent accusation, no.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So, does his family accuse her?' So I said, 'As for something apparent, no.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So how can you have the leeway that the child would not be necessitated on you?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza and Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel and Ibn Bukayr, regarding the child of a free man and a slave woman, he said: 'He goes to the free one from them'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail, from Abu al-Fadl al-Makfouf (the author of Al-Arabiyya), from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl al-Taqi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about a male slave who marries a free woman, what is the status of the child? He said: 'Free.' I said, 'And if a free man marries a slave woman?' He said: 'The child is attached to the free status, wherever it is. If the mother is free, he is freed with his mother, and if the father is free, he is freed with his father.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asami narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi from Ali ibn Asbaat from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Jameel ibn Darraj who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When the male slave marries a free woman, his children are free, and when the free man marries a slave woman, his children are free.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the free man marrying the slave woman, or a slave marrying a free woman. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The child would not be enslaved when one of its parents was free. It would be attached with the free one of the two, whichever of them, be it a father or a mother'.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all together, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:' When the slave marries the free woman, his children are free, and when the free man marries the slave woman, his children are (also) free.
