Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the slave who has a free woman under him (as a wife), he said: His children are free. So if the slave is emancipated, he attaches to his father.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a free man who marries a slave girl of a group of people, are the children slaves or free? He said: If one of the parents is free, then the children are free. A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a free man, a slave, and a polytheist have intercourse with one woman in one pure period, and they claim the child, a lot is drawn between them, and the child belongs to the one whose lot comes out.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Ali (peace be upon him) to Yemen, so he (peace be upon him) said to him (peace be upon him) when he returned: 'Tell me the most wondrous thing that came to you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah! A group of people came to me who had purchased a slave girl, and they all had intercourse with her in one period of purity. So she gave birth to a boy, and they disputed over him, all of them claiming him. So I drew lots among them and assigned him to the one whose lot came out, and I guaranteed their share.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no group of people who dispute and then delegate their affair to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that the lot of the rightful one comes out.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When there is a slave girl for one of you, whom he sleeps with, and then he frees her, and she observes her waiting period and marries, if she gives birth in five months, then the child is from her master who freed her; and if she gives birth after marrying in six months, then the child is for her later husband.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying, and he was asked about a man who bought a slave girl, then had intercourse with her before she had completed her istibra' (period of waiting to confirm pregnancy). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done. He should seek forgiveness from Allah and not repeat (the act of selling without istibra' or the specific fault).' I said, 'Suppose he sold her to another, and did not clear her womb (did not perform istibra'), then the second owner sold her to another man, so he had intercourse with her, and did not clear her womb, so her pregnancy became manifest in the presence of the third?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (the last owner who had intercourse with her), and for the adulterer (or the one who had intercourse without full certainty of lineage) are the stones.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan from Sa'id al-A'raj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about two men who had intercourse with a slave girl during one period of purity (from menstruation). For whom would the child be? He said: For the one in whose possession she is, due to the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'The child belongs to the bed (the one with whom she resides), and for the adulterer is the stone.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, and Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel, and Ibn Bukayr, regarding the child of the free man and the slave woman, he said: 'He goes to the free one from them'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail, from Abu al-Fadl al-Makfuf (the author of Al-Arabiyya), from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl al-Taqi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about a male slave who marries a free woman, what is the status of the child? He said: 'Free.' I said: 'And if a free man marries a slave woman?' He said: 'The child is attached to the free parent. If the mother is free, he is freed with his mother, and if the father is free, he is freed with his father.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asami narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi from Ali ibn Asbaat from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Jameel ibn Darraj who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When the slave marries the free woman, so his children are free, and when the free man marries the slave woman, so his children are free.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the free man marrying the slave woman, or a slave marrying a free woman. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The child would not be enslaved when one of its parents was free. Indeed, it is attached to the free one of the two, whichever of them, be it a father or a mother.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbaat and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all together, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the slave marries the free woman, so his children are free, and when the free man marries the slave woman, so his children are free'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the slave man who has a free woman as his wife, he (peace be upon him) said: 'His children are free. So if the slave is emancipated, he joins his father (in terms of lineage/status).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a free man who marries a slave girl of a group of people, are the children slaves or free? He said: If one of the two parents is free, then the children are free. A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a woman who let herself be enabled upon by her slave, so he slept with her, that she would be whipped one hundred lashes and the slave would be whipped fifty lashes, and he would be sold for a price cheaper than her. He (peace be upon him) said: And it is prohibited upon every Muslim that he sells to her an adult slave, after that.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Abbas, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the free woman who is under the ownership of a slave (as his wife), and she buys him [to free him]. Does that invalidate his marriage? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, because he is an owned slave who has no power over anything.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The wife of Usman bin Maz'un came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Usman fasts during the day and prays during the night.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out angry, carrying his slippers, until he came to Usman and found him praying. So Usman finished his prayer when he saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said to him, 'O Usman! Allah the Exalted did not send me with monasticism, but He sent me with the easy, tolerant Hanifiyyah. I fast and I pray and I touch my wife. So whoever loves my nature, let him follow my Sunnah, and from my Sunnah is marriage.'

Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man: 'Did you become a fasting person this morning?' He said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Have you fed a poor person?' He said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'So return to your family, for it is charity from you upon them'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has his wife with him on a journey and cannot find water; can he sleep with his wife? He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like him to do so, except if he fears upon himself.' I said: 'Does he seek pleasure thereby, or is he craving for women?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The craving is [considered] fearing upon himself.' I said: 'He seeks pleasure thereby?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible.' I said: 'For it is reported from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) asked him about this, so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Go to your wife, you will be rewarded.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Do I go to them and get rewarded?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Just as when you go to the forbidden, you are burdened [with sin], so similarly, when you go to the permissible, you will be rewarded.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not see that he, when he fears upon himself, so he goes to the permissible, would be rewarded?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Is'haq ibn Ibrahim Al-Ju'fi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered the chamber of Umm Salma (peace be upon her) and smelled a good aroma, so he said: "Has Al-Hawla come to you?"' She said: 'It is she. She is complaining about her husband.' So Al-Hawla came out to him and said: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! My husband has turned away from me.' He said: 'Increase it (the perfume), O Hawla.' She said: 'I have not left any good perfume that I do not use it for him, and he turns away from me.' He said: 'But if only he knew what is for him with his facing towards you.' She said: 'And what is for him with facing towards me?' He said: 'Indeed, when he faces you, two angels encircle him, so he is like the striker of his sword in the Way of Allah. And when he copulates, the sins fall off from him as the leaves of the tree fall. And when he bathes, he is stripped of the sins.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, three women came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so one of them said, 'My husband does not eat meat,' and the other said, 'My husband does not smell perfume,' and the third said, 'My husband does not approach women.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out dragging his robe until he ascended the pulpit. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'What is the matter with a group of people from my companions who do not eat meat, nor smell perfume, nor approach women?' Indeed, I eat meat, I smell perfume, and I approach women. So whoever shows preference for my Sunnah, he is from me.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who loves that he be upon my fitrah (natural disposition), let him follow my Sunnah, and indeed, marriage is from my Sunnah.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Prophet of Allah, I have a cousin whom I have approved for her beauty, grace, and piety, but she is barren.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not marry her.' He (peace be upon him) mentioned that Yusuf ibn Yaqoub met his brother and said, 'O my brother, how did you manage to marry women after me?' He said, 'My father instructed me and said: If you can have offspring who will make the earth heavy with glorification (of Allah), then do so.' So I did. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man came the next day to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said something similar to him. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: Marry a barren-less (fertile) one, for I will boast about you among the nations on the Day of Resurrection.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), What is the 'saw'a' (barren-less/fertile)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The ugly one.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry a virgin and a fertile woman, and do not marry a beautiful woman who is barren, for I will boast about you to the nations on the Day of Resurrection.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, from the one who narrated it, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the scarcity of my children, and that I had no children. So he said to me: 'When you go to Iraq, marry a woman, and it does not matter if she is ugly.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is the ugly one?' He said: 'A woman in whom there is ugliness, for they bear more children.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Saeed al-Raqqi, who said: Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fary narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man: 'Marry the child-bearing one who is not necessarily beautiful, and do not marry the beautiful barren woman, for I will pride myself with you among the nations on the Day of Resurrection. Or do you not know that the children are beneath the Throne seeking forgiveness for their parents? Ibrahim (peace be upon him) cuddles them, and Sarah (peace be upon him) nourishes them in a mountain of Musk, Amber, and Saffron.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you copulates, let him not come to her as the bird comes [quickly]. Let him endure and let him linger.' Some of them said, 'And let him linger.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr al-Nahhas, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding the man who copulates, so his garment falls off from him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Hammam, from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who kisses the front private part of the wife. He said, 'There is no problem'.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of speaking at the meeting of the two circumcised parts (penis and anus), for it causes dumbness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who applies dye (henna) should not copulate.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Why should the one who applies dye not copulate?' He said: 'Because he is restricted (by the dye layer).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Aban from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, 'One who has dyed (his hair) does not go to bed with his wife.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, why does one who has dyed not go to bed with his wife?' He said, 'Because he is confined.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Is intercourse disliked during a specific time among the times, even if it is permissible?' He said, 'Yes. Between the emergence of dawn and the emergence of the sun, and from the setting of the sun to the disappearance of the redness (shafaq), and on the day in which the sun is eclipsed, and on the night in which the moon is eclipsed, and on the night and the day in which there is the black wind, the red wind, and the yellow wind, and the day and the night in which there is an earthquake.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spent the night with one of his wives during a night in which the moon was eclipsed. So there did not occur from him during that night what usually occurred from him during other nights, until he morninged. So she said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah! Is it due to hatred from you during this night?' He said, 'No, but this sign appeared during this night, so I disliked that I should delight and be engrossed therein. And Allah has rebuked a people, so the Mighty and Majestic said in His Book: "If they see a fragment of the sky falling, they will say: Piled up clouds." So leave them until they meet their day on which they will be thunderstruck.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'And I swear by Allah, whoever has intercourse during these times which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade, and the news has reached him, will be granted a child, but he will see in that child what he does not like.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The one who comes to his wife during the obliteration (of the moon at the end of) the month, so he would not be safe from the miscarriage of the child.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: It is disliked for the man, when he returns from travel, to visit his family at night until morning.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I dislike for my community that a man should have intercourse with his wife during the middle of the month or at the beginning of the crescent, for the rebellious devils and Jinn overwhelm the children of Adam, causing them to become insane and deranged. Do you not see that the afflicted ones suffer epileptic fits during the middle of the month and at the beginning of the crescent?'

Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman from Misma' Abu Sayyar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I dislike for my nation that a man goes to bed with his wife in the middle of the month or at the new moon, for the rebels of the devils and Jinn overwhelm the children of Adam, causing them to become possessed and insane. Have you not seen that the one afflicted by epilepsy is struck down in the middle of the month and at the new moon?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Is'hāq ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Rashid, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man should not have intercourse with his wife or his slave girl while a child is in the room, for that is from what begets adultery.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd from his father from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'By the One in whose Hand is my soul, if a man engages in sexual intercourse with his wife while a child is in the house, awake, seeing them and hearing their speech and their breathing, the child will not escape (from being affected), whether a boy, he becomes a fornicator, or a girl, she becomes a fornicator.' And 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), whenever he intended to engage in sexual intercourse with his wife, would close the door, lower the curtains, and send the servants out.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! I am a man who has aged, and I have married a young virgin woman, and I have not yet entered with her, and I fear that when she comes to me, she will see me and dislike me due to my dyeing and my old age.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When she comes, instruct her before she reaches you that she should be in ablution. Then you do not reach her until you have performed ablution and prayed two cycles. Then glorify Allah, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Then supplicate, and instruct those who are with her to say Ameen to your supplication, and say: O Allah! Grant me her affection, her love, and her pleasure, and make me pleased with her, and gather us together with the best of gatherings and the most comforting of unions, for You love the permissible and dislike the forbidden.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And know that the affection is from Allah, and the separation is from Satan, to make disliked what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has permitted.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you enter into intimacy with your wife, take her by the nasa (forehead/hair), face the Qiblah, and say: 'O Allah, by Your trust I have taken her, and by Your words I have permitted her. So if You have decreed for me a child from her, make it blessed, pious, from the Shiah of the Family of Muhammad, and do not make for Satan any share or portion in it.'

From him, from Abu Yusuf, from Al-Mitham, raising it, he said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I have married, so supplicate to Allah for me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Say, O Allah! By Your words I have permitted her, and by Your Security I have taken her. O Allah! Make her child-bearing, affectionate, not separating, consuming from what is comfortable, and not asking about what is not available.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayn, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man intends to marry a woman, let him say, 'I affirm the Covenant which Allah took: to keep [them] in good fellowship or to let [them] go with kindness.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the man when he approaches his wife, and he fears that Satan may share/participate with him, he said: He should say 'Bismillah' (In the Name of Allah), and he should seek Refuge with Allah from Satan.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you copulates, let him say: In the Name of Allah, and with Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from me and keep Satan away from what You have granted me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So if Allah decrees a child between the two of them, Satan will not harm him in any way, ever.'

And from him, from his father, from Hamza ibn Abdullah, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu al-Walid, from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad! Whenever you go to your wife, so which thing are you saying?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and can I endure saying anything?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Say, O Allah! With Your Words do I permit her private parts, and by Your Security I take her.' So if You were to Judge anything for me in her womb, so Make it to be pious, pure, and do not Make a participation for the Satan to be in it.' He (Abu Baseer) said, 'I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And there happens to be a participation for the Satan therein?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Have you not heard the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: and share with them in wealth and the children.' The Satan comes over, so he sits just as the man sits (upon the wife) and descends just as the man descends'. I said, 'And by which thing is that recognised?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By love for us and hatred for us'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the two seeds, one for the human and one for the Satan, when they are combined. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Sometimes the creation is from one of them, and sometimes the creation is from both of them together.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about coitus interruptus, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to the man'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with coitus interruptus (al-'azl) from the free woman if her husband likes it, and if she dislikes it, she has no authority in the matter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the coitus interruptus, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to the man; he can place it (seed) wherever he so desires.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) did not see a problem with al-'azl (coitus interruptus). So everything from which Allah took the covenant, it comes out. Even if it be upon a solid rock.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The sense of honor (ghayrah) is not except for the men, and as for the women, then that from them is envy. And the sense of honor is for the men, and for that reason Allah prohibited it upon the women, except for her husband, and He permitted for the men four (wives), and indeed Allah is more Benevolent than that He would test them with the sense of honor and permit for the men along with her three (more).

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Sa'd ibn al-Jallab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah (Exalted and Majestic) did not make al-ghayrah (sense of honor/jealousy) for the women, and rather it is the evil ones of them who express it; as for the believing women, they do not. But rather, Allah made al-ghayrah for the men because He permitted the man four (wives) and whatever his right hand possesses, and did not make it for the woman except for her husband. So if she were to intend someone else along with him, she would be an adulteress in the Presence of Allah. He said, and Al-Qasim ibn Yahya reported it from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), except that he said: 'So if she were to be immoral with someone else along with him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, raised it, saying: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting, a nude woman came until she stood before him, so she said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have committed fornication, so purify me.' He said. And a man came running after her and threw a cloak over her. So he (peace be upon him) said, 'And what is she to you?' So he said, 'My companion, O Messenger of Allah. I was alone with my slave girl, so she did what you see.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Keep her close to you.' Then he said, 'Indeed, the jealous one cannot distinguish between the top of the valley and the bottom of it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Yusuf ibn Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Jabir who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The 'ghayrah' (sense of honour/ jealousy) of women is envy, and envy is the root of disbelief. Indeed, when women feel ghayrah, they become angry, and when they are angry, they disbelieve, except for the Muslim women among them.

From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, who said: A man mentioned his wife to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), praising her well. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Have you made her jealous (with ghayrah)?' He said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So make her feel jealous.' So he made her feel jealous, and she remained steadfast (in her loyalty). So he said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have made her feel jealous, and she remained steadfast.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'She is as you say.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The woman is jealous of the man, causing him distress.' He said, 'That is from love.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A woman came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband upon the wife?' He said to her, 'That she obeys him and does not disobey him, nor gives charity from his house except by his permission, nor fasts voluntarily except by his permission, nor prevents him from herself even if she is on the back of a hump (camel), nor goes out from her house except by his permission. And if she goes out from her house without his permission, the angels of the sky, the angels of the earth, the angels of wrath, and the angels of mercy curse her until she returns to her house.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, who has the greatest right upon the man?' He said, 'His father.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, who has the greatest right upon the woman?' He said, 'Her husband.' She said, 'So what right do I have upon him similar to what he has upon me?' He said, 'No, and not even one from every hundred.' He said, so she said, 'By the One Who sent you with the Truth as a Prophet, no man will ever own my neck.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Sa'd ibn Abi Amr al-Jallab, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any woman who spends the night while her husband is displeased with her regarding a right, her prayer will not be accepted until he is pleased with her; and any woman who perfumes herself for other than her husband, her prayer will not be accepted until she bathes from her perfume as she bathes from her major ritual impurity (janabah).'

Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There are three for whom their deeds will not be raised: an absconder slave, and a woman whose husband is angered upon her, and the one who drags his trousers in arrogance.
A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Hassan, from Musa bin Bakr, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said: The jihad of the wife is goodness with the husband.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Munzir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three are there for whom a Prayer is not accepted: an absconder slave from his masters until he places his hand in their hands, and a woman who spent the night while her husband was angry with her, and a man who leads a group in prayer while they are displeased with him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Khalid, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Amr ibn Jubayr Al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband upon the woman?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'There are many more than that.' She said, 'So inform me about something from it.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'It is not for her to fast except with his permission, meaning voluntary fasting, and she should not leave her house except with his permission, and it is upon her to perfume herself with the best of her perfume, and wear the best of her clothes, and adorn herself with the best of her adornments, and present herself to him morning and evening, and much more than that are his rights upon her.'

From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'What is the right of the husband upon the wife?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'That she answers his call to intimacy, even if she is on a camel's hump (from fatigue or position), and does not give anything (of her body or self) except with his permission. If she does so, the burden (of disobedience) is upon her and the reward is for him. And that she does not spend a night while he is angry with her.' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, even if he is unjust?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Yes.' She said, 'By the One Who sent you with the Truth, I will never marry a husband!'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to the women: 'Do not prolong your Prayers in order to prevent your husbands.'

From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Jameela, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for one of her needs, so he said to her: 'Perhaps you are from the Musawwifaat (women who delay).' She said, 'And what are the Musawwifaat, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The woman whose husband calls her for one of his needs, but she does not cease to delay him until her husband becomes drowsy and sleeps. That is the one whom the Angels do not cease cursing until her husband wakes up.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the women from being celibate and from withholding themselves from husbands.

Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the woman to neglect herself, even if she attaches a necklace to her neck, nor is it befitting that she leaves her hand from the dyeing, even if she wipes it with a touch of henna, even if she was old.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdul Samad ibn Basheer, who said: A woman came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May Allah keep you well! I am a celibate woman.' He said, 'And what is celibacy with you?' She said, 'I do not get married.' He said, 'And why?' She said, 'I seek merit by that.' He said, 'Leave! If that were merit, Fatima (peace be upon her) would have been more rightful for it than you, for there is no one who precedes her to the merit.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abu Maryam from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How can one of you strike the woman and then continue to embrace her?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Anbasa, from Abbad ibn Ziyad Al-Asadi, from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him); and Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Asimi, from the one who narrated it to him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad Al-Basri, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In the letter of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Do not give the woman authority in matters that exceed her own nature, for that is more favorable for her state, more relaxing for her mind, and more lasting for her beauty. Indeed, the woman is an aroma (delicate) and not a wrestling champion (strong/dominant). Do not let her soul surpass her honor, lower her gaze with your covering, restrain her with your veil, and do not incite her to intercede for others so that the one for whom she intercedes may incline against you along with her. Preserve a remnant of yourself from them, for restraining yourself from them while they see you as capable is better than them seeing you in a state of breaking apart.' Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Hasani, from Ali ibn Abdak, from Al-Hasan ibn Tariq ibn Nasih, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), similar to it, except that he said: 'The Commander of the Faithful, may Allah's prayers be upon him, wrote this letter to his son Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the right of the wife upon her husband such that if he fulfills it, he is considered doing good?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should satisfy her hunger and clothe her, and if she is ignorant (of faults), he should forgive her.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There was a wife with my father (peace be upon him) who used to hurt him, so he would forgive her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Hamza, from Amr ibn Jubayr Al-Arami, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A woman came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him about the right of the husband upon the wife. He informed her. Then she said, 'And what is her right upon him?' He said: 'He must clothe her from nakedness and feed her from hunger, and if she sins, he must forgive her.' She said, 'So is there nothing for her upon him besides this?' He said, 'No.' She said, 'No, by Allah, I will not get married ever!' Then she turned to leave. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Return.' So she returned. He said, 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: And if they restrain themselves, it is better for them.'

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Fear Allah regarding the two weak ones, meaning by that the orphan and the women, and indeed they are exposed (vulnerable).

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from the one who narrated it, from Shihaab ibn Abd Rabbihi who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the right of the woman upon her husband?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should satisfy her hunger, cover her nakedness, and not spoil her face. So when he does that, by Allah, he has fulfilled her right.' I said, 'And the oil?' He said: 'Intermittently, one day and one day not.' I said, 'And the meat?' He said: 'Every three days, so it becomes ten times in the month, no more than that.' I said, 'And the dye?' He said: 'And the dye is every six months, and he should clothe her with four garments each year, two for winter and two for summer.' And it is not befitting that he impoverish his house from three things: hair oil, vinegar, and olive oil, and he should provide them with a mud (of food), for I provide myself and my family with it. And he should measure the food portion for each person from them; if he wishes, he eats it, and if he wishes, he gifts it, and if he wishes, he gives it in charity. And when fruit is generally available, he should feed his family from it, and he should not fail to have an excess of food for the Eid with them, so that he makes a special dish for them from that which he does not make for them on other days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) advised me with the women until I thought that it is not befitting to divorce her except due to manifest immorality'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, or someone else, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The Words of the Mighty and Majestic: And whoever's provision is straitened, let him spend of that which Allah has given him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he spends upon her what sustains her back (i.e., provides for her maintenance) along with clothing, or else separation is effected between the two of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: The man is compelled only for the spending (maintenance) of the two parents and the children. Ibn Abi Umeyr said, I said to Jameel, 'And (what about) the wife?' He said, 'It has been reported from Anbasah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When he covers her with what covers her nakedness, and feeds her with what maintains her strength/dignity, she stays with him, or else he divorces her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a man from the Ansar in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out for one of his needs, so he made a pledge to his wife that she should not leave her house until he returns. And her father fell ill, so the woman sent a message to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saying, 'My husband went out and pledged to me that I should not leave my house until he returns, and my father has become ill, so order me to visit him.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'No, sit in your house and obey your husband.' So he became seriously ill, so she sent to him a second time with that, saying, 'So if you order me, I can visit him.' So he said, 'Sit in your house and obey your husband.' So her father died, and she sent to him, 'My father has died, so order me to pray over him.' So he said, 'No, sit in your house and obey your husband.' So the man was buried, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent to her, 'Indeed, Allah has forgiven you and your father due to your obedience to your husband.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the women, so he said: 'O group of women! Give charity, and even if it is from your ornaments, and even if it is with a date, and even if it is a part of a date, for the majority of you would be the fuel of Hell, for you frequently curse and are ungrateful to your spouses.' So a woman from the Clan of Suleym, who possessed intellect, said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Are we not the mothers, the carriers, the breast-feeders? Are there not from us, the daughters who stay (with their husbands), and the sisters who are kind?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was moved emotionally and said to her: 'Childbearing, birth-giving, breast-feeders, merciful ones, if only they do not bring to their husbands what would make them arrive to the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out on the Day of Sacrifice to the rear of the city upon a camel that was bare-backed (without a saddle). So he passed by the women, stopped by them, and then said: 'O group of women! Give charity and obey your husbands, for most of you will be in the Fire.' When they heard that, they wept. Then a woman from among them stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! In the Fire along with the disbelievers? By Allah, we are not disbelievers, so we should become from the inhabitants of the Fire.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'You are disbelievers by virtue of the rights of your husbands.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A woman has no independent authority with her husband regarding emancipation, nor charity, nor management, nor gifting, nor a vow in her wealth, except by the permission of her husband, except regarding Zakat, or righteousness with her parents, or maintaining good relationships with her near relatives.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any woman who goes out from her house without the permission of her husband, there is no maintenance (nafaqah) for her until she returns.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Al-Thu'mali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is saved among men is few, and among women is fewer and fewer.' It was said, 'And why, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Because they are disbelievers in anger and believers in pleasure.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Sa'd ibn Abi Amr al-Jallab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: He said to the wife of Sa'd: 'Congratulations to you, O Khansa'a! So even if Allah did not give you anything except your daughter, Umm al-Husayn, Allah would have given you abundant goodness. Indeed, the example of a righteous woman among women is like the example of the 'Asam crow among crows, and it is the one with a white leg.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The example of the believing woman is like the example of the mole in the black bull.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The example of the righteous woman is the example of the chough (a type of crow) which is rarely found. It was said, 'And what is the chough which is rarely found?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One of its legs is white.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no greater army for Iblees than women and anger.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Abu Ali al-Wasiti, who raised it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), saying: Indeed, when the woman ages, the goodness of her two halves departs and her evil remains; her beauty departs, her womb becomes barren, and her tongue becomes sharp (rages).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not lodge the women in the rooms (upper chambers), and do not teach them writing, and teach them the spinning (of wool/thread), and [teach them] Surah Al-Nur.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, raising it, said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not teach your women Surah Yusuf, nor recite it to them, for therein is the strife, and teach them Surah Al-Nur, for therein is the advice.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the saddle to be ridden by a female.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ismail ibn Yasar, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Israil, from Yunus, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Harith Al-Awr, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not carry the females upon the saddles, lest you incite them to immorality.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and asked him about the affluent woman who had performed the Hajj of Islam (her first obligatory Hajj), so she says to her husband, 'Take me to Hajj from my own wealth.' Is it for him to forbid her? He said: 'Yes. He should say, 'My right upon you is greater than your right upon me, with regard to this.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Women were mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Disobey them in what is good (al-ma'ruf) before they command you to do what is evil (al-munkar), and seek refuge with Allah from their evil ones, and be cautious regarding their good ones.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever obeys his wife, Allah will cast him face-down into the Fire.' It was said, 'And what is that obedience?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She seeks from him going to the bathhouses, the weddings, the festivals, the mourning gatherings, and (buying) thin clothes.'
And by his chain, he said: Rasool-Allah said: Obedience to the woman is remorse.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Fear the evil ones of the women, and become cautious upon their good ones, and if they were to instruct you with the goodness, so oppose them so they would not expect obedience from you regarding the evil'.

And from him, from his father, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: 'The women were mentioned in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he said: Do not consult them in the secret counsels, nor obey them among the near relatives'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from al-Muttalib ibn Ziyad, raising it to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Seek refuge with Allah from the wicked ones of your womenfolk, and be cautious regarding their good ones, and do not obey them in what is good so that they may enjoin upon you what is evil.

And from him, from Abu Abdullah Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Sandal, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Beware of consulting with women, for in them is weakness, frailty, and inability.'

And from him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from a man from our companions who is teknonymed Abu Abdullah, who raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: In opposing the women is the blessing.
And by this chain, he said, Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Every man who is managed by a woman, so he is accursed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, raising it (to the Prophet), said: Whenever Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) intended the battle, he would call his wives, consult them, and then oppose them.

Ali, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from one of his companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Seek refuge with Allah from the evil ones of your women, and be cautious of the good ones among them, and do not obey them in what is good, lest they invite you to evil. And he (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women should not be consulted in secret counsels, nor should they be obeyed regarding close relatives.' Indeed, when a woman ages, the good of her two halves departs and her evil remains, and that is because her womb becomes barren, her manners become bad, and her tongue becomes sharp. And indeed, when a man ages, the evil of his two halves departs and his good remains, and that is because his intellect returns to soundness, his opinion becomes firm, and his manners improve.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women have no share in the center of the road, but rather they should walk on the side near the wall and the road.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any woman who perfumes herself, then goes out from her house, is cursed until she returns to her house, whenever she returns.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Basheer, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting for the woman that she aromatises her clothes when she goes out from her house.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is not for the women from the center of the road, but on its sides, meaning the middle [is for men/others].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the woman that she uncovers herself in front of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, for they describe that to their husbands.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding what Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took from the allegiances upon the women is that they would not be sitting with their knees up, nor would be sitting with the men in private.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade al-qanazi' (hairstyles with raised portions), al-qisas (braided/interwoven hair), and painting henna on the palm, and said: 'The women of the Children of Israel were destroyed because of al-qisas and painting henna on the palm.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is not permissible for a menstruating woman to take a qusrah or a jummah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Thabit ibn Abi Saeed, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the women who place qaramil (hairpieces/extensions) on their heads. He said: Wool is permissible, and whatever is from the hair of the woman herself [is permissible]. He disliked for the woman to make the qaramil from the hair of someone else. So if she joins her hair with wool or with her own hair, it does not harm her.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Adhere to those with large hips, for they are the most child-bearing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Malik ibn Ashyam, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Marry a brunette, of large eyes, of a medium stature, so if you dislike her, then her dowry would be upon me (peace be upon him).'
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you marry, marry a woman with large buttocks.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions, raised the hadith, saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he intended to marry a woman, would send someone to look at her, and he would say to the sent one: 'Smell her neck; if her neck is good, her scent (habit) will be good. And look at her heels; if her heels are trim, her knees will be large.'

Ahmad, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from his brother, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'I tested white slave-girls and black ones, and there was a disparity between them.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from one of his companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: From the happiness of the man is that he removes the veil from a white woman.

Sahl, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Malik ibn Ashyam, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Marry her (for her) large eyes, brunette (colour), (large) buttocks, medium stature, so if you dislike her, upon me (would be) the dower.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the two arms of the woman, are they from the adornment of which Allah (Blessed and High is He) said: 'and let them not display their adornment except to their husbands'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and what is below the headscarf is from the adornment, and what is below the two bracelets.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, 'except what appears thereof,' he said: The apparent adornment is the kohl and the ring.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah the Exalted, 'And do not display their ornaments except what appears thereof.' He said: 'The ring, and the bracelet, and it is the anklet.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn 'Amirah from Sa'd al-Iskaf from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: A young man from the Ansar faced a woman in Medina, and the women used to wear their scarves behind their ears. So he looked at her while she was coming towards him. When she passed by, he continued looking at her as she entered an alleyway which had been named by the Clan of so-and-so. He kept looking behind her, and a bone in the wall or a piece of glass struck his face and cut it. When the woman went away, he looked and saw that blood was flowing onto his chest and his garment. So he said, 'By Allah, I will surely go to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and inform him.' He said: So he came to him. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw him, he said to him, 'What is this?' So he informed him. Then Jibra'il (peace be upon him) descended with this Verse: 'Say to the believing men that they should cast down their looks and guard their private parts; that is purer for them; surely Allah is Aware of what they are doing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He recited: 'that they should lay aside their outer garments', he said: 'the khimar (headscarf) and the jilbab (outer cloak)'. I asked: 'In front of whom?'. He said: 'In front of those who are not displaying adornment'. If she does not do so, it is better for her. And the adornment that they display of it is mentioned in the other verse.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding His Mighty and Majestic saying: 'And the elderly women among the women who do not hope for marriage' — what is suitable for them to remove from their garments? He said: 'The robe (jilab)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) He recited: 'that they should put off their outer garments', he said: 'the jilbab and the khimar', when the woman has aged.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Or those following on [in their tracks] who do not have sexual desire (ahlī al-irbah) of the men' up to the end of the Verse. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fool who does not go to the women.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the 'ulī al-irbah' (those devoid of physical desire) from among the men. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The foolish slave who does not approach women.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: There were two men in Medina, one called Hayt and the other Mani'. They said to a man, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was listening: 'When you go to Al-Taif, God willing, then take the daughter of Ghaylan al-Thaqafiyyah, for she is a candle, miserly, moist, slender, sweet. When she sits, she bends; when she speaks, she sings. She comes with four and goes back with eight, and between her legs is like the cup.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not view you two as being among the men devoid of physical desire.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that they be exiled to a place called Al-Araya, and they would trade there every Friday.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the mothers of the children, is it permissible for her to uncover her head in front of the men? He (peace be upon him) said: She should wear a scarf (cover her head).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not upon the slave girl to wear the scarf during the Prayer, nor upon the slave girl assigned to be free upon the death of her master, nor upon the contracted slave girl when it is stipulated upon her to wear the scarf during the Prayer, and she is an owned slave until she pays off the entirety of her contract, and there shall flow upon her whatever flows upon the owned slaves from the legal punishments (Hadd), all of them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man shaking hands with a woman. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for a man to shake hands with a woman, except for a woman whom he is forbidden to marry (due to close kinship), such as a sister, daughter, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, or daughter of a sister, or similar. As for the woman whom it is permissible for him to marry, he should not shake her hand except from behind the garment, and he should not squeeze her palm.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man shake hands with a woman who is not his mahram?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except from behind the garment.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from one of his companions, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, who said: Sa'idah and Minnat, the two sisters of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, the seller of Sabir, narrated to me, saying: 'We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said,

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim al-Ashal, from al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touch the hands of the women when they pledged their allegiance to him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He called for his bowl in which he used to perform ablution, so he poured water into it, then immersed his right hand. So every time one of them pledged her allegiance, he said to her: 'Immerse your hand.' So she would immerse just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had immersed. Thus, this was his 'touching' of their hands.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know how the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) accepted the allegiance of the women?' I said: 'Allah knows best, and the son of His Messenger knows best.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He gathered them around him, then called for a Baram bowl, poured a little water into it, then immersed his hand in it, then said:

A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, '...that they do not disobey you in lawful matters.' He said, 'Lawful matters means that they do not tear their shirt, nor slap their cheek, nor cry 'woe is me', nor stay behind near the grave, nor blacken their clothes, nor spread their hair.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Sulayman ibn Sama'ah al-Khuza'i from Ali ibn Isma'il from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do you know what is the meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: “...that they must not disobey you in lawful matters”?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Fatimah (peace be upon her): “When I die, do not cause abrasion to any face, do not spread for me any hairs, do not cry ‘woe is me,’ and do not call any gathering to mourn for me.” He then said: “This is the lawful matter about which Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, has spoken.”'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) liberated Mecca, the men pledged allegiance; then the women came to pledge allegiance to him. O Holy Prophet, when believing women come to you to pledge allegiance with you not to call anything as partner of Allah, not to steal, not to commit fornication, not to kill their children, not to accuse falsely of their own making, must not disobey you in lawful matters, then pledge allegiance with them and ask forgiveness from Allah for them, Allah is forgiving and merciful. Hind then said, 'As for the children, we brought them up when they were infants, but we killed them when they grew up.' Umm Hakim, daughter of al-Harith ibn Hisham, who was with Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is that 'lawful matter' that Allah has commanded us not to disobey you in?' He replied, 'You must not slap a cheek, abrade a face, pull out hair, tear the front of a shirt, blacken clothes, and you must not cry out woe.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pledged allegiance with them on this basis. She said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how can we pledge allegiance to you?' He said, 'Indeed, I do not place my hand in the hands of women.' He asked for a bowl of water, immersed his hand, then removed it, and said, 'Immerse your hands in this water,' and that was the pledge of allegiance.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Ja'far ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade men from entering upon women except with their permission.

And by this chain, (it is established that) a person should not enter upon the women except with the permission of their guardians. And by this chain, (it is established that) a person should not enter upon the women except with the permission of their guardians.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man should seek permission when he enters upon his father, and the father does not seek permission from the son. He said: And the man should seek permission from his daughter and his sister when they are married.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man seek permission to enter upon his father?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. I used to seek permission to enter upon my father, and my mother was not with him; rather, she was the wife of my father. My mother had died and I was a boy, and there might be matters of their privacy that I did not like to surprise them in, nor would they like that from me. Greeting (with Salam) is more correct and better.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ubayd ibn Muawiya ibn Shurayh, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out intending to visit Fatima (peace be upon her), and I was with him. When he reached the door, he placed his hand on it and knocked, then said: 'Peace be upon you.' Fatima said: 'And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'May I enter?' She said: 'Enter, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I and the one who is with me?' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not have a headscarf.' He said: 'O Fatima, take the excess of your bedspread and cover your head with it.' So she did. Then he said: 'Peace be upon you.' Fatima said: 'And upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'May I enter?' She said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I and the one who is with me?' She said: 'And the one who is with you?' Jabir said: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered and I entered, and behold, the face of Fatima (peace be upon her) was yellow, like the belly of a locust. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Why do I see your face as yellow?' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, hunger.' He said (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Allah, Satiator of the hungry and Repeller of loss, satiate Fatima, daughter of Muhammad.' Jabir said: 'By Allah, I looked at the blood flowing from her veins until her face returned to being red. So she did not suffer hunger after that day.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Let those whom your right hands possess, and those who have not yet reached puberty from you, seek permission three times, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you. And whoever has reached puberty, let him not enter upon his mother, nor his sister, nor his maternal aunt, nor anyone besides that, except by permission. So do not give permission until they have greeted, and the greeting is obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Let your servant seek permission from you when he has reached puberty during three times of privacy, when he enters any one of them, even if his room is in your house. And let him seek permission from you after the evening prayer which is called Al-Atamah, and when it is morning, and when you put off your clothes from the midday heat. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only commanded that for privacy, for these are times of inattention and privacy.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad al-Halby, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Those whom your right hands possess,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is specific to men, not women.' I said, 'So do women seek permission during these three times?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but they enter and exit. And those who have not yet reached puberty from you?' He said: 'From yourselves.' He said: 'Upon you is seeking permission like the permission of those who have reached puberty during these three times.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, all together, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Let those whom your right hands possess, and those among you who have not yet attained puberty, seek permission from you three times: before the Dawn Prayer, and when you put off your clothes at midday, and after the Evening Prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you nor upon them after these times, as they circulate among you. And whoever among you has attained puberty, let him not enter upon his mother, nor his sister, nor his daughter, nor anyone else besides that, except by permission. And let him not permit anyone unless he greets, for the greeting is obedience to the Beneficent.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from his father, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The beautiful woman cuts the phlegm, and the ugly woman stirs the black bile.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Sayyari from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from one of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he complained to him about phlegm, so he said: 'Is there a slave girl for you who makes you laugh?' He said, 'I said, No.' He said, 'So take her, for that cuts down the phlegm.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah and Ahmad, the two sons of Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave who sees the hair of his mistress. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad and Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), about thirty men, when my father entered. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) welcomed him and seated him by his side, then faced him for a long time. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Muawiya has a need, so if you would lighten [the gathering], we will all stand up.' So my father said to me: 'Return, O Muawiya!' So I returned. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is your son?' He said: 'Yes, and he alleges that the people of Medina are doing something that is not permissible for them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?' I said: 'The Qurashi Hashimite woman rides [a slave] and places her hand on the head of the black [slave], and her forearms on his neck.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son, do you not read the Quran?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Recite this verse: There is no blame on them [the wives] in respect of their fathers, nor their sons, until he reached: nor of what their right hands possess.' Then he said: 'O my son, there is no problem if the slave sees the hair and the leg.'
