Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The slave sees the hair and the leg of his mistress.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar and Yunus ibn Yaqoub, altogether, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not permissible for the woman that her slave should look at anything from her body except for her hair, without deliberate intention for that. And in another report, (he said): There is no problem if he looks at her hair when he is trustworthy (a believer).

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdul Malik ibn Utba al-Nak Utba al-Nakha'i said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Umm al-Walad (mother of the child), is it permissible for a eunuch of her master to look at her while she is bathing? He said: That is not permissible.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), saying: 'A man has a eunuch who enters upon his womenfolk, and he gives them the wudu, so he sees their hair.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida' (peace be upon him) about the veil of the free women in the presence of the eunuchs. He (the Imam) said, 'They would enter upon the daughters of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and they would not veil themselves.' I asked, 'Were they free?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'So do the free ones veil themselves in their presence?' He said, 'No.'

A number of our companions, from among our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: It is not correct for the girl when she menstruates unless she wears a scarf, unless she does not find it.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the girl who has not yet attained puberty: when is it befitting for her to cover her head from those with whom there is no close kinship (mahram), and when is it obligatory upon her to cover her head for the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: 'She does not cover her head until the prayer becomes obligatory upon her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Ahmad al-Kahili, and I think I have seen him, said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a young girl, with whom there is no close kinship (mahram), who captivates me, so I carry her and kiss her. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When six years have passed for her, do not place her on your lap.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from one of his men, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) That one of the Banu Hashim invited him along with a group of his family. So he came with a young girl of his, and the people of the gathering all brought her near to them. So when she approached him, he asked about her age. So it was said, 'Five'. So he forbade her from it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked about the young child who cups the woman. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is good at it and can describe it, then [it is permissible/no objection].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, who said: Ibn Umm Maktum sought permission to enter upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and with him were Ayesha and Hafsa, so he said to them both, 'Arise and enter the room.' So they both said, 'He is blind.' So he said, 'If he does not see you, then you see him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen () said: 'Do not initiate the greetings with the women nor invite them to the meal, for the Prophet () said: 'The women are inarticulate and exposed, therefore veil their inability to express themselves with the silence, and veil their exposure with the houses'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The women are inarticulate and exposed, therefore veil the exposure with the houses, and veil their inability to express themselves with the silence'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women are a source of fatigue (or weakness in communication) and a matter of private nature; therefore, cover their private nature with homes, and cover their fatigue with silence.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High is He, is Most Honourable (Ghayur), He loves every honourable one, and due to His Sense of Honour He has prohibited the immoralities, their apparent and their hidden (forms).

From him, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Habib Al-Khash'ami, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'asws ) saying: 'When the man has no sense of honour (ghayrah), he is of an inverted heart.'

From him, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Jareer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man is not watchful of guarding the honour of his wife or those married to him, so he does not act with a sense of honour, Allah Mighty and Majestic sends a bird called Al-Qanfadar to him which settles upon a joist of his door, then gives him respite for forty days. Then it shouts out, 'Allah is most Honourable and Loves every honourable one'. So either he (starts) acting vigilantly, and changes and shows remorse to his lack of protectionism, otherwise it flies over until it settles upon his head, so it spreads out its wings upon his eyes, then it flies away. So Allah Mighty and Majestic snatches away from him, after that, the spirit of the 'Eman' (faith), and the Angels name him as the cuckold (pimp).

Ibn Mahboub, from someone else, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was a person with a sense of honour, and I (peace be upon him) am with a more sense of honour than him, and Allah (exalted be He) would stub the nose of the one who does not have a sense of honour, from the Believers and the Muslims'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'O people of Iraq! I have been informed that your women push against men on the road. Are you not ashamed?' And in another hadith, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Are you not ashamed nor do you feel ghayrah (protective jealousy/honor) that your women go out to the markets and jostle with the 'uluj (uneducated/faithless men)?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three are those to whom Allah will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: the elderly adulterer, the cuckold, and the woman who allows men to share her husband's bed.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him), who said: The Paradise is prohibited to the cuckold.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Ja'far ibn Anbasa, from Ubada ibn Ziyad Al-Asadi, from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Asimi, from the one who narrated to him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote in his letter to Al- Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Beware of excessive vigilance (ghayra) in places where it is not due, for that calls the sound/healthy one among them to illness. But regulate their affairs; if you see a flaw, hasten to express disapproval regarding both the small and the large. And if you discern doubt/suspicion from them, then the sin becomes great and the reprimand becomes light.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Shurayh who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the going out of the women during the two Eids, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except for the elderly woman wearing their pair of shoes'.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except for an elderly woman'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie from Mansur ibn Yunus from Is'haq ibn Ammar from Abdul Malik ibn Amr who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for the owner of the menstruating woman from her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything except the front part in particular.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the menstruating woman, what is permissible for her husband from her? He said: Whatever is besides the private part.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza from Dawud al-Raqqi from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for a man from his wife while she is menstruating?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'That which is below the private part.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Aban ibn Uthman and al-Husayn ibn Abi Yusuf, from Abdul Malik ibn Amr, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is permissible for the man from the woman while she is menstruating?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything except the front private part.' He then said: 'Indeed, the woman is the toy of the man.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Uzafir Al-Sayrafi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you see these disfigured in creation?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are those whose fathers had intercourse with their wives during menstruation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman from whom the blood of menstruation ceases at the end of her days, he (peace be upon him) said: When her husband is seized by craving, let him instruct her to wash her private part, then he may touch her, if he wishes, before she performs the full ritual bath.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who sees the sign of purity, and her husband copulates with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, and the ritual bath (ghusl) is more beloved to me.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Ali from Aban from one of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about coming to the women in their behinds, so he said: 'She is your plaything, do not hurt her'. She is your plaything, do not hurt her'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam said, 'I heard Safwan ibn Yahya saying,' I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'A man from your followers commanded me to ask you about a matter; he feared you and felt shy to ask you himself.' He (the Imam) said, 'What is it?' I said, 'A man comes to his wife in her anus.' He (the Imam) said, 'It is up to him.' I said to him, 'And do you do so?' He (the Imam) said, 'We do not do so.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about Al-Khadkhadah, so he said: 'It is from the immoralities, and marrying the slave girl is better than it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Ismail al-Basri, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the rubbing (of the penis). He said: He is having sex with himself, there is nothing upon it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who copulates with an animal or rubs (masturbates). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything by which a man causes his water to descend in this and what resembles it, so it is adultery (Zina).'

Ali ibn Muhammad al-Kulayni, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfali, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Accursed is the one who copulates with an animal'.

Ali ibn Muhammad al-Kulayni narrated from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfali from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Condemned is one who engages in sexual intercourse with an animal.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: 'The most intense of the people in punishment on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who caused his seed to fall into a womb which was prohibited unto him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Salim, who said: Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'Fear adultery, for it obliterates sustenance and invalidates the Religion.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said: For the adulterer there are six characteristics: three in the world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in the world, it removes the light of the face, causes poverty, and hastens destruction; and as for those in the Hereafter, it is the anger of the Lord, the evil reckoning, and eternity in the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When adultery becomes abundant after me, sudden death will become abundant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hamza, who said: I was in the presence of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and a man came to him and said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad! I am afflicted with women, so I commit adultery one day and fast one day, so that one becomes expiation for the other.' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'There is nothing more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than that He is obeyed and not disobeyed. Therefore, do not commit adultery and do not fast.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) pulled him towards him, took his hand, and said, 'O Abu Zannah (Father of Adultery)! You are doing the deed of the inhabitants of the Fire and you hope that you will enter Paradise?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Suwayd, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'I am being tested with looking at a beautiful woman, and looking at her fascinates me.' He said to me: 'O Ali! There is no harm if Allah recognizes sincerity from your intention, and beware of adultery, for it obliterates blessings and destroys the religion.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi, all of them from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The disciples gathered to Jesus (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O teacher of goodness, guide us.' He said to them, 'Indeed, Moses, the Speaker of God (peace be upon him), ordered you not to swear by God, Blessed and Exalted, while being liars, and I order you not to swear by God, whether liars or truthful.' They said, 'O Spirit of God, increase it for us.' He said, 'Indeed, Moses, the Prophet of God (peace be upon him), ordered you not to commit adultery, and I order you not to converse with your souls regarding adultery, in addition to actually committing it. Indeed, whoever converses with his soul regarding adultery is like one who lights a fire in a decorated house; the smoke spoils the decorations even if the house does not burn down.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Yaqoub (peace be upon him) said to his son: 'O my son, do not commit adultery, for if the bird commits adultery, its feathers fall off.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said regarding adultery: 'Five characteristics remove the water of the face, cause poverty, shorten the lifespan, anger the Beneficent, and necessitate eternity in the Fire. We seek Refuge with Allah from the Fire.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three [types of people] to whom Allah will neither speak nor purify, and for them is a painful punishment — from them is the woman who tramples the bed of her husband.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Abi Al-Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I inform you of the great adultery?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a woman who tramples the bed of her husband, then brings a child from someone else, and imposes him upon her husband. So that is the one whom Allah will not speak to, nor will He look at her on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify her, and for her is a painful punishment.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The anger of Allah intensified upon a woman who brought into her household someone other than them, so he ate their goodness and looked at their nakedness.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sanctity of the anus is greater than the sanctity of the vagina. Indeed, Allah destroyed a community due to the sanctity of the anus, and He did not destroy anyone due to the sanctity of the vagina.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who copulates with a boy will come as Junub (sexually impure) on the Day of Resurrection; the water of the world will not purify him, and Allah will be Wrathful upon him, and will Curse him, and Prepare Hell for him, and it is an evil destination.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, when the male rides the male, the Throne trembles because of that. And indeed, the man is brought in his anus, and Allah keeps him upon the Bridge of Hell until He finishes the Reckoning of the creatures. Then he is commanded to be taken to Hell, and he is punished by its layers, layer after layer, until he is returned to its lowest part, and he does not exit from it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Liwat (sodomy) is what is less than the anus, and the anus is the blasphemy (kufr).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding the people of Lut (peace be upon him): 'You are committing an indecency, which no one in the worlds has done before you.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Iblees came to them in a beautiful form, in which there was femininity, upon him were beautiful clothes. So he came to the youths from them and instructed them that they should fall upon him. Had he sought to them that he should fall upon them, they would have refused to him, but he sought to them that they should fall upon him. So when they did it, they attained pleasure. Then he went away from them and left them, so they fell upon each other.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Yazeed al-Hammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent four angels for the destruction of the people of Lut: Jibra'il, Mikail, Israfil, and Karoubil. So they passed by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) while they were wearing turbans. They greeted him, but he did not recognize them. He saw their good physical build and said: 'None shall serve these except I myself,' and he was a man of hospitality. So he roasted a fat calf for them until it was cooked, then he brought it near to them. When he placed it in front of them, he saw that their hands did not reach for it. He deemed them strange and conceived fear of them. When Jibra'il saw that, he removed the turban from his face, and Ibrahim recognized him. He said: 'You are he.' He said: 'Yes.' And Sarah, his wife, passed by. They gave her the good news of Is'haq and after Is'haq of Yaqoub. She said: 'What did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say?' So they answered her with what is in the Book. So Ibrahim said to them: 'For what have you come?' They said: 'For the destruction of the people of Lut.' He said to them: 'If there are among them one hundred believers, would you destroy them?' Jibra'il said: 'No.' He said: 'If there are fifty?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'If there are thirty?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'If there are twenty?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'If there are ten?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'If there are five?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'If there is one?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Indeed, in it is Lut.' They said: 'We know better who is in it; we shall rescue him and his family, except for his wife; she shall be of those who remain behind.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of Lut (peace be upon him): 'These are my daughters, they are purer for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He presented to them for marriage.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beware of the children of the rich and the tyrant kings, for their trial (fitnah) is more intense than the trial of the virgins in their private chambers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Maymun al-Bann, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), verses from the chapter of Hud were recited in his presence. So when it reached the verse: 'And We rained upon them stones of clay, one after another, marked with your Lord, and it is not far from the unjust.' He said: 'The one who dies persisting upon sodomy will not die until Allah pelt him with a stone from those stones, in which his death will occur, and no one will see it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever kisses a boy out of lust, Allah will bridle him on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who enables (other men) unto himself willingly to play with him, Allah would Cast the desires of the women upon him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah al-Dihqan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Atiyya, the brother of Abu al-Uram, who said: I mentioned to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) the one who is copulated with from the men, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah will not afflict anyone with this affliction and there is a need for him. Indeed, in their behinds are inverted wombs, and the modesty of their behinds is like the modesty of the woman. A son of Iblis called Zawal has participated among them. So whoever among the men he has participated in is the passive one, and whoever among the women he participates in are the ones from whom the men act upon this. And the one acting upon this among the men, when he reaches forty years, does not leave it. And they are the remnant of Sodom. Indeed, I do not mean by their remnant that they are their children, but they are from their essence.' He said: I said, 'Sodom which was turned upside down?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is four cities: Sodom, and Sareem, and Ladma', and Umeyra'. He said: So Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to them and they were uprooted to the boundaries of the seventh earth. So he placed his wing under the lowest of them and raised them all until the inhabitants of the sky of the world heard the barking of their dogs, then he turned them upside down.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'For Allah there are servants for whom in their loins are wombs like the wombs of women.' He was asked, 'So why do they not bear (children)?' He said: 'They are inverted, and for them in their behinds is a gland like the gland of the camel or the she-camel. So whenever it stirs, they stir, and when it is calm, they are calm.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abdullah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Abu Khadeeja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed the men who resemble the women, and the women who resemble the men. He said: And they are the effeminate men and the women who marry each other.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Al-Hasan, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Umar, from his brother Al-Husayn, from his father Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and with him was a man. The man said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I love the children.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'So what do you do?' He said, 'I carry them on my back.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) placed his hand on his forehead and turned his face away from him. The man wept, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at him as if he pitied him, and said, 'When you go to your city, buy a fat camel, tie it with a strong rope, take the sword and strike the hump with a strike that peels off its skin, and sit upon it while it is warm.' Umar said, 'The man said, 'I went to my city and bought a camel, tied it with a strong rope, took the sword and struck the hump with it, peeled off its skin, and sat upon it while it was warm. Something resembling a lizard, smaller than a lizard, dropped from me onto the back of the camel, and what was in me settled down.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Haytham al-Nahdi, raising it, said: A man complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of al-ubnah (anal fissure/hemorrhoids), so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) wiped upon his back, and a red worm dropped from him, so he was cured.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Amr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Allah swore upon Himself that he shall not sit upon the cushions of Paradise the one who allows others into his behind. So I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'So-and-so is intellectual and understanding, inviting people unto himself. Allah has afflicted him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Does he do that in the congregational mosque?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So, does he do it upon the door of his house?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So where does he do it?' I said: 'When he is alone.' He said: 'So Allah has not afflicted him. This one is doing it for pleasure. He shall not sit upon the cushions of Paradise.'

Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn Asbaat, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whatever was among our Shias, three things would not be among them: the one who begs in his hand; and there would not be among them a blue-eyed or green-eyed person; and there would not be among them the one who is invited to his behind.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi from Ubays ibn Hisham from Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari from Hisham Al-Saydani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man asked him about this Verse: 'The people of Nuh and the dwellers of Ar-Rass rejected (prophets) before them.' So he (peace be upon him) said with his hand, 'Like this,' and he wiped one of them with the other, and he said: 'Hunna al-lawati bi al-lawati,' meaning women with women.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, who said: A woman asked me to seek permission for her from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), so I sought permission for her. She entered, and with her was a slave-girl of hers. She said, 'O Abū ʿAbdillāh! What is meant by the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'A olive-tree, neither of the East nor of the West'?' He said, 'O woman! Indeed, Allah did not strike the examples for the tree; rather, He struck the examples for the Children of Adam. Ask what you intend.' She said, 'Inform me about the lesbian with the lesbian, what is their legal punishment (ḥadd) regarding it?' He said, 'The legal punishment of adultery. Indeed, when it is the Day of Resurrection, they will be brought having been dressed in garments cut from Fire, veiled with veils of Fire, and wearing trousers of Fire, and pillars of Fire will be inserted into their bellies up to their heads, and they will be thrown into the Fire. O woman! The first people to perform this act were the people of Lūṭ. The men sufficed themselves with the men, so the women remained without men, so they did as their men had done.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Yazeed al-Nakha'i, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said: I saw a man in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding the lesbian with the lesbian?' He said to him, 'I will not inform you until you swear that you will inform the women with what I inform you with.' He said, so he swore an oath for him. He said, then he said: 'They are both in the Fire, and upon them are seventy garments of Fire. Above those garments is a dry, thick skin of Fire. Upon them are two belts of Fire and two crowns of Fire above those garments, and two shoes of Fire, and they are both in the Fire.'

From him, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Qasim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Ja'far, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah or Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the woman who performs lesbian acts with the woman; and he (peace be upon him) was reclining, so he sat up and said: 'Accursed! The rider as well as the ridden, until she comes out from their clothes, the rider as well as the ridden one, for Allah, Blessed and High, and the Angels, and the Guardians (peace be upon him) are cursing them both, and myself (peace be upon him), and the ones who remain in the loins of the men and the wombs of the women, for by Allah it is the greatest adultery, and by Allah, there is no repentance for them. May Allah kill Laqis, daughter of Iblees, with what she came up with.' So the man said, 'This is what the people of Al-Iraq are coming up with'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! It was happening upon the era of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) before the existence of Al-Iraq, and regarding them Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah curse the women resembling themselves with the men, and may Allah curse the men resembling themselves with the women'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do those who look at the behinds of women not fear that they will be tested with that regarding their own women?

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Mufazzal al-Ju'fi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'How ugly it is for a man that he is seen in the place of immorality, so that it is attributed to us and to the righteous of our companions. O Mufazzal! Do you know why it was said: 'The one who commits adultery, one day adultery will be committed with him'? I said, 'No, may I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There was a prostitute among the Children of Israel, and there was a man among the Children of Israel who used to frequently visit her. So when it was the end of his going to her, Allah caused to flow upon her tongue: 'Indeed, you will return to your family and you will find a man with her'. He said: 'So he went out, and he was ill-tempered. So he entered his house in a manner different from the manner in which he used to enter before that day, and he used to enter with permission, so he entered that day without permission, and he found a man on his bed. So they raised the matter to Musa (peace be upon him)'. So Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended upon Musa (peace be upon him) and he said: 'O Musa! The one who commits adultery, one day adultery will be committed with him'. So he looked at the two of them and he said: 'Restrain, and your womenfolk will restrain'.

A number of our companions, from our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Abdul Hamid, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry into the family of so-and-so, for they are chaste, and their women are chaste; and do not marry into the family of so-and-so, for they are adulterous, and their women are adulterous.' And he said: 'It is inscribed in the Torah: I am Allah, the Killer of the killers, and the Impoverisher of the adulterers. O people! Do not commit adultery, lest your women commit adultery; just as you do, it shall be done with you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is upon you with the restraint and neglect of the immoralities'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Maymun al-Qaddah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no act of worship superior to restraining the belly and the private parts.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: From the happiness of the man is that his daughter does not experience menses in his house.

One of our companions, his chain having dropped from me, narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not leave out anything that is needed except that He taught it to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So, from His teaching him was that he ascended the pulpit one day, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! Jibraeel came to me from the Subtle, the All-Knowing, and said: 'The virgins are like fruit on a tree. When the fruit ripens and is not picked, the sun spoils it and the winds scatter it. And so are the virgins when they reach what women reach; there is no cure for them except the husband, otherwise there is no safety for them from corruption, for they are human beings.' He said: So a man stood up to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, whom should we marry them to?' He said, 'Their matches.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and who are their matches?' He said, 'The believers are matches for one another. The believers are matches for one another.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah created Hawwa from Adam, so the keenness/desire of the women is [directed toward] the men; therefore, fortify/guard them in the houses.

Aban, from Al-Wasiti, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah created Adam (peace be upon him) from water and clay, so the keenness/desire of the son of Adam is in water and clay; and He created Hawwa from Adam, so the keenness/desire of women is in men, therefore fortify/protect them in the houses.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, raising it (to the Imam), said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said in one of his speeches: 'The wild beasts, their keenness is their bellies, and the women, their keenness is the men'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Men were created from the earth, and their preoccupation is in the earth. And the woman was created from the men, and her preoccupation is in the men. Restrain your women, O assembly of men!'

Abu Abdillah Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Anbasa, from Ubada ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him); and Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Asimi, from the one who narrated to him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in his letter to Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Beware of consulting women, for their opinion leads to annihilation and their determination leads to weakness. Restrain their gaze from you by veiling them, for strict veiling is better for you and for them than doubt. And their going out is not more difficult than the entry of one whom you do not trust regarding them. So if you can ensure that no man other than you knows them, then do so.' Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Husayni, from Ali ibn Abdak, from Al-Hasan ibn Zarif ibn Nasih, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), similar to it, except that he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) wrote this letter to his son Muhammad [ibn Al-Hanafiyya].'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when his son-in-law came to him (either as the husband of his daughter or his sister), would spread his cloak for him, then seat him, then say: 'Welcome to the one who suffices the needs and veils the privacy'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I have not seen among the weak in religion and deficient in intellect anyone more robbing of the reason of a man of sound mind than you (women).'
Ahmad ibn al-Hajjal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Uqba ibn Khalid, who said: I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he came out to me, then said: 'O Uqba! These women have kept us from you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from the one who narrated it, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah made the patience of ten men to be for the woman. So whenever she is excited, there would be for her the strength of desire of ten men'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Durays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying that women have been given twelve parts of desire and twelve parts of patience.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Zurays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the women were given twelve parts of desire and twelve parts of patience.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'at ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The woman is favored over the man by ninety-nine parts of pleasure, but Allah has attached shyness to them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah has made for the woman that she should endure the patience of ten men; so when she attains [her desire], He increases her strength [of desire] to that of ten men.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Umar ibn Abi Bakkar, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad to Zuba'ah, daughter of Al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib. And he married him for the marriages to be humble/modest, and for them to follow the example of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and for them to know that the most noble of them in the sight of Allah is the most pious of them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah ibn 'A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man from the people of Basrah, a Shaybani named 'Abd al-Malik ibn Harmalah, passed by Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) asked him, 'Do you have a sister?' He replied, 'Yes.' He said, 'Marry her to me.' He replied, 'Yes.' The man left, and a companion of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) followed him until he reached his house. He asked about him, and it was said to him, 'So-and-so son of so-and-so,' and he was the master of his people. Then he returned to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O Abu al-Hasan, I asked about this brother-in-law of yours, the Shaybani, and they claimed that he is the master of his people.' Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I will explain to you, O so-and-so, what I see and what I hear. Have you not known that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, elevated the lowly through Islam, perfected the deficient through it, and honored the blame-worthy through it? So there is no blame on the Muslim; indeed, the blame is the blame of the Time of Ignorance.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Yazeed ibn Hatim, who said: There was a spy for Abdul Malik ibn Marwan in Medina who used to write to him with the news of whatever transpired therein, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) emancipated a slave girl, then married her. So the spy wrote to Abdul Malik, and Abdul Malik wrote to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Thereafter, it has reached me that you married your slave girl, and you know that there are matches for you from Qureysh, one you can glorify with regarding the relationship and have excellence regarding the children, but you did not consider for yourself nor upon your children to remain. Greetings!' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Thereafter, your letter has reached me, chiding me due to my marrying my slave girl, and you alleged that there are women among Qureysh ones I can glorify with regarding the relationship, and have excellence regarding the children, and there is no higher level than that of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with regards to glory, nor any more in benevolence. But rather, she was a possession of my right hand. When Allah (Mighty and Majestic) Intended a matter from me, I sought His Rewards by it. Then I returned her upon a Sunnah. And whoever was pure in the Religion of Allah, so there is nothing which can isolate him from His Command, and Allah has Raised by Al-Islam the despicability and completed the short-comings with it, and removed the blames. Thus, there is no blame upon a Muslim person, but rather the blame is upon the ignorance. Greetings!' So when he read the letter, he threw it to his son Suleyman, so he read it, and he said, 'O commander of the faithful! How intense is what Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) has prided over you!' So he said, 'O my son! Do not say that, for it is the tongues of the Clan of Hashim (peace be upon him) which splits the rocks and scoops from an ocean. It is Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), O my son, who rises from where the people are humbled'.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hashimi, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from al-Sayyari, from one of the Baghdadis, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said: One of the Khawarij met Hisham ibn al-Hakam and said, 'O Hisham! What do you say regarding the non-Arabs (Ajami), is it permissible for them to marry among the Arabs?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So the Arabs can marry from Quraysh?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So Quraysh can marry into the Clan of Hashim?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'From whom did you take this?' He said, 'From Ja'far ibn Muhammad. I heard him saying: 'Is your blood equal, but your reproductive organs not equal?'' So the Kharijite went out until he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'I met Hisham and I asked him about such and such, so he informed me with such and such, and he mentioned that he heard it from you.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, I have said that.' The Kharijite said, 'So here I am, I have come to you as a suitor.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'You are a match in your blood and nobility among your people, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, protected us from the charity (Sadaqat), and it is the dirt of the hands of the people. Thus, we dislike that we associate with us in what Allah has preferred us with, someone whom Allah has not made equal to what Allah has made for us.' So the Kharijite arose while saying, 'By Allah! I have not seen a man like him at all! He repulsed me, by Allah, with the ugliest of repulsions, but he did not deviate from the statement of his companion (the Prophet/Imam).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hammad, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the marriage of Umm Kulthum. He said: 'Indeed, that was a private part (of the body) that was usurped from us.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When he proposed marriage to her, Amir al-Mu'minin said to him, 'She is yet a child.' He said that he met al-Abbas and asked him, 'What is wrong with me, is there something wrong with me?' He said, 'What is the matter?' He replied, 'I proposed marriage to the son of your brother for his daughter, but he rejected me. By Allah, I will shut down Zamzam, and I will not leave any honor for you without destroying it, and I will establish two witnesses against him that he stole, and I will cut off his right hand.' So al-Abbas came to him, informed him, and asked him to leave the matter to him, so he left it to him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashaar Al-Wasity, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about marriage, so he wrote to me: 'The one who proposes to you, if you are pleased with his religion and his trustworthiness, then marry (your daughter) to him. If you do not, there will be strife in the land and great mischief.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: Ali ibn Asbaat wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a matter of his daughters, and that he could not find anyone like him. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'I understood what you mentioned from the matter of your daughters, and that you cannot find anyone like you, but do not wait regarding that, may Allah have Mercy on you, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When there comes to you one whose mannerisms you are pleased with, and his Religion, so marry to him, or if you do not do it, there would happen strife in the land and a great mischief'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding marriage, so his letter came to me in his own handwriting: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When there comes to you one whose manners and religion you are pleased with, marry him; if you do not, there will be strife in the land and great mischief.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who marries his daughter to a drinker of the wine, so he has cut off his relationship'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A drinker of wine, do not marry to him when he proposes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine after Allah prohibited it upon my tongue is not worthy to be married when he proposes (have his proposal) accepted for marriage when he proposes.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Marry among the uncertain (in religion) but do not marry them (to your daughters), because the woman adopts the etiquette of her husband, and he compels her upon his religion.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Yahya al-Halbi, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can I marry a Murji'ah or a Haruriyyah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, marry the simple-minded one from the women.' Zurara said, 'I said, 'By Allah, she is nothing but a believer or an infidel.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'And where are the people of Thana' Allah (the dualists) Mighty and Majestic?' The Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'Except the weak from among the men and the women and the children who cannot devise a means nor are they guided a way.' '[They are] more truthful than your words.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Believer cannot marry a Hostile woman (Nasibi), the one who is well known with that.

Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Fudayl said to him (peace be upon him): 'Do you marry the Nasibi (Hostile one)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and there is no prestige.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, I am only saying this to you, and even if she came to me with a house filled with dirhams, I would not do it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara ibn Bakr, from Zurara ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Marry into the weak (in religion) but do not marry to them, for the woman takes from the etiquettes of her husband, and he compels her upon his religion.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Yaqoub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa Al-Hannat, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'My wife has a sister who is known to be upon our view, and there are not upon our view in Al-Basra except for a few, so can I marry her to the one who does not agree with her view?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and there is neither a Blessing nor a prestige [nor a distinction].' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: 'Do not send them back to the unbelievers, neither are these (women) lawful for them, nor are those (men) lawful for them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Nasibi (one who is hostile to the Imams) whose hostility and enmity are known. Can we marry him to a believing woman, when he is able to reject her (or his proposal is rejected), and he does not know of the rejection? He (peace be upon him) said: The believer does not marry the Nasibiyyah, nor does the Nasibi marry the believing woman, nor does the weak one (in religion) marry a believing woman.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Humran ibn Ayn, who said: One of his family members wanted to get married but he could not find a compatible Muslim woman. So I mentioned that to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where are you from the simple ones who do not know anything?'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Jamil from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'May Allah improve you, I fear that it is not permissible for me to marry, meaning from those who are not upon his matter (Wilayah).' He said, 'What prevents you from the simple ones among the women?' And he said, 'They are the weak ones, those who do not establish hostility (Nasibi) nor do they know what you are upon.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the marriage of the Nasibi, so he said: No, by Allah, it is not permissible. Al-Fudayl said: Then I asked him once again, so I said: May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding their marriage? He said: And the woman is one who understands ( Wilayah)? I said: She understands. He said: The understanding woman is not placed (married) except with an understanding man.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, Ibn Bukayr, and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'What do you say regarding marrying the people, for I have reached the age you see and have never married.' He said, 'And what prevents you from that?' I said, 'Nothing prevents me except that I fear that marrying them may not be permissible for me. So what do you order me?' He said, 'How do you deal with it while you are young? Do you remain patient?' I said, 'I take the slave girls.' He said, 'Tell me now, so how do you make the slave girls permissible? Inform me.' I said, 'The slave girl is not at the status of the free woman. If the slave girl causes me doubt about something, I sell her or keep away from her.' He said, 'Explain to me, so how do you make her permissible?' He said, 'So there was no answer with me.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me, what is your view, shall I get married?' He said, 'What do I care if you were to do it.' I said, 'Can you see your words, He said, 'Surely, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had married, and there was from the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has related, and Allah the Exalted has said: Allah sets forth an example to those who disbelieve - the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut: they were both under two of Our righteous servants, but they acted treacherously towards them.' So I said, 'Surely, as for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), I am not of a status like that. But rather, she was in his hands and she agreed with his ruling, manifesting his religion. But, by Allah, I do not mean by that except with regards to the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: I said, 'May Allah keep you well! So what do you order me for? Shall I go and get married by your order?' So he said, 'If you were to do so, upon you is with the simple ones from the women.' I said, 'And what is the simple one?' He said, 'The veiled one, the chaste.' So I said, 'The one who is upon the religion of Salim Abu Hafs?' So he said, 'No.' I said, 'The one who is upon the religion of Rabi'ah al-Ra'i?' He said, 'No, but the young ones who are not hostile (Nasibi) and are not understanding what you are understanding (Wilayah).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There was a woman from Thaqif under his guardianship, and from her he had a son named Ibrahim. A slave girl of Thaqif came to her and said to her, 'Who is this husband of yours?' She said, 'Muhammad ibn Ali.' She said, 'Because of that, there are companions in Kufa, a people who insult the Salaf (early generations) and they say...' He said, 'So he freed her way (divorced her).' He said, 'I saw him after that, and it had become apparent upon him, and something had eroded from his body.' He said, 'So I said to him, 'The separation from her has become apparent upon you.' He said, 'And you have seen that?' I said, 'Yes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said, 'Your wife, the Shaybaniyya, is a Kharijite who insults Ali (peace be upon him). If it pleases you that I let you hear it from her, I will let you hear it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So when tomorrow comes, at the time you intend to go out as you usually do, return and hide by the side of the house.' He said, 'So when it was the next day, he hid by the side of the house. The man came and spoke to her, and that (insulting Ali) became clear from her. So he freed her way (divorced her), and although he used to like her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father asked him (peace be upon him) and I was listening, about the marriage of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Their marriage is more beloved to me than the marriage of the Hostile one (Nasibiyyah), and I do not like for the Muslim man to marry the Jewish woman nor the Christian woman, for fear that his son would become Jewish or Christian.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Marrying the Jewish woman and the Christian woman is preferable, or he said: better than marrying the Nasibi (Hostile one) and the Nasibiyyah (Hostile woman).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of marrying the Zanj, for they are a disfigured creation.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Makki, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Do not buy anyone from the Sudanese, and if it is inevitable, then (buy) from the Nubians, for they are among those for whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And with those who say, We are Christians, We made a Covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded with.' Indeed, they will remember that portion, and a brigade from them will come out with Al-Qaim (peace be upon him) from us. And do not marry anyone from the Kurds, for they are a species from the Jinn, the cover having been removed from them.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from 'Amr ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hashimi, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf, from Ali ibn Dawud al-Haddad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not marry the Zanj and the Khazar, for they have wombs (lineages) that indicate disloyalty. And the people of Hind, Sind, and Qand, there are no nobles among them, meaning Qandahar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the wicked (immoral) woman, can I marry her? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding the man who buys the slave girl or marries her. Without rishdah (maturity/prudence), and he takes her for himself, so he (peace be upon him) said: If he does not fear the defect (of illegitimacy) upon his children, then there is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the child of adultery married?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, and the child of her (the mother) is not sought (for lineage attribution to the father).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the wicked (immoral) woman, can the man marry her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is a slave girl for him, he can copulate with her, but he should not take her as a mother of his children'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who has a servant who is the child of adultery; is there any blame upon him if he copulates with her? He said: No, and if he remains aloof from that, it is more beloved to me.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) — or said: the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) — said: 'Women are of four types: one who gathers and unites, one who is like a flourishing spring bringing fertility, one who is a crushing distress, and one who is a filthy yoke.'

I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) — we were seated with him in the Mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — we discussed the matter of women and engaged extensively in the topic, while he remained silent, not entering our conversation with a single word. When we fell silent, he said: 'As for free women, do not mention them. But the best of slave girls is the one toward whom you have desire, and she possesses intellect and good manners, so you need not command or prohibit her.' Below that is one toward whom you have desire but she lacks good manners, so you need to command and prohibit. Below her is one toward whom you have desire but she has neither intellect nor good manners; you endure patience with her because of your passion for her. And a slave girl toward whom you have no desire, and she has neither intellect nor good manners — place the green ocean between yourself and her. He (the narrator) said: So I grabbed my beard, wanting to make a derisive sound at our excessive discussion since we had not arrived at any conclusion, and at his comprehensive statement. He then said to me: 'Enough! If you do that, I will not sit with you.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): My companion (wife) has died, and she was compatible for me, and I have thought about getting married. So he said to me: Consider where you are placing yourself, and whom you are associating in your wealth, and making privy to your religion and your secrets. If you must do it, then marry a virgin who is attributed to goodness and to good character. And know that they (women) are as has been said: 'Indeed! Women were created of various sorts — among them is the beneficial and the loss-maker, and among them is the crescent moon when it shines for its companion, and among them is the darkness. So whoever succeeds with the righteous among them will be fortunate, and whoever is deceived, there is no recourse for him.' And they are three types: A fertile, affectionate woman who supports her husband against the trials of time for his worldly life and his hereafter, and does not let time work against him; and a barren woman without beauty or good character, who does not assist her husband toward goodness; and a clamorous, intrusive, fault-finding woman who belittles what is much and does not accept what is little.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Sulayman ibn Sama'a, from al-Hazza', from his uncle Asim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women are four (types) — an all-encompassing good, and a fruitful spring, and a careless destructive one, and a lice-ridden shackle.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Marry off the foolish man and do not marry off the foolish woman, for the foolish man begets (children who are useful) and the foolish woman does not beget (useful children).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: One of our companions asked him (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who is fascinated by the beauty of a woman, is it permissible for him to marry her while she is insane? He (peace be upon him) said: No. But if there is an insane slave girl with him, there is no problem if he copulates with her, and he should not seek her children.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The adulterer marries not except an adulteress or an idolatress.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'These are women well-known for adultery and men well-known for adultery; they became famous and recognized by it, and the people today are in that same status.' So whoever upon whom the legal penalty for adultery has been established, or who is accused of adultery, it is not befitting for anyone to marry him until repentance is recognized from him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The adulterer marries not except an adulteress or an idolatress.' He said: 'These were women well-known for adultery and men well-known for adultery, who were recognized by that, and the people today are in that same status.' So whoever upon whom the legal penalty for adultery has been established, or who is publicized for it, it is not befitting for anyone to marry him until repentance is recognized from him.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic The adulterer maries not except an adulteress or a polytheess He said: They were men and women who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) known for adultery, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, forbade [marrying] those men and women; and the people today are upon that status, whoever publicized any of that or a legal penalty was established upon him, do not marry him until his repentance is recognized.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and he learned after marrying her that she had committed adultery. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If her husband so desires, he can take the dower from the one who married her off, and for her is the dower in exchange for what she permitted of her chastity, and if he so desires, he may leave her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no goodness in the child of adultery, nor in his skin, nor in his hair, nor in his flesh, nor in his blood, nor in anything from him. He was left out from the ship (of Noah), and the dog and the pig were carried therein.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban from Hakam ibn Hukeym from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And the adulteress, none shall marry her except an adulterer or an idolater.' He said: 'That is only regarding the open (blatant).' Then he said: 'If a person commits adultery, then repents, he may marry wherever he desires.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man, is it permissible for him to marry a woman with whom he had been immoral? He said: If he discerns maturity/reason from her, then yes; and if not, let him entice her to the forbidden (sexual act); if she follows him (to the forbidden act), then she is forbidden to him; and if she refuses, then let him marry her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Any man who commits fornication with a woman, then it becomes pleasing to him to marry her, [the ruling is] permissible. He said: Its beginning is fornication (zina), and its end is marriage. And its example is like that of a palm tree: a man takes its fruit unlawfully, then he buys it afterwards, so it becomes permissible for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who was immoral with a woman, then it occurred to him to marry her. So he said: It is permissible. Its beginning was fornication and its end was marriage. Its beginning was prohibited and its end was permissible.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Usman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Jareer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man commits fornication with a woman, then it becomes inevitable for him to marry her. Is it permissible for him?' He said, 'Yes, if he keeps away from her until her waiting period expires by clearing her womb from the water of fornication, then it is permissible for him to marry her. And rather, it is permissible for him to marry her after he ascertains her repentance.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the believing man who marries the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he attains a Muslim woman, so what does he do with the Jewish woman and the Christian woman?' So I said to him: 'If he happens to have passion for her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he does, let him prevent her from drinking wine and eating the flesh of the swine, and know that there is a shortcoming upon him in his religion.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the marriage of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for the Muslim to marry a Jewish woman, nor a Christian woman, but rather it is permissible for him from them to marry the simple ones (those unaware of their religion).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Can one marry a Magian woman?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but if there was such a slave girl for him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: One does not marry the Jewish woman, nor the Christian woman, upon (as an additional wife to) the Muslim woman.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, can the man marry her upon (as an additional wife) the Muslim woman? He (peace be upon him) said: No, and he can marry the Muslim woman upon the Jewish woman and the Christian woman.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Jaham, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad, what do you say regarding a man who marries a Christian woman upon a Muslim woman?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is my opinion in front of you?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say it, for in that you will come to learn my opinion.' I said: 'It is not allowed to marry the Christian woman upon a Muslim woman, nor a non-Muslim woman.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why?' I said: 'Due to the Words of Allah (Exalted and Majestic): And do not marry the idolatresses until they believe.' And do not marry the idolatresses until they believe. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what do you say regarding this Verse: And the chaste women from among those who have been Given the Book before you?' I said: 'So His Words: And do not marry the idolatresses, abrogate this Verse?' So he (peace be upon him) smiled, then was silent.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the chaste women from among those who have been Given the Book before you' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is Abrogated by His Words: 'and hold not to the ties of marriage of unbelieving women''

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The People of the Book and all those who have a covenant (dhimmah), if one of the two spouses becomes a Muslim, they remain upon their marriage, and it is not for him to expel her from the House of Islam to another, nor should he spend the night with her, but he should come to her during the day. As for the Polytheists, such as the polytheists of the Arabs and others, they remain upon their marriage until the expiry of the waiting period (iddah). If the woman becomes a Muslim, then the man becomes a Muslim before the expiry of her term, she is his wife; but if he does not become a Muslim except after the expiry of the term, she has been irrevocably divorced from him, and there is no way for him to her. And similarly is all those who have no covenant, nor is it befitting for the Muslim man to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman when he can find a Muslim woman, whether she is free or a slave girl.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting for the Muslim man to marry a Jewish woman or a Christian woman when he can find a Muslim woman, whether she is free or a slave girl.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked about a man who has a Christian wife, is it permissible for him to marry a Jewish woman upon her? He said: The People of the Book are slaves (under the authority) of the Imam, and that is a leeway expanded by us upon you specifically, so there is no problem if he marries. I said: What if he marries a slave girl? He said: No, it is not correct for him to marry three slave girls. So if he marries a free Muslim woman upon them both, and she does not know that he has a Christian wife and a Jewish wife, then he consummates the marriage with her, then for her is what she took of the dowry. If she wishes to stay with him afterwards, she stays; and if she wishes to go to her family, she goes.
