And when she has three menstrual periods, or three months pass for her, she becomes permissible for marriage (to others). I said: What if he divorces the Jewish woman and the Christian woman before the waiting period of the Muslim woman expires, is there a way for him to return her to his house? He said: Yes.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the free man marrying the slave girl, he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem when he is desperate to her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Marry a free woman upon a slave girl, and do not marry a slave girl upon a free woman; and whoever marries a slave girl upon a free woman, his marriage is void.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about marrying the slave girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A free man marries a free woman upon a slave girl, and a slave girl is not married upon a free woman; and the marriage of a slave girl upon a free woman is void. And if a free woman and a slave girl gather together with you, then for the free woman are two days and for the slave girl is one day. The marriage of the slave girl is not valid except with the permission of her masters.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yahya al-Lahham, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a free woman and for him is a slave wife, and the free woman did not know that for him is a slave wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the free woman desires to stay with the slave wife, she stays; and if she desires, she goes back to her family.' I said to him: 'If she is not pleased with that and goes back to her family, is there a way for him upon her when she is not pleased with staying?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no way for him upon her when she is not pleased when she comes to know.' I said: 'So her going back to her family is her divorce?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. When she goes out from his house, she observes a waiting period of three months or three menses-free periods, then she marries if she desires.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it for the man to marry the Christian woman upon the Muslim woman, and the slave girl upon the free woman? He said: No. One of the two (the Christian or the slave) is not married upon the Muslim woman, but the Muslim woman is married upon the slave girl and the Christian woman; and for the Muslim woman is two-thirds, and for the slave girl and the Christian woman is one-third.
Aban, from Zurara bin A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked about the man who marries the slave girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he is compelled to do so.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting that the free man marries the slave woman today. Rather, that was when Allah Mighty and Majestic said: 'And whoever among you has not within his power ampleness of means', and the ampleness of means is the dower, and a dower of the free woman today is a dower of the slave girl or even less.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar and others, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the affluent Muslim to marry a slave girl except if he cannot find a free woman. Thus, similarly, it is not befitting for him to marry a woman from the People of the Book except in a state of necessity when he cannot find a Muslim woman, neither a free one nor a slave girl.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting for the free man that he marries the slave girl while he is able to marry the free woman, and it is not befitting that he marries the slave girl in addition to the free woman; and there is no problem if he marries the free woman in addition to the slave girl. So if he were to marry the free woman in addition to the slave girl, then for the free woman is two days, and for the slave girl is one day.

Muhammad ibn ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) or from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), who said: He forbade the marriage of two women [to one man] where there is no dower for either of them except the sexual intercourse [consummation] of her companion [the other wife], and he said: It is not permissible for him to marry one of the two except with a dower, and [with] the marriage [customs] of the Muslims.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Basheer, from Ghayath ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no Jalab, nor Janab, nor Shighar in Islam; and Shighar is that a man marries a man his daughter or his sister, and he marries the daughter or sister of the one who married him, and there is no dowry between them other than this marriage of this one from this one, and this one from this one.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the marriage of Shighaar, and it is Al-Mumanah, and it is that a man says to another man, 'Marry your daughter to me so that I may marry my daughter to you,' on the condition that there is no dower between them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who marries a woman and also marries the mother of her children (from another husband). He said: There is no problem with that. So I said to him: It has reached us from your father that Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) married the daughter of Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and the mother of the children of Al-Hasan. And that is, a man from our companions asked me to ask you about it. So he said: It is not like this. Rather, Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) married the daughter of Al-Hasan and the mother of a child for Ali ibn Al-Husayn, the one who was martyred among you. So he wrote about that to Abd Al-Malik ibn Marwan, so he criticized Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So he wrote to him regarding that, and he wrote to him the answer. So when he read the letter, he said: Surely, Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) humbles himself, and surely Allah raises him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who marries a woman and also marries the mother of her child (from another man), and he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who gifts the slave girl to the husband of his daughter, and he had copulated with her. Can the husband of his daughter copulate with her? He said: There is no problem with it.

From him, from Imran ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I was in the presence of Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so Safwan asked him about a man who married the daughter of a man, and that man had a wife and a mother of a child (from another wife). So the father of the girl died. Is it permissible for the man who married the daughter to marry his [own] wife and the mother of his child? He said: There is no problem with it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from 'Ubay ibn Hisham, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who marries a woman, and her father gifts to her a slave girl whom he had copulated with? Is it permissible for her husband to copulate with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a mother of the children of a man. So her master died, and for the deceased was a child from other than the mother of his children. What is your view if the one who married the mother of the children were to marry the daughter of her master who had emancipated her, so that he would gather between her and the daughter of her master who had emancipated her? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi al-Awjah asked Hisham ibn al-Hakam, so he said to him, 'Is Allah not All-Wise?' He said, 'Yes, and He is the most Wise of the wise.' He said, 'So inform me about His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: "Then marry such women as seem good to you, two and three and four; but if you fear that you will not do justice (between them), then (marry) only one." Is this not an obligation?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So inform me about His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: "And you have it not in your power to do justice between wives, even though you may wish (it), but be not disinclined (from one) with total disinclination." Which Wise One would speak with this?' So there did not happen to be an answer with him. So he traveled to Medina to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So he said, 'O Hisham! (You have come) at such a time which is neither of Hajj nor of Umrah?' He said, 'Yes, May I be sacrificed for you.' It has concerned me that Ibn Abi al-Awjah asked me a question for which there was no answer with me with regards to it.' He said, 'And what is it?' He said, 'So I informed him of the story.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: "Then marry such women as seem good to you, two and three and four; but if you fear that you will not do justice (between them), then (marry) only one," meaning regarding the expenditure.' And as for His Words: "And you have it not in your power to do justice between wives, even though you may wish (it), but be not disinclined (from one) with total disinclination, so that you leave her as it were in suspense," so it is regarding the cordiality.' He (the narrator) said, 'So when Hisham proceeded to him with the answer and informed him, he said, 'By Allah! This is not from yourself'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted permitted the private parts based on the capacity of the servants regarding strength in paying the dower and ability to keep (them), so He said: 'Marry such women as seem good to you, two and three and four; but if you fear that you will not do justice (between them), then (marry) only one or what your right hands possess'; and He said: 'And whoever among you has not within his power ampleness of means to marry free believing women, then (he may marry) of those whom your right hands possess from among your believing maidens'; and He said: 'Then as to those whom you enjoy with, give them their dowries as appointed; and there is no blame on you about what you mutually agree after what is appointed'. Thus, Allah permitted the private parts for the people of strength according to their strength in giving the dower and ability to keep: four for the one who is able to do that; and for the one below that, three, two, and one; and the one who is not able to keep one should marry the possession of the right hand. And when he is not able to keep her, nor able to marry the free woman, nor able to buy the slave girl, then Allah has permitted temporary marriage with the easiest of what he can manage from the dower, and without the necessity of expenses. And Allah made self-sufficient each group from them with whatever He gave them of strength in giving the dower and ability in expenses regarding keeping, and regarding keeping regarding chastity from immorality; otherwise they would be given from Allah Mighty and Majestic good assistance, and given strength, and pointed towards the permissible aspect due to what He gave them that would make them chaste from the prohibited in what He gave them and made them needless from the prohibited, and clarified that for them. Thus, at that time, He placed the legal punishments upon them, from whipping, stoning, cursing, and separation; and had Allah not made self-sufficient each group from them with what He made for them the way to the permissible aspects, He would not have placed a legal punishment from these legal punishments upon them. So, as for the aspect of permanent marriage and the aspect of possession of the right hand, its proof is clear and obvious in the hands of the people due to the frequency of their dealin

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The private part (of a man) becomes permissible through three: marriage with inheritance, and marriage without inheritance, and marriage of possession of the right hand (slave girl).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The private parts become permissible through three: marriage by inheritance, and marriage without inheritance, and marriage by possession of the right hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Zayd, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The private parts are made permissible by three: marriage by inheritance, and marriage without inheritance, and marriage of the possession of the right hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who intends to marry the woman, can he look at her? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. He is buying her with the highest of the prices.

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Hammad ibn Uthman, and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with looking at her face and her two wrists when he intends to marry her.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn al-Sari, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man intends to marry a woman; can he examine her and look at her back and her face?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no harm in the man looking at the woman when he intends to marry her; he looks at her back and her face.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of our companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he asked him about the man looking at the woman before he marries her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, so why is he giving his wealth'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from his father, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I said to him, 'Should a man look at the woman he intends to marry, so he looks at her hair and her beauty?' He said, 'There is no problem with that when there is no deriving pleasure.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Hamza who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: We were in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and he said: 'The best of your women are the child-bearing, the affectionate, the chaste, the honored among her family, humble with her husband, adorning herself for her husband, a fortress toward others, who listens to his words and obeys his instructions, and whenever he is alone with her she gives him whatever he desires from her, and does not show immodesty as a man does.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The best of your women is she who, when she is alone with her husband, removes for him the shield of modesty, and when she dresses up, she dresses up with it the shield of modesty.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of your women is the chaste, the ardently loving.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best women of my community are the most beautiful-faced and the least in dowry.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of your women have five (qualities).' It was said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, and what are the five?' He said: 'The modest, the gentle, the supportive — the one who, when her husband is angered, does not neglect him even for the blink of an eye until he is pleased; and when her husband is absent from her, she protects him (his interests) during his absence. Thus, that (woman) is a worker from the workers of God, and a worker of God will not fail.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The best of your women is the one with a pleasant fragrance, skilled in cooking, who when she spends, spends with moderation, and when she refrains, refrains with moderation. Such a woman is a worker from among the workers of God, and a worker of God will neither fail nor be remorseful.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from Amr ibn Jami', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of your women is the one who is wholesome in food, pleasant in fragrance; when she spends, she spends with propriety, and when she withholds, she withholds with propriety. Such a woman is a worker among the workers of God, and the worker of God does not fail.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khash'ami, from Zurays ibn Abdul Malik, who said: When it reached Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that a man got married during a time of heat at midday, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see the two of them as being concordant'. So they ended up being separated.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Ubayd ibn Zurarah and Abū al-ʿAbbās, who both said: Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the man to have sexual intercourse with his wife on the night of Wednesday.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami from Aban ibn 'Uthman from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah and Abu al-'Abbas, both said: He said: Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for a man to go to bed with his wife on Wednesday night.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say regarding marriage: 'From the Sunnah is marriage at night, because Allah made the night for rest, and the women are indeed a tranquility.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Conduct the procession of your brides at night, and feed [your guests] in the forenoon.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Muyassar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'O Muyassar! Marry at night, for Allah has made it for rest, and do not seek a need at night, for the night is dark.' Then he said: 'Surely, for the night visitor there is a great right, and for the owner there is a great right.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Al-Najjashi proposed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for Amina, daughter of Abu Sufyan, and he married her, he called for food and said: "Indeed, among the Sunnah of the sent messengers is feeding people at the time of marriage."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he married Maymuna bint al-Harith, gave a banquet (Waleema) for it and fed the people Al-Hays (a mixture of dates and butter).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, raised it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) He said: The wedding feast (Waleema) for one day is a mark of honor, and for two days it is prestige, and for three days it is showing-off and seeking fame.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wedding feast (walimah) on the first day is a right (Sunnah), and the second day is goodness (recommended), and whatever is added beyond that is for show-off and fame.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a group from the Banu Umayya, during the emirate of Uthman, gathered in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on a Friday. They wanted to marry a man from among them, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was nearby. Some of them said to others, 'Shall we shame Ali at this moment? We will ask him to address us, and we will keep talking, for he will be shy and weary of speech.' So they approached him and said, 'O Abu al-Hasan! We want to marry so-and-so to so-and-so, and we want you to address us.' He said, 'Are you waiting for anyone?' They said, 'No.' By Allah, he did not delay long before he said: 'Praise is to Allah, the One particularized with Oneness, the Foremost with Warning, the Doer of what He wills, the Veiled by Light from His creation, the Possessor of the Lofty Horizon and the Exalted Honor and the Luxurious Kingdom, worshipped for His Bounties, Lord of the Earth and the Sky. I praise Him for the beauty of affliction and the grace of giving and the plenteous blessings, and for what our Lord defends from affliction; a praise for which the servants begin and upon which the lands flourish. And I testify that there is no god but Allah, One, with no partner, for whom there was no thing before, and for whom there will be no thing after.' And I testify that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger, whom He chose with preference and guided by him from misguidance. He singled him out for Himself and sent him to His creation with His messages and His speech, inviting them to His worship, His Oneness, and acknowledgment of His Lordship, and belief in His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He sent him at a time of interval from the Messengers, when people had turned away from the Truth, were ignorant of the Lord, and disbelieved in the Resurrection and the Warning. So he delivered His messages, strove in His way, advised his community, and worshipped Him until death came to him. May Allah bless him and his family abundantly. I advise you and myself with the fear of Allah the Magnificent. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made for the pious an exit from what they dislike and sustenance from where they do n

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ayman ibn Muhraz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) married off a woman from the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, and he was in charge of her matter, so he said: 'All praise is for Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Lenient, the Forgiver, the One, the Subduer, the Great, the Exalted. It is the same from you all, whether you speak secretly or publicly, whether you are concealed by night or visible by day. I testify that there is no god but Allah, One, with no partner, to whom belongs the Kingdom and the Praise, and He is Able over all things. And I testify that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with His Book as a proof upon His servants. Whoever obeys him obeys Allah, and whoever disobeys him disobeys Allah. May Allah bless him and his family abundantly. The Imam of Guidance and the Chosen Prophet. Then I advise you with the fear of Allah, for it is Allah's advice in the past and the bygone days.' Then he solemnized the marriage.

Ahmad from Ismail ibn Mihran said, 'Abdul Malik ibn Abi al-Harith narrated to us from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said,' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) delivered this sermon, saying: 'All praise is for Allah. I praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, seek His guidance, believe in Him, and rely upon Him. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and the true religion, to make it prevail over all other religions, as evidence for Him and a caller to Him.' So He demolished the pillars of disbelief and illuminated the lanterns of faith. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, the path of true guidance becomes his path and the light of piety becomes his evidence; and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger misses all true guidance and harms only himself. I advise you, servants of Allah, with the fear of Allah, as the advice of one who gave sincere counsel and the preaching of one who delivered and strived. Thereafter, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Islam an enlightened path, with shining beacons, wherein hearts unite and upon it brothers become brothers. And that which is between us and you from that is constant affection and an ancient covenant, a recognition from each to all of everything upon which we are. May Allah forgive us and you, and peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Azrami, from his father, who said: When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) intended to solemnize a marriage, he would say: 'All praise is for Allah, I praise Him and seek His help, and I believe in Him and rely upon Him, and I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with Guidance and the Religion of Truth to make it prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists dislike it. And may Allah bless Muhammad and his Progeny, and peace and mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you.' 'I advise you, servants of Allah, with the fear of Allah, the Guardian of the Bounties and Mercy, Creator of the beings and Manager of their affairs with Power and Mastery. Indeed, to Allah belongs the praise for what is to come and what has passed. To Him belongs exclusive praise and sincere eulogy for whatever grace from Him has been a bountiful blessing to us, a covering upon us, and an adornment for us; the Creator of what is honored and the humbler of what is difficult, the facilitator of what is hard, and the achiever of what is easy.' 'The Initiator of creation with an initial beginning, on the day He originated the sky while it was smoke, so He said to it and the earth: 'Come willingly or unwillingly.' They said: 'We come willingly.' So He completed them as seven heavens in two days. And neither does a severe [force] confuse Him, nor does a fleeing one precede Him, nor does a departing one escape Him. On the Day when every soul is paid what it has earned, and they are not wronged.' Then, indeed, so-and-so ibn so-and-so...

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, who said, 'Al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Baghdadi narrated to me, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):' An answer regarding the marriage sermon: All praise is for Allah, the Chosen for Praise, who singles it out for Himself, glorified by His Mention and exalted by His Command. We praise Him, not doubting in Him; we consider what we prepare as hope for its success and key to its gain, and we attain needs from Him through it. We seek guidance from Allah by the firmness of guidance, the bonds of security, and the resolutions of piety, and we seek refuge with Allah from blindness after guidance, and action in the straying paths of desire. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, a servant who did not worship anyone other than Him. He chose him with His Knowledge, and made him trustworthy over His Revelation, and a Messenger to His creation. So may Allah send blessings upon him and his family. Thereafter, we have heard your speech, and you are the close relatives; we desire alliance with you, assist you in your needs, and cherish your brotherhood. We have accepted your intercessor's intercession, and we have married your suitor, stipulating that for her is from the dower what you mentioned. We ask Allah, Who established affairs by His Power, to make the outcome of this gathering of ours what He loves. Indeed, He is the Guardian of that and the Able over it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) address with this sermon: 'The Praise is for Allah, the Knower of what is to occur before any of His creatures realizes it.' The Originator of the skies and the earth. The Composer of the causes with what the Pens flow with, and the Ordained matters occur from the precedence of His Knowledge, and a measurement of His Wisdom. I praise Him upon His Bounties, and I seek Refuge with Him from His Vengeance, seeking Guidance of Allah, and I seek Refuge with Him from the straying and the destruction. The one whom Allah Guides, so he has travelled upon the ideal road, and has acquired the best of the booties; and the one whom Allah Lets to stray, so he is perplexed from the guidance and collapsed into the destruction. And I testify that there is no god except for Allah, One, there being no associates for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, the Chosen one, and His Guardian with whom He is Pleased with, and Sent him with the Guidance. He sent him upon where there was an interval from the Messengers and there was differing among the nations, and there was an interruption from the ways and the teachings from the Wisdom, and obscurities from the banners of the Guidance and the proofs. So he delivered the Message of his Lord, and implemented His Commands and fulfilled the Truth which he was upon, and he passed away and the Praiser is very much missed. Then, these matters are in the Hands of Allah, all of them, causing them to flow to its reasons and its measurements. So Allah's Command flows by His Measurement, and Measured it to flow to its term, and flowing it to its prescribed time, and for every term there is a prescribed time. Allah Obliterates whatever He so Desires to and Establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Thereafter, Allah Mighty and Majestic made the marital bond a cordiality for the hearts, and as a link linking it to the womb relationships, and Made it a kindness and a mercy, and in that are signs for the worlds. And He it is Who Created a mortal from the water, so He made for him relationships of lineage and marriage. And marry those among you who are single and those who are fit among your male slaves and your female slaves. And, so and so, son of so and so is from the ones who

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muawiya ibn Hukeym said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) delivered this sermon: All praise is for Allah who praised Himself in the Book, and opened His Book with praise, and made praise the first recompense for the abode of His bounty and the last call of the inhabitants of His Paradise. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, without a partner, a testimony I purify for Him and store with Him. And Allah blesses Muhammad, the seal of prophethood and the best of creation, and his Progeny, the Progeny of mercy, the tree of bounty, the mine of messengership, and the destination of the angels. And praise is for Allah, who in His prior knowledge and speaking Book and truthful explanation, made the most rightful cause for kinship and preference, and the most deserving matter for desire, a cause that obligates a cause and a matter that results in self-sufficiency. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And it is He who created from water a human being and made for him lineage and marriage, and ever is your Lord Powerful.' And He said: 'And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves; if they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.' And even if there were not in marriage and intermarriage a decisive verse, nor a followed sunnah, nor a widespread tradition, it would be among what Allah made of kindness to the near, bringing the distant close, uniting hearts, interlacing rights, increasing numbers, and providing offspring for the calamities of time and events of affairs, that which the wise intellect desires above it, the successful one hastens to it, and the educated one strives for it. So the closest of people to Allah is he who follows His command, implements His ruling, fulfills His decree, and hopes for His reward. And So-and-so, son of So-and-so, whose state and majesty you know, was pleased with himself and came to you preferring you and choosing for the proposal of So-and-so, daughter of So-and-so, your noble one, and offered her such and such as dower. So receive him with acceptance and respond to him with desire, and seek Allah's guidance in your affairs, that He may strengthen you upon your right path, if Allah wills. We ask Allah to join what is between you with righteousness and piety, to unite it with love and desire,

Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) would deliver the marriage sermon: 'All praise is to Allah, to glorify His power, and there is no god except Allah, in humility to His majesty, and blessings be upon Muhammad and his progeny,' and upon mentioning Him, Indeed, Allah created from water a human being, so He made for him relationships of lineage and marriage up to the end of the Verse.

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) intended to marry Khadeejah bint Khuwaylid, Abu Talib came with his family and a number of Quraish, until he entered upon Waraqah ibn Nawfal, the uncle of Khadeejah. Abu Talib began with speech, saying: 'Praise is to the Lord of this House, who made us from the offspring of Ibrahim and the descendants of Ismail, and sent down to us a secure sanctuary, and made us rulers over the people, and blessed us in our land in which we are.' Then, this son of my brother, meaning the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), is one who, when weighed against any man from Quraish, is heavier; when compared to any man, he is greater; and there is no equal for him among creation. And even if he is poor in wealth, for wealth is a flowing provision and a transient shade. And he has desire for Khadeejah, and she has desire for him. We have come to you to propose her to you with her consent and command. The dower is upon me in my wealth, whatever you ask for, both immediate and delayed. And for him, by the Lord of this House, is a great share, a widespread religion, and a complete judgment. Then Abu Talib fell silent, and her uncle spoke. He hesitated and was deficient in answering Abu Talib, and stuttering and confusion overtook him, and he was a man from the clergymen. So Khadeejah said, initiating: 'O my uncle! You, even though you are more entitled to my person than I am in witnessing, you are not more entitled to me than my own self. I have married myself to you, O Muhammad, and the dower is upon me in my wealth. So command your uncle to sacrifice a she-camel, to prepare a feast with it, and enter upon your family.' Abu Talib said: 'Bear witness upon her for accepting Muhammad, and for her guaranteeing the dower in her wealth.' So some of Quraish said, 'O wonder! The dower is upon the women for the men?' So Abu Talib became angry with intense anger, and stood on his feet. He was one whom the men feared and whose anger was disliked. He said: 'When they are like this son of my brother, the men are sought with the most expensive prices and the greatest dower. And when they are like you, they are not married except with the expensive dower.' And Abu Talib s

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Jameel ibn Darraj, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The dower of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was twelve Owqiya and one Nash, and the Owqiya is forty Dirhams, and the Nash is twenty Dirhams, and it is half the Owqiya.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) dispatched to his wives twelve Owqiya and one Nash, and the Owqiya is forty Dirhams, and the Nash is half the Owqiya, being twenty Dirhams. So that was five hundred Dirhams.' I said, 'By our weighing?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the dowry, is there a specific time for it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dowry of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was twelve Owqiya and one Nash, and the Nash is half the Owqiya, and the Owqiya is forty Dirhams, so that is five hundred Dirhams.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The dowry of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for his wives was twelve Uqiyyah and one Nash, and the Uqiyyah is forty Dirhams, and the Nash is half the Uqiyyah, and it is twenty Dirhams.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: My father (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not marry off the rest of his daughters, nor did he marry any of his wives for more than twelve Owqiya and one Nash; the Owqiya is forty [Dirhams], and the Nash is twenty [Dirhams].
And Hammad reported from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: And the dirhams at that time weighed six (units).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz, from a man, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Sunnah dowry, how it became five hundred. He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, obligated upon Himself that if a believer glorifies Him (Allahu Akbar) one hundred times, glorifies Him (SubhanAllah) one hundred times, praises Him (Alhamdulillah) one hundred times, proclaims His Oneness (La ilaha illallah) one hundred times, and sends blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny one hundred times, then says, 'O Allah, marry me to the Houris with large beautiful eyes,' Allah will marry him to Hawra' (a specific Houri) and make that (recitation) her dowry. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that the Sunnah dowry of the believing women is five hundred dirhams. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did that. And any believer who proposes to his brother for his honorable daughter and states the dowry as five hundred dirhams, but he does not marry her to him, has been disloyal to him, and deserves from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He does not marry him to a Houri.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khasha'i, from Ibn Abi Yafour, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) married Fatima (peace be upon her) upon a threadbare garment, a shield, and a bed which was from the skin of a ram.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Fatima (peace be upon her) upon a cracked shield valued at thirty dirhams.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Ali to Fatima (peace be upon her) upon a cracked shield, and her bed was of sheep skin. They would make the wool to be underneath its side when sleeping.

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Fatima (peace be upon her) to Ali (peace be upon him) with a dower of a cracked shield valued at thirty dirhams.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Khazzaz, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The dower of Fatima (peace be upon her) was a threadbare garment, a cracked shield, and her bed was a sheepskin; they would cast it down, spread it out, and sleep upon it.

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ali ibn Asbat from Dawud from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Ali to Fatimah (peace be upon her), he entered upon her while she was weeping, so he asked her, 'What is making you weep? By Allah, if there were anyone better in my family than him, I would not have married you to him, and I did not marry you to him, but it is Allah who married you to him and gave you in marriage with the Khums (one-fifth) as long as the heavens and the earth exist.'

Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Sulayman, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Fatimah (peace be upon her) said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'You have married me off with a meager mahr (dower).' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'I did not marry you off, but rather Allah married you off from the heavens, and He made your mahr one-fifth of the world, as long as the heavens and the earth exist.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the dower (mahr), what is it? He said: 'Whatever the people agree upon.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The dower is whatever the people agree upon, or twelve Owqiya and one Nashsha, or five hundred Dirhams.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The dower is whatever the two parties agree upon, whether little or much, so this is the dower.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The dower (mahr) is anything upon which the people agree, whether little or much, in a temporary marriage or a permanent marriage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the dower (mahr), so he said: 'Whatever the people agree upon, or twelve awqiya and one nashsh, or five hundred dirhams.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Abu Ayyoub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a man who married a woman upon her decision or upon his decision. So he died or she died before he had copulated with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'For her would be the enjoyment, and the inheritance, and there is no dower for her'. I said, 'Supposing he divorces her and he had married her upon her decision?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he divorces her and he had married her upon her decision, her decision upon him cannot exceed to be more than the weight of five hundred Dirhams of silver, a dower of the wives of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family)'.

Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Nu'man Al-Ahowl, from Buraib Al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman on the condition that he teach her a chapter from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: 'I do not like that he should enter (consume) with her until he has taught her the chapter and given her something.' I said: 'Is it permissible if he gives her a date or a raisin?' He said: 'There is no problem with that if she is pleased with it, whatever it may be.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A woman came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Marry me off.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Who is for this one?' A man stood up and said, 'I am, O Messenger of Allah, marry me to her.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What will you give her?' He said, 'I have nothing.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'No.' She repeated, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) repeated the question, but no one stood up except that man. Then she repeated again. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said on the third time: 'Do you know anything from the Quran?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'I have married you to her on whatever you know from the Quran, so teach her it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman with a thousand dirhams, so he gave her an absconded slave of his and a silken gown, as the thousand dirhams which was her dower. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she was pleased with the slave and had known it, so there is no problem when she takes possession of the cloth and is pleased with the slave.' I said, 'Supposing he divorces her before he enters with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dower for her, and she returns to him five hundred dirhams, and the slave becomes hers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man married a woman with a servant as the dower.' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'An average from the servants.' I said: 'With a house?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'An average from the houses.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his daughter to his brother's son, and gave her as dower a house and a servant. Then the man died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The dower is taken from the middle of the wealth.' I said: 'And the house and the servant?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The middle of the houses, and the servant is the middle of the servants.' I said: 'Thirty or forty dinars, and the house is about that much.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is seventy, eighty dinars, or a hundred, about that much.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who married a woman and did not specify a dower for her, then consummated the marriage with her: He said: 'For her is the dower of her womenfolk.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries with an immediate (dower) and a delayed (dower), he (peace be upon him) said: 'The delayed one is until death or separation'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who kept a dower secret and announced as more than it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is that which he kept a secret, and upon it would be the marriage'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know from where the dowries of women became four thousand?' I said, 'No'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Umm Habib, daughter of Abu Sufyan, was in Abyssinia. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) proposed to her, and Al-Najashi sent to her on his behalf four thousand. From there, they take it as a precedent. As for the dower, it is twelve Oqiyah and one Nash.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn Bishr, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Battakhi, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a woman on the condition of teaching her a Chapter from the Book of Allah, then divorced her before consummating the marriage, with what does he have recourse upon her? He said: With half of what he would teach, similar to that Chapter.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any woman who donates her dower to her husband before he has intercourse with her, Allah will write for her the emancipation of a slave for every dinar.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what about gifting it after intercourse?' He said: 'That is from affection and companionship.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the lowest amount that suffices as the dower (mahr)?' He said, 'A lump of sugar.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah will forgive every sin on the Day of Judgement except the dower of a woman, and the one who usurps the wages of an employee, and the one who sells a free person'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Mashraqi, from a number who narrated it to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Imam would pay off the debts of the believers, except for the dowries of the women.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Najran, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries the woman and copulates with her, then she claims upon him for her dower, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he copulates with her, it demolishes the immediate (dower).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who enters with the woman. then she claims upon him her dower, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he enters with her, then it demolishes the immediate (dower).'

I heard him saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you all about the most evil of your women? She is the one who is disgraced among her own family yet arrogant toward her husband; the sterile one, the vengeful one, who has no qualms about anything indecent; the one who displays herself (to strangers) whenever her husband is away from her, but becomes reserved and chaste when he is present — she does not listen to his words nor obey his instructions; and whenever her husband is alone with her she withholds herself from him, just as a stubborn animal resists being ridden, not accepting any excuse from him and not forgiving him any mistake.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of his companions, from Milhan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The worst of your women are the barren one who causes ruin, the impure/profane, the stubborn, the disobedient, the disgraceful among her people, the one who thinks highly of herself, the one who withholds from her husband, and the one who is loose with others.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was among the supplications of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family): 'I seek refuge in You from a woman who ages me before my (natural) time of old age.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The one who marries the woman but does not make it in his self that he would be giving her dower to her, so he is an adulterer.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries the woman but does not make it within himself that he would be giving her her dower, so he is an adulterer.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Sinan, all from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halbi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who gifts herself to the man who marries her without a dower. He said: 'This was only for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). As for others, this is not correct until he compensates her with something, which he presents to her before he consummates the marriage with her, whether little or much, even if it is a garment or a dirham.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dirham suffices.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And a believing woman if she gave herself to the Prophet' So he said: 'The gifting is not permissible except for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and as for others, so a marriage is not correct except with a dower.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The gift (of oneself) is not permissible except for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and as for others, then marriage is not valid except with a dower.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who gifts herself to a man, or her guardian gifts her to him, he said: 'No, that was for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and it is not for others except if he compensates her with something, little or much.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who gifted herself to a man from the Muslims, he said: 'If he were to offset it (with a payment), so that would be straight (correct)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda and Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a woman, consummated the marriage with her, and she bore him children, then he died from her. She claimed a portion of her dower from her husband's heirs, coming to seek it from them and also seeking the inheritance. He (peace be upon him) said: As for the inheritance, she may seek it. As for the dower, it is that which she took from the husband before he consummated the marriage with her; that is what made her private part permissible to him, whether it was little or much. When she took possession of it from him, accepted it, and went to him (to live with him), she has nothing else after that.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the husband and wife who both die, so the inheritors of the woman come and claim the dower upon the inheritors of the man. He said: 'And they had both died and the inheritance was distributed?' I said: 'Yes'. He said: 'There is nothing for them.' I said: 'And if the woman was alive, and she came after the death of her husband to claim her dower?' He said: 'There is nothing for her, and she had stayed with him acknowledging [the debt] until her husband died.' I said: 'And if she died while he was alive, so her inheritors came seeking her dower from him?' He said: 'And she had stayed with him until she died not seeking it?' I said: 'Yes'. He said: 'There is nothing for them.' I said: 'And if he divorced her, so she came seeking her dower?' He said: 'And she had stayed not seeking it until he divorced her, there is nothing for her.' I said: 'So when is the limit of that which, if she were to seek it, it would be for her?' He said: 'If it was gifted to her and she entered his house, then she seeks it after that, so there is nothing for her.' It is sufficient for her if she makes him swear an oath by Allah that there is no dower for her with him, neither little nor much.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding a man who married a woman but did not enter (consume) with her, so she claimed that her dower was one hundred dinars, and the husband mentioned that her dower was fifty dinars, and there was no proof between them, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The word is the word of the husband with his oath.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man copulates with his wife, then she claims the dower and he says, 'I have given you,' then upon him is the proof and upon him is the oath.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the man who marries the woman without witnesses, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with the marriage of the couple regarding what is between him and Allah. The witnesses were made (necessary) in the marriage of the couple only for the sake of the children. Had it not been for that, there would not be a problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the proofs (evidence) were made for the lineage and the inheritances. And in another report: And the legal punishments (Hudud).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries without a proof (witnesses), he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards, nor that you should change them for other wives, though their beauty be pleasing to you, except what your right hand possesses.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that you are alleging that it is permissible for you whatever was not permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and indeed Allah, the Exalted, permitted His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) to marry from the women whatever he wished.' He only said 'It is not allowed to you to take women afterwards' after what He prohibited to you, as in His Words: 'Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters' up to the end of the verse.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Jameel ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How many of the women were permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever he so desired,' gesturing with his hand like this, 'and it is permissible for him,' meaning by the grasping of his hand.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdul Kareem bin Amr, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives' — how many women were permissible for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever he desired from anything.' I said, 'And a believing woman if she gave herself to the Prophet.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The gifting is not permissible except for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and as for the others than the Messenger of Allah, marriage is not correct except with a dowry.' I said, 'What is your view of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is not permissible for you to take women afterwards'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, it means by it, 'It is not permissible for you the women which Allah had prohibited in this Verse: 'Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters and your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts' — up to the end of it.' And had the matter been as you are saying, it would have been permissible for you what was not permissible for him, because one of you changes [wives] whenever he wants, but the matter is not as they are saying. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he marry from the women whatever he wanted, except what was prohibited to him in this Verse, in the Surah Al-Nisa.

And from him, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, and others, regarding the names of the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), their lineages, and their descriptions. Ayesha, and Hafsa, and Umm Habeeb bint Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Zaynab bint Jahsh, and Sawda bint Zam'a, and Maymuna bint al-Harith, and Safiyya bint Hayy ibn Akhtab, and Umm Salama bint Abu Umayya, and Juwayriya bint al-Harith. And Ayesha was from Taym, and Hafsa was from Adi, and Umm Salama was from Banu Makhzum, and Sawda was from Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, and Zaynab bint Jahsh was from Banu Asad; and a number of them were from Banu Umayya, and Umm Habib bint Abu Sufyan was from Banu Umayya, and Maymuna bint al-Harith was from Banu Hilal, and Safiyya bint Hayy ibn Akhtab was from Banu Israel. And he (peace be upon him and his family) passed away with nine wives, and besides these were those who had gifted themselves to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and Khadeeja bint Khuwaylid, the mother of his child, and Zaynab bint Abi al-Jawn who was deceived, and al-Kindiya. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not marry (another wife) upon Khadeeja.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Umm Salama. Umar ibn Abi Salama married her to him, and he was young and had not yet attained puberty.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is your view of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is not permissible for you [to take more] women after this'? He said: 'Rather, the women who were not permissible for him were those whom Allah prohibited for him in this Verse: Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters in this Verse, all of it. And had the matter been as they are saying, it would have been permissible for you what was not permissible for him, because one of you changes [wives] whenever he wishes, but the matter is not as they are saying. The narrations of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) are different from the narrations of the people. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to marry from the women whatever he wished, except what was prohibited for him in Surah Al-Nisa, in this Verse.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-‘Asemiy narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya‘qub ibn Salim from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'What do you make of the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “Thereafter women are not lawful for you”' He said, 'Unlawful for him were only the women whom Allah had forbidden to him in this verse: “Unlawful for you to marry are your mothers, daughters…” in this verse entirely.' 'And if the matter were as they say, then he would have made lawful for you what he himself did not make lawful, because one of you would exchange [wives] whenever he wished.' 'But the matter is not as they say. The ahadith of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) are different from the ahadith of people.' 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made lawful for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny) to marry of the women whatever he wished, except what He had forbidden to him in the Surah of Women, in this verse.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Maryam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The young virgin girl who has a father cannot get married except with the permission of her father. And he said: If she is in control of her affairs, she can get married whenever she desires.

Aban, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The woman marries whomever she wishes, if she is in control of her affairs; so if she wishes, she appoints a guardian.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Umar ibn Aban Al-Kalbi, from Maysarat, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'If I meet a woman in the wilderness where there is no one, and I ask her,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the mature/divorced or widowed woman who proposes marriage to herself, he (peace be upon him) said: She has more authority over herself; she may entrust her affair to whomever she wishes, provided he is a match, after she has previously married a man.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The mature/divorced woman proposes herself.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is the one most entitled to herself; she may entrust her affair to whomever she wishes, provided there is no objection to it, after she has previously married a husband.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a slave girl who was shared between me and an inheritor with me, so we freed her, and she had an absent brother, and she was a virgin. Is it permissible for me to marry her, or is it not permissible except by the order of her brother? He said: Yes, it is permissible for you to marry her. I said: So I can marry her if I intend that? He said: Yes.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'None can revoke the marriage except the father.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala'a ibn Razin, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The virgins who have a father cannot be married off except by the permission of their fathers.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The young girl is not consulted for marriage if she is between her two parents, for she has no authority alongside the father. And he (peace be upon him) said: Everyone else may consult her, except the father.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who wants to marry off his sister, he said: He should consult her; if she remains silent, that is her consent; and if she refuses, he should not marry her off; and if she says, 'Marry me to so-and-so,' let him marry her to the one she is pleased with; and as for the orphan girl in the care of a man, he should not marry her off except with her consent.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the virgin girl whom her father maries off without her consent, he (peace be upon him) said: She has no authority with her father; if he marries her off, the marriage is valid, even if she dislikes it. He (peace be upon him) said: And he was asked about a man who wanted to marry off his sister. He said: He should consult her; if she remains silent, it is her consent, but if she refuses, he should not marry her off.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The young virgin girl who is under the guardianship of her parents is not asked for her permission when her father intends to marry her off; he is more considerate for her. And as for the mature woman (thayyib), she is asked for her permission even if she is under the guardianship of her parents when they intend to marry her off.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Al-Salt, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the young girl whose father marries her off: does she have authority (to choose) when she reaches adulthood? He (peace be upon him) said: No, she does not have authority with her father. He said, And I asked him about the virgin when she reaches the maturity of women: does she have authority with her father? He (peace be upon him) said: No, she does not have authority with her father as long as she has not grown up (reached full maturity).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said: One of my uncles' clan wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second: 'What do you say regarding a young girl whom her uncle married off, and when she grew up, she refused the marriage?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'She is not compelled to that, and the command is her command'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said regarding the virgin woman, her permission is her silence, and the divorced/widow, her command is in her (control).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a young girl whom her father marries off, then he dies while she is still young, and she grows older before her husband enters into her. Is the marriage contracted by her father valid upon her, or is the decision left to her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage contracted by her father is valid upon her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A girl, her father wants to marry her to a man, and her grandfather wants to marry her to another man.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The grandfather is more entitled to that, as long as there is no harm, if the father has not married her off before him; and the marriage of the father and the grandfather is permissible upon her.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: When a man marries off his daughter-in-law (his son's daughter), it is valid upon his son, and for the son also to marry her off. So I said, 'If her father desires a man and her grandfather desires a man?' He said: 'The grandfather is more entitled to her marriage.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the father and the grandfather give in marriage, the marriage is valid for the first one. So if they are both in one situation, the grandfather is more entitled.
Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man marries off (his daughter) but his father refuses that, then the marriage of the father is valid, even if the grandfather dislikes it. This is not like what the grandfather does, then the father wants to reject it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Waleed the seller of carpets, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, while I was in his presence, about a girl who had two brothers: the elder married her in Kufa, and the younger married her in another land. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first is more entitled to her, unless the other has already consummated the marriage with her. If he has consummated it with her, then she is his wife and his marriage is valid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said: A man asked him about a man who died and left two brothers and a daughter, and the daughter was young. So one of the two brothers, the executor, married the daughter to his own son. Then the father of the married son died. So when he died, the other brother said, 'My brother did not marry his son, so he married the girl to his son.' So it was said to the girl, 'Which of the two husbands is more beloved to you, the first or the last?' She said, 'The last.' Then the second brother died, and for the first brother was a son closer (older) than the son who had been given in marriage. So he said to the girl, 'Choose which of the two is more beloved to you, the first husband or the last husband?' So he said, 'The report in it is that she is for the last husband, and that is because she had reached adulthood when she was married off, and it is not for her to break what she had bonded to after her adulthood.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of women who rode the mounts are the women of Quraysh — most compassionate toward children and the best to a husband.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from more than one person, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abu Waki', from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-A'war, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: The best of your women are the women of Quraysh — the most kind toward their husbands, and the most merciful toward their children. The mujun toward her husband, the chaste toward others. We said: And what is the mujun? He said: The one who does not withhold.
