Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from one of them both (peace be upon them), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) proposed (for marriage) to Umm Hani', daughter of Abu Talib (peace be upon him), and she said: 'O Messenger of God! I am indeed afflicted — there are orphans in my care, and none would be appropriate for you except a woman who is free (of such responsibilities).' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'None have ridden the camel like the women of Quraysh — most compassionate toward a child, and most protective of a husband's wealth.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: One cannot copulate with the girl until there come to her nine years or ten years.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man marries the girl and she is young, he should not enter into her (consummate the marriage) until nine years come to her.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: One cannot have sexual intercourse with the girl until she reaches nine years or ten years.

From him, from Zakariyya Al-Mumin, or between him and him is a man, and I do not know him except that he narrated to me from Ammar Al-Sajistani, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to a slave of his: 'Go and say to the judge: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The limit of the woman is that she is entered into by her husband when she is a daughter of nine years.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife, then another man marries her afterwards, and she gives birth to the latter. Are her children from the latter permissible for the children of the first [man], from another woman? He said: Yes. He said, And I asked him about a man who freed his concubine, then another man married her after him, and she gave birth to the latter. Are her children permissible for the one who freed her? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal from al-Abbas ibn Aamir from Safwan ibn Yahya from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a slave girl, lies with her seeking offspring, but is not granted a child from her. So he gifts her to his brother or sells her, and she bears him children. Can his son from another woman marry the daughter of his brother from her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat it to me.' So I repeated it to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid Al-Sayrafi, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about this matter, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Repeat it to me.' I said to him: 'There was a slave girl for me, but she was not granted a child from me. So I sold her, and she gave birth to a child from someone else, and I have a child from another woman. So, can I marry my child from another woman to her child?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You can marry [your child] to what was for her from the child before you,' meaning before she came to be for you.

And from him, from Zayd ibn al-Juhaym al-Hilali who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries the woman, and his son marries her daughter. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the daughter was for her before he married her, so there is no problem'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries off his son while he is young. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' I said: 'Is the father's divorce valid?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'Upon whom is the dower?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon the father, if he guaranteed it for them, and if he did not guarantee it, then it is upon the boy, unless the boy has no wealth, in which case the father is responsible for it even if he did not guarantee it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the man marries off his son, that is up to him (the son), and when he marries off his daughter, it is valid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about a man who had children, so he married two of them and stipulated the dower (sadaq), then he died. From where is the dower calculated: from the total wealth or from their respective shares? He said: From the total wealth. It is in the status of a debt.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda al-Hazza, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a boy and a girl who were married by their guardians, and both of them were not yet mature. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage is valid, and whichever of the two matures, he/she will have the choice (to annul or confirm). And if they die before they mature, there is no inheritance between them, nor any dower, except if both had matured and were pleased (with the marriage).' I said, 'What if one of them matures before the other?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is allowed upon him if he is pleased.' I said, 'What if the man who matured before the girl, and was pleased with the marriage, then died before the girl matured? Would she inherit him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, her inheritance from him is set aside until she matures. Then she swears by Allah that what prompted her to take the inheritance is only her consent to the marriage. Then the inheritance is handed over to her, and half the dower.' I said, 'What if the girl died and she had not yet matured? Would the mature husband inherit her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because she has the choice when she matures.' I said, 'What if her father was the one who married her before she matured?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The father's marriage is valid upon her, and it is valid upon the boy, and the dower is upon the father for the girl.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Habib al-Khasha'i, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I wish to marry a woman, but my parents desire another for me.' He said, 'Marry the one you desire, and leave the one your parents desire.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Hadrami, from Al-Kahili, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man whose mother married him while he was absent. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage is valid. If the groom wishes, he may accept it; and if he wishes, he may reject it. So if the groom rejects the marriage arranged for him, the dowry remains obligatory upon his mother.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries the woman for a specified term: if he brings her dower by the specified term, she is his wife; but if he does not bring her dower by the term, there is no authority for him over her. And that is their stipulation between them when they married her, so he judged for the man that in his hand is the body (possession) of his wife, and he nullified their stipulation.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Sali, from Abu Al Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries a woman and stipulates to her that he will not take her out of her city, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He must fulfill that for her,' or he said: 'That is binding upon him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman and stipulated upon her that he would come to her whenever he wished, and provide for her a specified amount every month. He said: 'There is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hassan, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about the skilled woman, upon whom it is stipulated at the time of the marriage contract that he will come to her whenever he wishes, every month, and every Friday for a day, and from the expenses such and such. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That stipulation is not valid (of itself). And whoever marries a woman, she is entitled to what is due to women regarding maintenance and sharing of time. However, if a woman marries and fears ill-conduct from him, or fears that he will marry another woman in addition to her, or that he will divorce her, and she reconciles with him regarding her rights for something from her maintenance or her share of time, then that is permissible, there is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Alaa' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding a man who says to his slave, 'I free you on the condition that I marry you to my daughter; if you marry (another wife) or take a concubine, one hundred dinars are upon you.' So he frees him on that condition, and he either takes a concubine or marries (another wife). He (peace be upon him) said: 'The condition is upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, that Durays had under him (as a wife) the daughter of Humran, so he stipulated for her that he would not marry another wife upon her, and that he would not keep a concubine ever during her lifetime, nor after her death; upon a stipulation that she made for him that she would not marry after him; and they both stipulated upon themselves, from the sacrifice (hady), and the Hajj, and the sacrificial animal (badanah), and all their wealth to be for the poor, if one of them did not fulfill his obligation to the other. Then he went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned that to him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the daughter of Humran there are rights, and that will not burden us so that we do not tell you the truth. Go and marry, and keep a concubine, for that (stipulation of hers) is not with anything (valid), and nothing is upon you nor upon her, and that which the two of you did is not with anything.' So he came, kept a concubine, and children were born to him after that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman whom a man married, and the woman gave him the dower and stipulated upon him that copulation and divorce would be in her hand. He (peace be upon him) said: He opposed the Sunnah and assigned the right to one who is not its rightful owner, and the judgement is that upon the man is the dower, and that copulation and divorce are in his hand, and that is the Sunnah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Mansur ibn Buzurj, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), while I was standing: 'May Allah make me your ransom. A partner of mine had a wife under him, so he divorced her and she became irrevocably divorced from him. Then he wanted to return to her, and the woman said: 'No, by Allah, I will not marry you ever until you make Allah a condition upon you that you will not divorce me, nor will you marry (another wife) upon me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And he did so?' I said: 'Yes, he has done so, may Allah make me your ransom.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what he has done, and he does not know what may occur in his heart in the middle of the night or the day.' Then he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'As for now, so tell him to complete for the woman her stipulation, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Muslims are (bound) by their stipulations.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have doubts regarding a word.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not Imran who passes by you, is he not with you in Al-Madina?' So I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So tell him to write it, and let him send it to me.' So Imran came to us after that, so we wrote it for him, and there was neither any increase nor reduction in it. So he returned after that and met me in the flour market, so he rubbed his shoulder against my shoulder, so he said: 'He conveys the greetings to you, and he is saying to you: Tell the man to fulfill his stipulation.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali bin Raib, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked (and I was present) about a man who married a woman for one hundred dinars, with the stipulation that she would go with him to his land/country. If she does not go with him, then her dower is fifty dinars, if she refuses to go with him to his land. He said, so he (peace be upon him) said: If he intends to take her to the land of polytheism, then there is no stipulation valid for him upon her regarding that, and she is entitled to the one hundred dinars which he had dowered for her. And if he intends to take her to the land of the Muslims and the abode of Islam, then he has what he stipulated upon her; and the Muslims are upon their stipulations. And it is not for him to take her to his land until he pays her her dower, or she is pleased with him from that with whatever she is pleased with, and that is permissible for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a free woman, so he found her to be a slave who had concealed herself to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had married him from without her master, so the marriage is invalidated.' I said, 'So how would the dower be dealt with, which she had taken from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he can find anything from what he had given her, so let him take it, and if he does not find anything, so there is nothing for him upon her; and if it was such that her master had married her to him, he would have recourse to her master with what was taken from him, and for her master, upon him, would be a tenth of her price if she was a virgin, and if she was not a virgin, so it would be half of the tenth of her price due to what she has permitted from her private parts.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And she would observe the waiting period of the slave girl.' I said, 'Supposing she were to come with a child?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her children from him are free ones, when the marriage was without the permission of the master.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a slave girl of a group who went to a tribe other than her own tribe and informed them that she was a free woman. So a man from them married her, and she gave birth to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His children are slaves, except if the proof is established that a witness testified for her that she was a free woman, so her children would not be owned and they would be free.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A slave girl absconded from her masters, so she went to a tribe other than her own tribe, and she claimed that she was a free woman. So a man married her. Then her master captured her afterwards, and she had given birth to children. He (peace be upon him) said: If the husband establishes the proof that he married her on the basis that she was a free woman, her children will be freed, and the people will take their slave girl. If he does not establish the proof, his back will be struck (for judicial beating), and his children will be enslaved.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abdul Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who proposed to a man for a daughter of his from a free woman. So when it was the night she was to enter upon her husband, he made another daughter of his from a slave girl go over to him instead. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She would be returned to her father, and his wife would be returned to him, and her dower would be upon her father.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who proposed to a man for his daughter from the free ones, so he came to him with another one. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is returned to him, the one who was named for him, with another dower from her father, and the first dower is for the one with whom he had intercourse.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who married into a family, and his wife turned out to be blind, and they had not indicated this to him. He said: The marriage is repudiated due to vitiligo, leprosy, insanity, and impotence.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from one of his companions, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries a woman who has insanity, vitiligo, and similar conditions. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is responsible for the dower.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The woman with vitiligo (barsha') and the insane woman and the leper woman can be returned [from the marriage]. I said, 'The blind woman?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is the restricted (physically) man and the restricted woman repudiated from the marriage?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. Rifa'ah said: 'And I asked him about the vitiligo woman. So he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a woman whose guardian married her off and she was vitiligo, that she has the dower for what she permitted of her private part, and that the dower is upon the one who married her off; and the dower came to be upon him because he deceived her. And if a man married a woman and a man who married her off did not know the interior of her matter, there would not be anything upon him, and the dower would be taken from her'.

Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man to whom a woman had authorized her affairs, or a near relative of hers, or a neighbor of hers, who did not know of the hidden matter of her affairs, so he was found to have concealed a defect that was in her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The dower is taken from her, and there is nothing upon the one who married her off.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Jameel ibn Salih from one of the companions of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding two sisters who were gifted to two brothers in one night, so the wife of this one was entered to that one, and the wife of that one was entered to this one. He (peace be upon him) said: For each of the two is the dower with the copulation, and if their guardian deliberately did that, the dower would be fined, and each of the two would not go near his wife until the waiting period has expired. So when the waiting period has expired, each one of them would return to her husband with the first marriage. It was said to him: If they die before the expiration of the waiting period? He said: The two husbands would return half the dower to their heirs, and the two men would inherit them. It was said: If the two men died while they were in the waiting period? He said: They would inherit them both, and for both of them is half the specified dower, and upon them is the waiting period after they finish from the first waiting period. They would observe the waiting period of the one whose husband died.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: He said regarding a man who marries a woman and finds 'qarn' in her, which is al-'afal (inability to copulate due to uterine horns), or vitiligo, or leprosy, that he can return her as long as he has not entered (consummated) with her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabr who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who looked at a woman, so she fascinated him. So he asked about her, and it was said that she is the daughter of so-and-so. So he went to her father and said, 'Marry me your daughter.' But he married someone else to him, and she gave birth from him. So he came to know that it was not his daughter, and that she is a slave. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The mother is returned to her master, and the child is for the man, and upon the one who married her to him is the value of the child's price to be given to the masters of the mother, as he deceived the man and cheated him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad altogether, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding a man who married a woman from her guardian, and he found a fault with her after he had copulated with her, he said: When the 'Afla' (one unable to copulate due to uterine horns), the 'Barsa' (one with vitiligo), the 'Majnouna' (insane), the 'Mufda' (deflowered), and the one with an apparent disability are cheated (concealed), then she is returned to her family without a divorce, and the husband takes the dower from her guardian who had cheated him. So if her guardian did not know of anything from that, then there is nothing upon him, and she is returned to her family. He said: And if the husband gets anything from what was taken from him, so it is for him, and if he does not get anything, so there is nothing for him. He said: And she observes the waiting period of the divorced woman from him, if he had copulated with her, and if he had not copulated with her, so there is no waiting period for her, and there would be no dower for her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the woman who gives birth from adultery, and no one knows of that except her guardian: Is it permissible for him to marry her off and remain silent about it, provided he has seen repentance or a good deed from her? He (peace be upon him) said: If he does not mention that to her husband, and then the husband learns of it afterwards, and wishes to take her dower from her guardian for what he concealed from him, then he has that right against her guardian. And the dower which she took for herself, the husband has no claim upon her regarding it, due to what she permitted of her private part. And if her husband wishes to keep her, there is no problem.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The woman is returned (from the dowry/marriage contract) for four conditions: vitiligo, leprosy, insanity, and uterine horns (Al-Qaran), which is inability to copulate (Al-Afal), as long as it has not fallen upon her (i.e., the husband has not consummated the marriage with her). So when it has fallen upon her, then no (she is not returned).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and found a 'horn' in her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This one will not get pregnant. She is returned to her family; if her husband abstains from copulating with her, she is returned to her family.' I said: 'And if he had consummated the marriage with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he knew of it before copulating with her, then he copulated with her, he has accepted her. And if he did not know except after copulating with her, then if he wishes afterwards, he keeps her, and if he wishes, he releases her to her family. And for her is what she took from him, by virtue of what she permitted of her private part.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Al-Sabbah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and found uterine horns in her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She will not get pregnant, and her husband will not be able to copulate with her. He can return her to her family belittled, and there is no dower for her.' I said, 'What if he had copulated with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he knew of that before he married her, meaning the copulation, then he copulated with her, so he was pleased with it. And if he did not know except after having copulated with her, then if he so desires afterwards, he keeps her, and if he so desires, he divorces her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Bureyd al-Ijli, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, so her sister escorted her to him, and she was older than her. So she entered the house of her husband at night, and she went to the clothes of his wife, removed them from her, and wore them. Then she sat in the room of her sister, and she pushed aside his wife, and extinguished the lamp, and the girl was shy to speak. So the husband entered the room and had intercourse with her, while he thought that she was his wife whom he had married. So when it was morning, the man's wife stood up to him and said to him, 'I am your so-and-so wife whom you married, and my sister plotted against me, so she took my clothes and wore them, and sat in the room, and pushed me aside.' So the man investigated that matter and found it as she had mentioned. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that there is no dower for the one who deceived herself, and I view the legal punishment upon her for what she did, the punishment of the unmarried adulteress. And the husband should not approach his wife whom he married until the waiting period of the one who deceived herself expires. So when her waiting period expires, he joins his wife to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a free woman, a slave cheated her, so he married her, and she did not know except that he was a free man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Separation is effected between the two of them if the woman so desires it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a free woman who married a slave under the stipulation that he was free, and she later learned that he was a slave. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She has the choice. If she wishes, she can remain with him, and if she wishes, she can leave. If he had consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dower; and if he had not consummated it with her, she is entitled to nothing. If he consummated the marriage with her after she knew he was a slave and she agreed to remain, then he has the choice over her.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Ibn Bukayr, from his father, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding a eunuch who deceived a Muslim woman, so she married him. He said: Separation would be effected between the two of them if the woman so desires it, and his head would be pained, and if she is pleased with it and stays with him, it would not be for her, after her agreement with it, that she refuses him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Aban, from Abbad al-Dbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the 'injin' (impotent man), when it is known that he is 'injin' and does not have intercourse with women, separation is effected between the two; and when he has intercourse with her with one thrust, they are not separated; and the man is not rejected due to a defect.

From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband was tried (with impotence), so he was not able to perform sexual intercourse; can she separate from him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if she so desires.' Ibn Muskan said, 'And in another Hadith: She waits for a year. If he comes to her, [the marriage continues], otherwise she separates from him. But if she loves to stay with him, let her stay.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, from Sama'at, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That a eunuch deceived a woman regarding his potency. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are separated, and the woman takes her dower from him, and his back is struck (with the cane) just as he deceived himself.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: When a man marries a thayyib (previously married) woman who had been married to another husband, and she alleges that he did not come near her since he entered into marriage with her, then the word regarding that is the word of the man, and upon him is to swear by Allah that he has copulated with her, because she is the plaintiff. He (peace be upon him) said: So if he married her and she was a virgin, and she claims that he did not reach her, then in a situation like this, women know (how to determine), so let her be examined by the one who is reliable from among them. So when she mentions that she is a virgin, then it is upon the Imam to delay him for a year. So if he reached her, or else there would be a separation between the two, and she would be given half the dower, and there would be no waiting period upon her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from one of his elders, who said: A woman said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and a man had asked about a man whose wife had claimed upon him that he is impotent, and the man denied it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The midwife would apply Al-Kahlouq (a perfume) on her and not let the man know, and the man would go over to her. So if he comes out, and Al-Khalouq is upon his manhood, he would be ratified, and she would be belied, or else she would be ratified, and he would be belied'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who was prevented from his wife, so he was not able to have intercourse with her, so he (peace be upon him) said: If he is not able to have intercourse with other women besides her, then he should not keep her except with her agreement to that; and if he is able to have intercourse with other women, then there is no problem with keeping her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever has intercourse with his wife once, and then is seized (from it), there is no choice for her.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Hamdan al-Qalanisi from Ishaq ibn Bunan from Ibn Baqqah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A woman claimed against her husband, in the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), that he does not copulate with her, and he claimed that he does copulate with her. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered her to apply saffron to herself, then he should wash his penis. If the water came out yellow, he was believed; otherwise, he was ordered to divorce her.

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A Muslim person has not gained a benefit after Islam superior to a Muslim wife who delights him when he looks at her, obeys him when he instructs her, and preserves him when he is absent from her — regarding her own person and his wealth.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ijali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'When I intend to gather for a Muslim the good of this world and the Hereafter, I grant him a submissive heart, a tongue engaged in remembrance, a body patient in affliction, and a believing wife who delights him when he looks at her and who protects him when he is absent from her, in regard to herself and his wealth.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said: No servant ever gained a benefit better than a righteous wife. Whenever he looks at her, she delights him, and whenever he is absent from her, she preserves him — in respect to her own person and his wealth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the good fortune of a person is a righteous wife.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the things that are conducive to good for the Muslim man is that he has a wife who, when he looks at her, she delights him; when he is absent from her, she preserves his interests; and when he gives her an instruction, she obeys him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Shu'ayb ibn Janah, from Matar, the freed slave of Ma'n, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There are three things wherein lies rest for the believer: a spacious house that conceals his private affairs and the wretchedness of his condition from the people; a righteous wife who supports him in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter; and a daughter whom he sends away either by death or by marriage.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Fuzayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries the woman upon a stipulation that she is a virgin, so he finds her as having been married before. Is it allowed for him that he resides with her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The virginity can be torn from the riding and from the jumping.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Jazzaki, who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who married a virgin girl, so he found her to be non-virgin (previously married). Is the full dower obligatory for her, or is it reduced? He said: It is reduced.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abdul Hameed ibn Awwaz, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I marry the woman; is it correct for me to have sexual relations with her, and I have not yet paid her anything from her dower?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes. It is merely a debt upon you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A man marries a woman upon the known dower and enters with her before he gives it to her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should forward to her whatever little or much, unless there is for him a fulfillment from an asset; if an event occurs with him, it is paid from it, so there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abdul Hameed Al-Taiy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Can I marry the woman and consummate the marriage with her without giving her anything?' He said, 'Yes, it becomes a debt upon you for her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Hameed ibn Awwaz al-Taiy, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries the woman, but he does not have with him what he can give her, so he enters into her (consummates the marriage). He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; it is merely a debt for her upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding the words of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him): 'I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be of your own free will,' whichever of the two terms he fulfilled? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fulfillment from these two was the furthest of the two, ten years.' I said: 'So did he go to her before the condition expired, or after its expiration?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Before it expired.' I said to him: 'So if a man marries a woman and stipulates to her father the wage of two months, is that permissible?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Moses (peace be upon him) knew that he would complete the condition for him, but how can it be for this one that he would know that he would remain (alive) until he fulfills it for him? And indeed, during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a man used to marry a woman on the basis of a Surah from the Quran, or on the basis of a Dirham, or on the basis of a handful of wheat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Marriage is not permissible today in Islam through wage (ijarah); if he says, 'I will work for you for such and such years on the condition that you marry me your daughter or your sister,' it is prohibited because it is the price of her neck, and she is more rightful to her dower.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), that he was asked: About the man who is immoral with the woman, can he marry her daughter?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. But if he had a wife, then he was immoral with her mother, or her daughter, or her sister, his wife would not be prohibited to him. Indeed, the prohibited does not spoil the permissible.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with a woman and kissed her, other than that he did not copulate with her, then he married her daughter. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he did not copulate with the mother, there is no problem, but if he did copulate with her, he cannot marry her daughter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a girl, so he consummated the marriage with her. Then he was tested with her mother and committed fornication with her. Would his wife be prohibited to him? He said: No. Indeed, the permissible is not prohibited by the prohibition.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who committed adultery with the mother of his wife, or with her daughter, or with her sister, he said: 'That does not make his wife prohibited to him.' Then he said: 'A prohibition (by a forbidden act) never prohibits a permissible (thing) at all.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man between whom and a woman there was immorality, can he marry her daughter? He said: If it was from a kiss or something similar, let him marry her daughter; and if it was copulation, let him not marry her daughter, and let him marry her (the mother) if he wishes.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali bin Raib, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who committed adultery with the mother of his wife, or with her sister. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That would not make his wife prohibited unto him. The prohibited does not spoil the permissible, nor does it prohibit it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man between whom and a woman there was immorality (fujur). He said: If it was a kiss or something similar, let him marry her daughter if he wishes; and if it was sexual intercourse, let him not marry her daughter, and let him marry her (the mother).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about a man who was immoral with a woman; can he marry her mother from breastfeeding, or her daughter? He said: No. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Yazeed al-Kunasi, who said: A man from our companions married a woman. He said to me, 'I would like you to ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and say to him: A man from our companions married a woman, and he claims that he used to play with her mother and kiss her, without having had sexual intercourse with her.' So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'He has lied. Tell him to separate from her.' He said, 'So I returned from my journey and informed the man of what Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) had said. By Allah, he did not refute that from himself, and he divorced her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was seated, about a man who had attained from his maternal aunt during his youth, then he restrained. Can he marry her daughter? He said: No. I said: He did not happen to have copulated with her; rather, it was something less than a thing. He said: His words are not accepted, and it is not honourable.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man had intercourse with a boy, is his sister permissible for him?' He said, 'If there was penetration, then no.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who tampered with the boy, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has penetrated, his daughter and his sister become prohibited unto him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father or from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from one of his men, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man came to him and said to him, 'May I be your ransom. What do you think of two young men who were lying together, so a son was born to this one and a girl to this one and a girl to the other. Can the son of this one marry the daughter of this one?' He said, 'Yes, Glory be to Allah, why should it not be permissible?' He said, 'He was a friend of his.' He said, 'And even if he was, there is no problem.' He said, 'But, he was doing it with him.' He said, 'So he turned his face away from him, then answered him while he was veiling with his arms, and said, 'If that which was from him was less than penetration, then there is no problem if they marry, but if he had penetrated, then it is not permissible for them to marry.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who goes to the brother of his wife, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he penetrates him, then the wife is prohibited to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and touched her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her dower is obligatory, and she is prohibited to his father and his son.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the man who has a slave girl and kisses her; would she be permissible for his son? He (peace be upon him) said: 'With lust?' I said: 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has not left anything [unforbidden] when he kissed her with lust.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, initiating the explanation: 'If he exposed her and looked at her with lust, she is prohibited to his father and his son.' I said: 'When he looks at her body?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he looks at her private part and her body with lust, she is prohibited to him [the father and son].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man looks at the slave girl intending to buy her, is she permissible for his son?' He said: 'Yes, unless he looked at her nakedness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, while I was in his presence, about a man who bought a slave girl and did not touch her. So his wife instructed his son, who was a boy of ten years, to have intercourse with her, and he had intercourse with her. So what is your view regarding it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The boy has sinned, and his mother has sinned, and I do not view for the father, when the son has been near to her, that he should have intercourse with her.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man who had a slave girl, so his father laid his hand upon her out of desire, or looked at her prohibited part out of desire. So he (peace be upon him) disliked that the son should touch her.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rabi'i ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the man bares the slave girl and places his hand upon her, she is not permitted for his son.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to him (peace be upon him), 'A man married a woman, so he touched her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is prohibited to his father and his son, and her dower is obligatory.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When a man commits adultery with his father's wife or his father's slave girl, that does not prohibit her from her husband, nor does it prohibit the slave girl from her master. That prohibition from him occurs only when he has intercourse with the slave girl while she is lawful (to him), so that slave girl becomes permanently unlawful to his son and to his father. And when a man marries a woman with a lawful marriage, that woman becomes unlawful to his father and to his son.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Murazim who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he was asked about a woman who instructed her son to have intercourse with a slave girl of his father, and he did. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'She sins and her son sins, and one of these people asked me about this matter, so I said to him: 'Keep her, for the permissible does not spoil due to the prohibited'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has a slave girl, and the son of his son falls upon her before the grandfather has had intercourse with her; or the man commits adultery with the woman, so would it be permissible for his father to marry her? He (peace be upon him) said: No. Rather, that is when the man marries her, so he has intercourse with her, then his son commits adultery with her, it would not harm him, because the prohibited does not spoil the permissible, and similarly is the case with the slave girl.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), that he said: If the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had not been prohibited to the people due to the Words of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, "And it does not behove you that you should hurt the Messenger of Allah, nor that you should marry his wives after him ever. They are prohibited." for al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) due to the Words of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, "And marry not the women whom your fathers married." And it does not befit a man to marry the wife of his grandfather.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Jaroud who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, and he mentioned this Verse: And We enjoined upon the human being [to be] good to his parents Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is one of the two parents. So Abdullah ibn Ajlan said, 'Who is the other one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him), and his wives are prohibited unto us, and this is for us in particular.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Similar to it, and he said in his Hadith: 'And they do not permit that they marry their own mothers, if they were believers, and the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in terms of sanctity are like their own mothers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The mother and the daughter are equal, when he does not enter with her, meaning when he marries the woman then divorces her before entering with her, then if he wishes he may marry her mother, and if he wishes he may marry her daughter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the man who marries the woman with a temporary marriage, would it be Permissible for him that he marries her daughter? He (peace be upon him) said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who married a woman, so he looked at her head and at a part of her body. Can he marry her daughter? He said: No. When he has seen from her what is prohibited to others, so it is not for him to marry her daughter.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a man came to him and asked him about a man who married a woman, and she died before he had consummated the marriage with her: 'Can he marry her mother?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from us has done it, and we did not see any problem with that.' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Shia do not pride themselves except with the judgment of Ali (peace be upon him) regarding this 'Shamkhiyya' case, about which Ibn Mas'ud had issued a fatwa that there is no problem with that. Then he went to Ali (peace be upon him) and asked him, so Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'From where did you take it?' And your step-daughters who are in your guardianship, (born) of your wives to whom you have gone in, but if you have not gone in to them, there is no blame on you He said, 'From the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And your step-daughters who are in your guardianship, (born) of your wives to whom you have gone in, but if you have not gone in to them, there is no blame on you.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'This is an exclusion, and this is for copulation, and mothers of your wives.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to the man: 'Did you hear what this one is reporting from Ali (peace be upon him)?' So when I stood up, I was remorseful, and I said (to myself): 'What have I done? He (peace be upon him) was saying, 'A man from us has done it, and we did not see any problem with that', and I was saying, 'Ali (peace be upon him) has judged with regards to it.' So I met him (peace be upon him) after that, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The question of the man, that which I had said was a slip from me, so what are you saying with regards to it?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sheikh! You inform me that Ali (peace be upon him) has judged with it, and you are asking me what I am saying with regards to it?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jareer, from Abu Al-Rabie, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who married a woman, so he stayed with her for days, not being able to consummate the marriage, except that he had seen from her what is prohibited to others. Then he divorced her. Is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He (peace be upon him) said: Is it permissible for him, given that he had seen from her mother what he had seen?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Beware of the marriages of the women who are divorced upon other than the Sunnah. I said to him, 'Supposing a man from them divorces his wife and there is a need for me with her?' He said, 'So meet up with him after he has divorced her, and she has observed her waiting period with her companions, so you should be saying to him, 'You have divorced so and so?' So if he says, 'Yes', so it has become one divorce upon a pure period. So leave her from when he divorced her with that divorce until she has observed her waiting period. Then marry her, so that divorce would have made her to be irrevocably divorced'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man from your mawalis conveys greetings to you and has intended to marry a woman who is compatible with him and some of her affairs have pleased him, and she had a husband who divorced her three times not according to the Sunnah, and he was reluctant to proceed with marrying her until he seeks your advice, so that you would command him.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the private part (of the body), and the matter of the private part is severe, and from it comes the child, and we are cautious, so let him not marry her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorced his wife three times, so a man intended to marry her, how should he deal? He (peace be upon him) said: Leave her until she menstruates and is pure, then he should go to him (her husband) and with him should be two men as witnesses, so he should be saying, 'Did you divorce so and so?' So when he says, 'Yes', he should leave her for three months, then propose to herself.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ali ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Beware of the woman who is divorced with three (divorces) in one sitting, for they are with husbands.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A daughter of the brother and a daughter of the sister are not married (as an additional wife) upon the paternal aunt or the maternal aunt, except with their permission; and the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt are married upon a daughter of the brother and a daughter of the sister without their permission.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda Al-Hadda', who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'A woman is not married (as an additional wife) upon her paternal aunt, nor upon her maternal aunt, except with the permission of the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife with three divorces, then another man had temporary marriage with her. Is she permissible for the first one? He said: No.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife with a divorce that makes her not permissible to him until she marries another husband, and a man marries her with a temporary marriage, would she be permissible for him if he marries her? He (peace be upon him) said: No, until she enters into what she has come out from.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Muthanna from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with a divorce that makes her not permissible to him until she marries another husband, so a slave married her, then divorced her, is the divorce demolished (nullified)? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. Due to the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: 'until she marries another husband'. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is one of the husbands'.

Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musanna, from Abu Hatim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who divorces his wife with the divorce by which she becomes permissible to him only after marrying another husband. Then another man married her but did not consummate the marriage with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, [she is not permissible to the first husband] until he tastes her honey.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with one divorce, then left her until her waiting period ended. Then another man married her. Then that man died or divorced her, so the first husband remarried her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is with him upon two remaining divorces.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Some of our companions reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who divorces his wife upon the Book and the Sunnah, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him with one (divorce). So she marries another husband, and he dies from her, or divorces her, she can return to her former husband, for her to be with him upon two divorces and one (of it) having expired. So he (peace be upon him) signed with his own handwriting: 'They speak the truth'. And some of them had reported that she would happen to be with him upon three future divorces, and that which he had divorced her with would not be with anything, because she had married another husband. So he (peace be upon him) signed with his own handwriting: 'No'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Muthanna, from Zurara ibn A'yan and Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Udaym the seller of Al-Harawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The Mu'allaqah (woman subjected to li'an), if her husband curses her, she does not become permissible for him ever; and the one who marries the woman during her waiting period while he knows, she does not become permissible for him ever; and the one who divores with the divorce of 'Iddah which is not permissible for him until she marries another husband, having divorced her three times and married her three times, she does not become permissible for him ever; and the Muhrim (one in consecration for Hajj or Umrah), when he marries while he knows that it is prohibited upon him, she does not become permissible for him ever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man marries the woman during her waiting period and enters into her (consummates the marriage), she becomes permanently prohibited for him, whether he was knowing or ignorant; and if he does not enter into her, she becomes permissible for the ignorant one but does not become permissible for the knowing one.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who marries a woman during her waiting period out of ignorance, is she among those who are permanently prohibited to him? He said: No. As for if he was ignorant, let him marry her after her waiting period has ended, and people are excused in ignorance by what is greater than that. So I said: By which of the two ignorances is he excused? Is it by his ignorance knowing that it is prohibited for him, or by his ignorance that she is in her waiting period? He said: One of the two ignorances is easier than the other: the ignorance that Allah has prohibited that upon him, and that is because he is not able to be cautious with her. So I said: So he is excused in the other? He said: Yes, when her waiting period has ended, he is excused in marrying her. So I said: If one of the two was deliberate and the other was ignorant? He said: The one who was deliberate, it is not permissible for him to return to his companion (the woman) ever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the pregnant woman whose husband dies, so she gives birth and marries before four months and ten days have expired for her. He said: If he had consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever, and she observes the waiting period for what remains of it from the first (husband), and she begins another waiting period from the second (husband) of three menstrual periods; and if he had not consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she observes the waiting period for what remains of it from the first (husband), and he is a suitor among suitors.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): 'If a pregnant woman, her husband having died, gives birth and then marries before completing the waiting period of four months and ten days,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who married her has consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever; she completes the remainder of the waiting period of the first husband, and begins a new waiting period of three pure periods from the second husband. And if he has not consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she completes the remainder of her waiting period, and he is considered a suitor among suitors.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah and Ibn Muskann, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman during her waiting period. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are separated, and if he had consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dower corresponding to what she permitted of her private part, and they are separated so she is not permissible for him ever; and if he had not consummated the marriage with her, then she has nothing from her dower.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Abdillah and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: When a man divorces a woman, and she marries another, then her husband divorces her, and she marries the first (husband), then he divorces her, and she marries a man, then he divorces her, and she marries the first (husband), then the first husband divorces her like this, three times, she becomes permanently prohibited for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who married a woman while she was in her waiting period, he said: They are separated, then she completes her waiting period. If he had consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dower for what he permitted of her private part, and they are separated; and if he had not consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to nothing. He said: And I asked him about the one who divorces, then reverts, then divorces, then reverts, then divorces. He said: She is not permissible for him until she marries another husband. So another man marries her, then divorces her upon the Sunnah, then she returns to her first husband, so he divorces her three times upon the Sunnah. So she marries another husband, so he divorces her, then she returns to her first husband, so he divorces her three times upon the Sunnah, then she marries. So that is the one who is not permissible for him, ever, and the accursed one is not permissible for him, ever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'It has reached us from your father that if a man marries the woman during her waiting period, she does not become permissible for him ever.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is when he is knowledgeable. But if he is ignorant, he divorces her, and she observes her waiting period, then he marries her with a new marriage.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, that when a man marries a woman and knows that she has a husband, separation is effected between them, and she is not permissible for him, ever.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man proposes to a woman and consummates the marriage with her before she reaches nine years of age, separation is effected between them, and she is not permissible for him ever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man divorces a woman, and she marries another man, then he divorces her, and the first (husband) marries her, then he divorces her, and she marries another man, then he divorces her, and the first (husband) marries her, then he divorces her, she is not permissible for him ever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara ibn A'yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man gathers four (wives), so he divorces one of them, so he cannot marry the fifth until the expiration of the waiting period of the wife he has divorced. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The man cannot gather his water (seed) in five (wives)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who has four wives and divorces one of them: Can he marry another in her place? He (peace be upon him) said: No, until her waiting period expires.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who had four wives under him, so he divorced one, then married another before the divorced woman had completed her waiting period. He said: So let him keep her with her family until the divorced woman completes her term, and the other one would face another waiting period. And for her is her dower, if he had consummated the marriage with her. So, if he did not happen to have consummated the marriage with her, then for him is her wealth (dower), and there is no waiting period upon her. Then, if her family so desires, after the expiration of her waiting period, to get her married (to him), and if they so desire, they do not get her married (to him).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had three wives, so he married two additional women to them in one marriage contract. He slept with one of them, then died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he slept with the wife whom he initiated with her name and mentioned her at the time of the marriage contract, then her marriage is valid, and she has inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period. And if he slept with the wife who was named and mentioned after the mention of the first wife, then her marriage is invalid, and there is no inheritance for her, and upon her is the waiting period.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who marries five (women) in one marriage tie, he (peace be upon him) said: He frees the way (divorces) whichever one he desires, and keeps the four.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding two sisters: a man married one of them, then divorced her while she was pregnant, then he proposed to her sister, so he married them both before the divorced sister gave birth to her child. So he ordered that he separate from the second one until the divorced sister gives birth to her child, then he should propose to her and give her a dowry, [giving] two dowries.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man married a woman, then he went to a land and married her sister, while he did not know. He (peace be upon him) said: He keeps whichever of the two he wishes, and he releases the other one.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said: Regarding a man who married two sisters in one marriage contract, he said: He has the choice; he may keep whichever of the two he desires and release the other. And he said regarding a man who had a slave girl, so he slept with her, then bought her mother or her daughter: She is not permissible for him [ever].

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukayr and Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman in Iraq, then went to Syria and married another woman, who turned out to be the sister of the woman in Iraq. He (peace be upon him) said: He is separated from the one he married in Syria, and he does not approach her until the waiting period of the Syrian woman expires. I said: What if he married a woman, then married her mother, while he did not know that she was her mother? He (peace be upon him) said: Allah has excused his ignorance in that. Then he (peace be upon him) said: When he knows that she is her mother, he should not approach her, nor approach the daughter, until the mother's waiting period expires from him. So when the mother's waiting period expires, the marriage with the daughter becomes permissible for him. I said: What if the mother gives birth to a child? He (peace be upon him) said: It is his child, and it will be his son, and the brother of his wife.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said: I read in a letter of a man to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man marries a woman in temporary marriage (mut'ah) to a specified term, and the term expires between them. Is it permissible for him to marry her sister before her waiting period (iddah) expires?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is not permissible for him to marry her until her waiting period has expired.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man whose wife had divorced him by mutual agreement (khula'); is it permissible for him to propose to her sister before her waiting period expires? He said: When her bond of marriage is freed and there is no reversion (raj'a) for him, then it is permissible for him to propose to her sister. He said: And he was asked about a man who had two slave-sister concubines, so he slept with one of them, then he slept with the other. He said: When he slept with the second, the first becomes prohibited to him until the second dies. I said: What is your view if he sells her? He said: If he sells her due to a need and no thought of the second comes to his mind, then I see no problem with that; and if he sells her in order to return to the first, then no.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorces his wife, or by mutual agreement (khula'), or she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, is it for him to marry her sister? He said: When her bond of marriage is freed and there is no reversion (raj'ah) for him upon her, then for him is that he proposes to her sister. He said: And he was asked about a man who had two slave-sisters, so he slept with one of them, then slept with the other. He said: When he sleeps with the other, the first becomes prohibited to him until the other dies. I said: What is your view if he sells her, would the first be permissible for him? He said: If he sells her due to a need and no thought of the other crosses his heart, then I do not see a problem with that; and if he sells her only to return to the first, then no, and no prestige.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Moalla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorced his wife while she was pregnant, can he marry her sister before she gives birth? He (peace be upon him) said: He cannot marry her until her waiting period is completed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces a woman, can he marry her sister? He said: No, until her waiting period (iddah) has expired. He said, And I asked him about a man who owned two sisters, can he sleep with both of them together? He said: He can sleep with one of them, and when he sleeps with the second one, the first one which he slept with becomes prohibited to him until the second one dies or he separates from her; and it is not for him to sell the second one due to the first in order to return to her, except if he sells for a need, or gives her in charity, or she dies. He said, And I asked him about a man who had a wife, so she died, can he marry her sister? So he said: From that very moment, if he desires.
