Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a slave girl, so he freed her, and she married, and gave birth. Is it permissible for her former master to marry her daughter? He (peace be upon him) said: She is prohibited to him, and she is his daughter, and the free woman and the slave girl are equal in this. And your step-daughters who are in your guardianship, (born) of your wives. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), similar to it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashr, who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who has a slave girl, and she has a daughter, and he has sexual relations with her. Is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with her daughter? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Would the righteous man marry his own daughter?'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has a slave girl whom he has sexual relations with, is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said: No. It is like the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And your step-daughters who are in your guardianship'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man divorces his wife, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, and she has a daughter who is a slave. He buys her. Is it permissible for him to sleep with her? He said: No. And regarding the man who has the slave girl and her daughter with him, so he sleeps with one of the two, and she dies, and the other remains. Is it correct for him to sleep with her? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man buys two sisters, so he sleeps with one of them, then he sleeps with the other out of ignorance.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he sleeps with the other one out of ignorance, the first one does not become prohibited to him, but if he sleeps with the other one while knowing that she is prohibited to him, both together become prohibited to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but do not give them a promise in secret unless you speak in a goodly manner'. He said: It is the man who says to the woman before her waiting period expires, 'I promise you a house from the family of so-and-so,' in order to introduce her with the proposal. And the meaning of His Words 'unless you speak in a goodly manner' is the introduction with the proposal, and 'do not confirm the marriage tie until the writing is fulfilled'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but do not give them a promise in secret unless you speak in a goodly manner and do not confirm the marriage tie until the writing is fulfilled'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The secret is that the man says, 'I promise you the house of so-and-so family', then he seeks from her that she does not precede him (in marriage) when her waiting period expires.' I said, 'So (what about) His Words: 'unless you speak in a goodly manner'?' (He said): 'It is seeking the Permissible without confirming the tie of marriage until the writing reaches its term'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but do not give them a promise in secret'. He said: 'The man says, unless you speak to them in a goodly manner and the goodly word is the hint of proposal in its proper aspect and its lawfulness, and do not confirm the marriage tie until the book fulfills its term.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'unless you speak in a goodly manner.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He meets her, so he says, 'I have a desire in you, and I am honourable to the women, so do not precede me (before someone else) with yourself,' and the secret is that he should not be alone with her when he promises her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who emigrated and left his wife with the polytheists, then she joined him afterwards. [I asked]: Does he keep her with the first marriage, or does her bond of marriage cease? He said: He keeps her, and she is his wife.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a woman becomes a Muslim and her husband remains upon other than Islam, separation is effected between them. He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who emigrated and left his wife among the Polytheists, then she joined him afterwards. Can he retain her under the first marriage, or does her bond of marriage cease? He (peace be upon him) said: No, he retains her and she is his wife.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Magi man, or a polytheist from other than the People of the Book, under whom is a wife, so he becomes a Muslim, or she becomes a Muslim. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should await with that the expiration of her waiting period, and if he has become a Muslim, or she has become a Muslim before the expiration of her waiting period, so they are both upon their first marriage; and if he does not become a Muslim until after the expiration of the waiting period, so she is irrevocably divorced from him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a Christian man who married a Christian woman, and she became a Muslim before he had intercourse with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The bond of marriage has been severed from him, and there is no dower for her, nor is there a waiting period upon her from him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked him about two men from the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma) or from the People of War, each of whom married a woman and dowered her with wine and pigs. Then they both became Muslim. So he said: 'The marriage is valid, permissible; it is not rendered unlawful due to the wine nor due to the pigs.' I said, 'What if they became Muslim before they handed over to her the wine and the pigs?' So he said: 'When they became Muslim, it is upon him to hand over something to her from that [dower], but he should give her her dowry (sadaqah).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a Magian woman who embraced Islam before her husband had sexual intercourse with her. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to her husband: 'Embrace Islam.' But her husband refused to embrace Islam. So he judged for her that upon him is half the dower, and said: 'Islam has not increased her except in honor.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a Magian man who became a Muslim, and for him were seven wives, and they all became Muslims along with him. How should he deal with (them)? He said: He keeps four, and divorces three.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said: The dhimmi man has a dhimmi wife, so his wife becomes a Muslim. He said: 'She is his wife; he is with her by the day and is not with her by the night.' He said: 'So if the man becomes a Muslim and the wife does not become a Muslim, the man is with her by the night and the day.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Roumi ibn Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A Christian man marries a Christian woman upon thirty kegs of wine and thirty pigs. Then they both become Muslim after that, and he did not enter with her. He (peace be upon him) said: He considers the value of the wine and the value of the pigs, so he sends it to her. Then he enters with her, and they are upon their first marriage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'That which is prohibited due to blood relationship is also prohibited due to breast-feeding.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about breast-feeding. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which is prohibited due to lineage is also prohibited due to breast-feeding.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: That which is prohibited due to lineage is also prohibited due to breast-feeding.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) the daughter of Hamza, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that she is the daughter of my brother from breast-feeding?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabiy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the daughter of the brother due to breastfeeding: I do not command anyone [to marry her] nor do I prohibit it, but I only prohibit it for myself and my sons. And it was said: The daughter of Hamzah was proposed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for marriage, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) refused and said: 'She is the daughter of my brother due to breastfeeding.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Breast-feeding does not make (marriage) prohibited except that which causes the flesh to grow and the bones to strengthen.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Yaqoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about breast-feeding, what is the least amount that makes marriage prohibited? He said: 'That which builds the flesh or the blood.' Then he said: 'Do you consider one (feeding) to build it?' I said: 'I ask you, may Allah improve you, (what about) two?' He said: 'No.' So I did not cease to count for him until it reached ten feedings.

And from him, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about breast-feeding, what is the least of it that prohibits [marriage]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'That which builds the flesh and the blood.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you consider one [session] to build it?' So I said, 'I ask you, may Allah improve you, what about two?' He said, 'No.' And I did not cease to count/reiterate to him until it reached ten breast-feedings.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Breast-feeding does not cause prohibition (to marriage) except that which produces flesh and blood.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ziyad al-Qandy, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Does the single breast-feeding, the two breast-feedings, and the three breast-feedings make marriage prohibited?' He said, 'No, except what is upon which the bone has strengthened and the flesh has grown.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about breast-feeding, what is prohibited by it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man asked my father (peace be upon him) about it, so he (peace be upon him) said: One (session) is fine, and two, until it reaches five breast-feedings.' I said: 'Sequentially, or a sip after a sip?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Such is what he said to him.' And another man asked about it, so he (peace be upon him) extended it to nine. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'How often I am asked about breast-feeding!' So I said: 'May I be your ransom, inform me about your words: are you in this matter with a limit that is more than this?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I have already informed you with that which my father answered regarding it.' I said: 'I know what your father answered regarding it, but I said, perhaps there is a limit in it which he did not inform with, so you inform me with it.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Such is what my father said.' I said: 'So my mother breast-fed a slave girl with my milk.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'She is your sister from breast-feeding.' I said: 'So is she permissible for a brother of mine from my mother, whom my mother did not breast-feed with his milk?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So the stallion (father) is one?' I said: 'Yes, he is my brother from father and mother.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The milk of the stallion (father) made your father her father, and your mother her mother.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the boy who is breast-fed one feeding and two feedings, so he said: 'It does not make prohibition.' So I counted for him until I completed ten feedings, so he said: 'If they were separated, then no.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We are a large family, so sometimes during occasions of joy and sorrow where men and women gather, the woman might be shy to uncover her head in the presence of the man with whom she has a breastfeeding relationship, and the man might be hesitant to look at that. So what is it that prohibits (marriage) due to breastfeeding?' He said: 'That which builds the flesh and blood.' I said: 'And what is that which builds the flesh and blood?' He said: 'It was said, ten sucklings.' I said: 'Do ten sucklings impose prohibition?' He said: 'Leave that (the specific number).' And he said: 'Whatever is prohibited due to lineage, that is what is prohibited due to breastfeeding.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Breast-feeding causes prohibition only in that which strengthens the bone and grows the flesh; as for the single feeding, the two feedings, and the three, until they reach ten, if they are separate, then there is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the milk of the stallion (father). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is what your wife breast-feeds from your milk, and the milk of your child, (breast-fed to a) child of another, so it (brings about the) Prohibition'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about a man who had two wives, and each of them gave birth to a boy. So one of his wives went and breast-fed a girl from the people. Is it befitting for his son to marry this girl? He said: No, because she was breast-fed with the milk of the Sheikh (father).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the milk of the stallion (father). He (peace be upon him) said: 'What your wife breast-feeds from the milk of your child (breast-fed to a) child of another, so it is prohibited.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who breast-fed a girl, and her husband had a son from another woman. Is it permissible for the boy, the husband's son, to marry the girl whom she breast-fed? He said: 'The milk belongs to the stallion (father).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a woman, and she gave birth to a girl from him. Then the woman died, so he married another, and she gave birth to a son from him. Then she breastfed a boy from her milk. Is it permissible for that boy whom she breastfed to marry the daughter of the wife who was under the man before the last wife? He said: 'I do not like it that he marries the daughter of a stallion (father) who has been breastfed from his milk.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A concubine of a man breastfeeds a young child, and that man has a daughter from another woman. Is it permissible for that child to marry this daughter?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that he marries the daughter of a man from whom you have been breastfed by the milk of his son.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: 'Isa ibn Ja'far ibn 'Isa asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second: 'A woman breast-fed a child for me, so is it permissible for me to marry the daughter of her husband?' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'How excellent is what you asked from here; it may be that the people will say, So I said to him (peace be upon him): 'The girl is not the daughter of the woman who breast-fed for me, she is the daughter of someone else.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Even if there were ten [women] scattered [in different places], nothing would be permissible for you from them, and they would be in the place of your daughters.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Bureyd al-Ijaly, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And He it is Who created from water a human, then made for him lineage and marriage.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted created Adam from fresh water and created his wife from his rib, so He formed her from the lower of his ribs. Thus, by that rib flowed the cause and lineage. Then He married her to him, and by that cause, kinship by marriage flowed between them. And that is His Words, Mighty and Majestic: 'lineage and marriage.' So lineage, O brother of Banu Ijlan, is what is by the cause of the men, and marriage (kinship by marriage) is what is by the cause of the women.' He (the narrator) said: So I said to him, 'What is your view of the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'That which is prohibited by lineage is also prohibited by breastfeeding'? Explain that to me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Every woman who breastfeeds from the milk of her stallion (husband) the child of another woman, whether a girl or a boy, that is the breastfeeding which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spoke of. And every woman who breastfeeds from the milk of two stallions (husbands) which were for her, one after another, to a girl or a boy, then that is breastfeeding which is not the breastfeeding which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spoke of saying: 'That which is prohibited by lineage is also prohibited by breastfeeding'. Rather, it is breastfeeding from the side of lineage by way of marriage, and it does not prohibit anything, and it is not the cause of breastfeeding from the side of the milk of the stallions (fathers) so as to prohibit.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a boy who was breast-fed by a woman: Is it permissible for him to marry her sister (who is related) by the father, through breast-feeding? He (peace be upon him) said: No, for they have both been breast-fed from the milk of one stallion (father), from one woman. He (the narrator) said: So can he marry her sister (who is related) by the mother, through breast-feeding? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that, for her sister, who did not breast-feed him, had a different stallion (husband) from the one who breast-fed the boy. So if the two stallions (fathers) are different, there is no problem.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al-Khazzaz, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is breastfed by a woman while he is a boy, is it permissible for him to marry her sister from the mother via breastfeeding? He (peace be upon him) said: If the two women were breastfed by one woman from the milk of one stallion (father), then it is not permissible; and if the two women were breastfed by one woman from the milk of two stallions (fathers), then there is no problem with that.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Two rak'ahs prayed by a married man are better than seventy rak'ahs prayed by a bachelor.' A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Jamourani, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Kulayb ibn Mu'awiya al-Asadi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever gets married has protected half of his religion.' And in another hadith: 'Let him then be mindful of God regarding the other half,' or 'the remainder.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid, from Muhammad al-Asamm, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worthless ones of your deceased are the celibates (those who died unmarried).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Yusuf (peace be upon him) met his brother, he said: 'O my brother! How were you able to marry women after me?' He replied: 'My father commanded me.' He said: 'If you are able to have offspring who will fill the earth with glorification (of Allah), then do so.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Get married, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever loves to follow my Sunnah, then marriage is from my Sunnah.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ibn Faddal and Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he said to him: 'Do you have a wife?' He said: 'No.' So he said: 'My father said: I would not prefer that the world and all it contains were mine, if it meant spending a single night without a wife.' Then he said: 'Two rak'as prayed by a married man are superior to those of an unmarried man who stands in prayer throughout his night and fasts throughout his day.' Then his father gave him seven dinars and said to him: 'Get married with these.' Then his father said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Take wives, for it will bring more sustenance to you.'

And from him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), similar to it — and there is an addition in it: Muhammad ibn Ubayd said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I do not have a wife.' He (the Imam) said: 'Do you not have slave girls?' — or he said: 'Mothers of children?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then you are not a bachelor.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no breast-feeding (creating kinship) after weaning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Breast-feeding is valid before the two years, before he is weaned.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no breast-feeding (creating kinship) after weaning.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is the weaning?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The two years which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, speaks of.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who milked herself from her own milk, and she gave it to her husband so that she would become prohibited to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would keep her, and her back would be struck (with pain).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no breast-feeding after weaning, nor copulation during fasting, nor orphan-hood after puberty, nor silence for a day up to the night, nor conforming to Arab customs after the emigration, nor an emigration after the victory, nor a divorce before the marriage, nor an emancipation before ownership, nor an oath for the son with his father, nor for the slave with his master, nor for the woman with her husband, nor a vow regarding disobedience, nor an oath regarding cutting-off of relationships.' Thus, the meaning of his words: 'There is no breast-feeding after weaning', is that the child, when it drinks from the milk of the woman after she has weaned him, that breast-feeding would not bring about the prohibition of marriage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I married a woman, and I found that a woman had breast-fed me and breast-fed her sister.' He said, 'How much?' I said, 'A little bit.' He said, 'May Allah bless you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married the sister of his brother from breast-feeding, he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that I marry the sister of my brother from breast-feeding.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'My mother breast-fed a girl with my milk.' He said, 'She is your sister from breast-feeding.' I said, 'So would it be permissible for my brother from my mother, who did not breast-feed her with his milk — meaning not with this pregnancy, but with another pregnancy?' He said, 'And the stallion (father) is one?' I said, 'Yes, she is my sister of my father and my mother.' He said, 'The milk is of the stallion (father). Your father has become her father, and your mother, her mother.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man were to marry a girl who was a breast-fed infant, and his wife breast-fed her, then his marriage is void. He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man's wife who breast-fed a girl; would she be permissible for his son from another woman?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'So she is placed in the status of a sister through breast-feeding?' He said: 'Yes, from the side of the father.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! My wife milked from her own breast milk into a drinking cup and gave it to my slave-girl.' He said, 'Inflict pain upon your wife, and it is upon you with your slave-girl.' And this is the ruling of Ali (peace be upon him).

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby and Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who married a young girl, so his wife breast-fed her, or a mother of his child. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is prohibited unto him'.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The breast-feeding that builds the flesh and the blood is that which he breast-feeds until he is weary, and disinterested, and his breathing (sucking) ends.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a woman who claimed that she had breast-fed the woman and the boy, then she denied. He said: 'She is believed when she denies.' I said: 'But she said and claimed afterwards, "I have breast-fed them both."' He said: 'She is not believed, nor is there a blessing (of kinship established).'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not correct for the woman that her paternal uncle marries her, nor her maternal uncle, from the breast-feeding.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) About a woman whose milk flowed without giving birth, so she breastfed a girl and a boy with that milk. Is what is prohibited due to breast-feeding prohibited due to that milk? He said: No.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, narrated it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to him that a man married a young girl, so his wife breast-fed her, and then another wife of his breast-fed her. Ibn Shubrumah said: 'The girl and both his wives are prohibited to him.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Ibn Shubrumah erred. The girl is prohibited to him, and the wife who breast-fed her first. As for the last one, she is not prohibited to him, as if she had breast-fed her own daughter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Forbid your women from breastfeeding (multiple children) on the right and left, for they tend to forget.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribaat, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the boy is breast-fed from various women, so that it constitutes a number, or his flesh and blood grow upon it, the daughters of all of them become prohibited to him.

From him, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked (and I was present) about a woman who breast-fed a boy who was her slave from her milk until she weaned him: Is it permissible for her to sell him? He said: No, he is her son from breast-feeding. It is prohibited for her to sell him and to consume his price. He said, then he said: Did not the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'That which is prohibited due to lineage is also prohibited due to breast-feeding.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), 'A woman breast-fed a man's child. Is it permissible for that man to marry the daughter of this breast-feeder or not?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'No, she is not permissible to him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), asking: 'A woman breastfed a man's son; is it lawful for that man to marry the daughter of this breastfeeding woman or not?' He signed (the answer): 'No, it is not lawful for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Khallad al-Sindy, from Amr ibn Shimr, [from Jabir], from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man marries his midwife.' He said: 'No, nor her daughter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the midwife, is it permissible for the newborn to marry her? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and nor her daughter. She is one of his mothers.' And in the narration of Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: 'If she was a midwife and moved on, then the midwives are many from that, and if she was a midwife and nourished, she is prohibited to him.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa, the seller of Sabir, from Aban ibn Uthman from Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the child faces the midwife with his face, she becomes prohibited to him, and her children become prohibited to him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Mut'ah. So he said: It was revealed in the Quran. Then as to those whom you enjoy with, give them their dowries as appointed; and there is no blame on you about what you mutually agree after what is appointed.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'Had the son of Khattab not preceded me (in the Caliphate), none would have committed adultery except for a wretch'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, it was revealed: 'Then as to those whom you enjoy with,' (referring to temporary marriage). give them their dowries as appointed.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: Abdullah ibn Umeyr al-Laythi came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'What do you say regarding the Mut'ah of women?' He said, 'Allah permitted it in His Book and upon the tongue of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so it is permissible until the Day of Resurrection.' He said, 'O Abu Ja'far! The likes of you say this, and yet Umar prohibited it and forbade it.' He said, 'Even if he did so.' He said, 'I seek refuge with Allah for you from that, that you should permit something which Umar has prohibited.' So he said to him, 'So you are upon the saying of your companion, and I am upon the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So come, I shall curse you if the true saying is what the Messenger of Allah said, and the falsehood is what your companion said.' He said, so Abdullah ibn Umeyr turned to him and said, 'Would it please you if your wives, and your daughters, and your sisters, and the daughters of your paternal uncle did it?' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) turned away from him when he mentioned his wives and the daughters of his paternal uncle.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Mut'ah: the Quran was revealed concerning it, and the Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed by it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Hariz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I heard Abu Hanifa ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mut'a, so he said: 'Which of the two Mut'as are you asking about?' He said, 'I asked you about the Mut'a of Hajj, so inform me about the Mut'a of women, is it true?' So for whatever you have enjoyed of them, give them their dowries as an obligation. So Abu Hanifa said, 'By Allah, it is as if it is a verse that I have never read before.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali al-Sa'iyy, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom. I used to marry for Mut'ah (temporary marriage), but I disliked it and took it as an ill omen, so I gave Allah a pledge between the Rukn and the Maqam, and made a vow upon myself regarding that, including fasting, that I would not marry for Mut'ah. Then that became difficult for me, and I regretted my oath, and I did not have the financial means to marry publicly (permanent marriage). He said to me: 'You pledged to Allah that you would not obey Him? By Allah, if you do not obey Him, you will disobey Him.'

Ali (peace be upon him) raised it (in the chain of narration), he said: Abu Hanifa asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad (peace be upon him), so he said to him: 'O Abu Ja'far! What do you say regarding Mut'a (temporary marriage)? Do you claim that it is halal (permissible)?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'So what prevents you from instructing your womenfolk that they should be enjoyed (perform Mut'a) and earn for you?' So Abu Ja'far said to him: 'Not every craft/work is desired in it, even though it may be permissible, and people have different capacities and ranks which elevate their capacities.' 'But what do you say, O Abu Hanifa, regarding Al-Nabeez (a type of drink)? Do you claim that it is permissible?' So he said: 'Yes.' He said: 'So what prevents you from getting your womenfolk to sit in the shops as sellers of Nabeez, so they would earn for you?' So Abu Hanifa said: 'One with one, and your share is more effective (or: your share is purer/stronger).' Then he said to him: 'O Abu Ja'far! The Verse in the chapter 'Sa'ala Sa'il' speaks with the prohibition of Mut'a, and the narration from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) has come with its abrogation.' So Abu Ja'far said to him: 'O Abu Hanifa! The Chapter 'Sa'ala Sa'il' is Meccan, and the Verse of Mut'a is Medinite, and your narration is abnormal (shadh) and refuted.' So Abu Hanifa said to him: 'And the Verse of Inheritance also speaks with the abrogation of Mut'a.' So Abu Ja'far said: 'Marriage is established without inheritance.' Abu Hanifa said: 'From where do you say that?' So Abu Ja'far said: 'If a man from the Muslims were to marry a woman from the People of the Book, then he dies from her, what would you say regarding it?' He said: 'She does not inherit from him.' He said: 'So marriage is established without inheritance.' Then they departed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'How many are permissible from Mut'ah?' He said, then he said: 'They are at the status of the slave girls.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ash'ari, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), is she from the four (permanent wives)? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said: I said, 'What is permissible from Mut'ah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'As many as you desire.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), is she from the four (permanent wives)? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, nor from the seventy.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Barqi, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdul-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding Mut'ah (temporary marriage), he said: She is not from the four (permanent wives), because she is not divorced, and does not inherit. Rather, she is only hired.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah (temporary marriage), so he said: 'Meet Abdul Malik ibn Jurayj and ask him about it, for he has knowledge of it from us.' So I met him and he dictated to me much regarding its permissibility. Among what Ibn Jurayj narrated to me was that he said: 'There is no time limit nor a number [limit] in it. Rather, she is at the status of slave girls. He may marry from them as many as he wishes, and the one with four wives may marry from them as many as he wishes, without a guardian and without witnesses. So when the term expires, she becomes divorced from him without a formal divorce pronouncement, and he gives her a small amount, and her waiting period is two menstruations. And if she does not menstruate, then it is forty-five days.' So I came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with the book and presented it to him, and he said: 'He is truthful and I confirm it.' Ibn Udhaynah said: 'And Zurarah ibn A'yan used to say this and swore that it is the truth, except that he used to say: If she menstruates, then it is one menstruation, and if she does not menstruate, then it is a month and a half.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I mentioned Mut'ah (temporary marriage) to him, asking if she is from the four (permanent wives). So he said: 'Marry from them a thousand, for they are hired (temporary wives).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah, so he said: 'And what is it with you and that, for Allah has made you needless from it?' I said, 'I only intended to know it.' So he said: 'It is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).' I said, 'We increase it and she increases it?' So he said: 'And what makes it pleasing to him except that?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all from al-Fatah ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about Mut'ah, so he said: 'It is permissible, freely authorized for the one whom Allah has not made needless through marriage, so let him maintain chastity with Mut'ah. So if he is needless from it through marriage, then it is authorized for him when he is absent from her.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) wrote to one of his freed slaves: 'Do not persist upon Mut'ah (temporary marriage). Rather, upon you is the establishment of the Sunnah, so do not be preoccupied with it to the neglect of your beds and your free wives, for they would disbelieve, and disavow, and supplicate against the one who commands that, and curse us.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding Mut'ah: 'Leave it! Is it not that one of you feels shy to be seen in a place of blemish, so that this would be carried upon the righteous ones of his brethren and companions'?

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the Mut'a. So he said: 'Indeed, the Mut'a today is not as it was before today. Indeed, those women were believed (to be valid) at that time, and today they are not believed (to be valid), so ask about them.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Is-haq, from Abu Sarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about it, meaning the Mut'ah, so he said to me: 'It is permissible, so do not marry except chaste women.' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And those who guard their private parts.' Therefore, do not place your private part where you would not feel safe regarding your Dirham.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said: A man asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) — and I was listening — about a man who married a woman with Mut'a and stipulated upon her that he would not seek/acknowledge her child. So she came after that with a child. So he was intense in the denial of the child and said: 'Did he deny it greatly due to that?' The man said: 'But, he was accusing her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for you that you marry except a believing woman, or a Muslim woman, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: The adulterer shall not marry any but an adulteress or an idolatress, and the adulteress none shall marry her but an adulterer or an idolater; and that is forbidden to the believers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, raising it, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman, and I do not know her state, can the man marry her with Mut'ah? He said: He presents himself to her, so if she responds to him with immorality (fajur), then he should not do it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the beautiful, immoral woman: Is it permissible for a man to enjoy her for a day or more? He said: If she is well-known for adultery, then he should not enjoy her, nor marry her.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Temporary marriage (Mut'a) does not occur except with two matters: a specified term and a specified recompense.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: It is inevitable that you should be saying regarding these stipulations, 'I hereby marry you with Mut'a, for such and such day, and with such and such Dirhams, a marriage without adultery, upon the Book of Allah Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and upon a stipulation that neither will you inherit me nor will I inherit you, and upon a stipulation that you will be observing a waiting period of forty five days'. And some of them (reporters) have said, 'One menstruation'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Taghlib, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran and Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I say to her when I am alone with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say, I marry you as a Mut'a marriage upon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), neither inheriting nor being inherited from, for such and such days, and if you wish, such and such years, for such and such dirhams, and you specify the compensation which you two agree upon, whether little or much. So when she says 'Yes', she has consented, so she is your wife, and you are the closest of people to her. I said, 'But I am shy to mention the stipulation of the days.' He said, 'It is more harmful to you.' I said, 'And how?' He said, 'If you do not stipulate, it becomes a permanent marriage, and maintenance becomes obligatory upon you during the waiting period, and she becomes an heir, and you cannot divorce her except by a Sunnah divorce.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Sa'labah, said: You should say, 'I marry you as Mut'ah upon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), a marriage without adultery, and upon a stipulation that neither will you inherit me nor will I inherit you, for such and such days, with such and such Dirhams, and upon a stipulation that upon you is the waiting period.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I said, 'How is one to marry for Mut'ah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever was a stipulation before the marriage, the marriage nullified it, and whatever was after the marriage, then it is valid.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the term is specified, then it is Mut'ah, and if the term is not specified, then it is a lasting marriage.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Riab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agreed upon after the obligation'. He said: 'What you agree upon after the marriage contract is valid, and what was before the marriage contract is not valid except with her consent and by giving her something with which she is pleased'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Suleiman ibn Salim, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: When you stipulate the conditions of Mut'ah upon the woman, and she accepts it and makes the marriage binding, then return to her your first condition after the marriage. If she approves it, then it is approved; and if she does not approve it, then what was from the condition before the marriage is not binding upon her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the man marrying the woman by Mut'ah that they inherit each other if they did not stipulate [otherwise], and the stipulation is after the marriage.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Suleyman ibn Salim, from Ibn Bukayr ibn Ayn, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you stipulate the conditions of Mut'a upon the woman, and she accepts them and makes the marriage binding, then return to her your first condition after the marriage. If she approves it, it is approved; and if she does not approve it, then what was from the condition before the marriage is not binding upon her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The righteous child is an aromatic flower from God, distributed by Him among His servants. And indeed, my two aromatic flowers from this world are al-Hasan and al-Husayn. I named them both by the names of two grandsons from the Children of Israel: Shabbar and Shabbir.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from some of his companions, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the happiness of a man is that he has children through whom he seeks assistance.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Have many children; through you I shall outstrip the other nations in number on the morrow (the Day of Judgment).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Yusuf met his brother, he said to him: 'O my brother, how were you able to marry women after me?' He said: 'My father commanded me and said: If you are able to have offspring for yourself who fill the earth with the glorification (of God), then do so.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Indeed, so-and-so — a man whose name he mentioned — said: I was ascetic regarding children, until I stood at Arafat, and behold, beside me was a young boy, supplicating, weeping, and saying: O Lord! My parents! My parents! So he made me desire children when I heard that.'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Among the happiness of a man is a righteous son.

And from him, from Bakr ibn Salih, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that I had refrained from seeking children for five years, and that was because my wife disliked it and said: 'Their upbringing is difficult for me due to the scarcity of means. So what is your opinion?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'Seek children, for God, Mighty and Majestic, will provide for them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the children of Muslims are designated in the presence of God as intercessors and ones interceded for. So when they reach twelve years of age, good deeds are recorded for them. And when they reach puberty, evil deeds are recorded against them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to recite: 'And indeed I fear my relatives after me' — meaning that he (Zakariyya) did not have an inheritor until God granted him one after old age.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The righteous son is an aromatic flower from the flowers of Paradise.'
And by this chain, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: From the happiness of the man is the righteous son.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) passed by a grave whose inhabitant was being punished. Then he passed by it the following year, and behold, he was not being punished. So he said: 'O Lord! I passed by this grave the first year, so he was being punished, and I passed by it this year and he is not being punished.' So Allah revealed to him: 'A righteous son of his has come of age, so he repaired a road and sheltered an orphan, thus for this I have forgiven him for what his son did.' Then Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The inheritance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from His believing servant is a son who worships Him after him.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited the Verse of Zakariyya (peace be upon him): 'My Lord, grant me from Yourself a successor. Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Yaqoub, and make him, my Lord, one with whom You are well pleased.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Ishaq Thalabah ibn Maymun, from a man who had named him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The most truthful of the names are those named by servitude (to Allah), and the best of them are the names of the Prophets.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The first righteous deed a man does for his child is that he names it with a good name, so let each one of you give a good name to his child.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A child is not born to us except that we name him Muhammad. So when seven days have passed for us, if we wish, we change [the name], and if we wish, we leave it [as is].

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Mabbah, from so-and-so ibn Humayd, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and consulted him regarding the name of his child, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Name him with names from servitude.' He said, 'Which names are these?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abd al-Rahman.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Azrami, who said: Muawiya appointed Marwan ibn al-Hakam over Medina and ordered him to assign stipends for the youth of Quraysh, so he assigned them. Then Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'So I went to him, and he said, Then he assigned a stipend for me. So I returned to my father and informed him. He said: 'Woe to the son of al-Zarqa, the tanner of the unseeded land. If a hundred were born to me, I would love that I not name any of them except Ali.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Poverty does not enter a house in which is the name Muhammad, or Ahmad, or Ali, or al-Hasan, or al-Husayn, or Ja'far, or Talib, or Abd Allah, or Fatima from the women.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a boy has been born to me, so what should I name him?' He said: 'Name him with the name most beloved to me, Hamza.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, from Zayd, from Ali, from al-Husayn, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beautify your names, for you will be called by them on the Day of Resurrection: 'Arise, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, to your light,' and 'Arise, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, there is no light for you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sa'id ibn Khuthaym, from Ma'mar ibn Khuthaym, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is your teknonym (kunyah)?' I said: 'I have not yet taken a teknonym, and I have no son, nor a wife, nor a slave girl.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what prevents you from that?' I said: 'A hadith reached us from Ali (peace be upon him).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?' I said: 'It reached us from Ali (peace be upon him) that he said: The one who takes a teknonym and has no family, is Abu Ja'ar (Father of Dung).' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Falsified! This is not from the hadith of Ali (peace be upon him). We (peace be upon him) take our children's teknonyms in their childhood, for fear of the nickname being attached to them.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Al-Husayn ibn Nasr, from his father, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wanted to ride to visit one of his Shias, so he said: 'O Jabir, accompany me.' So I followed him. When he reached the door of the house, a young son of his came out to us. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is your name?' He said, 'Muhammad.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By what are you teknonymed (kunya)?' He said, 'With Ali.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You have guarded yourself against Satan with intense guarding. Indeed, when Satan hears a caller calling out, 'O Muhammad! O Ali!', he melts just as lead melts, until when he hears a caller calling out with the name of an enemy from our enemies, he trembles and struts.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called for a parchment when death approached him, intending to forbid certain names by which one is named. So he was taken (in death) and did not specify them. Among them are Al-Hakam, Hakeem, Khalid, and Malik; and he mentioned that there are six or seven of those that are not permissible to be named with.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade four teknonyms: Abu Isa, and Abu al-Hakam, and Abu Malik, and Abu al-Qasim when the name is Muhammad.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The most hateful of the names to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are Harith, Malik, and Khalid.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man used to visit Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and he was known as Abu Murra. So when he sought permission to enter, he would say, "Abu Murra is at the door." Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: "By Allah, when you come to our door, do not say, 'Abu Murra'."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Shurhbeel ibn Muslim, that he said: Regarding the pregnant woman: she should eat the quince, for the child will be of pleasant aroma and clear colour.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, and he looked at a beautiful boy: 'It is fitting that the father of this boy would have eaten the quince.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdul Aziz ibn Hassan, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of your dates are Al-Barny, therefore feed these to your womenfolk during their postpartum period, so that your children come out pure and forebearing.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, who raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let the first thing eaten by the postpartum woman be fresh ripe dates (rutab), for Allah the Exalted said to Maryam: And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree, it will drop on you fresh ripe dates.' It was said, 'O Rasool-Allah! Suppose it is not the season for the fresh dates?' He said: 'Seven dates from the dates of Al-Medina. So if they are not available, then seven dates from the dates of your cities.' For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'By My Might, and My Majesty, and My Greatness, and the Elevation of My Status! A woman who eats fresh dates on the day she gives birth, if it is a boy, he will be forbearing (patient), and if it is a girl, she will be forbearing.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Saeed al-Shami, from Salih ibn Uqba who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Feed Al-Barny (dates) to your womenfolk during their postpartum bleeding, your children would be forbearing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Qabisah, from Abdullah al-Naysaburi, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Abu Musa, from Abu al-A'la al-Shami, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Feed your pregnant women the dairy (products), for the child, when it feeds in the belly of its mother with the dairy (products), its heart gets stronger and there is an increase in its intellect. So if it happens to be a boy, he would be brave and if a female is born her buttocks would be larger, so she would enjoy by that with her husband'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: Feed your pregnant women the dairy (products), so if there happens to be a boy in her belly, he would come out as pure of heart, knowledgeable, brave; and if there happens to be a girl, she would be of beautiful in her appearance, and in her manners, and of large buttocks, and she would enjoy with her husband.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Ismail al-Sayqal, from Abu Yahya al-Razi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the newborn is born for you, what do you do with it? I said, 'I do not know what we do with it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Take a lentil of Jawashir, soak it in water, then drip it into his nose: two drops in the right nostril and one drop in the left. Recite the Adhan in his right ear and the Iqamah in his left. Do this before his umbilical cord is cut, for he will never be startled, nor will he be affected by Umm al-Sibyan.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Hafs al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Instruct the midwife or someone who is next to her that the Prayer be established in its (new-born's) right ear, so it would not be touched by insanity, nor by a following eye, ever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The newborn is anointed with the water of the Euphrates, and Iqaamah is recited in his ear.

And in another report He (peace be upon him) said: 'Open the mouth of your children with water of the Euphrates and with the dust of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so if there does not happen to be (these), so with the water of the sky (rain)'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Palate your children with dates; thus did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) do with Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever has a newborn child, let him recite the Adhan (call to prayer) in his right ear with the Adhan of the Prayer, and let him recite the Iqamah in the left, for it is a safeguarding from the Pelted Satan.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said: The Aqeeqa is obligatory when a child is born to a man, so if he wishes to name him on that day, let him do so.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from al-Wassa, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every newborn is held in pledge by the 'Aqeeqa.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'By Allah, I do not know whether my father performed the Aqeeqa for me or not.' He said, 'So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me, and I performed the Aqeeqa for myself, and I am an old man.' And Umar said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Every person is pledged with his Aqeeqa, and the Aqeeqa is more obligatory than the Udhiyah (sacrifice).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every newborn is pledged with his Aqeeqa.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Aqeeqa, is it obligatory? He said: Yes, it is obligatory.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). A messenger of his uncle, Abd Allah ibn Ali, came to him and said to him: Your uncle says to you, 'We sought the Aqeeqa (sacrificial animal for a newborn), but we did not find it, so what do you think? Should we give in charity the price of it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Indeed, Allah loves the feeding of the food and the shedding of the blood.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra, from Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Aqeeqa is obligatory.

Ali, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marar, from Yunus and Ibn Abi Umeyr, both together, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Two boys were born to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at the same time, so he ordered Zayd ibn Ali to buy for him two camels for the Aqeeqa. It was a time of high prices, so he bought one for him, but the second was difficult for him. So he said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The second has become difficult for me, so give its price in charity.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, seek it until you are able to afford it, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the pouring out of blood (of sacrifice) and the feeding of food.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Mu'az al-Farra from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The boy is a pledge for his seventh (day), with a ram; he is named during it, and Aqeeqa is performed for him. And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Fatima (peace be upon her) shaved her two sons and gave in charity silver equal to the weight of their hair.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the Aqeeqa, so he said: 'Regarding the male and the female, it is the same.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Aqeeqa for the boy and the girl is the same.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Aqeeqa, so he said: 'The Aqeeqa of the boy and the girl is a ram, a ram.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Aqeeqa of the boy and the girl is a ram.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Aqeeqa upon the solvent and the insolvent, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon the one who cannot find (the means).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the Aqeeqa upon the insolvent and the solvent, so he said: 'There is nothing upon the one who cannot find (the means).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ibn Jabala and Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Slaughter for him (the newborn), and shave his head on the seventh day, and give in charity silver equal to the weight of his hair, and cut the Aqeeqa meat into pieces, and cook it, and invite a group of Muslims to eat it.

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Hammad ibn Udays, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'By which of those shall we begin?' He said, 'Shave his head, and perform Aqeeqa for him, and give silver in charity equal to the weight of his hair, and that should happen in one place.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Aqeeqa, is it obligatory? He said: Yes. An animal is sacrificed for him, and his head is shaved when he is seven days old, and his hair is weighed in silver or gold and given in charity, and the midwife is fed a quarter of a sheep, and the Aqeeqa is a sheep or a camel.

And from him, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: When it is the seventh day, and a boy or a girl has been born to one of you, let him perform Aqeeqa for him: a ram for the male, and similarly for the female. Perform Aqeeqa for him, feed the midwife from the Aqeeqa, and name him on the seventh day.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Hafs al-Kunasi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the newborn is born, an Aqeeqa sacrifice is performed for it, its head is shaved, and the weight of its hair in silver is given in charity, and the leg and thigh are presented to the midwife, and a group of Muslims are invited to eat and supplicate for the boy, and he is named on the seventh day.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Aqeeqa is performed for the child, and his head is shaved when he is seven days old, and his hair is weighed and charity is given in his name equal to the weight of his hair in gold or silver, and the midwife is fed with the leg and the thigh.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Aqeeqa is a camel or a sheep.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a boy or a girl is born to you, sacrifice for him on the seventh day a sheep or a camel, eat from it, feed [others], name [him], shave his head on the seventh day, and give in charity the weight of his hair in gold or silver, and give to the midwife a portion of that. So whatever of that you do, it has sufficed you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all together, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the newborn child: when should one slaughter for him, shave his head, give in charity the weight of his hair, and name him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of that is on the seventh day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Aqeeqa for the newborn, how it is? He said: When seven days come upon the newborn, name him by the name that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has named him with. Then shave his head, and give in charity the weight of his hair in gold or silver, and slaughter a ram for him. And if a ram is not found, suffice it with whatever suffices in the Udhiyah (Qurbani), or else a lamb, the largest of the lambs of the year. And give the midwife a quarter of it. And if there is no midwife, it is for his mother; she gives it to whomever she wishes, and feeds from it ten of the Muslims. If they increase, that is better, and eat from it. And the Aqeeqa is obligatory whether one is rich or poor, when one is able. And if one does not perform the Aqeeqa for him until he performs the Udhiyah for him, then the Udhiyah suffices for him. And he said: If the midwife is a Jewess, who does not eat from the slaughter of the Muslims, she is given the value of a quarter of the ram.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the newborn. He said: It is named on the seventh day, and an Aqeeqa is performed for it, and its head is shaved, and silver equal to the weight of its hair is given in charity, and the leg is sent to the midwife along with the shoulder, and one feeds from it, and gives in charity.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Aqeeqa is on the seventh day, and the midwife is given the leg along with the thigh, and the bone is not broken.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Hafs al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the child is born, an Aqeeqa sacrifice is performed for him, his head is shaved, charity is given equal to the weight of his hair, the leg along with the thigh is gifted to the midwife, a group of Muslims are invited to eat and supplicate for the boy, and he is named on the seventh day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, both together from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Safwan, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: You should say upon the Aqeeqa, when you perform it: 'In the Name of Allah and by Allah. O Allah, an Aqeeqa for so-and-so, its flesh for his flesh, its blood for his blood, and its bones for his bones. O Allah, make it a shield for the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'
