Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you slaughter, say: 'In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and all praise is for Allah, and Allah is the Greatest; with faith in Allah, and praise upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and infallibility for His command, and gratitude for His sustenance, and knowledge of His grace upon us, the People of the Household.' So if it is a male, say: 'O Allah, You have bestowed upon us a male, and You are more Knowing of what You have bestowed, and from You is what You have granted; so accept from us whatever we do, upon Your Sunnah and the Sunnah of Your Prophet and Your Messenger (peace be upon him and his family); and banish from us the Pelted Satan; for You the blood has been spilt, there is no partner for You, and all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: You should say upon the Aqeeqa: [a similar supplication was mentioned], and he added in it: 'O Allah, its flesh for his flesh, and its blood for his blood, and its bone for his bone, and its hair for his hair, and its skin for his skin. O Allah, make it a shield for so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you intend to slaughter the Aqeeqa, you say: 'O my people! I am clear of what you associate (with Allah). I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth, upright and submitting, and I am not of the polytheists. Surely my prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no associate for Him, and with that I am commanded, and I am of the Muslims.' O Allah, from You and for You, in the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and accept from so-and-so, son of so-and-so' – and name the newborn with his name, then slaughter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Muhammad ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Marid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One should say during the Aqeeqa: 'O Allah, from You and for You is what You have gifted, and You gave it. O Allah, so accept from us upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and we seek refuge with Allah from the Pelted Satan.' And you name [the animal], and slaughter it, and you say: 'For You I spill the blood, there is no associate for You, and the praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, expel the Pelted Satan.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the Aqeeqa: when you slaughter, you should say: I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth, upright and submitting. And I am not of the polytheists. Surely my Prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are (all) for Allah, the Lord of the worlds. There is no associate for Him. O Allah, from You and for You. O Allah, this is on behalf of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the blessings of God upon a man is that his child resembles him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, from Sudayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Among the happiness of a man is that he has a child in whom his resemblance is recognised — his physical form, his character, and his noble qualities.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (AS) saying: 'Blessed is the man who does not die until he sees a successor from himself.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman should not eat from the Aqeeqa of her child, and there is no problem if she were to give to the needy neighbour, from the meat.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from al-Wassa, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He does not eat, nor anyone from his family, from the 'Aqeeqa. He said: And for the midwife is one-third of the 'Aqeeqa. So if the midwife was the mother of the man, or among his family members, then she is not entitled to anything from it. And it should be made into parts, then cooked, and distributed, and it is not given except to the people of Wilayah. And he said: Everyone eats from the 'Aqeeqa except the mother.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Aqeeqa, he said: 'The mother should not eat anything from it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed the Aqeeqa for Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) with his own hand and said: 'In the Name of Allah, an Aqeeqa for Al-Hasan.' And he said: 'O Allah, its bone with his bone, its flesh with his flesh, its blood with his blood, and its hair with his hair. O Allah, make it a shield for Muhammad and his Progeny.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Fatima (peace be upon him) performed the Aqeeqa for her two sons, and shaved their heads on the seventh day, and gave in charity the weight of their hair in silver. And he (peace be upon him) said: And some people used to stain the head of the child with the blood of the Aqeeqa, and my father used to say: That is Shirk (associating partners with God).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from 'Asim al-Kuzi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioning from his father that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed the 'Aqeeqa for Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) with a ram, and for Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with a ram, and gave something to the midwife, and shaved their heads on the seventh day, and weighed their hair, and gave silver in charity equal to its weight. He (the narrator) said, So I said to him, 'Should the blood be taken and the head of the infant smeared with it?' He said, 'That is Shirk (associating partners with God).' I said, 'Glory be to Allah, Shirk?' He said, 'Even if that were not Shirk, it was practiced in the Pre-Islamic period (Jahiliyyah) and was forbidden in Islam.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Aqeeqa, the shaving, and the naming, asking which of these should be done first. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of that is done in one time: shaving, slaughtering, and naming.' Then he mentioned what Fatima (peace be upon her) did for her children, then said: 'The hair is weighed and silver is given in charity equal to its weight.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) named Hasan and Husayn (peace be upon them) on their seventh day, and performed the 'Aqeeqa for them, a sheep for each, and they sent a leg of a sheep to the midwife, and he ate from the rest, and gifted to the neighbors. And Fatima (peace be upon her) shaved their heads and gave silver in charity equal to the weight of their hair.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about congratulating the birth of a child, when (should it be done)? So he said: 'He (peace be upon him) said: When Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was born, Jibraeel descended with congratulations upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on the seventh day, and instructed him to name him, teknonym him, shave his head, perform Aqeeqa for him, and pierce his ear. And similarly, when Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was born, he came to him on the seventh day and instructed him with similar actions.' He said: And for both of them were two forelocks in the left horn (side of the head), and the piercing was in the right ear in the lobe, and in the left, it was in the upper part of the ear. So the earring (Al-Qurt) was in the right, and the ear-ring (Al-Shanf) in the left. And it has been reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) left for both of them two forelocks in the middle of the head, and this is more correct than the side (horn).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Circumcise your children at seven days, for it is purer and faster for the growth of the flesh, and indeed the earth dislikes the urine of the uncircumcised. And by this chain, it was said that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The piercing of the ear of the boy is from the Sunnah, and his circumcision at seven days is from the Sunnah.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Purify your children on the seventh day, for it is more fragrant, purer, and faster for the growth of the flesh, and indeed the earth becomes impure from the urine of the uncircumcised for forty mornings.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, that he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): It has been reported from the two Truthful Ones (peace be upon them) that: 'Circumcise your children on the seventh day to purify them, and indeed the earth resounds with noise to Allah from the urine of the uncircumcised.' And I, may I be your ransom, said: The surgeons of our city are not skilled in that, and they do not circumcise him on the seventh day. And among us is a Jewish surgeon, so is it permissible for the Jew to circumcise the children of the Muslims or not, if Allah wills? So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'The Sunnah is on the seventh day, therefore do not oppose the Sunnah, if Allah wills.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Qaza'a, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The ones in front of us are saying that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) circumcised himself with a curved knife upon a large jar.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! It is not as what they are saying. They are lying upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him).' I said: 'And how is that?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophets (peace be upon them), their wrapping used to drop off from them along with their navel during the seventh day. So when (Ismail) was born to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) from Hajar, Sarah reproached Hajar with what slaves are reproached with. So Hajar cried, and that was grievous upon her. So when Ismail saw her crying, he cried as well due to her crying, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) entered. So he said: So Ibrahim stood upon his Prayer Mat, so he whispered unto his Lord, and asked Him to Cast that away from Hajar. So Allah Cast that off from Hajar. So when Sarah gave birth to Is'haq, and it was the seventh day, there fell down from him, his navel, but his wrapping did not fall. So Sarah panicked from that. So when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came over to her, she said: 'O Ibrahim! What is this occurrence which has occurred in the Progeny of Ibrahim, and the children of the Prophets? This is your son Is'haq. His navel has fallen off from him and his wrapping did not fall off from him.' So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stood upon his Prayer Mat, so he whispered to his Lord, and said: 'O Lord! What is this occurrence which has occurred in the Progeny of Ibrahim and the children of the Prophets, and this is my son Is'haq. His navel has fallen off from him and his wrapping did not fall off from him.' So Allah the High Revealed unto him: 'O Ibrahim! This is due to what Sarah reproached Hajar with, so I Swore that, that would not fall off from anyone from the children of the Prophets due to the reproach of Sarah to Hajar. Therefore, circumcise Is'haq with the iron, and make him taste the heat of the iron'. He said: 'So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) circumcised him with the iron, and the Sunnah flowed with the circumcision in the children of Is'haq after that'.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Piercing the ear of the boy is from the Sunnah, and circumcision of the boy is from the Sunnah.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureyd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: From the Sunnah of the Sent Prophets is the cleaning oneself after relieving oneself, and circumcision.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about circumcising the child on the seventh day, is it from the Sunnah or can it be delayed, and which of the two is preferable? He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the seventh day is from the Sunnah, and if it is delayed, there is no problem.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From the uprightness (or Hanifism) is circumcision.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The newborn is sacrificed for (Aqeeqa) and circumcised on the seventh day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man embraces Islam, he is circumcised, even if he has reached eighty (years of age).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the girl captured from the land of the girl who is captured from the land of Polytheism, so she becomes a Muslim. So someone was sought who could lower (cut) her, but we were not able to find a woman. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the Sunnah regarding the circumcision, it is upon the men, and it is not upon the women'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Circumcision of the boy is from the Sunnah, and cutting (the genitals) of the girls is not from the Sunnah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The lowering (of the female child's genitals) is a noble deed, and it is not from the Sunnah, nor is it anything obligatory, and which thing is more preferable than the noble deed?

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from one of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Circumcision in men is a Sunnah, and in women it is a noble deed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was a woman called Umm Tayba who used to perform circumcision on girls. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called her and said to her: 'O Umm Tayba! When you circumcise a woman, make a snip and do not scrape excessively, for it is clearer for the complexion and more pleasurable for the husband.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the women emigrated to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a woman among them named Umm Habeeb emigrated, and she was a circumciser who would circumcise the girls. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw her, he said to her: 'O Umm Habeeb, the work that was in your hand is in your hand today.' She said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, except if it is forbidden, so forbid me from it.' He said, 'No, but it is permissible. So come closer to me until I teach you.' She said, 'So I came closer to him, and he said: O Umm Habeeb, when you do it, do not overdo it, i.e., do not amputate it completely, and snip it, for it is brighter for the face and more pleasing to the husband.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a newborn, [whether] his head should be shaved after the seventh day, so he said: 'When seven days have passed, the shaving is not obligatory upon him.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Aqeeqa, he said: 'When seven days are exceeded, so there is no Aqeeqa for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Idrees ibn Abdullah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a newborn who is born and then dies on the seventh day, should Aqeeqa be performed for him? He (peace be upon him) said: If he dies before midday, Aqeeqa is not performed for him, and if he dies after midday, Aqeeqa is performed for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Harun, the freedman of the family of Ja'da, who said: I was sitting with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in Medina. He missed me for a few days, then I came to him. He said to me: 'I have not seen you for a few days, O Abu Harun.' I said: 'A boy was born to me.' He said: 'May Allah bless him.' I said: 'What did you name him?' I said: 'I named him Muhammad.' He said: 'So he turned his cheek towards the ground, saying: 'Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad', until his cheek almost touched the ground. Then he said: 'By my soul, and by my children, and by my family, and by my parents, and by all the people of the earth, let them be sacrificed for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Do not insult him, do not hit him, and do not harm him. And know that there is no house on earth in which the name Muhammad is not, except that it is sanctified every day.' Then he said to me: 'Did you perform the Aqeeqa for him?' I remained silent. He saw me where I remained silent, thinking that I had not done it, so he said: 'O Musaddaf, come closer to me.' By Allah, I did not know what he said to him, except that I guessed he had ordered something for me. So I went to stand up, so he said to me: 'Stay as you are, O Abu Harun.' So Musaddaf came to me with three dinars, so he placed them in my hand. He said: 'O Abu Harun, go and buy two rams, fatten them, slaughter them, eat and feed.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had not performed the Aqeeqa for his child until he grew up, and was a youthful boy, or a man who had matured. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When a sacrifice is offered on his behalf, or the boy offers a sacrifice for himself, then his Aqeeqa has sufficed for him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The newborn is held in pledge by his Aqeeqa; his parents either free him (from the pledge) or leave him (in it).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not shave the children in the manner of al-Qaza', and al-Qaza is that one shaves a part and leaves a part.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he used to dislike the qaza' (partly shaven head) in the heads of the children, and mentioned that the qaza' is that the head is shaved except for a little, and the middle of the head is left, it is named the qaza'ah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A young boy was brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to supplicate for him, and he had 'qanazi' (partly shaven head), so he refused to supplicate for him and ordered that his head be shaved, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ordered the shaving of the stomach hair.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no milk by which the infant is nursed that is greater in blessing upon him than the milk of its mother.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salma ibn al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Musa from Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Walid from his father from his mother Umm Is'haq bint Sulayman She said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at me while I was breastfeeding one of my sons, Muhammad or Is'haq. He said: 'O Umm Is'haq! Do not breastfeed him from one breast, but breastfeed him from both of them, so that one becomes food and the other a drink.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Breast-feeding is for twenty-one months, so whatever is deficient [from this period], it is an injustice upon the child.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about breast-feeding, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The free woman is not compelled to breast-feed the child, and the mother of the child (slave) is compelled.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who died and left a child, so they found a wet-nurse for him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wages of breast-feeding of the child is from what it has inherited from its father and its mother'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who died and left a wife, and with her, from him, was a child. So she cast him upon a servant of her to breast-feed him. Then she came over seeking the (wages for) breast-feeding the boy, from the successor. So he (peace be upon him) said: ‘For her is a recompense (wages) similar to it, and it is not for the successor that he should throw him out from her lap until he becomes aware (attains puberty), and he should hand over his wealth’.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the child, can he be breastfed for more than two years? So he said: 'Two years'. I said, 'So if it is increased upon the two years, is there anything upon its parents from that?' He said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj and Hammad, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who employed a wet-nurse, so he handed over to her his son. So the wet-nurse went and handed over his son to another wet-nurse. So she disappeared with him for a while. Then the man sought his son from the wet-nurse whom he had given his son to. So she confessed that she had contracted it out, and confessed of the capture of his son, and that she had handed him over to another wet-nurse. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon her is the wergild (blood money), or she comes up with him'.

Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who employed a wet-nurse, so she disappeared with his son for years. Then she came with him, but his mother denied him, and her family claimed that they do not recognize him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon her. The wet-nurse is trustworthy.'

I got married in Medina, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'How do you find her?' I said, 'Whatever good a man may find in a woman, I have found it in her — but she betrayed me.' So he said: 'And what is it?' I said, 'She gave birth to a girl.' He said: 'Perhaps you disliked her.' Verily, Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: 'your parents and your children — you know not which of them is nearer to you in benefit.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was a father of daughters.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad al-Wasiti, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, my father Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to grant him a daughter who would weep over him and lament him after his passing.

Jarud said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have daughters.' So he said: 'Perhaps you are wishing for their deaths. Know that if you wish for their deaths and they die, you will not be rewarded, and you will meet God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day you encounter Him, while you are a disobedient one.'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How excellent are the daughters as children — kind, serving, caring, blessed, loving.'

A man came while he was in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he was informed of a newborn that had arrived for him. The face of the man changed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'Nothing.' He said, 'Speak.' He said, 'I went out while the woman was in labour, and I was informed that she had given birth to a girl.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'The earth will carry her, the sky will shade her, God will provide for her, and she is a fragrant flower you will smell.'

Whoever has a daughter is burdened; and whoever has two daughters — 'O, help from Allah!'; and whoever has three, jihad and every hardship is lifted from him; and whoever has four — O servants of God, help him! O servants of God, lend to him! O servants of God, have mercy on him! And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Abu Ayyub Sulayman ibn Muqbil al-Mada'ini, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed God, Blessed and Exalted, is more compassionate toward females than toward males; and there is no man who brings joy to a woman with whom he has a close relationship, except that God the Exalted will make him happy on the Day of Resurrection.
The daughters are hasanat (good deeds/blessings), and the sons are ni'mah (a bounty). For indeed, one is rewarded for the hasanat, but one is questioned about the ni'mah.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-'Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his father, from al-Jarud ibn al-Mundhir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'It has reached me that a daughter has been born unto you, yet it has displeased you — but what you have from her is a fragrant flower to smell, and her sustenance has already been provided for you, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was a father of daughters.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever supports three daughters or three sisters, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and two?' He said, 'And two.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and one?' He said, 'And one.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The sons are a bounties (or delight), and the daughters are good deeds (or blessings), and Allah will ask about the bounties and will reward for the good deeds.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman gave birth from adultery (zina). Should I take her as a wet-nurse?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not take her as a wet-nurse, nor her daughter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the employment (of wet-nurses) of the Magian, so he said: No, but (the wet-nurses of) the People of the Book.
And from him, from Al-Kahili, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When they breast-feed for you, then forbid them from drinking wine.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible for a man that the Jewish woman, the Christian woman, and the polytheist woman breastfeed him?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem,' and he said, 'Prevent them from drinking wine.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The milk of the Jewish woman, and the Christian woman, and the Magian woman is more beloved to me than the milk of the one born of adultery. A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a slave of mine who leapt upon a slave girl of mine, so he impregnated her. So she gave birth, and we were in need of her milk. So if I permitted them what they had done, is her milk good? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Jameel ibn Darraj, and Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who has a servant (slave) who has been immoral, so we need her milk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Order her to give permission (for sexual relations), the milk will be good (permissible/clean).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not employ foolish wet-nurses, for the milk affects [the child], and the boy is drawn to the milk, meaning to the wet-nurse with regards to frivolity and foolishness.'

Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Do not employ foolish wet-nurses, for the milk overcomes the natures.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not employ foolish wet-nurses, for the child grows upon it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Consider whom you breastfeed your children with, for the child grows upon it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amari ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a woman who gave birth from adultery, is it permissible to breastfeed by her milk? He said: It is not permissible, nor the milk of her daughter who was born from the adultery.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Haytham, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Breast-feed your child with the milk of the good (women), and beware of the bad (fornicatress), for the milk indeed transmits (qualities/traits).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Rabi', from Fuzayl, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Be with the wet-nurses who have clear milk, for the milk transmits [kinship].

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Sa'id ibn Yasar from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not hire a Zoroastrian woman for breastfeeding your child, but hire for him a Jewish or Christian woman, and they must not drink wine and you must prevent them from doing so.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban, from Fazl Abu al-Abbas, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is the man more deserving of his child, or the woman?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the man. So if the woman says to her husband who divorced her, I will breastfeed my son for a wage similar to what you would find [paid] to the one who would breastfeed him,' then she is more deserving of it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces his wife while she is pregnant, he must spend upon her until she gives birth to her child; and when she gives birth, he gives her her recompense (for breastfeeding), and he should not harm her, except if he finds someone who is cheaper in recompense than her. So if she is pleased with that recompense, she is more rightful with her son until she weans him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from the one who mentioned it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who divorces his wife, and between the two of them is a child, which of the two is more rightful with the child? He (peace be upon him) said: The woman is more rightful with the child so long as she does not marry (again).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: And the mothers should suckle their children. He (peace be upon him) said: As long as the child is in the stage of breastfeeding, he is between the two parents with equal right. So when he is weaned, the father has more right to him than the mother. So when the father dies, the mother has more right to him than the agnates (relatives). If the father finds someone to breastfeed him for four dirhams, and the mother says, 'I will not breastfeed him except for five dirhams,' then he has the right to take him from her. However, it is better for him and more gentle with the child if he leaves him with his mother.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a free woman who married a slave, and he fathered children for her. Then he divorced her, so she did not stay with her children, and she remarried. When the news reached the slave that she had remarried, he wanted to take his children from her and said, 'I am more rightful with them than you, if you have remarried.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the slave to take her children from her, even if she remarried, until he is freed; she is more rightful with her children than him as long as he is a slave. So when he is freed, then he is more rightful with them than her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Madaini, from A'iz ibn Habib al-Baya' al-Harawi, from Isa ibn Zayd, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The boy is circumcised at seven years, and is commanded to perform the Prayer at nine years, and they are separated in their beds at ten years, and he experiences seminal emission at fourteen years, and the end of his height growth is at twenty-two years, and the end of his intellect is at twenty-eight years, except for those with experience.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Darir from Hammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The child grows every year by four fingers, by his own fingers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), said: The boy does not become capable of impregnation until his breasts are rounded and the smell of his armpits rises.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Leave your son to play for seven years, and impose yourself (upon him) for seven. So if he succeeds (fine), or else he is from the ones who have no good in them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Respite your child until he reaches six years; then attach him to yourself for seven years, so discipline him with your discipline. So if he accepts and is correct, or else let him go.

Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, raising it, said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Rasool Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Teach your children swimming and archery.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from a man, from Jameel ibn Darraj and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Hasten to teach your children the Hadith before the Murji'ah spoil it to them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Separation is made between the boys and the women in the beds when they reach ten years of age.

And by this chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: We order the children to combine the first two prayers (Dhuhr and Asr) and the last two prayers (Maghrib and Isha), as long as they remain in a state of ablution, before they become occupied.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Discipline the orphan with what you discipline your child with, and strike him with what you strike your child with.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Durust, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of this son of mine?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Improve his name, and his discipline, and place him in a good position.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said: Dawud ibn Zurbi complained of his son to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding what he had spoiled for him. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Reform him. For what is a hundred thousand compared to what Allah has favored you with in him?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah have mercy upon the parents who support their children in their righteousness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Asr with the people, so he shortened the two final cycles. When he finished, the people said to him, 'Did something happen during the prayer?' He said, 'And what is that?' They said, 'You shortened the two final cycles.' So he said to them, 'Did you not hear the child crying?'

From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Wasiti, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It necessitates the parents from the disloyalty for their children, what necessitates the child to them both from being disloyal to them'.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Fazala ibn Ayoub, from Al-Sakuni, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was gloomy and distressed, so he said to me: 'O Sakuni, from what is your gloom?' I said, 'A daughter has been born to me.' He said: 'O Sakuni, upon the earth is her weight (to carry), and upon Allah is her sustenance. She will live outside your lifespan and eat from other than your sustenance.' So, by Allah, he comforted me. He said to me, 'What have you named her?' I said, 'Fatima.' He said, 'Aah! Aah!' Then he placed his hand on his forehead and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The right of a child upon its parent, if it is male, is that he respects his mother, approves of his name, teaches him the Book of Allah, purifies him, and teaches him swimming. And if it is female, he respects her mother, approves of her name, teaches her Surah Al-Nur, does not teach her Surah Yusuf, does not keep her in the chambers, and hastens her release to the house of her husband.' As for if you name her Fatima, do not insult her, do not curse her, and do not hit her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever kisses his child, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, writes for him a good deed; and whoever makes him happy, Allah will make him happy on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever teaches him the Quran, he will be called by the title of the two parents, so they will be clothed with two garments, from whose light the faces of the people of Paradise will shine.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Talib, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man from the Ansar asked him, 'To whom shall I be righteous?' He said, 'Your parents.' He said, 'They have passed away.' He said, 'Be righteous with your children.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Bajali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Love the children and be merciful to them, and when you promise them something, fulfill it for them, for they do not know except that you are sustaining them.'
Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameel, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who has a child, aspires.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah is merciful to the servant due to the intensity of his love for his child.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Yunus ibn Ribat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah have mercy on the one who assists his child in his righteousness.' I said, 'How does he assist him in his righteousness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He accepts what is easy for him and overlooks what is difficult for him, and he does not burden him nor is he awkward with him. So there is nothing between it and between one coming in a limit from the limits of Infidelity, except that one enters into disloyalty, or cutting off of a relationship.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Paradise is pleasant, Allah made it pleasant and aromatised its winds. Its wind is found from a travel distance of a thousand years, but he who is disloyal (to his parents), nor a cutter off of a relationship, nor a relaxer of the trousers (an adulterer), a snobbish one, will not find its wind.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf Al-Azdi, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I have not kissed a child at all.' So when he turned away, the Messenger of Allah said, 'This man, in my presence, is from the inhabitants of the Fire.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Kulayb al-Saydawi, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you promise the children, fulfill it for them, for they view you as the ones who sustain them. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not angered for anything like His anger for the women and the children.'
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The child is a trial (fitna).

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub from Khaleel ibn Amr al-Yashkuri from Jameel ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: When the boy is one with cloudy testicular fluid, small of the penis, and relaxed in gaze, he is one from whom goodness is hoped and his evil is secured. And when the boy is one with hard testicular fluid, large of the penis, and sharp in gaze, he is one from whom goodness is not hoped and his evil is secured.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Abu Saeed al-Shami, who said: Salih ibn Uqba informed me, saying: I heard Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) say: It is recommended to involve the child in hard work during his young age so that he becomes forbearing in his old age. Then he said: It is not befitting except if it happens like this.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad Al-Nawfaly, from the offspring of Nawfal ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: He informed me, Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isa from Abdullah al-Umari from his father from his grandfather who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the illness that befalls the child, he said: It is an expiation for his parents.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The child lives for six months, and for seven months, and for nine months, but does not live for eight months.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the maximum limit of pregnancy with the child in its mother's belly, how long is it? For the people say, 'Perhaps it remains in her belly for years.' So he said: 'They are lying! The maximum limit of pregnancy is nine months, not exceeding a moment; and if it were to exceed an hour, it would kill its mother before he comes out.'
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hajjal, from Tha'laba, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The midwife is trusted.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Hamdan ibn Ishaq, who said: I had a son, and gallstones would afflict him. So it was said to me, 'There is no cure for him except that you perform surgery (batth).' So I performed surgery, and he died. So the Shia said, 'You participated in the blood of your son.' He said, 'So I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him), and he signed: O Ahmad! There is nothing upon you regarding what you did. Rather, you sought the medicine, and his time of death was due to what you did.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When the child reaches four months, perform cupping on him every month in the fovea (hollow of the neck/back), for it dries up his saliva and lowers the heat from his head and body.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from one of his companions who said: A man had two boys in one womb, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) congratulated him, then said: 'Which of the two is the elder?' He said: 'The one who came out first.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who came out last is the elder. Do you not know that she was pregnant with that one first, and this one entered upon that one, so it was not possible for him to come out until this one came out? So the one who comes out last is the elder of the two.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindy, from Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Khazzaz, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whenever there is a delay in the birth of a child for any of you, let him say: 'O Allah! Do not leave me alone while You are the Best of Inheritors, isolated and frightened, so that my gratitude falls short of my reflection. Rather, grant me a truthful posterity — males and females — through whom I find comfort from loneliness and tranquility from isolation, and I thank You for the completion of the blessing. O Endower! O Magnificent! O Exalted One!' 'Then grant me, in every good health, gratitude until You bring me through it to Your pleasure, in truthful speech, fulfillment of trusts, and faithfulness to the covenant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from al-Harith al-Nasri who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I am from a family that has become extinct and there is no child for me.' He said: 'Supplicate while you are in prostration:' O Lord! Grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me. O Lord! Grant me from Yourself good offspring; indeed You are the All-Hearing of supplication. O Lord! Do not leave me alone, and You are the Best of inheritors. He said: 'So I did it, and there were born unto me Ali and al-Husayn.'

Whoever desires that a pregnancy occur for him, let him pray two rak'ahs after the Friday prayer, prolonging the ruku' and sujud in both. Then he should say: 'O Allah, I ask You with what Zakariyya asked You: O Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the Best of inheritors. O Allah, grant me from Your presence good offspring; indeed You are the Hearer of supplication.' 'O Allah, by Your Name I have made her permissible to me, and in Your trust I have taken her. So if You have decreed a child in her womb, make him a blessed, pure boy, and do not give Satan any share or portion in him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions who said: Al-Abrash al-Kalbi complained to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that no child was being born to him. So he said to him (AS): 'Teach me something.' He (AS) said: 'Seek forgiveness of God during every day or every night one hundred times.' For God says: 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord, surely He is the Most Forgiving — up to His words: And He will aid you with wealth and sons.'

went to visit Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, but the permission to see him was delayed until he became distressed. Hisham had a gatekeeper who was wealthy in worldly goods but had no children. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) approached the gatekeeper and said: 'Is there something with you by which you could bring me to Hisham, and I will teach you a supplication by which you will have children?' He said: 'Yes.' So he brought him to Hisham and fulfilled all of his needs. He said: When he had finished, the gatekeeper said to him: 'May I be your ransom! The supplication you mentioned to me?' He said to him: 'Yes — say each day, in the morning and the evening, "Glory be to God" seventy times, seek forgiveness ten times, glorify nine times, and conclude the tenth with seeking forgiveness. Then recite the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic: "Ask forgiveness of your Lord, surely He is Most Forgiving. He will send the sky upon you in abundance. And will aid you with wealth and sons, and will make for you gardens, and will make for you rivers." [Quran 71:10-12] The gatekeeper recited it and was blessed with abundant offspring. And after that, he maintained connection with Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both). Sulayman said: So I recited it too — I had married a cousin of mine and a child had been delayed from her — and I taught it to my wife and was blessed with a child. The woman claimed that whenever she desired to become pregnant, she would become pregnant when she recited it. And I taught it to more than one person among the Hashimites who had not been having children, and they were blessed with many children. And praise be to God.

A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'No children are being born for me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord during the pre-dawn time, one hundred times. And if you forget it, then fulfill it (make it up).'

And from him, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man complained to him that no children were being born for him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'When you have intercourse, then say: O Allah, if You grant me a male, I shall name him Muhammad.' He said: So he did that, and he was granted (a son).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq, from one of our companions, from Abu Ubayda, who said: Sixty years came upon me with no children born for me. So I performed hajj and entered upon Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) and complained to him of that. He said to me: 'Has there truly never been a birth for you?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'When you return to Iraq, marry a woman, and do not worry if she happens to be of poor appearance.' I said: 'And what is the poor appearance?' He said: 'A woman in whom there is ugliness, for they have more children. And supplicate with this supplication, for I hope that God will grant you males and females.' And the supplication is: O God, do not leave me alone, solitary and fearful, so that my gratitude would fall short of my contemplation. Rather, grant me companionship and a righteous posterity — males and females — through whom I find rest from my loneliness and find comfort from my isolation, and I thank You for the completion of Your blessing. O Bestower! O Magnificent One! O Granter! Grant me good in every circumstance until You bring me to the ultimate of Your pleasure with me — in truthfulness of speech, fulfillment of trust, and loyalty to the covenant.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Rashid who said: Hisham ibn Ibrahim narrated to me that he complained to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) of his illness and that no children were born to him. So he (the Imam) commanded him to raise his voice with the adhan in his house. He (Hisham) said: So I did it, and God removed my illness from me, and my children became abundant. Muhammad ibn Rashid said: I was perpetually afflicted with illness, never free from it — myself, a group of my servants, and my family — to the extent that I used to remain alone with no one to serve me. So when I heard that from Hisham, I acted upon it. And God removed the illnesses from me and from my family. And all praise is due to God.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man from the people of Khurasan in al-Rabadhah said to him: 'May I be your ransom, I have not been granted a child.' So he said to him: 'When you return to your land and intend to go to your wife, so recite when you intend that.' The one with the whale (Yunus), when he went away in anger, so he thought that We had no Power over him, so he called out in the darkness: There is no god but You, Glory be to You; surely I am from the unjust ones. Up to three verses, so you will be granted a child, God willing.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: No child had been born to me at all, and I went out to Makkah and I had no son. A person met me and gave me the good news of a boy. So I passed by and entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in Al-Madina. When I came to be in his presence, he said to me: 'How are you, and how is your son?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I went out and I had no son. A neighbor of mine met me and said to me: A boy has been born to you.' He smiled, then said: 'Have you named him?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Name him Ali, for my father, whenever a delay occurred with one of his slave girls, would say to her: O So-and-so, intend (for him) Ali, so it would not be long before she would become pregnant and give birth to a boy.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When you desire a child, say during copulation: 'O Allah, grant me a child and make him pious, with no excess or deficiency in his creation, and make his end result good.'

Whenever one of you has a pregnancy with a woman and four months have passed over her, let him face her toward the Qiblah and let him recite Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), and let him strike upon her side and let him say: 'O Allah, I have named him Muhammad.' Thus it will make him a boy. Then if he is faithful to the name, Allah will bless him in it; and if he retracts from the name, the choice will belong to Allah therein — if He wills, He takes him (back), and if He wills, He leaves him.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id who said: I and Ibn Ghaylan al-Madaini went to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him). Ibn Ghaylan said to him: 'May God keep you well! It has reached me that whoever has a pregnancy and intends to name [the child] Muhammad, a boy will be born for him.' He (the Imam) said: 'Whoever has a pregnancy and intends to name him Ali, a boy will be born for him.' Then he said: 'Ali [is] Muhammad and Muhammad [is] Ali — they are one thing.' He (Ibn Ghaylan) said: 'May God keep you well! I have left my wife behind and she is pregnant. Supplicate to God that He make [the child] a boy.' So he (the Imam) bowed his head toward the ground for a long time, then raised his head and said to him: 'Name him Ali, for it will be a prolongation of his life.' So we entered Mecca, and a letter came to us from al-Mada'in that a boy had been born for him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: 'There is not a man for whom a pregnancy is carried, and he intends to name him Muhammad, except that it will always be a male — God Willing.' And he said: 'Over here are three, all of them named Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad.' And he (the narrator) said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in another hadith: He should take her hand and face her toward the qiblah during the fourth month, and he should say: "O Allah, I have named him Muhammad." There would be born unto him a boy, and if he changes his name, he (the child) would be taken from him.'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever has a pregnant wife and intends to name [the child] Muhammad or Ali, a boy will be born for him.'

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'formed and unformed' [22:5]. So he said: 'The formed ones are the primordial particles (al-dharr) whom God created in the loins of Adam (peace be upon him), taking the Covenant from them. Then He caused them to flow through the loins of men and the wombs of women, and they are the ones who come out into the world until they are questioned about the Covenant. As for His saying 'and unformed,' they are every soul whom God did not create in the loins of Adam (peace be upon him) when He created the particles and took the Covenant from them. They are the sperms resulting from coitus interruptus, and the miscarriage before the Spirit, life, and permanence are blown into it.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hareez, from the one who mentioned it, from one of the two (peace be upon them both) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'He knows what every female bears, and that of which the wombs fall short of completion and that in which they increase' He said: 'The decrease is every pregnancy which is less than nine months, and the increase is everything which exceeds nine months. So every time a woman sees pure blood during her pregnancy, she increases by the number of days during which she saw blood in her pregnancy.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Verily, the nutfa (sperm-drop) remains in the womb for forty days, then it becomes a 'alaqa (clot) for forty days, then it becomes a mudgha (morsel of flesh) for forty days. When four months are complete, God dispatches two creative angels. They say: 'O Lord! What will You create — male or female?' So they are commanded. Then they say: 'O Lord! Wretched or happy?' So they are commanded. Then they say: 'O Lord! What is its appointed term, and what is its provision?' — and everything of its condition, and he enumerated several such things — and they write down the covenant between its two eyes. Then when God completes the appointed term for it, God sends an angel who rebukes it with a severe rebuke, and it comes out having forgotten the covenant. Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said: I said to him: Is it permissible to supplicate God so that He changes a female to a male, and a male to a female? He said: God does whatever He wills.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whenever God, Mighty and Majestic, intends to create the seed (nutfa) regarding which He took the covenant in the loins of Adam — or whatever He wills concerning it — and to place it in the womb, He stirs the man toward intercourse, and He reveals to the womb: 'Open your door so that My creation may enter you, and My irrevocable decree and My power [may be carried out].' So the womb opens its door, and the seed reaches the womb and circulates within it for forty days. Then it becomes a clot ('alaqa) for forty days. Then it becomes a lump (mudgha) for forty days. Then it becomes flesh through which intertwined veins run. Then God sends two creative angels who create in the wombs whatever God wills. They enter into the belly of the woman through the woman's mouth, and reach the womb, in which is the ancient spirit that has been transferred through the loins of men and the wombs of women. They breathe into it the spirit of life and continuity, and they cleave open for it hearing, sight, and all the limbs, and everything in the belly, by God's permission. Then God reveals to the two angels: 'Write upon him My decree and My predestination and My binding command, and stipulate for Me the possibility of change (bada') in what you write.' They say: 'O Lord! What shall we write?' So God reveals to them both: 'Raise your heads toward the head of his mother.' They raise their heads, and the Tablet is striking the forehead of his mother. They look into it and find in the Tablet his image, his adornment, his appointed term, and his covenant — whether he is wretched or fortunate — and all his affairs. He said: So one of them dictates to his companion, and they both write down all that is in the Tablet, and stipulate the possibility of change (bada') in what they write. Then they seal the document and place it between his eyes. Then they stand him upright in the belly of his mother. He said: Perhaps he is obstinate and turns over — and that happens only with every obstinate or rebellious one. When the time comes for the child to emerge, complete or incomplete, God, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to the womb: 'Open your door so that My creature may come out to My earth and My command may be

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about creation. He said: When God, Blessed and Exalted, created the creatures from clay, He distributed them like the casting of divination arrows. He brought forth the Muslim and made him fortunate, and made the disbeliever miserable. Then when the seed (sperm) falls, the angels receive it and give it form, then they say: O Lord, male or female? The Lord — Majestic is His majesty — says: whichever He wills. And they both say: Blessed is God, the Best of Creators! Then it is placed in her womb and circulates for nine days through every vein and joint. The womb has three locks: a lock at its upper part adjacent to the top of the navel from the right side, another lock at its middle, and another lock at the lower part of the womb. After nine days it is placed in the upper lock and remains there for three months; during this time the woman is affected by nausea and vomiting. Then it descends to the middle lock and remains there for three months; the child's navel is the confluence of veins, and all the woman's veins lead from it, through which its food and drink enter from those veins. Then it descends to the lower lock and remains there for three months — making nine months in all. Then the woman goes into labor; with each contraction, a vein is severed from the child's navel, and the pain from this strikes her, while the child's hand is upon its navel until it falls to the ground with its hand outstretched; from that point onward, its sustenance comes through its mouth.

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man supplicates for a pregnant woman that God may make what is in her womb a well-formed male.' He said: 'He may supplicate within the time between it and four months, for it is a sperm-drop for forty nights, a clot for forty nights, and a lump of flesh for forty nights — that completes four months.' Then God sends two creative angels, and they say: 'O Lord! What shall we create — a male or a female, miserable or fortunate?' So that is told to them. Then they say: 'O Lord! What is its sustenance, what is its term, and what is its duration?' So that is told to them. And its covenant is between its eyes — it gazes upon it. And it does not cease to be upright in the belly of its mother until, when its birth approaches, God Mighty and Majestic sends an angel to it. He rebukes it with a rebuke, so it comes out and forgets the covenant.

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: When the seed (nutfa) falls into the womb, it settles in it for forty days, and it becomes a clinging clot ('alaqa) for forty days, and it becomes a lump of flesh (mudgha) for forty days. Then God sends two creating angels, and it is said to both of them: Create as God wills, male or female; form it, and write its appointed term, its sustenance, its death, and whether it is miserable or fortunate; and write for God the covenant which He took from it in the realm of particles, between its eyes. So when its exit from the belly of its mother draws near, God sends to it an angel called Zajir (the Rebuker). He rebukes it with a rebuke, and it panics in great fright, and forgets the covenant, and falls to the ground crying from the rebuke of the angel.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ismail ibn Umar, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed for the womb there are four pathways; whichever pathway the fluid travels through, from it can come one child, and two, and three, and four; and to one pathway there cannot be more than one (at a time).

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it (mursal), from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created four containers for the womb. So whatever was in the first is (similar to) the father, and whatever was in the second is (similar to) the mother, and whatever was in the third is (similar to) the paternal uncles, and whatever was in the fourth is (similar to) the maternal uncles.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn, from Murazim, from his brother who said: A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A boy has been born to me.' So he said: 'May Allah grant you thanking the Bestower, and bless you in the gift, and may he reach adulthood, and may Allah grant you his righteousness.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Barza al-Aslami who said: A child was born to al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and the Quraysh came to him and said: 'Congratulations for the horse-rider!' So he said: 'And what is this as a saying? Say instead: May you have thanked the Endower, and may blessing be upon you in the endowed (child), and may God bring him to his full maturity, and grant you (to witness) his righteousness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man congratulated another man who had been blessed with a son, saying: 'Congratulations to you — may he become a horseman!' So al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What knowledge do you have that he will be a horseman or a foot-soldier?' The man said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Then what should I say?' He said: 'Say: You have given thanks to the Bestower, and may blessings be upon you in the endowment (the child), and may he reach full maturity, and may you be graced with his righteousness.'

A number of our companions informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamila, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a man and said: 'What did you do with your wife?' He said: 'I divorced her, O Messenger of God.' He asked: 'Without any wrongdoing (on her part)?' He said: 'Without any wrongdoing.' Then [the narrator] said: The man got married again. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him and said: 'You got married?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said to him some time after: 'What did you do with your wife?' He said: 'I divorced her.' He asked: 'Without any wrongdoing?' He said: 'Without any wrongdoing.' Then the man got married again. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him and said: 'You got married?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said to him some time after: 'What did you do with your wife?' He said: 'I divorced her.' He asked: 'Without any wrongdoing?' He said: 'Without any wrongdoing.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed God — Mighty and Majestic — hates, or curses, every taster (dhawwaq) from among the men and every taster (dhawwaqah) from among the women.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one (narrator), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'There is nothing among the things that God, Mighty and Majestic, has made permissible that is more hateful to Him than divorce, and indeed God hates the frequent divorcer, al-dhawwaq (the taster).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the house in which there is a wedding, and hates the house in which there is a divorce. And there is nothing more hateful to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than divorce.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, hates every frequent divorcer, the taster.

And by his chain of narration, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that Abu Ayyub intends to divorce his wife. So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, the divorce of the mother of Ayyub is a wrongdoing.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife three times in one sitting, or more, while she was pure (from menstruation). He said: 'It is one (divorce).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the one who divorces [his wife] during a state of purity, in one sitting, three [times]. He said: 'It is one [divorce].'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh, all together, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Baseer al-Asadi and Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halbi and Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Divorcing three times in one sitting, if it was upon a state of purity, then it is one (divorce), and if it was not upon purity, then it is nothing.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Ali ibn Khalid from Abdul Karim ibn Amr from Amr ibn al-Bara' said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Our companions are saying that if a man divorces a woman once or a hundred times, it is only one (divorce). And it had reached us from you and from your forefathers (peace be upon them) that they were saying: if he divorces once or a hundred times, it is only one.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is as it has reached you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife during a period of purity, without sexual intercourse, and called one man as a witness on that day, then waited for five days, then called another [man as a witness]. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is only ordered to have both [witnesses] together.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man whose wife had become pure from her menstruation, so he said, 'So-and-so woman is divorced,' and a group was listening to his speech, and he did not tell them, 'Bear witness.' Has the divorce taken effect upon her? He said, 'Yes, it is a witnessing; otherwise, would she be left hanging (in uncertainty)?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who had a wife who had become pure from her menstruation, so he went to a group and said, 'So-and-so woman is divorced.' Does the divorce occur upon her, and he did not say to them, 'Bear witness'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Ali, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about a man whose wife had become pure from her menstruation, so he said, 'So-and-so woman is divorced,' and a group was listening to his speech, and he did not say to them, 'Bear witness.' Does the divorce occur upon her? He said: 'Yes, this is witnessing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one who reverts (to his wife) and did not keep witnesses, he said: 'Witnessing is more beloved to me, and I do not see any problem with what he has done'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He should have two men bear witness when he divorces and when he reverts (to her). If he is ignorant (of the need for witnesses), so he copulates with her, let him keep witnesses now upon what he has done, and she is his wife. So if he had not kept witnesses when he divorced her, his divorce is nothing.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Divorce does not occur without witnesses, and revocation (of divorce) without witnesses is a valid revocation, but it is better to have witnesses afterwards, for that is preferable.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who divorced his wife once, then took her back before her waiting period expired, and did not bear witness to his taking her back. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is his wife as long as her waiting period has not expired, and it was befitting for him to bear witness to his taking her back. So if he was ignorant of that, let him bear witness when he knows, and I do not see any harm in what he has done.
