And indeed, many of the people, if they wanted proof for their marriages today, would not find anyone to establish the testimony regarding their matter, and I do not see any harm in what he has done, and if he bears witness, that is better.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife once. He said: 'He has the right to take her back as long as the waiting period has not expired.' I said: 'So if he does not keep witnesses for his taking her back?' He said: 'So let him keep witnesses.' I said: 'So if he is oblivious to that?' He said: 'So let him keep witnesses when he remembers, and the witnesses were made for the sake of inheritance.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The reversion (raj'ah) is the copulation, or else, it is only one (divorce).

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who divorces his wife: 'It is for him that he reverts [to her without a new contract].' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He cannot give the final divorce until he touches her [consummates the marriage with her].'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bukeyr who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: When a man divorces his wife, and two just witnesses witness it prior to her waiting period, so it is not for him that he should divorce her until she has completed her waiting period, except if he reverts to her.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife during a period of purity, without sexual intercourse, then revives her during that same day, then divorces her again, so that three divorces are completed from him during one period of purity. He said: 'He acted contrary to the Sunnah.' I said: 'So it is not befitting for him, when he revives her, to divorce her except during a period of purity?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Until he has sexual intercourse with her?' He said: 'Yes.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: The reversion (raj'ah) is with sexual intercourse, and otherwise, it is only one (divorce).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who claimed against her husband that he had divorced her with a single divorce, a valid divorce of the waiting period, meaning during purity from non-coitus, and witnesses testified for her regarding that. Then the husband denied it afterwards. So he (peace be upon him) said: If his denial of the divorce was before the completion of the waiting period, then his denial of the divorce is a revocation (raj'ah) for her. And if he denied the divorce after the completion of the waiting period, then it is upon the Imam (peace be upon him) to separate them after the testimony of the witnesses, after making him swear an oath that his denial of the divorce was after the completion of the waiting period, and he would be one of the proposers (from those who propose marriage).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Al-Marzuban who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who said to his wife, 'Observe your waiting period, for I have freed your way,' then he bore witness to her reversion (raj'a) after a few days, then remained absent from her before he copulated with her until months passed after the waiting period, or more. So how would you order him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he bore witness to his reversion, so she is his wife.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who divorces his wife and calls two witnesses, then he witnesses upon her reversion secretly from her, and those witnesses conceal it, so the woman does not know about the reversion until her waiting period has passed. He (peace be upon him) said: The woman has a choice; if she wishes, she keeps her husband, and if she wishes, she chooses otherwise. And if she marries before she knows about the reversion which her husband witnessed upon, then there is no claim for the one who divorced her, and her last husband is more rightful with her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the divorce that results in her not being permissible for him unless she marries another husband. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I inform you of what I did with a woman who was with me, and I intended to divorce her. So I left her until when she menstruated and was pure, I divorced her without sexual intercourse, and I bore witness upon that with two witnesses. Then I left her until when she was about to complete her waiting period, I reverted back to her and had sexual intercourse with her, and I left her until when she menstruated and was pure. Then I divorced her upon purity without sexual intercourse with two witnesses. Then I left her until when it was before her waiting period completed, I reverted back to her and had sexual intercourse with her. Until when she menstruated and was pure, I divorced her upon purity without sexual intercourse with witnesses; and I did that with her because there was no need for me with her.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and Ali ibn Khalid, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'The woman who is not permissible for her husband until she marries another husband.' He said: 'She is the one who is divorced, then reverted to, then divorced, then reverted to, then divorced. So she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband.' And he said: 'The reversion is with copulation, or else, it is only one (divorce).'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The woman who is not permissible for her husband until she marries another husband.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is the one who is divorced, then reverted to, then divorced, then reverted to, then divorced for the third time, so she is the one who is not permissible for her husband until she marries another husband, and he tastes her honey.'

Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding the man who divorces his wife with a single divorce, then revives her after the expiration of her waiting period. So when he divorces her for the third time, she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband. So when another one marries her, and does not copulate with her, and divorces her, or dies from her, she would (still) not be permissible for her first husband until another (husband) tastes her honey.

Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman given three divorces, she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband and he tastes her honey.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said: I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'A man divorced his wife with the divorce by which she becomes not permissible to him until she marries another husband. So she married a boy who had not yet reached puberty (bed-wet). He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, [she is not permissible] until he reaches adulthood.' So I wrote to him, 'What is the limit of adulthood?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which obligates the legal penalties (Hudud) upon the believers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorced his wife, then did not revert to her until she had three menstrual periods, then he married her, then divorced her, and left her until she had three menstrual periods without him reverting to her (meaning touching her). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can marry her forever, as long as he does not revert to her and touch her.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Safwan from Rifa'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife until she became irrevocably divorced from him and her waiting period ended, then she married another husband, so he divorced her as well, then her first husband married her again. Does that demolish the first divorce? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Muawiya ibn Hukaym from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira said: I asked Abdullah ibn Bukayr about a man who divorced his wife once, then left her until she became irrevocably divorced from him, then he married her. He said: 'She is with him as she was in the marriage.' I said to him, 'For the report of Rifah states: if there is a husband between them.' So Abdullah said to me, 'This is a husband, and this is from what Allah has granted of opinion.' And when he divorces her once, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, then she marries another husband. Then her husband divorces her, so she marries her former husband, so she is with him accepted as she used to be. I said to Abdullah, 'With whose report is this?' So he said, 'This is from what Allah has granted.' Muawiya ibn Hukaym said: 'Our companions narrated from Rifah ibn Musa that the husband demolishes the first divorce. So if he marries her, she is with him accepted.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The third demolishes, and the first and the second do not.' And the report of Rifah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) is that which Ibn Bukayh argues by.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hajjaj al-Khashab, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was on a journey. So when he entered the city, he came with two witnesses, and when his wife met him at the door, he made them bear witness to his divorcing her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A divorce does not occur by it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man is absent from his wife for a year, or two years, or more, then returns and intends to divorce her, and she is menstruating, he leaves her until she becomes pure, then he divorces her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he he had a wife who astounded him and he loved her. So one morning he had divorced her, and was grieved because of that. So one of his companions said to him: 'May I be your ransom! Why did you divorce her?' So he said: 'Indeed I mentioned Ali (peace be upon him), and she belittled him. So I disliked that I should press an ember from the embers of Hell to my skin.'

There was a wife with me who practiced this matter (al-wilayah), and her father was likewise, and she was of evil character. So I abhorred divorcing her due to my recognition of her faith and the faith of her father. So I met Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), while I intended to ask him about divorcing her. So I said: May I be made a ransom for you! Indeed, for me there is a need to you, so permit me to ask you about it. So he said: Come to me tomorrow at the Zuhr prayer. He said: So when I had prayed the Zuhr, I came to him and found him having already prayed and seated. So I entered to him and sat before him. He began speaking to me first and said: O Khattab! My father had married me to a daughter of a paternal uncle of mine, and she was of evil character; and sometimes my father would lock the door upon me and upon her, hoping that I would meet her. So I would climb the wall and flee from her. So when my father passed away, I divorced her. So I said: Allah is Greatest! By Allah, He has answered me about my need without being asked.

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Khattab ibn Salama, who said: I went to him — meaning Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) — and I intended to complain to him about what I was enduring from my wife because of her bad character. But he spoke to me first and said: 'My father had once given me in marriage to a woman of bad character. So I complained of that to him, and he said to me: What prevents you from separating from her? God has placed that matter in your hands.' So I said to myself: 'He has relieved me.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: Three (types of people) have their supplication returned to them (unanswered): one of them is a man who supplicates against his wife while he is unjust to her, so it is said to him: 'Did We not place her matter in your hands?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) divorced fifty women. Then Ali (peace be upon him) stood in al-Kufah and said: 'O people of al-Kufah! Do not give your women in marriage to al-Hasan, for he is a man who divorces frequently.' Then a man stood up toward him and said: 'On the contrary, by God, we will surely give him in marriage, for he is the son of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) and the son of Fatimah (peace be upon her). If she pleases him, he keeps her; if he dislikes her, he divorces.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), he said: I heard him saying: 'Three kinds of people have their supplications returned to them unanswered. One of them is a man who prays against his wife while he is unjust to her, and it is said to him: Did We not place her affair in your hand?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There are five [women] whom the man can divorce in every state: the pregnant one, the one whom her husband has not had sexual relations with, the one whose husband is absent, the one who has not yet menstruated, and the one who has despaired of menstruation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with the divorce of five women in every state: the one from whom her husband is absent, the one who has not menstruated, the one with whom her husband has not had intercourse, the pregnant one, and the one who has despaired of menstruation.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah and Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Jameel from Ismail al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Five [types of women] can be divorced in every state: the pregnant, the one from whom her husband is absent, the one who has not yet menstruated, the one who has despaired of menstruation, and the one who has not been entered into (consummated). Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jameel from Ismail al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Bukayr, who said: I testify regarding Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that I heard him saying: 'The absentee divorces by the new moons and the months.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The absentee, when he intends to divorce her, should leave her for a month.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, and Husayn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The absentee, when he intends to divorce her, should leave her for a month.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was absent in another city, and he had two men bear witness to her divorce. Then he returned to her before the expiration of the waiting period (iddah) but did not bear witness to the reversion. Then he arrived at her after the expiration of the waiting period, and she had married another man. So he sent her a message saying: 'I had returned to you before the expiration of the waiting period, and I did not bear witness.' He (the narrator) said, 'So he (peace be upon him) said: There is no way for him to her, because he acknowledged the divorce and claimed the reversion without proof. Thus, there is no way for him to her. And for this reason, it is fitting for the one who divorces to bear witness, and for the one who reverts to bear witness to the reversion, just as he bore witness to the divorce. And if he had reached her before she married, he would have been a suitor among the suitors.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was absent and kept witnesses upon her divorce. Then he returned and stayed with the woman for months, not informing her of her divorce. Then the woman claimed pregnancy, so the man said, 'I have divorced you, and I kept witnesses upon your divorce.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The child is necessitated upon him, and his word is not accepted.'

Ali, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a man who has four wives, and he divorces one of them while he is absent from them? When is it permissible for him to marry?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'After nine months, and in it are two terms – the duration of menstruation and the duration of pregnancy.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the man who divorces his wife while he is absent. He said: His divorce is valid in every state, and his wife observes the waiting period from the day he divorces her.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah who said, 'I asked Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, 'When does the absentee divorce?' He said, 'Is-haq ibn 'Ammar narrated to me, or Is-haq ibn 'Ammar reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)' He said, 'When a month passes for him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahiyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said: One of our friends wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'With me is a woman I know. Her husband did something and fled from the country. Some of the wife's family followed the husband and said,
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The pregnant woman is divorced with one divorce.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (divorce), and her waiting period is the closest of the two terms.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabala and Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Jamil, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (revocation). So when she gives birth to what is in her belly, she is irrevocably divorced.
And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The pregnant woman is divorced with one divorce.

A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Jameel, from Ismail Al Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of a pregnant woman is one (revocation). So when she places what is in her belly, she has been irrevocably divorced from him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz, from Ayub ibn Nuh, all together from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The divorce of the pregnant woman is one [pronouncement], and her waiting period is that she gives birth to her burden, and it is the closer of the two periods.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the divorce of a pregnant woman, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'One [divorce], and her term is that she places her load (gives birth)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (revocation), and her waiting period is that she gives birth to her load, and it is the closer of the two periods.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the pregnant woman when her husband divorces her, and she gives birth to a miscarriage that is complete or incomplete, or she gives birth to a lump. He said: 'Everything she gives birth to, if it is evident that it is a pregnancy, complete or incomplete, then her waiting period has ended, even if it was a lump.'

And from him, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Imran al-Shafa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah al-Basri, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife while she was pregnant, and there were two (fetuses) in her womb. She gave birth to one, and one remained. He said: The divorce is established by the first one, and she is not permissible for the husbands until she gives birth to what is in her womb.

And from him, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the woman is divorced and she is pregnant, her term is that she gives birth to her pregnancy, and even if she gives birth immediately.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Mahboub from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz from Yazeed al-Kunasi who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the pregnant woman, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He divorces her once for the waiting period by the months, and the witnesses.' I said to him, 'So is it for him to revert back to her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and she is his wife.' I said, 'So if he reverts back to her and touches her, then intends to divorce her with another divorce?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He cannot divorce her until there pass by for her one month after him having touched her.' I said, 'So if he divorces her second (divorce), and keeps witnesses, then reverts back to her, and keeps witnesses upon his reversion, and touches her, then divorces her with the third divorce, and keeps witnesses upon divorcing her, with every waiting period being a month. Would there be manifested from him just as it is manifest from the divorced woman, upon the waiting period which she would not be Permissible for her husband until she marries another husband?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So what is her waiting period?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her waiting period is that she places what is in her belly, then she would be permitted for the marriage'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, so he said: 'She is irrevocably separated from him, and she may marry whomever she wishes from that very moment.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said: When the woman who has not been consummated is divorced, she becomes irrevocably divorced with one divorce.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, there is no waiting period upon her; she may marry from that very moment if she wishes, and one divorce makes her irrevocably divorced; and if he had stipulated a dower for her, she is entitled to half of what he stipulated.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, and Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them). Regarding a man who married a virgin woman, then divorced her before consummating the marriage with three divorces, one per month. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes irrevocably divorced from him at the first divorce, and the other two are superfluous, and he is a suitor who may marry her whenever she wishes and he wishes, with a new dower.' It was said to him (peace be upon him): 'Does he have the right to revert to her if he divorces her with one divorce before three months pass?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, he would have the right to revert to her if he had first consummated the marriage. As for before he consummates it, there is no reversion for him to her. She has become irrevocably divorced from him from the moment he divorces her.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Thabit ibn Sharih, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man marries a woman and divorces her before consummating the marriage, there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her, and she may marry whomever she wishes from that moment, and one divorce makes her irrevocably divorced. Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Salih ibn Khalid and Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Thabit ibn Sharih, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

Abu Al-Abbas Al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage with her, with one irrevocable divorce, she becomes separated from him, and she may marry immediately if she wishes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: The waiting period (iddah) is from the water.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), regarding the man who divorces the young girl who has not yet reached the age of bearing children, and he had consummated the marriage with her; and the woman who has despaired of menstruation, and her menstruation has ceased, so she cannot bear children. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no waiting period upon them, even if he had consummated the marriage with them both.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad ibn Usman, from the one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the young girl who does not menstruate like others, and the woman who has despaired of menstruation, he (peace be upon him) said: There is no waiting period upon both of them, even if they had been copulated with.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all together from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The woman the likes of whom do not get pregnant, there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three women may marry in every state: the one who has not yet menstruated, and the like of her who does not menstruate.' I said, 'And what is her limit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When less than nine years have come for her.' And the one who has not been entered into (consummated), and the one who has despaired of menstruation, and the like of her who does not menstruate.' I said, 'And what is her limit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When she is fifty years old.'

One of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Hakeem, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman who has despaired of menstruation: 'She is irrevocably divorced from him, and there is no waiting period for her'. And it has been reported as well that: 'Upon her is the waiting period when she has been slept with'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad narrated from Ibn Sama'ah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir who said: The waiting period of the girl who has not yet reached menstruation is three months, and of the one who has ceased menstruating is three months. Ibn Sama'ah would adhere to this and say: 'This applies to slave-girls, who do not require Istibra' if they have not reached menstruation.' As for free women, their ruling is in the Quran, where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you have doubts, their waiting period is three months; and those who do not menstruate." Mu'awiyah ibn Hukaym would say: 'There is no waiting period for them.' And the argument Ibn Sama'ah used is based on "if you have doubts," which only applies when there is doubt regarding whether they have despaired of menstruation or not. But if the limit has passed and the doubt is removed that the girl has not reached the limit, then there is no waiting period for them.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, all together, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The divorced woman, when she sees the blood of the third menstruation, has become irrevocably divorced from him.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Bukeyr, and Jameel Bin Darraj, and Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorced woman becomes irrevocably divorced (bayna'nah) at the first drop of the third menstruation. He said: I said, 'It has reached me that Rabi'ah al-Ra'y said, 'She becomes irrevocably divorced at the first drop.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He lied. It is not from his opinion. Rather, it is something that reached him from Ali (peace be upon him).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man divorces his wife.' He said, 'He is more rightful in revoking her as long as blood has not fallen from the third menstruation.'

And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: The divorced woman inherits and is inherited from until she sees the third blood. So when she sees it, then it is cut off.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'a from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Jameel ibn Darraj and Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Bukayr and Ja'far ibn Sama'a from Ibn Bukayr and Jameel, all of them from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The first blood she sees from the third menstruation, so she is irrevocably divorced from him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Zurara, similar to it. Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, I heard him saying: The divorced woman becomes irrevocably divorced at the first drop of blood in the final menstruation.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) regarding the man who divorces his wife, he said: 'He is more rightful with reverting back to her, for as long as the blood has not fallen regarding the third (menstruation)'.

From him, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I heard Rabi'at al-Ra'y saying: When she sees blood from the third menstruation, she is irrevocably divorced from him, and the period is only what is between the two menstruations,' and he claimed that he took this by his own opinion. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He lied! By my life, he did not say that by his own opinion, but he took it from Ali (peace be upon him).' He (the narrator) said, 'I said to him, 'And what did Ali (peace be upon him) say regarding it?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He (peace be upon him) used to say: When she sees blood from the third menstruation, her waiting period has ended, and there is no way for him upon her, and the period is only what is between the two menstruations, and it is not for her to marry until she performs the ritual bath from the third menstruation.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman when her husband divorces her, when does she become in control of herself? He said: When she sees the blood of the third menstruation, then she is in control of herself. I said: And if the blood hastens to her before the days of her period? He said: If the blood is before ten days, then he is in control of her, and it is from the menstruation from which she was purified; and if the blood is after the ten days, then it is from the third menstruation, and she is in control of herself.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from one of his companions (I think it was Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal or Ali ibn al-Hakam), from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who divorces his wife, when does she become irrevocably divorced from him? He said: When the blood emerges from the third menstruation, she controls herself. I said: So is it for her that she may marry in that state? He said: Yes, but she does not give herself over [to her husband] until she has purified from the blood.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, all from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Quroo (menses-free period) is what is between the two menstruations.
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Quroo is what is between the two menstruations.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Aqra' (menses-free period) are the pure ones.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for the divorced woman to go out except by the permission of her husband until her waiting period is completed, which is three quroos (pure periods), or three months if she does not menstruate.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The waiting period (Iddah) of the divorced woman is three pure periods (Quroo'), or three months if she does not menstruate.

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the divorced woman, where she waits. He (peace be upon him) said: In her house, she should not go out; and if she wants to visit, she goes out after midnight, and does not go out during the day, and it is not for her to perform Hajj until her waiting period has expired. And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one whose husband died, is she like that? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, and she performs Hajj if she wishes.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The divorced woman waits in her house and it is not befitting for her that she goes out until she has fulfilled her waiting period; and her waiting period is of three Quroos (pure periods), or three months, except if she happens to menstruate.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) about something from the divorce. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man divorces his wife with a divorce in which he has no control regarding the reversion, so she is irrevocably divorced from him the moment he divorces her, and she is in control of herself, and there is no way for him upon her, and she waits wherever she desires, and there is no expenses for her.' I said: 'Is not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Saying: Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they themselves go forth?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'But rather it Means by that who is divorced with a divorce after a divorce, so she is the one who should not be driven out nor go out until she is divorced by the third divorce. So when she is divorced with the third, so she is irrevocably divorced from him, and there is no expenses for her.' And the woman whom the man divorces with a divorce, then leaves her until her term is free, so this one as well should sit in the house of her husband, and for her is the expenses, and the dwelling until she fulfills her waiting period.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorced woman waits in her house, and it is not befitting for her husband to expel her, nor should she go out.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The divorced woman beautifies herself for her husband as long as he has the right of reversion (raj'ah) upon her, and he does not need permission to go to her.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ibn Ribat from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the divorced woman, where she should observe her waiting period, so he said: In the house of her husband.

From him, from Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) regarding the divorced woman. Where should she observe her waiting period? He said: In her house. If it is a revocable divorce (raj'ah) for him over her, it is not for him to expel her, nor for her to leave, until her waiting period (iddah) is completed.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, similar to it. Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them). Regarding the divorced woman, she should wait in her house and manifest her adornments for him, perhaps Allah may after that bring about a matter [of reunion].

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu al-Abbas, who said: It is not befitting for the divorced woman that she goes out except by the permission of her husband, until her waiting period is fulfilled by three quroo' (pure periods), or three months if she does not menstruate.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Jalal ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Al-'Ala' ibn Ra'ab from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: The divorced woman performs Hajj and testifies for the rights.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The divorced woman may apply kohl, dye her hair, use perfume, and wear whatever clothes she desires. Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Perhaps Allah will bring about after that a new situation; perhaps she will come to his mind, so he will remarry her.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfa, from Ma'mar ibn Ata' ibn Washeeka who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The people will not be correct regarding divorce except by the sword, and if I were to rule over them, I would refer them in it to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic.'

And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If I were appointed guardian over the people, I would surely teach them how it is proper for them to divorce. Then I would not have a man who had violated (the ruling) brought to me except that I would inflict pain upon his back. And whoever divorces contrary to the Sunnah shall be referred back to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, even if his nose is forced into the dust.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Umar ibn Ma'mar ibn Ata' ibn Washika, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The people will not be set right regarding divorce except by the sword, and if I were their guardian I would return them to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad said, and some of our companions mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (AS), and Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Abu Basir, from al-'Abd al-Salih (AS) that he said: 'If I were to take charge of the affairs of the people, I would teach them divorce, then no one who opposed would be brought to me except that I would cause him pain by striking.'

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'By God! If I owned anything from the affairs of the people, I would straighten them by the sword and the whip until they would be divorcing according to the waiting period, just as God, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they themselves go forth, unless they commit an open indecency.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her hurting the family of the man and her evil manners.'

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: who said: Al-Mamun asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they themselves go forth, unless they commit an open indecency He said: It means by the 'open indecency', if she hurts the family of her husband. So when she does that, so if he so desires to exit her from before the completion of her waiting period, so he can do it.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The waiting period of the woman who does not menstruate and the woman suffering from irregular bleeding from which she is not pure, is three months; and the waiting period of the woman who menstruates and her menstruation is regular, is three Quroo (pure periods), and Al-Quroo is the coagulation of the blood between the two menstruations.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman who menstruates once every three months, how should she observe her waiting period? He said: She should wait for the equivalent of her pure periods (quro') which she used to have during regular menstruation, so let her observe three pure periods, then let her marry if she wishes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), that he said: Regarding the woman who menstruates once every three months, or in six months, or in seven months; and the istihadah (continuous bleeding) woman who has not reached the age of menstruation; and the woman who menstruates once and then stops once; and the woman who has no hope of bearing children; and the woman whose menstruation has stopped but she claims she has not despaired (of menopause); and the woman who sees yellowish discharge from menstruation which is not regular. He mentioned that the waiting period (iddah) of all of these is three months.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the woman whose husband divorces her while she is menstruating once every three months, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When three months have passed, her waiting period is fulfilled. Each month is counted for her as a menstruation.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife after she had given birth and purified herself, and she is a woman who does not see blood for as long as she breastfeeds. What is her waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: Three months.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The waiting period of the woman who does not menstruate, and the woman suffering from vaginal bleeding and is not pure, is of three months; and the waiting period of the menstruating woman, and her menstruation is regular, is of three pure periods. He said, And I asked him about the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic [65:4] if you have a doubt – what is the doubt? So he said: What is increased upon a month, so it is a doubt, therefore let her wait three months, and neglect the menstruation, and whatever was in the month does not exceed in the menstruation upon it for three menstruations, so her waiting period is of three menstruations.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Whichever of the two matters precedes her, her waiting period is fulfilled: if three months pass and she does not see blood in them, her waiting period is fulfilled; and if three pure periods pass, her waiting period is fulfilled.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said: When she looks [for her menstrual cycle], and she does not find the pure periods (al-aqra') except for three months, so if her menstruation is not regular for her, she menstruates multiple times in the month, then her waiting period is the waiting period of the one suffering from irregular bleeding (al-mustahadha), which is three months; and if she menstruates a regular menstruation, then it is one menstruation in each month, with a month between every two menstruations, and that is the pure period (al-quroo).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Ishaq Sha'ir, from Harun ibn Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who was divorced and had reached an advanced age, she menstruated once, then her menstruation ceased. He (peace be upon him) said: She should observe the waiting period with that one menstruation and two following months, for she has despaired of menstruation (reached menopause).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saying: When a man divorces his wife and she claims to be pregnant, he should wait for nine months. If she gives birth, [the waiting period is complete]; otherwise, she observes a waiting period of three months, and then she is irrevocably divorced from him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'A young woman who menstruates like others, her husband divorces her, and her menstruation ceases. What is her waiting period?' He said: 'Three months.' I said, 'So if she claims pregnancy after three months?' He said: 'Her waiting period is nine months.' I said, 'So if she claims pregnancy after nine months?' He said: 'Rather, the pregnancy is nine months.' I said, 'She can marry?' He said: 'She should be cautious for three months.' I said, 'So if she claims [pregnancy] after three months?' He said: 'There is no doubt upon her. She can marry if she wishes.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Ibn Hakim from Abu Ibrahim or his father (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding the divorced woman, her husband divorces her and she says, 'I am pregnant,' so she remains for a year. He said: If she brings him after more than a year, she will not be believed, even if it is one hour in her claim.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Hakim from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) said: I said to him, 'What is the waiting period of a young woman who menstruates like others, whose husband divorces her, and her menstruation is lifted?' He said: 'Three months.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, if she marries after three months and it becomes clear after she enters upon her husband that she is pregnant?' He said: 'Far be it from that, O Ibn Hakim! The lifting of menstruation is of two types: either it is the spoiling of a menstruation, so the husbands are permissible for her and she is not pregnant, or if she is pregnant, it will become apparent within three months, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made it a time in which the pregnancy becomes apparent.' I said, 'If she is in doubt?' He said: 'Her waiting period is nine months.' I said, 'If she is in doubt after nine months?' He said: 'The pregnancy is nine months.' I said, 'So if she marries?' He said: 'She should be cautious for three months.' I said, 'If she is in doubt after three months?' He said: 'There is no doubt upon her; she may marry.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Hakam, from Abu Abdillah or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man divorces his wife, and when three months pass, she claims to be pregnant.' He said, 'Wait with her for nine months.' I said, 'And if she claims pregnancy after that?' He said, 'Far be it, far be it! The cessation of menstruation is of two types: either clear pregnancy, or irregularity from menstruation. But she should observe precautionary waiting for three months afterwards.' And he also said regarding the woman who used to menstruate, then her menstruation ceases for a year: 'How is she divorced?' He said, 'She is divorced by witnesses.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The pregnant woman's term is that she gives birth, and upon the husband is her maintenance in a reasonable manner until she gives birth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces a woman while she is pregnant, he must spend upon her until she gives birth to her child. When she gives birth, he gives her her recompense (for breastfeeding), and he should not cause her hardship, except if he finds someone who is cheaper in recompense than her. If she agrees to that recompense, she is more deserving to breastfeed her son until she weans him.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The pregnant divorced woman is provided for until she gives birth to her child, and she is more deserving of her son if she breastfeeds him, for the amount that another woman would accept. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child, and upon the heir is similar to that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman from us would raise her hand to her husband when he wanted to have intercourse with her, so she would say, And as for His words 'and upon the heir is similar to that', then He forbade that the child be harmed, or his mother be harmed regarding his breastfeeding. And it is not for her to take (recompense) for his breastfeeding for more than two complete years. And if they both intend weaning before that by mutual consent, it is good. And weaning is the cessation of breastfeeding.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her waiting period (iddah) is that she gives birth to her child, and upon him is her maintenance (nafaqah) until she gives birth to her child.'

Abu Al-Abbas Al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The woman who is thrice divorced has no maintenance (nafaqah) upon her husband. Rather, it is for the one upon whom her husband has the right of reversion (raj'ah).

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the woman who is divorced thrice upon the Sunnah, is there for her a dwelling or expenses? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa or a man, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked: About the woman who has been divorced three times, is there for her a dwelling and expenses?' He said: 'Is she pregnant?' I said, 'No'. He said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The woman who has been given a triple divorce has no maintenance (nafaqah) upon her husband. Rather, that is for the woman upon whom her husband has a right of reversion.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I said, 'For the woman who has been thrice divorced, is there for her dwelling (sukna) or expenses (nafaqah)?' He said, 'Is she pregnant?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'There is neither a dwelling for her nor expenses.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who divorces his wife, does he provide her with mut'ah (provision)? He said: Yes. Does he not love to be among the do-gooders? Does he not want to be among the pious?

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Abdul Kareem, from al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for the divorced women a provision with goodness; this is a right upon the pious.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her provision, after her waiting period ends, is upon the affluent according to his ability, and upon the poor according to his ability.' And how can he not provide for her while she is in her waiting period, hoping for him and he for her; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings about between them whatever He wills. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the man is affluent, he provides for his wife with a slave boy and a slave girl; and the poor provides with wheat, barley, raisins, clothing, and dirhams.' And indeed, Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) provided for a wife of his with a slave girl, and he did not divorce any woman except that he provided for her.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for the divorced women a provision with goodness; this is a right upon the pious.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her provision is after her waiting period ends, upon the affluent according to his ability, and upon the poor according to his ability.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'How can he provide for her during her waiting period while she hopes for him and he hopes for her, and Allah brings about whatever He wills?' As for the affluent man, he provides the woman with a slave and a maid, and the poor man provides with wheat, dates, raisins, clothing, and dirhams. And indeed Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) provided a woman he divorced with a maid, and he did not divorce a woman except that he provided for her. Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to it, except that he said: 'And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) used to provide his women with a maid.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for the divorced women a provision with the goodness; this is a right upon the pious.' What is the lowest of that provision when he is financially tight, he cannot find it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A scarf or something resembling it.'

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim from Abi Basir who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Inform me about the words of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: 'And for the divorced women is provision in a fair manner, a right upon the pious.' What is the minimum of that provision if one is poor and cannot find much? He said: A scarf or similar things.

I said to him: It has reached me that you say that whoever divorces contrary to the Sunnah, you do not consider his divorce as anything. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I am not saying it — rather it is God, Mighty and Majestic, Who says it. By God! If we were to issue fatwas to you with injustice, we would be worse than you, because God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Why do not the Rabbis and the scholars prohibit them from their speaking of what is sinful and their eating of what is unlawfully acquired?' — up to the end of the verse.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Sayrafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Everything that contradicts the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is to be referred back to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah.

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The man divorces his wife while she is menstruating.' He said: 'Divorce contrary to the Sunnah is void.' I said: 'So the man pronounces divorce three times in one sitting?' He said: 'He is to be returned to the Sunnah.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever divorces contrary to the Sunnah shall be returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, even if his nose is rubbed in the dust.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about divorce when one does not divorce according to the waiting period ('iddah). So he said: 'He is referred back to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife while she is menstruating. So he said: 'A divorce contrary to the Sunnah is invalid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Whoever pronounces three divorces in one sitting while not in a state of purity (during menstruation), this amounts to nothing. The only divorce is that which God, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded; so whoever violates this, there is no divorce for him. And indeed Ibn Umar divorced his wife three times in one sitting while she was menstruating, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ordered him to take her back and not count the divorce. He said: And a man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have divorced my wife.' He said: 'Do you have witnesses?' He said: 'No.' So he said: 'Be gone.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Abbas, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I heard Abu Basir saying: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband had divorced her contrary to the Sunnah, and we said that they are a private family and no one knows them. So he said: It is not anything (i.e., the divorce is null and void).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said, I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ibn Umar divorced his wife three (times) while she was menstruating. So Umar asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he ordered him to take her back. So I said: 'The people are saying that he only divorced her once while she was menstruating'. So he (AS) said: 'Then for what reason did he ask the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), if he had the right to take her back (anyway)? They lied! Rather, he divorced her three (times), so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered him to take her back, then said: If you wish, divorce, and if you wish, keep (her)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a woman who heard that a man had divorced her, and he denied it. Should she stay with him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, for his divorce without witnesses is not a divorce, and the divorce to other than the waiting period is not a divorce, and it is not permissible for him to do so by divorcing her without witnesses and to other than the waiting period which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr ibn Ayn and Burayd and Fudayl and Ismail al-Azraq and Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they said: When a man divorces [his wife] during the blood of childbirth, or divorces her after he has touched her, then his divorcing her is not a [valid] divorce. And if he divorces her at the commencement of her waiting period, while she is clean from non-coitus, and two just witnesses do not testify to that, then his divorcing her is not a [valid] divorce.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife during a period of purity without sexual intercourse, then returns to her on the same day, then divorces her again, so that three divorces are completed in one period of purity. He said: 'He acted contrary to the Sunnah.' I said: 'So it is not befitting for him, when he returns to her, to divorce her except in another period of purity?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Until he has intercourse with her?' He said: 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever divorces without witnesses, it is not valid.

Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, Umar ibn Yazeed, and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated, saying: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) in Kufa and said, 'I have divorced my wife after she had become clean from her menstruation, before I had intercourse with her.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, 'Did you have two just witnesses, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded?' He said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go, for your divorce is not valid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever divorces his wife three times in one sitting, while she is menstruating, it is not valid. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rejected the divorce of Abdullah ibn Umar when he divorced his wife three times while she was menstruating, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) invalidated that divorce. And he (peace be upon him) said: Everything that contradicts the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, is returned to the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty. And he (peace be upon him) said: There is no divorce except during a waiting period.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I asked Amr ibn Ubayd about the divorce of Ibn Umar, and he said: He divorced her while she was in a state of menstruation (taharah), one time.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Did you not say to him, 'When he divorced her once, whether she was menstruating or not, he has the right to take her back (raj'ah)?' He said, 'I had said that to him.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He lied against him, may the curse of Allah be upon him. Rather, he divorced her three times.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) returned her (to the state of being divorced once), and he said: 'Keep her or divorce her upon the Sunnah, if you intend to divorce.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, Umar ibn Udhaynah, Bukayr, and others, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Every divorce that is not for the waiting period is not a valid divorce: if he divorces her while she is menstruating, or in the blood of her postpartum bleeding, or after he has had intercourse with her before she menstruates, so his divorce of her is not a valid divorce. And if he divorces her for the waiting period more than once, there is no preference of the second over the first in terms of being a divorce; and if he divorces her for the waiting period without two just witnesses, his divorce is not a valid divorce, and the testimony of women is not permissible in it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I was with him when Nafi', the slave of Ibn Umar, passed by. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Are you the one who alleges that Ibn Umar divorced his wife once while she was menstruating, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered Umar to instruct him to return to her?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You lie, by Allah, the One there is no god except Him, regarding Ibn Umar. I heard Ibn Umar saying: I divorced her in the era of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) three times, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) returned it to me, and I kept her after the divorce. Therefore, fear Allah, O Nafi', and do not narrate falsehood about Ibn Umar!'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage with her, she is irrevocably divorced from him, and she may marry if she wishes from that very moment; and if he had stipulated a dower for her, then she is entitled to half of the dower; and if he had not stipulated a dower for her, then he should provide her with gifts (mut'ah).

Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, and Ali from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have appointed for them a portion, then (pay to them) half of what you have appointed, unless they relinquish or he should relinquish in whose hand is the marriage tie.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is the father, or the brother, or the man who has been bequeathed for it and his instructions are allowed with regards to the wealth of the woman, so he should provide for her. So it would be allowed, when he excuses in accordance to what is allowed.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is half the dower, if something was obligated for her; and if it was not obligated for her, then let him provide for her with provision in the manner that he would provide for similar women.' He (the narrator) said, 'And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Or he should relinquish in whose hand is the marriage tie.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is the father, or the brother, and the man who has been bequeathed to it, and the man whose instructions are allowed in the wealth of the woman, so he buys for her and sells for her. So when he excuses, it is allowed.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man married a woman for one hundred sheep, then brought the sheep to her, then divorced her before consummating the marriage, and the sheep had given birth. He (peace be upon him) said: If the sheep were pregnant with him, he returns half of the sheep and half of their offspring; and if the pregnancy was not with him, he returns half of the sheep and does not return anything from the offspring. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, except that he said: He brought to her sheep and slaves, so the sheep and the slaves gave birth.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from Abu al-Hasan, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who marries the non-virgin woman or the virgin slave girl, and divorces her the moment she is brought to him, he said: 'These two are examined by the reliable women. If they remain in their state as they were brought to him, then they are entitled to half the dower which was stipulated for them, and there is no waiting period (iddah) for them from him.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Al-Fudayl bin Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman for a thousand dirhams, so he gave her a fugitive slave of his and a garment, a veil, valued at the thousand dirhams which was her dower. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she is pleased with the slave, and she had known him, there is no problem when she takes possession of the garment and is pleased with the slave.' I said, 'And if he divorces her before he enters with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dower for her, and she returns to him five hundred dirhams, and the slave is for her.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Ibn Abi Yafur who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and made her dower her father, on condition that she return to him one thousand dirhams. Then he divorced her before consummating the marriage. What is appropriate for her to return to him? And indeed, she is entitled to half the dower. Her father is an old man, his value is five hundred dirhams, and he says, 'If it were not for you, I would not have sold him for three thousand dirhams.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No consideration is given to his words, and she does not return to him anything.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Salih ibn Razin, from Shihab who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman for one thousand dirhams, so he paid it to her, and she gifted it to him and said, 'I am desirous of you.' So he divorced her before entering with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He returns to her five hundred dirhams.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who married a woman and set her father as her dower, and the value of her father was five hundred dirhams, on condition that she would give him one thousand dirhams. Then he divorced her before entering into her. He (peace be upon him) said: There is nothing upon her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife before he enters (consummates marriage) with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is half the dower, if he had stipulated something for her; and if he had not stipulated anything for her, then let him provide for her with a provision similar to what is provided for similar women.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the woman who marries a domestic servant (slave), and he grows older with her, so his value increases or decreases, then he divorces her before consummating the marriage, he said: 'Upon her is half his value on the day he was handed over to her; the increase and the decrease are not considered.'

And by this chain Regarding the man who emancipates his slave girl, so he makes her emancipation as her dower. Then he divorces her before he sleeps with her. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘She would return to him half of her price. She would have to work with regards to it’.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had intercourse with his wife, he said: When the two circumcised parts meet, the dower becomes obligatory and the waiting period [is established].

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When the two circumcisions meet, it obligates the dower, and the waiting period, and the washing.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When he enters her (completes penetration), then the ritual bath (ghusl) becomes obligatory, and the whipping, and the stoning, and the dower becomes obligatory.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Touching the women is the consummation (or finalization) with them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, so he locked the door, and pulled the curtain, and touched, and kissed. Then he divorced her. Is the dower obligated upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: The dower is not obligated upon him except by copulation.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father asked him, and I was present, about a man who married a woman, and she was brought to him, but he did not touch her and did not reach her until he divorced her. Is there a waiting period (iddah) upon her from him? He said: 'The waiting period is from the water (seminal discharge).' It was said to him: 'So if he copulated with her in the vagina but did not ejaculate?' He said: 'When he entered (the penis) into her, the ritual bath (ghusl), the dower (mahr), and the waiting period (iddah) become obligatory.'
