Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife, and he had touched everything from her, except that he did not copulate with her. Is there a waiting period for her? So he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was tested with this, so his father, Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), said to him: If he closed the door and lowered the curtain, the dower and the waiting period become obligatory.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man marries a woman, lowers the veil over both of them, and closes the door. Then he divorces her. The woman is asked, 'Did he come to you?' She says, 'He did not come to me.' He is asked, 'Did you go to her?' He says, 'I did not go to her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Both of them are not believed, and that is because she wants to repel the waiting period (iddah) from herself, and he wants to repel the dower (mahr) from himself. Meaning if they are both suspected (of collusion).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman, enters into her, closes the door, and lowers a veil over her, and claims that he did not touch her, and she believes him regarding that. Is there a waiting period (iddah) upon her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'So it is something less than something.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the water (semen) came out, she would observe the waiting period.' Meaning: if they were both trusted, they would be believed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent from her, from which day should she observe the waiting period? He said: If she establishes just proof that she was divorced on a known day, and she is convinced, let her observe the waiting period from the day she was divorced; and if she did not preserve [the knowledge] of which day and which month, let her observe the waiting period from the day it reaches her.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding the absentee when he divorces his wife, she should observe the waiting period from the day he divorces her.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Muthanna, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent from her, when should she observe the waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When proof is established for her that she was divorced on a known day and a known month, let her observe the waiting period from the day she was divorced; and if she does not remember which day and which month, let her observe the waiting period from the day the news reaches her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the divorced woman, her husband divorces her but he does not let her know except after a year. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If two just witnesses come, she should not observe the waiting period, or else let her observe it from the day it reaches her'.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Razi, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man divorces [his wife] while he is absent, let him bear witness to that. So when three pure periods pass from that day, her waiting period has been fulfilled.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: He said regarding the divorced woman: When the proof is established that he has divorced her since such and such (a day), and her waiting period has passed, then she is irrevocably divorced.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man divorces his wife while he is absent, and the proof is established for that, then her waiting period (iddah) is from the day he divorced her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man divorces his wife while he is absent, and proof is established for her that he divorced her in such and such a month, she observes her waiting period (iddah) from the day on which the divorce occurred with her husband; and if she does not remember that day, she observes the waiting period from the day she knows.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding a man who dies while his wife is under him (married to him) and he is absent. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should observe the waiting period from the day his death reaches her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman from whom her husband dies and he is absent, so her waiting period is from the day (the news) reaches her, whether the proof is established or not established.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Bureyd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the woman whose husband is absent from her, when he dies: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman widowed from her husband should observe the waiting period from the day the news comes to her, because she mourns over him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh, both together, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the woman, when the news of her husband's death reaches her, he said: She observes the waiting period (Iddah) from the day the news reaches her, as if she is mourning for him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband dies while he is absent, when should she observe her waiting period? He said: 'The day the news reaches her.' And he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One of you women used to remain for a year when her husband died and he was absent, then she would cast her desires behind her back.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If her husband dies while he is absent, and proof is established for his death, then her waiting period (iddah) is from the day the news reaches her, four months and ten days, because she must mourn for him in death for four months and ten days, so she should refrain from kohl, perfume, and dyes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The woman whose husband has died, she observes the waiting period when the news reaches her, because she intends to mourn for him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the pregnant woman whose husband dies, her waiting period is the later of the two terms. If she is pregnant and four months and ten days are completed for her and she has not given birth, then her waiting period is until she gives birth. And if she gives birth before the completion of four months and ten days, she waits after giving birth for the complete four months and ten days, and that is the further of the two terms.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the pregnant woman whose husband dies, indeed there is no maintenance (nafaqah) for her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The waiting period (iddah) of the woman whose husband dies is the later of the two terms, because upon her is that she should mourn for four months and ten (days), and it is not upon her with the divorce that she should mourn.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth before four months and ten days had passed. She then married. He ruled that the new husband should keep her, then not propose to her (or finalize the marriage) until the end of the later of the two terms (widowhood or pregnancy). If the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her off, and if they wish, they may keep her. If they keep her, they return his wealth (dowry) to him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The pregnant woman whose husband dies, her waiting period is the later of the two terms.

From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The pregnant woman whose husband dies, gives birth and remarries before the expiration of four months and ten days.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If her husband, from whom she married, had consummated the marriage with her, separation is effected between them, and she observes the remainder of her first waiting period, and another waiting period from the latter one.' And if he had not consummated the marriage with her, separation is effected between them, and she observes the remainder of her waiting period, and he is a suitor among suitors.'

And from him, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and Ali ibn Khalid al-Aqouli, from Karram, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the pregnant woman whose husband dies, is there for her expenses (nafaqah)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the pregnant woman whose husband has died, is there expense (nafaqah) for her? He said: No. And it is reported as well that her expense is from the wealth of her child which is in her belly. He reported it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The pregnant woman whose husband has died, her expenses are provided from the wealth of her child which is in her belly.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, or someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband dies, should she go out to the house of her father and her mother from her house if she so desires, so she observes the waiting period? So he (peace be upon him) said: If she so desires, she observes the waiting period in the house of her husband, and if she so desires, she observes the waiting period among her family, and she should not apply Kohl nor wear jewellery. And she should not apply Kohl nor wear jewellery.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman whose husband dies, can she perform Hajj and testify for the rights? He said: Yes.

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Rabat, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Al-Abbas, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The woman whose husband has died from her [i.e., she is widowed].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should not apply kohl for adornment, nor perfume herself, nor wear dyed clothes, nor go out during the day, nor spend the night away from her house.' I said, 'What is your view if she wants to go out for a right [need], how should she do it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should go out after midnight, and return by late evening.'

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman whose husband has died, can she go out from her husband's house? He said: She can go out from her husband's house, and perform Hajj, and move from one house to another.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the woman whose husband died, where should she observe her waiting period? He said: Wherever she wishes, and she should not spend a night away from her house.

Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman whose husband dies, should she observe her waiting period in a house, remaining in it for a month, or less than a month, or more, then move from it to another, so she remains in the house she moved to for a period similar to what she remained in the house she moved from? Such is her practice until her waiting period is completed. He said: That is permissible for her, and there is no problem.

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: A woman came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) seeking a verdict regarding spending the night in a place other than her own house, while her husband had died. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the people of the Pre-Islamic period, when the husband of a woman died, his wife would mourn for him for twelve months. So when Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), out of mercy for their weakness, He made their waiting period four months and ten (days), and you do not have patience for this?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the woman whose husband dies, is it suitable for her to perform Hajj or to visit the sick? He said: Yes, she goes out in the way of Allah, and she should not apply kohl, nor perfume.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The woman whose husband has died, it is not for her to perfume herself nor to adorn herself until her waiting period (iddah) of four months and ten days is completed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the woman whose husband dies while she is in her waiting period (Iddah), can she go out for a right (claim/affair)? He said: Indeed, some of the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked him, saying: 'So-and-so woman's husband died, so she wants to go out for a right that is due to her.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Uff to you! Before I was sent, when a woman from you had her husband die, she would take a clod of cow dung and throw it behind her back.' Then she said: 'I shall neither comb my hair, nor apply kohl, nor dye (henna) for a full year. But I have only commanded you with four months and ten days. Then, be patient (in abstaining): do not comb, do not apply kohl, do not dye, do not go out from her house during the day, and do not spend the night away from her house.' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what should she do if a right presents itself to her?' He said: 'She goes out after the decline of the night (midnight), and returns at evening, so she is considered not to have spent the night away from her house.' I said to him: 'Can she perform Hajj?' He said: 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband dies, can she perform Hajj? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, and she goes out and moves from a house to a house.

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband dies; can she perform Hajj? He said, 'Yes,' and she can move from one house to another house.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Ahmad, son of Muhammad, from Ali, son of Al-Hakam, from Al-'Ala', son of Razin, from Muhammad, son of Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)... ...regarding the man who dies while having a wife under him whom he had not entered (consummated the marriage with). He (peace be upon him) said: For her is half the dower, and for her is the complete inheritance, and upon her is the complete waiting period.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and did not enter (consume the marriage) with her. He (peace be upon him) said: If she dies, or he dies, or he divorces her, then for her is half (the dower), and upon her is the complete waiting period, and for her is the inheritance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from a man, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the woman whose husband dies and he had not entered (consummated marriage) with her, indeed for her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If he had not yet consummated the marriage with her, and he had obligated a dower for her, then she is entitled to half of what he obligated for her, and she is entitled to inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.

Ali, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said: I asked him about the wife who dies before she is entered into (consummated), or the husband dies before he enters into her. So he said: Whichever of the two dies, for the woman is half of what was obligated for her, and if it was not obligated for her, then there is no dower for her.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Aban from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a woman who died before she had been slept with, what is for her from the dower, and how is her inheritance? So he said: If he had obligated a dower for her, then for her is half the dower, and he inherits her; and if he had not obligated a dower for her, then there is no dower for her. And he said regarding a man who died before he had slept with his wife: If he had obligated a dower for her, then for her is half the dower, and she inherits him; and if he had not obligated a dower for her, then there is no dower for her.

And by his chain, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara and Fazl Abu al-Abbas, who said: We said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who marries a woman, then dies while she is still his wife, and he has obligated the dower for her?' He said: 'For her is half the dower, and she inherits him from everything, and if she had died, so it would be like that.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding the woman widowed from her husband and he had not touched her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She cannot get married until she observes the waiting period of four months and ten (days), a waiting period of the woman widowed from her husband'.

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman whose husband dies while she is his wife, and he has not entered (consummated marriage) with her, he (peace be upon him) said: 'She is in the status of the divorced woman whom the husband has not entered with. If he had specified a dower for her, then she has half of it, and she inherits him. And if he had not specified a dower for her, then there is no dower for her, and she inherits him.' I said: 'And the waiting period (iddah)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Refrain from this (question).'

Humayd from Ibn Sama'a, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Hasan al-Sayqal and Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the woman whose husband dies before he has entered into her. He (peace be upon him) said: For her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband died and he had not entered into marital relations with her. He (The Imam) said: 'For her is the inheritance, and upon her is the complete waiting period (iddah). And if he had specified a dower for her, then for her is half of it. And if he had not specified a dower for her, then there is nothing for her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them). Regarding a man who divorces his wife with a divorce in which he retains the right of reversion, then he dies while she is in her waiting period, he said: She observes the waiting period of the longer of the two terms, four months and ten days.

From him, from one of our companions, with regards to the irrevocably divorced woman, when (her husband) dies from her, and she is in her waiting period, he said: 'She should observe the waiting period by the further of the two terms'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (peace be upon them) who said: The woman whose husband dies, is maintained from his wealth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any woman who is divorced, then her husband dies before her waiting period (iddah) expires and she has not become forbidden to him, then she inherits him, and then she observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died; and if she dies while she is in her waiting period and has not become forbidden to him, then he inherits her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sick man: Is it for him to divorce his wife in that state? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but for him is that he may marry if he wishes. So if he enters with her, she inherits him, and if he does not enter with her, then his marriage is invalid.

And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Rabi' al-Asam, from Abu Ubayda al-Hazza', and Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu al-Ward, both of them, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man divorces his wife with a single divorce during his illness, then she remains in his illness until her waiting period expires, then she inherits him as long as she has not remarried. And if she remarries after the expiration of the waiting period, then she does not inherit him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who divorces his wife while he is sick, he said: If he dies in his illness and she has not remarried, she inherits him; and if she has remarried, then she has accepted what was done, there is no inheritance for her.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the sick person is valid, and his marriage is valid.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhassan, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill, until he died in that year. He said: She inherits him if it was during the illness in which he divorced her, and he did not recover in between.

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Rabat, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man divorces his wife with one divorce while he is sick, and he had previously divorced her with two divorces.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him if it is during his illness.' I said, 'And what is the limit of the illness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He remains sick until he dies, and if that is prolonged, up to a year.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abi Al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces his wife during his illness, she inherits him as long as he remains in that illness, even if her waiting period has expired, except if he recovers from it. He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'And if the illness is prolonged?'' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What is between that and one year.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not for the sick man that he divorces, but for him is that he can marry.

Muhammad narrated from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife while he is ill. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him as long as she is in her waiting period; and if he divorces her during the state of restlessness (marad al-maut), she inherits him up to a year. So if there is an increase upon the year by one day, she does not inherit him, and she observes the waiting period from him, for four months and ten days, the waiting period of the woman whose husband has died.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who divorces his wife with two divorces while in good health, then divorces her with the third divorce while he is sick: she inherits him for as long as he remains in his illness, even if it lasts up to a year.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, that he was asked about the man to whom death approaches, so he divorces his wife, is her divorce valid? He said: Yes, and if he dies, she inherits him, and if she dies, he does not inherit her.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: It is not for the sick man to divorce, but for him is that he can marry. So if he marries and enters into her (consummates), it is valid. And if he does not enter into her until he dies during his illness, then his marriage is invalid, and there is no dower for her, nor inheritance.
that he said: 'There is no divorce except when what is intended by it is the divorce.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from al-Yasa', from Abu 'Abdillah (AS), and from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ja'far (AS) — both of them said: There is no divorce except for the one who intended the divorce.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from al-Yasa' who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: There is no divorce except upon the Sunnah, and there is no divorce upon the Sunnah except during a period of purity (tuhr) without copulation, and there is no divorce upon the Sunnah and during a period of purity without copulation except with witnesses; and if a man divorced according to the Sunnah and during a period of purity without copulation, but did not have it witnessed, his divorce would not be a (valid) divorce; and if a man divorced according to the Sunnah and during a period of purity without copulation, and had it witnessed, but did not intend the divorce, his divorce would not be a (valid) divorce.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man must not harm his wife when he divorces her by straitening her (financially) until she moves out before the expiration of her waiting period. For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden that. And do not injure them in order to straiten them.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the young boy who has not yet reached puberty (hadith) and his mahr (dowry). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he divorces in accordance with the Sunnah and places the mahr in its rightful place and due share, then there is no problem, and it is valid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the child is not with anything.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the child is not valid, nor is the divorce of the intoxicated one.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from a number of his companions, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The divorce of the young boy is valid when he has attained intellect, and so is his bequest and his charity, even if he has not yet undergone seminal emission.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn together, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'The divorce of the child is valid/permissible when he reaches ten years of age.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Khalid Al-Qammat, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is the divorce of the fool, the one whose intellect has gone, allowed to be performed by his guardian over him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Why does he not divorce himself?' I said: 'It is not trusted that if he divorces, he will say tomorrow, "I did not divorce," or he is not proficient in divorcing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see his guardian except as being at the status of the Sultan (ruling authority).'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan from Abu Khalid al-Qammam, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man whose opinion is recognized at one time and denied at another, is the divorce of his guardian allowed over him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is the matter with him that he does not divorce (himself)?' I said: 'He does not know the limit of the divorce, and is not secure upon it; if he divorces today, he might say tomorrow,

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the deranged one who has lost his intellect: Is his divorce allowed? He said: No. And about the woman when she is like that: Is her selling or her charity (gift) allowed? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Shihab ibn Abdi Rabbihi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The deranged one who does not know how to divorce properly, his guardian divorces on his behalf according to the Sunnah.' I said, 'And if he was ignorant and divorced her three times in one sitting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is returned to the Sunnah. So when three months or three menstrual periods have passed, she has been irrevocably divorced from him by one (divorce).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the divorce of the deranged, he (peace be upon him) said: 'His guardian divorces on his behalf, for I consider him to be at the status of the Imam.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the divorce of the intoxicated one, so he said: 'It is not valid, and there is no prestige (or: it is not considered a proper divorce).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the intoxicated one is not with anything.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the intoxicated one, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid, and there is no prestige (or: it is not a matter of grace/discretion).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ibn Rabat and Al-Husayn ibn Hashim from Safwan, all from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the divorce of the intoxicated one, so he said: It is not valid, nor is his emancipation (of a slave).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abi Umeyr or someone else, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a Muslim man passes by a group of people who do not possess authority, and they compel him until he fears for his life, that he should either emancipate (a slave) or divorce (his wife), and he does so, there is no blame upon him.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the divorce of the coerced and his emancipation (of a slave), so he said: 'His divorce is not a valid divorce, nor is his emancipation a valid emancipation.' So I said, 'I am a businessman; I pass by the tax collector and with me is wealth.' So he said: 'Hide it as much as you can, and place it in its proper places.' So I said, 'And if he makes me swear an oath with the divorce and the emancipation (of a slave)?' So he said: 'Swear for him.' Then he took a date, and scooped with it from the butter that was in front of him. So he said: 'I do not mind if you swear for them with the divorce and the emancipation, or I eat it (the date).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ubays ibn Hisham and Salih ibn Khalid from Mansur ibn Yunus who said: I asked the Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), and he was at Al-Urayz, so I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I have married a woman and she used to love me, then I married upon her a daughter of my maternal uncle, and there was a son for me from the woman. So I returned to Baghdad, so I divorced her once. Then I reverted to her, then divorced her the second (divorce). Then I went from her presence intending this journey, until I was at Al-Kufa. I wanted to look at the daughter of my maternal uncle, so my sister and my maternal aunt said, 'You will not look at her ever, by Allah, until you divorce so and so'. So I said, 'Woe be unto you! By Allah, there is no way for me to divorce her'. So he said to me: 'It is from your affairs, there is no way for you to divorce her'. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! There was a daughter for me from her, and she was at Baghdad, and this one is at Al-Kufa, and I went out from her presence before that by four (days), so they refused me (to see her) except that I divorce her three times, and no, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you! I did not intend (for the Sake of) Allah except that I manage them from myself, and it has afflicted my heart due to that, may I be sacrificed for you!' So he remained silent for a long time, then raised his head towards me, and he was smiling. So he said: 'As for what is between you and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so it is not with anything, but, when they proceed you to the Sultan (ruling authority), they would irrevocably divorce her from you'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Divorce is not valid under compulsion, nor is emancipation valid under compulsion, nor is an oath valid for cutting off kinship, nor for anything from the disobedience of Allah. So whoever swears or is made to swear regarding any of this, and he acts upon it, there is nothing upon him (no expiation is required).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, the divorce is that which is intended by it without compulsion, and without harm to the waiting period, and the Sunnah is upon purity (from menses) without sexual intercourse, and with two witnesses. So whoever opposes this, then neither his divorce nor his oath is valid, and it is returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I pass by the tax collector and with me is wealth, so he makes me swear an oath. So if I were to swear for him, he leaves me (alone), and if I do not swear for him, he ransacks me and oppresses me'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Swear for him'. I said, 'Suppose he makes me swear with the divorce?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Swear for him'. I said, 'So if the wealth does not happen to be mine?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So (do it) for (the sake of) the wealth of your brother. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rebuffed a divorce of Ibn Umar and he had divorced his wife three (divorces) and she was menstruating. Thus Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) viewed that (divorce) as nothing'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who has his wife with him, then he remains silent and does not speak. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is he mute?' I said: 'Yes.' So it is known from him that he hates his wife and dislikes her. Is it permissible for his guardian to divorce her on his behalf?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he can write it and bear witness to that.' I said: 'He cannot write nor hear, how does he divorce her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By that which is recognized from him through his actions, like what you mentioned of his dislike and hatred for her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban ibn Uthman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the mute woman. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wrap her veil upon her head and pull it away.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The divorce of the mute woman is that he takes her veil, places it upon her head, and then separates from her.

Ali, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, regarding a mute man who wrote in the ground [indicating] the divorce of his wife. He (AS) said: When he does that, at the acceptance of purity, with witnesses, and it is understood from him as it is understood from one like him, and he intends the divorce, then his divorce is valid upon the Sunnah.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who delegated the affair of his wife to a man, so he said, 'Bear witness that I have delegated the affair of so-and-so to so-and-so.' Is that permissible for the man? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, all together from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who appoints a man to handle the matter of his wife, so he said, 'Bear witness that I have appointed So-and-so to handle the matter of So-and-so woman,' and he (the representative) divorces her. Is that permissible for the man?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hands of two men: so one of them divorced her and the other refused. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) refused to validate that until both of them gather together in consensus upon the divorce.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hilal al-Razi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man appointed a man as his representative to divorce his wife when she menstruates and becomes pure. The man went out, and then it occurred to him (to change his mind), so he testified that he had annulled what he had ordered him to do, and that it had occurred to him regarding that. He (peace be upon him) said: So let him inform his wife, and let him inform the representative.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hands of two men, so one of them divorced and the other refused. So Ali (peace be upon him) refused to validate that until they both gather upon the divorce together. And it is reported that he (peace be upon him) did not allow the representation in the divorce.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, all from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The representation (agency) is not valid in the divorce.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the solemn oath (Ila'): When a man takes an oath that he will not approach his wife, nor touch her, nor join his head with her head, he is in a period of grace as long as four months do not pass. When four months have passed, he is paused (given a choice): either he fulfills (the oath by returning), so he touches her, or he is determined upon divorce, so he separates from her until she menstruates and becomes pure from her menstruation, then he divorces her with one divorce before he sleeps with her, with the testimony of two just witnesses. Then he is more rightful in reverting to her as long as the three pure periods (Quroo') do not pass.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said, I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who abandons his wife without a divorce or an oath, for a year, not approaching her bed. He (peace be upon him) said: Let him go to his wife. And he (peace be upon him) said: Whichever man solemnly oaths from his wife, and the solemn oath is that he says, 'No, by Allah, I will not sleep with you, such and such', and he says, 'By Allah, I shall constrict you (due to my anger with you)', then he is angry with her, so he awaits with her for four months. Then he should be seized by it, after four months. So he pauses, and he meets and the meeting is that he reconciles with his wife, so Allah (azwj) is most Forgiving more Merciful. So if he does not meet, he is compelled that he divorces, and a divorce does not happen between the two of them until he pauses, even if it was as well after the four months, he would be compelled upon that he either meets (reconciles) or divorces.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man makes a solemn oath (ila') from his wife, and the solemn oath is that he says, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you, such and such [a period],' and he says, 'By Allah, I shall constrict you [in anger],' then he angers her, then he awaits her for four months. So if he returns (fa'a), and the return is that he reconciles with his family or divorces her at that time, and a divorce does not take place between the two of them until he pauses, even if it is after the four months, until he either returns or divorces.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan and Bureyd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they said: When a man makes a solemn oath not to approach his wife, she has no say and no right during the four months, and there is no sin upon him in refraining from her during the four months. So if the four months pass before he touches her, and she is silent and pleased, then he is in a state of solution and leeway. So if she raises her matter, it is said to him: either you return (to intimacy) and touch her, or you divorce her. And the decisive divorce is that he keeps her away. So when she menstruates and becomes pure, he divorces her, and he is more rightful in revoking her as long as three menstrual periods do not pass. This is the solemn oath (Ila') which Allah, Blessed and High, revealed in His Book, and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! My wife breastfed a boy, and I swore by Allah, I will not go near you until you wean him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no vow of abstinence (ila') in reconciliation.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Abu Maryam from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The one who takes an oath of abstention (muda'ib) is paused for four months; if he wishes, he may keep her in a good manner or release her with kindness; if he determines divorce, then it is one revocable divorce, and he has the right to take her back.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about al-Ila' (solemn oath of abstention), what is it? He said: It is when a man says to his wife, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period,' and he says, 'By Allah, I shall keep you in suspense (by withholding intimacy).' So she is awaited for four months, then he is seized and held. If he returns (reconciles), and it is that he makes peace with his wife, then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And if he does not return, he is compelled to divorce her, and a divorce does not take effect between them, even if it be after the four months, provided he does not refer the matter to the Imam.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the one who makes a solemn oath (al-mu'li), if he refuses to divorce, he said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would make for him an enclosure of reeds, imprison him in it, and prevent him from food and drink until he divorces.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, he raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the one who delays (paying the dowry), either he reconciles (pays) or he divorces (her). So if he does it, or else his neck is struck.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man is angered with his wife and does not approach her, without an oath, for four months, and she seeks enforcement against him, then either he returns (to her) or he divorces her. So if he leaves her from other than anger or an oath, he is not considered a mu'll (one who has taken an oath of abstention).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Is'haq ibn Bunan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when the one who took the solemn oath refused to divorce, would make an enclosure for him from cane and give him a quarter of his provision until he divorces.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Hamdan al-Qalanisi from Ishaq ibn Bunan from Ibn Baqqah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) would, if the one who swore (not to have intercourse) refused to divorce, place him in an enclosure of reeds and give him one-fourth of his food until he divorced.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the ruling for a man who makes a solemn oath (ila') from his wife before he has intercourse with her?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The solemn oath does not take effect until he has intercourse with her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, who said: 'I do not know it except from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He does not become a solemn oather until he enters with her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who swore an oath of abstention (ila') from his wife and had not yet consummated the marriage with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no ila' until he consummates the marriage with her.' So he (peace be upon him) asked: 'Do you see if a man were to swear that he would not cohabit with his wife for two years or more than that, would that be considered ila'?'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from his father Sulayman who said: I was in the mosque when Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered, and I did not recognize him. So I asked about him and was informed of his name. Then I and others arose toward him, surrounded him, and greeted him. A man then said to him: 'May Allah keep you well! What is your view regarding a man who names a specific woman and says on the day he marries her, she is divorced three times, then later changes his mind and wishes to marry her — is that permissible for him?' He said: 'Divorce is only after marriage.'
I asked him about the man who says, 'On the day I marry so-and-so woman, she is divorced.' So he said: 'It is nothing. Indeed, divorce cannot occur until he has contracted the marriage.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Those who came before us used to say: There is neither emancipation nor divorce except after what the man possesses.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from his father who said: I was in the mosque when Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered, and I did not recognize him. He had on a black turban with both its ends hanging between his shoulders. So I asked a man sitting near me, 'Who is this elder?' He said, 'What is the matter with you — you have not asked me about anyone who entered the mosque except this elder?' I said to him, 'I have not seen anyone enter the mosque with a finer appearance in my eyes than this elder, which is why I asked you about him.' He said, 'He is Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' So I arose, and the man and others arose; we gathered around him and greeted him. The man said to him, 'What is your view — may God keep you well — regarding a man who named a specific woman and said: on the day I marry her, she is divorced three times — then he later changes his mind and wants to marry her; is that permissible for him?' So he said: 'Divorce is only after marriage.' Abdullah (son of the narrator) said: I and my father then went to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), and my father narrated this hadith to him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You are bearing witness upon Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with this hadith?' He said: 'Yes.'

I asked him about a man who said: 'If I marry so-and-so woman, then she is divorced; and if I buy so-and-so (slave), then he is free; and if I buy this cloth, then it is for the poor.' So he said: 'It amounts to nothing. One cannot divorce except what one owns, and one cannot give in charity except from what one owns.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who says to his wife, 'You are free from me,' or 'disavowed,' or 'severed,' or 'prohibited.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not with anything.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who said to his wife, 'You are separate from me,' and 'You are free from me,' and 'You are disavowed from me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not anything (i.e., it does not constitute a formal divorce).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who said to his wife, 'You are free from me,' or 'disavowed from me,' or 'severed,' or 'prohibited.' He said: 'It is not anything (i.e., it does not constitute a formal divorce).'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah from Muawiya ibn Hukaym from Safwan and Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the choice (al-khiyar), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it, and what is that? That is something which was for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ibn Ribat from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I heard your father saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave a choice to his wives, so they chose Allah and His Messenger, so he did not keep them upon a divorce, and if they had chosen themselves, they would have been irrevocably divorced.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'This is a hadith which my father used to narrate from Aisha. And what is for the people and the choice? Rather, this is something which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, specialized His Messenger with.'

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Ibn Rabat, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who gave his wife the choice (khul'), so she chose herself [to be divorced], and she was irrevocably divorced from him. He said: No, this is something that was specific to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He was commanded with that, so he did it. And if they had chosen themselves, he would have divorced them. And this is the Word of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: 'Say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and let you go with a good release.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Harun ibn Muslim, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What do you say regarding a man who made the matter of his wife to be in her hands?' So he said: 'He has given the matter to the one who is not deserving of it, and he has opposed the Sunnah, and the marriage is not allowed'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Her khul' (compensatory divorce) is not valid until she says to her husband: 'By Allah, I will not fulfill a promise for you, and I will not obey you in a matter, and I will not perform ghusl for you from major ritual impurity, and I will lie on your bed (with another), and I will permit entry upon you without your permission.' And indeed, the people used to be lenient with what is less than this. So when the woman says this to her husband, it becomes permissible for him to take whatever he took from her. Thus, she remains with him having two remaining divorces left, and the khul' counts as one divorce. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'And the speech must come from her.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the matter were up to us, we would not validate a divorce except for the waiting period (iddah).'

And from him, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, all from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the woman who performs Khul'a (compensatory divorce). He said: It is not permissible for her husband to divorce her by Khul'a until she says: 'I shall not fulfill a vow for you, nor establish the limits of Allah with regard to you, nor wash myself for you from major impurity, and I will surely settle on your bed, and I will let into your house the one whom you dislike, without you knowing this, and they will not speak to her, and she is the one who says this.' So when she performs Khul'a, she is irrevocably divorced, and for him is that he takes from her wealth whatever he is able to, and it is not for him that he takes from the woman who disavows (the marriage) everything which he had given her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The woman who gives Khula (compensatory divorce) is the one who says to her husband, 'Divorce me, and I will give you whatever I have taken from you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to take anything from her until she says, By Allah, I will not fulfill a vow for you, and I will not obey you in a matter, and I will permit in your house without your permission, and I will settle in your bed another than you. So when she does that without him knowing it, it is permissible for him whatever he takes from her, and it would be a divorce without a divorce following it. So she would be irrevocably divorced by that, and he would be a proposer from the proposers.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces his wife by Khul'a, it is one irrevocable divorce, and he is a suitor among the suitors. It is not permissible for him to divorce her by Khul'a until she is the one who seeks that from him, without him having beaten her, and until she says: 'I shall not fulfill a vow for you, nor wash for you from major impurity, and I will bring into your house the one you dislike, and I will settle in your bed, and I will not establish the limits of Allah.' So when this is from her, then what he takes from her is suitable/permissible.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jamil, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the woman says to her husband the sentence, 'I will not obey you in a matter,' whether it is specified or not specified, it is permissible for him what he takes from her, and there is no return (revocation of divorce) for him upon her.
And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Khul'a and the Mubarayah are an irrevocable divorce, and he is a proposer from the proposers.

Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Jameel, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When the woman says, 'By Allah, I will not obey you in a matter, whether specified or unspecified,' it is permissible for him what he takes from her, and there is no right of reversion for him to her.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah that Jamil witnessed one of our companions, and he intended to detach (Khul'a) his daughter from one of our companions. So Jamil said to the man, 'What are you saying? Have you accepted this which you have taken and left her?' He said, 'Yes.' So Jamil said to them, 'Arise!' They said, 'O Abu Ali! Do you not want the divorce to follow it?' He said, 'No.' And Ja'far ibn Sama'ah used to say, 'The divorce follows it during the waiting period,' and he argued by the narration of Musa ibn Bakr from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'For the woman who is divorced by Khul'a, the divorce follows her as long as she is in the waiting period.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the woman who gives Khul'a, she is not permissible for him until she repents from the words which she said to him during the Khul'a.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The waiting period of the woman who gives Khul'a is similar to the waiting period of the divorced woman, and her Khul'a is her divorce.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said: The woman divorced by Khul'a is not to be provided for.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washha, from Aban, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the waiting period of the woman who gives herself in divorce (Khul'a), how much is it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the waiting period of the divorced woman (by Talaq), and let her observe it in her house; and the woman who divorces by mutual agreement (Mubarat) is in the same status as the woman who divorces by Khul'a.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The waiting period of the woman who gives Khul'a is the waiting period of the divorced woman, and her Khul'a is her divorce. He said: And I asked him, 'Does she receive something (as maintenance during the waiting period)?' He said: 'No'.

Humayd, from Al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman who gives Khul'a (mutual divorce), he said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of the divorced woman, and she waits in her house, and the woman who gives Khul'a is in the status of the woman who gives Mubara'ah.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, and Safwan, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The woman who is divorced by Khul'a has neither a dwelling for her nor expenses.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'For every divorced woman is a provision (mut'ah), except for the woman who divorces by al-khul', for she has bought herself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man whose wife divorced herself from him by Khul'a, is it permissible for him to propose to her sister before the waiting period of the woman who gave Khul'a has expired? He said: Yes, her bond of marriage has been severed from him and there is no reversion for him to her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or desertion'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is like that, so he intends to divorce her, she says to him, Keep me, and I shall leave part of what is upon you (dower), and waive for you from my days and my nights, that would be permissible for him, and there is no blame upon both of them'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or desertion'. He said: This is when the woman is with him, and he does not find her pleasing, so he desires to divorce her. So she says to him, 'Keep me and do not divorce me, and I will leave for you what is upon your back (the dower), and give you from my wealth, and free you from my day and my night,' so all that is agreeable to him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if you fear a discord between the two, then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' He said: 'The two judges stipulate; if they wish, they separate them, and if they wish, they gather them. So whether they separate or gather, it is valid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the two judges to separate them until they consult the man and the woman and stipulate upon them both: "If we so desire, we will gather you together, and if we so desire, we will separate you both."' So if they gather them both, it is valid/permissible; and if they separate them both, it is valid/permissible.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The two judges stipulate: If they wish, they separate [the couple], and if they wish, they gather [them]. So if they gather them, it is valid, and if they separate them, it is valid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' What is your view if the two judges seek permission, so they both say to the man and the woman, 'Is it not that you have both made your matter to us regarding reconciliation and separation?' So the man and the woman say, 'Yes'. So they bear witness with that upon them both. Is their separation allowed? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but it does not happen except upon purity of the woman, from without copulation from the husband.' It was said to him (peace be upon him), 'What is your view if one of the two judges says, 'I have separated them,' and the other says, 'I have not separated them'?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Separation does not happen until they both agree upon the separation. So when they are both gathered upon the separation, their separation is allowed.'

And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, and others, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' He said: 'It is not for the two judges to effect separation until they are instructed for it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the missing person, so he said: The missing person, when four years have passed for him, the ruler sends or writes to the region in which he is absent. If no trace is found for him, the ruler orders his guardian to spend upon her. Whatever he spends upon her, she is his wife. I said, 'Suppose she says, 'I want what the women want.' He said: 'That is not for her, nor is it honorable. If his guardian or his representative does not spend upon her, he is ordered to divorce her, and that becomes an obligatory divorce for her.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the lost one, how should his wife be dealt with? He (peace be upon him) said: If she is silent from it and has been patient, she would be left alone, but if she raises her matter to the ruler, her term is four years. Then he should write to the region in which he disappeared. So let him ask about him, and if there is news of him being alive, she has to be patient, and if there is no news about him, until the four years have passed, he would call the guardian of the lost husband, so he would say to him, ‘Is there wealth for the lost one?’ So if there was wealth for the lost for him, it would be spent upon her until his living from his death would be known. And if there is no wealth for him, he would say to the guardian, ‘Spend upon her. So if he were to do that, so there is no way for her to be remarried, and if he does not spend upon her, the ruler would compel him that he should divorce with one divorce during the inception of the waiting period and she is pure. Thus a divorce of the guardian would be a divorce of the husband. So if her husband were to come before the fulfillment of her waiting period, from the day the guardian divorced her, so it would be inevitable for him to revert to her, for she is his wife, and she is with him upon the two (remaining) divorces. So if her waiting period has passed before he is (found) alive, or he returns, so she is free for the marriage, and there is no way for the first (husband) upon her’.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman from whom her husband is absent for four years, and he did not spend upon her, and it is not known whether he is alive or dead. Is his guardian compelled to divorce her? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. And if there is no guardian for him, the ruler divorces her. I said: If the guardian says, 'I shall spend upon her,' He (peace be upon him) said: So he is not compelled to divorce her. I said: What is your view if she says, 'I want what the women want, and I am not patient, and will not sit as I am'? He (peace be upon him) said: That is not for her, nor is it honourable, when he spends upon her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the lost one (al-mafqud), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is known that he is in a land, she waits for him forever until his death comes to her or his divorce comes to her. And if it is not known where he is from the whole of the earth, and no letter comes from him, nor any news, then she goes to the Imam (peace be upon him). He orders her to wait for four years, and he seeks him in the earth. So if no trace is found for him until four years pass, he orders her to observe the waiting period (iddah) of four months and ten days, then she becomes permissible for men. So if her husband comes after her waiting period has expired, it is not for him any reversion to her. And if he comes while she is in her waiting period of four months and ten days, then he is in control with reverting back to her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the death of a man is announced to his family, or they are informed that he has divorced her, so she observes the waiting period, then she remarries, and her husband comes afterwards, then the first [husband] is more rightful with her than this latter one, whether he entered with her or did not enter with her, and for her is the dower from the latter with what he made permissible of her private part. He (peace be upon him) said: And it is not for the latter one that he remarries her, ever. He (peace be upon him) said: And it is not for the latter one that he remarries her, ever.

Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from al-Ala', and Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: 'I asked him about two men who testified upon an absent man in the presence of a woman that he had divorced her. So the woman observed the waiting period and remarried. Then the absent husband arrived and claimed that he had not divorced her, and one of the two witnesses belied himself. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no claim for the later one upon her, and the dower is taken from the one who testified and returned to the later one, and the first one has control over her, and she observes the waiting period from the later one, and the first one does not approach her until her waiting period expires.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man whose family reckoned that he had died or been killed, so his wife married [another] and his concubine married [another]. So each one of them gave birth from her husband. Then the first husband and the master of the concubine came. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He takes his wife, for he is more rightful with her, and he takes his concubine and her child, or he takes compensation from her price.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Baseer and others from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding two witnesses who testified for a woman that her husband had divorced her or had died, so she remarried, then her (former) husband came. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are whipped the legal penalty (Hadd) and are liable for the dower to the husband for what they deceived him with. Then she observes the waiting period and returns to her first husband.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the death of a man is announced to his family, or she is informed that he has divorced her, so she observes the waiting period, then remarries. So her first husband comes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first (husband) is more rightful with her than the later one, whether he has copulated with her or not copulated with her, and for her is the dower from the later one with what he had permitted from her relief'.

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who said to another man: 'Write, O so-and-so, to my wife regarding her divorce,' or 'Write to my slave regarding his emancipation' — does that constitute a divorce or an emancipation? He said: Neither a divorce nor an emancipation comes into effect until he utters it with his tongue or writes it with his own hand, while intending the divorce or the emancipation, and this must be done by him in accordance with (the counting of) the new moons and with witnesses, and he must be absent from his wife.
