I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man wrote [a document for] the divorce of his wife or the emancipation of his slave, then he changed his mind and erased it.' He said: 'That is not a divorce nor an emancipation until he speaks it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman to whom the obituary of her husband was brought, so she observed the waiting period and remarried. Then her first husband came, so he separated from her and the second husband separated from her. How long does she observe the waiting period to be permissible to the people? He (peace be upon him) said: Three quroo' (menstrual periods). And indeed, her womb is cleared by three quroo', making her permissible to all the people. Zurara said: And that is because some people said: She observes two waiting periods, one waiting period from each one. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rejected that saying: She observes three quroo', so she becomes permissible to the men.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, Regarding a woman whose husband's obituary came to her, so she remarried. Then her first husband came. So he divorced her, and the second one divorced her. Ibrahim al-Nakhai'i said she must observe two waiting periods. Zurara brought her to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he said: She must observe one waiting period.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'A woman from the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so is my husband. I gave him my belly (for bearing his children) and supported him in his worldly and afterlife affairs, yet he did not find anything displeasing in me. I complain about him to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to you.' He (peace be upon him) asked: 'From what are you complaining?' She said to him: 'He said to me today, "You are prohibited to me like the back of my mother," and he has thrown me out of my house. So look into my matter.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah has not yet revealed to me a Book by which I may judge between you and your husband, and I dislike that I become one of the pretenders.' So she began weeping and complaining of what was with her to Allah and to His Messenger, and she departed. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, heard her argument with His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) regarding her husband, and what she complained to him. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed a Quranic verse because of that. Allah has heard the words of her who pleads with you about her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your contention; indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing. (As for) those of you who put away their wives by likening their backs to the backs of their mothers, they are not their mothers; their mothers are no others than those who gave them birth; and indeed, they utter a hateful word and a falsehood; and indeed, Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent for the woman, so she came to him. He said to her: 'Bring me your husband.' So she brought him. He said to him: 'Did you say to this wife of yours, "You are prohibited to me like the back of my mother"?' He said: 'I had said that to her.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has revealed a Quranic verse regarding you and your wife.' So he recited to him what Allah had revealed from His Words: "Allah has heard the words of her who pleads with you about her husb

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no divorce except what is intended by it as divorce, and there is no Zihar except what is intended by it as Zihar.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Zahaar, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from everyone who is with close un-marriageable relationship, a mother, or a sister, or a paternal aunt, or a maternal aunt, and Al Zahaar does not happen during a vow'. I said, 'So how does it happen?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The man is saying to his wife, and she is pure (from menstruation) from without copulation, 'You are prohibited unto me like a back of my mother', or 'my sister', and he is intending the Zahaar by that'.
Ibn Fazzal, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Zahaar does not occur except upon the similar place of the divorce.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira and others, who said: Hamza ibn Humran married the daughter of Bukayr. When it was the night she was brought to him, the women said to him, 'You do not care about divorce, and it is not with anything in your presence, and we will not let her come to you until you perform Dhahar from the mothers of your children.' He said, so he did it. He mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he ordered him to go near them.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, all from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: Hamza ibn Humran married the daughter of Bukayr. So when he intended to enter with her (consummate the marriage), the women said to him, 'We will not let her come to you until you swear an oath to us.' And we are not pleased if you swear by emancipation (liberation of a slave), because you do not consider it anything. But swear to us by Zihar, and do Zihar from the mothers of your children and your female slaves. So he did Zihar from them. Then he mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is nothing upon you. Return to them.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who prays the prayer or performs ablution, then doubts regarding it afterwards, so he says: 'If I repeat the prayer or repeat the ablution, my wife will be unto me like the back of my mother,' and he swears upon that with divorce. He said: 'This is from the footsteps of Satan; there is nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have performed Zihar with my wife.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so emancipate a neck (slave).' He said, 'I have nothing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so fast for two consecutive months.' He said, 'I am not strong enough.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so feed sixty poor ones.' He said, 'I have nothing (with me).' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I shall give charity on your behalf,' and gave him dates for feeding sixty poor ones. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so give in charity with it.' He said, 'By the One Who sent you with the truth, I do not know anyone between these two mountains more in need of it than myself and my family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So go, eat and feed your family.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man says to his wife, And we asked him about the Zahaar, when does the expiation fall upon its perpetrator? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he intends to copulate with his wife.' I said: 'If he divorces her before he copulates with her, is there an expiation upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, the expiation has dropped from him.' I said: 'If he fasts part of it, then falls ill and breaks the fast, does he start again or complete what remains upon him?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he fasts a month and falls ill, he starts again; and if he exceeds the month by one day or two days, he builds upon what remains.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The free woman and the slave woman are equal, except that upon the slave is half of what is upon the free from the expiation, and there is no emancipation upon him nor charity, but rather upon him is the fasting of a month.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abdul Jabbar and Al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Zahir from his slave girl, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The free woman and the slave woman are equal in that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about a man who performed Zihar from his wife five times or more, so he said: Ali (peace be said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'For each time, there is an expiation.' He said: And I asked him about a man who performed Zihar from his wife, then divorced her before he copulated with her; is there an expiation? He said: 'No.' He said: And I asked him about Zihar upon the free woman and the slave woman, so he said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'If he performed Zihar in Sha'ban and did not find what he could emancipate?' He said: 'He should wait until he fasts the month of Ramadan, then he should fast two consecutive months.' And if he performed Zihar while he was a traveler, he should wait until he returns. If he fasts and attains wealth, let him fulfill that which he had begun with.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the owned slave, is there Zihar upon him? So he said: Half of what is upon the free person, from the fasting, and there is no expiation upon him of a charity, nor an emancipation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had ten slave girls, so he did Zahaar from all of them together by one speech. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him are ten expiations.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and one other, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: When he copulates for the second time before he has expiated, so upon him is another expiation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no differing in this'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Sayf al-Tammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man says to his wife, You are unto me like the back of my sister, or my paternal aunt, or my maternal aunt. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah has only mentioned the mothers, and in this is the prohibition.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Some of your mawali allege that when a man speaks with Zahaar, the expiation becomes obligatory upon him, whether he violates the oath or not, and they say that his violation is his speaking with Zahaar, and the expiation is made upon him as a punishment for the speech; and some of them allege that the expiation does not become obligatory upon him until he violates the matter upon which he swore, so if he violates it, the expiation becomes obligatory upon him, and otherwise there is no expiation upon him.' So he (peace be upon him) signed with his own handwriting: 'The expiation is not obligatory until the violation becomes obligatory.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Mahran asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Zahir from four women, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He must expiate for each one of them with an expiation.' And he asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Zahir from his wife and his slave girl, 'What is upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him for each one of them is an expiation: freeing a neck, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Fuzayl ibn Yasaar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about an owned man who pronounced Zahaar from his wife, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Zahaar does not occur, nor Ila', until he copulates with her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who says to his wife, 'She is unto him like the back of his mother.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The freeing of a neck, or fasting for two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people, and the freeing of a neck is sufficient for it a child who was born in Islam.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, and Ibn Bukayr, and Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The perpetrator of Zahaar, when he divorces, the expiation drops off from him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Zayyat, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I performed Zihar with my wife.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'How did you say it?' I said, 'I said to her,
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Zahaar does not occur upon anger.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the obligatory Zihar. He said: 'That which the man intends by it, exactly.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When the woman says, "My husband is prohibited to me like the back of my mother," then there is no expiation upon her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And a man from the Ansar, from the Banu Al-Najjar, came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, "I pronounced Zihar from my wife, then I had intercourse with her before I expiated."' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what carried you to do that?' He said, 'When I pronounced Zihar, I saw the glitter of her anklet and the whiteness of her leg in the moonlight, so I had intercourse with her before I expiated.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Alienate her until you expiate,' and he ordered him with one expiation and that he should seek forgiveness from Allah.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, or someone else, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed Zahr, then divorced: He (peace be upon him) said: The expiation is dropped from him if he divorces before he resumes sexual intercourse. It was said: What if he reverts to her? He (peace be upon him) said: If he divorced her specifically to drop the expiation from him, then he reverted to her, the expiation remains obligatory upon him always when he resumes sexual intercourse. And if he divorced her and he did not intend anything from that, then there is no harm if he reverts to her, and there is no expiation upon him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, all from Safwan, who said: Abu Uyayna narrated to us from Zurara. He said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I performed Zihar with a mother of a child of mine, then I had intercourse with her, then I expiated.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is what the Faqih (jurist) does; when he has intercourse, he expiates.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performed Zihar, then had intercourse before he expiated. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: Is this not how the Faqih (jurist) acts?

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who does Zahir from his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him expiate.' I said, 'Supposing he copulates before he expiates?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has exceeded a limit from the limits of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and let him seek forgiveness of Allah, and let him refrain (from his wife) until he has expiated.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Zahaar is of two types: one in which the expiation is required before copulation, and the other after it. That which requires expiation before copulation is the one in which he says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and does not say, 'If I do such and such with you.' And that which requires expiation after copulation is the one in which he says, 'You are to me like the back of my mother if I approach you.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, from Muawiya ibn Hakim, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man swears an oath of Zihar and then breaks it, the expiation is upon him before he copulates; and if the Zihar was from him without being an oath, then the expiation is upon him after he copulates.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Yazeed al-Kunasy, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who pronounced Zihar from his wife, then divorced her with a single divorce. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he divorces her with a single divorce, the Zihar becomes invalid, and the divorce demolishes the Zihar.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I said, 'Is there for him to revert to her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, she is his wife. So if he were to revert back to her, it would obligate upon him what obligates upon the perpetrator of Zihar from before they touch each other.' I said, 'So if he were to leave her until her term expires and she is in control of herself, then he maries her after that, would the Zihar necessitate upon him before he touches her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. She was irrevocably divorced from him, and in control of herself.' I said, 'So if he does Zihar from her, and does not touch her, and leaves her, not touching her except that he sees her naked without touching her, would anything from that necessitate upon him?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'She is his wife, and it is not prohibited on him copulating with her, but it obligates upon him what obligates upon the perpetrator of Zihar, before he copulates with her, and she is his wife.' I said, 'Supposing if she were to raise it to the Sultan (ruler) and says, 'This is my husband, and he had done Zihar from me, and has kept me, not touching me fearing that it would obligate upon him what obligates upon the perpetrator of Zihar'.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not upon him that he should be compelled to emancipation, and fasting, and feeding, if there does not happen to be for him what he can emancipate with, and give charity with, from before he touches her, and from after having touched her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So if he is able to emancipate, then it is upon the Imam to compel him to emancipation and charity, from before he touches her, and from after he touches her.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who pronounced Zahaar from his wife, then divorced her before he copulated with her, so she became irrevocably divorced from him. Is there an expiation upon him? He (He) said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from one of his men, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who said to his wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' or 'like her hand,' or 'like her belly,' or 'like her private part,' or 'like herself,' or 'like her heel.' Does that constitute Zahaar, and does it necessitate upon him what necessitates the perpetrator of Zahaar? He said: The perpetrator of Zahaar, when he does Zahaar from his wife, saying 'She is like the back of his mother,' or 'her hand,' or 'her leg,' or 'her hair,' or 'anything from her,' intending by that the prohibition, then the expiation becomes obligatory upon him in every little or much of it. And similarly, when he says it to some of the close relatives (for marriage), the expiation becomes obligatory upon him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The cursing (li'an) does not occur until the man copulates with his wife.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Al-mula'ana (mutual cursing/divorce) and al-ila' (oath of abstinence) do not occur except after consummation (entry).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, And (as for) those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except for themselves He said: He is the slanderer who slanders his wife. So when he has slandered her, then he accepts that he had lied against her. He would be whipped the legal penalty (Hadd), and his wife would be returned to him. And if he refuses except that he stands by it, so he should testify against her with four testimonies by Allah that he is from the truthful ones, and fifthly he should curse himself in it, if he was from the liars. So if she intends to repel the punishment from herself, and the punishment is the stoning, she should testify with four testimonies with Allah that he is from the liars, and the fifth that the Wrath of Allah would be upon her if he was from the truthful ones. So if she does not do that, she would be stoned, and if she does do it, it would stave off the legal penalty (Hadd) from her, then she would not be Permissible for him until the Day of Judgement. I said, What is your view if there is separation between the two of them and for her is a child, so it dies. He said: Its mother would inherit it, and if its mother dies, its maternal uncles would inherit it, and the one who says that he is a son of adultery would be whipped the legal penalty (Hadd). I said, Would the child be returned to him if he accepts it? He said: No, and there is no honour, and the father would not inherit it, but the son would inherit him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Indeed, 'Abbad al-Basri asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I was present, 'How does a man perform li'an (cursing) with the woman?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a man from the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is your view if a man enters his house and finds a man copulating with his wife, what should he do?' He said, 'So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned away from him, and that man went away, and that man was the one who was afflicted by that from his wife.' He said: 'So Revelation descended upon him from the Presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with the judgement regarding both of them. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent to that man and called him, and said to him, 'Are you the one who saw a man with your wife?' He said, 'Yes.' He said to him, 'Go and bring me your wife, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed the judgement regarding you and regarding her.' He said: 'So her husband presented her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) paused both of them, then said to the husband, 'Testify with four testimonies by Allah that you are from the truthful ones regarding what you are accusing her with.' He said, 'He testified.' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Wait,' and he advised him, then said, 'Fear Allah, for the curse of Allah is severe.' Then he said to him, 'Testify the fifth that the curse of Allah be upon you if you are from the liars.' He said, 'He testified.' Then he commanded for him to be set aside. Then he said to the woman, 'Testify with four testimonies by Allah that your husband is from the liars regarding what he is accusing you with.' She said, 'She testified.' Then he said to her, 'Wait,' and he advised her and said to her, 'Fear Allah, for the wrath of Allah is severe.' Then he said to her, 'Testify the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon you if your husband is from the truthful ones regarding what he is accusing you with.' She said, 'She testified.' He said, 'So he separated the two of them and said to both of them, 'Do not join in marriage ever, after what you both have cursed with.'

Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from 'Abbad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man whom the Imam paused for the *li'an* (cursing), so he testified with two testimonies, then hesitated/backed down, so he belied himself before he was finished with the *li'an*. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped the penalty (*hadd*) of the slanderer, and there is no separation between him and his wife.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man slanders his wife, he does not perform li'an with her unless he says, 'I saw a man between her legs committing adultery with her.' He (peace be upon him) was asked about the man who slanders his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He performs li'an with her, then they are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever. If he confesses against himself before the li'an, he is whipped with the hadd penalty, and she remains his wife.' And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the free woman whose husband accuses her, and he is a slave. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He performs li'an with her, then they are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever. If he confesses against himself after the li'an, he is whipped with the hadd penalty, and she remains his wife.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about the free man who has a slave girl, and he accuses her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He performs li'an with her.' And I asked him about the woman subjected to li'an by her husband, who denies her child, and he performs li'an with her and separates from her. Then he says afterwards, 'The child is my child,' while lying about himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the woman, she does not return to him ever. As for the child, I return it to him when he claims it, but I do not consider it his child. There is no inheritance for him (the father in the child), and the son inherits from the father, but the father does not inherit the son, and its inheritance goes to its maternal uncles. If its father does not claim it, then its maternal uncles inherit it, and it does not inherit them. If anyone calls him the son of adultery, he is whipped with the hadd penalty.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the free man, is there cursing between him and the slave girl? He said: Yes, and between the slave man and the free woman, and between the slave and the slave woman, and between the Muslim and the Jewess and the Christianess; and they do not inherit each other, nor does the free man and the slave woman inherit each other.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed li'an with his wife while she was pregnant, then he claimed her child after she had given birth, and asserted that it was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The child is returned to him, and he is not whipped, because the li'an has passed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who slandered his wife, and she was mute, he (peace be upon him) said: They are separated.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Jameel, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the cursing man and the cursing woman, how should they both be dealt with? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Imam (peace be upon him) would sit with his back towards the Qiblah, so he would place both of them in front of him facing the Qiblah, aligned with him, and he would begin with the man, then the woman, and the woman upon whom stoning is obligated, would be stoned from behind her back, and would not be stoned from her face, because the striking and the stoning do not hit the face; they are struck upon the body, upon all of the parts.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), and I said to him, 'May Allah keep you well! How is the cursing (Al-Mula'ana)?' He said, 'He said: The Imam sits, and makes his back towards the Qiblah, and makes the man to be on his right, and the woman on his left.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who performed li'an (cursing) with his wife, so he swore four testimonies by Allah, then abstained (from swearing) in the fifth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he abstained in the fifth, then she is his wife, and he is whipped; and if the woman abstained from that, when the oath is upon her, then upon her is similar to that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about the cursing, would he curse standing or sitting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The cursing and what resembles it is from standing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about a man who divorced his wife before he entered (consummated) with her, so she claimed that she was pregnant. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she establishes the proof that he loosened the veil (consummated), then denies the child, he can curse her, then she is irrevocably divorced from him, and upon him is the complete dower.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali bin Raib, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed *li'an* (cursing) with his wife while she was pregnant, and her pregnancy had become evident. So he denied what was in her belly. So when she gave birth, he claimed her child and confessed to it, and claimed that it was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His child is returned to him, and he inherits him, and he is not whipped, because the *li'an* has passed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, that he was asked about a slave who slandered his wife. He said: 'They both curse each other (perform li'an) just as the free men curse each other.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who forges a lie upon his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped, then they are separated, and li'an (cursing) is not performed between them until he says, "I bear witness that I saw you doing such and such."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said: The cursing (li'an) does not occur except by the denial of a child. And he said: When a man slanders his wife, he would curse her.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man cannot perform li'an (cursing) with the woman with the woman whom he is temporarily married to.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who slandered his wife with adultery, and she is mute, deaf, not hearing what he said. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she has proof (witnesses), so they testify in the presence of the Imam, he is whipped the legal penalty (Hadd), and they are separated between the two of them, then she is not permissible for him forever; and if there is no proof, so she is prohibited unto him for as long as he stays with her, and there is no sin upon her from him.'

From him, from Al-Hasan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a woman who slandered her husband, and he was deaf, he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are separated between her and him, and she is not permissible for him ever.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the mute woman, how does her husband perform the cursing (li'an) with her? He (peace be upon him) said: They are separated, and she does not become permissible for him ever.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The cursing (li'an) does not occur until he claims that he has seen it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a free man who has a slave girl under him, or a slave who has a free woman under him: what is the number of her divorces and what is her waiting period? He said: The Sunnah regarding women in divorce is that if she is a free woman, her divorce is three, and her waiting period is three menstrual periods; and if a free man has a slave girl under him, her divorce is two divorces, and her waiting period is one menstrual period.

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'When the free woman is under the slave, so the divorce and the waiting period is with the women, meaning he divorces her three times, and she waits for three menstruations.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: Indeed, Ibn Shubrumah said, 'Divorce is for the man.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Divorce is for the women,' and the clarification of that is that the slave may have a free woman under him, so her divorce is three, and the free man may have a slave girl under him, so her divorce is two divorces.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the slave man to the free woman is three divorces, and the divorce of the free man to the slave woman is two divorces.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawood bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The divorce of a free man when there is a slave girl with him is two divorces, and the divorce of a free woman when she is under the ownership of a slave is three.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If the slave and his wife belong to one master, then the master takes her when he wills, and when he wills, he returns her. And he (peace be upon him) said: The divorce of the slave is not valid if he and his wife belong to one master, except if the slave belongs to one man and the woman belongs to another man, and he married her with the permission of his master and the permission of her master. So if he divorces her while in this status, then his divorce is valid.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Lays al-Muradi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave woman, is her divorce allowed? He said: If she is your bondmaid, then no. Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says: 'A slave, the property of another, who has no power over anything.' And if she is a bondmaid of other people, or a free woman, her divorce is allowed.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who permits his slave to marry a free woman or a slave girl of a people; is the divorce right with the master or with the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: The divorce is with the slave.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man whose slave married a free woman, so he said: The divorce is in the hand of the slave. So if he married her without the permission of his master, then the divorce is in the hand of the master.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqteen from Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who married his slave to a free girl, so he said: The divorce is in the hand of the slave. He said, And I asked him about a man who married his slave girl to a free man, so he said: The divorce is in the hand of the free man. And I asked him about a man who married his slave to his slave girl, so he said: The divorce is in the hand of the master. And I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl and for her was a slave husband, so he said: Selling her is her divorce.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): 'A man marries his slave girl to a free man, then he wants to remove her from him and take from him half the dower.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who married her to him sees what you are upon and makes a religion by it, then for him is that he removes her from him and takes from him half the dower, because he has proceeded from that upon the understanding that that is for the master. And if the husband does not know this, and he is from the masses of the people, the master would deal with him upon what he deals with one similar to him, so he has proceeded upon the understanding of that from him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his slave girl to a free man, or to a slave of other people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for him to remove her. So if he sells her, and the one who buys her wishes to remove her from her husband, he may do so.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man has a slave girl and he marries her to his owned slave, he separates them if he wishes, and joins them if he wishes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The divorce of a male slave for his female slave is two divorces, and her waiting period is two menstruations if she menstruates; and if she does not menstruate, then her waiting period is a month and a half.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the slave girl, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Two divorces'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Usama from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Umar stood on the pulpit and said, 'What do you say, O companions of Muhammad, regarding the divorce of a slave girl?' So no one answered him. Then he said, 'What do you say, O owner of the Ma'afari cloak?' — meaning Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). So he gestured with his hand, indicating two divorces.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The waiting period (iddah) of the slave girl is two menstruations. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'When she does not menstruate, then [her waiting period is] half the waiting period of the free woman.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a slave girl whose husband had divorced her with two divorces, then had sexual relations with her, so he had him whipped.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ib, and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the slave girl and the free woman, both of them, when their husbands die, are equal regarding the waiting period (iddah), except that the free woman observes mourning (hudd) and the slave girl does not observe mourning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl when she is divorced, what is her waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Two menstruations, or two months, until she menstruates.' I said, 'Supposing her husband dies from her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) said regarding the mothers of the children: They should not get married until they observe the waiting period of four months and ten (days), and they are slaves.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the slave girl whose master dies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She observes the waiting period of the one widowed from her husband.' I said: 'If a man marries her before her waiting period ends?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He separates from her, then he marries her with a new marriage after the completion of her waiting period.' I said: 'So where is what has reached us from your father (peace be upon him) regarding the man who marries the woman during her waiting period, that she does not become permissible for him forever?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is an ignorant (person).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'When a man has a concubine under him and he frees her,' so he said, 'It is not permissible for her to marry until her waiting period (iddah) of three months has elapsed, and if her master dies, her waiting period is four months and ten days.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who had a slave girl, so he copulated with her, then freed her, and she had menstruated while with him, a menstruation after he had copulated with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She observes a waiting period of two menstruations.'

And by his chain, from Al-Halby who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who emancipated his concubine, is it correct for him that he marries her without a waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So others?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until she observes the waiting period of three months'. He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who copulated with his slave girl, is it correct for him that he marries her before she observes the waiting period?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'How much is her waiting period?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One menstruation or two'.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions, who said: Regarding a man who emancipated a mother of his children, then died from her before she had fulfilled her waiting period. He said: 'She would observe the waiting period of four months and ten (days), and if she was pregnant, she would wait with the further of the two terms'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who emancipated his female slave at the time of his death, so he said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of the free woman whose husband has died, four months and ten (days). He said, And I asked him about a man who emancipated his female slave while he was alive, and he had already copulated with her, so he said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of the free divorced woman, three menstrual periods.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood Al-Raqy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Mudabbira (slave woman promised freedom upon her master's death), when her master dies, that her waiting period is four months and ten days from the day her master dies, if her master had copulated with her. It was said to him, 'Supposing the man emancipates his slave girl before his death, by an hour or by a day, then he dies.' He said: 'This one observes the waiting period of three menstruations or three pure periods from the day her master emancipated her.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'dan bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man has a concubine of his, and she has given birth to him, and her child has died, then he emancipates her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for her to marry until her waiting period of three months has elapsed.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who had an Umm al-Walad (concubine who bore him a child), so he married her to a man, and she bore him a boy. Then the man died, so she returned to her master. Is it for him to have intercourse with her? He said: She observes the waiting period from the husband, four months and ten days, then he has intercourse with her by ownership, without a new marriage contract.

Divorce of the Sunnah is (where) he divorces her with a (valid) divorce, meaning upon the purity (from menstruation) without copulation, with the testimony of two witnesses. Then he leaves her until she completes her menstrual periods ('idda). So when her menstrual periods are gone, she is irrevocably separated from him, and he would be a suitor among the (other) suitors — if she wishes she may marry him, and if she wishes not, then (she need not). And if he intends to return to her (ruju'), he should call witnesses to his returning to her before her menstrual periods pass, so she will be with him upon the previous divorce. He (the narrator) said: And Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: 'These are the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: "Divorce is (only permissible) twice, then retention in good fellowship or release with kindness" The second divorce is the release with kindness.'

Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'I would love it for the understanding man, when he intends to divorce his wife, that he should divorce her with the divorce of the Sunnah.' He (Zurara) said: 'Then he (the Imam) said: And it is that which God — Mighty and Majestic — said: «Perhaps God will bring about a matter after that» — meaning after the divorce and the completion of the waiting period ('idda), the remarriage of both of them, before she marries another husband.' He said: 'How just and how accommodating it is for them both together: that he divorce her in a state of ritual purity without intercourse, with a single pronouncement of divorce before witnesses, then leave her until her term expires — three months or three menstrual cycles — and then he may become one suitor among the suitors.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran — or someone else — from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: I asked him about the divorce of the Sunnah. He said: The divorce of the Sunnah is that when a man intends to divorce his wife, he leaves her — if he has consummated the marriage — until she menstruates and then becomes pure. When she becomes pure, he divorces her once with the testimony of two witnesses, then leaves her until she observes an 'iddah of three menstrual cycles. When the three cycles have passed, she is irrevocably separated from him by one (divorce), and her ex-husband becomes a suitor among suitors: if she wishes, she may marry him, and if she wishes, she may not. If he marries her with a new dowry, she is with him with two (divorces) remaining and one having passed. If he then divorces her with another (divorce) in a state of purity and without intercourse, with the testimony of two witnesses, then leaves her until her menstrual cycles pass — if her cycles pass before he returns to her — she is irrevocably separated from him by two (divorces), she controls her own affairs, and she is free to marry. Her ex-husband is a suitor among suitors: if she wishes she may marry him, if she wishes she may not. If he marries her with a new marriage and new dowry, she is with him with one (divorce) remaining and two having passed. If he intends to divorce her with a divorce after which she is not lawful for him until she marries another husband, he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then has witnessed against her divorce one pronouncement — then she is not lawful for him until she marries another husband. As for the revocable divorce (talaq al-raj'ah): he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then divorces her with the testimony of two witnesses, then returns to her and has intercourse with her, then waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has two witnesses witness another divorce. Then he returns to her and has intercourse with her, then waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has two witnesses witness the third divorce. Then she is never lawful for him until she marries another husband, and it is upon her to observe an 'iddah of three menstrual cycles from the day he pronounced the third divorce. If he divorces her

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, all together from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about divorce according to the Sunnah — how should a man divorce his wife? He said: He divorces her during a period of purity, before her waiting period, without sexual intercourse, with witnesses. So if he divorces her once and then leaves her until her term expires, she is irrevocably separated from him and he becomes a suitor among the suitors. And if he reverts to her, then she is with him counting one previous divorce, and two divorces remain. So if he divorces her for the second time and leaves her until her term expires, she is irrevocably separated from him. And if he calls witnesses for his reversion to her before her term expires, then she is with him counting two previous divorces, and one divorce remains. So if he divorces her for the third time, she is irrevocably separated from him, and she will not be permissible for him until she marries another husband. She inherits him and he inherits her for as long as there is a right of reversion for him over her, from the two first divorces.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife after having cohabited with her, with two just witnesses. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not a valid divorce.' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How is the divorce of the Sunnah?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He divorces her when she is purified from her menstruation, before he cohabits with her, with two just witnesses, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said in His Book. So if he violates that, he must be returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' So I said to him: 'But if he divorces her during a period of purity from without sexual intercourse, with one witness and two women?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is not permissible in divorce; however their testimony is allowed along with others in the matter of blood, when she is present.' So I said: 'What if he called two Nasibi men as witnesses for the divorce — would that be a valid divorce?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is born upon the natural disposition (fitrah), his testimony is accepted for divorce, after you recognise goodness from him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaina, from Ibn Bukayr and others, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Indeed, the divorce which God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded in His Book, and which the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) established as Sunnah, is that the man should separate from the wife. Then when she menstruates and becomes pure from her menstruation, he should call two just men as witnesses to a divorce pronouncement while she is pure and without sexual intercourse. And he is more entitled to take her back (rij'ah) as long as three quru' have not elapsed. And every divorce apart from this is invalid — it is not a divorce.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce of the Sunnah is: when the woman becomes pure (from menstruation), let him divorce her once in that state, without (having had) sexual intercourse (with her since her purification), keeping witnesses upon her divorce. So when he intends to revert to her, he should keep witnesses upon the return.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: When a man intends divorce, he should divorce her before her waiting period, without sexual intercourse. So if he divorces her once, then leaves her until her term expires, he may — if he so desires — propose along with the other suitors. If he reverts to her before her term expires, or after it, she would be with him upon one (previous) divorce. If he also divorces her a second time, and desires to propose to her along with the suitors — if he had left her until her term expired — and if he desires to revert to her before her term expires, and he does so, then she is with him upon two (previous) divorces. If he then divorces her for the third time, she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband. And she inherits from him and he inherits from her, as long as she is in the blood (of menstruation) from the first two divorces.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who had a slave girl under his ownership, so he divorced her according to the Sunnah, then she became irrevocably divorced from him, then he bought her after that before she married another husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) has judged regarding this: a Verse permits her and another Verse prohibits her, and I myself and my sons would prohibit from her.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a free man who had a slave girl under his ownership. He divorced her with an irrevocable divorce, then bought her. Is it permissible for him to copulate with her? He said: No.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who married an owned woman, then divorced her, then bought her afterwards. Is she permissible for him? He (peace be upon him) said: No, until she marries another husband.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Bureyd al-Ajli from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Regarding a man who has a slave girl under him, so he divorces her with two divorces, then buys her afterwards. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to marry her until she marries another husband, and until he enters with her in a manner similar to what she went out from him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabaty, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Every Muslim, between two Muslims, who reneges from Islam and denies the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) of his prophethood and belies him, then his blood is permissible for whoever hears that from him, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him on the day he reneges, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband has died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him if they bring him to him, and he does not ask him to repent.'

And from him, from Al-A'ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who desires away from Islam and disbelieves in what was revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, there is no repentance for him, and his killing is obligatory, and his wife is divorced from him, and what he leaves is distributed among his children.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ib, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a Christian woman who was married to a Christian, and he divorced her. Is there a waiting period upon her similar to the waiting period of a Muslim woman? He said: No, because the People of the Book are slaves (in domain) of the Imam. Do you not see that they pay the Jizya to him just as the slave pays the tribute to his master? He said: And whoever from them embraces Islam, he is free, and the Jizya is dropped from him. I said: So what is her waiting period if a Muslim man intends to marry her? He said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of a slave woman, two menstruations, or forty-five days, before she becomes Muslim. I said to him: And if she becomes Muslim after he has divorced her? He said: If she becomes Muslim after he has divorced her, then her waiting period is the waiting period of a Muslim woman. I said: And if he dies from her, and she is a Christian and he is a Christian, and a man from the Muslims intends to marry her? He said: The Muslim man cannot marry her until she observes the waiting period from the Christian, of four months and ten days, which is the waiting period of a Muslim woman whose husband has died. I said to him: How is it that when she is divorced her waiting period is that of a slave woman, and her waiting period when her husband dies from her is that of a free Muslim woman, while you mention that they are slaves of the Imam? He said: Her waiting period in divorce is not like her waiting period when her husband dies from her. Then he said: Indeed, the slave woman and the free woman, both of them, when their husband dies from them, are equal in the waiting period, except that the free woman observes mourning (Iddah with restriction) and the slave woman does not observe mourning.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said: The waiting period of the non-Muslim woman (Al-Ajlaja) when she becomes a Muslim is the waiting period of the divorced woman, when she intends to marry someone else.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yaqoub al-Sarraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Christian woman whose husband died while she was with him, and he was a Christian, what is her waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The waiting period of the free Muslim woman, four months and ten (days).'

And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a mother of a child (Umm al-Walad) of a Christian man who became a Muslim, can the Muslim man marry her? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, and her waiting period (Iddah) from the Christian man, when she becomes a Muslim, is the waiting period of a free divorced woman, being three months or three pure periods (Quroo'). So when her waiting period is completed, let him marry her if she desires.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Ibn Ribat, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr — both together — from Ibn Udhayna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, that he asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who says to his wife: 'You are forbidden unto me', or 'a stranger', or 'cut-off', or 'disavowed', or 'free'. He said: 'All of this is nothing. The divorce is only when he says to her at the beginning of the waiting period, after she has been purified from her menstruation, before he has intercourse with her: "You are divorced" or "Begin your waiting period", intending by that the divorce — and he calls two just men as witnesses to that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The divorce is that he says to her, Begin your waiting period (iddah), or he says to her, You are divorced.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'The divorce for the waiting period ('idda) is that the man divorces his wife at every period of purity (tuhr), sending a message to her: "Observe your waiting period, for so-and-so has divorced you."' He said: 'And he has the greater right to revoke it as long as her waiting period has not expired.'
He sends [a messenger] to her, and the messenger says: 'Begin your waiting period ('iddah), for so-and-so has separated from you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far the First (peace be upon him) who said: When a man comes to own his parents, or his sister, or his maternal aunt, or his paternal aunt, they are automatically emancipated. But he may own the son of his brother, and his paternal uncle; and he may own his brother, his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle through the breastfeeding relationship.

And by his chain, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'A man cannot own his father, nor his mother, nor his paternal aunt, nor his maternal aunt; but he can own his brother, and others from his male relatives.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Asad ibn Abi al-Ala, from Abu Hamza who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman — what she can own from her relatives. He said: Everyone, except five: her father, her mother, her son, her daughter, and her husband.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man owns his parents, or his sister, or his paternal aunt, or his maternal aunt, they are emancipated; and he may own the son of his brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle; and he may own his brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle through the breastfeeding relationship.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: regarding a woman who breast-fed the son of her slave girl: 'She emancipates him.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who takes his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister as slaves. So he said: 'As for the sister, she is emancipated the moment he owns her; and as for the brother, he may enslave him; and as for the two parents, they are both emancipated the moment he owns them both.' He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about the woman who breastfeeds her slave — can she take him as a slave? He said: 'She emancipates him, and it is an abhorrence (for her to breastfeed her slave).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Ubayd ibn Zurara who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what a man may own from among his relatives. He said: He cannot own his father, nor his mother, nor his sister, nor a daughter of his brother, nor a daughter of his sister, nor his paternal aunt, nor his maternal aunt; and he may own what is besides that from among the men from his relatives, and he cannot own his mother through the nursing (relationship).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipates his slave while he is in good financial condition, then later becomes needy. Is it permissible for him to sell him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when he is in need of that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Mudabbir (slave manumitted upon the master's death), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is in the status of the bequest; he returns in it and in whatever he desires from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Mudabbir (slave manumitted upon the owner's death), is he from the third (of the bequest)? So he said: 'Yes, and it is for the bequeather to retract [the bequest] during good health or illness, if it was his bequest.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who emancipated his slave girl while she was pregnant, so he said: If he knew of her pregnancy, then what is in her belly is of her status, and if he did not know, then what is in her belly is a slave.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa al-Kilabi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who emancipated her slave girl, and the slave girl gave birth to a precious girl. The woman did not know the status of the newborn: whether she is emancipated or not. He said to me: 'When was the pregnancy with the emancipated one? Was it before she emancipated her, or after she emancipated her?' I said: 'I do not know, but answer me regarding both (situations).' He said: 'If the woman emancipated her while she was pregnant, and she did not specify what was in her belly, then the slave girl is emancipated and the child is a slave. And if the pregnancy occurred only after the emancipation, then the child is emancipated along with the emancipation of its mother.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Aban ibn Taghlib who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated his slave girl, then married her to another man, so she bore children from him. Then her husband died and left children from her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her children are like her status. So when the one who emancipated their mother dies, they are free.' I said to him: 'Is it permissible for the one who emancipated their mother to retract his emancipation if he is in need?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is your view if their mother dies after the husband, and her children from the free husband remain? Is it permissible for her master to sell her children and retract the emancipation regarding them?' He said: 'No. Rather, he may only retract the emancipation of their mother if he is in need and she is pleased with that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Mudabbir (slave with arranged emancipation) is a slave, and for his master is the right to retract regarding his emancipation; if he so desires, he sells him, and if he so desires, he gifts him, and if he so desires, he makes him a dower. He (peace be upon him) said: And if his master leaves him upon the emancipation arrangement, and an event does not occur until his master dies, then the Mudabbir is free when his master dies, and he is from the third (of the bequest). He is at the status of a man who bequeaths with a bequest, then changes his mind for it, so he alters it before his death; and if he leaves it and does not change it until he dies, he is seized by it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ajaly, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who arranged (the emancipation) of an owned slave of his, a businessman, financially affluent. So the arranged slave buys a slave girl by the order of his master. So she gives birth to children from him. Then the arranged slave dies before his master. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that the entirety of what the arranged slave has left, from wealth or provisions, so it is for the one who had the arrangement for him, and I view that the mother of his children is for the one who had the arrangement, and I view that her children are (all) with the arrangement just like their father. So when the one who arranged for their father were to die, so they are free'.

And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who arranged (the emancipation of) an owned slave of his. Then he became needy to his price. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is his slave; if he so desires, he sells him, and if he so desires, he emancipates him, and if he so desires, he keeps him until he dies. So when the master dies, he is free, from his third (of the deceased's estate).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I contracted a slave girl for our orphans, and I stipulated upon her that if she is unable (to pay), she returns to slavery, and I am free from whatever I take from her.' He said to me, 'For you is your condition, and it will be said to you that Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The contracted slave is emancipated by the measure of what he has paid from his contract.' So say, 'Rather, that was from the words of Ali (peace be upon him) before the stipulation of the condition. So when the people stipulate, for them is their condition.' So I said to him, 'And what is the limit of inability?' He said, 'Our judges say that the inability of the contracted slave is that he delays the installment to the next installment, and until a year passes over him.' I said, 'So what do you say?' He said, 'No, and no honor. It is not for him to delay an installment from its term if that was in his condition.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The contracted slave (mukatab) is not permitted to have emancipation, nor gifting, nor marriage, nor testimony, nor Hajj, until he pays off the entirety of what is upon him. If his master had stipulated upon him that if he was unable to pay an installment from his installments, he would be returned to slavery.

Ibn Mahboub, from Umar bin Yazeed, from Bureyd al-Ajli, who said: I asked him about a man who contracted a slave of his for one thousand dirhams, and did not stipulate upon him when he contracted him that if he was unable to pay off his contract, he would be returned to slavery. And the contracted slave paid five hundred dirhams to his master. Then the contracted slave died, leaving wealth, and left a son who was an adult. He said: Half of whatever the contracted slave left of anything is for his master who contracted him, and the remaining half is for the son of the contracted slave, because the contracted slave died and half of him was free and half of him was a slave to the one who contracted him. So the son of the contracted slave is like his father: half of him is free and half of him is a slave. So if he pays to the one who contracted his father whatever remained upon his father, then he is free, and there is no way for anyone of the people over him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who contracted a slave girl of his. So the slave girl said, 'Whatever I pay off from my contract, so I would be free by it upon the accounting of that.' So he said to her, 'Yes.' So she paid off part of her contract and her master copulated with her after that. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he compelled her to that, he would be whipped from the legal penalty (Hadd) by the measurement of what she had paid off from her contract, and it would be staved off from the legal penalty (Hadd) by the measurement of what remains for him from her contract; and if she followed him, so she is an associate of his in the legal penalty (Hadd), and she would be whipped similar to what he would be whipped.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the contracted slave (mukatab). He said: 'What you stipulated upon him is valid/permissible upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The contracted slave, when he pays off something, is emancipated by the measure of what he pays off, except if his master had stipulated that if he was frustrated (from paying it) so he would be returned (into slavery). So for them is their stipulated conditions.

And by his chain, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you.' He said: 'That which you intend to contract upon him. Do not say, And regarding His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Contract with them if you know any good in them.' He said: 'The good is if you know that he has wealth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a contracted slave-woman who had paid two-thirds of her contract, and it had been stipulated upon her that if she became unable (to pay the remainder), she would be returned to slavery, and we would be released from what we had taken from her, and two installments had accumulated upon her. He (peace be upon him) said: She is returned (to slavery), and it pleases them (is accepted) what they took from her. And he (peace be upon him) said: It is not for her to delay the installment after its due date for one month, except with their permission.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the contracted slave (mukatab), when he pays part of his contract, he said: 'The people used not to stipulate conditions, and today they do stipulate, and the Muslims are bound by their conditions. So if it was stipulated upon him that if he was unable (to pay), he would be returned (to slavery), then he is returned; and if it was not stipulated upon him, he is not returned.' And regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Contract them if you know in them any good.' He said: 'Contract them if you know that they have wealth.' He said, 'And he said regarding the contracted slave: His master stipulates upon him that he should not marry except with his permission until he pays off his contract.' He said: 'It is befitting for him not to marry except with permission from him, for it is a condition for him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His Mighty and Majestic saying: 'Give them a deed of manumission if you know any good in them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you know that they have wealth and religion (piety).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the slave whose master contracts him (for manumission), and he knows that he does not possess little or much.
