He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should contract him, and if he asks the people, he is not prevented from contracting him on account of not having wealth, for Allah provides for the servants, some from others, and the Believer is assisted, and it is said, and the Benevolent is assisted.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who had a father who was a slave, and for his father was a wife, a contracted slave (mukattab) who had paid part of what was upon her. So the son of the slave said to her, 'Is it for you if I assist you in your contract until you pay what is upon you, with the stipulation that you do not have the choice regarding my father when you own yourself?' She said, 'Yes'. So he gave her in her contract, upon the stipulation that there is no choice for her upon him after she owns herself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The choice does not belong to her; the Muslims are upon their stipulations.'

And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated half of his slave girl, then he contracted her upon the other half after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him stipulate upon her that if she is unable to pay her installments, she will be returned to slavery regarding half of her body.' He said: 'If he wishes, there will be for him her service for a day, and for her a day.' I said: 'Is it for her that she marries in that state?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until she pays off all that is upon her regarding half of her body.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a man who contracted his slave. He said after contracting him, 'Gift me part of it, and I will hasten for you what was in my contract.' Is that permissible? He said: 'If it is a gift, there is no problem. And if he says, 'Settle from me, and I will hasten for you,' then it is not correct.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a contracted slave girl whom her master copulates with and she becomes pregnant, he said: 'A dower similar to hers is returned to her, and she works to pay off her price. If she is unable (to pay), then she is from the mothers of the children (ummahat al-awlad).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Give them the writing if you know any good in them, and give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You reduce from his installments (the agreed portions) which you did not intend to deduct from them, and do not exceed what is in your mind (or what you agreed upon).' So I said, 'How much?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) reduced from his owned slave one thousand from six thousand.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every slave who is tortured with, so he is free.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the owned slave is blinded, there is no slavery upon him; and the slave, when he suffers from leprosy, there is no slavery upon him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the owned slave is blinded, his master should emancipate him, and it would not be for him that he keeps him.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the owned slave is blinded, he has been emancipated.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub from Umar ibn Yazeed who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who intended to emancipate a slave of his, and his master had taken from him a tax that he had imposed upon him every year. The master was pleased with that, and the slave was pleased with that. So the slave acquired wealth in his trade besides what he used to give to his master from the tax. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he pays to his master what was imposed upon him, then whatever he acquires after the imposition is for the slave.' Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has imposed obligations upon the servants? So when they fulfill them to Him, He does not question them about what is besides that.' I said to him, 'So what do you think regarding the slave if he gives in charity from what he has acquired and emancipates (a slave) after the obligation which he used to pay to his master?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, that is obligatory for him.' I said, 'If the slave emancipates (a slave) from what he has acquired besides the obligation, for whom will be the guardianship (wala') of the emancipated one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He goes and the guardianship attaches to whomever he likes. So when he guarantees his blood-money (diyah) and his compensation, he becomes his master and inherits him.' I said to him, 'Did not the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a free person (sa'ibah), his guardianship does not belong to a slave like him.' I said, 'If the slave who emancipated him guarantees his blood-money and his actions, does that bind him, and he becomes his master and inherits him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not permissible, and a slave does not inherit a free man.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man contracts his owned slave and emancipates him, and he knows that for him is wealth, and the master did not exclude the wealth when he emancipated him, then it is for the slave.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), narrated: Regarding a man who emancipated his slave, and the slave had wealth. For whom is the wealth of the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: If he (the master) knew that the slave had wealth, it would follow him (the slave), otherwise it belongs to the emancipator (the master).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, Muhammad ibn Humran, and Zurara narrated, saying: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated his slave, and the slave had wealth. Whose is the wealth? He (peace be upon him) said: If he knew that there is wealth for him, his wealth follows him, otherwise it is for him (the slave).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu Jarir, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who said to his owned slave, 'You are free, and for me is your wealth'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would not begin with the freedom before the wealth. He should be saying to him, 'For me is your wealth, and you are free', with the pleasure of the slave, for that is more beloved to me (peace be upon him)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the emancipation of the coerced, so he said: 'His emancipation is not (a valid) emancipation.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the demented woman whose intellect has gone, is her selling and her charity allowed? He said: No. And about the divorce of the intoxicated man and his emancipation, he said: It is not allowed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, or he said, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Bureyd ibn Muawiya, and Fuzayl, and Ismail al-Azraq, and Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the bewitched (one under hypnosis or trance) is not emancipated with a (valid) emancipation.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ibn Ribat and Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Safwan all together from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The emancipation of the intoxicated person is not valid.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Umar ibn Yazeed from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a mother of the child (umm al-walad) being sold for debt; he said: 'Yes, for the price of her neck (slavery).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Any man who leaves a concubine who has a child, or has a child in her womb, or has no child, if her lord emancipates her, she is emancipated. And if he does not emancipate her until he dies, the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has preceded regarding her, and the Book of Allah is more rightful. If she has a child, and he leaves wealth, it is placed in the share of her child.' And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who left a slave girl who had given birth to a daughter from him, and she was small but could distinguish speech. So her mother was emancipated. The guardians of the father of the slave girl disputed regarding her, so he (peace be upon him) validated her emancipation for the mother.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who bought a slave girl and copulated with her, so she gave birth to a child for him, and her child died. He (peace be upon him) said: If they wish, they sell her to cover the debt that is upon her master from her price, and if she has a child, she is evaluated based on her child from his share.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or he said, to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'I ask you.' So he said, 'Ask.' I said, 'Why did Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) sell the mothers of the children?' He said, 'For the freeing of their necks [from slavery].' I said, 'And how is that?' He said, 'Any man who buys a slave girl, she bears a child by him, then he does not pay her price, and he does not leave from his wealth what is to be paid off from her, her child is taken from her, and she is sold, so her price is paid.' I said, 'Can they be sold for what is besides that, from the avenues of debt and its various forms?' He said, 'No.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, and others, from Yunus, regarding A mother of a child (Umm al-Walad) who has no child of her own, her child died, and her master died without emancipating her. Is it permissible for anyone to marry her? He said: No, she is a slave. It is not permissible for anyone to marry her except by emancipation from the inheritors. So if she has a child, and there is no debt upon the deceased, then she belongs to the child. And when the child owns her, she has been emancipated by the ownership of her child. And if she is shared between partners, she has been emancipated from the share of her child, and she would work (pay) for the remainder of her price.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was present, about a man who sold a slave girl to another man for a specific price for up to a year. So when the buyer took possession of her, he emancipated her the next day, married her, and made her dower to be her emancipation. Then, a month later, he died. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: If there was wealth for the one who bought her for up to a year, or a contract which covers the fulfillment of what is upon him from the debt regarding her slavery, then his emancipation and his marriage are both valid. He (peace be upon him) said: And if there does not happen to be any wealth for the one who bought her, so he emancipated her and married her, and there is no contract on the day he died which covers the fulfillment of what is upon him from the debts by her slavery, then his emancipation and his marriage are both invalid, because he emancipated what he did not own, and I view her as being a slave of her former master. It was said to him (peace be upon him): If it was such that she conceived, meaning from the emancipator of her, the one who married her, what is the state of that which is in her belly? So he (peace be upon him) said: That which is in her belly is with its mother, like her.

Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the slave who gives wealth to a man to buy him so that he would emancipate him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not correct for him'.

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi, said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, Hisham ibn Udayn asked me to ask you about a man who designated the emancipation of his slave to take effect upon the occurrence of death by his master. So the master died, and upon him was an obligatory freeing of a neck as an expiation. Is the emancipation of that slave, which the master had designated for him, valid on behalf of the deceased for the freeing of the neck that was upon the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked him, and I was present, saying: 'A slave belongs to me who drinks wine and enters into these disliked matters (or: the matter of Wilayah, unwillingly). I intend to emancipate him. Is his emancipation more beloved to you, or should I sell him and give his price in charity?' He said: 'Emancipation is better in some times, and in some times charity is better. So when the people's state is good, emancipation is better. So when their state is severe (or: committing sins), charity is better. And selling this one is more beloved to me when he is in this state.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: All people are free, except for the one who confesses upon himself with slavery, and he is an adult from a slave or a slave girl; and the one against whom is testified with slavery, whether he was young or old.'

Ali, from his father, from Dawood Al Nahdy, from one of our companions who said: Ibn Abu Saeed Al-Mukari came to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May Allah grant you the capacity to claim what your father claimed.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'What is the matter with you? May Allah extinguish your light and bring poverty into your house. Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Imran, 'I shall endow you with a male,' so He endowed him with Maryam, and endowed Maryam with Isa (peace be upon him). Thus Isa is from Maryam, and Maryam is from Isa, and Maryam and Isa are one thing; and I am from my father, and my father is from me, and I and my father are one thing.' He said, 'So he left from his presence, became poor until he died, and did not have the means for an overnight stay. May Allah curse him.' Ibn Abu Saeed said to him, 'And I ask you a question.' He said, 'I do not think you will accept from me, and you are not from my flock, but come with it.' He said: 'A man said upon his death, 'Every slave of mine who is old, he is free for the Face of Allah.' He said, 'Yes. Allah, Mighty is His Mention, says in His Book, 'Until it becomes like an old dry palm branch.' Thus whatever was from his slaves, upon whom six months have passed, is considered old, and he is free.' He (the narrator) said, 'So he went out from his presence, and contemplated until he died, and there did not happen to be an overnight stay. May Allah curse him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from his father, raising it, said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who married a slave-girl of a man whose lord had emancipated the first child she gave birth to. So she gave birth to twins. So he said: 'Both of them are emancipated'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: I wrote to him asking him about the slave upon whom death is presented, so the master emancipates him at that moment, so he exits the world as a free man. Is there for his master a reward in that, or should he leave him so that there is for him his reward when he dies and he is a slave? So he wrote to him: 'Leave the slave as a slave in the state of his death, so it is a reward for his master, and this emancipation at this time is not beneficial for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Nahik from Ali ibn al-Harith from Sabbah al-Muzani from Najiya who said: I saw a man in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I emancipated a female servant of mine, and I have been seeking to buy a servant for years but I cannot find one.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What does the servant do?' He said: 'She is a snake (hypocrite/unfamiliar).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Return her to her slavery. Whatever Allah has made one of you self-sufficient from emancipation, you are emancipating today, and it will be upon us tomorrow. It is not permissible for you to emancipate except one whom you recognize.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Al-Amraki ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man upon whom is the emancipation of a neck, and he intended to emancipate a person. Which of these two is better, if he emancipates an old man, or a beardless youth? He said: Emancipate the one who can be self-sufficient himself. The old weak sheikh is better than the beardless youth.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The blind and the seated cripple are not valid for emancipation, and the one with a hand defect and the lame are valid.'

Ahmad narrated from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurara, from one of the progeny of A'ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever was a Believer, he is emancipated after seven years, whether his master emancipates him or does not emancipate him, and it is not permissible to have the services of the one who was a Believer after seven years.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Ismail ibn Sahl, from Muawiya ibn Maysara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who sells his slave for less than the price in order to emancipate him. So the slave said to him, 'Regarding what is between the two (prices), for you upon me is such and such.' Can he take it from him? He said: 'He takes it from him as a pardon (gift), and he asks him for it as an excused gift. So if he refuses, let him leave it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said: Regarding a man who had several slaves, he said, 'Whichever of you teaches me a Verse from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he is free.' One of them taught him. Then the master died, and it was not known which of them was the one who taught him the Verse. 'Can a lot be drawn?' He said: 'Yes, and it is not allowed for anyone to extract him except for the Imam, for he has a specific speech at the time of drawing the lot which he recites, and a supplication which no one knows besides him, nor is anyone able over it apart from him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarrāj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Ismail Haqeeba and Al-Harith al-Nasri: 'Seek out for me a slave girl from the one they call Kadbanouj, to be with Umm Farwa.' So they pointed us to a slave girl of a man from the al-Sarrajeen who had given birth to a son for him, and her son had died. So they informed him of her news. So he ordered them, and they bought her, and her name was Rasala, so he changed her name and called her Salma, and Salim, her master, married her, and she is the mother of Al-Husayn ibn Salim.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guardianship (walayah) is for the one who emancipates.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man when he is emancipated: is it for him to place himself wherever he wishes and to take as guardian whom he loves? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he is emancipated for the Sake of Allah, he is a slave of the one who emancipated him. So when he is emancipated and is made a freed slave (sa'ibah), then for him is that he places himself wherever he wishes and takes as guardian whom he wishes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in the hadith of Barirah that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Aisha: 'Emancipate her, for the guardianship (wilayah) belongs to the one who emancipates.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ayesha said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'The people of Barirah stipulated their guardianship (walayah).' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a woman who emancipated a man, [the Imam was asked]: For whom is his guardianship, and for whom is his inheritance? He (peace be upon him) said: For the one who emancipated him, except if there happens to be an inheritor for him apart from her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Suleym al-Farra, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, who said: My maternal aunt narrated to me. She said, 'I was seated by the courtyard of the Ka'bah, when Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) came over. So when he saw me, he altered his course towards me. So he greeted me and he said: 'What makes you sit over here?' So I said, 'I am awaiting a slave of ours'. She said, 'So he said to me: 'Emancipate him'. I said, 'No, but we have emancipated his father'. So he said: 'That is not your slave. This is your brother, and a son of your uncle. But rather, the slave is the one upon whom the bounty flowed. So when it flowed upon his father and his grandfather, so he is a son of your uncle, and your brother'.

From him, from Al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abdullah ibn Junadab, who narrates it up to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The slave is the free man (who was freed), and his son is an Arab, and the son of his son is from himself (of his essence/lineage).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and with me was Ali ibn Abdul Aziz. So he said to me: 'Who is this?' So I said, 'A slave of ours'. So he said: 'Have you emancipated him, or his father?' So I said, 'But his father'. So he said: 'This one is not your slave. This is your brother, and a son of your uncle. But rather, the slave is the one upon whom the bounty flows. So when it flowed upon his father, so he is your brother, and a son of your uncle'.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Umar, from a man, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A companion of twenty years is a relative.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed altogether, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abdul-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Three (people) Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept their prayer; one of them is the absconding slave until he returns to his master.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man whose owned slave had absconded from him, is he allowed that he emancipates him regarding an expiation of Al-Zahaar? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it, for as long as death is not recognised from him. Abu Hashim, may Allah be Pleased with him, said: And it was Nasr ibn Aamir al-Qummi who had asked me that I ask him (peace be upon him) about that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a slave girl with arranged emancipation (mudabbarah) who absconded from her master's will) who ran away from her master for a period of many years. Then she returned after her master had died, with children and much property, and two witnesses testified for her that her master had arranged her emancipation during his lifetime before she had absconded. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that she and all that is with her belong to the inheritors.' I said: 'Is she not emancipated from a third of her master's estate?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because she absconded, being disobedient to Allah and her master, so the absconding invalidated the emancipation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khash'ami, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the absconding Muslim slave: he is returned to the Muslim. And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who seized an absconding slave, so he absconded from him: he said, there is nothing upon him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The owned slave, when he flees and does not exit from his city, does not constitute as having absconded.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who came across an absconding slave, so he seized him, and the slave escaped from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him.' I said, 'Supposing he came across a slave girl who had stolen from a neighbour of his, so he seized her in order to bring her to him, and she died.' (He (peace be upon him) said): 'There is nothing upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about making the absconding slave suffer humiliation. He said: There is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no patronage (guarantee) regarding the absconding slave.
He said: 'There is no emancipation except what is intended by it the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no [valid] emancipation except what is sought by it the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no divorce before marriage, and no emancipation before ownership.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Misma' Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no emancipation except after ownership.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) made a bequest, saying: Abu Nayzar, Rabah, and Jubayr are to be emancipated on the condition that they work in the estate for five years.

From Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated his slave girl and stipulated upon her that she serve him for five years. So she fled, then the man died. His heirs found her. Do they have the right to make her serve them? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman and Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the man who emancipates his slave and marries him to his daughter, and stipulates a condition upon him that if he were to wrong/deceive her, he would be returned to slavery. He said: His stipulation stands.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), regarding The man who says to his slave: 'I emancipate you upon the condition that I marry you to my daughter; so if you marry (another) in addition to her, or take a concubine, then upon you is one hundred dinars.' So he emancipated him upon that condition and married him (to his daughter), and he (the freed slave) either took a concubine or married (another). He (the Imam) said: For his master (the former owner), upon him (the freed slave) is his first stipulation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Muawiya ibn Ammar and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said regarding the man who emancipates the slave: He said: 'Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — will emancipate for every organ of his (the slave's), an organ (of the emancipator) from the Fire.' He said: 'And it is recommended for the man to draw closer to God on the evening of Arafah and the day of Arafah through emancipation and charity.'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever emancipates a Muslim, Allah Mighty and Majestic will emancipate him for every organ of his — an organ from the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, raising it (to the Prophet), he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'Whoever emancipates a believing [slave], God — Mighty and Majestic — will emancipate, for every limb of his (the slave), a limb of his (the emancipator) from the Fire. And if she (the slave) was a female, God — Mighty and Majestic — will emancipate, for every two of her limbs, one of his limbs from the Fire, because the woman is [valued at] half of the man.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever emancipates a righteous soul for the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah will expiate from him, in place of every organ of his, an organ from the Fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) and asked him about the man who emancipates a young boy, or an elderly old man, or one afflicted with a chronic illness, or one who has no means of livelihood. So he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever emancipates an owned slave who has no means of livelihood, it is obligatory upon him (the emancipator) to support him (the freed slave) until he becomes self-sufficient. And similarly did Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to do when he emancipated the young and those with no means of livelihood.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), who said: I asked him about the child whom the man emancipates. So he said: Yes, Ali (peace be upon him) had emancipated numerous children.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about emancipating the slave woman (al-nasama). So he said: Emancipate one who can make herself self-sufficient.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from a slave whom Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) emancipated — 'This is what Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) emancipated: he emancipated his Sindhi slave, so-and-so, upon the condition that he would testify that there is no deity except Allah, alone, with no partner for Him; and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger; and that the Resurrection is true; and that Paradise is true; and that the Fire is true; and upon the condition that he would befriend the friends of Allah, and would disavow from the enemies of Allah, and would permit what Allah has permitted, and would forbid what Allah has forbidden, and would believe in the Messengers of Allah, and would acknowledge what came from the presence of Allah. I emancipate him for the Face of Allah, not seeking by it any recompense nor gratitude, and no one has any claim over him except in goodness.' Witnessed by so-and-so.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad who said: I read the emancipation deed of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and behold its text was: 'This is what Ja'far ibn Muhammad has emancipated — he freed so-and-so, his slave, for the face of Allah, not intending by it any recompense nor thanks, upon (the stipulation) that he establish the salat, give the zakat, perform the Hajj of the House, fast the month of Ramadan, befriend the friends of Allah, and disavow the enemies of Allah.' Witnessed by so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so — three (of them).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Ali (peace be upon him) emancipated a Christian slave of his, and he embraced Islam when he emancipated him.
Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hafs, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with emancipating a child born of adultery.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from his father Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Can a slave be emancipated from among the oppressed (mustadh'afin)?' He said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a slave owned among partners, and one of them emancipates his share. He said: 'That is a harm against his companions — they are not able to sell him nor to hire out his services.' He said: 'He (the slave) is appraised at a price, and it is then imposed upon the one who emancipated him as a punishment. And indeed it was only made (obligatory) upon him because of what he damaged.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about two men who had a slave between them, and one of them emancipated his share. So he said: If it was harmful, he would be obligated to emancipate the whole of him; otherwise, the slave would work to (earn the value of) the other half.

Whoever was a partner in a male slave or a female slave — little or more — and emancipated his portion, and he has the financial means, let him buy him from his companion and emancipate the whole of him. But if he does not have the financial means from wealth, the slave's value should be assessed on the day he was emancipated, then the slave shall work according to the reckoning of what remains until he is completely emancipated.

And by his chain, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) judged regarding a slave who was co-owned between two men: one of them emancipated his share while the slave was young, and the other retained his share until the one who had freed his half grew up. He said: He shall be appraised at the value on the day the first (owner) freed his share, and the freed slave is ordered to work to earn his other half that has not yet been freed, until he pays it off.

I asked him about the slave jointly owned between partners, when one of them emancipates his share. So he said: This is a spoiling/harm against his companions; he [the slave] is appraised at a price, and the one who emancipated him is liable for the price, because he has spoiled it against his companions.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who jointly inherited a slave, and one of them emancipated his share of him. How would the one who emancipated his share be dealt with? Would he be held accountable for what remains? He said: Yes, he would be held accountable for what remains of him, at his price on the day he emancipated (his share).

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us; he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa — all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), concerning the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and what you have taught of the hunting animals, trained ones' He said: 'These are the dogs.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayyna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and more than one other, from them both (peace be upon them) together, that they both said regarding the dog that the man sends (to hunt) while invoking God's name: 'If it (the dog) seizes it (the prey) and you reach it while it can still be slaughtered, then slaughter it; and if you reach it and it has already killed it and eaten from it, then eat what remains, and do not concern yourselves with what you are thinking regarding the dog.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Salim al-Ashall who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog which holds upon its prey and has already eaten from it. He said: There is no problem with what it ate, and it is permissible for you.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who releases his trained dog and says 'Bismillah' when he releases it. So he said: 'He may eat from what it holds for him. But if he reaches it before it dies, he should slaughter it. And if he finds an untrained dog with it, then he may not eat from it.' So I said: 'And the leopard?' He said: 'When you come upon it while still alive to slaughter it, eat; otherwise, no.' I said: 'Is not the leopard in the same status as the dog?' So he said to me: 'Nothing is considered a trained hunting animal (mukallab) except the dog.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: Whatever is killed by the trained hunting animals, and the Name of God, Mighty and Majestic, is mentioned over it, then eat from it. And whatever is killed by the dogs that you had not trained before you came upon it, do not consume it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: Hakam ibn Hukaym al-Sayrafi narrated to me, he said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you say regarding a dog that hunts prey and kills it? He said: There is no problem with eating it. He said: I said: But they say that if it kills it and eats from it, then it has only kept it for itself, so do not eat it. He said: Eat! Have they not already agreed with you that if it kills it, that is its ritual slaughter? I said: Yes. He said: So what do they say regarding a sheep that a man slaughtered — has he purified it? I said: Yes. He said: But if a wild beast came after he had slaughtered it and ate part of it, would the remainder be eaten? I said: Yes. He said: So when they answer you to this, say to them: How do you say that when that one (the dog) slaughtered and ate from it you do not eat, yet when this one (the man) slaughtered it and it (the wild beast) ate, you do eat?
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his dog (for hunting), and when he reached the game, it had already killed it He said: 'Eat, even if it (the dog) has eaten (from it).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who sends his dog after game and it seizes it, but he does not have a knife to slaughter it with. Should he leave it until the dog kills it and then eat from it? He said: 'There is no problem.' God, Mighty and Majestic, said: so eat from what they catch for you [5:4] and it is not befitting that one eat from what the leopard kills.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prey of the buzzards and the falcons, and the dogs, and the leopards. So he said: 'Do not eat the prey of anything from these except what you slaughter, except the trained hunting dog.' I said: 'What if it kills it?' He said: 'Eat.' Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: '...and what you have taught from the hunting animals, trained ones... so eat of that which they catch for you and mention the Name of Allah over it.'

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umeyra, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Salman saying: Eat from what the dog catches, even if it has eaten two-thirds of it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfaly, from al-Sakuny, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He said: The Kurdish dogs, when trained, are at the status of the Saluqiyya (Yemeni trained dogs).

And from him, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Salim al-Ashalli, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the prey of the trained dog who has eaten from its prey. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat from it'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his dog, so it seized a prey and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat from what the dog kills when you have named (Bismillah) over it. So if you were forgetful, eat from it as well, and eat its remains.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the prey of the dog: if a man sends it and mentions (the name of Allah), let him eat from what it holds onto; and if it kills and if it eats, eat what remains. And if it was not trained, he trains it in that very moment, then sends it, and it eats from it, for it is trained. As for that which is different from the dog, from what is hunted by the leopard and the falcon and similar to that, do not eat from its prey except what you reach and slaughter, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says 'Trained ones'. So whatever is different from the dog, its prey is not from what is eaten unless you reach it and slaughter it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was asked about the prey of the falcon and the dog when they hunt, kill the prey, and eat from it: Do you eat from their remains or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: As for what the bird has killed, do not eat it unless you slaughter it; and as for what the dog kills, and you have mentioned the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over it, then eat, even if it has eaten from it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a dog that fled and was not sent by its owner, so it hunted, and its owner caught up with it and it had killed the prey. Can he eat from it? He said: No. And he (peace be upon him) said: When it hunts and has been named (Bismillah), let him eat; and if it hunts and has not been named, let him not eat. And this is from what you have taught the hunting animals, trained ones.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muawiya ibn Hukaym, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I send the dog and say Bismillah over it, and it hunts, but I do not have with me what to slaughter it with.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Leave it until it kills it, and eat.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man sends his dog (to hunt) and forgets to say 'Bismillah', he is in the same status as the one who slaughters (an animal) and forgets to say 'Bismillah', and similarly, when he throws an arrow and forgets to say 'Bismillah'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a group of people who sent their dogs, and all of them were trained, and they had named (Bismillah) over them. So when the dogs went, a strange dog joined them, whose owner they did not know, so they all participated in the hunt. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It should not be eaten from, because you do not know whether it was seized by a trained dog or not.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The black beastly dog, its prey is not eaten, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ordered its killing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The black, beastly dog, its game is not edible, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) commanded to kill it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not come to the chicks in their nests, nor the bird during its sleep until morning.' A man said to him: 'And what is its sleep, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The night is its sleep, so do not hunt it during its sleep until morning, and do not come to the chick in its nest until it has grown feathers and flies. So when it flies, then aim your bow at it, and set up your net for it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade coming to the birds at night, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'The night is a security for them.'

A number of our companions narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman from Misma' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited hunting birds at night, and he said (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, the night is a sanctuary for them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about hunting fish, and if one does not recite the Name of Allah over it, so he said: There is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about hunting fish, and if he has not named (Bismillah) over it, so he said: There is no problem with it, if it is alive that he seizes it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fish that is caught, then placed in something, then returned to the water, so it dies in it. He said: 'Do not eat it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who caught a fish, tied it with a thread, and sent it in the water, so it died. Can it be eaten? He said: No.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the hunting of the Magian for the fish when they strike with the net and do not name (God), and similarly the Jew. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem. Rather, the hunting of the fish is seizing it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fishes which the Magians are hunting. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: The fishes and the grass-hoppers are pure (sacrificed by slaughter).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the hunting of the Magians for the fish when they strike over it with nets, and they name it with Shirk (polytheism). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with their hunting. Indeed, the hunting of fish is catching it.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the enclosure of reeds made in the water for the fish. The fish enter it, so some of them die in it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. Indeed, that enclosure was made to be hunted with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who sets up a net in the water, then returns to his house, leaves it set up, and comes to it later, and fish have fallen into it and died, he (peace be upon him) said: 'What his hands worked [caused], so there is no problem with eating what falls into it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a fish that leapt out of the river, fell onto the bank of the river, and died. Is it permissible to eat it? He said: If you catch it before it dies, then it dies, eat it; and if it died before you catch it, do not eat it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a fish whose belly was slit, and a fish was found inside it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat both of them together.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no problem with the fish which the Magian hunts.'

Abu Ali Al-Ashari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked, 'A man caught a fish and found a fish inside its belly.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Both may be eaten together.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the owner of the net strikes with the net, whatever is caught in it, whether living or dead, is permissible, except that which does not have a shell/scales, and the floating one of the fish is not to be eaten.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ahmad ibn al-Mubarak, from Salih ibn Ayn, from al-Washa, from Ayoub ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding a snake that swallowed a fish, then regurgitated it, and it is still a snake writhing? Can I eat it?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'If its scales had peeled off, do not eat it, and if they had not peeled off, then eat it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade a man from hunting fish on Friday before the prayer, and he (peace be upon him) would pass by the fishmongers on Friday and forbid them from hunting fish on Friday before the prayer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). And the floating [fish] was mentioned, and what people dislike from it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The floating [fish] that is disliked is from the fish, and it is that whose smell has changed.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, all from Al-A'ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had me read something from the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), and it contained: 'You are forbidden from the catfish, the glyptothorax, the sea horse, the floating fish, and the spleen.' I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you, fish without scales are brought to us.' He said, 'Eat what has scales from the fish, and do not eat what does not have scales.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn Uthman said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, as for fish, what is permissible to eat from them?' He said, 'That which has scales.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say about the sea bass (kandath)?' He said, 'There is no problem with eating it.' I said to him, 'But it does not have scales.' He said to me, 'Yes, but it is a fish of bad disposition; it buries itself in everything, and if you look at the root of its ear, you will find scales on it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not eat the eel, nor the sea horse, nor the floating one, nor the spleen, because it is the house of blood and a morsel of Satan. Because it is the house of blood and a morsel of Satan.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said: Dried sea bass (Rabeetha) were brought to me in a basket. So I went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and asked him about it. He said: 'Eat it, for it has scales (skin/shell).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), was in Kufa, riding the mule of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then he passed by the fish market and said: 'Do not eat and do not sell from the fish that do not have scales.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan ibn Sudeyr, who said: Al-A'la ibn Kamil asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I was present, about the catfish (or eel). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) certain things forbidden from the fish, so do not go near them.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'That which does not have a skin/scales from the fish, do not go near it.'

Hanan ibn Sadeer said: Al-Fayz ibn al-Mukhtar gifted a sea bass to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and brought it to him, and I was with him. So he looked at it and said: 'This has scales on it,' so he ate from it, and we were watching him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to ride the mule of the Messenger of Allah, then he would pass by the fish market and say: 'Indeed, do not eat and do not sell what does not have a shell/scales.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from his uncle Muhammad from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, who said: Is'haq, the owner of the fish, narrated to me: He said: We went out with fish to meet Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), and we had exited from Medina, and he (peace be upon him) had returned from a journey of his. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe be unto you, O so-and-so! Perhaps there is fish with you?' So I said: 'Yes, O my master, may I be sacrificed for you.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Descend, all of you!' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe be unto you, perhaps it is Siganus?' I said: 'Yes.' So I showed it to him (peace be upon him). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ride! There is no need for us with regards to it, and the Siganus is a fish which has no scales on it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Al-Amraki ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) said: The eating of the catfish (Jirri), the tortoise, and the crab is not permissible. I asked him about the flesh that is in the shells of the sea and the Euphrates, is it permissible to eat? He said: That is the flesh of frogs, its eating is not permissible.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from al-Kalbi al-Nassab, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the catfish, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, metamorphosed a group from the Children of Israel, so whatever of them the sea seized, it is the catfish, and the glyptothorax, and the sea horse, and what is besides that; and whatever the land seized from them, it is the monkeys, and the pigs, and the short-haired rabbit, and the lizard, and what is besides that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Yunus, who said: I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'Fish that do not have scales, can they be eaten?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the fish, there are some that have spines/roughness, so they rub against everything, and their scales go away. But when its two ends differ, meaning its tail and its head, then eat it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about eating the locust, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with eating it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a spawn/offspring of the fish in the sea.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: The fish and the locusts, when they come out from the water, are pure (sacrificed), and the land is a trap for the locusts, and for the fish it may also be (a trap).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the locust, if we find it dead in the desert or in the water, is it permissible to eat? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat it.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Dabba (young locust) from the locusts, is it permissible to eat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until it is capable of flying.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who hunts a bird that is worth many dirhams, and it is level-winged (capable of flight), and its owner is known, or it comes to him and he seeks it, from one who does not accuse him (of stealing it). He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to keep it; he should return it to him.' So I said to him (peace be upon him): 'And if he hunts what has no control over its two wings, and its seeker is not known? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for him.'
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the bird owns its wings, so it is for the one who seizes it.

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a hunted dove that is worth half a dirham or one dirham. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you know its owner, return it to him, and if you do not know its owner, and it has level wings, flying with both of them, then it is for you.'

And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ubayd ibn Hafs ibn Qurat Qurat, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A bird falls upon the house, so it is seized. Is it permissible or prohibited for the one who seizes it?' So he said, 'O Ismail! Is it complete or not complete?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is complete?' He said, 'The one whose wings are level, in control of its wings, going wherever it desires.' He said, 'It is for the one who seizes it, permissible.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The bird, when it takes control of its wings, is prey, and it is permissible for the one who seizes it.'

And by his chain that, Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who saw a bird, so he pursued it until it fell upon a tree. So another man came over, so he seized it. So Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for the eye what it sees, and for the hand what it seizes'.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it to Dawood al-Raqqi or someone else, said: While we were seated in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), a man passed by with a slaughtered swallow in his hand. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) leapt towards him until he took it from his hand, then he pressed it into the ground and said (peace be upon him): 'Has your scholar or your jurist ordered you with this? My father informed me from my grandfather that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the killing of six, among them was the swallow.' And he said: 'Its circling in the sky is regret for what was done to the People of the Household of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its glorification is the recitation of 'Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbil-'Alameen'. Do you not see it saying 'Wa la ad-dalleen' (and not those who go astray)?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, altogether from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Tameemi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from his father, who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Treat the wagtails with goodness, meaning the swallows, for these are the friendliest of the birds of the people with the people'. Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'And do you know what the wagtail (swallow) says when it passes by and sings? It says: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful'. The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the Worlds until he (peace be upon him and his family) recited the 'Mother of the Book' (Surah Al-Fatiha). So when it comes the end of its singing, so she says, 'Wa La Zalleen' (the last words of Surah al-Fatiha). Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) extended his voice with it, 'Wa La Zalleen'. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) extended his voice with it, 'Wa La Zalleen'. Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) extended his voice with it, 'Wa La Zalleen'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about killing the swallows, or hurting them in the Sanctuary. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not kill them, for I was in the presence of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he saw me troubling them. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O my son! Do not kill them and do not harm them, for they are not harming anything'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abu Ayyub al-Madani, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: In each wing of the hoopoe is inscribed in Syriac: 'The Progeny of Muhammad are the best of the creation.'

And from him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about the Hoopoe, and killing it and slaughtering it, so he said: 'It is not harmed and it is not slaughtered, for it is a good bird.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ayyub al-Madiny, from Suleyman al-Ja'fary, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the killing of the hoopoe, the shrike, the skua gull, and the honey bee.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abu Ayyub al-Madaini, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: Do not eat the grouse, nor insult it, nor give it to the children to play with it, for it is frequent in the glorification of Allah (Exalted), and its glorification is: 'May Allah curse those who hate the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them)'.

And by his chain, he said: ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: ‘I do not sow the crop to seek surplus/profit in it, and I do not sow it except so that the beggar may take from it, and the one with need, and the grouse may take from it, particularly among the birds.’

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah al-Jamourani, from Suleiman al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not kill the grouse, and do not eat its flesh, for it is frequent in glorification. It says at the end of its glorification: "May Allah curse those who hate the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them)."'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi, from one of our companions, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'The topknot on the head of the grouse is from the wiping of Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him). And that is, the male intended to copulate with its female, but she prevented him. So he said to her, "Do not prevent me, for I do not intend except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would extract from me a soul that would be remembered by you." So she answered him to what he sought.' So when it wanted to lay eggs, he said to her, "Where do you want to lay eggs?" So she said to him, "I do not know, shall I move it away from the road?" He said to her, "I am afraid that the passers-by would pass by you, but I see for you that you should lay eggs near the road, so whoever sees you near it would think that you are picking seeds from the road." So she answered him to that and laid eggs, and incubated them until she oversaw the births. So while the two of them were involved in that, when there noticed Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) in his army, and the birds were shading him. So she said to him, "This is Sulayman who is coming over to us in his army, and there is no safety if he were to trample us, and trample our eggs." So he said to her, "Sulayman (peace be upon him) would be a merciful man with us, so is there anything with you to gift to him for (the safety of) your chicks when they are born?" She said, "Yes, a grasshopper which I hid from you, awaiting for my chicks for it when they are born. So is there anything with you?" He said, "Yes, I have a date with me, which I hid from you for my chicks." She said, "So you take your date, and I take my grasshopper, and we go to Sulayman (peace be upon him) and we present these to him, for he is a man who loves the gifts." So he took the date in his beak, and she took the grasshopper in her claws, then they went to Sulayman (peace be upon him). So when he saw them both, and he was upon his throne, he extended his hands for them. So they went over and the male sat upon the right hand and the female sat upon the left hand, and he asked them both of their state. So they informed him. So he accepted both their gifts, and diverted his army away from them and their eggs, and he wiped upon their heads,

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — all together from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to give legal rulings and he practiced caution (taqiyya), and we used to fear regarding the prey of falcons and hawks. But as for now, we do not fear, and we do not declare their prey permissible, except when the ritual slaughter (dhakah) is performed upon it. For it is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) that God, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And what you have trained of hunting animals, trained ones" — (this is) regarding dogs.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you send a falcon, or a hawk, or an eagle (to hunt), do not eat until you reach it and slaughter it. And if it has killed (the prey), do not eat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his dog and his hawk. He said: As for the hawk, do not eat from its prey until you come to it and perform its ritual slaughter; and as for the dog, eat from it when you have mentioned the Name of God over it, whether the dog ate from it or did not eat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he abhorred the prey of the falcon, except what one reaches and performs its ritual slaughter.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his falcon or his dog (to hunt), and it seized a prey and ate from it. May I eat from their remains? He said: No. Whatever the falcon killed, do not eat from it unless you slaughter it.

Aban, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: I asked him about the prey of the falcon and the hawk. So he said: 'Do not eat what the falcon and the hawk have killed, and do not eat what the predatory birds have killed.'

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the falcon, and the hawk, and the eagle?' So he said, 'If you reach it (while alive) for its slaughter, then eat from it. And if you do not reach it for its slaughter, then do not eat.'

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to issue fatwas during the era of the Banu Umayya that whatever the falcon and the hawk kills is permissible, and he was observing dissimulation (taqiyya) from them. But I do not fear them, and it is forbidden — what they kill.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prey of a falcon when it hunts and kills and eats from it — may I eat from its remainder or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: As for what the bird ate, do not eat (from it), unless you slaughter it (properly).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays al-Muradi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hawks and the falcons, and about their prey. He said: 'Eat what they have not killed, when you find it slaughtered. The end of slaughtering is when the eye twitches, the leg kicks, and the tail moves.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The hawks and the falcons are not mentioned in the Quran.'
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, who said: Do not eat from that which the predatory birds kill.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog of the Magian — the Muslim man takes it, then he says Bismillah when he releases it [to hunt]. May he eat from what it catches for him? He (AS) said: 'Yes, because it is a trained hunting animal and the Name of Allah has been mentioned over it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I borrow a dog from the Magian and hunt with it. So he (peace be upon him) said: Do not eat from its prey, except if a Muslim has trained it and it has learned.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The dog of the Magian — do not eat its prey, except if a Muslim takes it, trains it, and sends it (to hunt). And similarly is the falcon. And the dogs of the Ahl al-Dhimma and their falcons — it is permissible for Muslims to eat their prey.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Buraid ibn Mu'awiya al-'Ijli, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Eat from the hunt that which was killed by the sword, the arrow, and the spear. And he was asked about game that was hunted and then the people divided it among themselves before it died; so he said: There is no problem with it.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'Whoever injures a game animal with a weapon and invokes the name of God, Mighty and Majestic, over it, then it remains for a night or two nights without a predator eating from it, and he knows that his weapon is what killed it, then he may eat from it if he so desires.' And he said regarding a mountain goat that a man hunted, then the people tore it apart while the man was pursuing it: 'Do you consider this to be plunder?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not plunder, and there is no objection to it.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the shot game whose owner finds it the next morning. Can he eat from it? So he said: If he knows that it was his shot which killed it, then let him eat from that, when he had already invoked the name (of Allah).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who shot an arrow at a wild donkey or a deer and hit it, then he was in search of it and found it the next morning with his arrow in it. So he (peace be upon him) said: If he knows that he hit it and that his arrow is the one that killed it, then let him eat from it; otherwise, he should not eat from it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isa al-Qummi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I shoot my arrow and I do not know whether I named (said bismillah) or did not name.' He said: 'Eat — there is no problem.' He (the narrator) said: I said: 'I shoot and it disappears from me, then I find my arrow in it.' He said: 'Eat what has not been eaten from it, but if it had been eaten from, do not eat from it.'

Al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the game which a man strikes with a sword, or stabs with a spear, or shoots with an arrow, killing it, having invoked the name of God (Bismillah) when he did so So he said: Eat, there is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hunted prey that its owner finds — may he eat it? He said: If he knows that it was his shooting which killed it, then let him eat.
