Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding a hunt in which an arrow was found, and it was dead, not known who killed it: 'Do not eat it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad al-Halabi who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who shoots at the hunted prey and knocks it down, then the people rush toward it and cut it up. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you shoot (an arrow), so you find it, and there are not traces of other than the arrow, and you see that it has not been killed by other than your arrow, so eat, whether it had disappeared from you or not disappeared from you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who shoots at the hunted prey while he is on the mountain, so the arrow pierces it until it exits from the other side. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But if it falls into water or tumbles from the mountain and dies, do not eat it.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from a man, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The prey is not shot with something that is bigger than it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara and Ismail al-Ju'fi, that both of them asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what the mi'rad (blunt/crosswise arrow) kills. He said: 'There is no problem, provided it was your projectile or you made it for that purpose.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about what the mi'rad (blunt weapon) knocks down from the hunted prey. So he said: 'If he does not have an arrow other than the mi'rad, and he mentioned the name of God, Mighty and Majestic, over it, then let him eat what was killed.' I said: 'And if he had an arrow other than it?' He said: 'No.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you shoot at it with the mi'rad (blunt arrow) and it pierces, then eat; but if it does not pierce and falls sideways, then do not eat.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hunted prey which the man shoots at with an arrow, and it hits it sideways and kills it, and he had invoked the Name (Bismillah) when he shot it, but the iron (arrowhead) did not hit it. So he (peace be upon him) said: If it was the arrow which struck it that also killed it, then when he sees it as such, let him eat.

I asked him about the hunted prey that the arrow strikes sideways and does not strike it with the iron (arrowhead), and he had named (said Bismillah) when he shot. He said: He may eat it when he struck it and he saw it (fall). And about the prey hunted by the blunt weapon (mi'rad), he said: If he does not have an arrow other than it, and he had named (said Bismillah) when he threw, then let him eat from it; but if he had an arrow other than it, then no.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them both, who said: I asked him about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He was asked about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), he said: I asked him about (hunting by) killing with the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? So he said: No.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he disliked the julahiq (pellet bow/sling).

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who throws the pellet and the stone and kills (the game) — can he eat from it? He said: Do not eat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: What the snare seizes from the game, such that it cuts off its foreleg or hindleg — then leave it, for it is dead carrion. And eat what you find while it is still alive, having mentioned the Name of God, Mighty and Majestic, over it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one person, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: What the snare seizes and cuts off something from it, that is dead (impermissible to eat); but what you find of the rest of its body still alive, slaughter it (Islamically) and then eat from it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: What the snare seizes and cuts off something from it — that part is dead (maytah). But what you find of the rest of its body still alive — slaughter it, then eat from it.
Aban, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: What the snare seizes, so something is cut off from it, or it dies, then it is dead meat (mayta).
What the snares seize, and they cut off something from it, then that is dead (carrion). And what you reach of the rest of its body, then slaughter it ritually, then eat from it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Do not eat from the hunted prey if it falls into the water and dies.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): he was asked about a man who shot at prey while he was upon a mountain or a wall, and the arrow pierced into it and it died. So he said: Eat from it. But if it fell into the water from your shooting and it died, then do not eat from it.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the animal slaughtered with plaster and with flint. So he said: There is no valid ritual slaughter except with iron.
I asked him about the (animal) slaughtered with wood, stone, and cane. He said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: Slaughter is not valid except with iron.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Do not eat what has not been slaughtered with iron.
I asked him about the ritual slaughter (dhakah). So he said: 'Do not slaughter except by iron. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) forbade from that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The butted one, the fallen one, and what the predator has eaten, when you find its throat intact, slaughter it and eat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not eat from the prey of the predator, nor the one beaten to death, nor the one fallen to death, except if you come to it alive, so you slaughter it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Muskān, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to dislike slaughter and the spilling of blood on Friday before the prayer, except out of necessity.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to order his servants that they should not slaughter until the dawn emerges. In the Miscellaneous (Hadith) regarding Friday.

Ali ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) while he was saying to his servants: 'Do not slaughter until the dawn rises, for Allah has made the night a tranquility for everything.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, but what if we fear?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you fear death, then slaughter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the slaughtered meat of the Murji'ite and the Haruriyya, so he said: 'Eat, and be decisive and steady, until what is to happen happens.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl, and Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, that they asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about buying meat from the markets, and it is not known what the butchers have done. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat, when that is in the markets of the Muslims, and do not ask about it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughter by a child, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he moves, and has five palm-lengths, and can wield the blade.' And about the slaughter by a woman, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If there are women and no man is with them, let the most intelligent of them slaughter, and let her mention the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the slaughter of a boy. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he is strong enough for slaughtering, and is good at slaughtering, and mentions the Name of Allah over it, then eat.' He (the narrator) said, 'And he was asked about the slaughter of a woman, so he said: 'When she is a Muslim, and she mentions the Name of Allah over it, then eat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the boy and the woman, can it be eaten? So he (peace be upon him) said: When the woman is a Muslim, and she mentions the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon her slaughter, her slaughter becomes permissible, and similarly the boy, when he is strong enough for the slaughter, and mentions the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over it, and that is when there is fear of losing the slaughtered animal, and there is no one else to slaughter it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions who said: The Marzaban asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the child before he attains puberty, and the slaughter of the woman. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with the slaughter of the eunuch, and the child, and the woman, when there is desperation to it'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from someone else, they narrated from both of them (peace be upon them) together. That the slaughter of a woman, when she is proficient in the slaughter and she names (God), there is no problem with eating it, and similarly the blind man when he is assisted.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the eunuch, so he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was a slave girl for Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who used to slaughter for him whenever he so intended.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the child reaches five palms (in height), his slaughtered animal is eaten.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the slaughtered meat of the Dhimmi (people of the book under covenant), so he said: 'Do not eat it, whether he has named (God) or if he has not named (God).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mundhir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We are a people who travel to the mountain, and the road is distant between us and the mountain, [consisting of] farsakhs. So we buy the flock, and the two [flocks], and the three [flocks], and there may be in the flock one thousand five hundred sheep, and one thousand six hundred sheep, and one thousand seven hundred sheep. So one sheep, or two, or three are slaughtered. So we ask the shepherds who bring them about their religion, and they say:

And from him, from Hanan who said, I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed Al-Husayn ibn Al-Munzar narrated from you that you said: The slaughter is [valid] by the Naming, and it is not trusted upon except for its rightful ones.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'They have introduced something in it which I do not desire.' Hanan said, 'So I asked a Christian, and I said to him, 'What do you say when you slaughter?' So he said, 'We say, 'In the name of the Messiah'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Christians of the Arabs, 'Is their slaughter permissible to eat?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) forbade their slaughter, their hunted prey, and intermarrying with them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'ah, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the slaughter of the Jew and the Christian, so he said: 'Do not go near it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We are in the mountain, so we send the shepherds with the sheep. Sometimes the sheep is injured or something strikes it, so they slaughter it, and we eat it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the slaughtered animal, and one does not rely upon it except from a Muslim.'

And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah, who said: Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and Ibn Abi Yafur accompanied each other on a journey. One of them ate the slaughtered meat of the Jews and Christians, while the other refused to eat it. They both gathered in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: 'Which one of you two refused?' He said: 'I did.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Well done.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn Al-Ahmasy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him, 'May Allah improve you! We have a neighbor who is a butcher; a Jew comes to him and slaughters [an animal] for him, so that the Jews buy from him.' He said, 'Do not eat from his slaughter, and do not buy from him.'
Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn Al-Ahmasy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'It is the Naming (Bismillah), therefore none can be relied upon except for a Muslim.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ibn Miskan from Qutaybah al-A'sha who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him, saying to him: 'In the flock, the Jew and the Christian are sent; the exhibitor presents it and slaughters it. Can we eat his slaughter?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not include its price in your wealth, and do not eat it, for it is merely the Name (Bismillah), and one cannot be relied upon except a Muslim.' The man said to him: 'Allah the Exalted says: This day the good things are made lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: Rather, it is the grains and their like.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir and Abdullah ibn Talha, who said: Ibn Sinan said: Isma'il ibn Jabir said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat from the slaughter of the Jews and the Christians, and do not eat in their vessels.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not eat their slaughters, nor eat in their vessels, meaning the People of the Book'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughters of the People of the Book, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem when they mention the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but I mean from them those who are upon the command of Musa and Isa (peace be upon them).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sudeyr, who said: My father and I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May Allah make us your ransom! We have companions among the Christians, and we go to them, and they slaughter for us poultry, chicks, and young goats. Can we eat them?' He said, 'Do not eat them, and do not go near them, for they say upon their slaughters something that I do not like for you to eat.' He (the narrator) said, 'So when we arrived in Kufa, one of them invited us, so we refused to go. He said, 'What is the matter with you? You used to come to us, then you left it today?' We said, 'A knowledgeable one among us (peace be upon him) forbade us, and he claimed that you say upon your slaughters something that he does not like for us to eat.' He said, 'Who is this knowledgeable one? By Allah, he is the most knowledgeable of the people, and the most knowledgeable one whom Allah created. By Allah, he spoke the truth; we say, 'In the name of the Messiah (peace be upon him)'.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the People of the Book. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, they do not eat your slaughters, so how do you permit yourselves to eat their slaughters? It is merely the name (Bismillah), and none can be relied upon regarding it except a Muslim.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said regarding the (animal) slaughtered without iron: 'When you are compelled to do so, and you do not find an iron, then slaughter it with a stone.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the flint, the cane, and the wood — can one slaughter with them when a knife cannot be found? He said: When it tears the jugular veins, there is no problem with that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Zayd al-Shahham, He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who did not have a knife in his possession — can he slaughter with a cane? So he said: 'Slaughter with the cane, and with the stone, and with the bone, and with the wood, when you cannot find the iron; when the throat is severed and the blood flows — there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The nahr (camel sacrifice) is in the labba (upper chest), and the dhabh (slaughter) is in the throat.'

Ali, from his father, from Safwan who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of a cow in the upper chest area. So he said: 'For the cow, the [correct method] is slaughter (dhabh), and what is done by nahr — that is not a valid slaughter (dhaki).'

I said to Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him): The people of Mecca do not slaughter the cow (at the throat), but rather they slaughter in the upper chest (labbah). So what is your view regarding eating its flesh? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They slaughtered it, and almost did not do it. Do not eat except what is properly slaughtered (at the throat).'

I asked him about the slaughter, so he said: 'When you slaughter, release it and do not restrain the forelimbs, and do not flip the knife so as to insert it from beneath the throat and cut upward. And releasing applies to birds in particular. So if it falls into a well or a hollow in the ground, do not eat it and do not feed it (to others), for you do not know whether the falling killed it or the slaughter. And if it is from the sheep, then hold it by its wool or its hair, and do not hold a foreleg or a hind leg. As for cattle, hobble their legs and leave the tail free. As for camels, tie their hooves to their flanks and leave their hind legs free. And if something from the birds escapes you while you intend to slaughter it, or breaks free from you, shoot it with your arrow. And when it falls, purify it (slaughter it) in the manner of hunted game.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the slaughter (dhabihah), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Face your slaughtered animal toward the Qiblah, and do not cut its spinal marrow (nakha') until it dies, and do not eat from a slaughtered animal that was not slaughtered from its proper place of slaughter.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do not sever the spinal cord of the slaughtered animal until it dies. When it has died, then sever it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said: Do not slaughter the sheep in the presence of another sheep, nor the camel in the presence of another camel, while it is looking at it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it (marfu'), said: Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sheep is slaughtered and skinned, or something from it is stripped before it dies, eating it is not permissible.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughtered, but his knife transcended and cut off its head. So he (peace be upon him) said: It is a vivid, valid slaughter. There is no problem with it, nor with eating it.

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Muslim who slaughtered a sheep and named (said Bismillah), but the knife, by its sharpness, outpaced him and severed the head. He (peace be upon him) said: If the blood flows out, then eat.

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he had been asked about a man who slaughters and the knife hastens and cuts off the head. He said: 'The swift slaughter — there is no problem with eating it if it was not done deliberately.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a camel resists you and you intend to slaughter it, then it runs away from you — if you fear it will escape you, strike it with a sword or stab it with a spear, after invoking the Name (Bismillah). Then eat it. Except if you reach it while it has not yet died, then slaughter it (properly).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A bull at al-Kufa went on a rampage, so the people rushed toward it with their swords and struck it down. Then they came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked him, and he said: It was a valid slaughter while alive, and its flesh is permissible.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a bull that disobeyed (resisted slaughter): they rushed at it with their swords and named (said Bismillah), then they came to Ali (peace be upon him) and he said: 'This is a valid slaughter and its meat is permissible.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that a group of people came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so they said: 'A cow of ours overcame us and became unruly against us, so we struck it with the sword.' So he ordered them to eat it.
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A camel has fallen into a well; how can it be slaughtered? He said: Insert the spear and stab it with it, and say the name (Bismillah), and eat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): When the eye blinks, or the leg kicks, or the tail moves, and you reach it, then slaughter it.

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam came to him and said: May I be your ransom, my grandfather is saying to you that a man struck a cow with an axe, so it fell, then he slaughtered it. But he (the Imam) did not send an answer with him, and instead called Saeeda, the slave girl of Umm Farwa. He said to her: Muhammad came to me with a message from you, but I disliked sending the answer with him. So if the man who slaughtered the cow, when he slaughtered it, the blood came out moderately, then eat and feed others; but if it came out sluggishly, do not go near it.
In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): When the eye blinks, or the foot kicks, or the tail moves, then eat from it, for you have realised its ritual slaughter.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you doubt regarding the life of a sheep, and you see it blink its eye, or move its ears, or beat its tail, then slaughter it, for it is halal (permissible) for you.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the slaughtered animal, and he said: 'If the tail moves, or the eyelid, or the ear, then it is validly slaughtered.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said regarding the sheep: if it blinks its eye or moves its tail, then it is lawfully slaughtered.

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughtered an animal but was ignorant that he should face it toward the qiblah. He said: 'Eat from it.' So I said to him: 'What if he (intentionally) did not face it (toward the qiblah)?' He said: 'Then do not eat from it, and do not eat from any slaughtered animal upon which the Name of God, Mighty and Majestic, was not pronounced.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you intend to slaughter, face the qiblah with your animal.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who slaughters and does not say (Bismillah). He said: If he had forgotten, there is no problem, provided that he was a Muslim and was skilled at slaughtering, and does not pierce the spinal cord, and does not cut off the neck after having slaughtered.

He was asked about an animal slaughtered facing other than the Qibla. He said: 'There is no problem, as long as it was not done deliberately.' And about a man who slaughters but forgets to say the name (Bismillah) — can his slaughter be eaten? He said: 'Yes, if he is not suspected (of bad faith), and if he was proficient in slaughtering before this, and he does not sever the spinal cord, and does not break the neck until the slaughtered animal is cold.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slaughtered animal slaughtered toward other than the Qibla. He said: Eat, and there is no problem with that, as long as it was not intentional. He said: And I asked him about a man who slaughtered and did not say the Name (Bismillah). He said: If he had forgotten, then let him say the Name when he remembers, saying: In the Name of God upon its beginning and upon its ending.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughtered while saying the tasbih (Subhanallah), or the takbir (Allahu Akbar), or the tahlil (La ilaha illa Allah), or praised God Mighty and Majestic. He said: All of these are from the Names of God Mighty and Majestic, and there is no objection to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem if a man slaughters while he is in a state of sexual impurity (junub).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Adhina, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked one of the two (peace be upon them both) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'The cattle quadrupeds are permissible for you' [5:1]. So he said: The foetus in the belly of its mother, when it grows hair and fluff, then its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother — that is what God, Mighty and Majestic, meant.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you slaughter a slaughtered animal and find a complete foetus in its belly, then eat (it); and if it does not happen to be complete, then do not eat (it).

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the camel foetus whose mother is ritually slaughtered — can it be eaten by virtue of her slaughter? So he said: When it is fully formed and hair has grown upon it, then eat.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, who said: I asked him about the sheep that one slaughters while in its belly is a young one that has already grown hair. So he (peace be upon him) said: Its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.
He said: regarding the foetus: 'When it grows hair, then eat; or else do not eat — meaning if it has not grown hair.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever starts his morning with twenty-one red raisins will not fall ill except with the sickness of death, if Allah wills.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Twenty-one red raisins, every day upon the saliva (empty stomach), dispel all diseases except the disease of death.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: A man from the people of Egypt narrated to me from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) He said: Raisins strengthen the nerves, remove exhaustion, and improve the breath.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from an Egyptian, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The raisins of Al-Ta'if tighten the nerves, remove exhaustion, and aromatize the breath.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Adhere to the pomegranate, for it does not suffice a hungry person except that it satisfies him, nor does it satisfy a satiated person except that it increases his appetite.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The fruits are of one hundred and twenty types, the chief of these being the Pomegranate.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Umar ibn Aban Al-Kalbi, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon them) saying: 'There is no fruit upon the face of the earth that was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) than the pomegranate, and by Allah, whenever he ate it, he loved that no one else should share it with him.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: From what Adam (peace be upon him) bequeathed to Hibatullah was that he said to him: 'Upon you is the pomegranate, for if you eat it while you are hungry, it will suffice you, and if you eat it while you are satiated, it will order you (for more food).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no thing in which participation is more hateful to me than the pomegranate, and there is no pomegranate except that it contains a seed from Paradise. So when the disbeliever eats it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends an angel to him who removes it from him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever eats a seed from a pomegranate, it sickens the Satan of whispering for forty days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, altogether from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik al-Nawfaly, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and in his hand was a pomegranate, so he said: 'O Mu'ttab! Give him a pomegranate, for there is nothing more hateful to me than being shared in something than being shared in a pomegranate.' Then he had cupping done and ordered me to have cupping done, so I had cupping done. Then he called for another pomegranate and said: 'O Yazeed! Whoever of the believers eats a pomegranate until he finishes it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for forty mornings; and whoever eats two, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for a hundred days; and whoever eats three until he finishes them, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for a year; and whoever Allah removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for a year, he does not sin, and whoever does not sin enters Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Adhere to the sweet pomegranate and eat it, for there is no seed that falls into the stomach of a believer except that it annihilates an illness and extinguishes the Satan of whispering from him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who eats a pomegranate upon the empty stomach, illuminates his heart for forty days.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Abu Saeed al-Raqam, from Salih ibn Uqba, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eat the pomegranate with its lining, for it tans (hardens/strengthens) the stomach and increases the intellect.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Eat the pomegranate with its dividing lining (membrane), for it is a tanning (healing/fortifying) for the stomach.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The sweet pomegranate was mentioned, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Muzz is corrective in the belly.'
From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Khurasani, who said: Eating the sweet pomegranate increases the semen of the man and improves the offspring.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ziyad, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The smoke of the pomegranate tree repels vermin.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The apple radiates the stomach'.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, who said: Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar sent me to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) as a courtesy. So I entered upon him on a scorching hot day, and in front of him was a tray containing green apples. By Allah, I could not bear it and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! You are eating from this while people dislike it?' He said to me as if he had not ceased to recognize me: 'I woke up with a chill in this night of mine, so I sent for it and it was brought to me. I ate it, and it removes the fever and calms the heat.' So I returned home and found my family suffering from fever, so I fed them (apples), and the fever was lifted from them.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ziyad al-Qindy, who said: I entered Medina and with me was my brother Sayf, and the people had been struck with nosebleed, so that if a man had a nosebleed for two days, he died. So I returned to the house and found Sayf with a severe nosebleed. So I entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said: 'O Ziyad! Feed Sayf the apple.' So I fed it to him, and he was cured.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said: A plague struck the people in Makkah, so I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he wrote to me: 'Eat the apple'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: I had a nosebleed for a year in Medina, so our companions asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something that stops the nosebleed. He said to them: 'Give him to drink suwiq of apples.' So they gave me to drink it, and the nosebleed ceased from me.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from one of our companions, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: I do not know for the toxins any cure more beneficial than a suweeq (a type of porridge or soft food) of apples.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yazeed, who said: Whenever a snake or a scorpion stung a person from the household, he said: 'Make him drink apple suweeq (porridge/paste).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Al-Qandi, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Fever was mentioned to him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'We, the People of the Household, do not cure it except by pouring cold water upon us and eating apples.'

From him, from his father, from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: If the people knew what was in the apple, they would not cure their sick ones except by it. He said, 'And some of them have reported from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Feed the apple to your feverish ones, for there is none of the things more beneficial than the apple.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat the apple, for it repairs the stomach.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating quince is strengthening for the weak heart, it sweetens the stomach, sharpens the intellect/heart, and emboldens the timid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib was in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). A quince was gifted to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) cut a piece from it and handed it to Ja'far. He refused to eat it, so he said: 'Take it and eat it, for it purifies the heart and emboldens the timid.' And in another report: 'Eat it, for it clears the complexion and improves the offspring.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who eats a quince upon the empty stomach would make good his water and improve the child birth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazie, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'O Ja'far, eat the quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the timid.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who eats a quince, Allah (Exalted and Majestic) will make wisdom speak from his tongue for forty mornings.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from his father, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send a Prophet except that with him was the fragrance of the quince.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: 'The quince removes the distress of the grieving one, just as the hand removes the sweat from the forehead.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The fig removes bad breath, strengthens the mouth and the bone, promotes hair growth, removes illness, and with it one has no need for medicine. And he (peace be upon him) said: The fig is most similar to the vegetation of Paradise.
And Sahl ibn Ziyad reported it from Ahmad ibn al-Ash'ath, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, also similarly.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Eat the pear, for it clears the heart and soothes the pains of the interior by the permission of Allah, the Exalted.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Washa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The pear repairs the stomach and strengthens it; it and the quince are the same. It is more beneficial when the stomach is full than when it is empty (with saliva). And whoever is afflicted by overwhelming stress, let him eat it, meaning while eating food.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and al-Washa' together, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I had a guest with me, so he desired to eat a citron with honey, so I fed it to him and ate with him. Then I went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and there was a meal spread before him. He said to me, 'Approach and eat.' I said, 'I have eaten before coming to you a citron with honey, and I still feel its heaviness because I ate a lot of it.' He said, 'O servant, go to the maid and tell her to send us a piece of dry bread from what she dries in the oven.' So it was brought to him, and he said to me, 'Eat from this dry bread, for it digests the citron.' So I ate it. Then I stood up, and it was as if I had not eaten anything.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: ‘What are your physicians instructing you with regarding the Citron?’ So I said, ‘They are instructing us that we eat it before the meal’. So he (peace be upon him) said: ‘I am ordering you all with it after the meal’.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Eat the citron after the meal, for the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them) do that.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: The dried bread digests the Citron.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar Al-Yamani, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'They claim that the citron eaten on an empty stomach is the best of what it can be.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'If it is before the meal, it is good, and if it is after the meal, it is good, and better, and best.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Abu Ayyub al-Madani, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) liked looking at the green citron and the red apple.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yahya ibn Musa Al-San'ani, who said: I entered upon Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) at Mina, and Abu Ja'far (the second, i.e., the third Imam) was upon his thigh, and he was peeling a banana for him and feeding him.
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Usamah, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he brought closer to me a banana, and I ate it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yahya al-Sana'ani, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), and he was in Mecca, and he was peeling a banana and feeding it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is this the newborn, the Blessed?' He said: 'Yes, O Yahya! This is the newborn the like of whom has not been born in Islam, a birth of great blessing upon our Shias from him.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Yasar al-Khadim, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The melon eaten on an empty stomach causes the stroke; we seek refuge with Allah from it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat fresh dates with melon.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat watermelon with dates.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ary, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) liked the fresh dates with the melon.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ate the melon with sugar, and ate the melon with fresh dates.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Harun, from Mufazzal al-Madaini, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Imam (peace be upon him) sent for me one day and seated me for lunch. When they brought the meal spread, there were no vegetables on it, so he restrained his hand. Then he said to the servant, 'Do you not know that I do not eat on a spread that has no greens? Bring me the greens.' The servant went and brought the vegetables and placed them on the spread. Then he (peace be upon him) extended his hand and ate.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hannan, who said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) at the food-spread, so he inclined upon the vegetables, and I abstained from them due to an illness that was with me. So he turned towards me and said, 'O Hannan! Do you not know that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was never brought a platter except that upon it were vegetables?' I said, 'And why, may I be sacrificed for you?' So he said: 'Because the hearts of the believers are green, and they yearn for their forms.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever spends the night with seven leaves of endive inside his stomach will be safe from colitis that night, if God wills.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Khalid ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather Sufyan ibn al-Samti, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who loves that his water and his children be abundant, so let him be habitual in eating the endive.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who loves that his water and his children be abundant, so let him frequent in eating the endive.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The best of vegetables is the endive (hinda'), and there is no leaf of it except that upon it is a drop from Paradise. So eat it and do not shake it off when eating it. He said: And my father (peace be upon him) forbade us from shaking it when we ate it.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The endive is the chief of the vegetables.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from al-Hajjal, from Thal'ah, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: ‘You should consume endive, for it increases semen, improves the child, and it is hot and moist, increasing in male children.’

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Suleyman al-Hazza' al-Jabali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz, who said: I had lunch with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and upon the food-spread were vegetables, and with us was an old man who avoided the endive. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'But you all are thinking that the endive is cold, and it is not like that, but it is moderate, and its merits upon the vegetables is like our merits upon the people'.

From him, from one of our companions, from Al-Asamm, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat the endive, for there is no morning but that a drop from Paradise descends upon it. So when you eat it, do not shake it off.' He said: And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) forbade us from shaking it off whenever we ate it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said: I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'The endive is a healing from a thousand illnesses. There is no illness in the inside of a son of Adam except that the endive suppresses it.' He (the narrator) said, 'And one day he called for it for one of the servants, and the fever had seized him, and the headache. So he ordered that it should be pounded and rendered upon a paper, and the viola oil be poured over it, and for it to be placed upon his forehead. Then he said: 'But, it removes the fever and benefits from the headache, and eliminates it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The vegetable of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was endive, and the vegetable of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was basil, and the vegetable of Fatima (peace be upon her) was purslane.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Hassam, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: A slave of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) fell ill, so he (peace be upon him) asked about him, and it was said to him, 'He has a spleen ailment.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Feed him leeks for three days.' So we fed them to him, the blood settled, then he was cured.
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaqoub who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) cutting the leek by its roots, so he washed it with water and ate it.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Amr ibn Isa, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the leek, so he said: 'Eat it, for therein are four qualities – It aromatises the breath, and it dispels the wind, and it cuts off the hemorrhoids, and it is a safety from the leprosy for the one who is habitual over it'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa or someone else, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Vegetables were mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Eat the leek, for its example among the vegetables is like the example of bread among the rest of the food,' or he said: 'Among the sauces.'

From him, from one of his companions, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer who said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) at the food-spread, so I inclined towards the endive. He said to me: 'O Hanaan, why are you not eating the leek?' I said, 'Because of what has come from you regarding the reports about the endive.' He said: 'And what is that which has come from us?' I said, 'It is said from you that you said that a drop falls upon it from Paradise every day.' He said: 'So upon the leek, then, seven drops.' I said, 'So how should I eat it?' He said: 'Cut off its roots and throw away its heads.'
From him, from one of his companions, raising it, said, Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) used to eat the leek with the grained salt.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa or someone else, from Qutayba ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is upon you with (eating) the celery, for it is a food of Ilyas (peace be upon him), and Al-Yas'a (peace be upon him), and Yoshua ibn Noun (peace be upon him).'

From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb al-Naysaburi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, regarding what is known from Nadir the servant, He said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) mentioned celery, so he said: 'You all desire it, and there is no animal except that it rubs itself with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no vegetable upon the surface of the earth more noble, nor more beneficial than the Purslane, and it is the vegetable of Fatima (peace be upon her).' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah curse the Clan of Umayya! They named it the 'vegetable of the foolish' out of hatred for us and enmity towards Fatima (peace be upon her).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) trod upon the scorching ground, so it burned him. So he trod upon the purslane, which is referred to as the 'vegetable of the idiots', so the heat of the scorching ground settled from him. So he supplicated for it, and he used to love it, and he was saying: 'From the vegetables, there is none more Blessed.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Isa, from Ya'qub ibn 'Amir, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: The rue increases in the intellect.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hamdani, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Ja'far or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — the uncertainty being from Muhammad ibn Musa — he said: The rue was mentioned, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, there are benefits in it — it increases the intellect and augments the brain, apart from the fact that it decays the water of the back.' And it is reported that it is good for earache.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who had sheep and cows, and he was aware of the slaughtered from these, so he isolated it, and isolated the dead. Then the dead and the slaughtered got mixed up. So how should he deal with it?' So he said: 'He should sell it to the one who considers the dead as permissible (to eat), and he can eat from its price, for there is no problem with it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the properly slaughtered animal and the dead meat are mixed together, sell it to the one who considers the dead meat permissible (to eat), and eat its price.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, and others, from Qutaybah al-A'sha or he said Qutaybah ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'If a man fills his stomach with watercress after he has prayed the last Isha prayer, and sleeps during that night, his soul will pull him towards leprosy, except [if he is protected by God].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever eats watercress at night, the vein of leprosy will strike him from his nose, and he will spend the night with blood flowing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibnasan, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the vegetables: the endive (al-hindaba'), the basil (al-badharuj), and the watercress (al-jarjir). He (peace be upon him) said: 'The endive and the basil are for us (the Ahl al-Bayt), and the watercress is for the Banu Umayya.'

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Nusayr, the mawla of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Muwaffaq, the mawla of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: My master, Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), when he ordered the purchase of herbs, ordered that a large amount be bought, including watercress, and it would be purchased for him. He would say (peace be upon him): 'How foolish some people are! They say that it grows in a valley in Hell, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "Its fuel is people and stones"; so how can herbs grow therein?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Uthman, who raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), He said: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed the leprosy from the Jews by their eating the chard and their pulling out the roots.'
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The best of the vegetables is the chard.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Suleiman ibn Abbad, from Isa ibn Abu al-Ward, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). That the Children of Israel complained to Musa (peace be upon him) about the whiteness (vitiligo) they were experiencing, so he took that complaint to Allah, Glorious and High. So Allah revealed to him: 'Order them to eat the meat of the cow with the chard (salt/celery greens).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said: Feed your sick ones the chard (silq), meaning its leaves, for therein is a healing, and there is no cure with it, nor is there a suffering for it, and it calms the sleep of the patient, and avoid its root for it agitates the black bile.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of the Husayniyyun, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) That the chard suppresses the vein of leprosy, and what enters the inside of the vitiligo sufferer is like the leaf of the chard.
And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) liked the gourd in the pots the gourd, and it is the pumpkin.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) liked the gourd (pumpkin), and he used to pick it up from the platter.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Shami, from al-Husayn ibn Hanzala, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The gourd increases the mind.
From him, from Ali ibn Hassān, from Mūsā ibn Bakr, who said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The gourd increases the intellect.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Al-Sayyari, raising it, said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) liked the gourd, and he would order his wives, when they cooked a pot, to be frequent with the gourd, and it is the pumpkin.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from some of our companions, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Among what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed to Ali (peace be upon him) was that he said to him: 'O Ali! Upon you is the gourd, so eat it, for it increases the brain and the intellect.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Hanaan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was with him upon the food-spread, so he gave me a radish and said: 'O Hanaan! Eat the radish, for therein are three qualities – its leaf dispels the wind, and its core eases the flow of urine, and its root cuts the phlegm'. And in another report: 'And its leaf nourishes'.

From him, from Al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Al-Mubarak, from Abu Uthman, from Dorust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The radish: its root cuts the phlegm, and its core digests, and its leaf causes urine to flow with a flow.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, or someone else, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Eating carrots warms the two kidneys and strengthens the manhood.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Jallab, from Musa ibn Ismail, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The carrots are a security from the colitis, and the hemorrhoids, and it aids upon the copulation'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eating carrots warms the kidneys and establishes the manhood.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How can I eat it when I have no teeth?' So he said to me, 'Instruct the maid to boil it, and eat it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) said: 'Adhere to the Laft (turnip), so eat it, meaning the turnip, for there is no one except that he has a vein of leprosy, and the Laft dissolves it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdul Aziz al-Muhtadi, who raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), saying: There is no one except that there is a vein of leprosy in him, so melt it with the turnip.

From him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, [from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak], from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) or he said, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He said: There is no one except that there is a vein of leprosy in him, so melt it by eating the turnip.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Be persistent with the turnip, eat it, and make eating it a habit, and keep it secret except from its deserving one, for there is no one but that he has a vein of leprosy within him, so melt it by eating it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat the cucumbers with the salt.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durusta al-Wasiti, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you eat cucumbers, eat them from their lower part, for it is greater in its blessing.'

A number of our companions, from our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ali ibn Aamir, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Ja'far ibn Yahya, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Eat the aubergine, for it removes the illness and there is no disease in it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the 3rd said to one of his workers: 'Frequent for us from the aubergines, for it is hot during the time of heat, and cool in the times of coldness, being moderate in all of the times, good upon every state'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi, who said: He (peace be upon him) said to one of his slaves: 'Buy less for us from the onions, and more for us from the aubergines.' So he said to him (peace be upon him) inquiring, 'The aubergines?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the aubergines, it gathers all tastes, removes illness, is suitable for the constitution, balanced in its states, suitable for the old man and the young man, moderate in its heat and coldness, hot in the place of heat and cold in the place of cold.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Abdul Aziz ibn Hassan al-Baghdadi, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioned the onion, so he said: 'It aromatises the breath, and does away with the phlegm, and increases in the copulation'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The onion removes mental breakdown (or fatigue), strengthens the nerves, increases walking ability, increases in the water (semen/fluids), and removes fever.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kaslan, from Maysar the seller of al-Zutti, and he was his maternal uncle, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eat the onion, for in it are three qualities: it improves the breath, strengthens the gums, and increases in the semen and sexual intercourse.'

From him, from Al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Al-Mubarak Al-Dinawari, from Abu Uthman, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The onion improves the breath, strengthens the back, and softens the skin.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you enter a land, eat from its onions, so that it may dispel its plague from you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about eating garlic, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade it only because of its smell, so he said: 'The one who eats this bad vegetable should not approach our mosques.' As for the one who eats it and does not come to the mosque, there is no problem.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about eating garlic, onion, and leeks, so he said: 'There is no problem in eating them raw and in the pots, and there is no problem in being treated with garlic, but when one of you eats that, he should not go out to the Masjid.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan Al-Zayyat, who said: When I had fulfilled my rituals, I passed by Al-Medina, so I asked about Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and was told that he is at Al-Yanba'a. So I went to Yanba'a. He said to me: 'O Hassan, have you walked to over here?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you, as I disliked going out and not seeing you.' He said (peace be upon him): 'I ate from this vegetable, meaning the garlic, so I wanted to keep away from the Masjid of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The medicine of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was thyme, and he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'It becomes for the stomach a lining like the lining of the plush brocade.'

From him, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Sulayman, from one of the Wasitis, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) That he complained to him of moisture (acidity), so he ordered him to eat the thyme upon the empty stomach.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended to me with the khilal (toothpick).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended unto the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the toothbrush, the toothpick, and the cupping.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbihi, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) picking his teeth, so I looked at him. He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pick his teeth, and he was of the aromatic mouth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim al-Hazza', from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) gave a toothpick to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and said to him: 'O Ja'far! Use the toothpick, for it is a remedy for the mouth,' or he said: 'For the gums, and it brings sustenance.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Use the toothpick, for it is a remedy for the gums and the back teeth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Do not pick your teeth with a twig of basil, nor with a shoot of pomegranate, for these two agitate the vein of leprosy.

Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who picks his teeth with reeds, his needs will not be fulfilled for six days.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade picking teeth with the reed and the basil stem.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to pick his teeth with everything he came across, except for the palm leaves and the reeds.

From him, from one of those who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade picking teeth with pomegranate stems, myrtle leaves, and reeds, and said: 'These stir the vein of the eater.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Jarir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meat that remains in the teeth, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for what is in the front of the mouth, swallow it, and as for what is in the molars, discard it.'

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: As for what remains on the gums, swallow it and gulp it down, and whatever is between the teeth, throw it out.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Not one of you should swallow what he picks teeth with, for pus can happen from it'.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ahmad ibn Yazeed, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Eating the saltwort disinfects the mouth.

One of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadrami, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'We eat the ushnana.' He said: 'Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), when he performed ablution with it, closed his lips. And in it is an abhorrent quality: it causes tuberculosis, removes the water of the back, and weakens the knees.' I said, 'And what about the clay?' He said: 'Every clay is prohibited, like the dead body, blood, and flesh of the pig, except for the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for indeed in it is a healing from every illness, but do not use it excessively, and in it is security from every fear.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Umar, from Umar, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: The one who cleans himself with the cyperus after defecation, and washes his mouth with it after eating, will not be afflicted by an illness in his mouth, nor will he fear anything from the winds of hemorrhoids.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Hasan ibn al-Zibarqan al-Ansari, from al-Fadl ibn Uthman, from Abu Aziz al-Muradi, who said: And he is the maternal uncle of my mother. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Take the cyperus (suda) for your teeth, for it aromatises the mouth and increases in copulation.'
