Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from some of his companions from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Balad who said: Al-‘Abbas ibn Musa took me and commanded to hit my mouth, so my teeth became shaky and I could not chew food. I then saw my father in my dream. There was an old man with him whom I could not recognize. My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said to me to offer greeting of peace to him. I then asked, ‘Father, who is he?’ He replied, ‘He is Abu Shaybah al-Khurasani.’ I offered him greeting of peace and he asked, ‘Why do I see you in this condition?’ I replied, ‘Sinful al-‘Abbas ibn Musa commanded to hit on my mouth and my teeth have become shaky.’ He said, ‘Tie them down with cyperus.’ In the morning I rinsed my teeth with al-Sa‘d and my teeth calmed down.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in Al-Hijr, and he was seated, and with him were a number of his family members, so I heard him saying: 'My teeth hurt, so I took the cyperus and rubbed it by my teeth, and that benefitted me, and it settled down from me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a mouse falls into the butter (clarified animal fat) and dies in it, if it was solid, then throw it out and what is adjacent to it, and eat what remains; and if it was melted, then do not eat it and kindle the lamp with it; and oil is similar to that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A rat died in butter, or oil, or honey.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the butter and the honey, the rat and what is around it are taken out, and the oil is used for lighting (by removing the rat).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about a pot in which food was cooked, and there was a mouse in the pot. He said: 'Its broth is poured out, the meat is washed, and it is eaten.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mouse and the dog that fall into the butter and the oil, then come out from it alive, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with eating it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) And he (peace be upon him) said: He was asked about the 'Jirri' (a type of fish) that is on the skewer with the fish. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat what is above the Jirri, and discard what the Jirri's juices have flowed onto.' He (peace be upon him) was asked about the spleen on a skewer with the meat, and underneath it is bread, which is called 'Juthab'. Can one eat what is beneath it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, eat the meat and the bread, and discard the spleen, because the spleen is in a membrane (veil) and nothing flows from it. So if the spleen is pierced or torn, do not eat from what the spleen's juices have flowed onto.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about a heap of wheat upon which the fat of the pig had melted. He said: If they are able to wash it, it is eaten, and if they are not able to wash it, it is not eaten. And it was said: Sow it until it sprouts.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the food of the People of the Book and what is permissible from it. He said: The grains.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about eating with the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian. He said: 'If it was from your food, then perform ablution, and there is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a group of Muslims who were eating and a Magian man presented himself, should they invite him to their meal? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, I would not eat with the Magian, and I dislike that I should prohibit upon you something which you are doing in your cities.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the vessels of the Ahl al-Zimma and the Magians, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat in their vessels, nor from their food which they cook, nor in their vessels in which they drink wine.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the food of those who were Given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The grains and the vegetables.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ali ibn Ja' from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about eating with the Magian from one bowl, and lying down with him on one bed, and shaking hands with him. He said: No.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Jariya who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I intermingle with the Magians, so I eat from their meals.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ismail ibn Jabir, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the food of the People of the Book?' He said, 'Do not eat it.' Then he was silent for a moment, then said, 'Do not eat it.' Then he was silent for a moment, then said, 'Do not eat it, and do not leave it saying that it is forbidden, but leave it turning away from it, for in their vessels is wine and the flesh of the swine.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Zakariyya who said: I was a Christian, so I became a Muslim. So I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'My family are upon the religion of Christianity, so I am with them in one house and I eat from their vessels.' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do they eat the flesh of the swine?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim bin Mihran, from Talha bin Zayd, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who engages in the eating of the clay so he has participated in (shedding) his own blood'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam from clay, so He prohibited eating clay upon his offspring.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) regarding a man who eats clay, so he forbade it, and he said: 'Do not eat it, for if you eat it and die, you have aided in killing yourself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, wishful thinking (daydreaming) is the work of undue concern (whispering), and the most frequent trap of Satan is eating clay; and it bequeaths illness to the body and stirs up disease. And whoever eats clay, so he becomes weaker than the strength he had before he ate it, and weaker than the action he was doing before he ate it, he will be held accountable for what is between his strength and his weakness, and will be punished for it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What are the people reporting regarding eating clay and its abhorrence?' So he said: 'Rather, that is the wet [clay], and that is the loam [soil].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who eats clay and dies, he has aided upon himself.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadrami, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about clay, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating clay is forbidden, like the dead animal, blood, and flesh of the pig, except for the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for indeed in it is healing from every illness and security from every fear.'
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassa from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not eat in vessels of gold and silver.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about vessels of gold and silver, so he disliked them. I said, 'Some of our companions have narrated that there used to be a mirror for Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) clad in silver?' He said, 'No, and praise be to Allah. It only had a ring of silver, and it is with me.' Then he said, 'When Al-Abbas was circumcised, a stick clad in silver was made for him, similar to what is made for children, its silver being worth about ten dirhams. So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ordered it to be broken.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not eat in vessels of silver, nor in silver-coated vessels.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he forbade (using) vessels of gold and silver

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah, from Bureyd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he disliked drinking from silver, and from a silver-coated cup, and similarly that one anoints from a silver-coated container, and the comb is similar to that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) having been brought a cup of water in which was a handle of silver, so I saw him remove it by his teeth.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: The vessels of gold and silver are belongings of those who have no conviction.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Bistam ibn Murra from Is'haq ibn Hassan from Haytham ibn Waqid from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Abdi from Abu Harun from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he was asked: 'What is your opinion regarding this fish which our brethren from the people of Kufa allege is prohibited?' So Abu Sa'id said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Kufa is the skull of the Arabs, and the spear of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and a treasure of faith, so take from them. I inform you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stayed in Mecca for a day and a night, hungry. Then he went out and I went out with him. We passed by a group sitting and eating lunch. They said: O Messenger of Allah, the lunch! He said to them: Yes, make way for your Prophet. So he sat between two men, and I sat, and he took a loaf and broke it in half. Then he looked at their sauce and said: What is this sauce of yours? They said: The sea bass, O Messenger of Allah. So he threw the piece from his hand and arose.' Abu Sa'id said: 'And I stayed behind after him to see what the people's opinion was. The people differed among themselves. A group said: The Messenger of Allah prohibited the sea bass. And a group said: He did not prohibit it, but excused himself from it. For if he had prohibited it, he would have forbidden us from eating it. So I memorized their discussion and followed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) trotting until I caught up with him.' Then we came to another group eating lunch. They said: O Messenger of Allah, the lunch! He said: Yes, make way for your Prophet. So he sat between two men, and I sat with him. When he took a piece, he looked at the sauce of the people and said: What is this sauce of yours? They said: Lizard, O Messenger of Allah. So he threw the piece and arose. Abu Sa'id said: 'So I stayed behind afterwards, and the people were in two groups. One group said: The Messenger of Allah prohibited it, so from there they did not eat it. And another group said: He only excused himself from it. And if he had prohibited it, he would have forbidden us from eating it. Then I followed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) until I caught up with him.' So we passed by the base of Safa, and there were pots boiling. They said: O Messenger of Allah, if yo

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: All those possessing fangs from the predatory animals, and claws from the birds, are forbidden.

Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every possessor of fangs from the predatory animals and (every possessor of) claws from the birds is forbidden.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat anything from the predators.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan — meaning Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) — 'Is it permissible to eat the meat of the elephant?' So he said: 'No.' I said: 'And why?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because it is a transformed creature (mathula), and God — Mighty and Majestic — has forbidden the morphed ones (amsakh) and the flesh of what has been transformed in their forms.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about eating the lizard (dabb). So he said: 'Indeed the lizard, the mouse, the monkeys, and the pigs are transformed creatures (musukh).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Sahl al-Qurshi who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the meat of the dog. He said: 'It is a morphed creature (mash).' I said: 'It is haram (forbidden)?' He said: 'It is najis (impure).' I repeated the question to him three times, and each time he said: 'It is najis.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he disliked the eating of every creature possessing a sting.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the speckled crow and the black one — is it permissible to eat them both? So he said: 'It is not permissible to eat anything from the crows — neither the rook nor any other.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: The peacock — it is not permissible to eat it, nor its eggs.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that they both asked him: about eating the meat of domesticated donkeys. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade it, and forbade eating it on the day of Khayber.' And he only forbade eating it at that time because it was the carriers of the people, and the prohibition is only what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited in the Quran.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Muslims were exhausted in Khaybar, so the Muslims hastened with their animals (to slaughter them). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered them to restrain the cooking-pots (from the animals), and he did not say that they were prohibited (حرام), and that was for the preservation of the animals.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the meat of horses, so he said: 'Do not eat it unless necessity befalls you.' And [I asked] about the meat of domesticated donkeys, so he said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is recorded that he forbade eating it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibn Muskan who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meat of donkeys, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade eating it on the day of Khaybar. He said, And I asked him about eating horses and mules, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade it, so do not eat them unless you are compelled to do so.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The elephant is a morphed creature; it was an adulterous king. And the wolf is a morphed creature; it was a Bedouin pimp. And the rabbit is a morphed creature; it was a woman who betrayed her husband and did not perform the ritual bath from her menstruation. And the bat is a morphed creature; it was one who stole people's dates. And the monkeys and the pigs were a people from the Children of Israel who exceeded the limits in the Sabbath. And the sea bass and the lizard are a sect from the Children of Israel who did not believe when the Table Spread (Al-Ma'idah) was sent down to Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him); they strayed, so a sect fell into the sea and a sect fell onto the land. And the mouse is the immoral woman. And the scorpion was a malicious gossiper. And the bear and the wasp were butchers who used to steal (cheat) in the weighing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, who said: Im al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked about the speckled crow, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not to be eaten.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'And who permitted to you the black (one)?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Suleiman al-Ja'fary, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The peacock is a morphed creature; it was a handsome man who insisted stubbornly upon the wife of a believing man who loved him, so he copulated with her. Then she sent messages to him afterwards, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, morphed both of them into peacocks, a female and a male. And their meat is not eaten, nor their eggs.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, raising it (to the Prophet), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a speech of his: 'There will be a year after me in which the Believer eats in one gut, and the Infidel eats in seven guts.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Abundant eating is abhorred (makruh).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst support against the Religion is a heart that is defeated (or weak), a belly that is desirous, and intense sexual arousal.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wuheyb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad! The belly becomes arrogant from its eating, and the closest a servant is to Allah, Exalted and Mighty, is when his belly is light, and the most hateful a servant is to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is when his belly is full.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one of you who belches the most in the world, he will be the one who hungers the most in the Hereafter' or he said: 'on the Day of Judgment'.
And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When you belch, do not raise (the sound of) your belching.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqteeni, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Eating upon satiation inherits vitiligo.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every illness is from satiation (overeating), except for fever, for it arrives gradually. for it arrives gradually.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Salih al-Nayli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah (Exalted and Majestic) hates abundant eating. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no escape for the son of Adam from a meal by which he sustains his body. So when one of you eats food, let him make a third of his belly for food, a third for drink, and a third for breathing. And do not fatten yourselves like the fattening of pigs for slaughter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the belly is satiated, it rebels.
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing more hateful to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than a filled belly.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When one of you is invited to a meal, let him not let his child follow him, for if he does, he will be eating unlawfully and entering as a usurper.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari, from his maternal uncle who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who eats a meal he had not been invited to, so rather is eating a piece from the Fire'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That he disliked for the man that he eats with his left hand, or drinks with it, or takes (something) with it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not eat with the left hand while you are able (to eat with the right).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), peace be upon him, said: I asked him about the man who eats with his left hand or drinks with it, so he said: 'He should not eat with his left hand, nor drink with his left hand, nor take anything with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out before the Fajr prayer (subuh), and with him was a piece of bread which he had dipped in milk, and he was eating while walking, and Bilal was calling the Adhan for prayer, so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prayed with the people.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman al-Azramy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if a man eats while he is walking; the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The food of one is sufficient for two, and the food of two is sufficient for three, and the food of three is sufficient for four.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The meal is complete when it gathers four characteristics: when it is from permissible [food], when there are many hands [partakers], when it is named [Bismillah] at its beginning, and when Allah is praised (Alhamdulillah) at its end.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If a believer were to invite me to the food of an arm of a sheep, I would accept, and that would be from the religion; and if a polytheist or a hypocrite were to invite me to the food of a whole camel, I would not accept, and that would be from the religion. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refused me the scum of the polytheists and the hypocrites and their food.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Is'haq ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, from the rights of the Muslim upon the Muslim is that he answers him when he invites him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, among the obligatory rights of the believer is that his invitation (for a meal) be answered.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I bequeath to the present one from my community, and the absentee, that he should answer the invitation of the Muslim, even if it is over five miles away, for that is from the Religion.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ibn Fazzal from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Abd al-A'ala, the mawla of the family of Sam, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, among the obligatory rights of the Muslim upon his brother is answering his invitation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Accept the invitation for the wedding feast and the circumcision, and do not accept the invitation for the lowering (or circumcising) of the female slaves.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani, from Abu Ayyub Suleiman ibn Muqatil al-Madani, from Dawud ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ja'fari, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in one of his military expeditions, so a group of riders passed by him while he was praying. They stopped by the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked them about the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), supplicated, praised, and said, 'If we were not in a hurry, we would have waited for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so convey our greetings to him,' and they went away. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came back in anger, then said to them: 'The riders stopped by you and asked you about me, delivered the greeting to me, and you did not offer them lunch. It would be hard on a people in whom my dear friend Ja'far is, that they should pass by without having lunch with him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from a number (of narrators), they raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When your brother comes to you, offer him food. If he does not eat, offer him water. If he does not drink, offer him ablution (wudu).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Sama'a ibn Mihran who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the edible from the birds and the wild beasts. So he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited every bird with claws and every wild beast with fangs. So I said: The people are saying (it is prohibited) from predatory animals. So he said to me: O Sama'a! All predatory animals are forbidden, even if the predatory animal has no fangs; the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said this in detail. And God, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited all transformed creatures. So now, eat from the birds of land those that have a crop, and from the birds of water those that have a gizzard like the gizzard of a dove — not a stomach like the stomach of a human. Every bird that soars and has claws is forbidden, and the soaring flight is like the flight of the hawk, the falcon, the kite, and whatever resembles that. Every bird that flaps its wings is permissible. The crop and gizzard are used to examine those birds whose flight pattern is unknown, and every unknown bird.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'The birds — what may be eaten from them?' So he said: 'Do not eat from them what does not have a gizzard.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali al-Zayyat, from Zurara — that he said: By Allah, I have never seen anyone like Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at all. And that is because I asked him, saying: 'May Allah keep you well! What may be eaten from birds?' He said: 'Eat what flaps (its wings) and do not eat what glides (with wings held out).' I said: 'What about eggs in the thickets?' He said: 'What has equal ends (rounded), do not eat it; and what has different ends (oblong), eat it.' I said: 'What about water birds?' He said: 'What has a gizzard, eat it; and what has no gizzard, do not eat it.'
Eat from the bird that has a gizzard for it, but no claw for it. He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about the birds of the water, so he said: Similar to that.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Eat from the birds what had a gizzard, or a spur, or a crop (craw).'

Some of our companions, from Ibn Jumhur, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I happen to be in the thickets/marshes, and various birds come over me. What can I eat from them?' He said: 'Eat what flaps its wings, and do not eat what glides (with outstretched wings).' I said: 'I am brought (birds) that are already slaughtered.' He said: 'Eat what had a craw (gizzard).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the benevolence of the man to his brother is that he accepts his gift, and that he should gift to him with what is with him, and he should not burden anything for him.' And Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not like the ones who burden others.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The believer is not shy/embarrassed from his brother, and it is not known which of the two is more wonderful: the one who burdens his brother to make effort for him when he enters, or the one who is burdened by his brother.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Sinan came to me and said, 'Do you have anything?' I said, 'Yes.' So I sent my son and gave him a dirham to buy meat and eggs with it. He said to me, 'Where did you send your son?' So I informed him. He said, 'Send him back, send him back! Do you have oil?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Bring it, for I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man is ruined who belittles to his brother what is present with him, and a man is ruined who belittles to his brother what he brings to him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazam ibn Hakeem, from the one who raised it to him, said: Al-Harith al-Awar came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! I would love for you to honor me by eating with me.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him, 'On the condition that you do not exert yourself for me in anything.' And he entered. So Al-Harith brought him a piece of bread, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) began to eat it. So Al-Harith said to him, 'I have dirhams with me,' and he showed them, and they were in his sleeve. 'So if you permit me, I will buy something for you other than this.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him, 'This [bread] is from what is in your house.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Destroyed is the Muslim person who belittles what is with him for the guest.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When your brother comes to you, bring him what you have, and when you invite him, exert effort for him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about this Verse: 'Nor is there blame on you that you eat from your houses, or your fathers' houses' — up to the end of the Verse. I said, 'What is the meaning of His Words: 'or your friends'? He said: 'By Allah, it is the man who enters the house of his friend and eats without his permission.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'or what you possess the keys of, or your friends', he said: 'These are those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named in this verse. They eat without their permission from the dates and the curries (food), and similarly the wife eats from the house of her husband without his permission. So as for what is besides that from the food, then no (permission is needed).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The wife may eat and give charity, and the friend may eat in the house of his brother and give charity.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about this Verse: 'Nor is there blame on you that you eat from your houses, or your fathers' houses or your mothers' houses' – the Verse. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no blame on you regarding what you eat and consume from what you possess its keys, as long as you do not spoil it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it from him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'or what you possess the keys of'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man who has a representative managing his wealth, so he eats without his permission.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) along with Ibn Abi Yafour, and we were a group. So he called for breakfast, and we had breakfast and he had breakfast with us. I was the youngest of the men in age, so I began to be cautious (in my eating) while I was eating. So he said to me: 'Eat! Do you not know that the affection of a man for his brother is recognized by his eating from his food?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from a man, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: We ate with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and we were brought a bowl of rice. So we began excusing ourselves (from eating), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'What are you doing? The one of you with the strongest love for us is the best of you in eating with us.' Abd al-Rahman said: 'So I lifted the covering of the meal and ate.' He said: 'Yes, now.' And he began narrating to us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was gifted a bowl of rice from the side of the Ansar. So he called Salman, Al-Miqdad, and Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with them). They began excusing themselves regarding eating. So he said: 'What are you doing? The strongest of you in love for us is the best of you in eating with us.' So they began eating well. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on them, and be pleased with them, and send blessings upon them.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdullah ibn Suleiman al-Sayrafi, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he presented to us food containing roast meat and other items after it. Then he brought a bowl containing rice, so I ate with him. He said, 'Eat.' I said, 'I have already eaten.' He said, 'Eat, for the love of a man for his brother is considered by his extending himself in eating.' Then he marked a portion for me with his finger in the bowl and said to me, 'You must eat up to that,' after I had already eaten. So I ate it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Yunus from Abu al-Rabi' who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) called for food, so a mash (porridge) was brought to him. He said to us: 'Approach and eat.' He said: 'So the people began to be reserved.' He said (peace be upon him): 'Eat, for the affection of a man for his brother is manifested in his eating with him.' He said: 'So we began to gorge ourselves, as the camels gorge themselves.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would sometimes feed us al-Farani and al-Akhbisa, then he would feed us bread and oil. So it was said to him, 'If only you would manage your affairs until you equalize it.' He said: 'We manage by the Command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So when He expands for us, we expand, and when He rations for us, we ration accordingly.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three things for which the believer is not reckoned: food that he eats, and clothing that he wears, and a righteous wife who assists him, and by whom he protects his chastity.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Sa'id, from Abu Hamza, who said: We were a group in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He called for food that we had no prior experience of being so delicious and fragrant. We were served dates so clear and beautiful that we looked at our own faces in them. A man said, 'We will surely be questioned about this bounty with which we have been favored in the presence of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is more generous and noble than to feed you food, make it palatable, and then question you about it. But He will question you about what He has favored upon you through Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no extravagance regarding the meal.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Al-Harith ibn Hariz, from Sadeer Al-Sayrafi, from Abu Khalid Al-Kabuli, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he called for the midday meal, and I ate with him food that I had never eaten before, cleaner than it nor more delicious. When we had finished the meal, he said: 'O Abu Khalid, how did you find your food?' or he said: 'Our food?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have not seen anything more delicious than it, nor cleaner at all.' But I remembered the Verse which is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'You shall certainly be questioned about the Bounties on that Day.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but rather you will be questioned about what you are upon from the Truth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Prepare food, be choosy in it, and invite your companions over it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one of our companions, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) hosted a banquet for one of his sons, so he fed the people of the city faludhaj (a type of sweet dish) for three days in large bowls, in the mosques and the alleyways. Some of the people of the city criticized him for this. So that reached him (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not grant anything to any of His prophets except that He granted Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) the like of it, and added to it what He did not grant them.' He said to Sulayman (peace be upon him): 'This is Our gift, so bestow it or withhold it without measure.' And He said to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family): 'And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and from whatever he forbids you, refrain.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrouq, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The invitation is not obligatory except in four cases: the wedding, the circumcision, the return (from a journey), and the excuse (for a specific event).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The banquet (walimah) is for four occasions: the wedding, the circumcision (khars), which is the newborn for whom the aqiqah is performed and food is served, the excuse/apology (i'dhar), which is the circumcision of the boy, and the return (i'ab), which is when a man invites his brothers when he returns from his absence.' And in another report, or 'tawkir', which is the construction of the house, or other such occasions.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, by a chain mentioning it, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the food of a banquet in which the rich are singled out and the poor are left out.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: A man said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We find an aroma in the food of a wedding feast that is not found elsewhere.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'There is no wedding in which a camel is sacrificed, or a cow is slaughtered, or a sheep, except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sends an angel with it carrying a carat of musk from Paradise until it blends into their food. That is the aroma which is smelled because of that.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from one of the Iraqis, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Ja'far al-Qalanisi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'We prepare the food, make it good, and are particular about it, but we do not find in it the aroma of the food of the wedding feast.' He said, 'That is because the food of the wedding feast has an aroma blowing from Paradise, because it is food prepared for the permissible (halal).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, by his chain, from the one who mentioned it, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man enters a city, he is a guest upon those in it from his brethren and the people of his religion, until he departs from them.'

Abu Abdillah al-Ash'ari, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Karkhi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man enters a city, he is a guest upon those in it from the people of his religion, until he departs from them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Hafs Al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guest is treated with kindness for two nights. So when it is the third night, he is from the people of the household; he eats what he finds.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Wasil from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Hospitality is for the first day, and the second, and the third, and whatever is after that, so it is a charity by which you give charity upon him.' He said: Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let not one of you lodge upon his brother until he burdens him with it.' It was said, 'O Rasool-Allah, how does he burden him?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Until there is not in his possession anything that he can spend upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Musa, from Zubyan ibn Hakim, from Musa al-Numayri, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I saw a guest with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). One day, the guest stood up to attend to one of the needs. He (peace be upon him) forbade him from doing that, and stood up himself to that particular need, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade making the guest serve.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ubayd ibn Abi Abdillah Al-Baghdadi, from the one who informed him, said: A guest lodged with Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), and was seated in his presence discussing with him during one of the nights. So the lantern dimmed, and the man extended his hand to correct it. So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) stopped him, then attended to it himself, so he corrected it. Then he said to him: 'We are a people who do not make our guests serve.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Musa, from Zubyan ibn Hakim, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Numayri, from Maysara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from the weakening (of character) to neglect to reward (the guest), and from the roughness (of character) to make the guest serve (you). So when the guest lodges with you, aid him, and when he departs, do not aid him (in his departure), for it is from the lowness (of character). And provide for him, and make good his provision, for it is from the generosity.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Hafs Al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guest, when he comes and lodges with a people, brings his sustenance with him from the sky. So when he eats, Allah forgives them due to his lodging among them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: Assistance descends upon a people according to their needs, and indeed the guest lodges with a people so his sustenance descends with him in his lap.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no guest who camps with a people except that his sustenance is in his lap.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Our companions mentioned a people, so I said, 'By Allah, I do not have lunch or dinner except that two or three, or fewer or more, of them are with me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their grace upon you is greater than your grace upon them.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, how is that, while I feed them my food, and spend from my wealth upon them, and my servant serves them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When they come to you, they come with abundant sustenance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and when they leave, they leave with forgiveness for you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Is'haq ibn Abd al-Aziz and Jamil and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught Fatima (peace be upon her) is that he said to her: 'O Fatima! The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Zurāra, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), who said: From what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught ʿAlī (peace be upon him), he said: 'Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the rights of the guest is that he should be honoured, and that the toothpick be prepared for him'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both) who said: When you enter a thicket and find eggs, do not eat from them except what differs in its two ends (i.e., oblong-shaped eggs).
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), '(What about) the eggs in the thickets?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever has equal ends — do not eat it; and whatever has different ends — eat it.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynan, from Zurara, from Abu al-Khattab who said: I asked him — meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — about a man who enters the thicket and finds different eggs therein; he does not know what [bird's] eggs they are — whether eggs of birds that are disliked [to eat] or recommended. So he [the Imam] said: Therein is a sign that is not hidden. Look at every egg: if you can distinguish its top from its bottom, then eat it; and whatever is equal [i.e. rounded, with both ends the same] in that regard, then leave it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eat from the eggs that which is not equal in its two ends.' And he said: 'Whatever is from the eggs of water birds, similar to the egg of the chicken, and in accordance with its natural shape one of its two ends is wider — (eat it); otherwise, do not eat.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I happen to be in the thickets, and various eggs come before me — what can I eat from them? So he (peace be upon him) said: Eat from them those whose two ends differ (i.e., the oblong ones).

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ary, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat with the people, he was the first to place his hand with them and the last to raise it, until the people had eaten.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate food with a group of people, he was the first to place his hand and the last to raise it, so that the people could eat.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the visitor visits the host and eats with him, he should cast off modesty from himself; and when he eats with him, he should take a little.'

From him, from Suleyman ibn Hafs, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) whenever the guest came to him, would eat with him, and would not raise his hand from the table-spread until the guest raised his hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Abrash al-Kalbi asked him about the Words of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: 'The Day when the earth shall be Changed into a different earth'. He said: 'It would be turned into pure bread. The people would eat from it until they are free from the Reckoning'. Al-Abrash said, 'I said, 'The people on that Day would be too pre-occupied from the eating'. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'They would be in the Fire, not being too pre-occupied from eating the thorny bushes and drinking the scalding water, and they would be in the Punishment, so how would they be too pre-occupied from it during the Reckoning?'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the son of Adam as hollow.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The body is built upon bread.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The Day when the earth shall be changed into a different earth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It shall be changed into a pure bread. The people will eat from it until they are finished with the Reckoning.' So a speaker said to him: 'They are in an occupation on that Day from eating and drinking.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the son of Adam hollow, and there is no escape for him from food and drink. Are they more occupied on that Day, or those in the Fire?' So they cry for help, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: 'And if they cry for help, they shall be given water like molten brass which will scald their faces; evil is the drink.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a narrative about Musa (peace be upon him): 'My Lord! Surely I stand in need of whatever good You may Send down upon me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He asked for the food.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, raising it (to the Prophet), said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah! Bless us in the bread, and do not Cause separation between us and it, for had there not been for the bread, neither would we have (been able to) Fast, nor Pray, nor fulfill the Obligations of our Lord, Mighty and Majestic'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The body is built upon bread.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Yaqoub ibn Salim, from Al-Muthanna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Yaqoub (peace be upon him) had a caller who would call out every morning from his house for a distance of a farsakh: 'Indeed, whoever desires the morning meal, let him come to the house of Yaqoub.' And when it was evening, he would call out: 'Indeed, whoever desires the evening meal, let him come to the house of Yaqoub.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ali ibn Al-Salt, from the cousin of Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the pains and indigestion I was experiencing. So he said to me: 'Have lunch and have dinner, and do not eat anything between them, for therein is the spoiling of the body.' Have you not heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying to them: 'Their sustenance therein is morning and evening'?

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The dinner of the Prophets (peace be upon them) is after 'atamah (late night/dusk), so do not neglect it, for neglecting the dinner is the ruin of the body.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The origin of the ruination of the body is the neglect of the dinner.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Neglecting the evening meal is a sin, and it is befitting for a man when he becomes aged that he does not sleep unless his stomach is filled with food.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Saeed ibn Janah, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said: When the man reaches middle age, he should not leave eating something at night, for it is a gift for sleep and more aromatic for the breath.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) did not leave the evening meal, even if it were just a cake, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is strength for the body.' And he said, and I do not know except that he said: 'And it is beneficial for intercourse.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no good for the one who enters old age to sleep lightly, but rather to sleep filled is better for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, who said: I had dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'The dinner after the last Isha prayer is the dinner of the Prophets (peace be upon them).'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Abu Suleiman, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Jabali, from his father, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who neglects the dinner on the night of Saturday and the night of Sunday consecutively, his strength would go away from him, so it would not return to him for forty days'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Zareeh, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The old man should not neglect the dinner, even though it may be a morsel.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali al-Lahabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'What do your physicians say regarding the evening meal?' I said, 'They forbid us from it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But I command you to have it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from a man he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The meal of the night is more beneficial than the meal of the day.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of the people of Ahvaz, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: 'There is a vein in the body called Al-Asha (Dinner). So if a man neglects the dinner, that vein does not cease supplicating against him until morning, saying: "May Allah keep you hungry as you kept me hungry, and may Allah keep you thirsty as you kept me thirsty." Therefore, let not one of you neglect the dinner, even if it is a morsel of bread or a drink of water.'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever washes his hands before the meal and after it, he will live in ease and be cured of affliction in his body.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'O Abu Hamza! The ablution before the meal and after it both remove poverty.' I said, 'May my father and my mother be sacrificed for you! They both remove poverty?' So he said: 'Yes, they both remove it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Washing the two hands before eating and after it increases longevity, removes stains from clothing, and clarifies the vision.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One who is pleased that goodness should increase in his house, let him perform ablution (wudu) at the time his food is presented.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Awf al-Bajali, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The ablution before the meal and after it both increase in the livelihood.' And it is reported that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Its first (ablution before the meal) negates poverty, and its end (ablution after the meal) negates worries.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The ablution before the meal: the owner of the house begins, so that one person is not embarrassed. So when they finish from the meal, he begins with the one on his right, whether he be a freeman or a slave. He said, 'And in another Hadith: First the lord of the house washes his hand, then he begins with the one on his right. And when the meal is raised, he begins with the one on the left of the owner of the house, and the last one to wash his hand will be the owner of the house, because he is more deserving of patience with the stains.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Wash your hands in one vessel, so that your manners may be improved.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Fadl ibn al-Mubarak from al-Fadl ibn Yunus who said: When Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had lunch with me, and the washing tray was brought, he (peace be upon him) was given precedence, and he was in the center of the gathering, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the one on your right.' So when one had performed ablution, the slave intended to raise the tray, so Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Leave it, and wash your hands in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the meal is placed, four thousand angels surround it. So when the servant says, “In the Name of Allah,” the angels say, “May Allah bless you in your meal.” Then they say to the Satan, “Exit, O mischievous one! You have no authority over them.”' And when they finish and say, “All praise is for Allah,” the angels say, “A people upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, so they have fulfilled the gratitude of their Lord.”' And if they do not say the Name (of Allah), the angels say to the Satan, “Approach, O mischievous one, so eat with them.”' So when the meal is raised and they do not mention the Name of Allah upon it, the angels say, “A people upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, so they forgot their Lord, the Majestic and Mighty.”'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the meal is placed, say 'Bismillah' (In the Name of Allah), and when you eat, say 'Bismillah' at its beginning and its end, and when it is raised, say 'Al-Hamdulillah' (The Praise is for Allah).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the lunch and the dinner are placed, say 'Bismillah' (In the Name of Allah), for the Satan, may Allah curse him, says to his companions, 'Come out, for there is no dinner here and no overnight stay.' And when he forgets to say 'Bismillah', he says to his companions, 'Come, for there is dinner for you here and an overnight stay.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever eats food, let him mention the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over it. So if he forgets and remembers Allah afterwards, the Satan (may Allah curse him) vomits what he had eaten with him, and the man finds the food to be little.'
And by this chain, he said: He said: The one who mentions Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon the meal would not be questioned about that Bounty, ever.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Kulaib al-Asadi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when a Muslim man intends to eat food and extends his hand, saying 'Bismillah' and 'Al-hamdu lillah Rabb al-'alamin', Allah (Mighty and Majestic) forgives him before the morsel reaches his mouth.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, raising it, said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever the meal was placed in front of him, said: 'Glory be to You, O Allah! How Goodly You are Testing us. Glory be to You! How frequently You are Feeding us. Glory be to You! How frequently You are Excusing us. O Allah! Expand upon us and upon the poor Believing men and the believing women, and the Muslim men and the Muslim women'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the meal is presented, and a man from them has named (Bismillah), it suffices for them altogether.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate at the home of a family, he would say to them: 'The fasting ones have eaten with you, and the righteous have eaten with you, and the chosen angels have sent blessings upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you eat food, say 'Bismillah' at its beginning and its end. For if the servant mentions the Name before eating, Satan does not eat with him; and if he does not mention the Name, Satan eats with him. So when he mentions the Name after having eaten, and Satan had eaten with him, Satan vomits what he had eaten.

And from him, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman Al-Azramy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever mentions the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at the beginning of food or drink, and praises Allah at its end, will not be questioned about the blessing of that food ever.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the meal was raised, would say: 'O Allah, You have increased [the provision], made it pleasant, and blessed it, so You have satiated us and quenched us. The praise is for Allah who feeds and is not fed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Praise is to Allah, Who satisfied us among the hungry, and quenched us among the thirsty, and sheltered us among the homeless, and carried us among the walkers, and secured us among the fearful, and provided service for us among the toil-stricken.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I ate a meal with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I could not count how many times he said: 'The Praise is to Allah, Who made me desire it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I guarantee that the one who names (Bismillah) over his food will not complain from it.' So Ibn al-Kawwa said to him: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I ate a meal yesterday, I named over it, and it harmed me.' He said: 'Perhaps you ate various types, so you named over some of it and did not name over some, O dimwit!'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from Abu Talib, from Misma'a, who said: I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the harm I experienced from the food when I ate it. He said: 'Did you not say Bismillah?' I said: 'I do say it, and it still harms me.' He said to me: 'When you interrupt the saying of Bismillah by talking, then you return to the food, do you say Bismillah?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So from here it harms you. If you had said Bismillah when you returned to the food, it would not have harmed you.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I say Bismillah upon the food?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the vessels are different, say Bismillah upon each vessel.' I said, 'And if I forget to say Bismillah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say, Bismillah upon its first and its last.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ibn Bukayr, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He fed us, then we raised our hands and said, 'The praise is for Allah.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, this is from You and from Muhammad, Your Messenger. O Allah, to You is the praise. Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, over the food, and do not be heedless/noisy, for it is a bounty from the bounties of Allah and a sustenance from His sustenance. It is obligatory upon you regarding it to thank Him, remember Him, and praise Him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ismail al-Madainy, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from a man who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered meat, and it became cold. Then it was brought to him later, so he said: 'Praise is to Allah, the One who made me desire it.' Then he said: 'The blessing in health is superior to the blessing upon ability (to acquire/eat).'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no man who gathers his family and places a meal before him, and he says the name of Allah (Bismillah) and they say the name of Allah at the beginning of the food, and they praise Allah (Al-Hamdulillah) at its end, so the meal is raised while they are forgiven.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat from the top of the tharid (bread and meat stew), and eat from its sides, for the blessing is in its top.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever one of you eats, let him eat from what is next to him.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashshab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to lick the plate and say: 'Whoever licks a plate, it is as if he has given in charity with its like.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) used to brush his teeth sideways and eat in a Herta manner. And he said: 'Al-Herta is that he ate with all of his fingers together'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he used to sit the sitting of a slave, and place his hand on the ground, and eat with three fingers, and that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat like this, not as the tyrants do, one of them eating with his two fingers.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever one of you eats food, let him lick the fingers with which he ate.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Allah will bless you in it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Yasir al-Khadim, who said: The boys ate a fruit one day and did not scrutinize it, and threw it away. So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to them: 'Glory be to Allah! If you are needless, so there are people who are not needless. Feed the ones who are needy to it'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Prayer when it is time and the food has been placed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is at the beginning of the time, begin with the food; and if some of the time has passed, and you fear that it will be lost so you would have to repeat the Prayer, then begin with the Prayer.'

From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Yassir al-Khadim and Nadir, all together said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to us: 'If I am standing over your heads while you are eating, do not get up until you have finished. And sometimes he would call one of us, and it would be said to him,
And it is reported from Nadir the servant who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), whenever one of us was eating, would not get him to attend to something until he was free from his meal.
And Nadir the servant narrated, saying: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) would place one jawzinja (a sweet) upon the other, and hand it to me.

Ahmad, from his father, from Suleyman Al-Ja'fari, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Sometimes when the meal is brought, one of the people intends to wash his hand, so he (peace be upon him) would say: 'The one whose hand is clean, there is no harm in him eating without washing his hand.'

Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Bazie ibn Umar ibn Bazie, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while he was eating vinegar and oil in a black bowl, with the inscription 'Say, He is Allah, One' written in gold in its center. He said to me: 'Approach, O Bazie.' So I approached and ate with him. Then he sipped water three sips when nothing of the bread remained, then he handed it to me, so I sipped the remainder.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who eats food in his house, so something falls from it, let him take it; and the one who eats in the desert or outside, let him leave it for the birds or the wild animals.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: Ismail held a banquet, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You should invite the poor, so feed them until they are satisfied.' For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And what falsehood starts, it will not return.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, raising it from them (peace be upon him) They said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he ate, would feed the one in front of his eyes, and whenever he drank, he would give drink to the one on his right.
