A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not leave the food-stained towel in the house, for it is a play-pen for the devils'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Entertain your families every Friday with something of fruit or meat, so that they may rejoice because of Friday.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever builds a dwelling, let him slaughter a fat ram and feed its meat to the poor. Then he should say: O Allah, avert from me the castaways of the Jinn, humans, and devils, and bless us in our homes, and he will be given what he asked for.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: When you have eaten something, lie down on your back and place your right leg upon the left.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat what falls from the food-spread, for it is a healing from every illness by the Permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the one who wants to be healed by it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Dawud ibn Kathir, who said: I had dinner in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) late into the evening. So when he was free from his dinner, he praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and said: 'This is my dinner, and a dinner of my forefathers.' So when the meal was raised, he proceeded to eat what had fallen from it, then cast it into his mouth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abd Allah ibn Salih al-Khash'ami, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about pain in the loins. He said: 'Adopt what falls from the food-spread and eat it.' I said: 'So I did that, and it went away from me.' Ibrahim said: 'I had found that in the right side and the left, so I took that (eating the fallen crumbs), and I benefited by it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Muawiya ibn Wahb, from his father, who said: We ate in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So when the meal was raised, he picked up what had fallen from it and ate it. Then he said to us: 'It negates poverty and increases children.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashshab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Amr ibn Jumi'ah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever finds a piece of bread and eats it, it will be a good deed for him; and whoever finds it in dirt, washes it, then picks it up, it will be seventy good deeds for him.'

And by this chain, from Amr ibn Jumi', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) visited Aisha, and he saw a crumb of bread which he almost trod upon, so he took it and ate it. Then he said: 'O Humayra! Honour the neighbourliness of the Bounties of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon you, for it does not flee from a people, so it almost does not return to them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzan, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: A man complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the pain he was experiencing in his loins. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is preventing you from eating what falls from the food-spread?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever eats food in his house and something falls from it, let him pick it up; and whoever eats in the desert or outdoors, let him leave it for the birds and the wild animals.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Al-Asamm, from Abdullah Al-Arjani, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was eating, and I saw him picking up sesame-seed-sized pieces of food that had fallen from the food-spread. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you are picking up this?' He said, 'O Abdullah, this is your sustenance, so do not leave it. Indeed, in it is a healing from every illness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sudeyr who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked — and I was present with him — about a kid (baby goat) that was breastfed by a female pig until it grew big, matured, and its bones became strong. Then a man used it as a stud among his flock, so offspring were produced from it. So he (peace be upon him) said: As for what you recognize from its offspring specifically, do not go near it. As for what you do not recognize, then eat it — for it is at the status of cheese, and do not ask about it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Nahiki, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Bishr ibn Maslama, from Abu al-Hasan al-Reza (peace be upon him), regarding a kid (baby goat) that had been breast-fed from a female pig (sow) and was then let loose among the flock. He said: 'It is at the status of cheese. So whatever you recognize as having been mated by it, do not eat it; and whatever you do not recognize, eat it.'
Do not eat from the meat of a baby lamb that suckles from the milk of a female pig.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: I wrote to him (peace be upon him): May I be made your sacrifice from every evil! A woman breastfed a baby female goat until she was weaned, and she grew up, and the stallion mounted her, then she gave birth. Is it permissible to eat its flesh and its milk? So he wrote (peace be upon him): It is an abhorrent deed, and there is no problem with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about a baby lamb that had been nourished with the milk of a female pig. So he said: 'Confine it and feed it oilseed cake, date kernels, barley, and bread, if it has become independent of the milk. But if it has not become independent of the milk, then place it on the udder of a sheep for seven days; then its flesh may be eaten.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr ibn Shimir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I lick my fingers from the sauce until I fear that my servant will see me, and he will think that this is from greed, and that is not so.' Indeed, a people upon whom blessings were poured, and they are the people of Tharthar, so they took the core of the wheat and made it bread for firewood, and they used it to clean their children with, until a great mountain gathered from that. He said: So a righteous man passed by them, and there was a woman, and she was doing that with a child of hers. So he said to them, 'Woe to you! Fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not change what is with you from the blessings.' So she said to him, 'It is as if you are frightening us with hunger. But as long as our Tharthar is flowing, we do not fear hunger.' He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made them regret, and He weakened the Tharthar for them, and withheld from them the drops of the sky and the vegetation of the earth. He said: So they became in need of that mountain, and it was distributed among them by the scale.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Honor the bread, for it has been worked upon by much of the creation between the Throne and the earth and what is in it.' Then he said to those around him: 'Shall I inform you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, may the fathers and mothers be sacrificed for you.' So he said: 'There was a Prophet among those who were before you, called Daniel, and he gave a loaf of bread to the owner of a crossing so that he might cross with it.' So the owner of the crossing threw down the bread and said: 'What do I do with this bread? The bread is with us, it is trampled by feet.' So when Daniel saw that from him, he raised his hand to the sky and said: 'O Allah, honor the bread, for You have seen, O Lord, what this servant did and what he said.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the sky to withhold the rain, and revealed to the earth to become layers like pottery. So they did not rain until their affairs reached such that some of them ate each other. So when what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended from that reached them, a woman said to another, and for both of them were two children: 'O So-and-so, come, let I and you eat my child today, and when it is tomorrow, we will eat your child.' She said to her, 'Yes.' So they ate him. So when they became hungry afterwards, the other enticed her to eat her child, but she refused her. So she said to her: 'Between me and you is the Prophet of Allah.' So they brought their dispute to Daniel (peace be upon him). So he said to them both, 'And has the matter reached to what I see?' They said to him, 'Yes, O Prophet of Allah, and even more difficult.' So he raised his hand to the sky and said: 'O Allah, return upon us with Your Grace, and the Grace of Your Mercy, and do not punish the children and those in it who are good, by the sin of the owner of the crossing and his trampling of Your Bounty.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the sky: 'Rain upon the earth,' and commanded the earth: 'Grow for My creation what they have missed of your goodness, for I have shown mercy to them through the young child.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from al-Mithammi, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not place the bread beneath the bowl.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Sayyari from Ali ibn Asbat from one of his companions who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Honor the bread.' It was said, 'And what is its honoring?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is placed, do not wait with it for something else.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talha ibn Zayd, from one of our companions, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Honor the bread.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is its honoring?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When it is placed, do not wait with it for something else.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'And from its honoring is that it should not be trodden upon nor cut (into pieces before it is placed).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beware of smelling the bread as the wild beasts smell it, for the bread is blessed. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the sky for it with torrential rain, and for it Allah caused the pasture to grow, and by it you pray, and by it you fast, and by it you perform Hajj to the House of your Lord.'

And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When you are brought the bread and the meat, so begin with the bread, so close by it the emptiness of the hunger, then eat the meat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Make your bread small, for with each loaf is a blessing.' And Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen said: 'I saw Abu Al-Hasan, meaning Al-Reza (peace be upon him), breaking the bread upwards.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, raised it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when he did not have a sauce (udm) for him, would cut the bread with the knife.
Al-Sayyari raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) He said: 'The lowest of the sauces is to cut the bread with the knife.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfaly, from al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had lunch with me, so a bowl was brought with bread underneath it. He said: 'Honor the bread, so that it should not be under the bowl.' And he said to me: 'Instruct the servant to take the loaf out from beneath the bowl.'
Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mithamī, from Abū Baseer, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) that he disliked that the bread be placed under the bowl.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Jamhour, from Idrees ibn Yusuf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not cut the bread with the knife, but break it with the hand, and let your breaking be opposite to that of the non-Arabs'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Do not cut the bread with the knife, but break it by hand, and oppose the non-Arabs.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said: Nothing enters the belly of the consumptive (sufferer of tuberculosis) that is more beneficial for him than rice bread.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Al-Khashaab, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of our companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Feed the one suffering from stomach ailments rice bread, for nothing that enters the stomach of the one suffering from stomach ailments is more beneficial than it; indeed, it tans (strengthens) the stomach and pulls out the illness with a pull.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Yahya ibn Abi Rafi'a and others, they raise it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Nothing remains in the stomach from the early morning until the night except rice bread.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hammam, from Suleiman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The best sustenance is al-sawiq; if you are hungry, it stays (in the stomach), and if you are satiated, it digests your food.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from one of his companions, who said: As-Sawiq was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, it was prepared by the Revelation.'
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Sawiq builds the flesh and strengthens the bones.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abi Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Sawiq is the food of the sent messengers, or he said: the prophets.

From him, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Sayaba, from Jundab ibn Abdullah, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'Al-Sawiq was revealed by the Revelation from the sky.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The dry suweeq (flour soup) removes the whiteness (vitiligo).

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Drinking as-sawiq with oil builds the flesh, strengthens the bone, softens the skin, and increases in sexual desire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three handfuls of dry Suweyq (flour soup) on an empty stomach dries the phlegm and the bile until it almost leaves nothing.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Nadr ibn Qirwash, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him) said: 'As-Sawiq, when you wash it seven times and transfer it from one vessel to another, it removes fever and brings strength to the two legs and the two feet.'
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Sawiq digests the heads (crusts of the stomach).

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Yahya ibn Musawir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Suweiq (a type of flour soup) strips the bile and phlegm from the stomach with a stripping, and repels seventy types from the types of afflictions.

From him, from his father, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Khaythama, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever drinks as-sawiq for forty mornings, his shoulders will be filled with strength.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Sayyari, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) wrote from Khurasan to Medina: 'Do not give Abu Ja'far the second Suweeq with sugar, for it is a destruction for the men.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sayf al-Tammar, who said: One of our companions fell ill in Mecca and became delirious/hallucinated, so I visited Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said to me: 'Give him to drink the suweeq of barley, for it cures, God willing, and it is nourishment in the stomach of the sick.' He said: 'We did not give him the suweeq except for two days' (or he said 'twice') until our companion was healed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The suweeq (porridge) of lentils quenches thirst, strengthens the stomach, and in it is a cure for seventy diseases, it extinguishes the yellowness (bile), and cools the interior. And whenever he (peace be upon him) traveled, it did not leave him, and he (peace be upon him) would say: 'When the blood of one of his household becomes agitated, he would say to him: Drink from the suweeq of lentils, for it settles the agitation of the blood and extinguishes the heat.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: A slave girl of ours was afflicted with menstruation, and it did not cease from her until she was near death. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) ordered that she be given Suweeq of lentils to drink. She was given it, so it ceased from her, and she recovered.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ibrahim ibn Bustam, from a man from the people of Marv, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent to us while he was with us seeking Al-Suweyq, so we sent him a mixture of Suweyq. He returned it and sent a message to me that Al-Suweyq, when drunk on an empty stomach and it is dry, extinguishes the heat and settles the bile; and when it is mixed, it does not do that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the chief of the sauces (cooked food) in the world and the Hereafter, so he (peace be upon him) said: The meat. Have you not heard the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the flesh of fowl such as they would be desiring'.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Meat is the chief of foods in the world and the Hereafter.'

And from him, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, he raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The chief of the sauces of the Paradise is the meat (sauce)'.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The chief of the foods is the meat.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abdul-A'la, the mawla of the family of Sam, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We are reported in our presence from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates the 'House of Meat'.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying! Rather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The house in which people backbite one another and eat their brothers' flesh.' And my father (peace be upon him) was 'meat'-loving, and he passed away; and on the day he passed away, in the sleeve of the mother of his child, there were thirty dirhams for the meat.

And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a man said to him: 'The ones facing us are reporting that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Hates the house of meat.' So he said: 'They speak the truth, and it is not where you are going (with it). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Hates the house in which the meats of the people are eaten.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was a meat-lover; he loved meat.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from al-Hasan ibn Harun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) left thirty dirhams for meat on the day he passed away, and he was a man who loved meat.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'We, the group of Qureysh, are a meat-loving people'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Meat builds meat, and whoever leaves meat for forty days, his character will worsen, and whoever has a worsened character, give the Adhan in his ear.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) 'The people are saying that the one who does not eat meat for three days, his character/mannerisms would worsen.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying. But the one who does not eat meat for forty days, his character/mannerisms and his body will change, and that is due to the transference of the seed in the span of forty days.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Baqqah, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Abu Asama Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever has forty days pass by him and he does not eat meat, then let him borrow upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and let him eat it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions (I think it was Muhammad ibn Ismail), who said: One of us mentioned meat in the presence of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), so he said: 'What meat is more delicious than the meat of the goat?' He said, 'So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) looked at him and said: 'Had Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a morsel that is more delicious than the lamb, it would have been sacrificed for Ismail (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'My family do not eat the meat of the sheep.' He said, 'And why?' I said, 'They say that it stirs up the black bile, headache, and pains in them.' He said to me, 'O Sa'd!' I said, 'At your service.' He said, 'If Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had known of a thing more prestigious than the sheep, He would have sacrificed it for Ismail (peace be upon him).'

One of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadrami, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'My family eats the meat of the goat and does not eat the meat of the lamb.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why?' I said: 'They say that it is meat which stirs the bitterness (acidity).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Had Allah, Mighty and Majestic, known of anything better than the lamb, He would have sacrificed with it,' meaning Isaac. This is how it has come in the hadith.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Suleiman ibn Abbad, from Isa ibn Abu al-Ward, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Children of Israel complained to Musa (peace be upon him) about the whiteness (vitiligo) they were suffering from, so he took that complaint to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Order them to eat the meat of the cow with the beet (or leek/green vegetable).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak (I think), from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The broth of the meat of the cow does away with the whiteness (vitiligo).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The milk of the cow is a medicine, and its butter is a healing, and its meat is an ailment.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Meat builds meat, and whoever puts a morsel of fat into his stomach, it expels a like amount of disease.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Muhammad ibn Sowqat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever eats a morsel of fat, it expels the like of it from the ailments.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of his companions, having delivered with it by Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! The fat which throws out the likes of it from the ailments, which fat is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the fat of the cow, and O Zurara, no one has asked me about it before you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Yahya ibn Masour, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Suweeq (barley flour porridge) and the broth of beef meat remove the vitiligo (white patches on the skin).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the meats of the bukh (strutting/racing) camels and their milks, so he said: There is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man from the companions of Abu al-Khattab forbade eating al-Bukht and eating the meat of al-Masruwalah pigeons.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with riding al-Bukht, drinking their milk, and eating the meat of al-Masruwalah pigeons.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not eat the meats of the jallalat — and these are the animals that eat human excrement — and if any of their sweat touches you, then wash it off.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Do not drink from the milk of the dung-eating camel, and if something from its sweat touches you, then wash it.

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The dung-eating chicken — its meat is not to be eaten until it is confined for three days; and the dung-eating duck (for) five days; and the dung-eating sheep (for) ten days; and the dung-eating cow (for) twenty days; and the she-camel (for) forty days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a sheep that drank wine until it became intoxicated, then was slaughtered in that state. He said: 'Do not eat what is in her belly.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukayl, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a sheep which drank urine, then was slaughtered. He said: So he said: 'What is inside it shall be washed, then there is no problem with it; and similarly when it ate human excrement, as long as it had not become a dung-eater (jalala) — and the dung-eater (jalala) is one whose (regular) feed is that (filth).'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The dung-eating camels — when you intend to slaughter them, confine the camel for forty days, and the cow for thirty days, and the sheep for ten days.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Khashab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who reported concerning the dung-eaters. He said: There is no problem with eating them when they are mixed (with normal feed).

I asked him about eating the meat of chicken in the villages, where they do not prevent them from anything — they pass over human excrement and are left free upon it — and about eating their eggs. So he said: There is no problem with it.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Al-Fadl, from Yunus, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him) regarding the dung-eating fish — he had asked him about it, so he said: 'It is to be kept for one day and one night'. And Al-Sayyari said: 'This does not happen except at Basra'. And he said regarding the chicken: 'It is to be confined for three days; and the duck for seven days; and the sheep for fourteen days; and the cow for thirty days; and the camel for forty days — then they are slaughtered'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ismail. He said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the egg of the crow, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat it'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Bassam al-Sayrāfī from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the dung-eating camel, he said: 'Its meat is not to be eaten, nor is it to be ridden for forty days.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The dung-eating she-camel: do not eat its meat, nor drink its milk, until it is fed for forty days; and the dung-eating cow: do not eat its meat, nor drink its milk, until it is fed for thirty days; and the dung-eating sheep: do not eat its meat, nor drink its milk, until it is fed for ten days; and the dung-eating duck: do not eat its meat until it is restrained for five days; and the chicken for three days.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, raising it, said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The goose is the buffalo of the birds, and the chicken is the pig of the birds, and the pheasant is the Abyssinian (turkey) of the birds. And where are you from the two rising chicks, which a woman from Rabi'ah raised by the surplus of her food?'

From him, from al-Sayyari, raising it (to the Imam), said: Meats were mentioned in front of Umar, so Umar said, 'The best of the meats is the meat of the chicken.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said, 'No! Those are the pigs of the birds, and the best of the meats is the meat of a chick that has risen (stood up) or is near to rising.'

Al-Sayyari, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is keen to reduce his anger, so let him eat the meat of the pheasant'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, who said: 'It narrated to me Ali ibn Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:' Feed the feverish the meat of Al-Qibaj (a type of pheasant), for it strengthens the two legs and repulses the fever with a repelling.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I had lunch with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he brought a sand grouse and said: 'It is blessed.' My father (peace be upon him) was fond of it, and he used to instruct that the sufferer of jaundice be fed with it, grilled for him, for it benefits him.

From him, from Ali ibn Sulayman, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Nashit ibn Salih, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'I do not see any harm in eating the bustard, and it is good for hemorrhoids and back pain, and it is among what aids in frequent intercourse.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, both together, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: There is no problem with eating the meat of buffaloes, drinking their milk, and eating their butter.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the meat of buffaloes and their milk, so he said: There is no problem with them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdul-Sammad ibn Bashir, from Atiyya, the brother of Abu Al-Maghra', who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The companions of Al-Mughira are forbidding the eating of the Qadeed (dried meat) which fire has not touched.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with eating it.'

From him, raising it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), said: I said to him, 'The meat is dried, salt is sprinkled upon it, and it is dried in the shade.' So he said, 'There is no problem with eating it because the salt has changed it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Hasan the third (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I have not eaten a foodstuff which is more remaining nor more stirring for the illnesses than the dried meat, meaning the Jerk'.

From him, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he used to say: The Qadeed (dried meat) is evil meat because it relaxes in the stomach and agitates every illness, and it does not benefit anything, but it harms it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Two things are corrective; if either enters the stomach of a person who is spoilt (ill), it corrects it. And two things are spoilers; if either enters the stomach of a person who is sound (healthy), it spoils it. The two correctives are the pomegranate and lukewarm water, and the two spoilers are cheese and dried meat (jerk).'

He said, and it has been reported from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Three (things) demolish the body, and perhaps may even kill – Eating the Jerk of the forest, and entering the bathroom upon the (full) belly, and marrying the old women. He said, and Abu Is’haq Al-Nahawandy has increased in it: ‘And copulating with the women upon the filled (belly)’.

From him, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three things are not eaten and they fatten, and three are eaten and they slim (the body), and two benefit from every thing and do not harm from anything, and two harm from every thing and do not benefit from anything.' So as for those which are not eaten and fatten: wearing linen, perfume, and Noura (lime-wax); and as for those which are eaten and slim: dried meat, cheese, and spadix; and in another Hadith: the prairie herb and oil-cake; and the two which benefit from everything and do not harm: lukewarm water and pomegranate; and the two which harm from everything and do not benefit: dried meat and cheese. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you said here they slim, and you said here they harm.' So he said, 'Do you not know that slimming is from the harm?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, raising it (to the Imam), said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Why did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) love the arm more than his love for the rest of the sheep's body parts?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Because Adam (peace be upon him) offered a sacrifice on behalf of the Prophets from his offspring, so he named a part for each Prophet from his offspring, and named the arm for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Therefore, he (peace be upon him) used to love it, desire it, and prefer it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) liked the arm (of the sheep).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Jewish woman poisoned the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in an arm, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to love the arm and the shoulder, and he disliked the hip due to its proximity to the urinating part.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Meat with milk is the gravy (or stew) of the Prophets (peace be upon them).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When a Muslim is weak, let him eat meat with milk.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallal, who said: I had dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) consisting of meat with milk, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is the gravy of the Prophets (peace be upon him)'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A Prophet from the Prophets complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about weakness, so it was said to him: 'Cook the meat with the milk, for these two strengthen the body.' He said: 'Is it Al-Muzeyra?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the meat with the milk of the udder (fresh milk/yoghurt milk).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: The most beloved of the food to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was Al-Narbaja.

Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaqub said: I sent a basket to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) containing Narbaj, so he ate from it and said: 'Withhold the remainder of it for me.' It was brought to him twice or three times. Then the slave poured water into it and brought it to him, so he said to him: 'Woe be unto you! You have spoiled it for me.'
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) liked Al-Zabibiyya.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Varieties (of food) enlarge the belly and numb the buttocks.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Suleyman ibn Rushayd, from his father, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I ate in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a variety of food was brought to him. He said: 'Eat from this.' As for me, there is nothing more beloved to me than al-tharid, and I wish that al-isfanajat had been forbidden.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The first one to variegate [goods] was Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and the first one to soften Al-Tharid was Hashim.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah, bless my community in the thard and the thareed.' Ja'far said: 'The thard is what is small, and the thareed is what is big.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Tharid is the food of the Arabs.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Salama ibn Muhraz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Adhere to Al-Thareed, for I did not find anything more suitable than it.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ismail ibn Jabir, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he called for the meal, and they brought him thareed and meat. He called for oil and poured it over the meat, so I ate with him.
And Zurarah reported it from one of his companions, raising it (to the Prophet), he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Al-Thareed is blessed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat from the top of the tharid, and eat from its sides, for the blessing is in its top.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umayya ibn Amr, from Al-Sha'iri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Extinguish the fires of grudges with meat and thareed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ja'far ibn Basheer, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Abu Maryam, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: I entered upon the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and in front of him was grilled meat. He said to me, 'Approach and eat.' I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, this is harmful to me.' He said to me, 'Approach. I will teach you some words with which nothing from what you fear will harm you. Say: In the Name of Allah, the Best of Names, filling the earth and the sky, the Beneficent, the Merciful, He with Whose Name nothing harms and no illness [comes]. Have lunch with us.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), meaning the first (Imam Al-Rida), said to me: 'Why do I see you as pale?' So I said to him, 'A chill has struck me.' So he said to me, 'Eat the meat.' So I ate it. Then he saw me after Friday, and I was still in my pale state, so he said to me, 'Did I not order you to eat the meat?' I said, 'I have not eaten anything else since you ordered me.' So he said, 'And how do you eat it?' I said, 'As a stew (thick soup).' So he said, 'No, eat it as Kabab (roast).' So I ate it. Then he sent for me and called me over after Friday, and behold, the blood had returned to my face. So he said to me, 'Now, yes!'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Shami, from Husayn ibn Hanzala, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Eating kabab removes the fever.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Durust, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: We mentioned the heads of the sheep, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The head is the place of slaughter, and it is nearest to the pasture and furthest from harm.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a Prophet from the Prophets complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about weakness and infrequent intercourse, so He commanded him to eat al-Hareesah.

And in another Hadith, raising it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) complained to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, about back pain, so He commanded him to eat grain with meat, meaning Al-Hareys.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mansur al-Sayqal, from his father, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) a dish of hareesah from the hareesah of Paradise, which was planted in the gardens of Paradise, and the Houries churned it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate it, and it increased his strength by that of forty men. And that was something Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended to make His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) joyful with.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: Seven things are forbidden from the sheep — the blood, the two testicles, the penis, the bladder, the glands, the spleen, and the gallbladder.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, raising it (marfu'), said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed by the butchers and forbade them from selling seven things from the sheep. He forbade them from selling blood, glands, the two ventricles of the heart, the spleen, the spinal marrow, the testicles, and the penis. One of the butchers said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, is the liver and the spleen not the same?' He said to him: 'You lie, O dimwit! Bring me two containers of water; I shall inform you of the difference between the two.' So they brought a liver, a spleen, and two containers of water. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Cut the spleen from its middle, and cut the liver from its middle.' Then he (peace be upon him) ordered that both be immersed in the water together. The liver whitened and nothing was lost from it, but the spleen did not whiten — all that was inside it came out and became blood entirely, until only the skin of the spleen and its veins remained. He then said: 'This is the difference between the two: this (liver) is flesh, and this (spleen) is blood.'

Do not eat ten things from the sheep: the excrement (stomach contents), the blood, the spleen, the spinal cord, the neck sinew/thyroid glands, the glands (lymph nodes), the penis, the two testicles, the vulva, and the gallbladder.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from them (peace be upon them), who said: Do not eat from what is found in the camel, the cow, the sheep, and other animals whose meat is permissible — the genitals with what is in them, their exterior and interior, and the penis, and the two testicles, and the placenta (which is the place of the birth), and the spleen because it is blood, and the glands along with the veins, and the brain/marrow, and that which is found in the loins, and the gallbladder, and the eyeballs, and the cord/nodule that is found in the brain, and the blood.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: When one of you buys meat, let him remove the glands from it, for indeed it stirs up the vein of leprosy.
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from some of our companions, that he disliked the two kidneys and said: 'But rather these two are the reservoir of the urine.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What do you feed your family in the winter?' I said, 'Meat. So when there is no meat, then oil and butter.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what prevents you from this Karkour, for it is a matter of something in the body, meaning the Musallatha (the trio).' He (the narrator) said, 'And one of our companions informed me that the Musallatha is taken as a Qafiz of rice, and a Qafiz of chickpeas, and a Qafiz of broad beans, or something else from the seeds, then all is ground and cooked.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Talbeena (a porridge made from barley flour) clears the sorrowful heart, just as the fingers clear sweat from the forehead.

And it is reported from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If anything could have sufficed you from death, it would have been Al-Talbeyn.' So it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is Al-Talbeyn?' He said: 'Al-Hasou with milk, Al-Hasou with milk,' and he repeated it three times.
And Sahl ibn Ziyad reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Harun ibn Mufaffaq al-Madaini, from his father, who said: The late one (peace be upon him) sent for me one day, so I ate in his presence, and there was much sweet dish (halwa). So I said, 'How abundant is this sweet dish!' He (peace be upon him) said: 'We and our Shias were created from sweetness, so we love the sweet dish.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who does not want the sweet dishes from us, wants the drinks.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said: I ate with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) one day, and a stuffed chicken, prepared as khabeeص (a type of sweet dough/confection), was brought to us. We broke it apart and ate it. Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said: I ate with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) – like the first report.

Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: We were in Medina, so he sent a message to us: 'Prepare for us Falouzaj, and make only a little.' So we sent it to him in a small bowl.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Allow the hot [food] to cool down, for hot food was brought near the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Allow it until it cools down. It was not for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to feed us the fire, and the blessing is in the cooled [food].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was brought very hot food, so he said: 'It was not fitting for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to feed us with fire. Let it cool down until it is manageable, for it is food devoid of blessing, and for Satan there is a share in it.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakeem, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The hot food is other than with Blessing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Hot food was brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not Feed us the fire. Set it aside until it cools.' So it was left until it cooled.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I attended the evening meal of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in the summer, and a platter was brought with bread, and a bowl of tharid (bread soaked in broth) and meat was brought. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Come to me with this food.' So I approached, and he placed his hand in it and raised it while saying: 'I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire, I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire, I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire. This is what we cannot be patient with, so how (will we be patient with) the Fire? This is what we do not have the strength to bear, so how (will we bear) the Fire? This is what we cannot endure, so how (will we endure) the Fire?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And he (peace be upon him) repeated that until the food was manageable, so he ate and we ate with him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Saeed ibn Janaah, from a slave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He called for dates and ate them, then said: 'I have no desire [for them], but I have eaten fish.' Then he said: 'Whoever sleeps and there is fish in his stomach, and he does not follow it up with dates or honey, the vein of leprosy will not cease to strike upon him until morning.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he ate fish, would say: 'O Allah, bless us in it and replace it for us with something better than it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani from Mu'ttab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or he said from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) He said: One day he said, 'O Mu'ttab! Seek out fresh fish for us, for I intend to get cupping done.' So I sought it out, then came to him with it, so he said to me, 'O Mu'ttab! Cook part of it in vinegar for us, and grill part of it for us.' So he had lunch from it, and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had dinner.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, and Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, all from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Hamadani, similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said: 'I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Adhere to eating fish, for if you eat it without bread, it will suffice you, and if you eat it with bread, it will fill you up.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ibn al-Yasa', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not make eating fish a habit, for it melts the body.'
Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Eating the fish melts the body.
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Hassan from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: The fresh fish melts the body.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, raising it (to the Imam), said: The fresh fish melts the fat of the eye.
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The fresh fish melts the fat of the two eyes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya said, One of our companions wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) complaining to him about blood and paleness, saying, 'When I get cupping done, the paleness increases, and when I delay the cupping, the blood harms me. So what is your view regarding that?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Get cupping done and eat upon the effects of the cupping, fresh grilled fish.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I re-iterated the same question to him, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Get cupping done and eat upon the effects of the cupping, fresh grilled fish with water and salt.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I acted upon that, so I was in good health and it became my regular intake.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Yunus, from Murazam who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioned the eggs, so he said: 'Indeed, it is light, it reduces the nibbling of the meat'. He said, and Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee' narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Murazam, that he added to it: 'And it does not have for it the suffering pain of the meat'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from Umar ibn Abu Hasana al-Jammal who said: I complained to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the scarcity of children, so he said to me: 'Seek forgiveness of Allah and eat eggs with onions.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A Prophet from the Prophets (peace be upon them) complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about the scarcity of offspring, so He said: 'Eat the meat with the eggs.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Frequent eating of eggs increases in offspring.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from his grandfather, and Qays ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The yolk of the egg is light, and the albumen is heavy.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The chicken is in the house and there is no rooster with her; she feeds on the sweepings and other things, and she lays an egg without the rooster mating with her. So what do you say about eating that egg?' He said to me: 'The egg, when it is from that whose flesh is eaten, there is no problem with it and with eating it, and it is permissible.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sheep and the cow, that sometimes they yield milk without the ram striking/mating with them, and the hen, that sometimes she lays eggs without the rooster mounting her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of this is permissible and pure for you. Everything whose meat is edible, all that comes from it—whether milk, or eggs, or rennet—is permissible and pure. And sometimes this occurs after the ram has mated with her, yet it is delayed; and all of this is permissible.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Begin your meal with salt and end with salt, for whoever begins his meal with salt and ends with it, Allah will repel from him seventy types of afflictions, the easiest of which is leprosy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Begin your meal with salt and end with salt, for the one who begins his meal with salt and ends with salt will be cured from seventy-two types of affliction, among them leprosy, insanity, and vitiligo.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from a man, from Sa'd al-Askaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, in salt is a cure for seventy illnesses, or he said: seventy types of pains. Then he said: If the people knew what is in the salt, they would not cure (themselves) except by it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the salt at the inception of your meal, for had the people known what is in the salt, they would choose it over the experimental antidote.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Ja'fari, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: A food-spread is not fruitful (beneficial) without salt upon it, and it is more corrective for the body that one begins with it at the start of the meal.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Sukayn ibn 'Ammar, from Fudayl al-Rassan, from Farwa, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'Order your people to begin with salt and end with it, or else let them not blame anyone but themselves.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abu Mahmoud, who said: Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to us: 'Which condiment is most worthy?' So one of us said, 'Meat,' and one of us said, 'Oil,' and one of us said, 'Milk.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but it is salt.' And we had gone out on a trip of ours, and one of the slaves had forgotten the salt, so they slaughtered a sheep for us that was as fat as it could be, but we derived no benefit from it until we returned.
From him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who sprinkles salt upon the first morsel of his meal, the blemishes will go away from his face.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Indeed, a scorpion bit the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'May Allah curse you, for you do not care whether it is a believer you harm or an infidel.' Then he called for salt, rubbed it on the wound, and it healed. Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If people knew what is in the salt, they would not seek any other antidote with it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, and Amr ibn Ibrahim, all from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: A scorpion stung the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he shook it off and said: 'May Allah curse you, for neither a believer nor an infidel is safe from you.' Then he called for salt, placed it upon the site of the sting, and pressed it with his thumb until it melted. Then he said: 'If people knew what is in the salt, they would not be in need of an antidote alongside it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, who said: I used to break the fast with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and with Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) in the month of Ramadan. The first thing brought to him was a bowl of tharid made with vinegar and oil. The first thing he would take from it was three morsels, then the large bowl was brought.

From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Salama al-Qalanisi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). When I spoke, he said to me: 'What is the matter? I hear your speech has weakened.' I said: 'My tooth has fallen out.' It was as if that was grievous to him. Then he said: 'So what do you eat?' I said: 'I eat whatever is in the house.' He said: 'Stick to ath-tharid, for therein is a blessing. If there is no meat, then vinegar and oil.'

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Zayd ibn al-Hasan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was the most resembling of the people in his meal to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He used to eat bread, vinegar, and oil, and he would feed the people bread and meat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ubayda al-Wasiti, from Ajlan, who said: I had dinner with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) after darkness, and he used to have dinner after darkness. So vinegar, oil, and cold meat were brought to him. He began to pick at the meat and feed it to me, while he himself ate the vinegar and the oil and left the meat. He said: 'This is our food, and the food of the Prophets (peace be upon them).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said: I ate with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'O maid, bring us our well-known meal.' So she brought a dish containing vinegar and oil, so we ate.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The best of the dishes to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was the vinegar and the oil, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the meal of the Prophets (peace be upon them).'

And by this chain, he said, Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: A family will never be poor that uses vinegar and oil for their sauce, and that is the sauce of the Prophets (peace be upon them).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halbi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meal, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Adhere to vinegar and oil, for it is nourishing. Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to eat it frequently, and I eat it frequently, and it is nourishing.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) used to eat the vinegar and the oil, and he kept the expenditure (for it) under his carpet.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered upon Umm Salma (may Allah be pleased with her), and she brought forward a piece of bread to him. He said: 'Do you have any sauce (idam)?' She said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing except vinegar.' He said (peace be upon him and his family): 'Excellent is the sauce, vinegar; a house is never impoverished if it has vinegar.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The vinegar strengthens the intellect.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'A house in which there is vinegar does not become impoverished, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said that.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Aban ibn Abdul Malik, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: We begin with vinegar in our presence, just as you begin with salt in your presence, for vinegar indeed strengthens the intellect.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The most beloved of the dyes to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was the vinegar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of sauces is vinegar; it breaks the bitterness, extinguishes the yellow bile, and revives the heart.'

Ali, from his father, from Hannan, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), said: Vinegar of wine was mentioned in his presence, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It kills the insects of the belly and strengthens the mouth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Vinegar of the wine strengthens the gums, and kills the insects of the belly, and strengthens the intellect.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of Umar ibn Musa, from their father, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Dyeing (the hair) with vinegar cuts the desire for adultery.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabie al-Musally, from Ahmad ibn Razin, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: ‘Upon you is with the vinegar of wine, so immerse (in it), for there would not remain in your belly any insect but it would kill it’.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Suleiman ibn Rushayd, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Suleyman al-Daylami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Children of Israel would begin (their meals) with vinegar and end with it, and we begin with salt and end with vinegar.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Kahili who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while I was in his presence one day, about cutting off the fat tails of sheep. So he said: 'There is no problem with cutting them if you are thereby improving your livestock.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), it is written that whatever is cut off from them is dead (maytah) and cannot be used.'
He said regarding the fat tails of lambs that are cut off while they are alive: Indeed, it (the cut tail) is dead (impure/carrion).

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), so I said to him: 'May I be your sacrifice! The people of the mountains — the fat tails of the sheep become heavy in their possession so they cut them off.' He said: 'It is haram.' I said: 'May I be your sacrifice! We use them to light fires.' He said: 'Do you not know that it touches the hand and the clothing, and it is haram?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqub ibn Yazid and Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who struck a gazelle with his sword until he cut it into two halves — can he eat it? He said: 'Yes, he may eat from what follows the head, then leave the tail (rear half).'

I said to him: 'Sometimes I shoot with the blunt arrow (mi'rad) and I kill.' So he said: 'When it cuts it into two parts, throw away the smaller of the two and eat the larger. And if they are equal, then eat them both.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from some of our companions, raising it (to the Imam): Regarding the antelope and the wild donkey that are intercepted with the sword and cut in two — so he said: There is no problem with eating both of them, as long as one of the two halves is not moving. But if one of the two moves, then the other shall not be eaten, because it is carrion.

Regarding the man who strikes the hunted prey and cuts it in two halves — he said: He may eat both of them together. But if he struck it and a part was cut off from it, he should not eat from it what was cut off, and he may eat the rest of it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Eat the oil, and massage with the oil, for it is from a Blessed tree'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it. Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) He said: 'From what Adam (peace be upon him) bequeathed to his son Hibatullah was: "Eat the olives, for they are from a blessed tree."'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, or someone else, said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'They are saying that olives stimulate the winds.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, olives dispel the winds.'

From him, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Wasi', from Ishaq ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Yazeed, from Abu Dawud al-Nakha'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Anoint yourselves with oil and use it as a condiment, for it is the anointing of the best and the condiment of the chosen ones. It was wiped with the Holy [spirit/essence] twice, blessed coming and blessed going, no illness harms with it.'

Mansour ibn al-Abbas, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Zari' al-Basri, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We mentioned the olives in his presence, so the man said, 'It brings the wind.' He said: 'No, but it dispels the wind.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Jariri, from Abdul-Mumin Al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Oil is the anointing oil of the righteous and the condiment of the best. Blessing is in it when facing forward and blessing is in it when facing backward; immerse it in the Holy [oil] twice.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, raising it (to the Imam), said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The olives increase in the water.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The people are not healed with the likes of (healing with) the honey.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Licking honey is a cure for every illness.' There comes forth from their bellies a drink of varying colors, in which is healing for the people. And it, along with the recitation of the Quran and chewing frankincense, melts the phlegm.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) liked honey.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sukayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat honey and say: 'A verse from the Quran and chewing frankincense melts the phlegm'.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: A patient is not healed with anything like honey.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first used to frequently eat sugar at sleep time.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If cheese harms from everything and does not benefit, then sugar benefits from everything and does not harm from anything.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Azdi, from one of our companions, raising it (to the Imam), said: A man complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying, 'I am a complaining man.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Where is it from the Blessed?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is the Blessed?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The sugar.' I said, 'Which sugar, may I be sacrificed for you?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Your Suleymaniyya, this.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), or he said, 'one of our companions, from al-Rida (peace be upon him)' He said: 'The Tabarzand sugar consumes the phlegm with a devouring consumption.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Numan, from one of our companions, who said: I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the pain, so he said to me: 'When you go to your bed, eat two (lumps of) sugar.' He said: 'So I did that and I was cured. So I informed one of the physicians, and he was the most splendid of the people of our city, so he said: 'From where did Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) recognize this? This is from the treasures of our knowledge. Indeed, he is the owner of Books, so it is befitting that he happened to have found it in one of his Books.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Mu'tab who said: When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had dinner, he said to me: 'When you enter the storage, seek out for me two (lumps of) sugar.' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! There is nothing there.' So he said, 'Enter, woe be unto you!' So I entered and found two (lumps of) sugar, so came with these to him.
