Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man complained to him about the epidemic, so he said to him: 'And where are you from the good, the Blessed?' He said, 'I said, 'And what is the good, the Blessed?'' So he said: 'Your Suleymaniyya (sugar), this.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The first one to take the sugar was Suleyman ibn Dawood (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ubayd al-Khayyat, from Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a man has a thousand dirhams with him, and he has nothing else, then he buys sugar with it, he would not be considered extravagant.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yahya ibn Bashir al-Nabbal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to my father: 'O Bashir! By what are you curing your sick ones?' He said, 'By these bitter medicines.' He said to him, 'No. When one of you is sick, take the white sugar, pound it, and pour cold water over it, and give it to him to drink, for the One Who made the healing in bitterness is Able to make it in sweetness.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yasser, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The Tabarzand sugar consumes the phlegm with a devouring.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from one of our companions who said: One of our family members had fever, so the physicians prescribed Al-Ghafis (a herb) for him. So we made him drink it, but he did not benefit from it. So I complained of that to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah has not Made a healing in anything from the bitter. Take a (lump of) sugar and a half, so grind it in a vessel and pour water over it until it melts in it, and place iron over it, and apportion it from the beginning of the night. So when it becomes (a solution), so take it with your hand and make him drink it. So when it is the second night, so make it with two (lumps of) sugar and a half, and apportion it just as you had done beforehand, and make him drink it. And when it was the third night, so take three (lumps of) sugar and a half, and apportion it like that'. He (the narrator) said, 'So I did, and Allah Mighty and Majestic Healed our sick'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The butter of the cow is a healing.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The clarified butter (saman) is a medicine, and it is better in the summer than in the winter, and nothing enters the stomach like it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Muttalib ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The best of the sauces (accompaniments) is the ghee (melted butter).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the man reaches fifty years, he should not sleep with anything of ghee (clarified butter) in his stomach.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so an old man from the people of Iraq spoke to him and said to him, 'Why do I see your speech as changed?' He said to him, 'The front (teeth) of my mouth have fallen off, so my speech is deficient.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And I as well, some of my teeth have fallen off, to the extent that Satan whispers to me, saying,

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Hafs al-Abbar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The ghee (or clarified butter) is that which enters a stomach like it (i.e., digests easily or is pure), and indeed I dislike it for the old man.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not eat food nor drink a drink except that he said: 'O Allah, bless us in it and replace it with something better than it,' except for milk, for he would say: 'O Allah, bless us in it and increase us from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Abbad ibn Yaqub, from Ubayd ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The milk of the black sheep is better than the milk of the red ones, and the milk of the red cow is better than the milk of the black ones.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ary, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he drank milk, would say: 'O Allah, bless us in it and increase us from it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Abdillah al-Farisi, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him, 'I drank milk and it harmed me.' He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'No, by Allah, milk does not harm at all, but you ate it with something else, so that which you ate harmed you, and you thought that harm was from the milk.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No one chokes when drinking milk,' because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Milk, pure and palatable for the drinkers.'
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The milk is the food of the sent (Prophets).

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Asbahani, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him while I was listening: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I find weakness in my body.' He said to him: 'Stick to milk, for it builds flesh and strengthens bone.'

From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first, who said: The one to whom the water of the back changes, so it would be beneficial for him, the milk and the honey.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: We ate with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so they brought us meat from a slaughtered camel. I thought it was from his house, so we ate. Then they brought us a bowl of milk, and he drank from it. Then he said to me, 'Drink, O Abu Muhammad.' So I tasted it, and I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, milk!' He said, 'It is the nature (fitrah).' Then they brought us dates, and we ate them.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The milk of the cow is a medicine.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I complained to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) of a stomach ache that I had found, so he said to me: 'What prevents you from drinking the milk of cows?' He said to me: 'Do you drink it at all?' So I said to him: 'Yes, repeatedly.' He said: 'How do you find it?' So I said: 'I find it tanning the stomach, covering the two kidneys with fat, and making the food desirable.' He said to me: 'If it were its days, I and you would have gone out to Yanbu' until we drank it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Adhere to the milk of the cow, for it mingles with every tree.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Ja'fari who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: The urine of camels is better than their milk, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has placed cure in their milk.

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from certain persons of our people, from Musa ibn Abdillah ibn al-Hasan, who said: I heard our shaykhs saying The milk of camels is a cure for all kinds of illness and defects, and for one’s stomach trouble it is their urine.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I had lunch with him, so he said to me: 'Do you know what this is?' I said, 'No'. He said: 'This is Shiraz al-Atun (a type of yogurt drink). We have prepared it for one of our sick people, so if you wish to eat from it, then eat.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Yahya ibn Abdullah, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and small dishes were brought to us. So he pointed with his hand to one of them and said: 'This is Shiraz al-Utun. We have taken it for the sick among us, and whoever wishes may eat it, and whoever wishes may leave it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about drinking the milk of donkeys, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Drink it'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mubarak, from Abu Maryam Al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about drinking the milk of donkeys, so he said to me: 'There is no problem with it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I was sitting in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) when a man approached, greeted, and asked, 'Who are you, O servant of Allah?' I said, 'A man from the people of Kufa.' He asked, 'What is your need?' I said to him, 'Do you know Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'What is your need to him?' He said, 'I have prepared forty questions to ask him about them; whatever is truth I will take, and whatever is falsehood I will leave.' Abu Hamza said, 'So I said to him, 'Do you know the difference between truth and falsehood?' He said, 'Yes.' I said to him, 'Then what is your need for him if you know the difference between truth and falsehood?' He said to me, 'O people of Kufa! You are a people who cannot be tolerated. When you see Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), inform me.' My speech with him did not cease until Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) approached, and around him were the people of Khurasan and others, asking him about the rituals of Hajj. He proceeded until he sat in his place, and the man sat near him. Abu Hamza said, 'So I sat where I could hear the speech, and around him was a multitude of people. When he had fulfilled their needs and they departed, he turned to the man and said to him, 'Who are you?' He said, 'I am Qatada ibn Di'ama al-Basri.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'You are a jurist of the people of Basra?' He said, 'Yes.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Woe to you, O Qatada! Indeed, Allah, Glorious and Mighty, created a people from His creation and made them proofs upon His creation. They are the pegs in His earth, standing by His command, excellent in His knowledge. He chose them before creating them as shades on the right of His Throne.' Qatada was silent for a long time, then said, 'May Allah rectify you! By Allah, I have sat before the jurists and in front of Ibn Abbas, and my heart did not tremble before any of them as it trembled before you.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Woe to you! Do you know where you are? You are in front of houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted and that His Name be mentioned in them; glorifying Him therein in the mornings and the evenings. Men whom neit

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus — from them (peace be upon them) who said: Five things are pure (ritually permissible), from those which have benefits for people: the rennet, and the egg, and the wool, and the hair, and the fur. There is no problem with eating cheese — all of it — whether made by a Muslim or another. And it is only disliked to eat, besides the rennet, from what is in the vessels of the Magians and the People of the Book, because they do not refrain from carrion and wine.

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and my father was asking him about the milk from a dead animal, the egg from a dead animal, and the rennet of a dead animal. He said: 'All of this is ritually clean.' He (al-Husayn) said: So I said to him, 'What about pig hair that is made into a rope and used to draw water from a well from which people drink or perform wudu?' He said: 'There is no problem with it.' Ali ibn Uqba and Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat added to this, saying: He (the Imam) said, 'And hair and wool — all of it is ritually clean.' And in the report of Safwan, from al-Husayn ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: 'Hair, wool, fur, feathers, and everything that grows does not become dead (ritually impure).' He (al-Husayn) said: And I asked him about an egg extracted from the belly of a dead chicken. He said: 'You may eat it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim: The milk, and the colostrum, and the egg, and the hair, and the wool, and the horn, and the tooth, and the hoof, and everything separated from the sheep and the riding animal — it is ritually pure (zakiy). But if you take it from the animal after it has died, wash it and pray in it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — regarding an egg that came out from (the body of) a dead chicken. So he said: 'If the egg has acquired the hard shell, then there is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Mukhtar, and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn Al-Hasan Al-Alawi, all together from Al-Fath ibn Yazid Al-Jurjani, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: 'I wrote to him (peace be upon him) asking him about the skins of the dead (animal) whose meat is (permissible to) eat if it is properly slaughtered.' So he wrote: 'One may not benefit from a dead (animal) by [using] its skin nor its sinew; but everything that was from the young animals — from the wool if it is sheared, and the hair, and the fur, and the rennet, and the horn — and do not exceed to other than these, God willing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom! Can one derive any benefit from a dead animal?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'It has reached us that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a dead sheep and said: What prevented the owners of this sheep, since they could not benefit from its flesh, from benefiting from its hide?' He said: 'That was a sheep belonging to Sawda bint Zam'a, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). It was an emaciated sheep from whose flesh no benefit could be derived. They left it until it died. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: What prevented its owners, since they could not benefit from its flesh, from benefiting from its hide — meaning, by slaughtering it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating walnuts during intense heat agitates the heat in the body cavity and agitates sores on the body, and eating it in winter warms the kidneys and dispels the cold.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Cheese and walnuts, when they are combined, in each one of them is a healing, and if they are separated, in each one of them is an illness.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Idris ibn al-Hasan, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, walnuts and cheese, when they are combined, are a cure, and when they are separated, they are an illness.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam and al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal from Yunus ibn Yaqub who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Nothing that comes to us from your area is more beloved to me than rice and the violet. I complained of that severe pain, so I was inspired to eat rice. So I ordered it to be washed and dried, then fried and ground, and made for me as an oiled powder and a cooked dish which I would consume, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed that pain from me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, and others, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Zurara, who said: I saw the nursemaid of Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) feeding him rice and striking it onto him, so what I saw grieved me. I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'I reckon your grief is due to what you saw from the nursemaid of Abu al-Hasan Musa.' I said to him, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said to me, 'Excellent is the food, rice; it expands the intestines and cuts off the hemorrhoids. And we envy the people of Iraq for their eating of rice and partially-ripened dates, for these two expand the intestines and cut off the hemorrhoids.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Suleiman al-Hazza', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man came to him and said to him, 'My daughter has withered and she is pregnant.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents you from the rice with the fat? Take four or five stones, place them by the side of the fire, and put the rice in the pot and cook it until it is done. Take the fat of fresh kidneys. When the rice is done, place the fat in a bowl along with the stones, and cover it with another bowl. Then stir it well and keep it steady so that its steam does not escape. When the fat has melted, mix it into the rice, then she can eat it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Usman ibn Isa, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: ‘The best of the foods is the rice, and we preserve it for our sick ones’.
From him, from Yahya ibn Isa, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'The best of foods is rice, and we cure our illnesses with it.'

From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about stomach pain, so he said to me: 'Take the rice, wash it, then dry it in the shade, then powder it, and take from it every morning an amount that fits in the palm of your hand.' And Is'haq al-Jariri added: 'Fry it slightly, the weight of one Awqiya, and drink it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Humran, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had stomach pain, so he instructed that rice be cooked for him and sumac sprinkled upon it. He ate it and was cured.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Nadir the servant, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to eat the cooked chick-peas before the meal and after it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah, from Rifa'ah, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, restored health to Ayoub (peace be upon him), he looked at the Children of Israel who had sown (crops), so he raised his gaze to the sky and said: 'My God and my Master, Your servant Ayoub, the afflicted, You granted him health, and he has no place to sow anything, and this is a plantation of the Children of Israel.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Ayoub, take a handful from your rosary (or prayer beads), and sow it.' And his rosary contained salt in it. So Ayoub (peace be upon him) took a handful from it and sowed it, and this lentil came out. And you call it chickpeas, and we call it lentils.'
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: The chick-peas is good for the back pain, and he used to call for it before the meal and after it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating lentils softens the heart and increases weeping.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, that one of the Children of Israel complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about the hardness of the heart and the scarcity of tears. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Eat the lentils.' So he ate the lentils, his heart softened, and his tears flowed. From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: 'A man complained to the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about the hardness of the heart. So he said to him: 'Stick to the lentils, for it softens the heart and hastens the tears.'

From him, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadhdha', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said: I ate lentil broth with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be your ransom, these people say that eighty prophets have sanctified lentils.' He said, 'They have lied, no, by Allah, not even twenty prophets.' And it is narrated that it softens the heart and hastens the flow of tears.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Umar ibn Salma, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Eating the broad-beans enhances the two thighs, and increases in the brain, and gives birth to fresh blood.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said: Eating the broad-beans enhances the two thighs, and gives birth to the fresh blood.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of his companions, from Salih ibn Uqba who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eat the broad beans with their skin, for it tans (hardens/strengthens) the stomach.'
Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The kidney-beans expel the underlying wind.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Muyassar, from Muhammad ibn Abdul Aziz, from his father, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'then let him see which of them has purest food, so let him bring you provision from it'. He said: 'The purest food is dates.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Anbasa ibn Bajad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: ‘Never was a meal presented to Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him) in which were dates, except that he (peace be upon him) began with the dates’.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sudeyr, from his father, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) loved to see a man who was fond of dates, due to the love of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for dates.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra', from one of his companions, from Uqba ibn Bashir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We entered upon him, so he called for dates, and we ate them. Then he increased it for us from it, then he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I love the man,' or he said: 'I like the man who is fond of dates.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Amr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The best of your dates is Al-Barni; it removes the illness and there is no illness in it, and it removes the fatigue and there is no harm for it, and it removes the phlegm; and with every date is a good deed (reward). And in another report: It is palatable and wholesome, and it removes the fatigue, and it satiates.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Razi, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), and in front of him were Barni dates, and he was diligent in eating them, eating them with desire. So he said to me: 'O Suleiman, approach and eat.' He said: So I approached him and ate with him, and I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I see you eating this date with desire.' So he said: 'Yes, I indeed love it.' He said: I said, 'And why is that?' He said: 'Because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was a date-lover, and Ali (peace be upon him) was a date-lover, and al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was a date-lover, and Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was a date-lover, and Zayn al-Abideen (peace be upon him) was a date-lover, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was a date-lover, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was a date-lover, and my father (peace be upon him) was a date-lover, and I am a date-lover. And our Shias love dates because they were created from our clay. And our enemies, O Suleiman, love the intoxicants because they were created from a smokeless fire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Barni dates satiate, are palatable, and are nourishing; they are the cure and there is no illness for them. They remove fatigue, and with every date is a good deed (reward).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Khattab al-Hallal, from A'ala ibn Razin, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O A'ala! Do you know what is the first tree that sprouted upon the surface of the earth?' I said, 'Allah and His Messenger and the son of His Messenger know best.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the Ajwa (date palm). So whatever is pure/selected, it is the Ajwa, and whatever is other than that, it is merely from its resemblances.'

From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Ajwa and the Ateeq from the sky. I said, 'And what is the Ateeq?' He said, 'The stallion.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Ajwa is the mother of the dates which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to Adam (peace be upon him) from Paradise.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Ahmad ibn A'idh from Abu Khadeeja from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Al-Ajwa is the mother of dates, and it is that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down from Paradise to Adam (peace be upon him). Whatever palm-trees you cut down or leave standing upon their roots He said, it means Al-Ajwa.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The palm tree of Maryam (peace be upon her) was Al-Ajwa, and it was sent down in the month of Kanun (December/January), and Al-Ateeq and Al-Ajwa were sent down with Adam (peace be upon him), and from it the varieties of palm trees disseminated.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadeeja, who said: We took seeds of Ajwa dates from Medina, and a companion of ours planted them in an orchard. From them grew the Sakkar, al-Heyroun, al-Shahriz, al-Sarfan, and every type of date.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Sarfan is the chief of your dates.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, all together from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from one of our companions, who said: When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in Al-Hira, he rode his animal and went to Al-Khwarraq. So he descended and took shade in the shadow of his animal, and with him was a black slave of his. He saw a man from the people of Kufa who had bought a palm tree. He said to the slave, 'Who is this?' He said to him, 'This is Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him)'. So he brought a large platter and placed it in front of him. He said to the man, 'What is this?' He said, 'This is Al-Barniy'. He said, 'Therein is a healing'. And he looked at Al-Sabiri, so he said, 'What is this?' He said, 'Al-Sabiri'. He said, 'This with us is Al-Bayd'. And he said for Al-Mushan, 'What is this?' So the man said, 'Al-Mushan'. He said (peace be upon him), 'This with us is Umm Jirzan'. And he looked at Al-Sarfan, so he said, 'What is this?' So the man said, 'Al-Sarfan'. He said, 'With us it is Al-Ajwa and therein is a healing'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Dates were mentioned in his presence, so he said: 'One date with you is better than one date with us, and all the dates with us are better than all the dates with you.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Abu Suleiman al-Hammar, who said: We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he brought us a sauce (madiarah) and food after it. Then he brought a basket of soft dates (rutab) upon which were various kinds. So he (peace be upon him) took one with his hand after another, saying: 'What do you call this?' So we said such and such, until he took one and said: 'What do you call this?' So we said: 'Al-Mushan'. He said: 'We call it Umm Jirzan. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was brought something from it, so he ate from it and supplicated for it, so there is nothing from the palm trees that bears more than it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so fresh dates were brought to him. He began eating from them and drinking water, and he handed me the bowl. I disliked returning it, so I drank until he did that repeatedly. He said, so I said: 'I used to have excess phlegm, so I complained about it to Ahran, the physician of Al-Hajjaj.' He said to me: 'Do you have a palm tree in your orchard?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Are there palm trees in it?' I said: 'Yes.' So he said to me: 'Count for me what is in it.' So I counted until I reached Al-Hayrun (a type of date). He said to me: 'Eat seven of them whenever you intend to sleep, and do not drink water.' So I did that, and I wanted to spit but I was unable to do so. So I complained to him about that, so he said to me: 'Drink a little water and hold back until your constitution becomes balanced.' So I did that. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, had it not been for the water, I would not care if I did not taste it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever eats seven Ajwa dates every day upon the empty stomach from the dates of Al-Aaliya, neither poison will harm him, nor sorcery, nor Satan.

From him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandy, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who eats seven Ajwa dates at his sleep time, would kill the insects in his belly.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Suleyman, from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Tahhan, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Five are from the fruits of Paradise in the world: the Amleysi pomegranate, and the Sheysqan apple, and the quince, and the Raziqy grapes, and the Mushan dates.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Abdul Aziz ibn Zakariyya al-Lu'lu'i, from Suleyman ibn al-Mufazzal, who said: 'I heard Abu al-Jaroud narrating from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)' He said: 'Four things descended from Paradise: the Raziqiy grape, the Mushan date, the Imleysi pomegranate, and the Sheysqan apple.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he disliked peeling the fruit.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Munthir, from the one who mentioned it, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'For every fruit there is poison, so whenever you are given it, wipe it with water or immerse it in water, meaning wash it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Rabi' al-Musally, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbouz, from the one who saw the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) eating bread with grapes. He was eating bread with grapes.

From him, from Al-Qasim al-Zayyat, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Musa ibn al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the water laid bare the bones of the dead, Noah (peace be upon him) saw that and panicked with an intense panic, and was aggrieved due to that. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed unto him: 'This is your doing, you supplicated against them'. So he said: 'O Lord! I seek Forgiveness from You and I repent to You'. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed unto him: 'If you were to eat the black grapes, it would do away with (remove) your grief'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) liked grapes. So one day he was fasting, and when he broke his fast, the first thing that came was grapes. A mother of his child came to him with a cluster of grapes and placed it in front of him. A beggar came, so he gave it to him. His mother of child went to the beggar and bought it from him. Then she came with it and placed it in front of him. Another beggar came, so he gave it to him. The mother of the child did the same. Then she came with it and placed it in front of him. Another beggar came, so he gave it to him. The mother of the child did the same. When it was the fourth time, he ate it (peace be upon him).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A Prophet from the Prophets complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about gloom (melancholy/sorrow), so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to eat grapes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from one of his companions, from Ibn Baqqah, from Harun ibn al-Khattab, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rassan, who said: I was grazing my camels on the road of al-Khwarraq, so I saw a group of people coming. I inclined towards one of those with them and said, 'Who are these?' He said, 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn al-Hasan. They were presented to al-Mansur.' He said: So I asked about them afterwards, and it was said to me, 'They have lodged at al-Hira.' So I rose early to greet them. I entered and found in front of them baskets containing fresh dates that had been gifted to them from Kufa. They were uncovered in front of them. Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) extended his hand, ate, and said to me, 'Eat.' Then he said to Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, 'O Abu Muhammad, what do you think? How good are these fresh dates?' Then Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) turned to me and said, 'O people of Kufa! You have been preferred over the people in food with three things: your fish, this al-Bunani; your grapes, this al-Raziqi; and your dates, this al-Mushan.'

The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said: Water is the chief of drinks in this world and the Hereafter. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdillah, by his chain — similar to it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying — and he mentioned the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — then he said: 'O Allah! Indeed You know that he is more beloved to us than fathers, mothers, and cold water.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from more than one, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The first thing Allah — Mighty is His mention — will question the servant about is that He will say to him: Did I not quench you from the fresh waters of the Euphrates?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, raising it (the chain), said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The chief of the drinks of Paradise is water.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Water is the chief of drinks in this world and the Hereafter.
He (Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him) said: Whoever finds pleasure in water in this world, God — Mighty and Majestic — will make him enjoy from the drinks of Paradise.
A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the taste of water, so he said: 'Ask to understand, and do not ask to harass. The taste of water is the taste of life.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade seeking healing by the hot springs, and these are the hot springs that are in the mountains in which the smell of sulphur is found, and it has been said that they are from the breath of Hell.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Noah (peace be upon him), when he was in the days of the flood, called upon all the waters, so they responded to him except for the water of sulfur and the bitter water, so he cursed them both.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman al-Naysaburi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Zakariyya, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, all together, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Saeed Aqeysa al-Taymi, who said: I passed by al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), and they were in the Euphrates, soaking their lower garments. So I said to them, 'O sons of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)! Have you spoiled your lower garments?' They said to me, 'O Abu Saeed! The spoiling of our lower garments is more beloved to us than the spoiling of the Religion. Indeed, for the water there are its rightful ones and dwellers, like the dwellers of the earth.' Then they said, 'Where do you intend to go?' I said, 'To this water.' They said, 'And what is this water?' I said, 'I want its remedy; I drink from this bitter water for an ailment in me, hoping that the body will lighten and the belly will be eased.' They said, 'We do not reckon that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made healing in something which He has cursed.' I said, 'And why is that?' They said, 'Because when Allah, Blessed and High, was angered by the people of Noah (peace be upon him), He opened the sky with a downpour of water, and revealed to the earth. But certain springs from it disobeyed Him, so He cursed them and made them salty and bitter.' And in the narration of Hamdan ibn Suleyman, they (peace be upon them) said, 'O Abu Saeed! You have come to a water which denies our Wilayah three times each day. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, presented our Wilayah to the waters; so whatever accepted our Wilayah became fresh and sweet, and whatever denied our Wilayah, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made it bitter or salty and burning.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) disliked being treated/healed with bitter water and with sulphuric water, and he used to say: 'Indeed, Noah (peace be upon him), when the flood occurred, called upon the waters, so all of them responded to him except for the bitter water and the sulphuric water, so he supplicated against them and cursed them both.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I was at the fountain of Zamzam, and a man came to me and said to me, 'Do not drink from this water, O Abu Hamza, for in this the Jinn and humans share, and in this only humans share.' I was surprised by his statement and said, 'From where does he know this?' Then I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) what the man had said to me, so he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'That man is from the Jinn, intending to guide you.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The water of the Nile of Egypt deadens the hearts'.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Nawfali, from al-Yaqubi, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And We send down water from the sky according to a measure, then We settle it in the earth, and We are able to take it away.' He said: 'Meaning the water of the ravines.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Madainy, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Two rivers are Believers, and two rivers are Infidels. So as for the two Believers, the Euphrates and the Nile of Egypt, and as for the two Infidels, the Tigris and the river of Balkh.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Khashab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he asked for water. So when he drank it, I saw him bewail and his eyes filled with his tears. Then he said to me: 'O Dawood! May Allah curse the killers of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). And there is no servant who drinks water, so he remembers Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the People of his household, and curses his killers, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him one hundred thousand good deeds, and deletes from him one hundred thousand sins, and raises for him one hundred thousand levels, and it is as if he has liberated one hundred thousand persons, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment as cool-hearted.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wine is from five: the juice pressed from the vine, the infusion of raisins, the mead from honey, the ale from barley, and the Nabeez from dates.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan Al-Hazramy, from the one who informed him, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The wine is from five things: from dates, raisins, wheat, barley, and honey.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Aamir ibn al-Simt, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) – similar to it. Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Ishaq al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The wine is from five: the juice from the grapes, the marinade from the raisins, the mead from the honey, the ale from the barley, and Al-Nabeez from the dates.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the origin of wine, how its permissibility began and its prohibition, and when wine was taken. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, when Adam (peace be upon him) descended from Paradise, he desired from its fruits. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to him two branches of grapes, so he planted them. When they grew leaves and bore fruit and became large, Iblees (may Allah curse him) came and built a wall around them. Adam (peace be upon him) said: What is your state, O Accursed? Iblees said: These two are mine. He said to him: You are lying!' So they both agreed to have the Holy Spirit decide between them. When they went to him, Adam (peace be upon him) related his story to him. The Holy Spirit took a bundle of fire and threw it upon them, with the grapes still in their branches, to the extent that Adam (peace be upon him) thought that nothing remained of them, and Iblees (may Allah curse him) thought the same. He said: So the fire entered where it entered, and two-thirds of them had gone (burned), and one-third remained. So the Spirit said: As for what went from them, that is the share of Iblees (may Allah curse him), and whatever remains is for you, O Adam. Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Nafi', from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from al-Husayn ibn Yazeed from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He caused Adam (peace be upon him) to descend, commanded him with ploughing and planting, and cast down to him a shoot from the shoots of Paradise, so He gave him the palm tree, the grapes, the olives, and the pomegranate, so he planted them so that they would be for his offspring and descendants. So he ate from its fruits, then Iblis (may Allah curse him) said to him: 'O Adam, what is this shoot which I did not know in the earth, although I was in it before you? Allow me to eat something from it.' So Adam (peace be upon him) refused to let him. So Iblis came at the end of the lifetime of Adam (peace be upon him) and said to Hawwa: 'Hunger and thirst have exhausted me.' So Hawwa said to him: 'So what do you want?' He said: 'I want you to make me taste from these fruits.' So Hawwa said: 'Adam (peace be upon him) has made me vow that I will not feed you anything from this shoot because it is from Paradise, and it is not befitting for you to eat anything from it.' So he said to her: 'So squeeze something of it in my palm.' But she refused to him. So he said: 'Allow me to suck it and I will not eat it.' So she took a cluster of grapes and gave it to him, so he sucked it and did not eat from it because Hawwa had insisted upon him. So when he went to bite it, Hawwa pulled it from his mouth. So Allah, Blessed and High, revealed to Adam (peace be upon him): 'The grapes have been sucked by My enemy and your enemy, Iblis, and I have prohibited upon you from the juice of wine that which was mixed with the breath of Iblis.' So wine was prohibited because the enemy of Allah, Iblis, plotted with Hawwa until he sucked the grapes. And if he had eaten it, the vine would have been prohibited from its beginning to its end, and all its fruit, and whatever comes out of it. Then he said to Hawwa: 'If only you would let me suck something from this date as you let me suck from the grapes.' So she gave him a date, so he sucked it. And the grapes and the date were more intense in scent and purer than Al-Azfar musk, and sweeter than honey. So when the enemy of Allah, Iblis (may Allah curse him), sucked them, their scent went away and their sweetness decreased. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Iblis (may Allah curse him) disputed with Noah (peace be upon him) regarding the vineyard. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: 'Indeed, he has a right, so give it to him.' So he gave him one-third. But Iblis did not agree. Then he gave him one-half, but he did not agree. So Gabriel threw fire, and it burned the two-thirds, and the one-third remained. So he said: 'Whatever the fire burned, that is his share, and whatever remains, that is permissible for you, O Noah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet at all except that it was in the Knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that when He completed the Religion for him, the prohibition of wine was included in it, and wine did not cease to be unlawful. Indeed, the Religion is merely transformed from one characteristic to another, so if that had been in its entirety (all characteristics at once), they would have been cut off from the Religion.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet at all except that it was in the Knowledge of Allah, Blessed and High, that when He completed His Religion for him, among it would be the prohibition of wine, and wine never ceased to be unlawful. Rather, the Religion changes from one characteristic to another, and had that (change) been in its entirety, they (people) would have been cut-off from the Religion.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about wine, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent me as a mercy to the worlds, and to obliterate the musical instruments, and the pipes, and the affairs of the Pre-Islamic period, and the idols.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'My Lord swore that no servant of Mine will drink wine in the world except that I shall give him to drink of its equivalent from the scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, punished or forgiven; and no servant of Mine will give it to a young child or a slave except that I shall give him to drink of its equivalent from the scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, punished afterwards or forgiven.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine after Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has prohibited it upon my tongue, is not deserving of being married to when he proposes, nor is he to be interceded for when intercession is made, nor is he to be believed when he narrates, nor is he to be trusted with an entrustment. So whoever trusts him after having knowledge of him in this regard, there is no guarantee for the one who trusted him with Allah, Exalted and Mighty, nor is there any reward for him, nor a compensation.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Husayn ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The drinker of wine will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with his face blackened and his tongue drooping, his saliva dripping upon his chest. And it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to give him drink from the essence of Khabal, or he said: from a well of Khabal. I said: 'And what is the well of Khabal?' He said: 'A well in which the pus of the adulterers flows.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wine drinker is not visited when he is sick, nor is his funeral attended, nor is his testimony verified when he testifies, nor is he given in marriage when he proposes, nor is he entrusted with a trust.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-Ala' from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wine drinker, if he falls sick, do not visit him; and if he dies, do not attend his funeral; and if he testifies, do not accept his testimony; and if he proposes marriage, do not give him in marriage; and if he asks you for an entrustment, do not entrust it to him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Bashir al-Hudhali, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'When the newborn is born, we give him wine to drink.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever gives a newborn wine to drink, or said: an intoxicant, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will quench him with al-Hameem (scalding water), even if He has forgiven him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Durust, and Hisham ibn Salim, all from Ajlan Abi Salih, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The one who drinks an intoxicant, or gives it to a child who does not have intellect, I will quench him with scalding water as a punishment or grant him forgiveness; and the one who leaves the intoxicant seeking My pleasure, I will admit him into Paradise, quench him from the sealed nectar, and deal with him in terms of prestige as I deal with My guardians.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The wine drinker will come on the Day of Resurrection with a blackened face, a bent side, a drooping tongue, calling out, 'The thirst! The thirst!'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Hammad ibn Bashir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine after Allah the Exalted prohibited it upon my tongue, is not deserving of being married to when he proposes, nor to be believed when he narrates, nor interceded for when he intercedes, nor relied upon for an entrustment. So whoever trusts him with an entrustment and he consumes it or wastes it, it is not for the one who entrusted him, upon Allah Mighty and Majestic, that He rewards him or compensates him.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I intended to send goods to Yemen, so I went to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I intend to send so-and-so for the goods.' He said to me, 'Do you not know that he drinks wine?' I said, 'It has reached me from the believers that they say that.' He said to me, 'Believe them, for indeed Allah Mighty and Majestic says: He believes in Allah and believes in the believers.' Then he said: 'If you send him and the goods perish or are lost, it is not for you upon Allah Mighty and Majestic that He rewards you or compensates you.' So I sent him and he wasted it, and I supplicated to Allah Mighty and Majestic that He reward me. He said: 'O my son, no, it is not for you upon Allah that He rewards you or compensates you.' I said to him, 'And why is that?' He said to me, 'Indeed Allah Mighty and Majestic says: And do not give away your property to the foolish, which Allah has made for you a means of support. Do you know of any one more foolish than the wine drinker?' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant does not cease to be in a leeway from Allah Mighty and Majestic until he drinks wine. So when he drinks it, Allah Mighty and Majestic tears down his protective covering, and his guardian and his brother would be Iblis, may Allah curse him, and his hearing, and his vision, and his hand, and his foot, ushering him to every straying, and turning him away from every goodness.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed wine, and the one who squeezes it, and the one who orders it to be squeezed, and its seller, and its buyer, and its server, and the consumer of its price, and its drinker, and its carrier, and the one to whom it is carried.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali al-Sufi, from Khadir al-Sayrafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who drinks al-Nabeez upon the belief that it is permissible (halal) will abide eternally in the Fire, and the one who drinks it upon the belief that it is prohibited (haram) will be punished in the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Minqari, from Yazeed ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who drinks an intoxicant and dies, and in his inside is something from it, not having repented from it, would be Resurrected from his grave confused, his jaw inclined, his saliva oozing, calling for the woe and the doom.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Umar ibn Aban, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who drinks an intoxicant, it becomes a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He quenches him from the essence of Khabal.' I said, 'And what is the essence of Khabal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Puss from the private parts of a prostitute.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muhraz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not pray over the one drowned in wine.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Shaybani, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Yunus ibn Zabyan! Convey to Atiyya from me that whoever drinks a gulp of wine, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, curses him, and His Angels, and His Messengers, and the Believers. So if he drinks it until he becomes intoxicated from it, the Spirit of Faith is removed from his body, and a stupid, malicious, Accursed spirit rides in him, so he neglects the Prayer. So when he neglects the Prayer, the Angels rebuke him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to him: 'My servant! You have disbelieved,' and the Angels have rebuked you with a disgrace for you, 'My servant!' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A disgrace, a disgrace, just as the disgrace is. And by Allah, the rebuke of the Sublime, Majestic is His Name, for one hour is more severe than the punishment of a thousand years.' He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Accursed, wherever they are found, they are seized and killed with a fierce killing.' Then he said: 'O Yunus! Accursed, accursed is the one who neglects the Command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If he takes to the land, He ravages him, and if he takes to the sea, He drowns him. He is angered for the anger of the Sublime, Mighty is His Name.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Marwak, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the people of quenching (drinking) in the world from the intoxicant die thirsty, and are resurrected thirsty, and enter the Fire thirsty.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, and there is an increase in it: 'If a man were to apply kohl in his eye from wine with an applicator, it would be deserving upon Allah that He apply fire in his eye with an applicator.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He will not attain my intercession, the one who belittles his prayer, and he will not return to me at the Fountain, no, by Allah. He will not attain my intercession, the one who drinks the intoxicant, and he will not return to me at the Fountain, no, by Allah.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer is withheld for forty days, and if he dies during the forty days, he dies the death of ignorance; and if he repents, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repents towards him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty days. So if he dies during the forty days, he dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah); and if he repents, Allah turns towards him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty days; and if he repeats, Allah will quench him from the essence of Khabal. He said, I said, 'And what is the essence of Khabal?' So he said, 'Water that comes out from the private parts of the adulteresses.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who drinks wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said: Whoever drinks from the wine a single drink, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at the breaking of the fast every night of the month of Ramadan, there are those liberated from the Fire, except for the one who breaks his fast upon an intoxicant, and the one who drinks an intoxicant, his prayer is not reckoned for him for forty days, so if he dies during them, he dies a death of ignorance (pre-Islamic period).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: When my father (peace be upon him) was about to pass away, he said to me: 'O my son! He who holds the Prayer in light estimation will not attain our intercession, and he who is habitual in these drinks will not return to us at the Fountain.' So I said: 'O father! And which drinks?' So he said: 'Every intoxicant.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one among you who drinks an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty nights.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Amr ibn Shimr, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who drinks a drink of wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for seven days, and the one who becomes intoxicated, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty mornings.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine until he becomes intoxicated, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept his prayer from him for forty mornings.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever drinks a draught of wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We have been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'They speak the truth.' I said: 'And how is it that his prayer is not counted for forty mornings, neither less than that nor more?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, measured the creation of man, so He made it a nutfah (drop) for forty days. Then He transferred it and made it an 'alaqah (clot) for forty days. Then He transferred it and made it a mudghah (lump) for forty days.' So when he drinks wine, it remains in his bone marrow (mushash) for forty days, according to the measure of the transition of his creation.' He said, then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And similarly, all of his nourishment, his eating and drinking, remains in his bone marrow for forty days.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ismail ibn Bashaar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked him, so he said to him, 'May Allah keep you well! Is the drinking of wine more evil or the abandoning of the Prayer?' He said: 'The drinking of wine.' Then he said: 'Or do you know why that is so?' He said, 'No.' He said: 'Because he comes to be in a state in which he does not recognize his Lord with it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Halbi and Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, wine is the head of every sin.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wine is the starting point of every sin'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made locks for evil, and made its keys, or said: the keys to those locks are drinking (wine).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made a house for disobedience, then made a door for the house, then made a lock for the door, then made a key for the lock, so the key of disobedience is wine.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Allah Mighty and Majestic has not been disobeyed by anything more severe than drinking wine; indeed, one of them (the drinker) would neglect the obligatory prayer and leap upon his mother, his sister, and his daughter, while he is not fully conscious (of what he is doing).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, raised it (to the Imam), saying: It was said to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), 'You claim that drinking wine is more severe than adultery and theft?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes. The perpetrator of adultery may not proceed to other sins, but the wine drinker, when he drinks wine, commits adultery, and theft, and kills the soul whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited, and neglects the Prayer.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Drinking of the wine is a key to all evil.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, like an idol worshipper.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: He said: The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when he meets Him, like an idol worshipper.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Amr ibn Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The habitual drinker of wine meets Allah when he meets Him like an idol worshipper.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day he meets Him, as an infidel.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, Blessed and Exalted, on the Day he meets Him, like an idol worshipper.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Al-Halbi and Zurara as well, and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Humran ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that they said: The habitual drinker of wine is like an idol worshipper.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The habitual drinker of wine is like an idol worshipper. When he dies while being habitual over it, he will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when he meets Him, like an idol worshipper.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Dazawayi who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), asking him about the wine drinker. So he wrote: 'The wine drinker is an Infidel'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The habitual (drinker) of wine is like an idol worshipper.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father narrated to me, from his father (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The habitual drinker of wine is like an idol worshipper. I said to him, 'And what is the habitual drinker?' He said, 'The one who, whenever he finds it, drinks it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Hashim ibn Khalid, from Nuaym al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The habitual drinker of the intoxicant is the one who, whenever he finds it, drinks it.
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Sip the water with a sipping and do not gulp it down with a gulping, for indeed liver disease arises from it.

Abu Tayfour al-Mutattab said: I went to see Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), and I cautioned him against drinking water. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is the problem with water, when it circulates the food in the stomach, calms anger, increases intellect, and extinguishes bile?'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Abu Dawud al-Mustaraqqy, from one who narrated it to him, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He called for dates, ate them, and then proceeded to drink water after them. So I said to him: 'May I be your ransom! If only you would refrain from the water.' He said: 'I eat the dates precisely so that I may find the water pleasant afterward.'
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'I wonder at the one who eats the like of this' – and he gestured with his hand – 'and does not drink water after it; how does his stomach not burst?'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: Al-Mahdi asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about wine, 'Is it prohibited in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? For the people only know the prohibition (prevention) from it, and do not know its specific prohibition (haram status).' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Yes, it is prohibited in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, O Commander of the Faithful.' He said to him, 'In which place is it prohibited in the Book of Allah, Majestic is His Name, O Abu al-Hasan?' He said, 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Say: Indeed, my Lord has only prohibited the immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and the sin and the rebellion without right.' As for His Words 'what is apparent of them', it means open adultery, and the raising of flags which the promiscuous women used to raise for their immorality in the Pre-Islamic period. And as for His Words, Mighty and Majestic, 'and what is concealed', it means what the fathers married (i.e., the son marrying the father's wife), because the people, before the Prophet was sent (peace be upon him and his family), when a man had a wife and he died, his son would marry her after him, if she was not his mother. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited that. And as for 'the sin', it is the wine itself. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said in another place: 'They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In both of them is a great sin and benefits for the people.' As for the sin in the Book of Allah, it is the wine and the gambling, and their sin is greater, as Allah, the Exalted, has said. He said, 'So Al-Mahdi said, 'O Ali ibn Yaqteen! By Allah, these are Hashimite fatwas.' I said to him, 'You speak the truth, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful! Praise is for Allah, Who did not remove this knowledge from you, the People of the House.' He said, 'By Allah, Al-Mahdi could not be patient and said to me, 'You speak the truth, O Rafidi (Rejector).'

Some of our companions have narrated in a mursal manner saying: The first thing that was revealed regarding the prohibition of wine is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, "They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, 'In them is great sin and benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.'" When this verse was revealed, the people sensed its prohibition and the prohibition of gambling, and they knew that the sin is something to be avoided, and Allah, Exalted and Glorious, does not impose on them in every way because He said: 'and benefits for people.' Then Allah, Exalted and Glorious, sent down another verse: "Indeed, wine, gambling, idolatry, and drawing lots with arrows are impure acts of Satan, so avoid them that you may succeed. (1)" So this verse was more intense than the first and more forceful in prohibition. Then He made it a third stage with another verse, which was more forceful than the first and second and more intense, as He, Exalted and Glorious, said: "Indeed, Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through wine and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer, so will you not desist? (2)" So Allah, Exalted and Glorious, commanded avoiding it and explained its reasons for which it was prohibited. Then Allah, Exalted and Glorious, clarified its prohibition and revealed it in the fourth verse, along with what these mentioned preceding verses indicated, by His saying, Exalted and Glorious: "Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin, and aggression without right.'" And He, Exalted and Glorious, said in the first verse: "They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, 'In them is great sin and benefits for people.'" Then He said in the fourth verse: "Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin.'" So Allah, Exalted and Glorious, informed that the sin is in wine and other than it, and that it is unlawful. (3) And that is because when Allah, Exalted and Glorious, intends to impose an obligation, He reveals it little by little until He accustoms people's souls to it and they find peace with His command and prohibition regarding it. And this was from the action of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, in a manner of better management for them, closer to them for accepting it, and le

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Kuleyb al-Saydawi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed (the people) and said in his sermon: Every intoxicant is prohibited.'
