Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited wine specifically, so its little and its much is forbidden, just as He prohibited the dead animal, and the blood, and the flesh of the pig; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited the drink from every intoxicant; and whatever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited, then indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited it.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam from his father from Ata' ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited and every intoxicant is wine.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man from the clan of my uncle, and he is a man from your righteous mawla (clients/friends), has instructed me to ask you about al-nabidh, so I should describe it to you.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I shall describe it to you.' Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited; therefore, whatever its large quantity intoxicates, its small quantity is prohibited.' I said, 'So the small quantity of the prohibited substance is made permissible if a large quantity of water is added?' So he responded to him with his palm twice: 'No! No!'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about al-Nabeez, so he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited wine in its essence, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited from the drinks every intoxicant.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Kuleyb al-Asadi who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about al-Nabeez, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people, so he (peace be upon him) said in his sermon: O people! Indeed, every intoxicant is prohibited. Indeed, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, a little of it is prohibited.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about dates and raisins being cooked for Nabeez, so he said: 'No'. And he said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited'. And he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whatever the large quantity of it intoxicates, the small quantity of it is prohibited'. And he said: 'Yeast is not suitable for Nabeez, and it is the turbid (cloudy) substance'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) initiated me one day without my asking him, so he said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every intoxicant is prohibited.' I said, 'May Allah keep you well! Is all of it prohibited?' So he said: 'Yes, even one gulp from it is prohibited.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Ismail, all from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah prohibited the wine, its little and its much, just as He prohibited the dead, the blood, and the flesh of the pig; and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited from the drinks the intoxicant, and whatever the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever its much intoxicates, its little is prohibited.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I sought permission for one of our companions to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he asked him about al-nabidh, so he said: 'It is permissible.' He said: 'May Allah keep you well, I only asked you about the nabidh in which the residue is placed and it boils until it intoxicates.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every intoxicant is forbidden.' The man said: 'May Allah keep you well, for those with us in Iraq say that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) only meant by that the cup that intoxicates.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, a little of it is forbidden.' The man said to him: 'What if we dilute it with water?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and it is not for the water to make permissible that which is forbidden. Fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not drink it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding al-nabeez? For Abu Maryam drinks it, and he claims that you have ordered with its drinking.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Far be it from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that I should order with the drinking of an intoxicant. By Allah, it is something for which I fear the authorities, and nothing else.' Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited, therefore whatever a lot of it were to intoxicate, so a little of it is prohibited.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Amr ibn Marwan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'These people, sometimes I am present with them for the evening meal, and they bring Al-Nabeez after that. If I do not drink it, I fear they will say,

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Ma'bad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abu Khidash from Ali ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn 'Abdah al-Naysaburi who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is the cup of Nabidh and the cup of wine equal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, equal.' I said, 'So the legal penalty (Hadd) in both of them is equal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Equal.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra, from Umar ibn Hanzala who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is your view regarding a cup of an intoxicant upon which water is poured until its normality goes away and its intoxication goes away?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by Allah, and there is no drop which drops into a container except that container must be emptied'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Yazeed ibn Khalifa, and he is a man from the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, who said: I heard him saying, 'I went to Medina, and Ziyad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Harithi was its governor. So I sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), entered, greeted him, and settled in my place. I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I am a man from Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guided me to your love and affection, O People of the Household.' He said to me, 'And how have you been guided to our affection, O People of the Household? By Allah, our love in Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b is scarce.' He said, 'I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! I have a Khurasani slave who works as a bleacher, and he has four fellow countrymen. They invite each other every Friday, and the invitation falls upon one of them, so my slave's turn comes every five Fridays. He prepares Nabidh and meat for them. He said that when they finish eating the food and meat, he brings a bowl, fills it with Nabidh, then brings a clean jug. When he hands it to one of them, he says to him, 'Do not drink until you send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Thus I was guided to your love through this slave.' He said, 'So he said to me, 'Advise him well, and convey greetings from me to him, and say to him that Ja'far ibn Muhammad says to you: 'Look at this drink of yours which you are drinking. If a lot of it intoxicates, do not approach the little of it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden,' and said: 'Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, the little of it is forbidden.' He said, 'So I went to Kufa and conveyed the greetings to the slave from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He wept, then said to me, 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) took such care of me that he conveyed greetings to me?' I said, 'Yes, and he told me to say to you: 'Look at this drink of yours which you are drinking. If a lot of it intoxicates, do not approach the little of it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, the little of it is forbidden,' and he advised me regarding you. Therefo

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Kuleyb ibn Muawiya, who said: Abu Baseer and his companions were drinking Al-Nabeez, breaking it with water. So I narrated that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'And how did the water make permissible the intoxicant? Tell them not to drink from it, neither a little nor a lot.' I said: 'They mention that the approval of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him) makes it permissible for them.' He said: 'And how could the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him) permit the intoxicant, while they do not drink from it, neither a little nor a lot? Refrain from drinking it.' So we gathered in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abu Baseer said to him: 'They have come to us from you with such and such.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'True, O Abu Muhammad! The water does not make permissible the intoxicant, therefore do not drink from it, neither a little nor a lot.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not prohibit wine (khamr) because of its name, but He prohibited it because of its consequence/effect. So whatever produces the effect of wine, it is wine.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mazi (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not prohibit wine for its name, but He prohibited it for its consequence. So whatever has the consequence of wine, it is wine.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from one of our companions, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Why did Allah prohibit the wine?' He said: 'He prohibited it due to its action/effect, and whatever is inherited from its spoiling/decay.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muawiya ibn Hakam, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Why did Allah prohibit the wine?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He prohibited it due to its effects and its spoiling.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muawiya ibn Hukaym, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about al-Nabeez, is it wine? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever increases in excellence (pleasure) upon leaving it, so it is wine.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from one of our companions, from Ibrahim ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Waddah, from Abu Baseer, who said: Umm Khalid al-Abdiyyah came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I was in his presence. So she said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The growling in my stomach is squeezing me.' She asked him about the ailments of women and said, 'The physicians of Iraq have prescribed Al-Nabeez with Al-Suweq for me, and I paused because I recognized your dislike for it, so I wished to ask you about that.' He said to her, 'And what prevents you from drinking it?' She said, 'I have emulated you in my religion, so when I meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, whenever I meet Him, I can tell Him that Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) ordered me and forbade me.' He said, 'O Abu Muhammad! Do you listen to this woman and this question? By Allah, I do not grant you permission for one drop of it, and do not taste from it one drop, for you will regret when your soul reaches here.' And he gestured with his hand to his throat, saying it to her three times: 'Did you understand?' She said, 'Yes.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What wets the needle, dirties a container of water,' saying it to her three times.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halbi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a medicine that was kneaded with wine. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by Allah, I do not like to look at it, so how can I cure myself with it? Indeed, it is in the status of the fat of the swine or the flesh of the swine, and indeed some people cure themselves with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed together, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Amr, from Ibn al-Hurr, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) during the days he came to Iraq, so he said to me: 'Enter upon Ismail ibn Ja'far, for he is ill; look at what his ailment is and describe to me something of the pain he feels.' He said: 'So I rose from his presence and entered upon Ismail, and I asked him about the pain he feels. He informed me of it, and a cure was prescribed for him in which was Nabidh. So he (Ismail) said: 'Nabidh is Haram (forbidden), and we, the People of the Household, do not seek cure with the forbidden (substances).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a medicine kneaded with wine, can we apply it in the eyes from it? So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed in what He forbade is not a healing.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who applies kohl (in the eyes) with a needle from an intoxicant, Allah Mighty and Majestic will apply (in his eyes) a needle from Fire.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah Al-Arjani, from Malik Al-Misma'i, from Qa'id ibn Talha, who asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): About Al-Nabeez being placed in medicine, he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, it is not befitting for anyone to seek healing with the prohibited (substances).'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about kohl that is kneaded with Nabidh (fermented drink), is that permissible? So he said: No.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a medication kneaded with wine, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like to look at it, nor to smell it, so how can I cure myself with it?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dissimulation (applicable) regarding drinking Al-Nabeez'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from someone else, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Is the wiping upon the two socks [done] in dissimulation (taqiyyah)?' He said, 'Dissimulation is not done in three [matters].' I said, 'And what are they?' He said, 'Drinking wine,' or he said, 'Drinking the intoxicant, and the wiping upon the two socks, and Mut'at al-Hajj.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding Al-Nabeez? For Abu Maryam drinks it and claims that you ordered him to drink it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Maryam spoke the truth. He asked me about Al-Nabeez, so I informed him that it is permissible, and he did not ask me about the intoxicant.' He said, then he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the intoxicant, I did not practice dissimulation (taqiyyah) regarding it for anyone, neither authority nor anyone else.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, a little of it is forbidden.' So the man said to him (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! This Al-Nabeez which you permitted Abu Maryam to drink, what is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for my father (peace be upon him), he used to order the servant to bring a cup, put raisins in it, and wash it with a clean washing. Then he put it in a vessel, then poured over it water three or four times its amount. Then he left it at night and drank it during the day, and left it in the morning and drank it in the evening. And he used to order the servant to wash the vessel every three days, lest it become sour. So if you want Al-Nabeez, this is Al-Nabeez.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Ali ibn Abdullah al-Hannat, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from al-Kalbi al-Nassab, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about al-Nabeez, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Permissible.' I said, 'We soak it, so we throw into it the residue (of an intoxicant) and what is besides that.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Shh! Shh! That is the rotten wine.' He (the narrator) said, 'I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so which al-Nabeez do you mean?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The people of Al-Medina complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of the changed water and spoiling of their health. So he (peace be upon him) ordered them that they should be drinking al-Nabeez. So the man from them was instructing his servant that he should make al-Nabeez for him, so he would extend his handful of dates, so he would cast these in the container. So from it, he would be drinking, and from it he would be purifying.' So I said, 'And how much was the number of the dates which was cast?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever a palm could gather.' I said, 'One and two?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Sometimes it was one, and sometimes it was two.' So I said, 'And how much was the capacity of the container of water?' (He (peace be upon him) said): 'What is between forty to eighty, to what is above that?' So I said, 'By the Ratls (A unit of measurement)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ratls by the measurement of Al-Iraq.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from someone else who was present with him, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so I said, 'O maid, give me a drink of water.' So he (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Give him a drink of my Nabeez.' So she came to me with Nabeez made from partially-ripened dates (Busr) in a brass cup. He said, so I said, 'The people of Kufa are not satisfied with this.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is their Nabeez?' I said to him (peace be upon him), 'They put Al-Qa'wa in it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is Al-Qa'wa?' I said, 'Al-Daazy.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is Al-Daazy?' So I said, 'Pressed dates.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The vessel is stained by it until the Nabeez ferments, then it boils, then it intoxicates, so it is drunk.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is Prohibited.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far ibn al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I want to press my belly against your belly.' He said, 'Here, O Abu Ismail,' and he uncovered his belly. I uncovered my belly and pressed it against his. Then he seated me and called for a platter containing raisins, so I ate. Then he began speaking and complained to me about his stomach. I was thirsty, so I fetched water. He said, 'O Maid! Give him a drink from my nabidh.' She brought me nabidh made from partially-ripened dates in a yellow cup. I drank it and found it sweeter than honey. I said to him, 'This is what spoils your stomach.' He said to me, 'These are dates from the charity of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). They are taken in the morning, water is poured over them, the maid soaks them, and I drink them after the meal and throughout the rest of my day. When it is night, the maid takes it and gives it to the people of the house to drink.' I said to him, 'The people of Kufa are not satisfied with this.' He said, 'And what is their nabidh?' I said, 'They take the dates, clean them, and pour Al-Qa'wa over them.' He said, 'And what is Al-Qa'wa?' I said, 'Al-Daazy.' He said, 'And what is Al-Daazy?' I said, 'A grain brought from Basra, which is poured into this nabidh until it boils and intoxicates, then it is drunk.' He said, 'That is prohibited.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I sought permission to enter for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on behalf of one of our companions, so he asked him about al-Nabeez, saying, 'It is permissible.' He said, 'May Allah keep you well, I only asked about the al-Nabeez in which the residue is left, so it boils until it intoxicates.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every intoxicant is forbidden.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about nabidh whose boiling had settled, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden.' He said: And I asked him about the containers, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the pumpkin (container), the asphalted one, and you have added the hantam, meaning the clay, and the asphalted means the bitumen that is in the skin bag and is poured into the mixture to make it better for the wine. He said: And I asked him about the green urns and the lead, so he said: There is no problem with them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he forbade from what intoxicates from the drinks, all of it, and forbade the date husk and the pumpkin Nabidh, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, a little of it is forbidden.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade every intoxicant, so every intoxicant is prohibited. I said to him, 'And what about the containers from which it is made?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the dubba', the muzaffat, the huntam, and the naqir.' I said, 'And what is that?' He said: 'The dubba is the gourd, and the muzaffat is the bitumen-coated vessel, and the huntam are green clay urns, and the naqir are wood which the people of the Pre-Islamic period used to hollow out until they became hollow vessels in which they would ferment Nabidh.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The (grape) juice is not Prohibited until it boils.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Aasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with drinking the grape juice for six days. Ibn Abi Umeyr said, 'Its meaning is, as long as it has not boiled.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about drinking the juice, so he said: 'Drink it as long as it has not boiled. So when it boils, do not drink it.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, which thing is the boiling?' He said: 'The fermentation (transformation into wine).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Zareeh, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the juice simmers or boils, it is Prohibited'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every juice that is hit by fire is prohibited until two-thirds of it goes away and one-third remains.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Haytham, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the juice that is cooked by fire until it boils from its time, so its owner drinks it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it changes from its state and boils, there is no goodness in it until two-thirds of it disappears and one-third remains.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and he had been asked about Al-Tala'a, so he said: 'If it is cooked until two (parts) of it evaporate and one remains, then it is Halal, and whatever is less than that, there is no goodness in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The grape juice, when it is cooked until two-thirds of it evaporates and there remains a third of it, so it is Permissible'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Tala'a (evaporated grape juice) exceeds one-third, it is prohibited.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man from among our non-companions gifted me Bukhtuj.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is from those who consider the intoxicant permissible, do not drink it; and if he is from those who do not consider its drinking permissible, accept it,' or he said: 'Drink it.'
Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar Bin Yazeed, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the vessel is coloured (by the residue), drink it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Bukhtuj, so he said: 'If it is sweet and colors the vessel,' and its owner said: 'Two-thirds of it has gone away and one-third remains, so drink it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man from the people of understanding with the truth who came to me with Al-Bukhtuj (boiled grape juice), and he was saying that he had cooked it upon the third, and I know that he tends to drink upon the half, so shall I drink by his word and he is drinking upon the half? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not drink it'. So I said, 'Suppose it is a man from other than the people of the understanding, from the ones we do not recognise drinking upon the third nor their permitting it upon the half, informing us that with him is Bukhtuj (made) upon the third, the two-thirds of it having evaporated and there remains a third of it. Shall we drink from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man drinks the fermented Nabidh, his testimony is not valid in anything (regarding drinks), even if he were described as being upon the belief that you are upon.

One of our companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Mansur, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Tila' (residue of evaporated grape juice) increases upon the one-third by one Awqiya (a unit of measurement), so it is Prohibited.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about raisins: is it permissible to cook them until their flavor is extracted, then that water is taken and cooked until two-thirds of it evaporates and one-third remains, then it is removed and drunk from it for the year? He said: There is no problem with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who took ten arṭals of grape juice, so he poured twenty ritals of water over it and cooked it until twenty ritals from it evaporated and ten arṭals remained, is the drinking of that permissible or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is cooked upon the third of it, so it is permissible.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Drinking cold water is a greater enjoyment.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), while he was advising a man, said to him: 'Reduce your drinking of water, for it extends every illness; and avoid medication for as long as your body can bear the illness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasir the servant, from al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said: 'There is no problem with drinking water abundantly with food, but do not be excessive with it other than with food.' And he said: 'Do you not see that if a man ate the likes of this' — and he gathered both his hands neither joining them together nor separating them — 'then did not drink water over it, his stomach would burst?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Do not drink water excessively, for indeed it is a source of every illness.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the fermented drink, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is an unknown wine, therefore do not drink it, O Suleyman! If the house was mine or the rule, I would kill its seller and whip its drinker'.

From him, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Madaini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about al-fuqqa' (a fermented drink), so he said: 'It is wine.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Husayn al-Qalanisi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Mazi (peace be upon him) asking him about al-fuqqa' (fermented drink), so he said: 'Do not go near it, for it is from the wine.'
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the fermented drink, so he wrote forbidding me from it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah Al-Qurashi, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdullah Al-Nawfaly, from Zadan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'If I had authority over the markets of the Muslims, I would have removed this wine from them, meaning the fermented drink (fuqaa').

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Jameela Al-Basri who said: I was with Yunus in Baghdad, and while I was walking with him in the market, the owner of the fermented drink opened his container, and it splashed onto Yunus's garment. I saw him become distressed by this until the sun set. I said to him, 'Will you not pray, O Abu Muhammad?' He said, 'I do not wish to pray until I return home and wash this wine from my garment.' I said to him, 'Is this your own opinion or a report you are conveying?' He said, 'Hisham ibn al-Hakam informed me that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fermented drink, and he (peace be upon him) said: Do not drink it, for it is an unknown wine. So if it touches your garment, wash it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm and Ibn Fazzal together, said: We asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about Al-Fuqqa' (a fermented drink), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is forbidden, and it is an unknown wine, and in it is the legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Washa, who said: I wrote to him, meaning Al-Rida (peace be upon him), asking him about Al-Fuqaa'. He said, so he wrote: 'It is prohibited, and it is wine, and whoever drinks it is in the status of the wine drinker.' He said, and Abu Al-Hasan the Last (peace be upon him) said: 'If the house were my house, I would have killed its seller and whipped its drinker.' And Abu Al-Hasan the Last (peace be upon him) said: 'Its legal penalty (Hadd) is the legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a wine which the people have considered trivial.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the drinking of al-fuqqa'?' He said: 'It is an unknown wine, O Suleyman, so do not drink it. Indeed, O Suleyman, if the ruling were mine and the house were mine, I would whip its drinker and kill its seller.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about drinking the fermented drink, so he abhorred it with an intense abhorrence.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad ibn Ismail — similar to it. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Zakariyya Abu Yahya, who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the fermented drink (al-fuqqa'), and I described it to him. So he said: 'Do not drink it.' So I repeated to him all of that, describing it to him as to how it is made. So he said: 'Do not drink it, and do not come back to me regarding it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fermented drink, so he said to me: 'It is wine'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Every intoxicant is prohibited, and every fermented drink is prohibited, and Al-Fuqqa' is prohibited.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the fermented drink. So he wrote: 'It is the wine and regarding it is a legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, or from a man, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) described the cooked drink to me, how it is to be cooked until it becomes permissible, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Take a quarter of raisins, clean them, and pour twelve ratls of water over it, then soak it overnight. So when it is the days of summer and you fear that it will simmer, place it in an oven, a little full, until it does not simmer. Then remove all the water from it until morning, pour upon it water sufficient to submerge it, then boil it until its sweetness is gone.' Then remove the last water and pour the first water over it, then measure all of it and see how much water there is, then measure a third of it and place it in the vessel in which you intend to cook it, and pour water sufficient to submerge it, and measure it with a stick, making its measure a cane or a stick, and mark it at the end of the water. Then boil the final third until the remaining water evaporates. Then boil it by the fire and do not cease boiling it until two-thirds evaporate and one-third remains. Then take for every quarter a ratl of honey, boil it until the foam of the honey goes away and the mist of the honey goes away in the cooked drink. Then strike it with a stick with a strong strike until it mixes, and if you wish to perfume it with something from saffron or with something from ginger, do so. Then drink it, and if you wish for its staying with you to be prolonged, keep it clean.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about raisins, how to cook them so that their drink is permissible. He said: 'Take a quarter of raisins, clean them, then pour twelve ratls of water over them, then soak them overnight. When it is the next day, remove their foam, then pour water over them sufficient to submerge them, then boil them with fire until they boil, then remove their water and pour it over the first water.' Then place it all in one vessel, then light a fire beneath it until two-thirds of it evaporates and one-third remains, with the fire still beneath it. Then take a ratl of honey, boil it with fire until it boils, and remove its foam. Then place it upon the cooked mixture, then stir it until it mixes with it. And if you wish, add saffron to it, and if you wish, flavor it with a little ginger. He said: 'So if you want to divide it into three parts to cook it, measure it with one thing until you know how much it is. Then place the first part in the vessel in which you boil it, then make a measurement and mark it where the water reaches. Then place the other third, then mark it where the water reaches. Then place the final third, then mark it where the last one reaches. Then ignite a gentle fire beneath it until two-thirds of it evaporates and one-third remains.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from the one who informed him, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the rumbling that afflicted me in my stomach and the scarcity of my digestion of food. So he said to me: 'Why do you not take Nabidh which we drink, and it digests the food and removes the rumbling and the winds from the belly?' I said to him: 'Describe it for me, may I be sacrificed for you.' So he said to me: 'Take a Sa' of raisins, so clean its seeds and whatever is in it, then wash it with water with a good washing. Then soak it in an equal amount of water or whatever submerges it. Then leave it in the winter for three days and nights, and in the summer for one day and one night. So when that time is up, you strain it and take its clear liquid and put it in a vessel, and take its measure with a stick. Then cook it gently until two-thirds of it goes away and one-third remains.' Then put half a ratl of honey on it, and take the measure of the honey. Then cook it until that increment evaporates. Then take ginger, Alpinia, cinnamon, saffron, cloves, and mastic resin, and pound them and put them in a thin cloth, and drop it in and boil it with it with a boil. Then take it off. So when it has cooled, strain it and take from it for your lunch and your dinner. He said: 'So I did it, and it removed from me what I was feeling, and it was a pleasant drink. It does not change if it remains, God willing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Al-Sayyari, from the one who mentioned it, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about some pain, and I said, 'The physician has prescribed a drink for me: I take raisins and pour water upon them, two parts water to one part raisins. Then I pour honey upon it, then I cook it until two-thirds of it evaporates and one-third remains.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not sweet?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Drink it.' (The narrator said), 'And I did not inform him how much the honey was.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Makfuf, who said: I wrote to him, meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), asking him about the ginger drink, and the rose water, and the mulberry jam, and the apple jam, and the quince jam, and the pomegranate jam. So he wrote: 'Permissible'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hamdan ibn Suleyman from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Makfouf who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) asking him about drinks that are available to us: sikanjabin, julab, mulberry jam, pomegranate jam, quince jam, and apple jam, when the one who sells them is not an expert, and they are sold in our markets. So he wrote: 'It is permissible, there is no problem with them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from Khaleylan ibn Hisham who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! With us there is a drink called Al-Mayba, made from quince. We peel it and place it in water, then we take the juice and cook it until one-third remains. Then we pound that quince and take its water. Then we take the water of this reduced juice and this quince, and we cast musk, cloves, saffron, and honey into it, and cook it until two-thirds evaporates and one-third remains. Is it permissible to drink it?' So he wrote: 'There is no problem with it, as long as it has not changed.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the vat in which wine is, is it permissible for there to be vinegar or water or kamakh (a type of sauce/condiment) or olives in it? He said: If it is washed, there is no problem. And about the pitcher and other than it in which wine is, is it permissible for there to be water in it? He said: If it is washed, there is no problem. And he said regarding a cup or a vessel in which wine is drunk: Wash it three times. He was asked: Is it sufficient that water is poured into it? He said: It is not sufficient until it is rubbed by the hand and washed three times.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Hafs Al-Awr, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The large jar in which wine has been kept, then it is dried out, and vinegar is made in it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about wine, in which something is done until it acidifies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If that which was done in it is dominant over what was made in it, then there is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about old wine that is turned into vinegar. He said: There is no problem.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who takes wine and makes it into vinegar. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

From him, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about wine being made into vinegar. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if that which overwhelms it is not put into it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Aysama, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and his wives were with him. He said, 'He smelled the scent of the perfume container,' and asked, 'What is this?' They said, 'It is a perfume container in which the hair oil (safflower oil) is placed.' He said, 'Order it to be poured out into the gutter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the meal-table when wine or an intoxicant is drunk upon it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The meal-table is prohibited.' And he (peace be upon him) was asked: 'If a man stands by a set-up meal-table, eating from what is on it, and with the man is an intoxicant, and he did not give it to anyone who is on it to drink afterwards,' so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not prohibited until it is drunk upon it. And if it is placed after it is drunk, [then] the Falouzaj [a sweet drink], so eat it, for it is another meal-table,' meaning: eat the Falouzaj.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ahmad ibn Ismail the scribe, from his father, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was in the Sacred Mosque, and a group from the Quraysh looked at him and said, 'Who is this?' It was said to them, 'The Imam of the people of Iraq.' Some of them said, 'Send one of you to him to ask him.' So a young man from them came to him and said to him, 'O cousin, what is the greatest of the major sins?' He said: 'Drinking wine.' He went to them and informed them, so they said to him, 'Go back to him.' So he went back to him, and he said to him, 'Did I not tell you, O cousin, drinking wine?' He went to them and informed them, so they said to him, 'Go back to him.' They did not cease with him until he went back to him and asked him. He said to him, 'Did I not tell you, O cousin, drinking wine?' Indeed, drinking wine causes its drinker to enter into adultery, and theft, and the murder of the soul which Allah has prohibited, and into associating partners with Allah. And the effects of wine override every sin, just as its tree climbs over every tree.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed ten [people] regarding wine: its planter, its keeper, its seller, its buyer, its drinker, the consumer of its price, its presser, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, and its server.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, raising it from Hafs al-Awr, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I take the rakwah (a type of vessel/pot). They say that if wine is placed in it, and the bukhtuj (fermented drink) is placed in it, it is better for it. So he takes the rakwah, places the wine in it, shakes it, then pours it out. Then he places the bukhtuj in it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was a group of people in the presence of my father, and they differed regarding Al-Nabeez. Some of them said, 'The cup which intoxicates is prohibited.' And some of them said, 'A little of what intoxicates, and its lot is prohibited.' So they referred the matter to my father (peace be upon him). So my father said: 'Do you see the measure (qist)? If not for what is poured into it first, it would be full. And similarly, the other cup, if not for the first one, it would not intoxicate.' He (the narrator) said, 'Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever enters one vein from his veins with a little of what a lot of it would intoxicate, Allah will punish that vein with three hundred and sixty types from the types of punishment.'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Giyas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) disliked that the animals be given wine to drink.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid the false words.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The singing (music).'
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Usama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Singing is the nest of hypocrisy.

From him, from Suleyman ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Sama'ah who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When Adam (peace be upon him) died, Iblis and Qabil rejoiced over him, and they gathered in the earth. So Iblis and Qabil made the musical instruments and amusements as a gloating over Adam (peace be upon him). Thus, everything in the earth from this type, which people derive pleasure from, is indeed from that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying, 'Singing is from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised the Fire for it,' and he recited this Verse: 'And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to lead astray from the way of Allah without knowledge and to take it in mockery. Those will have a humiliating punishment.'

Ibn Abi Umeyr from Mihran bin Muhammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The singing is from what Allah said, And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah’s Way.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who do not witness Al-Zur' — He said: 'Al-Ghina' (singing/music).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I forbid you from the dancing (or music), the flute, and the cups and the drums.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Washa, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about singing. So he said: It is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah’s Way.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Saeed ibn Janaah, from Hammad, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, who said: We lodged in Medina, so we went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said to us, 'Where have you lodged?' We said, 'With so-and-so, the owner of the singing girls.' He said, 'Be honorable.' By Allah, we did not know what he intended by it, and we thought he meant 'Be gracious to him.' So we returned to him and said, 'We do not know what you intended by your saying, "Be honorable."' 'Have you not heard the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by nobly.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! I enter my toilet, and I have neighbors who have slave girls who sing and strike with the oud. Sometimes I prolong my sitting to listen to them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not do it.' The man said, 'By Allah, I do not go to them; it is merely a sound that I hear with my ears.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'For the sake of Allah, have you not heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: Indeed, the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of these will be questioned about?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah! It is as if I had not heard this verse from the Book of Allah from a non-Arab nor an Arab. I will not return to it, if Allah wills, and I seek forgiveness from Allah.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Rise and perform ritual bath, and ask whatever comes to your mind, for you were standing upon a great matter. How evil would your state have been had you died upon that. Praise Allah and ask Him for repentance from everything He dislikes, for He does not dislike except every ugliness, and leave the ugliness for its people, for everything has its people.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Imran al-Za'farani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever Allah favors with a bounty, and he comes at that time of the bounty with a clarinet (mizmar), he has denied it; and whoever is struck by a calamity, and he comes at that time of the calamity with a lamenter (na'ihah), he has denied it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about singing/music, and I said: 'They claim that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the saying: He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying!' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. If We had wanted to take a pastime, We would have taken it from before Ourselves, if We were to do [so]. But We cast the truth against falsehood, so it demolishes it, and thereupon it vanishes. And for you is destruction from what you describe.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to so-and-so from what he described,' [referring to] a man who was not present in the gathering.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinany, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who do not witness Al-Zur,' he said: 'It is Al-Gina' (singing/music).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Usman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Jarir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A devil called Al-Qafandar, whenever in the house of a man a flute is played for forty days, and men come over for it, that devil places every part of his upon a similar part of the owner of the house, then blows into him with a blowing, so he does not care after that until they (the other men) come on to his wives, so he does not care'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'In the house of singing (music), one is not safe from calamity, nor are supplications answered therein, nor do the angels enter it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Harun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The singing gathering is one upon which Allah does not look.' And it is from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah's Way.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, or from someone else, from Abu Dawood al-Mustarriq, who said: Whoever has a flute struck (played) in his house for forty days, Allah will cause a devil called Al-Qafandar to overcome him, so he will not leave any limb of his body parts except that he (the devil) will sit upon it. So when it is like that, modesty will be removed from him, and he will not care what he says, nor what is said about him.

Sahl narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Madainy, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about singing/music, and I was present, so he said: 'Do not enter houses in which Allah is turned away from its inhabitants.'

From him, from Yasser the servant, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: The one who removes himself from singing, then in Paradise there is a tree which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands the winds to stir, so a sound is heard for it the likes of which have not been heard, and the one who does not remove himself from it, will not hear it.

From him, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Kuleyb Al-Saydawi who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Striking the drumsticks grows hypocrisy in the heart just as water grows vegetation.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from his father, from Musa ibn Habeeb, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Allah does not Sanctify a community in which there is clanging by the clarets and its eulogies cause grief.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Jaham ibn Humayd, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Where were you?' So I thought that he (peace be upon him) knew the place, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I was passing by so-and-so, so he withheld me, and I entered into his house and looked at his slave girls.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'That is a gathering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not Look at its inhabitants. May there be safety from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon your family and your wealth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Anbasa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Listening to singing and vanities grows hypocrisy in the heart just as water grows the crop.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Armani, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever listens attentively to a speaker has worshipped him. So if the speaker is conveying from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he has worshipped Allah; and if the speaker is conveying from Satan, he has worshipped Satan.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Yunus, who said: I asked Al-Khurasani (peace be upon him) and said, 'Indeed, Al-Abbasi mentioned that you allow regarding singing (music).' He said, 'The apostate has lied! I did not say to him like this. He asked me about singing, so I said to him, 'A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him about singing. He said, 'O so-and-so, if Allah differentiates between the Truth and the Falsehood, where would singing be?' He said, 'With the Falsehood.' He said, 'So you have judged.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Nard (backgammon) and Al-Shatranj (chess) and Al-Arba'ata 'Ashara (a dice game) are in one status, and everything upon which gambling is played, it is Maysir (gambling).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, altogether, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid false words.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The uncleanness of the idols' is chess, and 'false words' is singing.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Chess and backgammon are both al-maysir (gambling).'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The chess is from the falsehood.

Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, the brother of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for Allah, on every night of the month of Ramadan, are those emancipated from the Fire, except the one who breaks his fast while consuming an intoxicant, or a bickerer, or the owner of the two kings. I said, 'And what is the 'owner of the two kings'?' He said, 'Chess.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about chess, and about the game of youths which is called the game of the Emir, and about the game of the three, so he said: He said: 'Do you see, if the truth were differentiated from the falsehood, with which of these two would it be?' I said: 'With the falsehood.' He said: 'Therefore, there is no goodness in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'Therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid false words.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The uncleanness of the idols is chess, and the false words is singing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul Malik al-Qummi, who said: I and my brother Idris were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). Idris said, 'May we be sacrificed for you, what is al-maysir (gambling)?' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'It is chess (al-shatranj).' I said, 'But people say it is backgammon (al-nard).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And backgammon as well.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Aasim, from Ali ibn Ismail al-Mithammi, from Rabie ibn Abdullah, from al-Fudayl who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about these things which the people play with, the dice and the chess, until I ended up to (mentioning) Al-Suddary (a game). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah were to Differentiate between the truth and the falsehood, in which of these two (categories) would (these games) fall into'. I said, 'With the falsehood'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is it to you with the falsehood'.

Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah forgives during the month of Ramadan except for three: the owner of an intoxicant, or the owner of the two kings (chess), or the bickerer.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Chess is gambling (maysir), and backgammon (nard) is gambling (maysir).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said: A man from the people of Basra came to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom! I sit with a people who play with chess, and I do not play with it, but I just look.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What is it to you and a gathering to which Allah does not look?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about chess, so he said: Leave the Magian thing to its people, may Allah curse it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Abu Ja'far! What do you say about chess (al-shatranj) with which people play?' He said, 'My father Ali ibn al-Husayn informed me from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever speaks, and his speech is for other than the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is vain; and whoever is silent, and his silence is for other than the remembrance of Allah, is heedless.' Then he was silent, so the man stood up and departed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding chess?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who moves it is like the one who moves the flesh of the pig.' So I said, 'And what is upon the one who moves the flesh of the pig?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He washes his hand.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Saeed, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The one familiar regarding the chess is like the one familiar regarding the Fire.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade playing with chess and backgammon (dice).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Drinking water while standing during the daytime is more strengthening and more healthful for the body.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Mahmud, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Drinking water whilst standing during the daytime nourishes the food, and drinking water whilst standing at nighttime causes the yellow water (jaundice).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Hashim ibn Yahya al-Mada'ini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) went to a water container and drank from it while he was standing.

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Abd al-Malik al-Qummi came to him and said: 'May God keep you well! Can I drink water while standing?' He said to him: 'If you so desire.' He said: 'Shall I drink in one breath until I am quenched?' He said: 'If you so desire.' He said: 'May I prostrate with my hands inside my garment?' He said: 'If you so desire.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By God, it is not from this and the likes of it that I fear for you.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), I and my father, so they brought a clay vessel containing water. So he (peace be upon him) drank while standing, then he handed it to my father, and he drank from it while standing. Then he handed it to me, so I drank from it while standing.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn al-'Arzami, from Hatim ibn Isma'il al-Madini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to drink water while standing, then drank from the remainder of his ablution water while standing. Then he turned toward al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'O my son! I saw your grandfather, the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), do like this.'
Three breaths during drinking is better than one breath.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three breaths are better than one breath (whilst drinking).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from some of his companions, from Uthman ibn Isa, from an elder from the people of al-Madinah who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who drinks water without interrupting his breath until he is quenched. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And is the enjoyment (of water) anything other than that?' I said: 'But they say that it is the drinking of the heem (thirsty camels).' So he said: 'They are lying! Rather, the drinking of the heem is that upon which the name of God, Mighty and Majestic, is not mentioned.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man drinks a sip from the water and God, Mighty and Majestic, admits him to Paradise by it. I said: And how is that, O son of the Messenger of God? He said: A man drinks the water, then he stops and puts away the vessel while he still desires it, so he praises God, Mighty and Majestic. Then he returns to it and drinks, then he puts it away while he still desires it, so he praises God, Mighty and Majestic, then he returns and drinks — thus God, Mighty and Majestic, makes Paradise obligatory for him by that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to say when he drank water: 'Praise be to God who gave us sweet and pure water to drink, and did not give us salty and bitter water to drink, and did not hold us accountable for our sins.'

Whenever one of you drinks water, and says 'In the Name of God,' then drinks, then pauses and says 'Praise be to God,' then drinks and says 'In the Name of God,' then pauses and says 'Praise be to God,' then drinks and says 'In the Name of God,' then pauses and says 'Praise be to God' — that water glorifies God on his behalf for as long as it remains in his belly, until it exits.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whenever you want to drink water at night, stir the water and say: 'O water, the water of Zamzam and the water of the Euphrates convey to you their greetings.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to drink from Syrian cups that were brought from Syria and gifted to him (peace be upon him and his family).

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he was drinking from a ceramic cup.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting to drink from vessels of gold or silver.

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Hajar (the Black Stone area), so he asked for water. Then a cup of brass/copper was brought to him. Then a man said: 'Indeed, Abbad ibn Kathir dislikes drinking from brass vessels.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' And he (peace be upon him) said to the man: 'Did you not ask him whether it was gold or silver?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not drink water from the notch of a vessel, nor from its handle, for Satan sits upon the handle and the notch.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Mukram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: My father said to Amr ibn Ubayd, Bashir al-Rahhal and Wasil in a narration: 'Neither drink from the ear (spout/handle) of the pitcher, nor from its crack if there is one in it — for it is a drinking place of the satans.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a group of people who were drinking water with their mouths during the military expedition of Tabuk. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'Drink with your hands, for they are the best of your utensils.'
The Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) used to like drinking from the Syrian vessel, and he used to say: 'It is the cleanest of your vessels.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad — all together from Ali ibn Asbat — from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying, and Egypt was mentioned, so he said: The Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Do not eat in its pottery, and do not wash your heads with its clay, for indeed it removes the sense of protective honour (ghayra) and begets the depravity of pimping (diayatha).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from whoever mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Zamzam used to be whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and it flowed freely. Then it transgressed against the other waters, so God — Majestic and Mighty — resented it and caused a spring of aloe to flow over it.

Zamzam was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'A spring was caused to flow to it from beneath the Black Stone (al-Hijr), so when the water of the spring prevails, the water of Zamzam becomes sweet.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The water of Zamzam is the best water upon the surface of the earth, and the most evil water upon the surface of the earth is the water of Barhout which is at Hadramawt — the souls of the disbelievers come to it at night.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The water of Zamzam is a healing from every illness' — and I think he said: 'Whatever it may be.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The water of Zamzam is a remedy for whatever it is drunk for.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far and others, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah — all together — from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Musadif who said: A man from our brethren fell gravely ill in Mecca until he was near death. We met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on the road, and he said: 'O Musadif, what happened to so-and-so?' I said, 'I left him near death, may I be your sacrifice.' He said: 'Had I been in your place, I would have given him water from the Mizab (the spout of the Ka'bah) to drink.' So we sought it from everyone but could not find any. While we were in this situation, suddenly a cloud appeared with thunder, lightning, and rain. I went to someone in the mosque, gave him a dirham, and took his drinking cup. Then I took water from the Mizab, brought it to him and gave him to drink from it. I did not leave his side until he had drunk sawiq and recovered, and he was cured after that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, regarding the word of the Most High: 'And We send down from the sky blessed water' [Quran 50:9] He said: 'There is no water on earth except that the water of the sky has mixed with it.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Drink water of the sky (rain), for it purifies the body and repels diseases. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby, and remove from you the uncleanness of Satan, and to fortify your hearts and steady (your) footsteps thereby.' [8:11]

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Hail cannot be eaten, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'He afflicts with it whomsoever He wills.' [Quran 13:13]

I do not think anyone is welcomed as a newborn with the water of the Euphrates except that he would love us, the People of the Household. And he (peace be upon him) said: The people of Kufa do not quench themselves with the water of the Euphrates except for a certain matter. And he said: Two water-spouts from Paradise flow into it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There burst into the Euphrates every day bursts from Paradise.

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'This river of yours — meaning the water of the Euphrates — two water-spouts from the spouts of Paradise pour into it.' He (the narrator) said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Had there been miles between us and it, we would have gone to it and sought water from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, raising it (mursal), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'How far is it between you and the Euphrates?' So I informed him. So he said: 'If I were in its presence, I would love to go to it at the two ends of the day.'
