Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, together from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Sa'dan, from more than one person — they traced it back (marfu') to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the people of Kufa — had they performed tahnik upon their newborn children with the water of the Euphrates, they would have been our Shia.

I heard our master Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: Verily, an angel descends from the sky every night carrying three mithqals of musk from the musk of Paradise, and he casts it into the Euphrates. And there is no river in the east of the earth nor in its west with a greater blessing than it.
The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, God is Beautiful and loves beauty, and He loves that He sees the effects of His bounty upon His servant.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it (mursal), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: When God bestows a bounty upon His servant and it appears upon him (with gratitude), he is named a beloved of God who speaks of God's bounty; and when God bestows a bounty upon a servant and it does not appear upon him, he is named the one hated by God, a denier of God's bounty.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Uqba ibn Muhammad, from Salama ibn Muhammad, the cap-seller, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by a man who had raised his voice against a man, demanding something trivial from him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'For how much are you demanding from him?' He said: 'For such and such.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Has it not reached you that it has been said: There is no religion for the one who has no muru'a (magnanimity/dignity)?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When God bestows a bounty upon His servant, He loves to see it upon him, because He is Beautiful and loves beauty.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw a man with dishevelled hair on his head, dirty clothes, and in a bad state. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the Religion is the enjoyment and the manifestation of the Bounty.'
And by this chain, he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The most evil servant is the filthy/obscene one.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Muawiya ibn Wahb who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw me while I was carrying vegetables, so he said: 'It is disliked for a man of magnanimity to carry a lowly thing, lest people become audacious (disrespectful) toward him.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the people are reporting that you possess much wealth. So he said: That does not bother me. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed one day by various people from Quraysh, and upon him was a torn shirt. They said: 'Ali has reached the morning with no wealth for him.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) heard this and ordered the one in charge of his charitable endowments to gather his dates and not send anything to anyone, and to store them. Then he said to him: Sell them to the first buyer then the next, and convert them into dirhams; then put them where you store the dates and press them in where they cannot be seen. He said to the one who maintained the store: When I call for the dates, go up and look at the money; then strike it with your foot as if you do not intend the dirhams, until you scatter them. Then he sent to one of those men to invite them. Then he called for the dates. When the man climbed up and was descending with the dates, he struck with his foot and the dirhams were scattered. So they said: 'What is this, O Abu al-Hasan?' He said: 'This is the wealth of the one who has no wealth.' Then he instructed regarding that wealth and said: 'Look for the deserving ones of every household to which I used to send; look at its amount and send it to them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, raising it (mursal), said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed I dislike it for the man that a bounty from God be upon him, yet he does not manifest it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Let one of you adorn himself for his Muslim brother just as he adorns himself for the stranger whom he loves to see in the best appearance.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Fazzal, all together from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, who said: It reached Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that Talha and Al-Zubayr were saying, 'Ali has no wealth.' He said, 'So that was grievous upon him, so he ordered his representatives to gather his harvest until when a year passed, they came to him, and they had gathered from the price of the harvest one hundred thousand dirhams.' So it was displayed in front of him, and he sent for Talha and Al-Zubayr, and they came to him. He said to them both, 'This wealth, by Allah, is for me, there is no share for anyone else in it,' and it was verified in their eyes. He said, 'So they left from his presence, and they were saying, 'Indeed, he has wealth.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, and Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, some people in Al-Madina said, 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) has no wealth.' So Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent for a man in Al-Madina, borrowed a thousand dirhams from him, and sent it to the collector (of khums/charity), saying, 'This is the charity of our wealth.' So they said, 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) would not have sent this from himself except that he indeed has wealth.'

From him, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazam ibn Hakeem, from Abdul-A'ala, the freedman of the family of Saam, who said: Indeed, the condition of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) became severe until the people of Al-Madina were discussing it. So that reached him, and he designated a thousand Dirhams, then sent them to the governor of Al-Madina and said: 'This is the charity of my wealth.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Abu Hashim, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves beauty and beautification, and hates misery and wretchedness.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Ubayd ibn Ziyad: 'The manifestation of the bounty is more beloved to Allah than its maintenance, so beware that you should not be outfitting except in the best of outfits of your people.' He said, 'So Ubayd was not seen except in the best of outfits of his people until he died.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasser, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Buy Khazz for yourself, and if you wish, Washy.' I said: 'All of the Washy.' He said: 'And what is the Washy?' I said: 'That which does not contain cotton. They say it is Haram.' He said: 'Wear that which contains cotton.'
From him, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Al-Husayn ibn Salim Al-Ijli, that Al-Washy was brought to him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The man should not wear silk and brocade except during the battle.

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Lays Al-Murady, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) clothed Usamah ibn Zayd with a silk garment (hullah), so he went out wearing it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wait, O Usamah! Indeed, it is worn by the one who has no manners (khalaq) for him, so distribute it among your women.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the wearing of silk and brocade, so he said: 'As for during the battle, there is no problem with it, even if there were images in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not correct for the man to wear silk except during the battle.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He disliked wearing the shirt hemmed with brocade, and disliked wearing silk, and wearing embroidered qassi (fine linen/cotton), and disliked wearing the red cushion cover (mitharah), for it is the cushion of Iblis.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban al-Ahmar from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The wearing of silk and brocade is not permissible (for men), so as for selling them, there is no problem.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The women wear silk and brocade, except in the state of Ihram.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas ibn Musa, from his father who said: I asked him about Al-Abbas ibn Musa asked him (peace be upon him) about Al-Ibrisam and Al-Qazz. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are both the same.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with wearing silk (al-qazz) when its warp or its flesh (weft/body) is mixed with cotton or flax.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said: Al-Hasan ibn Qiyama asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the garment seamed with silk and cotton, where the silk is more than half; can one pray in it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to have gowns from it like that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'at, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not befitting for the woman that she should wear the pure silk while she is in Ihram, and as for during the heat and the cold, so there is no problem.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Basheer, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ahmasy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Saeed asked him about the qamis (gown), and I was in his presence, its warp being of silk: 'Can one wear it?' He was feeling cold, so he instructed him to wear it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the garment in which there is silk, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is mixed in it, then there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And your garments purify,' he said: 'Roll them up.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdullah ibn Yaqoub, from Abdullah ibn Hilal who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me to buy him an izar (lower garment). So I said to him, 'I could not find except for the extensive ones.' He said: 'Cut off from it and hem it.' He (the narrator) said, 'Then he said: My father said: And whatever exceeds the two heels, so it is in the Fire.' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub – similar to it.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Aban, from Abu Hamza, raising it (to the Imam), said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) looked at a youth who had let his garment hang low, so he said: 'O my son! Raise your garment, for it is more lasting for your clothes and more cleansing for your heart.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wore the shirt, he extended his hand; and when it reached the tips of the fingers, he cut it off.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do you want me to show you the shirt of Ali (peace be upon him) in which he was struck, and show you his blood?' I said, 'Yes'. So he called for it, and it was in a basket. He took it out and spread it, and behold, it was a shirt of Qarabis cloth, resembling Al-Sunbulani. The place of the pocket down to the ground had blood, which was white like milk, resembling a stroke of the sword. He said: 'This is the shirt of Ali (peace be upon him) in which he was struck, and this is the trace of his blood.' So I measured its body with the span, and it was three spans, and I measured its lower part with the span, and it was twelve spans.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said: I saw the shirt of Ali (peace be upon him) in which he was killed, in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Its lower part was twelve shibr, and its body (main part) was three shibr, and I saw blood splashes in it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from a man, from Salma the seller of caps, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered upon him. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son! Will you not purify your shirt?' So he went, and we thought that something had touched his garment. So he returned and said: 'It is like this.' So we said: 'May Allah make us your ransom, what is the matter with his shirt?' He said: 'His shirt was long, and I instructed him to shorten it.' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And your garments, purify.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Abdul-Hamid Al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at a man who had worn a shirt that touched the ground, so he said: 'Is this not a clean garment?'
From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the man who drags his garment, he said: 'I dislike that he resembles the women.'

From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He called for a garment, measured it, and took five cubits from it, then cut it. Then he measured its width as six shibars (open-palm widths). Then he split it and said, 'Stitch its sides and trim its edges.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who wears a new garment. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should say: O Allah, make it a garment of bounty and piety and blessing. O Allah, grant me in it the goodness of worshipping You, and an action in obedience to You, and the discharge of gratitude for Your favor. The praise is for Allah, Who clothed me with what I cover my nakedness with and beautify with among the people.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Uthman, from Khalid al-Jawwan, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is befitting for one of you, when he wears a new garment, to pass his hand over it and say: All praise is to Allah, Who clothed me with what I cover my nakedness with, and beautify myself with among people, and adorn myself with among them.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever recites 'We have indeed revealed it' thirty-two times in a new vessel, and sprinkles his new garment with it when he wears it, he will continue to eat in ease (plentifully) as long as a thread from it remains.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: When Allah, the Exalted, clothes the believer with a new garment, let him perform ablution and pray two cycles, reciting in them the Mother of the Book (Al-Fatiha), the Verse of the Chair (Ayat al-Kursi), and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Al-Ikhlas), and 'We have revealed it' (Al-Qadr). Then let him praise Allah, who veiled his nakedness and adorned him among the people. And let him frequently say, 'There is no might and no power except with Allah,' for he does not disobey Allah in it, and for him, for every thread in it, is an angel who sanctifies Allah for him, seeks forgiveness for him, and beseeches mercy for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I intended to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I put on my clothes and spread out a new pallium (cloak) that I was fond of. A camel squeezed me on one of the paths, so it tore from every side, and I was saddened by that. So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he looked at the pallium and said to me: 'What is the matter? I see you as torn.' So I informed him of the story. So he said: 'O Umar! When you wear a new garment, say: 'There is no god except Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' you will be free from misfortune. And when you love something, do not mention it frequently, for that is from what crushes you. And if you have a need from a man, do not insult him from behind (in his absence), for Allah will place that in his heart.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The lowest form of extravagance is discarding the remnants of the vessel, and wearing out the protective clothing, and throwing away the cores.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleyman ibn Salih, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the lowest form of extravagance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Your degrading your protective garment, and pouring out the remainder from your vessel, and eating the dates and discarding the pits here and there.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Al-Fadl ibn Kathir Al-Madainy, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One of his companions entered upon him and saw upon him a shirt with a patch that had been sewn onto it, so he kept looking at it. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is the matter with you, that you are looking?' He said: 'A patch attached in your shirt.' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Strike your hand to this book and read what is in it.' And in front of him was a book, or near to him. So the man looked in it, and there was in it: 'There is no faith for the one who has no shame, nor any wealth for the one who has no esteem, nor anything new for the one who does not have (anything) old for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who wears a turban and does not let one end hang in front and the other at the back, so an illness strikes him and there is no cure for it, so he should not blame anyone except for himself.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hammam, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Musawwimin' (Marked/Signs). He said: 'The turbans. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wore a turban and let it hang from in front of him and from behind him, and Jibraeel (peace be upon him) wore a turban and let it hang from in front of him and from behind him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There were white, loose turbans upon the Angels on the Day of Badr.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali Al-Uqayli, from Ali ibn Abi Ali Al-Lahbi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) put the turban on Ali (peace be upon him) with his hand, so he let it hang from in front of him and shortened it from behind him by the measure of four fingers. Then he said: 'Turn around,' so he turned. Then he said: 'Face me,' so he faced. Then he said: 'This is how the crowns of the angels are.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever goes out from his house wearing a turban beneath his chin, intending a journey, will not be affected during his journey by theft, nor by burning, nor by misfortune.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Isa ibn Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who wears a turban and does not wrap it beneath his chin, and a pain strikes him for which there is no cure, let him not blame anyone except himself.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to wear the Yemeni caps, the white ones, the quilted ones, and the ones with two ear-covers during battle, and his turban was the 'Sahab', and he had a 'Burnus' which he would wrap himself in.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to wear a white quilted cap, and he used to wear in battle a cap that had two ear-coverings.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Make for me white caps and do not break them, for the Master like me does not wear the broken one'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Take a cap for me and do not make it dyed (single-colored), for the Master like me does not wear it, meaning do not break it (into multiple pieces).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The wearing of new shoes is a protection for the body and an aid to prayer and purity.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The first one to take to the sandals was Ibrahim (peace be upon him).
And by this chain, it was said, Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who takes to a sandal, so let it be a good one.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not wear the mals (flat shoes), for they are the footwear of Pharaoh, and he was the first to adopt the mals.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I detest the man if I do not see him with his heel-covers on his sandals.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Usman, from a man, from Minhal, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and upon me was a sleek sandal, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a shoe (footwear) of the Jews'. So Minhal went and took a knife, so he (made a) curve in the middle with it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Hasan ibn al-Zibrqan al-Ansari, who said: Is'haq al-Hadda' told me, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent for me while we were in Mina: 'Come to me, and with you are your tools.' So I went to him in his tent, greeted him, and he responded and gestured for me to sit. So I sat down. Then he took a new sandal and threw it to me. When I wanted to leave, I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! If you were to gift me this sandal, I could replicate it.' So he threw the other one to me and said, 'One? What benefit can it give you?' He said, 'And it was such that it has a support for the heel, narrow from its middle, and for it were two straps, and for it were heads. So he said: This is the footwear of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'.

From him, he said: Dawud ibn Ishaq Abu Suleyman al-Hazza’ narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz from Taym al-Ribaab, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I dislike the man if I see in his leg a sandal that is not narrowed (at the instep). Indeed, the first one to change the shoe-style of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was So-and-so.' Then he said: 'What do you call this shoe-style?' I said: 'Al-Mamsouh.' He said: 'This is Al-Mamsouh.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Suwayd, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) looked at me, and upon me were two sandals that had been wiped (mamsuhat). He took them and turned them over, then said to me, 'Do you intend to be like a Jew?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, a person gifted them to me.' He said, 'So there is no problem.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father used to lengthen the soles of his sandals.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Abu Imran, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He (peace be upon him) looked at a sandal with its strap tied, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) took it, untied it, and then said: 'Do not tie (it).'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said: I was walking with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so the strap of his sandal broke. I took out a strap from my sleeve and he repaired his sandal with it. Then he struck his hand on my left shoulder and said: 'O Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir! Whoever supports a believer upon the strap of his sandal, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will carry him upon a red camel when he emerges from his grave until he knocks at the door of Paradise.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yaqoub al-Sarraj, who said: We were walking with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he wished to console a relative of his due to the death of a child. The strap of the sandal of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) snapped, so he took his sandal from his foot, then walked barefoot. Ibn Abi Yaf'ur looked at him, so he took off his own sandal from his foot, untied the strap from it, and handed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He turned away from it as if he were displeased, then refused to accept it, then said: 'Indeed, the owner of the calamity is most deserving of patience over it.' So he walked barefoot until he entered upon the man to whom he had come to offer condolences.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Abbas ibn Aamir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he went to a man, took off his sandal, then said: 'Take off your sandals, for the sandal, when it is taken off, gives rest to the two feet'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he looked at one of his companions, and upon him was a black sandal, so he said: 'What is your reason for the black sandal? Do you not know that it harms the vision, and it slackens the manhood, and it is more expensive in price than others, and none wear it except he swaggers (pompously) in it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and in my leg was a black sandal, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hanaan! What is it to you and the black? Do you not know that in it are three characteristics? It weakens the vision, and slackens the manhood, and inherits the worries, and along with that, it is an apparel of the tyrants'. So I said, 'So what shall I wear from the sandals?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon you with the yellow, for therein are three qualities – It polishes the vision, and intensifies the manhood, and wards off the worries, and along with that, it is from the apparels of the Prophets (peace be upon them)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sayyari from Abu Suleiman al-Khawwas from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn from Sadir al-Sayrafi who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and upon me was a white sandal. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadir! What is this sandal? Did you wear it knowingly?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you!' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who enters the market intending a white sandal, will not wear it out until he acquires wealth from where he does not expect.' Abu Nu'aym said, 'Sadir informed me that he did not wear out that sandal until he acquired one hundred dinars from where he did not expect.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Buraed ibn Muhammad al-Ghadiri, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw me, and I was wearing black sandals. So he said: 'O Ubayd, what is it with you and the black sandals? Do you not know that in them are three characteristics: they slacken the manhood, weaken the vision, and they are more expensive in price than others. And indeed, a man wears them while he possesses only enough for his family and children, so Allah resurrects him as a tyrant.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever wears a yellow sandal will be in delight until he wears it out.

From him, from one of our companions, it reached Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever wears yellow sandals will not cease to look with delight as long as they are on him, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Yellow is its color, giving delight to the beholders.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Suleyman ibn Sama'ah, from Dawood al-Hazza', from Abdul Malik ibn Bahr, the companion of Al-Lu'lu', who said: Whoever intends to wear a sandal and a yellowish one (gradually turning to white) falls to him, he will not be deprived of wealth and children; and whoever falls to him a black one, he will not be deprived of grief and anxiety.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Salama ibn Abi Habba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Wearing the socks increases the strength of the vision.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Awsy, from Abu Ja'far Al-Musly, from Suleyman ibn Sa'd, from Mani', who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Wearing the socks is a security from tuberculosis.'
From him, from one of our companions, from Mubarak, the slave of Al-Aqarquqi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Habitual wearing of the socks is a security from the tuberculosis.

From him, from one who mentioned it, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I went out with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) to Yanbu'. So when he came out, I saw red socks upon him, so I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What is this, the red socks which I see to be upon you?' So he said: 'Socks which I have taken for the journey, and it is more lasting upon the clay, and the rain, and more load-bearing for it'. I said, 'So shall I take it and wear it?' He said, 'As for during the journey, so yes, and as for during the present, so do not change anything with the black'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn al-Munthir, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). And upon me was a pair of decorated socks (khuff), so he said: 'O Ziyad, what is this sock that I see upon you?' I said, 'A sock that I have taken.' So he said: 'Do you not know that the white [socks] are from the footwear, meaning the decorated ones, from the attire of the tyrants (jababirah), and they are the first to adopt it; and the red [socks] are from the attire of the Caesars, and they are the first to adopt it; and the black [socks] are from the attire of the Banu Hashim, and [it is] a Sunnah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The clean garment suppresses the enemy.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) wore al-Taq (a cap), and al-Saj (a cloak), and al-Khamais (striped woolen garments).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever acquires a garment, let him keep it clean.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Can a believer have ten shirts?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Twenty?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Thirty?' He said: 'Yes. This is not extravagance. Extravagance is when you use your best-preserved garment as your everyday work wear.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', who said: I heard al-Ridha (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to wear two garments in the summer, both purchased for five hundred dirhams.

Amir al-Mu'mineen (peace be upon him) sent Abdullah ibn al-Abbas to Ibn al-Kawwa' and his companions, and upon him (Ibn al-Abbas) was a thin shirt and a garment. When they looked at him, they said: 'O Ibn Abbas! You are the best among us in our own eyes, yet you wear such clothing?' He replied: 'And this is the first matter I dispute with you:' [7:32] Say: Who has forbidden the adornments of God which He has brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? And He said: [7:31] Take to your adornments at every mosque.

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while wearing a khazz coat and a khazz pallium. He looked at me, so I said: 'May I be your ransom! Upon me is a khazz coat and a khazz pallium — what do you say about it?' He said: 'And what is the problem with khazz?' I said: 'And its warp is silk (ibraysam).' He said: 'And what is the problem with silk? For indeed al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was struck down while upon him was a khazz coat.' Then he said: 'Indeed, when Abdullah ibn Abbas — when Amir al-Mu'mineen (peace be upon him) sent him to the Khawarij to confront them — he wore the best of his garments, perfumed himself with the best of his perfumes, and rode the best of his mounts. Then he went out and confronted them. They said: O Ibn Abbas! Even though you are the best of the people, you have come to us in the garments of tyrants and their mounts!' So he recited to them this verse: 'Say: Who has forbidden the adornments of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions?' So wear (fine garments) and beautify yourself, for Allah is Beautiful and He loves beauty — but let it be from the permissible.

Sufyan al-Thawri passed by in the Sacred Mosque and saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) wearing many expensive and fine clothes. He said: 'By God, I will go to him and rebuke him.' So he approached him and said: 'O son of the Messenger of God! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not wear such clothing, nor did Ali (peace be upon him), nor did anyone from your forefathers.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was in a time of scarcity and financial straitness, and he used to take according to his straitness and his means. But the world after that has released its floodgates of abundance, and the most deserving of its people with it are its righteous ones.' Then he recited: 'Say: Who has forbidden the adornments of God which He brought forth for His servants and the good provisions?' 'And we are the most rightful of those who take from it what God has granted. However, O Thawri, what you see on me of clothing — I wear it only for the people.' Then he grasped Sufyan's hand and drew it toward himself, then raised the upper garment and showed a rough cloth beneath it against his skin. He said: 'This I wear for myself, and what you saw is for the people.' Then he pulled at Sufyan's upper garment — its outer layer was thick and coarse, and its inner part was soft. He said: 'You wore this outer garment for the people, and you wore this one for yourself, to please it.'

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whilst I was in the tawaf (circumambulation), suddenly a man grabbed my garment, and he was Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri. He said: O Ja'far ibn Muhammad! You are wearing the likes of these clothes, while you are in this sacred place, along with the rank you hold from Ali (peace be upon him)? So I said: It is a Furqubi (Egyptian linen) garment I bought for one dinar. Ali (peace be upon him) lived in an era when what he wore was appropriate for that time, and if I were to wear the likes of that attire in our time, the people would say: This one is a show-off like Abbad.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has ten shirts and rotates between them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

And by this chain, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'There happen to be three shirts for me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' So he did not cease (numbering) until it reached ten. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do they not make each other last longer?' I said, 'Yes, and were I to wear one, it would last for a little (while).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the affluent man who acquires many clothes, new ones, the pallium (a type of cloak), and many shirts, preserving one set by another, beautifying himself with them. Would he be considered extravagant? He said: No, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Let him who has abundance spend out of his abundance.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was leaning upon me, or he said, upon my father, so Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri came upon him, and upon him were Mervian clothes that were beautiful. He said, 'O Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)! You are from the People of the Household of the Prophethood, and your father was [such and such], so what are these Mervian clothes upon you? If only you would wear [something] besides these clothes.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Woe be unto you, O Abbad! Who has prohibited the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions? Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He bestows a favor upon His servant, loves that He sees it upon him. There is no problem with it. Woe be unto you, O Abbad! I am but a part of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so do not hurt me.' And it was so that Abbad wore two Qatary clothes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Cleanliness of the clothes removes anxiety and grief, and it is a purifier for the prayer.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I was present in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man said to him: 'May Allah improve you! You mentioned that Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) used to wear coarse clothing, wearing a shirt for four dirhams, and something similar to that, and we see upon you good clothing.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Indeed, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) wore that in an era where it was not disputed, and if he were to wear the like of that today, he would be known/defamed by it. So the best of clothing for every era is the clothing of its people, except that our Qaim (peace be upon him), when he rises, will wear the clothing of Ali (peace be upon him) and walk in his way.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if there happen to be twenty shirts for the man.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: From the Sunnah is taking off the left sock before the right, and wearing the right before the left.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When one of you wears his sandal, let him wear the right one before the left, and when he takes it off, let him take off the left one before the right one.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not walk in one shoe. I said, 'And why?' He said, 'Because if you are hit by the touch of Satan, it would barely separate from you except what Allah so Desires.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever walks in one shoe, a touch of Satan strikes him, and it does not leave him except what Allah wills.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), from Ali (peace be upon him) that he used to walk in one shoe and repair the other, and he did not see any problem with that

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The ring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was of silver. I said to him, 'Was there a stone in it?' He said, 'No.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: From the Sunnah is wearing the ring.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, who said: The stone (in the ring) should be circular. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is how the ring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to be.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not wear a ring [for sealing] other than silver, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The palm is not purified wherein is a ring of iron'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not place a ring of gold in your hand.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about wearing a ring in the right hand, and I said, 'I saw the Banu Hashim wearing rings in their right hands.' So he said: 'My father wore rings in his left, and he was superior to them and more knowledgeable.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about the ring being worn in the right hand, so he said: 'If you wish, [wear it] in the right hand, and if you wish, [wear it] in the left hand.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not wear a ring except for a short while, until he left it.
And by this chain, (He) said: ‘Ali, and Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) were wearing rings in their left hands.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Hatim ibn Ismail, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) used to wear rings on their left hands.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) used to wear their rings on their left hands.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to wear his ring on his right hand.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: They evaluated the ring of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so my father took it from them for seven. I said, 'Seven dirhams?' He said, 'Seven dinars.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: The carnelian negates poverty, and wearing the carnelian negates hypocrisy.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam al-Tanukhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Adorn yourselves with the carnelian (aqiq), for it is blessed, and whoever adorns himself with the carnelian, it is likely that goodness will be decreed for him.'

From him, from one of his companions, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Fuzayl ibn Uman, from Rabi'a al-Ra'y who said: I saw in the hand of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) an embedded stone of carnelian, so I said, 'What is this stone?' So he said: 'Roman carnelian'. And he said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who wears a ring with the carnelian, his needs would be fulfilled'.
From him, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Prophet or Imam), said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The carnelian is a safety during the journey'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The one who takes a ring whose stone is carnelian will not be impoverished, and judgment will not be passed for him except with that which is better.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Sayaba ibn Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abdul Raheem al-Qasir, who said: The governor sent for a man from the progeny of Abu Talib regarding a felony. He passed by Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Follow him with a carnelian ring.' So a carnelian ring was brought to him, and he did not see any abhorrence in it.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, raising it, said: A man complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that his way had been cut off (by bandits), so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Why did you not wear a ring with the carnelian, for it is a protection from every evil.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Wear rings with rubies, for they remove poverty.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Adorn yourselves with rubies, for they remove poverty.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from a man from our companions, and he was Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl, and he was nicknamed Sikbaj, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, the owner of the hostels, and he used to manage some of the affairs of the Imam (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me one day and dictated to me from a book: 'Wearing a ring of emerald is ease, there is no difficulty in it.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Dahqan Ubaydullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Wear rings with rubies, for they remove poverty.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is desirable (recommended) to wear a ring with a ruby.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: 'The one who wears a ring with the turquoise, would not impoverish his palm'.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from al-Hasan ibn Sahl, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mihran, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), and on his finger was a ring with a turquoise stone, engraved with 'Allah al-Malik'. I kept looking at it, so he said: 'What is the matter with you, that you keep looking at it?' I said: 'It has reached me that there was for Ali, Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), a ring with a turquoise stone, engraved with 'Allah al-Malik'.' He said: 'Do you recognize it?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'This is it. Do you know the reason for it?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'This is a stone that Jibra'il (peace be upon him) gifted to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gifted it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). Do you know its name?' I said: 'Turquoise.' He said: 'This is in Persian. So what is its name in Arabic?' I said: 'I do not know.' He said: 'Its name is Al-Zafar.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ubayd ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Wear rings with Yemeni onyx, for it repels the plots of the rebellious devils.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Ali ibn Muhammad, known as Ibn Wahba al-Abdasi, and it is a town from the towns of Wasit, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The best of the stones (for rings) is the crystal.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The engraving of the ring of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was 'Muhammad, Messenger of Allah', and the engraving of the ring of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was 'Allah, the King', and the engraving of the ring of my father (peace be upon him) was 'The Honour is for Allah'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Yunus ibn 'Abyan and Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We said: 'May we be sacrificed for you, is it disliked that a man should write in his ring other than his own name and the name of his father?' He said: 'In my ring is written: Allah is the Creator of all things; and in the ring of my father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and he was the best of the Muhammads I saw with my own eyes, is written: The Honour is for Allah; and in the ring of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is written: The Praise is for Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent; and in the ring of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is written: Allah is Sufficient for me; and in the ring of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) is written: Allah is the King.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so he brought out to us the ring of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and the ring of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). And it was inscribed on the ring of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'You are my trusted one, so protect me from the people.' And the engraving of the ring of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was: 'Allah is sufficient for me,' and in it was a rose and a crescent in its upper part.

From him, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the engraving on his ring and the ring of his father (peace be upon him). He said: 'The engraving on my ring is: Whatever Allah willed, there is no strength except by Allah; and the engraving of my father's ring is: "Allah is Sufficient for me," and it is that which I used to wear with.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: It was (inscribed) upon the ring of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Disgraceful and wretched is the murderer of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)'.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Wasil ibn Suleyman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: We mentioned the ring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Would you like for me to show it to you?' So I said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him) called for a sealed covering, opened it, and brought it out in a piece of cotton. Behold, it was a silver ring, and in it was a black stone, upon which were inscribed two lines: 'Muhammad, Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the stone of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was black.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid from Abu Al-Hasan the Second (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'We have been narrated in the hadith that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would clean himself (with stones/water) and his ring was on his finger, and similarly the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did that. And the engraving of the ring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was: Muhammad (peace be upon him) the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'They spoke the truth.' I said, 'So should we do it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, those people were wearing their rings on the right hand, and indeed you are wearing your rings on the left hand.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I was silent, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know what was the engraving of the ring of Adam (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'No.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' And the engraving of the ring of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was: Muhammad the Messenger of Allah; and the ring of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was: Allah the King; and the ring of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was: The Honour is for Allah; and the ring of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was: Indeed Allah will fulfill His command; and Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) [wore] the ring of his father; and Abu Ja'far al-Akbar [wore] the ring of his grandfather Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); and the ring of Ja'far (peace be upon him) was: Allah is my Guardian and my protection from His creation; and Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) [wore]: Allah is Sufficient for me; and Abu Al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him) [wore]: Whatever Allah willed, there is no strength except with Allah.' And Al-Husayn ibn Khalid said, 'And he extended his hand to me and said: 'My ring is also the ring of my father (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who engraves upon his ring the Name of Allah, let him withdraw it from the hand with which he cleans himself during the ablution.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the gold with which children are ornamented, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to ornament his children and his women with gold and silver.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, all from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the gold with which children are ornamented, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, my father (peace be upon him) used to ornament his children and his women with gold and silver, so there is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the adornment of women with gold and silver, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The scabbard of the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and its handle were of silver, and between that was a ring of silver. And I wore the armor of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and it dragged, and therein were three silver rings in front of it and two at the back of it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with encircling the sword with the gold and the silver.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with ornamenting the Qur'ans and the swords with gold and silver.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The women have not ceased to wear the ornaments.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Rabi', from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a bed in which is the gold, is it correct to keep it in the house? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was of gold, so no, and if it was the water of the gold, so there is no problem'.

A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Rib'i from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a bed that has gold in it; is it proper to keep it in the house? He said: 'If it is [made of] gold, then no [it is not proper/lawful]; and if it is 'water of gold' (gold-plated), then there is no harm [in keeping it].'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Saeed ibn Janaah, from Abu Khalid al-Zaydi, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A group of people came to al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We see in your dwelling things we dislike.' And in his house were rugs and cushions. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'We marry women, so we give them their dowries, and they buy whatever they wish. There is nothing for us from it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Malik al-Juhani, from Abdullah ibn Ata'a, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and saw in his house rugs, pillows, patterns (carpets/rugs), and amenities (furnishings). So I said, 'What is this?' He said, 'The belongings of the wife.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There used to be for Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) cushions and patterns with images therein. He used to sit upon these.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan al-Zayyat, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a refurbished room. Then I returned to him the next day, and he was in a room in which there was nothing except a mat, and upon him was a coarse shirt. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The room which you saw was not my room. Rather, it is the room of the wife, and yesterday was her day.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ali ibn Ismail al-Mithammi, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while he was sitting upon a chattel (carpet/furnishing), so I began to touch the chattel with my hand. He said: 'This which you are touching with your hand, is Armenian.' I said to him: 'And what have you to do with the Armenian?' He said: 'This is a chattel which the mother of Ali, a wife of his, brought with her.' So when it was another time, I entered upon him and began to touch what was beneath me. He said: 'It is as if you want to see what is beneath you.' I said: 'No, but the blind tend to tamper (or feel around).' He said to me: 'That chattel was for the mother of Ali, and she used to hold the opinion of the Khawarij, so I kept her for a night until morning, that she might retract from her opinion and accept the Wilayah of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), but she refrained from me. So when it was morning, I divorced her.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: A speaker said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The man sits upon a rug in which are images.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The non-Arabs venerate it, and we belittle it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the silk mattress and the like of it from brocade, and the silk prayer mat and the like of it from brocade, is it permissible for the man to sleep on it, recline upon it, and pray? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He may spread it out, stand upon it, but not prostrate upon it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said: Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih asked me to seek permission for him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). So I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of this, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Tell him to come to us whenever he wishes.' So I brought him in to him at night, and Shihab was wearing a head covering. A cushion was placed for him, so he sat on it. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Remove your veil, O Shihab, for the veil is a source of doubt (or suspicion) by night and a sign of humility (or disgrace) by day.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When the hoods that are left behind (or neglected) appear, adultery will appear.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dihqan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), that he used to say: Folding the clothes is their resting, and it is more lasting for them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I went out intending to visit Dawud ibn Isa ibn Ali, who was staying at Bi'r Maymoun. I was wearing two coarse garments. I saw an old woman with two young slave girls, so I said, 'O old woman, are these two girls being sold?' She said, 'Yes, but the likes of you cannot buy them.' I said, 'Why?' She said, 'Because one of them is a singer and the other is a musician.' So I entered upon Dawud ibn Isa, and he raised me up and seated me in his place. When I left his presence, he said to his companions, 'Do you know who this is? This is Ali ibn Musa, whom the people of Iraq claim has obligatory obedience (due to him).'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he disliked wearing the burtala (a deep cape)

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at a mattress in the house of a man and said: 'There is a mattress for the man, and a mattress for his family, and a mattress for his guest, and a mattress for the Satan.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Tayalisi, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who wears trousers whilst seated would not get groin pain.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ali al-Qummi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The expansiveness of the shirt (garment) and the growth of hair in the nose is a safety from leprosy. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Have you not heard the words of the poet: 'And you will not see my shirt except as wide of the collar and the sleeves'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Alawi, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'From the honor (mur'uah) of a man is that his mounts/beasts be plump (siman)'. He (the narrator) said, 'And I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Three (things) are from the honor: the agility of the animal, and the beauty of the face of the slave, and the enjoyable mattress (fursh al-sari)'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Not one of you should touch the clothes of the one who has not worn them yet'.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah Jabala al-Kinani, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) met me while I was dangling a fish in my hand, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Throw it away! I dislike for the eminent man that he should carry the humble thing by himself.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'You are a people whose enemies are many; the creation has been hostile to you, O group of Shiah, the creation has been hostile to you. Therefore, adorn yourselves to them with what you are able to do.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates the notoriety/ostentation of clothing.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is sufficient disgrace for a person that he wears clothing by which he is defamed, or rides an animal which defames him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Fame — its good and its evil — is in the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Sa'id, from al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever wears clothes that make him notorious, God will clothe him on the Day of Resurrection in a garment from the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: I was with Abu Alqama, Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, and Abu Hassan in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Alqama had dyed [his beard] with henna, Al-Harith had dyed with woad (black dye), and Abu Hassan did not dye. Each of them said to him, 'What do you think of this? May Allah have mercy on you,' while gesturing towards his own beard. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'It is beautiful.' They said, 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to dye with woad?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, that was when he married the Saqafiyya; her slave girls took him and dyed him.'

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woad (a dyeing plant), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it for the old man, the aged'.
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The woad loosened my molars.'

From him, from his father, from Yunus, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about dyeing with the woad (a dyeing plant), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem. Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed and he (peace be upon him) was dyed with the woad.'

From him, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Dyeing with black is pleasing to the women and inspires awe in the enemy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Henna increases the water (juice/sap) of the face and increases grey hair.
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The henna ignites the greying.'

From him, from Ubdous ibn Ibrahim al-Baghdadi, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Henna removes the odour, increases the moisture of the face, aromatises the breath, and improves the offspring.'

From him, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from Malik ibn Ashyam, from Ismail ibn Bazi' who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'For me there is a young daughter whose regularity (of menstruation) is lifted.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Dye her head with the henna so the menstruation would be returning to her.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I did that, so the menstruation returned to her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Three (things): one who recognizes these would not leave them – cutting the hair, and rolling up of the clothes, and copulating with the slave-girls.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said to me: 'Cut your hair completely, so that its smell, its insects, and its dirt decrease, and your neck thickens, and your vision clears. And in another report: 'And your body rests.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Our companions report that shaving the head, other than for Hajj or Umrah, is mutilation (muthlah). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), when he fulfilled his rituals, would turn to a town called Sayah and shave (his head).'

Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The people say that shaving the head is a mutilation.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is an Umrah for us and a mutilation for our enemies.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Umar ibn Aslam, who said: The cupper performed cupping on me and shaved from the site of the fovea (the puncture mark). So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saw me and said: 'What is this? Go and shave your head.' He said: 'So I went and shaved my head.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding lengthening the hair?' He said: 'The companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) were hairy (mush'irin), meaning the trimming (al-tamm).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sa'dan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I shave every Friday from the first trimming to the second trimming.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Sometimes there is much hair on the back of my neck, which causes me intense grief.' He said to me, 'O Is'haq! Do you not know that shaving the back of the neck removes the grief?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas al-Baqbaaq, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has abundance (of hair), should he part it or leave it? So he (peace be upon him) said: He should part it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever grows hair, let him take good care of it or trim it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Ayoub ibn Harun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) part his hair?' He said, 'No. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when his hair grew long, it reached the lobe of his ear.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from 'Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'They are reporting that the parting (styling) is from the Sunnah.' He said, 'From the Sunnah?' I said, 'They are alleging that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) parted (his hair).' He said, 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not part, nor did the Prophets (peace be upon them) keep (long) hair.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is the parting of the hair from the Sunnah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No.' I said, 'So did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) part (his hair)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' I said, 'How is it that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) parted (his hair) and it is not from the Sunnah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The one who is hit by what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was hit by, parts just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) parted, so he has attained the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); otherwise, no.' I said to him, 'How is that?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was turned away from the House (the Kaaba), and he had brought the sacrificial animal and was in Ihram, Allah showed him the vision which Allah had informed him of in His Book, when He says: "Certainly Allah had endorsed to His Messenger the vision with the truth: You shall enter the Sacred Masjid, if Allah Pleases, in security, having your heads shaved and having your hair cut, you shall not be fearing."' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) knew that Allah would fulfill for him what He had shown him. From then on, he preserved the hair that was on his head when he was in Ihram, awaiting its shaving in the Sanctuary, where Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had promised him. So when he shaved it, he did not repeat the preservation of the hair, nor was that (preservation) from before him (peace be upon him and his family).
