Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) pluck his two cheeks and line his beard.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, all from al-Wassa, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abi Khadeejah, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whatever exceeds from the beard beyond the fist, so it is in the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the extent of the beard, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Clutch the beard with your hand and trim what remains.'
From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan al-Zayyat, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) having lightened his beard.

From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from one of his companions, from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and the barber was plucking from his beard, so he said: 'Curve it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, from the Sunnah is that you take (pluck/cut) from the moustache until it reaches the edge (of the lip).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: We mentioned the plucking from the moustache, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a good display, and it is from the Sunnah'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abdullah ibn Usman, that he saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) He trimmed his moustache until he pressed it against the palate.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whatever increases upon the fist, so it is in the Fire – meaning the beard.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let not one of you lengthen his moustache, for indeed Satan takes it as a hiding place to conceal himself by.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man with a long beard passed by the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What is wrong with this one? If only he had adjusted his beard.' So that reached the man, so he adjusted his beard to be between the two beards (medium length). Then he entered upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So when he (peace be upon him and his family) saw him, he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Like this, so keep doing it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samit, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The clean garment suppresses the enemy, and the oil removes anguish, and combing the head removes illness.' I said, 'And what is illness?' He said, 'The fever.' And combing the beard strengthens the teeth.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Muhammad ibn Ishaq from 'Ammar al-Nawfali from his father who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Combing removes the fever (al-waba'), and for Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) there was a comb in the mosque with which he would comb himself whenever he finished from his prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan ibn Asim, from his father, who said: I entered upon Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and in his hand was an ivory comb with which he combed himself. So I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! There are some among us in Iraq who claim that it is not permissible to comb with ivory.' He said, 'And why? For there used to be from my father (peace be upon him) one or two combs of ivory.' Then he said, 'Comb with ivory, for ivory removes the illness (fever).'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) combing with an ivory comb, and I had bought it for him.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the ivory, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it, and indeed I have a comb from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nadr ibn Ishaq, from Anbasa ibn Sa'id, raised the hadith to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: Frequent combing of the head removes the illness (fever), brings the livelihood, and increases in copulation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Take your adornment at every Masjid.' He said: 'From that is combing at every Prayer.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Ibn Mayyah, from Yunus, from the one who informed him, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: When you comb your head and your beard, then wipe the comb upon your chest, for it removes the worry and the illness (fever).
From him, from his father, he said: Frequent combing reduces the phlegm.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who combs his beard seventy times, and enumerates it one by one, the Satan would not come near him for forty days.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Walid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the bones of the elephant, its oils, and its combs. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Trimming the nails prevents the greatest illness and brings about livelihood.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Trimming the nails on the day of Friday ensures protection from leprosy, vitiligo, and blindness; and if you do not need to trim them, then file them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Suleyman, from his uncle Abdullah ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Take (pluck/cut) from your moustache and your nails every Friday. If there is nothing to take, then file them. Insanity will not befall you, nor leprosy, nor vitiligo.'
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Trimming the nails and removing the moustache every Friday is a protection from vitiligo and insanity.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from Ibn Uqba, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: From the Sunnah is the trimming of the nails.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Hama, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Clip the nails, for they are the resting-place of the Satan, and from them comes forgetfulness.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The most veiled and most concealed (place) from where Satan overcomes a son of Adam is that he settles underneath the nails.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali al-Hannat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'What is the reward for the one who trims his moustache and clips his nails every Friday?' He said, 'He remains purified until the next Friday.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Talhah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Trimming the nails, clipping the moustache, and washing the head with the khitmah (a type of plant) every Friday removes poverty and increases livelihood.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, who said: A man said to Abdullah ibn Al-Hasan, 'Teach me something regarding sustenance.' He said, 'Stick to your prayer mat when you have prayed Al-Fajr until the sun rises, for it is more effective in seeking sustenance than traveling in the land.' I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of this, so he said, 'Shall I teach you regarding sustenance what is more beneficial than that?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Trim your moustache and your nails every Friday.'

From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said: I went to Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and said, 'Teach me a supplication for livelihood.' He said, 'Say: O Allah, manage my affairs and do not let anyone other than You manage my affairs.' I presented it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said, 'Shall I guide you to what is more beneficial than this for livelihood? Clip your nails and your moustache every Friday, even if by filing them.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Khalaf who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saw me in Khurasan while I was complaining about my eyes, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I point you to something that if you do it, your eye will not complain?' So I said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Take from your nails every Thursday.' He said: 'So I did it, and I did not complain about my eye until the day I informed you.'

From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from his father and his uncle together, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is habitual in clipping his nails every Thursday, his eye will not suffer from conjunctivitis.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to the men: 'Clip your nails', and to the women: 'Leave them, for it is an adornment for you'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, raised it regarding clipping the nails, begin with the little finger of the left hand, then end with the right hand.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Ibn al-Qaddah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Revelation was withheld from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so it was said to him, 'The Revelation has been withheld from you.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'And how can it not be withheld while you do not clip your nails and do not clean your palms?'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem with cutting the grey hair, and plucking it, and cutting it is more beloved to me than plucking it.
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem with cutting the grey hair and plucking it from the beard.

And by this chain, He (peace be upon him) said: The first one to be grey-haired was Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He said: 'O Lord, what is this?' So He said: 'A radiance and a reverence.' He said: 'Lord, increase for me from it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The people did not become grey-haired. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw grey hair in his beard, so he said: 'O Lord, what is this?' He said: 'This is reverence/grace.' So he said: 'O Lord, increase me in reverence/grace.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Ayoub al-Madainy, from Suleyman al-Ja'fary, from al-Rida, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: Grey hair in the front part of the head is a blessing, and in the two sides is generosity, and in the top is courage, and in the back is inauspiciousness.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wear the white, for it is better and purer, and enshroud your deceased in it.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wear white, for it is better and purer, and enshroud your dead in it.'

I transported Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for the second time to al-Kufa, while Abu Ja'far al-Mansur was stationed there. When he drew near to al-Hashimiyya — the city of Abu Ja'far — he withdrew his foot from the stirrup, dismounted, called for a grey mule, and dressed in white garments and a white skullcap. When he entered upon him, Abu Ja'far said to him: 'You have likened yourself to the Prophets.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied: 'And how can you distance me from the descendants of the Prophets?' He then said: 'I had resolved to send to Medina someone who would uproot its palm trees and take its offspring captive.' He (the Imam) said: 'And why is that, O Commander of the Faithful?' He replied: 'It has been reported to me that your servant al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays is calling people to you and gathering wealth for you.' He (the Imam) said: 'By God, that is not the case.' He said: 'I will not be satisfied with you unless you swear by divorce, emancipation, sacrifice, and pilgrimage on foot.' He (the Imam) said: 'Are you commanding me to swear by rivals besides God? Truly, the one who is not satisfied with God has no part with God in anything.' He said: 'Are you teaching me jurisprudence?' He (the Imam) replied: 'And how can you distance me from jurisprudence, when I am the son of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'Then I shall bring you face to face with the one who informed against you.' He (the Imam) said: 'Do so.' The man who had informed against him came forward. Abu Abdillah said to him: 'O you!' He said: 'Yes, by God — Who, there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful — I indeed did it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Woe to you! You are glorifying God so that He would be too ashamed to punish you. But say: I disavow the might and power of God, and I rely upon my own might and power.' The man swore by that, and before he could finish the oath, he fell down dead. Abu Ja'far said to him (the Imam): 'I will never give credence to anyone against you henceforth.' And he treated him generously and sent him on his way.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Wear the cotton garments, for they are the attire of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and it is our attire.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Suleym al-Farra', from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to apply kohl with antimony when he went to his bed, once, once.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) showed me an iron needle (kohl applicator) and a kohl container made of bone, and he said: 'This was for Abu Al-Hasan, so apply kohl with it,' and I applied kohl.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The kohl (eyeliner) applied at night benefits the eye, and it is an adornment by the day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from his father and his uncle, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Applying kohl with antimony (ithmid) aromatises the breath and strengthens the edges of the eyes'.
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The kohl freshens the mouth.

From him, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from the one who mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The kohl (eyeliner) grows the hair, sharpens the vision, and assists in prolonged prostration.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The kohl (antimony) clears the vision, promotes hair growth, and removes tears.
Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The kohl (eyeliner) increases in copulation.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ahmad ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aasim, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who sleeps upon antimony (kohl) that is not secured (with musk or similar) will be safe from the black water (blackness in the eyes) forever, as long as he sleeps upon it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Kohl grows the hair, dries the tears, freshens the saliva, and clears the vision.

From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to apply kohl before sleeping: four times in the right eye and three times in the left.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'From the character/manners of the Prophets (peace be upon them) is the Siwak (brushing teeth with a twig)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed together, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Brushing the teeth (using the miswak) is from the Sunnah of the Sent Prophets.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) did not cease to advise me with the siwak (brushing of the teeth) to the extent that I feared being toothless and with thin teeth'.
And by this chain – he said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: The brushing of the teeth is a cleansing for the mouth and a Pleasure of the Lord.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Hasan ibn Bahr from Mihzam Al-Asadi said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: In the Siwak (brushing the teeth) are ten qualities: Cleansing for the mouth, and a Pleasure of the Lord, and a happiness for the Angels, and it is from the Sunnah, and it strengthens the gums, and polishes the vision, and it removes the phlegm, and removes the cavities.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In the Siwak (brushing the teeth) are twelve qualities: It is from the Sunnah, and a cleansing for the mouth, and a polishing for the vision, and it pleases the Lord, and it removes the phlegm, and it increases in memorization, and it whitens the teeth, and it multiplies the good deeds, and it removes the cavities, and it strengthens the gums, and it makes the food desirable, and the Angels are happy with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The siwak (brushing of teeth) removes the tear (from the eyes) and polishes the vision.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) advised me with the siwak (brushing teeth) to the extent that I feared for my teeth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Marzaban ibn al-Nu'man, raising it, said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What is the matter that I see you all with yellow teeth? What is the matter with you that you are not brushing your teeth?'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the bequest of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to the Commander of the Faithful (may Allah's prayers be upon him): 'Upon you is the Siwak (brushing the teeth) for every prayer.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not enter the bathhouse except with a loincloth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Suleiman al-Ja'fari, who said: I was sick to the extent that my flesh wasted away, so I visited Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: 'Would you be pleased if your flesh were to return to you?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Frequent the bathhouse intermittently, for it will cause your flesh to return. And beware of making it a habit, for habitual bathing causes tuberculosis (consumption).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not enter the bathhouse unless there is something in your stomach to extinguish the heat of the stomach with, and it is stronger for the body, and do not enter it while you are filled with food.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, all from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, who said: I, my father, my grandfather, and my uncle entered a bathhouse in Medina, and there was a man in the dressing room. He said to us, 'From whom are the people?' We said, 'From the people of Iraq.' He said, 'And from which part of Iraq?' We said, 'We are Kufans.' He said, 'Welcome to you, O people of Kufa. You are wearing clothes and are without a towel.' Then he said, 'What prevents you from using the loincloth? For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The nakedness of the believer upon the believer is prohibited.' He said, 'He sent a cloth to my father, so he tore it into four pieces. Then each one of us took one, and we entered into it. When we were in the hot room, he turned towards my grandfather and said, 'O elderly man, what prevents you from dyeing (your beard)?' My grandfather said to him, 'I was with someone who was better than me and you, and he did not dye.' He said, 'He became angry because of that, to the extent that we recognized his anger in the bathhouse.' He said, 'And who is that who is better than me?' He said, 'I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and he did not dye.' He said, 'So he bowed his head and sweat poured out, and he said, 'You have spoken the truth and been righteous.' Then he said, 'O elderly man, if you dye, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had dyed, and he was better than Ali (peace be upon him). And if you leave it, then for you is the Sunnah of Ali (peace be upon him).' He said, 'When we exited the bathhouse, we asked about the man, and it was Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and with him was his son Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I entered the bathhouse with Abu Baseer, and I looked at Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); he had waxed (his body hair) and his two armpits had been waxed with Al-Noura. So I informed Abu Baseer, and he said, 'Guide me to him so I may ask him about it.' I said, 'I have seen him.' He said, 'You have seen him, but I have not seen him' (for he was blind). 'Guide me to him.' So I guided him to him, and he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! My guide informed me that you have waxed and waxed your armpits with Al-Noura.' He said, 'Yes, O Abu Muhammad! Plucking the armpits weakens the vision. Wax, O Abu Muhammad.' He said, 'I have waxed a few days ago.' He said, 'Wax, for it is purifying.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man from the Banu Hashim, who said: I entered upon a group from the Banu Hashim and greeted them in a dark room. One of them said, 'Greet Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), for he is in the center.' So I greeted him and sat in front of him and said to him, 'I have desired to meet you for a while to ask you about certain things.' He said, 'Ask whatever comes to you.' I said, 'What do you say regarding the bathhouse?' He said, 'Do not enter the bathhouse except with a loincloth, and lower your gaze, and do not wash from the used water of the bathhouse, for in it is washed the adulterer, and the son of the adulterer, and the hostile one (Nasibi) towards us, the People of the Household, and he is the worst of them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, who said: Whoever wants to gain flesh (weight), let him enter the bathhouse one day and be absent from it one day; and whoever wants to slim down and is of much flesh, let him enter the bathhouse every day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who applies al-nurah (a hair removal paste), so he makes for himself a mixture of fine flour with oil to paste with it, so he wipes with it after the al-nurah to remove its smell from himself. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

And in another Hadith of Abdul Rahman, he said, 'I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and he had massaged with flour mixed with oil. So I said to him, 'The people are disliking that'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about massaging with flour after the bath (noura), so he said: 'There is no problem.' I said: 'People allege that it is extravagance.' So he said: 'There is no extravagance in that which improves the body. Indeed, I sometimes order the pure [flour] to be mixed for me with oil, so I massage with it. The extravagance is only in that which consumes wealth and harms the body.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who applies oil and massages himself with oil and flour, he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

Ali narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We travel and do not have bran with us, so we rub ourselves with fine flour.' He said, 'There is no problem. The spoilage is in what harms the body and wastes wealth. As for what improves the body, it is not spoilage. I sometimes order my slave to prepare for me pure flour with oil, so I rub myself with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) came out of the bathhouse, put on his clothes and wrapped his turban. He said to me: 'When you come out of the bathhouse, wear a turban.' He (the narrator) said: 'So I did not leave off wearing the turban when coming out of the bathhouse, in winter or in summer.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Indeed, let not one of you lie down fully reclined in the bathhouse, for it melts the fat of the kidneys, and let him not rub his feet with the clay/rough stone, for it causes leprosy.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abdullah ibn Muskan who said: We were a group of our companions, and we entered the bathhouse. So when we went out, we met Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said to us: ‘Where are you coming back from?’ So we said to him, ‘From the bathhouse’. So he said: ‘May Allah purify your bathing’. So we said to him, ‘May we be sacrificed for you’. And we went with him until he entered the bathhouse. So we sat around (waiting) for him until he came out. So we said to him, ‘May Allah purify your bathing’. So he said: ‘May Allah clean you all’.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, raising it, said: Indeed, al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) went out from the bathhouse, and a man came across him, so he said, 'May your istihmamuk (bathing) be good.' He said, 'O dimwit, and what are you doing with the 'ist' here?' He said, 'May your hameemuk (perspiration) be good.' He said, 'Do you not know that al-hameem is the perspiration?' He said, 'May your hammamuk (bathhouse) be good.' He said, 'And when my hammam is good, so what is for me? But say, 'May it be purified what is good from you, and may it be good what is purified from you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ismail ibn Yasar, from Uthman ibn Affan al-Sadusi, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the bathhouse, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you want the bathhouse?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) ordered the bathhouse to be warmed, then entered and wore an izar (garment), covering his knees and navel. Then he ordered the owner of the bathhouse to anoint what was outside the izar, then said: 'Go out from me'. Then he (peace be upon him) anointed what was underneath it with his own hand, then said: 'Thus, do it'.
Sahl raised it (in the chain) and said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so that he would look at his nakedness'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not wash your heads with Egyptian clay, for it removes the self-esteem and inherits the despicability'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said: The private part (awrah) consists of two parts: the front (qubul) and the back (dubur). As for the back, it is covered by the two buttocks. So when you cover the penis and the two testicles, you have covered the private part. And he said in another report: As for the back, the two buttocks have covered it, and as for the front, cover it with your hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from someone else, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The looking at the private part of the one who is not a Muslim is like looking at the private part of the donkey.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the man uncover himself when the water is poured, so his private parts are seen, or is the water poured over him, or does he see the private parts of others? He said: My father disliked that from everyone.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not let his wife go to the bathhouse.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not send his wife to the bathhouse.

From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Reciting the Quran in the bathhouse and copulation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Did Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) forbid reciting the Quran in the bathhouse?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, he only forbade a man from reciting while he is naked. As for when he has an izar (loincloth) on, there is no problem.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem for the man to recite the Quran in the bathhouse if he intends thereby the Face of Allah, and he does not want to look at how (good) his voice is.

One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Do not lie down in the bathhouse, for it melts the fat of the two kidneys.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazeed from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar from one who narrated to him that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was saying: The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not enter the bathhouse except with a loin cloth. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Ja'far from one of his men from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so he would look at his nakedness.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the parents that they should look at the private part of the children, and it is not for the children that they should look at the nakedness of the parents.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed the onlooker and the one looked at in the bathhouse, without a trouser.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered the bathhouse, so the owner of the bathhouse said to him, 'Shall I empty it for you?' He said, 'I have no need for that; the believer is more modest than that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan from Abu Basir who said: Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) entered the bathhouse, and the owner of the bathhouse said to him, 'Shall I vacate it for you?' He said, 'There is no need for that. A believing person is lighter (less burdensome) than that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Clipping the nails, trimming the moustache, and washing the head with the hibiscus plant removes poverty and increases sustenance.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Washing the head with the hibiscus (khitmah) every Friday is a safety from vitiligo and insanity.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Washing the head with the hibiscus removes the dirt and eliminates the filth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever trims his moustache, clips his nails, and washes his head with the hibiscus on the day of Friday, he is like the one who emancipated a slave.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Sayrafi, from Ismail ibn Abdul Khaliq, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Washing the head with the hibiscus is an advertisement (of beauty).

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Mansur ibn Buzraj, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Washing the head with the sidr (lotus/jujube) brings livelihood with a strong bringing.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ubayd ibn Yahya al-Thawri al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) with the manifestation of Islam and the Revelation appeared, he saw the scarcity of the Muslims and the abundance of the Polytheists. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was deeply grieved. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent to him Jibreel (peace be upon him) with a lotus from the Lotus Tree (Sidrat al-Muntaha). So he washed his head with it, and his grief was removed by it.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleym al-Farra', who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'An-nurah is a cleanser (purifier).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said: I entered the bathhouse with Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said to me: 'O 'Abd al-Rahman, get waxed.' I said: 'I only got waxed a few days ago.' He said: 'Get waxed, for it is a cleansing (tahur).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered the bathhouse and I wanted to exit from it, so he said: 'O Muhammad! Did you not get waxing done?' So I said: 'I did apply with it a few days ago'. So he said: 'But do you not know that it is a cleansing?'
From him, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Nahiki, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Cast off the hair from yourselves, for it beautifies.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said: I was with him guiding him, so I entered the bathhouse and saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) applying Noura. So Abu Baseer approached him and greeted him, so he said: 'O Abu Baseer, apply Noura.' He said, 'I only applied it first thing yesterday, and it is the third day.' So he said: 'Do you not know that it is a cleanser? So apply it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Noura is an advertisement (of beauty) and a cleanser for the body'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I love for the believer to remove unwanted hair every fifteen days.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ahmad ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn al-Minqari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Sunnah regarding the Noura is every fifteen days, so if twenty days come upon you and it is not with you, then borrow upon Allah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: It was said to him, 'Some people claim that Al-Noura is disliked on the day of Friday.' So he said, 'It is not where you are going. Which cleanser is more purifying than Al-Noura on the day of Friday?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not leave his pubic hair for more than forty days, and it is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to leave that from her for more than twenty days.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn Tha'labah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: One application of lime paste in the summer is better than ten in the winter.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar from al-Sayyari, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who wishes to apply the lime paste (al-Noura), let him take some of the al-Noura with his finger, smell it, and place it on the tip of his nose, and say: May Allah send blessings upon Sulayman ibn Dawud, just as He ordered us regarding the al-Noura, the al-Noura will not burn him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzyefa ibn Mansur, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to apply lime paste to the pubic area and what is beneath the kidneys, every Friday.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zureyq ibn al-Zubayr, from Sadeyr, that he heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever says, when he applies the lime paste (for hair removal): 'O Allah, make good what is clean from me, and purify what is good from me, and replace for me with clean hair that does not disobey You. O Allah, I have purified myself seeking the Sunnah of the Messengers, and seeking Your pleasure and Your forgiveness, so prohibit my hair and my skin from the Fire, and purify my creation, and make good my character, and purify my deeds, and make me from those who meet You upon the upright, tolerant religion of Ibrahim, Your friend, and the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), Your beloved and Your Messenger, acting by Your laws, following the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), holding fast to it, being well-educated by the excellence of Your education, and the education of Your Messenger, and the education of Your Guardians, whom You nourished with Your education, and planted wisdom in their chests, and made them mines for Your knowledge, may Your blessings be upon them.' Whoever says that, Allah will purify him from the filth in the world and from the sins, and replace for him with hair that does not disobey Allah, and Allah will create for every hair from his body an angel who glorifies Him for him until the Hour is established, and indeed one glorification from their glorifications equals one thousand glorifications from the glorification of the people of the earth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let not one of you prolong the hair of his armpit, for indeed Satan takes it as a hiding place to conceal himself with it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'dan who said: I was with Abu Baseer in the bathhouse, so I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) waxing his armpit, so I informed Abu Baseer of that, so he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Which is preferable, plucking the armpit or shaving it?' So he said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Plucking the armpit frails or weakens (the shoulders). Shave it'.

One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht al-Basri, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi al-Bilad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mihran, all from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, who said: We were in Medina, and Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. So I said, 'Shaving it is preferable,' and Zurara said, 'Plucking it is preferable.' So we sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he permitted us while he was in the bathhouse waxing; he had already waxed his armpits. So I said to Zurara, 'Do you suffice with that?' He said, 'No, perhaps he did this for what is not permissible for me to do.' He said, 'In what are you?' So I said, 'Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it; I said shaving is preferable, and he said plucking is preferable.' He said, 'You have hit the Sunnah and Zurara erred. Shaving it is preferable to plucking it, and waxing it is preferable to shaving it.' Then he said to us, 'Go and get waxed.' We said, 'We did that three days ago.' He said, 'Repeat it, for waxing is a cleanser.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to enter the bathhouse, so he would wax his armpit alone when he was in need of that alone.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: It has reached me that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would sometimes enter the bathhouse deliberately to wax his armpit alone.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said: The perfume (or pleasant scent) is from the etiquettes of the Prophets.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Asama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The perfume is from the Sunnah of the Messengered Prophets.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and I was with Abu Baseer, so I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and he (peace be upon him) was saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The fragrance of the perfume strengthens the heart and increases in the copulation'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: It is not befitting for a man to leave the perfume (on himself) on any day, so if he is unable to do so, then (on) one day and (skip) one day, so if he is unable (to do that), then (on) every Friday, and he should not leave it (completely).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The perfume in the moustache is from the character/mannerisms of the Prophets (peace be upon them) and a prestige/honor for the scribes (Recording Angels).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The perfume strengthens the heart.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: 'The one who applies perfume at the inception of the day, his intellect would not cease to be with him up to the night.' And he said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'A prayer performed whilst perfumed is superior to seventy prayers without perfuming.'
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas ibn Musa, who said: I heard my father saying: 'The perfume is from the Sunnah of the Sent (Prophets)'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three (things) were given to the Prophets (peace be upon them): perfume, wives, and the siwak (tooth-stick).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Furat, from Ali ibn Matar, from al-Sakan al-Khazzaz, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is a right upon every adolescent male during every Friday to trim his moustache and his nails, and to touch himself with something from the perfume; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever it was the day of Friday and there was no perfume with him, would call for one of the headscarves of his wives, moisten it with water, then place it upon his face.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The place of prostration of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was recognized by the pleasant scent of it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'My beloved Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said to me: Apply perfume one day, and one day do not, and the day of Friday is inevitable from it, and do not neglect it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let one of you apply perfume on the day of Friday, even if it is from a flask of his wife.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, raising it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Uthman ibn Mazoun said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'I have intended to leave the perfume and certain things that he mentioned.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not leave the perfume, for the angels inhale the scent of the perfume from the believer, therefore do not leave the perfume on every Friday.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The perfume in the moustache is from the character of the Prophets (peace be upon them) and a prestige for the Scribes.
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, raising it, he said: Whatever you spend on perfume, it is not extravagance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The perfume of women is that which displays its color and hides its smell, and the perfume of men is that which manifests its smell and hides its color.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Suleyman ibn Muhammad al-Khash'ami, from Ishaq al-Taweel al-Attar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to spend on perfume more than what he used to spend on food.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who rejects the perfume. He said: 'It is not befitting that he rejects the prestige (or honor/gift).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought anointing oil, and he used to anoint himself. So he anointed and said: 'We do not reject the perfume.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Jahm, who said: I entered upon Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), so he brought out to me a perfume box containing musk and said: 'Take from this.' So I took something from it and applied it. He said: 'Refine it (apply more) and put some in your chest.' I said: So I took a little from it and put it in my chest. He said to me: 'Refine it.' So I took from it again, and something remained in my hand. He said to me: 'Put it in your chest.' So I did. Then he said: 'Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: No one refuses the prestige except a donkey.' I said: 'What is the meaning of that?' He said: 'The perfume, and the pillow,' and he listed other things.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not reject the perfume and the sweets.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Maysara, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utayba who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he was in a furnished room, wearing a damp shirt and a dyed sheet, the effects of the dye showing on his shoulders. So I began looking at the room and looking at his appearance. He said: 'O Hakam! What do you say about this?' I said: 'And what could I say while I see it upon you? Among us, only the reckless young man does this.' He said to me: 'O Hakam! Who has forbidden the adornments of God which He brought forth for His servants and the wholesome things of provision?' [Quran 7:32] And this is from what God has brought forth for His servants. As for this room you see, it is the ladies' chamber, and I am recently wed. My room is the one you know.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them both) who said: There is no problem with wearing the safflower-dyed (clothing).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Zurara who said: I saw upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) a saffron-dyed garment, and he said: Indeed I have married a woman from Quraysh.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade me from wearing the clothes of notoriety, and I am not saying he forbade you all from wearing the saffron-dyed and vibrant-colored garments.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The intensely dyed (vibrant-colored) garment is disliked, except for the bride/groom.
Via Sahl ibn Ziyad, Muhammad ibn Isa, al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, and Jarrah al-Mada'ini: Abu Ja'far (AS) said: Indeed we wear the saffron-dyed garments and the vibrant red-dyed ones.

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and upon him was a red sheet, new, intensely red. So I smiled when I entered, and he said: 'It is as if I know why you laughed — you laughed at this garment which is upon me. The Thaqafi woman compelled me to it, and I love her, so she compelled me to wear it.' Then he said: 'We do not pray in this, nor should you pray in the fully saturated, blood-red dyed garment.' He (the narrator) said: Then I entered upon him and he had already divorced her. He said: 'I heard her disavowing from Ali (peace be upon him), so there was no leeway for me to keep her while she disavows from him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to wear the dyed (saffron-colored) and the radiant (bright) clothes.

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had a Wars-dyed sheet that he would wear among his family until it turned against his body. And he (the narrator) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'We used to wear dyed clothing at home.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Our dye is Al-Bahraman, and the dye of the Banu Umayya is saffron.
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said: I saw a blue pallium upon Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him).
Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: I saw a seed-shaped cloth upon Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan Al-Zayyat Al-Basri, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and I had a companion with me, and behold, he was in a room with padded walls, and upon him was a pink sheet, and he had trimmed his beard and applied kohl. So we asked him about some matters. When we arose, he said to me, 'O Hassan!' I said, 'At your service.' He said, 'When it is tomorrow, come to me, you and your companion.' So I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' When it was the next day, I entered upon him, and behold, he was in a room in which there was nothing except a mat, and upon him was a coarse shirt. Then he turned to my companion and said, 'O brother of the people of Basra! You came to me yesterday and I was in the wife's chamber, and yesterday was her day, and the room was her room, and the chattels were her chattels. So she adorned herself for me on the condition that I would adorn myself for her just as she adorned herself for me, so do not let anything enter your heart.' My companion said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, something had entered my heart, but as for now, by Allah, Allah has removed what was (in my heart), and I know that the truth is in what you said.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Adam (peace be upon him) was sent down from Paradise to Al-Safa, and Hawwa (peace be upon him) to Al-Marwa, and she had been combing her hair in Paradise with perfume from the perfumes of Paradise. So when she came to be on earth, she said: 'What hope is there for me in combing, while I am loathsome to my hair?' So she loosened her braids, and from her combing which she used to comb with in Paradise, there scattered [particles], and the wind carried it and cast most of it in India. Thus, it is due to that, came to be the perfume in India. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Ali ibn Hassan – similar to it. He said: 'And in another Hadith: She loosened her braids, so Allah sent upon what was therein from that perfume, a wind, so it descended in the East and the West. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Yahya, from Ali al-Qasir, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the origin of perfume, from what thing is it? So he said: 'What thing do the people say?' I said, 'They allege that Adam descended from Paradise and upon his head was a crown.' So he said: 'He was too preoccupied for a crown to be upon his head.' Then he said: 'Indeed, Hawwa combed herself in Paradise with perfume from the perfumes of Paradise before her error occurred. So when she descended to the earth, she loosened her hair, so Allah, the Exalted, sent upon what was in it a wind, so it carried it to the East and the West. Thus, the origin of perfume is from that.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Allah the Exalted caused Adam to descend, he began patching [his body] with leaves of Paradise, and the garment that was upon him from the garments of Paradise flew off from him. So he picked up a leaf and covered his nakedness with it. When he descended, the aroma of that leaf remained in India with the vegetation. Thus, the perfume came to be in the earth from the cause of that leaf upon which remained the aroma of Paradise. From there, the perfume is in India, because the south wind fell upon the leaf, so its aroma led to the west because it carried the aroma of the leaf in the atmosphere. When the wind stagnated in India, it remained in their trees and their vegetation. The first animal that grazed from that leaf was the musk deer. From there, the musk came to be in the navel of the deer, because the aroma of the vegetation flowed in its body and in its blood, until it gathered in the navel of the deer.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'There used to be for Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) a lead container wherein was musk. So whenever he wanted to go out and wear his clothes, he would take it and extract from it, so he would apply with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There used to be for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) a musk holder. Whenever he performed ablution, he would take it in his hand while it was wet. So when he went out, they would recognize that he was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by its fragrance.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) brought out to me a perfume box of ebony interior in which was musk, compartmentalised from what the women would take.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Muttalib ibn Ziyad, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah Al-Ash'ari, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the musk, 'Is it permissible to smell it?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'We do smell it'.

From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from one of our companions, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: The gleam of musk could be seen in the parting of the hair of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about musk in oil (anointing/massage), is it permissible? He said: I make it in the oil and there is no problem. And it is reported that there is no problem with making musk in food.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I deal with the merchants, so I prepare myself for the people, disliking that they see me in a state of destitution, so I purchase Al-Ghaliya.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'O Is'haq! A little of Al-Ghaliya suffices, and a lot of it is the same. Whoever takes a little of Al-Ghaliya constantly, that will suffice for him.' Is'haq said, 'And I buy from it during the year for ten dirhams, so I suffice myself with it, and its aroma remains fixed for a long duration.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) ordered me, so I made a flask for him containing musk and amber. He ordered me to write on a piece of paper the Verse of the Chair, the Mother of the Book, the Two Protecting Chapters, and some striking verses from the Quran, and to place it between the cover and the flask. So I did so, then I brought it to him, and he covered it with the covering while I was looking at him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from a slave of the Banu Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) went out one night wearing a robe of khazz and a cloak of khazz, and he had covered his beard with al-ghaliya. So they said, 'At this time and in this appearance?' He said, 'I intend to court the Houris for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during this night.' Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a slave of the Banu Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far — similar to it.

From him, from Abu Al-Qasim Al-Kufi, from the one who narrated it, from Muhammad ibn Al-Walid Al-Kirmani, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second, 'What do you say regarding musk?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) ordered for musk to be made for him in a container for seven hundred dirhams. So Al-Fadl ibn Sahl wrote to him, informing him that the people were criticizing that. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'O Fadl! Do you not know that Yusuf (peace be upon him), and he was a prophet, used to wear brocade buttoned with gold, and would sit upon chairs of gold, and that did not reduce anything from his wisdom?' He (the narrator) said, 'So he ordered for a Ghaliya to be made for him for four thousand dirhams.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) met a slave of his on a cold night, and he was wearing a coat of khazz (fine wool), a turban of khazz, and a turban of khazz, and he was wrapped in Al-Ghaliya (a type of perfume). So he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! In a time like this, upon this attire, where are you going?' He said, 'To the mosque of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), to address the Maiden Hourie to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about Al-Khaluq, 'Do I take from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it, but I do not like that you remain perpetually upon it.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no problem in touching the khaluq (perfume/musk) in the bathhouse, or touching your hands with it to cure the cracks (dryness), and I do not like making it a habit. And he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem for a man to apply khaluq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: There is no problem if you touch the khaluq in the bathhouse, or wipe your hand with it to cure by it, and I do not like making it a habit.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from a man, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, that which pleases me is Al-Khaluq.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban, from a man who had affirmed it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq for his wife, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban, from al-Fudayl, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from one of his companions, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The scent of the oud (agarwood) which is in the body remains for forty days, and the scent of the oud of the perfumed cloth remains for twenty days.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from al-Hasan ibn Jahm, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) came out to me, so I found from him an aroma of incense.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Murazam who said: I entered the bathhouse with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). So when he came out to the dressing room, he called for an incense burner and applied the incense with it. Then he said: 'Apply the incense, O Murazam.' I said, 'The one who wants to take his share, can he take it?' He said: 'Yes'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf, the mawla of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who had bought him, his father, his mother, and his brother, so he freed them, and he contracted Ahmad (to pay for his freedom) and made him his butler. So Ahmad said: 'The women of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), when they would incense, would take a pit from the pits of al-Sayhani dates, cleaned of the date flesh, removing the date flesh and the peel, and cast it upon the fire before the incense. When the pit had smoked a little smoke, they would throw the pit away and then incense. They would say:

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Oil smoothens the skin, increases in the brain, eases the flow of water (urine), removes scaling (dryness), and brightens the complexion.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Sufyan ibn al-Samt, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The oiling (massaging) removes the evil.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The oiling manifests the riches.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Oil smoothens the skin, increases strength in the brain, eases the flow of water (urine), removes scaling (dryness), and improves the complexion.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The oiling (massaging) at night flows in the veins, irrigates the skin, and whitens the face.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Bahr, from Mihzam Al-Asady, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you take the oil upon your palm, say: 'O Allah, I ask You for beauty and adornment and love, and I seek refuge in You from disgrace, ugliness, and detestation.' Then place it on your forehead, beginning with what Allah began with.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever oils (massages) a believer, Allah writes for him a light with every hair on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man should not oil (massage) every day. The man should look shaggier and he should not look smooth like a woman.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I mingle with the people of distinction from the people, and I suffice with a little oil, so I wipe myself with it every day.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I do not like that for you.' I said, 'A day and not a day?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And I do not like that for you.' I said, 'One day, and not for two days?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'From Friday to Friday, one day or two days.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Jarir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How much shall I oil (my body)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Once during every year.' So I said, 'Then the people would look at me as a destitute.' So I did not cease bargaining with him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'So in every month, once,' and he (peace be upon him) did not increase over it.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The violet (oil) is the chief of your oils.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd al-Razi, from his father, from Salih ibn Uqba, from his father, who said: I gifted a mule to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so it dislodged the rider which I had sent along with it. So we went over to him (peace be upon him) and we entered Al-Medina. So we informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Why don't you make it sniff the violet (oil)?' So I made it to sniff violet (oil) and it was cured. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Uqba! The violet (oil) is cold in the summer and hot in the winter, soft upon our Shias, dry upon our enemies. Had the people known what was in the violet (oil), they would have evaluated one Owqiya (a unit of measurement) of it, for one Dinar'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There has not come to us from your area anything more beloved to us than the violet (oil)'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba, from Asbat ibn Salim, from Israil ibn Abu Usama al-Baya' al-Zutti, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The example of the violet (oil) among the oils is like our example among the people.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The merit of the violet (oil) over the (other) oils is like the merit of Islam over the religions. The best of the oils is the violet (oil), for it removes the illness from the head and the two eyes, so anoint yourselves with it.

Ali ibn Hassan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Mihzam entered upon him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Call the maid for us to bring us oil and kohl.' So I called her, and she came with a flask of violet (oil). It was a day of intense cold. So Mihzam poured some of it into his palm, then said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is violet (oil), and this is the intense cold.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is the matter with it, O Mihzam?' He said: 'Our physicians in Kufa claim that the violet (oil) is cold.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is cold in the summer, soft and hot in the winter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Sniff the banafsjah (violet oil), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If people knew what was in the banafsjah, they would drink it with a slurping sound.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Violet oil calms the brain.
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbaat, raising it, said: Oiling the two eyebrows with violet oil removes the headache.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The example of the violet (oil) among the oils is like the example of our Shias among the people.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Break the heat of the fever with the violet (oil).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all together from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'aba ibn Maymoun, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He mentioned the oil of violet, so he purified it, then said: 'And the gillyflower oil is gentle.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, and Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) oiling with gillyflower oil, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Oil (yourself).' So I said to him (peace be upon him): 'What is your stance regarding the violet (oil), and what has been reported with regards to it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike its smell.' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'So I also disliked its smell, and I disliked saying that to you due to what reached me regarding it from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of his companions raising it (to the Prophet), said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to dislike black, except in three (garments): the leather sock, the turban, and the cloak.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from some of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfa ibn Mansur who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Hira when a messenger of Abu Ja'far the Caliph came to him, summoning him. So he called for a raincoat, one side of which was black and the other white, and he wore it. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: But I am wearing it while I know that it is the clothing of the inhabitants of the Fire.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Rashid, from his father who said: I saw Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and upon him was a black cloak and a blue pallium.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz, who said: The oils were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so the violet oil was mentioned and its merit; he said: 'Violet oil is an excellent oil, anoint yourselves with it, for its merit over the other oils is like our merit over the people.' And the frankincense oil is a manly oil; it is an excellent oil, and indeed, the khalouq (a type of musk/ambergris scent) pleases me.
