Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: A man complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of cracks in his hands and his legs, so he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Take a piece of cotton and put some frankincense oil in it and place it in your navel'. So Is'haq ibn Ammar said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Put the frankincense oil in the cotton and make it to be in his navel?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for you, O Is'haq, so pour the frankincense in your navel, for it is bigger (task)'. Ibn Udhaynah said, 'I met the man after that, so he informed me that he had done it once, so it went away from him'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Ishaq, Abu Suleyman al-Hadda', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of oils is the frankincense oil.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Al-Sayyari, raising it (to the Prophet), said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is nothing better for the body than the oil of the lily, meaning the jasmine.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Yaqubi, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) used to sniff Al-Shaleetha (a perfume) and the lily in intense heat, causing his nostrils to drop (moisture). He said: And Al-Reza (peace be upon him) also used to sniff with it. So I said to Ali ibn Ja'far, 'Why is that?' So Ali said, 'I mentioned that to one of the physicians, so he mentioned that it is good for copulation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from someone else, from Al-Khashaab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalloob, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would, when he complained of his head, sniff the oil of Al-Juljulân, and it is sesame.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of his companions, from the cousin of Al-Wazaie, from Mas'ada ibn Al-Yasa', from Qays Al-Bahili, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to love to smell the sesame oil.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Talha ibn Zayd, from the one who raised it, said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you is brought basil, let him smell it and place it upon his eyes, for it is from Paradise, and when one of you is brought it, let him not reject it.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you is brought the basil, let him smell it and let him place it upon his eyes, for it is from Paradise.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The basil is of twenty one types, the chief of it is the myrtle.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and in his hand was a dyeing-box wherein was basil.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan, the Master of the Camp (peace be upon him), and a boy from his children came and handed him a rose. He kissed it and placed it on his eyes, then handed it to me and said: 'O Abu Hashim! Whoever takes a rose or a basil leaf, kisses it, and places it on his eyes, then sends blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, the Imams, Allah will write for him good deeds equal to the sand of 'Araj, and erase from him bad deeds equal to that.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: From the happiness is the spaciousness of the home.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said: Indeed, Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) bought a house and ordered one of his slaves to move into it, and said: 'Your home is narrow.' So he said: 'My father had built this house.' So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'If your father was foolish, it is befitting that you become like him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Mutarraf, the mawla of Ma'an, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There are three things for the believer in which there is ease/comfort: a spacious house that conceals his nakedness and his poor condition from the people; and a righteous wife who assists him in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter; and a daughter or a sister whom he removes from his home either by her death or by marrying her off.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Suleyman ibn Rushayd, from his father, from Bashir, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The good life is in the spaciousness of the home, and the graciousness regarding the servants'.

From him, from Mansour bin Al-Abbas, from Saeed, from someone else, that Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked about the gracious living of the world. He said: Spaciousness of the home and the abundance of those that love you.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: From the misery of living is a narrow home.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the happiness of the Muslim person is the spacious dwelling.'

And by this chain, it was said: A man from the Ansar complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that the houses had congested him. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Raise your voice as much as you can and ask Allah that He makes it spacious for you.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'O Muhammad! Indeed your Lord conveys greetings to you and forbids the decoration of houses.' Abu Baseer said, 'So I said, 'What is the decoration of the houses?' He said, 'The images of statues.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'We, the assembly of Angels, do not enter a house in which is a dog, nor a statue of a body, nor a vessel in which is urine.'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not enter a house in which there is a picture, nor a dog, meaning the picture of a human, nor a house in which there are statues.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who creates a statue will be commanded on the Day of Resurrection to blow the spirit into it.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Muthanna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) disliked the picture in the houses.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the pillow and the rug in which there are images/resemblances, so he said: 'There is no problem with it if it is in the house.' I said, 'The images/resembles?' He said: 'Everything that is trampled upon, so there is no problem with it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no problem if there happen to be the resemblances in the houses when its heads are changed from it and it is left, what is besides that.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, all together from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithammi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Munthir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three will be punished on the Day of Resurrection: a man who lied in his dream, he will be commanded to tie a knot between two grains, and he will not be able to tie a knot between them; and a man who created images, he will be commanded to breathe into them, and he will not be able to breathe into them.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent me regarding the demolishing of the graves and breaking of the pictures.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah! We do not enter a house that contains a picture of a human, nor a house in which one urinates, nor a house that contains a dog.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kindi, from his father, who was the master of the water-pourer (mihdar) of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Jibril (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not enter a house in which there is a statue/image that is not trampled upon.' The hadith is shortened.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent me to Medina and said: 'Do not leave any image except that you erase it, nor any grave except that you level it, nor any dog except that you kill it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfaly, from Ziyad ibn Amr al-Ju'fy, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned an Angel to construction, saying to the one who raises a roof above eight cubits: 'Where are you intending (to go to), O wicked one?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the height of the room is above seven cubits, or he said: eight cubits, then what is above the seven and eight cubits is a meeting place (for prayer), and some of them said: a dwelling.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, and Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, all together from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the height of the house, when it is raised to eight cubits, it is considered a dwelling. So when it exceeds eight, let him write at the top of the eight, the Verse of the Chair.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said: A man complained to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'The Jinn have driven us out of our homes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Make the ceilings of your houses seven cubits high, and place the bathroom in the fringes of the house.' The man said: 'So we did that, and we did not see anything we disliked after that.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Al-Husayn ibn Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Build your house up to seven cubits, so whatever is above that, the Satans would dwell in it. The Satans are neither in the sky nor in the ground, but rather they dwell in the atmosphere'.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the room is above eight cubits, write in its upper part the Verse of the Chair.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade sleeping on a roof that is not enclosed by a wall.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Ishaq, from Sahl ibn al-Yasa', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever spends the night on a roof that is not enclosed (by a wall), and something hits him, let him not blame anyone but himself.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the roof upon which one sleeps, and it is not enclosed (by a boundary wall), he (peace be upon him) said: 'It suffices for him if the height of the wall is two cubits.'

From him, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the roof, can one sleep upon it without an enclosure? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade from that'. So I asked him (peace be upon him) about three walls, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless it is four'. I said, 'How much should the height of the walls be?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The shortest of it is one cubit and one open-palms width (Shibr)'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Sayyari, who said: A sheikh from our companions narrated to me from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: From the bitterness of the living is moving from one house to another and eating the bread of barley (or coarse bread).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever acquires wealth from that which is not permissible, Allah causes to be dominant over him the construction, and the water, and the clay.
Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Husayn ibn Uthman, who said: I saw Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) and he had built a construction at Mina, then demolished it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And there is not a single thing but it Glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their Glorification.' He said: 'The cracking of the wall is its Glorification.'
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Sweep your courtyards and do not resemble the Jews.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, raising it (to the Imam), said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not accumulate the dust behind the door, for it is a shelter of the Satans.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Jameela, from Humayd al-Sayrafi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Every construction that is not complete (or has a boundary/limit), it is a burden/evil consequence for its owner on the Day of Resurrection.
From him, from one of his companions, (it has been) raised to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Sweeping the house negates poverty.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade entering a dark house except with a lantern.

From him, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Ibrahim ibn al-Khattab, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The bottom part of the wall complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from the weight of its upper part. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed unto it: 'Bear each other's weight'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from his grandfather, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The house of the devils among your houses is the house of the spider.'
Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, raising it, said, Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said: Igniting the lantern before the sun sets negates poverty.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he went out from the house in the summer, would go out on Thursday. And when he wanted to enter [the house] in the winter from the cold, he would enter on Friday. And it is also reported that his entry and his exit was on the night of Friday.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Qaddah, from his father who said: I lodged at Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Maymoun! Who slumbers with you at night? Is there a slave with you?' I said, 'No'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So do not sleep alone, for the most audacious that the Satan can become, does so upon the human being when he is alone'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahboub from Al-ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Whoever defecates upon a grave, or urinates standing, or urinates in water while standing, or walks in one shoe, or drinks standing, or isolates himself alone in a house, and sleeps upon dripping [food] stains, then something from the Shaytan will strike him; it will not leave him unless Allah wills it, and the quickest that Shaytan comes to the human being is when he is upon one of these states. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out in a military brigade, so he came to the Valley of the Jinn. He called out to his companions: 'Let each man from you hold the hand of his companion; no man should enter alone, nor should a man pass alone.' He said: So a man went forward alone and reached it, and he had been struck with fits. So he was informed of that by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he took his thumb and touched him, then said: 'In the Name of Allah, get out, Wicked one! I am the Messenger of Allah.' He said: So he stood up.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'The Satan is most troublesome with the human being when he is alone, isolated. I (peace be upon him) should not see him sleeping alone.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who spends the night in a house alone, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that, and if he is compelled to do so, then there is no problem, but he should increase the remembrance of Allah in his sleep as much as he can.'

From him, from his father, from Abdullah bin Al-Mughirah and Muhammad bin Sinan, from Talha bin Zayd, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). That he disliked that one should sleep in a house in which there is no door, nor a veil.
And by his chain, he said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) disliked entering a dark house except with a lantern.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from his father Maymoun, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: To Muhammad bin Suleyman: 'Where have you lodged?' He said, 'In such and such a place.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there anyone with you?' He said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not be alone, move from it, O Maymoun, for Satan is most audacious towards the human being when he is alone.'

Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), that he said: 'Do not drink while you are standing, nor urinate in stagnant water, nor walk around a grave, nor be isolated in a house alone, nor walk in one shoe, for the Satan is quickest to be with the servant when he is in one of these states.' And he said: 'If anything were to befall anyone in this state, it would hardly leave him, unless Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills otherwise.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Satan troubles the human being most when he is alone, so do not sleep alone, nor travel alone.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, altogether from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Dahqaan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Three (things) from which insanity is feared: defecating between the graves, walking in one shoe, and a man sleeping alone; and these things are disliked for this reason, and they are not prohibited.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Do not wear wool and animal hair, except for a reason.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (AS), from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: Wear the cotton garments, for it is the clothing of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and our clothing; and he did not use to wear wool or hair except out of necessity.

I said to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): Our city is a cold city, so what do you say regarding wearing this fur? He said: Wear from it what can be eaten (permissible animals) and is guaranteed (properly slaughtered).

I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and upon him was a coarse, rough shirt beneath his clothes, and above it a woolen coat, and above it another coarse shirt. I touched it and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people dislike wearing wool.' So he said: 'Never! My father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) used to wear it, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to wear it, and they (peace be upon them) used to wear the roughest of their garments when they stood for salat, and we do that (as well).'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jarir al-Qummi who said: I asked al-Reza (peace be upon him) about feathers — are they ritually pure (from a slaughtered animal)? So he said: My father (peace be upon him) used to stuff his pillow with feathers.
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) went out to perform the funeral prayer over one of their children, and upon him was a yellow al-khazz coat and a yellow al-khazz shawl.
'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to wear the khazz coat for fifty dinars and the khazz shawl for fifty dinars.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was in his presence about the skins of al-Khazz. So he said: 'There is no problem with them.' The man said: 'May I be your ransom! In my land they are indeed nothing but dogs that come out from the water.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When it comes out from the water, does it live outside the water?' The man said: 'No.' He said: 'Then there is no problem.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to wear al-Khazz in the winter, and the al-Khazz shawl, and a hood of al-Khazz. He would spend the winter in it, and sell the shawl in the summer and give charity with its price. Then he would say: [Quran 7:32] "Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of God which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions?"

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was wearing a khazz cloak, its lining was khazz, and a high-quality khazz pallium. So I said: 'Verily, upon me is a garment that I dislike wearing.' He said: 'And what is it?' I said: 'This pallium of mine.' He said: 'And what is the matter with the pallium?' I said: 'It is khazz.' He said: 'And what is the matter with the khazz?' I said: 'Its warp is silk.' He said: 'And what is the matter with the silk?' He said: 'It is not disliked that the warp of the garment be silk, nor its buttons, nor its emblem. But rather, what is disliked is the entirely silk for men; and it is not disliked for women.'
Indeed, we — the community of the Progeny of Muhammad — wear al-Khazz and the Yemeni (cloth).

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the skins of al-Khazz, so he said: 'It is that al-Khazz which we wear.' So I said: 'May I be your sacrifice! That is the fur?' He said: 'When its fur is permissible, its skin is permissible.'

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) asking him about the animals from which al-Khazz is made from their fur — are they predators? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Al-Husayn ibn Ali and after him my grandfather (peace be upon them both) wore al-Khazz.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was martyred, and upon him was a dark-colored coat of khazz, and they found therein sixty-three [wounds], from among strikes with the sword, stabbings with the spear, or shootings with the arrow.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hafs ibn Amr, Abu Muhammad, the announcer of Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I saw upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he was praying in the garden, a quince-coloured Khazz cloak.

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asked me, 'What do you ride?' I said, 'A donkey.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'For how much did you buy it?' I said, 'For thirteen dinars.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'This is extravagance — to buy a donkey for thirteen dinars and neglect a work-horse.' I said, 'My Master, the upkeep of a work-horse is more than the upkeep of a donkey.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The One Who provides for the donkey will provide for the work-horse. Do you not know that whoever keeps an animal in expectation of our matter (the Rising of al-Qa'im), by which he provokes our enemy, and he is affiliated with us — Allah will make his livelihood flow abundantly, open his chest, fulfill his aspirations, and it will be an aid for his needs.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said: a man from our companions narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Nine-tenths of livelihood is with the owner of the riding animal.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, both together, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gifted four horses from Yemen to the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). So he [the Prophet] said: "Name them for me." So he [Ali] said: "They are of different types." He said: "So is there a spotted one among them?" So he said: "Yes, among them is a chestnut one with white markings." He said: "Then keep it for me." He said: "And among them are two bay ones with white markings." So he said: "Give them to your two sons." He said: "And the fourth is jet-black with no markings." He said: "Sell it and set aside from its proceeds provision for your family; for the blessing of horses is in those with white markings." He said: And I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: "We consider the plain/unmarked ones among all animals as undesirable, except for the donkey and the mule. And I dislike the pattern of white markings on the donkey and the variegated mule. And I dislike bright-hoofed markings on the mule, unless there is an extended blaze on its forehead — and even then I do not desire it in any state."

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy an animal, for its benefit is for you and its sustenance is upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever buys an animal, its back (for riding) would be for him, and upon Allah would be its sustenance.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Take a donkey to carry your belongings, for its sustenance is upon God.' He said: So I acquired a donkey, and I and my brother Yusuf — when a year was completed — would calculate our expenditures to know their amount. So we calculated our expenditures after purchasing the donkey, and they were the same as they had always been every year — nothing had increased.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'From the happiness of the believer is a riding animal he rides for his needs, and upon which he fulfils the rights of his brethren.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the happiness of a Muslim man is a comfortable mount.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad altogether, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Acquire a riding animal, for indeed it is an adornment, and needs are fulfilled upon it, and its sustenance is upon God, Majestic is His mention.' He said: 'And Ammar ibn al-Mubarak narrated the same to me and added to it: and upon it you meet your brethren.' And it is reported that he said: 'How wondrous is the owner of the riding animal — how could any need escape him?'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: From the misery of life is the bad mount.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever keeps a bird in his house, let him keep the Warshaan (wood-pigeon), for it is the one that most frequently mentions Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and most frequently glorifies Him, and it is a bird that loves us, the People of the Household.

From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Uthman al-Asbahani, who said: Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) gifted me a bird from the birds of Iraq, so I gifted him a Warshaan (wood-pigeon). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered, saw it, and said: 'The Warshaan is saying, Blessing be upon you, Blessing be upon you! Therefore, keep it.

From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Saif, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he forbade his son Ismail from keeping the ring-dove, and he said: If you must keep one, then keep the Warshaan (wood-pigeon), for it frequently remembers Allah, Blessed and High.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was in the house of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) a fakhta (ring-dove). He heard it one day while it was shrieking, so he said to them: 'Do you know what this fakhta is saying?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'It is saying, I have lost you, I have lost you.' Then he said: 'We will lose it before it loses us.' Then he ordered for it to be slaughtered.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Usman al-Asbahani, who said: I gifted a sulsul (ring-dove) to Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered, and when he saw it, he said: 'This is the inauspicious bird. Remove it, for it is saying, "I have lost you, I have lost you." Therefore, lose it before it loses you.'

From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad, go with us to visit Ismail, for he has been complaining.' So we arose and entered upon Ismail, and there was a Fakhta (ring-dove) in a cage in his house, shrieking. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son, what calls you to keep this Fakhta? Do you not know that it is inauspicious? Do you not know what it is saying?' Ismail said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is supplicating against its owners, saying: We are lost, we are lost! Therefore exit it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is disliked (makruh) that there be in the house of the Muslim man a dog.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no one who takes a dog except that one qirat (unit of measurement) would be reduced from his deeds every day.
From him, from Usman, from Sama'at who said: I asked him about the dog, 'Can we keep it in the house?' He said: 'No'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no goodness in the dogs except for the hunting dog, or a herding dog.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Do not keep a hunting dog in the house except if there is a door between you and it.
From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about a hunting dog being kept in the house. He said: If a door can be closed on it, then there is no problem.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The black dogs, the beasts, are from the Jinn.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in what is between Mecca and Medina. When he turned to his left, there was a black, beastly dog. He said: 'What is the matter with you? May Allah make you ugly, how fierce is your rushing!' And it was resembling a bird. I said: 'What is this? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'This is Gusaym, the postman of the Jinn. Hisham died at this moment, and he (Gusaym) flies, announcing it in every city.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The dogs are from the weak ones of the Jinn. So when one of you is eating the meal, and something from them is in front of him, let him feed it or let him repel it, for it has an evil self.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Abi Salama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the dogs, so he said: 'Every entirely black one is a beast, and every entirely red one is a beast, and every entirely white one is a beast; that is a creation from the dogs from the Jinn, and whatever is speckled is a morphed form from the Jinn and humans.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the squeezer dog (greyhound). He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you touch it, wash your hand.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the instigation (fighting) between animals, so he said: 'All of it is abhorred, except for the dog.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Misma'a who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the instigation between the animals, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that, except for the dogs.'

For the animal, upon its owner, are six rights: he must not burden it beyond its strength; he must not use its back as a seat for conversations; he must begin by feeding it when he dismounts; he must not brand it; he must not strike it on its face, for indeed it glorifies (God); and he must offer water to it whenever he passes by it.

In what I think [is narrated] from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: Abu Dharr (may God be pleased with him) was seen watering a donkey at al-Rabadha. So some of the people said to him: 'Is there no one, O Abu Dharr, who could water the donkey for you?' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) saying: There is no animal except that it asks God every morning: O God, grant me a righteous owner who will feed me until I am full, give me water until I am quenched, and not burden me beyond my strength. So I love to water it myself.'

I passed by Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he had lodged at al-Hira. He said to me: 'What is your occupation?' I said: 'Animal trader.' So he said: 'Find a fazaa mule for me.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is al-fazaa?' He said: 'Dark, with a white belly, white thighs, and a white mouth.' He said: So I said: 'By Allah! I have not seen the likes of this description.' So I returned from his presence, and after a while I entered the ditch (market), and suddenly there was a slave who had been riding a mule of this very description. So I asked the slave: 'Whose mule is this?' He said: 'My master's.' I said: 'Will he sell it?' He said: 'I do not know.' So I followed him until I came to his master and I bought it from him, and I came to him (the Imam) with it. So he said: 'This is the description I wanted.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Supplicate to Allah for me.' So he said: 'May Allah amplify your wealth and your children.' He said: So I became the most abundant of the people of al-Kufa in wealth and children.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not strike the animals upon their faces, for they glorify with the praise of Allah.' He said, and in another hadith: 'Do not brand them in their faces.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yasar, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When the riding animal stumbles beneath a man, and he says to it, 'May you be ruined,' it says, 'May the most disobedient of us to the Lord be ruined.'
I asked al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'When may I strike my animal under me?' He said: 'When it does not walk under you as it walks to its feeding place.'
And it is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'Strike it (the animal) for fleeing, and do not strike it for stumbling.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from 'Amr ibn Jumai', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not sit sideways upon the riding animals, and do not take their backs as gathering places.'

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whatever dullness afflicts the animals, they are not left ignorant of four things: their recognition of the Lord, their recognition of death, their recognition of the female from the male, and their recognition of the pasture from the fertile land.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: For everything is a sanctity, and the sanctity of the animals is in their faces.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal and Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah, from Yaqoub ibn Salim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whatever aspect may be obscure or dull in the beasts, four characteristics are not obscure to them: knowing that they have a Creator, knowing the seeking of sustenance, knowing the male from the female, and the fear of death.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun from al-Asam from Misma' ibn Abdul Malik from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Strike it upon the fleeing but do not strike it upon the stumbling'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Ja'far, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Upon each nostril of the animals is a shaytan. So whenever one of you wishes to bridle it, let him name Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Whichever animal becomes difficult for its owner due to bridling and fleeing (resisting commands) let him recite in its ear or upon it Is it other than Allah's Religion that they seek (to follow), and to Him submits whoever is in the skies and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him shall they be returning.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from the right that the rider says to the walker, "The road" (Make way). And in another copy: "It is from the inequity that the rider should be saying to the walker, "The road" (Make way)."'

And by his chain, he said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) went out while he was riding, so they walked along with him. He said to them: 'Is there any need for you?' They said: 'No, but we love to walk with you.' He said to them: 'Disperse, for the walking of the walker with the rider is a spoil for the rider and a humiliation for the walker.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, raising it, said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three must not ride upon one animal, for one of them would be an Accursed'.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The saddle is a detestable riding position for women.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the skins of predatory animals, so he said: 'Ride them, but do not wear anything from them while you are praying.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the saddle and the reins that have silver on them — can one ride with them? He said: If it is coated (with silver) such that one is not able to remove it, then there is no objection; otherwise, do not ride with it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): Beware of riding on a red saddlecloth, for it is a saddlecloth of Satan.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Madini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to ride upon red velvet.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The nose-ring of the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was of silver.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to purchase the riding camel for one hundred dinars, honouring himself with it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Safwan al-Jammal who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Had the people known the true nature of how God facilitates bearing (burdens) for the weak, they would not consider any animal expensive.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily upon the hump of every camel is a satan, so degrade it and subdue it for yourselves, and mention the name of God — for it is God, Mighty and Majestic, who carries [you].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Had the pilgrim known what rewards await him from the carriers (mounts), no one would consider a camel to be expensive.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was walking alongside my she-camel. He said: 'What is the matter — why are you not riding?' I said: 'My she-camel has weakened, and I wanted to lighten the burden on her.' He said: 'May God have mercy on you! Ride, for God carries the burden of both the weak and the strong.'

From him, from his father, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) forbade crossing the line of camels. It was said: 'O Messenger of God, and why?' He said: 'Indeed, there is no caravan line except that between every camel and the next there is a devil.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from his father who said: I bought camels while I was residing in Al-Medina, and they fascinated me with an intense fascination. So I went to Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) and mentioned them to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is it to you and the camels? Did you not know that they are full of misfortunes?' He said: So from my fascination with them, I hired them out and sent them with some of my servants to Al-Kufa. He said: Then they all perished. So I went to him and informed him. So he said: 'Therefore let those who go against his command beware lest a trial afflict them or there befalls them a painful punishment.' [Quran 24:63]

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Safwan! Buy a camel for me and take it deformed, for it is the thing with the longest lifespan.' So I bought a camel for him for eighty dirhams and went to him with it. And in another narration, he said: 'Buy the black, ugly ones, for they are the thing with the longest lifespan.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and from his father Maymun who said: We went out with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to the land of Tayba, and with him were Amr ibn Dinar and a group of his companions. We stayed in Tayba for as long as God willed. Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rode upon a difficult camel. Amr ibn Dinar said to him: 'How difficult is your camel!' He said: 'Do you not know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Upon the peak of every camel is a satan, so disgrace it and subdue it, and mention the name of God upon it, for it is God Who carries'? Then he entered Mecca and we entered with him without ihram.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Saeed, from a man, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Beware of the red camels, for they are the camels with the shortest lifespan.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassa' from Abdullah ibn Sinan said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chose something from every thing. He chose the she-camel from the camels, and from the sheep, the ewe.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O my son! Keep sheep and do not keep camels.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Amr ibn Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of wealth is the sheep.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Clean their pens and wipe their dust (from their fur).'

And by this chain, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a household keeps a sheep, God brings them its sustenance and increases their provisions, and poverty departs from them by one stage. If they keep two sheep, God brings them the sustenance of both and increases their provisions, and poverty departs from them by two stages. If they keep three, God brings them their sustenance and poverty departs from them entirely.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no household that has a milking sheep with them, except that they are sanctified twice every day.' I said: 'And how is it said to them?' He said: 'It is said to them: You are blessed! You are blessed!'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Marid, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no believer who has a dairy goat in his home, except that the inhabitants of that home are sanctified and blessings are bestowed upon them. And if there were two, they are sanctified and blessings are bestowed upon them twice every day. He said: Then one of our companions said, 'And how are they sanctified?' He said: An angel stands over them every morning and says to them: You are sanctified, and blessings be upon you, and you are made wholesome, and your food is made wholesome. He said: I said to him, 'And what is the meaning of "you are sanctified"?' He said: You are purified (from sins).

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his paternal aunt: 'What prevents you from keeping a blessing in your house?' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is the blessing?' He said: 'A sheep you can milk. For indeed, whoever has in his house a sheep to milk, or an ewe, or a cow to milk — these are all blessings.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) went to Umm Salama, and said to her: 'Why is it that I do not see the blessing in your house?' She said: 'Yes indeed, and praise be to God, for the blessing is certainly in my house.' So he said: 'Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down three blessings: water, fire, and the sheep.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no household to whom thirty sheep return [in the evening] except that the angels do not cease to guard them until the morning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Shall I brand the sheep on their faces?' He said: 'Brand them on their ears.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about branding livestock, and he said: There is no problem with it, except on their faces.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said: The pigeon is from the birds of the Prophets (peace be upon them).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abd al-A'la, freed slave of the progeny of Sam, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The first pigeon that was in Mecca was a pigeon of Ismail (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The origin of the pigeons of the Sanctuary is the remnant of the pigeons that belonged to Ismail ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon him) — he kept them as he was comforted by them. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is recommended that you keep a bird with clipped wings to be comforted by it, for fear of the vermin.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'This pigeon — the pigeon of the Sanctuary — it is from the lineage of the pigeon of Ismail ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon him) which belonged to him.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, altogether, from Al-Washa', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Khadija, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is none from the house wherein is a pigeon, except that the inhabitants of that house would not be hit by an affliction from the Jinn. The foolish ones from the Jinn tend to tamper in the house, so they would be tampering with the pigeons and they would be neglecting the human beings.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man complained to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) of loneliness, and he ordered him to take a pair of pigeons in his house.

The pigeon was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: Keep them in your homes, for indeed they are beloved — the supplication of Noah (peace be upon him) reached them, and they are the most comforting thing in homes.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The pigeon is a bird from the birds of the Prophets (peace be upon them) which they used to keep in their houses, and there is no house in which there is a pigeon except that no affliction from the jinn would befall the inhabitants of that house. The foolish ones among the jinn tamper in the house, so they tamper with the pigeons and leave the people alone.' He (the narrator) said: 'So I saw in the rooms of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a pigeon for his son Ismail.'

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, while looking at pigeons in his house: 'There is not a single flutter with which it flutters, except that God repels through it those who enter the house from among the determined evildoers of the earth.'

From him, from Al-Jamourani, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Sandal, from Dawood ibn Farqad, who said: I was sitting in the house of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I looked at a Ra'ibi pigeon cooing for a long time. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) looked at me and said: 'O Dawood! Do you know what this bird is saying?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is supplicating against the killers of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), therefore take it to be in your houses.'
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from a man, from Yahya al-Azraq who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The swishing of the wings of the pigeons expels the satans.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, defends the house from crumbling by the pigeons.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Keep the Ra'abiyyah pigeons in your houses, for they curse the killers of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and may Allah curse his killer.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Uthman al-Asbahani, who said: Ismail ibn Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) gifted (something) to me, so I gifted to him a Ra'ibi bird (pigeon). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered and said: 'Place this Ra'ibi bird with me in the house, for it comforts me.' He (the narrator) said, 'And Uthman said, I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and in front of him was a pigeon, and he was breaking bread for it.'

From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ash'ath ibn Muhammad al-Bariqi, from Abdul Karim ibn Salih who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and saw three green pigeons on his mattress, which had defecated on it. I said, 'May I be your ransom, these pigeons have dirtied the mattress.' He said, 'No, it is recommended that they dwell in the house.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There was in the house of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a pair of red pigeons.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibrahim al-Sindi, from Yahya al-Azraq, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) dug a well, so they threw (things) into it. He was informed of that, so he came until he stood over it and said: 'You should refrain, or I will dwell the pigeons in it.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The swishing of their wings repels the devils.'

From him, from his father, from one of our companions who said: Pigeons were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him, 'It has reached me that Umar saw a pigeon flying and a man running under it, so Umar said, 'A satan running under a satan.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'What was Ismail among you?' So it was said, 'A truthful one.' So he said, 'The remaining pigeons of the Sanctuary are from a pigeon of Ismail.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Nasr, who said: A man asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a pair of pigeons with him that had incubated [eggs], asking: 'Does the bird marry its mother and its daughter?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with what is between the beasts.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the bird that is sent from a distant city which it had never seen at all, yet it comes [back]. He said: O Ibn Udhaafir! It comes to the home of its owner from thirty farsakhs based on its recognition and reckoning. But when [the distance] exceeds thirty farsakhs, it goes to its keepers with its sustenance.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: What (bird) comes from thirty farsakhs, so it is by guidance (instinct), and what was more than that, so it is by eating (training).
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The bird comes from the remote place.' He said: 'But rather, it comes for its sustenance.'

I said: 'The pigeons which are sent with a message from the remote places come back, while those sent from the nearby places do not come back.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When its feed is cut off, it will not come.'
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A white rooster with a split crest guards the dwelling of its inhabitants and seven dwellings around it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi, from Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-Ahwazi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A white rooster with a split comb guards its little house and seven little houses around it, and a single wing-flutter from a speckled pigeon is superior to seven white roosters with split combs.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, who said: The beauty of peacocks was mentioned in the presence of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said: 'It would not surpass for you the beauty of the white rooster in anything.' He said: And I heard him saying: 'The rooster has a better voice than the peacock, and it is greater in blessing; it alerts you at the times of the salat, whereas the peacock cries out in lamentation because of the sin with which it has been afflicted.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The white rooster is my friend and a friend of every believer.

He said: 'In the rooster are five characteristics from the characteristics of the Prophets — generosity, bravery, contentment, knowledge of the times of prayers, and frequency of mating and protective jealousy.'

From him, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said: 'The crowing of the rooster is its prayer (salat), and the flapping of its wings are its bowing (ruku') and its prostration (sujud).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ali ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Hazim al-Kalbi — nephew of Hisham ibn Salim — from Sulayman ibn Ja'far, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever does not make his bequest well at the time of death, it is a deficiency in his chivalry and his intellect.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and how does the dying person make a bequest?' He said: 'When his death approaches and the people gather around him,' he says: O Allah! Originator of the heavens and earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. O Allah! I make a covenant with You in the abode of this world: I bear witness that there is no god but You alone, You have no partner; and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your messenger; and that Paradise is true; and that the Fire is true; and that the Resurrection is true; and that the Reckoning is true; and that divine decree and the Scale are true; and that the religion is as You have described; and that Islam is as You have legislated; and that the Word is as You have spoken; and that the Quran is as You have revealed; and that You are Allah, the Manifest Truth. May Allah reward Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with the best of rewards, and may Allah greet Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with peace. O Allah! O my provision in my affliction, and O my companion in my distress, and O Guardian of my blessings — my God and the God of my fathers — do not leave me to myself for even the blink of an eye, ever. For if You leave me to myself for even the blink of an eye, I would draw nearer to evil and grow farther from good. So soothe my loneliness in the grave, and grant me a covenant for the day I meet You, resurrected. Then he makes his bequest for his needs. The confirmation of this bequest is in the Quran, in the chapter in which Maryam is mentioned, in His words — Mighty and Majestic: 'They shall not have power of intercession, save he who has made a covenant with the All-beneficent' [19:87]. And this is the covenant of the dying person. And the bequest is a right upon every Muslim to preserve this bequest and teach it. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught it to me, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his fami

A freed slave (mawla) of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), called A'yan, accompanied me. He fell ill for some days, then recovered, then died. So I took his belongings and all that was his, and brought them to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him that he had been ill for some days, then recovered, then died. He said: That is the comfort of death. Know that there is no one who dies until God, Mighty and Majestic, restores to him his hearing, his sight, and his intellect for the bequest — whether he makes it or leaves it.

A man said to him: 'I went out to Makkah, so a man accompanied me and he was my travel companion. When we were on one of the roads, he fell ill and became severely burdened. I used to take care of him. Then he regained consciousness to the extent that there was no problem with him in my estimation. When the day came in which he died, he regained consciousness, then died on that very day.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is not a dying person upon whom death presents itself except that God, Mighty and Majestic, restores to him his hearing, his eyesight, and his intellect for the bequest — whether he makes the bequest or neglects it. And it is the comfort that is called 'the comfort of death', and it is a right upon every Muslim.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the bequest, and he said: 'It is a right upon every Muslim.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The bequest is truth, and the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) had made a bequest, so it is befitting for the Muslim that he bequeaths.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed his wealth in the way of Allah. He said: Give it to the one he bequeathed it for, even if he was a Jew or a Christian. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then its sin is only upon those who alter it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding a man who bequeathed his wealth in the Way of Allah. He (peace be upon him) said: Give it to the one to whom he bequeathed it, even if he was a Jew or a Christian. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it is only upon those who alter it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to Ja'far and Musa: 'And regarding what I have ordered you both, from the witnessing with such and such, is a safety for you both in your Hereafter, and the enforcement of what your parents bequeathed, and righteousness from you both to them, and beware that you do not replace their bequest, nor change it from its state, because they both have exited from that, may Allah be Pleased with them, and that has become a burden upon your necks.' Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has said in His Book regarding the bequest: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin of it is only upon those who alter it; surely Allah is Hearing, Knowing.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, that a man was in Hamadan he mentioned that his father died and he did not know this matter, so he bequeathed a bequest at the time of death and bequeathed that something be given in the Way of Allah, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about it, how should it be dealt with so we informed him that he did not know this matter, so he said: 'If a man had bequeathed to me that I should place it with a Jew or a Christian, I would have placed it with them' Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin of it is only upon those who alter it' So look to the one who goes out to this direction, meaning one of the borders/frontiers, so send it to him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Al-Husayn ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man bequeathed to me something in the Way (of God/Jihad).' He said to me, 'Spend it on Hajj.' I said to him, 'He bequeathed to me in the Way.' He said, 'Spend it on Hajj, for I do not know anything from His Way that is superior to Hajj.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hajjaj al-Khashab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a woman who bequeathed to me wealth, saying, 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah.' So it was said to her, 'Shall we perform Hajj with it?' She said, 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah.' So they said to her, 'Shall we give it to the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them)?' She said, 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Let it be spent in the Way of Allah just as she ordered.' I said, 'Order me how I should spend it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let it be spent just as she ordered you. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High is, says: "So the one who alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it then is only upon the one who alters it; surely Allah is Hearing, Knowing." Do you see that if she had ordered you to give it to a Jew, would you have given it to a Christian?' He (the narrator) said: 'So I remained after that for three years, then I came to him and said to him what I had said the first time. So he was silent for a while, then said: 'Give it.' I said, 'To whom shall I give it?' He said: 'Isa Shalqan.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan ibn Rashid who said: I asked al-Askari (peace be upon him) in al-Madina about a man who bequeathed wealth in the way of Allah, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The way of Allah is our Shias'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Talib Abdullah ibn al-Salt, who said: Al-Khalil ibn Hashim wrote to Zil al-Ri'asatayn (the one with two governorships), who was the governor of Naysabur, that a man from the Magians had died and bequeathed something of his wealth to the poor. So the judge of Naysabur took it and placed it among the poor Muslims. So Al-Khalil wrote to Zil al-Ri'asatayn about that. So he asked Al-Ma'mun about it, and he said, 'I have nothing regarding it.' So he asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'The Magian did not bequeath to the poor Muslims, but it is fitting that the amount of that wealth be taken from the charity funds (sadaqah) and returned to the poor Magians.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Rayyan ibn Shubayb, who said: Maradah bequeathed a bequest to a group of Christian workers. So our companions said, 'Distribute this among the poor believers from your companions.' So I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said, 'My sister bequeathed a bequest to a group of Christians, and I intended to divert that to a group of our Muslim companions.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Enforce the bequest upon what she bequeathed.' Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Indeed, its sin is upon those who alter it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding a man who bequeathed more than the third, and emancipated his slave during his illness, he said: If it was more than the third, return it to the third, and the emancipation is valid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a man emancipates a servant of his at the time of his death, then makes another bequest, the bequest is dropped and the servant is freed from one-third of the estate, unless there remains from the one-third an amount sufficient to cover the bequest.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Hammam, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding a man who bequeathed wealth for his relatives at the time of his death, and emancipated a slave of his, and the entirety of what he bequeathed exceeded one-third. How should one deal with his bequest? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the emancipation, and enforce it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man to whom death presented itself, so he freed his slave and made a bequest, and it was more than one-third. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The emancipation of the slave is enforced, and the deficit is taken from what remains.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Indeed, Alqamah ibn Muhammad bequeathed to me that I should emancipate a neck on his behalf, so I emancipated a woman on his behalf. Is that sufficient for him, or should I emancipate on his behalf from my own wealth?' He said, 'It is sufficient.' Then he said to me, 'Indeed, Fatima, the mother of my son, bequeathed that I should emancipate a neck on her behalf, so I emancipated a woman on her behalf.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man asked me about a woman who died and had not performed Hajj, and she bequeathed [money] to be used for Hajj. I was asked about it: if it was more preferable that it be placed among the poor of the offspring of Fatimah, it was placed among them; and if Hajj was more preferable, Hajj was performed for her. So I said to him: If an obligatory Hajj was due upon her, then spending what she bequeathed on Hajj is more beloved to me than distributing it in other than that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, regarding a man who died and bequeathed that Hajj be performed for him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was the first Hajj, Hajj is performed for him from the middle of the wealth, and if it was other than the first Hajj, then it is from the one-third.'

From him, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, regarding a woman who bequeathed wealth for emancipation, charity, and Hajj, but it did not reach (the required amount). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with the Hajj, for it is obligatory. So if anything remains, make a portion of it for charity and a portion for emancipation.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed thirty dinars to emancipate a man from our companions with it, but he could not be found. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy (a slave) from the people, then emancipate him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) about a man who died and bequeathed the emancipation of a Muslim slave for thirty dinars, but the amount specified could not be found. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that they should increase upon that which has been named.' I said: 'And if they cannot find it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let them buy from the general wealth of the people, provided it is not from a Nasibi (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Al-Sheikh (peace be upon him) that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed away and left sixty slaves, so I emancipated a third of them, drawing lots between them, and extracted the third.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a slave girl freed by my brother, who used to serve with the other slave girls and was part of his household. He bequeathed to me to spend upon her from the middle (of the legacy). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If she was with the slave girls and was supervising over them, then spend upon her, and follow his bequest.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed that a slave be freed for him with five hundred dirhams from his third. So a slave was bought for less than five hundred dirhams, and a remainder remained. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The remainder should be given to the slave before he is freed, then he is freed on behalf of the deceased.'
