Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: A woman from my family bequeathed to me a third of her wealth and ordered that a slave be emancipated, Hajj be performed, and charity be given, but the amount did not reach the requirement. So I asked Abu Hanifa about it, and he said: 'Make it three parts: a third for emancipation, a third for Hajj, and a third for charity.' So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'A woman from my family died and bequeathed to me a third of her wealth, and ordered that a slave be emancipated from it, charity be given, and Hajj be performed from it. So I looked into it but the amount did not reach the requirement.' He said: 'Begin with Hajj, for it is an obligation from the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and make whatever remains a portion for emancipation and a portion for charity.' So I informed Abu Hanifa with the words of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he retracted from his own words and spoke with the words of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Jameela, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bequeathed at the time of his death, 'Free so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so.' I looked into his one-third share, but it did not reach the price/value of the five slaves whom he ordered to be freed. He said: 'Look at those he named and begin by freeing them. Appraise them and look at his one-third share, so free from it the first one, then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth. If the one-third is insufficient for what he named, stop, for the one he named last is freed after the one-third is exhausted, which is what he does not own, so that is not permissible for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who was on a journey with him, and with him was a slave girl and two slave boys. So he said to them both, 'You are both free for the sake of Allah, and testify that what is in the belly of this slave girl of mine is from me.' So she gave birth to a boy. When they returned to the heirs, they denied that and enslaved them. Then the two boys were emancipated after that, so they testified after being emancipated that their first master had testified that what was in the belly of his slave girl was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their testimony is valid for the boy, and the boy whom they testified for cannot enslave them, because they affirmed his lineage.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ahmad ibn Ziyad, from Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man upon whom death was approaching, who had slaves for his own exclusive use, and who had slaves in partnership with another man. So he bequeathed in his will that his slaves be freed. What is the status of his slaves who were in the partnership? He said: They are evaluated against him; if his wealth can bear their value, then they are freed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left a slave girl, having emancipated a third of her. So the executor married her before anything from the inheritance was distributed. That she is evaluated, and she and her husband are made to work to pay off the remainder of her price after being evaluated. So whatever of emancipation or enslavement befalls the woman, it flows upon her child.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his men, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has released for the executor the permission to change the bequest if it is not in accordance with what is customary/fair, and there is injustice in it, and to return it to what is customary/fair. So whoever fears from the testator an inclination to a wrong course or an act of disobedience, and effects an agreement between the parties, then there is no blame on him. Due to His (Mighty and Majestic) Words.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyoub, from Muhammad ibn Sowqat, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin is upon those who alter it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was abrogated by the verse that follows it, His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: 'But he who fears from the testator an inclination to a wrong course or an act of disobedience, and makes peace between them, then there is no blame on him.' He said: 'It means the executor; if he fears injustice from the testator regarding what he bequeathed to him, from that which Allah is not pleased with, being contrary to the right, then there is no blame on him, i.e., upon the executor, to alter it to the right and to that which Allah is pleased with, from the way of goodness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad, both together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Narsi, from Ali ibn Farqad, the companion of al-Sabiri, who said: A man bequeathed his estate to me and ordered me to perform Hajj with it on his behalf. So I looked into it and found it to be a small amount, not sufficient for Hajj. So I asked Abu Hanifa and the jurists of the people of Kufa, and they said: 'Give it in charity on his behalf.' So when I performed Hajj, I met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan during the Tawaf. So I asked him and said to him: 'Indeed, a man from your mawali (clients/followers) from the people of Kufa died and bequeathed his estate to me and ordered me to perform Hajj with it on his behalf. So I looked into it, but it was not sufficient for Hajj. So I asked the jurists from our side, and they said: He said to me: 'This is Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the Hujr, so go to him and ask him.' He said: So I entered the Hujr, and there was Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) beneath the Mizab (spout of the Kaaba), facing with his face towards the House, supplicating. Then he turned towards me and saw me, so he said: 'What is your need?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! I am a man from the people of Kufa, from your mawali.' He said: 'Leave that aside, what is your need?' I said: 'A man died and bequeathed his estate that I should perform Hajj with it on his behalf. So I looked into it, but it was not sufficient for Hajj. So I asked the jurists who are with us, and they said: He said: 'What did you do?' I said: 'I gave it in charity.' He said: 'You are responsible (guaranteed), except if it happens that it is not sufficient to perform Hajj with it from Makkah. So if it is not sufficient to perform Hajj with it from Makkah, then there is no responsibility upon you. And if it is sufficient to perform Hajj with it from Makkah, then you are responsible.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Saeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who bequeathed for a Hajj, so his executor made it regarding a person (freeing a slave). He said: 'The executor bears the cost, and he makes it regarding a Hajj just as he had been bequeathed.' So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin of it is only upon those who alter it. Indeed Allah, Blessed and High is, says:

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Marad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a man and ordered him to emancip a slave on his behalf with six hundred dirhams from his third. So the executor went and gave the six hundred dirhams to a man to perform Hajj with it on his behalf. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that the executor should bear the cost of six hundred dirhams from his own wealth, and the six hundred dirhams should be counted towards what the deceased bequeathed for the emancipation of a slave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The Mudabbar (slave whose emancipation is conditional upon the death of the master) is from the third.

From him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who conditionally emancipates his slave, is there for him to retract with regards to it? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. He is at the status of the bequest.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Mudabbar (conditionally emancipated slave) is from the third. And he (peace be upon him) said that the man may retract regarding his third, whether he had bequeathed during good health or illness.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mudabbar (conditionally emancipated slave). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is in the status of the bequest; the master may retract from him whatever he desires of the emancipation.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The shroud is from the entirety of the wealth.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Mu'adh, from Zurara, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who died and upon him was a debt to the value of the price of his shroud. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'What he leaves should be used for the price of his shroud, except if some of the people were to trade with him, so they shroud him, and pay off what is upon him from what he leaves.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The first thing to begin with from the wealth is the shroud, then the debt, then the bequest, then the inheritance.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a man and upon him was a debt. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The man should pay off whatever was upon him from his debts, and distribute what remains among the inheritors.' I said, '(Supposing) whatever he had bequeathed with from the debts gets stolen, so from which of the inheritors would it be taken for the debt?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It will not be taken from the inheritors, but the executor is responsible for it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, both together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Sha'iri, from al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said: We were at the door of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and we were a group waiting for him to come out, when a woman came and said, 'Which one of you is Abu Ja'far?' The people said to her, 'What do you want from him?' She said, 'I want to ask him about a matter.' They said to her, 'This is the jurist of the people of Iraq, so ask him.' She said, 'My husband died and left a thousand dirhams, and there was for me upon him from my dowry five hundred dirhams. So I took my dowry and took my inheritance. Then a man came and claimed a thousand dirhams from him, so I testified for him.' Al-Hakam said: 'While I was counting, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out and said, I said, 'This woman mentioned that her husband died and left a thousand dirhams, and there was for her upon him from her dowry five hundred dirhams. So she took her dowry and took her inheritance. Then a man came and claimed a thousand dirhams from him, so she testified for him.' Al-Hakam said: 'By Allah, I had not even completed my speech until he said, Al-Hakam said: 'So I had not seen, by Allah, anyone more understanding than Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at all.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who sold goods to another man, so the buyer took possession of the goods and did not pay the price. Then the buyer died and the goods remained exactly as they were. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the goods are exactly as they were, they are returned to the owner of the goods.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the creditors to dispute them.' Ibn Abi Umayr said, 'And the interpretation of that is that there is no inheritance for her until the debt is paid. Rather, he left a thousand dirhams, and upon him was a debt of a thousand and five hundred dirhams for her and for the man. So her share is one third of the thousand, and for the man is two thirds.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who dies and upon him is a debt, so a guarantor took responsibility for the creditors. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the creditors are pleased, then the liability of the deceased has been freed.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who was killed and upon him was a debt, and he did not leave wealth, so his family took the blood money (diyah) from his killer. Should they pay off his debt? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And he did not leave anything?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They have taken the blood money, so it is upon them to pay off his debt.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who died and had a debt upon me, and he left behind children: men, women, and young boys. So a man from among them came and said, 'You are free from what my father had upon you from my share, and you are free from what is for my brothers and sisters, and I am responsible for their pleasure regarding you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You will be at ease from that and free.' I said, 'But if he does not give them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That would be upon his neck.' I said, 'But if the inheritors return to me and say, 'Give us our right'?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is for them in the apparent judgment. As for between you and Allah (Exalted and Majestic), you are free from it, if the man who freed you takes responsibility for you regarding their pleasure, so the guarantor carries it for you.' I said, 'So what do you say about the child, for his mother to free (on his behalf)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if she has what satisfies him or gives him.' I said, 'But if she does not have anything?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then no.' I said, 'I have heard you say that her freeing is permissible?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I only mean that if she has wealth.' I said, 'So is it permissible for the father to free (on behalf of) his son?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'For him is what was for us with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), a matter he does regarding that whatever he wishes.' I said, 'The man guaranteed to me regarding that child, and I am free from his share. So if the man dies before the child reaches adulthood, there is nothing upon him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The matter is permissible according to what he stipulated for you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked me: 'Did Ibn Abi Layla and Ibn Shubrumah differ?' So I said, 'It reached me that the master of Isa ibn Musa died and left a large debt upon him, and left slaves whose value encompassed his debt. So he freed them at the time of death. Isa ibn Musa asked both of them about that. Ibn Shubrumah said, 'I view that they should be made to work to cover their price, and that amount should be paid to the creditors, for he had freed them at the time of his death.' And Ibn Abi Layla said, 'I view that they should be sold and their prices paid to the creditors, for it was not for him to free them at the time of death while he had a debt that encompassed them.' And this is what the people of al-Hijaz do today: if a man frees his slave and upon him is a large debt, they do not validate his emancipation if there is a large debt upon him. So Ibn Shubrumah raised his hand to the sky and said, 'Glory be to Allah, O Ibn Abi Layla! When did I say this opinion? By Allah, I did not say it except that you sought to go against me.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So which of the two opinions did he implement?' I said, 'It reached me that he took the opinion of Ibn Abi Layla, and he had a desire in that. So he sold them and paid off his debt.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So which of the two opinions are you with?' I said to him, 'With Ibn Shubrumah, and Ibn Abi Layla had returned to the opinion of Ibn Shubrumah after that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, the truth is in that which Ibn Abi Layla said, even though he had retracted from it.' So I said to him, 'This breaks what is with them regarding analogy.' He said, 'Come, analogize for me.' I said, 'I analogize for you?' He said, 'So that you say what is stronger in terms of what is included in the analogy.' So I said to him, 'A man left a slave and did not leave wealth other than him, and the value of the slave is six hundred dirhams, and his debt is five hundred dirhams. So he freed him at the time of death, how should one deal with it?' He said, 'The slave is sold, so the creditors take five hundred dirhams, and the heirs take one hundred dirhams.' I said, 'Is it

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who emancipated his slave, and death had presented itself, and that was witnessed for him, and his value was six hundred dirhams, and upon him was a debt of three hundred dirhams, and he did not leave anything apart from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be one-sixth free from it. But rather, from it for him were three hundred dirhams, and three hundred dirhams were paid off from it, therefore, for him from the three hundred is a third, and it is a sixth from the total'.

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'O you who believe! The testimony between you when death approaches one of you, at the time of making the will, is two just persons from among you, or two others from among others than you' [5:106]. I said, 'What are "two others from among others than you"?' He said, 'They are two unbelievers (kafirs).' I said, '"Two just persons from among you"?' So he said, 'Two Muslims.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: Is the testimony of the people of one (religious) community valid from other than the people of their own community? He said: Yes, when they cannot be found from the people of their own community, the testimony of others is valid. It is indeed not right for anyone's right to be lost.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father — both together — from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'or two others from among others than you' He said: 'If the man was in a city in which there is no Muslim, the testimony of one who is not a Muslim upon the bequest is permissible.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the testimony of a woman who was present with a man making a bequest, with no other man with her. So he said: A quarter of what was bequeathed is permitted, in proportion to her testimony.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said regarding a bequest which none had witnessed except a woman: he permitted the testimony of the woman for one quarter of the bequest, in accordance with the measure of her testimony.

[Yahya ibn Muhammad said:] I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'O you who believe! The testimony between you when death approaches one of you, at the time of making the will, shall be two just persons from among you, or two others from among others than you.' He said: 'Those who are from among you are two Muslims, and those who are from among others than you are from the People of the Book. But if you do not find any from the People of the Book, then from the Magians, because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) established for the Magians the same Sunnah as the People of the Book with regard to the jizyah.' And that is when a man dies in a foreign land and does not find two Muslims; he should call two men from the People of the Book as witnesses, who shall be detained after the prayer, and they shall both swear by God, Mighty and Majestic: 'We shall not sell it for a price, even if it were a near kinsman, and we shall not conceal God's testimony, for then we would certainly be among the sinners.' He said: 'And that is when the guardian of the deceased has doubt about their testimony. If it becomes known that the two testified falsely, the guardian is not permitted to invalidate their testimony until he comes with two witnesses who shall stand in place of the first two witnesses, and they shall both swear by God: Our testimony is more rightful than theirs, and we have not transgressed, for then we would certainly be among the wrongdoers.' So when he does that, the testimony of the first two is invalidated, and the testimony of the later two becomes valid. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'This is more appropriate so that they should give testimony in its proper manner, or fear that oaths may be rejected after their oaths.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his men, raising it (marfu'), said: Tamim al-Dari, Ibn Baydi, and Ibn Abi Mariya went out on a journey. Tamim al-Dari was a Muslim, and Ibn Baydi and Ibn Abi Mariya were two Christians. With Tamim al-Dari was a bag containing goods, vessels engraved with gold, and a necklace, which he had brought out to one of the Arab markets for sale. Tamim al-Dari fell severely ill, and when death approached him, he handed over what was with him to Ibn Baydi and Ibn Abi Mariya, and instructed them both to deliver it to his heirs. So they both proceeded to Medina, having taken from the baggage the vessels and the necklace, and delivered the rest to his heirs. So the people noticed the absence of the vessels and the necklace, and the family of Tamim said to them: 'Was our companion ill for a long time and spent much on expenses?' They said: 'No, he was only sick for a few days.' They said: 'Was anything stolen from him on this journey?' They said: 'No.' They said: 'Did he trade and incur a loss?' They said: 'No.' They said: 'We are missing the finest things that were with him — vessels engraved with gold adorned with gems, and a necklace.' They said: 'Whatever was handed to us, we have delivered to you.' So they were brought before the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of God imposed an oath upon both of them. They swore, and he released them. Then those vessels and the necklace were found to be in their possession. So the guardians of Tamim came to the Messenger of God and said: 'O Messenger of God! What we claimed against Ibn Baydi and Ibn Abi Mariya has been proven.' So the Messenger of God awaited the ruling from God, Mighty and Majestic, in that matter. Then God, Blessed and Exalted, revealed: 'O you who believe! Take as witnesses between you two just persons from among you, or two others from outside you, when death approaches one of you at the time of making a will, if you are traveling in the land.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, permitted the testimony of the People of the Book for the bequest only, when one is traveling and cannot find Muslims. 'When the calamity of death befalls you, detain the two witnesses after prayer; then if you doubt them, they shall both swear by God: "We will not sell it for any price, even if a relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of God — for then we would certainly be

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When ten years come upon the boy, it is allowed for him with regards to his wealth, what he emancipates, gives in charity, and bequeaths, upon a known limit and right, so it is valid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The boy, when death presents itself to him, so he bequeaths and has not attained awareness (puberty), his bequest is valid for the relatives and is not valid for the strangers.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the boy reaches ten years, his bequest is valid.'

Humeed ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abu Al-Maghra' from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the boy reaches ten years, if he bequeaths a third of his wealth rightfully, his bequest is valid. And if he is a boy of seven years, and he bequeaths a small amount from his wealth rightfully, his bequest is valid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him) said: I wrote to him regarding a man who died, and he had an umm al-walad (concubine who bore a child), and he had allocated something for her during his lifetime, then he died. He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'For her is what her master remunerated to her during his lifetime in goodness, that is for her. The testimony of the man, and the woman, and the servant not having been accused of any wrong, would be acceptable upon that'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) Regarding the Umm al-Walad (concubine who bore her master a child), when her master dies and had bequeathed to her, he (peace be upon him) said: 'She is emancipated within the one-third share, and for her is the bequest.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubeyda who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a mother of a child of his, and from her was a boy for him. So when death presented itself to him, he bequeathed to her two thousand Dirhams, or more. Is it for the inheritors that they enslave her? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but she would be emancipated from a third of the deceased (legacy), and she would be given whatever was bequeathed to her by it. And in the Book of Al-Abbas, she would be emancipated from the share of her son, and she would be given from his third whatever he had bequeathed to her by it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abdul Rahman ibn Zayaba, who said: A woman bequeathed to me, saying: 'From my third, pay off my debt, and a part of it is for So-and-so.' So I asked Ibn Abi Layla about that, and he said: 'I do not see anything for her, as I do not know what 'a part' is.' Then I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about it after that, and informed him how the woman had spoken and what Ibn Abi Layla had said. He said: 'Ibn Abi Layla has lied. For her is a tenth of the third. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him), saying: 'Place on every mountain of them a part' — and the mountains at that time were ten, and 'a part' is the tenth of the thing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a part of his wealth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A part is one of ten.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Place on each of them a part on every mountain' — and the mountains were ten.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The part is one of ten, because the mountains are ten, and the birds are four'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Jamil, from Aban, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who bequeathed 'something' from his wealth, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The 'something' in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is one from six (1/6)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal or someone else, from Jameel, from Aban, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who bequeathed 'something' from his wealth. He said: 'The 'something' in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is one-sixth.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who bequeathed a 'portion' of his wealth, so he said: The 'portion' is one from eight (1/8). Due to the Words of Allah, Blessed and High, Indeed, the charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials (appointed) over them, and those whose hearts are made to incline (to Truth) and the (ransoming of) captives and those in debts and in the Way of Allah and the wayfarer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, who said, 'I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him)'; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who both said, 'We asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him)' about a man who bequeathed a 'portion' (sahm) from his wealth, and we do not know what this 'portion' is. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there not with you, among what has reached you from Ja'far (peace be upon him) nor from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), anything regarding it?' We said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! We have not heard our companions mentioning anything of this from your forefathers (peace be upon him).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The 'portion' is one from eight.' So we said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! How did it become one from eight?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not read the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I do read it, but I do not know which place it is.' The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials appointed over them, and those whose hearts are made to incline (to Truth) and the (ransoming of) captives and those in debts and in the Way of Allah and the wayfarer.' Then he (peace be upon him) made (the number) eight with his hand, and said: 'And similarly, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) divided it upon eight portions. Therefore, the 'portion' is one from eight.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man acknowledges a debt to an inheritor.' He said, 'It is permissible if he is wealthy (has the means to pay).'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to one of his inheritors that he had a debt upon himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the deceased was pleased (with the other heirs regarding the debt), then give it to the one to whom he bequeathed it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-'Ala' Bayya' al-Sabiri, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who entrusted a man with wealth. When death approached her, she said to him, 'The wealth that I gave to you is for so-and-so.' The woman died, and her guardians came to the man and said to him, 'There was wealth for our companion, and we do not see it except with you; so swear to us that there is nothing of hers with you.' Is he to swear to them? He said: 'If she was trustworthy in his presence, he should swear to them; and if she was suspected (of owing more), he should not swear, and he should place the matter upon what it was. Indeed, for her from her wealth is one-third.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who acknowledged to an inheritor of his, and he was ill, with a debt being upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is allowed for him (to pay off), when he acknowledge with it, besides the third'.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Walad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a sick man who acknowledged at the time of death to an inheritor that there was a debt for him upon himself. He (peace be upon him) said: That is permissible. I said: So if he were to bequeath to the inheritor something? He (peace be upon him) said: Permissible.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left a slave, so one of his children testified that his father had emancipated him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His testimony is accepted, and he is not liable for compensation, and the slave is made to work (serve) for what belonged to the other inheritors.'

Humeed ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who died and left a slave boy, so one of the inheritors testified that he was free. He said: If the witness is reliable, his testimony is accepted for his share, and he is asked to work (or compensate) for what belongs to the other inheritors.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, and Husayn ibn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died, and one of his inheritors acknowledged a debt on his behalf to a man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is binding upon him in his share (of the inheritance).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, by a chain of his, that he was asked about a man who dies and leaves dependents and upon him is a debt, 'Should he spend upon them from his wealth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is convinced that the debt which is upon him encompasses the entirety of the wealth, so he should not spend upon them, and if he is not convinced, so let him spend over them from the middle of the wealth.'

Humeed ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad, both together, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Similar to it, except that he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is established that what he left is insufficient to cover all his debt, then no expenditure should be made on them [the dependents], and if it is not established, then expenditure should be made on them from the middle of the wealth.'

Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Sulayman ibn Dawud or one of our companions, from him, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man from your mawali died and left behind young children, and left some property, and upon him was a debt, and the creditors do not know about it. If it is paid to his creditors, his children will remain, and they will have nothing.' So he said, 'Spend it upon his children.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If a man appoints another man as executor of his will while he (the latter) is absent, then it is not for him to repudiate (turn down) his appointment. But if he appoints him and he is in the city, then he has the choice: if he wishes he accepts, and if he does not wish he does not accept.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, from Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is appointed as executor of a will. He said: If it was sent to him from a city (far away), then he does not have the right to refuse it. But if he was in a city where someone else can be found (to serve as executor), then that is up to him.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man appoints his brother as executor of his will and he (the brother) is absent, then it is not permissible for him to refuse his appointment as executor, because if he were present and he refused to accept it, someone else would be sought.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fuzayl, from Rabi'i, from al-Fuzayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Concerning the man who is appointed as executor of a will, he said: 'If it (the appointment) was sent to him from a city, then it is not permissible for him to reject it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim — from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who appoints a man as executor of his will but he dislikes accepting it — Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not abandon him in this state.'

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A man whose father invited him to accept appointment as executor of his will — is it permissible for him to refuse to accept the executorship?' So he (peace be upon him) endorsed (in reply): 'It is not permissible for him to refuse.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Jameela, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a sword to a man, and it was in a sheath, and upon it were ornaments. So the inheritors said to him, 'For you is only the blade, and the wealth (ornaments) is not for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the sword with whatever is in it is for him.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I said, 'A man bequeathed a container to a man, and there was wealth in it. So the inheritors said, 'For you is only the container, and the wealth is not for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The container with whatever is in it is for him.''

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who said, 'This ship is for so-and-so,' and did not specify what was in it, and there was food in it. Should the man be given the ship and what is in it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It belongs to the one to whom it was bequeathed, unless the owner is accused (of insolvency or deceit), and there is nothing for the inheritors.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who bequeathed a sword to a man. So the inheritors said, 'You have only the iron, and the ornaments are not for you; other than the iron is not for you.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'The sword is for him, and its ornaments.'

From him, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a man a container (box), and there was wealth in the container. So the inheritors said, 'For you is the container, and whatever is in it is not for you'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The container along with whatever is in it, is for him'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man had two sons, so one of them died, and he left behind male and female children. So their grandfather bequeathed to them the portion of their father. Is this portion such that the male and the female are equal in it, or does the male have the share of two females? He (peace be upon him) signed: 'They enforce the bequest of their grandfather just as he ordered, God willing.' He said: And I wrote to him: A man had male and female children, so he acknowledged for them a property that it is for his children, and did not mention that it is to be divided between them according to the shares of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His obligations. Is the male and the female equal in it? He (peace be upon him) signed: 'They enforce in it the bequest of their father upon what he named. So if he had not named anything, they return it to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), God willing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya said, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man bequeathed a third of his wealth to his male mawali and his female mawali. Are the male and female equal in it, or is there for the male the share of two females from the bequest? So he (peace be upon him) signed: What the deceased bequeathed is valid, upon what he bequeathed, God willing.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who bequeathed a third of his wealth to his paternal uncles and his maternal uncles, he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the paternal uncles is two-thirds, and for the maternal uncles is one-third.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from his brother Ja'far ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a woman, so he associated in the bequest a child along with her. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is allowed, and the woman enforces the bequest and does not wait for the adulthood of the child. So when the child reaches adulthood, it is not for him to reject it, except for what was from alteration or change. Indeed, he has the right to return it to what the deceased had bequeathed to him.'

Muhammad said, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man bequeathed to his children, and among them were adults who had attained maturity, and among them were young ones. Is it permissible for the adults to execute his bequest and pay his debt, for whom the debt was established upon the deceased with just witnesses, before the young heirs reach maturity? So he (peace be upon him) signed: Yes, it is upon the adults from the children to pay their father's debt, and not to detain him because of that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya said, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'A man died and bequeathed to two men (as executors), is it allowed for one of them to deal separately with half the legacy, and the other with the other half?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'It is not befitting for both of them that they oppose the deceased, and that they should act according to what he ordered both of them, Allah willing.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, from their father, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: A man died and bequeathed to me and to another, or to two men (as executors). So one of them said, 'Take half of what he left and give me the half from what he left.' So the other refused him. They asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: 'That is for him (that he should refuse to take the half but they both should act as per the original bequest)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the seven walled gardens (enclosures) which were the legacy of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) for Fatima (peace be upon her). So he said: 'No, but rather they were a Waqf (endowment), and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to take from them whatever he spent on his guests, and the maintenance that was required for them. So when he passed away, Al-Abbas came disputing with Fatima (peace be upon her) regarding them. So Ali (peace be upon him) and others testified that they were a Waqf upon Fatima (peace be upon her), and they are: Al-Dallal, Al-Awaf, Al-Husna, Al-Safiya, what belonged to Umm Ibrahim, Al-Maysab, and Al-Burqa.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubaydullah al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: We asked him (peace be upon him) about the charity (khums) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the charity of Fatima (peace be upon her). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their charity is for Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib.'

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Madani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Maysab is that which Salman (peace be upon him) was contracted for, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed it upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), thus it is in her charities.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from his father, from Abu Maryam who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the charity of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the charity of Ali (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for us (peace be upon him).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Fatima (peace be upon her) made her charity to be for the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I read to you the bequest of Fatima (peace be upon her)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, so he brought out a box or a basket, and extracted a letter from it. So he read it: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is what Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), bequeathed. I bequeath her seven walled gardens: Al-Awaf, Al-Dallal, Al-Barqa, Al-Maysab, Al-Husna, Al-Safiya, and what belonged to the mother of Ibrahim, to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So if Ali passes away, then to Al-Hasan. So if Al-Hasan passes away, then to Al-Husayn. So if Al-Husayn passes away, then to the eldest of my children.' Allah was a Witness upon that, and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam; and it was written by Ali ibn Abi Talib. And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Asim ibn Humayd, similar to it, but did not mention a box or a basket, and she said: 'To the eldest of my children besides your children.'

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I read to you the bequest of Fatima (peace be upon her)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, so he brought out to me a parchment: 'This is what Fatima, daughter of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), bequeathed of her wealth to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and if he dies, then to Al-Hasan, and if he dies, then to Al-Husayn; and if Al-Husayn dies, then to the eldest of my children excluding your children: Al-Dallal, and Al-Awaf, and Al-Maysab, and Burqa, and Al-Husna, and Al-Safiya, and what was for the mother of Ibrahim. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Witness to that, and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) sent to me the will of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and it is: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is what Abd Allah Ali bequeathed and decreed regarding his wealth, seeking the Face of Allah, so that He may admit me into Paradise by it, and turn me away from the Fire by it, and turn the Fire away from me on the Day when faces become white and faces become black. That which was mine of wealth in Yanbu', known to me therein and what is around it, is charity, along with its slaves, except that Rabah, Abu Nayzar, and Jubayr are emancipated, there is no way for anyone over them, so they are my mawali, who work in the property for five years (hijj), and in it is their expenses and their livelihood, and the livelihoods of their families. And with that, all that was mine of wealth in Wadi al-Qura is for the children of Fatima, and its slaves are charity. And what was mine in Dayma and its people is charity, except that Zureeq has what I wrote for his companions. And what was mine in Udhaynah and its people is charity, and the two poor ones, as you know, are charity in the way of Allah. And that which I wrote from this wealth of mine is an obligatory, final charity, whether I am alive or dead. It is spent in every expenditure sought by which is the Face of Allah, in the way of Allah and His Face, and the relatives from the children of Hashim and the children of al-Muttalib, and the near and the far. For al-Hasan ibn Ali will oversee that, consuming from it with goodness and spending it wherever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sees fit, in a permissible manner, with no hardship upon him in it. So if he wishes to sell a share of the property to pay off a debt, let him do so if he wishes, and there is no hardship upon him in it. And if he wishes, he can make it a series of properties (waqf). And the children of Ali, their mawali, and their wealth are to al-Hasan ibn Ali. And if the house of al-Hasan ibn Ali is other than the house of charity, and it seems to him that he should sell it, let him sell if he wishes, with no hardship upon him in it. And if he sells, he divides its price into three thirds: he makes one third in the

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Ayoub ibn Atiyya Al-Hazza', who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) distributed the Fay (booty/wealth), and Ali (peace be upon him) was assigned a piece of land. He dug a well in it, and water gushed out towards the sky in the form of a camel's neck. So he named it 'Yanbu' (the gusher). The herald of good news came with the good news, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give the good news to the inheritors. It is a charity, irrevocable, for the pilgrims of the House of Allah and the passers-by in the Way of Allah. It shall not be sold, nor gifted, nor inherited.' So whoever sells it or gifts it, upon him is the Curse of Allah, the Angels, and all people. Allah will not accept from him any exchange or ransom.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Hisham ibn Ahmad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, all together, from Salima, the slave-girl of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when death presented itself to him, so he fell unconscious. When he regained consciousness, he said: 'Give seventy dinars to al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, and he was al-Aftas, and give so-and-so such and such, and to so-and-so such and such.' I said: 'Do you want to give a man who attacked you with a blade?' He said: 'Woe be unto you! Do you not read the Quran?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Have you not heard the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Those who join what Allah has bidden to be joined, and have awe of their Lord, and they are fearing the evil Reckoning?' Ibn Mahboub said in his hadith: 'He attacked you with a blade, intending to kill you?' So he said: 'Do you want that I should happen to be from those about whom Allah, Blessed and High, said: Those who join what Allah has bidden to be joined, and have awe of their Lord, and they are fearing the evil Reckoning?' Yes, O Salima! Indeed, Allah created Paradise and made it fragrant, and made its aroma fragrant, and its aroma can be found from a travel distance of two thousand years, and it would not be smelt by one disobedient to his parents (Aaq) and one who cuts off relationships.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about what the people say regarding bequeathing a third and a quarter at the time of death: Is it a correct, well-known matter, or how did your father do it? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A third, that is the matter which my father did. May Allah have mercy upon him.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and others, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed away and left sixty male slaves, so he emancipated a third of them. So I drew lots among them, and selected twenty, and I emancipated them.'

From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala and others, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) emancipated the mischievous ones from his slaves at the time of his death, and retained the good ones. So I said, 'O father! You are freeing these and retaining those.' He said, 'They had been subjected to discipline from me, so this is for that.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) fell ill with three illnesses. During every illness he bequeathed with a bequest, so when he recovered, he signed (approved) his bequest.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Nothing from the recompense follows the man after his death except for three qualities: a charity which he set flowing during his lifetime, so it continues to flow after his death; and a charity of an untouched woman not inherited, or a Sunnah of guidance which is acted upon after him, or a righteous child who supplicates for him. Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it, except that he said: 'Or a righteous child who seeks forgiveness for him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There does not follow the man after his death except for three qualities: a charity he made flow for the Sake of Allah during his lifetime, so it flows for him after his death; and a Sunnah of guidance which he enacted so it is acted upon after his death; and a righteous child who supplicates for him.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What attaches to a man after his death?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A Sunnah that he established which is acted upon after his death, so there will be for him a reward like that of the one who acts by it, without any deficiency in their rewards; and flowing charity which flows after him; and a righteous child who supplicates for his parents after their death, and performs Hajj on their behalf, and gives charity on their behalf, and emancipates (a slave), and fasts, and prays on their behalf.' I said: 'Shall I share them in my Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Shuayb, from Abu Kahmas, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Six (things) attach to the Believer after his death: a child who seeks Forgiveness for him, and a book he leaves behind, and a plant which he plants, and a well which he digs, and a charity which he makes to flow, and a Sunnah which is taken with (acted upon) from after it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man bequeathed to me (to be an executor), so I asked that he should associate with me a near relative of his. So he did it, and he, the one who bequeathed to me, mentioned that for him with the one who is an associate with regards to the bequest, are one hundred and fifty Dirhams as security, a bowl of silver. So when the man died, the executor said that he has a claim against him (the deceased) a certain measurements of wheat.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he establishes the evidence, otherwise there is nothing for him.' I said to him, 'Is it permissible for him that he takes anything from what is in his hands?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him.' I said, 'What is your view, if that man is inimical towards him, so he takes his wealth, and he is able to take from his wealth what he takes, that would be for him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This (situation) is not similar to this.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man bequeathed thirty dinars for the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her). He said: So the man brought it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it to so-and-so, an elder from the children of Fatimah (peace be upon her), and he was a breadwinner with scarcity (of means).' The man said to him: 'But rather, the man bequeathed it for the children of Fatimah.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, it does not fall upon the (general) children of Fatimah, and it falls upon this man (who is among them), and for him are dependants.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Hamza, who said: I said to him (peace be upon him): 'In our city, sometimes wealth is bequeathed to the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him), so they bring it to me. I dislike carrying it to you until I consult you.' He said: 'Do not bring it to me, and do not concern yourself with it.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it from them (peace be upon him), said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who bequeaths with the one-third, it would be reckoned for him from his Zakat'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is just in his bequest is like the one who gave it in charity during his lifetime; and whoever is inequitable in his bequest will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, and He will turn away from him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan, who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a person who made a bequest, but the executor did not memorize it except for one aspect from it. How should he deal with the remainder? So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'The remaining aspects, he should make them among the righteous (causes).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ja'far ibn Isa who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him regarding a man who bequeathed some of his one-third from after his death, from the yield of his estate, to an executor to place half of it in known places he had mentioned to him during every year, and the remainder of the one-third he can act regarding it with whatever he so desires and the executor agrees with it. So the executor enforced what had been bequeathed to him from the known named, and said regarding the remainder, 'I have rendered for so and so such and such (amount), and for so and so such and such (amount), in every year, and regarding the Hajj, such and such (amount), and regarding the charity such and such (amount) during every year. Then he changed with regards to all of that', so he said, 'I have decided that the first of what I view as being opposite of my first desires and views'. Is it for him that he retracts with regards to it, and give what he gives to others, or reduces them, or includes other along with them, if he so wants that?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is for him that he does whatever he so desires to, except if there happens to be a written agreement upon himself'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, from Sahib al-Askar (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We are brought something, and it is said, 'This is what was for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) with us.' So how should we deal with it?' He said: 'Whatever was for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) by reason of the Imamate, it is for me; and whatever was other than that, it is an inheritance according to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Malik, who said: I wrote to him: A man died and made everything of his during his lifetime, to be for you, and there was no child for him. Then a child was born (after his death) and his wealth had reached three thousand Dirham, and I had sent to you a thousand Dirhams. May I be sacrificed for you, So if you could let me know your view with regards to it, so that I can act upon it. So he wrote: 'I leave it for them'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Al-Husayn ibn Malik, who said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Know, my Master, that the son of a brother of mine died, so he bequeathed to my Master a place, and he bequeathed that everything in his house should be handed over, even the pegs, to be sold, and the price be given to my Master, and he bequeathed for Hajj, and he bequeathed for the poor from his family, and he bequeathed to his aunt and his sister with wealth. So I looked, and found that what he bequeathed was more than one-third, and perhaps it was close to half of what he left, and he left behind a son of his who was three years old, and left debts. So what is your view, my Master?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'Limit his bequest to one-third of his wealth, and distribute that among those he bequeathed to according to the measure of their shares, if Allah wills.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Ismail, from his father who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man to whom death presented itself, so he bequeathed to his son and two brothers. The son witnessed his bequest and the two brothers were absent. So when it was after a few days they both refused to accept the executorship in fear that his son would pounce upon the two of them, and they would not be able to act with what is befitting. So a cousin of theirs guaranteed to them both, and that he would be obedient among them, and that he would suffice for the two of them from his son. So they both entered into it with this condition, but his son did not suffice for the two of them, and it had been stipulated upon his son, and they both said, 'We are free from the executorship, and we are excused from neglecting the entirety of the matters and exiting from it.' Is it correct for both of them that they absolve themselves from what was in their hands and come out from it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is necessary for you to join upon whichever aspect it was, for you would be recompensed, perhaps that would resolve (the matters) with his son.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha and Muhammad ibn Yahya from the executor of Ali ibn al-Sari, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Ali ibn al-Sari died and bequeathed to me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'May Allah have mercy on him.' I said, 'And his son Ja'far ibn Ali had intercourse with his mother (from another wife), so he ordered me to remove him from the inheritance.' He (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Remove him from the inheritance, and if you are truthful, insanity will befall him.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I returned and presented myself to Abu Yusuf the Judge. He said to him, 'May Allah rectify you! I am Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Sari, and this is the executor of my father. Order him to hand over to me my inheritance from my father.' Abu Yusuf the Judge said to me, 'What do you say?' I said to him, 'Yes, this is Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Sari, and I am the executor of Ali ibn al-Sari.' He said, 'Then hand over his wealth to him.' I said, 'I want to speak with you.' He said, 'Approach me.' So I approached where no one could hear my speech, so I said to him, 'This one had intercourse with the mother of his father (his half-brother's mother), so his father ordered me and bequeathed to me to remove him from the inheritance and not to leave him anything. So I went to Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) in Medina, informed him and asked him, so he ordered me to remove him from the inheritance and not to leave him anything.' He said, 'By Allah, did Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) order you?' I said, 'Yes.' He made me swear an oath three times, then said to me, 'Execute what Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ordered you with, for his word is the word.' The executor said, 'So insanity befall him after that.' Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha said, 'So I saw him after that, and insanity had indeed befallen him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn Bukayr al-Taweel, who said: My father called me when death approached him, and he said: 'O my son! Take hold of the wealth of your younger brothers, conduct business with it, take half the profit for yourself, and give them the other half. And there is no guarantee (liability) upon you.' So the mother who gave birth to my father (his concubine) brought me before Ibn Abi Layla after my father's death, and she said to him: 'This one is eating the wealth of my son.' I said, so I narrated to him what my father had ordered me with. Ibn Abi Layla said: 'If your father ordered you with falsehood, I would not approve of it.' Then Ibn Abi Layla established a witness upon me: 'If I move it, then I am responsible for it.' So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) later, and I narrated to him my story, then I said to him: 'What do you see?' He said: 'As for the words of Ibn Abi Layla, I cannot refute them. And as for what is between you and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, there is no guarantee upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'My father was visited by death, so he was told to bequeath. He said, 'This is my son' — meaning Umar — 'so whatever he does, it is valid.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Your father has bequeathed and has been concise.' I said, 'He ordered such and such for you.' He said, 'It is valid.' I said, 'And he bequeathed the emancipation of a believing, knowledgeable slave-girl. When we emancipated her, it became clear to us that she was not of sound judgment (minor).' He said, 'It is valid for him. The example of that is like a man who buys a sacrificial animal on the understanding that it is fat, but finds it thin. It is valid for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who makes a bequest and is not unfair, and does not harm (anyone), is like the one who gives it in charity during his lifetime.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muthanna ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about a man who bequeathed to a man his children and their wealth, and permitted him at the time of the bequest to conduct business with the wealth and that the profit would be between him and them. So he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it, because the father had permitted him in that regard while he was alive.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Salih ibn Razin from Ibn Ahyam from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding A slave belonging to a group of people, permitted for him to trade, a man handed over to him one thousand dirhams and said to him, 'Buy a person from it and emancipate him on my behalf, and perform Hajj on my behalf with the remainder.' Then the owner of the thousand dirhams died. So the slave went and bought his own father and emancipated him on behalf of the deceased, and handed over to him the remainder regarding the Hajj on behalf of the deceased, so he performed Hajj on his behalf. So that reached the masters of his father, and his own master, and the inheritors of the deceased, so they all disputed over the one thousand dirhams. So the masters of the emancipated (father) said, 'You bought your father with our wealth,' and the inheritors said, 'You bought your father with our wealth,' and the masters of the slave said, 'You bought your father with our wealth.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the Hajj, it has passed with what was in it, it will not be returned, and as for the emancipated one, he is returned in slavery to the masters of his father, and whichever of the two groups established the evidence that the slave bought his father from their wealth, his slavery would be for them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran or someone else, from Aasim ibn Humyd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man bequeathed to a man a bequest from his wealth, a third or a quarter. The man was killed in error, meaning the testator.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This bequest is held from his inheritance and from his blood money (diyah).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: Muawiya ibn 'Ammar narrated to me, saying: The sister of Mufaddal ibn Ghayath died, and she bequeathed from her wealth: one-third in the Way of Allah, one-third to the poor, and one-third for Hajj. However, the wealth did not reach the amount required to fulfill all three fully. So I and he went to Ibn Abi Layla and related the story to him. He said, 'Allocate one-third to this, one-third to that, and one-third to that.' Then we went to Ibn Shubrumah, and he also said what Ibn Abi Layla had said. Then we went to Abu Hanifah, and he said as they both had said. So we went to Mecca, and he said to me, 'Ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' The woman had not yet performed Hajj. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'Begin with Hajj, for it is an obligation from Allah upon her. And whatever remains, allocate part of it to this and part of it to that.' He (the narrator) said: So I proceeded and entered the mosque, and I faced Abu Hanifah and said to him, 'I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about that which I asked you about, and he said to me, By Allah, he neither said good to me nor bad. And I came to his circle (gathering), and they had spread it out (as a ruling), and they said, 'Abu Hanifah said, I said, 'By Allah, it was such and such (anyway).' So they said, 'He (Abu Hanifah) informed us of this.' I said, 'By Allah, it was such and such.' So they said, 'He informed us of this.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Ismail ibn al-Ahwas, from his father, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a traveling man to whom death came, so he handed his wealth to a merchant and said, 'This wealth is for so-and-so son of so-and-so. I have neither little nor much in it, so hand it over to him; he may place it wherever he wishes.' The man died and did not give his companion (the one to whom he entrusted it) a specific instruction, nor did his companion know what motivated him to do so. He asked, 'What should he do with it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He places it wherever he wishes, if he is not commanded otherwise.'

And from him, from a man who bequeathed to a man that he should give his relatives from his estate such and such a Jarib of food. So years passed by and there was no surplus in his estate, but rather he needed loans and advances. Is it for him to borrow a loan in advance or not? So if he profits after that, does he compensate them for what was missed from the past years? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not mind if he gives them or takes, then pays it back.'

And from him, from a man who bequeathed bequests to his relatives, and the inheritor attained puberty, so he said to the executor that he should isolate a piece of land of the measure of what his bequests can be taken out from, when the inheritors distribute, and not include this land in their distribution, or how should he deal with it? So he said: 'Yes, such is befitting.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from his grandfather, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, that he said: I asked him, meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), about a man who had a son whom he acknowledged, but then disowned him and excluded him from the inheritance, while I am his executor. So what should I do? He (peace be upon him) said: The son is bound by his acknowledgment in public; the executor cannot repel him from anything that is known.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who had some dinars with me, and he was ill. So he said to me, 'If something happens to me, give so-and-so twenty dinars, and give my brother the remainder of the dinars.' So he died, and I did not witness his death. Then a truthful Muslim man came to me and said to me, 'He ordered me to say to you: Look at the dinars which I ordered you to give to my brother, so give in charity from them ten dinars, distribute them among the Muslims.' And his brother did not know that he had anything with me. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that you should give in charity from them ten dinars, just as he said.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt and died, so some of his sons took over what was upon him (his business/estate), and they were assessed a debt on behalf of their father. So they went to his house and bought it. With them were other inheritors, women and men, who had not approved of the sale nor consulted them regarding it. So is there anything upon them regarding that? He (peace be upon him) said: If the house was acquired from that business of his, then they were assessed regarding that business, so it is upon all of them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Mahzam, from Anbasa al-Abid, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Advise me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Prepare your apparatus and send forward your provision, and be your own executor, and do not say to others that they should send to you with what is adequate for you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) informing him that Is'haq ibn Ibrahim endowed a property for Hajj, and its mother of child, and what remained from it for the poor; and that Muhammad ibn Ibrahim witnessed me upon himself with wealth to be distributed among our brethren; and that among the Banu Hashim there is one whose right is known, who speaks with our words, who is in need, so do you think I should direct that to them if his way is the way of charity, because the endowment of Is'haq is indeed charity? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'I understood, may Allah have mercy on you, what you mentioned from the bequest of Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, may Allah be pleased with him, and what Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, may Allah be pleased with him, witnessed to you with that, and what you asked about regarding sending some of that to those from the Banu Hashim who have inclination and affection, who are deserving and poor. So send that to them, may Allah have mercy on you. For they, when they become to this scheme, are more deserving of it than others, due to a meaning, if I were to explain it to you, you would know it, if Allah wills.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding A man handed over wealth to another man and said, 'I am only handing it to you to be a reserve for my two daughters, So-and-so and So-and-so.' Then the old man changed his mind after handing over the wealth and took from it one hundred and twenty-five dinars, and bought a slave girl for his grandson. Then the old man died. A dispute arose between the two girls and the boy (or one of them), and they said to him, 'Woe to you, by Allah, you are marrying your slave girl unlawfully.
