Our father bought her for you from our wealth which he handed over to So-and-so, so he bought this slave girl for you from it. So you are marrying her unlawfully; she is not permissible for you.' So the youth refrained from the slave girl. What do you think about that? He (peace be upon him) said, 'Is not the man who handed over the wealth the father of the two girls, and he is the grandfather of the boy, and he is the one who bought the slave girl for him?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So tell him, let him go to his slave girl, since it was the grandfather who gave it to him and he is the one who took it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who died without a will, leaving male children [and female children] and young boys, and left slave girls and slaves. Is it permissible for the slave girls to be sold? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. And [I asked] about a man who accompanies another man on a journey, and the event of death befalls him, and he does not reach the will. How should he deal with his belongings? He has young and adult children. Is it permissible for him to hand over his belongings and his animals to his adult children or to the judge? If there is no judge in his town, how should he deal with it? And if he handed the wealth to his adult children and did not inform them, so he left and was not able to return, how should he deal with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the young ones come of age and seek him, but do not find him, there is no alternative but to take it out, unless it is by the order of the ruler.' And [I asked] about a man who dies without a will, and he has young and adult inheritors. Is it permissible to buy his servants and his belongings without the judge overseeing the sale of that? If a judge oversees it whom they have mutually agreed upon, and the Caliph did not consult him, is the buying from him acceptable or not? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the adults from his children are with him during the sale, there is no harm with it, if the inheritors are pleased with the sale, and a just price is established regarding that.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib who said: I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man, between me and him was a relationship, who died and left young children, and left slaves for him, boys and girls, and did not make a bequest. So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them to serve as the mother of his child, and what is your view regarding their sale? He said: 'If there is a guardian for them who manages their affairs, sells them on their behalf, and looks out for their interests, he is rewarded in doing so.' I said, 'So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, so he takes her as the mother of his child?' He said: 'There is no problem with that, if that evaluation is established for them by the supervisor with regards to what is correct for them, and there is not for them to retract with regards to what the supervisor establishes for them with regards to what is right for them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Zur'a, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died intestate (without leaving a will) and for him were sons and daughters, young and old, and for him were servants and slaves, and contracted ones. How should the inheritors deal with the distribution of that inheritance? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If a reliable man stands to distribute all of that for them, so there is no problem'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Ismail, from his father who said: I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about an executor of orphans, whose orphans reach adulthood, and he offers them what is theirs, but they refuse him. How should he deal with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return it to them and compel them to take it.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Muthanna ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about an orphan who has recited the Quran, and there is nothing wrong with his intellect, and he has wealth in the hands of a man. So the man who holds the wealth wanted to do business with the orphan's wealth on a profit-sharing basis (mudarabah). So the boy permitted him in that. He (the Imam) said: 'It is not correct that he works with it until he reaches puberty (ihtilam) and hands over his wealth to him.' He said: 'And if he were to reach puberty and there was not intellect for him, nothing would be handed over to him ever.' Humayd, from al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to that.

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Ribat and Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn Al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the orphan girl, when should her wealth be handed over to her? He said: When you know that she will neither spoil it nor waste it. So I asked him, if she had married? He said: If she were to get married, the possession (authority) of the executor is cut-off from her.

From him, from Al-Hasan, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Penetration (consummation) is not permitted with the girl until she reaches nine or ten years of age.

From him, from Al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Adam Bayy al-Lulu, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the boy reaches thirteen years, the good deed is written for him, and the evil deed is written against him, and he is punished. And when the girl reaches nine years, so it is like that, and that is because she menstruates at nine years.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a boy reaches his maturity at thirteen years, and enters the fourteenth, it becomes obligatory upon him what is obligatory upon those who have reached puberty, whether he has experienced wet dreams or not. Evil deeds are recorded against him, and good deeds are recorded for him, and everything is permissible for him unless he is weak-minded or foolish.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and appointed an executor, and he had a young son. The boy reached adulthood and went to the executor, saying to him, 'Return my wealth to me so that I may marry.' But he refused him. So he went and committed adultery. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Two-thirds of the sin of the adultery of this man is upon that executor, because he prevented the wealth from him and did not give it to him, so he could have married.'

He heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The owner of wealth is more rightful with (the disposition of) his wealth for as long as there remains something of the soul within him — he may place it wherever he wishes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Tha'laba, from Abu al-Hasan Umar ibn Shaddad al-Azdi and al-Sarri, both together, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man has greater right over his wealth for as long as the soul remains within him. If he were to bequeath the whole of it, it is permissible for him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi al-Sammal al-Asadi, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The dying person has more right over his wealth for as long as the soul remains within him.

The brother of Rumi ibn Umar bequeathed that all his wealth was for Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Amru said: Rumi informed me that he placed the will before Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, this is what my brother has bequeathed to you. I began to read it to him, and he would say to me: Pause! and he would say: Take such and such, and I have gifted you such and such, until I reached the end of the will. I looked, and he had taken only the one-third. Amru said: So I said to him, you have ordered me to carry a third to you, and you have gifted me the two-thirds? He said: Yes. I said, shall I sell it and bring it to you? He said: No, fulfill it according to what is easy for you — do not sell anything.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'a who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man who has a son — does he have the leeway to assign his wealth to his near relatives?' He said: 'It is his wealth; he can do with it whatever he wishes until death comes to him.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, both together from Safwan, from Murazim, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who gives something from his wealth during his illness. So he said: 'If he has set it aside (designated it), then it is permissible (valid), and if he bequeathed it, then it is from the one-third (of the estate).'

The dying one is more rightful with his wealth for as long as the soul is within him, distributing it. He (the Imam) said: Yes. So if he bequeaths by it, and if he exceeds, then there is nothing for him except the third.
I said to him: 'A man has a child — is it permissible for him to give his wealth to his relatives?' He said: 'It is his wealth. He may do with it whatever he wishes until death comes to him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Mahamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The human being is more rightful over (the distribution of) his wealth for as long as the soul is in his body.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'If a man has children, is it permissible for him to give his wealth to his relatives?' He said, 'It is his wealth; he does with it whatever he wishes until death comes to him. Indeed, the owner of the wealth may do with his wealth whatever he wishes as long as he is alive. If he wishes, he gifts it; and if he wishes, he gives it in charity; and if he wishes, he keeps it until death comes to him. But if he bequeaths it, then there is for him only the third [portion], except that the preference lies in that he does not neglect those he supports, nor harm his heirs. And it has been reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man from the Ansar who had freed his slaves, having no other slaves than them, so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) faulted him and said: "He left young children begging from the people."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra, from Abu Basir who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the bequest for the inheritor, so he said: It is permissible.
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased making a bequest for the inheritor with something. He said: 'Yes,' or he said: 'It is permissible for him.'
The bequest for the inheritor — there is no problem with it. Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similarly.
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the bequest for the inheritor, so he said: 'Permissible.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the bequest for the inheritor, so he said: 'It is permissible.' He said: Then he recited this verse: 'If he leaves behind wealth, the bequest is for the parents and near relatives.'
Muhammad ibn Qays said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who gives preference to some of his children over others. He said: Yes, and also his wives.

Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Ansari was in al-Medina while the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca. Death came to him, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca along with his companions, and the Muslims were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). Al-Bara' bequeathed that when he was buried, his face should be directed toward the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) — toward the qibla. He also bequeathed a third of his wealth. Thus the Sunnah was established by this.

Ahmad ibn Ishaq wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that Durrah, daughter of Muqatil, had died and left an estate — shares of land in various places — and she had bequeathed to her master from her shares an amount exceeding one-third. We are her executors and wished to report to our master: if he commanded that the bequest be executed as it stands, we would execute it; and if he commanded otherwise, we would comply with his command in everything he commands, Allah Willing. He said: So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'It is not obligatory for her from her estate except one-third; and if you are generous, and you are the inheritors, it would be permissible for you, Allah Willing.'
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who dies — what would he be entitled to from his wealth. So he said: 'For him is one-third of his wealth, and for the woman as well.'

The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) used to say: 'If I were to bequeath a fifth of my wealth, it would be more beloved to me than bequeathing a quarter; and if I were to bequeath a quarter, it would be more beloved to me than bequeathing a third; and whoever bequeaths a third and leaves nothing back, he has gone to the extreme.' He said: And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who died and bequeathed all or most of his wealth, saying: 'The bequest is to be returned to what is acceptable and away from what is reprehensible. So whoever wrongs himself and commits the reprehensible and injustice in his bequest, it shall be returned to what is acceptable, and the share of the inheritance shall be left for the heirs.' And he said: 'Whoever bequeaths a third of his wealth and leaves nothing back, he has reached the (upper) limit.' Then he said: 'If I were to bequeath a fifth of my wealth, it would be more beloved to me than bequeathing a quarter.'

al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — both together — from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever bequeaths a third has indeed harmed the inheritors; and the bequest of a fifth and a quarter is better than the bequest of a third; and whoever bequeaths a third has not held anything back.
Whoever bequeaths [with] a third has not left anything out.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Whoever bequeaths one-third of his wealth and is then killed by mistake, the one-third of his blood money is included in his bequest.
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: It is permissible for the testator to retract his bequest whether he was in good health or illness.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Buraid al-Ijli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is permissible for the owner of a bequest to retract it and to introduce changes in his will for as long as he remains alive.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) ruled that the mudabbar (slave to be freed upon the master's death) is counted from the one-third (of the estate), and that it is within the man's right to revoke his bequest, so he may increase or decrease in it, as long as he has not died.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from some of his companions, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: It is permissible for a man to change his bequest — freeing the one whom he had ordered to be kept as a slave, and enslaving the one whom he had ordered to be freed, and giving to the one whom he had deprived, and depriving the one whom he had given to — for as long as he has not died.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who bequeathed to another, and the beneficiary was absent, then the one who was bequeathed to died before the testator. He said: The bequest belongs to the heir of the one who was bequeathed to. He said: Whoever bequeaths to someone, whether present or absent, and the beneficiary dies before the testator, then the bequest belongs to the heir of the one who was bequeathed to, unless he (the testator) retracts his bequest before his death.

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to me (as executor) and ordered me to give something to an uncle of his every year. Then the uncle died. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Give it to his inheritors.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir who said: I asked him about a man who had been bequeathed to with a bequest, then he died before taking possession of it and did not leave any offspring. He said: 'Seek out an inheritor or a guardian for him, and hand it over to him.' I said: 'So if I do not know a guardian for him?' He said: 'Strive to the best of your ability to find a guardian for him; and if you still cannot find one, and God — Mighty and Majestic — knows the earnest striving from you, then give it in charity.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How did it come to be that when a man dies and his children are of the same kinship (equal in relation), the women inherit half the inheritance of the men, while they are weaker than the men and have less capability?' So he said: 'Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, preferred the men over the women by a degree, and because the women return to be dependents upon the men.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Nakhāʾī, who said: Al-Fahfakī asked Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him): 'What is the matter that the poor, weak woman takes one share, while the man takes two shares?' So Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, upon the woman there is no Jiḥād, nor Nafaqah (maintenance expenses), nor Maʿqilah (bride price/dowry payment), but rather that is upon the men.' So I said to myself: 'It was said to me that Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about this issue, and he answered him with this answer.' So Abū Muḥammad (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: 'Yes, this is the issue of Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ, and the answer from us is one. When the meaning of the issue is one, what happened to our last one [Imam] happened to our first one [Imam], and our first one and our last one are equal in Knowledge, and for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) is their preference.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Hisham, from Al-Ahwal, who said: Ibn Abi Al-Awja said to me, 'What is the matter that the poor, weak woman takes one share and the man takes two shares?' So one of our companions mentioned this to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Indeed, the woman is not obligated with Jihad, nor expenses, nor a stronghold (household expenses), and rather that is upon the men. And for that reason, He made for the woman one share and for the man two shares.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man dies and leaves sons, the eldest is entitled to the sword, the armor, the ring, and the Quran. If an event (death) befalls him, then it is for the eldest among them.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) that when a man leaves behind a sword and weapons, it is for his son, and if he has sons, it is for the eldest among them.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When the man dies, the eldest of his sons inherits his sword, his Mus'haf (Quran codex), his ring, and his armor.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) inherited the Knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Fatima (peace be upon her) inherited his legacy.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdul Malik, from Haydar, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Who inherited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Fatima (peace be upon her), and she inherited the chattels of the house, and the assets, and all that which belonged to him (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Salama ibn Muhraz, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'An Armenian man died and bequeathed to me.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'And what is an Armenian?' I said, 'A Nabatean from the Nabateans of the mountains, died and bequeathed to me his legacy, and left a daughter.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Give her half.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I informed Zurara of that, and he said to me, 'I was being cautious for you; rather, the wealth is for her.' So I entered upon him (peace be upon him) afterwards and said, 'May Allah improve you! Our companions claimed that you were cautious with me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, by Allah, I was not cautious with you, but I was cautious over you lest you be held responsible (for giving too little). So did anyone know of that?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So give her what remains.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Khidash Al-Minqari, that he asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left his daughter and his brother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth is for the daughter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a man who died and left his daughter and a sister of his father and mother. He said: 'The wealth is for the daughter, and there is not for the sister of the father and the mother anything.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Bureyd Al-Ajaly, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man died and left his daughter and his uncle.' He said, 'The wealth is for the daughter and there is nothing for the uncle,' or he said, 'There is nothing for the uncle with the daughter.'

Humayd ibn al-Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Hamzah ibn Humran from al-Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i from Abdullah ibn Muhraz, the seller of Qalanis, who said: A man bequeathed to me (as executor) and left five hundred dirhams or six hundred dirhams, and left a daughter, and said to me, 'The paternal relatives (asabah) are in Syria.' So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: 'Give the daughter half, and the other half to the paternal relatives.' So when I arrived in Kufa, I informed our companions of his saying, so they said, 'He was dissimulating (taqaya) for you.' So I gave the other half to the daughter. Then I went for Hajj and met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I informed him with what our companions had said, and I informed him that I had handed over the other half to the daughter. So he said: 'You did well. I only gave you the ruling out of fear of the paternal relatives being upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Muhraz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man left behind his daughter and a sister of his father and mother.' He said, 'All the wealth is for the daughter, and there is nothing for the sister of the father and mother.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-K Muhammad al-Kinji from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn Muhraz who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to me and died, and left a daughter. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give the daughter half, and leave for the guardians half.' So I returned. So our companions said, 'No, by Allah, there is nothing for the guardians.' So I returned to him the next day and said to him, 'Our companions said, there is nothing for the guardians, and it was out of dissimulation for you.' So he said, 'No, by Allah, I was not dissimulative to you, but I feared over you that you would be seized for the half. So if you are not afraid, hand over the other half to the daughter, for Allah will be Leading you.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: The daughters of the daughter stand in the place of the daughter when there are no daughters of the deceased and no other heir besides them; and the daughters of the son stand in the place of the son when there are no daughters or sons of the deceased and no other heir besides them.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: The son of the son stands in the place of his father.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The daughters of the daughter inherit when there are no daughters; they take the place of the daughters.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The daughters of the daughter stand in the place of the daughter when there are no daughters for the deceased and no other heir besides them; and the daughters of the son stand in the place of the son when there is no son for the deceased and no other heir besides them.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, and Ali bin Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali bin Ra'ab and Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left his two parents, he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the father are two shares, and for the mother is one share.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who left his mother and his brother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sheikh, do you want (the ruling) based on the Book (Quran)?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the closest (relative), then the closest.' I said, 'So the brother does not inherit anything?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I have informed you that Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the closest (relative), then the closest.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Hammad from Ibn Miskin from Mushamil ibn Sa'd from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who left his parents. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from three shares: for the mother one share, and for the father two shares.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I said to Zurara: 'Indeed, people narrated to me from him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from his father (peace be upon him), regarding matters of inheritance (al-fara'id). So I will present them to you. Whatever of it is false, say And I said to him: 'A man narrated to me from one of the two (peace be upon them) regarding two parents and brothers of the mother, that they are barred (blocked) and do not inherit.' He said: 'This, by Allah, is false. But I will inform you, and I will not narrate to you anything (as a formal hadith). And that which I am saying to you, by Allah, is the truth.' Indeed, if a man leaves behind his two parents, then for the mother is one-third and for the father is two-thirds in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Majestic. So if there are brothers for him (meaning for the deceased), meaning brothers of the father and mother, or brothers of the father, then for his mother is one-sixth, and for the father is five-sixths. And the father is given the extra share due to his dependents. And as for the brothers of the mother who are not of the father, then they do not block the mother from the one-third, nor do they inherit. And if a man dies and leaves his mother, and brothers and sisters of the mother and father, and brothers and sisters of the father, and brothers and sisters of the mother, and the father is not alive, then they do not inherit, nor do they block her, because he is not a Kalala (one who has neither parents nor offspring).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the deceased leaves two brothers, they are brothers with the deceased; they both block the mother from the third [share]. And if there was one, he would not block the mother. And he (peace be upon him) said: When there are four sisters, they block the mother from the third because they are in the position of the two brothers. And if there were three, they would not block [her].

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mohsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Fazl Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaaq, said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about two parents and two sisters (of the father and mother); would these two block the mother from the third? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'So if they are three?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'So if they are four?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The mother is not excluded from the one-third share if there is no child, except for two brothers or four sisters.

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Fazl Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaaq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The mother is not barred from the third except by two brothers or four sisters of the father and mother, or of the father.

And by his chain, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying that the siblings from the mother do not bar the mother from the third.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Zurara! What do you say regarding a man who leaves his two parents and his brothers from his mother?' I said, 'A sixth for his mother, and whatever remains is for the father.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From where did you say this?' I said, 'I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying in His Book: "If he has brothers, then his mother shall have the sixth."' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to you, O Zurara! Those are the brothers from the father. So if the brothers were from the mother, they would not bar the mother from the third.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubyd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Safwan, or he said, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had me read a sheet of the Book of Obligations (inheritance shares), which was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and written by Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand. So I found therein: a man who left his daughter and his mother. For the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the mother is the sixth, one share. The wealth is divided upon four shares. So whatever comes to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to one share, it is for the mother. He said, 'And I read in it: a man who left his daughter and his father. So for the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the father is the sixth, one share. The wealth is divided upon four shares. So whatever comes to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to one share, it is for the mother.' Muhammad said, 'And I found in it: a man who left his two parents and a daughter. So for the daughter is the half, three shares, and for the two parents, for each one of them, is the sixth, (one share for each of the two). The wealth is divided upon five shares. So whatever comes to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever comes to two shares, it is for the two parents.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said: I found in the Parchment of Inheritance Shares that a man died and left behind his daughter and his two parents, so for the daughter is three shares, and for the two parents, for each one of them is one share. The wealth is divided into five parts, so whatever amount constitutes three parts belongs to the daughter, and whatever amount constitutes two parts belongs to the two parents.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the grandfather, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not find anyone who has spoken regarding it except by his own opinion, except for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' I said: 'May Allah perfect you, so what did the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say regarding it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is tomorrow, meet me until I make you read it in a book.' I said: 'May Allah perfect you, narrate to me, for your hadith is more beloved to me than you making me read it in a book.' So he said to me for the second time: 'Listen to what I am saying to you. When it is tomorrow, meet me until I make you read it in a book.' So I went to him the next day after the noon prayer, and it was my time when I would be alone with him, between the noon and afternoon prayers. I disliked asking him except when alone, out of fear that he would issue a verdict to me due to the presence of others, through dissimulation (taqiyyah). So when I entered upon him, he turned to his son Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'Make Zurara read the Parchment of the Inheritance Shares.' Then he arose to sleep. So I and Ja'far (peace be upon him) remained in the room. He stood up and brought me a parchment like the thigh of a camel, and said: 'I will not make you read it until you make Allah a guarantee upon you that you will not narrate to anyone what you read in it, ever, until I permit you' — and he did not say 'until my father permits you'. I said: 'May Allah perfect you, and why do you restrict me, and your father did not command you with that?' He said to me: 'You will not look in it except upon what I have said to you.' I said: 'So that is for you.' And I was a man knowledgeable about the inheritance shares and bequests, perceptive of them, and calculating them. I had waited a long time seeking something cast to me from the inheritance shares and bequests that I did not know, so I could not attain it. So when he cast towards me a side of the parchment, it was a thick book, recognizable as being from the books of the predecessors. So I looked into it, and found in it the opposite of what was in the hands of the people regarding the close relative (al-sila

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said: I said to Zurara, 'I heard Muhammad ibn Muslim and Bukayr narrating from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a husband, two parents, and a daughter. So for the husband is a quarter, three shares from twelve, and for the two parents are two sixths, four shares from twelve, and five shares remain, so they are for the daughter, because if she were a male, she would not have other than five shares from twelve; and if there were two females, so for both of them is five shares from twelve, because if they were two males, they would not have other than what remains, five shares from twelve.' Zurara said, 'This is the truth, when you want to apply the 'awl (deficiency/proportioning), so make the fixed shares such that they do not suffer 'awl. Indeed, the reduction enters only upon those who have the excess from the children and the sisters from the father and the mother. As for the husband and the brothers from the mother, indeed they are not reduced from what Allah has named for them.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Safwan handed over to me a book for Musa ibn Bakr, so he said to me, 'This is what I heard from Musa ibn Bakr and read out to him.' So, in it was Musa ibn Bakr from Ali ibn Saeed from Zurara who said: 'This is from what there is no differing therein in the presence of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), having both been asked about a woman who left her husband, and her mother, and her two daughters. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the husband is the quarter, and for the mother is the sixth, and for the two daughters is what remains because both of them, had they been men, there would not be for the two of them anything except what remains, and (the share of) the woman does not exceed the share of the man, even if she were to be in his place.' And if the deceased leaves a mother, and a father, and a wife, and a daughter, so the Obligatory (legislated shares) are from twenty four shares – for the wife would be an eighth, being three shares from twenty four shares; for the two parents would be two sixths, being eight shares, for each one of them, four shares; and for the wife would be the eight, being three shares, and for the daughter would be the half, being twelve shares, and the remaining one share would revert upon the daughter and the two parents in accordance of their shares, and nothing would revert to the wife (from that one remaining share). And if he left a father, and a husband, and a daughter, so for the father would be two shares from twelve, and it is the sixth; and for the husband would be the quarter, being three shares from twelve; and for the daughter would be the half, being six shares from twelve, and the remaining one share would revert upon the daughter and the father upon the measurement of both their shares, and nothing would revert to the husband (from that one remaining share). And if he left a father, and a husband, and a daughter, so for the father would be two shares from twelve, and it is the sixth; and for the husband would be the quarter, being three shares from twelve; and for the daughter would be the half, being six shares from twelve, and the remaining one share would revert upon the daughter and the father upon the measurement of both their shares, and nothing would revert to the husband (from that

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mohsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a husband and two parents, he said: 'For the husband is the half, and for the mother is the one-third, and for the father is what remains.' And he said regarding a woman with two parents: 'For the woman is the one-quarter, and for the mother is the one-third, and what remains is for the father.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a husband and two parents, he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the husband is the half, and for the mother is the third, and what remains is for the father'.

And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah who said: I said to Zurara, 'Some people have narrated to me from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) various matters regarding the fixed shares (of inheritance), so I will present them to you. Whatever of them is false, say,

Humeyd ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abdullah ibn Wazzah from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who passed away and left her husband, and her mother, and her father. He said: 'It is from six shares – for the husband is the half, being three shares, and for the mother is the one-third, being two shares, and for the father is the one-sixth, being one share'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Yazid al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Your son is more entitled with respect to you than your grandson; and your grandson is more entitled with respect to you than your brother. And your full brother (from your father and mother) is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal half-brother. And your paternal half-brother is more entitled with respect to you than your maternal half-brother. And the son of your full brother is more entitled with respect to you than the son of your paternal half-brother. And the son of your paternal half-brother is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal uncle. And your paternal uncle who is a full brother of your father (from both his father and mother) is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father. And your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father is more entitled with respect to you than your paternal uncle who is a maternal half-brother of your father. And the son of your paternal uncle who is a full brother of your father is more entitled with respect to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father. And the son of your paternal uncle who is a paternal half-brother of your father is more entitled with respect to you than the son of your paternal uncle who is a maternal half-brother of your father.

Ibn Bukayr narrated to me from Zurara who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'And to everyone We have appointed heirs of what parents and near relatives leave' [Quran 4:33]. He said: 'It only means by that the priority of entitlement of the womb relations in inheritances, and it does not mean the guardians of bounty. Thus, the most entitled to the deceased is the nearest of them to him from the womb relation which flows toward him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, and from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man leaves his father or his mother or his son or his daughter, if he leaves one of these four, then they are not those meant by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He said: 'Say: Allah gives you a verdict concerning the Kalala.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ali ibn Ribat from Hamzah ibn Humran who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Kalalah, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which is not a son and not a father'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Kalalah is one who has neither a son nor a father.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said: A dispute arose between two men from the sons of my uncle regarding inheritance, so I advised them to write a letter to him regarding that so they might derive his view. So they both wrote to him together: 'May Allah make us your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who left her husband and her daughter and her mother?' And I said: 'May I be your ransom, if you see fit to answer us, answer us with the bitterness of the truth.' So a letter came out to them both: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. May Allah grant us and you good health, with the best of health. I understood your letter wherein you mentioned that a woman died and left her husband and her daughter and her sister from her father and her mother. So the prescribed share is for the husband one-quarter, and whatever remains is for the daughter.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Muhraz, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man left his daughter and his sister (from his father and mother).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth, all of it, is for the daughter, and there is nothing for the sister (from the father and mother).' So I said, 'We have need for this ruling, and the deceased was a man from those people (non-Muslims), and his sister was a believer, understanding.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So take the half for her. Take from them as they take from you regarding their ways and their judgments.' Ibn Udhaynah said, 'So I mentioned that to Zurara, so he said, 'Surely what Ibn Muhraz has come with is enlightening.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A woman left behind her husband, her brothers from her mother, and her sisters from her father. He said: For the husband is the half, which is three shares; and for the brothers from the mother is the third, the male and the female are equal in it; and a share remains, so it is for the brothers and sisters from the father, for the male is like the share of the two females, because the shares do not increase (due to deficiency) and the husband is not reduced from the half, nor the brothers from the mother from their third. So if they are more than that, they are partners in the third. And if there is one, then for her is the sixth. And what Allah Blessed and High meant by His words: 'And if a man is inherited by a Kalala or a woman, and for him is a brother or a sister, so for each one of them is the sixth. So if they are more than that, they are partners in the third' — He meant by that specifically the brothers and sisters from the mother. They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the Kalala. If a person dies and has no child, and for him is a sister, meaning a sister from mother and father or a sister from father, so for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if there is no child for her. And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is like the share of the two females. So they are the ones who are increased and decreased, and similarly are their children who are increased and decreased. And if a woman left her husband, her brothers from her mother, and her two sisters from her father, then for the husband is the half, three shares, and for the brothers from the mother are two shares, and a share remains, so it is for the two sisters from the father. And if there was one, it is for her, because the two sisters from the father, if they were two brothers from the father, would not be increased over what remains. And if there was one, or there was in the place of the one a brother, he would not be increased over what remains. And the female from the sisters and from the children is not increased over what if it were a male, it would not be increased upon him.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin and Abu Ayyub and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'What do you say regarding a woman who died and left her husband, and her brothers from her mother, and brothers and sisters from her father?' He said: 'For the husband is the half, being three shares, and for her brothers from her mother is the one-third, being two shares, male and female being equal in it, and the one remaining share, so it is for the brothers and sisters from the father, for the male is like the portion of two females, because the shares do not increase (deficiency), and that the husband is not reduced from the half, nor the brothers from the mother, from their third, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "But if they are more than that, they shall be sharers in the third." And if there was one, so for him is the one-sixth.' And what Allah means by His Elevated Words, 'And if a man is inherited by a Kalala or a woman, and for him is a brother or a sister, so for each one from them is the one-sixth,' is that He means by that the brothers and sisters from the mother in particular. They ask you for a verdict. Say: Allah gives you a verdict concerning the Kalala. If a person died and there is no child for him, and for him is a sister, meaning a sister from a father and a mother, or a sister from a father, so for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if there is no child for her. So if there are two, so for the two of them is two-thirds from what he left, and if there were brethren, men and women, so for the male is like the portion of two females. And they are the ones who are increased and decreased. He said: 'And if a woman left her husband, and her two sisters from her mother, and her two sisters from her father, for the husband is the half, being three shares, and for her two sisters from her mother is the one-third, being two shares, and for her two sisters from her father is the one-sixth, being one share. And if she was only one, so it is for her, because the two sisters from the father do not increase over what remains. And if there was a brother from the father, he would not increase over what remains.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Bukayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked him about two sisters and a husband, so he said: 'The half and the half'. So the man said, 'May Allah keep you well! Allah has named for them both more than this. For the two of them is the two-thirds'. So he said: 'So what would you say regarding a brother and a husband?' So he said, 'The half and the half'. So he said, 'Has not Allah named the wealth, so He said [4:176] and he shall be her heir when there is no child for her?'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man leaves his daughter, and his sister from his father and his mother.' So he said, 'The wealth, all of it, is for his daughter.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Musa ibn Bakr who said: I said to Zurarah: Indeed, Bukayr narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that the shares of brothers (from the father) and sisters (from father and mother) are increased and decreased, because their shares are not greater than the share of brothers and sisters (from father and mother) if they were in their place. Because Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, says: 'If a man dies leaving no child, and he has a sister, then she receives one-half of what he left; and he inherits her if she leaves no child.' He says that he inherits all her property if she leaves no child. Despite this, they give the complete share to the one whom Allah has specified as receiving one-half, and they give to the one whom Allah has specified as receiving the entire property less than one-half. And the woman's share is never more than the man's share if he were in her place. He said: Then Zurarah said, 'This is established among our companions; they do not differ regarding it.'

A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Jamil from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad who has narrated the following: I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who dies and leaves behind his daughter, his sister from his both parents. He (the Imam) said, ‘The entire legacy belongs to his daughter.’” Al-Fadl has said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made a share for the sister if she does not leave behind a child saying, ‘. . . if a man dies and does not leave behind a child and has a sister her share is one-half of the legacy.’ If he leaves behind a child then there is nothing for her. If anyone gives to her, it is opposing Allah and His messenger. The same is the case with the children of children male or female regardless how far below they may be. Brothers and sisters do not inherit with a child and so also is the case with the existence of one or both parents. [Note: The words of al-Fadl continues for the next several pages of the Arabic text and are not translated.]

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, all of them, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the obligatory share of the grandfather, so he said: 'I do not know anyone among the people who has a ruling for it except by personal opinion, except for Ali (peace be upon him), for he ruled in it with the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Bukayr and Al-Fadl and Muhammad and Bureyd, from one of the two (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the grandfather with the brothers (from the father) becomes like one of the brothers, whatever number they reach. He said, I said, 'A man left his brother from his father and mother, and his grandfather,' or I said, 'Left his grandfather, and his brother from his father and mother.' He said, 'The wealth is divided between them, and even if there were two brothers or a hundred thousand, so for him is like the share of one of the brothers.' He said, I said, 'A man left his grandfather and his sister.' So he said, 'For the male is like the portion of the two females, and if there were two sisters, so the half is for the grandfather and the other half for the two sisters, and if they were more than that, then upon this calculation, and if he left brothers and sisters from a father and mother, or from a father and a grandfather, so the grandfather is one of the brothers, so the wealth is between them, for the male is like the portion of the two females.' Zurara said, 'This is from what is not taken against me; I have heard it from his father, and from him before that, and there is no doubt or difference with us regarding that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left behind his wife, his sister, and his grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from four shares: for the wife is the quarter, and for the sister is one share, and for the grandfather are two shares.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding six brothers and a grandfather: He said: For the grandfather is the seventh.

And from him, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Mushma’al Bin Sa’ad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who left five brothers and a grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from six (shares), for every one among them, a share'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who left his brother from his father and mother, and his grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth is divided between the two of them, two halves. And if there were two brothers, or a hundred, the grandfather would be with them like one of them; the grandfather receives what one of the brothers receives.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he left his sister, then for the grandfather are two shares, and for the sister is one share. And if there were two sisters, then for the grandfather is the half, and for the two sisters is the half.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he left brothers and sisters from a father and a mother, the grandfather would be like one of the brothers; for the male is the portion of two females.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left his wife, his sister, and his grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from four shares – for the wife is the quarter, and for the sister is one share, and for the grandfather are two shares'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Jamil ibn Darraj, from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: The grandfather is apportioned equally with the brothers, whatever their number may be, even if they were one hundred thousand.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A brother from the father, and the grandfather?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth is between the two of them, equally'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all together from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the brothers from the mother with the grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The brothers from the mother, their prescribed share is one-third, with the grandfather.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Husayn ibn Umara, from Misma'a Abu Sayyar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left brothers and sisters from the mother, and a grandfather. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The grandfather is at the status of the brother from the father, for him is two-thirds; and for the brothers and sisters from the mother is one-third, so they are partners in it, equally.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Give to the sisters from the mother their legislated shares with the grandfather.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the brothers from the mother with the grandfather, he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the brothers from the mother with the grandfather, their share is the third with the grandfather'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Salih ibn Khalid from Abu Jameelah from Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the brothers from the mother with the grandfather, he (peace be upon him) said: 'For the brothers from the mother is their share, being one-third, with the grandfather.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the brothers from the mother, with the grandfather, so he said: For the brothers from the mother, their legislated share is one-third, with the grandfather.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) spread out a parchment, and the first thing that met my eyes in it was: 'A son of a brother and a grandfather, the wealth is divided between them into two halves.' So I said, 'May I be your ransom, the judges with us do not rule for a son of a brother with a grandfather in anything.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed this book is written by Ali (peace be upon him) and dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Qasim ibn Suleyman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) would make the son of the brother inherit with the grandfather the inheritance of his father.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Abu Shu'ayb narrated from Rifa'ah from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him about a son of a brother and a grandfather, so he said: The wealth is divided between the two of them, two halves.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I looked at a parchment which Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was looking at, so I read in it written: 'A son of a brother and a grandfather, the wealth between them is equal.' So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, those among us do not judge by this judgment, nor do they give anything to a son of a brother along with a grandfather.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'But indeed, it was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from his mouth and written by Ali (peace be upon him) by his hand.'

Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abu al-Maghra' from Sama'ah from Abu Baseer who said: I heard a man asking Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I was in his presence, about a son of a brother (nephew) and a grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth is to be divided between the two of them, in two halves.'

Al-Fadl, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from some of the companions of Abu Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the daughters of a sister and a grandfather, he said: 'For the daughters of the sister is one-third, and what remains is for the grandfather. So he established the daughters of the sister in the place of the sister, and made the grandfather at the status of the brother.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who was owned by her husband (i.e., a concubine or wife) but her husband had not yet had sexual intercourse with her, and she died, leaving behind her mother, two brothers from her father and mother, her grandfather (father of her mother), and her husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The husband is given half, and the mother is given the remainder, and the grandfather is given nothing because his daughter (the mother) blocks him from the inheritance, and the brothers are given nothing.'

Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahboub from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left his father, and his uncle, and his grandfather. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The father blocks the grandfather. The inheritance is for the father and there is nothing for the uncle and the grandfather'.

And from him and Ali ibn Abdullah, both together, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), 'A woman died and left her husband, and her two parents, or her grandfather, or her grandmother. How should her inheritance be distributed?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'For the husband is the half, and what remains, so it is for the two parents'. And it has also been reported as well that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) provided the one-sixth for the grandfather and the grandmother.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) provided the grandmother with one-sixth.

From him, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave the grandmother, mother of the father, one-sixth, and her son was alive; and gave the grandmother, mother of the mother, one-sixth, and her daughter was alive.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) provided the grandmother with one-sixth, and did not legislate anything specific for her.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) provided the grandmother with one-sixth as a provision.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Aban ibn Taghlb was with him. So I said, 'May Allah improve your state.' Indeed, my daughter died and my mother is alive.' So Aban said, 'There is nothing for your mother.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! Give her the one-sixth.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ismail ibn Mansur, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When four grandmothers gather, two from the side of the mother and two from the side of the father, one is discarded from the side of the mother by lot, so the one-sixth share is divided among the three. And similarly, when four grandfathers gather, one is discarded from the side of the mother by lot, and the one-sixth share is divided among the three.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, all of them from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something from the obligatory inheritance shares, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I bring out for you the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?' So I said, 'The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not been studied.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not been studied?' So he (peace be upon him) brought it out, and it was a splendid book, and therein was: a man who died and left his paternal uncle and his maternal uncle. He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the paternal uncle is two-thirds and for the maternal uncle is the one-third'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The maternal uncle and the maternal aunt inherit when there is no one else with them. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Wuheyb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The maternal uncle and the maternal aunt inherit when there is no one else with them who inherits other than them. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'And those of kinship among each other are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mohsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a paternal aunt and a maternal aunt, he (peace be upon him) said: 'One-third and two-thirds' — meaning for the paternal aunt is two-thirds and for the maternal aunt is one-third. Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Al-Muthanna, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Similar to it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan from Wahb from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who left his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, he said: For the paternal aunt is two-thirds and for the maternal aunt is one-third.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and leaves behind his maternal uncle, his maternal aunt, his paternal uncle, his paternal aunt, his son, his daughter, his brother, and his sister. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of these inherit and possess. So when the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt gather together, then for the paternal aunt is two-thirds, and for the maternal aunt is one-third.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and left his two maternal aunts and his adherents, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The possessors of relationships are nearer to each other' – the wealth is divided between the two maternal aunts.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abu Al-Maghra, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: If a man dies and leaves behind his paternal aunt and his maternal aunt, then for the paternal aunt are two-thirds, and for the maternal aunt is one-third.
And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) has said: 'The maternal uncle is an inheritor of the one who has no inheritor for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, altogether from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who died and no one was known to be for her, and she had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritance, all of it, is for her husband.' From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halbi, from Ayub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Baseer who said, 'I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he called for Al-Jami'a (the Book). So we looked into it, and therein was, a woman who died and left her husband, not having an inheritor for her other than him, for him was the wealth, all of it'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wahb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who died and left her husband, he said: The wealth is for the husband, meaning when there is no other inheritor for her besides him.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, similar to that. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him (peace be upon him). Regarding a woman who died and left her husband, he said: 'The wealth is for the husband,' meaning if there is no other inheritor for her besides him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'A woman died and left her husband.' He said, 'The wealth is for him.' He said, 'Its meaning is that there is no inheritor for her besides him.'

Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who dies and does not leave an inheritor other than her husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritance, all of it, is for him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Uyayna, the seller of reeds, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A woman died and left her husband.' He said, 'The wealth, all of it, is for the husband.'

A number of our companions narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from 'Uyaynah, the seller of reeds, from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'A woman died and left behind her husband.' He said, 'All of her property belongs to the husband.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Nueym al-Sahhaf who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, the merchant of al-Sabiriyyah, died and bequeathed to me, and left a wife for him, and did not leave an heir other than her. So I wrote to al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), and he wrote to me: 'Give the woman one-quarter, and carry the remainder to us.'

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn and Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Mushamil, and from Ibn Ribat, from Mushamil, all of them from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) read out to me regarding the obligatory shares of inheritance: A woman who passed away and left her husband. He said: 'The wealth, all of it is for the husband.' And (regarding) a man who passed away and left his wife, he said: 'For the wife is the one-quarter, and whatever remains, so it is for the Imam.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who passed away and left his wife, he said: 'For the woman is the one-quarter, and whatever remains, so it is for the Imam.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Muhammad ibn Hamza al-Alawi wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second: 'A master of yours bequeathed to me one hundred dirhams, and I used to hear him say, He wrote to him: 'Look to hand over from these dirhams to the two wives of the man, and their right from that is one-eighth, if he had a child. If he did not have a child, then one-quarter, and give in charity with the remainder upon whomever you know has need of it, God willing.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a husband who died and left a wife, he (peace be upon him) said: 'For her is the quarter, and hand over the remainder to us (peace be upon us).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The women do not inherit from the land, nor from the realty, anything.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, and Bukayr, and Fudayl, and Burayd, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), among them being ones who reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and among them being ones who reported from one of the two (peace be upon them both). That the woman does not inherit from the legacy of her husband from the dust of the house (land value) or land, except that the bricks and the wood would be valued, so she would be given her quarter, or her eighth if there was a child for her, from the value of the bricks, and the timber, and the canes.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The women do not inherit anything from the realty of the land.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman inherits from the bricks and does not inherit anything from the land.' I said, 'How is it that she inherits from the branches and does not inherit anything from the roots?' So he said to me: 'There is no lineage for her from them by which she inherits. Rather, she is an outsider to them, so she inherits from the branches and does not inherit from the roots, and an outsider is not included upon them by reason of her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Zurara [or] Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The women do not inherit anything from the real estate of the houses, but the construction and the bricks are evaluated, and they are given one-eighth or one-quarter of its value. He said: And that is so that the women do not get married, thereby spoiling the inheritance of the heirs.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman's value is made only that of wood and bricks, so that they do not marry her, and then enter upon them, meaning the inheritors, one who would spoil their inheritance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halbi, from Shu'ayb, from Yazeed al-Sa'igh, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the women, do they inherit the land?
