He said: 'No, but they inherit the value of the construction.' I said: 'But the people will not be pleased with that.' He said: 'When we rule, and if they are not pleased, we will strike them with the whip. If they do not straighten out, we will strike them with the sword.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from his uncle Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Muthanna, from Abdul-Malik ibn A'yn, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: The women have nothing from the houses and the real estate.

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Muawiya ibn Hakim from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Muthanna from Yazeed al-Sa'igh, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The women do not inherit anything from the walls of the earth (foundations), but for them is the value of the bricks and the wood.' He said, so I said to him: 'The people do not act upon this.' He said: 'When we appoint them (as rulers/judges), we will strike them with the whip. If they desist, or else we will strike against them with the sword.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, who said, 'I do not know him except from Muyassar, the seller of al-Zutti, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).' He said: 'I asked him about the women, what is for them from the inheritance.' He said: 'For them is the value of the bricks and the construction, and the timber, and the canes. As for the land and the realty, so it is not an inheritance for them therein.' I said, 'So (what about) the clothes.' He said: 'The clothes for them is their share.' I said, 'How it came to be that and for her is the eighth and for her is the quarter, specified.' He said: 'Because the woman, there is no lineage for her to inherit by. But rather, she has entered upon them, and this has become like this, perhaps the woman would get married and her husband would come, or her child from another people, so he would rival them with regards to their realty.'

'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is that every person with a womb relationship is at the status of the womb through which he is connected, except if there happens to be an heir closer to the deceased than him, so he supersedes him.'

Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad Abu Yusuf al-Khazzaz, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: When there is an heir from among those who have a legislated share, then he has greater right to the wealth.

He said: When the relatives converge, the one who is closer (in kinship) has a greater right to the inheritance of his close relative. If they are equal (in closeness), each one of them takes the place of his close relative.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Ubayda who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a boy and a girl, their guardians got them married, and they were both not matured yet. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage is allowed, and whichever of the two matures, the choice would be for him. So if he were to die before he matures, so there would not be any inheritance between the two of them, nor any dowry except if they had matured and were happy (with the marriage)'. I said, 'So if one of the two were to mature before the other?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is allowed upon him if he was happy (with the marriage)'. I said, 'So if the man were to mature before the girl and he was happy with the marriage, then he dies before the girl having matured, would she inherit him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Her inheritance would be isolated from him until she matures, and she would have to swear by Allah (exalted is He) that she is not claiming to take the inheritance except that she was happy with the marriage, then the inheritance would be handed over to her, and half of the dower'. I said, 'So if she the girl dies and not having matured, would the mature husband inherit her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because for her was a choice when she matured'. I said, 'So if it was her father who had got her married before she had matured?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage by her father is allowed upon her, and it is allowed upon the boy, and the dower is (due) upon the father of the girl'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem ibn Ibrahim, from Abbad ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his mature son to an orphan girl in his custody. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him if he dies, and he does not inherit her, because she has the choice (to annul the marriage), and there is no choice against her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a young boy who marries a young girl, do they inherit from each other? He said: If their fathers are the ones who married them, then yes. I said: Is the father's divorce permissible? He said: No.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from a man from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) Regarding the woman whose husband died while she was married to him, but he had not yet entered (consummated) with her, he said: Half the dower is for her, and she is entitled to inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died before having intercourse with his wife, he said: If he had assigned a dower for her, then she is entitled to half of it, and she inherits him. And if he had not assigned a dower for her, then there is no dower for her, and he inherits her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding the man who dies while his wife is under his guardianship, but he has not yet consummated the marriage with her, he said: 'For her is half the dower, and for her is the inheritance complete.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, all from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries a woman and does not assign a dower (mahr) for her, so he dies from her or divorces her before he has entered (consummated) with her. What is for her against him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dower for her, and she inherits him, and he inherits her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When the woman is divorced, then her husband dies while she is in her waiting period (iddah) from him, she has not become prohibited to him; therefore, she inherits him and he inherits her as long as she is in the blood (flow) of her second menstruation from the first two divorces. If he divorces her for the third time, she does not inherit anything from her husband, nor does he inherit from her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who divorces his wife, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him and he inherits her as long as he has the right of return (raj'ah) over her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the man divorces his wife while he is healthy (not in the deathbed illness), and there is no retraction (revocation of divorce) for him regarding her, she does not inherit him and he does not inherit her. And he (peace be upon him) said: He inherits and is inherited as long as she does not see the blood of the third menstruation, if there is a retraction for him regarding her.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who divorces his wife with two divorces while in good health, then divorces the third time while he is ill. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him for as long as he remains in his illness, even if it lasts up to a year.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man divorces his wife during his illness, she inherits him for as long as he remains in that illness, even if her waiting period has expired, except if he recovers from it. So I said to him, 'And if the illness prolongs with him?' He said, 'What is between it and a year.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Halbi and Abu Basir and Abu Al-Abbas, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: She inherits him and he does not inherit her when the waiting period is fulfilled.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the sick man who divorces his wife while he is sick, he (peace be upon him) said: If he dies in that illness of his, and she is residing with him and has not remarried, she inherits him; and if she has remarried, then she is content with what was done, and there is no inheritance for her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) did not take the inheritance of any of his mawali upon their death if he had relatives; he would hand it over to his relatives.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a maternal aunt who came disputing over the slave of a man who had died. And those of relationship are protection of one another in the Book of Allah So he handed over the inheritance to the maternal aunt and did not give it to the master.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Hanan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is for the Mawali (freed slaves/clients)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing for them from the inheritance except what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: except that you should do good to your guardians. except that you should do good to your guardians.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Abu Al-Hamra', who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What portion of the inheritance is for the Mawali (freed slaves/masters)?' He said, 'There is nothing for them except the Tarrabah, meaning the dust.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him), when a mawla (client/slave) of his died and left behind relatives, he would not take anything from his inheritance.' And he would say: 'Those of kinship are closer to one another [in inheritance].'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn Tasneem the scribe, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr al-Azraq, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, and a man asked him about a man who died and left a daughter of his sister, and left mawali (freed slaves), and for him, with me, are a thousand dirhams, and no one knew about it. So the daughter of his sister came and pledged a mus'haf (Quran codex) with me as security, so I gave her thirty dirhams. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When I told him, did anyone know about it?' I said, 'No.' He said: 'So give it to her piece by piece, and do not let anyone know.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) would not take from the inheritance of a slave of his if there was a relative of his, and even if they were not among those entitled to the obligatory inheritance, so he would hand over the money to them.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Thabit, from Hanan, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: A mawlā (client/freedman) of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) died, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look, can you find an inheritor for him?' So it was said to him (peace be upon him): 'There are two daughters in al-Yamāmah, both slaves.' So he bought them both from the wealth of the deceased mawlā, then handed over the remainder of the wealth to them both.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Abu Thabit, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Is'haq, who said: A mawla (client/freedman) of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Look, do you find an heir for him?' It was said to him: 'Two daughters for him in Al-Yamama, both slaves.' So he bought them both from the wealth of the deceased, then handed over to them the remainder of the wealth. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Thabit — similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the people who drown in a ship or are crushed by a collapsing house, so they die, and it is not known who died before his companion. He said: 'They inherit from each other; such is how it is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, similar to it, except that he said: 'Such is how we found it in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a house that fell upon a group of people who were gathered together, so it was not known which one of them died first. He said: 'They inherit from each other.' I said, 'But Abu Hanifa has included something in it.' He said, 'And what has he included?' I said, 'Two men, brothers, one of them was my slave and the other was a slave of another man. For one of them was a hundred thousand dirhams, and the other had nothing. They both sailed in the ship, so they drowned, and it was not known which of the two died first. The wealth is for the inheritors of the one who had nothing, and nothing will be for the inheritors of the one who had the wealth.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He (Abu Hanifa) has heard it, and it is like this.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man and a woman, upon whom the house collapsed, so they both died. He said: The man inherits from the woman, and the woman inherits from the man. I said: Indeed, Abu Hanifa has introduced something regarding this. He said: And what has he introduced regarding them? I said: Two men, brothers, non-Arabs, not having any inheritor except their masters. One of them had a hundred thousand Dirhams, well known, and the other had nothing. They both sailed in a ship, so it drowned. So the one hundred thousand were extracted. What should be done with it? He said: It should be handed over to the master of the one who had nothing. He said: I do not deny what he has introduced in it as true, and it is like this. Then he said: Hand over the wealth to the master of the one who had nothing, and there would not be anything for the man who had wealth, to be inherited by the other master. So there is nothing for his inheritors.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged in Yemen regarding a people upon whom a house of theirs had collapsed, so two young children remained from them, one of them a slave and the other free. So he drew lots between the two of them, and the lot fell upon one of them, so he made the wealth for him and emancipated the other.

Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Al-ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the man upon whom and his wife falls a house. He (peace be upon him) said: The woman inherits from the man, and the man inherits from the woman. Its meaning is that they inherit from each other from the origins of their wealth; they do not inherit from what they have inherited from each other anything.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, raising it, said, 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)': He judged regarding a man and a woman who both died together in the plague. They both died upon one bed, and the hand and the leg of the man were found upon the woman. So he made the inheritance to be for the man and said: 'He died after her'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Abu Haneefa: 'O Abu Haneefa! What do you say regarding a house that fell upon a group of people, and two children remained from them, one of whom was free and the other a slave of his companion, and the free one was not distinguished from the slave?' So Abu Haneefa said, 'Half of this one is liberated, and half of this one is liberated, and the wealth is divided between them.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not like that, but a lot is drawn between them, so whoever the lot hits, he is free, and this one is liberated, so he is made a master to him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Sawwar, from Al-Hasan, who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him), when he defeated Talha and Al-Zubayr, the people turned in retreat. They passed by a pregnant woman on the road, so she panicked from them and cast out what was in her belly alive. It struggled until it died, then its mother died after it. So Ali (peace be upon him) and his companions passed by her, and she was lying there with her child on the road. He asked them about her matter, so they said to him, 'Indeed, she was pregnant; she panicked when she saw the fighting and the defeat.' He said, 'So he asked them, which of the two died before its companion?' So it was said, 'Her son died before her.' He said, 'So he called her husband, the father of the dead boy, and made him inherit from his son two-thirds of the wergild (blood money). And he made the mother inherit one-third of the wergild. Then he made the husband inherit from his dead wife half of the one-third wergild which she had inherited from her son, and he made the relatives of the dead woman inherit the remainder.' Then he made the husband inherit also from the wergild of his dead wife, half of the wergild, which was two thousand and five hundred dirhams. And he made the relatives of the dead woman inherit half of the wergild, which was two thousand and five hundred dirhams. And that is because there was no child for her other than that which she cast out when she panicked. He said, 'And he paid all of that from the Public Treasury of Al-Basra.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the blood money (diyah) of the murdered that the inheritors inherit it according to the Book of Allah and their shares, if there is no debt upon the murdered, except for the brothers and sisters from the mother, for they do not inherit anything from his blood money.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, said: Abu Abdillah said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged that the wergild (blood money) is inherited by the heirs, except for the brothers and sisters from the mother.

And from him who said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged that the wergild (blood money) is inherited by the inheritors, except for the brothers from the mother, for they do not inherit anything from the wergild.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The blood money (diyah) is inherited by the heirs according to the shares of inheritance, except for the brothers from the mother, for they do not inherit anything from the blood money.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala and Ali ibn Rabat from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The brothers from the mother do not inherit anything from the blood money.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Yahya al-Azraq, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who is killed and leaves a debt, and has no wealth, so his guardians take the blood money (diyah). Is it upon them to pay off his debt? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And if he had not left anything [else]?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. They took his blood money, therefore it is upon them to pay off his debt.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Is there anything for the brothers from the mother (maternal brothers) from the blood money (diyah)?' He said: 'No'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Two men do not inherit from each other when one of them has killed his companion.

Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed his mother, would he inherit her? He (peace be upon him) said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: Whichever man with a kinship bond kills his relative, he will not inherit from him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, all from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: The man does not inherit if he kills his child or his parent, but the inheritance belongs to the inheritors of the killer.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who killed his mother, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not inherit her, and he is killed due to it in humiliation, and I do not think that his being killed due to it is an expiation for his sin.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no inheritance for the killer'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who drank medicine while she was pregnant, and her husband did not know of that, so she miscarried her child. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had bones and flesh had grown upon them, the wergild (diyah) is upon her to be paid to his father. And if when she cast him out it was a clot (alaqah) or a lump (mudghah), then upon her is forty dinars or a ghurrah (unified price, often a slave) to be paid to his father.' I said to him, 'And she does not inherit her child's wergild along with his father?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because she killed him, so she does not inherit him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The man is not killed if he kills his child, and the child is killed if he kills his parent, and the man does not inherit his father if he kills him, even if it was in error.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The woman inherits from the wergild (blood money) of her husband, and he inherits from her wergild, so long as one of the two has not killed his partner.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is there anything for the woman from the wergild (blood money) of her husband, and is there anything for the man from the wergild of his wife?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, so long as one of the two has not killed the other.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man kills his father, he is killed because of it, and if his father kills him, he is not killed because of it, and he does not inherit him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel and Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding what the people have narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'The people of two religions do not inherit each other,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'We inherit them and they do not inherit us, because Islam did not increase in his favor except for harshness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Neither the Jew nor the Christian inherits the Muslim, and the Muslim inherits the Jew and the Christian.'

From him, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abdullah ibn Ayn who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A Christian dies and he has a Muslim son, would he inherit him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not increase him with Islam except for honour, so we inherit them, but they do not inherit us.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Muslim blocks the infidel and inherits him, but the infidel does not block the Believer and does not inherit him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Muslim inherits his Zimmi wife, and she does not inherit him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Malik ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a Christian who died, leaving a son of his Muslim brother and a son of his Muslim sister, and the Christian had children and a Christian wife. children and a Christian wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that the son of his Muslim brother should be given two-thirds of what he left, and the son of his Muslim sister should be given one-third of what he left, if he does not have young children. But if he has young children, then upon the two inheritors is that they should spend upon the young children from what they inherited from their father, until they mature.' It was said to him (peace be upon him): 'How should they spend?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritor of the two-thirds should take out two-thirds of the expenses, and the inheritor of the one-third should take out one-third of the expenses. And if they mature, they cease the expenses for them.' It was said to him (peace be upon him): 'And if the children become Muslim while they are young?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever their father left should be handed over to the Imam (peace be upon him) until they mature. If they remain upon Islam, the Imam hands over their inheritance to them. And if they do not remain upon Islam when they mature, the Imam hands over their inheritance to the son of his brother and the son of his sister, the two Muslims. He hands over to the son of the brother two-thirds of what was left, and he hands over to the son of the sister one-third of what was left.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about a Muslim man who died, and for him was a Christian mother, and for him was a Muslim wife and Muslim children. So he said: 'If his mother becomes a Muslim before his inheritance is distributed, give her the one-sixth.' I said: 'So if there did not happen to be a wife for him, nor children, nor any inheritor for him from the Muslims with a legislated share in the Book, and his mother is a Christian, and for him are Christian relatives, from the ones who have a legislated share in the Book had they been Muslims. For whom would the inheritance be?' He said: 'If the mother becomes a Muslim, then the entirety of the inheritance is for her, and if his mother does not become a Muslim, and some of his relatives become Muslim, from the ones who have a legislated share in the Book, so the inheritance would be for him.' And if no one from his relatives becomes Muslim, so his inheritance is for the Imam.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who becomes a Muslim upon an inheritance before the distribution, so for him is his inheritance, and if he becomes a Muslim after the distribution, so there is no inheritance for him.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Whoever becomes Muslim upon an inheritance before the inheritance is distributed, it is for him; and whoever becomes Muslim after it has been distributed, there is no inheritance for him; and whoever is emancipated upon an inheritance before the inheritances are distributed, it is for him; and whoever is emancipated after it has been distributed, there is no inheritance for him. And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the woman: If she becomes Muslim before the inheritance is distributed, then for her is the inheritance.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The people will not be upright regarding the obligations (the obligatory shares of inheritance) and divorce, except by the sword.
The Obligations (legislated shares of inheritance) and divorce cannot be established except by the sword.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Yazid al-Sa'igh who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about women — do they inherit the real estate (riba')? He said: No, but they inherit the value of the building. He said: I said: But the people are not pleased with this. He said: So he said: When we are placed in authority and the people are not pleased with that, we will strike them with the whip. If they do not comply, we will strike them with the sword.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to judge regarding inheritances concerning what was acquired by Islam from the wealth of a polytheist which he left undistributed before Islam. He used to assign for the women and the men their shares from it, according to the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the inheritances: what Islam acquired from the wealth of the Polytheists which had not been distributed, then for the women are their shares from it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from his brother Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Rabat, raising it, said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: If a Zimmi man (a Jew or Christian under protection) becomes a Muslim while his father is alive, and his father has other children besides him, then when the father dies, the Muslim son inherits all of his wealth, and his (other) children and his wife do not inherit anything along with the Muslim.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and has Muslim children and non-Muslim children, he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are upon their inheritances.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a free man who dies and has a slave mother: 'She should be bought from her son's wealth, then emancipated, then she inherits.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who died and left wealth, and for him was a mother who was a slave. He said: 'His mother should be bought and emancipated, then the remainder of the wealth should be handed over to her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man dies and leaves his father, and he is a slave, or his mother, and she is a slave, and the deceased is a free man, his father or his relatives are purchased from what he left, and they inherit the remainder of the wealth.

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a free man who dies and leaves behind a mother who is a slave: She should be bought from her son's wealth, then emancipated, and then she inherits (the remainder).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who died and left much wealth, and left a mother who was a slave and a sister who was a slave. He said: 'They are bought from the wealth of the deceased, then they are emancipated and they inherit.' I said: 'What do you think if the owners of the slave-girls refuse, what is to be done?' He said: 'It is not for them to refuse, and they are evaluated at a just price, then what is due to them is given according to the price.' I said: 'What do you think if they were bought, then emancipated, then they inherited him, who would inherit them afterwards?' He said: 'The freedmen of their son would inherit them, because they were bought from the wealth of the son.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who dies and has a mother who is a slave, and has wealth, that his mother should be bought from his wealth and the remainder of the wealth be handed over to her, if there is no relative of hers who has a share in the Book (Quran).

Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Abu Thabit, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: A slave of Ali (peace be upon him) died, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look, do you find an inheritor for him?' So it was said to him: 'He has two daughters in al-Yamama, both slaves.' So he bought them from the wealth of the deceased, then handed over to them the remainder of the wealth.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibnag and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The free person and the slave do not inherit (each other).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The free person and the slave do not inherit (each other).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: The free person and the slave do not inherit (each other).

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfa from Jamil from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The slave does not inherit and the free person does not inherit.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had a mother who was a slave. When death approached him, a man from our companions went and bought his mother, and stipulated upon her: 'I am buying you and emancipating you, so when your son, so-and-so son of so-and-so, dies and you inherit him, give me half of what you inherit, on the condition that you give me the pledge of Allah and the pledge of His Messenger.' She was pleased with that, so she gave him the pledge of Allah and the pledge of His Messenger to fulfill it for him. The man bought her and emancipated her upon that condition, and her son died after that. So she inherited him, and there was no other heir for him. He said, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He did well by her and will be rewarded for it. This is a jurist (faqih), and the Muslims are upon their conditions, and it is upon her to fulfill for him what she pledged to Allah and His Messenger regarding it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who contracted his slave and stipulated a condition upon him that his inheritance would be for him. So that was raised to Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him), so he invalidated his condition and said: 'The Stipulated Condition of Allah is before the stipulation of your condition'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The contracted slave inherits and is inherited from, according to the portion of the manumission price he has paid off.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is muqatib (a slave contracted to pay a sum for his freedom) who dies and has paid some of his contract amount, and he has a son from his slave girl: He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was stipulated upon him that if he was unable (to pay), he would remain a slave, then his son returns as a slave along with the slave girl; and if it was not stipulated upon him, his son pays what remains of the contract amount and inherits what remains.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, altogether from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who was a mukatab (contracted slave), under whom was a free wife, so she bequeathed at the time of her death with a bequest. The people of the inheritance said: 'He does not inherit, and we do not validate her bequest for him because he is a mukatab who has not yet been emancipated, and he does not inherit.' So he (peace be upon him) judged that he would inherit by the calculation of whatever portion of his contract had been emancipated from it.

And by the chain, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a contracted slave who died and for him was wealth, he said: 'His inheritance would be calculated in accordance with what he had been emancipated from it, to be for his inheritors, and whatever he had not been emancipated from it, is for his masters who had contracted him, from his wealth'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who was contracted (mukatab) to pay for his freedom, who died without having paid off his contract, and left behind wealth and children. He (peace be upon him) said: If his master, when he contracted him, had stipulated upon him that if he was unable to pay one of the installments, he would be returned to slavery, and he had indeed been unable to pay an installment, then whatever he left of anything would be for his master, and his son would be returned to slavery if he had a son before the contract. And if he contracted him later and did not stipulate upon him, then his son is free, and he would pay on behalf of his father whatever remained upon him from what his father left. And there is nothing of the inheritance for his son until he pays off what is upon him. So if his father had not left anything, then there is nothing upon his son.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Humran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a contracted slave who paid off part of his contract, then died, leaving a son from his slave girl. He said: If a condition was stipulated upon him, his son and his mother would become two slaves; and if no condition was stipulated upon him, his son would become free, pay the remainder of the contract to the masters, and the son would inherit what remained.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), regarding a contracted slave who died, having paid a portion of his manumission amount, and left wealth, and he had two free children. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'His wealth is to be distributed among them by shares.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A contracted slave bought himself, and left wealth valued at one hundred thousand, and he had no inheritor.' He said: 'The one who is the guardian of his actions will inherit him.' I said, 'Who is the guarantor of his actions?' He said: 'The guarantor of the actions of the Muslims.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who dies an apostate from Islam, and he has children, so he said: His wealth is for his Muslim children.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hanaat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who reneged from Islam, for whom would his inheritance be? He said: His inheritance is distributed among his heirs according to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Mahboub, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hazramy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Muslim man reneges from Islam, his wife becomes irrevocably divorced from him just as the irrevocably divorced woman. And if he were to be killed, or die before the fulfillment of her waiting period, so she would inherit him during the waiting period, and he would not inherit her if she had died and he had reneged from Islam.

Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who turns away from the Religion of Islam and disbelieves in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, there is no repentance for him, and his killing is obligated, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him. Therefore, whatever he leaves should be distributed among his children.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from [Yunus], from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Al-Khattab al-Awr asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and I was seated there, so he said: 'There was a hired worker with my father who worked for him for wages. So we lost him, and there remained for whom we lost him, and there remained for him something from his wages, and we do not know an heir for him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So seek him.' He said: 'We have sought him, but we did not find him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Poor' – and he moved his hands (gestured). He (the narrator) said, 'So I repeated to him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek and strive. If you can find him, [keep it for him]; otherwise, it is like your wealth until there comes to him a claimant.' So if death befalls you, bequeath with it that if a claimant comes to him, then it should be handed over to him.

Yunus, from Abu Sabit and Ibn Awn, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who had a right upon another man, so he lost him and did not know where to seek him, and did not know if he was alive or dead, and did not know of an inheritor for him, nor a clan, nor a city. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek him.' He said, 'If that is prolonged, should I give it in charity?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek him.'

Yunus narrated from Nasr ibn Habeeb, the owner of the inn (Al-Khan), who said: I wrote to Abdullah ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'A sum of one hundred and four dirhams has come into my possession, and I am an innkeeper. The owner of the money died, and I do not know of any heirs for him. What is your opinion regarding informing me of its status and what I should do with it? For I have grown weary of holding it.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Work with it, and give it out as charity little by little until it is exhausted.'

Yunus narrated from Al-Haysam Abu Rawh, the owner of the inn (hotel), who said: I wrote to Abd Allah ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): 'I manage hotels, so a man lodges with me and dies suddenly. I do not know him, nor do I know his homeland, nor his heirs. So the wealth remains with me; how should I deal with it, and to whom does that wealth belong?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Leave it in its current state.'
Yunus narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said: Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The lost one (mafqūd), his wealth is waited for (for four years), then it is distributed.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second [Imam al-Kazim] regarding a house that belonged to a woman, and she had a son and a daughter. The son disappeared at sea, and the woman died. Her daughter claimed that her mother had designated this house for her, and she had sold parts of it, leaving a portion in the house next to the house of one of our companions. He disliked buying it due to the absence of the son, and feared that it might not be permissible for him to buy it, and no news was known of the son. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Since how long has he been absent?' I said: 'Since many years.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wait for his absence for ten years, then it may be bought.' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'So if one waits for his absence of ten years, is it permissible to buy it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked him about a man who had children, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. How should we deal with the inheritance of the missing one from his father? He said: 'Keep it aside until he comes.' I said: 'The man is lost and will not be coming.' So he said: 'If the inheritors of the man were reliable with his wealth, distribute it between them, so when he comes, they can return it to him.' A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), similar to it.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Ribat and Abdullah ibn Jabalat, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who had children, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. So what should be done with the inheritance of the man for the absent one from his father? He said: 'It is set aside until he comes.' I said: 'So upon his wealth is Zakat?' He said: 'No, until he comes.' I said: 'So if he comes, does he purify it?' He said: 'No, until a year passes with it being in his hand.' So I said: 'The man is lost and does not come?' He said: 'If the inheritors of the man are reliable with his wealth, they distribute it among themselves. So whenever he comes, they return it to him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: For the lost one (al-mafqud), the inheritors should withhold his wealth, striving to seek him in the land, for four years. So if they are not able to locate him, his wealth is distributed among the inheritors. And if he had children, the wealth is withheld, and spent upon his children for those four years.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying regarding the newborn: 'If it moves, it inherits, for perhaps it is speechless.'

Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the miscarried child (saqit), when it falls from the belly of its mother, if it moves with a distinct movement, it inherits and is inherited from, for perhaps it was mute.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left his wife while she was pregnant, so she gave birth to a boy after his death. Then the boy died after falling onto the ground. The midwife who received him testified that he cried out and shrieked when he fell onto the ground, then died after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon the Imam to validate her testimony regarding one-quarter of the inheritance of the boy.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Sinan, said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The testimony of the midwife is valid regarding the newborn, when it cries and shouts, concerning inheritance, and he inherits one-quarter of the inheritance by the measure of the testimony of one woman. I said, 'And if there were two women?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their testimony is valid regarding half of the inheritance.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the inheritance of the newborn from the wergild, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not inherit anything from the wergild until he shrieks and his voice is heard.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Awn, from one of them, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying that the newborn does not inherit anything from the wergild until it moves and its voice is heard.

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) at Basra with a parchment and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, look at this parchment, for it contains advice.' So he looked into it, then looked at the face of the man and said: 'If you are truthful, we will remunerate you; if you are a liar, we will punish you; and if you wish that we release you, we shall release you.' The man said: 'Rather, release me, O Commander of the Faithful.' When the man turned back, he said: 'O you community, confused after its Prophet! Indeed, had you prioritised the one whom God has prioritised, and pushed back the one whom God has pushed back, and placed the wilayah and inheritance where God has placed them, the Guardian of God would not be in need, nor would any portion of God's obligations be neglected, nor would two people differ regarding God's judgment, nor would the community dispute any of God's commands — except that the knowledge of all that is with us from the Book of God. Therefore, taste the evil consequences of what your own hands have sent before, and God is not in the least unjust to the servants, and they who act unjustly shall come to know the turning they shall be overturned with.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said: 'Praise be to God, who admits no one to advance what He has placed last, nor to delay what He has placed first.' Then he struck one of his hands upon the other, then said: 'O you community, bewildered after its Prophet! Had you placed first the one whom God placed first, and placed last the one whom God placed last, and established the wilayah and the inheritance where God has established them, the Guardian of God would not be in need, nor would any share from the obligatory portions of God be neglected, nor would two people disagree concerning a ruling of God, nor would the community dispute anything regarding the commands of God, except that with us is its knowledge from the Book of God. Therefore taste the evil consequences of your affair and what you have squandered of what your hands have sent before — and God is not in the least unjust to the servants — and those who have done wrong shall come to know the manner of overturning they shall be overturned with.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) was asked about a newborn who was born with both a female organ (qubul) and a male organ (dhakar), how is it inherited? He (peace be upon him) said: If it urinates from its male part, then it has the inheritance of the male, and if it urinates from the female part, then it has the inheritance of the female.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to make the hermaphrodite inherit, (based upon) where it urinated from.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'The child is born with what is for men and with what is for women.' He said, 'It inherits from where its urine precedes. So if it comes out from both equally, then from where it spurts out. So if they are equal, it inherits the inheritance of men and women.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him) Regarding the hermaphrodite who has both what is for males and what is for females, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It inherits from the place from which it urinates. If it urinates from the male part, it inherits the inheritance of the male, and if it urinates from the place of the female, it inherits the inheritance of the female.' And regarding the hermaphrodite who has neither what is for men nor what is for women, except for a hole from which urine comes out, upon which inheritance would it inherit? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If, when it urinates, it projects its urine (to a distance), it inherits the inheritance of the male, and if it does not project its urine, it inherits the inheritance of the female.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jowhary, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: A child was born in the era of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who had two heads and two chests in one lower part. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Does it inherit the inheritance of two or one?' He said: 'Leave it until it sleeps, then shout at it. So if both wake up together, it has the inheritance of one, and if one wakes up and the other remains sleeping, it inherits the inheritance of two.'
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Saif ibn 'Umeyra, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When a son of al-mula'ana (the cursed mother) dies, and for him are brothers, his wealth would be upon the (legislated) shares of Allah.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) That the inheritance of the child of the mother cursed by her husband is for its mother. So if its mother was not alive, then it goes to the closest people to the mother, his maternal uncles.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said regarding the one who performs li'an: If he admits his lie before the cursing, his wife is returned to him, and he is whipped the limit; and if he refuses, he curses, and she does not become permissible to him ever. And if a man accuses his wife, upon him is the limit; and if his child dies, his maternal uncles inherit him. So if his father claims him, he is attached to him; and if he dies, the son inherits him, and the father does not inherit him.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the child of al-mula'ana (the cursing/disowning), who would inherit him? He said: 'His mother'. So I said, 'If his mother is dead, who would inherit him?' He said: 'His maternal uncles'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed li'an with his wife and denied her child, then admitted his own lie after the li'an and claimed that her child was his child. [I asked:] Will she be returned to him? He (peace be upon him) said: No, and it is not [merely] an honour; she will not be returned to him, nor will she be permissible to him until the Day of Resurrection. He (the narrator) said: And I asked him, 'Who inherits the child?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His mother.' So I said, 'What is your view if the mother dies and the boy inherits her, then the boy dies afterwards, who would inherit him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His maternal uncles.' So I said, 'If the father acknowledges him, does the father inherit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but the father does not inherit from the son.'

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When a son of the al-mula'ana (cursing) mother dies, and he has brothers, his wealth is distributed according to the shares of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed li'an (mutual cursing) with his wife while she was pregnant. So when she gave birth, he claimed her child and acknowledged it and asserted that it was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His child is returned to him, and he does not inherit him, and he is not whipped, because the li'an has passed.'

From him, from Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who performed Li'an with his wife. He said: 'The child is attached to its mother, and her maternal uncles inherit him, and he does not inherit them.' So I asked him about the man if he admits to having lied himself, he said: 'The child is attached to him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Thabit, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the child of al-mu'lanah (cursing) when they cursed each other and separated, and her husband said afterwards, 'The child is my child,' while he was lying about himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the woman, she does not return to him, but I return the child to him, and I do not leave him as his son; he has no inheritance. If his father does not claim him, then his maternal uncles inherit him, and they do not inherit from him. If anyone claims him as the son of adultery, he is whipped with the limit punishment.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whichever man falls upon a slave girl of a people unlawfully, then buys her, then claims her child, so he would not inherit from him anything. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The child is for the bed, and for the adulterer is the stone. And the son of the adultery would not inherit except a man who claims a son of his slave girl. And whichever man accepts his child, then denies from it, so that is not for him. Nor is it honourable; his child would be attached to him whether it was from his wife or from his slave girl.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said: One of our companions wrote a letter to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second, with me, asking him about a man who was immoral with a woman, then he married her after the pregnancy, so she came with a child, and he resembles the creation of Allah most by him. So he wrote by his own handwriting and his seal: The child is for him, he does not inherit.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Salim, from Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had unlawful intercourse with a slave girl, then bought her, and claimed her son. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would not inherit from him.' Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child is for the bed (conception), and for the adulterer is the stone, and the child of adultery would not inherit except a man who claims a son of his slave girl.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Mahziyar, from Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Ash'ari, who said: One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second, along with me, asking him about a man who was immoral with a woman, then he married her after the pregnancy, so she came with a child, and he resembled him the most from the creatures of Allah. So he wrote by his handwriting and his seal: 'The child of sin does not inherit'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who was immoral with a Christian woman, so she gave birth to a boy from him. He acknowledged him, then died, and did not leave any child other than him. Would he inherit him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie and Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who was immoral with a Jewish woman, so she gave birth to a child. Then he died and did not leave any inheritors. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritance is handed over to his child from the Jewish woman.' I said: 'And what about a Christian man who was immoral with a Muslim woman, so she gave birth to a boy, then the Christian man died and left wealth; for whom would be his inheritance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His inheritance would be for his son from the Muslim woman.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleym, the mawla of Tirbal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had intercourse with his slave girl, and that he used to send her for his needs, and that she became pregnant, and that he accused her and news of her mischief reached him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When she gives birth, he should keep the child and not sell him, and make for him a share from his house [and his wealth]' He said, 'It was said to him: A man had intercourse with his slave girl, and that he had not sent her for his needs, and that he accused her, and she became pregnant.' So he said: 'When she gives birth, he should keep the child and not sell him, and make for him a share from his house and his wealth, and this is not similar to that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man from the Ansar came to my father and said to him, 'I have been afflicted with a great matter. I have a slave girl whom I used to have intercourse with. One day I went to her, then I went out for a need of mine after having performed ghusl from her, and I forgot some maintenance money of mine. So I returned to the house to take it, and I found my slave girl on her belly. So I counted for her from that day of mine nine months, and she gave birth to a girl.' He said, so my father said to him, 'It is not befitting for you to approach her, nor to sell her, but spend upon her from your wealth as long as you are alive. Then bequeath at your death that she should be spent upon from your wealth until Allah makes for her a way out.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the One who knows the number of the grains of sand in 'Alij (desert) surely knows that the obligatory shares (of inheritance) do not exceed six.

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Perhaps (sometimes) the shares (of inheritance) are increased until they become a hundred, or less, or more.' So he said: 'They do not exceed six.' Then he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: Indeed, the One Who counted the grains of sand of 'Alij certainly knows that the shares of inheritance do not exceed six. If they perceived its principle, they would not exceed six.'

I sat with Ibn 'Abbas when the mention of the ordained shares in inheritances arose. Ibn 'Abbas said: Glory be to Allah, the Most Great! Do you think that He who enumerated the grains of sand in the valley of 'Alij has assigned in an estate a half and a half and a third? These two halves have already consumed the estate — so where is the place for the third? Zufar ibn Aws al-Basri said to him: O Abu al-'Abbas, who was the first to apply al-'awl to the ordained shares? He replied: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when the ordained shares crowded together before him and each excluded another. He said: By Allah, I do not know which of you Allah has placed first and which He has placed last, and I find nothing more appropriate than to divide this estate among you in proportional shares — so he imposed upon each person with a right what fell upon him from the reduction of the ordained share. But by Allah, if he had placed first whom Allah placed first, and placed last whom Allah placed last, no ordained share would have exceeded. Zufar ibn Aws said to him: Which did He place first and which did He place last? He replied: Every ordained share that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought down from its level only to another level — that is what Allah placed first. As for what Allah placed last: every ordained share that, when it moves from its fixed amount, has nothing except what remains — that is what Allah placed last. As for those He placed first: the husband has a half; when something comes to displace him from it, he reverts to a quarter, and nothing displaces him below that. The wife has a quarter; when she is displaced from it, she goes to an eighth, nothing displaces her below that. The mother has a third; when she is displaced from it, she goes to a sixth, nothing displaces her below that — these are the ordained shares Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed first. As for what Allah placed last: the share of daughters and sisters — they have a half and two-thirds. When the other shares displace them from that, they have nothing but what remains — those are what Allah placed last. When what Allah placed first and what He placed last come together, one begins with what Allah placed first, giving each their complete right. If anything remains, it is for those Allah placed last. If nothing remains, there is nothing for them. Zufar ibn Aws said to him: What stopped you from advis

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who were 'hameelayn' (adopted/brothers by contract), who were brought from the land of polytheism. One of them said to the other, 'You are my brother,' and they were recognized by this. Then they were emancipated (freed), and remained acknowledging the brotherhood. Then one of the two died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritance is for the brother; both are verified.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjajaj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-Hameel, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is Al-Hameel?' I said: 'A woman is taken captive from her land, and with her is a young child, so she says, 'He is my son.' And a man is taken captive, so he meets his brother, so he says, 'He is my brother,' and they recognize each other, and there is no proof for them regarding that except their own words.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What do those before you say?' I said: 'They do not inherit them, because there was no proof for them regarding that; rather, the birth was in Polytheism.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! If she comes with her son or her daughter with her, and she does not cease to affirm it, and when he recognizes his brother, and that was in soundness of their intellects, and they do not cease affirming that, they inherit from one another.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Al-Sha'iri, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said: We were at the door of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and we were a group waiting for him to come out, when a woman came and said, 'Which one of you is Abu Ja'far?' The people said to her, 'What do you want from him?' She said, 'I want to ask him a question.' They said to her, 'This is the jurist of the people of Iraq, so ask him.' She said, 'My husband died and left a thousand dirhams, and there was due to me from my dower five hundred dirhams. So I took my dower and I took my inheritance. Then a man came and claimed a thousand dirhams against him, so I testified for him.' Al-Hakam said, 'While I was calculating what she would receive, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out and said, 'What is this that I see you moving your fingers with, O Hakam?' So I informed him of the woman's statement and what she asked about. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'She acknowledged a third of what is in her hands, and there is no inheritance for her.' Al-Hakam said, 'By Allah, I have not seen anyone more understanding than Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, and Husayn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who died and one of his inheritors acknowledged a debt for a man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is binding upon him in his share.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever dies and leaves a debt, then the debt is upon us and his dependents are upon us. And whoever dies and leaves wealth, then it is for his inheritors. And whoever dies and has no guardians (relatives with inheritance rights), then his wealth is from the spoils (public treasury).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The one who dies and has no inheritor from his relatives, nor a master who freed him and assumed responsibility for his crimes, then his wealth is from the spoils (public treasury).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: The Imam is the inheritor of the one who has no inheritor for him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'They ask you about the spoils of war.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who dies and has no guardian (mawla), then his wealth is from the spoils of war (anfal).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawud, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A man died in the era of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who had no inheritor, so Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) handed over his inheritance to his fellow city folk.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Khallad al-Sindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) was saying regarding the man who dies and leaves wealth, and there is no one for him: 'Give the inheritance to his city folk'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guardianship (wilayah) is for the one who emancipates.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in the hadith of Barirah, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Aisha: 'Emancipate (her), for the guardianship (walayah) is for the one who emancipates.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ayesha said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'The people of Bureyra stipulated the condition of her guardianship (walāʾ). So the Messenger of Allah said: 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates.'

Safwan, from Al-Ays ibn Al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who bought a slave who had children from a free woman, so he emancipated him. He said: The guardianship (walā’) of his children is for the one who emancipated him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who emancipated a man, for whom is his guardianship and for whom is his inheritance? He (peace be upon him) said: For the one who emancipated him, except if there happen to be for him an inheritor other than her.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A slave of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib died, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) handed over his inheritance to the daughter of Hamza.
