Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who intended to emancipate a slave of his, and his master used to take a tax from him that he had obligated upon him every year, and the master was pleased with that from him, and the slave was pleased with that. So the slave acquired wealth in his trade besides what he used to give his master from the tax. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he pays to his master what was obligated upon him, then whatever he earns after the obligation, it is for the slave.' He said, then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that Allah has obligated obligations upon the servants, so when they fulfill them to Him, He does not ask them about what is besides it?' So I said to him: 'So the slave may give charity from what he earns and emancipate [others] after the obligation which he used to pay to his master?' He said: 'Yes, and the reward of that is for him.' I said: 'So if he emancipates a slave from what he had earned besides the obligation, to whom will belong the guardianship of the emancipated one?' He said: 'He goes and gives guardianship to whomever he likes. If he guarantees his crimes and his wergild, he will be his master and inherit him.' I said: 'Is it not that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates?'' He said: 'This is a Sa'iba [unconditionally freed slave], his guardianship cannot be for a slave like him.' I said: 'So if the slave who emancipates him guarantees his crimes and his liabilities, will that necessitate it and he will become his master and inherit him?' He said: 'That is not allowed, and a slave does not inherit a free one.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Sa'iba (unconditionally freed slave), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look in the Quran, so whatever was in it, so [the ruling is] the freeing of a slave. So that, O Ammar, is the Sa'iba, for whom there is no guardianship for anyone over her except Allah. So whatever was the guardianship for Allah, it is for His Messenger, and whatever was the guardianship for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then his guardianship is for the Imam, and his crimes are upon the Imam, and his inheritance is for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man is the guardian of a man, then for him is his inheritance and upon him is his wergild.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the slave who is emancipated unconditionally (sa'ibah). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is under the guardianship of whomever he desires, and upon the one who is guardian is his liability (for debts/crimes), and for him is his inheritance.' We said to him (peace be upon him): 'So if he remains silent until he dies and does not appoint anyone as guardian?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His wealth is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever emancipates a man as a Sa'ibah, there is nothing upon him from his crimes, and there is nothing for him from his inheritance, and let him bear witness to that.

Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Sa'ibah, so he said: 'He is the man who emancipates his slave, then says to him, “Go wherever you wish. There is nothing from your inheritance for me, nor is there upon me from your crimes anything,” and he should have two witnesses testify to that.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ajli, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man upon whom was the emancipation of a slave (neck), so he died before he could emancipate a slave. So his son went and bought a slave from his own earnings and emancipated him on behalf of his father. And indeed, the freed slave acquired wealth after that, then died and left it for whoever would be his inheritor. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the emancipation upon his father was for Dhihar (verbal divorce), or thanksgiving, or an obligation upon him, then the freed one is a Sa'ibah (unconditionally freed), there is no right of guardianship for anyone over him. And if he had attached himself (given his Wilayah) before dying to one of the Muslims, and guaranteed his blood-money and his liabilities, he would be his master and his inheritor, if there is no close relative to inherit him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he did not attach himself to any of the Muslims until he died, then his inheritance is for the Imam of the Muslims, if there is no close relative to inherit him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if the emancipation upon his father was voluntary, and his father had instructed him to emancipate a person on his behalf, then the guardianship of the freed one is the inheritance for all the sons of the deceased, from the men.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the one who bought him and emancipated him by the command of his father would be like one of the inheritors, if there is no relative among the free Muslims who would inherit him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if it was that the son who bought the slave emancipated him on behalf of his father from his own wealth, after the death of his father, voluntarily from himself, without his father having instructed him to do so, then his guardianship and his inheritance is for the one who bought him from his own wealth and emancipated him on behalf of his father, if there is no inheritor for the freed one from his relatives.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a slave who was emancipated as a Sa'ibah (unconditionally freed slave). He said: 'He has a guardian of his choice, and upon the one who becomes his guardian is his liability (for his debts/crimes), and for him is his inheritance.' I said: 'So if he remains without a guardian until he dies?' He said: 'His wealth is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the one who severely punished his slave, that he was free, there being no way for him (the master) against him (the slave), being unconditionally freed, he can go and give his guardianship to whoever he so likes to. So when he is responsible for his crimes, so he would inherit him.

The (legislated) shares (of inheritance) do not increase/exceed, and they cannot be more than six. And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Umar ibn Udhayna — similar to that.

I said to Zurara that Bukayr ibn A'yan narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that the (legislated) shares of inheritance do not exceed (the total) and do not become more than six So he (Zurara) said: This is something about which there is no disagreement among our companions, (transmitted) from Abu Abdillah and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them)

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The (legislated) shares do not exceed (their limits).

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) commanded Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), so he made me read a scroll of the obligatory shares (of inheritance), and I saw that most of what was in it was based on four shares.
The (legislated) shares (of inheritance) cannot be more than six shares.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) recited to me the obligatory inheritance shares of Ali (peace be upon him). Most of them were from five, or from four, and the majority of them were from six shares.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Khuzayma ibn Yaqtin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The origins of the obligatory shares (of inheritance) are from six portions — they do not exceed that, nor is there deficiency/excess (awl) upon them. Then the remaining wealth, after that, belongs to the people of the shares who are mentioned in the Book (Quran).

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu al-Maghra', from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Salim al-Ashall, that he heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, God Mighty and Majestic included the two parents alongside all other heirs of the inheritances, and did not reduce anything from the sixth for them; and He included the husband and wife, and did not reduce anything from the quarter and the eighth for them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Four [categories of heirs] — no harm shall be imposed on them with regards to the inheritance: the two parents, the husband, and the wife.'

Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, has included the two parents against all those entitled to the obligatory shares, so He has not reduced the two of them below one-sixth, for each one of the two; and He has included the husband and the wife against all those entitled to the inheritances, so He has not reduced the two of them below the quarter and the eighth.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abu al-Mughira', from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Most Majestic, Most Glorious, has placed both parents alongside all other heirs who have ordained shares, and has not reduced their share below one-sixth for each of them. And He has placed the husband and wife alongside all other heirs, and has not reduced their share below one-fourth and one-eighth.

There shall not inherit along with the mother, nor with the father, nor with the son, nor with the daughter, except for the husband and the wife. And indeed the husband shall not be reduced anything from the half share when there is no child, nor shall the wife be reduced anything from the quarter when there is no child. So if there is a child with them both, then for the husband is the quarter and for the wife is the eighth.

A number of our companions narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr; and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa; and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father — all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah who said: When a man leaves behind his mother, or his father, or his son, or his daughter — when he leaves behind any one of the four — then this is not what God, Mighty and Majestic, intended in His Book: 'Say, God gives you a ruling regarding al-kalalah.' No one among all the creatures of God, Mighty and Majestic, inherits along with the mother, or along with the father, or along with the son, or along with the daughter — except a husband or a wife.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Hanan ibn Sudayr, from his father, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'A prescribed punishment (hadd) which is established in the earth is more purifying therein than the rain of forty nights and days.'

Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'He revives the earth after its death' He said: He does not revive it with the drops of rain, but rather God sends men who revive justice, and thus the earth is revived through the revival of justice. And the establishment of God's prescribed punishments is more beneficial for the earth than the drops of rain for forty days.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Establishment of a hadd (prescribed punishment) is better than the rain of forty mornings.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said to Sa'd ibn Ubada: 'Indeed, God has established a limit (hadd) for every thing, and He has established a penalty (hadd) for everyone who transgresses a limit from the limits of God, Mighty and Majestic, and He has made what falls short of four witnesses a veil [of concealment] for the Muslims.'

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding half a lash and a third of a lash — one grabs the whip at half its length and two-thirds of its length.
For everything there is a limit (hadd), and whoever exceeds that limit, there shall be a penalty (hadd) upon him.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Amr ibn Qays! Are you aware that God, Mighty and Majestic, sent a Messenger and revealed to him a Book, and revealed in the Book everything that is needed, and made for it a guide pointing towards it, and made a limit (hadd) for everything, and for whoever exceeds the limit, a penalty (hadd)?' He (the narrator) said: I said, 'He sent a Messenger and revealed to him a Book, and revealed in the Book everything that is needed, and made for it a guide, and made a limit for everything.' He said: 'Yes.' I said, 'And how did He make a penalty for whoever exceeds the limit?' He said: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, has set a limit concerning wealth: that it cannot be taken except through its permissible means. So whoever takes it through other than its permissible means, his hand is cut off as a penalty for transgressing the limit. And God, Mighty and Majestic, has set a limit that marriage must not be contracted except through its permissible means, and whoever does otherwise — if he is unmarried, he receives the hadd penalty, and if he is married, he is stoned — for transgressing the limit.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Hafs ibn Awn, who raised it (mursal), said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A moment from a just Imam is superior to seventy years of worship, and a hadd penalty enacted for the sake of God on earth is superior to forty mornings of rain.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Sulayman, nephew of Hassan al-'Ijli, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'God did not create any permissible thing nor any forbidden thing except that it has limits — like the limits of this house of mine. Whatever was from the road is from the road, and whatever was from the house is from the house, even down to the compensation for a scratch and whatever is beyond that, and the lashing and half of the lashing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The stoning is the greater Penalty of Allah, and the lashing is the lesser Penalty of Allah.

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from Husayn ibn al-Munthir, from Amr ibn Qays al-Masir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not leave anything that the community needs until the Day of Resurrection except that He revealed it in His Book and clarified it for His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and He made a limit for every thing, and He made a sign upon it that points to it, and He made a limit upon whoever exceeds the limit.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), he used to strike with the whip, and with half the whip, and with part of it regarding the Penalties (Hudud). And when a boy and a girl who had not yet reached maturity were brought to him, he would not invalidate a single Penalty from the Penalties of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' It was said to him: 'And how did he strike?' He said: 'He would take the whip in his hand from its middle or from its third, then strike with it according to the measure of their ages, and he would not invalidate a single Penalty from the Penalties of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd al-Ajaly, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who raped a woman of her chastity. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should be killed, whether he was married or unmarried.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who raped a woman of herself, he said: He is struck with the sword, [and the strike] reaches him as much as it reaches [whether he lives or dies].

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding a man who raped a woman (of herself), he (peace be upon him) said: He should be killed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the man forces the woman upon herself, he should be struck with one stroke of the sword, either he dies from it or lives.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Humran, altogether, from Zurara who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The man rapes the woman of herself.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should be killed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, who said: 'I heard Bukeyr ibn Ayn narrating from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).' He said: 'The one who commits adultery with a close female relative (mahram) until he consummates it with her, is struck with one strike of the sword, which takes from him what it takes (life or death). And if she was the one pursuing him, she is struck with one strike of the sword, which takes from her what it takes.' It was said to him: 'So who strikes them both, when there is no adversary for the two of them?' He said: 'That is upon the Imam, when the matter is raised to him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Where is the one who commits incest with a close relative struck with the sword? Where is this strike?' He said: 'His neck is struck,' or he said: 'His throat is struck.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Mihran, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his sister. He said: 'He should be struck with one strike of the sword.' I said: 'So he would be finished (from it)?' He said: 'He should be imprisoned forever until he dies.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The man comes to his mahram.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is struck with one strike of the sword.'

Ibn Bukayr said, 'Hariz narrated to me from Bukayr with that.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from one of our companions, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Jamil who said, I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The man who comes to a close relative (Mahram), where should he be struck with the sword?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His throat.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who comes to a Mahram (close female relative) would be struck with a strike of the sword, taking from him what it takes (i.e., causing death or taking his life).'

Sahl, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Where is this strike to be applied?' meaning the one who has sexual relations with a Mahram (close relative). He (peace be upon him) said: 'His neck is struck,' or he said: 'His throat.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The adulterer, when he commits adultery, is whipped three times, and is killed in the fourth, meaning when he has been whipped three times.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mazi (peace be upon him), who said: The committers of all the major sins, when the Penalty (Hadd) is established twice upon them, they would be killed after the third.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding an insane woman who committed adultery and became pregnant: 'She is like the Sa'iba (unconditionally freed slave), she does not control her own affairs, and there is no stoning upon her, nor whipping, nor exile.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a woman who testified against herself that a man forced himself upon her: 'She is like the Sa'iba, she does not control her own affairs; had he wished, he could have killed her. Therefore, there is no whipping upon her, nor exile, nor stoning.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding an insane woman who committed adultery. He said: 'She has no control over her affair, and there is nothing upon her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the insane or the feeble-minded man commits adultery, he is whipped with the Hadd penalty, and if he is married, he is stoned.' I said: 'And what is the difference between the insane man and the insane woman, and the feeble-minded man and the feeble-minded woman?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman is merely come to (by the man), and the man comes to her, and he commits adultery when he understands how the pleasure comes, and indeed the woman is merely forced, and what is done to her is done while she does not understand what is being done to her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a woman who married a man while she had a husband. He said: If her first husband was residing with her in the city where she is, and she can reach him and he can reach her, then upon her is the ruling of the married adulterer, which is stoning. And if her first husband was absent from her, or was residing with her in the city but they could not reach each other, then upon her is the ruling of the unmarried adulteress, and there is no Li'an between them, nor separation. I said: Who will stone them or whip them with the Hadd, and her husband does not bring her to the Imam, nor does he intend that from her? He said: The Hadd remains for Allah in her body until one who establishes it does so, or she meets Allah while He is angry with her. I said: And if she was ignorant of what she did? He said: Is she not in the Dar al-Hijra (era of emigration)? I said: Yes. He said: So there is no woman among the Muslim women today except that she knows that it is permissible for the Muslim woman to have two husbands. And if the woman, when she commits fornication, says 'I did not know' or 'I was ignorant' that what I did was forbidden, and the Hadd is not established upon her, then the Huddud would be nullified.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Yazeed al-Kunasi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who married during her waiting period. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she married during the waiting period of a divorce where the husband has the right of return, then upon her is stoning; and if she married during a waiting period where the husband does not have the right of return, then upon her is the penalty (hadd) of the unmarried adulterer; and if she married during the waiting period after the death of her husband, before the expiry of four months and ten days, then there is no stoning upon her, and upon her is one hundred lashes.' I said, 'What is your view if that was from her due to ignorance?' He said, 'There is no woman today from the Muslim women except that she knows that upon her is a waiting period in divorce or death, and indeed the women of the pre-Islamic period used to know that.' I said, 'So if she knew that upon her is a waiting period, and she did not know how much it is?' He said, 'When she knew that upon her is the waiting period, the proof was necessitated upon her, so she should ask until she knows.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a woman whom a man married, and he found that she already had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the whipping, and upon her is the stoning, because he proceeded without knowledge, and she proceeded with knowledge. And his expiation, if one does not proceed to the Imam, is that he should give in charity five Aswaa' of fine flour.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a woman who had a husband absent from her, so she married another husband. He said: If the matter is raised to the Imam, then witnesses testify against her that she has an absent husband, and that his materials and news come to her, and that she has married another husband, it is upon the Imam to establish the Hadd penalty on her and to separate her from the one she married. I said, 'And what is done with the dower (mahr) which she took from him?' He said: 'If he can attain anything from it, let him take it, and if he cannot attain anything from it, then everything she took from it is prohibited upon her, similar to the payment of the immoral woman (prostitute).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A group of men participated in buying a slave girl, so they entrusted one of them and left the girl with him, and he had intercourse with her. He (peace be upon him) said: He is whipped with the penalty (Hadd), and the penalty is deferred from him by the measure of his share in her. The girl is evaluated, and her price is paid to the partners. If her value on the day he had intercourse with her is less than what she was bought for, he is liable for the excess of the price because he has spoiled her for his partners; and if her value on the day he had intercourse with her is more than what she was bought for, he is liable for the excess due to spoiling her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who acquired a slave girl from the war booty (al-fay') and copulated with her before it was distributed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The slave girl is evaluated and handed over to him at the price, and what his share was from the war booty is deducted for him from that price. He is whipped with the hadd (penalty), and the hadd is deferred from him by the measure of what was his share in her.' So I said, 'And how did the slave girl come to be handed over to him at the price, while others are not?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because he copulated with her, and it is not feared that she might be pregnant.'

Yunus from Al-Halby said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his contracted slave-girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had paid the quarter [of the manumission price], he would be whipped; and if he was married, he would be stoned; and if she had not paid anything, then there is nothing upon him [i.e., no hadd punishment].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a slave girl shared between two men. One of them emancipated his share of her. When his partner saw that, he leapt upon the slave girl and had intercourse with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who had intercourse with her shall be whipped with fifty lashes, and fifty lashes shall be deducted from his manumission, and half of her shall be free. And from the remaining half which was not emancipated, a tenth of her value shall be deducted if she is a virgin, and half of a tenth of her value if she is not a virgin. And she shall be compelled to work for the remainder.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Malik Bin Ayn, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a slave girl shared between two men, one of them emancipated his share. When his partner heard that from him, he leapt upon the girl and deflowered her on that very day. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who deflowered her shall be whipped fifty lashes, and fifty lashes shall be subtracted from him due to his right in her. A tenth of her value shall be paid to the slave girl as compensation for his intercourse with her, and she shall be employed (to work off the remainder).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a slave girl shared between two men, one of whom copulated with her without the other's knowledge, thereby impregnating her, he said: 'He is struck with half the penalty (hadd) and is liable for half her value (qimah).'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban from Isma'il al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding two men who bought a slave girl, and one of them copulated with her without his companion, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is struck with half the penalty and is liable for half the value, if she becomes pregnant.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj who said, 'I heard Abbad Al-Basri saying,' Ja'far (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The Hadd penalty is deferred from him by the measure of his share in her, and he is struck with what is other than that, meaning regarding the man when he has intercourse with a slave girl in which he has a share.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Exile is from one city to another city. And he said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) had exiled two men from Al-Kufa to Al-Basra.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man commits adultery and is whipped, it is befitting for the Imam to exile him from the land in which he was whipped to another. Indeed, it is upon the Imam to remove him from the city in which he was whipped.

Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the adulterer when he commits adultery, should he be exiled? He said: 'Yes, from the city in which he was whipped to another.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the adulterer when he is whipped the Hadd (penalty). He said: 'He is exiled from the land to a town where he will remain for a year.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Stoning is the greater Hadd of Allah, and whipping is the lesser Hadd of Allah. So when a married man commits adultery, he is stoned and not whipped.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The free man and the free woman, when they commit adultery, every one of the two shall be flogged with one hundred lashes. So, as for the married man and the married woman, upon both of them is stoning.

And by his chain, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The stoning is in the Quran — the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "When the old man and the old woman commit adultery, then stone both of them without question, for indeed they have fulfilled the desire."'

And by his chain, from Yunus, from the one who reported it, from Zurara, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) has said: The married man (muhsan) would be stoned, and the one who had a slave girl and did not copulate with her, so (his punishment is) whipping of one hundred lashes and exile for a year.

The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) stoned and did not whip. And they mentioned that Ali (peace be upon him) stoned in Kufa and whipped. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) denied that and said: We do not know this, i.e., why would he impose upon a man two hadd penalties — stoning and whipping — for one sin?

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazala, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The one who is not married (muhsan) shall be flogged one hundred lashes and shall not be exiled. And the one who has (taken a slave girl in possession) and has not consummated (the marriage) with her shall be flogged one hundred lashes and shall be exiled.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the old man and the old woman that they should both be flogged one hundred lashes; and he ruled stoning for the married person (muhsan); and he ruled regarding the virgin man and the virgin woman, when they commit fornication, flogging of one hundred lashes and exile for one year outside their own city — these are those who have had a marriage contract concluded but have not consummated it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Humran, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), saying to him, 'When is it obligatory upon the boy that he should be seized with the complete Penalties (Hudud), and for it to be established upon him and for him to be seized by it?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the orphan-hood exits from him, and he attains realisation (adراك).' I said, 'So for that is a Penalty (Hadd) to be recognised by?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he bed-wets (ihtalam), or reaches fifteen years of age, or grows hair (ash'ara), or grows pubic hair (anbata) before that, the complete Penalties would be established upon him, and he would be seized by it, and it would be taken for him.' I said, 'So, for the girl, when would the complete Penalties be Obligated upon her, and these would be taken for her, and she would be seized by it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The girl is not like the boy. The girl, when she gets married and copulated with (dakhila biha), and for her are nine years, the orphan-hood goes away from her, and her wealth is handed over to her, and her instructions are allowed with regards to the buying and the selling, and the complete Penalties would be established upon her, and she would be seized by it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the boy, his instructions are not allowed with regards to the buying and the selling, and he does not come out from the orphan-hood until he reaches fifteen years of age, or bed-wets, or grows hair, or grows pubic hair before that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Yazeed al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The girl, when she reaches nine years of age, the orphan-hood goes away from her, and she gets married, and the complete Penalties are established upon her, and for her. I said, 'The boy, when his father gets him married, and copulates with his wife, and he is without realisation, would the Penalties be established upon him, and he would be upon that state?' So he said: 'As for the complete Penalties by which the men are seized with, so no, but he would be whipped with regards to the Penalties, all of them, upon his years of age. So he would be seized by that what is between him and between fifteen years, and the Penalties of Allah would not be invalidated among His creatures, nor would the rights of Muslims be invalidated between them'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-'Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hadd (fixed penalty) of the Luti (sodomist) is like the Hadd of the Zani (adulterer/fornicator). And he said: If he was Muhsan (married), he is stoned, and otherwise he is whipped.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man came to a man.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was married (muhsan), then upon him is the killing (qatl), and if he was not married, then upon him is the whipping (jald). I said: 'So what is upon the passive one (al-muta')?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the killing in every state, whether he was married or not married.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was befitting for anyone that he should be stoned twice, it would be the sodomist (Luti) to be stoned.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man and a woman; her husband had sodomized her son (who was from another father) and had penetrated him, and the witnesses testified to that. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ordered that he be struck with the sword until he died, and the boy was struck with less than the Hadd (fixed penalty), and he said: 'But, had you been mature, I would have killed you because you had made it possible for him to penetrate you through your penetration.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yusuf ibn al-Harith, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Arzmī, from his father Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said: Umar was brought a man who had been sodomized in his backside, so he intended to whip him. He said to the witnesses, 'Did you see him entering it as the reed is inserted into the kohl container?' They said, 'Yes.' He said to Ali (peace be upon him), 'What do you view regarding this?' So he sought the stallion that had copulated with him but did not find him. Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'I view that his neck should be struck.' He said, 'So he ordered for his neck to be struck off. Then he said, 'Hold him, for there remains for him another punishment.' They said, 'And what is it?' He said, 'Call for a tun of firewood!' So he called for a tun of firewood. So he (the body) was wrapped in it, then brought out and incinerated with the fire. He said, 'Then he said: Allah has servants for whom in their loins are wombs like the wombs of women.' He said, 'So why do they not become pregnant in them?' He said, 'Because it is inverted in their backsides, a gland like the gland of the camel. So when it stirs, they stir, and when it is calm, they are calm.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Sayf ibn Umira, from Abd al-Rahman al-Arzami, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man was found with a man during the emirate of Umar, so one of them fled and the other was seized. He was brought to Umar, who said to the people, "What do you think?" This one said, "Do this," and that one said, "Do this." Then he said, "What do you say, O Abu al-Hasan?" He said, "Strike his neck," so they struck his neck.' He said: 'Then he intended to have him carried away, so he said, "Wait! There still remains something from his Hadd (penalty)." He said, "What remains?" He said, "Call for firewood." So Umar called for firewood, and Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ordered him to be incinerated with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Abdul Samad ibn Basheer, from Suleyman ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who does it with the man. He said: If it was without penetration, then whipping; and if it was with penetration, stand him up straight, then strike with the sword with one strike. The sword takes from him what it takes. So I said to him, 'It is the killing.' He said, 'It is that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The passive sodomist, his Penalty (Hadd) is the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'One in Ihram kissed a boy out of desire.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped one hundred lashes.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man came to a man.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him, if he was married (muhsan), is the killing (rajm), and if he was not married, then upon him is the Penalty (Hadd).' I said: 'So what is upon the passive one (al-mu'ta)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the killing, in every state, whether he was married or not married.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Harun, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, raising it, said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who engage in mutual sodomy. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalty (hadd) for both of them is the penalty (hadd) of the adulterer. So if one of them is the active partner upon his companion, the active one is struck with one strike with the sword, which takes from him what it takes and leaves from him what it leaves, intending his death by it; and the passive one is burnt in the fire.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), when a man is seized with a boy in one quilt, both naked, the man would be struck (whipped), and the boy be disciplined. And if he has penetrated and was married, he would be stoned.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza and Hisham and Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That some women entered upon him, and a woman from them asked him about Al-Sahq (lesbianism), so he said: 'Its penalty is the penalty of the adulterer.' The woman said, 'Has Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned that in the Quran?' He said, 'Yes.' She said, 'And where is it?' He said, 'They are the dwellers of Al-Rass.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about two women who are found in one quilt. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Each one of them should be whipped one hundred lashes'.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The lesbian would be whipped.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: It is not permissible for two women to spend the night in one quilt, unless there is a partition between them. If they do so, they are prohibited from that. If they are found after the prohibition, each one of them is whipped a hadd (a fixed penalty). If they are found again in one quilt, they are whipped. If they are found for the third time, they are killed.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Amr ibn Uthman and from his father, all together, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: While Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was in the gathering of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), a group of people came and said, 'O Abu Muhammad, we seek Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' He said, 'What is your need?' They said, 'We want to ask him a question.' He said, 'And what is it? Inform us of it.' They said, 'A woman, her husband copulated with her. When he rose from her, she rose with her warmth, and fell upon a virgin slave-girl, and pressed against her, so the sperm fell into her, and she became pregnant. What do you say about this?' Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a dilemma, and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) is suited for it. And I say: If I am correct, it is from Allah, then from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him); and if I err, it is from myself. So I hope that I will not err, God willing. One should proceed against the woman and take from her the dowry of the virgin slave-girl during the first opportunity, because the child will not exit from her until she is split, so her virginity will be lost. Then the woman will be stoned because she is married (muhsan). Then the slave-girl will be awaited until she gives birth to what is in her belly, and the child will be returned to its father, the owner of the sperm. Then the slave-girl will be whipped with the Hadd.' He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: So the people departed from the presence of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and met Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). They said, 'What did you say to Abu Muhammad and what did he say to you?' So they informed him. He said, 'Had I been the one questioned, I would not have had more knowledge about it than what my son said.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ziyad called us and said, 'Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful wrote to me that I should ask you about this matter.' So I said, 'And what is it?' He said, 'A man went to a woman, and she carried his water (sperm). Then she rubbed it with a slave girl, and she became pregnant.' So I said to him, 'Ask the people of Medina about it.' He said, 'So he threw a letter to me, and therein was: Ask Ja'far ibn Muhammad about it. If he answers you, fine; otherwise, carry it back to me.' So I said to him, 'The woman would be stoned, and the slave girl would be whipped, and the child would be attached to its father.' He said, 'And I do not know it except that he said, 'And he (the caliph) is the one who is involved in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a woman who deflowered a slave girl by her hand. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon her is her dower, and she would be whipped eighty lashes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Jareer, from Sadeer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who goes to the animal, he said: He is penalized less than the (complete) Penalty (Hadd), and he must compensate the price of the animal to its owner, because he has spoiled it for him. It is slaughtered, burnt, and buried if it is from those whose flesh is eaten; and if it is from those whose back is ridden upon, he must compensate its price, be whipped less than the (complete) Penalty (Hadd), and it is taken out from the city in which the act was committed with it to other lands where it is not known, so that it is sold there, lest it be scoffed at with it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has intercourse with a beast, or a sheep, or a camel, or a cow. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is that he be whipped a penalty (hadd) that is not the complete penalty (hadd). Then he would be exiled from one land to another. And they mentioned that the flesh of that beast is prohibited, along with its milk.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from one of his companions, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), and Sabbah al-Hazza', from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), regarding the man who goes to the animal. They all said: If the animal belonged to the doer, it would be slaughtered; so when it is dead, it would be burnt with fire and no benefit would be taken from it, and he would be struck with twenty-five lashes, which is a quarter of the penalty (hadd) of the adulterer. And if the animal did not belong to him, it would be evaluated, its price taken from him, and given to its owner; and it would be slaughtered, burnt with fire, no benefit taken from it, and he would be struck with twenty-five lashes. So I said, 'And what is the sin of the animal?' He said: 'It has no sin, but the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did this and ordered it, so that people would not be bold with the animals and the lineage would be cut off.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the one who approaches the animal and penetrates, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the Penalty (Hadd).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged that the slander (fabrication of accusation) is three, meaning three aspects: when a man accuses a man of adultery, and when he says 'his mother is an adulteress', and when he is called by the name of someone other than his father; for that there is a Hadd (fixed penalty) of eighty (lashes). Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He said regarding the man when he slanders a married woman: He is lashed eighty (lashes), whether he is free or a slave.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who slanders another man with adultery, he said: He is whipped, as established in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said, And I asked Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who slanders a young slave girl, so he said: He is not whipped unless she has reached maturity or is near to it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a woman who slandered a man, he said: 'She is whipped eighty lashes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Maryam Al-Ansari, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the boy who had not yet reached puberty (had not bed-wetted), if he slanders a man, would he be whipped? He (peace be upon him) said: No, and that is because if a man slandered the boy, he would not be whipped (either).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hakam Al-A'ma and Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who said to another man, 'O son of the fornicator,' meaning adultery. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother was alive and present, then she came seeking her right, he would be whipped eighty lashes; and if she was absent, he would be awaited with her until she arrives so she seeks her right; and if she had died and nothing was known about her except for goodness, the fabricator upon her would be whipped the limit, eighty lashes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who slandered a woman cursed by her husband, he said: Upon him is the Penalty (Hadd).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about the son of the raped woman, when a man fabricates against her and says, 'O son of the doer (of fornication),' so he said: 'I view that upon him is the Hadd (penalty) of eighty lashes, and he should repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from what he said.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) had judged regarding a woman who gifted her maid to her husband, so he fell upon her. So the slave girl became pregnant and the woman denied that she had gifted her to him, and she said, 'She is my servant'. So when she feared that the Penalty (Hadd) would be established upon the man, she confessed that she had gifted her to him. So when she has accepted having gifted, she should be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) due to her having slandered her husband.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hakam Al-A'ma and Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who said to another man, 'O son of the fornicator' (meaning adultery), he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother was alive and present, then she came to claim her right, he would be whipped eighty lashes; and if she was absent, he would be awaited until she arrived so she could claim her right; and if she had died and nothing was known of her except goodness, the fabricator would be whipped the prescribed punishment of eighty lashes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from one of his companions, raising it, said: It was in the era of Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him), two men had established brotherhood between themselves for the Sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So, one of the two died and bequeathed to the other regarding the protection of a daughter he had. So the man protected her and made her status to be of the status of his children with regards to the kindness, and the honour, and the care. Then a journey presented itself, so he went out, and bequeathed to his wife with regards to the young girl. His journey got prolonged to the extent that the young girl matured, and she had beauty for her, and the man had been contracted with regard to her protection and the care for her. So when his wife saw that, she feared that he would proceed, and he would see her to have reached the age of the women, so he would be astounded by her beauty, so he would marry her. So she and the women who were with her pre-conceived malice against her, a number of whom held her down, then she destroyed her virginity by her fingers. So when the man came over from his journey and came to be in his house, called the young girl. But, she refused to answer him being too embarassed from what had happened. So he insisted calling her, she refused to answer him with all of that. So when he had frequented that, his wife said to him, ‘Leave her, for she is too embarassed as she had come to a sin which she has done’. He said to her, ‘And what is it?’ She said, ‘Such and such’, and accused her with the immorality. So the man said, ‘We are for Allah and to Him we are returning’. Then he stood up to the girl, so he rebuked her and said to her, ‘Woe be unto you! Do you not know what I have done with you from the kindness? By Allah! I had not promised you except to one of my sons or my brothers, even if you were my own daughter. So what called you to what you did?’ So the girl said, ‘But when she said to you what she said, by Allah, I did not do what your wife is accusing me with, and she had lied against me, and that the story is such and such’, and she described to him what his wife had done with her. He said: ‘So the man grabbed the hand of his wife and a hand of the girl, so he went with the two of them until he sat both of them down in front of Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him), and i

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Suleiman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The slanderer of the woman cursed by her husband (in the context of li'an) is whipped.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub and Ibn Bakeyr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who slanders another man, so he is whipped, and he repeats the slander against him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he says to him, "That which I said to you was true," he would not be whipped; and if he were to slander him with adultery after having been whipped, so upon him would be the Penalty (Hadd); and if he slanders him before he is whipped, by ten slanders, there would not happen to be upon him, except for one Penalty (Hadd).'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: When a man says to another man, "O passive sodomist!" and "O one copulated with in his backside!", then upon him is the Penalty (Hadd), the Penalty of the slanderer.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a man were brought to me who had slandered a Muslim servant with adultery, and we know nothing of him except goodness, I would strike him with the penalty, the penalty of a free man, except for one lash.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Hamza ibn Humran, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: I asked him about a man who emancipated half of his slave girl, then accused her of adultery. He said: 'I view upon him fifty lashes, and he should seek forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for his deed.' I said, 'What is your view if she frees him from his accusation of her and forgives him?' He said: 'There is no whipping upon him if she forgives him before she raises the case (to the judge).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The slanderer of the foundling is penalized (by the Hadd), and the slanderer of the son of al-mula'ana is penalized (by the Hadd).

From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When the immoral woman is asked, "Who committed fornication with you?" and she says, "So-and-so," then upon her are two penalties: a penalty for her immorality, and a penalty for her accusation against the Muslim man.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Christian woman and the Jewish woman, if they are under the Muslim man, and she is flogged, and he is slandered regarding her son? He (peace be upon him) said: He is flogged with the penalty (hadd) because the Muslim man has protected her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who slanders the young girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not whipped unless she has reached puberty or is near to it.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who slanders a young girl, he is flogged. He (peace be upon him) said: No, until she reaches adulthood.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who fabricated [a charge of adultery] upon a group of people. He said: If they come with it [the charge] collectively, he is whipped with one Hadd (penalty); and if they come with it separately, a Hadd is inflicted upon each one of them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan al-Attar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man who slanders a group of people?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'With one statement?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said, 'He is given one Hadd (penalty). But if he differentiates between them in the slander, a Hadd is given to each one of them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who fabricated (a slander) upon a group of people. He said: If they come with it together, he is whipped with one penalty (Hadd); and if they come with it separately, he is whipped for each man, one penalty (Hadd).
From him, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Similar to it

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem ibn Ibrahim, from Abbad al-Basri, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about three men who testified against a man for adultery, and they said, 'We will now bring the fourth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are whipped with the penalty of the slanderer, eighty lashes, each man among them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'May I not be the first of the four witnesses upon the adulterer, for fear that one of them might withdraw, so I would be whipped.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man against whom three testified that he had committed adultery with so-and-so, and the fourth testified that he did not know with whom he had committed adultery. He said: 'He is neither whipped nor stoned.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him) Regarding three men who testified against a man for adultery, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Where is the fourth?' They said, 'He is coming now.' He said: 'Apply the Hadd (penalty) upon them, for in the Hadd punishments there is no waiting for a moment.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin and Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who said to his wife, 'O adulteress, I have committed adultery with you,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is one Hadd (penalty) for slandering her, and as for his words, I have committed adultery with you, there is no Hadd (penalty) in it, except if he testifies against himself with four testimonies of adultery in the presence of the Imam.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man accuses his wife before he consummates the marriage with her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is given the Hadd (punishment), and separation is effected between him and her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Mudarrib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever accuses his wife before he has intercourse with her, he is whipped with the Hadd penalty, and she remains his wife.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except for themselves He said: He is the one who accuses his wife. So when he accuses her, then he admits that he lied against her, he is whipped the Hadd (penalty), and his wife is returned to him. And if he refuses (to admit lying) and stands by it, so he testifies against her four times with Allah that he is from the truthful ones, and the fifth time then the Curse of Allah be upon him if he is from the liars. And if she intends to stave off the punishment from herself, and the punishment is the stoning, she testifies four times with Allah that he is from the liars, and the fifth time that the Anger of Allah be upon her if he is from the truthful ones. And if she does not do it, she is stoned; and if she does it, the Hadd is staved off from herself, then she is not permissible for him until the Day of Resurrection.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man whom the Imam paused for the Lian (cursing). He testified with two testimonies, then withdrew and lied about himself before finishing the Lian. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped the Hadd of the slanderer, and he is not separated from his wife.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who performed li'an with his wife while she was pregnant, then he claimed her child after she gave birth, alleging that it was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The child is returned to him, and he is not whipped, because the li'an has passed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked him about the man who fabricates (slanders) upon his wife. He said: He is whipped, then separation is made between them, and he does not perform Li'an with her until he says: 'I testify that I saw you doing such and such.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the man who slanders his wife: he is whipped, then they are separated, and he is not subjected to li'an (mutual cursing) until he says that he has seen someone committing immorality with her between her two legs.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who accused his wife of adultery, so they performed li'an (mutual cursing), then he accused her again after they had separated, also of adultery. Is there a hadd (fixed penalty) upon him? He said: Yes, there is a hadd upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), regarding a man who said to his wife, 'I did not find you a virgin.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be whipped.' I said, 'So if he were to repeat it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be whipped, for he would probably stop.'

Yunus narrated from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who said to his wife, 'You did not come to me as a virgin.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him because virginity can be lost without sexual intercourse.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Ibn Mudarib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever accuses his wife before he consummates the marriage with her, he is whipped the Hadd penalty, and she remains his wife.

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who commits adultery while he has a concubine and a slave girl whom he has intercourse with and who is with him — does the slave girl make him muhsan? He said: Yes, because with him is what makes him needless of adultery. I said: What if he has a slave girl but claims that he does not have intercourse with her? He said: He will not be believed. I said: What if he has a woman in temporary marriage (mut'a), does she make him muhsan? He said: No. It is only based on what is permanently with him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from the one who mentioned him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — regarding the man who marries in temporary marriage (mut'a) — does it make him muhsan (married)? He said: No. That is only applicable to the permanent thing with him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Rabi' al-Asam, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a wife in al-Iraq and committed immorality while he was in al-Hijaz. He said: He shall be struck with the prescribed penalty (hadd) of the fornicator — one hundred lashes — and he shall not be stoned. I said: But if he was with her in the same city, yet is imprisoned in a prison, unable to go out to her and she is unable to come to him — what is your view if he commits adultery in the prison? He said: He is at the status of the one absent from his wife; he shall be flogged one hundred lashes.
Hareez said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the muhsan. He said: 'The one who commits adultery/fornication while he has with him what makes him needless of it.'

Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The absent man and the absent woman — there is no stoning upon them both, except if the man happens to be with the woman and the woman with the man.

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'A man who has a slave girl — does she make him muhsan (married/protected)?' Then he said: 'Yes, but rather it is on the basis of needlessness (of sexual satisfaction).' He said: I said: 'And the woman of temporary marriage (mut'a)?' He said: Then he said: 'No, that (ihsan) is conditional upon that which is permanent (i.e., permanent marriage).' He said: I said: 'But if he claims that he had not had intercourse with her?' He said: Then he said: 'He will not be believed, and rather that (hadd penalty) is imposed upon him because he owns her.'
From him, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, who said: A man does not have the status of being married (muhsan) until there is a woman with him whose door he can lock upon her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Rifa'a who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who commits fornication before he consummates his marriage — is he stoned? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the slave who marries a free woman, then is freed, and then commits immorality: so he said: 'There is no stoning upon him until he has intercourse with the free woman after he has been emancipated.' I said, 'Does the free woman have a right of choice over him when he is emancipated?' He said, 'No. She has already consented to him while he was a slave, so he remains upon his first marriage.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked, 'What is the al-muhsan?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'May Allah have mercy on you. The one who has a woman for whom he goes out in the morning and returns in the evening, so he is al-muhsan.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, he raised it (to the Imam), saying: The Penalty (Hadd) during travel is for the one who commits adultery; he is not stoned even if he is married (Muhsan), (i.e., a journey where he) shortens (the Prayer) and breaks the Fast.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the man who had a wife in Basra, so he committed fornication in Kufa, that the stoning be deferred from him and the penalty of the fornicator be lashed. He (peace be upon him) said: And he judged regarding a man imprisoned in prison, and for him was a free woman in his house in the city, and he could not reach her, so he committed adultery in the prison. He said: Upon him is the lashing, and the stoning is deferred from him.

Ali, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about the man who is absent from his family and commits adultery; is he stoned if he has a wife and he is absent from her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one absent from his family is not stoned, nor the slave who has not yet cohabited with his wife, nor the owner of temporary marriage (Mut'ah).' I said, 'So in which stage of his journey is he not considered married (Muhsan)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he shortens (the prayer) and breaks (the fast), so he is not considered married.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him about a man who fabricates [testimony], how it befits the Imam to whip him? He said: He is whipped between the two whippings.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that nothing should be removed from the clothes of the slanderer except the robe.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The fabricator (of slander) is whipped with a whipping between the two whippings; all of his body is whipped.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The fabricator (of slander) is struck between the two strikes; his whole body is struck, over his clothes.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The adulterer is whipped more intensely than the drinker of wine, and the drinker of wine is whipped more intensely than the slanderer, and the slanderer is whipped more intensely than the one who receives ta'zir (disciplinary punishment).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who drank a sip of wine. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is to be whipped eighty lashes. A little of it or more of it is Prohibited.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'How did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to administer the lash?' So he said: 'He used to strike with the slippers (feet) and he increased, every time they brought the drinker. Then the people did not cease to increase until it stopped at eighty. Ali (peace be upon him) pointed that out to Umar, so he was pleased with it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn Umar was made to stand, and he had drunk wine, so Umar ordered that he be struck. No one stepped forward to strike him until Ali (peace be upon him) arose with a doubled belt and struck him with it forty times.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), the drinker of wine is to be whipped eighty (lashes) and the drinker of Al-Nabeez is to be whipped eighty (lashes).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Al-Walid ibn Uqba was witnessed with the drinking of wine, Uthman said to Ali (peace be upon him), Judge between him and those who alleged that he drank wine. So Ali (peace be upon him) ordered, and he was whipped with a whip that had two strands, forty lashes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: When a man drinks wine, he becomes intoxicated; and when he is intoxicated, he raves; and when he raves, he fabricates (lies); so flog him with the penalty of the fabricator.'
