Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to administer eighty lashes for wine and Al-Nabeez, to the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian. I said, 'And what is the relevance of the Jew and the Christian?' He said, 'It is not for them to display their drinking; that happens in their homes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would lash the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian regarding wine and Al-Nabeez with eighty (lashes). So I said, 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian?' He said: 'When they display that in a city from the cities, because it is not for them that they should be displaying their drinking of it.'

Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalty (hadd) regarding wine is established whether a little or much is drunk from it.' Then he (Abu Abdillah) said: 'Umar was brought Qudamah ibn Maz'un, who had drunk wine, and the proof was established upon him. So he asked Ali (peace be upon him), who ordered that he be whipped eighty (lashes).' Qudamah said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! There is no penalty upon me; I am among those rightful for this Verse: "On those who believe and do righteous deeds, there is no blame for what they eat."' So Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'You are not among its rightful ones. The food of its rightful ones is permissible to them; they do not eat or drink except what Allah has permitted to them.' Then Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The drinker, when he drinks, does not know what he eats or what he drinks.' So they whipped him eighty lashes.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), the drinker of wine is to be whipped, and the drinker of the intoxicant.' I said, 'How much?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their penalty (Hadd) is one (and the same).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abi al-Maghra', from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to flog the free man and the slave, the Jew and the Christian, regarding wine, with eighty (lashes).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Every intoxicant from the drinks obligates the penalty (Hadd) with regards to it, just as it obligates regarding the wine.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalty (hadd) of the Jew, the Christian, and the slave regarding wine and fabrication (slander) is the same. And indeed, the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma) were agreed upon that they may drink it in their own houses.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the intoxicated one and the adulterer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are both whipped with whips, bare between the shoulders. As for the penalty regarding slander (al-qadhf), he is whipped upon his clothes, a beating between the two beatings.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, raising it, from Abu Maryam, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought Al-Najjashi the poet, who had drunk wine during the month of Ramadan. So he (peace be upon him) whipped him eighty (lashes). Then he (peace be upon him) detained him for one night. Then he (peace be upon him) called for him the next day and whipped him twenty lashes with a whip. He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful! You have already whipped me for drinking wine, and what are these twenty?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for your audacity in drinking wine during the month of Ramadan.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man drank wine during the time of Abu Bakr, so it was brought to Abu Bakr. He said to him, 'Did you drink wine?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'And why, while it is prohibited?' The man said to him, 'I embraced Islam, and my Islam was good, and my home is among a people who drink wine and consider it permissible. Had I known that it was forbidden, I would have avoided it.' Abu Bakr turned to Umar and said, 'What do you say regarding the matter of this man?' Umar said, 'It is a perplexing matter, and there is none for it except Abu al-Hasan.' So Abu Bakr said, 'Call Ali for us.' Umar said, 'The judge is summoned from his home.' So they stood up, with the man and those present among the people accompanying them, until they came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). They informed him of the man's story, and the man recounted his own story. He said, 'Send with him someone who will go around with him to the gatherings of the Emigrants and the Helpers; whoever recited the Verse of Prohibition to him, let him testify against him.' So they did that with him, but no one testified against him that he had recited the Verse of Prohibition to him. So he freed him and said to him, 'If you drink after this, we will establish the Hadd (penalty) upon you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Al-Husayn ibn Atiyya, from Hisham ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him), said: He was seated in the Masjid, and I was with him, so he heard the voice of a man being whipped at the morning prayer on a day of intense cold. He said: 'What is this?' They said, 'A man being whipped.' He said: 'Glory be to Allah! In a time like this? No one is whipped regarding any of the fixed penalties during winter except during the last hour of the day, nor in summer except during the coldest part of the day.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mirdas from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from one of our companions who said: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) went out for one of his needs, so he passed by a man being penalized during the winter. So he said: 'Glory be to Allah! This is not befitting!' So I said, 'And for this is a Penalty (Hadd)?' He said: 'It befits the man applying the Penalty during the winter that he applies it during the heat of the day, and for the one who applies a Penalty during the summer, is that he should apply it during the coldness of the day'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'A Penalty (Hadd) would not be established upon anyone in the land of the enemy'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Mu'alla, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever a drinker of wine was brought to him, would whip him. Then if he was brought to him a second time, he would whip him. Then if he was brought to him a third time, he would strike his neck.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever drinks wine, flog him; if he repeats, flog him; if he repeats, kill him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine, so whip him. So if he repeats, so whip him. So if he repeats for the third time, so kill him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding the drinker of wine: when he drinks, he is whipped. So if he repeats, he is whipped. So if he repeats, he is killed on the third (offence). Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them): He said: 'The one who drinks wine, so whip him. So if he repeats, so whip him. So if he repeats, so kill him.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mazi (peace be upon him), who said: The commiters of all the major sins, when the Penalty (Hadd) is established upon them twice, they are killed in the third.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), regarding a man who confessed upon himself for a Hadd (fixed penalty), and did not specify which Hadd it was. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is ordered to be whipped until he is the one who prevents the Hadd from himself [by specifying it].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them), regarding a man who confessed to adultery four times, and he was married (muhsan), that he would be stoned until he dies, or he denies himself before being stoned, saying 'I did not do it'. So if he says that, he is left alone and is not stoned. And he (peace be upon him) said: The thief is not cut until he confesses to the theft twice. So if he retracts, he guarantees the theft, and is not cut if there are no witnesses. And he (peace be upon him) said: The adulterer is not stoned until he confesses four times to adultery, if there are no witnesses. So if he retracts, he is left alone and is not stoned.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man confesses upon himself with a penalty (Hadd) or a fabrication, then denies it, he is whipped. I said, 'What is your view if he confesses with a penalty (Hadd) upon himself, in which stoning is reached, would you have him stoned?' He said, 'No. But, I would have whipped him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who confessed to a hadd penalty upon himself, then denied it afterwards. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he confesses in the presence of the Imam that he stole, then denies, his hand is cut off, even if his nose is crushed (i.e., despite his haughtiness). If he confesses that he drank wine, or by accusation, they lash him eighty lashes.' I said: 'If he confesses to a hadd in which stoning is obligatory, would you stone him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but I would lash him with the hadd.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said: When a man confesses upon himself for murder, he is killed if there are no witnesses against him. So if he retracts and says, 'I did not do it,' he is left alone and is not killed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Riab, from Durays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The slave, when he confesses once before the Imam that he has stolen, his hand is cut, and the slave girl, when she confesses upon herself regarding the theft, her hand is cut.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The thief, when he comes from his own self, repentant to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and returns the stolen goods to its owner, so there is not cutting (of the hand) upon him.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Whoever acknowledges upon himself, in the presence of the Imam, the right of one of the Muslims, it is not incumbent upon the Imam to establish the Hadd (penalty) upon him, which he acknowledged in his presence, until the owner of the Hadd right or his guardian is present, so that he may claim his right.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to cut [the hand of the thief] regarding a 'Bayza'. I said, 'And what is a Bayza?' He said, 'A Bayza, its value is a quarter of a Dinar.' And I said, 'Is it the lowest threshold for the Hadd [punishment] of the thief?' So he was silent.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The hand of the thief is not cut off except for an item whose value reaches a Mijann, and it is a quarter of a Dinar.

Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, and from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, all together from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The lowest amount with which the hand of the thief is cut is five dinars.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The lowest amount with which a man is cut (amputated) is one-fifth of a Dinar.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'In how much is the thief's hand cut?' He said, 'In a quarter of a Dinar.' I said to him, 'In two Dirhams?' He said, 'In a quarter of a Dinar, [the value of] the Dinar reaching what it reaches.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I said to him, 'What is your view of the one who steals less than a quarter of a Dinar? Does the name of the thief befall him, and is he a thief in the Presence of Allah in that state?' He said, 'Every one who steals anything from a Muslim, so he has taken it and secured it in his possession, upon him befalls the name of the thief, and he is a thief in the Presence of Allah. But, his hand is not cut except in a quarter of a Dinar or more. And if the hands of the thieves were to be cut regarding what is less than a quarter of a Dinar, you would find the generality of the people as being (hand) cut.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'From where is the cutting obligated?' So he extended his fingers and said, 'From here,' meaning from the hinge of the palm.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The cutting is from the middle of the palm, and the thumb is not cut; and when the foot is cut, the heel is left and is not cut.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) did not increase upon cutting the hand and the leg, and he said: 'I am shy of my Lord that I should leave him without having for him what he uses for cleansing after relieving himself or purifying himself with.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him, if he were to steal after the cutting of the hand and the leg?' So he said: 'I would keep him in prison forever, and spare the people from his evil.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the thief: 'When he steals, I cut off his right hand; and when he steals a second time, I cut off his left leg. Then if he steals a third time, I imprison him and leave his right leg so he may walk upon it to the latrine, and his left hand so he may eat with it and clean himself (from the latrine) with it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'I am shy of Allah that I would leave him unable to benefit from anything, but rather I imprison him until he dies in prison.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not cut off (any further limbs) from a thief after (cutting) his hand and his leg.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who stole, so he said: I heard my father saying: A man who had stolen was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) during his time, so he cut his hand. Then he was brought to him a second time, so he cut his leg from the opposite side. Then he was brought to him a third time, so he kept him imprisoned for life and spent upon him from the treasury of the Muslims, and said: This is what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do. I will not oppose him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The cutting of the foot of the thief after the cutting of the hand, then it is not cut afterwards. So if he repeats, he is imprisoned, and he is provided for from the public treasury of the Muslims.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man whom he ordered to have his right hand cut off. So his left hand was presented, and they cut it off, and reckoned it as his right, and they said, 'We have only cut his left; should his right be cut off as well?' He said, 'His right hand would not be cut off, and his left has already been cut.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who took an egg from the war booty, and they said, 'He has stolen, so cut him,' that, 'I would not cut anyone who has a share in what he has taken.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: When the thief is seized, his hand is cut from the middle of the palm. If he returns [to stealing], his foot is cut from the middle of the foot. If he returns, he is confined to prison. If he steals in prison, he is killed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who stole an item, but he denied it (argued against the claim). So he was whipped. Then he produced it (the stolen item) exactly. Would the cutting be obligated upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. But, had he acknowledged (the theft) and did not produce the stolen item, his hand would not be cut, because he acknowledged (the theft) while bearing the punishment (of whipping).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who pierced a house, but was seized before he could reach anything. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be punished. So if he was seized and he had extracted goods, then upon him is the cutting (of the hand).' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man who was seized and he was carrying a bundle of clothes, and he said that the owner of the house had given them to him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The cutting would be staved off from him except if proof is established upon him. So if the proof is established upon him, he is cut.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The hand and the leg are cut, then no other (parts) are cut afterwards, but if he repeats, he is imprisoned and is maintained from the treasury of the Muslims.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the thief: When he is seized and he has taken the goods, and he is in the house and has not yet come out, so he said: There is no cutting upon him until he comes out with it from the house.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Bukayr ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who stole but they were not able to catch him, then he stole again but they were not able to catch him, and he stole a third time so he was seized. The proof came, and they testified against him for the first theft and the last theft. He said: 'His hand is cut for the first theft and his leg is not cut for the last theft.' It was said: 'How is that?' He said: 'Because the witnesses testified together in one place for the first and the last theft before he was cut for the first theft. And if the witnesses had testified against him for the first theft, then waited until he was cut, then testified against him for the last theft, his left leg would be cut.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: The hand of the thief is cut, and his thumb is left, along with the center of his palm; and his leg is cut, and his heel is left for him so he may walk upon it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Men who had stolen were brought to Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), so he cut their hands. Then he said: "That which has separated from your bodies has arrived to the Fire. So if you repent, you will pull it (out from the Fire), and if you do not repent, it will pull you (into the Fire)."'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the thief steals, his hand is cut, and he is liable to compensate for what he took.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who is crippled in the right hand or crippled in the left hand who steals, he said: His right hand is cut off in all cases.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'Inform me about the thief, why is his right hand and his left leg cut, and not his right hand and right leg?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'How good is what you asked. If his right hand and right leg were cut, he would fall on his left side and would not be able to stand. But if his right hand and left leg are cut, he balances and stands upright.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and how can he stand when his leg is cut?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The cutting is not from where you think. Rather, the leg is cut from the ankle, and what remains of his foot allows him to stand, to pray and worship Allah.' I said to him, 'From where is the hand cut?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The four fingers are cut, and the thumb is left, so he can depend on it during prayer and wash his face with it for prayer.' I said, 'So this cutting, who was the first to cut in this manner?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Uthman ibn Affan approved it for Muawiya.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I heard him saying: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: I do not apply the hadd of cutting (for theft) regarding open Daghara, and it is Khalsah, but I reprimand him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad all together, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who pilfered a garment from the market. So they said, 'This man has stolen.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'I do not cut [the hand] for the open theft (al-daghara), but I cut the hand of the one who takes and then hides.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from a number of our companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no cutting (amputation of the hand) upon the one who embezzles, and there is no cutting upon the one who displaces the dirhams from the cloth of the man.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who steals with stealthy embezzlement, he would not be cut, but he would be whipped with an intense whipping'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a pickpocket who had stolen dirhams from a man's sleeve. He said: 'If he had stolen it from his outer shirt, I would not cut his hand, but if he had stolen it from his inner shirt, I would cut his hand.'

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Four [types of thieves] do not have the hand-cutting penalty applied to them: the embezzler, the one who steals from the war booty, the one who steals from the war booty, and the employee thief; for these are treachery.'

And by this chain, that Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had picked an earring from the ear of a girl. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is open snatching'. So he (peace be upon him) whipped him and imprisoned him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ali ibn Saeed, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who hired a donkey, then turned with it to the owners of the clothes (shop), and bought from them a garment or two garments, and left the donkey. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The donkey is returned to its owner, and the one who took the two garments is pursued, and there is no cutting upon him; rather, it is betrayal (of trust).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who employs a worker, and the worker steals from his house. Would his hand be cut? He (peace be upon him) said: 'This one is a trustee, he is not a thief. This is treachery.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The guest, when he steals, his hand is not cut, and if the guest invites a guest and he steals, the hand of the guest of the guest is cut.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a group of people who accompanied each other on a journey as friends, so one of them stole the belongings of the other. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is treachery; he would not be cut (for haram theft), but he would be pursued for his theft and his treachery.' It was said to him (peace be upon him), 'So if one steals from the house of his own father?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He would not be cut, because a son of the man is not barred from entering the house of his father. This is treachery, and similar to that is the one who steals from the house of his brother, and his sister, when he enters (their house), as he is not barred from the entering.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The penalty (hadd) of the grave robber is the penalty (hadd) of the thief.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and a letter came to him from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik regarding a man who dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and then married her. The people have differed regarding us here; one group said, 'Kill him,' and another group said, 'Burn him.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'The sanctity of the deceased is like the sanctity of the living. His Hadd is that his hand be cut off for his digging up and stripping the clothes, and the Hadd for adultery be established upon him; if he were married, he would be stoned, and if he were not married, he would be flogged with one hundred lashes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a grave robber. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) grabbed him by his hair, struck him against the ground, then ordered the people to trample him with their feet. So they trampled him until he died.

Habib ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from 'Amr ibn Thabit, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The thief of the dead is cut, just as the thief of the living is cut.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Sayyar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A grave robber was seized in the era of Muawiya, so he said to his companions, 'What are your views?' So they said, 'Punish him and free his way'. So a man from the people said, 'This is not what Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) did'. He (Muawiya) said, 'So what did he do?' So he said, 'He cut (the hand) of the grave robber and said, 'He is a thief, and a desecrator of the dead'.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The grave robber is cut, and the pickpocket is cut, and the embezzler is not cut.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a young boy who had not reached maturity, a boy of ten years, who committed fornication with a woman. He said: 'The boy shall be flogged less than the full Hadd, and the woman shall receive the complete Hadd.' It was said to him: 'What if she was married?' He said: 'She shall not be stoned, because the one who copulated with her had not reached maturity; and if he had been mature, she would have been stoned.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Ibn Bukayr who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the last meeting I had with him about a boy who had not reached puberty who fell upon a woman or committed fornication with a woman — what should be done with both of them? He said: The boy shall be flogged less than the prescribed penalty (hadd), and the full prescribed penalty shall be established upon the woman. I said: A girl who had not reached puberty was found with a man committing fornication with her. He said: The girl shall be flogged less than the prescribed penalty (hadd), and the full prescribed penalty shall be established upon the man.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The young boy is not penalised by the hadd punishment when he falls upon a woman, and the man is penalised by the hadd punishment when he falls upon the young girl.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Hanan, from Muawiya ibn Taref, from Sufyan al-Thawri, who said: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about a man who stole a free woman and sold her. He said: 'In her case, there are four penalties (hudud). As for the first, he is a thief, so his hand is cut off. And the second: if he copulated with her, he is whipped the penalty (hadd). And upon the one who bought her: if he copulated with her and knew (she was stolen), if he was married (muhsan), he is stoned; and if he was not married, he is whipped the penalty (hadd). And if he did not know, then there is nothing upon him. And upon her: if he coerced her, then there is nothing upon her; and if she obeyed him, she is whipped the penalty (hadd).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had sold a free person, so he cut his hand.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abdullah ibn Talha, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who sells another man, and they are both free; this one sells this one, and that one sells that one, and they flee from a city to a city, so they sell themselves, and they flee with the wealth of the people. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their hands are cut off because they are both thieves, stealing themselves and the wealth of the people.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no cutting (of the hand) for a feather, meaning the whole bird.'
And by this chain, he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no cutting (of the hand) upon the one who stole stones, meaning marble and similar to that.

And by this chain, he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the one who stole the fruits being in their clusters. So whatever he ate from it, there was nothing upon him; and whatever he carried, so he was rebuked and made to compensate its price, twice (double).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Every place entered without the permission of its owner, if a thief steals from it, there is no cutting (amputation) upon him, meaning the baths, the caravanserais, and the mills.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no cutting (of the limb) for fruit, nor for sap, and the sap is the fat of the palm tree.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The thief is not cut (amputated) during a year of drought/famine with regard to everything that is eaten, such as bread and meat, and similar to that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The thief's hand is not cut off during a year of famine, meaning during a year of scarcity.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) did not cut the thief during the days of famine.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the child who steals. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is excused from it once and twice, and he is rebuked in the third. So if he repeats, the tips of his fingers are cut. So if he repeats, lower than that is cut.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the child who steals. He said: 'When he steals once and he is small, he is excused. If he repeats, he is excused. If he repeats, his fingertip is cut. If he repeats, he is cut lower than that.'

From him, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'When the children were brought to Ali (peace be upon him), he cut their fingertips. From where did he cut?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'From the joint, the joint of the fingertips.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the child steals, he is excused (from cutting the hand). If he repeats, he is rebuked (with a light punishment). If he repeats, the ends of the fingers are cut. If he repeats, he is cut lower than that. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'A boy was brought to Ali (peace be upon him) with doubt regarding whether he had reached the age of sexual maturity (had bed-wetted), so he cut the ends of the fingers.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) was brought an unmarried girl who had stolen, so he lashed her with a whip and did not cut her.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the child who steals, he said: He is excused once. If he repeats, his fingertips are cut, or they are scratched until they bleed. If he repeats, his fingers are cut. If he repeats, he is cut lower than that.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A boy who had stolen was brought to Ali (peace be upon him). He scratched his fingers, then said: Indeed, if you were to repeat (the theft), I would cut them. Then he said: 'But it has not been done except by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and myself.'

Aban, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: When the child steals and has not yet reached puberty (bed-wetting), the ends of his fingers are cut. He said, and Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'It was done by none except the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and myself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from one of his companions, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the child who steals, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is nine years of age, his hand is cut, and a penalty (hadd) from the penalties of Allah (Exalted and Glorious) is not wasted.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A boy who had stolen was brought to Ali (peace be upon him), so he scratched his fingers, then said: But, if you were to repeat, I would cut these. He said, then he said: 'But, it was not done except by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and myself.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Nahiki from Ibn Abi Umayr from a number of our companions from Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abdullah al-Qasri who said: I was in Medina, and a boy who had stolen was brought to me. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about him. He said: 'Ask him, when he stole, did he know that there was a punishment upon him for the theft? If he says yes, it is said to him: 'What is that punishment?' If he does not know that the punishment for the theft is cutting (of the hand), then free him.' He said: 'So I took the boy and asked him, and said to him: 'Did you know that there is a punishment for the theft?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is it?' He said: 'The whipping.' So I freed him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the slave slanders the free man, he is whipped eighty (lashes). And he (peace be upon him) said: This is from the rights of the people.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: I asked him about the slave who fabricates (accuses falsely) upon the free man. He said: 'He is whipped eighty (lashes)'. I said: 'So if he committed adultery?' He said: 'He is whipped fifty (lashes)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a slave who fabricated [a false testimony] upon a free person. He said: 'He is whipped eighty [lashes].'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Ahowl, from Bureyd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding the slave woman who commits adultery, He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is whipped half the penalty (Hadd) of the free person, whether she had a husband or not.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a slave who stole and betrayed from the wealth of his master. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no cutting upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah the Exalted: 'And when they are taken in marriage' (fa-idha uhsinna). He said: 'Their being taken in marriage (ih-san) is that they are copulated with.' I said, 'If they have not been copulated with, is there no Penalty (Hadd) on them?' He said: 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Asbagh ibn Al-Asbagh, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara or from Bureyd al-Ajaly (the doubt is from Muhammad), who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'If a slave woman commits adultery,' he said, 'She is whipped fifty.' I said, 'And if she repeats?' He said, 'She is whipped fifty.' I said, 'Is stoning obligatory upon her in any of the situations?' He said, 'If she commits adultery eight times, stoning is obligatory upon her.' I said, 'How did it become eight times?' He said, 'Because the free man, if he commits adultery four times and the Penalty is established upon him, he is killed. So when the slave woman commits adultery eight times, she is stoned in the ninth.' I said, 'And what is the reason for that?' So he said, 'Allah has been Merciful to her that He would not gather upon her the rope of slavery and the Penalty of the free.' Then he said, 'And it is upon the Imam of the Muslims that he hand over her price to her master from the portion of the slaves.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Anbasah ibn Mus'ab al-'Abid, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'There was a slave girl for me, so she committed adultery. Shall I apply the Hadd penalty on her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but that should happen in secret, due to the state of the authorities.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding a slave who slandered a free, married woman, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped eighty (lashes) because he is whipped for her rights.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the slave commits adultery, he is whipped fifty (lashes). If he repeats, he is whipped fifty. If he repeats, he is whipped fifty, up to eight times. If he commits adultery eight times, he is killed, and the Imam pays his price to his master from the public treasury.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a slave who divorced his wife with two divorces, then copulated with her afterwards. So he ordered a man to whip both of them and separate what is between them; he flogged each one of them with fifty lashes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the contracted slave who commits adultery, he said: He is whipped for the Hadd penalty by the measure of what has been freed from him.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: The contracted slave (mukatab) is whipped when he commits adultery, according to the measure of what has been freed from him. So if he slanders a chaste woman, upon him is that he be whipped eighty, whether he is free or a slave.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a muqatabah (contracted slave) who committed adultery. He said: 'Look at what has been taken from her contract; that portion constitutes the penalty (hadd) of the free woman, and whatever remains unpaid constitutes the penalty (hadd) of the slave woman.' And he said regarding a muqatabah who committed adultery, where three-quarters of her contract had been paid and one quarter remained: 'She is lashed three-quarters of the penalty of the free woman, calculated from one hundred, which is seventy-five lashes. And she is lashed one-quarter of the penalty of the slave woman, calculated from fifty, which is twelve and a half lashes. So that totals eighty-seven and a half lashes. And he refused to stone her and exile her before her emancipation is clarified.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, and from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, altogether from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Similar to it, except that Yunus said, 'The whip is taken from its halfway point, so he is whipped with it, and similarly for the lesser (amount) and the greater (amount).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the contracted slave who fabricated (lied) upon a Muslim man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped the penalty of the free man, eighty (lashes), whether he has paid something from his contract or has not paid.' It was said to him: 'So if he commits adultery and he is contracted, and has not paid anything from his contract?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the Right of Allah. Fifty lashes are staved off from him, and he is whipped fifty.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The male slave, when he confesses upon himself in the presence of the Imam once that he has stolen, his hand is cut; and the female slave, when she confesses upon herself in the presence of the Imam regarding the theft, her hand is cut.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyr, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave who slandered a free person. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped eighty [lashes]. This is from the rights of the people. So as for what is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then he is whipped half the penalty (Hadd).' I said, 'What is that which is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he commits adultery or drinks wine, then these are from the rights for which he is whipped half the penalty (Hadd) with regards to it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'My slave, if he steals from me, I do not cut him, and my slave, if he steals from others, I cut him, and the slave of the Emirate, if he steals, I do not cut him, because he is Fay' (war booty).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked: About a man who had a slave girl, so he contracted her (mukatabah). She said to him, 'Whatever I pay from my contract, I am free by it upon that accounting.' He said to her, 'Yes.' So she paid some of her contract, and her master copulated with her after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he compelled her to that, he is whipped from the Hadd by the measure of whatever she paid from her contract, and the Hadd is staved off from him by the measure of whatever remained from her contract. And if she obeyed him, she is his partner in the Hadd; she is whipped like what he is whipped.'

Ali, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The slave, when he steals from his masters, is not cut (hand); so if he steals from other than his masters, he is cut.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding the slave men and the slave women when one of them committed adultery, that he would be whipped fifty lashes whether he was a Muslim, or an Infidel, or a Christian, and would neither be stoned nor exiled.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to whip the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian for wine and the intoxicant al-Nabeez, eighty (lashes). So it was said, 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When they display that openly in a city from the cities, because it is not for them that they should be displaying (it openly).' Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ja'far ibn Rizqallah or a man from Ja'far ibn Rizqallah who said: A Christian man was brought before Al-Mutawakkal who had committed fornication with a Muslim woman, so he wanted to establish the Hadd penalty upon him, but he became a Muslim. So Yahya ibn Aktham said, 'His faith has demolished his polytheism and his deed.' And some of them said, 'Whip him with three Hadd penalties,' and some of them said, 'Do with him such and such.' So Al-Mutawakkal ordered a letter to be sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him) asking him about that. So when he read the letter, he wrote: 'He is whipped until he dies.' But Yahya ibn Aktham disagreed, and the jurists of al-Askar disagreed with that, and they said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, ask about this, for it is a thing which the Book does not speak of and a Sunnah has not come with it.' So he wrote to him that the jurists of the Muslims had disagreed with this and said, 'A Sunnah has not come with it, and the Book does not speak of it. Therefore, explain to us why you made whipping until death obligatory upon him.' In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. [40:84] When they saw Our Punishment, they said: 'We believe in Allah alone and we deny what we used to associate with Him.' [40:85] But their belief was not going to profit them when they had seen Our Punishment; (this is) Allah's Way, which has been customary regarding His servants, and there the unbelievers are in loss. He (the narrator) said, 'So Al-Mutawakkal ordered by it, and he was whipped until he died.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a Jew who had been immoral with a Muslim woman. He said: 'He should be killed'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalty (hadd) of the Jew, the Christian, and the owned slave regarding wine and fabrication (of evidence) is the same. And indeed, the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma) were reconciled upon the condition that they drink it in their houses.'

Yunus from Sama'at who said: I asked him about the Jew and the Christian who slandered his companion of a same religion, and the Magian who slandered the Muslim. He said: 'He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheyb who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a Christian who slandered a Muslim, so he said to him, 'O adulterer!' He said: 'He would be whipped eighty lashes due to the right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes except for one due to the sanctity of Islam, and his head would be shaved, and he would be paraded among the people of his religion so that others might be deterred.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Washa, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled that the Jew and the Christian are to be lashed eighty lashes for wine and the intoxicating nabidh, if they display drinking it in a city from the cities of the Muslims. And similarly for the Magian; and they are not to be subjected to it if they drink it in their houses and their churches, until they become among the Muslims.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he forbade slandering one who was upon other than Islam, except that you had come to know that from him.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Hazza', who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man asked me, 'What did your creditor do?' I said, 'That one is the son of the sexually active (immoral) woman.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) looked at me with a harsh look. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, he is a Magian. His mother is his sister.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Or is that not (considered a valid) marriage in their religion?'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the reprimand (ta'zir), how much is it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'A part of ten lashes, what is between ten and twenty.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about two men, each one of the two fabricated upon his companion. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Penalty (Hadd) would be staved off from them, and they would both be reprimanded'.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban ibn Uthman from Ismail ibn al-Fadl who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fabrication (iftira') upon the Ahl al-Zimma and the People of the Book. Would the Muslim be whipped the Hadd penalty regarding the fabrication against them? He (peace be upon him) said: No, but he would be reprimanded (mu'azzar).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How much is the reprimand (Ta'zir)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Less than the Penalty (Hadd).' I said, 'Less than eighty?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but it is less than forty, for it is the Penalty (Hadd) of the slave.' I said, 'And how much is that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'According to what the Governor sees fit regarding the sin of the man and the strength of his body.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man says to another man, 'You are filthy' and 'You are a pig', there is no fixed penalty (Hadd) for it, but there is admonition and part of the punishment.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about false testifiers. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are whipped with a penalty (hadd) that has no fixed time, and that is upon the Imam (peace be upon him), and they are paraded until the people recognize them.' And as for the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not accept any testimony from them ever... Except those who repent'. He (peace be upon him) said. I said, 'How is their repentance recognized?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He lies about himself before the chiefs of the people until he is whipped, and he seeks Forgiveness of his Lord. And when he does that, so his repentance has been manifested.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from one of his companions, from Mansur ibn Hazam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who married a Zimmiyyah (non-Muslim woman under treaty) over a Muslim woman, and did not ask her permission. He said: 'And they are separated.' I said: 'So is there discipline upon him?' He said: 'Yes, twelve lashes, and half of eighty being the Hadd of the adulterer, and he is Saqir (belittled/disgraced).' I said: 'So if the free Muslim woman were to be pleased with his deed after what he had done?' He said: 'He is not whipped, nor are they separated between them; they remain upon the first marriage.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer who said: I said, 'What is the ruling for the consumer of usury after the evidence (is clarified to him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be disciplined. So if he repeats, he would be disciplined. So if he repeats, he would be killed'.

And by this chain, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), that he said: The consumer of the dead animal, and the blood, and the flesh of the swine, upon him is the disciplining. So if he repeats, he is disciplined. So if he repeats, he is disciplined, and there is no Penalty (Ḥadd) upon him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who called another 'son of the insane'. So the other one said to him, 'You are a son of the insane'. So he (peace be upon him) ordered the first one to whip his companion with twenty lashes, and said to him, 'Know that he is also deserving the like of it, twenty'. So when he had whipped him, he (peace be upon him) gave the whip to the whipped one, so he whipped him, as a lesson to be learnt by both of them.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandaar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who came to his wife while she was fasting and he was fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: If he compelled her, then upon him are two expiations. And if he did not compel her, then upon him is one expiation and upon her is one expiation. And if he forced her, then upon him is the striking of fifty lashes, half the Hadd. And if she obeyed him, he is struck with twenty-five lashes, and she is struck with twenty-five lashes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who came to his wife while she was menstruating. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should seek forgiveness of Allah and not repeat it.' I said: 'So upon him is the disciplining (adab)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, twenty-five lashes, a quarter of the penalty (hadd) of the adulterer, and he is belittled (saghir), because he came for unlawful intercourse (sifah).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Two men were brought to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), each of whom had accused his companion of adultery in his body. So he (peace be upon him) repelled the Hadd penalty from both of them and reprimanded them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Minqari, from Al-Nu'man ibn Abd al-Salam, from Abu Haneefa, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who said to another, 'O wicked one!' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no fixed penalty (Hadd) upon him, and he is subject to discretionary punishment (Ta'zir).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said: The false testifiers are whipped with a penalty (hadd) that has no fixed time; that is up to the Imam, and they are paraded until they are recognized, so they do not repeat. I said to him, 'So if they repent and improve, will their testimony be accepted afterwards?' He said: 'When they repent, Allah turns to them with mercy, and their testimony is accepted afterwards.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who insulted a man without slander, hinting at it, is there a Penalty (Hadd) upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the reprimanding (Ta'zir).
Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said:

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding the defamation, (to be) the reprimanding.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Abu Habeeb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to the woman while she is menstruating. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is obligatory upon him, at the beginning of the menstruation, one Dinar, and at its ending, half a Dinar.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, is something of the Hadd (fixed penalty) obligatory upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, twenty-five lashes, a quarter of the Hadd of the adulterer, because he engaged in unlawful intercourse.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub and Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Yahya ibn Abbad al-Makki, who said: Sufyan al-Thawri said to me, 'I see that you have a status with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so ask him about a man who committed adultery and is ill; if the hadd penalty were established upon him, he would die. What do you say about it?' So I asked him, and he said, 'Is this from yourself, or did someone tell you to ask me about it?' I said, 'Sufyan al-Thawri asked me to ask you.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'A man was brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who suffered from dropsy (fluid retention in the belly), with the veins of his thighs visible, and he had committed adultery with a sick woman. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered a palm branch with a hundred stalks, and the man was struck with it once, and the woman was struck with it once, then he freed both their ways (exempted them from further punishment).' Then he recited this verse: 'And take in your hand a clump of grass and strike with it and do not break your oath.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about the penalty (Hadd) of the speechless, the deaf, and the blind, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The penalties are upon them, when they have the intellect for what they do.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had incurred the Hadd penalty, and he had numerous sores on his body. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Delay it until he is cured. Do not peel them off him, lest you kill him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: They brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) a short, ugly man whose belly was swollen with illness and the veins of his belly had turned around. He had committed fornication with a woman, so the woman said, 'I did not know of him except that he entered upon me.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Did you commit adultery?' He said, 'Yes,' and he was not married. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) raised his gaze and lowered it, then called for a palm branch, counted a hundred, and then whipped him with its stalks.

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all of them from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The prescribed penalty (hadd) of flogging applies when two people are found in one bed covering. So the two men shall be flogged the hadd punishment when they are apprehended in one bed covering, and the two women shall be flogged the hadd punishment when they are apprehended in one bed covering.
Regarding the man and the woman both found in one quilt, he said: 'They would both be whipped one hundred lashes each, minus one lash.'

I heard him saying: The prescribed penalty (hadd) of lashing in fornication/adultery (zina) is that the two are found in one blanket, and the two men are found in one blanket, and the two women are found in one blanket.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man and a woman are found in one quilt, and proof is established against them both regarding that, and nothing else emerges from them besides that, each one of them shall be flogged one hundred lashes.'
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man and a woman are found in one quilt, they shall both be given a hundred lashes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man and the woman who are found in one quilt — both shall be lashed one hundred, one hundred.

Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr; and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ali (peace be upon him), when he seized two men in one quilt, would flog them both with the hadd (prescribed penalty); and when he seized two women in one quilt, he would flog them both with the hadd.

When the witnesses testify against the adulterer that he sat with her in the position of a man with his wife, the hadd (prescribed punishment) shall be enacted upon him. He (the Imam) said: And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: O Allah, if You were to give me power over al-Mughira, I would certainly stone him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a woman who was found with a man under one garment. So he said: Both of them shall be flogged one hundred lashes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When Ali (peace be upon him) found two men in one quilt, naked, he would lash them with the penalty of the adulterer, one hundred lashes, each one of them, and similarly for the two women if they were found in one quilt, naked, he would lash each one of them one hundred lashes.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Abbad al-Basri entered upon him, accompanied by some of his companions. He said to him, 'Narrate to me: when two men are taken in one quilt.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Ali (peace be upon him), when he took two men in one quilt, would strike them with the Hadd (penalty).' Abbad said, 'You said to me: other than one lash.' So he repeated the mention of the hadith to him until he repeated it to him several times. Then he said, 'Other than one lash.' So the people present wrote down that hadith.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, all together, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A group of sick people from the Banu Dabba arrived at the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'Stay with me, so when you are cured, I will send you in a raiding party.' They said, 'Take us out of the city.' So he sent them to the charity camels, drinking from their urine and eating from their milk. When they were cured and became strong, they killed three of those who were with the camels. The news reached the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he sent Ali (peace be upon him) to them. They were in a valley, confused, unable to exit it, near the land of Yemen. So he captured them and brought them to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Indeed, the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to make corruption in the land is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) chose the cutting, so he cut their hands and feet from opposite sides.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Talha al-Nahdi, from Sawrat ibn Kuleyb, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man leaves his house intending to go to the mosque or for a need, and a man meets him or follows him, beats him, and takes his clothes. He (peace be upon him) said: What do the people around you say about it? I said: They say this is an open violation, but rather the warrior (muharib) is in the towns of the polytheists. He (peace be upon him) said: Which is greater in sanctity, the house of Islam or the house of polytheism? I said: The house of Islam. He (peace be upon him) said: These are the ones subject to this Verse: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger'... up to the end of the Verse.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off,' up to the end of the verse. So I said, 'Which of these penalties, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has named, is upon them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is for the Imam; if he wills, he cuts (the hand), and if he wills, he crucifies, and if he wills, he exiles, and if he wills, he kills.' I said, 'Exile to where?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He is exiled from one city to another city.' And he (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) exiled two men from Kufa to Basra.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger' up to the end of the verse He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not given allegiance, nor sheltered, nor given charity.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Only the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to the Imam; he does with him whatever he desires.' I said, 'So is that delegated to him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but it is like the crime (blood money/diyyah).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The one who carries the weapon at night, he is a combatant (muharib), except if he is a man who is not from the doubtful people.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) crucified a man at Al-Hira for three days, then brought him down on the fourth day, so he prayed over him and buried him.

Ali, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ishaq al-Madaini, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to make mischief in the land is that they be killed,' the Verse. So what is it that, when done, obligates one of these four [penalties]? He said: When he wages war against Allah and His Messenger and strives to make mischief in the land and kills, he is killed. And if he kills and takes wealth, he is killed and crucified. And if he takes wealth and does not kill, his hand and foot are cut from opposite sides. And if he brandishes the sword, wages war against Allah and His Messenger, strives to make mischief in the land, and does not kill and does not take wealth, he is exiled from the land. I said, 'How is he exiled, and what is the limit of his exile?' He said: 'He is exiled from the city in which he did what he did to another city, and it is written to the people of that city that he is exiled, so do not sit with him, nor pledge allegiance to him, nor inter-marry with him, nor eat with him, nor drink with him.' So that is done with him for a year. If he goes out from that city to another, it is written to them similarly, until the year is completed. I said, 'And if he directs himself to the land of polytheism to enter it?' He said: 'If he directs himself to the land of polytheism to enter it, its people are fought against him.'

Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ishaq, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) (He narrated) similar to it, except that he said at the end: 'That would be done with him for a year, for he will repent before that, and he is humble.' I said, 'If he leads [prayer in] the land of polytheism and enters it?' He said: 'He would be killed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land is that they be killed,' the Verse. This is the exile of the combatant; it is other than this exile. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The ruler rules upon him according to what he has done, and he is exiled and carried in the sea, then thrown by it. If the exile is from one city to another, as if his expulsion is from one city to another, it is equivalent to the killing, and the crucifixion, and the cutting, but the Penalty (Hadd) is that which corresponds to the cutting and the crucifixion.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Ubayda ibn Bashir al-Khasha'i, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cutter of the way (bandit), and I said, 'The people are saying that the Imam has a choice in it, to do whatever he desires.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not whatever he desires, but he deals with them according to their crimes. The one who cuts the way, kills, and takes the property, his hand and leg are cut, and he is crucified. And the one who cuts the way, kills, and does not take the property, he is killed. And the one who cuts the way, takes the property, and does not kill, his hand and leg are cut (from opposite sides). And the one who cuts the way and does not take property and does not kill, he is exiled from the land.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The one who brandishes the weapon in a city from the cities, so he injures, he would be retaliated due to it, and he would be exiled from that city. And the one who brandishes the weapon in another city and strikes and injures, and takes the property, and does not kill, so he is a combatant, and his recompense is the Recompense of the combatant, and his matter is up to the Imam, if he so desire to he kills him, and if he so desires to, he crucifies him, and if he so desires to, he cuts his hand and his leg. He said: And if he strikes and kills, and takes the property, so it is upon the Imam that he cuts his right hand due to the theft, then hands him over to the guardians of the murdered one, to pursue him for the property, then they kill him. He (the narrator) said, So Abu Ubeyda said, May I be sacrificed for you! What is your view if he is forgiven by the guardians of the murdered one? So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: If they excuse him from it, so it is up to the Imam that he kills him, because he has waged war, and killed, and stolen. He (the narrator) said, So Abu Ubeyda said, What is your view if the guardians of the murdered one intend that the wergild (blood money) should be taken from it, and then leave him, is that for them (to do)? So he said: No. Upon him is the killing.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud al-Ta'i, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the combatant (al-muharib), so I said to him, 'Our companions say that the Imam has a choice in it: if he desires, he cuts; if he desires, he crucifies; and if he desires, he kills.'
