He said, 'No! These are matters limited in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Majestic. So if he kills and seizes (property), he is killed and crucified; and if he kills and does not seize, he is killed; and if he seizes and does not kill, he is cut; and if he flees and is not able to be caught, then he is seized, he is cut, except if he repents. So if he repents, he is not cut.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'We invited a man to the entirety of what we are upon, from the entirety of Islam, so he accepted it. Then he drank wine, committed adultery, and consumed usury, and nothing from the permissible and the prohibited had been explained to him. Would the penalty be established upon him if he was ignorant of it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if proof is established upon him that he had previously accepted with its prohibition.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who reported it, from Abu Ubeyda who said: Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) said: 'If I were to find a man from the non-Arabs who accepted with the entirety of Al-Islam, not been given anything from the explanation of adultery, or theft, or drinking the wine, I would not establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon him when he is ignorant, except if the proof were to be established that he had previously accepted with that, and recognised it'.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them). Regarding a man who entered into Islam and drank wine while he was ignorant (of the prohibition), he (peace be upon him) said: 'I would not establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon him when he was ignorant, but I would inform him of that and teach him. So if he were to repeat, I would establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged with a judgment that no one before him had judged with, and it was the first judgment he judged with after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). This was when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away and the affair was entrusted to Abu Bakr. A man who had drunk wine was brought to him. Abu Bakr said to him, 'Did you drink wine?' The man said, 'Yes.' He said, 'And why did you drink it when it is prohibited?' He said, 'When I became a Muslim, my house was in the midst of a people who were drinking wine and permitting it, and if I had known that it was forbidden, I would have avoided it.' Abu Bakr turned to Umar and said, 'What do you say, O Abu Hafs, regarding the matter of this man?' He said, 'It is a dilemma, and Abu al-Hasan (Ali) is right for it.' Abu Bakr said, 'O slave, call Ali for us.' Umar said, 'But he gives judgment in his house.' So they went to him, and with him was Salman al-Farsi. He informed him of the story of the man, and the man related his own story to him. Ali (peace be upon him) said to Abu Bakr, 'Send someone with him who will go around with him to the gatherings of the Emigrants and the Helpers. Whoever recited the Verse of Prohibition to him, let him testify against him. If no one recited the Verse of Prohibition to him, then there is nothing upon him.' Abu Bakr did with the man what Ali (peace be upon him) said. No one testified against him, so he freed his way. Salman said to Ali (peace be upon him), 'You have guided them.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'I only wanted to renew the emphasis of this Verse among me and among them: Is he who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not guide unless he is guided? So what is the matter with you; how do you judge?'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who is seized and upon him are penalties, one of which is killing. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to establish the penalties upon him, then he would kill him, and Ali (peace be upon him) will not be opposed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who has penalties due upon him, one of which is killing, he said: The penalties are established upon him, then he is killed.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the one who murdered, drank wine, and stole, so he established the Penalty (Hadd) upon him. So he whipped him due to his drinking the wine, and cut his hand regarding his theft, and killed him due to his committing murder.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man upon whom multiple penalties had gathered, including killing, he said: Begin with the penalties that are less than killing, then he is killed afterwards.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed and Ibn Abi Umeyr, altogether from Jameel ibn Darraj, from a man, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them). Regarding a man who stole, or drank wine, or committed adultery, so he was not known to be with that and he was not seized, until he repented and corrected himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When his correctness is recognized from him, it is a beautiful matter, the Hadd (penalty) would not be established upon him.' Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr said, 'I said, 'So if it was a matter close by, would the Hadd not be established?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was five months or less from it, and he had manifested a beautiful matter, the Huddud (penalties) would not be established upon him.' And that has been reported from some of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man upon whom the proof is established that he committed adultery, then he fled before he was whipped. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he repents, there is nothing upon him, and if he falls in the hands of the Imam, he will establish the Hadd penalty upon him, and if his whereabouts are known, he will send (a summoner) to him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever seizes a thief and pardons him, that is up to him; but if it is raised to the Imam, he cuts him. So if the one from whom it was stolen says, 'I gift it to him,' the Imam will not leave him until he cuts him, when it is raised to him. And indeed, the gifting is before it is raised to the Imam. And the preservers of the Penalties of Allah So when the Penalty ends up with the Imam, it is not for anyone that he should leave it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who seizes the thief, should he raise him (to the Imam) or leave him? So he said: Indeed Safwan ibn Umayya was lying in the Sacred Mosque, so he placed down his robe and went out to pour water. He found that his robe had been stolen when he returned to it, so he said, 'Who has taken my robe?' So he went seeking it and seized the one who was with it. So he raised him to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Cut off his hand.' Safwan said: 'Will you cut off his hand for the sake of my robe, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then I gift it to him.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Why wasn't this done before you raised him to me?' I said: 'So the Imam is in his position when it is raised to him?' He said: 'Yes.' And I asked him about the pardon before it reaches the Imam, so he said: 'It is good.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'ala, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who seizes the thief: is it better to leave him (the thief) or to raise (the matter) (to the Imam)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed Sufyan ibn Umayyah was reclining in the Masjid on his cloak. He arose to urinate, and when he returned, his cloak had been taken. He sought its owner and found him, and brought him to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He (peace be upon him) said: "Cut his hand." Sufyan said: "O Messenger of Allah, I gift that to him." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: "Why was that not done before you brought him to me?"' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about excusing (forgiving) regarding the fixed penalties before they reach the Imam, and he said: It is good.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The penalties that are for Allah cannot be excused except by the Imam. As for what is from the rights of the people regarding a penalty, there is no problem if one is excused from it, except by the Imam.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man committed a crime against me. Should I pardon him or refer him to the ruler?' He said, 'It is your right. If you pardon him, that is good; and if you refer him to the Imam, you are merely seeking your right. And how would it be for you with the Imam?'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who accuses another man of adultery, so he pardons him and makes him free from that. Then it occurs to him that he should bring him forward until he is whipped. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Hadd (penalty) for him after the pardon.' So I said to him: 'What is your view if he said, 'O son of the adulteress', so he pardoned him and left that to Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother was alive, it is not for him to pardon; the pardon is for his mother. Whenever she wishes, she takes her right.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother had died, then he is the guardian of her affairs, and his pardon is valid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no Penalty (Hadd) for the one upon whom there is no Penalty (Hadd).

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no Hadd (fixed penalty) for the one upon whom there is no Hadd, meaning, if an insane person were to slander a man, I do not see any penalty upon him, and if a man were to slander him, so he says to him, "O adulterer", there would be no Hadd upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Salma, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Usama ibn Zayd used to intercede regarding matters in which there was no fixed penalty (Hadd). So a person upon whom a fixed penalty had become obligatory was brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Usama interceded for him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Intercession is not accepted regarding a fixed penalty (Hadd).'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There was a slave girl for Umm Salma, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who stole from a group of people. So she was brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Umm Salma spoke to him regarding her. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Umm Salma! This is a Hadd (fixed penalty) from the Hadd of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which is not to be neglected.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cut her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Let no one intercede regarding a Hadd (fixed penalty) when it reaches the Imam, for he has authority over it. And intercede in what has not reached the Imam when you see remorse. And intercede before the Imam in matters other than the Hadd, with the return of the one for whom you interceded. And do not intercede regarding the right of a Muslim man, nor of others, except with his permission.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Usamah bin Zayd: 'O Usamah, do not intercede regarding a Hadd (penalty).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Hadd (fixed penalty) is not inherited as the Diyah (blood money) and wealth and real estate are inherited. But whoever of the inheritors stands by it and seeks it, he is its guardian (has the right to it), and whoever leaves it and does not seek it, then there is no right for him. And that is like a man who slanders a man, and for the slandered one is a brother. So if one of the two excuses him, the other has the right to seek his right, because she is their mother together, and the excusing is for both of them together.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Hadd (penalty) is not inherited.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The man is flogged the Hadd (prescribed penalty) while standing, and the woman while seated; and every body part is struck, but the head and the genitals are spared.

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the adulterer — how should he be flogged? He said: The most intense of the flogging. I said: From over his clothes? He said: Rather, his clothes are stripped off. I said: And the slanderer (false accuser of adultery)? He said: He is struck between the two strokes — his whole body is struck over his clothes.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the adulterer — how he should be flogged. He said: 'The most intense of the flogging.' I said, 'Over his clothes?' He said: 'Rather, he is stripped bare.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who desires away from Islam and disbelieves in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, so there is no repentance for him, and his killing becomes obligatory, and his wife is divorced from him, and what he leaves is distributed among his children.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from someone else from our companions, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding the apostate: he is asked to repent. So if he repents (fine), or else he is killed. And the woman, when she reneges from Islam, is asked to repent. So if she repents and returns (fine), or else she is kept imprisoned for ever, and her imprisonment is constricted upon her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the child who chooses polytheism while he is between his two parents, he said: 'He is not left (alone), and that is when one of his parents is a Christian.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, and others, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them). Regarding a man who retracted from Islam, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is asked to repent, so if he repents (it is fine), or else he is killed.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought an atheist (Zindiq), so he struck his neck.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from one of his companions from Aban ibn Uthman from one of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the child, when he becomes a youth, so he chooses Christianity, and one of his parents is a Christian, or they are both Muslims. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would not be left, but he would be whipped upon Islam.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A group of people came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'Peace be upon you, O our Lord!' So he asked them to repent, but they did not repent. So he dug a pit for them and kindled a fire in it, and dug another pit beside it, and connected them. So when they did not repent, he cast them into the pit and kindled the fire in the other pit until they died.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali Al-Neysabouri, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a Muslim who became a Christian. He said: 'He is killed and is not asked to repent.' I said, 'So if a Christian became a Muslim, then reneged from Islam?' He said: 'He is asked to repent; if he returns (to Islam), fine, otherwise he is killed.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub from Hisham ibn Salim from Ammar al-Sabati, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Every Muslim, in the presence of two other Muslims, who reneges from Islam and denies the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and belies him, then his blood is permissible for anyone who hears that from him, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him on the day he reneges, so do not approach her, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband has died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him, and he does not ask him to repent.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who is seized in the month of Ramadan and had broken his fast, so it is raised to the Imam, he would be killed on the third (offence).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Baziya alleges that he is a Prophet.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you were to hear him saying that, kill him.' He said, 'So I sat with him (awaiting) many a time, but was not able to do so.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman al-Abzari al-Kunasi, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is your view if a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'By Allah, I do not know whether you are a Prophet or not,' would he accept from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he would kill him. Indeed, if he had accepted that from him, no hypocrite would ever become a Muslim.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought an atheist (Zindiq), so he struck his neck. It was said to him, 'He has a lot of wealth, so for whom should his wealth be made?' He said: 'For his children, and for his inheritors, and for his wife.'

And by this chain that Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) used to judge regarding an atheist (Zindiq) when two just, acceptable witnesses testify against him, and a thousand testify for him with his freedom/exemption; he accepted the testimony of the two men and invalidated the testimony of the thousand because it is an undisclosed religion.

And by this chain, he said, Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: The apostate, his wife is separated from him, and his slaughtered meat is not eaten, and he is asked to repent for three days; if he repents, (he lives), otherwise he is killed on the fourth day.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A group of people came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'Peace be upon you, O our Lord.' He asked them to repent, but they did not repent. So he dug a pit for them and ignited a fire in it, and dug another pit beside it, and connected the space between them. When they did not repent, he cast them into the pit and ignited fire in the other pit until they died.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The slave, when he flees from his masters, then steals, his hand is not cut while he is a fugitive because he is a renegade from Islam, but he is called to return to his masters and enter into Islam. If he refuses to return to his masters, his hand is cut due to the theft, then he is killed; and the apostate, when he steals, is treated at his status.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Bazi'a claims that he is a prophet.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So if you hear him saying that, kill him.' He (the narrator) said, 'I sat [waiting] more than once, but I was not able to do that.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Kirdayn, from a man, from Abu Abdillah and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, when Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) finished with the people of Basra, seventy men from the Zut came to him. They greeted him and spoke to him in their language, so he responded to them in their language. Then he said to them: 'I am not as you say; I am a servant of Allah, a created being.' But they refused him and said, 'You are He.' So he said to them: 'If you do not cease and retract from what you said about me, and repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, I will surely kill you.' So they refused to retract and repent. He ordered wells to be dug for them, and they were dug. Then he made holes connecting some to others, then threw them into them. Then he covered their tops, then fire was kindled in one of the wells that had no one from them in it. So the smoke entered upon them in it, and they died.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The sorcerer of the Muslims is killed, and the sorcerer of the disbelievers is not killed.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and why is the sorcerer of the disbelievers not killed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because disbelief is greater than sorcery, and because sorcery and polytheism are paired.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Habib ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Bashar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The sorcerer is struck with the sword with one strike on top of his head.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The prescribed penalty (hadd) of stoning is applied when four testify that they saw him insert and withdraw.
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Neither a man nor a woman shall be stoned until four witnesses testify against him/her upon the penetration and the withdrawal.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'The stoning (rajm) is not obligated until the four testimonies (bayyinah) are established — that they have seen him copulating with her.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The man and the woman shall not be stoned until four witnesses testify against both of them to the sexual intercourse, the penetration, and the entering — like the applicator in the kohl container.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Basri, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The prescribed penalty (hadd) of stoning in adultery (zina) is that four witnesses testify that they saw him insert and withdraw.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman is buried up to her waist when they intend to stone her, and the Imam pelts first, then the people afterwards, with small stones.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The woman is buried up to her waist, then the Imam pelts, then the people pelt with small stones.'

When the married fornicator confesses, the first one to stone him would be the Imam, then the people. So when the proof (four witnesses) is established against him, the first ones to stone him would be the witnesses, then the Imam, then the people.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The woman is buried up to her waist, then the Imam throws and the people throw with small stones; and the man is not buried when stoned, except up to his loins.

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Inform me about the married person when he flees from the pit — will he be returned until the prescribed penalty (hadd) is carried out upon him?' He said: 'He will be returned and not returned.' I said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'If he was the one who confessed against himself, then fled from the pit after some stones had hit him, he will not be returned. But if only the proof (bayyina) was established against him while he was denying it, then he fled, he shall be returned humiliated until the prescribed penalty is carried out against him. And that is because Ma'iz ibn Malik confessed before the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) to having committed adultery (zina), so he ordered that he be stoned. He fled from the pit. Al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam struck him with a camel's leg, tripping him so that he fell. The people caught up with him and killed him. Then they informed the Messenger of God of that, and he said to them: 'Why did you not leave him alone when he fled, to go away? For he was only the one who had confessed against himself.' And he said to them: 'Had Ali been present with you, you would not have gone astray.' He (the Imam) said: And the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) paid his blood money (diya) from the public treasury of the Muslims.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I have committed adultery, so purify me.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) turned his face away from him. He came to him from his other side and said the same thing, and he turned his face away from him again. Then he came a third time and said to him: 'O Messenger of God! I have committed adultery, and the punishment of this world is easier for me than the punishment of the Hereafter.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) asked: 'Is there something wrong with your companion?' — meaning insanity. They said: 'No.' So he confessed against himself for the fourth time. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that he be stoned, and they dug a pit for him. When he felt the touch of the stones, he fled running fast. Al-Zubayr encountered him and threw a camel's leg-bone at him, so he fell and was restrained by it. Then the people caught up with him and killed him. They informed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) of that, so he said: 'Why did you not leave him alone?' Then he said: 'Had he concealed himself and then repented, that would have been better for him.'

A pregnant woman came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! I have committed adultery — purify me, may God purify you, for the punishment of this world is easier than the unending punishment of the Hereafter.' He said to her: 'From what shall I purify you?' She said: 'I have committed adultery.' He said to her: 'Are you a married woman or otherwise?' She said: 'Rather, I am married.' He said: 'Was your husband present when you did what you did, or was he absent from you?' She said: 'Rather, he was present.' He said to her: 'Go and give birth to what is in your womb, then come to me and I will purify you.' When the woman had turned away from him and reached a place where she could not hear his words, he said: 'O God, this is one testimony.' Shortly thereafter she came to him and said: 'I have given birth — purify me.' He feigned ignorance and said: 'Purify you, O servant of God? From what?' She said: 'I committed adultery — purify me.' He said: 'And you were a married woman when you did what you did?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And was your husband present or absent?' She said: 'Rather, he was present.' He said: 'Go and breastfeed him for two complete years as God commanded you.' The woman departed, and when she reached where she could not hear his words, he said: 'O God, this is two testimonies.' When two years had passed, the woman came and said: 'I have breastfed him for two years — purify me, O Commander of the Faithful.' He feigned ignorance and said: 'Purify you from what?' She said: 'I committed adultery — purify me.' He said: 'And you were a married woman when you did what you did?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And was your husband absent from you when you did what you did, or was he present?' She said: 'Rather, he was present.' He said: 'Go and provide for him until he is old enough to eat, drink, not fall from a rooftop, and not tumble into a well.' She departed weeping. When she turned away and reached where she could not hear his words, he said: 'O God, this is three testimonies.' Amr ibn Hurayth al-Makhzumi met her and said: 'Why are you weeping, O servant of God? I have seen you coming repeatedly to Ali asking him to purify you.' She said: 'I came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked him to purify me, and he said: Provide for your child until he can eat, drink, not fa

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man was brought to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who had confessed against himself of immorality. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to his companions: 'Come to me tomorrow morning with your faces veiled.' So they came to him in the morning with their faces veiled. Then he said to them: 'Whoever has done the like of his deed, let him not stone him — let him leave.' He said: So some of them left, and some remained, and those who remained from among them stoned him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, raising it (as a marfu' narration) to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), said: A man came to him at al-Kufa and said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have committed adultery, so purify me.' He said: 'From where are you?' He said: 'From Muzayna.' He said: 'Do you recite anything from the Quran?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then recite.' He recited and recited well. He said: 'Are you afflicted with madness?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then go away until we inquire about you.' So the man went away. Then he returned to him afterwards and said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have committed adultery, so purify me.' So he said: 'Do you have a wife?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Is she residing with you in the city?' He said: 'Yes.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ordered him and said: 'Go away until we inquire about you.' So he sent someone to his people and asked about his situation. They said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! He is of sound mind.' So he returned to him the third time and said to him the same as before. He said to him: 'Go away until we inquire about you.' So he returned to him the fourth time. When he confessed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to Qanbar: 'Keep him detained.' Then he became displeased, then said: 'How ugly it is for a man among you to commit one of these acts of immorality and then disgrace himself before the leaders of the community! Could he not have repented in his own home? By Allah, his repentance between himself and Allah is superior to my establishing the hadd penalty upon him.' Then he brought him out and called among the people: 'O community of Muslims! Come out so that the hadd penalty may be established upon this man, and let none of you recognize his companion.' So he brought him to the open ground. He said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! Give me respite to pray two rak'ahs (cycles of prayer).' Then he placed him in his pit and faced the people. He said: 'O community of Muslims! This is a right from the rights of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic! So whoever has upon his neck a right owed to Allah, let him depart; and he should not establish the penalties of Allah, the one upon whose neck is a hadd owed to Allah.' So the people dispersed and there remained only he and al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He took a stone and proclaimed Allah's greatness three times, then pelted him

Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Humran who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the meaning of the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'For this reason We prescribed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul — except in retaliation for a soul or for corruption in the land — it is as if he has killed all people altogether' He said: I said, 'And how is it as if he has killed all people altogether, when he has only killed one?' So he said: 'He will be placed in a place in Hell where the most severe punishment of its inhabitants reaches its peak — as if he had killed all people altogether, he would still only enter that same place.' I said, 'And if he kills another?' He said: 'It is doubled upon him.'

Ali, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The first of what God will judge concerning on the Day of Resurrection is bloodshed. He will stop the two sons of Adam and decide between them. Then those who followed them among the perpetrators of bloodshed, until none of them remains. Then the rest of the people after that, until the murdered one comes with his murderer, his face dripping in his blood, and he says: "This one killed me." So He will say: "Did you kill him?" And he will not be able to conceal any matter from God.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no soul that is killed — righteous or immoral — except that it will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection clinging to its killer, its (own severed) head in his right hand and its jugular veins streaming with blood, saying: 'O Lord! Ask this one why he killed me.' So if it was killed in obedience to God, the killer will be rewarded with Paradise and the killed one will be taken to the Fire; but if he says it was in obedience to so-and-so (other than God), it will be said to him: 'Kill him just as he killed you.' Then God, Mighty and Majestic, will deal with both of them afterwards as He wills.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not be deceived by the one who is skilled with the two forearms in bloodshed, for indeed he has with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a killer that does not die.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is a killer that does not die?' So he said: 'The Fire.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not let the one whose arms are wide with blood impress you, for indeed Allah has for him a killer who does not die.'

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter... it is as though he slew all the people' [5:32]. He said: 'For him is a seat in the Fire. Even if he had killed all the people altogether, he would not be returned except to that very seat.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The believer does not cease to be in ample space in his religion for as long as he does not shed blood unlawfully. And he said: The deliberate killer of a believer would not be granted the opportunity for repentance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza, from one of the two (peace be upon them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was approached and it was said to him: 'O Messenger of God, there has been a killing in Juhayna.' So the Messenger of God arose and walked until he reached their mosque. He said: The people heard (the news) and came to him. He said: 'Who killed this person?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, we do not know.' So he said: 'A person killed among the Muslims and it is not known who killed him! By the One Who sent me with the Truth, if the inhabitants of the sky and the earth were to participate in the shedding of the blood of a Muslim person and were pleased with it, God would surely cast them headlong upon their nostrils into the Fire' — or he said: 'upon their faces.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umayr, from Sa'id al-Azraq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who killed a believing man. He said: 'It will be said to him: Die whichever death you like — if you like, as a Jew; if you like, as a Christian; if you like, as a Magian.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a man will come on the Day of Resurrection with him the measure of a cup of blood, so he will say, 'By Allah, I did not kill, nor did I participate in his blood.' He (peace be upon him) will say, 'Yes, you mentioned My servant so-and-so, and that escalated until he was killed, and his blood fell upon you.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He would not enter Paradise: the shedder of blood, nor the drinker of wine, nor the backbiter who goes about spreading slander.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shammam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood at Mina when he had completed its rituals during the Farewell Hajj, so he said: 'O people! Listen to what I say to you and understand it from me, for I do not know, perhaps I will not meet you again at this standing place after our year.' Then he said: 'Which day is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This day.' He said: 'So which month is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This month.' He said: 'So which city is greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This city.' He said: 'Indeed, your blood and your wealth are sacred upon you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours, until the day you meet Him, and He will question you about your deeds.' 'Indeed, have I delivered (the message)?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'O Allah, bear witness! Indeed, whoever has an entrustment, let him return it to the one who entrusted it to him. For the blood of a Muslim and his wealth are not permissible except with his consent, and do not do injustice to yourselves, and do not return to disbelief after me.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding two men: one of whom restrained [the victim], and the other killed [him]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The killer shall be killed, and the other one shall be imprisoned until he dies of anguish, just as he held him until he died of anguish.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who seized another man in order to kill him, and the man was fleeing from him, so another man came across him and restrained him for him until the first man came and killed him. So he (peace be upon him) said: The man who killed him would be killed (qisas), and the judgment upon the other one who restrained him is that he be thrown into prison forever until he dies in it, because he restrained him to the death.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said: I was present at the Sacred House (Kaaba), and a man was calling out to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur while he was circumambulating, saying: 'O Commander of the Faithful! These two men came to my brother at night and took him out of his house, and he has not returned to me. By Allah, I do not know what they did with him.' So he said to them, 'What did you do with him?' They said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, we spoke to him and he returned to his house.' So he said to them, 'Meet me tomorrow after the Asr prayer in this place.' So they met him the next day after the Asr prayer, and I was present. He said to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), while holding his hand, 'O Ja'far, judge between them.' He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, you judge between them.' He said to him, 'By my right upon you, you must judge between them.' So Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out, and a reed prayer mat was spread for him, and he sat on it. Then the disputants came and sat before him. He said, 'What are you saying?' He said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, these two came to my brother at night and took him out of his house. By Allah, he has not returned to me, and by Allah, I do not know what they did with him.' He said, 'What do you two say?' They said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, we spoke to him, then he returned to his house.' So Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'O scribe, write: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to a man at night and takes him out of his house, he is responsible for him, unless he establishes proof that he returned him to his house.' O scribe, remove this one and strike his neck.' He said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I did not kill him, but I restrained him. Then this one came and ambushed him and killed him.' He said, 'I am the Son of the Messenger of Allah. O scribe, remove this one and strike the neck of the other.' He said, 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I did not torment him, but I killed him with one strike.' So he ordered his brother to strike the first man's neck. Then he ordered the other one, so they struck his sides, imprisoned him, and wrote on his head:

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That three men were brought to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). One of them had restrained a man, and another faced him and killed him, and the third watched them. He judged regarding the onlooker that his eyes be gouged out, and regarding the one who restrained that he be imprisoned until he dies just as he had restrained him, and judged regarding the one who killed that he be killed.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who fell upon a man and killed him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib and Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who pushed another man onto a third man, so he killed him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wergild (blood money) is upon the one who fell upon the man and killed him, for the guardians of the killed one.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the pushed one can demand the wergild from the one who pushed him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if the pushed one was hit by anything (injured), then it is upon the pusher as well.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fell upon a man from the top of the house, so one of the two died. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is not upon the higher one anything, and there is not upon the lower one anything'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was found killed, so two men came to his guardian. One of them said, 'I killed him deliberately,' and the other said, 'I killed him in error.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he accepts the word of the one who killed deliberately, then there is no way for him against the one who killed in error; and if he accepts the word of the one who killed in error, then there is no way for him against the one who killed deliberately.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, who said: 'One of our companions informed me, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)' He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a man who was found in some ruins, and in his hand was a knife stained with blood, and behold, a slaughtered man was rolling in his blood. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: "What do you say?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful! I killed him." He (peace be upon him) said: "Go with him and kill him." So when they went with him to kill him, a man came hurrying and said: "Do not be hasty, and return him to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)!" So they returned him.' So he said: 'By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful! This one is not its perpetrator, it was I who killed him.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to the first one: 'What carried you to confess against yourself when you did not do it?' He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, and I did not have the ability to say (anything in my defense), and there had testified against me the likes of these men, and they seized me, and in my hand was a knife stained with blood, and the man was rolling in his blood, and I was standing over him, and I feared the beating, so I confessed.' 'And I am a man who had slaughtered a sheep by the side of these ruins, and the need for urination seized me, so I entered the ruins and saw the man rolling in his blood. So I stood there wondering, and these men came to me and seized me.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Take these two and go with them both to Al-Hasan, and relate both their stories to him and say to him: "What is the ruling with regards to these two?"' So they went to Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and related both their stories to him. So Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Say to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): "If this one has killed him, then he has revived this one, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And whoever keeps it alive, it is as though he kept alive all men." Free them both and take the wergild of the slaughtered one from the public treasury."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who killed, so they carried him to the governor, and a group came so the witnesses testified against him that he killed him deliberately. So the governor handed over the killer to the guardians of the killed one in order for them to retaliate against him. So, they had not begun with him when a man came over and confessed in the presence of the governor that he had killed their companion deliberately, and that this man against whom the witnesses had testified is free from the killing of so and so companion of yours, therefore he should not be killed for it, and seize me (instead) for his blood. He said, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If the guardians of the killed one intend to kill the one who confessed against himself, so let them kill him, and there would be no way for them against the other one. Then there is no way for the inheritors of the one who confessed against himself against the inheritors of the one testified against. And if they intend to kill the one who has been testified against, so let them kill him, and there would be no way for them against the one who confessed. Then the one who confessed against himself should pay the wergild to the guardians of the one testified against, of half the wergild'. I said, 'What is your view if they intend to kill both of them together?' He said: 'That is for them, and upon them would be that they should hand over half the wergild to the guardians of the one testified against in particular, besides his companion. Then they can kill both of them'. I said, 'What is your view if they intend to take the wergild?' So he said: 'The wergild is in two halves in between them both, because one of the two confessed, and the other one has been testified against'. I said, 'How come you made half the wergild to be for the guardians of the one who was testified against, over the one who confessed against himself that he had killed, and did not make it for the guardians of the one who confessed against himself over the one who was testified against, and he did not kill?'. So he said: 'Because the one who was testified against is not similar to the one who confessed. The one who was testified against d

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Any man who is killed by the legal penalty (Hadd) in retaliation (Qisas), there is no wergild (Diyah) for him. And he said: Any man who attacks another man to strike him, and he defends himself against him, injuring him or killing him, there is nothing upon him (no compensation). And he said: Any man who peers at a people in their house to look at their private parts, and they pelt him, blinding his eyes or injuring him, there is no wergild for them. And he said: Whoever initiates (an attack) and exceeds (in it), and is attacked against, there is no retaliation (Qawd) for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who intended to have unlawful intercourse with a woman, so she threw a rock at him and it struck him and killed him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon her regarding what is between her and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and if she is brought to a just Imam, he would stave off his blood (wergild).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was killed by al-qisas (retaliation/executory death), is there a diya (blood money) for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it were so, no one would be retaliated against from [the killer], and whoever is killed by the hadd (legal penalty), there is no diya for him.'

From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn al-Fudayl, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man intends to strike another man unjustly, so the man defends himself or repels him from his own self, and causes him harm, then there is no compensation upon him.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man looks down upon a people, overlooking them, or looks at them from a crack in something of theirs, and they throw something at him and hit him, so they kill him or blind his eye, then there is no penalty (blood money) upon them. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a man peeked from a crack in the chamber of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came with an arrow to blind his eye, but he found him to have gone away. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O the filthy one! By Allah, if he had remained for me, I would have blinded his two eyes.

Yunus narrated from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who struck a man unjustly, so the man repulsed him from himself, so he was hit by something. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There were young boys in the time of Ali (peace be upon him) who were playing with their toys, so one of them threw his toy at the other and broke his four front teeth. This matter was raised to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), so the thrower established the evidence that he had said, 'Beware, beware!' So he (peace be upon him) staved off the retaliation (qisas) from him, then said: 'He has excused himself, the one who cautioned.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man killed by retaliation (qisas), is there wergild (diyah) for him?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it were so, no one would be retaliated from; and the one who is killed by the legal penalty (hadd), there is no wergild for him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man peeked at the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) from the reeds. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'If I knew that you would stand still for me, I would come to you with the arrow until I blind your eye with it.' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'Is that for us as well?' He said: 'Woe to you or suffering to you! I am telling you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did it, and you say, 'Is that for us?''

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who initiates (a killing), so he attacks and gets counter-attacked, so there is no retaliation (qasas) for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih Al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The one upon whom we inflict a legal penalty (Hadd) from the penalties of Allah and he dies, so there is no wergild (Diya) for him upon us; and the one upon whom we inflict a legal penalty regarding something from the rights of the people and he dies, so his wergild is upon us.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in his chambers with one of his wives, and with him was a spindle which he was turning, when he saw two eyes peeking at him. So he said: 'If I knew that you would remain fixed for me, I would arise until I blind you.' So I said: 'Shall we do the like of this, if the like of this is done to us?' He said: 'If it is hidden from you (i.e., you are not seen), then do it.'

Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a thief who entered upon a woman to steal her belongings. When he had gathered the clothes, his soul followed him, so he overpowered her and had intercourse with her. Her son stirred, so he (the thief) stood up and killed him with an axe that was with him. When he was finished, he carried the clothes and went to exit. She attacked him with the axe and killed him. His family came the next day seeking his blood. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Judge regarding this as I have described to you.' He said: 'The guardians of the deceased, who are seeking his blood, are responsible for the wergild of the boy. The thief is responsible, from what he left, for four thousand dirhams, because he overpowered her and had intercourse with her, so he is an adulterer, and he is a debtor in his wealth. There is nothing upon her regarding her killing him.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever overpowers a woman to have illicit relations with her, and she kills him, then there is no wergild for him, nor retaliation.'

And from him, he said, I said, 'A man married a woman. So when it was the night of the consummation, the woman brought a male friend of hers so she entered him into (one of) the rooms. So when the man entered in order to copulate with his wife, the friend leapt and they both fought in the house. So the husband killed the friend, and the woman stood up, so she struck the husband with a strike, so she killed him for the (killing of) the friend'. So he said: 'The woman is responsible for the wergild of the friend, and she would be killed for (having killed her) husband'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a man who came to a man while he was asleep. So when he came to be upon his back, he woke up due to it, so he poked him with a knife, so he killed him. So he said: 'There is neither a wergild for him, nor a retaliation'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali bin Raib, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who killed an insane man. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the insane man intended (to kill) him, so he defended himself, so he killed him, then there is nothing upon him from a retaliation (qawd), nor a wergild (diyah), and his inheritors would be given his wergild from the public treasury of the Muslims.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if he killed him from other than the insane happened to have intended (to kill) him, so there is no retaliation for the one from whom there is no retaliation. So I see the wergild to be upon his killer from his own wealth, to be handed over to the inheritors of the insane, and he should seek Forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Al-Wardi, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May Allah keep you well. An insane man attacked a man, so the insane one struck him with a strike. The man grabbed the sword from the insane man, struck him, and killed him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that he would not be killed (for it), nor would he be fined his blood money (diyah), and his blood money would be upon the Imam, and his blood would not be invalidated.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Isa al-Zaif, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man kills a man deliberately, what is his repentance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He makes himself available (to the guardians of the killed one)'. I said, 'He fears that they would kill him'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him give them the wergild (blood money)'. I said, 'He fears that they would come to know him due to that'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him consider the wergild, so let him make it as small packages, then await the timings of the Prayers, so let him cast these in their houses'.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu al-Khazraj, who said: Fuzayl ibn Uthman al-Awr narrated to me from al-Zuhri. He said: I was an official for the Banu Umayya, so I killed a man. I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) after that, 'What should I do with it?' He said: 'Present the blood money (diyah) to his people.' I presented it, but they refused, and I strove (to persuade them), but they refused. So I informed Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) of that, and he said: 'Go with a group of your people and have them bear witness upon them.' I did so, but they refused (to witness). So they bore witness upon them. I returned to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: 'Take the blood money and bundle it separately, then go to the door during the time of Dhuhr or Fajr, and throw it into the house. Whoever takes anything, it will be counted for you as part of the blood money. For the time of Dhuhr and Fajr is an hour when the people of the house come out.' Al-Zuhri said: 'I did that, and had it not been for Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), I would have been destroyed.' He said: 'And one of our companions narrated to me that al-Zuhri had struck a man with wounds, and he died from his strike.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Ibn Bukayr, and others, said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was performing the circumambulation (Tawaf), so he looked towards a group at the side of the Masjid and said, 'What is this group?' They said, 'This is Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri. His intellect is muddled, so he does not speak. His family brought him out, hoping that when he sees the people, he will speak.' So when Ali ibn al-Husayn finished his Tawaf, he went out until he approached him. When Muhammad ibn Shihab saw him, he recognized him. Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'I was appointed to a governorship, so I shed blood. I killed a man, so what you see has entered me.' Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I am more fearful for you regarding your despair from the Mercy of Allah than I am fearful for you regarding what you have done.' Then he said to him, 'Give them the blood money (Diyah).' He said, 'I have done it, but they refused.' So he said, 'Make it into small packages, then watch the times of the Prayers, and throw them into their houses.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: When you have power over the burglar, surprise him, and I am a participant in his blood.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who fights for his wealth, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is killed protecting his wealth, he is in the rank of a martyr.' We said to him (peace be upon him): 'So is fighting better?' He said: 'If you do not fight, there is no problem. As for me, if it were me, I would leave him and not fight.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, who said: I heard him saying, and there had flowed among us a mention of the vagabonds, so Abdullah ibn Aamir said, 'This one narrated to me' – and he gestured towards Ahmad ibn Is'haq that he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), asking him about them, so he wrote back to him: 'Kill them'.
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah and others, that he wrote to him asking him about the Kurds, so he wrote back to him: Do not awaken them except by the edge of the sword.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Fazara, from Anas or Haysam ibn al-Bara', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'The burglar enters upon me in my house intending [to take] my life and my wealth.' He said, 'Kill him, and I will call Allah and whoever hears me as witness that his blood is upon my neck.' He said, 'I said, 'May Allah make you well! So where is the sign of this matter?' He said, 'Do you see [the dawn] from concealment?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So our matter, when it comes, will be clearer than the break of dawn.' He said, 'Then he said, 'Engaging with a mountain by fingernail is easier than engaging with a kingdom whose consumption has not yet expired. Therefore, fear Allah, Blessed and High, and do not kill yourselves for the unjust ones.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz, from Humran, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said: The father is not retaliated for (killing) his son, and the son is killed if he kills his father deliberately.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubaydah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who killed his mother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be killed due to it, belittled, and I do not think killing him would be an expiation for him, and he would not inherit her'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The father is not killed for his son if he killed him, and the son is killed for his father if he killed his father.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who kills his son, would he be killed for it? He said: No.

Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn al-Fudayl, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The father is not killed for his son, and the son is killed for his father; and a man does not inherit from another man when he kills him, even if it were in error.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a woman kills a man, she is executed for it; and when a man kills a woman, if retaliation is intended, they pay the remainder of the man's wergild and retaliate him with it; and if they do not do so if they do not do it, they accept from the killer the wergild of the woman in full, and the wergild of the woman is half the wergild of the man.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who kills a woman deliberately, and the family of the woman intend to kill him: He (peace be upon him) said: That is for them, if they pay to his family half the blood-money (diyah). And if they accept the blood-money, then for them is half the blood-money of the man. And if the woman kills the man, she is killed due to it, and there is nothing for them except her soul. And he (peace be upon him) said: The injuries of men and women are equal: the tooth of the woman is like the tooth of the man, and the bone of the woman is like the bone of the man, and the finger of the woman is like the finger of the man, until the injury reaches one-third of the blood-money. So when it reaches one-third of the blood-money, the blood-money of the man is doubled over the blood-money of the woman.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the injuries, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The injury of the woman is like the injury of the man until it reaches a third of the wergild (blood money). So when it reaches a third of the wergild, the injury of the man is doubled upon the injury of the woman; and the age of the man and the age of the woman are equal.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man kills a woman deliberately, and the family of the woman intend to kill the man, they should return half the wergild to the family of the man, and they kill him.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who killed a man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She would be killed due to it, and her family would not be fined anything.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a.s. ) saying regarding a man who killed a woman deliberately, so he ( a.s. ) said: 'If her family so desire, they can kill him, and pay half the wergild to his family; and if they so desire, they can take half the wergild of five thousand Dirhams'. And he ( a.s. ) said regarding a woman who killed her husband deliberately, so he ( a.s. ) said: 'If his family so desire, they can kill her for his killing, and no one reaps more than the crime upon himself'.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Al-Halabi and Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about a man who killed a woman by error, while she was pregnant with a child. He said: Upon him is the blood money of five thousand dirhams, and upon him for that which was in her belly is a ghurrah (one-tenth), a male or female slave, or forty dinars.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a man who cuts off a finger from the fingers of a woman? How much is its compensation?' He said: 'Ten camels.' I said: 'If he cuts off two?' He said: 'Twenty.' I said: 'If he cuts off three?' He said: 'Thirty.' I said: 'If he cuts off four?' He said: 'Twenty.' I said: 'Glory be to Allah! He cuts off three, so thirty is upon him, and he cuts off four, so twenty is upon him. This used to reach us while we were in Iraq, so we distanced ourselves from the one who said it, and we said that the one who brought it was a devil.' So he said: 'Wait, O Aban! This is how the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged: The woman is equal to the man up to a third of the blood money. When it reaches the third, she returns to half. O Aban! You seized me with analogy (qiyas), but the Sunnah, when it is analogized, destroys the Religion.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman, regarding retaliation between her and a man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, in injuries, until it reaches one-third, it is equal. So when it reaches one-third, the man is higher [in compensation] and the woman is lower.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the injuries of men and women regarding the blood money (diyah) and retaliation (qisas). He said: 'Men and women are equal in retaliation; the tooth for the tooth, the fracture for the fracture, and the finger for the finger are equal, until the injuries reach one-third of the blood money. When they exceed one-third, the blood money of the man regarding the injuries becomes two-thirds of the blood money, and the blood money of the woman becomes one-third of the blood money.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, from Abu Maryam Al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A man was brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who had struck a pregnant woman with a tent pole and killed her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave her guardians the choice: either to take the blood money (diyah) of five thousand dirhams, and a 'ghurrah' (a male or female slave) for the fetus in her belly, or to pay five thousand dirhams to the killer's guardians and kill him.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I said to him, 'A man killed a woman.' He said, 'If the family of the woman intend to kill him, they must pay half his wergild (blood money) and kill him; otherwise, they accept the wergild.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The injuries of the woman and the man are equal until they reach one-third of the wergild (blood money). So when it exceeds that, the injury of the man is doubled over the injury of the woman by two times.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who blinded an eye of a woman, he said: If they so desire, they can blind his eye and pay him a quarter of the wergild; and if she so desires, she can take the quarter of the wergild. And he said regarding a woman who blinded an eye of a man: If he so desires, he can blind her eye, or else he takes the wergild for his eye.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: If a man kills a woman and the family of the woman intend to kill him (in retaliation), they should pay half the blood money (diyah) to the family of the man.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdul Kareem, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who cut a finger of a woman. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His finger is cut until it reaches a third of the wergild (blood money). So when it exceeds the third, there is double (liability) for the man.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muthanna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A parchment was found in the sheath of the sword of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'Verily, the most transgressive of people toward God, Mighty and Majestic, is the killer who kills other than the one who was trying to kill him, and the one who strikes someone other than the one who struck him. And whoever claims lineage other than his (biological) father, then he is a disbeliever in what God revealed to Muhammad. And whoever initiates a criminal act, or shelters one who initiated a criminal act — God, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection, any ransom nor any substitute.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most defiant of people toward God Almighty and Majestic is the one who killed someone other than his (attempted) killer, and the one who struck someone who did not strike him.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all of them from Al-Washa', who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May God curse whoever kills someone other than his (intended) killer, or strikes someone other than the one who struck him.' And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May God curse whoever initiates an unlawful incident, or shelters the initiator of one.' I said: 'And what is the initiator?' He said: 'The one who kills.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim al-Sayqal who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: A parchment was found in the handle of the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and in it was: In the name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. The most insolent of people toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection is the one who kills someone other than his (intended) killer, and the one who strikes someone other than the one who struck him, and whoever befriends other than his (rightful) guardians — he is a disbeliever in what Allah revealed to Muhammad. And whoever initiates an offense or shelters an initiator, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any exchange nor any ransom.
