He said: Then he (the Imam) said to me: 'Do you know what is meant by the one who befriends other than his guardians?' I said: 'What does it mean?' He said: 'It means the people of the Religion.' And 'the exchange' is repentance according to the words of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and 'the ransom' is the sacrifice according to the words of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) paused at Mina when he completed his rituals during the Farewell Hajj. He said: 'O people! Listen to what I say to you, and understand it from me, for I do not know — perhaps I will not meet you in this standing place after this year of ours.' Then he said: 'Which day is the greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This day.' He said: 'So which month is the greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This month.' He said: 'And which land is the greatest in sanctity?' They said, 'This land.' He said: 'Indeed, your blood and your wealth are forbidden to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours, until the day you meet Him and He questions you about your deeds.' Behold, have I delivered (the message)?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'O God, bear witness! Verily, whoever has a trust with him, let him return it to the one who entrusted it to him. For the blood of a Muslim person is not permissible, nor his wealth, except with his own consent. Do not be unjust to yourselves, and do not return to being disbelievers after me.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) cursed whoever initiates an event (a killing) in Medina, or shelters the one who initiates it.' I said: 'What is the event?' He said: 'The killing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Kulayb al-Asadi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: A parchment was found in the handle of the sword of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), in which was written: The curse of God and the angels is upon whoever initiates an offense or shelters an offender; and whoever claims (descent from) other than his (biological) father is a disbeliever in what God — Mighty and Majestic — revealed; and whoever calls (for help) to other than his patrons (people of the Religion), upon him is the curse of God.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about a boy who had not yet reached maturity and a woman, who both killed a man in error. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The error of the woman and the boy is (considered) deliberate. So if the guardians of the killed one like to kill both of them, they can kill them both and pay five thousand Dirhams to the guardians of the boy; and if they like to kill the boy, they kill him and the woman returns a quarter of the wergild to the guardians of the boy; and if the guardians of the killed one kill the woman, and the boy returns a quarter of the wergild to the guardians of the woman; and if the guardians of the killed one like to take the wergild, upon the boy is half the wergild, and upon the woman is half the wergild.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Zureys Al-Kunasi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman and a slave who killed a man by error. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The error of the woman and the slave is like the deliberate. So if the guardians of the slain wish to kill both of them, they kill both of them. If the value of the slave is more than five thousand dirhams, let them return to the master of the slave what remains after the five thousand dirhams. And if they wish to kill the woman and take the slave, they take him, unless his value is more than five thousand dirhams, in which case let them return to the master of the slave what remains after the five thousand dirhams, and take the slave, or his master ransoms him. And if the value of the slave is less than five thousand dirhams, they have nothing except the slave.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Ubeyda, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a blind man who deliberately blinded the eye of a healthy person. He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Ubeyda! The deliberation of the blind man is like the error. In this case, the wergild (diyah) is from his own wealth. So if he does not have wealth, then his wergild is upon the Imam, and the right of a Muslim is not invalidated.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who killed his slave. He said: 'He emancipes a neck, and fasts for two consecutive months, and repents to Allah.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, similar to it.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He (peace be upon him) said regarding the man who kills his slave deliberately: I would like it if he would emancip a neck, and fast for two consecutive months, and feed sixty poor persons, then repentance would be after that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who kills his slave, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He must emancipate a neck, and fast for two consecutive months, and repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever kills his slave deliberately, then upon him is that he should emancipate a neck, and that he should feed sixty poor persons, and fast for two months consecutively.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all together, from al-Fath ibn Yazeed al-Jurjani, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who killed his slave girl or his slave man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the slave was owned by him, he would be disciplined and imprisoned, except if he is known for killing slaves, in which case he is killed for it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was raised to him a man who punished his slave until he died. So he whipped him one hundred as a punishment, and imprisoned him for a year, and fined him the price of the slave, so it was given out in charity from him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), said: He was asked about a man who killed his slave. He said: If he was not well-known for killing, he would be struck with severe strikes, and the price of the slave would be taken from him and paid to the treasury of the Muslims; and if he was habitual in killing, he would be killed due to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding a woman who cut off the breast of her slave girl: 'She is free, there is no way for her mistress upon her.' And he judged regarding the one who tortured his slave: 'So he is free, there is no way for him upon him. He is a Sa'iba (unconditionally free), he can go and give his mastership to the one he likes. So when he takes the responsibility of his crimes, he would inherit him.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) said: I said to him: The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, 'Retaliation is prescribed for you in the matter of the slain: the free for the free, and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.' So he said: The free is not killed for the slave, but he is given a severe beating, and he is fined his value as the blood money (diyah) for the slave.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The slave is killed due to the free man, and the free man is not killed due to the slave, but he is fined his value and whipped with a severe whipping until he does not repeat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The free man is not killed for the slave. And when the free man kills the slave, he is fined its price, and is whipped with a severe whipping.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A free man is not killed for a slave, even if he kills him deliberately, but he is fined its price and is whipped with a severe whipping if he kills him deliberately. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wergild (blood money) of the slave is his price.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The wergild (blood money) of the slave is his value. So if he was precious, the highest of his value would be ten thousand dirhams, and it does not exceed the wergild of the free man.

Yunus, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the slave kills the free man, he is handed over to the guardians of the killed. If they wish, they kill him; and if they wish, they imprison him; and if they wish, they enslave him, and he becomes a slave to them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)... ...regarding the slave: if he kills a free man, he is handed over to the guardians of the killed one; so if they desire, they kill him, and if they desire, they enslave him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Mudabbir (slave promised freedom upon his master's death) who killed a man deliberately, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is killed due to it.' I said: 'And if he killed him by error?' He said: 'He is handed over to the guardians of the killed one, so he becomes a slave for them; if they wish, they can sell him, and if they wish, they can keep him, and it is not for them to kill him.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! The Mudabbir is a slave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A 'Mudabbir' (a slave promised freedom upon his master's death) killed a man by error. Who is responsible for him? He (peace be upon him) said: His master reconciles on his behalf. But if they refuse, he is handed over to the guardians of the killed one to serve them until the one who promised him freedom dies. Then he returns as free, and there is no way against him. And in another report: And he is sought to be compensated for his value.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group that claimed a crime upon a slave, the damage of which exceeded his value, so the slave confessed to it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The confession of the slave upon his master is not valid. So if they establish proof upon what they claimed against the slave, the slave is taken for it, or his master ransoms him.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the free man kills the slave, he is fined his value and disciplined. It was said: 'And if his value was twenty thousand dirhams?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The value of a slave does not exceed the blood money (diyah) of the free men.'

And from him, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a slave who injured a free man, he said: If the free man desires, he can take retaliation from him; and if he desires, he can seize him, if the injury exceeds his freedom price, and if it does not exceed his freedom price, his master ransoms him. So if his master refuses to ransom him, there is for the injured free man from the slave an amount equal to the blood money of his injury, and the remainder is for the master. The slave is sold, so the injured man takes his right, and the remainder is returned to the master.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who fractured a bone of a slave, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is half of the tenth of his price.

Ibn Mahboub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Salih who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a slave who cut off the hand of a free man, and for him were three paralysed fingers from his hand. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is the value of the slave?' I said, 'Make it to be whatever you like'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the value of the slave was more than the wergild of the two correct fingers, and the three paralysed fingers, the one whose hand was cut off has to return to the master of the slave whatever was the remainder from the value, and seize the slave; and if he so desire to he can take the value of the two correct fingers and the three paralysed fingers'. I said, 'And how much is the value of the two correct fingers along with the palm, and the three paralysed fingers?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The value of the two correct fingers along with the palm is two thousand Dirhams, and the value of the three paralysed fingers along with the palm is a thousand Dirhams, because it is the third from the wergild of the correct (fingers).'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if it was such that the value of the slave is less than the wergild of the two correct fingers, and the three paralysed fingers, the slave would be handed over to the one whose hand was cut off, or his master has to ransom him, and he can take the slave'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who reported it, said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'It necessitates the master of the slave to accept the retaliation of an injury of his slave from the value of his wergild, upon the accounting which comes to compensate for the injury; and when the free man injures the slave, the value of his injury is from the accounting of his (own) value'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, all from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a Mudabbir (slave promised freedom upon the death of his master) who killed a man in error, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his master so desires, he can pay the wergild to them, or else hand him over to them, for him to serve them. So when his master dies, meaning the one who promised to free him, he would return as free. And in the report of Yunus: There would be nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim, from Misma' ibn Abdul Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The mother of the child (umm al-walad), her crimes regarding the rights of people are upon her master, and whatever of the Rights of Allah (Exalted and Majestic) is in the legal penalties (hudud), then that is upon her body. He said: And retaliation (qiṣāṣ) is taken from her for the slaves, and there is no retaliation between the free and the slave.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had two slaves, one of whom killed the other. Is it for him to exact retaliation from him without the Sultan, if he wishes that? He (peace be upon him) said: He is his property; he does with him what he wishes. If he wishes, he kills him, and if he wishes, he pardons.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Al-Khattab ibn Salama, from Hisham ibn Ahmad, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a Mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon his master's death) who killed a man by error. He (peace be upon him) said: 'What have you been narrated regarding this?' I said: 'We have been narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: He is handed over in full to the guardians of the slain. So when the one who promised his freedom (upon his own death) dies, he is freed.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! So the blood of a Muslim man is invalidated?' I said: 'This is how we have been narrated.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You have erred regarding my father. He is handed over in full to the guardians of the slain. So when the one who promised his freedom dies, he is asked to pay his value.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding a nose of the slave, or his manhood, or something which overcame his value, that he has to pay to his master the value of the slave, and take the slave.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a contracted slave who was killed. He said: 'What portion of him was freed is calculated, so the wergild of the free man is paid, and what portion of him remained enslaved is the ransom of the slave.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a contracted slave (mukatab) whose master stipulated a condition upon him when he contracted him: that he would pay compensation to a man if he committed a crime against him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he has paid something from his contract, he is fined for his crime in proportion to what he has paid from his contract, to the free man. If he is unable to pay anything from the right of the crime, that is taken from the wealth of the master who contracted him.' I said: 'And if the crime was against a slave?' He said: 'A similar amount is paid to the master of the slave whom the contracted slave injured, and there is no retaliation (taqass) between the contracted slave and the slave if the contracted slave has paid something from his contract. If he has not paid anything from his contract, then the slave is retaliated from him, or the master is fined for every crime the contracted slave committed, because he is his slave, as long as he has not paid anything from his contract.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a contracted slave who killed a man in error. He said: 'If his master, when he contracted him, had stipulated upon him that if he was unable to pay, he would return to slavery, then he is at the status of the owned slave. He is handed over to the guardians of the killed one; if they wish, they kill him, and if they wish, they sell him.' And if his master, when he contracted him, did not stipulate upon him, and he had paid something from his contract, then Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'He is freed from the contract in proportion to what he has paid from his contract.' Thus, it is upon the Imam to pay to the guardians of the killed one from the blood money in proportion to what was freed from the contract, and the blood of a Muslim man is not invalidated. And I see that whatever remains upon the contracted slave, from what he has not paid, is slavery to the guardians of the killed one; they utilize him for his life in proportion to what remains upon him, and it is not for them to sell him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a contracted slave (mukatab) who killed a man in error, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him from his blood money (diyah) is in proportion to what has been freed of his debt, and upon his master is what remains from the value of the slave. So if the contracted slave is unable (to pay), there is no blood-money guarantors (aqilah) for him; rather, that is upon the Imam of the Muslims.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a free man who killed a slave whose value was twenty thousand dirhams, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible that the value of a slave exceeds the blood money (diyah) of a free man.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The wergild (blood money) of the Jew, and the Christian, and the Magian, is eight hundred Dirhams.

And from him, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Muslim kills a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, so they intend that they retaliate, they have to return the excess wergild to the (guardians of the) Muslim, and retaliate him.

And from him, from Zur'a, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding a Muslim man who killed a man from the Ahl al-Dhimma. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a harsh Hadith, the people cannot bear it, but the Dhimmi must pay the blood money of the Muslim, then the Muslim would be killed due to it'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, or someone else, from Aban, from Ismail ibn al-Fad-Fadl, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the blood-money of the Magians, the Jews, and the Christians: is there anything upon them and upon the one who kills them, when they overcome the Muslims and display enmity to them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he is habitual in killing them.' He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the Muslim: would he be killed due to the People of the Covenant (Zimmi) and the People of the Book, when he kills them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if it happens to be habitual for that, not leaving killing them, so he would be killed due to it, and he would be belittled.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) — similar to it is like it. Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Ibrahim is alleging that the wergild (blood money) of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian is the same. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, he said the truth.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Dureys al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Regarding a Christian who killed a Muslim, so when he was seized, he became a Muslim. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Kill him due to it.' It was said: 'And if he had not become a Muslim?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be handed over to the guardians of the killed one [if they wish, they kill him, and if they wish, they pardon him, and if they wish, they enslave him, and if there was wealth with him, it would be handed over to the guardians of the killed one], him and his wealth.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Muslim kills the Christian, and the family of the Christian intend to kill him, they can kill him and pay the excess of what is between the two blood-money amounts.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A Muslim is not retaliated against for a Zimmi in killing, nor in injuries, but the crime compensation is taken from the Muslim for the Zimmi according to the blood money of the Zimmi, eight hundred dirhams.

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bureyd Al-Ajaly, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who blinded an eye of a Christian. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wergild (blood money) of the eye of a Christian is four hundred dirhams.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, and Ibn Bukayr, from Lays Al-Muradi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the wergild (blood money) of the Christian, the Jew, and the Magian. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their wergilds are all the same – eight hundred dirhams, eight hundred dirhams.'

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Muslim, would he be killed due to the Ahl al-Dhimma? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except if he happens to be habitual of killing them, so he would be killed, and he would be belittled'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, that he presented to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) the book of wergild (blood money). And it was in it: for the loss of hearing entirely, one thousand dinars; and for the loss of voice entirely, from the sound of the nose and the hoarse sound, one thousand dinars; and the paralysis of the two hands, both of them, and the paralysis entirely, one thousand dinars; and the paralysis of the two feet, one thousand dinars; and the two lips when they are severed from the root, one thousand dinars; and the back when it humps, one thousand dinars; and the manhood when it is severed from the root, one thousand dinars; and the two testicles, one thousand dinars. And regarding the temple of the man when he is struck, so he is not able to turn except by swerving, is half the wergild, five hundred dinars. So whatever is less than that, it is by its calculation.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), similar to it. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the hand, so he said: Half the wergild, and regarding the ear, half the wergild when it is cut off from its root.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the man whose back is broken, he said: For it is the complete wergild; and for the two eyes is the (complete) wergild, and for one of them is half the wergild; and for the two ears is the (complete) wergild, and for one of them is half the wergild; and for the penis, when the foreskin and what is above it is cut off, is the (complete) wergild; and for the nose, when the soft part is cut off, is the wergild; and for the two lips is the (complete) wergild.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the nose, when its stump is eradicated, is the complete wergild; and regarding the eye, when it is blinded, is half the wergild; and regarding the ear, when it is cut, is half the wergild; and regarding the hand, is half the wergild; and regarding the manhood, when it is cut off from the place of the tip, is the complete wergild.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Jameela, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the lower lip is six thousand, and regarding the upper lip is four thousand, because the lower (lip) retains the water.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the hand is half the wergild; and regarding the two hands together is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two feet is similar to that; and regarding the manhood when the tip is cut off, and what is above that, is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the nose when the soft parts are cut off, is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two lips is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two eyes is the (complete) wergild, and regarding of the two is half the wergild.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the single leg, half the wergild; and regarding the ear, half the wergild when it is cut off from its root, and when its tip is cut, then in it is the value of a just person; and regarding the nose, when it is cut, the complete wergild; and regarding the back, when it breaks until its owner cannot discharge semen, the complete wergild; and regarding the manhood, when it is cut, the complete wergild; and regarding the tongue, when it is cut, the complete wergild.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Suleiman al-Hammar, from Bureyd al-Ajaly, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man whose back was broken so that he could not sit, that regarding it is the complete wergild.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the nose is cut from the soft part, the complete blood-money is due for it; and for the teeth of the man, the complete blood-money is due; and for his two ears, the complete blood-money is due; and the two feet and the two eyes are in that same status.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: A neighbour of mine married a woman. So when he intended to copulate with her, she kicked him with her leg and ruptured his testicle, so it became swollen. So after that he copulated with her and a child was born to him. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and about a man whose navel was struck and ruptured. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding all ruptures is a third of the wergild.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man whose tail bone was broken, so he lost control of his excretion, so what is due regarding it from the wergild? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The complete wergild.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who copulated with a slave girl, so he was rough with her, and when she came down from that situation, she could no longer give birth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The complete wergild'.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding the man who was struck upon his lower area, so he could no longer withhold his faeces nor his urine - regarding that is the complete wergild'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding the male part of the child is the (complete) wergild, and regarding the male part of an impotent man is the (complete) wergild'.
Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Bureyd Al-Ajaly, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the male child, the wergild (blood money) is complete.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man were to cut the female part of a woman, I would fine him her wergild. So if he were not to pay the wergild to her, I would cut off his male part if she were to seek that.

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is your view regarding a man who struck a young woman on her belly, thereby injuring her womb and spoiling her menstruation?' And I mentioned that her menstruation had ceased due to that, whereas previously her menstruation had been regular. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is awaited for a year; if her menstruation returns to what it was, [the matter is resolved], otherwise she is made to swear an oath, and the striker is fined one-third of her blood-money due to the spoiling of her womb and the cessation of her menstruation.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who cut off the breast of his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then he would be fined half a wergild for her'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Nu'man, the owner of Al-Taqq, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a man who caused injury to a slave-girl, meaning his wife, and injured her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the blood-money (diyah) if he had intercourse with her before she reached nine years of age.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he kept her and did not divorce her, there is nothing upon him. And if he had intercourse with her and she was nine years of age, there is nothing upon him; if he wishes, he keeps her, and if he wishes, he divorces her.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Regarding the heart, when it shakes and is damaged, is the (complete) wergild (blood money). And Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Regarding the contortion (of the neck), is the (complete) wergild; and the contortion is that his neck is bent and it comes to be on its side.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding the man who was struck upon his lower part, so he was no longer able to withhold his faeces nor his urine, that with regards to that is the complete wergild'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked him (peace be upon him) while I was in his presence, regarding a man who struck another man and his urine stream was interrupted. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the urine trickles into the night, upon him is the complete wergild (diyah), because it has prevented him from his livelihood; and if it is into the end of the day, upon him is the complete wergild; and if it is into half the day, upon him is two-thirds of the wergild; and if it is into the raising of the day, upon him is one-third of the wergild.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: That which is in the body and consists of two, for one of them is half the wergild, like the two hands and the two eyes. He (the narrator) said: So I said, 'A man whose eye was blinded?' He said: 'Half the wergild.' I said, 'So a man whose hand was cut off?' He said: 'Regarding it is half the wergild.' I said, 'So a man, one of his testicles is lost?' He said: 'If it was the left one, then for it is the (complete) wergild.' I said, 'And why? Did you not say, 'That which is in the body and consists of two, for each one is half the wergild?' He said: 'Because the offspring comes from the left testicle.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the beard: if it is shaved and does not grow back, the wergild is complete; and if it grows back, it is a third of the wergild.

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Khalid from one of his men from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: I said, 'A man enters the bathhouse, and the owner of the bathhouse splashes hot water upon him, causing the hair of his head to wither and not grow back.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the complete wergild (blood money).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a one-eyed man whose healthy eye was struck and blinded: 'He may blind one of the eyes of his companion, and half the blood-money is settled for him; and if he wishes, he may take a complete blood-money, and be excused from the eye of his companion.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Regarding the eye of the one-eyed person, it is the wergild (blood money).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the eye of the one-eyed person, the blood money (diyah) is complete.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad ibn Ziyad, from Suleiman ibn Khalid Regarding a man who cut the hand of a paralytic man, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is a third of the wergild.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, from Abdillah ibn Sulayman, from Abdillah ibn Abu Ja'far, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) [that he said]: Regarding the eye of the one-eyed person, which was firm (functional), then it became blurred (lost function). So he (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) had judged with regards to it being half the wergild for the healthy eye.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: For the tongue of the mute, and the eye of the blind, and the manhood of the castrated man and his two testicles, is a third of the wergild.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: One of the progeny of Zurara asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who cut the tongue of a mute man. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother gave birth to him and he was mute, then upon him is a third of the wergild; and if his tongue was lost due to illness or affliction after he had been speaking, then upon the one who cut his tongue is a third of the wergild of his tongue.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And similarly is the judgement regarding the two eyes and the limbs.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is how we found it in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).'

Ali, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who blinded an eye of a man, (whose vision) had gone, and it (the eye) was firm. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the quarter of the wergild of an eye.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): he said, 'I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his punishment is Hell, abiding eternally in it." He said: The one who kills a believer on account of his religion — that is the deliberate killer whom God, Mighty and Majestic, speaks of, and He has prepared for him a great punishment. I said: What of a man between whom and another man something happens, so he strikes him with his sword and kills him? He said: That is not the deliberate (killer) whom God, Mighty and Majestic, speaks of.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He was asked about the believer who deliberately kills a believer — is there repentance for him? So he said: If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him. But if he killed him out of anger, or due to some worldly matter, then his repentance is that he be subject to retaliation (qisas) from him. And if it was not known about him, he should go to the guardians of the slain and confess to them his murder of their companion. If they then forgive him and do not execute him, he shall pay them the blood money (diya), emancipate a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty poor people — as a repentance to God, Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who killed a believer while knowing he was a believer, except that anger drove him to kill him — is there repentance for him if he intends it, or is there no repentance for him? He said: Retaliation is applied to him. And if it is not publicly known, he should go to his (victim's) guardians and inform them that he killed him. If they forgive him, he shall give them the blood money, emancipate a slave, fast for two consecutive months, and give charity to sixty poor persons.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Isa al-Zarir who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man kills a man deliberately — what is his repentance? He said: He should make himself available (to the guardians of the slain). I said: He fears they will kill him. He said: Then let him give them the blood money (diya). I said: He fears they will come to know (it was him) because of that. He said: Then let him be mindful of the blood money and make it into small packages, then watch for the times of the prayers and place them in their home.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Suleiman al-Dahhan, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, a man from Qays came to Uthman with his slave who had slapped his eye, so water was poured into it, and it remained firm but he could not see anything with it. So he said to him, 'I will give you the blood money,' but he refused. He said, 'So he sent both of them to Ali (peace be upon him) and said, 'Judge between these two.' So he gave him the blood money, but he refused. He said, 'So they did not cease giving him until they gave him two blood monies.' He said, 'So he said, 'I do not want anything except retaliation (qisas).' He said, 'So Ali called for a mirror, so he heated it. Then he called for cotton wool, so he moistened it, then placed it on the lids of his eyes and around them. Then he made him face the sun with his eye. He said, 'And he brought the mirror and said, 'Look!' So he looked, and the fat melted, and his eye remained firm, and his vision was gone.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The hand of the man and his legs are cut in retaliation (qisas).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A one-eyed man blinded the eye of a healthy man.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His eye is blinded.' I said: 'He remains blind.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The right belongs to the one who was blinded.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habeeb al-Sajistani, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who cut the two right hands of two men. He said: 'O Habeeb! His right hand is cut for the man whose right hand he cut first, and his left hand is cut for the man whose right hand he cut last, because he only cut the hand of the last man, and his right hand is retaliation for the first man.' He said: 'I said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to cut the right hand and the left leg.' He said: 'Indeed, he used to do that regarding what is obligatory from the Rights of Allah. But as for the Rights of the Muslims, O Habeeb, their rights are taken for them in retaliation: the hand for the hand, if the cutter has a hand, and the leg for the hand, if the cutter does not have a hand.' So I said to him: 'Does it not obligate the wergild upon him, and his leg is left for him?' He said: 'The wergild is only obligated upon him when he cuts a man's hand, and the cutter has neither two hands nor two legs; then the wergild is obligated upon him because he has no limb from which retaliation can be taken.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the injuries of the body that there is retaliation (qisas) for them, or the injured party may accept the blood money (diyah) for the injury, and it should be given to him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), regarding a man who broke the hand of a man, then the hand of the man was cured. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no retaliation regarding this, but he would be given the compensation (Arsh).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the teeth and the arms which are broken deliberately; is there a compensation (arsh) for them or retaliation (qawd)? He said: Retaliation. I said: So if they double the wergild? He said: If they please him with whatever he desires, then it is for him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr and Ali ibn Hadeed together, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them) that he said: Regarding the tooth of a child, if a man strikes it so it falls out and then grows back, he said: 'There is no retaliation (qisas) upon him, and upon him is the compensation (arsh).' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'And Jameel was asked, 'How much is the compensation for the tooth of a child and for breaking the hand?' So he said: 'Something small, and I do not see anything definite regarding it.''

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a one-eyed man who deliberately blinded the eye of a healthy person. He said: 'His eye is blinded.' I said: 'He becomes completely blind.' He said: 'It is the right (of the victim) which is blinded by him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding a man who struck another man on the head, causing his tongue to become heavy (impaired speech), he is presented with all the letters of the alphabet. Then, he is given the blood money (diyah) proportional to the letters he could not pronounce clearly from among them.

From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who struck a man with a stick upon his head, so his tongue became heavy. So he (peace be upon him) said: ‘There would be presented to him the letters of the alphabet, so whatever he pronounces eloquently from it, and whatever he cannot pronounce eloquently from it, the wergild would be (based) upon it, and these are twenty nine letters’.

From him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who struck another man in the ear with a bone, and the victim claimed that he could not hear, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is placed under surveillance and tested (for hearing), and awaited for one year. If he hears, or two men testify against him that he can hear, then otherwise he is made to swear an oath, and he is given the blood money (diya).' It was said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)! What if it is discovered afterwards that he can hear?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, returns his hearing, I do not see any liability upon him.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who was hit in his ear, so he claimed that one of his ears had lost some of its hearing. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The struck ear is covered with a tight seal, and the healthy one is kept open. A bell is sounded towards his face, and it is said to him, 'Listen'. When the sound becomes hidden to him, its location is noted. Then it is sounded from behind him, and it is said to him, 'Listen'. When the sound becomes hidden to him, its location is noted. Then the distance between the two is measured. If they are equal, it is known that he has spoken the truth.' Then he is taken to his right, and it is sounded until the sound becomes hidden to him, then its location is noted. Then he is taken to his left, and it is sounded until the sound becomes hidden to him, then its location is noted. Then the distance between the two is measured. If it is equal, it is known that he has spoken the truth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then his damaged ear is opened, and the other is sealed well. Then the bell is sounded from in front of him, and it is noted where the sound becomes hidden to him. He is treated as he was treated the first time with his healthy ear. Then the excess of the healthy ear over the damaged one is measured by that calculation.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man is struck on his head and his tongue becomes heavy, the letters of the alphabet are presented to him. He reads, then the wergild (blood money) is divided among the letters of the alphabet. Whatever he cannot pronounce clearly with his speech, the wergild is quantified based on that.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Hasan ibn Kathir, from his father, who said: An eye of a man was hit, and it was firm (in its place). So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ordered for his healthy eye to be tied up, and had a man stand beside him with an egg in his hand. He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Can you see it?' So when he said 'Yes', he (peace be upon him) made him stand back a little, until it was hidden from him, he (peace be upon him) noted that place. And the struck eye was tied up, and he made the man move further away while he was looking with his healthy eye, until it was hidden from him. Then he measured the distance between them, and he was given the 'arsh (compensation) for that.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn Furat, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who struck another man on his head. The struck man claimed that he could not see anything, nor smell the scent, and that his tongue had gone. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is truthful, he is entitled to three blood-wits (diyas).' It was said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, how is it known that he is truthful?' He said: 'As for what he claimed regarding not smelling the scent, the tinder (firewood) is brought near him. If he is as he says, or else he turns his head away and his eyes water. As for what he claimed regarding his eyes, he is made to face the sun with his eyes. If he is lying, he cannot control himself until he closes his eyes; and if he is truthful, they remain open. As for what he claimed regarding his tongue, a needle is struck upon his tongue. If red blood comes out, he has lied; and if black blood comes out, he has spoken truthfully.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who is struck in the eye, so part of his vision is lost. What is given to him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'One of them (the eyes) is tied/covered, then an egg is placed for him, then it is said to him, "Look!" As long as he claims that he sees its place, (it is moved away) until it reaches a place where, if he passes it, he says, "I do not see it." It is brought nearer until he sees it, then that place is marked. Then it is measured with that measurement from behind him, and from his right, and from his left. So if it comes out equal, or else it is said to him, "You are lying," until he speaks the truth.' I said, 'Is he not trusted?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and there is no honor (guaranteed), and the same is done with the other eye. Then that is measured against the wergild (blood money) of the eye.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, and from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, all together, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Yunus said: 'I presented the book to him, and he said: It is correct.' And Ibn Fazzal said: 'Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged: When a man is injured in one of his eyes, it is measured with an egg tied over the injured eye, and the vision of the healthy eye is observed to see where it ends. Then the healthy eye is covered, and the vision of the injured eye is observed to see where it ends. He is given his blood money (diyah) based on this calculation, and the compurgation (qasamah/oath-swearing) along with it is from the six parts, according to the extent of the injury to his eye.' If it was a sixth of his vision, he alone swears and is given; if it was a third, he swears and another man swears with him; if it was half, he swears and two men swear with him; if it was two-thirds, he swears and three persons swear with him; if it was four-fifths, he swears and four persons swear with him; if it was all his vision, he swears and five persons swear with him. And thus is the compurgation in all cases regarding injuries. And if there is no one for the injured person to swear with, the oaths are doubled upon him. If it was a sixth of his vision, he swears once; if it was a third, he swears twice; and if it is more, it is according to this calculation. And indeed, the compurgation is based on the extent of his vision. And if it is hearing, it is upon a similar manner, except that something is struck for him until the extent of his hearing is known. Then that is measured, and the compurgation is according to what is lacking from his hearing. If his hearing was complete, and mischief is feared from him, he is left until he sleeps a little, then he is shouted at. If he hears, the judge judges between them by his opinion. And if the deficiency is in the upper arm or thigh, the measure of that is known. His healthy leg is measured with a cord, then his injured leg is measured, so the measure of what his leg or hand has lost is known. If the shin or forearm is injured, it is measured from the thigh and upper arm, and the judge looks at the measure of his thigh. A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Zareef, from his father Zareef ibn Nasih, from a man called Abdullah ibn Ayoub

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Rafa'ah who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding a man who struck a man, so some of his breathing was deficient. With what thing would that be known?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By the hours.' I said, 'And how by the hours?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'For indeed, the breath rises at dawn, and it is in the right side of the nose. So when an hour passes, it moves to the left side. So you look at the difference between your breathing and his breathing. Then it is reckoned, so he is taken by that calculation from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub from Jameel ibn Salih from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda' who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who struck a man with a tent pole on his head with one strike, causing it to pierce to the brain, so his intellect was lost. He (peace be upon him) said: If the struck one does not comprehend the prayer from it, nor comprehend what he says, nor what is said to him, then he is awaited for a year. If he dies in the period between the strike and the year, the striker is retaliated with (qisas); and if he does not die in that period and his intellect does not return to him, the striker is liable for the blood money (diyah) from his wealth due to the loss of his intellect. I said to him, 'So what do you view upon him for the fracture?' He said, 'No, because he struck him with one strike, so the one strike committed two crimes. Therefore, I hold him liable for the harshest of the two crimes, which is the blood money. And if he had struck him with two strikes, so the two strikes committed two crimes, I would hold him liable for the crime of what they committed, whatever they were, except if death occurs in them, then the striker is retaliated with (qisas).' [Note: The phrase 'بِوَاحِدَةٍ وَ تُطْرَحَ الْأُخْرَى' is implied in the context of qisas vs diyah for multiple strikes where one causes death, though the text provided in the prompt's Arabic block for this specific segment ends at 'ضَارِبُهُ'. The prompt's Arabic text for this chunk is: 'قُلْتُ لَهُ فَمَا تَرَى عَلَيْهِ فِي الشَّجَّةِ شَيْئاً قَالَ لَا لِأَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً فَجَنَتِ الضَّرْبَةُ جِنَايَتَيْنِ فَأُلْزِمُهُ أَغْلَظَ الْجِنَايَتَيْنِ وَ هِيَ الدِّيَةُ وَ لَوْ كَانَ ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَتَيْنِ فَجَنَتِ الضَّرْبَتَانِ جِنَايَتَيْنِ لَأَلْزَمْتُهُ جِنَايَةَ مَا جَنَتَا كَانَتَا مَا كَانَتَا إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ فِيهِمَا الْمَوْتُ فَيُقَادَ بِهِ ضَارِبُهُ'] He said, 'And he said: If he struck him with three strikes, one after another, so they committed three crimes, I would hold him liable for the crime of what the three strikes committed, whatever they were, as long as death is not in them, then the striker is retaliated with.' He said, 'And he said: If he struck him with ten strikes, so they committed one crime, I would hold him liable for that one crime which the

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who struck another man with a stick, so his hearing, vision, tongue, intellect, and private parts were lost, and his ability to copulate ceased, while he was alive — (a judgement of) six wergilds.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled regarding Al-Mamouma (skull fracture reaching the brain) as one-third of the blood money; and regarding Al-Munqila (bone-displacing injury) as fifteen camels; and regarding Al-Mudhiha (bone-exposing injury) as five camels; and regarding Al-Damiya (bloody injury) as one camel; and regarding Al-Bazi'a (flesh-exposing injury) as two camels. And he ruled regarding Al-Mutalahima (flesh injury) as three camels, and ruled regarding Al-Simhaq (injury reaching the bone) as four camels.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said: We both asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the al-mamouma fracture, so he said: 'Regarding it is a third of the wergild, and regarding the al-jaifa is a third of the wergild, and regarding the al-mudhiha is five camels.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding Al-Mudhiha (bone-exposing injury), it is five camels; and regarding Al-Simhaq (injury reaching the bone), it is four camels; and Al-Badhi'a (flesh-exposing injury), it is three camels; and Al-Ma'muma (skull fracture reaching the brain), it is thirty-three camels; and Al-Jaifa (skull injury reaching the inside of the brain), it is thirty-three camels; and Al-Munqila (bone-displacing injury), it is fifteen camels.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih Al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the bone-exposing injury (al-mudhiha) in the head, just as it is in the face. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The bone-exposing injury and the fracture in the face and the head are equal in the wergild (diyah), because the face is part of the head, and the injuries in the body are not like those in the head.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and from him, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, who said: I presented the book to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said: 'It is correct. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the wergild (blood money) for injuries to all limbs, in the head and the face and the rest of the body, concerning hearing and vision and voice and intellect and the two hands and the two feet, regarding cutting and breaking and dysfunction and tearing and bone-exposing injury and bloody injury and displacement of bones and piercing, which occur in any of those.' So whatever bone was broken, set properly without deformity or defect, and its bones were not displaced, its wergild is known. If it was exposed (bone visible) and its bones were not displaced, then its wergild is for the break and for the exposure. For the wergild of every broken bone is known; and the displacement of its bones is half the wergild of its break, and the wergild of its exposure is a quarter of the wergild of its break. So whatever is covered by the clothes, apart from the two forearms and the fingers, and in a wound that does not heal, is a third of the wergild of that bone in which it is. And he issued a verdict regarding the piercing when it is pierced from a spear or a dagger in any part of the man's extremities, so its wergild is a tenth of the wergild of the man, being one hundred dinars.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the injuries in the fingers when the bone is exposed, [the compensation is] a tenth of the wergild of the finger, if the injured one does not intend to retaliate.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who fractured another man, exposing the bone. Then he sought (forgiveness) so he gifted it to him. Then it worsened, so it killed him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is responsible for the wergild except for the price of the exposed bone, because he had gifted it to him, and he had not gifted the self.' And regarding the Simhaq (cut reaching the bone but less than exposure), it is five hundred Dirhams. And regarding it, if it is in the face, it is double the wergild according to the degree of shame (it causes). And regarding the Ma'mumah (skull fracture), it is a third of the wergild. And it is that which has penetrated but has not reached the cavity (of the brain), so it is what is between the two (exposure and Simhaq). And regarding the Ja'ifah (piercing), it is a third of the wergild. And it is that which has reached the cavity of the brain. And regarding the Munqiliah (bone displacement), it is fifteen camels. And it is that which has become a wound from which the bones are displaced.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the upper arm when it is struck, so the wrist breaks from it. He said: If the palm dries up from it, so the fingers of the palm are all paralysed, then in it is two-thirds of the wergild of the hand. He said: And if some of the fingers are paralysed and some remain, then in each paralysed finger is two-thirds of its wergild. He said: And the same is the ruling regarding the leg and the foot when the toes of the foot are paralysed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the finger, its wergild is one-tenth of the full blood money if it is cut off from its root or becomes paralyzed. He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the fingers, are they equal in wergild?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the teeth, so he said: Their wergild is the same'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The fingers of the two hands and the two legs are equal regarding the wergild. For each finger is ten camels, and for the nail is five dinars.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the displacement that occurs in a limb, [stating that it is] one-third of the wergild of that limb.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May Allah improve you. Indeed, some people have thirty-two teeth in their mouths, and some have twenty-eight. So upon how much is the blood-money (diyah) of the teeth divided?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The natural creation is only twenty-eight teeth: twelve in the front of the mouth and sixteen in the back. Upon this, the blood-money of the teeth is divided.' So the blood-money of each tooth from the front, when it breaks until it is gone, is five hundred dirhams, so the total of them is six thousand dirhams. And for each tooth from the back, when it breaks until it is gone, its blood-money is two hundred and fifty dirhams, and there are sixteen of them, so the total of them is four thousand dirhams. So the total blood-money of the front and back teeth is ten thousand dirhams. And the blood-money was established upon this: so whatever exceeds twenty-eight teeth, there is no blood-money for it, and whatever is less, there is no blood-money for it. This is how we found it in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him). He (the narrator) said: So Al-Hakam said: 'I said: Indeed, the blood-moneys used to be taken before today from camels, cows, and sheep.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That was only in the villages (bedouin areas) before Islam. So when Islam became prominent and silver coins (wariq) became abundant among the people, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) divided it upon the silver coins.' Al-Hakam said: So I said to him: 'What is your view of the one who is from the people of the villages today? What is taken from them regarding the blood-money today, camels or silver?' He said: 'Camels today are like silver. But they are better than silver regarding the blood-money.' Indeed, they used to take from them regarding the accidental blood-money one hundred camels, calculated at one hundred dirhams for each camel, so that is ten thousand dirhams. I said to him: 'So what are the ages of the one hundred camels?' He said: 'Whatever a year has passed upon them, all of them males.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ziyad ibn Suqata, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the fingers of the two hands and the toes of the two feet: 'Do you see that for what exceeds ten fingers or is deficient from ten in them, there is a wergild?' He said to me: 'O Hakam! The creation upon which the wergild is distributed is ten fingers in the two hands; so whatever is additional or deficient, there is no wergild for it. And ten toes in the two feet; so whatever is additional or deficient, there is no wergild for it. And for every finger from the fingers of the two hands is one thousand dirhams, and for every toe from the toes of the two feet is one thousand dirhams. And whatever is from paralysis, it is upon one-third of the wergild of the healthy.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fadhal and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all together said: We presented the Book of Obligations (Inheritance) from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), so he said: 'It is correct.'

And a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Zareyf, from his father Zareyf ibn Nasih, who said: 'A man called Abdullah ibn Ayub narrated to me, who said: Abu Amr al-Mutatabbib narrated to me, who said: I presented it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:' 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued verdicts, so the people wrote down his verdicts, and Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) wrote them to his governors and the heads of his battalions.' So from what was in it: If the upper eyelid is hit, so it tears, its wergild is a third of the wergild of the eye, being one hundred and sixty-six and two-thirds Dinars. And if the lower eyelid is hit, so it tears, its wergild is half the wergild of the eye, being one hundred and fifty Dinars. And if the eyebrow is hit and all of its hair is gone, so its wergild is half the wergild of the eye, being two hundred and fifty Dinars. So whatever is hit from it, so it is based upon the accounting of that. The nose: So if the side of the nose is cut, and it is its edge, so its wergild is five hundred Dinars. If it has been pierced by a piercing by an arrow or a spear, and does not close, so its wergild is three hundred and thirty-three and a third Dinars. And if it was pierced, so it was cured and was complete, so its wergild is a fifth of the wergild of the side of the nose, being one hundred Dinars. So whatever was hit from it, so it would be based upon the accounting of that. And if it was pierced in one of the two nostrils to the nasopharynx, and it is the barrier between the two nostrils, so its wergild is a tenth of the wergild of the nose, being fifty Dinars. Because it is the half. And if it was pierced in one of the nostrils, or the nasopharynx to the other nostril, so its wergild is sixty-six Dinars and two-thirds of a Dinar.

He said: When the upper lip is cut and eradicated, its wergild is five hundred dinars. Whatever is cut from it is accounted for based on that. If it splits to the extent that the teeth become visible from it, then it is medicated, heals, and knits together, its wergild is one hundred dinars. That is one-fifth of the wergild of the lip when it is cut and eradicated, and whatever is cut from it is accounted for based on that. If it is torn and shows an ugly scar, its wergild is one hundred and thirty dinars and one-third of a dinar. And the wergild of the lower lip when it is eradicated is two-thirds of the wergild: six hundred and sixty-six dinars and two-thirds of a dinar. Whatever is cut from it is accounted for based on that. If it splits to the extent that the teeth become visible from it, then it heals and knits together, its wergild is one hundred and thirty dinars and one-third of a dinar. And if it is struck and shows an ugly scar, its wergild is three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar, and that is half of its wergild. And in the report of Zarif ibn Nasih, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: It has reached us that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) preferred it (the lower lip), because it holds the food along with the teeth, therefore he preferred it in his judgment.

And regarding the cheek, if there is a perforation in it from which the inside of the mouth can be seen, its wergild is two hundred dinars; and if it was treated, healed, and united, and there is a clear mark and a prominent scar upon it, its wergild is fifty dinars. So if the perforation was in both cheeks, its wergild is one hundred dinars, and that is half the wergild of that from which the mouth is seen. So if it was a strike with a blade that embeds in the bone to the extent that it pierces to the jaw, its wergild is one hundred and fifty dinars, fifty of which are assigned for exposing the bone; and if it was a perforation and did not pierce into it, its wergild is one hundred dinars. So if it has a scar, the wergild for its scar is in addition to the wergild for exposing the bone. So if it was a wound and did not expose (bone), then it healed and was in the two cheeks, its wergild is ten dinars. So if it was in the face as a fracture, its wergild is eighty dinars. So if a piece of flesh fell from it and it did not expose (bone), and it was the size of a dirham or more, its wergild is thirty dinars. And the wergild of the strike when it exposes (bone) is forty dinars when it is in the cheek. And regarding the exposing of the bone in the head, it is fifty dinars. So if the bones were displaced from it, its wergild is one hundred and fifty dinars. So if it was a perforation in the head, that is the Al-Ma'mumah, its wergild is three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the slap that blackens the face, that its compensation (arsh) is six dinars. So if it does not blacken, but turns green, then its compensation is three dinars. So if it reddens and does not turn green, then its compensation is one and a half dinars.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) judged regarding the ear lobe, [assigning] one-third of the wergild of the ear. And by the first chain, regarding the two ears, if one of them is cut, its wergild is five hundred dinars, and whatever is cut from it is calculated accordingly.

He (peace be upon him) said: And regarding the teeth, for every tooth is fifty Dinars, and all the teeth are equal; and before that it was judged with regards to the incisors being fifty Dinars, and regarding the quadrilaterals is forty Dinars, and regarding the canines is thirty Dinars, and regarding the molars is twenty five Dinars. If the tooth blackens to its surroundings and does not fall off, so its wergild is the wergild of the falling, being fifty Dinars; and if it cracks and does not fall off, so its wergild is twenty five Dinars, and whatever breaks from it, from something, so it would be by its accounting from the fifty Dinars. So if it falls of afterwards and it has blackened, so its wergild is twelve Dinars and a half a Dinar. So whatever breaks from it from something, so its accounting would be from the twenty five Dinars.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: All the teeth are equal; for each tooth is five hundred dirhams.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, or someone else, from Aban, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When the incisor blackens, the wergild (blood money) is applicable regarding it.'
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the teeth, so he said: 'These, with regards to the wergild, are the same'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The tooth, when it is struck, is awaited for a year; if it falls out, the striker is fined five hundred dirhams, and if it does not fall out but blackens, he is fined two-thirds of its wergild.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) judged regarding the tooth of a child before it extrudes, [paying] a camel for each tooth in each age.

Referring to the first chain, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And regarding the clavicle when it breaks, so it is bandaged upon and becomes flawless, is forty Dinars. So if it cracks, its wergild is four fifths of its breaking, being thirty-two Dinars. So if it is exposed, its wergild is twenty-five Dinars, and this is a fifth part from one-eight from its wergild, when it breaks. So if the bone is displaced from it, its wergild is half the wergild of its breaking, being twenty Dinars.
