Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said regarding the compurgation (sworn endorsements): fifty men for the deliberate [killing], and for the erroneous [killing], twenty-five men, and upon them is that they should swear by Allah.

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub from Abu Wallad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no mutual compensation (by blood relatives) among the People of the Covenant regarding what they incur of killing or injury; rather, that is taken from their wealth. So if they do not have wealth, the crime liability returns to the Imam of the Muslims, because they pay the Jizya to him, just as the slave pays the tribute to his master. He (peace be upon him) said: And they are the slaves of the Imam, so whoever from them becomes Muslim, he is free.

Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from his father, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had killed a man by error. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Who is your clan and your relatives?' He said, 'I have no clan nor relatives in this city.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So from which of the cities are you?' He said, 'I am a man from the people of Mosul, born in it, and I have relatives and a family there.' He said: So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) inquired about him, but did not find for him any relatives or clan in Kufa. He said: So he wrote to his governor in Mosul: 'As for after, so-and-so son of so-and-so, and his appearance is such and such, killed a man from the Muslims by error. He mentioned that he is a man from Mosul, and that he has relatives and a family there. And I have sent him to you with my messenger, so-and-so son of so-and-so, and his appearance is such and such. So when he comes to you, God willing, and you read my letter, investigate his matter and ask about his relatives from the Muslims.' If he is from the people of Mosul, from those born in it, and you find for him relatives among the Muslims there, gather them to you. Then look: if there is among them a man who inherits him, having a share in the Book (Quran), whom no one from his relatives bars from his inheritance, then obligate him the blood money (diya) and take it from him in installments over three years. If there is not among his relatives anyone who has a share in the Book, and his relatives are equal in lineage, and he has relatives from his father and his mother equal in lineage, then distribute the blood money upon his relatives from his father and upon his relatives from his mother, from the adult Muslim males. Then assign two-thirds of the blood money upon his relatives from his father, and one-third upon his relatives from his mother. And if he has no relatives from his father, then distribute the blood money upon his relatives from his mother, from the adult Muslim males. Then seize them with it and make them pay the blood money over three years. If he has no relatives from his mother nor any relatives from his father, then distribute the blood money upon the people of Mosul, from those born in it and raised there, and do not include others among them from the people of the city. Then c

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a man deliberately, then the killer fled and they were not able to catch him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had wealth, the blood money (diyah) would be taken from his wealth, and if not, then from the nearest [relative] to the nearest. If he had no relatives, the Imam would pay it, for the blood of a Muslim man would not be invalidated.' And in another report: 'Then it is for the ruler afterwards to imprison him and discipline him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged that there would be no burden upon the blood relatives (diyah payers) except for the bone-exposing injury upwards. And he (peace be upon him) said: What is below the reaching-of-bone injury, the fee of the doctor is in addition to the wergild.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The 'Aqilah (blood relatives) are not liable/guarantors for deliberate (killing), nor for confession, nor for reconciliation.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding four who testified upon a married man with the adultery. Then one of them retracted after the man had been killed. He said: If the fourth one says, 'I was delusional', he would be struck the legal penalty, and fined the wergild. And if he says, 'I was deliberate', he would be killed.

Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Nu'aym al-Azdi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about four who testified against a man for adultery. So when he was killed, one of them retracted from his testimony. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fourth one is killed, and the three pay three-quarters of the blood money to his family.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all together from al-Fath ibn Yazeed al-Jurjani, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding four who testified against a man that he had committed adultery, so he was stoned. Then they retracted and said, 'We erred.' They are obligated to pay the blood money (diyah). And if they say, 'We were deliberate,' the guardian of the killed one may kill whichever of the four he wishes. The three (who are killed) pay three-quarters of the blood money to the guardians of the second one killed, and the three are each whipped eighty lashes. And if the guardian of the killed one wishes to kill them all, he pays three blood monies to the guardians of the four witnesses, and they are each whipped eighty lashes, then the Imam kills them. And he (peace be upon him) said regarding two men who testified against a man that he had stolen, so his hand was cut. Then one of them retracted and said, 'I erred regarding this, but it was someone else.' He is obligated to pay half the blood money of the hand, and his testimony is not accepted regarding the other. If both retract and say, 'We erred, but so-and-so was the thief,' they are both obligated to pay the blood money of the hand, and their testimony is not accepted regarding the other. And if they say, 'We were deliberate,' the hand of one of the two is cut by the hand of the one whose hand was cut, and the one whose hand was not cut pays a quarter of the blood money of the man to the guardians of the one whose hand was cut. If the first one (whose hand was) cut says, 'I am not pleased until both their hands are cut together,' he returns the blood money of one hand to be divided between them, and both their hands are cut.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding an eye of a horse whose eye was blinded, [paying] a quarter of its price on the day its eye was blinded.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Muhammad from Al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Al-Abbas who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who blinds an eye of an animal, so upon him is a quarter of its price'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was raised to him a case of a man who killed a pig, so he made him responsible for its price, and a case was raised to him of a man who broke a guitar, so he dismissed it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the wergild (blood money) of the Saluqi dog, it is forty dirhams. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that it be paid to the Clan of Juzayma.

Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said: The wergild (blood money) of the greyhound dog is forty dirhams, which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established; and the wergild of the sheepdog is a ram; and the wergild of the field-guarding dog is a jarib of wheat; and the wergild of the domestic dog is a qafeez of soil from its owners.

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding the one who killed the hunting dog: 'It is evaluated [for compensation], and similarly [is the case for] the falcon, and similarly [is the case for] the sheep dog, and similarly [is the case for] the wall (guard) dog.'

Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said regarding the foetus of the animal: when it is struck and it aborts it, (the compensation is) one-tenth of its price.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marwazi, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding two horses that collided, so one of them died; therefore, he made the remaining one liable for the blood-money (diyah) of the dead one.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — both together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — regarding ten (people) who participated jointly in killing a man. He said: 'The family of the killed one has the option: whichever of them they so desire, they may execute (in retaliation), and his guardians have recourse against the remaining ones for nine-tenths of the blood money.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding two men who both killed one man. He said: 'If the guardians of the killed one intend to kill both of them, they must pay a complete blood money and kill both of them, and the blood money will be divided among the guardians of the two who were executed. If they intend to kill only one of the two and kill him, the one left must pay half the blood money to the family of the killed one. And if they do not demand blood money from either of them and do not kill either of them, the guardian of the killed one may accept the blood money from both of them.'

From him, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When two or three men kill one man, if his guardians want to execute them all, they must pay back the excess blood money; otherwise they take the blood money of their companion (the killed).

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Ten people killed one man.' He said: 'If his next of kin wish, they may kill them all together, and [the killers' families] pay nine blood-monies; or if they wish, they may select one man and kill him, while the remaining nine each pay one-tenth of the blood-money to the family of the last one killed.' He said: 'Thereafter, the ruler takes charge of disciplining them and imprisoning them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, both together from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding four who had drunk (wine) and became intoxicated. They then took weapons against each other and fought, so two were killed and two were wounded. He ordered the two wounded to each be flogged eighty lashes, and ruled that the blood-money for the two killed be borne by the two wounded. He also ordered that the injuries of the two wounded be assessed and deducted from the blood-money. If the two wounded then die, there is nothing owed by anyone from among the guardians of the two killed.

It was brought before Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): six boys had been in the Euphrates, and one of them drowned. Three of them testified against two that those two had drowned him, and two testified against the three that they had drowned him. So he (peace be upon him) ruled that the blood money be divided into fifths: three-fifths upon the two, and two-fifths upon the three.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding two men who joined together to cut off a man's hand. He said: 'If he (the victim) wishes to have both their hands cut off, he shall pay them both the blood money of one hand, which they divide between themselves, and then their hands are cut off; and if he wishes, he may take from both of them the blood money of one hand.' He said: 'And if the hand of only one of the two is cut off, the one whose hand was not cut off must pay a quarter of the blood money to the one whose hand was cut off.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a wall that three persons collaborated to demolish: it fell upon one of them and he died. So he held the remaining two liable for his blood money (diya), because each one of them is responsible for his companion.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu al-Abbas and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a group gathers to kill one man, the guardian (of the deceased) decides which one of them shall be killed — and it is not permitted for them to kill more than one. Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority, so let him not be excessive in killing.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a slave and a free man who both killed a free man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he (the guardian of the deceased) so desires, he can kill the free one, and if he so desires, he can kill the slave. So if he were to choose to kill the free one, he should whip the side of the slave.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad, both together from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a man who orders a man with the killing of a man, so he killed him. So he said: 'The one who killed him shall be killed for it (qisas), and the one who ordered his killing shall be imprisoned in prison until he dies.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Mahbub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him. He said: So he (the Imam) said: The master shall be killed for it.

Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him: 'And is the slave of a man anything but like his whip or like his sword? The master is executed because of it, and the slave is placed in prison.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When a man kills two men or more than that, he shall be killed by them (the guardians of the deceased).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a group of people dug a pit (trap) for the lion in Yemen. The lion fell into it, and the people thronged around it looking at the lion. Then a man fell into it and grabbed hold of another, and the other grabbed hold of another, and that other to yet another. The lion wounded them; among them was one who died from the wounds of the lion, and among them was one who was pulled out but then died. They quarreled over this matter to the point of drawing their swords. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Come, I shall judge between you.' He ruled that the first one receives one quarter of the blood money, the second one receives one third, the third one receives one half, and the fourth receives a full blood money — and he made this obligation incumbent upon the tribes of those who had thronged. Some of the people were satisfied and some were angered. So the matter was referred to the Prophet (may God bless him and his family), and he was informed of the Commander of the Faithful's ruling (peace be upon him), and he endorsed it.

In the narration of Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) ruled regarding four persons who peered into a pit dug for a lion, so one of them fell and grabbed hold of the second, and the second grabbed hold of the third, and the third grabbed hold of the fourth, until they dragged each other down upon the lion and the lion killed them all. So he (AS) ruled that the first was the prey of the lion, and imposed upon his family one-third of the blood money (diyah) to the family of the second; imposed upon the family of the second two-thirds of the blood money to the family of the third; and imposed upon the third a complete blood money to the family of the fourth.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) came to Abu al-Abbas while he was at al-Hira, one day he went out intending (to meet) Isa ibn Musa. He met him between al-Hira and al-Kufa, and with him was Ibn Shubruma, the judge. He said to him (the Imam): 'Where are you going, O Abu Abdillah?' He said: 'I intended (to meet) you.' He said: 'Allah has shortened your steps.' He said: So he went along with him. Then Ibn Shubruma said to him (the Imam): 'What do you say, O Abu Abdillah, regarding something which the Emir asked me about, but I had nothing to say about it?' He said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'He asked me about the first letter/document written on earth.' He (the Imam) said: 'Yes. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, presented to Adam (peace be upon him) his offspring to his eyes, in the form of particles — prophet after prophet, king after king, believer after believer, and disbeliever after disbeliever. When He reached David (peace be upon him), he (Adam) said: Who is this whom You have granted prophethood, honoured him, yet shortened his lifespan?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'This is your son David; his age is forty years, and I have indeed written the lifespans, distributed the provisions, and I obliterate what I will and affirm (what I will), and with Me is the Mother of the Book. So if you make something of your lifespan for him, I shall attach it to him.' He (Adam) said: 'O Lord! I have made sixty years from my lifespan for him, to complete one hundred.' He (the narrator) said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Jibrail, Mika'il and the Angel of Death: 'Write upon him a document, for he will indeed forget.' He said: So they wrote a document upon him (Adam) and sealed it with their wings from the clay of Illiyeen. He said: So when death presented itself to Adam, the Angel of Death came to him. Adam said: 'O Angel of Death! What has brought you?' He said: 'I have come to seize your soul.' He said: 'But sixty years remain of my lifespan.' He (the Angel of Death) said: 'You made it for your son David.' He (the narrator) said: And Jibrail descended upon him and brought out the document. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: For that reason, when the promissory note (sakk) is produced against the de

When Adam's (AS) children were presented to him, he looked at Dawud (AS) and was impressed by him, so he gave him fifty years from his own lifespan. He said: And Jibreel and Mikaeel descended to him, and the Angel of Death wrote a promissory note upon him for the fifty years. When death came to Adam (AS), the Angel of Death was sent to him and Adam (AS) said: 'There are still fifty years remaining from my lifespan.' He (the Angel) said: 'Then where are the fifty years that you gave to your son Dawud?' He (the Imam) said: He had either forgotten it or denied it. So Jibreel and Mikaeel (AS) descended and both testified against him, and the Angel of Death took his soul. Then Abu Abdillah (AS) said: 'It was the first promissory note written in the world.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has a right upon another man, so the debtor denies the right and swears that he owes nothing, and the creditor has no proof for his right. Is it permissible for us to revive his right by false testimony if there is fear of its loss? He said: That is not permissible due to the reason of fraud/deception.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, I said to him: A man from your mawali has a debt owed to a man (from the) adversaries. He wants to bankrupt him and have him imprisoned, and it is known that there is nothing with him, and he has no ability over (paying) it, and there is no proof for his creditors. Is it allowed for him that he should swear an oath in order to repel them from himself until Allah makes solvency for him, and if there are witnesses from the ones in your Wilayah who recognise that he has no ability (to pay), is it allowed for them that they would be testifying upon it? He said: It is not allowed that they should be testifying upon it, and he (the creditor) is not intending injustice to him.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the testimony of the children allowed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, regarding the killing, he would be taken with the first of his speech, and he would not be taken from the second one from it'.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jab-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said: Regarding the child testifying to the testimony, he said: 'If he understands it when he reaches maturity, that he is telling the truth, his testimony is valid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of children, when they are called as witnesses while they are young, is valid when they grow up, provided they have not forgotten it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the child, is his testimony allowed regarding the killing? He (peace be upon him) said: He is taken by the first of his speech, and he is not taken by the second.

A number of our companions narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Jamil who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a child, if his testimony is valid in the case of murder. He said: 'His first words are accepted, and his second words are not accepted.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with the testimony of the owned slave when he is just.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all together, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdul-Hamid Al-Taiy, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the testimony of the owned slave, he said: 'When he is just (adl), his testimony is valid. The first one to reject the testimony of the owned slave was Umar ibn Al-Khattab, and that is when a slave came to him regarding a testimony, so he said, 'If I establish the testimony, I fear for my self, and if I conceal it, I would sin with my Lord.' So he said, 'Give your testimony. Indeed, we will not validate the testimony of a slave after you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the owned slave, is his testimony allowed? He said: Yes, the first one who rejected the testimony of the owned slave was so-and-so.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We said, 'Is the testimony of women permissible regarding the legal penalties (Hudud)?' He said, 'Regarding killing alone.' Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The blood of a Muslim man is not invalidated.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him about the testimony of women regarding stoning, so he said: If there are three men and two women, and if there are two men and four women, it is not valid for stoning.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked him about the testimony of women, so he said: The testimony of women alone is valid for what men cannot look at; and the testimony of women in marriage is valid if a man is with them, and it is not valid in divorce, nor in blood (diyah), except that her testimony is valid in the legal penalty of adultery when there are three men and two women; and the testimony of two men and four women is not valid.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: I asked him, 'Is the testimony of women permissible in marriage, or divorce, or in stoning?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is permissible in what men are unable to look at, and there is no man with them; and their testimony is permissible in marriage if there is a man with them; and their testimony is permissible in the legal penalty (hadd) of adultery if there are three men and two women; but the testimony of two men and four women is not permissible in adultery and stoning; and their testimony is not permissible in divorce, nor in blood (diya (blood money).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is not valid regarding the new moon, nor regarding divorce.' And he (the narrator) said: 'I asked him (peace be upon him) about women, is their testimony valid?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, regarding virginity and the postpartum period.'
Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The testimony of women is valid regarding virginity and every defect that men cannot look at.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The testimony of women is not valid regarding the sighting of the crescent moon, and the testimony of two men and four women is not valid regarding stoning, but the testimony of three men and two women is valid in that matter. And he said: The testimony of women alone, without men, is valid regarding everything for which men are not allowed to look, and the testimony of the midwife alone is valid regarding the newborn.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the testimony of women, is it valid in marriage? He said: 'Yes, and it is not valid in divorce.' He said: And Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is valid in stoning when there are three men and two women, but when there are four women and two men, it is not valid in stoning.' I said: 'Is the testimony of women valid with men in blood (diyah)?' He said: 'No.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a woman whose death was approaching, and there was no one with her except a woman. Is her testimony valid or not valid? So he said: The testimony of women is valid regarding childbirth and virginity.

A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I allow the testimony of women regarding the boy, whether he cried or did not cry, and in everything that men do not look at, the testimony of women is allowed regarding it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The testimony of the man is allowed for his wife, and of the woman for her husband, when there was someone else with her.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, Ibn Mahbub, Hisham ibn Salim, and Ammar ibn Marwan said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), or said, one of our companions asked him, about the man who testifies for his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is good, his testimony for his wife is valid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of the son for his parent and of the parent for his son, and of the brother for his brother. He said, so he said: It is allowed.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the testimony of the father for his son, and of the son for his father, and of the brother for his brother, so he said: It is allowed.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of the son for his father, and of the father for his son, and of the brother for his brother, is valid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), or he said, 'One of our companions asked him,' about the man who testifies for his father, or the father testifies for his son, or the brother for his brother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that when it is good; his testimony for his father, and the father for his son, and the brother for his brother, is accepted.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, all together from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithammi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about three partners, two testified against one. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their testimony is not valid.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a group of friends who were on a road, and the road was cut off to them (by bandits). So the thieves were seized, and some of them testified against others. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their testimonies are not accepted except by the confession of the thieves themselves, or a testimony from others against them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya said, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): Is the testimony of the trustee for the deceased accepted regarding a debt he has upon a man, along with another just witness? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: If another just witness testifies with him, then it is upon the claimant to swear an oath. And he wrote: Is it permissible for the trustee to testify for the heir of the deceased, whether young or old, regarding a right he has upon the deceased or upon someone else, and he is the holder for the young heir, and not a holder for the adult? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Yes, it is befitting for the trustee to testify with the truth and not conceal the testimony. And he wrote: Or is the testimony of the trustee accepted against the deceased, along with another just witness? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Yes, after an oath.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from al-Ala' ibn Sayabat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) did not validate the testimony of the employee.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one who is rejected from among the witnesses, so he said: 'The suspicious (al-zannin) and the adversary (al-khasm)'. I said, 'So what about the immoral (al-fasiq) and the treacherous (al-kha'in)?' He said, 'All of this is included in the suspicious (al-zannin)'.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about what is rejected from the witnesses. He said: The suspicious one, the accused one, and the adversary. I said: The immoral one and the treacherous one? He said: All of this is included in the suspicious one.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the son of the adulterer, is his testimony allowed? So he (peace be upon him) said: No. So I said, 'Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba is alleging that it is allowed'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, do not forgive his sin'. What Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba: 'And it is a Reminder for you and your people'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayyoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The testimony of the son of adultery is not valid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'If four people testified in my presence against a man for adultery, and among them is a son of the adultery (a bastard), I would apply the legal penalty (hadd) upon them all, because his testimony is not valid, nor can he lead the people (in prayer).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from al-Ala' ibn Sayaba, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The testimony of the owner of the nard (dice) and the fourteen (pieces) and the owner of the two shahs (chess) is not accepted. He says, "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah," "Died, by Allah, the Shah," and "Killed, by Allah, the Shah," and he did not die, and was not killed.'

And by this chain, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The testimony of the precursor of the pilgrims (the one who leads the group on wages) is not accepted because he kills his mount, consumes his provisions, exhausts himself, and takes his prayer lightly. I said, 'And what about the hirer of camels, the camel-driver, and the navigator?' He said, 'And what is the problem with them? Their testimonies are accepted if they are righteous.'
And by this chain, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Prayer is not performed behind the one who seeks payment for the Adhan and the Prayer, and his testimony is not accepted.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) did not validate the testimony of the 'Sābiq al-Hājj' (the precursor of the pilgrims).

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rejected the testimony of the beggar who begs in his palm. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Because he is not trusted regarding the testimony, and that is because if he is given, he is pleased, and if he is prevented, he becomes angry.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amari ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the beggar who begs by his palm, would his testimony be accepted? So he said: My father (peace be upon him) did not accept his testimony when he begs by his palm.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slanderer after the legal penalty has been established upon him, what is his repentance? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should belie himself.' I said: 'What is your view if he belies himself and repents, would his testimony be accepted?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Hammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who slandered another man, so he was whipped with a legal penalty (hadd). Then he repented, and nothing was known from him except goodness. Is his testimony accepted? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What is said among you?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What are they saying among you?' I said: 'They say that his repentance is between him and Allah, and his testimony will never be accepted.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Evil is what they said. My father (peace be upon him) used to say: When one repents and nothing is known from him except goodness, his testimony is valid.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Naw ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had a man testify in his presence, and his hand and leg had been cut off due to his testimony, so he accepted his testimony, and he had repented and his repentance was known.

And by this chain, he said: 'Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said:' 'There is none upon whom a legal penalty (Hadd) was applicable, so it is established upon him, then he repents, except that his testimony is allowed'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the one who slanders chaste women, whether his testimony is accepted after the legal penalty if he repents? He said: Yes. I said: And what is his repentance? He said: He comes and belies himself in the presence of the Imam and says: 'I had forged [the charge] against so-and-so,' and he repents from what he said.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one subjected to the penal limit (al-mahdud), if he repents, is his testimony accepted? He (peace be upon him) said: When he repents, and his repentance is that he retracts from what he had said, and declares himself a liar in the presence of the Imam and in the presence of the Muslims. So when he does that, then it is upon the Imam to accept his testimony after that.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The testimony of the Muslims is accepted over all the people of the religions, and the testimony of the people of the Dhimma is not accepted against the Muslims.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of the people of the (other) religions. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Not allowed, except against the people of their own religions. So if others cannot be found, their testimony would be allowed upon the bequest, because it is not correct for a right of anyone to go away'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The Jews and the Christians, when they testify, then they become Muslims, their testimonies are accepted.'

Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about the child, the slave, and the Christian who testify with a testimony. So the Christian becomes a Muslim, would his testimony be allowed? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a Christian who testified upon a testimony, then became a Muslim afterwards, would his testimony be allowed? He said: Yes. He is in a position to testify.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'or two others from among others than you'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man is in a land of strangers, not finding a Muslim in it, the testimony of one who is not a Muslim would be allowed upon the bequest.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyoub al-Khazzaz, from Durays al-Kunasi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the testimony of the people of the religions (non-Muslims), is it permissible upon a man from other than their religion? So he (peace be upon him) said: No, except that others cannot be found in that situation. So if others cannot be found, their testimonies are permissible regarding the bequest, because it is not correct for the right of a Muslim person to go away, and his bequest would not be invalidated.

Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Two just persons from among you, or two others from among others than you.' He said: 'Those from among you are Muslims, and those from among others than you are from the People of the Book.' He said: 'That is only when a Muslim man dies in a land of strangers, so he seeks two Muslim men to bear witness to his bequest. But if he cannot find two Muslims, let him have two men from the People of the Book, who are acceptable among their own companions, bear witness to his bequest.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the witnesses should not refuse when they are summoned' [2:282]. So he said: 'It is not befitting for anyone who, when summoned to testify regarding what he has witnessed, to say: I shall not testify for you.'

(Regarding) Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'and the witnesses should not refuse when they are summoned' — so he (AS) said: 'It is not befitting for anyone who is summoned to testify upon something he has witnessed that he should say: I will not testify for you.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (AS) similar to it, and said: 'So that is before the writing (documentation).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And let not the witnesses refuse when they are summoned' [2:282]. So he said: 'When a man summons you to testify for him regarding a debt or a right, it is not befitting for you to hold back from it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, 'and the witnesses should not refuse when they are summoned' he said: 'Before the testimony.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Mada'ini, he said: When you are summoned to the testimony, then answer.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The witnesses must not refuse to answer when they are summoned, before the writing (of the contract).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who testified upon the testimony of another man. So the man came and said, 'I did not appoint him as a witness.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of the more just of the two is valid, but if the more just of the two is only one, his testimony is not valid due to fairness between them.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who testified upon the testimony of another man, so the man came and said, 'I did not appoint him as a witness,' so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of the more just of the two is valid.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the testimony of the blind man, so he said: 'Yes, if it is established/proven.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the blind man, is his testimony accepted? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, if he is established (as competent).

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi from Ja'far ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Husayn ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab was brought Qudama ibn Maz'un, and he had drunk wine. So two men testified against him, one of them was a eunuch (castrated) and he was Amr al-Tameemi, and the other was al-Mu'alla ibn al-Jarud. So one of them testified that he saw him drinking, and the other testified that he saw him vomiting the wine. So Umar sent for some people from the companions of the Messenger of Allah, among them was the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), 'What do you say, O Abu al-Hasan, for you are the one regarding whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: You are the most knowledgeable of this community and its judge with the truth. For these two have differed in their testimonies.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no difference in their testimonies, and he could not have vomited it until he had drunk it.' So he said, 'Is the testimony of the eunuch allowed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The loss of his beard is not except like the loss of some of his limbs.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Al-Hakam ibn Abi Aqeel, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'For me there is an adversary who frequently bears false testimony upon me, and I did not like to compensate him [for his testimony], although I do not know if that is suitable for me or not.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Has it not reached you that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was saying: Do not imprison yourselves and your wealth with false testimonies? For it is not upon a man to restrain himself in his religion, nor is there a sin from his Lord that he should defend that from him, just as if he were to defend by his testimony about an unlawful sexual organ and shedding of unlawful blood, that would be better for him, and similarly is the wealth of the Muslim man.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan that he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who sold his estate to another man, and it was a piece of land, and the boundaries were not defined at the time he called witnesses, and he said, 'When they bring you the boundaries, then bear witness with them.' Is that allowed for him, or is it not allowed for him to testify?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Yes, it is allowed, and the praise is to Allah.' And a man wrote to him who had a piece of land. So he was preparing to depart for Mecca, and the town was a few stages from his house, and he did not bring the boundaries of his land, but he defined the four boundaries of the town. So he said to the witnesses, 'Bear witness that I have sold to so-and-so the entirety of the town, whose one boundary is such-and-such, and the second, and the third, and the fourth.' But rather, for him in this town was only a piece of land. So is that correct for the buyer, when for him was only part of this town, and he acknowledged for him the entirety of it?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is not allowed to sell what one does not own, and the purchase is obligatory upon the seller according to what he owns.' And he wrote, 'Is it allowed for the witness whom he called to witness with the entirety of this town that he testifies with the boundaries of the piece of land which is for him in it, when the boundaries of this piece are recognized by a people from the inhabitants of this town, if they are just?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Yes, they testify upon something understood and known.' And a man wrote, 'A man says to a man, 'Bear witness that the entirety of the house which is for him in such-and-such a place, with all its boundaries, is for so-and-so son of so-and-so, and the entirety of what is for him in the house from the chattels.' Is that correct for the buyer, whatever is in the house from the chattels, which things are they?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is correct for him whatever the purchase encompassed of all that, if Allah wills.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Abu Ayoub from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding four who testified against a married man for adultery, two of them were considered just and the other two were not. He (peace be upon him) said: If they are four Muslims who are not known for false testimony, their testimony is accepted collectively and the legal penalty is established upon the one they testified against. It is upon them to testify with what they saw and knew, and it is upon the ruler to accept their testimony unless they are known for moral corruption.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from one of the Qumis, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) – similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ismail ibn Abi Haneefa, from Abi Haneefa who said: 'I said to Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him): How did it come to be that regarding killing, two witnesses are allowed, and regarding adultery, there are not allowed in it except four witnesses, and killing is more severe than adultery?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because killing is one act, but adultery is two acts, thus it is not allowed except for four witnesses, upon the man two witnesses and upon the woman two witnesses.' And it is reported from one of our companions, from him (Abi Haneefa), who said: 'So he (peace be upon him) said to me: What is with you, O Abi Haneefa?' I said: 'There is nothing with me regarding it except a narration of Umar, that Allah took two words in testimony upon the servants.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'It is not like that, O Abi Haneefa! But, in adultery there are two legal penalties, and it is not allowed except that two should testify upon each one, because the man and the woman both together, upon them both is the legal penalty, while killing is established upon the killer and averted from the killed.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: An unmarried woman was brought to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and they claimed that she had committed adultery. So he ordered the women to look at her, and they said, 'She is a virgin.' So he said, 'I would not whip one upon whom is a seal from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' And he (peace be upon him) used to accept the testimony of women in cases similar to this.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Sa'd al-Iskaaf, who said: 'I do not know him except to say, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):' 'There was a worshipper among the Children of Israel to whom Dawood (peace be upon him) marveled. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "Do not marvel at anything from his affairs, for he is a show-off."' 'So the man died, and they came to Dawood (peace be upon him) and said to him: "The man has died." So Dawood (peace be upon him) said: "Bury your companion." The Children of Israel objected and said: "How is it that you did not attend it?"' 'So when he was washed, fifty men arose and testified by Allah that they knew nothing from him except goodness. So when they prayed over him, fifty others arose and testified by Allah that they knew nothing from him except goodness. And when they buried him, fifty [more] arose and testified by Allah that they knew nothing from him except goodness.' 'So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawood (peace be upon him): "What prevented you from testifying for so-and-so?" Dawood (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, [it was] that which You informed me of, from his affairs."' 'He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "That is so, but a group of Rabbis and Monks have testified that they knew nothing from him except goodness, so I accepted their testimony over him and Forgave him for what was in My Knowledge regarding him."'

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Balad from Sa'd al-Iskaf who said:af who said: I know him to have said from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him): Among the Children of Israel there was a worshipper, so Dawud (peace be upon him) liked him for it. Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, sent revelation to him saying: 'Let not anything in his matter please you, for he is a show-off.' He said: The man died, and Dawud (peace be upon him) was informed, and it was said to him: 'The man has died.' Dawud (peace be upon him) said: 'Bury your companion.' He said: The Children of Israel disapproved and said: 'Why did he not attend (the funeral)?' He said: When he was washed (for burial), fifty men stood up and testified by Allah that they knew of him only good. He said: When they performed the funeral prayer for him, fifty others stood up and testified by Allah that they knew of him only good. When they buried him, fifty (more) stood up and testified by Allah that they knew of him only good. Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, sent revelation to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'What prevented you from testifying (attending the funeral) for so-and-so?' Dawud (peace be upon him) said: 'O my Lord, because of what You revealed to me regarding his matter.' He said: Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, sent revelation to him saying: 'That is so, but a people of learned men and monks have testified that they knew of him only good, so I accepted their testimony regarding him and forgave (overlooked) My knowledge of him.' This is the end of the Book of Testimonimonies from al-Kafi, composed by Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is followed by the Book of Judgments and Rulings, if Allah the Exalted wills.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilah, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever conceals a testimony or testifies with it in order to shed the blood of a Muslim person, or to usurp the wealth of a Muslim person, will come on the Day of Resurrection with darkness on his face extending as far as the eye can see, and on his face will be marks of toil; the creatures will recognize him by his name and his lineage. And whoever testifies with a true testimony in order to revive the right of a Muslim person, will come on the Day of Resurrection with light on his face extending as far as the eye can see; the creatures will recognize him by his name and his lineage.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not see that God, Blessed and Exalted, says: "And establish the testimony for the sake of God"?' [65:2]

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God Mighty and Majestic: 'and whoever conceals it, so he has a sinful heart' — he said: (This applies) after the witnessing.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Khuzai, from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Saie, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: My father wrote in his letter to me, and I asked him about the testimony for them: So establish the testimony for the sake of Allah, even if it be against yourself, or the parents, and the near-relatives, regarding what is between you and them. But if you fear injustice for your brother (in faith), then no (do not testify).
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Ismail ibn Mihran similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man hears testimony but was not called to witness upon it, he has the choice: if he wishes he may testify, and if he wishes he may remain silent. And he said: When he was made to witness it, there would be for him no option except that he testify.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man hears testimony and was not called to witness upon it, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he testifies, and if he wishes, he remains silent.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When a man hears a testimony but was not called to witness upon it, he is free to choose — if he so desires, he may testify, and if he so desires, he may remain silent — except when he knows [the matter involves wrongdoing] from the oppressor, then he must testify, and it is not permissible for him except that he testifies.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar and someone else, from Yunus, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man hears the testimony but was not called as a witness upon it, then he is with the choice: if he desires he testifies, and if he desires he remains silent — except when he knows of an oppressor, then he testifies, and it is not permissible for him not to testify.
When a man hears the testimony, and he was not called as a witness upon it, then he is free to choose: if he desires, he testifies, and if he desires, he remains silent.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who is present at the accounting/settlement of a man, and they (both) seek from him testimony about what he heard from them. He said: That is up to him — if he wishes, he testifies, and if he wishes, he does not testify. Then if he testifies, it would be with the truth of what he heard. And if he does not testify, then there is nothing against him, because the two of them did not make him a witness (beforehand).

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man had me witness a testimony, and I recognize my handwriting and my seal, but I do not remember anything from the remainder, neither little nor much.' He (the narrator) said: So he said to me: 'If your companion was trustworthy and there is with you a trustworthy man, then testify for him.'

Ja'far ibn 'Isa wrote to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Neighbors of ours came to me with a document, claiming that they had made me a witness to what was in it. In the document is my name in my own handwriting, which I recognized — yet I do not remember the act of testimony. They have summoned me to testify. Shall I testify for them based on my recognition that my name is in the document, even though I do not remember the testimony — or is it not obligatory for me to give testimony for them until I remember it, regardless of whether my name is in the document in my handwriting or not?' So he wrote: 'Do not testify.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Idris ibn al-Hassan, from Ali ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Do not testify with a testimony until you recognise it just as you recognise your palm.'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not testify to a testimony you do not remember, for indeed whoever wishes can write a document and engrave a seal (forging it).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man, from Salih ibn Maytham, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is no man who gives false testimony against the property of a Muslim man in order to dispossess him, except that God writes for him in his place a deed toward the Fire.
The false testifier — his feet do not move until the Fire is made obligatory for him.

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The speech of the false witness does not finish in front of the judge until (immediately) he assumes his seat in the Fire; and likewise is the one who conceals testimony.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one who informed him, from one of the two (peace be upon them both) regarding the witnesses: when they testify against a man and then retract from their testimonies, and the judgement has already been passed upon the man, they are held responsible for what they testified with and are fined However, if the judgement has not yet been passed, their testimonies are dismissed and the witnesses are not fined anything.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the false testifier: 'What is his repentance?' He said: 'He pays from the wealth concerning which he testified against [the victim], in proportion to what was taken from his wealth — whether it was the half or the third — if this one testified and another one was with him.'

Regarding the false testifier, he said: If the thing remains intact exactly as it was, it is returned to its owner; and if it no longer remains intact, he is liable for the measure of what was destroyed from the wealth of the man.

Four witnesses testified against a married man (muhsan) for adultery (zina), then one of them retracted after the man was killed. He said: If the fourth witness says 'I was mistaken', he is to be lashed the legal penalty (hadd) and fined the blood money (diya); but if he says 'I did it deliberately', he is to be killed.

Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Nu'aym al-Azdi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about four witnesses who testified against a man for adultery. So when he was killed, one of them retracted from his testimony. He said: So he (the Imam) said: The fourth shall be killed, and the three shall pay to his family three-quarters of the blood money (diya).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding false testimony: 'If the thing remains exactly as it was, it shall be returned to its owner; otherwise he is liable to the measure of what was destroyed from the man's property.'

Regarding two witnesses who testified against a woman that her husband had divorced her, and so she remarried, then her husband came and denied the divorce — he said: 'They shall both be given the legal penalty (hadd), and both shall be liable for the dowry (mahr) to the husband. Then she shall observe the waiting period ('iddah), then return to her first husband.'

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a man against whom two witnesses testified that he had committed theft. So his hand was cut. But then afterwards, the two witnesses came forward with another man and said, 'This is the thief, not the one whose hand you cut — we only confused that one with this one.' So he (peace be upon him) ruled against them both, imposing upon them both a fine of half the blood-money (diya), and did not allow their testimony against the other man.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ali (peace be upon him) used to allow, regarding debt, the testimony of one man and the oath of the claimant.
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father narrated to me that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) judged with a witness and an oath.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a right owed to him by another man and he has one witness. He said: So he (the Imam) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to judge with one witness and the oath of the holder of the right, and that is in the matter of debt.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to judge with one witness along with an oath from the owner of the right.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: Al-Hakm ibn Utayba and Salama ibn Kuhayl came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him about a single witness and an oath. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ruled by it, and Ali (peace be upon him) ruled by it in your presence in Kufa. They both said: This is contrary to the Quran! He said: And where did you find it to be contrary to the Quran? They both said: God, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'And call to witness two men of justice from among you'. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to both of them: Does His saying 'and call to witness two men of justice from among you' mean that you should not accept the testimony of one and an oath? Then he said: Ali (peace be upon him) was seated in the Mosque of Kufa, when Abdullah ibn Qufl al-Tamimi passed by him carrying the shield of Talha. So Ali (peace be upon him) said: This is the shield of Talha — it was taken as stolen war-booty on the day of Basra. So Abdullah ibn Qufl said to him: Appoint between me and you your judge, the one whom you have approved for the Muslims. So he appointed Shurayh between himself and him. Ali (peace be upon him) said: This is the shield of Talha — it was taken as stolen war-booty on the day of Basra. Shurayh said to him: Bring proof for what you are saying. So he brought al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who testified that it was the shield of Talha taken as stolen war-booty on the day of Basra. Shurayh said: This is one witness, and I will not judge based on the testimony of one witness until there is another with him. Then he called Qanbar, who testified that it was the shield of Talha taken as stolen war-booty on the day of Basra. Shurayh said: This is a slave, and I will not judge based on the testimony of a slave. He said: So Ali (peace be upon him) became angry and said: Take it! For this one has judged unjustly three times. He said: So Shurayh turned around and then said: I will not judge between two until you inform me from where I judged unjustly three times. So he said to him: Woe to you! — or fie upon you! — When I informed you that it was the shield of Talha taken as stolen war-booty on the day of Basra, and you said: Bring proof for what you are saying — while the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Wherever stolen war

Some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: The reliable one narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: When two women testify for the owner of the right, along with his oath, then it is permissible.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the testimony of women together with the oath of the claimant regarding a debt — he swears by God that his claim is indeed valid.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to permit regarding (a dispute over) a debt: the testimony of one man and the oath of the owner of the debt. But regarding the (sighting of the) new moon, he would not permit it except with two just witnesses.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, both together from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man said to him, 'What is your view — if I see something in a man's hands, is it permissible for me to testify that it belongs to him?' He said: 'Yes.' The man said, 'I can testify that it is in his hand, but I cannot testify that it belongs to him, for perhaps it belongs to someone else.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Is it then permissible to buy it from him?' He said, 'Yes.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'But perhaps it belongs to someone else — so from where is it permissible for you to buy it and have ownership transfer to you, then after acquiring ownership say «it is mine» and swear an oath over it, yet not be permitted to attribute it to the one from whom its ownership came to you?' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If this were not permissible, no market would be established for the Muslims.'

I said to him (peace be upon him): 'Ibn Abi Layla asks me to testify that this is the house in which a certain person died and left as his inheritance, and that there is no heir for him other than the one for whom we have testified.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Testify with what is in your knowledge.' I said: 'Ibn Abi Layla makes us swear the al-ghamus oath.' He said: 'Swear — it is only based on your knowledge.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — he said: I said: 'There happens to be a testimony with me for a man from my brethren, and the judges among us do not accept all of it.' He said: 'So when you know that it is true, then correct it by every means until his right is established for him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man happens to be in his house, then he is absent from it for thirty years, and he leaves his family in it. Then news of his death comes to us, and we do not know what occurred in his house, nor do we know what occurred for him in terms of children — we only know that we are not aware that he made any change in his house, nor that any child was born to him, and this house should not be divided among his heirs whom he left in the house until two just witnesses testify that this is the house of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, who died and left it as an inheritance between so-and-so and so-and-so. Should we testify to this?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'A man has a slave and a slave-girl, and he says: "My slave has absconded and my slave-girl has absconded." They are found in the city, and the judge requires of him proof that this is the slave of so-and-so, who was neither sold nor gifted. Should we testify to this when we are required to do so, while we do not know if any change has occurred?' He said: 'Whenever the slave or slave-girl of a Muslim is absent from his hand, or is absent from you, do not testify about it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Fear the governance, for the governance is but for the Imam who is knowledgeable in just judgement among the Muslims — for a Prophet or the successor of a Prophet.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jamila, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Shurayh: 'O Shurayh! You have taken a seat that none sits in except a Prophet, a successor of a Prophet, or a wretch (oppressor).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace of God be upon him) appointed Shurayh as the judge, he stipulated upon him that he would not enforce any judgement until he had first presented it to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I judge among you based on proofs and oaths, and some of you are more eloquent in presenting their argument than others. So whoever I award a portion of his brother's wealth, I am merely giving him a piece of Hellfire.'

Ali, from his father, from one of his companions, from Asim ibn companions, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A Prophet from the Prophets complained to his Lord: 'How can I judge in matters in which I have not been informed of their explanation?' He said, so He said to him: 'Refer them to Me, and add them to My Name to swear by.'

And from him, from Al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), that a Prophet from the Prophets complained to his Lord, saying: 'O Lord! How can I judge regarding what I did not witness and did not see?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Judge between them by My Book, and add them to My Name, so make them swear by it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is for the one for whom a clear proof cannot be established.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Jamil and Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The proof is upon the one who claims, and the oath is upon the one who is claimed against.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah judged regarding your blood with a different ruling than what He judged regarding your wealth. He judged regarding your wealth that the proof is upon the claimant and the oath is upon the defendant; and He judged regarding your blood that the proof is upon the one against whom it is claimed and the oath is upon the one who claims, so that the blood of a Muslim man is not invalidated.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) regarding the man who claims and has no proof for him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is made to swear an oath, so if he turns the oath upon the owner of the right, and he does not swear, then there is no right for him.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayn, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who is claimed against (defendant), and there is no proof for the claimant. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Either he swears an oath or he turns the oath to be upon the owner of the right. So if he does not do it, so there is no right for him'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who reported it, he said: The extraction of rights is by four ways: by the testimony of two just men; so if there are not two just men, then one man and two women. So if there are not two women, then one man and the oath of the claimant. So if there is no witness, then the oath is upon the defendant.
