So if he does not swear, and returns the oath to the claimant, then it is obligatory upon him to swear and take his right. But if he refuses to swear, then there is nothing for him.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the man who is claimed against for a right, and there is no proof for the owner of the right: He said: The defendant is sworn an oath. So if he refuses to swear and says, 'I turn the oath upon you,' to the owner of the right, then that is obligatory upon the owner of the right that he swears and takes his wealth.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The oath is returned to the claimant.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Nuymari, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the owner of the right is pleased with the oath of the denier regarding his right, so he makes him swear, and he swears that there is no right for him against him, the oath removes the right of the claimant, so there is no claim for him. I said to him, 'And if there was just proof over it?' He said, 'Yes, and even if he establishes after what he made him swear by Allah, fifty oaths, it would not be for him, and the oath had invalidated everything he had claimed before it, from what had been sworn against him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Khadir al-Nakha'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who has a debt due from another man, and the debtor denies it: He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the creditor asks him to swear an oath, it is not for him (the creditor) to take anything (if he swears); and if he leaves it and does not ask him to swear, then he (the creditor) is upon his right (to claim the debt).'

Ali, from his father, from Abdul Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hameed, from one Hameed, from one of his companions, regarding the man who has wealth due from another man. He denies it, so he swears an oath of patience (yamin sabr) to him. Is there anything due from him? He (peace be upon him) said: It is not for him to seek it from him, and similarly, if he reckons it with Allah (waives it), it is not for him to seek it from him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who came to a group of people and claimed a house that was in their possession, and the one in whose hand the house was established the proof that he had inherited it from his father, and it was not known how its matter was. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one with the most proof is made to swear an oath, and it is handed over to him.' And he (peace be upon him) mentioned that a group of people came to Ali (peace be upon him) disputing over a mule. So the proof was established for these ones that they had bred it in their stable, and neither had they sold it nor had they gifted it; and those ones established the proof that they had bred it in their stable, and neither had they sold it nor gifted it. So he (peace be upon him) judged by it based upon the one with the most proof, and made them swear an oath. He (the narrator) said, 'So I asked him (peace be upon him) at that time, 'What is your view if the one who claimed the house...?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the father of the one who was in it acquired it without a price, and the one who was in it cannot establish proof except that he inherited it from his father?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If its matter is like that, then it is for the one who claims it and establishes the proof for it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Khashab from Ghiyas ibn Kalub from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) That two men disputed before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding an animal which was in both their hands, and each one of them established the proof that it had been established the evidence that it had been bred in his presence, so 'Ali (peace be upon him) made them both swear an oath, so one of them swore and the other refused to swear, so he judged it for the one who swore. So it was said to him, 'And if it were not in the hand of either of them and they both established the proof?' He said: 'I would make them both swear, so whichever of the two swears and the other shirks, I would give it to the one who swore. And if they both swear, I would give it between them as two halves.' It was said, 'And if it was in the hand of one of them and they both established the proof?' He said: 'I would judge it for the one who swore, in whose hand it is.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa' from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Ali (peace be upon him), when two men came to him with witnesses, their justice being equal and their number equal, would draw lots between them to see upon which of them the oath would fall. He said: And he would say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, whichever of them had the right, grant it to him.' Then he would assign the right to the one to whom the lot fell, when he swore the oath.

From him, from Mulla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding two witnesses who testified upon one matter, and two others came and testified upon other than which they had testified, and they differed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Lots would be drawn between them, so whoever the lot comes out to for the swearing of the oath, he is the first to be judged for [the claim].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man had two witnesses testify for him that he had fifty dirhams with a man, and two others came and testified that he had one hundred dirhams with him; all of them testified in one standing. He (peace be upon him) said: Cast lots among them, then make those upon whom the lot fell swear by Allah that they are swearing with the truth.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawood ibn Abu Yazeed al-Attar, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding a man who had a wife, a man came with witnesses that this woman is the wife of so-and-so, and others came and testified that she is the wife of so-and-so. The witnesses were all just and deemed reliable. He (peace be upon him) said: A lot is drawn between the witnesses; whoever's lot comes out, he is the rightful one, and he is the first to have the right to her.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, who raised it (as marfu') from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The judges are four: three are in the Fire and one is in Paradise — a man who judges with injustice and he knows, so he is in the Fire; a man who judges with injustice and he does not know, so he is in the Fire; a man who judges with the truth and he does not know, so he is in the Fire; and a man who judges with the truth and he does know, so he is in Paradise. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Judgment is of two kinds — the judgment of God and the judgment of Jahiliyya. So whoever errs in the judgment of God has judged by the judgment of Jahiliyya'.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The judgements are two judgements — a Judgement of God and a judgement of ignorance (Jahiliyya). And indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, has said: And who is better than God to judge for a people who are certain? And bear witness against Zayd ibn Thabit — indeed he judged in matters of obligatory inheritance according to the judgement of ignorance.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba, from Sabbah al-Azraq, from Hakam al-Hannat, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Hakam from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — they both said: 'Whoever judges regarding two dirhams by other than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed, from among those who have a whip or a staff (i.e., hold ruling authority), then he is a disbeliever in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever judges in a matter involving two dirhams by other than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed, is a disbeliever in Allah the Great.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, who traced it back (marfu'): He said, The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever judges in a matter of two dirhams with an unjust ruling and then compels [acceptance of] it would be among the people of this verse: "and whoever did not judge by what God revealed, those are the disbelievers" [Quran 5:44] So I said: 'And how does he compel [acceptance of] it?' So he said: 'He would have a whip and a prison, so he judges over it. If [the aggrieved party] accepts his ruling, [well and good]; otherwise he strikes them with his whip and imprisons them in his prison.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whichever judge judges between two (parties) and errs, he falls from further than the sky.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Dawud ibn Farqad who said: a man narrated to me from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Khudayb al-Bajali who said: I was accompanying Ibn Abi Layla as his traveling companion until we came to Medina. While we were in the mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) entered. I said to Ibn Abi Layla, Shall we go to him? He said, And what shall we do in his presence? I said, We would ask him and converse with him. He said, Arise. So we arose and went to him. He asked me about myself and my family, then said: Who is this with you? I said, Ibn Abi Layla, the judge of the Muslims. He said to him: Are you Ibn Abi Layla, the judge of the Muslims? He said, Yes. He (peace be upon him) said: You take the wealth of this one and give it to that one, and you execute, and you separate husband from wife, fearing no one in that? He said, Yes. He said: So by what do you judge? He said, By what has reached me from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and from Ali (peace be upon him), and from Abu Bakr and Umar. He said: Has it reached you from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: Verily Ali (peace be upon him) is the most judicious among you? He said, Yes. He said: Then how do you judge by other than the judgment of Ali (peace be upon him) when this has reached you? So what will you say when they bring a land of silver and a sky of silver, then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) takes your hand and stands you before your Lord, saying: O Lord! This one judged by other than what I judged! He said: So the face of Ibn Abi Layla turned pale until it became like saffron. Then he said to me, Find yourself another traveling companion. By Allah, I shall never speak a single word to you from my own head, ever.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was seated in the circle of Rabi'ah al-Ra'y. A Bedouin came and asked Rabi'ah al-Ra'y about a legal question, and he answered him. When he fell silent, the Bedouin said to him: 'Is it upon your neck?' So Rabi'ah was silent and did not reply anything to him. Then he repeated the question and he answered with the like of that. The Bedouin said: 'Is it upon your neck?' So Rabi'ah was silent. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'It is upon his neck, or he should not say it; and every mufti is liable.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubayda, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Whoever issues fatwas to the people without knowledge and without guidance from God — the Angels of Mercy and the Angels of Punishment curse him, and the burden of sin of those who acted by his fatwa attaches to him.

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a judge serving between two towns who takes livelihood from the ruling authority in exchange for his judgements. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is the ill-gotten (forbidden).'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Bribery in judgment is disbelief in God.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazid ibn Farqad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-suht (forbidden earnings). So he said: It is bribery in judgment.
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hand of God is above the head of the ruler, hovering with mercy. So when he acts unjustly, God leaves him to himself.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: There used to be among the Children of Israel a judge who used to judge with the truth among them. When death came to him, he said to his wife: 'When I die, wash me, shroud me, place me on my bed, and cover my face — for you will not see evil.' When he died, she did that and remained thus for a while. Then she uncovered his face in order to look at him, and behold there was a worm gnawing at his nostril! She was terrified by that. When night came, he appeared to her in her dream and said to her: 'Did what you saw terrify you?' She said: 'Yes, I was indeed terrified.' So he said to her: 'Know that if you were frightened, that which you saw was nothing but because of your brother, so-and-so. He came to me with an adversary of his. When they both sat before me, I said: O Allah, make the right be for him and direct the judgment against his companion! When they disputed before me, the right was indeed with him and I saw that clearly in the case — so I directed the judgment in his favor against his companion. Thus what you saw struck me, because of where my desire was — even though it was in agreement with the truth.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whichever believer proceeds with a believer regarding a dispute to a judge or a tyrannous ruler, so he judges against him with other than the judgment of God, then he has indeed become his partner in sin.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Hariz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Whichever man who has a dispute with a (believing) brother of his regarding a right, and then invites him to a man from his (believing) brethren to judge between them, but he refuses — except to have the matter raised to those (unjust judges) — he is at the status of those about whom God Mighty and Majestic said: 'Have you not seen those who allege that they believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They desire to seek judgment from the taghut, though they were commanded to deny it' — the Verse.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): [What is the meaning of] the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: 'And do not consume your property among yourselves by false means, and present it to the judges' So he said: O Abu Basir! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has known that in the community there are judges who are tyrannous. Indeed, He did not mean the judges of the people of justice, but He meant the judges of the people of tyranny. O Abu Muhammad! If there were a right for you against a man, and you summoned him to the judges of the people of justice, but he refused you unless you took the matter to the judges of the people of tyranny so that they judge in his favor — he would be among those who sought judgment from the taghut. And this is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Have you not seen those who allege that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They desire to seek judgment from the taghut.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Beware of taking each other for judgement to the people of injustice. But look for a man from among you who knows something of our rulings, then make him the arbiter between you — for I have indeed appointed him as a judge — so bring your disputes to him.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Umar ibn Hanzala who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two men from our companions who had a dispute between them regarding a debt or inheritance, and they both sought judgment from the Sultan (ruling authority) or the judges. Is that permissible? So he said: Whoever seeks judgment from the Taghut and it rules in his favor, then he has only taken ill-gotten gains, even if his right was proven — because he accepted it by the ruling of the Taghut, and God has commanded that it be denied. I said: How should they both proceed? He said: They should seek out the one among you who has narrated our hadiths, has studied our permissibles and our forbidden, and knows our rulings. Then accept him as an arbitrator, for I have indeed appointed him as a judge over you. And when he judges by our ruling and it is not accepted from him, then it is God's judgment that has been treated with contempt and against us has been the rejection — and the one who rejects us is the one who rejects God, and he is at the boundary of associating partners with God.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said: I heard Ali (may the blessings of God be upon him) saying to Shurayh: Look to the people of evasion and delay, who withhold the rights of people — from among the wealthy and affluent — those who contest the (payment of) Muslims' property before the judges. So take the people's rights from them and sell their real estate and houses for it. For I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him and his family) saying: 'The delay of the affluent Muslim is injustice to the Muslim. And the one who has no real estate, no house, and no wealth — there is no way against him.' And know that none can lead people to the truth except the one who restrains them from falsehood. Then treat the Muslims equitably with your countenance, your speech, and your assembly, so that your close ones do not covet your injustice, and your enemies do not despair of your justice. And return the oath to the claimant alongside proof, for that is clearer against obscurity and more established in judgment. And know that Muslims are upright witnesses for one another except: one who has been lashed for a hadd penalty and has not repented therefrom, or one known for bearing false witness, or one who is under suspicion. And beware of expressing annoyance and displeasure in the judicial assembly, in which God has made the reward obligatory and beautified the treasure for the one who judges with truth. And know that reconciliation is permissible between Muslims, except a reconciliation that forbids the permissible or permits the forbidden. And set a time limit for the one claiming absent witnesses between the two parties; if he produces them, take his right for him, and if he does not produce them, enforce the judgment against him. Therefore, beware of executing a judgment regarding retaliation, or a hadd from the limits of God, or a right from the rights of Muslims, until you present that to me, God willing. And do not sit in the judicial assembly until you have eaten.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Whoever is involved in adjudication, let him not judge while he is angry.
He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is entrusted with judging, let him be equitable between them in his gestures, his gaze, and his seating.'

A man lodged with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and remained with him for days. Then he came to him regarding a dispute which he had not mentioned to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Are you a claimant?' He said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You must move out from us, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that a claimant be entertained as a guest unless his opponent is with him.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Shurayh: 'Do not whisper privately to anyone in your gathering, and if you become angry, then arise, and do not issue a judgment while you are angry.' He (the narrator) said: And Abu Abdillah (blessings of God be upon him) said: 'The tongue of a judge is behind his heart — if it is in his favor, he speaks; and if it is against him, he remains silent.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from one who heard it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'When a judge says to the one on his right and to the one on his left, "What is your view? What do you say?" — upon such a one is the curse of Allah, and the angels, and all the people. Why does he not arise from his seat and seat them in his own place?'
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not swear by Allah, neither truthfully nor falsely,' 'for indeed He, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And do not make Allah an excuse for your oaths."'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever holds God in such reverence that he does not swear by Him, God gives him better than what would have gone from him.

The disciples gathered to Isa (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'O teacher of goodness, guide us aright.' So he said to them: 'Musa, the Prophet of God, ordered you that you should not swear by God as liars, and I order you that you should not swear by God, neither as liars nor as truthful ones.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Sallam al-Muta'abbid, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to Sudeyr: O Sudeyr! Whoever swears by Allah falsely has disbelieved, and whoever swears by Allah truthfully has sinned. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And do not make Allah an obstacle for your swearing of oaths' [2:224].

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to me that his father — there was in his presence a woman from the Kharijites, I believe he said from the Clan of Hanifa. So a slave of his said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of God! In your presence is a woman who disavows your grandfather.' So it was decided for my father that he divorce her. Then she claimed her dower against him, and brought him before the Emir of Medina seeking his aid. So the Emir of Medina said to him: 'O Ali! Either you swear an oath, or you give her her right.' So he said to me: 'Arise, my son, and give her four hundred dinars.' So I said to him: 'O Father! May I be sacrificed for you! Are you not in the right?' He said: 'Yes, my son. But I held God in too high esteem to swear by Him a forced oath.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When wealth is claimed against you and there is no right of his upon you, and he intends to make you swear an oath — if it reaches the amount of thirty dirhams, give it to him and do not swear an oath; and if it is more than that, swear an oath and do not give it to him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: He was asked about what is permissible and what is not permissible regarding the intention by concealment (in the heart) in an oath. He said: It is permissible in one case and not permissible in another. As for what is permissible: when one is the oppressed party, whatever he swears with and intends for the oath is upon his intention. And as for when he is the oppressor, the oath is upon the intention of the oppressed party.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who swore an oath while his inner intention was upon something other than what he had sworn. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The oath is upon the inner intention.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who swears, and his inner intention (conscience) is upon something other than what he swore upon. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The oath is upon the inner intention (conscience).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man must not swear an oath except based upon his knowledge.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Khalid ibn Ayman al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man is not made to swear an oath except upon what is based upon his knowledge.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The man must not swear an oath except based upon his knowledge.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The man is not made to swear an oath except based upon his knowledge, and the oath does not take effect except upon the knowledge, whether he has been made to swear or not.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Every oath you swear upon, in which there is benefit for you regarding a matter of religion or the world, so there is no expiation upon you regarding it. And rather, the expiation falls upon you regarding what you swore upon, which is disobedience to Allah, that you do not do it, then you do it.

From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Not every oath requires an expiation. As for what is obligatory upon you to do, and you swear not to do it, then you do it, there is no expiation upon you for it; and as for what is not obligatory upon you to do, and you swear not to do it, then you do it, then upon you is the expiation for it.'

From him, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Humran, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The oath that necessitates expiation upon me.' So they both said: 'Whatever you swore upon, from what is obedience to Allah therein, if you were to do it but did not do it, then upon you is the expiation regarding it; and whatever you swore upon, from what is disobedience to Allah therein, then its expiation is leaving it; and whatever does not contain disobedience nor obedience, then it is nothing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said: I asked him about what necessitates expiation from oaths. He said: 'Whatever was obligatory upon you to do, and you swore not to do it, then you did it, there is nothing upon you when you do it; and whatever was not obligatory upon you to do, and you swore not to do it, then you did it, upon you is the expiation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Ibn Mukan, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which is the thing in which is the expiation from the oaths?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever you swear upon from what is the righteousness therein, so upon is the expiation when you do not fulfill it; and whatever you swear upon from what is the disobedience therein, so there is not expiation upon you regarding it when you retract from it; and whatever was besides that from what therein is neither a righteousness nor a disobedience, so it is not with anything'.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about the man who swears to another man regarding food, telling him to eat, but he does not eat it. Is there expiation upon him for that? And what is the oath in which expiation is obligatory? He said: The expiation is for the one who swears regarding chattels that he will not sell them or buy them, then it becomes apparent to him [to do the opposite], so he expiates for his oath. And if he swears regarding something, and doing it is better than leaving it, let him do that which is better, and there is no expiation upon him. That is merely from the footsteps of Satan.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Falah ibn Ayyub, from Al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about oaths, vows, and the oath that is for Allah's obedience. He said: 'Whatever is made for Allah in obedience, let it be fulfilled. If something from that is made for Allah, then he does not do it, let him expiate his oath. And as for what was an oath in disobedience, it is of no consequence.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, both together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Every oath upon which a man swears that he will not do it, from what has benefit for him in this world and the Hereafter, there is no expiation upon him. And rather, the expiation is when a man swears, 'By Allah I will not commit adultery,' 'By Allah I will not drink wine,' 'By Allah I will not steal,' 'By Allah I will not be treacherous,' and the like of this, 'I will not disobey,' then he does it, so upon him is the expiation with regards to it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah, and he narrated to us from the one who mentioned him, from Maysara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The oath upon which expiation becomes obligatory is that which was obligatory upon you to do, so you swore that you would not do it, and then you did it; so there is nothing upon you, because your deed is obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And that which was obligatory upon you not to do, so you swore that you would not do it, and then you did it; so upon you is the expiation.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jameela al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Muhammad al-Halbi, and Zurara, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And remember your Lord when you forget.' He said: 'When a man swears and forgets to make a condition (Insha-Allah), let him make the condition when he remembers.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And remember your Lord when you forget'. He said: 'That is regarding the oath, when you say, 'By Allah, I will not do such and such'. So when you remember that you did not make an exclusion, then say, 'If Allah wills'.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn Al-Qalanisi, or one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The servant may make an exception in his oath for a period between it and forty days, if he forgets.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever makes an exception in an oath, there is no breaking (of the oath) and no expiation.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The exception (istithna') in an oath is valid whenever it is remembered, even if it is after forty mornings.' Then he recited this Verse: 'And remember your Lord when you forget.'

Ali, from his father, by his chain, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever swears secretly, let him make his exception secretly, and whoever swears publicly, let him make his exception publicly.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Husayn ibn Zurara, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And remember your Lord when you forget' [18:24]. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you swear an oath and forget to make an exception (by saying 'If Allah wills'), then make the exception when you remember.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I do not see that a man should swear except by Allah. As for the man's saying, 'No, by your adversary!', it is from the speech of the people of Ignorance, and if the man were to swear by this and its like, he would have neglected swearing by Allah. As for the man's saying, 'Ya Hayah and Ya Hanah', that is merely for seeking the name, and I do not see any harm in it. And as for his saying, 'La amr Allah' and his saying, 'La hahu', that is indeed by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I do not see for the man that he should swear except by Allah. And he said: The words of the man when he says 'No, by your adversary!', rather it is from the words of the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance. And if the people were to swear by this, and the likes of it, it would neglect the swearing by Allah.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So do not swear by the places of the stars,' that: 'It was the people of ignorance who used to swear by it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: So do not swear by the places of the stars He (peace be upon him) said: 'The matter of the one who swears by it is great.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the people of ignorance used to revere the Sacred Month (al-Muharram) and did not swear by it, nor by the month of Rajab, nor did they violate the sanctity of anyone who was traveling or returning during these two months, even if he had killed his father, nor for anything would they expel from the Sanctuary any beast, or sheep, or camel, or other than that.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'I swear by this city, and you are a dweller of this city.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So it reached from their ignorance that they permitted the killing of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), while they revered the days of the month where they were swearing by it, so they would fulfill it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marar, from Yunus, from one of our companions, who said: I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So do not swear by the places of the stars.' He said: 'I consider it a great sin for the one who swears by it.' And the people of the Pre-Islamic period revered the Sanctuary (Mecca) and did not swear by it, permitting the sanctity of Allah within it, and did not expel an animal from it. So Allah, Blessed and High, said: 'Indeed! I swear by this city, And you are a dweller of this city, And father and son.' They revered the city if they were to swear by it, and they permitted in it the violation of the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about whether the people of the religions (Ahl al-Kitab) are to be made to swear an oath, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not make them swear except by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Is it permissible for anyone to make someone from the Jews, Christians, and Magians swear by their gods?' He said, 'It is not permissible for anyone to make someone swear except by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) made a Jew swear by the Torah which was revealed to Moses (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Jews, the Christians, and the Magians are not sworn (in oaths) by other than Allah. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Therefore judge between them by what Allah has Revealed.'

From him, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: 'Do not make (anyone) swear by other than Allah.' And he said: 'Make the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian swear by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Halbi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the expiation for an oath, he should feed ten poor people; for each poor person, a mud of wheat or a mud of flour and a handful, or their clothing, for each person two garments, or freeing a slave. He has the choice among these three; whichever of the three he does. If he is unable to do any one of the three, then fasting is upon him for three days.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I asked him about the expiation for an oath, in the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but whosoever cannot find (means) then fasting for three days.' What is the limit of the one who does not find? And if a man is asked about what is in his hand, and he finds it? He said: 'When there is no excess with him beyond the livelihood of his family, then he is from those who do not find.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the expiation for an oath, so he said: Freeing a slave, or clothing, and the clothing is two garments, or feeding ten poor people; whichever of these he does, it suffices for him. If he cannot find [the means], then fasting three consecutive days, and feeding ten poor people, a handful, a handful.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Regarding the expiation for an oath, it is freeing a slave, or feeding ten poor people from the average of what you feed your family, or clothing them. The average (food) is vinegar and oil, and the higher quality is bread and meat, and the charity is a handful, a handful of wheat for each poor person, and the clothing is two garments. So whoever cannot find (the means), then upon him is fasting. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: 'So whoever cannot find (means), then fasting for three days.'

Ali, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, and Al-Hajjaj, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Ma'mar ibn Umar, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one upon whom clothing is obligated regarding the expiation of an oath. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A garment by which he covers his nakedness.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'out of the food you feed your families with,' he said: It is as it happens; indeed, in the house there is one who eats more than a mud, and among them is one who eats less than a mud, so it is between that. And if you wish, you can make for them a ud'm (side dish/sauce), and the ud'm, its lowest is salt, its average is vinegar and oil, and its highest is meat.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the expiation of the oath, it is a mudd, a mudd from wheat; and a handful, so that the handful is from his wheat (grain) or his oven (bread).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'If one finds for the expiation only one man or two men, then let it be repeated upon them until ten are completed; he gives them [food] today, then gives them [food] tomorrow.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about something from the expiation for an oath, so he said: 'He should fast for three days.' I said, 'He is weak from fasting and is unable (to do it).' He said: 'He should give charity to ten poor people.' I said, 'He is unable to do that.' He said: 'So let him seek forgiveness of Allah and not repeat it, for it is the best of the expiations, and its maximum and its minimum. So let him seek forgiveness of his Lord and display repentance and remorse.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Feeding one child is not sufficient for the expiation of an oath, but rather two children are equivalent to one adult.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The one who has food to give, it is not for him to fast; he should feed ten poor people, a handful, a handful. And the one who cannot find [food], he should fast for three days.

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the average of what one feeds his family. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'What you sustain your dependents with, from the average of that.' I said, 'And what is the average of that?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Vinegar, and oil, and dates, and bread, satiating them with it once.' I said, 'Their clothing?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One garment.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When a man says, 'Upon me is the walking to the House of Allah,' while he is in Ihram for a Hajj, or 'Upon me is such and such an offering,' it is not valid (as a vow) until he says, 'For the sake of Allah, upon me is the walking to His House,' or he says, 'For the sake of Allah, upon me is that I should enter Ihram for a Hajj,' or he says, 'For the sake of Allah, upon me is such and such an offering, if I do not do such and such.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who says, 'Upon me is a vow.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The vow is not binding until he specifies something for the Sake of Allah: a fast, or charity, or an offering, or Hajj.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who says, 'Upon me is a vow.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not binding until he specifies the vow and says, 'Upon me is a fast for Allah,' or he gives charity, or frees a slave, or offers a gift. And if the man says, 'I gift this food,' then this is not binding; rather, the offering is the camel (or livestock).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have made upon myself, as gratitude to Allah, two cycles of prayer which I pray in residence and in travel. Shall I pray these two in travel during the day?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'My father disliked the obligation if a man obligates upon himself.' I said, 'I did not make these two obligatory upon myself for the sake of Allah; rather I made that upon myself to pray these two as gratitude to Allah, and I did not obligate them upon myself. So, can I leave them if I wish?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said: I said to him: A man upon whom was the obligation of the Hajj of Islam, so he intended to perform Hajj. It was said to him: 'Marry, then perform Hajj.' So he said: 'If I marry before I perform Hajj, then my slave is free.' So he married before he performed Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His slave should be freed.' I said: 'He did not intend the Face of Allah by freeing him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a vow in obedience to Allah, and Hajj is more rightful than marriage, and more obligatory upon him than marriage.' I said: 'Suppose Hajj is optional (voluntary)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Even if it is voluntary, it is an obedience to Allah, and he has freed his slave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If you say, 'For the sake of Allah it is upon me', then its expiation is that of an oath.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Bundar, the slave of Idris, wrote: 'O my master! I vowed that I would fast every Saturday. If I do not fast it, what expiation is required of me?' He wrote back, and I read it: 'Do not leave it except due to a valid excuse, and you are not required to fast it during a journey or illness, unless you intended to do so. And if you break the fast from it without a valid excuse, then give charity for the number of each day missed to seven poor people. We ask Allah for success in what He loves and is pleased with.'

And from him, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man made a vow upon himself that if Allah fulfilled his need, he would give in charity with dirhams. So Allah fulfilled his need. He turned the dirhams into gold and directed them to you. Is that allowed, or should he repeat? He (peace be upon him) said: He should repeat.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, similar to it. And he wrote to him, 'O my master! A man vowed to fast on Friday permanently for the remainder of his life. That day coincided with Eid al-Fitr, or Eid al-Adha, or the days of Tashreeq, or travel, or illness. Is the fast of that day upon him, or its fulfillment, or what should he do, O my master?' So he wrote to him, 'Allah has relieved him of fasting on all these days, and he should fast one day in exchange for one day, if Allah wills.' And he wrote to him, asking him, 'O my master! A man vowed to fast a day, and that day coincided with his having relations with his wife. What is upon him regarding the expiation?' So he wrote to him, 'He should fast one day in exchange for one day, and free a believing slave.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the expiation of the vow, so he said: 'The expiation of the vow is the expiation of the oath. And whoever vows an offering (hadyan), upon him is a camel which he should collar, mark, and stop with at Arafat. And whoever vows a 'Juzur' (young camel), he may slaughter it wherever he desires.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man says, 'Upon me is a vow,' and he does not specify anything.' He said: 'A palmful of wheat, whether it is made hard upon him or made difficult.'

From him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who makes fasting obligatory upon himself in a vow, but he is not strong enough (to fast), he said: He should give to the one who fasts on his behalf, for each day, two mudds.

And by this chain, from Abdullah ibn Jundab who said: 'Ubbad ibn Maymoun was asked, and I was present, about a man who made a vow upon himself for fasting, and he wanted to travel to Mecca. So Abdullah ibn Jundab said: 'I heard from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who made a vow upon himself for fasting, and his intention presented itself regarding the visitation of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should go out and not fast during the journey. So when he returns, he fulfills that (fasts the days he missed).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), that he said: Every one who is unable to fulfill a vow he made, his expiation is the expiation of an oath.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rifa'ah and Hafs, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed to walk to the House of Allah barefoot. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him walk, and when he is tired, let him ride.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, [from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him)], said: I asked him about a man who made it upon himself to walk to the House of Allah, and he could not do it. He said: 'He should perform Hajj riding.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who made it upon himself to walk to the House of Allah, but could not do it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him perform Hajj riding.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he was asked about the man who swears with a vow, and his intention in his oath which he had sworn upon is one Dirham or less. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he does not dedicate it for Allah, then it is nothing.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khash'ami, who said: A group was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when a man from the adherents of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) entered, greeted him, sat down, and wept. Then he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I made a vow to Allah that if He healed me from something I feared for myself, I would give in charity all that I own. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, healed me from it, and I have moved my family from my house to a tent among the ruins of the Ansar, and carried all that I own. So I am selling my house and all that I own to give in charity with it.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Go and evaluate your house, all your belongings, and whatever you own at a fair price, and note that. Then take a white parchment and write in it the total of what you have evaluated. Then look to the most reliable person in your eyes, hand over the parchment to him, bequeath to him, and instruct him that if death befalls you, he should sell your house and all that you own and give it in charity on your behalf. Then return to your house and manage your wealth as you were doing, so you and your family eat as you used to eat.' Then consider everything you give in charity from what you are facing, whether in charity, maintaining kinship, or in aspects of righteousness, and write all of that down and count it. When the start of the year comes, go to the man to whom you bequeathed and instruct him to bring the parchment to you. Then write in it the total of what you gave in charity and spent on maintaining kinship or righteousness during that year. Then do that every year until you fulfill for Allah all that you vowed, and your house and wealth remain for you, if Allah wills.' He said, and the man said, 'You have relieved me, O son of the Messenger of Allah! May Allah make me sacrificed for you.'

Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said: My mother had made a vow upon herself; she vowed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding one of her children, concerning something she feared for him, that she would fast the day that came upon her for as long as she lived. So she traveled with us to Mecca, and it became confusing for us regarding her fasting during the journey, so she did not know whether to fast or break her fast. So I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about that, and he said: 'She should not fast during the journey, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has removed His right from her during the journey, and she should fast what she made upon herself.' So I said to him, 'So what is that when she returns, if she leaves that (fasting)?' He said: 'No, I fear that she will see in her child, regarding whom she vowed, some of what she dislikes.'

From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma'a who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A slave girl of mine was pregnant, so I vowed for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that if she gave birth to a boy, I would send him for Hajj or perform Hajj on his behalf.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man vowed for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding a son of his, that if he reached maturity, he would either perform Hajj on his behalf or send him. The father died, and the boy reached maturity afterwards. The boy came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him about that. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that he should perform Hajj on his behalf, from what his father had left.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Imran Al-Armani, from Abdullah ibn Al-Hakam, from Isa ibn Atiyya, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I had vowed not to drink from the milk of my goat, nor eat from its flesh, so I sold it, and with me are its children.' He said, 'Do not drink from their milk, nor eat from their flesh, for they are from her.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal from Uqba ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who had a debt upon him for another man, so the creditor enforced it. The debtor said: 'Every permissible thing upon me becomes prohibited if I remain until I satisfy you.' He left before satisfying him. How should he deal with it, and he does not know the extent of his oath, and there was no specific intention for it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not with anything (i.e., it is not binding).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever is unable to pay the expiation that is obligatory upon him, whether it be fasting, or emancipation, or charity, regarding an oath, or a vow, or killing, or other than that from what is obligatory upon its perpetrator to pay expiation, then seeking forgiveness is an expiation for him, except for the oath of Dhihar. For if he does not find what he expiates with, it is prohibited for him to have intercourse with her, and they are separated, unless the woman is pleased that she remains with him and he does not have intercourse with her.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Zihar, when its perpetrator is unable to perform the expiation, let him seek forgiveness from his Lord and intend not to repeat it before he copulates. Then let him copulate, and that will suffice for him as the expiation. So when he finds the means to what expiates, on a day from the days, let him expiate. And if he gives charity and feeds himself and his family, that suffices for him if he is needy. And if he does not find that, let him seek forgiveness from his Lord and intend not to repeat it; that suffices for him, and by Allah, it is an expiation.

Muhammad ibn Yahya said, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), 'A man swore by disavowal from Allah and from His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), then he reneged. What is his repentance and his expiation?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should feed ten poor people, for each poor person a handful, and he should seek forgiveness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever swears and says, "No, by the Lord of the Book," and then breaks his oath, upon him is one expiation.'

And by his chain, he said, Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) was asked, 'Can one feed the poor with regards to an expiation, the flesh of the sacrifice?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because it is an offering for Allah.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man has an oath upon him, so his creditor makes him swear with the harsh oath that he cannot leave the city except by letting him know.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He should not go out until he lets him know.' I said, 'If he lets him know, he will not let him go.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If his letting him know is harmful to him and to his family, then let him go out, and there is nothing upon him (no expiation).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ala'a the seller of As-Sabiriyyah, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman who entrusted a man with wealth. When death approached her, she said to him, 'The wealth that I gave to you is for so-and-so woman.' The woman died, and her guardians came to the man and said to him, 'There was wealth for our companion, and we do not see it except with you, so swear to us that there is nothing for us with you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she was trusted (reliable) in his presence, let him swear; and if she was suspected (unreliable) in his presence, he should not swear, and he should place the matter upon what it was. Indeed, for her from her wealth is one-third.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hafs, and one or more of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: He was asked about the man who swears by his brother. He said: 'There is nothing upon him; he merely intended to honour him'.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who copulated with his wife while she was menstruating. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he had copulated with her during the beginning of the blood, let him seek the Forgiveness of Allah, and let him give in charity to seven persons from the Believers in a measurement of a provision for each man among them for his day, and he should not repeat. And if he had copulated with her at the declining of the blood, during the end of her days, before the washing, so there is nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn Suqat, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which thing is [such that] there is no vow regarding a disobedience?' He said, 'Everything in which there is benefit for you in religion or in the world, so there is no reneging upon you in it.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Ibn Abi Umeyr, both together, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the man who performs Zihaar from his wife: Is the emancipation of a newborn slave permissible in the expiation? He said: Every emancipation is permissible in which is the newborn, except in the expiation for killing, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'So free a believing slave,' meaning by that one who has accepted (Islam) who has reached the age of discretion.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), regarding a man who made it upon himself to free a slave, and he freed a lame [or] a paralytic. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was from what is being sold, it would suffice for him, except if he had specified [a particular slave], so upon him would be what he had stipulated and specified.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) regarding a man who swears in dissimulation (taqiyyah). He (peace be upon him) said: If you fear for your wealth and your life, then swear to repel it with your oath. But if you see that this does not repel anything, then do not swear for them.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a man to whom it was said, 'You did such and such', and he said, 'No, by Allah, I did not do it', although he had indeed done it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A lie is what he has lied; he should seek forgiveness from Allah for it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Nawfali, from Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: From the oaths of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was: 'No, and I seek forgiveness of Allah.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, mentioned it, saying: When Al-Mutawakkil was bitten (by a snake), he vowed that if he was healed, he would give a large amount of wealth in charity. When he was healed, he asked the jurists about the limit of 'a large amount', so they differed regarding it. Some of them said 'one hundred thousand', and some of them said 'ten thousand'. They gave differing opinions about it, so the matter became confused for him. So a man from his courtiers, called Saf'an, said, 'Why don't you send to this blackie to ask him?' Al-Mutawakkil said to him, 'Whom do you mean, woe be unto you!' He said to him, 'Ibn al-Rida.' He said to him, 'And is he better than this thing?' He said, 'If he takes you out of this dilemma, then such and such is for me upon you, or else whip me one hundred lashes.' Al-Mutawakkil said, 'I am pleased. O Ja'far ibn Mahmoud, go to him and ask him about the limit of 'a large amount'. So Ja'far ibn Mahmoud went to Abu Al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) and asked him about the limit of 'a large amount'. He said, 'The large amount is eighty.' Ja'far said to him, 'O my master, he will ask me about the reason for it.' Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Certainly, Allah helped you in many places" - so we counted those places and they were eighty.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Ya'qub al-Ahmar who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever swears an oath while he knows that he is a liar has indeed challenged God, Mighty and Majestic.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The rash, immoral oath leaves homes desolate.'

Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uthman ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Furat, maternal uncle of Abu Ammar al-Sayrafi, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beware of the wicked oath, for it leaves homes deserted of their inhabitants.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan, from Fuleyh ibn Abi Bakr al-Shaybani, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The constrained false oath bequeaths poverty to the descendants.'

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed God has an angel whose feet are in the lowest earth — a journey of five hundred years — and his head is in the highest heaven — a journey of a thousand years — saying: 'Glory be to You! Glory be to You, wherever You are! How great are You!' He said: Then God, Mighty and Majestic, reveals to him: 'He does not know that, the one who swears falsely by Me.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the impatient false oath leaves the houses deserted.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Hammad, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The false oath (al-yamin al-ghamoos) — calamities are awaited with it for forty nights.
The calamitous oath (al-yameen al-ghamus) that necessitates the Fire is (when) the man swears (an oath) against the right of a Muslim person, concerning the withholding of his wealth.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'Indeed, in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is written that the false oath and the severing of family ties both cause houses to be deserted by their inhabitants, and block the womb — meaning the cutting-off of progeny.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the false oath locks the wombs. He said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the meaning of 'locks the wombs'?' He said, 'It sterilises.'

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, both together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from a sheikh from our companions known as Abu al-Hasan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, created a white rooster, its neck is beneath the Throne, and its feet are at the edges of the seventh earth. It has a wing in the East and a wing in the West. The roosters do not crow until it crows. So whenever it crows, it flaps its wings, then says: 'Glory be to Allah! Glory be to Allah the Magnificent, Who does not resemble anything.' He said: So Allah, Blessed and High, answers it, saying: 'He would not swear by Me falsely, the one who recognizes what you are saying.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbihi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says, 'Allah knows' what he does not know, His Throne shakes due to that, in magnification for Him.

From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlub who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the servant says, "Allah knows," while he is lying, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Could you not find anyone other than Me to lie against?"'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says, 'God knows what He did not know,' the Throne shakes in magnification for Him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not swear oaths except by God. And whoever swears by God, let him be truthful. And whoever is sworn to by God, let him be pleased. And whoever is sworn to by God but is not pleased — he is not of God, Mighty and Majestic.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever swears by Allah, let him be truthful; and whoever is not truthful, he is not of Allah. And whoever has an oath sworn to him by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, let him be pleased with it; and whoever is not pleased, he is not of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, raising it (marfu'), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) heard a man saying, 'I disavow the religion of Muhammad.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Woe to you! If you disavow the religion of Muhammad, then upon whose religion will you be?' He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not speak to him until he died.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yunus ibn Zabyan who said: He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Yunus! Do not swear an oath by disavowing from us, for whoever swears by disavowing from us, truthfully or falsely, he has indeed been disavowed from us.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no oath for the son against his father, nor for the woman against her husband, nor for the slave against his master.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: An oath is not valid regarding the making permissible of the forbidden, nor the forbidding of the permissible, nor the severing of family ties.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: An oath is not valid for making permissible what is forbidden, nor for forbidding what is permissible, nor for severing family ties.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who swore an oath regarding the severing of family ties. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no (valid) vow in an act of disobedience, and no (valid) oath regarding the severing of family ties.' He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man whom the Sultan compelled to swear by divorce and other than that, and he swore. He said: 'There is no sin upon him.' And I asked him about a man who fears for his wealth from the Sultan, so he swears an oath to save it from him. He said: 'There is no sin upon him.' And I asked him: 'Should a man swear an oath to protect the wealth of his brother just as he would for his own wealth?' He said: 'Yes.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, while I was listening, about a man who made upon himself to walk to the House of God and the sacrificial offering. He said: And he swore by every solemn oath that he would never speak to his father, nor testify in his favor, nor would he ever eat with him at the table, nor would a roof shelter both him and his father ever. He said: Then he was silent. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Does anything remain?' He said: 'No, may I be your sacrifice.' He said: 'Every oath of cutting off kinship ties is nothing (i.e., such oaths are void).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no oath for a son against his father, nor for an owned slave against his master, nor for a woman against her husband, nor is there a vow in disobedience, nor an oath regarding the severing of family ties.'

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who imposed oaths upon himself to walk to the Kaaba, or to give charity, or to free a slave, or a vow, or a sacrificial offering, if he were to speak to his father, or his mother, or his brother, or a relative, or [if he were to] cut off kinship ties, or a sin in which he persists, or a matter which is not proper for him to do. So he (AS) said: 'The Book of God takes precedence over the oath, and there is no oath regarding disobedience.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, that A woman from the progeny of al-Mukhtar swore an oath against her sister, or a relative of hers. She said: 'Come closer, so-and-so, and eat with me.' She replied: 'No.' So she swore and imposed upon herself: the walking to the House of God, and freeing all her slaves, and that neither herself nor the other would ever be shaded under the same roof, nor eat together at a table, ever. Then the other woman said the same. So Umar ibn Hanzala brought both their statements to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: 'I am the arbiter in this matter. Tell her: let her eat, and let both of them be shaded under the same roof, and she need not walk (to the Kaaba), nor free (slaves), and let her fear God, her Lord, and not return to such things, for this is from the footsteps of Satan.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Ma'mar ibn Umar who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who says 'Upon me is a vow' and he did not specify anything. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid (it amounts to nothing).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding a man who made a vow for Allah upon himself and did not specify it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he specified it, then it is that which he specified, and if he did not specify it, then there is nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who said, 'For the sake of Allah, upon me is the walking to the Kaaba if I buy something on credit for my family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is that difficult for them?' He said: 'Yes, it is difficult for them if he does not take something for them on credit.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him take it for them on credit, and there is nothing upon him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Regarding a man who swore an oath that he would not speak to any of his relatives, he said: It is not binding, so let him speak to the one he swore against. And he said: Every oath in which the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not intended, is not binding regarding divorce or manumission. He said: And I asked him about a woman who dedicated her wealth as a Hadi (sacrificial animal/gift) for the House of Allah, if she lent her belongings to So-and-so and So-and-so, and some of her family lent them without her command. He said: There is no Hadi upon her. Rather, the Hadi is what is dedicated for Allah as a Hadi for the Kaaba; that is what is fulfilled when dedicated for Allah. And whatever is similar to this is not binding, nor a Hadi, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not mentioned in it. And he was asked about a man who says, 'Upon me is a thousand camels,' and he is in Ihram for a thousand Hajjs. He said: That is from the footsteps of Satan. And regarding a man who says, and he is in Ihram for a Hajj, he said: It is not binding. Or he says, 'I gift this food,' he said: It is not binding. Indeed, food is not gifted as a Hadi. Or he says, 'The carcass, after it has been slaughtered, I gift it for the House of Allah,' he said: Rather, the camels are gifted while they are alive, and they are not gifted when they have become meat.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Every oath not intended for the Sake of Allah, the Exalted, regarding a divorce or freeing a slave, is not valid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'A man swears with severe oaths that he will not buy anything for his family.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Let him buy for them, and there is nothing upon him regarding his oath.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umeyra, from Abu al-Subbah, who said: By Allah, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Allah taught His Prophet the Revelation (al-Tanzil) and the Interpretation (al-Ta'wil). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him).' He said: 'And He taught us, by Allah.'
