Then he said: 'Whatever you do, or oaths you swear during dissimulation (taqiyyah), you are in a state of leeway (ease) from it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no oath in anger, nor in cutting off kinship, nor in compulsion (jabr), nor in coercion (ikrah).' I said, 'May Allah keep you well, so what is the difference between coercion and compulsion?' He said: 'Compulsion is from the Sultan (ruling authority), and coercion is from the wife, the mother, and the father, and that is not [considered valid/obligatory].'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: There is no oath in anger, nor in cutting off kinship, nor in compulsion, nor in coercion. I said: May Allah improve you, so what is the difference between coercion and compulsion? He said: Compulsion is from the Sultan (ruling authority), and coercion happens from the wife, the mother, and the father, and that is not [considered valid/obligatory].

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said: I said to Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'I had bought a slave girl secretly from my wife, and that reached her, so she went out from my house and refused to return to my house. So I went to her in the house of her family, and I said to her: That which has reached you is false, and the one who brought this to you is your enemy, intending to cause separation between us. She said: 'By Allah, there will never be goodness between me and you ever, until you swear to me by freeing every slave girl you own, and by giving your wealth in charity, if you have bought a slave girl and she is in your possession today.' So I swore to her with that, and she made me repeat the oath and said to me: 'So say, I said to her: 'Every slave girl of mine at this moment, so she is free.' And I had separated from my slave girl and intended to free her and marry her for my desire regarding her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon you regarding what she made you swear, and know that neither freeing nor charity is valid except what is intended by it is the Face of Allah and His Reward.'

When a man swears an oath upon something, and that which he has sworn upon — doing it is better than leaving it, then let him do that which is better, and there is no expiation upon him. Rather, that is from the footsteps of Satan.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever swears an oath, then sees other than it to be better than it, and does that — then it is the expiation for his oath, and for him is a reward.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who swears an oath, then sees that leaving it is better, and if he does not leave it, he fears that he would sin. Should he leave it? So he (peace be upon him) said: Have you not heard the words of the Messenger of God (blessings of God be upon him and his family): 'Whenever you see something better than your oath, then leave it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees what is better than it, let him do that which is better, and for him is a reward.

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who swears an oath but then sees that leaving it is better, and if he does not leave it he fears he may be sinning — should he leave it? So he (peace be upon him) said: Have you not heard the saying of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'When you see something better than your oath, then leave it'?

A number from our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Umar al-Sayqal, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'A time will surely come upon the people in which the debauched will be treated with delicacy/respect, and the immoral will be brought near [to power], and the fair-minded will be weakened.' He said, and it was said to him, 'When will that be, O Amir al-Mu'minin?' He said: 'When the trust (al-amanah) is taken as a gain, and Zakat as a loss, and worship as a protracted engagement, and maintaining ties of kinship as a favor.' He said, and it was said, 'When will that be, O Amir al-Mu'minin?' He said: 'When women become dominant, and bondmaids are empowered, and young boys assume command.'

A number from our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Aqabiy, with an unbroken chain, said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) gave a sermon, so he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! Surely Adam did not give birth to a slave or a bondmaid, and all people are free, but Allah granted some of you authority over others. So whoever had an affliction and bore it patiently in goodness, let him not consider it a favor to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, something has occurred, and we are making equality between the black and the red in it.' So Marwan said to Talha and al-Zubayr, 'He has not intended by this other than the two of you.' He said, 'So he gave each one of them three dinars, and gave a man from the Ansar three dinars, and afterwards a black slave boy came, so he gave him three dinars.' So the Ansari said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, this is a slave whom I freed yesterday; do you make me and him equal?' So he said, 'I looked in the Book of Allah and did not find any preference for the sons of Ismail over the sons of Ishaq.'

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Salim, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Qatada, all from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out for the display of the horses, and passed by the grave of Abu Uhayhah. So Abu Bakr said, 'May Allah curse the occupant of this grave, for by Allah, he used to divert people from the way of Allah and deny the Messenger of Allah.' So Khalid, his son, said, 'Rather, may Allah curse Abu Qahafa (Abu Bakr's father), for by Allah, he neither hosted guests nor fought the enemy.' So may Allah curse the more worthless of the two in the clan. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) placed the bridle of his mount on its shoulder, then said, 'When you mention the polytheists, speak in general terms and do not be specific, lest his son become angry.' Then he stopped and the horses were presented to him. A horse passed by him, and Uyayna ibn Hisn said, 'Such and such is the matter of this horse.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Leave us, for I am more knowledgeable of horses than you.' Uyayna said, 'And I am more knowledgeable of men than you.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became angry until blood appeared in his face. He said to him, 'So which of the men are the best?' Uyayna ibn Hisn said, 'Men who are in Najd, placing their swords on their shoulders and their spears on the saddles of their horses, then striking with them forward, forward.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'You are lying. Rather, the men of Yemen are best. Faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni, and if it were not for the Hijrah, I would have been a man of the people of Yemen.' Alienation and harshness are in the Fadadeen (owners of wool), the people of the hair, Rabi'ah and Muzar from where the horn of the sun rises. And Muzhaj, most of the tribe will enter Paradise. And Hazramaut is better than Amr ibn Sa'sa' (and some narrated: better than al-Harith ibn Mu'awiya). And Bajila is better than Ra'il and Dhakwan. And if Liyan were to perish, I would not care. Then he said, 'May Allah curse the four kings: Jamad, Makhwas, Mashrah, and Abza'a, and their sister al

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A slave of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) asked him for wealth, so he said: 'My share will come out, and I will share it with you.' He said, 'I am not content,' and he went to Muawiya, who gave it to him. So he wrote to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) informing him of what he had obtained from the wealth. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'As for after, that which is in your hand from the wealth, there used to be an owner for it before you, and it will go to its owner after you. And what is for you from it is what you pave the way for yourself. So prefer yourself over the rectification of your children, for you are gathering for one of two men: either a man who works in it with the obedience of Allah, so he is fortunate with what you were unfortunate for, or a man who works in it with the disobedience of Allah, so he is unfortunate with what you gathered for him. And neither of these two is deserving that you prefer him over yourself and place a burden on your back.' So hope for what has passed for the mercy of Allah, and trust for what remains for the sustenance of Allah.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There was a man who used to sell oil, and he loved the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with intense love. Whenever he intended to go for his business needs, he would not leave until he looked at the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). This was known about him, for when he came, he would stretch himself out so that he could look at him. It happened one day that he came to him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stretched out to him until he looked at him, then he went away for his business needs. He did not take long before he returned. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw him do that, he gestured to him with his hand, saying, 'Sit.' So he sat in front of him. He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What is the matter? You have done something today that you had not done before.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, by the One who sent you with the Truth as a Prophet, a portion of your remembrance overwhelmed my heart to the extent that I could not go about my business until I returned to you.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated for him and wished him well. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) waited a few days but did not see him. When he missed him, he asked about him, and it was said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have not seen him for days.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) put on his shoes, and his companions put on theirs with him, and they set out until they came to the oil market. They found the man's shop empty, with no one in it. So he asked his neighbors about him. They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, he died. He was indeed trustworthy and truthful among us, except that he had a peculiar habit.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'And what was that?' They said, 'He used to exhaust himself following the women.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'May Allah have mercy upon him. By Allah, he used to love me with such love that even if he had been a slave trader, Allah would forgive him.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muyassar, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'How are your companions?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, we are considered worse in their eyes than the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and those who associate partners [with God].' He (the narrator) said: 'He had been leaning [on a pillow], so he sat up straight, then said: 'How did you say?' I said, 'By Allah, we are considered worse in their eyes than the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and those who associate [partners with God].' He said: 'By Allah, no two of you will enter the Fire. No, by Allah, and not even one. By Allah, you are the ones about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And they shall say: What is the matter with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil? Was it that we (only) took them in scorn, or have our eyes (now) turned aside from them? That most surely is the truth: the contending one with another of the inmates of the fire.”' Then he said: 'By Allah, they will be seeking you in the Fire, so they will not find even one of you therein.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: In the bequest of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him), he said: 'O Ali, I bequeath to you regarding yourself certain qualities, so preserve them from me.' Then he said: 'O Allah, support him. As for the first, it is truthfulness, and do not let a lie come out of your mouth ever. And the second is piety (al-wara'), and do not be audacious in treachery ever. And the third is fear of Allah, Mighty is His Mention, as if you see Him. And the fourth is much weeping from the fear of Allah; a thousand houses will be built for you in Paradise for every tear. And the fifth is spending your wealth and your blood for the sake of your Religion. And the sixth is adhering to my Sunnah in my Prayer, my Fasting, and my Charity.' As for the Prayer, it is fifty Rakaat. And as for the Fasting, it is three days in the month: Thursday in the first part, Wednesday in the middle, and Thursday in the last part. And as for the Charity, it is your utmost effort, to the point that you say 'I have been excessive,' yet you have not been excessive. And upon you is the Night Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer, and upon you is the Noon Prayer. And upon you is reciting the Quran in every condition. And upon you is raising your hands in your Prayer and turning them. And upon you is using the Siwak at every ablution. And upon you is adopting good morals and avoiding bad morals; if you do not do so, do not blame anyone but yourself.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira who said: It has been narrated to me by Ja'far ibn Ibrahim [ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Tayyar], from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The status of the man is (in accordance to) his Religion, and his chivalry, and his intellect, and his nobility, and his beauty, and his generosity, and his piety.

From them, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba and Tha'labah ibn Maymun and Ghalib ibn Uthman and Harun ibn Muslim, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in his tent at Mina. He looked at Ziyad al-Aswad, whose leg was swollen/inflamed, and pitied him. He said to him, 'What is the matter with your legs that they are like this?' He said, 'I came upon a weak mount (donkey), so I walked for most of the way.' He pitied him, and at that time Ziyad said to him, 'I am afflicted by sins to the extent that when I thought I was destroyed, I remembered my love for you, and I hoped for salvation, and clarity/lightness came to me.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'And is the Religion anything except for love?' He made faith lovely to you and adorned it in your hearts And He said, 'If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you' And He said, 'They love those who have migrated to them' Indeed, a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I love those who pray but I do not pray, and I love those who fast but I do not fast.' The Messenger of Allah said to him, 'You are with the one whom you love, and for you is what you have acquired.' And he (peace be upon him) said, 'What you seek and what you desire: Indeed, if there were a scare from the sky, every people would flee to their place of safety, and we would flee to our Prophet, and you would flee to us.'

Sahl, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Praise is to Allah. There became a sect of the Murji'ah, and there became a sect of the Haruriyyah, and there became a sect of the Qadariyyah, and you were named the Tarabiyyah and the Shi'a of Ali. But, by Allah, what is it except that there is Allah alone, without a partner, and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and the Progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon them), and the Shi'a of the Progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). And the people are none but them. Ali (peace be upon him) was the most excellent of the people after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the most worthy of the people to the people.' He said it three times.

From him, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abdul Hamid al-Wasiti, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May Allah keep you well. We have left our markets waiting for this matter, to the extent that one of us is about to beg with his hand.' He said, 'O Abdul Hamid, do you think that the one who confines himself to Allah, Allah will not find a way out for him? Yes, by Allah, Allah will surely find a way out for him. May Allah have mercy on a servant who revives our matter.' I said, 'May Allah keep you well. These Murji'ah are saying that it is not for us to remain as we are until what you say comes to pass; then we and you would be equal.' He said, 'O Abdul Hamid, they have spoken the truth. The one who repents, Allah accepts his repentance, and the one who conceals hypocrisy, Allah will humble him (rub his nose). And the one who makes apparent our matter, Allah will shed his blood; Allah will slaughter them upon Islam just as the butcher slaughters his sheep.' He said, I asked, 'So on that day we and the people will be equal?' He said, 'No. On that day you will be the pinnacle of the earth and its rulers. There is no leeway in our religion except for that.' I said, 'And if I die before I meet the Qaim (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'Indeed, the one among you who says,

From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Al-Walid Al-Kindi who said: We entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) during the time of Marwan. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Who are you?' So we said, 'We are from the people of Kufa.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no city among the cities with more people loving us than the people of Kufa, and especially this group. Allah, Exalted is His Mention, has guided you to a matter which the people were ignorant of. You loved us while the people hated us, you followed us while the people opposed us, you affirmed us while the people denied us. So Allah has made you live our life and die our death.' So I testify regarding my father that he used to say: 'There is nothing between any one of you and seeing what pleases Allah with his eyes and rejoicing, except that his soul reaches here' — and he gestured with his hand to his throat. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said in His Book: 'And certainly We sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring.' So we are the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kindi from Ahmad ibn Udeys from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Subah who said: I heard a speech reported from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and from Ali (peace be upon him) and from Ibn Mas'ud, so I presented it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: This is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I recognize it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The wretched one is the one who is wretched in the womb of his mother, and the happy one is the one who heeds the advice given to others. And the most intelligent of the intelligent is the pious one, and the most foolish of the foolish is the immoral one. And the worst of the reporters is the reporter of lies, and the worst of matters is their innovations. And the greatest of blindness is the blindness of the heart, and the worst of regrets is the regret on the Day of Judgment. And the greatest of sins in the presence of Allah is the lying tongue, and the worst of gains is the gain of usury, and the worst of consumptions is eating the wealth of the orphan. And the best of adornments is the adornment of a man: good conduct with faith, and the control of his affairs by it and the strengthening of its conclusions. And whoever follows fame, Allah will make him known as a liar. And whoever turns his heart to the world, he will be frustrated by it. And whoever recognizes affliction, he will be patient with it, and whoever does not recognize it, he will be afflicted. And doubt is disbelief. And whoever is arrogant, Allah will humble him. And whoever obeys Satan, he disobeys Allah. And whoever disobeys Allah, Allah will punish him. And whoever is grateful, Allah will increase him. And whoever is patient with a calamity, Allah will help him. And whoever places his reliance on Allah, Allah is sufficient for him. Do not anger Allah by pleasing anyone from His creation, and do not draw near to anyone from the creation such that you move away from Allah. For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is nothing between Him and anyone from His creation that gives him good or repels evil from him except by His obedience and following His pleasure. And indeed the obedience of Allah is success from every good that is sought and salvation from every evil that is feared. And indeed Allah, Mighty is His menti

And by this chain, from Abaan, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Mankind were one community' so he said: 'The people before Noah were a misguided nation' So Allah initiated by sending the Messengers And it is not as they are saying that it never ceased and they are lying Allah differentiates in the Night of Power what was of hardship or ease or rain in accordance with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, desires to decree, until the similar like it comes (Next Night of Power)

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ma'rouf ibn Kharabouz, from Al-Hakam ibn Mustawrid, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, among the sustenance that Allah has measured out for the people, from what they need, is the sea (atmosphere), which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created between the sky and the earth. He said: And Allah has determined in it the flows of the sun, the moon, the stars, and the planets, and has determined all of that upon the orbit. Then He assigned an angel to the orbit, and with him are seventy thousand angels, so they turn the orbit. So when they turn it, the sun, the moon, the stars, and the planets turn with it, and they descend in their stations which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has determined for them, for their day and their night. So when the sins of the servants become numerous and Allah, Blessed and High, intends to admonish them with a Sign from His Signs, He orders the angel assigned to the orbit to remove the orbit upon which are the flows of the sun, the moon, the stars, and the planets. So the angel orders those seventy thousand angels to remove it from its flows. He said: So they remove it, and the sun becomes in that sea which flows in the orbit. He said: So its light is obliterated and its color changes. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intends to magnify the Sign, the sun is obliterated in the sea, according to what Allah loves that His creatures should fear regarding the Sign. He said: And that is during the eclipse of the sun. He said: And He does similarly with the moon. He said: So when Allah intends to clear it or return it to its flow, He orders the angel assigned to the orbit to return the orbit to its flow. So he returns the orbit, and the sun returns to its flow. He said: So it emerges from the water, and it is dim. He said: And the moon is like that. He said: Then Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, no one is startled by them nor fears these two Signs except one who is from our Shiites. So when that is so, be startled to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then return to Him.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Al-Fadl ibn Ismail al-Hashimi, from his father, who said: I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what I faced from my family regarding their taking the religion lightly. He said: 'O Ismail, do not find it strange that from your family, for indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made for every family a proof by which He argues against its members on the Day of Resurrection. It will be said to them: 'Did you not see so-and-so among you? Did you not see his guidance among you? Did you not see his prayer among you? Did you not see his religion? Why did you not follow him?' So he will become a proof against them on the Day of Resurrection.

From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Usaym al-Nakhas, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, a man from among you lives in the neighborhood, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will use him as an argument against his neighbors on the Day of Resurrection. It will be said to them: 'Was not so-and-so among you? Did you not hear his speech? Did you not hear his weeping at night?' So he will be the argument of Allah against them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And sent against them birds in flocks' 'Striking them with stones of baked clay.' He said: 'These were low-flying birds that came to them from the sea. Their heads were like the heads of predatory beasts, and their claws were like the claws of predatory beasts among birds. With each bird were three stones: two in its legs and one in its beak. So it kept striking them with them until their bodies became covered in smallpox blisters, and killed them with them. And before that, nothing of smallpox had been seen, nor did they see such birds before that day, nor after it.' He said: 'And whoever escaped from them on that day went forth until they reached Hazramaut, which is a valley below Yemen. Allah sent a flood against them and drowned them all.' He said: 'And no water had been seen in that valley at all for fifteen years before that day.' He said: 'Therefore, it was named Hazramaut (Death Arrived) when they died in it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr and Thal'abah ibn Maymun and Ali ibn Uqba, from Zurara, from Abdul Malik, who said: A discussion occurred between Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and the children of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). That reached me, so I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and went to speak, but he said to me, 'Hush! Do not interfere in what is between us. For our example and the example of the sons of our uncle is like the example of a man who was among the Children of Israel. He had two daughters, so he married one of them to a farmer and married the other to a potter.' Then he visited them both. He began with the wife of the farmer and said to her, 'What is your condition?' She said, 'My husband has planted much crop. If Allah sends rain from the sky, we will be in the best condition of the Children of Israel.' Then he proceeded to the wife of the potter and said to her, 'What is your condition?' She said, 'My husband has made much pottery. If Allah withholds rain from the sky, we will be in the best condition of the Children of Israel.' So he returned, saying, 'O Allah, You are for them both,' and so it is with us.

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Zareeh who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) seeking refuge for one of his sons, and he was saying: 'I am resolved against you, O wind, and O pain, whatever you are, with the determination with which Ali bin Abi Talib, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), Messenger of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), resolved against the Jinn of Wadi al-Sabrah. So they answered and obeyed. You answer and obey, and go out from my son so-and-so, son of my daughter so-and-so, at this moment, at this moment.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who misses (someone in his absence) is himself missed (by others), and the one who does not prepare patience against the calamities of time will be frustrated, and the one who troubles the people will be troubled by them, and the one who leaves them alone will not be left alone by them.' It was said, 'So what shall I do, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Lend them from your dignity for the day of your poverty.'

From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: Musa ibn Isa was in his house, which was in the place of Sa'i, overlooking it, when he saw Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) coming from Al-Marwa on a mule. So he ordered Ibn Hayyaj, a man from Hamdan who was attached to him, to hold on to the rein and claim the mule. So he came to him, held on to the rein, and claimed the mule. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) folded his leg and dismounted from it, and said to his servants: 'Take its saddle and hand it over to him.' He said, 'And the saddle is mine as well.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'You are lying. The evidence with us is that it is the saddle of Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). As for the mule, we bought it not long ago, and you know it, and what you are saying.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Murazim, from his father who said: We went out with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he left from the presence of Abu Ja'far Al-Mansur from Al-Hira. He left at the time permitted for him and arrived at Al-Saliheen at the beginning of the night. A tax collector, who was stationed at Al-Saliheen at the beginning of the night, presented himself to him and said, 'I will not let you pass.' So he urged him and requested him, but he refused firmly. I and Musaddaf were with him. Musaddaf said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, this one is a dog; he has troubled you, and I fear he will make you return, and I do not know what will happen regarding the order of Abu Ja'far. If you permit us, I and Murazim can strike his neck and then throw him into the river?' He said, 'Restrain yourself, O Musaddaf.' He did not stop requesting him until most of the night had passed, so he permitted him. He passed. He said, 'O Murazim, is this better or that which you said?' I said, 'This is better, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'Indeed, a man exits from minor humiliation, but that [action] causes him to enter into major humiliation.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Hafs ibn Abu A'isha, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent one of his servants on an errand, but he was delayed. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out after him because of his delay, and found him sleeping. He sat by his head, soothing him, until he woke up. When he woke up, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O so-and-so, by Allah, that is not for you. You sleep during the night and the day, but the day is for us from you.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hassaan, from Abu Ali who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Do not mention our secrets in opposition to our public statements, and do not mention our public statements in opposition to our secrets. It suffices for you that you say what we say, and remain silent about what we remain silent about. Indeed, you have seen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not made any good for anyone of the people in opposition to us. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'So let those beware who go against his order lest a trial afflict them or there befalls upon them a painful chastisement.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hallaal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Musa (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, from where is the illness?' He said: 'From Me.' He said: 'And the cure?' He said: 'From Me.' He said: 'So what do Your servants do with the healer?' He said: 'They soothe themselves by him.' From that day, the healer was called the doctor.

From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no illness but it hastens to the body, waiting to see when it is ordered to take it, and in another narration: 'Except for fever, for it comes with a coming.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from Yunus ibn Abdul Rahman, from Dawud ibn Zurbiyy, who said: I fell ill in Medina with a severe illness, and that reached Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So he wrote to me: 'It has reached me your illness. Buy one Sa'a of wheat, then lie on your back and scatter it upon your chest however it scatters, and say: O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which, when the distressed asks You by it, You remove the adversity from him, and establish him in the earth, and make him Your vicegerent upon Your creatures, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the People of his Household, and to cure me from my illness.' Then sit upright, gather the wheat from around you, and say the like of that, and distribute it Mudd by Mudd to each poor person, and say the like of that.' Dawud said: 'I did the like of that, and it was as if I had been untied from a knot. And more than one person did that, so they benefited by it.'

Abu Hamza said: I have not heard of anyone among the people who was more ascetic than Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), except for what has reached me from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). Abu Hamza said: When Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) would speak about ascetism and give admonition, he would make those in his presence weep. Abu Hamza said: I read a parchment containing speech on ascetism from the words of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and I wrote down what was in it. Then I came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (may God's blessings be upon him), and I presented what was in it to him. He recognized it and corrected it. And what was in it was: In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. May God suffice us and you from the scheming of the unjust, the aggression of the envious, and the violence of the tyrants. O believers! Do not let the tyrants and their followers — those who covet this world, who are inclined towards it, deceived by it, rushing towards it and towards its lifeless ruins and its chaff that will perish tomorrow — tempt you. Beware of what God has warned you about it, and practice abstinence from what God has told you to abstain from, and do not incline towards what is in this world as one who has taken it as a permanent abode and settled dwelling. By God, that which is in it is evidence and warning for you — from the changing of its days, the reversal of its conditions, its punishments, and its mockery of its inhabitants. Truly it elevates the lowly and degrades the noble, and it will drive peoples into the Fire tomorrow. In this there is a lesson, a trial, and a deterrent for the wakeful. Truly the affairs that come upon you every day and night — the darknesses of strife, the occurrences of innovations, the traditions of oppression, the calamities of the age, the awe of rulers, and the whisperings of Satan — discourage hearts from awakening and distract them from finding guidance and recognizing the people of truth, except for the few whom God has protected. No one will understand the turns of its days, the changes of its conditions, and the harmful consequences of its strife, except one whom God protects, who has traveled the way of right guidance and followed the road of purpose. No one understands the turns of its days, the shifts of its conditions, and the harmful consequences of its strife, except one whom

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Kufi, who is al-'Asimi, from Abd al-Wahid ibn al-Sawwaf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Hamdani, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to counsel his companions and say: 'I enjoin upon you taqwa of God, for it is the joy of the hopeful seeker and the refuge of the fleeing one who seeks shelter. Internalize taqwa as your innermost garment, and remember God with a sincere remembrance — you shall live by it the finest of lives and walk by it the path of salvation. Look at the world with the gaze of the ascetic who has parted from it, for it uproots the settled dweller and brings grief to the affluent who feels secure. Do not hope for what has turned away from it and departed, nor is what is yet to come from it known so that it may be awaited. Affliction from it is joined with ease, and what remains of it ends in extinction. So its joy is tainted with sorrow, and remaining in it leads to weakness and frailty. It is like a garden whose pasture is lush, amazing those who look upon it — its water is sweet, its soil is good, its roots pour out moisture from the earth, and its branches drip with dew — until the grass reaches its prime and its shoots stand erect, then a wind arises that strips the leaves and scatters what was orderly, so it becomes — as God said — 'dry broken stubble that the winds scatter, and God is the Holder of power over all things.' (Quran 18:45) Look at this world — at the abundance of what amazes you, and the scarcity of what benefits you.'

Muhammad narrated from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the earth, upon what is it? He said: 'It is upon a whale.' I said: 'So the whale, upon what is it?' He said: 'Upon the water.' I said: 'So the water, upon what is it?' He said: 'Upon a rock.' I said: 'So upon what is the rock?' He said: 'Upon the horn of a smooth bull.' I said: 'So upon what is the bull?' He said: 'Upon the earth/dust.' I said: 'So upon what is the earth?' He said: 'Far off! At that point, the knowledge of the scholars is exhausted/strays.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zarara, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the earth, then sent upon it salty water for forty mornings, and sweet water for forty mornings, until they met and mixed. Then He took a handful with His hand and rubbed it with a strong rubbing all together, then separated it into two parts. So from each one of them came out a neck (or particle) like the neck (or particle) of a gnat. So He took a neck to Paradise and a neck to the Fire.

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Shaykh's companions, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: Dreams did not exist in the past at the beginning of creation, but rather they occurred later. I said, 'And what is the reason for that?' He said, 'Allah, Exalted is His mention, sent a Messenger to the people of his time and called them to the worship of Allah and His obedience. They said, 'If we do that, what is in it for us? By Allah, you are not wealthier than us, nor is your clan stronger than ours.' He said, 'If you obey me, Allah will make you enter Paradise, and if you disobey me, Allah will make you enter the Fire.' They said, 'And what is Paradise and the Fire?' So he described that for them. They said, 'When do we go to that?' He said, 'When you die.' They said, 'We have seen our dead become bones and dust.' So they increased in their denial and contempt of it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, caused dreams to occur among them. So they came to him and informed him of what they saw and what they had denied from that. He said, 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended to establish the argument against you by this. This is how your spirits will be when you die, and even if your bodies decay, the spirits will go to punishment until the bodies are resurrected.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: The opinion and the dream of a believer in the latter part of the time are a seventieth part of the parts of the Prophethood.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muammar ibn Khallaad, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would, when morning came, say to his companions: 'Is there any good tidings?', meaning by it, the dreams.

From them, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the Statement of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: 'For them is good news in the worldly life.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the good vision which the believer sees, so he is given good news by it in his worldly life.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The dream is upon three aspects: Good news from Allah for the believer, and a caution from the Satan, and confused dreams.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, the true dream and the false dream both originate from one place.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You have spoken the truth.' As for the false, contradictory dream, indeed a man sees it in the first part of the night during the dominion of the sinful rebels, and it is merely an imaginary thing presented to the man, and it is false and contradictory, with no good in it. And as for the true dream, if he sees it after two-thirds of the night, with the arrival of the angels, and that is before dawn, then it is true and will not be delayed, God willing. Unless he is in a state of major ritual impurity (Junub), or he sleeps without being in a state of minor ritual purity (Tahur), and he did not remember Allah, Exalted and Majestic, with true remembrance, for then it will be contradictory and delayed to its owner.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was nothing more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) than remaining hungry and fearful for the sake of Allah.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Sa'id ibn Amr al-Ju'fi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) one day while he was eating while leaning (upon something). He said: 'And it had reached us that this is disliked.' So I began looking at him, and he invited me to his food. When he had finished, he said: 'O Muhammad, perhaps you think that no eye saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) eating while he was leaning from the time Allah sent him until He took him.' He said: 'Then he corrected himself and said: No, by Allah, no eye saw him eating while he was leaning from the time Allah sent him until He took him.' Then he said: 'O Muhammad, perhaps you think that he was satisfied with wheat bread for three consecutive days from the time Allah sent him until He took him.' Then he corrected himself, then said: 'No, by Allah, he was not satisfied with wheat bread for three consecutive days since Allah sent him until He took him. Indeed, I do not say that he could not find it; he used to gift one man a hundred camels. So if he had intended to eat it, he would have eaten.' And Jibril (peace be upon him) had come to him with the keys of the treasures of the earth three times, giving him the choice, without Allah, Blessed and Exalted, deducting anything from what Allah had prepared for him on the Day of Resurrection. So he chose modesty to his Lord, Glorified and Exalted. And whenever he was asked for anything, he never said 'No'. If he had given, he would say 'Yes'; if he had not, he would say 'It will be'. And whatever he gave to Allah, he never failed to deliver it to him, to the extent that if he gave a man Paradise, Allah would deliver that to him. Then he reached out to me with his hand and said: 'And indeed, your Master (Ali) used to sit with the sitting of a slave, and eat with the eating of a slave, and feed the people with wheat bread and meat, and would return to his family to eat bread and oil.' And if he were to buy a Sunbulani shirt, he would let his slave choose the better of the two, then wear the remaining one. So if it exceeded his fingers, he would cut it, and if it exceeded his heel, he would remove it. And no two matters ever came to him, both for the sake of Allah's pleasure, e

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: Ali ibn al-Mughira narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and offered him the choice, and indicated to him humility, and was his advisor. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat the food of a slave and sit the sitting of a slave, out of humility to Allah, the Exalted. Then he came to him at the time of death with the keys of the treasures of the world, and said: These are the keys of the treasures of the world which your Lord has sent to you, so that there will be for you all that the earth carries, without anything being reduced from you. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the companions of the Most High'.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abdul Mu'min al-Ansari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Batḥā' of Mecca was presented to me as gold, so I said: 'O Lord, no, but rather I shall be satiated one day and hungry one day. When I am satiated, I will praise You and give thanks to You, and when I am hungry, I will supplicate to You and remember You.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Who is the harshest of the people against you?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, all of them.' He said: 'Do you know why that is so, O Yaqub?' I said, 'I do not know, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'Indeed, Iblis called them, so they answered him, and ordered them, so they obeyed him, and he called you, so you did not answer him, and he ordered you, so you did not obey him, so he instigated the people against you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a man sees what he dislikes in his dream, let him turn over to the other side from the side on which he was sleeping. Indeed, the whispering is from Satan, to grieve those who believe, but he will not harm them except by permission of Allah. Then let him say: I seek refuge with what the closely neared angels of Allah, and His prophets, and His righteous servants sought refuge with, from the evil of what I saw, and from the evil of the castaway Satan.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibraheem, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Harun ibn Mansur al-Abdi, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Fatima (peace be upon her) regarding the dream she saw: 'Say: I seek Refuge by what the Proximate Angels of Allah, and His Sent Prophets, and His Righteous Servants seek Refuge with, from the evil of what I have seen in this night of mine, that any harm or anything I dislike from it should befall me. Then turn towards your left three times.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad altogether, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you intends that whenever he asks his Lord for something He would give it to him, so he should despair from all the people, and do not have any hope for himself except from Allah, Mighty is His Remembrance. So when Allah, Exalted and Glorious, knows that to be in his heart, never would He ask for anything but it would be given to him. So take account of yourselves before Accounting is taken against you, for on the Day of Judgement there will be fifty pausing stations, with each stop being of the measurement of a thousand years'. Then he recited: 'in a day the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count'.

And by this chain, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is a traveler should travel on the day of Saturday. Even if a stone were to fall from a mountain on the day of Saturday, Allah, Exalted is His mention, would return it to its place. And whoever finds their needs difficult to fulfill should seek to obtain them on the day of Tuesday, for it is the day in which Allah softened the iron for Dawud (peace be upon him).

And by this chain, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The example of the people on the Day of Resurrection when they stand before the Lord of the Worlds is like the arrow in the quiver; it has no space on the ground except for the place of its foot, like the arrow in the quiver, not able to move here or there.

And by this chain, from Hafs who said: I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) walking through the gardens of Kufa. He came to a palm tree, performed ablution near it, then bowed and prostrated. I counted in his prostration five hundred glorifications. Then he leaned against the palm tree and supplicated with supplications. Then he said: 'O Abu Hafs! By Allah, it is the palm tree about which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Maryam (peace be upon her): And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree, it will drop on you fresh ripe dates.'

Hafs narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: ‘Isa (peace be upon him) said: The provision of the world has become difficult, and the provision of the Hereafter [is also difficult]. As for the provision of the world, you do not extend your hand to anything from it except that you find an immoral person who has preceded you to it. And as for the provision of the Hereafter, you do not find helpers who assist you in it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whichever believer complains of his need and distress to an infidel or to one who differs from him in religion, it is as if he has complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to an enemy from the enemies of Allah. And whichever believing man complains of his need and distress to a believer like him, his complaint is to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them) that the sign of your death is a tree emerging from Bayt al-Maqdis, called Al-Kharnuba. So Sulayman looked one day, and behold, the Al-Kharnuba tree had emerged from Bayt al-Maqdis. He said to it, 'What is your name?' It said, 'Al-Kharnuba.' Sulayman turned back towards his prayer niche and stood in it, leaning on his staff. His soul was captured at that very moment. The Jinn and humans continued to serve him and strive in his affairs as they had been, thinking that he was alive and had not died. They would go in the morning and return in the evening, while he stood firm. Until the woodworm gnawed into his staff, ate through the joint, and it broke. Then Sulayman fell to the ground. Do you not hear the statement of the Mighty and Majestic: 'And when he fell, the Jinn came to know plainly that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ja'far Al-Howl, from Sallam ibn Al-Mustaneer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created Paradise before He created the Fire, and created obedience before He created disobedience, and created Mercy before Anger, and created Good before Evil, and created the Earth before the Sky, and created Life before Death, and created the Sun before the Moon, and created Light before Darkness.

From him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah created the good on Sunday, and He did not create evil before the good. And on Sunday and Monday He created the earths, and created their sustenance on Tuesday. And He created the heavens on Wednesday and Thursday, and created their sustenance on Friday. And that is His statement, the Mighty and Majestic: "He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days."'

Ibn Mahboub, from Hanaan and Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said: I said to him: The Statement of the Mighty and Majestic: 'I will certainly lie in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will certainly come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left; and You will not find most of them thankful.' He said, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Zurara! Indeed, he (Satan) only lay in wait for you and your companions. As for the others, he has finished with them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id altogether from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn 'Imran Al-Halbi from Abdullah ibn Miskan from Badr ibn Al-Walid Al-Khash'ami who said: Yahya ibn Sabur came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to bid him farewell, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'By Allah, you are upon the Truth, and whoever opposes you is upon that which is not the Truth. By Allah, I have no doubt for you regarding Paradise, and I hope that Allah will delight your eyes [with the sight of victory/fulfillment] very soon.'

Yahya al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, do you see the one who rejects this matter to me as if he has rejected you?' He said, 'O Abu Muhammad! The one who rejects this matter to you, so he has rejected against the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and against Allah, Blessed and High. O Abu Muhammad! The dead one from among you who was upon this matter is a martyr.' I said, 'Even if he died upon his bed?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, even if he died upon his bed, he is alive in the Presence of his Lord, being given Sustenance.'

Yahya al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Habeeb who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, there is no one from the people more beloved to me than you. Indeed, people have taken various paths; among them is one who took his own opinion, among them is one who followed his desires, and among them is one who followed narration. But you have taken hold of a matter that has an origin. So upon you is piety and independent reasoning, and to witness the funerals, and to visit the sick, and to be present with your people in their mosques for prayer. Is it not shameful for a man among you that his neighbor knows his right while he does not know the right of his neighbor?'

From him, from Ibn Muskaan, from Malik Al-Juhani who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Malik! Will you not be pleased be you that you establish the Prayer, and give the Zakat, and restrain yourselves, and enter the Paradise? O Malik! Indeed, there is not from the people who followed an Imam in the world except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection cursing them and they will be cursing him, except for you and whoever is upon your condition. O Malik! By Allah, the dead among you who were upon this matter are a martyr of the status of the one who strikes with his sword in the Way of Allah.'

Yahya al-Halabi from Bashir al-Kunasi who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: You maintained relations whilst the people cut-off, and you loved whilst the people hated, and you recognized whilst the people denied, and it is the Truth. Indeed, Allah took Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a servant before He took him as a Prophet, and indeed Ali (peace be upon him) was a servant, sincere to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so He was sincere to Him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loved him, and he loved Him. Surely, our rights in the Book of Allah are clear. For us is the pure wealth, and for us is the Spoils of War (Al-Anfal), and we are a people whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated obedience to, and you follow those whom people have no excuse for their ignorance regarding. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever dies and has no Imam for him, has died the death of ignorance. Upon you is obedience, for you have seen the companions of Ali (peace be upon him).' Then he said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said during his illness in which he passed away: 'Call my friend for me!'. So two (females) sent for their respective fathers, but when they came, he turned his face away, then said: 'Call my friend for me!'. They said, 'He would have looked at us had he intended to speak to us'. So they sent for Ali (peace be upon him). So when he came, he leaned across towards him, and he narrated to him, and narrated to him, until he finished. So they met him and said, 'What did he narrate to you?' He said: 'He narrated to me by a thousand doors of knowledge, each door of which opens to a thousand doors'.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masrouq Al-Nahdy, from Musa ibn Umar ibn Bazi’e, who said: I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'The people have reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he took to a road, would return via another road. So this is what he used to do.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and I do so frequently, so do it.' Then he said to me: 'Indeed, it is better for your sustenance.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you, a man from my brethren, a matter reaches me about him which I dislike, so I ask him about it and he denies it, and reliable people have informed me about him.' He said to me: 'O Muhammad, deny your hearing and your sight regarding your brother. Even if fifty have testified in your presence under oath, and he says something to you, believe him and disbelieve them. Do not publicize anything about him that would disgrace him and destroy his magnanimity.' So you will be among those about whom Allah said in His Book: 'Surely those who love that scandal should circulate respecting those who believe, they shall have a grievous chastisement.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Abdu Rabbih ibn Rafi', from Al-Hubab ibn Musa, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever is born in Islam as a free person, he is an Arab; and whoever had a treaty (of manumission) and it was fulfilled in his treaty, he is a slave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and whoever entered Islam willingly, he is an emigrant.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever wakes up and goes to sleep with three things, the blessing is complete for him in the world: whoever wakes up and goes to sleep with good health in his body, security in his flock, and his day's provisions with him. If he has the fourth, the blessing is complete for him in the world and the Hereafter, and it is Islam.'

From him, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) [from his father (from his father, peace be upon him), that he said: To a man who had spoken to him with a lengthy speech, so he said: 'O man, you belittle speech and consider it insignificant. Know that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not send His messengers with whom He sent gold or silver, but He sent them with speech. And indeed, Allah, Glorious and Mighty, made Himself known to His creation through speech, and the indications towards Him, and the signs.'

And by this chain: He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not create any creature except that He appointed another over it to overcome it. And that is because when Allah, Blessed and High, created the lower seas, they prided themselves and surged, and said, 'Which thing can overcome me?' So He created the earth, and it surfaced upon its back, and it became submissive. Then he said: Indeed, the earth prided itself and said, 'Which thing can overcome me?' So He created the mountains and established them upon its back as pegs so that it would not sway due to what is upon it. So the earth became submissive and settled. Then indeed the mountains prided themselves over the earth, so they rose high and elongated, and said, 'Which thing can overcome me?' So He created the iron, which cut them, so the mountains calmed down and became submissive. Then indeed the iron prided itself over the mountains and said, 'Which thing can overcome me?' So He created the Fire, which melted the iron, so the iron became submissive. Then indeed the Fire exhaled and gasped and prided itself and said, 'Which thing can overcome me?' So He created the water, which extinguished it, so it became submissive. Then indeed the water prided itself and surged and said, 'Which thing can overcome me?' So He created the wind, which moved its waves and raised what was in its bottom, and restrained it from its currents, so the water became submissive. Then indeed the wind prided itself, raged, and loosened its tails, and said, 'Which thing can overcome me?' So He created the human being, who built and devised, and took what he could hide from the wind and other things, so the wind became humble. Then indeed the human being rebelled and said, 'Who is stronger than me in power?' So Allah created Death for him, which subdued him, so the human being became submissive. Then indeed Death prided itself in its own self, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Do not be proud, for I will slaughter you between the two groups - the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. Then I will not revive you ever, so you are hoped for or feared.' And he also said: 'Forbearance overcomes anger, and mercy overcomes harshness, and charity overcomes sin.' Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is similar to that which may overcome something else.'

From him, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Will you follow it if I advise you?' He said that to him three times, and in each of them the man said to him, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'I advise you that when you intend to do something, ponder its consequence; if it is guidance, then proceed with it, and if it is straying, then abstain from it.'

And by this chain, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Be merciful towards a mighty one who has been humbled, and a rich one who has become poor, and a scholar who is wasted in the era of the ignorant ones.

And by this chain, he said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying to his companions one day: 'Do not find faults with the one who comes to you with his cordiality, and do not let him remain upon the sin which he is indulging in, for it is not from the morals of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), nor is it from the morals of his friends.' He (the narrator) said, 'And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The best inheritance which the fathers can leave for their children is the etiquettes (discipline) and not the wealth, for the wealth goes away whilst the discipline remains'. Mas'adat (the narrator) said, 'What is meant by the discipline is the knowledge'. He (the narrator) said, 'Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'If there are two days left from your life, so make one of them for your manners to seek help for the day of your death'. So it was said to him (peace be upon him), 'And what is that which is the help?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Good management of what you leave behind and what you order for'. He (the narrator) said, 'And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) wrote to a man: 'In the Name of Allah (the Exalted) the Beneficent, the Merciful. Having said that, so the hypocrite does not like that which makes the Believers to be happy, and the happy one is he who heeds the advice of the piety, even if the advice is meant for the others'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat who said, 'Informed me some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said,' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ibn Muslim, the people are people of show-off, apart from you, and that is because you have concealed what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves, and displayed what the people love, while the people have displayed what angers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and concealed what Allah loves. O Ibn Muslim, indeed Allah, Blessed and High, was merciful to you, so He made Mut'ah a substitute for you instead of the drinks.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muammar ibn Khallaad, who said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Al-Ma'mun said to me, "O Abu Al-Hasan, if you could write to some of those who obey you in these regions where our relationship has become strained." I said to him, "O Chief of the Believers, if you fulfill [your promise] to me, I will fulfill [my promise] to you. I have entered into this matter on the condition that I do not command, nor prohibit, nor appoint, nor dismiss, and this matter has not increased anything for me in terms of favor."' "And I was in Medina, and my letter would reach the East and the West. I would ride my donkey and pass through the streets of Medina, and there was no one more prestigious than me in it, and no one among them would ask me for a need that I could fulfill, except that I would fulfill it for him."' He said, 'I will fulfill [my promise] to you.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nowfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is a right upon the Muslim if he intends to travel that he should inform his brothers, and it is a right upon his brothers that when he returns, they should come to him.'
And by this chain, it was said that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two qualities in which many people are infatuated are health and leisure.'

And by this chain, it was said, it was said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) He who exposes himself to suspicion, let him not blame the one who thinks ill of him; and he who conceals his secret, the choice is in his hand.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Shazan, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: My father said to me: 'Indeed, in Paradise is a river called Ja'far. On its right bank is a white pearl, in which are a thousand castles; in each castle, a thousand castles for Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). And on its left bank is a yellow pearl, in which are a thousand castles; in each castle, a thousand castles for Ibrahim and the Progeny of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: No two groups of the people of falsehood ever confronted each other at all except that the victory was with the better one of them, while the other way round (opposite) being for the people of Al-Islam.

From him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdurrahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Hearts are created with a love for the one who benefits them and a hatred for the one who harms them.

Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Musa ibn 'ibn 'Imran from his uncle Al-Husayn 'ibn 'Isa 'ibn Abdillah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said: My father took my hand, then said: 'O my son, indeed my father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) took my hand just as I took your hand, and said: 'Indeed my father Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) took my hand and said: 'O my son, do good to everyone who seeks it from you. If he is deserving of it, then you have hit its mark; and if he is not deserving of it, then you are deserving of it. And if a man insults you from your right, then turns to your left, and apologizes to you, accept his apology.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahboub from Al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Al-Hajjal from Al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Everything was water, and His Throne was upon the water. So Allah, Exalted is His mention, commanded the water, and it ignited into fire. Then He commanded the fire, and it was extinguished, and from its smoldering smoke arose. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the heavens from that smoke, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the earth from the ashes. Then the water, the fire, and the wind contended. The water said, I am the greatest army of Allah. And the fire said, I am the greatest army of Allah. And the wind said, I am the greatest army of Allah. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the wind: You are My greatest army.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'O Jabir! When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will gather the first and the last for the Decisive Speech. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be called, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) will be called. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be clothed in a green garment that illuminates what is between the East and the West, and Ali (peace be upon him) will be clothed with the like of it. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be clothed in a rosy garment that illuminates what is between the East and the West, and Ali (peace be upon him) will be clothed with the like of it. Then they will both ascend wearing them.' Then we will be called, and the accounting of the people will be handed over to us. By Allah, we are the ones who will make the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Fire enter Fire. Then the Prophets (peace be upon them) will be called, and they will stand in two rows near the Throne of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until we finish with the accounting of the people. So when the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Fire enter Fire, the Lord of Glory will send Ali (peace be upon him), and he will place them in their stations in Paradise and marry them. For Ali, by Allah, is the one who marries the people of Paradise in Paradise. And that is not for anyone other than him, as a honor from Allah, whose memory is exalted, and a favor which Allah has preferred him with and bestowed upon him. And he, by Allah, is the one who makes the people of Fire enter Fire, and he is the one who closes the doors upon the people of Paradise when they enter it, because the doors of Paradise are under his control and the doors of Fire are under his control.

Ali ibn Ibrahim from Salih ibn Al-Sindy from Ja'far ibn Basheer from Anbasah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Intermingle with the people, for if the love for Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them) does not benefit you in the privacy, it will not benefit you publicly.'

Ja'far, from Anbasah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Beware of the mention of Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them), for there is nothing more hateful to them than the mention of Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them).

Ja'far, from Anbasah, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, when He intends the demise of the dominion of a people, commands the celestial sphere to accelerate its movement, and it proceeds according to the measure of what He intends.

Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Shibl, who said: I and Suleiman ibn Khalid entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Suleiman ibn Khalid said to him: 'The Zaydiyyah are a people who are known, tested, and made famous by the people, and the most beloved person to them from among those on earth is you. So if you see fit to bring them closer and make them close to you, then do so.' He said: 'O Suleiman ibn Khalid! If these fools intend to turn us away from our knowledge to their ignorance, then welcome to them is not expected, nor are they suitable. But if they listen to our words and await our command, then there is no harm in it.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The strap of the slipper of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) broke while he was in a funeral. So a man came with his strap to hand it to him He said: 'Hold on to your strap, for the owner of the misfortune is more deserving of patience with it.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazal, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Cupping in the head is the reliever; it benefits from every illness except Al-Sam (death/epidemic). And [the area is] a span from the two eyebrows to where the thumb reaches. Then he said: 'Here.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Ahmad, son of Muhammad, from Maruk, son of Ubayd, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'Do you know, O Rifa'ah, why the believer is called a believer?' I said, 'I do not know.' He said: 'Because he entrusts himself to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so Allah validates his safety/guarantee.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazal, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The hostile one (Al-Nasibi) does not care whether he prays or commits adultery. And this Verse was revealed regarding them: Labouring, (hostile one) Entering into burning fire

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Yaqub ibn Yazeed from Muhammad ibn Marazim and Yazeed ibn Hammad all from Abdillah ibn Sinan, in what I think, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: If someone who is not a friend of Ali (peace be upon him) came to the Euphrates, and its water was clear on both sides of him, gushing forth, and he reached out with his hand and said 'Bismillah', and when he finished he said 'Alhamdulillah', it would be like (drinking) gushing blood or flesh of a pig.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man he mentioned, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What did you do to my uncle Zayd?' I said, 'They were guarding him, so when the people dispersed, we took his body and buried him in a cliff on the shore of the Euphrates. When it was morning, the horsemen came looking for him, so they found him and burnt him.' He said: 'So why did you not tie iron to him and throw him in the Euphrates? Greetings of Allah be upon him, and Curse of Allah be upon his killers.' Greetings of Allah be upon him, and Curse of Allah be upon his killers.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, gave permission for the destruction of the Banu Umayya after they burned Zayd over seven days.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from the one whom he mentioned, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, protects the one who protects His friend.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sinan, from Sa'dan, from Sama'ah, who said: I was seated with Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), while the people were performing circumambulation (Tawaf) in the middle of the night. He said: 'O Sama'ah! To us is the return of this creation, and upon us is their accounting. Whatever sin of theirs is between them and Allah (Exalted and Majestic), we have decreed upon Allah to leave it to us, so He responded to us regarding that. And whatever is between them and the people, we have taken it from them (as a right to be claimed), and they responded to that, and Allah (Exalted and Majestic) will recompense them for it.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Sulayman al-Mustarriq, from Salih al-Ahwal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established brotherhood between Salman and Abu Dharr, and stipulated upon Abu Dharr that he would not disobey Salman.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khattab ibn Muhammad, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) met me on a road in Medina and said: 'Who is that?
