Is it Harith?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, I shall carry the sins of your foolish ones upon your knowledgeable ones.' Then he passed by. So I came to him and sought permission to enter. I entered and said: 'You met me and said, "I shall carry the sins of your foolish ones upon your knowledgeable ones," and a great matter entered my heart because of that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. What prevents you, when word reaches you about a man among you that you dislike, and which causes us hurt, that you go to him, reproach him, correct him, and speak to him with eloquent words?' I said to him (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, then they will not obey us and will not accept from us?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Flee from them and avoid their gatherings.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Sayaaba ibn Ayyoub and Muhammad ibn al-Walid and Ali ibn Asbaat, they raise it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah will punish six (groups) for six (sins): the Arabs for tribal prejudice (al-'asabiyyah), the landlords (al-dahaqeen) for arrogance (al-kibr), the rulers (al-umara') for tyranny (al-jawr), the jurists (al-fuqaha') for jealousy (al-hasad), the merchants (al-tujjar) for fraud/betrayal (al-khiyanah), and the villagers (ahl al-rasatiq) for ignorance (al-jahl).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There was nothing more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) than to remain fearful and hungry for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Salama the seller of the Sabiri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when he took the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) and looked into it, would say: 'Who can endure this? Who can endure this?' Then he would act upon it. And when he would stand for the prayer, his complexion would change to the extent that it became recognizable on his face. And no one from his sons after him could endure the actions of Ali (peace be upon him) except Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from a worker who was with Muhammad ibn Rashid, who said: I attended the evening meal of Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the summer. A tray was brought with bread, and a bowl was brought containing tharid (bread soaked in broth) and boiling meat. He placed his hand in it and found it hot, then raised it while saying: 'We seek refuge with Allah from the Fire, we seek refuge with Allah from the Fire. We cannot bear this, so how can we bear the Fire?' He kept repeating this until the bowl was cool enough to touch, so he placed his hand in it, and we placed our hands when it was possible for us, so he ate and we ate with him. Then the tray was removed, and he said: 'O boy, bring us something.' He was brought dates on a platter. I extended my hand, and they were dates, so I said: 'May Allah keep you well, this is the season of grapes and fruit.' He said: 'These are dates.' Then he said: 'Remove this and bring us something.' He was brought dates, I extended my hand and said: 'These are dates.' He said: 'They are good.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not eat while leaning, from the time Allah Mighty and Majestic sent him until He took his soul, out of humility for Allah Mighty and Majestic, and he never had his two knees seen in front of his companion in any gathering. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never shook hands with a man and then pulled his hand away until the man himself pulled his hand away. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never repelled an evil deed with an evil deed. Allah the Exalted said to him: 'Repel evil by what is best.' So he did it. And he never denied a beggar at all; if he had it with him, he gave it, or else he said: 'Allah will bring it.' And he did not give anything on the authority of Allah Mighty and Majestic except that Allah authorized it for him; if it were Paradise, Allah Mighty and Majestic would authorize it for him. He said: And his brother after him, by the One who took his soul, did not eat anything prohibited from the world until he exited from it. By Allah, if two matters were presented to him, both of which were obedience to Allah Mighty and Majestic, he would take the one that was more difficult upon his body. By Allah, he freed a thousand slaves for the sake of Allah Mighty and Majestic, from the work of his own hands. By Allah, no one else could endure the deeds of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) after him, apart from him. By Allah, no difficulty ever descended upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) except that he placed him in it first, as a reliable one from him for it. And whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent him with his flag, Jibraeel would fight on his right and Mikaeel on his left. Then he would not return until Allah Mighty and Majestic granted him victory.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zayd ibn al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was the most similar to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in food and manner, and he used to eat bread and oil, and he used to feed the people bread and meat.' He said: 'And 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to fetch water and gather firewood, and Fatima (peace be upon her) used to grind, knead, bake, and stitch. She was of the most beautiful of people in face, as if her two cheeks were two roses. May Allah bless her, and her father, and her husband, and her purified children.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Rayyan ibn Al-Salt, from Yunus, who raised it (to the Imam), said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet at all except that he would have a clear black seal (Mirrah), and Allah did not send any Prophet at all until He affirmed for him the Beginning (Al-Bada').

Sahl, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Abdul Hameed, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When they frightened the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the she-camel said to him: By Allah, I did not cease moving one hoof from the other, and even if I were cut into pieces, piece by piece.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, all together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: 'Would that we were a caravan like the family of Yaqoub, until Allah judges between us and His creatures.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazal, from Thal'ata ibn Maymun, from Al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own souls, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth He said: Submerging, metamorphosis, and stoning. I said: 'Until it becomes clear to them'? He said: Leave that. That is the rising of the Rising One.

Sahl, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and Ibn Sinan and Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Obedience to Ali is humility, and disobedience to him is disbelief in Allah.' It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how can obedience to Ali be humility and disobedience to him be disbelief in Allah?' So he replied: 'Indeed, Ali carries you upon the Truth; so if you obey him, you will be humbled, and if you disobey him, you will have disbelieved in Allah.'

From him, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar or someone else, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We are the Clan of Hashim, and our Shiites are the Arabs, and the rest of the people are Bedouins'.

Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hanaan, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We are Quraysh, and our Shiites are the Arabs, and the rest of the people are the 'Uluuj of the Romans.'

Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: It is as if I am with Al-Qaim (peace be upon him) upon the pulpit of Kufa, wearing a gown; he takes out from the fold of his gown a book sealed with a gold seal, unties it, and reads it to the people. They flee from him as sheep flee, so none remain except the commanders. He speaks a speech, and they do not find a refuge until they return to him. And I know the speech that he will speak.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Wisdom is the lost property of the believer, so wherever one of you finds his lost property, let him take it.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed or someone else, from Sulayman the scribe of Ali ibn Yaqteen, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays participated in the blood (killing) of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and his daughter Ja'dah poisoned Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and his son Muhammad participated in the blood (killing) of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sabbah al-Hadda', from Abu Usama who said: I accompanied Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said to me: 'Read.' So I opened a Chapter from the Quran and recited it. He became soft-hearted and wept. Then he said: 'O Abu Usama! Nurture your hearts by the Mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and be cautious of the instigation (nakat), for it comes upon the heart once or for many hours.' Doubt is from Sabbah. It is neither in it belief nor disbelief, like a worn-out piece of cloth or a decayed bone. 'O Abu Usama! Is it not that sometimes you inspect your heart, so you neither remember any good nor any evil by it, and nor do you know where it is?' I said to him, 'Yes, it has happened to me, and I have seen it happen to the people.' He said: 'Yes, everyone is exposed to it.' So if it is like that, remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and be cautious of the instigation, for if He intends good for a servant, He instigates belief, and if He intends by it other than that, He instigates other than that. I said, 'What is other than that, may I be sacrificed for you, what is it?' He said: 'If He intends infidelity, He instigates infidelity.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Magra'a, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Saeed ibn Hilal, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I hardly ever meet you except after years, so advise me with something that I can take to it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I advise you to fear Allah, and be truthful in narration, and have piety (war'), and strive hard (ijtihad). And know that striving does not benefit one who does not have piety with him.' And beware of your soul craving for those who are above you, and sufficient is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family): 'Let not their wealth and their children excite you.' And do not stretch your eyes to that with which We have provided different classes of them, (of) the splendour of this world's life. So if you fear any of that, remember the lifestyle of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for his food was barley, his sweetness was dates, and his fuel was palm twigs if he found them. And when you are afflicted with a calamity, remember your affliction with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for the creatures have never been afflicted with the like of what he (peace be upon him) was afflicted with, at all.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn al-Sari, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by us one day while we were in our gathering, we were in our gathering, and he was upon his she-camel, and that was when he had returned from the Farewell Pilgrimage. He stopped by us, greeted us, and we returned the greeting to him. Then he said: 'Why do I see that love of the world has overwhelmed many of the people, to the extent that it seems as if death in this world has been decreed for others than them, and as if the truth in this world has been obligated upon others than them, and to the extent that they have not heard or seen the news of the dead before them. Their path is the path of a people traveling; after a short while they will return to their homes, their graves, and their heirs will consume their legacy, thinking that they will be immortal after them. Alas, alas! [A] Will not the latter take lesson from the former? They have indeed been ignorant and forgotten all the advisors in the Book of Allah, and felt safe from the evil of every bad consequence, and did not fear the descent of a calamity and the events of misfortune.' Goodness is for the one whose fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, occupied him from the fear of people. Goodness is for the one whose own fault prevented him from finding faults with the believers from his brothers. Goodness is for the one who humbled himself to Allah, Mighty is His mention, and renounced what Allah had made permissible for him without desiring to deviate from my way of life, and rejected the blossoms of the world without turning away from my Sunnah, and followed the best ones from my progeny after me, and avoided the people of vanity and boasting, and those infatuated with the world, the innovators who oppose my Sunnah, the workers who act upon other than my way. Goodness is for the one who acquired wealth from the believers without disobedience, so he spent it in non-disobedience, and returned it to the people of poverty. Goodness is for the one whose character was good with people, and who offered them assistance, and turned away from them his evil. Goodness is for the one who spent moderately, and gave the excess, and restrained his speech from vain

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, raising it up from some of the wise ones, who said: Indeed, the most deserving of people to wish for the wealth of people are the stingy ones, because if people become rich, they would refrain from their wealth. And the most deserving of people to wish for the rectification of people are those with faults, because if people are rectified, they would refrain from pursuing their faults. And the most deserving of people to wish for the forbearance of people are the foolish ones, who need to be excused for their foolishness. But the stingy ones have come to wish for the poverty of people, and the fault-finders have come to wish for their mischief, and the sinful ones have come to wish for their foolishness. And in poverty, there is need for the stingy one; and in mischief, there is the seeking of the faults of the fault-finders; and in foolishness, the recompense is by the sins.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hassan! When a calamity befalls you, do not complain about it to anyone from the people of opposition (Ahl al-Khilaf), but mention it to one of your brothers, for you will not lack one of four qualities: either sufficiency by wealth, or assistance by prestige, or a supplication that is answered, or consultation by opinion.'

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ma'mar from Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: Abdullah ibn Ayyub al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Amr al-Awza'i from Amr ibn Shimr from Salama ibn Kuhayl from Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) preached to the people in Medina. He said: All praise is due to Allah, besides Whom there is no god. He was Alive without a 'how', and there was no 'being' for Him, nor was there a 'how' for His 'being', nor was there a 'where' for Him, nor was He in anything, nor upon anything, nor did He create a place for His 'being', nor did He become strong after creating something, nor was He weak before creating something, nor was He lonely before He began something, nor does He resemble anything, nor was He without dominion before He created it, nor will He be without it after it passes. He was a Living God without a lifespan, and a Master before He created anything, and a Master after He created the universe. And for Allah there is no 'how' nor 'where', nor a limit to be recognized, nor anything that resembles Him. He does not age due to the duration of His remaining, nor does He weaken due to solitude, nor does He fear as His creatures fear something. But He is All-Hearing without hearing, All-Seeing without sight, and Almighty without strength from His creation. The pupils of the lookers cannot perceive Him, and the hearing of the listeners cannot encompass His hearing. When He intends something, it is without consultation, or assistance, or informing, and He does not ask anyone about anything from His creation that He intended. The visions cannot perceive Him, but He perceives the visions. And He is the Subtle, the Aware. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, without a partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He sent him with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists dislike it. So he conveyed the message and paved the way for guidance (peace be upon him and his family). O community that was deceived and fell for the deception, and recognized the deception of the one who deceived it, but persisted upon what it recognized, and followed its desires, and wandered in the darkness of its misguidance. And the truth had become clear to it, so it turned away from it, and the path was clear, so it deviated from it. By the O

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Abu Baseer entered, panting heavily. When he took his seat, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Abu Muhammad, what is this heavy breathing?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah — great is my age, my bones have become frail, and my appointed time approaches, yet I do not know what I shall encounter from the matters of my Hereafter.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad, are you really saying this?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — how can I not say this?' He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, do you not know that Allah the Most High honours the young ones among you and is bashful toward the elderly?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — how does He honour the young and be bashful toward the elderly?' He said: 'Allah honours the young by not punishing them, and is bashful toward the elderly by not calling them to account.' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — is this exclusively for us or for all the people of Tawhid?' He said: 'No, by Allah, it is exclusively for you (Shia) apart from all the worlds.' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — we have been given a name that has broken our backs, killed our hearts, and because of which the rulers have declared our blood permissible to shed, in a hadith narrated to them by their jurists.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it al-Rafida (the Rejectors)?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'No, by Allah — it is not they who named you thus; rather, it is Allah Who named you with it.' Do you not know, O Abu Muhammad, that seventy men from the Children of Israel rejected Pharaoh and his people when his misguidance became clear to them, so they joined Moses (peace be upon him) when his guidance became clear to them? They were called al-Rafida in the army of Moses because they had rejected Pharaoh, and they were the most intense worshippers in that army and the most fervent in their love for Moses, Harun, and their offspring (peace be upon them both). So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Moses (peace be upon him): 'Establish this name for them in the Torah, for I have named them with it and bestowed it upon them.' So Moses (peace be upon him) established the name for them, then Allah

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran and others, from Ismail ibn al-Subah, who said: I heard an old man narrating from Saif ibn Umair, who said: 'I was with Abu al-Dawaniq, and I heard him saying, starting from himself: O Saif ibn Umair! There must be a caller who calls out the name of a man from the descendants of Abu Talib.' I said, 'Does anyone from the people narrate it?' He said, 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, my own ears heard him saying: There must be a caller who calls out the name of a man.' I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, as for this Hadith, I have not heard anything like it before.' He said to me, 'O Saif! If that is the case, then we will be the first to respond to it. Indeed, he is one of the sons of our uncle.' I said, 'Which son of our uncle?' He said, 'A man from the children of Fatima (peace be upon her).' Then he said, 'O Saif! Had I not heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying it, and then the people of the earth narrated it to me, I would not have accepted it from them, but it is Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I was sitting with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the mosque when Dawud ibn Ali, Suleiman ibn Khalid, and Abu Ja'far Abdullah ibn Muhammad Abu al-Dawaniq came and sat in a corner of the mosque. It was said to them, 'This is Muhammad ibn Ali sitting here.' So Dawud ibn Ali and Suleiman ibn Khalid stood up and went to him, while Abu al-Dawaniq remained seated in his place until they greeted Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to them, 'What prevented your tyrant from coming to me?' So they excused him in his presence. At that, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, nights and days will not pass before he rules over the two regions. Then men will strengthen his rule, then the necks of men will be humbled to him, then he will possess a severe dominion.' Dawud ibn Ali said to him, 'And will our rule be before your rule?' He said, 'Yes, O Dawud! Your rule is before our rule, and your authority is before our authority.' He said to him, 'May Allah keep you well, is there a time frame for it?' He said, 'Yes, O Dawud. By Allah, the Banu Umayya will not rule for a day except that you will rule for twice as much, and will not rule for a year except that you will rule for twice as much, and the children among you will seize it just as children seize the ball.' Dawud ibn Ali stood up from the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rejoicing, intending to inform Abu al-Dawaniq of that. When both he and Suleiman ibn Khalid arose, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) called from behind him, 'O Suleiman ibn Khalid! The people will not cease from having space in their rule as long as they do not shed unlawful blood from us.' And he gestured with his hand to his chest. 'So if they shed that blood, the inside of the earth will be better for them than its surface, for on that day there will be no helper for them in the earth, nor a forgiver for them in the sky.' Then Suleiman ibn Khalid went and informed Abu al-Dawaniq. So Abu al-Dawaniq came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), greeted him, and then informed him of what Dawud ibn Ali and Suleiman ibn Khalid had told him. He said to him, 'Yes, O Abu Ja'far! Your government is before our government, and your authority is before our authority. Your authority is severe and di

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Mazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'During the days of Abdullah ibn Ali, these people disputed among themselves.' So he said, 'Leave that aside. The spoiling of their affair will come from where their success began.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Badr ibn al-Khalil al-Azdi, who said: I was sitting in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Two signs will occur before the rising of Al-Qaim (peace be upon him) which have not occurred since Adam descended to the earth: the sun will be eclipsed in the middle of the month of Ramadan, and the moon at its end.' A man said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! The sun is eclipsed at the end of the month, and the moon in the middle.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'I know what you say, but these two signs have not occurred since Adam (peace be upon him) descended.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I and my father went out until we were between the Grave and the Pulpit, and behold, there was a group of the Shites, so he greeted them.' Then he said: 'By Allah, I love your aromas and your spirits, so help me with that through piety and striving. And know that our Wilayah cannot be attained except through piety and striving.' And whoever from among you follows a servant (Imam), let him emulate his actions. You are the Shites of Allah, and you are the Helpers of Allah, and you are the foremost of the former ones, and the foremost of the later ones, and the foremost in the world, and the foremost in the Hereafter to Paradise. We have guaranteed Paradise for you by the guarantee of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the guarantee of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). By Allah, there is no level of Paradise where there are more spirits than yours, so compete in the virtues of the levels. You are the good ones, and your women are the good ones. Every believing woman is a virgin Hourie, and every believing man is a Truthful one. And indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Qanbar: 'O Qanbar, receive good news, convey good news, and rejoice with good news. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away while he was angry with his community except for the Shites.' Indeed, for everything there is an honor, and the honor of Islam is the Shites. Indeed, for everything there is a pillar, and the pillar of Islam is the Shites. Indeed, for everything there is a chief, and the chief of Islam is the Shites. Indeed, for everything there is an honor/prestige, and the prestige of Islam is the Shites. Indeed, for everything there is a master, and the master of gatherings is the gatherings of the Shites. Indeed, for everything there is an Imam, and the Imam of the earth is the land upon which the Shites reside. By Allah, if it were not for what is in the earth from among you, an eye would never have seen herbs. By Allah, if it were not for what is in the earth from among you, Allah would not have favored those who oppose you. Nor would they have attained the good things. They have no share in the world, nor any share in the Hereafter. Every hostile one (Nasib

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it. Behold, and indeed for everything is an essence, and the essence of the children of Adam is Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and us, and our Shites after us. How lovely are our Shites! How close they are to the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and how excellent is the making of Allah towards them on the Day of Resurrection. By Allah! Had the people not magnified that, or pride entered into them, the Angels would have greeted them with kisses. By Allah! There is no servant from our Shites who recites the Quran while standing in his prayer, except that for him there is a hundred good deeds for every letter, and if he recited while sitting in his prayers, except that for him there are fifty good deeds for every letter, and if not in prayer, except that for him there are ten good deeds for every letter. And indeed for the silent one from our Shites is the reward of the one who recited the Quran from among those who opposed him. You are, by Allah, sleeping on your beds, and for you is the reward of the Mujahideen; and you are, by Allah, in your prayers, and for you is the reward of those who stand in rows in His way. You are, by Allah, the ones for whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And We removed whatever of rancour was in their breasts, [they are] brothers upon couches facing each other.' Indeed, our Shites are the people of the four eyes: two eyes in the head and two eyes in the heart. Behold, and all creatures are like that, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, opened your eyes and blinded their eyes.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I complain to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about my loneliness and my restlessness among the people of Medina, until you come and I see you and am comforted by you. If only this tyrant would permit me, I would take a fortress in al-Ta'if, dwell in it, and make you dwell with me. I would guarantee to him that no unpleasantness would come from our side to him ever.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said: Al-Kumayt chanted a poem for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'May Allah make my desire sincere for me, so I do not drown the drawing [of the bow], and my arrows do not waver.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not say like this, I do not drown the drawing but say, 'So I have drowned the drawing and my arrows do not waver'.

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq, from Sufyan ibn Mus'ab al-Abdi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Tell Umm Farwa to come and listen to what was done with her grandfather.' He said: So she came and sat behind the curtain. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Recite a poem to us.' I said: 'Let Farwa be generous with your flowing tears.' He said: So she wailed and the women wailed. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The door! The door!' So the people of Medina gathered at the door. He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent a message to them: 'A young one of ours fainted, hence the women wailed.'

Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from one of his men, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was digging the trench, they came across a rock. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the pickaxe from the hand of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), or from the hand of Salman (may Allah be pleased with him). He struck it with a blow, and it split into three pieces. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The treasures of Kisra and Caesar have been opened up for me with this strike of mine.' One of them said to his companion: 'He promises us with the treasures of Kisra and Caesar, yet none of us can control his own need to go out for relieving himself.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there is a wind called Al-Azyeb. If He were to send from it the measure of the nostril of a bull, it would stir up what is between the sky and the earth, and this is the South (wind).

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ruzayq Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A group of people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Our lands have suffered from drought, and the years have succeeded one another upon us, so supplicate to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to send the sky (rain) upon us.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered the pulpit to be brought out, the people gathered, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended, supplicated, and ordered the people to say 'Ameen'. It was not long before Jibra'il descended and said, 'O Muhammad! Inform the people that your Lord has promised them that He will send rain on such and such a day, and at such and such a time.' So the people did not cease waiting for that day and that time until, when that time arrived, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stirred a wind, which raised clouds, covered the sky, and released the rain. So those same individuals came in person to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah for us to withhold the sky (rain) from us, for we are on the verge of drowning.' So the people gathered, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated and ordered the people to say 'Ameen' to his supplication. A man from the people said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, make us hear (your supplication), for all that you say, we do not hear.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Say: O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, pour it in the depths of the valleys, and in the growth of the trees, and where the people of felt (nomads) pasture. O Allah, make it a mercy and do not make it a punishment.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Al-Azramy, with an unbroken chain, said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked about the clouds, where they are. He said: They are on trees, on dunes, on the shore of the sea, taking refuge there. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intends to send them, He sends a wind which stirs them, and appoints angels over them who strike them with 'makhariq' (thunderclaps/strikers), and that is lightning, so they rise up. It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds and spread them in the sky... And the angel's name is Al-Ra'd (Thunder).

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whose tongue is truthful, his deeds become pure; and the one whose intention is good, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, increases his sustenance; and the one whose kindness to his family is good, Allah increases his lifespan.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Mu'alla from Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi who said: My father narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me from his father from his grandfather from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: To the son of Adam: If your eye disputes with you regarding some of what I have prohibited to you, then I have aided you against it with two layers (eyelids), so close them and do not look. And if your tongue disputes with you regarding some of what I have prohibited to you, then I have aided you against it with two layers (lips), so close them and do not speak. And if your genitals dispute with you regarding some of what I have prohibited to you, then I have aided you against it with two layers (legs), so close them and do not come to the prohibited.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a slave of Banu Hashim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Three qualities: whoever possesses them, no hope of goodness is expected from him — one who is not ashamed of faults, and fears Allah in the unseen, and becomes pious/retreats into piety in old age.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hajjal, who said: I said to Jameel ibn Darraj, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When a respectable person of a people comes to you, honor him.' He said, 'Yes.' I said to him, 'And what is the respectable one?' He said, 'I had asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said that the respectable one is the one who has wealth.' I said, 'So what is the noble one?' He said: 'The one who performs good deeds with his wealth and the wealth of others.' I said, 'So what is generosity/karam?' He said: 'Piety (taqwa).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How intense is the grief of women, and how distant is the separation of death; and more intense than all of that is poverty, in which its owner flatters [others], yet is given nothing.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Musanna, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the people are of three levels: a level who are from us and we are from them; and a level who adorn themselves with us; and a level who consume one another with us.

From him, from Mu'alla, from Al-Washa, from Abdul-Karim ibn Amr, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you see that poverty and need have become abundant, and people are denying each other, then at that time await the Command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I recognize these two – poverty and need – so what is 'people denying each other'?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from among you comes to his brother and asks him for his need, and he looks at him with a look unlike the one he used to look with, and speaks to him with a tongue/manner unlike the one he used to speak with.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ubayhi, from Ubayd ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Sustenance is assigned to foolishness, and deprivation is assigned to intellect, and affliction is assigned to patience.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid al-Attar, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Umar the brother of Udhafir, who said: A man handed over to me six hundred or seven hundred dirhams for Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So it was in my bag. When I arrived at Al-Hafeera, my bag split and everything in it was taken. I met the governor of the city there, and he said, 'Are you the one whose bag split and belongings were taken?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'When we arrive in the city, come to me so that I may compensate you.' He said: So when I arrived in the city, I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He said, 'O Umar, your bag split and your belongings were taken?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'What Allah gave you is better than what was taken from you. The Messenger of Allah's (peace be upon him and his family) she-camel got lost, so the people said regarding it, 'He informs us about the sky but does not inform us about his she-camel.' Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said, 'O Muhammad, your she-camel is in such and such a valley, its bridle entangled with such and such a tree.' He said: So he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said, 'O people, you have burdened me regarding my she-camel. Indeed, what Allah gave me is better than what was taken from me. Indeed, my she-camel is in such and such a valley, its bridle entangled with such and such a tree.' So the people rushed towards it and found her as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said. He then said, 'Go to the governor of the city and take from him what he promised you, for it is something Allah invited you to; you did not seek it from him.'

Sahl, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Yunus, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Something is reported from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) that he used to say: Three things which people hate, but I love them. I love death, and I love poverty, and I love affliction.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not as they report it. Rather, he meant: Death in the obedience of Allah is more beloved to me than life in disobedience to Allah, and affliction in the obedience of Allah is more beloved to me than health in disobedience to Allah, and poverty in the obedience of Allah is more beloved to me than wealth in disobedience to Allah.'

Sahl, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Yunus, from Abdul A'ala, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Let those beware who go against His order, lest a trial afflict them or there befall them a painful chastisement.' He said: 'Fitnah' (strife/trial) in his religion, or a wound/penalty for which Allah does not reward them.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Allah sets forth an example: a man with several partners who quarrel with one another, and a man wholly owned by one man. Are they equal in condition? He said: As for the one with quarreling partners, it is because the first one gathers the scattered [people] for his leadership, and while doing so, some curse each other and some distance themselves from each other. As for the man of peace [wholly owned], he is the first truly [in authority] and his Shias. Then he said: The Jews differed after Musa (peace be upon him) into seventy-one sects, one of which is in Paradise and seventy are in the Fire. The Christians differed after Isa (peace be upon him) into seventy-two sects, one of which is in Paradise and seventy-one are in the Fire. And this Ummah differed after its Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) into seventy-three sects, seventy-two of which are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. And from the seventy-three sects, thirteen sects claim our Wilayah and our affection; twelve of them are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. And sixty sects from the rest of the people are in the Fire.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The government of falsehood has remained long, and the government of truth has been short.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yaqoub al-Sarraaj who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When will there be relief for your Shites?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the children of Al-Abbas differ, and their authority weakens, and he who was not greedy for it before covets it, and the Arabs remove their reins, and every horseman raises his spur, and the Syrian appears, and the Yemenite comes forward, and the Hasany moves, and the Master of this Command comes out from Medina to Mecca with the inheritance of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' So I said, 'What is the inheritance of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The sword of the Messenger of Allah, and his armor, and his turban, and his gown, and his staff, and his banner, and his helmet, and his saddle, until he descends to Mecca.' He will take out the sword from its sheath, and put on the armor, and display the banner, and (wear) the gown and the turban, and grab the staff by his hand, and seek Permission of Allah for his appearance. That will be announced to some of his friends. The Hasany would come. So he would inform him of the news. The Hasany would initiate the coming out. The people of Mecca would pounce upon him. So they will kill him and send his head to the Syrian. During that, the Master of this Command will appear. So the people would pledge their allegiances to him and follow him. And the Syrian would send an army to Medina. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would destroy them before it (gets there). On that day, those from the children of Ali (peace be upon him) who would be in Medina would flee to Mecca. So they would join up with the Master of this Command. And the Master of this Command would go towards Iraq and send his army to Medina. Its people would express belief and they would return to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from some of the companions of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) came out to us while he was angry, and he said: 'I had just gone out for a need, and some of the black people of Medina presented themselves to me and shouted at me, saying: Here I am (Labbaik), O Ja'far ibn Muhammad, here I am! So I returned back to my house, fearful and panicked from what they had said, until I prostrated to my Lord in my mosque, rubbed my face to Him, humbled myself to Him, and distanced myself to Him from what they had shouted at me. And if Isa ibn Maryam had added anything to what Allah said regarding him, then he would have become deaf and would not have been able to hear anything after that ever, and become blinded and would not have been able to see anything after that ever, and become dumb and would not have been able to speak anything after that ever. Then he said: 'May Allah curse Abu al-Khattab and kill him with the iron.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jahm ibn Abi Juheyma, from one of the freedmen of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him said: A man from Quraish was with Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), and he began mentioning Quraish and the Arabs. Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him at that: 'Leave this! The people are three: an Arab, a Mawla (freedman/client), and an 'Ilj (foreigner/outsider). So we are the Arabs, and our Shias are the Mawali, and whoever is not upon what we are upon, he is an 'Ilj.' The Quraishi said: 'You are saying this, O Abu Al-Hasan, so where are the prided ones (afkhadh) of Quraish and the Arabs?' Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'It is as I have said to you.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ahwal, from Sallam ibn Al-Mustanir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrate: 'When the Qaim arises, he will present Faith to every Nasibi (Hostile One). If they enter it truly, [he accepts them]; otherwise, he will strike his neck, or he will pay the Jizyah just as the People of the Book (Ahl al-Dhimma) pay it today, and a strap will be tied around his waist, and he will be taken out from the cities to the dark places (al-Sawad).'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abu Salma, from Muhammad ibn Saeed ibn Ghazwan, from Muhammad ibn Bunan, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: My father said one day, while his companions were with him: 'Which one of you is pleased to take a burning ember in his hand and hold it until it extinguishes?' He said: 'All the people were silent and hesitated, so I stood up and said: O my father, do you command me to do it?' He said: 'I did not mean you specifically; you are from me and I am from you, but rather I meant them.' He said: 'And he repeated it three times, then said: 'How abundant is description (talk) and how scarce is action. Indeed, the people of action are few. Indeed, the people of action are few. Know that we recognize both the people of action and the people of description, and this was not pretense of ignorance from us towards you, but rather to test your news and record your impressions.' He said: 'By Allah, it was as if the earth had sunk beneath them out of shame from what he had said, to the extent that I looked at one of them sweating profusely, not raising his eyes from the ground.' So when he saw that from them, he said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, for I did not intend except good. Indeed, Paradise has levels, so the level of the people of action cannot be reached by anyone from the people of speech, and the level of the people of speech cannot be reached by others.' He said: 'By Allah, it was as if they had been released from their chains.'

And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah Al-Sufy, who said: Musa ibn Bakr Al-Wasity told me, saying: Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'If I were to distinguish my Shias, I would not find them except as those who merely describe themselves (talk). And if I were to test them, I would not find them except as apostates. And if I were to scrutinize them, not one out of a thousand would remain pure. And if I were to screen them with a sieve, there would not remain from them except that which was truly mine. Indeed, they have leaned upon their couches for a long time and said, We are the Shias of Ali. But rather, the Shia of Ali is the one whose action confirms his word.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-A'la, the freedman of the family of Sam, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'On the Day of Resurrection, a beautiful woman will be brought forward who had been tested (fitnat) due to her beauty. She will say: "O Lord, You made my creation beautiful until I encountered what I encountered." Then Maryam (peace be upon her) will be brought, and it will be said to her: "Are you more beautiful, or her? We made her beautiful, but she was not tested (did not fall into sin)."' And a handsome man who had been tested due to his beauty will be brought, and he will say: "O Lord, You made my creation handsome until I encountered from the women what I encountered." Then Yusuf (peace be upon him) will be brought, and it will be said to him: "Are you more handsome, or this one? We made him handsome, but he was not tested (did not fall into sin)."' And the owner of affliction, upon whom the trial had befallen in his affliction, will be brought, and he will say: "O Lord, You intensified the affliction upon me until I was tested (fell into sin)." Then Ayyub (peace be upon him) will be brought, and it will be said: "Is your affliction more severe, or his affliction? He was tested, but he was not tested (did not fall into sin)."'

And by this chain, from Abaan ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Basri, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'You sit in a place, narrate (hadith), and say whatever you wish, and distance yourselves from whomever you wish, and befriend whomever you wish.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Is life (luxury) anything other than this?'

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'May Allah have mercy upon a servant who makes us beloved to the people and does not make us hateful to them. By Allah, if they were to narrate the beauties of our speech, they would be more honored by it, and no one would be able to attach any fault to us. But one of them hears a single word and degrades it tenfold.'

Wuheyb narrated from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And those who give that which they give with hearts afraid" He said: This is for their intercession, and their hopes; they fear that their deeds would be rejected if they had not obeyed Allah, Mighty is His Remembrance, and they hope that He would accept from them.
Wuhayb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who calls to misguidance except that he finds one who follows him.'

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from a man from the people of Balkh who said: I was with Al-Reza (peace be upon him) in his journey to Khurasan. One day he called for a meal spread for him, and gathered upon it his black slaves and others. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, if you could isolate a meal for these people.' So he said, 'Muuh! The Lord, Blessed and High, is One, and the mother is one, and the father is one, and the Recompense is by the deeds.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The constitution of the body is based on four elements: among them is the air, without which the soul cannot survive except by its flow, and it expels from the body what is in it of disease and decay; and the earth, which generates dryness and heat; and the food, from which blood is generated. Do you not see that it goes to the stomach, which nourishes it until it becomes soft, then it clarifies, so the natural process takes its clarified state as blood; then the residue descends with the water, and it generates phlegm.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Husayn ibn Ayn (the brother of Malik ibn Ayn) who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the words a man says to another man: 'May Allah reward you with goodness (Khair)', what is meant by it? So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Khair' is a river in Paradise, its source is from Al-Kawthar, and Al-Kawthar's source is from the pillar of the Throne. Upon it are the dwellings of the Successors (peace be upon them) and their Shias. On the banks of that river are maids growing; every time one is taken, another grows in its place. It was named after that river, and that is His Exalted Statement: 'In them are goodly things (Khair), beautiful ones.' So when a man says to his companion: 'May Allah reward you with goodness (Khair)', he means by that those dwellings which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for His elite and the chosen ones from His creation.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Usmaan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In Paradise is a river, its banks are lined with thriving Houries. So if the Believer passes by one of them and she pleases him, he uproots her, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, plants another in her place.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me one night while I was in his presence, and he looked at the sky. He said: 'O Abu Hamza! This is the dome of our father Adam (peace be upon him), and for Allah (Exalted and Majestic) there are thirty-nine others besides it, in which are creatures who did not disobey Allah even for the blink of an eye.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said: A man entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, is this the dome of Adam (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, and by Allah, there are many domes. Indeed, behind this West of yours are thirty-nine other Wests, white lands filled with creatures who illuminate themselves with its light. They have not disobeyed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the blink of an eye. They do not know whether Adam was created or not; they distance themselves from So-and-so and So-and-so.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammaad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabalat, from Is'haq ibn Ammaar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever repairs his own shoes, and patches his own clothes, and carries his own merchandise, has freed himself from arrogance.

From him, from Salih, from Muhammad ibn Awramah, from Ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said: I, along with my partner Al-Qasim, and Najm ibn Hateem, and Salih ibn Sahl, were in Medina. We were debating regarding the Lordship (Rububiyya). Some of us said to the others, 'What are we doing with this? We are close to him, and none of us is in dissimulation (taqiyyah). Let us go to him.' He said, so we stood up. By Allah, we had not reached the door when he had come out to us without shoes or a gown, every hair on his head was standing up, and he was saying: 'No, no! O Mufazzal, and O Al-Qasim, and O Najm. No, no! But they are honored servants who do not precede Him in speech, and they act according to His command.'

From him, from Salih, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, for Iblees there is a helper called Tamreeh. When the night comes, he fills what is between the two horizons.

From him, from Salih, from Al-Washa’, from Karraam, from Abdullah Bin Talha who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the lizard, so he (peace be upon him) said: ‘Filthy, and it is a metamorphosed (creature), all of them. So if you were to kill it, wash yourself (Ghusl)’. My father was seated in Al-Hijr, and with him was a man to whom he was narrating. So a lizard started ululating with its tongue. So my father said to the man: ‘Do you know what this lizard is saying?’ He said, ‘I have no knowledge of what it is saying’. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘It is saying that if you mention Usman by insults, I will insult Ali (peace be upon him) until he goes from there’. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘And my father said: ‘There is none from the Clan of Umayya who dies, but he gets metamorphosed as a lizard.’ He (peace be upon him) said: ‘Abdul Malik Bin Marwaan, when death descended upon him, was metamorphosed into a lizard in front of the children who were in his presence. So when he was lost, that was a great (problem) for them as they did not know what to do. Then they met in a gathering, and decided to take a trunk and make it to look like a man. So they did that and clothed that with a coat of iron armour. Then they wrapped it in the shroud. So no one from the people knew about it except for myself and his children’.

From him, from Salih, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Mihran, from Abdul Malik ibn Bashir, from Usaym ibn Sulayman, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When one of you wishes for the Qa'im, let him wish for him in 'afiyah (protection/wholeness), for Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a mercy, and He will send the Qa'im as a wrath.

From him, from Salih, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdul Malik ibn Bashir, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was the most similar of the people to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) from his head to his navel, and indeed Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was the most similar of the people to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) from his navel to his feet. Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was the most similar of the people to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) from his head to his navel, and indeed Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was the most similar of the people to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) from his navel to his feet.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muqatil ibn Suleyman, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What was the height of Adam (peace be upon him) when he was descended to the earth, and what was the height of Hawwa (peace be upon her)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'We found in the Book of Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) that when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, descended Adam and his wife Hawwa (peace be upon her) to the earth, his feet were at the twin peaks of Al-Safa and his head was below the horizon of the sky. And he complained to Allah from the heat of the sun that was befalling him. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Jibraeel (peace be upon him):

Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdul Momin Al-Ansary, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, has granted the believer three characteristics: honor in the world and the Hereafter, success in the world and the Hereafter, and prestige in the chests of the unjust.

Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three things are the pride and adornment of the Believer in this world and the Hereafter: Prayer at the end of the night, his dejection from what is in the hands of people, and his Wilayah (guardianship) of the Imam from the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them).' He said: 'And three are the worst of the creatures, by whom the best of the creatures were tested: Abu Sufyan, one of them, who fought the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and was inimical to him; and Muawiya, who fought Ali (peace be upon him) and was inimical to him; and Yazeed ibn Muawiya, may Allah curse him, who fought Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and was inimical to him until he killed him.'

Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: There is no nobility for a Qureyshite nor for an Arab except through humility, and there is no prestige except through piety, and there is no deed except through intention, and there is no worship except through understanding. Indeed, the most hateful of people to Allah is the one who emulates the Sunnah of an Imam but does not emulate him in his deeds.

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Salamah al-Lu'lu'i, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Shall I not inform you of how the Islam of Salman and Abu Dharr was? So the man said, and he was hasty: 'As for the Islam of Salman, I have known it. Inform me of the Islam of Abu Dharr.' He said: 'Indeed, Abu Dharr was in the valley of Mar, tending his sheep. A wolf came from the right of his sheep, so he struck the wolf with his staff. The wolf came from his left, so Abu Dharr struck it.' Then Abu Dharr said to it, 'I have not seen a wolf more vicious than you, nor more evil.' The wolf said to him, 'More evil than I, by Allah, are the people of Mecca.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent a Prophet to them, but they belied him and insulted him.' This fell into the ears of Abu Dharr. So he said to his wife, 'Bring me my provisions, my bag, and my staff.' Then he set out on foot, intending Mecca, to know the news of the wolf and what it had brought him. Until he reached Mecca and entered it in a hot hour, having grown weary and exhausted. He came to Zamzam, being thirsty, so he scooped a bucket and it turned out to be milk. So he said to himself, 'This, by Allah, indicates to me that what the wolf informed me of and what I have come for is true.' So he drank and came to a side of the Masjid. There was a circle of Quraysh, so he sat with them. He saw them insulting the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), just as the wolf had said. They did not cease in that, mentioning the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and insulting him, until Abu Talib came from the end of the day. When they saw him, some of them said to others, 'Refrain, for his uncle has come.' So they refrained. He did not cease talking to them and speaking to them until it was the end of the day. Then he stood up, and I rose following him. He turned to me and said, 'Mention your need.' I said, 'This is the Prophet sent among you.' He said, 'And what do you do with him?' I said, 'I believe in him and affirm him, and I present myself to him, and he does not command me with anything except that I obey him.' He said, 'And you will do that?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Come tomorrow at this time to me, until I take you to him.' He said: 'I spent that night in the Masjid. When it was the next day, I sat with them. They did not cease

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Asbat ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Amina bint Wahb went into labor and the pains of childbirth seized her for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), Fatima bint Asad, the wife of Abu Talib, was present with her. She did not cease to be with her until she gave birth. Then one of them said to the other, 'Do you see what I see?' She said, 'And what do you see?' She said, 'This light that has shone between the East and the West.' While they were in that state, Abu Talib entered upon them and said to them both, 'What is the matter with you two? From what thing are you amazed?' So Fatima informed him of the light that she had seen. So Abu Talib said to her, 'Shall I not give you good tidings?' She said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Indeed, you will give birth to a boy who will be the successor (Wasi) of this newborn.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, and from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him) Regarding the Statement of the Exalted: 'Who is he that will Loan to Allah a beautiful loan? for (Allah) will increase it manifold to his credit, and he will have (besides) a liberal Reward', he said: 'It is the 'good' towards the Imam during the government of the mischief'.

Yunus narrated from Sinan ibn Tariq, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: It is befitting for the believer to fear Allah, Exalted and Glorified, with a fear as if he is overlooking the Fire, and to hope in Him with a hope as if he is from the inhabitants of Paradise. Then he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is according to the expectation of His servant; if he expects good, it will be good, and if he expects evil, it will be evil.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in Makkah when a messenger from Medina came to him. He said to him, 'Who did you travel with?' He said, 'I did not travel with anyone.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'If I had preceded you (or visited you first), I would have taught you good manners.' Then he said, 'One is a Satan, two are two Satans, three are a company, and four are companions.'

From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, saying: A man from the Banu Nawfal ibn Abd al-Muttalib told us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The most beloved companions to Allah are four, and if a group exceeds seven, their noise (or confusion) increases.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them both), regarding the will of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him). 'Do not go out alone on a journey, for Satan is with the one, and he is further away from the two. O Ali! Indeed, if a man travels alone, he is misguided, and the two are misguided, and the three are a group.' He said, 'And some of them reported: for travelling.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Qasany, from Suleiman ibn Dawood, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In the will of Luqman to his son: O my son! Travel with your sword, your slippers, your turban, your tent, your water container, your needle, your threads, and your awl. Take provision with you of medicines that benefit you and those with you. And be in concordance with your companions, except in the disobedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ali, from his father, from Al-Nowfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is from the nobility of a man that he should make his provisions good when he sets out on a journey.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Waleed ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: I entered upon him one day, so he threw to me some clothes and said: 'O Waleed, fold them upon their corners.' So I stood up in front of him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays.' So I thought that he was comparing my standing in front of him with the standing of Al-Mu'alla in front of him. Then he said: 'Ugh to the world! Ugh to the world! Indeed, the world is a house of affliction in which Allah makes His enemy overcome His friend, and indeed after it is a house that is not like this.' So I said: 'May I be your ransom, and where is that house?' He said: 'Here!' and he pointed with his hand to the ground.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are angels who cast off sins from the backs of our Shias, just as the wind casts leaves from the tree in the season of their falling.' And that is His statement, Mighty and Majestic: 'They glorify with the praise of their Lord...' And they ask forgiveness for those who believe. By Allah, He did not intend by this other than you.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: Abu Al-Khattab narrated to me in the best of conditions He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink He said: And when Allah is mentioned alone, it is by the obedience of the one whom Allah commanded obedience to from the Progeny of Muhammad, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; and when those are mentioned whom Allah did not command obedience to, behold, they are joyful.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim, the owner of the barley, from Kathir ibn Kaltham, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) Regarding the Statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then Adam received from his Lord some words' He said: 'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so forgive me, and You are the best of those who forgive.' 'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful.' 'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so turn to me in forgiveness, for You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful.' And in another narration, regarding His Statement, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then Adam received from his Lord some words,' he said: 'He asked for forgiveness by the right of Muhammad, and Ali, and Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn, and Fatima, peace be upon them.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth, he turned and saw a man committing adultery, so he supplicated against him and he died. Then he saw another, supplicated against him, and he died, until he saw a third, supplicated against them, and they died. So Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, Revealed unto him: 'O Ibrahim! Indeed, your supplication is answered, so do not supplicate against My servants, for if I willed, I would not have created them. I created My creation in three categories: A servant who worships Me and does not associate anything with Me, so I reward him; and a servant who worships other than Me, so he will not escape Me; and a servant who worships other than Me, so I will bring out from his loins one who worships Me.' Then he turned and saw a carcass on the coast of the sea, half of it in the water and half on the land. The beasts of the sea came and ate what was in the water, then returned, and some of them pounced on others and ate each other. The beasts of the land came and ate from it, and some of them pounced on others and ate each other. At that, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was astonished at what he saw and said: 'My Lord, show me how You bring back the dead.' He said: 'How do You bring back that which has consumed each other?' He said: 'Have you no faith?' He said: 'Yes, but just to reassure my heart.' Meaning, until he sees this just as he sees all things. He said: 'Take four birds, draw them to you, then place a portion of them on each mountain, cut them up, and mix them up just as this carcass was mixed up among these beasts that ate each other.' So he mixed them, then placed a portion of them on each mountain, then called them, and they came to him hastening. When he called them, they responded, and the mountains were ten in number.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the heat and the cold, from what do they emanate? He said to me, 'O Abu Ayyub! Indeed, Mars is a hot planet and Saturn is a cold planet. So when Mars begins to rise, Saturn goes lower, and that is in the spring. So they do not cease being like that; every time Mars rises a degree, Saturn falls a degree for three months, until Mars ends in its height and Saturn ends in its decline, so Mars becomes clear/dominant, and therefore the heat intensifies.' So when it is at the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, Saturn begins to rise and Mars begins to decline. So they do not cease being like that; every time Saturn rises a degree, Mars falls a degree, until Mars ends in its decline and Saturn ends in its height, so Saturn becomes clear/dominant, and that is at the beginning of winter and the end of autumn, and therefore the cold intensifies. And every time this one rises, that one falls, and every time that one falls, this one rises. So if there is a cold day in the summer, the action in that is due to the Moon, and if there is a hot day in the winter, the action in that is due to the Sun. This is the ordinance of the Mighty, the Knowing, and I am the servant of the Lord of the Worlds.'

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Ali! Whoever loves you and then dies, he has fulfilled his destiny; and whoever loves you and has not yet died, he is awaiting [his turn]. And the sun does not rise nor set except that it brings him sustenance and faith; and in another copy, [it brings him] light.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon my community when their inner selves will be foul and their outward appearances beautiful, greedy for the world, and not intending what is with Allah, their Lord. Their religion will become show-off; fear will not mix with them. Allah will encompass them with punishment from it, so they will supplicate to Him with the supplication of the Drowning One, but He will not answer them.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ali, together from Ismail ibn Mihran, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, and Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, together from Ismail ibn Mihran, from al-Munzir ibn Jayfar, from al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, from Abdullah ibn Jarir al-Abdi, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar, and the son of Abu Bakr, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), seeking preferential treatment for themselves. So he ascended the pulpit, and the people turned towards him. So he said: All praise is to Allah, the Patron of Praise, and the utmost limit of Generosity. Descriptions do not encompass Him, nor is He defined by languages, nor is He known by limits. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is the Messenger of Allah, the Prophet of Guidance, and the place of Piety, and the Messenger of the Highest Lord. He came with the Truth from the Presence of the Truth, to warn by the Illuminating Quran and the Illuminating Proof. So he declared by the Manifest Book and proceeded upon what the former Messengers had proceeded upon. Now then, O people! Do not let men say that the world had overwhelmed them, so they acquired property, made canals flow, rode the finest beasts, and wore the softest clothes. That would become a source of shame and ignominy for them if the Forgiver does not forgive them. If I were to prevent them from what they were indulging in and turn them to what they deserve, they would lose that and ask, saying: 'The son of Abu Talib has been unjust to us, deprived us, and prevented us from our rights.' So Allah is the Helper against those who face our Qiblah, eat our slaughtered animals, believe in our Prophet, testify our testimony, and enter our religion. We will apply upon them the judgment of the Quran and the limits of Islam. There is no preference for anyone over anyone else except by piety. Indeed, for the pious, with Allah the Exalted, is the best reward, the best recompense, and the best return. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not make the world the reward for the pious, and what is with Allah is better for the righteous. Look, O people of the religion of Allah, at what you found in the Book of Allah and what you left with the Mess

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Basir, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Humran asked him, 'May Allah make me a ransom for you! If you were to narrate to us when this Matter will occur, it would make us happy.' He said, 'O Humran! You have friends, brothers, and acquaintances. There was a scholar in the past who had a son who was not interested in his father's knowledge and did not ask him about anything.
