He had a neighbor who would come to him, ask him, and take knowledge from him. When death approached the man, he called his son and said, 'O my son! You have shown disinterest in what I have, your desire for it is low, and you never asked me about anything. I have a neighbor who used to come to me, ask me, take from me, and memorize from me. So if you need anything, go to him.' He introduced his neighbor to him. The man died, and his son remained. The king of that era saw a dream and asked about the man. It was said to him, 'He has died.' The king said, 'Did he leave a son?' It was said, 'Yes, he left a son.' The king said, 'Bring him to me.' They were sent to him to bring him to the king. The boy said, 'By Allah, I do not know why the king is calling me, and I have no knowledge. If he asks me about something, I will be disgraced.' He remembered what his father had bequeathed to him, so he went to the man who used to take knowledge from his father. He said to him, 'The king has sent for me to ask me, and I do not know what he has sent for me. My father had ordered me to come to you if I needed anything.' The man said, 'But I know what he has sent for you. If I inform you, then whatever Allah brings out to you, it will be between you and me.' He said, 'Yes.' He took an oath from him and made a binding agreement that he would be loyal. The boy made a binding agreement with him. He said, 'He wants to ask you about a dream he saw, as to which era it is. So say to him, 'This is the era of the wolf.'' The boy went to him. The king said to him, 'Do you know why I sent for you?' He said, 'You sent for me intending to ask me about a dream you saw, as to which era it is.' The king said, 'You speak the truth, so inform me which era this is.' He said to him, 'The era of the wolf.' So he ordered an award for him,

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Statement of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And give good tidings to those who believe that they have a lofty rank of truth before their Lord,' he said: 'It is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And what are the signs and the warners to a people who do not believe?' He (peace be upon him) said: When the ascension took place for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), Gabriel came to him with the Buraq, so he rode it and came to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and he met those he met from his brothers among the Prophets (peace be upon them). Then he returned and narrated to his companions: 'I came to Bayt al-Maqdis and returned during the night, and Gabriel had come to me with the Buraq and I rode it. The sign of that is that I passed by a caravan of Abu Sufyan being watered at the water of the clan of so-and-so, and they had lost a red camel of theirs, and the people were eager in searching for it.' So some of them said to others: 'He has come to Syria while riding swiftly, but you have come to Syria and recognized it, so ask him about its markets, its gates, and its merchants.' So they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how is Syria, and how are its markets?' He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when asked about something he did not know, would be distressed until it was shown to him. He said: So while he was in that state, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this Syria has been raised [shown] to you.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned, and there he was with Syria, its gates, its markets, and its merchants. So he said: 'Where are the questioners about Syria?' So they said to him: 'So-and-so and so-and-so.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) answered them in all that they asked him about, yet few among them believed. And this is the statement of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And what are the signs and the warners to a people who do not believe?' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We seek refuge with Allah from not believing in Allah and His Messenger. We believe in Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Zurara, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a believer says to his brother, “Uff!” (a sound of mild annoyance/dismiss), he comes out of his guardianship. And if he says, “You are my enemy,” one of the two has blasphemed, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not accept from anyone any deed while he is reproaching a believer with sincerity, nor does He accept from a believer any deed while he harbors evil in his heart against a believer.' 'If the covering were lifted from the people, and they looked at the connection between Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the believer, their necks would become submissive to the believers, their affairs would become easy for them, and their obedience to them would be gentle. And if they looked at the rejected deeds from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, they would say, “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not accept from anyone any deed.”' And I heard him saying to a man from the Shites: 'You are the good ones, and your women are the good ones. Every believing woman is a beautiful Hourie, and every believing man is a truthful one.' He said, 'And I heard him saying: 'Our Shites are the closest of creatures to the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection after us. And there is no one from our Shites who stands to pray except that the number of angels equal to those who opposed him surround him in it, praying for him in congregation until he finishes his prayer. And indeed, the one from among you who fasts is grazing in the gardens of Paradise, and the angels supplicate for him until he breaks his fast.' And I heard him saying: 'You are the people of Allah's greeting with His peace, and the people of Allah's impact with His mercy, and the people of Allah's guidance with His protection, and the people of Allah's call with His obedience. There is no accounting for you, and no fear, and no grief. You are for Paradise, and Paradise is for you. Your names in our presence are 'the righteous' and 'the reformers'. And you are the people of pleasure from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with His pleasure for you, and the angels are your brothers in goodness. So if you strive, they supplicate for you, and if you are negligent, they strive for you. And you are

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ja'far (peace be upon him) when he returned from Abyssinia: 'What was the most astonishing thing you saw?' He said: 'I saw an Abyssinian woman pass by, and on her head was a basket (miktal). A man passed by and bumped into her, causing her to fall, and the basket fell from her head. She sat down, then said: Woe to you from the Reckoner of the Day of Judgment, when He sits upon the Throne and takes for the oppressed from the oppressor. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was astonished.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) That Azar, the father of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), was an astrologer for Nimrod, and he did not issue a decree except by his command. So he looked at the stars one night, and in the morning he said to Nimrod, 'I have seen something strange.' He said, 'And what is it?' He said, 'I saw a newborn being born in our land, whose hands will bring about our destruction, and he will not remain long before being conceived.' He was astounded by that and said, 'Has the woman fallen pregnant with him yet?' He said, 'Not yet.' So he separated the women from the men, leaving no woman in the city whom a man could not reach. Azar copulated with his wife, and she conceived Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He thought he was the one, so he sent for the midwives of that time, who knew if there was anything in the womb. They examined her, and Allah (Mighty and Majestic) made what was in the womb adhere to the back, so they said, 'We do not see anything in her belly.' And what he was given knowledge of was that he would be burnt by the fire, and he did not know that Allah (the High) would rescue him. He said: When the mother of Ibrahim gave birth, Azar wanted to take him to Nimrod to kill him. His wife said to him, 'Do not take your son to Nimrod so he will kill him. Let me take him to one of the caves and leave him there until his time comes, so you will not be the one to kill your son.' He said to her, 'Go with him.' So she took him to a cave, breastfed him, placed a rock at the entrance of the cave, and then left him. He said: So Allah (Mighty and Majestic) made his sustenance in his thumb. He would suck it, and its milk would flow. He grew in a day as others grow in a week, and grew in a week as others grow in a month, and grew in a month as others grow in a year. So he remained for as long as Allah willed. Then his mother said to his father, 'If you allow me, I will go to that child.' He said, 'Then do so.' So she went, and there was Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and his eyes were shining like two lanterns. She took him, pressed him to her bosom, breastfed him, and then left him. Azar asked her about him, and she said, 'I have hidden him in the soil.' She continued doing this; she would go out for her need, go to Ibrahim

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of his father, and a number of our companions, all from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Abu Ziyad Al-Karkhy, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born in Kutha Ruba, and his father was from its people. The mother of Ibrahim and the mother of Lut were Sara and Warqa' (and in one copy, Ruqayya), two sisters, and they were both daughters of Lahij. And Lahij was a Prophet, a Warner, but was not a Messenger. And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in his youth was upon the natural disposition upon which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation, until Allah, Blessed and High, guided him to His religion and chose him. And indeed he married Sara, the daughter of Lahij, and she was the daughter of his maternal aunt. And Sara was the owner of much livestock, vast land, and good financial condition. And she had granted Ibrahim (peace be upon him) ownership of all that she owned, so he managed it and improved it, and the livestock and crops increased until there was no man in the land of Kutha Ruba who had a better condition than him. And when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) broke the idols of Nimrod, Nimrod ordered that he be captured and bound. They built a platform for him, gathered firewood in it, and ignited the fire, then threw Ibrahim (peace be upon him) into the fire to burn him. Then they withdrew from it until the fire extinguished. Then they looked at the platform, and there was Ibrahim (peace be upon him) safe and sound, released from his bonds. So Nimrod was informed of his news, and he ordered them to exile Ibrahim (peace be upon him) from their land and prevent him from leaving with his livestock and wealth. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) disputed with them regarding that, saying: 'If you take my livestock and my wealth, then my right upon you is that you return to me what has passed of my lifetime in your land.' They argued before the judge of Nimrod, who ruled that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) should surrender to them all that he had acquired in their land, and ruled against the companions of Nimrod that they should return to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) what had passed of his lifetime in their land. When Nimrod was informed of this, he ordered them to clear his path and the path of his livestock and wealth, and to expel him

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Munqari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Why do you not forbid these two men from this man?' He said: 'Who is this man, and who are these two men?' I said: 'Why do you not forbid Hujr ibn Zaydah and Amr ibn Jud'ah from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar?' He said: 'O Yunus! I had asked them both to refrain from it, but they did not do so. So I summoned them, and asked them, and wrote to them, and made it my need from them, but they did not refrain from it. So may Allah not forgive them both. By Allah, Al-Kuthayyir 'Uzzah is more truthful in his friendship than they are in what they claim of friendship with me, where he said: 'Does she not claim by the unseen that I do not love her? If I were not honored by her noble one, [I would not love her].' By Allah, if they both loved me, they would love the one whom I love.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Al-Qasim, the companion of Al-Mufazzal, and he was a truthful man, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A group in the Masjid publicize us and publicize themselves; those are not from us, nor are we from them. I go away and hide, but they uncover my veil. May Allah violate their veils. They say: 'Is he an Imam?' By Allah, I am not an Imam except for the one who obeys me; as for the one who disobeys me, I am not an Imam for him. Why do they cling to my name? Should they not cease mentioning my name from their mouths? By Allah, may He not gather me and them in one abode.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Quraysh went out to Badr, and they took the sons of Abdul-Muttalib with them, Talib ibn Abi Talib went out. Their poetic chanters descended (began chanting) while they were chanting, and Talib ibn Abi Talib descended (began chanting) and said: 'O Lord, if they invade with Talib, in a group from these groups, in a group of the conquering, the fighter, make him the plundered, not the plunderer, and make him the conquered, not the conqueror.' So the Quraysh said, 'This one will conquer us,' so they sent him back. And in another report from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) is that he was a Muslim.

Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Al-Mufaddal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Fatima (peace be upon her) went to a pillar in the Masjid, and she was addressing the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Events have occurred after you, and differences. Had you witnessed them, the matter would not have increased so much. We have missed you as the earth misses its downpour of rain. And your people are in disturbance, so witness them and do not be absent.'

Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in the Masjid, every high thing was lowered for him and every low thing was raised for him, until he looked at Ja'far (peace be upon him) fighting the disbelievers. He said: 'Ja'far has been killed,' and a severe pain seized him in his stomach.

Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Dahqan from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, the seller of al-Sabiri, from Ajlan, Abu Salih, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) killed forty with his own hand on the Day of Hunayn.'

Aban, from Abdullah ibn Ata', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the Buraaq, which was smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey. It had two vibrating ears, its eyes were in its hooves, and its steps were as far as its eyes could extend. When it ascended a mountain, its forelegs shortened and its hind legs lengthened; and when it descended, its forelegs lengthened and its hind legs shortened. It had a drooping right mane, and two wings behind it.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I recited: 'Al-Ta'iboon Al-Abidoun' (The Repentant, the Worshippers). He said: 'Do not recite Al-Ta'ibeen Al-Abideen up to its end.' I was asked about the reason for that, and he said: 'He bought from the believers, the repentant, the worshippers.'

Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzaal, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) So Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and strengthened him with hosts which you did not see. I said, 'Like this?' He said, 'This is how we recite it, and this is how it was Revealed'.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Statement of Allah (Exalted and Majestic): 'And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community; and they will not cease to differ, except those on whom your Lord has mercy.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They were one community, so Allah sent the Prophets to establish the Proof against them.'

Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own souls, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth." He said: He shows them the metamorphosis (al-masakh) in their own selves, and He shows them the breakdown/collapse of the horizons upon them, so they see the Power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in their selves and in the horizons. I said to him: [What is meant by] 'until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth'? He said: The emergence of Al-Qa'im is the truth from the Presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which the creatures will see; it is inevitable.

Muhammad ibn Yahya and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, both from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abbad ibn Yaqoub, from Ahmad ibn Ismail, from Amr ibn Kaysan, from Abu Abdillah Al-Ju'fy, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to me: 'How many Ribaat (guards) are there in your presence?' I said, 'Forty.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But our Ribaat is the Ribaat of eternity. And whoever attaches an animal for us, he will have its weight, and the weight of its weight, as long as it is with him. And whoever attaches a weapon for us, he will have its weight, as long as it is with him.' Do not grieve from once, or twice, or three times, or four, for our example and your example is like the example of a Prophet who was among the Children of Israel. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Call your people to the fighting, for I will help you.' So he gathered them from the tops of the mountains and from other places, then he directed them. So they neither struck with their swords, nor did they stab with their spears, until they were defeated. Then Allah the Exalted revealed to him: 'Call your people to the fighting, for I will help you.' So he called them. They said, 'You promised us the help, but no help came to us'. So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: 'Either they choose the fighting or the Fire.' So he said: 'O Lord! The fighting is more beloved to me than the Fire.' So he called them, and three hundred and thirteen of them answered him, the same number of the people of Badr. So he directed them. They neither struck with their swords, nor stabbed with their spears, until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted victory to them.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih and Al-Nawfali, and others, with an unbroken chain going up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not treat himself for catarrh (runny nose), and he would say: 'There is no one but that he has a vein of leprosy in him; so if catarrh strikes him, it suppresses it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The flu is an army from the armies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends it to the illness to eradicate it.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, by his chain, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no one among the children of Adam except that he has two veins: a vein in his head that incites leprosy, and a vein in his body that incites vitiligo. So when the vein in the head becomes active, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends catarrh upon it until what is in it of the disease flows out. And when the vein in the body becomes active, Allah sends warts upon it until what is in it of the disease flows out. So when one of you sees catarrh and warts, let him praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the health.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Catarrh is excess in the head.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from a man who said: A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was complaining about his eyes, so he said to him: 'Where are you from these three parts – the Aloe, the Camphor, and the Myrrh'. The man did that, and it went away from him.

From him, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih who said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We have a young girl who used to see the planet like a jar.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and she sees it like a grain.' I said: 'Her eyesight is weak.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Apply kohl to her eyes with the Sabr (a type of shrub), Myrrh, and Camphor in equal parts.' So we applied it to her, and it benefited her.

From him, from Ahmad, from Dawood ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far, meaning Abu al-Dawaniq, when a packet came to him. He untied it and looked inside, then took something out from it. He said, 'O Abu Abdillah, do you know what this is?' I said, 'What is it?' He said, 'This is something that comes from behind Africa, from Tangier or Tubna (Muhammad doubted). I said, 'What is it?' He said, 'There is a mountain there from which drops drip in a year and solidify. It is good for the whiteness that occurs in the eye; if this is applied to it, it will go away by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' I said, 'Yes, I know it, and if you wish, I will inform you of its name and its condition.' He said, 'He did not ask me about its name.' He said, 'And what is its condition?' So I said, 'This is a mountain on which a Prophet from the Prophets of the Children of Israel was hiding from his people, worshipping Allah upon it. So his people learned about it and killed him. So it (the mountain) weeps over that Prophet (peace be upon him), and these drops are from his weeping. And on the other side of it is a spring from which that water flows by night and by day, and it does not reach that fountain (of tears).'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleym, the slave of Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: He used to suffer from conjunctivitis in his eyes. He said: Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) wrote to him, initiating from himself: 'What is preventing you from using the kohl of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)? It is one part of Rabahiyya camphor and one part of Asqutry aloe. They are crushed together and sifted with silk. You should apply it like the application of antimony, one application in the month. It drives away every illness in the head and expels it from the body.' He said: So he used to apply it, and he did not complain about his eyes until he died.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd ibn al-Munthir ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave a sermon. (And others have reported it with a different chain, mentioning that he gave the sermon at Dhi Qar). So he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'As for what follows, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with the truth to bring His servants from the worship of His servants to the worship of Him, and from the covenants of His servants to His Covenant, and from the obedience of His servants to His obedience, and from the guardianship of His servants to His guardianship, as a bearer of good news and a warner, and a caller to Allah by His permission, and an illuminating lamp.' A return and a beginning, an excuse and a warning, with a judgment that He detailed, and a clarification that He perfected, and a Criterion that He distinguished, and a Quran that He made clear, so that the servants may know their Lord when they were ignorant of Him, and acknowledge Him when they denied Him, and establish Him after they had rejected Him. So He manifested to them, Exalted is He, in His Book without them having seen Him. So He showed them His forbearance, how He forbore, and showed them His pardon, how He pardoned, and showed them His power, how He is powerful, and frightened them from His authority, and how He created what He created from the signs, and how He destroyed whom He destroyed from the disobedient by the examples, and reaped whom He reaped by the retributions, and how He provided, guided, and gave. And He showed them His judgment, how He judged, and was patient until He heard what He heard and saw. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with that. Then, indeed, an era will come upon you after me, in which there is nothing more hidden than the truth, nor anything more apparent than falsehood, nor more numerous than lies against Allah the Exalted and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And in that era, there is no commodity more worthless than the Book when it is recited as it deserves, nor any commodity more worthy of sale and more expensive in price than the Book when it is altered from its places. And th

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Umar ibn Ali, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from Ibn Udhaynah who said, 'I heard Umar ibn Yazeed saying, 'Ma'rouf ibn Kharbouz narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him)' 'He used to say: Woe to his mother, a sinner, who does not cease to be argumentative; woe to his mother, an immoral one, who does not cease to dispute; woe to his mother, a sinner, who speaks much regarding other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Hasan ibn Umarat, from Nueym Al-Qazy, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) woke up in the morning and saw a white hair in his beard, so he said: 'The praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, Who has brought me to this stage/age; I did not disobey Allah even for the blink of an eye.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleym al-Farra', from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly. Except that he said in his hadith: When the angel said, 'Its Lord made me enter it,' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) recognized that he was the Angel of Death (peace be upon him). So he said to him, 'What brought you down?' He said, 'I have come to give good news to a man that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has taken as a close friend.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him, 'So who is this man?' The angel said to him, 'And what do you want from him?' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him, 'I will serve him for the days of my life.' The angel said to him, 'You are he.'

Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, with an unbroken chain, said: Whenever Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) recited this Verse: 'And if you would count Allah's favours, you will not be able to number them', he would say: 'Glory be to the One Who never Made it to be in anyone the recognition of His Favours except for the recognition falling short of (Al-Taqseer) recognising, just as He has never Made it to be in anyone the recognition of being aware of Him more than the knowledge that He cannot be perceived.' So gratitude be to the Majestic and Mighty for the recognition of the recognisers by their reduced recognition as appreciation, so He Made their reduced recognition as an expression of gratitude, just as He Knows that the knowledge of the knowledgeable people would not be able to perceived Him, so He made Belief as knowledge from it, so they cannot exceed that. So no one from His creatures can reach the limit of worshipping Him, and how can one reach the limit of worship of the One Who has no Limits for Him, impossible! Allah is Higher than that, Exalted and Great.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Anbasah ibn Bijad al-Abid, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: We were in his presence, and they mentioned the authority of the Umayyads. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No one rises against Hisham except that he is killed.' He also mentioned that his rule would last for twenty years. We were distressed by this. He said: 'What is the matter with you? When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intends to destroy the authority of a people, He commands the Angel, who hastens the pace of the orbit, so he gains control over what He intends to.' We said to Zayd (peace be upon him): 'This is the discussion we had.' He said: 'I witnessed Hisham, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was insulted in his presence, yet he neither denied it nor changed it. By Allah, even if there were no one but myself and my son, I would rise against him.'

And by this chain, from Anbasah, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Muhammad ibn Abdullah came up, greeted, and then went away. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sympathized with him, and his eyes shed tears. So I said to him: 'I have seen you do with him something you never used to do.' He said: 'I sympathized with him because he is attributed to a command that is not his; I did not find him in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) among the caliphs of this community, nor among its kings.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, by an unbroken chain, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to a man: 'What is considered to be the young one (al-fata) among you?' He said to him, 'The youth.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'No! The young one (al-fata) is the Believer. Indeed, the Companions of the Cave were old men, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, called them young men (fityah) due to their belief.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Isa — in a raised chain (mursal). He said: Verily Musa (peace be upon him) was engaged in intimate discourse (munajaat) with Allah, the Blessed and Exalted. He said to him in His discourse: 'O Musa! Do not let your hope in the world be prolonged, for that would harden your heart, and the hard-hearted one is far from Me. O Musa! Be as My desire of you — My desire is that I be obeyed and not disobeyed. Kill your heart with awe, and wear worn-out clothes with a renewed heart. Be hidden from the people of the earth and be known among the people of the heavens — a permanent dweller in your home, a lamp of the night. Perform qunoot before Me with the qunoot of the patient ones, and cry out to Me from the abundance of sins like the cry of the sinner fleeing from his enemy. Seek help from Me for that, for I am the best Helper and the best One sought for help. O Musa! Verily I am Allah, above the servants, and the servants are beneath Me, and all are submissive before Me. Accuse your soul regarding your own self, and do not trust your son in your religion unless your son is like you, loving the righteous. O Musa! Wash yourself, perform the ritual bath (ghusl), and draw near to My righteous servants. O Musa! Be their Imam in their prayers and their Imam in what they dispute, and judge between them by what I have revealed to you — for I have sent it down as a clear decree, a luminous proof, and a light speaking of what was among the former ones and what will be among the latter ones. ...and what will be among the latter ones. I bequeath to you, O Musa, the bequest of the compassionate and merciful: regarding the son of the Purified Lady, Isa son of Maryam, owner of the she-donkey, the hooded cloak, the oil, the olive, and the prayer niche. And after him, regarding the owner of the red camel, the pure and purified one. His description in your Book is that he is a believer, guardian over all the Books, bowing, prostrating, desirous and fearful; his brothers are the poor, and his helpers are another people. And in his era there will be hardship, earthquake, killing, and shortage of wealth. His name is Ahmad, Muhammad, the Trustworthy — from the remaining ones, from the group of the first and foremost, who believes in all the Books, affirms all the Messengers, and sincerely bears witness for all the Prophe

I read a reply from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to a man from his companions. After this [having praised God]: I hereby advise you to fear God; for God has taken the responsibility for whoever is pious toward Him to turn them from what He abhors toward what He loves, and to provide for them from where they do not expect. So beware of being among those who fear for [other] servants [of God] because of their sins while feeling themselves safe from punishment for their own sins. For God, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be deceived concerning His Paradise, nor can what is with Him be attained except by obedience to Him, God willing.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Aytham ibn Ashyam, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: One day the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came out having received good news, smiling with joy. So the people said to him: 'May God keep you smiling, O Messenger of God, and increase your joy.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no day or night except that I receive a gift from God in both. Indeed! My Lord has gifted me on this day of mine with a gift the like of which He has never gifted me before. Gabriel came to me and conveyed to me greetings from my Lord, and said: O Muhammad! God, Mighty and Majestic, has chosen seven from the Clan of Hashim the like of whom He has never created in those who have passed, nor will He create their like among those who remain. You, O Messenger of God, are the Chief of the Prophets; and Ali ibn Abi Talib, your successor, is the Chief of the successors; and al-Hasan and al-Husayn, your two grandsons, are the two Chiefs of the grandsons; and Hamza, your uncle, is the Chief of the martyrs; and Ja'far, the son of your uncle, is the Flyer in Paradise, flying with the angels wherever he pleases; and from among you is the Qa'im behind whom Isa ibn Maryam will pray when God sends him down to the earth — he will be from the descendants of Ali and Fatima, from the children of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

I said to him: [What is the meaning of] the statement of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'This is Our Book that speaks against you with the truth'? He said: So he said: Surely the Book has never spoken and will never speak, but the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) — he is the speaker for the Book. God, Mighty and Majestic, has [truly] said: 'This is Our Book that is spoken against you with the truth.' He [the narrator] said: I said: May I be a sacrifice for you, we do not read it like this. He said: By God, this is how Gabriel descended with it upon Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), but it is among what was altered from the Book of God.

A group, from Sahl, from Muhammad, from his father, from Abu Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the statement of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'By the sun and its brilliance' (91:1). He said: The sun is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — through him God, Mighty and Majestic, clarified for the people their religion. He (the narrator) said: I then said (what about) 'And the moon when it follows it' (91:2)? He said: That is the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who followed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and emitted knowledge into him by a radiant infusion. He (the narrator) said: I said (what about) 'And the night when it covers it' (91:4)? He said: That refers to the imams of injustice who usurped authority to the exclusion of the family of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and they sat in a position which the family of the Messenger were more deserving of than them. Thus they veiled the religion of God with injustice and tyranny, and God recorded their deed and said: 'And the night when it covers it' (91:4). He (the narrator) said: I said (what about) 'And the day when it reveals its clarity' (91:3)? He said: That is the Imam from the descendants of Fatima (peace be upon her) — when asked about the religion of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) he clarifies it for whoever asks him. And so God, Mighty and Majestic, referred to this in His statement, saying: 'And the day when it reveals its clarity' (91:3).

I said: 'Has there not come to you the news of the Overwhelming (al-Ghashiya)?' He said: 'Al-Qa'im will overwhelm them with the sword.' He said, I said: '(What about) "faces, that Day, humiliated"?' He said: 'Submissive, unable to resist.' He said, I said: '(What about) "labouring"?' He said: 'They acted contrary to what God revealed.' He said, I said: '(What about) "toiling/appointing"?' He said: 'They appointed other than the masters of authority (Wulat al-Amr).' He said, I said: '(What about) "entering into a blazing fire"?' He said: 'They will enter the fire of war in this world during the era of al-Qa'im, and in the Hereafter the fire of Hell.'

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) [regarding] the Statement of the Blessed and Exalted: 'And they swore by Allah with the most energetic of their oaths: Allah will not raise up him who dies. Yea! it is a promise binding on Him, quite true, but most people do not know.' He said: Then he said to me, 'O Abu Baseer! What do you say about this Verse?' I said, 'The polytheists are alleging and swearing to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) that Allah does not resurrect the dead.' He said: Then he said, 'Woe unto those who say this. Ask them: Did the polytheists swear by Allah or by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, enlighten me.' He said: Then he said to me, 'O Abu Baseer! When our Rising One (Al-Qaim) makes the stand, Allah will send to him a group from our Shiites with the sheaths of their swords upon their shoulders. So that will reach a group from our Shiites who did not die. They will say: So-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so have been resurrected from their graves and they are with Al-Qaim. So that will reach a group from our enemies. They will say: O group of Shiites, how you lie! This is your government and you are speaking lies about it? No, by Allah, those have never lived and they will not be living until the Day of Judgement.' He said: Then Allah quoted their words, saying: 'And they swore by Allah with the most energetic of their oaths: Allah will not raise up him who dies.'

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the statement of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Yet when they felt Our punishment, behold, they (tried to) flee from it. Flee not, but return to the good things of this life which were given you, and to your homes in order that ye may be called to account.' He said: When al-Qa'im makes his stand and sends (an army) to the Banu Umayya in Syria, they will flee to Rome. The Romans will say to them: 'We will not let you enter until you become Christians.' So they will hang crosses upon their necks and they will let them enter. When the companions of al-Qa'im descend upon them, (the Romans) will seek security and reconciliation. The companions of al-Qa'im will say: 'We will not do that until you hand over to us those who came to you from among us.' So they will hand them over. That is His statement: 'Flee not, but return to the good things of this life which were given you, and to your homes in order that ye may be called to account.' He said: He (al-Qa'im) will question them about the treasures, though he knows more than they do about them. He said: They will say: 'O woe unto us! Verily, we were wrongdoers.' They will not cease that invocation of theirs until We make them reaped and extinguished by the sword.

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazi' who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to Sa'd al-Khayr: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Having said that, your letter came to me in which you mentioned the necessity of knowing what must not be abandoned, and of obeying the one whose pleasure is the pleasure of Allah. And then you said to yourself what would have mortgaged your soul had you abandoned it. You marvel that the pleasure of Allah, obedience to Him, and His sincere counsel are neither accepted, nor found, nor recognized except among servants who are strangers and alone from the people — people have taken them as objects of ridicule for the evil acts they attribute to them. And it was said: A believer cannot be a true believer until he becomes more hated by the people than the carcass of a donkey. And had it not been that you suffer from the affliction similar to what we have suffered — so that you make the strife of the people like the punishment of Allah — I seek refuge with Allah for you and for us from that — you would have drawn near despite the distance of your station. And know, may Allah have mercy upon you, that the love of Allah cannot be attained except through the hatred of many people, nor His wilayah except through enmity with them. And losing their friendship is a small and easy matter for the attainment of that from Allah — for a people who know. O my brother, verily Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has placed among the successors of every prophet remnants from the people of knowledge who call those who have gone astray toward guidance, and endure along with them the harm; they answer the call of Allah and call toward Allah. So look to them — may Allah have mercy upon you — for they are in a lofty station even if they suffer lowliness in the world. They revive the dead through the Book of Allah and give sight to the blind through the light of Allah. How many slain by Iblis have they revived, and how many lost and strayed ones have they guided! They sacrifice their blood to protect the servants from destruction. How excellent is their effect upon the servants, and how ugly the effect of the servants upon them.

A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Basir, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting when the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) arrived. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'In you there is a resemblance to Isa son of Mary, and had it not been that groups from my community would say about you what the Christians say about Isa son of Mary, I would have said about you something such that whenever you pass among any people they would take the dust from beneath your feet, seeking blessings thereby.' He (the narrator) said: The two Bedouin Arabs and al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah and a number from the Quraysh with them became angry and said: 'He was not satisfied until he took Isa son of Mary as an example for the son of his uncle.' So Allah revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), saying: 'And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, behold, your people raised a clamour at it. And they said: Are our gods better or is he? They do not cite it to you but by way of disputation; nay, they are a contentious people. He was but a servant whom We favoured and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And had We willed, We would have made from you — meaning from Banu Hashim — angels in the earth to succeed.' [43:57-60] He (the narrator) said: Al-Harith ibn Amr al-Fihri became angry and said: 'O Allah! If this is the truth from You that Banu Hashim will be inheriting like Heraclius after Heraclius, then rain stones upon us from the sky or bring upon us a painful punishment.' So Allah revealed in response to the words of al-Harith, and this verse descended: 'But Allah would not chastise them while you were among them, nor will Allah chastise them while they seek forgiveness.' [8:33] Then he (the Prophet) said to him: 'O Ibn Amr, either you repent or you leave.' He said: 'O Muhammad! Rather, give the rest of Quraysh something from what is in your hands, for Banu Hashim has taken away the prestige of the Arabs and the non-Arabs.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'That is not up to me; that is up to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.' He said: 'O Muhammad! My heart does not submit to repentance, but I shall leave you.' So he called for his mount and rode away. When he reache

Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: 'Corruption has appeared in the land and the sea on account of what the hands of people have wrought' He said: That was, by God, when the Ansar said, 'From us [should be] a commander and from you [should be] a commander.'

I [Muyassar] said [to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)]: [What is meant by] the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order'? He said: So he [the Imam] said: O Muyassar, verily the earth was in a state of corruption, so God, Mighty and Majestic, corrected it through His Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), and [then] He said: 'And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al- Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Do not consummate (the marriage with your) female slave until she reaches the age of nine or ten. He added, 'I either heard nine or ten.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever has sexual intercourse with his wife before she reaches nine years old and she sustains an injury, he is liable (for it).

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one person, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The age of puberty for a woman is nine years.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, on the authority of Musa ibn Umar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin'an, on the authority of Abi Sa'id al-Qamat, on the authority of someone who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) established the alms-tax upon nine things and he forgave other things. They are: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, cows, sheep and camels. Someone asked, 'How about corn?' The Imam became angry and said, 'I swear by God that in the Prophet's lifetime sesame seeds, corn and birds' seeds were all available.' He was told, 'It is said that these did not exist at the time of the Prophet. That is why he has only established the alms-tax on those nine items.' The Imam became angry again and said, 'They lie. The Prophet's explicit order was to forgive everything else. One may only forgive what exists. I swear by God that the alms-tax has been made obligatory on nothing else but these nine things. Whoever wishes can accept it and anyone who doesn't wish can deny it and become an atheist.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Jamil, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) In how many items is alms-tax due? He said: In nine things which God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) established, and forgave tax on what is besides that. Al-Tayyar said: We have a grain called rice? He said to him: We also have much grain. He asked him: Is there anything due on it? He said: Did I not tell you that God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) forgave tax on what is besides that? Among them are gold and silver, and three from animals: camels, sheep, and cows, and from what the earth produces: wheat, barley, raisins, and dates.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated said: Abu Ishaq (whose nickname was Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'r) narrated said: Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi al-Sayrafi narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the nine signs that were given to Moses (peace be upon him). He said: The locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the flood, the sea, the stone, the staff, and his hand.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, from Al-Salam ibn al-Mustanir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of God, the Exalted: 'And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs,' he said: 'The flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the stone, the sea, the staff, and his hand.'

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim al-Khurasi (or al-Karkhi), from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, from Atiyyah, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Prophet of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali, I have been granted nine characteristics due to you: three in this world, three in the Hereafter, two are for you, and one is what I fear for you. As for the three in this world, you are my Trustee, my Caliph over my people, and the judge of my religion. As for the three in the Hereafter, I will be given the Banner of Praise, and I will place it in your hand, and Adam and his progeny will be under my banner; you will assist me at the gates of Paradise, and I will grant you authority in my intercession for whomever you love. As for the two that are for you, you will not return as an unbeliever or go astray after me. And as for the one I fear for you, it is the treachery of Quraysh towards you after me, O Ali.'

Al-Hussein ibn Yahya al-Bajaly narrated that his father narrated that Abu Zar'at narrated that Ahmad ibn al-Qasim narrated that Qatn ibn Naseer narrated that Ja'far narrated that Yaqoob ibn al-Fazl, from Sharik ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Rahman al-Mozani, from his father, that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: I have been granted nine characteristics due to Ali: three are for this world; three are for the Hereafter; two are for him and one is what I fear for him. And the three for this world are: he will be the one to cover up my private parts; he will be the one in charge of the affairs of my Household; and he will be my Trustee in my family. And the three for the Hereafter are: when I am given the Flag of Praise in the Hereafter, I will grant it to him to carry and I will lean on it at the time of the Rising for Intercession; and he will assist me at the gates of Paradise. The two that are for him are that he will not turn into an unbeliever or go astray after me. And the one I fear for him is that the Quraysh will act treacherously with him after me.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Hamiri both narrated to us, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'ada ibn Sadaqa al-Ruba'i, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The corruption of speech is lying, and the corruption of knowledge is forgetting, and the corruption of forbearance is foolishness, and the corruption of worship is laziness, and the corruption of cleverness is haughtiness, and the corruption of bravery is transgression, and the corruption of generosity is mentioning it, and the corruption of beauty is pride, and the corruption of lineage is boasting.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Adamy narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Zayat narrated to us from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from someone he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'We were with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) when the delegation of Abdul Qays arrived, greeted, and then placed a large quantity of dates before him. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) asked:

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from Abd al-Mumin al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Blessing consists of ten parts; nine-tenths of it are in commerce, and the remaining tenth is in skins. The compiler of this book said, may God be pleased with him: By skins is meant sheep. Confirmation of this is what has been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'Nine-tenths of sustenance are in commerce and the remaining part is in the spoils (of war),' meaning sheep.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us about this, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: Nine-tenths of the sustenance is in commerce, and the remaining part is in the spoils of war (sabiyah), meaning the sheep.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Sa’dan ibn Muslim - whose name was Abdul Rahman ibn Muslim, on the authority of al-Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abi Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said: Ten [characteristics] by which one meets God, the Mighty and Majestic, shall enter Paradise: bearing witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family); confessing to what came from God, the Mighty and Majestic; establishing prayer; giving alms-tax; fasting in the month of Ramadan; pilgrimage to the House; accepting the Guardianship of the Divine Leaders; and condemning God’s enemies; and avoiding all intoxicating drinks.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi narrated that Sahib ibn Ibad narrated that his father narrated, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them): He said: Ten [qualities] are those by which anyone who meets God shall enter Paradise: bearing witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family); confessing to what came from God; establishing prayer; giving alms-tax; pilgrimage to the House; fasting in the month of Ramadan; accepting the guardianship of the friends of God; being free from the enemies of God; and avoiding every intoxicant.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Al-Hussein ibn Al-Hasan Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Hafs Al-Basri, from Abdullah ibn Al-Hussein ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, God, the Mighty and Majestic, when He created Paradise, created it from two adobes: one of gold and one of silver. He made its walls ruby, its ceiling chrysolite, its pebbles pearls, and its soil saffron and fine musk. Then He said to it, 'Speak,' so it said, 'There is no god but You, the Everlasting, the Sustainer. Blessed is he who enters me.' Then God, the Mighty and Majestic, said, 'By My Glory, My Majesty, My Grandeur, and My Exaltation, the alcoholics, the drunkards, the tale-bearers (who are slanderers), the effeminate men (who are pimps), the detectives (who are eavesdroppers), the effeminate (hermaphrodites), the grave-robbers, the tax-collectors, those who sever ties of kinship, and the Qadarites shall not enter it.'

Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar all narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hussein narrated to me through a chain of his own which he links up (to the Prophet), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: He will not enter Paradise: the one who frequently drinks wine (alcoholic), the haughty/arrogant, the dutiful-to-parents-failer (unfilial), the one with intensely black hair, the pimp, the detective (Qallaa), the effeminate (Zanooq), the grave robber (Khayuf), the tax collector (Ashar), the one who severs kinship ties, and the Qadarite (determinist). The compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: What is meant by 'intensely black' is the one whose head hair and beard hair do not turn white despite his advanced age, and he is called 'al-Gharib' (the stranger/outlander).

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both, He said: Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, has made for the woman the patience of ten men. And when she becomes pregnant, He adds to her the strength [patience] of ten other men.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has made for the woman the patience of ten men; and when she becomes excited (or passionate), she has the strength of ten men.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from someone he mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Eat melons, for in them are ten characteristics: It is the fat of the earth, there is no disease in it and no harm, it is food and it is drink, it is fruit, it is a herb, it is a side dish, it increases sexual potency, it washes the bladder, and it promotes urination.

And Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Yahya ibn Ishaq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to the above.

In another tradition and it dissolves stones in the bladder and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat melons with fresh dates and in another report, he (peace be upon him) used to eat melons with sugar and Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Eating melons on an empty stomach causes hemiplegia and eating Al-Barni dates on an empty stomach could also cause hemiplegia

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from a man, from Ja'far ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Pleasure (or delight) is in ten things: walking, riding, swimming in water, looking at greenery, eating and drinking, looking at a beautiful woman, sexual intercourse, using the siwak (tooth-stick), and conversing with men.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adavi narrated that Sahib ibn Abbad narrated that his father narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them): He said: Pleasure (al-nushwah) is in ten things: walking, riding, swimming in water, looking at greenery, eating and drinking, sexual intercourse, using the siwak (tooth-cleaning twig), washing the head with mallow, looking at a beautiful woman, and conversing with men.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Hamad al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Aziz al-Qaratisi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abd al-Aziz! Indeed, faith (Iman) consists of ten ranks, like a ladder from which one ascends step by step. So do not say to the one who has two ranks, 'You are nothing,' until he reaches the tenth. And do not dismiss those who are below you, lest the one who is above you dismiss you. When you see someone who is lower than you, raise him to you gently, and do not burden him with what he cannot bear, lest you break him. Indeed, whoever breaks a believer must repair him. Al-Miqdad was in the eighth rank, Abu Dharr in the ninth, and Salman in the tenth.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Mu'awiya, from Muhammad ibn Hammad (the brother of Yusuf ibn Hammad al-Khazzaz), from al-'Aziz al-Qaratisi, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned to him some matters of the Shias and their sayings. He said: 'O Aziz, Faith has ten ranks, like a ladder that has ten rungs, and one ascends from it rung after rung. So the owner of the first rank should not say to the owner of the second, You are not upon anything (i.e., you have no faith). And the owner of the second should not say to the owner of the third, 'You are not upon anything,' until it reaches the tenth rank. He said: Salman was in the tenth, Abu Dharr in the ninth, and Miqdad in the eighth. O Aziz, do not dismiss those who are below you, lest those above you dismiss you. When you see one who is below you, if you are able to raise him to your rank gently, then do so. And do not burden him with what he cannot bear, lest you break him. For whoever breaks a believer, he must mend him, because if you try to carry a young camel with the load of an adult camel, you will break its back.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Mus'ab ibn Salam al-Tamimi, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever calls the adhan for ten years, holding it for God's sake, God will forgive him for as far as his sight reaches and as far as his voice reaches in the sky. Every moist and dry thing that hears him will acknowledge him. He will have a share of the reward of whoever prays with him in his mosque, and he will have a good deed for whoever prays due to his voice.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'az Al-Jawhari, from Amr ibn Jamee'a, who linked it up through his chain to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: Using the miswak (tooth-stick) contains ten characteristics: It purifies the mouth, it pleases the Lord, it multiplies good deeds seventy times over, and it is from the Sunnah. It removes cavities and whitens the teeth, strengthens the gums, cuts the phlegm, removes the haze of vision, and stimulates the appetite.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, saying: He narrated to us Nasr ibn Mizahim al-Manqari, from Abu Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) He said: I have ten [characteristics] from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) which no one before me was given, and no one after me will be given. He said to me: O Ali, you are my brother in this world and the Hereafter. You are the closest of people to me in standing [before God] on the Day of Resurrection. My dwelling and your dwelling in Paradise are facing each other, like the dwellings of two brothers. You are the Trustee, you are the Guardian, you are the Vizier. Your enemy is my enemy, and my enemy is the enemy of God. Your friend is my friend, and my friend is the friend of God.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Saqr the goldsmith of Ray narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Basam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Musa al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad informed me, from his father, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: I had ten characteristics from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): Each of which would please me more than everything upon which the sun shines and sets. Some of his companions said to him: Explain them to us, O Ali. He (peace be upon him) said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: O Ali! You are the Trustee, and you are the Vizier, and you are the Caliph over the Household and the Property, and your friend is my friend, and your enemy is my enemy, and you are the master of the Muslims after me, and you are my brother, and you are the closest of creatures to me at the Standing [on Judgment Day], and you are the bearer of my banner in this world and the Hereafter.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him), saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: I had ten characteristics from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), each of which would please me more than everything upon which the sun shines. He said: You are my brother in this world and the Hereafter, and you are the closest of people to me in standing position on the Day of Resurrection. Your house is opposite my house in Paradise, just as brothers face each other for the sake of God. You are the holder of my flag in this world and the Hereafter. You are my Trustee, my inheritor, and my Caliph over my Household, my property, and the Muslims in every absence. Your intercession is my intercession. Your friend is my friend, and my friend is the friend of God. Your enemy is my enemy, and my enemy is the enemy of God.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The noble characteristics are ten. If you can, let them be in you. For they may exist in a man but not in his son, and they may exist in his son but not in his father, and they may exist in a slave but not in a free person. They are: courage in battle, honesty in speech, fulfilling trusts, maintaining kinship ties, honoring the guest, feeding the beggar, repaying favors, showing humility to the neighbor, showing humility to the companion, and their head (or essence) is modesty.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Our father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Blessed and Exalted God has granted His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) noble characteristics. Test yourselves; if they are in you, praise God, the Mighty and Majestic, and aspire to Him for an increase in them. He mentioned ten of them: Certainty, Contentment, Patience, Gratitude, Satisfaction, Good Character, Generosity, Zeal, Bravery, and Chivalry.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Suleiman ibn Ziyad al-Minqari, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Isma'il al-Sadi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit al-Qurashi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari. Regarding the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, narrating about Joseph: 'I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon: I saw them prostrate themselves to me.' He then spoke about the naming of the stars: They are Al-Tariq, Jirban, Al-Ziyal, Dhul-Kanfan, Dhul-Qur', Qabis, Was'sab, Amudan and Faylaq, Misbah, Al-Darur, Al-Diya' and Al-Nur, meaning the sun and the moon. And all these stars encompass the sky.

Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Hamid narrated to us; he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us; he said: Ibn Arafah (meaning Al-Hasan) narrated to us; he said: Al-Hakam ibn Zahir narrated to us, from Al-Suddi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit al-Qurashi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: A Jew called Bostan al-Yahudi came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad, inform me about the stars that Joseph (peace be upon him) saw prostrating to him, what are their names?' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not answer him at that time about anything. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and informed the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of their names. He said: So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) sent for Bostan, and when he came to him, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked him: 'Will you submit to Islam if I inform you of their names?' He said to him: 'Yes.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jirban, Al-Tariq, Al-Zial, Dhu al-Kanfayn, Qabis, Was'sab, Amoodan, Al-Faylaq, Al-Misbah, Al-Zaruh, Dhu al-Qar', Al-Diya' and Al-Nur. He saw them in the horizon of the sky prostrating to him. When Joseph (peace be upon him) recounted this to Jacob (peace be upon him), Jacob said: 'This is a scattered matter that God, the Exalted, will gather together later.' He said: And Bostan said: 'By God, these are indeed their names.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Aban, on the authority of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There are twelve hours in the night and twelve hours in the day, and the best times of the night and day are the times of prayer. Then he (peace be upon him) said: When the sun sets, the gates of heaven open, the winds blow, and Allah, the Exalted, looks upon His creation. And I love that a good deed of mine ascends to the heavens at that time. Then he said: Adhere to supplication after the prayers, for it is answered.

Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: My uncle informed me, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, saying: Tha'laba dictated to us the hours of the night: Al-Ghasq, Al-Fahme, Al-Eshwa, Al-Huda, Al-Jonh, Al-Hazia, Al-Faqd, Al-Aqr, Al-Zulfa, Al-Sahra, and Al-Bahra; and the hours of the day: Al-Rad, Al-Shuruq, Al-Matu, Al-Tarhil, Al-Dakuk, Al-Januh, Al-Hajeer, Al-Zahira, Al-Aseel, and Al-Tifl.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'az ibn al-Juhari, from Amr ibn Jami'a, who linked it up to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: In the toothbrush (siwak) there are twelve attributes: it purifies the mouth, pleases the Lord, whitens the teeth, removes cavities and reduces phlegm, stimulates the appetite, multiplies good deeds, the Sunnah is attained through it, the angels attend to it, it strengthens the gums, and it cleans what you recite the Quran with. Also, two units of prayer said after using a siwak are more beloved to God, the Exalted, than seventy units of prayer said without using a siwak.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durost, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: In the Siwak (brushing teeth with a twig) there are twelve characteristics: It is from the Sunnah, it purifies the mouth, it clarifies the vision, it pleases the Merciful, it whitens the teeth, it removes the hollows (or bad breath), it strengthens the gums, it stimulates the appetite, it removes the phlegm, it increases memory, it multiplies the good deeds, and the angels rejoice in it.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Abul-Husayn al-Khadim (the pearl seller), from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: My father asked him while I was present: 'When is the affair of an orphan permitted (i.e., when does he attain legal majority)?' He replied: 'Until he reaches his ashud (full strength/maturity).' He asked: 'And what is his ashud?' He replied: 'Al-ihlatam (seminal emission).' He said: 'I said: The boy may be eighteen years old, or less, or more, and not have a seminal emission?' He replied: 'When he reaches the age (thirteen) and the matter is written upon him, his affair is permitted, unless he is a safih (foolish/impulsive) or weak (in mind).'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When the boy reaches his maturity at thirteen years of age and enters his fourteenth year, whatever is incumbent upon the sexually mature becomes incumbent upon him, whether he has had a seminal emission or not; his bad deeds are recorded and his good deeds are recorded, and he is permitted to manage all his property unless he is weak-minded or foolish.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, who said: He narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Sin'an, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: Major ritual ablution (ghusl) is required in fourteen circumstances: the ghusl of the deceased, the ghusl of the one in a state of major impurity (janib), the ghusl of the one who washed the deceased, the ghusl of Friday, the two Eids, the day of Arafat, the ghusl of Ihram and entering the Ka'ba, entering the Ka'ba, entering the Sanctuary (Haram), the visitation (Ziyarah), the night of the nineteenth, the twenty-first, and the twenty-third of the month of Ramadan.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Haytham al-Ajali (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qattan said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Fazl al-Hashemi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, who said: A group of the elders narrated to me, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that he said: Those who startled the Prophet’s she-camel upon his return from Tabuk were fourteen: Abul Sharur, Abul Davahi, Abul Ma'azif, and his father, Talha, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Ubaydah, Abul A'war, al-Mughirah, Salim - the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, Khalid ibn al-Walid, Amr ibn al-As, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. They are the ones about whom God, the Exalted, revealed: '…and they meditated a plot which they were unable to carry out.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahzar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah ibn A'yun, who said: I asked Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him): Is the Takbir on the days of Tashriq said after the prayers? He replied: The Takbir is in Mina after fifteen prayers, and in the provinces after ten prayers.
