The first Takbir is after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice, saying: 'God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, and to God belongs the praise, God is the Greatest for what He guided us to, and God is the Greatest for what He provided us with from the grazing livestock.' And the Takbir was established in the other provinces after ten prayers, such that when the people depart in the first departure, the people of the provinces refrain from the Takbir, and the people of Mina continue to say it as long as they are in Mina until the final departure.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq the merchant, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fuzalat, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Takbir on the days of Tashriq for the people of the cities (non-Mina residents), so he said: On the Day of Sacrifice, [it is] after the Dhuhr prayer until the completion of ten prayers, and for the people of Mina, fifteen prayers. If he stays until Dhuhr and Asr, he says Takbir.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever deals justly with the people regarding himself will be pleased with how others judge about him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked: What is the minimum right of a believer upon his brother? He replied: That he does not monopolize for himself what the other needs more than he does.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of Ali ibn Hisan, from someone he mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever bears oppression would not thank for blessings.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari, from Ali ibn Asbat, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: Whoever is not angered by slight neglect (or rudeness) will not be grateful for blessings.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashany, from someone he mentioned, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja’fari, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Hereafter is the wedding of the pious ones.

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sukuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both) He said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him: Why is it that I do not love death? He said to him: Do you have wealth? He said: Yes. He said: Have you sent it ahead (of you)? He said: No. He said: Then that is why you do not love death.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Malik ibn Atiye, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them) who said: There is no honor for a Qurashi or an Arab except through humbleness, and no nobility except through piety, and no deed except with intention. Beware, the most hated of people to God, the Exalted, is the one who follows the Sunnah of an Imam but does not follow his actions.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khattab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Collyrium helps hair to grow, dries tears, sweetens the saliva, and improves sight.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever seeks the pleasure of the people through the wrath of God, God will make those who praise him blame him.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Fuzalat ibn Ayoob, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Abi Zyad, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Whoever wishes for something while God is pleased with him, he will not leave this world until he is granted it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God have mercy on him - narrated that Al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daq'qaq quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Awf al-Ajli, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Washing (the hands) before and after food increases one's provision.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Fudayl's brother, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Among the sins that are not forgiven is a person's saying: 'I wish I was not held accountable for any deeds other than this one.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to him, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Husayn al-Farsi narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Nothing has been combined with anything better than forbearance with knowledge.'

Suleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayoob al-Lakhmy narrated that Abdul Wahab ibn Kharajat said: Abu Kurayb narrated that Ali ibn Hafs al-Abasi narrated that Al-Hassan ibn al-Hussein al-Alavi, from his father Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, from Al-Hussein ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I swear by Him in whose Hand is my soul that no two things have been combined better than forbearance (hilm) with knowledge ('ilm).

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Daybali narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: I heard al-Sha'abi say: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: In man there is a morsel of flesh; if it is sound and healthy, the rest of the body is sound and healthy through it; if it becomes sick, the rest of the body becomes sick and corrupts through it, and that is the heart.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Abul Abbas al-Siraj narrated to us, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Rashdin ibn Sa'd al-Misri, Abul Hajjaj, narrated to us, saying: Sharahil ibn Yazid narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When a man's heart is pure, his body is pure; and when the heart is diseased, the body becomes diseased.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) would, when it was the night of the twenty-first and the twenty-third, begin supplicating until the night passed; and when the night passed, he would pray.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Hussein ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from al-Sulayman al-Ja'fari, that Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Pray one hundred units of prayer on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third, reciting 'Al-Hamd' once and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' ten times in each unit.

Our father narrated, may God be pleased with him, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Fadal, from Abu Jamilah, from Rafaa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Night of Power is the beginning of the year and it is its end. Our elders, may God be pleased with them, agreed that it is the night of the twenty-third of the month of Ramadan, and the ritual bath (Ghusl) on that night is performed from the beginning of the night, and it is sufficient until its end.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Hassan ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), He said: I asked him about the Night of Power, so he said: Seek it on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyri, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, and Ahmad ibn Idris all narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Mu'az ibn Kathir (who is also called Mu'az ibn Muslim al-Harra'), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The month of Ramadan is thirty days; by God, it never decreases.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Yasir the servant, who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Will the month of Ramadan be twenty-nine days?' He replied: 'Indeed, the month of Ramadan will not be less than thirty days.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Raqqi, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, from his forefathers, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both). He said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him, with the most knowledgeable among them asking questions. Among what they asked was: 'Why has God made fasting for thirty days during the day incumbent upon your nation, while He made it incumbent upon other nations for more than that?' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, when Adam ate from the tree, it remained in his stomach for thirty days. So God, the Exalted, made it incumbent upon his offspring for thirty days: hunger and thirst. And what they eat is by God's grace upon them. Thus it was with Adam, so God made that incumbent upon my nation.' Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous. God, the Exalted, said: 'For a fixed number of days.' The Jew said: 'You are right, O Muhammad.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the saying of God, the Exalted: 'And to complete the period.' He said: 'Thirty days.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with them) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said in a long narration: The month of Ramadan is thirty days, as the Honorable, the Exalted God says: 'And to complete the prescribed period...' and 'complete' means the full/thirty days.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qattan narrated to us, from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, from Tamim ibn Buhlool, who said: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) say: God has not burdened the servants except with less than what they can bear. He has only required of them five prayers in the day and night; He has required of them twenty-five dirhams for every one thousand dirhams; He has required of them fasting for thirty days in the year; and He has required of them one Hajj pilgrimage, while they are capable of more than that. The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: The view of the special ones of the Shi'a and those of insight among them regarding the month of Ramadan is that it never falls short of thirty days. The narrations in this regard agree with the Book (Quran) and contradict the general public. Those among the weak of the Shi'a who followed the narrations that came for Taqiyya (concealment) stating that it decreases and is affected by the months' deficiency and fullness, have been cautious like the general public, and were spoken to only as the general public is spoken to. And there is no power except with God.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us; he said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) He said: No believer commits forty major sins in a day and night, then says while repentant: 'I seek forgiveness from God, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Eternal, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, and I ask Him to accept my repentance,' except that God forgives them for him. Then he said: And there is no good in one who commits forty major sins every day and night.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When I was taken up for the Ascension, I saw a womb hanging from the Throne complaining to its Lord about another womb. I asked it, 'How many fathers are between you and it?' It said, 'We meet in the fortieth father.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ali ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, who said: Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marvazi informed me, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever memorizes from my nation forty traditions that they need regarding their religious affairs, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a learned jurist. Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Hayyah al-Faqih informed me, in what he authorized for me in Balkh, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Harawi narrated to us, saying: Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hijr al-Sa’di narrated to us, saying: Sa’id ibn Najih narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) Whoever memorizes from my nation forty traditions from the Sunnah, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.

Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Hayyah the jurisprudent informed me in what he authorized for me in Balkh, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Harawi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hijr al-Sa'di narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Najih narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), saying: Whoever from my nation memorizes forty traditions from the Sunnah, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.

Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Harawi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Ahmad al-Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Urwah ibn Marwan al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Rabi' ibn Badr narrated to us, from Aban, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever preserves from me among my nation forty traditions regarding his religious affairs, seeking thereby the Face of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Hereafter, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a learned jurist.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Sa'iq, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Varraq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Hamzah ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi said: Al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah Ali ibn Muhammad al-Shazi narrated to us, from Ali ibn Yusuf, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: Whoever memorizes forty traditions from our traditions regarding the permissible and the forbidden, God will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment as a jurist, learned, and will not punish him.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Hussein ibn al-Mukhtar, linking it up through his chain to Salman, may God have Mercy upon him, that he said in his hadith: 'Whoever takes a female slave and does not have intercourse with her once every forty days, and then she commits a forbidden act, the burden of that sin is upon him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Uthman ibn Isa who linked it up through a chain of narrations to Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: If one takes a female slave and doesn’t have sex with her once every forty days, he would be held responsible for her sins.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadl, from Abdullah ibn Bakir, from al-Bukayr, from al-Ala' ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: In the book of Ali (peace be upon him), the blood money for a hunting dog is forty dirhams.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Sabih, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The blood-money of a hunting dog (Saluqi) is forty dirhams, as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered for the tribe of Khuza'ah.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me who said: Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi narrated to me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jumhor, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says in every day of Sha'ban seventy times: 'I seek forgiveness of God, who is no god but He, the Beneficent, the Merciful, the Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to Him,' his name is written in the Clear Horizon. He said: I asked, 'What is the Clear Horizon?' He said: 'A plain before the Throne, in which are rivers, in which are poured from two cups the number of the stars.'

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn al-Muzaffar al-Alawi al-Samarqandi narrated that Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ood, from his father, narrated that Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from al-Abbas ibn Hilal, said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) say: Whoever fasts one day in Sha'ban seeking the reward of Allah will enter Paradise, and whoever seeks forgiveness seventy times each day in Sha'ban will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment in the company of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and honor from Allah will become due for him, and whoever gives charity in Sha'ban, even if it is half a date, Allah will forbid his body from the Fire, and whoever fasts three days in Sha'ban and connects them with the fasting of the month of Ramadan, Allah will record for him the fasting of two consecutive months.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says 'La ilaha illallah' one hundred times would be the best of people in deed that day, except for one who increased (the count).

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hussein ibn Sayf (from Sayf), from Salam ibn Ghanim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever says when he lies down in his bed 'There is no god but God' one hundred times, God will build a house for him in Paradise; and whoever seeks forgiveness from God when he lies down in his bed one hundred times, his sins will fall off as the leaves of a tree fall.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sin'ani, al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mokattib, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Sa'iq, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Varraq (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan said: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: These are the religious decrees for whoever wishes to adhere to them, and God guides him: Spreading the ablution as God the Exalted commanded in His Speaking Book: washing the face and hands to the elbows, wiping the head and feet to the ankles, once or twice is permissible. Ablution is only broken by urine, wind, sleep, feces, and major impurity. Whoever wipes over his slippers has contradicted God, His Messenger, and His Book, his ablution is not complete, and his prayer is not accepted. The ritual baths include: bath of major impurity, menstruation, bath of the dead, bath of one who touched the dead after it cools, bath of one who washed the dead, bath of Friday, bath of the two Eids, bath of entering Mecca, bath of entering Medina, bath of visitation, bath of Ihram, bath of the day of Arafat, bath of the 17th night of Ramadan, bath of the 19th night of Ramadan, bath of the 21st and 23rd nights thereof. As for the obligatory bath, it is the bath of major impurity, and the bath of major impurity and menstruation are one.

The obligatory prayer: Dhuhr is four units, Asr is four units, Maghrib is three units, the last 'Isha is four units, and Fajr is two units. The total obligatory prayer is seventeen units, and the Sunnah is thirty-four units. Among them, four units after Maghrib are not shortened on journey or in residence; two units while sitting after the last 'Isha count as one unit; eight units at dawn are the night prayer; the even (Shaf') is two units, the odd (Witr) is one unit, and the two units of Fajr are after the Witr; eight units before Dhuhr and eight units before Asr. Prayer is recommended at the beginning of the times. The merit of congregational prayer over individual prayer is twenty-four times. Do not pray behind a sinful person, and do not follow except those of Divine Leadership. Do not pray while wearing the skins of a dead animal, even if tanned seventy times, nor the skins of beasts. Do not prostrate except on the earth or what the earth produces, except for what is edible, cotton, and linen. In the opening of the prayer, one says: 'Ta'ala Arshak' (Exalted is Your Throne), and it is not said: 'Ta'ala Jaddak' (Exalted is Your Grandeur). And in the first Tashahhud, it is not said: 'As-salamu alayna wa ala ibadillah is-salihin' because the termination of the prayer is the Taslim, and if you say this, your prayer has ended. Shortening (Qasr) is valid after eight Farsakhs, which is two Barids. If you shorten, you break your fast. Whoever does not shorten on a journey, their prayer is not valid because they have added to what God has prescribed. Qunut in all prayers is a mandatory Sunnah in the second unit before bowing and after recitation. Funeral prayer has five Takbirat; whoever reduces them has opposed the Sunnah. The male corpse is lowered feet first, and the female is lowered sideways from the side of the grave. Graves are squared (leveled) and do not rise. Saying 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim' aloud in prayer is obligatory. The pillars of prayer are seven: Time, Purity, Orientation, Qibla, Bowing, Prostration, and Supplication. Zakat is an obligatory duty on every two hundred Dirhams, which is five Dirhams. It is not obligatory on less than that from silver. Zakat is not obligatory on wealth until a full year passes from the day the owner acquired it. Zakat should not be given except to those of Divine Leadership and Recognition. Zakat is obligatory

Goodness to parents is obligatory; if they are polytheists, do not obey them or anyone else in sin, for there is no obedience to the created in disobedience to the Creator. The Prophets and the Trustees have no sins because they are infallible and purified. The validity of the two Mutas is obligatory as God revealed them in His Book and the Messenger of God practiced them: the temporary Hajj and the temporary marriage of women. The inheritance laws are as ordained by God the Blessed and Exalted. The Aqiqah sacrifice is for the male and female child on the seventh day; the child is named on the seventh day, his head is shaved, and charity equal to the weight of his hair in gold or silver is given. God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. The actions of servants are created by creation of decree, not creation of formation; God is the Creator of all things. They do not say predestination (Jabr) nor total delegation (Tafwid). God does not take the innocent for the guilty, nor punish children for the sins of fathers, as He said: 'No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another,' and 'Man shall have nothing but what he strives for, and his striving will be seen.' God may forgive and grant favor, but He does not oppress. He does not command obedience to one He knows misleads, nor choose as Messenger one He knows disbelieves, nor make a proof over creation except an infallible one. Islam is distinct from Iman; every believer is a Muslim, but not every Muslim is a believer. A thief is not a believer while stealing, nor an adulterer while committing adultery. Those subject to Hadd punishments are Muslims, neither believers nor unbelievers. God does not put a believer in Hell who was promised Paradise, nor take an unbeliever out of Hell who was promised eternal punishment therein. He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Those subject to Hadd are sinners, neither believers nor unbelievers, and they do not remain in Hell forever, but will be taken out one day. Intercession is valid for them and for the oppressed if God is pleased with their religion. The Quran is the Speech of God; it is neither the Creator nor the created. The world today is a house of Taqiyyah (concealment), it is a house of Islam, not a house of Disbelief nor a house of Faith (in the strict sense). Enjoining good and forbidding evil is obligatory upon whoever has the ability and

And the major sins are forbidden namely: associating partners with Allah, the Exalted; killing the soul which Allah has forbidden; disrespecting parents; fleeing from the ranks in battle; devouring the property of an orphan oppressively; consuming usury after clear proof; falsely accusing chaste women; and after that, adultery, sodomy, and theft; eating dead animals, blood, and pork, and what is offered to other than Allah without necessity; consuming ill-gotten wealth; shortchanging in measure and weight; gambling; false testimony; losing hope in Allah's spirit (/forgiveness); feeling secure from Allah's plot; despairing of Allah's mercy; abandoning helping the oppressed and leaning towards the tyrants; the false oath that drowns (in sin); withholding rights without hardship; using haughtiness, arrogance, lying, extravagance, and wastefulness; treachery; underestimating the Hajj; fighting the friends of Allah, the Exalted; and entertainments that divert from the remembrance of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, such as singing and playing strings, are disliked, as is persisting in minor sins. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, in this is sufficient for a people of worshippers.' The compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'The major sins are seven, and after them [others]. So every sin is major in relation to what is smaller than it, and minor in relation to what is greater than it. This is the meaning of what As-Sadiq (peace be upon him) mentioned in this hadith regarding the major sins exceeding the seven, and there is no power except with Allah.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, and Ibrahim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Hamad al-Ansari, from Sabah al-Mazni, from Al-Harith ibn Hasira, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught me one thousand gates of the permissible and the forbidden, and what has been and what shall come all the way up until the Resurrection Day. Each of these gates opened one thousand gates, so that they turned into one million gates. Thus, I acquired the knowledge of deaths, calamities and the Divine Decrees.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hassanjani said: Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn Afir narrated to me, from Ibn Lahay'at and Rashdayn ibn Sa'd, from Hurayz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, from Abdullah ibn Amr [and] he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said during the illness in which he died: 'Call my brother.' So they sent for Ali (peace be upon him). When he entered, the Prophet and Ali turned their faces to the wall and covered themselves with a cloak, and he whispered to him while the people were crowded behind the door. Then Ali (peace be upon him) came out. A man from the people asked him, 'Did the Prophet of God disclose something to you?' He said, 'Yes. He disclosed to me a thousand gates, and in each gate a thousand gates.' The man said, 'Did you memorize them?' He said, 'Yes, and I understood them.' The man said, 'Then what is the blackness in the moon?' Indeed, God, the Mighty and Exalted, said: 'And We have made the night and the day two signs, so We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account [of time]. And everything We have set in detail.' The man said to him, 'You truly understood it, O Ali.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'If a person goes into a coma for one day, two days, three days, four days, or more than that, how much of his prayer must he compensate?' He said: 'Shall I not inform you of what encompasses this and its like? Whatever God, Exalted and Mighty, prevents from His command, He excuses the servant for, and adds to it for him. Indeed, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from the chapters which open each of its gates to one thousand gates.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me who said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Umar ibn Azineh, from Bakir ibn A'yn, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsa, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand chapters, each of which opens another one thousand chapters. So our companions went and asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about that, and it turned out that Salim had told the truth. Bakir said: And someone who heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrating this hadith narrated it to me, then he said: And not more than one or two of those chapters went out to the people. And most of my knowledge is that he said: Only one chapter.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Muhammad ibn Amer, from Ma'la ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Bastam ibn Marah, from Ishaq ibn Hisan, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Al-Asbagh ibn al-Nubatah said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered us to travel to Madaen from Kufa, so we set out on Sunday. Amr ibn Harith and seven others stayed behind and went to a place in Hira called Al-Khoranq, saying, 'We will amuse ourselves here, and when it is Wednesday, we will leave and catch up with Ali (peace be upon him) before he leads the Friday prayer.' While they were eating lunch, a lizard emerged before them. They hunted it, and Amr ibn Harith took it, raised his palm, and said, 'Pledge allegiance to this Commander of the Faithful.' The seven pledged allegiance to it, and Amr was the eighth. They departed on Wednesday night and arrived in Madaen on Friday while the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was delivering the sermon. They did not separate from one another and remained together until they arrived at the door of the mosque. When they entered, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) looked at them. He said, 'O people! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) disclosed to me one thousand narrations, each containing one thousand gates, and for each gate one thousand keys.' And I heard God, may His Majesty be Exalted, say: 'One day We shall call every group with their Imam...' And I swear to you by God that on the Day of Resurrection, eight people will be resurrected with their leader, who will be a lizard. If I wished, I could name them for you. He said, 'I saw Amr ibn Harith fall down as a date palm branch falls, from shame and reproach.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn Hamzah al-Adawi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a gate which opens one thousand gates, and each of those gates opens one thousand gates.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Bashir al-Dahan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was ill with the illness in which he died, he sent for Ali (peace be upon him). When Ali came, he leaned over him and kept speaking to him and he kept speaking to him. When he came out, they met him and said to him: 'What did your companion tell you?' He said: 'He told me of a gate that opens a thousand gates, each of which opens a thousand gates.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me: Ahmad and Abdullah, the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, narrated to me, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who said: I heard some of the trustworthy companions of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) say: There is in this chest of mine a vast amount of knowledge which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught me. If I could find guardians for it who would preserve it as it deserves and transmit it as they hear it from me, I would have bequeathed some of it to them. Thus, much of the knowledge was known through it. Indeed, knowledge is the key to every door, and every door opens a thousand doors.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd and Ibrahim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Hamad al-Ansari, from Sabah al-Mazni, from Harith ibn Hasira, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught me one thousand gates of the permissible and the forbidden, of what has been and what will be until the Day of Resurrection. Each of these gates opens one thousand gates, so that makes one million gates. Thus, I acquired the knowledge of deaths, calamities, and the distinction of speech (Divine Decree).

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with them) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hijjal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from al-Karim ibn Amr, from al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) advised Ali (peace be upon him) with one thousand gates; each gate opens one thousand gates.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Bajli, from Abu Yahya Mu'amar al-Qattan, from Bashir al-Dahan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), in the illness in which he died, said: 'Call my friend to me.' So they sent for his two fathers (Abu Bakr and Umar). When he looked at them, he turned his face away from them and said: 'Call my friend to me.' So Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was sent for. When he looked at him, he leaned over him and conversed with him. When he came out, the two men met him and asked: 'What did your friend tell you?' He said: 'He told me of a thousand gates, each gate opening a thousand gates.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Yahya ibn Imran al-Hamedany, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, on the authority of Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'It has reached us that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand gates, each of which opens one thousand gates?' He said: 'Yes.' [Then he said to me: 'Rather, He taught him a single gate, and that gate opened one thousand gates, and each of those gates opened one thousand gates.']

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Yaqoob ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught me one thousand gates, each of which opens one thousand gates.

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, (on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal), from Abdullah Bakir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) [a gate which opens up to him] one thousand gates, each of which opens up to one thousand gates.

Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from some of his companions, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from Abu Basir, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: The Shiites say that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a gate from which a thousand gates are opened, each gate opening a thousand gates. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Muhammad! I swear by God that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a thousand gates, each gate opening a thousand gates. I said to him: By God, this is true knowledge! He said: Indeed, it is knowledge, and for no one else but him, and it is not that (i.e., not exclusive in a way that implies exclusivity of the concept, but rather specific to Ali's station).

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ya'qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Murazim ibn Hakim al-Azdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand gates, each of which opens up to another one thousand gates.

Narrated to us my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hanifa ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, may God be pleased with them, who said: Narrated to us Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Aqbah, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Abu Bakr and Umar came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) when Fatimah (peace be upon her) was buried. In a long narration, he said to them: As for what you mentioned that I did not call you in for the task of the ritual washing of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), indeed he said: 'No one other than you shall see my private parts, except his sight will be lost.' Therefore, I did not permit you to do so. And as for my bowing over him (placing my ear near his mouth), indeed he taught me one thousand letters, each letter opening up one thousand letters. Therefore, I did not reveal it to you, as if it were the secret of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ya'qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Mansur ibn Yunus, on the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hudhrami, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand letters, each letter opens up one thousand letters, and the thousand [letters] is [but] one letter.

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hakam, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, on the authority of Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There was a small booklet in the cover (thong) of the sword of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What was in that booklet?' He said: 'It was the letters, each of which opens up a thousand letters.' They said: Abi Basir said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Only two of those letters have been revealed/interpreted until now.'

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Three hundred and thirteen will come to your mosque — that is in Mecca. The people of Mecca will know that their fathers and grandfathers did not give birth to them. They will have swords upon them. Written on each sword is a word that opens to a thousand words. The wind will be sent and call out in every valley: 'This is the Mahdi, who will judge with the judgment of the family of David.' He will not be asked for any proof/evidence regarding him.

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir and Abdul Karim ibn Amr, from Abdul Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entrusted Ali (peace be upon him) with a thousand doors, each word and each door opening to a thousand words and a thousand doors.

Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to me, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Bajali, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) covered Ali (peace be upon him) with a cloak, then taught him a thousand words.

His father, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil, Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih, Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Natanat, al-Hussein ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mo'adab, and Ahmad ibn Zyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamedany - may the Sublime God be pleased with them - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sani (peace be upon him) that he heard him say: God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand words. Each word opened up to one thousand new words.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both) That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand words, each word opening up to one thousand [new] words, so the people do not know what he had taught him.

Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abu al-Maghra' Humayd ibn al-Muthanna al-Ajli, from Dharih ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Muharibi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: We are the successors of the Prophets. Then he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) honored Ali (peace be upon him) with a cloak, then taught him one thousand words, each word opening up to one thousand words.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Mansoor ibn Hazim, on the authority of Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand words, each of which opens up to one thousand words.

My father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Bajali and al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said in the illness in which he passed away: 'Call for my friend.' So Aisha and Hafsa sent for their fathers. When they came, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) covered his face and head, so they returned. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) uncovered his head and said: 'Call for my friend.' So Hafsa sent for her father and Aisha sent for her father. When they came, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) covered his face. So they went away and said: 'We do not think the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) wanted us.' They said: 'Yes, he only said: Call for my friend' or he said: 'Call for my beloved,' so we hoped that you two were the ones. Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) came to him. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) pressed his chest to his chest and gestured to his ear, and he narrated to him one thousand narrations, each of which has one thousand chapters.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Senani al-Mokattib, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Mo’ad’dab, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Var’raq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: When it was time for the death of God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) called me in. When I went to see him, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told me, ‘O Ali! You are my Trustee and my successor over my Household and my Nation both during my life and after my death. Your friends will be my friends and my friends are God’s friends. Your enemies will be my enemies and my enemies are God’s enemies. O Ali! Whoever denies your mastery after me, it is as if he has denied my Messengership during my life. You are from me and I am from you.’ Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked me to get close to him and taught me one-thousand gates of knowledge each of which opens up to one-thousand gates.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu al-Jawza' al-Munabbih ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, the two-faced person will come with his tongue hanging out from behind his neck, and another tongue in front of him; the two tongues will burn with fire until they burn his body. Then it will be said to him: 'This is the one who had two faces and two tongues in the world; he will be known by that on the Day of Resurrection.'

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Muni'a narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba narrated to us, saying: Abu Muawiyah narrated from Al-A'amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, among the worst of people near God, the Exalted and Mighty, on the Day of Resurrection are the two-faced ones.'

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Muni'a told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba narrated to us, from Sharik, from Al-Rakin, from Na'eem ibn Hanzale, from Ammar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: He who has two faces in this world will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ibn Sinan, from al-Awn ibn Ma'yan (the hat-seller), from Ibn Abi Ya'foor, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Whoever meets the believers with one face (countenance), but gossips about them in their absence with another face, will come on the Day of Resurrection having two tongues of fire.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shaybah al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A servant who is two-faced and has two tongues is bad. He will praise his believing brother in front of him, but talk badly about him in his absence. He will be jealous of him whenever he gets a blessing and will not assist him when a calamity befalls him.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said: Abu Dharr (may God have Mercy upon him) stood by the Ka'ba and said, 'I am Jundab ibn Sakan.' The people gathered around him. He said, 'If one of you intended to travel, he would take provisions to sustain him. The journey of the Day of Resurrection is coming; do you not want to take what will sustain you?' A man stood up to him and said, 'Guide us.' He said, 'Fast on a day of intense heat for the Resurrection, and perform a Hajj for the major affairs. Pray two units in the darkness of the night for the loneliness of the graves. Speak a word of good and remain silent from a word of evil, or give charity from you to a poor person, perhaps you may be saved by it, O one who submits, from the Day of Hardship. Consider this world to be two Dirhams: one Dirham you spend on your family, and one Dirham you send ahead for your Hereafter. The third is harmful and does not benefit, so do not return it (keep it). Consider this world to be two words: one word in seeking the Halal (permissible sustenance) and one word for the Hereafter. The third is harmful and does not benefit, so do not return it.' Then he said, 'A sorrow killed me on a day I could not attain.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musa ibn Akeel, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: A man will not be a scholar (faqih) until he does not care which of his two shirts is more worn out, and what he eats to overcome his hunger.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: He told me Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Hamiri, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Any Muslim servant whom God advises sincerely regarding his own soul, giving it its due right and taking its due right for it, is granted two characteristics: sustenance from God, the Exalted and Mighty, with which he is content, and God's Pleasure with which he is saved.
And in another narration God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is pleased with his good deeds and feels bad about his bad deeds is a believer.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, saying: Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zahri narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abi Ali al-Lahabi narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, what I fear most for my nation is unbridled desire (al-hawa) and prolonging of hope (tawil al-amal). As for unbridled desire, it turns one away from the truth; and as for prolonging of hope, it causes one to forget the Hereafter. This world has departed, moving away, and the Hereafter has arrived, moving forward. Each of them has its own children. If you are able to be among the children of the Hereafter and not among the children of the world, then do so. Indeed, today you are in a house of action and no reckoning, and tomorrow you will be in a house of reckoning and no action.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Azineh, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said in his speech: The scholars are two types: a scholar who acts upon his knowledge, he is successful; and a scholar who abandons his knowledge, he is destroyed. And indeed, the people of Hell will be bothered by the smell of the scholar who abandons his knowledge. And the most regretful and remorseful of the people of Hell is a man who invited a servant to God, and God accepted his call and he obeyed God, so God entered him into Paradise, but He entered the caller into Hell for abandoning his knowledge and following his whims. Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the two things I fear most for you are following whims and long expectations. As for following whims, it diverts from the truth, and long expectations make one forget the Hereafter.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Mufaddal ibn Mazid, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: I admonish you against two characteristics in which men are ruined: to worship God with falsehood and to give fatwa to people based on what you do not know.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: I admonish you against two characteristics, in which those who perished perished: Beware of giving fatwa to people based on your own opinion, or basing your religion on what you do not know.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in his will to his son Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyah: Know that the chivalry (muru'ah) of a Muslim man consists of two types of chivalry: one in the city (home) and one while traveling. As for the chivalry in the city, it is reciting the Quran, associating with the scholars, pondering over jurisprudence, and maintaining prayer in congregations. As for the chivalry while traveling, it is providing provisions, minimizing disputes with one's companions, and frequently remembering God, the Exalted, in every ascent, descent, sitting, and standing.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Al-Nufali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Urinating while standing without a valid excuse is from Al-Jafa' (coarseness/ lack of refinement), and cleansing oneself with the right hand is from Al-Jafa'.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: There are two things in which most people are tested/tempted: health and leisure.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Mu'az narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and al-Fadl ibn Musa, who said: Abdullah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two blessings in which many people are tested are health and leisure.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), who said: His father (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Nothing that a believer spends in charity is more beloved to God, the Exalted, than saying the truth when pleased and when angry.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said: Homicide is of two types: homicide of expiation, and homicide of rank; and fighting is of two types: fighting the disbelieving faction until they submit, and fighting the rebellious faction until they return.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abi al-Rabi' al-Shami, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: No worship of God is better than being quiet and walking to his house.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Tawil al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The one who is commanded to do good and forbidden from evil is a believer who takes heed, or an ignorant person who learns; but as for the owner of the whip and sword, he will not (listen).

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Abil Ab'bas Jarir al-Bajaly, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: There are two wings for atheism: the Umayyads and the al-Muhlibs.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Al-Hakam ibn Maskin, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: Eating soap weakens the knees and spoils the semen.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, linking it up through his chain to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): He said: Two men on whom my intercession will not descend: a companion of an oppressive and harsh ruler, and one who is excessive in religion and deviates.

Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed me, regarding what he authorized for me in Balkh, saying: Ali ibn Abdul Aziz informed us, saying: Amr ibn Awon narrated to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Abdullah informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from Aisha, who said: Two prayers that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not abandon, in private or in public: two units after the afternoon prayer and two units before the dawn prayer.

Abu Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ali ibn Abdul Aziz told us, saying: Abu Na'eem told us, saying: Abdul Wahid ibn Aymain told us, saying: My father told me, from Ayesha, that a man entered upon her asking her about the two units of prayer after the afternoon prayer. She said: 'By the One who took His soul (meaning the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family), he did not leave them until he met Allah, the Exalted, and until he became heavy (ill) from prayer, and he used to pray much of his prayer while sitting. I said: 'Indeed, when Umar took power, he forbade them.' She said: 'You are truthful, but the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not pray them in the mosque for fear that it would be a burden on his nation, and he loved what was easy for them.'

Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Sabah al-At'tar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin'an (meaning al-O'aqi), on the authority of Abu Jamrah, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Qays, on the authority of his father, that God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever prays the two cool-time prayers shall enter Paradise," meaning after the morning prayer and after the afternoon prayer. The compiler of this book - may God increase his honor - said: "My intention in presenting these narrations here is to refute the opponents, because they do not consider there to be a prayer after the morning and after the afternoon prayers, so I wished to clarify that they have contradicted the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in his saying and his action."

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bashar al-Qazvini (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Muzaffar ibn Ahmad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Suleiman said: They narrated to us Ali ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon them) said: The least thing with which a man might be removed from faith is to sit with a Ghalī (Boaster/Exaggerator), listen to his narration, and affirm what he says. My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two groups from my nation have no share in Islam: The Ghalāt (Boasters) and the Qadarites.'

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Muni'a told us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn 'Arifah narrated to us, narrated 'Ali ibn Thabit, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Two groups of my nation have no share in Islam: the Marji'ah and the Qadariyyah.

The judge Abu Sa'id al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajisi told me: Al-Hasan ibn Hamdan narrated to us: Abu Mas'ud Isma'il ibn Masood narrated to us: Yazid (who is ibn Zurai') narrated to us - Sa'id (who is ibn Abi 'Urwah) narrated to us - from Qatadah, from Al-Hasan, that Samarah ibn Jundab and Imran ibn Hussayn discussed, and Samarah narrated that he memorized from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) two silences: a silence when he said Takbir, and a silence when he finished his recitation before bowing. Then Qatadah mentioned the last silence after finishing the recitation of 'Non-Guided and Not Astray' (Al-Fatiha), meaning that was what Samarah memorized, but Imran ibn Hussayn rejected it. He said: So we wrote to Abu ibn Ka'b about this, and it was in his letter to them or his reply to them that Samarah had indeed memorized correctly. The compiler of this book (may God increase his honor) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) only remained silent after the recitation so that the Takbir would not be continuous with the recitation, and so that there would be a break between the recitation and the Takbir. This indicates that he did not say 'Amin' after the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha) quietly or loudly, because the one speaking quietly or aloud is not silent. And in that is a strong proof for the Shi'a against their opponents in their saying 'Amin' after the Fatiha. And there is no strength save in God the Sublime the Great.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Awn ibn Amra al-Ansi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated from Malik ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Two characteristics do not coexist in a Muslim: stinginess and bad character.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather narrated to me, saying: Al-Zubayr ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hamzah al-Zubayri narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Ali al-Rafi'i, from his father, from his grandmother Bint Abi Rafi', who said: Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) with her two sons, Al-Hasan and Al-Hussein (peace be upon them), during the illness in which he passed away. She said: 'O Messenger of God, these are your sons, so bequeath something to them.' He said: 'As for Al-Hasan, he has my majesty and my mastery, and as for Al-Hussein, he has my bravery and my generosity.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alawi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad and Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Rafi' narrated to us, saying: My father informed me about an elder from the Ansar who traced it back to Zaynab bint Abi Rafi', from her mother, who said: Fatimah (peace be upon her) said: 'O Messenger of God, these are your sons, so grant them something.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'As for al-Hasan, I granted him my majesty and mastery, and as for al-Husayn, I granted him my generosity and bravery.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Suleiman, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: As for Al-Hasan, I have granted him grandeur and patience, and as for Al-Hussein, I have granted him benevolence and compassion.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Ibrahim ibn Mahzar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahzar, from Fudalah ibn Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Durostawayh, from 'Ajlan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three [groups] whom God will admit to Paradise without reckoning, and three whom God will admit to Hell without reckoning. As for those whom God will admit to Paradise without reckoning: a just Imam, an honest merchant, and an elder who spent his life in obedience to God, the Mighty and Exalted. And as for the three whom God will admit to Hell without reckoning: an unjust Imam, a lying merchant, and an adulterous elder.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ya'qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali, on the authority of Ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Halabi that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Three things for which God will not question a believer: the food he eats, the clothes he wears, and a good wife who helps him, and guards his chastity.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from 'Inbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Three things for which God has not granted anyone an excuse: Kindness to parents, whether they are righteous or wicked; Fulfillment of the covenant/promise, whether to the righteous or the wicked; And fulfilling the trust, whether to the righteous or the wicked.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Zayd Al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The believer is not tested with anything harder for him than three characteristics which he must refrain from (or: which are obligatory), it was said: And what are they? He said: Generosity with one's own wealth for the sake of God, being just with oneself, and frequently remembering God. Indeed, I do not mean for you [to merely recite] 'Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar', but rather remembering God when He permits [actions], and remembering God when He forbids [actions] for you.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riyab, from Al-Halabi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: A believer's nature is not lying, miserliness, and adultery, but perhaps he is afflicted by one of these for a time, but he does not persist in it. He was asked: Will he commit adultery? He said: Yes, he is tempted and repentant, but no child will be born from that sperm.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abdullah ibn Sin'an who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: God, may His Majesty be Exalted, said: "I have given the world among My servants as a loan. Whoever lends Me from it a loan, I will give him for each one of them ten to seven hundred times, and whatever I will from that. And whoever does not lend Me from it a loan, I will take from him by force, and I will give him three qualities: if one of them were given to My angels, they would be pleased: Salat (prayer/blessings), Guidance, and Mercy." Indeed God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Those who, when a calamity befalls them, say: Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we return. Those are upon whom are blessings from their Lord.' One of the three is 'and mercy', two are 'and those are the guided', three [are blessings/prayers], Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: This is for the one from whom God took something by force.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abi al-Sabah al-Kanani, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Three are the hardest things for the servants to do: a believer being fair to himself, a man sharing with his brother, and remembering God in every state. This is that he remembers God, the Exalted, when about to commit a sin, so the remembrance of God stands between him and that sin. Indeed, those who fear God, when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [God], and at once they see clearly. And this is the saying of God, the Exalted.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'd Abady narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Aqbah, from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Munthir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The hardest of deeds are three: to be fair to people regarding yourself, so that you do not desire for them from yourself anything unless you desire for them the like of it; supporting your brother in wealth; and remembering God in every state. It is not merely saying 'Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest', but rather when a command of God comes to you, you act upon it, and when something God has forbidden comes to you, you leave it.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibnillah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: When Noah (peace be upon him) supplicated to his Lord, the Exalted, against his people, Satan (may God curse him) came to him and said: 'O Noah, I have a favor owed to you, and I wish to repay it.' Noah said: 'By God, I dislike that you have a favor owed to me; what is it?' He said: 'Yes, you called upon God against your people and He drowned them, so no one remained whom I had led astray; thus I am at ease until another generation arises, and I will lead them astray.' Noah said to him: 'What do you want me to repay you with?' He said to him: 'Remember me in three situations, for I am closest to the servant when he is in one of them: Remember me when you are angry, and remember me when you judge between two people, and remember me when you are alone with a woman with no one else present.'
