Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God forgive him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Ubayd, from Al-Hussein ibn Alvan, from Amr ibn Sabit, from Abu Abdullah, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: Three people do not get what is rightfully theirs from three others: the honorable from the lowly, the patient from the ignorant, and the good-doer from the evildoer.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abi al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Abi Imran Amr ibn Mus'ab al-Arzami, from Abi Hamza al-Thumali, who said: I heard Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: The servant is between three things: calamity, destiny, and blessing. Upon him regarding the calamity from God is patience, which is obligatory; and upon him regarding the destiny from God is submission, which is obligatory; and upon him regarding the blessing from God, the Mighty and Exalted, is gratitude, which is obligatory.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Samak, from Ali ibn Shahab ibn Abdeh Rabbeh, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The donors are three: God, the Lord of the Worlds; the owner of the property; and the one who acts as the intermediary through whose hands it is distributed.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The donors are three: God the Donor; the one who donates from his property; and the one who strives in that [matter], [is considered] a donor.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Abu Abdillah, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them all peace be upon them) He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever enjoins to do good or forbids to do evil or guides to goodness or points towards it is a partner, and whoever orders to do evil, guides one towards evil or points towards it is also a partner.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abi Ayoob al-Khizaz, on the authority of Abdul-Mumin al-Ansari that Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, has granted the believer three qualities: nobility in the world through his religion; prosperity in the Hereafter; and dignity in the hearts of all people.

Our father and Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from some of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Abi al-Sakhr, both of whom linked it up to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). That he said: 'Traveling (for pilgrimage) is not to be undertaken except to three mosques: The Sacred Mosque (Al-Haram), the Mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and the Mosque of Kufa.'

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Yasir - the servant, that Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said: "You should not travel to any tombs other than our tombs. I have been oppressively poisoned to death and buried in a strange place. I hope the prayers of those who travel to visit my tomb are accepted and also their sins are forgiven."

Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Lakhmi narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih, Mutalib ibn Shu'ayb al-Azdi, and Ahmad ibn Rashid (the Basrans) narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hammad narrated to us from Abi Hazim al-Madini, who said: Imran ibn Umar ibn Sa'id al-Musaybi narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, for Allah are three sanctities: whoever preserves them, Allah will preserve for him his religious and worldly affairs; and whoever does not preserve them, Allah will not preserve anything for him: the sanctity of Islam, my sanctity, and the sanctity of my progeny (Ahl al-Bayt).

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Indeed, for God, Exalted and Mighty, are three unique things to respect: His Book, which is His Light and Wisdom; His House, which He established as the Qiblah for people, and God will not accept from anyone a face turned towards any other direction; and the Household of your Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi'a, from Muhammad ibn 'Idhafir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: While the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was on one of his journeys, a group of riders met him. They said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God.' He turned to them and said: 'Who are you?' They said: 'Believers.' He said: 'Then what is the reality/truth of your faith?' They said: 'Contentment with God's decree, submission to God's command, and entrusting matters to God.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'They are wise scholars, nearly prophets in wisdom. If you are truthful, do not build what you will not reside in, and do not accumulate what you will not consume. And fear God, to whom you will return.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir and Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The pilgrim is in one of three states: a man who performed Hajj al-Ifrad with the offering of a sacrificial animal, a man who performed Hajj al-Ifrad without taking the offering, and a man who performed Hajj al-Tamattu by combining Umrah with Hajj.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir al-Ja'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The pilgrims are of three types. The one with the greatest share is a man whose past and future sins are forgiven, and God protects him from the punishment of the Fire. As for the one next to him, it is a man whose past sins are forgiven, and he resumes his deeds for the remainder of his life. As for the one next to him, it is a man whose family and wealth are protected.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riyab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: No one is followed after his death with reward except for three things: a charity he established during his lifetime, which continues after his death until the Day of Resurrection; a charity that is endowed and not inherited; or a path of guidance he established, which he practiced and others practiced after him; or a righteous child who seeks forgiveness for him.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Munthir ibn Yazid who said: Abu Harun al-Makfuf narrated to me He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Harun! Indeed God the Blessed and Exalted has sworn by Himself not to be a neighbor to a treacherous one.' I asked: 'Who is the treacherous one?' He said: 'One who saves for himself a dirham of a believer's money or withholds from him anything of worldly affairs.' I said: 'I seek refuge in God from God's wrath.' Then he said: 'Indeed God the Blessed and Exalted has sworn by Himself not to house in His Paradise three types: one who rejects God's judgment, or one who rejects the judgment of a righteous Imam, or one who withholds the right of a believer.' I asked: 'Should he give him from the surplus of what he owns?' He said: 'He should give him from his own self and soul.' If a Muslim is stingy with his own self towards him, he is not of him; rather he is of the progeny of Satan.' The compiler of this book (may God increase his support) said: 'Giving from the self and soul means offering one's status/effort to him when he needs assistance, and striving for him in his needs.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Hamdani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kasa'i, from Maysar (the seller of black slaves), and Khalid said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: "Eat onions, for in them are three characteristics: they improve the breath, strengthen the gums, and increase the semen and sexual drive."

Muhammad ibn al-ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father (peace be upon them both) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charming/healing (ruqya) is not effective except in three cases: for a biting insect (hummah), or for the eye (ain), or for blood that does not stop flowing (dam la yarqa').

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'adab narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isbahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Yahya ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Furat al-Qazzaz informed me, saying: Harun ibn Ubaydat narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both). Umar said when death approached him: 'I repent to God for three things: My usurping of this authority, myself and Abu Bakr, from the people; and my appointing myself as ruler over them; and my preferring some Muslims over others.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'adab narrated, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isbahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi who said: Al-Mas'oodi narrated to me who said: Al-Hasan ibn Hammad al-Ta'i narrated, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Atiyyah (as he thinks) from Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: I witnessed Umar at his death saying: 'I repent to God for three things: 1- My dismissal of the slaves of Yemen; 2- My turning back from the army of Usamah after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had appointed him over us; and 3- Our mutual pledge regarding the people of this House (Ahl al-Bayt), that if God took away His Messenger, we would not appoint any of them.'

By this chain of narration, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali told me, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Sufyan told us, from his father, who said: Fadl ibn al-Zubayr told me, saying: Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha' Ziyad ibn Isa told me, saying: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: When death approached Umar, he said: I repent to God for my turning back from the army of Usamah, and I repent to God for freeing the captives of Yemen, and I repent to God for something we had made clear in our hearts, asking God to protect us from its harm, and that the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr was a hasty matter.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Arfah narrated to us, he said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Abu Hafs al-Abbar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Juhadah, from Bakir ibn 'Abdullah al-Madani, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: Beware of stinginess (al-shuḥ), for it was by stinginess that those before you were destroyed. It commanded you to lie, so you lied; it commanded you to oppress, so you oppressed; and it commanded you to cut off ties, so you cut off ties.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Abul Abbas al-Saraj informed us, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Ajlan narrated from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Beware of obscene language, for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, does not like the vulgar person who uses obscene language. And beware of oppression, for indeed oppression in the sight of Allah is the darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of stinginess, for it led those who were before you to shed their blood, and it led them to sever their kinship ties, and it led them to violate and make permissible their prohibitions.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih al-Razi, on the authority of Abu Salt al-Haravy, who said: 'I asked Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about faith.' He replied, 'Faith is a conviction of the heart, a verbal expression of the tongue, and an action of the limbs; faith is nothing else.'

Suleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayoob al-Lakhmy narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abdul Aziz and Mu’az ibn al-Mosana narrated to us, saying: Abdul Salam ibn Salih al-Haravy narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha, on the authority of his father Musa, on the authority of his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them all), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Faith is knowledge with the heart, verbal affirmation, and action with the pillars (of practice).

Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad Dawud ibn Suleiman al-Ghazi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) narrated to me, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: My father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir narrated to me, saying: My father Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: My father al-Husayn ibn Ali narrated to me, saying: My father the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them) narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Faith is affirmation by the tongue, knowledge by the heart, and action by the limbs. Hamzah ibn Muhammad (may God be pleased with him) said: And I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatam saying: I heard my father saying: And this hadith has been narrated from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi Abd al-Salam ibn Salih, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) with a similar chain of narrators. Abu Hatam said: 'If this chain of narrators were recited to a madman, he would be cured.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: He narrated to me Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn al-Mo'ala, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There are three things in which there is hatred from Allah, the Exalted: sleeping when not sleepy, laughing without cause, and eating on a full stomach.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ahmad ibn al-Jabbar, from his grandfather, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The gift is of three types: a gift in return (for a gift received), a gift for conciliation/friendship, and a gift for the sake of God, the Exalted.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Bandar narrated to us, saying: Abul Abbas al-Himadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayyagh narrated to us, saying: Al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'eb narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "It is not permissible for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days."

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Himran, on the authority of his father that Abi Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon them) said: There are no two believers who are on no talking terms for more than three days except that they are estranged from each other on the third day. He was asked, 'O son of the Messenger of God, this is the state of the oppressor, but what about the oppressed one?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What is it with the oppressed one that he does not go to the oppressor and say: I am the oppressor, so that they reconcile?'

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Ibn Khuzaymah informed me, saying: Abu Musa narrated to us, saying: Al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from Jamil - the mawla of Abdul Harith, from Nafi' ibn Abdul Harith, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: From the prosperity of the Muslim is a spacious dwelling, a good neighbor, and a good vehicle.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Khuzaymah told us, saying: Abu Musa told us, saying: Abdul Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan narrated, from Al-A'mash, from Suleiman ibn Meshar, from Kharash ibn al-Harr, from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said: Three people to whom God will not speak: the one who mentions his favor whenever he gives something, the one who drags down his garment (in arrogance), and the one who sells his goods with false oaths.

Our father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Uthman ibn Jabalah, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Three qualities: whoever possesses them, or even one of them, will be under the Shade of the Throne of God, the Mighty and Exalted, [on the Day of Resurrection], on the Day when there is no shade but His Shade: A man who gives to people from himself what they are in need of; a man who does not advance one person nor delay another until he knows that this is for God's pleasure or displeasure; and a man who does not criticize his Muslim brother with a fault until he removes that fault from himself, for indeed he does not remove a fault from himself but another fault appears to him. And sufficient is the man's occupation with himself rather than with people.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: Al-Khadr ibn Muslim al-Sayrafi narrated that I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Three [types of people] will be under the Shade of the Throne of God, the Exalted and Mighty, on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade: A man who judged people fairly regarding himself; a man who did not hasten to do something nor delay it until he knew that was for God's, the Exalted and Mighty, pleasure or displeasure; and a man who did not find fault with his brother with a fault until he removed that fault from himself, for indeed he does not remove a fault from himself except that another fault replaces it, and sufficient is the man's occupation with himself rather than with people.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Senani al-Mokattib (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qat'tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Fazl al-Hashemi that Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Of the following three I do not really know which one is a greater offense than the others. The first is following a funeral procession without having on one’s robe. The second is striking one’s buttocks with the hand at times of calamities. The third one is saying ‘Be benign to him. Have mercy upon him. May God have mercy upon you’ when attending a funeral procession.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Nufali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Three [people] — I do not know which of them is greater in sin: The one who walks with the funeral procession without a cloak (or shroud), The one who says: 'Be gentle with him,' And the one who says: 'Seek forgiveness for him, may God forgive you.'

Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them all) He said: Using good scent indicates affluence. Wearing good garments indicates beauty. Having a good temper defeats one’s enemies.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), He said: Three of the traditions of the Messengers are: perfume, trimming the hair, and frequent sexual intercourse.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Zyad, who said: Amr ibn Uthman narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talha al-Shami, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) Regarding the words of God, the Exalted: 'When they disregarded the warnings that had been given them,' he said: They were of three types: a group who accepted and informed others [so they were saved]; a group who accepted but did not inform others [so their arms were distorted]; and a group who did not accept and did not inform others [so they perished].

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, he said: He narrated to me Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from al-Husayn ibn Yusuf, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Attar Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Three [groups of people] are in the protection of God, the Exalted, until God finishes with the Reckoning: a man who has never committed adultery, a man who has never mixed his wealth with usury, and a man who has never strived in them [committing these two deeds].

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hisan, from Ibrahim ibn Asim ibn Hameed, from Salih ibn Maysam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Three qualities: whoever possesses them has perfected the qualities of faith: whoever is patient with oppression, restrains his anger and counts it as a reward (from God), and pardons and forgives, will be among those whom God admits to Paradise without reckoning, and He will accept his intercession on behalf of as many people as there were in the tribes of Rabi'ah and Mudar.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abu Ayoob al-Khizaz, from Abu Ubaydat al-Haza'a, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: A believer is one whose pleasure would not lead him into sin and wrongful deeds. A believer is one whose anger would not lead him away from rightful statements. A believer is one whose power would not force him to act unjustly and to acquire what doesn’t rightfully belong to him.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from his mother Fatimah bint al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), from her father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Three characteristics: whoever possesses them has perfected the characteristics of faith: The one who, when pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into sin or falsehood; and when angered, his anger does not lead him away from the truth; and when in power, he does not acquire what does not belong to him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin'an, who said: A believer was mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Indeed, the believer is the one who, when angered, his anger does not lead him away from the truth; and the believer is the one who, when pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into falsehood; and the believer is the one who, when in power, does not acquire what does not belong to him [by himself].'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalesi, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awn narrated from Ibn Abi Najran al-Tamimi, who said: 'Asim ibn Hamit al-Hannat narrated from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Three [types of people] to whom God will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: The one who plucks his white hair (beard), the one who masturbates, and the one who is penetrated anally.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Malik al-Juhani said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying Three people with whom God shall not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: One who claims a leader whose leadership is not from God; one who denies a leader whose leadership is from God the Exalted; and one who considers that both of them have a share in Islam.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Maysami, from Hisham ibn Ahmar and Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: Three people will be punished on the Day of Resurrection. One is the one who makes an image of an animal; he will be punished until he breathes life into it, but he is not one who breathes life into it. The one who fabricates (false) dreams will be punished until he ties together two grains of barley, but he is not one who ties them together. The one who eavesdrops on people's conversation while they dislike it for him, molten lead (or solder) will be poured into his ear, and that is the 'Asrab'.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Daybali narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiani, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever constructs an image shall be punished and will be commanded to give it life, but he cannot do so. And whoever lies in his dream shall be punished and commanded to tie together two strands of barley, but he cannot do so. And whoever eavesdrops on a conversation while they are unwilling for him to listen, molten lead shall be poured into his ears on the Day of Resurrection. Sufyan said: 'Al-annak' is from lead.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Amir ibn Ribah, from Amr ibn al-Walid, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Three things are back-breaking: a man who overestimates his deeds, forgets his sins, and is conceited of his own opinion.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Satan (may God curse him) said to his followers: 'When I gain mastery over the son of Adam in three things, I do not care what he does, for it will not be accepted from him: When he considers his deeds abundant, forgets his sin, and conceit enters him.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'ada ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: 'For a Muslim man there are three friends. A friend who says: I am with you alive and dead, and that is his deeds. A friend who says to him: I am with you until the door of your grave, then I leave you, and that is his child. A friend who says to him: I am with you until you die, and that is his wealth. So when he dies, it becomes for the inheritor.'

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sahkuni al-Muzakki in Kufa in the year 354 A.H. narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us: Al-Qasim ibn Zakariya ibn Dinar narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us: Ja'far al-Ahmar, from Ummi al-Sayrafi, from Abu Kathir al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn As'ad ibn Zurarah He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: My Lord ascended me [to the heavens] and revealed to me regarding Ali (peace be upon him) three [things]: Indeed, he is the leader of the pious, the master of the believers, and the commander of those with radiant foreheads.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadl, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Men are of three kinds: a man (known) by his wealth, a man by his status/prestige, and a man by his tongue. And that is the best of the three.

And with this chain he narrated that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Men are of three types: an intelligent one, a foolish one, and a corrupt one. As for the intelligent one, religion is his law, forbearance is his nature, and judgment is his character. If questioned, he answers; if he speaks, he is correct; if he hears, he understands; if he narrates, he is truthful; and if someone trusts him, he fulfills that trust. As for the foolish one, if invited to good, he neglects it; if invited away from good, he descends into it; if burdened with ignorance, he is ignorant; and if he narrates, he lies. He does not understand, and even if he understands, he does not gain deep insight. As for the corrupt one, if you entrust him with something, he betrays you; if you keep him as a companion, he debases you; and if you trust him, he does not advise you sincerely.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al- Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdul Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said: Imamate is not valid except for a man who possesses three characteristics: piety that restrains him from forbidden deeds; patience that enables him to control his anger; and good deputyship over those he leads, so that he is like a merciful father to them.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked By what sign is the Imam recognized after the Imam? He said: Indeed, the Imam has signs: that he be the eldest son of his father after him, and that excellence be in him. And when the caravan arrives in the city, they ask: To whom did so-and-so bequeath? They say: To so-and-so. And the armaments among us are like the Ark among the Children of Israel; it accompanies the Imam wherever he is.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khishab, from Al-Yazid ibn Ishaq al-Sha'r, from Harun ibn Hamz al-Ghanawi, from Al-Ala' ibn A'ayn, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is the proof against one who falsely claims this authority? He said: There are three signs of proof; if they do not all exist in one man, he is not the possessor of this authority: that he be the closest of people to the one whose heart it is, that he possess the armaments of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and that he be the possessor of the clear testament, such that when the city is entered, the common people and children ask: To whom did Fulan bequeath? They say: To Fulan.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi', from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Aiman ibn Mohraz, who narrated it from Al-Qasim [and] ibn Faz'al, that Hariz said: Whoever performs Hajj for three consecutive years, then performs Hajj or does not perform Hajj, he is in the status of one who is habitual in Hajj. The compiler of this book said: May God increase his support: This chain of narration is weak/unstable, and I did not change it because it was thus in my manuscript, and the hadith is sound.

My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hijjal [from Safwan ibn Yahya], from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jamal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever performs the Hajj pilgrimage three times, poverty will never afflict him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Thawir ibn Abi Fakhtah, from Abu Jamilyah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them) who said: There are three ranks, three expiations, three destroyers, and three saviors. As for the ranks: spreading peace (greeting), feeding food, and praying at night while people are asleep. As for the expiations: perfecting ablution in the cold, walking by night and day to the prayers, and maintaining attendance at congregational prayers. As for the three destroyers: stinginess that is obeyed, desires that are followed, and a person's self-admiration. As for the saviors: fearing God in private and in public, moderation in wealth and poverty, and saying the word of justice when pleased and when angry.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajistani the judge informed me, saying: Ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan and Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Sayyar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Atbah narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn Bakir al-Abdi, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: There are three things that destroy and three things that save. As for the three that save, they are: fearing Allah, the Exalted, in private and in public; moderation in wealth and poverty; and justice in pleasure and anger. And as for the three that destroy, they are: a widely obeyed stinginess, which is followed; and a person's admiration for themselves. And another hadith has been narrated from the Imam (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Widely obeyed stinginess is having a bad opinion of Allah, the Exalted.' And I have presented it with its chain of narration in the book Ma'ani al-Akhbar.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus'adat ibn Zyad, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father (peace be upon them both) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: There are three things which destroy: breaching transactions, abandoning traditions and leaving the society. There are three things which save: watching out what you say, crying over your mistakes, and staying at home.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sulayman ibn Dawud, who said: Hammad ibn Isa narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He looked at several beds in a man's house and said: One bed is for the man, a second bed is for his family, a third bed is for his guest, and the fourth bed is for Satan.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sejezy narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, saying: Suleiman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Khalid al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Abi Hani, from [Abi] Abd al-Rahman al-Hubli, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) mentioned beds, saying: A bed for the man, a bed for the woman, and a bed for the guest. The fourth is for Satan.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of al-asan ibn Ali al-Washa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn A'ez, on the authority of Abi Khadijeh, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The people go forth upon three types: a scholar, a seeker of knowledge, and scum (the rest). We are the scholars, and our followers are the seekers of knowledge, and the rest of the people are scum.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Be either a knowledgeable one, a student, or a lover of the scholars, and do not be the fourth group, lest you perish due to your enmity of them.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Wahb ibn Munabbah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both, Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Yasammata' is said to the sneezer three times; whatever is above that is due to the air.
In another tradition: that if the sneezer exceeds three [times], it is said to him: 'May God heal you.' since that is due to an illness.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us who said: Abu Sa'id Sahl ibn Zyad al-Adamy narrated to us who said: Ja'far ibn Bashar al-Wasiti narrated to me who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan narrated to us, from Durost ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Umar ibn Azineh, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Whoever does as much good in return for a favor as has been done for him has merely repaid the debt; whoever does more is being grateful. One who is grateful is also generous. One who knows that whatever good he does, he indeed does it for himself, will no longer expect anyone to return his favors, nor will he expect any friendship in return for his friendly deeds. Do not demand anything from others in return for what you do for yourself so as to guard your own honor. Know that anyone who asks you for something from you has indeed disregarded his own honor. So do not disregard your own reputation and fulfill his request.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Salim the freedman of Tarbal, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: 'The world is cycles (of gain and loss). Whatever is yours in it comes to you despite your weakness, and whatever is against you in it comes to you and you cannot resist it with strength.' Then he followed this statement by saying: 'Whoever despairs of what has passed away relieves his body, and whoever is content with what he has been given finds peace in his eyes.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from a man from Khuzaa, from Aslami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Learn Arabic, for it is the speech of God with which He spoke to His creation, and clean the chewing teeth, and wear the rings on the fingertips. Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hussein, the compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: This hadith has also been narrated by Abu Saeed al-Adami, who said at its end: 'Wear the rings,' meaning place the rings on the ends of the fingers and do not place them on the tips of the thumb, for it is narrated that this was the practice of the people of Lot.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people on the last Friday of Sha'ban. He praised God and extolled Him, then said: 'O People! Indeed, a month has come upon you in which there is a night better than a thousand months. It is the month of Ramadan. God has made its fasting obligatory, and He has made praying one night in it voluntarily equal to the reward of one who prays voluntarily for seventy nights in other months. He has made whoever does one good deed in it equal to the reward of one who performs an obligatory duty in other months, and whoever performs an obligatory duty in it is like one who performs seventy obligatory duties in other months. It is the month of patience, and the reward of patience is Paradise. It is the month of sharing, and it is the month in which God increases the sustenance of the believer. Whoever feeds a fasting believer in it, for him is the freeing of a slave and forgiveness of his sins for what has passed.' It was said to him: 'O Messenger of God, not all of us can afford to feed a fasting person.' He said: 'Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, is Generous. He will give this reward to whoever among you cannot afford more than a sip of milk to feed a fasting person, or a drink of fresh water, or a few dates, which is all he can afford. Whoever eases the burden on his slave in this month, God will ease his reckoning. It is a month whose beginning is mercy, whose middle is forgiveness, and whose end is acceptance and freedom from the Fire. You have no need in it to dispense with four qualities: two with which to please God, and two with which you have no need to dispense. As for the two with which to please God, they are testifying that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God. And as for the two with which you have no need to dispense, they are: asking God for your needs and Paradise, asking God for well-being, and seeking refuge in Him from the Fire.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumaydani narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, linking it through his chain to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: Four things are done in vain: planting seeds in salty ground, lighting a lamp in the moonlight, eating after satiety, and doing a favor for those who are not worthy of it.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid narrated that Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidy narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hatam al-Qattan, from Hammad ibn Amr, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said in his will to him: O Ali! Four things are done in vain: eating after satiety, a lamp in the moonlight, planting in salty ground, and doing a favor for those unworthy of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dihqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Four things are done in vain: friendship bestowed upon one who has no loyalty; kindness shown to one who does not give thanks; knowledge shared with one who does not listen; and a secret entrusted to one who has no capacity to safeguard it.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isma'il told me, saying: Abul Abbas ibn Muni'a told us, saying: Sheiban ibn Furukh told us, saying: Davud ibn Abi al-Furat told us, saying: Al-Ba' ibn Ahmar told us, saying: Akrama told us, from Ibn Abbas, saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) drew four lines on the ground and said: 'Do you know what this is?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The four best women of the people of Paradise are: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, Fatimah bint Muhammad, Mary bint Imran, and Asiya bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh.'

Suleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayoob al-Lakhmy narrated that Ali ibn Abdul Aziz quoted Hijaj ibn al-Minhal, on the authority of Davood ibn Abil Forat al-Kindi, on the authority of Al-ba’e ibn Ahmar, on the authority of Akrama, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) drew four lines on the ground and said: 'The best women of Paradise are Mary, daughter of Imran; Khadijah, daughter of Khuwaylid; Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad; and Asia, daughter of Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh.'

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us; he said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukri narrated to us; he said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Juwhari narrated to us; he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Truthful (Al-Sadiq), Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), said: The four things people seek in this ephemeral world are: wealth, comfort, lack of concern, and honor. As for wealth, it is found in contentment; whoever seeks it in the abundance of money will not find it. As for comfort, it is found in a light burden; whoever seeks it in a heavy burden will not find it. As for lack of concern, it is found in little busyness; whoever seeks it amidst much busyness will not find it. As for honor, it is found in serving the Creator; whoever seeks it in serving the creation will not find it.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajistani told me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hijr narrated to us, Hijr narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamar, from Rubay ibn Kharash, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: A servant does not believe until he believes in four things: until he bears witness that there is no god but God, alone, without a partner, and that I am the Messenger of God, sent by Him with the truth, and until he believes in the resurrection after death, and until he believes in the divine decree.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Hurry to do four [good deeds] before four [things happen]: use your youth before your old age, your health before your illness, your wealth before your poverty, and your life before your death.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidy narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Anas ibn Muhammad (Abu Malik) narrated to me, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said in his will to him: O Ali! Hasten to utilize four [things] before four [events]: utilize your youth before your old age, your health before your illness, your wealth before your poverty, and your life before your death.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Sufyan ibn Ayyinah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: I found that all the knowledge of the people is in four areas: the first is to know your Lord; the second is to know what He has done with you; the third is to know what He wants from you; and the fourth is to know what will take you out of your religion.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about Jihad, is it recommended (Sunnah) or obligatory (Fard)? He said: Jihad is of four types: Two are obligatory, one is recommended but is not performed except with an obligatory [context], and one is merely recommended. As for one of the two obligatory types, it is the striving of a person against his own self to avoid the sins of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and this is the greatest Jihad. And fighting those who are close to you from the disbelievers is obligatory. As for the Jihad that is recommended but is not performed except with an obligatory [context]: then fighting the enemy is obligatory upon the entire community, and if they abandon Jihad, punishment will befall them, and this is from the punishment of the community. And it is recommended for the Imam to go out with the community to fight the enemy. As for the Jihad that is merely recommended: then whatever Sunnah a person establishes and strives in its establishment, attainment, and revival, then the action and effort in it are among the best of deeds, because he has revived a Sunnah. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever establishes a good Sunnah, he has its reward and the reward of those who act upon it, without any reduction from their rewards.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Najih that Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Suleiman ibn Davood (peace be upon them both) said: 'We have been granted whatever has been granted to the people or not, and we have been taught whatever the people have been taught or not. We found nothing to be better than fearing God in public and private; frugality both at times of poverty and being wealthy; telling the truth whether it be pleasing to us or to our loss; and supplicating to the Honorable the Exalted God in all circumstances.'

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his grandfather, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad (al-Sakuni), from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women are of four types: Jam' Mujamm', Rabi' Murba', Karb Muqma', and Ghall Qamal.' The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: 'Jam' Mujamm' means abundant in goodness and fertile; Rabi' Murba' refers to the one who has a child in her lap and another in her womb; Karb Muqma' means bad-tempered with her husband; Ghall Qamal means she is to her husband like the 'Ghall Qamal' (a leather strap infested with lice that is difficult to remove), which is a simile used by the Arabs.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them) that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Among the signs of misery are: solidity of the eye, hard-heartedness, excessive greed to gain one’s daily bread and insisting on committing sins.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: He narrated to me Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: O Ali! Four characteristics are among the signs of misery: solidity of the eye, hard-heartedness, having high aspirations, and the love for a very long life.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'Which wealth is best?' He said: 'Crops that their owner cultivates and improves, and pays its due on the day of harvest.' It was said: 'Then which wealth is best after crops?' He said: 'A man with his flock of sheep, who follows them to grazing lands, establishes prayer, and pays alms-tax.' It was said: 'Then which wealth is best after sheep?' He said: 'Cows that go forth with good and return with good.' It was said: 'Then which wealth is best after cows?' He said: 'Palm trees deeply rooted in the soil and well-fed in their place; excellent are the palm trees. Whoever sells them, their price is like dust on the head of a mountain, which the wind scatters on a stormy day, unless he replaces them.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, then which wealth is best after palm trees?' He remained silent. A man said to him: 'What about camels?' He said: 'In them is misery, roughness, and exertion, and distance from the dwelling. They go forth retreating and return retreating. Their good comes only from their left side. Indeed, they do not lack the wretched sinners.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi, from Salih ibn Abi Himad, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from his father, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdullah, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) narrated: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Sheep, when they face you, face you [are profitable], and when they turn away, face you [are still profitable]. Cows, when they face you, face you, and when they turn away, turn away [are not profitable]. Camels are the reins of the devils; when they face you, they turn away, and when they turn away, they turn away. Their goodness does not come except from the unlucky side.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, then who should keep them?' He said: 'Then where are the wretched sinners?' Salih said: And Isma'il ibn Mihran recited a poem: 'It is wealth, were it not for the scarcity of lowering [price] around it, so whoever wishes can keep it, and whoever wishes can sell it.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: There are four prayers which a man prays at any time: a missed prayer which you make up whenever you remember it; the two units of the obligatory circumambulation prayer; the eclipse prayer; and the funeral prayer. These are the prayers which a man may pray at all times.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr and Safvan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Mus'ab that Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: I heard my father quote on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather (peace be upon them) that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Five things I will not abandon until death: eating on the ground along with the servants, riding my saddled donkey, milking the she-goat with my own hand, wearing wool, and greeting the children, so that these become a sunnah from me after me.

Muhammad ibn Umar al-Baghdadi al-Hafiz narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Abul Qasim Ishaq ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), saying: He narrated to me his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, saying: He narrated to me Ali ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, known as al-Mushallal, saying: He informed me Sulayman ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Five [things] I will not abandon until death: wearing wool, riding a saddled donkey, eating with the servants, mending my shoe with my hand, and greeting the children, so that these become a Sunnah after me."

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated to me, from Sajjada, from Durost, from Abu Khalid al-Sejestani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Five characteristics: whoever does not have one of them in himself is not of much benefit. The first is loyalty (al-wafa'), the second is management/planning (al-tadbir), the third is modesty (al-haya'), the fourth is good character (husn al-khuluq), and the fifth, which combines these five characteristics, is freedom/liberality (al-hurriyyah).

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Five characteristics: whoever lacks one of them will remain with an incomplete life, unstable intellect, and a distracted heart.' The first is health of the body, the second is security, the third is abundance in sustenance, and the fourth is a sympathetic companion. I asked: 'And who is the sympathetic companion?' He said: 'A righteous wife, a righteous child, and a righteous companion.' And the fifth, which encompasses these characteristics, is comfort (peace of mind).

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The prayer is not repeated except for five [issues]: purity, the time, the Qibla, the bowing, and the prostration. Then he (peace be upon him) added: Recitation is a sunnah, the Tashahhud is a sunnah, and the Takbir is a sunnah, and the sunnah does not invalidate the obligatory act.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Five things are distributed among the servants: certitude, contentment, patience, and gratitude, and that which perfects all of these for him is intellect.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Al-Ammar ibn Marvan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: There is one-fifth (khums) on what is extracted from mines, the sea, booties, on what is legally permissible mixed with what is forbidden when its owner is not known, and on treasures.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Yaqoobi, on the authority of Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alavi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them all) He said: Indeed, God, the One that has no substitute to be worshipped, when He made charity forbidden for us, He established the one-fifth levy for us. Therefore, giving charity to us is forbidden, giving the alms-tax to us is obligatory, and giving gifts to us is allowed.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of several others that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The khums is levied on five things: on treasures, mines, diving (for pearls), and booties. Ibn Abi Umayr forgot the fifth. The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: I think the fifth item which Ibn Abi Umayr forgot is wealth that a man inherits, and he knows that it contains both halal and haram, but he does not know the owners of the haram portion to pay it to them, nor does he know the haram specifically to avoid it; therefore, he pays the khums from it.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Sajjada al-Abid (the Prostrating Worshipper), whose name is al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no banquet (walimah) except in five situations: a wedding, childbirth, circumcision, a man buying a house, and returning from Mecca. As for the wedding, it is marriage; the childbirth is giving birth to a child; the circumcision is the cutting of the foreskin; the buying of a house is when a man purchases a home; and the returning is when one comes back from Mecca.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hussein said: Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidy narrated that Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi narrated from his father that Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik narrated from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said in his will to him: 'O Ali! There is no banquet (walimah) except in five cases: a wedding, childbirth, circumcision, buying a house, and returning from Mecca.' The wedding is marriage, the childbirth is the confinement with the baby, the circumcision is the cutting of the foreskin, the buying of the house is the banquet for purchasing a home, and the returning from Mecca is the banquet for one who comes back from Mecca. The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: The food to which people are invited when building or buying a house is called 'al-Wakirah', and 'al-Wakar' is derived from it. The food prepared for the one returning from travel is called 'al-Naqi'ah'. 'Al-Rakaz' means booty, as if he means that preparing food for the return from Mecca is a booty for its host from the abundant reward. And from this is the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Fasting in winter is the cool booty.'

Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi from Hamedan, upon his return from Hajj, narrated to us; Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Dimashqi narrated to him; Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to him; Muslima ibn Ali narrated from al-A'mash, from al-Shaqiq, from al-Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O assembly of Muslims, beware of adultery, for it contains six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, it removes beauty (al-baha'), causes poverty, and shortens life. As for those in the Hereafter, it incurs the Wrath of the Lord, results in a bad reckoning, and leads to eternal residence in the Fire. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) added: "It was made appealing to them by their own souls that the Wrath of Allah is upon them and in the Punishment they will abide eternally."

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said in his will to him: O Ali! In adultery there are six characteristics: three of them are in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, it removes beauty/happiness, hastens destruction, and cuts off sustenance. And as for those in the Hereafter, it is bad reckoning, the wrath of the Merciful, and eternity in the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Fazal, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: For the adulterer are six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, the light of his face fades, he inherits poverty, and his destruction is hastened. And as for those in the Hereafter: the Wrath of the Lord (may His Majesty be Exalted), a bad Reckoning, and eternal residence in the Fire.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) narrated: He said: The ill-gotten property (al-sah) is the price of the dead animal, the price of the dog, the price of wine, the dowry of the fornicatress, the bribe in judgment, and the wage of the fortune-teller.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Ammar ibn Marvan, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Ill-gotten wealth (Al-Sahut) is of many types, including what is acquired from the works of oppressive rulers, and the wages of judges and prostitutes, and the price of wine, and intoxicating drink, and usury after proof, but as for the bribe, O Ammar, in judgments, then that is atheism against God the Great and His Messenger.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Adamy narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Siyari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, on the authority of one who informed him, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, God, the Mighty and Exalted, has exempted our followers from six characteristics: insanity, leprosy, vitiligo, being born out of adultery (or having a child born out of adultery), and begging from the people with their hand.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Zura'ah ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Indeed, our God has protected our followers from six [characteristics]: that they may be greedy like a crow, or bark like dogs, or be gay, or have children born out of fornication, or have children born to them out of fornication, or go door-to-door to beg.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Khaliji, from Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the opening Takbir, so he said: Seven. I said: It has been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he used to say it once. He said: Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to say it once loudly and six times quietly.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bakir, from Zurarah, who said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and heard him start the prayer with seven continuous Takbirs.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you are the Imam (prayer leader), it suffices for you to say one Takbir aloud and say six in a low voice.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, said be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The minimum that suffices of the Takbir in turning towards the prayer is one Takbir, and three Takbirs, and five and seven are better. And I have explained the reason for the seven Takbirs in the Opening in my book 'Ilal al-Shara'i' wa al-Ahkam wa al-Asbab.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan Ali ibn Fadal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from some of our companions, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is the right of the believer upon the believer? He said: There are seven obligatory rights, and there is no right among them except that it is obligatory upon him; and if he opposes it, he leaves the guardianship of God and abandons His obedience, and God Almighty has no share in him. I said: May I be your ransom, tell me what they are? He said: Woe to you, O Mu'alla! I am affectionate towards you; I fear that you will be lost and not retain, and know but not act. I said: There is no power except with God. He said: The easiest of them is that you love for him what you love for yourself, and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. The second right is that you walk in his neighborhood and seek his pleasure and do not contradict his word, and the third right is that you connect to him with your self, your wealth, your hand, your foot, and your tongue. The fourth right is that you be his eye, his guide, his mirror, and his garment. The fifth right is that you are not full while he is hungry, and you are clothed while he is naked, and you are satisfied (with water) while he is thirsty.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, who said: Harun ibn Muslim ibn Sa'dan narrated to us, from Mus'ada ibn Sadaqah al-Rub'i, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said: For the believer upon the believer are seven obligatory rights from Allah, the Exalted: Honoring him in his sight, loving him in his chest, assisting him with his wealth, that he should deem for him what he deems good for himself, and that he should forbid backbiting him, and that he should visit him in his illness, and escort his funeral, and not speak of him after his death except good.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us about this, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) He said: The disbeliever eats with seven intestines

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The believer eats with one intestine, but the atheist eats with seven intestines.

My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abi Yahya al-Wasiti, who linked it through his chain to As-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said: The world is seven territories: Yajooj and Majooj, Rome, China, the Blacks (Zanj), the people of Moses, and the territories of Babel.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi'a, linking it up through his chain to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said: There are seven places/times in which there is no specific (time-bound) supplication: the funeral prayer, Qunut, Al-Mustajar, Safa and Marwa, standing at Arafat, and the two units of the circumambulation prayer.

Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), saying: Seven [types of people] are not to have the Quran recited to them [or do not recite the Quran]: the bowing one, the prostrating one, one in the toilet, one in the bath, the one in major ritual impurity, the woman in childbed, and the menstruating woman. The author of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: This indicates detestation (karahah), not absolute prohibition (nahy). This is because for the one in major ritual impurity and the menstruating woman, reciting the Quran is generally permissible, except for the four obligatory prostrations: Surah Luqman, Ha-Mim al-Sajdah, An-Najm when it runs, and Surah Iqra (Al-'Alaq). It has also been narrated that a man may recite the Quran in the bath provided his recitation is not vocalized loudly, as long as he is wearing a waistcloth. As for bowing and prostrating, one does not recite in them because the primary act in them is glorification, except what has been narrated regarding the Prayer of Need. As for the toilet, it is obligatory to keep the Quran from being recited in it. As for the woman in childbed, she follows the ruling of the menstruating woman in this regard.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman that he told Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Various narrations come to us from you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Quran was revealed in seven letters (ahruf), and the least that is permissible for an Imam is to issue decrees in seven different ways (wujuh).' 'This is Our bounty; bestow it or withhold it without account.' And he (peace be upon him) added: 'This is Our bounty; whether thou bestow them (on others) or withhold them, no account will be asked.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: A messenger from God came to me and said: 'Indeed, God the Exalted and Mighty commands you to recite the Quran in one letter.' I said: 'O Lord, be lenient with my nation.' He said: 'Indeed, God the Exalted and Mighty commands you to recite the Quran in one letter.' I said: 'O Lord, be lenient with my nation.' He said: 'Indeed, God commands you to recite the Quran in seven letters.'
