Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, saying: Abdul Rahman ibn al-Aswad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Mu'amir, from Ammar ibn Yasir, and from Jabir ibn Abdullah, that they said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'I shall reason with you on the Day of Resurrection, reasoning with you based on Prophethood, and you shall reason with your people, reasoning with them based on seven characteristics: establishment of prayer, payment of alms-tax, enjoining good, forbidding evil, justice among the subjects, fair division, and carrying out the command of God, the Mighty and Exalted. Do you not know, O Ali, that Abraham (peace be upon him) will be with us on the Day of Resurrection? He will be called and placed on the right side of the Throne, dressed in the attire of Paradise, adorned with its ornaments, and a gutter of gold will flow for him from Paradise, from which he will pour what is sweeter than honey, whiter than milk, and colder than snow. Then I will be called and placed on the left side of the Throne, and the same will be done to me. Then you, O Ali, will be called and the same will be done to you. Do you not like, O Ali, that you are called when I am called, dressed when I am dressed, and adorned when I am adorned? Indeed, God, the Mighty and Exalted, commanded me to bring you close so I do not distance you, and to teach you so I do not neglect you. It is incumbent upon you to learn, and it is incumbent upon me to obey my Lord, the Blessed and Exalted.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Hamzah ibn al-Qasim al-Alavi al-Abbasi said: Ja'far ibn Malik al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Qudus narrated to us, saying: Al-A'mash, from Musa ibn Tarif, from Ubayyah ibn Rabi', said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: I shall reason with the people on the Day of Resurrection with seven [things]: the establishment of prayer, the giving of alms-tax, enjoining good, forbidding evil, fair division with justice among the subjects, and the establishment of the prescribed limits.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sakuni al-Mazki al-Kufi in Kufa narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami said: Khalaf ibn Khalid al-Abdi narrated to us, saying: Bashr ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari narrated to us, on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma'dan, on the authority of Mu'az ibn Jabal, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): I contend with you regarding Prophethood and that there is no Prophet after me, and you shall contend with the people using seven [qualities], and none from the Quraysh will argue with you regarding them, because you are the first of them in faith, the most faithful to God's pledge, the most upright in God's command, the most equitable in division, the most just in ruling the subjects, the most perceptive in judgment, and the greatest in merit before God.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Asad al-Basri, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, who narrated on the authority of Khalaf ibn Hammad, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He passed by a group of people who were having blood-letting done for them. He told them: 'What would have been better for you if you had postponed it until Sunday evening, as that would be more effective in alleviating the ailment.'

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adamy, saying: Abu al-Hasan Umar ibn Sufyan al-Gorjany linked the narration up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), He said to one of his freedmen: 'O so-and-so, why did you not go out?' He replied: 'May I be your ransom, today is Sunday.' He asked: 'What is wrong with Sunday?' The man said: 'Because of the narration that came from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'Beware of Sunday, for it has a boundary like the boundary of a sword.' He said: 'They lied, they lied. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not say that, for 'Ahad' (One) is one of the Names of God, the Exalted.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, what about Monday?' He said: 'It was named after those two.' The man said: 'It was named after those two, yet they did not exist.' Abu Abdillah said to him: 'When you are told something, understand it! Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, knew the day on which He would take His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) back, and the day on which His Trustee would be oppressed, so He named it after those two.' I said: 'What about Tuesday?' He said: 'Hell was created on Tuesday, and that is His saying, the Exalted: "Go to that which you used to deny. Go to a shadow of three columns, which yields no shade and does not protect from the flame."' "Go to that which you used to deny. Go to a shadow of three columns, which yields no shade and does not protect from the flame." I said: 'What about Wednesday?' He said: 'The four pillars of Hell were built on Wednesday.' I said: 'What about Thursday?' He said: 'God created Paradise on Thursday.' I said: 'What about Friday?' He said: 'God, the Exalted, gathered the creation for our Wilayah (guardianship) on Friday.' I said: 'What about Saturday?' He said: 'The angels attended to their Lord on Saturday and found that He had always been One.'

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Yunus ibn Yaqoob, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had blood-letting performed on Monday and gave wheat to the phleotomist.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad, saying: He narrated to me Al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maysami or one of them, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, who mentioned it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to have blood-letting done on Monday after the afternoon prayer.

My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Yaqub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me, from Hammad ibn Isa, from someone he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Blood-letting (Hijamah) on Monday from the latter part of the day removes the disease completely from the body.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said: A man came to my brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) and said to him: May I be your ransom, I intend to go out, so pray for me. He said: When will you go out? He said: On Monday. He said to him: Why do you go out on Monday? He said: I seek blessings in it because the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was born on Monday. He said: They lied. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was born on Friday. And no day is greater in ill-omen than Monday, the day on which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) died and the revelation of heaven ceased on it, and we were wronged in it regarding our right. Shall I not guide you to an easy day on which God softened iron for David (peace be upon him)? The man said: Yes, may I be your ransom. He said: Go out on Tuesday.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Abi al-Zajra', from Suleiman, from Abi Nadrah, from Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever undergoes phlebotomy on the Tuesday of the seventeenth, nineteenth, or twenty-first day of the month, it will be a cure for him from every ailment of the year. And for what is other than that, it is a cure for headache, toothache, insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Munqeri, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha'i, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever wants to travel, it is better for him to go on a trip on Saturdays because if a stone becomes separated from the mountain, God will return it to its place on that day. It is better for those who have some need, to ask for it on a Tuesday since that is the day on which God softened iron for David (peace be upon him).

My father narrated to me, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from some of our companions, who said: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al- Askari (peace be upon them) on a Wednesday while he was having phlebotomy performed. I said to him: The residents of the two Harams narrate on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'Whoever has phlebotomy done on a Wednesday and suffers from white pigments (or blindness), let him blame only himself.' He replied: 'They lie. This only happens to those whose mothers were pregnant with them during menstruation.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Aslam, who said: I saw Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) performed phlebotomy on a Wednesday while he had a fever. The fever did not leave him, so he performed phlebotomy on Friday, and the fever left him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Al-Siyari narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq al-Baghdadi, I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (the second), peace be upon him, asking him about traveling on Wednesday, 'La Tudur' (the last Wednesday of the month). He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Whoever travels on Wednesday, La Tudur, to contradict the claim of those who consider it an ill omen, will be protected from every calamity, cured from every disease and ailment, and God will fulfill his needs.' I wrote to him again asking about blood-letting on Wednesday, 'La Tudur'. He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Whoever has blood-letting done on Wednesday, La Tudur, to contradict the claim of those who consider it an ill omen, will be cured from every calamity, protected from every ailment, and the place of blood-letting will not turn green.'

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Fadlata, from al-Aban, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Bashar ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Why do you not fast on Wednesday? He said: Because the Fire was created on Wednesday.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Adamy narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, he said: I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) have phlebotomy performed on him on a Wednesday after the afternoon prayer.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Abi Abdillah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them), who said: Avoid phlebotomy and depilation on Wednesday, for Wednesday is a day of continuous bad omen, and in it Hell was created.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: A man should have the hair removed (be shaved) on Wednesday, for it is a continuously unlucky day.

My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Yaqub ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mu'tab ibn al-Mubarak, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on a Thursday while he was undergoing phlebotomy (hijama). I asked him, 'O son of the Messenger of God, do you undergo phlebotomy on a Thursday?' He said, 'Yes. Whoever among you undergoes phlebotomy, let him do so on a Thursday, for on the evening of every Friday, the blood moves in scattered portions due to the Resurrection, and it does not return to its nest until the morning of Thursday.' Then he turned to his servant Rabih and said, 'O Rabih, hold the cup firmly, make the cupping glass soft, and make the incision a creeping one.' And Abu Abdillah said, 'Whoever undergoes phlebotomy on the last Thursday of the month in the early part of the day, the disease will leave him completely.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was first appointed [to prophethood], he would fast continuously until it was said: 'He will not break his fast.' And he would break his fast for days until it was said: 'He will not fast.' Then he abandoned that and fasted one day and skipped one day, which is the fasting of David (peace be upon him). Then he abandoned that, and he passed away while fasting on two Thursdays with a Wednesday in between them.

By the same chain of narration, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Sawid, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about fasting two Thursdays with a Wednesday in between them. He replied: As for Thursday, it is the day when deeds are presented; as for Wednesday, it is the day when Hell was created; and as for fasting, it is Paradise.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Aqabah, from Zakariya, from his father, from Yahya said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever cuts his nails on Thursday and leaves one to be cut on Friday, God will remove poverty from him.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Munqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever is a traveler should travel on Saturday, for if a stone were to shift from a mountain on Saturday, God would return it to its place.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Baghdadi al-Varraq narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Anbasat, the servant of al-Rashid, narrated that Darim ibn Qabaysa and Naim ibn Salih al-Tabari narrated that Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa, from his father Ja'far, from his father Muhammad, from his father Ali, from his father al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O God, bless my nation in their early hours on their Saturday and Thursday.

And by this chain of narration, he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Hasten to attend to your needs, for they will be easier to accomplish; accustom yourselves to writing letters, for they are more effective for fulfilling needs; and seek goodness near those with beautiful faces.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Muhammad al-Razi, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfaly, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever trims his nails on Saturday and on Thursday and removes hair from his moustache shall be cured from the pain of molars and the pain of the eye.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from more than one person, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Saturday is for us, Sunday is for our followers, Monday is for our enemies, Tuesday is for the Banu Umayya, Wednesday is the day of drinking medicine, Thursday is for fulfilling needs, Friday is for cleanliness and perfuming, and it is the Eid of the Muslims and it is better than Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, and the Day of Ghadir is the best of the Eids, and it is the eighteenth of Dhul-Hijjah and it was a Friday, and our Riser from the Ahl al-Bayt will emerge on a Friday, and the Resurrection will be on a Friday, and no deed on Friday is better than sending blessings upon Muhammad and his Household.

My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from Al-Fadl al-Ash'ari, from Al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Job (peace be upon him) was tested for seven years without having committed any sin.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Juwhari narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them. He said: Indeed, Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, was tested without sin, and indeed the Prophets do not sin because they are infallible and pure; they do not sin, nor do they deviate, nor do they commit a sin, small or large. And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, despite all that he was tested with, did not have a bad smell, nor was his appearance disfigured, nor did any amount of blood or pus come out from him, nor did anyone who saw him find him filthy, nor did anyone who witnessed him feel alienated from him, nor did any part of his body have worms, and thus God, the Exalted, does with all those He tests from among His Prophets and His honored friends, The people avoided him due to his poverty and weakness in the outward appearance of his condition, because of their ignorance of what he had with his Lord, Exalted is His remembrance, in terms of support and relief. And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people who suffer the greatest trials are the Prophets, then the next best, then the next best.' And God, the Exalted, tested him with the great trial that becomes trivial in the eyes of all people, so that they would not attribute lordship to him when they see what God intended to convey to him of great blessings, so that they may deduce from that that the reward from God, Exalted is His remembrance, is of two types: merit and special favor. And so that they do not belittle the weak for his weakness, nor the poor for his poverty, nor the sick for his illness, and so that they know that He makes ill whom He wills and cures whom He wills, whenever He wills, however He wills, by any means He wills. And He makes it a lesson for whom He wills, and misery for whom He wills, and happiness for whom He wills. And He is Just in His judgment and Wise in His actions. He does not do to His servants except what is best for them, and there is no power for them except through Him.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Ibn Muni’a said: Mus’ab narrated to me that Malik said: I was narrated from Aba Abdul Rahman, from Hafs ibn Asem, from Abi Sa’id al-Khidry, or from Abi Hurayrah. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Seven people will be shaded by God, the Mighty and Exalted, in His shade on the day when there is no shade except His shade: a just Imam, a youth who grew up in the worship of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man whose heart is attached to the mosque when he leaves it until he returns to it, two men who were in obedience to God, the Mighty and Exalted, so they gathered upon that and then separated, a man who remembered God, the Mighty and Exalted, in solitude and his eyes flowed with tears from the fear of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man whom a woman of good lineage and beauty invited and he said: Indeed I fear God, the Mighty and Exalted, and a man who gave charity and concealed it so that his left hand did not know what his right hand gave in charity.'

Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far (ibn al-Muzaffar) al-Alawi al-Umari al-Samarqandi (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masood al-Ayashi quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Ishkeeb, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufy, on the authority of Abi Jamileh Al-Asady, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Khizermi, on the authority of Salma ibn Kohayl who linked it up to Ibn Abbas that he said: The Prophet of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Seven [types of people] will be in the Shade of the Throne of God, the Mighty and Exalted, on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade: a just Imam, a young man who grew up in the worship of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man who gave charity with his right hand and concealed it from his left hand, a man who remembered God, the Mighty and Exalted, when he was alone and his eyes flowed with tears from the fear of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man who met his believing brother and said, "I love you for the sake of God, the Mighty and Exalted," a man who left the mosque with the intention of returning to it, and a man whom a beautiful woman invited to herself, but he said, "I fear God, Lord of the Worlds.'"

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had children from Khadijah: Al-Qasim and Al-Tahir (who was also called Abdullah), Umm Kulthum, Ruqayyah, Zaynab, and Fatimah. Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) married Fatimah (peace be upon her). Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', who was a man from Banu Umayyah, married Zaynab. Uthman ibn Affan married Umm Kulthum, but she died before he consummated the marriage with her. When they marched to Badr, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) married Ruqayyah to him. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) also had a son named Ibrahim from Maria al-Qibtiyya, who is also called Umm Ibrahim and Umm Walad.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who said: He narrated to me, Abu Ali al-Wasiti, from Abdullah ibn Ismat, from Yahya ibn Abdullah, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entered his house, and he found Aisha facing Fatimah, shouting at her, while she was saying: 'By God, O daughter of Khadijah, you do not think that your mother has superiority over us. What superiority did she have over us? She was nothing but like one of us.' Fatimah heard her statement, and when Fatimah saw the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), she cried. He said to her: 'What is making you cry, O daughter of Muhammad?' She replied: 'I remembered my mother and she slighted her, so I cried.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) became angry, then said: 'Be quiet, O Humayra (Aisha). Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, has blessed the fertile and affectionate woman. And indeed, Khadijah (may God have mercy on her) bore from me a pure one, who is Abdullah and he is al-Mutahhar, and she bore from me al-Qasim, and Fatimah, and Ruqayyah, and Umm Kulthum, and Zaynab. And you are one whom God made barren, so you did not bear anything for me.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Munqeri, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha'i that he had heard Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: There are eight who will carry God’s Throne. Each one of them has eight eyes, each of which equals all this world.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted (as a continuous chain) that As-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the bearers of the Throne are eight: one of them is in the form of a son of Adam, who asks God for the daily bread of Adam's offspring; the second is in the form of a rooster, who asks God for the daily bread for birds; the third is in the form of a lion, who asks God for the daily bread for beasts of prey; and the fourth is in the form of an ox, who asks God for the daily bread for quadrupeds. The ox lowered its head since the Children of Israel worshipped the calf, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, they will become eight.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hukam narrated to us, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Razqi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them all). He said: Indeed, Paradise has eight gates. One gate is for the Prophets and the Truthful ones. One gate is for the Martyrs and the Righteous ones. Five gates are for our Shiites and our beloved ones. I will remain standing at the Bridge (al-Sirat), supplicating and saying: 'O Lord, grant peace to my followers, my beloved, and my supporters, and whoever acknowledged my authority in this world.' Then the call will come from beneath the Throne, 'Your supplication has been answered and intercession has been granted for your followers.' And every man from my followers, and whoever acknowledged my authority, helped me, and fought whoever fought me, by deed or by word, will intercede for seventy thousand of his neighbors and relatives. And the last gate is for the rest of the Muslims, from those who testified that there is no god but Allah, and there was not in their hearts the weight of a speck of dust of hatred for us, the People of the House.

My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir al-Ja'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Have a good opinion of God, and know that for Paradise there are eight gates, the width of each of which is a journey of forty years.

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Bawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, who said: Abu Imran al-Ijli narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-'Ala' al-Khaffaf narrated to us, saying: 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi narrated, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "I did not say, nor did those who spoke before me say, anything like: 'There is no god but Allah.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfili, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The best act of worship is to say: 'There is no god but Allah.'

3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hilal, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, on the authority of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: There is nothing greater in reward than testifying that: 'There is no god but Allah,' because Allah, the Mighty and High, has nothing equal to Him, and no one shares His command.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakki (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi said, that Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i said, on the authority of his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfili, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, has given the believer a guarantee. I asked, 'What is it?' He replied, 'He guarantees him - if he acknowledges His Lordship, and Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) prophethood, and 'Ali's (peace be upon him) Imamate, and carries out what is obligatory upon him - that He will settle him in His Presence (jiwar). I said: 'By Allah! This is a blessing with which none of the blessings bestowed upon the children of Adam can compare!' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do little, and you will enjoy much.'

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever dies without ascribing a partner to Allah, whether he did good or evil, will enter Paradise.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted: "He is worthy of being feared and worthy of granting forgiveness," he said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "I am the most entitled to be feared, provided My servant does not associate anything with Me, and I am the most entitled, if My servant does not associate anything with Me, to admit him into Paradise." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has sworn by His might and majesty that He will never punish the people of His monotheism with the Fire."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shaybani (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi said, that Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, has forbidden Hellfire to the bodies of the monotheists.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn Umayrah, who said: Al-Hajjaj ibn Artat narrated to me, that Abu al-Zubayr narrated, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: The two inevitable outcomes: Whoever dies with testimony that there is no god but Allah (He is One, He has no partner) will enter Paradise, and whoever dies with testimony of associating partners with Allah will enter Hellfire.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn 'Umairah, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah, who said: Anas narrated to me, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said: Every stubborn tyrant is one who refuses to say 'There is no god but Allah.'

Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather, al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) He said: Jibra'il came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad! Blessed is he from among your Ummah who says: There is no god but Allah, Alone, Alone, Alone.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jamilah, from Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Jibra'il came to me while I was between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and said: 'O Muhammad! Blessed is anyone from your Ummah who says: There is no god but Allah, Unique, with sincerity.'

My father (Muhammad ibn al-Hasan) narrated to us, pleased with him, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi narrated from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Tufayl, from Ali (peace be upon him). He said: 'No Muslim servant says: There is no god but Allah, except that [the words] ascend, breaking through every roof, passing through nothing of his sins except that they obliterate them, until they reach an equal amount of good deeds, and then they stop.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar reported, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu `Abdillah al-Barqi, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sayf, on the authority of his brother `Ali, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, on the authority of `Ubayd ibn Zurarah, that Abu `Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The statement 'There is no god but Allah' is the price of Heaven.

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Sulayman ibn Amr, who said: 'Imran ibn Abu Ata' narrated to me, saying: Ata' narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: There is no word of speech more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and High, than 'La ilaha illa Allah' (There is no god but Allah). And there is no servant who says 'La ilaha illa Allah' and prolongs his voice with it until he finishes, except that his sins are scattered beneath his feet as the leaves of a tree are scattered beneath it.

Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Tamim al-Sarkhasi, the jurist of Sarkhas, said: Abu Labib Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami said: Harun ibn Abd Allah al-Jammal narrated to me from Abu Ayyub, who said: Qudamah ibn Muhraz al-Ashja'i narrated to me that Makhramah ibn Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Ashajj, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Harb ibn Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, said: I bear witness on my father, Zayd ibn Khalid, that I heard him say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent me saying, 'Give glad tidings to the people that whoever says: There is no god but Allah, Alone, who has no partner, will have Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated: Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Aban and others, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) He said: 'Whoever concludes his fasting with a virtuous word or a virtuous deed, Allah will accept his fasting.' He was asked: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the virtuous word?' He replied: 'The virtuous word is bearing witness that there is no god but Allah, and the virtuous deed is giving the Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast).'

Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bakr al-Khuri in Naysabur narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Faqih al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Juyibari, who is also called al-Hirawi, al-Niharawani, and al-Shaybani, narrated from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The reward for one upon whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has bestowed monotheism is nothing but Paradise.'

With this chain of narrators, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Verily, 'There is no god but Allah' is a great and noble word for Allah, the Mighty and High. Whoever says it sincerely deserves Paradise, and whoever says it falsely, his wealth and blood will be protected, but his final abode will be the Hellfire.

And with this chain of narrators, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Anyone who says: 'There is no god but Allah,' during an hour of the night or the day, will have what is in his book of evil deeds erased.

And with this chain of narrators, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Verily, Allah the Great and Almighty has a pillar of red ruby, the top of which is under the Throne, and the bottom of which is on the back of the fish in the lowest seventh Earth. When a servant says: 'There is no god but Allah', the Throne trembles, and the pillar moves, and the fish moves. So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Remain calm, O My Throne!' It replies: 'How shall I remain calm when You have not forgiven the one who uttered it?' Then Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Bear witness, O inhabitants of My heavens, that indeed I have forgiven the one who uttered it.'

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah, the jurist at Marw al-Rawdh, said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Naysaburi said: Abu al-Qasim Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abbas al-Ta'i said in Basra, that: My father related to me in the year 260 (AH) that: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) related to me in the year 194 (AH) that: My father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) related to me that: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) related to me that: My father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) related to me that: My father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) related to me that: My father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) related to me that: My father Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) related to me that: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Glorified be He, said: 'There is no god but Allah' is My Fortress. Whoever enters it is saved from My Chastisement.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Aqil narrated from Ishaq ibn Rahwayh, saying: When Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) arrived in Naysabur and intended to depart from there to al-Ma'mun, the traditionists gathered around him and said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! You are leaving us without narrating a hadith to us so that we may derive benefit from it? He was sitting in the 'ammariyyah (a camel-borne sedan), so he leaned his head out and said: I heard my father Musa ibn Ja'far say: I heard my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad say: I heard my father Muhammad ibn 'Ali say: I heard my father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn say: I heard my father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib say: I heard my father the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: I heard Jibra'il say: I heard Allah, Exalted be His Glory, say: 'There is no god but Allah is My Fortress. Whoever enters it is safe from My chastisement.' He said: Then when the camel passed by, he called out to us: 'It is subject to conditions, and I am among its conditions.' The Compiler of this book explains: Among its conditions is the acknowledgment that al-Rida (peace be upon him) is an Imam appointed by Allah, the Mighty and High, over the servants, with obedience to him being obligatory upon them.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ghalib al-Anmati narrated to us, saying: Abu Amr Ahmad ibn al-Hasn ibn Ghazwan informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: While a man was lying on his back, looking at the sky and the stars, and saying: 'By Allah, verily you have a Lord who is your Creator. O Allah, forgive me,' Allah, the Mighty and High, looked at him and forgave him. The compiler of this book said: And Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: 'Or do they not look into the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth and whatever things Allah created?' What is meant by this is: Have they not contemplated the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth and the wonders of their creation? Have they not looked at it with the gaze of one who reasons and reflects, so that they may know from what they see that which Allah established regarding the Heavens and the Earth, despite their great size and heaviness, supported without pillars and settled without tools? Thus they may deduce from this that their Creator, Master, and Sustainer does not resemble bodies, nor do the gods taken by the disbelievers besides Allah resemble Him, since bodies cannot sustain the smallest of particles in the air without pillars or tools. Through this, they recognize the Creator of the Heavens and the Earth and all other bodies, and recognize that He does not resemble them, nor do they resemble Him, in the power and dominion of Allah. As for the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth, it is Allah's dominion over them and His power upon them. What is meant is: Have they not looked and contemplated the Heavens and the Earth, seeing that Allah created them upon what they witness them to be upon, so that they may know that Allah is their Master and the One with power over them, because they are owned and created, and are within His power, authority, and dominion? He made their looking at the Heavens and the Earth and the creation of Allah for them as a look into their Kingdom and into Allah's dominion over them, because Allah does not create except what He owns and has power over. And by His words 'and whatever things Allah created,' He means: from the types of His creatio

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hamran, from Abu Abdillah (AS), said: Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah,' sincerely, will enter Paradise. And his sincerity is that the profession 'There is no god but Allah' refrains him from whatever Allah, the Mighty and High, has forbidden.

Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Amr al-Attar in Balkh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mamduh narrated to us, saying: Humran narrated from Malik ibn Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Abu Hasin, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was riding behind the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he said: 'O Mu'adh, do you know what is the right of Allah, the Mighty and High, upon the servants?' - he repeated it three times - I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'The right of Allah, the Mighty and High, upon the servants is that they do not associate anything with Him.' Then he said (peace be upon him and his family): 'Do you know what is the right of the servants upon Allah, the Mighty and High, if they do that?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'That He does not chastise them,' or he said: 'That He does not make them enter the Fire.'

Abu Ahmad al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us: He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Humran al-Qishiri narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Jarish Ahmad ibn Isa al-Kilabi narrated to us: Musa ibn Ismail ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon them all) narrated in the year 250 (AH): My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him). Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Is the reward of goodness aught but goodness?' Ali (peace be upon him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and High, said: What is the reward for one whom I have blessed with the best but Paradise?'

30. Al-Hakim `Abd al-Hamid ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Husayn said: Abu Yazid ibn Mahbub al-Muzni said: al-Husayn ibn `Isa al-Bastami said: `Abd al-Samad ibn `Abd al-Warith said: Shu`bah on the authority of Khalid al-Hadhdha’ on the authority of Abu Bushr `Anbari on the authority of Humran on the authority of `Uthman ib `Affan said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: “He who dies knowing that Allah is the Truth [Haqq] will enter Heaven.”

33 - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Abu Ayyub, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: He who says: 'There is no god but Allah' one hundred times will be the best of the people in deeds on that day, unless someone says it more often than he does.

Three narrators - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Salih, from Isa ibn Abd Allah who is from the children of Umar ibn Ali, from his forefathers, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said: Allah, Mighty be His Glory, said to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! If the heavens and their inhabitants, and the seven earths, were in one scale, and "There is no god but Allah" were in the other scale, then "There is no god but Allah" would tip the scale.'

35. My father (ra) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd al-Aziz al-Abdi, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (AS) who said: I heard him say: Whoever says in a day: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the One and Only, who has no partners; the God [ilah], the One [wahid], the Unique [ahad], on whom all depend, who has not taken a partner nor son,' Allah, the Majestic and Glorious, will record for him 45 thousand thousand good deeds, and erase from him 45 thousand thousand evil deeds, and raise for him in Paradise 45 thousand thousand degrees, and he will be like one who recited the Quran twelve times, and Allah will build a house for him in Paradise.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Musa ibn 'Imran, on the authority of his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sufyan, said: Abu 'Ali al-Qassab related to me, saying: I was in the presence of Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him). I said: 'All praise is to Allah, the limit of His Knowledge.' He said: 'Do not say that, for indeed, there is no limit to His Knowledge.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Kahili, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a supplication: 'All praise is to Allah, the end of His Knowledge.' He wrote back to me: 'Do not say: the end of His Knowledge, but say: the end of His Pleasure.'

3. 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi said: Musa ibn 'Imran narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Knowledge is part of His Perfection.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Sayrafi, from Bakkar al-Wasiti, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, from Humran ibn A'yun, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) concerning knowledge, who said: It is your hand from you. Muhammad ibn Ali, the compiler of this book, said: This means that knowledge is not other than Him, and it is from His essential attributes, because Allah, the Mighty and High, is a Self that is All-Knowing and All-Seeing. Our intent in describing Him with knowledge is to negate ignorance from Him. And we do not say that knowledge is separate from Him, because if we said that, and then said that Allah has always been Knowing, we would be affirming with Him something eternal that has always existed. Exalted is Allah, the Elevated and Great, from that.

5. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: 'What do you think of what has happened and what will happen until the Day of Resurrection? Is it not in the Knowledge of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, before He created the heavens and the earth.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of God upon him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Isma'il and Ibrahim ibn Hashim both, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked him — meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — 'Is there anything that exists today that was not in the Knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and High?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'No, but it was in His Knowledge before He raised the Heavens and the Earth.'

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (RA) said: My father related to me that Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma`il ibn Bazigh, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan, on the authority of Jabir that Abu Ja`far (AS) said: Verily, Allah, the One – may His Names be Blessed and Exalted in His Elevated Essence – united everything in His Unity, then applied it to His Creation. Therefore, He is Alone, the Needless, the Master, and the glorified. Everything serves Him, and everything depends upon Him. Our Lord is beyond our grasp, and our Lord’s Knowledge encompasses everything.

Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Bashshar narrated to us, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both) He (AS) said: I asked him: Does Allah know the thing that has not yet come into existence, how it would be if it were to come into existence, or does He know only what will come into existence? He (AS) said: Verily, Allah, the Exalted, is the Knower of things before they come into existence, Allah, the Mighty and High, says: 'Surely, We wrote what you did.' And He says to the people of Hell: 'And if they were sent back, they would certainly go back to that which they are forbidden, and most surely they are liars.' Hence, Allah the Mighty and High, knew that if He sent them back, they would certainly go back to what they were forbidden. And He said to the angels when they said: 'What! Wilt Thou place in it such as shall make mischief in it and shed blood, and we celebrate Thy praise and extol Thy holiness?' He said: 'Surely, I know what you do not know.' Therefore, the Knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and High, is eternal, and embraces all things even before they are created. Blessed be our Lord, the Exalted, the Elevated, and the Great, who created things and had knowledge of them prior to their creation as He willed. Thus, our Lord has always been All-Knowing, All-Hearing, and All-Seeing.

And with this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Abdullah, who said: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He: 'Did He have knowledge of location before He created location? Or did His knowledge come when He created it or after He had created it?' So he (peace be upon him) replied: 'Exalted is Allah! Rather, He was always knowing of location before its formation, just as His knowledge of it after He formed it. And likewise His knowledge of all things is like His knowledge of location.' The compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'A proof that Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, is Knowing is that actions, differing in estimation, opposite in planning, and unequal in craftsmanship, do not occur in the manner of wisdom from one who does not know it, nor do they continue on an organized path from one who is ignorant of it. Do you not see that one who does not know goldsmithing cannot craft an earring, governing its work and placing each of its fine and coarse parts in its place? Nor can one who does not know writing compose a book in which every letter follows the one before it? And the Knowing One is more subtle in craftsmanship and more brilliant in arrangement than what we have described. Therefore, its occurrence from one who is not Knowing of its manner before its existence is more distant and more impossible. And the confirmation of this is:'

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur al-Sayqal, from Abu Abd Allah (AS) who said: Verily, Allah is Knowledge as there is no ignorance in Him, Life as there is no death in Him, and Light as there is no darkness in Him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): "We have narrated that Allah is Knowledge, in which there is no ignorance; He is Life, in which there is no death; He is Light, in which there is no darkness." He (peace be upon him) replied: "That is exactly how He is."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from 'Isa ibn Abi Mansur, from al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: Verily, Allah is Light in which there is no darkness, and Knowledge in which there is no ignorance, and Life in which there is no death.

Allah's mercy be upon Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Imran, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Zayd ibn al-Mu'ddil al-Namiri and 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, there is knowledge known to Allah alone, and verily there is knowledge which is known to His Closest Angels and Messengers. We also know it.

And with this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn Abi Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from al-Ala', from the righteous servant Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: The Knowledge of Allah cannot be described in terms of 'where,' nor can the Knowledge of Allah be described in terms of 'how.' Knowledge cannot be separated from Allah, nor can Allah be separated from Knowledge. There is no boundary between Allah and His Knowledge.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Taylisi al-Khazzaz al-Kufi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, our Lord, the Mighty and Exalted, was ever-present with knowledge as His Essence and not as something known, hearing as His Essence and not as something heard, sight as His Essence and not as something seen, and power as His Essence and not as something acted upon. When He created the things, and He was the Known, knowledge descended from Him upon the known, hearing upon the heard, sight upon the seen, and power upon the acted upon. I asked: 'So was Allah always Speaking?' He replied: 'Verily, speech is an originated attribute, not eternal. Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, existed when there was no Speaker.'

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated: Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated, from Isma'il ibn Sahl, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) I said: 'Does Allah always know?' He said: 'How can He know when there is nothing to be known?' I said: 'Does Allah always hear?' He said: 'How can He hear when there is nothing to be heard?' I said: 'Does He always see?' He said: 'How can He see when there is nothing to be seen?' Then he said: 'Allah has always been All-Knowing, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, possessing knowledge, hearing, and seeing.'

3. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, who said: Al-Fadl ibn Sulayman al-Kufi narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Khalid, who said: I heard al-Rida, Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them), saying: Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Ever-Living, Ever-Lasting, All-Hearing, and All-Seeing. I asked him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, there is a group that says: Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has always been All-Knowing with knowledge, All-Powerful with power, Ever-Living with life, Ever-Lasting with antiquity, All-Hearing with hearing, and All-Seeing with sight.' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'Whoever says this and accepts it has taken other gods with Allah, and they are not under our guardianship at all.' He then added, 'Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Ever-Living, Ever-Lasting, All-Hearing, and All-Seeing by His Essence. Exalted is He, the Elevated, the Great, from what the polytheists and anthropomorphists say.'

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (RA) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Harun ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) was asked about Divine Unity. He said: He, the Mighty and High, is undoubtedly Existent. He is not vain or numerable, nor can He be described on the basis of the attributes of creation. He, the Mighty and High, possesses Qualities [nu'ut] and Attributes [sifat]. There are Attributes which apply to Him which can also be applied to the created such as hearing, seeing, affectionate, merciful, and their likes. Whereas the Qualities are qualities of Essence; they do not befit anyone but Allah, the Blessed and Exalted. Allah is Light as there is no darkness in Him. He is Ever-Living as there is no death for Him. He is All-Knowing as there is no ignorance in Him. He is Needless [Samad] as there is no need in Him. Our Lord is Light by Essence, Ever-Living by Essence, All-Knowing by Essence, and Needless by Essence.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (mercy of God be upon him) said: My paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim related to me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, on the authority of Amr ibn Shimr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, was there when there was nothing but Him. He was Light as there was no darkness in Him. He was the Truth as there was no falsehood in Him. He was Omniscient as there was no ignorance in Him. He was the EverLiving as there was no death in Him. And that is how He is today, and that is how He will remain forever.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Auramah, that Yahya ibn Yahya said on the authority of Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abd al-A'la, from the Servant of God Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: Verily, Allah - there is no god but He - is Ever-living without quality or place, and He was not in anything, nor on anything. He did not create for His Position any space, nor was He strengthened after creating things. Nothing that comes into being is like Him. He was not devoid of power over dominion before creating them, nor will He be devoid of power after they cease. He, the Mighty and High, is a God who is Ever-living without accidental life, a King before creating anything and a Master after creating it. Allah has no limit, and is not known by anything that resembles Him. He does not age due to permanence, nor does He become stunned by the call of anything; and by His Fear all things become stunned. Allah is Ever-living without accidental life or described existence, without limited quality or fixed place or stationary location, but He is Ever-living by Himself, and the Master who has always possessed power. He created what He willed when He willed, by His Will and Power. He is the First without quality, and will be the Last without place. Everything is perishable except His Face. His is the creation and the command; blessed is the Lord of the worlds.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (RA) said: my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim related to me that Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi al-Kufi related to me that Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar that I asked al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (AS): "Inform me about Allah, the Blessed and Exalted. Has He sempiternally been All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Knowing, and All-Powerful?" He (AS) replied, "Of course." Hence, I asked him, "There is a man who professes to be a friend of the Household of the Prophet (AS) and says: `Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has always been All-Seeing with an ear, All-Hearing with an eye, All-Knowing by Knowledge, and All-Powerful with power.'" He (AS) became angry and then said: "Verily, whoever says this and believes in it, is a polytheist and is not under our Guardianship at all. Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Possessor of the Knowledge of Hearing, Seeing, and Omnipotence."

Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (mercy of God be upon him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim informed us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: Among the attributes of the Eternal is that He is One, Unique, Self-Sufficient, Unique in meaning, and not [subject to] many different meanings. He said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom.' A group of Iraqis claim that He hears with something other than what He sees, and sees with something other than what He hears. He said: 'They have lied, apostatized, and anthropomorphized. Exalted is Allah from that. Verily, He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He hears with what He sees, and sees with what He hears.' I said: 'They claim that He is All-Seeing as they understand it.' He said: 'Exalted is Allah. Verily, [human] understanding applies only to that which has the attributes of created beings, and Allah is not like that.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakklin (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said regarding the hadith of the atheist who asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Do you say that He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing?' Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied: 'He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He is All-Hearing without a sense organ, and All-Seeing without a tool. Rather, He hears by His Own Self and sees by His Own Self. My statement that He hears by His Self does not mean that His Hearing is one entity and His Self is another entity. Rather, I intended to express myself using terminology suitable for when I was being questioned, and to make you understand since you were the questioner. Thus, I say: He hears with His Entire Essence, not that His Entire Essence is a part of Him. I intended to make you understand and to express Myself. My only recourse in this matter is to affirm that He is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Knowing, All-Aware, without any difference in His Essence and without any difference in His Meaning.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from al-Fadil ibn Sukkarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom! If you see fit to teach me: Did Allah, may His Remembrance be Exalted, know before He created the creation that He was alone? Your followers have differed regarding this. Some of them said: 'The Blessed and Exalted surely knew that He was alone before He created anything from His creation.' And some of them said: 'The meaning of 'He knows' is 'He does'; so He knows today that there is no other before the doing of things.' And they said: 'If we affirm that He has always been Knowing that there is no other, then we have affirmed with Him an 'other' in His eternity.' If you see fit, O my Master, to teach me what is not other than this, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Allah, the Exalted, has always been Knowing, Blessed and Exalted be His Remembrance.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Salim, from Ibn Maskin, from Ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: Allah was, and there was nothing else, and He has always been Knowing of what He created. His knowledge of them before their creation is like His knowledge of them after He created them.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh that he wrote to Abu al-Hasan (AS) asking him about Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Did He have knowledge of things before He created them and their existence, or did He not know that until He created them and willed their creation and formation, so He knew what He created when He created it and what He formed when He formed it?' He (AS) wrote in his own handwriting: 'Allah remained knowing of things before He created them, just as His knowledge of things after He created them.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa'd ibn Abd Allah both narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of his father, and al-Husayn ibn Sa'd, and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, on the authority of Ibn Abu Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, that I entered into the presence of Abu Abdillah (AS) so he asked me: 'Can you describe Allah?' I replied, 'Yes.' He said: 'Give it.' I said: 'He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' He said: 'This is an attribute shared by the created.' I asked: 'Then how do you describe Him?' He said: 'He is Light with no darkness in Him, Ever-Living with no death in Him, Knowing with no ignorance in Him, Truth with no falsehood in Him.' I left from his presence and I was the most learned of people regarding Divine Unity.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Aban narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him: 'Has Allah always been the Willer?' He replied: 'Indeed, the Willer is not [called such] except for a Will that is with Him; rather, He has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, then He intended.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Inform me about the Will, is it from Allah or from the creation?' He said: 'The will of the creation is the inner self (conscience), and what manifests from it afterwards in the form of action. As for Allah, the Mighty and High, His Will is His Creating (making), and nothing else, because He does not reflect, does not imagine, and does not think. These attributes are absent from Him, and they are attributes of the created beings. Thus, Allah’s Will is the Action itself, and nothing else. He says to it: “Be,” and it is, without a word or speech by the tongue, without imagination or thought, and without a “how” to it, just as He is without a “how.”'

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abd Allah (AS) who said: The walking is accidental [muhdathah].

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from al-Mansur ibn Yunus, from Jalis for Abu Hamzah, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): The Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Everything is perishable but He (His Face).' (1) He (AS) replied: Everything will perish, but the Face will remain. Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is Greater than being attributed with a face. However, the meaning of this is that everything will perish except His Religion and the Face from which He bestows.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Sa'id al-Makari from Abu Basir from al-Harith ibn al-Mughayrah al-Nasri, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (Everything is perishable but Him). He (AS) answered: Everything is perishable except the one who followed the Right Path.
And with this chain of narrators, he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: We are the Face of Allah, which does not perish.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated: `Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Barqi, from his father, from Rabi' al-Warraq, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu `Abd Allah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Every thing is perishable but His Face.' He (AS) said: 'We.'

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf ibn Umayrah al-Nakha'i, from Khaythamah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Everything is perishable but His Face.' He (peace be upon him) replied: It is His Religion. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) are the Religion of Allah, His Face and His Eye among His servants, His tongue with which He speaks, and His Hand over His creation. And we are the Face of Allah through which He is approached; we will remain among His servants as long as Allah has a 'viewing/consideration' (ru'yah) for them. I asked: And what is the 'viewing/consideration'? He said: Need (al-hajah). When Allah has no need for them, He removes us to Him and does what He pleases.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan said: Bakr, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, on the authority of al-Haytham ibn 'Abd Allah, on the authority of Marwan ibn Sabah, that Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah the Mighty and High, made us the best of creation, and moulded us from the best of moulds. He made us His Eye through which He sees His Servants. He made us the Tongue with which He speaks to His Creation. He made us the Outspread Hand of Mercy over His Servants. He made us the Face through which He bestows His Bounties. He made us the Gate that leads to Him. And He made us His Treasure in the Heaven and on His Earth. It is due to us that trees bear fruits, that fruit ripens, that rivers flow, that clouds shower down rain, and that the Earth grows grass. It is through our service [ibadah], Allah is served. If it were not for us, Allah would not have been worshipped.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub on the authority of 'Abd al-'Aziz on the authority of Ibn Abu Ya'fur that Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah is One, Alone, Sole in His Unity, Unique in His Affair. He created a creation and delegated to them the affair of His Religion, so we are that creation, O son of Abu Ya'fur! We are the Proof of Allah among His servants, and His Witnesses to His Creation, the Trustees of His Revelation, the Treasurers of His Knowledge, the Face with which He bestows [His bounties], the Eye in His creatures, the Speaking Tongue, the Embracing Heart, the Door that guides to Him, and we are those who act by His Command and call to His Path. Through us Allah was known, and through us Allah was worshipped. We are the Guides unto Allah, and were it not for us, Allah would not have been worshipped.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated from al-Jariri, from Abu al-Ward ibn Thumamah, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) heard a man say to another: 'May Allah make ugly your face and the face of one who resembles you.' So He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wait, do not say this, for indeed Allah created Adam in His image.' The compiler of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I left the anthropomorphists from the beginning of this hadith, and they said: 'Indeed Allah created Adam in His image.' Thus, they went astray in its meaning and led others astray.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him):' "O Son of the Messenger of Allah! Verily, the people relate that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah created Adam in His Image.'" He (peace be upon him) replied: "May Allah kill them! They have certainly removed the first part of the tradition. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by two men who were cursing each other. He (peace be upon him) heard one of them say to the other: 'May Allah make your face and the face of the one who resembles you ugly!' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O servant of Allah! Do not say this to your brother, for verily Allah, the Mighty and High, created Adam in His Image.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan said: Bakr, on the authority of Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Bahr, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) I said: His Word, the Mighty and High: 'O Iblis! What prevented you that you should do obeisance to him whom I created with My Two Hands?' He (AS) replied: The hand in the speech of the Arabs means power and bounty. He said: 'And remember Our servant Dawud, the Possessor of Power.' And He said: 'And the Heaven, We raised it high with power,' meaning with power. And He said: 'And whom He has strengthened with an inspiration from Him,' meaning He strengthened them. And it is said: So-and-so has many hands with me, meaning excess and beneficence, and so-and-so has a white hand with me, meaning bounty.

2. Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isam al-Kulayni, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Ya`qub al-Kulayni said: Ahmad ibn Idris on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa on the authority of `Ali ibn Sayf on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ubaydah that I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High, to Iblis: (What prevented you that you should do obeisance to him whom I created with My Two Hands? Are you proud or are you of the exalted ones?)? He (AS) replied: “It means `With My Omnipotence and My Power.’” The Compiler of this book says: I have heard one of the Shi`ite scholars in Naysabur mentioning that Imams (peace be upon them) used to stop at these Word of Allah when mentioning this verse: What prevented you that you should do obeisance to him whom I created. Then they would continue with Word of the Mighty and High: “With My Two Hands, are you proud or are you of the exalted ones?” He also said: It is like the statement of a person: “With my sword you are fighting with me, and with my spear you are attacking me.” It is as if the Mighty and High is saying that “My Bounties have strengthened your pride and insubordination.” What prevented you that you should do obeisance to him whom I created with My Two Hands?
