Are you proud or are you of the exalted ones? With my sword you are fighting with me, and with my spear you are attacking me. My Bounties have strengthened your pride and insubordination.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated from Bakr, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) Regarding His Mighty and Exalted Word: 'On the Day when there shall be a severe affliction,' he said: 'A veil of light will be revealed, causing the believers to fall prostrate, while the backbones of the hypocrites will be twisted tightly, preventing them from prostrating.'

My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Fuddal, from Abu Jamiilah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His Word, the Mighty and High: 'On the Day when there shall be severe affliction,' he said: 'Blessed be the Supreme [Jabbar]!' Then he pointed to his shin and lifted the clothing which covered it, saying: 'And they shall be called upon to make obeisance, but they shall not be able.' He said: 'The people will be silenced, fear will enter them, their eyes will look fixedly, their hearts will reach their throats, their eyes will be in a state of humbleness, and they will be humiliated when they are called upon to make obeisance, although they are sound.' Muhammad ibn Ali the Compiler of this book says: What he (peace be upon him) meant by his statement 'Blessed be the Supreme!' after which he pointed to his shin and uncovered it, was 'Blessed be the Supreme! He is far above having a shin, Who is such.'

3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, from al-Husayn ibn Musa, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) He (AS) said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'On the Day when there shall be a severe affliction.' He (AS) lifted the clothing that covered his shin, placed his other hand on his head, and said: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High!' The Compiler of this book says: The meaning of his statement 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High' is that Allah, the Mighty and High, is far Exalted from having a shin.

And it has been narrated from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the Earth; a likeness of His Light is as a niche in which is a lamp." So he replied: It is an example Allah has given for us. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imams, may Allah's blessings be upon them all, are the Signs of Allah and His miracles through which one is guided towards Divine Unity, towards the interests of Religion, towards Islamic laws, towards obligations and recommendations. And there is no power except with Allah, the Most High and Most Great.

And the confirmation of that is what Ibrahim ibn Harun al-Hiti narrated to us in the city of Al-Salam, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abu al-Thalj narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ghalib, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Dhahali, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): I asked: 'Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the Earth?' He answered: 'Thus is Allah, the Mighty and High.' I asked: 'A likeness of His Light?' He answered: 'Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' I asked: 'As a niche?' He replied: 'The chest of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' I asked: 'In which is a lamp?' He said: 'In it is the Light of Knowledge, meaning Prophethood.' I asked: 'The lamp is in a glass?' He answered: 'The knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is a chest [container] leading to the heart of Ali (peace be upon him).' I asked: 'As if it were?' He asked: 'To what do you read I asked: 'Lit from a blessed olive-tree, neither eastern nor western?' He replied: 'That is the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him), neither Jewish nor Christian.' I asked: 'The oil whereof almost gives light though fire touches it not?' He answered: 'The knowledge almost comes out of the mouth of the learned from the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him) before they even speak it.' I asked: 'Light upon light?' He said: 'An Imam (peace be upon him), one after another.'

Ibrahim ibn Harun al-Hiti narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abu al-Thalj narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Sabih narrated to us, saying: Zarif ibn Nasih narrated from Isa ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them). Regarding the Word of the Mighty and High: 'As a niche in which is a lamp.' He explained: The niche is the Light of Knowledge contained in the Chest of the Prophet (SA). The lamp is in a glass; the glass is the chest of 'Ali (AS). The knowledge of the Prophet (SA) was transferred to 'Ali’s Chest. The glass is as if it were a brightly shining star, lit from a blessed olive-tree. He added: Light, neither eastern nor western. He said: 'Neither Jewish nor Christian.' The oil whereof almost gives light though fire touches it not. He said: 'The learned from the Progeny of Muhammad (SA) more or less give knowledge before they are even asked.' Light upon light, meaning an Imam (AS), endorsed through the light of knowledge and wisdom, one after another, from the Progeny of Muhammad (SA), and that is from Adam (AS) to the Day of Judgement. These successors were appointed by Allah, the Mighty and High, as His Caliphs on Earth and His Proofs for His Creation. The Earth is not free at any time from at least one of them (AS). The proof of this statement can be found in the words of Abu Talib (AS) regarding the Messenger of Allah (SA): 'Muhammad! You are the Trustworthy, the Lord, and the Magnanimous Master, For the noble, the best, the generous, and the pure in lineage. You are the Most Auspicious of the fortunate surrounded by the luckiest. Since the time of Adam there has always been amongst us a divinely-guided successor. I have recognized you as the truthful in words that is not refuted. You spoke the truth when you were but a beardless child.' He (Abu Talib) says: 'You spoke with knowledge as a child, even before anything was revealed to you. You were like Abraham (AS) who told his people as a youth: Surely I am clear of what you set up (with Allah); and like Jesus (AS) when he spoke from his cradle that Surely I am a servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet; and He has made me blessed wherever I may be.' In a similar poem, Abu Talib (AS) said the following regarding the Messenger of Allah (SA): 'There is no one like him among m

5. Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Warraq said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab said: on the authority of Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, on the authority of al-Khattab ibn Umar and Mus'ab ibn Abd Allah al-Kufiyyin, on the authority of Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; a likeness of His Light is as a niche.' He replied: 'The niche is the Chest of the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in which is the lamp. The lamp is the knowledge in the glass. The glass is the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the knowledge of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is with him.' Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth; a likeness of His Light is as a niche. Chapter: The Commentary of the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'They forgot Allah, so He forgot them.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi said: Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i al-Kufi said on the authority of his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of whoever related to him, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "I am the Knowledge of Allah, I am the Containing Heart of Allah, the Speaking Tongue of Allah, the Eye of Allah, the Side of Allah, and I am the Hand of Allah." The Compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The meaning of his saying (peace be upon him): 'And I am the Containing Heart of Allah,' is: 'I am the heart that Allah has made a container for His Knowledge, and His heart towards His obedience.' It is a created heart of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, just as he is a servant of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted. And 'Heart of Allah' is said in the same way that one says 'Servant of Allah,' 'House of Allah,' 'Paradise of Allah,' and 'Hell of Allah.' As for his saying: 'The Eye of Allah,' he means by it: The Preserver of the Religion of Allah. And Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has said: 'Sailing by Our Eyes,' which means 'by Our Observance.' And similarly, His saying, the Mighty and Exalted: 'And that you might be brought up before My Eyes,' its meaning is 'with My Observance.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said; al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayb, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in his sermon: I am the Guide, and I am the Rightly-Guided, and I am the Father of the Orphans and the Poor, and the Husband of the Widows, and I am the Refuge of every weak one and the Shelter of every fearful one, and I am the Leader of the Believers to Paradise, and I am the Firm Rope of Allah, and I am the Firmest Handle of Allah and the Word of Piety, and I am the Eye of Allah, and His Truthful Tongue, and His Hand, and I am the Side of Allah who says: 'Lest a soul should say: O woe to me! For what I fell short of my duty to Allah,' and I am the Outspread Hand of Allah towards His Servants, granting mercy and forgiveness, and I am the Door of Divine Mercy. Whoever recognizes me and recognizes my right has recognized his Lord, because I am the Successor of my Prophet on His Earth, and His Proof upon His creation. No one denies this except one who rejects Allah and His Messenger. Lest a soul should say: O woe to me! For what I fell short of my duty to Allah. The Compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Al-Janb' (Side) in the language of the Arabs means obedience. It is said: 'This is little in the side of Allah,' meaning 'This is little in terms of obedience to Allah, the Mighty and High.' Therefore, the meaning of the statement of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'I am the Side of Allah,' is 'I am the one whose guardianship represents obedience to Allah.' Allah, the Mighty and High, said: 'Lest a soul should say: O woe to me! For what I fell short of my duty to Allah,' i.e., in the obedience of Allah, the Mighty and High.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Muhammad ibn Bishr al-Hamdani, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah say: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) related to me that on the Day of Resurrection, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be holding Allah's Waistband, we (the family of the Prophet) will be holding our Prophet's Waistband, and our Shi'ites will be holding our Waistband. I asked, 'O Commander of the Faithful, what is the Waistband?' He answered, 'Allah is greater than being characterized with a waistband or anything else. However, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be holding Allah's Affair, we (the family of Muhammad) will be holding our Prophet's Affair, and our Shi'ites will be holding our Affair.'

2. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Resurrection will be holding Allah's Waistband, and we will be holding the Prophet's Waistband, and our Shi'ites will be holding our Waistband. Then he said: And the Waistband is the Light.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas related to me that al-Hasan ibn Yusuf said on the authority of 'Abd al-Salam, on the authority of 'Ammar ibn Abu al-Yaqzan, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will come on the Day of Judgment holding the waistband of his Lord, and we will be holding the waistband of our Prophet, and our Shi'ites will be holding our waistband. So we and our Shi'ites are the Party of Allah, and the Party of Allah are the triumphant ones. By Allah, we do not claim that it is the waistband of the garment, but rather it is greater than that. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will come holding the religion of Allah, and we will come holding the religion of our Prophet, and our Shi'ites will come holding our religion.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn Nu'man, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from someone who heard it from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) that he said regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: ('And the Jews say: The hand of Allah is tied up') They did not mean it literally, but they said: 'The matter is complete, so it neither increases nor decreases.' So Allah, exalted by His glory, refuted their statement: ('Shall be shackled their hands, and cursed are they for what they say; Nay, both His hands are spread out; He expends as He pleases.') Have you not heard Allah, the Mighty and High, say: ('Allah makes to pass away and establishes what He pleases, and with Him is the basis of the Book?')

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Mashriqi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: 'Nay, both His Hands are spread out.' So I asked him, 'Does He have hands like this?' and I pointed with my hand to his hand. He replied, 'No, for if that were the case, He would have been created.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris related to me, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from al-Mashriqi, from Hamzah ibn al-Rabi`, from one he mentioned, that he said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja`far (peace be upon him) when `Amr ibn `Ubayd entered and said to him: May I be your ransom, regarding the Word of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted: 'And to whomsoever My Wrath is due shall perish indeed.' What is that wrath? Abu Ja`far (peace be upon him) replied: It is punishment, O `Amr. Verily, whoever claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, declines from one thing to another, then he has certainly given Him an attribute of the created. Verily, nothing instigates Allah, the Mighty and High, and nothing modifies Him.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkhil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amr al-Fuqaymi, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that a man asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) whether Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has pleasure and anger? He (peace be upon him) replied: Yes; however, it is not like what is found in created beings. This is because pleasure and anger are external intrusions that enter him, transferring him from one state to another, agitated, composite, with things having an influence in him. But our Creator has no influence of things in Him; He is One, One in Essence, and One in Meaning. His pleasure is His reward and His anger is His punishment, without anything intermingling with Him to stir Him up and transfer Him from one state to another. Indeed, that is the attribute of the helpless, needy created beings. He, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Powerful, the Honorable, who has no need of anything of what He created, and all His creation is in need of Him. He created things without any need or cause, by creation and innovation.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sakkari said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari said, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umrah, on the authority of his father, that I asked al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them): I said to him: 'O Son of the Messenger of Allah! Inform me about Allah, the Mighty and High. Does He have pleasure and anger?' He said: 'Yes, but not in the sense that is found among created beings. Indeed, the anger of Allah is His punishment, and His pleasure is His reward.' The chapter on the meaning of His saying, the Mighty and High: 'And I breathed into him of My spirit.'

Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ala' ibn Rizin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (And breathed into him of My Spirit). He (AS) replied, 'A spirit that Allah chose, selected, and created for Himself, and favored over all other spirits, so He commanded and breathed from it into Adam.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibn Fuddal, from al-Halabi and Zurarah, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Alone, the Needless, without an interior. Verily, the Spirit is a creation from His creations. It is a helper, aid, and a source of strength. Allah places it in the hearts of the messengers and the Believers.

3. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, who said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And I breathed into him of My Spirit.' What is this breathing? He (AS) said: Verily, the spirit moves like the wind. It is called a spirit because its name is derived from the word wind. He expressed it using the word 'spirit' because the spirit is homogeneous to the wind. He attributed it to Himself because He selected it over all other spirits, just as He selected a house from among houses and said: 'My House,' and said to a Messenger from among His Messengers: 'My Friend,' and similar things. All of that is created, made, originated, nurtured, and managed.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Ja'far al-Asamm, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the spirit that was in Adam (peace be upon him) and the one that was in 'Isa (peace be upon him), what are they? He (peace be upon him) replied: 'They are two created spirits, which He chose and selected, the spirit of Adam (peace be upon him) and the spirit of 'Isa (peace be upon him).'

5. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, who said: Ali ibn al-Abbas narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Asbat narrated from Sayf ibn 'Umairah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding His Mighty and Exalted Word: (And I breathed into him of My Spirit). He (peace be upon him) said: From My power.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani; al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mukattab, and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran (may Allah be pleased with them) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas said: 'Ubayn ibn Hisham said on the authority of 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Amr, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) In His Word, the Mighty and High: (So when I have made him complete and breathed into him of My Spirit), he replied: Verily Allah, the Mighty and High, created a creation and created a spirit, then commanded an angel to breathe into him; hence it is not that which nullified any of His power. (So when I have made him complete and breathed into him of My Spirit) Chapter: The Negation of Place, Time, Rest, Motion, Descent, Ascent, and Transition from Allah, the Mighty and High

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, who said: Nafi' ibn al-Azqar asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Inform me about Allah, since when has He existed? He (peace be upon him) replied to him: Woe be upon you! Tell me when He did not exist, so that I can tell you when He did exist. Glory be to Him, who has always been and will always be, the Peerless, the Needless, who has taken neither wife nor son.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said: A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him: 'O Abu Ja'far! Tell me about your Lord, when was He?' He said: 'Woe be upon you! Verily, it is said to a thing that did not exist and then came into being: 'When was it?' Verily, my Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, has always been Ever-Living without a how (quality). There was no 'when' for Him, nor a 'how' for His existence, nor a 'where' for Him. He was not in a thing, nor on a thing. He did not create a place for His existence, nor was He strengthened after creating something, nor weak before creating something. He was not lonely before He originated something, nor does He resemble any created thing. He was not devoid of power over sovereignty before its creation, nor will He be devoid of it after its passing. He has always been Ever-Living without accidental life, and Sovereign, Powerful, before creating anything, and Sovereign, Compelling, after creating existence.' So for His existence there is no 'how', no 'where' for Him, no limit, and He is not known by anything that resembles Him. He does not age due to long-lasting, nor is stunned by anything, nor does anything hollow Him out. All things become stunned from His fear. He is Ever-Living without a bare life or described existence, without a limited 'how', without a following effect, without a place that adjoined something. Rather, He is the Ever-Living Who is known, and the Sovereign who always has power and sovereignty. He created what He willed by His will. He is not limited, nor partial, nor perishing. He was the First without a 'how', and will be the Last without a 'where'. Everything is perishable except His Face. To Him belongs creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds. Woe be upon you, O questioner! Verily, my Lord is not covered by imaginations, nor do doubts descend upon Him. He is not joined by anything, nor does anything join Him. Incidents do not descend upon Him. He is not questioned about what He does. He does not fall upon anything. Slumber does not seize Him, nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is

3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Musili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A Jewish rabbi came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked him: 'O Commander of the Faithful! When did your Lord exist?' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'May your mother grieve you! When did He not exist so that it may be asked when did He exist? My Lord preceded the beginning, without a beginning, and will remain after the end, without an end. There is no end and no termination to His destination. The ends are cut off from Him, and He is the Utmost of all ends.' Then he asked, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Are you a Prophet?' So he (peace be upon him) answered, 'Woe be upon you! Verily, I am but a servant from the servants of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' The Compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: What he meant was that he was a servant in obedience, and nothing more than that.

And it is narrated that he (peace be upon him) was asked: Where was our Lord before He created the heaven and the earth? Therefore, he (peace be upon him) replied, “Where” [ayna] is a question about space, and Allah existed when there was no space.

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Salt (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt narrated to us, from his uncle Abu Talib Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both): "For what reason did Allah ascend His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to the Heaven, and from there to the Farthest Lote-Tree, and from there to the Veils of Light, and He addressed him and conversed with him there, while Allah is not described by being in a place?" He (peace be upon him) replied: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is not described by space, nor does time run over Him. However, He, the Mighty and Glorious, intended to honor His angels and the inhabitants of His heavens by giving them a vantage point to see the Prophet, and to honor them by his witnessing. He showed him from the wonders of His Greatness what he could inform others of after his descent. And this is not as the anthropomorphists say. Glory be to Allah and Exalted be He from what they associate.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqa (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi said: 'Ubays Allah ibn Musa Abu Trab al-Royani said, on the authority of Abd al-'Azim ibn Abd Allah al-Hasani, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abu Mahmud, who said: I asked al-Rida (AS): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the tradition that people narrate from the Messenger of Allah (SAW) that he said: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven?' He (AS) replied: 'May Allah curse those who alter words from their places! By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (SAW) did not say it that way. Rather, he (SAW) said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, sends down an angel to the lowest heaven every night during the last third, and on Friday night at the beginning of the night. He commands him, so he calls out: Is there any supplicant so I may grant his wish? Is there any repentant so I may forgive him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness so I may forgive him? O seeker of good, come forward! O seeker of evil, hold back! He continues calling with this until dawn breaks. When dawn breaks, he returns to his place in the realm of heaven.' My father related this to me from my grandfather, from the Messenger of Allah (SAW).

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam (mercy of God be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni said: 'Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), who said: I asked my father, the Master of the Worshippers (peace be upon him) I said to him: O father! Inform me about when our grandfather the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended to the heaven and his Lord commanded him with fifty prayers, why did he not ask for relief for his Ummah until Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him) said to him: Return to your Lord and ask for relief, for your Ummah cannot bear that? He (peace be upon him) answered: O son! Verily, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not suggest anything to his Lord, nor reconsider anything He commanded him to. When Musa (peace be upon him) asked him that and became an intercessor for his Ummah to him, it was not permissible for him to reject the intercession of his brother Musa (peace be upon him). So he returned to his Lord and asked for relief until it was reduced to five prayers. He said: I then asked: O father! Then why did he not return to his Lord and ask for relief after the five prayers? He replied: O son! He intended that his Ummah obtain relief along with the reward of fifty prayers, based on the word of Allah: 'Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have ten like it.' Do you not see that when he descended to the earth, Jibril (peace be upon him) revealed to him saying: O Muhammad, your Lord sends you greetings and says: They are five for fifty. 'My word shall not be changed, nor am I unjust to the servants.' He said: I asked him: O father! Is it not that Allah, the Exalted, is not described by place? He said: Yes, exalted is Allah from that. I said: Then what is the meaning of Musa's (peace be upon him) word to the Messenger of Allah: 'Return to your Lord'? He said: Its meaning is the meaning of Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) word: 'Surely I fly to my Lord; He will guide me.' And the meaning of Musa's (peace be upon him) word: 'And I hastened on to Thee, my Lord, that Thou might be pleased.' And the meaning of the Mighty and High's word: 'Therefore fly to Allah,' which means 'Pilgrimage to the House of Allah.' O son! Verily, the Ka'bah

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from Muhammad ibn Auramah, from Ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Hamzah, from Aban, from Asad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever claims that Allah is in a thing, from a thing, or on a thing, has become an infidel. If Allah, the Mighty and High, were on something then He would have been carried. If He were in something then He would have been surrounded, and if He were from something then He would have been caused.

My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu 'Abdillah (AS) He said: "He who claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is in a thing or from a thing or on a thing, has told a lie." The Compiler of this book (RA) said: The proof that Allah, the Mighty and High, is not in a place is that all places are created (hadith). The proof has been established that Allah, the Mighty and High, is Eternal (Qadim), preceding places. It is not permissible that the Self-Sufficient Eternal One needs what He was Self-Sufficient from, nor that He changes from what He has always been upon. Thus, it is correct today that He is not in a place, just as He has always been so. The confirmation of this is:

31 - What Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattān told us, he said: Ahmad ibn Yahyā ibn Zakariyyā al-Qattān told us, from Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn Ḥabīb, he said: Tamīm ibn Bahlūl told us, from his father, from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī, from Sulaymān ibn Mihrān, he said: I said to Ja‘far ibn Muḥammad (peace be upon them): “Is it permissible for us to say: Indeed, Allāh, the Mighty and Exalted, is in a place?” He said: “Glory be to Allāh and Exalted is He from that! Indeed, if He were in a place, He would be created (muḥdath), because that which exists in a place is in need of the place, and need (iḥtiyāj) is from the attributes of the created (muḥdath), not from the attributes of the Eternal (al-Qadīm).”

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said, on the authority of Ali ibn al-'Abbas, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, on the authority of Abu Ibrahim Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) that he said: Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, was ever without time and without place, and He is now as He was. No place is free from Him, nor is any place occupied by Him, nor does He dwell in any place. Wherever there is a secret counsel of three, He is the fourth; and of five, He is the sixth; and of fewer or more, He is with them wherever they are. There is no veil between Him and His creation other than His creation. He veiled Himself without a veil, being veiled; and He concealed Himself without a covering, being concealed. There is no god but He, the Great, the Exalted.

Abu Talib al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn al-Muzaffar al-'Alawi al-Samarqandi (RA) said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated from his father Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-'Ayyashi, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ishkib said: Harun ibn 'Uqbah al-Khuza'i reported to me, on the authority of Asad ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i, who said: 'Amr ibn Shimr reported to me, on the authority of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (AS) said: O Jabir! How great is the slander of the people of Syria against Allah, the Mighty and Exalted. They claim that when Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, ascended to the heaven, He placed His foot on the stone of Jerusalem. And indeed, a servant from among the servants of Allah placed his foot on his stone; hence, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, commanded us to take it as a place of prayer. O Jabir! Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has no rival and no likeness. He is exalted from the attribute of the attributers, and glorified above the imaginations of the imaginers. He is veiled from the eyes of the beholders; He does not decline with the decliners, nor does He set with the transitory. There is nothing whatsoever like unto Him; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who said: Sufyan al-Thawri saw Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) when he was a young boy praying, and people were passing in front of him. So he said to him, 'Verily, the people are passing by you while they are circumambulating (the Ka'bah).' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'The One to whom I pray is closer to me than these.'

15. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on them) both said: Ahmad ibn Yahya said: Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Hubayb said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah told me: Ali ibn al-Hakam said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had two Jewish friends who believed in Musa, the Messenger of Allah. They came to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and listened to him. They had read the Torah and the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa (peace be upon them), and had knowledge of the earlier books. When Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, took His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) [to death], they came asking about the one vested with authority after him, and said: 'Verily, a prophet does not die but he leaves behind a Caliph who executes affairs in his Ummah after him, who is close in kinship to him from his Household, of great significance and high prestige.' Then one of them asked his companion, 'Do you know the one vested with authority after this Prophet?' The other replied, 'I do not know him except by the description I find in the Torah: he is bald and pale, for he was the closest of the people to the Messenger of Allah.' When they entered Medina and asked about the Caliph, they were guided to Abu Bakr. When they looked at him, they said: 'This is not our companion.' Then they asked him, 'What is your relationship with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'I am a man from his clan, and he was the husband of my daughter A'ishah.' They said, 'Is there any other [relationship]?' He said, 'No.' They said, 'This is not [the] kinship.' They said, 'Then inform us, where is your Lord?' He said, 'Above the seven heavens.' They said, 'Is there anything else?' He said, 'No.' They said, 'Guide us to one who is more learned than you, for you are not the man whose description we find in the Torah as the successor of this Prophet and his Caliph.' He became angry at their words and rose from them, then guided them to Umar, because he knew that if they confronted him with something, he would seize them. When they came to him, they said, 'What is your relationship with this Prophet?' He said, 'I am from his clan, and he was the husb

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi Abu Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Nasawi narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Sughadi in Marw narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hakam al-`Askari and his brother Mu'adh ibn Ya'qub both narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hanzali narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Asim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays narrated, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Rummani, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Salman al-Farisi (may Allah have mercy on him), in a long hadith which mentions the arrival of the Catholicos to Medina with one hundred Christians after the death of the Prophet (SAWW), and his asking Abu Bakr about issues to which he did not answer, then he was guided to the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) and asked him about them, so he answered him. Among what he asked him was that he said to him: "Inform me about the face of the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted." Hence, Ali (AS) called for some fire and dry wood and then set fire to it. When it blazed, Ali (AS) asked, "Where is the face of this fire?" The Christian replied, "It has a face from all its sides." Ali (AS) responded, "This fire is supervised and produced, yet its face is not known, while its Creator does not resemble it. And Allah’s is the East and the West, therefore, whither you turn, thither is the Face of Allah. No secret is hidden from our Lord." The hadith is long; we have extracted from it the required passage.

Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ushnani al-Razi the Judge in Balkh narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mihrwayh al-Qazwini narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Farra' (thus), from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Verily, when Musa ibn 'Imran whispered to his Lord saying, 'O my Lord, are You far from me so I may shout to You or are You close to me so I may whisper to You?' Therefore, Allah, Lofty be His Majesty, revealed to him, 'I am in the Gathering of whoever remembers Me.' So Musa asked, 'O my Lord, in what state shall I remember You?' Thus, He replied, 'O Musa, remember Me in every state.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (mercy of God be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Abbas, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, on the authority of Abu Ibrahim Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: A group of people were mentioned before him who claimed that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, comes down to the Heaven of this world. He replied: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, does not come down, and does not need to come down. Verily, His view is the same in nearness and distance; what is close is not far from Him, and what is far is not close to Him. He is never in need, but everything is in need of Him. He is the Almighty. There is no god but He, the Honorable, the All-Wise. As for the statement of the attributers: 'Verily, He, the Blessed and Exalted, comes down,' the only ones who say such a thing are those who describe Him in terms of decrease and increase. Every moving thing requires something that moves it or by which it is moved. Thus, they assumed with Allah assumptions; hence, they were destroyed. So beware of limiting Him or seeing boundaries for Him such as decrease and increase, motion and decline, or rising and sitting. For, verily, Allah is loftier than the attribute of the attributers, the description of the describers, and the imagination of the imaginers! Rely on the Honorable, the Most Merciful, who sees you when you stand, when you bend, and when you prostrate.

And with this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he said: I do not say: Verily, He is definite so I remove Him from His place, nor do I bound Him to a place that He may be confined to it. Nor do I limit Him with words that are thrust from the mouth. The Blessed and Exalted says: “Be and it is,” by His Will, and without any hesitation in desire, the Peerless, the Needless. He is not in need of an associate in His Sovereignty, nor an associate to open the doors of His Knowledge for Him.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Asadi al-Kufi narrated, on the authority of Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, on the authority of his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Ali ibn Salm, on the authority of Abu Basir, on the authority of Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (AS) who said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be described in terms of time, space, motion, translocation or stillness. Rather, He is the Creator of time, space, motion and stillness. Exalted is Allah from what they say, the Elevated, the Great.

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Aza'mi said: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumayh al-Nisawi said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ishaq reported to us that Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani related to me that Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalaf al-Attar said: Bishr ibn al-Hasan al-Muradi said, on the authority of Abd al-Quddus who is the son of Hubayb, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, on the authority of al-Harith al-A'war that Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) entered the market. He found a man with his back turned towards him saying: 'No, I swear by the One Hidden over the seven.' Consequently, Ali (peace be upon him) tapped him on his back, and asked: 'Who is hidden over the seven?' He replied: 'Allah, O Commander of the Faithful!' He (peace be upon him) responded: 'You are wrong. May your mother grieve you! Verily, there is no veil between Allah, the Mighty and High, and His Creation, because He is with them wherever they may be.' He asked: 'What is the penalty of what I have said: O Commander of the Faithful?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'That you should know that Allah is with you wherever you are.' He asked: 'Should I feed the poor?' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) replied: 'No, for verily, you have sworn by other than your Lord.'

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi said: Abu Sa'id al-Rumayhi related to me that Abd al-Aziz ibn Ishaq reported to us that Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Harun al-Wasiti said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Makki reported to me that Munif, the freedman of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, said: My master Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to me, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was praying, when a man passed in front of him, and one of his companions stopped him. When he finished his prayer, he asked him: 'Why did you stop the man?' He answered: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! He passed between you and the prayer niche.' He replied: 'Woe unto you! Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is closer to me than anyone passing between me and Him.' Chapter: The Names of Allah (Exalted) and the Difference between their meanings and the meanings of the names of created beings.

11. My father (RA) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali the Second (AS) “What is the meaning of al-Wahid (The One)?” He replied, “He is the One whose Divine Unity (al-Wahdaniyyah) is professed by all tongues.”

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni and 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated from 'Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), 'What is the meaning of the One?' He answered, 'He is the One upon whom all tongues agree in affirming Divine Unity,' as Allah, the Mighty and High, says: 'And if you ask them, Who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, Allah.'

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I asked al-Rida 'Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them): "O son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me about the Qur'an. Is it uncreated or created?" He (AS) replied: "It is neither uncreated nor created; rather it is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him): He said: 'It is the Word of Allah; do not exceed it, and do not seek guidance in other than it, otherwise you will go astray.'

3. Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Muaddab (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Ali ibn Salim said, on the authority of his father that I enquired from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (AS): “O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say about the Qur’an?” Hence, he responded, “It is the Word of Allah, His Speech, His Book, the Revelation He revealed. It is the Honorable Book, which falsehood shall not come to it from before it not from behind it; a revelation from the Wise, the Praised One.”

My father (may Allah has mercy on him said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) wrote to some of his Shi'ites in Baghdad: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. May Allah guard us and you from the trial; if He does, then it is a great bounty. And if He does not, then it is a disaster. We consider that argument regarding the Qur'an is an innovation in which both the questioner and the answerer share. The questioner engages in what is not his due, and the answerer is constrained to answer what is not correct. There is no creator except Allah, the Mighty and High. Anything other than Him is created. The Qur'an is the Word of Allah. Do not make a name for it from your own self or you will be among the astray. May Allah count us and you among those who fear their Lord in the unseen and are apprehensive of the Hour.

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (RA) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari narrated to me, saying: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say about the Qur'an, for there has been a dispute among us regarding it? Some people said: 'It is created,' and some people said: 'It is not created.' He (AS) replied: 'As for me, I do not say what they say, but I say: It is the Word of Allah.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim and others narrated to us, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Hashimi, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: Zaynab, the squint-eyed perfume seller, came to the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his daughters, and she used to sell perfume to them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered while she was with them, and said to her: 'When you visit us, our houses become fragrant.' She said: 'Your houses are more fragrant due to your scent, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'When you sell, be good and do not deceive, for that is more pious and preserves wealth better.' She said: 'I did not come with anything from my selling, but I came to ask you about the Greatness of Allah.' He said: 'Glory be to His Majesty, I will tell you about some of that.' He said: Then he said: 'Verily, this earth, with what is in it and on it, in relation to what is beneath it, is like a ring in a vast desert. And these two (earth and what is below it), with what is in them and on them, in relation to what is beneath them, are like a ring in a vast desert. And the third, until he reached the seventh.' "He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them." And the seven heavens, and what is in them and on them, on the back of the rooster are like a ring in a vast desert. The rooster has two wings, one in the East and one in the West, and its feet are at the boundaries. And the seven, the rooster, and what is in them and on them, on the rock are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, and what is in them and on them, on the back of the fish are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, and the fish, in relation to the dark sea are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, the fish, and the dark sea, in relation to the air are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, the fish, the dark sea, and the air, in relation to the earth (dust) are like a ring in a vast desert. "To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them two and what is beneath the earth." Then the report continued. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, the fish, the dark sea, the air, and the eart

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about His Word, the Mighty and High: 'Did We grow weary of the first creation? But they are in confusion about a new creation.' He (AS) said: O Jabir! The interpretation of that is that when Allah, the Mighty and High, destroys this creation and this world, and the people of Paradise settle in Paradise and the people of Hell in Hell, Allah will create a world other than this world and create a creation without males or females who will worship Him and affirm His Unity. He will create for them an earth other than this earth that carries them, and a sky other than this sky that shades them. Perhaps you think that Allah only created this single world, and that Allah has not created humans other than you. Yes, by Allah, Allah has created a thousand thousand worlds, and a thousand thousand Adams; you are among the last of those worlds and those humans.

With this chain of transmission, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said: Verily, for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is an angel among the angels whose upper half is fire and whose lower half is ice; neither does the fire melt the ice, nor does the ice extinguish the fire. He stands calling with a high-pitched voice: 'Glory be to Allah, who withheld the heat of this fire so that it does not melt this ice, and withheld the cold of this ice so that it does not extinguish the heat of this fire. O Allah, O Combiner of the ice and fire, unite the hearts of Your believing servants in Your obedience.'

With this chain of transmission, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said: Verily, for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, are angels; nothing from the layers of their bodies is not glorifying Allah, the Mighty and High, and praising Him from one side with different voices. They do not lift their heads to the sky, nor lower them to their feet, from weeping and awe of Allah, the Mighty and High.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Nu'aym al-Balghi narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dharr, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may the mercy of Allah be upon him), who said: I was holding the hand of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while we were walking together, and we continued looking at the sun until it set. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, where does it set?' He said: 'In the sky, then it is raised from one sky to another until it is raised to the highest seventh sky, until it is beneath the Throne. It prostrates, and the angels entrusted with it prostrate with it.' Then it says: 'O my Lord, from where do You command me to rise? From my setting place or from my rising place?' And the sun runs [on its course] toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. He means thereby the making of the Mighty Lord in His dominion, the Knowing of His creation. He said: Then Gabriel comes to it with a garment of light from the light of the Throne, according to the measures of the hours of the day, lengthening them in summer or shortening them in winter, or something in between in autumn and spring. He said: It wears that garment as one of you wears his clothes, then it goes with it in the atmosphere of the sky until it rises from its rising place. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is as if I see it being held back for the duration of three nights, then it is not clothed with light and is commanded to rise from its west.' When the sun is wrapped up [in darkness] * And when the stars fall, dispersing, And the moon is similar in its rising place and its course in the horizon of the sky and its setting and its rising to the seventh sky, and it prostrates beneath the Throne. Then Gabriel comes to it with the garment from the light of the Throne. He made the sun a shining light and the moon a visible light Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Then I withdrew with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and we prayed the Maghrib prayer.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (mercy of God be upon him) said: My father said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Auramah, from al-Ziyad al-Qandi, from al-Daras, from the man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, there is an angel; from the lobe of his ear to his neck is a distance that a fluttering bird would take five hundred years to traverse.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sayyari, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Jamil ibn Durraj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (AS), 'Are there oceans in the sky/heaven?' He replied, 'Yes.' My father informed me, from his father, from his grandfather (AS), who said: The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said: 'Verily, in the seven heavens there are oceans, the depth of one of them is a journey of five hundred years. In them are angels standing in service since Allah created them, and the water reaches their knees. There is not an angel among them but that he has one thousand and four hundred wings. On each wing are four faces. On each face are four tongues. There is no wing, face, tongue, or mouth in them but that it glorifies Allah, the Mighty and High, with a glorification that does not resemble the type of the other.'

10. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Auramah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Abu al-Hasan al-Sha'iri, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! By Allah, verily there is a verse in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, that has destroyed my heart and made me doubt my religion.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'May your mother be bereaved of you and deprived of you! What is that verse?' The Word of Allah, the Exalted: 'And the birds with expanded wings, each knows its own prayer and its own glorification.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O son of al-Kawwa'! Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has created angels in various shapes. But for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, there is an angel in the form of a rooster, hoarse and gray. Its talons are in the seventh lower earth, and its dual comb is below the Throne. It has two wings; one in the East and one in the West. One is of fire and the other is of ice. When the time of prayer arrives, it stands on its talons, then raises its neck from below the Throne, and then flaps its two wings just as the roosters in your houses flap theirs. Neither the one from fire melts the ice, nor does the one from ice extinguish the fire. Then it calls out: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, He Alone, with no partner; and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Master of the Prophets and that his successor is the Master of the Successors, and that Allah is Pure, Holy, Lord of the Angels and the Spirit.' He said: Then the roosters in your homes flap their wings and answer him with his call, and that is the Word of the Exalted: 'And the birds with expanded wings, each knows its own prayer and its own glorification,' referring to the roosters on earth.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from 'Amr ibn Marwan, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, are angels half of whom are of cold and half of whom are of fire. They say: 'O Combiner of Hot and Cold, keep our hearts firm in Your Obedience.' And I will bring out the traditions which I have narrated regarding the remembrance of the Greatness of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, in the book 'Al-'Azamat', if Allah wills. Chapter: The Kindness of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn Mukhtar al-Hamdani, from al-Fath ibn Yazid al-Jurjani, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the least that is required for recognition, so he said: 'The affirmation that there is no god other than Him, and that He has no peer or rival, and that He is Eternal, Established, Existing, not confined, and that there is nothing whatsoever like unto Him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humid, who raised it (to the Imam), saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was asked about Divine Unity, so he said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, knew that there would be people in the Last Days who would think deeply therefore, Allah, the Mighty and High, revealed: 'Say: He Allah is One. Allah is the Needless.' and the verses from the surah 'the Iron' - until He says: 'And He is Cognizant of what is in the hearts.' Thus whosoever goes beyond that is ruined.

3. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Barmaki said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan related to me that Bakr ibn Ziyad related to me, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about Divine Unity, so he replied, 'All those who read: Say: He Allah is One, and believe in it, have professed their faith in Divine Unity.' I asked, 'How should one read it?' He (AS) responded, 'The same way that the people read it, adding `such is my Lord' three times.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tahi, from Tahir ibn Hatim ibn Mahawayh, who said: I wrote to al-Tayyib - meaning Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'What is that without which the recognition of the Creator is not valid?' So he wrote back: 'There is nothing whatsoever like unto Him, and He has always been All-Hearing, All-Knowing, and All-Seeing, and He is the Doer of what He wills.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (RA) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, who said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ya'la al-Kufi, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (SAWW) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me the wonders of knowledge.' He said: 'What have you done with the root of knowledge, that you ask about its wonders?' The man said: 'What is the root of knowledge, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Knowing Allah with true knowledge.' The Bedouin said: 'And what is knowing Allah with true knowledge?' He said: 'You know Him without a like, without a resemblance, and without an equal, that He is One, Unique, Manifest, Hidden, the First, the Last, without peer and without rival. That is true knowledge of Him.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il said, on the authority of al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of al-Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) "Verily, I debated with a group of people and said to them, 'Verily, Allah is far above being recognized through His Creation. In fact, the servants are those who are recognized through Allah.' He replied, 'May Allah have mercy on you!'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Uqbah ibn Qays ibn Sam'an ibn Abu Rabiha, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), who raised it (to the Prophet or Imam), saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked, 'With what do you recognize your Lord?' He said, 'With what He introduced Himself.' It was said, 'How did He introduce Himself to you?' He said, 'No image resembles Him, nor is He perceived by the senses, nor comparable to people. He is Near in His Farness, and Far in His Nearness. He is Above all things, yet it cannot be said that 'something is above Him.' He is in front of all things, yet it cannot be said that 'He has a front.' He is Inside the things, but not like something inside something else. He is Outside the things, but not like something outside something else. Glory be to Him who is thus, and there is none like Him thus. He is the Originator of all things.'

3. My father (RA) related to me that Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Humran, on the authority of al-Fadl ibn al-Sakan, on the authority of Abu Abd Allah (AS) that The Commander of the Faithful (AS) said: Recognize Allah through Allah, the Messenger through the message, and the ones vested with authority through their beneficence, justice, and good deeds.

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Sa'id al-Nisawi said: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Sughdi said in Marw that Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hakam al-Askari and his brother Mu'adh ibn Ya'qub both said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hanzali said: Abd Allah ibn Asim said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays said, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Rummani, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Salman the Persian, in a long tradition which mentions the arrival of the Catholicos to the city with one hundred Christians and what he asked Abu Bakr, but he did not answer him, then he was guided to the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) and asked him some questions, and he answered him. Among what he asked him was that he said to him: Tell me, did you recognize Allah through Muhammad or did you recognize Muhammad through Allah, the Mighty and High? Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) replied: I did not recognize Allah through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), but I recognized Muhammad through Allah, the Mighty and High, when He created him and established in him the boundaries of length and breadth. Hence I recognized that He was the Planner of the Produced through reasoning and inspiration from Him and will, just as He inspired the Angels to obey Him and made them know His self without similitude and without how. The tradition is long; we have taken from it the place of need, and I have transmitted it in its entirety at the end of the parts of the Book of Prophethood.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ya'qub saying: The meaning of His saying ('Recognize Allah through Allah') is that Allah, the Mighty and High, created persons, colors, and substances. Therefore, the essences are bodies and the substances are spirits. He, the Mighty and High, resembles neither body nor spirit. Nobody has any effect or cause in the creation of a sensitive, perceiving spirit. He is Matchless in the creation of spirits and bodies. Therefore, whoever negates from Him the two likenesses – the likeness of bodies and the likeness of spirits – recognizes Allah through Allah. And whoever views Him as a body, a spirit, or a light, has not recognized Allah through Allah.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (mercy of God be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhar, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all) He said: A man stood before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked, 'O Commander of the Faithful! With what did you recognize your Lord?' He replied, 'Through the abolishment of resolve and the invalidation of ambition. When I had an ambition, something obstructed it between me and it. And when I made a decision, the Divine Decree opposed my resolve. I knew that the Planner was other than me.' The man asked, 'Then with what did you thank His blessings?' He answered, 'I looked at a tribulation which He diverted from me and afflicted someone else with it. I learned that He had bestowed favor upon me, so I thanked Him.' The man asked, 'Why do you desire to meet Him?' He replied, 'Because I saw that He chose for me the religion of His angels, Messengers, and Prophets. I knew that He who honored me with this would not forget me, so I desired to meet Him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Marwazi al-Muqri said: Abu 'Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Muqri said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Musili said in Baghdad that Muhammad ibn 'Asim al-Tarifi said: 'Ayyash ibn Yazid ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Kahhal, the freed slave of Zayd ibn 'Ali, said: My father related to me that Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them) related to me that a group of people said to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): 'We supplicate but our supplication is not answered,' He (peace be upon him) responded: 'Because you supplicate to One whom you do not truly recognize.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) said: My) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked He was asked: 'By what did you recognize your Lord?' He replied: 'By the abolishment of resolve and the invalidation of ambition. I resolved, so My resolve was abolished; I had an ambition, so My ambition was invalidated.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (RA) narrated: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi narrated: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khazzaz al-Kufi narrated: Sulayman ibn Ja'far narrated: Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated: Hisham ibn Salim said: I was in the presence of Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal, when a man stood up before him and asked him, 'How did you recognize your Lord?' He replied, 'By His Direction, His Instruction, His Introduction, and His Guidance.' I left his presence and met Hisham ibn al-Hakam, so I asked him, 'What should I say to someone who asks me: how did you recognize your Lord?' He said: If someone asked me: 'With what did you recognize your Lord?' I would say: I recognized Allah, High be His Glory, through my own self, because it is the thing closest to me. I find it composed of assembled parts and formed of components, with clear structure and evident craftsmanship, manifesting various patterns of design and form, increasing after decrease, and decreasing after increase. He has created for it diverse senses and distinct limbs - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch - innate in weakness, deficiency, and humility. None of them perceives the function of the other, nor do they have strength over one another. They are incapable of attracting benefits to themselves or repelling harm from themselves. It became impossible in the intellect that there be a compilation without a compiler, and a fixed form without a form-maker. Thus, I knew that it has a Creator who created it, and a Form-maker who formed it, Who is contrary to it in all aspects. Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: 'And in your own souls (too); will you not then see?'

My father (RA) narrated, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) about the expression 'Subhan Allah'. He (AS) replied, 'It is pride belonging to Allah, the Mighty and High.'

3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi, from 'Abd al-'Azim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hasani, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from Sulayman, the freed slave of Tirbal, from Hisham al-Jawaliqi, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Glory be to Allah,' what is meant by it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'His transcendence (deanthropomorphism).' The chapter on the meaning of 'Allah is the Greatest.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Ibn Mahbub, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: A man said in his presence: 'Allah is the Greatest,' so he (AS) asked him: 'Allah is greater than what?' The man answered: 'Greater than everything,' so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You have defined/delimited it (by comparing it to something else),' the man asked: 'How should I say it?' He (AS) said: 'Say: Allah is greater than that which can be described.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from Jumay' ibn Amr, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is (Allah is the Greatest)?' I replied: 'Allah is greater than everything.' He said: 'And there was a thing, so would it be greater than Him?' I said: 'Then what is its meaning?' He replied: 'Allah is greater than what can be attributed to Him with any meaning (of the First and the Last).'

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutakalli (may Allah have mercy on him) reported: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Adhniyah, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from al-Maimun al-Ban, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) being asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'He is the First and the Last.' He said (peace be upon him): 'The First, not [meaning] a first that was before Him, nor a beginning that preceded Him; and the Last, not [meaning] an end as is understood in the attributes of created beings. Rather, He is Eternal, First, Last, who has always existed and will continue to exist, without beginning or end. Change does not befall Him, nor does He transition from one state to another, and He is the Creator of all things.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him mercy) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Fudayl ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'He is the First and the Last,' and I said: 'As for the First, we have understood it, but as for the Last, explain its interpretation to us.' He said: 'There is nothing except that it perishes or changes, or enters into alteration and decay, or transitions from one color to another, from one form to another, from one attribute to another, from increase to decrease, and from decrease to increase, except the Lord of the Universe. Indeed, He has always been and will always be One. He is the First before everything, and He is the Last as He has always been. The attributes and names do not differ for Him as they differ for others, like the human being who is at one time dust, at another time flesh, at another time blood, and at another time bones and decay. And like the date, which is at one time unripe (busr), at another time ripe (rutab), and at another time dried (tamr), so that names and attributes change for it. And Allah, the Mighty and High, is different from that. [This is the] Chapter on the meaning of the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The Rahman established Himself over the Throne.'

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Sahl ibn al-Adami, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Marid, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean) He (peace be upon him) replied: He is equal to everything, so there is no thing that is closer to Him than another thing.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean,' so he (peace be upon him) answered, 'He is equal with everything. Nothing is closer to Him than another. What is far is not far from Him, and what is close is not close to Him. He is equal in distance to everything.'

3. Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Sa'id al-Nisawi said: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Sughdi said in Marw that Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hakam al-Askari and his brother Mu'adh ibn Ya'qub both said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hanzali said: Abd Allah ibn Asim said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays said, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Rummani, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Salman al-Farisi, in a long tradition which mentions the arrival of the Catholicos to Medina with a hundred Christians after the death of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and his asking Abu Bakr about some matters which he did not answer, then he was directed to the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and asked him about them, and he answered. Among what he asked was that he said to him: Inform me about the Lord, where is He and where was He? Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: The Lord, Exalted be His Glory, is not described by place. He is as He was, and He was as He is. He was not in a place, nor did He remain from place to place, and place did not encompass Him. Rather, He has always been without limit and without quality. He said: You have spoken the truth. Inform me about the Lord, is He in this world or in the Hereafter? Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: Our Lord existed before the world, and He will exist forever. He is the Planner of the world, and the All-Knowing of the Hereafter. As for being encompassed by the world and the Hereafter, no. But He knows what is in the world and the Hereafter. He said: You have spoken the truth, may Allah have mercy on you. Then he said: Inform me about your Lord, does He carry or is He carried? Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: Verily, our Lord, Exalted be His Glory, carries and is not carried. The Christian said: How is that? And we find in the Gospel (And the Throne of your Lord will be carried above them that day by eight). Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: Verily, the angels carry the Throne. However, the Throne is not as you imagine, like the shape of a bed. Rather, it is something limited, created, and planned, and your Lord, Exalted and Mighty, is its owner. It is not that He is on it like one thing being on another. He commanded the angels to carry it, so they carry

4. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from some of his men (he elevated the chain), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean,' so he replied, 'He is equal in distance to everything, therefore He is not closer to one thing than another.'
