Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: “Whoever claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is from something or in something or on something, then he has certainly disbelieved.” I said: “Explain that to me.” He (AS) responded, “I refer to a person who claims that He is contained by something, that He is restrained by something, or that He is preceded by something.”

And in another tradition it says: Whoever claims that Allah is from something, he implies that He has been created. Whoever claims that He is in something, he implies that He is limited. And whoever claims that He is on something, he implies that He is carried by something.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, who said: Muqatil ibn Sulayman narrated to me that I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean,' so he (AS) replied, 'He is equal in distance to everything, so there is no thing closer to Him than another thing.'

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hammid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "He has lied who claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is from something, or in something, or on something."

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Aziz al-Samarqandi, the Jurist at Balkh, said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Zahid al-Samarqandi, with his own chain, raised it to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), that a man asked him, saying: 'Verily, the foundation of religion is Divine Unity and Divine Justice, and His Knowledge is vast, and a wise man cannot do without it. So mention what makes it easy to grasp and suitable for memorization.' He (peace be upon him) answered: 'As for Divine Unity, it is that you do not attribute to your Lord what is permissible for you [to have], and as for Divine Justice, it is that you do not attribute to your Creator what you do not have power over.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shaybani al-Muktab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdullah al-Kufi said: Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, on the authority of Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, on the authority of Imam Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them), said: Abu Hanifah left the presence of al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) one day, and Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) came across him and said to him: 'O young man, from whom is the insubordination (sin)?' He (AS) answered: 'It does not deviate from three possibilities: Either it is from Allah, the Mighty and High, and is not from Him, so it is not fitting for the Generous to punish His servant for something he does not acquire; Or it is from Allah, the Mighty and High, and from the servant, but this is not the case, so it is not fitting for the Strong Partner to oppress the weak partner; Or it is from the servant and is from him, so if Allah punishes him, it is because of his sin, and if He forgives him, it is due to His Grace and Generosity.'

My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from al-Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (AS) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.' He replied, 'His Knowledge.'

My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from `Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu `Abd Allah (AS) regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.' He (AS) said: 'The heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, are in the Kursi, and the `Arsh is the Knowledge over which no one has power.'

3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid said, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Rabi', on the authority of Fudayl ibn Yasar, that I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.' He (AS) replied, 'O Fudayl! The heavens and the earth and everything in the Kursi.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.' Are the heavens and the earth greater than the Kursi, or is the Kursi greater than the heavens and the earth? He replied, 'Nay, the Kursi is greater than the heavens, the earth, and the Throne, and everything is within the Kursi.'

5. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Fadalah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from al-Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Throne encompasses the heavens and the heavens and the earth.' Are the heavens and the earth greater than the Throne, or is the Throne greater than the heavens and the earth? He answered, 'Indeed, everything is in the Throne.' Chapter: The Fitrah of Allah, the Mighty and High, creating upon Tawhid.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala' ibn Fudayl, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "The nature made by Allah is which He has made men." He said: "It is Divine Unity."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked: 'What is the nature (fitrah) that Allah made people upon?' He replied: 'Divine Unity (Tawhid).'

3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakklin (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The nature of Allah which He created people upon.' What is that nature? He said: It is Islam. Allah created them upon it when He took their covenant regarding Divine Unity, saying: 'Am I not your Lord?' And in it are the believer and the disbeliever.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Ya`qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Fuddal, from Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (AS) In His Word, the Mighty and High: (the nature made by Allah is which He has made men). He (AS) said: He created them with Divine Unity.

5. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Fuddal, from Abu Jamilah, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The nature made by Allah is which He has made men.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He created them with Divine Unity.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad and Abd Allah, sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (The nature made by Allah is which He has made men upon). He (AS) said: He created them all upon Divine Unity.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ali ibn Hisan al-Wasiti, from al-Hasan ibn Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, the freed slave of Abu Ja'far, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (the nature made by Allah is which He has made men for). He replied: Divine Unity, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and Ali is the Commander of the Faithful.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurarah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (AS): May Allah rectify you, "The nature made by Allah is which He has made men upon"? He (AS) said: He created them with a predisposition towards Divine Unity at the time of the Covenant, upon knowing Him that He is their Lord, I asked: And did they address Him? He (AS) said: He lowered his head, then said: Had it not been for that, they would not have known who is their Lord or who is their Sustainer.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ya'qub ibn Yazid all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Being upright for Allah, not associating aught with Him,' and about being upright (al-hanifiyyah). He replied: 'It is the natural predisposition that Allah placed in human beings; there is no change in His Creation.' And he said: 'Allah created them with recognition (of Him).' Zurarah said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their backs, their progeny.' He explained: 'He brought forth from Adam's loins his progeny until the Day of Judgment. They all scattered before Him. He introduced them, and showed them His Creation. Had it not been so, no one would have recognized their Lord.' And he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every child is born with the natural predisposition.' Meaning, on the recognition that Allah, the Mighty and High, is his Creator. Thus, that is His Word: 'And if you ask them, who created the heavens and the earth? They will certainly say: Allah.'

10. Abu Ahmad al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sarraj al-Hamdani said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sarandibi said: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Harun al-Rashid said in Halab that Muhammad ibn Adam ibn Abu Iyas said: Ibn Abu Dhi'b said, on the authority of Nafi', on the authority of Ibn 'Umar, that The Messenger of Allah (SA) said: "Do not hit your children because of their crying. Verily, during the first four months, their cry is bearing witness that there is no god but Allah. During the next four months, when they cry they are sending their blessings upon the Prophet and His Progeny (AS). And during the next four months, they are praying for their parents.   Chapter of Al-Bada'"

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Abu Ishaq Tha'labah, from Zurarah, from one of the two Imams, meaning Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them), who said: Allah, the Mighty and High, has not been served by anything like the Appearance (Al-Bada').

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, the Mighty and High, has not been revered with anything like the Appearance (al-Bada').

3. Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (RA) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abu Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (AS) who said: Allah, the Mighty and High, has not sent a Prophet until He made a covenant with him regarding these three qualities: that he would acknowledge servitude [to Allah], and reject idols, and that Allah can hasten what He wills and delay what He wills.

And with this chain of transmission, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in Allah erases what He wills and confirms what He wills He (AS) said: He (AS) said: And does Allah erase except that which existed? And does He confirm except that which did not exist?!

Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-'Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah never sent a prophet but He commanded him to prohibit alcohol, and that he should affirm for himself the doctrine of Al-Bada'.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Ali ibn Ibrahim said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn 'Isa, on the authority of Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Malik al-Juhani, that he heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: If people knew what reward there is in speaking about the Appearance (Al-Bada'), they would never cease speaking about it.

And with this chain of transmission, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is there anything today that was not in the knowledge of Allah yesterday? He (peace be upon him) replied: No. May Allah disgrace anyone who says this! I said: What about what has happened and what will happen until the Day of Judgment? Is it not in the knowledge of Allah? He (peace be upon him) replied: Yes, even before He created the creation.

And from that is the saying of the Truthful One (peace be upon him): Nothing appeared to Allah as an appearance (change in knowledge/apparent decree) as it appeared to Him regarding my son Isma'il. He says: No matter became apparent to Allah as it became apparent to Him regarding my son Isma'il, when He cut him off [by death] before me, so that it may be known by that that he was not the Imam after me.

And it has been narrated to me via the path of Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi (may Allah be pleased with him) regarding that matter something strange. And it is that he narrated that Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'Nothing appeared to Allah as an appearance (Bada') as what appeared to Him regarding my father Isma'il, when He commanded his father Ibrahim to slaughter him, then He ransomed him with a great sacrifice.' And in the hadith, regarding both meanings, I have my consideration, except that I have included it for the meaning of the word 'Bada'', and Allah is the Director to the correctness.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Adhinah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Walking is muhaththah.

And with this chain of transmission, it was narrated: A man from the followers of the Umayyad dynasty entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). We feared for him, so we said to him: 'You should conceal yourself, or we should tell him that you are not here.' He said: 'On the contrary, grant him permission to enter. Verily, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is at the tongue of every speaker and the hand of every extender. This speaker cannot say except what Allah wills, and this extender cannot extend his hand except for what Allah wills.' So he entered upon him, asked him about some matters, believed in them, and left.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fudal narrated to us, from his father, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Thabit ibn Abu Safiyyah, from Sa'd al-Khaffaf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Allah, the Mighty and High, revealed to David (peace be upon him): 'O David, you will and I will. However, your will is not except what I will. Therefore, if you submit to My Will, I will bestow you with what you will. However, if you do not submit to My Will, I will trouble you in what you wish. In the end, it is always My will that will prevail.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: The Divine Will and the Divine Intent are among the Attributes of Action. So whoever claims that Allah, the Exalted, has always been the Intending Willer, then he is not a monotheist.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with them) both said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr al-Bazanti, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'Some of our companions say determinism (jabr), and some say ability (istita'ah).' He said to me, 'Write down:' Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: 'O son of Adam! By My Will you were, you are the one who wills for yourself whatever you will, and by My Power you fulfilled My obligations, and by My Bounty you were strengthened to disobey Me. I made you hearing, seeing, and strong. Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from your own self. And this is that I am worthier of your good deeds than yourself, and you are worthier of your bad deeds than I am. And this is that I will not be asked about what I do, while they will be asked. I have arranged for you everything you wish.'

My father (peace be upon him) narrated, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Arzami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He said: Ali (peace be upon him) had a slave named Qanbar, who loved Ali (peace be upon him) with a strong love. Whenever Ali (peace be upon him) went out, Qanbar would go out behind him with a sword. So Ali (peace be upon him) saw him one night and said: 'O Qanbar, what is it?' He replied: 'I came to walk behind you, for people are as you see them, O Commander of the Faithful, so I feared for you.' He said: 'Woe to you! Are you guarding me from the inhabitants of the heaven or from the inhabitants of the earth?' He answered: 'No, but from the inhabitants of the earth.' He said: 'Verily, the inhabitants of the earth cannot do anything to me except by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and High, from the heaven. So go back,' and he returned.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (mercy of God be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated from Musa ibn 'Amr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qummat, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah created the Divine Will before all things, then He created all things by means of His Will.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from `Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu `Abd Allah (peace be upon him) saying: He wills, He intends, He dislikes, and He is pleased. He wills that nothing should exist except with His Knowledge, and He intends similar to that. He dislikes it to be said of Him: 'The third of three,' and He is pleased with His servants' disbelief.

Tamim ibn Abd Allah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi (RA) said: My father narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ansari, from Abu al-Salt Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Hirawi, who said: Al-Ma'mun asked Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) one day He said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (And if your Lord had willed, all those who are in the earth would have believed, all of them; will you then force men till they become believers? And it is not for a soul to believe except by Allah's permission) Al-Rida (AS) replied: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) That the Muslims said to the Messenger of Allah (SAWW): O Messenger of Allah, if you compelled the people over whom you had power to embrace Islam, our numbers would increase and we would be strong against our enemy. The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) replied: I would not face Allah, the Mighty and High, with an innovation for which no instruction had been revealed to me, and I am not among those who force (people). So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: O Muhammad, (And if your Lord had willed, all those who are in the earth would have believed, all of them) through compulsion and constraint in this world, as they will believe upon direct observation and seeing the hardship in the Hereafter. And if you compelled them to do so, they would not deserve any reward or praise from Me, but I want them to believe choosing freely, not being compelled, so that they may earn My Proximity and Honor, and eternal life in Paradise. (Will you then force men till they become believers?) And as for His Word, the Mighty and High: (And it is not for a soul to believe except by Allah's permission), this is not on the basis of forbidding belief upon it. But rather on the meaning that it does not believe except by Allah's permission, and His permission is His command for it to believe, when it is not burdened with obligation, and His compelling it to belief occurs when the obligation and burden are removed from it. Al-Ma'mun said: You have relieved me, O Abu al-Hasan. May Allah relieve you!

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: They said, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Durust, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah willed for me to be capable of what He did not will for me to be the doer of. He said: I also heard him saying: He willed, He intended, He disliked, and He was pleased. He willed that nothing should exist in His Sovereignty except with His Knowledge, and He intended similar to that. He disliked that it be said to Him: 'The third of three,' and He was pleased with the disbelief of His servants.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with them) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Hassan, from Isma'il ibn Abu Ziyad al-Sha'iri, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Sa'dan, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Knowledge had precedence, the Pen dried up, and the Divine Decree proceeded with the confirmation of the Book and the verification of the Messengers. And with happiness from Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, for whoever believed and feared Him, and with misery for whoever lied and disbelieved, and with the guardianship of Allah for the believers and His immunity from the polytheists. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I transmit my tradition from Allah, indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: O son of Adam! By My Will you are, and you are the one who wills for yourself what you will. By My Intent you are, and you are the one who intends for yourself what you intend. And by the favor of My grace upon you, you have strength for My disobedience. And by My protection, My help, and My health, you have fulfilled My obligations for Me. So I am worthier of your good deeds than you are, and you are worthier of your evil deeds than I am. The good comes from Me to you as a gift from the beginning, and the evil comes from Me to you as a recompense for what you earned. And by My goodness to you, you have strength for My obedience. And by your bad opinion of Me, you have despaired of My mercy. So the praise and the argument are Mine against you through clear explanation. And the way is Mine over you through disobedience. And for you is the reward of good with Me through goodness. I did not neglect warning you, nor did I seize you at your honor, nor did I burden you beyond your capacity, nor did I impose upon you from the trust except what you confirmed upon yourself. I am pleased with Myself for you as you are pleased with yourself for Me.

Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab in Naysabur narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Mughayrah narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abu al-Husayn al-Qurayzi, from Sahl ibn Abu Muhammad al-Missisi, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), who said: A servant does not act or move unless ability is with him from Allah, the Mighty and High. Indeed, legal capacity (taklif) from Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, occurs after ability, and one is not legally obligated for an action except while capable.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) narrated, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said: Hamzah ibn Humran narrated to me, saying: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) about ability, but he did not answer me. So I entered his presence at another time and said: May Allah make you upright, a matter has entered my heart regarding it which none can remove but something I hear from you. He said: Verily, what is in your heart will not harm you. I said: May Allah make you upright, for I say: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has not burdened the servants except with what they can bear and what they are capable of, for they do not do anything of that except by the Will, Intent, Decree, and Power of Allah. He said: This is the religion of Allah in which I am and my forefathers are, or as he said. The Compiler of this book said: Allah's Intent and Will regarding obedience is the Command for it and the Pleasure in it, and regarding sins is the Prohibition from them and the Restriction from them through restraint and warning.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah and Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari both narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The servants have not been commanded except according to their capacity. Therefore, whatever thing Allah commanded people to do, they are capable of doing it; and whatever they are not capable of doing, it has been placed (lifted) from them. However, there is no good in people (who do not fulfill their obligations).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab said, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, that he asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about ability (al-istita'ah), so he said: 'A servant is capable when he possesses four characteristics: his route is free from trouble, his body is healthy, he has all his limbs, and has a means of sustenance provided to him by Allah, the Mighty and High.' I said: 'May I be your ransom! Explain these reasons for me.' He said: 'In order to be capable, a servant needs to have a route free from trouble. He needs to have a healthy body. And he needs to have all his limbs. He may intend to fornicate, but at first he does not find a woman then he finds one. Then, either he would be protected by Allah and he would stop from it as Yusuf (peace be upon him) did; or Allah would abandon him between him and his intentions. Thus, he would fornicate and would be labeled a fornicator. He has not obeyed Allah from compulsion, and did not disobey because he was coerced.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Isma'il ibn al-Jabir, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the creation and knew what they would return to. He commanded them and forbade them. Whatever He commanded them of anything, He made for them the way to take it; and whatever He forbade them from, He made for them the way to leave it. And they do not take or leave except by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and High, meaning: by His Knowledge.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And verily they were called upon to make obeisance while yet they were safe." He (AS) said: "The capable are capable of fulfilling the obligations that have been imposed on them. And the capable are capable of refraining from the prohibitions that were imposed on them. They will be tried through both obligation and prohibition." Then he added, "There is nothing which has been commanded or prohibited by Allah, the Exalted, the Mighty and High, that is not a trial and predestined."

My father and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah and Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari both narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of al-'Ala' ibn Razin, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, that I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And pilgrimage to the House is incumbent upon men for the sake of Allah, (upon) everyone who is able to undertake the journey to it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should have the means to perform the pilgrimage.' I asked, 'What happens if someone offers to pay for your pilgrimage, and you feel embarrassed about accepting his offer?' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'Such a person would be counted among those who have the ability.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Abu Basir, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever is offered the means to perform the pilgrimage, even if it means riding on the back of a mutilated, mangled-tailed donkey, and he refuses, then he is among those who have the capability to perform the pilgrimage.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Junah, from Awf ibn Abd Allah al-Azdi, from his paternal uncle, who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about capability, so he said: 'Have they done so?' I said: 'Yes. They claim that it does not exist except at the time of the action and an intention during the time of the action, not before it.' He said: 'The people have disbelieved.'

My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from one of those who narrated from our scholars, from Abu Abdillah (AS) who said: I heard him say: A servant is not an actor (doer of an action) unless he is capable, and he may be capable but not an actor, and he will never be an actor until capability is with him.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And pilgrimage to the House is incumbent upon men for the sake of Allah, (upon) every one who is able to undertake the journey to it.' What does He mean by this? He (peace be upon him) replied, 'He means that whoever has a healthy body, a route free from trouble, proper provision, and a mode of transportation.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal al-Asadi, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yun, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) regarding this verse: 'Had it been a near advantage and a short journey, they would certainly have followed you, but the tedious journey was too long for them; and they swear by Allah: If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you; they cause their own souls to perish, and Allah knows that they are most surely liars.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They indeed had the ability, and it was known that had it been a near advantage and a short journey, they would have done so.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Barqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And they will swear by Allah, 'If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you,' they cause their own souls to perish, and Allah knows that they are liars.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, the Mighty and High, refuted their statement: 'If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you,' stating that they indeed had the capability to go forth.'

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abd Allah (AS) who said: Allah does not oblige His servants with an obligation of action, nor does He forbid them from anything, without first granting them the ability (capacity). Then, and only then, He commands them and forbids them. Therefore, a servant cannot be one who takes (acts) or one who leaves (refrains) except by a preceding ability that comes before the command and prohibition, before the taking and leaving, and before the grasping and releasing.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, on the authority of 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Khalid, that he heard Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) saying: Apprehension and delight do not occur from a servant unless he has been granted the ability for apprehension and delight.

My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Miskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (AS), who said: I heard him say And with him were a group of people debating about deeds and actions, so he said: The ability precedes the action. Allah, the Mighty and High, did not command anything of grasping or expanding except that the servant is capable of it.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from 'Amr, one of our scholars, from the one who asked Abu Abd Allah (AS): He said to him: 'I have a family member who belongs to the Qadariya and who says: We are able to do so and so, and we are able not to do so.' He said: Abu Abd Allah (AS) said: 'Tell him: Do you have the ability to remember what you abhor, and to forget what you like?' If he says: 'No,' then he has denounced his statement, and if he says: 'Yes,' then do not speak to him again, for he has claimed to be God.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Abu al-Khayr Saliḥ ibn Abu Hammad said: Abu Khalid al-Sijistani related to me, on the authority of Ali ibn Yaqtin, on the authority of Abu Ibrahim (AS), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (AS) passed by a group in Kufah while they were arguing about the Divine Decree. He asked their speaker: 'Are you able to act because of Allah, with Allah, or without Allah?' The person did not know how to answer. So the Commander of the Faithful (AS) said: 'If you claim that you are able to act because of Allah, then you are not in trouble. However, if you claim that you are able to act with Allah, then you have claimed to be an associate with Him in His sovereignty. And if you claim that you are able to act without Him, then you have testified to a god other than Allah, the Mighty and High.' He replied, 'No, O Commander of the Faithful! I am able to act because of Allah.' So the Imam (AS) said: 'If you had said something else, I would have hit your neck.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Nine things have been raised (excused) from My Ummah: error, forgetfulness, what they were coerced into, what they are unable to do, what they do not know, what they were compelled to do, jealousy, good/bad omen, and pondering the whispers (of Satan) in the heart regarding creation, as long as they do not articulate it with the tongue.

Tamim ibn Abd Allah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi (RA) said in Farghanah that my father narrated from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ansari, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said: Al-Ma'mun asked al-Rida (AS) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: [Those whose eyes were under a cover from My Reminder and they could not even hear.] he (AS) replied, Verily, covering the eyes does not stop them from remembering Allah, and remembering Allah cannot be done with the eyes. However, Allah, the Mighty and High, has compared those who reject the guardianship of Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) with blindness, because they used to find the words of the Prophet (SA) burdensome, and they could not bear to hear them. Al-Ma'mun then said: 'You have relieved me. May Allah relieve you!' Chapter of Trial and Testing.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no constriction nor expansion except that Allah has in it a favor and a trial.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no constriction nor expansion except that for Allah in it is will, destiny, and trial.

3. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no action involving contraction (fear/awe) or expansion (delight/calmness) among that which Allah has commanded or prohibited, except that it contains a trial and decree from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Chapter of Happiness and Misery

Allah's mercy be upon him said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Ali ibn Muhammad (who elevated the chain) narrated from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Basir, who said: I was sitting before Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and a questioner asked him, saying: May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah! How does adversity reach the people of disobedience so that punishment is decreed for them in His Knowledge based on their actions? Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied: O questioner, the Knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and High, is that no one from His creation will truly fulfill His right. When He knew this, He bestowed upon His lovers the strength for recognizing Him and removed from them the weightiness of the action based on the reality of what they deserve. And He bestowed upon the people of disobedience the strength for their disobedience due to His prior Knowledge of them, and He did not prevent them from the capacity to accept Him, because His Knowledge is more entitled to the reality of confirmation. So they conformed to what was predestined for them in His Knowledge, even if they were able to do something that would save them from His disobedience. This is the meaning of 'He wills what He wills,' and it is a secret.

3. Al-Sharif Abu `Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn `Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn `Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) said: `Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah al-Naysaburi narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja`far (AS) about the meaning of the Word of the Messenger of Allah (SAWW): “The adverse is one who had been adverse in the womb of his mother, and the privileged in one who had been privileged in womb of his mother.” So he (AS) replied, The adverse person is he who Allah knows from the womb of his mother that he will perform the deeds of the adverse. And the privileged person is the one who Allah knows from the womb of his mother that he will perform the deeds of the privileged. I asked him, “Then what is the meaning of his (SAWW) Word: ‘All of you act! Everything has been made easy when created.’” He replied, Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the jinn and the human beings to serve Him and not to disobey Him. Hence, the Word of the Mighty and High: And I have not created the jinn and the men except that they should serve Me. Therefore, He made everything easy when He created it. Woe to him who preferred blindness over guidance.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Halabi, from Ma'la Abu 'Uthman, from 'Ali ibn Hanzalah, from Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) that he said: The privileged one is led along the path of the adverse until the people say: 'He is so similar to them that he must be one of them.' Then privilege reaches him. And sometimes the adverse one is led along the path of the privileged until the people say: 'He is so similar to them that he must be one of them.' Then adversity reaches him. Verily, whoever Allah, the Exalted, knows to be privileged, even if the only time that remains in the world is the hiccup of a she-camel, He will bring his life to an end with privilege.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created happiness (sa'adah) and misery (shaqawah) before He created His creation. So whoever Allah knows to be happy, He never hates him, even if he does an evil deed, Allah hates his deed but does not hate him. And if He knows someone to be miserable, He never loves him, even if he does a good deed, Allah loves his deed but hates him for what he will become. Thus, if Allah loves something, He never hates it; and if He hates something, He never loves it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa'd ibn Abd Allah both said: Ayyub ibn Nuh narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted: 'And know that Allah intervenes between man and his heart.' He (AS) said: 'He intervenes between him and the belief that falsehood is truth.' And it has been said: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, intervenes between man and his heart through death.' And Abu Abdillah (AS) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, transfers the servant from misery to happiness, but does not transfer him from happiness to misery.' Chapter: The Negation of Predestination (Al-Jabr) and Delegation (Al-Tafwid)

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the creation and knew what they would return to. He commanded them and forbade them. Whatever He commanded them of anything, He made for them the way to take it; and whatever He forbade them of anything, He made for them the way to leave it. And they do not take or leave except by the permission of Allah.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn Qurt, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever claims that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, commands immorality and indecency has attributed a lie to Allah. And whoever claims that good and evil take place without the will of Allah, has removed Allah from His Rule. Whoever claims that sins can take place without the power of Allah, has attributed a lie to Allah. And whoever attributes lie to Allah, Allah will cast him into Hell. He means by good and evil: health and illness, referring to His saying, the Majestic and Glorious: 'And We try you by evil and good by way of probation.' And We try you by evil and good by way of probation.

3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi, from his father, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from more than one person, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon them both), who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is more merciful to His creation than to compel them to commit sins and then punish them for them. And Allah is Mightier than intending a matter and it not coming to pass. He was asked (the two Imams): Is there a third position between compulsion (al-jabr) and free will (al-qadar)? They replied: Yes, and it is broader than what is between the heaven and the earth.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Hasan ibn Mattil narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is more Honorable than obliging people to do what they do not have the strength to do. And Allah is Mightier than allowing something to exist in His Rule that He does not intend.

Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Warraq (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Buttah said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, on the authority of Hariz ibn Abd Allah, on the authority of Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, people regarding divine decree (al-Qadar) are of three types: One man claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, compelled people to commit sins; this man has wronged Allah in His judgment, so he is an unbeliever. And one man claims that the matter has been delegated to them (absolute delegation); this man has weakened Allah in His sovereignty, so he is an unbeliever. And one man claims that Allah obligated the servants with what they can bear and did not obligate them with what they cannot bear; when he does good, he praises Allah, and when he does evil, he seeks forgiveness from Allah; this is a complete Muslim.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Determinism (al-Jabr) and Relinquishment/Free Will (al-Tafwid) were mentioned in his presence, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I not give you a foundational principle regarding this matter, upon which you will not differ and against which you will not argue with anyone, such that you will defeat them?' We said: 'If you deem it proper.' He said: 'Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is not obeyed through compulsion, nor is He disobeyed through overwhelming force. He does not neglect His servants within His dominion. He is the Owner of what He has made theirs, and the All-Powerful over what He has enabled them to do. If the servants unite in obeying Him, Allah will not prevent them from it nor withhold it from them. If they unite in disobeying Him, and He wishes to place a barrier between them and that act, He will do so. And if He does not place a barrier and they do it, it is not He who compelled them to enter into it.' Then he (peace be upon him) added: 'Whoever masters the boundaries of this statement will defeat whoever opposes him.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Khunays ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: There is no determinism (jabr) and no relinquishment (tafwid), but rather a matter between the two matters. He said: I asked, 'What is the matter between the two matters?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'The example of that is like a man whom you saw committing a sin, so you forbade him, but he did not stop. Then you left him, and he committed that sin. It is not the case that because he did not accept your forbidding and you left him, that you are the one who commanded him to commit the sin.'

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Mu'addab (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ansari narrated to us, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them) saying: Whoever believes in determinism, do not give him from the zakat, and do not accept his testimony, Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, does not burden a soul with more than it can bear, nor carry it beyond its capacity, and every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated, from Ma'la ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him and said to him: 'Has Allah relinquished the matter to the servants?' He (AS) replied: 'Allah is Mightier than that.' I said: 'Then has He compelled them to sins?' He (AS) answered: 'Allah is more Just and better Judge than that,' He then added: 'Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: O son of Adam, I am worthier of your good deeds than yourself, and you are worthier of your bad deeds than Me. You committed sins by means of My Power.'

Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated, on the authority of his father, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated, on the authority of Ali ibn Ma'bad, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both). He (AS) said: I said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! People attribute to us the belief in anthropomorphism and determinism, based on the traditions transmitted from your forefathers, the Imams (peace be upon them), regarding that.' He (AS) said, 'O son of Khalid! Tell me: Are the traditions transmitted from my forefathers, the Imams (peace be upon them), regarding anthropomorphism and determinism more numerous, or the traditions transmitted from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) regarding that?' I said, 'Rather, what is transmitted from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) regarding that is more numerous.' He said, 'Then they should say: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to believe in anthropomorphism and determinism.' I said to him, 'They claim: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not say anything of that, rather it has been falsely attributed to him.' He said, 'Then they should say about my forefathers (peace be upon them): They did not say anything of that, rather it has been falsely attributed to them.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever believes in anthropomorphism and determinism is an unbeliever and an infidel, and we are disowned by him in this world and the Hereafter. O son of Khalid! Indeed, the exaggerators (al-ghulah) who belittle the greatness of Allah have fabricated the traditions in our name regarding anthropomorphism and determinism. Therefore, whoever loves them has hated us, and whoever hates them has loved us. Whoever befriends them has shunned us, and whoever shuns them has befriended us. Whoever strengthens ties with them has severed ties with us, and whoever severs ties with them has strengthened ties with us. Whoever is harsh with them is kind to us, and whoever is kind to them is harsh with us. Whoever honors them has insulted us, and whoever insults them has honored us. Whoever accepts them has rejected us, and whoever rejects them has accepted us. Whoever is good to them

Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed us, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said: I described to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the statement of Hisham al-Jawaliqi and what he says about the fortunate young man, and I described to him the statement of Hisham ibn al-Hakam. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is not resembled by anything.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Ali ibn Muhammad, who elevated it (to the Imam), from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rukhji, said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about what Hisham ibn al-Hakam said regarding the body, and Hisham ibn Salim regarding the image. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: Leave aside the confusion of the bewildered, and seek refuge in Allah from Satan. The statement is not as the two Hishams claimed.

3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the body and the image/appearance, so he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: Glory to the One who has nothing like Him, no body and no image.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I heard Hisham ibn al-Hakam narrating from you that Allah, the Mighty and High, is a body, solid, luminous; His recognition is necessary, which He bestows upon whom He wills from His creation. He (peace be upon him) said: Glory to Him whom no one knows how He is except Himself. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. He is not bounded, nor sensed, nor corporeal, nor tangible, and the senses do not perceive Him. Nothing encompasses Him. He is not a body, nor an image, nor lineation, nor delineation.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd, who said: I came to al-Rida (AS) asking him about Divine Unity. He dictated to me: All praise be to Allah, the Originator of things by creation and the Initiator of them by inception, through His Power and Wisdom. Not from anything, lest creation be invalidated, nor for a cause, lest inception be invalid. He created what He willed, how He willed, being One in that, without manifestation of His Wisdom or reality of His Lordship. Intellects cannot grasp Him, imagination cannot reach Him, eyes cannot perceive Him, and scale cannot encompass Him. Speech is incapable without Him, eyes are expressionless without Him, and descriptions go astray in Him. He is hidden without a veiled veil, and covered without a covered covering. He is known without seeing, described without an image, and characterized without a body. There is no god but Allah, the Great, the Most Exalted.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abd Allah al-Barqi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said: I described to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) the statement of Hisham al-Jawaliqi, and narrated for him the statement of Hisham ibn al-Hakam: 'He is a body.' He said: 'Verily, nothing resembles Allah. What indecency or foulness is greater than the statement of one who affirms that the Creator of things is a body, or an image, or a created form, or defined, or having limbs? Exalted is Allah from that with a great exaltation.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hammani, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both): Hisham ibn al-Hakam claimed that Allah is a body, there is nothing whatsoever like unto Him, the All-knowing, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Omnipotent, the Speaker, and the Communicator. Speech, Omnipotence, and Knowledge flow from the One Same Source, none of these things are created. So he (AS) said: May Allah kill him! Does he not know that a body is limited, and that speech is other than the speaker? Allah forbid, I am free from such words. He is devoid of both body and image. He has no limits, and everything other than Him is created. Verily, everything that exists is the result of His Will and Intent which is expressed without words, the use of the tongue, or any reluctance or hesitation.

Allah has mercy on him, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani, who said: I wrote to the man, meaning Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), informing him that those before us from your followers have differed regarding Divine Unity; some of them say [God has] a body, and some of them say [God has] an image. So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'Glory be to Him who is not limited, and cannot be described; there is nothing whatsoever like unto Him; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing' — or he said: 'the All--Seeing'.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Isa said, on the authority of Hisham ibn Ibrahim, who said: Al-Abbasi said, I said to him (meaning Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon him): "May I be your ransom! One of your followers told me to ask you a question." He (AS) said: "And who is he?" I said: "Al-Hasan ibn Sahl." He (AS) asked: "What is the issue about?" I said: "It is about Divine Unity." He (AS) said: "What aspect of Divine Unity?" I said: "He wants to know whether Allah is a body or not?" He (AS) answered me: "Indeed, regarding Divine Unity, there are three positions: the position of affirmation with anthropomorphism, the position of negation, and the position of affirmation without anthropomorphism. The position of affirmation with anthropomorphism is not permissible, and the position of negation is not permissible. The correct path in the third position is affirmation without anthropomorphism."

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: on the authority of Imran ibn Musa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn Huraysh al-Razi, on the authority of some of our scholars, from al-Tayyib (meaning Ali ibn Muhammad), and from Abu Ja'far al-Jawad (peace be upon them both) that they said: He who claims that Allah has a body, do not give him the poor-rate, and do not pray behind him.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qasani who said: I wrote to him (peace be upon him) informing him that some of the people here differed on the subject of Divine Unity, He (peace be upon him) replied in writing: “Glory be to Him who has no limit, and who cannot be described! Nothing whatsoever is like unto Him. And he is the All-Hearing, and the All-Seeing.”

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Adami, from Bishr ibn Bashshar al-Naysaburi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) informing him that the people before us differed regarding Divine Unity; some of them say He is a body, and others say He is an image. So he (peace be upon him) wrote back: 'Glory be to Him who has no limit, and cannot be described, and with whom nothing resembles! Nothing whatsoever is like unto Him. And He is the All-Hearing and the All-Seeing.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the year 255 AH: O my Master! Our companions are divided regarding Divine Unity (Tawhid); some of them say that He is a body, and some of them say that He is an image. If you deem it appropriate, O my Master, to teach me that which I can rely upon and not pass over, I will do so, extending my letter to your servant. Hence, he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: You asked about Divine Unity, and this is far from your reach. Allah, the Exalted, is One, Alone, the Eternal Refuge, He begets not nor is He begotten, and none is equal to Him. He is the Creator and not created. He, the Blessed and Exalted, creates whatever He wishes from bodies and other than that, and fashions whatever He wishes, but He is not a fashioned image. Exalted is His Praise, and Hallowed are His Names, and He is High above having a resemblance. He is He, not other than Him. Nothing whatsoever is like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf said: Ibn Abu Najran said, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman, on the authority of Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, who said: I wrote by hand via Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with several questions, among them: Inform me about Allah, the Mighty and High, whether He can be described with image and lineation? If you see fit, may Allah make me your ransom, write back to me with the correct view regarding Divine Unity. So he (peace be upon him) wrote back to me, sending the letter via Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan: May Allah have mercy on you! You have enquired about Divine Unity and what your companions have ascribed. Allah is Greater than what is like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. Allah is Greater than the descriptions of the describers, those who compare Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with His creation, thus slandering Allah. And know, may Allah have mercy on you, that the correct view regarding Divine Unity is that which the Qur'an revealed regarding the attributes of Allah, the Mighty and High. Reject from Allah falsehood and anthropomorphism; there is neither negation nor comparison. He is Allah, the Firmly Present, the Existing. Allah is Greater than what the describers describe. Do not exceed the Qur'an, lest you go astray after the clear explanation has reached you.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated, from his father, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from some of our scholars, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the body and image, so he replied in writing: 'Glory be to Him who has nothing whatsoever like unto Him, and who is devoid of both body and image.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, from his father, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the body and the image, so he wrote in reply: 'Glory be to Him who has nothing whatsoever like unto Him.'

Allah (may He have mercy on him) narrated to us, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what they narrate that Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, created Adam in His Image; he said: It is a newly created image, Allah chose it and selected it over all other different images, so He attributed it to Himself just as He attributed the Ka'bah to Himself and the Spirit to Himself. "My House" "And I breathed into him from My Spirit"

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ya'qub al-Sarraj, who said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): "Some of our companions claim that Allah has a form like the form of a human being," and another said: "He is in the form of a beardless man with curly, wavy hair." Abu 'Abd Allah fell down in prostration, then raised his head, and said: Glory be to Allah who has nothing whatsoever like unto Him! Vision cannot perceive Him, and knowledge cannot encompass Him. He begets not, nor is He begotten, and none is equal to Him. Exalted is He, the High, and Mighty from such attributions!

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Durust, from Ibn Azhinah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding al-Qada' and al-Qadar?' He (peace be upon him) replied: I say: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, when He gathers the servants on the Day of Resurrection, will ask them about what He assigned to them, and will not ask them about what was predestined for them.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, who said: A man said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them): 'May Allah make me your ransom, is it by Divine Decree that people receive what befalls them, or by their actions?' He (AS) replied: 'Verily, Divine Decree and actions are like the spirit and the body. The spirit without a body is not sensed, and the body without a spirit is a shape with no movement. When they combine, they become strong and proper. Similarly, action and Divine Decree. If Divine Decree did not act upon action, the Creator would not be distinguished from the created, and Divine Decree would be something not sensed. If action did not occur in accordance with Divine Decree, it would not proceed nor be complete. But they become strong through their combination, and for Him is the help for His pious servants.' Then he (AS) said: 'Beware! Verily, among the oppression of people is that he views his own oppression as justice, and the justice of the rightly-guided as oppression. Verily, the servant has four eyes: two eyes with which he sees the affairs of his Hereafter, and two eyes with which he sees the affairs of his world. When Allah, the Mighty and High, intends good for a servant, He opens for him the two eyes that are in his heart, so he sees the flaw through them. And when He intends other than that, He leaves the heart as it is with what it contains. Then he turned to the one who asked about Divine Decree and said: This is from that, and this is from that.'

5. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qittan said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qittan said: Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Hubayb said: Ali ibn Ziyad said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah said, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, on the authority of his father who was with Ali (peace be upon him) in the Battle of Siffin and onwards, that While Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) was charging the battalions, Mu'awiyah came riding a horse towards him. Ali was on the horse of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called al-Murtajiz. He had the spear of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in his hand, and his own sword called Dhu al-Fiqar was hanging on his side. One of his companions said “Be careful, O Commander of the Faithful! Verily, we fear that this cursed man may kill you.” Consequently, he (peace be upon him) replied, Verily, if you had said that he is the most unfaithful and the most hard-hearted. He is the most wretched of the Kharijites due to his opposition to the rightly-guided Imams. Nonetheless, death is sufficient as a guardian. Everyone is protected by angels. They protect people fro falling into a well or a wall falling on them. They prevent people from other evils that may befall them. When the moment of death arrives, these angels guard people from what they are about to experience. I am the same. My death will come at the hands of the most wretched person of this Ummah, and my blood will color this and this. And he indicated his beard and head, saying it was “a well-know covenant and a true promise.” The tradition is detailed; we have extracted from it the required passage. I have transmitted all of it in the book Al-Dala'il wa al-Mu'jizat.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Just as the beginning of every blessing is from Allah, the Mighty and High, which He has bestowed upon you, so too is the good from yourselves, even if it flows through Divine Decree.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad said, on the authority of Yusuf ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Arzami, on the authority of his father Abd al-Rahman, who elevated the chain to the one who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: Allah decreed the destinies fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth.

Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Warraq and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan known as Ibn Maqbarah al-Qazwini said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: al-Haytham ibn Abu Masruq al-Nahdi narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabatah, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) turned from a tilted wall to another wall, so it was said to him, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Are you fleeing from the destiny of Allah?' He replied, 'I am fleeing from the destiny of Allah to the Divine Decree of Allah, the Mighty and High.'

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn `Amr ibn `Ali al-Basri said: Abu al-Hasan `Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Muthanna said: Abu al-Hasan `Ali ibn Mihraway al-Qazwini said: Abu Ahmad al-Ghazi said: `Ali ibn Musa al-Rida said: My father Musa ibn Ja`far said: My father Ja`far ibn Muhammad said: My father Muhammad ibn `Ali said: My father `Ali ibn al-Husayn said: My father al-Husayn ibn `Ali (peace be upon them) said: I heard my father `Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) say: Actions have three states: obligations, merits, and sins. As for obligations, they are by the command of Allah, the Mighty and High, His Pleasure, His Destiny, His Decree, His Will, and His Knowledge. As for merits, they are not by the command of Allah, but by His Pleasure, His Destiny, His Decree, His Will, and His Knowledge. As for sins, they are not by the command of Allah, but by His Destiny, His Decree, His Will, and His Knowledge. Then, He punishes for them. The Compiler of this book says: With regards to sins, the predestination of Allah, the Mighty and High, resides in His Order regarding them. With regards to sins, His Will resides in His Prohibition of them. With regards to sins, His Divine Decree resides in His Knowledge of their measures and their extents.

And with this chain of transmission, he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The world in its entirety is ignorance, except for the centers of knowledge; and all knowledge is evidence (against the owner), except that which is put into practice; and all action is showing off (riya'), except that which is sincere; and sincerity is precarious until the servant is judged by what is concluded for him (at death).

Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mu'adab (RA) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from 'Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from his father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, from his father 'Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (SA) saying: Allah, Great be His Glory, says: 'Whoever is displeased with My Destiny, and does not believe in My Decree, then he should invoke a deity other than Me.' The Messenger of Allah (SA) said: 'In every affair destined by Allah, there is goodness for the believer.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on one of his journeys, a group of riders met him and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' He turned to them and asked: 'Who are you?' They answered: 'We are believers.' He asked: 'What is the reality of your belief?' They replied: 'Contentment with the decree of Allah, submission to the command of Allah, and relinquishment of affairs to Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) responded: 'You are learned and wise; you are almost as wise as the prophets. If you are truthful, then do not build what you will not inhabit, do not collect what you will not eat, and fear Allah to whom you shall return.'

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fudal narrated to us, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Thabit ibn Abu Safiyyah, from Sa'd al-Khaffaf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: to a man: If you do not obey your Creator, then do not eat of His Sustenance. And if you are a supporter of His Enemy, then leave His Realm. And if you are not content with His Decree and Divine Decree, then seek a Lord other than Him.

And with this chain of transmission, he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said to Musa (peace be upon him): O Musa! Remember My Will concerning four things: First: As long as you do not see that your sins are forgiven, do not occupy yourself with the faults of others. Second: As long as you do not see that My Treasures have been exhausted, do not grieve over your sustenance. Third: As long as you do not see the end of My Sovereignty, do not place your hope in anyone other than Me. And fourth: As long as you do not see Satan dead, do not feel safe from his deception.

And with this chain of transmission from al-Isba' ibn Nubatah, he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'As for what follows, then concern for the world does not increase what is destined, and in it is a waste of effort; and turning to the Hereafter does not decrease from what is possible, and in it is securing the Return.' And he recited: (If it were in a rock in the sea, firm, hard, solid, smooth on its sides) (Sustenance for a soul that Allah sees; it will split from it and bring to him all that is in it) (Or if it were between the seven layers, his junction) (Allah will ease for him the ascents of its stairs) (Until he meets that which is written for him in the Tablet; if it comes to him, otherwise he goes to it). The compiler of this book said: Everything that Allah, the Mighty and High, enabled us to benefit from and did not make for anyone else that we were prevented from, we have been given sustenance and made it our sustenance; and everything that Allah, the Mighty and High, did not enable us to benefit from and made for others that we were prevented from, we have not been given sustenance and it was not made our sustenance.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, who said: A man asked Abu al-Hasan (AS) while he was circumambulating (the Ka'bah), saying to him: Tell me about the Generous. He replied to him: Verily, your word has two meanings: If you are asking about the created, then the generous person is one who gives what Allah, the Mighty and High, has made obligatory on him, and the miser is one who withholds what Allah has made obligatory on him. And if you mean the Creator, then He is the Generous whether He grants or He withholds, because if He grants to a servant, He grants him what is not his, and if He withholds, He withholds what is not his.
