Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon them) said: My grandfather Yahya ibn al-Hasan related to me that Ya'qub ibn Yazid said: Ibn Abu 'Umayr and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughayrah related to me, on the authority of Abu Hafs al-A'sha, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, on the authority of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them), who said: I went out until I reached this wall and leaned on it, and behold, a man wearing two white garments was looking at my face. Then he said to me: 'O 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, why do I see you sad and sorrowful? Is your sadness due to the world?' He said: 'Allah's provision is present for the pious and the wicked.' I said: 'I am not sad about that, and indeed it is as you say.' He asked: 'Is your sadness about the Hereafter?' He said: 'It is a true promise in which a Sovereign Subduer will judge.' I said: 'I am not sad about that either, and indeed it is as you say.' He said: 'Then what are you sad about?' I said: 'I fear the trial of Ibn al-Zubayr.' He laughed and said: 'O 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you seen anyone who feared Allah, the Exalted, and Allah did not save him?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'O 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you seen anyone who asked Allah, the Mighty and High, and He did not give him?' I said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then I looked, and there was no one in front of me.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of God be upon him) said: My father said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa said, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, on the authority of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, on the authority of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), who said: Verily, Musa son of 'Imran (peace be upon him) said: "O my Lord! I am pleased with what You have decreed, that You cause the elder to die and keep the young alive." Allah, the Mighty and High, replied: "O Musa! Are you not pleased with Me for being their Sustainer and Provider?" He said: "Of course, O Lord! You are the Best Custodian and the Best of Providers."

Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mu'adhi, said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, freed slave of the Hashimites, said: Yahya ibn Isma'il al-Jariri said reading (from his notes): Al-Husayn ibn Isma'il said: 'Amr ibn Jumay' narrated to me, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all). He said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) entered into the presence of Mu'awiyah, so he asked him: 'What possessed your father to kill the people of Basra, and then wander the streets at night wearing two undergarments?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'What drove him to that was his knowledge that what befall him would not miss him, and what missed him would not befall him.' He (Mu'awiyah) said: 'You have spoken the truth.' And when the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) intended to battle the Kharijites, it was said to him: 'Take your precautions, O Commander of the Faithful!' He (peace be upon him) composed: 'Which of my two days shall I escape from death? The day which is not decreed, or the day which is decreed? The day which is not decreed, I do not fear death; and if it is decreed, caution will not avail.'

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Isbahani narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'dawayh al-Burdh'i narrated to us, saying: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-'Ataki informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ashras narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Wahb ibn Hashim Abu al-Bakhtari narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: O Ali! Certainty is that you do not please anyone at the expense of Allah's anger, nor praise anyone for what Allah has granted you, nor blame anyone for what Allah has not granted you. Verily, sustenance is not drawn by the greed of a greedy person, nor diverted by the aversion of an aversive person. Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, through His wisdom and grace, placed refreshment and relief in certainty and contentment, and placed anxiety and sorrow in doubt and displeasure. Indeed, there is no poverty harder than ignorance, nor wealth more beneficial than intellect, nor solitude more lonely than conceit, nor support more secure than consultation, nor intellect like management, nor piety like abstaining from forbidden things, nor nobility like good conduct, nor worship like contemplation. The flaw of speech is lying, the flaw of knowledge is forgetfulness, the flaw of worship is lethargy, the flaw of intelligence is abruptness, the flaw of bravery is aggression, the flaw of magnanimity is showing favor, the flaw of beauty is vanity, and the flaw of nobility is arrogance.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: My father said: Muhammad ibn Abu al-Sahban said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi said: Aban al-Ahmar narrated to me from the Truth-teller, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) A man came to him and said to him: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, admonish me with an exhortation.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has guaranteed sustenance, then why is your concern [for accumulation]? And if sustenance is allocated, then why is your greed? And if reckoning is true, then why is your gathering [of wealth]? And if replacement from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is true, then why is your miserliness? And if the punishment from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the Hellfire, then why is your sinning? And if death is true, then why is your happiness [in worldly life]? And if presentation before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is true, then why is your cunning? And if Satan is an enemy, then why is your heedlessness? And if crossing the Bridge is true, then why is your pride? And if everything is by decree and destiny, then why is your grief? And if the world is perishable, then why is your tranquility [in it] towards it?'

Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bakr al-Khuri in Naysabur narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad the Jurist al-Khuri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Juybari al-Shaybani narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, had decreed the destinies and arranged the plans two thousand years before He created Adam.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ushnani al-Razi, the just one in Balkh, narrated to us; he said: 'Ali ibn Mihrawayh al-Qazwini narrated to us; he said: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida narrated to us, from his father, from his forefathers, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon them). He said: A Jewish man asked 'Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him): 'Tell me about what is not for Allah, what is not with Allah, and what Allah does not know.' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'As for what Allah, the Mighty and High, does not know, that is your statement, O assembly of Jews: 'Uzayr is the son of Allah, and Allah does not know of any son for Himself.' And as for your word, 'what is not for Allah,' then associating partners with Allah is not for Allah. And as for your word, 'what is not with Allah,' then oppression is not with Allah. The Jewish man said: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'

`Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Wahhab al-Sijzi in Naysabur said: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn `Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani reported to us that `Ali ibn `Abd Allah said: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Harrani said; Yahya ibn `Abd Allah ibn al-Dahhak said, on the authority of al-Awza'i, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abu Kathir, that The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked: "Shall we not guard you?" He (peace be upon him) said: "The guardian of every man is his death."

`Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Wahhab said: Mansur ibn `Abd Allah said: `Ali ibn `Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim said: Sharik said, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Wahab that One night in the Battle of Siffin, we were with Sa`id ibn Qays. The two army rows were standing opposite each other until the Commander of the Faithful (AS) came. We came down to his ground. Sa`id ibn Qays asked him: “O Commander of the Faithful! Do you not fear anything at this point?” He (AS) replied, And what should I fear? There is no anyone except that with him are two angels assigned to him so that he does not fall into a well or an animal does not hit him or he may not fall from a mountain until the decree comes for him. When that which is decreed comes, they vacate from between him and the decreed.

Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Tamim al-Sarkhasi said in Sarkhas that Abu Lubayd Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari said: Abu Damrah Anas ibn 'Ayad said, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: None of you believe unless he also believes in the Divine Decree, its good, its evil, its sweetness, and its bitterness.

28 - Allah's pleasure be upon him, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ta'i said: Abu Sa'id Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami al-Razi narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, who said: I heard my master Ali ibn Muhammad say: My father Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them all). And Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ishaq ibn Ja'far al-Alawi narrated to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi, from Ismail ibn Abu Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them); and the wording is for Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq. A man from the people of Iraq entered upon the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: Inform us about our departure to the people of Syria, is it by a decree from Allah and destiny? The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: Yes, O Shaykh, by Allah, you did not ascend a hill nor descend into the depth of a valley except by a decree from Allah and destiny. The Shaykh said: I account for my hardship before Allah, O Commander of the Faithful. He (peace be upon him) said: Hold back, O Shaykh, perhaps you think that the decree is irrevocable and the destiny is binding. If that were so, then reward and punishment, command and prohibition, and restraint would be annulled. The meaning of threat and promise would vanish. There would be no blame upon the evil-doer, nor praise for the good-doer. The good-doer would be more worthy of blame than the sinner, and the sinner more worthy of praise than the good-doer. That is the saying of the idol worshippers, the opponents of the Most Merciful, the predestinarians of this Ummah, and its Zoroastrians. O Shaykh, verily Allah, the Mighty and High, obliged with choice, forbade with warning, gave much for little, did not make the coerced disobey, nor the subjected obey, and did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain. This is the assumption of those who disbelieve. Woe to those who disbe

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i said, on the authority of his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Ali ibn Salim, on the authority of Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about charms (ruqy), do they remove anything from the Divine Decree? He said: They are from the Decree. And he (peace be upon him) added: The Free-willers (al-Qadariyyah) are the Zoroastrians of this Ummah, and they are the ones who intended to attribute to Allah with justice, but took Him out of His Rule. And in them was revealed this verse: (On the day when they shall be dragged upon their faces into the fire; taste the touch of hell. Surely We have created everything according to a measure).

30. Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi al-Aza'imi said: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumayh al-Nisawi related to me that Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Tamimi in Basra and Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mu'alla ibn Asad al-'Ammi both said: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Ghalabi said: Ahmad ibn 'Isa ibn Zayd said: Abd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abd Allah ibn Hasan said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) that he was asked about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (Surely We have created everything according to a measure). He (AS) replied, 'Verily, the Mighty and High has said: We have created everything according to a measure for the dwellers of hell according to their deeds.'

33. My father (RA) narrated, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi narrated from his father al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kufi, from his grandfather 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, that he asked Al-Sadiq (AS): about the prayer behind one who denies the decree of Allah, the Mighty and High. He (AS) said: 'Then he should repeat all the prayers he has prayed behind him.'

33. Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by some hoarders and ordered that their hoarding be taken out to the depths of the markets and where the eyes could see it. It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'Would that you fixed a price for them?' He (peace be upon him) became angry until the anger was evident on his face and said: 'Should I fix prices for them? Verily, the price is with Allah, the Mighty and High. He raises it if He wills and lowers it if He wills.' It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'Would that you set a price for us, for prices increase and decrease.' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'I would not meet Allah, the Mighty and High, with an innovation for which nothing was revealed to me. Leave the servants of Allah, so that some of them may eat from others.'

34. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), who said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has assigned an angel to regulate prices, who manages them with His Command. And Abu Hamzah al-Thumali said: High prices were mentioned to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), so he said: 'I do not have authority over their high prices; if they rise, it is upon them (the angel/God), and if they lower, it is upon them.' The Compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: High prices (Ghala') is the increase in the prices of items to the extent that an item is sold for more than what it was sold for in that place, and low prices (Rukhsh) is the decrease in that. Whatever of low or high prices is due to the abundance or scarcity of items, that is from Allah, the Mighty and High, and it is obligatory to be pleased with that and submit to Him. And whatever of high or low prices is caused by what is taken from people for no lack of items or excess of them, without their approval, or is due to one person purchasing all the food of a town causing the food to become expensive for that reason, then that is from the Price-Fixer (al-Mus'ir) and the Transgressor, by purchasing all the food of the city, as Hakim ibn Hizam did. When food entered Medina, he would buy it all. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him and said: 'O Hakim ibn Hizam! Beware of hoarding.'

35. My father (RA) narrated it, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Salmah al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (AS) He said: Whenever there is food in the town other than what one person has bought, it is permissible for him to seek the surplus with his commodity, because if there is food in the town sufficient for the people, the price will not rise because of him; rather, it rises only if one person buys all that enters the city.

Ahmad ibn Ziyad Ja'far al-Hamdani (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Hirawi, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) He (AS) said: I asked him, 'For what reason did Allah, the Mighty and High, drown the whole of the earth in the time of Nuh (peace be upon him), while there were children among them who were free of sin?' He replied: 'There were no children among them, because Allah, the Mighty and High, made the male reproductive systems of the people of Nuh and the wombs of their women barren for forty years, so their lineage was cut off; thus they drowned and there was no child among them. And Allah, the Mighty and High, would not destroy with His punishment anyone who is without sin. As for the rest of the people of Nuh (peace be upon him), they were drowned for denying the Prophet of Allah, Nuh (peace be upon him). And the rest of them were drowned by their agreement with the deniers. And whoever is absent from a matter and agrees to it is like one who witnessed it and committed it.'

3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: Verily, the children of the Muslims are designated at Allah, the Mighty and High, as intercessors and those who will receive intercession. When they reach twelve years of age, good deeds are written for them, and when they reach puberty, bad deeds are written against them.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, the Mighty and High, will hold objection against seven: the child, the one who died during the period between two prophets, the elderly senile man who lived during the period of prophecy, the simple-minded person, the mentally ill, the deaf and the dumb. Each of these will plead their case to Allah, the Mighty and High. He said: So Allah, the Mighty and High, will send to them a messenger who will light a fire for them and say: 'Verily, your Lord has commanded you to jump into it.' Thus, whoever jumps in it, it will become cool, and a means of peace for him, and whoever resists will be driven to the Hell.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Fadl ibn 'Amir, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah ibn A'yun, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) praying over the small son of Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he said the Takbir over him, then he said: O Zurarah! Verily, this and its like do not require the prayer (of the deceased). If it were not for the fact that people would say, 'The Hashimites do not pray on the children,' I would not have prayed over him. Zurarah said: I asked him, 'Was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked about them?' He said: 'Yes, he was asked about them, and he said: Allah knows best what they used to do.' Then he said: O Zurarah, do you know what His saying 'Allah knows best what they used to do' means?' I said: 'No, by Allah.' He said: For Allah, the Mighty and High, has the divine will regarding them. That is, when the Day of Judgment comes, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will hold evidence against seven: the child, the one who died between two prophets, the old man who lived in the time of a prophet but did not have full intellect, the simple-minded, the mentally ill who does not have intellect, the deaf, and the dumb. So all of these will have evidence held against them by Allah, the Mighty and High, on the Day of Judgment. Allah will send a messenger to them and bring forth a fire for them, and He will say to them: 'Verily, your Lord commands you to jump into this fire.' Whoever jumps into it, it will become cool and a means of peace for him, and whoever disobeys Him will be driven to the fire.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abu Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abd Allah (AS) who said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, made Ibrahim (AS) and Sarah feed the children of the believers from a tree in Paradise which has udders like the udders of cows, in palaces made of pearls. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be dressed, perfumed, and presented to their parents, so they and their parents will be kings in Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And those who believe and their offspring follow them in faith, We will unite with them their offspring." He (AS) said: "The sons fall short of the deeds of the fathers, so Allah, the Mighty and High, unites the sons with the fathers so that their eyes may rest."

My father (RA) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Zakariyya, from Abu Basir, that Abu Abdillah (AS) said: When a child of the believers passes away, a caller proclaims in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth: 'Verily, so-and-so's son has died.' If his father, mother, or one of them, or some of his family from among the believers have died, he is handed over to them to feed him. If not, he is handed over to Fatimah (peace be upon her) to feed him until his parents or one of them, or some of his family from among the believers arrive, and then he is handed over to them.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of God be upon him) narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, who said: Muhammad ibn Hassan narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali, from the progeny of Nawfal ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from 'Isa ibn Abd Allah al-'Umari, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him) Regarding the illness that befalls a child, he said: It is atonement for his parents.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Ala' ibn Sa'id the freed slave of Al Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry the virgins, for they are the purest in speech, the best in morals, and the most fertile. Do you not know that on the Day of Judgment I will boast of you among the nations, even for a miscarriage? The child who died in the womb will be waiting at the Gate of Paradise. Allah, the Mighty and High, will say to it: Enter Paradise. It will say: No, not until my parents enter before me. Allah, the Mighty and High, will say to one of the angels: Bring me his parents. And they will be brought to Paradise, and He will say: This is due to My Mercy upon you.'

My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Jamil ibn Durraj, from Abu Abdillah (AS) He said: I asked him about the children of the Prophets (AS), and he replied: They are not like the children of other people. I asked him about Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of Allah (SA), if he had remained alive, would he have been a truthful one (Siddiq)? He said: If he had remained alive, he would have been upon the path of his father (SA).

Abu Ahmad al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Karim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Rahman al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abu Salamah narrated to us, saying: I read to Abu Umar al-San'ani from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is many a beggar with unkempt hair, covered in dust, wearing two tattered garments, who is turned away from the doors. If he swears by Allah, the Mighty and High, He will grant his oath.

3. My father (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir that `Awn ibn `Abd Allah ibn Mas`ud became sick as I went to visit him. He said: “Shall I not related to you a tradition from `Abd Allah ibn mas`ud?” I replied, “Why not?” He said: `Abd Allah said: “While we were in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (SA), he smiled. So I asked him, “What is it, O Messenger of Allah?” He (SA) replied, “I am surprised at how a believer can worry about being sick. If he knew the reward which resides in illness, he would ask to be ill until he meets his Lord, the Mighty and High.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: A group of people came to a prophet and said: Pray to your Lord for us that He may remove death from us. So he prayed for them, and Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, removed death from them. They multiplied until their houses became congested and their offspring increased. A man would wake up in the morning and need to feed, please, and take care of his father, mother, grandfather, and great-grandfather. They became preoccupied with seeking means of subsistence. So they consulted him (the prophet) and said: Ask your Lord to return us to the lifespans we used to have. He asked his Lord, the Mighty and High, and He returned them to their appointed lifespans.

5. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: My father narrated to us, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fudal, from Ali ibn Uqbah, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abd Allah al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah smiled one day until his teeth were showing, then he said: 'Will you not ask me why I smiled?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I am astonished at the Muslim man that there is no decree that Allah, the Mighty and High, decrees for him except that it is good for him in the outcome of his affair.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Qatadah al-Qummi, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya narrated to us, on the authority of Aban al-Ahmar, from Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) He said: 'And by the One who sent my grandfather (peace be upon him and his family) as a righteous prophet, verily Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, provides sustenance to a servant according to his generosity. And verily, help descends from Heaven according to the extent of the need. And verily, patience descends according to the severity of the affliction.'

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of God be upon him) said: My father said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa said, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Najran, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), who said: Verily, Musa son of 'Imran (peace be upon him) said: 'O my Lord! I am pleased with what You have decreed: You cause the elderly to die and preserve the young.' Allah, the Mighty and High, replied: 'O Musa! Are you not pleased with Me for being their Sustainer and Provider?' He said: 'Of course, O Lord. You are the best Custodian, and the best Provider.'

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hazhaz, on the authority of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: 'I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:' Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, has provided the sustenance of the believers from where they do not expect, and this is that when the servant does not know the source of his sustenance, his supplication increases.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman ibn Ayyub al-Khazzaz said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): "For what reason did Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, place the souls in the bodies after they had been in His highest realm in the loftiest place?" He (peace be upon him) replied: "Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, knew that whenever the souls were left in their state of honor and elevation, most of them would incline towards claiming lordship for themselves other than Him, the Mighty and High, so He placed them by His Power into the bodies which He had decreed for them from the beginning of the Divine Decree, observing them and having mercy upon them, and made some of them in need of others, and attached some to others, and elevated some above others in degrees, and sufficed some by others, and sent to them His messengers and appointed for them His proofs, bearers of good news and warners, commanding them to engage in servitude and humility to their Lord through the types of acts that make them servants, and established for them punishments in the immediate world and punishments in the Hereafter, and rewards in the immediate world and rewards in the Hereafter, to make them desire good through that and to make them disdain evil, and to humble them through seeking sustenance and earnings, so that they may know thereby that they are servants and created beings, and devote themselves to His worship, so that they may deserve thereby the eternal bliss and the Garden of Eternity, and be safe from inclining to what is not rightfully theirs. Then he (peace be upon him) said: "O son of al-Fadl! Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has a better view for His servants than they have for themselves, do you not see that you see in them nothing but a love for elevation over others, so that among them is one who has inclined towards claiming lordship, and among them is one who has inclined towards claiming prophethood without its right, and among them is one who has inclined towards claiming Imamate without its right, despite what they see in themselves of deficiency, inability, weakness, lowliness, need, poverty, alternating pains, and the overpowering death that subdues

Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shaybani (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i said, on the authority of his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Ali ibn Salim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Basir, on the authority of Abu Abd Allah Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: And they shall continue to differ, except those on whom your Lord has mercy; and for this did He create them. He replied, “He created them to do what makes them deserve His Mercy so that He may have mercy on them.”

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to us on the authority of their father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them all). Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Who made the earth a resting place for you.' He said: He made it suitable for your natures and in harmony with your bodies. He did not make it severely hot and warm so it may burn you, nor severely cold so it may freeze you. Nor did He make it severely perfumed to give you headaches, nor terribly foul-smelling so it may sicken you. He neither made it severely soft like water so it may drown you, nor severely hard so it may obstruct you from making houses, buildings, and graves for your deceased. Rather, Allah, the Mighty and High, made it with firmness so that you may benefit from it, enabling you to hold together and your bodies and structures to hold together upon it. He placed in it what yields to your houses and graves and many of your benefits. Therefore, He made the earth a resting place for you. Then He, the Mighty and High, said: 'And the heaven a canopy,' meaning a protecting roof over you, preserved, wherein He directs its sun, moon, and stars for your benefits. Then He, the Mighty and High, said: 'And sent down from the heaven water,' meaning the rain, which He sent down from the High One, to reach the peaks of your mountains, hills, elevations, and low-lying lands. Then He separated it into drizzle, shower, heavy downpour, and sprinkles, so that your earth may absorb it. And He did not send that rain down upon you in one single block, lest it corrupt your lands, trees, crops, and fruits. Then He, the Mighty and High, said: 'Then brings forth with it subsistence for you of the fruits; therefore, do not set up rivals to Allah,' meaning counterparts and similar ones from among the idols, which cannot think, nor hear, nor see, nor have power over anything. While you know that they do not have power over any of the magnificent bounties which your Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, has bestowed upon you.

My father (RA) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdah, from Abu Ja'far (AS), who said: The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said: Allah, Great be His Glory, said: Verily, among My believing servants are those who strive in My worship. They rise from their sleep and the comfort of their pillows to perform supererogatory prayers during the nights and exhaust themselves in My worship. So I overpower them with sleep for a night or two, as a look-out by Me for them and to preserve them. They sleep until morning, and when they rise, they are disgusted with themselves and afflicted over it. And if I did not prevent them from doing what they desire of My worship, pride would enter them, and pride would lead them to destruction through their deeds and their satisfaction with themselves, until they think they have surpassed the worshippers, and they have exceeded the limit of inadequacy in their worship. Thus they become distant from Me at that time, while they think they are drawing close to Me.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Among what Allah, the Mighty and High, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him) was: 'O Musa, I have not created a creation more beloved to Me than My believing servant. Indeed, I test him with what is good for him, and I cure him with what is good for him. And I know what is best for My servant in his affairs. So let him be patient with My trials, let him give thanks for My bounties, and let him be pleased with My decree. I will record him among the truthful ones with Me if he acts for My pleasure and obeys My command.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The people are commanded and prohibited, and whoever has an excuse, Allah, the Mighty and High, forgives him.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa said, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Najran, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Habib al-Sajistani, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) who said: Verily, it is stated in the Torah: O Musa! Verily, I have created you, chosen you, strengthened you, commanded you for My Obedience, and prohibited you from disobeying Me. Therefore, if you obey Me I will help you to obey Me and if you disobey Me, I will not help you to disobey me. O Musa! I have favored you in your obedience to Me, and I have evidence over you in your disobedience of Me.

3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, on the authority of who he mentioned, on the authority of Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, on the authority of Abu Abdillah, on the authority of his forefathers (AS) He said: The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said: 'Whoever Allah promises to reward for an action, He will fulfill it for him. And whoever He threatens with punishment for an action, He is in it with the choice (to punish or pardon).'

Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi in Naysabur in the year 352 AH informed us; he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Suli informed us; he said: Ibn Dhukwan informed us; he said: I heard Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas say: We were in the presence of al-Rida (peace be upon him) when they discussed the major sins and the belief of the Mu'tazilites regarding them: that they are not forgiven. Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Qur'an descended contradicting the belief of the Mu'tazilites, Allah, the Mighty and High, says: 'Verily, your Lord is the Lord of forgiveness to people despite their injustice.' The tradition is long; we have extracted from it the required passage.

5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Haytham al-Ijli; Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qittan; Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani; al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mukattab; Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Sa'igh, and Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Warraq (may Allah be pleased with them) said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyyah al-Qittan said: Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Habib said: Tamim ibn Buhlul said: Abu Mu'awiyah said, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them): He said regarding what was described to him of the laws of religion: Verily, Allah does not impose on a soul except its capacity, nor does He burden it beyond its power. The actions of the servants are created with created [taqdir] creation, not with constitutive [takwin] creation, and Allah is the Creator of all things. We do not say with determinism (jabr), nor with relinquishment (tafwid). And Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, does not take the innocent for the guilty, nor does Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, punish children for the sins of their fathers, for He said in the clear part of His Book: 'And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another' and He said, the Mighty and Exalted: 'And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for.' And to Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, belongs the power to pardon and bestow favor, and it is not befitting for Him, the Mighty and Exalted, to oppress. Nor does Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, impose on His servants the obedience of one He knows will mislead them and lead them astray. Nor does He choose for His message or select from His servants one He knows will disbelieve in Him and worship Satan instead of Him. Nor does He appoint over His creation a proof except an infallible one. The hadith is long; we have taken from it the place of need, and I have included it in its entirety in the book Al-Khasa'il.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Hamzah ibn Humran, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, one good deed is recorded for him; if he does it, ten good deeds are recorded for him. Allah multiplies (the reward) for whom He wills up to seven hundred times. And whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, no bad deed is recorded against him until he does it. If he does not do it, one good deed is recorded for him because he refrained from doing it. And if he does it, it remains pending for nine hours; if he repents and regrets it, it is not recorded against him; but if he does not repent nor regret it, one bad deed is recorded against him.

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ghalib al-Shafi`i narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad Mujahid ibn A`yun ibn Dawud informed us, saying: `Isa ibn Ahmad al-`Asqalani informed us, saying: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayyil informed us, saying: Israfil informed us, saying: Thuwayr narrated from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) said: There is not a verse in the Qur'an more beloved to me than the Word of the Mighty and High: Surely Allah does not forgive that anything should be associated with Him, and forgives what is beside that to whomsoever He pleases.

10. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, blessings of Allah be upon them, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), from Jibra'il (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, great be His Glory, said: Whoever commits a sin, minor or major, and he does not know that I have the right to punish him for it or to forgive him, I will never forgive him that sin. And whoever commits a sin, whether minor or major, and he knows that I have the right to punish him and to forgive him, I forgive him.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hakim, that I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the origin of recognition?' He (peace be upon him) answered, 'It is from the making of Allah, the Mighty and High: The servants do not have any making in it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Durraj, from Ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, will hold evidence against the people with what He gave them and made them to recognize.

3. Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, from Ibn Fuddal, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Hamzah ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, will hold evidence against the people with what He gave them and made them to recognize.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (mercy of God be upon him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Ibn Fudal, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Hamzah ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) In His Word, the Mighty and High: "And it is not for Allah to lead people astray after guiding them. He even makes clear to them what they should guard against." He (AS) said: "He makes them recognize what pleases Him and what angers Him." And He said: "And inspired it with knowledge of evil and piety." He (AS) said: "He explained to it what it should do and what it should avoid." And He said: "Surely We have shown him the way: he may be thankful or unthankful." He (AS) said: "He made us recognize what to accept or to avoid." And concerning the Word of the Mighty and High: "And as to Thamud, We guided them, but they chose error above guidance." He (AS) said: "We made them recognize, but they consciously chose misguidance over guidance, while they knew."

Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And guided him to the two conspicuous ways." He (AS) said: "The way of good and the way of evil."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan, from Durust, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Six things in which the servants have no agency: knowledge, ignorance, contentment, anger, sleep, and wakefulness.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is not compulsory for the creation to recognize Allah until He introduces Himself to them. It is compulsory for Allah that He introduces Himself to the creation. It is compulsory for the creation to accept Allah when He introduces Himself to them.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yun, who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about one who knows nothing, is there any responsibility upon him? He (peace be upon him) replied, 'No.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fuddal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu al-Hasan Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whatever of His Knowledge Allah has concealed from the servants is unburdened from them.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Hamzah ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: 'Write down what I dictate to you: That among our beliefs is that Allah, the Mighty and High, will present proof against the servants based on what He granted them and what He made known to them. Then He sent a Messenger to them, and revealed to him the Book, commanding in it and forbidding. He commanded in it the prayer and the fasting,' then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) slept in and missed the prayer (1). So He said: 'I make you sleep, and I wake you up. Go and pray, so that they may learn what to do when this happens to them. It is not as they say: 'If one sleeps in and misses it, he is lost.' The same applies to fasting. I make you ill and I cure you. When I cure you, make up for it up.' Then Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'And so, when you look at all matters, you will not find anyone in hardship (of religion), nor will you find anyone except that Allah has presented proof against him and has will regarding him. And I do not say: They do whatever they wish.' Then he said: 'Verily, Allah guides and misleads.' And He said: 'They were commanded only according to their capacity.' Whatever Allah commanded people to do, they have the ability to do it. And whatever they do not have the ability to do, it is lifted from them. But most people are devoid of good.' Then he said: '(No blame is upon the weak nor upon the sick nor upon those who do not find what they should spend to stay being), so long as they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger; that is the way of the doers of good; * Nor upon those who when they came to you that you might carry them.' [The verse] He lifted from them because they do not find (the means). The Compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: His (peace be upon him) word: 'Verily, Allah guides and misleads' means that He, the Mighty and High, guides the believers on the Day of Judgment to Paradise, and misleads the unjust away from Paradise. Verily, the Mighty and High has said: (1) 'Surely (as for) those who believe and do good, their Lord will guide them by their faith; there shall flow

And with this chain of transmission, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'dan, who raises it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, has not bestowed a bounty upon a servant except that He has made incumbent upon him therein the proof (hujjah) from Allah, the Mighty and High. Therefore, whoever Allah favors by making him strong, his proof upon him is to fulfill what he is obligated to do and to bear with those below him who are weaker than him. And whoever Allah favors by making him wealthy, his proof upon him is his wealth; it is incumbent upon him therein to attend to the poor with his superogatory charity. And whoever Allah favors by making him noble in lineage and handsome in appearance, his proof upon him is that he praises Allah for that and does not arrogate himself over others in withholding the rights of the weak due to his status of nobility and beauty.

My father (RA) said: `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Fuddal, from `Ali ibn `Uqbah, from his father, who said: I heard Abu `Abd Allah (AS) say: Leave your matter for Allah, and do not leave it for the people. Whatever is for Allah belongs to Allah alone, and whatever is for the people will not ascend to Allah. Do not argue with the people about your religion, for verily arguing is an illness of the heart. Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He pleases. Will you then force men till they become believers? Leave the people, for verily the people take their knowledge from each other, while you have your knowledge from the messenger of Allah (SA). Verily, I have heard my father, Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) say that `Verily, when Allah, the Mighty and High, writes that a servant should enter a matter, then he is quicker than a bird to its nest.”

My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hamran, from al-Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, when Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, intends good for a servant, He marks a spot of light in his heart, opens the pores of his heart, and assigns an angel to guide him. And when He intends evil for a servant, He marks a black spot in his heart, closes the pores of his heart, and assigns a demon to mislead him, So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his breast for Islam; and whoever He intends to cause to err, He makes his breast strait and narrow, as though he were ascending upwards. He said: Then he recited this verse. The Compiler of this book said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, intends evil for a servant as a result of a sin he commits, thereby deserving that a seal be placed on his heart and a demon be assigned to mislead him. And He does not do this to him except by deserving it. And sometimes Allah, the Mighty and High, assigns an angel to guide His servant by deserving it or by favor, and He singles out for His mercy whom He wills, And Allah, the Mighty and High, says: 'And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Compassionate, We appoint for him a demon, so he becomes his associate.'

Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Mughayrah informed us, saying: Mansur ibn Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili narrated from Abd Allah ibn Mikkan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) He was asked about recognition (al-ma'rifa), is it acquired? He said: No. It was asked of him: Then is it from the making of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, and from His gift? He said: Yes, and the servants do not have a part in it, but they have the acquisition of actions. And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the actions of the servants are created with a created decree, not with constitutional creation. And the meaning of that is that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has always been Knowing of their measures before their existence.

Abd al-Walid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi al-Attar (RA) said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah al-Naysaburi said, on the authority of Hamdan ibn Sulayman that I wrote to al-Rida (AS) asking him whether the actions of the servants are created or uncreated? So he (AS) wrote back, “The actions of the servants were decreed through the Knowledge of Allah, the Might and High, two thousand years before the creation of the servants.”

My father (RA) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i al-Qadi, who said: Abu Abd Allah (AS) said: Whoever practices what he knows, suffices for him what he does not know. Chapter: The mention of the session of al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (AS) with the people of religions and owners of doctrines, such as the Katholikos, the head of the Jews, the leaders of the Sabians, and the Great Herbed, and what he spoke to Imran the Sabian regarding Tawhid in the presence of al-Ma'mun.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Ja'far (AS) said: Discuss the creation of Allah, but refrain from discussing about Allah. Verily, discussing about Allah causes nothing but confusion.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: Discuss about anything, but do not discuss about Allah.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kanasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Mention from the Greatness of Allah whatever you wish, but do not mention His Essence, for you do not mention anything from Him except that it is greater than it.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out to his companions and said: 'What has gathered you?' They replied: 'We have gathered to mention our Lord and to ponder upon His Greatness.' He said: 'You will not attain [the true reality of] pondering upon His Greatness.'

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Fudayl ibn Yasir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: O son of Adam! If a bird ate your heart, it would not be filled by it, and if your eye was covered with a piece of cloth the size of a needle's hole, it would be covered. You seek to understand the dominion of the heavens and the earth by means of them (your heart and your eye). If you are truthful, then here is the sun, a creation from the creations of Allah. If you are able to fill your eyes with it, then what you say is true.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: And whoever is blind in this [world], he shall (also) be blind in the Hereafter; and more erring from the way. He (AS) said: He who is not guided by the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the revolution of the celestial spheres, the sun and the moon, and the wondrous signs, to know that there is something greater behind all that, then he is blind in the Hereafter and more erring from the way. He (AS) added: He is blind and more erring from the way regarding what he did not see [with his own eyes].

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa said, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Tha'labah ibn Maymun, on the authority of al-Hasan al-Sayqal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Discuss about anything but the Throne, and discuss about anything other than what is above the Throne. For a group conversed about the Essence of Allah, the Mighty and High, and they became so bewildered that when someone called one of them from in front, he would answer from behind, and when someone called one of them from behind, he would answer from in front.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from 'Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about something from Divine Unity, so he raised his hands to the sky and said: 'Exalted is Allah, the Supreme [Jabbar]. Verily, whoever speculates about what is there will be destroyed.'

And with this chain of transmission, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And that to your Lord is the end of all.' He said: 'If the statement ends with Allah, the Mighty and High, then abstain.'

And with this chain of transmission, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Muhammad! The people will continue to engage in logical reasoning until they begin discussing the Essence of Allah. When you hear them doing so, say: There is no god but Allah, the One, and nothing whatsoever is like unto Him.

And with this chain of transmission, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: O Ziyad! Beware of quarrels/arguments, for they breed doubt, nullify deeds, and ruin their owner. It may be that he speaks about something for which he will not be forgiven. Verily, there were people in the past who abandoned the knowledge they were given and sought the knowledge they were prevented from knowing, until their speech reached Allah, the Mighty and High, and they became bewildered. Indeed, a man might be called from in front of him and answer from behind, and be called from behind and answer from in front.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu al-Yas', from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (AS) He said: Verily, there was a group of people before you who cast aside the knowledge they were granted, and sought knowledge that was not granted to them. Hence, they did not stop questioning until they asked about what was above Heaven. As a result, their hearts went astray. Among them was a man who, when called from the front, would answer from behind, and when called from behind, he would answer from the front.

And with this chain of transmission, from Aba al-Yasa', from Aba al-Jarud, from Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Abandon speculating about Allah, for indeed speculating about Allah does not increase except in bewilderment, because Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be perceived by the eyes, nor can the reports/reachings of the mind reach Him.

And with this chain of transmission, from Abu al-Yas', from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Beware of speculation about Allah, for speculation about Allah increases nothing but arrogance, because Allah, the Mighty and High, cannot be perceived by vision, and He cannot be attributed with measure.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, who said: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Fudayl ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) He said: A group of people entered his presence, those who speak about Lordship (al-Rububiyyah). He said to them: Fear Allah and revere Allah, and do not say what we do not say. For if you say one thing and we say another, then you will die and we will die. Then Allah will raise you, and He will raise us, and you will be where Allah wills, and we will be.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa said: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsah, from al-Mundhar al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyah, who said: Verily, this Ummah will not be ruined until they speak about their Lord.

And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of discussing Allah. Discuss His Greatness, but do not discuss His Essence, for discussing Allah leads only to astray/confusion.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi said: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid said, on the authority of 'Ali ibn Hasan al-Wasiti, on the authority of some of our scholars, on the authority of Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): "Verily, the people in our presence are talking increasingly about the attributes [of Allah]. What do you say?" He replied: "It is abhorred [makruh]. Do you not hear Allah, the Mighty and High, saying: 'And to your Lord is the end [of all].' Speak about other than that."

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Fī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Bakīr, from Zurārah, from Abū ‘Abd Allāh (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, there was a king of great status who was in his own gathering; he began to discuss the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, and then he disappeared, and it is not known what became of him.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Beware of speculating about Allah, but if you wish to look at the greatness of Allah, then look at the greatness of His creation.

From the father (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying Quarrelling destroys religion, puts an end to good deeds, and leaves nothing but doubt as its heir.
And with this chain of transmission, from Abu Basir, he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The quarrelers are ruined, and the Muslims are saved. Verily, the Muslims are the noble ones.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying: One is only argued with (in matters of faith) if he lacks piety or if he is a man of doubt.

Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fudayl, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: O Abu Ubaydah! Beware of the quarrelers and the liars about us, for they have left what they were ordered to know and have strived for the knowledge of Heaven. O Abu Ubaydah! Accustom people according to their dispositions and distance yourself from them according to their deeds. We do not consider a man among us to be wise until he recognizes the tone of speech. And most certainly you will recognize them by the tone of (their) speech.

My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid said, on the authority of al-Ghifari, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Abd Allah (AS) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said: Beware of arguing with every maniac, for every maniac has his proof dictated to him until the end of his term (death). When his term ends, his mischief will burn him in the Fire. It is also transmitted: 'His mistake troubles him and burns him.'

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from the man (Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)) said: It is narrated from your fathers (peace be upon them) that they prohibited speaking about religion. Your followers who speak have interpreted that those who are not skilled in speaking about it were prohibited, but whoever is skilled was not prohibited. Is this as they interpreted or not? He (peace be upon him) wrote: Both the skilled and the unskilled should not speak about it, for indeed its sin is greater than its benefit.

27. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris said; Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ali ibn Ismail, on the authority of al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, on the authority of more than one, on the authority of Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): "What is the proof of Allah over the servants?" He (peace be upon him) answered: "They should say what they know, and refrain (stop) when they do not know."

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyani narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Nujayyah al-Qawwas, from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Command your companions to restrain their tongues, abandon quarreling in religion, and strive in the worship of Allah, the Mighty and High.

Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from al-Muthanna, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: 'One is only argued with (or quarrels) if he is one who has doubts, or one who has no piety (war').'

And with this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Hafs Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: The debaters of this sect are more evil than them from every category.

32. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Hadrami, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Mufaddal! Whoever speculates about the state of Allah is ruined, and whoever seeks power is ruined as well.

33. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah has cursed those who made their religion a means of greed/striving, meaning argumentation, to refute the truth with falsehood.'

34. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Fadl ibn 'Amir, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abu Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am the guarantor of a house in the highest part of Paradise, a house in the middle of Paradise, and a house in the gardens of Paradise for whoever refrains from vain argument, even if he is correct.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah al-Ash'ari narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one he mentioned, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked: Is it permissible to say that Allah, the Might and High, is a Thing? He (peace be upon him) replied: Yes, it removes Him from both extremes: the extreme of annulment [ta'til] and the extreme of anthropomorphism [tashbih].

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is free from His creation, and His creation is free from Him. And whatever is designated by the name 'thing,' other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is created. And Allah is the Creator of all things. Blessed is He who is not like anything.

Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim informed us from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyyah, from Khaythamah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, is free from His creation, and His creation is free from Him. Whatever falls under the name of 'thing' other than Allah, the Mighty and High, is created. And Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of all things.

Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu al-Maghra, who elevated it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said: Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, is free from His creation, and His creation is free from Him. And whatever is designated by the name 'thing' is a creation, other than Allah, the Mighty and High.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran said: I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) about Divine Unity (Tawhid), so I said: 'Is He presumed to be a thing?' He replied: 'Yes, [He is] Incomprehensible and Unlimited. Whatever your imagination conceives of Him as, that is contrary to Him. Nothing resembles Him, and imagination does not perceive Him. How could imagination perceive Him when He is beyond what is rationally understood and beyond what is conceived in imagination? He is merely a Thing that is Incomprehensible and Unlimited.'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, who said: Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) was asked Is it permissible to say that Allah is a Thing? He answered: Yes, it removes Him from the two extremes: the extreme of annulment [ta'til] and the extreme of anthropomorphism [tashbih].

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Buttah said: A number of our companions narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: "What would you say if you were told: Inform me, is Allah, the Mighty and High, a Thing or is He not a thing?" I said to him: Allah, the Mighty and High, has established Himself as a Thing where He says: 'Say: What thing is the weightiest in testimony? Say: Allah is a witness between you and me.' So I say: He is a Thing unlike other things, for in negating 'thing-ness' from Him is His nullification and negation, He said to me: You are truthful and correct, Then al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: People have three schools of thought regarding Divine Unity: negation, anthropomorphism, and affirmation without anthropomorphism, The school of negation is not permissible, and the school of anthropomorphism is not permissible because nothing resembles Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He. The path in the third way is affirmation without anthropomorphism. Chapter: What has come regarding Vision

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid said, on the authority of some of our scholars, that Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) passed by a grave from the graves of his Household, so he placed his hand on it, and then said: O my God! Your Omnipotence is apparent, but Your Essence/Shape is not apparent, so they were ignorant of You and tried to measure You. And any measurement of You is other than what is in You. And I am free from those who sought You through comparison (anthropomorphism). Nothing is similar to You, O my God. And they will not comprehend You. And the apparent blessings upon them from You are their proof for You, if they knew You. And in Your creation, O my God, there is sufficiency that they should grasp You. But they equated You with Your creation, from which they did not know You. And they took some of Your signs as a lord, and for that reason they described You. You are exalted, O my Lord, from what the anthropomorphists described You with.

3. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: A group of people came from across the river to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said to him: We have come to ask you about three matters. If you answer us in them, we will know that you are learned. He said: Ask. They said: Inform us about Allah: Where was He? And how was He? And upon what was His reliance? He said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is the Creator of 'how', so He is without 'how'. And He is the Creator of 'where', so He is without 'where'. And His reliance was upon His Omnipotence. They said: We testify that you are learned. The compiler of this book said: By his statement 'And His reliance was upon His Omnipotence', he means upon His Essence, because Omnipotence is one of the attributes of the Essence of Allah, the Mighty and High.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (mercy of God be upon him) narrated to me, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, on the authority of one he mentioned, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) He said: Iblis said to Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him): 'Does your Lord have the power to place the Earth inside an egg, without making the Earth smaller or the egg any bigger?' Thus, Isa (peace be upon him) replied: 'Woe unto you! Verily, Allah cannot be described with limits. Who has more power than He who diminishes the Earth, and enlarges the egg?'

My father (RA) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rubay ibn Abd Allah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abd Allah (AS) saying: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, cannot be described. Zurarah said: Abu Ja'far (AS) said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, cannot be described, And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal. So whatever attribute of power they assign to Him, He is greater than that.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: My father (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyyah was a calm man (with a gesture of his hand). While he was performing the circumambulation of the Ka'bah, al-Hajjaj approached him and said: 'I am inclined to strike the one who has your eyes.' Muhammad replied to him: 'No, verily, for Allah, Blessed is His Name, in His creation are three hundred moments or glances every day. Perhaps one of them may suffice you instead of me.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It was said to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'Does your Lord have the power to place the world in an egg, without making the world smaller or the egg bigger?' He answered: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, cannot be described by means of limits. However, what you have asked is impossible.'
