Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated from his paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked: 'Does Allah have the power to place the Earth in an egg, without making the Earth smaller or the egg any bigger?' He replied: 'Woe unto you! Verily, Allah cannot be described by means of limits. Who has more power than He who diminishes the Earth and enlarges the egg?'

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Barqi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: My father narrated from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, who said: A man came to al-Rida (peace be upon him). He asked: 'Does Your Lord have the power to place the heavens and the Earth and whatever is between them inside an egg? He replied: Yes, and in something even smaller than an egg. He has placed it in your eye, while it is smaller than an egg. For when you open it, you see the Sky and the Earth and whatever is in between them. If He willed, He would have blinded you from it.

Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Abu al-Qasim al-'Alawi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, who said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Arafah, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) Did Allah create things through His Omnipotence or without it? He replied: It is not permissible to say that Allah created things by means of Omnipotence, because if you say 'He created things by Omnipotence,' it is as if you have made Omnipotence a thing other than Him, and made it a tool with which He created things, and that is polytheism. And if you say 'He created things with Omnipotence,' you are merely describing Him as having the ability and power over them, but He is neither weak nor incapable nor in need of anything else. Muhammad ibn 'Ali, the compiler of this book, said: When we say that Allah has always been Omnipotent, we intend thereby to negate inability from Him, and we do not intend to affirm a thing co-existing with Him, because He, the Mighty and High, has always been One with nothing co-existing with Him. I will explain the difference between the attributes of Essence and the attributes of Actions in its chapter, if Allah wills.

Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim informed us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Adhinah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) In His Word, the Mighty and High: 'No secret counsel of three is there but He is the fourth of them, nor of five but He is the sixth of them, nor of fewer than that nor more but He is with them wherever they are.' He said: He is One, Unique in Essence, distinct from His creation, and with this He described Himself. He encompasses all things by supervision, encompassing, and power. Nothing is hidden from Him, not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or the earth, nor smaller or larger than that, by encompassing and knowledge, not by Essence. Because spaces are limited, enclosed by four boundaries. If He were by Essence, it would be necessary for Him to be enclosed.

Tamim ibn Abd Allah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: My father narrated to me, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm, who said: I attended the assembly of al-Ma'mun, and with him was al-Rida, Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both). Al-Ma'mun asked him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, is it not from your saying that the Prophets are infallible?' He replied: 'Yes.' He asked him about some verses from the Quran, and among what he asked was: 'Then inform me about the saying of Ibrahim: My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said: What! And do you not believe? He said: Yes, but that my heart may be at ease.' Al-Rida (peace be upon him) replied: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that I will choose a friend for Me from among My servants; if he asks Me for the revival of the dead, I will answer him. It occurred to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he was that friend, so he said: 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' He said: 'What! And do you not believe?' He said: 'Yes, but that my heart may be at ease regarding the friendship.' He said: 'Then take four of the birds, then train them to follow you, then place on every mountain a part of them, then call them, they will come to you flying; and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise.' Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took an eagle, a duck, a peacock, and a rooster, and chopped them into small pieces. Then he placed a part of them on each of the ten mountains that were around him. He placed their beaks between his fingers, then called them by their names, and placed seeds and water near him. Those parts flew from one to another until the bodies were complete. Each body came and joined its neck and head. Ibrahim released their beaks, and they flew. Then they stood, drank from that water, and ate from that seed, and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, you have given us life; may Allah give you life.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'It is Allah who gives life and causes death, and He is Powerful over all things.' Al-Ma'mun said: 'May Allah bless you, O Abu al-Hasan.' The tradition is long; we have taken from it what was needed.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Ja'far (I think it is Muhammad ibn Nu'man) who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (AS) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: And He is Allah in the Heavens and in the Earth. He (AS) replied, 'Thus He is in every place.' I asked, 'By His Essence?' He (AS) responded, 'Woe unto you! Place implies restriction. If you say: He is in a place by His Essence, it necessarily implies restrictions and other than that. However, He is Evident in His Creation. He encompasses whatever He created through His Knowledge, Omnipotence, Omniscience, Reign, and Sovereignty. His Knowledge of whatever is in the Earth is not less than His Knowledge of what is in the Heavens. Nothing is far from Him. His Knowledge, Omnipotence, Reign, Sovereignty, and Omniscience embrace all things.'

My father (RA) narrated, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: Abu Shakir al-Daysani said: 'There is a verse in the Qur'an that is a strength for us.' I said: 'Which one is it?' He said: 'And He is the One in the Heaven is God and in the Earth is God.' I did not know how to answer him, so I went for Hajj and informed Abu 'Abd Allah (AS). He said: 'This is the speech of an evil atheist. When you return to him, say to him: What is your name in Kufah?' And he will say so-and-so. Then say: 'What is your name in Basra?' And he will say the same name. Then say to him: 'Thus is Allah, our Lord. He is God in the Heaven, and God in the Earth, and God in the Seas, and God in every place.' I said: 'So I returned and went to Abu Shakir and informed him.' He said: 'This is transmitted from Hijaz.'

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated from his paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muqatil ibn Sulayman, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: When Musa (peace be upon him) ascended to Mount Sinai and called upon his Lord, the Mighty and High, he said: 'O Lord, show me your treasures.' He replied: 'O Musa, My treasure is that when I intend something, I say to it: Be, and it is.' The compiler of this book says: Among the proofs that Allah, the Mighty and High, is Omnipotent is: since it is established that the Creator made the world, and we do not find that He creates what He is not capable of creating, as evidenced that the seated one cannot walk and the incapable cannot perform an action, it is correct that the One who created it is Omnipotent. If something other than this were possible, then it would be possible for us to fly without the necessary instrument, and for us to perceive without the senses. Since the possibility of the latter is contrary to reason, so is the former. Chapter of Knowledge

Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh al-Qumi al-Faqih informed us, saying: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from 'Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: While al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) was sitting on the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he raised his head and said to him, 'O father, what is the reward for those who visit you after your death?' He replied, 'O my son, whoever comes to me as a visitor after my death will have Paradise; and whoever comes to your father as a visitor after his death will have Paradise; and whoever comes to your brother as a visitor after his death will have Paradise; and whoever comes to you as a visitor after your death will have Paradise.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from al-Mu'alla ibn Abi Shihab, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'What is the reward for one who visits you?' He (peace be upon him and his family) replied, 'O my son! Whoever visits me while I am alive or after I am dead, or visits your father, or visits your brother, or visits you, it becomes a duty upon me to visit them on the Day of Judgment until I clear them of their sins.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who raised it (to the Prophet), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! Whoever visits me during my life or after my death, or visits you during your life or after your death, or visits your two sons during their lives or after their death, I guarantee for him on the Day of Resurrection that I will deliver him from its terrors and hardships until I place him with me in my rank.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me; he said: A number of our companions narrated to me, among them Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-'Amriki ibn Ali, from Yahya (who was the servant of Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him)), from some of our companions, who traced it back to Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever visits me or visits any one of my progeny, I will visit him on the Day of Judgment and I will save him from its terrors.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, al-Hasan, from his father, Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Uthman ibn Isa narrated from al-Mu'alla ibn Abi Shihab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O my father! What is the reward for one who visits you?' He (the Messenger of Allah) replied: 'O my son! Whoever visits me while I am alive or after I am dead, or visits your father, or visits your brother, or visits you, it becomes a duty upon me to visit them on the Day of Judgment and to deliver them from their sins.'

My father and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus, from Abu Wahb al-Basri, who said: I entered Madinah and went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have come to you but I have not visited the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him).' He said, 'How terrible what you have done! If you were not from our Shia, I would not have even looked at you. Do you not visit the one whom Allah, the Exalted, visits with the angels, and the prophets visit with the believers?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I did not know this.' He said, 'Then know that the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) is superior in the sight of Allah than all of the Imams, and he has the reward of their deeds, and they are elevated according to the measure of their deeds.'

‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Isā, from al-Mu‘allā ibn Abī Shihāb, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Ḥasan asked the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family), “O father! What is the reward for those who come to your Ziyārah?” He replied, “O my son! Whoever came to my Ziyārah while I was alive or after my death, or came to the Ziyārah of your father, it will be an obligation upon Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, that I go to their Ziyārah on the Day of Judgment, and I will deliver them from their sins.”

My scholars narrated to me from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi, from Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Whoever visits the grave of my father, for him is Paradise.

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Dāwūd Al-Ṣarmī, from Abā Ja’far the Second (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Whoever visits the grave of my father, for him is Paradise.

My father narrated to me from Sa'd, from Ibrahim ibn Rayyan, who said: Yahya ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni narrated to me, who said: Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Qutrub narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said: His son passed by him while he was a young lad, and his sons were gathered around him. He said: 'This son of mine will die in a land of exile. Whoever visits him, submitting to his command and knowing his right, will be with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, like the martyrs of Badr.'

My father and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim from Hamdan ibn Ishaq who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — or it was narrated to me from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — the doubt is from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Tus, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.' He said: So I performed Hajj after the visitation, and I met Ayyub ibn Nuh. He said to me: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Tus, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed, and He will build for him a pulpit beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and 'Ali (peace be upon him), until Allah finishes the reckoning of the creatures.' So I saw Ayyub ibn Nuh after that, and he had visited, and he said: 'I have come seeking the pulpit!'

My father, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ali ibn al-Husayn all narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Husayn ibn Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the Hajj of Islam (obligatory Hajj), entering with Tamattu' (combining 'Umrah and Hajj). Allah helped him complete his Hajj and 'Umrah. Then he went to Madinah and said Salam to the Messenger of Allah. Then he came to you, acknowledging your right, knowing that you are Allah's proof upon His creation and the door through which one is led, and said Salam to you. Then he went to Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said Salam to him. Then he went to Baghdad and said Salam to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). Then he returned to his country. When the time for Hajj came, Allah granted him what he needed to perform Hajj. Which is better for this man who has performed the Hajj of Islam: to return and perform Hajj again, or to go to Khurasan to your father, Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), and say Salam to him? He (peace be upon him) said: Rather, it is better to go to Khurasan and say Salam to Abu al-Hasan. And let that be in the month of Rajab. But it is not appropriate for them to do this now, for there is fear for us and for you from the Sultan, and it angers him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: I read in the book of Abi al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Tell my Shia that my Ziyarah is equal in the sight of Allah to one thousand Hajj.' He said, so I asked Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'One thousand Hajj?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, and one million Hajj for whoever visits him while knowing his rights.'

My father, and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh narrated to me from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Zayd al-Narsi, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever performs the Ziyarah of this son of mine – and he pointed to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) – will have Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub and Ali ibn al-Husayn and others narrated to me from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, is the Ziyarah of al-Rida better or the Ziyarah of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)?' He replied: 'The Ziyarah of my father is better. And that is because Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) is visited by all people, but my father is visited only by the special ones from among the Shia.'

And from them, may Allah have mercy on them, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Hamdan ibn Ishaq, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or a man narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — the doubt is from 'Ali — saying, and he mentioned like the hadith of Ayub ibn Nuḥ, the hadith of the pulpit.

Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Qurashi al-Kufi narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Razi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) say: Whoever is not enabled to visit us, let him visit the righteous of our followers; the reward of our visitation is recorded for him. And whoever is not able to connect with us, let him connect with the righteous of our followers; the reward of our connection is recorded for him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Muhammad ibn 'from Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Mihran, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, who said: I heard Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: Whoever is unable to connect with us, let him connect with our righteous followers; the reward for connecting with us is registered for him. And whoever is unable to perform Ziyarah (visitation) to us, let him perform Ziyarah to our righteous followers; the reward for our Ziyarah is registered for him.

My father and Muḥammad ibn Ya‘qūb and the group of my scholars (may God have mercy on them) narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: I was in Fayd, so I walked with ‘Alī ibn Bilāl to the grave of Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl ibn Bazī‘. He said to me: ‘Alī ibn Bilāl said to me: The owner of this grave narrated to me from Imam Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of his believing brother, then places his hand on the grave, and recites “Innā Anzalnāh” seven times, will be safe on the Day of Great Terror.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Matt al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran, who said: I was in Fayd when Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Bilal said, 'Let us go to the grave of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazī'. So we went to his grave, and Muhammad ibn 'Ali said: The owner of this grave narrated to me from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), that he said: Whoever visits the grave of his believing brother, faces the Qiblah, places his hand on the grave, and recites 'Innā Anzalnāh' seven times, will be safe from the Great Terror.

And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Matt al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from ‘Ali ibn Ismā‘īl, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr, from Abān, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), ‘How should I place my hand on the graves of the believers?’ He faced the Qiblah, pointed toward the earth with his hand, and then placed his hand on it.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn 'Imran, from 'Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to go out in the presence of a group of people from his companions every Thursday evening to the Baqi' of the Medinans, and he would say three times: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the dwellings,' and three times: 'May Allah have mercy on you.' Then he would turn to his companions and say, 'These are better than you.' So they would say, 'O Messenger of Allah, why? They believed and we believed, and they fought and we fought.' He would say, 'Indeed, these believed and did not mix their faith with oppression, and they passed away upon that [and I am a witness to that for them. However, you will remain after me and I do not know what you will instigate after me.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said: 'Ali, the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), entered a graveyard with his companions and called out: O people of the dust! O people of loneliness! O people of quietness! O people of stillness! As for the news we have, as for your wealth, it has been distributed, and your women have been remarried, and your houses have been occupied. So what is the news with you? Then he turned to his companions and said: By Allah, if they were permitted to speak, they would have said, 'No provision is like piety. The best provision is piety.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Does the believer know who visits his grave?' He replied, 'Yes, and he remains comforted by them as long as they are with him. But when they rise and depart from his grave, loneliness enters him upon their departure from his grave.'

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), “How should I say Salām to the people of the graves?” He replied: Yes, you say: “Salām upon the people of the dwellings from among the believers and the Muslims. You have preceded us and we shall join you, In-Shā`allāh.” My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to me from Ḥusain ibn Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said: He asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), and he mentioned the like of it.

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Amr ibn Abī al-Miqdām, from his father, who said: I passed by al-Baqī‘ with Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him), and we walked by the grave of a man from among the Shia of Kūfah. I said to Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is the grave of one of the Shia.' He stopped by it and said: 'O Allāh! Have mercy on his isolation; connect with him in his loneliness; keep him company in his desolation; make him feel safe in his fear; descend Your Mercy on him in a way that he will not need the mercy of others; and join him with those whom he loved.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ al-Madāʾinī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'How should one say salām to the people of the graves?' He replied: 'Say: Peace be upon the people of the dwellings, from among the believers and the Muslims. May Allah have mercy on those of you who preceded us and those who will follow, and we shall join you, if Allah wills.' Al-Barqī also narrated it from his father, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ al-Madāʾinī, who said: 'I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him),' and mentioned a similar narration.

I found in some books that Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from al-Mufaḍḍal [al-Fuḍayl], who said: If someone recites “Innā Anzalnāh” seven times next to the grave of a believer, Allāh will send an angel to that grave who will worship Allāh next to it. The rewards for this worship will be registered for the one who is dead and (also) for him (the person who came to visit the grave of the believer). When this believer will be resurrected, he will not undergo any terror without Allāh removing it from him through the angel who was dedicated to his grave, and he will enter Paradise in the company of that angel. He added, “(When you go to the graves of the believers), recite (the chapter of) Al-Ḥamd one time, (the chapter of) Innā Anzalnāh seven times, then recite the Mu’awwadhatayn, (the chapter of) Qul Huwallāhu Aḥad, and Ayatul Kursī, each three times.”

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would pass by the graves of a group of believers, he would say: 'Peace be upon you from the dwellings of a believing people, and indeed we, if Allah wills, shall be joining you.'

And from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ibn ‘Ajlān, who said: Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him) stood by the grave of a man and said: O Allāh! Connect with him in his loneliness; keep him company in his desolation; and descend Your Mercy on him in a way that he will not need the mercy of others.

And Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja‘far al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abū ‘Abdillāh al-Barqī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī al-Washshā, from ‘Alī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'How should we say salām to the people of the graves?' He replied: 'Yes, you say: Peace be upon the people of the dwellings, from among the believers and the believing women, and the Muslims and the Muslim women. You are forerunners for us, and we shall follow you, if God wills.'

My father and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and others narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khallid, from his father, from Harun ibn Jahm, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: Al-'Ali, the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), passed by the graves and stood in the thoroughfare. Then he said to his right: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the graves, who have moved from palaces. You have preceded us and we are your followers, and indeed, if God wills, we shall join you.' Then he turned to his left and said: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the graves,' repeating the same statement until the end.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from someone whose name he mentioned, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One of you goes out to the graves and offers salutation, saying: 'Peace be upon the people of the graves, peace be upon those who are in them from among the believers and the Muslims. You have preceded us and we are following you, and indeed we shall join you. And indeed we are Allah's and indeed to Him we shall return. O people of the graves, after having dwelt in palaces! O people of the graves, after having enjoyed blessings and joy! You have gone to the graves. O people of the graves, how did you find the taste of death?' Then he says: 'Woe to whoever has gone to the Fire.' Then he sheds his tears and departs.

And from him, through his chain, from Al-Barqi, who said: Some of our companions narrated to us from 'Abbas ibn 'Amir Al-Qasbani, from Yaqtin, who said: Rabi' ibn Muhammad Al-Musli informed us: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) would say, when he entered the graveyard: Peace be upon the people of Paradise.

‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Sa’d ibn Sa’d, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Ziyārah of Fāṭimah, daughter of Mūsā (peace be upon her). He said: ‘Whoever goes to her Ziyārah, for him is Paradise.’

My father, my brother, and the group narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, and from others, from ‘Amraki ibn ‘Ali Al-Būfaki, from someone whose name he mentioned, who said: The son of Riďā (Imam Jawād (a.s.)) said: Those who go to the Ziyārah of my aunt in Qum will be rewarded with Paradise.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Isa ibn Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali (peace be upon him), who said: Water is the master of drinks in this world and the Hereafter. And four rivers in this world are from Paradise: the Euphrates, the Nile, the Sayhan, and the Jayhan. The Euphrates is water, the Nile is honey, the Sayhan is wine, and the Jayhan is milk.

And from him, from Abu Jamilah, from Sulayman ibn Harun, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever drinks from the water of the Euphrates and is moistened with it, he is among those who love us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

And by his chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: If the distance between us and the Euphrates were this much and this much (a specific distance mentioned), we would go to it and seek cure with it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Sulayman ibn Harun al-Ijli, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'I do not think that anyone whose mouth is opened with water from the Euphrates will not love us, the Ahl al-Bayt.' Then he asked me: 'What is the distance between you and the water of the Euphrates?' I informed him, and he said: 'If I were there, I would love to go to it at the two ends of the day.'

And ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from ‘Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Nahik, from Abu ‘Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: “And We gave them both refuge on a mound, where there was rest and security, watered by a spring.” He said, “The mound is Najaf of Kufah, and the spring is the Euphrates.”

And ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Umar, from his father, from his grandfather, from ‘Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Euphrates is the master of the waters in this world and in the Hereafter.

And Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah narrated to me from his father 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from his father, from someone who narrated to him, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: 'An angel descends every night carrying three mithqals of musk from the musk of Paradise, and casts them into the Euphrates. There is no river in the East or in the West [in the East and in the West] greater in blessing than it.'

And ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Uthmān, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Drops fall into the Euphrates every day from Paradise.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said: When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in Kufah during the time of Abi al-Abbas, he came on his mount wearing his traveling clothes until he stopped on the bridge of Kufah. Then he said to his servant, 'Give me water.' So he took a jug from the water-seller, scooped water for him with it, and gave it to him. He drank, and the water flowed from the corners of his mouth, onto his beard, and onto his clothes. Then he asked for more, and he gave him more. He praised Allah and said: 'What a great blessing is this river of water! Verily, every day seven drops fall into it from Paradise. If people knew the blessing in it, they would pitch their tents on its banks. If it were not for what enters it from the sinners, no one with an ailment would immerse himself in it without being cured.'

My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Ḥusain ibn ‘Uthmān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), and Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him). He said: I do not foresee any (newborn baby) whose mouth is opened with water from the Euphrates River to be anything other than from among our Shia. Ibn Abī ‘Umayr said: And I do not know him except as Ibn Sīnān, except that he had narrated it to me. And Ibn Abī ‘Umayr narrated from some of our companions who said: Two spouts flow from Paradise into the Euphrates.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi, who said: I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah sends down an angel every night with him three mithqals of the musk of Paradise, and he drops them in this Euphrates of yours. And there is no river in the east of the earth nor in its west that is greater in blessing than it.

‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Tha’labah ibn Maymūn, from Sulaymān ibn Hārūn, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: I do not foresee any (newborn baby) whose mouth is opened with the water of the Euphrates River to be anything other than from among those who love us, the Ahlul Bayt.

My father narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mattīl, from ‘Imrān ibn Mūsā, from Abū ‘Abdillāh al-Jāmūrānī al-Rāzī, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Alī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Sayf ibn ‘Amīrah, from Sandal, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: No one drinks from the water of the Euphrates and is given a sweetening (of the palate) with it when born, except that he loves us, because the Euphrates is a believing river.

And through his chain, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Two believing rivers and two disbelieving rivers. The two disbelieving rivers are the Balkh River and the Tigris, and the two believing rivers are the Nile of Egypt and the Euphrates. Therefore, open the mouths of your children with the water of the Euphrates.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, and 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, and Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Attar, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn Al-Hakam and others, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from his brother Nuh, from Al-Ajlah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from 'Abd al-'Aziz, from 'Ali (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say, 'O 'Ali! These two boys — meaning Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them) — have caused me to forget about loving anyone else after them forever. Verily, my Lord commanded me to love them and to love those who love them.'

My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from someone who narrated to him, from Sufyān Al-Jarīfyān Al-Jarīri, from his father, from Abī Rāfi’, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abī Dhar Al-Ghifāri, who said: The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) ordered me to love Ḥasan and Ḥusain (a.s.). Therefore, I love them and I love those who love them because of the Messenger of Allāh’s love for (Ḥasan and Ḥusain (a.s.)).

My father narrated to me from ‘Abdillābdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, who said: He narrated to me from a man whose name I forgot from our companions, from ‘Ubaydillāh ibn Mūsā, from Muhalhal Al-‘Abdi, from Abī Hārūn Al-‘Abdi, from Rabī’ah Al-Sa’di, from Abī Dhar Al-Ghifāri who said: I saw the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) kiss Ḥasan and Ḥusain (a.s.) and say: The fire will not touch the face of those who are sincere in their love for Ḥasan and Ḥusain (a.s.) and their progeny, even if their sins are equal to the number of (grains of) sand, unless they have committed a sin that expels them from the faith.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from one whom he mentioned, from Ali ibn 'Abis, from al-Hajjal, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abdullah ibn Salamah, from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'Whoever loves me, let him love these two sons of mine, for indeed Allah has ordered me to love them.'

My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Bazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever wishes to hold fast to the firmest handhold of Allah, which Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book, should love [or be loyal to] Ali ibn Abi Talib, and al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), for indeed Allah loves them from above His Throne.'

And from him, and from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, and from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from a man, from Abbas ibn al-Walid, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever hates Hasan and Husayn will come on the Day of Judgment with no flesh on his face, and my intercession will not reach him.'

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Abī al-Magh rā’, from Abī Basīr, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) said, 'Women are the coolness of my eyes, and my two flowers are al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon them).'

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from someone whose name he mentioned, from ‘Ali ibn ‘Abbās, from Minhāl ibn ‘Amr, and from Asbagh, from Zādhān, who said: I heard ‘Ali ibn Abī Ťālib (peace be upon him) in al-Raḥbah say: “Ḥasan and Ḥusain are the two flowers (riḥānatā) of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him).”

A group of my scholars, including my father, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ali ibn al-Husayn, all narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd al-Yaqṭīnī, from Abī 'Abdillāh Zakariyyā al-Mu'min, from Abī Muskān, from Zayd, the freedman of Ibn Hubayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said: Hold on to the belt of this 'Anza' (the empty one), for he is the greatest Truthful One (Ṣiddīq Akbar) and the guide for whoever follows him. Whoever precedes him has apostatized from the religion of Allah. Whoever abandons him, Allah will destroy him. Whoever adheres to him has adhered to Allah [adhered to the Cord of Allah]. Whoever accepts his Wilayah, Allah guides him; and whoever neglects his Wilayah, Allah leads him astray. From him are the two chiefs of my nation, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and they are my sons. From the descendants of al-Ḥusayn are the guided Imams and the Qā'im al-Mahdī. Therefore, love them and be loyal to them, and do not take their enemies as allies instead of them, for if you do, the wrath of your Lord will befall you and humiliation in the worldly life. And he who forges a lie has certainly failed.

Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Za'farani narrated to me in Ray, saying: Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khaytham from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid from Ya'la ibn Murrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said: Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn. Allah loves those who love Husayn. Husayn is a chief (seed/offspring) from among the chiefs.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from Abi Sa'id Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Zakariyya Al-'Adwi Al-Basri, who said: 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad Al-Bursi narrated to us, Wahb narrated to us from 'Abdillah ibn 'Uthman from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid from Ya'la Al-'Amiri, who said: I left the presence of the Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) to go to a meal to which I had been invited. He found Al-Husayn (a.s.) playing with the children. The Prophet (s.a.a.w.) faced him in front of the people, then spread his arms. The boy ran here and there, and the Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) amused him until he caught him. He placed one hand under his chin and the other behind his neck, placed his mouth on his mouth, and kissed him. Then he said: 'Al-Husayn is from me and I am from Al-Husayn. Allah loves those who love Al-Husayn. Al-Husayn is a chief (sibt) from among the chiefs.'

And from him, from Abi Sa'id, who said: Narrated to us Nadr ibn Ali, who said: Narrated to us Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the hand of Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn and said: 'Whoever loves these two boys and their father and their mother, he will be with me in my rank on the Day of Judgment.'

And from him from Salamah from Abdullah ibn Ahmad from Bakr ibn Salih from Amr ibn Hisham [Hashim] from some of our companions from one of them [one of the two] (peace be upon him) said: When you come to the graves of the Imams in al-Baqi', stand by them and make the Qiblah behind you and the grave before you. Then say: Peace be upon you, O the wise Imams who are rightly guided [the guided ones]; Peace be upon you, O People of Devotion and Piety; Peace be upon you, O the Decisive Proofs upon the people of the world; Peace be upon you, O the Just Custodians of Creation; Peace be upon you, O Chosen Ones; Peace be upon you, O Family of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him); Peace be upon you, O Confidants. I testify that you have conveyed [the message], advised, and remained patient for the sake of Allah; you were belied and insulted, yet you forgave. And I testify that you are the wise, rightly guided Imams [the guided ones], that your obedience is obligatory, and that your word is truth. That you called [people] but were not answered, and commanded but were not obeyed; and that you are the pillars of the religion and the foundations of the earth. You have remained under the gaze of Allah, who transferred you from the backbones of every purified father and moved you from the wombs of the purified mothers. The darkness of ignorance did not defile you, nor did the afflictions of desires share in you. You were blessed and the places of your origin were blessed. The Undisputed Ruler of Religion has bestowed favours upon us through you, and He made you in houses which Allah permitted to be exalted and His name to be remembered therein. And He made our prayers upon you as a mercy for us and an expiation for our sins. When Allah chose you for us and purified our creation by bestowing upon us your guardianship, and we were named by Him for our knowledge of you, acknowledging our verification of you. And this is the position of one who has been excessive and erred, humbled himself, confessed to his crimes, and hoped for sincerity in his standing, and that the Saviour of the ruined would save him from destruction through you. So be my intercessors, for I have come to you as an envoy, while the people of the world have turned away from you, taken Allah's signs as mockery, and arrogantly turned from them. O He who is ever-present, never neglectful; ever-lasting, neve

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn and others narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq al-Ash‘arī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Aṭiyyah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Recite by the grave of ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn whatever you wish.

My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali Al-Washā`, from Aḥmad ibn ‘Ā`idh, from Abī Salamah Sālim ibn Mukram, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: When Fāťimah (peace be upon her) became pregnant with Ḥusain (peace be upon him), Jabra`īl (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) and said, “Verily Fāťimah will give birth to a son who will be killed by your nation after you.” Therefore, Fāťimah (peace be upon her) was averse to her pregnancy while she was carrying Ḥusain (peace be upon him), and she was averse to giving birth to him when she did. Then Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: “Have you ever seen a mother in this world being averse to giving birth to a son?! Her aversion came from knowing that he would be killed.” He said: And about him (Ḥusain) was revealed this verse, “We have enjoined on man to do good to his parents; his mother bears him with aversion, and with aversion she gives birth to him; and bearing him and weaning him takes thirty months.”

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from his brother Ahmad ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from his father, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Jabra'il (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'Peace be upon you, O Muhammad! Shall I give you glad tidings of a son whom your nation will kill after you?' He said, 'I do not need such a son.' He ascended to the heaven, then returned to him for the second time and said to him the same thing. He said, 'I do not need such a son.' He ascended to the heaven, then descended to him for the third time and said the same thing. He said, 'I do not need such a son.' He said, 'Verily your Lord is placing the succession in his progeny.' He said, 'Yes,' or he said that. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rose and entered upon Fatimah (peace be upon her) and said to her, 'Verily Jabra'il (peace be upon him) came to me and gave me glad tidings of a son whom my nation will kill after me.' She said, 'I do not need such a son.' He said to her, 'Verily my Lord is placing the succession in his progeny.' She said, 'Yes, then.' So Allah, the Exalted, revealed at that time this verse: 'His mother bore him with aversion, and with aversion she gave birth to him.' Because of the place of Jabra'il informing her of his killing, so she bore him with aversion because he would be killed, and she gave birth to him with aversion because he would be killed.

My father and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan both narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Fāṭimah (peace be upon her) came to the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) and saw that his eyes were filled with tears. She asked him, 'What is the matter with you?' He replied, 'Jabraʾīl (peace be upon him) informed me that my nation will kill Ḥusayn.' She became extremely grieved and restless. So he informed her of those from her children who would hold authority. This pleased her and relieved her.

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to visit us. Um Ayman had gifted us milk, butter, and dates, so we presented some of it to him. He ate, then stood up to a corner of the house and prayed two rak'ahs. When he was in the final prostration, he cried a severe cry. None of us asked him out of reverence and awe for him. Then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came and sat in his lap and said: 'O Father, you entered our house and we were not pleased by anything as pleased as by your entry. Then you cried a cry that grieved us; what made you cry?' He said: 'O my son, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to me just now and informed me that you will be killed and your places of martyrdom will be scattered.' He said: 'O Father, what is [the reward] for those who visit our graves while they are scattered?' He said: 'O my son, those are groups from my nation who visit you and seek blessings thereby. It is incumbent upon me to visit them on the Day of Resurrection until I deliver them from the terrors of the Hour and from their sins, and Allah will make them dwell in Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim Majilawayh narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi from Ubayd ibn Yahya al-Thawri from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) visited us one day, so we presented food to him. Um Ayman had sent us a platter of dates and a goblet of milk and butter, which we presented to him, and he ate from it. When he finished, I stood up and poured water over the hands of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When he washed his hands, he wiped his face and beard with the moisture of his hands. Then he went to the prayer place in the corner of the house, prayed, and fell into prostration, crying and prolonging his weeping. Then he raised his head, and none of us, the Ahl al-Bayt, dared to ask him about anything. So al-Husayn (peace be upon him) crawled until he climbed onto the thighs of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), took his head to his chest, and placed his chin on the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then he said, 'O Father, what is making you cry?' He said to him, 'O my son, I looked at you today and was pleased with you with a pleasure I had not been pleased with before like it. Then Jibril descended to me and informed me that you will be killed and that your graves will be scattered. So I praised Allah for that and asked for the best for you.' He said to him, 'O Father, then who will visit our graves and attend to them despite their scattering?' He said, 'Groups from my nation, seeking my goodness and kinship ties through that. I will attend to them on the Day of Standing and take them by their arms and save them from its terrors and hardships.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: He narrated to me Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Harizah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was playing in front of him, and he informed him that his nation would kill him. He said: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became restless and said: Shall I not show you the dust on which he will be killed? He said: So what was between the seat of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the place where al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed sank into the ground until the two pieces met. He took some of it, and it was rolled up in faster than a blink of an eye. He returned while saying: Bliss for you, O dust, and bliss for whoever is killed around you. And so did the companion of Sulayman (peace be upon him). He spoke with the Greatest Name of Allah, and what was between Sulayman's bed and the Throne sank from the flat and hilly parts of the earth until the two pieces met, and he lifted the Throne. Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: It seems to me that it came out from under my bed. He said: And it was rolled up in faster than a blink of an eye.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Jibra'il (peace be upon him) announced the news of the killing of al-Husayn to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in the house of Umm Salamah. Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered while Jibra'il was with him. Jibra'il said, 'Verily, your nation will kill him.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Show me from the dust upon which his blood will be shed.' So Jibra'il (peace be upon him) took a handful of that dust, and behold, it was red dust.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Isa, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it. And he added to it: 'It remained with Umm Salamah until she died, may Allah have mercy on her.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Khazzaz, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was in the house of Umm Salamah, and with him was Jibril (peace be upon him). Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered upon them. Jibril said to him, 'Verily, your nation will kill this son of yours. Shall I not show you some of the dust of the earth upon which he will be killed?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' So Jibril (peace be upon him) inclined his hand and took a handful of it, and showed it to the Prophet (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: While al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), Jabra'il (peace be upon him) came to him and said, 'O Muhammad! Do you love him?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Verily, your nation will kill him.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was extremely grieved. Jabra'il said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah! Do you wish [that it pleases you] for me to show you the land on which he will be killed?' He said, 'Yes.' Then the land between the place where the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting and Karbala sank into the ground until the two pieces met like this. Then he brought his two index fingers together. Then Jabra'il picked up some of the dust with his wing and handed it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then it returned faster than a blink of an eye. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to it, 'Blissful is you, O dust, and blissful is he who will be killed on you!'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali Al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abi Khadijah Salim ibn Mukarram Al-Jammal, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Fatimah gave birth to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Jabra'il came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'Your nation will kill Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) after you.' Then he said, 'Shall I not show you some of his dust?' So he struck the ground with his wing and brought forth dust from the land of Karbala and showed it to him, then said, 'This is the dust on which he will be killed.'

My father narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī al-Za‘farānī, who said: Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr al-Aslamī narrated to me, who said: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Anbasah narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Amr, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbās, who said: The angel who came to Muḥammad (peace be upon him) informing him of the killing of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) was Jibra‘īl (peace be upon him), the Trustworthy Spirit, with his wings spread out, crying and screaming. He had carried some of the dust of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), and it emitted a fragrance like musk. The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) said: 'Will my nation achieve salvation when they kill my chick?' Or he said: 'the chick of my daughter.' Jibra‘īl replied: 'Allāh will afflict them with discord, so their hearts will disagree with one another.'

Al-Naqid Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn 'Abdillah ibn 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to me from his father, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ghanawi, from Sulayman, who said: Was there any angel left in the heavens who did not descend to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) to console him regarding his son, al-Husayn (a.s.), and to inform him of Allah's reward for him, and to bring to him his dust, upon which he fell, was slaughtered, killed, wounded, thrown down, and abandoned? The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said: 'O Allah, abandon whoever abandoned him, kill whoever killed him, slaughter whoever slaughtered him, and do not let him enjoy what he sought.' 'Abd al-Rahman said: By Allah, the accursed Yazid was hastened [to his death], and he did not enjoy after his killing what he sought. 'Abd al-Rahman said: And he was taken suddenly; he spent the night drunk and became dead in the morning, changed, as if he were coated with tar. He was taken in grief. And no one remained from those who followed him in his killing or who were in his fighting except that madness, leprosy, or whitening of the skin afflicted him, and that became an inheritance in their progeny.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi al-Razzaz narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Musa ibn Sa'dan al-Hannat, from Abdullah ibn Qasim al-Hadrami, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: And We made known to the Children of Israel in the Book You will certainly make mischief in the land twice. He said: The killing of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) and the stabbing of al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him). And you will certainly become exceedingly arrogant The killing of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him). So when the promise of the first of the two comes He said: When the avenging of the blood of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) comes We sent over you servants of Ours, of great prowess, so they invaded the very inmost parts of your houses A group whom Allah sends before the rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him); they do not leave a single one of the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) except that they burn him. And it was a promise to be fulfilled

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He recited this verse: 'Verily, We will help Our messengers and those who believe in this world and on the Day the witnesses shall stand forth.' He said: 'Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) is among them, yet he has not been helped yet.' Then he said: 'By Allah, the killers of Husayn (peace be upon him) have been killed, but his blood has not been avenged yet.'

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: 'And when the buried female infant is asked, for what sin was she killed?' He said: 'It was revealed about Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hakim al-Hannat, from Durays, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Permission (to fight) has been given to those who are fought against because they have been oppressed, and indeed Allah is competent to support them.' He said: 'It is Ali, al- Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them).'

And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-‘Abbās ibn Ma’rūf, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from a man who said: I asked about Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of the Exalted: 'And whosoever is killed unjustly, then We have indeed given his heir an authority, but let him not exceed the limits in killing, verily he is helped.' He (peace be upon him) said: This is about the Qā’im of the family of Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family). He rises and kills avenging the blood of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him). Even if he kills the people of the earth, he will not have exceeded the limits. And His saying: 'but let him not exceed the limits in killing' means that he will not do anything that constitutes excess. Then Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: I swear to Allāh that he will kill the descendants of the killers of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) for the deeds of their fathers.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying, Exalted and Blessed is He: 'So there is no hostility except against the oppressors.' He said: 'The children of the killers of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, similarly.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abu Abdillah, from al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And We conveyed to the Children of Israel in the Book that you will surely cause corruption in the land twice,' he said: The killing of Ali and the stabbing of al-Hasan. And 'And you will surely be arrogant with great arrogance,' he said: The killing of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad 'Isa, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, and Ya'qub ibn Yazid, all from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Ismail, about whom Allah, the Exalted, said in His Book: 'And mention in the Book Ismail. Indeed, he was truthful in his promise, and he was a messenger, and a prophet' — this was not Ismail, the son of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He was a prophet among the prophets whom Allah sent to his people. They captured him and skinned the scalp of his head and his face. An angel came to him from Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and said, 'Indeed, Allah has sent me to you, so order me to do whatever you wish.' He said to me, 'I am an example for what will be done to al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from both of them together, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, there was for Allah a Messenger who was a Prophet, upon whom his people gained power, so they skinned the skin of his face and the fur (scalp) of his head. Then a Messenger came to him from the Lord of the Worlds and said to him: Your Lord conveys His greetings to you and says, 'I have seen what was done to you,' and He has ordered me to obey you, so order me to do whatever you wish. He replied, 'I will take the example of al-Husain (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from his father, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-'Ijli, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! Inform me about Ismail, whom Allah mentioned in His Book, where He says: "And mention in the Book Ismail. Indeed, he was truthful in his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet." Is this Ismail the son of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)? For the people claim that it is Ismail, the son of Ibrahim.' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Indeed, Ismail died before Ibrahim, and indeed Ibrahim was the decisive proof of Allah for the entire period, standing as the owner of a Shariah (law). So to whom was Ismail sent, then?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Then who was it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is Ismail, son of Hizqil, the prophet (peace be upon him). Allah sent him to his people, but they belied him, killed him, and skinned his face.' So Allah became angry on his behalf against them, and He sent to him Asfata'il, the Angel of Chastisement. He said to him: 'O Ismail! I am Asfata'il, the Angel of Chastisement. The Lord of Glory has sent me to you to torment your nation with various kinds of chastisement, if you wish.' Ismail said to him: 'I have no need for that.' So Allah revealed to him: 'What is your need, O Ismail?' He said: 'O Lord! You took the covenant for Yourself as Lord, for Muhammad as Prophet, and for his successors as Guardianship. And You informed the best of Your creation about what his nation would do to al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) after his prophet.' And You promised al-Husayn (peace be upon him) that You would send him back to the world so that he may take revenge upon himself against those who did that to him. So my need from You, O Lord, is that You send me back to the world so that I may take revenge upon those who did that to me, just as You send back al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So Allah promised Ismail, son of Hizqil, that, and he will return with al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Isma'il about whom Allah the Exalted said in His Book, 'And mention in the Book Isma'il. Indeed, he was true to his promise,' was captured, and the skin of his face and head was flayed. Then an angel came to him and said, 'Indeed, Allah has sent me to you, so order me to do whatever you wish.' He said, 'I follow the example of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd Al-Yaqťīni, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id Al-Qammāť, from Ibn Abi Ya'fūr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in the house of Fatimah (peace be upon her), with Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) sitting on his lap. Suddenly, he wept and fell in prostration. Then he said: 'O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad! Indeed, the Most High, the Most Exalted, appeared to me in your house at this hour in the most beautiful form and appearance, and said to me: 'O Muhammad, do you love Al-Husayn?' I replied, 'Yes, he is the coolness of my eye, my flower, the fruit of my heart, and the skin between my two eyes.' He said to me, O Muhammad, while placing His hand on the head of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Blessed is the newborn upon whom have come My blessings, My prayers, My mercy, and My pleasure. And upon him are My curse, My wrath, My punishment, My disgrace, and My chastisement, for whoever kills him, opposes him, contends with him, and competes with him. Indeed, he is the Master of Martyrs from the first to the last, in this world and the Hereafter.' And he mentioned the hadith.

And Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn 'Ali al-Naqid narrated to me, saying: Abu Harun al-'Issi [al-'Absi] narrated to me from Abu al-Ashhab Ja'far ibn Hanan [Hayyan], from Khalid al-Raba'i, who said: He narrated to me from someone who heard Ka'b saying: The first person to curse the killer of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) was Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful; he cursed him and ordered his children to do so, and took a covenant and pledge from them. Then Musa ibn 'Imran cursed him and ordered his nation to do so. Then Dawud cursed him and ordered the Children of Israel to do so. Then 'Isa cursed him and frequently said: 'O Children of Israel! Curse his killer, and if you meet his days, do not sit away from him, for the martyr with him is like the martyr with the prophets, facing forward not turning back [facing forward not turning back]. And it is as if I am looking at his place, and no prophet but that he visited Karbala and stood upon it and said: 'Verily you are a place full of goodness; in you will be buried the shining moon.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Abdillah Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Ayyub ibn Abd al-Rahman and Zayd ibn al-Hasan Abu al-Hasan and 'Abbād, all from Sa'd al-Iskaf, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is pleased to live my life and die my death and enter the Garden of Eden, let him hold fast to the branch that my Lord planted with His own hand; let him follow 'Ali and the successors after him and submit to their virtues, for they are the guided ones with whom Allah is pleased. Allah has given them my understanding and my knowledge, and they are my progeny from my flesh and my blood. I complain to Allah about their enemies from among my nation, those who deny their virtues and cut off my tie to them. By Allah, they will kill my son, and may Allah exclude them from my intercession.'

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Ali ibn Shajarah, from Salām Al-Ju’fi, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad Al-San’āni, from Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) would draw Ḥusain (peace be upon him) to himself whenever Ḥusain (peace be upon him) would enter. Then he would tell the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) to hold him, after which he would fall on him, kissing him and crying. So (Ḥusain) asked, 'O father! Why are you crying?' He replied, 'O my son! I am kissing the place of the swords from you.' (Ḥusain) said, 'O father! And I will be killed?' He replied, 'Yes, by Allāh, and your father and your brother and you.' (Ḥusain) said, 'O father! Then our places of martyrdom will be far apart.' He replied, 'Yes, O my son.' (Ḥusain) said, 'So who from your nation will come to our Ziyārah?' He replied, 'No one but the truthful ones from my nation will come to my Ziyārah, to the Ziyārah of your father, to the Ziyārah of your brother, or to your Ziyārah.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from Abi Sa'id Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Zakariyya Al-'Adwi Al-Basri, who said: 'Amr ibn Mukhtar narrated to us, who said: Isḥaq ibn Bishr narrated to us from Al-Qawwam, the freedman of Quraysh, who said: I heard my master 'Amr ibn Hubayrah say: I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn on his lap. He would kiss one, then the other, and say to Al-Husayn: 'Woe to those who will kill you.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him mercy) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammāt, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in the house of Fatimah, with al-Husain sitting on his lap, he began to cry and fell into prostration. Then he said: O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad! Indeed, the Most High, the Most Exalted, appeared to me in this house of yours at this hour in the most beautiful form and appearance. He said to me: O Muhammad, do you love al-Husain? I said: O my Lord, he is the coolness of my eyes, my flower, the fruit of my heart, and the skin between my two eyes. He said to me, O Muhammad, while placing His hand on the head of al-Husain (peace be upon him): Blessed is the newborn upon whom are My blessings, My prayers, My mercy, My pleasure, My blame, My curse, My wrath, My punishment, My disgrace, and My chastisement upon those who kill him, oppose him, contend with him, and compete with him. Indeed, he is the Master of Martyrs from the first to the last in this world and the Hereafter, and the Master of the Youth of Paradise from among all creation. His father is better and more excellent than he is. Convey My greetings to him and give him glad tidings that he is the flag of guidance, the beacon of My friends, My trustee, My witness over My creation, the keeper of My knowledge, and My proof upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earths, and the two weights, the Jinn and the humans.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Kufi, from Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Ansari, who said: Mus'ab narrated to me from Jabir, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is pleased to live my life and die my death and enter my Paradise—the Garden of Eden, whose trees my Lord planted with His own hand—should follow 'Ali, recognize his merit and that of the successors after him, and dissociate from my enemies. Allah has given them my understanding and my knowledge. They are my progeny, from my flesh and blood. I complain to my Lord about their enemies from among my nation, those who deny their virtues and cut off the tie of kinship with them. By Allah, my son will be killed, and then they will not attain my intercession.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Qurashi narrated to me; he said: My uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah from Abu Dawud al-Sab'i from Abu Abdillah al-Jadali who said: I entered upon the Commander of the Believers, and al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was beside him. He tapped the shoulder of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with his hand and said, 'This one will be killed and no one will help him.' I said, 'O Commander of the Believers! By Allah, that would be a miserable life.' He said, 'Verily it will happen.' And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, through his chain, similarly.

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Naṣr ibn Muzāḥim, from ‘Umar ibn Sa‘d [‘Amr ibn Sa‘īd, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from Hāni’ ibn Hāni’, from ‘Alī (peace be upon him) He said: ‘Verily al-Ḥusayn will be killed a killing, and indeed I know the dust of the land on which he will be killed, which is close to the two rivers.’

And from them (the two), from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said to al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'If you came to Mecca and stayed in the Haram (sanctuary).' Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'We will not make it permissible (by remaining in it) and it will not be made permissible by us (being killed in it). And to be killed on the mound of A'far is more beloved to me than to be killed in it.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) left Mecca one day before the Tarwiyah (the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah). So 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr accompanied him and said, 'O Abu Abdillah! The season of Hajj has arrived, yet you leave it and go to Iraq?' He replied, 'O son of al-Zubayr! To be buried by the shore of the Euphrates is more beloved to me than to be buried in the courtyard of the Ka'bah.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to his companions on the day they were killed: 'I testify that permission has been granted for your killing, so fear Allah and be patient.' Also narrated to me is Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', similarly.

And Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halabi, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) led his companions in the morning prayer, then turned to them and said, 'Verily, Allah has granted permission for your killing, so upon you is patience.'
