Al-Hasan narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said: He said: I swear to He toward whom the Throne was ascended, that your father mentioned to me the companions of al-Husayn, neither adding a man nor reducing a man. This nation will transgress against them just as the Children of Israel transgressed on the Sabbath. And he was killed on the Sabbath, on the day of 'Ashura.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Halabi, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) led his companions in prayer on the day they were martyred, then he said: 'I testify that permission has been granted for your killing, O people! So fear Allah and be patient.'

Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ali al-Naqid narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Aslami narrated to me from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: I heard Abu Dharr, and at that time Uthman had expelled him to al-Rabadhah, so the people said to him: O Abu Dharr! Rejoice, for this is little in the way of Allah, the Exalted. He said: How insignificant this is (in the way of Allah)! But how will you be when al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) is killed – or he said slaughtered – in such a terrible way? By Allah, no killing will be greater than his killing in Islam after the killing of the Caliph. And indeed Allah will unsheathe His sword against this nation and will never sheathe it again, and He will send an avenger [a standing one] from his progeny who will take revenge upon the people. And if you knew what would befall the inhabitants of the seas, the dwellers of the mountains in the thickets and hills, and the people of the sky from his killing, you would cry by Allah until your souls expire. And there is no sky through which the soul of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) passes but seventy thousand angels are alarmed for him; they stand up in a standing in which their joints tremble until the Day of Judgment. And there is no cloud that passes, thundering and lightninging, but it curses his killer. And there is no day but his soul is presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and they meet one another.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abd al-Samin, who narrated that he raised it to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was delivering a sermon to the people while saying, 'Ask me before you lose me! By Allah, you will not ask me about anything that has passed or anything that will occur, except that I will inform you of it.' He said, 'So Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas stood up to him and said, 'O Commander of the Believers! Inform me, how many hairs are on my head and in my beard?' He said to him, 'By Allah, you have asked me about a matter my beloved, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), informed me of: that you would ask me about it. And there is not a single hair on your head or in your beard except that a devil is seated at its root. And there is a lamb in your house that will kill my son, Husayn.' (Asbagh added), 'And Umar was playing at that time in front of his father.'

A group of my scholars, among them 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, narrated to me from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, all from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Abi Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Shihab ibn 'Abd Rabbih, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: When al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) ascended 'Aqabat al-Batn, he said to his companions, 'I see nothing for myself but being killed.' They said, 'Why is that, O Aba 'Abdillah?' He said, 'A vision I saw in my sleep.' They said, 'What is it?' He said, 'I saw dogs biting me, and the harshest of them upon me was a spotted dog.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my teachers narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Zayyat from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Husayn ibn Ali wrote from Mecca to Muhammad ibn Ali: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Husayn ibn Ali to Muhammad ibn Ali and those with him from the Banu Hashim: As for what follows, then whoever joins me will be martyred, and whoever does not join me will not achieve victory. And peace.

Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ali al-Naqid narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Balkhi [al-Sulami] narrated to me, and Abu al-Husayn said to me, and my uncle informed me from his father from Abu Nasr from a man from the people of Bayt al-Maqdis, that he said: By Allah, we, the people of Bayt al-Maqdis and its suburbs, knew of the killing of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) on the eve of the day he was killed. I asked, 'How did you know?' He replied: 'We did not lift a stone, a clod of earth, or a rock without seeing fresh, boiling blood beneath it. And the walls turned red like blood. It rained fresh blood for three days. And we heard a caller crying out in the depth of the night, saying: Does the nation that killed Husayn hope for the intercession of his grandfather on the Day of Reckoning? Far be it from Allah! You will not attain certainty. The intercession of Ahmad and Abu Turab. You killed the best of those who rode beasts, and the best of the gray-haired and the youth. And the sun was eclipsed for three days, then it cleared from it, and the stars became interlocked. And when it was the next day, we were shaken by his killing, and not much time had passed until the news of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came to us.'

Abul Ḥusain Aḥmad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Ali Al-Nāqid narrated to me through his Isnād, he said: ‘Umar ibn Sa’d said: Abū Ma’shar narrated to me from Al-Zuhri, When Ḥusain (a.s.) was killed, no stone was left in Bayt Al-Maqdis without finding fresh blood under it.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad, from Kulayb ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The killer of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was conceived illegitimately, and the killer of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was also conceived illegitimately. The sky did not weep for anyone except for them. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, both, narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from his father, from al-Hasan, from Fudalah ibn Ayyub, from Kulayb ibn Mu'awiya al-Asadi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is a position in Hellfire that no one from among the people deserves, except the killer of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him).

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abd al-Khalik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The killer of Husayn (peace be upon him) was a son of fornication, and the killer of Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him) was a son of fornication.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muthanna, from Sadir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: Verily, Allah has placed the killing of the children of the prophets from the previous nations in the hands of those who were conceived illegitimately.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The one who killed al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was a son of fornication, and the one who killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him) was a son of fornication.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Pharaoh: 'Let me kill Moses.' He was asked, 'Who prevented him?' He said, 'It was due to his legitimacy, because the prophets and the decisive proofs are only killed by the sons of fornication and the adulteresses.' And my father narrated to me, and the group of my scholars, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, with this hadith [with these hadiths].

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Ibn Muskān, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: the killer of Al-Husayn ibn Ali is a son of fornication.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: They do not kill the prophets or the descendants of the prophets except the sons of fornication.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abdillah ibn Ali al-Hasani, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-'Amri, from al-Husayn ibn Shaddad al-Ju'fi, from Jabir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The prophets and the sons of the prophets are not killed except by the son of fornication."

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Razzaz Al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Yahya ibn Ma'mar al-Attar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Mankind, Jinn, birds, and beasts wept over al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) until their tears flowed profusely. And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, all of them, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, through his chain, similarly.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Dāwūd, from Sa‘īd ibn ‘Umar al-Jullāb, from al-Ḥārith al-A‘war, who said: ‘Ali (peace be upon him) said: May I sacrifice my father and mother for al-Ḥusayn, the one killed on the outskirts of Kūfah. By Allah, it is as if I can see the wild beasts stretching their necks towards his grave, from various kinds of beasts, weeping for him and mourning him throughout the night until dawn. When this happens, beware of neglect (him/his grave).

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Qurashī al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn ‘Uthmān, from ‘Abd al-Jabbār al-Nahāwandī, from Abī Sa‘īd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah, and Yūnus ibn Ḍabyān, and Abī Salamah al-Sarrāj, and al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ‘Umar, all of them said: We heard Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: Verily, when Abū ‘Abdillāh, al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him), passed away, the seven heavens, the seven earths, and what is within them, and what is between them, and those that circulate around them, and Paradise, and Hell, and everything our Lord created, both that which is seen and that which is unseen, wept over him.

And my father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ubaydillah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Nahawandi, from Abi Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr, from Yunus and Abi Salamah al-Sarraj and al-Mufaḍḍal ibn 'Umar, who said: We heard Aba 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: When al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) died, all that Allah created wept for him except for three things: Basra, Damascus, and the family of 'Uthman.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr, who said: I, Yūnus ibn Żabyān, al-Mufaďďal ibn 'Umar, and Abū Salamah al-Sarrāj were sitting with Abī 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him). Yūnus was the speaker among us, and he was the eldest in age. He narrated a long hadith. He said: Then Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, when Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) passed away, the seven heavens and the seven earths, and what is within them and between them, and what moves in Paradise and Hell from the creation of our Lord, and what is seen and what is not seen, wept for him.' And they wept for Abū 'Abdillāh except for three things that did not weep for him. I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, what are these three things?' He said: 'Basra did not weep for him, nor Damascus, nor the family of 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān.' And he mentioned the hadith.

My father and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb and al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, all from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: When you enter the city, perform ritual bath before entering it or when you intend to enter it. Then go to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and send greetings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). Then stand at the forward pillar on the right side of the grave, at the head of the grave, facing the Qiblah, with your left shoulder toward the grave and your right shoulder toward the pulpit, for this is the location of the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him). And say: I testify that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and I testify that Muḥammad is His slave and Messenger. And I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah and that you are Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh. And I testify that you conveyed the messages of your Lord, advised your nation, strove in the way of Allah, and worshipped Allah until certainty came to you, with wisdom and good counsel, and fulfilled what was upon you of the truth, and that you were kind to the believers and harsh to the disbelievers. So Allah granted you the highest honor of the honored. Praise be to Allah who saved us through you from polytheism and misguidance. O Allah, make Your blessings, and the blessings of Your near angels, Your righteous servants, Your sent prophets, the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and whoever glorified the Lord of the Worlds from the first and the last, upon Muḥammad, Your slave, Your Messenger, Your Prophet, Your Trustee, Your Confidant [Your Noble One], Your Beloved, Your Chosen One, Your Purity, Your Special One, and Your Best of Creation. O Allah, grant him the Rank and the Proximity in Paradise, and raise him to a Praised Position which the first and the last will envy. O Allah, You said: 'And had they, when they were unjust to themselves, come to You and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Oft-returning, Most Merciful.' And I have come to Your Prophet, seeking forgiveness, repentant from my sins. And I turn to You through Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy, Muḥammad (peace be upon him). O Muḥammad, I turn to Allah, my

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Musawi narrated to me from 'Abdullah ibn Nuhayk, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished your supplication by the grave, go to the pulpit, rub it with your hand, and hold its two knobs (rummanatayhi), which are the lower ones. Rub your face and eyes with them, for it is said that they are a cure for the eyes. Stand by it, praise Allah, glorify Him, and ask for your needs. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Between my pulpit and my grave [my house] is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And my pulpit is upon an oasis from the oases of Paradise, and the pillars of the pulpit are ranks in Paradise, and the oasis is the small door.' Then go to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and pray there as long as you wish. When you enter the mosque, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and when you leave, do the same, and increase your prayers in the mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

Abū ‘Abdil Raḥmān Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥusain Al-‘Askari narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Umar ibn ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali ibn Abī Ťālib, from ‘Ali ibn Ja’far ibn Muḥammad, from his brother Abil Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Ja’far, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon him), who said: ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain (peace be upon him) used to stand by the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), say Salām, and testify that he conveyed the message. Then he would supplicate with whatever came to his mind. Thereafter, he would lean his back against the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), against the green marble that is narrow and attached to the side of the grave. He would lean his back against the grave, face the Qiblah, and say: 'O Allāh! To You I entrust my affair, and to the grave of Muḥammad (peace be upon him), Your slave and Your messenger, I have leaned my back. And to the Qiblah that You approved for Muḥammad (peace be upon him), I have turned my face. O Allāh! I have become in the morning unable to secure for myself any of the good that I hope for, nor to avert from myself any of the harm that I fear. And all affairs are in Your Hand. And there is no one more needy than I. I am in need of the good that You have sent down to me. O Allāh! Grant me a return from You with goodness, for there is none who can withhold Your grace. O Allāh! I seek refuge in You from You changing my name, or altering my body, or removing Your blessing from me. O Allāh! Adorn me with piety, beautify me with blessings, grant me a long healthy life, and provide me with gratitude for that health.'

My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and others, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, who said: I saw Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrive at the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he placed his hand on it and said: I ask Allah, who selected you and chose you and guided you and guided (creation) through you, to send His blessings upon you. Then he said: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe! Send your blessings on him and salute him with all respect.

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) asked me, “What do you recite in your salutation to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)?” I replied, “That which is known and which we have narrated.” He said, “Shall I not teach you something that is better than this?” I said, “Yes, may I be your ransom.” He wrote it for me while I was sitting, and read it to me, and said: “When you stand by his grave (peace be upon him), say: I testify that there is no god but Allāh, He is alone, He has no partner, and I testify that you are the Messenger of Allāh, that Muḥammad is His slave and Messenger, and I testify that you are Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh, and I testify that you are the Seal of the Prophets. And I testify that you have conveyed the messages of your Lord, advised your nation, strove in the way of your Lord, and worshipped Him until certainty (death) came to you, and you fulfilled what was upon you of the truth. O Allāh! Send blessing on Muḥammad, Your slave, Your Messenger, Your confidant, Your trustee, Your chosen one, and the best of Your creation, (blessings which are) greater than any of the blessings You have sent on any of Your prophets or messengers. O Allāh! Send Salām on Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad just as You sent Salām on Nūḥ among the worlds. Bestow favour on Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad just as You bestowed favour on Mūsā and Hārūn. And bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad just as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm. Verily You are the Praised, the Glorified. O Allāh! Send blessing on Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad and have mercy on Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad. O Allāh! Lord of the Sacred House, Lord of the Sacred Mosque, Lord of the Rukn and Maqām, Lord of the Sacred Land, Lord of the lawful and the unlawful, Lord of al-Mash’ar al-Ḥarām. Send my Salām to the soul of Your Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to me from a group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'How should I say peace to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at his grave?' He replied: 'Peace to the Messenger of Allah. Peace to you, O beloved of Allah! Peace to you, O choice of Allah! Peace to you, O trustee of Allah! I testify that you advised your nation, and you strove in the way of Allah, and worshipped Him sincerely until death (certainty) came to you. May Allah reward you with the best reward that He has given any prophet for his nation.' O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, (blessings) greater than that which You sent upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Verily You are the Praiseworthy, the Glorious.

With his chain of narration, from Sahl, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of our companions, who said: I was present with Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him), and Harun the Caliph, and Isa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Yahya in Medina. They had come to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Harun said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Go forward,' but he refused. So Harun went forward, said Salam, and stood aside. Then Isa ibn Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Go forward,' but he refused. So Isa ibn Ja'far went forward, said Salam, and stood with Harun. Then Ja'far said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Go forward,' but he refused. So Ja'far went forward, said Salam, and stood with Harun. Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) went forward and said: 'Peace be upon you, O my father! I ask Allah, who chose you and selected you and guided you and guided (people) through you, to send His blessings upon you.' Harun said to Isa, 'Did you hear what he said?' He said, 'Yes.' Harun said, 'I testify that he is truly his father.'

‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā ibn ‘Ubayd, from Abī ‘Abdillāh Zakariyyā al-Mu’min, from Ibrāhīm ibn Nājiyah, from Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār, who said: I said to Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), “Teach me a short Salām to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).” He said, “Say: I ask Allāh who selected you, chose you, chose you, guided you, and guided (the creation) through you, to send upon you abundant, delightful blessings.”

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ya'qub ibn Yazid, and Musa ibn 'Umar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked, 'How should I say peace upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at his grave?' He said, 'You say:' Peace upon the Messenger of Allah. Peace to you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace to you, O Messenger of Allah! Peace to you, O Muhammad ibn Abdillah! Peace to you, O chosen one of Allah! Peace to you, O beloved of Allah! Peace to you, O choice of Allah! Peace to you, O trustee of Allah! I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah and I testify that you are Muhammad ibn Abdillah, and I testify that you have advised your nation, and you strove in the way of Allah [your Lord], and you worshipped Him until certainty (death) came to you. So may Allah reward you with the best reward that He has given any prophet for his nation. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family [and the family of Muhammad] with the best blessings You sent upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Verily You are the Praiseworthy, the Glorified.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from ['Ali ibn Harun] from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Choose the Rabiyyah pigeons for your houses, for indeed they curse the killers of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

My father, my brother, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan all narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Idris ibn Ahmad, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Jamurani, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sandal [Safwan], from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said: I was sitting in the house of Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I looked at the cooing pigeon cooing for a long time. Then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at me and said, 'O Dawud! Do you know what this bird is saying?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be your ransom.' He said, 'It is calling down curses on the killers of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). Therefore, keep it in your houses.' And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Jamurani, through his chain, similarly.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Ghundar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say regarding the owl: He said, 'Has any one of you seen it during the day?' They said to him, 'It hardly appears during the day, and it does not appear except at night.' He said: 'Indeed, it has always taken developed structures as abodes. But when al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed, it vowed upon itself that it would not take developed structures as abodes ever again, and it would not take anything but wreckages as abodes. So it remains fasting and grieving during its day until night covers it. And when night covers it, it does not cease chanting in grief over al-Husayn (peace be upon him) until morning.'

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali ibn Sā’id Al-Barbari – the custodian of the grave of Imam Riďā (peace be upon him) – who said: I went to Imam Riďā (peace be upon him) and he asked me, 'What do people say about owls?' I replied, 'May I sacrifice myself for you! We have come here to ask you (about this).' He said: 'This owl used to live in the time of my grandfather, the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family), in houses, palaces, and dwellings. When people used to eat food, it would fly and sit in front of them, and food would be thrown to it and it would be given water, after which it would return to its place. However, when Ḥusain (peace be upon him) was killed, it left the developed structures for wreckages, mountains, and deserts, and said,

And Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, the owl fasts during the day, and when it breaks its fast, it laments over al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) until morning.

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali al-Maythami, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: “O Ya’qūb! Have you ever seen an owl during the day breathe?” I replied, “No.” He said, “Do you know why that is?” I replied, “No.” He said, “Because during the day it remains fasting upon what Allāh has sustained it with. When night covers it, it breaks its fast upon what it has been given sustenance. Then it continues chanting/lamenting over al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) until morning.”

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: Any believer whose eyes shed a tear for the killing of Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, until it runs down his cheek, Allah will provide for him thereby rooms in Paradise where he will dwell for long ages. And any believer whose eyes shed a tear until it runs down his cheek for us, due to the affliction that touched us from our enemy in this world, Allah will provide for him thereby a good settlement in Paradise. And any believer who is touched by affliction for us, and his eyes shed a tear until it runs down his cheek from the pain of what was endured for us, Allah will turn away affliction from his face and make him safe on the Day of Resurrection from His Wrath and from the Fire.

My father narrated to me (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah Al-Jamurani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Crying and grief (jaz') are disliked for the servant in any matter he grieves over, except crying and grief over Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him). Verily, in that, he is rewarded.

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Zayyāt, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abī Hārūn al-Makfūf, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said – as part of a longer ḥadīth: "Whoever is mentioned al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) in his presence, and tears flow from his eye [or eyes] the size of a fly's wing, his reward is with Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will not be satisfied for him with less than Paradise."

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu 'Umarah al-Munshid, who said: Whenever al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) was mentioned in the presence of Abu 'Abdillah, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), during the day, Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) would not be seen smiling on that day until nightfall.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr al-Arjani; and my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Zurara, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said: I accompanied Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) on a Hajj journey. In a long hadith, I asked him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, if the grave of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) were to be disinterred, would anything be found in it?' He said, 'O son of Bukayr, how great are your questions! Verily, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is with his father, his mother, and his brother in the house of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with him they are provided for and enriched. And verily, he is hanging on the right side of the Throne, clinging to it, saying: 'O my Lord, fulfill for me what You have promised me.' And verily, he looks at those who visit him, and he knows them better, and their names, and the names of their fathers, and that which is in their saddles, better than one of them knows his own son. And verily, he looks at those who weep for him, so he seeks forgiveness for them and asks his father for forgiveness for them. And he says to the weeper: 'O you who weep, if you knew what Allah has prepared for you, you would be happier than you are grieved.' And verily, he seeks forgiveness for them for every sin and every mistake.'

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Bakr ibn Muḥammad, from Fuďayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: The sins of whoever cries, even as little as (the width of) the wing of a fly, when we are mentioned in front of him will be forgiven, even if his sins are greater than the scum in the sea. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Barqi, from his father, from Bakr ibn Muḥammad, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), similarly.

Hakim ibn Dawud narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Any believer whose eyes shed tears for the killing of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), with a tear running down his cheek, Allah will prepare for him thereby rooms in Paradise, dwelling in them for long ages.

And from him, from Salamah, from 'Ali ibn Sayf, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Fudayl ibn [Zayd and] Fudalah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever is mentioned in his presence and his eyes shed tears, Allah has made his face haram (impermissible) for the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Hassam, from [Ibn] Abi Shu'bah, from Abdullah ibn Ghaliib, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and recited for him the elegy of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). When I reached this verse: 'What a great disaster! Instead of scattering dust over Husayn, he was rolled in the dust!' a woman who was crying from behind the curtain screamed, 'O father!'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever recites a verse of poetry about al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and weeps and makes ten people weep, he and they will have Paradise. And whoever recites a verse about al-Husayn and weeps and makes nine people weep, he and they will have Paradise. He kept reducing [the number] until he said: Whoever recites a verse about al-Husayn and weeps, or even weeps together [with others], he will have Paradise.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he said to me, 'Recite a poem for me.' So I recited, and he said, 'No, not the way you usually recite, but the way you eulogize him at his grave.' I said, so I recited: 'Pass by the grave of Husayn... and say to his pure bones...' He said, so when he cried, I stopped. He said, 'Pass (continue),' so I continued. He said, 'Add more, add more.' So I recited: 'O Maryam, arise and lament your master... and over Husayn, so be happy with your weeping.' He said, so he cried and the women became restless. He said, so when they calmed down, he said to me, 'O Abu Harun! Whoever recites a poem about Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes ten people cry, for him is Paradise.' Then he kept reducing one by one until he reached one, and said, 'Whoever recites a poem about Husayn and makes one person cry, for him is Paradise.' Then he said, 'Whoever remembers him and cries, for him is Paradise.'
And it is narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: There is a reward for every act except for the tear shed for us.

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-‘Askarī narrated to me from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn Mahziyār, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever recites a verse of poetry about al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and weeps and makes ten people weep, he and they will have Paradise. And whoever recites a verse about al-Ḥusayn and weeps and makes nine people weep, he and they will have Paradise. He kept reducing [the number] until he said: Whoever recites a verse about al-Ḥusayn and weeps, or even tries to weep, he will have Paradise.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from a group of my scholars, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) cried over his father, Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), for twenty years or forty years. And whenever food was placed before him, he would cry over Husayn (peace be upon him) until his servant said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! I fear that you will be among the perished.' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'I only complain of my distress and grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.' Verily, whenever I remember the killing of the children of Fatimah, I am choked with tears because of it.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab al-Zayyat, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ismail ibn Mansur, from some of our companions, who said: A servant of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) looked down at him while he was in his chamber, prostrating and weeping. He said to him, 'O my master, O Ali ibn al-Husayn! Is it not time for your grief to end?' He raised his head toward him and said, 'Woe unto you! Or may your mother weep on you! By Allah, Jacob complained to his Lord of a matter much less than what I have seen, until he said, "Alas for Joseph, that he has lost a single son," whereas I saw my father and a group of my family slaughtered around me.' And Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to sympathize with the children of Aqil. So it was said to him, 'Why do you have more sympathy for these children of your uncle than for the family of Ja'far?' He replied, 'I remember their day with Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), so I sympathize with them.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on them all, narrated from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Abu Yahya al-Hadda', from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) looked at al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said, 'O 'Abrat (tear) of every believer!' He (al-Husayn) said, 'Am I, O my father?' He (the Commander of the Believers) said, 'Yes, O my son!'

My scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Abdillāh, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn Abī ‘Uthmān, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abī ‘Umārah al-Munshid, who said: Whenever al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) was mentioned in front of Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) during the day, Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) would be seen smiling until nightfall. And he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is the tear of every believer.'

My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) said, "I am the Martyr of Tears. No believer remembers me without crying."

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'I am the Martyr of Tears.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'I am the Martyr of Tears.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khazzaz, from Harun ibn Harizah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: We were with him, and we mentioned al-Husayn (peace be upon him) – may Allah's curse be upon his killers. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) wept, and we wept with him. He said, then he raised his head and said: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said, 'I am the Martyr of Tears; no believer remembers me without weeping.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hanan who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Go to the Ziyarah of Husayn (peace be upon him) and do not be disinclined to it. Verily he is the Master of the Youth of Paradise from among the creation and he is the Master of the Martyrs.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Madinah, 'Where are the graves of the martyrs?' He said: 'Is not the best of the martyrs among you? And He to whom my soul belongs, there are around him four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, weeping for him until the Day of Judgment.'

Abul ‘Abbās Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Mustariq, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said: I was with Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) and I had sent someone to rent a donkey for me so that I could go to the graves of the martyrs. He asked me, 'What prevents you from going to the Ziyārah of the Master of the Martyrs?' I asked, 'Who is he?' He replied, 'Ḥusain (peace be upon him).' I asked, 'What is the reward for going to his Ziyārah?' He replied, 'One purified Hajj and ‘Umrah as well as this much reward.' Um Sa’īd added that the Imam extended his arms out and then closed them three times (to explain 'this much reward').

And from him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Umm Saʿīd al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said: I went to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and entered upon him. The bondmaid came and said, 'I have brought the beast of burden.' He said to me, 'O Umm Saʿīd! What is this beast for? Where do you intend to go?' I said, 'I am going to visit the graves of the martyrs.' He said, 'Postpone it for today. How strange are you, O people of Iraq! You come to the martyrs from a distant journey, but you leave the Master of the Martyrs and do not go to him.' I said to him, 'Who is the Master of the Martyrs?' He said, 'Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī (peace be upon him).' I said, 'I am a woman.' He said, 'There is no harm for one like you to go to him and visit him.' I said, 'What is for us in visiting him?' He said, 'It equals one Ḥajj and one ʿUmrah, and ʿItikāf (seclusion) for two months in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and fasting them, and its goodness is so and so.' She said, 'And he extended his hand and closed it three times.'

My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan, may Allāh have mercy on them, narrated from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Aḥmad ibn Rizq Al-Ghamshāni, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said: I entered Madīnah and rented a donkey to go around the graves of the martyrs. I said, 'I must start by visiting the son of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him), so I will enter upon him.' I delayed the renter a little, and he called out to me. Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me, 'What is this, O Um Sa’īd?' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I rented a donkey to go around the graves of the martyrs.' He said, 'Shall I not inform you of the Master of the Martyrs?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Al-Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him).' I said, 'And indeed he is the Master of the Martyrs.' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Then what is for the one who visits him?' He said, 'A Hajj and an ‘Umrah, and of the good, this much and this much.'

My father and Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari both narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Barqi, from his father, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Qāsim Al-Ḥārithi, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said: I entered Madīnah and I rented a mule (and a guide) to go to the Ziyārah of the graves of the martyrs. I thought to myself that no one is more worthy of being visited first than Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (a.s.). Therefore, I went and saw the Imam (a.s.) and I delayed (the guide a little). The guide raised his voice and said, “May Allāh keep you well! You are delaying me!” (When the Imam (a.s.) heard him) he said to me, “O Um Sa’īd! It looks like someone (is waiting for you and) wants you to hurry.” I replied, “May I sacrifice myself for you! I have rented a mule to go to the Ziyārah of the graves of the martyrs but I thought to myself that no one is more worthy of being visited first than Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (a.s.).” Imam (a.s.) asked, “O Um Sa’īd! What prevents you from going to the Ziyārah of the Master of the Martyrs?” (When the Imam (a.s.) said this), I hoped that he would reveal the location of the grave of ‘Ali ibn Abī Ťālib (a.s.) for me so I asked, “May I sacrifice my father and mother for you! Who is the Master of the Martyrs?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Ḥusain, son of Fāťimah (a.s.). O Um Sa’īd! Whoever goes to him longing for him and with insight (of his status) will earn the reward of a purified Hajj and ‘Umrah and he will have this much reward.”

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from one who narrated to him, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', Abu al-Ma'za, and 'Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat, their group, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: There is no martyr except that he wishes, if al-Husayn ibn Ali were alive, and he wishes to be with al-Husayn (peace be upon him) so that they may enter Paradise with him.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said: I heard Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: There is no prophet in the heavens or on earth who does not ask Allāh the Exalted for permission to go to the Ziyārah of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him). A crowd descends and a crowd ascends.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ash'ath, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: The grave of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) is twenty cubits by twenty cubits, divided; it is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And in it [and from it] is the ascension of the angels to the heaven. And there is no angel brought near nor a messenger prophet except that he asks Allah to visit him. So a group descends and a group ascends.

My father, my brother, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn Hajjaj, from Yunus, from Safwan, the goldsmith, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When I came to al-Hirah, do you go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I said: 'And you visit him? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'How can I not visit him when Allah visits him? Every Thursday night, He descends to him with the angels, the prophets, and the successors, and Muhammad is the best of the prophets, and we are the best of the successors.' Safwan said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, so we visit him every Thursday night so that we may attain the visitation of the Lord?' He said: 'Yes, O Safwan! Stick to that, and the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) will be recorded for you. And that is a privilege, and that is a privilege.' And al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hamadani narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: 'I went out in the late period of the Banu Umayyah,' and he mentioned a similar narration to the one preceding in the chapter. And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Amriki ibn Ali al-Bufaki, from a number of our companions, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Husayn ibn ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, who said: 'I went out in the late period of the Banu Marwan,' and he mentioned a similar narration to his which passed at the beginning of the chapter, exactly the same.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: There is no angel in the heavens or on earth who does not ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for permission to visit the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). A group descends and a group ascends.

And from him, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Dawud Al-Raqqi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Allah has not created any creation greater in number than the angels. Every evening, seventy thousand angels descend from the heavens. They perform Tawaf around the Holy Ka'bah for the night. When dawn breaks, they depart to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they ascend to the heavens before the sun rises. Then seventy thousand angels of the day descend. They perform Tawaf around the Holy Ka'bah for the day. When the sun sets, they depart to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they ascend to the heavens before the sun sets.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: The space between the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and the heaven is [filled with] the angels descending and ascending.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is twenty cubits by twenty cubits, square. It is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. From it is an ascent to the heaven. No near angel or messengered prophet is there except that he asks Allah, the Exalted, to visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him). A group descends and a group ascends.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from some of his companions, from Ahmad ibn Qutaybah al-Hamdani, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said: I said to Abī 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him): On the night of 'Arafah, I was in Ḥā`ir praying. I saw close to fifty thousand handsome men who smelled beautiful and who were praying Salāt all night. It was after dawn that I prostrated and when I raised my head, I could not see any of them. Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: Fifty thousand angels passed by Ḥusain (peace be upon him) while he was being killed so they ascended to the heavens. Allāh, the Exalted, revealed to them, 'You passed by the son of My love and he was being killed but you did not help him. Descend to the earth and dwell near his grave while you are disheveled and covered with dust until the rising of the Hour.'

My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf Al-Qummi Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Musa ibn Qasim Al-Bajali, from someone who narrated to him, from Murazim, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about praying in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: One prayer in my mosque is equal to one thousand prayers elsewhere, and one prayer in Masjid al-Haram is equal to one thousand prayers in my mosque. Then he said: Verily Allah has given preference to Makkah, and He has made some parts of it better than others, saying: 'And take for yourselves a place of prayer on the standing-place of Ibrahim'. And He said: Verily Allah has given preference to some people, and He ordered following them and loving them in the Book.

He narrated to me: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from his father Isma'il from Ibn Muskān from Abi al-Sāmit who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: One prayer in the Mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him) equals ten thousand prayers.

My group of scholars narrated to me from 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother 'Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, Ibn Abi 'Umayr, and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, all from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Ibn Abi Ya'fūr: 'Increase your prayers in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for he said: One prayer in my mosque here is equal to one thousand prayers in any other mosque, except for Al-Masjid Al-Harām, for one prayer in Al-Masjid Al-Harām is equal to one thousand prayers in my mosque.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Salamah, and Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn Sayf from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: One prayer in my mosque is equal to one thousand prayers elsewhere.

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammār ibn Mūsā Al-Sābāťi, from Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about praying in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), is it like praying in Madīnah? He (peace be upon him) replied, 'No, because one prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) is equal to one thousand prayers, and praying in Madīnah is like praying in other cities.'

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah, from ‘Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, who said: I heard Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) said: One prayer in my mosque is equal to one thousand prayers elsewhere.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Razzaz Al-Kufi narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There are four thousand angels by the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), disheveled and covered with dust, weeping for him until the Day of Judgment. Their chief is an angel named Mansur. No visitor comes to visit him but they receive him, and no one bids him farewell but they accompany him. No one falls ill but they visit him, and no one dies but they pray over him [and over his funeral] and seek forgiveness for him after his death.

And my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, the Blessed and the Exalted, has dedicated seventy thousand angels to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who are disheveled and covered with dust, and they send blessings upon him every day. They pray for whoever visits him, saying: 'O Lord! These are the visitors of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Do such-and-such for them and do such-and-such for them.'

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from Ḥassān [Ghassān] al-Baṣrī, from Mu’āwiyah ibn Wahb, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Do not neglect the Ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him). Do you not like to be among those for whom the angels pray?

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, the Exalted, has assigned seventy thousand angels to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). They are disheveled and covered with dust, sending blessings upon him every day from the day he was killed until what Allah wills, meaning the rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him). They pray for those who visit him, saying: 'O Lord, these are the visitors of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Do this for them and do that for them.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Ma'za, from 'Anbasah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: Allah has assigned seventy thousand angels to the grave of Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), who worship Allah near it. The prayer of one of them is equal to one thousand prayers of a human being, and the reward of their prayers is for those who visit the grave of Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). And upon his killer be the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people, for eternity.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Allah, the Exalted, assigned to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) seventy thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, weeping for him until the Day of Judgment. They pray near his grave; the prayer of one of them is equal to a thousand prayers of human beings. The reward of their prayers and the merit thereof is for whoever visits his grave.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mattil, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me all of them from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to me, who said: Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Order our Shia to go to the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Verily, going to his Ziyarah is obligatory on every believer who testifies that al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is an Imam appointed by Allah, the Great and Almighty.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from Umm Sa'id al-Ahmasiyyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He asked me, 'O Umm Sa'id, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn?' I said, 'Yes.' He said to me, 'Visit him, for verily the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn is obligatory upon men and women.'

My father and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan, may Allāh have mercy on them both, narrated from Ḥasan ibn Mattīl, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī al-Kūfī, from ‘Alī ibn Ḥassān al-Hāshimī, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, the servant of Abī Ja‘far (peace be upon him), from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: If one of you were to perform Ḥajj throughout his entire life, yet did not visit al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him), he would have abandoned a right of Allāh and a right of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family), because the right of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is a mandatory obligation from Allāh, incumbent upon every Muslim.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khālid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammād Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, from Muhammad Al-Basri, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard my father say to one of his servants, and he asked him about the Ziyarah, so he said to him: 'To whom are you going for Ziyarah and whom do you seek (to please) by it?' He replied: 'Allah, the Blessed and the Exalted.' He said: 'Whoever prays behind him one obligatory prayer (or one prayer) seeking Allah by it, will meet Allah on the Day he meets Him, and upon him will be from the light such that everything that looks at him will be covered (by its brightness).' And Allah will honor those who visit him, and He will prevent the Fire from touching them in any way. And indeed, the one who visits him will not be prevented (or overlooked) from reaching the Pool before him. And the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) will be standing by the Pool, shaking his hand and quenching his thirst with water. And no one will precede him in entering the Pool until he has quenched his thirst, then he will turn away to his dwelling in Paradise. And with him will be an angel from the Commander of the Believers, who will order the Sirat (bridge) to humble itself for him and will order the Fire not to touch him with its blaze until he crosses it. And with him will be his messenger whom the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) had sent.

And with this chain of narration, from Al-Asam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, in a long hadith: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O son of Bukayr! Verily Allah has chosen six places on earth: Al-Bait Al-Haram, Al-Haram, the graves of the prophets, the graves of the successors, the places of martyrdom [graves] of the martyrs, and the mosques in which the name of Allah is remembered. O son of Bukayr! Do you know what is for the one who visits the grave of Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when the ignorant neglect it? There is no morning but that an announcer from the angels is by his grave, calling out: O seeker of good! Turn towards the chosen one of Allah, depart with honour and be secured from regret. The people of the East and the people of the West hear it, except for the two Qalans (humankind and jinn). And no angel from the guardians remains on earth but he turns towards him when the servant sleeps, so that he glorifies Allah by him and asks Allah for His pleasure regarding him. And no angel in the air hears the voice but responds with glorifying Allah, the Exalted. So the voices of the angels intensify, and the people of the lowest heaven respond to them, so the voices of the angels and the people of the lowest heaven intensify until they reach the people of the seventh heaven. And Allah makes their voices heard by the prophets, so they send mercy and blessings upon Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and supplicate for the one who visited him.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, from Hammad (known as) Dhil Nab, from Rumi, from Zurarah, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say about one who visits your father while in fear?' He replied: 'Allah will grant him safety on the Day of Great Terror, and the angels will receive him with glad tidings, and it will be said to him: Do not fear nor grieve. This is your day in which you achieve success.'

And through his chain, from Al-Asam, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, 'I travel to Arjān, and my heart pulls me toward the grave of your father. However, when I go out, my heart is trembling and apprehensive until I return, fearing the ruler, the governors, and the armed men, until I return.' He said, 'O son of Bukayr! Do you not desire that Allāh sees you fearing for us? Do you not know that whoever fears out of fear for us, Allāh will shelter him under the shade of His Throne, and Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) will be conversing with him beneath the Throne? And Allāh will secure him from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection; people will be terrified, but he will not be terrified. And if he is terrified, the angels will strengthen him and calm his heart with glad tidings.'

Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim al-Sarraj narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from Hassan al-Basri, from Mu'awiah ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He said: O Mu'awiah! Do not leave visiting the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) due to fear, for whoever leaves it will see such regret that he will wish his grave were next to him. Do you not love that Allah sees your person and your blackness (or distinctiveness) among those for whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), 'Ali, Fatimah, and the Imams pray? Do you not love to be among those who return with forgiveness for what has passed, and for whom the sins of seventy years are forgiven? Do you not love to be among those who leave this world with no sin that will be pursued (against them)? Do you not love to be tomorrow among those whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) will shake hands with?

‘Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl ibn Bazī‘, from al-Khaybarī, from Yūnus ibn Ḍabyān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him, ‘May I be sacrificed for you, how is the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) performed in the state of Taqiyyah (precaution)?’ He said: ‘When you reach the Euphrates, perform Ghusl, then wear your purified garments [your two purified garments]. Then pass by opposite the grave and say: May Allāh’s blessings be upon you, O Abā ‘Abdillāh! May Allāh’s blessings be upon you, O Abā ‘Abdillāh! Then your Ziyārah is complete.’

And Muḥammad ibn ‘ammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥammād Al-Basri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Asam, from Ḥusain, from Al-Ḥalabi, from Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), in a long hadith: He said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say about one who leaves his Ziyārah while he is able to do so?' He said: 'I say that he has disowned the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) and disowned us, and he has belittled a matter that is obligatory on him.' And whoever goes to his Ziyārah, Allāh will look after his needs, and he will be spared whatever concerns him from the affairs of his worldly life. And verily it brings sustenance for the slave and compensates him for what he spent. And He forgives him the sins of fifty years, and he returns to his family, and whatever burden or mistake is upon him has been erased from his record. If he dies during his journey, the angels descend and perform his ritual bath, and the doors of Paradise are opened for him, and its fragrance descends upon him until he is resurrected. And if he is safe (returns), the door from which sustenance descends is opened for him, and for every Dirham he spent, ten thousand Dirhams are made for him, and that is stored for him. So when he is resurrected, it will be said to him: 'For you, for every Dirham, ten thousand Dirhams, and verily Allāh has kept it safely for you with Himself.'

And by his chain, from Al-Asam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a man came to him and said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, is your father visited? He said: Yes, and prayer is established near him, and prayer is established behind him, and one does not precede him. He said: What is the reward for the one who visits him? He said: Paradise, if he believes in his Imamate. He said: What is the reward for the one who neglects it out of preference? He said: Regret on the Day of Regret. He said: What is the reward for the one who stays near him? He said: Every day is equal to a thousand months. He said: What is the reward for the one who spends while traveling to him and the one who spends while at his grave? He said: One Dirham is equal to a thousand Dirhams. And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.

And through his chain of narration, from Al-Asamm, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom! Indeed, your father used to say regarding Hajj that for every Dirham he spent, a thousand Dirhams are recorded for him. So what is the reward for one who spends in traveling to your father, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)? He said: O son of Sinan! For every Dirham, a thousand and a thousand are recorded for him — until he counted ten times. And his ranks are elevated by the same amount. And the pleasure of Allah is better for him, and the supplication of Muhammad (peace be upon him), and the supplication of the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams (peace be upon them) is better for him.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Amriki ibn Ali, who said: Yahya narrated to us, and he was in the service of Abi Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), from Ali, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in a long hadith of his. He said: I asked, 'What is the reward for one who prays near him — meaning al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'Whoever prays two rak'ahs near him, Allah, the Exalted, will grant him whatever he asks for.' I asked, 'What is the reward for one who performs ghusl with the water of the Euphrates and then goes to him?' He replied, 'If he performs ghusl with the water of the Euphrates with the intention of going to him, his sins will fall away from him as on the day his mother gave birth to him.' I asked, 'What is the reward for one who sends provisions for him but does not go himself due to an illness?' He replied: 'Allah will give him for every dirham he spent [in sending others] good deeds equal to the weight of Mount Uhud, and He will compensate him with multiples of what he spent, and divert from him afflictions that had descended, so they will be repelled, and his wealth will be preserved.' And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars (may Allah have mercy on them), narrated from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of our companions, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I have been informed that some people who went to visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him) carried with them baskets containing halawah (sweetmeats) and akhbisah (a type of sweet bread/pastry) and similar foods. If they had gone to visit the graves of their loved ones, they would not have carried these with them.

And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad and others narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from Sāliḥ ibn Sindi Al-Jammāl, from a man from Ahl al-Raqqah, who was called Abū was called Abū al-Maḍā’, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: ‘Do you go to the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him)?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Do you take provisions (sufur) for that?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘If you were going to the graves of your fathers and mothers, you would not do that.’ I said: ‘Then what should we eat?’ He said: ‘Bread and milk.’ And Karrām said to Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him): ‘May I be your ransom! Some people who visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) take tasty provisions.’ He said: ‘Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: ‘If they were visiting the graves of their mothers and fathers, they would not do that.’

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from some of our companions, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: I have been informed that some people go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) carrying different kinds of food with them, including Akhbisah and other similar deserts. Verily if they had gone to the graves of their loved ones, they would not have taken such things with them.

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥusain narrated to me, saying: Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār narrated to me from his father, from Ḥusayn ibn Sa‘īd, from Zur‘ah ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaḍrami, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ‘Umar, Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: ‘Going to the Ziyārah is better than not going, and not going is better than going.’ I said, ‘You broke my back!’ He said: ‘By Allāh, one of you goes to the grave of his father anguished and grieved, but you come to him (Imam al-Ḥusayn) with provisions (food). No! Unless you come to him disheveled and covered with dust.’

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusain narrated to me from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Sa‘īd, from Zur‘ah ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaḍrami, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ‘Umar, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: ‘Going to the Ziyārah is better than not going, and not going is better than going.’ I said, ‘You broke my back!’ He said, ‘By Allāh, one of you goes to the grave of his father anguished and grieved, but you come to him (the Imam) with your own selves [dressed in fine clothes]. No! [It is better not to go] unless you go disheveled and covered with dust.’

My father, my brother, and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and others, may Allah have mercy on them, narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Ash'ari, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When you intend the Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), go to his Ziyarah while you are sorrowful, grieved, distressed, disheveled, covered with dust, hungry, and thirsty, for indeed al-Husayn was killed while he was grieved, distressed, disheveled, covered with dust, hungry, and thirsty. And ask him for your needs, then turn away from him, and do not take him as a permanent residence.

And with this chain of narration, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from Salih ibn al-Sindi al-Jammal, from the one he mentioned, from Karram ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Karram: When you intend to go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), visit him while you are sorrowful, grief-stricken, disheveled, and covered with dust, for indeed al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed while he was sorrowful, grief-stricken, disheveled, covered with dust, hungry, and thirsty.

My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya and 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari and Ahmad ibn Idris, all from Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubaydillah, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Jabbar Al-Nahawandi, from Abi Sa'id, from Al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhtah, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: O Husayn! Whoever leaves his house intending to visit the grave of Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), if he is walking, Allah will record for him one good deed for every step and erase one bad deed from him. Until when he arrives in the Hā'ir, Allah will record him among the successful and the chosen [the triumphant and the victorious]. Until when he completes his rituals, Allah will record him among the winners. Until when he intends to depart, an angel comes to him and says: Verily, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sends you greetings and says to you: Resume your deeds, for what has passed of your sins has been forgiven.

And with this chain of narration, from Sāliḥ, from al-Ḥarth ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allāh has angels assigned to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him). When a man decides to visit him, Allāh gives his sins to these angels. With the first step he takes, they erase his sins; then with every additional step, they multiply his good deeds. His good deeds continue to increase until they entitle him to Paradise. Then the angels surround him and sanctify him, and they call out to the angels of the heavens: 'Sanctify the visitors of the Beloved of Allāh.' When the visitors perform ritual bath (Ghusl), Muḥammad (peace be upon him) calls out to them: 'O guests of Allāh! Rejoice, for you will accompany me in Paradise.' Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) calls out to them: 'I guarantee the fulfillment of your needs and the removal of affliction from you in this world and the Hereafter.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) joins them, staying to their right and left, until they return to their families.

And ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh and a group (of scholars) narrated to me, may Allah have mercy on them, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir, from Jabir al-Makfuf, from Abi al-Samit, who said: I heard Abu ‘Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on foot, Allah will record for him one thousand good deeds for every step, erase one thousand bad deeds for him, and raise his status by one thousand degrees. So when you arrive at the Euphrates, perform ritual bath (ghusl), hang your shoes, and walk barefoot, walking with the gait of a humble slave. So when you arrive at the door of al-Ha’ir, recite Takbir four times, then walk a little, then recite Takbir four times, then approach his head and stand upon it, then recite Takbir four times [recite Takbir and pray near him and ask], and pray four units (rak’ahs) and ask Allah for your need.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the minimum (reward) for the visitor of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?'
