He said to me, 'O Abdullah! Verily, the minimum that befalls him is that Allah protects him in his own self and his family until He returns him to his family. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will be the Protector for him.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from one who narrated to him, from Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: O Ali! Visit Husayn and do not neglect it. I asked, "What is the reward for one who goes to him?" He said: "Whoever goes to him on foot, Allah will record for him one good deed for every step, erase one bad deed, and raise his rank." When he arrives, Allah will assign two angels to him who will write whatever good comes out of his mouth, and they will not write whatever bad comes out of his mouth or anything else. When he departs, they will bid him farewell and say, "O friend of Allah! You are forgiven. You are from the party of Allah, the party of His Messenger, and the party of the family of His Messenger." And by Allah, you will never see Hell with your own eyes, nor will it see you, nor burn you forever.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'ibn 'Abdillah and 'Abdillah 'ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ahmad 'ibn Muhammad 'ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from his father, from 'Abd al-'Azim 'ibn 'Abdillah 'ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn 'ibn al-Hakam al-Nakha'i, from Abi Hammad al-A'rabi, from Sadir al-Sayrifi, who said: We were with Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) when a young man mentioned the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'For every step a servant takes towards it, Allah records for him one good deed and erases one bad deed.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khālid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, from Abū 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever from our Shia visits Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) will not return until all of his sins are forgiven. For every step he takes and every hand his mount raises, one thousand good deeds are recorded for him and one thousand bad deeds are erased. His status is elevated by one thousand degrees.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Bashir al-Sarraj, from Abu Sa'id al-Qadi, who said: I entered the chamber of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and found Murazim with him. I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on foot, Allah will record for him, with every step and with every foot he raises and places, the freeing of a slave from the children of Ismail. And whoever visits him by ship, if their ship carries them, a caller from the heavens will call out to them: 'Be delighted, and Paradise will be pleasing to you.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muharibi, from Ahmad ibn Maytham, from Muhammad ibn 'Asim, from 'Abdillah ibn al-Najjar, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do you visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and ride ships?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you not know that if it drowns you, a caller will call out to you: 'Be delighted and enjoy the pleasures of Paradise.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Isma'il ibn Zayd, from Abdullah al-Tahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: There is no one on the Day of Judgment except that he wishes he were among the visitors of al-Husayn, because of what he sees being done for the visitors of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) in terms of their honour before Allah, the Exalted.

And Sāliḥ al-Ṣayrāfī narrated from ‘Imrān al-Mīthamī, from Sāliḥ ibn Mītham, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever desires to be at the tables of light on the Day of Judgment, let him be among the visitors of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, who said: He narrated to me from Ibn Sadaqah, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I swear to Allah, it is as if I see the angels crowding around the believers at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' I asked: 'Do they appear for him?' He replied: 'Far, far from it! I swear to Allah, they are attached to the believers, to the extent that they wipe their faces with their hands.' And Allah sends down to the visitors of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), morning and evening, from the food of Paradise, and the angels are their servants. Any servant of Allah who asks Allah for any need of this world or the Hereafter, He will grant it to him. I said: 'This, I swear to Allah, is the honour.' He said to me: 'O Mufaddal, shall I add to it?' I said: 'Yes, O my master.' He said: 'It is as if I see a throne made of light that has been placed, and a dome made of a red ruby, adorned with gems, has been erected over it. And it is as if I see al-Husayn (peace be upon him) sitting on that throne, and around him are ninety thousand green domes.' And it is as if I see the believers visiting him and sending him greetings. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to them: 'O My friends! Ask Me, for you have been hurt, humiliated, and oppressed for a long time. So this is the day that you will not ask Me for any need of this world or the Hereafter without Me fulfilling it for you.' So their eating and drinking will be in Paradise. This, I swear to Allah, is the honour which has no end and whose limit cannot be reached.

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn and ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh (may Allah have mercy on them) narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār and ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā ibn ‘Ubayd ibn Yaqṭīn al-Yaqṭīnī, from someone who narrated to him, from Abū Khālid Dhī al-Shāmah, who said: Abū Usāmah narrated to me, saying: I heard Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Whoever wishes to be in the neighbourhood of his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the neighbourhood of ‘Ali and Fāṭimah, let him not neglect the Ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him).

And through his chain of narration from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) – or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) – say: Whoever wishes for his dwelling and abode to be Paradise, let him not neglect the Ziyarah of the oppressed one. I asked, 'Who is he?' He replied: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), the master of Karbala. Whoever visits him with yearning for him, and love for the Messenger of Allah, and love for Fatimah, and love for the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), Allah will seat him at the tables of Paradise, eating with them while the people are undergoing judgment.

Muhammad ibn Hammam ibn Suhayl narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Imran narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Ayyub, from Al-Harith ibn Mughira Al-Nasri, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and the Exalted, has assigned angels to be in charge of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So when a man intends to visit him and performs Ghusl, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) will call out, 'O guests of Allah! Rejoice, for you will accompany me in Paradise.' And he mentioned the hadith.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, and Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father Abdullah, from Ali ibn Isma'il Al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn Amr Al-Zayyat, from Qa'id [Fayd] Al-Hannat, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) knowing his right, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.

Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Kathir, from Harun ibn Kharijah, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), "People hold the view that whoever visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), it counts for him as a Hajj and an 'Umrah." He said to me: "I swear to Allah that whoever visits him, knowing his right, is forgiven for what preceded of his sins and what followed." And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of our scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, through his chain, similarly.

And Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Al-Khaybari, from Ḥusain ibn Muḥammad Al-Qummi, who said: Abū Al-Ḥasan, Mūsā ibn Ja’far (peace be upon him) said: The minimum reward for the visitor of Al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) by the shore of the Euphrates, if he knows his right and sanctity and Wilayah, is that he is forgiven for what preceded of his sin and what followed.

And Abul-Abbās narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusain, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allāh will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Sufyan al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what followed.

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Hind al-Ḥannāṭ, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) knowing his right, following him, Allāh will forgive him his past and future sins.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah ibn Hammad Al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, will be forgiven for what preceded of his sin and what followed.

And my father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Al-Mughirah, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, who said: Yūsuf Al-Anbāri informed me from Qā'id Al-Ḥannāṭ He said: I said to Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'They go to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with the wailers and food.' He said, 'I have heard.' Then he said, 'O Qā'id! Whoever goes to the grave of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) knowing his rights, his past and future sins will be forgiven.'

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Qā’id, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allāh will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what followed.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Abu Dawud al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, will be forgiven for what preceded of his sins and what followed.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, will be forgiven for what preceded of his sin and what followed.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Ya'qub Al-Abzari, from Qa'id, from 'Abdillah ibn Salih (peace be upon him), who said: I went to him and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Indeed, people are visiting Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), both those who know this matter and those who deny it, and women have traveled to him, and the state of fame/publicity has occurred. I have withdrawn from it because of the fame I saw.' He said, so he remained silent for a while not answering me. Then he turned to me and said, 'O Iraqi! If they have publicized themselves, do not publicize yourself. By Allah, no one who comes to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) knowing his right will come except that Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin and what followed.'

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to me from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abi al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Whoever goes to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) knowing his right, all of his sins, past and future, will be forgiven.

‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Muḥammad ibn Sadaqah, from Sāliḥ Al-Nīli, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Those who go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights are like those who have performed Hajj three times accompanying the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.).

My father and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn 'Ubayd al-Ju'fi narrated to me, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Jarir al-Qummi narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: To my father: Whoever visits al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) knowing his right, will be among those whom Allah speaks to, above His Throne. Verily the pious ones will be amidst gardens and springs in the seat of truth, in the presence of the omnipotent sovereign.

My father narrated to me, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, and Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from some of his companions, from Juwayriyah ibn ‘Alā, from some of his companions, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: On the Day of Judgment, a caller will call out, 'Where are the visitors of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him)?' So a large number of people, who cannot be counted by anyone other than Allāh, the Exalted, will stand. Then He will ask them, 'What was your intention in visiting the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him)?' They will reply, 'O Lord! We went to him out of love for the Messenger of Allāh and out of love for ‘Ali and Fāťimah, and out of sympathy for him because of that which was committed against him.' It will be said to them, 'Here are Muḥammad, ‘Ali, Fāťimah, Ḥasan, and Ḥusain (peace be upon them). Join them, for you will be with them at their level. Follow the flag of the Messenger of Allāh.' Therefore, they will go to the flag of the Messenger of Allāh, which will be in the hand of ‘Ali (peace be upon him), and they will remain under its shade—until all of them enter Paradise. They will be in front of the flag, to its right, to its left, and behind it.

And through his chain of narration from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah – or [and] Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) – say: Whoever loves that his dwelling and abode be Paradise, let him not neglect the Ziyarah of the oppressed one. I asked, "And who is he?" He replied: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), the master of Karbala. Whoever goes to him with yearning for him, and love for the Messenger of Allah, and love for the Commander of the Believers, and love for Fatimah, Allah will seat him at the tables of Paradise, eating with them while the people are undergoing the reckoning.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf Al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa Al-Yaqtini, from a man, from Fudayl ibn 'Uthman Al-Sayrafi, from one who narrated to him, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Allah wills goodness for a slave, He places the love of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the love of his Ziyarah in his heart. And when Allah wills evil for a slave, He places the hatred of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the hatred of his Ziyarah in his heart.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) yearning for him, Allah will record him among the secure on the Day of Judgment, and he will be given his book in his right hand, and he will be under the flag of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) until he enters Paradise, and he will make him dwell at his level. Verily Allah is Mighty and Wise.

And it is narrated from Abī Basīr, from Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him), that whoever loves that his dwelling and abode be Paradise, let him not neglect the Ziyārah of the oppressed one. I asked, 'Who is he?' He said: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him), the master of Karbalā. Whoever goes to him with yearning for him, and with love for the Messenger of Allah, and love for the Commander of the Believers, and love for Fāṭimah (peace be upon her), Allah will seat him at the tables of Paradise, eating with them while the people are undergoing judgment.

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Alā ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said: If people knew the reward in the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), they would die of yearning and their souls would be torn apart with regret for it. I asked, 'What is in it?' He said: 'Whoever goes to him with yearning, Allāh will record for him one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified ‘Umrah.' And the reward of one thousand martyrs from the martyrs of Badr, and the reward of one thousand fasting people, and the recompense of one thousand accepted charities. And the recompense of freeing one thousand slaves seeking the Face of Allāh. And he will remain protected for his year from every plague, the least evil of which is Shayṭān. And an honourable angel will be assigned to him who will protect him from in front of him, from behind him, from his right, from his left, from above his head, and from beneath his feet. So if he dies in that year, the angels of mercy will attend him. They will attend his washing and shrouding, and seek forgiveness for him, and they will escort him to his grave while seeking forgiveness for him. And space will be widened for him in his grave as far as his eye can see. And Allāh will make him safe from the pressure of the grave and from Munkar and Nakīr so that they do not frighten him. And a door will be opened for him to Paradise. And his book will be given to him in his right hand. And on the Day of Judgment, a light will be given to him which illuminates for his light from the East to the West. And a caller will call out: 'This is the one who visited al-Ḥusayn with yearning for him.' So no one will remain on the Day of Judgment except that he will wish on that day that he had been among the visitors of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).

And from him, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn 'Uthman Al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is for the one who visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'Whoever visits him yearning for him will be among the honored servants of Allah, and will be under the flag of Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) until Allah admits them both into Paradise.'

And from him, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Al-Mi'za, from Dharih Al-Muharibi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What I endure from my people and my children when I inform them of the good in visiting the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is that they call me a liar and say, He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Dharih! Leave the people; let them go wherever they wish. By Allah, Allah boasts about the visitor of Al-Husayn, and the one who arrives is welcomed by the near angels and the bearers of His Throne. Indeed, He says to them: 'Do you not see the visitors of the grave of Al-Husayn? They have come to him yearning for him and for Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah. By My honor, My majesty, and My greatness, I will surely ordain for them My honor, and I will surely bring them into My Paradise, which I have prepared for My friends, My prophets, and My messengers. O My angels! These are the visitors of Al-Husayn, the beloved of Muhammad, My Messenger, and Muhammad is My beloved. And whoever loves Me, loves My beloved; and whoever loves My beloved, loves the one whom he loves; and whoever hates My beloved, hates Me. And whoever hates Me, it is incumbent upon Me to torment him with My severest torment, to burn him with the heat of My fire, and to make Hell his dwelling and his abode, and I will torment him with a torment that I do not torment anyone else with among the worlds.

My father, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan all narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani narrated to us from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn 'ibn 'Abd Allah [al-Rahman], from Qudamah ibn Malik, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits al-Husayn anticipating [reward from God], without arrogance and extravagance, and without showing off and seeking fame, his sins will be purified just as a garment is purified with water, so no impurity remains on it. And for him is recorded, with every step, a Hajj, and with every time he raises a foot, an 'Umrah.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khald, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khazzaz, from Harun ibn Harjah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn, knowing his right, seeking the Face of Allah the Exalted and the Hereafter?' He said to him, 'O Harun! Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, seeking the Face of Allah and the Hereafter, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sins and what followed.' Then he said to me three times, 'Did I not swear to you? Did I not swear to you? Did I not swear to you?'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abdillah, from 'Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Abdillah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), as a visitor, knowing his right, neither reluctant nor arrogant?' He said, 'One thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified 'Umrah are recorded for him. And if he was wretched, he is recorded as blissful, and he will continuously be submerged in the Mercy of Allah.'

My father narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūrī, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Manī‘ ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṣafwān ibn Mihrān al-Jammāl, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) while seeking (nearness to) Allāh, the Great and Almighty, will be accompanied by Jibra’īl, Mīkā’īl, and Isrāfīl until he is returned to his home.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, who said: I saw Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) when a group of people from Khurāsān had come to visit him. They asked him about going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him) and its rewards. He said: My father (peace be upon him) narrated to me that my grandfather (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever visits him seeking the Face of Allah, Allah will remove his sins as He removes the sins of a newborn whom its mother gave birth to. Angels will accompany him on his journey, flapping their wings over his head, having lined up their wings over him, until he returns to his family. The angels will seek forgiveness for him from his Lord, and Mercy will cover him from the highest part of the sky. The angels will call out to him, 'You have been blessed and blessed is the one to whose Ziyārah you have come,' and his family will be protected for him.

And 'Ubaydullāh ibn al-Faďl ibn Muḥammad ibn Hilāl narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sa'īd ibn Khaytham narrated to us from his brother Ma'mar, saying: I heard Zayd ibn 'Ali say: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), seeking nothing by it except the Face of Allāh, the Exalted, all of his sins will be forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea. So increase in visiting him, that Allāh may forgive your sins.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah Al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) for the sake of Allah and in the way of Allah, Allah will free him from the Hellfire and make him safe on the Day of the Great Terror. And whoever does not ask Allah, the Exalted, for any of the needs of this life or the Hereafter, He will grant it.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of our companions narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali Al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abi Khadijah, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He replied, 'Verily, it is the best of deeds.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abi Khadijah [Salama], from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He said: 'Verily, it is the best of deeds.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abi Khadijah, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He replied, 'Verily it is the best of deeds.'

Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from a man, from Aban al-Azraq, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One of the most beloved deeds to Allah, the Exalted, is the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and the best of deeds in the sight of Allah is bringing joy to a believer, and the closest a servant is to Allah, the Exalted, is when he is prostrating and weeping.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from Abi Jahm, from Abi Khadijah, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the extent (or greatness) of the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'It is the best of deeds.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars (may Allah have mercy on them) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said: I asked Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'It is like one who has visited Allah on His Throne.' I asked, 'What is the reward for one who visits any one of you (or one of you)?' He replied, 'It is like one who has visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him mercy) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Al-Khaybari, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad Al-Qummi, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever goes to the Ziyarah of the grave of Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) by the shore of the Euphrates is like the one who has gone to the Ziyarah of Allah above [in] His Throne.

And ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn and the group of my scholars narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Uyaynah the seller of reeds, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allāh will register him among the highest in ‘Illīyīn.

Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Dawud al-Mustariq, from Abdullah ibn Muskān, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allah will record him among those in A'alla 'Illiyin.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allah will register him among those in 'Illīyyīn.

And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, and from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, both from ‘Alī ibn Ismā‘īl, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr al-Zayyāt, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allāh will register him among those in A‘lā ‘Illīyyīn.

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl ibn Bazī‘, from al-Khaybari, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Qummī, who said: Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) said to me: Whoever visits the grave of my father in Baghdad is like whoever visited the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) and the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), except that the Messenger of Allāh and the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) have their own distinct status. He then said to me: Whoever visits the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh by the shore of the Euphrates is like whoever visited Allāh above His Throne [on His Kursi].

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Aban, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah will register him among those in 'Illīyyīn.

My father narrated to me (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdillah ibn Muskān, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), Allah will record him among the 'Illīyyīn.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Kufi, from 'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musalli, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah will register him among those in 'Illiyin.

And Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Shammūn Al-Basri narrated to me, who said: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to me from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said: I used to perform Hajj every year, but I delayed for one year. When the following year came, I performed Hajj and visited Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him). He said to me: 'O Bashīr, what prevented you from performing Hajj in our past year?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, I had a debt owed to me by people and I feared losing it, except that I spent the day of ‘Arafah near the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him).' He said to me: 'You did not miss anything of what the people of the Stand (at ‘Arafah) had. O Bashīr! Whoever visits the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him) while knowing his right, is like one who has visited Allāh on His Throne.' And from him, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Shammūn, who said: Ja’far ibn Muḥammad Al-Khuzā’i narrated to me from some of his companions from Jābir from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), similar to it. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’ from his uncle from a man from Jābir, similar to it.

My father and Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari (may Allāh have mercy on him) narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Al-Ḥasan, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥurayz, from someone who informed him, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to my mosque, the Mosque of Qubā, and prays two Rak’ah in it, will return with the reward of an ‘Umrah.

A group of our scholars narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali, from Ḥasan ibn Sa’īd, from Safwān ibn Yaḥyā, Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, and Faďālah ibn Ayyūb, all from Mu’āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said to Ibn Abī Ya’fūr: Do not neglect going to the sites (around Madīnah) or the Mosque of Qubā, for it is the “mosque founded on piety from the very first day.” (Do not neglect) the Well of Um Ibrāhīm, the Mosque of Faďīkh, the graves of the martyrs, nor the Mosque of Aḥzāb which is the Mosque of Fatḥ.

And it is narrated from one of them (the Imams) who said: If you have a stay in Madinah for three days, complete the prayer, and likewise in Makkah; and if you stay for three days, complete the prayer. And if you have a stay in Madinah for three days, fast three days; fast on Wednesday and pray on the night of Wednesday next to the Pillar of Repentance, which is the Pillar of Abu Lubabah, to which he tied himself until his excuse was revealed from the heavens. And sit by it on Wednesday, then come on the night of Thursday, which follows, next to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and sit by it your night and your day, and fast on Thursday. Then come to the pillar that is next to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him) on the night of Friday, and pray by it your night and your day, and fast in it on Friday. If you can, do not speak anything during these three days except what you must, and do not leave the mosque except for a need, and do not sleep at night or during the day [in night and day], then do so, for it is superior [for that is among that for which excellence is counted]. Then praise Allah on Friday, extol Him, send blessings on the Prophet, and ask for your need. And let what you say be: O Allah, whatever need I had to You, I hastened in seeking and requesting it, or a need I did not hasten, I asked You for it [or did not ask You for it], for I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), the Prophet of Mercy, in fulfilling my needs, small and large.

My group of scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I visit the mosques around the city; which one should I start with?' He said: 'Start with Quba and pray in it, and increase [your prayers], for it is the first mosque in this area in which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed. Then go to the Well of Umm Ibrahim and pray in it, for that is the dwelling place of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his place of prayer. Then you go to the Mosque of Fadikh and pray two Rak'ah in it, for your Prophet has prayed in it. When you have finished this side, go to the side of Uhud. Start with the mosque that is below the Harrah, and when you have prayed in it, then pass by the grave of Hamzah, and the hadith is long.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muḥammad ibn 'Īsā narrated to me from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Juwayriyah ibn al-'Alā', from some of our companions, who said: Whoever desires that he may look at Allāh on the Day of Judgment, and that the agony of death and the terror of the emergence [from the grave] may be made easy for him, let him increase in visiting the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him). Verily, visiting al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is visiting the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him).

And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz al-Kūfī narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb al-Zayyāt, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Faḍl ibn ‘Abd al-Malik – or from a man from al-Faḍl, from Abī Basīr, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, the visitor of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him) is the visitor of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab; and my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said: I asked Aba 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is [the reward] for one who visits one of you [one of you]?' He replied, '[It is] like [the reward of] one who visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad Al-Adami, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Zayd Al-Shahham, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who performs Ziyarah of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) [of the Messenger of Allah and Ali (peace be upon him)]?' He replied, 'It is like the Ziyarah of Allah on His Throne.' I asked, 'And what is the reward for one who performs Ziyarah of one of you (the Imams)?' He replied, 'It is like the Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Zayd Al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), the like of this.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, all of them, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Order our Shia to go to the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Verily, going to it increases sustenance, prolongs life, and repels the forces of evil. And going to it is obligatory upon every believer who acknowledges for al-Husayn the Imamate from Allah.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said: We heard him (Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)) say: If a full year passes and one does not visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah will reduce his lifespan by one year. And if I told you that one of you dies thirty years before his appointed time, I would be telling the truth, and this is because you neglect visiting al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So do not neglect his visitation, for Allah will prolong your lives and increase your sustenance. And if you neglect his visitation, Allah will reduce your lives and your sustenance. So compete with one another in visiting him and do not neglect that, for al-Husayn will testify on your behalf regarding that before Allah, His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), Fatimah (peace be upon her), and the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him).

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from someone who narrated to him, from Abdillah ibn Waddah, from Dawud al-Hammār, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever does not visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) has been deprived of much good, and one year will be reduced from his lifespan.

My father (peace be upon him) and the group of my scholars (peace be upon him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from some of our companions, from Aban, from 'Abd al-Malik al-Khath'ami, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He said to me: O 'Abd al-Malik! Do not neglect the Ziyarah of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) and order your companions to do so. Allah will prolong your life, increase your sustenance, Allah will make you live a blissful life, and you will not die except blissfully [as a martyr], and Allah will register you among the blissful ones.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the visitor of al-Husayn makes his sins a bridge at the door of his house, then crosses them, just as one of you leaves the bridge behind him when he crosses it.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Verily, when a man leaves his home to go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for him, upon leaving his family, with every step he takes, there is forgiveness of his sins. Then he continues to be purified with every step until he arrives at it. When he arrives, Allah speaks to him confidentially and says: 'O My slave! Ask Me and I will give you. Call Me and I will answer you. Seek from Me and I will give you. Ask Me for your need, and I will grant it for you.' And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) added: 'And it is a right upon Allah to give what was spent (by the pilgrim).'

And from him, through this chain, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from al-Ḥārith ibn Mughīrah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Allāh has angels dedicated to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him). When a man decides to visit him, Allāh gives his sins to these angels. With the first step he takes, they erase his sins; then with every additional step, they multiply his good deeds. His good deeds continue to multiply until they entitle him to Paradise. Then they surround him and sanctify him, and call out to the angels of the heavens: 'Sanctify the visitors of the beloved of the beloved of Allāh.' When the visitors perform Ghusl, Muḥammad (peace be upon him) calls out to them: 'O guests of Allāh! Be glad, for you will accompany me in Paradise.' Then the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) calls out to them: 'I am guarantor for the fulfillment of your needs and the removal of affliction from you in this world and the Hereafter.' Then they surround them on their right and left until they return to their families.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah Al-Jamurani Al-Razi, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Karim, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir Al-Ju'fi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in a long hadith: And when you return from the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), a caller will call out to you. If you heard his statement, you would spend your life at the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). And he will say: 'Bliss be to you, O servant of Allah! You have won and you are safe. Your past sins have been forgiven, so resume your deeds.' And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.

Abul ‘Abbās Al-Razzāz narrated to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb narrated to us from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Al-Khaybari, from Ḥusain ibn Muḥammad Al-Qummi, who said: Abul Ḥasan, Mūsā (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) said: The minimum reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) by the shores of the Euphrates (River) while knowing his rights and believing in his sanctity and Wilāyah is that all of their past and future sins will be forgiven.

My father narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from Zakariyyā al-Muʾmin Abū ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAbdillāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhili, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever wishes to be among the honoured by Allāh on the Day of Resurrection and to be included in the intercession of Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family), let him be a visitor of al-Ḥusayn. He will attain from Allāh bounty and honour, and good reward, and He will not question him about any sin he committed during his worldly life, even if his sins were as numerous as the grains of sand of ʿĀlij, the mountains of Ṭihāmah, and the foam of the sea. Verily, al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) was killed wrongfully and oppressed, his soul being thirsty, as were his family and his companions.

My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khālid Al-Barqi, from Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from his grandfather Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) who said: When one leaves his house to go to the Ziyārah of Abī ‘Abdillāh, Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him), Allāh will dedicate an angel to him who will place his finger on the back of the Zā`ir and who will start writing every word which comes out of his mouth until he arrives at the Ḥā`ir. After he exits from the doors of the Ḥā`ir, the angel will place his palm on the middle of the back of the Zā`ir and say, “Surely all of your past sins have been forgiven. Therefore, continue with good deeds.” The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: from Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abil Bilād, with the same chain.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khald, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, who said: I saw Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) when a group of people from Khurāsān had come to visit him. They asked him about going to the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and the rewards therein. He said: My father (peace be upon him) narrated to me that my grandfather (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever visits him, seeking the Face of Allah, Allah will remove his sins as He removes the sins of a newborn whom its mother gave birth to. Angels will accompany him on his journey, flapping their wings over his head, having lined up their wings over him, until he returns to his family. The angels will seek forgiveness for him from his Lord, and Mercy will cover him from the highest part of the sky. The angels will call out to him: 'You are blessed, and blessed is the one to whose Ziyārah you have come,' and he will be protected in his family.

My father, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub (may God be pleased with them) all narrated to me from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: Some of our companions asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about those who visited the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He replied, "It is equal to an 'Umrah."

And Muḥammad ibn Ja’far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Abī ‘Uthmān, from Ismā’īl ibn ‘Abbād, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali, from Abī Sa’īd Al-Madā’ini, who said: I entered upon Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, should I go to the grave of Ḥusain?' He said, 'Yes, O Abā Sa’īd! Go to the grave of the son of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family), the most blessed of the blessed ones, the most purified of the purified ones, and the most pious of the pious ones; for if you visit him, twenty-two ‘Umrah will be registered for you.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: The Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is equal to a purified and accepted 'Umrah.

My father (may God have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad and Abdillah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said to me: 'What is your opinion about it?' I said: 'Some of us say it is equal to one Hajj, and some of us say it is equal to one 'Umrah.' He said: 'It is equal to an accepted 'Umrah.'

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa‘d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from ‘Ali ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said: I asked Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) about the visitation (Ziyārah) of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him): ‘What is its virtue/reward?’ He (peace be upon him) said, ‘It is equal to an ‘Umrah.’

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn Abdillah both narrated to me from Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say: Indeed, the Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals a purified and accepted 'Umrah.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He said: 'What is its virtue? It is equal to an 'Umrah.'

A group of our companions narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā Al-‘Aťťār, from ‘Amraki ibn ‘Ali, from some of his companions, from one of them (the Imams), who said: Four ‘Umrah pilgrimages are equal to one Hajj, and the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is equal to one ‘Umrah.

And with this chain, from al-'Amriki ibn al-Bufaki, from one who narrated to him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Rabb [Ri'ab], who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He said, 'Yes, it equals an 'Umrah, and it is not fitting that one stay away from it for more than four years.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and the Ziyarah of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Ziyarah of the graves of the martyrs, equal the reward of a purified Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Abbas ibn 'Amir, who said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd al-Anbari informed me, I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, verily it is not every year that means are prepared for me to go out with for Hajj.' He said: 'When you desire Hajj and means are not prepared for you, go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for verily it will be registered for you as a Hajj. And when you desire 'Umrah and means are not prepared for you, go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for verily it will be registered for you as an 'Umrah.'

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Karim ibn Hassan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is meant by the saying that the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals one Hajj and one Umrah?' He replied: 'Verily, the Hajj and Umrah are here (in Makkah). And if a man intended to perform Hajj but was not able to do so, and he went (to the grave), Allah would record for him one Hajj. And if a man intended to perform Umrah but was not able to do so, one Umrah would be recorded for him.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Hariz, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: He (peace be upon him) said: The Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Ziyarah of the graves of the Martyrs, and the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals one Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) (he narrated) the same.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muḥammad ibn 'Īsā narrated to me from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasar, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Ziyārah (visitation) of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) equals a purified Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from them both, who said: The Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Ziyarah of the graves of the Martyrs, and the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equal the reward of one Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammāt, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: If a man intends to perform Hajj but is unable to do so, and he goes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and performs the 'Arafah standing (at his grave), that will suffice for him in place of Hajj.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah, who said: I wrote to the Righteous Slave (peace be upon him), 'If our Master deems it appropriate to inform me, (I would like to know) about the best rewards for the Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and whether it equals the reward of Hajj for those who have missed it.' He (peace be upon him) wrote back, 'It equals Hajj for those who have missed Hajj.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: The Ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is equal to twenty Hajjs and is better than twenty Hajjs. And Muḥammad ibn Ya'qūb narrated to me from a number of his companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, with his chain, similarly.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Shihab ibn 'Abd Rabbih, or from a man, from Shihab, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He asked me, saying: 'O Shihab! How many times have you performed Hajj?' I replied, 'Nineteen times.' He said to me, 'Complete it to twenty times, so that they are registered for you as the Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah, from Salih al-Nili, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, is like the one who performed Hajj one hundred times with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

And from him, from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah, from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah will register for him eighty purified Hajj.

Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Khaybari, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in the early days of the reign of Abu Ja'far, so he stayed in Najaf. He said: O Musa! Go to the main road and stand there and look, for a man will come to you from the direction of al-Qadisiyyah. When he comes close to you, say to him: 'Here is a man from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who is calling you,' and he will come with you. He said: So I went until I stood on the road, and the heat was intense. I kept standing until I was about to disobey [the Imam] and leave, when I saw something approaching that resembled a man on a camel. I kept looking at him until he came close to me, and I said: O this man, here is a man from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who is calling you, and he has described you to me. He said: Take us to him. He said: So I brought him until he made his camel rest in a place near the tent. The Imam called for him, so the Arab entered to him. I came close and stood at the door of the tent, hearing the speech but not seeing them. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked him: From where did you come? He said: From the furthest part of Yemen. He said: Are you from such and such place? He said: Yes, I am from such and such place. He said: What brought you here? He said: I came to visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: So you came without a specific need, solely for the visitation? He said: I came without a need, except that I pray near him and visit him, so I may send greetings to him and return to my family. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And what do you believe regarding his visitation? He said: We believe that in his visitation there is blessing for ourselves, our families, our children, our wealth, our livelihood, and the fulfillment of our needs. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Shall I not add to you from his virtue a virtue, O brother of Yemen? He said: Add to me, O son of the Messenger of Allah. He said: Verily, the visitation of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals one accepted, pure Hajj with the Messenger of Allah. He was amazed by that. He said: Yes, by Allah, and two accepted, pure, and pure Hajjs with t

And ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Yazīd ibn ‘Abdil Malik, who said: I was with Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) when a group of people passed by riding on donkeys. He asked me, 'Where are these people going?' I replied, 'To the graves of the martyrs.' He said, 'What prevents them from going to the Ziyārah of the lonely (abandoned) Martyr?' One of the people from Iraq asked him, 'Is his Ziyārah obligatory?' He said, 'His Ziyārah is better than one Hajj and one ‘Umrah, and another ‘Umrah and another Hajj,' until he counted twenty Hajjs and twenty ‘Umrahs, purified and accepted. Yazīd said: I swear to Allāh, I did not leave until a man came to him and said, 'I have performed Hajj nineteen times. Please pray to Allāh that He grants me the completion of the twentieth.' He asked, 'Have you visited al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' The man replied, 'No.' He said, 'Verily, his Ziyārah is better than twenty Hajjs.'

My father (peace be upon him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Abū al-Qāsim Hārūn ibn Muslim ibn Sa’dān, from Mas‘adah ibn Sadaqah, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who goes to the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'A Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) will be registered for him.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family)?!' He said, 'Yes, and two Ḥajj.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Two Ḥajj?' He said, 'Yes, and three.' He kept increasing the number until he reached ten. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Ten Ḥajj with the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family)?!' He said, 'Yes, and twenty Ḥajj.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Even twenty?' He kept increasing the number until he reached fifty, and then I fell silent.

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him, 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) as a visitor, knowing his right, neither arrogant nor disdainful?' He replied, 'A thousand purified Hajj and a thousand purified Umrah are recorded for him. And if he were among the wretched, he would be recorded among the blissful, and he would continuously be immersed in the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Matt al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from 'Ali ibn al-NuAli ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Abdillah ibn Muskān, who said: Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, manifests (His Mercy) to the Zuwwār of the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him) before the people of 'Arafāt. He fulfils their needs, forgives their sins, and accepts their intercession for their requests. Thereafter, He attends to the people of 'Arafāt and honours them in the same way.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him), and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ali ibn al-Husayn all narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from a man, from Sayf al-Tammār, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: The visitor of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) will be granted intercession on the Day of Judgment for one hundred men, all of whom Hell has become obligatory for, from those who were among the transgressors in this world.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from Abī ‘Abdillāh al-Mu’min, from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Verily, for Allah there are one hundred thousand glances (moments) every day and night towards the earth, through which He forgives whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills. And He specifically forgives those who perform Ziyārah to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), and their family members, and those for whom they will intercede on the Day of Resurrection, regardless of who they may be, even if they are a man upon whom Hell has been made obligatory. I asked: 'Even if he is a man upon whom Hell has been made obligatory?' He replied: 'Yes, as long as he is not a Nāṣibī.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abdillah ibn Waddah, from 'Abdillah ibn Shu'ayb Al-Tamimi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: On the Day of Judgment, a caller will call out, 'Where are the Shia of the family of Muhammad?' A group of people whose number cannot be counted except by Allah, the Exalted, will stand up and move aside from (the rest of) the people. Then a caller will call out, 'Where are the Zuwwar of the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him)?' A large group of people will stand up. They will be told, 'Take the hand of whomever you like and take them along (with you) to Paradise.' They will take whomever they like (to Paradise) to such an extent that a person will say to one of them, 'O so-and-so! Do you not remember me?! I stood up for you once (as an act of respect).' Therefore, the man will take him to Paradise without being stopped.

Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Musawi al-Alawi narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Hakam, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is a grave near you to which no anguished person goes without Allah removing his anguish and fulfilling his requests.

And from him, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Nahik, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Salamah, the companion of Al-Saburi, from Abi Al-Subah Al-Kinani, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is a grave near you to which no anguished person goes without Allah removing his anguish and fulfilling his request. And verily, next to it are four thousand angels since the day his life was taken, disheveled and covered with dust, weeping over him until the Day of Judgment. So whoever visits him, they escort him to his place of safety; and whoever is ill, they visit him; and whoever dies, they follow his funeral procession.'

My father narrated to me, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Zayyat, from Karam, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Verily, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed in anguish. And it is fitting for Allah that no one who comes to him in anguish returns except that Allah sends him back pleased.

And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Verily Allāh offered our Wilāyah to the inhabitants of different lands, but no one accepted it except the inhabitants of Kūfah. And verily, near it is a grave; no anguished person comes to it and prays four Rak’ah at it, except that Allāh sends him back pleased with the fulfillment of his request.

My father and the group of my scholars and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Amraki, from Yahya (who was in the service of Abi Ja'far (AS)), from some of our companions, from Abi Abdillah (AS) He said: Verily, on the outskirts of Kufah there is a grave; no distressed person visits it except that Allah relieves his distress, referring to the grave of al-Husayn (AS).

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Najiyah, from 'Amir ibn Kathir, from Abi al-Nuymir, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Verily, our Wilayah was presented to the inhabitants of the cities, but none accepted it as the people of Kufa did. And this is because the grave of Ali (peace be upon him) is in it, and close to it is another grave, meaning the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So, no one comes to it, prays two or four rak'ahs near it, and asks Allah for his need, except that Allah fulfills it for him. And verily, a thousand angels surround it every day.

Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Walid ibn Hassam, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My yearning for you made me endure the difficulties of traveling to you.' He said to me, 'Do not complain to your Lord! Why do you not go to the one who has more right upon you than I do?' Hearing that there was someone to whom I have more obligation than I have toward him was more difficult for me to handle than hearing him say, 'Do not complain to your Lord.' So I asked, 'To whom do I have more obligation than I have toward you?' He replied, 'Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him). Why do you not go to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and invoke Allah next to his grave and complain to Him about your needs?'

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad, from ‘Ali ibn Mu’allā, from Isḥāq ibn Ziyād [Yazdād], who said: A man came to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) and said, “I have sold all of my belongings and properties and I am thinking of moving to Makkah.” Imam (a.s.) said, “Do not do that because the people of Makkah disbelieve in Allāh publicly.” The man asked, “What about the city of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) (Madīnah)?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “The people there are even worse than the people of Makkah.” The man asked, “Then where should I move to?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Go to Kūfah in Iraq, for verily the blessings of that land span a twelve mile radius and there is a grave in its proximity which is not visited by any anguished and grieved person without Allāh relieving him from his anguish and grief.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, Ibn Abi Umayr, and Fadalah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you intend to leave the city, perform Ghusl, then go to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) after you have finished your needs, bid him farewell, and do as you did when you entered. And say: O Allah, do not make this the last visitation of my grave of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And if You cause me to die before that, then I testify in my death to what I testify to in my life, that there is no god but You and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your messenger.

My scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about bidding farewell to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: You say: 'May Allah bless you. Peace be upon you. May Allah not make this the last time I say peace to you.'

And by his chain, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, who said: I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when he intended to bid farewell before departing for 'Umrah. He approached the grave from the side of the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) after sunset, then offered salām to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and clung to the grave. Then he went to the pulpit, then turned back until he reached the grave, stood beside it, and prayed, pressing his left shoulder against the grave, close to the pillar that is below the carved, ringed pillar at the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him). He prayed six or eight rak'ahs while wearing his sandals. He said: The duration of his ruku' and sujud was three tasbihāt or more. When he finished that, he prostrated for a long prostration until his sweat moistened the pebbles. He said: And some of our companions mentioned that they saw him pressing his cheek to the ground of the mosque.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzaz Al-Kufi narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I go to perform 'Arfah (stand in devotion) near the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Well done, O Bashir! Whoever of the believers visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, on a day other than an Eid, Allah will record for him twenty Hajj, twenty Umrah (purified and accepted), and twenty battles with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam.' And whoever visits him on an Eid day, Allah will record for him one hundred Hajj, one hundred Umrah, and one hundred battles with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Arafah, knowing his right, Allah will record for him one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand Umrah, and one thousand battles with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam. I said to him, 'And how can I have something better than the standing (at 'Arafah)?' He looked at me as if slightly angry, then said, 'O Bashir! Indeed, when the believer visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Arafah, and performs Ghusl in the Euphrates, then turns towards it, Allah will record for him, with every step, a complete Hajj with all its rituals.' And I do not know him except that he said, 'And a battle.'

My father, ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan all narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from ‘Ali ibn Ismā‘īl ibn ‘Īsā, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Sa‘īd al-Zayyāt, from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh and Abā al-Ḥasan, and they both said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn on the Day of ‘Arafah, Allāh will turn him back with a heart filled with certainty.

And from them, from Sa'd, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrūq Al-Nahdī, from 'Ali ibn Asbāṭ, from some of our companions, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allāh, the Blessed and Exalted, begins by looking at the visitors of the grave of Al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) on the eve of 'Arafah. I asked, 'Before He looks at the people of the station (of 'Arafah)?' He said, 'Yes.' I asked, 'How is that?' He said, 'Because among those (people of 'Arafah) are illegitimately conceived children, and among these (visitors of Ḥusain) there are no illegitimately conceived children.'

My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Ali ibn Nu’mān, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muskān, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Verily, Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, manifests (His Mercy) to the Zuwwār of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) before He does (so) to the people who are in ‘Arafāt. He fulfils their needs, forgives their sins, and accepts their intercession for their requests, and thereafter He attends to the people in ‘Arafāt and honours them in the same way.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūrī, Abū Sa‘īd, who said: ‘Abdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Manī‘ ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus ibn Ya‘qūb ibn ‘Ammār, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever misses ‘Arafah in ‘Arafāt but catches it by the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), has not missed it. And verily, Allāh, the Blessed and Exalted, begins with the people of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) before the people of ‘Arafāt. Then he said: He mixes them with Himself [in Himself].

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqi, from al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from his grandfather al-Ḥasan, from Yūnus ibn Żabyān, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: Whoever performs the Ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha‘th of Sha‘bān, and the night of al-Fiṭr, and the night of ‘Arafah, all in one year, Allāh will register for him one thousand purified Hajj and one thousand accepted ‘Umrah, and one thousand needs from the needs of this world and the Hereafter will be fulfilled for him.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When it is the Day of 'Arafah, Allah, the Exalted, looks toward the visitors of the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and says to them, 'Continue (with good deeds), for I have forgiven you.' Then He directs His attention to the people in 'Arafat.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from someone he mentioned, from 'Umar ibn al-Hasan al-'Arzami, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: On the Day of 'Arafah, Allah looks toward the visitors of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and says, 'Return, forgiven for you is what has passed, and no sin will be recorded against any of them for seventy days from the day they return.'

My father (peace be upon him) and a group of my companions (peace be upon him) narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, all from al-‘Amrakī ibn ‘Alī, from Yaḥyā the servant of Abī Ja‘far the Second (peace be upon him), from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Bashīr al-Dahhān, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying while he was staying in al-Ḥīrah, with a group of the Shī‘ah around him. He turned his face toward me and said, 'O Bashīr! Did you perform Ḥajj this year?' I replied, 'May I be sacrificed for you! No, but I spent ‘Arafah at the grave—the grave of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him).' He said, 'O Bashīr! By Allāh, you did not miss anything of what the people of Ḥajj received in Makkah.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! ‘Arafah is only in Makkah, so explain this to me.' He said, 'O Bashīr! Verily, a man among you performs Ghusl on the shore of the Euphrates, then goes to the grave of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him), knowing his rights. Allāh grants him for every step he raises or places one hundred accepted Ḥajj, one hundred purified ‘Umrah, and one hundred battles alongside a sent Prophet against the enemies of Allāh and the enemies of His Messenger. O Bashīr! Listen and convey to those whose hearts can bear it: Whoever visits al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Arafah is like one who visits Allāh on His Throne.'
