Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Isma'il al-Abdi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman (or al-Hasan), from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will register for him one million Hajj with the Qa'im (peace be upon him) and one million 'Umrah with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and freeing one million slaves, and carrying one million horses in the way of Allah. And Allah will call him, 'My truthful slave who believed in My promise.' And the angels will say, 'So-and-so is truthful; Allah has purified him from above His Throne.' And he will be called 'Karub' on earth.

My father (peace be upon him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said: Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Arafah, recognizing his rights, Allāh will register for him the reward of one thousand Hajj and one thousand ‘Umrah and one thousand battles with a messenger Prophet. And whoever visits on the first day of Rajab, Allāh will forgive him completely.

My father, my brother, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Alī Al-Madā’īnī, who said: Muḥammad ibn Sa‘īd Al-Bajalī informed me from Qabīṣah, from Jābir Al-Ju‘fī, who said: I entered upon Ja‘far ibn Muḥammad (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā, and he said to me: These are the visitors of Allāh, and it is an obligation upon the visited to honor the visitor. Whoever spends the night by the grave of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the night of ‘Āshūrā will meet Allāh on the Day of Judgment stained with his blood, as if he had been killed with him in his courtyard. And he said: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā and spends the night by it is like one who was martyred in front of him.

Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ubayd al-Ju'fi narrated to me, saying: Husayn ibn Sulayman narrated from Husayn ibn Asad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Whoever visits Husayn on the Day of 'Ashura, Paradise becomes mandatory for him.

And Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd Al-Anbāri, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā, knowing his rights, is like the one who visits Allāh on His Throne.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to me from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur al-'Ami, from someone whom he mentioned, from them (the Imams (peace be upon him)), who said: Whoever goes to the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of 'Ashura is like one who was ensanguined with his blood in front of him.

And Muḥammad ibn Abī Yāsir [Sayyār] al-Madāʾinī narrated through his chain of transmission, saying: Whoever gives water on the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ near the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is like the one who gave water to the camp of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and stood witness with him.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al-Mawsawi narrated to me from Ubayd Allah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd Al-Shahham, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, Allah will forgive him his past and future sins. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him the reward of one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified 'Umrah. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Ashura, it is as if he has visited Allah above [in] His Throne.

My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb all narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: On the fifteenth of Sha’bān, a caller calls out from the highest horizon: O those who have come to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (peace be upon him)! Return forgiven and your rewards will be given (to you) by Allāh, your Lord, and by Muḥammad (peace be upon him and his family), your Prophet.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali Al-Zaytuni and others, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Hamzah, from 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), both said: Whoever wishes for one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand prophets to shake his hand, let him visit the grave of Abi 'Abdillah Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) on the fifteenth of Sha'ban. Verily, the souls of the prophets (peace be upon them) ask permission from Allah to visit him, and permission is granted to them. Among them are five: the Ulul 'Azm (Prophs of Determination) from the Messengers. We asked, 'Who are they?' He said, 'Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and Muhammad (peace be upon them all).' We asked him, 'What is the meaning of Ulul 'Azm?' He said, 'They were sent to the east and west of the earth, to its jinn and its humans.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Sandal, from Harun ibn Harizah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When it is the middle of Sha'ban, a caller calls out from the highest horizon: O those who have come to the Ziyarah of Husayn (peace be upon him)! Return, forgiven; your reward is with your Lord and Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), your Prophet.

And Sāfi Al-Barqi narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) for three consecutive years, without a break, on the fifteenth of Sha'bān, his sins will be forgiven.

And through his chain of narration, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, who said: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: The one who performs Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the fifteenth of Sha'ban, his sins will be forgiven, and no bad deed will be recorded against him in that year until the year passes. And if he performs Ziyarah in the following year, Allah will forgive his sins.

My scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Sarah al-Madaini, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj or someone else named al-Husayn, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on one of three nights, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what followed. I said, Which of the nights, may I be sacrificed for you? He said: The night of al-Fitr, the night of al-Adha, and the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban.

And my father, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khald, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Husayn ibn Rashid, from Yunus ibn 'Abdi, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, and the night of al-Fitr, and the night of 'Arafah, in one year, Allah will record for him one thousand purified Hajj and one thousand accepted 'Umrah, and a thousand needs of this life and the Hereafter will be fulfilled for him.

Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) on the fifteenth of Sha'bān, Allāh will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what followed.

Abū ‘Abdillāh Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb ibn Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn Walīd, from Yūnus ibn Ya’qūb, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: O Yūnus! On the night of the fifteenth of Sha‘bān, Allāh will forgive every believer who goes to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) all of their past and future sins, and they will be told, 'Go toward (committing) good deeds.' I said, 'Is all of this for those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the fifteenth of Sha‘bān?' He said, 'O Yūnus! If I told people about what is given to those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on this night, the males of the men would travel riding on wood (placed on the back of saddleless camels).'

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Musa narrated to me from Ubaydillah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, Allah will forgive him his past and future sins. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him the reward of one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified 'Umrah. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Ashura, it is as if he has visited Allah above His Throne.

Muhammad ibn Ja' ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad' ibn al-Husayn' ibn Abi al-Khattab' from Muhammad' ibn Isma'il' from Salih' ibn 'Uqbah' from Bashir' al-Dahhan' who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Any believer who visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, on a day other than an Eid or 'Arafah, Allah will record for him twenty Hajj (pilgrimages) and twenty 'Umrah (minor pilgrimages), purified and accepted, and twenty battles (of jihad) with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the minimum reward for the one who performs Ziyarah to al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said to me, 'O Abdullah, verily the minimum that will be for him is that Allah will protect him in his self and his wealth until He returns him to his family. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will be the Protector for him.' My father narrated to me (may he be pleased with him) from Saad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee, from Sahl, like his first hadith in the chapter.

My father narrated to me, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-'Amriki ibn 'Ali al-Bufaki, from Sandal, from Dawud ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) every Friday, Allah will surely forgive him, and he will not leave this world with any regret in his heart, and his dwelling will be in Paradise with al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). Then he said: O Dawud! Who does not like to be the neighbor of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) in Paradise? I said: Those who do not achieve salvation.

And from him, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from al-‘Amraki, from Ṣandal, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for the one who performs the Ziyārah of al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) every month?' He replied to him, 'The reward of one hundred thousand martyrs, like the martyrs of Badr.'

And by his chain, from Sandal, from Abi al-Subbah al-Kinani, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When it is the Night of Qadr, wherein every wise affair is made distinct, a caller will call out on that night from inside the Throne: 'Verily, Allah has forgiven whoever visited the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on this night.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I spend the Day of 'Arafah at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Well done, O Bashir! Any believer who visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), acknowledging his right, on a day other than an Eid or the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him twenty purified and accepted Hajj, twenty accepted 'Umrah, and twenty battles fought with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam.' And whoever visits him on an Eid day... and the hadith continues in its full length.

My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Manī‘ ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever performs Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates and visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), becomes like the day his mother gave birth to him, free of sins, even if he had committed major sins. And they used to love the man who, when visiting the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), would perform Ghusl. And when bidding farewell, he would not perform Ghusl, but would wipe his hand over his face when bidding farewell.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in a long hadith: He said, 'Woe to you, O Bashir! Verily, when a believer visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, and performs Ghusl in the Euphrates, then departs, for every step he takes, a Hajj and an 'Umrah, both accepted and purified, and a Ghaazwah (battle/expedition) with a Messenger Prophet or a Just Imam are written for him.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from al-‘Amrakī ibn ‘Alī, from Yaḥyā – who was in the service of Imam Abī Ja‘far the Second (peace be upon him) – from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Bashīr al-Dahhān, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), while he was staying in al-Ḥīrah, with a group of Shī‘ah around him. He turned his face toward me and said, 'O Bashīr! Did you perform Ḥajj this year?' I replied, 'May I be sacrificed for you! No, but instead I spent ‘Arafah at the Grave – the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'O Bashīr! By Allah, you did not miss anything of what was for the people of Makkah in Makkah.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! ‘Arafah is (only) in Makkah, so explain this to me.' He said, 'O Bashīr! Verily, a man from you performs Ghusl on the shore of the Euphrates, then comes to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his rights. Allah will give him, for every foot he raises or places, one hundred accepted Ḥajj, and with them one hundred purified ‘Umrah, and one hundred battles with a sent Messenger [against the most hostile enemy of his], against the enemies of Allah and the enemies of the Messenger, and he mentioned the hadith.'

Abū Muḥammad Hārūn ibn Mūsā Al-Tal’ukbari narrated to me from Abī ‘Ali Muḥammad ibn Hammām ibn Suhayl, from Aḥmad ibn Mābundād, from Aḥmad ibn Mu’āfā Al-Tha’labi, from the people of Ra’s Al-‘Ayn, from ‘Ali ibn Ja’far Al-Humāni, who said: I heard ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad Al-‘Askari (peace be upon him) say: Whoever leaves his home intending to perform the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (peace be upon him), and goes to the Euphrates and performs Ghusl with its water, Allāh will record him among the successful. And when he says Salām to Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), Allāh will record him among the winners. And when he finishes his prayer, an angel will come to him and say: Verily the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) conveys his Salām to you and tells you: As for your sins, they have been forgiven to you; start again with the deeds.

Muhammad ibn Hammām ibn Suhayl Al-Iskāfī narrated to me from Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Mālik Al-Fazārī, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Rawāsi, from someone who narrated to him, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever goes to (the Ziyārah of) Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) and performs Wuďū and Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates, does not raise a foot or place a foot down without Allāh registering for him a Hajj and an ‘Umrah.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan both narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Yusuf al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When you go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), go to the Euphrates and perform Ghusl near his grave.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubaydillah Al-Musi narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Muhammad Al-Farrash, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad Al-Tahhan, from Bashir Al-Dahhan, from Rifah ibn Musa Al-Nahhas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Verily, whoever travels to the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, arrives at the Euphrates, performs Ghusl in it, and steps out of the water, he will be like one who has stepped out of his sins. And when he walks toward the Hā'ir, for every step he takes, Allah will record ten good deeds for him and erase ten bad deeds.

My scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is it obligatory to perform Ghusl for the one who visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'No.'

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), from Jafar al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), narrated to me from Ubaydillah ibn Nahik, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hanifah al-Sabiq [al-Sa'iq], from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If you are close to him – referring to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) – and you are able to perform Ghusl, then perform it; otherwise, perform Wudu and then go to him.

Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn Faďďāl, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Abī Nāb Ḥasan ibn ‘Aťiyyāh, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about performing Ghusl when going to the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him). He replied, “Performing Ghusl is not obligatory.”

Al-Hasan ibn al-Zibriqan al-Tabari narrated to me through his own chain, elevating it to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'Sometimes when we visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), it is difficult for us to perform Ghusl for the visitation due to the cold or other reasons.' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'Whoever performs Ghusl in the Euphrates and visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), an incalculable amount of merit is recorded for him. And whenever he returns to the place where he performed Ghusl and performs Wuďū and visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), that same reward is recorded for him.'

Al-Hasan ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Asim ibn Humayd Al-Hannat, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever from among our Shia does not visit the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is deficient in faith and deficient in religion, and even if he enters Paradise, he will be below the believers in Paradise.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi al-Mi'za, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever does not visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) until he dies, he is deficient in religion and deficient in faith, and even if he enters Paradise, he will be below the believers in Paradise.

My father and ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from his father, from Sayf ibn ‘Amīrah, from a man, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever does not visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) while he claims to be among our Shī‘ah, until he dies, is not among our Shī‘ah. And even if he is among the people of Paradise, he is from the visitors of the people of Paradise.

And through his chain, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Whoever wants to know that he is from the people of Paradise, let him present our love to his heart; if it accepts it, then he is a believer. And whoever loves us, let him desire the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Whoever is a visitor to al-Husayn (peace be upon him), we recognize him by his love for us, the Ahl al-Bayt, and he will be from the people of Paradise. And whoever is not a visitor to al-Husayn, his faith is incomplete.

My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from ‘Amraki ibn ‘Alī Al-Būfaki, from someone who narrated to him, from Sandal, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a person who neglects the Ziyārah (visitation) of the grave of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him) without any excuse. He said: 'This is a man from the inhabitants of Hell.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Kufi al-Qurashi narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from someone who narrated to him, from Ali ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: If one of you performs Hajj a thousand times, but does not visit the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he has left a right among the rights of Allah, the Exalted. And when asked about that, he said: The right of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is obligatory upon every Muslim.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khālid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, who said: Hisham ibn Salim from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said in a long hadith of his: A man came to him and asked him, 'Is your father visited?' He said, 'Yes.' He asked, 'What is for the one who visits him?' He said, 'Paradise, if he believes in his Imamate.' He asked, 'What is for the one who leaves it, preferring to do so?' He said, 'Regret on the Day of Regret.' And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Sulayman ibn Zayd, the freedman of Tirbal, and others, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The charity of one Dirham in Kufah is counted as two hundred Dirhams elsewhere, and two Rak'ahs prayed in it are counted as one hundred Rak'ahs.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl ibn Zakariyya, from Najm ibn Hutm, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: If people knew what is in the Mosque of Kufah, they would prepare for it provisions and a mount from a distant place. And he said: An obligatory prayer in it equals one Hajj, and a recommended prayer in it equals one 'Umrah.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from someone who narrated to him, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: An obligatory prayer in the Mosque of Kufah is equal to an accepted Hajj, and a recommended prayer in it is equal to an accepted 'Umrah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Uthman, from one who narrated to him, from Harun ibn Harijah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you establish all of your prayers in the Mosque of Kufah?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'If I were close to it, I would hope that no prayer would be missed by me in it.' He said: 'Do you know its merit?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'There is no righteous slave nor prophet except that he has prayed in the Mosque of Kufan.' So much so that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you know where you are right now, O Muhammad?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'You are in front of the Mosque of Kufan.' So he said: 'Ask your Lord for permission so that I may descend and pray in it.' So he asked for permission and it was granted to him, so he descended and prayed two Rak'ah in it. And indeed, the obligatory prayer in it equals one thousand prayers, and the recommended prayer in it equals five hundred prayers. And indeed its front [its Qiblah] is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its right side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its left side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its back is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And indeed sitting in it without prayer or remembrance is worship, and if people knew what is in it, they would come to it even if they had to crawl.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say, 'One prayer in the Mosque of Kufah is equal to one thousand prayers.'

And with this chain of narration, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: Makkah is the sanctuary of Allah, His Messenger, and Ali (peace be upon him). One prayer in it is equal to one hundred thousand prayers, and one Dirham in it is equal to one hundred thousand Dirhams. And Madinah is the sanctuary of Allah, His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali, Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him). One prayer in its mosque is equal to ten thousand prayers, and one Dirham in it is equal to ten thousand Dirhams. And Kufah is the sanctuary of Allah, His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali, Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him). One prayer in its mosque is equal to one thousand prayers.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Matt al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abi Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of our companions, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The border of the Mosque of Sahlah is Rawha Rawha.

My brother ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs ibn Aḥmad, from ‘Imrān ibn Mūsā, from Ḥasan ibn Mūsā Al-Khashab, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥassān, from his uncle ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Kuthayr, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: I heard him (the Imam) say to Abā Ḥamzah Al-Thumāli, 'O Abā Ḥamzah! Did you see my uncle on the night of his uprising?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Did he pray in the Mosque of Suhayl?' He said, 'Where is the Mosque of Suhayl? Do you mean the Mosque of Sahlah?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Verily, if he had prayed two Rak’ah there and then sought refuge with Allāh, He would have protected him for one year.' Abū Ḥamzah said to him, 'May I sacrifice my father and mother for you! Are you referring to this (known) Mosque of Sahlah?' He said, 'Yes.' It contains the house of Ibrāhīm where he used to rise against the giants. It contains the house of Idrīs where he used to sew. It contains the place where the rider ties his camel. It contains a green rock which has the pictures of the prophets within it, and the clay under this rock is the clay from which Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, created the prophets. The Mi’rāj (ascension) took place in it, and it is the great Fārūq (separator). A part of it is a place, and it is the route people will pass. It is part of Kūfān, and the trumpet will be blown in it, and to it is the gathering. Seventy thousand people will be resurrected from its side and they will enter Paradise without any judgment. Those are the ones whom Allāh has set aright and upon whom He has increased His blessings. Verily they are the devout winners who will be rewarded before others. They love to repel any praise about themselves and they are terrified of meeting Allāh with His justice. They are quick in obeying Allāh, they perform good deeds, and they understand that Allāh sees what they do. There will not be any judgment nor torment for them. Verily Allāh removes the rancour and purifies the believers. From its middle moved the mountain of Ahwāz, and a time has come upon it and it was populated.

My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Abu 'Abdillah Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abdillah al-Razi al-Jamurani, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from his father Sayf, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) or from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'Which part of the earth is the most superior after the Sanctuary of Allah (Exalted and Mighty) and the Sanctuary of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family)?' He replied, 'Kufah, O Abu Bakr! It is the purified and virtuous land. It contains the graves of the sent prophets, the graves of those who were not sent, and the truthful successors. It contains the Mosque of Suhayl, in which every prophet sent by Allah had prayed. From it, the Justice of Allah will appear, and its Qa'im (Rising One) and those who will lead after him will be in it. It is indeed the abodes of the prophets, the successors, and the righteous ones.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when a man entered, said Salam, and sat down. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asked him, 'From which country are you?' The man said, 'I am from the people of Kufah, and I am a lover and follower of yours.' He said, 'Do you establish all of your prayers in the Mosque of Kufah?' The man said, 'No.' He said, 'Verily you are deprived of the good.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asked, 'Do you perform a Ghusl once a day with the water of your Euphrates?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a week?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a month?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a year?' He said, 'No.' He said to him, 'Verily you are deprived of the good.' Then he asked, 'Do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) once a week?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a month?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a year?' He said, 'No.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'Verily you are deprived of the good.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: O Abu 'Ubaydah! Do not neglect establishing prayers in the Mosque of Kufah even if you have to crawl to it, for establishing one prayer there is equal to establishing seventy prayers in other mosques.

Abū ‘Abdil Raḥmān Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥusain Al-‘Askari narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Sa’īd, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) say: Establishing one prayer alone in the Mosque of Kūfah has more value than establishing seventy congregational prayers in any other mosque.

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Mahziyar, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Khalid Al-Qalanisi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: One prayer in the Mosque of Kufah is equal to one thousand prayers.

My father and Muhammad ibn Abdillah both narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fudayl al-A'war, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said: I met him after the people had prayed 'Asr. He said, 'I have not prayed Dhuhr yet, so do not keep me, and proceed with success.' I asked, 'Why have you delayed it until now?' He said, 'I had a need in the market, so I delayed the prayer until I could pray in the mosque, for the merit that has reached me about it.' I asked, 'What has been narrated about it?' He said, 'So-and-so informed me from so-and-from A'ishah, who said, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) say: I was ascended to the heavens, and I descended to the earth, then I was brought down to the mosque of my father Nuh (a.s.) and my father Ibrahim, which is the Mosque of Kufa, and I prayed two Rak'ah in it.' Then it was said: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said, 'Verily, the obligatory prayer in it equals a purified Hajj, and the voluntary prayer in it equals a purified 'Umrah.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, who said: Abū Yūsuf Ya'qūb ibn 'Abdillah, from the descendants of Ab Fāṭimah, narrated to me from Ismā'īl ibn Zayd, the freedman of 'Abdillah ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī, from Abū 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) while he was in the Mosque of Kūfah and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Believers, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' He (peace be upon him) responded. The man said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I intend to go to the Farthest Mosque (Bayt al-Maqdis), so I wanted to bid you farewell.' He (peace be upon him) asked, 'What do you hope to gain by that?' The man said, 'The reward (al-faḍl), may I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Sell your camel, eat your provisions, and pray in this mosque, for the obligatory prayer performed in it is a purified Hajj, and the recommended prayer is a purified 'Umrah.' The blessings of it extend to twelve miles. Its right side is prosperity, and its left side is cunning. In its center is a spring of oil, a spring of milk, a spring of water for drinking for the believers, and a spring of water for purification for the believers. The ark of Noah sailed from it, and Nasr, Yaghuth, and Ya'q were placed in it. Seventy prophets and seventy successors prayed in it, and I am one of them. And he (peace be upon him) pointed to his chest with his hand, saying: 'No distressed person asks Allah for anything in it (the Mosque of Kūfah) regarding any of the needs, except that Allah answers him and relieves him of his distress.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khald al-Barqi; and Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah narrated to me from his father 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Najiyah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Pray at the head of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Musa ibn 'Umar, and Ayyub ibn Nuh, from 'Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abi al-Yasa', who said: A man asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening, saying: 'When I go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), do I make it my qiblah when I pray?' He replied, 'Move aside a little to the side.'

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Aṭiyyah, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: When you have finished saying salām to the martyrs, you come to the grave of al-Ḥusayn, then you place it before you, then you pray as much as seems good to you.

And from him, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from 'Ali ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said, 'We visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him); how should we establish prayer next to him?' He said, 'Stand behind him near his shoulders, then send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and send blessings upon al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khālid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, who said: Hisham ibn Salim from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that a man came to him and asked him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, is your father visited?' He said, 'Yes, and prayer is established next to him,' and he said, 'And prayer is established behind him, and one does not go forward (in front of him).'

‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Ya‘qūb al-Kisā‘ī narrated to me, saying: ‘‘Ali ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl narrated to us from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘īd from Muṣḍiq ibn Ṣadaqah from ‘Ammār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about establishing prayers in the Ḥā’ir. He replied, ‘Prayer is only the obligatory prayer with shortening (Qaṣr), and do not establish the voluntary (Nawāfil) prayers.’

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about voluntary prayers near the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and the shrines of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the two Holy Sanctuaries, and performing voluntary prayers in them while we are deficient (in obligatory prayers). He said: 'Yes, perform voluntary prayers as much as you are able; it is good.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Aba al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! Can I perform voluntary prayers in the two Ḥarams and next to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) while I am a Muqassir (one shortening prayers)?' He replied, 'Yes, as much as you are able.'

My father (peace be upon him) and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Sa‘īd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī, from ‘Alī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about voluntary prayer during Taqsīr (shortening) at the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), the sites of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the two Ḥarams. He replied, 'Yes, perform voluntary prayers as much as you are able.'

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Musiwi narrated to me from Ubaydillah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He said to a man: O so-and-so! What prevents you, when a need arises for you, from going to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), praying four Rak'ahs there, and then asking for your need? Verily, the obligatory prayer performed there equals a Hajj, and the Nafilah prayer equals an 'Umrah.

My father and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Abi 'Abdillah Al-Jamurani Al-Razi, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim Abi 'Ali, from Al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Jabir Al-Ju'fi, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Al-Mufaddal, as part of a long hadith about the Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Then you proceed to your prayer, and for you, for every Rak'ah you bow in prostration next to him, is the reward of one who performed one thousand Hajj, one thousand 'Umrah, freed one thousand slaves, and stood in the way of Allah one thousand times with a Messenger Prophet.' And he mentioned the hadith.

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Alā ibn Razīn, from Shu’ayb Al-‘Aqraqūfi, from Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him, 'What is the reward and recompense for the one who visits the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him)? May I be your ransom.' He replied, 'O Shu’ayb! No one establishes prayer next to him without Allāh accepting it, and no one supplicates next to him without his supplication being answered, either immediately or eventually.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, tell me more about it.' He replied, 'O Shu’ayb! The least (rewarding statement) with which a visitor of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) will be addressed is: 'O Slave of Allāh! Verily your sins have been forgiven.' Therefore, start again with new deeds.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said: I heard Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say, 'The location of the grave of Al-Ḥusayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) has been a garden from the gardens of Paradise since the day he was buried in it.' And he said, 'The location of the grave of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is an oasis from the oases of Paradise.'

My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd Al-Yaqťini, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il Al-Basri, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: The sacred boundary (hurmat) of the grave of Al-Husayn is one parasang by one parasang from each of its four sides.

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from Manṣūr ibn ‘Abbās, who narrated that: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: The sacred boundary (ḥaram) of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is five parasangs from each of the four sides of the grave.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said: I heard Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Verily there is a known boundary for the location of the grave of Ḥusain ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him); whoever knows it and seeks refuge in it will be protected. I said, 'Describe its boundary for me, may I be your ransom.' He replied, 'Wipe from the location of his grave today, and wipe twenty-five ells from the side of his feet, and twenty-five ells from what faces his face, and twenty-five ells from behind him, and twenty-five ells from the side of his head. And the location of his grave, since the day he was buried, is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and from it is a ladder by which the deeds of his visitors ascend to the heavens. So there is no angel nor prophet in the heavens except that they ask Allah for permission to go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him). So a crowd descends and a crowd ascends.'

My father and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Harun ibn Muslim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ash'ath, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from 'Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: The grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is twenty cubits by twenty cubits, square, a garden from the gardens of Paradise... and he mentioned the hadith. And from him (the narrator) from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Is'hak ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly.

My father, my brother, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on them all, narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said: I and 'Amir ibn 'Abdillah ibn Judh'ah al-Azdi were with Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him). 'Amir said to him, 'People claim that the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was buried in al-Rahbah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No.' 'Amir asked, 'So where was he buried?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When he died, al-Hasan (peace be upon him) carried him and brought him to the rear of Kufah, close to al-Najaf, to the left of al-Ghari and to the right of al-Hirah. He was buried among white gravel. I said, 'Afterwards, I went to the location and presumed I had found a place from it, then I came to him and informed him.' He said, 'You were right, you were right, three times. May Allah have mercy on you.' [You were right, may Allah have mercy on you, three times.]

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn al-Khallal, from his grandfather, who said: I asked al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), 'Where did you bury the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'We carried him out at night. We passed the mosque of al-Ash'ath and then moved toward the area behind Gharī.'

My group of scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Qasīm ibn Muḥammad, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said: ‘Umar (‘Amr) ibn Yazīd came to me and said, “Ride.” So I rode with him, and we traveled until we arrived at the house of Ḥafs Al-Kunāsi. He brought him out, and he rode with us. We traveled until we arrived in Gharī, and we reached a grave. He said, “Come down! This is the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him).” We asked him, “From where do you know this?” He said, “I came to it with Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) when he was in Ḥīrah more than once, and he informed me that it is his grave.”

My father and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, from Yazīd ibn ‘Umar ibn Ťalḥah, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said, while he was in Ḥīrah: 'Do you not want that which I promised you?' I said, 'Yes,' meaning going to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him). He said, so he rode, and his son Ismā’īl rode with him, and I rode with them. Until when he passed Thawiyyah, and it was between Ḥīrah and Najaf near some white gravel, he dismounted, and Ismā’īl dismounted, and I dismounted with them. So he prayed, and Ismā’īl prayed, and I prayed. Then he said to Ismā’īl, 'Stand and say Salām to your grandfather, Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him).' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is Ḥusain (peace be upon him) not in Karbalā?' He said, 'Yes. However, when his head was carried to Shām, a servant of ours stole it and buried it next to the Commander of the Believers.'

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan both narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqbah, from al-Hasan al-Khazzaz al-Washsha, from Abi al-Faraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he passed through the area behind Kufah. He stopped there and prayed two Rak'ah. Then he moved forward a little and prayed another two Rak'ah. Then he moved forward a little further and prayed another two Rak'ah. Then he said, 'This is the location of the grave of the Commander of the Believers.' I said, 'May I sacrifice myself for you! What were the other two locations on which you prayed?' He replied, 'The location of the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the location of the pulpit of the Qa'im (peace be upon him).'

And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan and Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn both narrated to me from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father ‘Ali, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm ibn Bukayr, who said: I mentioned it to Abī al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), and he narrated the hadith in its entirety.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn both narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar, from his father Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam narrated to me from a man from Yunus ibn Dhubyan, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Al-Hira during the days of his visit to Abu Ja'far on a clear, moonlit night. He looked up at the sky and said, 'O Yunus, do you not see how beautiful these stars are? Indeed, they are a source of security for the inhabitants of the heavens, and we are a source of security for the inhabitants of the earth.' Then he said, 'O Yunus, instruct them to saddle the mule and the donkey.' When they were saddled, he asked, 'O Yunus, which one do you think I prefer, the mule or the donkey?' I thought that the mule would be more preferable to him due to its strength, so I said, 'The donkey.' He then said, 'I would prefer that you bring it to me.' I said, 'I have done so.' So he mounted, and I mounted as well. When we left Al-Hira, he said, 'Proceed, O Yunus.' He then began to say, 'Turn right, turn left,' until we reached the red rocks. He said, 'This is the place.' I replied, 'Yes.' He then turned right and headed to a spot where there was water and a spring. He performed ablution. Then he approached a small hill, prayed there, then leaned on it and cried. After that, he moved to another smaller hill and did the same thing. Then he said, 'O Yunus, do as I have done.' So I did as he instructed. When I finished, he asked me, 'O Yunus, do you know this place?' I replied, 'No.' He said, 'The place where I first prayed is the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the other hill is the resting place of the head of al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).' The accursed Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad, may Allah curse him, when he sent the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) to Syria, it was returned to Kufa. He then ordered it to be removed from the city so that the people of Kufa would not be tempted by it. Thus, Allah placed it near the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), so the head is with the body, and the body is with the head.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab al-Zayyat, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isḥaq ibn Jarir, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: When I was in al-Hīrah, in the presence of Abū al-'Abbās, I would visit the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) at night, and he was in the region of al-Najaf, on the side of al-Ghārī al-Nu'mān. So I would pray the night prayer there, and I would depart before dawn.

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjāl, from Ṣafwān ibn Mihrān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the location of the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him). He said, so he described its location to me as being about a mile away. He said, so I went to it and prayed near it. Then I returned to Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) the following day and informed him of my going and my praying near it. He said, 'You were correct.' So I remained for twenty years praying near it.

My father and a group narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from a man who said: Abul Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) sent me some clothes that were wrapped up, in the middle of which there was some clay. I asked the person who had brought the clothes about this clay. He said, “It is the clay of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.). He (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) does not send clothes or anything else to anyone without putting some of this clay within it and he says, ‘It is protection with the permission of Allāh.”

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Rub the palates of your children with the clay of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for verily it is protection.

And from him, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-'Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq, from Yunus, from 'Isa ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from his aunt, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Verily, in the clay of the Hā'ir, where al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is buried, there is a cure for every disease and protection from every fear.

And my father narrated to me (may Allah have mercy on him) from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-‘Amrakī ibn ‘Alī al-Būfakī, from Yaḥyā – who was in the service of Abī Ja‘far the Second – from ‘Īsā ibn Sulaymān, from Muḥammad ibn Mārid, from his aunt, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Verily, in the clay of the Ḥā’ir, where al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is buried, is a cure for every disease and protection from every fear.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Khaybari, from Abi Wallad, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: If a sick believer knows the right of Abi Abdillah, his sanctity, and his divine authority, clay taken from his grave, even from a distance of one mile, will be a cure and healing for him.

My father narrated to me, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali, from Yūnus ibn Rafī’, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: There is indeed at the head of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him) a red dust, in which is a cure for every disease except death (al-sām). He said: So I went to the grave after we had heard this ḥadīth, and we dug at the head of the grave. When we had dug about an ell, red dust like sand, about the size of a dirham, flowed down upon us from the head of the grave. We carried it to Kūfah, mixed it, and stored it. Then we began giving it to the people, and they would cure themselves with it.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him), Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Rizq Allah ibn al-Ala, from Sulayman ibn Amr al-Sarraj, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The clay of the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) is taken from near the grave to the extent of seventy ba's.

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥammād al-Anṣārī, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: When one of you takes clay from the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), let him say: O Allāh! I ask You through the right of the angel who picked it, and the Messenger who appointed it, and the Successor who is lying within it, to make it a cure from every disease, such and such, and he mentions that disease.

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah, from ‘Ali ibn Rayyān ibn Salt, from Ḥusain ibn Asad, from Aḥmad ibn Musqalah, from his uncle, from Abī Ja’far Al-Mūsili, who said: Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) said: When you take from the clay of the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him), you should say: O Allāh! I ask You through the right of this dust, through the right of the angel who is dedicated to it and the angel who dug it, and through the right of the Successor who is (lying) in it to send Your blessing on Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad and to make this clay the cure from every disease and the protection against any fear. If you do this, then this clay will definitely be a cure for you from every disease and protection against any fear.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Rizqullah ibn al-Ala, from Sulayman ibn 'Amr al-Sarraj, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is taken from near the grave, an area of seventy fathoms by seventy fathoms from the grave.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali, who raised it (to the Imam), saying: He said: In order to seal the clay of the grave of Husain (peace be upon him), one should recite 'Inna Anzalnahu' (Surah Al-Qadr) on it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khallid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, from a man from Ahl al-Kufah, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The sacred boundary (haram) of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is one parasang by one parasang by one parasang by one parasang.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Musawi narrated to me from Abdullah [Ubaidullah] ibn Nahik, from Sa'd ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from one of our companions, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I am a man with many illnesses and diseases, and I have not left any medicine without having treated myself with it.' He said to me, 'Why are you not using the dust of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)? Verily, in it is the cure for every disease and safety from every fear.' And say when you take it: 'O Allah, I ask You by the right of this clay, and by the right of the angel who took it, and by the right of the Prophet who gathered it, and by the right of the Successor who lies in it. Send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and make for me in it a cure from every disease and safety from every fear.' He said, then he said: 'Verily, the angel who took it was Gabriel, and he showed it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, I said, 'I have understood the cure for every disease, but how is it a safety from every fear?' He said, 'If you fear a ruler or something similar, do not leave your house except that you have with you some of the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and in it is the cure and the safety.' And say when you take it: 'O Allah, verily this is the clay of the grave of al-Husayn, Your Wali and the son of Your Wali. I have taken it as a protection for what I fear and for what I do not fear, for indeed what you do not fear may befall you.' The man said: 'So I took it as he said, and by Allah my body became healthy, and it was for me a safety from everything I feared and everything I did not fear, as he said. So I did not see anything disliked by the grace of Allah after it.'

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah, from Aḥmad/Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq Al-Qazwīni, from Abī Bakkār, who said: I took some of the dust which is close to the head of the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.). It was a red-coloured clay. I took it to Imam Riďā (a.s.) to show it to him. He held it in his palm, smelled it, and started to cry, shedding tears. Then he (the Imam (a.s.)) said, “This is the dust of (the grave of) my grandfather.”

My father (peace be upon him) and a group narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Basri, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is a cure for every disease. And when you eat it, say: 'In the name of Allah and by Allah.' O Allah, make it (a cause of) extensive sustenance and beneficial knowledge and a cure from every disease. Verily, You have power over all things.

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Mālik ibn ‘Aťiyyah, from his father, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: When you take from the clay of the Oppressed One and place it in your mouth, recite: O Allāh! I ask You through the right of this dust, through the right of the angel who held it, through the right of the Prophet who embraced it, and through the right of the Imam who is buried in it to send Your blessing on Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and to allow it to be a beneficial cure and an extensive sustenance for me, and (allow it) to be my protection against any fear and disease. Verily if you recite disease. Verily if you recite this, Allāh will cure you and bestow you with good health.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: All clay is unlawful, like the flesh of a swine. And whoever eats it and then dies from it, I will not pray over him, except the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for verily it contains a cure for every disease. And whoever eats it with craving, there will not be a cure in it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about clay. He replied, 'Eating clay is unlawful, like the carcass, blood, and flesh of a swine, except for the clay of the grave of al-Husayn, for verily it contains a cure from every disease and safety from every fear.'

Abū ‘Abdillāh Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faḍḍāl, from his father, from some of our companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said: Verily Allāh, the Blessed and the Exalted, created Ādam (peace be upon him) from clay, so He forbade clay upon his offspring. I asked, 'What do you say about the clay of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'It is unlawful for people to eat their own flesh, but it is permissible for them to eat our flesh; however, a small amount of it is permissible, like a chickpea.'

And I found in the Ḥadīth of al-Ḥusayn ibn Mihrān al-Fārisī, from Muḥammad ibn Sayyār, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, who raised the Ḥadīth to al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him): He said: Anyone who sells the clay of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), then he sells the flesh of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and buys it.

My father narrated to me (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from someone who narrated to him, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: If any of you lives far (from us) and there is a great distance between you and us, you should ascend to the highest place of your house, establish two Rak'ah of prayers, point toward our graves, and say Salām to us, for verily it will reach us.

Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaṭṭāb, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Khaṭṭāb, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Manī’, from Yūnus ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from his father, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: O Sadīr! Do you perform the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) every day? I said: May I be sacrificed for you, no. He said: How negligent you people are! Do you perform his Ziyārah every month? I said: No. He said: Do you perform it every year? I said: Sometimes. He said: O Sadīr! How negligent you people are toward al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) in that! Do you not know that Allah has a million angels, disheveled and covered with dust, who weep and perform Ziyārah and do not cease? And what is difficult for you, O Sadīr, to perform the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) five times every Friday? And he mentioned like the first hadith.

Sulayman ibn 'Isa narrated from his father, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I perform your Ziyarah if I am not able to come?' He said to me, 'O 'Isa! When you are not able to come, if it is Friday, perform Ghusl or Wudu, ascend to your roof, pray two Rak'ah, and turn toward me. Verily, whoever visits me during my life has visited me after my death, and whoever visits me after my death has visited me during my life.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Dihqan [al-Dahhan], from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Sadir, do you not frequently perform the Ziyarah of the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'Because I am busy.' He said, 'Shall I not teach you something that if you do it, Allah will record for you the reward of that Ziyarah?' I said, 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' He said to me, 'Perform Ghusl in your house, ascend to the roof of your house, and point towards him with Salam. By doing this, the Ziyarah will be recorded for you.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah Al-Barqi, from his father, who narrated that the hadith was raised to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Hanān ibn Sadīr Al-Sayrafi visited Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) while a group of his companions were with him. He said: 'O Hanān ibn Sadīr, do you visit Abā 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) once every month?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'What about once every two months?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'What about once a year?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'How negligent you are toward your master!' He said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, it is due to lack of provisions and the long distance.' He said: 'Shall I not guide you to an accepted visitation even if the one visited is far?' He said: 'How should I visit him, O son of the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Perform Ghusl on Friday or any day you wish, wear your purest clothes, ascend to the highest place in your house or the desert, and face the Qiblah with your face after it becomes clear that the grave is there.' Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah.' Then say: 'Peace be upon you, O my master and son of my master, and my leader and son of my leader. Peace be upon you, O my master, the Martyr and son of the Martyr, the Slain and son of the Slain. Peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah. I am visiting you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, with my heart, my tongue, and my limbs, even if I do not visit you physically to see your dome.' Peace be upon you, O heir of Adam, the chosen one of Allah, and heir of Noah, the prophet of Allah, and heir of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah, and heir of Musa, the one spoken to by Allah, and heir of 'Isa, the spirit of Allah, and heir of Muhammad, the beloved of Allah, his prophet and messenger, and heir of 'Ali, Commander of the Faithful, the successor of the Messenger of Allah and his caliph, and heir of Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, the successor of the Commander of the Faithful. May Allah curse those who killed you, and may He renew their punishment in this hour and in every hour. I, O my master, seek nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Great, and to your grandfather, the Messenger of Allah, and to your father, the Commander of the Faithful, and to your brother, Al-Hasan, and to you, O my master. So peace be upon

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He asked: 'What is the distance between you and the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I replied: 'Sixteen parasangs.' He asked: 'Do you not go to him?' I replied: 'No.' He said: 'How negligent you people are!'

And from him, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Musa ibn al-Fadl, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one who narrated to him, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him, 'What do you say about the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'Visit him and do not neglect him, for indeed he is the Master of the Martyrs and the Master of the Youth of Paradise, and he is similar to Yahya ibn Zakariyya, and over the two of them the heavens and the earth wept.'

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Fadl al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Sa'd, from Abu Umar al-Jallab, from al-Harith al-A'war, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for Husayn, the one killed on the outskirts of Kufah. By Allah, it is as if I see the wild animals stretching their necks towards his grave, from various kinds of wild animals, weeping for him and mourning him by night until morning. When this happens, beware of neglecting (his grave).

My father, my brother, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father Sadir, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadir, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) every day?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'How negligent you people are!' He said, 'Do you visit him every Friday?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Do you visit him every month?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Do you visit him once a year?' I said, 'Sometimes.' He said: 'O Sadir, how negligent you people are toward al-Husayn (peace be upon him)! Do you not know that Allah has a thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, who weep for him and inherit him, who do not cease being visitors to the grave of al-Husayn, and their reward is for whoever visits him?' And he mentioned the hadith.

Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, who said: I was with Abī Ja’far (peace be upon him) when a man entered, said Salām to him, and sat down. Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) asked him, 'From which lands are you?' The man said, 'I am a man from the people of Kūfah, and I am a lover of yours and a follower (muwālī).' Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) asked him, 'Do you visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) every Friday?' He said, 'No.' He asked, 'What about every month?' He said, 'No.' He asked, 'What about every year?' He said, 'No.' Then Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Verily you are deprived of the good,' and he mentioned the hadith.

And Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: He narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Fudayl! How negligent you people are! You do not go to the Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Do you not know that there are four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, who weep for him until the Day of Judgment?

And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: He asked: 'What is the distance between you and the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I replied: 'Sixteen or seventeen parasangs.' He asked: 'Do you not go to him?' I replied: 'No.' He said: 'How negligent you are!'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Uramah, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaym ibn Khālid, who said: I heard Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: It is strange for some people who claim to be our Shī'ah, and it is said that one of them passes his lifetime without visiting the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), due to negligence from it, and [contempt, and weakness, and laziness; he was contemptuous, weak, and lazy]. By Allah, if they knew what is in it of merit, they would not be contemptuous or lazy. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is in it of merit?' He said, 'There is much merit and goodness. Indeed, the first thing that befalls him is that his past sins are forgiven, and he is told to resume his deeds.'

Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hanan, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadir, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) every day?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, no.' He said: 'How negligent you are! Do you visit him every Friday?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit him every month?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you visit him every year?' I said: 'Sometimes.' He said: 'O Sadir, how negligent you are toward al-Husayn (peace be upon him)!' and he mentioned the hadith.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Musawi narrated to me from Ubaydullah ibn Nahik, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: It is an obligation on the wealthy to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) twice a year, and it is an obligation on the poor to visit it once a year.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Amir ibn 'Umayr and Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) once a year.

Abu al-Abbas narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Muslim, from Amir ibn Umayr and Sa'id al-A'raj, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) once a year.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah Al-Mawsawi narrated to me from Abdillah [Ubaidillah] ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He said, 'Once a year, for I dislike being well-known (or having one's identity widely known).'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Ibn Abi Nabil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: It is an obligation on the poor to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) once a year, and it is an obligation on the wealthy to visit it twice a year.

My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) Regarding the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), he said: 'Once a year, for I dislike being widely known (or: being identified as a frequent visitor).'

Abul-Abbās narrated to me from Al-Zayyāt, from Ja’far ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād, from Ibn Muslim, from ‘Āmir ibn ‘Umayr, and from Sa’īd Al-A’raj, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: Go to the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him) once a year.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there an obligatory prayer for the Ziyarah of the Grave?' He replied, 'There is no obligatory prayer for it.' I asked him, 'On how many days should one go for Ziyarah?' He replied, 'As much as you wish.'

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, through his chain, raising it to 'Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said: O 'Ali! It has reached me that some of our Shias allow one or two years to pass without visiting al-Husayn. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I know many people with this description.' He said, 'By Allah, they have missed their fortune, turned away from Allah's reward, and distanced themselves from the proximity of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, how often is the visit?' He said, 'O 'Ali, if you are able to visit him every month, do so.' I said, 'I cannot reach that because I work with my hands, people's affairs are in my hands, and I cannot absent my face from my place for even one day.' He said, 'You are excused, and whoever works with his hands. I meant those who do not work with their hands, for whom if they go out every Friday, it is easy for them. Indeed, they have no excuse with Allah and no excuse with His Messenger on the Day of Judgment.' I said, 'If a man sends someone on his behalf, is that permissible?' He said, 'Yes, and his going himself is greater in reward and better for him with his Lord. His Lord will see him sleepless at night, bearing the toil of the day. Allah will look at him with a glance that obliges for him the highest Firdaws with Muhammad and his family. So compete in that and be among its people.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muḥammad ibn 'Īsā narrated to me from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ṣabbāḥ al-Ḥadhā, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: 'Visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), even if it is only once a year,' and he mentioned the hadith.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ‘Amraki ibn ‘Ali Al-Būfaki, who said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, and he was in the service of Abī Ja’far the Second (peace be upon him), from ‘Ali, from Safwān ibn Mihrān Al-Jammāl, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), in a long ḥadīth: I asked him: 'Whoever visits him and then departs, when should he return to him? And how often should he be visited? And what is the maximum time people are allowed to stay away from him?' He replied: 'It is not permissible to stay away for more than a month. As for those who live far away, [they should visit] once every three years. Whoever passes three years without visiting him, has been ungrateful to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and has severed his honor, except for one with a valid excuse.'

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ‘Ali ibn ‘Uqbah, from ‘Ubaydillāh al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said: I said, 'We visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) two or three times a year.' Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) replied, 'I dislike that you go there frequently. Visit him once a year.' I asked, 'How should I send blessings upon him?' He replied, 'Stand behind him, at his shoulders, then send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and send blessings upon al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).'

Al-Amraki narrated through his chain, saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, four thousand angels establish prayers next to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) from the rising of dawn until the sun sets.
