Then they ascend, and an equal number descend, and they pray until the rising of dawn. Therefore, it is not fitting for a Muslim to delay visiting his grave for more than four years.

And through his chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abi Nab, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He said: Yes, it equals an 'Umrah, and it is not appropriate to delay it for more than four years.

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali al-Washā, who said: I asked Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) about the Ziyārah of the grave of Abi al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him): is it like the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)? He replied, 'Yes.' And Muḥammad ibn Ya‘qūb narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, through his chain, the same.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Abi 'Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Yasar al-Wasiti, who said: I asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'Should I go to the Ziyarah of the grave of Abi al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in Baghdad?' He replied, 'If you must, then perform the Ziyarah from behind the covers.'

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh al-Barqi, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali al-Washshā, who said: I asked Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him): ‘What is the reward for one who visits the grave of your father, Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him)?’ He replied: ‘Visit him.’ I asked: ‘What is among its merits?’ He said to him: ‘[It is] like that of one who visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).’

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from 'Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti, from some of our companions, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), regarding going to the grave of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). He said: 'Establish prayers in the mosques around it.'

My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan, may Allāh have mercy on them all, narrated from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd, from Ḥusain ibn Yasār Al-Wāsiťi, who said: I asked Abal Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)), “What are the rewards for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of your father (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) – may Allāh’s blessings be upon him?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Go to his Ziyārah!” I asked, “What are its merits?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Its merits are the same as the merits for those who go to the Ziyārah of his father – referring to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.).” I asked, “What if I was in fear and could not enter (next to the grave)?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “(Then) say Salām from behind the walls.”

Abul-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', from Al-Khaybari, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari al-Qummi, who said: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Baghdad is like whoever visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), except that the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Believers have their own specific superiority. And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, through his chain, similarly.'

My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, who said: I asked Abā Ja’far (peace be upon him), “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) with the (sole) intention of Ziyārah?” He replied, “(Their reward is) Paradise and the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abil Ḥasan (peace be upon him) is (also) Paradise.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: The Ziyarah of the grave of my father is like the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn.

And from him, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdūs Al-Khalanjī, from his father Raḥīm, who said: I said to Al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Ziyārah of the grave of Abū Al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) in Baghdad is upon us with difficulty, and we only visit him and send him Salām from behind the wall. What is the reward for the one who visits him?' He said, and he said to him, 'By Allāh, it is the same as the reward for the one who visits the grave of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family).'

And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rahim, who said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'The Ziyarah of the grave of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in Baghdad involves difficulty for us. What is the reward for one who visits him?' He said to him, 'The same as the reward for one who goes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'And a man entered, said Salam to him, and sat down. He mentioned Baghdad and the inferiority of its people, and what was expected to befall them from the earth swallowing them, the clamor, and the lightning bolts, and enumerated from those things some items.' He said, 'So I stood up to leave, and I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying, 'As for Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), none (of this will affect him).'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hudhayni, from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Marwan, from Ibrahim ibn Uqbah, who said: I wrote to Abul Hasan the Third (peace be upon him) asking him about the Ziyarah of the grave of Abi Abdillah and about the Ziyarah of the graves of Abul Hasan and Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him). Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied, 'Abi Abdillah comes first, but that is more complete and has a greater reward.'

‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, who said: I asked Abā Ja‘far (peace be upon him), ‘What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with the (sole) intention of Ziyārah?’ He replied, ‘(Their reward is) Paradise. And whoever goes to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abī al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), for him is Paradise.’

Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayss ibn Hisham an-Nashiri narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Jibilla narrated from Salam ibn Abu 'Umayra, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharabudh, from Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathila, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin said: "Do you like for Allah and His Messenger to be considered liars? Narrate to the people what they know, and withhold from them what they deny."

And Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Bawari narrated to me, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Muqri' al-Saqti narrated to me in Wasit, saying: Khalaf al-Bazzar narrated to me, from Yazeed ibn Harun, from Hameed at-Taweel, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Do not tell people of what they do not know. Do you like for Allah and His Messenger to be considered liars?

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from Abdul A'la ibn A'yun, saying: Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) said to me: O Abdul A'la, undertaking our matter is not merely knowing it and accepting it. Undertaking our matter is preserving it and concealing it from those who are not of its people. So convey to them my greeting and the mercy of Allah - meaning the Shia - and say to them: He says to you: May Allah have mercy upon a servant who draws the love of people to himself and to us by showing them what they know and refraining from them what they deny. (Then he said) One who makes war against us is not more burdensome than the one who speaks against us with what we dislike.

And Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus al-Mawsili informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghiyath narrated to us from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, saying: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: Indeed, undertaking our matter is not merely believing in it and accepting it, but among undertaking our matter is concealing it and preserving it from those who are not qualified for it. So convey my greeting and the mercy of Allah to them (meaning the Shia) and tell them: He says to you: May Allah have mercy upon a servant who draws the love of people to me and to himself, by narrating to them what they know and concealing from them what they deny. Then he said to me: By Allah, the one who makes war against us is not more burdensome to us than the one who speaks against us with what we dislike.

And Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri informed us from Muhammad ibn al-Abbas al-Hasani from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abu Hamza al-Bata'i from Muhammad al-Khazzaz, who said: Abu Abdullah said: He who spreads our traditions among us is in the same rank as one who denies our right.

And with this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sariy, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I narrate a hadith to a man, and he goes off and narrates it from me just as he heard it, so I make permissible cursing him and disassociating from him because of it.'

And through it, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamrah, from al-Qasim al-Sayrafi, Ibn Miskan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: A people claim that I am their Imam. By Allah, I am not their Imam! May Allah curse them. Whenever I conceal something, they uncover it. I say 'such and such,' and they say: 'He means such and such.' I am only the Imam of whoever obeys me.

And through it, from al-Hasan, from Karram al-Khath'ami, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, if there were bands on your mouths, I would tell every one of you what is for him. By Allah, if I found the pious among you, I would speak. Allah is the One assisted by.'

And through it, from al-Hasan, from his father, from Abu Baseer who said: I heard Abu Ja'far saying: 'It is a secret that Allah revealed to Gabriel, and Gabriel revealed to Muhammad, and Muhammad revealed to Ali, and Ali revealed to whom Allah willed, one after the other, but you are speaking about it in the streets!'

And Muhammad ibn Hammam ibn Suhayl narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Ala' al-Mathari narrated to us, saying: Idris ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: One of our sheikhs narrated to us, saying: Al-Mufadhdhal said: I held your hand as Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) held my hand and said to me: 'O Mufadhdhal! This matter is not merely by saying [it], no, by Allah, until (we) preserve it as Allah has preserved it, honor it as Allah has honored it, and fulfill its due right as Allah has ordered.'

Abdul Wahid narrated through his chain, from al-Hasan, from Hafs bin Naseeb Far'an who said: I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) during the days when his mawla al-Mu'alla bin Khunays was killed. He said to me: 'O Hafs! I told al-Mu'alla some things, so he spread them, and he was afflicted with the iron (of execution). Indeed, I said to him: We have a tradition; whoever preserves it for us, Allah will preserve his religion and his worldly life, and whoever spreads it for us, Allah will deprive him of his religion and his worldly life. O Mu'alla! Indeed, whoever conceals the difficult (challenging) parts of our tradition, Allah will make it a light between his eyes and grant him honor among the people, and whoever spreads the difficult parts of our tradition, he will not die until a weapon bites him or he dies confused.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father and Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: Indeed, my father said to me: There must be a fire (war) from Azerbaijan that leaves nothing standing. When that occurs, stay in your homes and remain as we have remained. When our riser (al-Qa'im) moves, hasten to him even if crawling. By Allah, as if I see him between the Corner and the Maqam, the people are giving him allegiance upon a new covenant, he will be severe with the Arabs. And he said: Woe to the arrogant ones of the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated from some of his men, from Ali ibn Imara al-Kinani, who said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abul Jarood, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: 'Advise me.' He said: 'I advise you to fear Allah, to stay in your house and sit among the masses of these people. Beware of the Kharijites from us, for they are on nothing and lead to nothing. Know that the Umayyads have a dominion that people cannot restrain, and that the people of Truth will have a state; when it comes, Allah will entrust it to whomever He wishes from us, the Ahl al-Bayt. Whoever from you attains it will be with us in the highest peak (of Paradise), and if Allah takes him before that, He will choose for him what is best. Know that no group will rise to repel oppression or strengthen religion except that they are crushed by death and calamity, until a group rises who fought in Badr with the Messenger of Allah, whose dead are not buried, whose fallen are not lifted, and whose wounded are not cured.' I said: 'Who are they?' He said: 'The angels.'

(3) Three narrators - And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id told us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali told me, saying: Al-Hasan and Muhammad, the sons of Ali ibn Yousuf, narrated to us, from their father, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Salih ibn Abul Aswad, from Abu al-Jarood, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far saying: None of us, the Ahl al-Bayt, who repels an oppression or invites to truth, unless calamity strikes him down until a group rises that fought in Badr, whose killed are not buried and whose wounded are not cured. I said: 'Whom did Abu Ja'far mean by that?' He said: 'The angels.'

Muhammad ibn Hammam and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor narrated together, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor, from his father, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu al-Jarud, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Hamdani, from al-Harith al-A'war al-Hamdani, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (Ali) said from the pulpit: 'When the Ill-wisher perishes, the Master of the Age disappears, and hearts remain fluctuating—some fertile and some barren—then the Ill-wishers will perish, the vanishers will vanish, and the believers will remain, and they will be few, three hundred or a little more. A group that fought with the Messenger of Allah on the day of Badr, who were neither killed nor died, will fight with them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn as-Sabah ibn ad-Dhahhak narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a from Sayf at-Tammar from Abu al-Murhaf, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The hasteners will perish.' I asked: 'And who are the hasteners?' He said: 'Those who hurry. And the near ones will be saved, and the fortress stands firm on its pegs. Be the rear guard of your homes, for the dust is upon the one who stirs it, and they will not wish distress upon you except that Allah afflicts them with a distraction, except for whoever encounters them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to me, saying: Yusuf ibn Kulayb al-Mas'oodi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hakam ibn Sulayman narrated from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Abu Bakr al-Hadhrami, who said: Abban and I entered upon Abu Abdillah, and that was when the black banners had appeared in Khurasan. We said: 'What do you think?' He said: 'Stay in your houses, and when you see that we have united upon a man, then rush to us with your weapons.'

And Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: "Keep your tongues back (remain silent) and stay in your houses, for no matter will afflict you specifically that does not also afflict the general public, and the Zaydites will remain a shield/protector for you forever."

And Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-A'lawi narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abdurrahman ibn Kathir, who said: One day I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Muhzim al-Asadi was with him. He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, when is this matter that we are waiting for? It has been delayed too long for us.' He (peace be upon him) responded: 'O Muhzim, the wishful thinkers have lied, the hasteners will perish, the Muslims will be saved, and they will return to us.'

Ali ibn Ahmad, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, who said: He narrated to us Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abdurrahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Has come the command of Allah, so do not hasten it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate [with Him].' He said: It is our affair. Allah commanded that it not be hastened until Allah supports it with three armies: the angels, the believers, and fright. His emergence is like the emergence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and that is His saying, the Exalted: 'As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, and indeed, a party of the believers disliked it.'

Muhammad ibn Hammam and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor all narrated, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor, from his father, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Salih ibn Maytham and Yahya ibn Sabiq all, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said: The hasteners perished, and those nearest [to Allah] were saved, and the fortress remained firm on its pegs. Indeed, after distress there is a wonderful deliverance.

Ali ibn Ahmad said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi narrated to us from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abut-Tufayl, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): That Ibn Abbas sent someone to ask him about this verse: "O you who believe! Be patient and excel in patience and remain steadfast and fear Allah, that you may succeed." Ali ibn al-Husayn became angry and said to the messenger: "I wish that he who sent you with this had faced me with it himself." Then he said: "This verse was revealed about my father and us. The steadfastness (rabt) that we have been ordered to perform has not yet occurred; it will be for some of our descendants who remain steadfast." Then he said: "Indeed, in his loins (meaning Ibn Abbas) is a progeny created for the Fire of Hell. They will send forth great masses of people deviating from the religion of Allah. The earth will be dyed with the blood of the young ones from the young ones of the Family of Muhammad. Those young ones will rise in an unsuitable time and seek what is unattainable. The believers will remain steadfast and persevere until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges."

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) Regarding His saying: 'O you who have believed, be patient and vie in patience and compete in steadfastness and fear Allah that you may be successful.' He said: 'Be patient in performing the obligatory duties, strive against your enemy, and remain steadfast (waiting) for your expected Imam.'

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us; he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us; he said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Hadhrami, from his father, from Uthman ibn Zayd, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said: The advent of the Qa'im from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, is like the advent of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and the one from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, who rises before the advent of the Qa'im, is like a young bird that flew and fell from its nest, and children played with it.

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Aqaba, from Musa ibn Akeel an-Nimyari, from al-Ala' ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said: Whoever of you dies while holding fast to this matter, waiting (for the reappearance), is like one who is in the camp of al-Qa'im (peace be upon him).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father and Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said one day: "Shall I inform you of that which Allah does not accept any deed from His servants except through it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Testifying that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and affirming what Allah has commanded, and Wilayah (guardianship) for us, and disavowal from our enemies (meaning the Imams specifically), and submission to them, and piety (al-Wara'), and striving (al-Ijtihad), and tranquility, and waiting for the Qa'im." Then he said: "Indeed, for us is a dominion/state that Allah will bring about when He wills." Then he said: "Whoever is pleased to be among the companions of the Qa'im, let him wait and practice piety and good character while he is waiting. If he dies and the Qa'im rises after him, he will have a reward equal to the reward of one who accompanied him." So strive and wait. Good news for you, O the mercified group!

Ali ibn Ahmad, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Munakhkhal ibn Jameel, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said: Be quiet as long as the heavens and the earth are quiet (i.e., do not rise up against anyone), for your matter is not obscure. Indeed, it is a sign from Allah, not from people, but it is brighter than the sun. It does not hide from the pious nor from the dissolute. Do you know the dawn? Indeed, it is like the dawn, which is not obscure.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ya'qub al-Sarraj and from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was given allegiance as the caliph after the killing of Uthman, he ascended the minbar and delivered a speech which he recounted, saying in it: 'Indeed, your affliction has returned to its state as it was when Allah sent His Prophet. And by Him Who sent him with the truth, you will be confused with a great confusion and sifted with a great sifting until your lowest become your highest and your highest become your lowest. And those who were late will hasten, and those who hastened will be delayed. By Allah, I did not hide a sign nor did I tell a lie, and I was inspired with news of this position and this day.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us; he said: Some of our companions narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'mar ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: Do men think that they will be left alone on saying, 'We believe,' and not be tried? Then he asked me: 'What is the trial (fitnah)?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, we hold that the trial is in religion.' He said: 'They are tried as gold is tried.' Then he said: 'They are purified as gold is purified.'

(3) Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Iesa, from Yunus, from Sulayman ibn Salih, who raised it to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said: He said: Indeed, this talk of yours disgusts the hearts of men, so cast it to them forcefully. Whoever accepts it, add to him; and whoever denies it, leave him. There must be a sedition in which every companion and close friend falls, until even those who split a hair into two (due to strictness) fall in it, until no one remains except us and our Shia.

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 229 AH, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that one of his companions entered upon him. He said to him: 'May I be your ransom, by Allah I love you and love whoever loves you. O my master, how many your Shia are!' He said to him: 'Mention them.' He said: 'They are many.' He said: 'Can you count them?' He said: 'They are more than that.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'If the specified number were completed at three hundred and eleven, that would be what you want. But our Shia are those whose voice does not exceed their hearing, nor their zeal their body; nor do they praise us openly, nor quarrel with us publicly, nor sit with us criticizing, nor talk with us abusing, nor love whoever hates us, nor hate whoever loves us.' I said: 'Then what should I do with these differing Shia groups who claim they are Shia?' He said: 'Among them is distinction, among them is purification, and among them is alteration. Years will come that will perish them, a sword that will kill them, and disagreement that will scatter them. Our true Shia are those who do not growl like a dog, nor covet like a crow, nor ask people with their hand even if they die of hunger.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, where should I seek these described with this description?' He said: 'Seek them in the far corners of the earth. Those are they whose livelihood is humble, whose dwelling is transient. If they are present, they are not recognized; if absent, they are not missed; if sick, they are not visited; if proposed to, they are not married; if they die, they are not attended. Those are they who share their wealth among themselves, and visit each other in their graves, and their desires do not differ even if the lands differ. If they see a believer, they honor him; if they see a hypocrite, they leave him. At death they do not despair, and in their graves they visit each other…'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, from his book, said: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father and Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: “With the Qa'im (peace be upon him) there will be a small number of Arabs.” It was said to him: “But those who describe this matter among them are very many.” He said: “People must be tested and distinguished, and sifted, and a great multitude will be thrown out from the sieve.”

And Ali ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob al-Zarrad, from Abu al-Mughra, from Abdullah ibn Abu Ya'foor, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he heard him saying: Woe to the arrogant ones of the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. I said: May I be your ransom, how many of the Arabs will be with the Qa'im (peace be upon him)? He said: A small number. I said: By Allah, those who describe this matter among them are many. He said: People must be purified, distinguished, and sifted, and a great multitude will be thrown out from the sieve.

And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Abu Hamza from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali saying: By Allah, you will be distinguished, by Allah you will be purified, by Allah you will be sifted like the chaff is sifted from the wheat.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: 'Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jabla, from Miskeen al-Rahhal, from Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Umayra bint Nufayl, who said: I heard al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying: The matter that you are expecting will not occur until a time comes that you disavow each other, spit at the face of each other, and one of you declares unbelief against the other, and you curse each other. I said to him: 'There will be no goodness in that time!' He said: 'All the goodness will be in that time. Our Qa'im will rise and do away with all of that.'

Ali ibn Ahmad said: Obaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi informed us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Jibilla, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: That matter (the appearance of al-Qa'im) will not occur until a time comes that you spit at the face of each other, curse each other and call each other as liars.

And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Obaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi informed us, from Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: You will be tested, O Shia of the Family of Muhammad, with the testing of kohl in the eye. And the owner of the eye knows when the kohl is put into his eye but does not know when it comes out of it. And likewise, a man may be upon our doctrine in the morning and have recanted it by evening, or be upon our doctrine in the evening and have recanted it by morning.

(13) And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa informed us, from a man, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from ar-Rabee' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Muhzim ibn Abu Burda al-Asadi and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: By Allah, you will be broken like glass, and indeed glass is remade and returns as it was. By Allah, you will be broken like pottery, for indeed pottery breaks and does not return as it was. By Allah, you will be sifted, and by Allah you will be distinguished, and by Allah you will be purified until none of you remain except the fewest. And he shook his hand.

And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, that which you look forward to will not come to pass until you are tested and distinguished, and until none of you remains except the rarest of the rare.

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Muhammadi narrated to us from his book in the year sixty-eight and two hundred, saying: Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Sayqal narrated to us, from his father, saying: I entered upon Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) and there was a group with him. While we were conversing and he was facing one of his companions, he turned to us and said: 'In what matter are you? Far, far! That which you eagerly await will not come until you are tested (purified). Far! That which you eagerly await will not come until you are distinguished (clarified). That which you eagerly await will not come until you are sifted (separated from impurities). That which you eagerly await will not come except after despair. That which you eagerly await will not come until the wretched one becomes wretched and the happy one becomes happy.'

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha ibn Abu Hurasa al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from Sabah al-Muzni, from al-Harith ibn Hasira, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that he said: Be like the bees among the birds; no bird is there but it considers them weak, but if the birds knew what blessing is in their interiors, they would not do that to them. Mix with people with your tongues and bodies, and separate from them with your hearts and deeds. And by He in whose hand is my soul, you will not see what you love until some of you spit in the faces of others, and some of you call others liars, and until none of you remains (or he said: from my Shias) except like the kohl in the eye and the salt in the food. And I will give you an example: it is like a man who had food, he sifted it and purified it, then he put it in a room and left it there as long as God willed, then he returned to it and found that it had been eaten by worms. He took it out, sifted it, purified it, and put it back in the room and left it there as long as God willed. Then he returned to it and found that a portion of it had been eaten by worms, so he took it out, sifted it, purified it, and put it back. He continued thus until only a bundle remained, like the bundle of the finest grain, which the worms could not harm at all. So too are you: you will be sifted/refined until only a small group remains, whom affliction will not harm at all.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri al-Kufi narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Isa al-Hasani narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Bata'ini from his father from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the example of our Shia is like a threshing floor (meaning a large heap) containing grain. A worm afflicts it and it is purified, then another worm afflicts it and it is purified, until what remains is that which does not harm the worm. So too are our Shia: they are distinguished and purified until a small group remains, who are not harmed by the tribulation."

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Muhammadi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Sharif ibn Sabiq al-Taflisi, from al-Fadl ibn Abu Qurra al-Taflisi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, that he said: The believers are tested, then Allah distinguishes them. Indeed, Allah did not exempt the believers from the calamities and hardships of this world, but He secured them within it from blindness and wretchedness in the Hereafter. Then he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali used to lay his martyrs side by side, then say: 'Our martyrs are the martyrs of the prophets.'

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, saying: Abdullah ibn Jibla narrated to us from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'If the Qa'im arises, people will deny him because he returns to them as a young man, successful, and none will remain steadfast with him except a believer whom Allah has taken a covenant from in the first Creation.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqdah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn at-Taymali narrated to us from his book in the month of Safar, the year 274. He said: Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir ibn Rabah al-Thaqafi narrated to us from Musa ibn Bakr, from Bashir al-Nabal. And Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaniji narrated to us from 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Bashir ibn Abi Araakah al-Nabal (and the wording of the hadith is according to the narration of Ibn 'Uqdah), saying: When I arrived in Medina, I went to the house of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). I found his mule saddled at the door. I sat opposite the house. He came out, and I greeted him. He dismounted from the mule and came towards me. He asked: 'From where is the man?' I said: 'From Iraq.' He said: 'Which part of it?' I said: 'From the people of Kufa.' He said: 'Who accompanied you on this path?' I said: 'Some people of al-Muhaditha.' He asked: 'What is al-Muhaditha?' I said: 'Al-Murj'a.' He said: 'Woe to this al-Murj'a! To whom will they resort tomorrow when our Qa'im appears?' I said: 'They say: If that occurs, we and you will be equal in justice.' He said: 'Whoever repents, Allah accepts his repentance; and whoever conceals hypocrisy, Allah will not distance Himself from him; and whoever announces something [of hypocrisy], Allah will shed his blood.' Then he said: 'He will slaughter them, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, just as a butcher slaughters his sheep,' and he pointed to his throat with his hand. I said: 'They say: If that occurs, his affairs will be established, and he will not shed even a drop of blood.' He said: 'No, by the One in Whose hand is my soul! It will be so until we and you wipe together sweat and blood,' and he gestured with his hand towards his forehead.

Three - Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasī, from al-Hasan ibn Mu'awiya, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbūb, from 'Isa ibn Sulayman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioning al-Qa'im (peace be upon him). I said: 'I hope that his matter will be easy.' He said: 'It will not be so until you wipe blood and sweat together.'

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah Yunus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qarashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ribat, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah saying: 'Indeed, the people of the truth have always been in distress, but that is for a short period and a long relief.' And Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda informed us, from one of his men, who said: Ali ibn Ishaq al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Ribat, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and he mentioned the same.' Indeed, the people of the truth have always been in distress, but that is for a short period and a long relief.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar, saying: I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) during the circumambulation (of the Kaaba). He looked at me and said to me: 'O Mufadhdhal, why do I see you distressed and discolored?' I said to him: 'May I be your ransom, I look at the Banu Abbas and what is in their hands of this kingship, authority, and dominion. If that were for you, we would be with you in it.' He said: 'O Mufadhdhal, if it were so, it would not be but the politics of the night, the swimming (ease) of the day, eating coarse food, and wearing rough cloth, resembling Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him); otherwise, it is Hell. So that was veiled from us, and we became eating and drinking. And have you seen an oppression that Allah made a blessing like this?'

Abu Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shamar, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah in his house, and the house was crowded with his family. The people came to him asking questions, and he answered whatever they asked about. I began to cry from one side of the house. He said: 'What is making you cry, O Amr?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, how can I not cry? Is there anyone like you in this ummah, while the door is closed upon you and the curtain is lowered over you?' He said: 'Do not cry, O Amr. We eat the good foods and wear the soft clothes. If what you say were true, we would only eat coarse food and wear rough clothes, like Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib; otherwise, it is being treated with shackles in Hell.'

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi told us, saying: He told me, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, saying: Adh-Dhurays told me, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, saying: After the passing of Ali ibn al-Husayn, I entered upon Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, and I said to him: May I be your ransom, I know my detachment from others and my comfort with your father, and my loneliness from the people. He said: You are truthful, O Abu Khalid, so what do you want? I said: May I be your ransom, your father has described to me the Master of this Command (al-Qa'im) with a description that if I saw him on any path, I would take his hand. He said: So what do you want, O Abu Khalid? I said: I want you to name him for me so that I may know him by his name. He said: You have asked me, by Allah, O Abu Khalid, a tiring question, and you have asked me about a matter that I had not informed anyone of, and if I had informed anyone of it, I would have informed you. And you have asked me about a matter that if the children of Fatimah knew it, they would strive to cut it into pieces.

Three - Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Abbasi, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Whoever narrates to you from us regarding timing, do not hesitate to consider him a liar, for we do not assign a specific time to anyone.'

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us in Nahawand in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the month of Ramadan in the year 229 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated to us from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said: Allah does not consent save to reverse the timing of the diviners.

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Bakr al-Hadhrami, who said: We do not time this matter.

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Jibla narrated from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, when is the emergence of the Qa'im? He said: O Abu Muhammad, we, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not specify times, and Muhammad (peace be upon him) has said: 'The time-servers have lied.' O Abu Muhammad, before this matter there are five signs: the first is the call in the month of Ramadan, the emergence of al-Sufyani, the emergence of al-Khurāsani, the killing of al-Nafs al-Zakiyya, and the sinking in al-Bayda'. Then he said: O Abu Muhammad, it is necessary that before that there be two plagues: the white plague and the red plague. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, and what are they? He said: As for the white plague, it is the torrential death, and as for the red plague, it is the sword. And the Qa'im does not emerge until his name is called out from the throat of the sky on the twenty-third night of Ramadan, which is a Friday night. I said: With what will he be called? He said: With his name and his father's name: 'Behold, So-and-so son of So-and-so is the Qa'im of the Family of Muhammad, so listen to him and obey him.' And nothing that Allah created with a spirit will remain but that it hears the shout, so the sleeper awakens and goes out to his courtyard, and the virgin goes out from her veil, and the Qa'im emerges from what he hears, and it is the shout of Gabriel (peace be upon him).

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim ibn Qays ibn Rumana al-Ash'ari, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'id, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Malik, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qatawani all narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn Mahbub al-Zarrad narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah saying: There was a set time for this matter, and it was in the year forty and one hundred [140 AH], but when you announced it and made it public, Allah delayed it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us via this chain, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Ishaq, this matter has been delayed twice.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all together, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abu Hamath al-Thimali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) saying: O Thabit, indeed Allah the Exalted had timed this matter for the year seventy. But when al-Husayn was killed, Allah's anger intensified, so He delayed it until the year one hundred and forty. We told you of that, and you announced it and uncovered the veil of concealment, so after that Allah did not assign a specific time for this matter to us. And Allah blots out and establishes what He pleases, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Abu Hamza said: I narrated that to Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), and he said: 'It was so.'

And informed us Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abdurrahman ibn Kathir, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah when Muhzim entered upon him, and he said to him: 'May I be your ransom, inform me about this matter which we are waiting for, when is it?' He said: 'O Muhzim, the diviners have lied, the hasteners have perished, and the Muslims were saved.'

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, from some of his teachers, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), and he said: "The diviners (of the time) tell lies. We, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not fix a specific time." Then he said: "Allah does not consent save to reverse the timing of the diviners."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from al-Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'Does that matter have a specific time?' He said: 'The dividers of time are liars, the dividers of time are liars. Indeed, when Moses went as an envoy to his Lord and promised his people thirty days, and when Allah added ten days to the thirty, his people said: "Moses has broken his promise to us." So they did what they did. When we narrate a narration to you and it comes to pass as we narrated to you, say: "Allah has spoken the truth." And when we narrate a narration to you and it comes to pass contrary to what we narrated to you, say: "Allah has spoken the truth." You will be rewarded twice.'.

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from as-Siyari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far said to me: "O Ali, the Shia have been brought up with hopes since two hundred years." Yaqteen said to his son Ali ibn Yaqteen: "What is the matter? What was said to us occurred, but what was said to you did not occur?" (He meant the matter of the Banu al-Abbas). Ali said to him: "What was said to you and what was said to us came from the same source, except that the time of your matter arrived, so you were given its pure fulfillment and it happened as it was said to you. But the time of our matter had not yet arrived, so we justified it with hopes. If it had been said to us that this matter would not occur until two hundred or three hundred years, our hearts would harden and most people would revert from faith to Islam. But they said to us: 'How swift it is and how near,' to win over the hearts of people and to bring the deliverance closer."

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from al-Qassim ibn Isma'il al-Anbari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibrahim ibn Mahzam, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: We mentioned the rulers of Banu al-Fulan (the Abbasids) before him, so he said: 'People perished because of their hastening of this matter. Indeed, Allah does not hasten on account of the haste of the servants. This matter has a limit/terminus to which it reaches. If it reaches that limit, they will not advance an hour nor delay an hour.'

Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda said: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurara narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah saying: When our Qa'im rises, he will face from ignorance more severely than what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) faced from the ignorance of the pre-Islamic age. I said: 'How is that?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to people while they were worshipping stones, rocks, sticks, and carved wood. And when our Qa'im rises, he comes to people and they all interpret the Book of Allah for themselves, using it as evidence against him.' Then he said: 'By Allah, his justice will enter the insides of their houses just as heat and cold enter.'

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Abu Hamza al-Thimali, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, the Master of this Command (al-Qa'im), if he were to appear, would receive from the people what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) received, and more.

Three narrators - Muhammad ibn Hammam said: Humeed ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying: Al-Qa'im will face in his war what the Messenger of Allah did not face. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah came to them while they were worshipping hollowed stones and carved wood, but the people of al-Qa'im will come out against him, interpreting the Book of Allah against him, and fighting him on the basis of it.

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Abban ibn Taghlub, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: When the banner of the truth appears, the people of the East and the people of the West will curse it. Do you know why that is? I said: No. He said: Because of what the people endure from his family before his appearance.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, he said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: When the banner of the truth is raised, the people of the East and the West will curse it. I said to him: 'From what is that?' He said: 'From what they receive from the Banu Hashim.'

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa and Ahmad ibn Ali al-A'lam, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali as-Sayrafi narrated from Muhammad ibn Sadaqa, Ibn Othayna al-Abdi, and Muhammad ibn Sinan all together, from Ya'qub as-Sarraj, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Thirteen cities and tribes whose people Al-Qa'im will fight and who will fight him: the people of Mecca, the people of Medina, the people of Sham (Syria), the Umayyads, the people of Basra, the people of Dast Maysan, the Kurds, the Arab nomads, the tribe of Dhubban, Ghani, Bahila, Azd, and the people of Rayy.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda said to us: My father Muhammad ibn al-Mufadhdhal ibn Ibrahim ibn Qays ibn Rumana narrated to me from his book in the month of Rajab in the year two hundred and sixty-five, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl narrated to us, saying: Tha'laba ibn Maymun, Abu Ishaq, narrated to us from Isa ibn A'yun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The Sufyani is of the inevitable ones, and his emergence is in Rajab, and from the beginning of his emergence to its end is fifteen months, six months he fights in them, and when he conquers the five districts, he rules for nine months, and he does not add to them a single day.

(3) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqdah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to us in Safar of the year 274 AH, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob narrated to us, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) saying: Fear Allah and seek assistance in your state with piety (war') and striving in obedience to Allah. For the greatest happiness a person has in his religion is when he considers himself to be at the threshold of the Hereafter and this world has cut off from him. When he reaches that threshold, he knows that he has faced bliss and honor from Allah, good tidings of Paradise, and safety from what he feared, and he is certain that which he was upon is the truth, and that whoever opposes his religion is upon falsehood, and that he is perishing. So be glad, and be glad for what you desire. Do you not see your enemies fighting each other in sins against Allah, and killing one another for this world while you are safe in your homes, secluded from them? And sufficient for you is as-Sufyan as a vengeance from your enemy, and he is one of the signs for you. Even if the sinful one (al-Fasiq) rises, you would remain for a month or two after his rising without blame upon you until he kills many people other than you. Some of his companions said to him: 'What should we do with our families if that happens?' He said: 'The men among you should hide from him, for his anger and greed are only upon our followers. As for the women, there is no harm upon them, if Allah wills.' It was said to him: 'To where do the men escape and flee from him?' He said: 'Whoever of them wishes to leave, let him go to Medina or to Mecca or to some of the countries.' Then he said: 'What do you do in Medina? For the army of the sinful one will aim for it. But you should go to Mecca, for it is your gathering place. And his tribulation is the pregnancy of a woman: nine months, and she will not pass it, if Allah wills.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara ibn A'yun, from Abdul Malik ibn A'yun, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far when the mention of al-Qa'im came up, so I said to him: 'I hope that his appearance is soon and that as-Sufyani does not precede it.' He said: 'By Allah, no! It is an inevitable matter that must occur.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Assamm, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Zurara, from Hamran ibn A'yun, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) In His saying, Exalted is He: 'He it is Who created you from clay, then He decreed a term; and there is a term named with Him: then you doubt.' {2} He said: 'They are two terms: an inevitable term, and a pending term.' Hamran asked him: 'What is the inevitable one?' He said: 'That which has been determined by the will of Allah.' Hamran said: 'I hope that the term of As-Sufyani is among the pending ones.' Abu Ja'far said: 'No, by Allah, it is among the inevitable ones.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to us from his book in Shawwal in the year 271 AH, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Tawil narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Sulaym, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Among matters, there are pending matters, and there are inevitable matters, and the Sufyani is among the inevitable ones that must occur.

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us; he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to me; he said: Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me; he said: Khallad al-Sa'igh narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: The Sufyani is inevitable, and he will not emerge except in Rajab. A man asked him: O Abu Abdillah, when he emerges, what will be our state? He said: When that happens, you are to keep to us.

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us from Nahawand in the year 273 AH, saying: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 229 AH, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about al-Sufyani, and he said: 'How can you have al-Sufyani until al-Shaysabani rises before him? He will rise from the land of Kufa, flowing forth like water flows forth, and he will kill your delegation. So anticipate after that al-Sufyani, and the rising of al-Qa'im (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yasar al-Thawri narrated to us, he said: al-Khalil ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: I accompanied Abul Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far from Mecca to Medina. One day he said to me: 'O Ali, if the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth revolted against the Banu al-Abbas, the earth would be watered with their blood until al-Sufyani rises.' I said to him: 'O my master, is his rising inevitable?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he pondered for a while, then raised his head and said: 'The rule of the Banu al-Abbas is based on cunning and deceit. It will pass until it is said that nothing of it remains, then it will return until it is said that nothing like it has ever happened.'

(10) Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated that Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Khalanji narrated that Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qassim al-Ja'fari said: 'We were with Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him) when the mention of al-Sufyani came up, and what has come in the narrations that his matter is inevitable. I said to Abu Ja'far: 'Does Allah change His determination concerning the inevitable?' He said: 'Yes.' We said to him: 'We fear that He may change His determination concerning the Qa'im.' He said: 'Indeed, the Qa'im is from the Promise, and Allah does not fail to perform the Promise.'

Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said: I said to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'May Allah make you succeed! People narrate that as-Sufyani will rise after the rule of the Banu al-Abbas has declined.' He said: 'They tell falsehood! As-Sufyani will rise while their rule is still prevailing.'

Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala', from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'foor who said: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said to me: The Abbasids and the Marwanids will have a battle at Qarqeessiya in which a young boy will grow grey (from the intensity), and Allah will remove victory from them, and He will reveal to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth: 'Sate yourselves with the flesh of the tyrants.' Then as-Sufyani will emerge.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to us from his book in Safar of the year four and seventy (74) and two hundred (200), saying: Al-Abbas ibn Aamir ibn Rabah ath-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ar-Rabee' al-Aqra' narrated to me, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said: When as-Sufyani conquers the five districts, then count to him nine months. And Hisham claimed that the five districts were: Damascus, Palestine, Jordan, Hims and Halab.

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, who said: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Mubarak, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from al-Harith al-Hamdani, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that he said: Al-Mahdi will come, curly-haired, with a mole on his cheek; his beginning will be from the East. And when that occurs, As-Sufyani will rise, and he will rule for the duration of a woman's pregnancy, nine months. He will emerge in Sham, and the people of Sham will submit to him except for some groups who remain steadfast upon the truth, whom Allah preserves from going out with him. He will come to Medina with a mighty army until when he reaches the desert of Medina, Allah will cause the earth to swallow him, And that is the saying of Allah in His Book: 'And could you see when they shall become terrified, but (then) there shall be no escape and they shall be seized upon from a near place.'

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Al-Yamani and as-Sufyani are like two racehorses.

We were informed by Ali ibn Ahmad, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Musa, who said: Ahmad ibn Abu Ahmad, known as Abu Ja'far al-Warraq, informed me, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Muhajir ibn Hakim, from al-Mughira ibn Sa'id, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: "When the two spears (armies) clash in Sham, it will not conclude except with a sign of Allah." It was asked: "What is it, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "An earthquake will occur in Sham, in which more than one hundred thousand people will perish. Allah will make it a mercy for the believers and a torment for the disbelievers. When that happens, look for the riders of the gray horses with the cropped tails and the yellow banners, coming from the West until they settle in Sham. This will be at the time of the Great Panic and the Red Death. When that occurs, look for the sinking of a village of Damascus called Harasta. When that happens, the Son of the Liver-Eater will emerge from the dry valley until he stands on the pulpit of Damascus. When that happens, await the emergence of al-Mahdi."

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan ibn Wahb narrated to me, he said: Isma'il ibn Abban narrated to me, from Yunus ibn Abu Ya'foor, he said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: When as-Sufyani rises, he will send an army to us and an army to you. If that takes place, come to us by any means, whether difficult or easy.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Sabah ibn al-Dhahak narrated to me, saying: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), saying: As-Sufyani is red, blond, and blue-eyed. He has never worshipped Allah at all, and he has not seen Mecca nor Medina at all. He says: 'O my Lord, my revenge [even] with the Fire, O my Lord, my revenge [even] with the Fire.'

We were informed by Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Mas'oodi, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar in Qum informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Hassaan al-Razi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi informed us, from Abdurrahman ibn Abu Hammad, from Ya'qoob ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari, from Ataba ibn Sa'dan ibn Yazeed, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said: I entered upon Ali for my need, then Ibn al-Kawwa' and Shibth ibn Rabi' came and asked permission to enter. Ali said to me: If you wish, permit them, for you were the first to have your need. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, permit them. When they entered, he said to them: What made you secede from me in Harura'? They said: We loved to be from the Army of Anger. He said: Woe to you! Is there anger in my guardianship? Does anger come until it becomes from the calamity such and such? Then they gather in groups like the groups of autumn from the tribes, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, or ten.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Durays, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Ali ibn al-Husayn or from Muhammad ibn Ali, that he said: Al-Fuqada' are a people who are missed from their beds, and in the morning they are found in Mecca. This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'And for each is a direction toward which he turns. So compete in good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.' And they are the companions of Al-Qa'im.

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us in Nahawand in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 229 AH, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abban ibn Taghlib, who said: I was with Ja'far ibn Muhammad in a mosque in Mecca, and he was holding my hand, so he said: 'O Abban, Allah will bring three hundred and thirteen men to this mosque of yours. The people of Mecca will know that their fathers and grandfathers have not yet been created. They will have swords on them, and on each sword is written the name of the man, his father's name, his appearance, and his lineage. Then a caller will be commanded to call out: 'This is al-Mahdi. He judges with the judgments of David and Solomon, and he is not asked to provide evidence for that.'

Ali ibn Ahmad narrated from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Harun ibn Muslim the scribe who used to narrate in Sarr al-Manna, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abdul Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding His saying, Exalted is He: Or, who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil, and makes you successors in the earth? [Is] there a deity with Allah? Little do you remember. {62} He said: This verse was revealed regarding al-Qa'im (the Awaited Imam). Gabriel (peace be upon him) was on the drainspout in the form of a white bird, and he will be the first of God's creation to pay allegiance to him (I mean Gabriel). Then the people will pay allegiance to him, three hundred and thirteen. Whoever is tested with walking will arrive at that hour, and whoever is not tested with walking will disappear from his bed. This is the saying of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (peace be upon him): 'The missing ones are from their beds.' And it is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'For each is a direction towards which he turns; so compete in good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.' {148} He said: The good deeds are the Wilayah (guardianship) for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Allah will send three hundred and thirteen men to a mosque in Mecca. The people of Mecca will know that they were not born from their fathers or grandfathers. Swords will be upon them, written on which are one thousand words; each word is a key to one thousand words. And Allah will send the wind from every valley saying: 'This is the Mahdi; he rules with the ruling of David,' and he does not require any evidence.

Ahmad ibn Hawtha, Abu Sulayman, narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Abul Jarood, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said: The companions of al-Qa'im will be three hundred and thirteen men, sons of the Persians (foreigners). Some of them will be carried on the clouds during the day, known by their name, their father's name, their lineage, and their appearance. Some of them will be asleep on their beds, and they will arrive in Mecca without any prior appointment.

Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) That Al-Qa'im will descend from the defile of Thi Tuwa with the number of the people of Badr - three hundred and thirteen men - until he leans his back against the Black Stone, and shakes the victorious banner. Ali ibn Abu Hamza said: I mentioned that to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, and he said: It is an evidenced book.

Ten - Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Imran ibn Dhiyan, from Abu Tahya Hakim ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) say: Indeed, the companions of al-Qa'im will be young men; there will be no old men among them except like the kohl in the eye, or like the salt in the provisions, and the least part of the provisions is the salt.

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: While the young men of the Shia were sleeping on the roofs of their houses, they were gathered to their companion (al-Qa'im) in one night without any prior appointment, so they would become in Mecca in the morning.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Sabah, saying: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, saying: He who heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: When the Qa'im (peace be upon him) appears, those who thought themselves to be of his people will depart from this matter, and those who are like the worshippers of the sun and the moon will enter into it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub Abu al-Hasan al-Ja'fi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Mufaddal ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Hurayz, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, that he said: When the Qa'im arises, Allah will remove the ailment from every believer and restore to him his strength.

(3) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali, who said: al-Hasan and Muhammad, the sons of Ali ibn Yousuf, narrated from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Sabah al-Muzni from al-Harith ibn Haseera from Habba al-Orani, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: As if I see our Shia in the mosque of Kufa, who have set up pavilions teaching the people the Qur'an as it was revealed. Indeed, when our Qa'im arises, he will destroy it and level its mihrab.

Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal narrated to us, from Ali ibn Aqaba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: "As if I see the Shia of Ali with the Qur'an in their hands, teaching people the newly arrived (or new converts)."

(5) Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtah narrated: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated from Sabah al-Muzni, from al-Harith ibn Hasirah, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying: "It is as if I see the non-Arabs setting up their pavilions in the mosque of Kufa, teaching people the Quran as it was revealed." I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, is it not as it was revealed?" He said: "No, the names of seventy from Quraysh have been erased from it, along with the names of their fathers. And Abu Lahab was left only to show contempt for the Messenger of Allah, because he was his uncle."

Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaniji narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from one who narrated it, from Ja'far ibn Yahya, from his father, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said: "How will you be if the companions of al-Qa'im set up their pavilions in the mosque of Kufa, and then he appears to them with a new ideal, a new matter, severe upon the Arabs."

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: Abu Tahir al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Isa narrated to me, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, saying: I was with Abu Abdullah an old man entered upon him and said: 'My sons have been undutiful to me and my brothers have turned away from me.' Abu Abdullah said: 'Do you not know that the truth has a government (era/state) and the untruth also has a government? Each of them is lowly in the state of the other. Whoever is afflicted by the ease/prosperity of the untruth will be retributed for it in the state of the truth.'

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha narrated to us, he said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, he said: He narrated to me Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, who said: When the Qa'im arises, he will send out into the regions of the earth, to every region a man, saying: 'Your covenant is in your hand.' So when a matter comes to you that you do not understand and do not know the judgment for, look at your hand and act according to what is in it.' He said: 'And he will send an army to Constantinople. When they reach the sea, they will write something on their feet and walk on the water. When the Romans see them walking on the water, they will say: 'These are his companions walking on the water, so how is he (the Imam)?' At that, they will open the gates of the city for them, they will enter it, and rule in it as they wish.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qarashi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hurayz, from Abban ibn Taghlib, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: "This world will not pass away until a caller from the Heaven calls out: 'O people of the truth, gather together!' They will become in one plain. Then he will call out again: 'O people of falsehood, gather together!' They will become in one plain." I said: "Can these people enter among those people?" He said: "No, by Allah." "And that is the word of Allah: 'Never would Allah allow the believers to remain in your condition until He separates the evil from the good. And it is not for Allah to reveal to you the unseen. But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Him, then for you is a great reward.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub Abu al-Hasan al-Ja'fi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father and Wuhayb from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Let one of you prepare himself for the appearance of al-Qa'im even with one arrow, for if Allah, the Exalted, knows that from his intention, I hope that He will prolong his life until he meets him, and he becomes one of his assistants and supporters.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqdah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to me, saying: My two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, from their father, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, and from Jamee' ibn al-Kunasi all together, from Abu Baseer, from Kamil, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, our Qa'im, when he rises, will invite the people to a new matter, just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) invited them to it. And indeed, Islam began as something strange, and it will return as something strange as it began. So, good news to the strangers.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: Islam began as something strange and will return as something strange as it began, so good news for the strangers. I said: Explain this to me, may God rectify you. He said: From what the caller among us will initiate anew is a new call, just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) called.

And with this chain of narration, from Ibn Sinan, from Abdullah bin Miskan, from Malik al-Juhani, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far: 'We describe the master of this matter with the description that no one among the people has.' He said: 'No, by Allah, it will not be so forever, until he himself is the one who argues with you about that and invites you to it.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurara narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Abu Amr al-Jallab, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said: Islam began as something strange and will return as something strange as it began, so good news is for the strangers.
