Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abul Jarood, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he heard him say: The matter (of leadership/deliverance) is with the youngest of us in age and the most obscure in memory (or reputation).

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Mabindath narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Hadhrami, from Abu as-Safatij, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to them (to Abu Abdullah or to Abu Ja'far): Can this matter (imamate) be entrusted to one who has not yet reached adulthood? He said: It will be so. I said: What does he do? He said: He is granted knowledge and wisdom, and he is not left to his own self (fancies).

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarood, who said: He said to me, Abu Ja'far: This matter (of the Imamate/Leadership) will not occur except in the one of us who is the most obscure in memory (knowledge) and the youngest in age.

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Mabindath narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Is'haq ibn Sabbah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) that he said: Indeed, this [authority/imamate] will flow to the one who will bear the burden [of leadership].

(1) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqdah narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Muhammadi narrated to us from his book in Rajab of the year 268 AH, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl narrated to me, saying: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated to us from Is'haq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said: Isma'il ibn Ammar, the brother of Abu Abdillah, described his faith and belief, saying: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that you (describing them - meaning the Imams - one by one) until he reached Abu Abdillah, then he said: 'And Isma'il is [the Imam] after you.' He said: 'As for Isma'il, no.'

3 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqdah informed us, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us from his book, saying: 'Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from al-Walid ibn Subayh, who said: There was a conversation between me and a man called 'Abd al-Jalil regarding a succession (or appointment), so he said to me: 'Indeed, Abu 'Abdillah appointed Isma'il.' (He said) I said to Abu 'Abdillah: 'Indeed, 'Abd al-Jalil informed me that you appointed Isma'il during your lifetime, three years before your death.' He said: 'O Walid, by Allah! If I had done so, it would have been to so-and-so' (meaning Abu al-Hasan Musa) and he named him.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, saying: He (Al-Himyari) narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Jama'ah as-Sa'igh, who said: I heard al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Does Allah impose obedience upon a servant and then conceal the news of the heavens from him?' He (Abu Abdullah) said to him: 'Allah is more exalted, more generous, more compassionate to His servants, and more merciful than to impose obedience upon a servant and then conceal the news of the heavens from him morning and evening.' (He said): Then Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) appeared. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Does it please you to look at the keeper of the book of Ali?' Al-Mufadhdhal said to him: 'And what else would please me more than that?' He said: 'This is the keeper of the book of Ali; the hidden book about which Allah said, "None shall touch it save the purified ones."'

Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Suma'a narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from his father, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah and asked him about the master of the command after him, so he said to me: 'He is the master of the lamb.' And Musa was in a corner of the house as a boy, and with him was a Mekki lamb, and he was saying to it: 'Prostrate to Allah, Who created you!'

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I saw Abul Hasan Musa, who was then three years old, with him was a ewe from the Meek breed, and he was holding its bridle, and he was saying to it: 'Prostrate to Allah, Who created you.' So it did that three times. A young boy said to him: 'O my master, tell it to die!' He (Musa) said to him: 'Woe to you! Do I give life and cause death? Allah gives life and causes death.'

And from among the famous speech of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when he stood by the grave of Isma'il: My grief for you [in the afterlife] has overwhelmed my grief on you [in this world]. O Allah, I have gifted Isma'il all that he fell short of regarding my right upon him, so gift me all that he fell short of regarding Your right upon him.

Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, who said: Mansur ibn Hazim and Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while I was present with them, saying: 'May Allah make us ransom for you, indeed souls are taken in the morning and evening, so who will be ours after you?' He said: 'When that happens, this one.' He struck his hand towards the righteous servant Musa, who was a five-year-old boy wearing two white garments, and said: 'This one.' And Abdullah ibn Ja'far was present in the house at that time.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurara, who said: Abu Abdullah said: Know your Imam, for if you know him, it will not harm you whether this matter (deliverance) comes soon or is delayed.

(2) Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: My father al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir narrated to me, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'The Day We will call every people with their Imam. And whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their record and will not be wronged at all.' He said: 'O Fadhl, know your Imam, for if you know your Imam, it will not harm you whether this matter (the appearance of the Qa'im) comes early or late. And whoever knows his Imam and then dies before the one of this matter rises, he is like the one who is sitting in his camp, nay, he is like the one who sat under his banner.' (He said) And some of our companions narrated it with this addition: '...like the one who was martyred with the Messenger of Allah.'

3. Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who reported it to Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi Basir, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah, 'May I be sacrificed for you, when will the relief come?' He replied, 'O Aba Basir, are you among those who desire this world? Whoever understands this matter has already found relief by awaiting it.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Salih ibn al-Sindi from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Khuza'i, who said: Abu Baseer asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while I was listening, saying: 'Do you think I will live to see the Qa'im (the Awaited One)?' He said: 'O Abu Baseer, do you not know your Imam?' He said: 'Yes, by Allah, and it is you.' And he took his hand. He said: 'By Allah, O Abu Baseer, you should not mind if you are sitting with your sword in the shadow of the Qa'im's tent.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Several of our companions informed us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far saying: Whoever dies without an Imam, his death is the death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah), and whoever dies while recognizing his Imam, the advancement or delay of this matter does not harm him, and whoever dies while recognizing his Imam, he is like one standing with the Leader in his tent.

Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda al-Kufi informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Mastoor al-Ashja'i narrated from his book in Safar of the year 266 AH, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ubaydillah al-Halabi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated from Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad saying while we were with him in the house, about twenty men. He turned to us and said: 'Perhaps you think that this matter of the Imamate is for any man among us to place it wherever he wishes; by Allah, it is a covenant from Allah that descended upon the Messenger of Allah to specific men, one after another, until it reaches its owner.'

And Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Yousuf ibn Ya'qob al-Ju'fi narrated to me from his book, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abu Hamza narrated to us from his father and Wuhayb ibn Hafs together, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah Regarding the saying of Allah: 'Surely Allah commands you to make over trusts to their owners and that when you judge between people you judge with justice; surely Allah admonishes you with what is excellent. Surely Allah was All-Hearing, All-Seeing.' He said: It is the will (testament) that one of us delivers to the other.

Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji informed us from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah gave Ali a scroll sealed with twelve seals, and said to him: 'Open the first and act according to it, and give it to al-Hasan so he may open the second and act according to it, and he shall give it to al-Husayn who will open the third and act according to what is in it, then from one to another of the progeny of al-Husayn.'

And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about the saying of Allah: 'Surely Allah commands you to make over trusts to their owners and that when you judge between people you judge with justice; surely Allah admonishes you with what is excellent,' and Abu Ja'far al-Baqir said: The order of Allah in this verse concerns the imamate. Each imam of us has to deliver the imamate to the next imam coming after him. He does not have to hide it from him. Do you not hear Allah saying: (and that when you judge between people you judge with justice; surely Allah admonishes you with what is excellent)? It is the rulers. Do you not see that Allah has addressed the rulers with this verse?

And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda al-Kufi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qoob narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father, from Ya'qoob ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah saying: No, by Allah! Allah does not leave this matter aside unless He specifies ones, who will undertake it until the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn Uthman ad-Duhni narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far ar-Riqqi narrated to us, saying: Eesa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Mujalid ibn Sa'eed, from ash-Sha'bi, from Masrooq, who said: We were with Ibn Mas'ood when a man asked him: 'Did your Prophet tell you how many caliphs would be after him?' He said: 'Yes. And no one has asked me this before you, and you are the youngest of the people in age. I heard him saying: After me, there will be as many as the number of the chieftains of Moses.'

A group narrated it from Uthman ibn Abi Shayba, and Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Sa'id al-Ashajj, and Abu Kurayb, and Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, and Ali ibn Muhammad, and Ibraheem ibn Sa'id; they all said: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Mujalid, from ash-Sha'bi, from Masruq. He said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ood and asked him: 'Did your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) tell you how many caliphs would be after him?' He said: 'Yes, and no one has asked me about it before you, and you are the youngest of the people in age.' He said: 'After me, there will be as many as the chieftains of Moses.'

Three [narrators] - Abu Kurayb and Abu Sa'id said: Abu Usama narrated to us, he said: Al-Ash'ath narrated from Aamir, from his uncle, from Masrooq, who said: We were sitting with Abdullah ibn Mas'ood, and he was reciting the Quran to us. A man asked him: 'O Abu Abdurrahman, did you ask the Messenger of Allah how many caliphs will rule this Ummah after him?' He said: 'No one has asked me about this since I arrived in Iraq! Yes, we asked the Messenger of Allah, and he said: Twelve, the number of the chieftains of the Children of Israel.'

And from Uthman ibn Abi Shayba and Abu Ahmad, and Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan and Sufyan ibn Wakee', they said: Jareer narrated to us from al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from al-'Amir al-Sha'bi, from his uncle Qays ibn Abdillah who said: A nomad came to him while his companions were with him. He asked: 'Is Abdullah ibn Mas'ood among you?' They pointed to him. Abdullah said to him: 'You have found him, so what is your need?' He said: 'I want to ask you about something; if you heard it from the Messenger of Allah, inform us of it. How many caliphs will be after him?' He said: 'No one asked me about this since I arrived in Iraq! Yes, he said: The caliphs after me are twelve caliphs, like the number of the chieftains from the Children of Israel.'

And from Musaddad bin Mustawrid, who said: Hammad bin Zayd narrated to me, from Mujalid, from Masrooq, who said: We were sitting with Ibn Mas'ood after the sunset prayer, and he was teaching us the Qur'an. A man asked him, saying: 'O Abu Abdurrahman, did you ask the Prophet how many caliphs this umma will have?' He said: 'No one asked me about this since I arrived in Iraq. Yes.' And he said: 'Your caliphs are twelve, in the number of the chieftains of the Children of Israel.'

Amr bin Khalid bin Farrookh al-Harrani narrated: Zuhayr bin Muawiya narrated to us, saying: Ziyad bin Khaythama narrated to us, from al-Aswad bin Sa'id al-Hamadani, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This Umma will remain upright, prevailing over its enemy, until twelve Caliphs pass away, all of them from Quraysh.' When he returned to his home, delegations of Quraysh came to him and asked: 'Then what will happen?' He said: 'Commotion (Harj) will occur.' And he said: Zuhayr bin Muawiya narrated to us, saying: Ziyad bin Khaythama narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Aswad bin Sa'id al-Hamadani, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, and mentioned a similar narration.

Uthman bin Abu Shayba said: Jareer narrated to me, from Hussayn bin Abdurrahman, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'After me, twelve emirs will arise.' He said: Then he spoke something that I did not hear, so I asked the people and asked my father, who was closer to him than I was, and he said: He said: 'All of them are from Quraysh.'

Uthman ibn Abi Shayba said: Hatam ibn Isma'il narrated to us from Muhajir ibn Mismar, from Aamir ibn Sa'd, who said: I sent with my servant Nafi' to Jabir ibn Samra, asking him to inform me of something he had heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He wrote to me: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: On the eve of Friday, when al-Aslami was stoned: 'This religion will remain established until the Hour is established, or until twelve caliphs, all from Quraysh, will rule over the people.' And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. And from Abbad ibn Ya'qoob, who said: Hatam ibn Isma'il narrated to us with its chain, the like of it. And from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, who said: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Thi'b, from Muhajir ibn Mismar with its chain, the like of it.

And from Ghundar from Shu'ba who said: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abdul Malik ibn Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samra who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: This religion will remain upright until twelve caliphs will arise. Then he said a word that I did not understand, so I asked my father, and he said: He said: All of them are from Quraysh.

And from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Malik ibn Zayd who said: Ziyad ibn Aqilah narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Samra al-Sawwa'i narrated to us, saying: I was with my father near the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: 'After me, there will be twelve emirs.' Then he lowered his voice, so I asked my father, and he said: 'He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'

And from Khalaf bin al-Walid al-Lu'lu'i, from Israel, from Sammak, who said: I heard Jabir bin Samra saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: After him - or those after him - twelve leaders will arise. Then he spoke a word that I did not understand, so I asked the people what he had said? They said: He said: All of them are from Quraysh.

And from the narration of Khalaf ibn Hisham al-Bazzar, he said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us from Mujalid ibn Sa'id, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samura al-Saw'i, who said: The Messenger of Allah (saw) delivered a sermon to us at 'Arafah and said: 'This religion will remain strong, honored, and dominant over those who oppose it. It will not be harmed by those who separate from it or oppose it until twelve [leaders] rule.' He said: 'The people began to speak, and I did not understand, so I asked my father: O my father, what did the Messenger of Allah mean by And from the narration of al-Nufayli al-Harrani, he said: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, and he said: Ziyad ibn Khaythama narrated to us, and he said: al-Aswad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated from Jabir ibn Samura, who said: The Messenger of Allah (saw) said: 'The affairs of this nation will continue to be upright, and it will prevail over its enemies until twelve caliphs pass, all of them from Quraysh.' When he returned to his home, delegations of Quraysh came to him and asked: 'What will happen after that?' He said: 'Then there will be chaos.'

And from the hadith of Ali ibn al-Ja'd, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Aqlah, Sammak and Husayn, all of them, from Jabir ibn Samrah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There will be after me twelve emirs.' But Husayn said: 'Twelve caliphs.' Then he spoke something that I did not understand. And some of them said in his narration: 'So I asked my father.' And some of them said: 'So I asked the people,' and they said: 'He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'

And from Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani who said: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Khaythama narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, from Jabir ibn Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: This Umma will remain with its affairs upright and prevailing over its enemy until twelve Caliphs have passed away from it.

And from the hadith of Mu'ammār ibn Sulaymān, who said: I heard Ismā'īl ibn Abī Khālid narrating from Mujālid, from ash-Sha'bī, from Jābir ibn Samurah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He said: 'This religion will remain prominent, unaffected by its opponents, until twelve Caliphs have passed.' Then he said a word that I did not understand. I asked my father: 'What did he say?' He said: 'He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'

And from Yazeed bin Sinan and Uthman bin Abu Shayba, he said: Musa bin Ismaeel narrated to us, he said: Hammad bin Salama narrated to us, from Sammak bin Harb, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: I heard the Prophet saying: "This Islam will remain strong until twelve caliphs." Then he said a word that I did not understand, so I asked my father: What did he say? He said: He said: All of them are from Quraysh.

And from the hadith of Yazeed ibn Sinan, who said: Abur-Rabee' az-Zahrani narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: Mujalid ibn Sa'eed narrated to us, from ash-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave us a speech and I heard him saying: 'This matter will remain strong, dominant, and prevailing over its opponents until twelve (leaders) rule, all of them...' Then the people began talking and making noise, so I could not understand what he said after 'all of them'. I asked my father, 'O my father, what did he say after 'all of them'? He said: He said: 'All of them are from Quraysh.'

And from the hadith of Yazeed ibn Sinan, who said: Abdul-Hameed ibn Musa narrated to us, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samra, who said: I entered with my father to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and I heard him saying: 'The Umma will remain holding fast to this until twelve leaders or twelve caliphs will arise.' He said: 'And he lowered his voice with a word, and my father was closer to him than I was.' So when we went out, I asked: 'What was the word he lowered his voice for?' He said: 'He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'

And from the hadith of Yazeed bin Sinan, who said: Al-Hasan bin Umar bin Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: Jareer bin Abdul-Hameed narrated to us, from Hussayn bin Abdurrahman, from Jabir bin Samra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'After me, twelve emirs will arise among my umma.' Then he spoke something that I did not hear. He said: So I asked the people and I asked my father, who was closer to the Prophet than I was. He said: The Prophet said: 'All of them are from Quraysh.'

And from Ibn Abi Fudayk, who said: Ibn Abi Thi'b narrated to me from Muhajir bin Missmar, from Aamir bin Sa'd, that he sent to Ibn Samra asking: Tell us what you heard from the Messenger of Allah? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah saying: 'This religion will remain firm until there are twelve caliphs from Quraysh.' And he traced the hadith to its end.

And from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Sahl ibn Hammad (Abu Itab al-Dallal) narrated to us, who said: Yunus ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated to us, who said: Awl ibn Abi Jahimah narrated to us, from his father, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while he was delivering a sermon, and my uncle was sitting in front of him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The affair of my nation will remain sound until twelve caliphs have passed, all of them from Quraysh.

And from the hadith of Suwayd ibn Sa'id, who said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Abul Khayr, from Abdullah ibn Amr There is no doubt that it has been written in the Book of Allah: Twelve will rule over people.

And from Ibn Abi Khaythama who said: Affan and Yahya ibn Ishaq as-Saylaheeni narrated to us, they said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Uthman narrated from Abut-Tufayl, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr said: "O Abut-Tufayl, count twelve from the sons of Ka'b ibn Lu'ay, then comes al-Naqf and an-Naqaf." The narrations on this meaning from the paths of the general public (Sunni) are numerous, indicating that the Messenger of Allah mentioned the twelve and that they are his successors.

Ahmad ibn Nasr ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us from Nahawand in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 29 AH (of the century), saying: Yahya ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad said to me: O Yahya ibn Abdullah, He who spends a night without knowing his Imam will die a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).

And with the first chain, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'What is the status of one who denies an Imam from among you?' He said: 'He who denies an Imam from Allah and is exempt from him and his religion is an unbeliever and apostate from Islam, because the Imam is from Allah and his religion is the religion of Allah; and whoever is exempt from the religion of Allah, his blood is permissible to be killed in that state, unless he returns or repents to Allah Almighty from what he said.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to us in the year three and seventy of the two hundred, saying: Ali ibn Sayf ibn Umayra narrated to us, saying: Abban ibn Uthman narrated to us from Humran ibn A'yun, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah about the Imams, and he said: 'He who denies one of the living has denied the dead.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla, from Ibn Jumhur, from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah about the Imams, and he said: 'Whoever denies one of the living [Imams] has denied the dead [ones].'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us from his book, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Aamir narrated to us, from Abdul Malik ibn Atba, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever dies without knowing his Imam, dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us; he said: Narrated to me a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of the Exalted: 'So if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than he who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.' He said: It means one who made his own opinion his religion, without an Imam from the Imams of Guidance.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: He, who joins to an Imam whose imamate is from Allah another Imam whose imamate is not from Allah, is a polytheist.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Mansur ibn Yunus from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said: I said to Abu Abdillah: A man said to me: 'Know the last one of the Imams and it does not harm you if you have not known the first one.' He said: 'May Allah curse him! I hate him although I do not know him. Has the last one been known except by knowing the first one?'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated: Some of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Wahb, from Muhammad ibn Masnun, who said: I asked him (meaning Abu Abdillah)... ...about the saying of Allah: 'And when they commit an indecency, they say: We found our fathers doing this, and Allah has enjoined it on us. Say: Surely Allah does not enjoin indecency; do you say against Allah what you do not know?' He said: Have you seen anyone claiming that Allah ordered him to commit adultery, drink wine, or do any of these forbidden things? I said: No. He said: Then what is this indecency that they claim Allah ordered them to do? I said: Allah and His guardian are more aware. He said: This is among the followers of the Imams of injustice; they claimed that Allah ordered them to follow some people, whom Allah had never ordered them to follow. So Allah denied their saying and informed them that they had fabricated lies against Him, and He called that from among them an indecency.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Some of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Wahb, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said: I asked a virtuous servant (of Allah), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah: 'Say: My Lord has only prohibited indecencies, those of them that are apparent as well as those that are concealed, and the sin, and the transgression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.' (He) said, so he said: Indeed, the Qur'an has an apparent meaning and a hidden meaning, so all that which Allah has prohibited in the Qur'an is impermissible in its apparent sense as it is in the apparent sense, and the hidden aspect of that is the Imams of Injustice. And all that which Allah the Exalted has permitted in the Book is permissible and it is the apparent, and the hidden aspect of that is the Imams of Truth.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Jabir, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the meaning of Allah's saying: "And among men is he who takes for himself rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah. And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah." And if those who were unjust had seen, when they see the chastisement, that the power is wholly Allah's and that Allah is severe in requiting (evil)." He said: By Allah, they are the followers of so-and-so and so-and-so; they took them as imams instead of the Imam whom Allah appointed for people. And for this reason He said: "And among men is he who takes for himself rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah. And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah." And if those who were unjust had seen, when they see the chastisement, that the power is wholly Allah's and that Allah is severe in requiting (evil)." "When those who were followed shall renounce those who followed (them), and they see the chastisement and their ties are cut asunder. And those who followed shall say: Had there been for us a return, then we would renounce them as they have renounced us. Thus will Allah show them their deeds to be intense regret to them, and they shall not come forth from the fire." Then Abu Ja'far said: They are, by Allah, O Jabir, the imams of injustice and their followers.

And through him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sajistani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah the Almighty said: I will surely punish every group of Muslims in Islam that submits to the guardianship of every unjust Imam who is not from Allah, even if that group is pious and God-fearing in their actions; and I will surely forgive every group of Muslims in Islam that submits to the guardianship of every just Imam from Allah, even if that group is sinful and erring in their actions.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Allah is not ashamed to punish a nation that submits to an Imam who is not from Allah, even if they are pious and God-fearing in their deeds. And Allah is ashamed to punish a nation that submits to an Imam who is from Allah, even if they are unjust and sinful in their deeds.

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, he said: He narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Abdullah ibn Abu Ya'foor, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah A man who believes in your guardianship, exempts himself from your enemy, permits what you have permitted, prohibits what you have prohibited, and claims that the authority is still with you and has not passed to others, except that he says: They have disagreed among themselves while they are the leading Imams. If they agree upon a man and say 'This is he,' we say 'This is he.' He said: If he dies upon this opinion, he has died a death of ignorance (jahiliyyah).

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qarashi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Sa'dan narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah I said: A man who believes in the guardianship of Ali and exempts himself from his enemy, and believes in everything that he says, except that he says: They have disagreed among themselves whereas they are the leading imams. I do not know which of them is the Imam. If they agree upon a certain one, I will submit to his word, and I have known that the authority is among them. He (peace be upon him) said: If this man dies upon that state, he dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah). Then he said: The Qur'an has interpretations that occur as the day and the night run, and as the sun and the moon run. If an interpretation of something from it comes, it will occur. Some of it has come, and some of it has not come yet.

And Salama ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Dawood narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Mufaddhal ibn Za'ida, from al-Mufaddhal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah said: Whoever worships Allah without learning (the principles of worship) from a truthful jurisprudent, Allah will let him be confused and astray; and whoever claims that he has heard from other than the gate (source) that Allah has opened to His people, is considered as a polytheist. That gate is the trusted one, who has been entrusted (by Allah) with the hidden secret of Allah.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to us in Sha'ban in the year three and seventy of the two hundred, saying: Ali ibn Sayf ibn 'Umayra narrated to us, from his father, from Humran ibn A'yun, that he said: I described to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a man who believes in the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and exempts himself from his enemy, and believes in all that he says, except that he says: 'They have disagreed among themselves, and they are the leading Imams, and I do not know which of them is the Imam. And if they agree upon one man, we will submit to his word, and I have known that the matter is among them - may Allah have mercy on them all.' He (Abu Abdillah) said: 'If this man dies, he dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).' And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in delusion. And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and that which they invent.

(2) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda said: Muhammad ibn al-Mufadhdhal, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Malik, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qatawani narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us, from Hisham ibn al-Salam, from Abu Hamza ath-Thimali, from Abu Ishaq as-Subay'i, who said: I heard one of the trusted companions of the Commander of the Faithful saying: The Commander of the Faithful said in a long sermon he delivered in Kufa, mentioning it: "O Allah, it is necessary for You to have authorities on Your earth, one authority after another, over Your creation, guiding them to Your religion and teaching them Your knowledge, so that the followers of Your guardians do not become divided. They are either apparent but not obeyed, or concealed, fearful, and awaiting. If their persons are absent from people during their truce in the state of untruth, their scattered knowledge will not be absent knowledge will not be absent from them. Their principles are fixed in the hearts of the believers, and they act upon them. They find comfort in what the liars find alienating and what the extravagant regarding Allah reject. Speech that is measured without a price; if there were one who hears it with his mind, recognizes it, believes in it, and follows it, and adopts its path and succeeds thereby? Then he said: Who is this? And this is why knowledge is lost because it finds no bearers to preserve it and transmit it as they heard it from the scholars." "O Allah, and I know well that knowledge is not entirely lost nor its means cut off, for You do not leave Your earth without an authority over Your creation, either apparent and obeyed, or concealed and submerged, not obeyed, so that Your proof is not invalidated and Your friends do not go astray after You have guided them."

(3) Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated: Ali ibn Ibraheem ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus and Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say: The earth does not remain empty of a scholar (Imam), so that if the believers add something (to the religion), he corrects them, and if they omit something, he completes it for them.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ar-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musalli from Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Amiri from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: The earth does not cease to have an authority (Hujjah) from Allah in it, who knows the permissible and the impermissible, and invites people to the way of Allah.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from some of his men, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him: 'Does the earth remain without an Imam?' He replied: 'No.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said: Allah did not leave the earth without a scholar (Imam); and were it not for that, the truth would not be distinguished from the falsehood.

And from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Hamza al-Thimali, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said: By Allah, Allah has not left His earth since He took Adam (peace be upon him), except that there is in it an Imam who is followed to reach Allah, and he is His proof upon His servants, and the earth will not remain without an Imam who is the proof of Allah upon His servants.
And through it from Abu Hamza he said: I asked Abu Abdullah: 'Will the earth remain without an Imam?' He said: 'If the earth were to remain without an Imam, it would sink.'

And through him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: 'Will the earth remain without an Imam?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'We narrate from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that it will not remain without an Imam except if Allah becomes angry with the people of the earth (or he said: with the servants).' He said: 'The earth will not remain without an Imam, and if it were to remain without one, it would sink.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Abu 'Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Abu Hurasa, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said: If the Imam were removed from the earth for an hour, it would sink with its people and surge like the sea surges with its people.

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha' who said: I asked Imam ar-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Does the earth remain without an Imam?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'We narrate traditions saying that it does not remain [without an Imam] except if Allah becomes angry with the people.' He said: 'It does not remain [without an Imam], otherwise it would sink.'

Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Abu Amara Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah saying: If only two people remained on the earth, the second of them would be the Hujjah (Proof/Imam).

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us, from some of his men and Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya all together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Amara Hamza ibn at-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If two men remained on the earth, one of them would be the Hujjah (proof/authority) over the other.

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from someone he mentioned, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Karram, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If people were just two men, one of them would be the Imam.' And he said: 'The last one to die is the Imam, so that no one may have a claim against Allah that He left him without an authority from Him.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: If there remained on the earth only two people, one of them would be the Hujjah (or the second would be the Hujjah).

Among that, Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali and Ubayd Allah ibn al-Marzaban, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I visited Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) the year before he went to Iraq, and his son Ali was sitting in front of him. He looked at me and said: 'O Muhammad, indeed there will be a movement/disturbance in this year, so do not be anxious about it.' I said: 'And what will it be, may God make me your ransom? For it has filled me with anxiety.' He said: 'I will go to this despot, and indeed he will not initiate any evil from me, nor from the one who will be after me.' I said: 'And what will it be, may God make me your ransom?' He said: 'God will make the unjust err and do what He wills.' I said: 'And what is that, may God make me your ransom?' He said: 'Whoever wrongs this son of mine and denies his Imamate after me is like the one who wronged Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and denied his right after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' I said: 'By God, if God prolongs my life, I will submit to his right and affirm his Imamate.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth, O Muhammad. God will prolong your life, and you will submit to his right (peace be upon him) and affirm his Imamate and the Imamate of the one who will be after him.' I said: 'And who is that?' He said: 'His son, Muhammad.' I said: 'To him be the pleasure and submission.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ismail ibn Ibad al-Qasri together, from Dawood al-Raqi who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, I have grown old, so take my hand (and save me) from the Fire. (Who is our companion/leader after you)? He pointed to his son, Abul Hasan (peace be upon him), and said: This is your companion/leader after me.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Husayn ibn Naeem al-Saffaf, who said: I, Hisham ibn al-Hakam, and Ali ibn Yaqtin were in Baghdad. Ali ibn Yaqtin said: I was sitting with the Pious Servant (peace be upon him) when his son Ali entered. He said to me: O Ali ibn Yaqtin, this is Ali, the chief of my children. Indeed, I have bestowed upon him my kunya (agnomen). Hisham struck his forehead with his palm and said: Woe to you, how did you say that? Ali ibn Yaqtin replied: I heard it from him, by God, just as I said. Hisham said: The authority, by God, is for him after him.

From him, from a group of our scholars, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Naeem al-Qabusi, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) that he said: My son Ali, the eldest of my children, is the one most preferred by me and the one most loved by me. He examined the leather case (Jafr) with me. Only a prophet or the testamentary trustee (Wasi) of a prophet can examine it.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ali ibn Hakam together, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, who said: The ordinances (alwah) came to us from Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was in prison: My testament to the eldest of my sons is that he should do such-and-such. As for so-and-so, do not give him anything until you meet me or God decrees death for me.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi - (and he was from the Waqifiya) - he said: I visited Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and with him was his son Abul Hasan. He said to me: 'O Ziyad, this is my son Ali. His writing is my writing, his speech is my speech, his messenger is my messenger, and whatever he says, the saying is his saying.'

From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from al-Makhzumi (and his mother was from the descendants of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib), who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) sent for us and gathered us, then said to us: Do you know why I have gathered you? We said: No. He said: Bear witness that this son of mine is my testamentary trustee (Wasi), the one who will uphold my affair, and my successor after me. Whoever has a debt from me, let him take it from this son of mine. Whoever has a promise from me, let him have it fulfilled from him. And whoever cannot do without meeting me, let him not meet me except through his letter.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abi Ali al-Khazzaz, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): I am afraid that something may happen and I will not be able to meet you, so inform me about the Imam after you? He said: My son, so-and-so, meaning Abul Hasan (peace be upon him).

And with this chain, from Ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Nasr ibn Qabus, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): I asked your father (peace be upon him): Who will be after you? He informed me that you are he. So when Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) passed away, the people went right and left, and I and my companions declared for you. So inform me, who will be after you from your children? He said: My son, so-and-so.

From him, from Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Dahhak ibn al-Ash'ath, from Dawud ibn Zarbi, who said: I brought some wealth to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He took some of it and left some of it. I said: May God rectify you, why did you leave it with me? He said: The one who holds this authority will ask for it from you. When his obituary arrived, Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent for me and asked me for that wealth, and I handed it over to him.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, from al-Zayd ibn Sulayt, in a long tradition from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) That he said in the year in which he was taken (died): I will be taken in this year, and the authority (Amr) belongs to my son Ali, who is named after two Alis. As for the first Ali, it is Ali ibn Abi Talib, and as for the other Ali, it is Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them. He is given the understanding, forbearance, victory, love, and covenant of the first, and the tribulation of the other, and his patience for what he dislikes... The rest of the news.

And Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from a group of our companions, among them Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, and al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan (in his hadith), who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): May I ask you? He said: Ask your Imam. I said: Who do you mean? For I do not know any Imam other than you. He said: It is Ali, my son, whom I have given my kunya (agnomen). I said: My master, save me from the Fire, for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, you are the Qaim (the one standing/active) in this matter! He said: Was I not the Qaim? Then he said: O Hasan, there is no Imam who is the Qaim in a community except that he is their Qaim. And when they pass away from them, the one who succeeds them is the Qaim. The Hujjah (Divine Proof) until he becomes concealed from them, so all of us are Qaim. So direct all that you were treating me with to my son Ali. (By Allah) By Allah, it was not I who did that to him, but Allah did that to him.

Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan al-Nishapuri, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Safwan ibn Yahya and Uthman ibn Isa, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: I was in the company of Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), so he said to me: Indeed, Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: A man is fortunate if he lives to see his successor from his own self. Then he pointed with his hand to his son Ali and said: This is he, and Allah has shown me my successor from my own self.

From him, from Saad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubaid, from Ali ibn Hakam and Ali ibn Hasan ibn Nafe, from Harun ibn Kharja, who said: Harun ibn Saad al-Ajali said to me: 'Ismail, to whom you were looking forward [with hope for his Imamate], has died. And Ja'far is an old man who will die tomorrow or the day after, so you will remain without an Imam.' I did not know what to say, so I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of his statement. He said: 'Far off, far off! Allah willed, by Allah, that this matter [of Imamate] will not be cut off until the night and day are cut off. When you see him, tell him: This is Musa ibn Ja'far who is growing up, and we will marry him, and a son will be born to him, and he will be a successor, if Allah wills.'

And in another report, he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in a lengthy tradition: Our Master will appear, and he is from his loins; and he pointed with his hand to Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). Thus, he would fill it with justice as it had been filled with injustice and tyranny; and the world would be cleared and prepared for him.

Ayyub ibn Nuh narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, who said: I heard Ali ibn Ja'far saying: I was with my brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who by Allah was the Divine Proof on the earth after my father (peace be upon him and his family). Just then his son Ali arrived, and he said to me: 'O Ali, this is your master, and his position with me is like my position with my father. May Allah keep you firm on His religion.' I wept and said to myself: 'He is conveying the news of his death to me.' He said: 'O Ali, it is inevitable that divine destiny be issued regarding me, and I have as a model the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Commander of the Faithful, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husain (peace be upon them). This occurred three days before Harun al-Rashid took him away for the second time. The report is complete. The narrations on this theme are too numerous to count, and they exist in the books of the Imamiyyah, known and famous. Whoever wishes may refer to them from there, and what is mentioned here is sufficient, if Allah wills.'

Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Jamhur from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman who said: Abu Ibrahim (Imam al-Kadhim, peace be upon him) passed away, and there was no one among his representatives (quwwam) except that he had a large amount of wealth. This was the reason for their Waqifiyyah stance and their denial of his death, out of greed for the money. Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi possessed seventy thousand dinars, and Ali ibn Abi Hamza possessed thirty thousand dinars. When I saw this and the truth became clear to me, and I recognized the matter of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) as I knew it, I spoke up and called people to his Imamate. Then they sent two messengers to me and said: 'What is calling you to this? If you desire wealth, we will make you independent (rich)!' They guaranteed me ten thousand dinars and said to me: 'Refrain.' I refused and said to them: 'We have narrated from the Two Truthful Imams (peace be upon them) that they said: When innovations appear, it is upon the scholar to manifest his knowledge; if he does not do so, he will be deprived of the light of faith. And I would not abandon jihad and the command of God in any case.' So they antagonized me and harbored enmity against me.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated from al-Saffar and Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari, all together, from Yaqub ibn Yazid al-Anbari, from some of his companions, who said: Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) passed away, and with Ziyad al-Qandi were seventy thousand dinars, and with Uthman ibn Isa al-Rawasi were thirty thousand dinars and five slave girls, and his residence was in Egypt. So Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent to them: 'Carry over to me what is in your possession from the wealth and what has accumulated for my father with you from furniture and slave girls, for I am his heir and the one standing in his place, and we have divided his inheritance, and you have no excuse for withholding what has accumulated for me and his heir while you were holding it,' and words similar to this. As for Ibn Abi Hamza, he denied it and did not acknowledge what he had, and likewise Ziyad al-Qandi. But as for Uthman ibn Isa, he wrote to him: 'Your father (peace be upon him) has not died; he is alive and established, and whoever mentions that he died is a denier [of the truth]. And I act upon the fact that he has passed away as you say, so he did not command me to hand over anything to you, and as for the slave girls, I have emancipated them and married them.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed ibn Uqbah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Taymi, who said: I heard Harb ibn al-Hasan al-Tahhan narrating to Yahya ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi that Yahya ibn al-Masawar said: A group of Shia were present, and among them was Ali ibn Abi Hamza. I heard him say: Ali ibn Yaqtin entered upon Abul Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) and asked him about some matters, and he answered him. Then Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ali, your companion will kill me.' Ali ibn Yaqtin began to weep and said: 'Master, am I also with him?' He said: 'No, O Ali, do not be with him and do not witness my killing.' Ali said: 'Who is for us after you, O Master?' He replied: 'This Ali, my son; he is the best of those who will succeed me. His position to me is like my position with my father; he is for my Shia, with him is the knowledge they need. He is the leader in this world and the leader in the Hereafter, and indeed he is among the亲近 ones.' Yahya ibn al-Hasan said to Harb: 'So what caused Ali ibn Abi Hamza to disassociate from him and be jealous of him?' Harb said: 'I asked Yahya ibn al-Masawar about that, and he said: What motivated him was the wealth he had taken for himself, so that Allah would make him wretched in this world and the Hereafter.'

And Ali ibn Habashi ibn Qauni narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, who said: I used to see at my uncle Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal's place an old man from Baghdad who used to joke with my uncle. One day he said to him: 'There is no worse group in the world than you, O people of the Shia' - or he said 'the Rafidah'. My uncle asked him: 'Why? May Allah curse you.' He replied: 'I am the son-in-law of Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir al-Sarraj. When death approached him, he said to me: 'I have ten thousand dinars in deposit for Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). After his death, I did not hand them over to his son and claimed that he was not dead! By Allah, save me from the Fire and hand them over to al-Rida.' By Allah, we did not return even one dirham from that and left him to burn with it in the Fire of Hell.'
As for what has been reported regarding the criticism of the narrators of the Waqifiya, it is more than can be counted, and it is present in the books of our scholars; we mention a portion of it.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi al-Bilad who said: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: 'What has become of the wretched Hamza ibn Bazi?' I said: 'He has arrived.' He said: 'He claims that my father is alive! They are today among the doubters, and they will not die tomorrow except upon heresy (al-zandaqa).' Safwan said: 'I said to myself: I know them as doubters, so how can they die upon heresy?' We did not wait long until it reached us that one of them said at the time of his death: 'I am a disbeliever in my Lord who caused me to die!' Safwan said: 'This is confirmation of the tradition.'

Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Himam narrated from Ali ibn Rabah who said: I asked Qasim ibn Ismail al-Qurashi, who was a Mamtur: What did you hear from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza? He replied: I heard from him only one tradition. Ibn Rabah said: Then after that he produced many traditions and narrated them from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza. Ibn Rabah said: And I asked this Qasim: How many traditions did you hear from Hannan? He replied: Four or five traditions. He said: Then after that he produced many traditions and narrated them from him.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Saad ibn Saad from Ahmad ibn Umar who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) say regarding Ibn Abi Hamza: Is he not the one who narrated that the head of the Mahdi would be presented to Isa ibn Musa, who is the companion of al-Sufyani? And he said that Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) would return after eight months. So they did not recognize his falsehood.

And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from some of our scholars from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubaid from Muhammad ibn Sinan who said: Ali ibn Abi Hamza was mentioned before Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), so he cursed him, then said: 'Ali ibn Abi Hamza wanted that Allah should not be worshipped in His heavens and His earth, but Allah insisted on perfecting His light, even if the polytheists were displeased. And if the accursed polytheist were displeased.' I asked: 'The polytheist?' He replied: 'Yes, by Allah, and even if he grinds his nose [in disdain]. So it is, and it is in the Book of Allah: {They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths}, and it has been established regarding him and those like him that he wanted to extinguish the light of Allah.' {They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths} And it has been established regarding him and those like him that he wanted to extinguish the light of Allah.

This is also invalidated by the miracles that appeared through the hand of Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him), which indicate the validity of his Imamate, and these are mentioned in the books. Because of them, a group returned from the belief of Waqf (stopping), such as Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, Rifa'ah ibn Musa, Yunus ibn Yaqub, Jamil ibn Darraj, Hammad ibn Isa, and others; and these are from the companions of his father who doubted him and then returned. And likewise those who were in his era, such as Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, and others who had said Waqf, they committed to the Proof and said with his Imamate and the Imamate of those after him from his offspring.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who was from the family of Mehran, and they were followers of the Waqifite sect, and he was upon their opinion. He corresponded with Abul Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and posed difficult questions to him. He said: I wrote a letter to him and I harbored in my heart that whenever I entered upon him, I would ask him about three issues from the Quran: His saying, Exalted is He: 'Can you make the deaf to hear or guide the blind?' And His saying: 'So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his breast for Islam.' And His saying: 'Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.' Ahmad said: He answered my letter and wrote at its end the verses that I had harbored in my heart to ask him about, and I had not mentioned them in my letter to him. When the reply arrived, I forgot what I had harbored, so I said: What is this from my reply? Then I remembered that it was what I had harbored.

And likewise, Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, and he was one who held the view of Waqif (stopping). Then he returned (to belief in the Imamate). The cause of his return was that he said: I traveled to Khorasan for my trade. When I arrived, Abul Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent to me asking for a striped cloth. It was among my clothes, but its presence had been hidden from me. I said: I do not have any of it with me. The messenger returned and mentioned its sign and that it was in such-and-such bundle. I searched for it and it was as he said, so I sent it to him. Then I wrote some questions that I wanted to ask him. When I reached his door, he came out to me with the answers to those questions which I intended to ask him, without me having revealed them to him. He returned from the statement of Waqf to the certainty of his Imamate.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: Ibn Najjashi asked: Who is the Imam after your companion? I went to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: The Imam after me is my son? Then he said: Can anyone who does not have a son dare to say: 'My son'?

And Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini who said: When people differed regarding the matter of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), I collected from his questions, those that were asked of him and he answered, fifteen thousand questions.

And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Aftas narrated, saying: I entered upon al-Ma'mun; he drew me close and greeted me, then said: May Allah have mercy on al-Rida (peace be upon him); how knowledgeable he was. He informed me of something wondrous. I asked him one night when the people had already pledged allegiance to him, saying: May I be your ransom, I see it fitting for you to go to Iraq and for me to be your successor in Khorasan. He smiled and said: No, by my life! But before Khorasan, by degrees. We have a stay here, and I will not depart until death comes to me, and from there the Gathering [Place of Resurrection] without doubt. I said to him: May I be your ransom, and how do you know this? He said: My knowledge of my place is like my knowledge of your place. I said: And where is my place, may God rectify you? He said: The distance between me and you is great. I die in the East and you die in the West. I said: You are truthful. And Allah and His Messenger know best, and the Family of Muhammad. Then I exerted all my effort to entice him with the Caliphate and other ranks, but he did not entice me with himself.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Aftas narrated, saying: One day I was with al-Ma'mun, and we were drinking wine until the wine took its effect; he dismissed his companions and kept me behind. Then he brought out his slave girls, they played instruments and sang. He said to one of them: 'Sing for the one who is settled in Tus.' So she began to recite: 'A drink to those settled in Tus, and to one from the progeny of the Chosen One who is there, who has left us grief. I mean Abu al-Hasan [al-Ma'mun], he has a right upon everyone who is sorrowful there.' Muhammad ibn Abdullah said: He began to weep until he made me weep. Then he said to me: 'Woe to you, O Muhammad! Do my household and your household compel me to appoint Abu al-Hasan as a standard [of leadership]? By Allah, if he had not been hastened [to death], I would have seated him in my seat [as successor], but he was hastened. May Allah curse Abdullah and Hamza, the two sons of al-Hasan, for they killed him.' Then he said to me: 'O Muhammad ibn Abdullah, by Allah, I will tell you a strange story, so keep it confidential.' I said: 'What is that, O Commander of the Faithful?' He said: 'When Zahiriyah became pregnant with Badr, I went to him and said to him: 'May I be your ransom, I have received news that Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Ali, and Ali ibn al-Husayn, and al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them) used to cast divination arrows and did not err. You are the heir of the people and you possess the knowledge that was with them. Zahiriyah is my favorite, and I do not prefer any of my slave girls over her. She has been pregnant more than once, but it always miscarried. Do you have anything in this regard that we can benefit from?' He said: 'Do not fear its miscarriage, she will be safe and give birth to a healthy boy, the most resembling of people to his mother. Allah has added two things to his creation: an extra finger in his right hand and an extra finger in his right foot.' I said to myself: 'This is an opportunity, by Allah! If the matter is not as he described, I will remove him.' So I kept waiting for her delivery until labor seized her. I said to the nurse: 'When she gives birth, bring me the child, whether male or female.' I did not feel it but the nurse came to me with the boy as he had described him: extra in hand and foot, like a shining pearl. So

And his story with Hababa al-Walibiyya, the owner of the pebble on which Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) placed his seal, and he said to her: 'One who places a seal on this is an Imam.' And she remained until the days of al-Rida (peace be upon him), and he placed his seal on it, and she witnessed the placing of seals by those of his ancestors who preceded him (peace be upon them), and they placed their seals on it, and he (peace be upon him) was the last of them whom she met, and she died after meeting him, and he shrouded her in his shirt.

And likewise, his story with Umme Ghanim, the Bedouin woman, owner of the pebble, is also well known and famous; in which Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) placed his seal, and after him all the other Imams placed their seals until the time of Abu Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon him).

Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated, saying: Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari narrated to me, saying: I was with Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) at the time of the death of his son, Abu Ja'far, who had been indicated and pointed to by him. And I was reflecting in myself, saying: This is the story of Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and the story of Ismail. So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: Yes, O Abu Hashim. God manifested (Bada) regarding Abu Ja'far and made Abu Ja'far and replaced his place with Abu Muhammad, just as He manifested regarding Ismail after Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had indicated him and appointed him. And it is as your soul told you, although the disbelievers dislike it. Abu Muhammad is my son, the successor after me; with him is what you need and with him is the instrument of Imamate, and praise be to God.

As for the one who said that there is no offspring for Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), but that there is a well-known conception here who will be born: his statement is invalid, because this leads to the time being devoid of an Imam to whom one refers, and we have demonstrated the falsity of that. Furthermore, we will demonstrate that a known son was born to him and we will mention the traditions regarding that, which will also invalidate the saying of these people.

As for the saying that the situation is confusing and it cannot be decided whether Imam Hasan (peace be upon him) sired a son or not, and until the birth of his son is established, we will adhere to the Imamate of Hasan; it is also invalidated through our assertion that no time can be without an Imam, because we know Hasan (peace be upon him) is dead just as we know many other people to be dead, and we will prove the birth of his son as well, so their claim is also falsified.

As for the one who said that there is no Imam after Hasan (peace be upon him), his statement is invalid due to what we have proven regarding the fact that time is never devoid of a proof of God, rationally and legally. And as for the one who said that Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) died and will live after his death, his statement is invalid by the same reasoning, because it leads to the creation being devoid of an Imam from the time of his death until Allah brings him back to life.

Their argument based on what has been narrated that the Master of this Affair will live after he dies and that he was named Qaim because he will rise after he dies, is invalid, because that, if the report were reliable, could be interpreted to mean that he will rise after his name dies, so that no one mentions him except those who believe in his Imamate, and then Allah will manifest him to all the creation. Besides, we have established that every Imam who stands in place of the previous Imam is called the Qaim.

If it is said: We object to your statement regarding his Imamate on the basis of his occultation, We say: If you cannot describe the wisdom of his disappearance, it indicates invalidity of your belief in his Imamate, because if it were valid, you should be able to describe the wisdom of the occultation.

We said: If this conclusion were to be inferred from us, it would also be inferred from all the followers of justice by the view of the atheists, when they say, 'We reach the conclusion that its Doer is not wise through these actions which are not apparent in wisdom,' because if He were wise, you would have been able to explain the aspect of wisdom in them; otherwise, what is the distinction?

If you say: 'We first inquire into proving His wisdom,' once it is proved through independent proofs, we interpret the acts that are hard to explain on the basis of His wisdom, which has already been proved. Therefore, it does not lead to any contradiction of what we already know. And if they do not accept His wisdom for us, the discussion will transfer to proving Divine wisdom.

We said: The same applies here, that the discussion regarding his occultation is derived from his Imamate. So when we know his Imamate through a proof, and we know his infallibility through another proof, and we know that he is absent, we interpret his occultation in a manner that is consistent with his infallibility; therefore, there is no difference between the two cases.

Then the opponent of occultation is asked, 'Is it possible that the occultation may have a valid reason that has caused it and a wise explanation that has prompted it or it is not possible?' If he should say, 'It is possible,' he will be told, 'Then why does occultation lead you to conclude the non-existence of the Imam in this time despite considering it possible that it may have a reason not incompatible with the existence of Imam?' Is it not like the argument of a person, who negates the wisdom of the Creator on the basis of pains and diseases of children, notwithstanding his acknowledgement that their pains and diseases may have a valid explanation that does not violate divine wisdom?' Or the argument of a person who argues on the basis of the superficialities of 'ambiguous verses' that the Almighty is similar to physical bodies and creates the actions of people, despite his profession that these verses may have valid interpretations that do not violate the principles of wisdom, Divine justice, monotheism and negation of His physicality.'

And when it is said: 'We are capable of mentioning the aspects of the ambiguous verses, but you are unable to mention a valid reason for the occultation,' we say: Our discourse is directed at the one who says 'I do not need to know the detailed aspects of the ambiguous verses, but that a general understanding suffices for me.' If you undertake that, it is out of your own volition. And if you are satisfied with that for yourselves, then we too are capable of mentioning the validity of the occultation and a wise purpose that does not contradict his infallibility. We will mention that later, and we have discussed it comprehensively in the book of Imamate.

Then it is said: How can the validity of the Imamate of Ibn al-Hasan (peace be upon him), based on the rational principles we established, coexist with the claim that the Occultation cannot have a valid reason? Is this not a contradiction? Does it not run parallel to affirming Monotheism and Divine Justice while asserting that the ambiguous verses cannot have an interpretation that conforms to these principles?

If they say, 'We do not accept the Imamate of Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him),' then our discourse with them is with respect to proving the Imamate, not the reason for the occultation. And the proofs of his Imamate (peace be upon him) have preceded in a manner that does not require repetition. We said this because the discourse on the reason for the Imam's occultation (peace be upon him) is secondary to the proof of his Imamate, but before its proof, there is no basis for discourse on the reason for his occultation, just as there is no basis for discourse on the interpretations of the ambiguous verses, the pains of children, and the excellence of ritual worship by the laws before the proof of Divine Unity and Justice.

If it is said: Does the inquisitor not have the choice between speaking about the Imamate of Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him) to know its validity or invalidity, and speaking about the reason for the occultation?

We said: There is no choice in that, because a person who doubts the Imamate of Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him) must have discourse with him regarding the explicit narration of his Imamate and be occupied with providing proofs for it. It is not permissible, while doubting it, to speak about the reason for the occultation, because discourse on the offshoots is not valid except after the fundamentals are established for them, just as it is not permissible to speak about the reason for the harm to children before the wisdom of the Ancient One (God) is established and that He does not do the ugly. We preferred discourse on his Imamate (peace be upon him) over discourse on his occultation and its reason, because discourse on his Imamate is based on intellectual matters that do not admit doubt.

Therefore, to discuss the clear and the manifest is worthier than to discuss the perplexing and the complicated. This is parallel to our dialogue with the opponents of religion, where we give preference to the discussion of the prophethood of our Messenger over discussing their claim that their religion has come for eternity. Because the former is clear and manifest and the latter is complex. This criterion is identically present here. If they should argue back that there is a certain evil aspect involved in occultation, this has already been answered that aspects of evil are conceivable, such as that occultation is an act of oppression, lie, vanity, ignorance, or that it leads to mischief. And none of these are involved in the occultation of the Imam. Therefore, it should not be claimed that there is an evil aspect involved in it.

If it is said: Why does not Allah bar the people from reaching the Imam and why does not He protect him in a way so he may establish his rule and our grace is materialized for us? Just as we say about the Prophet when Allah sent him, He protected him until he had delivered the Shariah, it would be necessary that the Imam’s case be the same.

We said: Protection (al-Mana') is of two kinds: one is not incompatible with religious duty, as it does not compel the subject to forsake the wrong; and the other leads to such compulsion. The first kind Allah has enacted, by preventing oppression against him through forbidding it, encouraging the obligation of obedience to him, compliance with his command and prohibition, that he not be disobeyed in any of his commands, and that he be helped in all that strengthens his authority and consolidates his power. Indeed, all of this is not incompatible with duty. So if someone disobeys in this regard and does not do what is required for the desired objective to be realized, he has acted on his own, not from his Creator. The other kind is that He literally separates them from him by force and renders them incapable of oppressing and disobeying him. Therefore, this is not compatible with religious duty, which requires free choice, and thus, religious obligations must be annulled.

As for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), we say that God must protect him so that he may deliver the religious laws, because it is not possible to know that except through him; therefore, protection from him is obligatory. The Imam is not like him, because the excuse of the obligated ones is removed regarding the religious laws, and the proofs are established for what they need, and they have a way to know them without his words, and if we suppose that the situation reaches a point where the truth among the religious duties is not known except through his words, then it would be necessary for God Almighty to protect him and manifest him in such a way that no harm can reach him, as in the case of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). The like of the case of the Imam is that when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) has delivered [the message] and then what follows presents something that causes fear, it is not necessary for God to protect him from being prevented, because the excuse of the obligated ones has been removed by what he delivered to them, so they have a way to know His grace. Unless there is another delivery attached to him in the future, then protection from him is obligatory as it was obligatory at the beginning; thus we have equated the matter between the Prophet and the Imam.

If it is said: Explain to us, in any case, even if it is not obligatory upon you, the aspect of the reason for the occultation, and what can be a reason in a way that it becomes clearer in the argument and more convincing in the realm of demonstration.

We said: That which one can be certain of to be the reason for the occultation of the Imam is his fear for his life by murder, due to the oppressors threatening him and preventing him from administering the affairs he is responsible to direct and manage. If he is prevented from achieving his objective, the duty of assuming the Imamate falls away.
