And if he fears for his life, his occultation becomes obligatory and his hiding becomes necessary, just as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) once hid in the valley and another time in the cave, and there is no reason for this except the fear of harm reaching him. And no one can say that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) only hid from his people after he had delivered what was obligatory for him to deliver and they no longer had any need of him, whereas your statement regarding the Imam is contrary to that. Furthermore, the hiding of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was not prolonged nor did it last long, whereas the hiding of the Imam has seen ages pass and eras vanish.

We said: Fear from their enemies did not threaten his holy forefathers (a.s), as they adhered to dissimulation (taqiyyah) and ostensibly retracted from the claim of Imamate and exiled it from themselves, whereas, the Imam of the Age faces every fear, because he is the one to rise with the sword and raise the call for his leadership and fight his adversaries. Where is the similarity between his fear from his enemies and the fear of his forefathers, if there is no scarcity of reflection? Moreover, when anyone of his forefathers (a.s) was murdered or died, there was someone qualified for Imamate from their progeny to replace him and fill his position, whereas the case of the Master of the Age is diametrically opposite to this, since it is well-known that no one is to succeed him and take his position. Therefore, the difference between the two instances is clear.

We have also previously elucidated the difference between the instance that he exists in hiding where no one or few can reach him and the instance of his non-existence until his capacity of governance is known and then God creates him.

Likewise is their objection: What is the difference between his existence in a way that no one can reach him and his existence in the heavens? Because we shall say that if he exists in the heavens in a way that the conditions of dwellers of the earth do not remain concealed from him, the heaven is like the earth in such a case, and if they do remain concealed, such an existence equals his non-existence. Then the argument is turned around against them about the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) by asking: “What is the difference between the prophetic existence in hiding and his non-existence and his being in the heaven?” Whatever answer they will give to this question is our very answer to them to their question, as we elaborated earlier. They cannot make a distinction between the two cases, saying that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not hide from everyone and merely hid from his enemies and the Imam of the Age is hiding from everyone.

We said: The rightful punishments remain in the account of those who deserve them, if the Imam appears and those who deserve them are still alive, he will enforce them against them based on testimony or confession; and if this was missed because they died, then the sin of failing to enforce them rests on those who threatened the Imam and forced him into occultation. And this is not abrogation of the enforcement of punishments, because a penal code has to be upheld only when there is power and capacity for upholding it and when there is no encumbrance; its enforcement is not binding if there is an encumbrance. Abrogation is involved when a code is not enforced even when there is power and capacity to enforce it and there is no encumbrance.

Such people are asked, “What do you say about the state in which ‘those having a say’ (ahl hal wa aqd) are not able to select an Imam? What is the case of the penalties?” If you say they are not binding, this is abrogation on the same merits you accused us of; and if you say penalties remain enforceable with respect to their deservers; this is our very answer as well.

If it is said: Abu Ali has argued that in the conditions in which 'those having a say' are not able to select an Imam, Allah performs acts that stand in place of enforcing the penalties and take away the excuse of duty-bound; and Abu Hashim has said that enforcing penalties is a worldly matter and has no relationship with religion.

We say: As for what Abu Ali said, if we were to say the same, it would not harm us. Because the enforcement of penal codes is not the reason for which we consider the existence of the Imam necessary, so when they are not enforced, it could lead to the untenability of the proofs of Imamate. Enforcing penal codes is a religio-legal matter, and we said that it is possible that the obligation of its enforcement lose its imperativeness when the Imam lacks power, or that it may remain pending in the accounts of the criminals. It is also possible that Allah performs acts that replace enforcement of penal codes. If we were to accept Abu Ali’s assertion, it would not harm our stance at all.

As for what Abu Hashim said, that it is for worldly benefits, it is far-fetched, because it is an obligatory act of worship, and if it were for a worldly benefit, it would not be obligatory. Besides, enforcing the penalties in his view, in the manner of requital and legal punishment, is part of Divine punishment, and some of it has been brought forward in this life for the benefit it contains. So how can he say, despite that, that it is for worldly benefits? Therefore, what they said is invalid.
A section on discourse regarding the Occultation: Know that we have two paths in discussing the occultation of the Master of the Age (peace be upon him).

One is that we say: Since it is established that the necessity of Imamate is in every state, and that the creation, being fallible, cannot be without a leader at any time, and that a condition of the leader is that he be ascertained to be infallible, then that leader is either manifest and known, or hidden and concealed, when we know that everyone who claims for him a manifest Imamate is not ascertained to be infallible, rather the outward appearance of their actions and states contradicts infallibility, we know that he who is ascertained to be infallible is hidden and concealed. and when we know that everyone who claims for him infallibility absolutely, who is hidden, such as the Kaisaniyya, Nawusiyya, Fatihiyya, Waqifiyya and others, their claim is false, we know by this the validity of the Imamate of the son of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and the validity of his occultation and guardianship, and we do not need to exert in speech regarding the proof of his birth, and the reason for his occultation, given the establishment of what we mentioned, because the truth cannot be absent from the community.

The second mode of our argument is thus: The inquiry of occultation of the son of Imam Hasan (peace be upon him) is secondary to proving his Imamate, Our adversary either submits to us in the question of his Imamate and inquires about the reason of his occultation, obliging us to answer him or he does not submit to us, in which case, to inquire about the reason of occultation of someone, whose Imamate is not proved, will be meaningless. If disputed about his Imamate, we prove it as follows: The necessity of Imamate in every condition and age as long as Divine obligations and duties fall on the shoulders of the fallible human beings is proved through strong proofs. It is likewise proved that one of the conditions of the Imam is to be certain of his infallibility. At the same time, it is clear that truth is exclusive to this Ummah. With these premises proved, we find that the Ummah is divided into sects that follow different beliefs. One group says that there is no Imam. The premise asserting the necessity of Imam in every age and condition invalidates this statement.

Another group claims the Imamate of one whose infallibility is not certain is an assertion invalidated by our proofs with regard to the necessity of certainty about infallibility of the Imam. Observation testifies contrary to the contention of others, who maintain the infallibility of their supposed Imams; because their actions are apparent and their conditions violate infallibility, hence there is no need to disprove a belief, the contrary of which is so very evident and clear. Persons for whom infallibility was claimed and certain groups followed them, such as the Kaisaniyya, who believe in the Imamate of Muhammad Ibne Hanafiyyah, the Nawusiyya, who believe in the Imamate of Ja’far Ibne Muhammad and also believe that he is not dead, and the Waqifa, who believe that Musa Ibne Ja’far is not dead – all these beliefs are invalid for reasons we will shortly mention.

Thus, both paths depend on the invalidation of the beliefs of these groups in order that our purpose is established, and they require the establishment of the three principles we mentioned: the necessity of leadership (Imamate), the necessity of certainty regarding political authority), the necessity of certainty regarding infallibility, and that the truth does not depart from the Ummah. We provide evidence for each of these statements with a concise argument, as their full elaboration exists in our book on Imamate to an extent that cannot be exceeded. The purpose of this book is specifically to address the occultation and nothing else, and Allah is the One who grants success in this through His grace.

If it is said: What is the way of finding the truth during the occultation of the Imam? If you say that there is no way, you have led people to confusion, misguidance and doubt in all their affairs; and if you say that the truth is found through its proofs, you will be told that this is a clear admission of lack of need of the Imam through these proofs.

We said: The truth is of two types: intellectual and narrated. The intellectual is attained through its proofs, and the narrated has established proofs upon it, which comprise the sayings of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and his texts, and the sayings of the Imams (peace be upon them) from his progeny. They have explained that and clarified it, and left nothing from it without a proof.

However, this is as we have said, we have proven the necessity of the Imam, because the aspect of need for him, which is continuous in every state and time, is that he is a grace for us, as discussed earlier, and no one else can take his place. The need related to narration (hearing/transmission) is also clear, because although the narration comes from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the forefathers of the Imam (peace be upon them) regarding all that is needed in the jurisprudence, it is possible for the reliable narrators to deviate from it, either intentionally or due to a doubt, so the narration may become disconnected or remain through someone who is not reliable in his narration. We have fully discussed this method in *Talkhis al-Shafi*, so we will not prolong by mentioning it in the book.

If it is said: Suppose that the narrators concealed some of the Shariah from one another, and there was a need for the explanation of the Imam, and the truth was not known except through him, and the fear of being killed by his enemies continued, what would be the situation?

If you say that he will appear despite his fear for his life, it follows that his fear for his life does not warrant his occultation in the first place, and thus, he must appear. If you say that he will not appear and the duties that have not reached the Ummah are not binding, it is an assertion against consensus (Ijma), which says that everything the Prophet (s) has introduced in his Shariah and has explained it, is imperative and binding on the Ummah until Judgment Day. If you say that the duty is still binding, you are suggesting a duty that is beyond our capacity and an obligation to perform a task, which we do not know.

They have said that there is no purpose in his clandestine appearance to some of his devotees, because the expected benefit of leading the Ummah cannot be fulfilled, but through his appearance and exertion of leadership for all. Therefore, the reason for the Imam’s hiding in the way in which it is grace and prudent for all is the same.

It is possible to question this answer by saying: Although the enemies prevented him from appearing in a manner of general leadership and administration, they did not prevent him from meeting whomever he wished of his specific devotees, who believe in his obedience and are obliged to follow his orders, If there is no benefit in this meeting due to its specificity, because he is not the one whose command is binding for everyone, this is a clear statement that the Imami Shia derived no benefit from meeting their Imams from the death of Amir al-Mu'minin until the days of Hasan ibn Ali, Abu al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), for this reason. It also necessitates that the devotees of Amir al-Mu'minin and his Shia did not benefit from meeting him before the matter of leadership passed to his administration and was in his hand. This is a high level of reasoning reached by the speaker, which a thoughtful person would not reach. Moreover, if it is conceded that benefiting from the Imam occurs only when he is apparent to all subjects and his command is executed among them, their view is invalidated from another aspect, namely, it leads to the abrogation of the religious obligations for which the Imam is a grace, from his Shia. Because if he does not appear to them due to a reason that does not revert to them and is not in their power or ability to remove, then the obligations must be lifted from them. Because if it is permissible that a group of the obligated prevents another from their grace, and the obligation for which that grace is a grace remains binding on them, then it is permissible that one obligated person prevents another through imprisonment or similar means which he cannot remove, and the obligation of walking remains binding on him in reality.

And it is not for them to distinguish between the restriction (al-qayd) and the grace (al-lutf), in that the restriction makes the action impossible and its occurrence is not presumed, whereas it is not so with the absence of grace, because most of the people of justice hold that the absence of grace is like the absence of power and means, and that the duty (taklif) with the absence of grace, for one who has a known grace, is like the duty with the absence of power and means and the presence of obstacles, and that one for whom the grace is not given, from among those who have a known grace, is not removing the cause of the duty, just as the prevented one is not removing the cause.

The appropriate answer to this question, which we mentioned on behalf of the opponent, is to say that first, we don’t believe in his occultation from all his devotees. Rather, it is possible that he appears to most of them. Everyone can only know his own condition. If the Imam appears to him, his excuse not to comply with religious duties ends; and if he does not appear to him, he discerns that the non-appearance is because of himself though he may not know specifically why; due to his own shortcoming, otherwise, binding him with religious duties would be wrong.

When he knows that the obligation of religious duties remains upon him and that the Imam is in occultation from him, he discerns that it is because of a matter that refers back to himself, as our group says regarding one who did not contemplate the path to the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, and thus did not attain knowledge: it becomes obligatory for him to be certain that he did not attain it due to a shortcoming that refers back to himself; otherwise, it would be obligatory to remove the obligation from him, even if he does not know in what specific matter his shortcoming occurred.

Based on this report, the strongest reasoning for that is: if the Imam appears and his specific person is not known by way of observation, it is necessary that a miraculous knowledge appears from him indicating his truthfulness; and knowing that something is a miracle requires reflection, in which doubts may be raised; so it is not impossible that it be known from the condition of one to whom he has not appeared that when he appears and shows him the miracle, he may not reflect well, and a doubt enters him regarding it, so he believes that he is a liar, and spreads his news, leading to the harm mentioned earlier.

If it is said: What fault occurs from the devotee to whom the Imam has not appeared due to this known state of his, and what ability does he have to reflect on what will appear for him with the Imam, and to what does he refer to compensate for what necessitates his occultation?

We said: The reason for our being excused in the matter of the occultation from the devotees is only a known fact, where the shortcoming in it becomes apparent and its recompense is possible, because it is not impossible that it should be known from his condition that when the Imam appears to him, he will fall short in observing the miracle, for he will have done so due to the shortcoming inherent in his knowledge of the difference between the miracle and the possible, and the proof from this is the doubt, and if it were upon a correct principle, it would not be permissible for the Imam's miracle to be confused for him when it appears to him, so he must recompense this shortcoming and make up for it.

No one can say that this is a duty beyond capacity and reliance on an unknown event in the future, because this devotee does not know his specific shortcoming in contemplation and reasoning, so he could make up for it and prepare himself for it; we believe you are binding him to something that does not legitimately bind him. That can be the case with regard to a religious duty that is sometimes clear and sometimes confusing with some other duty; and if the capacity with respect to both duties exists, then when the devotee introspects and sees that the Imam does not appear to him and he does not consider the aforementioned wrong reasons of the occultation valid, he realizes that the reason of the occultation is indebted to himself; and when he realizes that the strongest proof is what we mentioned, he discerns that the shortcoming is his own with respect to the miraculous signs and their conditions. Therefore, he must reflect on it and get rid of doubts and anything causing confusion. Whoever toils in this regard and reflects well, will definitely discover the difference between right and wrong. Man is knowledgeable of himself on occasions as this. It is not possible to do anything beyond, to go to extremes in investigation and research and to find and submit to truth. We mentioned that this case is similar to what we say to our opponents when they see our proofs and do not attain satisfaction.

If it is said: If the matter is as you have stated, it would be necessary that he does not know any of the miracles in this condition, and this leads to not knowing prophethood and the veracity of the Messenger, which further takes him out of Islam, let alone faith.

We said: That does not follow because it is not impossible to be subject to doubts in certain miracles and not all of them. It is not necessary that if doubts arise with respect to some miracles, they do with respect to all of them. Therefore, it is possible that the miracle indicating Prophethood should not be subject to doubt and thus he attains certitude that it is a miracle and realizes the Prophethood of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the miracle that appears on the hands of the Imam be another matter, in which he could have doubts, and thus, he finds doubts in his Imamate, even if he is a believer in Prophethood.

This is as we say. If someone who knows the prophethood of Musa (peace be upon him) through the miracles indicating his prophethood, does not properly reflect on the miracles apparent on Isa (peace be upon him) and our Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), it is not necessary to conclude that he did not know those miracles, because it is not impossible that he is aware of them and the manner of their indication, even if he does not know these miracles and the manner of their indication has been unclear to him.

If it should be said: According to this, everyone to whom the Imam has not appeared should be certain that he is committing a major sin, which is an extension of disbelief (Kufr), because he is guilty, according to what you have presumed him to be, with respect to the occultation of the Imam and his loss of what is beneficial for him; this makes the devotee of the Imam his enemy.

We said: It is not necessary that the shortcoming to which we referred be disbelief or a great sin. Because in this state he believed that the Imam is not [the] Imam, nor did he fear for his life; he merely fell short in some sciences, a shortcoming that was like a cause for that doubt in the Imamate to occur from him in the future, and now it has not occurred, so it is not necessary that he be a disbeliever. And although it does not necessitate that he be a disbeliever, nor follow the course of denying the Imam and doubting his truthfulness, it is a sin and a mistake that do not negate faith and entitlement to reward. And the devotee would not be joined with the enemy in this case, because the enemy holds an opinion about the Imam that is disbelief and a major sin, while the devotee is the opposite of that. We said: That which is 'like a cause' for disbelief is not necessarily disbelief at this stage, because if one of us believes that he is an independent cause with respect to other objects, it will be ignorance and mistake, but not disbelief.

And when we said that what is like a cause for disbelief does not necessarily be disbelief in the moment, if one believed in the Capable among us regarding a power that it is valid for Him to do a new act in other bodies, that would be an error and ignorance, not disbelief, and it is not impossible that it is known from the state of this believer that if a prophet appeared calling to his prophethood and made a miracle that Allah Almighty would perform through his hand an act such that the causes of humans do not reach it, that he would not accept it, and this inevitably if he knew it were a miracle he would have accepted it, and what preceded of his belief in the capability of the Capable was like a cause for this, and it did not necessitate that it follows its course in disbelief.

If it is said: This answer too does not remain upon your principle, because the correct view in your school is that whoever knows Allah the Exalted by His attributes, and knows Prophethood and Imamate, and becomes a believer, it is not permissible for disbelief to occur from him at all. So if this is established, how can you make the reason for the hiding from the Wali that it is known from his state that when the Imam appears, and miracles appear by his hand, doubt will be cast upon them, and he will not recognize him as an Imam. And doubt in that is disbelief, and that refutes the principle which you have validated.

It was said: What you have mentioned is not correct, because doubt regarding the miracle that appears on the hand of the Imam is not a defect in knowing him for the general public in a general sense. Rather, it is a defect in whether what is generally known and whose knowledge is valid is this specific person or not. And doubt in this is not disbelief, because if it were disbelief, it would be disbelief even if the miracle does not appear, for surely before the appearance of this miracle in his hand, there is one who doubts about him, and it is permissible for him to be the Imam and for another to be so as well. Rather, the defect in the knowledge obtained by him in a general sense is if he doubts in the future regarding his Imamate in a general sense, and that is what prevents it from occurring from him in the future.

90 - That which informed me was Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Abdun, known as Ibn al-Hashir, who said: Narrated to me Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shuja'i the scribe, who said: Informed us Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, known as Ibn Abu Zainab al-Nu'mani the scribe, who said: Informed us Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Allan al-Dhahabi al-Baghdadi in Damascus, who said: Narrated to us Abu Bakr ibn Abu Khaithama, who said: Narrated to me Ali ibn al-Ja'd, who said: Narrated to me Zuhair ibn Mu'awiya from Ziyad ibn Khaithama from al-Aswad ibn Saeed al-Hamdani, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samra say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: After me, there will be twelve Caliphs, all of them from Quraish. He said: When he returned to his house, Quraish came to him and said: Then what will happen? He replied: Then there will be confusion (al-Harj).

And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad bin Uthman, he said: Ibn Abi Khaithama narrated to me, saying: Zuhair bin Muawiyah narrated to me from Ziyad bin Alaqa, Samak bin Harb, and Husain bin Abdur Rahman, all of them from Jabir bin Samra, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: After me, there will be twelve Caliphs. Then he spoke some words which I did not understand. One of them said: I asked the people [about what he said], and they replied: He said: All of them are from Quraish.

And with this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Ibn Awad from Al-Sha'bi from Jabir ibn Samra, who said: It was mentioned that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people of this religion will continue to be victorious over those who oppose them until there are twelve Caliphs.' People were standing and sitting (in restlessness), and he spoke a word that I did not understand, so I asked my father - or my brother: 'What did he say?' He replied: 'He said: All of them are from Quraish.'

And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Ahmad, he said: Narrated to us Ubaidullah ibn Umar, he said: Narrated to us Sulayman ibn Ahmar, he said: Narrated to us Ibn Aun, from Al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samra, who said: It was mentioned that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people of this religion will continue to be victorious over those who oppose them until there are twelve Caliphs.' So the people were standing and sitting, and he spoke a word that I did not understand, so I asked my father—or my brother: 'What did he say?' He replied: 'They are all from Quraish.'

And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Ahmad ibn Abi Khaithama, he said: Narrated to us Yahya ibn Ma'in, he said: Narrated to us Abdullah ibn Salih, he said: Narrated to us Al-Layth ibn Sa'd from Khalid ibn Yazid from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal from Rabi'ah ibn Saif, he said: We were with Shafi Al-Asbahi, and he said: I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: After me, there will be twelve Caliphs.

And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Ahmad, who said: Narrated to us Affan and Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Sailhani, who said: Narrated to us Hammad ibn Salama, who said: Narrated to us Abdullah ibn Uthman from Abi Tufayl, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar said to me: Then there will be the Naqf and the Naqaf.

And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Ahmad, he said: Narrated to us Al-Muqaddami from Asim ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Miqdam, Abu Yunus, he said: Narrated to me my father from Fitr ibn Khalifa from Abu Khalid Al-Walibi, he said: Narrated to us Jabir ibn Samra, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: This religion will remain victorious; those who oppose it will not be able to harm it, until twelve Caliphs arise, all of whom are from Quraish.

And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Raqqi, he said: Narrated to us Isa ibn Yunus from Mujalid ibn Saeed from al-Sha'bi from Masruq, who said: We were with Ibn Mas'ud when a man asked him: Did your Prophet inform you how many successors would be after him? He said: Yes. And no one else asked me about it before you, and indeed you are the youngest of the people in age. I heard him say: After me, there will be as many caliphs as there were chiefs of Musa (peace be upon him). Allah, the Mighty and High, said: '...and We raised up among them twelve chieftains...'

And a group informed me from Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa al-Tal'kabari, who said: Informed me Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ali, known as Ibn al-Khadib al-Razi, who said: Narrated to me some of our companions from Hanzala ibn Zakariya al-Tamimi, from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Tusi, from Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Abi Shaibah, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended with a scroll from Allah to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), in which were twelve seals of gold. He said to him: 'Surely, Allah the Exalted sends you greetings and commands you to deliver this scroll to the noble one from your family after you. He will break the first seal and act according to what is in it. When he passes away, he will deliver it to his successor after him. Thus, the first will deliver it to the last, one after another.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did as he was ordered. Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) broke the first one and acted according to what was in it, then delivered it to al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who broke his seal and acted according to what was in it. He delivered it after him to al-Husayn (peace be upon him), then al-Husayn delivered it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and so on, one after another, until it reaches the last of them (peace be upon them all).

And with this chain of narrators, from al-Tala'kbari, from Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Himam, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Quhistani, from Zaid ibn Ishaq, from his father, who said: I asked Isa ibn Musa, and I said to him: 'Who of the Tabi'un did you meet?' He replied: 'I do not know what you are saying. But I was in Kufa, and I heard an old man in its mosque narrating from Abdul Khair, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'O Ali! The rightly guided, the guided, the Imams whose rights are usurped from your progeny are eleven Imams, and you…' And the hadith is abbreviated.

And a group narrated to me from Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa al-Talakbari, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Hashimi who said: Narrated to me Abu Musa Isa ibn Ahmad ibn Isa ibn al-Mansur who said: Narrated to me Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari from his father Muhammad ibn Ali from his father Ali ibn Musa from his father Musa ibn Ja'far from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father Muhammad ibn Ali from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him and his family) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said to me: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever desires to meet Allah, Mighty and Glorified be He, in a state of safety and purity, and that the Great Fear should not terrify him, let him befriend you and let your sons befriend him: al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja'far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, and then al-Mahdi, who is their seal. And there will surely be in the last era a group who will befriend you, O Ali. People will hate them. And if they loved them, it would be better for them, if they but knew. They will give preference to you and your sons over their fathers and mothers, brothers and sisters, and over their clans and relatives. May the prayers of Allah be upon them, the best of prayers. Those people will be gathered beneath the Standard of Praise, their sins will be overlooked and their grades will be raised as a reward for what they used to do.

We mention a portion of the narrations that encompass this meaning, so that the truth of what we have said may be known, because the complete inclusion of all that has been narrated in this regard would be lengthy, and it is present in the books of traditions; whoever wishes may refer to it from there.

Of that, a group informed us from Abu Muhammad al-Talakbari from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi from Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Musa ibn Umar ibn Yazid from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Say: Have you considered if your water should go down, who is it then that will bring you flowing water?' He said: It was revealed concerning the Imam. He said: If your Imam becomes hidden from you, who will bring you an apparent Imam who will bring you the news of the heavens and the earth and the halal and haram of Allah, the Exalted? Then he said: By Allah, the interpretation of this verse has not yet come, and it is necessary that its interpretation will come.

Saad ibn Abdullah from Husayn ibn Amr ibn Yazid from Abi al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' al-Madani from Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Usayd ibn Thalaba from Umm Hani who said: I met Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'So I swear by the stars that hide (and) the ships that sail.' He replied: An Imam who will go into hiding in his time when those who know him disappear from the people, in the year two hundred and sixty, then he will appear like a blazing meteor. If you live to see that, your eye will be comforted.

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn Qasim al-Bajali and Abu Qatada Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hafth, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him: "What is the interpretation of the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Say: Have you considered if your water should go down, who is it then that will bring you flowing water?'" He said: "When you lose your Imam and do not see him, what will you do?"

And a group informed me from Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah from al-Fadl ibn al-Shadhan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a disappearance reaches you regarding your Master, do not reject it.'

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi from Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik from Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna al-Attar from Abdullah ibn Bukair from Ubayd ibn Zurarah said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'The people will lose their Imam, so he will attend the pilgrimage season; he will see them, but they will not see him.'

Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdullah ibn al-Mustanir from al-Munjaliq ibn Umar said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, for the Master of this Matter there are two occultations; one of them is long, until some say: He has died! And some say: He has been killed! And some say: He has gone! Until only a few of his companions remain upon his matter. None of his offspring or others will be informed of his location, except the Servant who manages his affairs.

And through this chain, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Nisaburi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The master of this matter must have seclusion, and in his seclusion there must be strength, and he is not lonely among thirty, and how good an abode is Tayba.

Saad ibn Abdullah from Hasan ibn Ali al-Zaituni from al-Zuhri al-Kufi from Banan ibn Hamdawayh said: The passing away of my father Ja'far (peace be upon him) was mentioned before Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him). He said: 'That is so long as I am alive and remaining. However, how would it be like when they miss the one after me?'

And Ibn Abi Ja'id al-Qummi informed us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Abdullah ibn Hamduya ibn al-Bara' from Thabit from Ismail from Abdul Alaa, slave of the family of Sam, who said: I traveled with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and when we arrived at al-Rawha', he looked at its mountain, gazing upon it, and said to me: 'Do you see this mountain? This is a mountain called Radwa, from the mountains of Fars. It loved us, so Allah transferred it to us. Indeed, every tree on it is edible, and it is a good refuge for the fearful, twice. Indeed, the Master of this Affair will have two occultations in it; one is short and the other is long.'

Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: When Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) entered Kufa and looked at it, he mentioned the tribulations that would befall it, until he mentioned the rule of Bani Umayyah and those who came after them. Then he said: 'When that occurs, remain in the sitting areas of your houses until the Pure One, son of the Pure, the Purifier, the one with occultation, the Wandering Exile, appears.'
Abu Basir narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: There is a similarity with Yusuf in the Qaim. I asked, 'And what is that?' He said, 'Perplexity and disappearance.'

And a group informed me from Abul Mufaddal from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari from his father from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Musa ibn Sadan from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of Jabir, He said: Do not narrate it to the common people (or those of low status) lest they publicize it. Do you not read the Book of Allah, the Exalted: 'For when the trumpet is sounded'? For when the trumpet is sounded Indeed, among us is an Imam in occultation, and when Allah wills to manifest His affair, He will inspire a stroke/inspiration in his heart, so he will appear and rise to carry out the command of Allah, the Exalted.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Kufi narrated from Mundhir ibn Muhammad ibn Qabus from Nasr ibn al-Sindi from Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Sufyan al-Mustariq from Thalaba ibn Maimun from Malik al-Juhani from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah; and Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Thalaba ibn Maimun from Malik al-Juhani from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said: I came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and found him thoughtful, drawing lines in the earth. I said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, why do I see you thoughtful, drawing lines in the earth? Is it out of desire for it?' He said: 'No, by Allah, I have never desired it, nor the world at all. But I was contemplating the offspring who will be born from the back of the eleventh of my sons; he is the Mahdi, who will fill it with justice and equity, as it was filled with oppression and tyranny. There will be for him a perplexity and an occultation, in which some people will go astray and others will be guided.' I said: 'O my master, how long will this perplexity and occultation be?' He said: 'Six days, or six months, or six years.' I said: 'And will this matter indeed come to pass?' He said: 'Yes, just as he is created.' 'And how do you know this, O Asbagh? They are the best of this Ummah, along with the righteous of this Household.' I said: 'Then what will happen after that?' He said: 'Then Allah will do what He wills, for He has beginnings, wills, ends, and terminations.'

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Isa al-Alawi, who said: My father, Isa ibn Muhammad, narrated to me from his father, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, from his father, Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said to me: He said to me: 'O my son, when the fifth descendant of the seventh of the Imams is lost, then by Allah, by Allah, be cautious about your faith, for there must be an occultation for the Master of this Command, during which many who believed in this matter will turn away from it. O my son, it is merely a trial from Allah by which He tests His creation. If your fathers and grandfathers had known a creed more sound than this creed, they would have followed it.' Abu al-Hasan said: 'So I said to him: O my master, who is the fifth descendant of the seventh?' He said: 'O my son, your intellects are too small to comprehend this and your dreams are too narrow to bear it, but if you live, you will attain it.'

Of the proofs of the Imamate of Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him), in addition to what has been mentioned so far, is that there is no dispute between the Ummah that a Mahdi will rise in this Ummah, who would fill the earth with justice and equity as it shall be fraught with oppression and inequity. When we have established that the Mahdi is from the progeny of Husain (peace be upon him) and have invalidated any claimant for this position other than Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him), it is proved that he is the one intended by these narrations.

Ibrahim ibn Salma narrated from Ahmad ibn Malik al-Fazari from Haydar ibn Muhammad al-Fazari from Abbad ibn Yaqub from Nasr ibn Muzahim from Muhammad ibn Marwan from al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “And in the heaven is your sustenance and what you are threatened with…” He said: “It is the emergence of the Mahdi (peace be upon him).”

And by this chain of narration, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: <q>Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death</q> It means He will restore the earth through the Qa'im (Riser) of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after its death. Meaning after the tyranny/corruption of the people of its kingdom. <q>Indeed, We have clarified the verses for you</q> refers to the Qa'im of the Family of Muhammad, <q>so that you may understand</q>.

And Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed us from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah al-Nishapuri from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Nishapuri from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Muthanna al-Hannat from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) say: 'The Qaim (the Rising One) will not rise until a caller from the sky calls, and the girl in her chamber will hear it, and the people of the East and the West will hear it.' And regarding this, this verse was revealed: 'If We please, We should send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks should stoop to it.'

And a group informed me from Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa al-Talakbari from Abu Ali al-Razi from Ibn Abi Daram from Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Sandi al-Maqani from Muhammad ibn Hashim al-Qaisi from Sahl ibn Tamam al-Basri from Imran al-Qattan from Qatada from Abu Nadra from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Mahdi will emerge in the last period of time.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Maqri narrated from al-Maqani'i, from Bakkar ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from al-Ma'la ibn Ziyad, from al-Ala' ibn Bashir al-Muradi, from Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Give glad tidings of the Mahdi; he will be raised among my ummah amidst the discord and upheaval of the people. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it was filled with injustice and oppression. The inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth will be pleased with him.

From him, from Al-Muqani'i, from Bakkar ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Talid, from Abu Al-Jahhaf, from Khalid ibn Abd al-Malik, from Matar Al-Warraq, from Al-Naji (meaning Abu Al-Siddiq), from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Give glad tidings of the Mahdi,' and he repeated this thrice. 'He will emerge when there is discord among the people and a severe earthquake. He will fill the earth with equity and justice, just as it was filled with oppression and tyranny. He will fill the hearts of his servants with worship, and his justice will encompass them.'

Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Maqri, from Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Maqani, from Bakkar ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from Abd al-Mu'min, from al-Harith ibn Hasira, from Ammarah ibn Juwayn al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say from the pulpit: The Mahdi is from my progeny, from my Ahl al-Bayt. He will emerge in the last period of time. Rain will descend for him from the sky, and the earth will bring forth its vegetation for him. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as the people had filled it with injustice and oppression.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Muqani'i, from Bakkar ibn Ahmad, from Misbah, from Qays, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Huraira, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: If only one day were to remain from the tenure of the world, Allah would prolong that day until a man from my Ahl al-Bayt emerges, filling the earth with justice, just as it had been filled with oppression and tyranny.

From him, from Ali, from Bakkar, from Ali bin Qadim, from Fatar, from Asim, from Zarr bin Habish, from Abdullah bin Masud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: If only a single day remained from the tenure of the world, Allah, the Mighty and the High, would prolong that day until He sends a man from my progeny whose name matches my name and whose father's name matches my father's name; he will fill the earth with justice, just as it had been filled with oppression.

And from him, from Al-Maqani, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Zuhri, from Ishaq ibn Mansur, from Qays ibn Rabi' and others, from Asim, from Zurr, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The world will not pass away until a man from my Ahl al-Bayt, who is called Al-Mahdi, takes charge of my Ummah.

Muhammad ibn Ali from Uthman ibn Ahmad al-Sammak from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Hashmi from al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl al-Busrai from Saad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Ansari from Abd Allah ibn Ziyad al-Yamani from Ikrimah ibn Ammar from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talha from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'We, the children of Abd al-Muttalib, are the chiefs of the people of Paradise: I am Ali, Hamza, Ja'far, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and al-Mahdi.'

From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad Al-Qati, from Ali ibn Hatim, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Ubayd ibn Yahya Al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him). Regarding His saying, Exalted is He: 'And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were deemed weak in the land, and to make them the Imams, and to make them the heirs...' He said: They are the Family of Muhammad. Allah will raise their Mahdi after their distress, so He will honor them and disgrace their enemy.
There are a large number of traditions on this topic, but we have quoted only some of them in order to keep the discussion brief.

A group informed me from Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah al-Nishapuri from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Nasr ibn Muzahim from Ibn Lahia from Abu Qabil from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a long tradition: '...And then will be the rise of the Mahdi, and he is a man from the offspring of this one,' pointing to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). 'Through him, Allah will take away lies. Through him time will take away severity. He will remove the disgrace of slavery from your necks.' Then he said: 'I am the first of this Ummah, Mahdi is the middle of it, and Isa is the last of it. And in between there are calamities and tyrant rulers.'

Muhammad ibn Ali from Uthman ibn Ahmad al-Sammak from Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Hashmi from Ibrahim ibn Hani from Naeem ibn Hammad al-Maruzi from Baqiya ibn Walid from Abu Bakr ibn Abu Maryam from al-Fadl ibn Yaqub al-Rakhami from Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Abu al-Malih from Ziyad ibn Bayan from Ali ibn Nufayl from Saeed ibn Musayyab from Umm Salama, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'The Mahdi is from my progeny, from the descendants of Fatima.'

Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Misbah from Abu Abd al-Rahman from one who heard Wahb ibn Munabbah saying: From Ibn Abbas in a lengthy report that he said: 'O Wahb, then the Mahdi will emerge.' I said: 'Is he from your progeny?' He said: 'No, by Allah, he is not from my progeny, but from the progeny of Ali. Bliss be for the one who reaches his time. Through him, Allah will relieve the Ummah [of distress] until he fills it with equity and justice... to the end of the report.'

Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ammar ibn Marwan from al-Munakhal ibn Jamil from Jabir al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Mahdi is a man from the progeny of Fatima, and he is a man of wheaten complexion.

Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn al-Fadl from Ahmad ibn Uthman from Ahmad ibn Rizq from Yahya ibn al-Ala' al-Razi said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Allah will bring forth in this Ummah a man from me and I from him. Allah will send through him the blessings of the heavens and the earth, so the heavens will rain down its drops and the earth will bring forth its seeds, and its beasts and wild animals will be secure, and He will fill the earth with equity and justice, as it had been filled with oppression and tyranny. He will kill [many] until the ignorant say: If this were from the progeny of Muhammad, he would have been merciful!'

And that which indicates the necessity of leadership is what has been established regarding its being a divine favor within the rational obligations, thus becoming obligatory, like knowledge, which no duty-bound person is devoid of the obligation of upon him, do you not see that it is known that when the fallible from among the people are without an awe-inspiring leader who restrains the stubborn, disciplines the offender, seizes the hand of the dominant, and prevents the strong from the weak, and they are secure from that, corruption occurs, deceptions spread, corruption increases, and goodness decreases, and when they have a leader with these qualities, the matter is the reverse of that, with the encompassment and abundance of goodness, and the scarcity and rarity of corruption, and knowledge of that is necessary, not hidden from the rational, so whoever denies it, good conversation with him is not appropriate, and we have fully responded to whatever is asked regarding that in Talkhis al-Shafi and Sharh al-Jamal, and we will not prolong by mentioning it here.

I found a statement by some of the later scholars which he raised as a counter-argument to the words of Al-Murtada (may Allah have mercy on him) regarding the Occultation, and he thought that he had succeeded in finding a profound point, so he adorned it with falsehood for those who lack insight and perception of the aspects of reasoning, and I will discuss it.

He said: The discourse regarding the occultation and the objection to it consists of three aspects. The first: We compel the Imamiyyah to establish that there is an aspect of ugliness (evil) in it, or in the obligation associated with it, so they are compelled to establish that the occultation does not contain an aspect of ugliness, because if an aspect of ugliness is established, the occultation becomes ugly, even if an aspect of goodness is established in it, as we say regarding the ugliness of imposing what is not bearable (that it has an aspect of ugliness), even if it has an aspect of goodness by being a grace for others.

Second: That the occultation invalidates the reasoning for the necessity of the Imamate in every age, because the presence of people with a venerable and awe-inspiring leader in charge is further from being wrong if his existence were a necessary grace in every state, and the wrongness of imposing obligations without him would be invalidated by the time of occultation, for in the time of occultation we would be with a leader having this description, further from being wrong, and this is the proof of the necessity of this leadership. Yet the existence of a leader with this description is not proved during occultation, nor is the wrongness of imposing obligations without him proved. Thus the proof exists but the proven is absent, and this is the invalidation of the proof.

Third: It is to say that according to you, the benefit of the Imamate is that it leads away from the ugly (wrong). However, this is not achieved with his existence being in hiding, so his existence does not differ from his non-existence. And if his hidden existence does not possess the mode of necessity they mentioned, your evidence does not necessitate his existence during the occultation. Therefore, your evidence, even though it is invalidated where the hand is extended (administration), and extending the hand was not necessitated during the occultation, is not related to the existence of an Imam who does not extend his hand, nor is it achieved in this state.

The discussion of it is that we say: As for the first segment of his statement, 'We prove to the Imamiyah that occultation involves an evil aspect,' it is a mere promise from him not accompanied by an argument. He should have clarified the 'evil aspect' which he wanted to prove to them, so we could consider it, but he did not, so his promise is not directed. And if he said that as a questioner in a certain manner: 'What do you reject about there being an evil aspect in it?' Then we say: The evil aspects are conceivable in the context of the thing being oppression, vanity, lie, debauchery, and ignorance, and none of these are present here, so we know by that the non-existence of the evil aspect. If it is said: The evil aspect is that the cause of the obligated one was not removed according to your view, because his outstretched hand, which is kindness in reality, and the fear of his discipline did not occur, so that became a lack of kindness to the obligated one, thus it is evil because of it.

We said: We had previously discussed in the chapter on the obligation of Imamate, where we indicated it, that the extension of his hand (peace be upon him) and the fear of his discipline were missed by the duty-bound (Mukallaf) only insofar as it pertains to them, because they forced him into concealment by fearing him and not allowing him [to act], so the deficiency came from their own selves. And that occurred in the manner of someone saying: 'He who does not attain knowledge of God Almighty during his period of obligation, his obligation is ugly/flawed,' because the favor of knowledge did not befall him, so his obligation ought to be considered flawed.

We said: We have explained in the chapter of the necessity of Imamate, where we indicated to it, that the extension of his hand (peace be upon him) and the fear of his reprimand are not availed by the duty-bound due to what returns to them, because they forced him to go into hiding by threatening him and did not empower him, so they caused it from themselves. And that occurred in the manner of someone saying: 'For one who does not attain knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, in his obligation, the ugliness is justified' because what is a grace for him from knowledge did not occur, so his obligation should be considered ugly.

What they say here is that the disbeliever is blamed for himself, because God has established for him the proof for knowledge and enabled him to reach it, so if he does not look and does not recognize, he is blamed for that by himself, and it is not blameworthy to hold him accountable, likewise we say: the extending of the Imam's hand (authority), even if it escapes the duty-bound, is only due to himself; and if he had enabled him, he would have appeared and his hand would have extended, and his grace would have materialized, so it would not be blameworthy to hold him accountable. For the proof is against him, not for him. And we have fully covered similar cases in the place to which we referred, and we will mention them later if the need arises to mention them.

As for the speech regarding the second part: It is based on the fallacy. We do not say that he did not understand what he presented, for the man is better than that; but he intended to disguise and confuse. In his saying: 'The argument for the necessity of leadership is invalidated by the state of occultation,' because if the fact that people are with an awe-inspiring leader who manages affairs keeps them far from the ugly (wrong), and if this necessitates his presence being a necessary grace in all times and the absence of him making obligation ugly (unjust), then this would not be invalidated during the time of occultation (because in the time of occultation) obligation was not ugly despite his absence. Thus, the argument was found but the conclusion (that it is invalidated) is not, and this is a contradiction.

We said: This is a disguise, because he presumed that we say: The proof for the obligation of the Imamate stands during the occultation while there is no Imam, which would be a contradiction. We do not say that. Rather, our proof during the presence of the Imam himself is the very proof of his occultation, that in both states the Imam is a grace. So we do not say: The time of occultation is devoid of the obligation of a leader, but with us the leader exists. And the extension of his hand did not cease due to what returns to the duty-bound, as we clarified, not because the extension of his hand ceased to be a grace. Rather, the aspect of grace through him remains, but it did not materialize due to what returns to other than Allah. This runs the course of someone saying: How can the knowledge of Allah be a grace, while the disbeliever does not know Allah? Since the obligation is upon the disbeliever and the knowledge is absent, it indicates that the knowledge is not a grace in every state. Because if it were so, that would be a contradiction.

Our response regarding the Imamate is like their response regarding the Knowledge (of God). That the grace (of God) for the disbeliever remains present in the Knowledge (of God), but he has deprived himself through negligence in the contemplation that leads to it, so imposing duties upon him is not unjust. Similarly, we say: The leadership (Imamate) is a grace for the duty-bound during the period of occultation. And what pertains to God from His providing it is present/available. But his administration and the extension of his hand have ceased due to a matter that returns to the duty-bound themselves, so the two matters (Imamate and Knowledge) have become equal. And the discourse on this meaning is also complete, as we have mentioned it.

As for the speech regarding the third chapter: From his saying: 'The benefit of the Imamate is that it keeps one away from the ugly (evil), according to your view, and this was not achieved with his occultation, so his existence did not differ from his non-existence. Therefore, if his hidden existence is not distinguished by the mode of necessity they mentioned, your evidence does not necessitate his existence during the occultation. Your evidence is also contradicted, as it was found with the 'extending of the hand' (administration), yet the 'extending of the hand' was not necessary during the occultation. So it is not related to the existence of an Imam who is not extending his hand, nor is it established in this state.'

We reply that he has only complicated his argument in this section, as logicians say, by turning around premises and referring them to one another, and undoubtedly he intended to disguise lunacy beneath lucidity and fallacy beneath logic; otherwise, the subject is clearer than to be ambiguous. When has the Imamiyah said that the administration of affairs by the Imam is not necessary during occultation, so it could be said your proof does not prove the necessity of existence of an Imam who is not administering the society, because this is the time of occultation? On the contrary, what we have stated time and again is that his administration of society is necessary in all conditions – his occultation as well as his appearance. However, during his appearance he is able to administer the society and he does that, and during occultation he is unable to perform that and does not do it, because it does not remain obligatory anymore. We explained that the duty-bound are to be blamed for this, as they prohibited him; they did not empower him, and took on the task themselves. We compared this to the subject of faith in God time and again.

We also know that the appointment of the leader is obligatory after the Law, because in his appointment there is grace, for his bearing the performance of what no one else performs. And with this, the empowerment is not realized by the people of resolution and contract from appointing one who is suitable for it specifically, according to the school of the people of justice, with whom our discourse is. And with this, no one says: that the obligation of appointing the leader has fallen now, in that the empowerment from him has not occurred.

Therefore, our answer regarding the occultation of the Imam is their answer regarding the prevention of the people of resolution and contract from choosing one suitable for the Imamate, and there is no difference between them, for the only difference between us is that we said: our knowledge of that is through reason, and they said: that is known through Islamic law, and that is a difference from a place of non-union.

If it is said: When 'those having a say' lack the power to choose one who is best for Imamate, Allah bestows other graces (altaf), which take the place of an Imam who is in power. Therefore, religious commands remain intact and are not relinquished. Some teachers (Shaykhs) have said that the appointment of an Imam is necessary in Shariah for worldly expediencies, and it is not necessary that Allah bestows grace when a worldly benefit is missing.

As for the one who said: Allah will do what takes its place, [this is] false, because if it were so, it would not be obligatory upon him to establish the Imam absolutely in every condition, and that would be a matter of choice, as we say regarding the obligatory duties (Kifayee obligations). And in our knowledge of specifying that and its obligation in every condition is proof of the falsity of what they said. Indeed, it is required in both cases together that [there be] knowledge. It is said: The disbeliever, if knowledge does not become established for him, Allah will do for him what takes its place, so knowledge will not be obligatory upon him in every condition.

If it is said: The existence of an obeyed leader with expanded authority cannot be otherwise than that it is obligatory upon Allah to create him entirely, or obligatory upon us to create him entirely, or obligatory upon Allah to create him and upon us to expand his authority.

If you say: All of that is obligatory upon Allah, then your assertion is contradicted by the state of occultation, because an Imam who is 'expanding his hand' (exercising authority) has not been found. And if it is obligatory upon us to do all of it, then that is a burden that is not bearable, for we do not have the ability to bring him into existence. And if it is obligatory upon Him to create him, and upon us to expand his hand and empower him, then what is your proof for this? And it proceeds that we should be required to do something which is actually a grace for someone else, How would it be possible that Zaid be required to empower the Imam so that Amr's grace can be materialized? Is it not a violation of principle?

We said: What we say is that the existence of the Imam with authority (Manbast al-Yad), if it is established that he is a grace upon us according to what we have demonstrated, and his creation is not within our power, it would not be fitting that we be required to create him, for it would be a duty that is beyond capacity. And empowering his hand and strengthening his authority may be within our capacity and within the capacity of Allah. So when Allah does not do that, we know that it is not obligatory upon Him, but that it is obligatory upon us. Because he must be one with authority for the purpose of the duty to be realized. And we explained by this that if empowering his hand were from His action, He would compel the creation to it. And His intervening between him and his enemies, and strengthening his command through the angels, might lead to the falling away of the purpose of the duty and the occurrence of compulsion. Therefore, it is obligatory upon us to empower him in every condition, and if we do not do so, it is from ourselves.

As for their assertion that this amounts to procuring grace for someone else, it is incorrect. Because we say, each person who helps the Imam and strengthens his rule, enjoys a benefit specific for himself, may it carry expediency for others as well. It is like what you say about the apostles that their carriage of the burden of Prophethood and delivery of message to the public bears expediency for others, because for them in doing so is a benefit specific to them, even if it contains benefit for others. This requires the opponent to answer a query about “those having a say” - how is it that it is obligatory on them to choose an Imam for expediencies that encompass the entire Ummah and is it not requiring one to do something that benefits someone else? Whatever may be your justification with regard to the situation of the apostles is our very answer here.

Objection: Why do you believe that he must exist during occultation, and why is it not possible that he does not exist? Reply: We consider his existence necessary for the following: His administration of the affairs and leadership of the society, which is grace with respect to us, is not possible without his existence. And as his creation is not in our capacity, we said it is obligatory on Allah, or else it would mean that we are not the missing part of the cause of materialization of grace, meaning that, missing the grace is His act and not ours. However, if He creates him, but we do not vest the power of running the society in him, it is our act, and therefore, ordainment of duties is correct, whereas in the previous supposition it would be incorrect.

If it is said: What do you mean by empowering him? Do you mean that we find him and converse with him, and that is not possible except with his existence. It was said to you: None of that is valid except with his manifestation and our knowledge, or the knowledge of some of us, of his place. And if you say: We mean by empowering him that we submit to his obedience and strengthen his hand, and refrain from helping the tyrants, and stand to support him whenever he calls us to his Imamate and indicates it to us through his miracle. We said to you: Then we can do that during the time of occultation, even if the Imam is not present in it, so how do you say that what we are ordained to do cannot be performed except with the presence of the Imam. We said: What we say in this matter is what Murtadha (may God have mercy on him) mentioned in Al-Dhakhira and what we mentioned in Talkhis Al-Shafi, that which is our grace from the Imam's action and the extension of his hand, is not complete except by three matters.

One pertains to Allah, and that is His creating him. The second pertains to him, which is carrying the burdens of Imamate and performing its duties. The third pertains to us, which is the resolve to support him, assist him, and submit to him. The obligation of his undertaking [the role] is secondary to his existence, because it is not permissible for the obligation to apply to a non-existent entity. Therefore, Allah's creating him is the primary basis for the obligation of his standing [in office], and the obligation of our supporting him is secondary to these two bases, because it is obligatory upon us to obey him only when he exists and has carried the burdens of Imamate and performed them. At that point, it becomes obligatory upon us to obey him. With this reasoning in mind, how can it be said: 'Why should he not be non-existent'?

Objection: What is the difference between him being existent and hidden (until Allah knows from us our determination to empower him, and that is when He reveals him), and being non-existent until Allah knows from us the determination to empower him and that is when He creates him? Reply: Our answer will be that it is not worthy of Allah, the Exalted, to oblige us to empower someone who is non-existent, for it is an impossible task. Therefore, he must exist.

Objection: When Allah comes to know that we are prepared to obey him, He would create him. Like according to your belief He will manifest him during his reappearance? Reply: The imperativeness of supporting him and determination to obey him is required in all conditions, which requires that to support and obey him and to follow his path should be possible in all conditions, or else, imposing this duty would be wrong. The suggestion would be relevant if we were not obliged in all conditions to his obedience and submission to his command and rather it were required of us at the time of his appearance. However, the reality is contrary to this.

Then it is said to the one who opposed us in that matter and insisted on its non-existence on the grounds of his occultation: Why is it not permissible that Allah, the Exalted, enacts the obligation of knowledge (belief) and does not establish a sign/proof for it, if He knows that we do not consider it? Until, when He knows from our condition that we intend to consider it and are determined to do so, He creates the proofs and establishes them. At that time, we consider and say: What is the difference between an established proof that we do not consider, and its non-existence, until when we are determined to consider it, Allah, the Exalted, creates it?

This is the state of the Imam's appearance with our providing him power; therefore, it is our lack of providing power that is the reason he has not appeared in these conditions, not his lack of existence, for if we had provided him power, peace be upon him, he would have come into being and appeared.

We said: This is the speech of one who thinks that it is obligatory upon us to empower him when he appears, and that this is not obligatory upon us in every condition, but we accepted the example he mentioned, because if Allah, the Exalted, had made drawing water obligatory upon us at that moment, it would have been necessary that the rope be present at that moment, because through it the excuse is eliminated, however, if He says: 'When you approach the well, I will create for you the rope,' then he is only obligated to approach, not to draw water, so the ability to approach is sufficient in this condition, because he is not yet obligated to draw water from it, so when he approaches the well, he then becomes obligated to draw water, and at that point it becomes necessary that the rope be created for him, an analogous instance to this is that if it were not obligatory upon us in every condition to obey the Imam and empower him, then his existence would not be necessary at that time, but since his obedience is obligatory at the present moment, and we do not know his condition or a waiting time, it becomes necessary that he be present to eliminate the excuse in the obligation, and this is fitting.

Besides, if the Imam bears the Divine duty of establishing order and carries the burden of Imamate, how is it possible for him to be non-existent? Would any sane person see it fair to commission someone non-existent with acts and duties? Bear in mind that these duties of his are not stipulated to our empowerment of him at all, but rather, our obligation of empowering and strengthening him is secondary to him carrying out these duties, as explained before and as is very much clear.

Then it is said to them: Did not the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) hide in the valley for three years, so that no one could reach him, and did he not hide in the Cave for three days? And by analogy, is it not valid that Allah should not deprive him of existence for that period, while the obligation remains upon the people for whom He sent him as a mercy? If they say: He only hid after he called people to himself and manifested his Prophethood, and when they threatened him, he concealed himself. We say: Likewise, the Imam did not go into hiding until his forefathers had manifested his position and description, and pointed him out. Then, when his father Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them) feared for him, he hid him and concealed him. Therefore, the two matters are equal. Then it is said to them: Inform me, if Allah knew from the condition of a person that it is in his interest that Allah sends a specific prophet to him to convey his affairs, and He knew that if He sent him, this person would kill him, and if He prevented him from killing him by force, there would be a detriment to him or to others, would it be fitting that Allah obligate this person and not send that prophet to him, or not obligate him?

If they say: He is not bound [by divine duties]. We say: And what prevents it, and there is a way for him to know his benefits by empowering the Prophet to deliver to him. And if you say: He binds him [Allah binds him] but does not send to him [a prophet]. We say: And how is it permissible that He binds him when He has not done for him what is a grace for him, which is within His power.

If they say that it is by the Imam's own choice. We will say that he has not done anything. Only Allah knew that he will not allow the apostle and knowing this does not justify that he should be bound by duties, which he does not know. If this should be fair, then it is fair that anyone should be bound by duties he does not know when Allah knows that he will not consider them. It is an absurd supposition. Thus it must be said that Allah will send the apostle to him and require him to submit to him to eliminate any legitimate excuse, and then He will protect His apostle through means, which do not violate free-will, or renders him unable to kill the apostle, in which case he will not be able to reach him through his own acts. This is our same situation with the Imam during occultation.

If it is said: He must inform him through someone other than the apostle that it is in his interest that the apostle is sent to him, so he may know it is his own wrongdoing, our reply will be that on parallel grounds, Allah has informed us through His Messenger and Imams (his forefathers), the Imam’s position and obliged us to obey him; and if we do not know what we should do, it is our own guilt, hence the similarity between two situations.

As for that which indicates that he will be from the offspring of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), the reports which we have cited regarding that the Imams are twelve and mentioned their details are inclusive of that, and because whoever enumerated the number we mentioned said: The Mahdi is from the offspring of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). And it is what we have alluded to. And that which increases its clarity is:

And with this chain of narrators, from Sufyan al-Jariri, that he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila say: By Allah, the Mahdi will not be, except from the progeny of Husain (peace be upon him).

And by this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Zahir, from Ismail ibn Ayyash, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wail, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) looked at his son, Husayn (peace be upon him), and said: 'Indeed, this son of mine is a master, as the Messenger of Allah named him a master. Allah will bring forth from his loins a man with the name of your Prophet, who will resemble him in appearance and character. He will emerge at a time when people are heedless, when righteousness is dead, and when injustice is manifest. By Allah, if he did not emerge, his neck would be struck. The people of the heavens and their inhabitants will rejoice at his emergence. He will fill the earth with justice, as it was filled with injustice and oppression.' The end of the report.

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ghazafar from Uqbah ibn Yunus from Abdullah ibn Sharik, in his hadith—which we have abridged— He said: Husain (peace be upon him) passed by a group of the Umayyads while they were sitting in the Masjid of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). He said: 'By Allah, the world will not pass away until Allah sends from me a man who will kill from you one thousand, and with the thousand another thousand, and with the thousand another thousand.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, these are the sons of so-and-so; they do not reach this number.' He said: 'Woe to you! At that time, a man will have from his loins so-and-so many men, and their chief will be from themselves.'

And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Saeed al-Ahwazi from al-Husayn ibn Alwan from Abu Harun al-Abdi from Abu Saeed al-Khudri, in a long hadith of his—which we have summarized—he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Fatima (peace be upon her): 'O my daughter, we, the People of the House, were given seven things that no one was given before us: Our prophet is the best of the prophets, and he is your father; our successor is the best of the successors, and he is your husband; our martyr is the best of the martyrs, and he is the uncle of your father, Hamzah; from us is one who has two green wings by which he flies in Paradise, and he is your cousin Ja'far; from us are the two scions of this Ummah, and they are your two sons, al-Hasan and al-Husayn; and from us is, by Allah, the One besides Whom there is no deity, the Mahdi of this Ummah, behind whom Isa ibn Maryam will pray.' Then he struck with his hand on the shoulder of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said three times: 'Who is this?'

As for the one who contradicts regarding the death of Amir al-Mu'minin and states that he is alive and remaining, he is obdurate.
