For the knowledge of his death and martyrdom is more evident and more famous than the killing of anyone else and the death of every person, and doubt in that leads to doubt in the death of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and all of his companions. Then what became apparent from his will and the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) news to him: 'You will be killed and your beard will be dyed with your blood,' also invalidates this, and that is more famous than to require narrations to be reported about it.

Ibn Abi Jayyad informed us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn Ali Abu Samina al-Kufi from Hammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Umar from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in his will to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): O Ali, indeed Quraish will overpower you and their unity will gather against your oppression and subjugation. So if you find helpers, strive against them in Jihad, and if you do not find helpers, restrain your hand and preserve your blood, for martyrdom is behind you. May Allah curse the one who kills you.
Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya said: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) sent me this will along with the other one.
And in another traditional report, it is mentioned that he was passed away on the eve of the 21st and was wounded on the eve of the 19th.}}], And this is the more apparent (accurate).

Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Ruba'i ibn Abdullah from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who said: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said to me: When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) moved to Iraq, he entrusted his will, books, and other matters to Umm Salma, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and said to her: When my eldest son comes to you, hand over to him what I have given you. When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was martyred, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came to Umm Salma, and she handed over to him everything that al-Husayn (peace be upon him) had deposited with her.

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubaid from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhtah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Imamate will not return to two brothers after Hasan and Husayn (peace be upon them), and after Ali ibn Husayn (peace be upon him) it will be only in the descendants, and the descendants of the descendants.

And what occurred between Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), and their arbitration by the Hajar (Black Stone), is well-known; we shall not prolong [the text] by mentioning it here.
As for the manifestation of miracles indicating the validity of his Imamate during the Occultation, they are more numerous than can be counted except that we will mention a portion of them

A group of scholars narrated from Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Quluwayh, from Muhammad ibn Yaqub, who raised it to Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said: After the passing of my father, Imam Muhammad al-Hasan (peace be upon him), doubts overwhelmed me. A large amount of wealth had been deposited with my father, so he carried it and boarded a ship. I went with him to accompany him. He fell ill with a severe fever. He said to me: 'My son, take me back, take me back; this is death. And fear Allah regarding this wealth.' He confided his final will to me and died. I said to myself: 'My father did not ask me to do anything wrong. I will carry this wealth to Iraq and rent a house by the river, and I will not inform anyone. If something becomes clear to me, as clear as it was during the days of my father, Imam Muhammad (peace be upon him), I will send it [to the Imam]; otherwise, I will give it in charity.' I arrived in Iraq and rented a house by the river. I remained there for a few days when suddenly a messenger came to me with a note saying: 'O Muhammad, you have with you such and such [amounts] in such and such parcels,' recounting all the wealth with me of which I had no knowledge. I handed the wealth to the messenger. I remained there for a few more days and received no attention, which made me sad. Then a message came to me: 'We have appointed you in the position of your father, so thank Allah.'

And by this chain, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Fadl ibn Zayd Al-Yamani, who said: I wrote about two issues and wanted to write about the third but refrained, fearing he would dislike that, so the answer came regarding the two issues and the third which I had kept to myself, explained.

And by this chain, from Badr -the slave of Ahmad ibn al-Hasan- who said: I arrived at the mountain region, and at that time I did not affirm the Imamate, but I loved them generally. Then Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik died, and he bequeathed to me in his illness that the Shahri Simand (horse), his sword, and his belt be delivered to his master. I feared that if I did not deliver the Shahri to Idhkutakain, he would subject me to humiliation. So I valued the beast, the sword, and the belt at seven hundred dinars for myself, and did not inform anyone of this. Then a letter arrived from Iraq ordering me: 'Send the seven hundred dinars that are ours from before you, from the price of the Shahri Simand, the sword, and the belt.'

And by this chain, from Ali, from those who narrated it to him, that he said: A son was born to me, so I wrote seeking permission to perform his circumcision (taher) on the seventh day. The reply came: Do not do it. He died on the seventh or eighth day. Then I wrote about his death, and the reply came: Allah will replace him with another, and name him Ahmad, and after Ahmad, Ja'far. It came to pass as he said.

And by this chain, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Aqil Isa ibn Nasr, who said: Ali ibn Ziyad al-Sa'imuri wrote requesting a burial shroud, so he was written to: 'You will need it in the year eighty.' He died in the year eighty, and a shroud was sent to him before his death.

Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who said: A prohibition was issued regarding the visitation of the graveyards of Quraish and Al-Hayr. When some months had passed, the minister Al-Baqitani called him and said to him: 'Convey to the people of Bani al-Furat and Al-Barasiyyin and tell them not to visit the graveyards of Quraish, for the Caliph has ordered that he closely monitors anyone who visits and arrests him.' As for what appeared from his side, peace be upon him, of the autographs (tawqi'at), they are numerous, and we mention a portion of them.

There is no reason preventing his appearance except his fear for his own life from being killed, because if it were otherwise, concealment would not have been permissible for him, and he would have borne hardships and annoyance; for the ranks of the Imams and likewise the Prophets, peace be upon them, are only exalted because of their bearing the great hardships for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.

If it is said: Is it not true that his forefathers, peace be upon them, were visible and did not fear, nor did they reach a state where no one could reach them? We said: The state of his forefathers, peace be upon them, is different from his state, because it was known from the state of his forefathers to the rulers of the time and others that they did not see themselves rising up against them, nor did they believe that they would rise with the sword and remove dynasties. Rather, it was known from their state that they were waiting for a Mahdi for themselves, and it did not harm the ruler if those who believed in their Imamate did so, as long as they were safe from them regarding their kingdom (and did not fear their side). And such is not the case with the Master of the Time, peace be upon him, because it is known from him that he will rise with the sword, remove kingdoms, subdue every ruler, spread justice, and extinguish tyranny. From this of his characteristic, they fear his side and guard against his sudden attack, so they pursue him and keep watch, and place eyes on him, and pay attention to him out of fear of his leap and suspicion of his consolidation, so he fears at that time and needs concealment and manifestation, by hiding his person from everyone whom he does not trust, whether friend or enemy, until the time of his emergence. Furthermore, his forefathers, peace be upon them, only appeared because it was known that if an incident occurred to them, there would be someone among their children to take his place and fill his position. And such is not the case with the Master of the Time, peace be upon him, because it is known that there is no one after him to take his place before the arrival of the time of his rising with the sword, therefore his concealment and occultation became necessary, and his state differed from the state of his forefathers, peace be upon them, and this is clear, praise to God. If it is said: By what does he know the removal of fear at the time of his appearance? Is it through divine revelation? But the Imam is not revealed to, or through necessary knowledge? But that contradicts obligation, or through a sign that necessitates conjecture for him? Then in that is deception of the self.

Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed me, from Abu Ja'far ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan al-Nisaburi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from al-Zurari who said: There is an occultation for the Qaim before his appearance. I asked: For what reason? He replied: He fears being killed.

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) kept his message concealed in Mecca, hiding and fearful, for five years, not publicizing it, while Ali (peace be upon him) and Khadija were with him. Then Allah, the Exalted, commanded him to announce what he was ordered to do, so he appeared and publicized his matter.

Saad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) remained in Mecca for thirteen years after the revelation came to him from Allah, the Exalted. Among these, three years were spent in secret, fearful, not appearing openly, until Allah commanded him to proclaim openly what he was ordered to do. At that time, he publicized the call.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Isa al-Ashari narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khasa'i, from Durays al-Kinasi, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli in a tradition of his which we have condensed He said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to name the Qaim so that I may recognize him by his name. He said: O Abu Khalid! You have asked me about a matter, if the children of Fatimah had known it, they would have desired to cut him into pieces.

And Saad ibn Abdullah narrated, from a group of our companions, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'There is an occultation for the Young Man (the Imam) before he rises (to claim authority).' I asked: 'Why?' He replied: 'He fears.' And he pointed with his hand to his belly. Then he said: 'O Zurarah! He is the Awaited One, and he is the one in whose birth people doubt. Some of them say: When his father died, he had no heir; some say: He was a fetus; some say: He is hidden; some say: He has not yet been born; and some say: He was born two years before his father's death. And he is the Awaited One, but Allah the Exalted loves to test the Shia, so at that time the false ones will waver in doubt.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, if I live to see that time, what should I do?' He said: 'O Zurarah, if you live to see that time, then supplicate with this supplication: O Allah, make me know Yourself, for if You do not make me know Yourself, I will not know Your Prophet... until the end.'

Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali narrated, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari and Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in his bequest to the Commander of the Faithful: 'O my brother, indeed Quraish will overpower you and their unity will be upon your oppression and subjugation; so if you find helpers, strive against them, and if you do not find helpers, restrain your hand and preserve your blood, for indeed martyrdom is behind you.'

As for what is recorded from the reports regarding the test of the Shia during the period of occultation, and the difficulty of the matter for them, and their being tested with patience for it, the reason for these reports is to inform about the hardships and troubles that would occur, not that Allah the Almighty concealed the Imam to cause that, and how can Allah intend that, whereas what befalls the believers from the oppressors is injustice on their part and sin, and Allah the Almighty does not intend that. On the contrary, the cause of the occultation is fear, as we have said, and they were informed about what would occur in this state, and the reward for the believer for patience with that, and holding fast to his religion until Allah the Almighty eases their circumstances. And I will mention a portion of the reports recorded in this meaning.

Husayn ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Safwan al-Bazufari, from Ahmad ibn Idris who said: He narrated to me from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Nisaburi, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, from his father who said: We were a group in the presence of Abu 'Abdullah (peace be upon him), talking, he turned to us and asked: 'What are you talking about? How far! How far! By Allah, that which you anticipate with your eyes will not happen until you are sifted (tested). By Allah, that which you anticipate will not happen until you are distinguished (separated). By Allah, that which you anticipate will not happen until you are purified (refined). By Allah, that which you anticipate will not happen except after despair. By Allah, that which you anticipate will not happen until the wretched one becomes wretched and the fortunate one becomes fortunate.'

And Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Thalabah ibn Maimun, from Malik al-Juhani, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: I came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and found him thoughtful, drawing lines in the earth. I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, why do I see you thoughtful, drawing lines in the earth? Is it out of desire for it?' He said: 'No, by Allah. I have never desired it, nor for the world for a day. But I was thinking about a son who will be born from my loins, the eleventh of my descendants, who is the Mahdi, who will fill it with equity and justice as it was filled with oppression and tyranny. There will be perplexity and occultation for him, in which some people will go astray and others will be guided.'

Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, that which you look forward to will not come about until you are distinguished or tested, until only the best of you remain. “Do you think that you will be left [as you are] while Allah has not yet known those who strive among you and do not take other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers as intimates?” Then he recited it.

Saad ibn Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Isa Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said: When the fifth [Imam] from the offspring of the seventh of the Imams is lost, then be careful of Allah regarding your religions; let no one remove you from it. O my sons, indeed the master of this affair must have an occultation, until those who used to affirm it will renounce it. It is merely a trial from Allah, with which Allah the Exalted tested His creation.

Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated from Abu Saeed al-Adami, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir, who said: We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: "This matter (the rise of the Mahdi) will not take place until two-thirds of the people perish." We asked: "If two-thirds of the people perish, who will remain?" He replied: "Are you not satisfied that you will be among the remaining one-third?"

And it is narrated from Jabir al-Ja'fi who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'When will your relief (or emergence) be?' He replied: 'Far off, far off! Our relief will not come until you are sieved, then sieved, then sieved,' he said it three times, 'until the dross is removed by Allah (the Exalted) and only the pure remains.'

And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: "By God, you, O community of the Shia of the progeny of Muhammad, will be tested like the kohl (ground cosmetic) in the eye. For the owner of the kohl knows when it is put into the eye, but does not know when it leaves. Thus, one of you may be in the morning believing that he is upon our doctrine, and in the evening find that he has left it; and he may be in the evening upon our doctrine, and in the morning find that he has left it."

From him, from his father, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musalli, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, you will be broken like glass, and indeed glass is restored and returns as it was. By Allah, you will be broken like earthenware, and indeed earthenware does not return as it was. By Allah, you will be distinguished; by Allah, you will be purified; by Allah, you will be sieved like chaff is sieved from wheat.

And Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi narrated, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hashim, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) mentioned the Qaim (peace be upon him) and said: 'He will be hidden from them, so that the ignorant will say: What does Allah need with the Family of Muhammad?'

From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Buzay', from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyabah, from Imran ibn Mitham, from Abaya ibn Rabi' al-Asadi, who said: I heard Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) say: 'How will you be when you remain without an Imam of guidance or a visible standard, when some of you turn away from the other with disdain?'

Al-Shalmaghani narrated in the Book of the Successors: Abu Ja'far al-Marwazi said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umar and a group went to al-Askar and witnessed the days of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) while he was alive. Among them was Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Tanin. Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umar wrote asking permission to enter the tomb. Ali ibn Ahmad said to him, 'Do not write my name, for I do not seek permission.' So he did not write his name, and the reply came to Ja'far, 'Enter you and the one who did not seek permission.'

Before mentioning those who were emissaries during the period of occultation, we will mention some reports about those who were specifically assigned to each Imam and managed his affairs, in a concise manner, and we will mention those among them who were praised for their good method, and those who were condemned for their poor creed, so that the situation may be known in that regard.
And it is narrated in some reports that they (peace be upon them) said: Our servants and our caretakers are the most evil of Allah’s creation.
Among the approved ones is Humran bin Ayyin:

Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdullah ibn Bukair, from Zurarah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said -and we mentioned Humran ibn A'yun-: 'By Allah, he will definitely never apostatize.' Then he paused for a moment, and then said: 'Yes, by Allah, he will definitely never apostatize.'
And among them is al-Mufaddal ibn Umar

Through this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Munqari, from Asad ibn Abi Al'a, from Hisham ibn Ahmar, who said: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I wanted to ask him about al-Mufaddal ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He was in his estate on a day of intense heat, and sweat was flowing down his chest. He initiated the conversation and said: Yes, by the God, except whom there is no god, the man is al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi. Yes, by the God, except whom there is no god, the man (he is) al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ja'fi. Until I counted thirty-seven times he repeated it, and he said: Indeed, he is father after father.

And it is narrated from Hisham ibn Ahmar that he said: I carried money to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to Medina, so he said: 'Return it and deliver it to Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar.' So I returned it to Juffa and placed it at the door of Al-Mufaddal.

And it is narrated from Musa ibn Bakr who said: I was in the service of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and I did not see anything reaching him except from the side of al-Mufaddal; and often I saw a man bring something, but he would not accept it from him and would say: Deliver it to al-Mufaddal.

And among them is al-Mu'alla ibn Khunais, and he was one of the servants (or stewards) of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and it was because of him that Dawud ibn Ali had him killed. He was praised by him, and he proceeded upon his path/method, and his affair/status is well-known.

It is narrated from Abu Basir that he said: When Dawood bin Ali had Mualla bin Khunais eliminated and had his body suspended in public view, it was a great tragedy for Imam Ja’far Sadiq (peace be upon him), which aggrieved him much. So he said to the killer: O Dawood, why have you got my friend and manager of the monetary affairs of my family, killed? By Allah, he is more honorable than you before Almighty Allah… It is a lengthy tradition.
And in another report, he said: Know by Allah, he has entered Paradise.
And among them is Nasr bin Qabus al-Lakhmi

And among them is what Abu Talib al-Qummi narrated, saying: I entered upon Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) in the last period of his life, and I heard him say: May Allah reward Safwan ibn Yahya, and Muhammad ibn Sinan, and Zakariyya ibn Adam, and Sa'd ibn Sa'd, on my behalf with good; for they have fulfilled their covenant [of Wilayah] for me, and Zakariyya ibn Adam was among those who had his Wilayah.

And it is narrated (in it) from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): I remembered what occurred regarding the decree of Allah in the deceased man, upon whom Allah's mercy is abundant, on the day he was born, the day he died, and the day he is resurrected alive. He lived the days of his life knowing the truth and affirming it, patient and counting his reward (for the truth), fulfilling what is obligatory for Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him), and he departed, upon whom Allah's mercy is, neither breaking his covenant nor changing it. So Allah rewarded him for his intention and gave him the recompense for his effort.

As for Muhammad ibn Sinan, it is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Dawood who said: I heard Abu Ja'far, the second (Imam al-Jawad), peace be upon him, mentioning Muhammad ibn Sinan in a good way, saying: 'Allah is pleased with him because I am pleased with him; he did not oppose me, nor did he oppose my father, ever.'
And among them is Abdul Aziz bin Al-Muhtadi Al-Qummi Al-Ashari:

It was narrated in it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) I have received [the amount], and praise be to Allah, and I have noticed the expenses that were sent to you from it. May Allah forgive you and them their sins, and have mercy on us and you.
Another epistle was issued with regard to him that Almighty Allah has forgiven your sin and has been merciful to us and you and because I am pleased with you, Almighty Allah is also pleased with you.
And among them was Ali ibn Mahziyar al-Ahwazi, and he was praised.

306 - A group of scholars narrated to me, from al-Talaqbari, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Abu al-Hasan al-Balkhi, from Ahmad ibn Mabandar al-Iskafi, from al-Ala' al-Nadari, from al-Hasan ibn Shammun, who said: I read this letter to Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him), in his own handwriting: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. O Ali, may Allah grant you a good reward, and settle you in His Paradise, and keep away the degradation of the world and the Hereafter from you, and may Allah raise you with us. O Ali, I have tested you and gained experience with you in well-wishing, obedience, and service, and in reverence and fulfilling what is obligatory upon you. If I say that I have not seen your like, I hope I would be truthful. May Allah reward you with the Gardens of Firdous as a dwelling. Your position and your service in heat and cold, in night and day, have not been hidden from me. I ask Allah, when He gathers the creatures for the Resurrection, to love you with a mercy that you will delight in. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing of the supplication.
And among them is Ayyub ibn Nuh ibn Darraj:

Amr ibn Saeed al-Madaini (who was a Fathi) narrated: I was with Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) in Sayr when Ayyub ibn Nuh entered and stood before him. He ordered him something, then he left. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: O Amr, if you wish to see a man from the people of Paradise, look at this man.
And among them is Ali ibn Ja'far al-Hammani, and he was an accomplished, pleasing man, from the representatives of Abu al-Hasan and Abu Muhammad (peace be upon them).

Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi narrated from Ali ibn Mukhallad al-Ayyadi, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Amari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me that: Abu Tahir ibn Bilal performed Hajj and saw Ali ibn Ja'far spending great expenditures. When he returned, he wrote about that to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), and it appeared in his reply: 'We had ordered him to take one hundred thousand dinars, then we ordered him to take the like of it, but he refused to accept it, keeping it for us. What is for people to enter into our matter regarding what we have not included them in?' He said: And he entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him), and he ordered him to take thirty thousand dinars.
And among them is Abu Ali ibn Rashid

333 - Ibn Abi Jayyid narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) wrote to the Shia in Baghdad, al-Mada'in, al-Sawad, and the surrounding areas: I have appointed Abu Ali ibn Rashid in the place of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abd Rabbih and those before him from my representatives, and I have made obedience to him equivalent to my obedience, and disobedience to him equivalent to my disobedience, and I wrote this in my own handwriting.

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, elevating it to Muhammad ibn Faraj, who said: I wrote to him asking about Abu Ali ibn Rashid, and Isa ibn Ja'far (ibn Asim), and Ibn Band. He wrote back to me: You mentioned Ibn Rashid, may Allah have mercy on him, for he lived a happy life and died a martyr. And he prayed for Ibn Band and the Asimi. Ibn Band was struck with a pillar and killed, and Ibn Asim was lashed with whips on the bridge three hundred times and thrown into the Tigris.
These were the group of the praised, and we left mentioning their exhaustive enumeration because they are well-known and mentioned in the books.

From another book: I saw you, may Allah prolong your honor, in contemplation of my letter, and bestowing what is easy for me to add to your other favors upon me. I requested, may Allah prolong your honor, that you ask some of the jurists about the worshipper when he rises from the first Tashahud for the third Rak'ah: is it obligatory for him to recite the Takbir? For some of our companions said: It is not obligatory for him to recite the Takbir, and it suffices for him to say: 'By the power and might of Allah, I rise and I sit.' The answer: He said: Indeed, there are two traditions in this matter. As for one of them, it is that when he transitions from one state to another, he must recite the Takbir. As for the other, it is narrated that when he raises his head from the second Sajdah, he recites the Takbir, then sits, then stands; thus he does not need to recite the Takbir for standing after sitting. And the first Tashahud follows this same pattern. Whichever of the two you follow regarding the Taslim, it is correct. And regarding the ring of the goldsmith, is it permissible to pray wearing it if it is on his finger? The answer: There is dislike (Karahah) in praying wearing it, and there is also permissibility (Itilaq). The practice is upon the dislike. And regarding a man who bought a sacrificial animal (Hady) for an absent man and asked him to sacrifice on his behalf in Mina, but when he wanted to slaughter the animal, he forgot the man's name and slaughtered the animal, then remembered him afterwards. Does it suffice for the man or not? The answer: There is no problem with that, and it has sufficed for his companion. And among us are weavers of the Majus (Zoroastrians) who eat carrion and do not perform Ghusl from Janabah, and they weave clothes for us. Is it permissible to pray in them before they are washed? The answer: There is no problem in praying in them. And regarding the worshipper who is in the night prayer in darkness, and when he prostrates, he mistakes the prayer mat and places his forehead on a cloth or rug. When he raises his head, he finds the prayer mat. Does he count this Sajdah or not? The answer: As long as he has not sat upright, there is no problem for him in raising his head to seek the cover (Turbah/Sajdah place). And regarding the Muhrim who raises the shades; does he raise the wood of the canopy or the church and raise the wings o
Ibn Nuh said: I have prepared this copy from two ancient scrolls, which contained letters and epistles.
And Abul Qasim (peace be upon him) was among the most intelligent of people in the view of both the opposing and the agreeing parties, and he practiced dissimulation (Taqiyyah).

Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad said: Abu Abdullah ibn Ghalib, the brother-in-law of Abul Hasan ibn Abi Tayyib, said: I did not see anyone wiser than the Shaykh Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh. I remember seeing him one day in the house of Ibn Yasar. He had a great position with the Sayyid (the Caliph) and al-Muqtadir. The common people also revered him, and Abul Qasim attended due to dissimulation (taqiyyah) and fear. I remember two men arguing; one claimed that Abu Bakr was the best of people after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then Umar, then Ali. The other said, 'Rather, Ali is better than Umar.' Their debate intensified. Abul Qasim (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'What the companions are unanimous upon is that the Siddiq (Abu Bakr) comes first, then after him the Faruq (Umar), then after him Uthman (Dhu al-Nurayn), then Ali (the Successor). The people of Hadith are upon this, and it is the correct view with us.' Those present in the gathering were amazed by this statement. The attending common people raised him above their heads (in joy), and there was much supplication for him and criticism of those who accused him of Rafidism. Laughter overwhelmed me; I tried to restrain myself, putting my sleeve in my mouth, fearing exposure. I jumped up from the gathering. He looked at me and noticed me. When I arrived home, there was a knock on the door. I went out quickly and found Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) riding his mule, who had come to me from the gathering before proceeding to his house. He said to me: 'O Abu Abdullah, may Allah support you, why did you laugh as if to cheer me, as if what I said was not true in your view?' I said: 'It is true in my view.' He said: 'Fear God, O Shaykh, for I will not make you excused if you consider this statement of mine great/strange.' I said: 'O my master, a man who believes he is the companion of the Imam and his representative, saying this statement, is it not awkward and laughable?' He said to me: 'By your life, if you repeat this, I will desert you.' He bid me farewell and left.

Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad said: Abu al-Hasan ibn Kibriya al-Nuubakhti narrated to us that: It reached Shaykh Abu al-Qasim (may Allah be pleased with him) that a doorman of his, stationed at the first door, had cursed Muawiyah and insulted him, so he ordered his dismissal and removal from his service. He remained for a long period asking about his matter, and by Allah, he did not return him to his service, and some of the family took him and employed him with them. All of this was due to dissimulation (Taqiyyah).

Abu Nasr Hibatullah said: Abu Ahmad Daranawayh the Leper, whose house was in the Alley of the Stationers, narrated to me, saying: I and my brothers used to enter to Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, may Allah be pleased with him, to transact business with him. He was a merchant and we were about ten people; nine of us would curse him and one would be unsure. So we would leave him after entering to him: nine of us would seek proximity to Allah through his love, and one would remain standing (unsure), because he would accompany us with the excellence of the Companions, what we had narrated and what we had not narrated, so we would write it down for his goodness from him, may Allah be pleased with him.

Among them is what Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed me about, from Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Sufyan Al-Bazufari (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: The Shaykh Abu al-Qasim Al-Husayn ibn Rauh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, saying: Our companions differed regarding al-tafwid (delegation of authority) and other matters, so I went to Abu Tahir ibn Bilal during the days of his correctness/orthodoxy and informed him of the difference of opinion. He said: Delay for me. So I delayed for him for some days, then I returned to him and he brought out for me a hadith with its chain leading to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: When Allah wills a matter, He presents it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and then to all the Imams, one after another, until it reaches the Master of the Age (peace be upon him), and then it is revealed to the world. And when the angels wish to raise a deed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it is presented to the Master of the Age (peace be upon him), then it goes out one after another until it is presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then it is presented to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So whatever descends from Allah is through their hands, and whatever ascends to Allah is through their hands, and they are never devoid of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the blink of an eye.

And a group informed me from Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Safwani, who said: Shaykh al-Husayn ibn Rawh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me that Yahya ibn Khalid poisoned Masuh ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) with twenty-one dates, and he died from it; and that the Prophet and the Imams (peace be upon them) did not die except by the sword or poison; and it has been mentioned regarding al-Rida (peace be upon him) that he was poisoned, and likewise his son and the son of his son.

A theologian, known as Turk al-Harawi, asked him: How many daughters did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) have? He said: Four. He asked: Which of them is most superior? He replied: Fatima. He asked: Why did she become the most superior, whereas she was the youngest in age and had the least companionship with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? He said: Because of two qualities, which Allah bestowed upon her exclusively, to prolong her status and honor and glorify her; one is that she inherited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and no other child of his did, and the second is that Allah the Exalted preserved the progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) through her and did not preserve it through anyone else. And He did not single her out for that except due to the excellence of sincerity which He knew from her intention. Al-Harawi said: I have not seen anyone who spoke and answered in this matter with a better or more concise reply than his answer.

And Abu Muhammad al-Muhammadi (may Allah be pleased with him) informed me from Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Thammam (may Allah have mercy on him) who said: I heard Abu Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Zakkuzaki (may Allah have mercy on him) and we had mentioned the Book of Taklif, and it was our belief that it was not possessed except by the Ghalis (Exaggerators). This was because, at the beginning when we started writing traditions, we heard him saying: 'What did Ibn Abi Azaqir have in the Book of Taklif?' He would only refine the chapter and bring it to the Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him), present it to him and scrutinize it. When the chapter was authenticated, it would be sent out, and he would transfer it and order us to make a copy. Meaning that which Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered them to do. Abu Ja'far said: 'I wrote it into the Idraj with my own hand in Baghdad.' Ibn Thammam said: 'I said to him: Please, my master, hand it to me so I may write it from your handwriting.' He said to me: 'It has gone out of my hand.' Ibn Thammam said: 'So I went out and took it from someone else and wrote it after I had heard this story.'

And Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed me on the authority of Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Qummi, who said: Salama ibn Muhammad told me: Shaykh Al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) sent the Book of Adab to Qom and wrote to a group of jurists there, saying to them: Examine this book and see if there is anything in it that disagrees with you. They wrote to him that all of it is correct and there is nothing in it that disagrees, except his statement regarding the sa' in fitra: half a sa' of food, and the food for us is like barley, from each one a sa'.

Ibn Nuh said: I heard a group of our companions in Egypt mentioned that Abu Sahl al-Nuubakhti was asked how this position reached Shaykh Abul Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh and not him. He said: They are more knowledgeable about who they have chosen. I am a man who meets the adversaries and debates with them. If I knew his place as Abul Qasim did, and the proof was pressed upon me regarding his place, perhaps I would indicate his place. But as for Abul Qasim, even if the Divine Proof were under his cloak and cut with scissors, he would not remove his cloak, or he said something like this.

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abul Azaqir al-Shalmaghani mentioned in the beginning of the Book of Occultation which he composed As for the dispute between me and the mentioned man, may Allah increase his success, I have no right to interfere in it except for one whom I involve, because the injury is upon me, so I am the one entitled to it.

And he said in another section: “For one upon whom God’s favor is great, the proof is multiplied against him, and truthfulness is incumbent upon him in what displeases and pleases him. It is not fitting for me, between me and Allah, but to speak the truth about his matter, despite his great fault. And this man is appointed to a duty from which the elite are not permitted to turn away. And the ruling of Islam, with that, applies to him as it applies to the others among the believers and their mention.”

Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa narrated: He said to me, Abu Ali ibn al-Junayd said to me, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shalmaghani said: "We did not enter into this matter with Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) except while we knew what we were entering into. We were fighting each other for this position like dogs fight over a corpse." Abu Muhammad said: "The Shia did not pay attention to this saying and remained united in cursing him and disavowing him."

The mention of the affair of Abul Hasan Ali bin Muhammad al-Samarrani after Shaykh Abul Qasim al-Husayn bin Ruh, may Allah be pleased with him, and the severing of the signs through him, and they are the Four Doors:

362 - A group of scholars narrated to me on the authority of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, who said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Zakariyya in the city of peace (al-Salam), who said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khallan narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather 'Attab, from the descendants of 'Attab ibn Umayd, who said: The successor - Mahdi (peace be upon him) was born on Friday, and his mother is Raihana, and she is called Narjis, and she is called Saiqal, and she is called Susan, except that it was said due to the pregnancy that she was called Saiqal.

And informed me Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man and al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Safwani, saying: The Shaykh Abul-Qasim (may Allah be pleased with him) bequeathed his authority to Abul-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samurri (may Allah be pleased with him), so he undertook the duties that were incumbent upon Abul-Qasim. When death approached him, the Shia gathered around him and asked him about the one appointed after him and who would take his place, but he did not reveal anything regarding that and mentioned that he had not been ordered to appoint anyone after him in this matter.

A group of scholars narrated to me from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, who said: Abu al-Hasan Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Taliqani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us in Dhul-Qa'dah of the year 339 AH: Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mukhallad narrated to us, saying: I was present in Baghdad among the scholars, may Allah bless them. Shaykh Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri, may his soul be sanctified, said spontaneously: May Allah have mercy on Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh al-Qummi. The scholars noted the date of that day, and news arrived that he had passed away on that very day. Abu al-Hasan al-Samuri died after that in the middle of Sha'ban in the year 329 AH.

A group of scholars informed us from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Muktabib told me: I was in the City of Peace (Baghdad) in the year in which the Shaykh Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri (may his soul be sanctified) passed away. I visited him a few days before his death, and he brought out a Tawqi' (letter) to the people, the text of which was: In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. O Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri, may Allah increase the reward of your brothers for you, for you shall die within six days. Tie up your affairs and do not appoint anyone to succeed you after your death, for the Complete Occultation has occurred, and there shall be no Appearance except by permission of Allah, exalted is His mention, and that will be after a long period, hardening of the hearts, and the earth being filled with injustice. And my Shia will come, one who claims to have seen me. Behold, whoever claims to have seen me before the emergence of al-Sufyani and the Call is a liar and a fabricator. And there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the High, the Great. He said: We transcribed this Tawqi' and left him. When it was the sixth day, we returned to him as he was breathing his last. He was asked: Who is your successor after you? He said: To Allah belongs the Order, and He is its Doer, and He has decreed. This was the last word we heard from him, may Allah be pleased with him and pleased him.

And a group informed me from Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, who said: A group from the people of Qom, among them Ali ibn Babawayh, narrated to me: A group from the people of Qom, among them Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Imran al-Saffar and his relative, the lady al-Saffar, and al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, may Allah have mercy on them, said: We were present in Baghdad in the year in which my father, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, passed away. And Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri, may his soul be sanctified, would ask us frequently about the news of Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on him). We would say: Letters have come stating he is well. Until came the day on which he was taken (died). He asked us about him, and we mentioned to him the same thing. He said to us: May Allah reward you regarding Ali ibn al-Husayn, for he has been taken (died) at this hour. They said: We recorded the date of the hour, the day, and the month. Then, after seventeen or eighteen days, news came that he had been taken (died) in that very hour which the Shaykh Abu al-Hasan (may his soul be sanctified) had mentioned.
During the period of the praiseworthy emissaries, there were reliable individuals to whom epistles were returned by those appointed for the deputyship from the source.
Among them is Abul Husain Muhammad ibn Ja'far Asadi, may Allah have mercy on him.

Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Jayyid al-Qummi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Salih ibn Abi Salih, saying: Some people asked me in the year two hundred and ninety to collect religious dues. I refused that request and wrote a letter seeking instructions. The answer came: 'In Ray is Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Arabi. He should deliver it to him, for he is from our men of trust.'

And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated from Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Shashi, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Katib al-Marwazi said to me: I sent two hundred dinars to Hajiz al-Washsha and wrote to the Gharim (peace be upon him) about it. The reply came, mentioning that he had previously owed me one thousand dinars, and that I had sent him two hundred dinars. He said: 'If you wish to deal with someone, refer to Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi in Ray.' Then news arrived of Hajiz's death after two or three days. I informed him of his death, and he became grieved. I said to him: 'Do not grieve, for in the Tawqi' (letter) addressed to you, there are two indications: one is his informing you that the money owed is one thousand dinars, and the second is his command to you to deal with Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi, knowing the death of Hajiz.'

And through this chain of narration from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Nubakht who said: I intended to go for Hajj and made preparations for this purpose. A message came, 'We dislike that.' I became much anxious and grievous. I wrote, 'I remain submissive and obedient. However, I am sad for missing the Hajj.' A holy letter came: 'Grieve not, for you will perform Hajj next year.' Next year, I sought permission and the answer came in positive. I wrote, 'I am leaving Muhammad Ibn Abbas behind, and I am certain of his piety and honesty.' The answer came, 'Asadi is the best caretaker. If he should arrive, do not choose anyone over him.' Asadi came and I left him as my caretaker.

394 - Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Shadhan al-Nishapuri said: Five hundred dirhams, short of twenty dirhams, were deposited with me. I did not like for this amount to be short, so I weighed twenty dirhams from my own money and sent them to al-Asadi. I did not inform him of the shortage, nor that I had completed the amount from my own wealth. The reply came: 'The five hundred, of which twenty were yours, have reached us.' Al-Asadi died upon apparent justice (honesty), he did not change, and no one raised an objection against him in the month of Rabi' al-Akhar in the year 312 AH.
And among them is Ahmad ibn Ishaq and a group; the Tawqi' (Decree) was issued regarding their praise:

Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Muhammad al-Razi, who said: I and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah were at al-Askar when a messenger came from 'the Man' and said: 'Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ashari, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, and Ahmad ibn Hamza ibn al-Yasa are all trusted men.'

We have clarified through authentic reports that the birth of the Master of the Era (peace be upon him) was in the year two hundred and fifty-six. And that his father (peace be upon him) passed away in the year two hundred and sixty, so at that time he was four years old. So his age until the time of his emergence is what calculation dictates. And that does not contradict the reports that have been narrated regarding the measure of his age, which differ in wording.

Similar to what is narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said: The Master of this Command (the Imam) — if he passes away, it is not after forty [years of age] — is the Master of this Command, the strong and energetic one. And similar to this are the reports that have come with differing words and divergent meanings.

And it strengthens that which Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik from Umar ibn Tarqan from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Ali ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, the Master of God will live a lifespan of one hundred and twenty years, like Prophet Ibrahim (the Friend), and he will appear in the form of a young man who has completed thirty years.

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Aquli, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: When the Qaim arises, people will deny him; he will return to them as a young man, and none will remain with him except every believer in whom Allah took the covenant in the first age of creation.

And it has been narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: Do you not deny that Allah will prolong the lifespan of the Master of this affair, just as He prolonged the lifespan of Nuh (peace be upon him)?
The Christians narrate that among those who preceded them, there was one who lived seven hundred years and more.
As for what has been narrated from the reports that include that the Master of the Age will die and then live, or be killed and then live, similar to what he narrated:

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Musa ibn Sadan, from Abdullah ibn Qasim al-Hadrami, from Abu Saeed al-Khorasani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Why is he named as the Qaim?' He said: 'Because he will rise after he dies. Indeed, he will rise with a great matter; he will rise by the command of Allah, the Glorified.'

And Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'The similitude of our Order in the Book of Allah is like the owner of the donkey; Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him up.'

And from him, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi', from Ali ibn Khattab, from the muezzin of the Red Mosque, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is there in the Book of Allah a similitude for the Qaim (peace be upon him)? He said: Yes, the verse of the owner of the donkey; Allah made him die for a hundred years, then raised him up.

And Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Hammad ibn Abd al-Karim, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When the Qaim (peace be upon him) rises, the people will say, 'How can this be, when his bones have decayed for a long time?'

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabla, from Salma ibn Junah al-Ja'fi, from Hazim ibn Habib, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hazim, indeed the master of this affair has two occultations; he will appear in the second one. If someone comes to you and says, "I have brushed the dust from his grave," do not believe him.'

And Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'For the owner of this affair, there are four traditions from four prophets: a tradition from Moses, a tradition from Jesus, a tradition from Joseph, and a tradition from Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). As for the tradition from Moses, it is being fearful and awaiting; as for the tradition from Joseph, it is the occultation; as for the tradition from Jesus, it is said: he died, yet he did not die; and as for the tradition from Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), it is the sword.'

And al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated from Ahmad ibn Isa al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Master of this Affair is from my offspring. It will be said about him: He has died! He was killed! No, rather he perished! No, rather he went down into some valley.
As for the time of his emergence, the Imam (peace be upon him), it is not known to us in detail; rather, he is hidden from us until Allah grants permission for the relief (reappearance).

As it is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) (that he said: "If only one day were to remain from the tenure of the world, Allah would prolong that day until a man from my progeny emerges, and he would fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it was filled with injustice and oppression.")

And Husayn ibn Abdillah informed me, from Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Safwan al-Bazufari, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ubays ibn Hashim, from Karam, from al-Fadl ibn Shaybah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) "Is there a fixed time for this matter?" He said: "The time-fixers have lied, the time-fixers have lied, the time-fixers have lied."

Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Sahhaf, from Al-Mundhir al-Jawwaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Those who fix (predict) the time have lied. Neither have we fixed a time for it in the past, nor would we do so in the future.

And by this chain, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Muhzim al-Asadi entered upon him. He said: Inform me, may I be your ransom, when is this affair that we are waiting for? It has been delayed too long. He (peace be upon him) said: O Muhzim, the time-keepers have lied, the hasteners will perish, and the Muslims will be saved, and they will return to us.

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: One who fixes the time for you among the people, do not hesitate to call him a liar, for we do not specify a time for anyone.

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Umar ibn Muslim al-Bajali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Muhammad ibn Bashir al-Hamadani, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah - in a tradition from which we have condensed the point of need - that he said: Indeed, for the people of so-and-so there is a kingdom appointed for a term. When they feel secure and at ease, and think that their kingdom will not cease, a cry will be raised among them, and no leader will remain to gather them, nor a caller to be heard by them. "Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think that they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest, as though it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who give thought." I said: May I be your ransom, is there a fixed time for that? He replied: No, because the knowledge of Allah surpasses the knowledge of those who fix times. Indeed, Allah the Exalted promised Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten, which Musa did not know, nor did the Children of Israel know. So when the time passed, they said: Musa has deceived us! And they worshipped the calf. But when need and poverty increase among the people, and one denies another, then at that time expect the command of Allah morning and evening.
As for what has been narrated from the reports that apparently contradict that, such as what he narrated:

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Sadan ibn ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him: 'Is there a fixed time for this matter (the reappearance), so that we can rest our bodies and wait for it?' He replied: 'Yes, but you publicized it, so God increased it (postponed it).'

And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: There will be tribulation until the seventieth [year]. And he used to say: After the tribulation, there will be ease/peace. But the seventy years have passed and we have not seen ease! So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: O Thabit, indeed Allah the Exalted had fixed this matter [the end of tribulation] at seventy. But when Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was martyred, the anger of Allah intensified upon the people of the earth, so He postponed it to one hundred and forty years. We informed you, but you publicized the hadith and revealed the veil of the secret, so Allah postponed it further and did not fix a specific time for it with us after that. Allah erases what He wills and confirms [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Abu Hamza said: And I said that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: That was indeed the case.

And Fadl narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Yahya al-Tamtam al-Salami, from Uthman al-Naww, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'This matter was initially with me; then Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, postponed it, and He will do in my progeny what He wills.'

The correct approach in these reports is that we say: if they are sound, it is not impossible that Allah, the Mighty and High, has fixed this matter in the times mentioned. Thus, when new conditions arise, the wisdom changes and necessitates delaying it to another time, and similarly thereafter. The first time, and every time that can be postponed, is conditional upon no new factor arising that necessitates delay until the time arrives which nothing can change, making it definite. On this basis, we interpret reports concerning the delay of lifespans from their appointed times, and their increase through supplication, charity, and connecting kinship; and reports concerning the reduction of lifespans from their times to an earlier time due to oppression, severing kinship, and other acts. And although He, the Exalted, is aware of both matters, it is not impossible that one is known conditionally and the other unconditionally. This statement is without dispute among the people of Justice (Ahl al-Adl). And on this basis, we also interpret our reports containing the word 'Bada' (occurrence/change), clarifying that its meaning is abrogation as all people of Justice intend regarding what allows abrogation, or the change of its conditions, if its method is news about events (Takweeni). Because 'Bada' in language means appearance/revelation. Thus, it is not impossible that an act of Allah becomes apparent to us which we had thought otherwise, or that we know it but do not know its condition.

Among such reports is the report of Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi (may Allah have mercy on him), from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: Allah did not send any prophet except to prohibit wine, and to confess to Allah regarding al-Bada (that ﴿Indeed, Allah does whatever He pleases﴾), and that incense should be in his inheritance.

Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn, and before him Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Muhammad ibn Ali and Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them all) said: How can we have knowledge of the future (hadith) in light of this verse: "Allah erases and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book"? "Allah erases and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book." As for one who says that the Almighty Allah does not know anything except after it comes into existence, he has become a disbeliever and has exited from monotheism.

And Saad ibn Abdullah has narrated from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari that he said: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Armani asked Abu Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Sublime: "Allah erases and establishes what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book," so Abu Muhammad said: "Is it not that He erases that which was and establishes that which was not?" I said to myself: This is contrary to what Hisham ibn al-Hakam says: that He does not know a thing until it comes into existence. So Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) looked at me and said: "Exalted is the Almighty, the Knower of things before their existence... and the hadith is condensed."

421 - Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Ali, from Al-Sadan ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked him: 'Is there a fixed time for this matter (the reappearance) in which we may rest our bodies and reach it?' He replied: 'Yes, but you people divulged it, so Allah increased it (postponed it).'

The correct view in these reports is what we previously mentioned: that the exigency (reason for action) in that matter changed, necessitating the postponement of the command to another time, as we clarified, without the exigency itself becoming known to Almighty Allah. Therefore, we do not say it nor do we approve of it; Allah is greatly exalted above that. If it is said: 'This leads to us not trusting in any of the reports of Allah,' we say: Reports are of two kinds. First kind: Those in which change is not permissible in their reported content, for we are certain of them, knowing that the reported content itself cannot change, such as reports about the attributes of Allah, past events, and that He will reward the believers. Second kind: Those in which change is possible in themselves due to the change of exigency when their conditions change; we approve of all such change, such as reports about future events. However, if a report comes in a manner where we know the reported content will not change, then we are certain of its occurrence. For this reason, certainty was linked with some reports, informing us that they are something that does not change at all, and at that point we are certain of them.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ataa, from Salam ibn Abi 'Umrah, who said: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said: 'The master of this matter will have a house called the House of Praise. In it is a lamp that shines from the day he was born until he rises with the sword.'

A group of scholars narrated to us from al-Talaqbari, from Ali ibn Habashi, from Ja'far ibn Malik, from Ahmad ibn Abi Naeem, from Ibrahim ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Ghazal, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: 'When our Qaim arises, the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the people will become needless [of sunlight]. A man will live long in his dominion until a thousand males are born to him, and no female is born among them. A mosque will be built on the outskirts of Kufa with a thousand doors, and the houses of Kufa will be connected to the river of Karbala and to al-Hira, so that a man will set out on Friday on a white mule intending to attend the Friday Prayer but will not be able to reach it in time.'

Abu Muhammad al-Muhammadi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Malik, from Ibrahim ibn Banan al-Kha'thami, from Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Amr ibn Thabit, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in a long tradition, who said: The Mahdi will enter Kufa, and there will be three standards which have become confused among them, so they will become clear to him. He will enter until he comes to the pulpit and preaches, and the people will not know what he is saying due to weeping. This is the statement of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'As if I see the Hasanid and the Husainid who have raised the flags, so he hands it over to the Husainid and they pay allegiance to him.' Then on the second Friday, the people will say: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, prayer behind you is equivalent to prayer behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), but the mosque does not accommodate us.' He will say: 'I will survey for you,' so he will go out to al-Ghari and mark a mosque for him with a thousand doors that accommodates the people, covered with tiles. He will send and dig a river from behind the tomb of Husain (peace be upon him) for them that flows to the Ghariyyan until it descends into Najaf. Bridges and mills will be working at its entrance on the path. And as if I see an old woman with a sack of wheat on her head, until she grinds it in Karbala.

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ismail ibn Ayyash, from Al-A'mash, from Abu Wael, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: When the Mahdi was mentioned: 'Indeed, he will be given allegiance between the Rukn and the Maqam. His name is Ahmad, Abdullah, and Al-Mahdi; these are his three names.'

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Masjid al-Sahla was mentioned, so he said: 'Indeed, it is the residence of our Master (Imam al-Mahdi) when he arrives with his family.'

From him, from Musa ibn Sadan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from Abu Saeed al-Khurasani, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the Mahdi and the Qaim one and the same?' He said: 'Yes.' I asked: 'Why is he named the Mahdi?' He said: 'Because he guides to every hidden matter, and he is named the Qaim because he rises after his death, indeed he will establish a great affair.'

From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr bin Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Whoever among you meets our Qaim, let him say when he sees him: Peace be upon you, O Ahl al-Bayt of prophethood, mine of knowledge, and place of messengership.

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Surely the companions of Musa were tested with a river, and it is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Surely Allah will try you with a river.' And surely the companions of the Qaim will be tested in the same way.

From him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Qaim (peace be upon him) will demolish the Sacred Mosque until he restores it to its foundation, and the Prophet's Mosque (peace be upon him and his family) to its foundation, and he will return the House to its place and establish it upon its foundation, and he will cut off the hands of the thieves of Bani Shaybah and hang them on the Kaaba.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from Abi Sadiq, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Our state/government is the last of the states, and no House will remain having a state/government except that it ruled before us, so that they would not say when they see our conduct: If we had ruled, we would have conducted ourselves like these people. And it is the word of Allah, the Exalted: '...and the end is for those who guard (against evil).'

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim and al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abi Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: When the Qaim (peace be upon him) arises, he will come with a system/unprecedented matter unlike that which was before.

From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Sa'd ibn Zarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in his hadith until he reached the Mosque of Kufa, which was built with pottery, bricks, and clay. He said: Woe to the one who demolished you! Woe to the one who facilitated your demolition! Woe to the one who built you with solid bricks, changing the Qibla of Nuh! Good fortune to the one who witnesses your demolition with the Qaim of my Ahl al-Bayt! Those are the best of the nation with the righteous of the 'Itrah.

And from him, from Ali ibn Abdullah, from Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abul Jarud who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Qaim will rule for three hundred and nine years, just as the people of the Cave remained in their cave. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, as it was filled with injustice and tyranny. Allah will open for him the east and west of the earth, and he will kill the people until no religion remains except that of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). He will proceed with the way of Sulaiman ibn Dawud... The rest of the report.

From him, from Abdur Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir (from Abu Ja'far) in a tradition of his which we have summarized, He said: When the Qaim (peace be upon him) arises, he will enter Kufa and order the demolition of the four mosques until their foundations are reached, making them like the canopies of Musa (peace be upon him). The mosques will all be plain, without upper stories or additions, as they were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He will widen the main highway to sixty cubits, demolish every mosque on the road, and block every window, balcony, latrine, and gutter facing the road. Allah will command the heavens in his time to slow their rotation, so that a day in his time is like ten of your days, a month like ten of your months, and a year like ten of your years. He will not remain long before the rebels from the Mawali emerge from Rumaylat al-Daskara, ten thousand in number, their slogan being: 'O Uthman, O Uthman!' He will summon one of the Mawali, attach a sword to his waist, and go out to them, killing them until not one remains. Then he will turn to Kabul Shah, a city that no one else has ever conquered, and he will conquer it. After that, he will return to Kufa, make it his residence, and defeat seventy Arab tribes… The end of the narration.
In another report (that) he would conquer Constantine, Rome and China.

From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his father Asbat ibn Salim, from Musa al-Ibar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Be wary of the Arabs, for they have a bad omen/portent. Indeed, not one of them will rise with the Qaim.

From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Imran ibn Zabyan, from Hakim ibn Saad, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said: The companions of the Mahdi will be young men; there will be no old men among them except like the kohl in the eye or the salt in the provisions, and the least part of the provisions is the salt.

From him, from Ahmad ibn Umar ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Uqbah ibn al-Nahmi, from Abu Ishaq al-Banna, from Jabir al-Ja'fi who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Qaim will receive allegiance between the Rukn and the Maqam by three hundred and thirteen, the number of the people of Badr. Among them are the nobles from Egypt, the Abdal from Syria, and the virtuous from Iraq. He will remain in power for as long as Allah wills.

From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Wahib ibn Hafas, from Abu Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: People will continue to decrease until it is no longer said: 'Allah'. When that happens, the leader of religion will rise up, and Allah will send a group from its extremities, coming like a sudden rush like the rush of autumn. By Allah, I know them, I know their names, their tribes, and the name of their commander (and the resting places of their mounts), and they are a group whom Allah carries however He wills; from one tribe He takes one man, from another two... until it reaches nine, so they gather from the horizons three hundred and thirteen (men), the number of the people of Badr, which is the word of Allah: 'Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together; indeed Allah is over all things competent.' So much so that a man might be in his tent, and his tent is not untied until Allah brings him there.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in a lengthy report, that he said: O Abu Hamza, indeed from us, after the Qa'im, there will be eleven Mahdis from the descendants of Husain (peace be upon him).

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'By Allah, a man from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, will rule after his death for three hundred and nine years.' I asked: 'When will this be?' He replied: 'After the Qaim (peace be upon him).' I asked: 'For how many years will the Qaim rule in his world?' He replied: 'Nineteen years. Then the Muntasir will emerge and seek revenge for the blood of Husayn (peace be upon him) and the blood of his companions, killing and capturing until the Saffah emerges.'

Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated: Husayn ibn Ali al-Rawasi attended the funeral of Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him). When the body was placed by the edge of the grave, a messenger from Sandi ibn Shahik arrived and said to Aba al-Muda, his deputy (who was with the funeral procession): 'Expose his face to the people before you bury him, so that they may see him healthy, that no new event (injury/torture) has happened to him.' He said: 'They uncovered the face of my Master, so I saw him and recognized him, then his face was covered and he was placed in his grave, may God's blessings be upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Ubaydi said: Rahim, the mother of al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, who was a free and virtuous woman who had performed Hajj twenty-seven times, informed me from Saeed, the servant of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) - who used to serve him in prison and be sent for his needs - that he was present when he died, just as people die from strength to weakness, until he passed away (peace be upon him).

And Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibad al-Muhallabi who said: When Harun al-Rashid imprisoned Abu Ibrahim Musa (peace be upon him) and he displayed signs and miracles while in prison, al-Rashid was bewildered. He summoned Yahya ibn Khalid al-Barmaki and said to him: 'O Abu Ali, do you not see what we are in from these wonders? Do you not consider the affair of this man with a plan that relieves us from his worry?' So Yahya ibn Khalid al-Barmaki said to him: 'What I advise you to do, O Commander of the Faithful, is to show him favor and connect his kinship, for by Allah, he has spoiled the hearts of our followers against us.' And Yahya was favoring him, while Harun did not know that. So Harun said: 'Go to him, release the iron from him, and convey my greetings to him, and say to him: Your cousin says: An oath has preceded from me concerning you that I will not release you until you admit to me the mistreatment, and ask me for forgiveness for what has passed from you. And there is no disgrace upon you in your admission, nor any deficiency in your asking me. And this is Yahya ibn Khalid (he is) my trustworthy one, my minister, and the manager of my affairs. So ask him to the extent that he removes me from my oath, and he will depart successfully.'

Muhammad ibn 'Ibad said: Musa ibn Yahya ibn Khalid informed me: Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to Yahya: 'O Abu Ali, I am dying; only a week remains for me. Keep my death secret and come to me on Friday at midday, and you and my friends pray for me individually. And observe when this tyrant travels to Ar-Raqqa and returns to Iraq; he should not see you and you should not see him, for my own sake, for I have seen in your star, the star of your son, and his star that he will come upon you, so beware of him.' Then he said: 'O Abu Ali, convey to him from me: Musa ibn Ja'far says to you: My messenger will come to you on Friday and inform you of what you see. And you will know tomorrow when you stand before Allah, who is the wrongdoer and the aggressor against his companion. And peace.' Yahya went out from his presence, his eyes reddened from weeping, until he entered upon Harun and informed him of his story and what he replied. Harun said to him: 'If he does not claim prophethood after a few days, how good our state will be!' When it was Friday, Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) died. Harun had already traveled to Al-Mada'in before that. He was brought out to the people so they could look at him, then he was buried (peace be upon him), and the people returned. They split into two groups: one group said: 'He died,' and the other group said: 'He did not die.'

From Zurarah, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was sitting with him, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: 'Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have ten like it… and whoever brings an evil deed, he shall not be recompensed except like it, and they will not be wronged.' Does it apply to these, from among those who do not recognize this affair (of Wilayah)? He replied: It is exclusively for the believers.
From Ya'qub ibn Shu'aib, he said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Allah has not taken it on Himself to reward anyone for good deeds except the believers.

And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: A believer's light shines for the inhabitants of the heavens like stars shining for the inhabitants of the earth. He also said: A believer is a friend of Allah; he helps Him and works for Him and he does not say concerning Allah anything but the truth; and he does not fear anyone other than Him.
